name: Nathan Pusey
profession: Harvard President Through Growth and Turmoil Alike
headline: Nathan Pusey, Harvard President Through Growth and Turmoil Alike, Dies at 94
abstract: Nathan M Pusey, who led Harvard University through tremendous growth and liberalization only to be swept away storm over Vietnam-era protests, dies at 94; in Pusey's tenure as Harvard's 24th president, from 1953 to 1971, university's budget quadrupled, as did its endowments; photos (L)

name: Dutch Warmerdam
headline: Dutch Warmerdam, Pole-Vaulter, Dies at 86
abstract: Cornelius (Dutch) Warmerdam, greatest pole-vaulter in era before fiberglass poles changed the sport, and first man to clear 15 feet, dies at 86; photo (M)

name: Frank Messer
headline: Frank Messer, Former Yankees Announcer, Dies at 76
abstract: Frank Messer, the straight arrow announcer of Yankee games for 18 seasons, died Tuesday at his home in Deerfield Beach, Fla. He was 76.    He died of heart problems, but also had lupus, said Rebecca Messer, his former wife.

name: Peggy Mount
headline: Peggy Mount, 85, British Actress Who Made Grown Men Tremble
abstract: Peggy Mount, for many years the fearsome battle-ax of British stage and screen with a voice to make henpecked husbands tremble, died on Tuesday at a London nursing home for actors. She was 85.    Although best known for her bullying, harridan roles, Ms. Mount was also successful in classical theater with much praised performances as the nurse to Judi Dench's Juliet in Franco Zeffirelli's memorable Old Vic production of ''Romeo and Juliet'' in 1960 and in the title role of Brecht's ''Mother Courage'' at the Birmingham Repertory Theater in 1977.

name: Roberta Pryor
headline: Roberta Pryor, 77, Literary Agent for 'Jaws'
abstract: Roberta Pryor, a literary agent who acquired the best-selling author Peter Benchley as a client when he was 16 and was still his agent two decades later, when he became famous as the author of ''Jaws,'' died on Monday in a hospital in Brooklyn. She was 77 and lived in Brooklyn.    She had Alzheimer's disease, said Jed Mattes, a friend.

name: Mitzi Myers
profession: Writer, Editor And Scholar of Children's Books
headline: Mitzi Myers, 62, Writer, Editor And Scholar of Children's Books
abstract: Mitzi Myers, an internationally recognized authority on children's literature and a longtime lecturer at the University of California at Los Angeles, died on Nov. 5 at her temporary residence in Anaheim Hills, Calif. She was 62.    The cause was complications from pneumonia she contracted after a fire last year at her permanent home in Fullerton, Calif., said Patsy Myers, her sister.

name: Franz Hoskins
headline: Franz Hoskins, 86, Dies; Aided in Surgery on Sub
abstract: Dr. Franz P. Hoskins, a Navy officer in World War II who took part in a storied appendectomy aboard a submarine years before he went to medical school, died on Nov. 8 in Kingsport, Tenn. He was 86.    On Sept. 11, 1942, at a depth of 120 feet in the China Sea, a pharmacist's mate and a group of officers -- none of them a doctor -- joined together on the Seadragon for what was evidently the first major surgical operation ever performed on a submerged submarine.

name: Panama Francis
headline: Panama Francis, 82, Jazz Drummer of Swing Era
abstract: Panama Francis, a drummer who played for dancers through the glory years of swing in high-profile bands  like Lucky Millinder's, Cab Calloway's and Slim Gaillard's, played on countless rhythm-and-blues and rock 'n' roll sessions and  became a standard-bearing swing-nostalgia musician, died on Sunday at a hospital in Orlando, Fla. He was 82 and lived in Altamont, Fla.     Mr. Francis was a soloing drummer, but he was most prized for keeping a strong, hard-swinging, behind-the-beat pulse. He worked at the Savoy Ballroom (the Home of Happy Feet) in Manhattan, when swing dancing was at its peak, and believed  in jazz as dance music. He said he was unhappy with jazz in recent years.

name: Max Hunter
profession: Rocket Engineer With Wealth of Ideas for Space
headline: Max Hunter, 79, Rocket Engineer With Wealth of Ideas for Space
abstract: Maxwell White Hunter, a rocket engineer, project manager and visionary of the space age, died on Nov. 10 at Stanford Hospital in Palo Alto, Calif. He was 79 and lived in San Carlos, Calif.    The cause was complications from  a fall, his family said.

name: Eugene Clark
headline: Eugene Clark: From the Terrace
abstract: In life, Eugene Clark observed the three D's: dance, drama and divas. He started early: Roberta Flack was his music teacher in Washington, D.C., during the 1960's. He could sing like Jennifer Holliday in the musical "Dreamgirls," he could emote like Norma Desmond in "Sunset Boulevard" and he danced "like Tina Turner," said Larry Courtney, Mr. Clark's partner for the last 13 years. "And he had legs almost as good."

name: Robert J. Fangman
headline: Robert J. Fangman: A Job That Fit
abstract: Money is little comfort when you hate your job. As a salesman for Verizon Wireless, the only part Robert J. Fangman liked about his job was the travel, said his mother, Ruth. So he kept the travel, threw out the selling, and took a 50 percent pay cut to become a flight attendant with United Airlines last November.

name: Satguru Subramuniyaswami
headline: Satguru Subramuniyaswami, Hindu Spiritual Leader, Dies at 74
abstract: Satguru Sivaya Subramuniya swami, a native Californian who sought spiritual meaning in India as a young man and became the spiritual leader of Sri Lankan Hindus, died on Tuesday.

name: H. Joseph Heller
headline: H. Joseph Heller: A Broker and a Fixer
abstract: Whenever H. Joseph Heller felt strongly that he should do something, he went out and did it. That's how he ended up owning a yellow turn-of- the-last-century farmhouse on a hilly acre in Ridgefield, Conn., a house that his wife, Mary Jean, calls "a major fixer-upper."

name: James Douglas Halvorson
headline: James Douglas Halvorson: Meticulous in Work and Play
abstract: As a managing director at Marsh & McLennan, the insurance brokerage company where he worked for 30 years, James Douglas Halvorson was meticulous in structuring complex deals for construction projects in Pakistan, Indonesia and other third world countries. He was similarly methodical in his pleasures.

name: Joseph E. Maloney
headline: Joseph E. Maloney: We Hardly Knew Ye
abstract: You probably think you know Firefighter Joseph E. Maloney. Son of a cop; grandson of a fireman; married forever to Kathy, the pretty, tough- talking nurse; father of Joe, 10, and Megan, 7.

name: Sharon Moore
headline: Sharon Moore: Laughing at Her Stumbles
abstract: For all of Sharon Moore's beauty and elegance -- a slender 5 feet, 9 inches, she was a sometime model whose photo was featured in an issue of Esquire -- she lacked a certain physical grace. "She was a very clumsy person," said Barbara Bridges, Ms. Moore's mother. "She was always falling."

name: Thomas Farino
headline: Thomas Farino: The Gift of Strength
abstract: Capt. Thomas Farino was the rock on which his wife, Mary, built her life. He was the baby in a family of six boys, sons of a New York City policeman. He was captain of Engine Company 26 in Manhattan, doing a job he loved. He was posthumously promoted to battalion chief.

name: Thierry Saada
headline: Thierry Saada: Bellybutton Melodies
abstract: When Thierry Saada came to New York in 1999 from Paris, he sublet Delphine Zana's apartment through mutual friends in the Sephardic Jewish community. Both their families were originally from Tunisia, but moved to France after Tunisian independence. Mr. Saada was tall, handsome, and "sportif," she said, and they fell in love.

name: Edward R. Vanacore
headline: Edward R. Vanacore: A Sunset Hog in the Rain
abstract: Eddie Vanacore had a smile that made everyone around him happy. He was also the youngest of six, and he learned early to be persistent in getting what he wanted. "He was a pain in the neck," said his brother John, the next oldest in the family.

name: Ronnie Lee Henderson
headline: Ronnie Lee Henderson: An Abundance of Family
abstract: He may have been earning a fireman's salary, but Ronnie Lee Henderson planned all along to turn that into more. He pared money from his paycheck and put it into bonds and mutual funds. In the quiet hours at the Engine Company 279 firehouse in Red Hook, he could be found reading books with titles like "How to Make Money Buying and Selling Houses."

name: Charles Mathers
headline: Charles Mathers: In Crisis or Comedy
abstract: Here is the man you want in a crisis: while everyone squawks, he is listening. A great bear of a fellow, his eyes bright blue and calm, white- haired head nodding, he says, "Hmmmm." Then, "I'll take care of it." And he does.

name: Salvatore Gitto
headline: Salvatore Gitto: Spirit in the Sky
abstract: The Gitto family did everything as a unit. They raked leaves together. They painted together. They fixed lights together. And everyone piled into the car for trips to the supermarket.

name: Albert C. Todd
headline: Albert C. Todd, 74, Professor and Translator
abstract: Albert C Todd, professor of European languages and literatures, dies at age 74 (S)

name: Peter A. Vega
headline: Peter A. Vega: Always Ready to Help
abstract: Regan Grice-Vega was pregnant and was on the way to the doctor for a checkup with her husband, Peter Vega, when they spotted a car stalled on the side of the road. In it was a woman who had been rushing to the hospital to see her husband, who had had a heart attack. Mr. Vega pushed her car to a safe spot and then drove her to the hospital.

name: Richard D. Rosenthal
headline: Richard D. Rosenthal: With That Devilish Grin
abstract: Richard D. Rosenthal was not a daredevil, but he did have a childlike adventurous streak. "My older daughter called him a man-kid," said his sister, Audrey Model. His 40th birthday party had a "Three Stooges" theme. For his 50th birthday party last May, Ms. Model toasted her brother, saying she hoped he would remain a man-kid.

name: Eric Steen
headline: Eric Steen: Man for All Callings
abstract: Eric Steen spent his days as a bond trader for Euro Brokers in 2 World Trade Center. But he had a secret desire to make his mark in the arts, and that is why he was working on a screenplay, finishing a novel and launching a film-production company in his spare time. "He didn't want to divulge that until it was all finished," said his friend David Hegarty, who attended Garden City High School with him. "He was a pretty deep thinker, and he was very well read, so that was a whole other area where he could feel fulfilled outside of Wall Street."

name: Daniel Rossetti
headline: Daniel Rossetti: His Days on the Water
abstract: Daniel Rossetti was a carpenter by trade, but he loved and lived to fish.

name: Vito Deleo
headline: Vito Deleo: 'Never Surrender'
abstract: Vito DeLeo was in court in March 1994 when four defendants were convicted in the 1993 bombing of the World Trade Center.

name: Douglas B. Gardner
headline: Douglas B. Gardner: Cards Full of Mad Love
abstract: When Joseph Gardner took his young son, Douglas B. Gardner, to watch his first Knicks game, Douglas said he wanted to play basketball in Madison Square Garden. His father told him he would have to own the team to do that.

name: Charles Lucania
headline: Charles Lucania: Man With a Beach Bug
abstract: On weekends, the gang gravitated to Charles Lucania's small but serene bungalow just a block off the surf at Atlantic Beach. His friends turned up with burgers for the barbecue. His nephews turned up with toys and bathing suits. Someone usually brought a backgammon board, not that Mr. Lucania, 34, ever sat still long enough to play.

name: Douglas G. Karpiloff
headline: Douglas G. Karpiloff: Security and Sweetness
abstract: After the World Trade Center was bombed in 1993, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey made Douglas G. Karpiloff the director of security and life safety for the center. He installed an array of protective systems, including huge concrete planters around the towers, a strict set of building passes and an identification and tracking system for vehicles entering the basement. He was also called in to consult about security in Denver before Timothy McVeigh's trial for the Oklahoma City bombing and on how to protect the White House and other federal buildings. Last year, his industry trade group named him security director of the year.

name: Margaret Seeliger
headline: Margaret Seeliger: A Mother's Leanings
abstract: Margaret Seeliger gave up her place on a crowded elevator leaving the 100th floor of 2 World Trade Center to two colleagues, an act of generosity that surprised neither her husband nor the oldest of her eight siblings. Worrying about others was her way.

name: Vincent Litto
headline: Vincent Litto: A Very Large Group of 'Us'
abstract: When Vincent Litto's sister was stricken with multiple sclerosis in 1979, she was no longer able to care for her daughter. So Mr. Litto and his wife, Linda, took the daughter in and raised her as their own. She was one of four girls Mr. Litto doted on.

name: Lars Qualben
headline: Lars Qualben: The Giving Trees
abstract: The abandoned lots were originally strewn with rusty cars, decrepit refrigerators and rubble. But over the years, the land became a secret garden, a tree-lined oasis with winding brick paths in the middle of Brooklyn.

name: Karl Smith
headline: Karl Smith: Boating and Breakfast
abstract: Karl Smith liked all things active: he got his wife, Joanne, started on running, and when they were first dating, they took karate together.

name: Aisha Harris
headline: Aisha Harris: Keeper of Confidences
abstract: Aisha Harris had a plan for her life, and she told her mother, Arvette Harris, that she was on schedule. At 22, she enjoyed her job at General Telecom as a customer services representative, dealing with accounts and troubleshooting. She switched her major at New York Technical College to telecommunications because she saw a future in the field.

name: Melvin Burkhart
headline: Melvin Burkhart, 'Human Blockhead' in Vanishing Sideshow Culture, Dies at 94
abstract: Melvin Burkhart, legendary sideshow performer, dies at age 94; photo (M)

name: Peter M. West
headline: Peter M. West: Terms of the Deal
abstract: For Eileen West, there was always "the deal" she had with her husband, Peter M. West. The deal was an agreement that spontaneity had its time and its place, and that Mrs. West was the one to say, gently, when and where. On vacations, Mr. West, a municipal bond broker at Cantor Fitzgerald, could do his latest daredevil thrill, like skydiving or hang-gliding. "But never on the first day of vacation," said Mrs. West, a hospital administrator, "always on the last."

name: Douglas D. Ketcham
headline: Douglas D. Ketcham: He Just Started Climbing
abstract: Douglas D. Ketcham climbed the corporate ladder. Literally.

name: Tommy Flanagan
headline: Tommy Flanagan, Elegant Jazz Pianist, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Tommy Flanagan, jazz pianist, dies at age 71; photo (M)

name: Harrison A. Williams Jr.
profession: Went to Prison Over Abscam Scandal
headline: Ex-Senator Harrison A. Williams Jr., 81, Dies; Went to Prison Over Abscam Scandal
abstract: Harrison A. Williams Jr., the Democratic senator from New Jersey who used his considerable power to further the interests of labor and education before being convicted of bribery and conspiracy in the Abscam scandal, died on Saturday. He was 81 and lived in Bedminster.    Dr. Bruce Mintz, his physician, said he died of heart disease at St. Clare's Hospital in Denville, N.J.

name: Augustus C. Long
headline: Augustus C. Long, 97, Chief Of Texaco in 50's and 60's
abstract: Augustus C Long, former chief executive of Texaco, dies at age 97; photo (S)

name: Gene Fenn
headline: OBITUARY : Gene Fenn, 90, Photographer
abstract: PARIS—  Gene Fenn, 90, a fashion photographer for Harper's Bazaar and other popular women's magazines, died Nov. 14 in Paris.

name: Billy Vessels
headline: Billy Vessels Is Dead at 70; Won the Heisman Trophy
abstract: Billy Vessels, Oklahoma running back who won 1952 Heisman Trophy, dies at age 70; photo (S)

name: Jerry Jerome
profession: Tenor Saxophonist of Big Band Era and Beyond
headline: Jerry Jerome, 89, Tenor Saxophonist of Big Band Era and Beyond
abstract: jerry jerome, tenor saxophone player of Big Band era, dies at age 89 (S)

name: Charlotte Coleman
headline: Charlotte Coleman, 33, Film Actress
abstract: Charlotte Coleman, British film actress, dies at age 33; photo (M)

name: John Babarovic
headline: John Babarovic, 69, Architect at Airports
abstract: John A Babarovic, architect who worked on major airport projects, dies at age 69 (M)

name: John W. Nason
headline: John W. Nason, 96, Educator; Helped Japanese-Americans
abstract: John W Nason, former president of Swarthmore College, dies at age 96 (M)

name: Robert H. Heilbrunn
headline: Robert H. Heilbrunn, 93, Philanthropist
abstract: Robert H Heilbrunn, investor and philanthropist, dies at age 93 (M)

name: Andrew McNally
profession: Ex-Chief Of Company Known for Maps
headline: Andrew McNally, 92, Ex-Chief Of Company Known for Maps
abstract: Andrew McNally III, former president of map maker Rand McNally & Company, dies at age 92 (M)

name: Byron Sanders
headline: Byron Sanders, 76, Actor in Soap Operas
abstract: Byron Sanders, actor in television soap operas, dies at age 76 (M)

name: V. Pasechnik
headline: V. Pasechnik, 64, Is Dead; Germ Expert Who Defected
abstract: Dr Vladimir Pasechnik, senior Soviet biologist who defected in 1989, dies at age 64 (M)

name: Mary Kay Ash
profession: Built a Cosmetics Empire and Adored Pink
headline: Mary Kay Ash, Who Built a Cosmetics Empire and Adored Pink, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mary Kay Ash, who built billion-dollar cosmetics empire, dies at age 83; photo (M)

name: Gardner McKay
headline: Gardner McKay, 69, TV Heartthrob Who Turned to Writing
abstract: Gardner McKay, popular television actor of 1960's, dies at age 69; photo (M)

name: Robert T. Lane
headline: Robert T. Lane: A Son's Cake and Candles
abstract: Robert T. Lane was a man whose size might have been intimidating were it not for his magnetic smile. Name a sport, and this towering firefighter played it, but his favorite hobby was cooking.

name: Denis Lavelle
headline: Denis Lavelle: A Mother's Devoted Son
abstract: Denis Lavelle idolized Rush Limbaugh and had cleared rooms at many a family gathering arguing his hard-line conservatism, but the last thing his relatives expected him to do was run for public office. But there was Mr. Lavelle over the summer, 42 and an absolute newcomer to retail politics, going door to door around Yonkers, where he was born and raised, collecting signatures for a run for the City Council on the Right to Life line.

name: Denease Conley
headline: Denease Conley: Tough, With a Studious Side
abstract: The seeds of Denease Conley's toughness could be seen early on. She once had a fight with an older sister who locked herself in the bathroom, and to get her out, Denny, as she was known, threw a cherry bomb at the bathroom door.

name: Farrell P. Lynch
headline: Farrell P. Lynch: Strivers, Like Their Parents
abstract: Whatever their achievements, the Lynch boys were products of their upbringing. The children of Irish immigrants, Sean P. Lynch, top, and his brother Farrell P. Lynch were strivers like their parents.

name: Kevin Pfeifer
headline: Kevin Pfeifer: Shouting With His Life
abstract: To the casual acquaintance, Kevin Pfeifer had a manner -- a quiet, thoughtful demeanor -- that seemed of a piece with all the philosophy courses he took at Marist College. His gift for abstractions, though, was far exceeded by his taste for the concrete. And adventure.

name: Edward R. Pykon
headline: Edward R. Pykon: Fast Eddy From Lehigh
abstract: Life was proceeding more or less on schedule for Edward R. Pykon and his wife, Jackie.

name: Peter Siracuse
headline: Peter Siracuse: Game Day, Every Day
abstract: Peter Siracuse lived for competition. As a child he jockeyed for attention with his three older brothers. As a young adult, he took his aggression out on the gridiron and in lacrosse. He also played football in college.

name: William H. Bernstein
headline: William H. Bernstein: The Late Bloomer
abstract: William H. was the oldest of four sons -- arriving three minutes before his fraternal twin, Robert. The two younger brothers, Steven and David, also twins, were born four years later.

name: Andrew M. King
headline: Andrew M. King: A Real Golfer
abstract: A lot of the Cantor Fitzgerald crowd played golf. And a lot of them were good at it. But Andrew M. King was REALLY, REALLY good. He had a four handicap and had shot three holes-in-one. "He had a beautiful swing," said his wife, Judy King.

name: Jan Maciejewski
headline: Jan Maciejewski: A Guy Just Like Him
abstract: Jan Maciejewski had a knack for being in the right place in the right time.

name: Salvatore F. Pepe
headline: Salvatore F. Pepe: For Family, a Tomatofest
abstract: Salvatore F. Pepe was an assistant vice president for technology at Marsh & McLennan, but to the Pepe clan he will be remembered as the originator of Tomatofest and the Pepe family calendar.

name: Salvatore Pepe
headline: Salvatore Pepe, 93, Real Estate Developer
abstract: Salvator Pepe, major developer of commercial real estate in Westchester County, dies at 93 (S)

name: Christopher S. Epps
headline: Christopher S. Epps: Accounting and Poetry
abstract: Geneva Epps has not given up hope that the son she had late in life is alive. "I'm just being hopeful and prayerful," she said of Christopher S. Epps, her seventh child and second son. "I just can't seem to give up. I know that I'm not considered very wise and not facing reality. But the reality is that no one has showed me any proof that he is not alive."

name: James R. Paul
headline: James R. Paul: Finding Their Place
abstract: In 1993, when James R. Paul decided to move to New York after two decades in Chicago, he was walking around Gramercy Park one day with a real estate broker when a building caught his eye. Built in 1883, it appealed to Mr. Paul's taste for the old and beautiful. "I wish we could find a place there," he told the broker, pointing to the red-brownish brick facade. They did.

name: Edna Cintron
headline: Edna Cintron: Her Courage and Strength
abstract: For Edna Cintron and her husband, William, every evening fit into a comforting routine. "She had everything prompt, clean, neat, organized," Mr. Cintron, a 44-year- old doorman, said of his 46-year-old wife, an administrative assistant for Marsh & McLennan. "She would come out of work, come home, cook, make sure that when I would come out of work there was food on the table and everything. And every night we would have ice cream and we would watch TV."

name: Frank Schott
headline: Frank Schott: In the Garden, at the Stove
abstract: Dina Schott could set her watch by her husband's daily routine. Every morning, Frank Schott was up at 5:20 a.m., on the train to his job in Manhattan at 6:09 a.m., and opening the front door again of their home in Massapequa Park, N.Y., at 7:00 p.m.

name: Strivers
headline: Sean P. and Farrell P. Lynch: Strivers, Like Their Parents
abstract: Whatever their achievements, the Lynch boys were products of their upbringing. The children of Irish immigrants, Sean P. Lynch, top, and his brother Farrell P. Lynch were strivers like their parents.

name: Garnet Bailey
headline: Garnet Bailey: Ace of 'Bailey-baisse'
abstract: When Garnet Bailey would come to scout a game in Worcester, Mass., he would announce himself by saying, "table for two, please" as a tribute to the legendary meals served when the IceCats were at home.

name: Gregory Richards
headline: Gregory Richards: The Call of the City
abstract: Gregory Richards just could not stay away from New York. He was born here, grew up in Greenwich Village and went to Stuyvesant High School.

name: Mark Francis Broderick
headline: Mark Francis Broderick: A Remarkable Smile
abstract: Mark Francis Broderick had a remarkable smile. It made everyone feel at ease with him, said Chris Dowd, his friend since they were fraternity brothers at St. John's University on Staten Island, N.Y.

name: Nereida De Jesus
headline: Nereida De Jesus: Life With Lauren
abstract: For Nereida De Jesus, life equaled Lauren. Lauren was her daughter, a bubbly 7-year-old whom Ms. De Jesus, 30, was raising alone in Woodlawn in the Bronx. Mother and daughter would do everything together -- get their hair done, go to movies, take bubble baths.

name: Carlton W. Bartels
headline: Carlton W. Bartels: Wraparound Buddha
abstract: Her father was aghast: there on the doorstep of her family's West Brighton home in Staten Island stood Carlton W. Bartels, suitor. "Carl had thick, wavy brown hair, down to his shoulders," recalled Jane Bartels, the object of his affection, decades later. "And a suede fringe jacket."

name: William H. Kelly Jr.
headline: William H. Kelly Jr.: Mr. Long Beach Island
abstract: If you lived on Long Beach Island in New Jersey, you knew William H. Kelly Jr. Although Mr. Kelly grew up in Bucks County, Pa., his family spent summers on the island, where he was able to indulge his passion for the water, learning to sail and surf. "My friends would joke around; they used to call him `Mr. L.B.I.,' " said his girlfriend of three years, Sue Magee, an employee of Bloomberg L.P., where Mr. Kelly also worked.

name: Anthony Jovic
headline: Anthony Jovic: A Special Plaque
abstract: Anthony Jovic videotaped his sons, Matthew, 10, and Peter, 9, at every swimming meet they entered. He went to their practices. And he took them along when he and his wife, Cynthia, went on a cruise in the Caribbean. And whenever he came home from work, the boys would rush up to him and say, "What did you do? Did you fight any fires?"

name: Irving Crane
headline: Irving Crane, a World Champion Who Brought Decorum to Billiards, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Irving Crane, whose gentlemanly, cautious approach to game of pool resulted in nickname the Deacon and seven world championships, dies at 88; photo (M)

name: Kevin S. Cohen
headline: Kevin S. Cohen: Friends Everywhere
abstract: When Kevin S. Cohen was 4, his family moved to a new house in Edison, N.J. Rather than being daunted by the move, little Kevin, the youngest of two boys, set out to make new friends. Soon, he was standing at his front door pointing to all the houses where he had made a friend.

name: Arthur Warren Scullin
headline: Arthur Warren Scullin: A Schmoozer Extraordinaire
abstract: Arthur Warren Scullin schmoozed with everyone, even telemarketers. "He never hung up on them," said Mr. Scullin's widow, Cathy. "He'd ask them where they were calling from. He would ask them what the weather was like, what time it was."

name: Jason Sekzer
headline: Jason Sekzer: Campers, United
abstract: Jason Sekzer started going to Camp Sussex as a boy, one of hundreds of city children who grabbed the chance to spend part of each summer in the country in New Jersey.

name: E. H. Colbert
headline: E. H. Colbert, 96, Dies; Wrote Dinosaur Books
abstract: Dr Edwin H Colbert, authority on paleontology who helped popularize study of dinosaurs through his work as curator at American Museum of Natural History in New York and as prolific writer of dinosaur books for lay audience, dies at 96; career reviewed; photo (M)

name: Thomas M. Brennan
headline: Thomas M. Brennan: Rock Tunes and Giggles
abstract: When Jennifer Brennan was pregnant with her first child, her husband, Thomas M. Brennan, would play Grateful Dead tapes loudly, hoping the music would reach the ears of his unborn daughter. When the baby kicked, as she invariably did, Mr. Brennan was delighted. She, too, he would say, was a fan.

name: Janice Ashley
headline: Janice Ashley: A Renaissance Woman
abstract: Janice Ashley was a modern-day Renaissance woman: literary, artistic and skilled in finance, as comfortable on Rollerblades as ordering a meal in a fancy restaurant. She was also outspoken and bubbly, someone who kept her friends from elementary school but relished new experiences, like a trip to Turkey in August.

name: Jean-Louis Palladin
headline: Jean-Louis Palladin, 55, a French Chef With Verve, Dies
abstract: Jean-Louis Palladin, influential chef who helped liberate French cuisine in America from rigorous orthodoxy, dies at age 55; photo (M)

name: Milton Shaw
headline: Milton Shaw, 80, Who Oversaw First Nuclear Submarine Project
abstract: Milton Shaw, who oversaw design and construction of nuclear aircraft carrier (M)

name: Sol Forman
headline: Sol Forman, 98, Owner of Famed Steakhouse
abstract: Sol Forman, owner of famed Peter Lugar steakhouse in Brooklyn, dies at age 98; photo (M)

name: Norman Granz
profession: Took Jazz Out of Smoky Clubs and Put It in Concert Halls
headline: Norman Granz, Who Took Jazz Out of Smoky Clubs and Put It in Concert Halls, Dies at 83
abstract: Norman Granz, impressario who founded Verve Records and Jazz at the Philharmonic, dies at age 83; photo (M)

name: Bo Belinsky
headline: Bo Belinsky, 64, the Playboy Pitcher, Dies
abstract: Bo Belinsky, pitcher for now-defunct Los Angeles Angels, dies at age 64; photo (M)

name: Paul Hume
headline: Paul Hume, 85, Washington Music Critic
abstract: paul hume, 85, washington music critic

name: W. Glenn Campbell
headline: W. Glenn Campbell, Shaper Of Hoover Center, Dies at 77
abstract: w. glenn

name: Ralph Burns
profession: Arranger and Composer From Big Bands to Broadway
headline: Ralph Burns, 79, an Arranger and Composer From Big Bands to Broadway
abstract: Ralph Burns, arrange and composer who rose to prominence in big band era, dies at age 79 (M)

name: Michael Hoffman
headline: Michael Hoffman, 59, Director Of Art Photography Publisher
abstract: Michael E. Hoffman, the longtime director of the Aperture Foundation, a nonprofit publisher of fine-art photography books and Aperture magazine, died on Friday in Manhattan. He was 59 and lived in New York City and Shekomeko, N.Y.    The cause was complications from meningitis, said his wife, Melissa Harris.

name: Joe Modise
headline: Joe Modise, 72, Fighter Against Apartheid
abstract: Joe Modise, a guerrilla fighter who led the armed struggle against apartheid and became South Africa's first black defense minister, died in his home near Pretoria on Monday night, government officials said Tuesday.     He was 72 and had cancer, said Snuki Zikalala, a family spokesman.

name: Francis Moore
headline: Dr. Francis Moore, 88, Dies; Innovative Leader in Surgery
abstract: Dr. Francis D. Moore, a giant of 20th-century surgery who made profound contributions to the understanding of how bodily fluids and chemicals change during surgery, the development of organ transplantation and the care of critically ill surgical patients, died on Saturday at his home in Westwood, Mass.    Dr. Moore, 88, was seriously ill with chronic heart failure and took his own life, his family said.

name: Jamie Shannon
headline: Jamie Shannon, 40, Chef Who Embraced Creole Cuisine
abstract: Jamie Shannon, chef, dies at age 40; photo (M)

name: John Dawson
headline: John Dawson, 71, Authority on Plasma Physics, Dies
abstract: Dr John M Dawson, leading authority on plasma physics, dies at age 71; photo (M)

name: John Dawson
headline: John Dawson, Country-Rock Songwriter, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Dawson was a singer and songwriter whose band New Riders of the Purple Sage began as a country-rock offshoot of the Grateful Dead but had a long life of its own.

name: Rachel Gurney
headline: Rachel Gurney, 81, Actress; 'Upstairs, Downstairs' Matriarch
abstract: Rachel Gurney, actress, dies at age 81; photo (M)

name: Irwin Weiner
headline: Irwin Weiner, 69, Entrepreneur Who Succeeded as Sports Agent
abstract: Irwin Weiner, sports agent, dies at age 69; photo (S)

name: George Harrison
headline: George Harrison, 'Quiet Beatle' And Lead Guitarist, Dies at 58
abstract: George Harrison, Beatles' lead guitarist who composed some of group's most venerated songs, dies of cancer at age 58, Los Angeles; his influence as anchor for quartet, leading others on spiritual quest toward Eastern philosophy that influenced their music in latter part of 1960's, discussed; photos (L)

name: Margaret Byrd Rawson
headline: Margaret Byrd Rawson, 102, Educator and Dyslexia Authority
abstract: Margaret Byrd Rawson, educator, researcher and author who spent some 70 years identifying and treatment reading disorders, dies at age 102; photo (S)

name: Budd Boetticher
headline: Budd Boetticher, Director Whose No-Frills 50's Westerns Became Classics, Dies at 85
abstract: Budd Boetticher, who directed series of stark, low-budget westerns in 1950's that are now regarded by film scholars as classics of genre, dies at age 85; photo (M)

name: John Knowles
headline: John Knowles, 75, Novelist Who Wrote 'A Separate Peace'
abstract: John Knowles, whose coming-of-age novel A Separate Peace became required reading for generation of high school students, dies at age 75; photo (M)

name: J. Herbert Fill
headline: J. Herbert Fill, 77, Ex-Commissioner Of Mental Health
abstract: Dr J Herbert Fill, psychiatrist who was New York City's commissioner of Mental Health and Mental Retardation Services for part of Lindsay administration, dies at age 77 (S)

name: Marion Manning
headline: Marion Manning: The World Beyond Queens
abstract: Those girls in Springfield Gardens were just tight like that. They grew up together and went to school in the neighborhood. They became young women and found husbands and homes near where the Q5 bus stops. They were starting to have little ones of their own, right there in Springfield Gardens.

name: Brenda E. Conway
headline: Brenda E. Conway: Half of a Lifelong Team
abstract: Brenda E. Conway was hard to miss. First, because of her unique style — an avid shopper, she preferred bright colors and patterns, and made funny socks her signature — and second, because you usually saw two of her. Mrs. Conway was rarely without her twin, Linda McGee. Though they were fraternal, the sisters still looked and sounded enough alike to draw attention.

name: Jérôme R. Lohez
headline: Jérôme R. Lohez: Vive l'Amérique!
abstract: Jérôme R. Lohez was French, Dening Wu was a Francophile, and their first date was a film at the Paris Theater on West 58th Street.

name: John B. Cahill
headline: John B. Cahill: Good Humor in 3 Languages
abstract: When John B. Cahill was an undergraduate at Boston College, he was a real good-time guy, and his friends nicknamed him Mad Dog. But he calmed down and matured into a gregarious family man with a quirky sense of humor.

name: Weibin Wang
headline: Weibin Wang: Living the American Dream
abstract: Weibin Wang and Wen Shi met as students in Beijing, and married three years later. A few months after the wedding in 1986, Mr. Wang left for the United States to study geophysics, at Yale and then at Columbia. Ms. Shi followed a year later.

name: Peter R. Kellerman
headline: Peter R. Kellerman: Dogs, Drums, Motorcycles
abstract: Robi and Peter R. Kellerman planned to have children, but first they had dogs.

name: William Anthony Karnes
headline: William Anthony Karnes: Discovering New York
abstract: William Anthony Karnes made his living as a software trainer for Marsh & McLennan. But his life's passion was touting the virtues of his adopted hometown, New York, regaling his sisters with stories about the wonders of living in the city where anything is possible, a place grander than anything he imagined growing up back in tiny Corryton, Tenn.

name: James C. Cappers
headline: James C. Cappers: Joys of the Outdoors
abstract: In her junior year at Quinnipiac College, Kathleen Vieira spotted a new man on campus. He was tall. He was handsome. He was wearing a pink rugby shirt.

name: Robert Helps
profession: Concert Pianist And a Wide-Ranging Composer
headline: Robert Helps, 73, Concert Pianist And a Wide-Ranging Composer
abstract: Robert Helps, American composer and concert pianist whose own works ranged through lexicon of contemporary styles and techniques, dies at age 73 (S)

name: Bradley James Fetchet
headline: Bradley James Fetchet: Turning the Focus to Others
abstract: To his family and friends, Bradley James Fetchet always seemed an odd fit for the dog-eat- dog world of Wall Street that became his life as an equity trader for Keefe, Bruyette & Woods. Quiet and reserved, Mr. Fetchet, 24, loathed being the center of attention, even on occasions when he deserved it. On his birthday, he preferred that the day go unnoticed, forbidding his mother from planning even the smallest celebration.

name: Paul Friedman
headline: Paul Friedman: A Problem-Solver
abstract: Shy Paul Friedman was a careful listener and an untangler of life's knots.

name: Michael A. Uliano
headline: Michael A. Uliano: Pleasures of Shore and Stage
abstract: Michael A. Uliano, a broker for Cantor Fitzgerald, never changed much from the grinning 10- year-old boy who was profiled in 1969 by his Canton, Mass., paper for snagging a 20-pound bass off Cape Cod. That he had just recovered from a broken wrist only added to his reputation for athleticism.

name: Eric Thorpe
headline: Eric Thorpe: Ball Carrier on Wall Street
abstract: The booming voice, competitiveness and self-assurance that helped Eric Thorpe become the star quarterback of his undefeated high school football team in Wilbraham, Mass., served him well on Wall Street. Mr. Thorpe, 35, known as Rick, was one of the top salesmen at Keefe, Bruyette & Woods.

name: Yaphet J. Aryee
headline: Yaphet J. Aryee: Taxes and Taxis
abstract: Yaphet J. Aryee was the person everyone went to for advice. "He was born in Ghana so he was the expert on that," said Ely Yulman, who worked with Mr. Aryee as an auditor with the State Division of Taxation and Finance, on the 86th floor of 2 World Trade Center. "He made his furniture when he got married, so people asked him how to fix the stairs in their house, or how to fix the engine in their car. But first of all, he was the smartest corporate tax auditor in the department. Millions and millions he brought in."

name: Ariel Louis Jacobs
headline: Ariel Louis Jacobs: Working the Room
abstract: Watch the salesman work the room. His banter is interrupted because his cellphone rings incessantly, but every comer's gaze is met. The people in this room feel important; they feel at ease. They like this guy. This skill has made him a success.

name: Michael Seaman
headline: Michael Seaman: Smile at the Finish Line
abstract: Michael Seaman was a determined dreamer who set and met goals with a smile.

name: Linda Mair Grayling
headline: Linda Mair Grayling: One Hot Summer
abstract: The Hotfoot Marathon, as everyone called it, began with a Bugs Bunny cartoon, during one of those endless summers at Linda Mair Grayling's grandmother's house on 139th Street in the Bronx. The idea was to emulate Bugs himself when he put a match between the toes of the snoozing Elmer Fudd: lighting it always produced a startling amount of jumping up and down.

name: Eric Lehrfeld
headline: Eric Lehrfeld: Comic Collector
abstract: Although Eric Lehrfeld grew up to be a computer consultant, he never lost his passion for comic books.

name: Debbie Paris
headline: Debbie Paris: General Factotum
abstract: Debbie Paris, an executive assistant, scheduled her bosses' flights, kept their calendars and managed payments, construction, staff and insurance on their three yachts and several homes — to list some of her duties. "When I needed an autographed photo of Sting," said Suzanne Murphy, a colleague, "I called Debbie. `No problem,' she said."

name: Rosemary Brown
headline: Rosemary Brown, a Friend of Dead Composers, Dies at 85
abstract: Rosemary Brown, medium who drew both support and ridicule from musical establishment for her claim of 'channeling' works from history's most illustrious composers, dies at age 85; photo (M)

name: Lorraine Lee
headline: Lorraine Lee: Too Happy at Work
abstract: In the end, it was all of those heart-stopping miseries with the elevators at 2 World Trade Center that prompted Joan Greene to tell her daughter, Lorraine Lee, "to leave that building, to get a job somewhere else," Mrs. Greene said.

name: Douglas Stone
headline: Douglas Stone: Perfect Business Partner
abstract: To know Douglas Stone was to know his distinctive brand of humor. "Cynical and dry" his son Zachary called it. "When he got going, everyone would be in tears." His business partner, Tad Parker, recalled the day that Mr. Stone, after dealing with some prickly personnel issue, sat down, looked up at the ceiling and stretched his arms out. "Can you feel the love?" he said, adding: "Human resources isn't my forte. Let's go have a toddy."

name: Laurence Michael Polatsch
headline: Laurence Michael Polatsch: No Date, but a Good Story
abstract: Laurence Michael Polatsch, an equities trader at Cantor Fitzgerald, hardly lacked for chutzpah, and may just have raised the meaning of the word to a new level. He was a free spirit who was able to talk his way into companies' holiday parties at Manhattan hotels year after year.

name: Carol Demitz
headline: Carol Demitz: Made Happy by Motherhood
abstract: Motherhood and the relationship she shared with her daughter Annie is what gave Carol Demitz's life balance.

name: Robert Treuhaft
headline: Robert Treuhaft, 89, Lawyer Who Inspired Funeral Exposé
abstract: Robert Treuhaft, crusading radical lawyer who inspired his wife Jessica Mitford to write her besteller The American Way of Death, expose of funeral profession, dies at age 89; photo (M)

name: Harry Ramos
headline: Harry Ramos: A Quest for Green Eyes
abstract: Migdalia Ramos remembers that she had just broken up with her boyfriend on her 18th birthday and was too despondent to dance. All evening, men asked her, and all evening she said no. Finally, the girlfriends trying to cheer her up told her, "If you don't dance with the next person who asks you, we're going to embarrass you."

name: John J. Ryan Jr.
headline: John J. Ryan Jr.: A Born Equity Trader
abstract: For John J. Ryan Jr., going to work on Wall Street was a natural: his father, John Sr., had been an equity trader. So, in due course, was his younger brother Patrick. "It was in the blood," said Patrick Ryan, who works for J. P. Morgan. `'We all have the personality where we get on with people, which you need. That and a sense of humor. And I guess we all like the energy you get on Wall Street."

name: Scott Bart
headline: Scott Bart: Start of a Marriage
abstract: Scott Bart and Elizabeth Cappell conducted their courtship in a 96th-floor office at 1 World Trade Center.

name: Robert T. Jordan
headline: Robert T. Jordan: Abstract and Focused
abstract: Robert T. Jordan had a laugh that friends said was a little louder and lasted a little longer than anyone else's. Behind that laugh was a 34-year- old man who by turns was kind and caring, imaginative and spontaneous, yet determined and focused.

name: Robert O. Jordan
profession: Ex-Chief Of New York Advertising Office
headline: Robert O. Jordan, 69, Ex-Chief Of New York Advertising Office
abstract: Robert O Jordan, who helped create advertising campaigns for clients as diverse as Procter & Gamble and The National Enquirer, dies at age 69 (M)

name: Robert Jordan
headline: Robert Jordan, 76, Bridge Player Who Was a Bridesmaid 3 Times
abstract: Robert Jordan, leading American bridge player, dies at age 76 (S)

name: Michael Iovenko
profession: Lawyer; Led Aid Society During Strike
headline: Michael Iovenko, 71, Lawyer; Led Aid Society During Strike
abstract: Michael Iovenko, Wall Street lawyer and former president of Legal Aid Society, dies at age 71; photo (M)

name: Viktor Astafyev
headline: Viktor Astafyev, Who Wrote of Rural Russia, Dies at 77
abstract: Viktor Astafyev, Russian novelist, dies at age 77 (M)

name: Arthur F. Kelly
headline: Arthur F. Kelly, 88, Ex-Airline Executive
abstract: Arthur F Kelly, former chief executive of Western Airlines, dies at age 88 (M)

name: Mary Whitehouse
profession: Foe Of Sexuality in British Culture
headline: Mary Whitehouse, 91, a Foe Of Sexuality in British Culture
abstract: Mary Whitehouse, who campaigned vociferously in England against permissive society, dies at age 91; photo (M)

name: John W. Collins
headline: John W. Collins, 89, Dies; Was Fischer's Chess Tutor
abstract: John William Collins, top

name: Joel Carlson
headline: Joel Carlson, 75, Lawyer Who Fought Apartheid in 50's
abstract: Joel Carlson, white South African lawyer who used spectacular political trials to battle apartheid and expose its practices of secret detention and torture (S)

name: Gino A. Circiello
headline: Gino A. Circiello, Restaurateur, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Gino A Circiello, Manhattan restaurateur, dies at age 89; photo (M)

name: Spencer Holst
headline: Spencer Holst, 75, Writer and Teller of Fables
abstract: Spence Holst, writer and teller of fables, dies at age 75; photo (M)

name: Gerhart Riegner
headline: Gerhart Riegner, 90, Dies; Disclosed Holocaust Plans
abstract: Gerhart Riegner, World Jewish Congress official who was first to warn that Nazi Germany planned to annihilate Europe's Jews, dies at age 90; photo (M)

name: William Jovanovich
headline: William Jovanovich, 81, Longtime Publishing Chief, Dies
abstract: William Jovanovich, 81, longtime publishin

name: George Scharffenberger
headline: George Scharffenberger, 82, Former Chief of City Investing
abstract: George T Scharffenberger, former chief of City Investing Company, dies at age 82; photo (M)

name: Mercedes Matter
headline: Mercedes Matter, 87, Artist And Studio School Founder
abstract: Mercedes Matter, artist and chief founder of New York Studio School in Greenwich Village, dies at age 87; photo (M)

name: Thelma Cuccinello
headline: Thelma Cuccinello: `Nuts at Christmas'
abstract: Christmas was Thelma Cuccinello's favorite holiday, a time when she could deck her house in Wilmot, N.H., with all the ornaments and decorations she had made over the years. And not just her house. Her eldest daughter, Cheryl O'Brien, who lives in Bedford, Mass., recently opened a box of Christmas wreaths, only to realize that every one had been made by her mother. "She made the skirt for our Christmas tree, the decoration for our mantlepiece," Mrs. O'Brien said. "She and Dad would go nuts at Christmas."

name: Seydou Keïta
headline: Seydou Keïta Dies; Photographed Common Man of Mali
abstract: Seydou Keita, photographer who concentrated on common man of Mali, dies; photo (M)

name: Keith Glascoe
headline: Keith Glascoe: Big Man, Big Heart
abstract: A firefighter known for his big heart, Keith Glascoe also had a small but successful acting career on the side.

name: Keithroy Maynard
headline: Keithroy Maynard: A Role Model by Choice
abstract: Keithroy Maynard was black. He was also a firefighter. Those two things meant everything to him, said his twin brother, Kevin.

name: David B. Brady
headline: David B. Brady: A Soccer Dad
abstract: At 41, David B. Brady had the trappings of success: an office on the 39th floor of the World Financial Center, where he was a first vice president at Merill Lynch, and a home in Summit, N.J.

name: Aaron Jacobs
headline: Aaron Jacobs: Well-Traveled at 27
abstract: An avid world traveler, Aaron Jacobs was making plans for the ultimate trip — his honeymoon with his bride-to-be, Jeannine.

name: Michael Clarke
headline: Michael Clarke: Born for a Firetruck
abstract: Jack Clarke may have been a New York City police officer, but from the very beginning his youngest son, Michael, had this affinity for firefighting.

name: Eric B. Evans
headline: Eric B. Evans: A Gardener With Standards
abstract: He was gorgeous. That much everybody agreed on.

name: Edward Keane
headline: Edward Keane: Too Restless to Retire
abstract: More than three years ago, Edward Keane retired. He had had a long and satisfying career as a mechanical engineer, and it made sense. He was 62.

name: Peter G. Wallace
headline: Peter G. Wallace: Opa's Second Chance
abstract: Peter G. Wallace believed that being a grandparent was a better deal than being a parent — all of the love and almost none of the work.

name: Gayle Greene
headline: Gayle Greene: Two Trips a Year
abstract: This year, for the first time, the Christmas lights outside Gayle Greene's town house in Montville, N.J., are red, white and blue.

name: Christopher R. Zarba
headline: Christopher R. Zarba: A Curious Mind
abstract: Christopher R. Zarba Jr. was just a baby when the Boston Pops performed a piece composed by his father, "Palm Sunday," in 1954. The younger Mr. Zarba inherited his family's musical genes, and grew up to be a talented pianist and French horn player who performed with local symphonies in his free time. He even married a fellow horn player, Sheila Kiernan.

name: Alan D. Kleinberg
headline: Alan D. Kleinberg: Planning a Park, and Legacy
abstract: On Sept. 10, Alan D. Kleinberg spent the evening at the East Brunswick Township Council, where he lobbied to move forward with a community skate park, a nod to his oldest son's affection for in-line skating. On the hot-button issue, known to provoke emotions, he was respected as a negotiator and mediator who helped gain acceptance for the idea.

name: Yudh V. Jain
headline: Yudh V. Jain: Finishing What He Started
abstract: Yudh V. Jain was his wife's dream. He encouraged her to buy clothes. He did the grocery shopping and showered her with flowers and greeting cards on not-so-special days. And every night, he remembered to make her a cup of tea.

name: Gregory R. Sikorsky
headline: Gregory R. Sikorsky: Taking Little Brother Along
abstract: There was the time that Gregory R. Sikorsky decided to take his youngest brother, Perry, up in a four-seater Cessna. But after they got up at 6 a.m., after they had driven an hour to the airport, the plane's battery turned out to be dead. So he drove his truck onto the highway and jump-started the plane. Then they took off.

name: Kathryn Anne Shatzoff
headline: Kathryn Anne Shatzoff: When Not Collecting, Giving
abstract: While Kathryn Anne Shatzoff had carried a torch for Barbie since childhood, it was her husband that got her starting collecting the dolls a couple of years ago.

name: George Hansen
headline: George Hansen, 92, Designer Of Popular Swing-Arm Lamp
abstract: George Hansen, designer of swing-arm lamp, dies at age 92; photo (M)

name: George Hansen
headline: George Hansen, Idaho Congressman and Convicted Swindler, Dies at 83
abstract: Found guilty three times of federal crimes, Mr. Hansen, an Idaho Republican, had a 1984 conviction overturned by the Supreme Court.

name: Christopher Quackenbush
headline: Christopher Quackenbush: `Christmas Carol' All Year
abstract: Most people think of "A Christmas Carol," the Charles Dickens classic, only during the holidays. But the tale of greed and redemption was on Christopher Quackenbush's mind his entire life.

name: Wanda Prince
headline: Wanda Prince: Coffee Healed All Wounds
abstract: Wanda Prince had a weakness for coffee. Whenever she was upset with her husband, Edward, about leaving his dirty clothes on the bathroom floor (again) or leaving his dirty dishes in the sink (again), Mr. Prince would woo her back with a strong cup of Joe. "She just loved coffee," said Mr. Prince.

name: James R. Coyle
headline: James R. Coyle: The Force Was With Him
abstract: James R. Coyle wanted to be Luke Skywalker. But because of certain difficulties in pursuing that career path, he decided to do what he thought was the next best thing, which was fighting fires.

name: Brian P. Monaghan Jr.
headline: Brian P. Monaghan Jr.: The Archetypal Good Kid
abstract: His friends nicknamed Brian P. Monaghan Jr., "slick" — but not the deceptive, smooth-talking, street-smart kind of slick. Around Inwood, where he lived, Mr. Monaghan was known as the archetypal good kid, a 21- year-old who helped elderly women across streets and went to the store for neighbors who could not.

name: Steven H. Russin
headline: Steven H. Russin: A Childlike Wonder
abstract: There was something about Steven H. Russin that made his wife, Andrea, think of Tom Hanks's character in the movie "Big."

name: Mark L. Rosenberg
headline: Mark L. Rosenberg: Saving Gas, and the World
abstract: Mark L. Rosenberg met his future wife, Jennifer, in 1995 on a seven-hour bus ride to Richmond, Va., for a Jewish youth program. He was trying to shine a flashlight on a book and turn the pages at the same time. She sat behind him, and finally offered to hold the flashlight. He gratefully accepted.

name: Sidney Kelley
headline: Sidney Kelley, 92, Part of Used-Car Empire
abstract: Sidney H Kelly, used car dealer, dies at age 92 (S)

name: Gerard Jean Baptiste
headline: Gerard Jean Baptiste: Treats for Dogs, and Himself
abstract: There is a decent chance that Gerard Jean Baptiste had dog biscuits in his pockets when he died. A New York firefighter, he routinely carried treats to give to the pets that walked past Ladder 9 in SoHo. That helped start conversations with the children — or the women — that the dogs towed with them.

name: Michel P. Colbert
headline: Michel P. Colbert: More Than a Good Résumé
abstract: Michel P. Colbert had the ideal résumé, the kind that might appear in a how-to book about résumés. A master's degree from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania. A succession of lucrative jobs in Paris, London and Milan. Fluency in French and Spanish. A balanced range of interests, from photography to scuba diving.

name: Mary Jo Kimelman
headline: Mary Jo Kimelman: 'Time Out New York,' Live
abstract: Whenever friends or friends of friends came to town, Mary Jo Kimelman eagerly became their tour guide. She knew so much about happenings in New York City that her mother once called her "Time Out New York," after the magazine.

name: Gary Bright
headline: Gary Bright: Not a Lot of Spare Time
abstract: Gary Bright was still working flat out, usually seven days a week, sometimes at two jobs. Late last summer, he put together a combination that suited him fine: working evenings as a waiter at Spazzio's restaurant on Columbus Avenue and, during the days, as a temporary insurance analyst at Aon Insurance in the World Trade Center.

name: Mary Jo Kimmelman
headline: Mary Jo Kimmelman: `Time Out New York,' Live

name: Thomas S. Strada
headline: Thomas S. Strada: `Sky Was the Limit'
abstract: What made Terry Strada fall fast in love with her husband, Thomas, when they met 20 years ago? "Oh my God, he was the most fun person I ever knew," Mrs. Strada said. "He would take me out, and the sky was the limit. Limos, dinners. I said I liked the Boston Celtics; he flew me to Boston to see them."

name: Bill Reid
profession: Heroic Bomber Pilot for British in World War II
headline: Bill Reid, 79, Heroic Bomber Pilot for British in World War II
abstract: Bill Reid, British Royal Air Force pilot in World War II, dies at age 79; photo (M)

name: Megan Boyd
headline: Megan Boyd, Who Made Tying Flies an Art, Dies at 86
abstract: Megan Boyd, whose fabled expertise at tying enchantingly delicate fishing flies put her work in museums and the hands of collectors around the world, died Nov. 15.

name: Sidney Silverstone
headline: Dr. Sidney Silverstone, Pioneer in Radiotherapy, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr Sidney Milton Silverstone, pioneer in radiotherapy and teacher whose association with Mount Sinai Hospital and School of Medicine spanned more than six decades, dies at age 93 (M)

name: George Young
headline: George Young, 71, Former Giants General Manager, Dies
abstract: George Young, former New York Giants general manager, dies at age 71; his career discussed; photo (M)

name: Laurie Johnston
headline: Laurie Johnston, 87, Former Times Reporter
abstract: Laurie Johnston, World War II correspondent, author and reporter for New York Times, dies at age 87; photo (M)

name: Faith Hubley
headline: Faith Hubley, Oscar Winner In Animation, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Faith Hubley, three-time Oscar winner for animation, dies at age 77; photo (M)

name: Pierre de Benouville
profession: Hero Of Resistance in World War II
headline: Pierre de Benouville, 87, Hero Of Resistance in World War II
abstract: Pierre de Benouville, hero of French resistance during World War II, dies at age 87 (M)

name: Helen Schneider
headline: Helen Schneider, 79, Hospitals Benefactor
abstract: Helen Schneider, philanthropist, dies at age 79 (S)

name: Dave Graue
profession: Cartoonist of Stone Age Tales of Alley Oop
headline: Dave Graue, 75, Cartoonist of Stone Age Tales of Alley Oop
abstract: Dave Graue, former cartoonist on Alley Oop comic strip, dies at age 75 in auto accident; drawing; photo (M)0

name: David Astor
profession: Liberal Voice As Editor of Britain's Observer
headline: David Astor, 89, Liberal Voice As Editor of Britain's Observer
abstract: david astor, 89, liberal voice as editor

name: Aubrey Lewis
headline: Aubrey Lewis, 66, Athlete Who Was an F.B.I. Pioneer
abstract: Aubrey Lewis, athlete who was part of first FBI training class to admit blacks, dies at age 66; photo (M)

name: Don Tennant
headline: Don Tennant, Creator of Characters for Ads, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Don Tennant, advertising agency executive who specialized in creating promotional characters like Tony the Tiger, dies at age 79; photo; drawing (M)

name: Pauline Campanelli
headline: Pauline Campanelli, 58, Artist Who Evoked Rustic Simplicity
abstract: Pauline Campanelli, painter whose super-realist still life prints sell in the hundreds of thousands, dies at age 58; photos (M)

name: Larry Costello
headline: Larry Costello, 70, Player and Coach in N.B.A., Is Dead
abstract: Larry Costello, former NBA player and coach, dies at age 70; photo (M)

name: Igor Zukelman
headline: Igor Zukelman: Ugly Car, Beautiful Dream
abstract: To Igor Zukelman, a Ukrainian immigrant, his Toyota Cressida was a steel chariot, a three-dimensional symbol of his cherished dream of becoming an American.

name: Edward J. Papa
headline: Edward J. Papa: The Center of Five Families
abstract: After graduation in 1976, Edward J. Papa and four friends went to Cape Cod for a vacation. The group never missed a summer -- 25 consecutive vacations together, complete with girlfriends, wives and kids. When Mr. Papa was lost on Sept. 11, five families were devastated.

name: W. G. Sebald
headline: W. G. Sebald, Elegiac German Novelist, Is Dead at 57
abstract: W G Sebald, profoundly elegiac and distinctive author of Austerlitz and other novels and one of most acclaimed of contemporary writers, dies at age 57; photo (M)

name: Abigail Medina
headline: Abigail Medina: Bible Stories and Dinner
abstract: Abigail Medina's life in Bushwick, Brooklyn, was blessedly far from the pace of Wall Street, where she worked on the 94th floor of 1 World Trade Center. At home she cooked, sang hymns and helped out at her church's Sunday school.

name: Christopher James Hanley
headline: Christopher James Hanley: He Liked What He Saw
abstract: Christopher James Hanley loved taking pictures around the world, but some of his favorites were of Manhattan -- a chandelier in Grand Central Terminal or a street sign in Greenwich Village, a fried chicken restaurant in Harlem.

name: Lynn Catherine
headline: Lynn Catherine Goodchild and Shawn M. Nassaney: Inseparable Travelers
abstract: It was supposed have been a quick getaway for Lynn Catherine Goodchild and Shawn M. Nassaney, a four-day trip to Maui before they hunkered down to study for their M.B.A.degrees. So, they woke up early on Sept. 11 and boarded United Airlines Flight 175.

name: John Pocher
headline: John Pocher: He Arranged the Trips
abstract: When John Pocher and his wife, Laura Grygotis, went to London a few years ago, they flew first class, stayed at the best hotels and ate at five-star restaurants. He planned it all.

name: Steve Pollicino
headline: Steve Pollicino: Living in the Moment
abstract: Steve Pollicino did not head for his easy chair after work. He would take his daughter to get an ice cream or shoot pool with his son during college holidays. Once he surprised his family with a vacation to the Bahamas.

name: John Skala
headline: John Skala: Always Time for His Friends
abstract: John Skala, a Port Authority police officer and part-time paramedic, could pull a 48-hour shift and still find the time to have some fun with his friends.

name: Gregory Saucedo
headline: Gregory Saucedo: Speaking His Mind
abstract: Firefighter Gregory Saucedo was not much of a diplomat. But "he was much the same way in telling you that he did like you and what he did like about you," said fellow firefighter and childhood friend Dave Simoes.

name: Erica Van Acker
profession: Subject of TV Documentary on Rape
headline: Erica Van Acker, 62, Subject of TV Documentary on Rape
abstract: Erica Van Acker, whose experience was basis of pioneering public television documentary on rape in 1971 and who became early public spokeswoman for those who had been raped, died on Sept 11 in terrorist attack on World Trade Center; she was 62; photo (M)

name: Christopher M. Duffy
headline: Christopher M. Duffy: Nice Suits, Hawaiian Shirts
abstract: Although Chris Duffy wore suits to his job as an assistant equity trader at Keefe, Bruyette & Woods, at home he was more often seen in flip-flops and a Hawaiian shirt.

name: Michael Lynch
headline: Michael Lynch: Lightening the Mood
abstract: In a family of 10 children, containing one Democrat, one Republican and some independents -- disagreements are bound to happen. And at family dinners, Michael Lynch, the seventh oldest, was the peacemaker.

name: James E. Hayden
headline: James E. Hayden: The Love Stayed Young
abstract: Looking back on their nearly 25 years of marriage, Elizabeth Gail Hayden credits James E. Hayden with bringing her much joy, to say nothing of chicken and fish.

name: Jim Cleere
headline: Jim Cleere: 'Good Man.' Good Voice.
abstract: One night in 1977, Jean Rieger, a divorced mother, got down on her knees and prayed to God to send her "a good man" to marry. When she got up, the phone rang. On the other end was Jim Cleere, a divorced father of two sons. They married one year later.

name: Bernard Mascarenhas
headline: Bernard Mascarenhas: An Anonymous Benefactor
abstract: Bernard Mascarenhas was a zealous bridge player, an executive who had risen steadily up the corporate ladder, and a man who liked to take it easy on weekends with his wife and two kids. But it was what he was not known for that is worth remembering as well.

name: David T. Wooley
headline: David T. Wooley: A Decorating Officer
abstract: Anyone could see that it was a strange combination of jobs, fighting fires and interior decorating. But not David T. Wooley. he was captain of Ladder Company 4 in Midtown Manhattan and also put up wallpaper on the side. One of his clients: Bill and Hillary Clinton.

name: John G. Coughlin
headline: John G. Coughlin: Civil Servant, Times Two
abstract: John G. Coughlin was a giving man. He worked with the emergency services unit of the New York Police Department, and in his spare time, he was a volunteer firefighter in Pomona, N.Y., where he lived with his family.

name: Oleh Wengerchuk
headline: Oleh Wengerchuk: Soul Mates From Age 2
abstract: Oleh Wengerchuk and his wife, Oksana, met as children, when their families were interred at a German displacement camp. Years later, they crossed paths again in America, and fell in love.

name: Sandra Campbell
headline: Sandra Campbell: Helpful Was Her Only Gear
abstract: Sandra Campbell was helpful to everyone around her. She gave her mother money for blood pressure medication, she donated her clothes, she even offered her car to anyone who needed it.

name: Catharina Robinson
headline: Catharina Robinson: She Was Aunt Patsy
abstract: Catharina Robinson's husband died six months after they married a decade ago, but the nine children of her brothers and sisters were almost like her own They don't want a Christmas tree this year, only a portrait of their aunt surrounded by gifts.

name: Brian McDonnell
headline: Brian McDonnell: 'A Cop's Cop'
abstract: Maggie McDonnell is trying to keep Christmas normal for her two children. Their Long Island lawn is decorated in lights and they will have a tree. The tree will be decorated in red, white and blue, and Daddy's police cap will stand atop it.

name: Brian Bilcher
headline: Brian Bilcher: Always to the Rescue
abstract: Firefighter Brian Bilcher was a lot like the patriotic comic book superhero, Captain America: calm, reasonable, good-looking and quick to the rescue of anyone who needed help.

name: Claude Richards
headline: Claude Richards: Bombs Were His Business
abstract: If ever a man was to the bomb squad born, it was Detective Claude Richards of the New York Police Department. Fearless, meticulous and disciplined, Detective Richards even spent his vacation time defusing land mines in Bosnia with a United Nations peacekeeping force.

name: Frederick Hoffmann
headline: Frederick J. Hoffmann and Michele L. Hoffmann: All Too Much in the Family
abstract: Last week, 5-year-old Derek Leohner said he wished he had a magic pebble. That way he could make a wish, and "Pop Pop and Aunt Shelly" would come home again.

name: Joanne Cregan
headline: Joanne Cregan: Everyone's Best Friend
abstract: There was something about Joanne Cregan that made most people think she was their best friend. When her friends needed advice, she gave it freely. Her laugh and her sense of humor made bleak situations brighter.

name: Bryan C. Bennett
headline: Bryan C. Bennett: He Filled the Time Available
abstract: Bryan C. Bennett, 25, lived an adventurous life.The highlights included working on a farm in Spain, teaching English to schoolchildren in Chile, visiting a remote village in Cuba, white-water rafting in Costa Rica, and backpacking in the Andes.

name: A. Keith Smiley
headline: A. Keith Smiley, 91, Executive Of Resort and Preservationist
abstract: a keith smiley, 91, executive of r8

name: Dominick Pezzulo
headline: Dominick Pezzulo: The Unusual Was Typical
abstract: Dominick Pezzulo fixed airplanes for T.W.A., taught shop at Herbert Lehman High School, restored a Porsche 944, pumped iron regularly, went on dinner cruises and just slipped under the 35-year-old age limit for the Port Authority police force.

name: Tyrone May
headline: Tyrone May: The Music, and Party, Man
abstract: Tyrone May, an auditor with the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance, was more likely to be crunching numbers than spinning records. And yet, his music collection was vast: hundreds and hundreds of records and CD's.

name: John P. Burnside
headline: John P. Burnside: Struck by Love's Lightning
abstract: John P. Burnside and his wife Sandra recently started having thoughts of a more settled life. "But just when you think you're going to get serious, buy a home and have kids, it gets taken away," Mrs. Burnside said.

name: Paul Curioli
headline: Paul Curioli: The Birdhouse Expert
abstract: The son and grandson of skilled craftsmen, Paul Curioli discovered his carpentry gene only after he married. But he quickly made up for lost time. His specialty? Birdhouses.

name: Brian Novotny
headline: Brian Novotny: Romantic Touches
abstract: A week before Sept. 11, Theresa Thomas and Brian Novotny were engaged. For a few days, the future seemed to unfold joyously before them.

name: Michael Cammarata
headline: Michael Cammarata: 'Don't Mourn Me'
abstract: On Sept. 12, Michael Cammarata's brother, Joseph, found a letter that no brother ever wants to read. It was a to-do list in case something happened to him.

name: Paul Martini
headline: Paul Martini: Maxims, but No Wristwatch
abstract: One of Paul Martini's cherished mottoes was, "Don't sweat the small things." He was so laid back that he never even wore a watch.

name: Patrick Waters
headline: Patrick Waters: Coffee and Nerves of Steel
abstract: Patrick Waters was what colleagues call "a good fireman," graceful under pressure and passionate about the job. Plus, when he was in the firehouse kitchen, he made sure there was always a pot of coffee brewing.

name: Dana Hannon
headline: Dana Hannon: Deer Hunter With a Heart
abstract: Dana Hannon lived to hunt. While his family knew he would always be there for them, they never asked for favors on the first day of hunting seasons for deer, ducks and geese.

name: Jeffrey Schreier
headline: Jeffrey Schreier: Adversities Conquered
abstract: Jeffrey Schreier conquered the severe learning disabilities he was born with to build a quiet, happy life with his wife.

name: Alexis Leduc
headline: Alexis Leduc: A Born Father
abstract: Some people are made to be fathers. Alexis Leduc, a maintenance supervisor for Franklin Templeton on the 97th floor of 2 World Trade Center, was like that. He and his wife, Isa, had four children.

name: Phyllis Talbot
headline: Phyllis Talbot: Cajun and Chaos
abstract: Phyllis Talbot liked to be challenged, especially at work where she was the vice president at Marsh USA. "When all hell was breaking loose, that's when she was in her element," said her son, Keith.

name: Mike A. Pelletier
headline: Mike A. Pelletier: Private Language
abstract: Mike A. Pelletier had a made-up language he shared with his daughter. "They developed all these inside jokes," said his wife, Sophie.

name: Joshua Aron
headline: Joshua Aron: Reveled in Life's Details
abstract: At age 7, Joshua Aron would sit at the kitchen table bent over a copy of The Wall Street Journal, analyzing the stock tables with his chocolate milk. Two decades later, Mr. Aron became an equities trader at Cantor Fitzgerald.

name: John Katsimatides
headline: John Katsimatides: Everything in Technicolor
abstract: Cool New Yorkers may drape themselves in black, but John Katsimatides loved color. His Jet Ski and his Jeep were bright yellow. His Harley was baby blue. And at a macho Super Bowl party, the underwear he flashed was hot pink.

name: Naomi Schor
headline: Naomi Schor, Literary Critic and Theorist, Is Dead at 58
abstract: Naomi Schor, literary critic and theorist who taught at Yale, dies at 58; photo (M)

name: Thomas Warren Hohlweck Jr.
headline: Thomas Warren Hohlweck Jr.: A Fast Engine, an Easy Pace
abstract: Boys will have their toys, and Thomas Warren Hohlweck Jr. had his. Starting with a used Fiat in high school, Mr. Hohlweck loved to tool around in racy vehicles, although he could not be described as a racy driver.

name: Nathaniel Webb
headline: Nathaniel Webb: The Path of Righteousness
abstract: Nathaniel Webb remained on the side of authority most of his life. He was always trying to keep everyone on the straight and narrow.

name: Thomas F. Swift
headline: Thomas F. Swift: Master of Factoids
abstract: No one wanted to play Trivial Pursuit or any game that relied on factoids and cultural flotsam with Thomas F. Swift. That was because Mr. Swift was known as "the book of useless information."

name: Nicholas Brandemarti
headline: Nicholas Brandemarti: A Believer in Teamwork
abstract: David Clawson, football coach at Fordham University, said Nicholas Brandemarti was "the ultimate teammate, and the ultimate friend."

name: Clarin Siegel Schwartz
headline: Clarin Siegel Schwartz: The Family Fixer
abstract: Clarin Siegel Schwartz had so much personal magnetism that more than 700 people showed up to her memorial service.

name: Meredith Lynn Whalen
headline: Meredith Lynn Whalen: Cruising Between Dreams
abstract: First Meredith Lynn Whalen wanted to be a successful portfolio manager, and then the owner of a horse farm in Kentucky. Between those goals, she planned to cram in a lot of travel, including many cruises.

name: James P. O'Brien Jr.
headline: James P. O'Brien Jr.: He Was 'Totally Normal'
abstract: Lisanne MacKenzie said James P. O'Brien Jr. was totally normal. He would come home from work, hang out in the house, do nothing, walk the dog, watch TV and hang out with the kids.

name: JoAnn Tabeek
headline: JoAnn Tabeek: Tough Cookie, Soft Heart
abstract: Many of JoAnn Tabeek's colleagues at Cantor Fitzgerald thought she was all-business. "But once you got to know her she would give you her heart," said Jennifer Megna, a friend and former co-worker.

name: Christopher Slattery
headline: Christopher Slattery: The Man Behind the Fun
abstract: To an ever-expanding circle of friends and relatives, Christopher Slattery, a trader at Cantor Fitzgerald, was a leader and a catalyst.

name: Nobuhiro Hayatsu
headline: Nobuhiro Hayatsu: Each City an Adventure
abstract: In the reserved world of Japanese banking, Nobuhiro Hayatsu stood out: he was outgoing, sunny and loquacious. He embraced foreign assignments, for each tour of duty was a chance to party in a new town.

name: Donna Marie Giordano
headline: Donna Marie Giordano: Family Friends
abstract: Donna Marie Giordano was very close to her son, Michael. "We did everything together. We were more like brother and sister," he said.

name: Thomas P. DeAngelis
headline: Thomas P. DeAngelis: In the Thick of Things
abstract: Thomas P. DeAngelis, a battalion chief in the New York City Fire Department, would never send a firefighter into a building he had not personally entered and checked out.

name: Gordy Aamoth
headline: Gordy Aamoth: Looking Good
abstract: Gordy Aamoth loved parties and looking good. "Every situation was more fun when Gordy was there," said his mother, Mary. "He was always beautifully put together."

name: Ysidro Hidalgo-Tejada
headline: Ysidro Hidalgo-Tejada: Seasoning With Love
abstract: Ysidro Hidalgo-Tejada had a gentle touch, one that he applied to making dinner for his huge extended family, planting flowers or taking care of his 90-year-old diabetic mother.

name: Rudolph Riccio
headline: Rudolph Riccio: Knowing What Matters
abstract: When Rudolph Riccio was a teenager, he worked a paper route for a few weeks to buy some boots he wanted. But after he saved enough money, he didn't buy them. Instead, he gave the money to his sister to use for food.

name: Frances E. Holberton
headline: Frances E. Holberton, 84, Early Computer Programmer
abstract: Frances Elizabeth Holberton, one of first computer programmers, dies at age 84; photo (M)

name: Arthur Edwin Bye
headline: Arthur Edwin Bye, Natural Garden Designer, Dies at 82
abstract: Arthur Edwin Bye, landscape architect, dies at age 82; photos (M)

name: Seymour V. Reit
profession: Creator of Casper the Friendly Ghost
headline: Seymour V. Reit, 83, a Creator of Casper the Friendly Ghost
abstract: Seymour V Reit, author and illustrator who created cartoon character Capser the Friendly Ghost, died Nov 21 at age 83; photos (M)

name: Stefan Heym
headline: Stefan Heym, Marxist-Leninist Novelist, Dies at 88 on Lecture Tour in Israel
abstract: Stefan Heym, widely published Marxist-Leninist novelist, dies at age 88 while on lecture tour in Israel; photo (M)

name: Erik Johns
headline: Erik Johns, 74, Librettist of Copland's 'Tender Land'
abstract: Erik Johns, who wrote libretto for Aaron Copland's opera The Tender Land, dies at age 74 (M)

profession: Noted Theorist Of Information and Computers
headline: Peter Elias, 78, Noted Theorist Of Information and Computers
abstract: Peter Elias, 78, Noted Theorist of Information an

abstract: Anthony Gigliotti, 79, Philadelphia Clairnet
