profession: President Of a New York U.A.W. Local
headline: Samuel Meyers, 83, President Of a New York U.A.W. Local
abstract: Samuel Meyers, labor activist and longtime president of union local representing automobile workers in New York area, dies at 83 (S)

name: Harrison Mosher Hayford
headline: Harrison Mosher Hayford, 85, Professor and Melville Expert
abstract: Harrison Mosher Mayford, leading expert on Herman Melville, dies at 85 (S)

name: José Fajardo
headline: José Fajardo, 82, Flutist And Bandleader, Is Dead
abstract: Jose Fajardo, Cuban flutist who was one of most influential bandleaders in Latin music, dies at 82; photo (M)

name: Leonard T. Kurland
headline: Leonard T. Kurland, 79, Neurologist-Researcher
abstract: Dr Leonard T Kurland, neurologist, dies at 79; photo (M)

name: Conte Candoli
headline: Conte Candoli, 74, Trumpeter for 'Tonight'
abstract: Conte Candoli, renowned mainstay trumpeter on Tonight television show with Johnny Carson, dies at age 74 (M)

name: Léopold Senghor
headline: Léopold Senghor Dies at 95; Senegal's Poet of Négritude
abstract: Leopold Sedar Senghor, poet, professor, philosopher and statesman who became Senegal's first president, dies at age 95; photo (M)

name: Pamela Chu
headline: Pamela Chu: Taking It in Stride
abstract: Pamela Chu was under constant pressure, but the 31-year-old vice president and United States equities trader at Cantor Fitzgerald never let it show.

name: H. Peter Kriendler
headline: H. Peter Kriendler, 96, Operator of '21' Club
abstract: H Peter Kriendler, operator of New York's 21 Club restaurant, dies at age 96; photo (M)

name: Dick Schaap
headline: Dick Schaap Dies at 67; Ubiquitous Sports Journalist
abstract: Dick Schaap, sports journalist and host of television sports talk show, dies at age 67; photos (M)

name: Andrew I. Rosenblum
headline: Andrew I. Rosenblum: Love Was All Around
abstract: Frustrated with realities of the legal world, Andrew Rosenblum entered the world of finance, eventually becoming a vice president at Cantor Fitzgerald.

name: Margaret Mattic
headline: Margaret Mattic: Dimples Right and Left
abstract: The acting bug bit Margaret Mattic early, a surprise since she seemed so quiet. But it was her soft soothing voice, as well as her two dimples, that brought her success and endeared her to many.

name: Kevin P. York
headline: Kevin P. York: Man With Snowblower
abstract: Kevin York's greatest enjoyment came from buying the best things and using them to take care of others, especially his wife and two sons.

name: Joseph McGovern
profession: Lawyer And Head of New York Regents
headline: Joseph McGovern, 92, Lawyer And Head of New York Regents
abstract: Josephn

name: Michael Edward Roberts
headline: Michael Edward Roberts: Firehouse Psychologist
abstract: Although Michael Edward Roberts took time to get a degree in psychology from the SUNY-Buffalo, there was never any doubt that he would end up in the firehouse.

name: Bruce Eagleson
headline: Bruce Eagleson: Attention to Detail
abstract: Bruce Eagleson was a perfectionist that also had a sense of humor. He had hoped to retire to golf and fishing in New Hampshire within the next seven years.

name: Simon V. Weiser
headline: Simon V. Weiser: Medieval History Buff
abstract: While it took 42 years for Simon Weiser to get to the United States, he spent the last 23 years making up for lost time, finding work as an engineer, collecting books and patenting an invention or two.

name: David Arce
headline: David Arce: Stray Cats, Dogs, Kids
abstract: When Margaret Arce opened up her son's apartment in Stuyvesant Town, she found remnants of his generosity, letters to Santa Claus from poor children. David Arce, a firefighter, would answer them by delivering wished-for toys, year after year.

name: Robert D. Mattson
headline: Robert D. Mattson: A Hero in 1993
abstract: Danger always seemed to have a way of finding Robert Mattson, from Vietnam to the first World Trade Center attack.

name: David L. W. Fodor
headline: David L. W. Fodor: Rescuer of Animals
abstract: David Fodor was a mountain man away from the office, an accountant that who loved cooking, laughing and enjoying life fully.

name: Sandra Conaty Brace
headline: Sandra Conaty Brace: 25 Cats, 55 Words
abstract: Sandra Conaty Brace might have appreciated a short biographical sketch about her. After all, she herself had mastered the 55-word short story as well as the 25 cats.

name: Arkady Zaltsman
headline: Arkady Zaltsman: A Man of Many Views
abstract: Architect Arkady Zaltsman loved New York City, hoping that one day his work would go a long way in beautifying Brooklyn, especially the Russian quarter in Brighton Beach. .

name: Christopher Larrabee
headline: Christopher Larrabee: Putting Life in Focus
abstract: Christopher Larrabee decided to trade his breezy California lifestyle for a career in finance in New York, just like his father and older sister, Nicole.

name: Alan D. Feinberg
headline: Alan D. Feinberg: Mr. Mom's Fire Truck
abstract: Alan Feinberg was a firefighter who often stayed home to take care of the kids but who never quite got over his childhood love of cars.

name: Mark H. Rosen
headline: Mark H. Rosen: Thrilled by Twirls
abstract: As a partner at Sandler O'Neill, Mark Rosen knew investment banking. As a father, he knew baton twirling.

name: Michael A. Tamuccio
headline: Michael A. Tamuccio: A Bud in Any Season
abstract: Michael A. Tamuccio was a true guy's guy, which is why his friends knew that Kathleen Horner was "the one" when the couple showed up at a Halloween party in Raggedy Ann and Andy costumes.

name: Anthony Fallone
headline: Anthony Fallone: A Joke Everywhere
abstract: Anthony Fallone had a no-nonsense style at business. But when he was not busy at work, he could be found sitting at his computer screen, roaring with laughter at an email that he either had just sent or just received.

name: James G. Geyer
headline: James G. Geyer: The Team Is the Goal
abstract: James G. Geyer worked as a bond broker and for a catering company on weekends. But his true calling was as a friend, a father and a coach in Rockville Centre, on L.I.

name: Frank Koestner
headline: Frank Koestner: Every Other Weekend
abstract: Frank Koestner never quite found the time for jogging, skiing or whitewater rafting. But on alternate weekends, the busy stockbroker carved out time for his daughter, Carolyn.

name: Nina Bell
headline: Nina Bell: Air Force Child
abstract: Nina Bell was every inch a fighter pilot's daughter - slender, athletic and confident. However, despite her degree, she was not always all business.

name: Alysia Basmajian
headline: Alysia Basmajian: In 2 Years, a Full Life
abstract: Alysia Basmajian and her husband would marvel at how they had lived their lives in fast forward. They had gotten married, graduated, raised a child, found a job and moved to a new city all within the last 18 months, together.

name: Paul Zois
headline: Paul Zois: Games as Sacred Rites
abstract: For Paul Zois, his children's ball games were sacred rites — events that took precedence over practically everything.

name: Matthew O'Mahony
headline: Matthew O'Mahony: No Waster of Sleep
abstract: Matthew O'Mahony refused to let sleep usurp time that could be put to better use. He also had a flair for drama, which he used to heighten the spectacle of gift giving.

name: Chris Orgielewicz
headline: Chris Orgielewicz: Straight Arrow
abstract: What strikes Chris Orgielewicz's college roommate was how little his kind, hardworking friend had changed since their college days.

name: Durrell V. Pearsall Jr.
headline: Durrell V. Pearsall Jr.: Imposing Yet Inviting
abstract: While his facade was fierce, friends say that Durrell V. Pearsall Jr. hasd a smile that could warm a room right up.

name: Vanessa Kolpak
headline: Vanessa Kolpak: Letters for a Mother
abstract: Friends remembered Vanessa Kolpak as a humble and beautiful soul who could make people melt with her smile.

name: William E. Krukowski
headline: William E. Krukowski: Pedal to the Metal
abstract: William E. Krukowski was firefighter who not only had a soft spot for junk, but a weakness for drag racing.

name: James Andrew O'Grady
headline: James Andrew O'Grady: A Place for Everything...
abstract: James Andrew O'Grady’s love of order and ritual might have seemed out of place in the tumultuous world of the bond market.

name: A. Todd Rancke
headline: A. Todd Rancke: A Community Fixture
abstract: A. Todd Rancke had a teasing sense of humor that played on people's flaws but did not generate any ill will. But for all his jocularity, he was a caring man whose primary concern was his family's happiness.

name: Deborah Kobus
headline: Deborah Kobus: Open to Adventure
abstract: Deborah Kobus was the type of person who knew how to cheer herself up, lately by sailing to Tahiti or going skiing in Argentina.

name: Christopher Sullivan
headline: Christopher Sullivan: True Partner at Home
abstract: Christopher Sullivan was a prince to his wife, a man with a heart of gold who was never too tired to play with their sons or to prepare her lunch for work.

name: Eugene Whelan
headline: Eugene Whelan: Guilty of Serial Hugging
abstract: Although firefighter Eugene Whelan sometimes jettisoned saint eligibility at a pub or concert, he was known mostly as generous hugger who understood what life was really about.

name: Jeffrey Giordano
headline: Jeffrey Giordano: He Shared His Bounty
abstract: Jeffrey Giordano spent 14 years at Ladder Company 3 in the East Village after his stepfather-in-law, clinging to life in the burn center at New York Hospital, made him promise to become a firefighter.

name: Palmina Delli Gatti
headline: Palmina Delli Gatti: Keeper of Helpful Secrets
abstract: Palmina Delli Gatti liked to get the finer things in life, like jewelry from Fifth Avenue or good seats at Yankees games.

name: Elkin Yuen
headline: Elkin Yuen: Creative Vacationer
abstract: Every year, Elkin Yuen and his wife would take a number of vacations to get away from the city. It was important, he always told her, to have fun and live in the moment.

name: Vincent Slavin
headline: Vincent Slavin: Outgoing and Outdoor Type
abstract: Vincent Slavin was a real New Yorker, a high-energy guy who walked to his own beat and never slowed down.

name: Brent J. Woodall
headline: Brent J. Woodall: A Present That Will Live On
abstract: Brent J. Woodall always loved kids and looked forward to having his own. But when his wife tried to announce the good news subtly a few weeks ago, Mr. Woodall missed the point entirely.

name: Edward Saiya
headline: Edward Saiya: Minor Fame, Major Fun
abstract: Edward Saiya was part of a band of tough Brooklyn brothers who were not afraid to express their love for one another.

name: Adam Rand
headline: Adam Rand: Doing What Came Naturally
abstract: Fighting fires was a calling for Adam Rand, who reveled in the camaraderie and in learning new techniques that he could teach to younger firefighters.

name: Sandra Fajardo Smith
headline: Sandra Fajardo Smith: Happy in New York
abstract: Sandra Fajardo Smith loved her job, loved working out at the gym and loved all of the city's cultural offerings. But what she especially loved was her cousin.

name: Christopher S. Gardner
headline: Christopher S. Gardner: The Captain of the Ship
abstract: Christopher Gardner was a combination of boss and friend to his employees. However, he never brought his work home and tried to share with his children his passion for the sea.

name: Robert L. Horohoe Jr.
headline: Robert L. Horohoe Jr.: In Love With His Work
abstract: For Robert L. Horohoe Jr., being corporate bond broker at Cantor Fitzgerald was a family tradition.

name: Kenneth Swenson
headline: Kenneth Swenson: Man of Inner Peace
abstract: While there was not much spare time in Mr. Swenson's life, he found time Saturday nights to volunteer as a medical technician with his town’s emergency squad, just like his father had before him.

name: Mary Stanley
headline: Mary Stanley: Modest Helpmate
abstract: Mary Stanley was not the kind to go on and on about herself. In fact, her closest friend didn’t know until after her death that Mrs. Stanley was a vice president at Marsh & McLennan.

name: Dorota Kopiczko
headline: Dorota Kopiczko: Sunny Personality
abstract: Dorota Kopiczko embraced America with a bubbly smile as soon as she arrived from Poland, teaching herself English and working her way through college to a promising accounting career.

name: Jayesh Shah
headline: Jayesh Shah: Provider of Memories
abstract: Jayesh Shah and his brother were always close, whether the family lived in India or Wisconsin or Tulsa or Houston.

name: Edward W. Schunk
headline: Edward W. Schunk: His Turn to Wait
abstract: No matter how his day as a broker went, Edward Schunk stepped off the afternoon train as if his day was just beginning.

name: Henry Miller Jr.
headline: Henry Miller Jr.: Gentle Procrastinator
abstract: Henry Miller Jr. was a steady, gentle man who covered his wife Diane and her children with a mantle of security.

name: Barry Simowitz
headline: Barry Simowitz: Of Cats and Cashmere
abstract: Not every cat is presented with its own futon. But then, not every cat owner is as devoted as Barry Simowitz was to his brown-and-white beauty with whom he shared the last five years

name: Dan DeCarlo
profession: Archie Artist and Creator Of Josie and the Pussycats
headline: Dan DeCarlo, Archie Artist and Creator Of Josie and the Pussycats, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Dan DeCarlo, top cartoonist for Archie Comics and creator of characters Josie and the Pussycats and Sabrina, dies at age of 82; photo (M)

name: Paul R. Hughes
headline: Paul R. Hughes: The Ultimate Technophile
abstract: Paul R. Hughes was a Yankee-loving computer guy who had the ability to give simple directions on tackling a technology problem.

name: Joseph Sisolak
headline: Joseph Sisolak: Helping Others to Think
abstract: Colleagues were grateful that Joseph Sisolak was a manager who attempted to walk his employees through the resolution of job-related dilemmas because it made them better workers.

name: James Straine
headline: James Straine: Pleasure From Fishing
abstract: James Straine was a dedicated bond trader that looked forward to pass on to his children his love of fishing.

name: Jon Schlissel
headline: Jon Schlissel: A Believer in Fitness
abstract: Co-workers at the New York State Department of Taxation and Finance knew him as a dedicated employee. But there were a lot of sides to Jon Schlissel.

name: Dennis Germain
headline: Dennis Germain: Daffy Downhill Skiing
abstract: Dennis Germain spent his working hours in the canyons of Midtown Manhattan as a firefighter. However, he spent his free time on the slopes as a ski instructor, training high school racing teams at Sterling Forest, near Tuxedo, N.Y.

name: Martha Mödl
headline: Martha Mödl, 89, a Soprano Who Gave Her Life to Her Art
abstract: Martha Modl, one of Germany's leading Wagnerian singers, dies at age of 89; photo (M)

name: Carlton F. Valvo II
headline: Carlton F. Valvo II: Traveler First Class
abstract: Carlton F. Valvo II lived an adventure-packed life, visiting dozens of countries in his 38 years as an international bond trader at Cantor Fitzgerald.

name: John Guedel
headline: John Guedel, 88, Producer Who Shaped Early Television
abstract: John Guedel, radio producer and television pioneer, dies at age 88; photo (M)

name: Foster Brooks
profession: Comedian Known for His Tipsy Persona
headline: Foster Brooks, 89, Comedian Known for His Tipsy Persona
abstract: Foster Brooks, comedian, dies at age 89; photo (M)

name: C. Carwood Lipton
headline: C. Carwood Lipton, 81, Figure in 'Band of Brothers,' Dies
abstract: C Carwood Lipton, who was among central figures portrayed in book and television miniseries Band of Brothers, dies at age 81; photo (M)

name: Robert Cronbach
headline: Robert Cronbach, 93, Sculptor and Teacher
abstract: Robert Cronbach, sculptor, dies at age 93 (M)

name: Ardito Desio
headline: Ardito Desio, Leader of K2 Ascent, Dies at 104
abstract: Ardito Desio, inveterate explorer who in 1954 organized first ascent of K2 in Himalayas, world's second highest mountain, dies at age 104; photos (M)

name: Franco Dino Rasetti
headline: Franco Dino Rasetti, 100, a Nuclear Pioneer
abstract: Dr Franco Dino Rasetti, who worked with Enrico Fermi on team that discovered one of key processes in nuclear reactions, dies at age 100; photo (M)

name: Edwin F. Russell
headline: Edwin F. Russell, 87, Newspaper Publisher
abstract: Edwin F Russell, former newspaper publisher who joined Royal Navy to fight Germany before United States entered World War II, dies at age 87; photo (M)

name: Agha Shahid Ali
headline: Agha Shahid Ali, 52, a Poet Who Had Roots in Kashmir
abstract: Agha Shahid Ali, Kashmiri-American poet, dies at 52 (S)

name: Daniel Pearl
headline: Daniel Pearl, 38, a Tenacious Newspaperman
abstract: As the South Asia bureau chief of The Wall Street Journal, Daniel Pearl moved to Bombay after spending time in London and Paris. But for much of his career he was based on the East Coast, where he wrote articles on land use and transportation, and built a reputation on the witty strength of his feature stories.    Colleagues and friends said that the work the 38-year-old Mr. Pearl left behind shows where his talents lay: in doggedly pursuing and explaining obscure topics, or superficially simple ones, with sensitivity and nuance. He saw that as his mission, friends said, and he died pursuing it.

abstract: Buddy Kaye, a songwriter and lyricist who wrote hits for Perry Como, Frank Sinatra, Dusty Springfield and others, died on Thursday in Rancho Mirage, Calif., where he lived. He was 84.    Among Mr. Kaye's songs were ''Till the End of Time,'' written with Ted Mossman, which was based on a Polonaise by Chopin and was included in the 1945 film ''A Song to Remember,'' about Chopin. When Como recorded the song, it became his first big hit, selling two million copies. It also became a hit for Les Brown, with Doris Day singing.

name: Angus Cameron
profession: Editor Forced Out in McCarthy Era
headline: Angus Cameron, 93, Editor Forced Out in McCarthy Era
abstract: Angus Cameron, a former editor in chief of one of America's foremost publishing houses, whose leftist sympathies forced him to resign during the anti-Communist fervor of the 1950's, died on Monday in Charlottesville, Va. He was 93.    Mr. Cameron was top editor at Little, Brown, the publisher of J. D. Salinger, Lillian Hellman and Evelyn Waugh. In his eight years there, he gained a reputation for his keen appreciation of authors' creativity and the public taste. When C. S. Forester wanted to stop writing his Horatio Hornblower series, Mr. Cameron inspired him to keep it going.

name: Lynda Van Devanter

abstract: Lynda Van Devanter, whose pained account of her life as an Army nurse in Vietnam focused attention on the burdens of American servicewomen in the war, died on Nov. 15 at her home in Herndon, Va. She was 55.     At the Vietnam Veterans of America, where Ms. Van Devanter founded and administered a project dealing with the concerns and complaints of the 7,465 women who had served in Vietnam, a spokesman said she had long been ill with a vascular disease that she attributed to wartime exposure to chemical agents.

name: Helen Travis
profession: Activist; Won Case on Right to Travel
headline: Helen Travis, 86, Activist; Won Case on Right to Travel
abstract: Helen Levi Travis, a peace and social activist and the subject of a 1967 Supreme Court ruling that upheld her right to travel abroad, died on Nov. 14 in San Pedro, Calif. She was 86.    Born in Manhattan, Mrs. Travis graduated from Barnard College in 1937. A student trip to the Soviet Union in 1934 impressed her with the promises of socialism, and after graduation she started traveling extensively with her first husband, Abbott Simon, a leader of the radical left-wing American Youth Congress.

He died at Seton Medical Center in Austin with a number of family members present, said his son-in-law Bruce Todd, a former mayor of Austin.

headline: Johnny Miles, Upset Winner of Boston Marathon, Dies at 97
abstract: Johnny Miles, a grocery deliveryman from Nova Scotia who came out of obscurity to win the 1926 Boston Marathon in one of distance running's greatest upsets, died last Sunday in Hamilton, Ontario. He was 97 and the marathon's oldest surviving winner.    When he arrived in Boston in April 1926, accompanied by his mother and father, Miles had never competed in a marathon. He had run through often-snowy hills along a streetcar line near his home for his distance training.

name: Belding H. Scribner

Scribner, who invented a device that allowed millions of people to live on long-term kidney dialysis and pioneered the development of bioethics committees, died on Thursday in Seattle. He was 82 and a professor emeritus at the University of Washington.    A kayaker found Dr. Scribner's body floating near the doctor's houseboat in Portage Bay, where he was eating lunch when his wife, Ethel, left for an appointment. On her return, she said, firefighters had just recovered his body.

name: Doris Andrews

The farm, in Ridgefield and Wilton, Conn., is now the Weir Farm National Historic Site, with programs for both artists and the public. The programs are run by the Weir Farm Trust, a private nonprofit organization that works in partnership with the National Park Service.

The Pickrick was noted for the quality of its fried chicken and for its reasonable prices, but Mr. Maddox was determined that no black should experience the ambience that he had reserved exclusively for whites.

He was 71 and lived in Great Neck.    A cause of death has not been announced, pending a coroner's report, but Mr. Heinemann suffered from diabetes and an irregular heartbeat and may have died of a heart attack while driving, said his wife, Sally. The car he was driving struck two other cars, she said, but no one in them was injured.

name: Charlotte Selver

abstract: Charlotte Selver, a teacher of sensory awareness who helped inspire the school of psychology that came to be known as the human potential movement, died on Aug. 22 at her home in Muir Beach, Calif., near San Francisco. She was 102.    In classes and individual sessions held as recently as this March, Ms. Selver taught students exercises focusing on breathing, movement and touch. She believed that these exercises, which she described as a kind of meditation in action, helped students shed social conditioning and recover an innate awareness.

name: Christabel Bielenberg
headline: Christabel Bielenberg, Anti-Nazi Memoirist, Dies at 94
abstract: Christabel Burton Bielenberg, a well-born Englishwoman who wrote a best-selling memoir about saving her German husband, a Nazi resister, from the Gestapo, died on Sunday at the family's home in rural Ireland. She was 94.    Her book, ''The Past Is Myself,'' published in 1968, was a runaway success and a Book of the Month Club selection as ''Ride Out the Dark'' (Norton, 1971). It formed the basis for a four-part television drama, called ''Christabel,'' written by Dennis Potter and starring Elizabeth Hurley, which was shown in this country on ''Masterpiece Theater'' on public television in 1989.

profession: San Francisco Artist Known for Layered Imagery

He was 80.    Jess, who dropped his last name, Collins, in the late 1940's when he broke from his family, was a reclusive artist whose Symbolist and Surrealist tendencies kept him working outside mainstream styles like Abstract Expressionism in the 1950's and Pop Art in the 60's. Nevertheless, he was revered in San Francisco, where he spent his entire adult life.

headline: All-Embracing Man of Action for a New Era of Papacy
abstract: On the night of Oct. 16, 1978, a vast, impatient throng in floodlit St. Peter's Square cheered wildly as white smoke curled from a chimney atop the Sistine Chapel, signaling the election of a new pope. A long wait had ended, but the enthusiasm was somewhat premature.    Cardinal Pericle Felici emerged minutes later to introduce Cardinal Karol Wojtyla of Poland, the first non-Italian pope since 1523. But even he had trouble pronouncing the name -- voy-TEE-wah. Hardly anyone, it seemed, knew who he was. Murmurs and questions rippled through the predominantly Roman crowd.

name: Saul Bellow
headline: Saul Bellow, Who Breathed Life Into American Novel, Dies at 89
abstract: Saul Bellow, Nobel laureate and self-proclaimed historian of society, dies at age 89; his more-than-lifesize heroes, Augie Marches, Hendersons, Herzog and Humboldts, and their scathing, darkly comic stories gave new immediacy to American fiction in second half of twentieth century; center of Bellow's fictional universe was Chicago, where he grew up and lived most of life; he was born in Quebec to Russian Jewish immigrants who moved to Chicago in 1924; photos (L)

name: Frank Conroy
headline: Frank Conroy Dies at 69; Led Noted Writers' Workshop
abstract: Frank Conroy, author of classic memoir Stop-Time and influence on generation of young writers, dies at age 69; headed Writers' Workshop at University of Iowa for 18 years, but published just five books, small number for writer of his reputation; photo (M)

name: Michael Roberts

abstract: Michael Roberts, restaurateur and chef who helped forge California culinary revolution of 1980's, dies at age 55; photo (M)

name: Rainier
headline: Prince Rainier, Who Brought Stardom to Monaco, Dies at 81
abstract: Rainier III of Monaco, prince whose storybook romance and marriage to actress Grace Kelly helped promote transformation of tiny country, dies at age 81; ran country with iron hand and cultivated captains of industry as Monaco's friends; photos (M)

name: J.C. Bacot
headline: J.C. Bacot, 72, Bank Chief Who Recast His Company, Dies
abstract: J. Carter Bacot, the former chairman and chief executive of the Bank of New York who transformed it from a traditional bank into a powerhouse in servicing other banks and the securities markets, died on Thursday at his home in Montclair, N. J. He was 72.     The cause was cardiac arrest, a spokesman for the Bank of New York said.

name: Jim Wiwa
profession: Nigerian Chief and Father of Dissident
headline: Jim Wiwa, Nigerian Chief and Father of Dissident, Is Dead
abstract: Jim Wiwa, chief of Ogoni of southern Nigeria who became symbol of his embattled people after execution of his son, dissident environmentalist and playwright Ken Saro-Wiwa, in 1995, dies; he is believed to have been 101 (M)

name: Kenneth Morley Wilson
headline: Kenneth Morley Wilson, 83, Renowned Glass Expert, Dies
abstract: Kenneth Morley Wilson, a noted historian of glass manufacture in America, who was long associated with the Corning Museum of Glass and the Henry Ford Museum, died on March 29 at his home in Punta Gorda, Fla. He was 83.    He died after a long illness, his family said.

name: Maynard J. Ramsay
headline: Maynard J. Ramsay, Insect Expert, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr Maynard Jack Ramsay, entomologist noted for efforts to track and eradicate exotic parasites carried in flowers, fruits and other cargo from overseas, dies at age 90 (M)

name: Chalmers Roberts

abstract: Chalmers McGeagh Roberts, retired chief diplomatic correspondent for Washington Post who covered Cold War, nuclear arms race and seats of power in Washington in 1950's and 1960's, dies at age 94 (M)

profession: Filmmaker and Pioneer of TV Documentaries
headline: Al Wasserman Dies at 84; Filmmaker and Pioneer of TV Documentaries
abstract: Al Wasserman, pioneering filmmaker of movie and television documentaries and winner of many major awards, dies at age 84; Wasserman was a producer of CBS series 60 Minutes from 1976 to 1986 (M)

name: Marilyn Levine
headline: Marilyn Levine Dies at 69; Sculptor of Leathery Works
abstract: Marilyn Levine, prominent ceramic sculptor known for deceptively realistic renditions of leather goods, dies at age 69; her work was initially seen as three-dimensional equivalent of Photo Realism; photo (M)

name: Charlotte Kempner Beyers
headline: Charlotte Kempner Beyers, 73, Filmmaker, Is Dead
abstract: Charlotte Kempner Beyers, documentary filmmaker whose works were among first to introduce students to realities of AIDS, dies at age 73 (M)

headline: Wilson McWilliams, 71, Dies; Wrote About Political Trends
abstract: Wilson Carey McWilliams, author and political scientist who took special interest in moral basis of politics, dies at age 71 (M)

name: Andrea Dworkin
headline: Andrea Dworkin, Writer and Crusading Feminist, Dies at 58
abstract: Andrea Dworkin, feminist writer and antipornography campaigner whose work was lightning rod for debate on pornography and censorship that raged through nation in 1980's, dies at age 58; photo (M)

name: Archbishop Iakovos
headline: Archbishop Iakovos, Major Ecumenical Force, Dies
abstract: Archbishop Iakovos, primate of Greek Orthodox Archdiocese in North and South America for 37 years, towering figure in ecumenical movement and first Greek archbishop in 350 years to confer with a pope, dies at age 93; photo; Iakovos was imposing religious presence and champion of social causes who moved Greek Orthodox Church into mainstream American life, sometimes conflicting with Ecumenical Patriarch Bartholomew I (M)

name: Maurice Hilleman
headline: Maurice Hilleman, Master in Creating Vaccines, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr Maurice R Hilleman, microbiologist who developed vaccines for mumps, measles, chickenpox, pneumonia, meningitis and other diseases, saving tens of millions of lives, dies at age of 85; much of modern preventive medicine is based on his work; he is credited with having developed more human and animal vaccines than any other scientist, helping to extend human life expectancy and improving economics of many countries; his career and accomplishments reviewed; photo (M)

name: Chen Yifei
headline: Chen Yifei, 59, Painter and Entrepreneur, Dies
abstract: Chen Yifei, Chinese painter and entrepreneur who was favorite of Chinese leaders and Western industrialists and amassed fortune selling his work in New York, dies at age 59; photo (M)

name: Paul K. Perry
headline: Paul K. Perry, Innovator in Polling, Dies at 95
abstract: Paul K. Perry, an architect of the Gallup Poll who pieced through the wreckage of pollsters' stunningly wrong predictions that President Harry S. Truman would be defeated in 1948 to improve forecasts for future elections, died on April 7 at a hospital in Princeton, N.J. He was 95.    The cause was a cerebral hemorrhage, a son, Dr. Paul G. Perry, said.

name: Wilbur A. Levin
profession: Guide to Brooklynites as Kings County Clerk
headline: Wilbur A. Levin, Guide to Brooklynites as Kings County Clerk, Dies at 84
abstract: Wilbur A. Levin, the Kings County clerk and a longtime civic and business leader in New York City, died yesterday at his home in Manhattan. He was 84.    The cause was cancer, his daughter Kate D. Levin said.

name: Jeanne Petrek
headline: Jeanne Petrek, Surgeon Known for Cancer Research, Dies at 57
abstract: Dr. Jeanne Petrek, a cancer researcher known for her investigations into the aftermath of breast cancer surgery, especially its impact on fertility, was killed in an accident in Manhattan on Monday. She was 57 and lived in Bronxville, N.Y.    Dr. Petrek died in surgery, hours after being struck by an ambulette while crossing the street at Second Avenue and 64th Street. At the time, she was on her way to work at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center, where she directed the surgical program at the Evelyn H. Lauder Breast Center.

abstract: Philip Pavia, sculptor who was powerful force in midcentury avant-garde art scene in New York, dies at age 94; photo (M)

abstract: John T. McTernan, a left-wing legal gunslinger who prowled the nation to defend people accused of being Communists in the McCarthy years and who aided unpopular clients like Angela Davis and Cesar Chavez's United Farm Workers, died on March 28 at a nursing home in Santa Monica, Calif. He was 94.    His son, Garrett, announced the death.

name: Ralph D. Gardner
headline: Ralph D. Gardner, Adman and Horatio Alger Biographer, Dies at 81
abstract: Ralph D. Gardner, a writer and advertising executive and a biographer of Horatio Alger, died on March 30 at Roosevelt Hospital in Manhattan. He was 81 and lived in Manhattan.    The cause was complications of diabetes, his son Ralph Jr. said.

name: Faith McNulty
headline: Faith McNulty Dies at 86; Wrote About Country Life
abstract: Faith McNulty, a New Yorker staff writer who wrote many books about animals and country life for adults and children, died last Sunday at her home in Wakefield, R.I. She was 86. The cause was complications of a stroke, her sister, Elisabeth Keiffer, said.    In 1980, Ms. McNulty notably departed from her usual subjects with "The Burning Bed: The True Story of an Abused Wife" (Harcourt), an account of how in 1977 Francine Hughes, a battered Michigan housewife, killed her husband by setting him on fire after he passed out from drinking. She was acquitted of murder by reason of temporary insanity.

name: Ellen Lentz
headline: Ellen Lentz, 88, a Berlin Reporter, Dies
abstract: Ellen Lentz, who reported from Berlin for The New York Times at the height of the cold war, died on April 10 at a hospital in Berlin. She was 88.    The cause was heart failure, her son, Dr. Ulrich Lentz-Bartens, said.

name: Phyllis T. Wofford
headline: Rev. Phyllis T. Wofford, Minister at Riverside Church, Dies at 96
abstract: The Rev. Phyllis Taylor Wofford, who in 1959 was the first woman to become a minister on the staff of Riverside Church in Manhattan, died on April 4 in Norristown, Pa. She was 96. A Pennsylvania resident since 1988, she lived in Lansdale.    Her death was announced by a stepson, former United States Senator Harris Wofford.

name: José Melis
headline: José Melis, a 'Tonight' Show Bandleader, Dies at 85
abstract: José Melis, a classically trained pianist who helped pioneer a broadcasting genre as orchestra leader for the ''Tonight'' show with Jack Paar, died April 7 at Boswell Memorial Hospital in Sun City, Ariz. He was 85.    The cause was a respiratory infection, said his son, Michael Melis, with whom Mr. Melis had been living in Peoria, Ariz.

name: Deena Burton
headline: Deena Burton, 56, Authority on Indonesian Dance Forms, Dies
abstract: Deena Burton, an expert on Indonesian dance, died April 3 at her mother's home in Queens. She was 56 and lived in Manhattan.     The cause was lung cancer, said Helene Browning, a friend.

headline: Kenneth Schermerhorn, Rigorous Conductor, Dies at 75
abstract: Kenneth Schermerhorn, conductor who directed Nashville Symphony and was music director of American Ballet Theater and New Jersey Symphony Orchestra, dies at age 75; photo (M)

abstract: Charles McC Hauser, longtime editor of The Providence Journal who risked prison by defying federal judge in First Amendment battle, dies at age 76 (M)

abstract: James A Houston, writer and artist almost single-handedly responsible for introducing contemporary Eskimo art to international audience, dies at age 83; was leading designer for Steuben Glass, author and illustrator; photo (M)

name: James D. Houston
headline: James D. Houston, Chronicler of a Diverse California, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Houston captured the promise, the harshness and the sheer beauty of California in novels like “Continental Drift” and “Snow Mountain Passage.”

name: H. Richard Uviller
headline: H. Richard Uviller, 75, Prosecutor and Law Professor, Dies
abstract: H Richard Uviller, provocative legal educator who salted scholarly analyses with gritty personal stories from his work as Manhattan prosecutor, dies at age 75 (M)

name: Gene Frankel
headline: Gene Frankel, Acting Coach and Director, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Gene Frankel, pioneering Off Broadway director and respected acting teacher whose career extended from Broadway to 70-seat theater on Bond Street that bears his name, dies at age 85 (M)

name: Norman Newell
headline: Norman Newell, 96, Scientist Who Studied Dying Species, Has Died
abstract: Dr. Norman D. Newell, an influential paleontologist who challenged opponents of evolutionary theory and helped shape theories explaining the mass extinctions of species, died on Monday at his home in Leonia, N.J., his family said. He was 96.     In a wide-ranging career that included scholarship, fieldwork and popular writing, he taught at Columbia and spent four decades as a curator of invertebrates at the American Museum of Natural History in Manhattan.

name: Cliff Montgomery
headline: Cliff Montgomery, Who Starred at Columbia, Dies at 94
abstract: Cliff Montgomery, the quarterback who called and executed the hidden-ball play known as KF-79 that propelled Columbia to a 7-0 upset of Stanford in the 1934 Rose Bowl, died Thursday at Winthrop-University Hospital in Mineola, N.Y. Montgomery, who lived in Roslyn Heights, N.Y., was 94.    He died after a short illness, his son, Clifford, said.

name: Diane Knippers
headline: Diane Knippers Dies at 53; Strategist for Christian Right
abstract: Diane Knippers, a religious strategist who helped conservative Christians raise an increasingly loud and unified voice in the traditionally liberal bastions of mainline Protestantism in recent years, died on Monday in Arlington, Va. She was 53.    The cause was cancer, according to the Institute on Religion and Democracy, a small but influential Washington group, of which Mrs. Knippers, a laywoman, was the longtime president.

name: David Hughes
headline: David Hughes Is Dead at 74; Novelist, Critic and Teacher
abstract: David Hughes, an English man of letters best known for exploring the individual's role in traumatic public events in his elegantly written novels, among them ''The Pork Butcher'' (Schocken, 1985) and ''The Joke of the Century'' (Taplinger, 1986), died on April 11. He was 74 and lived in London.    His death was reported in the British news media.

name: John Mills
headline: Sir John Mills, Actor Who Played The English 'Everyman,' Is Dead at 97
abstract: Sir John Mills, the celebrated British actor who portrayed war heroes, Dickensian upstarts and an extraordinary pantheon of English characters in a film, stage and television career that spanned much of the 20th century, died on Saturday at his home in Denham, west of London. He was 97.    The cause of death was not announced, but The Associated Press quoted a trustee of Sir John's estate as saying he had been ill for about a month with a chest infection. He had been almost blind since 1992, when the retinas of his eyes failed, though he continued acting, appearing earlier this year as A Tramp in a short titled ''Lights2.''

name: Robert Granville
headline: Robert Granville, Agent Who Arrested the Rosenbergs, Dies at 89
abstract: Robert R. Granville, an F.B.I. agent in New York who headed the team that arrested Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, died on April 12 at a hospital in Tampa, Fla. He was 89 and lived in Crystal River.    He had had a stroke two weeks earlier, said his son, Col. Robert R. Granville Jr., M.D.

name: Greg Jordan
headline: Greg Jordan, Who Designed Homes for the A-List, Dies at 48
abstract: Greg Jordan, a prominent Manhattan designer who created interiors for socialites like Blaine Trump and Elizabeth Johnson, with whom he formed close friendships, died on Wednesday at his apartment in Manhattan. He was 48.    The cause was a heart attack stemming from advanced coronary artery disease, his mother, Patricia Jordan, said.

name: Ezer Weizman
profession: Former President of Israel and Hero of 1967 War
headline: Ezer Weizman, Former President of Israel and Hero of 1967 War, Dies at 80
abstract: Ezer Weizman, the swashbuckling and acerbic former president of Israel, who built the country's air force and guided it in the startlingly swift victory over the Arab forces in the 1967 Arab-Israeli war, died last night, the government said. He was 80 and suffered recently from pneumonia.     Mr. Weizman made his name as one of Israel's most celebrated fighting men, yet he worked to transform himself into a dovish politician. He was involved in the 1978 peace negotiations with Egypt that led to Israel's withdrawal from the territory he helped capture a decade earlier.

name: John Hultberg
headline: John Hultberg, 83, Painter Prominent in the Avant-Garde, Dies
abstract: John Hultberg, an American abstract painter and printmaker who came to the fore with the avant-garde after World War II, died on April 15 at Roosevelt Hospital in Manhattan. He was 83 and lived on the Upper West Side.    The cause was complications of a stroke, according to Christopher Wieliczko, an associate.

name: Alexander J. Trotman
headline: Alexander J. Trotman, 71, Former Chief of Ford Motor, Dies
abstract: Alexander J. Trotman, who rose from a student trainee at Ford Motor to become the company's chief executive for much of the 1990's, died on Monday in Yorkshire, England. He was 71.    Ford said in a statement that Mr. Trotman had died after a brief illness.

name: Thomas J. Concannon
headline: Thomas J. Concannon, Longtime Lawyer to the Indigent, Dies at 61
abstract: Thomas J. Concannon, who abandoned a career in banking after a long bus ride across South Asia, then spent the next three decades wielding legendary charm and formidable negotiating skills as a lawyer for thousands of poor people in New York, died on Saturday at the Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center. He was 61 and lived in Manhattan.    The cause was complications of multiple myeloma, a blood cancer, according his wife, Janet Mardfin.

name: Philip Morrison
headline: Philip Morrison, 89, Builder of First Atom Bomb, Dies
abstract: Dr. Philip Morrison, who helped assemble the first atomic bomb with his own hands, and then campaigned for the rest of his life against weapons that could deliver such devastation, died Friday at his home in Cambridge, Mass. He was 89.    He died in his sleep, his family said.

name: John F. White
profession: Pioneer in the Development of Public TV
headline: John F. White, 87, a Pioneer in the Development of Public TV, Dies
abstract: John F. White, president emeritus of the Cooper Union for the Advancement of Science and Art and an architect of public broadcasting in the United States, died on Friday at his home in Virginia Beach. He was 87. A former resident of Tuxedo Park, N.Y., he also had a home in Sarasota, Fla.    His death was announced by his family.

name: Earl Wilson
headline: Earl Wilson, a Pitcher and '68 World Series Winner, Dies at 70
abstract: Earl Wilson, a leading pitcher for the Boston Red Sox and the 1968 World Series champion Detroit Tigers, and one of the top home run hitters among major league pitchers, died Saturday at his home in Southfield, Mich. He was 70.    The cause was a heart attack, said Jim Martin, the executive director of the Baseball Assistance Team, which provides financial aid to former baseball figures. Wilson served as the organization's president from 2000 through 2004 and headed its grants committee at his death.

name: Eduardo Paolozzi
headline: Eduardo Paolozzi, a Leading British Pop Artist, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Sir Eduardo Paolozzi, a father of British Pop Art and a leading sculptor of the postwar era, died in a London hospital on Friday. He was 81.     Sir Eduardo's death followed a period of decline that began when he suffered a stroke four years ago, said Emily Bishop, director of the New York branch of Flowers, the London gallery that handles his work.

name: Percy Heath
headline: Percy Heath, Bassist of Modern Jazz Quartet, Dies at 81
abstract: Percy Heath, whose forceful and buoyant bass playing anchored the Modern Jazz Quartet for its entire four-decade existence, died yesterday in Southampton, N.Y. He was 81 and lived in Montauk, on Long Island.    The cause of death was bone cancer, his family said.

name: J. B. Stoner
profession: Fervent Racist and Benchmark for Extremism
headline: J. B. Stoner, 81, Fervent Racist and Benchmark for Extremism, Dies
abstract: J.B. Stoner, an unapologetic racist whose conviction for bombing a church, divisive political campaigns and vituperations about Jews and blacks made him a benchmark for racial extremism in the United States, died on Saturday at a nursing home in La Fayette, Ga. He was 81.    The cause was complications of pneumonia, Judith Ragon, wife of Mr. Stoner's second cousin, Ronald Ragon, told The Associated Press.

name: Arnie Lawrence
profession: Mentor and Teacher on Jazz Scene
headline: Arnie Lawrence, 66, Mentor and Teacher on Jazz Scene, Dies
abstract: Arnie Lawrence, a jazz saxophonist and pioneering educator who helped found the jazz program at the New School University in New York and started an innovative program to train young jazz musicians of both Jewish and Arab backgrounds in Israel, died on April 22 in Jerusalem. He was 66 and lived in Jerusalem.     The cause was lung and liver cancer, said his son Erik Lawrence.

name: Jimmy Woode
headline: Jimmy Woode, Ex-Ellington Bassist, Dies at 78
abstract: Jimmy Woode, bassist and one of leading figures on European jazz scene who also played with Duke Ellington, dies at age 78 (M)

name: Red Horner
headline: Red Horner, One of Hockey's Toughest Players, Dies at 95
abstract: Red Horner, hockey Hall of Fame defenseman, dies at age 95 (M)

name: Miguel Martinez

abstract: Miguel Martinez, former member of New York City School Board of Education, dies at age 67 (M)

name: Hasil Adkins
headline: Hasil Adkins, Wild Man of Rockabilly, Dies at 68
abstract: Hasil Adkins, 78, rockabilly singer and cult figure among record collectors and musicians, is found dead at his home near Madison, West Va; photo (M)

name: David Bazelon
headline: David Bazelon, 82, Writer, Teacher, Social Critic
abstract: David T Bazelon, writer, social critic and political science teacher, dies at age 82 (M)

name: Willard C. Mackey Jr.
headline: Willard C. Mackey Jr., 82, Ex-Chief of McCann Erickson, Dies
abstract: Willard Clyde Mackey Jr., a former chief executive of McCann Erickson Worldwide who helped build it into one of advertising's foremost powerhouses, died on April 16 in Vero Beach, Fla. He was 82 and lived in Vero Beach and New Canaan, Conn.     The death was announced by Eugene H. Kummel, chairman emeritus of the company.

name: Mel Gussow
headline: Mel Gussow, Critic, Dies at 71; a Champion of Playwrights
abstract: Mel Gussow, the longtime critic and cultural reporter for The New York Times who championed the work of many of the major playwrights of the post World War II period, including Harold Pinter, Edward Albee and Tom Stoppard, died Friday at New York-Presbyterian Hospital. He was 71 and lived in Manhattan.    The cause was cancer, said his son, Ethan Gussow.

name: Carol Rothschild Noyes
headline: Carol Rothschild Noyes, Environment Advocate, Dies at 88
abstract: Carol Rothschild Noyes, a supporter of civic and environmental causes, died on April 18 at her home in Laurel Hollow, N.Y. She was 88.    Her family announced the death.

name: Robert Farnon
profession: Composer of Popular Postwar Light Music
headline: Robert Farnon, 87, Composer of Popular Postwar Light Music, Dies
abstract: Robert Farnon, a composer and arranger who was a leading figure in the once-popular genre of light orchestral music, died on April 23 on Guernsey, in the British Channel Islands. He was 87 and had been a longtime resident of Guernsey.    His death was announced by David Ades, a friend and music historian who is the secretary of the Robert Farnon Society.

name: Alvin Novick
profession: Biologist and Advocate for AIDS Victims
headline: Dr. Alvin Novick, Biologist and Advocate for AIDS Victims, Dies at 79
abstract: Dr. Alvin Novick, a Yale biologist who closed his laboratory in 1982 and curtailed his 25-year study of the sonar systems of bats to confront a widening international health crisis brought on by AIDS, died on April 10 at Yale University Health Services in New Haven. He was 79.     The cause was prostate cancer, said a close friend, Dr. Frederick L. Altice, an associate professor of medicine at Yale.

name: Evelyn A. Hall
headline: Evelyn A. Hall, 93, Arts Patron, Dies
abstract: Evelyn Annenberg Jaffe Hall, a New York arts patron for 50 years and a supporter of medical institutions, died on April 22 at her home on the Upper East Side of Manhattan. She was 93 and also had homes in Palm Beach, Fla., and Newport, R.I.    Mrs. Hall, a sister of the late publisher Walter H. Annenberg, shared her fortune with many beneficiaries. Among her favorites were the Museum of Modern Art and the Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center.

name: Kenneth Clark
headline: Kenneth Clark, WhoFought Segregation, Dies
abstract: Kenneth B Clark, psychologist and educator whose 1950 report showing destructive effect of school segregation influenced United States Supreme Court to hold school segregation to be unconstitutional, dies at age of 90; detailed recounting of case, and of his career; photo (L)

name: William Rashbaum
headline: William Rashbaum, 78, Abortion Rights Advocate
abstract: William K. Rashbaum, a prominent New York obstetrician and gynecologist who was a longtime advocate of abortion rights, died yesterday at New York-Presbyterian/Columbia in Manhattan. He was 78 and lived in Manhattan and Cornwall, Conn.    The cause was complications of lung cancer, said his son, William K. Jr.

name: Jack Nichols
headline: Jack Nichols, Gay Rights Pioneer, Dies at 67
abstract: Jack Nichols, a writer and early gay activist who campaigned publicly for gay rights nearly a decade before the Stonewall riots of 1969, died on Monday in Cocoa Beach, Fla., where he lived. He was 67.     The cause was complications of cancer, from which Mr. Nichols had suffered intermittently for more than 20 years, said Steve Yates, a longtime friend.

name: Edward von Kloberg III
headline: Edward von Kloberg III, Lobbyist for Many Dictators, Dies at 63
abstract: Edward von Kloberg III, a flamboyant lobbyist here who maintained a high-profile client roster that could easily be found in his Rolodex under ''d,'' for dictator, died on Sunday in Rome. He was 63.    Mr. von Kloberg, whose death was classified a suicide, apparently leapt from the parapet of a castle, the State Department said on Tuesday. He left behind a note, the contents of which were not disclosed.

name: Edward J. Schantz
headline: Edward J. Schantz, Pioneering Researcher of Toxins, Including Botox, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Edward J. Schantz, a biochemist who studied the deadly neurotoxins produced by shellfish and other organisms, first for the toxins' military potential and later for their broader medical benefits, including cosmetic treatments that led to Botox, died on April 28 at an extended-care center in Madison, Wis. He was 96.     The cause was congestive heart failure, his family said.

name: Raisa Struchkova
headline: Raisa Struchkova Dies at 79; Ballerina Who Leapt Into Husband's Arms
abstract: Raisa Struchkova, one of the Soviet Union's leading ballerinas in the Bolshoi Ballet when that company first took audiences abroad by storm in the 1950's and 60's, died in Moscow on Monday, the Bolshoi Theater announced. She was 79 and lived in Moscow.    Ms. Struchkova was highly praised at home for her classical dancing, especially in ''Giselle'' and ''Cinderella.'' But for American audiences who were stunned by the athletic vigor of the Bolshoi at its New York debut in 1959, Ms. Struchkova will always be associated with the high-flying virtuosity that she showed in Soviet-style bravura duets with her husband, Aleksandr Lapauri.

name: Peter Bramley
headline: Peter Bramley, a Designer of Early National Lampoon, Dies at 60
abstract: Peter Bramley, first art director of National Lampoon magazine, dies at age 60; photos (M)

name: Stephen Sloan
headline: Stephen Sloan Is Dead at 72; Executive and Top Fisherman
abstract: Stephen Sloan, former partner in Lehman Brothers and champion angler, dies at age 72; photo (M)

name: Jonathan Thomas
headline: Jonathan Thomas, Artist, Dies at 59
abstract: Jonathan Thomas, a sculptor who exhibited widely in North America, died on Monday at his home in New York. He was 59.    The cause was bladder cancer, said his partner, the playwright Edward Albee.

name: Robert N. Colwell
headline: Robert N. Colwell, Forester Who Studied Land From the Air, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Robert N. Colwell, a forester and specialist in remote sensing who helped adapt the military's aerial image-reading techniques to forestry, mapmaking, land planning, agriculture and other fields, died on April 14 in a hospital in Walnut Creek, Calif. He was 87 and lived in Walnut Creek.     The cause was respiratory failure, his family said.

name: David Hackworth
headline: Col. David Hackworth, Hero of Vietnam War, Dies at 74
abstract: David H. Hackworth, a much-decorated and highly unconventional former career Army officer who became a combat legend in Vietnam, then enraged his superiors by lambasting the war on national television, died on Wednesday at a hospital in Tijuana, Mexico. He was 74.    The cause was bladder cancer, his wife, Eilhys England, said.

name: Leonid Shamkovich
headline: Leonid Shamkovich, 81, Ex-Soviet Chess Grandmaster, Is Dead
abstract: Leonid Shamkovich, Russian-born chess grandmaster, dies at age 81 (M)

name: Robert Slutzky
headline: Robert Slutzky, 75, Painter and Architectural Theorist, Dies
abstract: Robert Slutzky, painter, writer and educator who explored connection between painting and architecture, dies at age 75; photo (M)

name: Ted Atkinson
profession: Hall of Fame Jockey for Tom Fool
headline: Ted Atkinson, Hall of Fame Jockey for Tom Fool, Dies at 88
abstract: Ted F Atkinson, member of racing Hall of Fame and first jockey to win more than $1 million in season, dies at age 88; photo (M)

name: Herb Sargent
headline: Herb Sargent, TV Writer, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Herb Sargent, veteran television comedy writer whose work included Tonight Show and Saturday Night Live, dies at age 81; photo (M)

name: Peter W. Rodino
headline: Peter W. Rodino Dies at 96; Led House Inquiry on Nixon
abstract: Peter W. Rodino Jr., an obscure congressman from the streets of Newark who impressed the nation by the dignity, fairness and firmness he showed as chairman of the impeachment hearings that induced Richard M. Nixon to resign as president, died yesterday at his home in West Orange, N.J.. He was 95.     The cause was congestive heart failure, said Christine Bland, a spokeswoman for Seton Hall University School of Law, where he was a professor emeritus and continued to lecture until February.

name: Nathaniel Weyl
headline: Nathaniel Weyl, Author Who Testified on Alger Hiss, Dies at 94
abstract: Nathaniel Weyl, a writer and economist who was best known for the minor role he played in the Alger Hiss spy case, died on April 13 at his home in Ojai, Calif. He was 94.    Mr. Weyl died of natural causes, said his stepdaughter Georgianne Cowan.

name: Eugene W. Friedman
headline: Dr. Eugene W. Friedman, Chief Surgeon, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Eugene W. Friedman, former chief of head and neck surgery at Mount Sinai Medical Center, died there on April 18. He was 86 and lived on the East Side of Manhattan.    The cause was complications of prostate cancer, his family said.

name: Bob Schiffer
headline: Bob Schiffer Dies at 88; Hollywood's Ace of Faces
abstract: Bob Schiffer, a celebrated Hollywood makeup artist who spent nearly 70 years turning men into monsters and beautiful women into breathtakingly beautiful women, died on April 26 in Los Angeles. He was 88.    The cause was complications of a stroke, said his son, Douglas.

name: Lloyd N. Cutler
headline: Lloyd N. Cutler, Counselor to Presidents, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Lloyd N Cutler, Washington power broker who helped found legal firm of Wilmer, Cutler & Pickering and also served as counselor to Presidents Jimmy Carter and Bill Clinton and adviser to other presidents, dies at age of 87; photo (M)

name: Benny Bailey
headline: Benny Bailey, U.S. Jazzman Whose Home Base Was Europe, Dies at 79
abstract: Benny Bailey, American trumpet player who for most of his career lived in Europe, died Apr 14 at age of 79 (M)

name: Fei Xiaotong
headline: Fei Xiaotong, 94, a Pioneer in Chinese Anthropology, Is Dead
abstract: Fei Xiaotong, one of China's pre-eminent social scientists, died Apr 24 at age of 94; photo (M)

name: Peter Karasz
profession: Managing Partner of an International Law Firm
headline: Peter Karasz, Managing Partner of an International Law Firm, Dies at 63
abstract: Peter Karasz, managing partner of Cleary Gottlieb, one of New York's leading international law firms, died Apr 30 at age of 63 (M)

name: Carolyn Brady
headline: Carolyn Brady, 67, Artist in Watercolor, Is Dead
abstract: Carolyn Brady, artist known for her large Photorealist watercolor paintings, dies at age of 67 (M)

name: Benjamin Mordecai
headline: Benjamin Mordecai, Stage Producer and Manager, Dies at 60
abstract: Benjamin Mordecai, Broadway producer, general manager and former managing director of Yale Repertory Theater, dies at age of 60; photo (M)

name: Zhang Chunqiao
profession: One of China's Gang of Four
headline: Zhang Chunqiao, 88, One of China's Gang of Four, Dies
abstract: Zhang Chunqiao, a radical Maoist who held several positions at the apex of China's government when he was convicted in 1981 as a member of the infamous Gang of Four, died April 21, the Chinese government reported yesterday. He was 88.    The state-run New China News Agency said Mr. Zhang had died of cancer. There have been erroneous reports of his death or of serious illness going back at least to 1980.

name: Helen Wilkins Claytor
headline: Helen Wilkins Claytor, Ex-President of Y.W.C.A., Dies at 98
abstract: Helen Jackson Wilkins Claytor, a pivotal figure in the racial desegregation of the Y.W.C.A. and its first African-American president, died yesterday in Grand Rapids, Mich. She was 98.    Her death was announced by her son, Roger Wilkins, the Robinson professor of history and American culture at George Mason University.

name: Betty Talmadge
headline: Betty Talmadge, Ex-Wife of Georgia Senator, Dies at 81
abstract: Betty Talmadge, former wife of late Sen Herman Talmadge and prominent Washington hostess, dies at age 81; photo (M)

name: Tony Fuller
headline: Tony Fuller, 62, Journalist Who Co-Wrote 'Charlie Company,' Dies
abstract: Tony Fuller, former journalist and co-author of Vietnam war book Charlie Company, dies at age 62 (S)

name: Jay Marshall
headline: Jay Marshall, 85, the Dean of Magic, Is Dead
abstract: Jay Marshall, a magician whose accomplishments -- from appearing 14 times on ''The Ed Sullivan Show'' to playing New York's Palace and London's Palladium -- persuaded America's conjurers to elect him their dean, died Tuesday in Chicago. He was 85.    The cause was a heart attack, his son Alexander said.

name: Louise Westergaard
headline: Louise Westergaard, Broadway Producer of Revues, Dies at 67
abstract: Louise Westergaard O'Neil, a theatrical producer best known for the hit Broadway musical revue ''Sophisticated Ladies,'' died on May 6 in New York. She was 67 and lived in Manhattan.    The cause was leukemia, her family said.

name: Milton Frederick Rosenthal
headline: Milton Frederick Rosenthal, 91, Former Chairman of Engelhard, Dies
abstract: Milton Frederick Rosenthal, a former chairman of the chemical giant Engelhard Corporation, died on May 2 at Mount Sinai Hospital in Manhattan. He was 91 and lived in Harrison, N.Y.    His death was announced by the family.

name: Tristan Egolf
profession: Novelist Known for His Elaborate Prose
headline: Tristan Egolf, 33, Novelist Known for His Elaborate Prose, Dies
abstract: Tristan Egolf, a young novelist whose lavish prose was dismissed by some critics as callow and rapturously compared by others to the work of Thomas Pynchon, William Faulkner and John Kennedy Toole, was found dead in his apartment in Lancaster, Pa., on May 7. He was 33.    The cause was a self-inflicted gunshot wound, said G. Gary Kirchner, the Lancaster County coroner.

name: Horton M. Davies
profession: Authority on Christianity's Impact on the Arts
headline: Horton M. Davies, 89, an Authority on Christianity's Impact on the Arts, Is Dead
abstract: Horton Marlais Davies, Putnam professor emeritus of religion at Princeton and an author of many books about church history, died on Wednesday at his home in Princeton, N.J. He was 89.    The death was announced by his family.

name: Stan Levey
headline: Stan Levey, Bebop Drummer, Dies at 79
abstract: Stan Levey, one of the first drummers to master the complex form of jazz known as bebop, died on April 19 in Van Nuys, Calif. He was 79 and lived in Sherman Oaks.    He died two months after surgery for cancer of the jaw, said his wife, Angela.

name: Jimmy Martin
headline: Jimmy Martin, 77, a Bluegrass Stalwart, Is Dead
abstract: Jimmy Martin, whose high tenor voice, driving guitar and plucky personality made him an exemplar of bluegrass music for more than 50 years, died on Saturday in Nashville. He was 77 and lived in Hermitage, Tenn.    The cause was bladder cancer and congestive heart failure, said his son Ray.

name: Andrew J. Goodpaster
headline: Andrew J. Goodpaster, 90, Soldier and Scholar, Dies
abstract: Gen. Andrew J. Goodpaster, a soldier and scholar who fought in World War II, commanded the North Atlantic Treaty Organization and came out of retirement to lead the United States Military Academy in a time of crisis, died on Monday at Walter Reed Army Medical Center here. He was 90 and a resident of Washington.    The cause was prostate cancer, said his granddaughter Sarah Nesnow.

name: Manny Gluck
headline: Manny Gluck, 65, Dies; Yankee Vendor No. 1
abstract: Emanuel Gluck, a retired middle-school principal who had a rich alternate life as Yankee Stadium's longest-working vendor, signified by his No. 1 badge, died on May 12 at NewYork-Presbyterian/Columbia hospital in Manhattan. He was 65.    The cause was a heart attack, his wife, Sharyn, said.

name: Elisabeth Fraser
headline: Elisabeth Fraser, 85, Character Actress
abstract: Elisabeth Fraser, a versatile character actress with a 40-year career on stage, screen and, most enduringly, television, died on May 5 at the Motion Picture and Television Hospital in Los Angeles. She was 85 and lived in Los Angeles.    The cause was congestive heart failure, said her daughter Meg McDonald Seltzer.

name: Norman D. Kurtz
headline: Norman D. Kurtz, 69, Founder of Skyscraper Outfitting Firm, Dies
abstract: Norman D. Kurtz, the chairman and founding partner of the engineering firm Flack & Kurtz, which supplied many skyscrapers with electrical and mechanical equipment, died on Friday at home in Scarsdale, N.Y. He was 69.    The death, apparently caused by a heart attack, was announced by his family and the firm, which he helped establish in 1969.

name: Paul K. Keene
headline: Paul K. Keene, 94, Organic Farming Pioneer, Dies
abstract: Paul K. Keene, a pioneer of organic farming in the United States whose products were among the first commercially available organic foods in the country, died on April 23 at a nursing home in Mechanicsburg, Pa. He was 94. Mr. Keene's family announced the death.    For more than half a century, Mr. Keene ran Walnut Acres Farm, near Penns Creek in central Pennsylvania, which produced and packaged an array of foods including peanut butter, granola and free-range chicken. Walnut Acres products were grown without pesticides or chemical fertilizers and were stocked by health food stores around the country and sold worldwide through the company's mail-order catalog.

name: Frank Gorshin
headline: Frank Gorshin, 'Batman' Riddler, Dies at 72
abstract: Frank Gorshin, prolific actor and impressionist whose career was long identified with questionable character, the Riddler on television's original Batman, dies at 72; photos (L)

name: Elizabeth Hoffman
headline: Elizabeth Hoffman, 82, Editor for Ladies' Home Journal, Dies
abstract: Elizabeth McFarland Hoffman, poetry editor of Ladies' Home Journal, dies at 83 (S)

name: Arthur Naftalin
headline: Arthur Naftalin, 87, Professor and Former Minneapolis Mayor, Dies
abstract: Arthur Naftalin, who led Minneapolis through turbulent 1960's as a four-term mayor, dies at 87 (S)

name: Piero Dorazio
profession: Italian Painter With a Geometric Eye
headline: Piero Dorazio, Italian Painter With a Geometric Eye, Dies at 77
abstract: Piero Dorazio, a celebrated Italian abstract painter and an important innovator of Modernism in that country, died on Tuesday in a hospital in Perugia, near his home in Todi, Umbria. He was 77.    The cause was complications of diabetes, said his dealer in New York, Achim Moeller.

name: Marc Lappé
headline: Marc Lappé, 62, Dies; Fought Against Chemical Perils
abstract: Marc Lappe, toxicologist, author and educator who championed against chemical perils, dies at age 62; photo (M)

name: Milton Wolf
headline: Milton Wolf, 80, Economist and Ambassador to Austria, Dies
abstract: Milton A Wolf, economist, investor, real estate developer and former US ambassador to Austria, dies at age 80 (M)

name: Leonid Khachiyan
headline: Leonid Khachiyan, 52; Helped to Advance Computer Math
abstract: Leonid Khachiyan, a Russian-born mathematician who helped to advance the field of linear programming, which is used by computer scientists to schedule complex rosters of airline flights and to solve problems in finance and industry, died on April 29 at his home in South Brunswick, N.J. He was 52.     The cause was a heart attack, his family said.

name: Eddie Barclay
headline: Eddie Barclay, Recording Magnate, Dies at 84
abstract: Eddie Barclay, who for three decades after World War II was arguably the most powerful music mogul in Europe and inarguably the most flamboyant, died on May 13 in Paris. He was 84.     The cause was a heart attack, his family told Agence France-Presse.

name: Chung Se Yung
headline: Chung Se Yung Dies at 76; Built Hyundai's Auto Division
abstract: Chung Se Yung, the man who helped build the Hyundai Motor Company of South Korea into one of the world's biggest car makers, died Saturday in Seoul. He was 76.    Mr. Chung died of pneumonia at the Asan Medical Center in Seoul, said a statement by Hyundai Development Company, part of the powerful Hyundai Group of companies run by Mr. Chung's family.

name: George B. Dantzig
profession: Devised Math Solution to Broad Problems
headline: George B. Dantzig Dies at 90; Devised Math Solution to Broad Problems
abstract: Dr. George B. Dantzig, a mathematician who devised an algorithm that helped create linear programming, now a vital tool in computing, industry and other fields, died on May 13 at his home in Stanford, Calif. He was 90.     The cause was complications from diabetes and heart disease, his family said.

name: Ellis Page
headline: Ellis Page, 81, a Developer of Computerized Grading, Dies
abstract: Ellis B. Page, an education professor who developed an early computer program for grading written essays, died Tuesday near his home in McLean, Va. He was 81.    The cause was pneumonia, his family said.

name: Paul Ricoeur
headline: Paul Ricoeur, 92, Wide-Ranging French Philosopher, Is Dead
abstract: Paul Ricoeur, whose work on fundamental questions about the nature of human existence made him one of the most eminent philosophers of the 20th century, died Friday at his home in Châtenay-Malabry, outside Paris. He was 92.    Dr. Ricoeur died in his sleep, Charles E. Reagan, the author of ''Paul Ricoeur: His Life and Work'' (University of Chicago, 1996), said in a telephone interview.

name: Sol Stetin
headline: Sol Stetin, 95, Labor Leader Who Unionized J. P. Stevens, Dies
abstract: Sol Stetin, who led the drive to unionize the J.P. Stevens textile company when he was president of the Textile Workers Union of America, died on Saturday at a nursing home in St. Louis. He was 95.    The cause was complications of leukemia, union officials said.

name: William T. Seawell
headline: Brig. Gen. William T. Seawell, 87, Former Chief of Pan American, Dies
abstract: Brig. Gen. William Thomas Seawell, who commanded bombers in World War II and the cadet corps at the Air Force Academy and led Pan American World Airways, died on Friday at home in Pine Bluff, Ark., his birthplace. He was 87.    The apparent cause was a heart attack, his family said.

name: Daniel Schwarz
headline: Daniel Schwarz, 96, Editor Who Led The Sunday Times, Is Dead
abstract: Daniel Schwarz, who rose from clerk to the top editor of the Sunday department of The New York Times in a 44-year-career, died on Saturday at a hospital in Bradenton, Fla. He was 96.    He died after injuring his head in a fall while on a visit to his wife, Peggy, who lives in a nursing home in Bradenton, their son Edward said..

name: Howard Morris
headline: Howard Morris, an Actor in Television Comedies, Dies at 85
abstract: Howard Morris, a character actor in the Golden Age of television best known for his work with Sid Caesar and for his brief, memorable role as the manic hillbilly poet Ernest T. Bass on ''The Andy Griffith Show,'' died on Saturday at his home in Los Angeles. He was 85.    No cause of death was announced, but Mr. Morris's son, David, told The Los Angeles Times that his father had had heart problems in recent years.

name: Sunil Dutt
headline: Sunil Dutt, Star in India and Politician, Dies at 75
abstract: Sunil Dutt, the rebel-hero of Indian cinema, who leveraged his Bollywood celebrity into national political influence, died on Wednesday at his home in Mumbai. He was 75.    The cause was cardiac arrest, an aide told The Press Trust of India, the state-owned agency.

name: Richard Lewine
headline: Richard Lewine, 94, a Television Producer Who Also Wrote Music for Broadway
abstract: Richard Lewine, a Broadway composer and television producer, and a custodian of the legacy of Richard Rodgers, a second cousin, died on May 19 at his home in Manhattan. He was 94.    The death was announced by his family.

name: Ismail Merchant
profession: Producer of Sumptuous and Literate Films
headline: Ismail Merchant, Producer of Sumptuous and Literate Films, Dies at 68
abstract: Ismail Merchant, whose filmmaking collaboration with James Ivory created a genre of films with visually sumptuous settings that told literate tales of individuals trying to adapt to shifting societal values, died yesterday in a London hospital. He was 68.    Mr. Merchant's New York office said that the cause was undetermined, but that he had had surgery for abdominal ulcers on Tuesday.

name: Ruth Laredo
headline: Ruth Laredo, Pianist Who Recorded Rachmaninoff, Dies at 67
abstract: Ruth Laredo, a pianist equally at home in chamber music and solo works who was known for landmark recordings of Scriabin and Rachmaninoff, died on Wednesday at her apartment in New York. She was 67.    Ms. Laredo, who played her last concert on May 6 at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, had cancer and died in her sleep, said her manager, James Murtha.

name: Keiiti Aki
profession: Developed a Way to Measure the Strength of an Earthquake
headline: Keiiti Aki, 75, Is Dead; Developed a Way to Measure the Strength of an Earthquake
abstract: Dr. Keiiti Aki, a seismologist whose penetrating studies of the behavior and origins of earthquakes contributed to a deeper understanding of natural disasters, died May 17 on Réunion island in the Indian Ocean. He was 75.     The cause was a brain hemorrhage suffered after a fall, said a close friend, John K. McRaney of the Southern California Earthquake Center, where Dr. Aki had been a director.

name: Harold Tyler
headline: Harold Tyler, 83, Lawyer and Former Federal Judge, Dies
abstract: Harold R. Tyler Jr., a prominent lawyer and a former deputy attorney general and federal judge, who was frequently enlisted to provide judicial balance on legal panels considering contentious issues, died on Wednesday outside his apartment in Manhattan. He was 83.    The death was announced yesterday by his law firm, Patterson, Belknap, Webb & Tyler. His family said that he was returning home when he collapsed in his building, apparently after a heart attack.

name: Michael L. Tarnopol
profession: Banker and Director at Bear Stearns
headline: Michael L. Tarnopol, 68, Banker and Director at Bear Stearns, Dies
abstract: Michael L. Tarnopol, a vice chairman of Bear Stearns and chairman of its investment banking division, died Monday at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center in New York. He was 68 and lived in Manhattan.     The cause was prostate cancer, Bear Stearns said.

name: Ludmilla N. Shapiro
headline: Ludmilla N. Shapiro, 91, Collector of Soviet Kitsch, Dies
abstract: Ludmilla Nikitina Shapiro, a Russian-born journalist and photographer who with her husband amassed a collection of Soviet-era political porcelain considered the most comprehensive in North America, died on May 8 in Madison, Wis., where she lived. She was 91.    Mrs. Shapiro's death was announced by her granddaughter, Alexandra Corten.

name: Chico Carrasquel
headline: Chico Carrasquel, Venezuelan All-Star, Dies at 77
abstract: Chico Carrasquel, the smooth-fielding Chicago White Sox shortstop of the 1950's who became the major leagues' first star player from Venezuela, died Thursday in Caracas. He was 77.    The cause was a heart attack, the White Sox announced.

name: Eddie Albert
headline: Eddie Albert, Character Actor, Dies at 99
abstract: Eddie Albert, a film and television actor known for his evocative portrayals of characters who ranged from the avuncular to the befuddled to the monomaniacal, died on Thursday at his home near Pacific Palisades, Calif. He was 99.    The cause was pneumonia, his son, the actor Edward Albert Jr., told The Associated Press.

name: Martin Lings
headline: Martin Lings, a Sufi Writer on Islamic Ideas, Dies at 96
abstract: Martin Lings, a widely acclaimed British scholar whose books on Islamic philosophy, mysticism and art reflected his own deep belief in Sufism, the esoteric, purely spiritual dimension of Islam, died on May 12 at his home in Westerham, Kent County, England. He was 96.    His publisher, Virginia Gray Henry, director of Fons Vitae Publishing, announced his death.

name: Margaret Popkin
headline: Margaret Popkin, 54, Human Rights Lawyer, Dies
abstract: Margaret Popkin, an American lawyer who worked to overhaul the judicial system in strife-torn El Salvador, died on May 18 at a hospital in Washington. She was 54.    The cause was complications of heart surgery, her family said.

name: Donald H. Ryan
headline: Donald H. Ryan, 80, Entrepreneur in Repair, Is Dead
abstract: Donald Hillsdon Ryan, an American entrepreneur with a Harvard M.B.A. degree who built an overseas network of quick-fix repair franchises in busy cities, died on May 9 at his home in London. He was 80 and also had a residence in the Bahamas.    The death was announced by his family.

name: Batya Gur
headline: Batya Gur, Mystery Writer and Critic, Is Dead at 57
abstract: Batya Gur, a writer and critic almost single-handedly responsible for making the detective novel a flourishing genre in Israeli letters, died on May 19 in Jerusalem. She was 57 and lived in Jerusalem.    The cause was cancer, her family told Agence France-Presse.

name: Oscar Brown Jr.
headline: Oscar Brown Jr., Entertainer and Social Activist, Dies at 78
abstract: Oscar Brown Jr., a singer, songwriter, playwright and actor known for his distinctive blend of show-business savvy and social consciousness, died on Sunday in a Chicago hospital. He was 78 and lived in Chicago.    The cause was complications of a blood infection, his family said.

name: Herbert Warren Wind
headline: Herbert Warren Wind, Golf Writer, Dies at 88
abstract: Herbert Warren Wind, whose richly detailed prose graced the pages of The New Yorker and Sports Illustrated for 43 years and established him as the dean of American golf writers, died Monday in an assisted-living facility in Bedford, Mass. He was 88.    The cause was pneumonia, said his nephew, Bill Scheft, a columnist for Sports Illustrated.

name: John D'Amico
headline: John D'Amico, 67, Linesman in the N.H.L., Dies
abstract: John D'Amico, a member of the Hockey Hall of Fame who worked as a National Hockey League linesman for 23 years, died Sunday in Toronto. He was 67.    The cause was leukemia and bone cancer, the league said.

name: George Rochberg
headline: George Rochberg, Composer, Dies at 86
abstract: George Rochberg, an American composer who broke ranks with the rigorous modernism of the mid-century avant-garde to write music of rare urgency and candor, died on Sunday at a hospital in Bryn Mawr, Pa. He was 86 and made his home in Newtown Square, Pa.     The cause was complications of recent surgery, said his wife, Gene.

name: Paul Hallingby Jr.
headline: Paul Hallingby Jr., Banker, Dies at 85; Helped Develop Javits Center
abstract: Paul Hallingby Jr., an investment banker who helped develop the Jacob K. Javits Convention Center, died yesterday at his home in Sutton Place in Manhattan.     He was 85 and also had homes in Southampton and in Lyford Cay, Bahamas.

name: Israel Epstein
headline: Israel Epstein, Prominent Chinese Communist, Dies at 90
abstract: Israel Epstein, a journalist, author and propagandist for China whose passion for Communism was fueled in long interviews with Mao in the 1940's and was not dimmed by imprisonment during the Cultural Revolution, died last Thursday at a hospital in Beijing. He was 90.    His death was announced by the official New China News Agency.

name: Gershon Jacobson
profession: Founder and Editor of Yiddish Journal
headline: Gershon Jacobson, 70, Founder and Editor of Yiddish Journal, Is Dead
abstract: Gershon Jacobson, the founder, editor and publisher of Der Algemeiner Journal, one of the largest Yiddish-language weekly newspapers in North America, died on Sunday at NYU Downtown Hospital in Manhattan. He was 70 and lived in Brooklyn.    The cause was complications of diabetes, his son Simon said.

name: William Lieberman
headline: William Lieberman, 82, Prominent Curator, Dies
abstract: William S. Lieberman, a legendary museum figure who held top curatorial posts at both the Museum of Modern Art and the Metropolitan Museum of Art, steering major collections to the institutions, died in his sleep at his home in Manhattan on the night of May 31. He was 82.    The apparent cause was cardiopulmonary arrest, a museum official said.

name: George Mikan
headline: George Mikan, 80, Dominant Center, Dies
abstract: George Mikan, the Minneapolis Lakers center who was the first superstar in modern professional basketball and a player so big and so dominant that college and pro rules were changed in an effort to handcuff him, died Wednesday at a rehabilitation center in Scottsdale, Ariz. He was 80.    His death was announced by his family, The Associated Press said. He had been treated for diabetes and kidney failure for several years.

name: Forrest Perrin
headline: Forrest Perrin, 88, Pianist and Society Orchestra Leader, Dies
abstract: Forrest Perrin, a pianist and orchestra leader who for decades provided the soundtrack for society and fashion events, died on Friday at New York-Presbyterian Hospital. He was 88 and lived on the West Side of Manhattan.    The cause was pneumonia, his family said.

name: E. Harris Nober
profession: Created Alarm System for Hearing Impaired
headline: E. Harris Nober Dies at 77; Created Alarm System for Hearing Impaired
abstract: Dr. E.
