headline: Wellington Mara, the Patriarch of the N.F.L., Dies at 89
abstract: Wellington Mara, patriarch of National Football League, who served as ball boy for leather-helmeted 1925 Giants and later turned team--founded by his father--into one of marquee names in professional sports, dies at his home in Rye, NY, at age 89; chronology shows high points of Mara's life in NFL; photos, including one of Mara and coach Bill Parcells after winning 1987 Super Bowl (L)

name: Marshall Clagett
profession: Scholar on Science in Ancient Times
headline: Marshall Clagett, 89, Scholar on Science in Ancient Times, Is Dead
abstract: Marshall Clagett, a scholar of science in ancient Egypt and Greece and the way it was received in medieval Europe, died on Oct. 21 at a hospital in Princeton, N.J. He was 89 and lived in Princeton.     His death was announced by the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, where he was a professor emeritus in the Department of Historical Studies. He arrived to teach in 1964 and took emeritus status in 1986, but continued to publish, and at his death was working on the fourth and final volume of his ''Ancient Egyptian Science,'' the institute reported.

name: Enid A. Haupt
headline: Enid A. Haupt, Philanthropist, Dies at 99
abstract: Enid A. Haupt, whose philanthropy benefited libraries, museums and hospitals but who devoted much of her considerable fortune to creating public gardens and preserving horticultural institutions, died on Tuesday at her home in Greenwich, Conn. She was 99, and also kept a residence in Manhattan.      Her death was announced by her niece Cynthia Hazen Polsky.

name: Rong Yiren
headline: Rong Yiren, a Chinese Billionaire, Dies at 89
abstract: Rong Yiren, a wealthy entrepreneur and former vice president of China who in the 1970's was asked by Deng Xiaoping to help initiate some of the nation's earliest economic reforms, died Wednesday in Beijing. He was 89.     His death was reported by the New China News Agency.

name: Kathryn O. Scott
headline: Kathryn O. Scott, 94, Textile Work Pioneer, Dies
abstract: Kathryn O. Scott, a pioneer in the meticulous art of textile conservation whose accomplishments included doing Napoleon's personal laundry, died on Oct. 15 at her home in Manhattan. She was 94.     Her death was confirmed by Mary Ballard, the senior textile conservator at the Smithsonian Center for Materials Research and Education and a former protégée. Ms. Scott leaves no immediate survivors.

name: Alastair G. W. Cameron
headline: Alastair G. W. Cameron, 80, Theorist on Creation of Moon, Dies
abstract: Alastair G. W. Cameron, a Harvard astrophysicist who helped develop a revolutionary theory to explain how the Moon was formed, died Oct. 3 at his home in Tucson. He was 80.      The cause was heart failure, his family said.

name: Michael Gill
headline: Michael Gill, 81, Filmmaker Known for TV's 'Civilisation,' Dies
abstract: Michael Gill, a British television producer and director best known in this country for innovative ''authored documentary'' series like ''Civilisation'' (1969), featuring Lord Kenneth Clark, and ''America'' (1972), with Alistair Cooke, died on Oct. 20 at a London hospital. A London resident, he was 81.      The cause was complications of Alzheimer's disease, said Murray Grigor, a friend and associate.

name: Richard E. Smalley
headline: Richard E. Smalley, 62, Dies; Chemistry Nobel Winner
abstract: Richard E. Smalley, the Rice University chemistry professor who shared a Nobel Prize for discovering a new spherical form of carbon and championed the potential of nanotechnology to create a more sustainable economy, died Friday at 62 at the M. D. Anderson Cancer Center in Houston.     The cause was leukemia, a spokesman for Rice said.

name: Frederic Quitkin
headline: Dr. Frederic Quitkin, 68, Depression Expert
abstract: Dr. Frederic Quitkin, a psychiatrist whose research helped establish that certain kinds of depression could best be treated with medications and that schizophrenia was related to neurological impairments rather than problems of childhood, died on Oct. 9 in New York. He was 68.      The cause was pancreatic cancer, said his son, Dr. Matt Quitkin of Washington.

name: Phil Hays
headline: Phil Hays, Illustrator and Teacher, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Phil Hays, an illustrator and teacher, whose lush watercolor portraits of legendary blues artists like Bessie Smith and Billie Holiday for LP covers defined a distinctive graphic style of album art in the 1970's, died on Monday at his home in Los Angeles. He was 74.      Mr. Hays, who lived alone, was found in his apartment, said a friend, the illustrator James McMullan. The cause of death was not officially known, although he had been suffering from emphysema.

name: Advertising Executive
headline: Advertising Executive John Elliott Jr. Is Dead at 84
abstract: John Elliott Jr., who for 17 years led one of the world's largest advertising agencies, Ogilvy & Mather, died on Saturday at a hospital in Mount Kisco, N.Y. He was 84 and lived in Cross River, N.Y.     The cause was a cerebral hemorrhage, said his wife, Eleanor Thomas Elliott.

name: Marvin Chodorow
profession: Expert in the Use of Microwave Tubes
headline: Marvin Chodorow, 92, Expert in the Use of Microwave Tubes, Dies
abstract: Marvin Chodorow, an applied physicist and administrator at Stanford who helped refine the use of microwave tubes in improving radar, telecommunications, cancer treatments and other applications, died Oct. 17 at his home in Stanford, Calif. He was 92.      Dr. Chodorow's family confirmed his death.

name: Al Lopez
headline: Al Lopez, a Hall of Fame Manager, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Al Lopez, one of baseball's most prominent managers of the 1950's and the oldest member of the Baseball Hall of Fame, died yesterday in Tampa, Fla. He was 97 and had briefly returned to the spotlight this month when the Chicago White Sox franchise he managed to a pennant in 1959 finally returned to the World Series.     His death was announced by his son, Al Jr., who said he had been hospitalized since having a heart attack on Friday, The Associated Press reported.

name: Paul Reynard
profession: Art Teacher And Painter in New York
headline: Paul Reynard, 78, Art Teacher And Painter in New York, Dies
abstract: Paul Reynard, French-born painter who was active for more than three decades as artist and teacher in New York, dies at age 78 (M)

name: Endre Marton
profession: Reported on the '56 Uprising in Hungary
headline: Endre Marton, 95, Dies; Reported on the '56 Uprising in Hungary
abstract: Endre Marton, prize-winning journalist who sent first account of Hungarian uprising of 1956 just weeks after serving year in prison for covering events preceding it, dies at age 95 (M)

name: Skitch Henderson
headline: Skitch Henderson, 'Tonight' Show Conductor, Dies at 87
abstract: Skitch Henderson, the conductor, pianist and radio and television entertainer, provided both music and repartee for the "Tonight" show from 1954 to 1966.

name: Skitch Henderson
headline: Skitch Henderson Service
abstract: Memorial service for Skitch Henderson, Tonight show bandleader and founder of New York Pops, will be held in Carnegie Hall on Feb 6 (S)

name: Tony Jackson
headline: Tony Jackson, 65, Who Led St. John's Basketball, Dies
abstract: Tony Jackson, brilliant jump shooter and two-time all-American who led St John's University to championships of National Invitation Tournament and Holiday Festival in era when those tournaments showcased college basketball's finest talent, dies at age 65; photo (M)

name: Lloyd Bochner
profession: Actor of Stage, Screen and TV
headline: Lloyd Bochner, 81, Actor of Stage, Screen and TV, Dies
abstract: Lloyd Bocher, classically trained actor who played suave heroes and villains for more than 50 years in theater, television and film, dies at age 81; photo (M)

name: William O. Baker
profession: Adviser to Five Presidents About Scientific Matters
headline: William O. Baker, 90, an Adviser to Five Presidents About Scientific Matters, Dies
abstract: William O Baker, prominent scientist and former head of Bell Laboratories who advised five presidents on scientific matters, dies at age 90 (M)

name: William Baker
headline: William Baker, Who Righted a 1906 Army Racial Wrong, Dies at 86
abstract: Driven by a tale of racial injustice from his childhood, Mr. Baker dusted off an old case about a shooting spree in Texas. His findings reversed a ruling made nearly 70 years earlier.

name: Waldemar Nielsen
headline: Waldemar Nielsen, Expert on Philanthropy, Dies at 88
abstract: Waldemar Nielsen, influential and widely recognized expert on workings of charitable foundations who wrote exhaustive, critical analyses of America's foremost philanthropies, their goals and their methods, dies at age 88; photo (M)

name: William L. McLaughlin
headline: William L. McLaughlin Dies at 77; Helped Measure Radiation
abstract: William L McLaughlin, radiation scientist who devised accurate and widely used methods for measuring radiation absorbed by cancer patients and by many foods and commercial products, dies at age 77 (M)

name: R. C. Gorman
headline: R. C. Gorman, Painter of Strong Navajo Women, Dies
abstract: R. C. Gorman, an internationally prominent Navajo artist whose portraits of voluptuous women in flowing traditional dress embodied the American Southwest for collectors around the world, died on Thursday at a hospital in Albuquerque. A longtime resident of Taos, N.M., he was believed to be in his mid-70's.     Gov. Bill Richardson of New Mexico announced the death. The cause was pneumonia following a blood infection for which Mr. Gorman had been hospitalized since September.

name: Alan Pifer
headline: Alan Pifer Is Dead at 84; Led Carnegie Corporation
abstract: Alan Pifer, under whose guidance the Carnegie Corporation of New York adjusted its educational focus to a wider context -- social and racial justice -- in the 1960's and 1970's, died on Monday in Shelburne, Vt. A former resident of Greens Farms, Conn., he was 84.     His death was announced by the corporation, which he led from 1967 to 1982 after years as a leading program officer and acting president. Until 1979, he also presided over the corporation's sister organization, the Carnegie Foundation for the Advancement of Teaching, now based in Stanford, Calif.

name: C. DeLores Tucker
headline: C. DeLores Tucker, a Voice for Minorities and Women, Is Dead at 78
abstract: C. DeLores Tucker, an outspoken advocate for minority and women's rights who marched arm in arm with Martin Luther King Jr. at Selma, Ala., and campaigned against profanity-ridden rap music lyrics, died on Oct. 12 at a rehabilitation center in Philadelphia. She was 78.     Peter Bailey, editor of ''Vital Issues: The Journal of African-American Speeches,'' which Mrs. Tucker founded, confirmed her death.

name: Emile Capouya
headline: Emile Capouya, 80, Publisher Who Wrote Books Late in Life, Dies
abstract: Emile Capouya, an essayist, critic and publisher who late in life published his first story collection, ''In the Sparrow Hills,'' died on Oct. 13 at his home in East Meredith, N.Y. He was 80.     His death was announced by his family.

name: E. Stewart Williams
headline: E. Stewart Williams, 95, 'Desert Modern' Architect, Dies
abstract: E. Stewart Williams, an architect whose many works in Palm Springs, Calif., including a home for Frank Sinatra, helped define what became known as the Desert Modern style, died on Sept. 10. He was 95.     He died at his home in Palm Springs, said Michael J. Stern, an artist who is writing a book on Mr. Williams's architecture.

name: Chester Cooper
profession: Player in Diplomacy for Two Decades
headline: Chester Cooper, 88, a Player in Diplomacy for Two Decades, Is Dead
abstract: Chester L. Cooper, a retired United States diplomat who in the 1950's and 60's was a backstage player in many of the most critical negotiations of the cold war, died on Oct. 30 in Washington. He was 88.     During his years in public service, Mr. Cooper often worked, as he later wrote, ''as deputy or special assistant to, of or for somebody or something.'' He held senior positions with the Central Intelligence Agency, the National Security Council, the State Department and other agencies.

name: John Fowles
headline: John Fowles, 79, British Postmodernist Who Tested Novel's Conventions, Dies
abstract: John Fowles, the British writer whose teasing, multilayered fiction explored the tensions between free will and the constraints of society, even as it played with traditional novelistic conventions and challenged readers to find their own interpretations, died on Saturday at his home in Lyme Regis, England. He was 79.     His death was announced by his publisher, Random House UK. No cause was given, but Random House said Mr. Fowles, who suffered a stroke in the late 1980's and had heart problems, had been ill for some time.

name: Maurice Rosenfield
headline: Maurice Rosenfield, 91, Stage Producer and Noted Lawyer, Dies
abstract: Maurice Rosenfield, a civil liberties lawyer turned theatrical producer who helped bring several well-received shows to Broadway, including the Tony Award-winning musical ''Barnum,'' died on Oct. 30 in Lake Forest, Ill. He was 91 and lived in Glencoe, Ill.     The cause was heart failure, his family said.

name: Milton Elkin
headline: Dr. Milton Elkin, 89, a Chief Radiologist, Dies
abstract: Milton Elkin, who founded the radiology department at Albert Einstein College of Medicine in 1954 and led it for 32 years, died on Oct. 31 in West Hartford, Conn. A former resident of Scarsdale, N.Y., he was 89.      His death was announced by the medical school, an affiliate of Yeshiva University. His family said the cause was complications of Alzheimer's disease.

name: Thomas P. Ronan
headline: Thomas P. Ronan, 96, Times Correspondent
abstract: Thomas P. Ronan, a former foreign correspondent for The New York Times, died on Oct. 31 in Kennett Square, Pa. He was 96.     His daughter Catherine confirmed the death.

name: Gordon A. Craig
headline: Gordon A. Craig, Historian Who Was an Expert on Germany, Dies at 91
abstract: Gordon A. Craig, a leading interpreter of modern Germany to the English-speaking world, died on Oct. 30 in Portola Valley, Calif. He was 91.     The cause was heart failure, according to Stanford University, where he taught from 1961 until retiring in 1979.

name: Beland Honderich
headline: Beland Honderich, Publisher Who Transformed Toronto Star, Dies at 86
abstract: Beland H. Honderich, the publisher and editor who transformed The Toronto Star from a publication focused on crime and sensationalism into an influential newspaper with Canada's largest circulation, died on Tuesday in Vancouver, British Columbia. He was 86.     The cause was complications of a stroke, his son John Honderich said.

name: K. R. Narayanan
headline: K. R. Narayanan Dies at 85; 'Untouchable' India President
abstract: Kocheril Raman Narayanan, India's first Dalit, or ''untouchable,'' president, died in a military hospital here on Wednesday evening, a Defense Ministry spokesman said. He was 85, according to the Press Trust of India, and he had been suffering from pneumonia and kidney failure.     More than half a century after Gandhi led India to independence with a vision of ridding the country of its ancient system of caste discrimination, Mr. Narayanan, a member of Hinduism's lowest caste, assumed the office of president on July 25, 1997.

name: Fernando Bujones
headline: Fernando Bujones, 50, International Ballet Star, Dies
abstract: Fernando Bujones, whose pure classical technique, sheer power and bold temperament made him one of the first American-born male dancers to become an international ballet superstar, died early Thursday in Miami.      He was 50 and had two homes in Florida: in Orlando, where he was artistic director of the Orlando Ballet for the past five years, and in Hallandale, near Miami.

name: Patrick Lichfield
headline: Obituary: Lord Patrick Lichfield, 66, photographer of royal family

name: Alan A. Reich
profession: Leader in Fighting for the Disabled
headline: Alan A. Reich, 75, a Leader in Fighting for the Disabled, Dies
abstract: Alan A. Reich, the founder and president emeritus of the National Organization on Disability, a voice in public forums for those disabled in any way, died on Tuesday at his home in McLean, Va. He was 75.     His death was announced on the Web site of the organization, which he ran until last April. The cause was heart failure resulting from longstanding respiratory problems, said Michael R. Deland, his successor as president.

name: Dorothy W. Raphaelson
headline: Dorothy W. Raphaelson, A Ziegfeld Girl, Dies at 100
abstract: Dorothy Wegman Raphaelson, who 80 years ago in chiffon, silk, feathers and lace floated across Jazz Age stages as a Ziegfeld Girl and went on to outlive all but one of her fellow dancers, died on Monday at her home in Manhattan. She was 100.     The cause was complications of a long-term heart ailment, her son, Joel Raphaelson, said.

name: Leonard Block
headline: Leonard Block, 93, Chief of Drug Company, Is Dead
abstract: Leonard N. Block, the retired chairman and chief executive of the Block Drug Company, a philanthropist and a former treasurer of Lincoln Center, died on Wednesday at his home on the Upper East Side. He was 93.     The death was announced by his family, who said he had suffered from Alzheimer's disease for many years.

name: Peter F. Drucker
profession: Pioneer in Social and Management Theory
headline: Peter F. Drucker, a Pioneer in Social and Management Theory, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Peter F. Drucker, the political economist and author, whose view that big business and nonprofit enterprises were the defining innovation of the 20th century led him to pioneering social and management theories, died yesterday at his home in Claremont, Calif. He was 95.     His death was announced by Claremont Graduate University.

name: Ruth Clement Bond
headline: Ruth Clement Bond, 101, Quilter and Civic Leader, Is Dead
abstract: Ruth Clement Bond, an educator and civic leader who in the mid-1930's, in her first and only foray into quilt design, helped transform the American quilt from a utilitarian bedcovering into a work of avant-garde social commentary, died on Oct. 24 at her daughter's home in Manhattan. She was 101.     Her death was confirmed by her family.

name: Ernest Crichlow
headline: Ernest Crichlow, 91, Lyrical Painter, Dies
abstract: Ernest Crichlow, influential Harlem Renaissance painter, dies at age of 91 (M)

name: Catherine M. Pessino
headline: Catherine M. Pessino, Naturalist and Educator, Dies at 80
abstract: Catherine M Pessino, naturalist and educator who was on staff of American Museum of Natural Hitory for many years, dies at age of 80; photo (M)

name: Graham Payn
headline: Graham Payn, 87, Debonair Actor, Dies
abstract: Graham Payn, debonair actor and singer, died Nov 4 at age of 87 (M)

name: Daniel Gribbon
headline: Daniel Gribbon, Commercial Lawyer, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Daniel McNamara Gribbon, former managing partner of the prominent Washington law firm Covington & Burling, died on Nov. 3 at his home in Washington. He was 88.     The cause was complications of kidney disease, his daughter Diana said.

name: Raymond Hains
headline: Raymond Hains, 78, French Artist, Dies
abstract: Raymond Hains, one of last surviving members of influential French Nouveaux Realistes group of artists, died Oct 28 at age of 78 (M)

name: Michael Mendelson
headline: Michael Mendelson, 63, Asset Manager, Dies
abstract: Michael Mendelson, former president of the investment firm Oppenheimer & Company, died on Nov. 4 at his home in Manhattan. He was 63.     The cause was stomach cancer, his family said.

name: Theodore Puck
profession: Leader in Growing Cells for Research
headline: Theodore Puck, 89, Leader in Growing Cells for Research, Dies
abstract: Theodore T Puck, geneticist who devised important tests for studying cell damage from radiation, dies at age of 89 (M)

name: Vine Deloria Jr.
headline: Vine Deloria Jr., Champion of Indian Rights, Dies at 72
abstract: Vine Deloria Jr., a Standing Rock Sioux who burst into the American consciousness in 1969 with his book ''Custer Died for Your Sins'' and later amplified his message through 20 more books about the Native American experience, died on Sunday, a family friend said.     He was 72 and lived in Golden, just west of Denver, and had recently been hospitalized with an aortic aneurysm.

name: James Fyfe
headline: James Fyfe, 63, Criminologist and Police Training Director, Is Dead
abstract: James J. Fyfe, an author and nationally recognized expert on the use of force by the police, and the top training official in the New York Police Department since 2002, died on Saturday in Princeton, N.J. He was 63.     He died at University Medical Center in Princeton after being treated for cancer for more than a year, said his wife, Candace S. McCoy.

name: Preston Robert Tisch
profession: Owner of Loews Hotels and Giants
headline: Preston Robert Tisch, Owner of Loews Hotels and Giants, Dies
abstract: Preston Robert Tisch, who with his older brother built a multibillion-dollar business empire and who himself was postmaster general, half-owner of the New York Giants football team and leader of many of the city's top business groups, died yesterday at his home in Manhattan. He was 79 and also had a home in Harrison, N.Y.     The cause was a brain tumor, said Jeffrey Stewart, spokesman for the family.

name: Adrian P. Rogers
headline: Adrian P. Rogers, 74, Leader of Conservative Baptist Group, Dies
abstract: The Rev. Adrian P. Rogers, the three-time president of the Southern Baptist Convention who led a conservative takeover of the powerful denomination that helped usher in a resurgence of conservative Christians on pulpits and in politics, died on Tuesday in Memphis. He was 74.      His death was announced on the Web site of a ministry he founded, Love Worth Finding, www.lwf.org. He had cancer and pneumonia, according to The Baptist Press News.

name: Ralph Edwards
headline: Ralph Edwards, TV Pioneer, Dies at 92
abstract: Ralph Edwards, broadcast pioneer who created television shows Truth or Consequences and This Is Your Life, dies at age 92; photo (M)

name: R. Gaynor McCown
headline: R. Gaynor McCown, 45, Who Led Education Panel, Dies
abstract: R. Gaynor McCown, the executive director of the Teaching Commission, a bipartisan advocacy group of leaders in business, government, philanthropy and education, died on Monday at her home on the Upper East Side of Manhattan. She was 45.     Her death was announced by the group's founder and chairman, Louis V. Gerstner Jr., a former chairman of the I.B.M. Corporation. The cause was bile duct cancer, the commission said.

name: Nobelist Henry Taube
headline: Nobelist Henry Taube Is Dead at 89
abstract: Henry Taube, who won a Nobel Prize in Chemistry for describing how electrons hop between molecules during chemical reactions, died on Wednesday at his home on the campus of Stanford University, where he had taught for two decades. He was 89.     Stanford announced his death yesterday.

name: Paul L. Ward
headline: Paul L. Ward, 94, Historian and College President, Dies
abstract: Paul Langdon Ward, a historian and former head of the American Historical Association who was president of Sarah Lawrence College in the 1960's, died last Sunday at his retirement home in Gwynedd, Pa. He was 94.     The death was announced by his family and on the association's Web site.

name: Dutch Hiller
profession: Speedy Ranger on 1940 Stanley Cup Team
headline: Dutch Hiller, 90, Speedy Ranger on 1940 Stanley Cup Team
abstract: Dutch Hiller, one of the three surviving players from the Rangers' 1940 Stanley Cup hockey champions, died Saturday at a hospital in Glendale, Calif. He was 90 and lived in Montrose, Calif.     The cause was congestive heart failure, his daughter Patricia Ornelas said.

name: Julius Edelstein
headline: Julius Edelstein, 93, Who Devised CUNY's Open Admissions, Dies
abstract: Julius C. C. Edelstein, a primary architect of open admissions at the City University of New York in the late 1960's, died on Friday morning at New York Hospital. He was 93.      His daughter, Suzy E. E. Edelstein, said the cause was complications of pneumonia.

name: Red Sarachek
headline: Red Sarachek, Innovator as Yeshiva Basketball Coach, Dies at 93
abstract: Red Sarachek, the Yeshiva University basketball coach for a quarter-century who was known for his innovative tactics in a program far from the sport's limelight, died Monday at his home in Deerfield Beach, Fla. He was 93.     His death was announced by Yeshiva.

name: Joseph Monserrat
profession: Leader in Efforts to Unify Latinos
headline: Joseph Monserrat, 84, Leader in Efforts to Unify Latinos, Dies
abstract: Joseph Monserrat, a leader among Puerto Ricans in New York and the continental United States beginning in the days of their mass migration in the 1950's, died last Sunday at a nursing home in Greenwich Village. He was 84 and lived in the Chelsea neighborhood of Manhattan.     His family said he died after a long illness.

name: Rutherford Aris
headline: Rutherford Aris, 76, Chemical Engineer, Dies
abstract: Rutherford Aris, a distinguished chemical engineer who, as the result of a mix-up three decades ago, had a short-lived but supremely accomplished alter ego -- Aris Rutherford -- with an official entry in Who's Who and one of the most enviable jobs in the world, died on Nov. 2 in Edina, Minn. He was 76.     The cause was complications of Parkinson's disease, according to the University of Minnesota, where he was Regents professor emeritus of chemical engineering and classics.

name: Dorothy Nolte
headline: Dorothy Nolte, 81, Author of Parenting Poem, Dies
abstract: Dorothy Law Nolte, a writer and family counselor whose ubiquitous inspirational poem, ''Children Learn What They Live,'' was photocopied, circulated, anthologized and affixed to refrigerator doors worldwide for nearly two decades before she claimed rightful authorship of it in the 1970's, died on Nov. 6 at her home in Rancho Santa Margarita, Calif. She was 81.     The cause was cancer, her family said.

name: Hal Anger
headline: Hal Anger Dies at 85; Invented Diagnostic Cameras
abstract: Hal O. Anger, an electrical engineer in the field of nuclear medicine who invented diagnostic cameras allowing doctors to view metabolic processes occurring inside the human body, died on Oct. 31 at his home in Berkeley, Calif. He was 85.      The cause was heart failure, said his brother, Clifford, of Canmore, Alberta.

name: Mike Mikell
profession: Owner of an Influential R&B and Jazz Club
headline: Mike Mikell, 80, Owner of an Influential R&B and Jazz Club, Dies
abstract: Mike Mikell, whose Upper West Side club, Mikell's, was a vital part of New York City rhythm-and-blues and jazz scenes for two decades, died on Friday in Kingston, N.Y. He was 80 and lived in Woodstock, N.Y.      The cause was cancer and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, known and Lou Gehrig's disease, his wife, Pat, said.

name: Steve Belichick
headline: Steve Belichick, Coach Who Wrote the Book on Scouting, Dies at 86
abstract: Steve Belichick, a college football coach and celebrated scout for 43 years and the father of New England Patriots Coach Bill Belichick, died of heart failure Saturday night at his home in Annapolis, Md. He was 86.     ''I found out about it the middle of last night,'' Bill Belichick told The Associated Press yesterday after the Patriots defeated New Orleans, 24-17, in Foxborough, Mass. ''I coached this game with a heavy heart.''

name: Lou Myers
headline: Lou Myers, Cartoonist With a Satiric Style, Dies at 90
abstract: Lou Myers, a satiric artist and graphic essayist whose expressive style helped modernize cartoons in advertisements and major American magazines, died yesterday at his home in Cortlandt Manor, N.Y. He was 90.      The cause of death was spindle cell carcinoma, said his daughter-in-law Alyse Myers, vice president for marketing services at The New York Times.

name: Derek Lamb
headline: Derek Lamb, 69, Short-Film Maker, Dies
abstract: Derek Lamb, an Academy Award-winning writer, director and producer of animated films, died on Nov. 5 in Poulsbo, Wash., where he was visiting a friend. He was 69 and lived in Cambridge, Mass.     The cause was cancer, said Janet Perlman, Mr. Lamb's former wife and a longtime collaborator.

name: Ben A. Franklin
headline: Ben A. Franklin, 78, Reporter for The Times, Dies
abstract: Ben A. Franklin, a former national correspondent for The New York Times, died on Saturday at his home in Garrett Park, Md. He was 78.     The cause was lung cancer, his family said.

name: Conrad Duberstein
headline: Conrad Duberstein, 90, Bankruptcy Judge, Dies
abstract: Conrad B. Duberstein, the chief judge of the United States Bankruptcy Court in Brooklyn since 1984, died on Friday at his home in Brooklyn. He was 90.     His death was announced by the court, on which he had continued to serve as chief judge on a year-to-year basis since nominally retiring in 1995.

name: John Campo
headline: John Campo, Trainer of 1981 Derby Winner, Is Dead at 67
abstract: John Campo, a New York-based trainer for three decades who saddled Pleasant Colony, the winner of the 1981 Kentucky Derby and Preakness Stakes, died on Nov. 13 at his home in Hewlett, N.Y. He was 67.     His death was announced by his son Paul, who said he had been treated for diabetes and strokes.

name: Link Wray
headline: Link Wray, 76, a Guitarist With Raw Rockabilly Sound, Dies
abstract: Link Wray, a rockabilly guitarist whose raw sound and inventive techniques influenced musicians from the early days of rock 'n' roll into the punk era, died on Nov. 5 at his home in Copenhagen. He was 76.     The cause was heart failure, said his wife, Olive.

name: Ruth M. Siems
headline: Ruth M. Siems, Inventor of Stuffing, Dies at 74
abstract: Ruth M Siems, retired home economist whose best-known innovation was Stove Top stuffing, Thanksgiving mainstay, dies at age 74; photo (S)

name: Hugh Sidey
headline: Hugh Sidey, Who Covered the Presidency for Time, Dies at 78
abstract: Hugh Sidey, who covered American presidency for Time magazine, dies at age 78; photo (M)

name: Sybil Shearer
profession: Dancer of the Spiritual and the Human
headline: Sybil Shearer, 93, Dancer of the Spiritual and the Human, Dies
abstract: Sybil Shearer, unpredictable individualist of modern dance, dies at age 93; photo (S)

name: Paul Roazen
headline: Paul Roazen, 69, Scholar Who Found Flaws in Freud, Dies
abstract: Paul Roazen, political scientist and chronicler of development of psychoanalysis who explored Sigmund Freud's complex relationships with his family, students and adherents, dies at age 69; photo (M)

name: Chris Whitley
headline: Chris Whitley, 45, Songwriter Whose Music Blended Genres, Dies
abstract: Chris Whitley, an innovative songwriter and guitarist who played traditional blues as well as hybrids made with the sounds of electronic dance music, died on Sunday at a friend's home near Houston. He was 45 and lived in New York.     The cause was lung cancer, said his brother, Daniel.

name: James King
profession: Tenor Known for Strauss and Wagner
headline: James King, 80, Tenor Known for Strauss and Wagner, Dies
abstract: James King, an American heldentenor whose bright, ringing voice and fluent high notes captivated critics and audiences in leading European opera houses in the 1960's, died on Sunday in Naples, Fla., where he had retired. He was 80.     The cause was a heart attack, according to Indiana University, where he taught music and voice from 1984 to 2002. His death was first announced by the Vienna Staatsoper, of which he was an honorary member. It was also noted by the Deutsche Oper in Berlin, where he had his first resident appointment in 1962 as a nearly unknown singer from the United States, and at the Metropolitan Opera, where he took on some of the most challenging tenor roles.

name: Joseph Thorndike
profession: Editor at Life and Other Magazines
headline: Joseph Thorndike, 92, Editor at Life and Other Magazines, Dies
abstract: Joseph J. Thorndike, a former managing editor of Life magazine who in 1954 helped found American Heritage magazine, died Tuesday at his home in Harwich, Mass. He was 92.     The cause was congestive heart failure and complications of Alzheimer's disease, his son John said.

name: Kingsbury Browne
headline: Kingsbury Browne, Land Preserver, Dies at 82
abstract: Kingsbury Browne, prominent Boston tax lawyer and outdoorsman, dies at 82 (S)

name: Ronald Rivlin
headline: Ronald Rivlin, 90, Expert on Properties of Rubber, Dies
abstract: Ronald S Rivlin, applied mathematician who conducted pioneering studies on elastic properties of rubber and other materials, dies Oct 4 at 90 (S)

name: George Best
headline: George Best, 59, Soccer's First Pop Icon, Dies
abstract: George Best, an Irish soccer star who captivated the public with his flamboyant skill on the field and his playboy exploits off the field, died today.

name: Frank Gatski
profession: Hall of Fame Lineman for Powerful Browns
headline: Frank Gatski, 84, Hall of Fame Lineman for Powerful Browns, Is Dead
abstract: Frank Gatski, the Hall of Fame center on the Cleveland Browns teams that played in 10 consecutive professional football championship games in the decade after World War II, died Tuesday at a nursing home in Morgantown, W.Va. He was 84.     His death was announced by his daughter Anne Harman.

name: Gopal Godse
headline: Obituary: Gopal Godse, 86, conspired to kill Gandhi

name: Ed Peterson
headline: Ed Peterson, 100, Seedsman Who Collected California Wildflowers, Dies
abstract: Ed Peterson, who prowled the deserts, mountains and meadows of Southern California, often on his hands and knees, to collect wildflower seeds as part of a foundation's mission to preserve the area's native flora, died on Nov. 14 at a nursing home in Los Angeles. He was 100.     The death was confirmed by his brother, Wilbur.

name: Cornelius Owens
headline: Cornelius Owens, Telephone Executive, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Cornelius W. Owens, a longtime employee of AT&T who was president of its subsidiary, the New York Telephone Company, during one of its most trying periods, died Nov. 14 in Atlanta. He was 92.     The cause was pulmonary fibrosis, his family said.

name: Harry Joe Brown Jr.
headline: Harry Joe Brown Jr., 71, Innovative Developer, Dies
abstract: Harry Joe Brown Jr., a real estate executive whose birth into Hollywood royalty presaged the pizazz he generated by enlisting 34 leading architects to design one house each for a Hamptons residential development, died on Wednesday at his Manhattan home. He was 71.     The cause was complications of prostate cancer, his family said in a statement. Mr. Brown also had a home in West Palm Beach.

name: George T. Conklin
headline: George T. Conklin, Guardian Life Chief, 90, Dies
abstract: George Taylor Conklin Jr., a former chief executive of the Guardian Life Insurance Company of America, died on Nov. 4 at his home in Port Washington, N.Y. He was 90.     His death was announced by Guardian Life, one of the country's oldest and largest life insurance companies, which is based in Manhattan. He retired as chief executive in 1980 and retired from the board of directors at the end of 1995, after nearly 57 years with the company.

name: Michael E. Vacek
headline: Michael E. Vacek, 53, Lawyer and Lobbyist, Is Dead
abstract: Michael E Vacek, lawyer widely considered one of most influential lobbyists in Albany, dies at age 53 (M)

name: Maurice S. Paprin
profession: Builder and Advocate for Liberal Causes
headline: Maurice S. Paprin, 85, Builder and Advocate for Liberal Causes, Is Dead
abstract: Maurice S Paprin, retired builder who was also liberal social activist, dies at age 85 (M)

name: Constance Cummings
headline: Constance Cummings, 95, Movie and Stage Actress, Dies
abstract: Constance Cummings, versatile American actress who lived mostly in England, dies at age 95; photos (M)

name: Vic Power
profession: Pioneer Latino And First Baseman With Flair
headline: Vic Power, 78, Pioneer Latino And First Baseman With Flair
abstract: Vic Power, the stylish-fielding first baseman who was one of the first Latino stars in the major leagues in the decade after World War II, died yesterday at a hospital in Bayamón, P.R. He was 78.      The cause was cancer, his sister Carmen Pellot Power told The Associated Press.

name: Stan Berenstain
headline: Stan Berenstain, Co-Creator of Those Fuzzy Bears, Dies at 82
abstract: Stan Berenstain, who with his wife, Jan, churned out more than 250 books showing how the warm and fuzzy Berenstain Bears -- Mama, Papa, Brother and Sister -- confronted and learned from life's little crises, died on Saturday in Doylestown, Pa. He was 82.     The cause was lymphoma, Mrs. Berenstain said.

name: Fanny Ellison
headline: Fanny Ellison, 93, Dies; Helped Husband Edit 'Invisible Man'
abstract: Fanny McConnell Ellison, who was involved in the theater, politics and civil rights before she married Ralph Ellison and helped him edit his masterpiece, ''Invisible Man,'' died on Nov. 19 at St. Luke's-Roosevelt Hospital Center in Manhattan. She was 93.     The cause was complications of hip surgery, said John F. Callahan, Ellison's literary executor.

name: Lewis Horowitz
headline: Lewis Horowitz, 70, Promoter of Financial Futures Trading, Dies
abstract: Lewis J. Horowitz, who helped usher in a new wave of high-octane financial trading as chairman of the New York Futures Exchange, died on Friday at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center in Manhattan. He was 70 and lived on the Upper East Side of Manhattan.     The cause was gall bladder cancer, said his wife, Jo-Ann Malkin Horowitz.

name: Thomas R. Dawber
headline: Thomas R. Dawber, 92, Dies; First Director of Heart Study
abstract: Dr. Thomas Royle Dawber, who led the revolutionary Framingham Heart Study that identified the major risk factors for heart disease, died Nov. 23 in Naples, Fla. He was 92.     He had Alzheimer's disease and was at a long-term care center, said his daughter, Dr. Nancy H. Dawber.

name: Clive Bradley
headline: Clive Bradley Dies at 69; Arranged Trinidadian Steel-Drum Music
abstract: Clive Bradley, whose arrangements for steel-drum orchestras in Trinidad and New York City won championships from 1970 to 2005, died on Saturday in Port of Spain, Trinidad. He was 69.      He died four days after a stroke, said Rawlston Charles, who owns the store and record label Charlie's Records in Bedford-Stuyvesant and was a longtime friend.

name: Frederic B. Vogel
headline: Frederic B. Vogel Is Dead; Taught Broadway Production
abstract: Frederic B Vogel, founder of Commercial Theater Institute, teaching program for prospective Broadway producers, and expert on theater management, dies; family estimates he was in his 70's (M)

name: Michael Evans
headline: Michael Evans, Photographer of Ronald Reagan, Dies at 61
abstract: Michael A W Evans, photographer whose iconic picture of Ronald Reagan in cowboy hat was on covers of several news magazines, dies at age 61; photo (M)

name: Cornell Mayer
profession: Pioneer in the Study of the Planets
headline: Cornell Mayer, 83, Pioneer in the Study of the Planets, Dies
abstract: Cornell H. Mayer, a pioneer in radio astronomy who found the first signs of searingly hot temperatures on the surface of Venus, died on Nov. 19 at his home in Alexandria, Va. He was 83.     The cause of death was congestive heart failure, said his wife, Carey Whitehead Mayer.

name: Peter D. Eimas
headline: Peter D. Eimas, Expert in How Infants Learn, Dies at 70
abstract: Peter D. Eimas, a Brown University scientist who found that babies can distinguish different sounds of speech as early as their first month and published his findings in a groundbreaking study explaining how infants acquire language, died Oct. 28 at his home in Providence, R.I. He was 70.      His death came after a long illness, his family said.

name: Franz Jolowicz
headline: Franz Jolowicz, 86, Dies; Owned a Noted Record Store
abstract: Franz Jolowicz, the owner of the former Discophile record shop, a Greenwich Village institution that was for decades a mecca for classical record collectors, from the ardent to the insatiable to the merely obsessive, died on Nov. 8 at his home in the Village. He was 86.     The cause was complications of lung cancer, said Pat Payandeh, a longtime friend. Mr. Jolowicz leaves no immediate survivors.

name: Msgr. Frederick McManus
headline: Msgr. Frederick McManus, 82, Expert in Catholic Canon Law, Dies
abstract: Msgr. Frederick R. McManus, a retired dean of canon law at Catholic University of America who helped draft revisions to the Roman Catholic liturgy at the Second Vatican Council in the 1960's, died Nov. 27 in Boston. He was 82 and lived at the Boston archdiocesan retirement home, Regina Cleri.     His death was announced by the Archdiocese of Boston.

name: Howard Gotlieb
headline: Howard Gotlieb, an Archivist With Persistence, Dies at 79
abstract: Howard B. Gotlieb, a Boston University archivist who cajoled, charmed, wheedled and -- most effectively, he said -- groveled to snare the papers of notables like the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and Bette Davis, not to mention Fred Astaire's dancing shoes, died Thursday at a Boston hospital. He was 79.     The cause was complications of surgery, the university said.

name: Reginald R. Myers
headline: Reginald R. Myers, Retired Marine Corps Officer, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Col. Reginald R. Myers, a retired Marine Corps officer who was awarded the Medal of Honor for leading an assault up an icy Korean hill in late 1950, died Oct. 23 in West Palm Beach, Fla. He was 85 and had lived in Jupiter, Fla.      His death was confirmed on the Web site of the corps' History and Museums Division.

name: Liu Binyan
headline: Liu Binyan, a Fierce Insider Critic of China, Dies at 80
abstract: Liu Binyan, the forceful dissident writer who repeatedly exposed official corruption and openly challenged the Chinese Communist Party to reform itself before and after he was exiled to the United States in the late 1980's, died Monday.     He was 80 years old and lived in East Windsor, N.J.

name: Peter Haas
headline: Peter Haas, 86, Executive During Levi Strauss Heyday, Dies
abstract: Peter Edgar Haas Sr., who with his brother Walter engineered the explosive growth of the family business, Levi Strauss, into the world's biggest maker of brand-name jeans, died Saturday at his home in San Francisco. He was 86.      His death was announced by Levi Strauss & Company, which he joined in 1945 and served as president, chairman and, finally, chairman emeritus. His chief contributions were in the company's financial and manufacturing operations and in its social and charitable activities.

name: H. L. Strock
headline: H. L. Strock, 87, Director of Horror Films, Dies
abstract: Herbert L. Strock, a television producer and director who directed B-movies like ''I Was a Teenage Frankenstein,'' ''How to Make a Monster'' and ''The Crawling Hand,'' died here on Wednesday. He was 87.     The cause was heart failure after a car accident, according to his daughter, Leslie Mitchner.

name: George Baker III
headline: George Baker III, 66, Financier and Pilot, Is Presumed Dead
abstract: George F. Baker III, the retired financier who has been lost since last Thursday, when the small plane he was flying disappeared off Nantucket, and is now presumed to be dead, was the senior trustee of the George F. Baker Trust, a family philanthropy. Mr. Baker was 66 and lived in Houston, Nantucket and, formerly, Manhattan.     An experienced pilot, Mr. Baker was at the controls of a twin-engine Beechcraft Baron when the plane, approaching Nantucket, disappeared from radar Thursday afternoon after a flight from Teterboro Airport in New Jersey. He was believed to be alone in the plane, according to the Federal Aviation Administration.

name: Frederik Philips
headline: Frederik Philips Dies at 100; Businessman Saved Dutch Jews
abstract: Frederik Jacques Philips, the former president of the Dutch electronics giant that bears his family's name, who was credited with saving hundreds of Jews during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands in World War II, died on Monday. He was 100.     The cause was pneumonia and complications from a fall last week, said Rene Westbroek, a company spokesman.

name: Charly Gaul
profession: Star Climber in Cycling During the 1950's
headline: Charly Gaul, 72, Star Climber in Cycling During the 1950's, Is Dead
abstract: Charly Gaul, one of the great climbers in bicycle racing history and the winner of the Tour de France and the Giro d'Italia nearly half a century ago, died in his native Luxembourg on Tuesday. He was 72.     Announcing the news in Paris, Tour de France organizers said he died in a hospital after a fall at his home. Gaul had suffered from Alzheimer's disease for several years.

name: Constance L. Hays
profession: Business Reporter at Times and an Author
headline: Constance L. Hays, 44, Business Reporter at Times and an Author, Dies
abstract: Constance L. Hays, a reporter for The New York Times for nearly two decades, died on Monday at Calvary Hospital in the Bronx. She was 44 and lived in Manhattan.     The cause was cancer, her husband, John Hays, said.

name: Frederick L. Ashworth
headline: Frederick L. Ashworth, 93, Atomic Bomb Handler, Dies
abstract: Vice Adm. Frederick L. Ashworth, a Navy weapons specialist who was the crewman in control of the atomic bomb dropped on Nagasaki, Japan, in World War II's climactic strike, died Saturday at a hospital in Scottsdale, Ariz. He was 93 and lived in Santa Fe, N.M.      The cause was complications of an aortic aneurysm, his son Frederick Jr. said.

name: Harold D. Shapiro
headline: Harold D. Shapiro, 78, Law Firm Chairman, Dies
abstract: Harold D. Shapiro, a partner in the law firm of Sonnenschein Nath & Rosenthal and its first chairman, died last Thursday in Evanston, Ill. He was 78 and lived in Wilmette, Ill.     His death was announced on the Web site of the firm. The cause was a ruptured aneurysm.

name: Edward L. Masry
headline: Edward L. Masry, 73, Pugnacious Lawyer, Dies
abstract: Edward L. Masry, a flamboyantly pugnacious lawyer who won millions from a utility in a toxic pollution suit and was portrayed by the actor Albert Finney in the 2000 movie ''Erin Brockovich,'' died on Monday at a hospital in Thousand Oaks, Calif. He was 73.     The cause was complications of diabetes, his son Louis told The Associated Press.

name: Kalman Ruttenstein
headline: Kalman Ruttenstein, 69, Who Kept Bloomingdale's Chic, Dies
abstract: Kalman Ruttenstein, fashion director at Bloomingdale's, whose instinct for trends was so keen and enthusiasm for promotion so vigorous that he frequently upstaged even his more famous designers, dies at age 69; photos (M)

name: Bud Carson
headline: Bud Carson, 75, Innovator With Steel Curtain Defenses
abstract: Bud Carson, renowned National Football League strategist who devised Pittsburgh Steelers' Steel Curtain defenses of 1970's, dies at age 75; photo (M)

name: Atsuko Tanaka
headline: Atsuko Tanaka, 73, Artist Who Challenged Convention, Dies
abstract: Atsuko Tanaka, one of Japan's most important avant-garde artists, died on Dec. 3 at a hospital near her home in Nara, Japan. She was 73.     The cause was pneumonia, said Midori Nishizawa of the Paula Cooper Gallery, which represents her work in New York. Ms. Tanaka had been hospitalized since being injured in an automobile accident last spring.

name: Roger Shattuck
headline: Roger Shattuck, Scholar, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Roger Shattuck, a polyglot scholar and writer whose many subjects ranged from the emergence of modernism to whether some knowledge might be too dangerous to know, died on Thursday at his home in Lincoln, Vt. He was 82.     The cause was prostate cancer, his daughter Patricia said.

name: Tommy Hanneford
profession: Performer in Longtime Family Circus Troupe
headline: Tommy Hanneford, 78, Performer in Longtime Family Circus Troupe, Dies
abstract: Tommy Hanneford of the Royal Hanneford Circus, known as ''the funniest man on horseback,'' died here on Monday. He was 78.     His death followed a short illness, said his wife, Gertrude, who was also co-owner and a producer of the circus, which they formed with Mr. Hanneford's sister in 1965.

name: Robert Sheckley
headline: Robert Sheckley, 77, Writer of Satirical Science Fiction, Is Dead
abstract: Robert Sheckley, a writer of science fiction whose disarmingly playful stories pack a nihilistic subtext, died yesterday in Poughkeepsie. He was 77 and lived in Red Hook, N.Y.      The cause was complications of a brain aneurysm, said his former wife, Ziva Kwitney. Mr. Sheckley wrote more than 15 novels and around 400 short stories; the actual total is uncertain since he was so prolific in his heyday, the 1950's and 60's, that magazine editors insisted he publish some stories under pseudonyms to avoid having his byline appear more than once in an issue.

name: Eugene J. McCarthy
headline: Eugene J. McCarthy, Senate Dove Who Jolted '68 Race, Dies at 89
abstract: Eugene J. McCarthy, the sardonic Senate dove who stunned the nation by upending President Lyndon B. Johnson's re-election drive amid the Vietnam War turmoil of 1968, died early yesterday. He was 89.     A courtly, sharp-witted presence in capital politics for half a century, Mr. McCarthy, a Minnesota Democrat, died in his sleep at an assisted-living home in the Georgetown neighborhood of Washington, where he had lived for the last several years.

name: Artine Artinian
headline: Artine Artinian, French Literature Scholar, 97, Dies
abstract: Artine Artinian, a noted manuscript collector and scholar of French literature who was immortalized as a fictional character by two of the most prominent American writers of the 20th century, died on Nov. 19 at his home in Lantana, Fla. He was 97 and had lived for many years in Palm Beach.     Professor Artinian's son, Robert, confirmed the death.

name: Richard Pryor
headline: Richard Pryor, Iconoclastic Comedian, Dies at 65
abstract: Richard Pryor, the iconoclastic standup comedian who transcended barriers of race and brought a biting, irreverent humor into America's living rooms, movie houses, clubs and concert halls, died Saturday. He was 65.      Mr. Pryor, who had been ill with multiple sclerosis, suffered a heart attack and died at a hospital in Los Angeles, his wife, Jennifer Lee Pryor, told CNN.

name: Obituary Comedian
headline: Obituary: Comedian Richard Pryor dies at 65

name: Donald Martino
headline: Donald Martino, 74, Creator of Atonal Musical Works, Dies
abstract: Donald Martino, the Pulitzer Prizewinning American composer widely respected for atonal works that combine intellectual rigor with expressive freedom, died on Thursday aboard a cruise ship in the Caribbean en route to Antigua. He was 74.      The cause was cardiac arrest following complications of diabetes, said Lora Martino, his wife of 36 years, who was vacationing with him. Mr. Martino lived in Newton, Mass.

name: Bob Richardson
headline: Bob Richardson, 77, Who Energized Fashion Photography, Dies
abstract: Bob Richardson, a fashion photographer of the 1960's and 70's who transmitted the excitements and regrets of a generation of free spirits before disappearing into a shadow land of mental illness and homelessness, died on Dec. 5 at his home in Manhattan. He was 77.     He died of natural causes, said his son, Terry.

name: Nathalie Babel Brown
headline: Nathalie Babel Brown, 76, Dies; Edited Isaac Babel
abstract: Nathalie Babel Brown, a daughter of Isaac Babel, the illustrious Russian-Jewish storyteller of the Soviet era, whose literary work she edited, died on Thursday in Washington. She was 76.     She died after surgery, said Beverly Sanders, a friend.

name: Ernest Schwiebert
headline: Ernest Schwiebert, Who'd Rather Be Fishing, Dies at 74
abstract: Ernest Schwiebert, an architect and planner whose lifelong passion for fishing led him to write influential books on piscatorial matters like how trout perceive insects -- all the better to make lures to catch them -- died on Saturday at his home in Princeton, N.J. He was 74.     The cause was renal cancer, said his son, Erik.

name: Débora Arango
headline: Débora Arango, 98, Painter Of Politically Charged Themes, Dies
abstract: Débora Arango, a prolific artist who at first repelled socially conservative Colombia with stark paintings of nudes and social conflict but who was later celebrated as one of the country's most inventive, daring artists, died on Dec. 4 at her rambling colonial home outside Medellín. She was 98.     Her death was confirmed by a great-nephew, Pedro Miguel Estrada.

name: Robert Newmyer
headline: Robert Newmyer, 49, a Producer of 'sex, lies and videotape,' Dies
abstract: Robert F. Newmyer, a prominent independent-film producer whose credits include ''sex, lies and videotape'' and the ''Santa Clause'' movies, died on Monday while on location in Toronto. He was 49 and had homes in Los Angeles and Telluride, Colo.     Mr. Newmyer, a lifelong asthma sufferer, died of a heart attack triggered by asthma after exercising at a health club, Michelle Kydd Lee, a family spokeswoman, said. He was in Toronto working on a film, ''Breach,'' starring Chris Cooper, Laura Linney and Ryan Phillippe, which is scheduled to be released next year.

name: Morton Birnbaum
headline: Morton Birnbaum, 79, Champion of Mentally Ill, Dies
abstract: Dr. Morton Birnbaum, a physician, lawyer and mental health advocate who worked to establish and expand rights for mentally ill patients, died on Nov. 26 at Cabrini Medical Center in New York. He was 79 and lived in Brooklyn Heights.     The cause was a stroke, his family said.

name: Harold Newman
headline: Harold Newman, 84, Who Led Public Employees Board, Dies
abstract: Harold Raymond Newman, former chairman of Public Employment Relations Board of New York State and a behind-the-scenes catalyst in many labor negotiations with public employees, died on Nov. 25 in West Palm Beach, Fla. A resident of Lake Worth, Fla., he was 84 and formerly lived in Albany.      His death was announced by the School of Industrial and Labor Relations at Cornell University, with which he had a long professional association.

name: Gyorgy Sandor
headline: Gyorgy Sandor, Pianist Who Trained Under Bartok, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Gyorgy Sandor, a pianist who studied with Bartok and remained a champion of his music throughout a long career as a performer and teacher, died on Friday at his home in Manhattan. He was 93.     The cause was heart failure, said his son, Michael Sandor.

name: Heinz Heinemann
headline: Heinz Heinemann, 92, Innovative Industrial Chemist, Dies
abstract: HEINZ HEINEMANN, 92, INNOV

name: W. G. Speed III
headline: W. G. Speed III, 87, Developer of Treatments for Migraines, Dies
abstract: W G SPEED III, 87,Ô

name: Anthony C. Russo
headline: Anthony C. Russo, 88, Labor Negotiator, Dies
abstract: Labor negotiator Anthony C Russo dies at age 88 (M)

name: Anthony J. Russo
headline: Anthony J. Russo, 71, Pentagon Papers Figure, Dies
abstract: Mr. Russo was a shaggy-haired, unemployed policy wonk when he teamed up with the buttoned-down Daniel Ellsberg to leak the top-secret government history of the Vietnam War called the Pentagon Papers.

name: John Langstaff
headline: John Langstaff, Founder of 'Revels,' Dies at 84
abstract: JOHN LANGSTAFF, FOUNDER OF 'REVELS,'

name: Leona Nevler
headline: Leona Nevler, Editor, Dies at 79; Shepherded 'Peyton Place'
abstract: Book editor Leona Nevler dies at age 79 (M)

name: William Proxmire
headline: William Proxmire, Maverick Democratic Senator From Wisconsin, Is Dead at 90
abstract: William Proxmire, a political maverick during 32 years in the Senate who crusaded against government waste and irritated presidents and lawmakers from both parties because of his contempt for the mutual back-scratching most politicians engage in, died yesterday in Sykesville, Md., about 40 miles from Washington. He was 90.     He died at the Copper Ridge Nursing Home, said Mindy Brandt, a spokeswoman for the home. Ms. Brandt said she could provide no further details.

name: James Ingo Freed
headline: James Ingo Freed, 75, Dies; Designed Holocaust Museum
abstract: James Ingo Freed, architect who designed United State Holocaust Museum and Jacob K Javits Convention Center, dies at age 75; photos (M)

name: Rodney Whitaker
headline: Rodney Whitaker, Writer, Is Dead at 74; Best Known as Trevanian
abstract: Rodney Whitaker, writer best known by one of his many pen names, Trevanian, dies at age 74 (M)

name: John Spencer
profession: TV Actor Starring on 'The West Wing,'
headline: John Spencer, 58, TV Actor Starring on 'The West Wing,' Dies
abstract: John Spencer, Emmy Award-winning actor who is best known for his role on television drama The West Wing, dies at age 58; photo (M)

name: John Spencer
headline: John Spencer, 71, Dies; Helped Popularize Snooker
abstract: John Spencer, a three-time world-champion snooker player, helped elevate his sport above soccer and cricket on British television in the 1970’s.

name: Jack Anderson
headline: Jack Anderson, Investigative Journalist Who Angered the Powerful, Dies at 83
abstract: Jack Anderson, whose investigative column once appeared in more than 1,000 newspapers with 40 million readers, won a Pulitzer Prize and prompted J. Edgar Hoover to call him ''lower than the regurgitated filth of vultures,'' died yesterday. He was 83.     The cause was Parkinson's disease, Mr. Anderson's daughter Laurie Anderson-Bruch told The Associated Press.

name: Jack Anderson
profession: Longtime Dance Critic for The Times
headline: Jack Anderson, Longtime Dance Critic for The Times, Dies at 88
abstract: He brought an all-embracing enthusiasm to about 4,000 articles for The New York Times on modern dance, tap, ballet and practically every other genre.

name: Mary A. Littauer
profession: Self-Taught Expert On Horses of Ancient Times
headline: Mary A. Littauer, Self-Taught Expert On Horses of Ancient Times, Dies at 93
abstract: Mary Aiken Littauer, whose love affair with horses began with a childhood pony, blossomed with her marriage to an officer in the cavalry of Czar Nicholas II, and flowered famously when she became a leading expert on horses of ancient times, died on Dec. 7 at her home in Syosset, N.Y. She was 93.     Her son, Andrew, announced the death.

name: M. M. Styles
headline: M. M. Styles, 75, Who Helped to Define Nursing Standards, Dies
abstract: Margretta Madden Styles, a nursing educator who conceived and helped establish precise national standards for certifying nurses in pediatrics, cardiology and other medical specialties, died on Nov. 20 at her home in Clearwater, Fla. She was 75.     The cause was colon cancer, her family said.

name: Marvin Schwam
headline: Marvin Schwam, 63, Holiday Display Creator, Dies
abstract: Marvin A. Schwam, who made it a year-round business to prepare for Christmas -- and Hanukkah and Kwanzaa -- as the founder of American Christmas Decorations Inc., died on Dec. 10 at his home in the Chelsea neighborhood in Manhattan. He was 63.     The cause was bladder cancer, said his son Frederic, who succeeded him as the company's owner and president.

name: Sydney Leff
profession: Artist With an Eye for Music
headline: Sydney Leff, 104, Artist With an Eye for Music, Dies
abstract: Sydney Leff, a commercial artist who was almost certainly the last surviving illustrator of sheet music from the golden age of Tin Pan Alley, died on Dec. 10 at his home in Ossining, N.Y. He was 104 and had lived for many years in West Palm Beach, Fla.     Mr. Leff's son-in-law Alfred Miller confirmed the death.

name: Robert Luce
profession: Former Editor And Publisher of New Republic
headline: Robert Luce, 83, Former Editor And Publisher of New Republic, Is Dead
abstract: Robert B. Luce, a former editor and publisher of The New Republic who founded his own book publishing house, died on Nov. 29 in Boca Raton, Fla. He was 83.     He died in a nursing home, his family said. Mr. Luce, known as Bob, began his career working for magazines, taking over at The New Republic in 1963. He edited a book compilation for the magazine's 50th anniversary, which was published in 1964.

name: T. Edward Hambleton
headline: T. Edward Hambleton, Theatrical Producer, Dies at 94
abstract: T. Edward Hambleton, the gentlemanly theatrical producer who was a founder of the Phoenix Theater, the trailblazing Off Broadway institution that helped develop the careers of actors, writers and directors for three decades, died on Saturday night in Baltimore. He was 94 and lived in Cockeysville, Md.      He became ill only the day before he died, his daughter Susan said. An esophageal tumor was found on Friday, but on Thursday he had been drinking Champagne and eating oysters.

name: Vincent Gigante
headline: Vincent Gigante, Mob Boss Who Feigned Incompetence to Avoid Jail, Dies at 77
abstract: Vincent Gigante, who feigned mental illness for decades to camouflage his position as one of the nation's most influential and dangerous Mafia leaders, died yesterday at the United States Medical Center for Federal Prisoners in Springfield, Mo. He was 77.     Mr. Gigante was serving a 12-year prison sentence imposed in 1997 after he was convicted on federal charges of racketeering and conspiring to kill other mobsters. The exact cause of death was unknown, said Al Quintero, a spokesman for the medical center, who noted Mr. Gigante's history of coronary disease.

name: Mary Aiken Littauer
headline: Obituary: Mary Aiken Littauer, historian

name: Tahsin Ozguc
headline: Tahsin Ozguc, 89, Is Dead; Archaeologist Who Worked Sites in Turkey
abstract: Tahsin Ozguc, an eminent Turkish archaeologist whose digs in Anatolia documented the intermingling of Bronze Age cultures and commerce in what is now central Turkey, died on Oct. 28 in Ankara. He was 89.     His death was announced on the Web site of Ankara University, but was only recently brought to The Times's attention.

name: Margaret Hodges
headline: Margaret Hodges, 94, Author of Children's Stories, Dies
abstract: Margaret Hodges, who filled bookshelves with retold legends and other books for young readers and with the awards she received for them, died on Tuesday at her home in Verona, Pa. She was 94.     Her death was announced by her son Arthur C. Hodges, who said two more of her books were to be published in the future.

name: Miller Upton
headline: Miller Upton, Innovative Head of Beloit College, Dies at 88
abstract: Miller Upton, who during 21 years as president of Beloit College found innovative and widely imitated ways to maximize the college's educational and financial resources, died yesterday at his home in Fontana, Wis. He was 88.     The college, in Beloit, Wis., announced his death.

name: Barry Halper
headline: Barry Halper, Baseball Memorabilia Collector, Dies at 66
abstract: Barry Halper, who began collecting autographs as an 8-year-old hanging around the Yankees' minor league ballpark in Newark and went on to assemble the nation's most acclaimed private collection of baseball memorabilia, died Sunday at a hospital in Livingston, N.J. Mr. Halper, who lived in New Vernon, N.J., was 66.     The cause was complications of diabetes, said his son Jason.

name: Alan Shields
headline: Alan Shields, Artist of 70's Style, Dies at 61
abstract: Alan Shields, whose radiantly colored, sewing-machine stitched, three-dimensional paintings made him prominent in the New York art world of the 1970's, died on Tuesday at his home on Shelter Island, New York. He was 61.      Mr. Shields was being treated for emphysema and died in his sleep, said Marla Gagnum, his companion.

name: W. J. Oswald
headline: W. J. Oswald, 86, Algae Miracle Worker, Dies
abstract: William J. Oswald, a scientist who pioneered ways to use algae to address immense human problems -- including treating sewage, increasing food supplies, generating energy and facilitating voyages into deep space -- died on Dec. 8 at his home in Concord, Calif. He was 86.     The cause was pancreatic cancer, said the University of California, Berkeley, where Dr. Oswald was a professor emeritus in civil and environmental engineering.

name: Swami Jagdishwaranand
headline: Swami Jagdishwaranand, 71, Spiritual Leader, Dies
abstract: Swami Jagdishwaranand, a prominent Hindu spiritual leader in New York City who was responsible for establishing several temples here, died last Thursday at the Geeta Temple in Elmhurst, Queens. The swami, who founded the temple more than 30 years ago and made his home there, was 71.     Swami Jagdishwaranand died after a short illness, according to Anil Dass, a temple member.

name: Jim Ostendarp
headline: Jim Ostendarp, Coach at Amherst, Dies at 82
abstract: JIM OSTENDARP, 82, COACH AND

name: Joseph L. Owades
profession: Developer of Recipe for Light Beer
headline: Joseph L. Owades, Developer of Recipe for Light Beer, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Biochemist Joseph L Owades, who developed light beer, dies at age 86 (M)l

name: John Laupheimer
headline: John Laupheimer, Golf Chief, Dies at 75
abstract: JOHN LAUPHEIMER, 75

name: Don Caswell
headline: Don Caswell, Times Copy Editor, Is Dead at 65
abstract: New York Times copy editor Don Caswell dies at age 65 (S)ÿ

name: Ted Tulchin
headline: Ted Tulchin, 79, a Producer of 'Sweeney Todd' Revival, Is Dead
abstract: Ted Tulchin, businessman and theatrical producer, dies at age 79 (M)

name: Charles F. Cummings
headline: Charles F. Cummings, Official Historian of Newark, Is Dead at 68
abstract: Charles F Cummings, official historian of Newark, NJ, dies at age 68; photo (M)

name: David Patterson
headline: David Patterson, 83, Scholar of European Jewish Culture, Dies
abstract: David Patterson, a scholar of Jewish life in Europe who established a center for Hebrew and Jewish studies at Oxford University to help revive a discipline that had been virtually destroyed during the Holocaust, died at a hospital in Oxford on Dec. 10. He was 83.     The cause was prostate cancer, according to Jackie Finlay, his personal assistant.

name: Elrod Hendricks
headline: Elrod Hendricks, 64, Baltimore's Favorite Catcher and Coach
abstract: Elrod Hendricks, who spent nearly four decades with the Orioles as a catcher and coach and came to be revered in Baltimore for his community work and his bonds with the fans, died Wednesday night at a hospital in Glen Burnie, Md., a day before his 65th birthday.     The cause was a heart attack, the Orioles said. They had planned to assign Hendricks to off-field work next season as a result of a minor stroke he had in April that kept him away from his bullpen-coaching duties for a time.

name: Albert L. Weimorts
headline: Albert L. Weimorts, Designer of Big Bombs, Dies at 67
abstract: Albert L. Weimorts, a civilian engineer for the Air Force who conceived and designed some of the biggest, most powerful nonnuclear bombs ever made, died on Wednesday at a hospital in Fort Walton Beach, Fla. He was 67.     The cause was brain cancer, his son Todd said.

name: Eliot Freidson
headline: Eliot Freidson, 82, Dies; Studied Structure of Professions
abstract: Eliot Freidson, a sociologist at New York University who studied the inner workings of society's professions, particularly the way doctors are organized to practice medicine, died on Dec. 14 in a hospice in San Francisco. He was 82.      The cause was non-Hodgkin's lymphoma, his family said.

name: Selma Jeanne Cohen
headline: Selma Jeanne Cohen, 85, a Historian of Dance, Is Dead
abstract: Selma Jeanne Cohen, a historian, editor and teacher who devoted her career to proclaiming dance an art worthy of the same scholarly respect traditionally awarded to painting, music and literature, died on Friday at her home in Greenwich Village. She was 85.      The cause was complications from Alzheimer's disease, said Leslie Steinau, her lawyer and a longtime friend.

name: Herman Roiphe
headline: Herman Roiphe, 81, Psychoanalyst, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Herman Roiphe, a psychoanalyst who explored the notion of sexual identity in early childhood development, died on Dec. 14 in Manhattan. He was 81.      The cause was a heart attack, his family said. Working with another researcher, Dr. Eleanor Galenson, Dr. Roiphe (pronounced ROY-fee) drew on his clinical practice and time spent with children in nurseries to refine existing Freudian notions of when children begin their psychosexual development.

name: Kerry Packer
headline: Kerry Packer, 68, Australia's Media Magnate, Is Dead
abstract: Kerry Packer, who became Australia's richest man by turning a magazine and television inheritance worth millions into a diverse business worth billions, died yesterday in Sydney. He was 68.     His death was reported by his family. The Associated Press reported Mr. Packer had been plagued by ill health.

name: Norman Dane Vaughan
headline: Norman Dane Vaughan, Antarctic Explorer, Dies at 100
abstract: Norman Vaughan, a legendary Alaskan explorer and dog sled racer, and the last surviving member of Adm. Richard E. Byrd's expedition to Antarctica in 1928-30, died Friday at a hospital in Anchorage. He was 100.     The death was confirmed by the Providence Alaska Medical Center.

name: John Diebold
headline: John Diebold, 79, a Visionary of the Computer Age, Dies
abstract: John Diebold, a visionary thinker whose early and persistent promotion of computers and other far-reaching innovations helped shape industrial development in America and beyond, died yesterday at his home in Bedford Hills, N.Y. He was 79.     The cause was esophageal cancer, said his nephew, also named John Diebold.

name: J. H. Herz
headline: J. H. Herz, a Scholar of Diplomacy, Is Dead at 97
abstract: John H Herz, City College of New York government professor and scholar of international relations and laws, dies at age 97 (M)

name: Charles W. Socarides
headline: Charles W. Socarides, Psychiatrist and Psychoanalyst, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Dr Charles W Socarides, well-known psychiatrist who held belief that homosexuality was treatable condition, dies at age 83 (M)

name: Constance Keene
headline: Constance Keene, 84, a Pianist in the Romantic Mold, Is Dead
abstract: Constance Keene, pianist and teacher, dies at age 84; photo (M)

name: Charles Engell France
headline: Charles Engell France, 59, a Presence in Ballet World, Dies
abstract: Charles Engell France, a writer on dance, a collector and the influential assistant to Mikhail Baryshnikov when he was artistic director of American Ballet Theater in the 1980's, died on Sunday. He was 59.     Mr. France collapsed in his apartment building on the Upper West Side of Manhattan and was dead on arrival at Roosevelt Hospital, said Ellen Levene, a colleague. The cause is not yet known but Mr. France had been in poor health for years.

name: Richard Grimsdale
headline: Richard Grimsdale, Computer Pioneer, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Richard L. Grimsdale, an electrical engineer who colleagues said built the first transistorized computer, died Dec. 6 at his home in Brighton, England. He was 76.     The cause was a heart infection, according to his wife, Shirley Roberts Grimsdale.

name: Donald Dawson
headline: Donald Dawson, 97, Dies; Master of Truman Whistle-Stop
abstract: Donald S. Dawson, who as a presidential aide marshaled Harry S. Truman's crucial whistle-stop tour in the 1948 election campaign and who later had a long career as a Washington lawyer, died on Sunday at his home in Bethesda, Md. He was 97.      The death was announced by his family.

name: Derek Bailey
headline: Derek Bailey, 75, Guitarist and Master of Improvisation, Dies
abstract: Derek Bailey, the English guitarist who helped to form a fractured style and a cohesive philosophy for European free improvisation, died at his home in London on Sunday. He was 75.      The cause was complications of a motor neuron disease, said Martin Davidson, a record producer and friend.

name: William W. Howells
headline: William W. Howells, Leading Anthropologist, Is Dead at 97
abstract: William W. Howells, a leading physical anthropologist who focused on the origins of humans and the evolution of races, died on Dec. 20 at his home in Kittery Point, Me. He was 97.     The death was announced by his family.

name: Rona Jaffe
headline: Rona Jaffe, Author of Popular Novels, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Rona Jaffe, the preternaturally youthful writer whose 1958 novel ''The Best of Everything'' told the melodramatic story of four nubile, cashmere-sweatered career girls torn between storybook romance and cutthroat corporate Manhattan, died yesterday at University College Hospital in London, where she was on vacation. She was 74.     She died of cancer, said Alan C. Rothfeld, her lawyer and longtime friend.

name: John Druze
profession: Last of Fordham's Seven Blocks of Granite
headline: John Druze, Last of Fordham's Seven Blocks of Granite, Dies at 91
abstract: John Druze, the last surviving member of Fordham University's football offensive line of the 1930's known as the Seven Blocks of Granite, died Tuesday in Scottsdale, Ariz. He was 91.     His death was announced by Fordham.

name: Marjorie Kellogg
headline: Marjorie Kellogg, 83, Writer of 'Junie Moon' and Movies, Dies
abstract: Marjorie Kellogg, who poured her personal experiences into the bestselling book ''Tell Me That You Love Me, Junie Moon,'' her story of three disabled people keeping house together, died on Dec. 19 at her home in Santa Barbara, Calif. She was 83 and was for many years a resident of Manhattan.      The death was announced by her companion, Sylvia Short, a stage and film actress, who is her only immediate survivor. The cause was complications of Alzheimer's disease, she said.

name: Alan M. Voorhees
headline: Alan M. Voorhees Is Dead at 83; Designed Transportation Systems
abstract: Alan M. Voorhees, a prominent transportation engineer and city planner whose work helped give rise to the Interstate highway system in the United States, died on Dec. 18 in Richmond, Va. Mr. Voorhees, who was also an entrepreneur and philanthropist, was 83 and made his home in Alexandria, Va.     No cause of death has been determined, his daughter Nancy Voorhees said.

name: Julius Wile
headline: Julius Wile Dies at 91; Wine Importer
abstract: Julius Wile, a noted wine importer and educator, died on Dec. 12 at his home in Scarsdale, N.Y. He was 91.     His death followed a long illness, according to his son, Andrew.

name: Truman Gibson
headline: Truman Gibson, Who Fought Army Segregation, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Truman K. Gibson Jr., who fought racial discrimination in the Army in World War II as a high-level adviser in the War Department and later became a powerful pro boxing promoter, died Dec. 23 in Chicago. He was 93.     His death was announced by Unity Funeral Parlors of Chicago.

name: Tory Dent
headline: Tory Dent, Poet Who Wrote of Living With H.I.V., Dies at 47
abstract: Tory Dent, a poet, essayist and art critic whose verse told of life with a diagnosis of H.I.V. and of the struggle to keep her creativity alive, died last Friday at her home in the East Village. She was 47.     The death was announced by her husband, Sean Harvey. The cause was an opportunistic infection associated with AIDS, to which her condition had progressed about nine years ago.

name: Frank Wilkinson
headline: Frank Wilkinson, Defiant Figureof Red Scare, Dies at 91
abstract: Frank Wilkinson, a Los Angeles housing official who lost his job in the Red Scare of the early 1950's and later became one of the last two people jailed for refusing to tell the House Un-American Activities Committee whether he was a Communist, died Monday in Los Angeles. He was 91.     Mr. Wilkinson, whose experiences inspired a half-century campaign against government spying, had been ill for several months and was recovering from surgery and a fall, said Donna Wilkinson, his wife of 40 years. ''It was just the complications of old age, '' Mrs. Wilkinson said.

name: Candy Barr
profession: Stripper and Star of 1950's Stag Film
headline: Candy Barr, 70, Stripper and Star of 1950's Stag Film, Dies
abstract: Candy Barr, an exotic dancer whose hardscrabble life became Texas legend as she befriended Jack Ruby (who killed President John F. Kennedy's assassin), dated a mobster, shot her husband went to prison for drug possession, and starred -- unwillingly, she insisted -- in a famous stag film, died on Friday in Victoria, Tex. She was 70.     The Slavik Funeral Home in Edna, Tex., confirmed the death, but provided no details. The Associated Press said she died of pneumonia.

name: Maktoum
headline: Maktoum, Modernizing Dubai Emir, Is Dead at 62
abstract: Sheik Maktoum bin Rashid al-Maktoum, emir of Dubai and prime minister and vice president of the United Arab Emirates, died Wednesday in Australia. He was 62.      No official cause of death was given, but Australian and Arab news media reported that he had suffered heart problems. His body was flown back to the Persian Gulf on Wednesday for a state burial to be held Thursday in Dubai.

name: Hugh Thompson
headline: Hugh Thompson, 62, Who Saved Civilians at My Lai, Dies
abstract: Hugh Thompson, an Army helicopter pilot who rescued Vietnamese civilians during the My Lai massacre, reported the killings to his superior officers in a rage over what he had seen, testified at the inquiries and received a commendation from the Army three decades later, died yesterday in Alexandria, La. He was 62.     The cause was cancer, Jay DeWorth, a spokesman for the Veterans Affairs Medical Center where Mr. Thompson died, told The Associated Press.

name: Jon de Cortina
headline: The Rev. Jon de Cortina, 71, Is Dead; Saved Salvadoran Children
abstract: The Rev. Jon de Cortina Garaigorta, a Jesuit priest who dedicated the last decade to searching for the missing children of El Salvador's brutal civil war, died in mid-December, officials of his organization said Wednesday. He was 71.     They said the cause was complications of a stroke.

name: Emmett Leith
profession: Pioneer in the Development of Holography
headline: Emmett Leith, 78, a Pioneer in the Development of Holography, Dies
abstract: Emmett Leith, a scientist who took the concept of the hologram and added the technology of the laser to help create three-dimensional photography, died on Dec. 23 at a hospital in Ann Arbor, Mich. He was 78.      The cause was an internal hemorrhage, said Kim Leith, his daughter.

name: Enrico Di Giuseppe
profession: Tenor at City and Metropolitan Operas
headline: Enrico Di Giuseppe, 73, Tenor at City and Metropolitan Operas, Dies
abstract: Enrico Di Giuseppe, an American tenor who sang for many years with both the New York City and Metropolitan Operas, died on Dec. 31 in Voorhees, N.J. He was 73.     The cause was small cell cancer, said his wife, Lorna.

name: Yao Wenyuan
headline: Yao Wenyuan, 74, Member of Gang of Four, Is Dead
abstract: Yao Wenyuan, the last surviving member of China's notorious Gang of Four, the powerful group that was blamed for many of the excesses of the Cultural Revolution, died Dec. 23, according to the official New China News Agency. He was 74.      The government did not immediately issue a statement. But the state-run media said Mr. Yao died of diabetes. It did not specify where he died.

name: Frank Cary
headline: Frank Cary, Past Chairman of I.B.M., Is Dead at 85
abstract: Frank T.
