Cary, the chairman and chief executive of International Business Machines during the tumultuous 1970's when I.B.M. confronted antitrust lawsuits, rising competition from Japanese manufacturers and the dawn of the personal computer, died Sunday. He was 85.     He died of unknown causes while asleep at his home in Darien, Conn., according to a son, Bryan Cary.

name: Lou Rawls
headline: Lou Rawls, Singer of Pop and Gospel, Dies at 72
abstract: Lou Rawls, the smooth-voiced, enduring singing star whose career traced a line from gospel to jazz and pop, died early yesterday morning at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles. He was 72.      The cause was cancer, said his longtime manager and publicist, David Brokaw.

name: Barry Cowsill
headline: Barry Cowsill, 51, Missing Since Hurricane, Is Dead
abstract: Barry Cowsill, a member of the popular 1960's and early 70's singing family the Cowsills, was identified Tuesday as among the dead nearly four months after he disappeared when Hurricane Katrina flooded this city. He was 51.     Mr. Cowsill's body, recovered Dec. 28 from the Chartres Street Wharf, was identified with dental records, said Dr. Louis Cataldie, head of the state hurricane morgue in Carville. The cause of death has not been determined.

name: Rod Dedeaux
profession: Led U.S.C. to 11 College World Series Titles
headline: Rod Dedeaux, Who Led U.S.C. to 11 College World Series Titles, Dies at 91
abstract: Rod Dedeaux, who coached the University of Southern California to a record 11 College World Series championships and sent some 60 players to the major leagues, died Thursday in Glendale, Calif. He was 91.     The cause was complications of a stroke, U.S.C. said.

name: Muriel Costa-Greenspon
headline: Muriel Costa-Greenspon, City Opera Mezzo for 30 Years, Is Dead at 68
abstract: Muriel Costa-Greenspon, a mezzo-soprano who was a fixture at the New York City Opera for 30 years, died on Dec. 26 at St. Vincent's Hospital in Manhattan. She was 68.     Her death was due to natural causes, said her son, Stefano Costa.

name: Raoul Bott
headline: Raoul Bott, an Innovator in Mathematics, Dies at 82
abstract: Raoul Bott, a mathematician who made innovative contributions to differential geometry and topology, a field that examines the properties of spaces, died on Dec. 20 in Carlsbad, Calif. He was 82.      The cause was lung cancer, his family said.

name: Heinrich Harrer
headline: Heinrich Harrer, 93, Explorer of Tibet, Dies
abstract: Heinrich Harrer, a swashbuckling explorer who told of his magical life of conquering the world's highest peaks and tutoring the young Dalai Lama when Tibet seemed as exotic as Mars, only to have news of his Nazi past mar his final years, died Jan. 7 in Friesach, Austria. He was 93.     The Associated Press said his family announced his death in a hospital there, saying only that ''in great peace, he carried out his final expedition.''

name: Abuna Yesehaq Mandefro
headline: Abuna Yesehaq Mandefro, Ethiopian Archbishop, 72, Dies
abstract: Archbishop Abuna Yesehaq Mandefro, a leader in the diaspora of the Orthodox Church of Ethiopia who, caught up in the political upheaval at home in the 1990's, split his congregations in the Americas from the mother church in Addis Ababa, died on Dec. 29 in Newark. He was 72 and lived in Union City, N.J.      The death was announced by a spokesman for the archbishopric in Dallas, where he recently moved his seat, and by Father Haile Malekot of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church in Kingston, Jamaica.

name: Donald Mackay
headline: Donald Mackay, Artist and Illustrator, Dies at 91
abstract: Donald A. Mackay, an artist and illustrator best known for drawing the evolution of Manhattan, died on Dec. 17 in Frederick, Md., where he retired in 1993. He was 91 and formerly lived in Ossining, N.Y.     The cause was heart disease, his family said.

name: Theodore H. Bullock
headline: Theodore H. Bullock, Animal Researcher, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Theodore H. Bullock, who made wide-ranging studies of sensory and nervous systems in fish and invertebrates and then used his research to explore the evolution of the brain in animals, died on Dec. 20 in San Diego. He was 90.      His family confirmed the death.

name: William Haxby
headline: William Haxby, Mapper of Ocean Floors, Is Dead at 56
abstract: William F. Haxby, who created the first maps of the ocean floor to be based on satellite measurements of the water's surface and became a master at translating complicated marine data into comprehensible visual displays, died on Wednesday at his home in Westwood, N.J. He was 56.      The cause was apparently a heart attack, said James V. Haxby, a brother.

name: David Rosenbaum
headline: David Rosenbaum, Reporter for Times Who Covered Politics, Dies at 63
abstract: David E. Rosenbaum, a retired reporter and editor for The New York Times who for more than 35 years wrote about the intersection of politics, economics and government policy with uncommon depth, clarity and a keen eye for the story behind the story, died Sunday. He was 63.     His death was caused by a brain injury suffered when he was struck in the head and robbed Friday night while walking near his home in Northwest Washington, police officials and his family members said.

name: Harry Magdoff
headline: Harry Magdoff, Economist, Dies at 92
abstract: Harry Magdoff, who fell in love with Marxist thought at 15 and became an influential socialist economist, author, editor and commentator -- and, some said, a Soviet spy -- died on Jan. 1 at his home in Burlington, Vt. He was 92.     His son, Frederick, announced the death.

name: William Guthman
headline: William Guthman, Antiques Dealer, Is Dead at 81
abstract: William H. Guthman, a prominent antiques dealer who specialized in items of historical and military Americana and helped make them stars of the collecting world, died on Dec. 28 at his home in Westport, Conn. He was 81.     The cause was lung cancer, said his wife, Elizabeth Stillinger.

name: Armand P. Bartos
headline: Armand P. Bartos, 95, Architect and Donor, Is Dead
abstract: Armand P. Bartos, an architect and philanthropist who, with his wife, Celeste, supported major New York City cultural institutions, died at his home in Manhattan on Dec. 29. He was 95.     His death followed several years of illness, said his son Armand Jr.

name: Birgit Nilsson
headline: Birgit Nilsson, Soprano Legend Who Tamed Wagner, Dies at 87
abstract: Birgit Nilsson, the Swedish soprano with a voice of impeccable trueness and impregnable stamina, died on Dec. 25 in Vastra Karup, the village where she was born, the Stockholm newspaper Svenska Dagbladet reported yesterday. She was 87.     A funeral was held yesterday at a church in her town, the presiding vicar, Fredrik Westerlund, told The Associated Press.

name: Jack Snow
profession: Top Receiver and Broadcaster for the Rams
headline: Jack Snow, Top Receiver and Broadcaster for the Rams, Dies at 62
abstract: Jack Snow, former receiver for Los Angeles Rams and longtime radio analyst for franchise, dies at 62 from staph infection following hip replacement surgery; photo (M)

name: G. Blakemore Evans
headline: G. Blakemore Evans, 93, Shakespeare Scholar, Dies
abstract: Eminent Elizabethan scholar G Blakemore Evans, who edited The Riverside Shakespeare, dies at home in Cambridge, Mass, at age 93 (S)

name: David S. Kruidenier
headline: David S. Kruidenier, 84, Publisher and Philanthropist, Dies
abstract: David S Kruidenier, former Des Moines Register publisher and philanthropist who contributed greatly to revitalizing downtown Des Moines, dies at age 84; photo (M)

name: Sidney Frank
profession: Took a German Drink and a Vodka Brand to Stylish Heights
headline: Sidney Frank, 86, Dies; Took a German Drink and a Vodka Brand to Stylish Heights
abstract: Sidney E. Frank, who was forced to leave Brown University as a freshman when his money ran out, went on to concoct spectacularly successful marketing campaigns for Jägermeister liqueur and Grey Goose vodka, then became so rich he gave Brown its biggest gift ever, died Tuesday in San Diego. He was 86.     His death was announced by the Sidney Frank Importing Company.

name: Ira B. Black
profession: Leader in New Jersey Stem Cell Effort
headline: Dr. Ira B. Black, 64, Leader in New Jersey Stem Cell Effort, Dies
abstract: Dr. Ira B. Black, a neuroscientist and brain researcher who became an early advocate for stem cell research and a founder of the Stem Cell Institute of New Jersey, died on Tuesday at a hospital in Philadelphia. He was 64.      The cause was an infection related to a tumor, his family said.

name: Mimmo Rotella
headline: Mimmo Rotella, Collagist, Dies at 87
abstract: Mimmo Rotella, the Italian artist who was one of the last surviving members of the influential French Nouveaux Réalistes group, died on Sunday in Milan. He was 87.      His death followed several months of illness, said his wife, Inna Rotella.

name: Hubert Schoemaker
headline: Hubert Schoemaker, a Biotech Pioneer, Dies at 55
abstract: Hubert J. P. Schoemaker, a founder and former president of one of the nation's first biotechnology companies, died on Jan. 1 at his home in Paoli, Pa. He was 55.     The cause was brain cancer, said his stepson, Jonathan Saruk.

name: Irving Layton
profession: Canadian Poet With a Worldwide Following
headline: Irving Layton, 93, Canadian Poet With a Worldwide Following, Dies
abstract: Irving Layton, a Canadian poet as quirky as he was prolific, died on Jan. 4 in Montreal. He was 93.     The death was announced on his Web site, www.irvinglayton.com. Press reports from Montreal said the cause was Alzheimer's disease, diagnosed in 1994.

name: Marshall A. Robinson
headline: Marshall A. Robinson, 83, Former Foundation Chief, Dies
abstract: Marshall A. Robinson, former president of the Russell Sage Foundation in New York, died on Saturday at his home on the East Side of Manhattan. He was 83, and died after a long illness, his family said.      After a career in academia and with the Ford Foundation, Dr. Robinson headed the Russell Sage Foundation, one of the nation's oldest private philanthropies, from 1979 to 1986. The foundation, established in 1907, focuses on research in the social sciences, supporting and publishing studies on topics like the social effects of economic inequality.

name: Frank Okamura
headline: Frank Okamura, Bonsai Expert, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Frank Okamura, who came to New York City as a gardener after his release from a wartime internment camp in California and ended up contributing to the spread of Japanese cultural influences in America as a bonsai master, restaurant owner and even as a landlord, died on Monday at his home in Manhattan. He was 94.     His death was announced by his daughter Reiko.

name: Eldon Dedini
headline: Eldon Dedini, 84, Magazine Gag Cartoonist, Dies
abstract: Eldon Dedini, a cartoonist who concocted a mythical world of satyrs and nymphs for Playboy and another of quirky, sophisticated wit for The New Yorker, died Thursday at his home in Carmel, Calif. He was 84.     The cause was esophageal cancer, his son, Giulio, said.

name: Elliot Forbes
headline: Elliot Forbes, 88, a Scholar Whose Specialty Was Beethoven, Dies
abstract: Elliot Forbes, a retired Harvard University professor of music whose revision of ''Thayer's Life of Beethoven'' became a pillar of Beethoven scholarship, died at his home in Cambridge, Mass., on Tuesday, family members said. He was 88.     A much-loved fixture on the campus, Mr. Forbes also conducted the Harvard Glee Club and the Radcliffe Choral Society in the 1960's and mentored several generations of Beethoven scholars. He retired as the Fanny Peabody professor of music in 1984 but stayed on as a professor emeritus.

name: Bradford Cannon
headline: Bradford Cannon, 98, Surgeon Who Improved Burn Treatment, Dies
abstract: Bradford Cannon, a Boston physician and pioneer in reconstructive plastic surgery who applied path-breaking medical techniques to advance skin grafting, especially in cases involving serious burns, died on Dec. 20 at his daughter's home in Lincoln, Mass. He was 98.      The cause was pneumonia, his family said.

name: Shelley Winters
profession: Tough-Talking Oscar Winner in 'Anne Frank' and 'Patch of Blue
headline: Shelley Winters, Tough-Talking Oscar Winner in 'Anne Frank' and 'Patch of Blue,' Dies
abstract: Shelley Winters, who once described her life as a ''rocky road out of the Brooklyn ghetto to one New York apartment, two Oscars, three California houses, four hit plays, five Impressionist paintings, six mink coats and 99 films,'' died yesterday. She was 83, although some sources say she was 85.     Ms. Winters died of heart failure at the Rehabilitation Centre of Beverly Hills, her publicist, Dale Olson, said. She had been hospitalized in October after suffering a heart attack.

name: Milton Himmelfarb
headline: Milton Himmelfarb, Wry Essayist, 87, Dies
abstract: Milton Himmelfarb, a leading essayist for Commentary and other publications who was known for his well wrought and witty observations on Jewish affairs, died on Jan. 4 at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center in Manhattan. He was 87 and lived in White Plains.     The cause was complications of skin cancer, his nephew William Kristol said.

name: of Kuwait
headline: Emir of Kuwait, 79, Dies
abstract: Sheik Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah helped guide his people through the long days when Iraq's military occupied, looted and ransacked their oil-rich nation.

name: Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah
headline: Sheik Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah, the Leader of Kuwait for 28 Years, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Emir of Kuwait Sheik Jaber al-Ahmad al-Sabah dies at age 79; ruled oil-rich nation for 28 years and was known for his modest life style; photo (M)

name: Donald Rauth
headline: Donald Rauth, 87, Aerospace Industry Execute, Dies
abstract: J Donald Rauth, Martin Marietta Corporation former chairman, dies at age 87 of apparent heart attack (S)

name: Leon Lobel
profession: Part Owner of a Storied Family Butcher Shop
headline: Leon Lobel, 77, a Part Owner of a Storied Family Butcher Shop, Dies
abstract: Leon Lobel, fourth-generation butcher and part owner of Lobel's Prime Meats on Upper East Side of Manhattan, dies at age 77 (M)

name: Bob Weinstock
profession: Founder of the Jazz Label Prestige
headline: Bob Weinstock, Founder of the Jazz Label Prestige, Dies at 77
abstract: Bob Weinstock, founder of Prestige, jazz record label, dies at age 77 (M)

name: Eric Namesnik
profession: Winner of 2 Silver Medals in Olympics
headline: Eric Namesnik, 35, Winner of 2 Silver Medals in Olympics, Dies
abstract: Eric J Namesnik, winner of 2 silver Olympic medals for swimming, dies at age 35 from injuries suffered in car crash; photo (S)

name: Philip Ressner
headline: Philip Ressner, 83, Children's Author And Book Editor
abstract: Philip Ressner, a retired book editor and the author of half a dozen successful children's books, died on Dec. 27 at Methodist Hospital in Brooklyn. He was 83.      The cause was heart failure, his family said.

name: Joan Root
headline: Joan Root, Wildlife Conservationist, Dies at 69
abstract: Joan Root, an animal lover and conservationist who collaborated with her husband, Alan, on a series of wildlife documentaries in the 1970's, was killed Friday in Naivasha, Kenya. She was 69.     Ms. Root was shot to death by assailants who invaded her lakefront farmhouse, the police said. Two men were arrested but the motive remains unknown, officials said.

name: Anne Meacham
profession: Actress On New York Stages and TV
headline: Anne Meacham, 80, Actress On New York Stages and TV
abstract: Anne Meacham, an actress whose notable stage appearances included roles in the original production of Tennessee Williams's ''Suddenly Last Summer'' and Eva Le Gallienne's 1964 Broadway staging of ''The Seagull,'' died on Thursday at her home in Canaan, N.Y. She was 80.      Her death was announced by her friend Marian Seldes.

name: Thomas Murphy
headline: Thomas Murphy, 90, Leader of G.M. in 1970's Prosperity, Dies
abstract: Thomas A. Murphy, who led General Motors for most of the 1970's, died Wednesday at his home in Boynton Beach, Fla. He was 90.     His death was announced by General Motors.

name: Thomas S. Murphy
headline: Thomas S. Murphy, Broadcasting ‘Minnow’ Who Swallowed ABC, Dies at 96
abstract: As the head of Capital Cities Communications, he engineered the acquisition of the TV giant. He later sold the company to Disney, at a huge profit.

name: Jim Gary
headline: Jim Gary, Sculptor Inspired by Junk, Dies at 66
abstract: Jim Gary, an internationally noted sculptor in metal whose best-known work transformed the skeletons of derelict cars into the hulking, playful and surprisingly graceful skeletons of dinosaurs, died on Saturday in Freehold, N.J. He was 66 and lived in Farmingdale, N.J.     The cause was complications of a cerebral hemorrhage he suffered last month, said Arlene Berg, a longtime friend and Mr. Gary's former business manager.

name: Fred K. Hoehler Jr.
headline: Fred K. Hoehler Jr., 87, a Labor College Founder, Dies
abstract: Fred K. Hoehler Jr., a pioneer in labor education and the founding director of the George Meany Center for Labor Studies of the A.F.L.-C.I.O., forerunner of the National Labor College in Maryland, died on Jan. 4 in Bellingham, Wash. He was 87.     His death was announced by his family.

name: Col. Edward N. Hall

name: Edward Hall
headline: Edward Hall, Expert on Nonverbal Communication, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Mr. Hall was a cultural anthropologist who pioneered the study of nonverbal communication and interactions between members of different ethnic groups.

name: Gideon Rodan
headline: Gideon Rodan, 71, Scientist Who Researched Bone Loss
abstract: Gideon A Rodan, biomedical researcher who helped formulate Fosomax, dies at age 71; photo (S)

name: Wilson Pickett
headline: Wilson Pickett, 64, Soul Singer of Great Passion, Dies
abstract: Wilson Pickett, legendary soul singer, dies at age 64; photo (M)

name: Stanley H. Biber
profession: Surgeon Among First to Do Sex Changes
headline: Stanley H. Biber, 82, Surgeon Among First to Do Sex Changes, Dies
abstract: Stanley H. Biber, a small-town Colorado doctor who for decades was internationally renowned as the dean of sex-change surgery, died on Monday at a hospital in Pueblo. He was 82 and lived in Hoehne, Colo.     The cause was complications of pneumonia, said his secretary, Marie Pacino.

name: Richard Bellucci
headline: Richard Bellucci, 91, Surgeon and Inventor, Dies
abstract: Dr. Richard Bellucci, a New York ear surgeon who invented an early instrument for microsurgery that is still in use, died on Dec. 22 at Calvary Hospital in the Bronx. He was 91 and lived on the Upper East Side of Manhattan.     The death was announced by his family.

name: Stephen Papich
headline: Stephen Papich, 80, Producer and Author, Is Dead
abstract: Stephen Papich, a former Hollywood choreographer and stage producer and a biographer of Josephine Baker, died on Dec. 16 at his home in Los Angeles. He was 80.     The cause was cancer, his companion, Robert Wood, said.

name: Erica Reiner
headline: Erica Reiner Is Dead at 81; Renowned Assyrian Scholar
abstract: Erica Reiner, an internationally renowned scholar of Assyrian, one of the world's oldest written languages, died on Dec. 31 at her home in the Hyde Park neighborhood of Chicago. She was 81.     The cause was lung cancer, according to the Oriental Institute of the University of Chicago, where she was the John A. Wilson Distinguished Service Professor emeritus.

name: Ibrahim Rugova
headline: Ibrahim Rugova, 61, Kosovo Albanian Leader, Is Dead
abstract: Ibrahim Rugova, the leader of the United Nations-administered Serbian province of Kosovo, died Saturday. He was 61.     The cause was lung cancer, a statement issued by the presidency said Saturday.

name: Allan Temko
headline: Allan Temko, 81 Architecture Critic, Dies
abstract: Allan Temko, a former architecture critic for The San Francisco Chronicle, who won a Pulitzer Prize for criticism in 1990 and wrote a definitive profile of the Cathedral of Notre Dame in Paris, died on Wednesday in Orinda, Calif. He was 81.      He died after a brief illness, his family said.

name: Richard W. Couper
headline: Richard W. Couper, 83, First Full-Time Library Chief, Dies
abstract: Richard W. Couper, a prominent foundation executive who was the first full-time president of the New York Public Library, died on Wednesday at a hospital in New Hartford, N.Y. He was 83 and lived in Clinton, N.Y.     He died after a long illness, according to a spokesman for his alma mater, Hamilton College.

name: Dunbar W. Bostwick
headline: Dunbar W. Bostwick, Harness Racing Innovator, Dies at 98
abstract: Dunbar W. Bostwick, a sportsman who bred and campaigned many winning trotters, founded racetracks and pioneered new gadgets and training techniques for harness racing, died on Wednesday at his home in Shelburne, Vt. He was 98.      His death was announced by Christopher W. Davis, a grandson and his executor.

name: Nellie Y. McKay
headline: Nellie Y. McKay, Who Championed Black Writers, Dies
abstract: Nellie Y. McKay, a distinguished scholar and critic who helped secure a place for African-American women in the modern literary canon, died last Sunday at a hospice in Fitchburg, Wis. She was a resident of Madison, Wis., and was believed to have been in her mid-70's.     The cause was cancer, said Craig Werner, chairman of the Afro-American studies department at the University of Wisconsin, where Ms. McKay was Evjue professor of American and African-American literature.

name: Beth Fallon
headline: Beth Fallon, 64, Columnist Who Needled the Powerful, Dies
abstract: Beth Fallon, a political reporter and columnist whose thrice-weekly columns in The Daily News and The New York Post brought an irreverent eye to city life in the 1970's and 80's, died Saturday at Calvary Hospital in the Bronx. She was 64.     She had been in declining health for more than a decade, said her husband, Maurice Carroll.

name: Wendy Wasserstein
profession: Her Plays Spoke to a Generation
headline: Wendy Wasserstein Dies at 55; Her Plays Spoke to a Generation
abstract: Wendy Wasserstein, who spoke for a generation of smart, driven but sometimes unsatisfied women in a series of popular plays that included the long-running Pulitzer Prize winner ''The Heidi Chronicles,'' died yesterday at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center in Manhattan. She was 55 and lived in New York.     The cause was complications of lymphoma, said André Bishop, the artistic director of Lincoln Center Theater.

name: Arthur Bloom
headline: Arthur Bloom, First Director of '60 Minutes,' Dies at 63
abstract: Arthur Bloom, who helped define the television newsmagazine concept as the original director of the CBS News program ''60 Minutes,'' died on Saturday at his home in Grandview-on-Hudson, N.Y. He was 63.     The cause was lung cancer, according to a spokesman for CBS News.

name: Neyda Martinez
headline: Neyda Martinez, Teacher and Guidance Counselor, Dies at 54
abstract: Neyda Martinez, a guidance counselor in the Bronx whose efforts to encourage her students to seek a college experience beyond the city was the subject of an article on the Education page on Dec. 28, died Thursday at Calvary Hospital in the Bronx. She was 54.     The cause was cancer, according to her daughter, Bennell LaPorte.

name: Coretta Scott King
headline: Coretta Scott King, a Civil Rights Icon, Dies at 78
abstract: Coretta Scott King, known first as the wife of the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., then as his widow, then as an avid proselytizer for his vision of racial peace and nonviolent social change, died Monday at a hospital in Mexico. She was 78.      The primary cause of death was ''insufficient cardio-respiratory,'' which simply means her heart and breathing stopped, said Dr. Carlos Guerrero Tejada, who certified her death. The underlying causes were cerebral vascular disease and ovarian cancer, according to the death certificate.

name: Nam June Paik
headline: Nam June Paik, 73, Dies; Pioneer of Video Art Whose Work Broke Cultural Barriers
abstract: Nam June Paik, avant-garde composer, performer and artist widely considered inventor of video art, dies at age 73; photo (M)

abstract: Endesha Ida Mae Holland, noted scholar and dramatist, dies at age 61 (M)

name: Moira Shearer
headline: Moira Shearer, Ballerina in 'The Red Shoes,' Dies at 80
abstract: Moira Shearer, a luminous star in the galaxy of British ballerinas who brought the Royal Ballet to international attention and whose dramatic portrayal as the doomed heroine of the 1948 film ''The Red Shoes'' was searingly impressed on generations of moviegoers, died in Oxford, England, on Tuesday. She was 80.     Her death was announced by her husband, the writer and broadcaster Ludovic Kennedy. He said Ms. Shearer had been weak since her birthday last month and died in John Radcliffe Hospital in Oxford, The Associated Press reported.

name: Christopher J. Makins
headline: Christopher J. Makins, 63, Expert on Foreign Relations, Dies
abstract: Christopher J. Makins, who followed his father into the British diplomatic service and then shifted course to become an influential expert on United States-European relations for Washington research organizations, died on Saturday at his home in Washington. He was 63.     The cause was complications of cancer of the head and neck, said his daughter, Marian Makins.

abstract: Boris Kostelanetz, considered dean of tax defense lawyers, dies at age 94 (M)

name: Tana Hoban

abstract: Tana Hoban, photographer of children who turned her photography into innovative kind of illustration for books for youngest audiences, dies at age 88; photos (M)

name: Betty Friedan
profession: Ignited a Movement With 'The Feminine Mystique
headline: Betty Friedan, Who Ignited a Movement With 'The Feminine Mystique,' Dies at 85
abstract: Betty Friedan, the feminist crusader and author whose searing first book, ''The Feminine Mystique,'' ignited the contemporary women's movement in 1963 and as a result permanently transformed the social fabric of the United States and countries around the world, died Saturday, her 85th birthday, at her home in Washington.     The cause was congestive heart failure, said Emily Bazelon, a family spokeswoman.

name: John L. Behler
headline: John L. Behler, 62, Dies; Influential Voice for Saving Reptiles
abstract: John L. Behler, a naturalist and curator of herpetology at the Bronx Zoo who became an influential and international voice for saving endangered turtles, snakes and other reptiles, died on Jan. 31 at his home in Amawalk, N.Y. He was 62.      The cause was congestive heart failure, his family said.

name: Herbert Schilder
headline: Herbert Schilder, 77, Surgeon Who Refined the Root Canal, Dies
abstract: Herbert Schilder, a Boston dental surgeon who refined the instruments and techniques used to perform root canals and made the procedure safer and more successful, died on Jan. 25 at his home in Newton, Mass. He was 77.      The cause was Lewy body disease, a brain malady, his family said.

name: Myron Waldman
headline: Myron Waldman, Who Drew Cartoon Stars, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Myron Waldman, an animator and illustrator who worked on such celebrated characters as Betty Boop, Popeye, Superman and Casper the Friendly Ghost during his long career, died Saturday at New Island Hospital in Bethpage, N.Y. He was 97 and lived in Wantagh, N.Y.      The cause was congestive heart failure, his family said.

name: Ronald Hector
headline: Ronald Hector, Face of the Carlyle Hotel, Is Dead at 66
abstract: Ronald Hector, the silver-haired fellow in the morning suit behind the front desk of the Carlyle hotel whose aplomb in juggling room preferences and protecting the privacy of princesses, prime ministers and pretenders was the stuff of lobby legend, died on Jan. 29 at Memorial Sloan-Kettering Cancer Center in Manhattan. He was 66.     The cause was pancreatic cancer, said his friend Martin Sonkin.

name: John S. Bainbridge
headline: John S. Bainbridge, 90, Legal Educator for African Leaders, Dies
abstract: John S. Bainbridge, who organized a law-education program that trained many leaders in emerging African nations in the 1960's and later helped establish the Touro College law center in Huntington, N.Y., died on Jan. 25 in Kennett Square, Pa. He was 90.     His family said he died after years of declining health.

name: Basil Worgul
headline: Basil Worgul, 58, Biologist, Who Studied Causes of Cataracts, Dies
abstract: Basil V. Worgul, a biologist at Columbia University who studied radiation's harmful effects on the eye, particularly as a cause of cataracts, and helped lead a long-term international study of thousands of workers exposed to radiation in the Chernobyl disaster in 1986, died on Jan. 19 at his home in Edgewater, N.J. He was 58.     The cause was a heart attack, his family said.

name: John Vaught
headline: John Vaught, 96, Longtime Mississippi Football Coach, Dies
abstract: John Vaught, who coached the University of Mississippi to national football prominence and developed the star quarterbacks Charlie Conerly and Archie Manning, died Friday in Oxford, Miss. He was 96.     His death was announced by the university.

name: Martin Feinstein
headline: Martin Feinstein, 84, Dies; Led the National Opera
abstract: Martin Feinstein, who helped the Kennedy Center in Washington and its resident opera company grow and fill a large, empty niche in the capital's cultural life as executive director of one, then general manager of the other, died on Sunday at his home in Potomac, Md. He was 84.     The cause was pancreatic cancer, according to the Washington National Opera, of which he was general manager from 1980 to 1995.

name: Jo Foxworth
headline: Jo Foxworth, Who Created D'Agostino Jingle, Dies at 87
abstract: Jo Foxworth, a doyenne of New York advertising, who wrote the words and commissioned the tune for the siren song intended to lure shoppers to D'Agostino supermarkets, died on Thursday at St. Vincent's Manhattan Hospital. She was 87 and lived in Greenwich Village.      The death was announced by her executrix, Renee Bennett.

name: Reuven Frank
headline: Reuven Frank, Producer Who Pioneered TV News Coverage at NBC, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Reuven Frank, a pioneering television news producer whose career at NBC ran from Huntley and Brinkley (whom he first paired on the evening news in the 1950's) to Tom Brokaw (whom he installed as a solo anchor in the 1980's), died Sunday at Englewood Hospital in New Jersey.     He was 85 and lived in Tenafly, N.J. The cause of death was complications of pneumonia, said a son, James A. Frank.

name: William A. Jones
headline: The Rev. William A. Jones, Civil Rights Activist, Dies at 71
abstract: The Rev. William A. Jones, who marshaled his golden voice and forceful personality to exert influence far beyond his Brooklyn pulpit in support of local and national civil rights causes, died on Feb. 4 at his home in Brooklyn. He was 71.     The cause was complications of kidney disease, said Carolyn McClair, publicist for Bethany Baptist Church, where Dr. Jones served for 43 years until his retirement last September.

name: Lou Jones
headline: Lou Jones, 74, Sprinting Star, Dies
abstract: Lou Jones, a former world-record holder in the 400 meters and a member of the United States 4x400-meter relay squad that won a gold medal at the 1956 Melbourne Olympics, died Friday at Montefiore Medical Center in the Bronx. He was 74 and lived in New Rochelle, N.Y.     His death was announced by his son Louis Jones IV.

name: Peter Ladefoged
headline: Peter Ladefoged, 80, Linguist Who Was Immersed in Speech, Is Dead
abstract: Peter Ladefoged, an internationally renowned linguist who spent his life blissfully awash in the whistles, murmurs, pops, clicks and trills that make up the world's spoken languages, died on Jan. 24 in London. Professor Ladefoged, who was returning to his home in Aliso Viejo, Calif., from fieldwork in India, was 80.     The cause was a stroke, said a spokesman for the University of California at Los Angeles, where he was distinguished professor emeritus of phonetics.

name: Frank Goodman
profession: Handler of Press and Broadway Stars
headline: Frank Goodman, 89, Handler of Press and Broadway Stars, Dies
abstract: Frank Goodman, one of the last of the old-time Broadway press agents, a star handler and headline hustler, died on Friday at the Tisch Hospital of the New York University Medical Center. He was 89 and lived on the Upper West Side of Manhattan.     The cause was congestive heart failure, said his daughter Karen Goodman.

name: Dave Tatsuno
headline: Dave Tatsuno, 92, Whose Home Movies Captured History, Dies
abstract: Dave Tatsuno, a Japanese-American businessman and amateur filmmaker whose home movies, shot in secret in the 1940's, offer a rare documentary portrait of life in an American internment camp during World War II, died on Jan. 26 at his home in San Jose, Calif. He was 92.     Mr. Tatsuno's family confirmed the death.

name: Peter Benchley
headline: Peter Benchley, Author of 'Jaws,' Dies at 65
abstract: Peter Benchley, whose 1974 novel ''Jaws'' turned shark attacks into a national obsession and who later used what he called his ''fish story'' to help promote oceanic conservation, died yesterday morning at his home in Princeton, N.J. He was 65.     The cause was pulmonary fibrosis, a progressive scarring of the lungs, said his wife, Wendy.

name: Edna Lewis
headline: Edna Lewis, 89, Dies; Wrote Cookbooks That Revived Refined Southern Cuisine
abstract: Edna Lewis, whose cookbooks revived nearly forgotten genre of refined Southern cooking while offering glimpse into African-American farm life in early 20th century, dies at age 89; photo (M)

name: James Yancey
headline: James Yancey, Producer Known for Soulful Hip-Hop, Dies at 32
abstract: James Yancey, innovative and influential hip-hop producer known as J Dilla or Jay Dee, dies at age 32; photo (M)

name: Michael Gilbert
headline: Michael Gilbert, 93, Dies; Wrote Law Into His Mysteries
abstract: Michael Gilbert, who somehow managed to produce dozens of intricately plotted and gracefully written detective stories and mysteries for stage, radio and television while carrying on separate career as senior partner in London law firm, dies at age 93; photo (M)

name: John Belluso
headline: John Belluso, Who Wrote Plays About Disability, Is Dead at 36
abstract: John Belluso, young playwright who translated his own experiences with physical disability into prolific body of promising work, dies at age 36 (S)

name: Robert B. Hotz

abstract: Robert B Hotz, aviation expert and writer who helped investigate NASA's role in explosion of space shuttle Challenger in 1986 and became strong critic of agency, dies at age 91 (M)

name: Yehuda Chitrik
headline: Rabbi Yehuda Chitrik, a Legend in Lubavitcher Circles, Is Dead at 106
abstract: Rabbi Yehuda Chitrik, legendary storyteller in Lubavitcher community, dies at age 106; photo (M)

name: Ernie Stautner
headline: Ernie Stautner, 80, Who Starred as Undersized N.F.L. Tackle, Is Dead
abstract: Ernie Stautner, undersized defensive tackle who became best player on Pittsburgh Steelers' woeful teams in 1950's, and was later enshrined in Pro Football Hall of Fame, dies at age 80; photo (M)

name: Barry Martin
headline: Barry Martin, Dancer and Choreographer, Dies at 44
abstract: Barry Martin, modern dancer who became choreographer after accident made him quadriplegic, dies at age 44; photo (M)

name: Ray Barretto
headline: Ray Barretto, a Master of the Conga Drum, Dies at 76

abstract: Helmut W Schulz, chemical engineer who received 64 patents in disparate fields like nuclear physics, rocketry and waste-to-energy porcesses despite having been blinded in laboratory accident as young man, dies at age 93 (S)

name: George T. Davis
headline: George T. Davis, 98, Dies; Celebrated Criminal Lawyer
abstract: George T Davis, swashbuckling criminal lawyer who over half century gained fame in high-profile cases, than 200 of them involving death penalty, dies at age 98; photo (M)

name: Who Won
headline: Lieutenant Who Won Pension Rights for Her Domestic Partner Dies at 49
abstract: Ocean County, NJ, police lieutenant Laurel Hester, who won battle with county freeholders to have her pension benefits passed on to domestic partner Stacie Andree, dies of lung cancer (M)

name: Dai Ailian

abstract: Dai Ailian, doyenne of dance in China, dies at age 89; photo (M)

name: William Cowsill
headline: William Cowsill, 58, Leader of Family Pop-Rock Band, Dies
abstract: William Cowsill, lead singer and guitarist of 1960's Cowsills band that inspired The Partridge Family television series, dies at age 58; photo (M)

name: Eli J. Segal
headline: Eli J. Segal, 63, Clinton Aide Who Led Major Initiatives, Dies
abstract: Eli J. Segal, who was the chief of staff in Gov. Bill Clinton's victorious campaign for president in 1992 and who went on to become an assistant in the Clinton White House, died Monday at his home in Boston. Mr. Segal, who headed the Clinton administration's AmeriCorps and Welfare-to-Work initiatives, was 63.     The cause was mesothelioma, an asbestos-related form of cancer, his family said in announcing the death.

name: Theodore Draper
headline: Theodore Draper, Freelance Historian, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Theodore Draper, a combative historian and social critic and one of the last of a generation of freelance intellectuals who wrote and lectured largely without academic affiliations or formal credentials, died yesterday at his home in Princeton, N.J. He was 93. His death was announced by his wife, Priscilla.     Mr. Draper went from Communist Party fellow traveler in the 1930's to liberal anticommunist in the 1950's and 60's before breaking with the Cold War hawks and attacking the United States' role in Vietnam. For a time he was also the leading historian of American Communism, writing two authoritative books about it.

name: Jill Fraser
profession: Directed Small but Noted British Theater
headline: Jill Fraser, 59, Who Directed Small but Noted British Theater, Dies
abstract: Jill Fraser, owner and artistic director of the Watermill Theater in Newbury, England, whose renown and influence far exceeds its size, died on Feb. 10. She was 59.      Although she had been battling cancer for four years, Ms. Fraser died of pneumonia at the Royal Berkshire Hospital in Reading, her husband and partner in the theater, James Sargant, said.

name: Archbishop Marcinkus
headline: Archbishop Marcinkus, 84, Banker at the Vatican, Dies
abstract: Paul C. Marcinkus, a prominent American archbishop and longtime head of the Vatican bank who was linked to a major Italian banking scandal in the 1980's, was found dead on Monday at his home in Sun City, Ariz. He was 84.     No cause of death had been determined yesterday, according to a spokeswoman for the Roman Catholic Diocese of Phoenix, which announced the death.

name: Slobodan Milosevic
profession: Former Yugoslav Leader Accused of War Crimes
headline: Slobodan Milosevic, 64, Former Yugoslav Leader Accused of War Crimes, Dies
abstract: Slobodan Milosevic, the Communist leader whose embrace of Serbian nationalism set off almost a decade of Balkan warfare, was found dead early Saturday in his cell at the United Nations detention center in The Hague, where he had been since 2001. He was 64.      Mr. Milosevic appeared to have died from natural causes, but tribunal officials said they would not be able to give a full account until an autopsy and toxicological report were completed. He was found lifeless on his bed in his cell, a court statement said. Mr. Milosevic's wife, and his partner of almost five decades, Mirjana Markovic, who, like his brother, Borislav, is living in Moscow, was informed of Mr. Milosevic's death, the court said.

headline: Lennart Meri, 76, of Estonia, Dies; President, Filmmaker, Writer
abstract: Lennart Meri, the first president of Estonia in the post-Soviet era and an internationally recognized filmmaker, travel writer and translator, died yesterday in the capital, Tallinn. He was 76.     The death was announced by the office of Estonia's current president, Arnold Ruutel, whose Web site said Mr. Meri had died in a hospital ''after a long and serious illness.'' Agence France-Presse reported that Mr. Meri had undergone an operation for brain cancer in August.

name: John Falotico
headline: John Falotico, Detective Who Arrested Berkowitz, Dies at 82
abstract: John M. Falotico, the detective who arrested David R. Berkowitz, the notorious ''Son of Sam'' killer, died on Saturday at his home in North Brunswick, N.J. He was 82.     The cause was colon cancer, said his niece, Jennifer Falotico Taylor.

name: Andrall E. Pearson
headline: Andrall E. Pearson, 80, Pepsi Executive Who Led a Spinoff, Is Dead
abstract: Andrall Edwin Pearson, a former president of PepsiCo who as an adviser after leaving the company helped engineer the spinoff of Pepsi's fast-food businesses -- KFC, Taco Bell and Pizza Hut -- died on Saturday at his home in Palm Beach, Fla. He was 80.      The cause was a heart attack, according to Alan Rappaport, his son-in-law.

name: Ray Meyer
headline: Ray Meyer, Former DePaul Coach, Dies at 92
abstract: Ray Meyer, a Hall of Fame basketball coach at DePaul University who began his career by tutoring an awkward George Mikan, modern basketball's first superstar, and went on to win 724 games over 42 seasons, died yesterday at an assisted-living facility outside Chicago, said Scott Reed, the university's sports information director. He was 92.     When Meyer arrived at DePaul in 1942, the Blue Demons played in the shadow of the Chicago elevated line at a drafty former theater known as the Old Barn. When he retired as coach in 1984, DePaul was a perennial national power showcasing its talent at the 17,500-seat Rosemont Horizon in the suburbs.

abstract: John Wilde, an American surrealist associated with the Magic Realist school of painting, whose fantastic, darkly humorous images brought him fame far beyond his native Wisconsin, died on March 9 at his home in Cooksville. He was 86.     The cause was cancer, said his dealer, Tory Folliard of the Tory Folliard Gallery in Milwaukee.

name: John Reynolds Gardiner
headline: John Reynolds Gardiner, 61, Author of Children's Books
abstract: John Reynolds Gardiner, an avowed nonreader throughout his childhood who became a best-selling children's book author, died on March 4 in Anaheim, Calif. He was 61 and lived in Huntington Beach, Calif.      The cause was longtime complications of necrotizing pancreatitis, his wife, Gloria Gardiner, said.

name: Oleg Cassini
profession: Designer for the Stars and Jacqueline Kennedy
headline: Oleg Cassini, Designer for the Stars and Jacqueline Kennedy, Dies at 92
abstract: Oleg Cassini, a son of impoverished Italian and Russian nobility who achieved fame and wealth as a fabulously successful couturier based in New York, designing clothes for some of the world's most glamorous women as well as middle-class shoppers, died on Friday on Long Island, where he had a home. He was 92.      His death was announced by his wife, Marianne Cassini. He also had a home in Manhattan.

name: Madeleine P. Cosman
headline: Madeleine P. Cosman, 68, Medieval Expert, Dies
abstract: Madeleine Pelner Cosman, a prominent writer, scholar and lecturer whose passion for what she called the ''glorious order'' of the past led her first to a career in medieval and Renaissance studies and more recently to wide public advocacy of tougher immigration laws, died on March 2 in Escondido, Calif. She was 68.     The cause was complications of scleroderma, a chronic disease of the connective tissue, her family said. Ms. Cosman, who moved to California in the late 1990's, was for decades a resident of Tenafly, N.J.

name: G. William Miller
headline: G. William Miller, 81, Former Top Economic Official, Dies
abstract: G. William Miller, a businessman and investment banker who was chairman of the Federal Reserve Board and treasury secretary under President Jimmy Carter, died Friday night at his home in Washington. He was 81.     The cause was idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, a relatively rare hardening and deterioration of the lungs, said Carol Juarer, his secretary at G. William Miller & Company in Washington. She said Mr. Miller was a nonsmoker who had been in good health all his life until the lung disease was diagnosed in June 2004.

name: O. Milton Gossett
headline: O. Milton Gossett, 80, Who Helped Globalize Ad Industry, Dies
abstract: O. Milton Gossett, a New York advertising executive who played a large role in the globalization of the industry in the 1980's, died on March 1 in Mount Kisco, N.Y. He was 80 and lived in South Salem, N.Y.     The cause was a stroke, his daughter, Lorraine said.

name: Lawrence M. Brass
headline: Dr. Lawrence M. Brass, Leader in Research on Stroke, Is Dead at 49
abstract: Dr. Lawrence M. Brass, a Yale neurologist and leader in the field of stroke research who played a major role in linking a common decongestant to a possible increased risk of strokes, died on March 8 at his home in Woodbridge, Conn. He was 49.     The cause was lung cancer, his family said. They said he was a nonsmoker.

name: Bill Beutel
profession: Longtime Anchor of 'Eyewitness News' in New York
headline: Bill Beutel, 75, Dies; Longtime Anchor of 'Eyewitness News' in New York
abstract: Bill Beutel, who helped bring about a sea change in the nature of local television news as the dapper and unruffled anchor of ''Eyewitness News'' at WABC-TV in New York for more than 30 years, died Saturday at his home in Pinehurst, N.C. He was 75.     The cause was complications from a progressive neurological disorder, his wife, Adair, said.

name: Andrew Sherratt
headline: Andrew Sherratt, 59, Who Studied Animal Husbandry, Is Dead
abstract: Andrew Sherratt, a British archaeologist whose explorations of animal husbandry and other civilizing practices shed light on European prehistory, died Feb. 24 near his home in Witney, Oxfordshire. He was 59.      The cause was heart failure, said a spokeswoman for the University of Sheffield, where Dr. Sherratt became a professor of Old World prehistory last year.

name: E. Russell Alexander
headline: E. Russell Alexander, 77, Public Health Expert
abstract: Dr. E. Russell Alexander, an epidemiologist and public health official who helped curb deadly disease outbreaks and raised concerns about federal plans to thwart a potential swine flu epidemic in the 1970's, when a vaccine was linked to a neurological disorder, died on Feb. 26 at his home in Seattle. He was 77.      The cause was islet cell carcinoma of the pancreas, his family said.

name: Luna Leopold
headline: Luna Leopold, River Researcher, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Luna B. Leopold, an ecologist and author whose studies of American rivers provided new insights into their depth, velocity and movement patterns that proved to be fundamental to all rivers, died on Feb. 23 at his home in Berkeley, Calif. He was 90.      His death was announced by the University of California, Berkeley, where he was a professor of geology and geophysics.

name: Charles Newman
headline: Charles Newman, 67, Writer and Literary Journal Editor, Dies
abstract: Charles Newman, an avant-garde novelist and critic who in 1964 turned a campus publication at Northwestern University into the prestigious literary magazine TriQuarterly and was its editor for more than a decade, died on March 15 in St. Louis. He was 67 and lived in St. Louis and Manhattan.     The cause was a heart attack, Mr. Newman's nephew Ben Ryder Howe said. At his death, Mr. Newman was a professor of English at Washington University in St. Louis, where he had taught since 1985.

name: Warren Bolster
headline: Warren Bolster, 59, Photographer of Surfers and Skateboarders, Is Dead
abstract: Warren Bolster’s innovative photography helped popularize surfing and skateboarding.

name: Ivan Luini
headline: Ivan Luini, 46, Dies in a Plane Crash; Executive Helped Popularize Plastics in American Stores
abstract: Ivan Luini helped bring plastic furniture out of the garden and into the American living room. Sergio Savarese also died in the crash, in Moffat County, Colo.

name: Robert Earl Jones
headline: Robert Earl Jones, 96, Broadway Actor, Dies
abstract: Robert Earl Jones was a stage and screen actor and the father of the actor James Earl Jones.

name: Edward J. King
headline: Ex-Gov. Edward J. King, 81, Who Defeated Dukakis, Dies
abstract: Edward J. King, a governor of Massachusetts who defeated the incumbent, Michael S. Dukakis, in the 1978 Democratic primary for governor but lost a rematch in 1982.

name: Margaret Phipps Boegner
headline: Margaret Phipps Boegner, 99, Who Founded Old Westbury Gardens, Is Dead
abstract: Margaret Phipps Boegner opened her family’s vast Long Island estate, Old Westbury Gardens, to the public.

name: David Lykken
headline: David Lykken, 78, Dies; Studied Behavior
abstract: David T. Lykken, whose studies of criminal behavior, polygraph testing and especially the genetics of personality in twins helped undermine some of the most cherished notions of social science, died Friday at his home in Minneapolis. He was 78.      The cause was heart failure, which struck Dr. Lykken in his sleep, his son Joseph said.

name: Mickey Hargitay
headline: Mickey Hargitay, 80, Actor and Former Mr. Universe, Dies
abstract: Mickey Hargitay, the Hungarian-born bodybuilder who won the 1955 Mr. Universe title, married the voluptuous actress Jayne Mansfield and went on to have his own acting career, died Thursday in Los Angeles. He was 80.     The cause was bone marrow cancer, said Bill Comstock, a spokesman for the family.

name: Joseph Hayes
headline: Joseph Hayes, 88, Author of ‘The Desperate Hours,’ Dies
abstract: Joseph Hayes, who wrote the novel ''The Desperate Hours,'' which he later turned into a Tony Award-winning play and a movie, died on Sept. 11 in St. Augustine, Fla., where he lived. He was 88.      Mr. Hayes died in a nursing home of complications from Alzheimer's disease, said his son Daniel Hayes.

name: Sven Nykvist
headline: Sven Nykvist, 83, a Master of Light in Films, Dies
abstract: Mr. Nykvist was one of the world’s foremost cinematographers, whose poetic use of light illuminated many of Ingmar Bergman’s greatest films.

name: Joe Glazer
headline: Joe Glazer, 88, a Singer and Songwriter for Labor, Dies
abstract: Joe Glazer, singer-songwriter known as Labor's Troubador who helped recruit new generation of protest singers, dies at age 88; photo (M)

name: V. Magistretti
headline: V. Magistretti, 85, Furniture Designer, Dies
abstract: Vico Magistretti was an architect and industrial designer celebrated as the dean of Italian modernism for his sculptural furniture and lamps.

name: Evelyn Ortner
headline: Evelyn Ortner, 82, a Booster of Brooklyn Brownstones, Dies
abstract: Mrs. Ortner, with her husband, Everett, was among the first, the most vocal and the most effective champions of the brownstone revival that spread from Brooklyn to the rest of the country.

name: Pham Xuan An
headline: Pham Xuan An Dies at 79; Reporter Spied for Hanoi
abstract: Pham Xuan An led a double life as a reporter for Western news organizations during the Vietnam War while spying for North Vietnam.

name: Henri Jayer
headline: Henri Jayer, Famed Maker of Burgundy Wines, Dies at 84
abstract: Henri Jayer was an untrained French vineyard worker who rose to become one of the most important winemakers in Burgundy.

name: Syd Thrift
headline: Syd Thrift, 77, Innovative Baseball Executive and Scout
abstract: Syd Thrift, the longtime major league executive and scout who revitalized the Pittsburgh Pirates franchise in the 1980's and championed innovative baseball techniques, died Monday in Milford, Del. He was 77.     Thrift's wife, Dolly, said he died hours after undergoing knee-replacement surgery and that autopsy results were expected next week.

name: Richard Caleal
headline: Richard Caleal, 94, Who Helped Design Innovative ’49 Ford, Dies
abstract: Richard D. Caleal helped create the hugely popular 1949 Ford credited with lifting the company out of its postwar financial slump.

name: Roy Brewer
headline: Roy Brewer, 97, Labor Chief in Blacklist-Era Hollywood, Dies
abstract: Roy M. Brewer was an ardent anti-Communist who headed the Hollywood branch of the movie industry’s leading union of stagehands during the blacklist era.

name: Beth Levine
headline: Beth Levine, ‘First Lady of Shoe Design,’ Is Dead at 91
abstract: Beth Levine, innovative American shoe designer, dies at age 91; photos (M)

name: Dean E. Wooldridge
headline: Dean E. Wooldridge, 93, Missile System Developer, Is Dead
abstract: Dean E. Wooldridge was a crucial figure in the development of the technology of nuclear warfare in the 1950’s.

name: Jack Banta
headline: Jack Banta, 81, Brooklyn Dodgers Pitcher
abstract: Jack Banta, pitcher for Brooklyn Dodgers who helped propel team to 1949 National League pennant, dies at age 81 (M)

name: Hélène Deschamps Adams
headline: Hélène Deschamps Adams, Wartime Hero, Dies at 85
abstract: Helene Deschamps Adams, French Resistance fighter during World War II, dies at age 85; photo (M)

name: Patrick Quinn
headline: Patrick Quinn, 56, an Official of Actors’ Equity Association, Dies
abstract: Patrick Quinn was about to become the first new executive director of the Actors’ Equity Association in 25 years.

name: Armin Jordan
profession: Swiss Conductor Known for French Music
headline: Armin Jordan, 74, Swiss Conductor Known for French Music, Dies
abstract: Armin Jordan had collapsed last Friday while conducting Prokofiev’s opera “The Love for Three Oranges.”

name: Fred N. Spiess
headline: Fred N. Spiess, 86, Is Dead; Helped Design Marine Station
abstract: Fred N. Spiess’s unusual floating laboratory has yielded a bounty of information about underwater acoustics and sea currents.

name: Malcolm Arnold
headline: Malcolm Arnold, Prolific British Composer, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Sir Malcolm Arnold was one of the best-known and most popular British composers of the 20th century.

name: Alan Fletcher
headline: Alan Fletcher, 74, Designer Whose Work Enlivened Britain, Dies
abstract: Alan Fletcher helped revive postwar British design and typography through his vibrant corporate identity work and book designs.

name: Thomas Stewart
headline: Thomas Stewart, 78, Baritone on Opera Stage, Dies
abstract: Thomas Stewart, baritone opera singer, dies at age 78; photo (M)

name: Gilbert Jonas
headline: Gilbert Jonas, 76, N.A.A.C.P. Fund-Raiser, Dies
abstract: Mr. Jonas was a longtime fund-raiser for the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People.

name: Alfred Mann
profession: Musicologist and Historian of the Baroque
headline: Alfred Mann, 89, Musicologist and Historian of the Baroque, Is Dead
abstract: Alfred Mann was perhaps best known for his translations of and commentary on the works of the Austrian composer and musical theorist J. J. Fux.

name: Alfred E. Mann
headline: Alfred E. Mann, Pioneer in Medical Devices, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Mann’s companies developed products ranging from pacemakers with rechargeable batteries to the first “artificial retina.”

name: Byron Nelson
profession: Standout for His Remarkable Golf Swing and 1945 Season
headline: Byron Nelson, a Standout for His Remarkable Golf Swing and 1945 Season, Dies at 94
abstract: Byron Nelson was the winner of a record 11 consecutive professional golf tournaments in 1945 and one of golf’s most renowned figures.

name: Iva Toguri D'Aquino
profession: Known as Tokyo Rose and Later Convicted of Treason
headline: Iva Toguri D’Aquino, Known as Tokyo Rose and Later Convicted of Treason, Dies at 90
abstract: Iva Toguri D'Aquino, Japanese-American convicted of treason for broadcasting Japanese wartime propaganda as Tokyo Rose, dies at age 90; photos (M)

name: Maureen Daly
headline: Maureen Daly, 85, Chronicler of Teenage Love, Dies
abstract: Ernestintine Bayer, pioneer of women's rowing, dies at age 97; photo (M)

name: Ernestine Bayer
headline: Ernestine Bayer, 97, Pioneer in Rowing, Dies
abstract: Ernestine Bayer, who founded a pioneering women's rowing club in 1938 on the Schuylkill in Philadelphia, rowed competitively into her 90's and became known as the mother of women's rowing, died Sept. 10 in Exeter, N.H. She was 97.     The cause was complications of pneumonia, said her daughter, Tina Bayer, a former world-class rower.

name: Harris Busch
profession: Expert on How Cancer Cells Work
headline: Harris Busch, 83, Expert on How Cancer Cells Work, Dies
abstract: Dr. Harris Busch helped unravel and describe aspects of the chemical structure of cancer cells.

name: Martha Holmes
headline: Martha Holmes, 83, Pioneer in Photography, Dies
abstract: Martha Holmes, pioneering photographer for Life magazine, dies at age 83; photos (M)

name: Frederic Wakeman
headline: Frederic Wakeman, 68, Scholar Who Enlivened Chinese History, Is Dead
abstract: Frederic Wakeman Jr. was an eminent scholar of Chinese history who wrote richly detailed books spanning seven centuries.

name: Padmini Ramachandran
headline: Padmini Ramachandran, 74, Actress and Dancer, Is Dead
abstract: Padmini Ramachandran, a star of Indian films who later started an influential school of Indian classical dance in New Jersey, died on Sept. 25 in Chennai (formerly Madras), India. She was 74.      The cause was a heart attack, according to hospital officials.

name: Robert H. Knight
headline: Robert H. Knight, 87, Influential Lawyer Who Served Several Presidents, Is Dead
abstract: Robert H. Knight was a Wall Street lawyer who played behind-the-scenes roles in sensitive political situations like the Bay of Pigs.

name: Marjorie G. Lewisohn
headline: Marjorie G. Lewisohn, Johns Hopkins Trustee, 87, Dies
abstract: Marjorie G. Lewisohn, a Manhattan internist, was the first woman to be a trustee of Johns Hopkins University.

name: Joseph F. Kauffman
headline: Joseph F. Kauffman, 84, Who Helped to Start Peace Corps, Dies
abstract: Joseph F. Kauffman helped start the Peace Corps and ran the basic training and then led the fight against war protesters at the University of Wisconsin.

name: Isabel Bigley
headline: Isabel Bigley, 80, Tony-Winning ‘Guys and Dolls’ Star, Dies
abstract: Isabel Bigley won a Tony Award in 1951 playing Sarah Brown, the Salvation Army missionary who falls in love with a handsome gambler in the raucous Broadway hit “Guys and Dolls.”

name: Helen Chenoweth-Hage
headline: Helen Chenoweth-Hage, 68, Former Representative, Dies
abstract: Former Representative Helen P. Chenoweth-Hage of Idaho was an archconservative who called for disbanding large parts of the federal government.

name: Joel T. Broyhill
headline: Joel T. Broyhill, 86, Congressman Who Opposed Integration, Dies
abstract: Joel T. Broyhill was an 11-term Republican congressman from Virginia known in the 50’s and 60’s for his energetic opposition to integration.

name: George Edwards
headline: George Edwards, 87, a Longtime Host on WQXR Radio
abstract: George Edward Steinhardt, who for 40 years, under name George Edwards, was host of Bright and Early program on WQXR, classical radio station owned by New York Times Co, dies at age 87 (M)

name: R. W. Apple Jr.
profession: Globe-Trotter for The Times and a Journalist in Full
headline: R. W. Apple Jr., Globe-Trotter for The Times and a Journalist in Full, Dies at 71
abstract: In more than 40 years, R.W. Apple Jr. wrote about war and revolution, politics and government, food and drink, and the revenge of living well from more than 100 countries.

name: Mary Orr
headline: Mary Orr, 95, an Author Who Inspired ‘All About Eve’, Is Dead
abstract: Mary Orr was an actress and writer whose first short story, about a scheming ingénue named Eve Harrington, became the Oscar-winning film “All About Eve.”

name: Robert Petersdorf
headline: Robert Petersdorf, 80, Major Force in U.S. Medicine, Dies
abstract: Dr. Robert G. Petersdorf was an internationally known infectious diseases expert who was also one of the most powerful figures in American medicine for many years.

name: Gary C. Comer
headline: Gary C. Comer, 78, Founder of Lands’ End, Dies
abstract: Gary C. Comer was the founder of the mail-order apparel company who printed a glossy catalog in the 1960’s that became a prototype of the magazinelike catalogs of today.

name: Peter M. Grosz
headline: Peter M. Grosz, 80, Authority on Early German Aircraft, Dies
abstract: Peter M. Grosz was an engineer and authority on German aircraft from World War I who was also the son of the German Expressionist painter George Grosz.

name: Friedrich Karl Flick
profession: Heir to a German Industrial Empire
headline: Friedrich Karl Flick, 79, Heir to a German Industrial Empire, Dies
abstract: Mr. Flick was an heir to vast wealth, a father’s notoriety and a name that stood for a sinister nexus of politics and big business.

name: Gilbert F. White
headline: Gilbert F. White, 94, Expert on Floods and Nature, Dies
abstract: Gilbert F. White was a geographer whose philosophy of accommodating nature instead of trying to master it had profound effects on policy and environmental thought.

name: Mortimer Ostow
headline: Mortimer Ostow, 88, Theorist on Anti-Semitism, Dies
abstract: Dr. Ostow was a psychiatrist and neuroscientist who studied the psychological sources of anti-Semitism and other expressions of religious and racial fanaticism.

name: Buck O’Neil
headline: Buck O’Neil, Negro Leagues Pioneer, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Buck O'Neil, starú

name: David G. Salten
headline: David G. Salten, 93, Expert on School Desegregation, Dies
abstract: David G. Salten was an innovative and influential educator who devised a desegregation plan for the New Rochelle, N.Y., school system.

name: Elizabeth Allen
profession: Stage Star Known for Memorable TV Line
headline: Elizabeth Allen, 77, Stage Star Known for Memorable TV Line, Is Dead
abstract: Elizabeth Allen, a leading actress on Broadway and in movies, got her start as the “Away we go!” girl on “The Jackie Gleason Show.”

name: Danial Shapiro
headline: Danial Shapiro, 48, Dancer Who Created Abstract Works, Dies
abstract: Danial Shapiro was a modern-dance choreographer known for his collaborations with his wife, Joanie Smith.

name: Kanshi Ram
headline: Kanshi Ram, 72, a Voice for India’s Outcasts, Dies
abstract: Kanshi Ram founded the Bahujan Samaj Party in India and achieved some success in mobilizing the voting power of the nation’s Dalits, or untouchables.

name: Timo Sarpaneva
headline: Timo Sarpaneva, 79, Glassmaker, Dies
abstract: Timo Sarpaneva, Finnish glassmaker, dies at age 79; photos (M)

name: Eve Adamson
headline: Eve Adamson, 68, Founder of Cocteau Troupe, Dies
abstract: Eve Adamson founded the Jean Cocteau Repertory and built it into a respected classical theater company.

name: William Whelan III
headline: William Whelan III, 66, Ex-Park Service Director, Dies
abstract: William Whelan III was a director of the National Park Service in the Carter administration who oversaw the doubling of the park system’s size with the creation of 10 parks in Alaska.

name: Raymond Noorda
headline: Raymond Noorda, 82, Novell Founder, Dies
abstract: Raymond J. Noorda was a co-founder of Novell Inc., a software company that helped pioneer computer networking.

name: Morris Tarshis
headline: Morris Tarshis, 87, Lawyer Who Oversaw City Franchises, Dies
abstract: Mr. Tarshis exercised behind-the-scenes power in New York City for a generation by settling labor strikes and, later, by determining who got city franchises.

name: Danièle Huillet
headline: Danièle Huillet, 70, Creator of Challenging Films, Dies
abstract: Daniele Huillet, creator of challenging and intensely debated films, dies at age 70; photo (M)

name: Saul Farber
headline: Dr. Saul Farber Dies at 88; Medical School Official
abstract: Dr. Saul J. Farber was a dean of New York University’s medical school who led prestigious medical organizations.

name: Robert Richenburg
headline: Robert Richenburg, 89, Artist of Abstract Expressionist Works, Dies
abstract: Robert Richenburg was an Abstract Expressionist painter whose early works were shown alongside those of Jackson Pollock and Willem de Kooning.

name: Howard Brett Kerzner
headline: Howard Brett Kerzner, 42, Dies; Led Global Resort Developer
abstract: Howard Brett Kerzner was the chief executive of Kerzner International Holdings, a global developer and operator of casinos and luxury resorts.

name: Peter H. Rossi
headline: Peter H. Rossi, 84, Sociologist Who Studied Homelessness, Dies
abstract: Peter H. Rossi was a prominent sociologist best known for documenting the changing face of American homelessness in the 1980’s.

name: Norman Salsitz
headline: Norman Salsitz, 86, Author Who Survived the Holocaust, Dies
abstract: Norman Salsitz’s harrowing tale of surviving the Holocaust by posing as a Christian took a particularly bizarre turn when he killed Polish partisans who were about to murder a group of Jews.

name: Gillo Pontecorvo
headline: Gillo Pontecorvo, 86, Director of ‘Battle of Algiers,’ Dies
abstract: Gillo Pontecorvo, Italian filmmaker who explored terrorism and torture in colonial Algeria in 1965 classic, The Battle of Algiers, dies at age 86; photos (M)

name: Gerry Studds
headline: Gerry Studds Dies at 69; First Openly Gay Congressman
abstract: Former Representative Gerry Studds was first elected in 1972 and represented Cape Cod and the Islands, New Bedford and the South Shore for 12 Congressional terms.

name: Winifred Bennett
headline: Winifred Bennett, 71, Is Dead; Proposed Jefferson DNA Tests
abstract: Winifred Bennett suggested that DNA testing might establish whether Thomas Jefferson fathered children by his slave Sally Hemings.

name: Todd Bolender
headline: Todd Bolender, a Dancer and Director, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Todd Bolender left a distinctive imprint on the New York City Ballet before leading the Kansas City Ballet and troupes abroad.

name: Freddy Fender
profession: Pop Singer in Both English and Spanish
headline: Freddy Fender, 69, Pop Singer in Both English and Spanish
abstract: Freddy Fender, popular singer in both English and Spanish, dies at age 69; photo (M)

name: Wang Guangmei
headline: Wang Guangmei, 85, Dies; Former First Lady of China
abstract: Wang Guangmei was the widow of President Liu Shaoqi and a powerful figure in China before she was imprisoned during the Cultural Revolution.

name: Carl A. Vergari
headline: Carl A. Vergari, 84, Leader of Westchester Prosecutors, Dies
abstract: Carl A. Vergari modernized and strengthened law enforcement efforts as district attorney of Westchester County.

name: Michelle Urry
headline: Michelle Urry, 66, the Editor of Cartoons for Playboy, Dies
abstract: Ms. Urry brought a wicked sense of humor and what she called an “inordinately dirty mind” to her position as cartoons editor of Playboy magazine.

name: Sheldon Meyer
headline: Sheldon Meyer, Oxford Press Editor, Dies at 80
abstract: Sheldon Meyer was a distinguished editor of nonfiction books who was almost single-handedly responsible for the Americanization of Oxford University Press.

name: Marcia Tucker
profession: Founder of a Radical Art Museum
headline: Marcia Tucker, 66, Founder of a Radical Art Museum, Dies
abstract: Marcia Tucker was a forceful curator who responded to being fired from the Whitney Museum of American Art by founding the New Museum of Contemporary Art.

name: Rafael Quintero
headline: Rafael Quintero, 66, Secret Agent Who Stalked Castro for C.I.A., Dies
abstract: Rafael Quintero Ibarbia, secret agent who stalked Castro for Central Intelligence Agency, dies at age 66 (M)

name: Christopher Glenn
profession: Voice on CBS Radio and Television
headline: Christopher Glenn, 68, a Voice on CBS Radio and Television, Dies
abstract: Joseph Christopher Glenn, CBS News correspondent, dies at age 68; photo (M)

name: Marc Hodler
headline: Marc Hodler, 87, Who Exposed Olympic Bribery, Is Dead
abstract: Marc Hodler, who in 1998 exposed widespread bribery among Olympic delegates, dies at age 87; photo (M)

name: Paul Halmos
headline: Paul Halmos, 90, Mathematician Known for Simplifying Concepts, Dies
abstract: Paul R. Halmos was a mathematician known for exploring the implications of probability theory and helping simplify the expression of mathematical concepts.

name: Anna Russell
headline: Anna Russell, Deft Parodist of Operatic Culture, Dies at 94
abstract: Anna Russell was the prima donna of operatic parody who claimed to have begun her career as “prima donna of the Ellis Island Opera House.”

name: Hermann F. Eilts
headline: Hermann F. Eilts, Adviser to Kissinger on Mideast, Dies
abstract: Hermann Frederick Eilts was a diplomat in the Middle East who helped Henry A. Kissinger with his shuttle diplomacy, nursed President Anwar el-Sadat of Egypt through the Camp David peace talks and dodged a Libyan hit team.

name: Alvin M. Weinberg
headline: Alvin M. Weinberg, 91, Dies; Advocated Nuclear Power
abstract: Alvin Martin Weinberg, nuclear scientist and leading advocate for commercial nuclear power, dies at age 91; photo (M)

name: Herbert B. Leonard
profession: Producer of Movies and TV Series
headline: Herbert B. Leonard, 84, Producer of Movies and TV Series, Dies
abstract: Herbert B. Leonard was a film and television producer who left an indelible mark on American popular culture with television series including “Route 66” and “Naked City.”

name: Sigmund Strochlitz
headline: Sigmund Strochlitz, 89, Leader in Holocaust Causes, Dies
abstract: Mr. Strochlitz was a Holocaust survivor who worked with his close friend Elie Wiesel to create the National Holocaust Memorial Museum.

name: Irene Galitzine
headline: Princess Irene Galitzine Dies; Founder of a Fashion House
abstract: Princess Irene Galitzine was a descendant of Russian nobility who founded a glamorous fashion house in Italy.

name: Jane Wyatt
headline: Jane Wyatt, Mother on ‘Father Knows Best,’ Dies at 96
abstract: Jane Wyatt starred in the 1950’s television sitcom “Father Knows Best,” as well as in films and on Broadway.

name: William Bright
headline: William Bright, 78, Expert in Indigenous Languages, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Bright spent more than half a century inventorying the vanishing riches of the indigenous languages of the United States.

name: John V. Murra
headline: John V. Murra, 90, Professor Who Recast Image of Incas, Dies
abstract: John V. Murra was a professor of anthropology who culled voluminous Spanish colonial archives for research that reshaped the image of the Incas and their vast South American empire.

name: Edgar Summerlin
headline: Edgar Summerlin, 78, Composer Who Brought Jazz to Church, Dies
abstract: Edgard E Summerlin, jazz musician and composer who wrote early jazz music for church services, dies at age 78 (M)

name: Eric Newby
headline: Eric Newby, 86, Acclaimed British Travel Writer, Dies
abstract: Eric Newby was a dean of postwar British travel writing who spent more than half a century visiting some of the world’s remotest places in journeys that to his great delight often went horribly wrong.

name: Spoony Singh
headline: Spoony Singh, 83, Dies; Created Hollywood Wax Museum
abstract: Spoony Singh was a canny but star-struck entrepreneur whose brainstorm was to offer gawking Hollywood tourists wax statues of movie stars.

name: S. Peter Rosen
headline: S. Peter Rosen, 73, Physicist Who Guided Federal Research, Dies
abstract: S. Peter Rosen was a physicist who combined pioneering studies of the subatomic particles called neutrinos with an administrative role in helping to guide federal research in high-energy physics.

name: Benjamin Meed
profession: Was a Key Advocate for Holocaust Survivors
headline: Benjamin Meed, 88, Who Was a Key Advocate for Holocaust Survivors, Dies
abstract: Mr. Meed in the decades after the war gathered Jewish Holocaust survivors together by the tens of thousands, reuniting people with friends, neighbors and family members.

name: Leonid Hambro
headline: Leonid Hambro, 86, Pianist With an Astounding Memory, Dies
abstract: Leonid Hambro was a concert pianist noted for his prodigious memory, improvising genius and humorous musical desecrations as Victor Borge’s straight man.

name: Arthur Hill
headline: Arthur Hill, Actor Who Won Tony for ‘Virginia Woolf,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Arthur Hill brought engrossing complexity and understated intelligence to hundreds of roles on stage, screen and television and won a Tony Award for his performance in “Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf?”

name: Todd Skinner
headline: Todd Skinner, a Pioneer of Free Climbing, Dies at 47
abstract: Todd Skinner was an internationally renowned rock climber who made first ascents on dozens of the world’s most treacherous routes and shared those adventures as a motivational speaker.

name: Lawrence C. Kolb
headline: Lawrence C. Kolb, 95, Leader in Mental Health Movement, Dies
abstract: Dr. Lawrence C. Kolb was a prominent mental health administrator and researcher who helped create the community mental health movement and became the public face of psychiatry for a generation of New Yorkers.

name: Ghulam Ishaq Khan
headline: Ghulam Ishaq Khan, 91, Former President of Pakistan, Dies
abstract: Mr. Khan was a powerful bureaucrat who led Pakistan from 1988 to 1993 and dismissed two governments on charges of corruption.

name: Lawrence W. Levine
headline: Lawrence W. Levine, 73, Historian and Multiculturalist, Dies
abstract: Lawrence W. Levine was a prolific historian whose deeply researched, tightly argued books challenged conventional wisdom in areas ranging from Shakespeare to slave songs to today’s college curriculums.

name: Petra Cabot
headline: Petra Cabot, Designer of the 1950s-Era Skotch Kooler, Dies at 99
abstract: Petra Cabot’s most famous work was an insulated pail covered with plaid, the ubiquitous Skotch Kooler of the 1950s.

name: Red Auerbach
headline: Red Auerbach, 89, Who Built a Basketball Dynasty
abstract: Red Auerbach, who built Boston Celtics into one of greatest sports dynasties and presided over 16 National Basketball Association championship teams as coach, general manager and club president, dies at age 89; photos (M)

name: Joe Niekro
headline: Joe Niekro, a Master of the Knuckleball, Is Dead at 61
abstract: Joe Niekro dies at age 61; knuckleballing pitcher won 221 major league games in 22 seasons and combined with his Hall of Fame brother Phil to win more games than any pair of brothers in major league history; pitched 11 seasons with Houston Astros and also played for Atlanta Braves and New York Yankees; photo (M)

name: Pontus Hulten
headline: Pontus Hulten, 82, Champion of Contemporary Art, Dies
abstract: Pontus Hulten’s achievements spanned many countries and the founding directorships of several museums.

name: Arthur Holleb
headline: Dr. Arthur Holleb, 85, Who Promoted Screening for Breast Cancer, Dies
abstract: Dr. Arthur I. Holleb, as chief medical officer of the American Cancer Society, pushed to have mammograms provided to women under 50.

name: Jozsef Gregor
headline: Jozsef Gregor, 66, Bass-Baritone Known for Compelling Portrayals, Dies
abstract: Jozsef Gregor was a bass-baritone who parlayed stardom in his native Hungary into a second-act opera career in the United States.

name: Arnold Sundgaard
headline: Arnold Sundgaard, Lyricist and Playwright, Is Dead at 96
abstract: Arnold Sundgaard was a lyricist, librettist and playwright who collaborated with some of the most distinguished artists of the 20th century.

name: Bernice Kanner
headline: Bernice Kanner, 57, Ad Columnist and Author, Dies
abstract: Bernice Kanner, author of books and articles on marketing, dies at age 57 (M)

name: Richard Gilman
headline: Richard Gilman, Theater Critic, Dies at 83
abstract: Richard Gilman's elegant, contentious voice resonated through four decades in American letters, earning him both admirers and enemies of partisan fierceness.

name: P.W. Botha
headline: P.W. Botha, South Africa’s Ex-Leader, Dies at 90
abstract: P.W. Botha was the hard-nosed South African leader who struggled vainly to preserve apartheid rule.

name: Clifford Geertz
headline: Clifford Geertz, Cultural Anthropologist, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Clifford Geertz was a cultural anthropologist whose work focused on interpreting the symbols he believed give meaning and order to people’s lives.

name: Sally Lilienthal
headline: Sally Lilienthal, 87, a Leader in Opposing Nuclear Weapons, Dies
abstract: Sally Lilienthal established one of the largest American foundations dedicated to preventing the spread of nuclear, chemical and biological weapons.

name: Thomas R. Jones
headline: Thomas R. Jones, 93, a Judge Who Agitated for Urban Revival, Dies
abstract: Justice Jones challenged Senator Robert F. Kennedy to address urban malaise and became the founding chairman of the Bedford-Stuyvesant Restoration Corporation.

name: Thomas V. Jones
profession: Builder of Northrop Into Big Military Contractor
headline: Thomas V. Jones, Builder of Northrop Into Big Military Contractor, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Jones was one of the last of the swashbuckling breed of aerospace-industry titans who were almost synonymous with their corporations and the aircraft they produced.

name: Silas Simmons
headline: Silas Simmons, 111, Veteran of Baseball’s Negro Leagues, Is Dead
abstract: Silas Simmons, former Negro Leagues baseball player believed to be longest-living professional baseball player in history, dies at age 111; photos (M)

name: William Styron
headline: William Styron, Novelist, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Styron's early work, including "Lie Down in Darkness," won him wide recognition as a distinctive voice of the South, and an heir to William Faulkner. In subsequent fiction, like "The Confessions of Nat Turner" and "Sophie's Choice," he transcended his own immediate world and moved across historical and cultural lines. Critics and readers alike ranked him among the best of the generation that suceeded Hemingway and Faulkner.

name: Robert Anderson
headline: Robert Anderson, Former Chairman of Rockwell, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Robert Anderson, former president and chairman of Rockwell International Corporation, dies at age 85 (M)

name: Robert O. Anderson
headline: Robert O. Anderson, Oil Executive, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Anderson’s accomplishments included discovering oil in Alaska, becoming America’s largest rancher and giving generously to environmental causes.

name: Robert Anderson
headline: Robert Anderson, Playwright of ‘Tea and Sympathy,’ Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Anderson was among the theater’s most visible, serious playwrights of the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Florence Klotz
headline: Florence Klotz, 86, Creator of Broadway Styles, Dies

headline: Henry Pearson, Op Art Painter Who Was Inspired by Mapmaking, Dies at 92

headline: Larry Zox, 69, Abstract Painter of Dynamic, Geometric Works, Dies

headline: Abdul-Amir al-Jamri, 67, Bahrain Shiite Cleric, Dies

name: Scotty Schulhofer
