name: George Latshaw
headline: George Latshaw, 83, Dies; Made Puppetry Into an Art
abstract: George Latshaw was an internationally renowned puppeteer who for half a century breathed life into a diverse array of inanimate objects.

name: Bertram Powers
headline: Bertram Powers, Leader of Newspaper Printers, Dies at 84
abstract: Bertram A. Powers was the longtime head of the New York printers’ union, who led one of the nation’s longest and most debilitating newspaper strikes.

name: Herman Klurfeld
headline: Herman Klurfeld, 90, Dies; Wrote Winchell Columns and Quips
abstract: Herman Klurfeld, ghostwriter for legendary newspaper and radio columnist Walter Winchell for almost 30 years, dies at age 90 (M)

name: Frank Stanton
headline: Frank Stanton, Broadcasting Pioneer, Dies at 98
abstract: Frank Stanton was the industry’s most articulate and persuasive spokesman while president of CBS.

name: James Brown
headline: James Brown, the ‘Godfather of Soul,’ Dies at 73
abstract: James Brown was the singer, songwriter, bandleader and dancer who indelibly transformed 20th-century music.

name: James F. Brown
headline: James F. Brown, Radio Free Europe Chief, Dies at 81
abstract: As director of the network, Mr. Brown played a seminal role in the rise of the Solidarity movement, which eventually toppled the Communist Party in Poland.

name: Frank Tremaine

abstract: As a young reporter Frank Tremaine filed what is believed to have been the first eyewitness account of the bombing of Pearl Harbor.

name: William Booth
headline: William Booth, Judge and Civil Rights Leader, Dies at 84
abstract: William H. Booth was a former New York City judge who challenged racial discrimination as a civil rights leader and as chairman of the city’s Commission on Human Rights.

name: Gerald Ford
headline: Gerald Ford, 38th President, Dies at 93
abstract: Gerald R. Ford was thrust into the presidency in 1974 in the wake of the Watergate scandal, but lost his own bid for election after pardoning President Richard M. Nixon.

name: Henry M. Beachell
headline: Henry M. Beachell Dies at 100; Developed New Rice Plant
abstract: Henry M. Beachell was a plant breeder whose cultivation of a remarkably fecund new rice plant led to greatly increased yields of the crop in developing countries of Asia.

name: Wilma Dykeman
profession: Writer on the Environment and Race

name: Rudolf de Crignis

name: Robert Boehm

abstract: Robert Boehm was the chairman of the Center for Constitutional Rights, a nonprofit group most recently in the forefront of an effort to secure the rights for those held at Guantánamo.

name: Seymour Martin Lipset
headline: Seymour Martin Lipset, Sociologist, Dies at 84
abstract: Seymour Martin Lipset was a pre-eminent sociologist, political scientist and incisive theorist on American uniqueness.

name: Vincent Sardi Jr.
profession: Restaurateur and Unofficial Mayor of Broadway
headline: Vincent Sardi Jr., Restaurateur and Unofficial ‘Mayor of Broadway,’ Dies at 91

name: Robert Noortman

name: Mary Stolz

name: E. Howard Hunt

name: Ryszard Kapuscinski

name: Lisa E. Goldberg

name: Helmut Wimmer

name: James Farley

name: John Lavelle

name: Donald E. Osterbrock

name: Liz Renay

name: Glen Tetley

name: Deborah Orin-Eilbeck

name: Robert Drinan

name: Bing Devine

abstract: Bing Devine transformed the St. Louis Cardinals and the Mets into World Series champions in the 1960s.

name: Carter Harman

abstract: Carter Harman worked for two decades as a music critic, first for The New York Times from 1947 to 1952, and for Time magazine from 1952 to 1957, and then in Puerto Rico through the mid-1960s.

name: Molly Ivins

name: Maureen Cannon

name: Schoolboy Friedkin

name: Joseph S. Farland
headline: Joseph S. Farland, 92, Envoy Who Helped in Kissinger Ruse, Dies
abstract: Joseph S. Farland helped Henry A. Kissinger surreptitiously slip into China for 36 hours to lay the groundwork for President Richard M. Nixon’s historic visit to China.

name: Gordon Macklin
headline: Gordon Macklin, 78, Pioneer in Electronic Stock Trading, Dies
abstract: Gordon S. Macklin helped usher in the era of electronic trading of securities when he oversaw the development of the Nasdaq.

name: Gian Carlo Menotti
profession: Composer of Amahl and Other Popular Operas
headline: Gian Carlo Menotti, Composer of ‘Amahl’ and Other Popular Operas, Dies at 95
abstract: Gian Carlo Menotti wrote his first opera before he was 11 and went on to become perhaps the most popular and prolific opera composer of his time.

name: Bob Carroll Jr.
profession: Writer of the Zany I Love Lucy
headline: Bob Carroll Jr., 88, a Writer of the Zany ‘I Love Lucy,’ Dies
abstract: Bob Carroll Jr. was a founding writer of “I Love Lucy” who helped introduce millions of viewers to the joys of frenzied grape stomping and warp-speed chocolate-stuffing.

name: Whitney Balliett
headline: Whitney Balliett, New Yorker Jazz Critic, Dies at 80
abstract: Whitney Balliett was a jazz critic who in more than 40 years at The New Yorker magazine encouraged readers to hear jazz through his vividly metaphorical writing.

name: Eric von Schmidt
profession: Performer and Inspiration to Folk Singers
headline: Eric von Schmidt, 75, a Performer and Inspiration to Folk Singers, Dies
abstract: Eric von Schmidt was a performer and composer of folk music and a mentor to singers like Bob Dylan and Joan Baez.

name: Calvin H. Plimpton
profession: Led Way for Women at Amherst
headline: Calvin H. Plimpton Dies at 88; Led Way for Women at Amherst
abstract: Calvin H. Plimpton was an educator instrumental in opening Amherst College’s doors to women.

name: Elizabeth Tashjian
headline: Elizabeth Tashjian, 94, an Expert on Nuts, Dies
abstract: Elizabeth Tashjian debated whether she was a nut culturist or a nut artist, but was indisputably, well, nuts enough about nuts.

name: Roy Kuhlman
headline: Roy Kuhlman Dies at 83; Designer for Grove Press
abstract: Roy Kuhlman’s jazzlike improvisational paintings and graphics for Grove Press books in the 1950s and ’60s introduced an Abstract Expressionist style to graphic design.

name: George Becker
profession: Led Steelworkers Through Period of Growth
headline: George Becker, Who Led Steelworkers Through Period of Growth, Dies at 78
abstract: George Becker followed his father’s footsteps into a steel mill in his Illinois hometown and rose to become the sixth president of the United Steelworkers union.

name: Ralph de Toledano
profession: Writer Known as a Nixon Friend
headline: Ralph de Toledano, 90, Writer Known as a Nixon Friend, Dies
abstract: Ralph de Toledano was a news magazine editor, syndicated columnist and author of 25 books who was best known for his friendship with Richard M. Nixon and his passionate embrace of the conservative cause.

name: Hans Wegner
headline: Hans Wegner Dies at 92; Danish Furniture Designer
abstract: Mr. Wegner’s furniture — most famously his chairs — helped change the course of design history in the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Barbara McNair
profession: Singer, Actress and Host of a TV Show
headline: Barbara McNair, 72, a Singer, Actress and Host of a TV Show, Dies
abstract: Ms. McNair was a cabaret singer, actress and television personality of the 1960s who was noted as much for her stunning appearance as for her versatile voice.

name: M. Lamar Muse
headline: M. Lamar Muse, 86, Dies; Led Southwest Airlines
abstract: M. Lamar Muse was the first president of Southwest Airlines and a pioneer of airline deregulation.

name: Frankie Laine
headline: Frankie Laine, 93, the Hit-Making Crooner Who Used His Voice ‘Like a Horn,’ Is Dead
abstract: Frankie Laine was a singer who achieved enormous popularity in the 1940s and 50s with a robust voice and a string of hits including “That’s My Desire,” “Mule Train,” “Ghost Riders in the Sky” and “Jezebel.”

name: David W. Denton
headline: David W. Denton, Former Federal Prosecutor, Dies at 57
abstract: David W. Denton was once the third-ranking prosecutor in the office of the United States attorney for the Southern District of New York.

name: Lew Burdette
headline: Lew Burdette, Masterful Pitcher, Dies at 80
abstract: The Milwaukee Braves’ right-hander beat the Yankees three times in the 1957 World Series in one of the most dominant pitching performances in baseball’s postseason history.

name: Willye B. White
headline: Willye B. White, the First 5-Time U.S. Track Olympian, Dies at 67
abstract: Willye B. White willed her way out of the Mississippi Delta cotton fields to become America’s best female long jumper.

name: Alan MacDiarmid
profession: Won Nobel for Work With Plastic
headline: Alan MacDiarmid, 79, Who Won Nobel for Work With Plastic, Dies
abstract: Alan G. MacDiarmid shared the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2000 for the discovery of plastics that conduct electricity like metals.

name: Anna Nicole Smith
headline: Anna Nicole Smith Dies at 39
abstract: Anna Nicole Smith was a former Playboy centerfold, actress and television personality who was famous for being rich (sporadically); litigious (chronically); and, above all, for being famous.

name: Bradley Krause
headline: Bradley Krause, 58, Kinko’s Partner, Is Dead
abstract: Bradley Krause became a founding partner of the office supply and printing company by raising his hand in his college graphics arts class.

name: Leon J. Thal
headline: Leon J. Thal, Neurologist Who Led Study for Alzheimer’s Drugs, Dies at 62
abstract: Leon J. Thal was a leading researcher on drugs to treat Alzheimer’s disease and other forms of dementia.

name: Ellis W. Williamson
headline: Ellis W. Williamson, Who Led Troops in Vietnam, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Maj. Gen. Ellis W. Williamson led the first Army combat troops into South Vietnam and participated in the D-Day landings in Normandy in World War II and the Inchon landings in the Korean War.

name: Nelson W. Polsby
profession: Author and a Scholar of Politics
headline: Nelson W. Polsby, 72, Author and a Scholar of Politics, Dies
abstract: Nelson W. Polsby marshaled intellectual rigor, lucid writing and a knack for drawing striking lessons from real-life observation in his enduring studies of Congress and the presidency.

name: Ken Kennedy
headline: Ken Kennedy, 61, a Pioneer of Computer Software, Dies
abstract: Ken Kennedy was a Rice University computer scientist whose software design work paved the way for the broad scientific and engineering use of modern supercomputers.

name: Harriett Woods
headline: Harriett Woods, 79, Women’s Political Leader, Dies
abstract: Harriett Woods was the first woman to win statewide office in Missouri before leading a national effort to promote women as candidates.

name: Ian Richardson
headline: Ian Richardson, 72, Versatile Scottish Actor, Dies
abstract: Ian Richardson was a Scottish film, television and stage actor who was a major figure at the Royal Shakespeare Company before gaining international fame for his television portrayal of a deliciously villainous politician.

name: George Sadek
headline: George Sadek, 78, Graphic Design Educator, Dies
abstract: George Sadek, a former dean of the Cooper Union School of Art in Manhattan, transformed graphic design education by having students work on actual projects for nonprofit institutions.

name: Michael Hurson
headline: Michael Hurson, Whimsical Artist, Dies at 65
abstract: Michael Hurson, a New York-based artist, created drawings and paintings that imbued human and inanimate subjects alike with a stylish caricatural energy.

name: Michael Shurtleff
profession: Casting Director for Broadway and Hollywood
headline: Michael Shurtleff, Casting Director for Broadway and Hollywood, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Shurtleff for years was a leading Broadway casting director and the author of an influential book about the audition process.

name: Edmund C. Arnold
headline: Edmund C. Arnold, Bold Newspaper Designer, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Arnold in the 1950s altered the rigid layouts then common in American newspapers and influenced a generation of newspaper designers.

name: Leonard Berg
headline: Leonard Berg, 79, Neurologist Who Specialized in Dementia, Dies
abstract: Dr. Berg helped design a leading test used to assess social functioning in patients with Alzheimer’s disease and other forms of dementia.

name: Fred Mustard Stewart
headline: Fred Mustard Stewart, 74, Novelist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Stewart was a best-selling writer of popular novels, several of which were adapted for the screen.

name: Roger Bacon
headline: Roger Bacon, 80, Researcher Known for Aerospace Innovation, Dies
abstract: The work of the physicist and materials scientist contributed to a revolution in the heat-resistant materials used in aircraft and satellites.

name: Eddie Feigner
headline: Eddie Feigner, Hard-Throwing, Barnstorming Showman of Softball, Dies at 81
abstract: For 60 years, Eddie Feigner barnstormed the globe with his four-man softball team, hurling 100-mile-an-hour pitches that struck out Willie Mays and 141,516 other batters.

name: Charles Walgreen Jr.
headline: Charles Walgreen Jr., 100, Who Built the Family Drug Chain, Is Dead
abstract: Charles Walgreen Jr.  helped build his father’s drugstore chain into America’s biggest.

name: Jeannette Ordman
headline: Jeannette Ordman, Director of Israeli Dance Company, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Ordman was a South African-born dancer and teacher who headed the Bat-Dor Dance Company, one of Israel’s most important contemporary-dance organizations.

name: Nat H. Hentel
headline: Nat H. Hentel, 87, Former Judge and Prosecutor, Dies
abstract: Nat H. Hentel was a former State Supreme Court justice and an interim Queens district attorney in 1966.

name: Ivan Boszormenyi-Nagy
headline: Ivan Boszormenyi-Nagy, 86, an Innovator of Family Therapy, Dies
abstract: Dr. Ivan Boszormenyi-Nagy was a psychiatrist who helped establish a powerful kind of therapy for mental illness that brings patients’ extended families into treatment as allies.

name: Florence Z. Melton
headline: Florence Z. Melton, 95, Creator of Slippers, Dies
abstract: Florence Zacks Melton took a material invented as a helmet liner for World War II tank crewmen and turned it into cushy foam-rubber slippers.

name: Bent Skovmand
headline: Bent Skovmand, Seed Protector, Dies at 61
abstract: The plant scientist helped to create the “doomsday vault,” a massively fortified cavern to safeguard three million kinds of unique crop seeds against catastrophe.

name: Thomas Fairchild
headline: Thomas Fairchild, 94, Dies; Tried to Unseat McCarthy
abstract: Thomas E. Fairchild was a federal appeals court judge for four decades who tried unsuccessfully to unseat Senator Joseph McCarthy in 1952.

name: Mordkhe Schaechter
headline: Mordkhe Schaechter, 79, Leading Yiddish Linguist, Dies
abstract: Dr. Schaechter was a teacher, author and promoter, founding organizations devoted to furthering the use of Yiddish.

name: Bruce Metzger
headline: Bruce Metzger, Scholar and Bible Translator, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Metzger, an eminent scholar and translator of the Bible, was a world-renowned authority on translating the New Testament from the original Greek.

name: Walter Sondheim Jr.
headline: Walter Sondheim Jr., 98, Leader in Baltimore Renewal, Dies
abstract: Walter Sondheim Jr., a longtime Baltimore civic leader, played key roles in desegregating the city’s schools and redeveloping its downtown.

name: Gordon Wright
headline: Gordon Wright, Founder of Arctic Chamber Orchestra, Dies at 72
abstract: Gordon Wright was a conductor who championed obscure composers and made music across the chilly climes of Alaska as founder of the Arctic Chamber Orchestra.

name: Ray Evans
profession: Lyricist of Hit Songs From Movies
headline: Ray Evans, Lyricist of Hit Songs From Movies, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Evans was a pop lyricist who teamed up with the composer and lyricist Jay Livingston to write three Academy Award-winning songs and one of Nat King Cole’s best-known classics.

name: Steven Pimlott
headline: Steven Pimlott, 53, Director of 1993 ‘Dreamcoat’ Revival, Dies
abstract: Steven Pimlott was a British theater and opera director best known in the United States for his productions of “Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat” and “Bombay Dreams.”

name: Maurice Papon
headline: Maurice Papon, Convicted Vichy Official, 96, Dies
abstract: Maurice Papon was a prominent French functionary convicted in 1998 of complicity in Nazi crimes against humanity during the German occupation in World War II.

name: Ian Stevenson
headline: Ian Stevenson Dies at 88; Studied Claims of Past Lives
abstract: Ian Stevenson, an academic psychiatrist, abandoned Freud as too unscientific and turned to the paranormal as a tool with which to plumb the human psyche.

name: Sheridan Morley
headline: Sheridan Morley, British Theater Critic and Biographer, Dies at 65
abstract: The prominent British critic, biographer and broadcaster  devoted his career to chronicling and, often, celebrating plays and players.

name: Aaron Lerner
headline: Aaron Lerner, 86, Innovative Skin Doctor, Dies
abstract: The Yale dermatologist was the leader of a team of researchers who discovered melatonin, a powerful hormone regulating human sleep-wake cycles.

name: Joseph Low
headline: Joseph Low, 95, Illustrator of Children’s Books, Dies
abstract: Joseph Low was an illustrator who did absurdist covers for The New Yorker and won Caldecott honors for the children’s book “Mice Twice.’'

name: Robert Adler
headline: Robert Adler, Zenith Physicist, Dies at 93
abstract: Robert Adler was a physicist and prolific inventor best known as the co-inventor of the television remote control device.

name: Charles Langford
headline: Charles Langford, 84, Lawyer Who Represented Rosa Parks, Dies
abstract: Charles Langford was a civil rights lawyer whose best-known client was a Montgomery, Ala., seamstress named Rosa Parks.

name: Elliott Baker
headline: Elliott Baker, a Screenwriter and Novelist, Dies at 84
abstract: Elliott Baker’s first book, “A Fine Madness,” was made into a Hollywood film starring Sean Connery.

name: Rosetta Miller
headline: Rosetta Miller, Museum Philanthropist, Dies
abstract: Mrs. Miller was a benefactor of the World Monuments Fund and the Newark Museum.

name: Ann Barzel
headline: Ann Barzel, 101, Dies; a Writer Whose Passion Was Dance
abstract: A dance writer and historian, Ann Barzel had a tenacity and passion for the art form that were legendary.

name: Siegfried Landau
headline: Siegfried Landau, Conductor, Dies at 85
abstract: Siegfried Landau was the founding conductor of what is now called the Brooklyn Philharmonic Orchestra.

name: John Lederle
headline: John Lederle, 94, UMass President, Dies
abstract: John W. Lederle led the transformation of the University of Massachusetts from a rural campus with fewer than 6,000 students to a major research center.

name: Celia Franca
headline: Celia Franca, 85, Dies; Founded National Ballet of Canada
abstract: Celia Franca was the London-born founder of the National Ballet of Canada and a pioneering figure in Canadian dance.

name: Campbell Moses Jr.
headline: Campbell Moses Jr., 89, Who Linked Doctors Through TV, Dies
abstract: Dr. Campbell Moses Jr. was an internist and a former medical director of the American Heart Association who in the 1950s and ’60s made innovative educational television programs intended for fellow physicians.

name: David B. Ast
profession: Pioneer in Efforts to Fluoridate Water
headline: Dr. David B. Ast, 104, Pioneer in Efforts to Fluoridate Water, Dies
abstract: Dr. Ast led an effort to begin fluoridating the water supply in New York State in the 1940s.

name: Joseph E. Gallo
headline: Joseph E. Gallo, 87, Brother Who Left Wine for Cheese, Dies
abstract: Joseph E. Gallo was the California cheese maker who battled his winemaking brothers over the use of the family name.

name: Ronald Hilton
headline: Ronald Hilton, 95, Scholar of Latin America, Dies
abstract: Ronald Hilton played a role in uncovering secret preparations for Cuban exiles’ invasion at the Bay of Pigs.

name: Sheldon K. Friedlander
headline: Sheldon K. Friedlander, Smog Scientist, Dies at 79
abstract: Sheldon K. Friedlander’s research helped identify the various pollutants in smog and quantify them by source.

name: Richard Lehman
headline: Richard Lehman, Creator of Crucial Intelligence Memo, Dies at 83
abstract: Richard Lehman developed the succinct intelligence summary that has been handed to presidents each morning for 45 years.

name: David Berger
headline: David Berger, Lawyer and Class-Action Hero, Dies at 94
abstract: David Berger was a lawyer who achieved fame, fortune and influence by helping to expand the ability of groups of people to file suits jointly in federal courts.

name: Peggy Gilbert
headline: Peggy Gilbert, 102, Dies; Led Female Jazz Ensembles
abstract: Peggy Gilbert was a noted saxophonist and bandleader who led all-female ensembles in hot jazz, a daring venture when she began her career.

name: Lamar Lundy
profession: Lineman on the Rams Fearsome Foursome
headline: Lamar Lundy, Lineman on the Rams’ Fearsome Foursome, Dies at 71
abstract: In the 1960s, Lamar Lundy was part of one of the National Football League’s most renowned defensive lines.

name: Leroy Jenkins
headline: Leroy Jenkins, 74, Violinist Who Pushed Limits of Jazz, Dies
abstract: The violinist and composer, one of the pre-eminent musicians of 1970s free jazz, worked on and around the lines between jazz and classical music.

name: Burt Beagle
headline: Burt Beagle, Ever-Present Sports Statistician, Dies at 73
abstract: By his own estimate, Burt Beagle was the official scorer for more than 6,000 baseball, football and basketball games, from youth league to college.

name: Hasan Ozbekhan
headline: Hasan Ozbekhan, 86, Economist Who Helped Found Global Group, Dies
abstract: The Turkish-born economist and management expert helped found the Club of Rome, which examined unwieldy global problems like food shortages and overpopulation.

name: Heinz Berggruen
headline: Heinz Berggruen, Influential Picasso Collector, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Berggruen was a German-born Jewish art collector who made a powerful gesture of reconciliation by moving his modern art collection to Berlin.

name: Alan D. Eames
profession: Scholar of Beers Around the World
headline: Alan D. Eames, 59, Scholar of Beers Around the World, Dies
abstract: Alan D. Eames cultivated his reputation as “the Indiana Jones of beer” by crawling into Egyptian tombs to read hieroglyphics about beer and voyaging along the Amazon in search of a mysterious lost black brew.

name: Will Maslow
headline: Will Maslow, 99, Lawyer Who Fought Discrimination, Dies
abstract: Will Maslow was a former executive director of the American Jewish Congress who fought discrimination against African-Americans as well as Jews, particularly in employment and education.

name: C. T. Oliver
headline: C. T. Oliver, 93, Envoy and Professor, Dies
abstract: Covey T. Oliver was a former assistant secretary of state, ambassador to Colombia and a professor of international law.

name: Frank M. Snowden Jr.
headline: Frank M. Snowden Jr., 95, Historian of Blacks in Antiquity, Dies
abstract: Frank M. Snowden Jr. was a historian who was a leading authority on the lives of black people in the ancient world.

name: Gnapa Béatrice Kombé
headline: Gnapa Béatrice Kombé, Choreographer, Dies at 35
abstract: Gnapa Béatrice Kombé was the powerful dancer and choreographer from the Ivory Coast.

name: Arthur M. Schlesinger Jr.
headline: Arthur M. Schlesinger Jr., a Partisan Historian of Power, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Arthur M. Schlesinger Jr.’s more than 20 books shaped discussions for two generations about America’s past.

name: Mai Ghoussoub
headline: Mai Ghoussoub, 54, Writer and Provocative Publisher, Dies
abstract: Mai Ghoussoub weaved together elements of her Arab heritage and an avant-garde sensibility to make bold, provocative statements as a publisher, author, sculptor, journalist and playwright.

name: Thomas C. Burke
headline: Thomas C. Burke, 82, Lawyer and Trustee, Dies
abstract: Thomas C. Burke was a lawyer who was a member of the New York City Board of Education in the 1960s and a trustee of the Altman Foundation.

name: Charles Forte
headline: Charles Forte, Who Founded a Hotel Empire, Dies at 98
abstract: Charles Forte was the owner of a hotel and restaurant empire that ranged from the Waldorf Hotel in London to the budget chain Travelodge.

name: Emmett Williams
headline: Emmett Williams, 81, Fluxus-Movement Poet, Dies
abstract: Emmett Williams was an American poet whose transposition of words into visual art and performances made him one of the founding artists of Fluxus, a performance-oriented avant-garde art movement of the 1960s.

name: Jay Harnick
headline: Jay Harnick, 78, Advocate of Theater for Children, Dies
abstract: Jay Harnick was the founder of Theaterworks/USA, the nation’s largest touring children’s theater company.

name: Herman Brix
headline: Herman Brix, 100, Athlete and a ‘Cultured’ Tarzan, Dies
abstract: Herman Brix played football in the Rose Bowl, set world shot-put records and portrayed Tarzan in the movies before becoming a dapper Hollywood leading man.

name: Bobby Rosengarden
headline: Bobby Rosengarden, 82, ‘Dick Cavett Show’ Bandleader, Dies
abstract: Bobby Rosengarden was a jazz drummer who worked with musicians from Igor Stravinsky to Jimi Hendrix but became best known for making musical wisecracks as the bandleader on “The Dick Cavett Show.”

name: Percival Leach
headline: Percival Leach, 80, Savior of a Crumbling Village, Dies
abstract: Percival Leach helped turn a ramshackle collection of pre-Revolutionary and mid-19th-century buildings along an old industrial canal in northern New Jersey into Waterloo Village, a version of Colonial Williamsburg.

name: Myer Feldman
headline: Myer Feldman, 92, Adviser to President Kennedy, Dies
abstract: Myer Feldman was an aide to President John F. Kennedy who remained virtually unknown to the public while playing an integral role in planning his presidential campaign.

name: Erich Windisch
headline: Erich Windisch, 89, Is Dead; Revolutionized Ski Jumping
abstract: Erich Windisch’s adjustment to an injured shoulder reshaped the sport of ski jumping by bringing competitors’ arms to their sides.

name: Thomas Eagleton
headline: Thomas Eagleton, Vice Presidential Nominee, Dies
abstract: Thomas F. Eagleton, a former senator, was removed as the Democratic vice presidential candidate in 1972 after revelations of mental illness and electroshock therapy.

name: Henri Troyat
headline: Henri Troyat, 95, a Force in French Literature, Dies
abstract: Henri Troyat was a Russian-born French writer whose novels and biographies earned him an immense following in France and considerable recognition abroad.

name: William Anderson
headline: William Anderson, Navy Hero, Dies at 85
abstract: William R. Anderson commanded the nuclear-powered submarine Nautilus on its historic cruise beneath the North Pole in August 1958 and later served three terms in Congress.

name: Bob Hattoy
profession: Clinton Aide and Powerful Voice on Gay Issues
headline: Bob Hattoy, 56, Clinton Aide and Powerful Voice on Gay Issues, Dies
abstract: Bob Hattoy drew wide attention with a nationally televised speech about AIDS at the 1992 Democratic National Convention and then became a forceful advocate for gay and lesbian issues in the Clinton White House.

name: Martin Trow
headline: Martin Trow, 80, Sociologist and Higher Education Expert, Is Dead
abstract: Martin A. Trow was a sociologist whose research on higher education reverberated through North America and Europe, particularly his description of the transition of a college education from elite privilege to mass product.

name: Jay Haley
headline: Jay Haley, 83, Pioneer in Family Therapy, Dies
abstract: Jay Haley advocated hypnosis and deeper social involvement for patients to cure emotional problems more rapidly.

name: Jean Baudrillard
headline: Jean Baudrillard, 77, Critic and Theorist of Hyperreality, Dies
abstract: Jean Baudrillard’s theories about the manufactured nature of reality were discussed both in philosophical circles and in blockbuster movies like “The Matrix.”

name: Ernest Gallo
headline: Ernest Gallo, 97, Founder of Winery, Dies
abstract: Ernest Gallo parlayed $5,900 and a wine recipe from a library into the world’s largest winemaking empire.

name: Paul Secon
headline: Paul Secon, 91, Who Helped Found Pottery Barn Chain, Dies
abstract: Paul Secon loaded the family station wagon in 1949 with ceramics, drove to Manhattan and opened the first Pottery Barn store.

name: Winthrop D. Jordan
profession: Expert in the History of Race Relations in America
headline: Winthrop D. Jordan, Expert in the History of Race Relations in America, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Winthrop D. Jordan, a National Book Award-winning historian, wrote several influential works on American slavery and race relations.

name: Rufina Amaya
headline: Rufina Amaya, 64, Dies; Salvador Survivor
abstract: Rufina Amaya dedicated her life to telling the story of the Salvadoran troops who slaughtered her family and many others in her village.

name: Nils Wessell
headline: Nils Wessell, 92, Leader Who Transformed Tufts, Is Dead
abstract: As president of Tufts University from 1953 to 1966, Nils Y. Wessell guided its transformation from a small college to a respected university.

name: John McCabe
headline: John McCabe, 78, Newspaper Executive, Dies
abstract: Mr. McCabe held top executive positions at five newspapers, including The New York Times, and also served in the administration of Mayor Edward I. Koch.

name: Brad Delp
headline: Brad Delp, 55, Lead Singer for Boston, Dies
abstract: Brad Delp’s vocals, overdubbed into group harmonies and grand chorales for songs like “More Than a Feeling,” were a vital ingredient in the sound of the rock band Boston.

name: Agustín Tamargo
headline: Agustín Tamargo, 82, Journalist Who Despised Castro’s Regime, Dies
abstract: Agustín Tamargo was an outspoken Cuban journalist who strongly criticized the regime of Fidel Castro in print and on the radio in Miami.

name: Natalie Bodanya
headline: Natalie Bodanya, 98, Soprano at Metropolitan, Dies
abstract: Natalie Bodanya was an American soprano who sang at the Metropolitan Opera in the 1930s and early ’40s and who later became a voice teacher.

name: Warren Alpert
headline: Warren Alpert, 86, Entrepreneur, Is Dead
abstract: Warren Alpert was an entrepreneur who sold sheets and towels from his father’s truck at age 13 and who two months ago donated $100 million to Brown University.

name: Marjabelle Y. Stewart
headline: Marjabelle Y. Stewart, 82, White-Gloved Author, Dies
abstract: Marjabelle Young Stewart was widely known as the Queen of Couth for her vast, genteel empire of books and classes about etiquette.

name: Tsai-Fan Yu
headline: Tsai-Fan Yu, 95, Physician, Dies; Helped Alleviate Gout
abstract: Dr. Tsai-Fan Yu helped explain a principal cause of gout and evaluated early drugs to treat the disease that are still in use.

name: Joseph Metcalf III
headline: Joseph Metcalf III Dies at 79; Led Invasion of Grenada
abstract: In October 1983, Vice Adm. Joseph Metcalf III was given less than two days to plan and start the controversial invasion of the Caribbean island of Grenada to overturn a Marxist coup.

name: Edith d’Addario
headline: Edith d’Addario, 84, Joffrey School Director, Dies
abstract: Mrs. d’Addario was the school’s ever-present doyenne who helped expand several programs, including pre-professional training, and helped form several junior touring ensembles.

name: Betty Hutton
headline: Betty Hutton, Film Star of ’40s and ’50s, Dies at 86
abstract: Betty Hutton was a singer and actress celebrated as a “blonde bombshell” of Hollywood musicals and comedies in the 1940s and 50s.

name: Ernie Ladd
profession: Hall of Famer in Football and Pro Wrestling
headline: Ernie Ladd, Hall of Famer in Football and Pro Wrestling, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Ladd played 112 consecutive games in the American Football League and appeared in the first Super Bowl before becoming a full-time wrestler.

name: John Thow
headline: John Thow, 57, Composer, Dies
abstract: John Thow was a prolific composer of chamber, symphonic and stage works and a professor at the University of California at Berkeley.

name: Barbara Gittings
headline: Barbara Gittings, 74, Prominent Gay Rights Activist Since ’50s, Dies
abstract: Barbara Gittings was a prominent gay rights activist who a decade before the Stonewall rebellion of 1969 was agitating for the rights of lesbians and gay men.

name: Clark Howell
profession: Leader in Study of Human Origins
headline: Clark Howell, 81, Leader in Study of Human Origins, Dies
abstract: F. Clark Howell was credited with transforming the study of human origins from just “stones and bones” to a broader discipline drawing on biology, ecology, geology and primatology.

name: Bowie Kuhn
headline: Bowie Kuhn, 80, Former Baseball Commissioner, Dies
abstract: Bowie Kuhn was the commissioner of baseball during a tumultuous 15-year period when the game experienced dramatic growth accompanied by unprecedented labor strife.

name: Maha Ghosananda
headline: Maha Ghosananda, Called Cambodia’s Gandhi, Dies
abstract: The Venerable Maha Ghosananda called for peace and reconciliation after the overthrow of the Khmer Rouge.

name: Antonio Ortiz Mena
headline: Antonio Ortiz Mena, 99, Mexican Finance Minister in 1960s, Dies
abstract: As Mexico’s finance minister in the 1960s, Antonio Ortiz Mena was the architect of a period of remarkable growth known as the “Mexican miracle.”

name: Eustace Lycett
profession: Designer of Special Effects for Disney Movies
headline: Eustace Lycett, 91, Designer of Special Effects for Disney Movies, Dies
abstract: Eustace Lycett made characters in “Mary Poppins” walk on smoke and seemingly empty suits of medieval armor engage in combat in “Bedknobs and Broomsticks.”

name: Marc Torsilieri
headline: Marc Torsilieri, 48, Provider of Annual Christmas Tree, Is Dead
abstract: Marc Torsilieri looked like a ginger-bearded lumberjack and played the part in splendid fashion by annually felling the Christmas tree for Rockefeller Center.

name: Richard S. Prather
headline: Richard S. Prather, Author of Naked Mysteries, Dies at 85
abstract: Richard S. Prather, a hugely popular mystery writer of the 1950s and ’60s, was known for novels with swift violence, loopy humor and an astonishing number of characters with no clothes on.

name: Lucie Aubrac
headline: Lucie Aubrac, Hero of French Resistance, Dies at 94
abstract: The French schoolteacher’s melding of romance and resistance to Nazi occupation inspired popular films based on her own life.

name: Jay Kennedy
profession: Editor and Scholar of Comic Strips
headline: Jay Kennedy, 50, an Editor and Scholar of Comic Strips, Is Dead
abstract: As editor in chief of King Features Syndicate, Mr. Kennedy revived “Prince Valiant” and introduced the popular newspaper comic strips “Curtis,” “Mutts” and “Zits.”

name: John W. Backus
headline: John W. Backus, 82, Fortran Developer, Dies
abstract: John W. Backus assembled and led the I.B.M. team that created Fortran, the first widely used programming language.

name: Stuart Rosenberg
headline: Stuart Rosenberg, Director of TV and Films, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Rosenberg captured the simmering anti-authoritarianism of the late 1960s in the widely popular Paul Newman prison drama “Cool Hand Luke.”

name: Raymond D. Nasher
headline: Raymond D. Nasher, 85, Dallas Art Collector Who Built a Museum, Dies
abstract: Mr. Nasher was a real-estate developer and banker who amassed one of the world’s best collections of Modern and contemporary sculpture and built a lavish public home for it in downtown Dallas.

name: Jim Cronin
profession: Foe of Illegal Trade in Primates
headline: Jim Cronin, Foe of Illegal Trade in Primates, Dies at 55
abstract: Jim Cronin was a self-trained zoologist who built a wildlife park on a deserted pig farm in southern England, then roamed the world with his wife to rescue illegally captured primates.

name: Janet Brown
profession: Retailer of Fashions for the Wealthy
headline: Janet Brown, 59, Retailer of Fashions for the Wealthy, Dies
abstract: Ms. Brown brought important designers to the wealthy clientele of her small store on Long Island, often before the designs were famous or even sold in Manhattan.

name: Ernst Haefliger
profession: Swiss Tenor Famous for Lieder and Oratorios
headline: Ernst Haefliger, 87, Swiss Tenor Famous for Lieder and Oratorios, Dies
abstract: Ernst Haefliger was a Swiss tenor who was most renowned as an interpreter of German art song and oratorio roles.

name: Stella Chess
headline: Dr. Stella Chess, Child Development Specialist, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Chess helped develop the influential theory that children are born with distinct temperaments that can powerfully affect their outlook and relationship with their parents.

name: Ann DeChiara Malamud
headline: Ann DeChiara Malamud, Helpmate to Writer, 89, Dies
abstract: Ann DeChiara Malamud’s marriage to Bernard Malamud helped him determine his course as a writer.

name: Calvert DeForest
headline: Calvert DeForest, 85, Larry (Bud) Melman on ‘Letterman,’ Dies
abstract: Calvert G. DeForest gained cult status on David Letterman’s late-night shows as the comic figure Larry (Bud) Melman.

name: B. Franklin Kahn
profession: Developer Credited With the REIT Strategy
headline: B. Franklin Kahn, 82, Developer Credited With the REIT Strategy, Dies
abstract: B. Franklin Kahn was one of the first developers to recognize that real estate investments could trade much like mutual funds.

name: Dwight Chamberlain
headline: Dwight Chamberlain, 68, Expert on Bird Talk, Dies
abstract: Dwight R. Chamberlain was a naturalist who studied the language of crows and ravens and helped to explain the intricate vocal cues they use in fighting, feeding and social interactions.

name: Tanya Reinhart
headline: Tanya Reinhart, 63, Pundit on Israeli-Palestinian Conflict, Dies
abstract: Tanya Reinhart, an Israeli linguist, was best known to the public as an ardent critic of her country’s policies toward the Palestinians.

name: Harold I. Lief
headline: Harold I. Lief, Advocate of Sex Education, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Harold I. Lief was a leading sex therapist who was an early advocate of having medical schools put greater emphasis on sex education in training doctors.

name: Alec Wyton
headline: Alec Wyton, 85, Organist Who Updated Church Music, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Wyton was an English-born organist, composer and teacher who brought contemporary influence to American church music.

name: Herman Stein
profession: Composer of Moody Horror and Science-Fiction Scores
headline: Herman Stein, 91, Composer of Moody Horror and Science-Fiction Scores, Dies
abstract: Herman Stein was a little-known craftsman who, unseen but very much heard, helped terrify the audiences of a spate of classic horror and science-fiction films.

name: Milton Wexler
headline: Milton Wexler, Groundbreaker on Huntington’s, Dies at 98
abstract: Milton Wexler was a psychoanalyst who applied his talent for conducting group therapy to brainstorming sessions for scientists working on the hereditary disease that ravaged his wife’s family.

name: Walter J. Turnbull
headline: Walter J. Turnbull, 62, Harlem Choir Founder, Dies
abstract: Walter J. Turnbull founded the Boys Choir of Harlem, which went on to sing for presidents and popes.

name: Howard Ronson
headline: Howard Ronson, 63, Builder of Towers, Dies
abstract: The British real estate developer became one of the most prolific builders of office space in Manhattan in the 1980s.

name: John T. Gilbride
profession: Former Chairman of Military and Commercial Shipbuilder
headline: John T. Gilbride, 90, Former Chairman of Military and Commercial Shipbuilder, Dies
abstract: John T. Gilbride was the former head of Todd Shipyards Corporation, once the largest independent shipbuilding company in the country.

name: Cathy Seipp
headline: Cathy Seipp, 49, Noted Columnist and Blogger, Dies
abstract: Ms. Seipp was widely known for poking fun at the liberal leanings popularly associated with Los Angeles.

name: Freddie Francis
headline: Freddie Francis, Cinematographer, Dies at 89
abstract: Freddie Francis was a versatile British cinematographer whose talent for creating atmosphere won him two Oscars.

name: Robert Petersen
headline: Robert Petersen, Publisher of Auto Buff Magazines, Dies at 80
abstract: Robert E. Petersen channeled his fervor for fast cars with tailfins and chrome-plated engines into a string of successful magazines.

name: J. Kirk Osborn
profession: Lawyer in the Duke Lacrosse Case
headline: J. Kirk Osborn, a Lawyer in the Duke Lacrosse Case, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Osborn was a noted defense lawyer before he gained prominence defending one of three lacrosse players against accusations of sexual assault.

name: Jerry Girard
headline: Jerry Girard, WPIX Sports Broadcaster, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Girard’s nightly appearances on the New York City station were characterized by frequent acidic commentary.

name: Orin Atkins
headline: Orin Atkins, 82, Executive Who Built Up Ashland Oil, Dies
abstract: Orin E. Atkins’s 16-year tenure as chief executive of Ashland Oil was also marred by improper business dealings.

name: Paul C. Lauterbur
headline: Paul C. Lauterbur, 77, Dies; Won Nobel Prize for M.R.I.
abstract: Paul C. Lauterbur shared the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 2003 for developing magnetic resonance imaging into a way to look inside living organisms.

name: Axel Rosin
profession: Longtime Head of the Book-of-the-Month Club
headline: Axel Rosin, 99, Longtime Head of the Book-of-the-Month Club, Dies
abstract: Axel G. Rosin was a former president of the Book-of-the-Month Club and later the head of the Scherman Foundation.

name: Amelia S. Haygood
headline: Amelia S. Haygood, 87, Who Founded Classical Record Label, Dies
abstract: Amelia S. Haygood was a former clinical psychologist who more than three decades ago parlayed her love of classical music into the independent record label Delos.

name: Morton Kornreich
headline: Morton Kornreich, 82, U.J.A. Leader, Dies
abstract: Mr. Kornreich was a former national chairman of the United Jewish Appeal and chairman of the UJA-Federation of New York.

name: Ransom A. Myers
profession: Expert on Loss of Fish Stocks
headline: Ransom A. Myers, 54, Dies; Expert on Loss of Fish Stocks
abstract: Ransom A. Myers was a fisheries biologist whose work brought wide attention to collapsing fish stocks around the world.

name: Marshall Rogers
headline: Marshall Rogers, 57, Artist Who Drew Batman Comics, Dies
abstract: Marshall Rogers was a comic-book artist who made his name illustrating Batman at a significant period in 1977 and ’78.

name: Robert Austrian
headline: Robert Austrian, 90, Dies; Developed Major Vaccine
abstract: Dr. Robert Austrian’s research led to a pneumococcal vaccine that has saved the lives of hundreds of thousands of people.

name: George Izenour
headline: George Izenour, 94, Designer of Technologies for Theaters, Dies
abstract: George C. Izenour, a pioneer in theater design and technology, helped bring automation to stagecraft.

name: Charlotte Winters
profession: Navy Enlistee in World War I
headline: Charlotte Winters, 109, a Navy Enlistee in World War I, Dies
abstract: Charlotte Winters was the last surviving woman to have served in the American armed forces in World War I and one of the first to enlist in the Navy.

name: Tony Scott
headline: Tony Scott, Jazz Clarinetist Who Mastered Bebop, Dies at 85
abstract: Tony Scott was a distinguished jazz clarinetist who in the 1950s helped steer his instrument out of the swing era and into the sax-infested waters of bebop.

name: J. Paul Sticht
headline: J. Paul Sticht, 89, Executive Who Expanded R. J. Reynolds, Dies
abstract: J. Paul Sticht, the first outsider to lead R. J. Reynolds, led the company through a time of rapid diversification.

name: B. R. Landau
headline: B. R. Landau, 80, Biochemist Who Helped Explain Diabetes, Dies
abstract: Bernard R. Landau was a biochemist and physician whose innovative studies of how the liver processes glucose helped shed light on what goes wrong in diabetes.

name: Toshio Sasaki
profession: Sculptor of Major Projects in New York
headline: Toshio Sasaki, 60, a Sculptor of Major Projects in New York, Dies
abstract: Toshio Sasaki was a Japanese sculptor known for works in public spaces, particularly “The First Symphony of the Sea,” a 322-foot-long wall relief at the New York Aquarium at Coney Island.

name: Hy Weiss
profession: Music Executive From Rock n Rolls Early Days
headline: Hy Weiss, 84, Music Executive From Rock ’n’ Roll’s Early Days, Dies
abstract: Hy Weiss was a music executive from the hardscrabble early days of rock ’n’ roll.

name: Joel Brodsky
headline: Joel Brodsky, 67, Photographer Who Specialized in Album Covers, Dies
abstract: Joel Brodsky was a photographer whose work appeared on the covers of hundreds of albums — most memorably “The Best of the Doors,” with its provocative Christlike image of Jim Morrison in black and white.

name: Freytag von Loringhoven
headline: Baron Freytag von Loringhoven, Aide to Hitler, Dies at 93
abstract: As a young German Army officer, Baron Bernd Freytag von Loringhoven was one of the last to flee Hitler’s Berlin bunker as Soviet troops closed in.

name: Abe Coleman
headline: Abe Coleman, Wrestler Known as Hebrew Hercules, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Coleman, who fought about 2,000 matches, was known to opponents by the vicious two-footed kick he copied from kangaroos.

name: Paul J. Cohen
headline: Paul J. Cohen, Mathematics Trailblazer, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Cohen was a versatile mathematician whose path-breaking work in the field of logic helped resolve a fundamental question of mathematics.

name: Thomas Rogers
headline: Thomas Rogers, 79, Writer and Teacher, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Rogers was a novelist whose wryly comic books chart the rocky landscape where youthful alienation — and youthful ardor — meet straight-backed WASP propriety.

name: K. I. Greisen
headline: K. I. Greisen, 89, Dies; Cosmic Ray Expert
abstract: Dr. Greisen was a physicist who helped broaden methods of studying cosmic rays, including sending unmanned balloons into the upper atmosphere.

name: Belinda Wright
headline: Belinda Wright, 78, Ballerina Who Excelled in Romantic Roles, Dies
abstract: Belinda Wright was a British ballerina who toured the world and excelled in the 19th-century Romantic and classical repertory.

name: John Billings
headline: John Billings, 89, Creator of Contraception Method, Dies
abstract: An Australian physician, Mr. Billings developed a natural contraception method endorsed by the Roman Catholic Church.

name: Neal Shine
headline: Neal Shine, 76, Former Publisher, Dies
abstract: The former publisher and editor of The Detroit Free Press played important roles as the newspaper won major awards.

name: Tom Moore
headline: Tom Moore, President of ABC Television in ’60s, Dies at 88
abstract: As president of the ABC Television Network in the 1960s, Tom Moore helped it narrow the ratings gap with NBC and CBS.

name: Tom Moore
profession: Inspired Covid-Ravaged U.K. With Charity Walks
headline: Tom Moore, 100, Dies; Inspired Covid-Ravaged U.K. With Charity Walks
abstract: An Army veteran nicknamed Captain Tom, he raised tens of millions of pounds for Britain’s health workers by walking 100 laps of his garden.

name: María Julia Hernández
headline: María Julia Hernández, 68, Rights Advocate in El Salvador, Dies
abstract: Ms. Hernández braved death squads to speak for the victims of the long civil war in El Salvador.

name: Eddie Robinson
headline: Eddie Robinson, 88, Pioneer Grambling Coach, Is Dead
abstract: In 55 seasons at Grambling State University, Eddie Robinson won more than 400 football games.

name: Eddie Robinson
headline: Eddie Robinson, Baseball Lifer Who Outlived His Peers, Dies at 100
abstract: He was a power-hitting All-Star in a career of more than 60 seasons as a player, executive, coach and scout. He had been the oldest living former major leaguer.

name: Nina Wang
profession: Outré Star of Hong Kong Estate Tussle
headline: Nina Wang, 69, Outré Star of Hong Kong Estate Tussle, Dies
abstract: Nina Wang, reported to be the richest woman in Asia, won control of her husband’s Hong Kong real-estate empire after a tumultuous legal melodrama.

name: Michael Dibdin
headline: Michael Dibdin, 60, Detective Novelist, Is Dead
abstract: Michael Dibdin was an internationally acclaimed British crime novelist whose best-known books feature the brooding Italian police detective Aurelio Zen.

name: Darryl Stingley
headline: Darryl Stingley, 55, Paralyzed Player, Dies
abstract: Darryl Stingley was a receiver for the New England Patriots who became a quadriplegic after an intentionally violent hit in a 1978 preseason game.

name: Diane Rothschild
headline: Diane Rothschild, 63, a Creative Force in Ads, Dies
abstract: Diane Rothschild was an advertising executive and copywriter who headed her own firm and created pithy and amusing ad campaigns, including some for the Range Rover off-road vehicle and J&B Scotch.

name: Jacques Courtin-Clarins
headline: Jacques Courtin-Clarins, 85, Innovator in Cosmetics, Dies
abstract: Jacques Courtin-Clarins was the founder and chairman of the Clarins Groupe, a French company that produces luxury skin-care products and makeup made primarily from plant extracts.

name: Walter Nicks
headline: Walter Nicks, 81, Dance Teacher and Choreographer, Dies
abstract: Walter Nicks was an internationally known dancer, teacher and choreographer.

name: Olcott Deming
headline: Olcott Deming, 98, Ambassador to Newly Independent Uganda, Dies
abstract: Olcott Hawthorne Deming was a career Foreign Service officer and the first American ambassador to Uganda after it gained independence from Britain in 1962.

name: Elizabeth Kals Reilley
headline: Elizabeth Kals Reilley, Scholar of Horticulture, Dies at 99
abstract: Elizabeth Kals Reilley was a horticultural librarian, scholar and book collector who amassed a major private collection of rare books on landscape design.

name: Laurie Baker
profession: Designer of Homes for Indias Poor
headline: Laurie Baker, Designer of Homes for India’s Poor, Is Dead at 90
abstract: A chance meeting with Mahatma Gandhi started Mr. Baker on a lifelong career of designing low-cost and environmentally respectful houses.

name: Sol LeWitt
headline: Sol LeWitt, Master of Conceptualism, Dies at 78
abstract: Sol LeWitt’s deceptively simple geometric sculptures and drawings and ecstatically colored and jazzy wall paintings established him as a lodestar of modern American art.

name: James Needham
headline: James Needham, 80, Dies; Ex-Head of Stock Exchange
abstract: James J. Needham was the first full-time paid chairman of the New York Stock Exchange.

name: Kurt Vonnegut
headline: Kurt Vonnegut, Novelist Who Caught the Imagination of His Age, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Kurt Vonnegut’s darkly comic novels became classics of the counterculture, making him a literary idol to students in the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Jagjit Singh Chauhan
headline: Jagjit Singh Chauhan, Sikh Militant Leader in India, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Chauhan began a campaign to create an independent state of Sikhs and was charged with sedition and other crimes in connection with his activities.

name: Elizabeth Jolley
headline: Elizabeth Jolley, ‘Australian Gothic’ Writer, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Jolley’s distinctive literary voice and eccentric literary preoccupations made her one of Australia’s most acclaimed novelists.

name: Rubin Caslow
headline: Rubin Caslow, 86, Leader of a Smoked-Fish Dynasty, Dies
abstract: Mr. Caslow presided over the Acme Smoked Fish Corporation, a family-owned concern now in its fourth generation.

name: Roscoe Lee Browne
headline: Roscoe Lee Browne, 81, Actor of Stage and Screen, Dies
abstract: Roscoe Lee Browne was a stage, film and television actor known for his rich voice.

name: Paul Leventhal
profession: Opposed Commercial Use of Nuclear Power
headline: Paul Leventhal, Who Opposed Commercial Use of Nuclear Power, Dies at 69
abstract: Paul Leventhal as president of the small but influential Nuclear Control Institute was one of the most vocal opponents of expanding the commercial use of nuclear power.

name: George Jenkins
profession: Set Designer for All the Presidents Men
headline: George Jenkins, 98, Set Designer for ‘All the President’s Men,’ Dies
abstract: George Jenkins was an Academy Award-winning production designer and three-time Tony nominee known for his architectural eye and scrupulous attention to detail.

name: George P. Jenkins
headline: George P. Jenkins, a MetLife Chairman, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Jenkins helped form the Municipal Assistance Corporation, which helped resolve New York City’s debt crisis in the 1970s.

name: Dakota Staton
profession: Jazz Singer With a Sharp, Bluesy Sound
headline: Dakota Staton, 76, Jazz Singer With a Sharp, Bluesy Sound, Dies
abstract: Dakota Staton was a highly respected jazz and blues singer known from the 1950s on for her bright, trumpetlike sound and tough, sassy style.

name: Edgar Young
headline: Edgar Young, 98, Steward of Lincoln Center Project, Dies
abstract: Edgar B. Young was the behind-the-scenes administrator who smoothed the way for the construction of Lincoln Center in the 1960s.

name: Eben Pyne
headline: Eben Pyne 89, Who Helped Revive Suburban Railroads, Dies
abstract: Mr. Pyne helped Gov. Nelson A. Rockefeller mold New York’s suburban transit system from a tangle of decrepit railroad lines.

name: Stan Daniels
headline: Stan Daniels, 72, a Writer of Emmy-Winning Sitcoms, Dies
abstract: Stan Daniels was a television writer who won Emmy Awards for his work on the groundbreaking situation comedies “Taxi” and “The Mary Tyler Moore Show.”

name: Barry Nelson
headline: Barry Nelson, Broadway and Film Actor, Dies at 86
abstract: Barry Nelson, an actor who had a long career in film and television, starred in some of the more durable Broadway comedies of the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Mimi Lerner
profession: Opera Singer With an Unconventional Career
headline: Mimi Lerner, 61, Opera Singer With an Unconventional Career, Dies
abstract: Mimi Lerner was an internationally renowned mezzo-soprano and educator who came to the operatic stage late in life.

name: Reginald H. Fuller
headline: Reginald H. Fuller, 92, New Testament Scholar, Dies
abstract: Reginald H. Fuller was a prominent British-born New Testament scholar who used his knowledge of Hebrew and Greek to hunt for the historical Jesus.

name: Warren E. Preece
headline: Warren E. Preece, 85, Who Revamped Encyclopedia Britannica, Dies
abstract: Warren E. Preece was a former editor of The Encyclopedia Britannica who in the early 1970s shepherded it through its first major redesign in decades, a task he likened publicly to fighting a war.

name: Paul Watzlawick
headline: Paul Watzlawick, Therapist Behind Rapid Diagnosis Strategy, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Watzlawick helped develop a theory known as brief therapy, in which behavioral and psychological problems are treated in no more than 10 sessions.

name: Egon Bondy
headline: Egon Bondy, Czech Writer and Critic, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Bondy’s whimsically demented verse lubricated the underground movement that helped topple Communism in Czechoslovakia.

name: Don Ho
headline: Don Ho, Hawaiian Musician, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Ho defined popular perceptions of Hawaiian music in the 1960s and was a durable spokesman for the image of Hawaii as a tourist playground.

name: Pat Buckley
headline: Pat Buckley, Writer’s Wife and Socialite, Dies at 80
abstract: Pat Buckley, the wife of William F. Buckley Jr., was a leading player on Manhattan’s social and charity benefit circuit for decades.

name: Salvatore Scarpitta
headline: Salvatore Scarpitta, New York Artist, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Scarpitta’s work ranged from three-dimensional wrapped canvases to sculptural renderings of cars and sleds.

name: James Lyons
headline: James Lyons, 46, Film Editor and Actor, Dies
abstract: Mr. Lyons was a film editor whose most notable collaborations were with the director Todd Haynes on several feature films.

name: Rexford Tompkins
headline: Rexford Tompkins, 90, Who Helped Shape City’s Rent Stabilization, Dies
abstract: Rexford E. Tompkins was a former chairman of the Real Estate Board of New York who was one of the industry’s leading voices in creating a rent stabilization system.

name: Mary D. Crisp
headline: Mary D. Crisp, 83, Feminist G.O.P. Leader, Dies
abstract: Mary D. Crisp’s stalwart advocacy of feminism and abortion rights as national co-chairman of the Republican Party led to her ouster in 1980 and a sharp rebuke from Ronald Reagan.

name: Mollie Orshansky
headline: Mollie Orshansky, Statistician, Dies at 91
abstract: Mollie Orshansky developed the federal poverty line, a measurement that shaped decades of social policy and welfare programs.

name: Kitty Carlisle Hart
headline: Kitty Carlisle Hart, Actress and Arts Advocate, Dies at 96
abstract: Kitty Carlisle Hart began her career in the theater in a 1932 musical comedy revue on Broadway and acted in films.

name: Hans Koning
headline: Hans Koning, 85, Prolific Left-Leaning Writer, Is Dead
abstract: Hans Koning’s outpouring of more than 40 fiction and nonfiction books ranged from exotic travel to erotic trauma to a withering indictment of Christopher Columbus.

name: Conrad Spizz
headline: Conrad Spizz, 90, an Opera-Loving Master of Smoked Fish, Dies
abstract: Mr. Spizz was a tough-talking, cigar-chewing artisan of smoked fish whose work was enshrined behind glass at some of New York’s best-known food shops.

name: Roy Moyer
headline: Roy Moyer, 85, a Painter and Curator, Dies
abstract: Roy Moyer was a painter who helped bring works by other artists to museums across the United States.

name: Brant Parker
profession: Co-Creator of The Wizard of Id Comics
headline: Brant Parker, 86, Co-Creator of ‘The Wizard of Id’ Comics, Dies
abstract: Brant Parker was a co-creator of “The Wizard of Id,” an award-winning comic strip that is set in medieval times and has poked fun at politics and cultural follies for more than 40 years.

name: Alvin Roth
headline: Alvin Roth, Bridge Champion, Dies at 92
abstract: Alvin L. Roth was one of the most talented bridge players of all time, winning 26 national championships with 11 different partners.

name: Chauncey Starr
headline: Chauncey Starr, 95, Pioneer in Nuclear Energy, Dies
abstract: Chauncey Starr was a pioneer in the fields of nuclear energy and risk analysis and an evangelist for the idea of electrification as a boon to humankind and the environment.

name: Steven B. Derounian
headline: Steven B. Derounian, 89, Judge and Nassau Ex-Congressman, Dies
abstract: Mr. Derounian won national attention as a champion of personal and public integrity when he sat on a 1950s subcommittee investigating quiz show scandals and payola on the public airwaves.

name: Natalia Clare
headline: Natalia Clare, 87, Dancer With Ballets Russes Troupes, Dies
abstract: Ms. Clare was a member of both of the influential Ballets Russes troupes of the 1940s and ’50s and the founder of a prominent Los Angeles ballet school.

name: Marie M. Clay
headline: Marie M. Clay, Remedial Reading Specialist, Dies at 81
abstract: Marie M. Clay was an internationally known educator who developed a remedial reading program known as Reading Recovery.

name: Andrew Hill
profession: Jazz Artist Known for His Daring Style
headline: Andrew Hill, 75, Jazz Artist Known for His Daring Style, Dies
abstract: Andrew Hill was a pianist and composer of highly original and sometimes opaquely inner-dwelling jazz whose work only recently found a wide audience.

name: Carlo Maria Badini
headline: Carlo Maria Badini, 81, an Innovative Leader of La Scala, Dies
abstract: Carlo Maria Badini was a former superintendent of the Teatro alla Scala in Milan who brought the opera house into the age of television and corporate sponsorship.

name: Helen Walton
headline: Helen Walton, Matriarch of Wal-Mart Family, Dies at 87
abstract: Helen Robson Walton’s husband, Sam Walton, founded Wal-Mart Stores and relied on her for advice.

name: Frank Westheimer
headline: Frank Westheimer, 95, Who Developed Model Valuable in Biochemistry, Dies
abstract: Frank H. Westheimer was a Harvard chemist whose work in understanding how the body metabolizes alcohol became a model for similar studies in the growing field of biochemistry.

name: John R. Drexel III
profession: Socialite and Scion of a Banking Family
headline: John R. Drexel III, Socialite and Scion of a Banking Family, Dies at 87
abstract: Through most of his life, Mr. Drexel directed his family’s philanthropic activities, taking particular interest in local hospitals and an animal shelter.

name: Kelsie B. Harder
headline: Kelsie B. Harder, Name Expert, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Harder wrote or edited more than 1,000 articles, books, reviews, notes and poems, and presided over organizations like the American Name Society.

name: Otto Natzler
profession: Ceramicist Celebrated for His Inventive Glazes
headline: Otto Natzler, 99, a Ceramicist Celebrated for His Inventive Glazes
abstract: In a famous collaboration of more than three decades, Mr. Natzler and his wife Gertrud Natzler produced wafer-thin pots with bold, violent glazes.

name: E. Dorrit Hoffleit
headline: E. Dorrit Hoffleit, Scientist, Dies at 100
abstract: Dr. Hoffleit was an astronomer who studied the features of stars visible to the naked eye.

name: Parry O’Brien
headline: Parry O’Brien, Pioneer in Shot-Putting Technique, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. O’Brien won three Olympic medals (two gold) and became the first man to reach 59, 60, 61, 62 and 63 feet.

name: David Halberstam
headline: David Halberstam, 73, Reporter and Author, Dies
abstract: The Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist wrote books on topics as varied as the Vietnam War and basketball.

name: Paul Erdman
headline: Paul Erdman, 74, Author of Finance-Based Novels, Dies
abstract: Paul E. Erdman was a writer of best-selling novels of financial intrigue who began his literary career in the comfort of a Swiss jail, where he was being held in connection with the collapse of the Swiss bank he ran.

name: Michael Smuin
headline: Michael Smuin, 68, Dancer and Eclectic Choreographer, Dies
abstract: Michael Smuin was a choreographer who worked for major ballet companies and led his own.

name: Warren E. Avis
headline: Warren E. Avis, 92, Founder of Car Rental Company, Dies
abstract: Warren E. Avis was a Michigan car dealership owner who founded a chain of car rental agencies and turned it into the nation’s second biggest.

name: James Richards
profession: Veterinarian and Expert on Cat Care
headline: James Richards, Veterinarian and Expert on Cat Care, Dies at 58
abstract: Dr. Richards was a prominent veterinarian who was a recognized authority on cat care.

name: Alan Ball
profession: Key Member of Englands Only Cup Winner
headline: Alan Ball, 61, a Key Member of England’s Only Cup Winner, Is Dead
abstract: Alan Ball was a crafty 5-foot-6 soccer midfielder who at 21 was the youngest member of the team that won England its only World Cup in 1966.

name: Bohdan Paczynski
headline: Bohdan Paczynski, Pioneering Astrophysicist, Dies at 67
abstract: Dr. Paczynski was a leading astrophysicist whose unconventional ideas led to new methods of studying distant stars and hidden planets.

name: Anne Pitoniak
headline: Anne Pitoniak, 85, Actress Who Played Strong Older Women, Dies
abstract: Anne Pitoniak began her stage career in late middle age, but received a Tony nomination for her Broadway debut, in “ ’night, Mother,” and had an enduring career playing strong-willed older women.

name: Jack Valenti
headline: Jack Valenti, Confidant of Presidents and Stars, Dies at 85
abstract: Jack Valenti became a confidant of President Lyndon B. Johnson and then led the Motion Picture Association of America.

name: William B. Lawless Jr.
headline: William B. Lawless Jr., 84, Former Justice and Law Dean, Dies
abstract: In perhaps his most noteworthy decision, he ruled as a State Supreme Court justice that the state prison system must recognize Black Muslims.

name: Emily Sunstein
headline: Emily Sunstein, 82, a Biographer and Scholar, Dies
abstract: Ms. Sunstein was an independent scholar known for her biographies of Mary Wollstonecraft and Mary Shelley.

name: Jim Moran
headline: Jim Moran, 88, Automobile Dealer and Philanthropist, Dies
abstract: Jim Moran became a billionaire by selling cars and building one of the largest closely held companies in the United States.

name: Walter Bareiss
headline: Walter Bareiss, 87, Dies; Specialist in African Art
abstract: Mr. Bareiss was a businessman who amassed vast collections of African, Western classical and contemporary art, much of which found homes in museums.

name: Robert Rosenthal
profession: Leader in Bombing Raids and Lawyer at Nuremberg
headline: Robert Rosenthal, Leader in Bombing Raids and Lawyer at Nuremberg, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Rosenthal was a highly decorated pilot in World War II who helped usher in a new kind of warfare.

name: Robert Rosenthal
headline: Robert Rosenthal, Who Linked Subtle Cues to Behavior, Dies at 90
abstract: His most famous finding was the “Pygmalion effect,” in which teachers’ high expectations of students can subconsciously make them better students.

name: Polly Hill
headline: Polly Hill Is Dead at 100; Tested Hardiness of Plants
abstract: A horticulturist, she gathered seeds from around the world, then studied which would endure New England winters.

name: Michael Malone
profession: Drew Tattoos With Flash and Flourish
headline: Michael Malone, 64, Who Drew Tattoos With Flash and Flourish, Is Dead
abstract: He was renowned for helping to popularize and standardize tattooing through images of dragons, daggers, cartoon characters and crests.

name: Joseph Saleh
headline: Joseph Saleh, 73, Film Center Founder, Dies
abstract: He converted a former cable car powerhouse into the Angelika Film Center, a cultural hub in Lower Manhattan.

name: Ivica Racan
headline: Ivica Racan,  Former Croatian Premier, Is Dead at 63
abstract: While prime minister of Croatia, Mr. Racan rebuilt economic and trade ties with Europe following the civil wars of the 1990s.

name: Tommy Newsom
headline: Tommy Newsom, Saxophonist, Dies at 78
abstract: The good-humored backup bandleader on “The Tonight Show” had earned fame as Johnny Carson’s comical punching bag.

name: Elliott Skinner
headline: Elliott Skinner, Scholar and Former Ambassador, Dies at 82
abstract: He was a former ambassador to the nation now known as Burkina Faso and a former chairman of the Columbia University anthropology department.

name: Octavio Frias
headline: Octavio Frias, 94, Brazilian Media Executive, Dies
abstract: Octavio Frias de Oliveira built one of Brazil’s biggest and most influential media empires.

name: Carl F. von Weizsäcker
headline: Carl F. von Weizsäcker, German Physicist and Thinker, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. von Weizsäcker wrote more than 30 books and founded the prestigious Max Planck Institute for Social Sciences.

name: Tom Poston
headline: Tom Poston, Virtuosic Comic Actor, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Tom Poston was an Emmy-winning comic actor whose television characters ranged from the slow-witted Everyman on “The Steve Allen Show” to a cantankerous  clown on the sitcom “Committed.”

name: Donald P. Lay
profession: Federal Judge Notable in Rights Cases
headline: Donald P. Lay, 80, Federal Judge Notable in Rights Cases, Dies
abstract: Donald P. Lay was a former chief judge of the United States Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit who rigorously defended the rights of women, Native Americans and convicts.

name: Henry LeTang
headline: Henry LeTang, Master of Tap, Dies at 91
abstract: Henry LeTang was a master dancer, teacher and Tony-winning choreographer who for three-quarters of a century taught the leading lights of Broadway and Hollywood how to tap dance.

name: Robert M. Warner
headline: Robert M. Warner, 79, the National Archivist, Dies
abstract: Robert M. Warner built a legislative consensus to wrest the National Archives from political control when he was its director.

name: Walter M. Schirra Jr.
headline: Walter M. Schirra Jr., Astronaut, Dies at 84
abstract: He was one of the original Mercury Seven astronauts and the only astronaut to fly in all three of NASA’s earliest manned space programs.

name: J. Robert Bradley
headline: J. Robert Bradley, 87, Charismatic Gospel Singer, Dies
abstract: J. Robert Bradley’s deep, swooping, octave-leaping voice and charismatic presence made him one of gospel music’s most important figures.

name: Ida R. Hoos
headline: Ida R. Hoos Is Dead at 94; a Critic of Systems Analysis
abstract: A sociologist, she opposed assessing technology solely on the basis of mathematical models that failed to take account of societal factors.

name: Edward F. Boyd
headline: Edward F. Boyd Dies at 92; Marketed Pepsi to Blacks
abstract: As a young sales executive, Mr. Boyd parlayed his assignment to promote Pepsi-Cola into a war against white racism and black stereotypes.

name: Russell W. Kruse
headline: Russell W. Kruse, Auctioneer of Classic Autos, Dies at 85
abstract: Russell W. Kruse achieved fame for thinking up and building the business of auctioning classic cars.

name: Isabella Blow
headline: Isabella Blow, Flamboyant Discoverer of Fashion Talent, Dies at 48
abstract: Ms. Blow’s gift for identifying and promoting new talent was occasionally overshadowed by her own Surrealist plumage.

name: Yahweh ben Yahweh
headline: Yahweh ben Yahweh, Leader of Separatist Sect, Dies at 71
abstract: Yahweh ben Yahweh was the charismatic leader of a religious, black separatist sect and was convicted of conspiring to murder white people as an initiation rite.

name: Diego Corrales
profession: Fighter and Victim of Motorcycle Crash
headline: Diego Corrales, Fighter and Victim of Motorcycle Crash, Dies at 29
abstract: Diego Corrales once held four world boxing championships and was remembered most for a pair of brutal lightweight bouts two years ago.

name: Alan Lowenstein
headline: Alan Lowenstein, 93, Lawyer, Is Dead; Revised Newark Government
abstract: Alan V. Lowenstein headed the commission that drafted the restructuring of Newark’s government in the 1950s.

name: Curtis Harrington
headline: Curtis Harrington, Director of Horror Films, Dies at 80
abstract: Curtis Harrington was a filmmaker known for his elegant, edgy cinematic forays into the macabre.

name: Lesley Blanch
headline: Lesley Blanch, 102, a Writer and Traveler, Dies
abstract: Ms. Blanch was an English writer and traveler best known for “The Wilder Shores of Love.”

name: Theodore Maiman
headline: Theodore Maiman, 79, Dies; Demonstrated First Laser
abstract: Mr. Maiman was a physicist who, in 1960, demonstrated the world’s first laser, a device small enough to fit in his hand.

name: Alfred D. Chandler Jr.
headline: Alfred D. Chandler Jr., a Business Historian, Dies at 88
abstract: Alfred D. Chandler Jr. argued in almost two dozen books that the emergence of professional management propelled modern capitalism.

name: Leonard Eron
profession: Researcher on TVs Tie to Violent Conduct
headline: Leonard Eron, 87, Is Dead; Researcher on TV’s Tie to Violent Conduct
abstract: A psychologist’s pioneering studies of youth violence led him to conclude that television had a significant role in prompting destructive behavior.

name: John K. Lattimer
headline: John K. Lattimer, Urologist of Varied Expertise, Dies at 92
abstract: He was the first nongovernmental medical specialist allowed to examine the evidence in President John F. Kennedy’s assassination.

name: Jerry Falwell
headline: Jerry Falwell, Moral Majority Founder, Dies at 73
abstract: The preacher helped bring the language and passions of religious conservatives into American politics.

name: Stanley Holden
headline: Stanley Holden, 79, a Dancer and Prominent Ballet Teacher, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Holden’s Chaplinesque blend of wistfulness and wit made him one of the finest character dancers in Britain’s Royal Ballet before he settled in Los Angeles and became one of the area’s most popular ballet teachers.

name: William Becker
profession: Creator of Concept of Motel 6 Chain
headline: William Becker, 85, Creator of Concept of Motel 6 Chain, Dies
abstract: William Becker got the idea for the Motel 6 chain after enduring a cross-country trip in 1960.

name: William Becker
headline: William Becker, Who Transformed Janus Films, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Becker, a culturally minded businessman, acquired Janus Films in 1965 with a partner, and they vastly expanded its library and broadened its distribution.

name: Kate Webb
headline: Kate Webb, War Correspondent, Dies at 64
abstract: Kate Webb was a brave, no-nonsense correspondent during the Vietnam War and was once erroneously reported to have been killed in Cambodia.

name: Robert S. Oelman
headline: Robert S. Oelman, 97, Chief Who Led NCR to Automation, Dies
abstract: Robert S. Oelman was chief executive of the NCR Corporation for 17 years and moved in the circles of leaders of business, politics and golf.

name: Thomas Curry
headline: Thomas Curry, 74, Officer Hit in Infamous Shooting, Dies
abstract: Officer Curry was one of New York City police officers who were seriously wounded by machine-gun fire in 1971 while guarding the home of the Manhattan district attorney.

name: Norman Frank
headline: Norman Frank, 82, Public Relations Adviser, Dies
abstract: Mr. Frank was the public relations executive who in 1966 devised the strategy by which New York City’s police union turned back Mayor John V. Lindsay’s attempt to create a civilian complaint review board.

name: Yolanda King
headline: Yolanda King, 51, Actor and Dr. King’s Daughter, Dies
abstract: Yolanda King was the eldest child of the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. who melded her father’s message of racial equality and nonviolence with her own calling as an actor and a motivational speaker.

name: Myer Shark
headline: Myer Shark, Lawyer Who Fought Utility, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Mr. Shark sought to recover $300 million of taxes that electric customers paid but that the government never received.

name: Denis Kuhn
headline: Denis Kuhn, 65, Dies; Restored New York Landmarks
abstract: Mr. Kuhn was an architect who oversaw many major restoration and reuse projects in New York City.

name: Giorgio Cavaglieri
headline: Giorgio Cavaglieri, Urban Preservationist, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Cavaglieri was an architect who took his fascination with how buildings and cities change over time from his native Italy to New York.

name: Donald M. Ginsberg
profession: Expert in the Working of Superconductors
headline: Donald M. Ginsberg, 73, Expert in the Working of Superconductors, Is Dead
abstract: A physicist, he was a leading expert on the production and functioning of superconductors, used in computers, electrical generators and medical equipment.

name: Mary Scheier
headline: Mary Scheier, 99, Creator of Elegant Pottery, Is Dead
abstract: The pioneer of the modern studio pottery movement was known for the lightness of her forms.

name: Lloyd Alexander
headline: Lloyd Alexander, Author of Fantasy Novels, Is Dead at 83
abstract: The work of the National Book Award-winning author was noted for its barely concealed allegorical depictions of the struggle against tyranny.

name: Karen Hess
headline: Karen Hess, 88, Dies; Culinary Historian Who Challenged Standards
abstract: She brought an academic rigor to the study of recipes, cooking techniques and ordinary American kitchen practices.

name: Bois Sec Ardoin
profession: Musician and Nurturer of Creole Tradition
headline: Bois Sec Ardoin, Musician and Nurturer of Creole Tradition, Dies at 91
abstract: For five decades, Mr. Ardoin played quick-fingered passages on some of the oldest known Creole tunes and infused Cajun waltzes with the blues.

name: Anthony M. Brooks
headline: Anthony M. Brooks, Undercover Foe of Nazis, Dies at 85
abstract: As a British undercover agent, Mr. Brooks led a network of saboteurs who delayed German reinforcements for weeks after the Normandy invasion.

name: Eugen Weber
headline: Eugen Weber, Authority on Modern France, Dies at 82
abstract: The Romanian-born, English-educated American historian was one of the world’s foremost interpreters of modern France and an authority on modern Europe.

name: Mary Douglas
headline: Dame Mary Douglas, 86, a Wide-Ranging Anthropologist, Is Dead
abstract: Her influence ranged beyond the traditional questions of her field to examine areas as diverse as kosher diets, consumer behavior, environmentalism and humor.

name: Stanley Miller
headline: Stanley Miller, Who Examined Origins of Life, Dies at 77
abstract: Stanley L. Miller was a scientist whose spectacular discovery as a young graduate student pioneered the study of the origin of life on earth.

name: Marian Radke-Yarrow
headline: Marian Radke-Yarrow, Child Psychology Researcher, Dies at 89
abstract: Marian Radke-Yarrow was a researcher in child psychology who did many influential studies on a range of sensitive issues.

name: Roy De Forest
headline: Roy De Forest, 77, Painter of Colorful, Comic Scenes, Dies
abstract: Roy De Forest was a Bay Area artist whose paintings depicted a comical, crowded frontier land of people and animals in patchworks of scorched, textured color.

name: Kenneth Sokoloff
headline: Kenneth Sokoloff, 54, Economist, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Sokoloff was a leading expert on the role the United States patent system played in technological and productivity advances in the 19th century.

name: Fannie Lee Chaney
profession: Mother of Slain Civil Rights Worker
headline: Fannie Lee Chaney, 84, Mother of Slain Civil Rights Worker, Is Dead
abstract: Fannie Lee Chaney became a target of racial hatred herself after her son James Chaney and two other civil rights workers were murdered by the Ku Klux Klan in Mississippi during the Freedom Summer of 1964.

name: Pierre-Gilles de Gennes
headline: Pierre-Gilles de Gennes, Nobel Prize Winner in Physics, Dies at 74
abstract: Pierre-Gilles de Gennes was an expert on the boundary lines between order and disorder in materials like liquid crystals and polymers.

name: William Peters
headline: William Peters, 85, Journalist Who Examined Race in U.S., Dies
abstract: Mr. Peters chronicled American race relations during the turbulent years of the mid-20th century.

name: Harvey Weinstein
headline: Harvey Weinstein, 82, Kidnapping Victim Who Kept His Cool, Dies
abstract: Mr. Weinstein’s kidnapping and survival after 12 days in a barrel-shaped pit near the Hudson River in Manhattan made headlines around the country in 1993.

name: Douglas Holmes
profession: Researcher Best Known for Work on Aging
headline: Douglas Holmes, Researcher Best Known for Work on Aging, Dies at 73
abstract: Douglas Holmes was a noted social psychologist who spent his career investigating means of improving social services for people.

name: P. M. Kaiser
headline: P. M. Kaiser, 93, Diplomat for Democratic Presidents, Is Dead
abstract: Philip M. Kaiser served as a diplomat or political appointee under every Democratic president from Harry S. Truman to Jimmy Carter.

name: Harold Froehlich
headline: Harold Froehlich, 84, Dies; Designed Deep-Sea Minisub
abstract: Mr. Froehlich applied the principles of aeronautics and balloons to the submarine Alvin, used to recover a misplaced hydrogen bomb and explore the Titanic wreck.
