name: Kawika Kapahulehua
headline: Kawika Kapahulehua Dies; Hawaiian Seafarer Was 76
abstract: As the seasoned captain of the first ocean-voyaging canoe to sail from Hawaii to Tahiti in perhaps 600 years, he battled fierce storms and a mutiny.

name: Charles Nelson Reilly
headline: Charles Nelson Reilly, Tony-Winning Comic Actor, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Reilly acted and directed on Broadway but came to be best known for his campy television appearances on talk shows and “Match Game.”

name: Indar Jit Rikhye
headline: Indar Jit Rikhye, 86, U.N. Adviser and Peacekeeper Trainer, Is Dead
abstract: General Rikhye was a key military adviser to United Nations peacekeepers and was the founding president of a research institute devoted to training peacekeepers.

name: Tod H. Mikuriya
headline: Tod H. Mikuriya, 73, Dies; Backed Medical Marijuana
abstract: A California psychiatrist, he was widely regarded as the grandfather of the medical marijuana movement in the United States.

name: James Beck
profession: Art Scholar and Critic of Conservation
headline: James Beck, 77, Art Scholar and Critic of Conservation, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Beck was a critic of what he viewed as the ruinous conservation of world masterpieces, including Michelangelo’s Sistine Chapel ceiling.

name: Parren Mitchell
headline: Parren Mitchell, 85, Congressman and Rights Leader, Dies
abstract: Parren J. Mitchell was the first black elected to Congress from Maryland and led the Congressional Black Caucus.

name: Gretchen Wyler
headline: Gretchen Wyler, 75, Actress and Advocate for Animals, Dies
abstract: Gretchen Wyler was an actress in Broadway musicals in the 1950s and ’60s who became known in later years as an animal-rights advocate.

name: Sam Kagel
headline: Sam Kagel, 98, Mediator of 1982 N.F.L. Strike, Is Dead
abstract: Sam Kagel was a mediator and arbitrator whose career settling labor disputes ranged from the rough-and-rowdy San Francisco docks of the 1930s to the N.F.L. fields of the early 1980s.

name: Jean-Claude Brialy
headline: Jean-Claude Brialy, French Film Star, Dies at 74
abstract: Jean-Claude Brialy was a dashing leading man of the French New Wave films of the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Jörg Immendorff
headline: Jörg Immendorff, 61, Painter With Provocative Themes, Dies
abstract: Jörg Immendorff was a German painter best known for crowded scenes depicting an acidic, often autobiographical comedy of art, politics and history.

name: Earl Ubell
headline: Earl Ubell, Who Enlightened Public on Science, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Ubell was a science reporter and editor familiar to generations of New Yorkers for his wide-ranging reports in newspapers and on television.

name: William Meredith
headline: William Meredith, 88, Poet Who Wed Depth to Form, Dies
abstract: Mr. Meredith used the rigorous constraints of meter and rhyme to subdue some of the most uncontrollable aspects of the human condition.

name: Edward S. Behr
headline: Edward S. Behr, 81, Writer and a War Correspondent, Dies
abstract: Edward S. Behr covered conflicts around the world for nearly three decades and wrote books about notable and sometimes notorious figures in 20th-century history.

name: Mark Harris
profession: Author of Bang the Drum Slowly
headline: Mark Harris, Author of ‘Bang the Drum Slowly,’ Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mark Harris took readers on a literary journey through the life of a mythical baseball player in four well-received novels.

name: Warren Anderson
headline: Warren Anderson, Albany G.O.P. Leader, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Anderson, a longtime Republican leader in the New York State Senate, helped bail New York City out of its fiscal crisis in the mid-1970s.

name: Warren Anderson
headline: Warren Anderson, 92, Dies; Faced India Plant Disaster
abstract: Mr. Anderson led the company through one of history’s most lethal industrial accidents, when thousands were killed in a gas leak at its plant in India.

name: William Silver
headline: William Silver, 59, Who Stirred Debate Over Gay Ministers, Dies
abstract: Mr. Silver’s application for ordination with United Presbyterian Church was the first by an openly gay man.

name: Huang Ju
headline: Huang Ju, Powerful Chinese Official, Dies at 68
abstract: Huang Ju, a Politburo member who rose out of Shanghai’s political elite to become one of the most powerful leaders in China, presided over reforms to the country’s banking system.

name: Wallace Seawell
headline: Wallace Seawell, 90, a Master at Shooting Stars, Is Dead
abstract: The celebrity photographer’s West Hollywood home was for decades one of the country’s most productive glamour factories.

name: John Macquarrie
headline: Rev. John Macquarrie, 87, Scottish Theologian, Dies
abstract: His melding of existentialist philosophy with orthodox Christian thought offered intellectually penetrating rationales for belief in God.

name: David Kirk
profession: Crusader for New York Citys Disenfranchised
headline: Rev. David Kirk, 72, Crusader for New York City’s Disenfranchised, Dies
abstract: Father Kirk, for decades a presence in the civil rights and antiwar movements, established Emmaus House, a communal residence for the homeless, in the mid-1960s.

name: Ed Yost
headline: Ed Yost, 87, Father of Modern Hot-Air Ballooning, Dies
abstract: In 1960, Mr. Yost fastened two propane tanks to what looked like a lawn chair, attached that to a 40-foot-diameter nylon balloon and sailed above the Nebraska plain.

name: Bill Whitman
profession: Scoured the Earth for Rare Fruit
headline: Bill Whitman, 92, Is Dead; Scoured the Earth for Rare Fruit
abstract: Among rare-fruit devotees, Mr. Whitman was hailed as the only person to have coaxed a mangosteen tree into bearing fruit outdoors in the continental United States.

name: Clete Boyer
profession: Yankee Known for His Slick Fielding
headline: Clete Boyer, 70, a Yankee Known for His Slick Fielding, Dies
abstract: Mr. Boyer played on Yankees teams that won five consecutive pennants in the 1960s.

name: Craig Thomas
headline: Craig Thomas, Senator From Wyoming, Dies at 74
abstract: Senator Craig Thomas of Wyoming combined a deep love of Western rural life with a 23-year public career in Cheyenne and Washington.

name: Bill France Jr.
headline: Bill France Jr., 74, Dies; Gave Nascar Its National Reach
abstract: Mr. France transformed Nascar into a multibillion-dollar enterprise after taking it over from his father.

name: Samuel A. Garrison
headline: Samuel A. Garrison, 65, Lawyer Who Fought Nixon Impeachment, Dies
abstract: Samuel A. Garrison III was chief Republican counsel to the House Judiciary Committee in its Watergate investigation in 1974.

name: Charles Evans
headline: Charles Evans, 81, a Founder of Fashion Line, Dies
abstract: Charles Evans was a founder of the fashion house Evan-Picone and was also executive producer of the film “Tootsie.”

name: Charles Maynes
headline: Charles Maynes, 68, Statesman, Is Dead
abstract: The longtime editor of Foreign Policy magazine was also a former assistant secretary of state.

name: D. Nelson Adams
headline: D. Nelson Adams, 97, Tax Law Specialist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Adams was a former managing partner of Davis Polk & Wardwell, one of the nation’s most prominent law firms.

name: Steven Gilliard Jr.
headline: Steven Gilliard Jr., 42, Dies; Founder of Liberal Political Blog
abstract: From The News Blog, whose advertisements and donations paid for his modest living expenses, Mr. Gilliard offered a blunt and passionate take on the events of the day.

name: Donald Johanos
headline: Donald Johanos, 79, a Conductor of Symphony Orchestras, Is Dead
abstract: Donald Johanos was a former music director of the Dallas and Honolulu Symphonies and a prominent member of the generation of American conductors who emerged after World War II.

name: Arnold Lappert
headline: Arnold Lappert, 86, Who Heard Corregidor Fall, Is Dead
abstract: Arnold Lappert was the Army radio technician in Hawaii who received the last messages from the island of Corregidor before its surrender to the Japanese in May 1942.

name: Martin Meyerson
headline: Martin Meyerson, 84, Leader at 3 Universities, Dies
abstract: Martin Meyerson was a former president of the University of Pennsylvania and the State University of New York at Buffalo.

name: Jim Clark
headline: Jim Clark, Sheriff Who Enforced Segregation, Dies at 84
abstract: Jim Clark was the former sheriff in Selma, Ala., whose violent, highly public attempts to maintain the status quo there in the Jim Crow era are widely believed to have contributed to the success of the voting rights movement.

name: Larry Leon Hamlin
headline: Larry Leon Hamlin, 58, Dies; Promoted Black Theaters
abstract: Mr. Hamlin was the founder and executive director of the National Black Theater Festival, a gathering for theater professionals and an influential showcase for artists.

name: Janet S. Sainer
profession: Leader of New York Office for Elderly
headline: Janet S. Sainer, 88, Leader of New York Office for Elderly, Dies
abstract: Mrs. Sainer created programs to keep older people active, educate them on health issues, provide them with meals on weekends and help their caregivers.

name: Harvey R. Colten
headline: Harvey R. Colten, 68, a Pediatric Immunologist, Is Dead
abstract: Research led by Dr. Colten helped isolate a gene tied to respiratory failure in infants.

name: Edwin Traisman
headline: Edwin Traisman, 91, Dies; Helped Create Iconic Foods
abstract: Mr. Traisman was a food scientist who helped standardize McDonald’s French fries and develop Cheez Whiz for Kraft Foods.

name: Sheila Ballantyne
headline: Sheila Ballantyne, 70, Portraitist of Family Angst, Is Dead
abstract: A critically praised novelist, Ms. Ballantyne was known in particular for her second novel, “Imaginary Crimes.”

name: Les Schwab
profession: Turned a Rundown Shop Into a Tire Chain
headline: Les Schwab, Who Turned a Rundown Shop Into a Tire Chain, Dies at 89
abstract: From the rundown shop Mr. Schwab bought with borrowed money, he built a chain of 410 stores throughout the West.

name: John McGovern
headline: John McGovern, 85, Allergist, Investor and Philanthropist, Dies
abstract: A Houston allergist and real-estate investor,  Dr. McGovern’s philanthropy helped endow medical facilities at Duke University, the Texas Medical Center and other institutions.

name: Richard Rorty
headline: Richard Rorty, Philosopher, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Rorty’s inventive work on philosophy, politics, literary theory and more made him one of the world’s most influential contemporary thinkers.

name: Homer J. Stewart
headline: Homer J. Stewart, 91, Aerospace Engineer, Dies
abstract: In 1958, Mr. Stewart helped launch the first successful American satellite, Explorer 1, while he kept tabs on rival efforts by the Russians.

name: Ousmane Sembène
headline: Ousmane Sembène, 84, Dies; Led Cinema’s Advance in Africa
abstract: Senegalese filmmaker and writer Ousmane Sembène said that he decided to go to film school after realizing that “pictures are more accessible than words.”

name: Amy Sullivan
headline: Amy Sullivan, 54, Who Led Advances at O’Neill Center, Dies
abstract: She restored the finances of the Eugene O’Neill Theater Center, long known for discovering significant playwrights early in their careers.

name: Lee Nagrin
headline: Lee Nagrin, 78, Innovator in Performance Art, Dies
abstract: Ms. Nagrin was a noted Off Broadway performance artist, director and member of Meredith Monk’s theater company, The House.

name: Don Herbert
headline: Don Herbert, ‘Mr. Wizard’ to Science Buffs, Dies at 89
abstract: Don Herbert unlocked the wonders of science for youngsters of the 1950s and ’60s as television’s Mr. Wizard.

name: Rudolf Arnheim
profession: Psychologist and Scholar of Art and Ideas
headline: Rudolf Arnheim, 102, Psychologist and Scholar of Art and Ideas, Dies
abstract: Rudolf Arnheim was a distinguished psychologist, philosopher and critic whose work explored the cognitive basis of art — how we interpret it and, by extension, the world.

name: Kurt Waldheim
headline: Kurt Waldheim, Former U.N. Chief, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Kurt Waldheim, who was elected Austrian president despite his military service for the Nazis, died today.

name: Guy de Rothschild
profession: Leader of French Arm of Bank Dynasty
headline: Baron Guy de Rothschild, Leader of French Arm of Bank Dynasty, Dies at 98
abstract: The heir to the House of Rothschild banking family twice rebuilt and expanded its Paris bank after it was seized by France during World War II.

name: Nellie Lutcher
headline: Nellie Lutcher, 94, R & B Singer, Dies
abstract: Ms. Lutcher had a string of rhythm-and-blues hits in the late 1940s and continued performing into the early 1990s.

name: R. F. Dial
headline: R. F. Dial, 62, Dies; Convict Fled With Warden’s Wife
abstract: The artist and confessed hit man fled a life sentence for murder to spend nearly 11 years on the run with a deputy warden’s wife.

name: Martin J. Weber
headline: Martin J. Weber, 102, Dies; Innovator in Graphic Techniques
abstract: A graphic artist, typographer and art director, he invented a technique that gave two-dimensional images the illusion of appearing in three dimensions.

name: Leonard Pickell Jr.
headline: Leonard Pickell Jr., 53, Is Dead; Ex-Leader Who Stole From Beard Foundation
abstract: Leonard F. Pickell Jr. was imprisoned for stealing from the James Beard Foundation after promoting it as a top culinary institution.

name: Claudia Cohen
profession: Socialite and a Reporter of Gossip
headline: Claudia Cohen, 56, Socialite and a Reporter of Gossip, Is Dead
abstract: The high-profile gossip reporter for television and newspapers was a frequent subject of the gossip columns herself.

name: Julie Thoma Wright
profession: Helped Create Market for Modern Design
headline: Julie Thoma Wright, 49, Who Helped Create Market for Modern Design, Is Dead
abstract: She was the founder and co-owner of Wright, the Chicago auction house that helped create the market for 20th-century modern design.

name: Juanita Swedenburg
headline: Juanita Swedenburg, 82, Dies; Won Suit on Wine Shipping
abstract: The Virginia winery owner won a Supreme Court battle to tear down barriers that kept wineries from shipping directly to consumers in other states.

name: Charles Lee Remington
headline: Charles Lee Remington, Butterfly Expert, Dies at 85
abstract: A professor at Yale University, Dr. Remington was the intellectual patriarch of modern American lepidopterology, the scientific study of butterflies and moths.

name: Israel Shenker
profession: Reporter With the Instincts of a Scholar
headline: Israel Shenker, 82, a Reporter With the Instincts of a Scholar, Dies
abstract: Mr. Shenker, a scholar trapped in a newsman’s body, was known to readers of The New York Times for his vast erudition and sly, subversive wit.

name: Gianfranco Ferré
headline: Gianfranco Ferré, Italian Designer, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Ferré was known for a consistently singular vision in his signature ready-to-wear collection and for opening the doors of French haute couture to foreign-born designers.

name: Robert Tracy
headline: Robert Tracy, 52, Dance Writer, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Tracy’s first book, “Balanchine’s Ballerinas: Conversations With the Muses,” was described by The Wall Street Journal as 1983’s “great ballet book.”

name: Wally Herbert
profession: Explorer of the Iciest Corners on Earth
headline: Sir Wally Herbert, Explorer of the Iciest Corners on Earth, Dies at 72
abstract: Sir Wally was the first man to walk across the icebound Arctic Ocean and, some contend, the first to reach the North Pole on foot.

name: Colin Fletcher
headline: Colin Fletcher, 85, a Trailblazer of Modern Backpacking, Dies
abstract: Colin Fletcher’s ornate prose and prosaic tips on subjects like choosing the right hiking boots helped start the modern backpacking movement.

name: Lola Wasserstein
headline: Lola Wasserstein, Playwright’s Mother, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Wasserstein’s larger-than-life personality provided inspiration for sprightly maternal characters in the plays of her daughter Wendy.

name: Thommie Walsh
headline: Thommie Walsh, Dancer and Tony Winner, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Walsh was a Tony-winning choreographer who also created the role of Bobby in the original production of “A Chorus Line.”

name: Mac Morgan
headline: Mac Morgan, 89, Bass-Baritone Who Went on to Teach Voice, Dies
abstract: Mac Morgan was an American bass-baritone who sang on radio, television and the stage from the 1940s to the 1970s and who was later chairman of the voice department at Boston University

name: Vilma Espín
profession: Rebel and Wife of Raúl Castro
headline: Vilma Espín, Rebel and Wife of Raúl Castro, Dies at 77
abstract: An idealistic socialite who fought alongside Fidel and Raúl Castro in the mountains of Cuba, Ms. Espín was Cuba’s unofficial first lady for decades.

name: Robin Olds
profession: Fighter Ace and Hero of Big Vietnam Battle
headline: Robin Olds, 84, Fighter Ace and Hero of Big Vietnam Battle, Dies
abstract: Brig. Gen. Robin Olds was a World War II fighter ace who became an aviation legend by commanding the Air Force wing that shot down seven MIGs over North Vietnam in the biggest air battle of the Vietnam War.

name: Terry Hoeppner
headline: Terry Hoeppner, 59, Who Coached Football at Two Universities, Dies
abstract: A college football coach, he led Miami of Ohio to two consecutive bowl appearances before becoming the head coach at Indiana.

name: Antonio Aguilar
headline: Antonio Aguilar, 88, Ranchera Singer, Dies
abstract: Antonio Aguilar was the film star and ranchera singer who was considered the undisputed master of his genre for decades.

name: William LeMessurier
headline: William LeMessurier, 81, Structural Engineer, Dies
abstract: Mr. LeMessurier became a hero to other structural engineers when he detected and repaired a potentially catastrophic flaw in the Citicorp building in Manhattan.

name: Zeev Schiff
profession: Author and Dean of Israel Military Correspondents
headline: Zeev Schiff, 74, Author and Dean of Israel Military Correspondents, Dies
abstract: Mr. Schiff,  defense editor of the newspaper Haaretz and author of numerous books, was a household name in Israel.

name: Kenneth Franklin
headline: Kenneth Franklin, Astronomer, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Franklin’s accomplishments included helping pinpoint the first noise known to have come from another planet and inventing a watch for use on the moon.

name: Hank Medress
profession: Doo-Wop Singer on Lion Sleeps Tonight
headline: Hank Medress, 68, Doo-Wop Singer on ‘Lion Sleeps Tonight’, Dies
abstract: Mr. Medress was a founding member of the 1960s doo-wop group the Tokens, known for their sole Top 10 hit.

name: Ed Friendly
headline: Ed Friendly, 85, a Producer of ‘Little House’, Dies
abstract: Mr. Friendly was the co-producer of hit television shows including the rambunctious “Rowan & Martin’s Laugh-In” and the frontier saga “Little House on the Prairie.”

name: Jim Shoulders
headline: Jim Shoulders, a Tenacious Rodeo Champion, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Shoulders, a city boy who gained renown as the Babe Ruth of professional rodeo, rode bucking broncos and snorting bulls to a record 16 world-championship titles.

name: Marshall D. Shulman
headline: Marshall D. Shulman, 91, Dies; Expert on Soviet Union
abstract: Dr. Shulman devoted his life to understanding the Soviet Union as a leading scholar, a policymaker and a principal builder of Columbia University’s Russian studies program.

name: Norman Hackerman
headline: Norman Hackerman, 95, Chemist and Former University President, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Hackerman was a noted chemist and a former president of both the University of Texas at Austin and Rice University.

name: Guy Vander Jagt
profession: Long a Leader Within House G.O.P
headline: Guy Vander Jagt, 75, Long a Leader Within House G.O.P., Dies
abstract: The former congressman from Michigan was a fund-raiser and campaigner in nearly two decades as chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee.

name: Serena Wilson
headline: Serena Wilson Dies at 73; Popularized Belly Dance
abstract: Ms. Wilson, a noted dancer, teacher and choreographer, was widely credited with helping to popularize belly dancing in the United States.

name: J.B. Handelsman
headline: J.B. Handelsman, 85, New Yorker Cartoonist, Is Dead
abstract: From 1961 to 2006, Mr. Handelsman had nearly a thousand cartoons in The New Yorker. His work also appeared regularly in Playboy and the British magazine Punch.

name: Bernd Becher
headline: Bernd Becher, 75, Photographer of German Industrial Landscape, Dies
abstract: Mr. Becher was known with his wife, Hilla, for photographing relics of industry in the changing urban landscapes of late-20th-century Europe and the United States.

name: Nguyen Chanh Thi
headline: Gen. Nguyen Chanh Thi, 84, Seen as Hero in Vietnam, Dies
abstract: General Thi was a popular South Vietnamese senior officer, whose firing in 1966 set off civil warfare in the south during the war with the Communist north.

name: Dana Bullen
headline: Dana Bullen, 75, Is Dead; Led Press Freedom Group
abstract: Mr. Bullen was director of the Press Freedom Committee, a nonprofit organization, from 1981 to 1996, and had been the foreign editor of The Washington Star.

name: Nazik al-Malaika
profession: Poet Widely Known in Arab World
headline: Nazik al-Malaika, 83, Poet Widely Known in Arab World, Is Dead
abstract: Nazik al-Malaika was an early exponent of the free verse movement in Arabic.

name: George Kovacs
headline: George Kovacs, Innovator in Lighting Fixtures, Dies at 80
abstract: A designer, manufacturer and importer of innovative and stylish modern lighting fixtures, Mr. Kovacs introduced the ubiquitous halogen torchiere to the U.S.

name: Liz Claiborne
headline: Liz Claiborne, Clothing Designer, Dies at 78
abstract: She defied the male-dominated ranks of the fashion industry and started her own hugely successful company.

name: Tina Brozman
profession: Former Judge and Bankruptcy Law Innovator
headline: Tina Brozman, 54, Former Judge and Bankruptcy Law Innovator, Dies
abstract: The former chief judge of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York helped change international bankruptcy law.

name: Kiichi Miyazawa
headline: Kiichi Miyazawa, Japan Premier in the ’90s, Dies at 87
abstract: The former prime minister and holder of many other top government posts helped guide Japan from postwar ruin to economic superpower.

name: William Hutt
headline: William Hutt, Actor, Dies at 87
abstract: William Hutt was one of the foremost Canadian stage actors of his generation and a founding member of the Stratford Festival of Canada in Ontario, where he appeared in or directed 130 productions.

name: Jupp Derwall
profession: Former Coach of West German Soccer Team
headline: Jupp Derwall,  Former Coach of West German Soccer Team, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Derwall coached the team to a European Championship and a second-place finish in the World Cup after a controversy-laden run to the title game.

name: Bill Barber
profession: Brought the Tuba to Famed Jazz Sessions
headline: Bill Barber, Who Brought the Tuba to Famed Jazz Sessions, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Bill Barber, who performed with Miles Davis and John Coltrane, was one of the first musicians to play modern jazz on the tuba.

name: Margaret Helfand
headline: Margaret Helfand, Architect, Dies at 59
abstract: Margaret Helfand was a Manhattan architect and urban planner who served as president of the American Institute of Architects’ New York chapter.

name: Joel Siegel
headline: Joel Siegel, 63, Movie Critic Who Instructed and Amused, Dies
abstract: Mr. Siegel was a longtime film critic for ABC News whose pithy reviews captured the essence of a new film quickly without giving too much away.

name: Abraham Klausner
headline: Abraham Klausner, 92, Dies; Aided Holocaust Survivors
abstract: Rabbi Klausner was the first Jewish chaplain in the United States Army to arrive at the Dachau concentration camp after its 1945 liberation.

name: Silas H. Rhodes
headline: Silas H. Rhodes Dies at 91; Built School of Visual Arts
abstract: Mr. Rhodes was the co-founder of a trade school for cartoonists and illustrators in Manhattan that he built into the School of Visual Arts.

name: Laurence Mancuso
headline: Laurence Mancuso Dies; Founding Abbot Was 72
abstract: The Rev. Mancuso was the founding abbot of the Monks of New Skete, whose hilltop monastery in upstate New York is renowned for breeding German shepherds.

name: Eugene B. Fluckey
headline: Eugene B. Fluckey, Daring Submarine Skipper, Dies at 93
abstract: Rear Adm. Eugene B. Fluckey was one of America’s most daring submarine commanders of World War II and a recipient of the Medal of Honor.

name: Edward Yang
profession: Director Prominent in New Taiwan Cinema
headline: Edward Yang, 59, Director Prominent in New Taiwan Cinema, Is Dead
abstract: A leading figure in the New Taiwan cinema movement of the 1980s, Mr. Yang was best known for “Yi Yi,” about one family’s life in Taipei.

name: Jay Monroe
headline: Jay Monroe, 80, Engineer Who Invented Tensor Lamp, Dies
abstract: Mr. Monroe invented a bright, low-voltage minilamp that would become an American staple because his wife didn’t like the strong light he used for bedtime reading.

name: Raymond Douglas
headline: Raymond Douglas, 58, an Executive Who Helped Add Color to The Times, Dies
abstract: Mr. Douglas had a major technological role when The New York Times introduced color in its news pages and added new sections in the 1990s.

name: Hy Zaret
headline: Hy Zaret, 99, Tin Pan Alley Lyricist, Is Dead
abstract: Hy Zaret was one of the last of the Tin Pan Alley lyricists, whose most indelible work was the oft-recorded 1955 hit “Unchained Melody” but whose oeuvre ranged from jingles to songs about science to ballads of love and war.

name: Mary Ellen Solt
headline: Mary Ellen Solt, Poet of Words and Shapes, Dead at  86
abstract: Ms. Solt was an American poet known for helping disseminate the art of concrete poetry, which marries words and typography to produce works in which the verbal and the visual are inextricably intertwined.

name: Beverly Sills
headline: Beverly Sills, All-American Diva, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Beverly Sills, the Brooklyn-born soprano, was a genuine celebrity and an invaluable advocate for the fine arts.

name: Luciano Fabro
headline: Luciano Fabro, Italian Artist, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Fabro was a prominent artist and theorist in Arte Povera, a movement that began in Italy in the 1960s and championed unusual materials and unorthodox ideas.

name: Jimmy Walker
profession: Star Guard at Providence and in N.B.A
headline: Jimmy Walker, 63, Star Guard at Providence and in N.B.A., Dies
abstract: Jimmy Walker was an all-American guard at Providence College in the 1960s and a two-time N.B.A. All-Star.

name: Eugene Bell
profession: Creator of Skin Cells for Grafting
headline: Eugene Bell, 88, a Creator of Skin Cells for Grafting, Dies
abstract: Eugene Bell helped develop a way to grow human skin for grafting onto wounds and later founded companies to make the technology commercially available.

name: Moshe Decter
headline: Moshe Decter, 85, Advocate for Soviet Jews, Dies
abstract: Mr. Decter was a writer and activist with a lifetime of devotion to Israel and Jewish causes.

name: Philip Baloun
headline: Philip Baloun, Party Auteur, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Baloun was considered one of America’s pre-eminent party planners, whose art combined in equal measure the skills of a florist, theater designer, engineer, sorcerer and psychotherapist.

name: Régine Crespin
headline: Régine Crespin, French Soprano, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Crespin was one of the most important vocal artists to emerge from France in the decades after World War II.

name: George Melly
profession: Jazz Singer With Flair for Extravagance
headline: George Melly, 80, Jazz Singer With Flair for Extravagance, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Melly was a jazz and blues singer who was also an expert on Surrealism, an author, a raconteur and a cultural critic.

name: Lois Wyse
headline: Lois Wyse, Ad Wordsmith and Prolific Author, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Wyse authored more than 65 books and coined the slogan, “With a name like Smucker’s, it has to be good.”

name: Joseph Cimino
headline: Dr. Joseph Cimino, 73, Dies; Was Leader in Public Health
abstract: Dr. Cimino was New York City commissioner of health under Mayor John V. Lindsay and later president and chief executive of New York Medical College in Valhalla.

name: John Szarkowski
headline: John Szarkowski, Eminent Curator of Photography, Dies at 81
abstract: John Szarkowski was a curator who almost single-handedly elevated photography’s status in the last half-century to that of a fine art.

name: Philip Booth
profession: Shy Poet Rooted in New England Life
headline: Philip Booth, a Shy Poet Rooted in New England Life, Dead at  81
abstract: Philip Booth was a poet known for his explorations of existence and New England in an intense, sparse style.

name: John R. Hogness
headline: John R. Hogness, 85, Dies; Led Institute of Medicine
abstract: As the first president of the Institute of Medicine of the National Academy of Sciences, Mr. Hogness molded it to be an independent critic of the nation’s health care system.

name: Charles Lane
headline: Charles Lane, Hollywood Character Actor, Dies at 102
abstract: Charles Lane was a veteran character actor whose lean frame and stern features were familiar to millions of movie and television fans, most of whom, it is safe to say, never knew his name.

name: Doug Marlette
headline: Doug Marlette,  Cartoonist Who Won the Pulitzer Prize, Dies at 57
abstract: Doug Marlette was a Pulitzer Prize winning editorial cartoonist who also created “Kudzu,” the popular syndicated strip.

name: Bird Johnson
headline: Lady Bird Johnson, 94, Dies; Eased a Path to Power
abstract: Mrs. Johnson was a calm and steadying force for her often moody or volatile husband, President Lyndon B. Johnson.

name: Bucko Kilroy
headline: Bucko Kilroy, 86, N.F.L. Star and Executive, Dies
abstract: Bucko Kilroy spent 64 years in the National Football League as an All-Pro lineman and was later celebrated as a personnel executive and scout.

name: Kathleen Woodiwiss
headline: Kathleen Woodiwiss, Novelist, Dies at 68
abstract: Mrs. Woodiwiss was a best-selling genre novelist widely credited with having founded the historical romance in its modern — carnal — incarnation.

name: Nigel Dempster
headline: Nigel Dempster Dies at 65; Made Gossip Respectable
abstract: Mr. Dempster fed the seemingly insatiable appetite for word of how minor aristocrats and wayward members of the British establishment were misbehaving.

name: Edward Kuriansky
headline: Edward Kuriansky, 63, Who Prosecuted Nursing Home Fraud, Dies
abstract: Mr. Kuriansky was a leading prosecutor in New York State’s nursing home scandals in the 1970s.

name: Kerwin Mathews
headline: Kerwin Mathews, 81, of ‘Sinbad’ Sword Fight, Dies
abstract: Mr. Mathews was a tall and strikingly handsome movie actor of the 1950s who is best known for his starring role in “The 7th Voyage of Sinbad,” and particularly for that film’s roiling sword fight with a skeleton.

name: Edwin McDowell
headline: Edwin McDowell, 72, Reporter at The Times, Dies
abstract: Mr. McDowell was a reporter for The New York Times for 26 years who also wrote three novels and a biography.

name: Richard H. Goodwin
headline: Richard H. Goodwin, Preserver of the Environment, Dies at 96
abstract: As national president of the Nature Conservancy, Mr. Goodwin helped preserve thousands of acres of open space on both coasts.

name: Richard N. Goodwin
headline: Richard N. Goodwin, Adviser to Democratic Presidents, Dies at 86
abstract: A committed liberal, he wrote speeches for John F. Kennedy and Lyndon B. Johnson and later worked as an author, journalist and political consultant.

name: Shag Crawford
headline: Shag Crawford, 90, Longtime Baseball Umpire, Dies
abstract: Shag Crawford was a National League umpire for two decades and the head of a prominent professional sports officiating family.

name: R. S. Paffenbarger Jr.
headline: R. S. Paffenbarger Jr., 84, Epidemiologist, Dies
abstract: Dr. Paffenbarger led a study that has been influential in promoting vigorous exercise as a primary tool in preventing heart disease.

name: Sylvan R. Shemitz
headline: Sylvan R. Shemitz, 82, Dies; Lighted Grand Central Facade
abstract: Mr. Shemitz’s lighting designs warmed the facade of Grand Central Terminal and flooded the Jefferson Memorial.

name: Vivienne Nearing
profession: Lawyer Convicted in Quiz Show Scandal
headline: Vivienne Nearing, 81, Lawyer Convicted in Quiz Show Scandal, Dies
abstract: Ms. Nearing made headlines as a contestant on a popular quiz show in the 1950s and then again when a grand jury investigated charges that the show was rigged.

name: John Ferguson
headline: John Ferguson, 68, Coach and Feisty Hockey Enforcer, Dies
abstract: John Ferguson was a renowned roughneck on five Stanley Cup championship teams with the Montreal Canadiens who later became a general manager and coach.

name: Nina Vyroubova
headline: Nina Vyroubova, 86, Romantic Ballerina, Is Dead
abstract: Nina Vyroubova was a leading ballerina in postwar France who displayed an unconventional blend of romantic temperament and elongated classical silhouette.

name: John Hill
headline: John Hill, 83, Is Dead; Texas Democrat Who Served in Many Positions
abstract: John Hill was he only Texan ever to serve as his state’s chief justice, attorney general and secretary of state.

name: Chandra Shekhar
headline: Chandra Shekhar Dies at 80; Led India
abstract: An argumentative proponent of social change, Chandra Shekhar served as prime minister in 1990 and 1991 as the leader of a coalition government.

name: Jack Odell
headline: Jack Odell, 87, Designer of Matchbox Cars, Is Dead
abstract: An invention spurred by his daughter’s mischievous habit of taking spiders to school in a matchbox led Mr. Odell to create Matchbox Toys.

name: Jack O’Dell
profession: King Aide Fired Over Communist Past
headline: Jack O’Dell, King Aide Fired Over Communist Past, Dies at 96
abstract: He worked on fund-raising and voter registration for the Southern Christian Leadership Conference. Then President Kennedy insisted on his dismissal.

name: Marguerite Vogt
profession: Biologist and Researcher on Polio Virus
headline: Marguerite Vogt, 94, Dies; Biologist and Researcher on Polio Virus
abstract: Dr. Marguerite Vogt was a biologist who helped shed light on the polio virus at a time when it was virulent in the United States, particularly among children.

name: F. C. Ward
headline: F. C. Ward, Who Helped Devise ‘Genius Award,’ Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Ward helped devise the process by which winners of the MacArthur Foundation’s “genius awards” are selected each year without their even knowing they have been nominated.

name: George W. Comstock
headline: George W. Comstock, 92, Dies; Leader in Fight Against TB
abstract: An epidemiologist, Dr. George W. Comstock made major contributions to the treatment and prevention of tuberculosis.

name: Carleton Mitchell
headline: Carleton Mitchell, 96, Sailor Who Wrote About Yachting, Is Dead
abstract: Carleton Mitchell won the prestigious Newport Bermuda Race a record three consecutive times, and chronicled the joys and challenges of sailing in his books, magazine articles and photographs.

name: Jerry Hadley
headline: Jerry Hadley, Adventurous Lyric Tenor, Dies at 55
abstract: Jerry Hadley was  noted for his bright lyric voice, lively acting and adventurous choice of repertory.

name: Wayne A. Downing
headline: Gen. Wayne A. Downing, 67, Special Operations Leader, Dies
abstract: Gen. Wayne A. Downing fought in jungles and deserts and commanded American Special Operations forces before becoming a senior adviser to President Bush.

name: Jim Mitchell
headline: Jim Mitchell, 63, Filmmaker, Is Dead; Made ‘Behind the Green Door’
abstract: Jim Mitchell, with his brother, Artie, nudged pornography closer to the mainstream with the movie “Behind the Green Door,” then was convicted of manslaughter for fatally shooting Artie.

name: Sekou Sundiata
headline: Sekou Sundiata Dies at 58; Performer of Text and Sound
abstract: Mr. Sundiata was a poet and performance artist whose work explored slavery, subjugation and the tension between personal and national identity.

name: Kenji Miyamoto
headline: Kenji Miyamoto, 98, Leader of Japan’s Communist Party, Dies
abstract: Mr. Miyamoto emerged from jail in 1945 to lead his party on a jagged postwar course in which it renounced Russian and Chinese Communism in favor of more popular bread-and-butter issues.

name: Dmitri Prigov
headline: Dmitri Prigov, 66, Poet Who Challenged Soviet Authority, Dies
abstract: Mr. Prigov was a prolific and influential Russian poet and artist who at one point was incarcerated in a Soviet psychiatric hospital as punishment for his work.

name: Thomas Pyle
headline: Thomas Pyle, 67, Innovator in 1980s Health Care Plans
abstract: Thomas O. Pyle built the Harvard Community Health Plan into one of the nation’s largest and most innovative health care providers.

name: Shirley Slesinger Lasswell
headline: Shirley Slesinger Lasswell, 84, Expander of Pooh’s Empire
abstract: Mrs. Slesinger Lasswell expanded the market for a panoply of children’s products based on the characters from stories of Winnie the Pooh.

name: Antonio Carlos Magalhães
headline: Antonio Carlos Magalhães, Brazil Politician, Dies at 79
abstract: For nearly five decades, Mr. Magalhães was one of Brazil’s most powerful and colorful political leaders.

name: M. M. Graff
headline: M. M. Graff Is Dead at 97; Fought for New York’s Parks
abstract: Ms. Graff was a self-trained master gardener who became a New York legend by crusading to improve the city’s parks.

name: Tammy Faye Bakker
headline: Tammy Faye Bakker, 65, Emotive Evangelist, Dies
abstract: The elaborately coiffed gospel singer built a commercial empire around television evangelism with her first husband, Jim Bakker, only to see it collapse.

name: Jesús de Polanco
profession: Media Mogul Helped Revive Free Speech in Spain
headline: Jesús de Polanco, 77, Dies; Media Mogul Helped Revive Free Speech in Spain
abstract: He was a billionaire media entrepreneur viewed by Spaniards as crucial to restoring the free press during the country’s transition to democracy in the 1970s.

name: Donald Michie
headline: Donald Michie, 83, Theorist of Artificial Intelligence, Dies
abstract: A versatile British scientist, he helped develop a “smart” industrial robot and then applied the technology to diverse fields.

name: Anne McLaren
headline: Anne McLaren, 80, Expert on the Embryo, Is Dead
abstract: As a developmental biologist, she conducted experiments on mice that were important in the development of human in vitro fertilization.

name: Teresa Stich-Randall
headline: Teresa Stich-Randall, 79, American Operatic Soprano, Is Dead
abstract: An American soprano, her reputation was won and maintained in European opera houses.

name: Albert Ellis
headline: Albert Ellis, 93, Influential Psychotherapist, Dies
abstract: His  innovative approach to psychotherapy made him one of the most provocative figures in modern psychology.

name: Mohammad Zahir Shah
headline: Mohammad Zahir Shah, Last Afghan King, Dies at 92
abstract: The 40-year reign of the former king, which ended in 1973, was esteemed enough to earn him the title “father of the nation” in the current Constitution.

name: Sherwin Wine
headline: Sherwin Wine, 79, Founder of Splinter Judaism Group, Dies
abstract: Rabbi Sherwin T. Wine founded a movement in Judaism that says there is no reason to believe in God but that the religion’s highest ethical traditions should be revered.

name: Bill Flemming
profession: Announcer on Wide World of Sports
headline: Bill Flemming, 80, Announcer on ‘Wide World of Sports,’ Is Dead
abstract: Bill Flemming, one of the original announcers on ABC’s “Wide World of Sports,” was also known for his Olympics, college football and golf broadcasts.

name: Laszlo Kovacs
headline: Laszlo Kovacs, Cinematographer, Dies at 74
abstract: The Hungarian cinematographer fell in love with the American landscape on a cross-country bus ride and then gave visual shape to seminal films like “Easy Rider.”

name: Ulrich Mühe
headline: Ulrich Mühe, Film and Stage Actor, Dies at 54
abstract: Ulrich Mühe was a popular German actor who won acclaim as a tormented Stasi officer in cold-war East Germany in the Oscar-winning film “The Lives of Others.”

name: George Tabori
headline: George Tabori, 93, Writer of Refugee Life, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Tabori was an internationally known playwright whose work sounded the depths of the refugee experience.

name: Gerhard Skrobek
headline: Gerhard Skrobek, 85, Artisan Behind Hummel Figurines, Dies
abstract: Mr. Skrobek was the premier postwar artisan of the figurines that have graced millions of mantels around the world for nearly three-quarters of a century.

name: E. A. Boyse
headline: E. A. Boyse, 83, Dies; Multifaceted Doctor
abstract: Dr. Boyse did some of the earliest studies of the body’s system for recognizing and fighting off disease organisms and other foreign substances.

name: Daniel Koshland Jr.
headline: Daniel Koshland Jr., Scientist and Editor, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Koshland was a biochemist and philanthropist who brought an unexpectedly puckish tone to Science, the international weekly journal of research that he edited.

name: Jack Raymond
profession: War Reporter and Fighter for the Environment
headline: Jack Raymond, 88, War Reporter and Fighter for the Environment, Dies
abstract: Mr. Raymond learned newspaper reporting in the Bronx, honed his skills on World War II battlefields and went on to help start an international environmental organization.

name: Alberto Villamizar
headline: Alberto Villamizar, 62, Foe of Colombian Drug Cartel, Dies
abstract: Mr. Villamizar, a Colombian politician and diplomat who fought the Medellín cocaine cartel, led his nation’s battle against a wave of abductions.

name: D. D. Ryan
headline: D. D. Ryan, Fashionable Godmother to ‘Eloise,’ Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. Ryan’s most widely appreciated achievement was helping to give birth to Eloise, the fictional little girl who lives at the Plaza Hotel.

name: Odile Crick
headline: Odile Crick, Who Drew Iconic Double Helix, Dies at 86
abstract: Mrs. Crick’s  original illustration of the structure of DNA, discovered by her husband, Francis H. C. Crick and James D. Watson, became a symbol of modern molecular biology.

name: Tom Snyder
headline: Tom Snyder, a Pioneer of Late-Night Television, Dies at 71
abstract: As host of NBC’s “Tomorrow” show for eight years, the cigarette-waving interviewer made conversation a kind of performance art.

name: Bill Walsh
headline: Bill Walsh, Innovator of West Coast Offense, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Walsh coached San Francisco to three Super Bowl titles and was one of pro football’s most influential figures.

name: Ingmar Bergman
headline: Ingmar Bergman, Master Filmmaker, Dies at 89
abstract: Widely considered one of history’s greatest directors, Ingmar Bergman found bleakness and despair as well as comedy and hope in his indelible explorations of the human condition.

name: Michel Serrault
headline: Michel Serrault, 79, a Star of ‘Cage aux Folles,’ Is Dead
abstract: Michel Serrault was known internationally for his role as the temperamental drag queen Zaza in the original film version of “La Cage aux Folles.”

name: Michelangelo Antonioni
headline: Michelangelo Antonioni, Director, Dies at 94
abstract: The director’s chilly depictions of alienation were cornerstones of international filmmaking in the 1960s.

name: Bill Robinson
profession: Coach and Player for Series Winners
headline: Bill Robinson, 64, a Coach and Player for Series Winners, Is Dead
abstract: Bill Robinson was a longtime outfielder who played on the Pittsburgh Pirates’ 1979 World Series champions and was the batting coach for World Series winners with the Mets and Florida Marlins.

name: Jeremy Blake
headline: Jeremy Blake, 35, Artist Who Used Lush-Toned Video, Dies
abstract: Jeremy Blake was an up-and-coming artist who sought to bridge the worlds of painting and film in lush, color-saturated, hallucinatory digital video works.

name: Norma Gabler
headline: Norma Gabler, Leader of Crusade on Textbooks, Dies at 84
abstract: Norma Gabler became the public face of a crusade with her husband to rid schoolbooks of content they considered antifamily, anti-American and anti-God.

name: Alan M. Pottasch
headline: Alan M. Pottasch, 79, Dies; Creator of ‘Pepsi Generation’
abstract: Mr. Pottasch led the team at BBDO that created  iconic Pepsi commercials in the 1960s and ’70s and became known as the “father of the Pepsi Generation.”

name: Marvin Zindler
profession: Crusader in Whorehouse in Texas Case
headline: Marvin Zindler, 85, Crusader in ‘Whorehouse in Texas’ Case, Is Dead
abstract: Marvin Zindler was an antic and a television crusader who became known when he had “the best little whorehouse in Texas” closed on corruption grounds.

name: Patriarch Teoctist
headline: Patriarch Teoctist, 92, Romanian Who Held Out Hand to John Paul II, Dies
abstract: As head of the Romanian Orthodox Church, Teoctist helped begin healing the thousand-year schism between Christianity’s Eastern and Western churches.

name: Tommy Makem
headline: Tommy Makem, 74, Hero of Irish Folk Music, Dies
abstract: Mr. Makem introduced a raucous, revolutionary take on time-honored Irish folk music, first in the United States and then in Ireland.

name: Sergei Antonov
profession: Bulgarian Accused in Plot to Kill a Pope
headline: Sergei Antonov, 59, Bulgarian Accused in Plot to Kill a Pope, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Antonov was arrested in 1982 for his so-called connection in the plot to assassinate Pope John Paul II, but was acquitted on all charges for lack of evidence.

name: Thaddeus E. Owens
profession: Was Judge in Racially Tense Case
headline: Thaddeus E. Owens, 88, Who Was Judge in Racially Tense Case, Dies
abstract: Justice Owens was best known for presiding over the series of trials stemming from the murder of Yusuf K. Hawkins on a street in Bensonhurst, Brooklyn, in 1989 — a killing that stoked racial tensions in New York City.

name: Leonard Lief
profession: Educator and a Lehman College President
headline: Leonard Lief, 83, an Educator and a Lehman College President, Dies
abstract: Dr. Lief was the first president of Herbert H. Lehman College of the City University of New York.

name: William J. Tuttle
headline: William J. Tuttle, Master Movie Makeup Man, Dies at 95
abstract: William J. Tuttle was a Hollywood makeup artist whose work was so renowned that he won an Oscar years before there was an official Academy Award for makeup.

name: Robert E. Keeton
headline: Robert E. Keeton, 87, Author of Influential Law Treatises, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Keeton was a former federal judge and Harvard law professor who wrote widely influential treatises on tort law, courtroom tactics and no-fault auto insurance.

name: Fannie Hillsmith
headline: Fannie Hillsmith, Distinctly American Cubist, Dies at 96
abstract: Fannie Hillsmith was a late-blooming Cubist painter.

name: Larry Mathews
headline: Larry Mathews, a 24-Hour Hairdresser, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Mathews earned a reputation as New York’s most wide-awake hairdresser by opening what seems to have been the city’s first 24-hour beauty parlor.

name: Jean-Marie Lustiger
headline: Jean-Marie Lustiger, French Cardinal, Dies at 80
abstract: Cardinal Lustiger, who was born to Polish Jews, rose to become leader of the French church and an adviser to Pope John Paul II.

name: Sal Mosca
headline: Sal Mosca, 80, a Jazz Pianist and Teacher, Dies
abstract: Sal Mosca’s career began when he played with giants like Charlie Parker, Miles Davis, Billie Holiday and Sarah Vaughan, but he later took himself out of the public eye.

name: Raul Hilberg
headline: Raul Hilberg, 81, Historian Who Wrote of the Holocaust as a Bureaucracy, Dies
abstract: A Jewish émigré from Nazi-occupied Vienna, Raul Hilberg helped begin the field of Holocaust studies with his long, detailed 1961 study of the massacre of European Jews.

name: Elie de Rothschild
headline: Baron Elie de Rothschild Is Dead at 90
abstract: Baron Elie oversaw the restoration and ascent of the renowned wine estate Château Lafite Rothschild after World War II.

name: Jerry Schneider
headline: Jerry Schneider, 87, Pioneer of Indoor Tennis, Dies
abstract: Jerry Schneider, a developer and promoter of indoor tennis, is said to have been the father of indoor tennis.

name: Kai Siegbahn
headline: Kai Siegbahn, Swedish Physicist, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Siegbahn’s work in developing a novel technique using electrons to test the composition and purity of materials received a Nobel Prize in 1981.

name: Lee Hazlewood
headline: Lee Hazlewood, ‘Boots’ Songwriter, Dies at 78
abstract: Lee Hazlewood was the songwriter behind hits by Duane Eddy, Nancy Sinatra and Frank Sinatra, including Ms. Sinatra’s “These Boots Are Made for Walkin.’”

name: Jack Cole
headline: Jack Cole, Creator of People Locator, Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Cole was a businessman who used early computer technology to sort the world — or at least millions of the people in it — by street address.

name: Chris Schwarz
headline: Chris Schwarz, 59, Dies; Photographer Who Honored Polish Jews
abstract: Mr. Schwarz, a freelance photographer, roamed the ancient heartland of Polish Jewry to record remnants of a disappeared people.

name: Veikko Karvonen
headline: Veikko Karvonen, 81, Top Marathoner in the ’50s, Dies
abstract: Veikko Karvonen was a Finnish postal clerk who became one of the world’s best marathon runners in the 1950s.

name: Louis Moyse
headline: Louis Moyse, Founder of Music School, Dies at 94
abstract: Louis Moyse was a flutist, composer and founder of the Marlboro Music School and Festival.

name: Frank Rosenfelt
headline: Frank Rosenfelt, Studio Chief, Dies at 85
abstract: Frank E. Rosenfelt helped steer MGM into new ways of making and showing movies, and he acquired and produced movies like “Doctor Zhivago” and “Network.”

name: Frank D. Rich Jr.
headline: Frank D. Rich Jr., 83, Real Estate Developer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Rich was chairman and former president of the real estate development company that led the resurgence of downtown Stamford, Conn.

name: Russell Johnson
profession: Transformed the Sound in Concert Halls
headline: Russell Johnson, Who Transformed the Sound in Concert Halls, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Johnson combined architectural training, a love of music and acute intuition to revolutionize the quality of sound in hundreds of the world’s concert halls.

name: Russell Johnson
headline: Russell Johnson, the Professor on ‘Gilligan’s Island,’ Dies at 89
abstract: After a busy career playing villains in westerns, Mr. Johnson was the brains of an otherwise clueless band of castaways that remains lost in reruns.

name: Mel Shavelson
headline: Mel Shavelson, 90, Film Writer-Director, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Shavelson was a noted screenwriter, producer and director who worked with some of Hollywood’s biggest, brightest and most temperamental stars.

name: Howard Judd
headline: Howard Judd, 71, Menopause Expert, Dies
abstract: Dr. Judd’s early studies of hot flashes led to refinements in the use of estrogen and other drugs to treat women who experience unpleasant symptoms during menopause.

name: Richmond Flowers
headline: Richmond Flowers Is Dead at 88; Challenged Segregation and Klan
abstract: As the Alabama attorney general in the early 1960s,  Mr. Flowers drew national attention when he challenged the segregationist policies of Gov. George C. Wallace.

name: Merv Griffin
headline: Merv Griffin, Television Impresario, Dies at 82
abstract: One of TV’s most popular talk-show hosts, Merv Griffin also created some of the most successful game shows.

name: Moe Fishman
headline: Moe Fishman Dies at 92; Fought in Lincoln Brigade
abstract: Mr. Fishman was severely wounded while fighting Fascists in Spain, but eventually outlived almost all of the 3,000 American veterans of the Spanish Civil War.

name: Ulrich Plenzdorf
profession: Writer for German Film and Stage
headline: Ulrich Plenzdorf, 72, Writer for German Film and Stage, Dies
abstract: Mr. Plenzdorf was a German screenwriter and playwright whose works include “The New Sufferings of Young W.”

name: Elizabeth Murray
headline: Elizabeth Murray, 66, Artist of Vivid Forms, Dies
abstract: Elizabeth Murray was a New York painter who reshaped Modernist abstraction into a high-spirited, cartoon-based language of form.

name: Irene Morgan Kirkaldy
headline: Irene Morgan Kirkaldy, 90, Rights Pioneer, Dies
abstract: Irene Morgan Kirkaldy’s defiance of white supremacy in the summer of 1944 led to a Supreme Court decision outlawing segregated seating on interstate bus lines.

name: Brooke Astor
headline: Brooke Astor, 105, First Lady of Philanthropy, Dies
abstract: By night Brooke Astor reigned over New York society with a disdain for pretension and by day devoted her time and considerable resources to New York’s unfortunate.

name: Phil Rizzuto
headline: Phil Rizzuto, Yankees Shortstop, Dies at 89
abstract: The sure-handed Hall of Fame shortstop, nicknamed the Scooter, went on to become a beloved broadcaster.

name: Joe O’Donnell
headline: Joe O’Donnell, 85, Dies; Long a Leading Photographer
abstract: Joe O’Donnell took some of the first disturbing pictures after the nuclear bombing of Japan and captured famous scenes as a White House photographer.

name: Tony Wilson
profession: Impresario and a Founder of Postpunk Label
headline: Tony Wilson, Impresario and a Founder of Postpunk Label, Dies at 57
abstract: Tony Wilson was a British television reporter who became one of the most influential figures in postpunk music with his Factory Records label.

name: Tikhon Khrennikov
headline: Tikhon Khrennikov, Prolific Soviet Composer, Dies at 94
abstract: A prolific Russian composer and pianist, Tikhon Khrennikov was best known in the West as an official Soviet antagonist of Shostakovich and Prokofiev.

name: Max Roach
headline: Max Roach, Master of Modern Jazz, Dies at 83
abstract: Max Roach was a founder of modern jazz who rewrote the rules of drumming in the 1940s and spent the rest of his career breaking musical barriers.

name: Bruce Wolmer
headline: Bruce Wolmer, Editor and Art World Explainer, Dies at  59
abstract: Bruce Wolmer was the longtime editor and publisher of Art & Auction magazine and an expert on the heavily moneyed byways of the international art world.

name: John Wallowitch
headline: John Wallowitch, Singer and Songwriter, Dies at 81
abstract: John Wallowitch was a cabaret singer and prolific songwriter who was a colorful figure in the New York cabaret world for more than 40 years.

name: Liam Rector
headline: Liam Rector, 57, a Poet and Educator, Dies
abstract: Mr. Rector was a well-regarded poet and educator whose work appeared in many distinguished publications.

name: Atle Selberg
headline: Atle Selberg, 90, Lauded Mathematician, Dies
abstract: Dr. Selberg’s theoretical work on the properties of numbers was recognized with the Fields Medal and other major prizes.

name: Sam Pollock
headline: Sam Pollock, 81, Hockey Executive, Dies
abstract: As the Montreal Canadiens’ general manager, Mr. Pollock  built nine Stanley Cup championship teams in the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Richard Bradshaw
headline: Richard Bradshaw, Opera Director, Dies at 63
abstract: Richard Bradshaw was the conductor and general director of the Canadian Opera Company who pushed through the construction of a major new opera house in Toronto.

name: Carolyn Goodman
headline: Carolyn Goodman, Rights Champion, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Goodman became a nationally prominent civil rights advocate after her son Andrew and two other civil rights workers were murdered by the Ku Klux Klan in 1964.

name: Ralph Alpher
profession: Expert in Work on the Big Bang
headline: Ralph Alpher, 86, Expert in Work on the Big Bang, Dies
abstract: As a physicist, Mr. Alpher made early calculations and predictions that supported the Big Bang concept for the origin of the universe, though his role was largely overlooked.

name: Michael Deaver
headline: Michael Deaver, 69, Dies; Shaped Reagan’s Image
abstract: Mr. Deaver was celebrated and scorned as an expert at media manipulation for focusing on how President Ronald Reagan looked as much as what he said.

name: Jeremiah Milbank Jr.
headline: Jeremiah Milbank Jr., Donor and G.O.P. Official, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Milbank Jr. followed in his father’s footsteps to become an important Republican fund-raiser and benefactor of people with disabilities.

name: Joybubbles
headline: Joybubbles, 58, Peter Pan of Phone Hackers, Dies
abstract: Joybubbles was a blind genius with perfect pitch who played a pivotal role in the 1970s subculture of “phone phreaks.”

name: Leona Helmsley
headline: Leona Helmsley, Hotel Queen, Dies at 87
abstract: Imprisoned for tax evasion and fraud, she was widely regarded as a 1980s symbol of arrogance and greed.

name: Ronald Bracewell
headline: Ronald Bracewell, 86, Radio Telescope Pioneer, Dies
abstract: Ronald N. Bracewell used radio telescopes to make early images of the Sun’s surface in work that also led to advances in medical imaging.

name: Duncan W. Clark
headline: Dr. Duncan W. Clark, Voice for Fluoridated Water, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Clark was a persuasive advocate for adding fluoride to New York City’s water supply at a time when opponents claimed that the health risks far outweighed the rewards.

name: Jon Lucien
profession: Smooth Singer of Mellow Jazz and Soul
headline: Jon Lucien,  Smooth Singer of Mellow Jazz and Soul, Dies at 65
abstract: Jon Lucien had been a mainstay of smooth jazz since the early 1970s.

name: Sylvia Siegel
headline: Sylvia Siegel, Activist on Utility Rates, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Sylvia Siegel spent 16 years fighting against rates and rules that she maintained were unfair to consumers.

name: Tanja Liedtke
headline: Tanja Liedtke, Dancer, 29, Is Killed by Truck in Australia
abstract: Tanja Liedtke was a dancer and choreographer who was named artistic director of the Sydney Dance Company in early May.

name: Philip Masters
headline: Philip Masters, True Amateur of History, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Masters, whose jobs ranged from jewelry salesman to lighting executive to cabdriver to stockbroker, was that unusual amateur who succeeds in a professionalized field.

name: Rose Bampton
headline: Rose Bampton, Versatile Met Singer, Dies at 99
abstract: Rose Bampton was an American opera singer who switched from mezzo-soprano to soprano and sang leading roles in both ranges at the Metropolitan Opera.

name: Edward Avedisian
headline: Edward Avedisian, Artist Who Painted Bold and Bright, Dies at 71
abstract: Edward Avedisian helped establish the hotly colored but emotionally cool abstract painting that succeeded Abstract Expressionism in the early 1960s.

name: Grace Paley
headline: Grace Paley, Writer and Activist, Dies
abstract: Grace Paley, who explored the struggles of ordinary women in precise, pungent stories, was 84.

name: Butch van Breda Kolff
headline: Butch van Breda Kolff, 84, Fiery Coach, Dies
abstract: Butch van Breda Kolff, a happy-go-lucky nonconformist, coached more than 1,300 college, professional and high school basketball games.

name: Madeleine B. Stern
headline: Madeleine B. Stern, Bookseller and Sleuth, Dies at 95
abstract: Madeleine B. Stern was a prominent rare-book dealer, biographer and literary sleuth who helped bring to print Louisa May Alcott’s long-lost Gothic tales.

name: Leslie Lukash
headline: Leslie Lukash, Medical Examiner, 86, Dies
abstract: Dr. Lukash, a self-described “diagnostician of death,” helped identify the corpse of Josef Mengele, the Nazi doctor.

name: John W. Gofman
profession: Scientist and Advocate for Nuclear Safety
headline: John W. Gofman, 88, Scientist and Advocate for Nuclear Safety, Dies
abstract: Dr. Gofman was a nuclear chemist and doctor who heightened public concerns about exposure to low-level radiation and spoke out against commercial nuclear power.

name: Louisa Livingston Kennedy
headline: Louisa Livingston Kennedy Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Kennedy, the wife of a senior American official held captive during the Iranian hostage crisis, became a highly visible spokeswoman for the hostages’ families.

name: Julius Wess
headline: Julius Wess, 72, Theoretical Physicist, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Wess, along with Bruno Zumino, introduced the idea of supersymmetry among fundamental particles, which may help explain the universe’s missing dark matter.

name: Norman Cohn
headline: Norman Cohn, Historian, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Cohn helped show how totalitarian ideologies of the 20th century were propelled by mythologies associated with medieval apocalyptic movements.

name: Raymond Barre
headline: Raymond Barre, 83, Former French Premier, Dies
abstract: Mr. Barre was a prominent economist and served as prime minister of France from 1976 to 1981.

name: Magdalen Nabb
headline: Magdalen Nabb, Mystery Writer in Italy, Dies at 60
abstract: Ms. Nabb was an expatriate English author whose crime novels won her the admiration and friendship of Georges Simenon, the writer whose sensibility most matched her own.

name: Peggy Samuels
headline: Peggy Samuels, Biographer and Art Historian, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Samuels was an amateur art historian who with her husband, Howard, wrote or edited 10 books on art and United States history, including a revealing biography of Frederic Remington, the renowned painter of the American West.

name: Hilly Kristal
headline: Hilly Kristal, 75, Catalyst for Punk at CBGB, Dies
abstract: Hilly Kristal  founded CBGB, the Bowery bar that became the cradle of New York punk and art-rock in the 1970s.

name: June Bingham Birge
headline: June Bingham Birge, Who Wrote Books and Plays, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Birge wrote several nonfiction books and her dramatic work was performed Off Broadway and in regional theaters.

name: Leon Shull
headline: Leon Shull, 93, Champion of Liberal Causes, Dies
abstract: Mr. Shull led the Americans for Democratic Action’s opposition to the Vietnam War and pursued its campaign on behalf of civil rights for blacks.

name: Chester Collier
headline: Chester Collier, 80, Dies; Led Westminster Show
abstract: Chester Collier helped develop “The Mike Douglas Show” and the Fox News Channel and was an official of the Westminster Kennel Club.

name: Arthur Jones
headline: Arthur Jones, 80, Exercise Machine Inventor, Dies
abstract: Mr. Jones’s Nautilus fitness machines helped transform the fitness industry and the way ordinary people exercises.

name: Arthur Jones
headline: Arthur Jones, Former Baltimore Ravens Player, Dies at 39
abstract: He played for the Ravens when the team won the Super Bowl in 2013.

name: Richard Jewell
headline: Richard Jewell, 44, Hero of Atlanta Attack, Dies
abstract: The transformation of Mr. Jewell from heroic security guard to Olympic bombing suspect and back again came to symbolize the excesses of law enforcement and the news media.

name: Edward Seidensticker
headline: Edward Seidensticker, Translator, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Seidensticker, an eminent translator from the Japanese, brought the work of ancient and modern writers to a wide English-speaking public.

name: P. B. MacCready
headline: P. B. MacCready, 81, Inventor, Dies
abstract: Dr. MacCready was an awesomely accomplished inventor who studied circling hawks and vultures to figure out how to realize the loftiest dream of Leonardo da Vinci — inventing a human-powered flying machine.

name: Benjamin Aaron
headline: Benjamin Aaron, an Expert in Labor Law, Dies at 91
abstract: Professor Aaron,  a leader in the field of comparative labor law, promoted increased democracy in the workplace and protection for workers not represented by unions.

name: Gay Brewer
headline: Gay Brewer, Golfer Who Won Masters in 1967, Dies at 75
abstract: Brewer won the 1967 Masters as well as nine other PGA Tour events during the 1960s and 1970s.

name: Edward N. Brandt Jr.
headline: Edward N. Brandt Jr., a Leader on AIDS, Dies at 74
abstract: Dr. Brandt oversaw the nation’s initial response to AIDS as the top-ranking doctor in the government in the early 1980s.

name: Judah Nadich
headline: Judah Nadich, Rabbi Who Improved Care of Holocaust Survivors, Is Dead at 95
abstract: As Gen. Dwight D. Eisenhower’s adviser on Jewish affairs, Rabbi Nadich battled the deplorable conditions faced by Holocaust survivors in displaced persons camps after World War II.

name: Alfred H. Peet
headline: Alfred H. Peet, 87, Dies; Leader of a Coffee Revolution
abstract: The son of a Dutch coffee merchant, he pioneered a revolution in roasting exotic dark beans that led to America’s love affair with high-end coffee.

name: Anacleto Angelini
headline: Anacleto Angelini, Chilean Billionaire, Dead at 93
abstract: Mr. Angelini  built his fortune by investing in fishing and then forestry companies in Chile after emigrating from Italy in 1948.

name: Hans Ruesch
headline: Hans Ruesch, Writer and Grand Prix Winner, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Ruesch was a successful Swiss racecar driver in the years before World War II who later became a writer of well-received novels of adventure, two of which became Hollywood films.

name: Edward McGaffigan
headline: Edward McGaffigan, 58, Atomic Official, Dies
abstract: The longest-serving member in the history of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, he was an often feisty advocate of nuclear technology.

name: Anthony Day
headline: Anthony Day, 74, Editorial Page Editor, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Day, a longtime editorial page editor of The Los Angeles Times, helped transform the paper into a respected voice in national affairs.

name: John T. Scott
headline: John T. Scott,  New Orleans Sculptor, Dies at 67
abstract: John T. Scott’s vibrantly colored kinetic art filtered the spirit of the African diaspora through a modernist lens.

name: John Scott
profession: Organist and Choirmaster in London and New York
headline: John Scott, Organist and Choirmaster in London and New York, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Scott was director of music at St. Thomas Church in Manhattan, and before that, organist and director of music at St. Paul’s Cathedral in London.

name: Bill Deedes
headline: Bill Deedes, Journalist in Britain, Is Dead at 94
abstract: A journalist for three-quarters of a century, Mr. Deedes was sometimes called the most popular man on Fleet Street.

name: Nancy Littlefield
profession: Director of New Yorks Film Office
headline: Nancy Littlefield, 77, Director of New York’s Film Office, Dies
abstract: Ms. Littlefield presided over a major renaissance in film production in New York City.

name: Max McNab
headline: Max McNab, Patriach of Hockey Family, Dies at 83
abstract: Max McNab spent 50 years in hockey as a player, coach and executive, and became the patriarch of a hockey family.

name: Edward Gramlich
headline: Edward Gramlich, 68, Dies; Ex-Governor of Fed
abstract: Mr. Gramlich had warned of a looming crisis in home mortgages and had run a federal board created to aid airlines after the September 2001 attacks.

name: William R. Hudgins
headline: William R. Hudgins, 100, Who Led Black-Owned Banks, Dies
abstract: Mr. Hudgins was a former door-to-door salesman in Harlem who helped start the Carver Federal Savings Bank, now the largest black-owned bank in the nation.

name: Jennifer Dunn
headline: Jennifer Dunn, 66, Former Washington Representative, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Dunn represented part of the Seattle area for six terms and became one of the most powerful Republicans in Congress.

name: D. James Kennedy
headline: Rev. D. James Kennedy, Broadcaster, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Kennedy was a Christian broadcaster and the pastor of a Florida megachurch, who played a critical role in the rise of conservative Christianity.

name: James Kennedy
headline: James Kennedy, Who Inspired the Movie ‘Radio,’ Dies at 72
abstract: Cuba Gooding Jr. played Mr. Kennedy in the film, which chronicled his friendship with a high school football coach in South Carolina.

name: Paul E. Gillmor
headline: Paul E. Gillmor, 68, Ohio  Lawmaker, Dies
abstract: Mr. Gillmor, an Ohio Republican, who was found dead in his apartment on Wednesday, apparently died of natural causes.

name: Luciano Pavarotti
headline: Luciano Pavarotti Is Dead at 71
abstract: The Italian singer’s ringing, pristine sound set a standard for operatic tenors of the postwar era.

name: Judith D. Zuk
profession: Led Revival of Brooklyn Botanic Garden
headline: Judith D. Zuk, 55, Dies; Led Revival of Brooklyn Botanic Garden
abstract: Judith D. Zuk was the president of the Brooklyn Botanic Garden, whose mission she broadened and whose grounds she rejuvenated.

name: Miyoshi Umeki
headline: Miyoshi Umeki, 78, Actress Who Won an Oscar in ’57, Dies
abstract: Miyoshi Umeki was the first Asian performer to win an Oscar, as best supporting actress in her first Hollywood film, “Sayonara.”

name: James Jackson
headline: James Jackson, Rights Activist, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Jackson was a civil rights activist and one of 21 Communist Party members who were indicted in 1951, for, among other things, teaching classes on violent revolution.

name: James Jackson
profession: Changed the Study of Black America
headline: James Jackson, Who Changed the Study of Black America, Dies at 76
abstract: Rather than focus on interracial comparisons, his National Survey of Black Americans explored the complexities within the Black population.

name: Eliot Fremont-Smith
headline: Eliot Fremont-Smith, 78, Former Times Critic, Dies
abstract: In his years at The Times, first at the Book Review and then as a daily book critic, Mr. Fremont-Smith helped usher in an era of modern criticism.

name: Richard Carter
headline: Richard Carter, Author of Racing Guides, Dies at 89
abstract: Richard Carter was a newspaper journalist and author best remembered for his books on race track handicapping he wrote under the pseudonym Tom Ainslie.

name: Mark Weil
headline: Mark Weil, Tashkent Theater Director, Dies at 55
abstract: Mark Weil was an internationally known theater director in Uzbekistan whose troupe, Ilkhom, caused controversy at home with its experimental productions.

name: Madeleine L’Engle
profession: Author of the Classic A Wrinkle in Time
headline: Madeleine L’Engle, Author of the Classic ‘A Wrinkle in Time,’ Is Dead at 88
abstract: Madeleine L’Engle was an author whose work transcended both genre and generation, most memorably in her children’s classic “A Wrinkle in Time.”

name: Jimmy Lee Sudduth
headline: Jimmy Lee Sudduth, Folk Artist, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Mr. Sudduth was an African-American folk artist whose evocative, textured paintings made partly from Alabama mud were prized by collectors around the world.

name: H. R. Dietrich
headline: H. R. Dietrich, Collector of Colonial Arts, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Dietrich was a philanthropist and collector of early American decorative and fine arts who often made his treasures available for public viewing.

name: Cuesta Benberry
headline: Cuesta Benberry, 83, Historian of Quilting, Dies
abstract: Cuesta Benberry was one of the leading historians and archivists of American quilting.

name: Jane Wyman
headline: Jane Wyman, 90, Star of Film and TV, Is Dead
abstract: Jane Wyman won an Oscar for her performance in the movie “Johnny Belinda” and was the first wife of President Ronald Reagan.

name: Arthur Ross
headline: Arthur Ross, Investor and Philanthropist Who Left Mark on the Park, Dies at 96
abstract: Arthur Ross’s contributions to the arts and the environment often reflected his passions, from promoting classicism to establishing a grove of pines in Central Park.

name: Joe Zawinul
headline: Joe Zawinul, 75, Jazz Fusion Pioneer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Zawinul was a classically trained Austrian pianist who achieved fame as a co-leader of the electrified jazz band Weather Report.

name: Anita Roddick
headline: Anita Roddick, Body Shop Founder, Dies at 64
abstract: The crusading entrepreneur founded the vast Body Shop network of cosmetics stores on principles of ending animal testing and supporting the environment.

name: Willie Tee
headline: Willie Tee,  New Orleans Musical Innovator, Dies at 63
abstract: Wilson Turbinton, known as Willie Tee, was a New Orleans keyboardist, singer, songwriter and producer.

name: Burt Hasen
headline: Burt Hasen, Artist Inspired by Maps, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Hasen was a New York painter who drew inspiration from his experience working with maps as a military technician during World War II.

name: Harvey Schultz
headline: Harvey Schultz, 66, Head of Environmental Agency, Dies
abstract: Mr. Schultz was New York City’s commissioner of environmental protection during the last of Mayor Edward I. Koch’s three terms.

name: Richard Cook
profession: Journalist and Author of Books on Jazz
headline: Richard Cook, Journalist and Author of Books on Jazz, Dies at 50
abstract: Mr. Cook was a veteran British music journalist and the author of several acclaimed books on jazz.

name: J. W. Eschbach
headline: J. W. Eschbach, 74, Dies; Developed Anemia Drug
abstract: Dr. Eschbach was a leading kidney specialist whose studies in the 1960s led to a dramatic improvement in the treatment of anemia in patients on dialysis.

name: Eva Crane
headline: Eva Crane, English Expert on World’s Bees, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Crane devoted herself to spreading knowledge about bees as a researcher, historian, archivist, editor and author.

name: Nora Ezell
headline: Nora Ezell, Alabama Quilter, Dies at 88
abstract: A quilter in the African-American tradition, Ms. Ezell was renowned for her storytelling panels and for vividly colorful abstract works.

name: James O. Rigney Jr.
headline: James O. Rigney Jr., Who Wrote as Robert Jordan, Dies at 58
abstract: James Oliver Rigney Jr. was a prolific author who under the pseudonym Robert Jordan wrote the “Wheel of Time” series, a best-selling multivolume fantasy saga.

name: John Swearingen
headline: John Swearingen, Oil Executive, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Swearingen was the most powerful oil executive of his generation and a highly visible defender of the industry during the energy crisis of the 1970s.

name: Alvin S. Lane
headline: Alvin S. Lane, Lawyer and Art Collector, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Lane was a former partner in a major New York City real estate law firm and a leader of efforts to protect art collectors from fraud.

name: Gene Savoy
headline: Gene Savoy, Flamboyant Explorer of Ruins, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Savoy was an amateur archaeologist whose success in finding some 40 Incan and pre-Incan ruins in Peru was matched by a flair for self-promotion that drew on his tales of peril in the jungle.

name: Laurel Burch
headline: Laurel Burch, Artist, Dies at 61
abstract: Ms. Burch as a 20-year-old single mother found metal in junkyards to hammer into jewelry to support her two children, and went on to win distinction as a fanciful designer and success as a savvy businesswoman.

name: Norman Gaylord
headline: Norman Gaylord, a Chemist, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Dr. Gaylord helped develop a safe and permeable material for hard contact lenses that allowed oxygen to reach the eye, thus avoiding a common lens problem.

name: James F. Clarity
profession: Reported on Crime, Politics and War
headline: James F. Clarity Dies at 75; Reported on Crime, Politics and War
abstract: Mr. Clarity was a reporter who covered crime, politics, sports and wars in 40 years of newspapering, mostly for The New York Times

name: David Carliner
headline: David Carliner,  Lawyer and Immigration Advocate, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Carliner was an influential left-leaning lawyer whose work for clients ranging from scholars and scoundrels to cooks and cabdrivers helped define modern immigration law.

name: Alice Ghostley
headline: Alice Ghostley, Comic TV and Stage Actress, Is Dead
abstract: Alice Ghostley was a Tony Award-winning actress who became known to television viewers for her roles as dizzy sidekicks on “Bewitched” and “Designing Women.”

name: Marcel Marceau
headline: Marcel Marceau, Renowned Mime, Dies at 84
abstract: The wiry French mime mostly performed as the chalk-faced Bip and did much to revive the art of pantomime.

name: Boris Grushin
headline: Boris Grushin, Pioneer Soviet Pollster, Is Dead at 78
abstract: In a Communist society where directives came from the top, Dr. Grushin set out to find what the average person thought.

name: Albert Fuller
profession: Conductor and Champion of Early Music
headline: Albert Fuller, Conductor and Champion of Early Music, Dies at 81
abstract: Albert Fuller was an influential harpsichordist, conductor, teacher and author, and the founder of two important early music organizations, the Aston Magna Foundation for Music and the Humanities and the Helicon Foundation.

name: André Emmerich
headline: André Emmerich, Eminent Art Dealer, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Emmerich’s gallery was an early champion of the 1950s and ’60s school of Color Field painting. He also mounted important shows of pre-Columbian art.

name: Haidar Abdel Shafi
headline: Haidar Abdel Shafi, Who Led P.L.O. and Red Crescent, Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Abdel Shafi was a Palestinian leader, physician and founder of the Palestine Red Crescent Society in Gaza.

name: Floria Lasky
headline: Floria Lasky, Lawyer for Broadway Stars, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Lasky was an influential lawyer in the theater world who represented some of its biggest names.

name: Calvin O. Pressley
headline: The Rev. Calvin O. Pressley, Who Urged Clergy to Reach Out, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Pressley was a former executive director of the New York City Mission Society and an adviser to members of the clergy nationwide on how to manage their churches.

name: Stanley Van Ness
headline: Stanley Van Ness, State Public Advocate, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Van Ness, as New Jersey’s and the nation’s first state public advocate, regularly roiled the political scene in the 1970s, weighing in and often filing suits on controversial issues.

name: Edmund H. Sonnenblick
profession: Pioneer in Treatments for Heart Failure
headline: Edmund H. Sonnenblick, a Pioneer in Treatments for Heart Failure, Dies at 74
abstract: Dr. Sonnenblick’s research formed a basis for the modern treatment of heart failure, which has extended the lives of millions of people.

name: Nina Schneider
headline: Nina Schneider, Author of Children’s Science Books, Dies at 94
abstract: Mrs. Schneider wrote dozens of science books for children that deftly explained the intricacies of stars, plants, the human body and even the networks of pipes and cables below city streets.

name: Herbert Gallen
headline: Herbert Gallen, Who Founded Ellen Tracy Line, Dies at 92
abstract: As women began entering the work force in greater numbers, Mr. Gallen’s company introduced a line of more stylish clothing for the workplace.

name: Wolfgang K. H. Panofsky
profession: Physicist and Adviser on Arms Control
headline: Wolfgang K. H. Panofsky, Physicist and Adviser on Arms Control, Dies at 88
abstract: A particle physicist and an adviser on arms control, he promoted stronger scientific ties to Russia and China as a deterrent to nuclear war.

name: Lenore Tawney
headline: Lenore Tawney, an Innovator in Weaving, Dies at 100
