abstract: Ms. Tawney’s monumental sculptural weavings redefined the possibilities of  her crafts and helped create the genre of fiber art.

name: William Wirtz
headline: William Wirtz, Hockey Team Owner, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Mr. Wirtz was the longtime owner of the Chicago Blackhawks, the National Hockey League franchise controlled by his family for more than half a century.

name: Joseph V. Noble
headline: Joseph V. Noble, an Expert in Antiquities, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Noble was a former director of the Museum of the City of New York who earlier exposed three famous works at the Metropolitan Museum of Art as fakes.

name: George Rieveschl
headline: George Rieveschl, 91, Allergy Reliever, Dies
abstract: Dr. Rieveschl, a chemical engineer, invented the antihistamine Benadryl.

name: Ken Danby
headline: Ken Danby, Prolific Canadian Painter, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Danby was already fairly well known for his crisp images of mountains and lakes when he and some friends returned to their childhood passion for hockey.

name: Helen E. Freeman
headline: Helen E. Freeman, Protector of Snow Leopards, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Helen Elaine Freeman was a conservationist who fell in love with two snow leopards when she was a volunteer at a zoo and eventually founded a leading advocacy organization working to preserve them.

name: Christian Herter Jr.
headline: Christian Herter Jr., Longtime Public Servant, Dies at 88
abstract: Christian A. Herter Jr. was a lawyer and longtime public servant who in the 1960s was the first chairman of the New York Urban Coalition.

name: Ray Timothy
headline: Ray Timothy, 75, Former President at NBC Television, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Timothy started working for NBC television as a tour guide and 34 years and more than 30 jobs later retired as one of the network’s top executives.

name: Al Oerter
headline: Al Oerter, Olympic Discus Champion, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Al Oerter, a discus thrower, became the first modern track and field athlete to win four consecutive Olympic titles in one event.

name: Bruce Smith
headline: Bruce Smith, Who Sued Libya in Bombing, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Bruce M. Smith was a former Pan Am pilot who lost his wife in the bombing of Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland, and became a driving force in efforts to thwart terrorists.

name: Harry Dent
headline: Harry Dent, an Architect of Nixon ‘Southern Strategy’, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Dent helped to devise the successful “Southern strategy”, which some called an appeal to people left on the political sidelines while others called it cloaked racism.

name: Martin Manulis
headline: Martin Manulis, TV Pioneer, Dies at 92
abstract: Martin Manulis was a television, film and theatrical producer who gave life, guidance and personality to “Playhouse 90,” the 1950s show that epitomized what is remembered as television’s golden age of live drama.

name: Harry Lee
headline: Harry Lee, Outspoken Louisiana Sheriff, Dies at 75
abstract: Sheriff Lee was a wide-girthed lawman in the suburbs of New Orleans who became an outspoken voice for hostility to the city and a magnet for the anger of its black citizens.

name: George Grizzard
headline: George Grizzard, Actor Noted for Albee Roles, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Grizzard was a versatile actor who achieved his greatest renown on the stage, playing everything from Shakespeare to Shaw, from Neil Simon to Edward Albee.

name: Ralph Sturges
headline: Ralph Sturges, Chief of Mohegan Tribe, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Sturges was among Native American leaders in the 1980s and 1990s who helped bring about a cultural and economic renaissance for fading or lost East Coast Indian tribes.

name: Tony Ryan
headline: Tony Ryan, Who Founded Discount Airline, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Ryan was founder of Ryanair Holdings, Europe’s biggest discount airline.

name: James Michaels
headline: James Michaels, Longtime Forbes Editor, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Michaels gave an acerbic, contrarian voice to Forbes magazine in 37 years as its editor and influenced generations of business journalists.

name: Ned Sherrin
headline: Ned Sherrin, Creator of Mock News ‘Week,’ Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Sherrin defied staid British standards with barbed, up-to-the-minute mockery of the powerful, pompous and preposterous in his groundbreaking ’60s TV show “That Was The Week That Was.”

name: Alfred J. Audi
headline: Alfred J. Audi, Who Revived a Furniture Maker, Dies at 69
abstract: Sensing a demand for Mission-style furniture, Mr. Audi built a large furniture maker and retailer on reproductions of the style.

name: Frederick H. Burkhardt
headline: Frederick H. Burkhardt, a Prominent Educator, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Burkhardt headed both the American Council of Learned Societies and Bennington College and also helped put the open-admissions policy into effect at the City University of New York.

name: Rogelio Salmona
headline: Rogelio Salmona, Colombian Architect Who Transformed Cities, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Salmona transformed Colombia’s urban look with soaring brick towers and structures that resembled pre-Columbian cities in miniature.

name: Oswald M. Ungers
profession: Design Theorist and Architect of Major German Projects
headline: Oswald M. Ungers, Design Theorist and Architect of Major German Projects, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Ungers was a German architect, planner and teacher known for the pure geometries of his buildings and for his theoretical writings.

name: Alexandra Boulat
headline: Alexandra Boulat, War Photographer, Is Dead at 45
abstract: Ms. Boulat was an award-winning photographer known for a clear, descriptive style and a knack for making emotionally moving, often idiosyncratic images of people affected by war.

name: J. Edward Lundy
headline: J. Edward Lundy, ‘Whiz Kid’ at Ford Motor, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Lundy helped resuscitate the Ford Motor Company after World War II and developed financial forecasting methods emulated throughout the auto industry.

name: Stanley P. Butchart
headline: Stanley P. Butchart Dies at 85; Pushed Airspeed Envelope
abstract: Mr. Butchart was a test pilot who flew and helped evaluate early rocket-powered aircraft in the 1950s, when he and fellow researchers were able to push the speed of an airplane past Mach 2.

name: William Zimmer
headline: William Zimmer, Critic With SoHo Focus, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Zimmer was an art critic who covered SoHo’s gallery scene in the 1970s and ’80s and later wrote for The New York Times and other publications.

name: John P. Henebry
headline: John P. Henebry, Innovative Combat Pilot, Dies at 89
abstract: Maj. Gen. John P. Henebry played a leading role in the Army Air Forces’ innovative low-level bombing of Japanese ships in the South Pacific during World War II.

name: Israel Kugler
headline: Israel Kugler, Union Official Who Led Strike at St. John’s, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Kugler was a union organizer for college teachers who became prominent in the mid-1960s when he led an 18-month strike by faculty members at St. John’s University.

name: Richard Graham
headline: Richard Graham, Equal Rights Leader, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Graham was an original member of the federal Equal Employment Opportunity Commission who also helped found the National Organization for Women.

name: Erik Hazelhoff Roelfzema
headline: Erik Hazelhoff Roelfzema, a ‘Soldier of Orange,’ Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Hazelhoff Roelfzema was acclaimed as one of the Netherlands’ greatest World War II heroes for leading missions against Nazi occupiers of his homeland.

name: Nathalie Gleboff
profession: Director of School of American Ballet
headline: Nathalie Gleboff, Director of School of American Ballet, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Gleboff was the former executive director of the School of American Ballet, the New York City Ballet’s affiliate school, and a longtime administrator there.

name: Lorraine Rothman
headline: Lorraine Rothman, Women’s Advocate, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Rothman was a leader of the feminist health movement in the 1970s who suggested that women could  end very early pregnancies without medical supervision.

name: William T. Golden
headline: William T. Golden,  Financier and Key Science Adviser, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Mr. Golden was an investment banker, a philanthropist and a main architect of American science policy in the 20th century.

name: Donald J. Mulvihill
headline: Donald J. Mulvihill, Who Led Crime Panel, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Mulvihill studied the causes of violent crime under President Lyndon B. Johnson and led the Washington office of the law firm Cahill Gordon & Reindel for more than 40 years.

name: Charles Griffith
headline: Charles Griffith, ‘Little Shop of Horrors’ Screenwriter, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Griffith, who was known for using dark humor in his scripts, wrote dozens of films in several genres, like science fiction, westerns and horror.

name: Eugene Saenger
headline: Eugene Saenger, Controversial Doctor, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Saenger set off a dispute over medical ethics by leading a cold-war research study that exposed patients in Cincinnati to intense doses of radiation.

name: Douglas Yearley
headline: Douglas Yearley, Who Led Phelps Dodge, Dies at 71
abstract: The former chairman and chief executive of the copper producer Phelps Dodge spent four decades at the Phoenix-based company.

name: Shane Wallace
headline: Shane Wallace, Who Advised on Mergers, Dies at 38
abstract: Mr. Wallace, an investment banker, played a leading role in several of the largest recent telecommunications mergers.

name: Walter Kempowski
headline: Walter Kempowski, German Author and Diarist, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Kempowski compiled thousands of pages of recollections from eyewitnesses of World War II into a monumental firsthand record of the German wartime experience.

name: Bud Ekins
headline: Bud Ekins, Stunt Cyclist, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Ekins went from racing through the mountain trails and desert rambles of Southern California in the late 1940s to renown as the stuntman double for Steve McQueen in a 65-foot flight over a barbed-wire barrier.

name: Nolan Herndon
headline: Nolan Herndon, Navigator in ’42 Raid, Dies at 88
abstract: Lieutenant Herndon, a navigator-bombardier in the storied Doolittle raid over Japan in World War II, spent more than a year interned in the Soviet Union after his plane made an emergency landing in Russia.

name: James Robbins
headline: James Robbins Dies at 65; Led Expansion of Cox Cable
abstract: Mr. Robbins made his mark not only by expanding Cox fourfold but also by giving customer service high priority in an industry where it had not always been valued.

name: Chinmoy
headline: Sri Chinmoy, Athletic Spiritual Leader, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Chinmoy used strenuous exercise and art to spread his message of world harmony and inner peace.

name: Alfred Russell
headline: Alfred Russell,  Painter With a Classical Style, Dies at 87
abstract: Alfred Russell was a New York School painter who abandoned abstraction for a classicizing, Surrealistic figurative style.

name: Margaret Carson
headline: Margaret Carson, Classical Music Publicist, Dies at 96
abstract: Margaret Carson was widely regarded as the leading lady of classical music publicists in New York, who shepherded a generation of singers through the Metropolitan Opera.

name: Enrico Banducci
headline: Enrico Banducci, 85, Dies; Ran Seminal San Francisco Nightclub
abstract: Mr. Banducci was the owner and host of the Hungry I, the intimate, brick-walled club that became a launching pad for performers like Mort Sahl, Barbra Streisand and Shelley Berman.

name: Richard D. Gidron
profession: Ran an Empire of Car Dealerships
headline: Richard D. Gidron Is Dead at 68; Ran an Empire of Car Dealerships
abstract: Mr. Gidron was one of America’s earliest and most successful black owners of a Cadillac dealership before falling on hard times and going to prison for a year for fraud and tax evasion.

name: Bob Denard
headline: Bob Denard, Hired Gun for Coups, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Denard was a legendary French soldier of fortune who for decades was involved in coups and mercenary activities across Africa and the Middle East.

name: James L. Oakes
headline: James L. Oakes Dies at 83; Nixon Choice for Federal Bench
abstract: Judge Oakes was appointed to the federal appeals court in New York by President Richard M. Nixon and yet quickly became one of its leading liberal voices.

name: Carol Bruce
headline: Carol Bruce, Actress on Film, Stage and TV, Dies at 87
abstract: Carol Bruce was a promising stage actress and singer from the 1940s who became best known late in her long career as Mama Carlson, the ruthless station owner on the television comedy “WKRP in Cincinnati.”

name: Ernest Withers
headline: Ernest Withers, Civil Rights Photographer, Dies at 85
abstract: Ernest C. Withers’s voluminous catalog of arresting black-and-white images illustrates a history of life in the segregated South in the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Judy Crichton
headline: Judy Crichton,  Producer of ‘American Experience’, Dies at 77
abstract: Judy Crichton was one of the first women to produce news on network television and the first executive producer of “American Experience,” the acclaimed public television history series.

name: Vernon Bellecourt
profession: Protested the Use of Indian Mascots
headline: Vernon Bellecourt, Who Protested the Use of Indian Mascots, Dies at 75
abstract: Vernon Bellecourt, an Ojibwa Indian who waged a long campaign for native rights, was most visible in battling the use of Indian nicknames by sports teams.

name: Teresa Brewer
profession: Cheerful Chart-Topper on the Hit Parade
headline: Teresa Brewer, Cheerful Chart-Topper on the Hit Parade, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Ms. Brewer topped the 1950s hit parade and then reinvented herself as an exuberant jazz singer in the 1970s.

name: Andrée de Jongh
headline: Andrée de Jongh, 90, Legend of Belgian Resistance, Dies
abstract: Ms. de Jongh became a World War II legend ushering many downed Allied airmen on a treacherous, 1,000-mile path from occupied Belgium to safety.

name: William Crowe
headline: Adm. William Crowe Dies at 82; Led Joint Chiefs
abstract: Admiral Crowe served as chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff during the Reagan administration and later as ambassador to Britain.

name: Joey Bishop
headline: Joey Bishop, 89, Last of the Rat Pack, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Bishop was the long-faced comedian and the last surviving member of the Rat Pack, Frank Sinatra’s celebrated retinue of the 1960’s.

name: Deborah Kerr
profession: Actress Known for Genteel Grace and a Sexy Beach Kiss
headline: Deborah Kerr, Actress Known for Genteel Grace and a Sexy Beach Kiss, Dies at 86
abstract: The versatile actress projected the quintessential image of the proper Englishwoman but was also indelible in one of the most sexually provocative scenes of the 1950s.

name: Robert Lantz
headline: Robert Lantz, 93, Agent to the Stars, Dies
abstract: Mr. Lantz was a talent agent whose clients ranged from Bette Davis to Leonard Bernstein to Chief Justice William H. Rehnquist.

name: Catherine Roraback
headline: Catherine Roraback, 87, Influential Lawyer, Dies
abstract: Ms. Roraback pressed the case that eventually led to the Supreme Court ruling that laws banning contraceptives were unconstitutional, a precursor to Roe v. Wade.

name: Kisho Kurokawa
headline: Kisho Kurokawa, Japanese Architect Who Pioneered Organic Structures, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Kurokawa was one of the youngest founding members of Japan’s Metabolist movement.

name: Arthur Richenthal
headline: Arthur Richenthal, Landlord Lawyer, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Richenthal won a decision by New York State’s highest court that shook the cornerstone of the city’s survival plan in the fiscal crisis of the mid-1970s.

name: G. Tom Shires
headline: G. Tom Shires, 81, Trauma Expert, Dies
abstract: Dr. Shires was a leading surgeon and expert on trauma who carried out path-breaking research, helped create the largest burn center in New York City and trained two generations of surgical leaders.

name: Peg Bracken
headline: Peg Bracken, ‘I Hate to Cook’ Author, Dies at 89
abstract: Peg Bracken parlayed her irreverent wit — and her passionate dislike of a traditional womanly duty — into a subversive best seller.

name: Vincent DeDomenico
headline: Vincent DeDomenico, an Inventor of Rice-A-Roni, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. DeDomenico Sr. and his brothers invented Rice-A-Roni, one of the classic kitchen helpers of the 1960s.

name: Ileana Sonnabend
headline: Ileana Sonnabend, Art World Figure, Dies at 92
abstract: Ileana Sonnabend’s eye, shrewdness and lasting alliance with her first husband, Leo Castelli, made her one of the most formidable contemporary art dealers of her time.

name: R. B. Kitaj
headline: R. B. Kitaj, Painter of Moody Human Dramas, Dies at 74
abstract: R. B. Kitaj was an American artist who became influential in Britain with figurative and Pop Art paintings that ran against the grain of 1960s and ’70s abstraction.

name: Tom Murphy
headline: Tom Murphy, Irish Actor, Dies at 39; Won Tony for ‘Beauty Queen’
abstract: Mr. Murphy won a Tony Award for his only Broadway role — a comically discontented Irishman in “The Beauty Queen of Leenane.”

name: Tom B. Murphy
headline: Tom B. Murphy, a Longtime Power in Georgia, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Murphy was a colorful and commanding legislator who ruled the House of Representatives in Georgia when Democrats were at the height of their power in the state.

name: Tom Murphy
headline: Tom Murphy, Acclaimed Irish Playwright, Is Dead at 83
abstract: His dark works avoided the stereotype of a rural Irish utopia, instead exploring subjects like the county’s famine and its history of emigration.

name: Bobby Mauch
headline: Bobby Mauch, Actor Who Played Opposite Twin, Dies at 86
abstract: Bobby Mauch played the pauper (or was it the prince?) in the rambunctious 1937 film of Mark Twain’s “Prince and the Pauper” opposite his twin brother.

name: Eve Curie Labouisse
headline: Eve Curie Labouisse,  Mother’s Biographer, Dies at 102
abstract: Eve Curie Labouisse was a journalist and humanitarian best known for her biography of her mother, the Nobel Prize-winning scientist Marie Curie.

name: Randall Forsberg
headline: Randall Forsberg, 64, Nuclear Freeze Advocate, Dies
abstract: Dr. Forsberg helped start the nuclear freeze movement that culminated in the largest political demonstration in American history.

name: G. A. Renner
headline: G. A. Renner Dies at 75; Wrote of Abuse Within Church
abstract: Mr. Renner helped uncover a trail of sexual abuse accusations against the powerful founder of a Roman Catholic religious order, the Legionaries of Christ.

name: Judy Mazel
profession: Creator of Best-Selling Beverly Hills Diet
headline: Judy Mazel, Creator of Best-Selling ‘Beverly Hills Diet,’ Is Dead at 63
abstract: Ms. Mazel’s 1981 best-selling book “The Beverly Hills Diet” recommended eating nothing but fruit, and lots it, for the first 10 days of a six-week regimen.

name: Abby Ray Catledge
headline: Abby Ray Catledge, 91, Editor’s Widow, Dies
abstract: Mrs. Catledge was the wife of Turner Catledge, a former executive editor of The New York Times.

name: Arthur Kornberg
headline: Arthur Kornberg, Biochemist, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Kornberg’s Nobel Prize-winning discovery of how DNA is assembled helped ignite the biotechnology revolution.

name: Nick Monte
headline: Nick Monte Dies at 90; Revamped Beach Resort
abstract: Mr. Monte, a lover of the ocean, transformed Gurney’s Inn from a modest summer hotel on the beach in Montauk, N.Y., into a celebrated year-round resort.

name: Robert Shields
headline: Robert Shields, Wordy Diarist, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Shields recorded his life in five-minute segments and ended up with a 37.5-million-word diary, perhaps the most verbose one ever.

name: Thomas J. Meskill
profession: Ex-Congressman, Connecticut Governor and Federal Judge
headline: Thomas J. Meskill Dies at 79; Ex-Congressman, Connecticut Governor and Federal Judge
abstract: Governor Meskill steered Connecticut away from the edge of bankruptcy, instituted a state lottery and oversaw the creation of a department of environmental protection in the 1970s.

name: Porter Wagoner
headline: Porter Wagoner, Singer, Dies at 80
abstract: Porter Wagoner was a country singer who mixed rhinestone suits, a towering pompadour and cornball jokes with direct, simple songs over a career best known for his partnership with Dolly Parton.

name: Robert Goulet
headline: Robert Goulet, Actor, Dies at 73
abstract: Robert Goulet played a dashing Lancelot in 1960 and went on to a wide-ranging career as a singer and actor, winning a Tony, a Grammy and an Emmy.

name: Khun Sa
headline: Khun Sa, Golden Triangle Drug King, Dies at 73
abstract: Khun Sa was a publicity-loving Golden Triangle drug lord who thrived in the region’s kill-or-be-killed cauldron of ethnic rivalries and heroin-financed private armies.

name: Aleksandr Feklisov
headline: Aleksandr Feklisov, Spy Tied to Rosenbergs, Dies at 93
abstract: Col. Aleksandr Feklisov directed Julius Rosenberg’s spying for the K.G.B. and acted as an intermediary between the White House and the Kremlin during the Cuban missile crisis.

name: Kay L. Anderson
headline: Kay L. Anderson, ‘Vows’ Subject, Dies at 41
abstract: Ms. Anderson was a woman with learning disabilities whose wedding to her husband, who has similar disabilities, was the subject of the Vows column of The New York Times on Sept. 16.

name: Paul W. Tibbets Jr.
headline: Paul W. Tibbets Jr., Pilot of Enola Gay, Dies at 92
abstract: General Tibbets commanded the B-29 Superfortress that dropped the atomic bomb on Hiroshima in World War II.

name: Sam Dana
headline: Sam Dana, 104, Oldest Former N.F.L. Player, Is Dead
abstract: Sam Dana emerged as a celebrity of sorts four years ago when he was found to be alive — contrary to reports in the football record book.

name: John Woodruff
headline: John Woodruff, an Olympian, Dies at 92
abstract: John Woodruff’s halting, come-from-behind victory in the 800-meter run in the 1936 Berlin Olympics astonished the sports world and helped embarrass Adolf Hitler.

name: Thomas Dawes
headline: Thomas Dawes, Musician and Jingle Writer, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Dawes wrote music for some of advertising’s best-known commercial jingles, including “Plop, Plop, Fizz, Fizz” for Alka-Seltzer and “7Up, the Uncola.”

name: Lowell Smith
headline: Lowell Smith, 56, Dancer in Harlem Troupe, Dies
abstract: Mr. Smith used precise mastery of classical ballet and exquisite expressiveness of body and face to convey emotions from tranquility to charged passion.

name: Igor Moiseyev
headline: Igor Moiseyev, Russian Choreographer, Dies at 101
abstract: Igor Moiseyev, who created a new form of theatrical folk dance and whose troupe was one of the most popular dance companies of the 20th century, died today in Moscow.

name: Johtje Vos
headline: Johtje Vos, Who Saved Wartime Jews, Dies at 97
abstract: Mrs. Vos and her husband hid three dozen Jews in their home in the Netherlands during World War II, shepherding them into a secret tunnel whenever the Gestapo pounded on the door.

name: Chef Tell
profession: Turned Kitchen Skill Into TV Fame
headline: Chef Tell, Who Turned Kitchen Skill Into TV Fame, Dies at 63
abstract: Before there were celebrity chefs, Chef Tell, who was born Friedman Paul Erhardt in Germany, came out of the kitchen to become one of the first chefs to appear on television.

name: Peter A. A. Berle
headline: Peter A. A. Berle, Lawmaker and Conservationist, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Berle spent decades fighting for open space and clean water as a New York State assemblyman, commissioner of the State Department of Environmental Conservation and president of the National Audubon Society.

name: Leon Brand
headline: Leon Brand, 74, Who Founded New York Architecture Prize, Dies
abstract: Mr. Brand conceived and administered the Albert S. Bard Award, an architectural prize intended to raise the standard of excellence for building design in New York City.

name: Leslie Orgel
headline: Leslie Orgel, Biochemist Who Studied Origins of Life, Dies at 80
abstract: Dr. Orgel’s studies of early life on primitive Earth helped lead to the formation of a now widely accepted theory about the development of DNA.

name: Mary Lillian Ellison
headline: Mary Lillian Ellison, 84, the  Fabulous Moolah, Is Dead
abstract: Mary Lillian Ellison’s flying head scissors and hair-pulling “flying mare” body slams brought her renown as the professional wrestler the Fabulous Moolah.

name: Peter Viertel
headline: Peter Viertel, 86, Author and Screenwriter, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Viertel plumbed his relationships with the aristocracy of Hollywood and literary lions like Hemingway to produce provocative works of fiction and memoir.

name: Bradford Kelleher
headline: Bradford Kelleher, Creator of Met’s Store, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Kelleher founded the the Metropolitan Museum of Art’s first full-fledged gift shop and oversaw the creation of countless artful and educational tchotchkes.

name: F. Maynard Sundman
headline: F. Maynard Sundman, Stamp Dealer, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Sundman’s innovative mail-order marketing, using everything from comic books to matchbook covers, introduced millions to the once exclusive worlds of philately and numismatics.

name: Frank Viola
profession: Leader in Sport of Racing Pigeons
headline: Frank Viola, Leader in Sport of Racing Pigeons, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Viola was best known for sponsoring what was considered one of the most prestigious races of the year, the Frank Viola Invitational, a 400-mile contest in which the birds are released in Ohio and fly back to New York.

name: Enzo Biagi
profession: Journalist Fired in Italian Political Fight
headline: Enzo Biagi, 87, Journalist Fired in Italian Political Fight, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Biagi’s criticism of Silvio Berlusconi during the 2001 election campaign got him ousted from state television when Mr. Berlusconi became prime minister.

name: Hank Thompson
headline: Hank Thompson Is Dead; Country Singer Was 82
abstract: Mr. Thompson fused jazz-inflected Western swing and hard-edged honky-tonk to produce seven decades of musical musings.

name: Fred W. McDarrah
headline: Fred W. McDarrah, Photographer, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. McDarrah was a self-described square who, as a longtime photographer for The Village Voice, documented the unwashed exploits of the Beat generation.

name: Paul Soloway
headline: Paul Soloway, 66, World Bridge Champion, Dies
abstract: Mr. Soloway won five Bermuda Bowl world-team titles with four different partners and placed second twice. He also gained silver medals in two World Team Olympiads.

name: John M. Kernochan
headline: John M. Kernochan, Copyright Defender, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Kernochan was a leading professor of copyright law and the founder of the Kernochan Center for Law, Media and the Arts at Columbia University.

name: Abram Lerner
headline: Abram Lerner, Museum Director, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Lerner was the first director of the Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden, the repository that includes works by Picasso, Rodin, Matisse and Mondrian.

name: Jane Cooper
headline: Jane Cooper, 83, Poet of Women’s Lives, Dies
abstract: Ms. Cooper’s work explored women’s struggle to maintain meaningful artistic lives in postwar America — or in fact in the America of any era.

name: George Ratterman
headline: George Ratterman, Football Star and Sheriff, Dies at 80
abstract: George Ratterman was a quarterback for Notre Dame’s 1946 national champions and the Cleveland Browns who later drew national attention when he was drugged and set up for an arrest.

name: Chad Varah
headline: Rev. Chad Varah, Anglican Priest Who Helped the Suicidal, Dies at 95
abstract: The Rev. Chad Varah was an outspoken, publicity-sly, sometimes cantankerous Anglican priest who started a telephone hot line for the suicidal.

name: Norman Mailer
headline: Norman Mailer, Towering Writer With Matching Ego, Dies at 84
abstract: Norman Mailer was an outspoken novelist who loomed over American letters longer and larger than any writer of his generation.

name: John E. Grenier
headline: John E. Grenier, 77, a Leader of Goldwater’s ’64 Bid, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Grenier was one of the architects of Senator Barry M. Goldwater’s Southern strategy in his failed bid for the presidency in 1964.

name: Ray S. Smith
headline: Ray S. Smith, Arkansas Lawmaker, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Smith cast the only vote against giving the Arkansas governor the power to close public schools during the turmoil after the integration of Central High School in Little Rock in 1957.

name: Carrie Rozelle
profession: Started a Center for Learning Disabilities
headline: Carrie Rozelle, 69, Child Advocate, Dies; Started a Center for Learning Disabilities
abstract: Mrs. Rozelle’s struggles with the daily “hurricane” of a son with learning disabilities prompted her to start the National Center for Learning Disabilities.

name: John Firor
headline: John Firor, 80, Early Voice on Environment, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Firor, an environmental scholar and former director of the National Center of Atmospheric Research, was an early voice linking climate change and human activity.

name: Laraine Day
headline: Laraine Day, ‘B+ Movie’ Star, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Day appeared in almost two dozen MGM movies during Hollywood’s Golden Age, notably as the nurse Mary Lamont in a series of Dr. Kildare movies.

name: Luis Herrera Campíns
headline: Luis Herrera Campíns, Venezuela Leader, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Herrera Campíns was a former president whose years in office were marked by bountiful oil riches and a painful economic bust when oil prices plunged in the early 1980s.

name: Delbert Mann
headline: Delbert Mann, Director, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Mann, a director from the heyday of live television, won an Oscar for his first big-screen effort, “Marty,” in 1955.

name: Dick Nolan
headline: Dick Nolan, 75, N.F.L. Coach and Player, Is Dead
abstract: Dick Nolan played nine seasons as a N.F.L. defensive back and was later a head coach for 11 years, twice guiding the San Francisco 49ers to conference championship games.

name: A. F. Hawkins
headline: A. F. Hawkins, Civil Rights Lawmaker, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Hawkins was California’s first black representative in Congress and had a hand in important civil rights legislation, including the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

name: Ira Levin
headline: Ira Levin, of ‘Rosemary’s Baby,’ Dies at 78
abstract: Ira Levin was a mild-mannered playwright and novelist who wrote creepy best sellers like “Rosemary’s Baby,” “The Stepford Wives” and “The Boys From Brazil.”

name: Gerald D. Feldman
profession: Historian of the Nazis and Finances
headline: Gerald D. Feldman, Historian of the Nazis and Finances, Dies at 70
abstract: Dr. Feldman was part of a team of international historians that found documents proving that Deutsche Bank had financed the building of Auschwitz.

name: George W. George
headline: George W. George, 87, Broadway Producer, Dies
abstract: Mr. George was a film and theatrical producer whose credits include the acclaimed film “My Dinner With Andre” as well as a run of successful Broadway productions.

name: Salome Gluecksohn-Waelsch
headline: Salome Gluecksohn-Waelsch, 100, Geneticist, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Waelsch, who had fled Nazi Germany to pursue her studies, was awarded the National Medal of Science for her work in developmental genetics.

name: Michael J. Biondi
headline: Michael J. Biondi, Banker and Deal Maker, Dies at 50
abstract: Mr. Biondi was a prominent investment banker who advised clients in some of the biggest deals in the last few years.

name: Joe Nuxhall
headline: Joe Nuxhall, Pitcher for Reds, Is Dead
abstract: Joe Nuxhall, who spent more than half a century with the Reds as a pitcher and broadcaster, died Thursday at 79.

name: Tadahiro Sekimoto
headline: Tadahiro Sekimoto, Electronics Executive, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Sekimoto presided over NEC, the Japanese electronics firm, during its rise into a top global computer maker before resigning in a military procurement scandal

name: Clara Fox
headline: Clara Fox, Tireless Advocate for Subsidized Housing, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mrs. Fox was  an advocate of subsidized housing for poor and moderate-income people and the founder of the Settlement Housing Fund, a nonprofit organization that now houses 2,200 families in 44 buildings in New York City.

name: Robert Taylor
headline: Robert Taylor Dies at 59; Won 2 Medals in ’72 Olympics
abstract: Mr. Taylor was an American sprinter who won gold and silver medals in the 1972 Olympics in Munich after two of his teammates were memorably disqualified because of a scheduling mix-up.

name: Robert E. L. Taylor
headline: Robert E. L. Taylor, Philadelphia Newsman, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Taylor was the publisher of The Philadelphia Bulletin when it was one of the nation’s largest newspapers and briefly went to jail in a test case of journalists’ right to keep sources confidential.

name: Robert Taylor
profession: Put Hand Soap in a Bottle
headline: Robert Taylor, Who Put Hand Soap in a Bottle, Dies at 77
abstract: From Softsoap to the fragrance Obsession by Calvin Klein, Mr. Taylor’s consumer products made their way into millions of homes.

name: Robert Taylor
headline: Robert Taylor, Innovator Who Shaped Modern Computing, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Taylor’s work was instrumental in the creation of the internet, the modern personal computer and the mouse.

name: Jack Kuney
profession: Producer of Notable Early TV Shows
headline: Jack Kuney, 88, Producer of Notable Early TV Shows, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Kuney was known in particular as a producer of “The Play of the Week,” a drama anthology broadcast in the late 1950s and early ’60s by WNTA-TV, Channel 13.

name: Harold Alfond
headline: Harold Alfond, Donor and Shoe Factory Owner, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Alfond parlayed a hitchhiker’s tip into a fortune by founding the Dexter Shoe Company and running it for four decades.

name: Sergio del Valle
headline: Sergio del Valle, a Castro Stalwart, Dies
abstract: Gen. Sergio del Valle Jimenez was a doctor in Fidel Castro’s rebel army in the late 1950s and army chief of staff during the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis.

name: Herbert Barrett
headline: Herbert Barrett, Musicians’ Manager, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Herbert Barrett was a leading business manager who oversaw the careers of prominent musicians.

name: Harold J. Berman
profession: Altered Beliefs About Origins of Western Law
headline: Harold J. Berman, 89, Who Altered Beliefs About Origins of Western Law, Dies
abstract: Mr. Berman wrote 25 books and more than 400 articles on subjects as diverse as Russian culture and comparative legal history.

name: Rita Hillman
profession: Art Lover and Advocate for Nursing
headline: Rita Hillman, Art Lover and Advocate for Nursing, Dies at 95
abstract: Mrs. Hillman, a philanthropist and art collector, used the proceeds from the sale of Picasso’s “Mother and Child” to support the education of hundreds of nurses.

name: Martin D. Raab
headline: Martin D. Raab, 75, an Architect for the City, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Raab was chosen by Mayor Rudolph W. Giuliani to lead the city’s School Construction Authority at a time when the agency was struggling.

name: Rudi Schmid
headline: Rudi Schmid, 85, Leading Liver Researcher, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Schmid taught medicine for more than 35 years, beginning at Harvard before moving to the University of Chicago and finally to San Francisco.

name: Craig Smith
profession: Boston-Based Conductor Noted for Bach Cantatas
headline: Craig Smith, Boston-Based Conductor Noted for Bach Cantatas, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Smith was best known internationally for his collaborations with the iconoclastic director Peter Sellars and the choreographer Mark Morris.

name: Dick Wilson
profession: Squeezer of Tissue Rolls on Television
headline: Dick Wilson, Squeezer of Tissue Rolls on Television, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Wilson, a British-born character actor, won American television fame as Mr. Whipple, the comically fussy star of two decades of Charmin toilet paper commercials.

name: Mary Walker Phillips
headline: Mary Walker Phillips, 83, Knitter of Art, Is Dead
abstract: Miss Phillips took the utilitarian craft of knitting and gave it bold new life as a modern art form to be displayed on the walls of museums around the world.

name: Victor Rabinowitz
headline: Victor Rabinowitz, 96, Leftist Lawyer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Rabinowitz’s causes and clients ranged from labor unions to Black Panthers to Cuba to Dashiell Hammett to Dr. Benjamin Spock to his own daughter.

name: Milo Radulovich
headline: Milo Radulovich, 81, Dies; Symbol of ’50s Red Scare
abstract: After being fired as an Air Force reserve officer, Mr. Radulovich became a searing symbol of the excesses of anti-Communism in the 1950s.

name: Ian Smith
profession: Defiant Symbol of White Rule in Africa
headline: Ian Smith, Defiant Symbol of White Rule in Africa, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Ian Smith, the former prime minister of Britain’s rebellious colony of Rhodesia, once promised that white rule in Africa would endure for 1,000 years.

name: Irving Bluestone
profession: Head of Union Talks With G.M
headline: Irving Bluestone, 90, Head of Union Talks With G.M., Dies
abstract: Mr. Bluestone was chief negotiator for more than 400,000 workers at General Motors in the 1970s and an advocate of worker participation in management.

name: Jim Ringo
profession: Pro Football Hall of Fame Center
headline: Jim Ringo, Pro Football Hall of Fame Center, Dies at 75
abstract: Ringo, an undersized center who played 15 seasons in the National Football League, was elected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1981.

name: John D. Rock
headline: John D. Rock, Former G.M. Executive, Is Dead at 71
abstract: John D. Rock was a blunt-talking General Motors executive who tried unsuccessfully to save the Oldsmobile division.

name: Paul Wasserman
headline: Paul Wasserman, 73, Publicist to Rock Stars, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Wasserman was one of the most sought-after music publicists from the mid-1960s into the ’90s.

name: Merle Sande
headline: Merle Sande, AIDS Pioneer, Dies at 68
abstract: Dr. Sande’s early recognition of the looming public health crisis posed by AIDS led to the development of basic protocols for how to handle infected patients.

name: Francine Parker
headline: Francine Parker, 81, Director of Antiwar Film, Dies
abstract: Ms. Parker directed a controversial anti-Vietnam War documentary film that mixed footage of spoofing entertainers including Jane Fonda and Donald Sutherland with interviews with disillusioned soldiers.

name: Samuel L. Leonard
headline: Samuel L. Leonard, Cornell Zoologist, Dies at 101
abstract: Dr. Leonard’s studies of reproductive hormones in animals helped prepare the foundation for in vitro fertilization in women.

name: Maurice Béjart
headline: Maurice Béjart, 80, Ballet Iconoclast, Dies
abstract: Mr. Béjart’s work attracted both adulation from mass audiences and skepticism from critics who doubted his ability to choreograph.

name: Robert McNair
profession: Governor of South Carolina in the 60s
headline: Robert McNair, Governor of South Carolina in the ’60s, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. McNair was a finalist to become Vice President Hubert H. Humphrey’s running mate, but his career was cut short by what became known as the Orangeburg Massacre.

name: Paul Roche
headline: Paul Roche, Poet in Bloomsbury Group, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Paul Roche was a noted English poet and translator who was among the last living associates of the Bloomsbury group, the skein of artists and writers twined around Virginia Woolf and her family.

name: William O’Neill
headline: William O’Neill, a Connecticut Governor, Is Dead at 77
abstract: William Atchison O’Neill was the son of a small-town tavern owner who rose through Connecticut politics to serve as governor for a decade.

name: William L. O’Neill
headline: William L. O’Neill, a Historian Who Wrote About Radicals, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. O’Neill, a professor at Rutgers until 2006, was the author of books about Stalinism, World War II, the 1960s and the activist Max Eastman.

name: Vladimir Kryuchkov
headline: Vladimir Kryuchkov, Ex-Chief of K.G.B., Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Kryuchkov helped to spearhead a coup against Mikhail S. Gorbachev in 1991 that collapsed after only three days.

name: Kevin DuBrow
headline: Kevin DuBrow, the Leader of Quiet Riot, Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. DuBrow was the gravelly voiced singer for heavy-metal band Quiet Riot, captivated fans with high-intensity musicality, quirky theatricality and a hint of menace.

name: Mel Tolkin
profession: Lead Writer for Show of Shows
headline: Mel Tolkin, Lead Writer for ‘Show of Shows,’ Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Tolkin, the long-suffering head of Sid Caesar’s celebrated television writing team, was present from the cramped, sweaty, malodorous beginning.

name: Frank Guarrera
headline: Frank Guarrera, 83, Lyric Baritone at the Met, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Guarrera, a lyric baritone who sang at the Metropolitan Opera for nearly 30 years, was known for his slender but firm voice and winning stage presence.

name: J. Robert Cade
headline: J. Robert Cade, the Inventor of Gatorade, Dies at 80
abstract: Dr. Cade  mixed water, sugar, salt and cunning dashes of whatever to invent Gatorade, which is now guzzled daily by electrolyte-depleted athletes, post-operative patients and the simply thirsty.

name: Bill Hartack
headline: Bill Hartack, 74, Champion Jockey, Dies
abstract: Bill Hartack was a Hall of Fame jockey who was a five-time winner of the Kentucky Derby.

name: Elaine Lorillard
profession: Founder of the Newport Jazz Festival
headline: Elaine Lorillard, 93, a Founder of the Newport Jazz Festival, Is Dead
abstract: Mrs. Lorillard with her husband, Louis, started the Newport Jazz Festival and created the model for what became a worldwide circuit of outdoor jazz festivals.

name: Herb McKenley
headline: Herb McKenley, 85, Top Jamaican Runner, Is Dead
abstract: Herb McKenley was the world’s fastest 400-meter runner more than half a century ago and later the driving force in Jamaica’s climb to track and field glory.

name: Bill Willis
headline: Bill Willis, 86, Racial Pioneer in Pro Football, Dies
abstract: Bill Willis was the Cleveland Browns’ Hall of Fame guard who played a major role in breaking pro football’s color barrier in the decade after World War II.

name: Gudrun Wagner
headline: Gudrun Wagner, of Bayreuth Festival, Dies at 63
abstract: Gudrun Wagner, who as the wife of Wolfgang Wagner, the director of the Bayreuth Festival, played a major behind-the-scenes role in guiding the event, the world’s pre-eminent Wagner opera festival.

name: Bobby Van
profession: Saloonkeeper and Pianist in the Hamptons
headline: Bobby Van, Saloonkeeper and Pianist in the Hamptons, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Van for nearly two decades presided over the Bridgehampton saloon that bore his name, an upscale oasis frequented by literary royalty like Truman Capote, Kurt Vonnegut and Joseph Heller.

name: Henry J. Hyde
profession: Power in the House of Representatives
headline: Henry J. Hyde, a Power in the House of Representatives, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Hyde won battles to prohibit federal financing of abortions and to impeach President Clinton but failed to persuade the Senate to convict and remove him from office.

name: Ralph Beard
profession: Kentucky Star Involved in Point-Shaving Scandal
headline: Ralph Beard, Kentucky Star Involved in Point-Shaving Scandal, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Beard propelled the University of Kentucky to two consecutive N.C.A.A. basketball championships before his career was shattered by involvement in a widespread collegiate point-shaving scandal.

name: Evel Knievel
headline: Evel Knievel, 69, Daredevil on a Motorcycle, Dies
abstract: Mr. Knievel was a hard-living, death-defying adventurer whose spectacular airborne stunts brought him worldwide fame as the quintessential daredevil performer.

name: Andrew Foldi
headline: Andrew Foldi, Opera Singer and Educator, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Foldi was a bass who sang character roles for decades at the Chicago Lyric Opera, the Metropolitan Opera and other houses and later directed the Chicago Lyric Opera Center for young artists.

name: Roger Smith
headline: Roger Smith, Former G.M. Chief, Dies
abstract: The executive who tried to modernize the automaker but instead became a scapegoat for its decline is dead at 82.

name: Roger Smith
profession: 77 Sunset Strip Actor and Manager of Ann-Margret
headline: Roger Smith, ‘77 Sunset Strip’ Actor and Manager of Ann-Margret, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Smith, who got his break after meeting James Cagney, played roles in films and on “Sunset Strip” before marrying Ann-Margret and developing her career.

name: Evan Jenkins
headline: Evan Jenkins, 72, Retired Editor at The Times, Dies
abstract: Mr. Jenkins was an authority on the linguistic bugbears that keep reporters, editors and many others awake at night.

name: Stephan Balint
headline: Stephan Balint, 64, a Founder of the Squat Theater, Dies
abstract: Mr. Balint, an underground Hungarian writer, actor and director, gained fame in New York with the above-ground Squat Theater in the late 1970s and ’80s.

name: David Oppenheim
headline: David Oppenheim, 85, Dean of N.Y.U. Arts, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Oppenheim was a clarinetist and a producer of classical music records and television documentaries who became the main architect of the Tisch School of the Arts.

name: Lester Ziffren
profession: First to Report Start of Spanish Civil War
headline: Lester Ziffren, 101, First to Report Start of Spanish Civil War, Dies
abstract: Mr. Ziffren was a foreign correspondent for United Press in the 1930s whose coded message from Madrid signaled to the world the start of the Spanish Civil War.

name: Moses Weinstein
headline: Moses Weinstein, 95, Legislator and Judge, Dies
abstract: Mr. Weinstein, a Queens Democrat, served in the State Assembly and as a trial and appellate judge of the State Supreme Court.

name: Larry Wachtel
headline: Larry Wachtel, Market Analyst, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Mr. Wachtel was a stock market analyst whose humor and trademark Brooklyn accent kept radio listeners attuned to the ups and downs of the markets for more than three decades.

name: Elizabeth Hardwick
headline: Elizabeth Hardwick, Writer, Dies at 91
abstract: Elizabeth Hardwick was a critic, essayist, fiction writer and a co-founder of The New York Review of Books.

name: Jefferson DeBlanc
headline: Jefferson DeBlanc, Hero Pilot, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. DeBlanc was a World War II fighter pilot who was awarded the Medal of Honor for shooting down five Japanese planes on a single day while running out of fuel.

name: Cecil Payne
headline: Cecil Payne, Baritone Saxophonist Who Mastered Bebop, Dies
abstract: Mr. Payne, 84, was one of the first baritone saxophonists to master the intricacies of modern jazz.

name: Richard Nolte
headline: Richard Nolte, Three-Week Ambassador During Six-Day War, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Nolte was a Middle East expert whose tenure as American ambassador to Egypt lasted only three weeks in 1967 because of the turmoil of the Six-Day War.

name: J. Richard Steffy
headline: J. Richard Steffy Is Dead at 83; Made Shipwreck Analysis Scientific
abstract: Mr. Steffy cast his career as an electrical contractor aside when he was 48 to pursue his passion, studying shipwrecks, and became a leading expert in the field.

name: Paul Brach
headline: Paul Brach, 83, Painter and Teacher, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Brach was a New York painter and teacher who became the first dean of the School of Art at the California Institute of the Arts and a mentor to some of the brightest stars of the art world of the 1980s.

name: Pimp C
headline: Pimp C, Southern Hip-Hop Rapper, Dies at 33
abstract: Pimp C helped define Southern hip-hop with his group, UGK.

name: Carlos Valdés
headline: Carlos Valdés, a Conga King of Jazz, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Valdés, better known as Patato, was a giant of Latin jazz in Cuba and then for more than half a century in America.

name: Murray Klein
profession: Helped Build Zabars Into Food Destination
headline: Murray Klein, Who Helped Build Zabar’s Into Food Destination, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Klein helped transform Zabar’s from a typical Jewish delicatessen on the Upper West Side of Manhattan into a culinary and cultural landmark.

name: Chip Reese
headline: Chip Reese, High-Stakes Card Champion, Is Dead at 56
abstract: Mr. Reese’s mix of intellect, poise and nerve propelled him to renowned eminence among the minuscule club of humans who convene to wager millions on poker games.

name: Peter Davi
profession: Pioneer of Pushing Surfings Limits in Big Waves
headline: Peter Davi, 45, a Pioneer of Pushing Surfing’s Limits in Big Waves, Dies
abstract: Peter Davi, a renowned big-wave surfer from Monterey, Calif., died Tuesday while riding giant waves at a spot he had helped pioneer off Pebble Beach. He was 45.

name: Karlheinz Stockhausen
headline: Karlheinz Stockhausen, Influential Composer, Dies at 79
abstract: Karlheinz Stockhausen, a German composer, made operas to express his spiritual vision of the cosmos.

name: Seymour Benzer
headline: Seymour Benzer, Geneticist, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Seymour Benzer made scientific history by discovering that genes were structured like words.

name: Norval Morrisseau
headline: Norval Morrisseau, Native Canadian Artist, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Morrisseau, also known as Copper Thunderbird, was one of Canada’s most celebrated painters.

name: Alois Kracher Jr.
headline: Alois Kracher Jr., Austrian Winemaker and Advocate, Is Dead at 48
abstract: Mr. Kracher’s wines are coveted throughout the world, admired as much for their silky finesse and balance as for the intensity of their sweet, honeyed fruit flavors.

name: John Strugnell
headline: John Strugnell, Scholar Undone by His Slur, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Strugnell was a biblical scholar whose tenure as the chief editor of the Dead Sea Scrolls ended in controversy over anti-Semitic remarks he made.

name: Jane Rule
headline: Jane Rule, Canadian Novelist, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Rule was a prominent Canadian writer whose first novel, “Desert of the Heart,” is considered a landmark work of lesbian fiction.

name: Andrew Imbrie
headline: Andrew Imbrie, 86, Composer and Teacher, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Imbrie was a prolific composer and influential teacher best known for his harmonically rugged but appealingly lyrical 1976 opera, “Angle of Repose.”

name: Susan Williams-Ellis
headline: Susan Williams-Ellis, 89, Designer of Popular Ceramic Tableware, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Williams-Ellis was the eccentric designer of Botanic Garden, the widely popular ceramic tableware that made its debut in 1972.

name: H. Wiley Hitchcock
headline: H. Wiley Hitchcock, Who Edited Dictionary of Music, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Hitchcock was a leading scholar of American music and the founding director of the Institute for Studies in American Music at Brooklyn College.

name: Ion Fiscuteanu
profession: Star of Romanian Stage and Film
headline: Ion Fiscuteanu, a Star of Romanian Stage and Film, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Fiscuteanu was known to international audiences for his role in “The Death of Mr. Lazarescu.”

name: Roger M. King
headline: Roger M. King, 63, TV Syndicator, Dies
abstract: Mr. King helped make national stars of talents like Oprah Winfrey, Alex Trebek and Dr. Phil McGraw through King World productions, a company he co-founded.

name: Gene H. Golub
headline: Gene H. Golub, an Innovator in Early Computing, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Golub developed early techniques for using computers to solve scientific and engineering problems.

name: Danny Newman
headline: Danny Newman, 88, Musical Publicity Expert, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Newman was a longtime director of press and public relations at Lyric Opera of Chicago and an influential thinker on the art of selling classical music to the public.

name: Stanton Wheeler
headline: Stanton Wheeler, 77, a Yale Law Professor, Dies
abstract: Mr. Wheeler, a professor at Yale Law School made notable studies of white-collar crime, prison systems and the way judges think, but who was not a lawyer.

name: Michael Shaheen Jr.
headline: Michael Shaheen Jr., Top Justice Dept. Official, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Shaheen spent 22 years as head of the Justice Department’s internal investigations office, sometimes issuing rebukes of perceived ethical lapses by the nation’s highest officials.

name: David H. Shepard
headline: David H. Shepard, 84, Dies; Optical Reader Inventor
abstract: Mr. Shepard invented one of the first machines that could read, and then, to facilitate its interpreting of credit-card receipts, came up with the near-rectilinear font still used for the cards’ numbers.

name: David Shepard
headline: David Shepard, Film Preservationist, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Shepard restored countless discarded, hidden or forgotten works by Charlie Chaplin, Buster Keaton and other notables.

name: Thomas P. Whitney
headline: Thomas P. Whitney, Solzhenitsyn Translator, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Whitney was a former diplomat and writer on Russian affairs who was best known for translating the work of the dissident writer Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn into English.

name: Freddie Fields
headline: Freddie Fields, Hollywood Talent Agent, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Fields was one of Hollywood’s most influential talent agents in the 1960s and early ’70s.

name: Ike Turner
profession: Musician and Songwriter in Duo With Tina Turner
headline: Ike Turner, Musician and Songwriter in Duo With Tina Turner, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Turner was an R&B musician, songwriter, bandleader, producer, talent scout and the ex-husband of Tina Turner.

name: Ted Corbitt
headline: Ted Corbitt, a Pioneer in American Distance Running, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Corbitt began running as a child on his father’s cotton farm in South Carolina and virtually never stopped, becoming a pioneer of ultramarathon running in the United States.

name: Marit Allen
headline: Marit Allen, Costume Designer for Movies, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Allen designed costumes for film characters as varied as the frumpy cross-dresser in “Mrs. Doubtfire,” the cowboys of “Brokeback Mountain” and the purple stretch-panted creature in “Hulk.”

name: Henrietta Yurchenco
headline: Henrietta Yurchenco, Pioneer Folklorist, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Yurchenco’s quest to save living music from the past took her from the mountains of Guatemala and southern Mexico to a New York City radio station to the Jewish community of Morocco.

name: Frank O. Braynard
headline: Frank O. Braynard, Ship Maven, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Braynard was the organizer of Operation Sail, the historic 1976 gathering of tall ships in New York Harbor that heralded the start of the city’s recovery.

name: David Maybury-Lewis
headline: David Maybury-Lewis, Who Studied Native Tribes, Dies at 78
abstract: Dr. Maybury-Lewis’s studies of native tribes in Amazonia pushed him, as the learned visage of a popular series on PBS, to advocate for the preservation of other indigenous groups.

name: Robert Kulicke
headline: Robert Kulicke, 83, Artist and Frame Maker, Is Dead
abstract: Robert M. Kulicke was a painter, goldsmith, teacher, businessman and designer who changed the look of postwar art by modernizing frame design.

name: Hirotaka Ono
headline: Hirotaka Ono, Auto Executive, Is Dead at 52
abstract: Mr. Ono was a senior operating officer at the Suzuki Motor Corporation who was considered a possible successor to his father-in-law, Osamu Suzuki, as chairman.

name: Allan Bérubé
headline: Allan Bérubé Is Dead at 61; Historian of Gays in Military
abstract: Mr. Bérubé was a MacArthur Award-winning independent scholar whose history of gay men and lesbians in the military in World War II is widely considered the definitive book on the subject.

name: Diane Wood Middlebrook
headline: Diane Wood Middlebrook, Biographer, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. Middlebrook was a biographer, poet and critic known for her best-selling, controversial life of the poet Anne Sexton.

name: St.Clair Bourne
headline: St.Clair Bourne, Filmmaker, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Bourne was a documentary filmmaker who recorded American black culture and produced portraits of eminent African-Americans.

name: Floyd Red Crow Westerman
headline: Floyd Red Crow Westerman, 71, an Actor, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Westerman used his talents as an actor, singer and songwriter to advance the cause of Native American rights and become one of the more famous Indian faces.

name: Frank Morgan
headline: Frank Morgan, Master of Bebop Sax, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Morgan was a jazz saxophonist whose promising career was derailed by drug problems in the 1950s, but had a triumphant comeback 30 years later, which led to an unexpected taste of midlife stardom.

name: Joel Dorn
headline: Joel Dorn, Record Producer, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Dorn influenced the shape of pop music in the work of artists like Roberta Flack, Bette Midler and the Neville Brothers.

name: Laura Huxley
headline: Laura Huxley, Her Husband’s Biographer, Dies at 96
abstract: Laura Archera Huxley was a writer who was best known for her memoir of her years with her husband, Aldous Huxley.

name: Douglas Kneeland
profession: Former Reporter for The New York Times
headline: Douglas Kneeland, Former Reporter for The New York Times, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Kneeland covered some of the major stories of the 1960s and ’70s and later became a high-level editor at The Chicago Tribune.

name: Joseph Henderson
headline: Joseph Henderson, an Early Jung Disciple, Dies at 104
abstract: Dr. Henderson was an early practitioner of methods developed by Carl Jung to explore cultural influences on the unconscious mind.

name: Jack Zander
headline: Jack Zander, Animator of Early TV Commercials, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Zander was a master animator who 60 years ago was among the first to apply his art to a brand-new form of communication — the television commercial.

name: Bill Strauss
headline: Bill Strauss, Parodist of Public Figures, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Strauss was a founder of the singing satirical troupe Capitol Steps, whose response to any political disaster of the last quarter-century was to find out whether it rhymed with anything.

name: Jack Linkletter
headline: Jack Linkletter, Second-Generation TV Host, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Linkletter followed his father, Art Linkletter, into broadcasting, serving as the host of several television shows in the late 1950s and 1960s.

name: Mel Cheren
headline: Mel Cheren, 74, an Entrepreneur of Disco, Dies
abstract: Mr. Cheren was an innovative record executive who helped start the Paradise Garage, a cavernous focal point of the downtown Manhattan gay disco scene in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Frank Capra Jr.
headline: Frank Capra Jr., Movie and TV Producer, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Capra Jr., the son of the noted Hollywood director Frank Capra, never wanted to go into his father’s business but found in the end he could not resist its pull.

name: Alan Wagner
profession: First President of the Disney Channel
headline: Alan Wagner, 76, First President of the Disney Channel, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Wagner was a former CBS programming executive who became the first president of the Disney Channel.

name: Arabella Spencer-Churchill
headline: Arabella Spencer-Churchill Dies at 58; Rebel Broke Family Mold
abstract: Arabella Spencer-Churchill, a granddaughter of Britain’s wartime prime minister, co-founded the Glastonbury rock festival, which became known as Britain’s Woodstock.

name: Sylvan Fox
headline: Sylvan Fox, 79, Pulitzer Prize-Winning Journalist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Fox was the first rewrite man in the history of journalism to be awarded the Pulitzer Prize.

name: Tatsuzo Shimaoka
headline: Tatsuzo Shimaoka, 88, Master of Pottery, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Shimaoka was designated a “living national treasure” in Japan for his mastery of his craft.

name: Tommy Byrne
headline: Tommy Byrne, 87, a Former Yankee Pitcher, Dies
abstract: Tommy Byrne was the longtime Yankees left-hander who was named the American League’s comeback player of the year in 1955.

name: Michael Tetherow
headline: Michael Tetherow, 65, Abstract Symbolist Artist, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Tetherow, a New York-based painter, placed great emphasis on the physical nature of paint and painting.

name: Oscar Peterson
headline: Oscar Peterson, 82, Jazz’s Piano Virtuoso, Dies
abstract: Oscar Peterson’s dazzling piano playing made him one of the most popular jazz artists in history.

name: Michael Kidd
headline: Michael Kidd, Choreographer, Dies
abstract: Michael Kidd was an award-winning choreographer of exuberant dance numbers for Broadway and Hollywood.

name: Douglas Morgan
headline: Douglas Morgan, a Collector of Typefaces, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Morgan was a publisher whose extensive collection of rare 19th-century wood type letterforms helped start a graphic design revival.

name: John A. Garraty
headline: John A. Garraty, Historian and Trailblazing Biographer, Dies at 87
abstract: Professor Garraty wrestled into print the American National Biography, which in 20 million words tells the story of the United States through the life histories of thousands of citizens.

name: Stephen Radich
headline: Stephen Radich, Owner of Controversial Art Gallery, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Radich was a New York art gallery owner who became embroiled in a famous legal case involving flag desecration in the late 1960s.

name: Harold J. Leavitt
headline: Harold J. Leavitt, 85, Management Expert, Dies
abstract: Mr. Leavitt was a longtime business professor who advocated a more democratic approach to organizational decision-making.

name: G. P. Sippy
headline: G. P. Sippy, Indian Filmmaker Whose ‘Sholay’ Was a Bollywood Hit, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Sippy was an Indian filmmaker whose 1975 blockbuster “Sholay” (“Embers”) remains the most famous Hindi movie and the biggest commercial success for Bollywood.

name: Thomas Morgan
headline: Thomas Morgan, a Journalist and Activist, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Morgan was a former reporter and editor at The New York Times who was a president of the National Association of Black Journalists.

name: Thomas B. Morgan
headline: Thomas B. Morgan, Writer, Editor and Lindsay Press Aide, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Morgan combined writing and a passion for public affairs to shape a career that also included top roles at The Village Voice and in public radio.

name: Benazir Bhutto
profession: Weathered Pakistans Political Storm for 3 Decades
headline: Benazir Bhutto, 54, Who Weathered Pakistan’s Political Storm for 3 Decades, Dies
abstract: Ms. Bhutto was the first woman democratically elected to lead a modern Muslim country.

name: Steven T. Florio
headline: Steven T. Florio, Executive Who Expanded Condé Nast, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Florio led Condé Nast during a period of great change in the magazine industry, with many companies downsizing because of the growth of the Internet.

name: Herman Rose
headline: Herman Rose, 98, Painter of Cityscapes, Is Dead
abstract: At a time when big-scale abstraction was ascendant, Mr. Rose painted small, airy, light-filled views of skies and rooftops in an Impressionistic manner.

name: James DeAngelis
headline: James DeAngelis, Last of Yale’s Ironmen, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. DeAngelis was the son of immigrants who became a Yale football celebrity and who was the last survivor of its famed 1934 lineup of “Ironmen.”

name: G. D. Warrington
headline: G. D. Warrington, 55, Transit Executive, Dies
abstract: Mr. Warrington ushered in the Acela high-speed service when he headed Amtrak and double-decker cars when he was chief executive of New Jersey Transit.

name: Hugh Massingberd
headline: Hugh Massingberd, 60, Laureate for the Departed, Dies
abstract: Mr. Massingberd was a celebrated former obituaries editor of The Daily Telegraph of London who made a once-dreary page required reading by speaking often gleefully ill of the dead.

name: Marvin Wachman
headline: Marvin Wachman, 90, Leader of Four Colleges, Dies
abstract: Dr. Wachman was president of Lincoln and Temple Universities and interim president of two other Pennsylvania colleges.

name: Philip B. Dusenberry
headline: Philip B. Dusenberry, 71, Adman, Dies
abstract: Mr. Dusenberry oversaw the 1980s Pepsi commercial in which Michael Jackson’s hair was accidentally set on fire.

name: Victor Navarra
headline: Victor Navarra Dies at 55; Directed Marathon Start
abstract: Mr. Navarra was a retired New York Fire Department lieutenant who coordinated the starts of the last 26 New York City Marathons.

name: Edward Brennan
headline: Edward Brennan, Who Led Sears at Its Peak, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Brennan became chief executive at Sears in 1986, when the company was the nation’s largest retailer.

name: Ettore Sottsass
headline: Ettore Sottsass, Designer, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Sottsass, an éminence grise of postmodern design, was responsible for the familiar bright red plastic Olivetti typewriter.

name: Louis Wolfson
profession: Central to the Fall of a Justice
headline: Louis Wolfson, Central to the Fall of a Justice, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Mr. Wolfson, a self-made industrialist who achieved a cliffhanging sweep of the Triple Crown as a thoroughbred owner, had legal troubles that were key to the resignation of Justice Abe Fortas of the Supreme Court in 1969.

name: Leonard B. Meyer
headline: Leonard B. Meyer, Scholar of Music’s Meaning, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Meyer was a pioneering musicologist whose 1956 book, “Emotion and Meaning in Music,” remains one of the most significant scholarly works in the field of music cognition.

name: Ruth Wallis
headline: Ruth Wallis,  Singer-Writer of Risqué Songs, Dies at 87
abstract: Ruth Wallis was a cabaret singer of the 1940s, ’50s and ’60s who was known as the Queen of the Party Song for the genteelly risqué.

name: Marie-Jeanne
headline: Marie-Jeanne, a Balanchine Ballerina, Dies at 87
abstract: Marie-Jeanne was an American ballerina long associated with George Balanchine and a member of the New York City Ballet during its first season.

name: George MacDonald Fraser
headline: George MacDonald Fraser, Author of Flashman Novels, Dies at 82
abstract: George MacDonald Fraser’s popular novels about the arch-rogue Harry Flashman followed their hero as he swashbuckled, drank and womanized his way through signal events of the 19th century.

name: Bill Bonanno
headline: Bill Bonanno, 75, Mob Family Member, Dies
abstract: Mr. Bonanno’s appointment by his father to the second most powerful position in the Bonanno crime family in the mid-1960s touched off what became known as the “Banana Wars.”

name: Michael Goldberg
headline: Michael Goldberg, 83, Abstract Expressionist, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Goldberg was an abstract painter of the New York School whose vibrant works are in major museums and private collections.

name: Michael H. Goldberg
headline: Michael H. Goldberg, 73, Lawyer Who Bridged A.B.A. and N.B.A., Dies
abstract: Goldberg served as general counsel for the American Basketball Association during its final years and headed the N.B.A.’s coaches’ union for almost four decades.

name: Gerald Astor
headline: Gerald Astor, 81, Writer on Americans in Combat, Dies
abstract: Through interviews and correspondence with veterans and accounts from their journals, Mr. Astor told of combat as experienced by foot soldiers, sailors and pilots.

name: Bert Bolin
headline: Bert Bolin, 82, Is Dead; Led U.N. Climate Panel
abstract: Bert Bolin was a pioneering climatologist and the first chairman of the United Nations Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change.

name: James Costigan
headline: James Costigan, Writer of Prestige TV, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Costigan was an Emmy-winning writer who worked with some of the leading actors of the postwar years.

name: Glenn W. Ferguson
headline: Glenn W. Ferguson, Former Ambassador to Kenya, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Ferguson served as the president or chancellor of three universities and, for a brief time in the 1980s, the president of Lincoln Center.

name: Liam O’Gallagher
headline: Liam O’Gallagher, 90, a Beat Avant-Gardist and Teacher, Dies
abstract: Mr. O’Gallagher was an avant-garde sound artist, painter and teacher whose San Francisco studio became an early gathering place for Beat writers and poets in the 1950s.

name: Kinkri Devi
headline: Kinkri Devi Is Dead at 82; Fought Illegal Mining in India
abstract: Kinkri Devi was a poor, illiterate woman who waged a long fight against illegal mining and quarrying in the mountainous northern Indian state of Himachal Pradesh.

name: Alberto Alonso
headline: Alberto Alonso, Founder of Cuban Troupe, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Alonso was a Cuban-born dancer, ballet master and choreographer who received political asylum in the United States in 1993.

name: P. K. Sethi
headline: P. K. Sethi, Inventor of the Low-Tech Limb, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Dr. P. K. Sethi invented the affordable prosthesis called the Jaipur foot, which has helped millions of amputees in developing countries to lead normal lives.

name: Gilbert Harrison
headline: Gilbert Harrison, 92, Ex-Editor, Dies
abstract: Mr. Harrison was the owner and editor of The New Republic, an influential though rarely profitable publication, from 1953 to 1974.

name: Jean-Claude Vrinat
headline: Jean-Claude Vrinat, Owner of Famed Paris Restaurant, Is Dead at 71
abstract: For more than three decades, Mr. Vrinat was the owner of the Taillevent restaurant in Paris, which is regarded by many as the pinnacle of elegance in French cuisine.

name: Ernestine Stodelle
headline: Ernestine Stodelle, 95, Modern Dancer, Dies
abstract: Ms. Stodelle had a multifaceted career in modern dance as a performer, author and teacher.

name: Paul MacLean
headline: Paul MacLean, 94, Neuroscientist Who Devised ‘Triune Brain’ Theory, Dies
abstract: Dr. MacLean developed an intriguing theory to explain the brain’s evolution and to try to reconcile rational human behavior with its more violent side.

name: Edmund Hillary
headline: Edmund Hillary, First on Everest, Dies at 88
abstract: Sir Edmund Hillary was the mountaineer who, with Tenzing Norgay, his Sherpa guide, was the first to scale the 29,035-foot summit of Mount Everest.

name: Ken Nelson
headline: Ken Nelson, Record Producer Behind Bakersfield Sound, Dies at 96
abstract: Ken Nelson was the record producer behind the twangy Bakersfield Sound made popular by Buck Owens and Merle Haggard.

name: Philip Agee
headline: Philip Agee, 72, Is Dead; Exposed Other C.I.A. Officers
abstract: Philip Agee was a former Central Intelligence Agency officer who turned against the agency and spent years exposing undercover American spies overseas.

name: Vincent Gruppuso
headline: Vincent Gruppuso, 67, Seller of Pudding Snacks, Dies
abstract: Mr. Gruppuso was the founder of Kozy Shack Enterprises, a company in Hicksville, Long Island, that sells millions of four-ounce cups of pudding, particularly rice pudding.

name: Buddy LeRoux
headline: Buddy LeRoux, 77, Boston Sports Fixture, Is Dead
abstract: Edward “Buddy” LeRoux was a former trainer for the Boston Red Sox who rose to become a controversial part owner of the team while amassing a fortune in real estate.

name: Herbert Keppler
profession: Covered Photo Gadgetry With Folksy Style
headline: Herbert Keppler, 82, Dies; Covered Photo Gadgetry With Folksy Style
abstract: Mr. Keppler was a publisher and columnist at leading photographic magazines who advised amateur photographers on everything from lenses and shutter speeds.

name: Charles M. Taylor
headline: Charles M. Taylor, 78, Atlanta Real Estate Developer, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Taylor’s projects helped shape skylines in several Southern metropolitan areas.

name: Irene Reid
headline: Irene Reid, Singer, Bandleader and Actress, Dies at 77
abstract: Irene Reid was a singer who toured and recorded with Count Basie’s band and appeared on Broadway in “The Wiz.”

name: Christopher Bowman
headline: Christopher Bowman, Skating Champion, Is Dead at 40
abstract: Mr. Bowman was a former U.S. figure skating champion dubbed “Bowman the Showman” for his flair on the ice.

name: W. F. Ganong
profession: Expert in Brains Control of Body
headline: W. F. Ganong, 83, Expert in Brain’s Control of Body, Dies
abstract: Mr. Ganong was one of the first scientists to trace how the brain controls important internal functions of the body.

name: Boris Lurie
profession: Leader of a Confrontational Art Movement
headline: Boris Lurie, Leader of a Confrontational Art Movement, Dies at 83
abstract: Boris Lurie was a Russian-born artist who survived the Holocaust and then depicted its horrors while leading a confrontational movement called No! Art.

name: Jack Brod
headline: Jack Brod, Early Tenant of Skyscraper, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Brod was a businessman who over nearly eight decades gradually worked his way from the 7th floor of the Empire State Building to the 76th, where he reigned as the skyscraper’s last original tenant.

name: Allison Eckardt Ledes
headline: Allison Eckardt Ledes, 53, Editor of Magazine Antiques, Is Dead
abstract: As editor of The Magazine Antiques, Ms. Ledes brought a new focus on European, Asian and 20th-century decorative arts to a publication traditionally devoted to Americana.

name: William J. McGuire
headline: William J. McGuire, 82, Art of Persuasion Pioneer, Dies
abstract: Mr. McGuire was a social psychologist at Yale whose work on the art of persuasion and how to resist it has been applied in political science, advertising and mass communications.

name: Herbert J.C. Kouts
headline: Herbert J.C. Kouts, Nuclear Power Safety Expert, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Dr. Kouts was a pioneer in nuclear power safety research and an expert in weapons proliferation.

name: Johnny Podres
headline: Johnny Podres, Series Star, Dies at 75
abstract: Podres became a celebrated figure in the storied history of the Brooklyn Dodgers in October 1955, when he pitched them to their only World Series championship.

name: Walter Bowart
headline: Walter Bowart, Alternative Journalist, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Bowart was a founder and the first publisher of The East Village Other, a New York newspaper so countercultural that it made The Village Voice look like a church circular.

name: Caroline K. Keck
headline: Caroline K. Keck, Art Conservator, Dies at 99
abstract: Ms.  Keck was instrumental in converting the centuries-old craft of art restoration into a profession based on scientific research.

name: Norman Morrice
headline: Norman Morrice, Director of Royal Ballet, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Morrice shook up traditional British dance sensibilities by championing modern-dance choreographers and mentoring young talent.

name: Don Cardwell
headline: Don Cardwell, 72, Pitcher for 1969 Mets, Is Dead
abstract: Don Cardwell was a right-handed pitcher who helped propel the Mets to their stunning 1969 World Series championship as he neared the end of a long career.

name: Judah Folkman
headline: Judah Folkman, Researcher, Dies at 74
abstract: Dr. Folkman championed the idea that cancer needs a growing network of blood vessels to survive and that blocking that process, called angiogenesis, would stop or even eliminate tumors.

name: Brad Renfro
headline: Brad Renfro, Who Portrayed Witness in ‘The Client,’ Dies at 25
abstract: Brad Renfro was a former child star who played a witness to a mob lawyer’s suicide in the 1994 legal thriller “The Client” and a suburban youth tutored in evil by an elderly Nazi war criminal in the 1998 film “Apt Pupil”.

name: Dusty Cohl
headline: Dusty Cohl, a Toronto Film Festival Founder, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Cohl and two other friends, Henk van der Kolk and Bill Marshall, started what was first called the Festival of Festivals in 1976.

name: Milton Wolff
headline: Milton Wolff, 92, Dies; Anti-Franco Leader
abstract: Mr. Wolff was the last commander of the American volunteers who fought against Franco in the Spanish Civil War.

name: Pete Candoli
headline: Pete Candoli, Jazz Trumpeter, Dies at 84
abstract: Pete Candoli was a jazz trumpeter who made his mark as a high-note specialist in the big-band era and went on to become one of the busiest studio musicians in Hollywood.

name: Clyde Otis
headline: Clyde Otis, 83, Executive and Songwriter, Dies
abstract: Mr. Otis, a songwriter and record producer, was one of the first black executives at a major record company.

name: Richard Knerr
headline: Richard Knerr, 82, Craze Creator, Dies
abstract: Mr. Knerr produced products that for two decades virtually defined frivolity in postwar America, from the Hula Hoop to the Frisbee to the SuperBall.

name: Bobby Fischer
headline: Bobby Fischer, Troubled Genius of Chess, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Fischer, one of the greatest chess players the world has ever seen, later lived under self-imposed exile.

name: Georgia Frontiere
headline: Georgia Frontiere, 80, First Female N.F.L. Owner, Is Dead
abstract: Georgia Frontiere was thrust into the pro football world in April 1979 when her husband, Carroll Rosenbloom, died, leaving her majority ownership of the Los Angeles Rams.

name: Anthony Solomon
headline: Anthony Solomon,  Finance Policy Maker, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Solomon was a former president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and an influential financial policy maker in three presidential administrations and at the World Bank.

name: Francis Childs
headline: Francis Childs, 68, Dies; Sage of High Corn Yields
abstract: Mr. Childs was a third-generation farmer who studied, schemed and tramped his fields with a spade to become the most productive corn grower ever.

name: Andy Palacio
headline: Andy Palacio, Who Saved Garifuna Music, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. Palacio was a bandleader and songwriter who spearheaded a revival of the Garifuna music of Central America.

name: Suzanne Pleshette
headline: Suzanne Pleshette, 70, ‘Newhart’ Actress, Dies
abstract: Suzanne Pleshette was the husky-voiced actress who redefined the television sitcom wife in the 1970s, playing the smart, sardonic Emily Hartley on “The Bob Newhart Show.”

name: Lois Nettleton
headline: Lois Nettleton, 80, Dies; Acted on Stage and TV
abstract: Ms. Nettleton’s dramatic and comic dexterity in theater, film and television earned her wide public recognition and deep professional respect for more than a half century.

name: Joe Burk
profession: Won Honors on Thames and in Pacific
headline: Joe Burk, 93, Won Honors on Thames and in Pacific, Is Dead
abstract: Joe Burk was a single sculls champion of the 1930s who became a leading figure in American rowing and a highly decorated PT boat skipper in World War II.

name: Lew Spence
headline: Lew Spence, a Songwriter for Sinatra, Dies at 87
abstract: His best-known song was “Nice ’n’ Easy,” the title tune of a Frank Sinatra album and later a staple of Sinatra’s repertory.

name: Albert Bowker
headline: Albert Bowker, 88, Dies; Ex-CUNY Head
abstract: Mr. Bowker, the outspoken head of the City University of New York, stunned the campus and ruffled the city’s self-esteem in 1971 when he left.

name: Terrence Elkes
headline: Terrence Elkes, 73, President of Viacom in ’80s, Dies
