abstract: Mr. Elkes rose to become president of Viacom and oversaw some major acquisitions, which began the transformation of Viacom into a major entertainment company.

name: Heath Ledger
headline: Heath Ledger, Actor, Is Found Dead at 28
abstract: The Australian-born actor was found in a New York apartment with sleeping pills nearby, the police said.

name: Edward D. Hoch
headline: Edward D. Hoch, Writer of Over 900 Mystery Stories, Is Dead at 77
abstract: For the last 35 years, Mr. Hoch was a fixture of Ellery Queen’s Mystery Magazine, which published a story of his every month from 1973 until his death.

name: Miles Lerman
headline: Miles Lerman, a Leading Force Behind Holocaust Museum, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Lerman, a Jewish resistance fighter in Nazi-occupied Poland, persuaded Soviet bloc countries to give the museum thousands of artifacts of the Holocaust.

name: Bill Hart
headline: Bill Hart, Theater Director, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Mr. Hart worked closely with Sam Shepard and other downtown theater artists like Joseph Chaikin and Nicky Paraiso.

name: Evan Galbraith
headline: Evan Galbraith, Ambassador, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Galbraith was a former ambassador to France and a Republican contender for governor of New York in 1994.

name: Philip Conisbee
headline: Philip Conisbee, 62, National Gallery Curator, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Conisbee organized some of the museum’s most popular exhibitions, such as “Cézanne in Provence.”

name: Richard G. Darman
headline: Richard G. Darman, 64, Aide for 5 Presidents, Dies
abstract: Mr. Darman guided policy and deal making in four Republican administrations, including the reversal of the first President Bush’s campaign pledge not to raise taxes.

name: Alton G. Marshall
headline: Alton G. Marshall, 86, Nelson Rockefeller’s Top Aide, Is Dead
abstract: Among the major initiatives in which Mr. Marshall was directly involved were the formation of the state university system, the development of Battery Park City and the expansion of the state park system.

name: H. Bradford Westerfield
headline: H. Bradford Westerfield, Influential Yale Professor, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Dr. Westerfield was a Yale political scientist whose courses attracted 10,000 students, mostly undergraduates, among them President Bush and Vice President Dick Cheney.

name: George Habash
headline: George Habash, Palestinian Terrorism Tactician, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Habash was the founder of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine, a hard-line Marxist group that shocked the world with a campaign of airline hijackings and bombings in the late 1960s and early 1970s.

name: Michael Abbott
headline: Michael Abbott, Producer,  Is Dead at 81
abstract: Michael Abbott was a television, film and theater producer who was bringing a revival of “Stalag 17” to Broadway 57 years after producing its premiere Off Broadway.

name: Gordon B. Hinckley
headline: Gordon B. Hinckley, Mormon Leader, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Gordon B. Hinckley, the president and prophet of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, led Mormonism through a period of global expansion.

name: Suharto
profession: Indonesian Dictator Brought Order and Bloodshed
headline: Suharto Dies at 86; Indonesian Dictator Brought Order and Bloodshed
abstract: Suharto’s 32-year dictatorship was one of the most brutal and corrupt of the 20th century.

name: Margaret Truman Daniel
headline: Margaret Truman Daniel Dies at 83
abstract: Mrs. Daniel’s achievements as a singer, TV host, and author won her renown in her own right.

name: Christodoulos
headline: Greek Orthodox Leader Dies at 69
abstract: Archbishop Christodoulos, who helped heal centuries-old grievances with the Roman Catholic Church but also but stirred controversy, was 69.

name: Zhang Hanzhi
headline: Zhang Hanzhi, Mao’s English Tutor, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Zhang was a former Chinese diplomat who once served as Mao’s English tutor and also interpreted for President Nixon during his trip to China in 1972.

name: Charles F. Luce
headline: Charles F. Luce, Ex-Chief of Con Ed, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Luce headed Con Ed from 1967 to 1982, dealing with the oil crisis of the 1970s and New York City’s 1977 blackout.

name: Thomas Barr
headline: Thomas Barr, Top Lawyer in I.B.M. Case, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Barr was best known for representing the International Business Machines Corporation in a 13-year antitrust battle with the federal government.

name: David Bradley
profession: Author, Antinuclear Advocate, Champion Skier and State Legislator
headline: David Bradley, 92, Author, Antinuclear Advocate, Champion Skier and State Legislator, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Bradley’s best-selling first book, “No Place to Hide,” was an eyewitness account of the postwar atomic tests on Bikini Atoll in the South Pacific.

name: Henry Froehlich
headline: Henry Froehlich, Pioneer in Japanese Camera Imports, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Froehlich was one of the first distributors of high-tech Japanese cameras in the United States.

name: Jimmy James
headline: Jimmy James, P.O.W. Plotter of Escapes, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. James was a British flier in World War II obsessed with escape plots during his five years in German captivity, most prominently the breakout portrayed in the movie “The Great Escape.”

name: Arthur B. Kramer
profession: Lawyer and Brother of Playwright Larry Kramer
headline: Arthur B. Kramer, Lawyer and Brother of Playwright Larry Kramer, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Kramer built a small New York law firm, intended as an alternative to the city’s white-shoe firms, into one with international reach.

name: Peter Staudhammer
headline: Peter Staudhammer, Who Designed NASA Instruments, Dies at 73
abstract: Peter Staudhammer, a wide-ranging aerospace engineer and executive, helped design instruments and engines used by NASA in landings on Mars and the Moon.

name: Robert M. Ball
headline: Robert M. Ball Is Dead at 93; Led Social Security
abstract: Mr. Ball was the commissioner of Social Security in the Kennedy, Johnson and Nixon administrations and an opponent of privatizing it.

name: Marcial Maciel
headline: The Rev. Marcial Maciel, 87, Conservative Catholic Leader, Dies
abstract: Father Maciel founded the influential Roman Catholic group the Legionaries of Christ and was the most prominent priest disciplined after accusations of sexual abuse.

name: Jens Quistgaard
headline: Jens Quistgaard, 88, a Designer of Popular Tableware, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Quistgaard’s clean-lined, popular pieces for the Dansk brand of tableware helped define the Scandinavian Modern style for postwar Americans.

name: Viktor Schreckengost
headline: Viktor Schreckengost, Master of Product Design, Dies at 101
abstract: Viktor Schreckengost was a distinguished yet largely unsung industrial designer who spent most of the 20th century quietly infusing every corner of the United States with his work.

name: Albert Landa
headline: Albert Landa Dies at 80; Helped the New School Develop
abstract: Albert W. Landa was a public relations executive who went far beyond that role in helping to develop the New School in Manhattan into a full-scale university.

name: Earl L. Butz
headline: Earl L. Butz, Secretary Felled by Racial Remark, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Mr. Butz, a secretary of agriculture under Presidents Nixon and Ford, resigned during the 1976 presidential election race over a vulgar racial comment.

name: Joshua Lederberg
headline: Joshua Lederberg, 82, a Nobel Winner, Dies
abstract: Dr. Lederberg was one of the 20th century’s leading scientists, whose work in bacterial genetics had vast medical implications and led to his receiving a Nobel Prize.

name: Barry Morse
profession: Played the Dogged Detective in The Fugitive
headline: Barry Morse, Who Played the Dogged Detective in ‘The Fugitive,’ Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Morse was famous for his portrayal of the cold-hearted detective who relentlessly pursues the wrongly convicted Richard Kimble in “The Fugitive,” one of the biggest TV hits of the 1960s.

name: LaVaughn Robinson
headline: LaVaughn Robinson, Tap Virtuoso and Teacher, Dies at 80
abstract: LaVaughn Robinson was a tap-dance virtuoso on the big-band circuit in the 1940s and ’50s who became a master teacher and a major force in tap’s revival.

name: Ernesto Illy
headline: Ernesto Illy, Chairman of Coffee Company, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Illy, who as chairman of Illycaffè, maker of an expensive brand of coffee, was renowned as a scientific perfectionist of coffee and as an evangelist of espresso.

name: Maharishi Mahesh Yogi
headline: Maharishi Mahesh Yogi, Spiritual Leader, Dies
abstract: Maharishi Mahesh Yogi introduced transcendental meditation to the West and gained fame in the 1960s as the spiritual guru to the Beatles.

name: Ruth Stafford Peale
headline: Ruth Stafford Peale, 101, Dies; Helped Ministry Flourish
abstract: Mrs. Peale and her husband, the Rev. Dr. Norman Vincent Peale, built one of the 20th century’s most influential ministries.

name: Abraham Brumberg
headline: Abraham Brumberg, Writer on Eastern Europe, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Brumberg came to wide public attention in the early 1950s as the first editor of the journal Problems of Communism, a respected scholarly cold-war-era forum.

name: Tata Güines
headline: Tata Güines, 77, Cuban Master of the Congas, Is Dead
abstract: Known for drawing a great range of sounds from his drums, with his fingernails as well as his hands, Tata Güines was highly imitated, one of the best conga drum soloists of his time.

name: James J. Fuld
headline: James J. Fuld, Collector of Rare Music Scores, Dies at 91
abstract: James J. Fuld was a New York lawyer whose love of music inspired him to assemble one of the world’s finest collections of first editions of musical scores.

name: Floyd M. Boring
headline: Floyd M. Boring, Agent Who Guarded 5 Presidents, Is Dead at 92
abstract: During his service, Mr. Boring took part in the gunfight with Puerto Rican nationalists who tried to assassinate President Harry S. Truman in November 1950.

name: E. Leroy Tolles
headline: E. Leroy Tolles, Law Firm Founder, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Tolles was a co-founder of the Los Angeles law firm of Munger, Tolles & Olson, which grew from seven lawyers into a nationally prominent firm with about 200 lawyers.

name: Mary Allen Engle
headline: Mary Allen Engle, Pediatric Cardiologist, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Engle began an international philanthropic exchange that brought needy children to Manhattan for heart treatments in the 1970s.

name: Karl Ehrhardt
profession: Sign Man and Shea Stadium Fixture
headline: Karl Ehrhardt, 83, Sign Man and Shea Stadium Fixture, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Ehrhardt always let the Mets know what he thought of them by raising block-lettered signs from his box seat behind third base at Shea Stadium.

name: Chris Anderson
headline: Chris Anderson, 81, Influential Jazz Pianist, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Anderson’s sophisticated and personal approach to harmony made him a pronounced influence on many other players, notably Herbie Hancock.

name: Phyllis A. Whitney
headline: Phyllis A. Whitney, Author, Dies at 104
abstract: Ms. Whitney was a prolific best-selling author of romantic mysteries, young-adult novels and children’s mysteries for more than a half-century.

name: John Myers
headline: John Myers, 96, World War II Test Pilot, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Myers was a leading civilian test pilot in World War II who helped develop the first American fighter plane designed specifically for night combat.

name: Dan H. Laurence
profession: Bibliographer and George Bernard Shaw Scholar
headline: Dan H. Laurence, 87, Bibliographer and George Bernard Shaw Scholar, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Laurence was a noted scholar, editor and bibliographer who devoted nearly every waking moment of his professional life to compiling the voluminous works of George Bernard Shaw.

name: John Alvin
headline: John Alvin, Designer of Memorable Film Posters, Is Dead at 59
abstract: Mr. Alvin created memorable images for movie posters, billboards and advertisements, including the two fingers touching above the Earth’s surface for “E.T.: The Extra-Terrestrial.”

name: Roy Scheider
headline: Roy Scheider, Actor in ‘Jaws,’ Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Scheider was a stage actor with a background in the classics who became one of the leading figures in the American film renaissance of the 1970s.

name: Robert Jastrow
headline: Robert Jastrow, Who Made Space Understandable, Dies at 82
abstract: Dr. Jastrow led a major space science institution and helped to bring space down to earth for millions of Americans.

name: Tom Lantos
headline: Tom Lantos, 80, Is Dead; Longtime Congressman
abstract: Mr. Lantos, who represented a district in California, was chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee and the only Holocaust survivor ever to serve in Congress.

name: Frank J. Dixon
headline: Frank J. Dixon Dies at 87; Led Way in Immunology
abstract: Dr. Dixon’s penetrating studies of how misdirected responses by the immune system can cause diseases that damage the kidneys and other organs won him an Albert Lasker Award in 1975.

name: Kirk Browning
headline: Kirk Browning, 86, Dies; Put the Arts on TV
abstract: Mr. Browning’s unusual career path took him from chicken farmer to television director of “Live From Lincoln Center.”

name: Steve Gerber
headline: Steve Gerber, Creator of Howard the Duck, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Gerber created Howard the Duck, the dour, dyspeptic, utterly disagreeable and therefore wildly popular comic-book hero of the 1970s.

name: Kon Ichikawa
headline: Kon Ichikawa, Japanese Film Director, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Ichikawa’s versatility ranged beyond his well-known antiwar dramas like “The Burmese Harp” and “Fires on the Plain” to comedies, documentaries and literary adaptations.

name: David Groh
headline: David Groh of ‘Rhoda’ Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Groh played Joe, the groom whose wedding to the title character of the 1970s sitcom became one of the highest-rated events of its time.

name: William D. Modell
headline: William D. Modell, Seller of Sporting Goods, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Modell joined Modell’s Sporting Goods, a 118-year-old family-owned business, at the end of World War II and became chairman in 1985.

name: Frank Piasecki
headline: Frank Piasecki, a Pioneer in Helicopters, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Piasecki was the first to develop a tandem-rotor helicopter — the so-called Flying Banana — capable of carrying large cargo loads or troops into combat.

name: Steve Fossett
headline: Steve Fossett, Missing Adventurer, Is Declared Dead at 63
abstract: Mr. Fossett was a record-setting adventurer who blithely sailed, soared and drove through all manner of danger.

name: Baba Amte
headline: Baba Amte, 93, Dies; Advocate for Lepers
abstract: Mr. Amte, a follower of Gandhi, gave up an early life of privilege to work for the poor, his direction irrevocably determined by an encounter with a destitute leper.

name: John Brunious
headline: John Brunious, 67, Louisiana Trumpeter, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Brunious, , a jazz trumpeter, devoted his career to the music of his native New Orleans, leading the Preservation Hall Jazz Band for more than a dozen years.

name: Gardner Lindzey
profession: Former President of the American Psychological Association
headline: Gardner Lindzey, Former President of the American Psychological Association, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Dr. Lindzey, a psychologist, editor and former president of the American Psychological Association, built a national framework to encourage scholarly exchanges in the social sciences.

name: Peter Newton
headline: Peter Newton, Napa Vintner, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Newton was a noted California vintner whose two wineries, Sterling Vineyards and Newton Vineyard, produced some of Napa Valley’s most highly regarded wines.

name: Jamie Davies
headline: Jamie Davies Is Dead at 73; Made Sparkling Wine
abstract: With her husband, Ms. Davies founded Schramsberg Vineyards and pioneered the production of fine sparkling wine in California.

name: David Oats
headline: David Oats, Park Advocate, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Oats was president of the Flushing Meadows-Corona Park World’s Fair Association, a civic group he started in 1967.

name: Dorothy Podber
headline: Dorothy Podber, 75, Artist and Trickster, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Podber was a wild child of the New York Art scene who is probably best known for shooting a stack of Andy Warhol’s paintings with a pistol.

name: Thomas T. Roberts
headline: Thomas T. Roberts Dies at 84; Ruled That Baseball Owners Engaged in Collusion
abstract: Mr. Roberts was a prominent arbitrator best known for his ruling that major league baseball owners had improperly colluded to prevent free-agent players from obtaining richer contracts.

name: Thomas Roberts
profession: Led Fight to Save Fire Island Lighthouse
headline: Thomas Roberts, Who Led Fight to Save Fire Island Lighthouse, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Roberts’s efforts to save the lighthouse in the early 1980s became a model for scores of lighthouse preservation campaigns.

name: Morton J. Savada
headline: Morton J. Savada, 85, Seller of 78-R.P.M. Records, Dies
abstract: For more than 30 years Mr. Savada’s second-floor store in Manhattan, Records Revisited, was a haven for die-hard record collectors.

name: Natalia Bessmertnova
headline: Natalia Bessmertnova, Ballerina of Innate Lyricism, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Bessmertnova was a ballerina with the Bolshoi Ballet known for her lightness, delicacy and Romantic style.

name: Walter J. Burghardt
headline: Walter J. Burghardt, Social Justice Advocate, Dies at 93
abstract: Father Burghardt was a Jesuit priest widely known for emphasizing social justice in the many books he wrote and the seminars he gave on the history and art of preaching.

name: Bob Howsam
headline: Bob Howsam, 89, Sports Executive, Dies
abstract: Mr. Howsam’s career as a sports executive spanned half a century. He founded the Denver Broncos and later built the Cincinnati Reds’ championship teams known as the Big Red Machine.

name: Samuel Karlin
headline: Samuel Karlin, Versatile Mathematician, Dies at 83
abstract: Dr. Karlin applied his theoretical brilliance to such far-flung areas as economics and population studies, before helping to find ways to analyze DNA swiftly and comprehensively.

name: Richard Westenburg
headline: Richard Westenburg, Choral Conductor, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Westenburg founded the Musica Sacra Chorus and Orchestra in 1964 and made it one of the most renowned choruses in New York by the end of the 1970s.

name: James E. Orange
headline: Rev. James E. Orange, 65, Aide to Dr. King, Dies
abstract: The Rev. Orange’s arrest in 1965 is considered one of the catalysts for the Selma-to-Montgomery civil rights march. Later he became a union organizer and an advocate for illegal immigrants.

name: Teo Macero
headline: Teo Macero, 82, Record Producer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Macero was most famous for his role in producing a series of albums by Miles Davis in the late 1960s and early 1970s.

name: Sidney Watters Jr.
headline: Sidney Watters Jr., 90, Trainer of Champion Racehorses, Is Dead
abstract: In his 60 years in racing, Mr. Watters proved a versatile figure. He rode steeplechase horses, then trained champions in steeplechase and flat racing.

name: Raymond Kennedy
headline: Raymond Kennedy, Novelist, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Kennedy was known for his dark, absurdist novels set largely in his native New England.

name: Orin Lehman
headline: Orin Lehman, 88, Parks Steward, Dies
abstract: Mr. Lehman turned to public service rather than a career in his family’s investment company becoming New York State’s longest-serving commissioner of Parks, Recreation and Historic Preservation.

name: Jonathan Maslow
headline: Jonathan Maslow, 59, a Journalist and Naturalist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Maslow wrote about the survival of rare, beautiful or otherwise beguiling animals in the wild, often in remote places.

name: Ernst Jaffé
headline: Ernst Jaffé, 83, Expert on Red Blood Cells, Dies
abstract: Dr. Jaffé was a groundbreaking hematologist who helped reveal the workings of a hereditary disorder that impairs red blood cells’ ability to transport oxygen.

name: Douglas A. Fraser
headline: Douglas A. Fraser, 91, Union Chief Who Helped Chrysler, Is Dead
abstract: As president of the United Automobile Workers union, Mr. Fraser agreed to concessions that helped the Chrysler Corporation avoid bankruptcy in the late 1970s.

name: Ray Wu
headline: Ray Wu, 79, a Genetic Transformer of Crops, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Wu was a biochemist and genetic engineer who helped lead research at Cornell University on genetically modifying crops to better withstand environmental stresses.

name: Stephen Marlowe
headline: Stephen Marlowe, 79, Detective Novelist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Marlowe was a prolific writer of popular fiction best known for his crime novels featuring the globe-trotting private eye Chester Drum.

name: Max Raab
headline: Max Raab, Maker of Fashion and Film, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Raab helped extend the button-down preppy look of the early 1960s to women’s clothing. He was also an executive producer of “A Clockwork Orange.”

name: Raymond Smith
profession: Founder and Editor of Literary Journal
headline: Raymond Smith, Founder and Editor of Literary Journal, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Smith was a founder and the longtime editor of The Ontario Review, a noted literary journal.

name: Dan Shomron
headline: Dan Shomron, Leader of Entebbe Airport Rescue, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Mr. Shomron was in command of the Israeli paratroopers in the 1976 hostage rescue at Entebbe International Airport in Uganda.

name: William F. Buckley Jr.
headline: William F. Buckley Jr. Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Buckley marshaled a refined, perspicacious mind to elevate conservatism to the center of American political discourse.

name: Buddy Miles
headline: Buddy Miles, 60, Hendrix Drummer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Miles played with a brisk, assertive, deeply funky attack that made him an apt partner for Jimi Hendrix.

name: W. C. Heinz
headline: W. C. Heinz, 93, Writing Craftsman, Dies
abstract: Mr. Heinz, a sports columnist, war correspondent, magazine writer and novelist, was considered one of the finest journalistic stylists of his era.

name: David Watkin
headline: David Watkin, 82, Cinematographer, Dies
abstract: Over a 50-year career, Mr. Watkin worked on more than 60 films and received the 1985 Academy Award for best cinematography for “Out of Africa.”

name: Myron Cope
headline: Myron Cope, 79, Writer and Steelers Broadcaster, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Cope was the radio color commentator for Steelers games from 1970 to 2004 and the host of radio and television sports shows in Pittsburgh.

name: Mike Smith
headline: Mike Smith, Lead Singer of Dave Clark 5, Is Dead
abstract: The Dave Clark Five, part of the so-called British Invasion of the early 1960s, recorded a string of hits including “Glad All Over” and “Catch Us If You Can.”

name: Barbara Seaman
headline: Barbara Seaman, 72, Dies; Cited Risks of the Pill
abstract: Ms. Seaman was one of the first people to bring the issue of women’s reproductive health to wide attention.

name: Boyd Coddington
headline: Boyd Coddington, 63, King of Hot Rods, Dies
abstract: Mr. Coddington was the owner of Boyds Wheels and of Hot Rods by Boyd and perhaps the best known of Southern California’s high-end car customizers.

name: Robert Skolrood
headline: Robert Skolrood Is Dead at 79; Argued Religion Cases
abstract: Mr. Skolrood was a lawyer who battled for fundamentalist Christians on issues that included nativity displays and gay rights.

name: Peter B. Neubauer
headline: Peter B. Neubauer, 94, Noted Child Psychiatrist, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Neubauer was a child psychiatrist who raised public alarms early on about the possible effects of television violence on the emotional development of children.

name: Joseph Juran
headline: Joseph Juran, 103, Pioneer in Quality Control, Dies
abstract: Mr. Juran wrote the “Quality Control Handbook,” which taught manufacturers worldwide how to be more efficient and productive.

name: Giuseppe di Stefano
headline: Giuseppe di Stefano, a Tenor Whose Career Flamed Out Too Early, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. di Stefano was a flamboyant, sometimes erratic opera star who in his prime after World War II was lauded as the most thrilling Italian tenor in a generation.

name: Jeff Healey
headline: Jeff Healey, Guitarist and Singer, Dies at 41
abstract: Jeff Healey was a Canadian guitarist, singer and songwriter whose band sold millions of blues-rock records and who also pursued a passion for old-time jazz, playing the trumpet and clarinet.

name: Larry Norman
headline: Larry Norman, Singer of Christian Rock Music, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Norman was a singer and songwriter considered by many to be the father of Christian rock despite years of being shunned by more traditional Christians.

name: Gary Gygax
headline: Gary Gygax, Game Pioneer, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Gygax transported a fantasy realm of wizards, goblins and elves onto millions of kitchen tables around the world through the game he helped create, Dungeons & Dragons.

name: Ray Kane
headline: Ray Kane, Master of Slack-Key Guitar, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Kane, a welder by trade who learned the slack-key guitar as a boy, was among the first people to bring the instrument into the concert hall.

name: Tony Silver
headline: Tony Silver, 72, Documentary Director, Dies
abstract: Mr. Silver was an award-winning independent filmmaker whose 1983 documentary, “Style Wars,” was one of the earliest accounts of hip-hop culture.

name: Ramón Barquín
headline: Ramón Barquín, Cuban Colonel, Dies at 93
abstract: Ramón M. Barquín’s struggles to restore the rule of law in Cuba clashed with both the dictator Fulgencio Batista and later the revolutionary government of Fidel Castro.

name: Leonard Rosenman
headline: Leonard Rosenman, Composer for Films, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Rosenman was an Oscar-winning film composer who helped introduce avant-garde music to Hollywood movie scores.

name: Frederick Seitz
headline: Frederick Seitz, Physicist Who Led Skeptics of Global Warming, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Seitz, a renowned physicist who led both the National Academy of Sciences and Rockefeller University, became a prominent skeptic on the issue of global warming.

name: Paul Raymond
headline: Paul Raymond, Britain’s Erotic Entertainment Magnate, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Raymond became one of Britain’s richest men, overseeing an empire of striptease clubs, salacious magazines and real estate holdings.

name: Norman Smith
headline: Norman Smith, Engineer for the Beatles, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Smith was the lead recording engineer for every Beatles song through 1965 and helped usher in an era of psychedelic rock when he discovered the band Pink Floyd.

name: George Fredrickson
headline: George Fredrickson, 73, Historian, Dies
abstract: Mr. Fredrickson cast new light on the study of race and helped define the field of comparative history with a penetrating examination of racial relations in the United States and South Africa.

name: Robert Kraichnan
headline: Robert Kraichnan, Physicist Who Studied Turbulence, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Dr. Kraichnan introduced a theory to explain the flow of energy in fluids, one that became known as the inverse energy cascade in two-dimensional turbulence.

name: Donald Lopez
profession: World War II Pilot and Smithsonian Official
headline: Donald Lopez, 84, World War II Pilot and Smithsonian Official, Dies
abstract: Mr. Lopez was a World War II ace flying fighter planes in China who later helped develop the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum.

name: Francis Pym
headline: Lord Francis Pym, Ex-Foreign Secretary of Britain, Dies at 86
abstract: Lord Pym of Sandy was a decorated veteran of World War II who earned respect for resisting the radical shake-up of British politics that became known as “Thatcherism.”

name: Richard J. Durrell
headline: Richard J. Durrell, First Publisher of People Magazine, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Durrell’s long career at Time Inc. began in 1950 when he answered a newspaper ad for a circulation newsstand representative in Minneapolis.

name: Vitaly Fedorchuk
headline: Vitaly Fedorchuk, 89, of K.G.B., Dies
abstract: After heading the K.G.B., General Fedorchuk was the Soviet Union’s interior minister from late 1982 to 1986.

name: Zev Segal
headline: Rabbi Zev Segal, Orthodox Leader Who Took Interfaith Approach to Social Issues, Dies at 91
abstract: Rabbi Segal often clashed with leaders of what he called “more liberal Jewish alternatives,” but also worked with Conservative and Reform Jews on social issues.

name: Malcolm McKenna
headline: Malcolm McKenna, 77, Fossil Seeker, Dies
abstract: Dr. McKenna hunted fossils from the Rockies to the Gobi Desert, from Patagonia to the Canadian Arctic, and published an authoritative classification of mammals.

name: Patricia N. Nanon
headline: Patricia N. Nanon, 84, Modern-Dance Patron, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Nanon supported the creation of modern-dance works as the founder and director of the Yard, a summer dance colony on Martha’s Vineyard.

name: George B. Litchford Sr.
headline: George B. Litchford Sr., 89, Aviation Inventor, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Litchford had a vital role in the development of the collision warning system now used on every airliner in the United States.

name: Samuel J. Hamrick
headline: Samuel J. Hamrick, Who Wrote as W. T. Tyler, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Hamrick was a former officer in the Foreign Service who, under the pseudonym W. T. Tyler, wrote spy novels about the adventures of burnt-out cases.

name: Gloria Shayne Baker
headline: Gloria Shayne Baker, Composer and Lyricist, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Baker composed the hit Christmas song “Do You Hear What I Hear?”

name: Malvin Wald
headline: Malvin Wald, Creator of ‘Naked City,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Wald conceived and was a co-writer of the 1948 crime film “The Naked City,” a prototype for modern police dramas.

name: Pearl Cornioley
headline: Pearl Cornioley, Resistance Fighter Who Opposed the Nazis, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Ms. Cornioley was a courier between the British and the French resistance against the Nazis and rose to command 3,000 underground fighters.

name: Dennis Irwin
profession: Bassist Popular in New York Jazz
headline: Dennis Irwin, 56, Bassist Popular in New York Jazz, Is Dead
abstract: For more than 30 years, Mr. Irwin was a much-in-demand New York jazz bassist. His recent illness became a rallying point for jazz musicians without medical insurance.

name: Henrietta Bell Wells
headline: Henrietta Bell Wells, a Pioneering Debater, Dies at 96
abstract: Mrs. Wells was the last surviving member of the 1930 Wiley College debate team, whose story was told in the movie “The Great Debaters.”

name: Otto Schnellbacher
profession: Football and Basketball Star at Kansas
headline: Otto Schnellbacher, Football and Basketball Star at Kansas, Dies at 84
abstract: Considered by Kansans to have been one of the state’s greatest athletes, Mr. Schnellbacher became an all-pro defensive back for the N.F.L. Giants and played pro basketball.

name: Gus Giordano
headline: Gus Giordano, 84, Innovator of Modern Jazz Dance, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Giordano was an early and tireless popularizer of American jazz dance who organized the first Jazz Dance World Congress.

name: Richard Burke
headline: Richard Burke, Founder of Trek Bicycle Company, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Mr. Burke’s company capitalized on the luster of Lance Armstrong’s victories in the Tour de France to reshape the way top-of-the-line bikes are manufactured.

name: Lazare Ponticelli
profession: Frances Last Veteran of World War I
headline: Lazare Ponticelli, France’s Last Veteran of World War I, Is Dead at 110
abstract: Mr. Ponticelli outlived more than 8.4 million other soldiers who fought under the French flag in World War I.

name: Joseph Weizenbaum
headline: Joseph Weizenbaum, Famed Programmer, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Weizenbaum’s computer program, Eliza, foreshadowed the potential of artificial intelligence.

name: Howard M. Metzenbaum
profession: Battled Big Business as Ohio Senator
headline: Howard M. Metzenbaum, Who Battled Big Business as Ohio Senator, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Metzenbaum fought conservatives and big business with such effectiveness and ferocity that he became known as “the last angry liberal.”

name: Erica Jesselson
headline: Erica Jesselson, Collector and Benefactor, Dies at 86
abstract: Mrs. Jesselson was a philanthropist and collector of Judaica who, with her late husband, founded the Yeshiva University Museum in Manhattan.

name: Chiara Lubich
headline: Chiara Lubich, Who Founded Catholic Lay Group, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Lubich became one of the most influential women in the Roman Catholic Church as the founder of the Focolare lay movement, which works to improve ties among faiths.

name: Stephen Colvin
headline: Stephen Colvin, 64, Inventive Heart Surgeon, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Colvin promoted the now widespread use of a pioneering procedure for repairing a leaky heart valve, and also performed heart surgery on children all over the world.

name: Louis Olah
headline: Louis Olah, 79, Racetracks’ Keeper of Silks, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Olah was a 4-foot-8-inch, 90-pound jockey who later became a giant in the thoroughbred industry among the jockeys and owners whose colorful silks he cleaned for more than 40 years.

name: Phillip Lloyd Powell
headline: Phillip Lloyd Powell, Furniture Designer, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Powell was a self-taught furniture designer who, working largely out of the public eye, produced elegant, sculptural pieces that are highly prized by collectors.

name: Phyllis Spira
headline: Phyllis Spira, 64, Cape Town Ballerina, Dies
abstract: Ms. Spira won international renown during her three-decade career with the Capab Ballet and co-founded Dance for All to spread dance classes into the townships.

name: Magda Cordell McHale
headline: Magda Cordell McHale, 86, Futurist Thinker, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. McHale was one of the founding members of the Independent Group in London in the early 1950s and later became a renowned sociologist and writer in the field of futurism.

name: Rafael Tufiño
headline: Rafael Tufiño, Artist, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Tufiño, a painter and printmaker, was considered one of Puerto Rico’s most prominent cultural figures.

name: Julia Vadala Taft
headline: Julia Vadala Taft, Official Who Led Relief Efforts, Is Dead at 65
abstract: The disasters Ms. Taft dealt with in 1988 alone included a Bangladesh flood that left 25 million people homeless, Ethiopian famine and a poisonous gas eruption in Cameroon.

name: Metropolitan Laurus
profession: Healed Rift in Russian Orthodox Church
headline: Metropolitan Laurus, Who Healed Rift in Russian Orthodox Church, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Metropolitan Laurus’s most historic moment was an exchange of kisses on the cheek last May with the Patriarch of Moscow, Aleksei II.

name: Arthur C. Clarke
headline: Arthur C. Clarke, Author Who Saw Science Fiction Become Real, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Clarke’s seamless blend of scientific expertise and poetic imagination helped usher in the space age.

name: Anthony Minghella
headline: Anthony Minghella, 54, Director, Dies
abstract: Mr. Minghella was the British filmmaker who won an Academy Award for his direction of “The English Patient.”

name: Philip Jones Griffiths
headline: Philip Jones Griffiths, War Photojournalist, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Griffiths’ pictures of civilian casualties and suffering were among the defining images of the war in Vietnam.

name: Roland Arnall
headline: Roland Arnall, Mortgage Innovator, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Arnall founded Ameriquest Mortgage, a company once billed as a sponsor of the American dream but later found itself at the center of the subprime mortgage crisis.

name: Ivan Dixon
headline: Ivan Dixon, Actor in ‘Hogan’s Heroes,’ Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Dixon was best known for playing Sgt. James Kinchloe on the 1960s sitcom “Hogan’s Heroes,” but his films included vivid portrayals of black struggles in the American South.

name: Frank Ayd
headline: Frank Ayd, 87, Who Advanced Thorazine Use, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Ayd studied his patients’ responses to early antipsychotic and antidepressant drugs, helping to give birth to the field of psychopharmacology.

name: Paul Scofield
headline: Paul Scofield, British Actor, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Scofield created the role of Sir Thomas More in Robert Bolt’s “A Man for All Seasons” and brought freshness and power to Hamlet, King Lear and many other classic roles.

name: Frank Berger
headline: Frank Berger, 94, Miltown Creator, Dies
abstract: Dr. Berger helped start the modern era of drug development with his invention of Miltown, the first mass-market psychiatric drug and a forerunner of Valium and Prozac.

name: Aaron Asher
headline: Aaron Asher, Editor of Literary Heavyweights, Dies at 78
abstract: Aaron Asher was a prominent book editor who for decades worked with writers such as Saul Bellow, Philip Roth and Arthur Miller.

name: William L. Hayward
headline: William L. Hayward, Film and Television Producer, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Hayward was a lawyer and producer whose best-known films include “Haywire,” a television movie based on a memoir by his sister Brooke about their charmed, tragic Hollywood family.

name: Mary Meader
headline: Mary Meader, 91, Pioneering Aerial Photographer, Dies
abstract: Ms. Meader, in the 1930s, took off on a 35,000-mile journey to advance geographic knowledge and made unprecedented aerial photographs of South America and Africa.

name: Jacob DeShazer
headline: Jacob DeShazer, Bombardier on Doolittle Raid, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. DeShazer endured 40 brutal months as a prisoner of the Japanese during World War II and returned later as a missionary spreading a message of Christian love and forgiveness.

name: Cachao
headline: Cachao, Mambo’s Inventor, Dies at 89
abstract: Israel Cachao López transformed the rhythm of Cuban music when he and his brother, the pianist and cellist Orestes López, extended and accelerated the final section of the stately Cuban danzón into the mambo.

name: David Challinor
headline: David Challinor, Conservationist, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Challinor combined his career as a top scientific administrator at the Smithsonian Institution with an equally intense pursuit of excellence as a champion oarsman.

name: Neil Aspinall
headline: Neil Aspinall, Beatles Aide, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Aspinall became the Beatles’ road manager when the group was still a local dance band and went on to manage the band’s production and management company.

name: Al Copeland
profession: Restaurateur Known for Spice and Speed
headline: Al Copeland, a Restaurateur Known for Spice and Speed, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Copeland made a fortune with the fried-chicken restaurant chain he started, Popeyes.

name: Hugo Claus
profession: One of Belgiums Most Renowned Authors
headline: Hugo Claus, One of Belgium’s Most Renowned Authors, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Claus was known for his often caustic portrayals of his nation, particularly of its ambiguous role in World War II.

name: John E. List
headline: John E. List, 82, Killer of 5 Family Members, Dies
abstract: Mr. List escaped his drab existence as a failed New Jersey accountant by killing his family in 1971, disappeared and built a new life far away until he was captured almost 18 years later.

name: Hal Riney
headline: Hal Riney, Adman for Reagan and G.M., Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Riney was an iconoclastic copywriter who helped build San Francisco into a creative center for advertising.

name: Richard Widmark
headline: Richard Widmark, Actor, Dies at 93
abstract: Richard Widmark created a villain in his first movie role who was so repellent and frightening that the actor became a star overnight.

name: Michael Lesch
headline: Michael Lesch, Who Helped Identify a Rare Disorder, Is Dead at 68
abstract: Dr. Lesch’s name is attached to a hereditary disorder characterized by self-mutilation that he helped identify as a medical student.

name: P. S. Penland
headline: P. S. Penland, Coast Expert, Dies at 54
abstract: Dr. Penland studied how Louisiana’s coastal marshes and barrier islands form, evolve and vanish, and became in the process a forceful advocate for their preservation.

name: Art Aragon
profession: Was One of the Rings Golden Boys
headline: Art Aragon Dies at 80; Was One of the Ring’s Golden Boys
abstract: Mr. Aragon, the lightweight and welterweight boxing contender of the 1950s, was known as Golden Boy for his flamboyant ring presence and love for the Hollywood life.

name: Abby Mann
headline: Abby Mann, ‘Nuremberg’ Screenwriter, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Mann brought incisive characterization and a searing sense of justice to “Judgment at Nuremberg,” for which he won an Academy Award for screenwriting.

name: Jon Hassler
headline: Jon Hassler, 74, Novelist Known for Minnesota Tales, Dies
abstract: Mr. Hassler authored a series of novels that affectionately mocked the foibles of small-town teachers, gossips, troublemakers and assorted other eccentrics.

name: Harvey Picker
headline: Harvey Picker, 92, Pioneer in Patient-Centered Care, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Picker, who led the Picker X-Ray Company, also started a foundation now considered a leader in promoting patient-friendly medical care.

name: William Hyland
headline: William Hyland, Who Guided Foreign Policy, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Hyland helped shape United States foreign policy, particularly toward the Soviet Union, and later became editor of Foreign Affairs.

name: Robert Fagles
headline: Robert Fagles, Translator of the Classics, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Fagles was a renowned translator of Latin and Greek whose versions of Homer and Virgil became unlikely best sellers.

name: Paul Arthur
headline: Paul Arthur, 60, Film Historian and Critic, Dies
abstract: A film historian, scholar and critic, Mr. Arthur was well known for writing about American avant-garde cinema and documentaries.

name: Jonathan Williams
headline: Jonathan Williams, Publisher, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Williams founded the Jargon Society, a small publishing house that has introduced the works of little-known writers, photographers and artists.

name: Dave Stevens
headline: Dave Stevens, 52, Artist Who Created the Rocketeer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Stevens invented the hero the Rocketeer and was famous for his ’50s-pinup-style renderings of women.

name: David Gale
headline: David Gale, Who Created Marriage Algorithm, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Gale’s algorithm created “stable” pairings from equal numbers of men and women and was applied to a broad range of settings.

name: Barth Healey
headline: Barth Healey, 68, Times Editor and Stamp Columnist, Dies
abstract: Drawing on his experience as a foreign correspondent, Mr. Healey mixed straight-up news with social commentary to explore philately in his column, “Stamps.”

name: Dith Pran
profession: Photojournalist and Survivor of the Killing Fields
headline: Dith Pran, Photojournalist and Survivor of the Killing Fields, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Dith was a photojournalist for The New York Times whose gruesome ordeal in the killing fields of Cambodia was re-created in a 1984 movie.

name: Robert F. Goheen
headline: Robert F. Goheen, Innovative Princeton President, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Goheen revolutionized the university by admitting its first women, pursuing minority faculty members, and doubling the space in campus buildings.

name: Jules Dassin
headline: Jules Dassin, Filmmaker on Blacklist, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Dassin is most widely remembered for films he made after he fled Hollywood in the 1950s, including “Never on Sunday,” “Topkapi,” and the 1954 French thriller “Rififi.”

name: David Todd
headline: David Todd, Architect and Official, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Todd was an architect of the towering Manhattan Plaza complex and later brought an imperturbable style to the chairmanship of the Landmarks Preservation Commission.

name: Sean Levert
profession: One-Third of the 1980s R&B Trio LeVert
headline: Sean Levert, One-Third of the 1980s R&B Trio LeVert, Dies at 39
abstract: Sean Levert was one-third of the 1980s R&B trio LeVert and a son of the lead singer of the O’Jays, Eddie Levert.

name: Jerry Kravat
headline: Jerry Kravat, Musician and Manager, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Kravat was a leading New York City nightclub and concert booker, bandleader and producer who was the longtime personal manager of the singer Barbara Cook.

name: Nikolai K. Baibakov
headline: Nikolai K. Baibakov, a Top Soviet Economic Official, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Baibakov oversaw Russian oil production during World War II and went on to become one of the Soviet Union’s top economic officials.

name: Angus Fairhurst
profession: One of the Group Known as Young British Artists
headline: Angus Fairhurst, One of the Group Known as Young British Artists, Dies at 41
abstract: Mr. Fairhurst was one of the group known as Young British Artists, or Y.B.A.’s, who stirred up the art scene in London and beyond in the 1990s.

name: Ralph Rapson
headline: Ralph Rapson, Modernist Architect, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Mr. Rapson designed the original Guthrie Theater in Minneapolis and a popular rocking chair that bore his name.

name: Ben Carnevale
headline: Ben Carnevale, 92, Basketball Coach and Administrator, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Carnevale was a successful coach at North Carolina and Navy and later an athletic director and a national and international basketball administrator.

name: Sherry Britton
headline: Sherry Britton, 89, a Star of the Burlesque Stage, Dies
abstract: Ms. Britton’s hour-glass figure, jet-black hair and rambunctious presence made her one of the queens of the burlesque stage in the 1930s and ’40s.

name: Wayne Frost
headline: Wayne Frost, Pioneering Break Dancer, Dies at 44
abstract: Mr. Frost was a hip-hop pioneer known as Frosty Freeze who helped inspire a worldwide break-dancing craze in the early 1980s as a member of the influential group Rock Steady Crew.

name: Roger P. Lang
headline: Roger P. Lang, an Architect Who Supported Preservation, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Lang often served as the public voice of the historical preservation movement in New York City.

name: Klaus Dinger
headline: Klaus Dinger, Drummer of Influential German Beat, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Dinger was the drummer for the 1970s band Neu!, whose mechanically repetitive yet buoyant beats had a wide influence in underground rock.

name: David Newsom
headline: David Newsom, 90, Diplomat in Iran Crisis, Dies
abstract: Mr. Newsom was a go-between in efforts to keep the deposed shah of Iran from entering the United States and tried to win the release of American hostages in Tehran.

name: Herbert Alexander
headline: Herbert Alexander, 80, Scholar of Money in Politics, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Alexander’s early, lonely pursuit of often closeted information on campaign finances illuminated the interplay of money and power in elections.

name: Robert A. Dentler
headline: Robert A. Dentler, Who Helped Shape Desegregation in Boston, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Dentler helped design and administer the groundbreaking desegregation plan that led to mob violence in Boston in the mid-1970s.

name: Charlton Heston
profession: Epic Film Star and Voice of N.R.A
headline: Charlton Heston, Epic Film Star and Voice of N.R.A., Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Heston appeared in some 100 films in his 60-year acting career, but he is remembered chiefly for his monumental, jut-jawed portrayals of Moses, Ben-Hur and Michelangelo.

name: George Switzer
headline: George Switzer, 92, Dies; Started a Gem Treasury
abstract: Mr. Switzer started the Smithsonian Institution’s vast collection of gems and minerals by acquiring the legendary, and some say bedeviled, Hope Diamond.

name: Charlotte Tan
headline: Dr. Charlotte Tan, 84, Oncologist, Dies
abstract: For many years, Dr. Tan was a driving force behind the testing of drugs that proved effective in treating children with leukemia and other cancers.

name: Helen Yglesias
headline: Helen Yglesias, Who Wrote of Women, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mrs. Yglesias’s novels examined women’s lives in an array of settings and situations — small towns, radical urban politics, abusive relationships, illness and old age.

name: Simon Michael Bessie
headline: Simon Michael Bessie, a Publisher of Major Literary Figures, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Bessie helped found Atheneum Publishers, perhaps the last major literary house to be started from scratch in the 20th century.

name: William D. Eberle
headline: William D. Eberle, Trade Representative for Nixon, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Eberle pushed Europe and Japan to lower trade barriers as President Richard M. Nixon’s chief trade negotiator in the 1970s.

name: S. C. Madison
headline: S. C. Madison, Charismatic Clergyman, Dies at 86
abstract: Bishop Madison was known to the faithful of the United House of Prayer for All People as Daddy and was the driving force in expanding his church’s influence over the last decade.

name: William L. Kraushaar
headline: William L. Kraushaar, Cosmic-Radiation Expert, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Kraushaar used early satellites to measure gamma rays and X-rays in space and then theorized about the ultimate sources of the cosmic radiation.

name: Doris Tillett
headline: Doris Tillett, 91, Designer of Hand-Printed Textiles, Dies
abstract: Ms. Tillett created hand-printed fabrics and helped establish community-run textile businesses in depressed New York neighborhoods.

name: Claus Luthe
headline: Claus Luthe, Car Design Innovator, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Mr. Luthe is credited with refining the work of Paul Bracq in developing BMW’s 3, 5 and 7 Series, sleek cars that became status symbols for many baby boomers.

name: Abe Osheroff
headline: Abe Osheroff, Veteran of Abraham Lincoln Brigade, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Osheroff was a carpenter and leftist provocateur who was wounded in the Spanish Civil War, then helped keep alive the memory of that struggle.

name: Marvin Sylvor
headline: Marvin Sylvor, a Designer of Carousels, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Sylvor dotted New York City parks with painted ponies and went on to help populate the world with galloping steeds, flying manes and sparkly gold trappings.

name: Robert Greene
headline: Robert Greene, 78, Dies; Investigative Journalist
abstract: Mr. Greene led teams that won two Pulitzer Prizes, one for stories following the murder of a journalist in Arizona and the other for reporting on the heroin trade.

name: Arturo Vivante
profession: Author of Tales Defined by Their Detail
headline: Arturo Vivante, Author of Tales Defined by Their Detail, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Vivante was the author of more than 70 short stories for The New Yorker.

name: Burt Glinn
profession: Chronicler of Cold War in Pictures
headline: Burt Glinn, Chronicler of Cold War in Pictures, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Glinn was a photojournalist, commercial photographer and former president of the Magnum photo agency.

name: John Herlitz
headline: John Herlitz, 65, Designer of Muscle Cars, Dies
abstract: John E. Herlitz made his reputation with the 1970 Plymouth Barracuda, which brought a touch of class to a genre of sporty compact cars started with the Ford Mustang.

name: Barry Gottehrer
headline: Barry Gottehrer, 73, Lindsay Aide, Dies
abstract: Mr. Gottehrer’s award-winning newspaper series “City in Crisis” helped elect John V. Lindsay mayor of New York in 1965. He later joined his administration.

name: John A. Wheeler
headline: John A. Wheeler, Physicist Who Coined the Term ‘Black Hole,’ Is Dead at 96
abstract: Mr. Wheeler helped invent the theory of nuclear fission, gave black holes their name and argued about the nature of reality with Albert Einstein and Niels Bohr.

name: Polly Lauder Tunney
headline: Polly Lauder Tunney, 100, Fighter’s Widow, Dies
abstract: Ms. Tunney’s secret romance and subsequent marriage to the former heavyweight champion Gene Tunney was one of the most sensational love stories of the 1920s.

name: Eugene Ehrlich
headline: Eugene Ehrlich, 85, Word Connoisseur, Dies
abstract: Mr. Ehrlich, a self-educated lexicographer, wrote 40 dictionaries, thesauruses and phrase books for the “extraordinarily literate.”

name: Tommy Holmes
headline: Tommy Holmes, 91, Who Set N.L. Hitting Mark, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Holmes, the Boston Braves outfielder who hit in 37 consecutive games in 1945, set a modern National League record that endured for 33 years.

name: Patrick J. Hillery
headline: Patrick J. Hillery, Who Helped Point Ireland to Peace, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Hillery served 14 years as Ireland’s president after a long ministerial career that won him admiration for his handling of the volatile issue of British rule in Northern Ireland.

name: Krister Stendahl
headline: Krister Stendahl, 86, Ecumenical Bishop, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Stendahl opened new ways of interpreting the Apostle Paul and pushed churches toward unity and tolerance.

name: Martin S. Kimmel
profession: Co-Founder of Retail Real Estate Firm
headline: Martin S. Kimmel, 92, Co-Founder of Retail Real Estate Firm, Dies
abstract: Mr. Kimmel built a portfolio that included about 1,900 properties in the United States, Canada, Mexico, Chile and Brazil, approximately 1,100 of them strip malls.

name: Edward N. Lorenz
profession: Meteorologist and a Father of Chaos Theory
headline: Edward N. Lorenz, a Meteorologist and a Father of Chaos Theory, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Lorenz was a meteorologist who tried to predict the weather with computers but instead gave rise to the modern field of chaos theory.

name: Iris Burton
headline: Iris Burton, Agent for Child Actors, Dies at 77
abstract: A chorus girl in the 1940s and ’50s, Ms. Burton later started a talent agency that represented River and Joaquin Phoenix and Henry Thomas, the boy in “E.T.”

name: Speed Vogel
headline: Speed Vogel, Author’s Aide, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Vogel’s care of an ailing friend, the novelist Joseph Heller, became the fodder for a darkly comic best-selling chronicle of a friendship, “No Laughing Matter.”

name: Joseph Solman
headline: Joseph Solman, Painter, Is Dead at 99
abstract: With Mark Rothko and other modernists, Mr. Solman helped shape American art as early as the 1930s.

name: Hazel Court
headline: Hazel Court, 82, Screaming Horror-Film Star, Dies
abstract: Ms. Court was a British actress who began as a popular ingénue and became a cult figure as a “scream queen” in horror films on both sides of the Atlantic.

name: Thomas Humphrey
headline: Thomas Humphrey, Guitar Designer and Maker, Is Dead at 59
abstract: Mr. Humphrey’s innovative designs and building techniques helped increase the volume, sustaining power and projection of the classical guitar.

name: Stephen Weiss
headline: Stephen Weiss, Benefactor to Cornell, Is Dead at 72
abstract: Mr. Weiss made major gifts to Cornell, his alma mater, and was chairman of its board of trustees from 1989 to 1997 and a board member for 16 years before that.

name: Robert Reed
headline: Robert Reed, Band Keyboard Player, Dies at 50
abstract: Mr. Reed, whose stage name was Syke Dyke, played keyboards in Trouble Funk, one of the definitive groups of go-go music.

name: Robert Hartmann
headline: Robert Hartmann, 91, Dies; Wrote Ford’s Noted Talk
abstract: Mr. Hartmann wrote the 1974 address in which Gerald R. Ford, assuming the presidency after the resignation of Richard M. Nixon, told the nation, “My fellow Americans, our long national nightmare is over.”

name: Martin Balin
headline: Martin Balin, 62, Vietnam-Era Conspirator, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Balin was one of six Vietnam War protesters whose plot to set fire to six buildings in Manhattan in 1970 was derailed at the last moment by undercover police officers.

name: Henry Moses
headline: Henry Moses, Educator and Trinity Headmaster, Is Dead at 66
abstract: During his tenure at the Trinity School, Mr. Moses saw the elite private school’s endowment grow to $51 million from $6 million.

name: Danny Federici
headline: Danny Federici, 58, Artist in Springsteen’s Band, Dies
abstract: Mr. Federici was Mr. Springsteen’s collaborator since they jammed together at clubs on the New Jersey shore in the 1960s.

name: George Butler
headline: George Butler, Executive at Prominent Jazz Labels, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Best known for syncing jazz with pop trends in the 1970s and ’80s, Mr. Butler also encouraged the movement that made stars of Wynton Marsalis and other neo-traditionalists.

name: George Butler
profession: Bodybuilding Chronicler in Photos and Film
headline: George Butler, 78, Bodybuilding Chronicler in Photos and Film, Dies
abstract: In his photographs for the book “Pumping Iron” and his documentary of the same name, Mr. Butler helped set Arnold Schwarzenegger on the road to stardom.

name: Alfonso López Trujillo
headline: Cardinal Alfonso López Trujillo, 72, Dies in Rome
abstract: Cardinal Trujillo was the Vatican’s leading voice in defense of traditional family values and in opposition to abortion, contraception and gay marriage.

name: Jerome H. Grossman
headline: Jerome H. Grossman, Health Care Policy Expert, Is Dead at 68
abstract: Mr. Grossman was influential in applying engineering solutions to make medical care more efficient

name: Buck Dawson
headline: Buck Dawson, 87, Promoter of Swimming, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Dawson was the first executive director of the International Swimming Hall of Fame in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., and a leading promoter of the sport.

name: Ozzie Cadena
headline: Ozzie Cadena, 83, Producer for Jazz Musicians, Dies
abstract: Mr. Cadena was a record producer of jazz and gospel music for the Savoy and Prestige labels, and later a promoter and booster of jazz in Los Angeles.

name: Geoffrey Polites
headline: Geoffrey Polites, Australian Ford Official, Is Dead at 60
abstract: Mr. Polites played a key role in arranging the March deal to sell the Jaguar and Land Rover brands to Indian automaker Tata Motors.

name: John Marzano
headline: John Marzano, Catcher and Analyst, Dies at 45
abstract: The former catcher became known to avid baseball fans as the co-host of “Leading Off,” the weekday morning analysis of the prior day’s games on MLB.com.

name: Alex Parker
headline: Alex Parker, Times Square Visionary, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Parker was a real estate developer whose vision of Times Square as the province of “nice people” was prescient but about two decades too early.

name: Werner Groebli
headline: Werner Groebli, Ice Skating’s Frick, Dies at 92
abstract: A member of the famous ice-skating comedy team of Frick & Frack, Mr. Groebli cracked up and wowed audiences for nearly 30 years.

name: Cecilia Colledge
headline: Cecilia Colledge, Olympian, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Colledge, an innovative British figure skater, was the youngest athlete to compete in the Winter Olympics and later won an Olympic silver medal.

name: Darell Garretson
headline: Darell Garretson, 76, Longtime N.B.A. Official, Dies
abstract: Mr. Garretson developed the concept of “refereeing the defense” and had a career that included more than 2,000 N.B.A. games and spanned 31 years.

name: Bebe Barron
headline: Bebe Barron, 82, Pioneer of Electronic Scores, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Barron composed the first electronic score for a feature film — the eerie gulps and burbles, echoes and weeeoooos of the 1956 science-fiction classic “Forbidden Planet.”

name: Germaine Tillion
headline: Germaine Tillion, French Anthropologist and Resistance Figure, Dies at 100
abstract: Ms. Tillion was a major figure in contemporary French thought who used experiences fighting Nazis and surviving a concentration camp as compelling intellectual fodder.

name: Jimmy Giuffre
headline: Jimmy Giuffre, Jazz Musician, Is Dead at 86
abstract: In his 50-year journey through jazz, the adventurous clarinetist, composer and arranger went from writing the Woody Herman anthem “Four Brothers” to creating striking experimental orchestral works.

name: Enrico Donati
headline: Enrico Donati, Surrealist Artist, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Donati was an Italian-born American painter and sculptor considered by many in the art world to be the last of the Surrealists.

name: John McConnell
headline: John McConnell, Steel Magnate and N.H.L. Owner, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. McConnell was a self-made steel magnate and sports enthusiast who borrowed $600 against his car to establish what became a multibillion-dollar company.

name: Kate Phillips
headline: Kate Phillips, Actress Who Christened ‘The Blob,’ Is Dead at 94
abstract: Ms. Phillips played mostly supporting roles on Broadway and in more than 50 films in the 1930s and ’40s and was a co-writer of the 1958 horror film “The Blob.”

name: M. Lois Murphy
headline: M. Lois Murphy, 91, Dies; Leader in Cancer Research
abstract: Dr. Murphy’s leadership advanced early work on chemotherapy, especially for childhood cancer, and led to markedly higher survival rates.

name: Cameron Argetsinger
headline: Cameron Argetsinger, 87, Road Racing Pioneer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Argetsinger’s love of speed cultivated on country roads led him to help revive road racing in postwar America.

name: Michael White
headline: Michael White, 59, Dies; Used Stories as Therapy
abstract: Mr. White, a social worker and family therapist, developed a technique known as narrative therapy, which used storytelling to help patients of all ages deal with childhood traumas.

name: Michael White
profession: Colorful Impresario With a Taste for the Outlandish
headline: Michael White, Colorful Impresario With a Taste for the Outlandish, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. White could depart from the mainstream to produce “The Rocky Horror Show,” “Oh! Calcutta!” and “Monty Python and the Holy Grail.”

name: Sallie Wilson
headline: Sallie Wilson, Dramatic Ballerina, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Wilson’s performances with American Ballet Theater during the 1960s and ’70s established her as one of America’s finest dramatic ballerinas.

name: William W. Warner
headline: William W. Warner, Chesapeake Bay Author, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Warner was the author of “Beautiful Swimmers,” a study of crabs and watermen in the Chesapeake Bay, which won the Pulitzer Prize for nonfiction in 1977.

name: Henry Brant
headline: Henry Brant, Avant-Garde Composer, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Brant was best known for his spatial music, in which the placement of performers on the stage and at carefully specified places around a concert hall is a crucial element.

name: Jason Shinder
profession: Poet and Founder of Arts Program
headline: Jason Shinder, 52, Poet and Founder of Arts Program, Dies
abstract: Mr. Shinder, a poet, anthologist and teacher, founded the Y.M.C.A. National Writer’s Voice program, one of the country’s largest networks of literary-arts centers.

name: Lewis Gibson
headline: Lewis Gibson, Cystic Fibrosis Expert, Dies at 80
abstract: Dr. Gibson developed a safe, highly reliable method to test children for cystic fibrosis, and later helped refine treatments for it.

name: Albert Hofmann
headline: Albert Hofmann, the Father of LSD, Dies at 102
abstract: Mr. Hofmann synthesized LSD in 1938 but did not discover its psychopharmacological effects until five years later, when he accidentally ingested the substance.

name: Will Robinson
headline: Will Robinson, Top Scout, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Robinson broke racial barriers as a college basketball coach and discovered talented players as a scout for both professional basketball and football teams.

name: Yossi Harel
headline: Yossi Harel, Who, Defying British, Brought Jews to Palestine, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Harel renamed the rickety ship he commanded Exodus 1947 and sailed it to legend as a symbol of the righteousness of the mission by Jews to settle Palestine in the face of British opposition.

name: James Day
headline: James Day, Public Television Host, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Day was probably best known as the host of two television programs: “Kaleidoscope” and “Day at Night.”

name: Gordon Bradley
headline: Gordon Bradley, Who Nurtured U.S. Soccer, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Bradley, a native of England, was a pioneering figure in American soccer and the first to sign with the New York Cosmos, as a player and as a coach.

name: Charles Tilly
headline: Charles Tilly, 78, Writer and a Social Scientist, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Tilly combined historical interpretation and quantitative analysis to forge novel intellectual interpretations, as when he compared nation states to protection rackets.

name: Buzzie Bavasi
headline: Buzzie Bavasi, a Dodgers Innovator, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Bavasi was the general manager of the Dodgers during their glory years in Brooklyn and their first decade in Los Angeles and a baseball executive for nearly a half-century.

name: Philipp von Boeselager
headline: Philipp von Boeselager, Who Attempted an Assassination of Hitler, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Boeselager is believed to have been the last surviving member of the circle of German Army officers who tried to assassinate Adolf Hitler with a briefcase bomb in 1944.

name: William Frankel
headline: William Frankel, Who Edited Jewish Chronicle, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Frankel reinvigorated the London-based newspaper The Jewish Chronicle as its editor for two decades, broadening its coverage of world affairs.

name: Peter Howard
headline: Peter Howard, 80, Dies; Put Music on Broadway
abstract: Mr. Howard arranged the dance music, composed the incidental music or conducted the orchestra for many of Broadway’s biggest hits of the last half-century, and sometimes did all three.

name: Frank Whiteley Jr.
headline: Frank Whiteley Jr., 93, Dies; Trained Ruffian
abstract: Mr. Whiteley was a thoroughbred racing Hall of Famer who trained the brilliant but ill-fated filly Ruffian.

name: Alan Seiden
profession: Key to a St. Johns N.I.T. Title
headline: Alan Seiden, a Key to a St. John’s N.I.T. Title, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Mr. Seiden was an all-American guard who helped lead the St. John’s basketball team to the 1959 National Invitation Tournament.

name: Giuseppe Attardi
profession: Studied Cells for Clues to Aging
headline: Giuseppe Attardi Is Dead at 84; Studied Cells for Clues to Aging
abstract: Dr. Attardi was a molecular biologist whose penetrating studies of mitochondria helped explain how cells grow and deteriorate with age.

name: Ted Key
headline: Ted Key, 95, Creator of ‘Hazel’ Cartoon, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Key’s cartoon creation was an independent-minded, impertinent maid who came to be known as Hazel, a name that became synonymous with live-in housekeepers.

name: Mildred Loving
headline: Mildred Loving, Who Battled Ban on Mixed-Race Marriage, Dies at 68
abstract: Mrs. Loving’s anger over being banished from Virginia for marrying a white man led to a landmark Supreme Court ruling overturning state miscegenation laws.

name: Ilyas Malayev
headline: Ilyas Malayev, 72, Uzbek Musician and Poet, Dies
abstract: Mr. Malayev was a musician and poet renowned in Uzbekistan and transplanted to Queens, where he was a legend among fellow Bukharan Jews.

name: Irvine Robbins
profession: Ice Cream Entrepreneur and a Maestro of 31 Flavors
headline: Irvine Robbins, Ice Cream Entrepreneur and a Maestro of 31 Flavors, Dies at 90
abstract: With his brother-in-law, Burton Baskin, Mr. Robbins started the Baskin-Robbins ice cream store chain, concocting quirky flavors like Daiquiri Ice and Here Comes the Fudge.

name: Alvin Colt
headline: Alvin Colt, Broadway Costume Designer, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Colt was a Tony Award-winning costume designer who created both serious and amusing costumes for more than 50 Broadway productions.

name: John Jay Iselin
headline: John Jay Iselin, Public TV Innovator, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Iselin led WNET, also known as Channel 13, the nation’s largest public television station, through a period of innovative programming.

name: Eddy Arnold
headline: Eddy Arnold, 89, Country Singer With Pop Luster, Dies
abstract: Mr. Arnold was a gentleman crooner who took country music uptown and sold more than 85 million recordings over seven decades.

name: Claude Rosenberg
headline: Claude Rosenberg, Advocate for Philanthropy, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Mr. Rosenberg developed a model that estimated that if people gave what they could afford, we would increase charitable giving in the U.S. by $100 billion a year.

name: Morgan Sparks
headline: Morgan Sparks, Bell Scientist, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Sparks made critical contributions to developing the second-generation transistor, which became a building block of modern electronic devices.

name: Frances Yeend
profession: Soprano at City Opera and the Met
headline: Frances Yeend, Soprano at City Opera and the Met, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Yeend was an internationally known soprano who appeared regularly with the New York City Opera and the Metropolitan Opera in the decades after World War II.

name: Victor Christ-Janer
headline: Victor Christ-Janer, Modernist Architect, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Christ-Janer was a member of a group of influential architects who built Modernist homes and offices in New Canaan, Conn.

name: Hanon Reznikov
headline: Hanon Reznikov, a Force Behind the Living Theater, Dies at 57
abstract: An actor, director and writer, Mr. Reznikov helped run the avant-garde Living Theater for 23 years.

name: Robert Vesco
headline: Robert Vesco, ’70s Financier, Is Dead at 71
abstract: The death of the financier Robert L. Vesco, confirmed by documents and interviews, has closed the books on one of Washington’s longest and most prominent fugitive hunts.

name: Beverlee McKinsey
profession: Actress in Decades of Soap Operas
headline: Beverlee McKinsey, 72, Actress in Decades of Soap Operas, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. McKinsey, a well-known soap opera actress of the 1970s, ’80s and ’90s, played memorably strong women on “Another World” and “Guiding Light.”

name: R. R. Knudson
headline: R. R. Knudson, a Writer Whose Subject Was Sports, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Knudson wrote more than 40 books, including the “Zan” novels, which were published in the years after the passage of Title IX and starred a young female athlete.

name: Charles R. Ellis
headline: Charles R. Ellis, President of John Wiley & Sons, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Ellis led the venerable family-owned publishing house John Wiley & Sons back to fiscal health in the 1990s after a period of misdirected expansion.

name: George Cressman
headline: George Cressman Dies at 88; Led Weather Service
abstract: Mr. Cressman, a pioneer in the use of computers to predict the weather, was a former director of the National Weather Service.

name: Elaine Dundy
headline: Elaine Dundy, Author of ‘The Dud Avocado,’ Is Dead at 86
abstract: Ms. Dundy was the author of “The Dud Avocado,” which was published in 1958 and whose heroine, a free-spirited American girl, was a forerunner to Isadora Wing and Carrie Bradshaw.

name: Nuala O’Faolain
headline: Nuala O’Faolain, 68, Irish Memoirist, Is Dead
abstract: Often seen as a feminine (and feminist) counterpart to Frank McCourt’s “Angela’s Ashes,” Ms. O’Faolain’s “Are You Somebody?,” (1996) created a sensation.

name: Diana Barnato Walker
headline: Diana Barnato Walker, Acclaimed Pilot, Dies at 90
abstract: Mrs. Walker took up flying in the 1930s and became celebrated as one of a group of women who delivered new fighters and bombers to combat squadrons in World War II.

name: Witold Woyda
headline: Witold Woyda, Fencer Who Won Gold for Poland, Is Dead at 68
abstract: Mr. Woyda was an Olympic champion fencer who was atypically short for his native Poland but who compensated for a lack of reach with dazzling dexterity.

name: Joseph Egan
headline: Joseph Egan, Lawyer Who Fought Nuclear Waste Site, Is Dead at 53
abstract: Mr. Egan, a nuclear engineer-turned-lawyer, led Nevada’s legal campaign to block a nuclear waste dump at Yucca Mountain.

name: Leyla Gencer
profession: Turkish-Born Soprano and a Popular Star of La Scala
headline: Leyla Gencer, Turkish-Born Soprano and a Popular Star of La Scala, Dies
abstract: Ms. Gencer was an operatic soprano who was among the last of a generation of larger-than-life divas that included Maria Callas.

name: Murray Jarvik
profession: Research Helped Lead to Nicotine Patch
headline: Murray Jarvik, 84, Whose Research Helped Lead to Nicotine Patch, Dies
abstract: Dr. Jarvik was among the first to study a precursor to LSD and researched the physiology and psychology of smoking.

name: Paul Haeberlin
headline: Paul Haeberlin, 3-Star Chef, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Haeberlin’s innovative spin on classical French cuisine helped transform his family’s modest restaurant on the Ill River in Alsace into a culinary powerhouse.

name: Irena Sendler
headline: Irena Sendler, Lifeline to Young Jews, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Mrs. Sendler created a network of rescuers in Poland who smuggled about 2,500 Jewish children out of the Warsaw ghetto in World War II.

name: Dottie Rambo
headline: Dottie Rambo, Singer and Songwriter, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Rambo was a singer and prolific songwriter who was one of the most successful women to write songs in gospel music.

name: Robert Rauschenberg
headline: Robert Rauschenberg, American Artist, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Rauschenberg, who time and again reshaped art in the 20th century, defied the traditional idea that an artist stick to one medium or style.

name: Shmuel Katz
headline: Shmuel Katz, an Opponent of Begin’s Peace Effort, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Katz was a close adviser to Menachem Begin, Israel’s prime minister in the late 1970s and early 1980s, but later became an opponent of Begin’s peace efforts with Egypt and the Palestinians.

name: Larry Levine
headline: Larry Levine, an Inventor of ‘Wall of Sound,’ Is Dead at 80
abstract: Mr. Levine helped create Phil Spector’s groundbreaking “wall of sound” technique on hit records by the Crystals, the Ronettes and the Righteous Brothers.

name: Benjamin Gaon
headline: Benjamin Gaon, Who Aided Israel-Arab Trade, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Gaon was an Israeli industrialist who tried to build trade links with the Arab world and helped the Israeli economy move toward privatization.

name: Harvey Schein
headline: Harvey Schein, Promoter of Betamax at Sony, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Schein led the Sony Corporation of America in the 1970s and doubled its size in spite of championing the failed Betamax video recording system.

name: Warren Cowan
headline: Warren Cowan, a Star at Promoting Stars, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Cowan represented generations of celebrities, from Doris Day to Bette Midler, Frank Sinatra to Elton John, Ronald Reagan to Arnold Schwarzenegger.

name: Oakley Hall
profession: Novelist Attuned to the Old West
headline: Oakley Hall, 87, Novelist Attuned to the Old West, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Hall was the author of the novels “Warlock” and “The Downhill Racers” and a literary heir to fellow California writers like Wallace Stegner.

name: Robert Mondavi
headline: Robert Mondavi, Napa Wine Champion, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Mondavi was the California vintner behind the rebirth of the Napa Valley wine industry.

name: Dick Netzer
headline: Dick Netzer, 79, Municipal Finance Expert, Dies
abstract: Mr. Netzer advised mayors of New York City and governors of New York State and served to help pry New York City out of bankruptcy in the 1970s.

name: Jimmy Slyde
profession: Dancer and a Giant of Rhythm Tap
headline: Jimmy Slyde, Dancer and a Giant of Rhythm Tap, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Slyde was one of the last great tap dancers of the big-band era, whose smooth moves carried him from swing and bebop to Broadway and the movies.

name: Will Elder
profession: Cartoonist of Satiric Gifts and Overpopulated Scenes
headline: Will Elder, Cartoonist of Satiric Gifts and Overpopulated Scenes, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Elder, whose frantic, gag-filled illustrations helped to define the comic identity of Mad magazine, was also a creator of the Playboy cartoon serial “Little Annie Fanny.”

name: André Galerne
headline: André Galerne, 81, an Entrepreneur of the Deep, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Galerne started what became the world’s largest privately owned deep-sea construction company.

name: Lucius Battle
headline: Lucius Battle, Diplomat and Official, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Battle, a career diplomat, served in the administration of President Harry S. Truman, and led a reorganization of the State Department under President John F. Kennedy.

name: Irving Rosenthal
headline: Irving Rosenthal, 95, Mentor to Journalists, Dies
abstract: Professor Rosenthal taught journalism at the City College of New York for 40 years and seeded the newsrooms and broadcast studios of America with thousands of reporters and editors.

name: Irving Rosenthal
profession: Low-Profile Force on the Beat Scene
headline: Irving Rosenthal, Low-Profile Force on the Beat Scene, Dies at 91
abstract: He published Ginsberg, Kerouac and Burroughs in the late 1950s. The university that oversaw his journal was not pleased with the “Naked Lunch” excerpt.

name: Arthur W. Burks
headline: Arthur W. Burks, 92, Dies; Early Computer Theorist
abstract: Mr. Burks was a member of the team that designed the Eniac computer, a frequent collaborator of John von Neumann and a pioneer in computing education.

name: Michael Rossman
headline: Michael Rossman, Who Fought for Campus Rights, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Rossman, an organizer of the Free Speech Movement at the University of California, Berkeley, was later known for his books on politics, society and education.

name: Beverly Rae Kimes
headline: Beverly Rae Kimes, Automotive Journalist and Historian, Is Dead at 68
abstract: Ms. Kimes parlayed a job as a secretary at a fledgling car magazine into a career as one of the nation’s pre-eminent historians of automobiles.

name: Huntington Hartford II
headline: Huntington Hartford II, A. & P. Heir, Dies at 97
abstract: Huntington Hartford II inherited a fortune from the A. & P. grocery business and lost most of it chasing his dreams as an entrepreneur and arts patron.

name: Willis Lamb Jr.
profession: Won Nobel for Work on Atom
headline: Willis Lamb Jr., 94, Dies; Won Nobel for Work on Atom
abstract: Mr. Lamb shared the 1955 Nobel Prize in Physics for the discovery of a discrepancy in the quantum theory describing how electrons behave in the hydrogen atom.

name: Regina Kellerman
profession: Locator of New Yorks First City Hall
headline: Regina Kellerman, 84, Locator of New York’s First City Hall, Dies
abstract: The research of Ms. Kellerman, an architectural historian, led to the literal unearthing of New York City’s first City Hall.

name: Jesse Edwards
headline: Jesse Edwards, Pathologist, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Edwards was a leading cardiac pathologist who assembled a formidable collection of human hearts to let doctors study coronary disease, congenital defects and trauma.

name: Hamilton Jordan
headline: Hamilton Jordan, Carter’s Right Hand, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Jordan, a self-proclaimed “political animal” and campaign whiz-kid, eventually became President Jimmy Carter’s chief of staff and top confidant.

name: Barbara Sears Rockefeller
profession: Actress With a Famous Divorce Settlement
headline: Barbara Sears Rockefeller, Actress With a Famous Divorce Settlement, Dies at 91
