abstract: Mrs. Rockefeller married one of the richest men in America and, after their divorce six years later, won a settlement regarded as a record in its day.

name: Zelma Henderson
headline: Zelma Henderson, Who Aided Desegregation, Dies at 88
abstract: Mrs. Henderson was the sole surviving plaintiff in Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka, the landmark federal desegregation case of 1954.

name: Charles Brenner
headline: Charles Brenner, Psychoanalyst, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Brenner reigned for nearly a half-century as the dean of American psychoanalysis, working to clarify, refine and fiercely defend its core principles.

name: Lloyd Moore
headline: Lloyd Moore, Pioneering Nascar Driver, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Moore, who drove in 49 races in Nascar’s Grand National series, now known as the Sprint Cup, was recognized by Nascar as its oldest living driver.

name: Catherine Mulkerrin
headline: Catherine Mulkerrin, Activist Boston Nun, Dies at 72
abstract: Sister Catherine lobbied ardently but in vain to persuade Roman Catholic leaders in the Boston Archdiocese to warn parishioners about priests who had been accused of sexually molesting children.

name: Wilfrid Mellers
headline: Wilfrid Mellers, 94, Musicologist and Critic, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Mellers, an English musicologist, composer, critic and teacher, published more than 20 books on subjects ranging from classical composers to the music of the Beatles and Bob Dylan.

name: J. C. Hurewitz
headline: J. C. Hurewitz, 93, Dies; Scholar of the Middle East
abstract: Mr. Hurewitz was a Columbia University professor whose voluminous research and evenhanded scholarship contributed depth and complexity to the emerging field of Middle Eastern studies.

name: Jan Pokorny
headline: Jan Pokorny, 93, Is Dead; Melded Architectural Styles
abstract: Mr. Pokorny was a Czech-born architect whose New York firm became known for restoring and adapting historic buildings for reuse.

name: Cornell Capa
headline: Cornell Capa, Photographer, Is Dead at 90
abstract: After a distinguished career as a photojournalist, Mr. Capa founded the International Center of Photography.

name: Siegmund Nissel
headline: Siegmund Nissel, 86, of Amadeus Group, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Nissel was the second violinist of the Amadeus Quartet, an internationally renowned ensemble that had its roots in the internment camps of wartime Britain.

name: Dick Sutcliffe
headline: Dick Sutcliffe, 90, Dies; Began ‘Davey and Goliath’
abstract: Mr. Sutcliffe’s idea to use animated characters to teach religious principles resulted in the cartoon show “Davey and Goliath.”

name: Sydney Pollack
headline: Sydney Pollack, Director of High-Profile Hollywood Movies, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Mr. Pollack defined an era with star-laden movies like “The Way We Were,” “Tootsie” and “Out of Africa.”

name: Dick Martin
headline: Dick Martin, ‘Laugh-In’ Host, Dies at 86
abstract: With his partner, Dan Rowan, Mr. Martin turned a midseason replacement slot at NBC in 1968 into a hit that redefined what could be done on television.

name: Manuel Marulanda
profession: Top Commander of Colombias Largest Guerrilla Group
headline: Manuel Marulanda, Top Commander of Colombia’s Largest Guerrilla Group, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Marulanda, who rose from peasant origins to being the top commander of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia rebel group, was a mythical feature of the country’s long internal war.

name: U. Utah Phillips
headline: U. Utah Phillips, Folk Troubadour, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Phillips jokingly called himself U. Utah Phillips, “the Golden Voice of the Great Southwest.”

name: J. R. Simplot
headline: J. R. Simplot, Farmer Who Developed First Frozen French Fries, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Simplot fashioned an entrepreneurial career that included developing the first commercial frozen French fry.

name: Earle Hagen
headline: Earle Hagen, Who Composed Noted TV Tunes, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Hagen was a onetime big-band trombonist who wrote some of the most famous theme songs in television history.

name: Jimmy McGriff
headline: Jimmy McGriff, Jazz and Blues Organist, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. McGriff was one of the most popular jazz and blues organists since the early 1960s.

name: Ernst Stuhlinger
profession: Rocket Scientist Crucial in Space Race
headline: Ernst Stuhlinger, Rocket Scientist Crucial in Space Race, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Dr. Stuhlinger was one of the most prominent of the Germans who brought their skills in rocket science to the United States after World War II.

name: David Gahr
headline: David Gahr, Photographer of Musicians, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Gahr turned his back on a promising career as a scholar and landed among the pre-eminent photographers of American folk, blues, jazz and rock musicians.

name: Sophie B. Altman
headline: Sophie B. Altman, Who Started Quiz Show in 1961, Dies at 95
abstract: Mrs. Altman started a television show for precocious high school students that became the world’s longest-running quiz show.

name: Harvey Korman
headline: Harvey Korman of ‘Burnett Show’ Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Korman won four Emmys for his contributions to “The Carol Burnett Show” and was seen to hilarious effect on the big screen in “Blazing Saddles.”

name: Martin Levin
headline: Martin Levin, Prolific Book Reviewer, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Levin was a writer, humorist and prolific book critic who reviewed five books a week for The New York Times for decades on end.

name: George Garrett
headline: George Garrett, 78, Southern Novelist, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Garrett was a highly regarded Southern novelist who never received the wide literary renown that his decades of glowing reviews would suggest.

name: Richard Lower
headline: Richard Lower Dies at 78; Transplanted Animal and Human Hearts
abstract: Dr. Lower’s daring heart surgeries on animals in the 1950s helped pave the way for the first successful transplant of a human heart in 1967.

name: Alvin M. Marks
headline: Alvin M. Marks, Inventor With 122 Patents, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Marks held patents on polarized film for sunglasses, a 3-D moviemaking process and a generator the size of a grapefruit that could produce enough electricity for a house.

name: Frank Shattuck II
headline: Frank Shattuck II, Who Helped Guide Schrafft’s, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Shattuck was the last president of the company that owned Schrafft’s restaurants, a New York City-based chain that offered home-style food in genteel surroundings.

name: Alexander Courage
headline: Alexander Courage, ‘Star Trek’ Composer, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Courage was an Emmy-winning Hollywood composer whose most famous work was the strange, soaring and instantly recognizable theme from “Star Trek.”

name: Earl Eaton
profession: Founder of the Vail Skiing Resort
headline: Earl Eaton, a Founder of the Vail Skiing Resort, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Eaton grew up in the Rocky Mountains of Colorado as a hunter, hiker, prospector and skier and envisioned what became Vail, one of America’s most popular ski resorts.

name: Joseph P. Hoey
headline: Joseph P. Hoey, 95, Wide-Ranging Prosecutor, Dies
abstract: Mr. Hoey was United States attorney for the Eastern District of New York for most of the 1960s after handling high-profile cases for the Brooklyn district attorney.

name: Yves Saint Laurent
headline: Yves Saint Laurent, Giant of Couture, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Saint Laurent exploded on the fashion scene in 1958 and endured as one of the best-known and most influential couturiers of the second half of the 20th century.

name: John Weber
headline: John Weber, 75, Contemporary-Art Dealer, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Weber was an art dealer known for his early advocacy of Conceptual Art, Post-Minimalist sculpture and Italian Arte Povera.

name: Jordan Wright
headline: Jordan Wright, 50, Political Archivist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Wright privately amassed what may be the largest and most comprehensive collection of U.S. political campaign artifacts known.

name: Jacob Robbins
headline: Jacob Robbins, 85, Thyroid Researcher, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Robbins’s studies of the thyroid gland helped explain how it helps govern metabolism and how thyroid cancers caused by radiation may be treated or possibly prevented.

name: Walter H. Diamond
headline: Walter H. Diamond, Expert on Taxation, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Mr. Diamond was an expert on international taxation and helped prepare the foreign exchange proposals for the Bretton Woods conference, which established the International Monetary Fund.

name: Louise Firouz
headline: Louise Firouz, Horse Breeder, Dies at 74
abstract: Mrs. Firouz in 1965 discovered a pony-size Caspian horse, from a breed that had long been thought extinct, which were found to be a precursor or modern racehorses.

name: Bo Diddley
headline: Bo Diddley, Who Gave Rock His Beat, Dies at 79
abstract: The singer and guitarist invented his own name, his own guitars, his own beat and, with a handful of other musical pioneers, rock ’n’ roll itself.

name: Anne d’Harnoncourt
headline: Anne d’Harnoncourt, Who Led Philadelphia Museum, Dies at 64
abstract: Ms. d’Harnoncourt revivified the Philadelphia Museum of Art and maintained the intellectual standards of its program of exhibitions.

name: William P. Ford
headline: William P. Ford, 72, Rights Advocate, Dies
abstract: Mr. Ford sought to bring military officials to justice after his sister and three other American churchwomen were murdered in El Salvador’s civil war in the 1980s.

name: William E. Odom
headline: William E. Odom, Former Director of N.S.A., Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Odom, a director of the National Security Agency in the Reagan administration, became an early and outspoken opponent of the Iraq war.

name: Paul Sills
headline: Paul Sills, a Guru of Improv Theater, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Sills was a founder of the Second City theater company and the godfather of modern improvisational sketch comedy.

name: Alton Kelley
headline: Alton Kelley, 67, Artist of the 1960s Rock Counterculture, Dies
abstract: Mr. Kelley created the visual equivalent of an acid trip in psychedelic concert posters for artists like the Grateful Dead and Jimi Hendrix.

name: Boris Shakhlin
headline: Boris Shakhlin, 76, Is Dead; Won 13 Olympic Medals in Gymnastics
abstract: Shakhlin, the brilliant Soviet gymnast of the 1950s and ’60s, won six individual Olympic gold medals, a record for men’s gymnastics.

name: Thomas A. Johnson
headline: Thomas A. Johnson, Pioneering Black Journalist, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Johnson was the first black reporter at Newsday and later, at The New York Times, one of the first black journalists to work as a foreign correspondent for a major daily newspaper.

name: Klaus Perls
headline: Klaus Perls, Art Dealer Who Gave Picassos to the Met, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Perls donated an important collection of African royal art from Benin and modern works by Picasso and Modigliani to the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

name: Charles Moskos
headline: Charles Moskos, Policy Adviser, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Moskos regularly advised policy makers, senators and generals on military matters, including coming up with the armed services’ “don’t ask, don’t tell” policy on gay personnel.

name: Oscar Ratnoff
headline: Oscar Ratnoff, 91, Expert on Blood Clots, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Ratnoff’s insightful research into how the blood coagulates helped reveal the “waterfall” biochemical response involved in the body’s reaction to wounds and trauma.

name: Vijay Tendulkar
headline: Vijay Tendulkar, Indian Theater Innovator, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Tendulkar was one of the most important and influential Indian playwrights of the last six decades and the writer for some critically acclaimed Hindi films.

name: Matthew J. Bruccoli
headline: Matthew J. Bruccoli, 76, Scholar, Dies; Academia’s Fitzgerald Record Keeper
abstract: Mr. Bruccoli’s biography of F. Scott Fitzgerald and outpouring of scholarly essays and critical editions made him the dean of Fitzgerald studies in the United States.

name: Sven Davidson
headline: Sven Davidson, 79, Hall of Famer in Tennis, Dies
abstract: Mr. Davidson was the first Swede to win a Grand Slam tennis championship, a leading international player of the 1950s and a member of the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

name: Harriet Johnson
headline: Harriet Johnson, 50, Activist for Disabled, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Johnson was a feisty champion of the rights of the disabled who came to prominence after she challenged a Princeton professor’s contention that severely disabled newborns could ethically be euthanized.

name: Jim McKay
headline: Jim McKay, Pioneer Sports Broadcaster, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. McKay covered 12 Olympic Games and was the voice of the ABC sports anthology series “Wide World of Sports.”

name: Bill Finegan
headline: Bill Finegan, Arranger and Big-Band Leader, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Finegan arranged hits for Glenn Miller and Tommy Dorsey and then formed a big band with Eddie Sauter that was famed for skill, daring and very, very odd instruments.

name: Randolph Chase Jr.
headline: Dr. Randolph Chase Jr., 79, Disease Expert, Dies
abstract: The research of Dr. Chase, one of the first tenured black members of the New York University medical school faculty, shed light on organ transplant rejections.

name: Dino Risi
headline: Dino Risi, Italian Filmmaker, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Risi helped establish a new style that became internationally known as commedia all’italiana.

name: Warren A. Croll Jr.
headline: Warren A. Croll Jr., Trainer, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Croll was a Hall of Fame trainer who won the 1987 Belmont Stakes with Bet Twice and trained four thoroughbred champions.

name: John S. Zinsser Jr.
headline: John S. Zinsser Jr., 84, Book Popularizer, Is Dead
abstract: As editor of Reader’s Digest Condensed Books in the 1960s, ’70s and ’80s, Mr. Zinsser made nearly 800 carefully crunched versions of popular books available to readers.

name: Eliot Asinof
headline: Eliot Asinof, ‘Eight Men Out’ Author, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Asinof’s journalistic re-creation of a 1919 Black Sox scandal, “Eight Men Out,” became a classic of baseball literature and narrative nonfiction.

name: Neil MacNeil
profession: Among First of TV Reporters on Congress
headline: Neil MacNeil, Among First of TV Reporters on Congress, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. MacNeil covered Congress for Time magazine through seven presidential administrations and was among television’s first Congressional correspondents.

name: David Mitton
headline: David Mitton, a Creator of ‘Thomas’ for TV, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Mitton created the children’s series “Thomas the Tank Engine and Friends,” which evolved into an international hit and a merchandising juggernaut.

name: Harlan Cleveland
headline: Harlan Cleveland, Diplomat and Scholar, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Cleveland, a former president of the University of Hawaii and an American ambassador to NATO, pressed for nuclear arms control and strengthening of the United Nations.

name: Trevor Wilkinson
headline: Trevor Wilkinson, 85, a Maker of Sports Cars, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Wilkinson was the founder of TVR, the small British carmaker known for nimble little sports cars that early owners often assembled from a kit.

name: John Rauch
profession: Coach of Raiders and the Bills
headline: John Rauch, 80, Coach of Raiders and the Bills, Dies
abstract: Mr. Rauch coached the Oakland Raiders in the second Super Bowl and later was O. J. Simpson’s first coach in professional football with the Buffalo Bills.

name: Edwina Froehlich
headline: Edwina Froehlich, 93, La Leche League Pioneer, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Froehlich was inspired to help found La Leche League to support breast-feeding after being told at the age of 35 that she was too old to make breast milk for her baby.

name: Tim Russert
headline: Tim Russert, 58, NBC’s Face of Politics, Dies
abstract: Mr. Russert, moderator of “Meet the Press,” was a fixture on television on Sunday mornings and election nights.

name: Stewart R. Mott
headline: Stewart R. Mott, 70, Offbeat Philanthropist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Mott’s gifts to progressive causes were often upstaged by his eccentricities, like cultivating a farm with 460 plant species.

name: Chingiz Aitmatov
headline: Chingiz Aitmatov, Who Wrote of Life in U.S.S.R., Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Aitmatov was a Communist writer who gave a voice to the people of the remote Soviet republic of Kyrgyz, and later became a diplomat and a friend and adviser to the Soviet leader Mikhail S. Gorbachev.

name: Anne C. Martindell
headline: Anne C. Martindell, Late Bloomer, Lawmaker and Diplomat, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Ms. Martindell entered politics in her 50s, found true love as ambassador to New Zealand in her 60s, earned a college degree in her 80s and published a memoir titled “Never Too Late” in her 90s.

name: Valentine Vester
headline: Valentine Vester, Jerusalem Hotelier, Is Dead at 96
abstract: Mrs. Vester was a Yorkshire homemaker who went to Jordanian Jerusalem in 1963 to take over a little hotel, the American Colony, and turned it into one of the city’s finest.

name: Gunther Stent
headline: Gunther Stent, an Early Researcher in Molecular Biology, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Dr. Stent was one of the original thinkers in the field of molecular biology whose research wrestled with and validated the breakthrough discovery of the structure of DNA.

name: Tony Schwartz
profession: Father of Daisy Ad for the Johnson Campaign
headline: Tony Schwartz, Father of ‘Daisy Ad’ for the Johnson Campaign, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Schwartz was a self-taught, sought-after and highly reclusive media consultant who helped create what is generally considered to be the most famous political ad to appear on television.

name: Esbjorn Svensson
profession: Leader of the Jazz Group E.S.T
headline: Esbjorn Svensson, Leader of the Jazz Group E.S.T., Dies at 44
abstract: Mr. Svensson was a Swedish pianist and leader of the jazz trio E.S.T., one of Europe’s most popular ensembles.

name: Walter Netsch
headline: Walter Netsch, Architect, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Netsch employed stubbornly individualistic theories to create the ethereal chapel at the United States Air Force Academy.

name: Stan Winston
headline: Stan Winston, 62, Special-Effects Artist, Dies
abstract: The Oscar-winning special-effects artist created the animatronic dinosaurs in “Jurassic Park” and the slimy 14-foot alien queen in “Aliens.”

name: Dennis Weatherstone
headline: Dennis Weatherstone, Banking Sage, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Weatherstone helped usher in a new era of banking during the early 1990s as chairman and chief executive at J. P. Morgan.

name: Cyd Charisse
headline: Cyd Charisse, 86, Silken Dancer of Movies, Dies
abstract: Ms. Charisse came of age in a sparkling era of Hollywood musicals, in which she achieved her lasting renown.

name: Donaldson C. Pillsbury
headline: Donaldson C. Pillsbury, Who Helped Sotheby’s Out of Morass, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Pillsbury was the lawyer who guided Sotheby’s, the auction house, through a welter of legal problems and helped restore its reputation after a price-fixing scandal.

name: Detlef Gromoll
headline: Detlef Gromoll, Known for Math ‘Soul’ Idea, Dies at 70
abstract: Dr. Gromoll was a mathematician who helped lay the foundations for studying the abstract distortions of shapes in three or more dimensions.

name: Tasha Tudor
headline: Tasha Tudor, Children’s Book Illustrator, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Tudor’s pastel watercolors and delicately penciled lines depicted an idyllic, old-fashioned vision of the 19th-century way of life she famously pursued.

name: Bert Shepard
profession: Pitched in Majors After War Amputation
headline: Bert Shepard, 87, Who Pitched in Majors After War Amputation, Dies
abstract: A World War II fighter pilot, Mr. Shepard lost his right leg but went on to pitch for the 1945 Washington Senators.

name: Elly Peterson
headline: Elly Peterson, 94, a Leader of Moderate Republicans, Is Dead
abstract: Mrs. Peterson advocated a big-tent brand of Republicanism that was reflected in her impassioned support for the Equal Rights Amendment.

name: J. Ward Kennedy
headline: J. Ward Kennedy Is Dead at 74; Studied Heart Pumping
abstract: Dr. Kennedy, a cardiologist, made novel studies of the heart’s pumping power and helped evaluate streptokinase, a clot-busting drug widely used to prevent heart attacks.

name: Jean Delannoy
headline: Jean Delannoy, Filmmaker, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Delannoy was a French director of lavish dramas whose career suffered after he was publicly reviled by proponents of the New Wave as the ultimate anti-auteur.

name: Gene Persson
headline: Gene Persson, Film and Theater Producer, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Persson was a movie and theater producer best known for a controversial racial drama, “Dutchman,” and a charming children’s musical, “You’re a Good Man, Charlie Brown.”

name: Michael Shernoff
headline: Michael Shernoff, 57, Gay-Health Therapist, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Shernoff was a psychotherapist who beginning in the early years of the AIDS epidemic wrote widely on its emotional toll on gay men.

name: Hewitt D. Crane
headline: Hewitt D. Crane, 81, Early Computer Engineer, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Crane was instrumental in the design and construction of the first commercial computer to automate checking accounts.

name: Henry Chadwick
headline: Henry Chadwick, Scholar of Early Christianity, Dies at 87
abstract: Professor Chadwick was an Anglican priest, professor, editor, translator and author whose historical voyages into early Christianity won praise for depth, insight and evenhandedness.

name: R. J. Vecoli
headline: R. J. Vecoli, Historian Who Studied Immigrants, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Vecoli was an Italian-American historian who gave a new view of what immigrants kept and left behind.

name: Arthur Galston
headline: Arthur Galston, Agent Orange Researcher, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Galston did early research that helped lead to the herbicide Agent Orange, then helped raise awareness of the military’s use of it in Vietnam.

name: Rudolph J. Vecoli
headline: Rudolph J. Vecoli, Scholar of Immigration, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Vecoli was an Italian-American historian who gave a new view of what immigrants kept and left behind.

name: Dody Goodman
headline: Dody Goodman, 93, Television Actress, Dies
abstract: Miss Goodman combined a dancer’s grace, a strawberry blond mane and exquisitely timed scatter-brained humor to create television legends.

name: Kermit Love
headline: Kermit Love, Costume Creator, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Love was the costume designer for some of ballet’s most renowned choreographers, but his greatest fame came from the beloved “Sesame Street” characters Big Bird and Mr. Snuffleupagus.

name: George Carlin
headline: George Carlin, Comic Who Chafed at Society and Its Constraints, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Carlin used stand-up and Grammy-winning records to take furious and often profane aim at society, its foibles, hypocrisies, and seven words not to be said on television.

name: Richard J. Koke
profession: Visionary Curator of New Yorks History
headline: Richard J. Koke, Visionary Curator of New York’s History, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Koke was a curator of the New-York Historical Society, helping turn it into an institution where visitors come face to face with relics of New York City.

name: Sonny Okosuns
headline: Sonny Okosuns, 61, Musician With Message, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Okosuns, a Nigerian singer and musician, achieved international stature by aiming his music at human rights abuses.

name: Leonid Hurwicz
headline: Leonid Hurwicz, Nobel Economist, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Hurwicz shared the Nobel Prize in economics last year for his work on mechanism design theory, which helps explain the interaction among individuals, markets and institutions.

name: Ira Tucker
headline: Ira Tucker, Gospel Singer Who Gave Dixie Hummingbirds Emotive Edge, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Tucker as lead singer of the Dixie Hummingbirds helped propel gospel music toward a harder-edged, more emotive style.

name: Wilber Hardee
headline: Wilber Hardee Dies at 89; Founded Restaurants
abstract: Mr. Hardee was a farm boy turned grill cook who went on to open the first Hardee’s hamburger stand in 1960, starting a chain that now has nearly 2,000 restaurants.

name: Ed Arno
headline: Ed Arno, Cartoonist of New Yorker Whimsy, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Arno created sketchy, casually rendered cartoons on topics domestic and cosmic that appeared regularly in The New Yorker for more than 30 years.

name: Vic Hershkowitz
headline: Vic Hershkowitz, Dominant Handball Star, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Hershkowitz, a New York City fireman who learned handball on the playgrounds of Brooklyn, was considered by many to be the sport’s most brilliant player.

name: Charles Parkhurst
headline: Charles Parkhurst, Who Tracked Down Looted Art, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Parkhurst was a museum director and one of the “monuments men,” an Allied Forces team that chased down leads in search of art stolen by the Nazis.

name: Leonard Pennario
headline: Leonard Pennario, 83, Classical Pianist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Pennario was a popular classical pianist and a life master in tournament bridge.

name: David Caminer
headline: David Caminer, a Pioneer in Computers, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Caminer, as an employee of a legendary chain of British tea shops, found the earliest ways to use a computer for business purposes.

name: Sam H.F.J. Manekshaw
profession: Key to Indias Victory in 1971 War
headline: Sam H.F.J. Manekshaw Dies at 94; Key to India’s Victory in 1971 War
abstract: Mr. Manekshaw was India’s best-known soldier and the architect of the country’s victory in the 1971 war with Pakistan that gave birth to Bangladesh.

name: Jozef Szajna
profession: Writer of Quiet Protest in Poland
headline: Jozef Szajna, 86, Writer of Quiet Protest in Poland, Dies
abstract: Mr. Szajna was a playwright, set designer and theater director who through often nearly wordless productions evoked the beastliness of humanity and the oppressiveness of dictatorship.

name: Edgar Vincent
headline: Edgar Vincent, 90, Opera Stars’ Publicist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Vincent was a press representative for a starry roster of opera singers, notably as the publicity agent and an adviser to Plácido Domingo for more than 25 years.

name: Kenneth Macke
headline: Kenneth Macke, Who Led Target, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Macke was a former chairman and chief executive of the Dayton Hudson Corporation, the forerunner of the retail giant Target Corporation.

name: Clay Felker
headline: Clay Felker, Magazine Pioneer, Dies at 82
abstract: At New York magazine, Mr. Felker was credited with inventing a widely imitated formula for glossy weeklies.

name: Ruth Cardoso
headline: Ruth Cardoso, Ex-First Lady of Brazil, Dies at 77
abstract: Ruth Vilaça Corrêa Leite Cardoso was a Brazilian anthropologist who carved out a career as one of her country’s most respected intellectuals and feminists.

name: Ronnie Mathews
headline: Ronnie Mathews, 72, Pianist Who Accompanied Jazz Stars, Dies
abstract: Mr. Mathews was a jazz pianist whose recorded output as a leader was sparse but whose résumé as a sideman with stars of jazz was substantial.

name: Irina Baronova
headline: Irina Baronova, Ballet Star, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Baronova was an international ballet star and one of three celebrated prodigies known as the “baby ballerinas” after George Balanchine discovered them in the 1930s.

name: John Pont
headline: John Pont, Who Coached Indiana to Rose Bowl, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Pont was a football-coaching lifer who was best remembered for taking Indiana University to its first bowl game in 1968.

name: R. C. Seamans Jr.
headline: R. C. Seamans Jr., NASA Figure, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Seamans was NASA’s nuts-and-bolts manager of the Apollo moon-landing program, later serving as the first administrator of the federal energy research agency.

name: Victor Remer
headline: Victor Remer, Children’s Aid Society Leader, Dies at 88
abstract: In the 1960s and ’70s, Mr. Remer pushed the agency in grittier, more urgent directions, including addressing the problems of young people convicted of minor crimes.

name: Jules Tygiel
headline: Jules Tygiel, Historian, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Tygiel was a historian and self-confessed baseball nut whose Brooklyn upbringing inspired his highly regarded scholarship on Jackie Robinson.

name: Jesse Helms
headline: Jesse Helms Dies at 86; Conservative Force in the Senate
abstract: The former North Carolina senator had a courtly manner and mossy drawl and turned his hard-edged conservatism against civil rights, gay rights, foreign aid and modern art.

name: Michael Turner
headline: Michael Turner, 37, Creator of Superheroines, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Turner was a popular comic-book artist who came to fame in the mid-1990s and was best known for creating two sexy female lead characters, Witchblade and Fathom.

name: Norman Marcus
headline: Norman Marcus, New York City Zoning Expert, Dies at 75
abstract: As general counsel to the New York City Planning Commission for more than 20 years, Mr. Marcus drafted many of its labyrinthine codes and designations.

name: Thomas Disch
headline: Thomas Disch, Novelist, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Disch twisted the inherently twisted genre of science fiction in new, disturbing directions, including writing his last book in the voice of God.

name: Dorian Leigh
headline: Dorian Leigh, Multifaceted Cover Girl of the ’40s, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Leigh combined pristine blue eyes, curling eyelashes, an arresting intelligence and intoxicating sexuality to become one of history’s most photographed models.

name: Bruce Conner
profession: San Francisco Artist With 1950s Beat Roots
headline: Bruce Conner, San Francisco Artist With 1950s Beat Roots, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Conner, an artist internationally admired for his sculptures and groundbreaking avant-garde films, also was a key figure in the San Francisco Beat scene.

name: Ruth Greenglass
profession: Key Witness in Trial of Rosenbergs
headline: Ruth Greenglass, Key Witness in Trial of Rosenbergs, Dies at 83
abstract: Mrs. Greenglass’s testimony in the Rosenberg spy case of the early 1950s helped lead to the execution of her sister-in-law Ethel Rosenberg.

name: John Templeton
headline: John Templeton, Investor, Dies at 95
abstract: Sir John was an investor who founded the Templeton Prize for “progress in religion” and “research or discoveries.”

name: Warren J. Ferguson
headline: Warren J. Ferguson, Who Declared That N.B.A. Rule Violated Antitrust Laws, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Ferguson was a federal judge whose rulings cleared the way for college undergraduates to jump to the National Basketball Association.

name: John Simon
headline: John Simon, Tireless Editor of Grant’s Papers, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Simon, a Civil War scholar, created a new standard for the organization of historical documents after his mammoth effort in editing the papers of Ulysses S. Grant.

name: John Simon
profession: Wide-Ranging Critic With a Cutting Pen
headline: John Simon, Wide-Ranging Critic With a Cutting Pen, Dies at 94
abstract: Prolific, erudite and caustic in his wit, he surveyed the entire cultural landscape — films, plays, books, art — and saw little that he liked.

name: Ralph Burgard
headline: Ralph Burgard, Advocate for Arts Programs, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Burgard was a leader in the movement to create arts programs in communities around the country.

name: Gerald Tsai
headline: Gerald Tsai, Innovative Investor, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Tsai pioneered the creation of performance funds in the 1950s and ’60s and later turned a canning company into the financial services giant Primerica.

name: Bobby Durham
headline: Bobby Durham, 71, Drummer Who Played With Jazz Greats, Dies
abstract: Mr. Durham’s precise, understated style made him much sought after as a sideman, and he was probably best known for his trio work with Oscar Peterson and Ray Brown.

name: Sherman Lee
headline: Sherman Lee, Who Led Cleveland Museum, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Lee was an expert on Asian art who as director of the Cleveland Museum of Art for a quarter of a century elevated it to the top echelon of American museums.

name: Mike Souchak
headline: Mike Souchak, 81, Touring Pro Who Held PGA Scoring Record, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Souchak was a leading pro golfer of the 1950s and early ’60s who set a PGA Tour record for the lowest 72-hole score in 1955 that stood for 46 years.

name: Evelyn Keyes
profession: Film Roles Included Gone With the Wind
headline: Evelyn Keyes, 91, Whose Film Roles Included ‘Gone With the Wind,’ Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Keyes played the pouty Suellen O’Hara, whose sister Scarlett steals her longtime boyfriend and marries him just to pay the taxes on the plantation, in the Academy Award-winning 1939 movie classic.

name: Rocky Aoki
headline: Rocky Aoki, Who Created Benihana Chain, Is Dead at 69
abstract: Mr. Aoki founded the theatrical Benihana chain of steakhouses, where Japanese chefs with flashing knives double as performers.

name: Tony Snow
headline: Tony Snow, Former Bush Spokesman, Dies at 53
abstract: The conservative columnist and commentator relished sparring with reporters as White House press secretary.

name: Bobby Murcer
profession: Yankee Mainstay on Field and in the Broadcast Booth
headline: Bobby Murcer, 62, Yankee Mainstay on Field and in the Broadcast Booth, Dies
abstract: Murcer, who played 17 seasons in the majors, was a fan favorite in New York and a longtime Yankees broadcaster.

name: Michael E. DeBakey
headline: Dr. Michael E. DeBakey, Rebuilder of Hearts, Dies at 99
abstract: Dr. DeBakey’s innovative heart and blood vessel operations made him one of America’s most influential doctors.

name: David H. Greene
headline: David H. Greene, Scholar of Irish Literature, Dies at 94
abstract: Professor Greene was a leading scholar of Irish literature and a biographer of the playwright J. M. Synge.

name: Arthur Weinstein
headline: Arthur Weinstein, Starter of Nightclubs, Dies at 60
abstract: In the glittery, manic, often ostentatiously naughty 1970s and ’80s, Mr. Weinstein was king of the night.

name: Bronislaw Geremek
profession: Helped End Communist Control of Poland
headline: Bronislaw Geremek, Who Helped End Communist Control of Poland, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Mr. Geremek was a pivotal figure in the fight to end Communist rule in Poland and one of the leading statesmen of the democratic era that followed.

name: Clem McSpadden
headline: Clem McSpadden, 82, Voice of Pro Rodeo, Dies
abstract: Mr. McSpadden was known as the voice of professional rodeo, his Oklahoma intonations a familiar presence through six decades.

name: Les Crane
headline: Les Crane, Talk-Show Host, Dies at 74
abstract: Personable, cocky and well-attuned to the tenor of the times, Mr. Crane was the first to challenge the primacy of Johnny Carson on late-night television — and lose.

name: Charles H. Joffe
headline: Charles H. Joffe, Movie Producer, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Joffe was a co-producer of Woody Allen’s movies and the business expert in the talent agency that managed the careers of a host of high-profile comedians.

name: Archie McCardell
headline: Archie McCardell, Harvester Chief Who Clashed With Union, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. McCardell’s gruff, bottom-line approach as the chief of International Harvester in the late 1970s drew praise from Wall Street but the enmity of labor.

name: William T. Sanders
headline: William T. Sanders, 82, Anthropologist, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Sanders was an anthropologist whose studies of Mexico and Central America included an invaluable aerial survey of ancient archaeological sites.

name: George Hartzog
headline: George Hartzog, Parks Chief, Dies at 88
abstract: As the director of the National Park Service in the 1960s and early ’70s, Mr. Hartzog’s political skills led to the addition of nearly 50 million acres to the park system.

name: Roy M. Huffington
headline: Roy M. Huffington, Independent Oilman, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Huffington was an independent oilman who defied industry precedent by signing an unusually generous deal with Indonesia and made a fortune on natural gas there.

name: Joseph McCrindle
headline: Joseph McCrindle, 85, Connoisseur of Art, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. McCrindle was an art collector who amassed a trove of old master drawings and who founded and edited the Transatlantic Review to showcase young writers.

name: Wistful Singer
headline: Wistful Singer, Jo Stafford, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Ms. Stafford was the wistful singing voice of the American home front during World War II and the Korean War.

name: Paul Byard
headline: Paul Byard, 68, Dies; Architect Renovated Landmarks
abstract: Mr. Byard, a land-use lawyer who returned to school in his late 30s to be an architect, became an important figure in the renovation of some of New York’s most prominent landmarks.

name: Robert Lewis Shayon
headline: Robert Lewis Shayon, 95, Is Dead; Elevated Radio
abstract: Mr. Shayon wrote and produced groundbreaking radio programs in the 1940s and later became a longtime television critic for The Saturday Review.

name: Michael Gregg
headline: Michael Gregg, 78, Editor of U.S. Medical Bulletin, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Gregg was an epidemiologist and former editor of the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report, a federal medical bulletin that published early warnings of the impending AIDS crisis in 1981.

name: Jo Stafford
headline: Jo Stafford, Wistful Voice of WWII Era, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Stafford was the singing voice of the American home front during World War II and the Korean War.

name: Sherman L. Maxwell
headline: Sherman L. Maxwell, 100, Sportscaster and Writer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Maxwell was a chronicler of Negro league baseball and, some believe, the first black sports broadcaster.

name: Anatoly I. Pristavkin
headline: Anatoly I. Pristavkin, 76, Russian Writer, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Pristavkin’s experience as a Russian orphan during World War II showed in the suffering of the children in his novels and in the toughness of his opposition to the Soviet authorities.

name: Joseph E. Fields
headline: Joseph E. Fields, Conductor, Composer and Pianist, Is Dead at 53
abstract: The former music director and principal conductor of Dance Theater of Harlem was noted for his arrangements of the 2003 premiere of “St. Louis Woman.”

name: Lyall Watson
profession: Adventurer and Explorer of the Soft Edges of Science
headline: Lyall Watson, 69, Adventurer and Explorer of the ‘Soft Edges of Science,’ Dies
abstract: Mr. Watson was a maverick scientific polymath and explorer who wrote the best-selling book “Supernature” and introduced the “hundredth monkey” theory.

name: Jacques Kaplan
headline: Jacques Kaplan, 83, Bold Furrier, Dies
abstract: Mr. Kaplan was an absurdist furrier and art gallery owner who brought a sense of mischief to the staid world of the mink stole.

name: Gladys Nederlander
headline: Gladys Nederlander, 83, Show Producer, Is Dead
abstract: Mrs. Nederlander was a producer of nine Broadway shows between 1976 and 1993, most notably of a revival of “West Side Story” in 1980.

name: Artie Traum
headline: Artie Traum, 65, Stalwart of ’60s Folk Music Scene, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Traum was a guitarist, songwriter and producer who helped carry the spirit of the 1960s Greenwich Village folk scene to Woodstock, N.Y.

name: Jerome Holtzman
headline: Jerome Holtzman, 82, ‘Dean’ of Sportswriters, Dies
abstract: The Chicago sportswriter and columnist and the author of “No Cheering in the Press Box” was a venerated presence in press boxes around the country.

name: Dinko Sakic
headline: Dinko Sakic, Who Led WWII Death Camp, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Sakic was found guilty of killing more than 2,000 Serbs, Jews and Gypsies at the concentration camp named Jasenovac.

name: Estelle Getty
headline: Estelle Getty, ‘Golden Girls’ Matriarch, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Getty’s portrayal of a crabbily charming octogenarian on the television sitcom “The Golden Girls” gave new prominence to elderly characters in prime time.

name: Victor McKusick
headline: Victor McKusick, 86, Dies; Medical Genetics Pioneer
abstract: Dr. McKusick was a cardiologist who went on to become a founder of medical genetics and helped make the discipline a central part of medicine.

name: Sidney Craig
headline: Sidney Craig, 76, a Founder of Jenny Craig, Dies
abstract: Craig, with his wife, Genevieve, founded Jenny Craig Inc., a successful weight-loss chain operating 600 centers in four countries.

name: Charles Wick
headline: Charles Wick, 90, Information Agency Head, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Wick was the longest-serving director of the United States Information Agency.

name: Eleanor Friede
headline: Eleanor Friede, 87, Is Dead; Edited 1970 Fable ‘Seagull’
abstract: Ms. Friede was the book editor who sent “Jonathan Livingston Seagull” on its nonstop flight to publishing glory in 1970.

name: Howard L. Bachrach
headline: Howard L. Bachrach, 88, Early Polio Researcher, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Bachrach was a biochemist who helped produce an early vaccine to prevent foot-and-mouth disease in livestock and did important early research on the polio virus.

name: Richard Wade
headline: Richard Wade, 87, Urban Historian, Dies
abstract: Dr. Wade helped put cities on the map as an academic subject and advised Democratic candidates including Adlai Stevenson, Robert F. Kennedy and George McGovern.

name: Barbara Ann Teer
headline: Barbara Ann Teer, 71, Dies; Promoted Black Arts
abstract: Ms. Teer, who founded the National Black Theater, gave up a promising career in commercial entertainment to concentrate on developing African-American culture in Harlem.

name: Eugene A. Foster
headline: Eugene A. Foster, 81, Dies; Linked Jefferson to Slave
abstract: Dr. Foster, a pathologist, helped establish genetically the long-alleged liaison between Thomas Jefferson and his slave mistress Sally Hemings.

name: Paul Bentley
headline: Paul Bentley, 87, Dies; Detective Arrested Oswald
abstract: Detective Bentley was a Dallas police detective who helped arrest Lee Harvey Oswald 80 minutes after the assassination of President John F. Kennedy.

name: Johnny Griffin
headline: Johnny Griffin, 80, Jazz Saxophonist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Griffin was a jazz tenor-saxophonist from Chicago whose speed, control and harmonic acuity made him one of the most talented musicians of his generation.

name: Randy Pausch
profession: His Last Lecture Inspired Many to Live With Wonder
headline: Randy Pausch, 47, Dies; His ‘Last Lecture’ Inspired Many to Live With Wonder
abstract: Dr. Pausch was the Carnegie Mellon University professor whose “last lecture” made him a Lou-Gehrig-like symbol of the beauty and briefness of life.

name: Kathleen Kinkade
headline: Kathleen Kinkade, Founder of Utopian Commune, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Ms. Kinkade was one of the founders of an experimental community near Charlottesville, Va., that was inspired by the behaviorist ideas of B. F. Skinner.

name: Charles L. Brieant Jr.
headline: Charles L. Brieant Jr., Longtime Federal Judge, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Brieant, a former chief judge of the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, presided over a raft of controversial cases.

name: Norman Dello Joio
headline: Norman Dello Joio, Prolific and Popular Composer, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Mr. Dello Joio achieved wide popularity in the mid-20th century by composing a proliferation of essentially tonal, lyrical works.

name: Youssef Chahine
headline: Youssef Chahine, Egyptian Filmmaker, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Chahine was an Egyptian filmmaker who was a pre-eminent figure in Arab cinema.

name: Donald Stokes
headline: Donald Stokes, 94, Auto Tycoon, Dies
abstract: Mr. Stokes was at the heart of the rise and fall of Britain’s automotive industry in the 1960s as chairman of the British Leyland Motor Corporation.

name: Larry Haines
headline: Larry Haines, a Star of ‘Search for Tomorrow’, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Haines was a successful Broadway actor who for 35 years played Stu Bergman, one of the convivial neighbors on “Search for Tomorrow.”

name: Brooks Jones
headline: Brooks Jones, Father of Summerfare, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Mr. Jones was a producer and director who rejected Broadway to devote himself to regional theater, including starting and directing Pepsico Summerfare.

name: Bruce Adler
headline: Bruce Adler, Actor With Yiddish Roots, Is Dead at 63
abstract: Mr. Adler was an actor and song-and-dance man with roots in the Yiddish theater who hoofed successfully onto Broadway and was nominated for two Tony Awards.

name: Michael Berniker
headline: Michael Berniker, 73, Record Producer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Berniker was a prolific record producer whose diverse projects won nine Grammy Awards over four decades.

name: Jamiel A. Chagra
headline: Jamiel A. Chagra, 63, Drug Kingpin, Dies
abstract: Mr. Chagra was an El Paso drug dealer and gambler who was accused but never convicted of masterminding the assassination of a federal judge in 1979.

name: J. Murdoch Ritchie
headline: J. Murdoch Ritchie, 83, Yale Biophysicist, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Ritchie was a biophysicist at Yale who used a potent neurotoxin derived from shellfish to help trace the way nerve cells conduct electrical impulses.

name: Michael Daly
headline: Michael Daly, 83, Dies; Won Medal of Honor
abstract: Mr. Daly was awarded the Medal of Honor for his single-handed offensive against German troops during the battle for Nuremberg in World War II.

name: Stuart W. Little
headline: Stuart W. Little, Writer of Theater, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Little’s many newspaper articles and books chronicled developments in the theater from the 1950s to the ’70s.

name: Julius B. Richmond
profession: Led Head Start and Battled Tobacco
headline: Dr. Julius B. Richmond, Who Led Head Start and Battled Tobacco, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Richmond was the first national director of Project Head Start and later as surgeon general was a fierce adversary of the tobacco industry.

name: Otto Fuerbringer
headline: Otto Fuerbringer, Former Time Editor, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Fuerbringer was the hard-driving, conservative-leaning managing editor of Time magazine during the political and social upheavals of the 1960s.

name: Daniel Bukantz
headline: Daniel Bukantz, Champion Fencer, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Bukantz was a national champion and Olympic fencer and a longtime Olympic fencing referee while pursuing a career in dentistry.

name: Clay T. Whitehead
headline: Clay T. Whitehead, Guide of Policy That Helped Cable TV, Is Dead at 69
abstract: Mr. Whitehead laid the groundwork for Open Skies, the policy that led to the creation of the domestic satellite system that brought cable television into millions of American homes.

name: Anne Armstrong
headline: Anne Armstrong, Presidential Adviser and Pioneering Politician, Dies at 80
abstract: Mrs. Armstrong advised Presidents Richard M. Nixon and Gerald R. Ford and was the first woman to serve as the U.S. ambassador to Britain.

name: Hiram Bullock
headline: Hiram Bullock, 52, Soulful Guitarist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Bullock was an adaptable jazz and rock guitarist who was a member of the original band for “Late Night with David Letterman.”

name: Eileen G. Slocum
headline: Eileen G. Slocum, 92, Dies; Society Doyenne and Republican Stalwart
abstract: Mrs. Slocum was a doyenne of Newport, R.I., society and a stalwart of the Republican Party in Rhode Island and nationally.

name: H. Tracy Hall
headline: H. Tracy Hall, a Maker of Diamonds, Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Hall was an inventor who in 1954 was a key part of a pioneering scientific team at General Electric that made the first synthetic diamonds.

name: Jack Nash
headline: Jack Nash, Pioneer in Hedge Funds, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Nash was a former chairman of Oppenheimer & Company who helped pioneer the modern hedge fund business.

name: Luther Davis
headline: Luther Davis, 91, Writer of Musicals and Movies, Dies
abstract: Mr. Davis was a playwright who won a Tony Award in 1954 for the book of the musical “Kismet” and a screenwriter whose films included “The Hucksters” and “Lady in a Cage.”

name: Martin Gradel
headline: Martin Gradel, a Times Editor, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Gradel was a deputy news editor of The New York Times who also worked at The San Jose Mercury News and The Dallas Times Herald.

name: Stanley E. Michels
headline: Stanley E. Michels, Longtime Councilman, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Michels was a former New York City councilman who was an advocate of environmental protection laws.

name: Pierre Berès
headline: Pierre Berès, Tenacious Book Collector, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Berès was renowned for his taste and connoisseurship, his vast financial resources and his ruthlessness in the pursuit of the rare and the beautiful.

name: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn
headline: Solzhenitsyn, Literary Giant Who Defied Soviets, Dies at 89
abstract: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn’s stubborn, lonely and combative literary struggles revealed the afflictions of Soviet Communism.

name: David H. Popper
headline: David H. Popper, Ex-Envoy, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Popper was a seasoned United States diplomat who, as ambassador to Chile in the tense early years of Gen. Augusto Pinochet’s government, struggled to balance military and human rights concern.

name: Skip Caray
profession: Atlanta Braves Voice Known for His Biting Wit
headline: Skip Caray, 68, Atlanta Braves Voice Known for His Biting Wit, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Caray’s nasal tone and sometimes playful, sometimes sardonic commentary on radio and television made him familiar to baseball fans.

name: Peter Rodman
headline: Peter Rodman, Foreign Affairs Expert, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Rodman served every Republican president from Richard M. Nixon to George W. Bush, including as an assistant secretary of defense for nearly six years in the current administration.

name: Lou Teicher
headline: Lou Teicher, of Ferrante & Teicher, Popular Piano Duo of ’60s, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Teicher’s florid and sentimental versions of movie themes and love songs made the duo gods of easy listening and earned them wide popularity.

name: Nicola Rescigno
profession: Helped Found Opera Companies in Chicago and Dallas
headline: Nicola Rescigno, Who Helped Found Opera Companies in Chicago and Dallas, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Rescigno seized advantage of a new interest in opera after World War II and helped found two major American opera companies.

name: Robert Maheu
headline: Robert Maheu, 90, Surrogate for Howard Hughes, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Maheu was a chief aide to Howard Hughes, and engineered the deals for the Hughes business empire that helped change the face of Las Vegas. He never once met his boss.

name: Andrea Pininfarina
headline: Andrea Pininfarina, Chief of Car Designer, Dies at 51
abstract: Mr. Pininfarina was the chairman and chief executive of the Italian company founded by his family that designs Ferraris and other cars.

name: Erik Darling
headline: Erik Darling Dies at 74; Musician in the Weavers
abstract: Mr. Darling replaced Pete Seeger in the Weavers and was associated with two of folk music’s biggest commercial hits, “The Banana Boat Song” and “Walk Right In.”

name: Peter Kass
headline: Peter Kass, 85, Bold Teacher of Acting, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Kass was a theater actor and director whose influence as a teacher was felt in several generations of performers.

name: Simon Gray
profession: Aimed Wit at Intellectuals, and Himself
headline: Simon Gray, Playwright, Dies at 71; Aimed Wit at Intellectuals, and Himself
abstract: Mr. Gray wrote bitingly comic plays like “Butley” and “Otherwise Engaged” about the educated British middle class and manically confessional late-in-life memoirs.

name: Bernie Brillstein
headline: Bernie Brillstein, Film Producer, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Brillstein was a Hollywood manager and producer who contributed to series like “Saturday Night Live” and “The Muppet Show.”

name: Bernie Mac
headline: Bernie Mac, Comic From TV and Film, Is Dead at 50
abstract: Mr. Mac, an imposing stage presence with a line of scabrous insults, parlayed his success as a stand-up comedian into film roles.

name: Lee Young
headline: Lee Young Dies at 94; Jazz Man and Producer
abstract: Mr. Young, from a family with musical roots deep in New Orleans jazz, drummed for greats like Ellington and Basie and became a pioneering black man in music’s executive suite.

name: Mahmoud Darwish
headline: Mahmoud Darwish, Leading Palestinian Poet, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Mr. Darwish’s prose gave voice to the Palestinian experience of exile, occupation and infighting.

name: Isaac Hayes
headline: Isaac Hayes, 65, a Creator of ’70s Soul Style, Dies
abstract: Mr. Hayes’s strutting funk arrangements in songs like “Theme From ‘Shaft’ ” defined the glories and the excesses of soul music.

name: Orville Moody
headline: Orville Moody, 74, Winner of the U.S. Open, Dies
abstract: Mr. Moody, known as Sarge, emerged from obscurity to win the 1969 United States Open, his only PGA Tour victory.

name: Geoffrey Ballard
headline: Geoffrey Ballard, 75, Fuel-Cell Pioneer Who Created Bus Powered by Hydrogen, Dies
abstract: The Canadian entrepreneur’s company became a bellwether in the use of hydrogen fuel cells to power cars and other vehicles.

name: George Furth
headline: George Furth, an Actor and Playwright, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Furth was a playwright who collaborated on the Tony Award-winning musical “Company” and a character actor whose distinct profile enlivened dozens of popular television series.

name: Theodore Solotaroff
profession: Founder of The New American Review
headline: Theodore Solotaroff, Founder of The New American Review, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Mr. Solotaroff started The New American Review in 1967 as a highly unusual showcase for a rising generation of writers.

name: Bertrand Castelli
profession: Bon Vivant and an Early Producer of Hair
headline: Bertrand Castelli, Bon Vivant and an Early Producer of ‘Hair,’ Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Castelli was a painter, a screenwriter, a balletomane and a choreographer as well as a producer.

name: Alexander Slobodyanik
headline: Alexander Slobodyanik, Pianist, Is Dead at 65
abstract: Mr. Slobodyanik was a Ukrainian-born pianist who earned stardom in the former Soviet Union with his virtuosity and emotional interpretations of Romantic composers.

name: L. Rust Hills
headline: L. Rust Hills, Fiction Editor at Esquire, Dies at 83
abstract: As Esquire’s curmudgeonly fiction editor, Mr. Hills published original works by scores of the country’s finest writers.

name: Eleo Pomare
headline: Eleo Pomare, Dancer and Rebel, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Pomare was a modern-dance choreographer whose mordant wit filtered through his angry social-protest pieces about the human condition and the plight of blacks in particular.

name: Jack A. Weil
headline: Jack A. Weil, the Cowboy’s Dresser, Dies at 107
abstract: Mr. Weil, a king of cowboy couture, was almost certainly the first to put snaps on Western shirts, and most likely the first to produce bolo ties commercially.

name: Jerry Wexler
headline: Jerry Wexler, a Behind-the-Scenes Force in Black Music, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Wexler christened black popular music with the name rhythm and blues and became a record producer who helped lead the genre to popularity.

name: Donald Erb
headline: Donald Erb, Composer of Early Electronic Music, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Erb, a distinguished professor emeritus of composition at the Cleveland Institute of Music, was prominent on the avant-garde scene of the 1960s and ’70s.

name: C. Lester Hogan
headline: C. Lester Hogan, Physicist Who Fought Motorola, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Hogan’s departure from his job in 1968 as a top executive at Motorola to one at Fairchild led to a celebrated lawsuit.

name: Dottie Collins
profession: Star Pitcher of Womens Baseball League
headline: Dottie Collins, 84, Star Pitcher of Women’s Baseball League, Dies
abstract: Ms. Collins was a star pitcher in women’s professional baseball in the 1940s and later played a major role in preserving the history of the women’s game.

name: Don Helms
profession: Put the Twang in the Hank Williams Songbook
headline: Don Helms, 81, Who Put the Twang in the Hank Williams Songbook, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Helms, whose piercing, forceful steel guitar helped define the sound of nearly all of Hank Williams’s hits, also performed and recorded with a long list of other country greats.

name: Robert N. Beck
profession: Leader in Advancing Scanning for Medical Diagnoses
headline: Robert N. Beck, 80, Leader in Advancing Scanning for Medical Diagnoses, Dies
abstract: Mr. Beck, who had studied mathematics and physics, did incisive early work on using radioactive materials for medical imaging.

name: Dorival Caymmi
headline: Dorival Caymmi, Singer of Brazil, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Mr. Caymmi, a Brazilian singer and songwriter, helped lay the foundations of bossa nova.

name: Leroy Sievers
headline: Leroy Sievers, 53, Journalist Who Wrote of Cancer Battle, Dies
abstract: Mr. Sievers was a television news producer who covered more than a dozen wars but became best known to the public as he chronicled his illness for NPR in a blog called “My Cancer.”

name: Manny Farber
headline: Manny Farber, Iconoclastic Film Critic and Artist, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Farber was a painter whose spiky, impassioned film criticism waged war against sacred cows like Orson Welles.

name: Levy Mwanawasa
headline: Levy Mwanawasa, Zambia President, Dies at 59
abstract: In Zambia, Mr. Mwanawasa may best be remembered as a crusader against corruption.

name: Jack C. Landau
profession: Fought for Rights of News Reporters
headline: Jack C. Landau, Who Fought for Rights of News Reporters, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Mr. Landau called himself a “First Amendment guerrilla,” and used his education as a lawyer in advocacy for journalists around the country.

name: Hua Guofeng
profession: Transitional Leader of China After Mao
headline: Hua Guofeng, Transitional Leader of China After Mao, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Hua helped steer China out of the chaos of the Cultural Revolution after Mao’s death in 1976, but he was later pushed aside by Deng Xiaoping.

name: Ronnie Drew
headline: Ronnie Drew, Folk Singer and Guitarist Who Founded the Dubliners, Dies at 73
abstract: Known for his distinctive long white beard and deep voice, Mr. Drew also sang with the Pogues and other rock bands.

name: Stephanie Tubbs Jones
headline: Stephanie Tubbs Jones, Lawmaker, Dies at 58
abstract: Ms. Tubbs Jones was the first African-American woman elected to the House from Ohio.

name: George Deem
headline: George Deem Dies at 75; Painted His Love: Art
abstract: Mr. Deem admired master painters so much that he spent his own career repainting their works, albeit with clever alterations.

name: LeRoi Moore
headline: LeRoi Moore, 46, Saxophone Player, Dies
abstract: Mr. Moore’s fevered riffs embroidered the distinctive music of the Dave Matthews Band with florets of jazz and funk.

name: Gene Upshaw
headline: Gene Upshaw, N.F.L. Union Chief, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Upshaw was the longtime head of the N.F.L. players association and a member of the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

name: Wolfgang Vogel
headline: Wolfgang Vogel, Negotiator in Spy Swaps, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Vogel became a wealthy man in the cold war by opening cracks in the Berlin Wall to swap captured spies and release political prisoners.

name: Ralph D. Feigin
headline: Ralph D. Feigin, 70, Children’s Diseases Book Editor, Dies
abstract: Dr. Feigin’s two-volume work, “Textbook of Pediatric Infectious Diseases,” is intended to aid diagnosticians and remains the standard in its field.

name: Buddy Harman
headline: Buddy Harman, 79, Busy Nashville Drummer, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Harman’s rhythmic signature can be heard on thousands of recordings by the likes of Elvis Presley, Johnny Cash, Patsy Cline and Simon and Garfunkel.

name: Leopoldo Serran
headline: Leopoldo Serran, 66, Screenwriter Known for ‘Dona Flor,’ Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Serran was a leading figure in the Brazilian movement Cinema Novo, and worked with the directors Carlos Diegues and Bruno Barreto.

name: Hugh R. Butt
headline: Hugh R. Butt, 98, Doctor Whose Studies Helped With Blood Problems, Dies
abstract: Dr. Butt showed that vitamin K could be highly effective in halting internal bleeding and that it could be used to reduce deaths markedly among patients with jaundice.

name: John Russell
headline: John Russell, Art Critic for The Times, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Russell contributed elegant, erudite art criticism for more than a half century to The Sunday Times of London and The New York Times.

name: Henri Cartan
headline: Henri Cartan, French Mathematician, Is Dead at 104
abstract: Mr. Cartan was known for meticulous proofs and for inspiring a revival of mathematics in France after World War II.

name: Laurence Urdang
headline: Laurence Urdang, Language Expert Who Edited Dictionaries, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Urdang was a prolific lexicographer who had a hand in more than 100 dictionaries and other reference books.

name: Ralph Young
headline: Ralph Young, Sandler & Young Singer, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Young was a singer best known as the English-language half of the popular multilingual duo Sandler & Young.

name: Tad Mosel
headline: Tad Mosel, TV Dramatist, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Mosel’s dramatic scripts for live television were regularly featured in prime-time programming in the 1950s, and his play “All the Way Home” won the Pulitzer Prize for drama in 1961.

name: Jerry Ford
headline: Jerry Ford, 83, Man Behind the Models, Dies
abstract: Mr. Ford, with his wife, Eileen, established one of the most recognizable modeling agencies in the world.

name: Riitta Immonen
headline: Riitta Immonen, Clothing Designer, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Immonen was a founder of the Finnish textile and clothing company Marimekko, and a designer of uniforms and ready to wear with a couture touch.

name: Kevin Duckworth
headline: Kevin Duckworth, 44, Former N.B.A. All-Star Center, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Duckworth was a two-time National Basketball Association All-Star who played most of his career for the Portland Trail Blazers.

name: Thomas H. Weller
profession: Work on Tissue Led to Nobel Prize
headline: Thomas H. Weller, Whose Work on Tissue Led to Nobel Prize, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Dr. Weller was a tropical-medicine specialist whose tissue-culture research in 1949 made development of the Salk and Sabin polio vaccines possible.

name: Jabir Herbert Muhammad
headline: Jabir Herbert Muhammad, Who Managed Muhammad Ali, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Muhammad became Muhammad Ali’s boxing manager after Ali’s conversion to Islam and negotiated his multimillion-dollar fights.

name: Del Martin
headline: Del Martin, Lesbian Activist, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Martin helped found the pioneering lesbian-rights group the Daughters of Bilitis.

name: Yuri Nosenko
headline: Yuri Nosenko, Soviet Spy Who Defected, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Nosenko was a former Soviet agent who was at the center of some of the most dramatic espionage episodes of the cold war.

name: Robert Bass
headline: Robert Bass, Director of the Collegiate Chorale, Dies at 55
abstract: Mr. Bass was the longtime music director and conductor of the Collegiate Chorale, a New York group whose performances and recordings have earned it international recognition.

name: Michael Baxandall
headline: Michael Baxandall, Pioneering Art Historian, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Baxandall’s analysis of the social forces shaping works of art and the way they were seen helped pave the way for the influential movement known as the new art history.

name: Abie Nathan
headline: Abie Nathan, Israeli Peace Champion, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Nathan is best remembered for his quirky quest for peace in a 30-year campaign waged through a series of audacious escapades by land, air and sea.

name: Phil Hill
profession: Racing Legend at Odds With the Sport at Times
headline: Phil Hill, a Racing Legend at Odds With the Sport at Times, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Hill was one of the greatest of American auto racers, an introspective and cerebral champion who led a celebrated driving career.

name: Barbara Warren
headline: Barbara Warren, Winner of Endurance Competitions, Dies at 65
abstract: Ms. Warren won the Ironman Triathlon World Championship at the age of 60, ran a seven-day race across the Sahara and was tested in many other grueling competitions.

name: Jeannette Eyerly
headline: Jeannette Eyerly, Writer for Teenage Girls, Dies at 100
abstract: Ms. Eyerly was one of the first writers for young adults to deal with themes like unwanted pregnancy, alcoholism and drugs.

name: Killer Kowalski
headline: Killer Kowalski, Wrestler, Dies at 81
abstract: Killer Kowalski was one of pro wrestling’s biggest stars and most heinous villains in the early years of television.

name: Harry L. Kozol
headline: Harry L. Kozol, Expert in Patty Hearst Trial, Is Dead at 102
abstract: Dr. Kozol, one of the country’s premier experts in brain disorders, helped establish the emerging fields of forensic psychiatry and neuropsychiatry.

name: Ahmed Faraz
headline: Ahmed Faraz, Outspoken Urdu Poet, Dies at 77
abstract: Popular among both the cognoscenti and the general public, Mr. Faraz was one of the few poets from the subcontinent whose verses were read as well as sung.

name: Edwin O. Guthman
headline: Edwin O. Guthman, 89, Editor, Dies
abstract: Mr. Guthman was a Pulitzer Prize-winning newspaper reporter and editor and an aide to Attorney General Robert F. Kennedy during the civil rights struggles of the early 1960s.

name: Ike Pappas
profession: Newsman With a Long Career at CBS
headline: Ike Pappas, a Newsman With a Long Career at CBS, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Pappas covered the Vietnam War and the assassination of the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., but is best remembered for being an arm’s length from Lee Harvey Oswald when he was killed.

name: Thomas Bata
headline: Thomas Bata, ‘Shoemaker to the World,’ Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Bata made the company founded by his father so pervasive that it became a generic noun for shoe in some parts of the developing world, particularly in Africa.

name: K. K. Birla
headline: K. K. Birla, a Leader of Indian Business, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Birla established one of India’s biggest business conglomerates, with interests in industries like sugar, fertilizers, chemicals, heavy engineering, and many others.

name: Calvin L. Beale
profession: Demographer With a Feel for Rural America
headline: Calvin L. Beale, Demographer With a Feel for Rural America, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Beale was among the first to recognize the transformation of America’s rural landscape from farms to a mixture of farms, industry and vacation homes.

name: Jerry Reed
headline: Jerry Reed, Country Singer and Actor, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Reed was a popular country singer and movie actor whose larger-than-life storytelling and flashy guitar work vividly evoked Southern life.

name: Don LaFontaine
profession: Voice of Trailers and TV Spots
headline: Don LaFontaine, Voice of Trailers and TV Spots, Is Dead at 68
abstract: Mr. LaFontaine brought his melodramatic baritone to so many movie trailers, commercials and television promos that he became known in the industry as “the voice of God.”

name: Tommy Bolt
headline: Tommy Bolt, a Top Golfer Who Was Known Better for His Temper, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Bolt was a golfer whose swing helped him win the 1958 United States Open but whose success was overshadowed by his reputation for throwing tantrums.

name: Sheldon Keller
headline: Sheldon Keller, TV Comedy Writer, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Keller was an Emmy-winning comedy writer whose work included “Caesar’s Hour,” one of the jewels of 1950s television.

name: Muriel Kallis Steinberg Newman
profession: Donor of Abstract Expressionist Works to the Met
headline: Muriel Kallis Steinberg Newman, Donor of Abstract Expressionist Works to the Met, Dies at 94
abstract: Mrs. Newman’s donation of artworks greatly bolstered the Metropolitan Museum of Art’s standing as an exhibitor of modern art.

name: Michael Hammer
headline: Michael Hammer, Business Writer, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Hammer was the co-author of a best-selling book, “Reengineering the Corporation,” that some say influenced the way many corporations reorganized their workplaces.

name: Bill Melendez
headline: Bill Melendez, ‘Peanuts’ Animator, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Melendez was an Emmy-winning animator who brought Charlie Brown and the “Peanuts” gang to blithe, blockheaded life on television and in films.

name: Mila Schön
headline: Mila Schön, 91, a Pioneer of High-End Ready-to-Wear, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Schön’s understated designs and precisely tailored clothes made her a stalwart of Italian haute couture beginning in the 1960s and a leader in high-end ready-to-wear.

name: Breno Mello
headline: Breno Mello, 76, Star of ‘Orpheus,’ Dies
abstract: Mr. Mello was known for his title role in the classic 1959 Brazilian movie “Black Orpheus,” based on the Greek myth of Orpheus and Eurydice, but set amid the frenzy of Rio’s carnival.

name: Robert Giroux
headline: Robert Giroux, Editor, Publisher and Nurturer of Literary Giants, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Mr. Giroux introduced and nurtured some of the major authors of the 20th century and ultimately added his name to one of the nation’s most distinguished publishing houses.

name: Paul Curran
headline: Paul Curran, Who Fought Corruption in New York, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Curran pursued mobsters, corrupt officials, crooked businessmen and other malefactors as the state investigation commissioner and as the top federal prosecutor in Manhattan.

name: Ralph Kovel
headline: Ralph Kovel, Antiques Writer, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Kovel was a nationally known writer on antiques, who for more than half a century put prices on the stuff of life, from baseball cards to bottle caps to Barbie’s lucrative girdles.

name: Joey Giardello
headline: Joey Giardello, Middleweight Champion, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Giardello fought for nearly two decades but was also known for a legal dispute involving the movie depiction of his title fight with Rubin (Hurricane) Carter.

name: Don Haskins
headline: Don Haskins, Barrier-Breaking Coach, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Haskins was the first man to start five black players in an N.C.A.A. championship.

name: Anita Page
headline: Anita Page, Silent-Film Siren, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Page was one of the last surviving stars of the silent screen.

name: Helen Galland
headline: Helen Galland, Former President of Bonwit Teller, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Galland began her career as a sales assistant at Lord & Taylor and became one of the few women of her time to run a fashion-oriented retailer as president of Bonwit Teller.

name: T. Norbu
headline: T. Norbu, Dalai Lama’s Brother, Dies at 86
abstract: Thubten J. Norbu was the eldest brother of the Dalai Lama and was also regarded as a reincarnated saint.

name: Edgardo Vega Yunqué
profession: Novelist of the Puerto Rican Experience in New York
headline: Edgardo Vega Yunqué, Novelist of the Puerto Rican Experience in New York, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Vega Yunqué's novels and stories about life on the Lower East Side of Manhattan were picaresque, combustive and sometimes flamboyantly comic expressions of the Puerto Rican experience.

name: Alain Jacquet
profession: Pop Artist Known for Playful Renditions
headline: Alain Jacquet, Pop Artist Known for Playful Renditions, Is Dead at 69
abstract: Mr. Jacquet was a French artist known for his playful modernizations of old master paintings.

name: Don Gutteridge
profession: Player for Famed St. Louis Teams
headline: Don Gutteridge, 96, Player for Famed St. Louis Teams, Is Dead
abstract: Gutteridge played for the St. Louis Cardinals’ Gashouse Gang and became the last surviving player for the St. Louis Browns to appear in that lowly franchise’s lone World Series.

name: W. Deen Mohammed
headline: W. Deen Mohammed, 74, Top U.S. Imam, Dies
abstract: Imam Mohammed renounced the black nationalism of his father Elijah Muhammad’s movement to lead a more traditional and racially tolerant form of Islam for black Muslims.

name: Mary Dunn
headline: Mary Dunn, Yoga Teacher to Thousands, Is Dead at 66
abstract: Ms. Dunn was a yoga teacher who guided thousands of students into the discipline known as Iyengar yoga beginning in Berkeley, Calif., in 1974.

name: Stuart Cary Welch
profession: Scholar and Collector of Islamic and Indian Art
headline: Stuart Cary Welch, Scholar and Collector of Islamic and Indian Art, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Welch, a scholar, curator and collector of Islamic and Indian art, brought many masterworks of these traditions to the attention of the West.

name: Oded Schramm
headline: Oded Schramm, 46, Mathematician, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Schramm melded ideas from two branches of mathematics into an equation that applies to a multitude of physics problems.

name: Richard Monette
headline: Richard Monette, Artistic Director for Shakespeare Festival, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Monette led the Stratford Shakespeare Festival and led it into the most robust artistic and financial period in its history.

name: Lucian W. Pye
headline: Lucian W. Pye, Bold Thinker on Asia, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Professor Pye was a political scientist who influenced new perspectives on area studies, particularly concerning China and other Asian nations.

name: Gregory Mcdonald
headline: Gregory Mcdonald, Novelist, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Mcdonald was an Edgar Award-winning crime writer whose novels starring I. M. Fletcher, breezily known as Fletch, have sold millions of copies and inspired two Hollywood films.

name: Martin K. Tytell
headline: Martin K. Tytell, Typewriter Wizard, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Tytell’s knowledge of typewriters was a boon to American spies during World War II, a tool for the defense lawyers for Alger Hiss and a necessity for literary luminaries.

name: Ralph Plaisted
headline: Ralph Plaisted, 80, Adventurer and Polar Pioneer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Plaisted was the first man to indisputably reach the North Pole when he crossed the ice by snowmobile in 1968.

name: Ron Rivera
headline: Ron Rivera, Potter Devoted to Clean Water, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Rivera pioneered ceramic water filters that cut in half the incidence of diarrhea, a leading cause of death in the third world, especially among children.

name: Olin J. Stephens II
headline: Olin J. Stephens II, Renowned Yacht Designer, Is Dead at 100
abstract: Mr. Stephens was one of the most prominent naval architects of the last century.

name: David Foster Wallace
headline: David Foster Wallace, Influential Writer, Dies at 46
abstract: Critics noted that Mr. Wallace was a versatile writer of seemingly bottomless energy, a moralist with a fierce honesty in confronting the existence of contradiction.

name: Lynn Kohlman
profession: Model and Muse to Major Designers
headline: Lynn Kohlman, Model and Muse to Major Designers, Dies at 62
abstract: Ms. Kohlman’s slightly androgynous look became an inspiration to the designers Perry Ellis and Donna Karan.

name: Betty Constable
profession: Early Squash Star and Coaching Pioneer
headline: Betty Constable, Early Squash Star and Coaching Pioneer, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Ms. Constable was the dominant female squash player of the 1950s and posted a formidable record as Princeton’s first women’s squash coach.

name: Richard Wright
headline: Richard Wright, Member of Pink Floyd, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Wright’s spacious, somber, enveloping keyboards, backing vocals and eerie effects were an essential part of Pink Floyd’s musical identity.

name: Frank Mundus
headline: Frank Mundus, 82, Dies; Inspired ‘Jaws’
abstract: Mr. Mundus was a hulking Long Island shark fisherman who was widely considered the inspiration for Captain Quint, the steely-eyed, grimly obsessed shark hunter in “Jaws.”

name: Vernon Handley
headline: Vernon Handley, 77, British Conductor, Dies
abstract: Mr. Handley, a conductor who championed British composers, made many premiere recordings of neglected music.

name: Mark Miller
headline: Mark Miller, 89, Champion of New York Wines, Dies
abstract: Mr. Miller was a magazine illustrator-turned-vintner who realized his vision of carving a world-class winemaking region from the rocky soil of the Hudson River Valley.

name: Nina Lawson
profession: Tamer of the Mets Wigs and Egos
headline: Nina Lawson, Tamer of the Met’s Wigs and Egos, Is Dead at 82
abstract: For more than 30 years, Miss Lawson ran the wig department at the Metropolitan Opera, tending the elaborate hairpieces of legendary singers.

name: John Booth
headline: John Booth, 89, Author of Theater Books, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Booth wrote books about the performing arts and was the first chairman of the Theater Development Fund, which for more than 40 years has offered discount tickets at its TKTS booths in Manhattan.

name: Georgi Kitov
headline: Georgi Kitov, Who Excavated Thrace, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Kitov gained fame for making sensational discoveries about the ancient people of Thrace and helping scientists develop a sharper picture of the kingdom.

name: P. E. Clapp
headline: P. E. Clapp, Environmental Advocate, Is Dead at 54
abstract: Mr. Clapp was an early and vigorous voice in the movement raising concern about global climate change.

name: Norman Whitfield
headline: Norman Whitfield, Motown Songwriter and Producer, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Whitfield, a songwriter, producer and arranger for Motown Records with many hits, including “I Heard It Through the Grapevine,” helped solidify the Motown sound.

name: Didier Dagueneau
headline: D. Dagueneau, Winemaker, Dies at 52
abstract: Didier Dagueneau was an iconoclastic Loire Valley winemaker whose Pouilly-Fumés displayed a purity and subtlety far beyond most other sauvignon blanc wines.

name: Henry Z. Steinway
headline: Henry Z. Steinway, Piano Maker, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Steinway, the great-grandson of the founder, was the last family member to run the piano-making company his family started in 1853.

name: S. A. Kliment
headline: S. A. Kliment, 78, Architect and Editor, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Kliment, an architect, steered Architectural Record through the economic straits of the 1990s.

name: Robert Steinberg
headline: Robert Steinberg, Chocolate Maker, Dies at 61
abstract: Dr. Steinberg was a food-loving doctor who threw himself into the chocolate business, eventually helping to make one of the most highly regarded fine American chocolates.

name: Charles A. Perlik Jr.
headline: Charles A. Perlik Jr., Who Led a News Union, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Perlik was a president of the Newspaper Guild from 1969 to 1987 and took liberal stands on issues like the rights of minorities and women in journalism.

name: Mauricio Kagel
headline: Mauricio Kagel, 76, Writer of Avant-Garde Music, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Kagel was an avant-garde composer whose often absurdist works blurred the boundaries of music, theater and film.

name: Richard M. Sudhalter
headline: Richard M. Sudhalter, 69, Author and Jazz Trumpeter, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Sudhalter won wide respect as a trumpet player and jazz historian, and he ignited controversy for a book arguing that white as well as black musicians shaped jazz.

name: James Crumley
