headline: James Crumley, Crime Novelist, Is Dead at 68
abstract: Mr. Crumley’s breathtakingly violent books swept the hard-boiled detective from the Raymond Chandler era into an amoral, dissolute, apocalyptic post-Vietnam universe.

name: Joan Winston
headline: Joan Winston, ‘Trek’ Superfan, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Winston played a leading role in creating the Star Trek convention and was also one of the program’s most avid fans.

name: Hyman Golden
headline: Hyman Golden, Co-Founder of Snapple, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Golden was a co-founder of the Snapple Beverage Corporation and served as its chairman as Snapple’s flavored teas and juices became a national phenomenon.

name: John Peragallo Jr.
headline: John Peragallo Jr., Who Kept Organs on Key, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Peragallo, the curator of the organs at St. Patrick’s Cathedral, could not go to a church service without straining to hear if there was anything the least bit amiss with his patient.

name: Nancy Hicks Maynard
headline: Nancy Hicks Maynard Dies at 61; A Groundbreaking Black Journalist
abstract: Ms. Hicks Maynard was one of the first black women to be a reporter at The New York Times and with her husband bought and published The Oakland Tribune.

name: Mary Garber
headline: Mary Garber, Sportswriter, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Garber began covering athletics in North Carolina more than 60 years ago, when female sportswriters were often regarded as a curiosity if not an imposition.

name: Dean R. Hoge
headline: Dean R. Hoge, 71, Expert on Catholic Priesthood, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Hoge was a prominent sociologist of American religion best known for incisive studies of an aging and dwindling Roman Catholic priesthood.

name: Robert Katzman
headline: Robert Katzman, Alzheimer’s Activist, Dies at 82
abstract: Dr. Katzman redefined Alzheimer’s disease as a major public health problem and as the most frequent progressive form of dementia in aging.

name: Barefoot Sanders
headline: Barefoot Sanders Dies; Dallas Judge Was 83
abstract: Judge Sanders played significant roles in matters from the Kennedy assassination to the desegregation of Dallas schools.

name: Dick Lynch
headline: Dick Lynch, Giants Star Who Became a Broadcaster, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Lynch twice led the N.F.L. in interceptions as a defensive back for the New York Giants and later spent 40 years as a radio broadcaster for the team.

name: Don Ultang
headline: Don Ultang, Pioneer in Aerial Photography, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Ultang won the 1952 Pulitzer Prize for photography for documenting a possibly racially motivated assault on the field during a college football game.

name: Nappy Brown
headline: Nappy Brown, 78, Blues and R&B Singer, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Brown’s playful songs of the mid-1950s — filled with nonsense syllables, eccentric pronunciation and a heavy beat — had touches of early rock ’n’ roll style.

name: Connie Haines
headline: Connie Haines, Peppy Singer, Dies at 87
abstract: Miss Haines famously teamed up with Frank Sinatra as lead vocalists with the Tommy Dorsey Orchestra, then went on to a prolific career of her own.

name: Joel Bloom
headline: Joel Bloom, Science Exhibit Innovator, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. Bloom was the director of the science museum and planetarium at the Franklin Institute in Philadelphia.

name: Joseph Shenker
headline: Joseph Shenker, a Pacesetter at CUNY, Is Dead at 68
abstract: Dr. Shenker was the first president of La Guardia Community College in New York and a leader in having students combine on-the-job experience with studies.

name: Miroslav Havel
headline: Miroslav Havel, a Glass Master, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Havel was one of a pair of unlikely Czech immigrants to Ireland who together revived the Waterford glass industry after a century’s dormancy.

name: Charlotte Kohler
headline: Charlotte Kohler, Literary Journal Editor, Is Dead at 99
abstract: Ms. Kohler was a longtime editor of The Virginia Quarterly Review and a quiet influence on the course of 20th-century American writing.

name: Mickey Vernon
headline: Mickey Vernon, a Star for a Lackluster Franchise, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Vernon won two American League batting titles with the Washington Senators and played first base in the major leagues for 20 seasons.

name: Marpessa Dawn
profession: Eurydice in the Film Black Orpheus
headline: Marpessa Dawn, Eurydice in the Film ‘Black Orpheus,’ Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Dawn played the beautiful, melancholic and doomed Eurydice in the classic 1959 Brazilian movie “Black Orpheus.”

name: Paul Newman
headline: Paul Newman, a Magnetic Titan of Hollywood, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. Newman, one of the last of the great 20th-century stars, acted in more than 65 movies over half a century.

name: Marc Raeff
headline: Marc Raeff, Russian History Scholar, Dies at 85
abstract: Professor Raeff was a Russian émigré who became one of the country’s leading scholars of Russian history, writing the first study of the Russian diaspora.

name: Osborn Elliott
headline: Osborn Elliott, Father of Newsweek’s Rebirth, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Elliott revitalized Newsweek magazine in the 1960s before he went on to serve as a $1-a-year deputy mayor in charge of economic development for a financially desperate New York City.

name: William Woodruff
headline: William Woodruff, 92, Dies; British Chronicler
abstract: Mr. Woodruff was an eminent historian who wrote two best-selling books that made him a celebrity in his native England and a living link to a vanished working-class Britain.

name: Marian Griffiths
headline: Marian Griffiths, Who Led Sculpture Center, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Griffiths was for two decades the director of the Sculpture Center, transforming it into a dynamic exhibition center that helped draw public attention to the medium.

name: Margot Gayle
profession: Urban Preservationist and Crusader With Style
headline: Margot Gayle, Urban Preservationist and Crusader With Style, Dies at 100
abstract: Ms. Gayle marshaled shrewdness, gentility and spunk to save the Victorian cast-iron buildings of New York in a crusade that led to the preservation of historic SoHo.

name: David Jones
headline: David Jones, Film Director, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Jones directed films such as “Betrayal” as well as dozens of productions by the Royal Shakespeare Company.

name: David C. Jones
headline: Gen. David C. Jones, Former Chairman of Joint Chiefs, Dies at 92
abstract: As chairman of the Joint Chiefs under Presidents Carter and Reagan, General Jones set in motion a sweeping reorganization of the nation’s military command.

name: David Jones
headline: David Jones, Florist to Hollywood, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Jones was probably best known as the floral designer for Elizabeth Taylor’s 1991 wedding and for Michael Jackson’s funeral in 2009.

name: David E.H. Jones
headline: David E.H. Jones, Scientist Whose Alter Ego Challenged Conventions, Dies at 79
abstract: In columns and books and on TV, Dr. Jones’s clever fictional creation, Daedalus, tweaked laymen and scientists alike.

name: David Jones
headline: David Jones, Health Care Entrepreneur Behind Humana, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Jones and a partner built large chains of nursing homes and hospitals. He later turned Humana into a major force in health insurance.

name: Elinor Guggenheimer
headline: Elinor Guggenheimer, Advocate for Women, Children and the Elderly, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Guggenheimer held prominent positions in New York City government and was a national spokeswoman for the concerns of children, women and the elderly.

name: Hayden Carruth
headline: Hayden Carruth, Poet and Critic, Dies at 87
abstract: Primarily known as a critic and editor, Mr. Carruth produced some 30 books of poetry that addressed subjects like madness, death and the fragility of the natural world.

name: Simon Hantaï
headline: Simon Hantaï, Painter of Silences, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Hantaï, a reclusive French painter whose work explored ideas of absence and silence, took those ideas so seriously that he disappeared completely from view for 15 years.

name: J.L. Chestnut Jr.
profession: Early Leader in Civil Rights Movement
headline: J.L. Chestnut Jr., Early Leader in Civil Rights Movement, Is Dead at 77
abstract: After attending law school in Washington, Mr. Chestnut returned to his hometown, Selma, Ala., and became the city’s first black lawyer, and went on to fight for voting rights for blacks.

name: Nick Reynolds
headline: Nick Reynolds, Kingston Trio Harmonizer, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Reynolds’s smooth tenor and gift for harmonizing helped propel the group, the Kingston Trio, to worldwide fame in the late 1950s and early ’60s.

name: Anthony Spero
profession: Name in the Bonanno Crime Family
headline: Anthony Spero, a Name in the Bonanno Crime Family, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Spero served the Bonnano family, one of the five Mafia clans in New York City, for more than three decades in a variety of roles.

name: Donald Blakeslee
profession: Decorated World War II Flying Ace
headline: Col. Donald Blakeslee, Decorated World War II Flying Ace, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Blakeslee was the commander of the first American fighter squadrons to reach Berlin as the Allies ground down the German Luftwaffe.

name: J. B. Jeyaretnam
headline: J. B. Jeyaretnam, Persistent Opposition Figure in Singapore, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Jeyaretnam was an opposition politician whose persistent outspokenness made him a leading dissident in Singapore and a hero to many there.

name: Edward S. Klima
headline: Edward S. Klima, Sign Language Expert, Dies at 77
abstract: Dr. Klima was an eminent linguist who was one of the first scholars to pay serious attention to sign languages.

name: Mario Maya
headline: Mario Maya, Interpreter of Flamenco Style, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Mr. Maya fused his Gypsy heritage and training in experimental American dance to become one of Spain’s most influential flamenco dancers and choreographers.

name: Boris Yefimov
headline: Boris Yefimov, Sharp Russian Cartoonist Who Was Beloved by Stalin, Dies at 109
abstract: Mr. Yefimov’s 70,000 drawings wielded his talent as a keen sword to advance the goals of his country.

name: Aaron Katz
headline: Aaron Katz, Advocate for Rosenbergs, Dies at 92
abstract: For more than 50 years, Mr. Katz publicly sought the exoneration of Julius and Ethel Rosenberg, the central figures in the nation’s most controversial spying case.

name: Avraham Biran
headline: Avraham Biran, Archaeologist Who Studied Biblical Sites, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Mr. Biran excavated Tel Dan, an ancient city along Israel’s northern border, and uncovered what might be the earliest reference to the House of David.

name: Irene Dailey
headline: Irene Dailey, Actress of Stage and TV, Dies at 88
abstract: Miss Dailey was an actress perhaps best known for her roles in television soap operas and for her portrayal of Nettie Cleary in the 1964 Tony Award-winning drama “The Subject Was Roses.”

name: Ruedi Rymann
headline: Ruedi Rymann, Swiss Yodeling Star, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Rymann was a Swiss farmer and cheesemaker renowned in his home country as a yodeler and the man who recorded what came to be known as “Switzerland’s greatest hit.”

name: Harry Albright
headline: Harry Albright, State Banking Chief, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Albright, a protégé of Gov. Nelson A. Rockefeller, championed the needs of consumers as superintendent of the New York State Banking Department in the early 1970s.

name: William M. Murphy
profession: Biographer of W. B. Yeatss Family
headline: William M. Murphy, Biographer of W. B. Yeats’s Family, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Murphy’s biographies of the family of William Butler Yeats shed light on his personal and creative relationships and led scholars to reassess the importance of his father and sisters.

name: William L. Murphy
headline: William L. Murphy, Ex-Prosecutor on Staten Island, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Murphy served for more than 20 years as the borough’s district attorney, prosecuting a notorious child kidnapper, a corrupt city official and the killer of two New York detectives.

name: William P. Murphy Jr.
headline: William P. Murphy Jr., Innovator of Life-Saving Medical Tools, Dies at 100
abstract: Dr. Murphy’s safe, reliable blood bag replaced breakable glass bottles used in transfusions in the Korean War. He also helped improve pacemakers and artificial kidneys.

name: William F. Murphy
profession: Led Diocese and Weathered Abuse Scandal
headline: William F. Murphy, 85, Dies; Led Diocese and Weathered Abuse Scandal
abstract: While serving as a Long Island bishop, his earlier tenure in Boston came under scrutiny during investigations of sex-abuse allegations involving pedophile priests.

name: George Kissell
headline: George Kissell, 88, Dies; Taught the Techniques of Baseball
abstract: Mr. Kissell became one of baseball’s most renowned teachers in a long career with the St. Louis Cardinals’ organization as a manager, player, coach and instructor.

name: Ernest Beutler
headline: Ernest Beutler, 80, Dies; Studied Blood Diseases
abstract: Dr. Beutler was a leading hematologist whose studies opened an important new window onto the treatment of leukemia.

name: Kim Chan
profession: Had Roles in TV and King of Comedy
headline: Kim Chan, Who Had Roles in TV and ‘King of Comedy,’ Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Chan was an actor who became a familiar face in a variety of Asian roles, notably as Jerry Lewis’s butler in the Martin Scorsese film “The King of Comedy.”

name: George Palade
profession: Nobel Winner for Work Inspiring Modern Cell Biology
headline: George Palade, Nobel Winner for Work Inspiring Modern Cell Biology, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Palade’s discoveries about the intricate inner workings of cells were useful in understanding protein production, the basis of the modern biotechnology industry.

name: Eileen Herlie
headline: Eileen Herlie, Actress of TV and Stage, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Herlie was for 32 years the wise matron Myrtle Fargate on the ABC soap opera “All My Children” and earlier an acclaimed performer on Broadway and the London stage.

name: Nadia Nerina
headline: Nadia Nerina, Royal Ballet Dancer, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Ms. Nerina was a principal ballerina for the Royal Ballet known for her technical virtuosity, lightness afoot, effortless-seeming jumps and joyful charm onstage, especially in comedic roles.

name: Jörg Haider
headline: Jörg Haider, Austrian Rightist, Is Dead at 58
abstract: Mr. Haider was a controversial and charismatic far-right politician known for his strong anti-immigrant and anti-European Union stances.

name: Francis Sayre Jr.
headline: Francis Sayre Jr., National Cathedral Dean, Dies at 93
abstract: In his 27 years as dean of the National Cathedral in Washington, Dean Sayre raised his sonorous voice against McCarthyism, segregation, poverty and the Vietnam War.

name: David Lett
headline: David Lett, Oregon Wine Pioneer, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Lett planted the first commercial pinot noir vineyard in Oregon, opening the way for what became a thriving pinot noir industry.

name: William Claxton
headline: William Claxton, Photographer, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Mr. Claxton was a photographer who captured images of the greats of jazz and made indelible images of pop stars and movie stars.

name: Paul G. Rogers
headline: Paul G. Rogers, ‘Mr. Health’ in Congress, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Rogers was called Mr. Health by his fellow congressmen for his leading role in passing dozens of measures promoting health care and the environment.

name: Paul Rogers
headline: Paul Rogers, Shakespearean Actor and Tony Winner, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Rogers came to fame as a versatile Shakespearean in his native England and, in 1956, played four demanding roles in a three-month run of Shakespeare on Broadway.

name: Peter Vansittart
headline: Peter Vansittart, Prolific Writer of Historical Fiction, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Vansittart breathed new life into the historical novel by mingling myth with modernity, and by injecting 20th-century preoccupations into historical settings.

name: Iba Ndiaye
headline: Iba Ndiaye, African Modernist Painter, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Mr. Ndiaye helped found a Senegalese art movement called École de Darkar, which was aligned with the literary movement of Négritude.

name: Neal Hefti
headline: Neal Hefti, 85, Jazz and Hollywood Composer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Hefti, a forward-looking composer and arranger, wrote the theme for the 1960s television show “Batman,” and for the movie and television versions of “The Odd Couple.”

name: Edie Adams
profession: Actress and Singer (and Flirt With a Cigar)
headline: Edie Adams, Actress and Singer (and Flirt With a Cigar), Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Adams was an actress, comedian and singer who both embodied and winked at the stereotypes of fetching chanteuse and sexpot blonde.

name: Allan Rosenfield
headline: Dr. Allan Rosenfield, Women’s Health Advocate, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Rosenfield, a dean of the Mailman School of Public Health at Columbia University, became a leading advocate for women’s health during the global H.I.V./AIDS epidemic.

name: Alton Ellis
headline: Alton Ellis, Jamaican Singer, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Ellis was the smooth Jamaican singer and songwriter known as the Godfather of Rock Steady.

name: Jack Narz
profession: Genial Host of Television Game Shows
headline: Jack Narz, 85, Genial Host of Television Game Shows, Dies
abstract: Mr. Narz was a television host who, though blameless, became ensnared in the quiz-show rigging scandal of the 1950s but made a comeback with the show “Concentration.”

name: Matthew J. Rinaldo
headline: Matthew J. Rinaldo, Former Congressman From New Jersey, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Rinaldo was a moderate Republican who chose not to seek re-election in 1992 after serving 20 years in the House of Representatives.

name: Tom Tresh
headline: Tom Tresh, a Two-Time Yankees All-Star, Dies at 70
abstract: Tresh, who played shortstop and left field for the Yankees, was the American League’s rookie of the year in 1962 and played on three World Series teams.

name: Ken Ogata
profession: Japanese Actor Famed for Films and TV
headline: Ken Ogata, Japanese Actor Famed for Films and TV, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Ogata was a versatile and prolific leading man in Japanese films and on Japanese television who also appeared in movies directed by Peter Greenaway and Paul Schrader.

name: George M. Keller
headline: George M. Keller, Whose Wager Created Chevron, Is Dead at 84
abstract: As chairman of the Standard Oil Company of California in the 1980s, Mr. Keller executed what was then the largest corporate takeover ever, in a deal that formed Chevron.

name: Levi Stubbs
headline: Levi Stubbs, 72, Powerful Voice for Four Tops, Dies
abstract: Mr. Stubbs, the gravelly voiced, plaintive lead singer of the Motown group the Four Tops, sang pop classics like “Reach Out (I’ll Be There),” and “Bernadette.”

name: Paul Montgomery
headline: Paul Montgomery, Former New York Times Reporter, Is Dead at 72
abstract: Mr. Montgomery covered riots in Harlem, the civil rights march from Selma to Montgomery, Ala., in 1965, and the search for Che Guevara in Bolivia.

name: Lefty Rosenthal
headline: Lefty Rosenthal, Kingpin in Las Vegas, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Rosenthal was a professional gambler and gangster-when-necessary who brought sports betting to casinos in Las Vegas and illicitly ran an empire of four hotel casinos.

name: Ed Turney
headline: Ed Turney, a Chip Maker Founder, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Turney co-founded Advanced Micro Devices and built the company’s first sales team.

name: Dave McKenna
profession: Pianist Known for Solo Jazz Work
headline: Dave McKenna, Pianist Known for Solo Jazz Work, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. McKenna, a jazz pianist, was known for a powerful left hand that made a bass player seem unnecessary.

name: Ardeshir Mohassess
headline: Ardeshir Mohassess, Iranian Cartoonist, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Mr. Mohassess pushed the art of the cartoon to almost Surrealist satire of his native land in work both popular and profound.

name: Bill Reilly
headline: Bill Reilly, Magazine Publishing Executive, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Reilly, a publishing and media executive, was a founder and former chairman of Primedia Inc., which amassed a portfolio of more than 200 magazines.

name: Ben Weider
headline: Ben Weider, 85, a Bodybuilding Pioneer
abstract: Mr. Weider brought bodybuilding into the international spotlight by organizing competitions like Mr. Olympia and by grooming stars like Arnold Schwarzenegger.

name: Blackwell
headline: Mr. Blackwell, Fashion Critic, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Blackwell was a designer of over-the-top fashions and originator of the outlandishly satiric, but globally ballyhooed worst-dressed list.

name: Gail Robinson
headline: Gail Robinson, Soprano Who Sang at the Metropolitan Opera, Dies at 62
abstract: Ms. Robinson sang with the Met for nearly two decades and went on to a career as a teacher and guide to emerging singers.

name: Vittorio Foa
headline: Vittorio Foa, Anti-Fascist, Labor Leader and Italian Senator, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Foa was an anti-Fascist intellectual, labor union leader and senator whose life traced the trajectory of the Italian left in the 20th century.

name: Rudy Ray Moore
headline: Rudy Ray Moore, 81, a Precursor of Rap, Dies
abstract: Mr. Moore’s standup comedy, records and movies — notably 1975’s “Dolemite” — related earthy tales that helped shape today’s hip-hop.

name: Dorothy Miner
headline: Dorothy Miner, 72, Legal Innovator, Dies
abstract: Ms. Miner developed legal protection for historic landmarks nationwide in her longtime role as counsel to the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission.

name: Pat Kavanagh
headline: Pat Kavanagh, Literary Agent, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. Kavanagh’s client roster included Ruth Rendell, William Trevor and Joanna Trollope, and had a leading role in the London literary world.

name: Born Madeleine Cinquin
profession: Revered in France for Candor and Caring
headline: Sister Emmanuelle, Revered in France for Candor and Caring, Is Dead at 99
abstract: Born Madeleine Cinquin, the nun was revered for her work with the disenfranchised and renowned for her television appearances as an advocate for the poor.

name: Lou Dorfsman
headline: Lou Dorfsman, Design Chief at CBS, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Dorfsman spent more than 40 years with CBS, and designed every aspect of the company’s advertising and corporate identity.

name: Mireille Marokvia
headline: Mireille Marokvia, 99, Memoirist, Dies
abstract: Ms. Marokvia wrote two stirring memoirs describing her childhood in a French village and her wartime ordeals in Nazi Germany.

name: Tony Hillerman
headline: Tony Hillerman, Novelist, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Hillerman’s evocative novels, which describe people struggling to maintain ancient traditions in the modern world, touched millions of readers, who made them best sellers.

name: Amos E. Joel Jr.
headline: Amos E. Joel Jr., Cellphone Pioneer, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Joel was perhaps best known for a 1972 patent that allows a cellphone user to make an uninterrupted call while moving from one cell region to another.

name: E. Roger Muir
headline: E. Roger Muir, 89, Dies; Backed Howdy Doody
abstract: Mr. Muir helped create and was executive producer of “The Howdy Doody Show,” the puppet-and-people program that first hooked millions of kids on television.

name: Herbert Mitchell
headline: Herbert Mitchell, 83, Collector of Images, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Mitchell filled his apartment with a unique collection of stereographs, daguerreotypes, ceramics and books that became a treasure trove for scholars.

name: Gerard Damiano
headline: Gerard Damiano, 80, Dies; Directed ‘Deep Throat’
abstract: Mr. Damiano’s best-known work created sensation in every possible meaning of the term when it was released in 1972.

name: R. R. Furman
headline: R. R. Furman, 93, Dies; Led Bomb-Project Spying
abstract: As chief of foreign intelligence for the American atomic bomb project, Major Furman coordinated and often joined harrowing espionage missions.

name: Gerald Arpino
headline: Gerald Arpino, Ballet Choreographer and Joffrey Co-Founder, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Arpino was a founder of the Joffrey Ballet and a distinctly American choreographer whose works popularized dance with their trendy finger on the nation’s pulse.

name: Estelle Reiner
headline: Estelle Reiner, 94, Comedy Matriarch, Is Dead
abstract: Mrs. Reiner was the matriarch of one of the leading families in American comedy, and delivered one of the most memorably funny lines in movie history herself.

name: William Wharton
headline: William Wharton, Author, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Wharton was a successful painter whose first novel, “Birdy,” won a National Book Award and became a critically acclaimed movie.

name: Edith Evans Asbury
headline: Edith Evans Asbury, 98, Veteran Times Reporter, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Asbury covered hard news in an era when most of her female colleagues were consigned to writing about white-gloved society luncheons.

name: Studs Terkel
headline: Studs Terkel, Listener to Americans, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Terkel was a Pulitzer Prize-winning author whose searching interviews with ordinary Americans helped establish oral history as an important historical genre.

name: Es’kia Mphahlele
headline: Es’kia Mphahlele, Chronicler of Apartheid, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Mphahlele’s 1959 memoir, “Down Second Avenue,” vividly dramatized the injustices of apartheid and became a landmark work of South African literature.

name: Robert Barrow
headline: Robert Barrow, a Marine Corps Reformer Who Became Commandant, Dies at 86
abstract: General Barrow, the 27th commandant of the Marine Corps, served heroically in World War II, the Korean War and the Vietnam War.

name: P. Cameron DeVore
profession: Early Expert on First Amendment Law
headline: P. Cameron DeVore, Early Expert on First Amendment Law, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. DeVore was a First Amendment lawyer who was an early expert in the field, representing news companies in many significant disputes over the freedom of the press.

name: C.W. Spangenberger
headline: C.W. Spangenberger, of Storied Hudson River Tugboat Line, Dies at 102
abstract: Mr. Spangenberger was the last president of what for many years was the largest tugboat company in the United States, and maybe the biggest in the world.

name: Albert Boime
headline: Albert Boime, Leading Art Historian, Dies at 75
abstract: Professor Boime, who wrote the four-volume “Social History of Modern Art,” was a scholar of art history who took the history every bit as seriously as the art.

name: Milton Katselas
headline: Milton Katselas, Acting Teacher and Director, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Katselas was an iconoclastic acting teacher whose 30 years in Hollywood raised him to guru status in the eyes of hundreds of actors, many of them famous.

name: Moshe Cotel
headline: Rabbi Moshe Cotel, Composer, Dies at 65
abstract: Rabbi Cotel was an acclaimed pianist and composer whose works were often infused with themes emanating from his deep Jewish roots.

name: John W. Ripley
headline: Col. John W. Ripley, Marine Who Halted Vietnamese Attack, Dies at 69
abstract: Colonel Ripley entered Marine Corps lore when he single-handedly blunted a major North Vietnamese offensive during the Vietnam War by blowing up a strategically placed bridge.

name: Terence D. Tolbert
headline: Terence D. Tolbert, Schools Official, Dies at 44
abstract: Mr. Tolbert was the state director in Nevada for Senator Barack Obama’s presidential campaign and an aide to the New York City schools chancellor, Joel I. Klein.

name: Yma Sumac
headline: Yma Sumac, Vocalist of the Exotic, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Sumac was a Peruvian singer who burst on the American scene in the 1950s in a tornado of exotic publicity with a voice that glided preternaturally across four octaves.

name: Rosella Hightower
headline: Rosella Hightower, Prima Ballerina and School Founder, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Miss Hightower was a ballerina who followed up a celebrated international career by founding the Centre de Danse Classique in Cannes, France.

name: Marilyn Ferguson
headline: Marilyn Ferguson, New Age Author, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Ferguson’s 1980 book “The Aquarian Conspiracy” became a bible of the New Age movement.

name: Domenico Leccisi
headline: Domenico Leccisi, Italian Political Figure, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Leccisi became known as “the Body Snatcher” in 1946 when he and two followers stole the corpse of the fascist dictator Mussolini from a pauper’s grave.

name: Michael Crichton
headline: Michael Crichton, Author of Thrillers, Dies at 66
abstract: By combining old-fashioned storytelling with gee-whiz science, Mr. Crichton’s books made for a compelling formula that was adapted easily by Hollywood.

name: Cecil Stoughton
headline: Cecil Stoughton Dies at 88; Documented White House
abstract: Mr. Stoughton, the chief photographer for the Kennedy White House, documented its glittering public moments and its intimate private ones.

name: Jimmy Carl Black
headline: Jimmy Carl Black, Rocker, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Black was the acerbic drummer of Frank Zappa’s mischievous, innovative band the Mothers of Invention.

name: Kenneth Johnson
headline: Kenneth Johnson, 74, Dies; Revitalized a Dallas Paper
abstract: As editor of The Dallas Times Herald in the 1970s and ’80s, Mr. Johnson transformed it into one of the most respected newspapers in the nation.

name: John Leonard
headline: John Leonard, 69, Cultural Critic, Dies
abstract: Mr. Leonard, an influential, visible cultural critic, was known for the breadth of his knowledge, the depth of his inquiries and the lavish passion of his prose.

name: G. Larry James
headline: G. Larry James, Olympic Gold Medalist, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. James was a former champion runner who won gold and silver medals in the racially charged 1968 Olympics in Mexico City.

name: Lennart Bergelin
headline: Lennart Bergelin, Who Guided Borg to Greatness, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. Bergelin, a leading Swedish tennis player of the 1940s and ’50s, was best known for coaching Bjorn Borg to 11 Grand Slam championships.

name: Jheryl Busby
headline: Jheryl Busby, 59, Reviver of the Motown Label, Dies
abstract: Mr. Busby was a music executive who helped return an industry giant to the top of the charts.

name: Philip Reed
headline: Philip Reed, Councilman Who Fought for Health Issues, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Reed, a former elevator salesman, became a champion of housing and health issues as an openly H.I.V.-positive member of the New York City Council.

name: Mike Davis
headline: Mike Davis, 68, Builder of Boats and Dreams, Dies
abstract: Mr. Davis’s vision of skimming a rowboat through the gentle chop of the Hudson River inspired something of a movement to reclaim New York’s waterways for recreational use.

name: Mike Davis
headline: Mike Davis, ‘World’s Grumpiest Boss,’ Dies at 85
abstract: The Houston oil and gas magnate, who owned Tiger Oil, gained notoriety as the author of blunt office memos that earned him the unofficial title.

name: Mike Davis
profession: Wrote of Los Angeles and Catastrophe
headline: Mike Davis, Who Wrote of Los Angeles and Catastrophe, Dies at 76
abstract: In “City of Quartz” and other books, he predicted trouble ahead. Events often proved him right.

name: Thomas Dunn
headline: Thomas Dunn, an Early-Music Conductor, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Dunn was a prominent conductor whose work helped animate the early music revival that took place in the mid-20th century and afterward.

name: B. R. Chopra
headline: B. R. Chopra, a Top Indian Filmmaker, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Chopra found rare success creating both hit Bollywood musicals and dramatic, socially conscious films.

name: Ronald Davis
headline: Ronald Davis, Health Crusader, Dies at 52
abstract: Dr. Davis was a former president of the American Medical Association who campaigned against tobacco, alcohol, obesity, illicit drugs and unhealthy lifestyles in his career as a public health official.

name: Ronald G. Davis
headline: Ronald G. Davis, a Mime Who Spoke Out, Dies at 92
abstract: At the height of the psychedelic era, he guided the very vocal San Francisco Mime Troupe’s pointed satire of American militarism, racism and bourgeois values.

name: Miriam Makeba
headline: Miriam Makeba, 76, Singer and Activist, Dies
abstract: Ms. Makeba was a South African singer whose voice stirred hopes of freedom in her own country even though her music was formally banned by the apartheid authorities she struggled against.

name: Preacher Roe
profession: Brooklyn Dodgers Star Known for His Spitball
headline: Preacher Roe, Brooklyn Dodgers Star Known for His Spitball, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Roe was a folksy pitcher from the Ozarks who became a star with the Brooklyn Dodgers, featuring superb control and a spitball he belatedly confessed to throwing.

name: Bernard W. Rogers
headline: Bernard W. Rogers Is Dead at 87; Innovative Army Chief
abstract: General Rogers developed strategies to help the United States Army adjust to an all-volunteer force and new generations of weapons.

name: Michael Higgins
profession: Actor Popular on New York Stages
headline: Michael Higgins, an Actor Popular on New York Stages, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Higgins was best known for the role of Frank Strang, the father of the disturbed youth who blinds horses, in the original Broadway production of “Equus.”

name: Tom Hunt
profession: Executive in His Familys Oil Business
headline: Tom Hunt, Executive in His Family’s Oil Business, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Hunt was a former chairman of Hunt Petroleum and an adviser to the founder of the family dynasty, his uncle H. L. Hunt.

name: Arthur J. Shawcross
headline: Arthur J. Shawcross, Serial Killer in Rochester, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Shawcross was serving a 250-year sentence for murdering 11 women in the Rochester area in the late 1980s.

name: Herb Score
profession: Indians Pitcher Derailed by Line Drive
headline: Herb Score, 75, Indians Pitcher Derailed by Line Drive, Dies
abstract: Mr. Score was the Cleveland Indians left-hander who seemed destined for the Hall of Fame only to have his career ruined when a line drive struck him in the face.

name: Mieczyslaw Rakowski
headline: Mieczyslaw Rakowski, former Polish Communist Premier, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Rakowski was for decades the editor of an influential weekly newspaper and was known for his carefully calibrated criticism of the Communist government.

name: Nikola Kavaja
headline: Nikola Kavaja, Anti-Tito Hijacker of Jet, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Kavaja was a Yugoslav-born anti-Communist whose hatred for the dictator Tito spurred him to a career of violent subversion and terrorism.

name: Abraham Woods
headline: Abraham Woods, Civil Rights Pioneer, Dies at 80
abstract: In the days of crowd-throttling fire-hosings and snarling police dogs, Mr. Woods led the first lunch-counter sit-ins in Birmingham, Ala., and later confronted racism at country clubs.

name: Mitch Mitchell
headline: Mitch Mitchell Dies at 62; Drummer for Jimi Hendrix
abstract: Mr. Mitchell, a jazzy and versatile drummer, was one of two Englishmen in the Jimi Hendrix Experience.

name: Henry Loomis
headline: Henry Loomis, Who Led Voice of America, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Loomis extended the reach and defended the independence of the Voice of America in the late 1950s and early 1960s before resigning in a clash with President Lyndon B. Johnson.

name: Florence S. Wald
headline: Florence S. Wald, American Pioneer in End-of-Life Care, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mrs. Wald’s vision of bringing the terminally ill peace of mind and, to whatever extent possible, freedom from pain led to the opening of the first palliative care hospice in the United States.

name: Carl D. Keith
headline: Carl D. Keith, a Father of the Catalytic Converter, Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Keith was a co-inventor of the three-way automotive catalytic converter — a major advance in eliminating the toxic tailpipe emissions that once blanketed cities in smog.

name: C. Harmon Brown
headline: C. Harmon Brown, Pioneer Sports Doctor, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Dr. Brown helped develop the field of sports medicine, including doing influential research on the effects of strenuous exercise on the female body.

name: Rosetta Reitz
headline: Rosetta Reitz, Champion of Jazz Women, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Reitz scavenged through the early history of jazz and the blues to resurrect the music of long-forgotten women and to create a record label dedicated to them.

name: Edward Sheehan
headline: Edward Sheehan, 78, Foreign Correspondent, Dies
abstract: Mr. Sheehan’s perceptive, literate dispatches from the Middle East, Africa and Central America explored the political machinations of the powerful and the misery of the powerless.

name: Peter Levinson
profession: Publicist and Biographer of Jazz Greats
headline: Peter Levinson, Publicist and Biographer of Jazz Greats, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Mr. Levinson, a music publicist, parlayed his close familiarity with jazz personalities into rich and sometimes intimate biographies of them.

name: I. Bernard Weinstein
headline: I. Bernard Weinstein, Who Studied Causes of Cancer, Dies at 78
abstract: Dr. Weinstein was a researcher at Columbia University who advanced the study of how pollutants and other environmental factors can cause cancer.

name: Alan Ford
headline: Alan Ford, Top Freestyler in 1940s, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Ford became the first swimmer to break 50 seconds for 100 yards, a barrier that some likened to the four-minute mile.

name: Pete Newell
headline: Pete Newell, Basketball Coach and Innovator, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Newell was one of the most influential coaches in the history of basketball, whose camp became a required seminar in low-post play for generations of professional stars.

name: Grace Hartigan
headline: Grace Hartigan, 86, Abstract Painter, Dies
abstract: Ms. Hartigan was a second-generation Abstract Expressionist whose gestural, intensely colored paintings often incorporated images drawn from popular culture.

name: Adrian Kantrowitz
headline: Dr. Adrian Kantrowitz, Cardiac Pioneer, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Kantrowitz performed the first human heart transplant in the United States and pioneered the development of devices to prolong the life of patients with heart failure.

name: Irving Brecher
headline: Irving Brecher, 94, Comedy-Script Writer, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Brecher wrote vaudeville sketches, jokes, comedies for the Marx Brothers, a television series and screenplays for movie musicals including “Meet Me in St. Louis” and “Bye Bye Birdie.”

name: James Armsey
headline: James Armsey Dies at 90; Oversaw College Grants
abstract: As a Ford Foundation executive, Mr. Armsey directed more than $350 million in grants to universities in the 1960s while prompting the foundation to deny grants to segregated universities.

name: Clive Barnes
profession: Raised Stakes in Dance and Theater Criticism
headline: Clive Barnes, Who Raised Stakes in Dance and Theater Criticism, Dies at 81
abstract: As a critic in Britain and later for The New York Times, Mr. Barnes helped bring dance to a broad audience with an exuberant style.

name: Jay Katz
headline: Dr. Jay Katz, 86, Dies; Explorer of Ethics Issues
abstract: Dr. Katz, a physician and a professor at Yale Law School, spent decades tackling confounding questions on the boundaries between law, medicine, psychology and ethics.

name: Jan Krugier
headline: Jan Krugier, Dealer in Modern Art, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Krugier survived two years in Nazi concentration camps and went on to become a highly regarded dealer of work by artists like Picasso, Morandi, Balthus and Giacometti.

name: Carole Caldwell Graebner
headline: Carole Caldwell Graebner, Tennis Star, Dies at 65
abstract: Graebner was a top-ranked player and tireless supporter of the Fed Cup, an international tennis competition that she and her longtime friend Billie Jean King helped inaugurate.

name: Irving Gertz
profession: Composer for Monsters of the Movies
headline: Irving Gertz, Composer for Monsters of the Movies, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Gertz was a prolific though often uncredited B-movie composer whose melodies haunt a spate of pictures with words like “Hell,” “Thing” and “Creature” in the titles.

name: Donald Finkel
headline: Donald Finkel, 79, Poet of Free-Ranging Styles, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Finkel was a noted American poet whose work teemed with curious juxtapositions, which in their unorthodoxy helped illuminate the function of poetry itself.

name: Boris Fyodorov
headline: Boris Fyodorov, 50, Dies; Guided Reforms in Russia
abstract: Mr. Fyodorov was prominent among the young economists responsible for post-Soviet Russia’s striking economic reforms.

name: Irwin C. Gunsalus
headline: Irwin C. Gunsalus, Vitamin Biochemist, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Gunsalus discovered lipoic acid, which has been used as a treatment for chronic liver disease, and one of the active forms of vitamin B6, essential in metabolism.

name: Bette S. Garber
profession: Saw the Beauty in Big Rigs
headline: Bette S. Garber Dies at 65; Saw the Beauty in Big Rigs
abstract: Among the small but lively fraternity of photojournalists who specialize in documenting trucks and truckers, Ms. Garber was considered the foremost in the country.

name: Kiyoshi Ito
headline: Kiyoshi Ito, 93, Mathematician Who Described Random Motion, Dies
abstract: Mr. Ito’s innovative models of random motion are used today in fields as diverse as finance and biology.

name: Betty James
headline: Betty James, Who Named the Slinky Toy, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mrs. James came up with the name for the toy using a dictionary.

name: Karl Bissinger
headline: Karl Bissinger, Portraitist, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Bissinger’s lustrous black and white portraits created a memorable gallery of the leading figures on the postwar American arts scene.

name: Richard Hickox
headline: Richard Hickox, British Conductor, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Hickox was a conductor who championed the works of his fellow Britons, recorded prodigiously and was most recently music director of Opera Australia.

name: John Michael Hayes
headline: John Michael Hayes, Who Adapted ‘Rear Window,’ Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Hayes was a screenwriter who wrote some of Alfred Hitchcock’s best-known films before breaking with the director in a fight over screen credit.

name: Gerald Schoenfeld
headline: He Relit Broadway: Gerald Schoenfeld Dies at 84
abstract: The chairman of the powerful Shubert Organization was one of the most influential figures in American theater.

name: MC Breed
headline: MC Breed, 37, Rapper With Midwest Roots, Is Dead
abstract: MC Breed, who began his career in Flint, Mich., was one of the first commercially successful and nationally recognized rappers from the Midwest.

name: Sandy Ruby
headline: Sandy Ruby, Co-Founder of Tech Hifi, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Ruby was a mathematician turned entrepreneur who co-founded a business in a dorm room and built it into Tech Hifi, a popular electronics retailer.

name: Frank Cieciorka
headline: Frank Cieciorka, Designer for the Left, Is Dead at 69
abstract: Mr. Cieciorka was a graphic artist, art director and watercolorist whose woodcut rendering of a clenched-fist salute was the model for the New Left’s most ubiquitous emblem.

name: William Gibson
headline: William Gibson, Playwright, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Gibson was a playwright who had a gift for creating strong, popular female characters and wrote “The Miracle Worker.”

name: Andrew J. McKelvey
headline: Andrew J. McKelvey, 74, Builder of Monster.com, Dies
abstract: Mr. McKelvey jumped into Internet commerce as the executive who built Monster.com into the leading job recruitment Web site.

name: Ennio De Concini
headline: Ennio De Concini, Oscar-Winning Writer, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. De Concini had won an Academy Award for the internationally popular comedy “Divorce — Italian Style,” released in 1961.

name: Jorn Utzon
headline: Jorn Utzon, 90, Dies; Created Sydney Opera House
abstract: Mr. Utzon was an architect who designed one of the world’s most recognizable buildings — the Sydney Opera House — but never saw it finished.

name: V. P. Singh
headline: V. P. Singh, a Leader of India Who Defended Poor, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Singh was a former prime minister of India who was considered the father of coalition politics there and who stirred controversy by championing the rights of the country’s poorest citizens.

name: Richard L. Fortman
headline: Richard L. Fortman, a Champion at Checkers, Dies at 93
abstract: For seven decades Mr. Fortman was considered one of the game’s foremost players, analysts and authors.

name: Doris Dungey
headline: Doris Dungey, Prescient Finance Blogger, Dies at 47
abstract: Ms. Dungey wrote under the pseudonym Tanta for Calculated Risk, the finance and economics blog.

name: H. N. Friedlaender
headline: H. N. Friedlaender, Bibliophile, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Friedlaender was a book-loving lawyer and financial adviser whose collection of early printed books caused a stir in bibliophilic circles when it went to auction.

name: Bill Drake
headline: Bill Drake, 71, Dies; Created a Winning Radio Style
abstract: Mr. Drake transformed radio programming with a syndicated format that delivered more music, fewer commercials and high-energy “Boss Jocks.”

name: Joseph M. Margiotta
headline: Joseph M. Margiotta, Long Island G.O.P. Leader, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Margiotta ruled the Nassau County Republican Party, once one of the most powerful political organizations in New York State, for 16 years .

name: Ramon S. Velez
headline: Ramon S. Velez, the South Bronx Padrino, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Velez became the baron of a sweeping array of poverty programs and received praise for his voter registration work and criticism for profiting from his humanitarian initiatives.

name: Edward S. Rogers Jr.
headline: Edward S. Rogers Jr., Canadian Media Mogul, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Rogers transformed Canada’s first FM radio station into one of North America’s most diverse communications and media companies.

name: Odetta
headline: Odetta, Voice of Civil Rights Movement, Dies at 77
abstract: The singer, whose voice wove together American folk music and the civil rights movement, died Tuesday.

name: Joza Karas
headline: Joza Karas, Who Recovered Music From Concentration Camp, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Karas was a musician and teacher who sought out the music and stories of composers from a Nazi concentration camp.

name: Oliver Selfridge
headline: Oliver Selfridge, an Early Innovator in Artificial Intelligence, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Selfridge was credited with coining the term "intelligent agents," for software programs capable of observing and responding to changes in their environment.

name: Emanuel Rackman
headline: Emanuel Rackman, Prominent Rabbi, Dies at 98
abstract: Rabbi Rackman was the spiritual leader of the prominent Fifth Avenue Synagogue in Manhattan and an outspoken advocate of a more inclusive, intellectually open Orthodox Judaism.

name: H. M.
headline: H. M., an Unforgettable Amnesiac, Dies at 82
abstract: Henry Gustav Molaison, or H.M., was recognized as the most important patient in the history of brain science.

name: Dorothea Rabkin
headline: Dorothea Rabkin, 87, Collector, Dies
abstract: Ms. Rabkin and her husband built a collection of American folk art noted for the whirligigs and other sculptures made by anonymous carvers in the 19th and early 20th centuries.

name: Dorothy Sterling
headline: Dorothy Sterling, 95, Children’s Author, Dies
abstract: Ms. Sterling wrote more than 35 books for children and adults including some of the first nonfiction works about black history for young readers.

name: Russian Orthodox Patriarch
headline: Russian Orthodox Patriarch Dies at 79
abstract: Aleksy II led a revival of the church after Communism and built ties to the Kremlin under Vladimir V. Putin.

name: Alex Widmer
headline: Alex Widmer, 52, Chief of Julius Baer, Dies Unexpectedly
abstract: A spokesman for Julius Baer declined to comment on the cause amid reports, attributed to unidentified sources, that it was suicide.

name: Forrest J Ackerman
headline: Forrest J Ackerman, High Elder of Fantasy Fans, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Ackerman’s devotion to science fiction and horror stories was so fierce that he helped propel their popularity, and he was widely credited with coining the term sci-fi.

name: Verne Orr
profession: Air Force Chief Known for Fight Against Waste
headline: Verne Orr, Air Force Chief Known for Fight Against Waste, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Orr was secretary of the Air Force under President Ronald Reagan and, in a campaign against waste, introduced more competition into the process of bidding for military contracts.

name: Constantin Dumitrescu
headline: Constantin Dumitrescu, Romanian Dissident, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Dumitrescu was a Romanian dissident who spent years in prison during the Communist era and later led the fight to open the files of the Securitate, the feared secret police.

name: Patriarch Aleksy II
headline: Patriarch Aleksy II, Russian Orthodox Leader, Dies at 79
abstract: The leader of the sprawling Russian Orthodox Church presided over its restoration as a powerful influence in Russian society after decades of Soviet persecution.

name: Sunny von Bülow
headline: Sunny von Bülow, 76, Focus of Society Drama, Dies
abstract: The husband of Mrs. von Bülow, who was in a coma for 28 years, was twice tried on charges of attempted murder.

name: Robert Zajonc
profession: Looked at Minds Ties to Actions
headline: Robert Zajonc, Who Looked at Mind’s Ties to Actions, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Professor Zajonc was a psychologist who illuminated the mental processes that underpin social behavior and in so doing helped create the modern field of social psychology.

name: Nina Foch
headline: Nina Foch, Actress in Sophisticated Roles, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Foch epitomized the cool, aloof blond sophisticate in films and on television for six decades while thriving as an acting teacher.

name: George S. Morrison
headline: George S. Morrison, Admiral and Singer’s Father, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Morrison commanded the fleet during the Gulf of Tonkin incident that led to an escalation of the Vietnam War and whose son Jim was the lead singer of the Doors.

name: Elmer Valentine
headline: Elmer Valentine, Owner of Rock Clubs, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Valentine opened the Whisky a Go Go in West Hollywood, one of the most celebrated clubs in the history of rock music.

name: Arthur R. Kantrowitz
headline: Arthur R. Kantrowitz, Whose Wide-Ranging Research Had Many Applications, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Dr. Kantrowitz’s research on the behavior of superhot gases and fluid dynamics led to nose cones for rockets, heart-assist pumps and the idea of nuclear fusion in magnetic bottles.

name: Cornelius C. Vermeule III
headline: Cornelius C. Vermeule III, a Curator of Classical Antiquities, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Dr. Vermeule built a reputation for astute acquisitions, prodigious scholarship and exuberant eccentricity over four decades as curator of classical antiquities at the Museum of Fine Arts in Boston.

name: Dennis Yost
headline: Dennis Yost, 65, Singer for the Classics IV, Is Dead
abstract: In the late 1960s and early ’70s, Mr. Yost’s rock group challenged the then-ascendant music of drugs and protest with a more laid-back, softer sound.

name: Robert Prosky
profession: Actor of Wide Range and Acumen
headline: Robert Prosky, 77, an Actor of Wide Range and Acumen, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Prosky was a familiar face on Broadway, in movies and on television, notably as a gruff desk sergeant in the later years of “Hill Street Blues.”

name: Bernard Ackerman
headline: Bernard Ackerman, 72, Dies; Expert at Skin Diagnosis
abstract: Dr. Ackerman was a founding figure in the field of dermatopathology who trained a generation of doctors to recognize skin diseases under the microscope.

name: Sal Yvars
headline: Sal Yvars Dies at 84; Revealed Baseball Scheme
abstract: Yvars was a catcher for the New York Giants who took part in, and later revealed, a sign-stealing scheme that might have helped propel the Giants to their 1951 pennant victory.

name: William H. Pierson Jr.
headline: William H. Pierson Jr., 97, Art Historian, Dies
abstract: As a member of the “art mafia” at Williams College, Mr. Pierson helped train a generation of prominent curators and museum officials.

name: William S. Stevens
headline: William S. Stevens, 60, Dies; Wrote Infield Fly Note
abstract: Mr. Stevens’s semi-parodic analogy between the infield-fly rule and development of Anglo-American common law achieved longstanding legal fame.

name: Jan Kemp
profession: Exposed Fraud in Grades of Players
headline: Jan Kemp Dies at 59; Exposed Fraud in Grades of Players
abstract: Dr. Kemp’s lawsuit against the University of Georgia in the 1980s drew national attention to preferential treatment of college athletes unable to meet academic standards.

name: Bettie Page
headline: Bettie Page, Queen of Pinups, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Page appeared in men’s magazines in the 1950s, setting the stage for the sexual revolution of the ’60s.

name: Lawrence R. Devlin
headline: Lawrence R. Devlin, 86, C.I.A. Officer Who Balked on a Congo Plot, Is Dead
abstract: As the Central Intelligence Agency’s station chief in Congo in 1960, Mr. Devlin avoided carrying out an order to assassinate the ousted prime minister, Patrice Lumumba.

name: Robin Toner
headline: Robin Toner, Times Reporter, Is Dead at 54
abstract: Ms. Toner was the first woman to have been the national political correspondent of The New York Times.

name: Avery Dulles
headline: Cardinal Avery Dulles, Theologian, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Cardinal Dulles was the only American theologian ever appointed to the College of Cardinals.

name: Van Johnson
headline: Van Johnson, Film Actor, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Johnson had boyish good looks and charm that made him a major Hollywood star during World War II.

name: Robert Chandler
headline: Robert Chandler, 80, a Creator of the ’60 Minutes’ Format, Dies
abstract: Mr. Chandler was a former CBS executive who played a crucial role in creating the critically acclaimed weekly newsmagazine “60 Minutes.”

name: Richard Topus
profession: Pigeon Trainer in World War II
headline: Richard Topus, a Pigeon Trainer in World War II, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Topus, just 18 when he enlisted in the Army, was among the last of the several thousand pigeoneers who served the United States in the war.

name: Mildred Constantine
headline: Mildred Constantine, 95, MoMA Curator, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Constantine was a curator who brought new prestige to the graphic design and poster collections of the Museum of Modern Art in the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Lawrence Fane
profession: Sculptor of Abstract Forms With Renaissance Touches
headline: Lawrence Fane, Sculptor of Abstract Forms With Renaissance Touches, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Fane was a sculptor known for using steel, bronze, concrete, wood and other materials to create Expressionistic forms.

name: François-Xavier Lalanne
headline: François-Xavier Lalanne, Surrealistic Sculptor, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Lalanne’s menagerie of surrealistic animal sculptures included a cast-iron baboon, giant turtledoves that doubled as armchairs and a herd of topiary dinosaurs.

name: D. Carleton Gajdusek
profession: Won Nobel for Work on Brain Disease
headline: D. Carleton Gajdusek, Who Won Nobel for Work on Brain Disease, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Dr. Gajdusek was a virologist who won the 1976 Nobel Prize in medicine for his work on the mysterious epidemics now known as prion diseases.

name: George Brecht
headline: George Brecht, 82, Fluxus Conceptual Artist, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Brecht was a core member of Fluxus, the loosely affiliated international group of playful Conceptual artists that emerged in the early 1960s.

name: Warren M. Robbins
headline: Warren M. Robbins, Collector of African Art, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Robbins’ purchase of a carved-wood figure in a German antiques shop became the seed of the Smithsonian Institution’s National Museum of African Art.

name: León Febres Cordero
headline: León Febres Cordero, Former Leader of Ecuador, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Mr. Cordero was a pistol-wielding, chain-smoking, horse-breeding businessman who served a tumultuous term as Ecuador’s president in the 1980s.

name: C. Caracciolo
headline: C. Caracciolo, 83, a Publisher and La Repubblica Founder, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Caracciolo was a leading Italian publisher who was a co-founder of the influential newspaper La Repubblica and was known as “the editor prince.”

name: G. Franco Romagnoli
headline: G. Franco Romagnoli, 82, Italian Chef, Dies
abstract: With his wife, Margaret, Mr. Romagnoli helped introduce Americans to authentic Italian home cooking on the 1970s PBS series “The Romagnolis’ Table” and in a series of best-selling cookbooks.

name: John W. Powell
headline: John W. Powell, 89, Dies; Writer in Sedition Case
abstract: Mr. Powell was tried for sedition in 1959 in a rare and highly public case after he asserted in print that the United States had used biological weapons in the Korean War.

name: John E. Sprizzo
headline: John E. Sprizzo, 73, U.S. Judge, Dies
abstract: Mr. Sprizzo’s intellect and temper made him one of the more colorful court presences in the Southern District of New York.

name: Sammy Baugh
profession: Top Quarterback and Key Figure in Early N.F.L
headline: Sammy Baugh, Top Quarterback and Key Figure in Early N.F.L., Dies at 94
abstract: As quarterback for the Washington Redskins, Baugh helped make the N.F.L. a high-scoring spectacle.

name: Martha Putney
headline: Martha Putney, Historian of Blacks, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mrs. Putney became one of the first black women to serve in the Women’s Army Corps during World War II and went on to write pioneering works on black Americans in the military.

name: Sam Bottoms
headline: Sam Bottoms, Film and TV Actor, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Bottoms, the third in a family of four acting brothers, was perhaps best known for his performance in “Apocalypse Now.”

name: Paul Weyrich
headline: Paul Weyrich, 66, a Conservative Strategist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Weyrich’s principles, fervor and skills were instrumental in propelling the right wing of the Republican Party to power and prominence in the 1980s and ’90s.

name: Howard Pack
headline: Howard Pack, 90, Magnate and Innovator in Shipping, Dies
abstract: Mr. Pack, who as president and later chairman of Seatrain Lines was a leader in the industry in changing the way ships carry goods from port to port.

name: Davy Graham
headline: Davy Graham, Widely Influential British Guitarist, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Graham was a British guitarist whose musical fusions, technique and tuning shaped generations of musicians.

name: W. Mark Felt
headline: W. Mark Felt, Watergate Deep Throat, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Felt, the No. 2 F.B.I. official when he helped bring down President Richard M. Nixon, became the most famous anonymous source in American history.

name: Conor Cruise O’Brien
headline: Conor Cruise O’Brien, Irish Diplomat, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. O’Brien was an Irish diplomat, politician, man of letters and public intellectual who staked out an independent position for Ireland in the United Nations.

name: David Margolis
profession: Industrialist and Aide to Mayor Koch
headline: David Margolis, Industrialist and Aide to Mayor Koch, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Margolis was an industrialist who revived Colt Industries and became a close adviser to former Mayor Edward I. Koch.

name: David Margolis
headline: David Margolis, a Justice Department Institution, Dies at 76
abstract: Known for a sharp legal mind and unpredictable attire, Mr. Margolis over 50 years led some of the nation’s biggest mobster and espionage investigations.

name: Julius Fast
profession: Writer of Both Fact and Fiction
headline: Julius Fast, 89, Writer of Both Fact and Fiction, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Fast won the first Edgar Award given by the Mystery Writers of America and went on to publish popular books on body language, the Beatles and human relationships.

name: Dock Ellis
headline: Dock Ellis, All-Star Pitcher Who Overcame Longtime Addictions, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Ellis infamously claimed he pitched a no-hitter for Pittsburgh under the influence of LSD and later fiercely spoke out against drug and alcohol addiction.

name: Carol Chomsky
headline: Carol Chomsky, 78, Linguist and Educator, Dies
abstract: Professor Chomsky was a linguist and education specialist whose work helped illuminate the ways in which language comes to children.

name: David Lieber
headline: Rabbi David Lieber, Scholar and University President, Dies at 83
abstract: Rabbi Lieber was a leader of Conservative Judaism in the United States and the editor of a controversial book of Torah translation and commentary.

name: William Kaufmann
headline: William Kaufmann, Nuclear Strategist Who Helped Reshape Policy, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Kaufmann was a close adviser to seven defense secretaries and a major proponent of a shift away from the early cold war strategy of mass nuclear retaliation.

name: Bernard Crick
headline: Sir Bernard Crick, Political Theorist, Dies at 79
abstract: Sir Bernard was a prominent democratic socialist and political theorist who also wrote the first complete biography of George Orwell, one of his heroes.

name: Olga Lepeshinskaya
headline: Olga Lepeshinskaya, 92, Soviet Ballerina, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Lepeshinskaya was a leading ballerina of the Bolshoi Ballet in the 1940s and ’50s, often praised for her spirited projection and versatility.

name: A. Carl Kotchian
headline: A. Carl Kotchian, Lockheed Executive, Dies at 94
abstract: The former president of the Lockheed Aircraft Corporation was a central figure in a bribery scandal that rocked Japan and the Netherlands during the 1970s.

name: James L. Bevel
headline: James L. Bevel, 72, an Adviser to Dr. King, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Bevel’s influence spurred the “children’s crusade” in Birmingham, Ala., a pivotal event of the civil rights movement, but his reputation was later marred by a conviction on incest charges.

name: Robert Mulligan
headline: Robert Mulligan, Director, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. Mulligan, best known for directing the 1962 classic film “To Kill a Mockingbird,” was often commended for his keen attention to the inner lives of young people.

name: Adrian Mitchell
profession: British Poetrys Voice of the Left
headline: Adrian Mitchell, British Poetry’s Voice of the Left, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Mitchell’s impassioned verse against social injustice, racism and violence was often declaimed at antiwar rallies and political demonstrations.

name: Robert Marshall
headline: Robert Marshall, Church Leader, 90, Dies
abstract: Dr. Marshall was an ecumenist who in the 1970s led the Lutheran Church in America, then the nation’s largest Lutheran church, and helped pave the way for its merger with two other denominations.

name: Robert O. Marshall
profession: Convicted in Blind Faith Murder-for-Hire Case
headline: Robert O. Marshall Dies at 75; Convicted in ‘Blind Faith’ Murder-for-Hire Case
abstract: Mr. Marshall was serving a life sentence in the 1984 contract murder of his wife, a case that became the subject of Joe McGinniss’s book “Blind Faith.”

name: Al Meyerhoff
headline: Al Meyerhoff, Legal Voice for the Poor, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Meyerhoff was a leading labor, environmental and civil rights lawyer who brought a landmark case to stop sweatshop conditions for 30,000 workers on the Pacific island of Saipan.

name: David Rampe
headline: David Rampe, Veteran Times Editor, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Rampe helped shape the newspaper’s coverage of the Sept. 11 attacks and the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq.

name: Thomas B. Congdon
profession: Editor of Best Sellers Like Jaws
headline: Thomas B. Congdon, Editor of Best Sellers Like ‘Jaws,’ Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Congdon shepherded into print Russell Baker’s memoir and David Halberstam’s mammoth tome about the auto industry, eventually founding his own publishing house.

name: Valentin Berlinsky
profession: Mainstay Cellist of the Borodin Quartet
headline: Valentin Berlinsky, Mainstay Cellist of the Borodin Quartet, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Berlinsky was the longest-serving member of the group, one of the most renowned string quartets in the world and by all accounts the longest continuously playing one.

name: Harold Pinter
headline: Harold Pinter, Playwright of the Pause, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Pinter’s gift for finding the noise within silence made him the most influential dramatist of his generation.

name: Eartha Kitt
headline: Eartha Kitt, a Seducer of Audiences, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Kitt purred and pounced her way through a career in show business that lasted more than six decades.

name: Hillary Waugh
headline: Hillary Waugh, Prolific Mystery Author, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Waugh helped pioneer the police procedural novel in dozens of mysteries, notably “Last Seen Wearing” (1952).

name: Dale Wasserman
headline: Dale Wasserman, Playwright, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Wasserman was an autodidact who became the playwright responsible for two Broadway hits of the 1960s, “One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest” and “Man of La Mancha.”

name: Alvah H. Chapman Jr.
headline: Alvah H. Chapman Jr., Civic-Minded Leader of Knight Ridder, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Chapman was the former publisher of The Miami Herald and chairman of the Knight Ridder newspapers and one of South Florida’s most influential philanthropic and civic leaders.

name: Dorothy Sarnoff
headline: Dorothy Sarnoff, a Pioneer of the Self-Help Movement, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Sarnoff was an opera singer and Broadway star, and one of the first, and most influential, image consultants.

name: Samuel P. Huntington
headline: Samuel P. Huntington, 81, Political Scientist, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Huntington was an influential political scientist who taught at Harvard for more than a half-century and produced new analyses of domestic and international conflicts.

name: Abbott Combes
headline: Abbott Combes, 64, Magazine Editor, Dies
abstract: Mr. Combes spent 27 years as a copy editor at The New York Times Magazine and helped create its "About Men" column.

name: Arnold Jacob Wolf
headline: Arnold Jacob Wolf, a Leading Reform Rabbi, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Rabbi Wolf was known for his progressive, sometimes provocative public stances, including opposition to the Vietnam War and accusations of anti-Semitism at Yale.

name: Freddie Hubbard
headline: Freddie Hubbard, Jazz Trumpeter, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Hubbard dazzled audiences and critics alike with his virtuosity, his melodicism and his infectious energy.

name: Delaney Bramlett
headline: Delaney Bramlett, Singer-Songwriter and Slide Guitarist, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Bramlett’s bluesy, gospel- and country-flavored music influenced Eric Clapton and George Harrison, and his songs were covered by popular musicians ranging from Ray Charles to Sonic Youth.

name: Willoughby Sharp
headline: Willoughby Sharp, Avant-Garde Artist and Performer, Dies at 72
abstract: In the 1960s and afterward, Mr. Sharp was on the cutting edge of the American avant-garde as a performer, producer, writer, publisher, curator, video artist and much else.

name: Werner Wiskari
headline: Werner Wiskari, Times Editor, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Wiskari was a former foreign correspondent and editor of international news for The New York Times.

name: Robert Nylen
headline: Robert Nylen, Magazine Founder and Publisher, Is Dead at 64
abstract: Mr. Nylen was a founder and the publisher of New England Monthly, a highly regarded regional magazine published from 1984 to 1990.

name: Jack D. Kuehler
headline: Jack D. Kuehler, Former I.B.M. President, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Kuehler guided the company while it dominated the world’s computing landscape in the 1980s.

name: Paul Hofmann
headline: Paul Hofmann, Author and Foe of Nazis, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Hofmann acted as an informer for the Allies while serving on the staff of the German commandants and later became a foreign correspondent for The New York Times.

name: Ted Lapidus
headline: Ted Lapidus, Designer Who Reshaped French Fashion, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Lapidus shook up French fashion in the 1960s and ’70s with the safari suit, military jackets for women and ready-to-wear unisex clothing.

name: Helen Suzman
headline: Helen Suzman, Relentless Challenger of Apartheid System, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mrs. Suzman befriended the imprisoned Nelson Mandela and offered an often lonely voice for change among South Africa’s white minority.

name: Donald E. Westlake
headline: Donald E. Westlake, Mystery Writer, Is Dead at 75
abstract: The prolific, award-winning novelist pounded out more than 100 books and five screenplays during his career.

name: Claiborne Pell
profession: Patrician Senator Behind College Grant Program
headline: Claiborne Pell, Patrician Senator Behind College Grant Program, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Pell, a six-term former senator from Rhode Island, created the college grant program that bears his name.

name: Michael Levey
headline: Sir Michael Levey, 81, Art Historian, Is Dead
abstract: The prolific and wide-ranging art historian presided over the expansion of the National Gallery in London as its director.

name: Daniel Nagrin
headline: Daniel Nagrin Dies at 91; Modern Dancer and Choreographer
abstract: Mr. Nagrin was known for intensely dramatic solos that became modern-dance classics.

name: Willard W. Scott Jr.
headline: Willard W. Scott Jr. Is Dead at 82; Led West Point Through Change
abstract: General Scott lifted academic and social standards as leader of the U.S. Military Academy at West Point after it was roiled by a cheating scandal and the introduction of women as cadets.

name: Willard Scott
profession: TVs Clown Prince of Sun and Showers
headline: Willard Scott, TV’s Clown Prince of Sun and Showers, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Scott, who played both Bozo the Clown and the original Ronald McDonald on television, was a longtime weather forecaster on the “Today” show who emphasized showmanship over science.

name: Christian Wölffer
headline: Christian Wölffer, a Long Island Vintner, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Mr. Wölffer was the founder of Wölffer Estate Vineyard, a highly regarded boutique winery on Long Island.

name: Lloyd E. Ohlin
headline: Lloyd E. Ohlin, Expert on Crime and Punishment, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Professor Ohlin was a prominent criminologist who explored both the social underpinnings of crime and the social consequences of punishment.

name: William R. Glendon
profession: Argued for Right to Publish Pentagon Papers
headline: William R. Glendon, 89, Dies; Argued for Right to Publish Pentagon Papers
abstract: Mr. Glendon was a First Amendment lawyer who represented The Washington Post in the Pentagon Papers case.

name: Oliver Lincoln Lundquist
headline: Oliver Lincoln Lundquist, Designer, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Lundquist, an architect and industrial designer, led the team that created the United Nations logo.

name: Vincent Ford
headline: Vincent Ford Dies at 68; Inspired Classic Bob Marley Songs
abstract: Writing credit and royalties for “No Woman, No Cry,” “Positive Vibration,” “Roots Rock Reggae” and “Crazy Baldheads,” went to Mr. Ford.

name: Victor H. Krulak
headline: Victor H. Krulak, Marine Behind U.S. Landing Craft, Dies at 95
abstract: General Krulak was a highly decorated Marine commander who championed innovative tactics in World War II, Korea and Vietnam.

name: Nick Scandone
headline: Nick Scandone, Winner of Paralympics Sailing Gold, Is Dead at 42
abstract: Scandone was a sailing gold medalist at the Beijing Paralympics and a former United States Yachtsman of the Year.

name: Pat Hingle
profession: Versatile Actor With Recurring Role in Batman Movies
headline: Pat Hingle, Versatile Actor With Recurring Role in Batman Movies, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Hingle was a versatile character actor of stage and screen who became accustomed to winning critical praise in a career that spanned five decades.

name: Griffin Bell
headline: Griffin Bell, Ex-Attorney General, Dies at 90
abstract: The dean of Georgia lawyers, Mr. Bell also served as a federal judge and prominent legal troubleshooter.

name: Carl R. Pohlad
headline: Carl R. Pohlad, Owner of Minnesota Twins, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Pohlad was a son of a railroad brakeman who grew up to become one of the richest men in America and a forceful owner of the Minnesota Twins.

name: Christopher Hibbert
headline: Christopher Hibbert, 84, Lively Historian, Dies
abstract: Mr. Hibbert won a wide readership with his popular approach to historical subjects.

name: G. Grinberg
headline: G. Grinberg, Watch Baron, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Grinberg amassed a fortune in the U.S. by helping turn expensive wristwatches like Piaget into widely advertised portable status symbols with mass appeal.

name: John F. McGillicuddy
headline: John F. McGillicuddy, 78, Banking Leader, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. McGillicuddy assembled one of first big bank mergers in the wave of consolidation that emerged from the economic slump of the early 1990s.

name: Richard Seaver
headline: Richard Seaver, Publisher, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Seaver defied censorship and conventional literary standards to bring works by rabble-rousing authors like Samuel Beckett, Henry Miller and William Burroughs to American readers.

name: Betty Freeman
headline: Betty Freeman, Patron of New Music, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Freeman was one of the most influential patrons of contemporary composers over the last 40 years and long the keeper of a famously gracious musical salon in Los Angeles.

name: Edd Cartier
headline: Edd Cartier, 94, Pulp Illustrator, Dies
abstract: Mr. Cartier’s noirish illustrations for the pulp magazine The Shadow and action-packed, often whimsical illustrations for stories by L. Ron Hubbard, Isaac Asimov and other writers made him one of the leading science-fiction and horror artists of his time.

name: Ron Asheton
headline: Ron Asheton, Guitarist in the Stooges, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Asheton was a guitarist of the Michigan proto-punk band the Stooges, and the guiding hand of some of the most simple, satisfying and copied riffs in rock ’n’ roll.

name: Didier Aaron
headline: Didier Aaron, 85, French Antiques Dealer, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Aaron was the Paris antiques dealer whose gallery on Rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré became the center of a mini-empire of fine French furniture.

name: Ned Tanen
profession: Movie Executive With a Taste for Youth Films
headline: Ned Tanen, Movie Executive With a Taste for Youth Films, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Tanen seemed to have a Midas touch in bringing youth-oriented films like “American Graffiti” and “Animal House” to the screen.

name: Israel Horowitz
headline: Israel Horowitz, Record Producer and Billboard Columnist, Dies at 92
abstract: As the director of classical artists and repertory for Decca Records from 1958 to 1971, Mr. Horowitz produced many influential recordings.

name: R. J. Neuhaus
headline: Rev. R. J. Neuhaus, Political Theologian, Dies at 72
abstract: The Rev. Richard John Neuhaus went from a liberal Lutheran leader of the struggles in the 1960s to a Roman Catholic beacon of the neoconservative movement.

name: Gaston Lenôtre
headline: Gaston Lenôtre, Who Built a Culinary Brand, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Lenôtre was the founder of the restaurant, catering, retail and cooking school empire of the same name, and rejuvenated pastry making in the early 1960s.

name: Charles Morgan Jr.
headline: Charles Morgan Jr., 78, Dies; Leading Civil Rights Lawyer
abstract: Mr. Morgan was often vilified and threatened by fellow whites, but he pressed on to win a lawsuit that helped establish the so-called one-person-one-vote rule, giving blacks more equitable representation.

name: W. D. Zantzinger
headline: W. D. Zantzinger, Subject of Dylan Song, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Zantzinger’s six-month sentence in the fatal caning of a black barmaid moved Bob Dylan to write a dramatic, almost journalistic song in 1963 that became a classic of modern American folk music.

name: Joe Hirsch
headline: Joe Hirsch, Horse Racing Writer, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Hirsch wrote about horse racing for The Daily Racing Form for 55 years and his personal access to the leaders of the sport made him unusually influential.

name: Donald F. Gleason
headline: Donald F. Gleason, 88, Dies; Devised Prostate Test
abstract: Dr. Gleason devised the Gleason score, which has been used to help determine the aggressiveness of prostate cancer in millions of men.

name: Harry W. O. Kinnard
headline: Harry W. O. Kinnard, Who Said One Word Would Do, Dies at 93
abstract: General Kinnard inspired the storied retort “nuts” to a German surrender ultimatum during the Battle of the Bulge.

name: Claude Jeter
headline: Claude Jeter, Gospel Singer With Wide Influence, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Jeter was the founder of the gospel group the Swan Silvertones and had a wide influence on both pop and religious singers in the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Philip Egan
headline: Philip Egan, a Designer of a Fabled Sedan, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Egan was an industrial designer and author who was one of the last surviving members of the Tucker ’48 design team.

name: Inger Christensen
headline: Inger Christensen, Scandinavian Poet, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Ms. Christensen was a distinguished Danish poet whose work was a cornerstone of modern Scandinavian poetry.

name: Steven Gilborn
headline: Steven Gilborn, Stage and Television Actor, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Gilborn was a ubiquitous stage, film and television actor best known for his role as Ellen DeGeneres’s father on the TV sitcom “Ellen” in the 1990s.

name: Harvey Ginsberg
profession: Editor of Saul Bellow and John Irving
headline: Harvey Ginsberg, Editor of Saul Bellow and John Irving, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Ginsberg spent 36 years in the close reading and persnickety polishing of prose.

name: Leonard E. B. Andrews
headline: Leonard E. B. Andrews, Buyer of Wyeth Art, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Andrews rocked the art world when he bought 240 previously unknown Andrew Wyeth works depicting a mysterious, sometimes nude woman known as Helga.

name: Sidney Wood
headline: Sidney Wood, Winner of Wimbledon by Default, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Wood was the only player to win a Wimbledon championship without having to show up for the final match.

name: Pio Laghi
headline: Pio Laghi, Papal Envoy, Dies at 86
abstract: Cardinal Laghi served as the Vatican’s first papal nuncio to Washington until 1990, and in 2003 urged President Bush not to start the war in Iraq.

name: Claude Berri
profession: French Filmmaker of Sweep and Charm
headline: Claude Berri, French Filmmaker of Sweep and Charm, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Berri was involved in every aspect of French cinema over more than a half-century as an actor, writer, director and producer.

name: Tom O’Horgan
headline: Tom O’Horgan, 84, Director of ‘Hair,’ Is Dead
abstract: Mr. O'Horgan was a famously innovative director who brought a Downtown, countercultural sensibility to Uptown theater.

name: Coosje van Bruggen
headline: Coosje van Bruggen, Sculptor, Dies at 66
