abstract: Ms. van Bruggen was a critic, art historian and artist known for the colorful public sculptures she created around the world with her husband, the Pop artist Claes Oldenburg.

name: Don Galloway
headline: Don Galloway, a Familiar Face on Television, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Galloway played well-groomed, straight-arrow characters in myriad television shows and movies.

name: Harold A. Ellis
headline: Harold A. Ellis Dies at 77; Started Realty Chain
abstract: Mr. Ellis was a founder of the international real estate company Grubb & Ellis and a leader in the consolidation of small neighborhood brokerage companies into major national chains.

name: Harold Snyder
headline: Harold Snyder, Generic Drug Pioneer, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Snyder started Biocraft Laboratories in Elmwood Park, N.J., an early and highly successful manufacturer of generic equivalents for brand-name pharmaceuticals.

name: Preston Gómez
headline: Preston Gómez, Native of Cuba Who Managed in Major Leagues, Dies at 85
abstract: Gómez, the second Latin manager in major league baseball, had a career that spanned 65 seasons.

name: Arne Naess
headline: Arne Naess, Norwegian Philosopher, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Naess’s ideas about promoting an intimate and all-embracing relationship between the earth and the human species inspired people around the world.

name: Hortense Calisher
headline: Hortense Calisher, Author, Dies at 97
abstract: Miss Calisher’s unpredictable turns of phrase, intellectually challenging fictional situations and complex plots captivated and puzzled readers for a half-century.

name: Ricardo Montalbán
headline: Ricardo Montalbán, Star of ‘Fantasy Island,’ Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Montalbán, one of Hollywood’s first Latino leading men, had a long career as a television and movie actor but is perhaps best remembered as the debonair concierge of “Fantasy Island.”

name: Patrick McGoohan
headline: Patrick McGoohan, Star of ‘The Prisoner,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. McGoohan was a multifaceted actor who spun television legend by creating and starring in the 1960s program “The Prisoner.”

name: W.D. Snodgrass
headline: W.D. Snodgrass, 83, a Poet of Intensely Autobiographical Themes, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Snodgrass found the stuff of poetry in the raw material of his emotional life and forged a bold, self-analytical poetic style in postwar America.

name: John DeFrancis
headline: John DeFrancis, Chinese Language Scholar, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Few scholars of Chinese wrote more probingly about the language than Mr. DeFrancis, and fewer still created teaching materials that had so widespread an impact on generations of students.

name: Gage Bush Englund
headline: Gage Bush Englund, Ballet Mistress and Dancer, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Englund was a ballet mistress of ABT II, a former dancer with American Ballet Theater and the Joffrey Ballet and a former ballet mistress of the Joffrey II Dancers.

name: Trammell Crow
headline: Trammell Crow, Innovative Developer, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Crow began his legendary business career as the teller behind the window at a Dallas bank and rose to become one of America’s largest real estate developers and landlords.

name: Peter E. Fleming Jr.
headline: Peter E. Fleming Jr., 79, Dies; Defense Lawyer Who Relished the Limelight
abstract: Mr. Fleming was a prominent criminal-defense lawyer whose client list included high-ranking politicians, flamboyant celebrities and a cast of characters from outbreaks of corporate crime.

name: Ray Yoshida
headline: Ray Yoshida, 78, Collagist and Painter, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Yoshida’s mysteriously comical, semi-abstract paintings and collages influenced generations of prominent artists.

name: Pedro Aguilar
headline: Pedro Aguilar, Inventive Mambo Dancer, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Aguilar’s innovative style of mambo dancing made him a legend at the Palladium ballroom in Manhattan and a one-man encyclopedia of Latin dance.

name: Gary Kurfirst
profession: Rock Promoter and Manager of the Talking Heads
headline: Gary Kurfirst, Rock Promoter and Manager of the Talking Heads, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Kurfirst helped shape a generation’s pop music aesthetic as a manager, promoter, publisher, producer and label executive.

name: Andrew Wyeth
headline: Andrew Wyeth, Painter, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Wyeth, whose precise realist views of rural life sparked endless debates about the nature of modern art, was 91.

name: John Mortimer
headline: John Mortimer, Barrister and Writer Who Created Rumpole, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Mortimer was a barrister, author, playwright and the creator of Horace Rumpole, the cunning defender of the British criminal classes.

name: Harlington Wood Jr.
headline: Harlington Wood Jr., 88, Siege Negotiator, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Wood was the government’s chief negotiator during the standoff with American Indian militants in South Dakota that became known as the siege of Wounded Knee.

name: John R. Stallings Jr.
headline: John R. Stallings Jr., 73, California Mathematician, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Stallings found a proof for part of the Poincaré Conjecture, one of the longest-standing problems in mathematics.

name: Henry Turner
headline: Henry Turner, 76, Historian and Author, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Turner was a leading historian whose book “German Big Business and the Rise of Hitler” (1985) challenged the widely held theory that German industrialists were the Nazi Party’s most influential supporters.

name: Clint Ballard Jr.
headline: Clint Ballard Jr., Writer of Hit Songs, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Ballard was a Texas-born songwriter whose songs included the 1965 hit “The Game of Love” and Linda Ronstadt’s No. 1 single “You’re No Good” from 1975.

name: Shigeo Fukuda
headline: Shigeo Fukuda, Graphic Designer, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Fukuda was an influential Japanese graphic designer who was known for acerbic antiwar and environmental advocacy posters.

name: José Torres
profession: Boxing Hall of Famer and Official
headline: José Torres, 72, Boxing Hall of Famer and Official, Dies
abstract: Mr. Torres was a former light-heavyweight champion who became a boxing official and a literary presence in the sport as a biographer of Muhammad Ali and Mike Tyson.

name: José Torres
headline: José Torres, 73, Restaurateur Beloved of Salsa Stars, Dies
abstract: His Joe’s Place was a must for a stop-off after a night of music-making. Mr. Torres died of Covid-19.

name: Edmund de Rothschild
headline: Edmund de Rothschild, Banker, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Mr. de Rothschild led the development of a major hydroelectric project in Canada while helping his firm expand globally and opening it to people outside his family.

name: Rob Roy Buckingham
headline: Rob Roy Buckingham, 88, Retired Editor at The Times, Dies
abstract: Mr. Buckingham was a former editor-manager of The New York Times News Service, which sent roughly 20,000 words of synopses of Times articles to 50 newspapers a day.

name: Dante Lavelli
profession: Cleveland Browns Receiver Known as Gluefingers
headline: Dante Lavelli, Cleveland Browns Receiver Known as Gluefingers, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Lavelli, a Hall of Fame receiver nicknamed Gluefingers, helped the Cleveland Browns build a football dynasty with seven championships in the 1940s and ’50s.

name: Jean Jadot
headline: Jean Jadot, Papal Envoy, Dies at 99
abstract: Archbishop Jadot was the chief papal representative to the United States in the 1970s who drew fire from conservatives for pushing liberal reforms in the American church.

name: David Newman
headline: David (Fathead) Newman, Saxophonist, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Newman was a soft-spoken, sweet-toned jazz and rhythm-and-blues saxophonist who made his name in Ray Charles’s bands from the 1950s to the early ’70s.

name: George Perle
headline: George Perle, a Composer and Theorist, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Perle was a composer, author, theorist and teacher who won the Pulitzer Prize for music in 1986 and was widely considered the poetic voice of atonal composition.

name: Bill Werber
headline: Bill Werber, Infielder Who Played With Ruth, Is Dead at 100
abstract: Mr. Werber was a link to the Yankees of Babe Ruth and Lou Gehrig and was the leadoff hitter in the first major league baseball game to be televised.

name: Constance E. Cook
headline: Constance E. Cook, 89, Who Wrote Abortion Law, Is Dead
abstract: Mrs. Cook was a former New York State assemblywoman who co-authored a law that legalized abortion in the state three years before Roe v. Wade.

name: Kay Yow
profession: Hall of Fame Womens Basketball Coach
headline: Kay Yow, Hall of Fame Women’s Basketball Coach, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Yow was the Hall of Fame basketball coach who became an inspiring figure while continuing to coach the North Carolina State women’s team during a long battle with cancer.

name: Sybil R. Moses
profession: Prosecutor and Longtime New Jersey Judge
headline: Sybil R. Moses, Prosecutor and Longtime New Jersey Judge, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Moses was the prosecuting attorney in the 1970s “Dr. X” trial and later became a judge in New Jersey.

name: Nora Kovach
headline: Nora Kovach, Ballerina Who Defected From Hungary, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Ms. Kovach caused a sensation in 1953 with Istvan Rabovsky when they became the first highly publicized dance defectors to the West from the Soviet bloc.

name: Jim Horne
profession: Familiar Face in Ads From the 1950s
headline: Jim Horne, a Familiar Face in Ads From the 1950s, Dies at 91
abstract: Beginning in the late 1940s, Mr. Horne was perhaps the most widely seen male model in the country, appearing in hundreds of advertisements.

name: Aron Moscona
headline: Aron Moscona, 87, Biologist Who Explored Embryonic Cells, Dies
abstract: Dr. Moscona provided early insights into how cells in the developing embryo find one another and interact.

name: James Swett
headline: James Swett, Who Downed 7 Planes in Attack, Dies at 88
abstract: Lieutenant Swett was a Marine fighter pilot who received the Medal of Honor for shooting down seven Japanese planes in the Solomon Islands during his first combat mission of World War II.

name: Lorene Rogers
profession: President of University of Texas in 70s
headline: Lorene Rogers, President of University of Texas in ’70s, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Dr. Rogers, a former president of the University of Texas, Austin, was believed to be the first woman to lead a public university in the country.

name: Jesse Olson
headline: Jesse Olson, 84, Organizer for 1199 Health Care Union, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Olson was a former union vice president who played a major role in expanding the nation’s largest health care workers’ local.

name: J. Lamar Worzel
headline: J. Lamar Worzel, Expert on Ocean’s Depths, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Worzel was an ocean geophysicist and a designer of jury-rigged devices that gave an early view of the peaks and troughs of the deep sea and revealed the way sound flows below the waves.

name: Jan Kaplicky
headline: Jan Kaplicky, Audacious Czech Architect, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Mr. Kaplicky was a Czech-born architect who challenged, dazzled and sometimes befuddled the British architectural establishment with his fiercely uncompromising vision.

name: Johannes M. Simmel
headline: Johannes M. Simmel, Writer of Cold-War Novels, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Simmel was an Austrian writer whose cold-war thrillers and sociopolitical novels sold tens of millions of copies.

name: Martin Delaney
headline: Martin Delaney, 63, AIDS Activist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Delaney was a prominent advocate for AIDS patients who challenged the government and drug companies to expedite access to experimental treatments in the early days of the epidemic.

name: Dina Vierny
headline: Dina Vierny, Artist’s Muse, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Vierny was the model whose ample flesh and soft curves inspired the sculptor Aristide Maillol, rejuvenating his career, and who eventually founded a museum dedicated to his work.

name: Charles H. Schneer
headline: Charles H. Schneer, Sci-Fi Film Producer, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Schneer was a noted film producer who for a quarter-century helped the Oscar-winning special-effects wizard Ray Harryhausen lay waste to Washington, San Francisco, Rome and many other places.

name: Allen Zwerdling
headline: Allen Zwerdling, Theater Journalist, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Zwerdling was a founder of Back Stage, the weekly theater newspaper that is widely considered the casting bible for performers.

name: Malcolm MacPherson
headline: Malcolm MacPherson, 65, War Reporter, Dies
abstract: Mr. MacPherson was a former foreign correspondent for Newsweek whose novels and nonfiction books dealt with subjects as varied as Disneyland, the Iraq war and special operations in Afghanistan.

name: John Updike
headline: John Updike, Tireless Chronicler of Small-Town America, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Updike’s novels highlighted so vast and protean a body of fiction, verse, essays and criticism they placed him in the first rank of American men of letters.

name: Aldo Crommelynck
headline: Aldo Crommelynck, Master Printer for Prominent Artists, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Mr. Crommelynck was a master printmaker whose self-effacing style and virtuosic command of traditional techniques coaxed the best out of European artists including Picasso, Braque and Matisse.

name: James Brady
headline: James Brady, Columnist Chronicling the Power Elite, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Brady helped start the Page Six gossip column at The New York Post, chronicled the doings of the New York power elite and wrote a gripping memoir of his combat experience in the Korean War.

name: John P. Diggins
headline: John P. Diggins, 73, Historian, Dies
abstract: Mr. Diggins was an intellectual historian who brought a provocative, revisionist approach to the history of the American left and right.

name: Roy A. Somlyo
headline: Roy A. Somlyo, 83, Theater Producer, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Somlyo produced or managed more than 100 shows on Broadway, in London or on tour and was managing producer of the annual Tony Awards telecast for more than a decade.

name: John Martyn
headline: John Martyn, Folk and Jazz Guitarist, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Martyn was a Scottish singer and guitarist whose gentle mix of folk and jazz and innovative use of electronic effects influenced a broad range of musicians.

name: George Schneeman
headline: George Schneeman, 74, Poet-Artist, Dies
abstract: Over four decades Mr. Schneeman produced hundreds of collaborative pieces that were neither pure visual art nor pure verbal art but something tantalizingly indefinable between the two.

name: Leon Klenicki
headline: Leon Klenicki, Rabbi Who Bridged Gaps Between Faiths, Dies at 78
abstract: Rabbi Klenicki was an influential advocate for improving interfaith relations, particularly with the Roman Catholic Church.

name: David Dodge
headline: David Dodge, an Early Lebanon Hostage, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Dodge was among the first Americans to be kidnapped in Lebanon and held hostage for an extended period during the country’s 15-year civil war.

name: Ingemar Johansson
headline: Ingemar Johansson, Who Beat Patterson for Heavyweight Title, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Johansson, of Sweden, knocked out Floyd Patterson in 1959 to win the world heavyweight boxing championship.

name: Ray Dennis Steckler
headline: Ray Dennis Steckler, Low-Budget Auteur, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Steckler was a director whose surrealistically impossible plots went beyond zombies to display superheroes, rockers, beach girls — and flourishes of what some saw as inspired moviemaking.

name: Lukas Foss
profession: Composer at Home in Many Stylistic Currents
headline: Lukas Foss, Composer at Home in Many Stylistic Currents, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Foss explored the byways of the avant-garde, focusing at different times on techniques from serialism and electronic music to Minimalism and improvisation.

name: John Isaacs
headline: John Isaacs, Star for Rens Basketball, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Isaacs was a key member of the Harlem Renaissance basketball team, which showcased some of New York City’s greatest black players during the Depression.

name: Stephen Zetterberg
headline: Stephen Zetterberg, Nixon Rival, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Zetterberg was a California Democrat whose loss to Richard M. Nixon in a primary race for Congress in 1948 helped propel Nixon’s early career.

name: Irving Feiner
profession: Central Figure in Constitutional Free-Speech Case
headline: Irving Feiner, 84, Central Figure in Constitutional Free-Speech Case, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Feiner played a significant role in the debate over free speech when the Supreme Court upheld his conviction on charges of disorderly conduct for provoking a crowd during a speech.

name: Hank Crawford
headline: Hank Crawford, Prolific Saxophonist, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Crawford’s fluidly emotional saxophone solos as a sideman for Ray Charles led to a long career as a leader of jazz and soul bands and a lengthy discography for Atlantic.

name: Blair Lent
headline: Blair Lent, 80, an Illustrator of Books, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Lent was a children’s book author and award-winning artist whose detailed work illustrated beloved books like “Tikki Tikki Tembo” and “The Funny Little Woman.”

name: Bernard Gladstone
headline: Bernard Gladstone, 87, Columnist, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Gladstone wrote a do-it-yourself home repair column for The New York Times for 32 years and published more than 20 books on the subject.

name: Millard Fuller
headline: Millard Fuller, 74, Who Founded Habitat for Humanity, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Fuller walked away from his life as a successful businessman at age 29 to devote himself to the poor and eventually founded Habitat for Humanity International, which built more than 30,000 homes worldwide.

name: Michael J. Homer
headline: Michael J. Homer, Netscape Executive, Dies at 50
abstract: Mr. Homer, a Silicon Valley executive, played important roles in the development of three waves of technology — the personal computer, the hand-held device and the Internet.

name: Milton Parker
headline: Milton Parker, Carnegie Deli Partner, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Parker brought long lines and renown to the Carnegie Deli in Manhattan with towering pastrami sandwiches and a voluble partner who kibitzed with common folk and celebrities alike.

name: Warren Kimbro
headline: Warren Kimbro, Ex-Panther Who Turned to Life of Service After Killing, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Kimbro, who shot and killed a suspected police informer in New Haven in 1969, later earned a Harvard degree and became a respected community leader.

name: Olga Raggio
headline: Olga Raggio, a Scholar and Art Curator, Dies at 82
abstract: Dr. Raggio, a fixture at the Metropolitan Museum for almost 60 years, organized some of the museum’s best-known exhibits.

name: Lux Interior
headline: Lux Interior, 62, Singer in the Punk-Rock Era, Is Dead
abstract: Lux Interior introduced the excitement of deviant rockabilly to the punk era as the lead singer of the Cramps.

name: Mira Rostova
headline: Mira Rostova, Coach to Montgomery Clift, Dies at 99
abstract: Ms. Rostova was a longtime New York acting teacher whose scene-by-scene, line-by-line coaching of Montgomery Clift earned his unwavering devotion.

name: Alan Scott
headline: Alan Scott, 72, Artisan of the Brick Oven, Dies
abstract: Mr. Scott’s skill in using radiant heat led to a revival of the ancient craft of building brick ovens, allowing bakers to turn out bread with luxuriously moist interiors and crisp crusts.

name: Alan Scott
profession: Doctor Behind the Medical Use of Botox
headline: Alan Scott, Doctor Behind the Medical Use of Botox, Dies at 89
abstract: An ophthalmologist and researcher, he discovered a drug that treated serious eye conditions. It also smoothed wrinkles — and an alternative industry was born.

name: Hans Beck
headline: Hans Beck, Designer of Little Plastic People, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Beck was the designer of the ubiquitous Playmobil figures — little plastic people who can fit into a child’s fist and be right at home in a toy medieval castle or a pony ranch.

name: Ralph Kaplowitz
headline: Ralph Kaplowitz, 89, Dies; Played in Knicks’ First Game
abstract: Mr. Kaplowitz was a guard from the Bronx who was an original Knick, in 1946.

name: Payton Jordan
headline: Payton Jordan, U.S. Track Team Coach, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Jordan was a standout collegiate sprinter who went on to coach the powerful United States track and field team at the 1968 Olympics in Mexico City.

name: James Whitmore
profession: Character Actor Skilled in One-Man Shows
headline: James Whitmore, Character Actor Skilled in One-Man Shows, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Whitmore, a versatile performer with a Tony Award and an Oscar nominee to his credit, won wide acclaim for a pair of one-man performances, as the humorist Will Rogers and a vinegary Harry S. Truman.

name: Dewey Martin
headline: Dewey Martin, 68, of Buffalo Springfield, Dies
abstract: Mr. Martin was the drummer for Buffalo Springfield, the short-lived but influential 1960s California rock band that spawned the careers of Neil Young and Stephen Stills.

name: Daniel Seligman
headline: Daniel Seligman, Longtime Fortune Columnist, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Seligman engaged readers of his “Keeping Up” column in Fortune magazine for more than two decades.

name: William T. Close
profession: Helped Control Ebola Epidemic in Congo
headline: William T. Close, Who Helped Control Ebola Epidemic in Congo, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Close was an American surgeon who played an important role in controlling the first epidemic of the deadly Ebola fever in central Africa and preventing it from spreading.

name: Blossom Dearie
headline: Blossom Dearie, Cult Chanteuse, Dies at 84
abstract: A singer, pianist and songwriter with an independent spirit, Ms. Dearie pursued a singular career that blurred the line between jazz and cabaret.

name: Donald C. Alexander
headline: Donald C. Alexander, 87, Who Resisted Nixon at I.R.S., Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Alexander was a former Internal Revenue Service commissioner who said that President Richard M. Nixon tried to fire him because he would not use the tax agency for political purposes.

name: Max Neuhaus
headline: Max Neuhaus, Who Made Aural Artwork, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Neuhaus was a percussionist known for creating site-specific works of “sound sculpture,” allowing unsuspecting passers-by to come upon musical sounds in unlikely places.

name: Howard Kanovitz
headline: Howard Kanovitz, 79, Who Recreated the Real, Dies
abstract: Mr. Kanovitz was a a pioneer of the Photo Realism style of painting, which emerged in the 1960s as a reaction against abstraction in general and Abstract Expressionism in particular.

name: Betty Jameson
headline: Betty Jameson, a Founder of the L.P.G.A., Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Jameson was a Hall of Fame golfer and a founding member of the women’s professional tour.

name: David C. Sabiston Jr.
headline: David C. Sabiston Jr., Heart Surgeon, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Sabiston led a surgical team in performing an early and daring coronary bypass operation in the 1960s, paving the way for more effective cardiac procedures.

name: Mark Shepherd
headline: Mark Shepherd, a Force in Electronics, Dies at 86
abstract: As an engineer, manager and chief executive of Texas Instruments, Mr. Shepherd headed its rise to power as a maker of semiconductors and consumer electronics.

name: Carolyn George
headline: Carolyn George, City Ballet Soloist, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. George was a photographer and a former soloist with the New York City Ballet whose performances contributed to the young company’s early impact in the 1950s.

name: Ralph E. Carpenter
headline: Ralph E. Carpenter, 99, Dies; Restored Landmarks
abstract: Mr. Carpenter was a self-taught connoisseur of Colonial furniture and decorative art whose passion for Newport, R.I., spurred him to restore many of its most important 18th-century landmarks.

name: Willem Kolff
headline: Willem Kolff, Doctor Who Invented Kidney and Heart Machines, Dies at 97
abstract: After inventing the first artificial kidney, Dr. Kolff went on to prove that biomedical engineers could build all sorts of artificial organs.

name: Hugh Leonard
headline: Hugh Leonard, 82, Dies; Wrote Broadway’s ‘Da’
abstract: Mr. Leonard was a prolific Irish playwright, memoirist, travel writer and dyspeptic newspaper columnist whose autobiographical play “Da” won four Tony Awards in 1978.

name: Alison Des Forges
headline: Alison Des Forges, 66, Human Rights Advocate, Dies
abstract: Dr. Des Forges, a historian who documented the 1994 genocide in Rwanda, was a passenger on Flight 3407.

name: Estelle Bennett
headline: Estelle Bennett, a Singer for the Ronettes, Is Dead at 67
abstract: She was one of the beehived queens of 1960s girl-group pop.

name: Beverly Eckert
headline: Beverly Eckert, Leader of Families of 9/11 Victims, Dies at 57
abstract: Ms. Eckert became a prominent spokeswoman for the families of 9/11 victims after her husband was killed in the attacks.

name: Leila Hadley
profession: Traveled the World and Then Wrote About It
headline: Leila Hadley, Who Traveled the World and Then Wrote About It, Dies at 83
abstract: Mrs. Hadley’s impulsive trip around the world in her 20s led to a career writing travel books like “Give Me the World” and “A Journey With Elsa Cloud.”

name: Joe Goldstein
headline: Joe Goldstein, Dogged New York Sports Promoter, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Goldstein was a publicist who promoted Madison Square Garden basketball, the New York City Marathon and a trotting horse with an addiction to artichoke.

name: Alfred A. Knopf Jr.
headline: Alfred A. Knopf Jr., Influential Publisher, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Knopf left the noted publishing house run by his parents to become one of the founders of Atheneum Publishers in 1959.

name: Jack Cover
headline: Jack Cover, 88, Physicist Who Invented the Taser Stun Gun, Dies
abstract: Mr. Cover invented the Taser stun gun, the police weapon that subdues its targets with jolts of electricity.

name: Stephen Kim Sou-hwan
headline: Stephen Kim Sou-hwan, Cardinal, Dies at 86
abstract: Cardinal Kim was South Korea’s first cardinal and a tireless advocate for democracy who stood up to a series of military dictators.

name: Sigurdur Helgason
headline: Sigurdur Helgason, 87, Airfare Pioneer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Helgason was an Icelander whose pioneering “hippie airline,” then called Icelandic, made low-cost air travel to Europe possible for a generation of Americans.

name: Louie Bellson
headline: Louie Bellson, Dynamic Jazz Drummer, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Bellson was a crisp and dazzling drummer who worked with major figures of the swing era. He proudly maintained that Duke Ellington called him the world’s greatest drummer.

name: Virgil Lee Griffin
headline: Virgil Lee Griffin, Klan Leader, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Griffin was involved in the bloody clash between the Ku Klux Klan and leftist union organizers in Greensboro, N.C., in 1979.

name: Jerry Yang
headline: Jerry Yang, Who Did Early Cloning Work, Dies at 49
abstract: Dr. Yang was a reproductive biologist who did early work on the cloning of farm animals and helped establish the safety of meat and milk produced by cloned cattle.

name: Ben Blank
profession: Innovator of Graphics for TV News
headline: Ben Blank, Innovator of Graphics for TV News, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Blank introduced the concept of using logolike images behind anchors as signatures for major news coverage.

name: Marina Svetlova
headline: Marina Svetlova, Dancer and Teacher, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Svetlova played an important role in American dance education after a wide-ranging performing career in international ballet from the 1930s to the 1960s.

name: Joe Cuba
profession: Bandleader Known as the Father of Latin Boogaloo
headline: Joe Cuba, Bandleader Known as the Father of Latin Boogaloo, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Cuba became known as the father of Latin boogaloo because of a string of innovative hits in the 1960s and ’70s that fused Latin and soul elements.

name: Brad Van Pelt
headline: Former Giants Linebacker Brad Van Pelt Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Van Pelt was a stalwart linebacker for the Giants who was perhaps the best player on the woeful squads fielded by the team in the 1970s.

name: J. Max Bond Jr.
headline: J. Max Bond Jr., Architect, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Bond was the most influential African-American architect in New York and one of a few black architects of national prominence.

name: John McGlinn
headline: John McGlinn, 55, Restorer of Musicals, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. McGlinn was a conductor and musical historian who delved deep into neglected archives to recreate musicals in their original form.

name: Bernard Ashley
headline: Bernard Ashley, Who Operated Laura Ashley Line, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Ashley and his wife founded Laura Ashley, the international company that fashioned tasteful women’s clothing and an array of housewares.

name: Boris Yavitz
headline: Boris Yavitz, 85, Columbia Business Dean, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Yavitz, a dean of the business school at Columbia University, restored its overall standing as a top-flight graduate institution after a period of turmoil.

name: Peer Portner
headline: Peer Portner, Heart Pioneer, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Portner’s studies of the heart led to development of the Novacor pump, an electrical device used to let seriously ill patients survive long enough for a heart transplant.

name: Conchita Cintrón
headline: Conchita Cintrón, ‘Goddess’ of Bullring, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Cintrón, a Peruvian who became known as the Blonde Goddess, broke into the male-dominated sport of bullfighting at age 13.

name: Mary Jacobus
headline: Mary Jacobus, a Times Co. Executive, Dies at 52
abstract: Ms. Jacobus was a New York Times Company executive who had headed The Boston Globe and later led the company’s chain of regional newspapers.

name: Alfred J. Kahn
headline: Alfred J. Kahn, Specialist in Child Welfare Issues, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Kahn was a social-policy scholar and an educator who turned a critical eye on failures of local and state governments in child development and family support.

name: Alfred E. Kahn
headline: Alfred E. Kahn Dies at 93; Prime Mover of Airline Deregulation
abstract: Mr. Kahn, a Cornell economist, knew virtually nothing about the airline industry when President Carter appointed him chairman of the Civil Aeronautics Board.

name: Edward Upward
headline: Edward Upward, Influential Author, Dies at 105
abstract: Mr. Upward was the last living link to writers like Isherwood, W. H. Auden and Stephen Spender who shaped English literature in the 1930s.

name: Wesley McDonald
headline: Wesley McDonald, Who Planned for Grenada, Dies at 84
abstract: Admiral McDonald was the commander of American forces in the Atlantic in 1983 who organized the invasion of the Caribbean island nation of Grenada.

name: Konrad Dannenberg
headline: Konrad Dannenberg, 96, Top Rocket Scientist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Dannenberg was a rocket propulsion expert and one of the last of a 1940s German military-scientific team that switched allegiances at the end of World War II.

name: Gerald Myers
headline: Gerald Myers, 85, Writer on Dance and Philosophy, Dies
abstract: Mr. Myers expressed his missionary zeal for modern dance through the highly unusual position of philosopher in residence of the American Dance Festival.

name: Christopher Nolan
headline: Christopher Nolan, Irish Author, Dies at 43
abstract: Mr. Nolan, who was mute and quadriplegic since birth, produced a highly praised volume at 15 and later published a prize-winning autobiography, “Under the Eye of the Clock.”

name: Eric Blau
headline: Eric Blau, a Creator of ‘Jacques Brel’ Show, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Blau turned his infatuation with the songs of a Belgian-born troubadour into one of Off Broadway’s most enduring hits, “Jacques Brel Is Alive and Well and Living in Paris.”

name: Nonnie Moore
headline: Nonnie Moore, Fashion Editor at Magazines, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Moore brought an eclectic mix to the fashion pages of Mademoiselle, Harper’s Bazaar and later the men’s magazine GQ.

name: Howard Zieff
headline: Howard Zieff, ‘a-Spicy’ Adman Who Became Director, Dies at 81
abstract: In Mr. Zieff’s best-known commercial, a middle-aged actor intones, “Mama mia, that’s a spicy meatball.”

name: Victor Zarnowitz
headline: Victor Zarnowitz, Who Faulted Business Forecasts, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Zarnowitz was an expert on business cycles who for decades traced the history of economic predictions — and often found the forecasting faulty.

name: Pearl Lang
headline: Pearl Lang, Dancer and Choreographer, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Lang was a major exponent of Martha Graham’s choreography, and founded a distinguished company of her own, the Pearl Lang Dance Theater.

name: Philip José Farmer
headline: Philip José Farmer, Daring Science Fiction Writer, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Farmer challenged conventional pieties of science fiction with caustic fables set on bizarre worlds of his own devising.

name: Wilbert Tatum
headline: Wilbert Tatum, Activist Editor, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Tatum was the often provocative former publisher and editor of The New York Amsterdam News, the oldest and best-known of the city’s black newspapers.

name: Sverre Fehn
headline: Sverre Fehn, 84, Architect of Modern Nordic Forms, Dies
abstract: Mr. Fehn’s talent for applying Modernist ideas to traditional Nordic forms and materials made him the most prominent Norwegian architect of the postwar era.

name: Noel Martin
headline: Noel Martin, Inventive Catalog Designer, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Martin was a nationally known graphic designer who was one of the first to modernize art museum catalogs and who simplified the cluttered look of industrial trade catalogs.

name: William J. Jorden
headline: William J. Jorden, Reporter and Envoy, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Jorden was a former diplomatic correspondent of The New York Times who became a diplomat himself, serving as the United States ambassador to Panama.

name: Johnny Kerr
profession: Former Chicago Bulls Coach and Broadcaster
headline: Johnny Kerr, 76, Former Chicago Bulls Coach and Broadcaster, Dies
abstract: Mr. Kerr was the first coach of the Chicago Bulls, and went on to spend more than 30 years as a broadcaster with the National Basketball Association team.

name: Antoinette K-Doe
profession: Turned Club Into Shrine to Husband
headline: Antoinette K-Doe, 66, Who Turned Club Into Shrine to Husband, Dies
abstract: Mrs. K-Doe transformed the Mother-in-Law Lounge in New Orleans into a shrine to her late husband, the rhythm and blues singer Ernie K-Doe.

name: Rhena Schweitzer Miller
headline: Rhena Schweitzer Miller, 90, Dies; Aided Father’s Work
abstract: Mrs. Miller was the child of the Nobel laureate Dr. Albert Schweitzer and the director of the hospital that her father and mother opened in a rain forest in west central Africa.

name: Mary Printz
headline: Mary Printz, an Ear for the Famous, Dies at 85
abstract: Mrs. Printz was a longtime answering service operator, and the inspiration for Adolph Green’s Broadway musical “Bells Are Ringing.”

name: Paul Harvey
profession: Homespun Radio Voice of Middle America
headline: Paul Harvey, Homespun Radio Voice of Middle America, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Harvey captivated millions of American listeners for nearly six decades with his radio news reports and conservative commentaries, delivered nationally on weekdays in a stentorian staccato.

name: Molly Kool
headline: Molly Kool, 93, a Pioneer of the Coastal Waters, Dies
abstract: In the 1930s and ’40s, Ms. Kool plied the lashing waters of the Bay of Fundy as the first woman in North America to be a licensed ship’s captain.

name: Jacob T. Schwartz
headline: Jacob T. Schwartz, 79, Restless Scientist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Schwartz was a mathematician and computer scientist who did seminal research in fields as diverse as molecular biology and robotics.

name: Alan Landers
headline: Alan Landers, Winston Man, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Landers was a model for advertisements of Winston cigarettes and Tiparillo cigars who contracted lung cancer and became a crusader against smoking.

name: Ilya Piatetski-Shapiro
headline: Ilya Piatetski-Shapiro, Math Theorist Who Clashed With Soviets, Dies at 79
abstract: Dr. Piatetski-Shapiro’s outstanding mathematical contributions came despite hardships in the Soviet Union and later the debilitating effects of Parkinson’s disease.

name: Horton Foote
profession: Chronicler of America in Plays and Film
headline: Horton Foote, Chronicler of America in Plays and Film, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Foote, who won the Pulitzer Prize and two Academy Awards, depicted the way ordinary people shoulder the ordinary burdens of life.

name: Tom Cole
headline: Tom Cole, Writer for Film and Stage, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Cole wrote the screenplay for the 1986 film “Smooth Talk,” and the enduring play “Medal of Honor Rag,” which explored the psychological torment of a black soldier in Vietnam.

name: George McAfee
headline: George McAfee, N.F.L. Hall of Famer, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. McAfee carried the football, passed it, kicked and punted it, and roamed the defensive backfield for the mighty Chicago Bears teams of the 1940s.

name: Alvin Klein
headline: Alvin Klein, Times Theater Reviewer, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Klein was a longtime theater reviewer for the Sunday regional sections of The New York Times and for WNYC radio.

name: James Bellows
headline: James Bellows, 86, Newspaper Editor Who Promoted New Journalism, Dies
abstract: Mr. Bellows insisted on stylish writing and bold, clean graphics while he was the editor of three major newspapers, including The New York Herald Tribune.

name: Vivien Raynor
headline: Vivien Raynor, Art Reviewer for The Times, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Raynor wrote wittily and incisively about contemporary art for The New York Times and other publications.

name: Sydney Chaplin
headline: Sydney Chaplin, Actor Who Dodged Father’s Shadow, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Chaplin emerged from the shadow of his famous father, Charlie Chaplin, to carve out a successful stage career that included leading roles opposite Judy Holliday and Barbra Streisand.

name: Ian Carr
profession: Jazz Trumpeter and Author of Miles Davis Biography
headline: Ian Carr, Jazz Trumpeter and Author of Miles Davis Biography, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Carr was a Scottish-born trumpeter who, like his formidable influence, Miles Davis, was an early practitioner of jazz-rock fusion.

name: John Cephas
profession: Guitarist With the Duo Cephas and Wiggins
headline: John Cephas, Guitarist With the Duo Cephas and Wiggins, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Cephas was a guitarist and singer who kept the Piedmont blues style alive as part of the duo Cephas and Wiggins.

name: Doris Cole Abrahams
headline: Doris Cole Abrahams, Theatrical Producer, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Abrahams, a theatrical producer, helped bring Peter Shaffer’s “Equus” and Tom Stoppard’s “Travesties” to Broadway.

name: Schuyler Chapin
profession: Champion of Arts in New York
headline: Schuyler Chapin, Champion of Arts in New York, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Chapin’s string of jobs in the arts included general manager of the Metropolitan Opera, cultural affairs commissioner of New York City and dean of the school of the arts at Columbia University.

name: Mark H. Beers
profession: Expert on Drugs Given to Elderly
headline: Mark H. Beers, 54, Expert on Drugs Given to Elderly, Dies
abstract: Dr. Beers’s seminal research found that some widely used prescription drugs led to harmful and unnecessary side effects in the elderly.

name: Alf Pike
profession: Member of Rangers 1940 Stanley Cup Team
headline: Alf Pike, Member of Rangers’ 1940 Stanley Cup Team, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Pike was one of the last two surviving members of the New York Rangers’ Stanley Cup-winning team of 1940 and later a Rangers coach

name: Hank Locklin
headline: Hank Locklin, Country Singer, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Locklin sang honky-tonk country music and helped shape the lusher, more refined Nashville sound of the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Jimmy Boyd
headline: Jimmy Boyd, Actor and Child Singer, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Boyd recorded “I Saw Mommy Kissing Santa Claus” as a child and went on to an acting career in movies and television.

name: Anna Manahan
headline: Anna Manahan, Tony-Winning Irish Actress, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Ms. Manahan won a Tony for her performance as a physically feeble but monstrously manipulative old woman in Martin McDonagh’s play “The Beauty Queen of Leenane”.

name: Robert J. Cole
headline: Robert J. Cole, Business Journalist, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Cole doggedly covered major mergers and acquisitions in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Charles Lieber
headline: Charles Lieber, Who Studied Alcohol as a Toxin, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Lieber upset scientific dogma by showing that alcohol in excess can cause cirrhosis despite an adequate diet.

name: Flemming Flindt
headline: Flemming Flindt, Dancer, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Flindt was a Danish dancer, choreographer and company director who both preserved his country’s ballet heritage and staged controversial new productions.

name: Willie King
headline: Willie King, Bluesman, Is Dead at 65
abstract: Mr. King first came to prominence outside west Alabama with his critically acclaimed 2001 CD, “Freedom Creek,” on the Rooster Blues record label.

name: Ian Alger
headline: Ian Alger, Pioneer in Innovative Therapeutic Techniques, Dies at 82
abstract: Dr. Alger, a New York psychiatrist, pioneered the use of video recordings in therapy and was an early proponent of therapy through videoconferencing.

name: Mary Warburg
headline: Mary Warburg, a Noted Philanthropist, Dies at 100
abstract: Mrs. Warburg, the widow of Edward M.M. Warburg, was a board member of many charitable organizations including the Henry Street Settlement and the United Negro College Fund.

name: Ralph Mercado
headline: Ralph Mercado, Impresario, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Mercado took his passion for Latin music and built an empire around it, staging concerts and creating a recording and publishing label, a film and video company, and nightclubs and restaurants.

name: Tullio Pinelli
headline: Tullio Pinelli, Screenwriter for Fellini, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Pinelli’s prolific screenwriting career included a long partnership with the director Federico Fellini, with whom he wrote “I Vitelloni,” “La Strada,” “La Dolce Vita” and “8 ½.”

name: Leonore Annenberg
headline: Leonore Annenberg, Philanthropist, Dies at 91
abstract: Mrs. Annenberg was the society doyenne who, with her husband, the ambassador and publisher Walter H. Annenberg, gave away billions to philanthropic causes.

name: Steve Bernard
headline: Steve Bernard, Who Founded Cape Cod Chips, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Bernard started Cape Cod Potato Chips in 1980 from a storefront in Hyannis, Mass., with the brand eventually finding its way to food markets nationwide.

name: Ernest Trova
headline: Ernest Trova, ‘Falling Man’ Artist, Is Dead at 82
abstract: The artist’s signature creation appeared in a series of sculptures and paintings and became a symbol of an imperfect humanity hurtling into the future.

name: James Purdy
profession: Literary Outsider With a Piercing Vision
headline: James Purdy, a Literary Outsider With a Piercing Vision, Is Dead at 94
abstract: The writer’s dark, often savagely comic fiction evoked an American psychic landscape of deluded innocence, sexual obsession, violence and isolation.

name: David G. Taylor
headline: David G. Taylor, Banker Who Helped Engineer a Bailout, Dies at 79
abstract: In 1984 Mr. Taylor helped negotiate what was then the biggest federal bailout of a financial institution.

name: Aaron Gural
headline: Aaron Gural, Real Estate Executive, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Gural was the longtime chairman of Newmark & Company, one of New York’s largest commercial real estate companies, from 1957 to 1998.

name: Joseph Bloch
headline: Joseph Bloch, Guide to Juilliard Pianists, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Bloch was a professor of piano literature at the Juilliard School for five decades, during which he taught many of the best-known performers of the second half of the 20th century.

name: Thomas T. Goldsmith Jr.
headline: Thomas T. Goldsmith Jr., a TV Technology Pioneer, Dies at 99
abstract: With his boss, Allen B. DuMont, Dr. Goldsmith and others in the nascent industry perfected the cathode ray tube that eventually let little wooden boxes bring moving images into millions of homes.

name: Joseph C. Martin
profession: Used Fight With Alcohol to Aid Others
headline: Rev. Joseph C. Martin Is Dead at 84; Used Fight With Alcohol to Aid Others
abstract: Father Martin’s battle with alcoholism inspired him to become a leader in the fight against the disease by speaking, writing books, making videos and starting a treatment center.

name: Ron Silver
headline: Ron Silver, 62, Persuasive Actor and Activist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Silver played Henry Kissinger, Alan Dershowitz and Angelo Dundee on the screen and supported Bill Clinton, Rudolph W. Giuliani and George W. Bush on the stump.

name: Alan W. Livingston
headline: Alan W. Livingston, Talent Spotter Who Signed Beatles, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Livingston was president of Capitol Records and had significant roles in bringing Bozo, the Beatles and “Bonanza” to American audiences.

name: Martin Knowlton
headline: Martin Knowlton, Co-Founder of Elderhostel, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Knowlton was the co-founder of Elderhostel, a nonprofit organization that made it possible for older Americans to pursue their love of travel and learning.

name: Claude S. Brinegar
headline: Claude S. Brinegar Is Dead at 82; Supported Mass Transit and Conrail
abstract: In the Nixon administration, Mr. Brinegar helped create Conrail and institute a national 55-mile-an-hour speed limit after the first Arab oil embargo.

name: Jack Lawrence
headline: Jack Lawrence, Writer of Hit Songs, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Lawrence was a reluctant podiatrist who chose to do what he had always wanted to do as a kid — write lyrics for songs, many of which became hits.

name: Anne Brown
headline: Anne Brown, Who Was Gershwin’s Bess, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Brown was the penetratingly pure soprano who literally put the Bess in “Porgy and Bess” by inspiring George Gershwin to expand the character’s part in a folk opera that was originally to be called “Porgy.”

name: Milan Stitt
profession: Playwright and a Nurturer of Talent
headline: Milan Stitt, 68, Playwright and a Nurturer of Talent, Dies
abstract: Mr. Stitt was the author of the critically praised 1976 Broadway drama “The Runner Stumbles” and founder and director of an Off Broadway incubator for playwrights.

name: Natasha Richardson
headline: Natasha Richardson, 45, Stage and Film Star, Dies
abstract: The Tony Award winner melded glamorous celebrity with the bloodline of theater royalty.

name: Millard Kaufman
headline: Millard Kaufman, 92, a Creator of Mr. Magoo, Dies
abstract: Mr. Kaufman wrote Oscar-nominated screenplays for “Take the High Ground!” and “Bad Day at Black Rock” and made a belated debut as a novelist at 90.

name: Betsy Blair
profession: Actress and Wife of Gene Kelly
headline: Betsy Blair, 85, Actress and Wife of Gene Kelly, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Blair was an Academy Award-nominated actress also known for her memoir describing her marriage to Gene Kelly and her experience with the Hollywood blacklist.

name: Nicholas Henderson
headline: Sir Nicholas Henderson, Former British Ambassador to U.S., Dies at 89
abstract: Sir Nicholas was a gregarious diplomat who labored to win the Reagan administration’s backing for Britain’s military campaign to retake the Falkland Islands.

name: Whitey Lockman
headline: Whitey Lockman Dies at 82; Set Up Epic Homer
abstract: Mr. Lockman, the New York Giants’ outfielder-first baseman, set the stage for Bobby Thomson’s pennant-winning home run with a double hit against the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1951.

name: Jane Mayhall
headline: Jane Mayhall, Poet Who Gained Prominence Late in Life, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Ms. Mayhall’s work was informed by the unhurried rhythms of her Kentucky girlhood, the bustle of her Manhattan adulthood and the abiding grief of her years of widowhood.

name: Lionel Ziprin
profession: Mystic of the Lower East Side
headline: Lionel Ziprin, Mystic of the Lower East Side, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Ziprin was a brilliant, baffling, beguiling voice of the Lower East Side and the East Village in all its phases — Jewish, hipster and hippie.

name: Nancy Eiesland
headline: Nancy Eiesland Is Dead at 44; Wrote of a Disabled God
abstract: Ms. Eiesland’s insights added a religious angle to a new consciousness among the disabled that emerged in the 1960s in the fight for access to public facilities.

name: Gianni Giansanti
profession: Unofficial Photographer of Pope John Paul II
headline: Gianni Giansanti, Unofficial Photographer of Pope John Paul II, Is Dead at 52
abstract: Mr. Giansanti’s photographs appeared regularly in newspapers and magazines around the world, with many of the images distributed by the Sygma photo agency.

name: Jade Goody
headline: Jade Goody, British Reality Television Star, Dies at 27
abstract: Ms. Goody was a dental technician who parlayed a “Big Brother” appearance into a career as a full-time celebrity.

name: Arthur Code
headline: Arthur Code, Astronomer and Professor, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Code was an astronomer and designer of space observatories who helped lead an experiment in the 1960s that yielded information about the composition of stars, comets and galactic gases.

name: Glenn Marlin Sundby
headline: Glenn Marlin Sundby, Acrobat and Gymnastics Pioneer, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Sundby helped propel gymnastics to national prominence as a magazine publisher and was a founder of the sport’s national governing body.

name: Pirkle Jones
headline: Pirkle Jones, Documentary Photographer, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Jones’s images of migrant farm workers, threatened California towns and valleys and the Black Panthers at the peak of their power made him one of the most admired photographers of his generation.

name: Howard Komives
headline: Howard Komives, Ex-Knick, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Komives, a sharpshooting guard who played for 10 years in the N.B.A., was perhaps best remembered for the trade that sent him to the Detroit Pistons for the future Hall of Famer Dave DeBusschere.

name: Ezio Flagello
headline: Ezio Flagello, 78, Met Stalwart, Dies
abstract: Mr. Flagello was a bass with a rich voice and wide range who sang 528 performances at the Metropolitan Opera as part of an international career.

name: Eddie Bo
headline: Eddie Bo, 79, New Orleans R&B Belter, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Bo was an exuberant New Orleans pianist and singer who wrote for and worked with artists like Irma Thomas, Etta James and Art Neville of the Neville Brothers.

name: Nicholas Hughes
headline: Nicholas Hughes, 47, Sylvia Plath’s Son, Dies
abstract: Mr. Hughes was a fisheries biologist and the son of the poets Sylvia Plath and Ted Hughes.

name: George Kell
profession: Tigers Hall of Famer and Broadcaster
headline: George Kell, 86, Tigers’ Hall of Famer and Broadcaster, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Kell was a 10-time All-Star and Hall of Fame third baseman who won the American League batting championship in 1949 with the Detroit Tigers and later became a longtime broadcaster for the team.

name: Lloyd Ruby
headline: Lloyd Ruby, Star-Crossed Indy 500 Racer, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Ruby was one of the best — and most star-crossed — Indy 500 auto racers in history, and was most famous for a race he never won.

name: Uriel Jones
headline: Uriel Jones, a Motown Drummer, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Jones was a drummer with the Funk Brothers, the studio musicians at Motown Records who played on virtually every hit during that label’s heyday in the 1960s.

name: Johnny Blanchard
headline: Johnny Blanchard, Yanks’ ’60s Super Sub, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Blanchard was a power-hitting catcher and outfielder known as Super Sub who played in five consecutive World Series for the Yankees in the 1960s.

name: John Hope Franklin
headline: John Hope Franklin, Scholar of African-American History, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Mr. Franklin was a prolific scholar of African-American history who profoundly influenced thinking about slavery and Reconstruction while helping to further the civil rights struggle.

name: Dan Seals
headline: Dan Seals, 61, Pop Duo’s England Dan, Dies
abstract: Mr. Seals performed as England Dan in the folk-pop duo England Dan and John Ford Coley and later returned to his roots as a country singer and songwriter.

name: Earl H. Wood
headline: Earl H. Wood Is Dead at 97; Helped Invent G-Suit
abstract: Dr. Wood, a physiologist, was an essential member of the team that invented a revolutionary pressurized garment, the G-suit, that helps pilots avoid blacking out while in flight.

name: Ronald Tavel
headline: Ronald Tavel, Proudly Ridiculous Writer, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Tavel was a playwright and screenwriter who brought a bawdy sense of the outrageous to some of Andy Warhol’s early films and helped mold the Off Off Broadway movement in the 1960s.

name: Jack Dreyfus
profession: Mutual Fund Pioneer and Wonder Drug Promoter
headline: Jack Dreyfus, 95, Mutual Fund Pioneer and ‘Wonder Drug’ Promoter, Is Dead
abstract: The New York financier ran one of the nation’s most successful mutual funds but left Wall Street on a quixotic crusade to promote an epilepsy drug as a miracle cure-all.

name: Irving R. Levine
headline: Irving R. Levine, NBC News Correspondent, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Levine’s easily accessible explanations of monetary policy made the economy a staple of television news.

name: Steven Bach
headline: Steven Bach, Producer, Biographer and Memoirist, Dies at 70
abstract: The former studio executive at United Artists took the fall for the colossal failure of the western epic “Heaven’s Gate” but went on to write “Final Cut,” a gripping insider account of the debacle.

name: Archie Green
headline: Archie Green, 91, Union Activist and Folklorist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Green was a shipwright turned folklorist whose interest in union workers and their culture transformed the study of American folklore.

name: Marjorie Grene
headline: Marjorie Grene, a Leading Philosopher of Biology, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Dr. Grene helped shape a modern philosophical approach to biology that strives to interpret the deepest meanings of the scientific study of life, including the meaning of humanness.

name: Janet Jagan
headline: Janet Jagan, Chicago Native Who Led Guyana, Dies at 88
abstract: With her husband, Cheddi, the former Janet Rosenberg became active in radical politics in colonial British Guiana.

name: Lou Saban
headline: Lou Saban, a Well-Traveled Coach, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Saban coached the Buffalo Bills of the old American Football League to two championships in a career that took him from professional football to college to high schools.

name: Helen Levitt
profession: Froze New York Street Life on Film
headline: Helen Levitt, Who Froze New York Street Life on Film, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Ms. Levitt was a major photographer of the 20th century who caught fleeting moments of surpassing lyricism, mystery and quiet drama on the streets of her native New York.

name: George Hedges
headline: George Hedges, Lawyer Who Explored Middle East, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Hedges represented Hollywood celebrities as a senior partner at a Los Angeles law firm and was an organizer of expeditions to the Middle East in the 1990s.

name: Maurice Jarre
headline: Maurice Jarre, Hollywood Composer, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Jarre was a composer who mastered the musical idiom of the Hollywood epic and was nominated nine times for Academy Awards, winning three.

name: Frances Blaisdell
headline: Frances Blaisdell, ‘Girl Flutist’ Who Opened Doors, Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Blaisdell was a flutist who played her way into what was then the male world of orchestral music, becoming one of the early women to play a woodwind instrument with the New York Philharmonic.

name: Kosuke Koyama
headline: Kosuke Koyama, 79, an Ecumenical Theologian, Dies
abstract: Dr. Koyama was internationally known for using arresting metaphors drawn from his experience as a missionary to convey an influential vision of Christianity as compatible with Asian traditions.

name: Baseball
headline: Baseball’s Herman Franks Dies at 95
abstract: In a baseball career going back to the early 1930s, Franks was a catcher, a coach and manager with the Giants, a manager with the Chicago Cubs, and a scout.

name: Raúl Alfonsín
headline: Raúl Alfonsín, 82, Former Argentine Leader, Dies
abstract: Mr. Alfonsín’s presidency in the 1980s symbolized the return of democracy in Argentina and other Latin American nations after an era of military dictatorships.

name: George Stoddard
headline: George Stoddard, Financing Pioneer, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Stoddard was a pioneer in the use of real estate transactions known as sale-leasebacks to provide financing for companies having trouble gaining access to traditional sources of capital.

name: R. Alfonsín
headline: R. Alfonsín, 82, Dies; Led Argentina
abstract: Mr. Alfonsín’s presidency in the 1980s symbolized the return of democracy in Argentina and other Latin American nations after an era of military dictatorships.

name: Andrea Mead Lawrence
headline: Andrea Mead Lawrence, Skiing Champion, Dies at 76
abstract: Lawrence, known as Andy, seized national attention by skiing at age 15 in the 1948 Winter Olympics in St. Moritz, Switzerland.

name: Martin J. Klein
headline: Martin J. Klein, Historian of Physics, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Klein was the editor of a collection of papers documenting the years in which Albert Einstein completed his work on the general theory of relativity.

name: Dorothy Ann Kelly
headline: Sister Dorothy Ann Kelly, College Leader, Dies at 79
abstract: Over 25 years as president of the College of New Rochelle, Sister Dorothy Ann oversaw an expansion of the institution from 900 students to more than 6,500.

name: Daniel J. O’Hern
profession: Longtime New Jersey Supreme Court Justice
headline: Daniel J. O’Hern, Longtime New Jersey Supreme Court Justice, Dies at 78
abstract: In 19 years on the State Supreme Court, Justice O’Hern wrote 231 majority opinions that helped define New Jersey’s policies.

name: W. B. Schwartz
headline: W. B. Schwartz, 86, Dies; Warned of Medical Costs
abstract: Dr. Schwartz was a leading health economist whose studies of the effects of market forces on medicine led him to predict that unbridled costs could lead to a rationing of care.

name: Earl Paulk
headline: Earl Paulk, Founder of a Megachurch, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Bishop Paulk was an influential evangelical preacher who helped build a Georgia megachurch but who was humbled by accusations of adultery and sexual misconduct.

name: Robert Delford Brown
headline: Robert Delford Brown, ‘Happenings’ Artist, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Brown was a painter, sculptor, performance artist and avant-garde philosopher whose provocative works challenged orthodoxies of both the art world and the world at large.

name: Eva Evdokimova
headline: Eva Evdokimova, Ballerina, Dies at 60
abstract: Ms. Evdokimova was an internationally known ballerina who stood out for the delicacy and eloquent purity of her dancing and stage presence.

name: Edgar F. Callahan
headline: Edgar F. Callahan, Credit Union Chief, Dies at 80
abstract: During the Reagan administration, Mr. Callahan raised capital requirements for the insurance fund amid a recession.

name: Bud Shank
headline: Bud Shank, Jazz Saxophonist, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Shank was an alto saxophonist and flutist who helped propel cool-school West Coast jazz to prominence in the 1950s.

name: Dorothy Cullman
headline: Dorothy Cullman, Patron of City Institutions, Dies at 91
abstract: Mrs. Cullman and her husband, Lewis B. Cullman, donated about $250 million to arts, science and educational institutions in New York.

name: Marvin Webster
headline: Marvin Webster, Basketball’s Human Eraser, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Webster was the 7-foot-1 shot-blocking center known as the Human Eraser, who took the Seattle SuperSonics to the 1978 N.B.A. finals, then spent six seasons with the Knicks.

name: Jack Wrangler
profession: Actor in Sex Films and Producer
headline: Jack Wrangler, Actor in Sex Films and Producer, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Wrangler, born John Stillman, who appeared in gay and straight sex films, and later wrote and directed cabarets, was a role model for the gay liberation movement.

name: Russell Dunham
headline: Russell Dunham, Hero in 1945, Dies at 89
abstract: Sergeant Dunham received the Medal of Honor for charging up a snowy hill in the Alsace region of France during World War II and single-handedly killing, wounding or capturing 18 German soldiers.

name: James G. Boswell II
headline: James G. Boswell II, 86, Owner of Cotton Empire, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Boswell inherited a huge expanse of farmland in the San Joaquin Valley of California and then quadrupled its acreage to create a cotton-growing empire.

name: David Winans
headline: David Winans, Gospel Patriarch, Dies at 74
abstract: David '‘Pop’' Winans Sr., a Grammy-nominated patriarch, appeared regularly on the Trinity Broadcasting Network’s '‘Praise the Lord’' program.

name: I. Herbert Scheinberg
headline: I. Herbert Scheinberg, Expert on Wilson Disease, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Scheinberg, a specialist in rare hereditary diseases, helped develop a diagnostic test and treatment for Wilson disease, a potentially fatal buildup of copper in the body.

name: Nancy Overton
headline: Nancy Overton, Singer for the Chordettes, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Ms. Overton joined the pop group in 1958 and melded her mellifluous low tones into their barbershop-quartet-like harmonies on some of their later hits.

name: Dave Arneson
headline: Dave Arneson, Conjuror of Games, Is Dead at 61
abstract: Mr. Arneson, through the popular game he helped create, Dungeons & Dragons, spawned a new form of interpersonal entertainment that has captivated millions.

name: Michael Stern
headline: Michael Stern, Adventurer, Journalist and Philanthropist, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Stern chronicled war, crime and intrigue, and was a driving force behind efforts to save the aircraft carrier Intrepid and to raise money for medical research.

name: Stanley L. Jaki
headline: The Rev. Stanley L. Jaki, Physicist and Theologian, Dies at 84
abstract: Father Jaki, a Benedictine priest, wrote extensively, delving into the histories of science and religion and exploring their boundaries.

name: Manny Oquendo
profession: Latin Band Leader and Stylistic Innovator
headline: Manny Oquendo, Latin Band Leader and Stylistic Innovator, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Oquendo adapted the carnival rhythm called Mozambique and reworked it for the timbales, introducing a hypnotic African beat to the dance halls of New York.

name: Harry Kalas
headline: Harry Kalas, Popular Voice of Phillies, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Kalas was the voice of the Philadelphia Phillies for four decades and a member of the broadcasters’ wing of the Baseball Hall of Fame.

name: Mark Fidrych
headline: Mark Fidrych, Baseball’s Beloved ‘Bird,’ Dies at 54
abstract: Fidrych was the golden-haired, eccentric pitcher known as the Bird, who became a rookie phenomenon for the Detroit Tigers in 1976 and later saw his career cut short by injury.

name: John Maddox
headline: John Maddox, Editor Who Enlivened Nature, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. Maddox turned the British journal Nature into an internationally influential showcase for the most recent developments in scientific research.

name: Marilyn Chambers
headline: Marilyn Chambers, Sex Star, Dies at 56
abstract: Ms. Chambers’s photograph as a mother on a laundry soap package and her performance as a fantasy-fulfilling wanton in a pornographic movie evoked contrasting portrayals of womanhood.

name: Judith Krug
headline: Judith Krug, Who Fought Ban on Books, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Krug led the campaign by libraries against efforts to ban books, then fought laws and regulations to limit children’s access to the Internet.

name: Eve Kosofsky Sedgwick
profession: Pioneer of Gay Studies and a Literary Theorist
headline: Eve Kosofsky Sedgwick, a Pioneer of Gay Studies and a Literary Theorist, Dies at 58
abstract: Ms. Sedgwick broke new ground when, drawing on feminist scholarship, she teased out the hidden socio-sexual subplots in writers, which later helped create the discipline known as queer studies.

name: Stephen Minarik
headline: Stephen Minarik, Who Led New York G.O.P., Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. Minarik, who developed a passion for politics early in his life, was a former Monroe County G.O.P. chairman and led the state’s Republicans from 2004 to 2006.

name: Les Keiter
headline: Les Keiter, Announcer Who Recreated Giants Games, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Keiter spent 50 years as a sportscaster but was best remembered for his recreating San Francisco Giants baseball games for abandoned fans from the Polo Grounds years.

name: Maurice Druon
headline: Maurice Druon, Prolific Writer, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Druon, co-writer of one of France’s most patriotic anthems during World War II, went on to write novels and serve his country as minister of culture.

name: Clement Freud
headline: Clement Freud, Wit, Politician and Grandson of Famous Psychoanalyst, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Freud’s eclectic career included stints as a British Army liaison officer at the Nuremberg trials, cookery expert, Liberal member of Parliament, and celebrated radio broadcaster.

name: Deborah Digges
headline: Deborah Digges, Poet Who Channeled Struggles, Dies at 59
abstract: Ms. Digges was a renowned poet and memoirist whose work often sprang from private adversity.

name: Michael O’Hare
headline: Michael O’Hare, Figure in Ethics Case, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. O’Hare was the bookkeeper to Senator Thomas J. Dodd of Connecticut and a central witness in a case that ultimately led the Senate to censure Mr. Dodd in 1967.

name: Simon Channing Williams
headline: Simon Channing Williams, Filmmaker, Is Dead at 63
abstract: A film producer, Mr. Williams’s partnership with the director Mike Leigh resulted in a string of quirky, critically praised films.

name: Samuel H. Beer
headline: Samuel H. Beer, Authority on British Government, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Beer, a leading American expert on British government and politics, was a longtime professor at Harvard and who led the liberal organization Americans for Democratic Action.

name: Michael Cox
profession: Editor and Author of The Meaning of Night
headline: Michael Cox, Editor and Author of ‘The Meaning of Night,’ Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Cox was an authority on the Victorian ghost story who, five years ago, spurred by the threat of blindness, sat down and wrote the vast Gothic novel that had been haunting him for three decades.

name: Whitelaw Reid
profession: Heir to New York Herald Tribune
headline: Whitelaw Reid, Heir to New York Herald Tribune, Dies at 95
abstract: After working as a war correspondent during World War II, Mr. Reid became The New York Herald Tribune’s editor and, ultimately, its chairman.

name: John Oros
headline: John Oros, Top Jockey as a 17-Year-Old, Dies at 87
abstract: In 1939 Oros was just 17 when he overtook perhaps the most notorious jockey of the time, Don Meade.

name: Doc Blanchard
headline: Doc Blanchard, Army’s Mr. Inside, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Blanchard, a Heisman Trophy winner, teamed up with Glenn Davis on the unbeaten Army teams of the mid-1940s in college football’s most storied backfield pairing.

name: J. G. Ballard
headline: J. G. Ballard, Novelist, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Ballard was a writer of dystopian, literary fiction whose novels and short stories of a contemporary society both expanded and defied the genre of science fiction.

name: Tharon Musser
headline: Tharon Musser, Stage Lighting Designer, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Musser said she “painted with light” and proved it with her lighting designs for more than 150 Broadway shows.

name: Charles Peebler
headline: Charles Peebler, Ad Executive, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Peebler turned a small Omaha advertising company called Bozell & Jacobs into a global powerhouse.

name: Stefan Brecht
headline: Stefan Brecht, Theater Historian, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Brecht, whose father was the playwright Bertolt Brecht, added to the family’s theatrical legacy by fastidiously chronicling the rise of avant-garde theater.

name: Ray Nance
headline: Ray Nance, Last of the Bedford Boys, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Nance was the last survivor of the Bedford Boys, soldiers from the Blue Ridge foothills whose losses at Omaha Beach symbolized the sacrifices of Americans who fell at Normandy on D-Day.

name: Timothy J. Holst
profession: Filled Circus Big Top With Talent
headline: Timothy J. Holst, Who Filled Circus Big Top With Talent, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Holst joined the Ringling Brothers and Barnum & Bailey Circus as a lowly Keystone Kops clown, then rose to the role of singing ringmaster and ultimately became the show’s talent czar.

name: Benjamin Edwards
headline: Benjamin Edwards, Brokerage Figure, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Edwards transformed A. G. Edwards, the St. Louis brokerage house founded by his great-grandfather, into the largest United States brokerage company based outside New York.

name: Jack Cardiff
headline: Jack Cardiff, Film Director, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Cardiff was an Oscar-winning British cinematographer and director who drew inspiration from Rembrandt and Alfred Hitchcock, as well as actresses like Marilyn Monroe.

name: Ken Annakin
headline: Ken Annakin, ‘Magnificent’ Director, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Annakin was a film director with a flair for both light comedy and sweeping action films; his most famous movie was “Those Magnificent Men in Their Flying Machines.”

name: Santha Rama Rau
profession: Wrote of Indias Landscape and Psyche
headline: Santha Rama Rau, Who Wrote of India’s Landscape and Psyche, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Rama Rau was an Indian-born, Western-educated journalist whose work helped demystify the Indian subcontinent after World War II.

name: Walter Schneir
headline: Walter Schneir, Who Wrote About Rosenbergs, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Schneir was an author whose hotly debated 1965 book initially argued that the Rosenbergs had been framed, though he later accepted that Julius, if not Ethel, Rosenberg was indeed a Soviet spy.

name: Marilyn Cooper
headline: Marilyn Cooper, Actress and Tony Award Winner, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Cooper was a longtime Broadway character actress who won a Tony in 1981 for just a few minutes of showstopping hilarity in the musical “Woman of the Year.

name: Timothy D. Wright
headline: Timothy D. Wright, Singer, Dies at 61
abstract: Pastor Wright was a Grammy-nominated gospel singer and composer who filled his recordings, and his Brooklyn church, with his rolling, booming baritone.

name: Catherine di Montezemolo
headline: Catherine di Montezemolo, Doyenne of Fashion and Society, Dies at 83
abstract: Mrs. di Montezemolo was a fashion editor and fixture of Southampton society who helped shape the look of postwar American sportswear in the pages of Vogue.

name: Louis Lowenstein
profession: Professor of Business Law and Critic of Wall St
headline: Louis Lowenstein, Professor of Business Law and Critic of Wall St., Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Lowenstein, a business law professor at Columbia, became known for exposing “a profound conflict of interest” in the mutual fund industry’s structure.

name: Bea Arthur
headline: Bea Arthur, Star of Two TV Comedies, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Arthur’s commanding stature and flair for the comic jab made her a star in the shows “Maude” and “The Golden Girls.”

name: John J. Marchi
profession: Fought for Staten Island in Senate
headline: John J. Marchi, Who Fought for Staten Island in Senate, Dies at 87
abstract: One of the longest-serving state legislators in the nation, Mr. Marchi was praised as an effective advocate for New York.

name: John King
headline: John King, Who Made Ukulele Ring With Bach, Dies at 55
abstract: Mr. King was known for playing on a ukulele Bach’s Partita No. 3 and other difficult classical works with dazzling mastery.

name: Frankie Manning
profession: Ambassador and Master of Lindy Hop
headline: Frankie Manning, the Ambassador and Master of Lindy Hop, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Manning was a master of swing-era dance who went from the Savoy Ballroom in Harlem to Broadway and Hollywood.

name: Greg Page
headline: Greg Page, Heavyweight Champion, Dies at 50
abstract: Mr. Page was a prizefighter who was hailed as the next Muhammad Ali as a teenager and briefly held a world heavyweight title in the mid-1980s.

name: Ekaterina Maximova
headline: Ekaterina Maximova, Ballerina, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Maximova’s lyrical lines, technical precision and luminous stage presence made her a star of the Bolshoi Theater and a darling of dance critics and balletomanes across the world.

name: Hans Holzer
headline: Hans Holzer, Ghost Hunter, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Holzer’s investigations into the paranormal took him to haunted houses all over the world, most notably the Long Island house that inspired “The Amityville Horror.”

name: Ernie Barnes
headline: Ernie Barnes, Artist and Athlete, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Barnes was an artist whose drawings and paintings of athletes, dancers and other figures in motion reflected his first career as a professional football player.

name: Irving D. Chais
headline: Irving D. Chais, Manhattan Doll Surgeon, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Chais was owner of the New York Doll Hospital, where he mended dolls and soothed the feelings of their owners for 45 years.

name: Kenneth Paul Block
headline: Kenneth Paul Block, Whose Illustrations Captured Fashion’s Elegance, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Block was a renowned fashion illustrator whose graceful strokes captured the elegance of form-fitted women of the 1950s and then the more daring, fluid look of later decades.

name: Maxime de la Falaise
headline: Maxime de la Falaise, Model, Designer and Muse, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Ms. de la Falaise was a celebrated fashion model who later became a fashion designer and food writer and who even appeared in “Andy Warhol’s Dracula.”

name: William A. Price
headline: William A. Price, Journalist Who Defied Senate Panel, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Price was fired by The Daily News after refusing to answer the questions of a Senate panel in 1956 about possible ties to the Communist Party.

name: Albert Gordon
headline: Albert Gordon, Who Rebuilt Kidder Peabody, Dies at 107
abstract: Mr. Gordon was an éminence grise of the investment community who began running marathons in his 80s.

name: Danny Gans
headline: Danny Gans, Impressionist, Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. Gans was virtually unknown outside Las Vegas but a superstar on the Strip for his bottomless repertory of impressions.

name: John Michell
headline: John Michell, Counterculture Author Who Cherished Idiosyncrasy, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Michell, a self-styled Merlin of the 1960s English counterculture, inspired disciples like the Rolling Stones with a deluge of writings about U.F.O.’s, prehistoric architecture and fairies.

name: Jack Kemp
profession: Star on Field and in Politics
headline: Jack Kemp, Star on Field and in Politics, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Kemp, a former football star turned congressman, moved the Republican Party to a commitment to tax cuts as the central focus of economic policy.

name: Salamo Arouch
profession: Boxed for His Life in Auschwitz
headline: Salamo Arouch, Who Boxed for His Life in Auschwitz, Is Dead at 86
abstract: The Greek-born Jewish boxer, who survived by winning fights against fellow prisoners to the delight of Nazi guards, was the basis of the 1989 movie “Triumph of the Spirit.”

name: Marilyn French
headline: Marilyn French, Novelist and Champion of Feminism, Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. French was a writer and feminist activist whose debut novel, “The Women’s Room,” propelled her into a leading role in the modern feminist movement.

name: James W. Davant
profession: Rose to Top of Paine Webber
headline: James W. Davant, Who Rose to Top of Paine Webber, Is Dead at 93
abstract: In a long career, Mr. Davant led the effort to transform a traditional brokerage partnership into an international full-service company.

name: Reza Seyed-Hosseini
headline: Reza Seyed-Hosseini, Iranian Translator and Literary Critic, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Seyed-Hosseini was instrumental in introducing Western literature to Persian-speaking readers.

name: Dom DeLuise
headline: Dom DeLuise, Comic Actor, Dies at 75
abstract: The actor’s manic grin and air of desperation added comic bounce to films like “The Twelve Chairs,” “Blazing Saddles” and “The Cannonball Run.”

name: Alex Lees
headline: Alex Lees, Who Helped Hide Escape Bid, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Lees was one of the last remaining links to the 1944 escape, made famous in the book, “The Great Escape,” from Stalag Luft III, a German prisoner-of-war camp.

name: Sam Cohn
headline: Sam Cohn, Powerful Talent Broker, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Cohn’s nearly endless client roster of actors, writers and directors and his imaginative rigging of deals for them made him a progenitor of the Hollywood superagent.

name: Carole C. Noon
headline: Carole C. Noon, Who Founded Save the Chimps, Dies at 59
abstract: Dr. Noon was a primatologist whose passion — and compassion — for her subjects led to her founding an organization that provides the world’s largest sanctuary for captive chimpanzees.

name: Eleanor Perenyi
headline: Eleanor Perenyi, Writer and Gardener, Dies at 91
abstract: Mrs. Perenyi was a writer and deliciously opinionated amateur gardener whose book “Green Thoughts” is widely considered a classic of garden writing.

name: Alfred Appel Jr.
headline: Alfred Appel Jr., Expert on Nabokov and Author, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Appel was a scholarly expert on Vladimir Nabokov and the author of wide-ranging interpretive books on modern art and jazz.

name: Valentin I. Varennikov
headline: Valentin I. Varennikov, Retired Soviet General Who Tried to Topple Gorbachev, Dies at 85
abstract: General Varennikov called the collapse of the Soviet Union “the greatest catastrophe of the 20th century.”

name: Harold E. Fischer Jr.
profession: American Flier Tortured in a Chinese Prison
headline: Harold E. Fischer Jr., an American Flier Tortured in a Chinese Prison, Dies at 83
abstract: Colonel Fischer, an American fighter pilot who was routinely tortured in a Chinese prison during and after the Korean War, became a symbol and victim of cold war tension.

name: Raymond Saulnier
headline: Raymond Saulnier, Adviser to Eisenhower, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Saulnier was the staunchly conservative chief economic adviser to President Eisenhower in the 1950s.

name: Dom DiMaggio
headline: Dom DiMaggio Dies at 92; Played in His Brother’s Shadow
abstract: Mr. DiMaggio was a perennial All-Star with the Boston Red Sox and the brother of the Yankee Clipper.

name: Mary Paul Janchill
headline: Sister Mary Paul Janchill, Social Services Innovator, Dies at 88
