abstract: As a co-founder of the Center for Family Life in Brooklyn, Sister Mary Paul embraced a holistic approach that became a national model for neighborhood-oriented family centers.

name: Bud Shrake
headline: Bud Shrake, Sportswriter and Author, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Shrake was a sportswriter and novelist who collaborated with the legendary golf teacher Harvey Penick on the best-selling sports title of all time.

name: Augusto Boal
headline: Augusto Boal, Stage Director Who Gave a Voice to Audiences, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Boal was a Brazilian director and drama theorist, who created interactive, politically expressive theater forms under the rubric of the Theater of the Oppressed.

name: Chuck Daly
headline: Chuck Daly, Pistons Coach, Dies at 78
abstract: Daly coached the Detroit Pistons’ Bad Boy teams to two N.B.A. championships, then coached the Olympic Dream Team to a gold medal in 1992.

name: Martha Mason
profession: Wrote Book About Her Decades in an Iron Lung
headline: Martha Mason, Who Wrote Book About Her Decades in an Iron Lung, Dies at 71
abstract: Paralyzed from the neck down as a result of childhood polio, Ms. Mason was one of the last handful of Americans, perhaps 30 people, who live full time in iron lungs.

name: Venetia Phair
profession: as a Girl, She Named Pluto
headline: Venetia Phair Dies at 90; as a Girl, She Named Pluto
abstract: As an 11-year-old in Britain, Mrs. Phair suggested the name Pluto to her well-connected grandfather.

name: Eugene Smith
headline: Eugene Smith, a Sparkplug of Gospel Music, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Smith’s ardent baritone and evangelical showmanship made him a celebrity among churchgoers on the South Side of Chicago and a national influence on generations of gospel singers.

name: Robert J. Cornell
headline: Robert J. Cornell, Priest Who Served as Congressman, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Father Cornell represented a Wisconsin district in the 1970s as one of only two Roman Catholic priests to serve as voting delegates to Congress.

name: Henry T. King Jr.
headline: Henry T. King Jr., Prosecutor at Nuremberg, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. King was one of the last Nuremberg war crimes prosecutors and an influential voice since World War II in international efforts to bring war criminals to justice.

name: Eden Ross Lipson
headline: Eden Ross Lipson, Books Editor at The Times, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Lipson held the position at the Book Review from 1984 to 2005, and wrote The New York Times Parent’s Guide to the Best Books for Children.

name: Honoré Sharrer
headline: Honoré Sharrer, a Realist Painter, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Sharrer was an American artist of the 1940s and afterward whose witty, incisive paintings documented the daily experiences of ordinary working people.

name: R. B. Choate Jr.
headline: R. B. Choate Jr., Food Lobbyist, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Choate gave up an engineering career to devote himself to fighting against poverty and malnutrition.

name: L. William Seidman
profession: Led F.D.I.C. During Savings and Loan Crisis
headline: L. William Seidman, Who Led F.D.I.C. During Savings and Loan Crisis, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Seidman’s credibility and unflinching stance in political skirmishes helped him transform the unglamorous job of chief banking regulator into one of the most powerful positions in Washington.

name: Robert Pauley
headline: Robert Pauley, Former Head of ABC Radio, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Pauley reinvigorated ABC Radio after he took over as president in 1961, a time at which the network was ailing.

name: Travis Edmonson
headline: Travis Edmonson, Influential Folk Singer, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Edmonson brought a Mexican flavor to the fertile San Francisco folk music scene of the 1950s and with the duo Bud and Travis influenced Bay Area groups.

name: María E. Ibarra Martín
headline: María E. Ibarra Martín, Cuban Biologist, Dies at 76
abstract: Dr. Ibarra was director of the Center for Marine Research at the University of Havana and a co-founder of the Cuban Society for the Protection of the Environment.

name: Achille Compagnoni
headline: Achille Compagnoni, a Conqueror of K2, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Compagnoni was one of the first two men to reach the summit of K2, the world’s second highest peak and among the most dangerous.

name: Jay C. Smith
profession: Convict Later Freed in Murder Case
headline: Jay C. Smith, Convict Later Freed in Murder Case, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Smith spent six years on death row before his conviction of the grisly 1979 murder of a suburban Philadelphia schoolteacher and her two children was overturned.

name: Hubert Van Es
headline: Hubert Van Es, War Photographer, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Van Es was a Dutch photojournalist who covered the Vietnam War and took one of the best-known images of the American evacuation of Saigon in 1975.

name: Wayman Tisdale
headline: Wayman Tisdale, Basketball Star Who Became Noted Jazz Musician, Dies at 44
abstract: Mr. Tisdale excelled at basketball at the college, Olympic and professional levels, then conquered new horizons by developing his own style of playing jazz melodies on the bass guitar.

name: Bob Rosburg
headline: Bob Rosburg, Golfer and TV Analyst, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Rosburg won the 1959 P.G.A. Championship but was probably best remembered as a longtime TV golf analyst for ABC Sports, gaining note as the first broadcaster to work entirely from the fairways.

name: Robert Sinclair
headline: Robert Sinclair, Who Found a Niche for Saab, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Sinclair’s bet on the Saab 900, at a time when rivals were shying away from convertibles, was seen as a major success.

name: Susanna Agnelli
profession: First Woman in Italy to Run Foreign Office
headline: Susanna Agnelli, First Woman in Italy to Run Foreign Office, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Agnelli, a scion of the Fiat car dynasty, was the only female foreign minister in Italian history and a formidable presence who brought American-style philanthropy to Italy.

name: Sid Laverents
headline: Sid Laverents, Auteur of Homemade Films, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Laverents was perhaps the most celebrated hobbyist in the amateur film world.

name: Elsie B. Washington
headline: Elsie B. Washington, a Novelist, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Washington wrote the 1980 book, “Entwined Destinies,” which is widely considered the first black romance novel.

name: Philip Stein
headline: Philip Stein, Muralist Who Adorned Village Vanguard Jazz Club, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Stein created the mural of a primordial man and woman bursting from a kaleidoscopic background that is on the back wall of the famous Greenwich Village jazz club.

name: Rodger McFarlane
headline: Rodger McFarlane, Who Led AIDS-Related Groups, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. McFarlane was the first executive director of the Gay Men’s Health Crisis, a group that was an early advocate for public and private research to deal with the disease.

name: David Herbert Donald
headline: David Herbert Donald, Writer on Lincoln, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Donald was a historian of Abraham Lincoln and the Civil War who won Pulitzer Prizes for his biographies of the abolitionist statesman Charles Sumner and the novelist Thomas Wolfe.

name: Rafael Escalona
profession: Folk Musician and Balladeer of Colombia
headline: Rafael Escalona, 81, Folk Musician and Balladeer of Colombia, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Escalona was a beloved writer of Colombian folk music and inspired the novelist Gabriel García Márquez.

name: Nicholas Maw
headline: Nicholas Maw, Iconoclastic Composer, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Maw was a British composer best known for a sumptuous Violin Concerto he composed for Joshua Bell and a powerfully emotional opera based on William Styron’s 1979 novel “Sophie’s Choice.”

name: Mario Benedetti
headline: Mario Benedetti, Writer Revered in Latin America, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Benedetti was one of Latin America’s most respected, popular and prolific writers, who excelled as a novelist, poet and playwright while immersing himself in the region’s political struggles.

name: Krishna Pattabhi Jois
headline: Krishna Pattabhi Jois, Leading Expert in Yoga, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Jois was the prominent and influential yoga teacher whose students included Western celebrities like Madonna and Sting.

name: Daniel Carasso
headline: Daniel Carasso, a Pioneer of Yogurt, Dies at 103
abstract: Mr. Carasso helped turn yogurt from an obscure ethnic food into an international staple through the Danone brand in Europe and Dannon in the United States.

name: Edwin Shneidman
headline: Edwin Shneidman, Authority on Suicide, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Shneidman was a psychologist who gave new direction to the study of suicide and was a founder of the nation’s first comprehensive suicide prevention center.

name: Turkan Saylan
headline: Turkan Saylan, Women’s Rights Champion, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Saylan was a champion of women’s rights and education for poor children in Turkey and a leader in the fight against leprosy.

name: Buddy Montgomery
headline: Buddy Montgomery, Played the Vibraphone, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Montgomery was a jazz pianist and vibraphonist best known for his work with the guitarist Wes Montgomery, his older brother.

name: Lee Solters
headline: Lee Solters, Razzle-Dazzle Press Agent, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Solters was a foxy, flamboyant press agent who cranked up his raspy Brooklyn-accented voice to hyperbolize about Broadway, Hollywood and Frank Sinatra.

name: Clint Smith
headline: Clint Smith, Who Won Stanley Cup With Rangers, Dies at 95
abstract: Smith was the oldest living member of the Hockey Hall of Fame and the last surviving player from the Rangers’ 1940 Stanley Cup champions.

name: Arthur Erickson
headline: Arthur Erickson, Canadian Architect Who Mirrored Landscapes, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Erickson was a Canadian Modernist architect who established an international reputation for designing innovative complexes and buildings.

name: Joan A. Stanton
headline: Joan A. Stanton, Radio Voice of Lois Lane, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Stanton was known as Joan Alexander in the 1940s when she was the voice of Lois Lane on the radio version of “The Adventures of Superman.”

name: Robert Furchgott
profession: Nobelist for Work on a Gas
headline: Robert Furchgott, Nobelist for Work on a Gas, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Furchgott was a pharmacologist whose work with the gas nitric oxide opened new vistas of research in cardiovascular functions and helped lead to the development of Viagra, the anti-impotency drug.

name: Roy Talbot
headline: Roy Talbot, Calypso Musician, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Talbot was the last surviving member of the original Talbot Brothers of Bermuda, one of the top calypso groups of the 1950s.

name: Oleg Yankovsky
headline: Oleg Yankovsky, Russian Film Star, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Yankovsky was a longtime Russian actor and a frequent star of films by Andrei Tarkovsky.

name: Herbert York
headline: Herbert York, 87, Top Nuclear Physicist Who Was Arms Control Advocate, Dies
abstract: Mr. York was a physicist who worked on the Manhattan Project developing the atomic bomb and later became a leading advocate of arms control and nuclear test bans.

name: Louise Deutschman
headline: Louise Deutschman, Curator in the Arts, Dies at 92
abstract: Mrs. Deutschman, who gave Gordon Parks his first art-gallery show, had a five-decade-long career as a curator and gallery director.

name: Jay Bennett
headline: Jay Bennett, Ex-Member of Wilco, Dies at 45
abstract: Mr. Bennett, a singer and songwriter, was a former member of the alternative-country band Wilco.

name: Amos Elon
headline: Amos Elon, Israeli Author, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Elon, whose work examined his society’s flaws and myths, was for many years Israel’s most renowned intellectual.

name: Brooks McNamara
headline: Brooks McNamara, Theater Historian, Is Dead at 72
abstract: Mr. McNamara shepherded a vast and disorganized array of memorabilia into a valuable historical collection known as the Shubert Archive.

name: Thomas Minter
profession: New York and Federal Education Official
headline: Thomas Minter, 84, New York and Federal Education Official, Dies
abstract: One of the first top officials in the federal Education Department, he lost a politicized, racially charged campaign to head New York City’s schools in 1983.

name: Alexander G. Bearn
headline: Alexander G. Bearn, Pioneer in Genetic Disease, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Bearn was a physician and scientist whose research on a rare liver disease in the 1950s helped lay the groundwork for the field of human biochemical genetics.

name: Sam Maloof
headline: Sam Maloof, Furniture Craftsman, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Maloof’s simple, elegant wooden furniture, which he designed and made by hand, made him a central figure in the postwar American crafts movement.

name: Christopher Randolph
headline: Christopher Randolph, Veteran and Marine Foundation Head, Is Dead at 64
abstract: Mr. Randolph served in combat in Vietnam, pursued a career in politics and finance, and was president of the Marine Corps Scholarship Foundation.

name: Gérard Jean-Juste
profession: Champion of Haitian Rights in U.S
headline: The Rev. Gérard Jean-Juste, Champion of Haitian Rights in U.S., Dies at 62
abstract: Father Jean-Juste came to prominence in the late 1970s as director of the Haitian Refugee Center in Miami, where he became a vocal advocate of Haitians seeking asylum in the United States.

name: Julie Coryell
headline: Julie Coryell, Jazz-Rock Historian, Dies at 61
abstract: Ms. Coryell wrote a seminal history of jazz-rock fusion while married to the guitarist Larry Coryell.

name: Karine Ruby
headline: Karine Ruby, French Snowboarding Star, Dies at 31
abstract: Ms. Ruby, who became one of snowboarding’s first stars when she won gold at the 1998 Nagano Olympics, died in a climbing accident in the Mont Blanc Massif in France.

name: Thomas Franck
headline: Thomas Franck, Who Advised Countries on Law, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Franck was a prominent expert on international law who was particularly committed to promoting justice in developing countries.

name: Franklin Littell
headline: Franklin Littell, Scholar of Holocaust, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Littell was the father of Holocaust studies who traced his engagement with the subject to the revulsion he felt as a young Methodist minister while witnessing a big Nazi rally in Nuremberg in 1939.

name: Clive Granger
headline: Clive Granger, Economist, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Granger was an economist and Nobel laureate whose work revolutionized the way stocks and other fluctuating series of data are analyzed and forecast.

name: Ronald Takaki
headline: Ronald Takaki, a Scholar on Ethnicity, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Takaki made it his life’s work to rewrite American history to include Asian-Americans and other ethnic groups excluded from traditional accounts.

name: Philip C. Bolger
headline: Philip C. Bolger, 81, Dies; Prolific Boat Designer
abstract: Mr. Bolger’s hundreds of boat designs ranked him among the most prolific and versatile recreational boat designers in the world.

name: Millvina Dean
headline: Millvina Dean, Titanic’s Last Survivor, Dies at 97
abstract: As a 9-week-old, Ms. Dean was lowered to safety in a mail sack, but her father died in the sinking.

name: Vincent O’Brien
headline: Vincent O’Brien, Irish Trainer of Champion Racehorses, Dies at 92
abstract: In his half-century as a trainer, Mr. O’Brien, who was put at the top of the list of horse racing’s hundred most important figures, compiled a stunning record of achievement.

name: Jerry Rosenberg
headline: Jerry Rosenberg, Jailhouse Lawyer, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Rosenberg was spared the death penalty for the murders of two New York City police detectives and became a pioneering jailhouse lawyer and adviser during the 1971 Attica prison uprising.

name: Paul Haney
headline: Paul Haney, Voice of Mission Control, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Haney was known as the voice of NASA’s mission control for his live commentary during the Gemini and Apollo space flights in the 1960s.

name: Daniel C. Tosteson
headline: Daniel C. Tosteson, Longtime Dean Who Reshaped Harvard Medical School, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Tosteson spent two decades as the forceful dean of Harvard Medical School, reconfiguring the curriculum there and thus influencing the education of doctors around the country and the world.

name: Samuel M. Ehrenhalt
profession: Added Color to Dry Economic Data
headline: Samuel M. Ehrenhalt, Who Added Color to Dry Economic Data, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Ehrenhalt was a regional commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics, who transformed colorless wage and employment figures into small, brightly lighted windows onto New Yorkers’ daily lives.

name: Danny La Rue
headline: Danny La Rue, Female Impersonator, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. La Rue was a female impersonator who became one of the highest-paid performers on the British stage.

name: Thomas Berry
profession: Writer and Lecturer With a Mission for Mankind
headline: Thomas Berry, Writer and Lecturer With a Mission for Mankind, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Berry was a Roman Catholic priest who called himself a “geologian” and whose influential writings were an early call to humanity to save nature in order to save itself.

name: Ephraim Katzir
headline: Ephraim Katzir, Former Israeli President, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Katzir was Israel’s fourth president and one of his nation’s pre-eminent scientists.

name: Koko Taylor
headline: Koko Taylor, Queen of Chicago Blues, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Best known for her 1965 hit single “Wang Dang Doodle,” Ms. Taylor was one of the few female singers to achieve success in the competitive world of Chicago blues.

name: David Carradine
headline: David Carradine, Actor, Is Dead at 72
abstract: An enigmatic actor, Mr. Carradine never outran the identity he earned in “Kung Fu,” the 1970s Chinese-western television series that made him an unlikely cult hero.

name: Sam Butera
headline: Sam Butera, Saxophonist for Louis Prima, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Butera was a bandleader and tenor saxophonist, who provided a raucous counterpoint to Louis Prima’s frenzied “jump, jive and wail” vocals for two decades.

name: Richard E. Jacobs
headline: Richard E. Jacobs, Former Owner of Cleveland Indians, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Jacobs, a major real estate developer, became the primary owner of the Cleveland Indians in 1986 and helped steer the team out of decades in the doldrums.

name: Randy Smith
headline: Randy Smith, N.B.A. Iron Man, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Smith was a speedy, high-scoring guard who set a National Basketball Association record by playing in 906 consecutive games over 12 seasons.

name: Boris Pokrovsky
headline: Boris Pokrovsky, Bolshoi Director, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Pokrovsky was an internationally renowned Russian theater director who for decades during the Soviet era staged nearly every production the Bolshoi Opera presented.

name: Bernard Barker
headline: Bernard Barker, 92, a Watergate Burglar, Dies
abstract: Bernard L. Barker, one of the burglars whose 1972 break-in at the Watergate building led to the resignation of President Richard M. Nixon.

name: Gerald W. Scully
headline: Gerald W. Scully, Who Wrote Landmark Baseball Analysis, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Scully was a sports economist who offered an early statistical argument that major league baseball players were being exploited by their teams.

name: Ernest May
headline: Ernest May, International Relations Expert, Dies at 80
abstract: Professor May was a leading historian of international relations who published major works on the United States’ entry into World War I and the fall of France in 1940.

name: George MacPherson
headline: George MacPherson, Theater Producer, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. MacPherson was a theater producer who helped bring down the curtain on bus-and-truck road shows and usher in the big-box-office age of polished national touring companies.

name: Peter L. Bernstein
headline: Peter L. Bernstein, Explainer of Risks of Stocks, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Bernstein embraced and spread efficient market theory, an alternative to stock-picking. He changed the way Americans invest.

name: Fleur Cowles
profession: Friend of the Elite and the Editor of a Magazine for Them
headline: Fleur Cowles, 101, Is Dead; Friend of the Elite and the Editor of a Magazine for Them
abstract: Ms. Cowles was a painter, a writer and a renowned hostess who oversaw Flair magazine, a chic but short-lived publication.

name: Omar Bongo
headline: Omar Bongo, Gabon Leader, Dies at 73
abstract: President El Hadj Omar Bongo Ondimba of Gabon ruled over his small West African nation for 41 years.

name: Roy Boe
profession: Owned Islanders and Nets but Sold Dr. J
headline: Roy Boe, Who Owned Islanders and Nets but Sold Dr. J, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Boe’s simultaneous stewardship of two New York area sports franchises, the Nets and the Islanders, brought championships, controversy and financial struggles.

name: Kenny Rankin
headline: Kenny Rankin, Melder of Jazz and Pop, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Rankin was an introspective singer-songwriter who drew inspiration from a wide range of sources. He was admired by everyone from The Beatles to Johnny Carson.

name: Robert Colescott
headline: Robert Colescott, Painter Who Toyed With Race and Sex, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Colescott’s garishly powerful canvases lampooned racial and sexual stereotypes with rakish imagery, lurid colors and tangible glee.

name: Kamala Das
headline: Kamala Das, Indian Poet and Memoirist, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Das was known for her open discussion of women’s sexual and romantic lives, of desire and its discontents.

name: Norman Brinker
headline: Norman Brinker, Casual Dining Innovator, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Brinker helped put casual dining and salad bars on the American menu with the Steak and Ale, Bennigan’s chains, and Chili’s restaurants.

name: Luke Cole
headline: Luke Cole, Court Advocate for Minorities, Dies at 46
abstract: Mr. Cole was an early leader of the environmental justice movement, which holds that many of the poorest minority neighborhoods have become toxic dumping grounds.

name: Rajeev Motwani
profession: Guide in the Creation of Google
headline: Rajeev Motwani, Guide in the Creation of Google, Dies at 47
abstract: Professor Motwani taught computer science at Stanford and was a mentor to many Silicon Valley start-ups.

name: Hugh Hopper
profession: Composer and Bassist for Soft Machine
headline: Hugh Hopper, Composer and Bassist for Soft Machine, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Hopper was the bassist for the British progressive rock band Soft Machine and a central figure in the forward-looking music scene that bloomed in Canterbury in the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Richard Quick
headline: Richard Quick, Olympic Swimming Coach, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Quick was a head coach of United States swimming teams in three Olympics and the winner of more N.C.A.A. team titles, 13, than any other coach.

name: Gaafar al-Nimeiry
headline: Gaafar al-Nimeiry, a Sudan Leader With Shifting Politics, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. al-Nimeiry took over Sudan in a 1969 coup and held on to the presidency until a bloodless coup ousted him in 1985.

name: Jean Hugel
headline: Jean Hugel, Alsace Winemaker, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Hugel was a leading force in resurrecting the Alsatian wine trade after the devastation of World War II and the longtime head of one of the best-known and oldest producers in Alsace.

name: Edward Hanrahan
headline: Edward Hanrahan, Prosecutor Tied to ’69 Panthers Raid, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Hanrahan was a Cook County state’s attorney who built a reputation by prosecuting criminals, but his political career was derailed by a deadly police raid on Black Panthers in 1969.

name: Huey Long
headline: Huey Long, Guitarist for Ink Spots, Dies at 105
abstract: Mr. Long, who took up the guitar in 1933, performed with an extensive list of greats in a journey that began with Dixieland, moved into swing and jumped forward to bebop.

name: Harold Norse
headline: Harold Norse, a Beat Poet, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Norse was a poet who broke new ground beginning in the 1950s by exploring sexuality in a distinctly American idiom relying on plain language and direct imagery.

name: Delbert Osguthorpe
headline: Delbert Osguthorpe, Early Voice for Environment, Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Osguthorpe was a prominent large-animal veterinarian, who fought to stop biological weapons testing.

name: Alan Berkman
headline: Alan Berkman, 63, Activist Doctor, Dies
abstract: Dr. Berkman was a Vietnam-era radical who founded a group that helped make AIDS medications available to some of the world’s poorest people.

name: Christian Albin
headline: Christian Albin, Four Seasons Head Chef, Dies at 61
abstract: Called a “culinary Rip van Winkle,” Mr. Albin was the executive chef of the Four Seasons restaurant in Manhattan.

name: Barry Beckett
headline: Barry Beckett, Muscle Shoals Musician, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Beckett was an Alabama-born keyboardist who helped create the distinctly Southern amalgamation of rhythm and blues, soul and country that became known as the Muscle Shoals sound.

name: Philip Curtin
headline: Philip Curtin, 87, Scholar of Slave Trade, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Curtin was an influential historian whose use of statistical methods suggested that fewer slaves were transported from Africa than had previously been thought.

name: James F. Calvert
headline: James F. Calvert, 88, Sub Captain Who Surfaced at North Pole, Dies
abstract: Vice Admiral Calvert was the commander of the first nuclear-powered submarine to surface at the North Pole.

name: Bob Bogle
headline: Bob Bogle, Ventures’ Guitarist, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Bogle was a founding member of the Ventures, the long-running guitar band whose jaunty 1960 hit “Walk — Don’t Run” became an early standard.

name: Selma Weiser
headline: Selma Weiser, Boutique Innovator, Dies at 84
abstract: Mrs. Weiser created Charivari, a forward-looking fashion boutique that grew into a retail mini-empire on the previously fashion-starved Upper West Side of Manhattan.

name: John A. Eddy
headline: John A. Eddy, Solar Detective, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Eddy was a solar astronomer, who studied the history of the sun and demonstrated that it is not a constant star with a regular cycle of behavior but rather one that has periods of anomaly.

name: Paul Fino
headline: Paul Fino, Politician Who Battled Lindsay, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Fino was a former congressman from the Bronx who stoked a long-running feud with Mayor John V. Lindsay of New York in the late 1960s.

name: Dusty Rhodes
headline: Dusty Rhodes, Star Pinch-Hitter in ’54 Series, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Rhodes’s pinch-hitting heroics led the New York Giants to win the 1954 World Series.

name: Ali Akbar Khan
headline: Ali Akbar Khan, Sarod Virtuoso, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Khan was the foremost virtuoso of the lutelike sarod, with a dazzling technique and gift for melodic invention.

name: John Houghtaling
profession: Inventor of Magic Fingers Vibrating Bed
headline: John Houghtaling, Inventor of Magic Fingers Vibrating Bed, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Houghtaling’s device, developed in 1958, was a ubiquitous presence in the roadside America of the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Frank J. Low
profession: Helped Drive Field of Infrared Astronomy
headline: Frank J. Low, Who Helped Drive Field of Infrared Astronomy, Dies at 75
abstract: Dr. Low helped astronomers extend their vision beyond visible light into a vast realm of previously invisible colors, revolutionizing the study of the birth of planets, stars and galaxies.

name: Wayne L. Horvitz
headline: Wayne L. Horvitz, 88, Labor Mediator, Dies
abstract: Mr. Horvitz was a Carter administration official who would sometimes go to the bargaining table himself to settle major labor-management disputes.

name: Ralf Dahrendorf
headline: Ralf Dahrendorf, Sociologist, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Dahrendorf’s experiences in Nazi Germany led him to develop a theory of liberalism and human freedom that often went against the grain of German politics in the postwar period.

name: Jean Dausset
headline: Jean Dausset, Nobel Laureate, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Dausset was a French immunologist who performed influential research that, among other things, improved the chances of success in organ transplants.

name: Heyward Isham
headline: Heyward Isham, a Negotiator With Hanoi, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Isham was a career Foreign Service officer who helped negotiate the American peace accord with North Vietnam in 1973 and later became ambassador to Haiti.

name: Ed McMahon
headline: Ed McMahon, Top Second Banana, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. McMahon was Johnny Carson’s affable sidekick on “The Tonight Show” for nearly 30 years.

name: Jerri FitzGerald
headline: Jerri FitzGerald, Who Treated Herself at South Pole, Dies at 57
abstract: Breast cancer recurred in Dr. FitzGerald whose treatment was guided via computer for months in 1999 until a rescue plane was able to land.

name: Shelly Gross
headline: Shelly Gross, Producer for Broadway and Suburbs, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Gross brought a broad spectrum of entertainment to suburban theaters along the East Coast and also produced more than a dozen Broadway shows.

name: T. Scott Cunningham
headline: T. Scott Cunningham, Seasoned Off Broadway Player, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. Cunningham was an actor who found comedy in the plight of the lovable loser in Nicky Silver’s breakthrough Off Broadway play “Pterodactyls” and Douglas Carter Beane’s “As Bees in Honey Drown.”

name: Betty Allen
headline: Betty Allen, Opera Singer and Educator, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Allen was an American mezzo-soprano who transcended a Dickensian girlhood to become an internationally known opera singer and later a prominent voice teacher and arts administrator.

name: Farrah Fawcett
headline: Farrah Fawcett Dies of Cancer at 62
abstract: Ms. Fawcett was an actress, television star and pop-culture phenomenon whose good looks and signature leonine hairstyle influenced a generation of women.

name: Michael Jackson
headline: A Star Idolized and Haunted, Michael Jackson Dies at 50
abstract: Michael Jackson, 50, who went from boy wonder to global pop superstar to sad figure haunted by lawsuits, paparazzi and failed plastic surgery, died Thursday in a Los Angeles hospital.

name: Michael Jackson
headline: Michael Jackson, British General Who Disobeyed U.S. Superior, Dies at 80
abstract: Labeled “the Prince of Darkness,” he refused to follow an order by NATO’s commander during the Balkans war, saying, “It’s not worth starting World War III.”

name: Sky Saxon
profession: Lead Singer and Bassist for the Seeds
headline: Sky Saxon, Lead Singer and Bassist for the Seeds, Dies
abstract: Mr. Saxon was the mop-haired bass player and front man for the protopunk band the Seeds, whose song “Pushin’ Too Hard” put a Los Angeles garage-band spin on the bad-boy rocker image personified by the Rolling Stones.

name: Morton Gottlieb
headline: Morton Gottlieb, a Broadway Producer, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Gottlieb was a Broadway stalwart who produced four plays that were nominated for best-play Tony Awards, one of which, “Sleuth,” was the winner in 1971.

name: George K. Fraenkel
headline: George K. Fraenkel, Pioneering Chemist, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Fraenkel was one of several chemists who developed high-sensitivity, high-resolution spectrometers that could track the spin of electrons and thereby obtain information on very small structures.

name: Robert A. Derzon
profession: First Director of Medicare and Medicaid
headline: Robert A. Derzon, First Director of Medicare and Medicaid, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Derzon was an early proponent of universal health care coverage who was charged with minimizing fraud and abuse and cutting costs at the merged health agencies.

name: Antonio Bianco
profession: Teased Luster and Light From Diamonds
headline: Antonio Bianco, Who Teased Luster and Light From Diamonds, Dies at 57
abstract: Called a Stradivari of stones, Mr. Bianco cut some of the world’s largest and most unusually colored gems, among them the “Dream,” the “Flame” and the “Golden Star.”

name: Billy Mays
headline: Billy Mays, Enthusiastic TV Pitchman, Dies at 50
abstract: Mr. Mays, the promoter of such products as OxiClean and Orange Glo, became widely known for his enthusiastic, boisterous delivery.

name: Michael Martin
profession: Subway Graffiti Artist Iz the Wiz
headline: Michael Martin, Subway Graffiti Artist Iz the Wiz, Is Dead at 50
abstract: Iz the Wiz was a legend among graffiti artists, by almost all accounts “the longest-reigning all-city king in N.Y.C. history,” as a graffiti Web site put it.

name: Gale Storm
profession: Earned Television Fame for Her Wholesome Roles
headline: Gale Storm, 87, Is Dead; Earned Television Fame for Her Wholesome Roles
abstract: Ms. Storm was a Texas-born actress who made wholesome perkiness a defining element of television’s golden age on two hit sitcoms, “My Little Margie” and “The Gale Storm Show.”

name: Fred Travalena
headline: Fred Travalena, Master of Impressions in Comedy, Is Dead at 66
abstract: Mr. Travalena, a comedian and singer, was known for a range of impressions of celebrities like Bugs Bunny, Ted Koppel and singers like Sammy Davis Jr. and Bobby Darin.

name: Pina Bausch
headline: Pina Bausch, German Choreographer, Dies at 68
abstract: The choreographer combined potent drama and dreamlike movement to create a powerful form of dance theater that influenced generations of dancemakers.

name: Fayette Pinkney
profession: Soulful Singer With the Three Degrees
headline: Fayette Pinkney, Soulful Singer With the Three Degrees, Dies at 61
abstract: Ms. Pinkney was an original member of the Three Degrees who lent her voice to the 1970s hits “When Will I See You Again?” and “T.S.O.P. (The Sound of Philadelphia).”

name: Karl Malden
headline: Karl Malden, Actor Who Played the Uncommon Everyman, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Malden’s half-century in show business carried him from theater to films to television’s “The Streets of San Francisco.”

name: Alexis Argüello
headline: Alexis Argüello, 57, Boxer and Politician, Dies
abstract: Mr. Argüello was a boxer who won titles in three weight classes, entered politics after his retirement and last fall was elected mayor of Managua, the capital of Nicaragua.

name: Shi Pei Pu
headline: Shi Pei Pu, Singer, Spy and ‘M. Butterfly,’ Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Shi was a Beijing opera singer and spy whose sexually convoluted love affair with a French Embassy worker was the inspiration for the Broadway show.

name: Harve Presnell
headline: Harve Presnell, Singing Actor, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Presnell’s operatic baritone thrilled audiences in the stage and film versions of “The Unsinkable Molly Brown.”

name: Mollie Sugden
headline: Mollie Sugden, Sitcom Star, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Sugden achieved wide popularity in Britain and the United States as Betty Slocombe in the long-running BBC comedy series “Are You Being Served?”

name: Herbert G. Klein
profession: Aide in the Nixon White House
headline: Herbert G. Klein, Aide in the Nixon White House, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Klein was a campaign and White House aide to President Richard M. Nixon who remained loyal to him despite personal and professional slights.

name: Tyeb Mehta
headline: Tyeb Mehta, Painter of Emerging India, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Mehta emerged as the leading light of India’s first post-colonial generation of Modernist painters.

name: Sandra Warfield
headline: Sandra Warfield, Opera and Cabaret Singer, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Warfield was an American mezzo-soprano who performed frequently with the Metropolitan Opera in the 1950s, ’60s and early ’70s.

name: Ken Roberts
headline: Ken Roberts, Announcer Whose Voice Graced the Heyday of Radio, Dies at 99
abstract: Known for his comforting voice, Mr. Roberts was welcomed in millions of American homes over the airwaves.

name: Allen Klein
headline: Allen Klein, 77, Dies; Managed Music Legends
abstract: Mr. Klein managed the business affairs of Sam Cooke, the Rolling Stones and, for a short time, the Beatles.

name: Joe Bowman
headline: Joe Bowman, Sharpshooter, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Bowman dazzled crowds with fancy gunplay and came to embody a vanishing cowboy culture.

name: Robert S. McNamara
headline: Robert S. McNamara, Architect of a Futile War, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. McNamara helped lead the U.S. into the Vietnam War and spent the rest of his life wrestling with its moral consequences.

name: Bela Kiraly
headline: Bela Kiraly Dies at 97; Led Revolt in Hungary
abstract: General Kiraly was the commander in chief of the revolutionary forces in the Hungarian uprising of 1956 and considered a folk hero for more than half a century.

name: Vasily Aksyonov
headline: Vasily Aksyonov, Exiled Soviet Writer, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Mr. Aksyonov was a writer who symbolized both the cultural flowering of the period after Stalin’s death and the clampdown that followed it.

name: John Bachar
headline: John Bachar, Rock Climber, Dies at 51
abstract: Mr. Bachar inspired awe as a daredevil, condescension as an anachronism and eventually respect as a legend.

name: D. Mark Hegsted
headline: D. Mark Hegsted, 95, Harvard Nutritionist, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Hegsted’s studies of fats and their role in promoting heart disease led to influential federal guidelines in the 1970s.

name: Jo Amar
headline: Jo Amar, Genre-Blending Jewish Singer, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Amar was a Moroccan-born Jewish singer whose melding of Andalusian and Israeli musical influences made him a star.

name: Harry J. Gray
profession: Led the Rise of United Technologies
headline: Harry J. Gray, Who Led the Rise of United Technologies, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Gray rose from poverty to lead the transformation of United Aircraft into United Technologies, one of the world’s broadest and most powerful conglomerates.

name: William F. Reedy
headline: William F. Reedy, Who Was Injured in Crash That Killed Billy Martin, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Reedy was convicted of drunken driving in the 1989 crash that killed the former Yankees manager.

name: Drake Levin
headline: Drake Levin, of Paul Revere & the Raiders, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Levin was lead guitarist for the teen-idol rock band Paul Revere & the Raiders during their biggest hit-making years in the mid-1960s.

name: Frank Mickens
profession: Brought Success to a Tough Brooklyn High School
headline: Frank Mickens, Who Brought Success to a Tough Brooklyn High School, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Mickens was a blunt, no-nonsense principal who brought order and significant academic improvement to what was once one of New York City’s most troubled schools.

name: Robert Isabell
headline: Robert Isabell, Who Turned Events Into Wondrous Occasions, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Isabell was the floral designer and events planner whose shrewdly lavish aesthetic helped create the buzz around Studio 54.

name: Peter Wheeler
headline: Peter Wheeler, British Car Executive, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Wheeler, a chemical engineer, was once the owner of the quirky sports car maker TVR , which designed several models in an effort to take on giants like Porsche and Ferrari.

name: Paul Hemphill
headline: Paul Hemphill, Chronicler of the South, Dies at 73
abstract: In newspaper columns, essays and novels, Mr. Hemphill wrote of the region’s blue-collar passions: stock-car racing, football and country music.

name: John Orman
headline: John Orman, Teacher of Politics Who Practiced It, Too, Dies at 60
abstract: Professor Orman was a Fairfield University politics teacher who seized control of Senator Joseph I. Lieberman’s personal party, saying he had to be true to his instructions to students.

name: Arturo Gatti
profession: Fearless Boxer Known for Relentless Violence
headline: Arturo Gatti, Fearless Boxer Known for Relentless Violence, Dies at 37
abstract: Mr. Gatti, best known for three brutal bouts with Micky Ward, was found dead in a Brazilian hotel room. His wife was detained.

name: Barbara Margolis
headline: Barbara Margolis, Prisoners’ Advocate, Dies at 79
abstract: Mrs. Margolis was the founder and director of Fresh Start, a program that trains Rikers Island inmates for employment upon release.

name: John Henry Moss
profession: Head of Minor League for 50 Years
headline: John Henry Moss, Head of Minor League for 50 Years, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Moss, a detail-oriented and forward-looking man, emphasized the fan experience and advocated for Internet marketing.

name: Robert Louis-Dreyfus
headline: Robert Louis-Dreyfus, Turnaround Specialist, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Louis-Dreyfus was an executive who worked in a range of companies, from sneaker makers to advertising. He earned a reputation for whipping weak companies into shape.

name: Lou Pagliaro
headline: Lou Pagliaro, National Table Tennis Champion, Dies at 90
abstract: At just over 5 feet tall but with nimble footwork and a rocketing forehand, Mr. Pagliaro won the national championship in 1940-42 and 1952.

name: Harry Edelstein
profession: Host of Popular Polish Tea Room
headline: Harry Edelstein, 91, Host of Popular Polish Tea Room, Dies
abstract: Mr. Edelstein, with his wife, Frances, owned the venerable Broadway hangout affectionately known as the Polish Tea Room.

name: Reggie Fleming
profession: Hockey Player Known for Physical Style
headline: Reggie Fleming, Hockey Player Known for Physical Style, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Fleming was one of the N.H.L.’s toughest players in the 1960s and a fan favorite in the cities where he played.

name: Kenneth M. Stampp
headline: Kenneth M. Stampp, Civil War Historian, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Stampp’s writings about the period turned accepted wisdom inside out and engendered seismic shifts in the scholarship.

name: Dash Snow
headline: Dash Snow, East Village Artistic Rebel, Dies at 27
abstract: Mr. Snow rebelled against his privileged and art-loving family in his teens to become a promising young New York artist in his own right.

name: Sam Church
headline: Sam Church, Who Led United Mine Workers, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Church led the United Mine Workers of America during a tumultuous time when the union was growing more democratic while its numbers were dwindling.

name: Jane Weinberger
headline: Jane Weinberger, Author Who Became Publisher, Dies at 91
abstract: The widow of former Defense Secretary Caspar W. Weinberger started out writing children’s books but her books for adults included her frank correspondence.

name: Julius Shulman
headline: Julius Shulman, Photographer of Modernist California Architecture, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Shulman’s photographs depicted modern houses as the ultimate expressions of modern living and helped idealize the California lifestyle in the postwar years.

name: Christopher Hipp
headline: Christopher Hipp, Who Bolstered Computer Power, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. Hipp was a designer of compact devices that gave companies substantially more computer power while using significantly less space.

name: Walter Cronkite
headline: Walter Cronkite, 92, Dies; Trusted Voice of TV News
abstract: Mr. Cronkite guided viewers with such plain-spoken grace that he was called the most trusted man in America.

name: Henry Allingham
profession: British Veteran of World War I
headline: Henry Allingham, British Veteran of World War I, Dies at 113
abstract: For years, Britain’s oldest man refused to talk about his wartime service, but later in life he opened up, though he resisted the idea that he was a hero.

name: Ralph F. Hirschmann
profession: Leading Scientist on Early Enzyme Research
headline: Ralph F. Hirschmann, Leading Scientist on Early Enzyme Research, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Hirschmann was a leader of a team of biochemists that for the first time synthesized an enzyme, one of the master chemicals of life.

name: Judi Ann Mason
headline: Judi Ann Mason, Who Wrote for Stage and Screen, Dies at 54
abstract: Ms. Mason, whose work often explored facets of the African-American experience, was among the first black female sitcom writers.

name: Frank McCourt
headline: Frank McCourt, Whose Irish Childhood Illuminated His Prose, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. McCourt, a former New York City schoolteacher, turned his miserable Irish childhood into a Pulitzer Prize-winning memoir, “Angela’s Ashes.”

name: William Conner
headline: William Conner, Judge Expert in Patent Law, Dies at 89
abstract: Appointed by President Richard M. Nixon, Mr. Conner handed down noted decisions involving songwriters’ royalty payments, the Marx Brothers and Howard Cosell.

name: Tom Wilkes
headline: Tom Wilkes, Album Cover Designer, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Wilkes was an art director, photographer and designer who illustrated the age of rock ’n’ roll.

name: Leszek Kolakowski
headline: Leszek Kolakowski, Polish Philosopher, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Kolakowski had embraced, and then rejected, the intellectual pillars of Communism and had been credited with serving a crucial role in Poland’s fate.

name: Gordon Waller
profession: Partner in the Band Peter and Gordon
headline: Gordon Waller, a Partner in the Band Peter and Gordon, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Waller formed half of Peter and Gordon, a successful pop duo that followed the Beatles to America as part of the British Invasion of the 1960s.

name: Sidney W. Bijou
headline: Sidney W. Bijou, Child Psychologist, Is Dead at 100
abstract: Mr. Bijou helped establish modern behavioral therapy for childhood disorders like autism and attention deficit disorder.

name: Yury Verlinsky
headline: Yury Verlinsky, Expert in Embryonic Screening, Is Dead at 65
abstract: Mr. Verlinsky was one of the first scientists to develop techniques to detect genetic disorders in embryos and helped make the screening available to parents worldwide.

name: Heinz Edelmann
headline: Heinz Edelmann, ‘Yellow Submarine’ Artist, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Edelmann was the graphic designer and illustrator who created the hallucinogenic landscape of Pepperland for the 1968 Beatles film “Yellow Submarine.”

name: H. A. Engle
headline: H. A. Engle, Tobacco Plaintiff, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Engle was a lifelong smoker and the lead plaintiff in a landmark class-action suit against the tobacco industry.

name: Les Lye
headline: Les Lye, Canadian TV Comic, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Lye was a Canadian actor and broadcaster best known in the United States as a cast member of the children’s comedy show “You Can’t Do That on Television.”

name: Ray Shaw
headline: Ray Shaw, Head of Business Newspapers, Dies at 75
abstract: After retiring from The Wall Street Journal, Mr. Shaw took over a chain of local business newsweeklies and made it the nation’s largest.

name: Lionel Casson
headline: Lionel Casson, Who Wrote of Ancient Maritime History, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Casson, a longtime New York University professor, wrote 23 books on Greek and Latin literature and seafaring in the ancient Western world.

name: E. Lynn Harris
profession: Wrote of Gay Black Mens Lives
headline: E. Lynn Harris, Who Wrote of Gay Black Men’s Lives, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Harris’s novels about successful and glamorous black men with sexual identity conflicts made him one of the nation’s most popular writers.

name: Harry Patch
profession: Last of Britains Army Veterans of World War I
headline: Harry Patch, the Last of Britain’s Army Veterans of World War I, Is Dead at 111
abstract: Mr. Patch was one of the last living links to what was called at the time “the war to end all wars.”

name: Alan G. Davenport
headline: Alan G. Davenport, Noted Wind Engineer, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Davenport devised ways to gauge the effects of wind on tall structures, then applied his expertise to some of the world’s biggest buildings and longest bridges.

name: Thomas Dao
profession: Expert on Treatment of Breast Cancer
headline: Dr. Thomas Dao, Expert on Treatment of Breast Cancer, Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Dao opposed radical mastectomy in favor of more conservative surgery and worked with a Nobel laureate on research into the role of hormones in human cancer.

name: Vernon Forrest
headline: Vernon Forrest, Ex-Boxing Champion, Dies at 38
abstract: Mr. Forrest, the former welterweight and light-middleweight titleholder known as the Viper for the speed of his fists, was apparently robbed before being shot.

name: Otto Heino
headline: Otto Heino, Ceramicist Who Elevated the Humble Pot to Art, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Mr. Heino, a driven craftsman who was said to produce up to 10,000 pieces a year, was known as a purist in his work with clay.

name: Merce Cunningham
headline: Merce Cunningham, Dance Visionary, Dies
abstract: The performer was among a handful of 20th-century figures to make dance a major art form. He was 90.

name: George Weissman
profession: Leader at Philip Morris and in the Arts in New York
headline: George Weissman, Leader at Philip Morris and in the Arts in New York, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Weissman helped transform Philip Morris into a diversified conglomerate, and then led Lincoln Center for nearly a decade.

name: Lois Hunt
headline: Lois Hunt, Half of Popular Operatic Duo, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Hunt’s operatic lyric soprano blended seamlessly with Earl Wrightson’s baritone in a partnership that lasted nearly 40 years.

name: Gerald Gardner
headline: Gerald Gardner, 83, Dies; Bolstered Sex Bias Suit
abstract: Dr. Gardner was a mathematician whose work bolstered a landmark legal case that led to a ban on sex discrimination in newspaper want ads.

name: Michael Steinberg
headline: Michael Steinberg, Music Critic, Teacher and Program Annotator, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Mr. Steinberg, an influential classical music critic, teacher, lecturer and author, was the pre-eminent program annotator of his day.

name: Zhuo Lin
headline: Zhuo Lin, Widow of Chinese Leader Deng, Dies at 93
abstract: Herself a Communist stalwart, she helped Deng Xiaoping survive political purges and become the country’s paramount leader during much of the post-Mao era.

name: George Russell
headline: George Russell, Composer Whose Theories Sent Jazz in a New Direction, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Russell was a major figure in one of the most important developments in post-World War II jazz: the emergence of modal jazz, the first major harmonic change in the music after bebop.

name: Ike
headline: Reverend Ike, Who Preached Riches, Dies at 74
abstract: The Rev. Frederick J. Eikerenkoetter II was one of the first evangelists to embrace television.

name: Jim Johnson
profession: Innovative Defensive Assistant in the N.F.L
headline: Jim Johnson, Innovative Defensive Assistant in the N.F.L., Dies at 68
abstract: The Philadelphia Eagles’ defensive coordinator was known for complicated schemes to pressure the opposing quarterback.

name: Olga Méndez
headline: Olga Méndez, Longtime State Senator, Dies at 84
abstract: Mrs. Méndez, a lawmaker who represented East Harlem and the South Bronx for 26 years, was the first Puerto Rican in the State Senate.

name: Elinor Gordon
headline: Elinor Gordon, Dealer in Chinese Porcelain, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Gordon was a dealer and collector who helped elevate the status of Chinese export porcelain and acquired important pieces for collectors and museums.

name: Gayatri Devi
headline: Gayatri Devi, 90, a Maharani and a Lawmaker, Dies
abstract: The former Maharani of Jaipur was a beauty Vogue once described as “a dream in sari and jewels,” and an advocate for women’s freedom.

name: Corazon Aquino
headline: Corazon Aquino, Ex-Leader of Philippines, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Mrs. Aquino was swept into office on a wave of “people power” in 1986 and then faced down many coup attempts as president.

name: Tony Rosenthal
headline: Tony Rosenthal, Sculptor of Public Art, Dies at 94
abstract: The artist created “Alamo,” the eternally popular revolving black cube in Astor Place in the East Village, and many other public sculptures.

name: Lynn Pressman Raymond
headline: Lynn Pressman Raymond, Toy Executive, Dies at 97
abstract: A savvy, innovative businesswoman, Mrs. Raymond brought flair to the toy industry.

name: Dina Babbitt
headline: Dina Babbitt, Artist at Auschwitz, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Ms. Babbitt was a prisoner at the Auschwitz concentration camp who bartered her services as a portrait painter for her life and her mother’s life.

name: Sidney Zion
headline: Sidney Zion, Writer Who Crusaded to Reduce Doctors’ Hours, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Zion’s grief and outrage at the death of his daughter, Libby, in a hospital led to changes in how young physicians are trained.

name: Michael A. Wiener
headline: Michael A. Wiener, Founder of a Radio Chain, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Wiener helped to found Infinity Broadcasting, which would go on to expand to dozens of stations and would hire Howard Stern.

name: John Kiermaier
headline: John Kiermaier, Channel 13 Executive, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Kiermaier steered Channel 13, the New York area’s major public television station, through precarious financial times in the 1960s.

name: Naomi Sims
headline: Naomi Sims, 61, Pioneering Cover Girl, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Sims’s appearance on the cover of Ladies’ Home Journal in November 1968 was a consummate moment of the Black is Beautiful movement.

name: Theodore Nierenberg
headline: Theodore Nierenberg, Founder of Dansk, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Nierenberg founded Dansk International Designs, whose cookware and dinnerware helped bring the Scandinavian Modern style to the postwar American table.

name: Charles Gwathmey
profession: Architect Loyal to Aesthetics of High Modernism
headline: Charles Gwathmey, Architect Loyal to Aesthetics of High Modernism, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Gwathmey turned his passion for geometrical complexity into a series of compelling houses and sometimes controversial public buildings.

name: Ernest W. Lefever
headline: Ernest W. Lefever, Rejected as a Reagan Nominee, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Lefever was a Protestant minister and scholar whose 1981 nomination to a human rights post was turned down by a Senate panel.

name: Thomas N. Schroth
headline: Thomas N. Schroth, Influential Washington Editor, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Schroth helped expand and deepen political coverage of Washington as the editor of Congressional Quarterly and a founding editor of National Journal.

name: Budd Schulberg
headline: Budd Schulberg, ‘On the Waterfront’ Writer, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Schulberg wrote the award-winning screenplay for “On the Waterfront” and created an archetype of naked ambition in his novel “What Makes Sammy Run?”

name: Amos Kenan
headline: Amos Kenan, Israeli Writer and Iconoclast, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Kenan was an Israeli writer whose anti-religious and anti-Zionist views made him a longstanding irritant to the political establishment.

name: John Hughes
profession: Captured the Lives of Teenagers in the 1980s
headline: John Hughes, Who Captured the Lives of Teenagers in the 1980s, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Hughes helped define a generation with films like “The Breakfast Club,” “Sixteen Candles” and “Ferris Bueller’s Day Off.”

name: Donald Marshall Jr.
headline: Donald Marshall Jr., Symbol of Bias, Dies at 55
abstract: A wrongful conviction revealed systemic racism against Indians in Canada and became a landmark case.

name: Eli Mason
headline: Eli Mason, 88, Outspoken Accountant, Is Dead
abstract: A defender of small and midsize accounting firms and a benefactor of Baruch College of the City University of New York.

name: Willy DeVille
headline: Willy DeVille, Mink DeVille Singer and Songwriter, Is Dead at 58
abstract: Mr. DeVille’s adventurous forays into rhythm and blues, Cajun music and salsa made him one of the most original figures of the New York punk scene of the 1970s.

name: R. M. Takasugi
headline: R. M. Takasugi, Pioneering Asian Judge, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Takasugi spent most of World War II with his family in a California internment camp and grew up to become one of the first Japanese-Americans to serve as a federal judge.

name: Anne Wexler
headline: Anne Wexler, an Influential Political Operative and Lobbyist, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Ms. Wexler, known as the “Rolodex Queen,” did just about everything in politics, from licking envelopes to serving as an aide in the Carter White House to becoming an influential lobbyist.

name: Carleen Hutchins
headline: Carleen Hutchins, Innovative Violin Maker, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Mrs. Hutchins helped reimagine the idea of what a violin could be and designed and built an entire family of violins, eight instruments known as the new violin family or the violin octet.

name: Evelyn Coke
headline: Evelyn Coke, Home Care Aide Who Fought Pay Rule, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Ms. Coke’s case seeking overtime wages was rejected by the Supreme Court, but others have taken up her cause.

name: Mike Seeger
headline: Mike Seeger, Singer and Music Historian, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Seeger was a singer and multi-instrumentalist who played an important role in the folk revival of the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Jimmy Bedford
headline: Jimmy Bedford, Guardian of Jack Daniel’s, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Bedford was the sixth master distiller in the 143-year history of the Jack Daniel’s distillery.

name: Marcey Jacobson
headline: Marcey Jacobson, a Photographer Inspired by Mexico, Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Jacobson was a self-taught photographer from New York City who spent decades in the southern Mexican highlands documenting the lives of the indigenous Indian peoples.

name: Eunice Kennedy Shriver
headline: Eunice Kennedy Shriver, Influential Founder of Special Olympics, Dies at 88
abstract: Mrs. Shriver, 88, was a sister of President John F. Kennedy and a trailblazer in improving the lives of people with disabilities.

name: Merlyn Mantle
profession: Was Married to Yankees Great for 43 Years
headline: Merlyn Mantle, Who Was Married to Yankees Great for 43 Years, Dies at 77
abstract: Merlyn and Mickey Mantle met in 1949 when he was a star player at Commerce (Okla.) High School and she was a cheerleader at archrival Picher High School.

name: Mark Rosenzweig
headline: Mark Rosenzweig, Brain Researcher, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Dr. Rosenzweig proved that the rodent brain reshapes itself in response to experience, even into adulthood.

name: Andy Kessler
headline: Andy Kessler, Skateboard Hero, Dies at 48
abstract: Mr. Kessler banded with graffiti artists to help give a distinctively New York spin to the nascent sport of skateboarding and then helped popularize it by designing skate parks.

name: Les Paul
headline: Les Paul, Guitar Innovator, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Paul was a virtuoso guitarist and inventor whose solid-body electric guitar and recording studio innovations changed the course of music.

name: Jack T. Kirby
headline: Jack T. Kirby, Southern Historian, Dies at 70
abstract: Dr. Kirby was a historian who decried stereotypes of the American South and traced the ways its people and landscapes have shaped one another.

name: Margaret Wilson
profession: First Black Woman to Head N.A.A.C.P. Board
headline: Margaret Wilson, First Black Woman to Head N.A.A.C.P. Board, Dies at 90
abstract: Mrs. Wilson became the first black woman to head the board of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People, then was ousted in a bitter power struggle in 1983.

name: Ruth Ford
headline: Ruth Ford, Film and Stage Actress, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Ford was a film and stage actress who turned her Manhattan apartment into a salon as she became something of a muse to writers, artists and musicians.

name: Rashied Ali
headline: Rashied Ali, Free-Jazz Drummer, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Ali’s expressionistic, free-jazz drumming helped define the experimental style of John Coltrane’s final years.

name: John Coburn
headline: John Coburn, Bishop in the Episcopal Church, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Coburn was a former bishop of Massachusetts and a nationally prominent leader of the Episcopal Church.

name: K. H. Bacon
headline: K. H. Bacon, an Advocate for Refugees, Is Dead at 64
abstract: Mr. Bacon was a former journalist and Pentagon spokesman who devoted his last years to highlighting the plight of refugees worldwide.

name: Riccardo Cassin
headline: Riccardo Cassin, 100, Dies; A Legendary Mountaineer
abstract: Mr. Cassin scaled hundreds of the world’s most daunting peaks with daring, tenacity and technical brilliance.

name: David Drew
headline: David Drew, Musicologist, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Drew was a music critic and musicologist who rescued the work of Kurt Weill from neglect and promoted him to his present position as an important 20th-century composer.

name: Lawrence Lucie
headline: Lawrence Lucie, Guitarist With Jelly Roll Morton, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Lucie was a master of the underrated art of keeping the beat, and over the years he kept it for some of the biggest names in jazz.

name: Jim Dickinson
profession: Pianist and Player in Memphis Music Scene
headline: Jim Dickinson, Pianist and Player in Memphis Music Scene, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Dickinson was a pianist, singer and producer who helped make Memphis a hot spot for recording artists and who played with Aretha Franklin, the Rolling Stones, Bob Dylan and Ry Cooder.

name: Richard Poirier
headline: Richard Poirier, a Scholar of Literature, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Poirier was a prolific and populist cultural critic who founded a literary journal and who was a founder of Library of America, the nonprofit publisher of American classics.

name: Kim Dae-jung
headline: Kim Dae-jung, Ex-President of S. Korea, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Kim, a dissident who became president, sought to warm ties with North Korea and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 2000.

name: Robert Novak
headline: Robert Novak, Pugnacious Columnist, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Novak was a political columnist and cable television fixture whose scoops reached across five decades.

name: Rose Friedman
headline: Rose Friedman, Economist and Collaborator, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Friedman said she never felt overshadowed by her husband, who made a habit of giving her full credit for her contributions to their work.

name: Adrian DeWind
profession: Tax Expert and Human Rights Watch Founder
headline: Adrian DeWind, Tax Expert and Human Rights Watch Founder, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. DeWind, an expert on tax law, was also an influential advocate for human rights and nuclear nonproliferation.

name: Don Hewitt
headline: Don Hewitt, Creator of ‘60 Minutes,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Hewitt changed the course of broadcast news by creating the TV magazine show.

name: Hildegard Behrens
headline: Hildegard Behrens, Soprano Acclaimed for Wagner, Is Dead at 72
abstract: The German soprano was a mesmerizing interpreter of touchstone dramatic soprano roles during the 1980s and early ’90s.

name: Robert Hilferty
headline: Robert Hilferty, Writer and AIDS Activist, Is Dead at 49
abstract: Mr. Hilferty was a writer and activist who made a documentary film in 1989 that roiled the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of New York and the Public Broadcasting Service.

name: André Prokovsky
headline: André Prokovsky, Dancer and Ballet Choreographer, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Prokovsky performed and choreographed around the world and was a former principal dancer with the New York City Ballet.

name: Burl Toler
headline: Burl Toler, First Black N.F.L. Official, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Toler played football for what Sports Illustrated called “the best team you never heard of” and became the focus of racial discrimination.

name: Virginia Davis McGhee
headline: Virginia Davis McGhee, Early Disney Star, Dies at 90
abstract: Miss Davis was best known for being a curly-haired 4-year-old child star who easily beat Mickey Mouse to the punch to become Walt Disney’s first cinematic star.

name: Karla Kuskin
headline: Karla Kuskin, Creator of Witty Children’s Books, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Kuskin was a noted children’s author and illustrator whose work combined sly wit with deep thoughtfulness about the essential natures of people, animals and things.

name: James Marsters
headline: James Marsters, Deaf Inventor, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Marsters helped convert Teletype machines to make communication by telephone possible for thousands with hearing problems.

name: A. Stone Freedberg
headline: A. Stone Freedberg, Pioneer in Study of Ulcers, Dies at 101
abstract: Dr. Freedberg developed an early treatment for angina and undertook pioneering work in identifying the bacteria that causes stomach ulcers.

name: Sammy Petrillo
headline: Sammy Petrillo, an Actor and Nightclub Comedian, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Petrillo built his career mostly on his striking resemblance to Jerry Lewis and a spot-on impression of him — much to Mr. Lewis’s ire.

name: Stanley Kaplan
profession: Pioneer in Preparing Students for Exams
headline: Stanley Kaplan, Pioneer in Preparing Students for Exams, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Kaplan carved out a lucrative niche in the world of for-profit education and made test-preparation classes a rite of passage for students across America.

name: Ernest Brown
profession: Last Member of the Original Tapping Copasetics
headline: Ernest Brown, Last Member of the Original Tapping Copasetics, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Brown was part of an ensemble of tap-dancing stars formed in 1949 that helped to revive the art of tap.

name: John E. Carter
headline: John E. Carter, Doo-Wop Falsetto, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Carter’s soaring falsetto was an instantly recognizable signature on hit records by the seminal doo-wop groups the Flamingos and the Dells.

name: Toni Sailer
headline: Toni Sailer, Record-Setting Gold Medal Skier, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Sailer was a charismatic and celebrated Austrian skier who became the first to win three gold medals in Alpine skiing in the same Olympic Games, in 1956.

name: Edward M. Kennedy
headline: Edward M. Kennedy, Senate Stalwart, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Senator Kennedy, a man who knew acclaim and tragedy in near-equal measure, will be remembered as one of the most effective lawmakers in the history of the Senate.

name: William A. Emerson Jr.
profession: Editor in Chief of Saturday Evening Post
headline: William A. Emerson Jr., Editor in Chief of Saturday Evening Post, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Emerson was an important chronicler of the tumultuous civil rights era in the South. He was known as a nimble, competitive and voluble editor and reporter.

name: Khalid bin Mahfouz
headline: Khalid bin Mahfouz, Saudi Banker, Dies at 60
abstract: Sheik Mahfouz paid $225 million to settle charges of bank fraud in 1993 and later won a string of lawsuits in Britain against writers who had accused him of supporting terrorism.

name: Ellie Greenwich
headline: Ellie Greenwich, Pop Songwriter, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. Greenwich was a pop music professional who collaborated with Phil Spector and others to create some of the greatest hits of the early 1960s.

name: Dominick Dunne
headline: Dominick Dunne, Chronicler of Crime, Dies at 83
abstract: After giving up producing movies in midlife and reinventing himself as a best-selling author, television personality and reporter, Mr. Dunne’s celebrity often outshone that of his subjects.

name: Sergei V. Mikhalkov
profession: Lyricist of Soviet and Russian Anthems
headline: Sergei V. Mikhalkov, Lyricist of Soviet and Russian Anthems, Dies at 96
abstract: A writer from a young age, Mr. Mikhalkov rose to fame quickly in the Soviet Union’s early days, winning the prestigious Order of Lenin, among many awards.

name: James Lord
headline: James Lord, Biographer and Memoirist, Dies at 86
abstract: An intimate of Picasso and Giacometti, Mr. Lord wrote biographies and memoirs that provided a vivid picture of the artistic milieu of Montparnasse after World War II.

name: Alex Grass
headline: Alex Grass, Who Helped to Start Rite Aid, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Grass helped transform a discount store in Scranton, Pa., into Rite Aid, one of the nation’s largest drugstore chains.

name: Doris Walker
headline: Doris Walker, Leader of Angela Davis’s Defense, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Ms. Walker was a radical lawyer who helped to defend Angela Davis against murder and kidnapping charges in the 1970s.

name: Michael Mazur
headline: Michael Mazur, Artist of Realism and Abstraction, Dies at 73
abstract: The work of Mr. Mazur, a relentlessly inventive printmaker, painter and sculptor, encompassed social documentation, narrative and landscape while moving between figuration and abstraction.

name: Edward Rondthaler
headline: Edward Rondthaler, Foenetic Speler, Dies at 104
abstract: In addition to trying to reform the spelling of English words, Mr. Rondthaler was a printer who helped invent phototypesetting.

name: Sheila Lukins
headline: Sheila Lukins, 66, Dies; Awakened Taste Buds
abstract: With her writing and in her West Side food store, Ms. Lukins helped working women cook in more adventurous ways.

name: Hyman Bloom
headline: Hyman Bloom, a Painter of the Mystical, Is Dead at 96
abstract: Mr. Bloom was a reclusive painter who for a brief time was regarded as a precursor to the Abstract Expressionists and one of the most significant American artists of the post-World War II era.

name: Joe Maneri
headline: Joe Maneri, Experimental Musician and Composer, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Maneri was a composer, saxophonist and clarinetist recognized later in life as an original force in experimental, improvisational music.

name: Alan F. Kiepper
headline: Alan F. Kiepper, Who Oversaw Transit in Atlanta, Houston and New York, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Kiepper took over the New York City transit system at a time when many people were afraid to ride the subway.

name: Richard Egan
headline: Richard Egan, a Founder of EMC Storage, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Mr. Egan was an entrepreneur who helped create an industry leader by changing data storage into specialized hardware.

name: Chris Connor
headline: Chris Connor, Jazz Singer Whose Voice Embodied a Wistful Cool, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Connor was the great jazz singer whose lush, foggy voice and compressed emotional intensity distilled a 1950s jazz reverie of faraway longing in a sad cafe.

name: Elmer Kelton
headline: Elmer Kelton, Prolific Western Novelist, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Kelton brought the sensibility of the old-style western to bear on a modern Texas landscape of oil fields and financially troubled ranches.

name: Beryl Sprinkel
headline: Beryl Sprinkel, Reagan Economic Adviser, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Sprinkel was an economist with a reputation for outspokenness, even toward supply-siders who thought tax cuts were the answer to every question.

name: Erich Kunzel
headline: Erich Kunzel, Maestro With an Irreverent Baton, Dies at 74
abstract: The conductor of the Cincinnati Pops Orchestra for more than three decades, Mr.Kunzel was known for undermining the pretensions of symphonic music.

name: Marie Knight
headline: Marie Knight, Rich-Voiced Gospel Singer, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Knight’s room-filling contralto voice was featured on some of the most popular gospel records of the 1940s.

name: Nancy Talbot
headline: Nancy Talbot, Who Helped Build a Retail Empire, Dies at 89
abstract: Mrs. Talbot helped her husband build his small clothing store into a giant retail and mail-order company catering to women looking for classic styles at affordable prices.

name: William Korey
headline: William Korey, B’nai B’rith Lobbyist, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Korey fought for the interests of Jews in the Soviet Union and pressed the United States to ratify the international genocide convention.

name: Kathryn Kennedy
headline: Kathryn Kennedy, a California Winemaker, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Kennedy took up winemaking in her 40s and produced highly rated cabernet sauvignon at her tiny estate winery in Saratoga, Calif.

name: F. M. Rogallo
headline: F. M. Rogallo, Father of Hang Gliding, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Rogallo, an aeronautical engineer who worked for NASA and its predecessor, developed a flexible wing that found many uses.

name: Edward Goldsmith
headline: Edward Goldsmith, Environmentalist, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Goldsmith was something of a utopian, something of a polemicist and, not surprisingly, something of a polarizing figure as well.

name: Keith Waterhouse
headline: Keith Waterhouse, Writer, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Waterhouse was a British novelist and playwright, known for his 1959 novel, “Billy Liar,” and play “Jeffrey Bernard Is Unwell.”

name: Louis Rosen
headline: Louis Rosen, 91, Dies; Worked on First Nuclear Bombs
abstract: Dr. Rosen was one of two young physicists at Los Alamos, N.M., who devised a way to confirm that thermonuclear fusion had occurred in a hydrogen bomb test.

name: Wycliffe Johnson
headline: Wycliffe Johnson, Boisterous Reggae Producer and Musician, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. Johnson, an innovative composer and producer known as Steely, held sway over two decades of reggae music.

name: Robert Spinrad
headline: Robert Spinrad, a Pioneer in Computing, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Spinrad’s work led to the commercial success of the modern personal computer, the ethernet local area network and the laser printer.

name: Charles Hughes
headline: Charles Hughes, 68, Dies; Led Union Until Disgrace
abstract: Mr. Hughes led a municipal labor union for 30 years, becoming a political power broker, but his career ended ignominiously with a corruption conviction.

name: Sylvia Schur
profession: Food Editor and Developer of Cran-Apple
headline: Sylvia Schur, Food Editor and Developer of Cran-Apple, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Schur, a consultant to food companies and restaurants, and a writer of recipes for Betty Crocker, became a creator of products like Clamato.

name: Dick Berg
headline: Dick Berg, TV Producer and Screenwriter, Dies at 87
abstract: In a career spanning more than 50 years, Mr. Berg produced or wrote scripts for nearly 100 television shows, starting with hourlong original dramas and detective shows in the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Finn Caspersen
headline: Finn Caspersen, Supporter of Many Causes, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Caspersen, a former chairman and chief executive of the Beneficial Corporation, was a major philanthropist and political donor in New Jersey politics.

name: Army Archerd
headline: Army Archerd, Columnist for Variety, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Archerd’s mannerly reporting on Hollywood executives and movie stars was a fixture in Variety, the entertainment trade newspaper, for more than 50 years.

name: Norman Crider
headline: Norman Crider, 70, Merchant of Ballet Memorabilia, Dies
abstract: The Ballet Shop of Mr. Crider, a former baton-twirling champion, became a mecca for both superstars and dance fans seeking out rare ballet books, prints, videotapes and posters.

name: Barry Flanagan
headline: Barry Flanagan, British Sculptor of Sly Works, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Flanagan was a British sculptor who abandoned the idiosyncratic arrangements of Postminimal sculpture to make sly bronzes of exuberant, loose-limbed hares.

name: Frank Batten Sr.
profession: Media Executive and Founder of Weather Channel
headline: Frank Batten Sr., Media Executive and Founder of Weather Channel, Dies at 82
abstract: From 1967 until 1998, Mr. Batten was chairman of Landmark Communications (now Landmark Media Enterprises), a company that owns newspapers, television stations and classified advertising publications.

name: Carl F. Hovde
headline: Carl F. Hovde, Former Columbia Dean, Dies at 82
abstract: A professor of comparative English literature, Mr. Hovde played a key role in restoring calm to the campus after student protests in the spring of 1968.

name: Aage Bohr
headline: Aage Bohr, Physicist’s Son Who Won Nobel, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Bohr, a son of the Nobel Prize-winning physicist Niels Bohr, did research that proved important in the development of human-made nuclear fusion.

name: Larry Gelbart
headline: Larry Gelbart, Writer of Comedy, Dies at 81
abstract: The writer’s caustic wit was a creative force behind the enduring success of the television series “M*A*S*H” and film comedies like “Tootsie.”

name: Gerhart Friedlander
headline: Gerhart Friedlander, Nuclear Chemist, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Friedlander’s work at Brookhaven National Laboratory led to calculations of nuclear reaction mechanisms.

name: Lou Bender
headline: Lou Bender, Columbia Star Who Helped Popularize Basketball in New York, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Bender was an all-American player at Columbia whose play during the Depression helped popularize the game and make Madison Square Garden a magnet for college basketball.

name: Richard Merkin
headline: Richard Merkin, Painter, Illustrator and Fashion Plate, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Merkin was a painter and illustrator whose fascination with the 1920s and 1930s defined his art and shaped his identity as a professional dandy.

name: Pierre Cossette
headline: Pierre Cossette, Who Brought Grammys to TV, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Cossette was a talent agent and producer who in 1971 convinced reluctant television executives to broadcast the Grammy Awards as a glittery live event.

name: Norman Seaman
profession: Filler of Concert Halls Odd Hours
headline: Norman Seaman, Filler of Concert Halls’ Odd Hours, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Seaman, a niche impresario who created series to fill empty weeks in the musical year, introduced curious audiences to hundreds of new performers aspiring to great careers.

name: Norman Borlaug
headline: Norman Borlaug, Plant Scientist Who Fought Famine, Dies at 95
abstract: A Nobel Peace Prize winner, Dr. Borlaug developed high-yielding crop varieties that helped to avert famines worldwide.

name: Jack Kramer
profession: Champion, Promoter and Powerful Force in Tennis
headline: Jack Kramer, 88, Champion, Promoter and Powerful Force in Tennis, Is Dead
abstract: A Wimbledon and United States singles titlist, Kramer led the way toward the open era and was a founder of the ATP, the men’s players union.

name: Francis Betters
headline: Francis Betters, Noted Fly Fisherman, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Betters was the owner of a well-known fishing shop and a man called “the ambassador for the Adirondack waters.”

name: Jim Carroll
headline: Jim Carroll, Poet and Punk Rocker Who Wrote ‘The Basketball Diaries’, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Carroll, the poet and punk rocker in the outlaw tradition of Rimbaud and Burroughs, chronicled his wild youth in “The Basketball Diaries.”

name: Patrick Swayze
headline: Patrick Swayze, Star of ‘Dirty Dancing,’ Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Swayze was a balletically athletic actor who rose to stardom in the films “Dirty Dancing” and “Ghost.”

name: Crystal Lee Sutton
headline: Crystal Lee Sutton, the Real-Life ‘Norma Rae,’ Is Dead at 68
abstract: Ms. Sutton’s battle to unionize workers at a North Carolina textile factory in 1973 inspired the Academy Award-winning film starring Sally Field.

name: Jody Powell
headline: Jody Powell, Trusted Aide to Jimmy Carter, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Powell was the closest adviser to Jimmy Carter from Mr. Carter’s days as governor to those as president.

name: Alfred Gottschalk
headline: Alfred Gottschalk, 79, Scholar of Reform Judaism, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Gottschalk led Hebrew Union College-Jewish Institute of Religion for three decades.

name: Zakes Mokae
headline: Zakes Mokae, Tony-Winning Actor, Is Dead at 75
