abstract: Mr. Mokae was a Tony-winning South African actor who brought the insidious psychological brutality of apartheid to the attention of a world audience.

name: James S. McDonald
headline: James S. McDonald, C.E.O. of Rockefeller & Co., Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. McDonald was also a member of the board of NYSE-Euronext and a former member of the board of the CIT Group.

name: Paul Burke
headline: Paul Burke, ‘Naked City’ Star, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Burke played the upright, soul-searching detective Adam Flint on the television drama “Naked City.” His career stalled after being acquitted of federal racketeering charges.

name: Myles Brand
headline: Myles Brand, N.C.A.A. President, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Brand was a former college president who pushed for academic reforms as president of the N.C.A.A.

name: Henry Gibson
headline: Henry Gibson, ‘Laugh-In’ Star, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Gibson recited inane poems in a Southern drawl on the 1960s television series “Laugh-In” but stood out in Robert Altman’s 1975 film “Nashville.”

name: Mary Travers
headline: Mary Travers of Peter, Paul and Mary Dies at 72
abstract: Ms. Travers’s ringing vocals helped make the folk trio’s songs enduring anthems of the 1960s protest movement.

name: Keith Floyd
headline: Keith Floyd, Jaunty British TV Chef, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Floyd revivified the television cooking-show format in the 1980s by injecting his own brand of wit, flamboyance and spontaneity.

name: Willy Ronis
headline: Willy Ronis, Photographer of Paris’s Warmer Side, Is Dead at 99
abstract: Mr. Ronis’ lyric black-and-white photographs of courting couples, busy street scenes and children at play lent a gentle but enduring mystique to postwar, working-class Paris.

name: Leon Kirchner
headline: Leon Kirchner, Composer and Teacher, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Kirchner was the eminent American composer who was also a pianist, a conductor and an influential teacher.

name: John T. Elson
headline: John T. Elson, Editor Who Asked ‘Is God Dead?’ at Time, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Elson’s 1966 cover article about new approaches to thinking about God caused an uproar, but it was an example of his serious coverage of ideas.

name: Melvin Simon
headline: Melvin Simon, Pioneer of the Suburban Mall, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Simon, who grew up in the Bronx, started his real estate empire by building small strip malls in Indianapolis.

name: Irving Kristol
headline: Irving Kristol, Godfather of Modern Conservatism, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Kristol was a political commentator who helped define modern conservatism and revitalize the Republican Party in the late 1960s and early ’70s.

name: Malcolm Wilkey
headline: Malcolm Wilkey, Noted Judge, Dies at 90
abstract: Judge Wilkey was not a household name, but he wrote influential opinions.

name: James Krenov
headline: James Krenov, Wood and Word Worker, Is Dead at 88
abstract: A renowned cabinetmaker, Mr. Krenov also inspired a generation of furniture makers through his writing.

name: W. Horace Carter
headline: W. Horace Carter, 88, a Publisher Whose Paper Challenged the Klan, Dies
abstract: Mr. Carter’s weekly paper’s four-year campaign against the Ku Klux Klan in North Carolina and South Carolina won it a Pulitzer Prize in 1953.

name: Lester Glassner
headline: Lester Glassner, Pop Culture Collector, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Mr. Glassner, whose collection had at its center five-and-dime treasures from the 1940s, wrote “Dime-Store Days,” a documentation of his eclectic holdings.

name: Trevor Rhone
profession: Writer of The Harder They Come
headline: Trevor Rhone, a Writer of ‘The Harder They Come,’ Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Rhone was an award-winning Jamaican playwright, director and actor who brought his island’s culture to the world as a writer of the film “The Harder They Come.”

name: Bernie Fuchs
headline: Bernie Fuchs, Illustrator for Magazines and Advertisements, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Fuchs was an artist of magazine illustrations, presidential portraits and postage stamps, whose vibrant paintings captured of middle-class life in pre-Vietnam America.

name: Lawrence B. Slobodkin
headline: Lawrence B. Slobodkin, Pioneering Ecologist, Dies at 81
abstract: Dr. Slobodkin, a co-author of a seminal paper informally known as “The World Is Green,” is credited with helping to transform ecology by using quantitative data to test models of nature.

name: Art Ferrante
headline: Art Ferrante, Pop Pianist in Famed Duo, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Ferrante entranced millions of listeners in the 1950s and 1960s with florid, arpeggio-packed versions of movie themes and popular songs as half of the piano duo Ferrante & Teicher.

name: Don Yarborough
headline: Don Yarborough Dies at 83; Stirred Texas Politics
abstract: Mr. Yarborough, a liberal Texas Democrat, challenged John B. Connally Jr. in a primary in 1962, exposing political tensions that John F. Kennedy hoped to smooth when he visited the next November.

name: Leon Eisenberg
headline: Dr. Leon Eisenberg, Pioneer in Autism Studies, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Eisenberg conducted some of the first rigorous studies of autism, attention deficit disorder and learning delays.

name: Eloise R. Giblett
headline: Eloise R. Giblett, Blood Research Leader, Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Giblett’s work helped make transfusions safer and bone marrow transplants more successful and led to her discovery of the first recognized immunodeficiency disease.

name: Freddy Bienstock
headline: Freddy Bienstock, Who Published Elvis Presley Hits, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Bienstock was a prominent music publishing executive who had a long association with Elvis Presley as his designated song screener.

name: Ertugrul Osman
headline: Ertugrul Osman, Link to Ottoman Dynasty, Dies at 97
abstract: Instead of inheriting a 285-room palace in Istanbul, Mr. Osman lived in a rent-controlled Manhattan walk-up for 64 years.

name: Milton Meltzer
headline: Milton Meltzer, Prolific Author, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Meltzer was a historian and prolific author of nonfiction books for young people who helped start a movement away from the arid textbook style of the past.

name: Wilma Cozart Fine
headline: Wilma Cozart Fine, Classical Music Record Producer, Dies at 82
abstract: Mrs. Fine ran the classical division of Mercury Records in the 1950s and early ’60s, and produced hundreds of recordings that are still prized by collectors for the depth and realism of their sound.

name: Susan Atkins
headline: Susan Atkins, Manson Follower, Dies at 61
abstract: Ms. Atkins, 61, spent four decades in prison for her role of the killings of Sharon Tate and seven others in 1969.

name: Alicia de Larrocha
headline: Alicia de Larrocha, Pianist, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. de Larrocha was esteemed for her elegant Mozart performances and for her interpretations of Albéniz, Granados, Mompou and other Spanish composers.

name: Kevork S. Hovnanian
headline: Kevork S. Hovnanian, Construction Company Founder, Dies at 86
abstract: An immigrant from Iraq, Mr. Hovnanian helped start a family company that operates in 18 states and is among the largest builders of residences in the country.

name: Forrest Church
headline: Rev. Forrest Church, Who Embraced a Gospel of Service, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Church, the longtime pastor of a Unitarian church on the Upper East Side, spent the last years of his life articulating a complete expression of his liberal theology in two books.

name: Joseph Gurwin
headline: Joseph Gurwin, Textile Manufacturer and Philanthropist, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Gurwin gave to a wide variety of causes and institutions, even after two family foundations were gutted by the swindler Bernard L. Madoff.

name: Francis Mason
headline: Francis Mason, Voice for Dance Over 5 Decades, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Mason was a writer and a critic who furthered the careers of George Balanchine and Martha Graham.

name: William Safire
profession: Political Columnist and Oracle of Language
headline: William Safire, Political Columnist and Oracle of Language, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Safire was a speechwriter for President Richard M. Nixon and a Pulitzer Prize-winning political columnist for The Times.

name: Edward Gelsthorpe
headline: Edward Gelsthorpe, Master Marketer, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Gelsthorpe helped put products like Ban roll-on deodorant and Cran-Apple on shelves and was chief executive at Ocean Spray Cranberries and Hunt-Wesson Foods.

name: Don Fisher
headline: Don Fisher, the Gap’s Founder, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Fisher started the Gap in 1969 to capitalize on the growing popularity of denim. Now the chain has more than 3,000 stores worldwide.

name: Paul B. Fay Jr.
headline: Paul B. Fay Jr., Confidant of President Kennedy, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Fay became friends with John F. Kennedy during World War II and went on to be under secretary of the Navy in his administration.

name: Guillermo Endara
profession: Helped Lead Panama From Noriega to Democracy
headline: Guillermo Endara, Who Helped Lead Panama From Noriega to Democracy, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Endara, who suffered electoral fraud, a cracked skull and hunger on his path to succeed the strongman Gen. Manuel Antonio Noriega, helped steer the country to democracy.

name: Henry Bellmon
headline: Henry Bellmon, Governor and Senator, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Bellmon was a former Oklahoma governor and U.S. senator and a leading figure in Richard M. Nixon’s 1968 presidential campaign.

name: Ben Feder
headline: Ben Feder, Hudson Valley Winemaker, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Feder was a New York real estate developer who in the 1970s began cultivating a French-American hybrid later credited with bringing “pride back to the local grape.”

name: Charles S. Houston
headline: Charles S. Houston, Who Led a Failed Himalayan Climb, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Houston was a mountain climber and an expert on high-altitude medicine whose effort to reach the summit of K-2 ended in the death of one of his team.

name: Mahlon Hoagland
headline: Mahlon Hoagland, RNA Expert, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Hoagland helped discover transfer RNA, which aided in unlocking the mystery of how DNA is translated into the proteins that carry out its genetic instructions.

name: Douglas Watt
headline: Douglas Watt, New York Theater Critic, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Watt’s career passed through and outlasted the era when plays and musicals were still the leading forms of entertainment and the theater writers were powerful tastemakers.

name: Donal McLaughlin
headline: Donal McLaughlin, Designer of United Nations Emblem, Dies at 102
abstract: Mr. McLaughlin’s hastily concocted design for a lapel pin that showed the continents embraced by olive branches became one of the world’s most recognizable symbols.

name: Merrill D. Peterson
headline: Merrill D. Peterson, Jefferson Scholar, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Peterson, a historian, enlarged the scope of Jeffersonian scholarship with a pair of books.

name: Magic
headline: Mr. Magic, Disc Jockey for Early Hip-Hop, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Magic’s panache and persistence in bringing once-reviled rap to mainstream radio in the 1980s helped pave the way for the breakout of hip-hop culture.

name: Sarah E. Wright
profession: Novelist of Black Experience in the Depression
headline: Sarah E. Wright, Novelist of Black Experience in the Depression, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Wright’s first and only published novel, “This Child’s Gonna Live,” was among the first to explore the black experience from a woman’s perspective.

name: Marek Edelman
headline: Marek Edelman, Commander in Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Edelman, a cardiologist, was the last surviving commander of the 1943 Warsaw ghetto uprising against the Germans. At the end, he found a way out, leading 50 others with him.

name: Frank Coghlan Jr.
headline: Frank Coghlan Jr., Child Actor of Silent Era, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Coghlan was a child actor of silent movies. In the sound era, he thrilled Saturday matinee audiences by shouting “Shazam!” before mutating into the superhero Captain Marvel.

name: Shoichi Nakagawa
headline: Shoichi Nakagawa, Former Japanese Finance Minister, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Nakagawa, who resigned in February after his erratic behavior at an international meeting, was an outspoken conservative and heavyweight in the recently ousted Liberal Democratic Party.

name: Reinhard Mohn
headline: Reinhard Mohn, 88, Dies; Built Bertelsmann Into a Giant
abstract: Mr. Mohn transformed Bertelsmann from a provincial, war-shattered German publisher into a global media giant.

name: Mercedes Sosa
headline: Mercedes Sosa, Who Sang of Argentina’s Turmoil, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Sosa was an Argentine folk singer whose politically charged repertory led her to be known throughout Latin America as “the voice of the voiceless.”

name: Kate Duffy
headline: Kate Duffy, Book Editor, Is Dead at 56
abstract: Ms. Duffy was one of the foremost editors of romance novels in the United States, and helped usher into print a new kind of romance novel featuring strong, capable women.

name: Mimi Weddell
headline: Mimi Weddell, Actress and Hat Devotee, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Ms. Weddell became a model, actress and style setter in her mid-60s and her flamboyant headwear figured prominently in “Hats Off,” a 2008 documentary about her life.

name: Peg Mullen
profession: Fanned Her Anger Over Sons Death Into Antiwar Drive
headline: Peg Mullen, 92, Who Fanned Her Anger Over Son’s Death Into Antiwar Drive, Dies
abstract: Mrs. Mullen, an Iowa farm wife who questioned the explanations given to her by the military, spurned her son’s medals and wrote a book on her torment.

name: John Wild
profession: Developer of Ultrasound in Cancer Diagnoses
headline: John Wild, 95, a Developer of Ultrasound in Cancer Diagnoses, Dies
abstract: Dr. Wild collaborated on some of the first equipment to use high-frequency sound waves to obtain images of human tissue, especially for cancer diagnosis.

name: Josef Burg
headline: Josef Burg, Who Wrote About Jewish Life, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Burg, one of the last Yiddish authors in Eastern Europe, preserved vestiges of a once-vibrant culture in fictional reflections on Jewish life.

name: Israel Gelfand
headline: Israel Gelfand, Math Giant, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Gelfand’s pioneering work in many areas has proved crucial in quantum mechanics, M.R.I. imaging and CAT scans.

name: Gilberto Zaldívar
headline: Gilberto Zaldívar, a Theater Founder, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Zaldívar was a co-founder of the Repertorio Español, New York City’s premiere Spanish-language theater company.

name: Suzanne Fiol
headline: Suzanne Fiol, Avant-Garde Impresario, Dies at 49
abstract: Ms. Fiol founded the performance space Issue Project Room and served as its artistic rudder.

name: Irving Penn
headline: Irving Penn, Fashion Photographer, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Penn’s blend of elegance and minimalism made him one of the most influential photographers of the century.

name: Charlotte S. Turgeon
headline: Charlotte S. Turgeon, Who Popularized French Cuisine, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Ms. Turgeon wrote cookbooks that helped popularize French cuisine in the United States, and she did it before her friend Julia Child.

name: Charles Seliger
headline: Charles Seliger, Abstract Expressionist, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Seliger’s small-scale, jewel-like paintings of imaginary natural forms made him the most idiosyncratic of the first-generation Abstract Expressionists.

name: John D. Loori
headline: John D. Loori, 78, Zen Abbot and Photographer, Dies
abstract: Abbot Loori founded a worldwide Zen order, was a respected photographer and teacher and wrote 20 books on Buddhism and art.

name: Shelby Singleton
headline: Shelby Singleton, Nashville Producer, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Singleton was a colorful Nashville record producer and entrepreneur who resurrected the historic Sun Records catalog.

name: Marty Forscher
headline: Marty Forscher, Who Tended Cameras and Owners, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Forscher’s intimate knowledge of the anatomy and physiology of the camera made him for decades the most sought-after camera repairman in the country.

name: Lionel Pincus
profession: Helped Bring Investors to Private Equity
headline: Lionel Pincus, Who Helped Bring Investors to Private Equity, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Pincus, an investor in companies including Mattel and Mellon Bank, led a mostly private life until he met Princess Firyal of Jordan.

name: Raymond A. Brown
headline: Raymond A. Brown, Civil Rights Lawyer, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Brown, who had a talent for courtroom bravado, represented controversial clients including the Black Panthers and the boxer Rubin “Hurricane” Carter.

name: Robert M. Murdock
headline: Robert M. Murdock, Curator and Scholar, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Murdock was an art historian and curator of 20th-century and contemporary art who organized some notable exhibitions.

name: Raymond Federman
headline: Raymond Federman, Novelist and Beckett Scholar, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Federman was a French-born writer who took an unorthodox approach to his art, creating books that aimed for the eye and the ear.

name: Paul L. Bloom
headline: Paul L. Bloom, Who Tackled Overcharging by Oil Companies, Dies at 70
abstract: As a lawyer in the Carter administration, Mr. Bloom pursued oil companies for overcharging and won billions of dollars in refunds for customers, the government and others.

name: Paul Bloom
headline: Paul Bloom, 70, Is Dead; Won Billions From Big Oil
abstract: Mr. Bloom was a lawyer in the Carter Energy Department who sued oil companies for overcharging and won billions of dollars in refunds for customers, the government and others.

name: Richard W. Sonnenfeldt
headline: Richard W. Sonnenfeldt, Nuremberg Interrogator, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Sonnenfeldt fled Germany as a teenager then later read indictments to, and helped question, Nazi leaders like Hermann Goering.

name: Stephen Gately
headline: Stephen Gately, Irish Pop Singer, Is Dead at 33
abstract: Mr. Gately made headlines when he came out as gay a decade ago and had, with Boyzone, announced a comeback tour at the end of last year.

name: Nat Finkelstein
profession: Court Photographer of Andy Warhols Factory
headline: Nat Finkelstein, ‘Court Photographer’ of Andy Warhol’s Factory, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Finkelstein’s photographs of Andy Warhol, Edie Sedgwick and the Velvet Underground are among the most famous images of Warhol’s Factory and its revolving cast of characters

name: Ben Williams
headline: Ben Williams, Circus Performer Whose Co-Star Was an Elephant, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Williams seized the attention of Big Top crowds by fearlessly and flamboyantly cavorting under, above and around elephants.

name: Larry Jansen
headline: Larry Jansen, Giants Pitcher, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Jansen won 23 games in 1951 and was the winning pitcher when Bobby Thomson’s home run defeated the Dodgers for the N.L. pennant.

name: Dickie Peterson
profession: Singer for Rock Band Blue Cheer
headline: Dickie Peterson, Singer for Rock Band Blue Cheer, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Peterson’s screaming vocals and pounding bass lines helped push the psychedelic blues-rock trio Blue Cheer into the musical territory that would later be called heavy metal.

name: Brendan Mullen
profession: Pillar of Los Angeles Punk Scene
headline: Brendan Mullen, Pillar of Los Angeles Punk Scene, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Mullen nurtured the early Los Angeles punk-rock scene in the 1970s with his club the Masque and later chronicled it in articles and books.

name: Stuart M. Kaminsky
headline: Stuart M. Kaminsky, Mystery Writer, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Kaminsky was a novelist who was widely known for his prodigious output, complex characters and rich evocations of time and place, including Hollywood in its Golden Age.

name: Al Martino
headline: Al Martino, Singer of Pop Ballads, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Martino was renowned for a string of hits, including “Spanish Eyes” and “Volare,” and for his role as the wedding singer in “The Godfather.”

name: Nan Robertson
profession: Chronicled Discrimination Suit at The Times
headline: Nan Robertson, Who Chronicled Discrimination Suit at The Times, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Ms. Robertson, a Pulitzer Prize-winning reporter for The New York Times, was widely known for her book “The Girls in the Balcony.”

name: Bruce Wasserstein
headline: Bruce Wasserstein, Lazard Banker, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Wasserstein was a Wall Street investment banker who helped pioneer the hostile takeover and reshaped the mergers and acquisitions business into a high art.

name: Lou Albano
headline: Captain Lou Albano, Wrestler and Showman, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Albano was a pro wrestling villain who reinvented himself as a pop culture celebrity in a Cyndi Lauper music video and in movies and television.

name: William Wayne Justice
headline: William Wayne Justice, Noted Judge, Dies at 89
abstract: Judge Justice of Federal District Court ruled on ground-breaking class-action suits that compelled Texas to integrate schools, reform prisons, and educate illegal immigrants.

name: Dietrich von Bothmer
headline: Dietrich von Bothmer, Curator and Art Historian, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. von Bothmer was regarded as the world’s leading expert on ancient Greek vases and was a curator at the Metropolitan Museum of Art for more than 60 years.

name: Jules Power
headline: Jules Power, a Producer of ‘Mr. Wizard,’ Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Power helped break the mold of cartoonish children’s shows in the early days of television by producing programs that entranced youngsters with basic science.

name: Douglas Campbell
headline: Douglas Campbell, Canadian Actor, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Campbell, drew wide acclaim in Canada and beyond, particularly for his many roles at the Stratford Shakespeare Festival in Ontario.

name: David Lake
headline: David Lake, Washington Wine Innovator, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Lake elevated the status of syrah, cabernet franc and pinot gris grapes in the world of winemaking in Washington State.

name: Daniel Melnick
headline: Daniel Melnick, Hollywood Producer, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Melnick, producer and studio executive, brought an innovative and often unconventional sensibility to films that included “Straw Dogs,” “All That Jazz” and “Altered States.”

name: Cullen Bryant
headline: Cullen Bryant, Ex-Ram Who Challenged Rozelle Rule, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Bryant, a powerful running back, played 13 seasons in the N.F.L., 11 of them for the Los Angeles Rams.

name: Elizabeth Prophet
headline: Elizabeth Prophet, 70, Church Founder, Is Dead
abstract: Mrs. Prophet was the leader of the Summit Lighthouse and the Church Universal and Triumphant, a New Age religion, who called on her followers in the late 1980s to prepare for nuclear Armageddon.

name: Donald Kaufman
headline: Donald Kaufman, Collector of Toy Cars, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Kaufman owned one of the largest and most valuable collections of antique toy cars and trucks in the world.

name: Steve Ferguson
profession: Rock Guitarist and a Founder of NRBQ
headline: Steve Ferguson, Rock Guitarist and a Founder of NRBQ, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Ferguson, a guitarist, singer and songwriter, formed the original version of NRBQ in Louisville, Ky., in 1967 with a high school friend, the keyboardist, singer and songwriter Terry Adams.

name: Rodger Doxsey
headline: Rodger Doxsey, Astronomer Who Worked on the Hubble, Dies at 62
abstract: Dr. Doxsey, the head of mission operations at the Space Telescope Science Institute in Baltimore, helped keep the space telescope working at peak performance.

name: Nancy Spero
headline: Nancy Spero, Artist of Feminism, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Ms. Spero was an American artist and feminist whose tough, exquisite figurative art addressed the realities of political violence.

name: Howard Unruh
profession: Killed 13 of His Neighbors in Camden in 1949
headline: Howard Unruh, 88, Dies; Killed 13 of His Neighbors in Camden in 1949
abstract: Mr. Unruh carried out one of America’s most infamous mass shootings during a morning stroll; he was found to have paranoid schizophrenia and never stood trial.

name: Joseph Wiseman
headline: Joseph Wiseman, James Bond’s Dr. No, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Wiseman, a longtime stage and screen actor, was most widely known for playing the villainous title character in “Dr. No,” the first feature film about James Bond.

name: Sheldon J. Segal
headline: Sheldon J. Segal, Who Developed Contraceptives, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Segal’s breakthroughs included Norplant, a surgically implanted long-lasting birth-control device that had a stormy history in the United States.

name: Vic Mizzy
headline: Vic Mizzy, Songwriter of ‘Addams Family’ Fame, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Mizzy wrote the infernally catchy themes for the 1960s television comedies “The Addams Family” and “Green Acres.”

name: Jack Nelson
headline: Jack Nelson, Journalist, Dies at 80
abstract: The former Pulitzer Prize-winning reporter and Washington bureau chief for The Los Angeles Times covered the civil rights movement and Watergate.

name: Jack Nelson
profession: Olympic Swimmer and Gold Medal Coach
headline: Jack Nelson, Olympic Swimmer and Gold Medal Coach, Dies at 82
abstract: A competitor in the 1956 Olympics, he coached the United States women’s team to gold in the 400-meter freestyle relay at the 1976 Games against powerhouse East Germany.

name: Stephen Barnett
headline: Stephen Barnett, a Leading Legal Scholar, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Barnett campaigned against federal law exempting news companies from antitrust legislation and was a fierce critic of the California Supreme Court.

name: Collin Wilcox
headline: Collin Wilcox, Actress in ‘Mockingbird’, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Wilcox worked actively in television and in theater, but she was best-known for her film role as Mayella Ewell in “To Kill a Mockingbird,” the 1962 adaptation of Harper Lee’s novel.

name: Theodore R. Sizer
headline: Theodore R. Sizer, Leading Education-Reform Advocate, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Sizer’s pluralistic vision of the American high school helped shape the national discourse on education and revise decades-old ideas of what a school should be.

name: Soupy Sales
profession: Flinger of Pies and Punch Lines
headline: Soupy Sales, Flinger of Pies and Punch Lines, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Sales’s zany television routines turned a pie in the face into a madcap art form.

name: Ignacio Ponseti
headline: Ignacio Ponseti, Hero to Many With Clubfoot, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Ponseti was an orthopedist whose gentle, nonsurgical method of correcting clubfoot has become the global standard for treatment.

name: Ruth Duckworth
headline: Ruth Duckworth, Sculptor and Muralist, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Duckworth was a sculptor whose work in clay and bronze included monumental sculptures and murals, as well as small-scale, intimate pieces.

name: Norma Fox Mazer
headline: Norma Fox Mazer, Novelist for Young Adults, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Mazer was an award-winning novelist for young people whose work helped illuminate many dark corners of adolescence.

name: Lou Jacobi
profession: Critically Acclaimed Actor of Film and Stage
headline: Lou Jacobi, Critically Acclaimed Actor of Film and Stage, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Jacobi’s career spanned five decades and included Broadway plays (“The Diary of Anne Frank”), television series (“That Girl”) and movies (“Avalon”).

name: Richard T. Whitcomb
profession: Revolutionized the Design of Jet Aircraft
headline: Richard T. Whitcomb Is Dead at 88; Revolutionized the Design of Jet Aircraft
abstract: Mr. Whitcomb’s understanding of the way air rips around an airplane as it approaches the sound barrier revolutionized the way jets are shaped, allowing them to fly faster on less fuel.

name: Bill Chadwick
headline: Bill Chadwick, Hockey Referee and Broadcaster, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Chadwick became a Hall of Fame referee in the National Hockey League despite losing his sight in one eye and was later a popular broadcaster for the Rangers.

name: Dee Anthony
headline: Dee Anthony, Manager to Rocker Peter Frampton, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Anthony managed the careers of Peter Frampton, Joe Cocker and others with a blunt, streetwise style that made him a rock power broker in the 1970s.

name: Ray Browne
headline: Ray Browne, 87, Founder of Pop-Culture Studies, Dies
abstract: Professor Browne presided over the somewhat unlikely, often uneasy and almost always stimulating marriage between the ivory tower and Mickey Mouse, Madonna and Michael Jackson.

name: Maryanne Amacher
headline: Maryanne Amacher, 71, Visceral Composer, Dies
abstract: Ms. Amacher was an influential composer whose experimental sound installations sometimes required full buildings to present their powerful melding of timbres and natural ambience.

name: Lawrence Halprin
headline: Lawrence Halprin, Landscape Architect, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Halprin melded modernism, nature and movement in his projects, including the memorial to President Franklin D. Roosevelt in Washington.

name: Roy DeCarava
headline: Roy DeCarava, Harlem Insider Who Photographed Ordinary Life, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. DeCarava turned Harlem into his canvas, becoming one of the most important photographers of his generation by chronicling the lives of its ordinary people and its jazz giants.

name: John Pemberton Jr.
headline: John Pemberton Jr., Civil Rights Crusader, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Pemberton, executive director of the American Civil Liberties Union during the turbulent 1960s, helped double its size and shift its focus to the criminal courts.

name: Amos Ferguson
headline: Amos Ferguson, 89, Bahamian Artist, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Ferguson was a folk artist known for his brilliantly colored Bible scenes and his depictions of the social rituals and the flora and fauna of the Bahamas.

name: Cordner Nelson
profession: Founding Editor of Track & Field News
headline: Cordner Nelson, Founding Editor of Track & Field News, Dies at 91
abstract: Covering the sport for more than a half-century, Mr. Nelson, a tall and dignified presence, attended 15 Olympics and wrote books and originated the magazine’s annual world rankings.

name: Elmer Winter
headline: Elmer Winter, 97, Co-Founder of Manpower Temp Agency, Dies
abstract: Mr. Winter’s very bad day at the office — he and his law partner scrambled to find emergency secretarial help — spurred them to start Manpower, the worldwide temp agency.

name: Michelle Triola Marvin
headline: Michelle Triola Marvin, of Landmark Palimony Suit, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Triola Marvin helped lead to the concept of “palimony” settlements for unmarried partners with her landmark lawsuit against the actor Lee Marvin.

name: John Kenley
profession: Took Big Stars to Small-Town Stages
headline: John Kenley, Who Took Big Stars to Small-Town Stages, Dies at 103
abstract: The Midwest theater impresario was renowned for taking large-scale productions to small towns and cities.

name: John O’Quinn
headline: John O’Quinn, 68, Star Personal-Injury Lawyer in Texas, Dies
abstract: Mr. O’Quinn was a plaintiff’s lawyer whose outsized personality matched the jury awards he won for his clients.

name: Albert York
headline: Albert York, Reclusive Landscape Painter, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. York was a painter of small, mysterious landscapes who shunned the art world yet had a fervent following within it.

name: Lionel Davidson
headline: Lionel Davidson, British Writer of Well-Traveled Thrillers, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Davidson was a noted British thriller writer whose novels brought to life far-flung settings like Prague, Tibet, Israel and Siberia.

name: Peter Shellem
headline: Peter Shellem, Investigative Reporter Who Wrote About Wrongful Convictions, Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. Shellem’s relentless digging during his 23 years as a reporter for The Patriot-News in Harrisburg, Pa., led to the release of five wrongly convicted prisoners.

name: Seymour Fromer
profession: Archivist of Jewish Contribution to West
headline: Seymour Fromer, Archivist of Jewish Contribution to West, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Fromer opened a museum in California that eventually came to hold one of the largest collections of Judaica in North America.

name: Don Ivan Punchatz
headline: Don Ivan Punchatz, Fantasy Illustrator, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Punchatz’s surreal art was splashed on popular horror and science-fiction paperbacks, magazines and the first “Star Wars” film poster.

name: Michael Goldsmith
headline: Michael Goldsmith, Who Raised Awareness of A.L.S., Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Goldsmith wrote a guest column in Newsweek calling on Major League Baseball to do more to fight Lou Gehrig’s disease.

name: Forest Evashevski
profession: Coached Iowa to Two Rose Bowl Titles
headline: Forest Evashevski, Who Coached Iowa to Two Rose Bowl Titles, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Evashevski, who was inducted into to the College Football Hall of Fame in 2000, was a skillful recruiter and outstanding motivator.

name: Troy Smith
headline: Troy Smith, Founder of Sonic, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Smith built a fast-food chain that benefited from America’s embrace of car culture and recreational eating.

name: Qian Xuesen
headline: Qian Xuesen, Father of China’s Space Program, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Qian was a rocket scientist who led China’s space and military rocketry efforts after he was drummed out of the U.S. during the redbaiting of the McCarthy era.

name: Esther Hautzig
headline: Esther Hautzig, Author of Wartime Survival Tale, Dies at 79
abstract: Mrs. Hautzig’s true-life tale of surviving World War II in the labor camps of Siberia, told in a guileless teenager’s voice, became a classic of young people’s literature.

name: Claude Lévi-Strauss
profession: Altered Western Views of the Primitive
headline: Claude Lévi-Strauss, 100, Dies; Altered Western Views of the ‘Primitive’
abstract: Mr. Lévi-Strauss, a towering intellectual, transformed the West’s understanding of what was once called “primitive man.”

name: Michael Ronis
headline: Michael Ronis, Manhattan Chef, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Ronis helped develop Carmine’s, one of New York City’s most popular restaurants.

name: William Belton
headline: William Belton, Self-Taught Ornithologist, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Belton was almost single-handedly responsible for the current body of knowledge of the bird life of Rio Grande do Sul, the southernmost Brazilian state.

name: George Na’ope
headline: George Na’ope, Master of Sacred Hula, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Na’ope’s mastery of the hula — the flowing, pantomimic dance of Hawaii — and its lilting chants made him a last link between an ancient ritual and modern entertainment.

name: Francisco Ayala
headline: Francisco Ayala, a Spanish Novelist and Literary Scholar, Dies at 103
abstract: Mr. Ayala was an eminent Spanish novelist whose work explored societies in which there is much despotism and little benevolence.

name: Francisco Ayala
headline: Francisco Ayala, Biologist and Defender of Evolution, Dies at 88
abstract: A leading evolutionary biologist who defended Darwin’s theory in books and in the courtroom, he was forced to retire amid charges of sexual harassment.

name: George Zoritch
headline: George Zoritch, Star in Ballet Russe Companies, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Zoritch was an international star in the rival Ballet Russe companies who stood out for his matinee-idol looks and bold stage presence and who later became one of American ballet’s respected teachers.

name: Art D’Lugoff
headline: Art D’Lugoff, Village Gate Impresario, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. D’Lugoff’s nightclub, the Village Gate, was home to performers as celebrated, and diverse, as Duke Ellington, Allen Ginsberg and John Belushi.

name: Nien Cheng
headline: Nien Cheng, Memoirist, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Ms. Cheng’s memoir, “Life and Death in Shanghai,” offered a harrowing account of the Cultural Revolution in China.

name: Stacy Rowles
headline: Stacy Rowles, Jazz Musician, Is Dead at 54
abstract: The jazz trumpeter, fluegelhorn player and singer had been active on the Los Angeles jazz scene since the 1980s.

name: Paul C. Zamecnik
headline: Paul C. Zamecnik, Biologist Who Helped Discover an RNA Molecule, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Zamecnik also revealed a method for blocking individual genes that pointed the way to a new class of drugs.

name: John Mashek
headline: John Mashek, Veteran Political Reporter, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Mr. Mashek was a reporter and columnist for nearly half a century for U.S. News & World Report, The Boston Globe and other publications.

name: Jeremy Morris
headline: Jeremy Morris, Who Proved Exercise Is Heart-Healthy, Dies at 99½
abstract: Mr. Morris was a British epidemiologist whose heart-attack research laid the scientific groundwork for the modern aerobics movement.

name: Robert Rines
headline: Robert Rines, Inventor and Monster Hunter, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Rines will be mainly remembered not for holding more than 800 patents, starting a law school or writing music for the stage, but for his pursuit of the Loch Ness monster.

name: Alice S. Rossi
headline: Alice S. Rossi, Sociologist and Feminist Scholar, Dies at 87
abstract: Professor Rossi was a noted sociologist and feminist scholar who was a founder of the National Organization for Women.

name: Samuel Heyman
headline: Samuel Heyman, a Corporate Raider, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Heyman stood out as a corporate raider who preferred to hold on to companies he bought and run them rather that sell them for a quick profit.

name: J. Nicholas Counter III
headline: J. Nicholas Counter III, Labor Lawyer, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Counter was a lawyer who changed the face of labor relations in Hollywood during his long tenure as chief negotiator for hundreds of film and television companies.

name: Vitaly Ginzburg
headline: Vitaly Ginzburg Dies at 93; Worked on Soviet H-Bomb
abstract: Mr. Ginzburg, a Russian physicist, helped develop the first Soviet hydrogen bomb and went on to win the Nobel Prize.

name: Charles P. Sifton
profession: Judge in City Case on Term Limits
headline: Charles P. Sifton, Judge in City Case on Term Limits, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Sifton was a federal judge in Brooklyn whose rulings paved the way for women to join the New York Fire Department and for Mayor Michael R. Bloomberg to run for a third term.

name: Antonio Luis Alves de Souza
headline: Antonio Luis Alves de Souza, Brazilian Drummer, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. de Souza led Olodum, a Brazilian percussion band notable for its social work as well as its music, and he lent his distinctive rhythms to a Paul Simon album and a Michael Jackson video.

name: Evelyn Hofer
profession: Subtle Photographer of People and Places
headline: Evelyn Hofer, Subtle Photographer of People and Places, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Hofer was a photographer whose portraits imparted a grave serenity to her subjects and who collaborated on a renowned series of travel books in the 1950s and 1960s.

name: Al Cervi
headline: Al Cervi, Hall of Fame N.B.A. Player-Coach, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Cervi, considered one of the strongest guards of the 1940s and ’50s, found even more success as an N.B.A. coach, leading Syracuse to a title in 1955.

name: Mildred Cohn
headline: Mildred Cohn, Biochemist, Is Dead at 96
abstract: Dr. Cohn was a leading researcher whose work contributed to the development of medical technologies like M.R.I.’s.

name: Carl Ballantine
headline: Carl Ballantine, Slapstick Magician, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Ballantine was an inveterate quipmeister whose stand-up comedy persona predated and influenced the antic characters of Steve Martin and others.

name: Gene D. Cohen
headline: Gene D. Cohen, Geriatric Psychiatrist, Dies at 65
abstract: Dr. Cohen was a pioneer in the field of geriatric psychiatry who helped shift the emphasis in gerontological research from the problems of people as they age to their potential.

name: Sheldon Dorf
headline: Sheldon Dorf, Founder of Comic-Con, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Dorf turned his passion for comic books and newspaper strips into a vocation by founding one of the world’s biggest annual comic-book conventions.

name: Donald Harington
headline: Donald Harington, Ozark Surrealist, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Harington created a surreal rural mini-world in more than a dozen novels set in the fictional Ozark hamlet of Stay More, Ark.

name: Thomas J. O’Malley
headline: Thomas J. O’Malley, Who Helped Launch Glenn Into Orbit, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. O’Malley was the aviation engineer who pushed the button that launched the rocket that carried John Glenn into orbit in 1962.

name: David Lloyd
headline: David Lloyd, 75, Dies; Wrote ‘Chuckles’ Episode
abstract: Mr. Lloyd wrote scores of scripts for some of the most popular television sitcoms of the 1970s, ’80s and ’90s.

name: David Lloyd
headline: David Lloyd, Tenor With City Opera, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Lloyd, an American lyric tenor with New York City Opera in the 1950s, was also known as a recitalist and oratorio soloist.

name: Dick Katz
profession: Jazzman of Many Gifts Over 6 Decades
headline: Dick Katz, 85, Jazzman of Many Gifts Over 6 Decades, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Katz was a pianist, record producer and writer whose knowledge of jazz made him a valuable presence on New York’s jazz scene for six decades.

name: William Ganz
headline: William Ganz, Catheter Inventor, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Ganz, a cardiologist and medical inventor, helped develop a revolutionary catheter to measure blood flow and heart functions.

name: Bruce King
headline: Bruce King, 3-Term Governor, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. King rose from a rough-hewn, rural upbringing on the family ranch to become the only three-term governor of New Mexico.

name: Earl Coleman
headline: Earl Coleman, Publisher and Poet, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Coleman started a custom translation service and built it into the Plenum Publishing Corporation, one of the world’s largest translators and publishers of scientific and technical material.

name: James R. Lilley
headline: James R. Lilley, 81, Envoy in Tiananmen Era, Dies
abstract: A native of China, Mr. Lilley worked there for the C.I.A. for years and served as the American ambassador from 1989 to 1991.

name: Amir Pnueli
headline: Amir Pnueli, Pioneer of Temporal Logic, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Pnueli turned a philosopher’s explorations of time, logic and free will, called temporal logic, into a critical technique for verifying the reliability of computers.

name: Earl Cooley
profession: Fought Fires as Original Smoke Jumper
headline: Earl Cooley Is Dead at 98; Fought Fires as Original Smoke Jumper
abstract: Mr. Cooley was one of the last links to the beginnings of a firefighting program famed for both efficiency and audacity.

name: Bobby Frankel
headline: Bobby Frankel, 68, Trainer of Champion Horses, Dies
abstract: Mr. Frankel was one of the most successful American thoroughbred trainers of the last 40 years, though he never won the Kentucky Derby.

name: Edward Woodward
headline: Edward Woodward, Star of Spy Series, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Woodward was a British actor with a long résumé in television and theater who was best known in the United States as the star of “The Equalizer.”

name: Ken Ober
profession: Host of Remote Control on TV
headline: Ken Ober, Host of ‘Remote Control’ on TV, Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. Ober was a brassy comedian best known as the host of the 1980s-era MTV game show “Remote Control.”

name: Pierre Harmel
headline: Pierre Harmel, Belgian Who Helped Reshape NATO, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Harmel was a former prime minister but had his greatest impact as the foreign minister when he was deeply involved in the future of the Atlantic alliance.

name: Sy Syms
headline: Sy Syms, Founder of Discount Chain, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Syms pioneered selling off-price clothing and built his retail chain, the Syms Corporation, into a national brand.

name: Allen Hughes
profession: Music and Dance Critic for The Times
headline: Allen Hughes, Music and Dance Critic for The Times, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Hughes was known for his encouragement of experimental dance companies and his love of the 20th-century French musical repertory.

name: Irving Kriesberg
headline: Irving Kriesberg, Artist of Dreamlike Landscapes, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Kriesberg was an American painter whose work combined the intense colors of Abstract Expressionism with haunting images of human and animal forms.

name: Wade F. B. Thompson
headline: Wade F. B. Thompson, Who Rebuilt Airstream Brand, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Thompson and his partner bought travel trailer businesses, including the popular Airstream brand, which they built up after a difficult period.

name: Glenn Remick
headline: Glenn Remick, Darts Promoter, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Remick became a professional darting promoter in 1977 when he opened a dart supply store in Holyoke, Mass., and founded the Western Massachusetts Darting Association.

name: Lewis Millett
headline: Col. Lewis Millett, Who Led ‘Bayonet Hill’ Charge, Dies at 88
abstract: Colonel Millett was an Army veteran of three wars who received the Medal of Honor for leading a rare bayonet charge up a hill in Korea.

name: Eugene Cotton
headline: Eugene Cotton, Labor Union Lawyer, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Cotton was a labor lawyer whose negotiating savvy helped improve the wages and conditions of tens of thousands of meatpacking workers.

name: Jeanne-Claude
headline: Jeanne-Claude, Christo’s Collaborator on Environmental Canvas, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Jeanne-Claude worked with her husband, Christo, on dozens of environmental arts projects, including “The Gates” in Central Park in 2005.

name: John Crofton
headline: Sir John Crofton, Pioneer in TB Cure, Dies at 97
abstract: The clinician showed that three antibiotics could be safely combined to provide a cure, providing the template for later combination therapies for cancer and AIDS.

name: Albert Crewe
headline: Albert Crewe, Physicist, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Dr. Crewe, a University of Chicago physicist, developed the high-resolution electron microscope that captured the first image of an individual atom.

name: Thomas J. Graff
profession: Expert on West Coast Water Use
headline: Thomas J. Graff, an Expert on West Coast Water Use, Is Dead at 65
abstract: Mr. Graff, a leading environmentalist, championed the idea of offering financial incentives for environmentally friendly behavior.

name: Herbert J. Miller Jr.
headline: Herbert J. Miller Jr., Justice Dept. Leader, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Miller was a Justice Department lawyer in the 1960s who relentlessly pursued James R. Hoffa. Later he helped negotiate the unconditional pardon of former President Richard M. Nixon for his role in the Watergate scandal.

name: Elisabeth Soderstrom
headline: Elisabeth Soderstrom, Swedish Soprano, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Soderstrom was an opera star, who was acclaimed for the plangent richness of her singing and for a repertory that included leading roles in the Janacek operas.

name: Robert Cameron
headline: Robert Cameron, High-Flying ‘Above’ Photographer, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Cameron was the creator and publisher of the popular “Above” series of photography books for the coffee table.

name: Paul Wendkos
headline: Paul Wendkos, Director of ‘Gidget’ Surfer Movies, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Wendkos was a movie and television director best known for the frothy surfer film “Gidget,” but whose other productions ranged from thrillers to historical dramas.

name: Konstantin Feoktistov
headline: Konstantin Feoktistov, a Soviet Spacecraft Engineer, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Feoktistov, for whom a crater was named on the Moon, was a Soviet engineer and astronaut, and a prominent spacecraft designer.

name: Rusty Kanokogi
headline: Rusty Kanokogi, Fiery Advocate for Women’s Judo, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Kanokogi was considered the mother of women’s judo after fighting for more than two decades to make it an Olympic sport.

name: Dell Hymes
headline: Dell Hymes, Linguist With a Wide Net, Dies at 82
abstract: Professor Hymes was a prominent anthropologist, linguist and folklorist whose work mined the rich, often overlooked territory where language and culture intersect.

name: Daniel Rowen
headline: Daniel Rowen, an Architect Who Favored Modernism, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Rowen was a highly regarded architect whose modernist designs for houses, apartments and commercial spaces attracted a number of prominent clients.

name: Dennis Cole
headline: Dennis Cole, ‘Felony Squad’ Actor, Is Dead at 69
abstract: Mr. Cole was a blond, chiseled former model who played a panoply of roles in more than a dozen prime-time series.

name: James Berg
profession: Negotiated Labor Peace for Citys Landlords
headline: James Berg, 65, Dies; Negotiated Labor Peace for City’s Landlords
abstract: Mr. Berg was a management representative who earned the respect of union leaders during nearly 30 years of contract bargaining for building owners in New York.

name: Charis Wilson
headline: Charis Wilson, Model and Muse, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Wilson was lover, muse, model, amanuensis and wife of the photographer Edward Weston and the subject of many of his best-known nude portraits.

name: Abe Pollin
headline: Abe Pollin, Team Owner and Philanthropist, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Pollin, the owner of the N.B.A.’s Washington Wizards who built the sports arena that revitalized downtown Washington, was known for his wide-ranging philanthropy.

name: H. C. Robbins Landon
headline: H. C. Robbins Landon, Haydn and Mozart Scholar, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Landon was an American musicologist who had a knack for making musicology seem exciting to the general public.

name: Waldo Hunt
headline: Waldo Hunt, King of the Pop-Up Book, Dies at 88
abstract: An advertising man turned novelty-book packager, Mr. Hunt was almost single-handedly responsible for the postwar revival of the pop-up book in the United States.

name: Ali Kordan
profession: Iranian Official Fired Over Fake Degree
headline: Ali Kordan, Iranian Official Fired Over Fake Degree, Dies at 51
abstract: Mr. Kordan was dismissed by Iran’s Parliament after it became clear that he had lied about an honorary doctor of law degree he said he had received from Oxford.

name: Hugh Morgan Hill
headline: Hugh Morgan Hill, the Storyteller Brother Blue, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Hill engaged bystanders on Boston streets with his parables and became a fixture at storytelling conferences abroad.

name: Hale Smith
profession: Broke Borders of Classical and Jazz
headline: Hale Smith, Who Broke Borders of Classical and Jazz, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Smith was a classical composer who also worked as a performer and arranger with jazz greats like Dizzy Gillespie and Chico Hamilton.

name: Jan Leighton
headline: Jan Leighton, Actor Who Played Everyone, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Leighton appeared in so many commercials, print advertisements and industrial films as historical figures that he was both ubiquitous and anonymous.

name: Yang Xianyi
headline: Yang Xianyi, Translator of Chinese Works, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Yang, a translator renowned for his skill at rendering both classic and contemporary Chinese literature into English, was regarded as the greatest translator of 20th-century China.

name: Lino Lacedelli
profession: One of First to Scale K2
headline: Lino Lacedelli Dies at 83; One of First to Scale K2
abstract: Mr. Lacedelli was one of the first two climbers to reach the summit of K2, the world’s second highest peak and among the most treacherous.

name: Ari Kiev
headline: Ari Kiev, a Psychiatrist, Dies at 75
abstract: Dr. Kiev applied visualization and relaxation techniques to coax faster times out of athletes, while helping them face down their fear of failure.

name: Jan Mitchell
profession: Put the ü Back in Lüchows
headline: Jan Mitchell, Who Put the ü Back in Lüchow’s, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Mitchell, who resurrected Longchamps Restaurants and others, collected pre-Columbian gold artifacts, which he gave to the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

name: Bess Lomax Hawes
headline: Bess Lomax Hawes, Folklorist and Singer Who Co-Wrote ‘M.T.A.,’ Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Hawes was a folklorist, teacher and singer who helped write “M.T.A.,” an enduring folk ditty that became a hit for the Kingston Trio in 1959.

name: Max Eisen
profession: Press Agent of Broadways Bygone Era
headline: Max Eisen, Press Agent of Broadway’s Bygone Era, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Eisen was a Broadway press agent from the days when feeding gossip to columnists like Walter Winchell and staging stunts were standard practice for stirring up more box-office appeal.

name: Fred Joseph
headline: Fred Joseph, Who Led Drexel in Its Heyday, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Joseph was an investment banker who helped to create the junk bond business as chief executive of Drexel Burnham Lambert.

name: Tommy Henrich
headline: Tommy Henrich, Yankees Clutch Hitter, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Henrich was a right fielder known as Old Reliable who helped propel the Yankees to seven World Series championships.

name: Bob Keane
headline: Bob Keane, Pop Record Producer, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Keane was a record producer who discovered Ritchie Valens and helped start the careers of Sam Cooke, the Bobby Fuller Four and Frank Zappa.

name: Lester Shubin
profession: Used Kevlar in Vests, Saving Lives
headline: Lester Shubin Dies at 84; Used Kevlar in Vests, Saving Lives
abstract: Mr. Shubin was a government researcher who helped develop bullet-proof vests for the police that have saved more than 3,000 lives.

name: Robert Degen
profession: Had a Hand in the Hokey Pokey
headline: Robert Degen, Who Had a Hand in the Hokey Pokey, Dies at 104
abstract: Mr. Degen was a musician who sued for copyright infringement of the popular song that inspired the hokey pokey dance.

name: Don Congdon
profession: Literary Agent for Ray Bradbury and Others
headline: Don Congdon, Literary Agent for Ray Bradbury and Others, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Congdon, a skilled editor and tough negotiator, launched the career of Ray Bradbury among others.

name: Hugh Hurt Jr.
headline: Hugh Hurt Jr., Engineer Who Studied Motorcycle Accidents, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Hurt did the first meticulous study of motorcycle accidents, emulating air-crash investigations to zero in on when cycle accidents were likely to occur.

name: Eric Woolfson
headline: Eric Woolfson, Co-Founder of Alan Parsons Project, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Woolfson was a founder and the principal songwriter and vocalist of the Alan Parsons Project, a British group that took its ambitious, sophisticated progressive rock to the pop charts.

name: Richard Todd
headline: Richard Todd, Dashing Actor, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Todd was an Oscar-nominated actor best known for war dramas like “The Hasty Heart,” “The Dam Busters” and “The Longest Day.”

name: Paula Hawkins
headline: Paula Hawkins, 82, Florida Ex-Senator, Dies
abstract: Mrs. Hawkins was a tart-tongued conservative Republican who served a single term, fighting to protect children and blazing a trail for women while shunning the label of “feminist.”

name: Liam Clancy
headline: Liam Clancy, Last of the Folk Group, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Clancy was the last surviving member of the singing Clancy Brothers, who found fame in the United States and helped spread the popularity of Irish folk music around the world.

name: Clarence Petty
headline: Clarence Petty, Protector of the Adirondacks, Dies at 104
abstract: Mr. Petty so revered the pristine Adirondack wilderness that he spent virtually all his adult life fighting to preserve it.

name: Malcolm Wells
headline: Malcolm Wells, Champion of ‘Gentle Architecture,’ Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Wells was an iconoclastic architect who advocated environmentally responsible design and promoted the idea of earth-sheltered architecture.

name: Aaron Schroeder
profession: Writer of Hit Songs for Elvis Presley
headline: Aaron Schroeder, Writer of Hit Songs for Elvis Presley, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Schroeder was a songwriter whose more than 2,000 songs included 17 recorded by Elvis Presley.

name: William A. Wilson
headline: William A. Wilson, Reagan’s Envoy to Vatican, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Wilson was appointed as the first full-fledged American ambassador to the Vatican, but his term was clouded by unauthorized dealings with Libya.

name: William P. Wilson
profession: Kennedys TV Aide for Historic 1960 Debate
headline: William P. Wilson, Kennedy’s TV Aide for Historic 1960 Debate, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Wilson negotiated the terms of the televised debate that John F. Kennedy later said “turned the tide” in the election campaign against Richard M. Nixon.

name: M.O. Perry
headline: M.O. Perry, Kennedy Surgeon, Dies at 80
abstract: Dr. Perry as a young surgeon performed a futile tracheotomy on President John F. Kennedy in 1963 and inadvertently provided grist for assassination conspiracy theorists.

name: M.J. Perry Jr.
headline: M.J. Perry Jr., Legal Pioneer, Dies at 89
abstract: Judge Perry won hundreds of civil rights legal battles and became the first black federal judge from the Deep South.

name: Torrie Zito
headline: Torrie Zito, Pianist and Arranger, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Mr. Zito was a versatile arranger who worked with swingers like Bobby Darin, Tony Bennett and Frank Sinatra as well as younger performers.

name: Otto Lambsdorff
headline: Otto Lambsdorff Dies at 82; Shaped Nazi Victims Fund
abstract: Mr. Lambsdorff was a former leader of a small but pivotal German political party and his country’s chief architect of a program that paid reparations to hundreds of thousands of Nazi-era slave laborers.

name: Richard Nader
headline: Richard Nader, Oldies’ Biggest Fan, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Nader’s popular oldies concerts at Madison Square Garden in the 1970s helped jump-start a revival of classic rock ’n’ roll.

name: Jack Rose
headline: Jack Rose, Versatile Master of the Guitar, Is Dead at 38
abstract: Mr. Rose’s complex improvisations on 6-string, 12-string and lap steel guitar earned him a devoted cult following.

name: Harold A. Ackerman
headline: Harold A. Ackerman, Federal Judge in New Jersey, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Ackerman was a federal judge in New Jersey for three decades whose hundreds of cases included trials of crooked politicians, corrupt union officials and reputed organized crime chieftains.

name: John Storm Roberts
headline: John Storm Roberts, World-Music Scholar, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Roberts was an English-born writer, record producer and independent scholar whose work explored the rich ways African and Latin American music influenced the United States.

name: Thomas Hoving
headline: Thomas Hoving, Remaker of the Met, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Hoving transformed the Metropolitan Museum of Art during his tumultuous decade-long tenure as director.

name: Peter R. Scanlon
profession: Led Coopers When Big 8 Ruled Auditing
headline: Peter R. Scanlon, Who Led Coopers When Big 8 Ruled Auditing, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Scanlon shunned the merger mania that engulfed the accounting profession but expanded its international franchise.

name: Yosef H. Yerushalmi
headline: Yosef H. Yerushalmi, Scholar of Jewish History, Dies at 77
abstract: Among his many works, Dr. Yerushalmi examined the conflict between the collective memory of the Jewish people and verifiable history.

name: Gene Barry
headline: Gene Barry, Actor of TV, Film and Stage, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Barry portrayed debonair lawmen on television but his career of more than 60 years ranged from song and dance on Broadway to science fiction.

name: Stephen Toulmin
headline: Stephen Toulmin, a Philosopher and Educator, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Toulmin was an influential philosopher who conducted inquiries into ethics, science and moral reasoning and developed a new approach to analyzing arguments.

name: Mark Ritts
profession: Actor Best Known as a Lab Rat
headline: Mark Ritts, an Actor Best Known as a Lab Rat, Is Dead at 63
abstract: Mr. Ritts scurried about in a costume with a six-foot tail as the smart-alecky Lester the Rat in “Beakman’s World,” a wacky but insidiously educational 1990s television science show.

name: William C. McInnes
headline: The Rev. William C. McInnes, Leader of 2 Jesuit Universities, Dies at 86
abstract: One of the first of his order to specialize in business administration, Father McInnes became president of Fairfield University and the University of San Francisco.

name: Paul Naschy
profession: Spains High Priest of Horror Movies
headline: Paul Naschy, Spain’s High Priest of Horror Movies, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Naschy was an actor, director and screenwriter widely acknowledged as the dean of Spanish horror films.

name: Giorgio Carbone
headline: Giorgio Carbone, Elected Prince of Seborga, Dies at 73
abstract: Prince Giorgio, a bewhiskered grower of mimosa flowers from a family of mimosa growers, was seized by a glorious vision: that Seborga was not part of the surrounding Italian nation.

name: Harold Bell
headline: Harold Bell, a Creator of Woodsy Owl, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Bell helped create the bird who for nearly four decades has exhorted youngsters to “Give a hoot. Don’t pollute!”.

name: Paul A. Samuelson
headline: Paul A. Samuelson, Economist, Dies at 94
abstract: The first American Nobel laureate in economics was the foremost academic economist of the 20th century.

name: Larry Sultan
headline: Larry Sultan, California Photographer, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Sultan was a highly influential California photographer whose 1977 collaboration “Evidence” became a watershed in the history of art photography.

name: Dennis deLeon
headline: Dennis deLeon, AIDS Activist, Dies at 61
abstract: The lawyer and former City Human Rights Commissioner disclosed his H.I.V.-positive status in the early 1990s, when AIDS was far more stigmatized than it is today.

name: Val Avery
headline: Val Avery, Tough-Guy Actor in Movies, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Avery was an actor who worked for nearly 50 years playing tough guys on both sides of the law in dozens of television series and films.

name: Oral Roberts
headline: Oral Roberts, Fiery Preacher, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Roberts’s televised ministry attracted millions of followers and made him one of the most controversial religious leaders of the 20th century.

name: Sol Price
headline: Sol Price, Who Founded Price Club, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Price Club, which Mr. Price founded with his son in 1976, was the forerunner for discount big-box stores like Costco and Sam’s Club.

name: Milorad Pavic
headline: Milorad Pavic, Unorthodox Novelist, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Pavic was an internationally prominent Serbian writer whose novels upended the traditional relationship between reader and text.

name: Russia
headline: Russia’s Market Reform Architect Dies at 53
abstract: Yegor T. Gaidar oversaw the transition from Communism to capitalism as the first finance minister of post-Soviet Russia.

name: Manto Tshabalala-Msimang
headline: Manto Tshabalala-Msimang, South African Who Oversaw Discredited AIDS Policy, Dies at 69
abstract: Dr. Tshabalala-Msimang questioned the causal connection between H.I.V. and AIDS and promoted dietary measures rather than drug treatments.

name: Frank Coffin
profession: Chief Judge of a Federal Appeals Court
headline: Frank Coffin, Chief Judge of a Federal Appeals Court, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Coffin was a former Maine congressman who served for 11 years as the chief judge of the federal appeals court that spans most of New England.

name: Roy E. Disney
headline: Roy E. Disney Dies at 79; Rejuvenated Animation
abstract: Mr. Disney helped revitalize the famed animation division of the company founded by his uncle, Walt Disney.

name: F. William McCalpin
profession: Champion of Legal Aid to Poor
headline: F. William McCalpin, Champion of Legal Aid to Poor, Dies at 88
abstract: A fierce advocate of the Legal Services Corporation, Mr. McCalpin was a proud Republican who nonetheless clashed with Ronald Regan over financing, and won.

name: Peter Forakis
headline: Peter Forakis, a Sculptor of Geometric Forms, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Forakis was a sculptor who helped found Park Place, a prominent New York artists’ cooperative gallery of the 1960s.

name: Jennifer Jones
headline: Jennifer Jones, Postwar Actress, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Jones, who was nominated for Oscars five times, won an Academy Award in 1943 for her performance in “The Song of Bernadette.”

name: C. Bryan
headline: C. Bryan, 73, ‘Friendly Fire’ Writer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Bryan’s 1976 book about the accidental death of a soldier in Vietnam became one of the enduring works of reportage on the Vietnam War.

name: Margaret B. Young
profession: Writer of Childrens Books on Blacks
headline: Margaret B. Young, Writer of Children’s Books on Blacks, Dies at 88
abstract: Mrs. Young, the widow of the civil rights leader Whitney Young Jr., wrote several books for children on the African-American experience.

name: Howard W. Johnson
headline: Howard W. Johnson, M.I.T. President During Vietnam, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Johnson brought a degree of calm and conciliation to the M.I.T. campus at the height of the Vietnam War protests there.

name: Howard Johnson
profession: Elevated the Tuba in Jazz and Beyond
headline: Howard Johnson, 79, Dies; Elevated the Tuba in Jazz and Beyond
abstract: He helped to find a new role for a notoriously cumbersome instrument in a wide range of musical settings, including the “Saturday Night Live” band.

name: Georgina Parkinson
headline: Georgina Parkinson, Star at Royal Ballet, Dies at 71
abstract: Ms. Parkinson was a ballet mistress and coach at American Ballet Theater.

name: James Rossant
headline: James Rossant, Architect and Planner, Dies at 81
abstract: The architect helped design the planned city of Reston, Va.

name: Arthur Cores
profession: Founder of the Boston Market Chain
headline: Arthur Cores, a Founder of the Boston Market Chain, Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. Cores went from making sandwiches at his father’s deli when he was barely more than a toddler to become a founder of the restaurant that eventually became Boston Market.

name: Dan O’Bannon
headline: Dan O’Bannon, 63, Who Wrote Screenplay for ‘Alien,’ Is Dead
abstract: Mr. O’Bannon’s screenplays for “Alien,” “Total Recall,” “The Return of the Living Dead” and other films made him a cult hero among science fiction aficionados.

name: Walter Stamm
headline: Walter Stamm Dies at 64; Helped Curb Chlamydia
abstract: Dr. Stamm’s research saved many women from infertility and helped prevent, control and treat certain common infectious diseases.

name: Lincoln Gordon
headline: Lincoln Gordon Dies at 96; Educator and Ambassador to Brazil
abstract: Dr. Gordon was a Harvard professor for years and served in the Kennedy and Johnson administrations and as the president of Johns Hopkins University.

name: Brittany Murphy
headline: Brittany Murphy, Actress in ‘Clueless,’ Dies at 32
abstract: The actress got her start in the sleeper hit “Clueless” and is best known for her parts in “Girl, Interrupted” and “8 Mile.”

name: Arnold Stang
headline: Arnold Stang, Milquetoast Actor, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Stang was an character actor whose bespectacled, owlish face and nasal urban twang gave him a singular and recognizable persona.

name: Robin Wood
headline: Robin Wood, Film Critic Who Wrote on Hitchcock, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Wood was a film critic who published the first serious work in English on Alfred Hitchcock.

name: Mary Curtis-Verna
headline: Mary Curtis-Verna, Opera’s Champion Pinch-Hitter, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Curtis-Verna was a Metropolitan Opera soprano of the 1950s and ’60s who became famous for stepping into the roles of ailing, stranded or otherwise indisposed divas.

name: Michael E. Ryan
headline: Michael E. Ryan, Dies at 71; Helped The Times Go Public
abstract: Mr. Ryan rose from office boy to help steer the company to public ownership in 1969.

name: Ann Nixon Cooper
headline: Ann Nixon Cooper, Named in Obama’s Victory Speech, Dies at 107
abstract: Ms. Cooper was recalled by President Obama in his election night speech as someone who had witnessed “the heartbreak and the hope” of the past century.

name: Alaina Reed-Amini
headline: Alaina Reed-Amini, ‘Sesame Street’ Resident, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Reed-Amini was an actress and singer whose best-known characters were in the television series “Sesame Street” and “227.”

name: John Edwin Smith
headline: John Edwin Smith, Philosopher at Yale, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Smith was a prominent philosopher and author whose work tackled large questions about the nature of truth from a pragmatic, pluralistic and specifically American perspective.

name: Lester Rodney
profession: Early Voice in Fight Against Racism in Sports
headline: Lester Rodney, Early Voice in Fight Against Racism in Sports, Dies at 98
abstract: A Dodger fan who grew up in Brooklyn, Mr. Rodney was a card-carrying member of the Communist Party and the Baseball Writers Association of America.

name: Yitzhak Ahronovitch
profession: Exodus Skipper in Defiant 47 Voyage of Jewish Refugees
headline: Yitzhak Ahronovitch, Exodus Skipper in Defiant ’47 Voyage of Jewish Refugees, Dies at 86
abstract: The violent interception of the ship by the British Navy in 1947 helped rally support for the creation of the state of Israel.

name: Loren Singer
headline: Loren Singer, ‘Parallax View’ Author, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Singer wrote the thriller, “The Parallax View,” which was one of the first novels to offer a paranoid vision of the United States as a country controlled by ruthless technocrats.

name: George Michael
headline: George Michael, Sportscaster, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Michael’s sports show, “The George Michael Sports Machine,” was the first nationally syndicated sports show to make liberal use of highlights.

name: George Michael
headline: George Michael, Pop Superstar, Is Dead at 53
abstract: The duo Wham! cultivated the image of carefree teenage rebels. Then, in his solo career, Mr. Michael chose to set pop superficiality aside.

name: Edwin Krebs
headline: Edwin Krebs Dies at 91; Discovered a Crucial Bodily Process
abstract: Dr. Krebs shared a Nobel Prize in 1992 for discovering a crucial bodily process that helps govern the movement of muscles, the shape and division of cells, and even learning and memory.

name: Robert Howard
headline: Robert Howard, Decorated Serviceman, Dies at 70
abstract: Colonel Howard was one of the Vietnam War’s most highly decorated servicemen, who was awarded the Medal of Honor for rescuing fellow Green Berets while wounded and under enemy fire.

name: James Gurley
headline: James Gurley, Guitarist in Big Brother, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Gurley played guitar in Big Brother and the Holding Company, the psychedelic rock band that brought Janis Joplin to fame.

name: Vic Chesnutt
headline: Vic Chesnutt, Singer and Songwriter, Dies at 45
abstract: Mr. Chesnutt, a quadriplegic who had a cracked, small voice, sang with disarming candor about a struggle for peace in a life filled with pain.

name: J.H. Fischer
headline: J.H. Fischer, Educator in Turbulent Times, Is Dead at 99
abstract: Mr. Fischer led Baltimore to become the first large American city to integrate its public schools and brought reform to Teachers College of Columbia University as its dean and president.

name: Alice Schiller
headline: Alice Schiller, Impresaria of Striptease, Dies at 95
abstract: Mrs. Schiller was co-owner of the Pink Pussycat of Hollywood, one of the most successful, celebrated and profusely feathered nightclubs of its era.

name: Tim Costello
headline: Tim Costello, Trucker-Author Who Fought Globalization, Dies at 64
abstract: Hailed by academics and labor advocates as a worker-intellectual, Mr. Costello helped found several groups and co-wrote four books.

name: Kim Peek
headline: Kim Peek, Inspiration for ‘Rain Man,’ Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Peek inspired the film that shed a humane light on the travails of autism while revealing the extraordinary powers of memory that a few mentally disabled people possess.

name: Percy E. Sutton
headline: Percy E. Sutton, Political Trailblazer, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Sutton was a pioneering figure who represented Malcolm X as a young lawyer and became one of the nation’s most prominent black political and business leaders.

name: Bob Willoughby
headline: Bob Willoughby, Candid Photographer of the Stars, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Willoughby’s photographs, taken on location, of Audrey Hepburn, Frank Sinatra, Dustin Hoffman and other stars brought a new intimacy and spontaneity to the Hollywood portrait

name: Morris Lasker
headline: Morris Lasker, Judge Who Forced City to Clean Up Jails, Dies at 92
abstract: With a series of rulings in the 1970s and ’80s, Judge Lasker forced New York City to come to grips with the horrendous conditions in its jails and ordered the closing of the notorious Tombs.

name: Matt Turney
headline: Matt Turney, Longtime Dancer With Martha Graham, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Turney was a principal dancer with the Martha Graham Dance Company in the 1950s, ’60s and ’70s.

name: David Levine
headline: David Levine, Biting Caricaturist, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Levine’s astringent drawings became the visual trademark of The New York Review of Books for nearly 50 years.

name: Eugene van Tamelen
headline: Eugene van Tamelen, 84, Dies; Chemist Inspired by Nature
abstract: Dr. van Tamelen, a professor of chemistry at Stanford University, turned to nature for inspiration in synthesizing molecules.

name: Norval White
headline: Norval White, of AIA Guide, Dies at 83
abstract: With the AIA Guide, Mr. White tapped into and fostered a growing national awareness that America had an architectural past worth preserving.

name: Abdurrahman Wahid
profession: Led Indonesia for 2 Years of Tumult
headline: Abdurrahman Wahid, 69, Is Dead; Led Indonesia for 2 Years of Tumult
abstract: Mr. Wahid was an eccentric, nearly blind Muslim cleric who served as Indonesia’s president, championing a tolerant brand of Islam.

name: Judy Kreston
headline: Judy Kreston, Singer and Cabaret Owner, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Ms. Kreston was a fixture as a New York cabaret singer and, for a time, a cabaret owner.

name: Carlene Hatcher Polite
headline: Carlene Hatcher Polite, Novelist, Dies at 77
abstract: Originally trained as a modern dancer, Ms. Polite wrote two novels, which were known for their lush, poetic language and extensive use of monologues.

name: Rachel Wetzsteon
profession: Poet of Keen Insights and Wit
headline: Rachel Wetzsteon, Poet of Keen Insights and Wit, Dies at 42
abstract: Ms. Wetzsteon was a prominent poet whose work was known for its mordant wit, formal elegance and cleareyed examination of the solitary yet defiant lives of single women.

name: David Barish
headline: David Barish, a Developer of the Paraglider, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Barish was an aeronautical engineer who helped design an early paraglider, in a competition for NASA in the 1960s.

name: Ruth Lilly
headline: Ruth Lilly, Drug Heiress and Poetry Patron, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Lilly was the last surviving great-grandchild of the pharmaceutical magnate Eli Lilly, and gave away an estimated $800 million, most notably in a nine-figure gift to Poetry magazine.

name: James L. Goddard
headline: James L. Goddard, Crusading F.D.A. Leader, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Goddard helped revolutionize the government’s methods of evaluating drugs beginning in the 1960s.

name: Dennis Brutus
headline: Dennis Brutus Dies at 85; Fought Apartheid With Sports
abstract: Mr. Brutus led the fight to use sports as a weapon against the racist policies of South Africa.

name: Jean Carroll
headline: Jean Carroll, 98, Is Dead; Blended Wit and Beauty
abstract: Ms. Carroll is widely credited with having blazed the trail for legions of female stand-up comics who came after her.

name: Knut Haugland
headline: Knut Haugland, Sailor on Kon-Tiki, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Haugland was the last surviving member of the six-man crew that sailed on the Kon-Tiki expedition in 1947.

name: Seymour Wittek
profession: World War II Hero at Home
headline: Seymour Wittek Dies at 88; World War II Hero at Home
abstract: As a Coast Guardsman, Mr. Wittek helped battle a fire that threatened New York Harbor, an act of bravery that was recognized six decades later.

name: Curtis Allina
profession: He Put the Heads on Pez
headline: Curtis Allina Dies at 87; He Put the Heads on Pez
abstract: Mr. Allina presided over a powerful innovation in marketing that was less about the candy than it was about the container it came in.

name: Ihor Sevcenko
headline: Ihor Sevcenko, Byzantine and Slavic Scholar, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Sevcenko was a leading scholar of Byzantine and Slavic history and literature who persuaded George Orwell to collaborate with him on a Ukrainian translation of “Animal Farm” for distribution to refugees.

name: Yao Liang
profession: Imprisoned in China for Loyalty to the Vatican
headline: Bishop Yao Liang, 87, Imprisoned in China for Loyalty to the Vatican, Dies
abstract: The bishop encouraged quiet opposition to China’s strictures on religion but also heeded the pope’s call to improve relations.

name: David Murbach
headline: David Murbach, Finder of Rockefeller Center Trees, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Murbach was a horticulturist who had one of the biggest jobs in the world of trees and gardens — finding the holiday tree for Rockefeller Center each year.

name: Smith Bagley
headline: Smith Bagley, Executive and Democratic Fund-Raiser, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Bagley was a former business executive who was active in philanthropic and public affairs work.

name: Donal Donnelly
headline: Donal Donnelly, Actor Who Nurtured Irish Roles, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Donnelly was an Irish actor who embodied a variety of Irish characters on the American stage and in American movies.

name: Kenneth Noland
profession: Abstract Painter of Brilliantly Colored Shapes
headline: Kenneth Noland, Abstract Painter of Brilliantly Colored Shapes, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Noland’s brilliantly colored concentric circles, chevrons and stripes were among the most recognized and admired signatures of the postwar style of abstraction known as Color Field painting.

name: Willie Mitchell
headline: Willie Mitchell, Soul Music Producer, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Mitchell shaped the elegant yet gritty sound of Al Green, Ann Peebles and other stars of soul music as the house producer at Hi Records in the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Tsutomu Yamaguchi
headline: Tsutomu Yamaguchi, Survivor of 2 Atomic Blasts, Dies at 93
abstract: Tsotomu Yamaguchi was in Hiroshima on business when the first atomic bomb was dropped, only to return to his hometown, Nagasaki, at the time of the second attack.

name: Art Bartlett
headline: Art Bartlett, Founder of Century 21 Real Estate, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Bartlett was among the first to enable hundreds, and later thousands, of brokers working from their own offices to compete with regional and national chains.

name: Mary Daly
headline: Mary Daly, a Leader in Feminist Theology, Dies at 81
abstract: Professor Daly made worldwide headlines a decade ago after she retired from Boston College rather than admit men to some of her classes.

name: Lhasa de Sela
headline: Lhasa de Sela, Singer Who Crossed Borders, Dies at 37
