abstract: Ms. de Sela was a Mexican-American singer and songwriter who became an international star after moving to Canada.

name: Charles Kleibacker
headline: Charles Kleibacker, Fashion Designer, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Kleibacker was a former fashion designer whose taste for intricately constructed gowns gave him the nickname Master of the Bias in the 1960s.

name: Mary Gardiner Jones
headline: Mary Gardiner Jones, Consumer Advocate, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Jones was a prominent consumer advocate who worked to ensure that goods — from clothing to cereal to cigarettes — were safer, less expensive and more truthfully advertised.

name: Catherine E. F. Biden
headline: Catherine E. F. Biden, Mother of the Vice President, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mrs. Biden was a presence on the campaign trail with her son, Vice President Joseph R. Biden Jr., in 2008 and was lauded in his 2007 biography, “Promises to Keep.”

name: Lew Allen
headline: Gen. Lew Allen, Who Lifted Veil on Security Agency, Is Dead at 84
abstract: General Allen served in many positions, including Air Force chief of staff, but gained the most attention for publicly discussing the National Security Agency’s secret work.

name: David Gerber
headline: David Gerber, Award-Winning Television Producer, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Gerber was an Emmy- and Peabody Award-winning television producer who brought forward-thinking series like “Police Story” and “Police Woman” to prime time in the 1970s.

name: Eunice Johnson
headline: Eunice Johnson Dies at 93; Gave Ebony Its Name
abstract: Mrs. Johnson was the founder of the grand traveling tour called Ebony Fashion Fair, as well as a force behind Ebony and Jet magazines.

name: Herbert Spiegel
headline: Herbert Spiegel, Doctor Who Popularized Hypnosis, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Spiegel was A New York psychiatrist who was the country’s most persuasive advocate for therapeutic hypnosis, having established it as a mainstream medical technique.

name: Freya von Moltke
profession: Part of a Core of Nazi Resistance
headline: Freya von Moltke, Part of a Core of Nazi Resistance, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Mrs. Moltke, who disdained the title of countess, was the last living active participant in the group that opposed Hitler.

name: Ray Solomonoff
headline: Ray Solomonoff, Pioneer in Artificial Intelligence, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Solomonoff was a physicist who was one of the founders of the field of artificial intelligence.

name: Art Clokey
headline: Art Clokey, Animator Who Created Gumby, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Clokey was the animator who half a century ago created Gumby, that most pliant of pop-cultural figures.

name: Eric Rohmer
profession: Leading Filmmaker of the French New Wave
headline: Eric Rohmer, a Leading Filmmaker of the French New Wave, Dies at 89
abstract: The critic and filmmaker was one of the founding figures of the internationally influential French New Wave movement.

name: Miep Gies
headline: Miep Gies, Protector of Anne Frank, Dies at 100
abstract: Mrs. Gies was the last survivor among Anne Frank’s protectors and the woman who preserved her diary.

name: Consuela Lee
headline: Consuela Lee, Jazz Pianist and Educator, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Lee, a jazz pianist, fought to establish an arts school for children in rural Alabama on the grounds of the moribund academy founded by her grandfather.

name: Shirley Rich
headline: Shirley Rich, Grand Dame of Casting, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Rich, widely regarded as the doyenne of New York casting directors, for half a century scoured the country for little-known actors.

name: Mina Bern
headline: Mina Bern, Versatile Yiddish Actress, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Bern was a plucky and versatile actress and singer who was one of the last links to the scrappy world of Yiddish theater in New York.

name: Knox Burger
headline: Knox Burger, Agent and Book Editor, Dies at 87
abstract: A fierce advocate of writers and writing who didn’t suffer pretenders gladly, Mr. Burger was one of the book industry’s notoriously crusty personages.

name: Ed Beach
profession: Host of Just Jazz Radio Show
headline: Ed Beach, Host of ‘Just Jazz’ Radio Show, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Beach attracted listeners in New York and elsewhere with his sonorous voice, eclectic taste, vast erudition and pleasurably irascible temperament.

name: Art Rust Jr.
headline: Art Rust Jr., Pioneer in Sports Talk Radio, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Rust was a pioneering figure in New York radio sports talk shows and a sports historian whose books focused on the interplay of race and athletics.

name: Donald Goerke
headline: Donald Goerke, Creator of SpaghettiOs, Dies at 83
abstract: In 35 years at Campbell Soup, Mr. Goerke created SpaghettiOs and Chunky soup.

name: William J. Lederer
headline: William J. Lederer, Co-Author of ‘The Ugly American,’ Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Lederer was a writer and career naval officer who co-wrote “The Ugly American,” a novel that barely veiled a blistering critique of the nation’s foreign policy in Southeast Asia.

name: Jay Reatard
headline: Jay Reatard, 29, a Force in Punk Rock, Is Dead
abstract: Jimmy Lee Lindsey Jr., who performed under the stage name Jay Reatard, was a force in the worlds of punk and garage rock.

name: Teddy Pendergrass
headline: Teddy Pendergrass, R&B Soul Singer, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Pendergrass was the Philadelphia soul singer whose husky, potent baritone was a definition of R&B seduction in the 1970s.

name: Dennis Stock
headline: Dennis Stock, Photographer of Intimate Portraits, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Stock was a photographer whose intimate and evocative portraits captured the essence of jazz performance and helped shape James Dean’s moody public persona.

name: Michael Kaufman
headline: Michael Kaufman, Times Reporter Who Roamed World, Is Dead at 71
abstract: A New York Times reporter covered the fall of Communism, topless cellists, and everything in between.

name: Hasib Sabbagh
headline: Hasib Sabbagh, Co-Founder of Middle East Builder, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Sabbagh’s company built major projects around the world, including Abu Ghraib prison in Iraq and an extension to Ronald Reagan National Airport near Washington.

name: Ruth McBride Jordan
profession: Subject of Sons Book Color of Water
headline: Ruth McBride Jordan, Subject of Son’s Book ‘Color of Water,’ Dies at 88
abstract: The recollections of Mrs. McBride Jordan by her son, James McBride, became the basis of a best-selling novel.

name: Edward Schillebeeckx
headline: Edward Schillebeeckx, Catholic Theologian, Dies at 95
abstract: Father Schillebeeckx was a prominent theologian who helped reshape Catholicism during the Second Vatican Council and whose writings were later investigated for heresy.

name: Thomas L. Petty
headline: Dr. Thomas L. Petty, Researcher of Long-Term Oxygen Therapy, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Dr. Petty was a pulmonologist whose research was instrumental in the development of long-term oxygen therapy for patients with severe chronic lung disease.

name: Mel Cuba
headline: Mel Cuba Dies at 99; Saved 4 Drowning Orphans in Queens
abstract: Then a lifeguard working on his 23rd birthday at the beach in Rockaway, Queens, Mr. Cuba raced into the water when 40 youngsters were swept away by a huge wave.

name: Jyoti Basu
headline: Jyoti Basu, Leader of Communists in India, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Basu, a powerful leftist leader who dominated politics in the state of West Bengal for more than two decades, nearly became India’s first Communist prime minister.

name: George Leonard
headline: George Leonard, Voice of ’60s Counterculture, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Leonard, a former journalist who foresaw the countercultural tides of the 1960s, helped define the human potential movement at its de facto headquarters.

name: Glen W. Bell Jr.
headline: Glen W. Bell Jr., Founder of Taco Bell, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Bell’s idea in 1951 to sell tacos from his hamburger stand became the foundation of the restaurant chain that turned Mexican fare into fast food for millions of Americans.

name: Edward H. Linde
headline: Edward H. Linde, Co-Founder of Boston Properties, Dies at 68
abstract: As chief executive of Boston Properties, Mr. Linde was the behind-the-scenes partner of Mortimer B. Zuckerman.

name: Harold Faber
profession: Longtime Reporter and Editor for The Times
headline: Harold Faber, Longtime Reporter and Editor for The Times, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Faber covered the Korean War, helped direct coverage of the civil rights movement and reported on the deaths of the Collyer brothers, which became the stuff of urban lore.

name: Carl Smith
headline: Carl Smith, Country Music Hitmaker, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Smith, who ranked among the most popular country hitmakers of the 1950s, had 58 consecutive Top 40 hits on the Billboard country chart.

name: Erich Segal
headline: Erich Segal, ‘Love Story’ Author, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Segal was a Yale classic professor turned popular writer whose first novel, “Love Story,” became a staggering commercial success if not quite a critical one when it appeared in 1970.

name: David Sarkisyan
headline: David Sarkisyan, Champion of Moscow Architecture, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Sarkisyan became famous for his campaigns to preserve architectural monuments against rampant post-Soviet development.

name: George Jellinek
headline: George Jellinek, WQXR Opera Host, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Jellinek’s weekly program, “The Vocal Scene,” allowed him to dip into his encyclopedic knowledge about singers and singing.

name: Robert B. Parker
headline: Robert B. Parker, the Prolific Writer Who Created Spenser, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Mr. Parker was the best-selling mystery writer who created Spenser, a tough, glib Boston private detective who was the hero of nearly 40 novels.

name: Kate McGarrigle
headline: Kate McGarrigle, Canadian Singer and Songwriter, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. McGarrigle, with her sister Anna, captivated critics and fellow musicians with warm harmonies and a style that drew on the personalized approach of 1970s singer-songwriters.

name: Laura Chapman Hruska
headline: Laura Chapman Hruska, Co-Founder of Soho Press, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Hruska was a co-founder and the editor in chief of Soho Press, an independent book publisher that specializes in literary fiction and exotic crime stories.

name: Alastair Martin
profession: Court Tennis Star and Modern Tennis Executive
headline: Alastair Martin, 94, Court Tennis Star and Modern Tennis Executive, Dies
abstract: Martin won a host of national championships playing the venerable game of court tennis, then helped forge the modern era of the Grand Slam-style game.

name: Marshall Nirenberg
headline: Marshall Nirenberg, Biologist Who Untangled Genetic Code, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Nirenberg was a biologist who deciphered the genetic code of life, earning a Nobel Prize for his achievement.

name: Robben W. Fleming
headline: Robben W. Fleming, University President in Turbulent Times, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Fleming was considered a patient leader for the University of Michigan in the late 1960s and ’70s, an era of student protests.

name: James E. Cheek
headline: James E. Cheek, Forceful University President, Dies at 77
abstract: Dr. Cheek saw Howard University in Washington through 20 years of growth, financial problems and campus unrest.

name: Jerilyn Ross
headline: Jerilyn Ross, Advocate for the Anxious, Dies at 63
abstract: A skilled therapist and exuberant optimist, Ms. Ross overcame her fears and helped others manage their own.

name: Steven Lovelady
headline: Steven Lovelady, Editor With a Deft Touch, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Lovelady was a respected editor with a deft touch who played a significant role in award-winning journalism at The Philadelphia Inquirer and magazines owned by Time Inc.

name: Daniel J. Freed
headline: Daniel J. Freed Dies at 82; Shaped Sentencing in U.S.
abstract: Mr. Freed was a Yale Law School professor who was a leading intellectual influence and commentator on how Americans convicted of crimes should be sentenced.

name: Irwin Dambrot
headline: Irwin Dambrot Dies at 81; Caught in Gambling Scandal
abstract: Mr. Dambrot was a basketball star who led City College to the 1950 N.I.T. and N.C.A.A. titles, only to be engulfed in a national point-shaving scandal.

name: Jean Simmons
headline: Jean Simmons Dies at 80; Actress Whose Talent Exceeded the Parts She Played
abstract: Ms. Simmons, a British actress known for her beauty as well as her acting, starred in “Hamlet,” “Guys and Dolls,” and “Spartacus.”

name: Earl Wild
headline: Earl Wild, Pianist, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Wild was known for his high-energy performances of Romantic works, but his tastes ranged from Baroque works and Mozart concertos to contemporary scores.

name: Abraham Sutzkever
headline: Abraham Sutzkever, 96, Jewish Poet and Partisan, Dies
abstract: Mr. Sutzkever was one of the great Yiddish poets of his generation who evoked the nightmare of the Holocaust with images of worn shoes and the silence of a sky of white stars.

name: Bob Noorda
headline: Bob Noorda Is Dead at 82; Designer Took Modernism Underground
abstract: Mr. Noorda was an internationally known graphic designer who helped introduce a Modernist look to advertising posters, corporate logos and the New York City subway system.

name: Jack T. Litman
profession: Lawyer for Preppy Killer and Others
headline: Jack T. Litman, Lawyer for ‘Preppy Killer’ and Others, Is Dead at 66
abstract: Mr. Litman, who had an uncanny ability to win sympathy from juries for unpopular clients, was a lightning rod for criticism for his “blame the victim” strategy.

name: Robert A. Mosbacher
headline: Robert A. Mosbacher, 82, Ex-Commerce Chief, Dies
abstract: A Texas oilman, Mr. Mosbacher helped George H. W. Bush win the 1988 presidential election and joined his cabinet.

name: Pernell Roberts
headline: Pernell Roberts, Star of TV’s ‘Bonanza,’ Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Roberts, who played Adam Cartwright, the eldest son on television’s seminal western series “Bonanza, ”was the last surviving member of the show’s original family.

name: Charles Mathias
headline: Charles Mathias, Former U.S. Senator, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Mathias was a lawmaker who was once called “the conscience of the Senate” by the leader of the opposition party.

name: Bobby Bragan
headline: Bobby Bragan, Ex-Baseball Manager and Executive, Dies at 92
abstract: Early in his career, Bragan was influenced by Jackie Robinson and Branch Rickey. To cap his career, he managed a game at age 87.

name: Ed Thigpen
headline: Ed Thigpen, Jazz Drummer, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Thigpen’s tasteful and understated style made him a favorite accompanist of some of the best-known performers in jazz, especially Oscar Peterson.

name: Ruth P. Smith
headline: Ruth P. Smith, Abortion-Rights Pioneer, Dies at 102
abstract: Mrs. Smith was a longtime reproductive rights advocate who helped found what is now Naral Pro-Choice America.

name: Lawrence Garfinkel
headline: Lawrence Garfinkel Dies at 88; Fought Smoking
abstract: Mr. Garfinkel, a student of statistics who learned epidemiology on the job, worked at the American Cancer Society for 43 years.

name: Louis Auchincloss
profession: Chronicler of New Yorks Upper Crust
headline: Louis Auchincloss, Chronicler of New York’s Upper Crust, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Auchincloss was one of America’s pre-eminent novelists of manners and a portraitist of wealthy, white Manhattanites.

name: Zelda Rubinstein
headline: Zelda Rubinstein, Clairvoyant in ‘Poltergeist,’ Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Rubinstein was a petite character actress best known for playing the indomitable ghost-purging psychic in “Poltergeist.”

name: Howard Zinn
headline: Howard Zinn, Historian, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Zinn was the author of “A People’s History of the United States,” which inspired a generation of high school and college students to rethink American history.

name: Andrew Lange
headline: Andrew Lange, Scholar of the Cosmos, Dies at 52
abstract: Dr. Lange’s work as an astrophysicist put him in the middle of one of the grandest quests in science and led to the discovery that the universe is flat.

name: J. D. Salinger
headline: J. D. Salinger, Literary Recluse, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Salinger, the author of “The Catcher in the Rye,” turned his back on success and adulation.

name: Louis R. Harlan
headline: Louis R. Harlan, Historian of Booker T. Washington, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Harlan’s definitive two-volume biography of Booker T. Washington convincingly embraced its subject’s daunting complexities and ambiguities and won the Pulitzer Prize.

name: Robert Joffe
headline: Robert Joffe, Noted Lawyer, Dies at 66
abstract: A partner at Cravath, Swaine & Moore, Mr. Joffe also had an interest in civil rights law and represented directors of companies related to the recent financial crisis.

name: Jane Jarvis
profession: Player of Jazz and Mets Music
headline: Jane Jarvis, Player of Jazz and Mets Music, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Jarvis brought a jazz sensibility to unlikely places as an organist for the New York Mets and a programmer for Muzak.

name: Shirley Bell Cole
headline: Shirley Bell Cole, the Voice of Little Orphan Annie, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Cole was the primary radio voice of the red-haired character from 1930 to 1940.

name: Tom Brookshier
headline: Tom Brookshier, 78, an N.F.L. Star and Voice
abstract: Tom Brookshier, a star defensive back who helped lead the Philadelphia Eagles to the 1960 National Football League championship and later teamed with Pat Summerall as CBS’s No. 1 pro football broadcasting duo, died Friday at a hospital in the Philadelphia suburb of Wynnewood, Pa. Brookshier, who lived in West Conshohocken, Pa., was 78.

name: Stephen Huneck
headline: Stephen Huneck, Artist of Dogs, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Huneck was an internationally known artist, woodcarver and furniture maker whose most famous work was the Dog Chapel, a hand-built church in Vermont.

name: David Brown
headline: David Brown, Film and Stage Producer, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Brown was an urbane New Yorker whose publishing background was the foundation of a producing career in Hollywood.

name: Earl A. Barthé
headline: Earl A. Barthé, a Master of Plaster, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Barthé, a fifth-generation plasterer, epitomized the old-time craftsmen who continue to provide a traditional flavor to the architectural jambalaya of New Orleans.

name: Aaron Ruben
headline: Aaron Ruben, TV Producer, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Ruben was a producer, writer and director for some of the most popular television comedies of the 1960s and ’70s, notably “The Andy Griffith Show” and “Sanford and Son.”

name: James H. Quello
headline: James H. Quello, Ex-Member of F.C.C., Dies at 95
abstract: On the Federal Communications Commission for more than 20 years, Mr. Quello helped propel the drive to deregulate broadcasting.

name: Frances Buss
headline: Frances Buss, Pioneer of Early Television, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Buss helped establish the talk show, the game show and the cooking show as television staples.

name: Dick McGuire
profession: Fixture With the Knicks for More Than Half a Century
headline: Dick McGuire, a Fixture With the Knicks for More Than Half a Century, Dies at 84
abstract: As a player, coach and scout, Mr. McGuire was identified indelibly with New York.

name: Lee A. Archer Jr.
headline: Lee A. Archer Jr., Tuskegee Fighter Pilot, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Archer was a pioneering black fighter pilot who was credited with shooting down four German planes when he flew with the Tuskegee Airmen of World War II.

name: Hans L. Trefousse
headline: Hans L. Trefousse, Historian and Author, Dies at 88
abstract: Professor Trefousse was a specialist in Civil War and Reconstruction-era history who taught at Brooklyn College for almost 50 years.

name: Frances Reid
profession: Actress of Stage and Daytime TV
headline: Frances Reid, Actress of Stage and Daytime TV, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Reid was one of daytime television’s most enduring performers, who played the family matriarch Alice Horton on the soap opera “Days of Our Lives.”

name: Bill Dudley
headline: Bill Dudley, Slow, Small, but an N.F.L. Star, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Dudley had a Hall of Fame career as one of college and professional football’s most dynamic running backs in the 1940s and early 1950s despite a small frame and a lack of speed.

name: Imari Obadele
headline: Imari Obadele, Who Fought for Reparations, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Obadele was a leader of the militant movement for slavery reparations and black separatism.

name: Tomás Eloy Martínez
headline: Tomás Eloy Martínez, Argentine Author Who Merged Fact With Fancy, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Martínez was an Argentine writer whose fiction mingled journalistic and novelistic techniques.

name: Margaret Dale
profession: Director of Dance for the BBC
headline: Margaret Dale, Director of Dance for the BBC, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Dale was an illustrious dancer who went on to become an important producer and director of dance for British television.

name: Lydia Csato Gasman
headline: Lydia Csato Gasman, Picasso Scholar, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Gasman was an art historian known for her groundbreaking scholarship on the work of Picasso.

name: Geoffrey Burbidge
headline: Geoffrey Burbidge, Who Traced Life to Stardust, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Dr. Burbidge was one of the last giants of the postwar era of astronomy, when big telescopes revealed a universe more diverse and violent than anybody had dreamed.

name: Jack Block
headline: Jack Block, Who Studied Young Children Into Adulthood, Dies at 85
abstract: Professor Block's project began in 1968 with a group of 3-year-olds, and ended when they turned 32.

name: David V. Becker
headline: David V. Becker, Expert on Thyroid Disease, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Dr. Becker was a pioneer in using radioactive materials to diagnose and treat thyroid disease and an expert on the thyroid damage caused by the Chernobyl nuclear reactor accident.

name: Seymour B. Sarason
headline: Seymour B. Sarason, Leader in Community Psychology, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Sarason was a psychologist whose groundbreaking work on social settings and their influence on individual problems helped establish the field of community psychology.

name: John P. Murtha
headline: Representative John P. Murtha Dies at 77; Ex-Marine Was Iraq War Critic
abstract: Mr. Murtha, a Pennsylvania Democrat, served 35 years in Congress and was alternately respected and feared by colleagues.

name: Frank Magid
headline: Frank Magid, Creator of ‘Action News,’ Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Magid was a marketing consultant who was widely credited with standardizing the face of local television news.

name: Ian Carmichael
headline: Ian Carmichael, Comic British Actor, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Carmichael was a debonair actor who made a specialty of playing an oblivious twit on television and then a lovable goofball in British films.

name: Carl Braun
headline: Carl Braun, an All-Star With the Knicks, Dies at 82
abstract: At 6 feet 5 inches and about 180 pounds, Mr. Braun was one of the top scorers in the early years of the National Basketball Association.

name: Charlie Wilson
profession: Texas Congressman Linked to Foreign Intrigue
headline: Charlie Wilson, Texas Congressman Linked to Foreign Intrigue, Dies at 76
abstract: The career of Mr. Wilson, a politician with a taste for whiskey and women, took on a new dimension with the revelation that he aided Afghan rebels.

name: John Dankworth
headline: John Dankworth, a Leader of British Jazz Scene, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Dankworth was one of the leading lights of the British jazz scene for more than a half-century.

name: Brooks Thomas
headline: Brooks Thomas, Publishing Executive at Harper & Row, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Thomas, a lawyer, was at the helm of the company during upheavals in the industry and a notable suit against The Nation magazine.

name: Phil Harris
headline: Phil Harris, Crusty Captain on ‘Deadliest Catch,’ Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Harris was the cantankerous captain of the Cornelia Marie, a crab-fishing boat that plied the Bering Sea on the hit reality television show “Deadliest Catch.”

name: Alexander McQueen
headline: Alexander McQueen, Designer, Is Dead at 40
abstract: The British fashion designer was known for some of the most controversial collections of the last two decades.

name: Jimmie Heuga
headline: Jimmie Heuga, an Early U.S. Ski Medalist, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Heuga was one of the first two American men to win an Olympic medal in Alpine skiing. He was also an advocate for multiple sclerosis, the disease that curtailed his athletic career.

name: Frederick C. Weyand
headline: Frederick C. Weyand, Vietnam Commander, Dies at 93
abstract: General Weyand, the commander of American forces in the final year of the war, had become convinced as early as 1967 that the war was unwinnable.

name: Fred Morrison
profession: Creator of a Popular Flying Plate
headline: Fred Morrison, Creator of a Popular Flying Plate, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Morrison at 17 sent the lid of a popcorn tin skimming through the air and as an adult remade the lid in plastic.

name: David Morrow
headline: David Morrow, Business Journalist, Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. Morrow worked at several publications through the years until taking the Donald W. Reynolds endowed chair at the University of Nevada in Reno in 2009.

name: Frank F. Fasi
headline: Frank F. Fasi, 89, Mayor of Honolulu for 22 Years, Is Dead
abstract: Brash and resilient, Mr. Fasi won three terms as a Democrat, then three more as a Republican.

name: William Tenn
headline: William Tenn, Science Fiction Author, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Tenn wrote satirical science fiction at a time when few writers in the genre displayed a sense of humor.

name: Dick Francis
headline: Dick Francis, Jockey and Writer, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Francis’s notable but blighted career as a champion steeplechase jockey for the British royal family was eclipsed by a second, more brilliant career as a popular thriller writer.

name: Bernard Lander
headline: Rabbi Bernard Lander, the Founder of Touro College, Is Dead at 94
abstract: An academic sociologist, he established the college in response to Jews who felt adrift and marginalized in American college culture.

name: Phillip Martin
headline: Phillip Martin, Who Led His Tribe to Wealth, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. Martin guided Choctaws from grinding poverty in east central Mississippi to become proprietor of one of the state’s leading business empires.

name: Doug Fieger
headline: Doug Fieger Dies at 57, Singer of ‘My Sharona’
abstract: Mr. Fieger was the lead singer and rhythm guitarist of the band the Knack, whose 1979 hit “My Sharona” has become an emblem of the new wave era in rock.

name: Ralph McInerny
headline: Ralph McInerny, Scholar and Mystery Novelist, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. McInerny was a prolific novelist and scholar of Roman Catholicism who taught at the University of Notre Dame for more than half a century.

name: Sylvia Pressler
headline: Judge Sylvia Pressler, Who Opened Little League to Girls, Dies at 75
abstract: Judge Pressler was a jurist who extended the rights of gay couples and opened the door for girls to play Little League baseball.

name: Lucille Clifton
headline: Lucille Clifton, Poet Who Explored Intricacies of Black Lives, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Clifton was a distinguished American poet whose work trained lenses wide and narrow on the experience of being black and female in the 20th century.

name: Howard Lotsof
profession: Saw Drug Cure in a Plant
headline: Howard Lotsof Dies at 66; Saw Drug Cure in a Plant
abstract: Mr. Lotsof’s belief that ibogaine could cure addiction to heroin persuaded the F.D.A. to approve a clinical trial, but the substance remains banned in the United States.

name: Rex Nettleford
headline: Rex Nettleford, Jamaican Scholar and Educator, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Nettleford devoted his life to studying postcolonial Caribbean culture and in the process helped shape it.

name: Dale Hawkins
headline: Dale Hawkins Dies at 73; Rockabilly Author of ‘Susie Q’
abstract: Mr. Hawkins was a songwriter and singer who drew deeply from the heavy blues sounds of South Louisiana to create a classic of what is sometimes called swamp rock.

name: Donald E. Welsh
headline: Donald E. Welsh, a Creator of Magazines, Dies at 66
abstract: After working at Rolling Stone and Outside, Mr. Welsh helped to create Arthur Frommer’s Budget Travel, Budget Living and children’s magazines.

name: Gareth Wigan
headline: Gareth Wigan, Who Urged Hollywood Abroad, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Wigan’s career in the film industry ranged from helping to shape seminal movies like “Star Wars” to forging Hollywood’s production strategy overseas.

name: Kathryn Grayson
headline: Kathryn Grayson, Operatic Film Star, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Grayson’s operatic voice and campus-sweetheart beauty embodied the glamour of Hollywood movie musicals in the 1940s and ’50s.

name: Carl Kaysen
profession: Nuclear Test Ban Negotiator (and Much More)
headline: Carl Kaysen, Nuclear Test Ban Negotiator (and Much More), Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Kaysen wove a tapestry of expertise through economics, foreign policy, sociology, environmentalism and the law, and played crucial behind-the-scenes roles in the Kennedy White House.

name: Fran Lee
headline: Fran Lee, Whose Work Led to Pooper-Scooper Law, Is Dead at 99
abstract: Ms. Lee counseled generations of New Yorkers on household and consumer issues, and later waged a campaign that led to New York’s pooper-scooper law.

name: Lionel Jeffries
headline: Lionel Jeffries, British Character Actor, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Jeffries was a mustachioed, bald-pated British character actor who excelled in rubber-faced comedic roles.

name: Alexander M. Haig Jr.
headline: Alexander M. Haig Jr. Dies at 85; Was Forceful Aide to 2 Presidents
abstract: Mr. Haig was secretary of state under President Reagan and was the White House chief of staff as President Richard M. Nixon’s administration crumbled.

name: Allan Kornblum
headline: Allan Kornblum, Counsel to F.B.I., Is Dead at 71
abstract: Mr. Kornblum helped steer the F.B.I. into the post-J. Edgar Hoover era by drafting guidelines for its surveillance operations in the 1970s.

name: Allan Kornblum
headline: Allan Kornblum, Independent Publisher, Dies at 65; Sought the Undiscovered
abstract: Mr. Kornblum started Coffee House Press, an independent publisher known for finding and nurturing new authors.

name: Sam D. Hamilton
headline: Sam D. Hamilton, Wildlife Service Director, Is Dead at 54
abstract: Mr. Hamilton turned a Southern youth’s love of fish and waterfowl into a 30-year career with the United States Fish and Wildlife Service, becoming the service’s director last year.

name: Albert M. Kligman
headline: Dr. Albert M. Kligman, Dermatologist, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Kligman was hailed for inventing the widely used acne medication Retin-A, but was criticized for tests that used inmates.

name: Ilona Copen
headline: Ilona Copen, a Founder of Dance Competition, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Copen was a founder of the New York International Ballet Competition and a champion of the exchange of ideas among dance companies around the world.

name: James Wieghart
headline: James Wieghart, Editor of Daily News, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Wieghart worked at several newspapers and in government, where he contributed to the independent counsel’s report on the Iran-contra affair.

name: John Babcock
profession: Last Canadian World War I Veteran
headline: John Babcock, Last Canadian World War I Veteran, Dies at 109
abstract: Mr. Babcock became a dual citizen of Canada and the United States, and was inspired to join the military, in part, by a poem.

name: Selma G. Hirsh
headline: Selma G. Hirsh, Humanitarian, Dies at 92
abstract: A longtime executive of the American Jewish Committee, Ms. Hirsh also co-wrote a history of the organization.

name: Raymond Mason
headline: Raymond Mason, Sculptor Who Focused on Street-Level Drama, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Mason was a British sculptor whose teeming street scenes and narrative tableaux evoked an animated world of ordinary people caught up in the drama of daily life.

name: Robert J. Myers
headline: Robert J. Myers, Actuary Who Shaped Social Security Program, Dies at 97
abstract: A six-week stint on a Roosevelt administration panel turned into a long career in social insurance programs for Mr. Myers.

name: Kermit Tyler
headline: Kermit Tyler, Player of a Fateful, if Minor, Role in Pearl Harbor Attack, Dies at 96
abstract: New in manning the aircraft tracking center, Mr. Tyler ignored a radar station’s report of many planes approaching Pearl Harbor on the morning of Dec. 7, 1941.

name: Nancy Sweezy
headline: Nancy Sweezy, Savior of Jugtown Pottery, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Sweezy revived the tradition of Jugtown pottery in the Piedmont hills of North Carolina.

name: David Soyer
headline: David Soyer, Cellist, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Soyer was the founding cellist for the Guarneri String Quartet and a link to the legendary cellists Pablo Casals and Emanuel Feuermann.

name: Ernst Beyeler
headline: Ernst Beyeler, Top Dealer of Modern Art, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Beyeler, one of the world’s foremost dealers of modern art, established a jewel-like small museum, the Fondation Beyeler, to display his private collection of important works.

name: W. E. Gordon
profession: Creator of Link to Deep Space
headline: W. E. Gordon, Creator of Link to Deep Space, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Gordon was an electrical engineer who conceived, designed, built and operated the world’s largest radio telescope.

name: John Reed
profession: Master of Gilbert and Sullivans Patter Songs
headline: John Reed, Master of Gilbert and Sullivan’s Patter Songs, Dies at 94
abstract: From 1959 to 1979, Mr. Reed, a silver-tongued Gilbert and Sullivan singer, was the principal comedian of the D’Oyly Carte Opera Company.

name: David Bankier
headline: David Bankier, Scholar of Holocaust, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Bankier, who was the head of the International Institute for Holocaust Research, examined the participation of ordinary Europeans in the extermination of their Jewish neighbors.

name: Arthur Hayes Jr.
headline: Arthur Hayes Jr., Who Led F.D.A. in Tylenol Case, Is Dead at 76
abstract: During the Reagan administration, Dr. Hayes helped calm consumer fears after a Tylenol poisoning case and, amid some controversy, approved the use of the artificial sweetener aspartame.

name: Sheldon Gilgore
headline: Sheldon Gilgore, Physician Who Led Drug Giants Pfizer and Searle, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Gilgore, an opera lover, had roles in the advancement of drugs like Ambien and Celebrex.

name: Jeanne Holm
headline: Jeanne Holm Dies at 88; A Pioneer in the Air Force
abstract: General Holm’s own rise could be seen as part of the change in the military she helped engineer.

name: Fabian Bachrach
headline: Fabian Bachrach, 92, Portraitist Who Photographed Kennedy, Dies
abstract: Mr. Bachrach was a prominent photographer best known for his portrait of a young senator named John Fitzgerald Kennedy.

name: Rose Gray
headline: Rose Gray, a Master of Italian Fare, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Ms. Gray was a founder and chef of the River Café in London, a restaurant that transformed the image of Italian cooking in Britain by emphasizing fresh ingredients and authentic country dishes.

name: Hank Rosenstein
headline: Hank Rosenstein, Player in First N.B.A. Game, Dies at 89
abstract: The 6-foot-4-inch, 185-pound center and forward was an original member of the 1946 New York Knickerbockers.

name: Barry Hannah
headline: Barry Hannah, Darkly Comic Writer, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Hannah was a writer who found wide acclaim with wild, darkly comic short stories and novels set in a phantasmagoric South moving at warp speed.

name: Michael Foot
headline: Michael Foot Dies at 96; Led Britain’s Labour Party
abstract: Mr. Foot failed to broker a peace between the party’s left and right wings, and presided over its crushing defeat in the 1983 general election.

name: Gene Chenault
headline: Gene Chenault, Who Changed Rock Radio, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Chenault helped reshaped rock radio in the 1960s with prepackaged programming that delivered more music and fewer commercials to hundreds of stations, creating the automated format common today.

name: Theodore Cross
headline: Theodore Cross Dies at 86, a Champion of Civil Rights
abstract: Mr. Cross wrote on black empowerment, released two books of his photos of birds and once bid unsuccessfully for Harper & Row.

name: Arnold Beichman
headline: Arnold Beichman, Political Analyst, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Beichman was a prominent political analyst, author and newspaper columnist known for being ardently anti-Communist.

name: Robert Crafton III
headline: Robert Crafton III, Bassist and Rapper, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. Crafton, known as Chilly B, was a bassist, songwriter and rapper whose rhythms and rhymes helped the 1980s hip-hop group Newcleus redefine the sound of electro-pop.

name: Modesto Cartagena
headline: Modesto Cartagena, Hero of Korea, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Fighting in an Army regiment made up almost entirely of Puerto Rican soldiers, Mr. Cartagena helped win victories over discrimination as well as Communist troops.

name: Thomas H. Pigford
headline: Thomas H. Pigford, Nuclear Engineer, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Dr. Pigford was recruited by the federal government for his advice on major nuclear accidents and nuclear waste.

name: Robert T. McCall
headline: Robert T. McCall, Space Artist, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. McCall was an artist whose fervor for space exploration found expression in his six-story-tall mural at the National Air and Space Museum and two postage stamps canceled on the Moon.

name: Andrew Jaffe
headline: Andrew Jaffe, Who Brought Clios to Adweek, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Mr. Jaffe presided over the expansion of the advertising trade magazine and helped revitalize the industry’s awards for excellence.

name: Raimund Abraham
headline: Raimund Abraham, Architect With Vision, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Abraham influenced a generation of architectural students as much through his insistence on the socially ennobling role of architecture, and its integrity as a discipline, as through his work.

name: Ruth Kligman
headline: Ruth Kligman, Muse and Artist, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Kligman was an abstract painter, who was known less for her own work than for her role as a muse, lover, friend and subject of an impressive number of American artists.

name: Bob Biniak
headline: Bob Biniak, a Member of Skateboarding’s Z-Boys, Dies at 51
abstract: Biniak was part of a rebellious wave of surfers in the 1970s who transformed the competitive sport of skateboarding.

name: Henri Salmide
profession: Germans Defiance Saved a French Port
headline: Henri Salmide, 90, Dies; German’s Defiance Saved a French Port
abstract: Mr. Salmide was a former German naval officer who defied orders to blow up the French port of Bordeaux.

name: Patricia Travers
headline: Patricia Travers, Violinist Who Vanished, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Travers was a child prodigy who appeared with many of the world’s leading orchestras, but left the spotlight from the early 1950s until her death.

name: Philip Langridge
headline: Philip Langridge, British Operatic Tenor, Dies at 70
abstract: At the height of his powers, Mr. Langridge produced a warm tone with a richness and flexibility he used astutely in complex, emotionally charged roles as well as in comic parts.

name: Aaron Cohen
headline: Aaron Cohen, Official and Engineer With NASA, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Cohen worked on the Apollo moon program, the space shuttles and the space station during a 30-year career with the agency.

name: Mark Linkous
headline: Mark Linkous, Leader of Sparklehorse Band, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. Linkous was a singer and songwriter whose music was renowned in indie-rock and alt-country circles for its haunted, allusive themes and fragile beauty.

name: Frank Williams
headline: Frank Williams, Architect of Skyscrapers, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Williams was the lead architect or collaborated with other prominent designers on 20 buildings in Manhattan.

name: Frank Williams
headline: Frank Williams, Dominant Formula 1 Manager, Is Dead at 79
abstract: He overcame frequent adversity, including a near-fatal car accident, to become one of the most successful figures in motorsports history.

name: Nan Martin
profession: Actress Known for Her Strong Roles
headline: Nan Martin, an Actress Known for Her Strong Roles, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Martin was a veteran stage, television and film actress whose Broadway credits include “J.B.” and “Under the Yum-Yum Tree” and who played Ali McGraw’s snooty mother in the film “Goodbye, Columbus.”

name: Barton Childs
headline: Dr. Barton Childs, Who Studied Inherited Diseases, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Dr. Childs helped shape the understanding of inherited diseases as scientists learned more about so-called inborn errors of metabolism, biochemistry and molecular biology.

name: David Kimche
profession: Israeli Adept as Spy and Diplomat
headline: David Kimche, an Israeli Adept as Spy and Diplomat, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Kimche was involved in some of the country’s most delicate foreign escapades, including the Iran-contra affair.

name: Willie Davis
headline: Willie Davis Is Dead at 69; Was Snider’s Successor
abstract: Mr. Davis, known for his blazing speed, led the National League in triples twice and set a record of three stolen bases in a World Series game.

name: Willie Davis
headline: Willie Davis, Packers Hall of Famer, Is Dead at 85
abstract: In his 10 seasons with Green Bay, as its defensive anchor, he helped the team win three N.F.L. championships and the first two Super Bowls.

name: Henry Wittenberg
headline: Henry Wittenberg, Champion Wrestler, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Wittenberg was an Olympic gold and silver medalist who had an undefeated streak of more than 300 matches and was one of the first wrestlers to lift weights.

name: John Thorbjarnarson
headline: John Thorbjarnarson, a Crocodile and Alligator Expert, Is Dead at 52
abstract: Mr. Thorbjarnarson was a scientist with wide interests in saving and learning about many species.

name: Bruce J. Graham
headline: Bruce J. Graham, Chicago Architect Who Designed Sears Tower, Dies at 84
abstract: Known for his integration of modernist design and sophisticated engineering in buildings, Mr. Graham played a role in changing Chicago’s skyline.

name: Edgar Wayburn
headline: Edgar Wayburn, a Leader in Saving the Wilderness, Dies at 103
abstract: Dr. Wayburn became a major figure in the conservation movement, leading campaigns that preserved more than 100 million wild acres.

name: Mohamed Sayed Tantawi
headline: Mohamed Sayed Tantawi, Top Cleric, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Tantawi was leader of Al Azhar University, the oldest and most prestigious center of learning in the Sunni Muslim world.

name: Corey Haim
headline: Corey Haim, Actor, Dies at 38
abstract: Mr. Haim was an actor whose status as a teenage heartthrob of the 1980s gave way to substance abuse and rehabilitation as an adult.

name: Merlin Olsen
headline: Merlin Olsen, Football Star, Commentator and Actor, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Olsen was a Hall of Fame tackle who anchored the Los Angeles Rams’ Fearsome Foursome, the line that glamorized defensive play in the N.F.L.

name: Johnny Alf
headline: Johnny Alf, a ‘Father of Bossa Nova,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Alf was an influential Brazilian songwriter, pianist and singer whose delicately swinging music was a precursor to the bossa nova.

name: Doris Haddock
headline: Doris Haddock Is Dead at 100; Walked for Campaign Finance Reform
abstract: Known as Granny D, Mrs. Haddock trekked 3,200 miles at age 89, and at 94 ran for the Senate from New Hampshire.

name: Carl E. Taylor
headline: Carl E. Taylor, Leader in Global Health Care, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Dr. Taylor conducted research in more than 70 countries and helped establish international health as a distinct academic field in the United States.

name: Richard Stites
headline: Richard Stites, Historian of Russian Culture, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Stites opened up new territory for historians with a landmark work on the Russian women’s movement.

name: Marilyn Gittell
headline: Marilyn Gittell, Advocate for Local School Decisions, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Gittell was a political scientist and education reformer who in the 1960s was an outspoken advocate of decentralizing New York City’s public school system.

name: Andrée Peel
headline: Andrée Peel, Rescuer of Allied Airmen, Dies at 105
abstract: Mrs. Peel was a highly decorated French resistance figure who helped save dozens of American and British airmen shot down over France during World War II.

name: Kenneth Dover
profession: Provocative Scholar of Ancient Greek Literature
headline: Kenneth Dover, a Provocative Scholar of Ancient Greek Literature, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Dover became known for his willingness to break taboos, from his frank descriptions of sexual behavior to his baldly stated desire to bring about the death of a vexing Oxford colleague.

name: Peter Graves
headline: Peter Graves, ‘Mission: Impossible’ Star, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Graves, the television spymaster and the host of the “Biography” series, also successfully spoofed his own gravitas in the “Airplane” movie farces.

name: Robert Carter
headline: Robert Carter, Priest and Gay Activist, Dies at 82
abstract: Father Carter, a professor and social worker, helped establish the National Gay and Lesbian Task Force and the New York chapter of DignityUSA.

name: Robert L. Carter
headline: Robert L. Carter, an Architect of School Desegregation, Dies at 94
abstract: Before Mr. Carter was a federal judge, he played a significant role in Brown v. Board of Education, the case that led the Supreme Court to abolish school segregation.

name: Arnall Patz
headline: Arnall Patz, a Doctor Who Prevented Blindness, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Doctors used to think they were helping premature babies by giving them a lot of oxygen. Dr. Patz proved they were hurting them.

name: Charles Moore
headline: Charles Moore, Rights-Era Photographer, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Moore braved physical peril to capture searing images that many credit with helping to propel landmark civil rights legislation.

name: Der Scutt
headline: Der Scutt, Modernist Architect, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Scutt was best known for whetting Donald Trump’s appetite for mirrored glass boxes, such as his design for Trump Tower.

name: Ron Lundy
headline: Ron Lundy, a Rock D.J. in New York, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Mr. Lundy’s Southern drawl projected good cheer on WABC and WCBS for decades.

name: Tim Holland
headline: Tim Holland, Backgammon Master, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Holland was widely considered the world’s greatest player during the game’s modern heyday, in the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Carmen Capalbo
headline: Carmen Capalbo, Theater Director, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Capalbo was a theater director and producer whose revival of “The Threepenny Opera” in the 1950s became one of the biggest hits in Off Broadway history.

name: Arthur H. Christy
headline: Arthur H. Christy, Special Prosecutor, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Christy investigated drug accusations against President Jimmy Carter’s chief of staff, but found no basis to the claims.

name: H. M. Koutoukas
headline: H. M. Koutoukas, Author of Surrealist Plays, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Koutoukas was a prolific playwright who helped create Off Off Broadway theater in the 1960s with a wildly surreal style of drama.

name: Miguel Delibes
headline: Miguel Delibes, Prolific Spanish Writer, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Delibes was a prolific and much-honored Spanish novelist who explored human nature through the lives of common folk living in the rich Castilian countryside.

name: Wayne Collett
profession: Track Medalist Barred Because of a Protest
headline: Wayne Collett, Track Medalist Barred Because of a Protest, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Collett was judged to have acted disrespectfully during a medal ceremony at the 1972 Olympics and was barred for life.

name: Fess Parker
profession: as Davy Crockett Set Off Coonskin Cap Craze
headline: Fess Parker, Who as Davy Crockett Set Off Coonskin Cap Craze, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Parker’s television portrayal of the American frontiersman Davy Crockett catapulted him to stardom in the mid-1950s.

name: Alex Chilton
headline: Alex Chilton, Influential Rock Singer, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Chilton was a mercurial rock musician whose work ranged from the soul songs of the Box Tops to the multiple incarnations of his pop band Big Star.

name: Charles Muscatine
headline: Charles Muscatine, Chaucer Scholar, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Muscatine was a scholar who transformed Chaucer studies by turning attention to the French models for Chaucer’s poetry and an education reformer.

name: Jane Sherman
headline: Jane Sherman, Dancer and Writer, Dies at 101
abstract: Ms. Sherman was a writer who not only chronicled the excitement of early-20th-century American dance but also lived through it as a performer.

name: Albert J. Rosenthal
headline: Albert J. Rosenthal, Columbia Law Dean, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Rosenthal helped to increase the number of women on the faculty during his stewardship of the school in the 1970s and 1980s.

name: Liz Carpenter
headline: Liz Carpenter,  Journalist, Feminist and Johnson Aide, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Carpenter spent much of her life working in Washington as a newspaper reporter, an aide to Lyndon B. Johnson and press secretary to Lady Bird Johnson.

name: Charlie Gillett
headline: Charlie Gillett, Disc Jockey and Historian, Dies at 68
abstract: As a broadcaster, journalist, author and musicologist, Mr. Gillett strove to bring deeper, broader dimensions to people’s appreciation of popular music.

name: Edmund Dinis
headline: Edmund Dinis,  Prosecutor in Chappaquiddick Case, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Dinis was accused of a less-than-vigorous prosecution of Senator Edward M. Kennedy in the 1969 accident in Chappaquiddick, Mass.

name: Stewart L. Udall
profession: Conservationist in Kennedy and Johnson Cabinets
headline: Stewart L. Udall, Conservationist in Kennedy and Johnson Cabinets, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Udall was the interior secretary in the 1960s who presided over vast increases in national park holdings and the public domain.

name: Girija Prasad Koirala
headline: Girija Prasad Koirala, Former Nepal Premier, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Koirala was a pivotal figure in establishing Nepal’s fragile democracy who also helped broker an end to the country’s Maoist rebellion.

name: Jerry Adler
headline: Jerry Adler, Harmonica Virtuoso, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Adler’s pure, open sound can be heard on the soundtracks to “Shane,” “High Noon,” “Mary Poppins” and other films.

name: Jerry Adler
headline: Jerry Adler, ‘Sopranos’ Actor Who Found Success Late in Life, Dies at 96
abstract: After years on Broadway in behind-the-scenes jobs, he had transformed into an actor late in life, in films and on television shows including “The Good Wife” and “Rescue Me.”

name: James Black
headline: Dr. James Black, Pharmacologist Who Discovered Beta Blockers, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Black was a Scottish pharmacologist whose discovery of beta blockers and another class of drugs extended the lives of millions of people with heart and stomach disorders.

name: Wolfgang Wagner
headline: Wolfgang Wagner, Director of Bayreuth, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Wagner was an opera director and impresario who for more than half a century ran Bayreuth, the international music festival conceived by his grandfather, Richard Wagner.

name: Robert M. White
headline: Robert M. White, Who Broke Limits in Flight, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. White played an important role in the development of manned spaceflight as the first pilot to fly a winged craft into outer space.

name: Robert E. White
headline: Robert E. White, Ex-Ambassador to Latin America, Dies at 88
abstract: He fought for justice on behalf of four churchwomen who were abducted, raped and murdered in El Salvador.

name: Robert M. White
headline: Robert M. White, Who Revolutionized Weather Forecasts, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. White, a meteorologist, was the first person to lead the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and warned of climate change long before it was widely recognized.

name: Robert White
headline: Robert White, Tenor Renowned for Irish Ballads, Dies at 89
abstract: A performer from childhood, he became a versatile singer in the mold of the Irish superstar John McCormack, adept at both classical repertoire and traditional songs.

name: Harold W. McGraw Jr.
headline: Harold W. McGraw Jr., Publisher, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. McGraw, as leader of McGraw-Hill, his family’s publishing business, helped build it into a billion-dollar enterprise.

name: Cherie DeCastro
headline: Cherie DeCastro, Singer With DeCastro Sisters, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Ms. DeCastro was the last surviving member of the DeCastro Sisters, whose sultry ballad “Teach Me Tonight” was a hit in 1954.

name: Sid Fleischman
headline: Sid Fleischman, Children’s Author, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Fleischman was a Newbery Award-winning author, who never set out to write for children but flung himself into the field on a dare.

name: Robert Culp
headline: Robert Culp, Star in ‘I Spy,’ Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Culp teamed with Bill Cosby as a secret agent in the hit 1960s television series “I Spy” and starred in the 1969 film “Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice.”

name: Midge Costanza
headline: Midge Costanza, a Top Assistant to Carter, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Costanza’s habit of criticizing her boss and her fractious relations with his advisers led her to resign after less than two years on the job.

name: Jim Marshall
headline: Jim Marshall, Rock ’n’ Roll Photographer, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Marshall was a photographer whose images of Jimi Hendrix, the Rolling Stones and others in the 1960s and ’70s helped define their subjects as well as rock ’n’ roll photography itself.

name: Jim Marshall
headline: Jim Marshall, Maker of Famed Fuzzy Amplifiers, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Marshall was asked by Pete Townshend to make something “bigger and louder,” and generations of guitarists have bought it.

name: Jim Marshall
profession: Iron Man Defensive End for the Vikings
headline: Jim Marshall, Iron Man Defensive End for the Vikings, Dies at 87
abstract: Part of Minnesota’s famed unit the Purple People Eaters, he started a record 270 consecutive games. Also famously, he once scooped up a fumble and ran to the wrong end zone.

name: Richard Engquist
headline: Richard Engquist, ‘Kuni-Leml’ Lyricist, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Mr. Engquist was a writer and editor, whose deft, witty way with a lyric sparked the Off Broadway musicals “Kuni-Leml” and “Little Ham.”

name: Vivian Blake
headline: Vivian Blake, 54, Founder of Jamaica Drug Gang, Dies
abstract: United States prosecutors say he was responsible for more than 1,400 drug-related killings in the country in the 1980s.

name: Johnny Maestro
headline: Johnny Maestro, Brooklyn Bridge Singer, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Maestro was the pure-toned tenor who was the lead singer for the Crests, the Del-Satins and the Brooklyn Bridge.

name: Chet Simmons
headline: Chet Simmons, a Founding Force of ESPN, Dies at 81
abstract: Before ESPN, Mr. Simmons was an NBC executive; after ESPN, he became the first commissioner of the United States Football League.

name: Harry Carpenter
headline: Harry Carpenter, the ‘Voice of Boxing’ in Britain, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Carpenter was a BBC sportscaster who announced some of the biggest fights in boxing’s history, including the “Rumble in the Jungle” in 1974.

name: Alberto Arroyo
headline: Alberto Arroyo, Jogger Familiar in Central Park, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Arroyo, known as the mayor of Central Park, circled one of its landmarks 10 times a day at the height of his conditioning.

name: Arnold Forster
headline: Arnold Forster, Who Fought Anti-Semitism With B’nai B’rith, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Mr. Forster was an American Jewish leader, lawyer and writer and a longtime executive of the Anti-Defamation League.

name: Donald P. Kelly
headline: Donald P. Kelly, Master of Leveraged Buyouts, Dies at 88
abstract: After helping engineer the leveraged buyout of the Beatrice Companies in 1987, Mr. Kelly became its chairman and presided over the lucrative sale of its assets.

name: Elinor Smith
profession: One of the Youngest Pioneers of Aviation
headline: Elinor Smith, One of the Youngest Pioneers of Aviation, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Elinor Smith was a pioneering female aviator who broke records, did daredevil stunts and made headlines as the “The Flying Flapper of Freeport.”

name: Ai
profession: Steadfast Poetic Channel of Hard Lives
headline: Ai, a Steadfast Poetic Channel of Hard Lives, Dies at 62
abstract: The poet Ai’s work — known for its raw power, jagged edges and unflinching examination of violence and despair — stood as a damning indictment of American society.

name: Blanche Thebom
profession: Star at the Met and Beyond
headline: Blanche Thebom, Star at the Met and Beyond, Dies at 94
abstract: Discovered in a ship’s lounge, Ms. Thebom went on to play the Met over 350 times.

name: Vasily Smyslov
headline: Vasily Smyslov, Former World Chess Champion, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Smyslov, who held the championship for just a year, was known for both the artistry of his play and the solidity of his technique.

name: Cliff Livingston
profession: Key Part of Giants in 1950s and 60s
headline: Cliff Livingston, Key Part of Giants in 1950s and ’60s, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Livingston, the former U.C.L.A. star, played in four National Football League championship games for the Giants in the 1950s and 1960s.

name: Donald N. Frey
headline: Donald N. Frey, Designer of the Mustang, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Frey was the force behind a car that was spunky and affordable. Not to mention that cool horse.

name: June Havoc
headline: June Havoc, Actress Who Outgrew Tyranny of Her ‘Momma Rose,’ Dies
abstract: Ms. Havoc, who first appeared on vaudeville stages when she was 2 as Baby, saw her accomplishments overshadowed by the fictionalized portrayal of her in “Gypsy.”

name: Charles Ryskamp
headline: Charles Ryskamp, Director of Morgan and Frick, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Ryskamp, a literary scholar and art collector, was the director of two of New York’s most prestigious small museums, the Pierpont Morgan Library and the Frick Collection, for nearly 30 years.

name: Herb Ellis
headline: Herb Ellis, Jazz Guitarist, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Ellis was a jazz guitarist whose blues-inflected playing earned him critical acclaim as a soloist and recognition as a member of the pianist Oscar Peterson’s trio.

name: Dan L. Duncan
headline: Dan L. Duncan, Oil Billionaire, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Duncan was an oilman known for his philanthropy and global hunting of exotic animals.

name: Edmund P. Pillsbury
headline: Edmund P. Pillsbury, Director at Kimbell, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Pillsbury added a string of European masterpieces to the collection of the Kimbell Museum in Fort Worth.

name: Dick Giordano
headline: Dick Giordano, Comic Book Artist, Dies at 77
abstract: The artist and former executive editor at DC Comics helped revive aging comic book characters and reimagine them for new audiences.

name: David Mills
headline: David Mills, Television Writer and Producer, Dies at 48
abstract: Mr. Mills was a former journalist who explored race relations and racial tensions as an Emmy-winning television writer for dramas like “NYPD Blue” and “The Wire.”

name: David L. Mills
profession: Kept the Internet Running on Time
headline: David L. Mills, Who Kept the Internet Running on Time, Dies at 85
abstract: He developed and implemented the protocol that synchronizes the digital clocks nestled within billions of networked devices.

name: Mortimer D. Sackler
headline: Mortimer D. Sackler, Arts Patron, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Sackler was a doctor who made his fortune with the company behind OxyContin. He was also known for his lavish gifts to New York museums.

name: Jaime Escalante
headline: Jaime Escalante, Inspiration for a Movie, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Escalante was the high school teacher whose ability to turn out high-achieving calculus students from a poor Hispanic neighborhood in East Los Angeles inspired the 1988 film “Stand and Deliver.”

name: Peter Gowland
headline: Peter Gowland, Pinup Photographer and Author, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Gowland used a camera, sunshine and imagination to portray ravishing women at a time when the pinup girl was a nearly ubiquitous fixture of American life.

name: Susan Tifft
headline: Susan Tifft, Chronicler of News Dynasties, Is Dead at 59
abstract: Ms. Tifft wrote sweeping histories of two newspaper dynasties in collaboration with her husband, Alex S. Jones.

name: John Bunch
headline: John Bunch, Pianist With Goodman and Bennett, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Bunch, who transitioned from swing to bebop, was a prominent sideman for Benny Goodman and Tony Bennett.

name: J.F. terHorst
headline: J.F. terHorst, Ford Press Secretary, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. terHorst was appointed White House press secretary by President Gerald R. Ford, but resigned shortly after Mr. Ford granted former President Richard M. Nixon a pardon in connection with the Watergate scandal.

name: John Forsythe
headline: John Forsythe, ‘Dynasty’ Actor, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Forsythe starred in three television series, as Bentley Gregg on “Bachelor Father,” as the sexy telephone voice of Charlie in “Charlie’s Angels” and as Blake Carrington in “Dynasty.”

name: H. Edward Roberts
headline: H. Edward Roberts, PC Pioneer, Dies at 68
abstract: Dr. Roberts made an early contribution to modern computing and was a mentor to Bill Gates.

name: Kit Horn
headline: Kit Horn, Pioneer Surfer, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Horn’s exploration of new surf spots along the California coast in the 1940s and 1950s helped the sport grow from a subculture to an international pastime.

name: Harriet Shetler
profession: Helped to Found Mental Illness Group
headline: Harriet Shetler, Who Helped to Found Mental Illness Group, Dies at 92
abstract: Mrs. Shetler, whose son had schizophrenia, helped start the National Alliance on Mental Illness, which now has affiliates in every state.

name: Burton Joseph
headline: Burton Joseph, Lawyer in First Amendment Cases, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Joseph, a civil liberties lawyer in Chicago, took on tough cases like the one involving Nazis’ right to march through a largely Jewish area.

name: David Slivka
headline: David Slivka, a Sculptor and Painter, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Slivka was one of the last living members of the New York school of Abstract Expressionists.

name: Mike Cuellar
headline: Mike Cuellar, Star Pitcher for Orioles, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Cuellar was part of a Baltimore starting staff that had four 20-game winners in 1971.

name: Mike Zwerin
headline: Mike Zwerin, Jazz Critic and Author, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Zwerin was a jazz trombonist, but it was as a critic and author that he made his mark on jazz.

name: John G. McCoy
headline: John G. McCoy, Innovator in Banking, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. McCoy transformed the smallest bank in Columbus, Ohio, into a national powerhouse.

name: Clifford Hardin
headline: Clifford Hardin, Who Cut Subsidies at Agriculture Dept., Dies at 94
abstract: As secretary during the Nixon administration, Mr. Hardin succeeded in limiting subsidy payments to the nation’s largest farmers.

name: Wilma Mankiller
profession: Cherokee Chief and First Woman to Lead Major Tribe
headline: Wilma Mankiller, Cherokee Chief and First Woman to Lead Major Tribe, Is Dead at 64
abstract: Ms. Mankiller was a groundbreaking leader who put her focus on education, health and housing.

name: Corin Redgrave
headline: Corin Redgrave, Actor and Activist, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Redgrave, a versatile actor and ardent left-wing political activist, was the prince of the royal family of English theater.

name: Philippe Braunschweig
headline: Philippe Braunschweig, Prix de Lausanne Founder, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Braunschweig, the heir to a Swiss watchmaking fortune, founded the innovative and prestigious Prix de Lausanne ballet competition for young dancers.

name: Nancy Paterson
headline: Nancy Paterson, Who Aided in Milosevic Investigation, Dies at  56
abstract: Ms. Paterson was an international war crimes prosecutor who played a leading role in building the case linking the former Yugoslav president to massacres, mass rape and ethnic cleansing in the Balkans in the 1990s.

name: Coots Matthews
headline: Coots Matthews, Cantankerous Hellfighter, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Matthews was a legend, like his colleague Red Adair, in the perilous art of detonating dynamite in oil well infernos to starve the fire of oxygen.

name: Morris Jeppson
headline: Morris Jeppson, Airman Who Flew on the Enola Gay, Dies at 87
abstract: In his only combat flight, Lieutenant Jeppson checked the atomic bomb before it was dropped on Hiroshima.

name: Anatoly F. Dobrynin
profession: Longtime Soviet Ambassador to the U.S
headline: Anatoly F. Dobrynin, Longtime Soviet Ambassador to the U.S., Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Dobrynin, the Soviet ambassador to the U.S. from 1962 to 1986, worked with six American presidents and served a crucial role during the Cuban missile crisis.

name: Malcolm McLaren
headline: Malcolm McLaren, Seminal Punk Figure, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. McLaren was an impresario, recording artist and fashion designer who, as the Sex Pistols’s manager, played a decisive role in creating the British punk movement.

name: Christopher Cazenove
headline: Christopher Cazenove, Suave British Actor, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Cazenove was a British actor best known to American audiences as Ben Carrington, the scheming brother of Blake Carrington on the ABC prime-time soap opera “Dynasty.”

name: Graciela Peréz-Gutierrez
headline: Graciela Peréz-Gutierrez, Afro-Cuban Singer, Dies at 94
abstract: One of the great voices in Afro-Cuban music, Graciela, as she was known, helped establish a high standard for the mambo orchestra.

name: J. Bruce Llewellyn
profession: Forged a Path for Blacks in Business
headline: J. Bruce Llewellyn, Who Forged a Path for Blacks in Business, Is Dead at 82
abstract: A leader in communications, banking and bottling, Mr. Llewellyn was among the nation’s most prominent and wealthiest black executives.

name: Meinhardt Raabe
headline: Meinhardt Raabe, Famous Munchkin, Is Dead at 94
abstract: The actor’s life was shaped by 13 seconds spent on screen in “The Wizard of Oz.”

name: Abel Muzorewa
headline: Abel Muzorewa, Cleric and Politician in Zimbabwe, Dies at 85
abstract: Bishop Muzorewa enjoyed fleeting fame as prime minister of the short-lived Zimbabwe-Rhodesia.

name: Robert D. Franks
headline: Robert D. Franks, G.O.P. Leader in New Jersey, Is Dead at 58
abstract: Mr. Franks reinvigorated the Republican Party in New Jersey and came close to defeating Jon S. Corzine for the United States Senate in 2000.

name: Victor Pesce
headline: Victor Pesce, Painter of Minimalist Still Lifes, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Pesce, the son of Italian immigrants and a plumber by trade, built his art career slowly and quietly, and came into his own as an artist during his early 50s.

name: Arthur Mercante Sr.
headline: Arthur Mercante Sr., Hall of Fame Boxing Referee, Dies at 90
abstract: Mercante was a presence at more than 140 championship bouts, and his son Arthur Mercante Jr. was also a well-known referee.

name: Dixie Carter
headline: Dixie Carter, TV Actress, Dies at 70
abstract: The actress who gave strong, Southern women a good name in the television series “Designing Women,” later enjoyed success as a cabaret singer.

name: Craig Noel
headline: Craig Noel, a Force in Regional Theater, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Noel was the man who transformed a small local playhouse into the theatrical powerhouse known as the Old Globe.

name: Anna Walentynowicz
headline: Anna Walentynowicz, Polish Provocateur Who Spurred Communism’s Fall, Dies at 80
abstract: Mrs. Walentynowicz was a retired labor leader whose firing as a crane operator at a shipyard in Gdansk touched off the strike that led to the unraveling of Communism in Poland.

name: George Nissen
headline: George Nissen, Father of the Trampoline, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Nissen devoted his life to promoting and manufacturing the trampoline — a device enjoyed by backyard tumblers, fitness freaks and Olympic athletes.

name: Nina Bourne
headline: Nina Bourne Is Dead at 93; Catapulted Sales of ‘Catch-22’
abstract: Ms. Bourne was a poet whose punchy copy made many a best seller, including the “Eloise” books and “The Chosen.”

name: H. G. Stever
headline: H. G. Stever, Who Advised Leaders on Science, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Stever was the chief science adviser to two presidents and the head of the committee that monitored the redesign of the space shuttle’s booster rockets after the Challenger disaster.

name: Fred Ascani
headline: Fred Ascani, Who Flew Supersonic Jets, Is Dead at 92
abstract: General Ascani’s long career as an Air Force test pilot followed a wartime record of 52 bombing missions over Europe.

name: John Schoenherr
headline: John Schoenherr, Children’s Book Illustrator, Dies at 74
abstract: A highly regarded nature artist, Mr. Schoenherr was a Caldecott Medal-winning illustrator who painted images for more than 40 children’s titles.

name: Helen Ranney
headline: Helen Ranney, Pioneer in Sickle Cell Research, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Ranney was a hematologist whose experiments in the 1950s elucidated the genetic basis of sickle cell disease.

name: Benjamin L. Hooks
headline: Benjamin L. Hooks, Civil Rights Leader, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Hooks was a Baptist minister, a criminal court judge and the leader of the  N.A.A.C.P. for 16 years.

name: Daryl F. Gates
profession: L.A.P.D. Chief in Rodney King Era
headline: Daryl F. Gates, L.A.P.D. Chief in Rodney King Era, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Gates’s aggressive approach in a period of intense urban turmoil was admired for its innovation and criticized for the racial unrest it provoked.

name: Antony Flew
headline: Antony Flew, Philosopher and Ex-Atheist, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Flew was an English philosopher and outspoken atheist who stunned and dismayed the unbelieving faithful when he announced in 2004 that God probably did exist.

name: Rasim Delic
headline: Rasim Delic, Bosnian Army Commander, Dies at 61
abstract: General Delic commanded Bosnia’s army during much of the catastrophic ethnic war in the former Yugoslavia in the 1990s.

name: David Simons
profession: Flew High on Eve of Space Age
headline: David Simons, Who Flew High on Eve of Space Age, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Simons, a physician turned Air Force officer, had sent animals aloft for several years before his record-breaking flight.

name: James Aubrey
profession: Portrayed the Hero in Lord of the Flies
headline: James Aubrey, Who Portrayed the Hero in ‘Lord of the Flies’, Is Dead at 62
abstract: Mr. Aubrey portrayed Ralph in the film version of the William Golding novel and had a busy career on stage and television in England.

name: Michel Chartrand
profession: Fiery Labor Union Leader in Quebec
headline: Michel Chartrand, Fiery Labor Union Leader in Quebec, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Mr. Chartrand was a firebrand whose support of leftist politics and Quebec nationalism landed him in jail and buoyed a radical separatist group.

name: James Masterson
headline: James Masterson,  Narcissism Expert, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Masterson, who helped inaugurate a new approach to the study and treatment of personality disorders, was a psychiatrist for those who needed the best (or thought they did).

name: Dede Allen
headline: Dede Allen, Pioneering Film Editor, Dies at 86
abstract: On films like “Reds” and “Dog Day Afternoon,” Ms. Allen revolutionized imagery, sound and stories with her cutting-edge style.

name: Carolyn Rodgers
headline: Carolyn Rodgers, Poet, Is Dead at 69
abstract: Ms. Rodgers, a leading voice of the Black Arts Movement of the 1960s and ’70s, wove feminism, black militancy and spirituality into her work.

name: Alejandro Robaina
headline: Alejandro Robaina, Grower for Top Cuban Cigars, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Robaina achieved cult status among smokers worldwide for the silken leaves that wrapped cigars known for their smoothness and richness.

name: Robert Pound
headline: Robert Pound, Physicist Whose Work Advanced Medicine, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Professor Pound was a Harvard physicist and tinkerer who built devices that helped him probe the workings of the atom.

name: Dorothy Height
profession: Largely Unsung Giant of the Civil Rights Era
headline: Dorothy Height, Largely Unsung Giant of the Civil Rights Era, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Height was a national leader in the civil rights and women’s movements for decades, but she was rarely in the news media spotlight.

name: Ralph Snodsmith
headline: Ralph Snodsmith, 70, Gardening Expert, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Snodsmith, the longtime host of the Sunday morning radio show “The Garden Hotline,” shared his knowledge and his sense of humor.

name: Werner Schroeter
headline: Werner Schroeter, German Film and Stage Director, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Schroeter’s flair for lush visuals and heightened emotions introduced an operatic sensibility to the New German Cinema movement of the 1970s.

name: Guru
headline: Guru, Rapper Known for Social Themes, Dies at 48
abstract: Guru was one of the most expressive rappers of the 1990s and a major figure in bridging hip-hop and jazz.

name: Arnold Spohr
profession: Former Artistic Director of Winnipeg Ballet
headline: Arnold Spohr, Former Artistic Director of Winnipeg Ballet, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Spohr propelled a small Canadian ballet troupe on the prairie onto the world stage.

name: Juan Antonio Samaranch
headline: Juan Antonio Samaranch, Who Transformed the Olympics, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Samaranch guided the Olympic movement for over two decades from tough times to unprecedented success, despite a tenure tarnished by scandal.

name: C. K. Prahalad
headline: C. K. Prahalad, Proponent of Poor as Consumers, Dies at 68
abstract: The native of India advised executives on how to reach the poor as customers and improve the lives of impoverished people in developing countries.

name: John Carl Warnecke
headline: John Carl Warnecke, Architect to Kennedy, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Warnecke was the court architect of the Kennedy administration and the designer of John F. Kennedy’s grave site at Arlington National Cemetery.

name: Jean Vergnes
headline: Jean Vergnes, Who Helped Open Le Cirque, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Vergnes, a classically trained French chef with a jolly demeanor, cooked at restaurants favored by Manhattan’s elite.

name: M. Edgar Rosenblum
headline: M. Edgar Rosenblum, Who Grew the Long Wharf Theater, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Rosenblum was an arts executive who helped steer the Long Wharf Theater in New Haven to prominence in the American theater landscape.

name: Purvis Young
headline: Purvis Young, Folk Artist Who Peppered Miami With Images, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Young was often called an outsider artist or a street artist, and he lived a life that only intermittently surfaced on the art-world grid.

name: Robert Hicks
headline: Robert Hicks, Leader in Armed Rights Group, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Hicks was one of the last surviving leaders of the Deacons for Defense and Justice, a paramilitary organization formed to protect people from the Ku Klux Klan.

name: Robert Hicks
headline: Robert Hicks, Blockbuster Author and Battlefield Savior, Dies at 71
abstract: He published “The Widow of the South” to promote his real passion: reclaiming a Tennessee Civil War site’s complicated history.

name: Paul Schaefer
profession: German Guilty of Chile Child Abuse
headline: Paul Schaefer, German Guilty of Chile Child Abuse, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Schaefer was a former Nazi-era German soldier who founded a secretive German cult in southern Chile, where he sexually abused about 25 children.

name: Allison Stacey Cowles
headline: Allison Stacey Cowles, Educational Advocate, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Cowles, a longtime trustee of Wellesley College, was the wife of a newspaper publisher in Spokane, Wash., and, after he died, of the former publisher of The New York Times.

name: W. Willard Wirtz
headline: W. Willard Wirtz, Labor Chief, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Wirtz was the last surviving member of President John F. Kennedy’s cabinet, having served as his  labor secretary.

name: Alan Rich
headline: Alan Rich, Los Angeles Music Critic, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr.  Rich was a critic whose passionate writing about classical music in both New York and Los Angeles made him an important voice in the musical world.

name: Alan Sillitoe
headline: Alan Sillitoe, ‘Angry’ British Novelist, Dies at 82
abstract: Fiction from the late 1950s like “Saturday Night and Sunday Morning” and “The Loneliness of the Long Distance Runner” spoke of working-class alienation.

name: Melvyn Zerman
headline: Melvyn Zerman, Publisher of Performing Arts Books, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Zerman’s  Limelight Editions gave a second life to neglected classics on the performing arts by bringing them back in paperback.

name: Franklin Mieuli
headline: Franklin Mieuli, Offbeat N.B.A. Owner, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Mieuli owned the Golden State Warriors for nearly a quarter century and won a championship in 1975.

name: Alice Miller
profession: Laid Human Problems to Parental Acts
headline: Alice Miller, Psychoanalyst, Dies at 87; Laid Human Problems to Parental Acts
abstract: Dr. Miller’s first book, “The Drama of the Gifted Child,” was popular among mental health professionals and the general public.

name: Gene Lees
headline: Gene Lees, Jazz Critic and Historian, Dies at 82
abstract: The author of numerous books, Mr. Lees approached his subject with a journalist’s rigor and an insider’s understanding.

name: Allen Swift
profession: Voice Actor for Radio and TV
headline: Allen Swift, Voice Actor for Radio and TV, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Swift was the voice of Mighty Mouse and numerous characters both human and inanimate in countless television and radio commercials.

name: Elizabeth Post
headline: Elizabeth Post of the Etiquette Family Dies at 89
abstract: A New Jersey native who married the grandson of a celebrated American arbiter of taste, Mrs. Post updated “Etiquette” five times.

name: Arthur Winograd
headline: Arthur Winograd, Hartford Symphony Music Director, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Winograd, a cellist, was a founder of the Juilliard String Quartet and a longtime music director of the Hartford Symphony Orchestra.

name: Thomas H. Connell III
headline: Thomas H. Connell III, Longtime Met Stage Manager, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Connell spent the past three decades in a crucial job requiring the abilities of a musician, computer whiz, psychotherapist and animal wrangler.

name: Robert Natkin
headline: Robert Natkin, Abstract Painter, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Natkin gained prominence in the late 1960s and 1970s with paintings that blended Abstraction with Post-Impressionist colors.

name: F. E. Dominy
