profession: Harnessed Water in the American West
headline: F. E. Dominy, Who Harnessed Water in the American West, Is Dead at 100
abstract: Mr. Dominy, a child of the Dust Bowl, persuaded reluctant politicians to approve big, controversial dam projects.

name: Whitney Harris
headline: Whitney Harris, Nuremberg Prosecutor, Dies at 97
abstract: One of the last of the prosecutors who brought high-ranking Nazi war criminals to justice, a half-century later Mr. Harris was a significant voice in the creation of the International Criminal Court.

name: Evelyn Cunningham
headline: Evelyn Cunningham, Civil Rights Reporter, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Cunningham was a journalist who covered the birth of the 1960s civil rights movement and later served as an aide to Gov. Nelson A. Rockefeller of New York.

name: Leslie Buck
headline: Leslie Buck, Designer of Iconic Coffee Cup, Dies at 87
abstract: The Grecian design seems to have been here forever, as if bestowed on New York by the gods. But in fact, it was created by man.

name: Victoria Manalo Draves
headline: Victoria Manalo Draves, Olympic Champion Diver, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Draves overcame ethnic prejudice early in her career to become the first woman to win a gold medal in both the springboard and the platform in the 1948 Olympic Games.

name: Dorothy Provine
headline: Dorothy Provine, Shapely Actress in ’60s, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Provine was perhaps best known for her appearance in the Stanley Kramer movie “It’s a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World.”

name: Clare Sabatini
headline: Clare Sabatini Dies at 77; Beat Trump in Land Fight
abstract: Mrs. Sabatini, who owned Sabatini’s restaurant, next to one of Donald Trump’s casinos, fended off condemnation proceedings that would have given the casino her property by eminent domain.

name: Avigdor Arikha
headline: Avigdor Arikha, Artist of the Everyday, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Arikha, who found beauty and unease in simple things, painted from a perspective informed by the Holocaust.

name: Furio Scarpelli
headline: Furio Scarpelli, Screenwriter of Italian Comedies, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Scarpelli was known for both satirizing and celebrating the average Italian’s capacity for survival under adverse circumstances.

name: Angus Maddison
headline: Angus Maddison, Economic Historian, Dies at 83
abstract: Professor Maddison, a British-born economic historian with a compulsion for quantification, spent many years calculating the size of economies over the last three millenniums.

name: Walter Murphy
headline: Walter Murphy, Author and Princeton Political Scientist, Dies at 80
abstract: Professor Murphy was a leading constitutional scholar who also wrote a best-selling political thriller, “The Vicar of Christ.”

name: Cecil Sherman
profession: Led a Faction of Moderate Baptists
headline: Cecil Sherman, Who Led a Faction of Moderate Baptists, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Sherman was a leader of the moderate faction of Southern Baptists that broke away in 1990 after conservatives had cemented their control of the denomination.

name: Susan Reed
profession: Fleeting Star in a Folk Music Revival
headline: Susan Reed,  a Fleeting Star in a Folk Music Revival, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Ms. Reed was once hailed as “a leading voice in a rebirth of the genre,” but mostly walked away from performing after less than six years.

name: Giuseppe Panza
headline: Giuseppe Panza, Collector of Postwar American Art, Dies at 87
abstract: Count Panza made deals that greatly enhanced the holdings of several American museums.

name: Tomio Tada
profession: Influential Immunologist and Author of Japanese Plays
headline: Tomio Tada, Influential Immunologist and Author of Japanese Plays, Dies at 76
abstract: Dr. Tada rose to prominence for a series of experiments that pointed to the existence of suppressor cells, and later took up writing traditional Noh plays.

name: Joseph Sarno
headline: Joseph Sarno, Sexploitation Film Director, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Sarno was a cult film director who helped break down taboos against erotic content in American cinema.

name: G. Douglas Pugh
headline: G. Douglas Pugh, State Labor Official, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Pugh started his career as a campaigner for civil rights and then ascended through the ranks of New York State government to hold major posts in labor relations.

name: Lynn Redgrave
headline: Lynn Redgrave, Actress and Playwright, Dies at 67
abstract: A member of a British theatrical dynasty, Ms. Redgrave forged her own career in films like “Georgy Girl” and her own personal plays about her family.

name: Jean-Louis Dumas
headline: Jean-Louis Dumas, Chief of Hermès, Dies at 72
abstract: As chief executive starting in the late 1970s, Mr. Dumas revived and transformed the French fashion house by hiring exciting new designers and extending the company’s lines.

name: Patricia Rico
profession: Proponent of Womens Track and Field
headline: Patricia Rico, Proponent of Women’s Track and Field, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Rico, a track and field administrator for more than 50 years, was the president of USA Track and Field and pushed for women’s participation in the sport.

name: Helen Wagner
profession: Longtime Actress on As the World Turns
headline: Helen Wagner, Longtime Actress on ‘As the World Turns,’ Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Wagner played the old-fashioned character Nancy Hughes on “As the World Turns” from its very first episode in 1956.

name: Stanley I. Greenspan
headline: Stanley I. Greenspan, Developer of ‘Floor Time’ Teaching, Dies at 68
abstract: Dr. Greenspan was a psychiatrist who encouraged parents, teachers and therapists to participate in playtime as a gateway to learning for some children.

name: Moshe Hirsch
headline: Rabbi Moshe Hirsch, Israel Opponent, Dies at 86
abstract: Rabbi Hirsch led an Orthodox sect that believes that God and Jewish law forbids a Jewish state until the Messiah comes.

name: John Tarbell Jr.
headline: John Tarbell Jr., Bank Executive, Dies at 67
abstract: As a founder of the Chemical Bank’s mergers-and-acquisitions unit, Mr. Tarbell played a crucial role in several notable deals.

name: Ernie Harwell
headline: Ernie Harwell, Homespun Baseball Broadcaster, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Harwell announced more than 8,500 games, conveying warmth through a relaxed and humorous style.

name: Florencio Campomanes
headline: Florencio Campomanes, Chess Official, Dies at 83
abstract: As the leader of the World Chess Federation, Mr. Campomanes ended a title match between Garry Kasparov and Anatoly Karpov.

name: Robin Roberts
profession: Led Phillies Whiz Kids to Pennant
headline: Robin Roberts Dies at 83; Led Phillies’ Whiz Kids to Pennant
abstract: The Hall of Fame right-handed pitcher used a seemingly effortless motion to win 286 games in 19 major league seasons.

name: Max Palevsky
headline: Max Palevsky, a Pioneer in Computers, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Palevsky was the founder of Intel, art collector and a major contributor to Democratic presidential politics.

name: Giulietta Simionato
headline: Giulietta Simionato Dies at 99; A Top Italian Mezzo-Soprano
abstract: Ms. Simionato, who sang in both European and American opera houses, was a specialist in the Bel Canto repertory.

name: Walter Sear
profession: Audio Engineer With a Passion for Analog
headline: Walter Sear, an Audio Engineer With a Passion for Analog, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Sear’s steadfast devotion to pre-digital recording technology led him to maintain a studio with vintage analog equipment and to gain admiration from musicians.

name: Sheena Duncan
headline: Sheena Duncan, White Who Fought Apartheid, Dies at 77
abstract: Mrs. Duncan’s campaign to help blacks was far removed from a traditional role for a middle-class white woman.

name: Jan van der Marck
headline: Jan van der Marck, Museum Administrator, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. van der Marck, whose museum career was somewhat tumultuous, championed modern and contemporary art.

name: James Leeson Jr.
headline: James Leeson Jr. Dies at 79; Taped Execution Scene
abstract: As a student in 1951, Mr. Leeson described the crowd at a Southern courthouse where a black man was electrocuted for the rape of a white woman.

name: Walter Hickel
headline: Walter Hickel, Nixon Interior Secretary, Dies at 90
abstract: As governor of Alaska and U.S. secretary of the interior, Walter J. Hickel confounded critics by ricocheting from pro-business stalwart to ardent environmentalist.

name: Peter O’Donnell
headline: Peter O’Donnell, the Creator of Modesty Blaise, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. O’Donnell, a British writer of novels and comic strips, was best known for creating the seductive crime fighter Modesty Blaise.

name: Devra G. Kleiman
headline: Devra G. Kleiman, Biologist Who Helped Change Zoos, Is Dead at 67
abstract: The scientist’s work became the model for more than 100 breeding programs for endangered species and led to a Washington star: the panda cub Tai Shan.

name: Rhonda Copelon
headline: Rhonda Copelon, Lawyer in Groundbreaking Rights Cases, Dies at 65
abstract: Ms. Copelon played a major role in a case that helped establish that victims of human rights abuses abroad had recourse in United States courts.

name: Lena Horne
headline: Lena Horne, Singer and Actress, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Horne broke new ground for black performers in Hollywood, and she achieved international success in nightclubs and on records.

name: David E. Apter
headline: David E. Apter, Yale Political Scientist, Is Dead  at 85
abstract: Professor Apter wove his expertise in political science and sociology into influential treatises on the often-tortured birth of developing nations.

name: S. J. Ledogar
headline: S. J. Ledogar, Who Shaped Arms Treaties, Is Dead at 80
abstract: As a United States ambassador, Mr. Ledogar helped draft agreements that limited conventional, chemical and nuclear arms.

name: Stephen Rosenfeld
headline: Stephen Rosenfeld, Retired Columnist, Dies at 77
abstract: A Washington Post columnist and editorial writer who specialized in foreign affairs

name: Bob Mercer
headline: Bob Mercer, Executive Who Signed the Sex Pistols, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Mercer managed Paul McCartney and oversaw the American version of the CD compilation series “Now That’s What I Call Music!”

name: Nathan Serota
headline: Nathan Serota, Developer in Suburbs, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Serota  changed the face of suburban Long Island with shopping centers where farmland once stood.

name: Callie Angell
headline: Callie Angell, Authority on Warhol Films, Dies at 62
abstract: Ms. Angell spent nearly two decades researching, cataloging and restoring Warhol films, helping to preserve part of his artistic legacy.

name: Frank Frazetta
headline: Frank Frazetta, Illustrator, Dies at 82; Helped Define Comic Book Heroes
abstract: Mr. Frazetta’s images of fighting musclebound men helped define characters like Tarzan and Conan.

name: Stephen Ledogar
headline: Stephen Ledogar Dies at 80; Drafted Arms Pacts
abstract: Mr. Ledogar was a United States ambassador wo helped draft agreements that limited conventional, chemical and nuclear arms.

name: William Lubtchansky
headline: William Lubtchansky, Cinematographer, Is Dead at 72
abstract: Mr. Lubtchansky worked closely with some of Europe’s leading directors, including François Truffaut, Jean-Luc Godard, Jacques Rivette and Claude Lanzmann.

name: Andor Lilienthal
headline: Andor Lilienthal, a Chess Grandmaster, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Lilienthal, the last of the original 27 chess grandmasters, played 10 world champions and beat 6 of them.

name: Doris E. Travis
headline: Doris E. Travis, Last of the Ziegfeld Girls, Dies at 106
abstract: Mrs. Travis, who may have been the youngest Ziegfeld Girl ever, went on to perform in stage productions and films.

name: Dave Fisher
headline: Dave Fisher, Member of the Highwaymen, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Fisher joined with four other freshmen at Wesleyan University to form the folk band, which became one of the most popular groups of the early 1960s.

name: Inna H. Grade
headline: Inna H. Grade, Fierce Literary Guardian, Dies at 85
abstract: Mrs. Grade, a translator of the work of her husband, Chaim Grade, zealously guarded his legacy while attacking the reputation of a chief rival, Isaac Bashevis Singer.

name: Francisco Aguabella
headline: Francisco Aguabella, Percussionist Who Crossed Genres, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Aguabella was a Cuban-born master percussionist whose impeccable rhythmic sense and drive enriched the recordings and live performances of jazz, salsa and pop artists.

name: Dustin Shuler
headline: Dustin Shuler, Sculptor Known Best for ‘Spindle,’ Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Shuler was known for impaling things, flattening things and putting things on top of other things — often full-size automobiles.

name: Rob McConnell
headline: Rob McConnell, Musician and Big Band Leader, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. McConnell’s ensemble, the Boss Brass, was successful despite being formed in 1968, long after the heyday of big bands.

name: Charlie Francis
headline: Charlie Francis, Coach Linked to Steroids, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Francis was the Canadian coach who was unapologetic about his athletes’ use of performance-enhancing drugs, forcing Olympic officials to confront the problem.

name: Ron Fimrite
headline: Ron Fimrite, Stylish Sportswriter, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Fimrite, a master story teller, was a fixture at Sports Illustrated for more than 34 years and wrote several books.

name: Rosa Rio
profession: Organist From Silent Films to Soap Operas
headline: Rosa Rio, Organist From Silent Films to Soap Operas, Dies at 107
abstract: For eight decades — until her final performance, last year — Miss Rio built a career as one of the country’s premier theater organists.

name: Craig Kauffman
headline: Craig Kauffman, Sculptor in Plastic, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Kauffman helped put Los Angeles on the art map with audacious experiments in molding industrial plastic to create ethereal wall-mounted sculptures.

name: David Randolph
headline: David Randolph, Conductor of Many Fleet ‘Messiahs,’ Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Randolph, the first conductor of the Masterwork Chorus and the longtime director of the St. Cecilia Chorus, led about 170 performances of “Messiah.”

name: Bud Mahurin
headline: Bud Mahurin, Fighter Pilot in 2 Wars, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Mahurin was a leading fighter pilot in World War II (both theaters) and in the Korean War.

name: K. Dun Gifford
profession: Started Group to Promote Healthy Eating
headline: K. Dun Gifford Dies at 71;  Started Group to Promote Healthy Eating
abstract: Mr. Gifford had a well-connected life that put him in celebrated company and at the scenes of many newsmaking events.

name: Mildred E. Orton
headline: Mildred E. Orton, a Founder of Vermont Country Store, Is Dead at 99
abstract: Mrs. Orton and her husband ran a store full of old-fashioned goods and built a thriving mail-order business.

name: Richard LaMotta
profession: Creator of Chipwich Ice Cream Sandwich
headline: Richard LaMotta, Creator of Chipwich Ice Cream Sandwich, Dies at 67
abstract: With his invention, the Chipwich, Mr.  LaMotta unleashed a runaway success with children, and their ice cream vendors.

name: Deborah Remington
headline: Deborah Remington, Abstract Artist, Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. Remington, a cousin of Frederic Remington, applied classic techniques to modern imagery.

name: Ronnie James Dio
headline: Ronnie James Dio, Rock Vocalist, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Dio’s powerful, semioperatic vocal style and attachment to demonic imagery made him a mainstay of the heavy metal genre.

name: Giuliana Camerino
headline: Giuliana Camerino Is Dead at 89; Designed Coveted Handbags
abstract: Ms. Camerino was an Italian designer whose handbags, sold under the Roberta di Camerino label, were postwar objects of desire for the international jet set.

name: Edward Uhl
headline: Edward Uhl, Who Helped Invent Bazooka, Dies at 92
abstract: Serving in the Army’s Ordnance Corps in World War II, Mr. Uhl helped invent a shoulder-fired rocket launcher that became an effective weapon against enemy tanks.

name: Hank Jones
headline: Hank Jones, Versatile Jazz Pianist, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Jones spent much of his career in the background, then became a popular nightclub headliner around the time he turned 60.

name: Norman Hand
profession: Helped Saints to First Playoff Win
headline: Norman Hand, Who Helped Saints to First Playoff Win, Dies at 37
abstract: Mr. Hand, who played for five N.F.L. teams, helped the New Orleans Saints to their first playoff victory, in 2000.

name: Robert J. Serling
headline: Robert J. Serling, Aviation Writer, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Serling was known for the best-selling novel “The President’s Plane Is Missing,” published in 1967.

name: Oswaldo López Arellano
headline: Oswaldo López Arellano, 88, Two-Time Honduran President
abstract: Mr. López Arellano, a top military officer, helped lead a coup in 1956 and twice assumed the presidency in Honduras in the early 1970s.

name: Bernard Schoenbaum
headline: Bernard Schoenbaum, New Yorker Cartoonist, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Schoenbaum’s hundreds of New Yorker cartoons often depicted well-fed-looking figures in settings that would ring with familiarity to upper-middle-class sophisticates.

name: James E. Burnett Jr.
headline: James E. Burnett Jr. Dies at 62; Led Safety Board in 1980s
abstract: A former judge in Arkansas, Mr. Burnett led campaigns against drunken driving and drug and alcohol use by railroad workers.

name: Yvonne Loriod
headline: Yvonne Loriod, Pianist and Messiaen Muse, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Loriod was a pianist whose musical exactitude and intensity inspired numerous masterpieces by her husband, the composer Olivier Messiaen.

name: Moshe Greenberg
headline: Moshe Greenberg, Biblical Scholar, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Professor Greenberg, a winner of the Israel Prize, took the historical-critical approach to the Bible.

name: Arakawa
headline: Arakawa, Whose Art Tried to Halt Aging, Dies at 73
abstract: Arakawa was a Japanese-born conceptual artist and designer, who with his wife, Madeline Gins, explored ideas about mortality by creating buildings meant to stop aging and preclude death.

name: Edwin E. Kintner
headline: Edwin E. Kintner, Nuclear Power Pioneer, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Kintner played an early role in efforts to harness nuclear power and oversaw the cleanup at Three Mile Island.

name: John Shepherd-Barron
headline: John Shepherd-Barron, Developer of the A.T.M., Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Shepherd-Barron’s machine became generally known as the first cash dispenser when it was installed at a Barclays bank in a suburb north of London in June 1967.

name: John Burton
headline: John Burton, a Columbia Dean, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Burton was a Columbia University administrator who also was an accountant and a public servant in Washington and New York.

name: John Burton
headline: John Burton, 92, Dies; California Political Boss Who Staged a Comeback
abstract: He left the House of Representatives while struggling with a crack addiction, his political career seemingly over. Actually, it had just begun.

name: Dorothy Kamenshek
headline: Dorothy Kamenshek, ‘League of Their Own’ Figure, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Kamenshek, a star player in the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League, helped form the basis for the lead character in “A League of Their Own.”

name: Moishe Rosen
headline: Moishe Rosen Dies at 78; Founder of Jews for Jesus
abstract: Mr. Rosen was born Jewish, ordained a Baptist minister and went on to found the largest messianic Jewish organization in the world.

name: Allan Manings
profession: Writer and Creator of Television Shows
headline: Allan Manings, Writer and Creator of Television Shows, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Manings, an Emmy-winning writer, created the sitcom “One Day at a Time” in the mid-1970s and also wrote for other hit television shows.

name: David E. Durston
profession: Wrote and Directed I Drink Your Blood
headline: David E. Durston, Who Wrote and Directed ‘I Drink Your Blood,’ Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Durston created the cult-classic film “I Drink Your Blood,” which became a staple of drive-ins.

name: Michael Kuchwara
headline: Michael Kuchwara, Prolific Theater Writer, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Kuchwara, who was based in New York, wrote reviews and articles about shows for a quarter-century.

name: Jose Lima
headline: Jose Lima, Colorful and Popular Pitcher, Dies at 37
abstract: Mr. Lima pitched for five teams in a 13-year career and won 21 games in 1999.

name: Martin Gardner
headline: Martin Gardner, Puzzler and Polymath, Dies at 95
abstract: A prolific and wide-ranging writer, Mr. Gardner was fascinated by mathematics, magic and Alice in Wonderland.

name: Stan Jones
headline: Stan Jones,  Chicago Bears Hall of Famer, Dies at 78
abstract: The Hall of Fame lineman was a standout for the Chicago Bears and an innovator in weight training.

name: Donald Lukens
headline: Donald Lukens, Scandal-Tainted Lawmaker, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Lukens was convicted in 1989 of offenses relating to paying a teenager to have sex, but he refused Republicans’ demands that he resign his House seat.

name: David Ginsburg
headline: David Ginsburg, Longtime Washington Insider, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Ginsburg helped found the Americans for Democratic Action and write the Kerner Report on race relations after the urban riots of the late 1960s.

name: Maurice J. Williams
headline: Maurice J. Williams, Directed United Nations Food Aid, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Williams pushed for more aggressive efforts by the United Nations to address world hunger during his time as leader of the Food Council from 1978 to 1986.

name: Maurice Williams
profession: His Stay Was a Hit for Him and Four Seasons
headline: Maurice Williams, 86, Dies; His ‘Stay’ Was a Hit for Him and Four Seasons
abstract: A chart topper in 1960 for his doo-wop group the Zodiacs, it inspired popular cover versions and was heard in the 1987 film “Dirty Dancing.”

name: Fritz Sennheiser
headline: Fritz Sennheiser, Founder of Audio Electronics Company, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Sennheiser founded Sennheiser Electronic, a manufacturer of equipment used by recording engineers worldwide, and by vocalists like Pink and the Jonas Brothers.

name: Donald Moss
headline: Donald Moss, Illustrator of Sports Art, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Moss captured the action, spectacle and personalities of sports for posters, postage stamps and covers of Sports Illustrated.

name: Mikhail Shatrov
headline: Mikhail Shatrov, Outspoken Soviet Playwright, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Shatrov’s plays shocked Soviet audiences with their fierce criticism of Stalin.

name: Art Linkletter
headline: Art Linkletter, TV Host, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Linkletter hosted the popular shows “People Are Funny” and “House Party” in the 1950s and 1960s.

name: Michael H. Jordan
headline: Michael H. Jordan, Turnaround Expert, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Jordan recast Westinghouse as a media company and revived both CBS  and Electronic Data Systems.

name: Clifford Grodd
headline: Clifford Grodd, the Driving Force at Paul Stuart, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Grodd, who took the reins at Paul Stuart in 1955, counted Mayor Michael Bloomberg and celebrities including Frank Sinatra and Paul Newman as clients.

name: John Finn
headline: John Finn, Medal of Honor Winner, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Finn was the last survivor of the 15 Navy men who received the Medal of Honor, the nation’s highest award for valor, for heroism during the Japanese attack.

name: Anneliese Rothenberger
headline: Anneliese Rothenberger, German Opera Singer, Dies
abstract: Ms. Rothenberger, a soprano, was best known for her performance as Sophie in “Der Rosenkavalier.”

name: Gary Coleman
headline: Gary Coleman, ‘Diff’rent Strokes’ Star, Dies at 42
abstract: The former child star dealt with a well-publicized string of financial and personal difficulties after the show ended.

name: Raymond Haysbert Sr.
headline: Raymond Haysbert Sr., Baltimore Civic Leader and Businessman, Is Dead at 90
abstract: A Tuskegee Airman in World War II, Mr. Haysbert later led Park Sausage, one of the first minority-owned companies to go public, and advised political candidates.

name: Curtiss Anderson
headline: Curtiss Anderson, Editor and Developer of Magazines, Dies at 81
abstract: At Hearst Magazines, Mr. Anderson helped develop Country Living, Smart Money and others, and he edited The Ladies Home Journal at a tumultuous time.

name: Dennis Hopper
headline: Dennis Hopper, 74, Hollywood Rebel, Dies
abstract: In his long career, Mr. Hopper was nominated for Oscars for the “Easy Rider” screenplay and for his supporting role in “Hoosiers.”

name: Gerald Roush
headline: Gerald Roush, Font of Ferrari Knowledge, Is Dead at 68
abstract: The former history professor became a go-to source on all things about the Italian sports car brand.

name: William Pflaumer
headline: William Pflaumer, Philadelphia Beer Baron, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Pflaumer turned the 116-year-old Christian Schmidt and Sons Inc. brewery into one of the nation’s largest.

name: Les Line
profession: Editor of Audubon Magazine During Ambitious Expansion
headline: Les Line, Editor of Audubon Magazine During Ambitious Expansion, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Line expanded the magazine’s mission beyond birds and beasts to environmental issues like oil spills.

name: Louise Bourgeois
headline: Louise Bourgeois, Influential Sculptor, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Bourgeois gained fame late in a long career, when her work had a galvanizing effect on younger artists.

name: Andrei Voznesensky
headline: Andrei Voznesensky, Russian Poet, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Voznesensky’s poetry captured the progress and setbacks of the post-Stalin years in Russia.

name: Kazuo Ohno
headline: Kazuo Ohno, a Founder of Japanese Butoh, Dies at 103
abstract: Mr. Ohno embodied the dual nature of Butoh, which mines the primeval darkness of life yet is also capable of raucous laughter.

name: Chris Haney
headline: Chris Haney, an Inventor of Trivial Pursuit, Dies at 59
abstract: A high school dropout at home in taverns, he and a fellow journalist developed the board game that became a favorite of baby boomers.

name: Paul Garabedian
headline: Paul Garabedian, Mathematician at N.Y.U., Dies at 82
abstract: Computer computations by Dr. Garabedian, a longtime New York University professor, helped lead to fuel-efficient wings for modern jetliners.

name: Peter Orlovsky
headline: Peter Orlovsky, Poet and Ginsberg Muse, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Orlovsky inspired Beat writers like Allen Ginsberg, his longtime partner, and was known for his own emotionally naked poetry.

name: Tobias Wong
headline: Tobias Wong, Witty Designer and Conceptual Artist, Dies at 35
abstract: Mr. Wong was known for his outrageous sendups of luxury goods and witty expropriation of work by other designers.

name: Hasan di Tiro
headline: Hasan di Tiro, Who Led Indonesia Rebels, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. di Tiro founded the Free Aceh Movement, which fought Jakarta in a three-decade war of independence before disbanding under a peace accord in 2005.

name: Rue McClanahan
headline: Rue McClanahan, Actress and Golden Girl, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. McClanahan, a screen and stage actor, helped make “The Golden Girls” a long-running television hit by playing the saucy Southern belle Blanche Devereaux.

name: Robert L. McNeil Jr.
headline: Robert L. McNeil Jr., Chemist Who Introduced Tylenol, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. McNeil was a pharmaceutical executive who introduced Tylenol in 1955 as a competitor to aspirin for pain relief.

name: Donald Windham
headline: Donald Windham, Novelist and Memoirist, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Windham left vivid pictures of literary life in New York, both fictional and factual, when he was an intimate of Tennessee Williams.

name: Giuseppe Taddei
headline: Giuseppe Taddei, Latecomer to the Met, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Taddei was a distinguished Italian baritone who made his Metropolitan Opera debut to glowing notices in 1985 at the astonishing age of 69.

name: Irwin Rosten
headline: Irwin Rosten, Nature Documentary Filmmaker, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Rosten wrote, produced and directed programming on the wonders of nature and wildlife, including “Birds Do It, Bees Do It.”

name: Benjamin Lees
headline: Benjamin Lees, Versatile Composer, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Lees was an iconoclastic American composer who spurned modern musical trends in favor of work that was lyrical, tonal and widely described as approachable.

name: Murray Stein
headline: Murray Stein, Crusader Against Water Pollution, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Stein led the federal government’s fight against water pollution for more than 20 years.

name: John Wooden
headline: John Wooden, Who Built Incomparable Dynasty at U.C.L.A., Dies at 99
abstract: College basketball’s most successful coach, Wooden created one of the greatest dynasties in sports.

name: John W. Douglas
profession: Champion of Civil and Human Rights
headline: John W. Douglas, Champion of Civil and Human Rights, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Douglas was an assistant United States attorney general in the Kennedy and Johnson administrations who later went into private practice.

name: Helen K. Chinoy
headline: Helen K. Chinoy, Theater Historian and Educator, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Chinoy documented the contributions of women to American drama.

name: Joe Gardi
headline: Joe Gardi, Jets Assistant Who Guided Hofstra’s Rise, Dies at 71
abstract: Gardi molded the Jets’ defensive schemes, working as an assistant coach from 1976 to 1984, before becoming Hofstra’s coach in 1990.

name: Himan Brown
headline: Himan Brown, Developer of Radio Dramas, Dies at 99
abstract: A producer who, before that box in the living room had a screen, knew the power of a foghorn and a creaking door.

name: David Markson
headline: David Markson, Postmodern Experimental Novelist, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Markson’s wry, elliptical novels were almost always surprisingly engaging and underappreciated.

name: Joseph Strick
headline: Joseph Strick, Who Filmed the Unfilmable, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Strick, director, screenwriter and producer, was known for filming the unfilmable — in particular literary works whose screen adaptations often ran afoul of censors.

name: Marvin Isley
headline: Marvin Isley, Bassist in Isley Brothers, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Isley provided the foundation for his family’s R&B band, whose hits included “Fight the Power Part 1” and “Livin’ in the Life.”

name: Vera B. Saeedpour
profession: Scholar and Archivist of the Kurdish Culture
headline: Vera B. Saeedpour, Scholar and Archivist of the Kurdish Culture, Dies at 80
abstract: A chance meeting in midlife led to a lifelong interest in an obscure, long-oppressed ethnic group.

name: Lester Johnson
headline: Lester Johnson, Expressionist Painter, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Johnson found his subject matter in the joys and sorrows of ordinary people on the street.

name: Arthur Herzog III
headline: Arthur Herzog III, Author of ‘The Swarm,’ Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Herzog, who wrote novels, nonfiction and short stories, is probably best known for “The Swarm.”

name: Jack Beeson
headline: Jack Beeson, Composer and Teacher, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Beeson, whose approach to music has been described as “enlightened utilitarianism,” was best known for his opera “Lizzie Borden.”

name: Abraham Nathanson
headline: Abraham Nathanson, Bananagrams Inventor, Dies at 80
abstract: Frustrated with the slow pace of Scrabble, Mr. Nathanson came up with the fast-moving letters-and-words game.

name: Marina Semyonova
headline: Marina Semyonova, Star of Bolshoi Ballet, Dies at 102
abstract: Ms. Semyonova was the first great Russian ballerina to emerge in the Soviet era and a prima ballerina of the Bolshoi Theater.

name: Peter J. Hall
headline: Peter J. Hall, Costume Designer for Opera, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Hall parlayed his experience designing camouflage for the British Army into a career as a costumer for opera and theater companies.

name: Peter Hall
headline: Peter Hall, Who Devised the Enterprise Zone, Dies at 82
abstract: Professor Hall was best known for proposing zones to help impoverished cities with no industry that needed drastic assistance.

name: Peter Hall
profession: British Theater Director and Founder of Royal Shakespeare Company
headline: Peter Hall, British Theater Director and Founder of Royal Shakespeare Company, Dies at 86
abstract: A champion of playwrights and actors, he was also artistic director of Britain’s National Theater, from 1973 to 1988.

name: Vladimir Arnold
headline: Vladimir Arnold Dies at 72; Pioneering Mathematician
abstract: Dr. Arnold’s work ranged widely across mathematics and he was a founder of singularity theory, or, as it is sometimes more ominously called, catastrophe theory.

name: Peter Keefe
headline: Peter Keefe, Creator of Cartoon ‘Voltron,’ Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Keefe’s hugely popular 1980s series helped pave the way for other Japanese-style animation in the United States.

name: Crispian St. Peters
profession: Singer of the Hit Pied Piper
headline: Crispian St. Peters, Singer of the Hit ‘Pied Piper,’ Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. St. Peters was the British pop singer best known for “Pied Piper” and “You Were on My Mind.”

name: Joan Hinton
headline: Joan Hinton, Physicist Who Chose China Over Atom Bomb, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Ms. Hinton worked on the Manhattan Project, which developed the atom bomb, but spent most of her life as a committed Maoist working on dairy farms in China.

name: Sigmar Polke
headline: Sigmar Polke, Whose Sly Works Shaped Contemporary Painting, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Polke’s sarcastic and vibrant layering of found images and maverick painting processes left an indelible mark on contemporary painting.

name: Fred Plum
headline: Fred Plum, Neurologist Who Helped Coin ‘Persistent Vegetative State,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Plum’s influential research improved the diagnosis and treatment of patients who lose consciousness from head injuries, strokes, metabolic disorders and drug overdoses.

name: Robert J. Wussler
profession: CBS Executive and Aide to Ted Turner
headline: Robert J. Wussler, CBS Executive and Aide to Ted Turner, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Wussler helped transform a superstation known mostly for its Atlanta Braves baseball coverage into a media enterprise including CNN and the TNT network.

name: Frank W. Ballard
headline: Frank W. Ballard, Who Trained Puppeteers at UConn, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Ballard helped introduce puppetry to the university curriculum.

name: James N. Wood
headline: James N. Wood, President of the Getty Trust, Dies at 69
abstract: A longtime director of the Institute of Art in Chicago, Mr. Wood led the Getty through a turbulent period.

name: James Wood
headline: James Wood Dies at 85; Revived A.&P. Supermarket Chain
abstract: Many thought A.&P. was a lost cause when Mr. Wood became chief in 1980, but he turned the company around and, in the process, renewed interest in stock options as executive compensation.

name: Jimmy Dean
headline: Jimmy Dean, Folksy Singer, Dies at 81
abstract: A country singer who found a second career with his own brand of sausages.

name: Egon Ronay
headline: Egon Ronay,  Publisher of Food Guides, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Ronay’s restaurant and hotel guides defined who’s who in British food culture.

name: William J. Mitchell
headline: William J. Mitchell, Architect and Urban Visionary, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Mitchell was an M.I.T. dean whose interests evolved beyond buildings to the technical and social problems presented by cities in the digital age.

name: E. Fleischmann
headline: E. Fleischmann, Impresario of Los Angeles, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Fleischmann ran the Los Angeles Philharmonic for nearly three decades, helping to elevate its stature to that of an orchestra of the first rank.

name: Jonathan Wolken
headline: Jonathan Wolken, a Founder of Pilobolus, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Wolken helped to create a modern dance troupe that became one of the most popular in the world.

name: Tom Stith
headline: Tom Stith, All-American at St. Bonaventure, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Stith was the forward-center who brought St. Bonaventure University to national basketball prominence in the early 1960s, then overcame tuberculosis and played for the Knicks.

name: Thomas S. Buechner
headline: Thomas S. Buechner, Former Director of Brooklyn Museum, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Buechner was one of the youngest museum directors in the United States when he led the Brooklyn Museum through an ambitious renovation in the 1960s.

name: Robert B. Radnitz
headline: Robert B. Radnitz, Producer of ‘Sounder,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Radnitz’s family movies showed youngsters maturing and expanding their abilities in exotic, dangerous or adventuresome situations.

name: Elzbieta Czyzewska
profession: Polish Actress Unwelcome in Her Own Country
headline: Elzbieta Czyzewska, Polish Actress Unwelcome in Her Own Country, Dies at 72
abstract: Ms. Czyzewska was a star in Poland, but marriage to the American journalist David Halberstam made her an outcast in her home country.

name: Maureen Forrester
headline: Maureen Forrester, Canadian Contralto, Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. Forrester was revered for her opulent voice and especially acclaimed for her performances of Mahler.

name: José Saramago
headline: José Saramago, Nobel Prize-Winning Portuguese Writer, Dies at 87
abstract: The Portuguese writer was known as much for his unfaltering Communist views as for his surrealist, sardonic novels.

name: Ronald Neame
headline: Ronald Neame, Filmmaker, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Neame produced and directed more than 70 films, including “Tunes of Glory” and “The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie.”

name: Marcel Bigeard
headline: Gen. Marcel Bigeard, French Hero of 3 Wars, Dies at 94
abstract: General Bigeard, one of France’s most decorated veterans, led troops in the French Resistance in World War II and in wars in Algeria and Indochina.

name: Bill Dixon
headline: Bill Dixon, Leading Edge of Avant-Garde Jazz, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Dixon, a trumpeter, composer and educator, fought to raise the profile of free improvisation.

name: Manute Bol
headline: Manute Bol, N.B.A. Player and Activist, Dies at 47
abstract: The 7-foot-6 center from the Sudan was a dominant shot blocker in the National Basketball Association and later returned to his homeland to try to heal the wounds of a civil war.

name: Al Williamson
headline: Al Williamson, Illustrator of Comic Books, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Williamson, who worked with almost every major comics publisher, put an indelible artistic stamp on “Flash Gordon.”

name: Garry Shider
headline: Garry Shider, a Pillar of Funk-Rock, Is Dead at 56
abstract: Mr. Shider, who was fond of performing dressed only in a loincloth, delivered incendiary solos and impressively funky rhythm work with Parliament and Funkadelic in the 1970s.

name: Raymond Parks
headline: Raymond Parks, Nascar Pioneer, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Parks, a former transporter of moonshine, was at the gathering that led to the founding of Nascar, and was the owner of its first championship team.

name: Carlos Monsiváis
headline: Carlos Monsiváis, Mexican Who Wrote of the Great and the Humble, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Monsiváis, not well known outside of Mexico, chronicled political foibles, social issues and the dignity of everyday life.

name: Kalmen Opperman
headline: Kalmen Opperman, Master Clarinetist and Teacher, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Opperman was a master clarinetist whose intensive teaching methods helped mold some of the top players of the last 50 years.

name: Wendell Logan
profession: Composer of Jazz and Concert Music
headline: Wendell Logan, Composer of Jazz and Concert Music, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Logan also founded the jazz department at the Oberlin Conservatory of Music, long a bastion of high-level classical training.

name: Chris Welles
headline: Chris Welles, Award-Winning Business Writer, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Welles was a leading business journalist from the 1960s to the early 1980s, and led a prestigious fellowship program at Columbia.

name: Gerald W. Heaney
headline: Gerald W. Heaney, a Judge Who Ruled for the Desegregation of Public Schools, Dies at 92
abstract: Judge Heaney oversaw the integration of St. Louis schools for 18 years and played a central role in other desegregation cases.

name: Joe Deal
headline: Joe Deal, a Landscape Photographer of Disquieting Images, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Deal rejected the romantic tradition of Ansel Adams and Edward Weston in favor of a dry-eyed inspection of the modern American landscape.

name: Charles Ensley
headline: Charles Ensley, Labor Leader and Union Critic, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Ensley led the union representing New York City social workers for 26 years and was a forceful critic of union corruption.

name: Edith Shain
profession: Said Famous Kiss Came Her Way
headline: Edith Shain, Who Said Famous Kiss Came Her Way,  Dies at 91
abstract: Alfred Eisenstaedt’s shot of a sailor kissing a nurse in Times Square captured the moment of joy at the end of World War II.

name: Nico Smith
headline: Nico Smith, Minister and Fighter of Apartheid, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Smith defied his racist upbringing in South Africa by living in a black township and leading a congregation there while organizing protests against apartheid.

name: Prescott Bush Jr.
headline: Prescott Bush Jr., Scion of a Political Family, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Bush was the brother of one president and uncle of another, and a retired insurance executive who tried but never made it far in politics.

name: Steven Krane
profession: Ex-Leader of New York State Bar
headline: Steven Krane, Ex-Leader of New York State Bar, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Krane worked to coordinate legal help for the families of people injured or killed on Sept. 11, 2001.

name: William S. Richardson
headline: William S. Richardson, Ex-Chief Justice in Hawaii, Dies at 90
abstract: In 16 years leading the state’s Supreme Court, he defended the rights of native Hawaiians, often relying on ancestral custom in his decisions.

name: Ben Sonnenberg
headline: Ben Sonnenberg, Founder of Literary Journal, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Sonnenberg, who created Grand Street in the spirit of high-minded but nonacademic magazines, consulted only his own taste.

name: Fred Anderson
headline: Fred Anderson, Saxophonist and Club Owner, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Anderson, a player best known in Chicago who nurtured local musicians, helped establish the city as a center of experimental jazz.

name: Pete Quaife
headline: Pete Quaife, a Bassist for the Kinks, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Quaife was a schoolmate of Ray and Dave Davies, the quarreling siblings behind one of the top bands of the British Invasion.

name: Walter Shorenstein
headline: Walter Shorenstein, Democratic Donor, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Shorenstein was a commercial real estate developer, philanthropist and adviser to presidents, including President Lyndon B. Johnson and President Bill Clinton.

name: Dwight Armstrong
headline: Dwight Armstrong, Who Bombed a College Building in 1970, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Armstrong was one of four men who bombed a building on the University of Wisconsin campus in Madison in 1970, killing one person and injuring several.

name: Richard B. Sellars
headline: Richard B. Sellars, Former Chief of Johnson & Johnson, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Sellars is credited with persuading the company to keep its headquarters in New Brunswick, N.J.

name: M.D. Ginsburg
headline: M.D. Ginsburg, 78, Dies; Lawyer and Tax Expert
abstract: Martin D. Ginsburg  was a tax lawyer and professor of tax law and the husband of Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg of the Supreme Court.

name: Robert C. Byrd
headline: Robert C. Byrd, a Pillar of the Senate, Dies at 92
abstract: Elected to a record nine terms in the Senate, Mr. Byrd championed the legislative branch and brought huge amounts of federal money to West Virginia.

name: Dolph Briscoe
headline: Dolph Briscoe, Texas Governor in the ’70s, Dies at 87
abstract: In the 1970s, Mr. Briscoe helped restore credibility to Texas state government after a major scandal.

name: Algirdas Brazauskas
headline: Algirdas Brazauskas, First Lithuanian President, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Brazauskas was a former Communist bureaucrat who helped steer his country through tempestuous political straits to independence from the Soviet Union.

name: Nicolas Hayek
headline: Nicolas Hayek Dies at 82; His Swatch Saved an Industry
abstract: Mr. Hayek was the founder and the chairman of the Swatch Group, which made him one of Switzerland’s wealthiest men.

name: John Willis
headline: John Willis, Ubiquitous Editor of Theatre World, Dies at 93
abstract: Besides producing a chronicle of record for the New York stage, Mr. Willis could be found in the audience eight times a week for 50 years.

name: Wu Guanzhong
headline: Wu Guanzhong, Leading Chinese Painter, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Wu’s fusion of Western modernism and traditional Chinese painting made him one of China’s most forward-looking artists.

name: Allyn Ferguson
headline: Allyn Ferguson, TV Composer, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Ferguson was a writer of the themes for “Charlie’s Angels” and “Barney Miller,” and wrote orchestral scores for adaptations of literary classics.

name: Rudolf Leopold
headline: Rudolf Leopold, Art Collector, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Leopold was a museum director who amassed a significant collection of Austrian art, but faced questions about the provenance of some his artworks.

name: Stanley Wagner
headline: Stanley Wagner, New York Winery Owner, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Wagner, a third-generation grape farmer, opened a successful winery in the Finger Lakes region of New York in 1979.

name: Corey Allen
headline: Corey Allen, Actor and Director, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Allen was best known for his scenes with James Dean in “Rebel Without a Cause.”

name: Elise Boulding
headline: Elise Boulding, Peace Scholar, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Boulding, an instructor at Dartmouth and the University of Colorado, was also an author of numerous books.

name: Louis Moyroud
headline: Louis Moyroud Dies at 96; Helped Revolutionize Printing
abstract: Louis Marius Moyroud and Rene Alphonse Higonnet created the first practical phototypesetting machine in 1946.

name: Elliott Kastner
headline: Elliott Kastner, Who Produced Literary Films, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Kastner, a filmmaker with an affinity for literary writers, produced films like “Equus,” “Harper” and “The Long Goodbye.”

name: Bill Aucoin
profession: Manager of the Rock Band Kiss
headline: Bill Aucoin, Manager of the Rock Band Kiss, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Aucoin helped four scruffy New York City kids with big, weird dreams formulate their flamboyant act.

name: Rammellzee
headline: Rammellzee, Hip-Hop and Graffiti Pioneer, Dies at 49
abstract: The artist, an elusive, self-mythologizing figure who cast himself as an urban philosopher, influenced the Beastie Boys and Cypress Hill.

name: Don Coryell
headline: Don Coryell, Innovator in N.F.L.’s Passing Game, Dies at 85
abstract: While coaching the San Diego Chargers he became the architect of a high-powered passing offense that was known as Air Coryell.

name: Arnold Friberg
headline: Arnold Friberg, Painter of Historical Scenes, Is Dead at 96
abstract: The artist, perhaps best known for “The Prayer at Valley Forge” (depicting a kneeling Washington), rendered subjects from sports, religion and British royalty, among others.

name: Beryl Bainbridge
headline: Beryl Bainbridge, Mordant Novelist, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Ms. Bainbridge’s sparely written, mordant novels — often with a dark comic edge — made her one of the most distinctive and admired voices in postwar British fiction.

name: Mohammed Oudeh
headline: Mohammed Oudeh, Who Planned ’72 Olympic Attack, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Mr. Oudeh, a leader of a Palestinian terrorist group, was the mastermind behind the attack at the 1972 Munich Olympics that killed 11 Israeli athletes.

name: Benny Powell
headline: Benny Powell, Who Played Trombone With Count Basie, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Mr. Powell recorded with everyone from Sinatra to Screamin’ Jay Hawkins but was best known for his long tenure with Count Basie’s big band.

name: Charles S. King
headline: Charles S. King, Range Rover Designer, Dies at 85
abstract: The vehicle Mr. King engineered was featured in an exhibition at the Louvre as an exemplary work of industrial design.

name: Grand Ayatollah Fadlallah
headline: Grand Ayatollah Fadlallah, Shiite Cleric, Dies at 75
abstract: Ayatollah Fadlallah’s writings and preachings inspired the Dawa Party of Iraq and a generation of militants, including the founders of Hezbollah.

name: Clement Finch
headline: Clement Finch, a Pioneer in Hematology, Dies at 94
abstract: A pioneering hematologist whose research on iron helped improve nutrition and led to advances in diagnosing and treating anemia.

name: Bob Probert
headline: Bob Probert, 45, Renowned Hockey Brawler, Dies
abstract: Probert was known as one of the most talented fighters in the N.H.L., and could also skate and score. But he also battled substance abuse.

name: Eleanor R. Morse
headline: Eleanor R. Morse, Dalí Collector, Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Morse, along with her husband, A. Reynolds Morse, founded the Salvador Dalí Museum in St. Petersburg, Fla.

name: Robert Butler
headline: Robert Butler, Aging Expert, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Dr. Butler was a psychiatrist whose painful youthful realization that death is inevitable prompted him to challenge and ultimately reform the treatment of the elderly through research.

name: Cesare Siepi
headline: Cesare Siepi, Renowned Italian Opera Singer, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Siepi was a classic Italian basso cantante, or “singing bass,” with a warm, slightly dark voice that was ideally suited to Mozart.

name: Ann Waldron
headline: Ann Waldron, Biographer of Southern Writers, Is Dead at 85
abstract: A daughter of the South, Ms. Waldron wrote three biographies about Southern writers and editors.

name: Juanita M. Kreps
headline: Juanita M. Kreps, Commerce Secretary, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Kreps was President Jimmy Carter’s Secretary of Commerce, the first woman to hold a post traditionally occupied by men with business interests.

name: Jim Bohlen
headline: Jim Bohlen, Who Led in Creation of Greenpeace, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Bohlen’s snap decision to sail to Amchitka Island to protest nuclear testing galvanized a movement.

name: Israel Hicks
headline: Israel Hicks, Director of August Wilson’s Cycle, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Hicks, a prolific stage director, recently completed a nearly 20-year project directing August Wilson’s entire decade-by-decade cycle about the black experience.

name: Joya Sherrill
headline: Joya Sherrill, Who Sang With Ellington and Goodman, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Ms. Sherrill was also one of the first African-American performers to host a children’s television show.

name: Sergei Tretyakov
headline: Sergei Tretyakov, Spy Who Fled to U.S., Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Tretyakov, who had led covert operations in New York City and the United Nations, defected in 2000, long after the end of the cold war.

name: Ed Limato
profession: Flashy Old-School Talent Agent to the Stars
headline: Ed Limato, Flashy Old-School Talent Agent to the Stars, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Limato provided exhaustive service, including hand-holding, to a number of Hollywood’s biggest names.

name: William R. Callahan
headline: Rev. William R. Callahan Dies at 78; Dissident Who Challenged Vatican
abstract: The Rev. Callahan was a priest whose vociferous and organized opposition to Vatican  policies prompted Jesuit officials to expel him from their order.

name: Bob Sheppard
headline: Bob Sheppard, Voice of the Yankees, Dies at 99
abstract: Bob Sheppard’s intonation as Yankee Stadium’s announcer for more than half a century personified Yankee grandeur.

name: Harvey Pekar
headline: Harvey Pekar, ‘American Splendor’ Creator, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Pekar’s comic book attracted a cult following for its unvarnished stories of an aggrieved Everyman.

name: Tuli Kupferberg
headline: Tuli Kupferberg, Bohemian and Fug, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Kupferberg was a poet and singer who went from being a noted Beat to becoming, in his words, “the world’s oldest rock star” when he helped found the Fugs.

name: George W. Webber
headline: George W. Webber, Social Activist Minister, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Webber’s initiatives included remaking a major New York seminary, starting storefront churches in Harlem and beginning a program to educate prison inmates as pastors.

name: Clara Claiborne Park
headline: Clara Claiborne Park, 86, Dies; Wrote About Autistic Child
abstract: Her 1967 book, “The Siege,” was credited with assuaging the guilt that so many parents of autistic children had felt and providing insight for psychiatrists, psychologists, educators and advocates.

name: George Steinbrenner
headline: George Steinbrenner, Who Built Yankees Into Powerhouse, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Steinbrenner bought a declining team in 1973, and then, in an often tumultuous reign, placed his stamp on seven World Series championship teams.

name: Walter Hawkins
headline: Walter Hawkins, Gospel Singer, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Hawkins brought a sense of contemporary rhythm to the howling, pleading, God-praising tradition of churchly ecstasy.

name: Vernon Baker
headline: Vernon Baker, Belated Medal of Honor Recipient, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Baker was the only living black veteran to receive the award — 52 years late — for his heroism in World War II.

name: Sugar Minott
headline: Sugar Minott, Reggae Star, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Minott’s joyful, lilting voice bridged four decades of transformation in reggae music.

name: Pius Njawé
headline: Pius Njawé, Noted African Journalist, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Njawé was considered a symbol of opposition to the autocratic regime of Paul Biya in Cameroon, who has been in power since 1982 in the resource-rich but poor Central African nation.

name: Marrack Goulding
profession: Former Chief Peacekeeper for the U.N
headline: Marrack Goulding, Former Chief Peacekeeper for the U.N., Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Goulding, a former British ambassador to Angola, led United Nations peacekeeping operations from 1986 to 1993, at times coming under fire himself.

name: Arnold Kramish
headline: Arnold Kramish, Expert on Nuclear Intelligence, Dies at 87
abstract: While working on the Manhattan Project in 1944, Mr. Kramish survived the explosion of a uranium enrichment device.

name: Robert Galambos
headline: Robert Galambos, Neuroscientist Who Showed How Bats Navigate, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Galambos’swork on humans resulted in learning the code by which nerves send messages about sound.

name: Vonetta McGee
headline: Vonetta McGee, Film and TV Actress, Dies at 65
abstract: Ms. McGee appeared in “Blacula,” “Hammer” and “Shaft in Africa,” in which she played an emir’s daughter.

name: Charles Mackerras
headline: Charles Mackerras, Elegant Conductor, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Mackerras, the Australian conductor, championed the works of Janacek.

name: David Blackwell
headline: David Blackwell, Scholar of Probability, Dies at 91
abstract: A statistician and author of influential academic papers on probability and game theory, he was the first black scholar to be admitted to the National Academy of Sciences.

name: Peter Fernandez
profession: Voice of Speed Racer in the U.S
headline: Peter Fernandez, Voice of Speed Racer in the U.S., Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Fernandez, in dubbing and writing some scripts of the TV series, provided Americans with an early introduction to Japanese animation.

name: Hank Cochran
headline: Hank Cochran, Writer for Country Music Stars, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Cochran was a singer and songwriter who wrote major hits for Patsy Cline, Eddy Arnold and George Strait.

name: Eduardo Sánchez Junco
headline: Eduardo Sánchez Junco, Founder of Fawning Magazine, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Mr. Junco, Hello magazine’s founder and publisher, presided over his family’s multimillion-dollar publishing empire.

name: Paulo Moura
headline: Paulo Moura, a Force in Brazilian Music, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Moura was known for playing and writing music that ranged from jazz, chorinho, samba and bossa nova to classical.

name: Stephen H. Schneider
headline: Stephen H. Schneider, Climatologist, Is Dead at 65
abstract: Dr. Schneider was an engineer and physicist who developed scientific models and used them to press for action on global warming.

name: James Gammon
headline: James Gammon, Character Actor, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Gammon was best known as the manager in the baseball film comedy “Major League” and for his work in the plays of Sam Shepard.

name: Denise Jefferson
headline: Denise Jefferson, 65, Director of the Ailey School, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Jefferson was an internationally known dance educator who oversaw the training of generations of world-class performers.

name: Bill McCabe
headline: Bill McCabe, Sanitation’s Perfect Man, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. McCabe scored the highest possible score on the test to become a sanitation worker in 1940, drawing admiring articles in New York newspapers.

name: Jim Neu
headline: Jim Neu, Creator of Wry Plays, Is Dead at 66
abstract: Mr. Neu, a playwright, took as his topic the effect of pop culture on the individual American psyche.

name: Buff Cobb
headline: Buff Cobb, Actress and TV Host, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Cobb and Mike Wallace, her husband at the time, adapted their radio program into the CBS talk show “Mike and Buff” in the early 1950s.

name: Larry Keith
headline: Larry Keith, Television and Stage Actor, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Keith was the first American to play Henry Higgins in “My Fair Lady” on Broadway.

name: Clint Hartung
headline: Clint Hartung, Once a Promising Giant, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Hartung was one of the most highly touted rookies of his generation, only to become a symbol of unfulfilled baseball promise.

name: Ralph Houk
headline: Ralph Houk, Yankees Manager, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Houk won two World Series and three American League pennants in his first three seasons in New York.

name: Peter Walls
headline: Peter Walls, General in Zimbabwe, Dies at 83
abstract: Lt. Gen. Walls played a central and sometimes ambiguous role in the first days of Zimbabwe’s transition to majority rule.

name: David Warren
headline: David Warren, Inventor of ‘Black Box,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Warren was an Australian aeronautical researcher who advanced air safety despite skepticism and ridicule.

name: John E. Irving
headline: John E. Irving, Canadian Who Built Empire on Lumber, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Irving helped transform a family lumber business into Atlantic Canada’s largest conglomerate.

name: Carl Gordon
headline: Carl Gordon, a Late-Blooming Actor, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Gordon heeded a surprising call late in life and became a successful character actor on television and the stage.

name: Daniel Schorr
headline: Daniel Schorr, Journalist, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Schorr’s aggressive reporting over 70 years brought him into conflict with censors, the Nixon administration and network superiors.

name: Vic Ziegel
headline: Vic Ziegel, Sportswriter and Editor, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Ziegel, who wrote for The New York Post and then The Daily News, often focused on baseball, boxing and thoroughbred racing.

name: Doug Ohlson
headline: Doug Ohlson, Painter of Vivid Abstracts, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Ohlson was Inspired by the vistas of his native Iowa and used color on a grand scale.

name: James E. Akins
headline: James E. Akins, Envoy to Saudi Arabia, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Akins, the State Department’s ambassador to Saudi Arabia, warned more than a year in advance of the 1973 Arab oil embargo that oil-exporting nations were poised to restrict shipments.

name: Cécile Aubry
profession: Actress and Writer of Childrens Stories
headline: Cécile Aubry, Actress and Writer of Children’s Stories, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Aubry, a French actress, had a short but glamorous film career and later became a writer, creating a children’s television series.

name: Gerson Goldhaber
headline: Gerson Goldhaber, Particle Physicist, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Goldhaber was a particle physicist before shifting his focus to dark energy and the outer reaches of the universe.

name: Wye Jamison Allanbrook
headline: Wye Jamison Allanbrook, an Expert on Mozart, Dies at 67
abstract: Ms. Allanbrook showed that the compositions of Mozart and his contemporaries were full of topical references to music of their social environment.

name: Judith Peabody
headline: Judith Peabody, Socialite and Volunteer,  Dies at 80
abstract: A boldface name in an elite family, Mrs. Peabody founded a drug rehabilitation center and cared for dozens of men with AIDS.

name: Nathan Quinones
headline: Nathan Quinones Dies at 79; Led New York City Schools
abstract: Mr. Quinones, the chancellor of the school system in the mid-1980s, pushed to reduce dropout rates and institute tougher achievement standards.

name: Anthony Rolfe Johnson
headline: Anthony Rolfe Johnson, Farmer Turned Opera Star, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Rolfe Johnson went from being an English farmer to a renowned lyric tenor at the world’s top opera houses.

name: Billy Loes
headline: Billy Loes, Quirky Pitcher for Dodgers, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Loes was a leading pitcher for three pennant-winning Brooklyn Dodgers teams of the 1950s.

name: Jack Tatum
headline: Jack Tatum, Whose Tackle Paralyzed Player, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Tatum, a former Oakland Raiders player, was known for his brutal hits, none of them more devastating than a blow that left New England Patriots wide receiver Darryl Stingley paralyzed in 1978.

name: John Callahan
headline: John Callahan, Cartoonist, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Callahan was a quadriplegic, alcoholic cartoonist who was known for drawings that made impolitic sport of people with disabilities and diseases.

name: Theo Albrecht
profession: Helped Build the Aldi Grocery Chain
headline: Theo Albrecht, Who Helped Build the Aldi Grocery Chain, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Albrecht ranked 31st on Forbes magazine’s most recent list of the world’s richest people.

name: Luis Corvalán
headline: Luis Corvalán Dies at 93; Led Communists in Chile
abstract: Mr. Corvalán’s party was critical to the rise of Salvador Allende, the first elected Marxist head of state in the Western Hemisphere.

name: Al Goodman
headline: Al Goodman, R&B Singer, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Goodman was the soothing bass in the trio the Moments, best known for the 1970 hit “Love on a Two-Way Street.”

name: Willem Breuker
headline: Willem Breuker, Dutch Composer and Bandleader, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Breuker’s compositions drew from both high and low culture, throwing Kurt Weill into the blender with ragtag circus music.

name: Nicolas Carone
headline: Nicolas Carone, Abstract Expressionist, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Carone was present at the beginning of the New York School and friends with Jackson Pollock, Willem de Kooning, and Mark Rothko. But his best work may have come long after the style faded.

name: Maury Chaykin
headline: Maury Chaykin, Character Actor, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Chaykin was a ubiquitous character actor in films and television who specialized in comic roles.

name: Michael Batterberry
headline: Michael Batterberry, Influential Food Editor, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Batterberry was a food writer and historian who founded two influential magazines, Food & Wine and Food Arts.

name: Lawrence Boadt
headline: Lawrence Boadt, Priest, Publisher and Bible Scholar, Dies at 67
abstract: The Roman Catholic priest, publisher and Bible scholar used his study of the Old Testament as a vehicle for promoting understanding between Christians and Jews.

name: David Alexander
headline: David Alexander, Overseer of Rhodes Selection, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Mr. Alexander, a former president of Pomona College who changed the face of that campus and its student body, also pressed the Rhodes Trust to grant scholarships to women.

name: Ben Keith
profession: Musician and Sideman to Neil Young
headline: Ben Keith, Musician and Sideman to Neil Young, Dies at 73
abstract: This multi-instrumentalist was a Nashville sideman for years, playing with Willie Nelson, Patsy Cline and many others.

name: Alex Higgins
profession: Bombastic Peoples Champion of Pro Snooker
headline: Alex Higgins, the Bombastic ‘People’s Champion’ of Pro Snooker, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Higgins helped lift a billiards-like sport with his charisma and intense style, but his appetites for excess brought him turmoil.

name: Robert C. Tucker
headline: Robert C. Tucker, a Scholar of Marx, Stalin and Soviet Affairs, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Tucker’s frustrations in persuading the authorities in Stalin’s Russia to let his new Russian wife accompany him home to the United States gave him crucial  insights into the Soviet leader.

name: Erich Steidtmann
headline: Erich Steidtmann, Ex-Nazi Officer in Inquiry, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Steidtmann died three months after German prosecutors reopened an investigation into whether he had participated in massacres of thousands of Polish Jews.

name: John R. Branca
headline: John R. Branca, Advocate for Boxers, Dies at 86
abstract: A former legislator, Mr. Branca worked to improve the safety of fighters in the boxing ring as chairman of the New York State Athletic Commission.

name: Mitch Miller
headline: Mitch Miller, Maestro of the Singalong, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Miller was an influential record producer who became an unlikely television star on “Sing Along With Mitch.”

name: Eugene R. Anderson
headline: Eugene R. Anderson Dies at 82; He Made Insurers Pay Up
abstract: The New York trial lawyer found innovative ways to get insurance companies to cover asbestos and toxic-spill claims.

name: Morrie Yohai
headline: Morrie Yohai, 90, the Man Behind Cheez Doodles, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Yohai insisted on sharing the acclaim as the snack’s developer with colleagues at the factory he owned in the Bronx.

name: Lolita Lebrón
headline: Lolita Lebrón, Puerto Rican Nationalist, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Lebrón blazed her way to notoriety as she led three other Puerto Rican nationalists in an attack on the United States House of Representatives on March 1, 1954.

name: Bernie West
profession: TV Writer Known for All in the Family
headline: Bernie West, a TV Writer Known for ‘All in the Family,’ Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. West was a standup comedian before he wrote and produced socially conscious sitcoms like “All in the Family” and “The Jeffersons.”

name: Robert F. Boyle
headline: Robert F. Boyle, Film Designer for Hitchcock, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Boyle, 100, created some of the most memorable scenes and images in cinematic history.

name: Robert H. Boyle
headline: Robert H. Boyle, a Watchdog of the Hudson River, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Boyle, whose affection for the river and for fishing began in childhood, was a crusading conservationist and a founder of the widely replicated group Riverkeeper.

name: John Aylesworth
headline: John Aylesworth, a ‘Hee-Haw’ Creator, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Aylesworth was a creator of the vaudeville-type country show that attracted top top music acts like Merle Haggard.

name: Suso Cecchi D’Amico
headline: Suso Cecchi D’Amico, Writer of Literate Screenplays, Dies at 96
abstract: Mrs. D’Amico, who worked with some of Italy’s greatest directors, including De Sica, Antonioni and Visconti, put her stamp on postwar neorealism.

name: Thomas C. Peebles
headline: Dr. Thomas C. Peebles, Who Identified Measles Virus, Dies at 89
abstract: A D in college biology disguised an aptitude for medical research that led him to make landmark scientific advances.

name: Robert M. Chanock
headline: Dr. Robert M. Chanock, Prominent Virologist, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Chanock was a pediatrician whose discoveries about viruses led to breakthrough medical treatments.

name: Reginald Levy
profession: Hailed as a Hero in a 72 Hijacking
headline: Reginald Levy Is Dead at 88; Hailed as a Hero in a ’72 Hijacking
abstract: Mr. Levy was captain of a hijacked Belgian airliner who enabled Israeli commandos to storm the plane and rescue all 100 passengers and crew members.

name: Marilyn Buck
headline: Marilyn Buck, Imprisoned for Brink’s Holdup, Dies at 62
abstract: Ms. Buck served more than two decades in prison for her role in the 1981 Brink’s armored-car robbery in Rockland County, N.Y., in which three people were killed.

name: Joanna Steichen
headline: Joanna Steichen, Photographer’s Wife and Aide, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Steichen, wife of the photographer Edward Steichen, edited an important survey of his work.

name: Lorene Yarnell
profession: Dancer and Half of a Comedy Duo
headline: Lorene Yarnell, Dancer and Half of a Comedy Duo, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Yarnell and her partner, Robert Shields, were a presence on television in the 1970s, at one point hosting their own variety show.

name: Martin Drew
headline: Martin Drew, British Jazz Drummer, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Drew was a drummer for Oscar Peterson and also for Ronnie Scott.

name: Tony Judt
headline: Tony Judt, Chronicler of History, Is Dead at 62
abstract: Mr. Judt, who taught at New York University, was known for his controversial essays on American foreign policy, the state of Israel and the future of Europe.

name: Fritz Teufel
headline: Fritz Teufel, a German Protester in the ’60s, Dies at 67
abstract: The ferment of the 1960s brought Mr. Teufel, a skinny, red-bearded figure with wire-rimmed glasses, bobbing to the surface of tumultuous events.

name: Lee Lockwood
headline: Lee Lockwood Dies at 78; Captured Life Under Communism
abstract: Mr. Lockwood, an American photojournalist, documented the treatment of an American prisoner of war in North Vietnam and persuaded Fidel Castro to sit for a highly personal interview.

name: Bruce M. Cohen
headline: Rabbi Bruce M. Cohen, Is Dead at 65; Worked to Promote Peace
abstract: Rabbi Cohen’s organization, Interns for Peace, has brought together hundreds of Israeli Jews and Arabs in activities in the past 34 years.

name: Patricia Neal
headline: Patricia Neal, an Oscar Winner Who Endured Tragedy, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Neal, the molasses-voiced actress whose life alternated surreally between triumph and tragedy, won both an Academy Award and a Tony.

name: David F. Dixon
headline: David F. Dixon, Force Behind Saints and Superdome, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Dixon, the longtime owner of a French Quarter shop, pursued pro football for New Orleans since the late 1950s.His efforts led to an expansion team in 1967.

name: Paul Milstein
headline: Paul Milstein, City Real Estate Titan, Dies at 88
abstract: The developer of Milford Plaza had a longstanding business partnership with his brother, Seymour Milstein, until a bitter dispute left them estranged.

name: Jerry Flint
headline: Jerry Flint, Longtime Auto Journalist, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Flint wrote the Backseat Driver column for Forbes magazine and was known for his deep knowledge of the industry and his blunt prose style.

name: Ted Stevens
headline: Ted Stevens, Longtime Alaska Senator, Dies at 86
abstract: The billions of dollars that Mr. Stevens won helped shape Alaska, but his career ended in an election defeat and a corruption conviction that was later overturned.

name: Dan Rostenkowski
headline: Dan Rostenkowski, Lawmaker, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Rostenkowski spent 13 years as chairman of a powerful House committee before serving prison time for fraud.

name: Antonio Pettigrew
headline: Antonio Pettigrew, Sprinter Who Doped, Dies at 42
abstract: Pettigrew, who gave up his 2000 Olympic sprint-relay gold medal after admitting to doping, was found dead in his car.

name: David L. Wolper
headline: David L. Wolper, Producer of Groundbreaking ‘Roots’, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Wolper, who produced the groundbreaking mini-series “Roots” and “The Thorn Birds,” dies at 82.

name: Jay Larkin
headline: Jay Larkin, Theatrical Producer of TV Boxing, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Larkin brought a theatrical background and hard-nosed negotiating to producing Showtime’s boxing telecasts.

name: David Dolby
headline: David Dolby, Hero in Vietnam Battle, Dies at 64
abstract: Specialist Fourth Class Dolby, a machine-gunner in the Vietnam War whose actions saved members of his platoon in a deadly attack, served five tours of duty.

name: Lou Smit
headline: Lou Smit, Detective in JonBenet Ramsey Case, Is Dead at 75
abstract: He came out of retirement to investigate the 1996 murder, but resigned after concluding that the police had wrongly focused on the parents.

name: Leon Breeden
headline: Leon Breeden, Jazz Educator, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Breeden transformed the jazz studies program at the University of North Texas from a clandestine enterprise into the international Mecca for jazz training.

name: Abbey Lincoln
headline: Abbey Lincoln, Bold and Introspective Jazz Singer, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Lincoln’s dramatic vocal command and tersely poetic songs made her a singular figure in jazz. She was also a civil rights advocate and acted in films with Sidney Poitier.

name: Paul Ryan Rudd
headline: Paul Ryan Rudd, Actor of Stage and Screen, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Rudd, who came to his profession late and left early, won praise for his work on Broadway and in the New York Shakespeare Festival.

name: Bruno S.
profession: Street Musician Turned Lead Actor in Herzog Classics
headline: Bruno S., Street Musician Turned Lead Actor in Herzog Classics, Dies at 78
abstract: The actor starred in “The Enigma of Kaspar Hauser” and “Stroszek,” which was based on his life.

name: Stanley Simon
headline: Stanley Simon, Who Assisted Veterans, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Mr. Simon, a former executive for the Bulova company, helped found a watchmaking school for soldiers who had been badly wounded in World War II.

name: Denis E. Dillon
headline: Denis E. Dillon, Prosecutor on Long Island, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Dillon, the longtime district attorney of Nassau County, N.Y., quietly oversaw high-profile prosecutions while using his office as a bully pulpit against abortion.

name: James J. Kilpatrick
profession: Conservative Voice in Print and on TV
headline: James J. Kilpatrick, Conservative Voice in Print and on TV, Dies at 89
abstract: A prolific writer and a sharp debater, Mr. Kilpatrick was a prominent conservative voice for half a century.

name: Andrew Roth
headline: Andrew Roth, American-Born Chronicler of British Politics, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Roth fled the McCarthy-era America of 1950 for a new life as a meticulous and often abrasive chronicler of British politicians.

name: Bernard Knox
headline: Bernard Knox, 95, Classics Scholar, Dies
abstract: Professor Knox was an authority on the works of Sophocles, a prolific scholar and the founding director of Harvard’s Center for Hellenic Studies.

name: Dimitrios Ioannidis
headline: Dimitrios Ioannidis, Greek Coup Leader, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Ioannidis, a Greek military officer, twice helped plot successful coups in his own country, and once in Cyprus.

name: Bobby Thomson
headline: Bobby Thomson Dies at 86; Hit Epic Home Run
abstract: Thomson’s 1951 “shot heard round the world” endures as perhaps the most dramatic play in baseball history.

name: Francesco Cossiga
profession: Led Italy and Its Antiterrorism Battle
headline: Francesco Cossiga Is Dead at 82; Led Italy and Its Antiterrorism Battle
abstract: Mr. Cossiga held a number of crucial positions, including prime minister and president, and led Italy’s fight against domestic terrorism in the mid-1970s.

name: Herman Leonard
headline: Herman Leonard Dies at 87; His Photos Visualized Jazz
abstract: Mr. Leonard’s photos, discovered years later, chronicled the postwar jazz scene.

name: Amin al-Hindi
headline: Amin al-Hindi, Former Palestinian Intelligence Chief, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Hindi was an associate of Yasir Arafat who was widely suspected of having played an organizing role in the deadly attack on Israeli athletes at the 1972 Munich Olympics.

name: Joe L. Brown
headline: Joe L. Brown, Built Pirates’ Championship Teams, Dies at 91
abstract: As general manager of the Pittsburgh Pirates from 1955 to 1976, Mr. Brown was the architect behind the 1960 and 1971 World Series teams.

name: Frank Kermode
headline: Frank Kermode, a Critic Who Wrote With Style, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Kermode was a professor at English and American universities who wrote or edited more than 50 books and who was knighted for his work.

name: John P. Fishwick
headline: John P. Fishwick, Railroad Executive, Dies at 93
abstract: As chief executive of the Norfolk and Western Railway, Mr. Fishwick opened talks to merge with Southern Railway, which eventually led to formation of Norfolk Southern.

name: Bill Millin
headline: Bill Millin, Scottish D-Day Piper, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Millin, who was asked to play the bagpipes as British troops landed in Normandy, was immortalized in the movie “The Longest Day.”

name: Harold Connolly
profession: Beat Odds in Olympics and Romance
headline: Harold Connolly, Who Beat Odds in Olympics and Romance, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Connolly won the hammer throw at the 1956 Olympics despite a withered left arm, and later married the women’s discus champion.

name: Mario Obledo
headline: Mario Obledo, Hispanic Rights Leader, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Obledo was a founder and leader of major Hispanic-American organizations and served as California’s secretary of health and welfare.

name: Roy Pinney
headline: Roy Pinney, Man of Snakes, Baby Photos and Adventure, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Mr. Pinney, who held many distinctions as a writer, journalist and snake lover, was once described as “a hard man to pin down” because of his achievements.

name: Harrison Price
headline: Harrison Price, a Planner of Disney Parks, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Price helped plan various Disney amusement parks, and also worked with SeaWorld, Knott’s Berry Farm and Six Flags.

name: Robert W. Gundlach
headline: Robert W. Gundlach, Leading Xerox Inventor, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Gundlach had 155 patents to his name on behalf of Xerox when he retired in 1995, including a crucial innovation in offset duplicating.

name: O. Ivar Lovaas
profession: Pioneer in Developing Therapies for Autism
headline: O. Ivar Lovaas, Pioneer in Developing Therapies for Autism, Dies at 83
abstract: A psychologist who developed widely used therapies for children with autism, and who helped change the treatment and the perception of the condition.

name: James M. Tanner
headline: Dr. James M. Tanner, an Expert in How Children Grow, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Dr. Tanner was a pediatrician who developed standards that helped define what constitutes normal growth.

name: George David Weiss
headline: George David Weiss, Writer of Hit Pop Songs, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Weiss was a songwriter whose credits include “The Lion Sleeps Tonight’ and “What a Wonderful World.”

name: Edward Kean
headline: Edward Kean, Chief Writer of ‘Howdy Doody,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Kean, the chief writer of “The Howdy Doody Show” and the man behind its theme song’s lyrics, once said he was probably best known for coining the word “cowabunga.”

name: Benjamin Kaplan
