headline: Benjamin Kaplan, Crucial Figure in Nazi Trials, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Kaplan, a state supreme court judge, helped craft the indictment of the Nazi war criminals who were tried at Nuremberg while an officer in the Army.

name: Christoph Schlingensief
headline: Christoph Schlingensief, Artistic Provocateur, Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. Schlingensief, a German filmmaker, theater director and all-purpose gadfly, waged a tireless assault on received opinion in the arts and politics.

name: William Saxbe
headline: William Saxbe, Attorney General During Watergate Inquiry, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Saxbe, a blunt-spoken Republican maverick from Ohio, was a Nixon appointee who as attorney general presided during the Watergate inquiry.

name: David Rowland
profession: Maker of a Tidily Stacked Chair
headline: David Rowland, Maker of a Tidily Stacked Chair, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Rowland’s invention, which was an alternative to the folding chair, made it possible to store many chairs in a small space.

name: Marcel Albert
profession: Air Ace of France in World War II
headline: Marcel Albert, Air Ace of France in World War II, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Albert was one of the leading French fighter pilots of World War II, flying Soviet-built planes against the Nazis on the Eastern front.

name: Satoshi Kon
headline: Satoshi Kon, Anime Filmmaker, Dies at 46
abstract: Mr. Kon was a Japanese filmmaker and comic-book artist whose dazzling visual compositions won him a devoted following.

name: Franz Schurmann
headline: Franz Schurmann, Cold War Expert on China, Dies at 84
abstract: A professor at the University of California, Berkeley, for nearly four decades, he traveled the world and helped found the Pacific News Service.

name: C. Joseph Genster
headline: C. Joseph Genster, Marketer of Metrecal, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Genster helped develop Metrecal, the meal in a can for dieters that swept America at the beginning of the 1960s, and led its expansion.

name: Michel Montignac
headline: Michel Montignac, Creator of Trend-Setting Diet, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Montignac, who was overweight as young man, had no medical training, but created a diet that was a precursor to the South Beach Diet.

name: Jack Pitney
headline: Jack Pitney, Who Made Much of the Mini, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. Pitney was the vice president for marketing at BMW of North America and led the wildly successful introduction of BMW’s updated Mini Cooper into the American market.

name: Thomas White Jr.
headline: Thomas White Jr., City Councilman From Queens, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. White pushed for economic development and was a champion of women and minority business owners.

name: Gloria Winters
profession: Perky Star of Wholesome Sky King
headline: Gloria Winters, Perky Star of Wholesome ‘Sky King’, Dies
abstract: Ms. Winters, who personified American innocence in the 1950s, also had roles in “The Life of Riley,” “Richard Diamond, Private Detective” and “Death Valley Days.”

name: John Holusha
headline: John Holusha, a Writer for The Times, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Holusha reported on business subjects, including the automobile industry and real estate, for nearly three decades.

name: Daniel Davison
headline: Daniel Davison, Banker Who Revitalized U.S. Trust, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Davison led a turnaround at United States Trust by riveting its attention on the very rich, even if it meant being willing to walk his clients’ dogs.

name: Martin Dannenberg
headline: Martin Dannenberg Is Dead at 94; Found Nuremberg Laws Document
abstract: In 1945, Mr. Dannenberg, an Army intelligence officer, discovered the German document signed by Adolf Hitler that stripped Jews of their citizenship and rights.

name: Robert Ingersoll
headline: Robert Ingersoll, who Served as Envoy to Japan, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Ingersoll took his business acumen as head of one of the country’s largest manufacturing corporations to the diplomatic table as ambassador to Japan and later deputy secretary of state.

name: Jackson Gillis
headline: Jackson Gillis, Prolific Writer of TV Drama, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Gillis, a slogger in the trenches of television writing whose career spanned more than four decades, put words in the mouths of numbers of TV icons.

name: William P. Foster
headline: William P. Foster, Pioneer of Florida A&M’s Marching 100, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Foster was an innovator of the distinctive style of the popular Florida A&M marching band.

name: Alain Corneau
headline: Alain Corneau, César-Winning Film Director, Dies at 67
abstract: The director was best known for his 1991 award-winning film “Tous les Matins du Monde.”

name: Jacob Bigeleisen
headline: Jacob Bigeleisen, Isotope Chemist on Manhattan Project, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Bigeleisen’s approach was ultimately unsuccessful, but he went on to open a new field of chemistry that studied ways to speed up or slow down chemical reactions.

name: Laurent Fignon
headline: Laurent Fignon, Gruff French Cyclist, Dies at 50
abstract: Mr. Fignon was a French cyclist who won more 75 races including the Tour de France in back-to-back years.

name: Anton Geesink
headline: Anton Geesink, Medalist Who Helped Popularize Judo, Dies at 76
abstract: Geesink stunned Japan when he defeated Japanese opponents to win the 1961 world title and capture a gold medal at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics.

name: Dorothy Sucher
headline: Dorothy Sucher, Reporter in Press-Freedom Case, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Sucher’s reporting for a small Maryland newspaper led to a Supreme Court ruling bolstering freedom of the press.

name: Corinne Day
headline: Corinne Day, Photographer of Kate Moss, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Day, whose photos of Ms. Moss in the 1990s took a startling detour from the glossy world of supermodels, helped usher in a new era in fashion photography.

name: Gail Koff
headline: Gail Koff, Principal in Jacoby & Meyers, Dies at 65
abstract: Ms. Koff was the “silent partner” when the national law firm opened its first New York office.

name: Vance Bourjaily
headline: Vance Bourjaily, Novelist Exploring Postwar America, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Bourjaily’s novels often explored what it meant to be an American at a particular historical moment.

name: Cammie King
headline: Cammie King, Scarlett and Rhett’s Girl, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. King played Scarlett O’Hara and Rhett Butler’s ill-fated little girl, Bonnie Blue Butler, in “Gone With the Wind.”

name: George Hitchcock
headline: George Hitchcock, Kayak Magazine Founder, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Hitchcock, a playwright and poet himself, included a wide variety of poets and writers in his literary magazine.

name: Robert Schimmel
headline: Robert Schimmel, Comic, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Schimmel, a comedian, was known for his direct, often scatological approach.

name: Raimon Panikkar
headline: Raimon Panikkar, Catholic Theologian, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Panikkar was a Roman Catholic whose embrace of Hindu scriptures and Buddhism made him an influential voice for promoting dialogue between the world’s religions.

name: Mick Lally
profession: Irish Actor and Founder of the Druid Theater
headline: Mick Lally, Irish Actor and Founder of the Druid Theater, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Lally’s troupe has received international acclaim for its productions of works by Irish playwrights, especially J. M. Synge and Martin McDonagh.

name: Larry Ashmead
profession: Editor With an Eye for Talent
headline: Larry Ashmead, Editor With an Eye for Talent, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Ashmead one of America’s most successful book editors, handling best-selling writers like Susan Isaacs, Tony Hillerman, Isaac Asimov and Quentin Crisp.

name: Frank C. Garland
profession: Connected Vitamin D Deficiency and Cancer
headline: Frank C. Garland, 60, Who Connected Vitamin D Deficiency and Cancer, Dies
abstract: An epidemiologist, Dr. Garland’s work helped establish a link between vitamin D deficiency and some cancers, including colon and breast cancer.

name: Paul Conrad
headline: Paul Conrad, Cartoonist, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Conrad’s editorial cartoons in The Los Angeles Times and other papers slashed presidents, skewered pomposity and exposed what he saw as injustice for six decades.

name: Tsung-yi Lin
headline: Tsung-yi Lin, 89, Psychiatrist With Global Approach, Dies
abstract: Dr. Lin also all but built the mental health system from the ground up in his native Taiwan, later helping governments in other developing nations to do the same.

name: Jefferson Thomas
headline: Jefferson Thomas, Who Helped Integrate Little Rock School, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Thomas was one of nine black students who, protected by federal soldiers, attended high school in a landmark civil rights case.

name: Corneille
profession: Dutch Artist With a Lyrical Modernism
headline: Corneille, Dutch Artist With a Lyrical Modernism, Dies at 88
abstract: Corneille was one of the founders of the Cobra group of artists who stressed color and vitality.

name: Seymour Pine
headline: Seymour Pine Dies at 91; Led Raid on Stonewall Inn
abstract: Inspector Pine, who was the deputy police inspector who led the raid on a gay bar in Greenwich Village in 1969, later apologized for his role in the raid.

name: Virginia B. Smith
headline: Virginia B. Smith, Former Vassar President, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Ms. Smith helped shaped education policy as a researcher, college president and public official.

name: Israel Tal
headline: Maj. Gen. Israel Tal, Israeli Military Strategist, Is Dead at 85
abstract: General Tal’s role in Israel’s wars and his work on the Merkava tank earned him recognition as one of the world’s greatest armor commanders.

name: Elizabeth Jenkins
headline: Elizabeth Jenkins, Woman of Letters, Dies at 104
abstract: In novels and biographies, Ms. Jenkins looked at lives with a psychological dimension.

name: John W. Kluge
headline: John W. Kluge, Founder of Metromedia, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Kluge parlayed a small fortune into a multibillion-dollar communications empire.

name: David Dortort
headline: David Dortort, ‘Bonanza’ Creator, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Dortort’s “Bonanza” broke the mold for westerns by focusing on a loving family rather than outlaws.

name: Clive Donner
headline: Clive Donner, 1960s-Era Film Director, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Donner was part of the British New Wave filmmakers with “The Caretaker” and “What’s New Pussycat?”

name: Thomas Guinzburg
headline: Thomas Guinzburg, Paris Review Co-Founder, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Guinzburg was an editor and publisher who helped create The Paris Review and who later led Viking Press.

name: R. Smith Simpson
headline: Foreign Service Officer R. Smith Simpson Dies at 103
abstract: Mr. Simpson contended that the great majority of college graduates were “wholly unprepared for diplomatic work” and did something about the problem.

name: Juan Mari Bras
headline: Juan Mari Bras, Voice for Separate Puerto Rico, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Mari Bras was a leading advocate for Puerto Rican independence who took his fight to Congress and the United Nations.

name: Irwin Silber
profession: Champion of the Folk Music Revival
headline: Irwin Silber, Champion of the Folk Music Revival, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Silber, a founder of the folk-music magazine Sing Out!, was one of the prime movers behind the folk-music revival of the 1950s and 1960s.

name: Bent Larsen
headline: Bent Larsen, Chess Grandmaster, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Larson was a perennial challenger for the world championship during the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Lucius Walker
headline: Lucius Walker, Baptist Pastor for Peace, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Walker gained national attention with calls for reparations for the descendants of slaves and with repeated violations of the United States embargo of Cuba through caravans of humanitarian aid.

name: William H. Goetzmann
headline: William H. Goetzmann, Pulitzer-Winning Historian, Dies at 80
abstract: With his 1966 book “Exploration and Empire,” Mr. Goetzmann showed that America’s exploration of the West was a calculated effort to gather information.

name: Claude Chabrol
headline: Claude Chabrol, 80, Director, Dies
abstract: Mr. Chabrol was one of the pioneers of the French New Wave and produced a series of stylish, suspense-filled films like “The Butcher” and “The Unfaithful Wife.”

name: Kevin McCarthy
headline: Kevin McCarthy, Actor, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. McCarthy will always be best known as the star of the 1956 sci-fi movie “Invasion of the Body Snatchers.”

name: Ron Kramer
profession: Tight End With Packers and Lions
headline: Ron Kramer, Tight End With Packers and Lions, Dies at 75
abstract: The former tight end for the Green Bay Packers and the Detroit Lions was a two-time all-American at the University of Michigan who became one of the first outstanding tight ends in the National Football League.

name: Gene Case
headline: Gene Case, Who Marketed After-Shave and Politicians, Is Dead at 72
abstract: Mr. Case, who marketed Lyndon B. Johnson and Tums, worked in advertising from the age of “Mad Men” to the age of Obama.

name: George C. Williams
headline: George C. Williams, 83, Theorist on Evolution, Dies
abstract: Dr. Williams was a biologist who helped shape the theory that natural selection works at the level of the individual and not for the benefit of the group.

name: Barbara Holland
headline: Barbara Holland, Defender of Small Vices, Dies at 77
abstract: A wry essayist and memoirist, Ms. Holland argued on behalf of drinking, cursing, even smoking.

name: Harold Gould
headline: Harold Gould, Character Actor, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Gould appeared on television shows like “Rhoda” and “Golden Girls” and in films like “Love and Death” and “Silent Movie” over five decades.

name: Ronald Walters
headline: Ronald Walters, Rights Leader and Scholar, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Walters organized one of the nation’s first lunch-counter sit-ins as a young man, and then went on to a distinguished academic career.

name: Michael Burn
headline: Michael Burn, Writer and Adventurer, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Burn’s life included an early flirtation with Nazism, a daring commando raid, imprisonment by the Germans and a love affair with a British spy.

name: Edwin Newman
headline: Edwin Newman, Journalist, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Newman, a genially grumpy NBC newsman, was equally famous as a defender of the English language.

name: Varnette Honeywood
headline: Varnette Honeywood, Whose Art Appeared on ‘Cosby Show,’ Dies at 59
abstract: Ms. Honeywood’s semiabstract paintings, with bright colors and complex patterns, presented an upbeat picture of black American life.

name: Jim Winner
profession: Developer of the Club Antitheft Device
headline: Jim Winner, Developer of the Club Antitheft Device, Dies at 81
abstract: The idea for the Club grew out of his days in the Army, when soldiers would secure their Jeeps by placing a chain on the steering wheel.

name: John Freeborn
headline: John Freeborn, British Fighter Pilot, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Freeborn was acclaimed for his exploits during World War II, but he was also a central figure in an episode of “friendly fire” that brought him great anguish.

name: Dodge Morgan
headline: Dodge Morgan, Who Sailed Around World, Dies at 78
abstract: The 1986 voyage — which lasted 150 days 1 hour 6 minutes — shattered the previous record of 292 days set by a British sailor.

name: Donald W. Davis
headline: Donald W. Davis, Who Headed Stanley Works, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Davis modernized the company, shifting Stanley Works’ focus from industrial supply to the nascent do-it-yourself market.

name: John Goeken
headline: John Goeken, Who Led MCI and Splintered AT&T, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Mr. Goeken was a tenacious entrepreneur who founded the long-distance carrier that changed the shape of the nation’s telephone industry by challenging the monopoly of AT&T.

name: Manfred Gans
profession: Combed Wartime Europe for His Parents
headline: Manfred Gans Is Dead at 88; Combed Wartime Europe for His Parents
abstract: Mr. Gans, after helping free his hometown in Germany and finding that his house had been used as a Nazi headquarters, embarked on a quest across hundreds of miles of German-held territory.

name: Wallace Turner
headline: Wallace Turner, Pulitzer Prize-Winning Reporter, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Turner shared the Prize for exposing corruption in Portland, Ore., and later illuminated the inner workings of the Mormon Church.

name: William Coblentz
headline: William Coblentz, California Power Broker, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Coblentz, who had notable dealings with Ronald Reagan, the Hearst family and Grace Slick, helped shape a swath of California’s postwar history.

name: Fathi Osman
headline: Fathi Osman, Scholar of Islam, Dies at 82
abstract: Dr. Osman was a scholar who worked to explain Islam to the non-Muslim world and demonstrate to Muslims the faith’s flexibility.

name: Jill Johnston
headline: Jill Johnston, Critic Who Wrote ‘Lesbian Nation,’ Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Johnston championed lesbian feminism and caused a scandal at a debate at Town Hall in Manhattan in 1971, when she and two women started hugging and kissing on stage.

name: Irving Ravetch
headline: Irving Ravetch, Screenwriter of ‘Hud,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Ravetch, who with his wife wrote “Hud,” “Norma Rae” and “The Long, Hot Summer,” said the couple “often needed an outside story” on which to “build a whole new drama.”

name: Eileen Nearne
headline: Eileen Nearne, Wartime Spy, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Nearne was one of the secret agents who helped prepare the French resistance for the D-Day landings in 1944.

name: Joyce Beber
profession: Creator of Hotel Ads for Leona Helmsley
headline: Joyce Beber, Creator of Hotel Ads for Leona Helmsley, Dies at 80
abstract: Her advertising agency, Beber Silverstein & Partners, helped promote the Helmsley hotel empire.

name: Antonina Pirozhkova
profession: Engineer and Widow of Isaac Babel
headline: Antonina Pirozhkova, Engineer and Widow of Isaac Babel, Dies at 101
abstract: Ms. Porizhkova campaigned for more than half a century to keep her husband’s literary legacy alive after his execution by Stalin’s K.G.B.

name: Gus Bevona
headline: Gus Bevona, Ex-Union Chief, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Bevona’s persona as a blunt-talking throwback to old-time labor leaders helped him make New York City janitors, handymen and elevator operators the highest paid in the nation.

name: Wayne Winterrowd
headline: Wayne Winterrowd, Gardening Expert, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Winterrowd wrote widely about the subject, designed gardens for others and spent more than 30 years building a seven-acre garden in Vermont that draws visitors from all over the world.

name: Jack Kershaw
headline: Jack Kershaw Is Dead at 96; Challenged Conviction in King’s Death
abstract: Mr. Kershaw was a Tennessee lawyer who argued that James Earl Ray, convicted in the 1968 assassination of the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., was an innocent participant in a conspiracy.

name: Stuart E. Hample
headline: Stuart E. Hample, Humorist and Cartoonist, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Hample, who was also a playwright and performer, wrote “The Silly Book” and was the co-author of “Children’s Letters to God.”

name: Howard Brodie
headline: Howard Brodie, 94, Combat and Courtroom Artist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Brodie sketched troops during World War II and the courtroom trials of the Chicago Seven, Charles Manson and Patty Hearst.

name: Frederick Jelinek
profession: Gave Machines the Key to Human Speech
headline: Frederick Jelinek, Who Gave Machines the Key to Human Speech, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Jelinek unlocked human speech for computers by thinking like a computer.

name: Gennadi I. Yanayev
headline: Gennadi I. Yanayev, 73, Soviet Coup Plotter, Dies
abstract: Mr. Yanayev was a former Soviet apparatchik who was part of an abortive and short-lived coup in 1991.

name: Eddie Fisher
headline: Eddie Fisher, Pop Singer, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Fisher saw his huge fame overshadowed by scandals around his marriages to Debbie Reynolds and Elizabeth Taylor.

name: William Harrison
headline: Dr. William Harrison, Defender of Abortion Rights, Dies at 75
abstract: Dr. Harrison, who was the only abortion provider in northwest Arkansas, owned the Fayetteville Women’s Clinic, a frequent target of protests and attacks.

name: William Harrison
headline: William Harrison, 79, Novelist and ‘Rollerball’ Writer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Harrison also wrote the film “Mountains of the Moon” and taught at the University of Arkansas.

name: Robert W. McCollum
headline: Robert W. McCollum, Who Studied Viral Diseases, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. McCollum made significant contributions to the understanding of viral diseases, including polio, hepatitis and mononucleosis.

name: Ralph T. Coe
headline: Ralph T. Coe, 81, Advocate for Native American Art, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Coe, a former museum director, played a central role in reviving interest in the works of American Indian artists.

name: Murray Sayle
headline: Murray Sayle, Reporter and Adventurer, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Sayle was a legend within the clan of globetrotting journalists, shrewd enough to locate a defected British spy, adventurous enough to track Che Guevara in Bolivian jungles.

name: James W. Heselden
headline: Owner of Segway Company Dies in a Segway Accident
abstract: James W. Heselden, 62, died Sunday after plunging from a cliff in West Yorkshire, England, apparently while on a Segway, the police said.

name: Gloria Stuart
headline: Gloria Stuart, an Actress Rediscovered Late, Dies at 100
abstract: Ms. Stuart was a glamorous blond actress in Hollywood’s golden age who was largely forgotten until she made a memorable comeback in her 80s in “Titanic.”

name: George Blanda
headline: George Blanda, Hall of Fame Football Player, Dies at 83
abstract: Blanda was a quarterback and place-kicker who played professional football longer than anyone else and who retired having scored more points than anyone else.

name: Stanley Chais
headline: Stanley Chais, Investor With Madoff Tie, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Chais, who built a reputation as a prominent investment manager and philanthropist, was caught up in the financial scandal of Bernard L. Madoff.

name: Buddy Collette
headline: Buddy Collette, Musician Who Played With Jazz Greats, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Collette, who played with many jazz greats, also was a leader in the struggle to break racial barriers in the music industry.

name: Sally Menke
headline: Sally Menke, Film Editor for Tarantino, Dies at 56
abstract: Ms. Menke, an Oscar-nominated editor, edited all of Quentin Tarantino’s feature films.

name: Arthur Holch
headline: Arthur Holch, Emmy-Winning Documentarian, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Holch won an Emmy in 1992 for a documentary on Hitler youth, but his most famous documentary depicted the daily lives of blacks in 1961.

name: Clinton Manges
headline: Clinton Manges, Volatile Texas Oilman and Rancher, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Manges amassed a fortune of $1 billion but eventually declared bankruptcy and spent time in prison.

name: Jure Robic
headline: Jure Robic, Endurance Bicyclist, Dies at 45
abstract: A five time-winner of the Race Across America who tested the body’s physical limits.

name: Robert Truax
headline: Robert Truax, a Top Rocket Scientist, Is Dead at 93
abstract: The Encyclopedia Astronautica called Mr. Truax “one of the great originals of American rocketry.” He died at age 93 of prostate cancer on Sept. 17 in Valley Center, Calif., said his wife, Marisol.

name: Greg Giraldo
headline: Greg Giraldo, Insult-Humor Comic, Dies at 44
abstract: Mr. Giraldo became famous for his stinging insult humor, disgruntled rants and frequent appearances on Comedy Central’s highly watched roast series.

name: Tony Curtis
headline: Tony Curtis, Hollywood Leading Man, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Curtis earned an Oscar nomination for “The Defiant Ones,” but the public preferred him in comic roles, as in “Some Like It Hot.”

name: Joe Mantell
headline: Joe Mantell Is Dead at 94; Played Sidekick in ‘Marty’
abstract: Mr. Mantell was a character actor who, nearly 20 years apart, delivered two of movie history’s more memorable lines, one to Ernest Borgnine and one to Jack Nicholson.

name: Joseph Sobran
headline: Joseph Sobran, Writer Whom Buckley Mentored, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Sobran was a hard-hitting conservative writer and moralist whose outspoken antipathy to Israel led to his removal as a senior editor of National Review.

name: Stephen J. Cannell
headline: Stephen J. Cannell, Prolific TV Writer, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Cannell wrote more than 1,000 episodes of various shows, primarily crime dramas, and created almost 20 series, including “The Rockford Files.”

name: Georges Charpak
headline: Georges Charpak, Physics Nobel Winner, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Charpak won the prize in 1992 for inventing a device to sift through the billions of hurtling subatomic particles liberated by collisions in atom smashers.

name: Georgi A. Arbatov
headline: Georgi A. Arbatov, a Bridge Between Cold War Superpowers, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Arbatov was the senior “Amerikanist” in the Soviet Communist Party in the final decades of the cold war and served as the Kremlin’s voice for a generation of American television viewers.

name: Art Gilmore
headline: Art Gilmore, the Voice of Coming Attractions, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Gilmore, an occasional actor, was best known for narrating radio and television shows, as well as movie trailers.

name: Buddy Morrow
headline: Buddy Morrow , Trombonist and Bandleader, Dies at 91
abstract: In a career spanning more than seven decades, Mr. Morrow led the Tommy Dorsey Orchestra and played for the “Tonight Show” band.

name: Maury Allen
headline: Maury Allen, Sportswriter and Prolific Author, Dies at 78
abstract: Maury Allen was a longtime sportswriter for The New York Post who may have set a record for the number of books on sports he turned out.

name: Gerald S. Lesser
headline: Gerald S. Lesser, Shaper of ‘Sesame Street,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Lesser, a Harvard psychologist, helped ensure from the start that the venture into education by television would be both enjoyable and instructive.

name: Dick Griffey
headline: Dick Griffey, Founder of Solar Records, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Mr. Griffey started the label — known for bringing a funky, laid back, California sound to soul, R&B and disco in the ’70s and ’80s — as a spinoff from Soul Train Records.

name: Dolores Wilson
headline: Dolores Wilson, Met Soprano, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Wilson, who appeared at the Met 26 times between 1954 and 1959, was praised by critics for her silvery voice and assured stage presence.

name: Sidney J. Weinberg Jr.
headline: Sidney J. Weinberg Jr., Former Goldman Executive, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Weinberg was a member of the family dynasty that played a central role at Goldman Sachs starting in 1907.

name: Norman Wisdom
headline: Norman Wisdom, Funnyman, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Wisdom was for six decades one of Britain’s most celebrated comics, appearing in nearly 20 films and many television shows as well as in live performances.

name: Andy Albeck
headline: Andy Albeck Is Dead at 89; Headed United Artists
abstract: Mr. Albeck’s three turbulent years as president of United Artists included the release of the praised “Raging Bull” and the damned “Heaven’s Gate.”

name: Sherman J. Maisel
headline: Sherman J. Maisel, Former Fed Governor, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Maisel’s research laid the intellectual groundwork for government support of the mortgage market.

name: Stephen Pace
headline: Stephen Pace, Painter and Abstract Expressionist, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Pace’s exuberant style applied Abstract Expressionist scale and directness to figurative painting.

name: Phillips Talbot
headline: Phillips Talbot, U.S. Envoy in Cold War, Dies at 95
abstract: Serving in the Kennedy and Johnson administrations, Mr. Talbot worked to avert conflicts in South Asia and the Middle East.

name: Milka Planinc
headline: Milka Planinc, Former Yugoslav Premier, Dies at 85
abstract: Mrs. Planinc, who served from 1982 to 1986, was Yugoslavia’s first female prime minister.

name: Roy Ward Baker
headline: Roy Ward Baker, Prolific British Filmmaker, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Baker, an undersung British filmmaker, is best known for directing “A Night to Remember,” a vivid black-and-white rendering of the sinking of the Titanic.

name: William M. Birenbaum
headline: William M. Birenbaum, College Leader, Dies at 87
abstract: A nationally known university administrator who helped rescue Antioch College from looming insolvency during his tenure as president there in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Albertina Walker
headline: Albertina Walker, Soulful Gospel Singer, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Walker founded The Caravans, a group that nurtured many gospel standouts, before embarking on a solo career in the 1970s.

name: Marshall Flaum
headline: Marshall Flaum, Documentary Filmmaker, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Flaum was nominated for Academy Awards for his films about the formation of the state of Israel and the United States involvement in World War I.

name: William Norton
headline: William Norton, Writer Wilder Than His Movies, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Norton was a Hollywood screenwriter whose own life story would stretch the credibility of most screenplays.

name: Johnny Edgecombe
headline: Johnny Edgecombe, British Scandal Figure, Dies at 77
abstract: On Dec. 14, 1962, Mr. Edgecombe fired shots at the London apartment where his former girlfriend and a sometime prostitute was staying, which led to a series of events that brought down a British government.

name: Philippa Foot
headline: Philippa Foot, Renowned Philosopher, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Foot argued that moral judgments have a rational basis, and introduced the renowned ethical thought experiment known as the Trolley Problem.

name: William C. Patrick III
headline: William C. Patrick III, Expert on Germ Warfare, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Patrick made enough germs to kill everyone on earth many times over. Then he worked for nearly four decades to build defenses against them.

name: Solomon Burke
headline: Solomon Burke, Influential Soul Singer, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Burke’s smooth, powerful articulation and mingling of sacred and profane themes helped define soul music in the early 1960s.

name: Joan Sutherland
headline: Joan Sutherland, Flawless Soprano, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Ms. Sutherland helped revitalize an entire repertory of early-19th-century Italian opera of the bel canto school.

name: Maurice Allais
headline: Maurice Allais, Nobel Winner, Dies at 99
abstract: Dr. Allais, the first Frenchman to win the Nobel in economic science, stood out for the quality of his original thinking and how little it was noticed outside France.

name: Carla Cohen
headline: Carla Cohen, Owner of Washington Bookstore, Dies at 74
abstract: Mrs. Cohen’s shop, Politics and Prose, sat at the nexus of Washington’s literary and political scenes and became a requisite stop for authors passing through town.

name: Marcel Lapierre
headline: Marcel Lapierre, Beaujolais Producer, Is Dead at 60
abstract: Mr. Lapierre played a leading role in restoring the diminishing reputation of Beaujolais wines.

name: Robert Tishman
headline: Robert Tishman, Real Estate Developer, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Tishman’s companies etched their mark on the skylines of cities around the nation, including construction of the World Trade Center.

name: Robert Goodnough
headline: Robert Goodnough, Painter Who Eluded Categories, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Goodnough moved among second-generation Abstract Expressionists but at the same time stood apart.

name: David F. Musto
headline: David F. Musto, Expert on Drug Control, Dies at 74
abstract: In offering a comprehensive account of drug use and government drug policy from the 1860s to the present, Mr. Musto’s writings struck a nonpolemical tone rare in a field dominated by partisan zealots.

name: John Huchra
headline: John Huchra Dies at 61; Maps Altered Ideas on Universe
abstract: John Huchra, an astronomer at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics, was part of a team whose maps suggested the existence of great clusters of galaxies.

name: Selma Al-Radi
headline: Selma Al-Radi, Restored Historic Madrasa, Dies at 71
abstract: When the archaeologist first saw the crumbling Yemeni structure, Dr. Radi said, “Wow, this we’ve got to save.”

name: Jerry Marshall
headline: Jerry Marshall, D.J. on New York Radio, Dies at 91
abstract: In his 30-year career, Mr. Marshall presided over shows like “Music Hall” and “The Make-Believe Ballroom” on WNEW and “Record Room” on WMGM.

name: Larry Siegfried
headline: Larry Siegfried, Guard Who Won 5 Titles With Celtics, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Known for solid shooting, mistake-free ball-handling and sticky defense, he played for the Celtics from 1963 to 1970.

name: Richard Morefield
headline: Richard Morefield, Held Hostage in Iran, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Morefield and 51 other Americans were held hostage in Iran in 1979.

name: Simon MacCorkindale
headline: Simon MacCorkindale, Dashing British Actor, Dies at 58
abstract: After being cast in “Death on the Nile,” Mr. MacCorkindale appeared on television shows from “Falcon Crest” to “Dukes of Hazzard.”

name: Benoît Mandelbrot
headline: Benoît Mandelbrot, Novel Mathematician, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Mandelbrot, a maverick mathematician, developed an innovative theory to study uneven shapes and applied it to physics, biology and many other fields.

name: Marzieh
profession: Iranian Singer and Voice of Dissent
headline: Marzieh, Iranian Singer and Voice of Dissent, Dies at 86
abstract: Marzieh was the great diva of Persian traditional song who was silenced after the Islamic Revolution in 1979 but who re-emerged years later outside Iran as a singer and a highly public supporter of the resistance.

name: Louis Henkin
profession: Leader in Field of Human Rights Law
headline: Louis Henkin, Leader in Field of Human Rights Law, Dies at 92
abstract: Professor Henkin was a legal scholar often credited with creating the field of human rights law and the author of classic works on constitutional law and the legal aspects of foreign policy.

name: Barbara Billingsley
headline: Barbara Billingsley, TV’s June Cleaver, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Billingsley, as June Cleaver on the series “Leave It to Beaver,” personified a Hollywood postwar family ideal.

name: Belva Plain
headline: Belva Plain, Novelist of Jewish-American Life, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Plain, who became a best-selling author at age 59, wrote multigenerational family sagas that won a loyal readership in the millions.

name: James E. Fuchs
headline: James E. Fuchs, Innovator in the Shot-Put, Dies at 82
abstract: Fuchs, who set four shot-putting world records, developed a new method that was widely copied in the event.

name: Louis F. Bantle
headline: Louis F. Bantle, Chief of U.S. Tobacco, Dies at 81
abstract: Under Mr. Bantle’s leadership, sales for U.S. Tobacco, best known for its Skoal and Copenhagen brands, grew tenfold.

name: Melvin Lane Powers
headline:
Melvin Lane Powers Is Dead at 68;
Cleared of Murder With Lover-Aunt
abstract: Mr. Powers managed to escape conviction thanks to a lawyer who persuaded the jury to overlook clear motive, bloodstains, palm prints, fingerprints and love letters.

name: Mildred Jefferson
headline: Mildred Jefferson, 84, Anti-Abortion Activist, Is Dead
abstract: In 1951, Dr. Jefferson became the first black woman to graduate from Harvard Medical School.

name: Patricia Herzog
headline: Patricia Herzog, 88, a Lawyer Who Changed Marital Law, Dies
abstract: A case that Ms. Herzog took through the California courts led to a significant change  allowing one divorcing spouse to be reimbursed for having helped the other obtain an advanced degree.

name: Freddy Sez
headline: Freddy Sez, the Yankees’ Pan-Banging Mascot, Dies at 85
abstract: Freddy Schuman, known to fans as Freddy Sez, roamed the stadium’s aisles for more than 20 years with a frying pan and spoon for spectators to whack.

name: Tom Bosley
headline: Tom Bosley, ‘Happy Days’ Dad, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Bosley played the reliably kind father on TV’s “Happy Days” and won a Tony onstage for “Fiorello!”

name: Eric Joisel
headline: Eric Joisel, French Sculptor of Origami, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Joisel, a solitary Frenchman, was widely regarded as one of the most illustrious origami artists in the world.

name: Bob Guccione
headline: Bob Guccione, Penthouse Founder, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Guccione built a pornographic media empire that outraged the guardians of taste and made billions.

name: Paul S. Miller
headline: Paul S. Miller, Advocate for Disabled, Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. Miller, a Harvard law graduate who was rejected by law firms because of his dwarfism, later advised presidents.

name: Georges Mathé
headline: Dr. Georges Mathé, Transplant Pioneer, Dies at 88
abstract: An experiment of Dr. Mathé‘s was called the first successful bone marrow transplant not performed on identical twins.

name: Robert Katz
profession: Wrote About Nazi Massacre in Italy
headline: Robert Katz, Who Wrote About Nazi Massacre in Italy, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Katz incurred the wrath of the Vatican when he accused Pope Pius XII of knowing in advance of the Ardeatine Caves massacre and failing to act.

name: Elizabeth L. Sturz
headline: Elizabeth L. Sturz, Salvaged Troubled Lives, Dies at 93
abstract: Mrs. Sturz started and ran renowned programs to help troubled youths and people suffering from both mental illness and drug addiction.

name: Ari Up
profession: Founder of the Slits Punk Band
headline: Ari Up, a Founder of the Slits Punk Band, Dies at 48
abstract: Ari Up’s rebel persona was an inspiration for women who followed her into the world of punk rock.

name: Hannelore Schmidt
headline: Hannelore Schmidt, 91, Wife of West German Chancellor, Dies
abstract: Mrs. Schmidt was a conservationist who won the affection of Germans as the down-to-earth, easygoing presence at the side of Helmut Schmidt, who led West Germany from 1974 to 1982.

name: James F. Neal
headline: James F. Neal, Litigated Historic Cases, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Neal was a lawyer who prosecuted Hoffa and Watergate figures and defended Elvis’s doctor.

name: Consuelo Crespi
headline: Consuelo Crespi, Aristocrat of Fashion, Dies at 82
abstract: Countess Crespi, a New Yorker turned Italian countess, helped shape postwar high fashion by modeling, and editing Italian Vogue.

name: Dick Miles
headline: Dick Miles, Record-Setting U.S. Table Tennis Player, Dies at 85
abstract: Miles had a powerful forehand and exceptional defensive skills, which helped him win a record-setting 10 national championships.

name: Michael Tabor
headline: Michael Tabor, Black Panther Who Fled to Algeria, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Tabor was one of 13 Black Panther Party members acquitted in 1971 of conspiring to bomb public buildings and murder police officers in New York City.

name: Marion Brown
headline: Marion Brown, Free-Jazz Saxophonist, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Brown performed in a low-key style that was distinctive in the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Harvey Phillips
headline: Harvey Phillips, a Titan of the Tuba, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Phillips, who created the tradition of holiday music for tuba at the Rockefeller Center skating rink, was a teacher and evangelist for that oft-maligned instrument.

name: Burton Roberts
headline: Burton Roberts, 88, Tom Wolfe’s Model Judge, Dies
abstract: Judge Roberts was a former justice in the Bronx and the inspiration for Myron Kovitsky in Tom Wolfe’s novel “Bonfire of the Vanities.”

name: Betty S. Murphy
headline: Betty S. Murphy, a Leader of the N.L.R.B., Dies at 77
abstract: Betty Southard Murphy was a former reporter who became the first woman to serve on the labor board.

name: Sol Steinmetz
headline: Sol Steinmetz, an Expert on Language, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Steinmetz, a lexicographer and author, was sought out for his opinions on matters semantical, grammatical and etymological.

name: Sylvia Sleigh
headline: Sylvia Sleigh, Provocative Portraitist and Feminist Artist, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Sleigh put a feminist spin on the portrait genre by painting male nudes in poses that recalled the female subjects of Ingres, Velázquez and Titian.

name: Leo Cullum
headline: Leo Cullum, New Yorker Cartoonist, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Cullum’s blustering businessmen, clueless doctors, venal lawyers and all-too-human dogs and cats amused readers of The New Yorker for the past 33 years.

name: Gregory Isaacs
headline: Gregory Isaacs, Reggae Singer and Songwriter, Dies at 60
abstract: A prolific output of songs added luster to a man called “the Frank Sinatra of Jamaica” for his elegant vocal phrasing.

name: Alex Anderson
headline: Alex Anderson, Creator of Rocky and Bullwinkle, Dies at 90
abstract: Rocky the flying squirrel and his buddy, the bumbling moose Bullwinkle, were television cartoon characters who captivated young baby boomers in the early ’60s.

name: Constance Reid
headline: Constance Reid, Biographer of Mathematicians, Dies at 92
abstract: Mrs. Reid popularized important mathematicians by drawing attention to her subjects’ often dramatic lives.

name: S. Neil Fujita
headline: S. Neil Fujita, Innovative Graphic Designer, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Fujita created some of the most striking album covers and designed the book jackets for “In Cold Blood” and “The Godfather.”

name: Lamont Johnson
headline: Lamont Johnson, Emmy-Winning Director, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Johnson, who directed more than 150 television shows, miniseries and movies of the week, was known for bringing an understated touch to delicate subjects.

name: Argentine Ex-Leader
headline: Argentine Ex-Leader Dies; Political Impact Is Murky
abstract: Néstor Kirchner guided Argentina out of financial crisis in 2001 and was expected to run for president again next year, seeking to succeed his wife, president since 2007.

name: Eva Ibbotson
headline: Eva Ibbotson, Children’s Book Author, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Ibbotson, who published her first children’s book at 50, was best known for her comic novels of enchantment.

name: Richard T. Gill
headline: Richard T. Gill, Economist and Opera Singer, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Gill was a Harvard economist who became an opera singer at the Met.

name: Hall Thompson
headline: Hall Thompson, Who Stirred Golf Controversy, Dies at 87
abstract: The founder of Shoal Creek Country Club, host of major golf events, was quoted as saying it would not be pressured into admitting black members.

name: James MacArthur
headline: James MacArthur, ‘Danno,’ Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. MacArthur chased thieves, hit men and other assorted loonies as Danno on “Hawaii Five-O.”

name: Lisa Blount
profession: Cynical Friend in Officer and a Gentleman
headline: Lisa Blount, Cynical Friend in ‘Officer and a Gentleman,’ Dies at 53
abstract: Ms. Blount played Lynette Pomeroy, a local girl hoping to marry a Navy pilot trainee in the 1982 film.

name: George Cain
headline: George Cain, Writer of ‘Blueschild Baby,’ Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Cain was a writer whose 1970 novel was greeted as an important exploration of the black urban experience in the United States.

name: Liang Congjie
headline: Liang Congjie, Chinese Environmental Pioneer, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Liang founded China’s first legally recognized environmental organization and came to be honored by international groups and the Chinese government alike.

name: Paul Kolton
headline: Paul Kolton, Who Led the American Stock Exchange, Dies at 87
abstract: When Mr. Kolton was named president of the Amex in 1971, it was the first time an in-house employee was put atop one of the major securities exchanges.

name: Mary Emma Allison
headline: Mary Emma Allison, Who Inspired Charitable Ghouls, Dies at 93
abstract: Mrs. Allison co-founded Trick-or-Treat for Unicef, in which American children get to help less fortunate ones abroad.

name: Ehud Netzer
headline: Ehud Netzer, Archeologist Who Unearthed Herod’s Tomb, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Netzer was professor emeritus of archeology at Hebrew University, had led high-profile digs across the country and helped educate several generations of Israeli archeologists.

name: Roy Skinner
profession: Recruited First Black Basketball Player in SEC
headline: Roy Skinner, Who Recruited First Black Basketball Player in SEC, Dies at 80
abstract: When Skinner was the coach at Vanderbilt University, he recruited Perry Wallace, a high school star in Nashville and the first black athlete to play varsity basketball.

name: Leigh Van Valen
headline: Leigh Van Valen, Evolution Revolutionary, Dies at 76
abstract: Dr. Van Valen was a scientist whose most famous hypothesis — which sought to explain why there are two sexes — was named for the Red Queen in Lewis Carroll’s “Through the Looking Glass.”

name: Theodore C. Sorensen
headline: Theodore C. Sorensen, 82, Kennedy Counselor, Dies
abstract: Mr. Sorensen was best known for passages of soaring rhetoric, but his role as an adviser went beyond that of presidential ghost-writer.

name: Harry Mulisch
headline: Harry Mulisch, Dutch Novelist, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Mulisch’s gift for writing with clarity about moral and philosophical themes made him an enormously influential figure in the Netherlands and earned him recognition abroad.

name: Maurice Lucas
headline: Maurice Lucas, Bruising Forward for Trail Blazers, Dies at 58
abstract: The prototype for a power forward, Lucas joined with Bill Walton to lead Portland to its only N.B.A. championship in 1977.

name: George Hickenlooper
headline: George Hickenlooper, Film Director, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. Hickenlooper won an Emmy for his documentary film about the making of Coppola’s “Apocalypse Now.”

name: Shannon Tavarez
headline: Shannon Tavarez, Nala in ‘Lion King’, Dies at 11
abstract: Shannon spent seven months performing in the show before receiving a diagnosis of leukemia in April.

name: Charlie O’Donnell
headline: Charlie O’Donnell, Whose Voice Was Fixture on TV, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. O’Donnell was best known for heralding the opening of “Wheel of Fortune,” but he was also the off-camera voice for other game shows and the Oscars and Emmys.

name: Viktor Chernomyrdin
headline: Viktor Chernomyrdin, Russian Ex-Premier, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Chernomyrdin founded the state-owned gas monopoly Gazprom and served as Russia’s prime minister during the economic turmoil of the 1990s.

name: Jerry Bock
headline: Jerry Bock, ‘Fiddler on the Roof’ Composer, Dies at 81
abstract: A partnership between Mr. Bock and the lyricist Sheldon Harnick yielded “Fiorello!” and “She Loves Me,” but their greatest triumph was “Fiddler”; its first production ran from 1964 to 1972.

name: Andy Irons
headline: Andy Irons, Surf Champion, Is Dead at 32
abstract: Mr. Irons, an intense competitor from Hawaii, had a progressive wave riding style and intense rivalty that invigorated the sport’s competitive scene.

name: Clyde King
headline: Clyde King, Who Found Niche as Steinbrenner’s Troubleshooter, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. King spent six decades in baseball as a player, coach, manager, scout and executive, notably as a longtime Yankees adviser.

name: Joseph Gavin
profession: Helped Put First Man on Moon
headline: Joseph Gavin, Who Helped Put First Man on Moon, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Gavin’s shepherding of the lunar module’s development elevated him to prominence.

name: Sparky Anderson
profession: Won World Series With Reds and Tigers
headline: Sparky Anderson Dies at 76;Won World Series With Reds and Tigers
abstract: Mr. Anderson won World Series championships with the Cincinnati Reds of the National League and the Detroit Tigers of the American League.

name: Glen Little
profession: Better Known as Frosty the Clown
headline: Glen Little, Better Known as Frosty the Clown, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Little was a teacher and mentor to a generation of clowns with the Ringling Brothers and Barnum & Bailey Circus.

name: Jill Clayburgh
headline: Jill Clayburgh Dies at 66; Starred in Feminist Roles
abstract: Ms. Clayburgh, who began her career on Broadway in the late 1960s, received two Oscar nominations for her screen work.

name: Charles McDowell
headline: Charles McDowell, Commentator, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. McDowell was a newspaper columnist also known for his roles on “Washington Week in Review” and in Ken Burns films.

name: Shirley Verrett
profession: Opera Singer of Power and Grace
headline: Shirley Verrett, Opera Singer of Power and Grace, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Ms. Verrett, called the Black Callas, sang both mezzo-soprano and soprano roles, including Lady Macbeth, Carmen and Tosca.

name: Jule Sugarman
profession: Director and Architect of Head Start
headline: Jule Sugarman, Director and Architect of Head Start, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Sugarman was one of the primary architects of the Head Start program, which has helped more than 27 millions children since its creation in 1965.

name: Geoffrey Crawley
headline: Geoffrey Crawley, 83, Dies; Gently Deflated a Fairy Hoax
abstract: Articles by Mr. Crawley, an English photographic scientist, helped one of the most enduring photographic hoaxes of the 20th century.

name: Charles Reynolds
headline: Charles Reynolds, Magicians’ Magician, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Reynolds helped magicians refine their acts and had two ways to make an elephant disappear.

name: Artie Wilson
headline: Artie Wilson, Shortstop Who Was Mentor to Mays, Dies at 90
abstract: Wilson, a slap-hitting shortstop, played five years for the Birmingham Black Barons, where he twice led the Negro American League in batting and guided Willie Mays.

name: Michael Seifert
profession: SS Guard at Camp in Italy
headline: Michael Seifert, SS Guard at Camp in Italy, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Seifert had been known as the “Beast of Bolzano,” for his brutality as a guard at a Nazi concentration camp in northern Italy, during World War II.

name: Howard Van Hyning
headline: Howard Van Hyning, Percussionist and Gong Enthusiast, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Van Hyning, a New York City Opera musician, became so entranced with a rare set of gongs for Puccini’s “Turandot” that he eventually acquired them.

name: Jack Levine
headline: Jack Levine, a Painter Who Twinned Realism and Satire, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Levine, a prolific painter, bucked the art world’s movement toward the abstract, drawing inspiration instead from old masters.

name: Emilio Massera
headline: Emilio Massera, Leader of Brutal Argentine Junta, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Massera had been in charge of a notorious political prison where thousands were tortured and killed.

name: Rudolf Barshai
headline: Rudolf Barshai, Conductor and Violist, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Barshai, a founder of the Borodin Quartet and founder of the Moscow Chamber Orchestra, defected from the Soviet Union in the 1970s.

name: Walter Isard
headline: Walter Isard, Economist Who Studied How Regions Evolve, Dies at 91
abstract: He was an economist who examined relationships between such factors as geography, migration and land use before the study of peace as a scientific discipline.

name: Quintin Dailey
headline: Quintin Dailey, Gifted but Troubled Player, Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. Dailey earned All-American honors at the University of San Francisco, but his missteps contributed to the university’s decision to drop its storied basketball program for three years.

name: Robert Lipshutz
headline: Robert Lipshutz, Carter Aide, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Lipshutz had an important behind-the-scenes role in the Camp David peace accords.

name: Dino De Laurentiis
headline: Dino De Laurentiis, Prolific Film Producer, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. De Laurentiis produced hundreds of movies in his career, including “Serpico” and “Three Days of the Condor.”

name: Clyde Summers
headline: Clyde Summers, Advocate of Labor Union Democracy, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Summers, a law professor, played a role in writing the 1959 federal law that guaranteed democratic rights to union members.

name: Harold P. Ford
headline: Harold P. Ford, C.I.A. Analyst, Dies at 89
abstract: Outside the agency, Mr. Ford was known for accusing Robert M. Gates, the former director and current defense secretary, of slanting reports on the Soviet Union.

name: Adam Pinsker
profession: Manager and Adviser of Arts Groups
headline: Adam Pinsker, Manager and Adviser of Arts Groups, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Pinsker managed orchestras, chamber music ensembles and dance troupes and successfully advised dance companies on how to survive by professionalizing their management.

name: Henryk Gorecki
headline: Henryk Gorecki, Polish Composer, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Mr. Gorecki was best known for his Symphony No. 3, which sold more than a million copies on CD in the 1990s.

name: Coleman Jacoby
headline: Coleman Jacoby, TV Comedy Writer, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Jacoby helped create some of Jackie Gleason’s most memorable characters.

name: Richard Bing
headline: Richard Bing, Pioneering Heart Researcher, Dies at 101
abstract: Dr. Bing’s work on congenital heart disease led to the identification of a variety of cardiac malformations that surgeons were then able to treat.

name: Lone Isaksen
headline: Lone Isaksen Dies at 68; Dancer of Fierce Elegance
abstract: Ms. Isaksen, a Danish-born dancer, transformed her deceptive fragility into a startling flexibility in contemporary works for American companies.

name: Philip Carlo
headline: Philip Carlo, Who Wrote About Killers, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Carlo produced novels and nonfiction accounts of serial killers and hit men before writing about his own struggles with disease.

name: Robbins Barstow
headline: Robbins Barstow, Home-Movie Maven, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Barstow’s tenderly shot documentaries, many of them travelogues, chronicled the ordinary doings of ordinary people in mid-century America.

name: Theodore W. Kheel
headline: Theodore W. Kheel, Labor Mediator, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Kheel was New York City’s pre-eminent labor peacemaker from the 1950s through the 1980s.

name: Record-Setting Track Star Wes Santee
headline: Record-Setting Track Star Wes Santee Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Santee, always a confident athlete, never ran the sub-four-minute mile that was expected of him, and a suspension ended his career.

name: Donald S. Kellermann
headline: Donald S. Kellermann, Who Led Public Research Group, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Kellermann helped start and then lead the organization now known as the Pew Research Center for the People and the Press.

name: Noel Taylor
headline: Noel Taylor, Creator of Costumes for Stage, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Taylor created costumes for more than 100 stage shows, including more than 70 on Broadway, and for countless TV shows and movies.

name: Fred Goldhaber
headline: Fred Goldhaber, 63, Dies; Taught at School for Gays
abstract: Mr. Goldhaber was a hero to many of the students at the Harvey Milk School in Manhattan.

name: Luis García Berlanga
headline: Luis García Berlanga, Spanish Filmmaker, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Berlanga was a maker of shrewdly satirical films that put him at odds with the fascist Franco regime.

name: Allan Sandage
headline: Allan Sandage, Astronomer, Dies at 84; Charted Cosmos’s Age and Expansion
abstract: Mr. Sandage spent his life measuring the universe, becoming the most influential astronomer of his generation.

name: Baby Marie Osborne
headline: Baby Marie Osborne, Silent-Film Child Star, Dies at 99
abstract: Often known simply as Baby Marie, the actress made almost 30 movies by the age of 8 but lost her fortune when her foster parents spent it.

name: Paul Calello
profession: Leader of a Credit Suisse Unit
headline: Paul Calello, Leader of a Credit Suisse Unit, Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. Calello helped the bank weather the financial crisis after he took over the investment banking unit in 2007.

name: Disque D. Deane
headline: Disque D. Deane, Real Estate Investor, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Deane controlled the General Motors Building, shopping malls in three states and Starrett City in Brooklyn.

name: Zena Rommett
headline: Zena Rommett, Ballet Dancer Who Developed Floor-Barre, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Rommett’s exercise method attracted notable students from ballet and elsewhere, including Tommy Tune, Melissa Hayden and Patrick Swayze.

name: Gertrude Rothschild
headline: Gertrude Rothschild, Dies at 83; Advanced LEDs
abstract: The Columbia professor waged a successful copyright-infringement battle against some big electronics companies.

name: Larry Evans
headline: Larry Evans, Chess Champ, Dies at 78
abstract: Though Mr. Evans was a grandmaster and a successful player, he was best known for his writing; he had a syndicated chess column for decades and wrote more than 20 books.

name: E. Lawrence Barcella
headline: E. Lawrence Barcella, Prosecutor of Terrorism Cases, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Barcella was a former federal prosecutor who handled major terrorism investigations in the 1970s and ’80s, including one in which he organized an elaborate trap that lured a C.I.A. turncoat out of exile in Libya.

name: W. Howard Lester
headline: W. Howard Lester, Williams-Sonoma Owner, Dies at 75
abstract: A millionaire seeking a challenge turned a small retailer into a home furnishings empire with 609 stores, a mail-order business and annual sales of $3.4 billion.

name: Nathan Oliveira
headline: Nathan Oliveira, 81, Dies; Painted Human Conflict
abstract: Mr. Oliveira gained national prominence when the Museum of Modern Art included his works in the exhibition “New Figures of Man” in 1959.

name: Helen Boehm
headline: Helen Boehm, the Princess of Porcelain, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Boehm built a company that created elaborate porcelain sculptures destined for the desks of heads of state and royalty for six decades.

name: Pat Burns
headline: Pat Burns Dies at 58; Won Stanley Cup With Devils
abstract: Mr. Burns, the coach of four National Hockey League teams, led the New Jersey Devils to a Stanley Cup title in 2003, his first season with the team.

name: William Self
headline: William Self, Television Producer, Dies at 89
abstract: As a prolific producer, Mr. Self brought many successful shows including “M*A*S*H” and “Peyton Place” to television.

name: Norris Church Mailer
headline: Norris Church Mailer, Artist and Ally, Dies at 61
abstract: Ms. Mailer, bred in the rural poverty of Arkansas, married Norman Mailer and managed his career and family life over three decades while carving out her own niche as a writer.

name: Hugh Prather
headline: Hugh Prather, Popular Self-Help Author, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Prather’s first book sold more than five million copies and inspired the “Saturday Night Live” segment “Deep Thoughts.”

name: Lawrencia Bembenek
headline: Lawrencia Bembenek, ‘Bambi’ in Murder Case, Dies at 52
abstract: Ms. Bembenek was a Milwaukee police officer whose conviction for the murder of her husband’s ex-wife and audacious escape from prison became tabloid and TV-movie fodder.

name: Philip Hoffman
headline: Philip Hoffman, Fearless Surfing Pioneer, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Hoffman’s pioneering big-wave riding in Hawaii in the 1950s charted the way for surfing pilgrimages to Oahu’s North Shore from around the world.

name: David Nolan
headline: David Nolan, 66, Is Dead; Started Libertarian Party
abstract: Mr. Nolan and a few friends joined in 1971 to found the Libertarian Party in opposition to President Richard M. Nixon’s policies.

name: Brian Marsden
headline: Brian Marsden, Tracker of Comets, Dies at 73
abstract: Dr. Marsden was an official certifier of discoveries by stargazers both amateur and professional.

name: Danny McDevitt
headline: Danny McDevitt, Dodgers Pitcher, Dies at 78
abstract: Danny McDevitt was the last pitcher for the Dodgers to win a game in Brooklyn before the team moved to Los Angeles.

name: Chalmers Johnson
headline: Chalmers Johnson Dies at 79; Criticized U.S. Role in World
abstract: The Asian studies scholar believed that the United States was using its military to try to control the world economy.

name: William Hohri
headline: William Hohri Dies at 83; Sought Money for Internees
abstract: Mr. Horhri, a veteran of a World War II internment camp for Japanese-Americans, was the lead plaintiff in a lawsuit that claimed $27 billion in damages for internees.

name: Huang Hua
headline: Huang Hua, 97, a Diplomat Who Served China, Dies
abstract: Mr. Huang served as China’s foreign minister during the 1970s and early 1980s and helped his country restore diplomatic relations with the United States.

name: Robert B. Daugherty
headline: Robert B. Daugherty, Who Helped Irrigate the Plains, Dies at 88
abstract: With center-pivot irrigation, a Nebraska businessman helped transform the rural landscape into a patchwork of circular fields. His charity supports research into agricultural policy.

name: Ingrid Pitt
headline: Ingrid Pitt, Horror Star Who Survived Nazis, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Pitt, who survived a Nazi concentration camp as a child, went on to become a star of Hammer horror films, billed as “the most beautiful ghoul in the world.”

name: Frank Fenner
headline: Frank Fenner Dies at 95; Tracked End of Smallpox
abstract: Mr. Fenner, an Australian scientist, played an important role in the World Health Organization’s campaign to eradicate smallpox and made the official announcement that it had been conquered.

name: Betty Jean Lifton
headline: Betty Jean Lifton Dies at 84; Urged Open Adoptions
abstract: Ms. Lifton lectured widely about the potential psychological effects of adoption and was best known for a nonfiction trilogy on the subject.

name: Donald Nyrop
headline: Donald Nyrop, Who Led Northwest Airlines, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Nyrop took over Northwest Airlines in 1954 and led it for nearly a quarter-century.

name: Margaret T. Burroughs
headline: Margaret T. Burroughs, Archivist of Black History, Dies at 95
abstract: Mrs. Burroughs, a professor and former commissioner of the Chicago Park District, founded the DuSable Museum of African American History in Chicago.

name: Britton Chance
headline: Britton Chance, Olympian and Biophysics Researcher, Dies at 97
abstract: Dr. Chance, who did pioneering research on how living organisms produce and manage energy, was also a world-class yachtsman and won an Olympic gold medal in sailing in 1952.

name: Britton Chance Jr.
headline: Britton Chance Jr., Designer of America’s Cup Boats, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Chance, an innovative yacht designer for three America’s Cup winners, was known for having a mathematician’s precision and a renegade’s willingness to experiment.

name: Alfred Balk
headline: Alfred Balk, Journalist and Author, Dies at 80
abstract: A journalist who wrote groundbreaking articles about housing segregation and the Nation of Islam, and whose refusal to identify a confidential source led to a landmark court case.

name: Leslie Nielsen
headline: Leslie Nielsen, 84, Romantic Hero Turned Comic, Dies
abstract: Mr. Nielsen was a Canadian-born actor who in middle age tossed aside three decades of credibility in dramatic and romantic roles to make a new career as a comic actor.

name: Irvin Kershner
headline: Irvin Kershner, Hollywood Director, Dies at 87
abstract: The director was talked into doing “The Empire Strikes Back” by his former student George Lucas.

name: Stephen J. Solarz
headline: Stephen J. Solarz, Former N.Y. Congressman, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Solarz was a nine-term Democratic congressman whose concerns ranged beyond traffic lights and beach erosion in his Brooklyn district to nuclear weapons, the Middle East and Imelda Marcos’s shoe collection.

name: Mario Monicelli
headline: Mario Monicelli, Italian Director, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Monicelli, the Italian director, was known as one of the great “commedia all’italiana” filmmakers for movies including “Big Deal on Madonna Street” and “La Grande Guerra.”

name: Gil McDougald
headline: Gil McDougald, Ex-Yankee, Dies at 82
abstract: McDougald, the Yankees’ versatile All-Star infielder, played on five World Series championship teams but was remembered as well for a single at-bat.

name: Bella Akhmadulina
headline: Bella Akhmadulina, Bold Voice in Russian Poetry, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Akhmadulina’s startling images and intensely personal style, couched in classical verse forms, established her as one of the leading literary talents in the post-Stalin Soviet Union.

name: Steven Posner
headline: Steven Posner, 67, Former Corporate Raider, Dies
abstract: Mr. Posner, who was killed in a boat collision in Florida, worked with his father, Victor, in hostile takeovers that led to the convictions of Michael Milken and Ivan Boesky.

name: Peter Hofmann
headline: Peter Hofmann, Singer of Rock, Opera and Musicals, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Hofmann, a versatile singer, was known for his good looks, nimble acting and sensitive phrasing.

name: Samuel T. Cohen
headline: Samuel T. Cohen, Neutron Bomb Inventor, Dies at 89
abstract: Samuel T. Cohen, 89, invented the small tactical nuclear weapon known as the neutron bomb.

name: Al Masini
headline: Al Masini, ‘Entertainment Tonight’ Creator, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Masini was a creator of hit television shows that often focused on glamour and fame, among them “Lifestyles of the Rich and Famous” and “Entertainment Tonight.”

name: Daya Mata
headline: Sri Daya Mata, Guiding Light for U.S. Hindus, Dies at 96
abstract: For more than five decades, Sri Daya Mata was the leader of one of the most influential Hindu groups in the United States and an ardent advocate of meditation.

name: Frank W. Lewis
headline: Frank W. Lewis, Master of the Cryptic Crossword, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Lewis, whose day job was at the National Security Agency, challenged The Nation’s puzzle players for more than six decades.

name: Ron Santo
headline: Ron Santo, Stalwart for Cubs, Dies at 70
abstract: A nine-time All Star for the Chicago Cubs and later their broadcaster, Santo was also revered for battling diabetes.

name: Elaine Kaufman
profession: Fed and Fussed Over the Famous
headline: Elaine Kaufman, Who Fed and Fussed Over the Famous, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Kaufman was the quirky owner of the Upper East Side celebrity hangout Elaine’s.

name: James P. Simpson
headline: James P. Simpson Dies at 87; Cleaned Up Galveston
abstract: Using civil court actions, Mr. Simpson, a former F.B.I. agent, helped close down illegal gambling, prostitution and nightclub operations in Galveston County, Tex., in the 1950s.

name: Richard N. Goldman
headline: Richard N. Goldman, Civic Leader and Patron, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Goldman, a San Francisco philanthropist, rewarded environmental activists.

name: Helen Boatwright
headline: Helen Boatwright, Celebrated Soprano, Dies at 94
abstract: Mrs. Boatwright was renowned for her pure, unfussy sound and her interpretations of Charles Ives.

name: Palle Huld
profession: Danish Actor Said to Be Model for Tintin
headline: Palle Huld, Danish Actor Said to Be Model for Tintin, Dies at 98
abstract: As a teenager, Mr. Huld made a solo trip around the world that was said to have inspired the Belgian cartoonist Hergé.

name: John Diebboll
headline: John Diebboll, Who Designed Offbeat Pianos, Is Dead at 54
abstract: Mr. Diebboll was an architect who discovered a second career as an artist when he began designing fantasy pianos.

name: Don Meredith
profession: Cowboys Quarterback and Cosells Broadcast Foil
headline: Don Meredith, Cowboys Quarterback and Cosell’s Broadcast Foil, Dies at 72
abstract: Meredith helped change the perception of professional football with the easy Texas charm and provocative wit he brought to its first prime-time telecasts on Monday nights.

name: María Ester Gatti
headline: María Ester Gatti, Uruguayan Activist, Dies at 92
abstract: Mrs. Gatti became a human rights activist while helping to find people lost to political repression in South America.

name: Hillard Elkins
headline: Hillard Elkins, Producer, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Elkins shocked the theater world in 1969 with the nudity-filled show “Oh! Calcutta!”

name: Garry Gross
profession: Photographer of Clothes and Their Absence
headline: Garry Gross Is Dead at 73; Photographer of Clothes and Their Absence
abstract: Mr. Gross became famous for a series of nude shots of Brooke Shields as a 10-year-old, before she began acting.

name: Elizabeth Edwards
headline: A Political Life Filled With Cruel Reversals
abstract: Mrs. Edwards shared John Edwards’s quest for the White House as she struggled with cancer, and, secretly, his infidelity.

name: Hugues Cuénod
headline: Hugues Cuénod Dies at 108; Versatile, Light-Voiced Tenor
abstract: Mr. Cuénod, known for his interpretations of French song, made his debut at the Metropolitan Opera when he was nearly 85.

name: Sergiu Luca
headline: Sergiu Luca, Violinist Who Founded Music Festivals, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Mr. Luca was a violinist who founded several important chamber music festivals and ensembles and who was renowned for the breadth of his repertory.

name: Heda Kovaly
headline: Heda Kovaly, Czech Who Wrote of Totalitarianism, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Ms. Kovaly’s memoir, “Under a Cruel Star,” described her imprisonment by the Nazis during World War II and her persecution by the Communists in the 1950s.

name: John E. du Pont
headline: John E. du Pont, Heir Who Killed an Olympian, Dies at 72
abstract: An heir to the du Pont fortune, Mr. du Pont was found guilty in 1997 of the shooting death of an Olympic athlete.

name: Martin Russ
headline: Martin Russ, a Marine Who Wrote About Combat, Dies at 79
abstract: A sergeant who served in the Korean War and went on to write about that and other conflicts.

name: James Moody
headline: James Moody, Jazz Saxophonist, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Moody, a saxophonist and flutist, was celebrated for his virtuosity, his versatility and his onstage ebullience.

name: James T. Lynn
headline: James T. Lynn, Budget Director in Ford Administration, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Lynn, who cut government spending in the Ford administration, later became chief of Aetna Life and Casualty.

name: Samuel P. King
profession: Judge and Critic of Hawaiian Charity
headline: Samuel P. King, Judge and Critic of Hawaiian Charity, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. King was a judge who helped topple overseers of one of the nation’s wealthiest charities, a 19th-century trust set up to educate native Hawaiians.

name: Beth Straus
headline: Beth Straus, Who Revamped New York Botanical Garden, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Straus helped to change the garden’s image from that of a public park to that of a museum and an educational institution.

name: Peter C. Marzio
headline: Peter C. Marzio, Houston Museum Director, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Marzio, the director of Houston’s Museum of Fine Arts for nearly 30 years, elevated it to the status of a major institution.

name: Nassos Daphnis
headline: Nassos Daphnis, an Artist of Geometry, Dies at 96
abstract: The Greek-born artist used colors of nature, some inspired by his beloved tree peonies, in precise geometric forms.

name: John B. Fenn
headline: John B. Fenn, Nobel Winner Who Studied Large Molecules, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Fenn shared the 2002 Nobel Prize for chemistry for developing a technique that sped up the development of new drugs and the study of the molecules of life.

name: Richard Holbrooke
headline: Strong American Voice in Diplomacy and Crisis
abstract: Mr. Holbrooke made a career that started with Vietnam, had a highlight with Bosnia and ended in Afghanistan and Pakistan.

name: Chuck Jordan
headline: Chuck Jordan, Innovative G.M. Designer, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Jordan was an auto industry trailblazer who loved tailfins, chrome and Ferraris and loathed focus groups.

name: Jacob Lateiner
headline: Jacob Lateiner, Pianist and Scholar, Dies at 82
abstract: A longtime teacher at Juilliard and Mannes, Mr. Lateiner was a Grammy winner and frequent partner of Jascha Heifitz and Gregor Piatigorsky.

name: Enrique Morente
headline: Enrique Morente, Celebrated Flamenco Singer, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Morente’s work embraced both traditional styles and contemporary influences as diverse as George Gershwin and Leonard Cohen.

name: MacKenzie Miller
headline: MacKenzie Miller, Trained Champion Horses, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Miller, who trained champion thoroughbred horses for nearly half a century, saddled the 1993 Kentucky Derby winner, Sea Hero, at the age of 71.

name: Bob Feller
headline: Bob Feller, Whose Fastball Dazzled, Dies at 92
abstract: Feller, a Hall of Fame pitcher, was a Cleveland Indians fixture and one of the hardest throwers in the game.

name: Maynard W. Glitman
headline: Maynard W. Glitman, Arms Negotiator, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Glitman, a career diplomat, led the American side in negotiating the intermediate-range nuclear forces treaty that was signed by the United States and the Soviet Union in 1987.

name: Blake Edwards
headline: Blake Edwards, Prolific Comedy Director, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Edwards was a master of screwball farces and rude comedies like “Victor/Victoria” and “The Pink Panther.”

name: Don Van Vliet
headline: Don Van Vliet, ‘Captain Beefheart,’ Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Van Vliet, the eccentric 1960s rocker known by his more creative moniker during his days of musical creativity, also found financial success as a painter.

name: Gary Chapman
headline: Gary Chapman, Internet Ethicist, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Chapman was an educator gave voice to many leaders in the computer field who struggled with the ethical implications of new technology.

name: Walter Haeussermann
headline: Walter Haeussermann, Rocket Scientist, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Haeussermann was a German-born electrical engineer who developed guidance and control systems that helped land Americans on the Moon.

name: Karen Sortito
headline: Karen Sortito, Who Told 007 to Start Drinking Smirnoff, Dies at 49
abstract: Ms. Sortito was a movie-marketing executive who pushed the limits of product tie-ins, most famously in James Bond movies.

name: Frank Emi
headline: Frank Emi, Defiant World War II Internee, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Emi, a Japanese-American, said no when ordered to fight for the country that had imprisoned him.

name: George Pickow
headline: George Pickow, Artist Who Chronicled Musical Life, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Pickow shot thousands of album covers for artists ranging from his own wife, the folk singer Jean Ritchie, to jazz greats like Louis Armstrong.

name: Phil Cavarretta
headline: Phil Cavarretta, National League M.V.P. in 1945, Dies at 94
abstract: Cavarretta played 20 seasons for the Chicago Cubs and won the National League’s most valuable player award and batting championship in 1945, the last time the Cubs captured a pennant.

name: Walt Dropo
profession: Star at UConn and 1950 Rookie of the Year
headline: Walt Dropo, Star at UConn and 1950 Rookie of the Year, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Dropo, a three-sport standout at Connecticut, went on to beat out Whitey Ford for American League rookie honors.

name: R. Richard Rubottom
headline: R. Richard Rubottom, Who Helped Shape Cuban Policy, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Rubottom was a witness to much of the upheaval in Latin America leading up to Fidel Castro’s takeover of Cuba.

name: René Le Berre
headline: René Le Berre, Entomologist Who Fought River Blindness, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Le Berre, a French entomologist, enlisted the World Bank in a campaign against onchocerciasis, an African parasitic disease, and helped direct spraying programs to control the disease.

name: J. M. Hagopian
headline: J. M. Hagopian, Who Told of Genocide, Dies at 97
abstract: A documentary filmmaker whose 12 movies about the killings of Armenians by Turks helped preserve the historical record.

name: Eugene Goldwasser
headline: Eugene Goldwasser, Biochemist Behind an Anemia Drug, Dies at 88
abstract: The biochemist isolated a protein that was the building block for Epo, now used by kidney patients.

name: Jacqueline de Romilly
headline: Jacqueline de Romilly, Who Studied Greek Culture, Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Romilly championed the humanities in France, especially Greek and Latin studies, and was only the second woman to be elected to the Académie Française.

name: Tommaso Padoa-Schioppa
headline: Tommaso Padoa-Schioppa, 70, a Champion of the Euro, Dies
abstract: Mr. Padoa-Schioppa worked for the single currency in Europe in the early 1980s when it was a little-known idea, then oversaw Europe’s introduction of the euro in the 1990s.

name: Steve Landesberg
headline: Steve Landesberg, ‘Barney Miller’ Actor, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Landesberg, an actor and comedian with a friendly and often deadpan manner, appeared on television and in movies, including “Barney Miller,” “The Golden Girls,” “Forgetting Sarah Marshall.”

name: Frank Baldino Jr.
headline: Frank Baldino Jr., Founder of Pharmaceutical Company, Dies at 57
abstract: Dr. Baldino founded Cephalon, seller of painkillers and the alertness drug Provigil.

name: Marcia Lewis
headline: Marcia Lewis, Stage Actress and Singer, Dies at 72
abstract: Ms. Lewis, a stage actress and singer, was known for bringing a comic brassiness to Broadway revivals of “Grease” and “Chicago.”

name: Eric Schmertz
headline: Eric Schmertz Dies at 84; Settled Many Labor Disputes
abstract: Mr. Schmertz, a lawyer and a onetime dean of Hofstra’s law school, was known for his ability to resolve labor disputes, but his first love was baseball.

name: Patricia Thompson
headline: Patricia Thompson, TV Producer and Documentary Maker, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Thompson, an American, moved to Paris in the 1970s and went on to cover the revolutions in Iran and the Philippines, the marriage and death of Diana, Princess of Wales, and other news events.

name: Enzo Bearzot
headline: Enzo Bearzot, Who Coached Italy to Cup Title, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Bearzot’s tenure as coach of Italy’s national soccer team was the longest for a national team coach in a country where soccer coaches are second-guessed more than politicians.

name: James Mann
headline: James Mann, 90, Dies; Worked on Nixon Impeachment
abstract: Mr. Mann helped persuade Republicans and fellow Southern Democrats to line up behind the impeachment of a president.

name: Fred Foy
headline: Fred Foy, ‘Lone Ranger’ Announcer, Dies at 89
abstract: For a decade, first on radio and then TV, Mr. Foy intoned the program’s evocative opening lines to the galloping strains of the “William Tell” overture.

name: Brian Hanrahan
headline: Brian Hanrahan, BBC Reporter, Dies at 61
abstract: He delivered perhaps his most celebrated report from an aircraft carrier during Britain’s war to reclaim the Falklands in 1982.

name: Clay Cole
headline: Clay Cole, Host of Teenage Dance Shows, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Cole’s loyal following among adolescent viewers in the New York area in the 1960s and gave many groups, including the Rolling Stones, early exposure on American television.

name: Roy R. Neuberger
profession: Applied a Stock Traders Acumen to Art
headline: Roy R. Neuberger Dies at 107; Applied a Stock Trader’s Acumen to Art
abstract: Mr. Neuberger, who founded the investment firm Neuberger Berman, became one of America’s leading art patrons by acquiring hundreds of paintings and sculptures.

name: Sally Goodrich
headline: Sally Goodrich, Who Aided Afghans After 9/11 Loss, Dies at 65
