abstract: After her son was killed in the 9/11 attacks, a teacher turned her grief into a living memorial.

name: Dan Kurzman
headline: Dan Kurzman, Military Historian, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Kurzman covered many topics in his books, including the lives of heads of state, but he frequently returned to World War II and Israel.

name: Karen Tuttle
headline: Karen Tuttle, Violist and Teacher, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Tuttle, an innovator in technique for her instrument, was praised by critics for her incisive musicianship and large, luminous sound.

name: Frank Bessac
headline: Frank Bessac, Scholar and Adventurer, Dies at 88
abstract: An anthropologist who fled revolution in China in a perilous yearlong trek through some of the most remote regions of Asia.

name: Bud Greenspan
headline: Bud Greenspan, 84, Dies; Filmed Olympics in Glory
abstract: Bud Greenspan, 84, disdained scandals to write, produce and direct uplifting documentaries about Olympic athletes facing triumph and tragedy.

name: Carlos Andrés Pérez
headline: Carlos Andrés Pérez, Former President of Venezuela, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Pérez tried to make Venezuela a leader of the developing world during a 1970s oil boom only to have his legacy upended.

name: Anthony Howard
headline: Anthony Howard, Political Commentator in Britain, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Howard was an editor, columnist and television pundit known for his incisive analyses of his country’s politics.

name: Teena Marie
headline: Teena Marie, 1980s R&B Hitmaker, Dies at 54
abstract: Teena Marie’s funky hits in the 1980s, like “Lovergirl” and “Square Biz,” made her one of the few white performers to consistently find success on the rhythm-and-blues charts.

name: Steven W. Fisher
headline: Steven W. Fisher, New York State Justice, Dies at 64
abstract: Justice Fisher was the last New York judge to impose the death penalty, against one of the killers of five Wendy’s employees.

name: E. Gene Smith
profession: Helped to Save Tibetan Literary Canon
headline: E. Gene Smith, Who Helped to Save Tibetan Literary Canon, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Smith amassed the largest collection of Tibetan books outside Tibet, saving the works from destruction by the Chinese and making them available to scholars worldwide.

name: Gene Smith
headline: Gene Smith Dies at 83; Wrote Biographies of World Leaders
abstract: Mr. Smith’s books examined the lives of presidents, generals and mounted warriors.

name: John Warhola
headline: John Warhola, Brother of Andy Warhol, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Warhola helped his younger brother to attend college and went on to serve as a trustee for Andy’s foundation.

name: Frances Ginsberg
headline: Frances Ginsberg, American Soprano, Dies at 55
abstract: Ms. Ginsberg, who often performed with the New York City Opera, was a soprano most closely associated with the spinto repertory.

name: Billy Taylor
headline: Billy Taylor, Jazz Pianist, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Taylor left his mark on jazz less as a musician than as a proselytizer, spreading the gospel of jazz as an art form.

name: Geraldine Doyle
profession: Iconic Face of World War II
headline: Geraldine Doyle, Iconic Face of World War II, Dies at 86
abstract: A factory photograph of Mrs. Doyle was turned into the “We Can Do It!” poster that was used during World War II and later embraced by the feminist movement.

name: Eugene Garfield
headline: Eugene Garfield, Founder of the Auto-Train Service, Dies at 74
abstract: Eugene K. Garfield originated the American Auto-Train, which carried passengers and their cars between Virginia and Florida.

name: Robert Macauley
headline: Robert Macauley, Founder of Humanitarian Aid Group, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Macauley, a paper company executive in Connecticut, started AmeriCares, which has sent billions of dollars worth of food and medicines to trouble spots around the world since 1982.

name: Isabelle Caro
headline: Isabelle Caro, Anorexic Model, Dies at 28
abstract: A French model, actress and author, Ms. Caro’s emaciated image appeared in a shock Italian advertising campaign against the disorder in 2007.

name: Paul Calle
headline: Paul Calle, Postage Stamp Designer, Is Dead at 82
abstract: “When you do a stamp,” Mr. Calle once said of his craft, “think big, but draw small.”

name: Roger Milliken
headline: Roger Milliken, Conservative Tycoon, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Milliken, a South Carolina textile tycoon, supported Jesse Helms and Strom Thurmond, and promoted a college’s integration.

name: Denis Dutton
headline: Denis Dutton, Philosopher, Dies at 66
abstract: Among myriad other pursuits, Mr. Dutton founded Arts & Letters Daily, one of the first Web sites to exploit the Internet as a vehicle for meaningful intellectual exchange.

name: Philip Burton Jr.
headline: Philip Burton Jr., Documentarian, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Burton won several Emmys for his productions, which focused on the struggle for African-American equality and the inner workings of American government,

name: Ruth Park
headline: Ruth Park, Australian Realist Author, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Park leaped from obscurity in 1946 when her novel “The Harp in the South” won first prize in The Sydney Morning Herald’s inaugural literary competition.

name: Arnold Weiss
headline: Arnold Weiss Dies at 86; Helped to Find Hitler’s Will
abstract: Mr. Weiss was a principal in the investigation that led to the discovery of Hitler’s last will and political testament.

name: Szeto Wah
headline: Szeto Wah, Political Activist in Hong Kong, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Szeto was a Hong Kong union leader and critic of British colonial rule who became an implacable critic of the Chinese Communist Party after the Tiananmen Square killings in 1989.

name: Janine Pommy Vega
headline: Janine Pommy Vega, Restless Poet, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. Vega was a poet who found adventure and inspiration among the Beats in Greenwich Village.

name: Hideko Takamine
headline: Hideko Takamine, Lauded Japanese Actress, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Takamine developed from an endearing child star into a powerful representative of the Japanese woman’s search for identity and autonomy in the years after World War II.

name: Pete Postlethwaite
headline: Pete Postlethwaite, an Actor With Broad Range, Dies at 64
abstract: Memorable films included “Distant Voices, Still Lives” and “In the Name of the Father.”

name: Ab Simon
headline: Ab Simon, Chairman of Seagram Wine Unit, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Simon imported and sold chateau wines from Bordeaux and estate wines from Burgundy, the Rhone and the Loire regions.

name: Gerry Rafferty
headline: Gerry Rafferty, Songwriter, Dies at 63
abstract: The Scottish singer was best known for his songs “Stuck in the Middle With You” and “Baker Street.”

name: Jill Haworth
headline: Jill Haworth, Original Sally in ‘Cabaret,’ Dies at 65
abstract: The British-born actress had an early start in films before being cast in the Broadway musical at 21.

name: Raphael Hillyer
headline: Raphael Hillyer, Founding Violist of Juilliard Quartet, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Hillyer was a soloist and teacher known for the warmth and expressivity of his tone.

name: Barry Zorthian
headline: Barry Zorthian, U.S. Diplomat in Vietnam, Dies at 90
abstract: As a public affairs officer in Saigon during the Vietnam War, Mr. Zorthian faced a skeptical press corps in what became known as the “five o’clock follies.”

name: Donald J. Tyson
headline: Donald J. Tyson, Food Tycoon, Is Dead at 80
abstract: The folksy Arkansan turned his father’s chicken business into a global enterprise, rolling over competitors and enraging environmentalists.

name: David G. Trager
headline: David G. Trager, Judge in Crown Heights Case, Dies at 73
abstract: Judge Trager’s rulings were pivotal in a racially charged case in Brooklyn and in a lawsuit challenging the Bush administration’s practice of “extraordinary rendition.”

name: Frank Bonilla
headline: Frank Bonilla, Scholar of Puerto Rican Studies, Dies at 85
abstract: For 20 years, starting in 1973, Dr. Bonilla was the founding director of a research program at Hunter College in New York.

name: Margot Stevenson
headline: Margot Stevenson, Prolific Broadway Actress, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Stevenson, who appeared in a handful of movies and television shows, spent most of her career on the stage.

name: Brenton Harries
headline: Brenton Harries Dies at 82; Warned of ’75 Fiscal Crisis
abstract: As the leader of the credit ratings company, Mr. Harries’s alarm over New York’s ballooning debt foreshadowed the city’s 1975 fiscal crisis

name: Ryne Duren
headline: Ryne Duren, Yankees Reliever Who Made Batters Nervous, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Duren was known for a 100-mile-an-hour fastball, thick eyeglasses and making batters nervous.

name: Vang Pao
headline: Gen. Vang Pao, Laotian Who Aided U.S., Dies at 81
abstract: Vang Pao was a charismatic Laotian general who commanded a secret army of his mountain people in a long, losing campaign against Communist insurgents.

name: Paul Soldner
headline: Paul Soldner, Who Created Towering Ceramic Sculptures, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Soldner adapted a Japanese firing technique known as raku.

name: Jiri Dienstbier
headline: Jiri Dienstbier, Czech Dissident, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Mr. Dienstbier was a reporter turned dissident who joined Vaclav Havel to help topple one of East Europe’s most repressive regimes, and then served in his government.

name: Joan Vass
headline: Joan Vass, Designer of Elegant Knitwear Line, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Vass created an elegantly understated fashion label that stood in contrast to her reputation as a bohemian and provocateur.

name: Cyril Harris
headline: Cyril Harris Dies at 93; Fine-Tuned Concert Halls
abstract: Mr. Harris was an acoustical engineer responsible for the sound in many prominent concert halls in the United States.

name: Malangatana Ngwenya
headline: Malangatana Ngwenya, Mozambican Painter and Poet, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Ngwenya, a beloved hero in Mozambique, was one of the few African artists to gain worldwide recognition while staying in Africa.

name: B. H. Friedman
headline: B. H. Friedman, a Novelist, Art Critic and Pollock Biographer, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Friedman gave up a life in the real-estate world to become a full-time author, writing novels as well as art biographies.

name: Louise Reiss
headline: Dr. Louise Reiss, Who Helped Ban Atomic Testing, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Reiss used baby teeth to show that radioactive fallout was getting into the food supply and working its way into human bones and teeth.

name: Cookie Gilchrist
headline: Cookie Gilchrist, Early Star of the A.F.L., Dies at 75
abstract: A four-time All-Pro fullback in the American Football League, Gilchrist was also a voice against discriminatory treatment of black players.

name: Richard Winters
headline: Richard Winters Dies at 92; Led ‘Band of Brothers’
abstract: Mr. Winters was the commanding officer of the Army unit whose World War II exploits were recounted in the book and miniseries “Band of Brothers.”

name: Peter Yates
headline: Peter Yates, Filmmaker, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Yates was a British-born director who directed two American classics, “Bullitt” and “Breaking Away.”

name: Debbie Friedman
headline: Debbie Friedman, Singer of Jewish Music, Dies at 59
abstract: Ms. Friedman’s work, which married traditional Jewish texts to contemporary folk-infused melodies, is credited with helping give ancient liturgy appeal to contemporary worshippers.

name: Margaret Whiting
profession: Fresh-Faced Singer of Jazz and Pop Standards
headline: Margaret Whiting, Fresh-Faced Singer of Jazz and Pop Standards, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Whiting, a songwriter’s daughter, had her own acclaimed career as a singer beginning in the 1940s.

name: Bobby Robinson
headline: Bobby Robinson, Harlem Music Impresario, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Robinson’s record store spawned a remarkable recording business and became a treasured Harlem institution.

name: John Gross
headline: John Gross Dies at 75; Critic, Essayist and Editor
abstract: Mr. Gross, known for his fluid style and easy erudition, was the editor of The Times Literary Supplement in London and a book critic for The New York Times.

name: Jack Oliver
headline: Jack Oliver, Who Proved Continental Drift, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Oliver’s studies of earthquakes provided convincing proof that Earth’s continents are constantly moving.

name: David Nelson
headline: David Nelson, Son in ‘Ozzie and Harriet,’ Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Nelson was the elder son of Ozzie and Harriet Nelson and the last surviving member of that Eisenhower-era television family.

name: Oleg Grabar
headline: Oleg Grabar, Historian Who Studied Islamic Culture, Dies at 81
abstract: Professor Grabar’s imposingly broad range and analytical subtlety helped transform the Western study of Islamic art and architecture.

name: Ellen Stewart
headline: Ellen Stewart, Off Off Broadway Pioneer, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Stewart was the founder of La MaMa Experimental Theater Club, a multicultural hive of avant-garde drama.

name: Ruth Cavin
profession: Editor Known to Cultivate Promising Writers
headline: Ruth Cavin, Editor Known to Cultivate Promising Writers, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Cavin, who at 60 began a second career in publishing, was respected for her hands-on editing of promising mystery-novel manuscripts.

name: Jack Towers
headline: Jack Towers Dies at 96; Remastered Jazz Recordings
abstract: Mr. Towers was an expert at remastering early jazz recordings and made an original 1940 recording of the Duke Ellington Orchestra that won a Grammy.

name: Joe Gores
profession: Crime Writer in Dashiell Hammett Mode
headline: Joe Gores, Crime Writer in Dashiell Hammett Mode, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Gores’s spare, chiseled sentences and deadpan dialogue persuaded Hammett’s daughter to let him write a follow-up to “The Maltese Falcon.”

name: Matthew Lipman
headline: Matthew Lipman, Philosopher and Educator, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Lipman put forth a radical idea: that the littlest pupils are helped by thinking about big ideas.

name: Judy Bonds
headline: Judy Bonds, an Enemy of Mountaintop Coal Mining, Dies at 58
abstract: A West Virginia coal miner’s daughter, she led a fight against mountaintop-removal mining after her grandson scooped up fistfuls of dead fish in 1996.

name: Romulus Linney
headline: Romulus Linney, Wide-Ranging Playwright, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Linney roved along many intellectual paths, refashioning classical works for modern times and adapting contemporary novels for the stage.

name: Flo Gibson
headline: Flo Gibson, Grande Dame of Audiobooks, Dies at 86
abstract: Mrs. Gibson narrated more than 1,100 books, including “Middlemarch” (31 hours, 7 minutes) and “Anna Karenina” (36 hours, 7 minutes).

name: Susannah York
headline: Susannah York, British Actress, Dies at 72
abstract: Ms. York was an Academy Award-nominated actress known for her portrayals of exquisite, often fragile young women in British and American films of the 1960s and ‘70s.

name: Remmy Ongala
headline: Remmy Ongala, Tanzanian Musical Star, Dies at 63
abstract: The Congo-born Mr. Ongala, popular in the West from recordings and tours, was not afraid to sing about difficult issues, like the spread of AIDS.

name: Liu Huaqing
headline: Liu Huaqing Dies at 94; Oversaw Modernization of China’s Navy
abstract: General Liu spearheaded efforts in the 1980s to turn the Chinese Navy from a coastal defense force to a blue-water navy able to operate far from China.

name: Milton Rogovin
headline: Milton Rogovin, Photographer, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Rogovin took up photography as a way to champion the underprivileged and went on to become one of America’s leading social documentarians.

name: R. Sargent Shriver
headline: R. Sargent Shriver, Peace Corps Leader, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Shriver was the architect of President Lyndon B. Johnson’s war on poverty, an ambassador to France and the Democratic candidate for vice president in 1972.

name: Don Kirshner
headline: Don Kirshner, Shaper of Hit Records, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Kirshner, a guiding force during the Brill Building era of pop, was perhaps best known for his television show “Don Kirshner’s Rock Concert.”

name: Wilfrid Sheed
headline: Wilfrid Sheed, Writer of Gentle Wit, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Sheed drew upon his Anglo-American background to write bittersweet essays, criticism, memoirs and fiction about cultural life on both sides of the Atlantic.

name: Michael Langham
headline: Michael Langham, Classical Theater Director, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Langham led a formidable roster of leading men and women through the rigors of Shakespeare, Shaw, Molière, Chekhov and others.

name: Reynolds Price
headline: Reynolds Price, a Literary Voice of the South, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Price, the novelist, poet and memoirist, found all the material he needed in the North Carolina he knew so well.

name: Paul Picerni
headline: Paul Picerni, Actor in ‘Untouchables,’ Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Picerni appeared in more than 60 movies and 450 television shows, but he was best known as Eliot Ness’s right-hand man.

name: Gordon Murray
headline: Gordon Murray, Retired Wall St. Executive, Dies at 60; Wrote Investment Guide
abstract: A cancer patient, Mr. Murray said writing “The Investment Answer,” a guide for laymen, probably added days to his life.

name: Phyllis K. Robinson
headline: Phyllis K. Robinson, a Top Copywriter, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Robinson helped created memorable campaigns for Polaroid cameras and Levy’s breads as the head copywriter for Doyle Dane Bernbach.

name: Theoni V. Aldredge
headline: Theoni V. Aldredge, Costume Designer, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Aldredge won an Academy Award for the costumes in “The Great Gatsby,” and created the clothing designs for hundreds of stage productions.

name: Georgia Carroll
headline: Georgia Carroll, Singer in Kay Kyser’s Band, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Carroll enjoyed short-lived stardom as the featured vocalist in Mr. Kyser’s popular big band before marrying him and retiring from show business.

name: Jack LaLanne
headline: Jack LaLanne, Founder of Modern Fitness Movement, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. LaLanne found recognition through his obsession with grueling workouts and nutrition, complemented by a salesman’s gift.

name: Dagmar Wilson
headline: Dagmar Wilson, Anti-Nuclear Leader, Dies at 94
abstract: She was the founder of Women Strike for Peace, a cold war movement that helped organize demonstrations around the world calling for nuclear disarmament.

name: John D. Kendall
headline: John D. Kendall, Early Suzuki Method Advocate, Dies at 93
abstract: An early advocate in America of the Suzuki method of teaching music to very young children.

name: William Schreyer
headline: William Schreyer, 83, Merrill Chief, Dies
abstract: Mr. Schreyer led Merrill Lynch’s transition from a stock brokerage firm to a diversified global investment bank.

name: Edgar Tafel
headline: Edgar Tafel, Wright-Trained Architect, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Tafel, thought to be the last living of Wright’s early apprentices, went on to a thriving architectural practice of his own.

name: Brian Rust
headline: Brian Rust, Father of Modern Discography, Dies at 88
abstract: In tracing and chasing obscure jazz records from the field’s earliest days, Mr. Rust set the standard for all of modern discography.

name: Bernd Eichinger
headline: Bernd Eichinger, Screenwriter and Producer, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Eichinger, a prominent force in the German film industry, worked on films including “The NeverEnding Story” and “Downfall.”

name: Daniel Bell
headline: Daniel Bell, Ardent Appraiser of Politics, Economics and Culture, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Bell was a writer, editor, sociologist and teacher who over seven decades came to epitomize the engaged intellectual.

name: Bruce Gordon
headline: Bruce Gordon, TV Mobster, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Gordon, a chiseled character actor, played tough guys, most memorably the mob boss Frank Nitti on the television series “The Untouchables.”

name: Charlie Louvin
headline: Charlie Louvin, Country Singer, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Louvin was a member of one of the pre-eminent brother acts in country music and an inspiration to several generations of rock musicians.

name: Dennis Oppenheim
profession: Pioneer in Earthworks and Conceptual Art
headline: Dennis Oppenheim, a Pioneer in Earthworks and Conceptual Art, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Oppenheim made emphatically tangible installations and public sculptures that veered between the demonically chaotic and the cheerfully Pop.

name: Tullia Zevi
headline: Tullia Zevi, Who Led Italian Jewish Community, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Ms. Zevi played a major role as the dialogue between the Vatican and the world Jewish community blossomed, and she helped negotiate thorny issues.

name: Samuel Ruiz García
headline: Bishop Samuel Ruiz García, Defender of Mexico’s Mayans, Dies at 86
abstract: During his 40 years presiding over a Roman Catholic diocese in Chiapas, Bishop Ruiz cast light on abuses suffered by the Indians and sought to bring them into the church as equals with other Mexicans.

name: Poppa Neutrino
headline: Poppa Neutrino, Trans-Atlantic Adventurer, Dies at 77
abstract: Poppa Neutrino, whose life was chronicled by a New Yorker writer, founded his own church and crossed the Atlantic on a raft made from scrap.

name: Guy J. Velella
headline: Guy J. Velella, State Senator From Bronx, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Velella, a former Republican state senator, was a formidable figure in Albany until he pleaded guilty to bribery conspiracy seven years ago.

name: John Horan
headline: John Horan, Former Chief of Merck, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Horan led Merck as the company’s portfolio of pharmaceuticals expanded, including a hepatitis B vaccine, new antibiotics and heart medications.

name: Gladys Horton
headline: Gladys Horton, Marvelettes’ Lead Singer, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Horton was a founding member of the Marvelettes, whose “Please Mr. Postman” gave Motown Records its first No. 1 hit.

name: Charlie Callas
headline: Charlie Callas, Zany Comedian, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Callas, a nightclub favorite, was also a frequent guest on TV talk shows, where he was known for his unpredictability and wacky sound effects.

name: Willi Dansgaard
headline: Willi Dansgaard Dies at 88; Read Climates in Old Ice
abstract: Drilling into the Greenland icecap, Mr. Dansgaard was able to analyze ancient bubbles of trapped oxygen and gauge temperature.

name: David Frye
headline: David Frye, Perfectly Clear Nixon Parodist, Dies at 77
abstract: An impressionist of many politicians and celebrities, Mr. Frye was associated with one beyond all others.

name: Milton M. Levine
headline: Milton M. Levine, Inventor of Ant Farm, Dies at 97
abstract: Recalling how as a boy he had collected ants in jars at his uncle’s farm in Pennsylvania, he told his brother-in-law, “We should make an antarium.”

name: Eleanor Galenson
headline: Eleanor Galenson, Expert on Children’s Sexual Identity, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Galenson and a colleague concluded that children make the discovery of genital difference between the ages of 15 to 19 months. Freud had postulated 4 to 5 years old.

name: Milton Babbitt
headline: Milton Babbitt, a Composer Who Gloried in Complexity, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Babbitt was regarded as the standard-bearer of the ultrarational extreme in American composition.

name: Tony Geiss
headline: Tony Geiss, Writer for ‘Sesame Street,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Geiss helped “Sesame Street” win 22 daytime Emmy Awards and invented several Muppets characters, including Abby Cadabby.

name: Ron Patterson
headline: Ron Patterson, Renaissance (Fair) Man, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Patterson and his wife at the time, Phyllis, are widely credited with having created the first modern Renaissance fair, begun in Southern California in 1963.

name: Charles Nolan
headline: Charles Nolan, Designer, Is Dead at 53
abstract: Mr. Nolan, an ardent Democrat, proudly wore his politics on his sleeve and also on his runway.

name: Ernest McCulloch
profession: Crucial Figure in Stem Cell Research
headline: Ernest McCulloch, Crucial Figure in Stem Cell Research, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. McCulloch was involved in the discovery of stem cells and thereby opening a path of research that some day may help treat a variety of serious, sometimes lethal, ailments.

name: Margaret Price
headline: Margaret Price Dies at 69, Soprano With Rich Voice
abstract: Ms. Price was a Welsh soprano who brought a voice of pure, floating richness to lieder and the operas of Mozart and Verdi.

name: Eugenio Arango
headline: Eugenio Arango, Cuban-Born Musician Known as Totico, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Arango was a percussionist and singer who was one of the most celebrated figures in the drumming, dancing and singing culture of New York rumba.

name: Alan Uglow
headline: Alan Uglow, Abstract Painter, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Uglow, whose paintings sometimes reflected his passion for soccer, was respected in the art world but not well known outside its circles.

name: Charles H. Kaman
headline: Charles H. Kaman, Helicopter Innovator, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Kaman was an innovator in the development and manufacture of helicopter technology and the inventor of one of the first electrically amplified acoustic guitars.

name: Barney Hajiro
headline: Barney Hajiro, Medal of Honor Recipient, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Hajiro was recommended for the Medal of Honor for bravery in combat during World War II, but did not receive the honor until 2000.

name: Maria Schneider
headline: Maria Schneider, Actress in ‘Last Tango,’ Dies at 58
abstract: Though Ms. Schneider tried to move beyond the notoriety, her sex scenes with Marlon Brando in “Last Tango in Paris” defined her career.

name: Charles Sellier Jr.
headline: Charles Sellier Jr., Creator of ‘Grizzly Adams,’ Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Sellier produced, and often wrote and directed, more than 30 movies and over 200 television shows, many with religious themes.

name: Michael Tolan
headline: Michael Tolan, Stage and Television Actor, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Tolan, who appeared on dozens of TV episodes, also helped found the American Place Theater.

name: René Verdon
headline: René Verdon, French Chef for the Kennedys, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Verdon’s position as the White House chef during the Kennedy administration helped him project the allure of classic French cuisine to the American public.

name: Lena Nyman
profession: Star of I Am Curious Films
headline: Lena Nyman, Star of ‘I Am Curious’ Films, Is Dead at 66
abstract: Ms. Nyman’s performance in the sexually explicit movie “I Am Curious (Yellow)” raised the hackles of censors in the 1960s and helped turn the film into a box office bonanza.

name: Tuviah Friedman
headline: Tuviah Friedman, Tireless Pursuer of Nazis, Dies at 88
abstract: In the months before and after the end of World War II, Mr. Friedman hunted Nazis as part of a militia in liberated Poland, and he reveled in his nickname, the Merciless One.

name: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi
headline: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi Dies at 88; Indian Classical Singer
abstract: Mr. Joshi was for decades one of the world’s most revered singers of Indian classical music.

name: Mary Cleere Haran
profession: Cabaret Singer With a Big-Band Style
headline: Mary Cleere Haran, Cabaret Singer With a Big-Band Style, Dies at 58
abstract: Ms. Haran sang with a remarkably pure voice in a simple pop-jazz style that echoed big band singers of the 1940s.

name: Tura Satana
headline: Tura Satana, Actress With a Cult Following, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Satana, a Japanese-American actress with tough demeanor and buxom appeal, was most famous for Russ Meyer’s “Faster, Pussycat! Kill! Kill!”

name: Emanuel Vardi
headline: Emanuel Vardi, a Champion of the Viola, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Vardi, an American violist, was an ambassador for the instrument in an era when it had few public champions.

name: Ken Olsen
headline: Ken Olsen, Who Built DEC Into a Power, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Olsen helped reshape the computer industry as a founder of the Digital Equipment Corporation, at one time the world’s second-largest computer company.

name: Johannes Somary
headline: Johannes Somary, Conductor of Neglected Works, Dies at 75
abstract: The founder and director of the Amor Artis choral group uncovered neglected gems from the Baroque and Classical periods.

name: Maria Altmann
headline: Maria Altmann, Pursuer of Family’s Stolen Paintings, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Altmann, a Jewish refugee, successfully won back five paintings by Gustav Klimt that the Nazis had seized from her family.

name: Brian Jacques
headline: Brian Jacques, Writer of Redwall Series, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Jacques worked many trades before finding his métier as a writer of the Redwall children’s fantasy books.

name: Mark J. Hulkower
headline: Mark J. Hulkower, Who Prosecuted Aldrich Ames, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Hulkower followed his successful prosecution of one of the nation’s most notorious traitors with the defense of high-profile executives accused of white-collar crimes.

name: Françoise Cachin
headline: Françoise Cachin, a Director of French Museums, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Cachin, who helped found the Musée d’Orsay in Paris, also organized major exhibitions of modern art and wrote important books on 19th-century French painting.

name: Alan Slifka
headline: Alan Slifka, Who Promoted Arab-Jewish Ties, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Slifka used his fortune to promote harmony among Israeli Arabs and Jews and to give New York the Big Apple Circus.

name: Emory Bellard
headline: Emory Bellard, Creator of Wishbone Offense, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Bellard was credited with introducing the wishbone formation to college football, providing the framework for many of the great running teams of the 1970s.

name: Peggy Rea
headline: Peggy Rea, TV Actress With Matronly Aura, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Rea had supporting roles on popular television series like “The Dukes of Hazzard” and “Grace Under Fire.”

name: Charles O. Perry
headline: Charles O. Perry Dies at 81; Sculptor Inspired by Geometry
abstract: Mr. Perry created “Continuum,” the knotted black Möbius strip in front of the Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum in Washington, among many other works.

name: Fred Kirby
headline: Fred Kirby, Who Built Giant Title Insurance Company, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Kirby transformed the Alleghany Corporation, initially a railroad holding company, into a title insurance leader.

name: Chuck Tanner
headline: Chuck Tanner, Who Managed Pirates to ’79 Title, Dies
abstract: Mr. Tanner, a manager for 19 years, was respected for coaxing more victories than expected from rosters with less-than-stellar talent.

name: Arthur Schatzkin
headline: Arthur Schatzkin, Who Studied High-Fiber Diet and Polyps, Dies at 62
abstract: Dr. Schatzkin, an epidemiologist who investigated the connections between diet and cancer, found that eating fiber did not prevent the recurrence of polyps in the colon.

name: Miriam Hansen
headline: Miriam Hansen, a Scholar of Cinema, Dies at 61
abstract: A founder of the cinema and media studies department at the University of Chicago, Ms. Hansen studied film audiences as well as films.

name: Charles E. Silberman
profession: Wrote About Racism in the U.S
headline: Charles E. Silberman, Who Wrote About Racism in the U.S., Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Silberman, a former writer and editor at Fortune magazine, was known for books on turbulent social subjects including education, crime and the state of American Jewry.

name: Betty Garrett
profession: Antsy Cabby in On the Town
headline: Betty Garrett, Antsy Cabby in ‘On the Town,’ Is Dead at 91
abstract: In a career covering more than six decades, Ms. Garrett also played Archie Bunker’s liberal foil and a sardonic landlady in “Laverne & Shirley.”

name: George Shearing
headline: George Shearing, ‘Lullaby of Birdland’ Jazz Virtuoso, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Shearing, who was born blind, composed about 300 tunes and worked with singing stars like Frank Sinatra, Peggy Lee and Mel Tormé.

name: Blanche Moyse
headline: Blanche Moyse, Music School Founder, Dies at 101
abstract: Ms. Moyse was a founder of the Marlboro Music School and Festival and, as a conductor, a leading interpreter of Bach’s choral works.

name: Josefa Iloilo
headline: Josefa Iloilo, Leader Who Revoked Fiji Constitution, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Iloilo provoked worldwide censure for his actions in 2009, which included firing Fiji’s judges and making himself head of state.

name: David F. Friedman
headline: David F. Friedman, Horror Film Pioneer, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Friedman cheerfully and cheesily exploited an audience’s hunger for bare-breasted women and blood-dripping corpses.

name: Margaret K. McElderry
headline: Margaret K. McElderry, Children’s Book Publisher, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. McElderry, the grande dame of children’s book publishing, recruited authors with a new sensibility, ventured into controversial subjects and led the way in publishing foreign works.

name: Joanne Siegel
headline: Joanne Siegel, the Model for Lois Lane, Dies at 93
abstract: During the Depression Ms. Siegel hired herself out as a model to an aspiring comic book artist, Joe Shuster, and thus became the first physical incarnation of Superman’s love interest.

name: Raymond D’Addario
headline: Raymond D’Addario, Photographer of Nazis, Dies at 90
abstract: An Army photographer whose camera captured images of Hitler’s associates at the Nuremberg trials, he retired from the service and opened a camera shop in his hometown.

name: Herschel W. Leibowitz
headline: Herschel W. Leibowitz Dies at 85; Studied Night Vision’s Tricks
abstract: Mr. Leibowitz’s research found that people can become myopic in the dark, so that drivers see not only less but less clearly, increasing the risk of accidents.

name: Jerry Ames
headline: Jerry Ames, Tap Dancer With Airy Style, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Mr. Ames, a tap dancer and choreographer known for his airy, balletic style and eclectic approach, performed as a soloist in New York and around the world.

name: Bill Monroe
headline: Bill Monroe, ‘Meet the Press’ Host, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Monroe, the moderator of the NBC Sunday morning news program from 1975 to 1984, also spent time as the network’s Washington bureau chief and as Washington editor of the “Today” show.

name: Joe Frazier
headline: Joe Frazier, Who Managed Mets in Turbulent Time, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Frazier, a baseball lifer, managed at Shea Stadium during the period between the tenures of Yogi Berra and Joe Torre.

name: Joe Frazier
headline: Joe Frazier, Ex-Heavyweight Champ, Dies at 67
abstract: Frazier, the former heavyweight champion, had an epic rivalry with Muhammad Ali that included the Thrilla in Manila, regarded as one of the greatest fights in boxing history.

name: Len Lesser
headline: Len Lesser, Uncle Leo on ‘Seinfeld,’ Dies at 88
abstract: After decades of work as a character actor, Mr. Lesser finally made an indelible impression as an annoying relative.

name: John Strauss
headline: John Strauss, Composer of ‘Car 54’ Theme, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Strauss was an Emmy-winning composer and music editor best known for the jaunty theme music for the early 1960s TV show “Car 54, Where Are You?”

name: Perry Moore
profession: Author of Book About Gay Superhero
headline: Perry Moore, Author of Book About Gay Superhero, Dies at 39
abstract: Mr. Moore, the author of “Hero,” was also an executive producer of the movie series “The Chronicles of Narnia.”

name: Dave Duerson
headline: Dave Duerson, Safety Who Made Pro Bowl 4 Times, Is Dead at 50
abstract: Duerson won his first championship with the Bears after the 1985 season, and a second with the Giants after the 1990 season.

name: Kathleen Mortimer
headline: Kathleen Mortimer, Rich and Adventurous, Dies at 93
abstract: A daughter of W. Averell Harriman, Mrs. Mortimer’s life was a window onto Gilded Age America and the changing role of American women in the era between the world wars.

name: Ernie Tyler
headline: Ernie Tyler, the Ironman of Umpire Attendants, Dies at 86
abstract: Umpires counted on Tyler  for baseballs, meals and laundry  at Baltimore Orioles games for more than 50 years.

name: Santi Santamaría
headline: Santi Santamaría, Catalan Chef, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Santamaría was in the forefront of a generation of chefs who helped draw the world’s attention to Spanish cuisine.

name: Chuck Allen
headline: Chuck Allen, Who Championed Surfing and Snowboarding, Dies at 74
abstract: The banker became a volunteer surfing coach, then helped found two nonprofit organizations that worked to bring respect and legitimacy to surfing and snowboarding,

name: Ollie Matson
headline: Ollie Matson, an All-Purpose Football Star, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Matson, who played multiple positions in the N.F.L. and was elected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1972, also won two Olympic medals as a sprinter.

name: Edmund de Unger
headline: Edmund de Unger, Islamic Art Collector, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. de Unger accumulated priceless objects from nearly every period of Islamic art and a geographical area extending from the Mediterranean to India.

name: Roy Gussow
headline: Roy Gussow, Abstract Sculptor, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Gussow was an abstract sculptor whose polished stainless-steel works with swooping contours gleam in public squares and corporate spaces.

name: B. N. Nathanson
headline: B. N. Nathanson, 84, Dies; Changed Sides on Abortion
abstract: Dr. Bernard N. Nathanson, an obstetrician-gynecologist, campaigned for abortion rights but later became a prominent opponent of abortion after performing 5,000 of them.

name: E.M. Nathanson
headline: E.M. Nathanson, Author of ‘The Dirty Dozen,’ Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Nathanson’s novel, set in World War II, was adapted to film and became one of the most enduring of its genre.

name: George Bugliarello
headline: George Bugliarello, Visionary Engineer, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Bugliarello, president of the Polytechnic Institute of New York for 21 years, spearheaded the creation of the MetroTech research park in Brooklyn.

name: Judith P. Sulzberger
headline: Judith P. Sulzberger, Physician and Times Family Member, Dies at 87
abstract: The philanthropy of Dr. Sulzberger — granddaughter, daughter and sister to newspaper publishers — produced a genome center at Columbia that bears her name.

name: Edward Zigo
profession: Detective in the Son of Sam Case
headline: Edward Zigo, a Detective in the ‘Son of Sam’ Case, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Zigo was a seasoned New York detective who helped arrest David Berkowitz for the so-called Son of Sam serial murders.

name: James McLure
headline: James McLure Dies at 59; Wrote Garrulous Plays
abstract: Mr. McLure, who was best known for plays like “Lone Star” and “Pvt. Wars,” had a following in the West and in regional theaters.

name: Charles Epstein
profession: Leading Medical Geneticist Injured by Unabomber
headline: Charles Epstein, Leading Medical Geneticist Injured by Unabomber, Dies at 77
abstract: Dr. Charles J. Epstein, best known for his work on Down syndrome, was seriously injured in a 1993 mail bomb attack by Theodore J. Kaczynski, the Unabomber.

name: Dwayne McDuffie
headline: Dwayne McDuffie, Comic-Book Writer, Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. McDuffie diversified the pantheon of superheroes by creating popular black characters in print and on television.

name: Sanford C. Sigoloff
headline: Sanford C. Sigoloff, Corporate Turnaround Expert, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Sigoloff was a corporate turnaround expert who called himself the “Skillful Scalpel” as he sought to preserve the value in failing companies.

name: Edwin Kilbourne
headline: Edwin Kilbourne, Flu Vaccine Expert, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Kilbourne was an adviser to President Gerald R. Ford on a controversial policy during the swine flu epidemic of 1976.

name: Haila Stoddard
headline: Haila Stoddard, Actress and Theatrical Producer, Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Stoddard, after a long career onstage and in television roles, brought the works of Noël Coward, James Thurber and Harold Pinter to Broadway.

name: Troy Jackson
headline: Troy Jackson, Street Basketball Star, Is Dead at 38
abstract: Nicknamed Escalade, the brother of the former Knicks player Mark Jackson had the size of a large center and the ball-handling skills of a small guard.

name: David T. Kearns
headline: David T. Kearns, Champion of Education Reform, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Kearns’s passion for education reform caught the attention of the first Bush administration, which tapped him to join the Education Department as a deputy secretary in 1991.

name: Christian Lambertsen
headline: Christian Lambertsen, Inventor of Scuba Precursor, Dies at 93
abstract: An underwater breathing device that Christian Lambertsen invented while in medical school was used by commandos in World War II.

name: Andy Jurinko
headline: Andy Jurinko, Painter Whose Art Memorialized Ballparks, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Jurinko specialized in baseball scenes from 1946 to 1960, like the Ebbets Field sign for Abe Stark’s clothing store.

name: Jay Landesman
headline: Jay Landesman, Beat Writer and Editor, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Landesman was a tireless impresario of one countercultural scene after another and a friend to the famous.

name: Snider
profession: Prince of New Yorks Golden Age of Baseball
headline: Duke Snider, a Prince of New York’s Golden Age of Baseball, Dies at 84
abstract: Snider was a center fielder renowned for his home run drives and defensive play in the Dodgers’ glory years.

name: Nobutoshi Kihara
headline: Nobutoshi Kihara, Sony Engineer, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Kihara was known as “the wizard of Sony” for his ingenuity in developing products, like Japan’s first tape recorder and transistor radio, and later the Betamax videocassette recorder.

name: Frank Buckles
headline: Frank Buckles, Last World War I Doughboy, Is Dead at 110
abstract: Mr. Buckles was the last living link to the two million men who served in the American Expeditionary Forces in France in “the war to end all wars.”

name: Anant Pai
profession: Comics Told Indian Children Their Countrys Stories
headline: Anant Pai, 81, Is Dead; Comics Told Indian Children Their Country’s Stories
abstract: In 1967, Mr. Pai founded Amar Chitra Katha, or Immortal Illustrated Stories, a comic book publisher whose series took their inspiration from India’s history and mythology.

name: Jane Russell
headline: Jane Russell, Sultry Star of 1940s and ’50s, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Russell was at the center of one of the most highly publicized censorship episodes in movie history, the release of the 1940s western “The Outlaw.”

name: Necmettin Erbakan
headline: Necmettin Erbakan, a Turkish Prime Minister, Dies at 84
abstract: During his year as Turkey’s first Islamist prime minister, Mr. Erbakan challenged the country’s secular dogma, vowing to create a pan-Islamic currency and rescue Turkey from “the unbelievers of Europe.”

name: Richard F. Daines
headline: Dr. Richard F. Daines, Former State Health Chief, Dies at 60
abstract: Dr. Daines was known for taking politically risky positions on public health policies like promoting a ban on using food stamps to buy soda.

name: Suze Rotolo
headline: Suze Rotolo, a Face, With Bob Dylan, of ’60s Music, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Ms. Rotolo became widely known for her romance with Bob Dylan in the early 1960s and strongly influenced his early songwriting.

name: Gary Winick
profession: Director of Small and Studio Films
headline: Gary Winick, Director of Small and Studio Films, Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. Winick was a producer and director of independent films who later graduated to big-budget studio work.

name: Peter J. Gomes
headline: Rev. Peter J. Gomes Is Dead at 68; A Leading Voice Against Intolerance
abstract: Mr. Gomes, a Harvard minister and theologian, embarked on a campaign to rebut literal and fundamentalist interpretations of the Bible.

name: Judith Coplon
headline: Judith Coplon, Haunted by Espionage Case, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Coplon, a political analyst for the Justice Department, was convicted of espionage more than 60 years ago after falling in love with a Soviet agent.

name: Annie Girardot
headline: Annie Girardot, Versatile French Actress, Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. Girardot, who played the doomed Milanese streetwalker in Luchino Visconti’s “Rocco and His Brothers,” moved easily from drama to comedy.

name: Eugene Fodor
headline: Eugene Fodor, Violin Virtuoso, Dies at 60
abstract: After an early competition success in Russia, the violinist was sometimes promoted as much for his image as for his talents.

name: James McClure
headline: James McClure, Powerful Western Senator, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. McClure was an Idaho Republican at a time when the party’s political pendulum was swinging West.

name: Carl B. Hess
headline: Carl B. Hess, Pioneer of Private Equity, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Hess founded AEA Investors, a precursor to the leveraged-buyout giants of the 1980s.

name: Greg Goossen
headline: Greg Goossen, Baseball Player Who Broke Mold, Dies at 65
abstract: The young prospect never lived up to expectations, but he still figured in some memorable moments in baseball history.

name: Wally Yonamine
headline: Wally Yonamine Dies at 85; Changed Japanese Baseball
abstract: When the Hawaiian-born athlete made his debut for the Yomiuri Giants in 1951, he was reviled by fans and players alike.

name: John Haines
headline: John Haines, a Poet of the Wild, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Haines, who won a lifetime achievement award from the Library of Congress, was a homesteader and hunter who extolled the Alaskan wilderness.

name: Arnost Lustig
headline: Arnost Lustig, Who Wrote Tales of Holocaust, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Lustig, a survivor of Auschwitz and Buchenwald, drew extensively on his wartime experiences for his novels and short stories.

name: Frank Chirkinian
headline: Frank Chirkinian, the Father of Televised Golf, Dies at 84
abstract: He was a CBS Sports producer who brought spectacle, multiple cameras and even a blimp to what was purely a black-and-white affair.

name: Moacyr Scliar
headline: Moacyr Scliar, Brazilian Novelist, Dies at 73
abstract: In existential fables like “Max and the Cats” and “The Centaur in the Garden,” Mr. Scliar explored the nature of Jewish identity in the Diaspora.

name: Alberto Granado
headline: Alberto Granado, 88, Friend of Che, Dies
abstract: Mr. Granado accompanied Che Guavara on a trip across South America.

name: Eddie Kirkland
profession: Known as the Gypsy of the Blues
headline: Eddie Kirkland, 87, Known as the Gypsy of the Blues, Dies
abstract: Mr. Kirkland, a guitarist, singer, songwriter and harmonica player, performed with some of the greatest names in blues and soul, including John Lee Hooker and Otis Redding.

name: Doyald Young
headline: Doyald Young, 84, Designer of Typefaces, Dies
abstract: Mr. Young’s three monographs on letterforms and alphabets reintroduced classical design principles to designers at a time when so-called grunge lettering was in vogue.

name: Walter Zacharius
headline: Walter Zacharius, Romance Publisher, Dies at 87
abstract: He rode the wave of romance fiction in the early 1980s to build Kensington Publishing into a leading purveyor of bodice-rippers.

name: Sam Chwat
headline: Sam Chwat, Dialect Tutor for Film Stars, Dies at 57
abstract: The founder of a speech therapy center in Manhattan taught Robert De Niro to sound Southern, and Julia Roberts not to.

name: Mike DeStefano
headline: Mike DeStefano, Stand-Up Comic, Is Dead
abstract: Years of addiction and recovery formed the basis of his popular comedy act.

name: Fateh Singh Rathore
headline: Fateh Singh Rathore, the ‘Tiger Guru,’ Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Rathore was a ranger, warden and field director at one of India’s best-known tiger preserves.

name: S. Hazard Gillespie
headline: S. Hazard Gillespie, Former U.S. Attorney, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Gillespie went after crooked financiers, labor racketeers and a Guatemalan diplomat doubling as a heroin smuggler.

name: David Broder
headline: David Broder, Political Journalist and Pundit, Dies at 81
abstract: The Pulitzer Prize-winning Washington Post reporter had covered politics since Eisenhower was president.

name: Owen Laster
headline: Owen Laster, Literary Agent at William Morris, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Laster ran William Morris’s worldwide literary operations and had best-selling writers who included James A. Michener and Gore Vidal.

name: Kim Hill
headline: Kim Hill, Inspiration for Ronald McDonald House, Dies at 44
abstract: Ms. Hill’s childhood battle with leukemia led to the creation of charitable efforts to house young patients’ families.

name: James Elliot
headline: James Elliot Is Dead at 67; Discovered Rings of Uranus
abstract: Mr. Elliot was an astronomer who used light from distant stars to study planetary objects throughout the solar system, leading to the discovery.

name: Alfred Brittain
headline: Alfred Brittain, Who Reshaped Bankers Trust, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Brittain, who became Bankers Trust’s top executive in 1975, sold retail branches and expanded what became a very lucrative merchant-banking business.

name: Simon van der Meer
headline: Simon van der Meer, Nobel Laureate, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. van der Meer shared the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1984 for a technological advance that was crucial to the discovery of fundamental building blocks of the universe.

name: Danny Stiles
headline: Danny Stiles, Radio Host Who Kept the Oldies New, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Stiles was a radio man who offered a journey to the past that fans couldn’t find anywhere else on the dial.

name: Jean Dinning
profession: Songwriter of Pop Tragedy Teen Angel
headline: Jean Dinning, Songwriter of Pop Tragedy ‘Teen Angel,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Dinning wrote a song, sung by her brother, Mark, that became almost mythical the minute it was released in October 1959.

name: E. B. Leisenring Jr.
headline: E. B. Leisenring Jr., Coal Executive, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Leisenring, who had worked in his family’s mines before rising to become president of one of the country’s biggest coal companies, was long a national spokesman for mine owners.

name: Jack Hardy
profession: Folk Singer and Keeper of the Tradition
headline: Jack Hardy, Folk Singer and Keeper of the Tradition, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Hardy’s Greenwich Village recordings and songwriting workshops kept alive the neighborhood tradition of counterculture troubadours.

name: Joe Morello
headline: Joe Morello, Drummer with Dave Brubeck Quartet, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Morello’s elegant, economical playing in the quartet sounded natural and effortless even in unusual time signatures.

name: D.L. Cox
headline: D.L. Cox, a Leader of Radicals During 1960s, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Cox was at the center of black radical politics as a member of the Black Panther Party high command and earned a moment of celebrity in 1970.

name: Hugh Martin
headline: Hugh Martin, Composer of Judy Garland Hits, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Martin’s credits included “Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas,” “The Boy Next Door,” and “The Trolley Song.”

name: Al Morgan
headline: Al Morgan, Novelist, Playwright and Television Producer, Is Dead at 91
abstract: In “The Great Man,” Mr. Morgan used his experience in the radio business to tell the story of a beloved radio personality who was really a sadistic lecher.

name: Leo Steinberg
headline: Leo Steinberg, Art Historian, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Steinberg, a keen intellect and writer, is credited with opening up generations of scholars to new ways of seeing.

name: Owsley Stanley
headline: Owsley Stanley, Artisan of Acid, Is Dead at 76
abstract: The man who pioneered the mass-production of LSD in the 1960s was killed in an automobile accident in Australia.

name: Donny George
headline: Donny George, Protector of Iraq’s Ancient Riches, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. George led in the recovery of thousands of archaeological treasures that had been stolen from the Iraq National Museum.

name: Steven Kroll
headline: Steven Kroll, an Author of Children’s Books, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Kroll was a prolific author of popular children’s books, many of them evoking his experiences growing up in New York City.

name: Hazel Rowley
profession: Biographer With Taste for the Singular
headline: Hazel Rowley, Biographer With Taste for the Singular, Dies at 59
abstract: Ms. Rowley’s subjects ranged from the Roosevelts’ marriage to Sartre and de Beauvoir.

name: Rick Martin
headline: Rick Martin, Part of Famed N.H.L. Line, Dies at 59 After Car Accident
abstract: Mr. Martin was a member of the Buffalo Sabres’ celebrated French Connection in the 1970s, and is the team’s career leader in hat tricks, scoring three or more goals in a game 21 times.

name: Gabriel Laderman
headline: Gabriel Laderman, Painter of Figurative Art, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Laderman played a leading role in the revival of figurative art in the 1960s and 1970s.

name: Shifra Lerer
headline: Shifra Lerer, Actress in Yiddish Theater, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Lerer was discovered at age 5 in Argentina by the great Yiddish actor Boris Thomashefsky and went on to have a 90-year career in Yiddish theater.

name: Marty Marion
headline: Marty Marion, Cardinals’s Slick-Fielding Shortstop, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Marion, known as the Octopus for his long arms and ability to gobble up ground balls, was an All-Star every season from 1943 to 1950.

name: Victor Blanco
headline: Victor Blanco, Stargazer, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Blanco, an astronomer, helped build a major outpost for American science in Chile and shepherded it through revolution and economic turmoil.

name: Nate Dogg
headline: Nate Dogg, Hip-Hop Collaborator, Dies at 41
abstract: Nate Dogg was a singer with a silky, burly voice who helped shape the sound of West Coast hip-hop.

name: Bob Marcucci
headline: Bob Marcucci, a Rock Music Idol Maker, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Marcucci, who discovered Frankie Avalon and Fabian, was a lyricist and co-owner of Chancellor Records.

name: Richard Wirthlin
headline: Richard Wirthlin, Pollster Who Advised Reagan, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Wirthlin helped Reagan shape his political message and strategies, both in presidential campaigns and in the White House.

name: Velvet-Voiced Ferlin Husky
headline: Velvet-Voiced Ferlin Husky Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Husky recorded the hit song “Gone” that crossed over to pop charts and helped country music bounce back commercially after an assault from rock ‘n’ roll.

name: Pierre de Beaumont
headline: Pierre de Beaumont, Brookstone Founder, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. de Beaumont and his wife, Mary, started the gadget catalog, which grew into a chain of stores, in their farmhouse in the Berkshires.

name: David Rumelhart
headline: David Rumelhart Dies at 68; Created Computer Simulations of Perception
abstract: Dr. Rumelhart work proved helpful in the development of machine learning and artificial intelligence.

name: Brian Lanker
headline: Brian Lanker, Pulitzer-Winning Photojournalist, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Lanker, who won a Pulitzer Prize in 1973, focused on intimate portrayals of American lives.

name: Warren Christopher
headline: Warren Christopher, Lawyer, Negotiator and Adviser to Presidents, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Christopher was secretary of state in President Clinton’s first term and the chief negotiator for the 1981 release of American hostages in Iran.

name: Carel Boshoff
profession: Founder of White Redoubt in South Africa
headline: Carel Boshoff, Founder of White Redoubt in South Africa, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Boshoff established Orania, the community in South Africa that remains the country’s last bastion of white separatism.

name: Toshiko Takaezu
headline: Toshiko Takaezu, Ceramic Artist, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Takaezu helped to move clay from a functional role to one of abstraction and creative expression.

name: Drew Hill
headline: Drew Hill, Receiver for Run-and-Shoot Oilers, Dies at 54
abstract: Drew Hill arrived in the N.F.L. as an unheralded 12th-round draft pick and became a Pro Bowl receiver in 1988 and 1990.

name: Melvin Sparks
headline: Melvin Sparks, Guitarist, Is Dead at 64
abstract: Mr. Sparks liked to say simply that he played “jazz over a funky beat.”

name: W.J. Stuntz
headline: W.J. Stuntz, Who Stimulated Legal Minds, Dies at 52
abstract: A Harvard law professor known for counterintuitive insights, Mr. Stuntz blamed judges, lawmakers and prosecutors for sending far too many people to prison.

name: Emmett J. Rice
headline: Emmett J. Rice, Former Fed Governor, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Rice served at the World Bank and at the Agency for International Development, where he helped Nigeria establish its central bank in the 1960s.

name: Pinetop Perkins
headline: Pinetop Perkins, Delta Boogie-Woogie Master, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Perkins was a member of Muddy Waters’s last great band and one of the last of a generation of Mississippi bluesmen.

name: G. A. Marlatt
profession: Advocate of Shift in Treating Addicts
headline: G. A. Marlatt, Advocate of Shift in Treating Addicts, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Marlatt challenged the belief that substance addiction is incurable and can be controlled only by abstinence.

name: David Nevin
headline: David Nevin, Author of Historical Novels, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Nevin’s best-known book, “Dream West,” told the epic tale of John Charles Frémont’s role in the opening of the American West.

name: Nikolai Andrianov
headline: Nikolai Andrianov, Gymnastics Icon, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Andrianov was a record-setting Russian gymnast who had won 15 Olympic medals, seven of them gold.

name: Sara Ruddick
headline: Sara Ruddick, Gave Due to Motherhood, Philosophically, Dies at 76
abstract: In her 1989 book, “Maternal Thinking,” she analyzed the practices and intellectual disciplines involved in raising children.

name: Frank Neuhauser
headline: Frank Neuhauser, a Speller’s Speller, Dies at 97
abstract: With a correct spelling of “G-L-A-D-I-O-L-U-S,” Mr. Neuhauser won the first National Spelling Bee in 1925.

name: Elizabeth Taylor
headline: A Lustrous Pinnacle of Hollywood Glamour
abstract: Elizabeth Taylor, whose name was synonymous with Hollywood glamour, dazzled generations of moviegoers with her beauty.

name: Helen Stenborg
headline: Helen Stenborg, Actress From Theatrical Family, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Stenborg’s myriad roles on Broadway ranged from the loopy Sarita Myrtle in Noël Coward’s “Waiting in the Wings” to Rebecca Nurse in “The Crucible.”

name: Loleatta Holloway
headline: Loleatta Holloway, Gospel and Disco Singer, Is Dead at 64
abstract: Ms. Holloway’s 1980 hit “Love Sensation” had a long afterlife when fragments of it were used in later hits.

name: Lanford Wilson
headline: Lanford Wilson, Pulitzer Prize-Winning Playwright, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Wilson’s work — earthy, realist, greatly admired, widely performed — centered on the sheer ordinariness of marginality.

name: Richard Leacock
headline: Richard Leacock, Innovative Documentary Maker, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Leacock helped create the documentary style known as cinéma vérité, and played a pivotal role in making some of the most novel documentaries of the 1960s.

name: Leonard I. Weinglass
headline: Leonard I. Weinglass, Lawyer, Dies at 77; Defended Renegades and the Notorious
abstract: Mr. Weinglass was at the center of many contentious cases, including the Chicago Seven, the Pentagon Papers and the Hearst kidnapping.

name: Dorothy Young
headline: Dorothy Young, Houdini’s Stage Assistant, Is Dead at 103
abstract: An aide to the magician at age 17, she kept her promise not to reveal his secrets.

name: Geraldine Ferraro
headline: She Ended the Men’s Club of National Politics
abstract: In 1984, Ms. Ferraro took her place in American history as the first woman nominated for national office by a major party.

name: John Cashin Jr.
headline: John Cashin Jr. Dies at 82; Campaigned for Civil Rights
abstract: Dr. Cashin was the first black person since Reconstruction to run for governor of Alabama.

name: Ralph Mooney
headline: Ralph Mooney, Master of the Steel Guitar, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Mooney played pedal steel guitar on hit recordings by Merle Haggard and Waylon Jennings and was a pioneer of the Bakersfield sound that took root in California in the late 1950s.

name: Harry Coover
headline: Harry Coover, Super Glue’s Inventor, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Coover first happened upon the super-sticky adhesive by accident when he was working on plastic gun-sights for Eastman Kodak during World War II.

name: Paul Baran
headline: Paul Baran, Internet Pioneer, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Baran was an engineer who helped create the technical underpinnings for the Arpanet, the government-sponsored precursor to today’s Internet.

name: Diana Wynne Jones
headline: Diana Wynne Jones, Children’s Author, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Jones was a creator of the Chrestomanci series and other works that imagined magical worlds with a skeptical eye.

name: Matteo
headline: Matteo, Master of Spanish Dance, Dies at 92
abstract: Matteo was a teacher, choreographer and scholar in a career that reached a wide audience after he and Carola Goya formed the Spanish dance team of Goya and Matteo in 1954.

name: Lee Hoiby
headline: Lee Hoiby, 85; Composed Operas and Songs
abstract: Mr. Hoiby composed operas and songs that balance unabashed lyricism and careful craftsmanship.

name: Farley Granger
headline: Farley Granger, Screen Star of the 1950s, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Granger, who had early roles for Hitchcock and Goldwyn, had the makings of a big movie star, but his passion for stage acting moved him to leave Hollywood behind.

name: George Tooker
headline: George Tooker, Painter Capturing Modern Anxieties, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Tooker’s haunting images of trapped clerical workers and forbidding government offices expressed a peculiarly 20th-century brand of anxiety and alienation.

name: Irving Shulman
headline: Irving Shulman, Retailer of Discount Apparel, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Shulman was a familiar sight as he helped customers at Daffy’s, mostly at the 57th Street store in Manhattan.

name: Ellen McCormack
headline: Ellen McCormack, Anti-Abortion Presidential Candidate, Dies at 84
abstract: Mrs. McCormack ran for president in 1976 and 1980, doing well enough to become the first woman to qualify as a candidate for federal financing and Secret Service protection.

name: Thomas Eisner
headline: Thomas Eisner, Who Cracked Chemistry of Bugs, Dies at 81
abstract: Dr. Eisner’s research revealed the complex chemistry that insects use to repel predators, attract mates and protect their young.

name: H. R. F. Keating
headline: H. R. F. Keating, Author of Crime Series, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Keating, the prolific British crime novelist who created Ganesh Ghote, the humble Indian police inspector, led a literary life saturated with crime.

name: Gil Clancy
headline: Gil Clancy, Boxing Manager and Trainer, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Clancy was a Hall of Fame boxing manager and trainer who guided Emile Griffith to the welterweight and middleweight championships.

name: Manning Marable
headline: Manning Marable, Historian and Social Critic, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Marable, a leading scholar of black history and critic of American social institutions, wrote a biography of Malcolm X that is to be published on Monday.

name: Lou Gorman
headline: Lou Gorman, Whose Red Sox Lost to Mets, Dies at 82
abstract: As Boston’s general manager, Mr. Gorman watched his team come within one strike of winning the 1986 World Series.

name: Don Hill
profession: Nightclub Owner and Fixture of SoHo Scene
headline: Don Hill, Nightclub Owner and Fixture of SoHo Scene, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Hill started his career in the late 1970s, managing Manhattan clubs like the popular Kenny’s Castaways and the Bitter End.

name: Stanley Bogdan
headline: Stanley Bogdan, Maker of Much-Coveted Fly Reels, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Bogdan’s reels were so coveted that anglers were willing to spend years on a waiting list to buy them and then to pay far more than they would have for reels of only ordinary excellence.

name: José Argüelles
headline: José Argüelles, New Ager Focused on Time, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Argüelles organized the Harmonic Convergence, which drew thousands of adherents to sites around the globe and also focused the popular imagination the Mayan calendar.

name: William Young
profession: Helped U.S. Organize Secret War in Laos
headline: William Young, Who Helped U.S. Organize Secret War in Laos, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Mr. Young was a member of a missionary family in Southeast Asia who mixed evangelical zeal with covert missions for the C.I.A.

name: Dino Anagnost
headline: Dino Anagnost, Who Led Little Orchestra Society, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Anagnost was the longtime conductor of the Little Orchestra Society, as well as leading choral groups.

name: Edwin Gaustad
headline: Edwin Gaustad, Religious Historian, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Gaustad wrote seminal works on the religious ideas of the founding fathers and on the arguments about church versus state.

name: Mandi Schwartz
profession: Athlete at Center of Marrow Drive
headline: Mandi Schwartz, Athlete at Center of Marrow Drive, Dies at 23
abstract: Ms. Schwartz was a Yale hockey player whose struggle with leukemia inspired thousands of people to volunteer to be bone marrow donors.

name: Ned McWherter
headline: Ned McWherter, Former Tennessee Governor, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. McWherter was a onetime factory worker who became a wealthy businessman and a two-term Democratic governor.

name: Henry Taub
headline: Henry Taub, a Founder of a Payroll Firm That Became a Global Giant, Dies at 83
abstract: The business he helped start on a shoestring in 1949 now has annual sales of more than $9 billion and 550,000 clients, and is one of the largest providers of business services.

name: Bernard Clayton Jr.
headline: Bernard Clayton Jr., Cookbook Author, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Mr. Clayton was a former newspaper reporter who wrote several classic cookbooks on bread and pastry.

name: D.M. French
headline: Dr. D.M. French Dies at 86; Treated ’60s Marchers
abstract: Dr. French helped found an organization of doctors that provided medical care to marchers during the civil rights era and who later organized health care programs in 20 African nations.

name: Baruch Blumberg
headline: Baruch Blumberg, Who Discovered and Tackled Hepatitis B, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Blumberg’s work led to the discovery of the hepatitis B virus in 1967, the first test for hepatitis B in the blood supply and the development of the hepatitis B vaccine.

name: W. H. Prusoff
headline: W. H. Prusoff, Who Developed AIDS Drug, Is Dead at 90
abstract: In the early 1950s, Dr. Prusoff also synthesized idoxuridine, a successful treatment for infant keratitis.

name: Jean Bartik
headline: Jean Bartik, Software Pioneer, Dies at 86
abstract: She worked on Eniac, the first all-electronic digital computer, as well as Univac, an early commercial computer.

name: Edward Bigelow
profession: Dancer With the New York City Ballet
headline: Edward Bigelow, Dancer With the New York City Ballet, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Bigelow, who originated many dramatic character roles, also served as an administrator for the company.

name: Bosko Radonjic
headline: Bosko Radonjic, Gambino Family Ally, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Radonjic, who was one of six Serbian nationalists convicted in a 1975 bombing in Yugoslavia, later exerted influence over organized crime in New York.

name: L. J. Davis
headline: L. J. Davis, Journalist and Novelist, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Mr. Davis, a contributing editor at Harper’s, wrote about business, home renovation, the Industrial Revolution and Brooklyn, often with wry or sardonic humor.

name: Sidney Lumet
headline: A Director of Classics, Focused on Conscience
abstract: Mr. Lumet, who preferred the streets of New York to the back lots of Hollywood, directed “12 Angry Men,” “Serpico,” “Dog Day Afternoon,” “The Verdict,” “Network,” among others.

name: Gil Robbins
headline: Gil Robbins, Folk Singer With the Highwaymen, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Robbins was a fixture on the folk music scene in the 1960s and the father of the actor Tim Robbins.

name: Mike Campbell
headline: Mike Campbell, Zimbabwean Farmer Who Fought Land Seizure, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Campbell won a 2008 court ruling to stop the seizure of his land, after he was severely beaten by loyalists of President Robert Mugabe. He lost the farm anyway.

name: John McCracken
headline: John McCracken, Sculptor of Geometric Forms, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. McCracken brought a sense of play and spirituality to his work with slabs, blocks and columns.

name: Yakov Kreizberg
headline: Yakov Kreizberg, Orchestral Conductor, Dies at 51
abstract: Mr. Kreizberg was music director of the Orchestre Philharmonique de Monte-Carlo and chief conductor of the Netherlands Philharmonic.

name: Hedda Sterne
headline: Hedda Sterne, an Artist of Many Styles, Dies at 100
abstract: Ms. Sterne was the last survivor of a famous 1951 Life magazine portrait of forward-thinking artists who included Jackson Pollock, Robert Motherwell and Mark Rothko.

name: Daniel Catán
headline: Daniel Catán, Composer of Operas in Spanish, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Catán, a Mexican composer, is credited with introducing Spanish-language operas into the world repertory.

name: Salvador Assael
headline: Salvador Assael, 88, Dies; Coaxed Riches From Pearls
abstract: Mr. Assael, founder and chairman of the pearl importer and producer Assael International, provided the black pearls that adorned many a famous décolletage.

name: Charles Laufer
headline: Charles Laufer, Founder of Tiger Beat, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Laufer was the founder of Tiger Beat, a glossy magazine aimed at teenage girls desperate to know more about the lives of stars.

name: Sidney Harman
headline: Sidney Harman, Newsweek Chairman, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Harman made a late-in-life splash by acquiring Newsweek magazine and wedding it with a sassy Web site, The Daily Beast.

name: Gerald A. Lawson
headline: Gerald A. Lawson, a Pioneer in Video Games, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Lawson, by creating interchangeable game cartridges, made it possible to play a variety of video games at home.

name: Michael C. Latham
profession: Expert on Nutrition in Developing World
headline: Michael C. Latham, Expert on Nutrition in Developing World, Dies at 82
abstract: Dr. Latham waged a long battle for the promotion of breastfeeding over infant formulas in developing countries.

name: Billy Bang
profession: Jazz Violinist Inspired by Vietnam Experience
headline: Billy Bang, Jazz Violinist Inspired by Vietnam Experience, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Bang’s best-known work involved two albums and a documentary drawn from his service in the Vietnam War.

name: Abraham Rothberg
headline: Abraham Rothberg, Who Wrote of Golem and Stalin, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Rothberg’s works roamed from the ghettos of medieval Prague through the counterculture upheavals of America in the 1960s to the machinations of Soviet Communism.

name: Arthur Marx
headline: Arthur Marx, Who Wrote About Groucho, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Marx, who wrote screenplays for film and television and a best-selling book about his father, Groucho, is dead at 89.

name: Randy Wood
headline: Randy Wood, Founder of Dot Records, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Wood’s label found success in the 1950s recording white artists like Pat Boone singing black artists’ rhythm-and-blues songs.

name: Homer Smith
headline: Homer Smith, Innovative College Football Coach, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Smith’s strategies enlivened the offenses at U.C.L.A., Alabama and Arizona, and he was the coach at Army in the difficult years at the end of the Vietnam War.

name: William N. Lipscomb Jr.
headline: William N. Lipscomb Jr., Nobel Prize-Winning Chemist, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Lipscomb, a Harvard professor and protégé of Linus Pauling, did not mind mixing music and humor into his repertory that focused on molecular structure and chemical bonding.

name: Paul Violi
headline: Paul Violi, a Poet Both Wry and Sly, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Violi created his own verse forms, many of them based on the most mundane of models.

name: Garry Reigenborn
headline: Garry Reigenborn, a Dancer and Influential Choreographer, Dies at 58
abstract: As a dancer, Mr. Reigenborn was the epitome of the deceptively cool Minimalist style that emerged in the dance avant-garde of the 1970s.

name: Cyrus Harvey
headline: Cyrus Harvey, an Extravagant Entrepreneur, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Harvey created two significant business brands in very disparate fields — a film company and a soap company.

name: Geoff Miller
headline: Geoff Miller, Co-Founder of Los Angeles Magazine, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Miller and David Brown started Los Angeles magazine, one of the nation’s first city magazines, in 1960, eight years before New York magazine was first published.

name: Arthur Lessac
headline: Arthur Lessac, Holistic Vocal Coach, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Lessac’s method, which he taught up to age 101, combined voice and movement in an almost spiritual mix.

name: Roger Nichols
headline: Roger Nichols, Artist Among Sound Engineers, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Nichols’s penchant for perfectionism earned him seven Grammys and made him the audio engineer of choice for Steely Dan.

name: Roger Nichols
headline: Roger Nichols, Songwriter Behind Carpenters Hits, Dies at 84
abstract: With Paul Williams, he wrote enduring 1970s pop classics like “We’ve Only Just Begun” and “Rainy Days and Mondays.”

name: William Rusher
headline: William Rusher, Champion of Conservatism, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Rusher advanced a conservative tide in the U.S. as a political strategist, author, columnist and publisher.

name: William Schaefer
headline: William Schaefer, Baltimore Mayor, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Schaefer was a political showman who captivated voters and infuriated critics as the mayor who rejuvenated decaying Baltimore and then as Maryland’s governor and comptroller.

name: Pietro Ferrero
headline: Pietro Ferrero, Food Company Scion, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. Ferrero helped lead a family business whose most popular brands include Nutella and Tic Tacs.

name: Bijan Pakzad
headline: Bijan Pakzad, Designer of High Fashion, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Pakzad’s by-appointment-only Rodeo Drive boutique is billed as “the most expensive store in the world.”

name: Evelyn Einstein
profession: Shaped by a Link to Fame
headline: Evelyn Einstein Dies at 70; Shaped by a Link to Fame
abstract: Her tumultuous life as the granddaughter of Albert Einstein was both defined and limited by her distinguished lineage.

name: Grete Waitz
headline: Grete Waitz, Marathon Champion, Dies at 57
abstract: The Norwegian runner won the New York marathon nine times, setting a record in her first race in 1978.

name: Allan Blakeney
headline: Allan Blakeney, Pioneer of Canadian Health Care, Dies at 85
abstract: As health minister in Saskatchewan, Mr. Blakeney oversaw the start of the province’s universal health care program in the early 1960s. He later became provincial premier.

name: Michael Sarrazin
headline: Michael Sarrazin, Actor, Dies at 70
abstract: A leading man in the late 1960s and ’70s, Mr. Sarrazin brought youthful innocence with a dash of countercultural rebelliousness to his films.

name: Robert Vickrey
headline: Robert Vickrey, Magic-Realist Painter, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Vickrey mastered the Renaissance technique of egg tempera painting, using his technical skills to create hyper-real scenes suffused by an atmosphere of dread.

name: Joseph Selame
headline: Joseph Selame, Designer of Corporate Logos, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Selame had a minimalist sensibility and defied convention to make a bank warm and approachable.

name: Mason Rudolph
headline: Mason Rudolph, Consistent Contender on PGA Tour, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Rudolph, who won five PGA Tour titles in a 23-year career, was known for his craftsmanship.

name: Alfred Freedman
headline: Alfred Freedman, a Leader in Psychiatry, Dies at 94
abstract: As president of the American Psychiatric Association, Dr. Freedman helped bring an end to the policy declaring homosexuality a mental illness.

name: Madelyn Pugh Davis
headline: Madelyn Pugh Davis, Writer for ‘I Love Lucy,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Davis and her 1950s writing partners were responsible for coming up with wacky physical predicaments for the show’s star, Lucille Ball, to get herself into.

name: Sol Saks
headline: Sol Saks, Writer of ‘Bewitched’ Pilot, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Saks was behind the first episode of the popular sitcom about a suburban housewife skilled in the uses of enchantment.

name: Jess Jackson
profession: Wine Grower With a Taste for Thoroughbred Racing
headline: Jess Jackson Dies at 81, a Wine Grower With a Taste for Thoroughbred Racing
abstract: Mr. Jackson started out as a lawyer, later building the Kendall-Jackson wine company.

name: Joel Colton
headline: Joel Colton, Who Kept History Current for 50 Years, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Colton updated the classic textbook “A History of the Modern World” for more than 50 years after its publication.

name: Lewis Binford
headline: Lewis Binford, Leading Archaeologist, Dies at 79
abstract: Dr. Binford studied living hunters and gatherers to better understand similar societies from the past.

name: Hazel Dickens
headline: Hazel Dickens, Folk Singer, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Dickens, who was a pioneer among women in bluegrass music, sang of hardships and struggles.

name: Vincenzo La Scola
headline: Vincenzo La Scola, Italian Tenor, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. La Scola, who was known as both an opera singer and a crossover artist, performed widely in Europe.

name: Violet Cowden
headline: Violet Cowden, Wartime Plane Pilot, Is Dead at 94
abstract: A member of the Women Airforce Service Pilots, Mrs. Cowden flew and transported some of the country’s most sophisticated military planes.

name: Max Mathews
headline: Max Mathews, Pioneer in Making Computer Music, Dies at 84
abstract: As an engineer for Bell Laboratories in 1957, Mr. Mathews wrote the first program to make it possible for a computer to synthesize sound and play it back.

name: Peter Lieberson
headline: Peter Lieberson, Composer Inspired by Buddhism, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Lieberson was an inventive voice in the generation of composers who sought to infuse academic music with a more accessible sound.

name: Norio Ohga
headline: Norio Ohga, Who Led Sony Beyond Electronics, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Ohga was the principal architect of Sony’s move beyond its stronghold of sleek consumer electronics gear and into music and movies.

name: Alan Champion
headline: Alan Champion, Sign-Language Interpreter for Theater, Dies at 55
abstract: With skilled hands and intense concentration, Mr. Champion brought theater to deaf and hearing-impaired audience members on Broadway and beyond.

name: Joan Peyser
headline: Joan Peyser, Bernstein and Gershwin Biographer, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Peyser’s biographies of Leonard Bernstein and George Gershwin were controversial in concentrating as much on their personal lives as on their music.

name: Bill Cook
