headline: Bill Cook, Medical Device Maker, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Cook created a company that makes heart stents and living-tissue transplants as well as other products, and was ranked by Forbes magazine as the 101st richest American.

name: Joe Perry
headline: Joe Perry, 49ers Hall of Fame Fullback, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Perry, who was known as the “Jet” throughout his career, was one of pro football’s top runners in the decade after World War II and the first to run for 1,000 yards two N.F.L. seasons in a row.

name: Marie-France Pisier
headline: Marie-France Pisier, New Wave Darling, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Pisier, who has dozens of French films to her credit, caught François Truffaut’s eye when she auditioned for him at the age of 17 and went on to appear in three of his films.

name: Phoebe Snow
headline: Phoebe Snow, Bluesy Singer-Songwriter, Dies at 60
abstract: Ms. Snow’s “Poetry Man” was her defining hit song, and the folk guitarist made forays into jazz and blues.

name: Nhu
headline: Madame Nhu, Vietnam War Lightning Rod, Dies
abstract: The glamorous official hostess in South Vietnam’s presidential palace became a politically powerful and harshly outspoken figure during the Vietnam War.

name: Poly Styrene
headline: Poly Styrene, Punk Singer of X-Ray Spex, Is Dead at 53
abstract: As the leader of the band X-Ray Spex in the late 1970s, Poly Styrene, real name Marianne Elliot-Said, made a place for feminine brashness in punk and challenged conformism with her searing lyrics.

name: Max van der Stoel
headline: Max van der Stoel, Diplomat Who Uncovered Hussein’s Abuses, Dies at 86
abstract: In a series of reports in the 1990s, Mr. van der Stoel painted a searing portrait of the human rights abuses under Saddam Hussein in Iraq.

name: Hubert Schlafly
headline: Hubert Schlafly, Who Helped Build Teleprompter, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Schlafly, an electrical engineer, formed the TelePrompTer Corporation with two colleagues after 20th Century Fox declined to invest in their device.

name: Sidney Michaels
headline: Sidney Michaels, Playwright, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. Michaels was the author of a farce called “Tchin-Tchin,” and the musical “Ben Franklin in Paris.”

name: Orlando Bosch
headline: Orlando Bosch, Cuban Exile, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Bosch became a lightning rod in the Cuban-exile world, accused of a 1976 bombing that killed 73 people.

name: Harry Jackson
headline: Harry Jackson, Artist Who Captured the West, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Jackson was a Marine combat artist who turned his back on a promising career as an Abstract Expressionist painter to produce paintings and bronze sculptures of cowboys and Indians.

name: David Wilkerson
headline: Rev. David Wilkerson Dies at 79; Started Times Square Church
abstract: Mr. Wilkerson, who worked with young drug addicts and gang members in the 1950s, founded the Times Square Church to minister to the downtrodden.

name: Vincent O’Leary
headline: Vincent O’Leary, Who Revived Albany University, Dies at 86
abstract: As president at the State University of New York at Albany, Mr. O’Leary developed 27 specialized graduate programs, invigorating the school after a period of decline.

name: Bill Blackbeard
headline: Bill Blackbeard, Comic Strip Champion, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Blackbeard rescued Mutt and Jeff, Little Nemo, Naughty Pete, Polly Sleepyhead and more, in their ephemeral form.

name: David L. Hackett
profession: Led Efforts on Poverty and Juvenile Crime
headline: David L. Hackett, Led Efforts on Poverty and Juvenile Crime, Dies at 84
abstract: A longtime friend of Robert Kennedy, he led President Kennedy’s “total attack” on juvenile delinquency.

name: David Hackett
headline: David Hackett, Historian and Holocaust Expert, Dies at 80
abstract: Professor Hackett translated “The Buchenwald Report,” a vital account of life at the Buchenwald concentration camp. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Ernesto Sábato
headline: Ernesto Sábato, Argentina’s Conscience, Is Dead at 99
abstract: Mr. Sábato was an acclaimed novelist who led a commission that documented the atrocities committed by Argentina’s military dictatorship.

name: James Regan
headline: James Regan, Who Led City Education Board, Dies at 81
abstract: At the height of New York City’s fiscal crisis in the mid-1970s, Mr. Regan clashed with the mayor over budget cuts, teacher layoffs and a plan to close schools.

name: Ira Cohen
headline: Ira Cohen, an Artist and a Touchstone, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Cohen, a filmmaker, photographer and poet, ranged from his artists’ salon on the Lower East Side to pilgrimages to Marrakesh, Katmandu and the banks of the Ganges.

name: Henry Cooper
headline: Henry Cooper, Dramatic Loser to Ali, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr Cooper, the popular British heavyweight, never held the world championship but earned renown for a 1963 fight he lost to Cassius Clay.

name: Henry S. F. Cooper Jr.
headline: Henry S. F. Cooper Jr., Space Reporter With Literary Lineage, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Cooper, a descendant of James Fenimore Cooper, was an author, a writer for The New Yorker and the bulletin editor for the Century Association.

name: Moshe Landau
headline: Moshe Landau Dies at 99; Oversaw Eichmann Trial
abstract: Justice Landau, a refugee from Nazi Germany and a member of the Israeli Supreme Court for nearly 30 years, was the presiding judge in the war-crimes trial of Adolf Eichmann.

name: Richard Cornuelle
headline: Richard Cornuelle, Libertarian Author, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Cornuelle’s book, “Reclaiming the American Dream,” promoted volunteerism to help solve social problems.

name: Harold Garfinkel
headline: Harold Garfinkel, a Common-Sense Sociologist, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Garfinkel, whose theories espoused the mind-sets and behaviorial patterns of jurors, was affiliated with the sociology department at U.C.L.A. for more than 50 years.

name: René Emilio Ponce
profession: El Salvador General Linked to Priests Murders
headline: René Emilio Ponce, El Salvador General Linked to Priests’ Murders, Dies at 64
abstract: Col. René Emilio Ponce led a military accused of atrocities during El Salvador’s civil war.

name: Ronald D. Asmus
headline: Ronald D. Asmus, Official Who Favored Expanded NATO, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Asmus advocated the inclusion of such nations as Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic into the alliance.

name: William Campbell
headline: William Campbell, Who Played ‘Star Trek’ Klingon, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Campbell, an actor with many film and television credits, was also the first husband of Judith Campbell Exner, a mistress of President John F. Kennedy.

name: William C. Campbell
headline: William C. Campbell, a Leader in Golf, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Campbell was a champion of golf’s amateur era who later led his sport’s two most prestigious governing organizations.

name: David J. Sencer
headline: David J. Sencer Dies at 86; Led Disease-Control Agency
abstract: As a federal and New York City public health official, Dr. Sencer confronted some of the most threatening infectious diseases of the past half century and found controversy in both roles.

name: Jackie Cooper
headline: Jackie Cooper, Film and Television Actor, Dies at 88
abstract: The pug-nosed kid who became America’s Boy in tear-jerker films of the Great Depression flourished as an adult in television and modern pictures.

name: Marian Mercer
headline: Marian Mercer, Actress With Zany Streak, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Ms. Mercer won a Tony in 1969 for her performance as a pickup girl in the hit musical “Promises, Promises.”

name: Arthur Laurents
headline: Arthur Laurents, Playwright and Director on Broadway, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Laurents was a playwright, screenwriter and director who wrote and ultimately transformed two of Broadway’s landmark shows, “Gypsy” and “West Side Story.”

name: Lanny Friedlander
headline: Lanny Friedlander, Founder of Reason Magazine, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Friedlander founded the libertarian magazine Reason in his college dorm room in 1968 and ran it briefly before dropping out of sight for the next 40 years.

name: Seve Ballesteros
headline: Seve Ballesteros, Dashing Golf Champion, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Ballesteros won five major titles and helped propel Europe’s rise in the Ryder Cup competition with the United States.

name: Albert Bachmann
headline: Albert Bachmann, a Colorful Swiss Spymaster, Dies at 81
abstract: His dread of a Soviet invasion led him to create a secret intelligence service and guerrilla force unknown to the Swiss government in the 1970s.

name: Steven Orszag
headline: Steven Orszag, Pioneer in Fluid Dynamics Study, Dies at 68
abstract: Dr. Orszag’s research had wide-ranging applications in airplane and auto design, meteorology and astrophysics.

name: Louis Stumberg
headline: Louis Stumberg, Who Brought Tex-Mex to TV Dinners, Dies at 87
abstract: Along with his father and his brother, Mr. Stumberg founded Patio Foods, distributing frozen tamales, burritos and enchiladas nationwide.

name: Joanna Russ
headline: Joanna Russ, Who Drew Women to Sci-Fi, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Russ was best known for her 1975 novel, “The Female Man,” which was considered a landmark of its genre.

name: Mildred Leet
headline: Mildred Leet, 88, Who Helped Empower the Poor, Dies
abstract: Mrs. Leet and her husband, Glen, started Trickle Up, one of the first nonprofits to provide microgrants to help poor people start their own businesses.

name: Gunter Sachs
headline: Gunter Sachs, Ex-Husband of Brigitte Bardot, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Sachs, the heir to a German industrial fortune, was known in his youth as a playboy; he later became a well-known art collector.

name: Willard S. Boyle
headline: Willard S. Boyle, Father of Digital Eye, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Boyle shared the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2009 for developing a device at the heart of virtually every camcorder, digital camera and telescope in use.

name: Kate Swift
headline: Kate Swift, Writer Who Rooted Out Sexism in Language, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Swift and her partner discovered an implicit bias against women in everyday English when they edited a sexual education manual for junior high school students.

name: Robert Stempel
headline: Robert Stempel, an Engineer Who Led G.M., Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Stempel, who succeeded Roger Smith as chief executive in August 1990, was a mechanical engineer who helped develop the catalytic converter.

name: Horace Freeland Judson
headline: Horace Freeland Judson, Science Historian, Dies at 80
abstract: A writer whose 1979 book “The Eighth Day of Creation” is regarded as the definitive account of the breakthroughs that transformed molecular biology.

name: Robert Traylor
profession: Center Known for Filling the Lane
headline: Robert Traylor, a Center Known for Filling the Lane, Dies at 34
abstract: Mr. Traylor, 34, who played seven seasons in the N.B.A. and whose wide frame earned him the nickname Tractor, was found dead in his apartment in Puerto Rico.

name: Burt Reinhardt
headline: Burt Reinhardt, Ex-CNN President, Is Dead at 91
abstract: During Mr. Reinhardt’s tenure at the network, he oversaw the opening of overseas news bureaus and the creation of shows like “Crossfire” and “Larry King Live.”

name: Bill Gallo
headline: Bill Gallo, Sports Cartoonist, Dies at 88
abstract: In the pages of The Daily News for more than 50 years, Mr. Gallo could be sharp and sentimental, and was a master of caricature.

name: Dolores Fuller
headline: Dolores Fuller, Actress and Ed Wood’s Muse, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Fuller answered a casting call in the 1950s in an angora sweater that would become memorable to the moviegoing public.

name: Robert Ellsworth
headline: Robert Ellsworth, Lawmaker and Nixon Aide, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Ellsworth, An independent-minded former Republican congressman from Kansas, helped run the 1968 presidential campaign of Richard M. Nixon.

name: Robert H. Ellsworth
headline: Robert H. Ellsworth Is Dead at 85 After a Life Devoted to Chinese Art
abstract: Mr. Ellsworth, a prominent dealer, helped shape the holdings of prominent collectors and museums.

name: Leo Kahn
headline: Leo Kahn, Trailblazer in Big-Box Retailing, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Kahn found success with supermarkets, and then helped create Staples, the office supply retailer.

name: Darnay Hoffman
headline: Darnay Hoffman Dies at 63; Lawyer With Notorious Clients
abstract: Mr. Hoffman’s life seemed to be lifted straight from the tabloids. Divorced from the woman known as the Mayflower Madam, he was a lawyer for the man known as the Subway Vigilante.

name: Ron Springs
headline: Ron Springs, 54, Fullback for Cowboys
abstract: Mr. Springs was drafted into the N.F.L. in 1979 and proved invaluable as a blocker for the Dallas tailback Tony Dorsett.

name: Bernard Greenhouse
headline: Bernard Greenhouse, Acclaimed Cellist, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Greenhouse was a founder of the Beaux Arts Trio and a member for 32 years.

name: Jeff Gralnick
profession: Power in News at 3 TV Networks
headline: Jeff Gralnick, Power in News at 3 TV Networks, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Gralnick was an executive producer for the evening news shows at CBS and ABC and helped revamp NBC’s “Nightly News” in the mid-1990s.

name: Reach Sambath
headline: Reach Sambath, Tribunal Spokesman in Cambodia, Dies at 47
abstract: A Cambodian who survived the 1970s killing fields rose through journalism and teaching to assist a tribunal trying the leaders of the Khmer Rouge.

name: Lawrence Johnson
headline: Lawrence Johnson, Who Helped Ease Boats Into Water, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Johnson, the founder of a boat trailer company, created a trailer that allowed a single person to unload a boat into shallow water.

name: Charles McPhee
profession: Host of Dream Doctor on Radio
headline: Charles McPhee, Host of ‘Dream Doctor’ on Radio, Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. McPhee, who ended his nationally syndicated talk radio show in 2006 after learning he had Lou Gehrig’s disease, made a career out of analyzing dreams.

name: Cornell Dupree
profession: Guitarist and Sideman to the Stars
headline: Cornell Dupree, Guitarist and Sideman to the Stars, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Dupree played on about 2,500 session dates, by his estimate, for the likes of Aretha Franklin, Paul Simon and Ringo Starr.

name: Doric Wilson
profession: Playwright and Mainstay of Gay Theater
headline: Doric Wilson, Playwright and Mainstay of Gay Theater, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Wilson, a pivotal player in the Off Off Broadway movement, got his start at Caffe Cino in Greenwich Village.

name: Murray Handwerker
headline: Murray Handwerker, 89, Dies; Made Nathan’s More Famous
abstract: Mr. Handwerker transformed his father’s Coney Island hot dog business into a celebrated national fast-food chain and took it public in 1968.

name: Wallace McCain
headline: Wallace McCain Dies at 81; Fed the World Frozen Fries
abstract: Mr. McCain helped create the world’s largest maker of frozen French fries, with 50 plants in 15 countries.

name: Sammy Wanjiru
headline: Sammy Wanjiru, Marathon Champion, Is Dead at 24
abstract: Wanjiru shattered the 24-year-old Olympic record in the marathon in 2008, becoming the youngest winner of the event, and also won marathons in London and Chicago.

name: Bob Flanigan
headline: Bob Flanigan, Four Freshmen Founder, Dies at 84
abstract: Bob Flanigan had sung, managed and advised the singing group since its founding in 1948.

name: Pam Gems
headline: Pam Gems, British Playwright, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Gems explored the temperament of impassioned, embattled artists and politically engaged women in works like “Piaf” and “Stanley.”

name: Harmon Killebrew
profession: Hall of Fame Slugger for the Minnesota Twins
headline: Harmon Killebrew, Hall of Fame Slugger for the Minnesota Twins, Dies at 74
abstract: Killebrew hit 573 home runs, 11th best on the career list, in 22 major league seasons. He played in 13 All-Star Games.

name: Joseph Wershba
headline: Joseph Wershba, a Journalist Who Helped Take On McCarthy, Dies at 90
abstract: Working with Edward R. Murrow, Mr. Wershba interviewed Lt. Milo Radulovich, whose dismissal from the Air Force became a symbol of the anti-Communism of the 1950s.

name: Maurice Goldhaber
headline: Maurice Goldhaber, Atomic Physicist, Is Dead at 100
abstract: Mr. Goldhaber delved into the intricacies of atoms and headed the Brookhaven National Laboratory on Long Island for more than a decade.

name: Bruce Ricker
headline: Bruce Ricker, Who Made Jazz Documentaries, Is Dead at 68
abstract: Mr. Ricker made jazz resoundingly visible in a series of highly regarded documentaries, including “The Last of the Blue Devils.”

name: Bill Skiles
profession: Frantic Clown to a Straight Man
headline: Bill Skiles, Frantic Clown to a Straight Man, Dies at 79
abstract: For more than 50 years, Mr. Skiles was the frenzied, jabbering clown to the straight man Pete Henderson.

name: Snooky Young
headline: Snooky Young, a Big Band Trumpeter, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Young played in some of the world’s most famous big bands, including Doc Severinsen’s “Tonight Show” orchestra.

name: Garret FitzGerald
headline: Garret FitzGerald, Ex-Irish Premier, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. FitzGerald served twice as Irish prime minister in the 1980s and laid the groundwork for peace in Northern Ireland.

name: Don Barden
headline: Don Barden, a Leading Black Businessman, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Barden’s business empire started with a single record store and grew into cable television and casinos.

name: Barbara Stuart
headline: Barbara Stuart, TV Actress, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Ms. Stuart compiled a long list of credits that included shows both renowned and long forgotten.

name: Jack Wolf
headline: Jack Wolf, Who Did the Math Behind Computers, Dies at 76
abstract: As an engineer, Dr. Wolf worked in electronic communications and data storage and helped build the technologies that power modern society.

name: Randy Savage
headline: Randy Savage, Pro Wrestling’s Macho Man, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Savage, with his trademark sunglasses, bandannas and raspy voice, was one of the most recognizable professional wrestlers of the 1980s and ’90s as the character Macho Man.

name: Bill Summers
headline: Bill Summers, Car Builder Who Set a Speed Record, Dies at 75
abstract: The Summers brothers built a spear-like vehicle that in 1965 set the world speed record for wheel-driven cars, a record that stood for 26 years.

name: Randall L. Wreghitt
headline: Randall L. Wreghitt, Producer, Dies at 55
abstract: Mr. Wreghitt helped produce plays including “Grey Gardens” and “The Lieutenant of Inishmore.”

name: Onslow
profession: Peer by Birth and Contrarian by Nature
headline: Lord Onslow, a Peer by Birth and Contrarian by Nature, Dies at 73
abstract: Michael William Coplestone Dillon Onslow, who held other titles, including viscount, baron and baronet, died in England on May 14.

name: Leonard Kastle
headline: Leonard Kastle, Composer and Filmmaker, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Kastle gained praise for the one film he directed, “The Honeymoon Killers.”

name: Nathaniel Davis
headline: Nathaniel Davis, Diplomat, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Davis was a seasoned envoy whose responsibilities ranged from coup-era Chile to warring Angola.

name: Donald Krim
headline: Donald Krim, Film Distributor, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Krim brought a wide range of movies, foreign and domestic, contemporary and classic, to American audiences in theaters and on home video.

name: Peter Frelinghuysen Jr.
headline: Peter Frelinghuysen Jr., 95, Former Congressman, Dies
abstract: Mr. Frelinghuysen served more than two decades in the House of Representatives and was a member of a New Jersey family that has produced four United States Senators

name: Joseph Brooks
headline: Joseph Brooks, a Maker of Jingles, Songs and Films, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Brooks carved out a glittering career as author of famous jingles and as the composer of a huge hit, “You Light Up My Life,” before tumbling into scandal with sexual assault charges in 2009.

name: Joseph Brooks
headline: Joseph Brooks, Who Refined Lord & Taylor, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Brooks became chief executive in 1975 during a recession, and was convinced that expansion was the cure for lagging sales.

name: Edward H. Harte
headline: Edward H. Harte, Texas Newspaper Executive, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Harte, the vice chairman of Harte-Hanks Newspapers and publisher of The Corpus Christi Caller-Times, was also a conservationist.

name: Joe Steffy
profession: Blocker for Stars at West Point
headline: Joe Steffy, Blocker for Stars at West Point, Dies at 85
abstract: Steffy was a star guard for Army’s undefeated national football champions in the mid-1940s.

name: Stephen De Staebler
headline: Stephen De Staebler, Sculptor of Bronze and Clay, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. De Staebler’s fractured, dislocated human figures gave a modern voice and a sense of mystery to traditional realist forms.

name: Dick Wimmer
headline: Dick Wimmer, Whose Persistence Got Him Published, Dies at 74
abstract: After 25 years of submissions and more than 150 rejections, Mr. Wimmer finally got his book “Irish Wine” published — to very positive reviews.

name: Paul Splittorff
headline: Paul Splittorff, Royals’ Biggest Winner, Dies at 64
abstract: Splittorff was a Royals lifer who not only spent his entire 15-year pitching career in Kansas City but who also became a color commentator and play-by-play announcer for the club.

name: Mark Haines
headline: Mark Haines, CNBC Host and Interviewer, Dies at 65
abstract: The host of “Squawk on the Street” and “Squawk Box,” among other financial news programs, was known as a sharp-tongued, contentious interviewer.

name: John Delaney
headline: John Delaney, Founder of Intrade, Dies at 42
abstract: Mr. Delaney was an Irish businessman who founded Intrade, an online exchange that allows customers to bet on world political, entertainment and financial events.

name: Leonora Carrington
profession: Artist and Author of Surrealist Work
headline: Leonora Carrington Is Dead at 94; Artist and Author of Surrealist Work
abstract: Ms. Carrington was a British-born Surrealist and onetime romantic partner of Max Ernst whose paintings depicted women and half-human beasts floating in a dreamscape of images.

name: Arthur Goldreich
profession: Leader of the Armed Fight to End Apartheid
headline: Arthur Goldreich, a Leader of the Armed Fight to End Apartheid, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Goldreich wrote a detailed plan for the overthrow of the South African state and once posed as the operator of a farm where Nelson Mandela, masquerading as his houseboy, plotted revolt.

name: Jeff Conaway
headline: Jeff Conaway, Actor In ‘Taxi,’ Is Dead at 60
abstract: Mr. Conaway, who earned praise as Kenickie, John Travolta’s bad-boy sidekick in the film version of “Grease,” was known to have an addiction to alcohol and drugs.

name: Margo Dydek
headline: Margo Dydek, Towering Women’s Basketball Center, Dies at 37
abstract: The 7-foot-2 former star, who led the league in blocks nine times, was the No. 1 draft pick in 1998 and the tallest player in the W.N.B.A.

name: Tom West
headline: Tom West Dies at 71; Was the Computer Engineer Incarnate
abstract: Mr. West was the leader of the engineering team portrayed in Tracy Kidder’s book, “The Soul of a New Machine.”

name: Steve Rutt
headline: Steve Rutt, an Inventor Behind Early Video Animation, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Rutt’s video animation system helped propel the video-art revolution of the 1970s.

name: Gil Scott-Heron
headline: Gil Scott-Heron, Voice of Black Protest Culture, Dies at 62
abstract: Though often called the “godfather of rap,” Mr. Scott-Heron preferred to call himself a “bluesologist,” drawing on blues, jazz and Harlem Renaissance poetics.

name: Dana Brand
profession: Blogged of Mets Fans Delight and Despair
headline: Dana Brand, Who Blogged of Mets Fans’ Delight and Despair, Dies at 56
abstract: Brand, a scholar of American literature who was chairman of the English department at Hofstra University, wrote of fans’ “delight and despair.”

name: Nicholas V. Riasanovsky
headline: Nicholas V. Riasanovsky Dies at 87; Set Standard for Russian History
abstract: Mr. Riasanovsky, a Russian émigré who came to the United States at 14, became one of the country’s leading scholars of Russian history.

name: Paul J. Wiedorfer
profession: Hero of the Battle of the Bulge
headline: Paul J. Wiedorfer, Hero of the Battle of the Bulge, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Wiedorfer, of Baltimore, took out two German machine-gun nests during the Battle of the Bulge in World War II.

name: Sergei Bagapsh
headline: Sergei Bagapsh, Abkhazia’s Leader, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Bagapsh was a skillful politician who steered Abkhazia through its break with the republic of Georgia while also maintaining its independence from neighboring Russia.

name: Abdias do Nascimento
headline: Abdias do Nascimento, Rights Voice, Dies at 97
abstract: The Brazilian writer, painter, politician and scholar who was an outspoken civil rights leader on behalf of black Brazilians has died in Rio de Janeiro.

name: Bill Clements
headline: Bill Clements Dies at 94; Set Texas on G.O.P. Path
abstract: Mr. Clements founded an international drilling company before going into politics and breaking the Democrats’ stranglehold on the Texas governor’s office in 1978.

name: Andy Robustelli
profession: Giants Hall of Fame Defensive End
headline: Andy Robustelli, Giants’ Hall of Fame Defensive End, Dies at 85
abstract: Robustelli was an All-Pro six times and the N.F.L.’s most outstanding player in 1962, helping the Giants’ defense evoke a celebrity aura.

name: Albert M. Sack
headline: Albert M. Sack, Antiques Dealer and Author, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Sack’s guidebook to early American furniture became the bible for a generation of weekend antiquers and professional collectors.

name: Rosalyn S. Yalow
headline: Rosalyn S. Yalow, Nobel Medical Physicist, Dies at 89
abstract: In 1972, Dr. Yalow, who is from the Bronx, was only the second woman to win the Nobel Prize in Medicine.

name: Philip Rose
headline: Philip Rose, ‘Raisin’ and ‘Purlie’ Producer, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Rose, the producer of shows like “A Raisin in the Sun” and “Purlie Victorious,” advanced the cause of black playwrights and actors and helped widen the scope of American theater.

name: Jonas Bevacqua
headline: Jonas Bevacqua, Co-Founder of LRG Clothing, Dies at 33
abstract: Mr. Bevacqua helped start the eclectic clothing maker LRG, which targeted people eager to push their appearance beyond conventional hip-hop and skateboarding wear.

name: Giorgio Tozzi
headline: Giorgio Tozzi, Esteemed Bass at the Met, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Tozzi spent two decades with the Metropolitan Opera and also appeared on film, television and Broadway.

name: Pauline Betz Addie
headline: Pauline Betz Addie, a Dominant Tennis Champion, Dies at 91
abstract: Betz Addie won five Grand Slam singles titles before she was barred from the sport because she considered turning professional.

name: Hans Keilson
profession: Novelist of Life in Nazi-Run Europe
headline: Hans Keilson, Novelist of Life in Nazi-Run Europe, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Keilson, a German-born psychoanalyst, won literary fame at the end of his long life when his long-forgotten stories, set in Nazi-occupied Europe, were republished to great acclaim.

name: Adolfas Mekas
headline: Adolfas Mekas, Avant-Garde Filmmaker and Teacher, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Mekas was a Lithuanian immigrant who became an influential avant-garde filmmaker and teacher and who, with his brother Jonas, founded Film Culture, the seminal journal for cinéastes.

name: Clarice Taylor
headline: Clarice Taylor Dies at 93; TV’s Cosby Called her Mom
abstract: Ms. Taylor was an actress who was best known as the endearing grandmother on “The Cosby Show” and who also won an Obie Award for her portrayal of Moms Mabley.

name: Jack Kevorkian
headline: Dr. Jack Kevorkian Dies at 83; A Doctor Who Helped End Lives
abstract: A medical pathologist, Dr. Kevorkian challenged social taboos about disease and dying and helped dozens of terminally ill patients end their lives.

name: James Arness
headline: James Arness, Marshal on ‘Gunsmoke,’ Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Arness burnished the legend of America’s epic West as the laconic peacemaker of Dodge City on one of the longest-running dramatic series in television history.

name: Elmer G. Pratt
headline: Elmer G. Pratt, Jailed Panther Leader, Dies at 63
abstract: A symbol for many of the victimization of black radicals, Mr. Pratt was exonerated only after serving 27 years in prison.

name: Ray Bryant
headline: Ray Bryant, Jazz Pianist, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Bryant was a jazz pianist whose sensitivity and easy authority made him a busy accompanist and a successful solo artist.

name: Johanna Fiedler
headline: Johanna Fiedler Dies at 65; Wrote of the Met Opera
abstract: Ms. Fiedler wrote tell-all books about the Metropolitan Opera and about her father, Arthur Fiedler.

name: Lawrence Eagleburger
headline: Lawrence Eagleburger, a Top Diplomat, Dies at 80
abstract: Lawrence S. Eagleburger was a foreign policy adviser and troubleshooting diplomat who served for over 40 years.

name: Sammy Ofer
headline: Sammy Ofer, Magnate and Israeli Power Broker, Dies at 89
abstract: An Israeli international shipping magnate, Mr. Ofer’s journey from rags to riches is tainted with scandal and intrigue.

name: Edwin Honig
headline: Edwin Honig, a Poet, Professor and Translator, Dies at 91
abstract: The critic and teacher elegantly translated seminal works of Spanish and Portuguese literature.

name: Leo Rangell
headline: Leo Rangell, a Stalwart of Freudian Talk Therapy, Dies at 97
abstract: Dr. Rangell was a relentless advocate for the slow approach to treating emotional distress even as antidepressants and managed care made short-term treatment the norm.

name: Albertina Sisulu
headline: Albertina Sisulu, Who Helped Lead Apartheid Fight, Dies at 92
abstract: Mrs. Sisulu was considered by many to be the mother of South Africa’s liberation struggle.

name: John Henry Johnson
headline: John Henry Johnson Dies at 81; Inspired Fear on the Field
abstract: Johnson was a brawny but agile runner who had a Hall of Fame career that spanned 13 professional football seasons.

name: Irwin D. Mandel
headline: Dr. Irwin D. Mandel, Expert on Dental Chemistry, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Mandel, a founder of the preventive dentistry movement, did research on the biochemistry of saliva that was important to many medical fields.

name: Josephine Hart
headline: Josephine Hart, Author of Best-Selling ‘Damage,’ Dies
abstract: “Damage,” Ms. Hart’s first novel, told the story of a powerful, married member of Parliament who embarks on an ultimately disastrous affair with his son’s fiancée.

name: Wally Boag
headline: Wally Boag, Cowboy Comedian at Disneyland, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Boag, as Pecos Bill, with Betty Taylor (who died a day after he did), pushed the Golden Horseshoe Revue into the Guinness record book as the most-performed stage production in history.

name: Harry Bernstein
headline: Harry Bernstein, Writer Who Gained Fame at 96, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Bernstein published a highly praised memoir of his poverty-stricken childhood in England at the age of 96.

name: Andrew Gold
headline: Andrew Gold, Singer and Songwriter, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Gold’s work with Linda Ronstadt as a very young man put him in the heart of the 1970s Los Angeles music scene.

name: Lilian Jackson Braun
headline: Lilian Jackson Braun, ‘Cat Who’ Writer, Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Braun wrote 29 mysteries starring her feline sleuth.

name: Genaro Hernandez
headline: Genaro Hernandez, Twice a World Champion, Dies at 45
abstract: Mr. Hernandez, a boxer known as Chicanito, the Little Mexican, was twice the world super featherweight champion.

name: Keith Irvine
headline: Keith Irvine, Interior Designer, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Irvine brought a sense of wit and unpredictability to the English country-house style that won the allegiance of clients like Jacqueline Onassis, Cary Grant and Diana Ross.

name: Maqbool Fida Husain
headline: Maqbool Fida Husain, India’s Most Famous Painter, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Husain’s modernist take on mythic and religious subjects made him a target of right-wing Hindu groups.

name: Leonard B. Stern
headline: Leonard B. Stern, Creator of Mad Libs, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Stern, an Emmy-winning television writer, created Mad Libs as he tried to find the right word for a script.

name: Edgar Tekere
profession: Leader in Fight for Zimbabwe Independence
headline: Edgar Tekere, Leader in Fight for Zimbabwe Independence, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Tekere was imprisoned with Robert Mugabe during the struggle to end white rule in Rhodesia, but broke with him after Mr. Mugabe became president.

name: John H. Sinfelt
headline: John H. Sinfelt, Who Helped Introduce Unleaded Gas, Dies at 80
abstract: Dr. Sinfelt devised a way to replace the lead and maintain octane levels when oil companies were pressured to remove lead from gasoline by the E.P.A.

name: John R. Alison
profession: Ace Fighter Pilot in World War II
headline: John R. Alison, Ace Fighter Pilot in World War II, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Alison helped organize an American air campaign that enabled British forces to bog down the Japanese in the jungles of Burma.

name: Jorge Semprún
profession: Blurred Line Between Novel and Memoir
headline: Jorge Semprún, Who Blurred Line Between Novel and Memoir, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Semprún was a member of the French Resistance, a Communist organizer, a novelist and a screenwriter.

name: Brian Lenihan
headline: Brian Lenihan, Ireland’s Finance Minister, Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. Lenihan led efforts to avoid bankruptcy during the economic collapse and negotiated a $93 billion bailout deal with the European Union.

name: Patrick Leigh Fermor
headline: Patrick Leigh Fermor, Travel Writer, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Fermor crossed Europe on a three-year journey, then wrote about his adventures.

name: Norman Redlich
headline: Norman Redlich, Ex-Dean of N.Y.U. Law School, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Redlich, a quiet luminary of the New York legal community, pioneered the pro bono defense of indigent death row inmates.

name: Gus Tyler
headline: Gus Tyler, Firebrand of Labor Movement, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Tyler’s most powerful weapons were words, in books, newspaper columns, radio commentaries and speeches he wrote for labor chieftains.

name: Clara Luper
headline: Clara Luper, a Leader of Civil Rights Sit-Ins, Dies at 88
abstract: A history teacher, Ms. Luper led one of the first sit-ins of the civil rights movement at a drugstore in Oklahoma City in 1958.

name: Zev Birger
headline: Zev Birger, Jerusalem Book Fair Leader, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Birger was a Holocaust survivor and former official of the young state of Israel who turned the book fair into a thriving literary event.

name: Claudio Bravo
headline: Claudio Bravo, Chilean Artist, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Bravo, who was born in Chile and lived in Morocco, was an established society portrait painter before he began depicting commonplace objects in the context of art history.

name: Leo Greenland
headline: Leo Greenland, Unconventional Adman Who Valued Truth-Telling, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Greenland, whose agency created head-turning campaigns for Johnnie Walker and Penthouse, was an advocate for truth in advertising.

name: Maynard L. Hill
headline: Maynard L. Hill, Small-Scale Lindbergh, Dies at 85
abstract: In August 2003, Mr. Hill was the first to create and guide a model airplane across the Atlantic.

name: Martin Rushent
headline: Martin Rushent, Versatile Record Producer, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Rushent became closely identified with the less frenzied, more melodic variation of punk known as new wave.

name: Laura Ziskin
profession: Producer of Spider-Man and Pretty Woman
headline: Laura Ziskin, Producer of ‘Spider-Man’ and ‘Pretty Woman,’ Dies at 61
abstract: As executive producer of “Pretty Woman” (1990), Ms. Ziskin insisted on an ending in which Julia Roberts has changed Richard Gere as fully as he has changed her.

name: Carl Gardner
headline: Carl Gardner, Singer With Coasters Pop Group, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Gardner’s tenor voice was heard on hits like “Yakety Yak” and “Searchin.’ ”

name: Gunnar Fischer
headline: Gunnar Fischer, Cinematographer for Bergman, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Fischer added expressionistic depth to Bergman classics like “The Seventh Seal” and “Wild Strawberries.”

name: David C. Baldus
headline: David C. Baldus, 75, Dies; Studied Race and the Law
abstract: Professor Baldus nearly convinced the Supreme Court that the race of the victim affected death sentences.

name: James J. Rahal
headline: Dr. James J. Rahal, 77, Virus Expert, Dies
abstract: Dr. Rahal was an infectious-disease specialist who was at the epicenter of a West Nile outbreak.

name: Kathryn T. Windham
headline: Kathryn T. Windham, a Storyteller of the South, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Windham was a chronicler of Southern life, from hoop snakes to ghosts, in books, recipes and commentaries on public radio.

name: Alan Haberman
headline: Alan Haberman, Who Ushered In the Bar Code, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Haberman cajoled a nation into into accepting a strange new symbol that first changed retailing and then spread to every corner of human endeavor.

name: Marion Fuller Brown
headline: Marion Fuller Brown, 94, Friend of Nature, Dies
abstract: Mrs. Fuller Brown was a state representative in Maine who sponsored legislation that banned billboards throughout the state.

name: Bob Banner
headline: Bob Banner Dies at 89; Producer in TV’s Infancy
abstract: Mr. Banner, a producer during television’s early years, encouraged Carol Burnett to open her show by answering questions and Dinah Shore to end hers by blowing a kiss.

name: Bill Haast
headline: Bill Haast, a Man Charmed by Snakes, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Haast relied on daily injections of snake venom to protect him from the 173 bites he sustained while handling some three million snakes.

name: Wild Man Fischer
headline: Wild Man Fischer, Outsider Musician, Dies at 66
abstract: Whether Wild Man Fischer was a naïve genius or simply a madman who ranted to music may never be determined, but he attracted — and retains — a cult following.

name: Jim Rodnunsky
headline: Jim Rodnunsky, Cablecam Creator, Dies at 54
abstract: While seeking images for a skiing simulator, he developed a camera system that provide overhead and rapid-moving shots for films and TV sporting events.

name: Zeke Sinicola
headline: Zeke Sinicola, 82, Basketball All-American, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Sinicola was a New York City schoolyard legend who starred at Niagara University but had only a brief professional career.

name: Joseph Miller
profession: Sold Horse Tack to the Well-Heeled
headline: Joseph Miller, Who Sold Horse Tack to the Well-Heeled, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Miller built his father’s humble harness shop in Manhattan into one of the nation’s largest suppliers of fashionable saddlery, riding apparel and other equestrian equipment.

name: Mietek Pemper
headline: Mietek Pemper, 91, Camp Inmate Who Compiled Schindler’s List
abstract: Mr. Pemper served as a secretary for a labor camp commander and risked his life to plot the rescue of enslaved workers.

name: Clarence Clemons
headline: Clarence Clemons, Springsteen’s Soulful Sideman, Dies at 69
abstract: The saxophonist in Bruce Springsteen’s band had a jovial onstage manner and soul-rooted style that made him one of rock’s most beloved sidemen.

name: Elena Bonner
headline: Elena Bonner, Widow of Sakharov, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Bonner was a fierce protector of her dissident husband and a force in her own right on behalf of human rights.

name: James P. Hosty
headline: James P. Hosty, Investigated Oswald, Dies at 86
abstract: The month before the Kennedy assassination in Dallas, Mr. Hosty got an assignment: a suspected communist agitator and possible spy named Lee Harvey Oswald.

name: Frederick Chiluba
headline: Frederick Chiluba, Infamous Zambia Leader, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Chiluba was a former president of Zambia whose administration did little to address Zambia’s poverty, and he was accused of stealing millions to support shopping sprees.

name: A. Whitney Ellsworth
profession: First Publisher of New York Review
headline: A. Whitney Ellsworth, First Publisher of New York Review, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Ellsworth helped get The New York Review of Books up and running as its first publisher and also served in the mid-1970s as chairman of Amnesty International USA.

name: Ryan Dunn
headline: Ryan Dunn, Daredevil Comedian, Dies at 34
abstract: Mr. Dunn, whose stunts and gags on the “Jackass” television show and movies often ran afoul of good taste, was killed in a car crash.

name: Brian Haw
profession: Camped in Front of Parliament to Protest War
headline: Brian Haw, 62, Dies; Camped in Front of Parliament to Protest War
abstract: Mr. Haw made his home outside Parliament for nearly a decade to protest England’s involvement in war.

name: Thomas N. Armstrong III
headline: Thomas N. Armstrong III, Museum Chief Who Once Led the Whitney, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Armstrong expanded the Whitney Museum’s collection and acquired works that are now cornerstones of its collection.

name: E. M. Broner
headline: E. M. Broner, Jewish Feminist, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Broner explored the double marginalization of being Jewish and female, producing a body of work that placed her in the vanguard of Jewish feminist letters.

name: David Rayfiel
headline: David Rayfiel, Screenwriter With Sydney Pollack, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Rayfiel collaborated with Mr. Pollack and Robert Redford on many of their most successful films, including “Three Days of the Condor” and “Out of Africa.”

name: George M. White
headline: George M. White, Architect of Capitol, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. White oversaw federal projects on Capitol Hill, including the construction of the Hart Senate Office Building and the restoration of the old Supreme Court and Senate chambers.

name: George C. White
profession: Founder of Eugene ONeill Theater Center
headline: George C. White, Founder of Eugene O’Neill Theater Center, Dies at 89
abstract: His summer conferences gave budding playwrights a chance to try out new works, many of which went on to success in New York.

name: Eric Swenson
headline: Eric Swenson, Co-Founder of Skateboarding Magazine, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Swenson’s Thrasher magazine helped propel skateboarding to an international form of recreation.

name: F. Gilman Spencer
headline: F. Gilman Spencer, Ex-Editor of Daily News, Dies at 85
abstract: A champion of writing talent and a Pulitzer Prize winner himself for editorial writing, F. Gilman Spencer also led newspapers in Philadelphia, Denver and Trenton.

name: Peter Falk
profession: Rumpled and Crafty Actor in Televisions Columbo
headline: Peter Falk, Rumpled and Crafty Actor in Television’s ‘Columbo,’ Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Falk, known for his signature role on television, had a wide-ranging career in comedy and drama in film and onstage.

name: Gene Colan
headline: Gene Colan, Prolific Comic-Book Artist, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Colan drew for a wide range of comic books across seven decades and was known for his painterly qualities.

name: Don Diamond
headline: Don Diamond, Character Actor, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Diamond, who specialized in supporting roles in westerns, worked in television, radio and film for nearly 40 years.

name: Randall Adams
headline: Randall Adams, 61, Dies; Freed With Help of Film
abstract: “The Thin Blue Line” told the story of how Mr. Adams was wrongly convicted of murder and put on death row.

name: Mike Waterson
headline: Mike Waterson, Member of British Folk Troupe, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Waterson, a bass, harmonized with the Watersons, long considered the royal family of British folk music.

name: Sidney Radner
headline: Sidney Radner, Guardian of Houdini Legacy, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Radner did his own magic as well as helping to preserve many of the props used by Harry Houdini.

name: Alice Playten
headline: Alice Playten, an Actress of Small Frame, Big Voice, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Playten played Baby Louise in the original “Gypsy” and was nominated for a Tony for “Henry, Sweet Henry.”

name: Byron Burford
headline: Byron Burford, Artist of Circus Life, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Burford, an American figurative artist, was perhaps best known for depicting circus life in his art, such as whip-cracking lion tamers and sideshow attractions like the tattooed man.

name: Mark Gerard
profession: Veterinarian at Center of a Horse Race Fraud
headline: Mark Gerard, Veterinarian at Center of a Horse Race Fraud, Dies at 76
abstract: Dr. Gerard cared for champions like Kelso and Secretariat but imported a horse that ran as a ringer who won at odds of 57 to 1.

name: Norma Lyon
headline: Norma Lyon, the ‘Butter-Cow Lady,’ Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Lyon won fame for sculpturing tons of U.S. Grade AA salted butter each year into life-size figures of cows, famous people and, once, a diorama of the Last Supper.

name: Margaret Tyzack
headline: Margaret Tyzack, Award-Winning Actress, Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. Tyzack was the winner of a Tony Award for “Lettice and Lovage” and two London Olivier Awards.

name: Elaine Stewart
headline: Elaine Stewart, Sultry 1950s Actress, Dies at 81
abstract: Promoted as a dark-haired Marilyn Monroe, Ms. Stewart appeared in films like “Brigadoon,” “The Bad and the Beautiful” and “The Adventures of Hajji Baba.”

name: Jan van Beveren
headline: Jan van Beveren, Star Dutch Goalkeeper, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Van Beveren was a longtime standout in the Netherlands who became a youth soccer official in Beaumont, Tex.

name: Lorenzo Charles
profession: Made Winning Dunk in 1983 N.C.A.A. Title Game
headline: Lorenzo Charles Dies at 47; Made Winning Dunk in 1983 N.C.A.A. Title Game
abstract: Charles last-second dunk in the 1983 N.C.A.A. national championship gave North Carolina State its second national title.

name: Eugene H. Kummel
profession: Led Major Ad Agency in Expansion
headline: Eugene H. Kummel, Who Led Major Ad Agency in Expansion, Dies at 88
abstract: Under Mr. Kummel’s leadership, McCann Erickson’s billings rose from about $170 million a year in 1973 to $1.8 billion by his retirement in 1987.

name: Larry Bogdanow
headline: Larry Bogdanow, 64, Dies; Crafted Cozy Restaurants
abstract: Mr. Bogdanow was best known for his design work on dozens of elegant, casual restaurant interiors, including Union Square Cafe, Savoy and the Cub Room.

name: Robert Morris
headline: Robert Morris, Pioneer in Computer Security, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Morris, once chief scientist of the National Security Agency’s computer security center, helped plan electronic attacks on Saddam Hussein’s government.

name: Robert Morris
profession: Founding Minimalist Sculptor With Manifold Passions
headline: Robert Morris, 87, Dies; Founding Minimalist Sculptor With Manifold Passions
abstract: He pioneered a style of radical simplification and wrote influential essays about it. But he also restlessly went beyond it, taking in performance, earthworks and more.

name: C.W. Whalen Jr.
headline: C.W. Whalen Jr., 90, Dies; Led Vietnam War Dissent
abstract: Mr. Whalen was a six-term Republican congressman from Ohio who espoused a variety of liberal causes.

name: George Ballas
headline: George Ballas, Inventor of the Weed Whacker, Dies at 85
abstract: Inspired by swirling soap brushes at a car wash, the owner of a Houston dance studio took tin can, fishing line and a rotary lawn edger in hand, and the Weed Eater was born.

name: Richard H. Poff
headline: Richard H. Poff, Who Withdrew Court Bid, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Poff surprised official Washington by withdrawing from consideration for a Supreme Court appointment by President Richard M. Nixon.

name: Billy Costello
headline: Billy Costello, Who Won Light Welterweight Crown, Dies at 55
abstract: Mr. Costello overcame a troubled youth and became a boxing star despite not putting on gloves until he was 19.

name: Robert H. Widmer
headline: Robert H. Widmer, Designer of Military Aircraft, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Widmer led the development of major aircraft as well as the Tomahawk cruise missile, helping to enforce the cold war strategic balance known as mutual assured destruction.

name: Edith Fellows
profession: 1930s Child Star Trailed by Dickensian Woes
headline: Edith Fellows, a 1930s Child Star Trailed by Dickensian Woes, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Fellows worked with some of the biggest stars in Hollywood, including Bing Crosby, W. C. Fields and Gene Autry.

name: Twins Seven-Seven
headline: Prince Twins Seven-Seven, Nigerian Artist, Dies at 67
abstract: A leading representative of the Oshogbo School, he had a consciously naïve style in which he depicted village scenes, animals and deities.

name: Eddy Nicholson
headline: Eddy Nicholson, 73, Colorful Collector, Dies
abstract: Mr. Nicholson was a wealthy businessman who became an enthusiastic buyer of early American furniture and art.

name: Otto von Hapsburg
headline: Otto von Hapsburg, a Would-Be Monarch, Dies at 98
abstract: Even in exile, Otto, the onetime heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne, remained deeply involved in the turbulent events of the last century.

name: Ruth Roberts
headline: Ruth Roberts, ‘Meet the Mets’ Songwriter, Dies at 84
abstract: With her collaborator Bill Katz, Ms. Roberts wrote the durable theme that is played at every home game of the New York Mets.

name: Cy Twombly
headline: American Artist Who Scribbled a Unique Path
abstract: Cy Twombly went contrary to all the fashions of his era, which spanned the postwar years.

name: Mika Myllyla
headline: Mika Myllyla, Olympic Skier in Doping Scandal, Dies at 41
abstract: Mr. Myllyla was a cross-country skier who became a national sports hero in Finland before leaving the sport in disgrace.

name: Jane Scott
headline: Jane Scott Is Dead at 92; Veteran Rock Music Critic
abstract: Ms. Scott, who called herself the world’s second-oldest teenager, covered rock music for The Cleveland Plain Dealer from 1964 until 2002, when she was almost 83.

name: George Lang
headline: George Lang, Mastermind Behind Café des Artistes, Dies at 86
abstract: Born in Hungary, Mr. Lang was famous for the transformation of the restaurant in the 1970s into a beloved dining spot.

name: Robert Sklar
headline: Robert Sklar, Film Scholar, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Mr. Sklar’s 1975 book “Movie-Made America: A History of American Movies” was one of the first histories to place Hollywood films in a social and political context.

name: Dick Williams
headline: Dick Williams, Hall of Fame Manager, Dies at 82
abstract: The hard-nosed Hall of Fame manager achieved the rare feat of taking three different teams to the World Series.

name: Edmund Carpenter
headline: Edmund Carpenter, Archaeologist and Anthropologist, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Carpenter did groundbreaking work in anthropological filmmaking and ethnomusicology and, with his friend Marshall McLuhan, laid the foundations of modern media studies.

name: John Mackey
headline: John Mackey Dies at 69; Helped Revolutionize N.F.L.
abstract: Mr. Mackey fought against free-agency restrictions as the president of the league’s players union, in addition to becoming one of the N.F.L.’s greatest tight ends.

name: Josef Suk
headline: Josef Suk, Czech Violinist, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Suk was a great-grandson of Dvorak and a grandson of the turn-of-the-century violinist and composer also named Josef Suk.

name: Betty Ford
headline: Betty Ford, Former First Lady, Dies at 93
abstract: The much-admired wife of President Gerald R. Ford overcame addiction and helped found one of the most well-known rehabilitation centers in the U.S.

name: Chris Cahill
headline: Chris Cahill, 54, of Skateboarding’s Z-Boys, Dies
abstract: Christopher Michael Cahill, an original member of the pioneering Z-Boys skateboarding team, transformed the sport with punk belligerence and a fluid surfing style.

name: Manuel Galbán
headline: Manuel Galbán, Guitarist With Cuban Bands, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Galbán was known for his work with the all-star ensemble Buena Vista Social Club.

name: Anne LaBastille
headline: Anne LaBastille, Advocate, Author and ‘Woodswoman’ of Adirondacks, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. LaBastille repeatedly set aside her hermitlike existence to document the fate of endangered species and to raise her voice against environmental degradation.

name: Fred Newman
headline: Fred Newman, Writer and Political Figure, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Newman, who founded a Marxist-Leninist party and fostered a sexually charged brand of psychotherapy, played an influential role in New York life and politics.

name: Jimmy Roselli
headline: Jimmy Roselli, Italian-American Singer, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Roselli, a crooner from Hoboken, N.J., who was often overshadowed by Frank Sinatra, sang standards to adoring crowds for decades.

name: Barry Bremen
headline: Barry Bremen, Professional Impostor, Dies at 64
abstract: A brazen faux celebrity was known for stunts in a less security-conscious time.

name: Roland Petit
headline: Roland Petit, Choreographer, Dies at 87; Conquered Ballet Taboos and Hollywood
abstract: Mr. Petit worked with Jean Cocteau, Danny Kaye and his own wife, the ballerina Zizi Jeanmaire, among many others. Sex and suffering were the themes of his most renowned pieces.

name: Facundo Cabral
headline: Facundo Cabral, Singer of Conscience, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Cabral was a protesting voice of conscience against social injustice and dictatorship in Latin America.

name: Sam Denoff
headline: Sam Denoff, TV Writer, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. Denoff won four Emmys, including two for “The Dick Van Dyke Show.”

name: Sherwood Schwartz
profession: Creator of Gilligan and the Bradys
headline: Sherwood Schwartz, Creator of Gilligan and the Bradys, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Schwartz created two of the most affectionately ridiculed and enduring television sitcoms of the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Kip Tiernan
profession: Founder of First Shelter for Homeless Women
headline: Kip Tiernan, Founder of First Shelter for Homeless Women, Dies at 85
abstract: In 1974, Ms. Tiernan founded Rosie’s Place in Boston, the nation’s first shelter specifically for homeless women.

name: Roberts Blossom
headline: Roberts Blossom, Quirky Character Actor, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Blossom played a great many curmudgeons but may be best recalled for his turn as the surprisingly sweet Old Man Marley in “Home Alone.”

name: Jaroslav Jirik
headline: Jaroslav Jirik, 71, Dies; 1st Eastern-Bloc Player in N.H.L.
abstract: Jirik was a Czech hockey star who played a role in his national team’s emotional victory over the Soviets in 1969.

name: Theodore Roszak
headline: Theodore Roszak, ’60s Expert, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Roszak popularized the term “counterculture” in referring to a generation that rebelled against war and sought new ways of thinking.

name: Rob Grill
profession: Lead Singer of the Grass Roots
headline: Rob Grill, Lead Singer of the Grass Roots, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Grill and the rest of the band filled the airwaves with hits that were bouncy, accessible and eminently danceable, like “Midnight Confession” and “Temptation Eyes.”

name: T. Lux Feininger
headline: T. Lux Feininger, Photographer and Painter, Dies at 101
abstract: A painter and photographer, his camera documented the artistic avant-garde in Germany between the wars.

name: George M. Ross
headline: George M. Ross, Who Helped Establish Major Jewish Museum, Dies at 77
abstract: George M. Ross, a Goldman Sachs executive and a philanthropist, raised $154 million to establish a major museum of Jewish history in Philadelphia.

name: Marketa Kimbrell
headline: Marketa Kimbrell, Who Brought Theater to the Forgotten, Is Dead at 82
abstract: For more than 25 years, the New York Street Theater Caravan, founded by Ms. Kimbrell and Richard Levy, performed in New York and beyond.

name: Leo Kirch
headline: Leo Kirch, German Media Giant, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Kirch built one of the biggest German media empires from scratch before losing it all in a bankruptcy in 2002 when a gamble on digital pay TV failed to pay off.

name: Stanley Seeger
headline: Stanley Seeger, Who Collected, but Didn’t Discuss, Art, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Seeger, a reclusive, American-born art collector, once owned Sutton Place, a grand manor house where Henry VIII in 1533 had been a guest.

name: Henry Carlisle
headline: Henry Carlisle, a Supporter of Oppressed Writers, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Carlisle wrote novels of his own, edited Camus and helped translate and publish Solzhenitsyn.

name: John C. Truesdale
headline: John C. Truesdale, Labor Relations Board Chief, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Truesdale joined the National Labor Relations Board in 1948 and rose from field investigator to executive secretary and ultimately chairman.

name: Jerry Ragovoy
headline: Jerry Ragovoy, Writer of Soulful Ballads, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Ragovoy infused his songs with a wrenching emotional quality, including “Time Is on My Side,” “Piece of My Heart,” and “Get It While You Can.”

name: Francisco Villagrán Kramer
headline: Francisco Villagrán Kramer, Guatemala Official, Dies at 84
abstract: The legal scholar and left-of-center politician dismayed some supporters by joining a harsh military government, though he later left it for exile.

name: Travis Bean
headline: Travis Bean, Aluminum Guitar Maker, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Bean, a machinist and musician, created unadorned electric guitars and basses that had an uncanny ability to sustain notes.

name: J. Terrence Lanni
headline: J. Terrence Lanni, Ex-Chief of MGM Mirage, Dies at 68
abstract: When Mr. Lanni retired, he had remade MGM Mirage into the largest casino operator in Las Vegas and the second-largest casino company in the world.

name: Geoff Fisken
profession: New Zealand Sheep Farmer and Scourge of Japanese Pilots
headline: Geoff Fisken, New Zealand Sheep Farmer and Scourge of Japanese Pilots, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Fisken was a sheep farmer turned combat pilot who led a seemingly charmed life in the Pacific theater of World War II, shooting down at least 11 Japanese planes.

name: Ardis James
headline: Ardis James, Who Established Center on Quilts, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mrs. James and her husband, Robert, established what has become the world’s largest public collection of quilts, at the University of Nebraska, Lincoln.

name: Juan Bordaberry
headline: Juan Bordaberry, Who Led Uruguay in Dark Era, Dies at 83
abstract: The former president participated in a 1973 coup that ushered in a 12-year military dictatorship marked by disappearances, torture and killings.

name: Cornell MacNeil
headline: Cornell MacNeil, Verdi Baritone at the Met, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. MacNeil, a regular star at the Metropolitan Opera, was most highly praised for his Verdi roles.

name: John S. Toll
headline: John S. Toll Dies at 87; Led Stony Brook University
abstract: Leaving Stony Brook after overseeing its transition to a major research institution, Mr. Toll oversaw a comparable expansion at the University of Maryland.

name: Magnus Malan
headline: Magnus Malan, Apartheid Defender, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Malan was a South African general and defense minister who in the 1980s helped devise and carry out his nation’s last-ditch strategy to preserve its system of rigid racial segregation.

name: John Mosca
headline: John Mosca, a Restaurant’s Patriarch, Dies at 86
abstract: A family man who blended Italian roots with Louisiana seafood, Mr. Mosca gained notoriety through his restaurant, west of New Orleans.

name: Alex Steinweiss
headline: Alex Steinweiss, Originator of Artistic Album Covers, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Steinweiss, an art director and graphic designer, adorned plain covers for 78 r.p.m. discs and designed the packaging for long-playing records.

name: Pierrette Alarie-Simoneau
headline: Pierrette Alarie-Simoneau, Canadian Soprano, Dies at 89
abstract: Mrs. Alarie-Simoneau, an internationally known Canadian soprano, made her Metropolitan Opera debut in 1945 and appeared 26 times there.

name: John C. Kenefick
headline: John C. Kenefick, Former Rail Executive, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Kenefick, a Princeton graduate, served as president and later chief executive of the Union Pacific Railroad in an era of deregulation and industry consolidation.

name: Noel Gayler
headline: Adm. Noel Gayler, Leader in the Pacific, Dies at 96
abstract: A career military man, Mr. Gayler was also an ardent advocate of nuclear disarmament.

name: Armando Orsini
headline: Armando Orsini, a New York Restaurateur, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Orsini cultivated an atmosphere of dolce vita that made his restaurant Orsini’s, on East 56th Street, a famous hangout in the 1960s.

name: Ed Flesh
headline: Ed Flesh, Who Designed the Wheel of Fortune, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Flesh, an art director, brought garish set design to game shows and created the horizontal spinner that revolves at the center of “Wheel of Fortune.”

name: Zygmunt Nagorski
headline: Zygmunt Nagorski, Founder of Leadership Center, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Mr. Nagorski, a Polish émigré, wrote widely about East-West relations during the cold war.

name: Lucian Freud
headline: Lucian Freud, Figurative Painter Who Redefined Portraiture, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Freud, a grandson of Sigmund Freud, was called “the greatest living realist painter” by one art critic in the late 1980s.

name: Joe Lee Wilson
headline: Joe Lee Wilson, a Leader of ’70s Loft-Jazz Movement, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Wilson, a baritone, gained critical praise but never attained stardom. He founded Ladies’ Fort, a small club in NoHo, a part of the loft-jazz movement.

name: Elliot Handler
headline: Elliot Handler, Co-Founder of Mattel Toys, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Handler helped introduce Barbie, helped design the talking doll Chatty Cathy and popularized Hot Wheels toy cars.

name: Bruce Sundlun
headline: Bruce Sundlun, Rhode Island Governor With Flair, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Sundlun cut a larger-than-life figure that seemed inversely proportional to the size of his state.

name: Mary M. Simpson
headline: Rev. Mary M. Simpson, a Pioneer in Episcopal Clergy, Dies at 85
abstract: Canon Simpson, the first Episcopal nun to be ordained as a priest, advocated for a greater role for women in the church.

name: Amy Winehouse
profession: British Soul Singer With a Troubled Life
headline: Amy Winehouse, British Soul Singer With a Troubled Life, Dies at 27
abstract: Ms. Winehouse, the British singer who found worldwide fame with a sassy, hip-hop-inflected take on retro soul, became a tabloid fixture because of addiction problems.

name: Nguyen Cao Ky
headline: Nguyen Cao Ky, South Vietnam Leader, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Ky, a former air force general, ruled South Vietnam with an iron fist for two years during the Vietnam War.

name: John M. Shalikashvili
headline: Gen. John M. Shalikashvili, Military Chief in 1990s, Dies at 75
abstract: General Shalikashvili was the first foreign-born soldier to become the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff.

name: Charles Manatt
headline: Charles Manatt, Former Democratic National Chairman, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Manatt was a lawyer who revitalized his party during the Reagan era.

name: James T. Molloy
headline: James T. Molloy, Last Doorkeeper of the House, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Five presidents — from Gerald R. Ford to Bill Clinton — were trumpeted into the House by Mr. Molloy to deliver State of the Union addresses in the years that he was doorkeeper.

name: Warren Leslie
headline: Warren Leslie Dies at 84; Wrote Book That Rankled Dallas
abstract: In a book that came out four months after the assassination of President John F. Kennedy, Mr. Leslie wrote that a climate of right-wing extremism had primed Dallas to become the scene of a national tragedy.

name: Butch Lewis
profession: Flashy Promoter for Boxings Spinks Brothers
headline: Butch Lewis, Flashy Promoter for Boxing’s Spinks Brothers, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Lewis was a former used-car salesman best known for getting Michael Spinks a $13.5 million payday for what became 91 seconds in the ring with Mike Tyson.

name: Michael Cacoyannis
headline: Michael Cacoyannis, Director of ‘Zorba the Greek,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Cacoyannis, most famous for “Zorba the Greek” with Anthony Quinn, also brought Greek drama to the stage and screen, including “Electra” with Irene Papas.

name: Tom Aldredge
headline: Tom Aldredge, Character Actor, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Aldredge was seen in everything from Sondheim to “The Sopranos” in his five decades of acting on the stage and screen.

name: Milton Gwirtzman
headline: Milton Gwirtzman, Adviser to Kennedys, Dies at 78
abstract: Within the Kennedy family, Mr. Gwirtzman’s strategizing, loyalty and oracular reputation made him a bit of a legend himself.

name: George Lascelles
headline: George Lascelles, Lord Harewood, Who Wrote Opera Reference, Is Dead at 88
abstract: A first cousin of Queen Elizabeth II, Mr. Lascelles was best known to American readers as the longtime editor of Kobbé’s Complete Opera Book.

name: G.D. Spradlin
headline: G.D. Spradlin, Prolific Character Actor, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Spradlin, who made a fortune in oil and then retired, took up acting later in life, and appeared in productions ranging from “Gomer Pyle, U.S.M.C.” to “Ed Wood.”

name: Dan Peek
headline: Dan Peek, of the Rock Band America, Dies at 60
abstract: Dan Peek was an original member of the rock band America, and during his tenure in the group, one of their best-known songs was “A Horse with No Name.”

name: Frank Foster
headline: Frank Foster, Jazz Saxophonist, Composer and Arranger, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Foster wrote and arranged, among other songs, “Shiny Stockings,” recorded by Count Basie on his 1955 album “April in Paris.”

name: Jeret Peterson
profession: Skier Known for a Daring Move
headline: Jeret Peterson, Skier Known for a Daring Move, Dies at 29
abstract: Peterson, who struggled with depression and alcoholism, won a silver medal in freestyle aerial skiing at the 2010 Vancouver Olympics.

name: John Stott
headline: Rev. John Stott, Major Evangelical Figure, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Stott was one of the world’s most influential figures in the spread of evangelical Christianity over the past half-century.

name: Hideki Irabu
headline: Hideki Irabu, Briefly a Yankee Sensation, Dies at 42
abstract: A former Japanese star who wanted to play for the Yankees, Irabu apparently hanged himself in a home near Los Angeles.

name: Jerome Liebling
headline: Jerome Liebling, Socially Minded Photographer, Dies at 87
abstract: With his photographs, Mr. Liebling brought about a deep awareness of the personal in the political, and influenced a generation of photographers and documentary filmmakers.

name: Archbishop Pietro Sambi
headline: Archbishop Pietro Sambi, Vatican Envoy, Dies at 73
abstract: Archbishop Sambi was a career Vatican diplomat who represented the Roman Catholic Church in diplomatically delicate postings around the globe.

name: Fonce Mizell
headline: Fonce Mizell, a Songwriter and Producer, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Mizell helped create the Jackson 5’s first hits, including “I Want You Back” and “ABC.”

name: Polly Platt
headline: Polly Platt, Producer and Production Designer, Dies at 72
abstract: Ms. Platt, who was nominated for an Oscar, collaborated with her ex-husband Peter Bogdanovich on films like “The Last Picture Show.” She was also a screenwriter and producer.

name: John H. Marburger
headline: John H. Marburger, Bush Science Adviser, Dies at 70
abstract: Dr. Marburger maintained the respect of most colleagues even as many of them were harshly critical of the Bush White House.

name: Robert C. W. Ettinger
headline: Robert C. W. Ettinger, a Proponent of Life After (Deep-Frozen) Death, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Ettinger’s idea of freezing the dead for future reanimation spawned what some refer to as the cryonics movement.

name: David Servan-Schreiber
headline: David Servan-Schreiber, Exponent of Cancer Treatments, Dies at 50
abstract: Dr. Servan-Schreiber, a psychiatrist and author, drew on his own experience in battling the disease.

name: Howard Stein
headline: Howard Stein, Who Helped Teach Public to Invest, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Stein was a former chief of the Dreyfus Corporation who, as one of the fathers of the mutual fund industry, introduced innovations like the first money market fund with no initial fee.

name: Frank Bender
headline: Frank Bender, ‘Recomposer’ of Faces of the Dead, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Bender was a forensic sculptor whose work — three-dimensional faces in clay — helped identify the forgotten dead and apprehend the fugitive living.

name: Joe Arroyo
profession: Star of Salsa and Colombian Music Giant
headline: Joe Arroyo, Star of Salsa and Colombian Music Giant, Dies at 55
abstract: Mr. Arroyo’s pan-Caribbean salsa hybrids made him one of Colombia’s most respected musicians.

name: Elmer Lower
headline: Elmer Lower, Former President of ABC News, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Lower, who led ABC News at a time of expansion in the 1960s and early ’70s, was responsible for recruiting the anchor Peter Jennings, among others.

name: Fran Landesman
headline: Fran Landesman, Lyricist With a Bittersweet Edge, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Landesman was best known for the jazz standards “Spring Can Really Hang You Up the Most” and “The Ballad of the Sad Young Men.”

name: Richard F. Pedersen
headline: Richard F. Pedersen, Cold War Era Diplomat, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Pedersen’s government career of more than 20 years encompassed posts at the United Nations and the State Department and in Hungary, where he was the United States ambassador.

name: Hanna Segal
headline: Hanna Segal, Who Popularized Play Therapy, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Segal was a British psychoanalyst who helped change child psychology in the United States by explaining techniques developed by her mentor.

name: Eugene McDaniels
headline: Eugene McDaniels, Singer-Songwriter of Soul and Blues, Dies at 76
abstract: After singing hits like “A Hundred Pounds of Clay,” Mr. McDaniels wrote the ballad “Feel Like Makin’ Love” and the jazz protest song “Compared to What.”

name: Kenny Baker
headline: Kenny Baker, Fiddler Steeped in Bluegrass Style, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Baker was one of the first fiddlers to introduce exotic stylistic elements into bluegrass, which he once called “the hillbilly version of jazz.”

name: Kenny Baker
headline: Kenny Baker, the R2-D2 Robot in ‘Star Wars,’ Dies at 81
abstract: R2-D2 so changed Mr. Baker’s career that in later years he told an interviewer that if he could go back in time, he would do it again for free.

name: Paul Franke
headline: Paul Franke, Ubiquitous Singer at the Met, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Franke, a tenor, appeared 1,980 times at the Metropolitan Opera as a comprimario, a character actor.

name: Baruj Benacerraf
headline: Baruj Benacerraf, Nobel Winner in Medicine, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Benacerraf, a onetime president of the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in Boston, shared the 1980 Nobel Prize for decades of work and intellectual leaps studying the immune system.

name: Agnes Varis
headline: Agnes Varis, Founder of Drug Company, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Varis, a daughter of Greek immigrants, founded Agvar Chemicals, a New Jersey supplier of active ingredients to drug makers, and championed generic drugs.

name: Bubba Smith
headline: Bubba Smith, N.F.L. Star and Actor, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Smith, a defensive lineman, was the No. 1 draft pick for the Baltimore Colts in 1967. The cause of his death was not yet known.

name: James Ford Seale
headline: James Ford Seale, Imprisoned Klansman, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Seale, who was convicted years after the 1964 kidnapping-torture episode on the Mississippi-Louisiana border and serving three life sentences, was reported dead before.

name: Arthur Murray
headline: Arthur Murray, Test Pilot, Is Dead at 92
abstract: In 1954, Mr. Murray, known as Kit, of the Air Force guided a Bell X-1A plane higher than any human being had ever been, 90,440 feet over the earth.

name: Delois Barrett Campbell
headline: Delois Barrett Campbell, Gospel Singer, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Campbell, a silvery soprano, helped define the sound of the Barrett Sisters, a prominent gospel trio featured in the documentary “Say Amen, Somebody.”

name: Rudolf Brazda
headline: Rudolf Brazda, Who Survived Pink Triangle, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Mr. Brazda was believed to be the last surviving man to wear the emblem sewn onto the striped uniforms of the thousands of homosexuals sent to Nazi concentration camps.

name: Andrzej Lepper
headline: Andrzej Lepper, Polish Firebrand Wary of Europe, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Lepper was a populist politician who rose from pig farmer to deputy prime minister of Poland but whose career was undone by scandal.

name: Elmer Staats
headline: Elmer Staats, Comptroller General in 4 Administrations, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Staats transformed the role of the Congressional agency that oversees federal spending from keeping track of the dollars to evaluating the efficacy of government programs.

name: M.H. Rindskopf
headline: M.H. Rindskopf, Submarine Commander, Dies at 93
abstract: As the youngest commander of an American fleet submarine during World War II, Admiral Rindskopf directed the sinking of 15 Japanese vessels.

name: William Sleator
headline: William Sleator, Fantasy Writer for Young Adults, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Sleator, a writer for young adults, worked in a genre that straddled fantasy, science fiction and horror.

name: Hugh Carey
profession: Led Fiscal Rescue of New York City
headline: Hugh Carey, Who Led Fiscal Rescue of New York City, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Carey helped rescue New York from the brink of financial collapse in the 1970s and tamed a culture of ever-growing spending.

name: Jane White
headline: Jane White, Actress and Singer Who Found Racial Attitudes to Be an Obstacle, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. White, a light-skinned black actress and singer, found that casting directors resisted putting her in roles both because she was too white to be black and because she was too black to be white.

name: Mark O. Hatfield
headline: Mark O. Hatfield, Republican Champion of Liberal Causes, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Hatfield, a senator from Oregon for 30 years, challenged his party on war, a balanced-budget amendment and nuclear weapons.

name: Bernadine P. Healy
profession: Pioneer at National Institutes of Health
headline: Bernadine P. Healy, a Pioneer at National Institutes of Health, Dies at 67
abstract: Dr. Healy, the first woman to run the National Institutes of Health, helped overturn assumptions that heart disease was mainly just a male problem.

name: Fred Imus
headline: Fred Imus, Radio Personality and Songwriter, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Imus appeared frequently on his older brother Don’s radio show.

name: Charles Wyly
headline: Charles Wyly Dies at 77; Amassed Fortune With Brother
abstract: Mr. Wyly was a businessman who, with his brother, Sam, built a broad business empire and supported the arts and Republican politicians.

name: Marshall Grant
headline: Marshall Grant, Bass Player With Johnny Cash, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Grant helped create the pulsing “boom-chicka-boom” sound of Cash’s band.

name: Roman Opalka
headline: Roman Opalka, an Artist of Numbers, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Opalka was known for a quixotic project in which he sought to paint every number to infinity.

name: Harry H. Wellington
profession: Dean at Yale and a Labor Law Expert
headline: Harry H. Wellington, Dean at Yale and a Labor Law Expert, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Wellington served on the faculties of Yale Law School and New York Law School and wrote influential works on labor law and constitutional interpretation.

name: Claude Laydu
headline: Claude Laydu, French Actor, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Laydu made his screen debut in the lead role of Robert Bresson’s critically acclaimed film “Diary of a Country Priest.”

name: Francesco Quinn
headline: Francesco Quinn, Actor in ‘Platoon,’ Dies at 48
abstract: Mr. Quinn, the son of Anthony Quinn, was known for his role as Rhah in Oliver Stone’s 1986 Vietnam War film, “Platoon.”

name: Sakyo Komatsu
headline: Sakyo Komatsu, 80, Science Fiction Writer, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Komatsu’s 1973 book, “Japan Sinks,” was prescient in its vision of Japan after an earthquake and tsunami.

name: Harri Holkeri
headline: Harri Holkeri, Northern Ireland Peace Negotiator, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Mr. Holkeri used his diplomatic skills to help shepherd talks that led to the Belfast Agreement and also in negotiations between Yugoslavia and Kosovo.

name: Eleanor M. Josaitis
headline: Eleanor M. Josaitis, Housewife-Turned-Urban Activist, Dies at 79
abstract: Mrs. Josaitis was a suburban housewife who moved her family into Detroit after the 1967 riots and helped create a highly regarded nonprofit organization to combat poverty and racism.

name: Ray Anderson
headline: Ray Anderson, Businessman Turned Environmentalist, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Anderson, an avowed “recovering plunderer,” re-invented his worldwide factory operation to reduce its environmental impact.

name: M. Kenneth Oshman
headline: M. Kenneth Oshman, Who Brought Fun to Silicon Valley, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Oshman, who co-founded Rolm Corporation, was known for an informal yet driven management style that helped make work like play.

name: John Wood
headline: John Wood, Actor Known for Nimbleness, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Wood was a Tony Award-winning British stage actor known for his agile interpretations of playwrights from Shakespeare to Stoppard.

name: Sherman White
headline: Sherman White, Star Caught in a Scandal, Dies at 82
abstract: Days after being named college basketball player of the year in 1951, White and several Long Island University teammates were implicated in a national point-shaving scandal.

name: Stanley Bosworth
headline: Stanley Bosworth, Iconoclastic Head of Brooklyn School, Dies at 83
abstract: At Saint Ann’s School in Brooklyn, Mr. Bosworth’s expansive, scampish personality was stamped everywhere, so much so that it was common to speak of a cult of personality there.

name: Scott LeDoux
headline: Scott LeDoux, Gritty Heavyweight Boxing Contender, Dies at 62
abstract: In his 10-year professional career, Mr. LeDoux had 33 wins, 22 of them knockouts; 13 losses; and 4 draws.

name: Don Chandler
headline: Don Chandler, Standout Kicker in N.F.L., Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Chandler was a punter and place-kicker for the Giants and the Packers who played on four title-winning teams.

name: Jani Lane
headline: Jani Lane, Heavy-Metal Lead Singer, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. Lane was the former lead singer for the band Warrant and wrote its 1990 hit “Cherry Pie.”

name: Daniel D. McCracken
headline: Daniel D. McCracken, Expert on Computers, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. McCracken, most recently a professor at City College, published his first book, “Digital Computer Programming,” in 1957, and wrote a total of 25 books on computers.

name: Paul Meier
headline: Paul Meier, Statistician Who Revolutionized Medical Trials, Dies at 87
