abstract: Dr. Meier was an influential advocate of “randomization,” which helped reduce bias in clinical tests of drugs and treatments.

name: Howard G. Paster
headline: Howard G. Paster, Clinton Aide Who Helped Pass Nafta, Dies at 66
abstract: As President Bill Clinton’s liaison to Congress, Mr. Paster had to overcome the opposition of most House Democrats to push through the North American Free Trade Agreement.

name: Nancy Wake
headline: Nancy Wake, Proud Spy and Nazi Foe, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Wake underwent a wartime metamorphosis, from a fun-loving youth to a highly decorated Resistance fighter.

name: George C. Devol
headline: George C. Devol, Inventor of Robot Arm, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Devol’s Unimate mechanical arm became the prototype for robots widely used in auto assembly lines and other industries.

name: Nat Allbright
profession: Voice of Dodgers Games He Did Not See
headline: Nat Allbright, Voice of Dodgers Games He Did Not See, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Allbright broadcast 1,500 Brooklyn Dodgers games by taking bare-bones telegraph messages transmitted by Morse code and embellishing them to recreate the feeling of being at a ballpark.

name: Albert Brown
headline: Albert Brown, Survivor of Bataan March, Dies at 105
abstract: Mr. Brown was the oldest American survivor of the Bataan Death March in 1942, and perhaps the oldest American veteran of World War II.

name: Pete Pihos
headline: Pete Pihos, Eagles Hall of Fame Receiver, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Pihos helped take the Philadelphia Eagles to two consecutive N.F.L. championships in the 1940s.

name: Charles P. Murray Jr.
headline: Charles P. Murray Jr., Medal of Honor Recipient, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Murray was recognized for single-handedly preventing 200 German soldiers from attacking an American battalion during World War II.

name: Ralph Albertazzie
headline: Ralph Albertazzie, Nixon’s Pilot, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Albertazzie flew Henry A. Kissinger on a secret mission to China and flew the Nixon family home to California after Nixon’s resignation.

name: Fritz Bach
headline: Fritz Bach, Who Aided Transplant Survival, Dies at 77
abstract: Dr. Fritz H. Bach was a medical researcher who developed techniques to help lessen the possibility of organ rejection.

name: Creed C. Black
headline: Creed C. Black, Newspaper Executive, Dies at 86
abstract: As publisher of The Lexington Herald-Leader, Mr. Black supported an investigation of the University of Kentucky basketball team that led to the first Pulitzer Prize for the paper.

name: Robert Breer
headline: Robert Breer, Pioneer of Avant-Garde Animation, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Breer’s use of novel techniques to set lines and forms scrambling across the screen opened up a new language for film.

name: Leon Schipper
headline: Leon Schipper, Physicist and Iconoclast, Dies at 64
abstract: A critic of conventional wisdom and an amateur musician, Dr. Schipper’s work focused on improving efficiency in energy use and transportation.

name: Ruth Brinker
headline: Ruth Brinker, Who Gave AIDS Patients Meals, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Ms. Brinker founded one of the first social service agencies dedicated to providing meals to AIDS victims who could not feed themselves.

name: Claudio Castiglioni
headline: Claudio Castiglioni, Motorbike Executive, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Castiglioni transformed a family metalworking business into the world’s fifth largest motorcycle manufacturer.

name: Gualtiero Jacopetti
headline: Gualtiero Jacopetti, Maker of ‘Mondo Cane,’ Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Jacopetti liked to say he had invented the “antidocumentary” or the “shockumentary” with “Mondo Cane.”

name: Bob Sherman
headline: Bob Sherman, a Force Behind ‘Shock Jock’ Radio, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Sherman, an executive at the New York radio station WNBC in the late 1970s and early ’80s, hired Howard Stern and rehired Don Imus.

name: Raúl Ruiz
headline: Raúl Ruiz, Prolific Director of Cryptic Films, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Ruiz, a Chilean director, delighted in the twisting and turning plots of his movies.

name: Clair George
headline: Clair George, Spy and Iran-Contra Figure, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. George was a renowned figure at the C.I.A., whose unshakable loyalty to that agency prompted him to lie to Congress about Iran-contra, for which he was convicted.

name: Carl Hanford
headline: Carl Hanford, Kelso’s Trainer, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Hanford was inducted into the National Museum of Racing and Hall of Fame in 2006. His thoroughbred, Kelso, won a record five Horse of the Year citations.

name: Jimmy Sangster
headline: Jimmy Sangster, Writer for British Horror Films, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Sangster helped create the horror genre in England in the 1950s with films like “The Curse of Frankenstein,” “Horror of Dracula” and “The Mummy.”

name: Jerry Leiber
headline: Jerry Leiber, Prolific Writer of 1950s Hits, Dies at 78
abstract: With his partner, Mike Stoller, Mr. Leiber wrote a string of hits including “Hound Dog” and “Stand By Me.”

name: Lane Venardos
headline: Lane Venardos, Ex-CBS News Vice President, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Venardos presided over breaking news events like the protests in Tiananmen Square and the death of Diana, Princess of Wales.

name: W. B. Kannel
headline: W. B. Kannel, Who Led Historic Heart Study, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Kannel was one of the principal researchers behind the life-changing Framingham Heart Study, which began in 1948 and continues today.

name: Nora Bredes
headline: Nora Bredes, Who Fought Long Island Nuclear Plant, Dies at 60
abstract: Ms. Bredes was the chief organizer of a grass-roots campaign in the 1980s that prevented the power plant from opening on the North Shore of Long Island.

name: Nick Ashford
headline: Nick Ashford, of Motown Writing Duo, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Ashford and his songwriting partner and later wife, Valerie Simpson, composed hits for Marvin Gaye and Tammi Terrell, Ray Charles, Diana Ross, Chaka Khan and themselves.

name: John Howard Davies
headline: John Howard Davies, TV Comedy Producer, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Davies, who, as a boy, played the title role in the 1948 film “Oliver Twist,” went on to become a producer and director of some of British television’s most popular comedies.

name: Ross Barbour
headline: Ross Barbour, a Founding ‘Freshman,’ Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Barbour was the last founding member of the Four Freshmen, a barbershop quartet that still perform today, years after the original members “graduated.”

name: Samuel Menashe
profession: New York Poet of Short Verse
headline: Samuel Menashe, New York Poet of Short Verse, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Menashe, who lived as a bohemian, specialized in very short, often unpunctuated poems of less than 10 lines, with a religious or metaphysical bent.

name: Jerome Shestack
headline: Jerome Shestack, Diplomat and Bar Association Leader, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Shestack, who was active in liberal causes, was said to have helped play a role in the demise of Judge Robert H. Bork’s Supreme Court nomination.

name: Frank Dileo
headline: Frank Dileo, Michael Jackson’s Manager, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Dileo, a stout, cigar-smoking former bookie, was Michael Jackson’s personal manager during much of his 1980s career peak.

name: Joey Vento
headline: Joey Vento, Founder of Cheese-Steak Institution, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Vento opened Geno’s Steaks in 1967, one of the Big Three of the Philly cheese-steak establishments.

name: Budd Hopkins
headline: Budd Hopkins, Abstract Expressionist and U.F.O. Author, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Hopkins was a distinguished Abstract Expressionist artist who also became the father of the alien-abduction movement.

name: Mike Flanagan
headline: Mike Flanagan, Former Orioles Pitching Star, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Flanagan, a pitcher for Baltimore, won the Cy Young Award as the top pitcher in the American League in 1979. The left-hander had a career record of 167-143 in 18 seasons, pitching mostly for the Baltimore Orioles.

name: Casey Ribicoff
profession: Senators Widow and a Style Leader
headline: Casey Ribicoff, Senator’s Widow and a Style Leader, Dies at 88
abstract: Mrs. Ribicoff, the widow of Abraham A. Ribicoff of Connecticut, straddled the worlds of New York politics, fashion and culture.

name: Tareque Masud
headline: Tareque Masud, Bangladeshi Filmmaker, Is Dead at 54
abstract: Mr. Masud’s “Clay Bird” won an International Critics’ award at the 2002 Cannes Film Festival.

name: Frank Potenza
headline: Frank Potenza, Foil for Kimmel, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Jimmy Kimmel, the late-night host, decided his Uncle Frank had a matchless comic appeal, simply by being himself.

name: Jeanette Ingberman
headline: Jeanette Ingberman, a Founder of Exit Art, Dies at 59
abstract: Ms. Ingberman was a founder of the cultural center, which showed avant-garde work by artists from around the world.

name: George Hendry
profession: Young and Old Table Tennis Master
headline: George Hendry, a Young and Old Table Tennis Master, Dies at 90
abstract: As a teenage star in the 1930s, Mr. Hendry was pictured on the Wheaties box.

name: Price Berkley
profession: Founder and Longtime Publisher of Theatrical Index
headline: Price Berkley, Founder and Longtime Publisher of Theatrical Index, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Berkley also served as editor and publisher of the weekly trade publication, which he started in 1964.

name: June Wayne
headline: June Wayne, Painter and Printmaker, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Wayne persuaded artists like Richard Diebenkorn, Sam Francis and Louise Nevelson to collaborate with printers at the Tamarind Lithography Workshop she founded.

name: Sally Goodgold
headline: Sally Goodgold, Civic Advocate Who Practiced ‘Bagel Diplomacy,’ Dies at 82
abstract: Mrs. Goodgold, the first woman elected president of the City Club of New York, was a bold, brassy civil advocate who was not easily intimidated.

name: Charles C. Edwards
headline: Dr. Charles C. Edwards, Influential F.D.A. Commissioner, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Edwards ordered that a message be inserted in each package of birth control pills discussing the benefits and hazards.

name: Sybil Jason
headline: Sybil Jason, Cherubic Child Actress, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Jason was signed by Warner Brothers to compete with Shirley Temple in the 1930s.

name: Edgar M. Cullman Sr.
profession: Helped Turn Cigars Into Objects of Desire
headline: Edgar M. Cullman Sr., Who Helped Turn Cigars Into Objects of Desire, Is Dead at 93
abstract: As a longtime executive at General Cigar Company, Mr. Cullman helped shift the public image of cigars from Edward G. Robinson gangsterism to Steve McQueen cool.

name: David Honeyboy Edwards
headline: David Honeyboy Edwards, Delta Bluesman, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Edwards was believed to have been the oldest surviving member of the first generation of Delta blues singers.

name: Stetson Kennedy
headline: Stetson Kennedy, Who Infiltrated and Exposed the Klan, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Kennedy was a folklorist and social crusader who infiltrated the Ku Klux Klan in the 1940s and wrote a lurid exposé of its activities.

name: Susan Fromberg Schaeffer
headline: Susan Fromberg Schaeffer, Inventive Novelist, Dies at 71
abstract: Ms. Schaeffer’s books explored a wide range of plots and ideas, from a semiautobiographical novel to the story of a soldier in Vietnam.

name: Patrick C. Fischer
headline: Patrick C. Fischer, Early Unabomber Target, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Mr. Fischer, a computer scientist whose theoretical work helped make Internet searches possible, was most widely known as an early target of the so-called Unabomber.

name: Leonard Harris
headline: Leonard Harris, Television Critic, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Harris, who was an arts and theater critic for WCBS-TV, played Senator Charles Palantine in Martin Scorsese’s “Taxi Driver.”

name: David Reynolds
headline: David Reynolds, Leader of Metals Company, Dies at 96
abstract: A former chief executive of Reynolds Metals, Mr. Reynolds aggressively promoted aluminum’s use in consumer goods and packaging to avoid a glut after World War II.

name: Bernard Wolfman
headline: Bernard Wolfman, Who Sought Tax Overhaul, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Wolfman concluded that only an independent commission could correct a flawed system, and advised simplicity as a means to ensure fairness.

name: William Wolff
headline: Dr. William Wolff, Colonoscopy Co-Developer, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Wolff and a colleague revolutionized the diagnosis and treatment of colon cancer.

name: Ronald Fernandez
profession: Scholar on Plight of Puerto Ricans
headline: Ronald Fernandez, Scholar on Plight of Puerto Ricans, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Fernandez’s curiosity about a 1983 armored car robbery near his Connecticut home led to a lifelong field of study.

name: Alvin Bunis
profession: Creator of a Senior Tennis Circuit
headline: Alvin Bunis, Creator of a Senior Tennis Circuit, Dies at 87
abstract: A longtime amateur player, Bunis created the Tennis Grand Masters circuit, for players over 45.

name: Maurice M. Rapport
headline: Maurice M. Rapport, Who Studied Serotonin, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Rapport was a biochemist who helped isolate and name the neurotransmitter serotonin, which plays a role in regulating mood and mental states.

name: John Cullen
headline: John Cullen, Coast Guardsman Who Detected Spies, Dies at 90
abstract: On a foggy night in 1942, Seaman Cullen spotted four German agents on the Long Island shore and derailed a plot to blow up rail facilities and war-industry plants.

name: Leo-Arthur Kelmenson
headline: Leo-Arthur Kelmenson, Ad Man Who Helped to Save Chrysler, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Kelmenson took a chance on an old friend and conceived the television ad campaign that made Lee Iacocca a household name.

name: Eugene A. Nida
headline: Rev. Eugene A. Nida, Who Spurred a Babel of Bibles, Is Dead at 96
abstract: Mr. Nida recruited and trained native speakers to translate Scripture into a host of languages around the world.

name: Rosel Zech
headline: Rosel Zech, a Movie Actress Favored by Fassbinder, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Zech was best known to American audiences for her title role in Rainer Werner Fassbinder’s “Veronika Voss.”

name: Frank C. Arricale
headline: Frank C. Arricale, Youth Board Leader Who Calmed Race Tensions, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Arricale garnered criticism when he enlisted the aid of Mafia leaders to help the city avoid racial violence in 1966, but the approach seemed to work.

name: Julio Casas Regueiro
headline: Julio Casas Regueiro, Cuba’s Defense Chief, Dies at 75
abstract: General Casas, a close associate of President Raúl Castro, was only the second person to serve as defense minister since the revolution in 1959.

name: Salvatore Licitra
headline: Salvatore Licitra, Operatic Tenor at Met, Is Dead at 43
abstract: Mr. Licitra gained fame in New York overnight when he substituted for Pavarotti at a 2002 Met gala.

name: Lee Roy Selmon
headline: Lee Roy Selmon, Buccaneer Cornerstone, Dies at 56
abstract: Selmon, a Hall of Fame defensive end, became a cornerstone of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during their first decade in the National Football League.

name: Vann Nath
headline: Vann Nath, Artist and Cambodia Torture Survivor, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Vann Nath was a painter and one of only a handful of survivors of the Khmer Rouge torture center Tuol Sleng.

name: Keith Tantlinger
headline: Keith Tantlinger, Builder of Cargo Container, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Tantlinger is credited with creating, in the 1950s, the first commercially viable modern shipping container, which changed the way nations do business.

name: Peter Twiss
headline: Peter Twiss, Record-Setting British Pilot, Dies at 90
abstract: Peter Twiss set the world aviation speed record in March 1956, flying at an average of 1,132 miles an hour.

name: Eve Brent
headline: Eve Brent, Played Jane in Tarzan Movies, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Brent was a veteran character actress best known for her role as Jane, which she said she took to please her young son.

name: Wardell Quezergue
headline: Wardell Quezergue, R&B Hitmaker, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Quezergue was a producer, arranger and bandleader for a long list of New Orleans artists that included the Dixie Cups, Professor Longhair, the Neville Brothers and Dr. John.

name: George Kuchar
headline: George Kuchar, Underground Filmmaker, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Kuchar was a filmmaker whose campy, low-budget movies helped kindle the do-it-yourself moviemaking aesthetic now ubiquitous on YouTube.

name: Michael Hart
headline: Michael Hart, a Pioneer of E-Books, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Hart began the digital library Project Gutenberg after a July 4 fireworks display, when he typed up the Declaration of Independence and made it available for download.

name: Charles Dubin
headline: Charles Dubin, Television Director, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Despite refusing to answer some questions before the House Committee on Un-American Activities, Mr. Dubin went on to a robust career in TV, especially with “M*A*S*H.”

name: Bill Kunkel
headline: Bill Kunkel, an Early Chronicler of Video Games, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Kunkel helped start the first published gaming column in 1978, and later the first video game magazine.

name: Jordan Belson
headline: Jordan Belson, Experimental Filmmaker, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Belson specialized in studies of color, movement and light that challenged notions of perception.

name: Sidney H. Asch
headline: Sidney H. Asch, a Judge and a Scholar, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Asch, a judge with a Ph.D. in sociology, wrote scholarly works about civil liberties and made notable decisions about landlord-tenant law and gay employment.

name: Betty Skelton
headline: Betty Skelton, Air and Land Daredevil, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Skelton was a three-time national aerobatic women’s flight champion when she turned to race-car driving, then went on to exceed 300 m.p.h. in a jet-powered car.

name: Christopher Small
headline: Christopher Small, Cultural Musicologist, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Small contended that music is a ritual involving not only its players but the audience and surroundings as well.

name: Bruce Dan
profession: Helped Link Toxic Shock and Tampons
headline: Bruce Dan, Who Helped Link Toxic Shock and Tampons, Is Dead at 64
abstract: As a member of a federal task force, Dr. Dan acted as a disease detective, delving into the daily habits and medical histories of victims.

name: Cliff Robertson
headline: Cliff Robertson, Oscar-Winning Rebel, Dies at 88
abstract: An Academy Award winner for “Charly,” Mr. Robertson later challenged a powerful studio boss as a forger and embezzler.

name: Andy Whitfield
headline: Andy Whitfield, Star of ‘Spartacus’ Series, Dies at 39
abstract: Mr. Whitfield was a relatively unknown actor when he was chosen for the lead role in the Starz series “Spartacus: Blood and Sand.”

name: Mary Fickett
headline: Mary Fickett, a Pillar of ‘All My Children,’ Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Fickett was well known to viewers of “All My Children” and received a Tony nomination for her role as Eleanor Roosevelt in the play “Sunrise at Campobello.”

name: Richard Hamilton
profession: British Painter and a Creator of Pop Art
headline: Richard Hamilton, British Painter and a Creator of Pop Art, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Hamilton, whose sly, trenchant take on consumer culture and advertising made him a pioneering figure in Pop Art, was known for his cover design of the Beatles’ “White Album.”

name: Richard Hamilton
headline: Richard Hamilton, Who Helped Solve a Mathematical Mystery, Dies at 81
abstract: He came up with an innovative equation called the Ricci flow that helped mathematicians explore fundamental questions that were once out of reach.

name: Carl Oglesby
headline: Carl Oglesby, Antiwar Leader in 1960s, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Oglesby led Students for a Democratic Society as it publicly opposed the Vietnam War, and his speech “Let Us Shape the Future” is considered a landmark of American political rhetoric.

name: John Calley
headline: John Calley, Hollywood Chief, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Calley rose to Hollywood’s highest ranks not by slashing and burning but by making gut-level bets on directors and writers, and by gently and quietly steering them.

name: Arthur Evans
headline: Arthur Evans, Leader in Gay Rights Fight, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Evans helped form and lead the movement that coalesced after gay people and their supporters protested a 1969 police raid on the Stonewall Inn, a Greenwich Village gay bar.

name: Wade Mainer
headline: Wade Mainer, a Pioneer of Bluegrass Banjo, Dies at 104
abstract: Mr. Mainer’s use of a two-finger picking style, his biographer said, “brought the music forward.”

name: Walter Bonatti
headline: Walter Bonatti, Daring Italian Mountaineer, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Bonatti was a member of the Italian team that conquered K2 in northern Pakistan, but he did not reach the summit and later accused two colleagues of denying him an opportunity to share the moment.

name: Malcolm Wallop
headline: Malcolm Wallop, Senator From Wyoming, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Wallop, a three-term Republican, became a leading conservative voice in Congress during the Reagan administration.

name: Sam DeLuca
headline: Sam DeLuca, a Former Jet and Broadcaster, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Mr. DeLuca played guard for the Jets in the 1960s and went on to a broadcasting career after a knee injury forced his retirement from football.

name: Vito Perrone Sr.
headline: Vito Perrone Sr., Who Fought Standardized Tests, Dies at 78
abstract: Dr. Perrone’s ideas on flexible teaching methods led to a loose network of public alternative schools in New York, Boston, Chicago and Philadelphia.

name: Jesús Silva
headline: Jesús Silva, Priest Who Founded Spanish Boys Town, Dies at 78
abstract: Father Silva aided 15 boys who had been orphaned by creating a town that was governed by children.

name: Charles Percy
headline: Charles Percy, Former Ill. Senator, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Percy was a moderate Republican who clashed with President Richard M. Nixon over the Watergate scandal.

name: Eleanor Poling
headline: Eleanor Poling, Daughter of Former Vice President, Dies at 51
abstract: Walter F. Mondale’s daughter achieved success as a radio and television personality.

name: Kara Kennedy
headline: Kara Kennedy, Daughter of Edward Kennedy, Is Dead at 51
abstract: Ms. Kennedy, the eldest of Senator Edward M. Kennedy’s children, led a more private life than most Kennedys of her generation.

name: Walter C. Righter
headline: Bishop Walter C. Righter, 87, Dies; Faced Heresy Trial
abstract: Bishop Righter was an Episcopal bishop who in 1996 was brought to trial and absolved of a charge of heresy for having ordained an actively gay man as a deacon.

name: Ralph J. Lomma
headline: Ralph J. Lomma, Who Shaped Miniature Golf, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Lomma and his brother, Alphonse, are credited with modernizing a static pastime by giving whimsical figures moving parts.

name: Dave Gavitt
profession: Founding Force of the Big East Conference
headline: Dave Gavitt, Founding Force of the Big East Conference, Dies at 73
abstract: Gavitt harnessed the burgeoning power of televised sports coverage with his nascent league to produce a powerful conference.

name: Wilma Lee Cooper
headline: Wilma Lee Cooper, Grand Ole Opry Singer, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Cooper, with her husband, Stoney, was a mainstay at the Grand Ole Opry and on country music radio.

name: Frances Bay
profession: Actress Known for Old Lady Roles
headline: Frances Bay, Actress Known for ‘Old Lady’ Roles, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Bay, ubiquitous as a character actress, played the Fonz’s grandmother and the lady who battles for a loaf of marble rye on “Seinfeld.”

name: Dolores Hope
headline: Dolores Hope, Singer and Bob Hope’s Widow, Dies at 102
abstract: Mrs. Hope gave up her singing career to to spend 69 years with her husband, pursuing philanthropy and projecting with him the image of an enduring Hollywood marriage.

name: Joe Dressner
headline: Joe Dressner, Importer of Old World Wines, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Dressner’s Manhattan company specialized in producers from Italy and France, and he championed wines that were expressions of local cultures.

name: James M. Cannon
headline: James M. Cannon, an Adviser to Ford, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Cannon was a former journalist who advised top policy makers in Washington, including President Gerald R. Ford.

name: Kurt Sanderling
headline: Kurt Sanderling, Eastern Bloc Conductor, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Sanderling spent most of his career in the Communist world after finding refuge from the Nazis there during World War II.

name: William F. May
headline: William F. May, 95, Dies; Helped Found Film Society
abstract: Mr. May, who led the American Can Company for 15 years, was also a longtime board member of The New York Times.

name: Tom Wilson
headline: Tom Wilson, Cartoonist Behind ‘Ziggy,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Wilson created a short, bald, big-nosed comic character meant to stand in for everyone stumbling through the frustrations and disappointments of life.

name: Mohammed Ghani Hikmat
headline: Mohammed Ghani Hikmat, Iraqi Sculptor, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Hikmat created many of Baghdad’s most famous landmarks and led the effort to recover works of art looted from the National Museum of Iraq.

name: Norma H. Johnson
headline: Norma H. Johnson, 79, Dies; Oversaw Lewinsky Inquiry
abstract: Judge Johnson was the first African-American woman appointed to the federal bench in Washington and oversaw the grand jury investigation into President Bill Clinton’s affair with Monica Lewinsky.

name: Brian J. Kelley
headline: Brian J. Kelley, Onetime Spying Suspect, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Kelley, a counterintelligence expert who helped focus attention on a possible Russian spy in Washington, was wrongly suspected of being a K.G.B. mole himself.

name: Donn A. Starry
headline: Gen. Donn A. Starry, Cold War Strategist, Dies at 86
abstract: General Starry’s AirLand Battle Doctrine, imagined for use against the Soviets, played a decisive role in the first Persian Gulf war.

name: Stephen Mueller
headline: Stephen Mueller, Color Field Painter, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Mueller’s mature paintings, which took shape in the early 1990s, were cross-cultural hybrids that presaged many current concerns in abstract painting.

name: Julius Blank
headline: Julius Blank, Who Built First Chip Maker, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Blank and a colleague scrounged parts, improvised equipment and tooled a set of machines that essentially became the first assembly line for computer chips.

name: A. Richard Turner
headline: A. Richard Turner Dies at 79; Wrote ‘Inventing Leonardo’
abstract: Mr. Turner focused on the multiple Leonardos created by biographers, critics and artists, from Vasari to Freud and beyond.

name: Orlando Brown
headline: Orlando Brown, Who Sued N.F.L. Over Errant Flag, Dies at 40
abstract: Brown, an offensive tackle for the Cleveland Browns and the Baltimore Ravens, was once temporarily blinded in one eye by a referee’s errant penalty flag.

name: Oscar Handlin
headline: Oscar Handlin, Historian Who Chronicled U.S. Immigration, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Handlin used unorthodox sources for his work, delving into newspaper accounts, personal letters and diaries as well as historic archives.

name: Justin N. Feldman
headline: Justin N. Feldman, 92, Dies; Opposed Tammany Hall
abstract: A lawyer and liberal Democrat, Mr. Feldman helped manage Robert F. Kennedy’s successful 1964 campaign to represent New York in the United States Senate.

name: Frank Driggs
headline: Frank Driggs, Collector of Jazz Photos, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Driggs, a writer, historian and record producer, was known for his collection of nearly 100,000 jazz photographs.

name: Wangari Maathai
headline: Wangari Maathai, Nobel Peace Prize Laureate, Dies at 71
abstract: Dr. Maathai was a Kenyan environmentalist who started out paying women a few shillings to plant trees and went on to become the first African woman to win a Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Jessy Dixon
headline: Jessy Dixon, Gospel Singer and Songwriter, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Dixon helped popularize gospel music with his energetic style and found a wider audience touring and recording with Paul Simon.

name: Douglas LaChance
headline: Douglas LaChance, Who Led Newspaper Deliverers’ Union, Dies at 69
abstract: A garrulous, two-fisted labor leader, Mr. LaChance served prison time for racketeering and extortion after being convicted of accepting $330,000 in payoffs.

name: Mo Rothman
headline: Mo Rothman Dies at 92; Revived Interest in Charlie Chaplin
abstract: Mr. Rothman, a film executive and entrepreneur, orchestrated the aging star’s triumphant return to the United States after a self-imposed exile.

name: Johnnie Wright
headline: Johnnie Wright, 97, Singer and Country Bandleader, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Wright, one of the first country musicians to use Latin rhythms, may have been more known as the manager for Kitty Wells, his wife.

name: Wilson Greatbatch
headline: Wilson Greatbatch, Inventor of Implantable Pacemaker, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Greatbatch was a “humble tinkerer” who patented more than 325 inventions, notably a long-life lithium battery used in a wide range of medical implants.

name: Arch West
headline: Arch West, Who Helped Create Doritos Corn Chips, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Mr. West, a marketing executive at Frito-Lay, got the idea for Doritos when he encountered a homemade fried corn chip while on vacation in San Diego, according to family members.

name: David Zelag Goodman
headline: David Zelag Goodman, Far-Ranging Screenwriter, Dies at 81
abstract: The prolific screenwriter helped Sam Peckinpah write “Straw Dogs” and was nominated for an Academy Award for his work on the romantic comedy “Lovers and Other Strangers.”

name: Claude R. Kirk Jr.
headline: Claude R. Kirk Jr., Former Florida Governor, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Kirk, who in 1966 became Florida’s first Republican governor since Reconstruction, opposed the racial integration of schools and signed a deal with Roy Disney for a theme park.

name: Owsley Brown II
headline: Owsley Brown II, Liquor Company Chief, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Brown expanded his family’s Kentucky liquor company to reach a global market for its brands, among them Jack Daniel’s Tennessee Whiskey.

name: Bob Cassilly
headline: Bob Cassilly, Playscape Creator Fueled by Whimsy, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Cassilly was a sculptor and artist, among other things, who was best known for City Museum, a children’s paradise of odd treasures, in St. Louis.

name: Dave Hill
headline: Dave Hill, Outspoken PGA Tour Pro, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Hill was a 13-time winner on the PGA Tour whose outspoken ways sometimes overshadowed his shotmaking.

name: Sylvia Robinson
headline: Sylvia Robinson, Pioneering Producer of Hip-Hop, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Ms. Robinson formed the Sugarhill Gang; oversaw “Rapper’s Delight,” the first commercially successful hip-hop single; and signed Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five.

name: Philip Hannan
headline: Philip Hannan, 98, Dies; New Orleans Archbishop
abstract: The archbishop was a confidant of President John F. Kennedy and the Roman Catholic leader in New Orleans for more than 20 years.

name: Roger Kennedy
headline: Roger Kennedy, Who Was Parks Chief Under Clinton, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Kennedy was an ardent preservationist of the nation’s cultural, historic and artistic heritage for much of his life.

name: Lee Davenport
headline: Lee Davenport Dies at 95; Developed Battlefront Radar
abstract: Mr. Davenport was a physicist who worked on a complex system used for tracking and shooting down enemy planes.

name: Mike Heimerdinger
profession: Helped to Coach Super Bowl Winners
headline: Mike Heimerdinger, 58, Who Helped to Coach Super Bowl Winners, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Heimerdinger, who coached offensive units for the Denver Broncos, the Jets and the Tennessee Titans, helped mold players like Steve McNair, Vince Young and Jay Cutler.

name: Khaled Abdel Nasser
headline: Khaled Abdel Nasser, Son of Egyptian Hero, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Nasser captured the world’s attention in the late 1980s when he was tried and acquitted of helping to assassinate two Israeli diplomats.

name: Joseph Carmichael Jr.
headline: Joseph Carmichael Jr., a Carrier Hero, Dies at 96
abstract: Commander Carmichael received the Navy Cross for his actions in helping to save the Bunker Hill after two kamikaze strikes.

name: Robert Whitaker
headline: Robert Whitaker, the Beatles’ Photographer, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Whitaker’s most talked-about work was the so-called “butcher cover” of the Beatles’ “Yesterday and Today,” which was pulled from store shelves.

name: Peter Gent
headline: Peter Gent, Football Novelist, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Gent, a receiver for the Dallas Cowboys of the 1960s, portrayed professional football as a dehumanizing business.

name: Michael J. Drake
headline: Michael J. Drake, Planetary Scientist, Dies at 65
abstract: Dr. Drake remained devoted to one idea until the end: sending a spacecraft to an asteroid to gather rock samples and bring them home for study. NASA is now planning to do just that.

name: Alexander Grant
headline: Alexander Grant, Dancer With Royal Ballet, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Grant was famous for his roles in Frederick Ashton’s ballets, creating roles in 22 premieres.

name: Leonard Dillon
headline: Leonard Dillon, Pioneering Reggae Singer, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Dillon, an influential Jamaican singer and songwriter, founded the vocal group the Ethiopians.

name: Ralph M. Steinman
profession: Nobel Recipient for Research on Immunology
headline: Ralph M. Steinman, a Nobel Recipient for Research on Immunology, Dies at 68
abstract: Dr. Steinman and two others were honored for discovering the essential steps in the immune system’s response to infection.

name: Everett Ellin
headline: Everett Ellin Dies at 82; Helped Computerize Art Catalogs
abstract: Mr. Ellin helped bring about the reluctant marriage between the conservative world of art museums and the wild frontier of information technology.

name: Emanuel Litvinoff
profession: Poet and Detractor of T. S. Eliot
headline: Emanuel Litvinoff, Poet and Detractor of T. S. Eliot, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Litvinoff wrote several volumes of poetry and novels, but is best known for criticizing T. S. Eliot as anti-Semitic in a poem he read aloud with Eliot present.

name: Clifford Olson
headline: Clifford Olson, Canadian Serial Killer, Is Dead at 71
abstract: The case of Mr. Olson caused a public uproar in the early 1980s after the authorities admitted paying him $100,000 to reveal the locations of his victims’ bodies.

name: Hanan Porat
headline: Hanan Porat, Jewish Settlement Leader, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Porat opposed the removal of Jews from any land in exchange for peace with Israel’s neighbors.

name: A.C. Nielsen Jr.
headline: A.C. Nielsen Jr., Who Built Ratings Firm, Dies at 92
abstract: Arthur C. Nielsen Jr. made his father’s company a global leader in market research whose name is synonymous with television ratings.

name: Marv Tarplin
headline: Marv Tarplin, Motown Guitarist and Songwriter, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Tarplin shaped the sound of Smokey Robinson and the Miracles and was a co-writer of “The Tracks of My Tears” and other hits.

name: David Mitchell
headline: David Mitchell, Broadway Set Designer, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Mitchell, who became one of the most sought-after designers on Broadway, won Tony Awards for “Annie” and “Barnum.”

name: David Mitchell
headline: David Mitchell, Weekly Editor Who Exposed a Corrupt Cult, Dies at 79
abstract: His tiny California newspaper won a Pulitzer Prize for its exposé of Synanon, a renowned drug rehabilitation program that had turned into a violent operation.

name: David Mitchell
headline: David Mitchell, Who Led Fight on Drug Prices, Dies at 75
abstract: After receiving a diagnosis of terminal cancer, he used his experience in public relations to draw attention to the skyrocketing cost of medication.

name: Bertel Bruun
headline: Bertel Bruun, Guidebook Designer, Dies at 73
abstract: Dr. Bruun’s 1966 layout for “Birds of North America,” which has sold in the millions, was a widely copied innovation.

name: Fred L. Shuttlesworth
headline: Rev. Fred L. Shuttlesworth, an Elder Statesman for Civil Rights, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Shuttlesworth survived beatings and bombings in Alabama more than four decades ago as he fought for equal rights for blacks alongside the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.

name: Steve Jobs
headline: Apple’s Visionary Redefined Digital Age
abstract: Mr. Jobs helped usher in the era of the personal computer and led a cultural transformation in mobile communications and music for the digital age.

name: Sarkis G. Soghanalian
headline: Sarkis G. Soghanalian, an Arms Dealer Who Aided U.S. Intelligence, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Soghanalian was a larger-than-life arms dealer who provided weapons to Saddam Hussein and others, worked closely with American intelligence and later told his story on television.

name: Bert Jansch
headline: Bert Jansch, an Influential Folk Guitarist, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Mr. Jansch, a founder of the progressive British folk group Pentangle, became an immediate sensation in 1965 with his self-titled debut album.

name: Derrick Bell
headline: Derrick Bell, Law Professor and Rights Advocate, Dies at 80
abstract: A pioneer of “critical race theory,” Mr. Bell was the first tenured black professor at Harvard Law School before moving to New York University.

name: Charles Napier
headline: Charles Napier, Actor Who Played Tough Guys, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Napier was a character actor who portrayed ruffians, military officers and other strong men in films like the second Rambo movie, but played against type as a judge in “Philadelphia.”

name: Ramiz Alia
profession: Enforcer for a Dictator and Later Ruler of Albania
headline: Ramiz Alia, an Enforcer for a Dictator and Later Ruler of Albania, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Alia, was a cult-of-personality enforcer who succeeded Enver Hoxha and presided over halting and often chaotic moves toward democracy before his own downfall in 1992.

name: Diane Cilento
headline: Diane Cilento, Oscar-Nominated Actress, Dies at 78
abstract: While Ms. Cilento had a long stage and screen career, she is most remembered for her supporting performance in the 1963 movie “Tom Jones.”

name: Piero Weiss
headline: Piero Weiss, Pianist and Musicologist, Dies at 83
abstract: Dr. Weiss, an expert on Italian opera, also was the co-author of a widely used anthology of historical documents about music.

name: Al Davis
headline: Al Davis, the Controversial and Combative Raiders Owner, Dies at 82
abstract: First as a coach, and then as an owner and managing general partner of the Oakland Raiders, Mr. Davis became the symbol of the franchise.

name: Kenneth H. Dahlberg
headline: Kenneth H. Dahlberg, Link in the Watergate Chain, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Dahlberg, who passed along a check that tied President Nixon’s re-election committee to the Watergate burglars, downed 15 German planes in World War II.

name: Roger Williams
headline: Roger Williams, Pianist Known for Sentimental Songs, Dies at 87
abstract: Among the nostalgia-inducing tunes Mr. Williams was known for are “Autumn Leaves,” “Born Free” and “Lara’s Theme” from “Dr. Zhivago.”

name: J. Willis Hurst
headline: Dr. J. Willis Hurst, Cardiologist to Lyndon B. Johnson, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Hurst was an expert in his field and the principal editor of one of the most widely used medical textbooks.

name: Paula L. Ettelbrick
profession: Legal Expert in Gay Rights Movement
headline: Paula L. Ettelbrick, Legal Expert in Gay Rights Movement, Dies at 56
abstract: Ms. Ettelbrick was a legal expert who held leadership positions in some of the more influential rights groups of the past 25 years.

name: Julio Mario Santo Domingo
headline: Julio Mario Santo Domingo, Colombian Billionaire, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Santo Domingo’s $8.5 billion fortune made him one of Latin America’s richest and most influential men.

name: Doris Belack
headline: Doris Belack, Judge on TV’s ‘Law & Order,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Belack was a stage and television actress best known for her roles as a “Law & Order” judge and as a soap opera producer in “Tootsie” with Dustin Hoffman.

name: Jagjit Singh
headline: Jagjit Singh, Reviver of Persian Ghazal Singing, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Singh was a popular singer in South Asia who helped revive and popularize ghazals, a form of Persian poetry set to music expressing the writer’s feelings.

name: Joe Aceti
headline: Joe Aceti, Director Who Shaped TV Sports, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Aceti was known for unorthodox camera shots, and his work included the Olympics, the World Series and the Ali-Frazier “Thrilla in Manila.”

name: Robert M. Schaeberle
headline: Robert M. Schaeberle, Nabisco Chief, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Schaeberle, who worked at Nabisco for 40 years, led the company through two mergers.

name: Robert Loughlin
headline: Robert Loughlin, Artist and Design Expert, Dies at 62
abstract: Scouring flea markets and thrift stores for discarded furnishings, Mr. Loughlin helped spark a market for sleek midcentury modern design.

name: Ruth Currier
headline: Ruth Currier, Principal Dancer With José Limón, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Currier, who embodied the solid early traditions of the American modern-dance lineage, became the director of Limón’s company after his death.

name: Fritz Manes
headline: Fritz Manes, Producer of Eastwood Films, Dies at 79
abstract: Among Mr. Manes’s films were “Any Which Way You Can” and “Heartbreak Ridge,” both starring Clint Eastwood.

name: Robert Finigan
headline: Robert Finigan, an Early Wine Critic, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Finigan attracted a national audience with a self-published bimonthly newsletter about wine and the wine business.

name: Allan Jefferys
headline: Allan Jefferys, Drama Critic for WABC-TV, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Jefferys also had a show on ABC radio that was broadcast nationwide as an alternative to Top 40 rock ’n’ roll stations in the early 1960s.

name: Franklin Kameny
headline: Franklin Kameny, Gay Rights Pioneer, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Kameny transformed his 1957 arrest as a “sex pervert” and his subsequent firing from the Army Map Service into a powerful animating spark of the gay rights movement.

name: Robert W. Galvin
profession: Ushered Motorola Into the Modern Era
headline: Robert W. Galvin, Who Ushered Motorola Into the Modern Era, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Galvin turned Motorola from a family business into a global maker of color television sets, cellphones and other ubiquities of the electronic age.

name: Nina Sorokina
headline: Nina Sorokina, Dancer With the Bolshoi Ballet, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Sorokina was a principal dancer with the Bolshoi Ballet, along with her husband and partner, Yuri Vladimirov.

name: David Hess
headline: David Hess, Songwriter and Actor, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Hess wrote songs for Elvis Presley and Pat Boone, and appeared in many films as a villain.

name: Mildred Savage
headline: Mildred Savage, Author of ‘Parrish,’ Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Savage also wrote another novel, “In Vivo,” and a nonfiction book, “A Great Fall: A Murder and Its Consequences.”

name: Arthur Dubin
headline: Arthur Dubin, Historian of Railroad’s Golden Era, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Dubin, an architect, became fascinated by trains as a child and went on to write two of the best-known works on American passenger railroads.

name: Dennis Ritchie
headline: Dennis Ritchie, Trailblazer in Digital Era, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Ritchie, the inventor of the C programming language and co-developer of the Unix operating system, influenced all facets of technology.

name: Philo Dibble
headline: Philo Dibble, Diplomat and Iran Expert, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Dibble was a career Foreign Service officer who played a central role in the release of two American hikers who had been held in an Iranian prison for more than two years.

name: Vic Miles
headline: Vic Miles, Reporter and Anchor on WCBS-TV, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Miles brought a no-nonsense, get-to-the-essence style to his 24 years as a reporter and anchorman for WCBS-TV/Channel 2 in New York and was among the first black television reporters in the city.

name: Ray Aghayan
headline: Ray Aghayan, Costume Designer, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Aghayan was the costume designer for stars like Judy Garland, Barbra Streisand, Diana Ross and Julie Andrews.

name: Michel Peissel
headline: Michel Peissel, Tibet Expert and Adventurer, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Peissel explored remote regions of the globe, including the Tibetan high plateau, remote Russian river towns and unrecorded Mayan ruins.

name: Laura Pollán Toledo
profession: Rallied Wives of Jailed Cuban Dissidents
headline: Laura Pollán Toledo, Who Rallied Wives of Jailed Cuban Dissidents, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Pollán founded the Ladies in White, who march in protest every Sunday in Havana, after a 2003 government crackdown.

name: Sue Mengers
headline: Sue Mengers, Hollywood Agent, Dies at 79
abstract: Among Ms. Mengers’s clients over the years were Barbra Streisand, Steve McQueen and Michael Caine.

name: Edgar M. Villchur
headline: Edgar M. Villchur, a Hi-Fi Innovator, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Mr. Villchur invented the AR-1 loudspeaker, which produced high-fidelity bass tones and was a quarter of the size of the speakers on the market.

name: Elouise Cobell
profession: Sued U.S. Over Indian Trust Funds
headline: Elouise Cobell, 65, Dies; Sued U.S. Over Indian Trust Funds
abstract: A $3.4 billion settlement was reached after Ms. Cobell, as the lead plaintiff, filed a lawsuit alleging federal mismanagement of Indian trust funds since the late 1800s.

name: Anita Caspary
headline: Anita Caspary, Nun Who Led Breakaway From Church, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Caspary, who went by her religious name, Mother Humiliata, led the largest single exodus of nuns from the Roman Catholic Church in American history.

name: Harold Leppo
headline: Harold Leppo, a President of Lord & Taylor, Dies at 74
abstract: While Mr. Leppo was the president of the department store, the company grew from 19 stores in one region to 46 stores nationwide.

name: Peter Mullen
profession: Power at a Leading Law Firm
headline: Peter Mullen, Power at a Leading Law Firm, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Mullen, a lawyer, drove the law firm of Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom from a small, specialized firm to a fixture in the top tier of the corporate bar.

name: Pete Rugolo
headline: Pete Rugolo, Arranger and Composer, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Mr. Rugolo was the chief arranger for the Stan Kenton Orchestra in its late-1940s heyday and a prolific composer and arranger for television and film.

name: Ingvar Wixell
headline: Ingvar Wixell, Swedish Baritone, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Wixell’s vivid performances in the Italian repertory made him a respected fixture on the world’s opera stages.

name: Barbara Kent
headline: Barbara Kent, Star of Silent Movies, Dies at 103
abstract: Ms. Kent was a silent-film star who transitioned easily into the talkies.

name: Piri Thomas
headline: Piri Thomas, Spanish Harlem Author, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Thomas’s 1967 memoir, “Down These Mean Streets,” became a classic portrait of ghetto life.

name: Norman Corwin
headline: Norman Corwin, Pioneer of Radio, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Corwin was best known for his dramatizations of American history, vivid human-interest reports from abroad during World War II, adaptations of American literary works and dozens of radio plays.

name: Matthew G. Martinez
headline: Matthew G. Martinez, Ex-Democratic Lawmaker, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Martinez was a party-line Democrat until he was defeated in a primary and switched to the Republican Party for his last months in office.

name: Muammar el-Qaddafi
profession: Brutal and Defiant to the End
headline: An Erratic Leader, Brutal and Defiant to the End
abstract: Throughout his rule, Colonel Qaddafi, 69, sanctioned spasms of violence and bedlam, as he sought to leverage Libya’s oil wealth into an outsize role on the world stage.

name: Morris Chafetz
headline: Morris Chafetz, 87, Dies; Altered View of Alcoholism
abstract: Dr. Chafetz played an important role in changing the perception of alcoholism from social crime or personal failing to a disease requiring treatment.

name: Barry Feinstein
headline: Barry Feinstein, Photographer of Defining Rock Portraits, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Feinstein’s images were the centerpieces of albums by Bob Dylan, Janis Joplin and George Harrison, among others.

name: Barry Feinstein
profession: Once a Labor Union Power in New York
headline: Barry Feinstein, Once a Labor Union Power in New York, Dies at 87
abstract: He used a small Teamsters local in the city to amass broad political influence over 25 years, only to be undone by corruption charges.

name: Manfred Gerlach
headline: Manfred Gerlach, East German Head of State, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Gerlach was a politician known for his support of liberal reforms and criticism of the Communist Party.

name: John M. Blum
headline: John M. Blum, Historian of Presidents, Dies at 90
abstract: Professor Blum’s 1954 biography of a maligned Theodore Roosevelt was pivotal in establishing the 26th president’s reputation as one of the country’s great chief executives.

name: Prince Sultan
headline: Prince Sultan bin Abdel Aziz of Saudi Arabia Dies
abstract: Prince Sultan was the heir apparent to the Saudi throne and one of the kingdom’s most powerful princes.

name: Paul Leka
profession: Songwriter of Na Na Hey Hey
headline: Paul Leka, a Songwriter of ‘Na Na Hey Hey,’ Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Leka was a songwriter and producer who was best known for helping to write “Na Na Hey Hey (Kiss Him Goodbye),” which has become a sports arena anthem.

name: Charles Hamm
headline: Charles Hamm, Author on American Popular Music, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Hamm, who became frustrated with the condescension of his fellow musicologists toward popular music, wrote two books that have become standard texts.

name: Robert Pierpoint
headline: Robert Pierpoint, 86, Dies; CBS News Correspondent
abstract: At CBS News, Robert Pierpoint brought a human touch to his coverage, which included the Korean War and six American presidencies.

name: Antonio Cassese
headline: Antonio Cassese, War Crimes Law Expert, Dies at 74
abstract: The founder of two war-crimes tribunals, Mr. Cassese played a vital role in creation of a modern system of international criminal justice.

name: Jerzy Bielecki
profession: Fell in Love in a Nazi Camp
headline: Jerzy Bielecki Dies at 90; Fell in Love in a Nazi Camp
abstract: For his daring rescue of a Jewish woman, Mr. Bielecki was recognized in 1985 as one of the so-called righteous gentiles by Yad Vashem, Israel’s center for Holocaust research and education.

name: Swami Bhaktipada
headline: Swami Bhaktipada, Ex-Hare Krishna Leader, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Bhaktipada, a charismatic spiritual leader, served eight years on charges connected to racketeering and murder for hire.

name: Herbert A. Hauptman
headline: Herbert A. Hauptman, Nobel Laureate, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Hauptman, a mathematician, shared the 1985 Nobel Prize in chemistry with Jerome Karle for their revolutionary methods of studying molecular structure.

name: Nusrat Bhutto
headline: Nusrat Bhutto, Political Force in Pakistan, Dies at 82
abstract: The mother and wife of prime ministers was an important figure in her own right.

name: Liviu Ciulei
headline: Liviu Ciulei, a Daring Theater Director, Dies at 88
abstract: The Romanian-born Mr. Ciulei was best known in the United States for leading the Guthrie Theater in Minneapolis and for productions at Arena Stage in Washington.

name: Daniel B. Burke
headline: Daniel B. Burke, Leading Media Executive, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Burke helped engineer the acquisition of the American Broadcasting Company by Capital Cities, one of the boldest corporate takeovers of the 1980s.

name: George L. Sherry
profession: Envoy and Well-Known Voice at U.N
headline: George L. Sherry, Envoy and Well-Known Voice at U.N., Dies at 87
abstract: In the years just after the founding of the United Nations in 1945, Mr. Sherry became known as the English-speaking voice of Andrei Y. Vishinsky, the Soviet delegate.

name: Florence Parry Heide
headline: Florence Parry Heide, Children’s Writer and Poet, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Heide’s prose and poetry, which included books for girls adjusting to adolescence, mysteries and sports stories, were often enhanced with drawings by famed illustrators.

name: James Hillman
headline: James Hillman, Therapist in Men’s Movement, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Hillman was a therapist and author whose theories helped revive interest in the ideas of Carl Jung and animated the so-called men’s movement in the 1990s.

name: Virginia Knauer
headline: Virginia Knauer, Consumer Advocate, Dies at 96
abstract: As head of the Office of Consumer Affairs under three presidents, Mrs. Knauer pushed for consumer protections, favoring persuasion over regulation.

name: Elizabeth Winship
headline: Elizabeth Winship Dies at 90; Advised Youths in ‘Ask Beth’
abstract: Thousands of youngsters — and sometimes their befuddled parents — sent letters to Mrs. Winship, seeking her solid, sympathetic and often witty advice.

name: William A. Niskanen
headline: William A. Niskanen, a Blunt Libertarian Economist, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Niskanen was fired by the Ford Motor Company for criticizing its embrace of trade protection and later was an adviser to President Ronald Reagan.

name: Dean Brackley
headline: Rev. Dean Brackley, 65, Dies; Served in El Salvador
abstract: The Jesuit priest moved to the San Salvador university dormitory where six priests and two women were murdered by government forces in 1989.

name: Howard Wolpe
headline: Howard Wolpe, Backer of ’86 Anti-Apartheid Act, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Wolpe played a key role in passing legislation that imposed economic sanctions on South Africa, despite two vetoes by President Ronald Reagan.

name: Bob Beaumont
headline: Bob Beaumont, Who Popularized Electric Cars, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Beaumont, appalled by the United States’ appetite for oil, sold some 2,000 electric cars, decades before General Motors and Nissan created their own versions.

name: Ruby Cohn
headline: Ruby Cohn, Writer and Expert on Beckett, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Cohn, a theater scholar and drama professor, became the playwright Samuel Beckett’s friend as well as a leading authority on his work.

name: Robert A. Pritzker
headline: Robert A. Pritzker Dies at 85; Led Family Business
abstract: Mr. Pritzker and his two brothers built a conglomerate that included the Hyatt hotel chain. A family dispute led to the sale of much of the business.

name: Tom McNeeley
headline: Tom McNeeley, Challenger to Patterson, Is Dead at 74
abstract: McNeeley fought professionally from 1958 to 1966, compiling a respectable 37-14 record with 28 knockouts, but became known for his losses, including a knockout loss to Floyd Patterson.

name: Joyce Clifford
headline: Joyce Clifford, Who Pushed for ‘Primary Nursing’ Approach, Dies at 76
abstract: Dr. Clifford advocated a partnership of equals between doctors and nurses in patient care, and her ideas were adopted in some of the nation’s best hospitals.

name: Dorothy Rodham
profession: Mother and Mentor of Hillary Clinton
headline: Dorothy Rodham, Mother and Mentor of Hillary Clinton, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mrs. Rodham was a strong influence in the life of her daughter, the former first lady, senator from New York and candidate for the Democratic presidential nomination.

name: Gilbert Cates
headline: Gilbert Cates, Producer of Oscar Shows, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Cates was a director and producer who shaped Hollywood’s labor relations through the Directors Guild of America and its glamour scene through a record 14 Oscar telecasts.

name: Tom Keith
headline: Tom Keith, Creator of Radio Soundscapes, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Keith was a sound-effects man who conjured animals, gunshots, screeching tires, even a man falling into piranha-infested waters for “A Prairie Home Companion.”

name: Beryl Davis
headline: Beryl Davis, British Singer With Big Bands, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Davis, beloved in England for continuing her performances during the bombing of London during World War II, later performed with Sinatra and the big bands of Benny Goodman and Glenn Miller.

name: Yvonne McCain
profession: Plaintiff in Suit on Shelter for Homeless Families
headline: Yvonne McCain, Plaintiff in Suit on Shelter for Homeless Families, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. McCain’s case against New York City led to a ruling that children were subject “to inevitable emotional scarring because of the failure of city and state officials to provide emergency shelter.”

name: Jimmy Savile
headline: Jimmy Savile, TV Personality, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Savile was an acclaimed English television host whose dress, hair and verbal flummery made all other comers in a nation renowned for eccentrics look like Puritans.

name: Liz Anderson
headline: Liz Anderson, Who Wrote Hit Country Songs, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Anderson wrote songs and recorded her own tunes about faithless men and beleaguered women.

name: Allen J. Bernstein
headline: Allen J. Bernstein, Owner of Morton’s Steakhouses, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Bernstein started in fast food and eventually bought nine Morton’s steakhouses, then expanded the chain to 69 restaurants by the time he retired in 2005.

name: Matty Alou
headline: Matty Alou, Batting Champion for Pirates, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Alou once shared the San Francisco Giants’ outfield with his brothers Felipe and Jesús.

name: Ricky Wyatt
profession: Plaintiff in Landmark Mental Care Suit
headline: Ricky Wyatt, 57, Dies; Plaintiff in Landmark Mental Care Suit
abstract: A class-action federal lawsuit in which Mr. Wyatt was the lead plaintiff led to a judgment in 1971 that set national guidelines for mental care.

name: Mary Hunt Kahlenberg
headline: Mary Hunt Kahlenberg, Native-Textile Expert, Dies at 71
abstract: Ms. Kahlenberg’s 1972 traveling exhibition on Navajo blankets broke with tradition by presenting Navajo weaving as fine art.

name: John R. Opel
headline: John R. Opel, Who Made I.B.M. a Colossus, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Opel joined I.B.M. in 1949, as the computer age was dawning, and was the company’s chief executive from January 1981 until January 1985.

name: Cardinals’ Bob Forsch
headline: Cardinals’ Bob Forsch, Dies at 61; Pitched in 3 World Series
abstract: Bob Forsch was never an All-Star, but he won more games for St. Louis than anyone except the Hall of Famers Bob Gibson and Jesse Haines.

name: Sam Fink
profession: Letterer and Illustrator of Historical Texts
headline: Sam Fink, Letterer and Illustrator of Historical Texts, Dies at 95
abstract: In a series of publications, Mr. Fink inscribed, sketched and commented on the Declaration of Independence, the Constitution, the Gettysburg Address and the Book of Exodus.

name: Allen Mandelbaum
headline: Allen Mandelbaum, Translator of ‘Divine Comedy,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Mandelbaum’s fluid and sensitive English version of Dante’s “Divine Comedy” stamped his reputation as one of the world’s premier translators of Italian and classical poetry.

name: Leonard Stone
headline: Leonard Stone, Actor in ‘Willy Wonka,’ Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Stone was known for his role as Violet Beauregarde’s father in “Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory.”

name: Andy Rooney
headline: Andy Rooney, a Cranky Voice of CBS, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Rooney’s homespun commentary, which he delivered on “60 Minutes” every week from 1978 until 2011, made him a household name.

name: John F. Burke
headline: Dr. John F. Burke, Dies at 89; Created Synthetic Skin
abstract: Dr. Burke helped develop the first commercially-reproducible, synthetic human skin, saving the lives of innumerable severely burned people worldwide.

name: James Van Doren
headline: James Van Doren Dies at 72; Designer of Popular Shoes
abstract: The company’s shoes, known simply as Vans, were embraced by West Coast skateboarders in the 1970s and, with the help of a 1982 film, became a national fad.

name: Norman Ramsey
profession: Work Led to the Atomic Clock
headline: Norman Ramsey Dies at 96; Work Led to the Atomic Clock
abstract: Dr. Ramsey received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1989 for his invention of a laboratory technique to measure the frequencies of electromagnetic radiation most readily absorbed by atoms and molecules.

name: Phyllis Love
headline: Phyllis Love, Actress on Broadway Stage, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Love, who often played ingénues on Broadway in the 1950s, originated the part of Rosa in a Tennessee Williams play.

name: Sid Melton
profession: Comic Actor of Film and TV
headline: Sid Melton, Comic Actor of Film and TV, Dies at 94
abstract: In a career more than half a century long, Mr. Melton was best known for roles on the sitcoms “Make Room for Daddy” and “Green Acres.”

name: Theadora Van Runkle
headline: Theadora Van Runkle, Costume Designer, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Van Runkle, a self-taught costume designer who earned an Oscar nomination for her first picture, “Bonnie and Clyde,” was known for designs that combined Hollywood glamour with historical fealty.

name: David C. Utz
headline: David C. Utz, Surgeon Who Operated on Reagan, Dies at 87
abstract: President Ronald Reagan was only one of Dr. Utz’s numerous well-known patients, who included Justices Lewis F. Powell Jr. and Harry A. Blackmun as well as the Rev. Billy Graham,

name: Heavy D
headline: Heavy D, Smooth-Talking Hip-Hop Star, Dies at 44
abstract: Heavy D, whose real name was Dwight Errington Myers, rose to prominence as a rapper in the early 1990s with a style infused with a touch of R&B.

name: Hal Kanter
profession: Creator of Julia Series on TV
headline: Hal Kanter, a Creator of ‘Julia’ Series on TV, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Kanter, who won or shared three Emmys, was a creator of “Julia” starring Diahann Carroll, the first TV series about a black professional woman.

name: Margaret Field
headline: Margaret Field, TV Actress, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Field, who appeared in countless television shows in the 1950s and ’60s, was the mother of the Academy Award winner Sally Field.

name: Ed Macauley
headline: Ed Macauley, Basketball Hall of Famer, Dies at 83
abstract: The collegiate player of the year in 1949 and first N.B.A. All-Star Game M.V.P., he was traded from the Boston Celtics to the St. Louis Hawks for Bill Russell.

name: Hal Bruno
profession: Director of Election Coverage at ABC
headline: Hal Bruno, Director of Election Coverage at ABC, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Bruno was a political director who often appeared on the air as an analyst and hosted an interview program on ABC Radio.

name: Bil Keane
headline: Bil Keane, Creator of ‘The Family Circus,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Keane said the comics were “the last frontier of good, wholesome family humor and entertainment.”

name: Lou Maletta
headline: Lou Maletta, Gay-Television Pioneer, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Maletta’s network had its roots in a program showing gay pornographic movies but expanded to include news, entertainment, political and health programming.

name: Alan Mootnick
profession: Studied and Gave a Home to Gibbons
headline: Alan Mootnick, Who Studied and Gave a Home to Gibbons, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Mootnick was a champion of gibbons who worked to prevent their extinction and also felt a kinship with them.

name: Ed Pauls
headline: Ed Pauls, Developer of Indoor Skiing Machine, Dies at 80
abstract: An outdoorsman tired of running and slipping on icy Minnesota roads created the NordicTrack, a cross-country skiing simulator.

name: Annabelle Lyon
headline: Annabelle Lyon, Dancer for Balanchine, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Lyon danced with some of the most important companies in the formative years of 20th-century American ballet.

name: Morris Philipson
profession: Led the University of Chicago Press
headline: Morris Philipson, Who Led the University of Chicago Press, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Philipson steered the University of Chicago Press as it became one of the nation’s most important publishers of monumental scholarly works, modern fiction and postwar European philosophy.

name: Henry D. Owen
headline: Henry D. Owen, 91, Dies; Shaped Global Fiscal Order
abstract: Mr. Owen was an influential diplomat who helped institutionalize global economic summitry in the 1970s and was considered an intellectual framer of the Trilateral Commission.

name: Norton Dodge
headline: Norton Dodge Dies at 84; Stored Soviet Dissident Art
abstract: Mr. Dodge, an economics professor, made many trips to the Soviet Union during which he often collected nonconformist art under authentic cover of scholarly research.

name: Robert A. Scalapino
headline: Robert A. Scalapino, a Scholar of Asian Politics, Dies at 92
abstract: In 1965, Mr. Scalapino wound up arguing the Johnson administration’s case for escalating the war at what was billed as a national teach-in on Vietnam policy.

name: Evelyn H. Lauder
headline: Evelyn H. Lauder, Champion of Breast Cancer Research, Dies at 75
abstract: She married into an illustrious family in the beauty business.

name: Roger Christian
headline: Roger Christian, Olympic Hockey Star, Dies at 75
abstract: Christian’s four-goal game propelled the United States team to an improbable championship at the 1960 Squaw Valley Winter Games.

name: Barbara Grier
headline: Barbara Grier, Publisher of Lesbian Books, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Grier became a revered figure to several generations of lesbian writers and readers after founding Naiad Press in 1973 with three other women.

name: William Aramony
headline: William Aramony, United Way Leader Who Was Jailed for Fraud, Dies at 84
abstract: In 22 years as chief executive, Mr. Aramony turned a jumble of loose affiliates with many names and fund-raising aims into a charitable drive with a common name and a strategy.

name: H. Gobind Khorana
headline: H. Gobind Khorana, 89, Nobel-Winning Scientist, Dies
abstract: Dr. Khorana and two other RNA researchers were honored in 1968 for showing how genetic information is translated into proteins.

name: Les Daniels
headline: Les Daniels, Historian of Comic Books, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Daniels was among the earliest chroniclers of the artists and their creations, from Superman to Felix the Cat to Wonder Woman.

name: Irving H. Franklin
headline: Irving H. Franklin, 93, Dies; Improved Batters’ Grip
abstract: Working with the great Phillies third baseman Mike Schmidt, Mr. Franklin developed the batting gloves whose use spread through the major leagues and all levels of baseball.

name: Paul Epstein
headline: Dr. Paul Epstein, Expert in Public Health, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Dr. Epstein, of Harvard Medical School, was among the first to warn of a link between infectious disease and extreme weather events.

name: Donya Feuer
headline: Donya Feuer, Modern-Dance Choreographer, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Feuer, an American, became a close collaborator of Ingmar Bergman as well as a theater director and filmmaker.

name: Pat Passlof
headline: Pat Passlof, Abstract Expressionist Painter, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Passlof, who has a gallery show opening this Saturday in Chelsea, was known for her thick brush strokes and luminous color.

name: Ilya Zhitomirskiy
headline: Ilya Zhitomirskiy Dies at 22; Co-Founded Social Network
abstract: Mr. Zhitomirskiy was a co-founder of the social network Diaspora*, which has been described as the “anti-Facebook.”

name: Lee Pockriss
headline: Lee Pockriss, Songwriter Behind ‘Itsy Bitsy’ Bikini, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Pockriss, who wrote the music for midcentury pop hits like “Itsy Bitsy Teenie Weenie Yellow Polka Dot Bikini,” also worked in musical theater for decades.

name: Irwin Schneiderman
headline: Irwin Schneiderman Dies at 88; Guided the City Opera
abstract: Mr. Schneiderman, a lawyer and a philanthropic leader, guided the New York City Opera through two tumultuous decades.

name: Al Boeke
headline: Al Boeke, Architect Who Sought Ecological Harmony, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Boeke tried to blend homes into the landscape in places like Sonoma County, Calif., and Oahu in Hawaii.

name: Dulcie Gray
headline: Dulcie Gray, Stalwart British Actress, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Gray, who played numerous ladylike, suffering wives on stage, screen, radio and television, achieved renown acting alongside her husband, Michael Denison.

name: Jamie Pierre
profession: Free Skier Known for Feats of Daring
headline: Jamie Pierre, Free Skier Known for Feats of Daring, Dies at 38
abstract: Pierre was a professional big-mountain skier, and his monumental leap in the Teton Mountains in 2006 was considered to have set the world height record for a cliff jump on skis.

name: Richard H. Kuh
headline: Richard H. Kuh, Ex-Manhattan Prosecutor, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Kuh served as Manhattan district attorney in 1974 and jousted in celebrated cases with the likes of Lenny Bruce and Claus von Bülow.

name: Jon B. Lovelace
headline: Jon B. Lovelace, Mutual Fund Industry Leader, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Lovelace’s guidance helped the Capital Group’s American Funds brand become “the biggest money managers you’ve never heard of.”

name: René Morel
headline: René Morel, Master Restorer of Rare Violins, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Morel has been widely described as among the finest violin restorers — perhaps the very finest — of his day, a calling that requires in equal measure the skills of diagnostician, acoustician and microsurgeon.

name: Theodore J. Forstmann
headline: Theodore J. Forstmann, a Takeover Pioneer, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Forstmann, a colorful financier and philanthropist who helped to usher in the leveraged buyout industry, also inadvertently coined the phrase “barbarians at the gate.”

name: John G. Smale
headline: John G. Smale, Procter & Gamble Chief, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Smale was the chief executive of Procter & Gamble at a time of extraordinary growth, and he later helped lead a shake-up at General Motors.

name: Sanford Garelik
headline: Sanford Garelik, Former Mayoral Candidate, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Garelik became president of the New York City Council under Mayor John V. Lindsay in 1970 and mounted an unsuccessful bid to succeed Mr. Lindsay three years later.

name: Eva Monley
profession: Intrepid Scout for Film Locations in Africa
headline: Eva Monley, Intrepid Scout for Film Locations in Africa, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Monley worked on more than 60 movies, including “The African Queen” and “Out of Africa.”

name: John Neville
headline: John Neville, Shakespearean Actor and ‘Munchausen’ Star, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Neville may be best known in the United States as the title character in “The Adventures of Baron Munchausen.”

name: Moogy Klingman
profession: Songwriter and Original Member of Utopia
headline: Moogy Klingman, Songwriter and Original Member of Utopia, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Klingman was a keyboardist, songwriter and an original member of Todd Rundgren’s band Utopia.

name: Paul Motian
headline: Paul Motian, Jazz Drummer, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Mr. Motian, a drummer, bandleader, and composer of grace and abstraction, was one of the most influential jazz musicians of the last 50 years.

name: Eli Hurvitz
headline: Eli Hurvitz, Founder of Pharmaceutical Giant Teva, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Hurvitz began his career washing lab equipment at a drug company and went on to build Teva Pharmaceutical Industries into the largest generic drug maker in the world.

name: George Gallup Jr.
headline: George Gallup Jr., of Polling Family, Dies at 81
abstract: Following in his father’s path, Mr. Gallup used snapshots of political and religious views to capture the American mood.

name: Danielle Mitterrand
headline: Danielle Mitterrand, Former First Lady of France, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mrs. Mitterrand, whose husband, François, was France’s Socialist leader from 1981 to 1995, championed human rights causes.

name: Ruth Stone
headline: Ruth Stone, a Poet Celebrated Late in Life, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Stone won the National Book Award for a poetry collection in 2002 at the age of 87.

name: Anne McCaffrey
headline: Anne McCaffrey, Author of ‘Dragonriders’ Fantasies, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. McCaffrey married elements of fantasy to pure science fiction in her young-adult “Dragonriders of Pern” series set on the planet Pern, which Earthlings have settled.

name: Andrea True
headline: Andrea True, Singer of Disco Hit, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. True sang in nightclubs, wrote music for television commercials and, for a while, was an actress in adult films. Her famous song “More, More, More” described that life.

name: Shelagh Delaney
profession: Author of the Play A Taste of Honey
headline: Shelagh Delaney, Author of the Play ‘A Taste of Honey,’ Dies at 72
abstract: Ms. Delaney, whose play “A Taste of Honey” found success in the West End and on Broadway, was just 19 when the work was first performed.

name: Christopher Ma
headline: Christopher Ma, Washington Post Executive, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Ma was the Post Company’s senior vice president for new business development and publisher of Express, the company’s free commuter tabloid newspaper for the Washington area.

name: Lynn Margulis
headline: Lynn Margulis, Evolution Theorist, Dies at 73
abstract: Dr. Margulis was a biologist whose work on the origin of cells helped transform the study of evolution.

name: Olga Bloom
headline: Olga Bloom, Violinist and Violist Who Created Bargemusic, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Bloom was responsible for converting an old coffee barge into a floating stage and one of the more magical places in New York’s classical music scene.

name: Tom Wicker
headline: Tom Wicker, Times Journalist, Dies at 85
abstract: Made prominent by his coverage of the Kennedy assassination, Mr. Wicker became Washington bureau chief for The New York Times and an iconoclastic columnist.

name: Jeno Paulucci
headline: Jeno Paulucci, a Pioneer of Ready-Made Ethnic Foods, Dies at 93
abstract: The son of Italian immigrants, Mr. Paulucci founded Chun King, Jeno’s and Michelina’s.

name: Sena Jurinac
headline: Sena Jurinac, Longtime Soprano in Vienna, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Jurinac was a graceful singer with a penetrating voice who was a star of postwar Europe.

name: Maurice Chase
headline: Rev. Maurice Chase, ‘Father Dollar Bill,’ Dies at 92
abstract: Father Chase was known on Los Angeles Skid Row for handing out about $3,000 a week, often in singles.

name: Jimmy Norman
headline: Jimmy Norman, R&B Singer Who Worked With Marley and Hendrix, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Norman was a rhythm-and-blues singer and songwriter who worked with Bob Marley and Jimi Hendrix in their early careers.

name: Odumegwu Ojukwu
headline: Odumegwu Ojukwu, Breakaway Biafra Leader, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Ojukwu proclaimed the Republic of Biafra in 1967, in a separation from Nigeria, leading to a war that cost more than a million lives.

name: Basil D’Oliveira
profession: Symbol for Cricket and for Equality
headline: Basil D’Oliveira, a Symbol for Cricket and for Equality, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. D’Oliveira’s struggles to become a high-level cricket player in a country of government-enforced racial segregation became a powerful symbol in the ultimately successful fight against apartheid.

name: Sergio Scaglietti
headline: Sergio Scaglietti, Sculptor of Sleekly Tailored Ferraris, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Scaglietti built the bodies of elegant Ferraris like the 250 Testa Rossa and 500 Mondial.

name: Montserrat Figueras
headline: Montserrat Figueras, Catalan Soprano, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Figueras and her husband, Jordi Savall, created ensembles that revitalized the performance of early music.

name: Ron Lyle
headline: Ron Lyle, Who Met Ali for Title, Dies at 70
abstract: After learning to box while in prison for murder, Lyle lost a title bout to Muhammad Ali and fought a memorably furious battle with George Foreman.

name: Francis H. Cabot
headline: Francis H. Cabot, 86, Dies; Created Notable Gardens
abstract: A financier and self-taught horticulturist, Mr. Cabot founded the Garden Conservancy, which works to preserve America’s greatest private gardens.

name: I. Michael Heyman
headline: I. Michael Heyman, Smithsonian Leader, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Heyman, a former chancellor of the University of California, Berkeley, presided over the Smithsonian during a controversy involving its display of the Enola Gay on the 50th anniversary of its bombing of Hiroshima.

name: Vasily Alekseyev
headline: Vasily Alekseyev, 69, Champion Weight Lifter, Dies
abstract: Alekseyev, known as the world’s strongest man, won two Olympic gold medals and set 80 world records in weight lifting.

name: Ken Russell
headline: Ken Russell, Director Fond of Provocation, Dies at 84
abstract: A polarizing figure who delighted in breaching the limits of propriety and cinematic good taste, Mr. Russell courted controversy through much of his career.

name: Lana Peters
headline: Lana Peters, Stalin’s Daughter, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Peters’s death, like the last years of her life, occurred away from public view.

name: Gary Speed
headline: Gary Speed, Welsh National Soccer Coach, Dies at 42
abstract: Before helping to lift Wales in the world rankings, Speed was a steady and skilled player in the top divisions of English soccer for more than 20 years.

name: Michael Hastings
headline: Michael Hastings, British Playwright, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Hastings’s best-known work, “Tom and Viv,” about the first marriage of T. S. Eliot, created a cultural brouhaha.

name: Michael Hastings
headline: Michael Hastings, 33, Winner of Polk Award, Dies
abstract: Mr. Hastings, an intrepid war zone reporter in Afghanistan and Iraq, won a Polk Award in 2010 for his Rolling Stone magazine cover story, “The Runaway General.”

name: Barry Llewellyn
headline: Barry Llewellyn, a Founder of the Heptones, Dies at 63
abstract: Founded by Mr. Llewellyn and Earl Morgan, the Heptones rose from singing on the streets of Trenchtown to take their place alongside the Wailers and the Maytals as one of Jamaica’s most important vocal groups.

name: Don DeVito
headline: Don DeVito, Producer of Bob Dylan Albums, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. DeVito’s work with Mr. Dylan was part of a career that lasted four decades at the Columbia label.

name: Patrice O’Neal
headline: Patrice O’Neal, Boisterous Comedian, Dies at 41
abstract: Mr. O’Neal was a stand-up comedian who took on topics like race, AIDS and his own struggle with diabetes.

name: Matthew P. Sapolin
headline: Matthew P. Sapolin, Who Led Bloomberg’s Office for Disabled, Dies at 41
abstract: Mr. Sapolin, who was blind, was also an accomplished wrestler, versatile musician, formidable chess player and occasional skier.

name: Andrew M. Kramer
headline: Andrew M. Kramer, Leading Labor Lawyer, Dies at 67
abstract: A sought-after negotiator, Mr. Kramer’s clients included General Motors, Westinghouse Electric and the Boston Red Sox.

name: Andrew Kazdin
headline: Andrew Kazdin, Record Producer, Dies at 77
