abstract: Mr. Kazdin, who insisted that the details of a work be heard clearly, revolutionized classical recording by using techniques more common to popular music.

name: Frederik Meijer
headline: Frederik Meijer, Grocery Store Pioneer, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Meijer’s stores throughout the Midwest predated Wal-Mart with their broad range of products and discount prices.

name: Judy Lewis
headline: Judy Lewis, Secret Daughter of Hollywood, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Lewis, the daughter of an unwed Loretta Young and Clark Gable, was 31 before she confronted her mother and learned the truth of her upbringing.

name: Ante Markovic
headline: Ante Markovic, Last Premier of Yugoslavia, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Markovic resigned in December 1991 as his nation broke apart, nearly three years after he became prime minister.

name: Louis Silverstein
profession: Gave a Bolder and Airier Look to The Times
headline: Louis Silverstein, Who Gave a Bolder and Airier Look to The Times, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Silverstein helped devise a bigger, more visually expansive New York Times and in doing so, influenced the redesign of newspapers from coast to coast.

name: François Lesage
headline: François Lesage, Who Led Embroidery Atelier, Dies at 82
abstract: For more than half a century, Mr. Lesage led the embroidery atelier that has served couture designers from Charles Frederick Worth through Karl Lagerfeld of Chanel.

name: Christa Wolf
headline: Christa Wolf Dies at 82; Wrote of the Germanys
abstract: Ms. Wolf, a leading writer from the former East Germany, explored the weight of history on ordinary people as well as her own struggles with Nazism and life in a Communist society.

name: Manuel Gilman
headline: Manuel Gilman, Influential Racetrack Veterinarian, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Gilman’s procedure for examining thoroughbred racehorses in New York became standard at racetracks around the country, improving safety for horses and jockeys.

name: Alan Sues
headline: Alan Sues, a ‘Laugh-In’ Cast Mainstay, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Sues, whose acting career began onstage with dramatic roles, played over-the-top characters like Uncle Al the Kiddies’ Pal on the 1960s hit variety-comedy show.

name: Jim Rathmann
headline: Jim Rathmann, 1960 Indianapolis 500 Winner, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Rathmann once held the record for fastest winning speed and parlayed his driving success into a Chevrolet-Cadillac dealership that leased cars to astronauts at virtually no cost.

name: Zdenek Miler
headline: Zdenek Miler, Creator of Krtek the Mole, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Miler’s cartoons drew audiences in more than 80 countries, though Krtek, a Czech native, never caught on in the United States.

name: William L. Waller
headline: William L. Waller, Ex-Governor of Mississippi, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Waller tried twice in 1964 to convict the segregationist Byron De La Beckwith of murdering the civil rights leader Medgar Evers, and in 1971 forged a coalition of poor whites and newly enfranchised blacks to become governor.

name: T. Franklin Williams
headline: T. Franklin Williams, Early Geriatric Specialist, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Williams was a former director of the National Institute on Aging and a longtime professor at the University of Rochester.

name: Betty Haas Pfister
headline: Betty Haas Pfister, a Woman With Wings, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Haas Pfister served as a member of the Women Airforce Service Pilots, or WASPs, in World War II, and her passion for flight never faded.

name: Sócrates
headline: Sócrates, Brazilian Soccer Star and Activist, Dies at 57
abstract: Sócrates Brasileiro Sampaio de Souza Vieira de Oliveira transcended the sport through his involvement in Brazil’s pro-democracy movement.

name: Lloyd Old
profession: Champion of Using Cells to Fight Cancer
headline: Lloyd J. Old, Champion of Using Cells to Fight Cancer, Dies at 78
abstract: Dr. Old made seminal discoveries about the relationship between cancer and the immune system and promoted the development of vaccines that use the body’s ability to fight disease.

name: Judd Woldin
headline: Judd Woldin, ‘Raisin’ Score Composer, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Woldin also traveled with the Ink Spots and Lionel Hampton, and played in the “Hello, Dolly!” orchestra on Broadway.

name: Patricia C. Dunn
headline: Patricia C. Dunn Dies at 58; Led H.P. During Spying Case
abstract: Ms. Dunn’s career was eclipsed by her involvement in an attempt at Hewlett-Packard to stop boardroom leaks by spying on directors, journalists and employees.

name: Hubert Sumlin
headline: Hubert Sumlin, Master of Blues Guitar, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Sumlin, who was best known for his blues with Howlin’ Wolf, inspired countless rockers including Jimmy Page and Eric Clapton.

name: Bill McKinney
headline: Bill McKinney, Actor in ‘Deliverance,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. McKinney acted in several Clint Eastwood films and various television shows.

name: Khan
headline: Sultan Khan, Indian Classical Musician, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Khan was the heir to multiple generations of his family’s style of improvising on the sarangi, the instrument of “a hundred singing colors.”

name: Khan
headline: Overlooked No More: Sultan Khan, Untrained Chess Player Who Became a Champion
abstract: He beat some of the world’s top players despite growing up with little access to chess books and not having the same knowledge his rivals possessed.

name: Elisabeth Young-Bruehl
profession: Probed Roots of Ideology and Bias
headline: Elisabeth Young-Bruehl, Who Probed Roots of Ideology and Bias, Dies at 65
abstract: Ms. Young-Bruehl was a philosopher, psychoanalyst and biographer known for her lives of two influential women, Hannah Arendt and Anna Freud.

name: Dev Anand
headline: Dev Anand, Bollywood Star, Producer and Director, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Anand and his older brother started their own production company, Navketan, which hired many actors and directors who were to shape Hindi cinema.

name: Leo Friedman
headline: Leo Friedman, Photographer of Broadway’s Glamour Years, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Friedman was a ubiquitous presence in and around New York theaters in the 1950s and 1960s

name: Paul Doty
headline: Paul Doty, Biochemist and Arms Control Advocate, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Doty was one of the scientists who worked out how to take apart and reassemble DNA, a discovery that became a foundation of modern molecular biology.

name: Harry Morgan
headline: Harry Morgan, Colonel Potter on ‘M*A*S*H,’ Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Morgan, an Emmy winner on TV, also appeared in more than 100 movies.

name: Dobie Gray
headline: Dobie Gray, Singer Known for ‘Drift Away,’ Dies
abstract: Mr. Gray was a versatile singer and songwriter who was probably best known for his 1973 soul anthem, “Drift Away.”

name: Dugald Stermer
headline: Dugald Stermer, Illustrator and Ramparts Art Director, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Stermer was an illustrator who achieved renown and sometimes angered the government as the art director of the influential left-wing magazine Ramparts in the 1960s.

name: Marion Dougherty
headline: Marion Dougherty, Hollywood Star-Maker, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Dougherty, who cast some of Hollywood’s biggest stars in their earliest parts, including Al Pacino and Dustin Hoffman, had a strong hand in reshaping the way Hollywood casts films.

name: Jerry Robinson
headline: Jerry Robinson, Godfather of a Comic-Book Villain, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Robinson was a prolific comic-book artist, comics historian and editorial cartoonist who is credited with having created the Joker, the archenemy of Batman.

name: Joseph E. Robert Jr.
headline: Joseph E. Robert Jr., Investor in Real Estate, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Robert had talent for turning troubled properties into profits, including billions of dollars worth of assets from the collapse of the savings and loan industry in the 1980s.

name: David Montgomery
headline: David Montgomery, 84, Dies; Chronicled Lives of Workers
abstract: Mr. Montgomery was a labor historian whose experience as a machinist informed his influential writing about the culture of the factory floor.

name: Muriel Petioni
headline: Muriel Petioni, 97, Prominent Harlem Physician, Dies
abstract: Called “the mother of medicine in Harlem,” Dr. Petioni was a leader of many community organizations promoting health care, housing development and education.

name: Bob Burnett
headline: Bob Burnett, 71, Performer in the Original Highwaymen, Dies
abstract: Mr. Burnett, known for his smooth tenor, was one of the founding members of the folk-revival group the Highwaymen.

name: Christopher Logue
headline: Christopher Logue Dies at 85; Modernized the ‘Iliad’
abstract: Mr. Logue was a poet, actor, soldier and ice-cream bandit in 85 colorful years.

name: Oscar Griffin Jr.
headline: Oscar Griffin Jr., 78, Pulitzer Prize Winner Who Brought Down Scheming Texas Tycoon, Dies
abstract: Mr. Griffin unraveled an elaborate fraud scheme in four articles that earned him a Pulitzer Prize for distinguished local reporting at age 29.

name: Philip Burrell
headline: Philip Burrell, Influential Jamaican Record Producer, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Burrell was one of the most prolific Jamaican record producers of the last 20 years, but his most important achievement was upholding the music’s great sonic and spiritual traditions.

name: Joseph Chamberlain
profession: Brought the Stars a Bit Closer
headline: Joseph Chamberlain, 88, Dies; Brought the Stars a Bit Closer
abstract: Dr. Chamberlain spent nearly four decades leading planetariums in New York and Chicago into a new era of technology, instruction and visitor experience.

name: Joe Restic
headline: Joe Restic, 85, an Innovator in Football at Harvard, Dies
abstract: Restic devised a complex offense known as the multiflex in Canada and later became the longest-serving football coach at Harvard.

name: Bill Tapia
headline: Bill Tapia, Virtuoso Ukulele Player, Dies at 103
abstract: Mr. Tapia was a premier musician from Honolulu who switched to guitar to play jazz and was then “discovered” as the ukulele had a recent resurgence.

name: Clive Robbins
profession: Developer of a Method of Music Therapy
headline: Clive Robbins, Developer of a Method of Music Therapy, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Robbins, with Paul Nordoff, designed a brand of music therapy for hard-to-reach children that is now used to help people with autism, stroke and Alzheimer’s disease.

name: John P. Foley
headline: Cardinal John P. Foley, 76, Vatican Spokesman, Dies
abstract: Cardinal Foley heeded God’s “whisper” to become a priest as well as his own inclinations to go to journalism school, then combined the roles as the Vatican’s communications director.

name: Park Tae-joon
profession: Founder of a Giant in Steel
headline: Park Tae-joon, Founder of a Giant in Steel, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Tae-joon, a former general, created Posco, one of the world’s largest steel companies and a driver of South Korea’s rise as an industrial power.

name: J. Lynn Helms
headline: J. Lynn Helms, Who Led the F.A.A., Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Helms, a decorated pilot, helped restore the nation’s crippled air traffic control system under President Reagan, but later resigned under a cloud after charges of unethical behavior.

name: Bert Schneider
headline: Bert Schneider, Producer Whose Films Reflected an Era, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Schneider’s films, like “Easy Rider” and “The Last Picture Show,” helped define the social unrest of the late 1960s and early ’70s.

name: Erica Wilson
headline: Erica Wilson Dies at 83; Led a Rebirth of Needleworking
abstract: Ms. Wilson built a public career as a teacher of the domestic arts that paralleled that of Julia Child.

name: Stephen Schlossberg
profession: Official of U.A.W. and Labor Dept
headline: Stephen Schlossberg, Official of U.A.W. and Labor Dept., Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Schlossberg was the general counsel of the United Automobile Workers and a top official in the Labor Department under President Ronald Reagan.

name: George Whitman
headline: George Whitman, Paris Bookseller and Cultural Beacon, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Mr. Whitman, the American-born owner of Shakespeare & Company in Paris, believed that “the book business is the business of life.”

name: Russell Hoban
headline: Russell Hoban, ‘Frances’ Author, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Hoban, a prolific author, created the “Frances” series of children’s books and the “Riddley Walker” science-fiction novel for adults.

name: Anthony Amato
headline: Anthony Amato, Founder of Amato Opera, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Amato’s opera company, Amato Opera, was long the brightest star in the constellation of semiprofessional opera companies spread over the city — the Off Broadway of the opera world.

name: Robert Lawrence Balzer
headline: Robert Lawrence Balzer, Wine Writer, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Balzer was an early champion of American wines and a widely read critic of them for more than 60 years as a journalist and author.

name: Boris Chertok
headline: Boris Chertok, Engineer With Russian Space Program, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Chertok was a rocket engineer who played a central role in designing the navigation systems for Soviet spacecraft during the race to the moon, among them the one that carried the first human into space.

name: Joe Simon
headline: Joe Simon, a Creator of Captain America, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Mr. Simon’s superhero Captain America was conceived out of a patriotic impulse in the years leading up to World War II.

name: Edie Stevenson
headline: Edie Stevenson Dies at 81; Wrote ‘Let’s Get Mikey’ Ad
abstract: Ms. Stevenson, a divorced mother of four, was the creative mind behind the television spot advertising Life cereal, which ran for more than a decade.

name: Mark Goldweber
headline: Mark Goldweber, Leading Dancer With Joffrey, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Goldweber won wide acclaim as the Blue Skater in Frederick Ashton’s ballet “Patineurs.”

name: Christopher Hitchens
headline: Christopher Hitchens, Polemicist Who Slashed All, Freely, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Hitchens wrote in the tradition of Thomas Paine and George Orwell and trained his sights on targets as various as Henry Kissinger, the British monarchy and Mother Teresa.

name: Billie Jo Spears
headline: Billie Jo Spears, Country Singer, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Spears, best known for “Blanket on the Ground,” a No. 1 country hit in 1975, sang songs with strong women as their protagonists.

name: Holden Withington
headline: Holden Withington, Last Living B-52 Designer, Dies at 94
abstract: It takes a vast team to design a complex airplane, particularly one like the B-52 Stratofortress. Mr. Withington played down the achievement.

name: Henry Lafont
headline: Henry Lafont, Pilot, Dies at 91; Fought in Battle of Britain
abstract: Mr. Lafont made a harrowing escape to answer General de Gaulle’s call for a crusade against Germany.

name: Paula E. Hyman
profession: Sought Rights for Women in Judaism
headline: Paula E. Hyman, Who Sought Rights for Women in Judaism, Dies at 65
abstract: Ms. Hyman’s work was seminal in creating a field of historical study — part women’s history, part Jewish history, part history of immigration in America.

name: Vaclav Havel
headline: Vaclav Havel, Former Czech President, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Havel’s eloquent dissections of Communist rule helped to destroy it in revolutions that brought down the Berlin Wall and swept him into power.

name: Cesária Évora
headline: Cesária Évora, Singer From Cape Verde, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Évora, a singer in the style called morna, brought the music of the tiny Cape Verde islands to a worldwide audience.

name: Bonnie Prudden
headline: Bonnie Prudden, 97, Dies; Promoted Fitness for TV Generation
abstract: Ms. Prudden helped write a report to President Eisenhower that led to the formation of the President’s Council on Youth Fitness.

name: Bob Brookmeyer
headline: Bob Brookmeyer, Jazz Musician and Educator, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Brookmeyer left a distinctive mark on jazz as a musician, composer and arranger, and as an educator.

name: Kim Jong-il
headline: Kim Jong-il, Dictator Who Turned North Korea Into a Nuclear State, Dies
abstract: Mr. Kim remained an unknowable figure but fostered perhaps the last personality cult in the Communist world.

name: Warren Hellman
headline: Warren Hellman, 77, Investor Who Loved Bluegrass, Dies
abstract: Mr. Hellman, the former president of Lehman Brothers, also financed the annual Hardly Strictly Bluegrass festival in San Francisco.

name: Dan Frazer
headline: Dan Frazer, Fretful Supervisor on ‘Kojak,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Frazer’s upbringing in Hell’s Kitchen prepared him for a long run of roles as a blue-collar type or a cop, most notably the beleaguered supervising officer Capt. Frank McNeil on “Kojak.”

name: Ralph MacDonald
headline: Ralph MacDonald, Pop Percussionist, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. MacDonald was a Grammy winner and a co-writer of the huge hit “Where Is the Love?”

name: Norman Krim
headline: Norman Krim, Who Championed the Transistor, Dies at 98
abstract: Working for Raytheon, Mr. Krim first put transistors into hearing aids. He later had a hand in the early growth of the RadioShack chain.

name: Gene Summers
headline: Gene Summers, Modernist Architect, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Summers worked with the Modernist master Mies van der Rohe before leaving the practice; his own projects included the McCormick Place convention center in Chicago.

name: John Chamberlain
profession: Wrested Rough Magic From Scrap Metal
headline: John Chamberlain, Who Wrested Rough Magic From Scrap Metal, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Chamberlain almost singlehandedly gave automotive metal a place in the history of sculpture.

name: Jacob Goldman
headline: Jacob Goldman, Founder of Xerox Lab, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Goldman, a physicist, persuaded Xerox to build a research center in Palo Alto, Calif., where significant computing technologies were invented.

name: Henry E. Catto Jr.
headline: Henry E. Catto Jr., Who Served 4 Presidents, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Catto’s was director of the United States Information Agency, a chief Pentagon spokesman and ambassador to Britain and El Salvador.

name: Don Sharp
headline: Don Sharp Dies at 89; Director Who Revived Hammer Horror Film Company
abstract: Mr. Sharp made “The Kiss of the Vampire,” considered by some to be one of the greatest Gothic horror movies ever made, and a remake of “The Thirty-Nine Steps,” among others.

name: Doe Avedon
headline: Doe Avedon, Fashion Model and Actress, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Avedon’s story inspired the musical “Funny Face.”

name: James Ramseur
headline: James Ramseur, Wounded in ’84 Subway Shooting, Dies at 45
abstract: Mr. Ramseur was one of four teenagers shot by Bernard H. Goetz in a case that engendered a furious public discourse about crime, self-defense and race.

name: Wolfgang Oehme
headline: Wolfgang Oehme, a Free-Form Landscape Architect, Dies at 81
abstract: For 30 years, Mr. Oehme, with James van Sweden, developed self-sustaining gardens, free of pesticides, that could remain beautiful even as the seasons changed.

name: Robert Easton
headline: Robert Easton, Hollywood’s Henry Higgins, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Easton was the entertainment industry’s dean of dialects as well as an actor on radio and television and in the movies.

name: Paul-Emile Deiber
headline: Paul-Emile Deiber, Actor Who Became an Opera Director, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Deiber was an actor and director with the Comédie-Française for nearly three decades who brought his dramatic expertise to a second career as an opera director.

name: Pupi Campo
profession: Cuban Bandleader and the Rumba Maestro
headline: Pupi Campo, Cuban Bandleader and ‘the Rumba Maestro,’ Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Campo provided comedy and brought rippling syncopation to Jack Paar’s “Morning Show” in the 1950s.

name: Robert Morvillo
headline: Robert Morvillo, Legal Pioneer, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Morvillo was a prominent New York trial lawyer who pioneered the practice of white-collar criminal defense and whose client list included the rich and famous.

name: Robert Ader
headline: Robert Ader, Who Linked Stress and Illness, Dies at 79
abstract: Dr. Ader’s findings, now widely accepted, contradicted a previous principle of biochemistry that the immune system was autonomous.

name: Joseph Farrell
profession: Used Market Research to Shape Films
headline: Joseph Farrell, Who Used Market Research to Shape Films, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Farrell was widely credited with expanding the use of opinion-tracking strategies for all the major studios in Hollywood, thus helping to transform how the industry thought about audiences.

name: Andrew Geller
headline: Andrew Geller, Modernist Architect, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Geller designed the “typical American house” for the American National Exhibition in Moscow in 1959 and created a line of vacation homes that were sold at Macy’s in Herald Square in the 1960s.

name: Lynn Samuels
headline: Lynn Samuels, a Brash Radio Talker, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Samuels made her name on WABC radio in the 1980s and ’90s as the voice of liberalism in a lineup composed mainly of right-leaning men.

name: Helen Frankenthaler
headline: Helen Frankenthaler, Abstract Painter Who Shaped a Movement, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Frankenthaler, whose staining technique was essential to the development of Color Field painting, was one of the most admired artists of her generation.

name: Sam Rivers
headline: Sam Rivers, Jazz Artist of Loft Scene, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Rivers, with a taut and throaty sound on his tenor saxophone, was among the pioneers in the postwar jazz avant-garde.

name: Sam Rivers
headline: Sam Rivers, Bassist for Limp Bizkit, Dies at 48
abstract: As a founding member of the band, he helped it achieve mainstream success.

name: Bettye Danoff
headline: Bettye Danoff, Founding Member of L.P.G.A., Dies at 88
abstract: Known as Mighty Mite, Danoff was a top amateur golfer before turning pro in 1949 and starting the Ladies Professional Golf Association with 12 others in 1950.

name: Adrienne Cooper
headline: Adrienne Cooper, Yiddish Singer, Dies at 65
abstract: Ms. Cooper was a curator and teacher who helped nurture the survival of a fading language.

name: Satyadev Dubey
headline: Satyadev Dubey, Playwright Who Modernized Hindi Theater, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Dubey revived the Hindi theater and enabled it to compete with the English-language theater that once dominated in India.

name: Evelyn Handler
headline: Evelyn Handler Dies at 78; Led Two Universities
abstract: Dr. Handler was at the center of a debate over the Jewish identity of Brandeis University.

name: Constantine Sidamon-Eristoff
headline: Constantine Sidamon-Eristoff, Environmental Advocate, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Sidamon-Eristoff, a prince of Georgian descent who grew up in New York City and the Hudson Valley, was a watchdog in posts in and out of government.

name: Kim Geun-tae
headline: Kim Geun-tae, South Korean Democracy Activist, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Kim suffered brutal torture as a dissident during South Korea’s military dictatorship, later rising to political prominence following the advent of democracy.

name: Don Mueller
headline: Don Mueller, Giants Outfielder, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Mueller, a singles hitter, helped set up Bobby Thomson’s 1951 pennant-winning home run and led the National League with 212 hits in 1954.

name: Eva Zeisel
headline: Eva Zeisel, Ceramic Artist and Designer, Dies at 105
abstract: In her dinnerware and vases, Ms. Zeisel applied modernist principles that fed a desire for less formal styles of living and objects of beauty and utility.

name: Sean Collins
headline: Sean Collins, Who Used Science to Help Surfers, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Collins created Surfline.com, whose forecasts and real-time views of beaches reach 1.5 million surfers a week.

name: Emmett L. Bennett Jr.
headline: Emmett L. Bennett Jr., Expert on Ancient Script, Dies at 93
abstract: Professor Bennett played a vital role in deciphering Linear B, the Bronze Age Aegean script that defied solution for more than 50 years.

name: Simms Taback
headline: Simms Taback, Author of Wry Children’s Books, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Taback won the Caldecott Medal in 2000 for his adaptation of the Yiddish folktale “Joseph Had a Little Overcoat.”

name: Barbara Lea
headline: Barbara Lea, Cabaret Singer, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Lea was a jazz-influenced cabaret singer known for her subtle interpretations of classic American popular songs.

name: Howard Halpern
headline: Howard Halpern, Therapist and Self-Help Author, Dies at 82
abstract: Dr. Halpern practiced for more than 50 years and wrote several books focusing on family and other relationships.

name: Johnny Wilson
headline: Johnny Wilson, N.H.L. Star, Dies at 82; Held Consecutive-Game Record
abstract: Wilson won four Stanley Cups with the Detroit Red Wings in the 1950s and set an N.H.L. record by appearing in 580 consecutive games.

name: Bob Anderson
headline: Bob Anderson, Sword Master, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Anderson fenced for England in the Olympics, created some of Hollywood’s greatest sword fights with actors from Errol Flynn to Antonio Banderas, and appeared on-screen himself as Darth Vader.

name: Yaffa Yarkoni
headline: Yaffa Yarkoni, Who Sang for Israeli Soldiers, Dies at 86
abstract: Though Ms. Yarkoni became famous for entertaining the troops during Israel’s wars, she later criticized the military and tried to forge a legacy as an advocate for peace.

name: Gordon Hirabayashi
headline: Gordon Hirabayashi, World War II Internment Opponent, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Hirabayashi, along with Fred Korematsu and Minoru Yasui, symbolized protest against unchecked governmental powers in a time of war.

name: Fred Milano
profession: Original Member of Dion and the Belmonts
headline: Fred Milano, an Original Member of Dion and the Belmonts, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Milano’s backup tenor helped seal the seamless doo-wop sound of hits like “A Teenager in Love” and “Where or When.”

name: Ronald Searle
headline: Ronald Searle, Slyly Caustic Cartoonist, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Searle’s witty illustrations for books, magazine covers, newspaper editorial pages and advertisements helped define postwar graphic humor.

name: Gene Bartow
profession: Successor to John Wooden at U.C.L.A
headline: Gene Bartow, Successor to John Wooden at U.C.L.A., Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Bartow began the athletic program at the University of Alabama, Birmingham, in 1977, coached at six universities, and was inducted into the National Collegiate Basketball Hall of Fame in 2009.

name: Charles W. Bailey
headline: Charles W. Bailey, Journalist and Political Novelist, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Bailey, a reporter and editor at The Minneapolis Tribune, won renown as a co-author of the novel “Seven Days in May,” about an American coup plot.

name: Josef Skvorecky
profession: Czech-Born Writer Oppressed by Right and Left
headline: Josef Skvorecky, Czech-Born Writer Oppressed by Right and Left, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Skvorecky left Czechoslovakia for a teaching position in Toronto after Prague Spring was crushed.

name: Jim Huber
headline: Jim Huber, Sports Broadcaster and Essayist, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Mr. Huber spent nearly three decades with Turner Broadcasting, and won an Emmy for his essay on the bombing at the 1996 Olympic Games in Atlanta.

name: Eve Arnold
profession: Photographer of Bold and Illuminating Images
headline: Eve Arnold, a Photographer of Bold and Illuminating Images, Dies at 99
abstract: Ms. Arnold, a grande dame of postwar photojournalism who belonged to the Magnum Photos cooperative for more than 50 years, captured subjects as diverse as Marylin Monroe, Malcolm X and migratory potato pickers.

name: William Duell
headline: William Duell, Puckish Character Actor, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Duell’s understated comic flare enlivened Broadway shows (“A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Forum”), television series (“Police Squad!) and Hollywood films (One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest).

name: Don Carter
profession: First Big Star of Golden Era of Bowling
headline: Don Carter, First Big Star of Golden Era of Bowling, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Carter’s prowess catapulted him to the top of the field of competitive bowlers that sprang up after neighborhood alleys began proliferating in the 1950s.

name: Omus Hirshbein
headline: Omus Hirshbein, Classical Music Impresario, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Hirshbein directed concert series at Hunter College and the 92nd Street Y, and founded the New York Chamber Symphony.

name: Anne Tyng
headline: Anne Tyng, Theorist of Architecture, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Tyng wrote extensively about geometric architecture, exploring ways to apply natural and numeric systems to buildings and urban design.

name: Jerzy Kluger
headline: Jerzy Kluger, John Paul’s Jewish Confidant, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Kluger, a boyhood friend from Poland, helped a determined pope forge new ties between religions.

name: Andy Carey
headline: Andy Carey, Third Baseman for 1950s Yankees, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Carey was an underappreciated cog in the powerful Yankees machine of the 1950s that won four consecutive American League pennants and two World Series.

name: William P. Carey
headline: William P. Carey, Leader in Commercial Real Estate, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Carey was the founder of W. P. Carey & Company, an investment management firm that innovatively used the sale-leaseback model.

name: Tony Blankley
headline: Tony Blankley, Gingrich Aide and Columnist, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Blankley served as Newt Gingrich’s press secretary during his rise to power in the House; he later became a columnist and editorial page editor at The Washington Times.

name: Ed Jenkins
headline: Ed Jenkins of Georgia, 78; Served in Congress 16 Years
abstract: A soft-spoken representative from Georgia who focused on the tax code and protecting the South’s textile industry, his moment in the spotlight came during the Iran-contra hearings.

name: Alexis Weissenberg
headline: Alexis Weissenberg, Pianist of Fire and Ice, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Weissenberg was known for his thundering aggressiveness and rational detachment at the keyboard.

name: Miguel Terekhov
headline: Miguel Terekhov, Dancer With Ballets Russes, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Terekhov was a co-founder, with his wife, of the School of Dance at the University of Oklahoma.

name: James F. Crow
headline: James F. Crow, Population Genetics Pioneer, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Crow was a leading exponent of a subject that aided the understanding of evolutionary change.

name: Denise Darcel
headline: Denise Darcel, Sultry French Actress, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Darcel played parts ranging from peasants to nobility in movies from the 1940s and ’50s.

name: Stanley Kwan
headline: Stanley Kwan, Hang Seng Index Creator, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Kwan worked with his staff at the Hang Seng Bank to devise a widely used gauge for the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

name: Mary Ellen Avery
headline: Mary Ellen Avery, Premature Babies’ Savior, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Avery was a medical researcher who made a single, crucial discovery about newborns’ ability to breathe.

name: John McWhinnie
headline: John McWhinnie, an Expert in Rare Books, Dies at 43
abstract: Mr. McWhinnie was a rare-book dealer and gallerist known as a champion of words and images on paper in an age of electronic reading.

name: Jan Groover
headline: Jan Groover, Postmodern Photographer, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. Groover’s formal still lifes of ordinary objects brought a sense of Renaissance stateliness to postmodern photography.

name: Mary Raftery
headline: Mary Raftery, 54, Dies; Irish Journalist Documented Child Abuse
abstract: Ms. Raftery’s documentary “States of Fear” detailed a Dickensian network of reformatories and residential schools for poor, neglected and abandoned children.

name: Roy Ash
headline: Roy Ash, Powerful Budget Director for Nixon, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Ash used tough-minded analytic acumen to become a force in the Nixon White House, where he spearheaded the creation of agencies like the Environmental Protection Agency.

name: Bill Janklow
headline: Bill Janklow, a Four-Term Governor of South Dakota, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Janklow was a Republican with an outsize persona whose career was ended after a manslaughter conviction in a fatal car accident.

name: Richard Threlkeld
headline: Richard Threlkeld, Award-Winning Journalist, Dies at 74
abstract: In his 33 years as a correspondent for CBS and ABC News, Mr. Threlkeld reported on wars, presidential campaigns, assassinations and the collapse of the Soviet Union.

name: Rauf Denktash
headline: Rauf Denktash, Who Led Turkish Cypriots, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Denktash, a former leader of the Turkish minority in Cyprus, for decades successfully opposed reunification of that divided island in pursuit of a separate state for his people.

name: Ruth Fernández
profession: Singer and Senator in Puerto Rico
headline: Ruth Fernández, Singer and Senator in Puerto Rico, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Fernández, “the soul of Puerto Rico made song,” had a repertory ranging from fiery Latin music to spirituals; she also served in the Puerto Rican Senate for eight years.

name: Tom Ardolino
profession: Drummer for NRBQ for Three Decades
headline: Tom Ardolino Dies at 56; Drummer for NRBQ for Three Decades
abstract: Mr. Ardolino had an unorthodox, loose-limbed style that mixed power and subtle musicality.

name: Joel J. Tyler
headline: Joel J. Tyler, Judge Who Pronounced ‘Deep Throat’ Obscene, Dies at 90
abstract: In the 1973 decision, the judge said the film’s “alleged story lines are the facade, the sheer negligee” that hid the producer’s purpose of showing hard-core pornography.

name: Frederica Sagor Maas
headline: Frederica Sagor Maas, Silent-Era Scriptwriter, Dies at 111
abstract: Mrs. Maas, who told of seeing Clara Bow dance naked and teaching Joan Crawford how to dress, was one of the last living links to Hollywood’s earliest days.

name: Wylie Vale Jr.
headline: Wylie Vale Jr., Groundbreaking Endocrinologist, Dies at 70
abstract: Dr. Vale helped identify the hormones through which the brain governs basic bodily functions and was involved in a combative race for the Nobel Prize.

name: Charles H. Price II
headline: Charles H. Price II, Ambassador to Britain, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Price took over as ambassador to the Court of St. James for President Ronald Reagan in November 1983, a moment of unease between the two nations.

name: Louise J. Kaplan
headline: Louise J. Kaplan, Psychoanalyst and Author, Dies at 82
abstract: Dr. Kaplan used a psychological lens, literary allusion and a feminist sensibility to soberly define and explain seemingly titillating topics like sexual perversity and fetishes.

name: Giuseppe Quintarelli
headline: Giuseppe Quintarelli, Revered Vintner, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Quintarelli’s wines, produced from grapes from the Veneto region of Italy, were expensive and rare, made with painstaking care and attention to detail.

name: Danny Evins
profession: Restaurant Founder and Focus of Controversy
headline: Danny Evins, Restaurant Founder and Focus of Controversy, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Evins created Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, expanded it into a $2 billion chain and then fought a losing battle to discriminate against gay employees.

name: Reginald Hill
headline: Reginald Hill, Prolific Writer of Crime Novels, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Hill is best known for his 24 idiosyncratic but elegant crime novels featuring the Yorkshire police detectives Andrew Dalziel and Peter Pascoe.

name: Gustav Leonhardt
headline: Gustav Leonhardt, Master Harpsichordist, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Leonhardt was a pioneer in the world of period instrument performance and research into Baroque music.

name: Jimmy Castor
headline: Jimmy Castor, Musician Who Mastered Many Genres, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Castor, a singer, instrumentalist and songwriter, moved easily from doo-wop to Latin soul to funk.

name: Niles Ford
headline: Niles Ford, Dancer and Choreographer, Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. Ford was part of a generation of young downtown New York choreographers who emerged in the 1980s.

name: Charles M. Haar
profession: Used Courts to Clean Boston Harbor
headline: Charles M. Haar Dies at 91; Used Courts to Clean Boston Harbor
abstract: Mr. Haar, a Harvard Law School professor, advocated robust government regulation of, and intervention in, urban development.

name: Marty Springstead
headline: Marty Springstead, Longtime Baseball Umpire and Supervisor, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Springstead was an American League umpire from 1966 to 1985 and worked in four League Championship Series, three World Series and three All-Star Games.

name: Edward J. Derwinski
headline: Edward J. Derwinski, First V.A. Secretary, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Derwinski, who honed an effusive political personality in Chicago, later put it to use as a top-ranking Republican congressman, a high State Department adviser and the first secretary of veterans affairs.

name: Michael Mussa
headline: Michael Mussa, Adviser to Reagan on Economy, Dies at 67
abstract: The former chief economist for the International Monetary Fund was known for his blunt and often witty economic assessments.

name: Byron Donzis
headline: Byron Donzis, Inventor of Football Flak Jacket, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Donzis took plenty of hits so quarterbacks would be able to withstand them.

name: Johnny Otis
headline: Johnny Otis, ‘Godfather of Rhythm and Blues,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Otis might be best known for his Top 10 pop hit “Willie and the Hand Jive” from 1958. He also steered a long list of performers to stardom.

name: Richard J. Sheirer
profession: Official in Charge of Sept. 11 Rescues
headline: Richard J. Sheirer, Official in Charge of Sept. 11 Rescues, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Sheirer, appointed the director of New York City’s Office of Emergency Management in 2000, was thrust into the spotlight after the Sept. 11 attacks.

name: Etta James
headline: Etta James Dies at 73; Voice Behind ‘At Last’
abstract: Ms. James, most often referred to as a rhythm and blues singer, is in both the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and the Blues Hall of Fame.

name: Richard M. Ketchum
headline: Richard M. Ketchum Dies at 89; Chronicled the Rural Life
abstract: Mr. Ketchum, who worked in publishing in New York, moved to a farm in Vermont and co-founded Country Journal with a fellow expatriate in 1974.

name: Robert Nelson
headline: Robert Nelson, Experimental Filmmaker, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Nelson’s movies are varied in tone and subject matter, but they all exhibit the subversive relish of a renegade, quirky wit.

name: Pilar Montero
profession: Bar Owner and Link to a Seafaring Past
headline: Pilar Montero, Bar Owner and Link to a Seafaring Past, Dies at 90
abstract: When Mrs. Montero opened a bar with her husband in 1945, it was one of a dozen similar establishments. But when dock traffic declined, only Montero’s kept its character.

name: Joe Paterno
headline: Joe Paterno, Longtime Penn State Coach, Dies at 85
abstract: Paterno became the face of Penn State and a symbol of integrity in collegiate athletics only to be fired during the 2011 season amid a child sexual-abuse scandal.

name: Mary C. Henderson
profession: Author and Scholar of Theater History
headline: Mary C. Henderson, Author and Scholar of Theater History, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Henderson wrote books that have become standard works on America’s players and playhouses.

name: Edgar Kaiser Jr.
headline: Edgar Kaiser Jr. Dies at 69; Owned Denver Broncos
abstract: Edgar F. Kaiser Jr. was a Canadian industrialist who as owner of the Denver Broncos brought the Hall of Fame quarterback John Elway to the team.

name: Thérèse Delpech
headline: Thérèse Delpech, French Political Adviser, Dies at 63
abstract: Respected as a debater, an author and an intellectual, Ms. Delpech counseled foreign ministers. Until her death, she was a director at her nation’s Atomic Energy Commission.

name: Bingham Ray
headline: Bingham Ray, Executive Who Championed Independent Films, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Ray was a colorful indie-film executive who helped steer art-house movies like “Bowling for Columbine” and “Hotel Rwanda” to the masses.

name: Archbishop Robert F. Sanchez
headline: Archbishop Robert F. Sanchez, Who Fought Discrimination, Dies at 77
abstract: Archbishop Sanchez created an Office for Native American Ministry and ordained the first Native American bishop, but resigned in 1993 when facing charges of having sex with three women.

name: Philip Vannatter
headline: Philip Vannatter, 70, Dies; O. J. Simpson Investigator
abstract: Detective Vannatter was a Los Angeles police detective who helped lead the investigation of the murders of Nicole Brown Simpson and Ronald L. Goldman in 1994.

name: Larry Butler
headline: Larry Butler, Producer for Kenny Rogers, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Butler was the only Nashville session leader ever to win a Grammy Award for producer of the year.

name: Bill Mardo
headline: Bill Mardo, Writer Who Pushed Baseball to Integrate, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Mardo campaigned against baseball’s color barrier as a sportswriter for the Communist Party newspaper The Daily Worker when the mainstream American media was largely silent on the subject.

name: Jacqueline G. Wexler
headline: Jacqueline G. Wexler, Ex-Nun Who Took On Church, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Wexler was a former Roman Catholic nun who fought the Vatican’s authority and won, then found herself on the other side of the barricades when she became president of Hunter College in 1970.

name: John Levy
headline: John Levy, Bassist and Talent Manager, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Levy, widely credited as the first African-American personal manager in jazz, represented big names like Nancy Wilson, Cannonball Adderley and Herbie Hancock.

name: Charla Krupp
headline: Charla Krupp, Magician of Everyday Style, Dies at 58
abstract: The author dispensed down-to-earth style tips.

name: Yuri Rasovsky
headline: Yuri Rasovsky, Dramatist for the Ear, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Mr. Rasovsky was an award-winning maker of audio books and founder of the Hollywood Theater of the Ear.

name: Wesley E. Brown
headline: Wesley E. Brown, Oldest Judge in Nation’s History, Dies at 104
abstract: Judge Brown’s work ethic and a hale constitution kept him climbing the stairs to his fourth-floor courtroom past his 100th birthday.

name: Wesley Brown
headline: Wesley Brown, Pioneer as Black Naval Graduate, Dies at 85
abstract: White midshipmen refused to sit next to Mr. Brown, racial epithets were whispered behind his back and fellow plebes barred him from joining the choir.

name: Nicol Williamson
headline: Nicol Williamson, a Mercurial Actor, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Mr. Williamson was a Scottish-born actor whose large, renegade talent made him a controversial Hamlet, an eccentric Macbeth, an angry, high-strung Vanya and, on the screen, a cocaine-sniffing Sherlock Holmes.

name: Theo Angelopoulos
headline: Theo Angelopoulos, Greek Filmmaker, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Angelopoulos was a renowned director whose films explored the human condition in general and the condition of modern Greece in particular.

name: Gerre Hancock
headline: Gerre Hancock, Church Organist, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Hancock was the organist and master of the choristers at St. Thomas Church in Manhattan for more than 30 years.

name: Dick Tufeld
profession: Robot Voice in TVs Lost in Space
headline: Dick Tufeld, Robot Voice in TV’s ‘Lost in Space,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Tufeld possessed one of Hollywood’s most often-heard disembodied voices, especially from the 1950s through the 1970s.

name: James Farentino
headline: James Farentino, a Dashing Leading Man, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Farentino was a handsome actor who in his nearly 100 roles on stage, screen and television often defied the stereotype of the leading man, even though he fit the picture.

name: Eiko Ishioka
headline: Eiko Ishioka, Multifaceted Designer and Oscar Winner, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Ishioka, who won a 1992 Academy Award in costume design for “Bram Stoker’s ‘Dracula,’” came to be known as one of Japan’s, then the world’s, foremost art directors.

name: Winston Riley
headline: Winston Riley, Jamaican Music Producer, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Riley helped to popularize Jamaican music globally through early hits like “Double Barrel” by Dave and Ansell Collins and later ones like Buju Banton’s “Stamina Daddy.”

name: Rudi van Dantzig
headline: Rudi van Dantzig, Provocative Dutch Choreographer, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. van Dantzig’s mix of idealism and protest gave the Dutch National Ballet an international profile.

name: Robert Hegyes
headline: Robert Hegyes, a Sweathog on ‘Kotter,’ Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Hegyes played Juan Epstein, a remedial student with a slouch and a towering Afro.

name: Kevin H. White
headline: Kevin H. White, Mayor Who Led Boston in Busing Crisis, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. White served four terms as mayor, much of it during a period of economic stagnation and racial unrest over court-ordered desegregation of the city’s schools.

name: Dick Kniss
headline: Dick Kniss, a Bassist for Peter, Paul and Mary, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Kniss also helped write one of John Denver’s biggest hits, “Sunshine on My Shoulders.”

name: Homai Vyarawalla
headline: Homai Vyarawalla, Pioneering Indian Photojournalist, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Vyarawalla was hailed as the first Indian woman to work as a photojournalist and for chronicling the country’s march toward independence.

name: Joseph Mattioli
profession: Gave Up Dentistry to Build Pocono Raceway
headline: Joseph Mattioli, Who Gave Up Dentistry to Build Pocono Raceway, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Mattioli, tired of the daily grind, bought a spinach farm in northeast Pennsylvania in 1960 and transformed it into one of the primary stock-car racetracks.

name: Oscar Luigi Scalfaro
headline: Oscar Luigi Scalfaro, Ex-President of Italy, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Scalfaro was Italy’s president during seven tumultuous years marked by a corruption scandal that brought down an entire political class.

name: Jonathan Idema
profession: Con Man and Afghan Bounty Hunter
headline: Jonathan Idema, Con Man and Afghan Bounty Hunter, Dies at 55
abstract: Mr. Idema gained notoriety in post-invasion Afghanistan as a swaggering hunter of terrorists, then ignominy when he was imprisoned for taking Afghans hostage and torturing them.

name: John F. Baker Jr.
headline: John F. Baker Jr., Who Saved 8 G.I.’s in 1966, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Baker received the Medal of Honor for saving eight fellow soldiers during the Vietnam War while under heavy fire.

name: Paavo Berglund
headline: Paavo Berglund, Finnish Conductor, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Berglund was renowned for his interpretations of Sibelius’s symphonies and tone poems.

name: Patricia Neway
headline: Patricia Neway, Operatic Soprano Who Won a Tony, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Neway, who won a Tony for “The Sound of Music,” was also heroine of Gian Carlo Menotti’s opera “The Consul.”

name: Frank Cioffi
headline: Frank Cioffi, Philosopher and Critic of Freud, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Cioffi’s scathing critique of Sigmund Freud’s work was one of the opening salvos in the bitter debate in recent decades over the legitimacy of psychoanalytic theories.

name: Don Cornelius
headline: Don Cornelius, ‘Soul Train’ Creator, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Mr. Cornelius was the smooth-voiced television host who brought black music and culture into America’s living rooms when he created the dance show “Soul Train.”

name: Samuel S. Vaughan
headline: Samuel S. Vaughan, Publisher at Doubleday, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Vaughan, known for a decorous manner and democratic instincts, worked with a wide range of writers, including Dwight D. Eisenhower, William F. Buckley Jr. and Fannie Flagg.

name: Wislawa Szymborska
headline: Wislawa Szymborska, Nobel-Winning Polish Poet, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Szymborska was a gentle and reclusive Polish poet who won the 1996 Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: Anthony J. Bevilacqua
headline: Anthony J. Bevilacqua, Retired Cardinal of Philadelphia, Dies at 88
abstract: After 15 years as archbishop, Cardinal Bevilacqua saw his accomplishments tarnished by accusations that he covered up sexual abuse by priests.

name: Mike Kelley
headline: Mike Kelley, an Artist With Attitude, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Kelley’s art mined the abjection and gross-out anarchy associated with youth culture.

name: Dorothea Tanning
headline: Dorothea Tanning, Surrealist Painter, Dies at 101
abstract: Ms. Tanning, a versatile artist, began as a Surrealist in the 1930s and, later, after many other incarnations, also added poet and author to her roster of achievements.

name: John Rich
profession: Challenged Taboos With an Interracial TV Kiss
headline: John Rich Dies at 86; Challenged Taboos With an Interracial TV Kiss
abstract: Mr. Rich, who won Emmys for his work on “All in the Family” and “The Dick Van Dyke Show,” broke interracial boundaries with a simple kiss.

name: Angelo Dundee
headline: Angelo Dundee, Trainer of Ali and Leonard, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Dundee gained acclaim as a brilliant cornerman, whether healing cuts, inspiring his fighters to battle on when they seemed to be reeling or adjusting strategy between rounds.

name: Camilla Williams
headline: Camilla Williams, Barrier-Breaking Opera Star, Dies at 92
abstract: Miss Williams made her debut at the New York City Opera in 1946 to rave notices. She was the first black woman to secure a contract with a major United States opera company.

name: Richard K. Olney
profession: Felled by the Disease He Studied
headline: Dr. Richard K. Olney, Felled by the Disease He Studied, Is Dead at 64
abstract: Dr. Olney, a leading researcher of A.L.S., commonly known as Lou Gehrig’s disease, learned in 2004 that he himself had it.

name: Clare Fischer
headline: Clare Fischer, Arranger and Keyboardist, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. Fischer was influential in jazz and arranged pop and R&B compositions for the likes of Paul McCartney, Michael Jackson, Prince and Celine Dion.

name: Ben Gazzara
headline: Ben Gazzara, Risk-Taking Actor, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Gazzara’s long acting career included playing Brick in the original “Cat on a Hot Tin Roof” on Broadway and roles in influential films by John Cassavetes.

name: Gianpiero Moretti
headline: Gianpiero Moretti, Modernizer of Racecar Steering Wheels, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Moretti started his automotive accessories company Momo in 1966, and it expanded to make an array of racing products.

name: Roger Boisjoly
headline: Roger Boisjoly, 73, Dies; Warned of Shuttle Danger
abstract: Mr. Boisjoly wrote a portentous memo six months before the Space Shuttle Challenger’s explosion, warning that if it was too cold, seals connecting sections of the shuttle’s rocket boosters could fail.

name: Dorothy Gilman
headline: Dorothy Gilman, ‘Mrs. Pollifax’ Novelist, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Gilman was best known for her “Mrs. Pollifax” series of books about a widow who goes to work as a secret agent.

name: Una Mulzac
profession: Bookseller With Passion for Black Politics
headline: Una Mulzac, Bookseller With Passion for Black Politics, Dies at 88
abstract: Known for a bold and cantankerous personality, Ms. Mulzac built Liberation Bookstore over four decades into a Harlem landmark.

name: Steven Leiber
headline: Steven Leiber, Dealer in Artists’ Ephemera, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Leiber founded a San Francisco gallery that is a prime source for brochures, posters, fliers and the like produced by artists.

name: Robert B. Cohen
headline: Robert B. Cohen, Hudson News Chain Founder, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Cohen was president of the Hudson County News Company, a newspaper distributorship, when it went into the retail field in the mid-1970s by taking over a newsstand at the Newark airport.

name: Antoni Tàpies
headline: Antoni Tàpies, Spanish Abstract Painter, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Tàpies grounded his work in the brute reality of the Spanish street and in the turbulent political dramas of his youth in Catalonia.

name: Mike deGruy
headline: Mike deGruy, Who Filmed the Oceans, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. deGruy was an Emmy Award-winning documentary filmmaker and marine biologist.

name: Florence Green
headline: Florence Green, Last World War I Veteran, Dies at 110
abstract: Mrs. Green, a teenage officers’ mess waitress, signed up in the last months of the war and recalled the officers’ courtly behavior.

name: Norton D. Zinder
headline: Norton D. Zinder, Researcher in Molecular Biology, Dies at 83
abstract: Dr. Zinder helped lay the basis for molecular biology in the 1950s and ’60s.

name: John Christopher
headline: John Christopher, Science Fiction Writer, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Christopher was author of the “Tripods” trilogy among many other books under many other names.

name: John Sargent
headline: John Sargent, Former Doubleday President, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Sargent oversaw the expansion of a modest-size family-controlled book publisher into an industry giant with interests extending into broadcasting and baseball.

name: Zalman King
headline: Zalman King, Creator of Soft-Core Films, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. King brought television audiences “Red Shoe Diaries” and wrote and directed several soft-core films, some in collaboration with his wife, Patricia Knop.

name: Damien Bona
profession: Creator of Guide for Oscar Buffs
headline: Damien Bona Dies at 56; Creator of Guide for Oscar Buffs
abstract: Mr. Bona, along with Mason Wiley, wrote an encyclopedic, usually affectionate but sometimes acerbic guide called “Inside Oscar: The Unofficial History of the Academy Awards.”

name: Robert Hecht
headline: Robert Hecht, Antiquities Dealer, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Hecht, who sold the Euphronios krater to the Metropolitan Museum of Art in 1972 for $1.3 million, was long suspected of illegal trafficking in looted artifacts.

name: Janice Voss
headline: Janice Voss, Shuttle Astronaut and Scientist, Dies at 55
abstract: Dr. Voss explored the behavior of fire in weightlessness, how plants adapt to extraterrestrial flight and an array of other phenomena while logging nearly 19 million miles circling Earth.

name: Jill Kinmont Boothe
headline: Jill Kinmont Boothe, Skier in Inspiring Film, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Boothe’s struggle to recuperate from a paralyzing fall became the subject of the popular 1975 film “The Other Side of the Mountain.”

name: Peter Breck
profession: TV Actor Known for The Big Valley
headline: Peter Breck, TV Actor Known for ‘The Big Valley,’ Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Breck played a temperamental son in a ranching family headed by Barbara Stanwyck.

name: Jeffrey Zaslow
profession: Columnist and Author of The Last Lecture
headline: Jeffrey Zaslow, Columnist and Author of ‘The Last Lecture,’ Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Zaslow was a columnist and author whose books included a best seller with Randy Pausch and a chronicle of Gabrielle Giffords’s recovery.

name: W. Gunther Plaut
headline: W. Gunther Plaut, Defined Reform Judaism, Dies at 99
abstract: Rabbi Plaut’s vast, scholarly and ardently contemporary edition of the Torah helped define Reform Judaism in late-20th-century North America.

name: Istvan Csurka
headline: Istvan Csurka, Hungarian Playwright and Gadfly, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Csurka, the founder of a far-right political party and a fierce anti-Semite, appealed to older Hungarians with his evocation of the nation’s glory days before World War I.

name: Whitney Houston
headline: Whitney Houston, Pop Superstar, Dies at 48
abstract: Ms. Houston reigned as pop music’s queen until her majestic voice and regal image were ravaged by drug use, erratic behavior and a tumultuous marriage.

name: Patricia Stephens Due
headline: Patricia Stephens Due Dies at 72; Campaigned for Civil Rights
abstract: Mrs. Due’s lifelong civil rights activism led to injury from a tear-gas canister, and time in a brutal jail.

name: Stephen M. Levin
headline: Stephen M. Levin, Who Ran a Clinic for 9/11 Responders, Dies at 70
abstract: Dr. Levin helped set up a clinic to provide firefighters and responders with comprehensive examinations and continued to study their conditions.

name: Lillian Bassman
headline: Lillian Bassman, Fashion and Fine-Art Photographer, Dies at 94
abstract: In the 1990s, reinterpretations of Ms. Bassman’s photographs found a new generation of admirers, and a full-fledged revival of her career ensued, with gallery shows and international exhibitions.

name: Tristram P. Coffin
headline: Tristram P. Coffin, Folklorist, Dies at 89
abstract: Professor Coffin, a retired faculty member at the University of Pennsylvania, looked into ordinary rituals to find worlds of hidden meanings.

name: Dory Previn
headline: Dory Previn, Songwriter, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Ms. Previn, the lyricist for three Oscar-nominated songs, became famous for her own confessional albums in the early 1970s.

name: Freddie Solomon
headline: Freddie Solomon, a Star N.F.L. Receiver, Dies at 59
abstract: Solomon gave up his dream of being a pro quarterback to become an outstanding receiver for the Miami Dolphins and a San Francisco 49ers team that won two Super Bowls.

name: Charles Anthony
headline: Charles Anthony Dies at 82; Sang 2,928 Times at Met
abstract: Mr. Anthony, a tenor, broke records, singing 111 roles in 69 operas at the Met in 57 years.

name: Phil Bruns
headline: Phil Bruns, Hard-Hat Dad on ‘Mary Hartman,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Bruns was a film and TV character actor best known as the cigar-chomping dad on the 1970s soap-opera parody “Mary Hartman, Mary Hartman.”

name: Robert Glaser
profession: Shaped the Science of Student Testing
headline: Robert Glaser, Who Shaped the Science of Student Testing, Dies at 91
abstract: A cognitive psychologist, Dr. Glaser pioneered ways of measuring not only how students learn but how teachers teach.

name: Gary Carter
headline: Gary Carter, Star Catcher Who Helped Mets to Series Title, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Carter, who entered the Baseball Hall of Fame as a Montreal Expo, most famously helped propel the Mets to their dramatic 1986 World Series championship.

name: Anthony Shadid
headline: Anthony Shadid, Reporter in the Middle East, Dies at 43
abstract: Mr. Shadid, a two-time winner of the Pulitzer Prize, spent most of his professional life covering the Middle East and was esteemed throughout his career for being an insightful analyst.

name: Bruce Herman
headline: Bruce Herman, Worker Training Expert, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Herman fought to preserve New York City’s garment district and to revive manufacturing across the country.

name: Zina Bethune
headline: Zina Bethune Dies at 66; Actress, Dancer and Choreographer
abstract: Ms. Bethune balanced careers in ballet and acting from the 1950s to the ’60s. She is best known for her role as a nursing student on “The Nurses.”

name: Harry C. McPherson
headline: Harry C. McPherson, a Presidential Counsel, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. McPherson helped draft bills that became the Civil Rights Act of 1957 and helped shape President Johnson’s Great Society programs.

name: Zelda Kaplan
profession: Fixture of New Yorks Fashion Scene
headline: Zelda Kaplan, a Fixture of New York’s Fashion Scene, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Kaplan held a colorful place in a layer of New York society made up of flamboyant, surprising and self-invented people who are largely known for being seen.

name: John Fairfax
headline: John Fairfax, Who Rowed Across Oceans, Dies at 74
abstract: In 1969, after six months alone on the Atlantic battling storms, sharks and encroaching madness, Mr. Fairfax became the first lone oarsman in recorded history to traverse any ocean.

name: Adam Adamowicz
profession: Artist for Lush Video Game Worlds
headline: Adam Adamowicz, Artist for Lush Video Game Worlds, Dies at 43
abstract: Mr. Adamowicz was a concept artist whose paintings formed the visual foundation for two of the most popular single-player role-playing video games of all time.

name: Jimmy Sabater
headline: Jimmy Sabater, Boogaloo Musician, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Sabater, a singer and timbales player, was one of the architects of boogaloo in the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Ronald Fraser
headline: Ronald Fraser, People’s Historian, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Fraser was known for his deftness at collecting and presenting ordinary people’s experiences during momentous events like the Spanish Civil War.

name: Renato Dulbecco
headline: Renato Dulbecco, 97, Dies; Won Prize for Cancer Study
abstract: Dr. Dulbecco, who won the Nobel Prize in 1975, worked with colleagues to draw a link between genetic mutations and cancer.

name: James Whitaker
headline: James Whitaker, King of Royal Reporters, Dies at 71
abstract: For 45 years, Mr. Whitaker managed to keep good relations with those he covered, even though he sometimes used tactics associated with the tabloid press.

name: Roger J. Miner
headline: Roger J. Miner, 77, Dies; Judge Valued Neutrality
abstract: Judge Miner, a member of the federal appeals court in Manhattan, may have lost a chance to join the Supreme Court by refusing to pledge to rule against abortion.

name: Dick Anthony Williams
headline: Dick Anthony Williams, Actor and Theater Producer, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Williams’s roles ranged from blaxploitation films to the stage, where he gained two Tony nominations.

name: Amalia de Fortabat
headline: Amalia de Fortabat, 90, Dies; Noted for Art and Scandal
abstract: Mrs. Fortabat married a cement tycoon, expanded his empire after his death and became an art collector and philanthropist as well as the richest woman in Argentina.

name: Kay Davis
headline: Kay Davis, Coloratura, Soared in Wordless Songs, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Davis, a classically trained coloratura soprano, excelled at singing wordless works.

name: Barney Rosset
profession: Defied Censors, Making Racy a Literary Staple
headline: Barney Rosset Dies at 89; Defied Censors, Making Racy a Literary Staple
abstract: Mr. Rosset helped change the course of publishing in the United States, bringing masters like Samuel Beckett to Americans’ attention, and won celebrated First Amendment slugfests against censorship.

name: Pierre Juneau
profession: Champion of Canadas Pop Music Industry
headline: Pierre Juneau, Champion of Canada’s Pop Music Industry, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Juneau helped create Canada’s pop music industry when, as a member of the Trudeau government in 1970, he required radio stations to broadcast more Canadian music.

name: Steve Kordek
headline: Steve Kordek, a Pinball Innovator, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Kordek changed the game of pinball in the 1940s by designing what became the standard two-flipper machine found in bars and penny arcades around the world.

name: Ken Price
headline: Ken Price, Sculptor Whose Artworks Helped Elevate Ceramics, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Price molded clay into vibrant, abstract objects featuring exquisite finishes that was worthy of consideration as high art.

name: Billy Strange
headline: Billy Strange, ’60s Session Guitarist, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Strange recorded with Elvis Presley, Nat King Cole and the Beach Boys, wrote a No. 1 single for Chubby Checker and arranged Nancy Sinatra’s No. 1 pop hit “These Boots Are Made for Walkin’.”

name: Theodore Mann
profession: Producer and a Founder of Circle in the Square
headline: Theodore Mann, Producer and a Founder of Circle in the Square, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Mann was a founder of the influential Circle in the Square Theater, and a driving force in the rise of Off Broadway theater in the 1950s.

name: Dmitri Nabokov
headline: Dmitri Nabokov, Steward of Father’s Literary Legacy, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Nabokov translated Vladimir Nabokov’s early works, then published an unfinished novel his father had insisted be burned.

name: Ulric Neisser
headline: Ulric Neisser Is Dead at 83; Reshaped Study of the Mind
abstract: Mr. Neisser helped lead a postwar revolution in the study of the human mind by advancing the understanding of mental processes like perception and memory.

name: Dennis Gomes
profession: Operator of Casino in Atlantic City
headline: Dennis Gomes, Operator of Casino in Atlantic City, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Gomes started out by investigating the gambling industry, and later went to work in it.

name: Howard Kissel
headline: Howard Kissel, Daily News Theater Critic, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Kissel also wrote books on Broadway subjects, including a book of New York City theater walks and a biography of the producer David Merrick.

name: Erland Josephson
headline: Erland Josephson, Actor With Bergman, Dies at 88
abstract: Among Mr. Josephson’s landmark roles was the male lead in “Scenes From a Marriage.”

name: Jan Berenstain
headline: Jan Berenstain Dies at 88; Created Berenstain Bears
abstract: Ms. Berenstain and her husband wrote and illustrated the Berenstain Bears books, which taught children simple lessons about kindness, tidiness and some of life’s challenges.

name: Shaun O’Brien
headline: Shaun O’Brien, Dancer Known for Character Roles, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. O’Brien danced with the New York City Ballet for 42 years, a remarkably long career made possible by his focus on character roles.

name: Neil Hope
headline: Neil Hope Is Dead at 35; Teenage Actor Whose Life Unraveled
abstract: Mr. Hope starred as a troubled teenager in the popular Canadian shows “Degrassi Junior High” and “Degrassi High” in the 1980s.

name: Eleanor Callahan
headline: Eleanor Callahan, Photographic Muse, Dies at 95
abstract: Mrs. Callahan posed from the 1940s through the ’90s for the sensual images shot by her husband, Harry, and became known as one of the most recognizable models in the history of art photography.

name: Buck Compton
headline: Buck Compton, Decorated Veteran, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Compton was a lawyer and prosecutor of Sirhan Sirhan whose World War II heroism was later publicized in “Band of Brothers.”

name: Red Holloway
headline: Red Holloway, Swinger of the Sax, Dies at 84
abstract: As an alto and tenor saxophonist, Mr. Holloway played with Billie Holliday, B. B. King, Muddy Waters and other greats.

name: Bruce Surtees
headline: Bruce Surtees, Oscar-Nominated Cinematographer, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Surtees, known as the Prince of Darkness for his nuanced lighting, was known in particular for his long association with Clint Eastwood.

name: Tina Strobos
headline: Dr. Tina Strobos, Who Harbored Jews From the Nazis, Dies at 91
abstract: As a young medical student in Amsterdam, Dr. Strobos protected more than 100 Jews from capture during the German occupation of the Netherlands.

name: Anna Lou Dehavenon
headline: Anna Lou Dehavenon, Who Drew Attention to the Homeless, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Dehavenon became an anthropological authority on poverty, hunger and homelessness in New York City after her husband, William Kapell, died in a plane crash.

name: Davy Jones
headline: Davy Jones, Monkees Singer, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Jones was a singer and, by long-held public consensus, the handsomest and most popular of the Monkees, the wildly famous pop group of the 1960s and afterward.

name: William Gay
headline: William Gay Dies at 70; Writer Tied to Tennessee
abstract: Mr. Gay was a self-taught novelist from rural Tennessee who emerged from obscurity in his late 50s with critically praised books in the Southern Gothic style.

name: Terri Dial
profession: Executive at Citigroup and Wells Fargo
headline: Terri Dial, Executive at Citigroup and Wells Fargo, Dies at 62
abstract: During a four-decade career in finance, Ms. Dial was regularly one of only a few top female executives at Fortune 500 companies.

name: Erwin Frankel
headline: Erwin Frankel Dies at 76; Brought World Music to U.S.
abstract: Mr. Frankel had his widest audience when he hosted a one-hour nightly show on WABC-FM, “Music From Around the World,” which aired from 1959 to 1972.

name: Robert R. McElroy
headline: Robert R. McElroy Dies at 84; Documented Art ‘Happenings’
abstract: Mr. McElroy photographed young artists as they used painting, sculpture, music, dance, acting, poetry, light, sound, scents and even trash to influence modern art.

name: Andrew Breitbart
headline: Andrew Breitbart, Conservative Blogger, Dies at 43
abstract: Mr. Breitbart built a national media persona by putting undercover video on the Internet to bring discredit and disgrace to his liberal targets.

name: Joe Thompson
profession: Helped Preserve the Black String Band
headline: Joe Thompson Dies at 93; Helped Preserve the Black String Band
abstract: Until 1973, Mr. Thompson wasn’t known outside of North Carolina. But later, he played at Carnegie Hall and was awarded a National Heritage Fellowship.

name: Zollie Volchok
headline: Zollie Volchok, an N.B.A. Showman, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Mr. Volchok was a one-time theater manager and entertainment promoter who helped the Seattle franchise set attendance records and win an N.B.A. title.

name: James Q. Wilson
headline: James Q. Wilson Dies at 80; Originated ‘Broken Windows’ Policing Strategy
abstract: Mr. Wilson was a social scientist whose research laid the groundwork for crime reduction efforts in several cities.

name: Maurice André
headline: Maurice André, Trumpeter, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. André, who was a teenage coal miner, became a soloist with the trumpet, rarely a solo instrument in classical music.

name: Stan Stearns
profession: Photographer of John F. Kennedy Jr.s Salute to Father
headline: Stan Stearns, Photographer of John F. Kennedy Jr.’s Salute to Father, Dies at 76
abstract: The famous image of the 3-year-old next to his mother as the president’s casket passed cemented the journalist’s reputation.

name: Alex Webster
headline: Alex Webster, Giants Running Back and Coach, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Webster was a powerful running back who helped propel the Giants to six division titles and an N.F.L. championship in the late 1950s and early ’60s and later coached the team.

name: Sol Schiff
headline: Sol Schiff, ‘Mr. Table Tennis,’ Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Schiff, whose rocketing, flat forehand propelled him to national and world table tennis championships in the 1930s when he was in his teens, later became an ardent advocate for his sport.

name: James Trager
headline: James Trager, Brought Facts to the Masses, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Trager, an advertising writer turned chronologist, could not tell readers exactly when the world was created, but he certainly detailed how history unraveled.

name: Lucio Dalla
headline: Lucio Dalla, Italian Troubadour, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Dalla was one of Italy’s leading “cantautori,” singers and songwriters who expressed the postwar generation’s hopes and frustrations.

name: Van Barfoot
headline: Van Barfoot, Medal of Honor Recipient, Dies at 92
abstract: Decades after receiving the nation’s highest award for valor, Colonel Barfoot overcame a neighborhood rule against flying a flag from a pole outside his Virginia home.

name: Amid Capeci
headline: Amid Capeci, Who Led Magazine Face-Lifts, Dies at 50
abstract: As an art director, Mr. Capeci helped shape the new looks of Rolling Stone and Newsweek as they sought to highlight their serious journalistic work.

name: Ralph McQuarrie
headline: Ralph McQuarrie, Artist Who Helped Bring ‘Star Wars’ to Life, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. McQuarrie transformed George Lucas’s rudimentary concepts and earliest scripts into lush, vivid images that became the visual core of the “Star Wars” saga.

name: Ronnie Montrose
headline: Ronnie Montrose, Hard-Rock Guitarist, Dies at 64
abstract: In 1973, Mr. Montrose formed the band Montrose, whose first album was a sleeper success, eventually going platinum and becoming a minor landmark of heavy metal.

name: Donald M. Payne
profession: First Black Elected to Congress From New Jersey
headline: Donald M. Payne, First Black Elected to Congress From New Jersey, Dies at 77
abstract: Though known as a low-key and unassuming lawmaker, Mr. Payne nonetheless made a mark in a number of areas, including education and global affairs.

name: Donald M. Payne Jr.
profession: New Jersey Representative in Sixth Term
headline: Donald M. Payne Jr., 65, New Jersey Representative in Sixth Term, Is Dead
abstract: A Newark Democrat, he succeeded his father, who was the first Black member of his state’s congressional delegation.

name: Robert B. Sherman
headline: Robert B. Sherman, a Songwriter for Disney and Others, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Sherman and his brother, Richard M. Sherman, wrote the scores for “Mary Poppins” and “Chitty Chitty Bang Bang,” and won two Academy Awards for their music.

name: Robert Sherman
profession: Veteran of the New York Airwaves
headline: Robert Sherman, Veteran of the New York Airwaves, Dies at 90
abstract: For more than five decades, he brought together emerging classical and folk performers as well as established stars for interviews and live performances.

name: William Heirens
headline: William Heirens, the ‘Lipstick Killer,’ Dies at 83
abstract: After confessing in 1946 to three notorious murders in Chicago, Mr. Heirens recanted and went on to profess his innocence for decades.

name: Christopher Lyles
headline: Christopher Lyles, Got Synthetic Trachea, Dies at 30
abstract: In only the second surgery of its kind, Mr. Lyles’s cancerous windpipe was replaced in November with a synthetic one that had been seeded with his own cells.

name: Florence Wolfson Howitt
headline: Florence Wolfson Howitt, Famed for Rediscovered Diary, Dies at 96
abstract: Recognition as a writer eluded Mrs. Howitt until a diary she had kept as a teenager was discovered in a trash bin in 2003.

name: Andrij Dobriansky
profession: Sang at the Met More Than 900 Times
headline: Andrij Dobriansky Dies at 81; Sang at the Met More Than 900 Times
abstract: Mr. Dobriansky studied chemistry and worked at Schrafft’s before he found his vocal vocation.

name: Franklin McMahon
headline: Franklin McMahon, Who Drew the News, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. McMahon was an artist who defied journalism’s preference for photographs to make a renowned career of drawing historic scenes in elegant, emphatic lines.

name: Sheldon Moldoff
headline: Sheldon Moldoff, Batman Comic Book Artist, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Moldoff received belated recognition for drawing some of the most recognizable superheroes of comic books’ golden age, including characters for Batman.

name: Leonard Joy
headline: Leonard Joy, 81, Longtime Public Defender, Dies
abstract: Mr. Joy was a lawyer with the Legal Aid Society who later led New York’s federal public defender’s office for more than two decades.

name: Benedict Freedman
headline: Benedict Freedman, Author of ‘Mrs. Mike,’ Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Freedman’s first novel, “Mrs. Mike” — based on the true story of a young woman’s life in the Canadian wilderness — was a publishing sensation and inspired a Hollywood film.

name: Jimmy Ellis
profession: Lead Singer in Dance Band Trammps
headline: Jimmy Ellis Dies at 74; Lead Singer in Dance Band Trammps
abstract: Mr. Ellis was the soulful lead singer of the Trammps, whose 1970s hit “Disco Inferno” was immortalized in the film “Saturday Night Fever.”

name: Jimmy Ellis
headline: Jimmy Ellis, a Boxer Long in Ali’s Shadow, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Ellis, a former sparring partner for Muhammad Ali, captured the heavyweight championship after it had been stripped from Ali for his refusing military induction.

name: Norman St. John-Stevas
headline: Norman St. John-Stevas, Dapper Tory Dismissed by Thatcher, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. St. John-Stevas, later Lord St. John of Fawsley, was among the left-leaning Tories culled by Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher in the early 1980s.

name: Harry Wendelstedt
headline: Harry Wendelstedt, Umpire in Five World Series, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Wendelstedt was an umpire in five World Series during a 33-year major league career and taught hundreds of aspiring professional umpires at his Florida school.

name: Peter Bergman
headline: Peter Bergman, Satirist With the Firesign Theater, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Bergman was a founding member of the surrealist comedy troupe Firesign Theater, whose albums became cult favorites among college students in the late 1960s and ’70s.

name: Leonardo Cimino
headline: Leonardo Cimino Dies at 94; Distinctive Actor
abstract: Despite once believing his singular appearance would hinder an acting career, Mr. Cimino ended up spending more than 60 years as an in-demand character actor.

name: Frisner Augustin
headline: Frisner Augustin, Haitian Vodou Drummer, Dies at 63
abstract: In his leadership of La Troupe Makandal, a drum and dance group, Mr. Augustin helped to preserve and popularize Afro-Haitian music.

name: Maxwell S. Keith
headline: Maxwell S. Keith Dies at 87; Replacement Lawyer in Manson Case
abstract: Mr. Keith represented Leslie Van Houten, one of three women on trial with Charles Manson, after her previous attorney vanished.

name: Lawrence Anthony
headline: Lawrence Anthony, Baghdad Zoo Savior, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Anthony abandoned a career in insurance and real estate in South Africa to devote his time to rescuing endangered species, including animals in Iraq after the American invasion.

name: Jay McMullen
headline: Jay McMullen, CBS Investigative Journalist, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. McMullen’s 37-year career included early uses of hidden cameras and undercover reporting.

name: F. Sherwood Rowland
headline: F. Sherwood Rowland, Cited Aerosols’ Danger, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Dr. Rowland’s discovery of the danger to the ozone layer presented by chlorinated fluorocarbons in aerosols was met with disdain, but the research later won him a Nobel Prize.

name: Rushworth M. Kidder
headline: Rushworth M. Kidder, Ethicist, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Kidder was an academic-turned-journalist who set up the Institute for Global Ethics to examine and teach about different approaches to ethical dilemmas.

name: Rushworth M. Kidder
headline: Rushworth M. Kidder, Journalist Who Studied Ethics, Dies at 67
abstract: An academic-turned-journalist who set up the Institute for Global Ethics to examine and teach about different approaches to ethical dilemmas.

name: Albert Abramson
headline: Albert Abramson, Holocaust Museum Backer, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Mr. Abramson, a successful developer, brought a sense of urgency to the drive in the 1980s to create a United States Holocaust Memorial Museum.

name: Peter Novick
headline: Peter Novick, Wrote Controversial Book on Holocaust, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Novick, a history professor, contended in “The Holocaust in American Life” that the legacy of the Nazi genocide unduly dominated American Jewish identity.

name: Thomas Puccio
profession: Ex-Prosecutor and Lawyer for Notorious Clients
headline: Thomas Puccio, Ex-Prosecutor and Lawyer for Notorious Clients, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Puccio won fame prosecuting congressmen in the 1980s Abscam scandals, then switched sides and defended Claus von Bülow, corrupt politicians and other notorious clients.

name: Ruth Barcan Marcus
headline: Ruth Barcan Marcus, Philosopher-Logician, Dies at 90
abstract: Professor Marcus was esteemed for her advances in the traditionally male-dominated field of logic, long one of philosophy’s most swaggering strains.

name: Donald F. Smith
headline: Donald F. Smith, Champion of Cabaret, Dies at 79
