abstract: Mr. Smith founded both the Mabel Mercer Foundation and the New York Cabaret Convention.

name: Donald Smith
headline: Donald Smith, Who Produced ‘The Silent Scream,’ Dies at 94
abstract: His controversial anti-abortion documentary, professing to show a fetus expressing pain, became a formidable weapon for abortion opponents.

name: Minoru Mori
headline: Minoru Mori, Builder Who Changed the Face of Modern Tokyo, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Mori built some of Tokyo’s most prominent developments and helped mold the city’s skyline with towering buildings.

name: George Kerchner
headline: George Kerchner, Led a D-Day Maneuver, Dies at 93
abstract: Lieutenant Kerchner, as an Army Ranger, led his company up the face of a towering cliff to seize German big guns overlooking the American invasion beaches of D-Day.

name: Jean Giraud
headline: Jean Giraud, the Comic-Book Artist Known as ‘Moebius,’ Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Giraud, the French comic-book artist who used “Moebius” as his nom de plume, was known for a dystopian vision and characters like Blueberry.

name: Pierre Schoendoerffer
headline: Pierre Schoendoerffer, French Filmmaker, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Schoendoerffer, a French filmmaker and novelist who drew on firsthand experiences during the Indochina War, earned many honors for his work, including an Academy Award.

name: Tom Murrin
headline: Tom Murrin, Alien Comic Performance Artist, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Murrin, a playwright and avant-garde impresario who became known as the Alien Comic, was apt to put on performances almost anywhere.

name: Noble Fleming
headline: Noble Fleming, Arbiter of Tea Taste, Dies at 92
abstract: A “tea master,” Mr. Fleming’s legendary taste determined the tea used by the Thomas J. Lipton Company.

name: Moshe Hager
headline: Rabbi Moshe Hager, a Hasidic Leader, Dies at 95
abstract: Rabbi Hager led the Viznitz sect, which has families in Israel, Brooklyn and Rockland County, N.Y.

name: Gloria Sachs
headline: Gloria Sachs, Fashion Designer for Working Women, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Sachs produced a portfolio of complementary suits, jackets, shirts and skirts that worked with women’s need for professional clothes for the office.

name: Simin Daneshvar
headline: Simin Daneshvar, Eminent Iranian Author, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Daneshvar was the author of the sprawling family saga “Savushun,” and was a translator of Chekhov, Shaw, Hawthorne and other writers.

name: Jerome Albert
profession: Helped Bring Space Age to Coney Island
headline: Jerome Albert, Who Helped Bring Space Age to Coney Island, Dies at 74
abstract: With his father, Mr. Albert helped to revitalize the Coney Island Boardwalk in the 1960s with their amusement park, Astroland.

name: John Demjanjuk
profession: Dogged by Charges of Atrocities as Nazi Camp Guard
headline: John Demjanjuk, 91, Dogged by Charges of Atrocities as Nazi Camp Guard, Dies
abstract: Mr. Demjanjuk was convicted of collaborating with the Nazis at death camps, reprieved and convicted again, but steadfastly denied the accusations.

name: Ethel Winter
headline: Ethel Winter, Dancer With Martha Graham, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Winter brought lyricism and passion to her roles with the company over nearly 30 years.

name: Mike Silverstein
headline: Mike Silverstein, a Founder of Nina Footwear, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Silverstein, who grew up in Havana, founded the company with his brother Stanley, who designed the shoes while Mike merchandised them.

name: Chaleo Yoovidhya
headline: Chaleo Yoovidhya, Who Created Red Bull Beverage, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Chaleo founded a pharmaceutical company that produced the first iteration of the energy drink, which was embraced by late-night revelers, paper-writing students and the practitioners of extreme sports.

name: James Morehead
headline: James Morehead, World War II Flying Ace, Dies at 95
abstract: Colonel Morehead was among the most highly decorated American fighter pilots of the war, downing eight enemy planes in the Pacific and Europe.

name: John Cowles Jr.
headline: John Cowles Jr., 82, Dies; Led Minneapolis Newspapers
abstract: Mr. Cowles was a Minneapolis newspaper executive and philanthropist who supported arts, sports and entertainment.

name: Ulu Grosbard
headline: Ulu Grosbard, 83, Broadway and Film Director, Dies
abstract: Mr. Grosbard’s work was divided evenly between the theater and the movies, and though his career stretched across nearly half a century, he was highly selective in his projects.

name: Samuel Glazer
headline: Samuel Glazer Dies at 89; Popularized Drip Coffee
abstract: Mr. Glazer and his business partner gave the world Mr. Coffee, one of the first and best-selling automatic drip coffee makers in America.

name: Mel Parnell
headline: Mel Parnell, 89, Dies; Dominated Yanks
abstract: He won more games for the Red Sox than any other left-handed pitcher, frequently beating their archrivals.

name: Sanford McDonnell
headline: Sanford McDonnell, Aerospace Leader, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. McDonnell led the aerospace company McDonnell Douglas to higher earnings and helped develop some of the company’s most successful fighter planes.

name: Murray Lender
profession: Gave All America a Taste of Bagels
headline: Murray Lender, Who Gave All America a Taste of Bagels, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Lender and his brothers took over what started as their father’s bakery in a garage and expanded the company into the nation’s leading distributor of packaged frozen bagels.

name: Ron Erhardt
headline: Ron Erhardt, Super Bowl-Winning Offensive Coach, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Erhardt, a coordinator for the Giants 1986 and 1990 N.F.L. championship teams under Bill Parcells, is dead at 81.

name: Tonino Guerra
headline: Tonino Guerra, Poetic Italian Screenwriter, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Guerra was a prolific Italian screenwriter and poet during the golden age of European cinema.

name: Marina Salye
headline: Marina Salye, Politician Who Tried to Prosecute Putin, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Salye dropped out of public life and moved to a remote village after Vladimir V. Putin was elected president in 2000, saying she felt threatened by his power.

name: Al Ross
headline: Al Ross, Cartoonist for The New Yorker, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Ross, one of four cartooning brothers, had his first cartoon published in a 1937 issue of The New Yorker.

name: Abdullahi Yusuf Ahmed
headline: Abdullahi Yusuf Ahmed, Former Somali Strongman, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Ahmed was an ex-warlord who led Somalia’s beleaguered transitional government as president from 2004 to 2008.

name: David L. Waltz
headline: David L. Waltz, Computer Science Pioneer, Dies at 68
abstract: Dr. Waltz made fundamental contributions to computer science in areas ranging from computer vision to machine learning.

name: John Payton
headline: John Payton, Lawyer Who Fought for Civil Rights, Dies at 65
abstract: President of the NAACP Legal Defense and Educational Fund since 2008, Mr. Payton guided it to several major victories before the United States Supreme Court.

name: Cris Alexander
headline: Cris Alexander, Actor and Photographer, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Alexander had a major part in Broadway’s “On the Town” in 1944, but eventually made his name as a photographer.

name: Melvyn Kaufman
headline: Melvyn Kaufman, Whimsical Developer, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Kaufman, who erected half a dozen skyscrapers in Midtown Manhattan, had a fascination with office buildings as public spaces with which tenants and passers-by could engage.

name: Lincoln Hall
headline: Lincoln Hall, Climber Who Survived on Everest, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Hall was an Australian mountaineer who in May 2006 was rescued on Mount Everest after being left for dead and surviving a night alone at more than 28,000 feet.

name: Anita Steckel
headline: Anita Steckel, Artist Who Created Erotic Works, Dies at 82
abstract: After her erotic artworks that depicted nude male figures set off controversy, Ms. Steckel formed an organization of female artists, known as the Fight Censorship Group.

name: Irving Louis Horowitz
headline: Irving Louis Horowitz, Sociologist and Ideological Critic, Dies at 82
abstract: Professor Horowitz, an expert on C. Wright Mills, argued that left-wing advocacy was endangering an empirical approach to the social sciences.

name: Bert Sugar
headline: Bert Sugar, Boxing Writer and Commentator, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Mr. Sugar, who was elected to the International Boxing Hall of Fame in 2005, was a ubiquitous presence in the sport and wrote about it with swagger and style.

name: Priscilla Buckley
headline: Priscilla Buckley, Editor at National Review, Dies at 90
abstract: Miss Buckley was the longtime managing editor of National Review, the conservative magazine founded by her brother William F. Buckley Jr.

name: Larry Stevenson
headline: Larry Stevenson, Innovative Skateboard Designer, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Stevenson introduced the kicktail, a skateboard feature that made the aerial maneuvers that define contemporary skateboarding possible.

name: Henry S. Ruth
headline: Henry S. Ruth, Who Helped Lead Watergate Prosecution, Dies at 80
abstract: With the Justice Department, Mr. Ruth served as chief deputy and later special prosecutor in the Watergate break-in case.

name: Hilton Kramer
profession: Art Critic and Champion of Tradition in Culture Wars
headline: Hilton Kramer, Art Critic and Champion of Tradition in Culture Wars, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Kramer had an incisive style and combative temperament that made him one of the most influential critics of his era, both at The New York Times and The New Criterion, which he founded.

name: Eric Lowen
headline: Eric Lowen, Half of a Singing-Writing Duo, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Lowen and his longtime musical partner, Dan Navarro, wrote the Pat Benatar hit “We Belong,” then continued to write and perform together for over two decades.

name: Adrienne Rich
headline: Adrienne Rich, Influential Feminist Poet, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Rich, one of the most influential and widely read writers of the feminist movement, took on sexism and racial oppression in her poems and prose.

name: Ron Stewart
headline: Ron Stewart, Star of Maple Leafs Champs, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Stewart, a wing on three Stanley Cup championship teams of the Toronto Maple Leafs, was involved in an incident that led to the death of his Rangers teammate Terry Sawchuk.

name: Earl Scruggs
headline: Earl Scruggs, Bluegrass Pioneer, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Scruggs was a banjo player whose hard-driving picking style influenced a generation of players and helped shape the sound of 20th-century country music.

name: James Endler
profession: Oversaw Construction of World Trade Center
headline: James Endler, Who Oversaw Construction of World Trade Center, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Endler, an engineer, helped manage some of the biggest construction projects of the 1970s, ’80s and ’90s, including Epcot Center at Walt Disney World, and the Renaissance Center in Detroit.

name: Harry Crews
headline: Harry Crews, Writer of Dark Fiction, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Mr. Crews developed a cult following for violent yet sympathetic novels like “The Gospel Singer” and “The Knockout Artist.”

name: Warren Stevens
headline: Warren Stevens, Busy Character Actor, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Stevens was a lanky, square-jawed actor whose face became familiar through his more than 100 roles on television and in movies over six decades.

name: Shirley May France Setters
headline: Shirley May France Setters, Long-Distance Swimmer, Dies at 79
abstract: The Massachusetts woman won wide popularity despite several failures to reach England’s white cliffs of Dover from France.

name: Albert Hadley
headline: Albert Hadley, High Society’s Decorator, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Hadley was the creator of residences for a roster of clients with names like Astor, Paley, Rockefeller, Getty, Whitney and Mellon.

name: Roger C. Molander
headline: Roger C. Molander, Nuclear Protest Leader, Dies at 71
abstract: As a government analyst, Mr. Molander was shaken on hearing a military official say that “only 500 million people” would die in a nuclear war.

name: Patience Abbe
headline: Patience Abbe, Chronicler of Her Childhood Travels, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Abbe was the dominant voice in a best-selling childhood travelogue of voyaging through a turbulent Europe with her parents and younger brothers.

name: Edson W. Spencer
profession: Turned Honeywells Attention to the Skies
headline: Edson W. Spencer, Who Turned Honeywell’s Attention to the Skies, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Spencer began his career at Honeywell as an aeronautical engineer and ended it with a long tenure at the top, shifting the company away from computers and toward aeronautics.

name: Miguel de la Madrid
headline: Miguel de la Madrid, President of Mexico in 1980s, Dies at 77
abstract: His tenure marred by economic crisis and an earthquake, Mr. de la Madrid is credited for setting Mexico on a path to a free-market economy and, inadvertently, multiparty rule.

name: Paul S. Boyer
headline: Paul S. Boyer, 76, Dies; Historian Studied A-Bomb and Witches
abstract: Dr. Boyer, an intellectual historian, was known for research on the religious underpinnings of American culture, and especially on how Americans respond to perceived threats.

name: Paul D. Boyer
headline: Paul D. Boyer, 99, Dies; Nobel Winner Decoded Enzyme That Powers Life
abstract: He shared the 1997 prize in chemistry for his work on understanding how organisms get energy from their environments and process it to stay alive.

name: Charles Lockwood
headline: Charles Lockwood, Who Wrote the Row-House Bible, Dies at 63
abstract: A specialist in restoration, he chronicled and furthered the row-house revival that transformed many New York neighborhoods.

name: Giorgio Chinaglia
profession: Italian Star and the Cosmos Leader
headline: Giorgio Chinaglia, Italian Star and the Cosmos’ Leader, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Chinaglia came to the New York Cosmos professional soccer team as one of Europe’s greatest goal scorers, then attracted almost as much attention for his impenitent candor.

name: John Arden
headline: John Arden, British Playwright, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Arden, a major British playwright of the 1950s and 1960s, produced work that was politically engaged, theatrically inventive and conscience-provoking.

name: Elizabeth Catlett
profession: Sculptor With Eye on Social Issues
headline: Elizabeth Catlett, Sculptor With Eye on Social Issues, Is Dead at 96
abstract: Ms. Catlett’s abstracted sculptures of the human form reflected her deep concern with the African-American experience and the struggle for civil rights.

name: Bill Jenkins
headline: Bill Jenkins, 81, Drag Racing Driver and Innovator, Dies
abstract: Jenkins, an inductee in the Motorsports Hall of Fame of America, helped lift the National Hot Rod Association from the streets to the professional track.

name: Bill Jenkins
profession: Tried to Halt Tuskegee Syphilis Study
headline: Bill Jenkins, Who Tried to Halt Tuskegee Syphilis Study, Dies at 73
abstract: Black men were being used as guinea pigs, an alarmed Dr. Jenkins told his health agency supervisor, not knowing that the supervisor was involved.

name: Antonio Tabucchi
headline: Antonio Tabucchi, Elegiac Italian Writer, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Tabucchi, a distinguished Italian novelist, wrote novels that became a standard held aloft by opponents of the right-wing government of former Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi.

name: Robert R. Beezer
headline: Robert R. Beezer, Conservative Voice on Liberal Court, Dies at 83
abstract: In 28 years on the federal bench, Judge Beezer wrote influential opinions on capital punishment, copyright law on the Internet and Anna Nicole Smith’s claim to a huge inheritance.

name: Ferdinand A. Porsche
headline: Ferdinand A. Porsche, Designer of the 911, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Porsche, the creator of one of the most revered sports cars of the 20th century, was the scion of a German automaking family.

name: Joe Scarpa
profession: Gained Wrestling Fame as Chief Jay Strongbow
headline: Joe Scarpa, Who Gained Wrestling Fame as Chief Jay Strongbow, Dies
abstract: Scarpa became one of the best-known professional wrestlers of the 1970s and ’80s after he took on the persona of Chief Jay Strongbow.

name: Dale Corson
headline: Dale Corson, Cornell Administrator Who Helped Quell Protest, Dies at 97
abstract: Dr. Corson, a nuclear physicist, was Cornell’s provost during the 1960s, when students demanded a black studies program, and its president during the 1970s, when students protested the Vietnam War.

name: Gil Noble
profession: Host of Pioneering TV Show Focusing on Black Issues
headline: Gil Noble, Host of Pioneering TV Show Focusing on Black Issues, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Noble’s interviews on the weekly program called “Like It Is” comprised a veritable archive of contemporary black history in America.

name: Katherine Russell Rich
headline: Katherine Russell Rich, Who Wrote of Battle With Cancer, Dies at 56
abstract: Ms. Rich wrote a memoir about the daily trials encountered in a place she called Cancerland, and ended up living there far longer than the year or two she had expected.

name: Joe Avezzano
headline: Joe Avezzano, a Cowboys Coach for 3 Titles, Dies at 68
abstract: Avezzano coached the kicking and kick-return units for Dallas teams that won Super Bowls in the 1992, 1993 and 1995 seasons.

name: Elan Steinberg
headline: Elan Steinberg Dies at 59; Led World Jewish Congress
abstract: Mr. Steinberg brought what he called a new, “American style” assertiveness to the World Jewish Congress as its top executive.

name: Fang Lizhi
headline: Fang Lizhi, Chinese Physicist and Seminal Dissident, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Fang’s advocacy of economic and democratic freedoms shaped the brief era of student dissent in China that ended with the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests and his exile.

name: Thomas Kinkade
headline: Thomas Kinkade, Artist to Mass Market, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Kinkade, who was often disdained by the fine art establishment, made no apologies for commercializing the art field.

name: Mauricio Lasansky
headline: Mauricio Lasansky, Master Printmaker, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Lasansky was known for his multiprocess prints, as well as a series of drawings depicting the horrors of Nazism.

name: Edmund L. Epstein
headline: Edmund L. Epstein, Scholar Who Saved ‘Lord of the Flies,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Epstein was a Joyce scholar for most of his life, but he touched more readers with his decision to reprint a British book called “Lord of the Flies” as a paperback in the United States.

name: Mike Wallace
headline: Mike Wallace, CBS Pioneer of ‘60 Minutes,’ Dies at 93
abstract: A reporter with the presence of a performer, Mr. Wallace went head-to-head with chiefs of state, celebrities and con artists for more than 50 years.

name: Mike Wallace
profession: Wrote an Acclaimed History of New York
headline: Mike Wallace, Who Wrote an Acclaimed History of New York, Dies at 83
abstract: His 1998 book, “Gotham,” which told the city’s story to 1898, focused on social and economic conflict. It won a Pulitzer Prize and inspired two sequels.

name: Peter Douglas
headline: Peter Douglas, Sentry of California’s Coast, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Douglas helped created the state’s coastal commission, which limits construction, ensures public access to beaches and seeks to regulate offshore drilling.

name: Kenneth Libo
headline: Kenneth Libo, Scholar of Immigrant Life, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Libo’s research added a level of emotional detail to “World of Our Fathers,” Irving Howe’s landmark 1976 history of the East European Jewish migration to America.

name: Roger Furst
headline: Roger Furst Dies at 78; Equipped Mountaineers in the Northeast
abstract: Tired of bulky equipment, Mr. Furst co-founded the Eastern Mountain Sports retail chain with a fishing buddy, helping those in the Northeast ski in the backcountry and scale peaks.

name: Barney McKenna
headline: Barney McKenna, Banjo Player in the Dubliners, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. McKenna, known as Banjo Barney, played a raucous and often lyrically haunting banjo that helped propel the Irish folk band to fame.

name: Frank H. Strickler
headline: Frank H. Strickler, Watergate Defense Lawyer, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Strickler was a Washington lawyer who represented two of President Richard M. Nixon’s top aides in the aftermath of the 1972 Watergate break-in and subsequent cover-up.

name: Christine Brooke-Rose
headline: Christine Brooke-Rose, Inventive Writer, Dies at 89
abstract: The author of more than a dozen novels, as well as short stories, essays and criticism, Ms. Brooke-Rose was one of relatively few Britons to maintain a long association with experimental fiction.

name: Edward Harbert II
headline: Edward Harbert II, Who Led Times Productions, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Harbert led an early venture into television by The New York Times.

name: Jack Tramiel
headline: Jack Tramiel, a Pioneer in Computers, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Tramiel championed Commodore computers, inexpensive machines that were to personal computers what Henry Ford’s Model T was to automobiles.

name: Reed Whittemore
headline: Reed Whittemore, Former Poet Laureate, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Whittemore was also a biographer of poets, including William Carlos Williams.

name: Ahmed Ben Bella
headline: Ahmed Ben Bella, Revolutionary Who Led Algeria After Independence, Dies at 93
abstract: A man for whom life was combat, Mr. Ben Bella fought both for and against France, and in Algeria he went from being the president to being a prisoner.

name: Raymond Aubrac
profession: Exalted Leader of the French Resistance
headline: Raymond Aubrac, an Exalted Leader of the French Resistance, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Aubrac and his wife, Lucie, became symbols of heroism in their country’s fight against the Germans, who defeated France in 1940. Their story of valor and love was told in movies and books.

name: Lili Chookasian
profession: Contralto Praised for Her Velvety Voice
headline: Lili Chookasian, Contralto Praised for Her Velvety Voice, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Chookasian, praised for her immense and velvety voice, was a principal singer with the Metropolitan Opera, appearing there 290 times from 1962 to 1986.

name: Jamaa Fanaka
headline: Jamaa Fanaka, Film Director, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Fanaka, who found success with his 1979 film “Penitentiary,” also fought for the rights of black directors in Hollywood.

name: Jane Taylor
headline: Jane Taylor, Bassoonist of Dorian Quintet, Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. Taylor co-founded the Dorian Wind Quintet in 1961, and remained with it for 40 years as it became one of the premier ensembles to feature flute, oboe, clarinet, French horn and bassoon.

name: Luke Askew
headline: Luke Askew, Character Actor, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Mr. Askew was perhaps best known for his role as a wayward stranger in the 1969 film “Easy Rider.”

name: Claude Miller
headline: Claude Miller, Film Director and Truffaut Protégé, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Miller’s films often focused on troubled children and the bad hands dealt them by their parents. Mr. Miller had worked as an assistant director and production manager for François Truffaut.

name: Dora Saint
profession: k a Miss Read of Fiction Fame
headline: Dora Saint, a k a Miss Read of Fiction Fame, Dies at 98
abstract: Mrs. Saint’s gentle books, about the quaint and quirky English villages of Fairacre and Thrush Green, were a balm to postwar readers.

name: Andrew Love
profession: Tenor Saxophonist for the Memphis Horns
headline: Andrew Love, Tenor Saxophonist for the Memphis Horns, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Love, with his musical partner, the trumpeter Wayne Jackson, added blast to songs by Otis Redding, Aretha Franklin and many others.

name: Lester Breslow
profession: Linked Healthy Habits and Long Life
headline: Lester Breslow, Who Linked Healthy Habits and Long Life, Dies at 97
abstract: Dr. Breslow was a public health leader whose research gave mathematical proof to the notion that people can live longer and healthier by changing habits like smoking, diet and sleep.

name: Murray Rose
headline: Murray Rose, Australian Olympic Swimming Star, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Rose set 15 world records and won six Olympic medals, including four golds, becoming a sports hero in Australia before giving Hollywood a try.

name: Butch Bouchard
profession: Imposing Pillar of Montreal Canadiens Defense
headline: Butch Bouchard, Imposing Pillar of Montreal Canadiens’ Defense, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Bouchard was a stalwart defenseman for the Montreal Canadiens during 15 seasons in the 1940 and ’50s.

name: Lou Goldstein
profession: Borscht Belt Master of Simon Says
headline: Lou Goldstein, Borscht Belt Master of Simon Says, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Goldstein was a tummler, hired to amuse hotel guests with songs and shtick; few people could defeat him at Simon Says.

name: Lewis Nordan
headline: Lewis Nordan, Writer Who Spun Lyrical Tales, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Nordan’s best-known novel, “Wolf Whistle,” was based on the murder of Emmett Till in 1955.

name: Maersk Mc-Kinney Moeller
headline: Maersk Mc-Kinney Moeller, Longtime Shipping Magnate, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Mc-Kinney Moeller transformed his family’s shipping company, A. P. Moeller-Maersk Group, into the world’s largest.

name: Paul Bogart
headline: Paul Bogart, TV Director, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Bogart was recognized as a master of live television, from game shows to high drama, and later as the respected director of sitcoms like “All in the Family.”

name: William Finley
headline: William Finley, Actor in De Palma Movies, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Finley’s most famous role was in the 1974 cult classic “The Phantom of the Paradise.”

name: TV Emperor
headline: TV Emperor of Rock ’n’ Roll and New Year’s Eve Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Clark was the perpetually youthful-looking television host of “American Bandstand,” which advanced the influence of teenagers and rock ’n’ roll on American culture.

name: John Golding
headline: John Golding Dies at 82; Zeroed In on Abstraction
abstract: Mr. Golding, a British critic, scholar and painter, was an authority on Cubism.

name: Levon Helm
profession: Drummer and Rough-Throated Singer for the Band
headline: Levon Helm, Drummer and Rough-Throated Singer for the Band, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Helm, whose drumming merged muscle, swing, economy and finesse, helped forge a deep-rooted American music as a linchpin of the Band.

name: Stanley R. Resor
headline: Stanley R. Resor, Vietnam War Army Chief, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Resor, secretary of the Army from 1965 to 1971, oversaw the troop buildup in Vietnam and laid the groundwork for the all-volunteer Army.

name: Jonathan Frid
headline: Jonathan Frid, Ghoulish ‘Dark Shadows’ Star, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Frid was a Shakespearean actor who found unexpected, and by his own account unwanted, celebrity as the vampire Barnabas Collins in the cult soap opera.

name: Hillman Curtis
headline: Hillman Curtis, a Pioneer in Web Design, Dies at 51
abstract: Mr. Curtis, who called himself a serial self-reinventor, played in a rock band in the 1980s and early ’90s before teaching himself Web design and then moved on to film, his third career.

name: Teddy Charles
headline: Teddy Charles, Jazz Musician Turned Sea Captain, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Charles was a gifted vibraphonist who teamed up with many of the musicians who revolutionized jazz in the 1940s and ’50s and then literally sailed away to become a sea captain.

name: Martin Poll
profession: Built a Movie Studio in New York
headline: Martin Poll Dies at 89; Built a Movie Studio in New York
abstract: Mr. Poll helped revitalize film production in New York in the 1950s and ’60s and later made his name in Hollywood.

name: Charles W. Colson
headline: Charles W. Colson, Watergate Felon Who Became Evangelical Leader, Dies at 80
abstract: A political saboteur for President Richard M. Nixon, Mr. Colson masterminded some of the dirty tricks that led to the president’s downfall.

name: Alex Cassie
headline: Alex Cassie, Who Aided ‘Great Escape’ From Nazis, Dies at 95
abstract: Lieutenant Cassie forged documents for months, playing a central role in the larger conspiracy to free hundreds of the nearly 1,000 airmen in a Nazi prisoner-of-war camp.

name: Bert Weedon
headline: Bert Weedon, Guitar Teacher to a Generation, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Weedon’s instructional manual “Play in a Day” taught the instrument to budding guitarists like Eric Clapton, John Lennon and Paul McCartney.

name: John A. Hoyt
headline: John A. Hoyt, Champion for Animals, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Mr. Hoyt made the Humane Society of the United States the largest anticruelty organization in the country through a presence in Washington and an eye on realism.

name: Valeri Vasiliev
headline: Valeri Vasiliev, Defenseman on Soviet Hockey Dynasty, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Vasiliev won two Olympic gold medals and eight world championships with the Soviet teams of the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Bernard Rapoport
headline: Bernard Rapoport, Deep-Pocketed Texas Liberal, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Rapoport, who founded the American Income Life Insurance Company, used his wealth to support Democrats, Israel and the University of Texas.

name: George Rathmann
headline: George Rathmann, Amgen Chief, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Rathmann oversaw Amgen as it developed what would become two of the most successful drugs in history and became the world’s largest biotechnology company.

name: LeRoy T. Walker
headline: LeRoy T. Walker, a Pioneer of U.S. Olympics, Dies at 93
abstract: As the track and field coach at North Carolina Central in Durham, Mr. Walker developed Olympic medalists and numerous national champions.

name: Doris Betts
headline: Doris Betts, Novelist in Southern Tradition, Dies at 79
abstract: The characters in Mrs. Betts’s novels and short stories grappled with religious faith, freedom, captivity and original sin.

name: George Cowan
headline: George Cowan, Nuclear Scientist, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Cowan helped build the first atomic bomb and test the first hydrogen bomb.

name: Virginia Spencer Carr
headline: Virginia Spencer Carr, Literary Biographer, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Carr, a literary scholar whose book “The Lonely Hunter” remains the standard biography of Carson McCullers, also wrote about John Dos Passos and Paul Bowles.

name: Irving Millman
headline: Irving Millman Dies at 88; Worked to Stop Hepatitis B
abstract: A microbiologist, Dr. Millman helped develop not only a vaccine for hepatitis B but also a test for it.

name: Pete Fornatale
headline: Pete Fornatale, a Pioneer of FM Rock, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Fornatale was a free-form disc jockey when FM was coming of age in the 1960s. One of his signatures was playing songs that followed a theme.

name: Ernest Callenbach
headline: Ernest Callenbach, Author of ‘Ecotopia,’ Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Callenbach’s tale of an awakening paradise in the Pacific Northwest developed a devoted cult following as a harbinger of the environmental movement.

name: Hugo Fiorato
headline: Hugo Fiorato, Conductor at City Ballet, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Fiorato was a former child prodigy who would go on to become the conductor of the New York City Ballet and one of its most enduring influences.

name: Robert Miles Parker
headline: Robert Miles Parker, Artist and Preservationist, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Parker, discussing the theaters he drew, once said: “They’re full of ghosts. Theaters are phenomenally holy places.”

name: Bill Skowron
headline: Bill Skowron, Slugger in Yankee Golden Era, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Skowron, a first baseman known as Moose, played for the Yankees in the 1950s and early ’60s.

name: Enoch Williams
headline: Enoch Williams, New York Councilman, Dies at 84
abstract: A moderate Democrat, Mr. Williams used his leadership positions to pass a law banning smoking in most public spaces and to help stop the Giuliani administration from selling city-owned hospitals.

name: Joe Muranyi
headline: Joe Muranyi, Clarinetist for Louis Armstrong, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Muranyi was among a handful of jazz musicians who began their careers in the 1950s but looked to an earlier era for inspiration.

name: Amos Vogel
headline: Amos Vogel, Champion of Films, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Vogel, founder of the Cinema 16 film society, provided a place for daring filmmakers to find an audience.

name: Richard Bellman
headline: Richard Bellman, Lawyer Who Fought Discrimination, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Bellman fought local governments over racially discriminatory zoning, including in a landmark case against Mount Laurel, N.J., in 1975.

name: George Vujnovich
headline: George Vujnovich is Dead at 96; Led War Rescue
abstract: Mr. Vujnovich planned and ran a World War II rescue mission that recovered 500 downed Allied airmen from German-occupied Yugoslavia.

name: Moscelyne Larkin
headline: Moscelyne Larkin, a Founder of Tulsa Ballet, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Ms. Larkin was one of a group of five famous dancers of American Indian descent.

name: Benzion Netanyahu
headline: Benzion Netanyahu, Hawkish Scholar, Dies at 102
abstract: Mr. Netanyahu, the father of the Israeli prime minister, fought for the creation of the Jewish state by lobbying in the United States.

name: Bob Smith
headline: Bob Smith, Inventor of Fog-Free Ski Goggles, Dies at 78
abstract: Dr. Smith, an orthodontist, designed ski goggles that led to today’s fog-free and condensation-free goggles.

name: Bob Smith
headline: Bob Smith, Groundbreaking Gay Comedian, Is Dead at 59
abstract: His 1994 appearance on “The Tonight Show” is widely regarded as the first by an openly gay comic. But Lou Gehrig’s disease cut his stand-up career short.

name: Fred Hakim
headline: Fred Hakim, Times Square Hot-Dog Vendor, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Hakim took over a hot-dog counter on 42nd Street from his father, but the business fell victim to the city’s revitalization efforts in Times Square in the 1990s.

name: Amarillo Slim
headline: Amarillo Slim, Gambler With a Sly Wit, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Slim won five times in World Series of Poker events and was elected to at least four gambling halls of fame.

name: Tomás Borge Martínez
profession: Sandinista Rebel and Nicaragua Interior Minister
headline: Tomás Borge Martínez, Sandinista Rebel and Nicaragua Interior Minister, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Borge, the last surviving founder of the Sandinista rebel group that toppled Nicaragua’s dictatorship in 1979, went from student radical to one of the leading officials of his nation’s government.

name: Norman Fruman
headline: Norman Fruman, a Scholar of Coleridge, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Fruman roiled literary waters in the 1970s with a biography of Samuel Taylor Coleridge that accused the poet of stealing ideas.

name: Greg Jackson
headline: Greg Jackson Dies at 60; Ran a Haven in Brooklyn
abstract: Mr. Jackson turned a recreation center in Brownsville into a hive of activity for children and adults.

name: Earl Rose
headline: Earl Rose, Coroner When Kennedy Was Shot, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Rose, the Dallas County medical examiner in 1963, waged an unsuccessful battle to perform the autopsy on the assassinated president.

name: Fuzzy Levane
profession: Fixture of New York City Basketball
headline: Fuzzy Levane, Fixture of New York City Basketball, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Levane was head coach of the Knicks during the 1958-59 season, leading them to a 40-32 record, a second-place finish in the N.B.A.’s Eastern Division and a playoff appearance.

name: Floyd D. Hall
headline: Floyd D. Hall, Head of Eastern Airlines, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Hall, who helped to resuscitate Trans World Airlines, did not fare so well after moving to Eastern in the early 1960s.

name: Charles Higham
headline: Charles Higham, Celebrity Biographer, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Higham, whose books drew vast attention for their memorably vast claims, wrote a number of biographies on some of Hollywood’s biggest stars.

name: David Bowman
headline: David Bowman, Satirical Novelist, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Bowman was a novelist and cultural critic whose first books, “Let the Dog Drive” and “Bunny Modern,” received wide praise in the 1990s for their satirical voice.

name: Adam Yauch
headline: Rapper Conquered Music World in ’80s With Beastie Boys
abstract: Mr. Yauch, whose nom de rap was MCA, helped make the first hip-hop album to top the Billboard chart, and later became involved in championing freedom in Tibet.

name: Phoebe Jacobs
headline: Phoebe Jacobs, Publicist for Jazz Greats, Dies at 93
abstract: In a sprawling behind-the-scenes career in jazz, primarily in publicity, Ms. Jacobs worked for some of the biggest stars in the field.

name: Zvi Zeitlin
headline: Zvi Zeitlin, Violinist Who Championed Modernist Composers, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Zeitlin was an internationally renowned violinist who was closely associated with the work of modernist composers like Aaron Copland and Lukas Foss.

name: Frank H. Pearl
profession: Publisher With a Zeal for the Serious
headline: Frank H. Pearl, Publisher With a Zeal for the Serious, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Pearl was a lawyer and investor in Washington who entered the book business on a quest to publish the serious, quality literature that he felt large corporate publishing houses had neglected.

name: Bill Granger
headline: Bill Granger, Journalist Turned Author of Fiction, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Granger, who was once a Chicago newspaperman, also wrote more than a score of mysteries and spy thrillers, many of which evoked the rougher environs of Chicago.

name: Bill Granger
headline: Bill Granger, Chef Who Brought Avocado Toast to the World, Dies at 54
abstract: His breakfast cuisine catapulted Australian cafe culture to international acclaim, although some saw his best-known dish as an example of millennial excess.

name: Margie Stewart
profession: WWII Pinup Girl With Wholesome Air
headline: Margie Stewart, WWII Pinup Girl With Wholesome Air, Dies at 92
abstract: A wholesome-looking pinup girl who hit a tender spot in homesick soldiers’ hearts.

name: George Lindsey
headline: George Lindsey, TV’s Goober Pyle, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Lindsey introduced the character of Goober — the quintessential grinning hayseed, equal parts annoying and endearing — on “The Andy Griffith Show.”

name: Bob Stewart
headline: Bob Stewart, Inventor of Game Shows, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Stewart was a television producer with a penchant for transforming the seemingly mundane into blockbuster shows like “The Price Is Right” and “To Tell the Truth.”

name: Carl Bernadotte
headline: Carl Bernadotte, Prince Whose First Loyalty Was Love, Dies at 95
abstract: The former Swedish prince, whom the Grand Duchess of Luxembourg made a count five years after he wed Kerstin Wijkmark, became a businessman in Manhattan.

name: Maurice Sendak
headline: Maurice Sendak, Author of Splendid Nightmares, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Sendak, known in particular for “Where the Wild Things Are,” was widely considered the most important children’s book artist of the 20th century.

name: Digby Wolfe
headline: Digby Wolfe, ‘Laugh-In’ Writer, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Wolfe, who got his start at the BBC, went on to help start up a zany American comedy.

name: Roman Totenberg
headline: Roman Totenberg, Violinist and Teacher, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Totenberg influenced generations of musicians, and appeared on countless recordings.

name: Mort Lindsey
profession: TV Bandleader and Accompanist to Stars
headline: Mort Lindsey, TV Bandleader and Accompanist to Stars, Dies at 89
abstract: Working with luminaries like Merv Griffin on television, Barbra Streisand in Central Park and Judy Garland at Carnegie Hall, Mr. Lindsey had a musical career spanning six decades.

name: Nicholas Katzenbach
headline: Nicholas Katzenbach, 90, Dies; Policy Maker at ’60s Turning Points
abstract: Mr. Katzenbach, an attorney general under President Lyndon B. Johnson, tackled segregation, the Cuban missile crisis, Vietnam War strategy and the Kennedy assassination in his government service.

name: Vidal Sassoon
headline: Vidal Sassoon, Hairdresser and Trendsetter, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Sassoon changed the way women wore and cared for their hair, fashioning short, often striking styles known for their geometric shapes and sharp angles that were also easy to maintain.

name: C. David Heymann
profession: Biographer of the Rich and Famous
headline: C. David Heymann, Biographer of the Rich and Famous, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Heymann’s biographies were admired for their comprehensiveness and criticized for their use of single sources to reconstruct historical events.

name: Carroll Shelby
headline: Carroll Shelby, Car Builder Who Added Muscle to American Racing, Dies at 89
abstract: After he quit driving, Mr. Shelby began building his Cobras in 1962, and his company became one of the most successful independent sports-car builders of the era.

name: Evelyn B. Johnson
headline: Evelyn B. Johnson, Pilot and Instructor, Dies at 102
abstract: No woman has piloted an airplane more than Mrs. Johnson, who flew 5.5 million miles and the equivalent of more than six and a half years in flight hours.

name: Joyce Redman
headline: Joyce Redman, Actress Who Feasted on Many Roles, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Redman was widely acclaimed for her intelligent stage presence in Shakespearean drama and French comedy.

name: E. J. Potter
headline: E. J. Potter, ‘Michigan Madman’ of Motorcycle Racing, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Potter reached incredibly high speeds on motorcycles he modified himself, including one that he rigged with a Chevy V-8 and another that he fitted with a jet engine.

name: Louis H. Pollak
profession: Civil Rights Advocate and Federal Judge
headline: Louis H. Pollak, Civil Rights Advocate and Federal Judge, Dies at 89
abstract: Judge Pollak, who was recruited to the NAACP Legal Defense Fund, worked on Brown v. Board of Education and later argued successfully on behalf of convicted Freedom Riders before the Supreme Court.

name: Angelica Garnett
profession: Writer of Frank Memoir of Bloomsbury Childhood
headline: Angelica Garnett, Writer of Frank Memoir of Bloomsbury Childhood, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Garnett, the last direct link to the Bloomsbury set, was raised amid secrets by parents who prized literature, art and sex.

name: Horst Faas
headline: Horst Faas, Photographer Who Showed Horrors of War, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Faas, a two-time Pulitzer Prize-winning war photographer who later was editor of The Associated Press staff in Saigon, produced the most haunting photographs of the Vietnam War.

name: Duck Dunn
profession: Bassist in Booker T. and the MGs
headline: Duck Dunn, Bassist in Booker T. and the MG’s, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Dunn’s simple but inventive bass playing helped define the sound of Memphis soul music.

name: Everett Lilly
headline: Everett Lilly, Bluegrass Musician, Dies at 87
abstract: When Mr. Lilly and his brother moved from West Virginia to Boston in 1952, they brought bluegrass and old-time music with them to the Northeast.

name: Mike McGrady
headline: Mike McGrady, Known for a Literary Hoax, Dies at 78
abstract: As a Newsday journalist, Mr. McGrady led his colleagues in the creation of “Naked Came the Stranger,” a steamy parody novel.

name: Carlos Fuentes
headline: Carlos Fuentes, Mexican Man of Letters, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Fuentes was Mexico’s elegant public intellectual and grand man of letters whose panoramic novels captured the complicated essence of his country’s history.

name: Harold A. Poling
headline: Harold A. Poling, 86, a Chairman of Ford, Dies
abstract: Mr. Poling rose through the ranks with a management style that brought stability in tough times.

name: James Abdnor
headline: James Abdnor, Former South Dakota Senator, Dies at 89
abstract: James Abdnor, a Republican, served four terms in the House and one in the Senate after defeating George S. McGovern in 1980.

name: Jean Craighead George
headline: Jean Craighead George, Children’s Author, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. George’s home held a menagerie, as did her books, most of them written for children and young adults.

name: Donna Summer
headline: Donna Summer, Queen of Disco Who Transcended the Era, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Summer was a five-time Grammy winner who became a superstar in the 1970s with hits like “Last Dance.”

name: Chuck Brown
headline: Chuck Brown, Godfather of Go-Go, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Brown became a local hero in Washington for creating a strutting funk variant that is the city’s signature dance genre.

name: Dietrich Fischer-Dieskau
headline: Dietrich Fischer-Dieskau, Lyrical and Powerful Baritone, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Fischer-Dieskau’s beautiful voice and mastery of technique made him the 20th century’s pre-eminent interpreter of art songs.

name: Ed Ray
headline: Ed Ray, Bus Driver During Kidnapping, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Ray was hailed as a hero in 1976 for leading 26 children to safety after they were all kidnapped and buried below ground in a truck trailer.

name: Archie Peck
headline: Archie Peck, Competitive Croquet Star, Dies at 76
abstract: A six-time national champion, commonly called Silky Legs, Mr. Peck was known for his rugged good looks, effortless athleticism and aggressive style of play.

name: Barbara D’Arcy White
headline: Barbara D’Arcy White, Interior Design Guru, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. D’Arcy was an interior decorator whose eclectic sense of style helped change Americans’ taste in home furnishings in the 1950s, ’60s and ’70s, when she worked at Bloomingdale’s.

name: Crawford Greenewalt Jr.
profession: Shed Light on an Ancient City
headline: Crawford Greenewalt Jr., Who Shed Light on an Ancient City, Dies at 74
abstract: Professor Greenewalt, an archaeologist, transformed scholars’ understanding of Sardis, now western Turkey.

name: Peter D. Fuller
headline: Peter D. Fuller Dies at 89; Had to Return Derby Purse
abstract: The owner of Dancer’s Image, Mr. Fuller had to return his Kentucky Derby winner’s purse of $122,600 after the painkiller Phenylbutazone was found in the horse’s urine.

name: Herbert Breslin
headline: Herbert Breslin, Pavarotti’s Hard-Driving Manager, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Breslin was the brash publicist and manager of the tenor Luciano Pavarotti who described his philosophy this way: “Marketing an artist is basically like marketing a bar of soap.”

name: Walter Wink
headline: Walter Wink, Theologian and Author, Dies at 76
abstract: A liberal scholar, Dr. Wink’s views on homosexuality, nonviolence and the nature of Jesus caused many theologians to bridle.

name: Megrahi
headline: Megrahi, Convicted in 1988 Lockerbie Bombing, Dies at 60
abstract: Abdel Basset Ali al-Megrahi was the only person convicted in the attack on Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland, which killed 270 people.

name: Robin Gibb
profession: Bee Gee With a Taciturn Manner
headline: Robin Gibb, a Bee Gee With a Taciturn Manner, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Gibb was the second member of this brother act, whose sound helped define the disco era, to die.

name: Frederick J. Brown
headline: Frederick J. Brown, Painter of Musicians, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Brown explored the relationship between music and painting in portraits of hundreds of jazz and blues artists.

name: Eugene Polley
headline: Eugene Polley, Conjuror of a Device That Changed TV Habits, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Polley, a Zenith engineer, invented the Flash-Matic remote control for television, and spent years reminding people he was the device’s sole inventor.

name: Katie Beckett
headline: Katie Beckett, Who Inspired Health Reform, Dies at 34
abstract: Kathleen Sebelius, the secretary of health and human services, called Ms. Beckett “an inadvertent pioneer in the civil rights movement for people with disabilities.”

name: Jean Pakter
profession: Made New York a Model for Safe Abortions
headline: Jean Pakter, Who Made New York a Model for Safe Abortions, Dies at 101
abstract: As head of the city’s maternity services bureau, Dr. Pakter supported a law that legalized abortion in New York before Roe v. Wade, and one of her studies led to a breakthrough in care for premature babies.

name: Henry Denker
headline: Henry Denker, Author in Many Genres, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Denker’s large output ranged from novels and movies to TV and Broadway plays.

name: Paul Fussell
headline: Paul Fussell, Literary Scholar and Critic, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Fussell, a wide-ranging author, may be best remembered for “The Great War and Modern Memory,” his study of World War I and the influence of its horrors on art and literature.

name: Hal Jackson
headline: Hal Jackson, 96, New York Broadcaster Who Broke Racial Barriers in Radio, Dies
abstract: Mr. Jackson, a major presence on New York City airwaves for decades, influenced generations of broadcasters.

name: Eddie Blazonczyk
headline: Eddie Blazonczyk, 70, Polka Singer and Bandleader, Dies
abstract: Mr. Blazonczyk was a former rock ’n’ roller who switched to polka and found lasting success, winning a Grammy and vigorously touring.

name: Edoardo Mangiarotti
headline: Edoardo Mangiarotti, Olympian Fencer, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Mangiarotti, of Italy, won more Olympic medals and world championships than any fencer in the history of the sport, starting with the Berlin Games in 1936.

name: H. H. Brookins
headline: H. H. Brookins, Influential A.M.E. Bishop, Dies at 86
abstract: As a leader of the African Methodist Episcopal Church, Bishop Brookins marched with the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. in the South and mentored other important civil rights figures.

name: Carrie Smith
profession: Singer in Black and Blue on Broadway
headline: Carrie Smith, Singer in ‘Black and Blue’ on Broadway, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Smith, who sang at the 1957 Newport Jazz Festival as well as Carnegie Hall, earned a reputation as a blues belter.

name: Everett Ortner
headline: Everett Ortner, Leader in Brooklyn Brownstones’ Revival, Dies at 92
abstract: With his wife, Evelyn, Mr. Ortner promoted a vision of Park Slope and other neighborhoods that led to the restoration of the splendor of fading buildings.

name: Al Gordon
profession: Skit Writer for Benny and Burnett
headline: Al Gordon, Skit Writer for Benny and Burnett, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Gordon also came up with jokes for the Smothers Brothers, Flip Wilson and Carol Channing.

name: Doug Dillard
headline: Doug Dillard, Bluegrass Banjo Virtuoso, Dies at 75
abstract: In the early 1960s, Mr. Dillard helped to introduce a generation of listeners to bluegrass, ending the decade as an early advocate of country-rock.

name: Howie Richmond
headline: Howie Richmond, Music Publisher, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Richmond, with a diverse stable of artists, was among the last of a Runyonesque breed that was long a vital if largely unheralded segment of the music business.

name: Johnny Tapia
headline: Johnny Tapia, Champion Boxer Amid Chaos, Dies at 45
abstract: Tapia won titles in three weight divisions but struggled with mental illness and addiction, having been declared clinically dead five times as a result of drug overdoses.

name: Doc Watson
headline: Doc Watson, Blind Guitar Wizard Who Influenced Generations, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Watson’s flat-picking style elevated the acoustic guitar to solo status in bluegrass and country music, and his interpretations of traditional American music influenced generations of guitarists.

name: Marina Keegan
headline: Marina Keegan, Journalist and Playwright, Dies at 22
abstract: Ms. Keegan, a Yale graduate, encouraged students to resist careers in finance.

name: Kathi Kamen Goldmark
headline: Kathi Kamen Goldmark, Writers’ Catalyst, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Goldmark formed a rock band with best-selling authors like Stephen King and Amy Tan.

name: Richard W. Lyman
headline: Richard W. Lyman, Ex-President of Stanford University, Dies at 88
abstract: As president in the 1970s, Mr. Lyman shepherded the university through an era of political turbulence.

name: Lee Rich
profession: Helped Create Both J.R. and John-Boy
headline: Lee Rich Dies at 93; Helped Create Both J.R. and John-Boy
abstract: Mr. Rich was a founder of Lorimar Productions, which developed “Dallas,” “The Waltons” and many other hit TV shows and films.

name: Michael J. O’Neill
headline: Michael J. O’Neill, Ex-Editor of The Daily News, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. O’Neill directed the breathless coverage of the “Son of Sam” serial killer, but then became a strong national voice for responsible media behavior.

name: Leo Dillon
headline: Leo Dillon, Celebrated Illustrator of Children’s Books, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Dillon, with his wife and collaborator, Diane, was one of the world’s pre-eminent illustrators for young people.

name: Dudley Clendinen
headline: Dudley Clendinen, Reporter and Editor, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Clendinen, a seasoned journalist, spent his final years writing about his own approaching death as a gay alcoholic victim of Lou Gehrig’s disease.

name: Jack Twyman
profession: N.B.A. Star Known for Off-Court Assist
headline: Jack Twyman, N.B.A. Star Known for Off-Court Assist, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Twyman, a Hall of Fame basketball player, became the legal guardian for his teammate Maurice Stokes, who sustained a paralyzing brain injury during the 1958 season.

name: Klaas Faber
headline: Klaas Faber, War Criminal Who Escaped Punishment, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Faber, a Nazi collaborator, was convicted of taking part in killings at three Dutch locations. He escaped prison and lived in Germany for nearly 60 years.

name: Kaneto Shindo
headline: Kaneto Shindo, Wide-Ranging Filmmaker, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Shindo, who directed nearly 50 movies, was perhaps best known for films with themes relating to the wartime atomic devastation in his native Japan.

name: Jim Paratore
headline: Jim Paratore, Co-Creator of TMZ, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Paratore was a television executive and producer who partnered with Harvey Levin to create the entertainment Web site TMZ.

name: Dick Beals
headline: Dick Beals, Actor Who Gave a Voice to Gumby and Speedy, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Beals, whose youthful voice resulted from a childhood glandular problem, made a long career of playing children and childlike characters on television shows and commercials.

name: Orlando Woolridge
headline: Orlando Woolridge, N.B.A. Star and W.N.B.A. Coach, Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. Woolridge, a flashy forward, played for seven N.B.A teams over 13 seasons and coached the women’s professional team the Los Angeles Sparks.

name: Earl Shorris
headline: Earl Shorris, 75, Dies; Fought Poverty With Knowledge
abstract: Mr. Shorris created the Clemente Course in the Humanities, a free class in philosophy, the arts and history for the poor and forgotten.

name: William Hanley
headline: William Hanley, Playwright and TV Writer, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Hanley, an acclaimed playwright, went on to win two Emmys for his television scripts.

name: Richard Dawson
headline: Richard Dawson, Host Who Kissed on ‘Family Feud’, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Dawson gained initial fame in the 1960s playing Cpl. Peter Newkirk, a con man, forger and pickpocket, in the CBS series “Hogan’s Heroes.”

name: Adolfo Calero
headline: Adolfo Calero, Contra Leader in Nicaragua, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Mr. Calero played a major role in the Iran-contra scandal, lobbying in Washington for aid and testifying before Congress when it began investigating the Reagan administration’s efforts.

name: LeRoy Ellis
profession: Star Big Man at St. Johns
headline: LeRoy Ellis, a Star Big Man at St. John’s, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Ellis, a center, was on the outstanding St. John’s teams of the early 1960s and went on to win an N.B.A. championship with the Lakers in 1972.

name: Andrew Huxley
headline: Andrew Huxley, Nobel-Winning Physiologist, Dies at 94
abstract: Professor Huxley shared the 1963 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for a breakthrough discovery that helped better understand the electrical stimulation of nerve cells.

name: Pedro Borbon
headline: Pedro Borbon, Helped Reds Win 2 Titles, Dies at 65
abstract: Borbon appeared in more games than any other National League pitcher from 1970 to 1978, and he helped Cincinnati win back-to-back World Series titles.

name: Randy Paar
headline: Randy Paar, Talk-Show Host’s Daughter and Guest, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Paar is remembered by many 1950s and ’60s television viewers as the cute, precocious girl whom her father, the late-night talk-show host Jack Paar, introduced to a national audience.

name: Ada María Isasi-Díaz
headline: Ada María Isasi-Díaz, Dissident Catholic Theologian, Dies at 69
abstract: Dr. Isasi-Díaz was a university professor who pushed for more representation for Catholic Hispanic women in the church and advocated for the ordination of women as priests.

name: William Lee Miller
headline: William Lee Miller, Scholar on Abraham Lincoln, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Professor Miller, who taught at the University of Virginia, wove the national debate over slavery into his books about Abraham Lincoln and John Quincy Adams.

name: Herb Reed
headline: Herb Reed, an Original Platter, Dies at 83
abstract: The Platters, with hits like “Only You” and “The Great Pretender,” were one of the first groups to be promoted across racial barriers. Mr. Reed was credited with naming the group in 1953.

name: Eduard Khil
headline: Eduard Khil, Unlikely YouTube Sensation, Dies at 77
abstract: It wasn’t clear if the audience was laughing with him or at him, but the classically trained Mr. Khil enjoyed the Internet acclaim his very sunny rendition of a wordless song brought him.

name: Ray Bradbury
profession: Brought Mars to Earth With a Lyrical Mastery
headline: Ray Bradbury, Who Brought Mars to Earth With a Lyrical Mastery, Dies at 91
abstract: The imaginative evocations of the future in Mr. Bradbury’s science fiction reflected both the optimism and the anxieties of his own postwar America.

name: Pete Cosey
headline: Pete Cosey, Guitarist With Miles Davis, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Cosey became best known for his work in Miles Davis’s electric band of 1973-75.

name: Eugene Ferkauf
headline: Eugene Ferkauf, 91, Dies; Restyled Retail
abstract: Mr. Ferkauf was the founder of the E. J. Korvette chain of discount department stores, whose 1950s strategy of low prices, quick turnover and high volume helped shape today’s retail landscape.

name: Rosa Guy
profession: Author of Forthright Novels for Young People
headline: Rosa Guy, 89, Author of Forthright Novels for Young People, Dies
abstract: Ms. Guy, a Caribbean-born novelist, was widely considered one of the 20th century’s most distinguished writers for young adults.

name: Barry Unsworth
headline: Barry Unsworth, Writer of Historical Fiction, Dies at 81
abstract: A writer of prose distinguished by deep research and powerful narrative force, Mr. Unsworth won a Booker Prize in 1992 for “Sacred Hunger.”

name: Nolan Miller
headline: Nolan Miller, Designer of ‘Dynasty’ Power Looks, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Miller’s over-the-top glamour for the “Dynasty” TV series, which influenced a decade of power dressing, included sequined gowns, luncheon suits and the occasional turban.

name: Vladimir Krutov
profession: Wing for Soviet Hockey Teams in the 80s
headline: Vladimir Krutov, Wing for Soviet Hockey Teams in the ’80s, Dies at 52
abstract: Krutov played on teams that won gold medals in the 1984 and 1988 Olympics and a silver medal in 1980, when the United States defeated the Soviets in the Miracle on Ice game at Lake Placid.

name: David L. Rimoin
headline: David L. Rimoin, Geneticist and Expert on Dwarfism, Dies at 75
abstract: Dr. Rimoin made major discoveries on skeletal disorders and helped develop large-scale testing for inherited diseases.

name: David M. Helpern
profession: Chief of Joan & David Apparel Brand
headline: David M. Helpern, Chief of Joan & David Apparel Brand, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Helpern, the chief executive of the business, and his wife, the designer and creative director, built their company into a retail preserve of high-quality, moderately priced stylishness.

name: Anna Teresa Callen
headline: Anna Teresa Callen, Teacher of Italian Cooking, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Callen was a successful cookbook author who specialized in the regional food of Italy.

name: Friedrich Hirzebruch
headline: Friedrich Hirzebruch, Mathematician, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Hirzebruch helped revive the German mathematical community after World War II and worked on unifying disparate parts of mathematics.

name: Willard Bond
headline: Willard Bond, Vivid Artist of Yachting, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Bond was known for his ability to capture on the canvas the look of boat races, as well as the feel of them.

name: Phillip V. Tobias
headline: Phillip V. Tobias, Who Analyzed Apelike Fossils, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Dr. Tobias, a South African paleoanthropologist who fiercely opposed apartheid, set the benchmark for meticulous analyses of fossil remains.

name: Frank Cady
headline: Frank Cady, Kept Store on ‘Green Acres,’ Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Cady was best known for playing Sam Drucker on the popular 1960s sitcoms “Green Acres” and “Petticoat Junction.”

name: Wayne Roberts
headline: Wayne Roberts, ‘Stay High 149’ in Graffiti Circles, Is Dead at 61
abstract: Mr. Roberts left the New York graffiti scene for 25 years but, when he returned, was remembered for his work, including his “Smoker” tag, based on the haloed stick figure from “The Saint” TV series.

name: Elinor Ostrom
headline: Elinor Ostrom, Winner of Nobel in Economics, Dies at 78
abstract: Professor Ostrom’s prizewinning work examined how people collaborate and organize themselves to manage common resources like forests or fisheries, even when governments are not involved.

name: Ann Rutherford
headline: Ann Rutherford, Studio Film Sweetheart, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Rutherford, a Hollywood actress cast in innocent parts, also played Scarlett O’Hara’s sister in “Gone With the Wind.”

name: Ghassan Tueni
headline: Ghassan Tueni, Top Lebanese Journalist, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Tueni was considered the foremost journalist in Lebanon, if not the Arab world, and in the vanguard of a generation of postwar Arab intellectuals.

name: Teófilo Stevenson
headline: Teófilo Stevenson, Cuban Boxing Great, Dies at 60
abstract: With formidable size and a powerful right hand, the Cuban heavyweight won three Olympic gold medals. He had 301 victories in 321 bouts over a 20-year career.

name: Henry Hill
headline: Henry Hill, Mobster and Movie Inspiration, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Hill, a soldier in the Luchese crime family until he turned government witness, was portrayed in Martin Scorsese’s acclaimed film “Goodfellas.”

name: Ruth Sims
profession: First Woman Elected to Lead Greenwich
headline: Ruth Sims, First Woman Elected to Lead Greenwich, Dies at 92
abstract: Mrs. Sims, a Democrat in the historically Republican Connecticut town, succeeded in the 1977 race for first selectman after two recounts and a second vote.

name: Dave Boswell
headline: Dave Boswell, Pitcher Who Fought Billy Martin, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Boswell, a former Twins pitcher, won 20 games in 1969 but his accomplishment was overshadowed by an off-the-field brawl with his manager.

name: Mehdi Hassan
headline: Mehdi Hassan, Who Sang Urdu Lyric Verse, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Hassan’s baritone was heard both at royal courts and on the soundtracks of more than 300 movies.

name: F. Herbert Bormann
headline: F. Herbert Bormann Dies at 90; Helped Discover Acid Rain Threat
abstract: Dr. Bormann, an ecologist who taught at Dartmouth and Yale, spotted the new environmental danger with a team of scientists while doing research in a New Hampshire forest in 1971.

name: Richard F. Stolz
profession: Headed C.I.A. Spy Operations After Iran-Contra
headline: Richard F. Stolz Dies at 86; Headed C.I.A. Spy Operations After Iran-Contra
abstract: Mr. Stolz, who had retired from the agency in 1981 after failing to get a deputy director post, was called back to help repair its image.

name: William Knowles
headline: William Knowles, Nobel Winner in Chemistry, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Knowles’s work helped to advance treatment for Parkinson’s disease.

name: Reggie Pearman
headline: Reggie Pearman, Postwar Middle-Distance Runner, Dies at 89
abstract: A top national competitor in events of 440, 600, 880 and 1,000 yards, Reggie Pearman was one of America’s outstanding middle-distance runners in the post-World War II era.

name: Judy Freudberg
profession: Writer for Sesame Street for 35 Years
headline: Judy Freudberg, a Writer for ‘Sesame Street’ for 35 Years, Dies at 62
abstract: Ms. Freudberg, who started in the show’s music department, shared more than 15 daytime Emmys.

name: Nayef bin Abdul Aziz
headline: Nayef bin Abdul Aziz, Saudi Crown Prince Who Led Crackdown on Al Qaeda, Dies at 78
abstract: The death of Crown Prince Nayef bin Abdul Aziz al-Saud reopens the question of succession in this crucial American ally and oil powerhouse for the second time in less than a year.

name: Eugene Selznick
headline: Eugene Selznick, Beach Volleyball Pioneer, Dies at 82
abstract: An accomplished former player and coach, Eugene Selznick helped to promote beach volleyball, which became an Olympic sport in 1996.

name: Steve Ben Israel
headline: Steve Ben Israel, a Living Theater Performance Artist, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Israel, who toured for 15 years with the avant-garde group Living Theater, sought to undermine capitalist society with comedy.

name: Paul Jenkins
headline: Paul Jenkins, Painter of Abstract Artwork, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Jenkins, an Abstract Expressionist, was a friend of Mark Rothko and adopted techniques similar to those of Jackson Pollock.

name: Rodney King
headline: Rodney King Dies at 47; Police Beating Victim Who Asked ‘Can We All Get Along?’
abstract: Mr. King, whose 1991 videotaped beating by the Los Angeles police became a symbol of racial tensions and led to deadly race riots after the officers were acquitted, was found dead at 47.

name: Bob Chappuis
profession: Halfback Rescued in World War II
headline: Bob Chappuis, Halfback Rescued in World War II, Dies at 89
abstract: During World War II, Chappuis’s bomber was shot down, and he was hidden from the Nazis by an Italian family before returning to play at Michigan.

name: Barton Lidice Benes
headline: Barton Lidice Benes, Provocative Artist, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Benes, a New York sculptor who worked in materials that he called artifacts of everyday life, was acclaimed for confronting the toll of the AIDS epidemic.

name: Erica Kennedy
headline: Erica Kennedy, a Music Writer Who Satirized the Hip-Hop World, Dies at 42
abstract: Ms. Kennedy, who gave chick lit a black focus, rose to prominence with her roman à clef “Bling,” in 2004.

name: R. C. Owens
headline: R. C. Owens, Receiver Who Made the Alley-Oop Famous, Dies at 77
abstract: The former wide receiver for the San Francisco 49ers, known for kangaroolike leaps above defenders to catch passes, introduced a new phrase to sports.

name: Owens
headline: Major Owens, 77, Education Advocate in Congress, Dies
abstract: Mr. Owens, a state senator and a former chief administrator of New York City’s antipoverty program, went to Congress from Brooklyn and remained there for 24 years.

name: Dan Dorfman
headline: Dan Dorfman, 82, Dies; His Tips Moved Markets
abstract: Mr. Dorfman’s televised market reports could send a stock soaring — or plummeting — but his career was tarnished by accusations of insider trading.

name: Victor Spinetti
headline: Victor Spinetti, Favorite in Beatles Films, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Spinetti, a film and stage actor, won a Tony Award but was best known for appearing in all of the Beatles’ movies.

name: Norman Lent
headline: Norman Lent, Moderate Congressman Who Served 11 Terms, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Lent, a Republican who represented a large swath of Long Island’s South Shore, was a significant voice in shaping environmental legislation, despite always being in the minority.

name: Andrew Sarris
headline: Andrew Sarris, Village Voice Film Critic, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Sarris’s courtly and acerbic movie reviews appeared in The Village Voice and The New York Observer, and he became known for his intellectual duels with the critic Pauline Kael.

name: Frances W. Preston
headline: Frances W. Preston, Defender of Songwriters’ Copyright, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Preston, head of the BMI music licensing group for two decades, was described as the highest-ranking woman in the music industry when she retired.

name: LeRoy Neiman
profession: Artist of Bold Life and Bright Canvases
headline: LeRoy Neiman Dies at 91; Artist of Bold Life and Bright Canvases
abstract: Mr. Neiman, who painted racetrack scenes and Olympic contests, depicted public life in gaudy colors.

name: Judith S. Wallerstein
headline: Judith S. Wallerstein, Psychologist Who Analyzed Divorce, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Wallerstein touched off a national debate about the consequences of divorce by reporting that it hurt children more than previously thought, with the pain continuing well into adulthood.

name: Susan Tyrrell
headline: Susan Tyrrell, Oscar Nominee, Dies at 67
abstract: Ms. Tyrrell specialized in playing odd and grotesque characters in films like “Cry-Baby” and “Big Top Pee-wee.”

name: Anna Schwartz
headline: Anna Schwartz, Economist Who Collaborated With Friedman, Dies at 96
abstract: Mrs. Schwartz wrote, with Milton Friedman, “A Monetary History of the United States, 1867-1960” and “Monetary Statistics of the United States: Estimates, Sources, Methods.”

name: Jack Caulfield
headline: Jack Caulfield, Bearer of a Watergate Message, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Caulfield was once a master of dirty tricks for the Nixon White House who had his biggest brush with history in the role of a messenger.

name: Ralph Wenzel
headline: Ralph Wenzel, Whose Dementia Helped Start a Debate, Dies at 69
abstract: The condition of Mr. Wenzel, a former N.F.L. lineman, has been discussed in the debate about the safety of football, which has resulted in policy and rule changes.

name: Kevin Tucker
headline: Kevin Tucker Is Dead at 71; Led Philadelphia Police
abstract: Mr. Tucker was credited with turning around the troubled Philadelphia Police Department in the 1980s.

name: Robert J. Kelleher
headline: Robert J. Kelleher, Judge and Tennis Official, Dies at 99
abstract: Judge Kelleher helped change tennis by leading efforts to admit professionals into major tournaments.

name: Richard Adler
headline: Richard Adler, ‘Pajama Game’ Collaborator, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Adler co-wrote the music and lyrics for the Broadway hits “The Pajama Game” and “Damn Yankees.”

name: Edward N. Costikyan
headline: Edward N. Costikyan, Adviser to New York Politicians, Is Dead at 87
abstract: An adviser to New York mayors and governors, Mr. Costikyan was a Democratic insurgent who took over leadership of Tammany Hall in the 1960s.

name: Lesley Brown
profession: Mother of Worlds First Test-Tube Baby
headline: Lesley Brown, Mother of World’s First ‘Test-Tube Baby,’ Dies at 64
abstract: The birth of Mrs. Brown’s daughter using the in vitro fertilization technique was an instant global sensation and a turning point in the treatment of infertility.

name: Gitta Sereny
headline: Gitta Sereny, Author Who Focused on Evildoers, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Sereny’s books, which included portraits of Nazi concentration camp commanders and young murderers, concentrated on psychology as much as chronology.

name: Gerhard Kallmann
headline: Gerhard Kallmann, Architect, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Mr. Kallmann designed stately buildings like Boston City Hall and was a co-founder of the firm Kallmann, McKinnell & Knowles.

name: Anthony Schulte
headline: Anthony Schulte, Publisher and Early Audiobook Proponent, Dies at 82
abstract: The Random House audiobooks division, which began at Mr. Schulte’s suggestion in 1985, is now the largest in the market.

name: Paula Hays Harper
headline: Paula Hays Harper, Art Historian, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Dr. Harper provided the creative spark for “Womanhouse,” a celebrated exhibition of art by and about women that became a milestone in feminist art.

name: Nora Ephron
profession: Writer and Filmmaker With a Genius for Humor
headline: Nora Ephron Dies at 71; Writer and Filmmaker With a Genius for Humor
abstract: Among Ms. Ephron’s best-known films were “When Harry Met Sally...,” “Sleepless in Seattle” and “Julie & Julia.”

name: George R. Hearst Jr.
headline: George R. Hearst Jr., Leader of Publishing Giant, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Hearst was the force behind the expansion of Hearst in newspapers, magazines, television stations, cable television, real estate and other enterprises.

name: Michael J. Dontzin
profession: Counsel to New York Mayor in 70s
headline: Michael J. Dontzin, Counsel to New York Mayor in ’70s, Dies at 89
abstract: On behalf of Mayor John V. Lindsay, Mr. Dontzin negotiated the release of guards held hostage during a jail riot in 1970; he later became a State Supreme Court judge.

name: Anthony J. Wiener
headline: Anthony J. Wiener, Forecaster of the Future, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Wiener was a self-described futurist who used advance techniques to predict the year 2000 from the 1960s.

name: Harry Levinson
headline: Harry Levinson, Psychologist for the Workplace, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Levinson linked job conditions and satisfaction with an employee’s emotional health and changed the way companies dealt with workers.

name: Judy Agnew
headline: Judy Agnew, Wife of Vice President, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Agnew stood by her husband, Spiro T. Agnew, when he resigned in 1973 because of criminal charges.

name: Don Grady
headline: Don Grady, Robbie on ‘My Three Sons,’ Is Dead at 68
abstract: Mr. Grady played one of the Douglas sons for the life of the television series, then pursued a career in music.

name: Pat Cummings
headline: Pat Cummings, Rugged N.B.A. Forward, Dies at 55
abstract: Cummings, a 12-season N.B.A. veteran, spent four seasons with the Knicks, averaging double-digit scoring in two of them.

name: Ivan Karp
headline: Ivan Karp, Pop Art Dealer, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Karp was one of the first gallery owners to follow artists to SoHo, helping find, popularize and market artists like Andy Warhol, Roy Lichtenstein and Robert Rauschenberg.

name: Richard Isay
headline: Dr. Richard Isay, Who Fought Illness Tag for Gays, Dies at 77
abstract: Dr. Isay, a psychiatrist, won a pitched battle to persuade his own profession to stop treating homosexuality as a disease.

name: Brigitte Engerer
headline: Brigitte Engerer, Pianist With Singular Style, Dies at 59
abstract: Ms. Engerer, ranked among the world’s foremost pianists, played with both fiery Russian emotionalism and cool French rationalism.

name: Horacio Coppola
headline: Horacio Coppola, Evocative Argentine Photographer, Dies at 105
abstract: Mr. Coppola’s black-and-white works offered views of Buenos Aires, as well as perspectives on ordinary objects.

name: Barry Becher
headline: Barry Becher, a Creator of Ginsu Knife Commercials, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Becher, with Ed Valenti and Arthur Schiff, produced television spots that became kitsch classics and made their company millions in sales.

name: Yitzhak Shamir
headline: Yitzhak Shamir, Former Israeli Prime Minister, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Shamir was part of a group of right-wing politicians who rose to power in the 1970s and who adopted an unyielding opposition to territorial concessions for Palestinians.

name: Joan Dunlop
headline: Joan Dunlop, Advocate for Women’s Health Rights, Dies at 78
abstract: She devoted herself to expanding women’s rights to control their own bodies.

name: Abram Wilson
headline: Abram Wilson, Jazz Trumpeter, Dies at 38
abstract: Mr. Wilson helped lead a new generation of jazz artists in Britain, performing as a kind of cultural attaché from New Orleans.

name: Doris Sams
headline: Doris Sams, Pro Baseball Star, Dies at 85
abstract: Part of the women’s professional baseball world of the 1940s and 50s that inspired the movie “A League of Their Own,” Ms. Sams held a home run record and pitched a perfect game.

name: Yomo Toro
headline: Yomo Toro, Virtuoso of Latin Music, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Toro, a force in New York’s Latin music scene since the 1950s, was a master of the cuatro, a mandolinlike Puerto Rican instrument.

name: Julian Goodman
headline: Julian Goodman Dies at 90; Led NBC
abstract: Mr. Goodman produced the second Kennedy-Nixon debate and defended his network when it was pressured by the Nixon White House.

name: Andy Griffith
headline: Andy Griffith, TV’s Lawman and Moral Compass, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Griffith was a veteran of stage and screen when “The Andy Griffith Show” made its debut in 1960. He went on to delight a later generation as the lawyer on “Matlock.”

name: Sergio Pininfarina
headline: Sergio Pininfarina, Designer of Sports Cars, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Pininfarina’s design firm created the rakish and elegant auto bodies of some of the most popular, and fastest, cars ever made by Ferrari, Alfa Romeo, Maserati and Fiat.

name: Evelyn Lear
headline: Evelyn Lear, Versatile Soprano, Dies at 86
abstract: Miss Lear became a star in Europe and won acclaim in the United States for singing some of the most difficult roles in contemporary opera.

name: John E. Brooks
headline: The Rev. John E. Brooks Dies at 88; Widened Paths to Holy Cross
abstract: As a professor at the College of the Holy Cross in Worcester, Mass., Father Brooks set out on a mission that led to the integration of what had been an all-male and virtually all-white institution.

name: Jack Richardson
headline: Jack Richardson, New York Playwright, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Richardson won Obie and Drama Desk awards for his first play produced off Broadway in 1960. He turned to writing magazine articles and books after two of his plays failed on Broadway.

name: Jimmy Bivins
headline: Jimmy Bivins, Top Boxing Contender, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Bivins was a heavyweight boxer who in the 1940s and ’50s beat eight future world champions but, to his lasting regret, never got a shot at the title himself.

name: Michael J. Ybarra
headline: Michael J. Ybarra, Extreme-Sports Reporter, Dies at 45
abstract: Mr. Ybarra was an author and reporter who had been covering extreme sports like rock climbing and kayaking for The Wall Street Journal since 2007.

name: Martin L. Swig
headline: Martin L. Swig Dies at 78; Started Vintage Car Rally
abstract: Mr. Swig founded the California Mille, an internationally known rally that runs vintage sports cars over 1,000 miles of hilly Northern California roads.

name: Joyce D. Miller
headline: Joyce D. Miller, Breaker of Glass Ceilings, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Miller used labor unions to press for equal rights for women in the workplace and broke into the male-dominated leadership of the A.F.L.-C.I.O.

name: Gabriel G. Nahas
headline: Dr. Gabriel G. Nahas, Marijuana Opponent, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Nahas became a prominent crusader against marijuana after being shocked to hear, at a PTA meeting in 1969, about the drug’s widespread use.

name: Daphne Zepos
headline: Daphne Zepos, Champion of Fine Cheese, Dies at 52
