abstract: Ms. Zepos was an international authority on the buying, selling, making and above all the almost transcendental experience of eating cheese.

name: Ernest Borgnine
headline: Ernest Borgnine, Oscar-Winning Actor, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Borgnine, a rough-hewn actor who seemed destined for tough-guy characters, won an Oscar for embodying the gentlest of souls, a lonely Bronx butcher, in “Marty.”

name: Frances Alenikoff
headline: Frances Alenikoff, Dancer and Visual Artist, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Alenikoff, a dancer who was doing multimedia performances before the term was coined, used slides and chanting in her work.

name: Sunil Janah
headline: Sunil Janah, Who Chronicled India in Photographs, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Janah documented India’s ethnic and religious diversity, as well as important events in its modern history.

name: Martin Pakledinaz
headline: Martin Pakledinaz, Costume Designer, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Pakledinaz was nominated 10 times for Tony Awards and won twice, for “Kiss Me, Kate” and “Thoroughly Modern Millie.” He also worked in opera, dance and regional theater.

name: Robert de La Rochefoucauld
headline: Robert de La Rochefoucauld, Wartime Hero and Spy, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. de La Rochefoucauld is best remembered as a celebrated saboteur who fought for the honor of France in World War II as a secret agent with the British.

name: Donald D. Kummerfeld
headline: Donald D. Kummerfeld, Crisis Budgeter, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Kummerfeld was a budget director and first deputy mayor whose financial acumen and deft political touch helped steer New York City away from the brink of bankruptcy in the 1970s.

name: Calvin Marsh
headline: Calvin Marsh, Baritone and Met Stalwart, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Marsh sang more than 900 performances with the Metropolitan Opera before forsaking the stage for a life in religious music.

name: Marion Cunningham
headline: Marion Cunningham, Home Cooking Advocate, Dies at 90
abstract: Mrs. Cunningham, a mentor to many top chefs and foodies, rewrote “The Fannie Farmer Cookbook,” a project that spawned more of her books, a TV show and a newspaper column.

name: Marvin S. Traub
headline: Marvin S. Traub, Impresario of Bloomingdale’s, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Traub turned retailing on its ear by making Bloomingdale’s a trendsetting international showcase that drew movie stars and royalty.

name: Colin Marshall
headline: Colin Marshall Dies at 78; Helped Turn Around British Airways
abstract: Mr. Marshall played a central role in making the airline one of the world’s most profitable in the 1980s.

name: Norman Sas
headline: Norman Sas, Inventor of Electric Football, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Sas’s tabletop game, which still exists, thrived until hand-held and video competitors arrived in the 1980s.

name: Richard Zanuck
headline: Richard Zanuck, Producer of Blockbusters, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Zanuck produced films including “Driving Miss Daisy” and “Jaws.”

name: Else Holmelund Minarik
headline: Else Holmelund Minarik, Author of Little Bear Books, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Minarik began working on her series of Little Bear books after teaching grade school.

name: Maria Cole
profession: Singer and Wife of Nat King Cole
headline: Maria Cole, Singer and Wife of Nat King Cole, Dies at 89
abstract: Mrs. Cole, a jazz singer, was performing in Harlem when she met her husband.

name: Estelle Ellis Rubinstein
headline: Estelle Ellis Rubinstein, a Pioneer at Seventeen, Dies at 92
abstract: To promote Seventeen to advertisers, Ms. Rubinstein dreamed up “Teena,” a girl who embodied the demographics and concerns of the magazine’s readers.

name: Philip Fradkin
headline: Philip Fradkin, Writer Who Explored Themes of the West, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Fradkin often focused on the legacy of environmental destruction in the West.

name: George C. Stoney
headline: George C. Stoney, Documentary Filmmaker, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Stoney, acclaimed for his roles as a filmmaker, teacher and prophet of social change, lobbied for cable systems to be required to provide public access channels for members of the public.

name: Dara Singh
headline: Dara Singh, Wrestler and Bollywood Action Hero, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Singh’s fame in the ring won him movie roles that made him India’s first action hero and, later, a member of Parliament.

name: Isuzu Yamada
headline: Isuzu Yamada, Actress Who Worked With Kurosawa, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Yamada was a versatile, classically trained actress who brought a poise and toughness to varied roles as a victim, a villain, a rebellious girl or a “fallen woman.”

name: Celeste Holm
headline: Celeste Holm, Witty Character Actress, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Ms. Holm was 25 in 1943 when she was cast as Ado Annie in “Oklahoma!,” and in 1947 her performance in “Gentleman’s Agreement” garnered her the Oscar for best supporting actress.

name: Richard B. Scudder
headline: Richard B. Scudder, Co-Founder of MediaNews Group, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Scudder led one of the nation’s largest newspaper chains, and was an innovator in recycling newsprint.

name: L. Scott Bailey
headline: L. Scott Bailey, Founder of Automobile Quarterly, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Bailey’s magazine became known as the gold standard of “automotive literature,” in his phrase — a cross between The New Yorker and the Encyclopaedia Britannica.

name: Kitty Wells
headline: Kitty Wells, Trailblazing Country Singer, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Wells, perhaps best known for her 1952 hit “It Wasn’t God Who Made Honky Tonk Angels,” became a prototype for generations of female country music stars.

name: Stephen R. Covey
headline: Stephen R. Covey, Herald of Good Habits, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Covey had an enduring best seller in “The Seven Habits of Highly Effective People,” a synthesis of self-help and business literature.

name: Donald J. Sobol
headline: Donald J. Sobol, Creator of Encyclopedia Brown, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Sobol’s books about a clever boy detective made bookworms of many a reluctant reader.

name: Jon Lord
headline: Jon Lord, Keyboardist With Deep Purple, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Lord’s Hammond B-3 organ — with its signal routed through a Marshall amplifier to give it a distorted tang — was key to Deep Purple’s style.

name: William Raspberry
headline: William Raspberry, Prizewinning Columnist, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Raspberry’s columns, known for a moderate outlook on social issues, including race relations, appeared in The Washington Post from 1966 to 2005.

name: William Asher
headline: William Asher, Director of Classic TV Comedies, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Asher’s hits included “I Love Lucy” and “Bewitched” and popular 1960s beach-blanket movies.

name: Gustin Reichbach
headline: Gustin Reichbach, Judge With a Radical History, Dies at 65
abstract: A leader of student protests at Columbia University in 1968, Justice Reichbach went on to be a well respected, if sometimes controversial, judge of the New York State Supreme Court.

name: Ilhan Mimaroglu
headline: Ilhan Mimaroglu, Composer and Producer, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Mimaroglu wrote electronic music, worked with Charles Mingus on some of Mingus’s last albums and was the president of his own record label, Finnadar.

name: Y. S. Elyashiv
headline: Rabbi Y. S. Elyashiv, Master of Talmudic Law, Dies at 102
abstract: Rabbi Elyashiv’s influential decisions applying the Torah and Talmudic law to modern times sometimes roiled Israeli politics.

name: Rajesh Khanna
headline: Rajesh Khanna, a Star of ’60s and ’70s Bollywood, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Khanna was a romantic leading man and superstar in Indian cinema in the period preceding the rise of the action hero in the 1970s.

name: Omar Suleiman
headline: Omar Suleiman, Powerful Egypt Spy Chief, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Suleiman, who once led the Egyptian intelligence service, was apparently in the United States for medical treatment.

name: Tom Davis
headline: Tom Davis, Comedian and ‘SNL’ Sketch Writer, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Davis and his Minnesota high school friend Al Franken were among the first writers hired in 1975 to help shape the fresh take that a new show, live from New York, would bring to topical humor.

name: Sylvia Woods
headline: Sylvia Woods, Soul-Food Restaurateur, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Ms. Woods’s namesake Harlem soul-food restaurant was frequented by local and national politicians, international celebrities, tourists, epicures and ordinary neighborhood residents.

name: Robert W. Creamer
headline: Robert W. Creamer, Biographer of Babe Ruth, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Creamer was one of the first writers to go to work for Sports Illustrated, where he became a senior editor.

name: Vincent R. Mancusi
headline: Vincent R. Mancusi, Warden at Attica During Riot, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Mancusi was warden when inmates rebelled in 1971, sparking a riot that left scores of guards and prisoners dead or injured.

name: Stuart R. Schram
headline: Stuart R. Schram, Nuclear Physicist and Mao Scholar, Dies at 88
abstract: After working on the Manhattan Project, Mr. Schram published works in French and German and taught himself Russian and Japanese before turning to the study of Mao Zedong.

name: Stephen Dwoskin
profession: Maker of Films Focused on the Body
headline: Stephen Dwoskin, Maker of Films Focused on the Body, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Dwoskin made dozens of movies that often blurred the boundaries among fiction, documentary and autobiography.

name: Alexander Cockburn
headline: Alexander Cockburn, Acerbic Writer and Critic, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Cockburn took pleasure in condemning what he saw as the outrages of the right and what he often considered the tepidness and timidity of the American liberal establishment.

name: Forrest S. McCartney
headline: Forrest S. McCartney, a Top NASA Official, Dies at 81
abstract: General McCartney played a central role in developing military spy satellites and the MX intercontinental missile system before being appointed head of the Kennedy Space Center.

name: Nelson Lyon
profession: TV Writer Steeped in the Counterculture
headline: Nelson Lyon, TV Writer Steeped in the Counterculture, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Lyon, a screenwriter and photographer, was a participant in the drug binge that killed the actor and comedian John Belushi in 1982.

name: Oswaldo Payá
profession: Cuban Leader of Petition Drive for Human Rights
headline: Oswaldo Payá, Cuban Leader of Petition Drive for Human Rights, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Payá, an engineer deeply inspired by his strong Roman Catholic faith, spent decades trying to build a domestic rights movement in Cuba.

name: Sally Ride
headline: American Woman Who Shattered Space Ceiling
abstract: Dr. Ride was the first American woman in space, flying on two missions on the shuttle Challenger.

name: Simon Ward
headline: Simon Ward, Star of ‘Young Winston,’ Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Ward’s piercing good looks and archetypical Englishness made him Hollywood’s go-to British actor for a time, the Hugh Grant of the early ’70s.

name: Herbert Vogel
headline: Herbert Vogel, Fabled Art Collector, Dies at 89
abstract: In 1992, when Mr. Vogel and his wife, Dorothy, gave thousands of artworks to the National Gallery of Art, the director J. Carter Brown called their collection “a work of art in itself.”

name: Ginny Tyler
headline: Ginny Tyler, Mouseketeer, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Tyler started her career as Mother Goose on children’s television and moved on to become a Disneyland Storyteller and Mouseketeer.

name: John Atta Mills
headline: John Atta Mills, President of Ghana, Dies at 68
abstract: A respected if uncharismatic former law professor, Mr. Atta Mills presided over Ghana’s continuing experiment in stable democracy.

name: Sherman Hemsley
headline: Sherman Hemsley, ‘Jeffersons’ Star, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Mr. Hemsley was most famous for his role as the scrappy, nouveau riche George Jefferson on the hit 1970s sitcom.

name: Frank Pierson
headline: Frank Pierson, Oscar-Winning Writer, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Pierson’s richly textured work included the scripts for “Cool Hand Luke” and “Dog Day Afternoon.”

name: Ann Curtis
headline: Ann Curtis, Barrier-Breaking Star Swimmer, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Curtis was widely regarded as one of the greatest female swimmers, winning two Olympic gold medals in 1948 and 34 United States championships.

name: Chad Everett
profession: Dashing Dr. Gannon of Medical Center
headline: Chad Everett, Dashing Dr. Gannon of ‘Medical Center’, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Everett played dozens of roles after he was Dr. Joe Gannon, but the impression he left as the leading man of “Medical Center” was a lasting one.

name: Robert S. Ledley
headline: Robert S. Ledley, Who Revolutionized Radiology, Is Dead at 86
abstract: A dentist turned biomedical researcher, Dr. Ledley invented the first CT scanner capable of producing cross-sectional images of any part of the human body.

name: Mike Lynn
headline: Mike Lynn, Vikings’ General Manager, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Lynn helped Minnesota reach the Super Bowl but also engineered what proved to be one of the worst trades in N.F.L. history, a deal to land Herschel Walker.

name: Margaret Mahy
headline: Margaret Mahy, Children’s Author, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Mahy was an award-winning author who was known for her humorous, often fantastical stories for children and young adults.

name: Franz West
headline: Franz West Is Dead at 65; Creator of an Art Universe
abstract: Mr. West’s work ranged from collages to furniture to large, colorful public sculptures.

name: Ed Stevens
headline: Ed Stevens, a Dodger Replaced by Jackie Robinson, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Stevens was one of two first basemen Jackie Robinson replaced when he broke the major league color barrier with the Dodgers in April 1947.

name: Miriam Ben-Porat
headline: Miriam Ben-Porat, Israeli Judge and Civic Watchdog, Dies at 94
abstract: Mrs. Ben-Porat was the first woman to serve as a justice on Israel’s Supreme Court and to hold the post of state comptroller.

name: Fioravante G. Perrotta
profession: Influential Aide to Governor Rockefeller and Others
headline: Fioravante G. Perrotta, Influential Aide to Governor Rockefeller and Others, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Perrotta moved seamlessly between influential jobs with Gov. Nelson A. Rockefeller and Mayor John V. Lindsay as a young lawyer in New York in the 1960s.

name: Thelma Glass
headline: Thelma Glass, Who Helped Organize Alabama Bus Boycott, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Glass, a professor of geography at Alabama State University, is the last surviving member of the Women’s Political Council, which demonstrated against the arrest of Rosa Parks in 1955.

name: Lupe Ontiveros
headline: Lupe Ontiveros, Who Portrayed Maids and Moms, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Ontiveros, who played a suspicious mother-in-law on “Desperate Housewives,” estimated that she had been cast as a Hispanic maid more than 150 times on TV and in movies.

name: William Staub
headline: William Staub, Engineer Who Built an Affordable Treadmill, Dies at 96
abstract: A book that said being able to run an eight-minute mile was a sign of top-tier physical fitness inspired Mr. Staub to build the machine for home use.

name: Walter Pichler
headline: Walter Pichler, an Artist Who Bucked the Status Quo, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Pichler was an Austrian architect who, after a flurry of shows that won him international acclaim, moved away from the world of galleries, exhibitions and collectors.

name: Marc deCoster
profession: Hairdresser to Members of High Society
headline: Marc deCoster, Hairdresser to Members of High Society, Dies at 81
abstract: Known as Monsieur Marc, he styled the hair of clients like Nancy Reagan.

name: Suzy Gershman
profession: Author of Born to Shop Guides
headline: Suzy Gershman, Author of ‘Born to Shop’ Guides, Dies at 64
abstract: Ms. Gershman wrote 16 “Born to Shop” guides to various cities, compiled during hundreds of thousands of miles of worldwide travel.

name: Irvin Faust
headline: Irvin Faust, Author and Guidance Counselor, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Faust, best known for “The Steagle,” a novel, and his short-story collection “Roar Lion Roar,” was also a high school guidance counselor.

name: Tony Martin
headline: Tony Martin, Debonair Pop Troubadour, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Martin represented the fantasy of the impossibly elegant troubadour warbling to equally elegant (and mythical) audiences at nightclubs and balls.

name: Chris Marker
headline: Chris Marker, Pioneer of the Essay Film, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Marker, who pioneered the flexible hybrid form known as the essay film, resisted categorization throughout his career.

name: R. G. Armstrong
headline: R. G. Armstrong, Character Actor in Westerns, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Armstrong’s five-decade career took off with guest spots on the popular Western television shows of the 1950s and ’60s, including “Have Gun — Will Travel” and “Gunsmoke.”

name: James D. Watkins
profession: Led Energy Dept. and AIDS Panel
headline: Adm. James D. Watkins, Who Led Energy Dept. and AIDS Panel, Dies at 85
abstract: After serving in the Navy’s top ranks during the cold war, Admiral Watkins was involved in battles of a different kind, opposing AIDS discrimination and seeking greater domestic oil production.

name: Maeve Binchy
headline: Maeve Binchy, Writer Who Evoked Ireland, Dies at 72
abstract: Ms. Binchy’s sprawling novels of Ireland portrayed women confronting all manner of adversity.

name: Judith Martin
headline: Judith Martin, Force in Children’s Theater, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Martin was a founder and artistic director of the Paper Bag Players, which has been entertaining children since 1958.

name: Rita Miljo
headline: Rita Miljo, ‘the Mother Teresa of Baboons,’ Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Miljo was killed in a fire at the sanctuary she established for orphaned and injured baboons in South Africa, a nation where they are mostly reviled.

name: Gore Vidal
headline: Gore Vidal Dies at 86; Prolific, Elegant, Acerbic Writer
abstract: Mr. Vidal was an elegant, acerbic all-around man of letters who presided with a certain relish over what he declared to be the end of American civilization.

name: George A. Miller
headline: George A. Miller, a Pioneer in Cognitive Psychology, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Dr. Miller was a psychologist and professor who helped create the cognitive psychology movement.

name: Norman Alden
headline: Norman Alden, a Character Actor for 50 Years, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Alden was an actor for 50 years, on TV shows like “The Legend of Wyatt Earp,” “The Untouchables” and “My Three Sons,” and in movies like “Back to the Future” and “Ed Wood.”

name: John Keegan
headline: John Keegan, Historian Who Put a Face on War, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Keegan was an Englishman widely considered to be the pre-eminent military historian of his era and the author of more than 20 books, including the masterwork “The Face of Battle.”

name: Gerald Gold
headline: Gerald Gold, Editor on the Pentagon Papers, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Gold helped supervise the herculean task of combing through a secret 2.5 million-word Defense Department history of the Vietnam War.

name: Karl Benjamin
headline: Karl Benjamin, Rebel of Midcentury Art Scene, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Benjamin was a painter who came to art almost by accident and then rose to prominence in the 1950s as part of a West Coast artists’ rebellion against the reign of Abstract Expressionism.

name: Paul W. McCracken
headline: Paul W. McCracken, Adviser to Presidents, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. McCracken was a moderate Republican who led President Richard M. Nixon’s largely unsuccessful effort to tame the rising inflation of the late 1960s and early 1970s.

name: Mihaela Ursuleasa
headline: Mihaela Ursuleasa, Classical Pianist, Dies at 33
abstract: Ms. Ursuleasa, a Romanian-born pianist renowned for her prodigious technique and often idiosyncratic interpretations, was performing internationally by the time she was a teenager.

name: Florence Waren
headline: Florence Waren, Jewish Dancer Who Resisted Nazis, Dies at 95
abstract: In occupied France, Ms. Waren, who danced as Nazis sat in her audience, hid her identity and helped to hide other Jews and to smuggle weapons to the resistance.

name: Mary Louise Rasmuson
headline: Mary Louise Rasmuson, Who Led Women’s Army Corps, Dies at 101
abstract: Mrs. Rasmuson, one of the original officers of the corps, went on to serve as its director, before moving to Alaska and beginning a new life as a philanthropist.

name: Esther Kartiganer
headline: Esther Kartiganer, a Force as a ‘60 Minutes’ Producer, Dies at 74
abstract: Her 40-year career at CBS was overshadowed at the end by her role in a controversial “60 Minutes II” segment questioning President George W. Bush’s Texas Air National Guard service.

name: Martin E. Segal
profession: Titan of the Arts in New York City
headline: Martin E. Segal, Titan of the Arts in New York City, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Segal, who made his fortune with the Segal Company, an international consulting business, remained a larger-than-life presence on New York’s cultural scene well into his 90s.

name: Warren Winkelstein Jr.
headline: Warren Winkelstein Jr., Medical Sleuth, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Winkelstein’s studies connected unprotected sex between men to AIDS, smoking to cervical cancer, and air pollution to chronic lung disease.

name: Marguerite Piazza
headline: Marguerite Piazza, Popular Singer of Opera, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Piazza sang with the Metropolitan Opera, appeared on TV and performed on the supper-club circuit in the United States and Cuba.

name: Chavela Vargas
headline: Chavela Vargas, Mexican Ranchera Singer, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Vargas’s collaboration with Mexico’s great ranchera composers, particularly José Alfredo Jiménez, gave rise to definitive recordings of some of Mexico’s best-known songs.

name: Robert Hughes
headline: Robert Hughes, Art Critic Whose Writing Was Elegant and Contentious, Dies at 74
abstract: With a Hemingwayesque build and the distinctively rounded vowels of his native Australia, Mr. Hughes became as familiar a presence on television as he was in print.

name: Judith Crist
headline: Judith Crist, a Blunt and Influential Film Critic, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Crist, whose enthusiastic and often acerbic reviews were seen in newspapers and magazines and on television, was cited as moviegoers’ favorite critic in a 1960s poll.

name: Marvin Hamlisch
headline: Marvin Hamlisch, Whose Notes Struck Gold, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Hamlisch, the singularly productive composer of musicals like “A Chorus Line” and songs like “The Way We Were,” won Oscars, Grammys, Emmys, a Tony and a Pulitzer Prize.

name: Anna Piaggi
profession: Fashion Editor With a Keen Eye for Trends
headline: Anna Piaggi, Fashion Editor With a Keen Eye for Trends, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Piaggi was known for her wildly colorful style of dress and a collection of clothes spanning more than 200 years.

name: Mark O’Donnell
headline: Mark O’Donnell, ‘Hairspray’ Writer, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. O’Donnell was a co-author of the book for the Broadway musical “Hairspray,” which became a phenomenal success, winning eight Tonys, including best book of a musical.

name: Bernard Lovell
headline: Sir Bernard Lovell Dies at 98; a Radio Telescope Bears His Name
abstract: A pioneer in radar and radio telescopes, Mr. Lovell was especially renowned for creating the Jodrell Bank radio telescope, near Manchester, England.

name: R. Peter Straus
headline: R. Peter Straus, Radio Pioneer, Dies at 89
abstract: Under Mr. Straus’s leadership, WMCA in New York broadcast what were regarded as the first radio editorials and political endorsements.

name: Roy S. Bryce-Laporte
headline: Roy S. Bryce-Laporte, Who Led Black Studies at Yale, Dies at 78
abstract: Professor Bryce-Laporte headed one of the nation’s first African-American studies departments, emphasizing that black studies must address hot-button topics like racial stereotyping while retaining academic rigor.

name: William C. Reeves
headline: Dr. William C. Reeves, Who Sought Cause of Fatigue Syndrome, Dies at 69
abstract: When Dr. Reeves took charge of research on the syndrome, patients and advocacy groups had been complaining that the government was not taking it seriously.

name: Raymond Harding
headline: Raymond Harding, 77, Dies; Liberal Party Power Broker
abstract: Mr. Harding, whose political influence was felt for decades from New York City to Albany as the state’s Liberal Party leader, fell from grace in 2009 after a corruption investigation.

name: DeAndre McCullough
headline: DeAndre McCullough, Drug Dealer Who Inspired ‘The Corner,’ Dies at 35
abstract: As a 15-year-old street seller of drugs in Baltimore, Mr. McCullough became a focus of David Simon’s book and TV mini-series “The Corner.”

name: Ruggiero Ricci
headline: Ruggiero Ricci Dies at 94; Prodigy Whose Violin Mastery Grew
abstract: Mr. Ricci, a prodigy who first performed at age 10, went on to master Paganini’s Caprices as well as extend his range to contemporary works.

name: Ben Heineman
headline: Ben Heineman, Multifaceted Businessman, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Heineman held various government jobs in Illinois serving Gov. Adlai E. Stevenson and Mayor Richard J. Daley of Chicago.

name: David Rakoff
headline: David Rakoff, 47, Comic Essayist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Rakoff, a humorist and essayist, was known for his incisive wit and keen eye for the preposterous.

name: Richard Cragun
headline: Richard Cragun, Stuttgart Ballet Dancer, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Cragun was the partner of Marcia Haydée, the prima ballerina, in an acclaimed series of classical dance dramas in the 1960s and 1970s.

name: Carlo Rambaldi
profession: Maestro of Special Effects in Movies
headline: Carlo Rambaldi Dies at 86; Maestro of Special Effects in Movies
abstract: Mr. Rambaldi was a special-effects virtuoso who won two Academy Awards for his work on Steven Spielberg’s “E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial” and Ridley Scott’s “Alien.”

name: Sami Rohr
profession: Jewish Philanthropist Remembered by a Writing Prize
headline: Sami Rohr, Jewish Philanthropist Remembered by a Writing Prize, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Rohr, who made a fortune in real estate after fleeing the Nazis, was honored by his children in 2006 with the creation of the Sami Rohr Prize for Jewish Literature.

name: Mel Stuart
headline: Mel Stuart, Documentarian and ‘Willy Wonka’ Director, Dies at 83
abstract: In addition to directing “Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory,” Mr. Stuart won three Emmy Awards as a producer or director of documentaries.

name: Martin Fleischmann
headline: Martin Fleischmann, Seeker of Cold Fusion, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Fleischmann believed he had achieved cold fusion in a lab, but his announcement proved premature and he was discredited.

name: Jean Merrill
headline: Jean Merrill, a Writer of Children’s Underdog Tales, Dies at 89
abstract: In “The Pushcart War,” “The Toothpaste Millionaire” and many other books, Ms. Merrill’s characters overcome the odds.

name: James Naughton
headline: James Naughton, Newsman and Puckish Inspiration, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Naughton was a writer, mentor and irrepressible prankster whose career took him to The New York Times, The Philadelphia Inquirer and a leading journalism institute.

name: Dale Olson
headline: Dale Olson, Top Hollywood Publicist, Dies at 78
abstract: Among the biggest stories handled by Mr. Olson in his career, perhaps his most important was persuading Rock Hudson to announce that he had AIDS.

name: Helen Gurley Brown
profession: Gave Single Girl a Life in Full
headline: Helen Gurley Brown, Who Gave ‘Single Girl’ a Life in Full, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Brown, who wrote the best-selling book “Sex and the Single Girl” and was the longtime editor of Cosmopolitan, was widely credited with being the first to introduce frank discussions of sex into magazines for women.

name: Iver Peterson
headline: Iver Peterson, New York Times Reporter, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Peterson was one of a generation of young reporters who earned distinction as war correspondents in Vietnam.

name: Johnny Pesky
headline: Johnny Pesky, Red Sox Fixture, Dies at 92
abstract: Pesky was a star Red Sox shortstop of the 1940s and early ’50s who spent seven decades at Fenway Park as a player, manager, coach, broadcaster and instructor.

name: Joe Kubert
headline: Joe Kubert Dies at 85; Influential Comic-Book Artist
abstract: Mr. Kubert’s work, which included Sgt. Rock and Tor, stretched from the Golden Age of the superhero to the gritty realism of the graphic novel.

name: Michael Dokes
headline: Michael Dokes, Larger-Than-Life Heavyweight Boxer, Dies at 54
abstract: Dokes used his punishing fists to become the world heavyweight boxing champion in 1982 and, 15 years later, to beat his girlfriend so savagely that he was convicted of attempted murder.

name: Gregory Powell
headline: Gregory Powell, ‘The Onion Field’ Killer, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Powell was convicted of kidnapping and killing a Los Angeles police officer in 1963, a brutal crime that inspired the popular book and film “The Onion Field.”

name: Ron Palillo
headline: Ron Palillo Dies at 63; Played Horshack on TV
abstract: Mr. Palillo portrayed the goofy high school underachiever Arnold Horshack in the hit 1970s sitcom “Welcome Back, Kotter.”

name: William N. Wallace
headline: William N. Wallace, Former Times Reporter, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Wallace was one of the first reporters assigned to write about broader issues affecting both the National and American Football Leagues.

name: Al Freeman Jr.
profession: Actor Prominent in Civil Rights Era
headline: Al Freeman Jr., Actor Prominent in Civil Rights Era, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Freeman was a stage and screen actor who made his mark in both drama and race relations with roles like Malcolm X and Elijah Muhammad.

name: Nellie Gray
profession: Abortion Foe and Leader of Annual March
headline: Nellie Gray, Abortion Foe and Leader of Annual March, Dies at 88
abstract: For almost 40 years, Ms. Gray led a yearly anti-abortion protest with her battle cry of “No exception! No compromise!”

name: Joan Roberts
headline: Joan Roberts Dies at 95; Original ‘Oklahoma!’ Star
abstract: Ms. Roberts was one of the last living members of the cast of the original musical, which was Richard Rodgers and Oscar Hammerstein’s first collaboration.

name: Svetozar Gligoric
headline: Svetozar Gligoric, Who Pioneered Chess Moves, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Gligoric was considered one of the greatest players of the 20th century and pioneered several systems of moves, but he never won the chance to compete for the world championship.

name: Hugo Bedau
headline: Hugo Bedau, Philosopher Who Opposed Death Penalty, Dies at 85
abstract: Professor Bedau’s half-century career encompassed several cycles in the national debate over capital punishment, which he opposed as immoral, unjust and ineffective.

name: Michael Olexa
headline: Michael Olexa, Newlywed Truck Driver Who Had Cancer, Dies at 42
abstract: Mr. Olexa, a truck driver who was the subject of a Vows column in The New York Times, married Angela Sclafani on Aug. 2 and was taken to the hospital the next day.

name: Karl Fleming
headline: Karl Fleming, Reporter Who Covered Civil Rights Era, Dies at 84
abstract: As a Newsweek reporter, Mr. Fleming dodged bullets and choked on tear gas while covering some of the most momentous events of the civil rights era.

name: George F. Cahill Jr.
headline: George F. Cahill Jr., Diabetes Expert, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Cahill clarified insulin’s role in metabolism by studying research subjects on starvation diets. He also testified for the prosecution at the trials of Claus von Bülow on charges of trying to murder his wife with insulin.

name: Carl Davis
headline: Carl Davis, Chicago Music Impresario, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Davis was a record producer who helped shape the sound of Chicago soul on classics like “Duke of Earl” and “(Your Love Keeps Lifting Me) Higher and Higher.”

name: Harry Barnes Jr.
headline: Harry Barnes Jr., a Top U.S. Diplomat, Is Dead at 86
abstract: As ambassador to Chile in the 1980s, Mr. Barnes aggressively promoted democracy there and clashed frequently with the country’s dictatorial president, Gen. Augusto Pinochet.

name: Harry Harrison
profession: Prolific Writer of Satiric Science Fiction
headline: Harry Harrison, a Prolific Writer of Satiric Science Fiction, Dies at 87
abstract: Among Mr. Harrison’s books was “Make Room! Make Room!” which was made into the film “Soylent Green.”

name: Harry Harrison
headline: Harry Harrison, ‘Good Guy’ Radio D.J., Is Dead at 89
abstract: As the ‘Morning Mayor of New York’ from 1959 to 2003, he hosted shows on WMCA, WABC and WCBS-FM, a singular trifecta.

name: Remy Charlip
headline: Remy Charlip, Dancer and Children’s Author, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Charlip’s half-century of work cut across a wide spectrum of art forms and aesthetic registers, dazzling avant-garde audiences with dances and writing books like “Arm in Arm” and “Fortunately.”

name: Von Freeman
headline: Von Freeman, Fiery Tenor Saxophonist, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Freeman, who played jazz since he was a boy, was considered one of the finest tenor saxophonists in jazz but attained wide fame only late in life.

name: Phyllis Thaxter
headline: Phyllis Thaxter, Actress Who Played Superman’s Mother, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Thaxter, whose first film was “Thirty Seconds Over Tokyo” and last was “Superman,” enjoyed a lengthy acting career despite contracting polio.

name: Milton Bassin
headline: Milton Bassin Dies at 88; Expanded York College
abstract: As president of York College in Jamaica, Queens, Mr. Bassin oversaw the construction of a vast campus and fulfilled a mission to educate minority and low-income students.

name: William Windom
headline: William Windom, TV Everyman, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Windom won the Emmy for best actor in 1970 for the short-lived show “My World and Welcome to It,” but is better known to most viewers for his roles on “Murder, She Wrote” and “Star Trek.”

name: Victor Poor
headline: Victor Poor, Who Helped Create Early Intel Chips, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Poor, a computer engineer and amateur radio enthusiast, collaborated on development of microprocessors that propelled Intel to dominance in the computer chip industry.

name: Brent Grulke
profession: Builder of South by Southwest Fest
headline: Brent Grulke, a Builder of South by Southwest Fest, Dies at 51
abstract: Mr. Grulke, responsible for booking the music groups at the South by Southwest festival in Austin, Tex., helped to build it into an event of more than 2,000 acts.

name: Simon P. Gourdine
headline: Simon P. Gourdine, Pioneer in Sports Management, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Gourdine became the highest ranking black executive in professional sports in the 1970s when he was named the N.B.A.’s deputy commissioner.

name: Donal Henahan
headline: Donal Henahan, Thought-Provoking Music Critic, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Henahan, a Pulitzer Prize winner for distinguished criticism, wrote on a wide range of cultural subjects for The Times, retiring in 1991.

name: Phyllis Diller
headline: Phyllis Diller, Sassy Comedian, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Diller’s screeching, sassy, rapid-fire stand-up comedy helped open the door for funny women.

name: Scott McKenzie
headline: Scott McKenzie, Singer Known for ‘San Francisco,’ Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. McKenzie’s 1967 ballad “San Francisco (Be Sure to Wear Flowers in Your Hair)” became a defining hit for the counterculture generation.

name: Phil Moriarty
profession: Coach of Swimmers and Divers at Yale and Olympics
headline: Phil Moriarty, Coach of Swimmers and Divers at Yale and Olympics, Dies at 98
abstract: Moriarty succeeded a legend, Bob Kiphuth, at Yale and then built his own legend, training gold medal swimmers like Don Schollander and coaching the United States divers in the 1960 Olympics.

name: Dom Mintoff
headline: Dom Mintoff, Fiery Proponent of Maltese Independence, Dies at 96
abstract: Britain ruled the country since the 19th century, but Mr. Mintoff worked to get the English out and eventually got his way.

name: Meles Zenawi
headline: Meles Zenawi, Prime Minister of Ethiopia, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Meles oversaw substantial economic growth as prime minister and made Ethiopia a staunch American counterterrorism ally but drew criticism for harsh treatment of dissidents.

name: Samuel H. Lindenbaum
profession: Dean of New York Zoning Lawyers
headline: Samuel H. Lindenbaum, ‘Dean’ of New York Zoning Lawyers, Dies at 77
abstract: Armed with a scholar’s knowledge, Mr. Lindenbaum helped his clients bend the city’s zoning rules without breaking them.

name: Nina Bawden
headline: Nina Bawden, Author of ‘Carrie’s War,’ Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Bawden, the author of more than 40 books for children and adults, was best-known for a novel based on her World War II childhood, which was adapted twice for television.

name: Martine Franck
headline: Martine Franck, Documentary Photographer, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Franck, a photographer who rose to the highest echelons of her profession, fiercely protected the artistic legacy of her husband, Henri Cartier-Bresson.

name: Willa Ward
headline: Willa Ward, Gospel Singer, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Ward joined her mother and sister in making the Ward Singers possibly the most influential group of the golden era of gospel music.

name: Rosemary Rice
headline: Rosemary Rice, Oldest Daughter of TV’s ‘Mama,’ Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Rice, as Katrin, the perky oldest daughter, introduced the hit show “Mama” weekly on CBS from 1949 to 1957.

name: Matthew Ianniello
profession: Mafia Boss Known as Matty the Horse
headline: Matthew Ianniello, the Mafia Boss Known as ‘Matty the Horse,’ Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Ianniello was convicted of rigging construction bids, skimming union dues and wringing protection money from bar owners during a half-century career in crime.

name: William P. Thurston
headline: William P. Thurston, Theoretical Mathematician, Dies at 65
abstract: Dr. Thurston revolutionized understanding of the structure of three-dimensional spaces and won the Fields Medal, often described as the equivalent of the Nobel Prize

name: Robert Treboux
headline: Robert Treboux, Restaurateur, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Treboux, an unbending traditionalist at his East Side bistro, Le Veau d’Or, had a devoted clientele who wanted familiarity, not innovation.

name: Patrick Ricard
headline: Patrick Ricard, Who Expanded Spirits Company, Dies at 67
abstract: As head of the family business, Mr. Ricard acquired a number of wine and spirit labels and built a huge conglomerate.

name: Don Raleigh
headline: Don Raleigh, All-Star Center for Rangers, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Raleigh was the first N.H.L. player to score sudden-death overtime goals in two consecutive games of a Stanley Cup final series.

name: Steve Van Buren
headline: Steve Van Buren, 91, Dies; Hall of Fame Halfback
abstract: Nicknamed Wham Bam, Mr. Van Buren was ahead of his time in the 1940s, combining power and speed while leading the Philadelphia Eagles to two championships.

name: Jerry Grant
headline: Jerry Grant, Racecar Driver Who Broke Speed Barrier, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Grant was the first driver to go faster than 200 miles per hour in an Indy-style racecar but may be best remembered for his heartbreaking defeats.

name: Daryl Hine
headline: Daryl Hine, Poet, Editor and Translator, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Hine was an admired poet, a translator of classic works and, for several years, the editor of Poetry magazine.

name: Neil Armstrong
headline: Neil Armstrong, First Man on the Moon, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Armstrong became a global hero when, as a steely-nerved pilot, he made “one giant leap for mankind” with a small step on the moon.

name: R. Palmer Beasley
headline: R. Palmer Beasley, Expert on Hepatitis B, Dies at 76
abstract: Dr. Beasley discovered that the virus is easily transferred from mothers to infants during childbirth, and confirmed its role in causing liver cancer.

name: Terry Tracy
headline: Terry Tracy, Model for the Big Kahuna, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Tracy, who as an easygoing, fun-loving surfer, inspired the “Gidget” movies and helped make surfing an international sport.

name: Roger D. Fisher
headline: Roger D. Fisher, Expert at ‘Getting to Yes,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Fisher, a Harvard law professor who was a co-author of the 1981 best seller “Getting to Yes: Negotiating Agreement Without Giving In,” led a role in drafting the Camp David accords.

name: Jan Sawka
headline: Jan Sawka, Polish Artist, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Sawka’s body of work included paintings, sculptures, architectural installations, light shows and a movable 10-story stage set for the Grateful Dead’s 25th-anniversary concert tour.

name: Robert Kotlowitz
headline: Robert Kotlowitz, a Shaper of Channel 13, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Kotlowitz was a cultural force at the public TV station, responsible for bringing “The MacNeil/Lehrer Report,” “Brideshead Revisited,” music and ballet to the screen.

name: Malcolm W. Browne
headline: Malcolm W. Browne, Pulitzer-Prize Winning Reporter, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Browne, who took one of the most memorable photos of the Vietnam War, won a Pulitzer Prize in 1964 for his reporting.

name: David Lederman
headline: David Lederman, Pioneer of Artificial Heart, Dies at 68
abstract: Dr. Lederman helped develop the first fully implantable artificial heart, which prompted further advances in the treatment of late-stage heart disease.

name: George L. Gunther
headline: George L. Gunther, Connecticut Legislator, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Gunther spent 40 years in office as a state senator, making him the longest-serving member of the General Assembly in Hartford.

name: James Fogle
headline: James Fogle, Author of ‘Drugstore Cowboy,’ Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Fogle was imprisoned in Washington State in a life filled with true crimes, and used his experiences for fictional accounts in novels and an eventual movie.

name: Steve Franken
headline: Steve Franken, Actor in ‘Dobie Gillis,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Franken, a comedic character actor who appeared in films with Peter Sellers and others, was best known for playing Chatsworth Osborne Jr. on the sitcom “The Many Loves of Dobie Gillis.”

name: Reginald Bartholomew
headline: Reginald Bartholomew, Busy Diplomat, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Bartholomew, a senior American diplomat, negotiated for nuclear disarmament with the Soviet Union and survived a bomb attack while he was ambassador to Lebanon in 1984.

name: Chris Lighty
headline: Chris Lighty, Manager of Hip-Hop Stars, Dies at 44
abstract: Mr. Lighty, whose clients included 50 Cent, LL Cool J, Missy Elliott and Diddy, helped establish the genre as a major commercial force.

name: Lawrence Mead Jr.
headline: Lawrence Mead Jr., Aerospace Engineer, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Mead, an executive at Grumman, led the design team for the A-6 Intruder, which became the Navy’s primary attack bomber.

name: Art Heyman
headline: Art Heyman, Star at Duke, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Heyman led Duke to its first Final Four appearance and helped fuel the university’s rivalry with North Carolina.

name: Shulamith Firestone
headline: Shulamith Firestone, Feminist Writer, Dies at 67
abstract: At 25, Ms. Firestone wrote “The Dialectic of Sex,” a radical and arresting second-wave feminist book that remains widely taught in women’s-studies courses. She then retreated to a quiet life of painting and writing.

name: Carlo Martini
headline: Cardinal Carlo Martini, Papal Contender, Dies at 85
abstract: Cardinal Martini, one of the Roman Catholic Church’s most influential progressive thinkers, was considered a possible successor to Pope John Paul II.

name: Hal David
headline: Hal David, Songwriter, Is Dead at 91
abstract: The Oscar- and Grammy-winning lyricist was best known for the long strand of hits he and the composer Burt Bacharach wrote for Dionne Warwick.

name: Alexander Saxton
headline: Alexander Saxton, Historian and Novelist, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Saxton was a writer ostracized as a Communist, who went on to become a prominent cultural historian, transforming his life in his 40s.

name: Byard Lancaster
headline: Byard Lancaster, Jazz Alto Saxophonist, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Lancaster was an alto saxophonist who took part in the great wave of free jazz inspired by John Coltrane.

name: Peter Shelton
headline: Peter Shelton, Architect Who Made Luxury Minimal, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Shelton and his longtime design partner, Lee Mindel, were known for interior designs that blended clean lines with references to classical periods to create opulent settings.

name: Kurt Maetzig
headline: Kurt Maetzig, Pioneering German Director, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Maetzig, a pioneering figure in East Germany’s socialist film industry after World War II, helped postwar Germany come to terms with its Nazi past.

name: Henry Herx
headline: Henry Herx, Film Critic for Catholic Publications, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Herx judged the moral qualities of movies as well as their aesthetic ones.

name: Sun Myung Moon
headline: Rev. Sun Myung Moon, Self-Proclaimed Messiah Who Built Religious Movement, Dies at 92
abstract: The Korean evangelist’s Unification Church was notable for mass weddings, fresh-faced proselytizers and links to vast commercial interests.

name: Alan M. Kriegsman
headline: Alan M. Kriegsman, Who Won Pulitzer for Criticism, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Kriegsman, whose long career at The Washington Post coincided with a period of growth and diversification in American dance, was the first dance critic to win a Pulitzer Prize.

name: William W. Momyer
headline: Gen. William W. Momyer, Celebrated Pilot, Dies at 95
abstract: General Momyer was a famed World War II fighter pilot who would go on to command aerial combat and bombing operations during the early years of the Vietnam War.

name: Michael Clarke Duncan
headline: Michael Clarke Duncan, Actor, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Duncan rose from working as a ditch digger to employ his booming bass voice and immense physical presence in many movie roles, most notably a tragic prisoner with a healing touch in the 1999 film “The Green Mile.”

name: Charlie Rose
headline: Representative Charlie Rose, Tobacco’s Friend in the House, Dies at 73
abstract: As a Congressman in rural North Carolina, Mr. Rose worked to protect the tobacco industry and its farmers when political pressure on the industry was on the rise.

name: Jack Cermak
headline: Jack Cermak, a Wind Tunnel Innovator, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Cermak’s tunnel, which was roughly 10 times as long as aeronautical tunnels, could produce vertical wind currents and simulate powerful gusts.

name: Joe South
profession: Singer and Writer of Hit Songs
headline: Joe South, Singer and Writer of Hit Songs, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. South was a singer-songwriter who wove confrontational lyrics into bouncy pop hits of the late 1960s and early ’70s, including “Games People Play” and “(I Never Promised You a) Rose Garden.”

name: John F. Stacks
headline: John F. Stacks, Writer and Editor, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Stacks was a longtime reporter and editor at Time and the author of a biography of James B. Reston.

name: Art Modell
profession: Influential N.F.L. Owner but Not Always Beloved One
headline: Art Modell, Influential N.F.L. Owner but Not Always Beloved One, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Modell, an innovative promoter of the game, was idolized by N.F.L. fans in Cleveland, then vilified when he moved the club to Baltimore for the 1996 season.

name: Said K. Aburish
headline: Said K. Aburish, Palestinian Journalist, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Aburish, a former arms dealer with a Harvard M.B.A., skewered Arab leaders in his 11 books.

name: Gabriel Vahanian
profession: Was Linked to Death of God Movement
headline: Gabriel Vahanian, Professor, Dies at 85; Was Linked to ‘Death of God’ Movement
abstract: Mr. Vahanian’s 1961 social critique, “The Death of God: The Culture of Our Post-Christian Era,” gave a name to a seemingly atheistic but widely misunderstood theological movement.

name: Max Bygraves
headline: Max Bygraves, Jovial British Entertainer, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Bygraves’s easy singing and humor — a signature phrase was “I wanna tell you a story” — led to a long career of radio and stage shows, music and films.

name: Sy J. Schulman
profession: Planner for New York City Parks
headline: Sy J. Schulman, Planner for New York City Parks, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Schulman, a former mayor of White Plains, was a New York City parks official who helped ease residents’ opposition to a sewage plant in Harlem by creating Riverbank State Park.

name: William Moggridge
headline: William Moggridge, Designer and Laptop Pioneer, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Moggridge designed the first laptop, called the Grid Compass. Most recently, he was director of the Cooper-Hewitt National Design Museum.

name: Albert Marre
headline: Albert Marre, Director, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Marre directed or staged more than two-dozen Broadway shows during his more than 50 years in theater, but it was “Man of La Mancha” that brought him his greatest acclaim.

name: Verghese Kurien
headline: Verghese Kurien, Leader of India’s Milk Cooperatives, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Kurien helped thousands of dairy farmers create cooperatives to produce and market milk, reducing hunger and poverty and eventually transforming India into the world’s largest milk producer.

name: Munnu Kasliwal
headline: Munnu Kasliwal, a Favorite Jeweler of Connoisseurs, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Kasliwal’s designs were sold in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, collected by European royals and prized by celebrities, who were drawn to his sometimes monumental gems.

name: Gaeton Fonzi
headline: Gaeton Fonzi, Investigator of Kennedy Assassination, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Fonzi was called Ahab by colleagues who likened his relentless pursuit of details of the Kennedy assassination to the fictional hunt for a white whale.

name: Thomas Szasz
headline: Dr. Thomas Szasz, Psychiatrist Who Led Movement Against His Field, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Szasz wrote “The Myth of Mental Illness,” a book that questioned the legitimacy of his field and made enemies of many fellow doctors.

name: Jake Eberts
profession: Accidental Film Producer of Oscar Winners
headline: Jake Eberts, Accidental Film Producer of Oscar Winners, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Eberts, after trying engineering and banking without success, turned to film and produced gems like “Chariots of Fire,” “Gandhi,” “Dances With Wolves,” “The Killing Fields” and “Watership Down.”

name: Eli Zborowski
headline: Eli Zborowski, 86, Leader in Holocaust Remembrance, Dies
abstract: Mr. Zborowski, a Holocaust survivor, founded the American Society for Yad Vashem and fought for compensation for the victims of Nazi medical experiments.

name: Pedro Guerrero
headline: Pedro Guerrero, Who Captured Art in Photos, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Guerrero said that in photographing architecture he approached it as if it were sculpture.

name: Howard Moody
headline: Howard Moody, Who Led a Historic Church, Dies at 91
abstract: Rev. Moody was a church leader who hurled himself and his Greenwich Village congregation into roiling social issues.

name: Lia Lee
profession: Life Went On Around Her, Redefining Care
headline: Lia Lee Dies; Life Went On Around Her, Redefining Care
abstract: The story of Lia Lee, the severely brain-damaged daughter of Hmong refugees, inspired a book that affected the way American medicine is practiced across cultures.

name: Peter Lougheed
headline: Peter Lougheed, Ex-Premier of Alberta, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Lougheed turned Alberta into a major player in oil and gas and a pioneer in the development of oil sands.

name: Sid Watkins
profession: Safety Innovator in Formula One Racing
headline: Sid Watkins, Safety Innovator in Formula One Racing, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Watkins is credited with helping to save lives through methods on and off the track.

name: Jerome Kilty
profession: Made a Career of Interpreting Shaw
headline: Jerome Kilty, Who Made a Career of Interpreting Shaw, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Kilty was best known for “Dear Liar,” a play based on letters between George Bernard Shaw and Mrs. Patrick Campbell.

name: Michael Wreszin
headline: Michael Wreszin, Biographer of American Radicals, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Wreszin wrote biographies of Dwight Macdonald and other American antiwar activists.

name: Tony Goldman
headline: Tony Goldman, SoHo Pioneer, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Goldman was a real estate visionary who saw himself as a long-term investor in the revitalization of historic neighborhoods.

name: Eva Figes
headline: Eva Figes, Author and Feminist, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Figes was a refugee from Nazi Germany who became an acclaimed novelist, memoirist and critic best known for an influential feminist treatise, “Patriarchal Attitudes.”

name: Mary Rose McGeady
headline: Mary Rose McGeady, Nun Who Led Youth Homes, Dies at 84
abstract: Sister Mary Rose, a Roman Catholic nun, resuscitated Covenant House, the nation’s largest network of shelters for homeless youngsters, in the wake of a sex abuse scandal involving its founder.

name: Louis Simpson
headline: Louis Simpson, Poet of Everyday Life, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Simpson won the Pulitzer Prize in 1964 for “At the End of the Open Road,” and taught for many years at Berkeley and Stony Brook.

name: Russell E. Train
headline: Russell E. Train, Conservationist Who Helped Create the E.P.A., Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Train was among a select group of officials who shaped the world’s first comprehensive program for scrubbing the skies and waters of pollution.

name: Steve Sabol
headline: Steve Sabol, Cinematic Force for N.F.L., Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Sabol, a producer, writer, director and cameraman, took his father’s idea and, through cinematic ingenuity, helped propel the National Football League’s enormous popularity.

name: Tom Sims
headline: Tom Sims, Pioneer in Sport of Snowboarding, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Sims was credited with inventing one of the earliest snowboards and, as a world-champion competitor, with helping to further the acceptance of snowboarding in the sporting world.

name: Ashbel Green
headline: Ashbel Green, Longtime Editor at Knopf, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Green was a widely respected editor who shepherded more than 500 books into print, including the autobiography of Walter Cronkite and the works of Gabriel García Márquez.

name: Santiago Carrillo
headline: Santiago Carrillo, a Spanish Communist Leader, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Carrillo fought Gen. Francisco Franco’s fascist forces during the Spanish Civil War, and later promoted a new, more moderate Communism.

name: Rubén Zuno Arce
headline: Rubén Zuno Arce, Guilty in Drug Killing, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Zuno was a central defendant in the 1985 torture and killing of Enrique Camarena Salazar, an American drug enforcement agent, in Mexico.

name: Joshua Morse III
headline: Joshua Morse III, Law School Dean Who Defied Segregation, Dies at 89
abstract: In a time of often violent racial strife in the Deep South, the former dean of the University of Mississippi School of Law challenged prejudice and parochialism.

name: Haim Hefer
headline: Haim Hefer, Israeli Songwriter and Poet, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Hefer, who could be an acerbic critic of Israeli political leaders, helped forge a national identity in contemporary Hebrew with his lyrics and newspaper columns written in verse.

name: Tedi Thurman
headline: Tedi Thurman Dies at 89; Radio’s Miss Monitor
abstract: The “weather girl” on the NBC radio show “Monitor” in the late 1950s and early ’60s, Ms. Thurman made the forecasts “sound like an irresistible invitation to an unforgettable evening.”

name: Jerome Horwitz
headline: Jerome Horwitz, AZT Creator, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Horwitz created AZT in 1964 in the hope that it would cure cancer, but he entered the medical pantheon decades later when AZT became the first successful drug treatment for people with AIDS.

name: William Duckworth
headline: William Duckworth, Internet Composer, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Duckworth, a post-Minimalist who wrote “Time Curve Preludes,” grew to embrace the Internet as a focus of electronic works.

name: José Curbelo
headline: José Curbelo, Manager Behind Latin Music Acts, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Curbelo, a bandleader in his own right, had his biggest influence as manager of stars like Tito Puente and Machito Grillo.

name: Bettye Lane
headline: Bettye Lane Dies at 82; Photographer of Protests and Causes
abstract: Ms. Lane gained wide recognition for her rich trove of pictures documenting the feminist movement in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Claudine Mawby Walker
headline: Claudine Mawby Walker Dies at 90; Hollywood ‘Triplet’
abstract: Ms. Mawby Walker, her twin, Claudette, and their other sister, Angella, were three English girls who were child stars in the days of Jackie Coogan and the Little Rascals.

name: Edwin P. Wilson
headline: Edwin P. Wilson, the Spy Who Lived It Up, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Wilson’s larger-than-life world of business and espionage collapsed with his arrest in 1982 on charges of selling Libya 20 tons of powerful explosives.

name: Jennifer Jaff
headline: Jennifer Jaff, Advocate for the Ill, Dies at 55
abstract: Ms. Jaff was a lawyer whose nearly four-decade struggle with Crohn’s disease, an incurable gastrointestinal disorder, led her to become a leading advocate for people with chronic illnesses.

name: Marv Kessler
headline: Marv Kessler, Coach and Basketball Instructor, Dies at 80
abstract: Kessler, a product of Brooklyn’s schoolyards, spent more than half a century in basketball as a player, coach, scout and, most prominently, a camp instructor who molded young athletes.

name: Tereska Torrès
headline: Tereska Torrès, 92, Writer of Lesbian Fiction, Dies
abstract: Ms. Torrès was best known for “Women’s Barracks,” considered a landmark in lesbian fiction.

name: Gerard I. Nierenberg
headline: Gerard I. Nierenberg, Negotiation Expert, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Nierenberg’s frustration with the adversarial nature of legal disputes led him to develop methods of negotiating that he promoted in training seminars and popular books.

name: Maurice H. Keen
headline: Maurice H. Keen Dies at 78; Redefined Chivalry
abstract: Mr. Keen was a scholar who re-examined the code used among knights and determined it was meant to protect the warrior class rather than to emphasize good deeds.

name: Griffith Edwards
headline: Dr. Griffith Edwards, Addiction Specialist, Dies at 83
abstract: Dr. Edwards, a British psychiatrist, reshaped thinking about heavy drinking, the psychology of drug use and the implications for public policy.

name: Andy Williams
headline: Andy Williams, Crooner of ‘Moon River,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Williams became famous for his smooth easy-listening style and his successful TV shows of the 1960s.

name: Billy Barnes
headline: Billy Barnes Dies at 85; Helped Revive Revues
abstract: Mr. Barnes’s comic revues in the late 1950s and early ’60s skewered beatniks, television and other contemporary targets.

name: Herbert Lom
headline: Herbert Lom, Frustrated Boss of Inspector Clouseau, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Lom, a Czech-born actor, played roles including Peter Sellers’s boss in the Pink Panther franchise, Napoleon Bonaparte and a witch hunter in the horror film “Mark of the Devil.”

name: John Silber
headline: John Silber Dies at 86; Led Boston University
abstract: As its longtime president, Dr. Silber built B.U. into a world-class research center and one of the nation’s largest private universities but attracted critics.

name: Irving Adler
headline: Irving Adler, Teacher Fired in Red Scare, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Adler, a former New York City teacher, became a prolific writer of books on math and science for young people after being forced from the classroom during the early 1950s.

name: Robert Newton
headline: Robert Newton, Maker of Racing Tires, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Newton wanted a tire that could hold up on the track, so he developed his own and built Hoosier Racing Tire in 1957 with his wife.

name: Chris Economaki
headline: Chris Economaki, Rumbling Voice of Auto Racing, Dies at 91
abstract: A longtime writer and broadcaster, Mr. Economaki was considered the dean of American motorsports journalism.

name: Arthur O. Sulzberger
headline: Arthur O. Sulzberger, Publisher Who Transformed The Times for New Era, Dies at 86
abstract: Arthur Ochs Sulzberger guided The Times and its parent company through a period of expansion and change on a scale not seen since the newspaper’s founding.

name: Peter Praeger
profession: Surgeon With a Health Food Company
headline: Peter Praeger, a Surgeon With a Health Food Company, Dies at 65
abstract: Dr. Praeger was a co-chief of cardiothoracic surgery at Hackensack University Medical Center and chief executive of Dr. Praeger’s Sensible Foods, a maker of frozen natural foods.

name: Eugene D. Genovese
headline: Eugene D. Genovese, Historian of South, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Genovese, a Marxist who became a conservative Catholic, argued that slavery had a paternalistic side.

name: Leonard Lerman
headline: Leonard Lerman, a Pioneer in DNA Study, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Lerman, a molecular biologist, discovered how to manipulate DNA, and in doing so, helped other scientists further pursue the genetic code.

name: Reubin Andres
headline: Reubin Andres, an Advocate of Weight Gain, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Andres, noted in the study of diabetes, gained his widest attention for challenging the conventional standards of late-life weight maintenance.

name: Eddie Bert
headline: Eddie Bert, Jazz Trombone Player, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Bert played in pit orchestras on Broadway, onstage with jazz legends and on dozens of recordings.

name: Barry Commoner
headline: Scientist, Candidate and Planet Earth’s Lifeguard
abstract: Dr. Commoner, a biologist, was a leader among a generation of scientist-activists who recognized the toxic consequences of America’s technology boom.

name: Eric J. Hobsbawm
headline: Eric J. Hobsbawm, Marxist Historian, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Hobsbawm, author of a three-volume masterwork on the rise of industrial capitalism, was a leading light in a group of historians within the British Communist Party.

name: Barbara Ann Scott
headline: Barbara Ann Scott, Canadian Figure Skater, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Scott was 19 when she became the first Canadian to win an Olympic gold medal in figure skating singles, in 1948 in St. Moritz, Switzerland, and she remains the only one.

name: Carlos Moseley
headline: Carlos Moseley, Philharmonic Manager, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Moseley presided over the New York Philharmonic’s enormous growth as managing director, president and chairman.

name: James E. Burke
headline: James E. Burke, 87, Dies; Candid Ex-Chief of Johnson & Johnson
abstract: Mr. Burke’s handling of Tylenol’s poisonings in the 1980s is regarded as a textbook example of how to handle a public relations crisis.

name: Yvonne Mounsey
profession: City Ballet Dancer and a Teacher
headline: Yvonne Mounsey, City Ballet Dancer and a Teacher, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Mounsey put such a stamp on roles — even ones she did not create — that people still recall her delivery of certain moments after more than 50 years.

name: Stephen Frankfurt
headline: Stephen Frankfurt, Artist on Madison Ave., Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Frankfurt steered commercials away from the talking-head format and helped transform them into sophisticated, art-designed productions.

name: R. B. Greaves
headline: R. B. Greaves, Pop Singer, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Greaves’s 1969 hit, “Take a Letter, Maria,” about a man dictating a “Dear Jane” letter, reached No. 2 on the Billboard pop chart.

name: Robert J. Manning
headline: Robert J. Manning, Former Editor of The Atlantic, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Manning covered the final term of President Franklin D. Roosevelt for United Press and later edited The Atlantic Monthly, now known as The Atlantic, for 14 years.

name: Frank Wilson
headline: Frank Wilson, Motown Songwriter and Producer, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Wilson had a hand in composing “Love Child” by the Supremes and numerous other hits by the likes of Stevie Wonder and Marvin Gaye before becoming a minister in Los Angeles.

name: Irving Cohen
headline: Irving Cohen, King Cupid of the Catskills, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Cohen, the maître d’ of the Concord Hotel for half a century, helped thousands of nice Jewish boys meet nice Jewish girls.

name: Michael Henry Heim
headline: Michael Henry Heim, Literary Translator, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Heim, who taught for many years at the University of California, Los Angeles, translated literature from eight different languages.

name: Robert F. Christy
headline: Robert F. Christy, Atom Bomb Physicist, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Christy was a young physicist working on the Manhattan Project who came up with a critical insight that led to the creation of the world’s first atom bomb.

name: Sam Steiger
headline: Sam Steiger, Lawmaker and Lightning Rod, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Steiger, a New Yorker who transformed himself into a Western rancher, served five terms in the House as a Republican from Arizona and barged brashly through scandals.

name: Pedro A. Sanjuan
profession: Cleared U.S. Path for African Envoys
headline: Pedro A. Sanjuan Dies at 82; Cleared U.S. Path for African Envoys
abstract: Mr. Sanjuan, who worked in the Kennedy administration, implored businesses like drive-ins and restaurants to serve black diplomats.

name: Maurice S. Friedman
headline: Maurice S. Friedman, Martin Buber’s Biographer, Dies at 90
abstract: In translating Buber’s writings, Mr. Friedman introduced the Austrian-born philosopher and his influential work to an English-reading public.

name: Carroll F. Johnson
headline: Carroll F. Johnson, Schools Integrator, Dies at 99
abstract: Dr. Johnson, a Southern-born educator who was one of the first superintendents to voluntarily use busing to integrate an urban school district, did so in White Plains in the 1960s.

name: Howard H. Scott
headline: Howard H. Scott, a Developer of the LP, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Scott enjoyed a substantial career in record production, working with Glenn Gould and many leading orchestras.

name: Shlomo Venezia
headline: Shlomo Venezia Dies at 88; Wrote of Auschwitz Horror
abstract: For nearly 50 years, Mr. Venezia said little about his concentration camp experiences. That changed when he saw right-wing extremism re-emerge in Italy.

name: Sven Hassel
headline: Sven Hassel, Novelist Who Depicted Nazi Soldiers’ Lives, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Hassel, whose claims of serving in the German military were disputed, wrote pulp war fiction he hoped would be regarded as antimilitary.

name: Nguyen Chi Thien
headline: Nguyen Chi Thien, Whose Poems Spoke Truth to Power, From a Cell, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Thien, a dissident writer who wrote poetry opposing the Communist government in Vietnam, endured prolonged imprisonment, torture and solitary confinement.

name: Mervyn M. Dymally
headline: Mervyn M. Dymally, Who Broke Racial Barriers in California, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Dymally, who worked in poor areas to organize a new black Democratic base in the Los Angeles area, became California’s first foreign-born black state assemblyman in 1962.

name: Lois Smith
headline: Lois Smith, Publicist Who Mothered Star Clients, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Smith helped redefine the role of publicist from relentless promoter to savvy protector of star clients like Robert Redford and Meryl Streep.

name: Eric Lomax
headline: Eric Lomax, World War II Prisoner Who Forgave, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Lomax, a World War II British prisoner who was tortured by the Japanese and later forgave one of his tormentors, wrote the best-selling memoir, “The Railway Man.”

name: Alex Karras
headline: Alex Karras, All-Pro N.F.L. Lineman Who Also Starred as an Actor, Dies at 77
abstract: Karras, an All-Pro lineman for the Detroit Lions, gained attention for roles in the movies, like in “Blazing Saddles,” and on television, like in the sitcom “Webster.”

name: Barbara Blum
headline: Barbara Blum, Who Rescued Abused Willowbrook Residents, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Blum, a former social services official, made it her mission to find homes for mentally disabled people after their mistreatment at the Willowbrook State School on Staten Island became a national scandal in the 1970s.

name: John Tchicai
profession: Saxophone Player in Free Jazz Movement
headline: John Tchicai, Saxophone Player in Free Jazz Movement, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Tchicai played in Europe and in New York, composed works for orchestras and taught at the University of California in Davis.

name: Sam Gibbons
headline: Sam Gibbons, Democrat of Florida, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Gibbons, a longtime Democratic congressman from Florida was a D-Day veteran and a champion of free trade.

name: Turhan Bey
headline: Turhan Bey, Actor With Continental Charm, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Bey appeared in a string of films in the 1940s and ’50s and earned the nickname “the Turkish delight.”

name: Beano Cook
headline: Beano Cook, Irreverent College Football Analyst, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Cook’s witty observations as a commentator for ESPN and other networks earned him the nickname the Pope of College Football.

name: Keith Campbell
headline: Keith Campbell, Cloner of Sheep, Dies at 58
abstract: Dr. Campbell, a British cell biologist, helped create Dolly, the first mammal to be cloned from an adult animal.

name: Harris Savides
headline: Harris Savides, Visual Poet, Dies at 55
abstract: Mr. Savides, one of America’s most respected cinematographers, helped directors like Woody Allen and Gus Van Sant achieve the visual expressivity they sought.

name: Andrew Brimmer
profession: First Black Member on Fed Board
headline: Andrew Brimmer, First Black Member on Fed Board, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Brimmer, hailed for his international monetary policy expertise, was concerned with the economic conditions of poor blacks.

name: George Friedman
headline: George Friedman, Developer of Designer Perfumes, Dies at 77
abstract: The man behind scents named for fashion designers like Ralph Lauren, Paloma Picasso and Gloria Vanderbilt.

name: Roy Bates
headline: Roy Bates, Bigger-Than-Life Founder of a Micronation, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Bates commandeered a former British military outpost in the North Sea in 1966 and declared a sovereign nation that his family still lays claim to.

name: Ulrich Franzen
headline: Ulrich Franzen, Designer of Brutalist Buildings, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Franzen, whose fortresslike buildings seemed to buttress the interior landscape of New York City during the 1970s, helped design concrete and glass towers for Hunter College.

name: Gary Collins
headline: Gary Collins, Host of Miss America Pageant, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Collins became a familiar face in American living rooms in the 1980s as the congenial host of the syndicated afternoon talk show “Hour Magazine,” for which he won an Emmy.

name: William C. Friday
headline: William C. Friday, University of North Carolina Leader, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Friday, president of the University of North Carolina from 1956 to 1986, oversaw vast growth and a response to federal desegregation orders.

name: Eduard Volodarsky
headline: Eduard Volodarsky, Screenwriter Banned by Soviets, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Volodarsky’s films are recognized classics today in Russia, but his scripts cast doubt on the carefully manicured history of the Soviet Union and spent years on the shelves of state studios.

name: Arlen Specter
headline: Arlen Specter, Pennsylvania Senator, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Specter was at the center of many of the Senate’s most divisive legal battles, only to lose his seat in 2010 after quitting the Republican Party to become a Democrat.

name: Norodom Sihanouk
headline: Norodom Sihanouk, Cambodian Leader Through Shifting Allegiances, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Sihanouk, who was alternately charming and ruthless, raised the stature of Cambodia and won its independence from French colonial rulers in 1953.

name: George Whitmore Jr.
headline: George Whitmore Jr., Who Falsely Confessed to 3 Murders in 1964, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Whitmore’s coerced confession to “the Career Girl Murders” influenced the Supreme Court’s Miranda ruling and New York’s partial repeal of capital punishment.

name: George Whitmore
headline: George Whitmore, Climber Who Vanquished El Capitan, Dies at 89
abstract: In 1958, he was one of the first people to climb the 2,900-foot-tall sheer granite wall that looms over Yosemite National Park.

name: Basil L. Plumley
headline: Basil L. Plumley, Veteran of Three Wars, Dies at 92
abstract: Sergeant Major Plumley served in World War II, Korea and Vietnam and received the Silver Star, one of the more than 30 commendations during his 32-year military career.

name: Kyle Bennett
headline: Kyle Bennett, Bicycle Motocross Champion, Dies at 33
abstract: Mr. Bennett, nicknamed Butter for his fluid style, was the BMX world champion in 2002, 2003 and 2007.

name: S. Ward Casscells
headline: S. Ward Casscells, Pentagon Medical Chief, Dies at 60
abstract: Dr. Casscells, a successful cardiologist, stunned those who knew him when he joined the Army Reserve at age 54 and volunteered to go to Iraq.

name: John Hoffman
headline: John Hoffman, a Force in Energy Efficiency, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Hoffman developed the government’s Energy Star program and helped shape a treaty to protect the ozone layer.

name: Raoul De Keyser
headline: Raoul De Keyser, Intuitive Abstract Painter, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. De Keyser created abstractions with a striking economy of means, exhibited primarily in Belgium and the Netherlands until receiving international recognition in 1992.

name: Michael Asher
headline: Michael Asher, Conceptual Artist, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Asher, who used an approach known as institutional critique in his work, taught at the California Institute of the Arts for more than 30 years.

name: Eddie Yost
headline: Eddie Yost, Baseball’s Walking Man, Dies at 86
abstract: A durable third baseman in the American League, Mr. Yost had a penchant for garnering bases on balls. He was also a coach on the Mets’ 1969 World Series team.

name: Joseph Rosenmiller
headline: Joseph Rosenmiller, Nontraditional Philanthropist, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Rosenmiller earned a fortune building a chain of radio stations and then donated tens of millions to promote causes that he felt traditional philanthropies largely ignored.

name: Stanford R. Ovshinsky
headline: Stanford R. Ovshinsky Dies at 89, a Self-Taught Maverick in Electronics
abstract: A self-taught scientist, Mr. Ovshinsky invented the nickel-metal hybrid battery and contributed to the development of many other devices.

name: Sylvia Kristel
headline: Sylvia Kristel, 60, Dies; Starred in ‘Emmanuelle’
abstract: In addition to her “Emmanuelle” films, Ms. Kristel acted in mainstream movies by European directors and worked in Hollywood.

name: Slater Martin
headline: Slater Martin, Hall of Fame Lakers Guard, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Martin’s playmaking and defensive brilliance helped take the Minneapolis Lakers to four N.B.A. championship in the league’s first decade.

name: Norma-Lee
headline: Norma-Lee, Western Swing Artist, Dies at 58
abstract: She was a Canadian who became honorary mayor in a free-spirited California town.

name: Torkom Manoogian
headline: Torkom Manoogian, Archbishop of Armenian Orthodox Church, Dies at 93
abstract: Archbishop Manoogian was an advocate who worked to broaden public awareness of the Armenian genocide and who finished building the church’s first cathedral in North America.

name: David S. Ware
headline: David S. Ware, Adventurous Saxophonist, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Ware was a powerful and contemplative jazz saxophonist who helped lead a resurgence of free jazz in New York.

name: Frank Moore Cross
headline: Frank Moore Cross, Biblical Scholar, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Cross was an influential Harvard biblical scholar who played a central role in interpreting the Dead Sea Scrolls.

name: James R. Grover Jr.
headline: James R. Grover Jr., Ex-Congressman From Long Island, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Grover, a Republican from Suffolk County who served from 1963 to 1975, was known as steady and unpretentious.

name: Émile Allais
profession: Hailed as the Father of Modern Skiing
headline: Émile Allais, Hailed as the Father of Modern Skiing, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Allais, a champion French skier, helped shape the sport by developing and popularizing a new style of skiing in the 1930s.

name: Koji Wakamatsu
headline: Koji Wakamatsu, Self-Taught Movie Director, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Wakamatsu, a Japanese director and provocateur who flung sex, violence and politics on the screen in more than 100 films, was named Asian filmmaker of the year at the Busan International Film Festival two weeks ago.

name: Ethel Person
headline: Ethel Person, Who Studied Sexual Fantasies, Dies at 77
abstract: Dr. Person was a psychiatrist who examined what motivates transsexuals and transvestites, and argued that people shaped their lives by trying to live out their desires.

name: George McGovern
headline: George McGovern Dies at 90, a Liberal Trounced but Never Silenced
abstract: To the liberal Democratic faithful, Mr. McGovern remained a standard-bearer well into old age, writing and lecturing even as his name was routinely invoked by conservatives as synonymous with what they considered the failures of liberal politics.

name: E. Donnall Thomas
headline: E. Donnall Thomas, Who Advanced Bone Marrow Transplants, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Thomas showed it was possible to transplant bone marrow to save the lives of patients dying from blood cancer, a discovery that earned him a Nobel Prize.

name: Leon Jaroff
profession: Editor at Time and Discover Magazines
headline: Leon Jaroff, Editor at Time and Discover Magazines, Dies at 85
abstract: After nearly a decade of lobbying, Mr. Jaroff, a senior editor at Time magazine, convinced his corporate bosses that there was a market for a Time Inc. science magazine.

name: Russell Means
profession: Clashed With Law as He Fought for Indians
headline: Russell Means, Who Clashed With Law as He Fought for Indians, Is Dead at 72
abstract: Mr. Means, an Oglala Sioux, staged guerrilla-tactic protests that called attention to the nation’s history of injustices against its indigenous peoples.

name: Lincoln Alexander
headline: Lincoln Alexander, Canadian Trailblazer, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Alexander was the first black member of Canada’s Parliament and the nation’s first black lieutenant governor.

name: Claude Cheysson
headline: Claude Cheysson, Candid French Foreign Minister, Dies at 92
abstract: As an outspoken foreign minister in the socialist government of François Mitterrand in the 1980s, Mr. Cheysson barreled into difficult issues with often undiplomatic zeal.

name: Paul Kurtz
headline: Paul Kurtz, 86, Humanist Publisher, Dies
abstract: Mr. Kurtz was a philosophy professor, but his wider influence came as a writer and publisher of books and magazines advocating reason over faith.

name: Steve Paul
headline: Steve Paul Dies at 71; Owned ’60s Club in New York
