abstract: Mr. Paul opened the Scene in 1964. It became famous for brilliant moments in the history of rock music, as the place where Pink Floyd and the Doors shaped the music of the era.

name: Wilhelm Brasse
headline: Wilhelm Brasse Dies at 94; Documented Nazis’ Victims
abstract: Mr. Brasse was a photographer and prisoner at Auschwitz who was haunted by the pictures he was forced to take.

name: Jeff Blatnick
headline: Jeff Blatnick, 55, Dies; Won Olympic Gold in Wrestling
abstract: Mr. Blatnick overcame cancer to win gold in Greco-Roman wrestling at the 1984 Summer Games in Los Angeles.

name: Betty Binns Fletcher
headline: Betty Binns Fletcher Dies at 89; Liberal Stalwart on the Bench
abstract: Judge Fletcher generally wrote liberal opinions on matters like employment discrimination, environmental protection and the death penalty

name: Chester Hansen
profession: Rare Diarist of World War II
headline: Chester Hansen, a Rare Diarist of World War II, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Hansen’s diaries offered of view of World War II from his insider’s perch as an aide to Gen. Omar N. Bradley.

name: Betty Hart
profession: Studied Disparities in Childrens Vocabulary Growth
headline: Betty Hart Dies at 85; Studied Disparities in Children’s Vocabulary Growth
abstract: Dr. Hart’s work became a touchstone in debates over education policy, including what kind of investments governments should make in early intervention programs.

name: Anita Bjork
headline: Anita Bjork, Once ‘the New Garbo,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Bjork appeared onstage and in film both in Europe and the United States and was the star of a celebrated screen adaptation of Strindberg’s “Miss Julie.”

name: Margaret Osborne duPont
headline: Margaret Osborne duPont, Tennis Champion, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. duPont won six Grand Slam singles titles in the middle decades of the 20th century and also became one of the most dominant doubles players of her era.

name: Jacques Barzun
profession: Cultural Critic Saw the Sun Setting on the West
headline: Jacques Barzun Dies at 104; Cultural Critic Saw the Sun Setting on the West
abstract: Mr. Barzun was a wide-ranging scholar, educator and author of dozens of books who tried to reconcile the cultural achievements of Europe with the tastes of American life.

name: Emanuel Steward
headline: Emanuel Steward Dies at 68; Trainer of Boxing Champions
abstract: A genial presence in a hard-nosed sport, Mr. Steward trained more than 30 world champions, including Lennox Lewis and Evander Holyfield.

name: John Johansen
headline: John Johansen, 96, Last of ‘Harvard Five’ Architects, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Johansen designed many residences and other structures, several in Connecticut, that are regarded as Modernist classics.

name: Eloy Gutiérrez-Menoyo
headline: Eloy Gutiérrez-Menoyo, Cuban Dissident, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Gutiérrez-Menoyo went from fighting beside Fidel Castro as a rebel commander to spending 22 years in prison for trying to topple him.

name: Fiorenzo Magni
headline: Fiorenzo Magni, Italian Cyclist, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Magni was a bicycle racing champion whose fearlessness on descents and fortitude in difficult conditions earned him victories in Europe’s most prominent road races.

name: Hans Werner Henze
headline: Hans Werner Henze, Composer, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Henze’s prolific output, over more than 60 years, hewed to older forms like opera, ballet and symphonies.

name: Gudmund Vigtel
headline: Gudmund Vigtel, Pivotal Director of High Museum, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Vigtel’s efforts were said to have put Atlanta on the cultural map.

name: Arnold Greenberg
headline: Arnold Greenberg, a Founder of Snapple, Dies at 80
abstract: Along with two partners, Mr. Greenberg, a Brooklyn native, started a company that became one of the first to offer a line of beverages made with natural ingredients.

name: Arnold Greenberg
headline: Arnold Greenberg, Whose Manhattan Bookstore Fostered Wanderlust, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Greenberg left behind a law firm in favor of an independent bookstore, Complete Traveller, which he and his wife ran for more than three decades.

name: Dave May
headline: Dave May Dies at 68; Player Included in Aaron Trade
abstract: Mr. May, an outfielder for 12 seasons, was traded to Atlanta so that Hank Aaron could return to Milwaukee.

name: Danny Sims
headline: Danny Sims, Producer Who Signed Bob Marley, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Sims was a pivotal figure in the success of the reggae star Bob Marley when he was little known outside of Jamaica.

name: Terry Callier
headline: Terry Callier,  Singer and Songwriter, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Callier’s thoughtul baritone, which met with limited success in the ’70s, brought him fame and a revived career over two decades later, when he was rediscovered by British fans.

name: Letitia Baldrige
headline: Letitia Baldrige, Etiquette Maven, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Ms. Baldrige was an author, entrepreneur and authority on contemporary manners, but she was always identified with her Kennedy White House days.

name: John Fitch
profession: Glamorous Racer With a Flair for Danger
headline: John Fitch, Glamorous Racer With a Flair for Danger, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Fitch was a superstar speedster whose greatest achievement, the Fitch Inertial Barrier, can be found on public highways.

name: Lebbeus Woods
headline: Lebbeus Woods, Architect Who Bucked Convention, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Woods conceived of a radical environment, one intended for a world in conflict, in an era when many of his peers focused on corporate headquarters and high-rises.

name: Bill Dees
headline: Bill Dees, 73, Orbison Collaborator, Dies
abstract: Mr. Dees helped to write “Oh, Pretty Woman,” a song inspired by Roy Orbison’s wife, Claudette.

name: Gae Aulenti
headline: Gae Aulenti, Musée d’Orsay Architect, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Aulenti, one of the few Italian women to rise to prominence in architecture during the postwar years, was best known for her museum renovations and interior designs.

name: Arthur R. Jensen
headline: Arthur R. Jensen Dies at 89; Set Off Debate About I.Q.
abstract: Mr. Jensen was an educational psychologist whose 1969 article suggested that the gap in intelligence-test scores between black and white students might be rooted in genetic differences.

name: Jack Hood Vaughn
headline: Jack Hood Vaughn, Who Led Peace Corps in ’60s, Dies at 92
abstract: As the second director of the Peace Corps, Mr. Vaughn oversaw the corps at the height of its volunteer enrollment.

name: Larry Bloch
headline: Larry Bloch,  Who Built the Wetlands Club, Dies at 59
abstract: In an 1995 interview, Mr. Bloch spoke of his passions — to entertain people and to be an activist and environmentalist.

name: Richard N. Current
headline: Richard N. Current, Civil War Historian, Dies at 100
abstract: Professor Current was among the historians who raised the study of Abraham Lincoln to rigorous academic standards.

name: Milt Campbell
headline: Milt Campbell, 78, Olympic Decathlon Champion, Dies
abstract: Mr. Campbell was a gold medalist at the 1956 Summer Olympics in Melbourne, Australia, in the event said to determine the “world’s greatest athlete.”

name: Jacques Dupin
headline: Jacques Dupin,  Art Scholar and Poet, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Dupin was the author of a biography and monographs on Miró and for a long time one of the directors of the renowned Galerie Maeght in Paris.

name: Roger Wood
headline: Roger Wood, a Brazen New York Post Editor, Dies at 87
abstract: The former editor of The New York Post led a no-holds-barred style of reporting crime and other events in the city.

name: Elliott Carter
headline: Elliott Carter, Composer Who Decisively Snapped Tradition, Dies at 103
abstract: Mr. Carter, whose work won dozens of awards, spent nine decades in contemporary music and continued to explore new ground into his later years.

name: Han Suyin
headline: Han Suyin Dies; Wrote Sweeping Fiction
abstract: Dr. Han, who was believed to have been 96, was a medical doctor and proponent of Mao who also wrote novels and memoirs, including one that became the Hollywood film “Love Is a Many-Splendored Thing.”

name: Teri Shields
profession: Mother and Manager of Brooke Shields
headline: Teri Shields, Mother and Manager of Brooke Shields, Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. Shields was a single mother when she began managing her 11-month-old daughter, and when Brooke was 10, she arranged for a photographer to take nude pictures of her.

name: Thomas K. McCraw
headline: Thomas K. McCraw, Historian Who Enlivened Economics, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. McCraw was a Pulitzer Prize-winning author and a Harvard professor hailed for melding engaging prose and scholarship.

name: Robert W. Castle Jr.
profession: Outspoken Harlem Priest and Accidental Actor
headline: Robert W. Castle Jr., Outspoken Harlem Priest and Accidental Actor, Dies at 83
abstract: Father Castle, who ran an energetic ministry in Harlem in which spirituality and social action were indissolubly linked, was the subject of Jonathan Demme’s acclaimed documentary, “Cousin Bobby.”

name: Darrell Royal
headline: Darrell Royal, Football Coach at Texas, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Royal won three national championships and 11 Southwest Conference titles with the University of Texas and was elected to the College Football Hall of Fame in 1983.

name: Carmen Basilio
headline: Carmen Basilio Dies at 85; Took Title From Robinson
abstract: Mr. Basilio stepped up a weight class when he beat Sugar Ray Robinson in a split decision for his middleweight crown in 1957 at Yankee Stadium, but lost to him in 1958.

name: Frank J. Prial
profession: Guide to the World of Fine Wine
headline: Frank J. Prial, a Guide to the World of Fine Wine, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Prial’s down-to-earth Wine Talk column in The New York Times catered to ever more sophisticated connoisseurs of fine food and drink.

name: Leonardo Favio
headline: Leonardo Favio, Argentine Film Director, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Favio, an Argentine actor, movie director and popular ballad singer, became politically active as his popularity increased.

name: Jim Flick
headline: Jim Flick, Top Golf Instructor, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Flick, an adviser to more than 200 touring pros and countless weekend warriors, helped Jack Nicklaus improve his game on the senior tour.

name: James R. Dumpson
headline: James R. Dumpson, a Defender of the Poor, Dies at 103
abstract: Mr. Dumpson, as New York City’s commissioner of welfare in the 1960s, fiercely defended relief payments to the poor as both necessary and moral.

name: Ted Curson
profession: Trumpeter of the New and the Blue
headline: Ted Curson, Trumpeter of the New and the Blue, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Curson, a trumpeter who worked with mainstays and mavericks of jazz as well as leading his own bands, came of age during a time of seismic change in the form.

name: Theodore T. Jones Jr.
profession: Judge on New Yorks Top Court
headline: Theodore T. Jones Jr., Judge on New York’s Top Court, Dies at 68
abstract: Judge Jones, a leading proponent of measures to prevent wrongful convictions, first came to public attention in 2005, when he issued an injunction against a transit strike, which was defied by workers.

name: Lee MacPhail
headline: Lee MacPhail, Executive Who Led American League, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. MacPhail, a former general manager of the Yankees and the Baltimore Orioles, was president of the American League during the pine-tar dispute of July 1983.

name: Joseph Sargent
headline: Joseph Sargent, a Founder of a Ski Resort, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Sargent, a financier helped found the Killington ski area in Vermont, a once-little-known peak that grew into one of America’s largest winter sports resorts.

name: Joseph Sargent
headline: Joseph Sargent, an Emmy Winner Who Directed ‘Pelham One Two Three,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Sargent, who won four Primetime Emmys, was director of the film “The Taking of Pelham One Two Three,” in 1974.

name: Derek Hutchinson
profession: Pioneer of Sea Kayaking as a Sport
headline: Derek Hutchinson, Pioneer of Sea Kayaking as a Sport, Dies at 79
abstract: The kayak instructor, author and boat designer, completed a 100-plus-mile crossing of the North Sea from England to Belgium in a record 31 hours in 1976, a year after the same attempt ended in a spectacular failure.

name: Isaiah Sheffer
headline: Isaiah Sheffer, a Founder of Symphony Space, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Sheffer turned a rundown theater on the Upper West Side into the home of “Selected Shorts” and many other cultural events.

name: Susan Jeffers
headline: Susan Jeffers, Psychologist and Author, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Jeffers’s popular titles included “Feel the Fear and Do It Anyway” and other books that encouraged self-confidence.

name: Ellen Douglas
headline: Ellen Douglas, Novelist of Southern Life, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Douglas was praised for her attention to the nuances of Southern speech and for her unflinching but sympathetic characterizations.

name: Frank Peppiatt
headline: Frank Peppiatt, a Creator of ‘Hee Haw,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Peppiatt was a top producer of variety shows who created his biggest hit with his business partner John Aylesworth.

name: Valerie Eliot
headline: Valerie Eliot, Poet’s Wife and Defender, Dies at 86
abstract: Mrs. Eliot, who early on served as T.S. Eliot’s secretary, later went on to edit his letters and guard his reputation.

name: David Durk
headline: David Durk, Serpico’s Ally Against Graft, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Durk worked with Officer Frank Serpico to call attention to a culture of corruption in the New York Police Department in the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Will Barnet
headline: Will Barnet, Visionary Artist, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Barnet often used family members and friends as his subjects, and was known for elegantly stylized portraits and classically composed visions of beautiful women and children.

name: James L. Stone
headline: James L. Stone, Officer Decorated in Korean War, Dies at 89
abstract: Colonel Stone, then a first lieutenant, rallied his men in the face of overwhelming Chinese forces, then stayed to cover their retreat, actions that earned him the Medal of Honor.

name: Jack Gilbert
headline: Jack Gilbert, a Poet Whose Words Transformed Lives, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Gilbert, who won the National Book Critics Circle Award in 2005 for “Refusing Heaven,” was a peculiar figure in the contemporary poetry world in the sense that he wasn’t exactly in it.

name: Cleve Duncan
headline: Cleve Duncan, the Voice of ‘Earth Angel’, Dies
abstract: Mr. Duncan and the Penguins never replicated the success they enjoyed with “Earth Angel,” which sold more than 10 million copies.

name: Alf Kumalo
headline: Alf Kumalo, Whose Photography Indicted Apartheid, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Kumalo used his journalism experience to become a chronicler of the cruelties of apartheid and South Africa’s eventual emergence as a biracial democracy.

name: Lawrence Beaupre
headline: Lawrence Beaupre, Editor for Chiquita Articles, Dies at 68
abstract: He served as editor of The Cincinnati Enquirer when it renounced articles questioning the business practices of the Chiquita banana company in Central America.

name: Bertram Wyatt-Brown
headline: Bertram Wyatt-Brown, Historian Who Examined Southern Conduct, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Wyatt-Brown was a historian who documented how honor played a special role in the antebellum South and its institution of slavery.

name: Marshall J. Bouldin III
headline: Marshall J. Bouldin III, Painter of Politicians, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Bouldin’s subjects included 20th-century Southern politicians, President Richard M. Nixon’s daughters and William Faulkner. His portraits hung in the White House and in Congress.

name: Olympe Bradna
headline: Olympe Bradna, Stage and Screen Actress, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Bradna was a star of the Folies Bergère touring company before she won movie roles in Hollywood.

name: Martin Fay
headline: Martin Fay, Fiddler With the Chieftains, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Fay was a founding member of the Grammy-winning traditional Irish band, which was formed in 1962.

name: Wendell D. Garrett
headline: Wendell D. Garrett, Expert on Americana, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Garrett was an authority on decorative arts and known to the public as an appraiser on the PBS series “Antiques Roadshow.”

name: Bernard Lansky
headline: Bernard Lansky, Clothier Catering to Music Royalty, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Lansky, who owned a men’s wear store in the music district of Memphis, sold outfits to Elvis Presley, Carl Perkins, Isaac Hayes, the Jacksons, the Beach Boys, Johnny Cash and others.

name: Connie Wald
headline: Connie Wald, Whose Meals Became a Hollywood Tradition, Dies at 96
abstract: Mrs. Wald’s dinners became a social institution for the film community, as low-key and cozy as the guest lists were glamorous.

name: Bal K. Thackeray
headline: Bal K. Thackeray, Right-Wing Indian Party Leader, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Thackeray was a newspaper cartoonist who became a powerful influence in Mumbai by stoking the grievances of the native population and Hindus against outsiders.

name: Lucille Bliss
profession: Voice of Crusader Rabbit and Smurfette
headline: Lucille Bliss, Voice of Crusader Rabbit and Smurfette, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Bliss was the voice of the female character on “The Smurfs” in the 1980s and did work on the early cartoon series “Crusader Rabbit.”

name: Rex Hunt
profession: Symbol of British Defiance in the Windswept Falklands
headline: Sir Rex Hunt, Symbol of British Defiance in the Windswept Falklands, Dies at 86
abstract: In 1982, Sir Rex found himself, literally overnight, directing a tiny band of British military men against an amphibious Argentine invasion.

name: Cornel Lucas
headline: Cornel Lucas, Photographer Whose Portraits Defined Film Stars, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Lucas combined his patience, talent for lighting and large cameras to create memorable images of subjects like Marlene Dietrich, Lauren Bacall and Gregory Peck.

name: Leah Gottlieb
headline: Leah Gottlieb, a Designer of Swimsuits, Dies at 94
abstract: Born in Hungary, Mrs. Gottlieb made bathing suits that were worn by royalty, movie stars and Sports Illustrated swimsuit models.

name: Warren B. Rudman
headline: Warren B. Rudman, Blunt Senator Who Led Budget Struggle, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Rudman, a moderate and sometimes combative Republican, left his name on laws that sought to force the government to spend within its means.

name: Jane Holtz Kay
headline: Jane Holtz Kay, a Prophet of Climate Change, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Kay’s 1997 book, “Asphalt Nation,” told harsh truths about the environmental consequences of a car-centered society.

name: Elena Donaldson
profession: Chess Champion in U.S.S.R. and Then U.S
headline: Elena Donaldson, Chess Champion in U.S.S.R. and Then U.S., Dies at 55
abstract: Ms. Donaldson, who played for years for the Soviet Union, made her biggest headlines at a 1988 tournament when she eloped with the captain of the American team.

name: William Turnbull
headline: William Turnbull, Scottish Sculptor, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Turnbull blended modernism with archaic and primitive forms.

name: Gail Harris
profession: Last New York Giant to Hit Home Run
headline: Gail Harris, Last New York Giant to Hit Home Run, Dies at 81
abstract: After the team moved to San Francisco, Mr. Harris, a first baseman, had success with the Detroit Tigers before retiring in 1960.

name: Helmut Sonnenfeldt
profession: Expert on Soviet and European Affairs
headline: Helmut Sonnenfeldt, Expert on Soviet and European Affairs, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Sonnenfeldt was known as “Kissinger’s Kissinger” for his influence in advising Henry A. Kissinger, the architect of American foreign policy in the Nixon and Ford administrations.

name: Joseph Blotner
headline: Joseph Blotner, Faulkner Expert and Friend, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Blotner, a longtime professor and chronicler, may have been best known for a book about William Faulkner that went on for more than 2,000 pages.

name: David Taub
profession: Introducer of Pinot Grigio Wine to U.S
headline: David Taub, Introducer of Pinot Grigio Wine to U.S., Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Taub and his father expanded Americans’ palate for Italian wine beyond Soave Bolla and Chianti.

name: Art Ginsburg
headline: Art Ginsburg, TV Chef Who Didn’t Scoff at Cake Mix, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Ginsburg, who billed himself as Mr. Food, taught simple recipes in 90-second snippets aimed at hard-pressed working people, preaching an “anybody can do it” philosophy.

name: Bryce Courtenay
headline: Bryce Courtenay, Popular Australian Novelist, Dies at 79
abstract: Readers in the United States knew Mr. Courtenay mainly for his first novel, “The Power of One,” but he sold more than 20 million copies of 21 books in all. His last novel came out this month.

name: Larry Hagman
headline: Larry Hagman, Who Played J.R. Ewing in ‘Dallas,’ Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Hagman portrayed J.R. Ewing, one of television’s most beloved villains, and led the CBS series to global popularity.

name: Hector Camacho
headline: Hector Camacho, 50, Boxer Who Lived Dangerously, Dies
abstract: Mr. Camacho, the flamboyant boxer known as Macho, emerged from a delinquent childhood in New York City’s Spanish Harlem to become a world champion.

name: Vladka Meed
headline: Vladka Meed, Who Infiltrated Warsaw Ghetto, Dies at 90
abstract: Mrs. Meed, with her flawless Polish and Aryan good looks, was able to smuggle pistols, gasoline for firebombs and even dynamite to the Jewish fighters inside the Warsaw Ghetto during World War II.

name: Boris Strugatsky
headline: Boris Strugatsky, Writer Who Slyly Criticized Soviets, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Strugatsky collaborated with his brother, Arkady, on science fiction works that mirrored the Soviet Union.

name: Pete La Roca Sims
headline: Pete La Roca Sims, Distinctive Jazz Drummer, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Sims was one of the leading drummers of the postbop era of 1950s and ’60s.

name: Reis Leming
headline: Reis Leming, American Airman Who Saved Britons During a Disaster, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Leming was serving in an Air Force squadron in England in 1953 when Britain was hit by an enormous flood, killing hundreds.

name: Emily Squires
headline: Emily Squires, Emmy-Winning Director of ‘Sesame Street,’ Dies at 71
abstract: Ms. Squires was a member of a team of “Sesame Street” directors that won six Daytime Emmys for outstanding directing of a children’s series between 1995 and 2007.

name: Lawrence Guyot
headline: Lawrence Guyot, Civil Rights Activist Who Bore the Fight’s Scars, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Guyot was repeatedly jailed and beaten for helping blacks in Mississippi register to vote.

name: Patrick Edlinger
headline: Patrick Edlinger, a Trendsetter for Sport Climbing, Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. Edlinger and his 1988 ascent at a climbing competition in Utah helped popularize the sport, which he called “a form of yoga.”

name: Earl Carroll
headline: Earl (Speedo) Carroll, Lead Singer of the Cadillacs, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Carroll performed with the 1950s doo-wop group the Cadillacs, and later found contentment, plus a measure of abiding renown, as a New York City school custodian.

name: Joseph E. Murray
profession: Transplant Doctor and Nobel Prize Winner
headline: Joseph E. Murray, Transplant Doctor and Nobel Prize Winner, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Murray died in the hospital where he performed the first successful human organ transplant in 1954, when he gave a 23-year-old’s kidney to his identical twin.

name: Marvin Miller
headline: Marvin Miller, Union Leader Who Changed Baseball, Dies at 95
abstract: By building the Major League Baseball Players Association into a force that revolutionized the game, Mr. Miller became one of the most influential figures in the sport’s history.

name: Martin Richards
headline: Martin Richards, Broadway Producer, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Richards won an Oscar for the film adaptation of the musical “Chicago” 27 years after he helped bring it to Broadway.

name: Jerry Finkelstein
headline: Jerry Finkelstein, New York Power Broker, Dies at 96
abstract: For decades he was a man to see for political support and connections, and he derived much of his power from his ownership of The New York Law Journal.

name: Bryce Bayer
profession: Inventor of a Filter to Make Color Digital Pictures
headline: Bryce Bayer, Inventor of a Filter to Make Color Digital Pictures, Dies at 83
abstract: “Without his invention we’d still be getting only black-and-white pictures from our digital cameras,” an industry expert said.

name: Lois Bewley
headline: Lois Bewley, Multifaceted Ballerina, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Bewley, a dancer with the New York City Ballet and other companies, expanded into choreography, costume and stage design, opera direction and art.

name: Zig Ziglar
headline: Zig Ziglar, Motivational Speaker, Dies at 86
abstract: For more than 40 years, Mr. Ziglar stirred corporate groups with his distinctive blend of country wit, sound-bite optimism, Christian faith and good-natured nudging.

name: Frank Barsalona
headline: Frank Barsalona, Pioneering Rock Agent, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Barsalona, a New York talent agent who was a virtual quartermaster for the British Invasion, booked the first American concert tours of the Beatles and the Rolling Stones.

name: Mickey Baker
headline: Mickey Baker, Guitarist, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Baker rose from a difficult childhood to become an influence on future musicians in more than one genre.

name: George C. Kern Jr.
headline: George C. Kern Jr., Expert in Merger Law, Dies at 86
abstract: As a lawyer at the firm of Sullivan & Cromwell, Mr. Kern pioneered strategies for corporate takeovers.

name: Alan S. Oser
headline: Alan S. Oser, a Times Real Estate Writer, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Oser was an authority on the neighborhoods of New York and wrote and edited on the topic for more than 30 years.

name: Farish Jenkins
headline: Farish Jenkins, Expert on Evolving Fossils, Dies at 72
abstract: Dr. Jenkins discovered fossilized fish, hundreds of millions of years old, that resembled early mammals.

name: Lisa de Kooning
headline: Lisa de Kooning, Painter’s Daughter, Dies at 56
abstract: Ms. de Kooning, a sculptor herself, established the Willem de Kooning Foundation.

name: Ken Regan
headline: Ken Regan, Photojournalist Trusted by Celebrities, Dies
abstract: Mr. Regan photographed, among many others, Bob Dylan, Muhammad Ali and Edward M. Kennedy, often in quiet, personal moments.

name: David Schwendeman
headline: David Schwendeman, Museum’s Chief Taxidermist, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Schwendeman captured hundreds of specimens in seemingly everlasting life as the last full-time taxidermist at the American Museum of Natural History.

name: Gray Foy
profession: Artist and Avatar of a Gilded Age
headline: Gray Foy, Artist and Avatar of a Gilded Age, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Foy, an artist of considerable early reputation, was later known as a collector, host, tastemaker and perennial fixture of New York cultural life.

name: Chris Stamp
headline: Chris Stamp, a Manager and Discoverer of the Who, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Stamp hoped to make a documentary about a rising rock group, but he ended up becoming far more than an observer of the Who.

name: Rick Majerus
headline: Rick Majerus, College Basketball Coach, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Majerus, who was awaiting a heart transplant, compiled more than 500 wins combined at Marquette, Ball State, Utah and St. Louis University.

name: David Oliver Relin
headline: David Oliver Relin, Adventurous Journalist, Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. Relin suffered financially and emotionally after details in the best-selling book “Three Cups of Tea” were questioned.

name: Spain Rodriguez
headline: Spain Rodriguez, Artist of Underground Comics, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Rodriguez was part of the heyday of the underground “comix” movement in publications like The East Village Other and Zap.

name: James R. Whelan
profession: First Editor of The Washington Times
headline: James R. Whelan, First Editor of The Washington Times, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Whelan, who had a long career in journalism, was the founding editor and publisher of the newspaper. He resigned after two years, saying it was a “Moonie newspaper.”

name: Arthur Chaskalson
headline: Arthur Chaskalson, Chief South African Jurist, Dies at 81
abstract: Justice Chaskalson was the first presiding judge of the post-apartheid Constitutional Court and served as chief justice from 2001 to 2005.

name: Willis Whitfield
headline: Willis Whitfield, Inventor of Clean Room That Purges Tiny Particles, Dies at 92
abstract: The process created by Mr. Whitfield could completely replace the air in the room 10 times a minute.

name: Eileen Moran
headline: Eileen Moran, Special Effects Wizard, Dies at 60
abstract: Ms. Moran worked on landmarks of special effects like “Avatar,” the “Lord of the Rings” trilogy and “The Hobbit.”

name: Jack Brooks
headline: Jack Brooks, Former Texas Congressman, Dies at 89
abstract: Over 42 years, Mr. Brooks defied fellow Southerners to support civil rights, investigated abuses by Presidents Nixon and Reagan and attacked government waste.

name: Dave Brubeck
profession: Distinctive Sound Gave Jazz New Pop
headline: Dave Brubeck, Whose Distinctive Sound Gave Jazz New Pop, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Brubeck, best known for “Take Five,” experimented with time signatures and polytonality and explored baroque compositional devices and foreign modes.

name: Elisabeth Murdoch
headline: Elisabeth Murdoch, Matriarch of a Journalism Family, Dies at 103
abstract: Dame Elisabeth was the mother of the media tycoon Rupert Murdoch, and one of Australia’s most noted philanthropists.

name: Mona Ackerman
headline: Mona Ackerman, Advice Columnist, Dies at 66
abstract: Dr. Ackerman’s experience as a clinical psychologist informed a weekly advice column for The Huffington Post.

name: Oscar Niemeyer
headline: Oscar Niemeyer, Architect Who Gave Brasília Its Flair, Dies at 104
abstract: Mr. Niemeyer, the Brazilian architect, created flowing designs that infused Modernism with a new sensuality and inspired generations of architects worldwide.

name: Frederick Neumann
headline: Frederick Neumann, Actor, Director and Interpreter of Beckett, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Neumann was an early member of the New York experimental troupe Mabou Mines which, by 1990, had produced eight works by his friend Samuel Beckett.

name: Kanzaburo Nakamura
headline: Kanzaburo Nakamura, Stalwart of Kabuki, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Kanzaburo, whose career spanned five decades, initially immersed himself in the Kabuki classics before forging his own path both in Japan and worldwide.

name: Jonathan Harvey
headline: Jonathan Harvey, Modernist Composer, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Harvey, a British composer, was admired for his use of electronic sound in concert works and operas that could range from plainsonglike melody to elaborate orchestral textures.

name: Lars V. Hormander
headline: Lars V. Hormander Dies at 81; Unlocked Partial Differential Equations
abstract: Dr. Hormander’s work had broad applications in many scientific fields, including seismology and climatology.

name: Ray L. Heffner
headline: Ray L. Heffner, Often-‘Besieged’ University President, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Heffner guided Brown University during the late 1960s, when students protested against the Vietnam War and blacks strived for racial equality and greater acceptance.

name: Jon Kest
profession: Advocate for Low-Wage Workers in New York
headline: Jon Kest, Advocate for Low-Wage Workers in New York, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Kest, who organized a strike last month by New York City’s fast-food employees, was a founder of the Working Families Party.

name: Marty Reisman
headline: Marty Reisman, 82, a Wizard of Table Tennis, Dies
abstract: Mr. Reisman won national championships, won and lost fortunes on wagers and moved crowds to laughter as an opening act for the Harlem Globetrotters.

name: Peter Johnson
headline: Peter Johnson, Crusader Against Corruption, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Johnson — a war hero, police officer, crusader against Tammany Hall and lawyer — led a battle against union bosses who colluded with gangsters.

name: Robert Lescher
headline: Robert Lescher, Editor and Literary Agent, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Lescher’s writers included Robert Frost, Isaac Bashevis Singer, Alice B. Toklas, Benjamin Spock and Georgia O’Keeffe.

name: Patrick Moore
headline: Patrick Moore, Eccentric Astronomer and TV Host, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Moore, who hosted BBC’s “The Sky at Night” astronomy program, was known for both his outsize personality and his scientific work.

name: John Silva
headline: John Silva, Father of Helicopter Journalism, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Silva earned two Emmy Awards for his pioneering technical work, including for his conversion of a small helicopter into the first airborne virtual television studio.

name: Birger Stromsheim
profession: Hero on Skis in an Anti-Nazi Raid
headline: Birger Stromsheim, Hero on Skis in an Anti-Nazi Raid, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Stromsheim helped to destroy equipment that the Germans were using to produce what is known as heavy water, a crucial ingredient in making a nuclear weapon.

name: Jenni Rivera
headline: Jenni Rivera, Mexican-American Singer, Dies at 43
abstract: Ms. Rivera was one of the biggest stars of banda, a brassy, percussive form of Spanish-language pop music.

name: Homer R. Warner
profession: Pioneer of Using Computers in Patient Care
headline: Homer R. Warner, a Pioneer of Using Computers in Patient Care, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Warner was a trailblazer in a field that has come to be known as medical informatics, which involves the use of computers to help make medical decisions.

name: Saul P. Steinberg
headline: Saul P. Steinberg, Icon of the Corporate Takeover, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Steinberg was a leading figure of the deal-making era of the 1980s, mounting a well-publicized, but unsuccessful, takeover of Chemical Bank.

name: James D. Hodgson
headline: James D. Hodgson,  Labor Secretary and Ambassador, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Hodgson, appointed by President Richard M. Nixon, promoted construction jobs for minority workers and safer American workplaces.

name: Gloria Davy
profession: First African-American to Sing Aida at the Met
headline: Gloria Davy, First African-American to Sing Aida at the Met, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Davy, a Brooklyn-born soprano, was known as an interpreter of 20th-century music, including the work of Richard Strauss, Benjamin Britten and Paul Hindemith.

name: Galina Vishnevskaya
headline: Galina Vishnevskaya, Soprano and Dissident, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Vishnevskaya was a soprano of the postwar Soviet Union and later one of its most prominent political dissidents.

name: Ed Cassidy
headline: Ed Cassidy, Drummer for Jazz-Rock Band Spirit, Dies at 89
abstract: A musician with a jazz background, Mr. Cassidy brought a particularly tight backbeat to rock while playing with his stepson, Randy California.

name: Reinhold Weege
headline: Reinhold Weege, Creator of ‘Night Court,’ Dies at 62
abstract: After working on the sitcom “Barney Miller,” Mr. Weege developed the quirky comedy “Night Court,” which ran from 1984 until 1992.

name: Ravi Shankar
headline: Ravi Shankar, Sitarist Who Introduced Indian Music to the West, Dies at 92
abstract: A composer, trained in both Eastern and Western musical traditions, Mr. Shankar helped foster a worldwide appreciation of India’s traditional music.

name: Lisa Della Casa
headline: Lisa Della Casa, Soprano, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Della Casa, who combined an outstanding voice, stunning beauty and exceptional stage presence, became one of the foremost interpreters of Richard Strauss.

name: Russell Libby
headline: Russell Libby, Organic Farming Advocate, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Libby’s lifelong passion for growing food began when his fourth-grade teacher in Maine handed out packets of vegetable seeds to the class.

name: Colleen Walker
headline: Colleen Walker, Nine-Time Winner on L.P.G.A. Tour, Dies at 56
abstract: Ms. Walker won a major tournament, the 1997 du Maurier Classic, 10 months after giving birth.

name: Joe Allbritton
headline: Joe Allbritton, TV and Banking Titan, Dies at 87
abstract: The owner of a major communications company, Mr. Allbritton also climbed Washington’s social hierarchy, becoming the foremost banker to Embassy Row.

name: Hal Schaefer
profession: Jazz Pianist and Marilyn Monroe Friend
headline: Hal Schaefer, Jazz Pianist and Marilyn Monroe Friend, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Schaefer was an arranger and modern jazz composer, as well as a vocal coach to Marilyn Monroe and other film stars.

name: N. Joseph Woodland
headline: N. Joseph Woodland, Inventor of the Bar Code, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Woodland helped conceive of a technology that helped revolutionize the retail industry and today graces nearly every surface of contemporary life.

name: Forrest Shumway
headline: Forrest Shumway, a White Knight of Deal Making, Dies at 85
abstract: After his uncle pressured him to work for Signal Oil, Mr. Shumway built the company into a successful conglomerate.

name: Maurice Herzog
headline: Maurice Herzog, 93, Dies; Led Historic Himalaya Climb
abstract: Mr. Herzog was hailed as a hero in France in 1950 when he and a fellow climber became the first men to conquer a peak of more than 26,000 feet.

name: Mary Ann Fischer
headline: Mary Ann Fischer, Whose Quintuplets Were a U.S. First, Dies at 79
abstract: Mrs. Fischer, who already had five children at home in Aberdeen, S.D., made big news in 1963 by delivering five more.

name: Donnie Andrews
headline: Donnie Andrews, the Real-Life Omar Little, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Andrews, a drug dealer and robber who later counseled addicts and helped the government bring down a gang, inspired a character on “The Wire,” an acclaimed HBO drama.

name: William F. House
headline: Dr. William F. House, Inventor of Pioneering Ear-Implant Device, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. House developed a surgical procedure for a debilitating form of vertigo that cured the astronaut Alan B. Shepard.

name: Gustavo Archilla
headline: Gustavo Archilla, an Inspiration for Gay Marriage, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Archilla and his partner, Elmer Lokkins, lived together in Manhattan for 58 years before eloping to Canada in 2003 and coming out publicly.

name: Roger Prigent
headline: Roger Prigent, 89, Photographer and Antiquarian, Dies
abstract: After a diagnosis of macular degeneration, Mr. Prigent reinvented himself as a dealer in antiques and was a connoisseur of the French Empire style.

name: John Rosen
headline: Dr. John Rosen, Who Pushed to Prevent Lead Poisoning, Dies at 77
abstract: Dr. Rosen went on to persuade New York City to adopt stricter standards for removing lead paint from tens of thousands of old buildings.

name: Jeni LeGon
headline: Jeni LeGon, Singer and Solo Tap-Dancer, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. LeGon’s career in movies was frustrated by Hollywood racism that relegated her to maids’ roles.

name: Daniel Inouye
profession: Hawaiis Quiet Voice of Conscience in Senate
headline: Daniel Inouye, Hawaii’s Quiet Voice of Conscience in Senate, Dies at 88
abstract: Daniel K. Inouye, who served nearly 48 years in the Senate, was a Democrat who broke racial barriers on Capitol Hill.

name: Mary Griggs Burke
headline: Mary Griggs Burke, Japanese Art Connoisseur, Dies at 96
abstract: Mrs. Burke amassed the most comprehensive collection of Japanese art in the West and has left her collection to museums.

name: Frank Macchiarola
profession: Called the Standard for a New York Schools Chief
headline: Frank Macchiarola, Called the ‘Standard’ for a New York Schools Chief, Dies at 71
abstract: A sanitation worker’s son and a product of Roman Catholic schools, Dr. Macchiarola led New York’s public school system from 1978 to 1983.

name: Alex Moulton
headline: Alex Moulton, Creator of Quirky Small-Wheeled Bike, Dies at 92
abstract: The Moulton bicycle, the forerunner of the collapsible, portable bikes of today, was spurred by the determination of Mr. Moulton, an automotive engineer, to improve upon the traditional bicycle.

name: Robert Bork
headline: A Conservative Whose Supreme Court Bid Set the Senate Afire
abstract: Judge Bork’s 1987 nomination to the Supreme Court was rejected by the Senate, not on qualifications but on judicial philosophy and temperament. He died Wednesday at 85.

name: Amnon Lipkin-Shahak
profession: Israeli Military Leader and Peace Negotiator
headline: Amnon Lipkin-Shahak, Israeli Military Leader and Peace Negotiator, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Lipkin-Shahak, a former chief of staff of the Israeli military and cabinet minister, was a trusted intermediary in talks with the Palestinians before and after the Oslo Accords.

name: Frank Beardsley
headline: Frank Beardsley, 97, Storied Father of 20
abstract: Mr. Beardsley, a retired Navy chief warrant officer, married Helen North in 1961, and their merger of two large families inspired a book and two movies, both titled “Yours, Mine and Ours.”

name: Gil Friesen
headline: Gil Friesen, Entertainment Executive, Dies at 75
abstract: Musicians who were taken under Mr. Friesen’s wing say he went beyond his responsibilities to become a mentor and an ally.

name: Spencer Cox
headline: Spencer Cox, AIDS Activist, Dies at 44
abstract: A member of the Treatment Action Group, Mr. Cox helped push antiretroviral drugs forward, leading to the first effective medical protocols to combat AIDS.

name: Vernice D. Ferguson
headline: Vernice D. Ferguson, Leader and Advocate of Nurses, Dies at 84
abstract: As chief nursing officer at the Veterans Administration, Ms. Ferguson fought to win better opportunities and more respect for nurses.

name: Larry L. King
headline: Larry L. King, Texan Author and Playwright, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. King mined his home state for material in a range of books, essays and plays, among them “The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas.”

name: Larry King
profession: Breezy Interviewer of the Famous and Infamous
headline: Larry King, Breezy Interviewer of the Famous and Infamous, Dies at 87
abstract: Over five decades, he chatted with an estimated 50,000 people from all walks of life, from presidents and pundits to swindlers and U.F.O. “experts.”

name: Inez Andrews
headline: Inez Andrews, Gospel Singer, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Andrews performed with the Caravans, with her own group and as a solo artist.

name: Lee Dorman
headline: Lee Dorman, Bass Guitarist, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Dorman, a member of the psychedelic rock band Iron Butterfly, played on one of the genre’s most recognizable songs, “In-a-Gadda-da-Vida.”

name: Midge Turk Richardson
headline: Midge Turk Richardson, Ex-Nun and Editor, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Richardson, who appeared as an extra in more than 100 Hollywood films as a child, spent years as Sister Agnes Marie before coming to New York and eventually becoming editor of Seventeen magazine.

name: Jimmy McCracklin
headline: Jimmy McCracklin, R&B Singer and Songwriter, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. McCracklin, whose music spanned eras of rhythm and blues styles, recorded hundreds of songs, including the rock ’n’ roll classic “The Walk.”

name: Albert Hirschman
headline: Albert Hirschman, Optimistic Economist, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Hirschman, who in his youth helped rescue thousands of artists and intellectuals from Nazi-occupied France, went on to become an influential economist known for his optimism.

name: Larry Morris
headline: Larry Morris, ’63 Title Game Star, Dies at 79
abstract: Known as the Brahma Bull for his bruising play as an all-American at Georgia Tech and as an 11-year professional, Mr. Morris was named to the N.F.L.’s all-decade team for the 1960s.

name: Jack Klugman
headline: Jack Klugman, Actor of Everyman Integrity, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Klugman was a character actor who leapt to television stardom as Oscar Madison on “The Odd Couple” and as the crusading pathologist of “Quincy, M.E.”

name: Richard Adams
headline: Richard Adams, Same-Sex Spouse Who Sued U.S., Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Adams legally married Tony Sullivan during a brief window in Colorado, but their lawsuit seeking federal recognition, the first of its kind, did not succeed.

name: Richard Adams
profession: Novel Watership Down Became a Phenomenon
headline: Richard Adams, Whose Novel ‘Watership Down’ Became a Phenomenon, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Adams’s theme-rich rabbit tale from the early 1970s made him one of the world’s best-selling writers.

name: Charles Durning
headline: Charles Durning, Prolific Character Actor, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Durning was a familiar presence on both stage and screen, with roles including a lonely widower in the film “Tootsie” and Big Daddy in the play “Cat on a Hot Tin Roof.”

name: Richard Baum
profession: Connected China Watchers on the Web
headline: Richard Baum, 72, Dies; Connected China Watchers on the Web
abstract: Mr. Baum presided over Chinapol, an online discussion group about China that has become an essential forum for many experts, diplomats and journalists.

name: Art Larsen
headline: Art Larsen, Quirky Tennis Champion, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Larsen, whose habit of tapping things earned him the nickname Tappy, won the precursor to the United States Open in 1950 and was inducted into the Tennis Hall of Fame in 1969.

name: Brad Corbett
headline: Brad Corbett, Who Owned Texas Rangers, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Corbett’s tenure as principal owner of the Texas Rangers baseball team brought the franchise Steinbrenner-like hubris and pocketbook diplomacy, but only middling success.

name: Elwood V. Jensen
headline: Elwood V. Jensen, Pioneer in Breast Cancer Treatment, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Jensen’s studies of steroid hormones led to new treatments for breast cancer that have been credited with saving or extending hundreds of thousands of lives.

name: Ray Collins
headline: Ray Collins of the Mothers of Invention Dies
abstract: Though Mr. Collins hired Frank Zappa and with him recorded avant-garde rock, his tastes were more mainstream.

name: Fontella Bass
headline: Fontella Bass, 72, Singer of ‘Rescue Me,’ Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Bass, born into a musical family, said no one rescued her. She had to stand up for her own rights as an artist.

name: H. Norman Schwarzkopf
headline: Gen. H. Norman Schwarzkopf, U.S. Commander in Gulf War, Dies at 78
abstract: General Schwarzkopf, who was lauded for his leadership during the war, was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom, and Queen Elizabeth II made him an honorary knight.

name: Gerry Anderson
headline: Gerry Anderson, 83, Dies; Made Futuristic Puppets
abstract: Mr. Anderson was known for his children’s show “Thunderbirds,” but he also was a force behind more grown-up fare like “Space 1999.”

name: Frank Calabrese
headline: Frank Calabrese, Chicago Mob Hit Man, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Calabrese, also known as Frankie Breeze, was responsible for at least 13 murders.

name: Cliff Osmond
headline: Cliff Osmond, Prolific Character Actor, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Osmond appeared in films including “The Front Page” and television shows, among them “The Twilight Zone.”

name: Headmistress
headline: Headmistress, Jilted Lover, Killer, Then a Force for Good in Jail
abstract: Mrs. Harris’s 1981 murder trial galvanized a nation mulling feminist perspectives with its story of vengeance by an aging woman scorned.

name: Jeffrey Potter
headline: Jeffrey Potter, Biographer of Pollock, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Potter’s work “To a Violent Grave” was based on his own recollections as well as interviews with many who knew Jackson Pollock.

name: Rita Levi-Montalcini
headline: Dr. Rita Levi-Montalcini, Nobel Winner, Dies at 103
abstract: By studying chicken embryos in the bedroom of her house in Turin, Italy, Dr. Levi-Montalcini discovered how embryo cells built a latticework of intricate connections.

name: Richard Rodney Bennett
headline: Richard Rodney Bennett, British Composer, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Bennett had a long, distinguished career that moved with ease among classical concert music, jazz and film.

name: Catherine O’Neill
headline: Catherine O’Neill, Advocate for Women and Children, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. O’Neill, the co-founder of the Women’s Commission for Refugee Women and Children, had a professional career that included stops in the private, public and charitable sectors.

name: Jane Holmes Dixon
headline: Jane Holmes Dixon, Bishop Who Stared Down Barriers, Dies at 75
abstract: Bishop Dixon, a leader in the Diocese of Washington, was elected as the second female bishop in the history of the Episcopal Church.

name: Carl Woese
headline: Carl Woese Dies at 84; Discovered Life’s ‘Third Domain’
abstract: Dr. Woese was a biophysicist and evolutionary microbiologist who made a discovery 35 years ago that altered scientific understanding of evolution.

name: Marva Whitney
profession: Singer in the James Brown Revue
headline: Marva Whitney, Singer in the James Brown Revue, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. Whitney, who was nicknamed Soul Sister No. 1, found her greatest measure of success as a vocalist whom James Brown trusted to hold her own onstage.

name: Mike Auldridge
headline: Mike Auldridge Dies at 73; Lent Dobro Fresh Elegance
abstract: Mr. Auldridge, a guitarist known for his liquid, round-toned phrasing, performed with Alison Krauss and Lyle Lovett, among other singers.

name: Harry Carey Jr.
headline: Harry Carey Jr., Sidekick to John Wayne, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Carey Jr. was considered the last surviving member of a group known informally in Hollywood as the John Ford stock company.

name: Beate Gordon
profession: Long-Unsung Heroine of Japanese Womens Rights
headline: Beate Gordon, Long-Unsung Heroine of Japanese Women’s Rights, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Gordon almost single-handedly wrote women’s rights into the Constitution of modern Japan at 22, and then kept silent about it for decades.

name: Patti Page
headline: Patti Page, Honey-Voiced ’50s Pop Sensation, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Page was known for hits like “Tennessee Waltz,” “Old Cape Cod” and “(How Much Is) That Doggie in the Window.”

name: Rebecca Tarbotton
headline: Rebecca Tarbotton, Environmental Activist, Dies at 39
abstract: Ms. Tarbotton helped convince big banks to stop financing mountaintop removal mining and helped persuade Disney to reduce its use of paper made from trees cut down in rain forests.

name: Estelle Cooper
headline: Estelle Cooper, Park Chief Accused of Theft, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Cooper, credited with turning around the dilapidated Flushing Meadows-Corona Park, stepped down last year amid charges that she stole over $50,000 from a nonprofit group.

name: Gerda Lerner
headline: Gerda Lerner, a Feminist and Historian, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Lerner was a prolific writer whose novels, short stories, essays and teachings helped forge graduate programs for women and college courses on women and society.

name: Jayne Cortez
headline: Jayne Cortez, Jazz Poet, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Cortez’s work embodied many categories simultaneously: written verse, African and African-American oral tradition, the discourse of political protest, and jazz and blues.

name: Arthur Caliandro
headline: Arthur Caliandro, Minister at Marble Collegiate, Dies at 79
abstract: Dr. Caliandro, who succeeded the Rev. Norman Vincent Peale as the senior minister at the Manhattan church, developed his own style by promoting women and focusing on local needs.

name: Andrew P. O’Rourke
headline: Andrew P. O’Rourke, 79, Rival to Mario Cuomo, Dies
abstract: Mr. O’Rourke, a Republican, managed Westchester County for 14 years and ran for New York governor against the popular incumbent in 1986.

name: John Sheardown
headline: John Sheardown, Canadian Who Sheltered Americans in Tehran, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Sheardown, a diplomat, played a consequential role in the “Canadian caper” during the Iran hostage crisis, though his role was unmentioned in the recent movie “Argo.”

name: William Rees-Mogg
profession: Ex-Editor of The Times of London
headline: William Rees-Mogg, Ex-Editor of The Times of London, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Rees-Mogg was one of Britain’s most respected, if mercurial, conservative voices, rising to the defense of Richard Nixon as well as the Rolling Stones.

name: Michael Cronan
profession: Gave TiVo and Kindle Their Names
headline: Michael Cronan, Who Gave TiVo and Kindle Their Names, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Cronan, a San Francisco-based graphic designer and marketing executive, placed his stamp on popular culture with the pair of brand names he came up with a decade apart.

name: Bob Jones
profession: New York D.J. Heard on Milkmans Matinee
headline: Bob Jones, New York D.J. Heard on ‘Milkman’s Matinee’, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Jones, who loved to play the music of stars like Sinatra and Ellington, was known for sprinkling his WNEW-AM broadcast with details about the singers and composers.

name: Bob Jones
headline: Bob Jones, Behind-the-Stage Force at Newport Festivals, Dies at 86
abstract: For decades he helped shape Rhode Island’s venerable folk and jazz events, presenting stars and unknowns alike. One colleague called him a “test pilot of jazz.”

name: Tingye Li
profession: Played Crucial Role in Lasers Development
headline: Tingye Li Dies at 81; Played Crucial Role in Laser’s Development
abstract: Dr. Li’s calculations in the early 1960s helped guide the development of the laser and propel the dizzying increase in the speed of fiber-optic communication.

name: Pete Elliott
headline: Pete Elliott, Football All-American and Coach, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Elliott, who played on two unbeaten Michigan teams and was a head coach at four universities (Nebraska, California, Illinois and Miami), later became the longest tenured executive director of the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

name: Alexander Leaf
headline: Alexander Leaf Dies at 92; Linked Diet and Health
abstract: Dr. Leaf was a physician, researcher, administrator and professor who studied heart disease, longevity and the dangers of global warming.

name: Klemens von Klemperer
headline: Klemens von Klemperer Dies at 96; Wrote of Nazi Era
abstract: Dr. von Klemperer, a refugee from Nazi Germany, wrote what is considered the seminal history of the movement among the country’s conservative elite to overthrow Hitler.

name: Ada Louise Huxtable
headline: Ada Louise Huxtable, Champion of Livable Architecture, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Huxtable pioneered modern architectural criticism in The New York Times, celebrating buildings that respected human dignity and civic history.

name: Robert C. Holland
headline: Robert C. Holland, Governor for Fed, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Holland was the first staff member of the Federal Reserve System to be appointed directly to its Board of Governors.

name: Harvey Shapiro
headline: Harvey Shapiro, Poet and Editor, Dies at 88
abstract: In his work Mr. Shapiro examined his life as a man, a husband, a father and a Jew.

name: Richard Ben Cramer
headline: Richard Ben Cramer, Writer of Big Ambitions, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Cramer, a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist, was the author of “What It Takes,” an intimate, deeply reported account of the 1988 presidential election.

name: Claude-Anne Lopez
headline: Claude-Anne Lopez Dies at 92; Told of Franklin’s Private Life
abstract: Ms. Lopez, seeking work in academia, started as a transcriber for the Papers of Benjamin Franklin at Yale University. She would become an authority — and an admirer.

name: Fred L. Turner
headline: Fred L. Turner, Innovative Chief of McDonald’s, Dies at 80
abstract: During Mr. Turner’s tenure, the restaurant chain expanded, and the Chicken McNugget, the Egg McMuffin and the Happy Meal were introduced.

name: Sol Yurick
profession: Author of The Warriors Gang Novel
headline: Sol Yurick, 87, Author of ‘The Warriors’ Gang Novel
abstract: Mr. Yurick’s best-known work, the 1965 gang novel “The Warriors,” was based on his experiences in the New York City Welfare Department, and was turned into a movie in 1979.

name: James M. Buchanan
headline: James M. Buchanan, Economic Scholar and Nobel Laureate, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Buchanan, a professor emeritus at George Mason University and a conservative thinker on taxes and size of government, won the 1986 Nobel in economic sciences.

name: Celeste Bartos
headline: Celeste Bartos, New York Philanthropist, Dies at 99
abstract: Mrs. Bartos, whose gifts included support for the New York Public Library and the Museum of Modern Art, has her name on the lecture hall and education center at the library’s flagship branch.

name: Richard McWilliam
headline: Richard McWilliam, Trading Card Innovator, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. McWilliam’s leadership made Upper Deck an industry powerhouse at a time when baseball and other sports cards were increasingly coveted by adult collectors.

name: Jeanne Manford
profession: Stood Up for Her Gay Son, Inspiring Others
headline: Jeanne Manford, 92, Who Stood Up for Her Gay Son, Inspiring Others, Dies
abstract: Mrs. Manford, whose son, a gay-rights advocate, was beaten in 1972, founded Parents, Families and Friends of Lesbians and Gays.

name: Jeffrey O’Connell
headline: Jeffrey O’Connell, Legal Scholar of No-Fault Coverage, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. O’Connell helped devise the model for “no fault” auto insurance to protect traffic accident victims, lower car insurance rates and curb ambulance-chasing lawyers.

name: Evan Connell
headline: Evan Connell, Novelist of Many Genres, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Connell’s diverse writing included two books, “Mrs. Bridge” and “Mr. Bridge,” that ended up being made into a film starring Paul Newman and Joanne Woodward.

name: Huell Howser
headline: Huell Howser, Folksy Public TV Host, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Mr. Howser roamed the highways of the Golden State as the host of “California’s Gold,” perhaps the most popular public television show in the state.

name: Claude Nobs
headline: Claude Nobs, Founder of Montreux Jazz Festival, Dies at 76
abstract: A job at a local tourist board led Mr. Nobs to found “the Rolls-Royce of jazz festivals.”

name: Mariangela Melato
headline: Mariangela Melato, Italian Actress, Dies at 71
abstract: Ms. Melato starred alongside Giancarlo Giannini in films by Lina Wertmüller.

name: Ruth Carter Stevenson
headline: Ruth Carter Stevenson of the Amon Carter Museum Dies at 89
abstract: Mrs. Stevenson, a loyal daughter who followed the wishes of her father, Amon G. Carter Sr., built a museum of American art.

name: Jeanne Vertefeuille
headline: Jeanne Vertefeuille, C.I.A. Official Who Helped Catch a Notorious Mole, Dies at 80
abstract: A career C.I.A. employee who kept a low profile, she helped unmask one of the nation’s most notorious traitors, Aldrich Ames.

name: Kenojuak Ashevak
headline: Kenojuak Ashevak, Artist From the Canadian Arctic, Dies at 85
abstract: The once-nomadic artist from Canada’s Arctic regions is best remembered for her prints and drawings.

name: Aaron Swartz
headline: Internet Activist, a Creator of RSS, Is Dead at 26, Apparently a Suicide
abstract: Aaron Swartz helped create RSS, a now ubiquitous format, and later became known for his efforts to make many Internet files available free online.

name: Eugene C. Patterson
headline: Eugene C. Patterson, Editor and Civil Rights Crusader, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Patterson was a Pulitzer Prize winner who fought racial injustice in his columns for The Atlanta Constitution and was later an editor at The Washington Post and The St. Petersburg Times.

name: Ralph G. Martin
headline: Ralph G. Martin, a Best-Selling Biographer, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Martin’s subjects included Winston Churchill’s mother, Golda Meir and the Kennedys.

name: Susan Nolen-Hoeksema
headline: Susan Nolen-Hoeksema, Psychologist Who Studied Depression in Women, Dies at 53
abstract: Dr. Nolen-Hoeksema wrote for both academic and popular audiences, and argued that women would be happier if they stopped overthinking.

name: Nagisa Oshima
headline: Nagisa Oshima, Iconoclastic Filmmaker, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Oshima, who challenged Japanese society with his movies, gained international notoriety with “In the Realm of the Senses.”

name: Daniel J. Edelman
headline: Daniel J. Edelman, a Publicity Pioneer, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Edelman was the founder and chairman of one of the largest public relations firms in the world and a groundbreaker in the field.

name: D. Brainerd Holmes
headline: D. Brainerd Holmes, a Leader in Space Race, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Holmes led NASA’s manned spaceflight program during a period that included John Glenn’s orbit of Earth and helped set the stage for the first moon landing.

name: Vincent Sombrotto
headline: Vincent Sombrotto, Who Led Postal Strike, Dies at 89
abstract: After the wildcat strike in 1970, Mr. Sombrotto went on to lead one of the nation’s most powerful postal workers’ unions.

name: Yuri M. Schmidt
headline: Yuri M. Schmidt, Rights Lawyer in Russia, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Schmidt was a winner of many landmark cases in a court system known for “telephone justice,” in which party bosses dictated verdicts.

name: Conrad Bain
headline: Conrad Bain, Father on ‘Diff’rent Strokes’, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Bain was a stage and film actor best known for a late-career TV role as the white adoptive father of two poor black boys on the long-running comedy “Diff’rent Strokes.”

name: Pauline Phillips
profession: Flinty Adviser to Millions as Dear Abby
headline: Pauline Phillips, Flinty Adviser to Millions as Dear Abby, Dies at 94
abstract: With her comic, tart-tongued yet fundamentally sympathetic voice, Mrs. Phillips helped wrestle the advice column from its weepy Victorian past into a hard-nosed 20th-century present.

name: Robert Citron
headline: Robert Citron, Culprit in California Fraud, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Citron’s financial actions astounded bankers and bureaucrats, and put the county in bankruptcy in 1994, and himself in prison the following year.

name: Yang Baibing
headline: Gen. Yang Baibing Dies at 93; Led Tiananmen Crackdown
abstract: General Yang carried out the suppression of student-led protests in Tiananmen Square in 1989 and was later purged for accruing too much power.

name: Robert H. Levenson
headline: Robert H. Levenson, a Visionary Adman, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Levenson was an advertising executive who helped produce some of the mid-20th century’s most memorable campaigns for clients like Volkswagen, El Al and Sara Lee.

name: Prospero Gallinari
headline: Prospero Gallinari, a Terrorist, Is Dead at 62
abstract: Mr. Gallinari helped kidnap Prime Minister Aldo Moro of Italy, who was killed after 55 days in captivity.

name: Gussie Moran
headline: Gussie Moran, a Tennis Star Who Wore a Daring Wimbledon Outfit, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Moran, who made it as high as No. 4 in the United States rankings, showed up at Wimbledon in 1949 wearing an unconventional short skirt with lace-trimmed underwear.

name: Robert F. Chew
headline: Robert F. Chew, Actor on ‘The Wire,’ Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. Chew, an actor best known for his roles in HBO dramas like “The Corner” and “The Wire,” was a well-regarded stage actor when he began appearing in television shows.

name: Earl Weaver
headline: Earl Weaver, a Volatile, Visionary Manager, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Weaver was the Hall of Fame manager who brought pugnacity and pragmatism to the Baltimore Orioles dugout, tormenting a generation of umpires along the way.

name: Stan Musial
profession: Gentlemanly Slugger and Cardinals Stan the Man
headline: Stan Musial, Gentlemanly Slugger and Cardinals’ Stan the Man, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Musial, who played his entire career in St. Louis, won seven batting titles, hit 475 home runs, amassed 3,630 hits and was voted into the Hall of Fame in his first year of eligibility.

name: John Thomas
headline: John Thomas, Who Set Standard in High Jump, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Thomas, the first high jumper to clear 7 feet indoors, was perhaps best known for his cold war rivalry with Valery Brumel of the Soviet Union.

name: J. Richard Hackman
headline: J. Richard Hackman, an Expert in Team Dynamics, Dies at 72
abstract: Dr. Hackman, a professor of psychology, wrote or helped write 10 books on the dynamics of teamwork and effective leadership.

name: Andrée Putman
headline: Andrée Putman, Global Interior Designer, Dies at 87
abstract: The picture of a chic Parisian intellectual, Ms. Putman all but invented the boutique hotel genre when she designed Morgans in New York in 1984.

name: James A. Hood
headline: James A. Hood, Student Who Challenged Segregation, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Hood integrated the University of Alabama in 1963 together with his fellow student Vivian Malone after Gov. George C. Wallace capitulated to the federal government.

name: Burhan Dogancay
headline: Burhan Dogancay, Artist Inspired by Urban Walls, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Dogancay, a Turkish artist fascinated by art on city walls, was known for abstract paintings that have been exhibited at dozens of museums worldwide.

name: George Gund III
headline: George Gund III, Owner of Sports Teams, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Gund loved hockey, buying several teams, and he loved film, nurturing directors like Francis Ford Coppola and supporting film festivals around the world, including Sundance.

name: Antonio Frasconi
headline: Antonio Frasconi, Woodcut Master, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Frasconi used his woodcuts to comment on everything from the dictatorship in Uruguay, where he grew up, to the Kent State shootings of 1970.

name: Michael Winner
headline: Michael Winner, ‘Death Wish’ Director, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Winner, a British director who specialized in violent action movies, partnered with Charles Bronson for several films.

name: Taiho
headline: Taiho, Dominant Postwar Sumo Champ, Dies at 72
abstract: Taiho, widely considered the greatest sumo wrestler of postwar Japan, had a career record of 746-144-136.

name: Dolores Prida
headline: Dolores Prida, Columnist and Playwright, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Prida was a longtime writer for The Daily News and El Diario/La Prensa in New York.

name: Joseph Eger
headline: Joseph Eger, Horn Player and Activist, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Eger, a French horn player, was a conductor and advocate for progressive causes whose work sought to promote harmony in both senses of the word.

name: Linda Riss Pugach
headline: Linda Riss Pugach, Whose Life Was Ripped From Headlines, Dies at 75
abstract: Mrs. Pugach’s blinding by her lover, Burton N. Pugach, in 1959 became a news media sensation, and her later marriage to Mr. Pugach in 1974 became an equally sensational sequel.

name: Jozef Glemp
headline: Cardinal Jozef Glemp of Poland Is Dead at 83
abstract: Cardinal Glemp helped steer his nation through a historic and relatively peaceful transition from communism to democracy in 1989.

name: Corinne Jacker
profession: Playwright With Light Touch on Dark Subjects
headline: Corinne Jacker, Playwright With Light Touch on Dark Subjects, Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. Jacker’s earliest plays, “Bits & Pieces,” from 1974, and “Harry Outside,” from 1975, earned Obie Awards.

name: Larry Selman
headline: Larry Selman, Who Aided Others $1 at a Time, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Selman, who was said to have a low I.Q. but was an active fund-raiser for multiple causes, was the subject of the 2002 documentary “The Collector of Bedford Street.”

name: Richard G. Stern
headline: Richard G. Stern, Writers’ Writer, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Stern’s classroom at the University of Chicago became a showcase for visiting literary eminences like Philip Roth.

name: Dolours Price
headline: Dolours Price, Defiant I.R.A. Bomber, Dies at 61
abstract: Ms. Price accused the Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams of involvement in Irish Republican Army killings and bombings, charges he has always denied.

name: A. W. Clausen
headline: A. W. Clausen, a Bank of America Chief, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Clausen rose from a part-time position counting cash to become chief executive of Bank of America — twice — and president of the World Bank in between.

name: Sherman Cohen
headline: Sherman Cohen, Who Helped Build Real Estate Empire, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Cohen and his brothers first built apartment houses on Third Avenue and later office towers on Park and Third Avenues.

name: Donald Hornig
headline: Donald Hornig, Last to See First A-Bomb, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Hornig was a chemist on the Manhattan Project, science adviser to President Lyndon B. Johnson and a former president of Brown University.

name: Mary Jane Phillips-Matz
headline: Mary Jane Phillips-Matz, Verdi Biographer, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Phillips-Matz’s monumental “Verdi: A Biography,” the product of some 30 years’ research, was published in 1993 and spanned 941 pages.

name: Balthazar Korab
headline: Balthazar Korab, Architectural Photographer, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Korab was one of a handful of commercial photographers who introduced postwar architecture to Americans.

name: Stanley Karnow
headline: Stanley Karnow, Historian and Journalist, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Karnow’s books “Vietnam: A History” (1983) and “In Our Image: America’s Empire in the Philippines” (1989) were adapted into successful PBS documentary mini-series.

name: Nguyen Khanh
headline: Nguyen Khanh, General Who Led Coup, Dies at 86
abstract: General Khanh bloodlessly seized control of South Vietnam’s government in 1964, but his rule as premier lasted only a year as he was deposed by a junta of junior officers.

name: George Gruntz
headline: George Gruntz, Musician and Bandleader, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Gruntz wrote and arranged music specifically for the individual members of his band and gave them generous solo time, with music that reflected much of jazz history, from Ellington and Basie through Gil Evans and beyond.

name: Dave Purchase
headline: Dave Purchase Dies at 73; Led Early Needle Exchange
abstract: Mr. Purchase, a biker from Tacoma, Wash., began handing out sterile syringes on the streets to prevent AIDS among drug addicts 24 years ago.

name: Max Kampelman
headline: Max Kampelman, Who Led Arms Talks, Dies at 92
abstract: Democratic and Republican presidents enlisted Mr. Kampelman to negotiate cold war treaties with the Soviet Union.

name: Hiroshi Nakajima
headline: Hiroshi Nakajima, Leader of W.H.O., Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Nakajima enlarged the World Health Organization’s focus on preventive medicine and vaccinations for children, but was criticized for mismanagement.

name: Butch Morris
headline: Butch Morris Dies at 65; Creator of ‘Conduction’
abstract: Mr. Morris created a distinctive form of large-ensemble music built on collective improvisation. He referred to his method as “conduction,” short for “conducted improvisation.”

name: Jean-Léon Destiné
headline: Jean-Léon Destiné, Dancer, Dies at 94
abstract: Considered the father of Haitian professional dance, Mr. Destiné first came to international attention in the 1940s and remained prominent for decades afterward.

name: Geraldine Rhoads
headline: Geraldine Rhoads Dies at 98; Edited Woman’s Day
abstract: As editor in chief of Woman’s Day for 16 years, Miss Rhoads guided the magazine toward covering a wider variety of issues of concern to women.

name: Edward M. Kresky
headline: Edward M. Kresky, Who Calmed Fiscal Panic, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Kresky, an investment banker, was an architect of the debt refinancing plan that saved New York City from bankruptcy in the 1970s.

name: Patty Andrews
headline: Patty Andrews, Singer With Her Sisters, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Ms. Andrews was the last living member of the sister trio that gained fame with hit songs like “Boogie Woogie Bugle Boy (of Company B).”

name: Charlotte Smallwood-Cook
headline: Charlotte Smallwood-Cook, a Pioneering District Attorney, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Smallwood-Cook, who won her office in a landslide victory, had to defy Republican Party political bosses in Wyoming County, N.Y., to run in a 1949 primary.

name: Stefan Kudelski
headline: Stefan Kudelski, Polish Inventor of Recorder That Changed Hollywood, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Kudelski’s portable tape recorder changed how movies were made and expanded the reach of documentarians and eavesdroppers on both sides in the cold war.

name: Xu Liangying
headline: Xu Liangying, Scientist and Advocate, Dies at 92
abstract: In a life that spanned many of the convulsions of 20th-century China, Mr. Xu evolved from an ardent supporter of the Communist Party into an outspoken critic of the government.

name: Edward I. Koch
headline: Edward I. Koch, a Mayor as Brash, Shrewd and Colorful as the City He Led, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Koch, a showman of City Hall, was a three-term mayor who steered New York City through the fiscal austerity of the late 1970s and the racial conflicts of the 1980s.

name: Earl Williams
headline: Earl Williams, Baseball Slugger, Dies at 64
abstract: Williams won the National League’s rookie of the year award in 1971, but was out of major league baseball by the end of the decade.

name: Ferrol Sams
headline: Ferrol Sams, Doctor Turned Novelist, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Sams, a country doctor in Georgia, was in his 50s before he began a career as a novelist, drawing on his practice and rural upbringing for material.

name: Stephen Simon
headline: Stephen Simon, Conductor Who Led a Handel Revival, Dies at 75
abstract: The founder of the resident chamber orchestra of the Kennedy Center, Mr. Simon showed audiences that there was more to a composer than the “Messiah.”

name: Malcolm Douglas-Hamilton
headline: Lady Malcolm Douglas-Hamilton, American Who Aided Britain in War, Dies at 103
abstract: A Manhattan socialite, she started Bundles for Britain, which became an enormous World War II relief operation.

name: Diane Wolkstein
headline: Diane Wolkstein, Children’s Author Who Spurred a Storytelling Revival, Dies at 70
abstract: During her years a New York City’s lone full-time storyteller, Ms. Wolkstein set off a national wave of interest in the ancient art of the yarn.

name: André Cassagnes
headline: André Cassagnes, Etch A Sketch Inventor, Is Dead at 86
abstract: A chance inspiration involving metal particles and the tip of a pencil led Mr. Cassagnes to develop Etch A Sketch in the late 1950s.

name: Lavonne Paire Davis
headline: Lavonne Paire Davis, Baseball Pioneer, Dies at 88
abstract: Davis was a star in the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League of the 1940s and 1950s and a consultant for the hit movie “A League of Their Own.”

name: Arlene C. Ackerman
headline: Arlene C. Ackerman, Superintendent, Dies at 66
abstract: Dr. Ackerman improved students’ test scores, including those in the most severely underperforming schools, in each of the three cities in which she presided.

name: John D’Arcy
headline: Bishop John D’Arcy, Who Sounded Alarm on Sex Abuse, Dies at 80
abstract: Bishop D’Arcy was ignored by his superiors in the 1980s when he warned about priests who later figured in the sex-abuse scandal that rocked the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Boston.

name: Essie Mae Washington-Williams
profession: Child of Famous but Secret Father
headline: Essie Mae Washington-Williams, Child of Famous but Secret Father, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Washington-Williams lived for decades with a stunning secret — that she was the interracial daughter of Senator Strom Thurmond of South Carolina, who never publicly acknowledged her as his child.

name: Reg Presley
headline: Reg Presley, Lead Singer of Troggs, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Presley’s growl made the song “Wild Thing” a classic hit.

name: Walt Sweeney
headline: Walt Sweeney, All-Pro and Critic of N.F.L., Dies at 71
abstract: Sweeney, a star with the San Diego Chargers in the 1960s and ’70s, accused the team of handing out drugs to players and fostering his own addiction.

name: Guy F. Tozzoli
headline: Guy F. Tozzoli, 90, Who Led Team That Built Twin Towers, Is Dead
abstract: It seemed, one article said, as if Mr. Tozzoli had personally willed the trade center into existence, outfoxing enemies, bullying colleagues and maneuvering around problems.

name: Asbury H. Sallenger Jr.
headline: Asbury H. Sallenger Jr., Coastal Risks Expert, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Sallenger led research into the causes and effects of sea level rise, storms and other coastal hazards and was an adviser “in the post-Superstorm Sandy era.”

name: Cardiss Collins
profession: Fighter in Congress for Equality and the Poor
headline: Cardiss Collins, Fighter in Congress for Equality and the Poor, Dies at 81
abstract: Mrs. Collins, after succeeding her husband and becoming Illinois’s first black congresswoman, served from 1973 to 1997.

name: Stuart Freeborn
headline: Stuart Freeborn, ‘Star Wars’ Makeup Artist, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Freeborn created characters like Yoda and did extensive work on dozens of other films. George Lucas, the “Star Wars” director, called him “a makeup legend.”

name: Peter Hauri
headline: Peter Hauri, Psychologist Who Focused on Insomnia, Dies at 79
abstract: Dr. Hauri was one of the first researchers to study the mechanics of a good night’s sleep.

name: John E. Karlin
profession: Led the Way to All-Digit Dialing
headline: John E. Karlin, Who Led the Way to All-Digit Dialing, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Karlin, a Bell Labs industrial research psychologist, was also instrumental in the shortening of telephone cords and the creation of rectangular keypads for touch-tone models.

name: Paul Tanner
headline: Paul Tanner, Musician With ‘Good Vibrations,’ Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Tanner, a trombonist for Glenn Miller, played the electro-theremin for the Beach Boys and became a music educator at the University of California, Los Angeles.

name: John Kerr
headline: John Kerr, Star of ‘Tea and Sympathy,’ Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Kerr was a Tony Award winner known for roles in the 1950s that challenged bigotry.

name: John Kerr
headline: John Kerr, Chronicler of Freud-Jung Rift, Is Dead at 66
abstract: Mr. Kerr wrote a book about the theorists’ feud, which became the basis for a play and a movie, and edited books written by psychologists.

name: James Muri
profession: Bomber Pilot Honored for Valor in Battle of Midway
headline: James Muri, Bomber Pilot Honored for Valor in Battle of Midway, Is Dead at 94
abstract: The World War II pilot bombed a Japanese aircraft carrier in the Pacific and then survived by flying his B-26 bomber directly over the enemy ship’s deck.

name: Starr Saphir
headline: Starr Saphir, Bird-Watching Guide in Central Park, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Saphir was reknowned among birders, thousands of whom followed her through Central Park on the tours she led four times a week for nearly four decades.

name: James DePreist
headline: James DePreist, a Pioneering Conductor, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. DePreist, one of the few black conductors to achieve international renown, refused to let disability derail his career.

name: Richard Artschwager
headline: Richard Artschwager, Painter and Sculptor, Dies at 89
abstract: At a time when most artists worked in clearly determined styles, Mr. Artschwager slyly confounded the usual categories.

name: Ira Rubin
profession: Champion and the Beast of the Bridge Table
headline: Ira Rubin, Champion and the Beast of the Bridge Table, Dies at 82
