abstract: Mr. Rubin, an innovator in bidding theory who earned 20 national or world team titles, was nicknamed the Beast for the emotional intensity of his play.

name: David Hartman
headline: Rabbi David Hartman, Champion of an Adaptive Judaism, Dies at 81
abstract: A charismatic teacher and prolific author, he encouraged students to question tradition and urged people of different backgrounds and ideologies to pore over Jewish texts together.

name: Donald Byrd
headline: Donald Byrd, Jazz Trumpeter, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Byrd became successful and controversial in the 1970s by blending jazz, funk and R&B on the album “Black Byrd.”

name: Nevin S. Scrimshaw
headline: Nevin S. Scrimshaw, Pioneer Nutritionist, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Scrimshaw helped build organizations dedicated to nutrition and improved the health of children in developing nations by making affordable gruels.

name: Jake McNiece
headline: Jake McNiece, Who Led Incorrigible D-Day Unit, Is Dead at 93
abstract: The Filthy 13 were famed during World War II as model soldiers, except for maybe the obeying orders part.

name: Alan Sharp
headline: Alan Sharp, Writer of Dark Screenplays, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Sharp wrote scripts for films starring Gene Hackman, Liam Neeson and other Hollywood notables.

name: Ronald Dworkin
headline: Ronald Dworkin, Scholar of the Law, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Professor Dworkin, a public intellectual with liberal views who taught at New York University and University College, London, influenced many judges on a number of courts worldwide.

name: Rem Vyakhirev
headline: Rem Vyakhirev, Former Chief of Gazprom, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Vyakhirev, as chief executive of the huge Russian energy company during the 1990s, resisted efforts by reformers to break up and privatize it.

name: Bill Eadington
headline: Bill Eadington, Economist and Gambling Expert, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Eadington was one of the first academics to study gambling, as both a force for economic development and a challenging social problem.

name: Shadow Morton
headline: Shadow Morton, Songwriter and Producer, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Morton, with songs like “Remember (Walking in the Sand)” and “Leader of the Pack,” helped propel the Shangri-Las, a 1960s girl group from Queens, to stardom.

name: Edith Houghton
headline: Edith Houghton, Rare Woman Among Baseball Scouts, Dies at 100
abstract: A shortstop at 10, Ms. Houghton later became a pioneer with the Philadelphia Phillies.

name: Richard L. Murphy
headline: Richard L. Murphy, Who Aided Disadvantaged Youths, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Murphy helped tens of thousands in New York City through his community organization in Harlem and as the city’s youth commissioner.

name: Richard W. Murphy
profession: Roving Diplomat in World Hot Spots
headline: Richard W. Murphy, Roving Diplomat in World Hot Spots, Dies at 95
abstract: As a State Department Arabist, he served as ambassador to three Arab countries and helped broker the end of a 15-year civil war in Lebanon.

name: Keiko Fukuda
headline: Keiko Fukuda, a Trailblazer in Judo, Dies at 99
abstract: Ms. Fukuda learned judo from its founder and went on to become the sport’s highest-ranked woman.

name: Barnaby Conrad
profession: Man of Many Hats and a Cape
headline: Barnaby Conrad, Man of Many Hats and a Cape, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Conrad was also a painter, Sinclair Lewis’s personal secretary, and owner of the nightclub El Matador in San Francisco.

name: Tony Sheridan
headline: Tony Sheridan, Colleague of Beatles, Is Dead at 72
abstract: Mr. Sheridan was a guitarist and singer in Hamburg in 1960 when he met the Beatles, who were his backup group on recordings.

name: Jerry Buss
headline: Jerry Buss, Lakers Owner and Innovator, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Buss bought the Los Angeles Lakers in 1979 and won 10 N.B.A. titles while melding basketball and show business.

name: Steuart Pittman
headline: Steuart Pittman, Head of Fallout Shelter Program, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Pittman was appointed by President John F. Kennedy to create enough shelters to protect every American in the event of a nuclear attack.

name: W. Watts Biggers
headline: W. Watts Biggers, Creator of ‘Underdog’ Cartoon, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Biggers, an advertising account manager, also wrote the infectious “Underdog” theme song.

name: Mindy McCready
headline: Mindy McCready, a Singer Long Troubled, Dies at 37
abstract: Ms. McCready rose to stardom, only to find depression and battles with drugs and alcohol.

name: Donald Richie
headline: Donald Richie, 88, American Expert on Japan, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Richie is best known for introducing the English-speaking world to the golden age of Japanese cinema, including the director Akira Kurosawa.

name: Petro Vlahos
headline: Petro Vlahos, Special-Effects Innovator, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Vlahos developed the blue-screen and green-screen process that creates illusions in movies and other formats.

name: Debbie Ford
headline: Debbie Ford, Author of Self-Help Books, Is Dead at 57
abstract: Ms. Ford’s “Dark Side of the Light Chasers” was a best-seller that encouraged people to acknowledge their faults rather than pursue perfection.

name: Robert C. Richardson
headline: Robert C. Richardson, Laureate in Physics, Dies at 75
abstract: Dr. Richardson’s prize-winning work involved cooling helium to liquid form, a breakthrough that has enabled research into a variety of scientific problems.

name: Robert Richardson Jr.
headline: Robert Richardson Jr., Biographer of Literary Giants, Dies at 86
abstract: His books about Thoreau, Emerson and William James won him national awards — and a fan letter from the celebrated author who would become his wife.

name: Martin Zweig
headline: Martin Zweig, Who Forecast ’87 Market Crash, Dies at 70
abstract: The investor, author and analyst had a history of accurately predicting the stock market.

name: Otto Beisheim
headline: Otto Beisheim, German Retailing Pioneer, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Beisheim, who introduced the concept of selling wholesale goods directly to German consumers and built the country’s largest retailer, Metro, was known as intensely private.

name: Pat Derby
headline: Pat Derby, Champion of Animal Welfare, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Derby was among the first animal rights advocates to champion performing animals, especially exotic species like elephants, apes, monkeys, lions and tigers.

name: Kevin Ayers
headline: Kevin Ayers, a Psychedelic Rocker, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Ayers helped shape early psychedelia, influencing Jimi Hendrix and Pink Floyd.

name: Alan F. Westin
profession: Transformed Privacy Debate Before the Web Era
headline: Alan F. Westin, Who Transformed Privacy Debate Before the Web Era, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Westin was considered to have created, almost single-handedly, the modern field of privacy law.

name: Rex Scouten
headline: Rex Scouten, an Overseer of Presidential Households, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Scouten, a former Secret Service agent, served commanders in chief from Harry S. Truman to Bill Clinton.

name: Magic Slim
headline: Magic Slim, Blues Singer and Guitarist Who Blazed Onstage, Dies at 75
abstract: Magic Slim, who moved to Chicago from Mississippi, was known for his intense live performances.

name: Ozzie Sweet
profession: Helped Define New Era of Photography
headline: Ozzie Sweet, Who Helped Define New Era of Photography, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Sweet was a photographic illustrator known for his use of fierce hues that emulated the emergent Technicolor palate of American movies, and helped define — visually, anyway — an era.

name: Aleksei German
headline: Aleksei German, Director of Anti-Soviet Movies, Dies at 74
abstract: In movies like “Trial of the Road” and “My Friend Ivan Lapshin,” Mr. German captured the darkness of the Soviet era and especially Stalin’s rule.

name: Wolfgang Sawallisch
headline: Wolfgang Sawallisch, Conductor, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Sawallisch, a conductor steeped in German tradition, gained a new lease on life at the Philadelphia Orchestra.

name: Paul McIlhenny
headline: Paul McIlhenny, Head of a Tabasco Empire, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Ilhenny, the culinary instigator and chief executive of the McIlhenny Company, invited guests to lick fiery daubs of Tabasco sauce, earning them entry into the Not So Ancient Order of the Not So Silver Spoon.

name: Matt Mattox
headline: Matt Mattox, Jazz Dance Pioneer, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Mattox, known for his “catlike agility” in “Seven Brides for Seven Brothers,” was also a pioneer of the art of jazz dancing.

name: Michael J. Maye
headline: Michael J. Maye, Scrappy Leader of Firefighters’ Union, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Maye led the Uniformed Firefighters Association in the early 1970s, when fires in New York City increased by more than half and the number of firefighters decreased by a third.

name: Otfried Preussler
headline: Otfried Preussler, Children’s Book Author, Dies at 89
abstract: One of Mr. Preussler’s most famous creations was the thief Hotzenplotz and his nemesis, Dimpfelmoser the policeman.

name: C. Everett Koop
headline: C. Everett Koop, Forceful U.S. Surgeon General, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Koop was widely regarded as the most influential surgeon general in American history and played a crucial role in changing public attitudes about smoking.

name: John Merwin
headline: John Merwin, Angler With Story Angles, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Merwin lived to fish and chronicle it. An editor and writer for Field & Stream, he also founded Rod & Reel magazine and wrote a number of critically acclaimed books.

name: Denis Forman
headline: Denis Forman, British TV Innovator, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Mr. Forman was the executive responsible for hit series like “The Jewel in the Crown” and “Brideshead Revisited.”

name: Van Cliburn
headline: Van Cliburn, Cold War Musical Envoy, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Cliburn won the first-place award at the 1958 Tchaikovsky International Competition, a victory viewed as an American triumph over the Soviet Union at the height of the cold war.

name: Dale Robertson
headline: Dale Robertson, a Horse-Savvy Actor in Westerns, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Robertson appeared in more than 60 movies but was very likely known more for his television work in shows like “Tales of Wells Fargo” and “Iron Horse” and as a host of “Death Valley Days.”

name: Stéphane Hessel
headline: Stéphane Hessel, Author and Activist, Dies at 95
abstract: A hero of the French Resistance, Mr. Hessel marshaled the same defiant spirit more than 60 years later in a manifesto that inspired social protesters in Europe and the United States.

name: Bruce Reynolds
profession: Audacious Mastermind of Great Train Robbery
headline: Bruce Reynolds, Audacious Mastermind of Great Train Robbery, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Reynolds, who at the time of the theft was known to the police as a burglar well-connected in the London underworld, referred to the heist in a 1996 interview as “my Sistine Chapel.”

name: Jane C. Wright
headline: Jane C. Wright, Pioneering Oncologist, Dies at 93
abstract: As a black woman, Dr. Wright was an unusual presence in medical institutions, but she said she never felt she was a victim of racial prejudice.

name: Wojciech Inglot
headline: Wojciech Inglot, Polish Cosmetics Maker, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Inglot developed a “breathable” nail polish that found an unexpected market among Muslim women.

name: Bonnie Franklin
profession: Steadfast Mom on One Day at a Time
headline: Bonnie Franklin, Steadfast Mom on ‘One Day at a Time,’ Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Franklin, an accomplished stage and film actress, was best known for playing Ann Romano, a divorced mother of two daughters, on television.

name: Sylvia Smith
headline: Sylvia Smith, Memoirist of the Life Banal, Dies at 67
abstract: Ms. Smith was a British secretary whose memoir “Misadventures” was seen by some as an existential masterpiece of tedium.

name: Stanley Snadowsky
headline: Stanley Snadowsky, Nightclub Founder, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Snadowsky was a lawyer and music promoter who with his partner opened the Bottom Line nightclub in Greenwich Village that showcased Bruce Springsteen and Miles Davis  among others.

name: Mary Ellen Moore-Richard
headline: Mary Ellen Moore-Richard, American Indian Memoirist, Dies at 58
abstract: Ms. Moore-Richard was a member of the American Indian Movement during its militant actions of the 1970s and, under the name Mary Crow Dog, later wrote a well-received memoir, “Lakota Woman.”

name: Marie-Claire Alain
headline: Marie-Claire Alain, Master of the Organ, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Alain’s 300 recordings include, on organs of different periods, J. S. Bach’s complete organ works and collaborations with the trumpeter Maurice André.

name: Joseph Frank
headline: Joseph Frank, Biographer of Dostoevsky, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Frank’s five-volume biography of Fyodor Dostoevsky is considered one of the finest 20th-century literary biographies on any subject.

name: Thomas C. Griffin
headline: Maj. Thomas C. Griffin, Doolittle Raider, Dies at 96
abstract: Maj. Thomas C. Griffin navigated a B-25 bomber in the daring air raid on Japan led by Lt. Col. James H. Doolittle in 1942, four months after the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor.

name: Donald Glaser
headline: Donald Glaser, Nobel Winner in Physics, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Glaser, a scientist who later turned to microbiology and developing cancer therapies, invented a device called the bubble chamber to trace the paths of subatomic particles.

name: Bobby Rogers
headline: Bobby Rogers, Sang in the Miracles, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Rogers was born in the same hospital on the same day as Smokey Robinson, with whom he harmonized in high school and in the Hall of Fame singing group the Miracles.

name: John Wilpers
headline: John Wilpers Dies at 93; Captured Tojo
abstract: Mr. Wilpers was an Army intelligence officer in World War II who finally received military honors in 2010 for his role in capturing Hideki Tojo, the former Japanese prime minister.

name: Hugo Chávez
headline: A Polarizing Figure Who Led a Movement
abstract: Mr. Chávez led a nationalist movement that lashed out at the United States and wealthy Venezuelans, tapping into the resentments of his country’s poor.

name: Roy Brown Jr.
headline: Roy Brown Jr., Edsel Designer, Dies at 96
abstract: Though his ill-fated design became a synonym for bad ideas, Mr. Brown was proud of it and drove one into his 90s.

name: Allan Calhamer
headline: Allan Calhamer Dies at 81; Invented Diplomacy Game
abstract: The objective of Mr. Calhamer’s game, reportedly a favorite of Henry Kissinger, is simple: to achieve world domination in as many hours (or days, or even years) as it takes.

name: Alvin Lee
headline: Alvin Lee, British Blues-Rock Guitarist, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Lee and Ten Years After played at the Woodstock festival in 1969 and were in the movie “Woodstock” and on its soundtrack with “I’m Going Home.”

name: Stompin’ Tom Connors
headline: Stompin’ Tom Connors, Canadian Singer, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Connors sang often about his hardscrabble life and shunned American music as he built a wide following in his native country.

name: Lillian Cahn
headline: Lillian Cahn, Creator of the Coach Handbag, Dies at 89
abstract: Mrs. Cahn suggested the design for what became the first successful bag for Coach, the company she helped found: a tote modeled on a type of paper shopping bag she had used as a girl.

name: Joseph Kelner
headline: Joseph Kelner, 98, Dies; Led Kent State Lawsuit
abstract: Besides Kent State, other high-profile cases included those of Bernhard Goetz, the subway vigilante, and a pair of fired baseball umpires.

name: Menachem Froman
headline: Menachem Froman, Rabbi Seeking Peace, Dies at 68
abstract: Rabbi Froman’s grand, unrealized vision was that the enmity between Jewish settlers and their Palestinian neighbors could be erased by appeals to religious ideals.

name: Dirk Coetzee
headline: Dirk Coetzee, South African Official Who Led Apartheid-Era Killings, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Coetzee was a divisive figure who led killings of antiapartheid activists in South Africa and later detailed accounts of a corrupt police force.

name: Arthur Storch
headline: Arthur Storch, Stage Director, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Storch, an Actors Studio alumnus, directed on and off Broadway and created Syracuse Stage, a regional theater he brought to national prominence.

name: Mildred Manning
headline: Mildred Manning, ‘Angel’ of Corregidor, Dies at 98
abstract: Mrs. Manning was the last survivor of 77 nurses who served in the Philippines and were known as the Angels of Bataan and Corregidor.

name: Lilian Craig
headline: Lilian Craig, Beloved of Prince Who Could Be King, Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Craig and Sweden’s Prince Bertil were unable to marry for decades because she was a commoner. But when the rules changed, wed they did.

name: William Moody
headline: William Moody, 58, Pro Wrestling’s Paul Bearer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Moody gained fame as the urn-carrying manager Paul Bearer for the pro wrestlers the Undertaker and Kane in World Wrestling Entertainment.

name: Sybil Christopher
headline: Sybil Christopher, Nightclub Founder, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Christopher was a former actress, famous ex-wife and founder of Arthur, one of Manhattan’s most popular celebrity nightclubs in the 1960s.

name: Ewald-Heinrich von Kleist
headline: Ewald-Heinrich von Kleist, Anti-Hitler Plotter, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. von Kleist was believed to be the last surviving member of an elaborate German assassination plan led by Col. Claus von Stauffenberg in 1944.

name: John J. Byrne
headline: John J. Byrne Dies at 80; Turned Around Geico
abstract: Mr. Byrne became an insurance legend by rescuing Geico in the 1970s, and later took Fireman’s Fund public in what was then the biggest I.P.O. in history.

name: Merton D. Simpson
headline: Merton D. Simpson, Painter, Collector and Dealer in African Art, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Simpson’s voice was important in his field and he achieved his stature as a collector before integration.

name: Ieng Sary
headline: Ieng Sary, Former Official of Khmer Rouge, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Ieng Sary was part of an inner circle of communists who led the movement that caused the deaths of 1.7 million people in Cambodia from 1975 to 1979.

name: Jack Curran
headline: Jack Curran, a Mentor in Two Sports, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Curran coached generations of baseball and basketball players for 55 years at Archbishop Molloy High School in Queens, N.Y., winning more than 2,600 games.

name: Niculae Asciu
headline: Niculae Asciu, Illustrator With Wit, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Asciu’s work appeared for decades in publications like The New York Times and The New Yorker.

name: Peter Banks
headline: Peter Banks, Original Guitarist of Yes, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Banks played guitar and sang with Yes, Flash and a number of other British bands.

name: Cartha D. DeLoach
headline: Cartha D. DeLoach, No. 3 in the F.B.I., Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. DeLoach, who spent more than 25 years in the F.B.I., served as a powerful intermediary between J. Edgar Hoover and President Lyndon B. Johnson.

name: Rafael Puyana
headline: Rafael Puyana, Famed Harpsichordist, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Puyana was one of the last disciples of Wanda Landowska, the great 20th-century emissary of the harpsichord.

name: Ian M. Ross
headline: Ian M. Ross, a President at Bell Labs, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Ross was president of Bell Labs when its mission changed radically in 1984, after the breakup of its corporate parent, AT&T.

name: Walter Pierce
headline: Walter Pierce, Modernist Architect, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Pierce, who was born in Brooklyn, lived his last 55 years in a house he built in Peacock Farm, Mass., a 45-acre subdivision of stylish, affordable homes that he designed.

name: Richard D. Lyons
headline: Richard D. Lyons, Versatile Times Reporter, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Lyons covered science, Congress and the United Nations in nearly 30 years at The New York Times.

name: Richard Lyons
profession: Founder of the Subversive Band Negativland
headline: Richard Lyons, 57, a Founder of the Subversive Band Negativland, Dies
abstract: Since the late 1970s, Mr. Lyons’s subversive media-hacking band has functioned more like a collective with a fluctuating membership.

name: José Alfredo Martínez de Hoz
headline: José Alfredo Martínez de Hoz, Argentine Official During Dictatorship, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Martínez de Hoz, a former law professor, was in charge of Argentina’s economy from 1976 to 1981.

name: Erwin Harris
headline: Erwin Harris, Ad Executive Who Seized Cuban Assets, Dies at 91
abstract: Armed with a court order, Mr. Harris took planes, a Navy boat, cigars and a trainload of lard to cover an advertising contract the Castro government stopped paying.

name: Olen Burrage
headline: Olen Burrage Dies at 82; Linked to Killings in 1964
abstract: Mr. Burrage was a Ku Klux Klan member who owned the Mississippi farm where the bodies of three civil rights workers were found, and he was later acquitted in a federal trial.

name: Booth Gardner
headline: Booth Gardner Dies at 76; Ex-Washington Governor
abstract: Mr. Gardner served two terms and then led a campaign to allow physician-assisted suicide after becoming a Parkinson’s disease patient.

name: Francis Ruddle
headline: Francis Ruddle, Who Led Transgenic Research, Dies at 83
abstract: Dr. Ruddle, one of the first scientists to map genes’ locations on specific human chromosomes, helped lay the groundwork for the Human Genome Project.

name: Murrey Marder
headline: Murrey Marder, Early McCarthy Skeptic, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Marder may not have gotten a lot of the glory for helping bring down a Red-baiting Senator Joe McCarthy, but he deserves much of the credit, colleagues said.

name: Mariam Farhat
headline: Mariam Farhat, Known as ‘Mother of Martyrs,’ Dies at 64
abstract: Ms. Farhat, a Palestinian lawmaker also known as Umm Nidal, had three sons who died in attacks against Israel.

name: Harry Reems
headline: Harry Reems, Star of ‘Deep Throat’ Film, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Reems became America’s first bona fide male porn star by appearing in the 1972 movie “Deep Throat.”

name: Henry Bromell
headline: Henry Bromell, Writer of TV Dramas, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Bromell found rich sources of inspiration in the secretive past of his father, a C.I.A. agent.

name: Bobbie Smith
headline: Bobbie Smith, Voice of the Spinners, Dies at 76
abstract: The faces of the Spinners may have changed over the years, but Mr. Smith was there from the start.

name: Fran Warren
headline: Fran Warren, Singer in Big-Band Era, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Warren, best known for her hit “A Sunday Kind of Love,” sang professionally for more than half a century.

name: Paul Rose
profession: Quebec Separatist Involved in a Kidnapping and Murder
headline: Paul Rose, Quebec Separatist Involved in a Kidnapping and Murder, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Rose was a member of the FLQ extremist group that kidnapped Canadian political leaders and committed dozens of terrorist bombings. He was later convicted of murder.

name: Risë Stevens
profession: Stalwart at the Met for Decades in Carmen Role
headline: Risë Stevens, 99, Stalwart at the Met for Decades in Carmen Role, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Stevens, a mezzo-soprano, practically owned the role of Carmen during the 1940s and ’50, and gained popularity through her appearances on radio, television and in movies.

name: Maurice Barbash
headline: Maurice Barbash, Who Saved Fire Island’s Terrain, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Barbash maintained the character of the landscape in his designs and took on a nuclear power company and Robert Moses to block projects that would have altered Long Island’s environment.

name: Chinua Achebe
headline: Chinua Achebe, African Literary Titan, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Achebe, the celebrated author of “Things Fall Apart,” wrote stirring essays and poignant poems rooted in his native Nigeria’s cities and countryside.

name: Bud Palmer
headline: Bud Palmer, Jump Shot Pioneer, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Palmer gained fame as a sports telecaster, but his most consequential role was in helping to change basketball in a fundamental way by being the first to shoot a jump shot.

name: Boris A. Berezovsky
headline: Russian Oligarch and Critic of Putin Dies in Britain
abstract: Once a close ally of Boris N. Yeltsin who helped install Vladimir V. Putin as president, Boris A. Berezovsky later exiled himself to Britain after a bitter falling-out with the Kremlin.

name: Ruth Ann Steinhagen
headline: Ruth Ann Steinhagen Is Dead at 83; Shot a Ballplayer
abstract: Ms. Steinhagen’s 1949 shooting of the Phillies’ Eddie Waitkus made its way into the novel “The Natural” and its film adaptation.

name: Jacquelin Perry
headline: Dr. Jacquelin Perry, Surgeon Who Aided Polio Victims, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Perry earned attention for her work in analyzing the human gait, which she broke down into eight motion patterns governed by 28 major muscles in each leg.

name: Helen Kutsher
profession: Pampering Matriarch of a Grand Borscht Belt Resort
headline: Helen Kutsher, Pampering Matriarch of a Grand Borscht Belt Resort, Dies at 89
abstract: Mrs. Kutsher would circulate around the dining room, send food baskets up to rooms, and, until a few years ago, handle reservations to ensure that regulars got the lakeside views.

name: Joe Weider
headline: Joe Weider, Creator of Bodybuilding Empire, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Weider, who was a mentor to Arnold Schwarzenegger, created a world of muscle magazines, fitness equipment and dietary supplements, helping popularize the sport.

name: Bebo Valdés
profession: Force in World of Cuban Music
headline: Bebo Valdés, a Force in World of Cuban Music, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Valdés, a pianist, arranger and composer, was at the center of Havana’s musical life in the pre-Castro era.

name: Ray Williams
headline: Ray Williams Dies at 58; Itinerant in Pros and Life
abstract: Mr. Williams played 10 well-traveled seasons with the National Basketball Association, but he became homeless and declared bankruptcy after his career until landing a job in his hometown.

name: Malachi Throne
headline: Malachi Throne, Actor on TV, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Throne, of the ’60s television shows “It Takes a Thief” and “Batman,” was in both Gene Roddenberry’s original “Star Trek” and “Star Trek: The Next Generation.”

name: James Herbert
headline: James Herbert, British Horror Novelist, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Herbert wrote supernatural thrillers and horror stories, like “The Rats,” that made fans like Stephen King squirm.

name: Cal Whipple
profession: Won 1943 Fight to Print Photo of War
headline: Cal Whipple, 94, Dies; Won 1943 Fight to Print Photo of War Dead
abstract: When censors refused Life magazine permission to publish a photo showing the bodies of three American soldiers, Mr. Whipple got President Franklin D. Roosevelt to reverse the decision.

name: Eddie Bond
headline: Eddie Bond, Elvis Contemporary, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Bond was known, among other things, for telling a young Elvis Presley that he wouldn’t make it big as a singer.

name: Anthony Lewis
headline: Anthony Lewis, Supreme Court Reporter Who Brought Law to Life, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Lewis, a former reporter and columnist for The Times, won two Pulitzer Prizes and altered legal journalism with his authoritative and accessible prose.

name: Harlon Hill
headline: Harlon Hill, N.F.L. Star and Trophy Name, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Hill, a receiver, was a rookie of the year, an all-N.F.L. and Pro Bowl player, and a key contributor to a Chicago Bears team that reached the league’s championship game.

name: Edward Bland
profession: Cry of Jazz Filmmaker and Composer
headline: Edward Bland, ‘Cry of Jazz’ Filmmaker and Composer, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Bland’s documentary, released in 1959, explained jazz in the context of black history. He went on to work on commercial and avant-garde musical ventures.

name: Herschel Schacter
profession: Cried to the Jews of Buchenwald: You Are Free
headline: Rabbi Herschel Schacter Is Dead at 95; Cried to the Jews of Buchenwald: ‘You Are Free’
abstract: As an American Army chaplain, Rabbi Schacter entered the concentration camp an hour after its liberation in 1945 and told frightened inmates, “Peace be upon you, Jews, you are free!”

name: Jason Molina
headline: Jason Molina, a Balladeer of Heartbreak, Dies at 39
abstract: Mr. Molina, a singer and songwriter, led the alternative bands Songs: Ohia and Magnolia Electric Co.

name: Lori March
headline: Lori March, ‘Secret Storm’ Actress, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. March played a matriarch in the daytime television drama “The Secret Storm” and also worked on Broadway and in film.

name: Virgil Trucks
headline: Virgil Trucks, Who Threw 2 No-Hitters in 1952, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Trucks was a hard-throwing pitcher known as Fire, and he finished only 5-19 in his milestone season.

name: Deke Richards
headline: Deke Richards, Creator of Motown Hits, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Richards helped write and produce top-selling singles like “I Want You Back and “ABC” for the Jackson 5 and “Love Child” for Diana Ross and the Supremes.

name: Hjalmar Andersen
headline: Hjalmar Andersen, Norwegian Speedskater, Dies at 90
abstract: Hjalmar Andersen broke world records in the early 1950s and won three gold medals at the 1952 Winter Olympics in Oslo.

name: James M. Nabrit
headline: James M. Nabrit, a Fighter for Civil Rights, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Nabrit was a longtime lawyer for the NAACP Legal Defense and Education Fund who argued for school integration at the Supreme Court.

name: Bob Teague
headline: Bob Teague, WNBC Reporter Who Helped Integrate TV News, Is Dead at 84
abstract: When he joined WNBC-TV, there were few black reporters. But Mr. Teague was eventually disillusioned with TV newscasts.

name: Fay Kanin
headline: Fay Kanin, Writer for Film and Stage, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Kanin wrote comedies and dramas about relationships for film, stage and television as well as movies about death in the Vietnam War and prostitution.

name: Tom Boerwinkle
profession: Had Night to Remember as a Rebounder
headline: Tom Boerwinkle, Who Had Night to Remember as a Rebounder, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Boerwinkle, a stalwart center for the Chicago Bulls in the 1970s, set a franchise record with 37 rebounds.

name: Don Payne
headline: Don Payne, ‘Simpsons’ Scriptwriter, Dies at 48
abstract: Mr. Payne, who also wrote for film, shared four Emmys with other “Simpsons” staff members.

name: Richard Griffiths
headline: Richard Griffiths, Falstaffian English Actor, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Griffiths, who played Uncle Vernon in the Harry Potter movies, reached a career peak as a schoolteacher in “The History Boys” on Broadway and the West End.

name: Yvonne Brill
headline: Yvonne Brill, a Pioneering Rocket Scientist, Dies at 88
abstract: In the early 1970s, Mrs. Brill invented a propulsion system to help keep communications satellites from slipping out of their orbits.

name: Thomas McEvilley
profession: Critic and Defender of Non-Western Art
headline: Thomas McEvilley, Critic and Defender of Non-Western Art, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. McEvilley’s evisceration of a Museum of Modern Art show on “primitivism” in 1984 put curators on the defensive and changed the debate about multiculturalism in art.

name: Phil Ramone
headline: Phil Ramone, Producer for Music’s Biggest Stars, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Ramone defined the role of record producer as being roughly equivalent to that of a movie director.

name: Bob Turley
headline: Bob Turley, Pitcher With a Blazing Fastball, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Turley was a Cy Young-winning, right-handed pitcher who helped lift the Yankees to a come-from-behind victory over the Milwaukee Braves in the 1958 World Series.

name: Elwin Wilson
headline: Elwin Wilson, Who Apologized for Racist Acts, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Wilson was a former Ku Klux Klan supporter who made apologies late in life for acts he committed earlier — including the beating of a civil rights worker who became a member of Congress.

name: Lawrence McKiver
headline: Lawrence McKiver, a Singer in Long Tradition, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. McKiver helped found a Georgia group that practiced the traditional ring shout, a centuries-old black form of ecstatic worship.

name: Ralph Klein
headline: Ralph Klein, 70, Politician in Alberta Oil Boom, Dies
abstract: Mr. Klein presided as premier of oil-rich Alberta for 14 years as the industry’s profit poured in.

name: Jack Pardee
profession: Star at Texas A&M and an N.F.L. Coach
headline: Jack Pardee, a Star at Texas A&M and an N.F.L. Coach, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Pardee endured the brutal conditions of Bear Bryant’s “Junction Boys” training camp at Texas A&M and went on to become an All-Pro linebacker and N.F.L. coach.

name: John J. Gumperz
headline: John J. Gumperz, Linguist of Cultural Interchange, Dies at 91
abstract: Professor Gumperz created a subfield, known as interactional sociolinguistics, that studies exchanges in a range of social situations, especially discourse across cultures.

name: Chuck Fairbanks
headline: Chuck Fairbanks, a Fitful Football Coach, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Fairbanks built successful football teams in college at the University of Oklahoma and in the N.F.L. with New England. But controversy often followed him.

name: Ruth Prawer Jhabvala
headline: Ruth Prawer Jhabvala, Screenwriter, Dies at 85
abstract: Mrs. Jhabvala, a Booker Prize winner for her 1975 book, “Heat and Dust,” won Academy Awards as a screenwriter for “A Room With a View” and “Howards End.”

name: William H. Ginsburg
headline: William H. Ginsburg, Monica Lewinsky’s Lawyer, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Ginsburg’s career took a startling turn in 1998, when he went to Washington to represent Monica Lewinsky during the scandal over her relationship with President Bill Clinton.

name: Barbara Piasecka Johnson
headline: Barbara Piasecka Johnson, Maid Who Married Multimillionaire, Dies at 76
abstract: Three years after arriving from Poland with $200, Barbara Piasecka married an heir to the Band-Aid fortune.

name: Milo O’Shea
profession: Actor of the Stage and Screen
headline: Milo O’Shea, an Actor of the Stage and Screen, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. O’Shea was an Irish actor known for his roles in films like “Ulysses,” “Barbarella” and “The Verdict” and plays like “Staircase” and “Mass Appeal.”

name: Jane Henson
headline: Jane Henson, a Partner in Creating the Muppets, Dies at 78
abstract: Mrs. Henson, the former wife of Jim Henson, was influential in the creation of the popular television puppet program.

name: Hugh McCracken
headline: Hugh McCracken, a Studio Musician in High Demand, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. McCracken accompanied hundreds of musicians, including Paul Simon, Bob Dylan, Steely Dan and B. B. King, and he recorded with all four Beatles after their breakup.

name: Roger Ebert
headline: Roger Ebert Dies at 70; a Critic for the Common Man
abstract: Roger Ebert, the popular film critic and television co-host, could lift or sink the fortunes of a movie along with his partner, Gene Siskel.

name: Daniel Hoffman
profession: Poet Laureate Versatile in Many Forms
headline: Daniel Hoffman, Poet Laureate Versatile in Many Forms, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Hoffman was the nation’s poet laureate from 1973 to 1974, and his books include a collection of sonnets and an epic poem about the founding of Pennsylvania.

name: Carmine Infantino
headline: Carmine Infantino, Reviver of Batman and Flash, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Infantino, a creator of a spate of superheroes, rose from artist to editor to publisher of the comic-book titan DC Comics.

name: Robert Remini
headline: Robert Remini, Exhaustive Andrew Jackson Biographer, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Remini’s three-volume study of the seventh United States president depicted Jackson as imperfect but often heroic, a passionate defender of the common man.

name: J. David Kuo
headline: J. David Kuo, Who Split From Bush Faith Effort, Dies at 44
abstract: Mr. Kuo was instrumental in implementing President George W. Bush’s promise to link religious groups with the delivery of social services but later became a critic.

name: Ralph Sanchez
headline: Ralph Sanchez, Founder of Major Speedway, Dies at 64
abstract: A Cuban-born businessman, Mr. Sanchez built a major automobile racetrack in Homestead, Fla., after the city was ravaged by Hurricane Andrew.

name: Lawrence Fuchs
headline: Lawrence Fuchs, Expert on Immigration, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Fuchs, a scholar of American ethnicity, helped lay the groundwork for the last major overhaul of American immigration law, in 1986.

name: Edith Schaeffer
headline: Edith Schaeffer, Definer of Christian Family Values, Dies at 98
abstract: Mrs. Schaeffer wrote books describing women’s domestic role in an increasingly secular world, and with her husband, founded the Christian commune L’Abri.

name: Matthew Warren
headline: Matthew Warren, Son of Influential Minister, Dies at 27
abstract: The Rev. Rick Warren said in a statement that his youngest son, Matthew, who committed suicide, had struggled with mental illness and depression all his life.

name: Lilly Pulitzer
headline: Lilly Pulitzer Dies at 81; Heiress Who Gave Elite Clothes a Tropical Splash
abstract: Ms. Pulitzer, whose tropical print dresses became a fashion classic, got her start in 1959 by spilling orange juice on her clothes.

name: Les Blank
headline: Les Blank, Filmmaker of America’s Periphery, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Blank’s films are considered timeless, well-crafted essays on subjects like garlic and its devotees, Mardi Gras, gaptoothed women and polka enthusiasts.

name: Mariam Chamberlain
headline: Mariam Chamberlain, Women’s Champion, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Chamberlain played a pivotal yet little-known role in establishing women’s studies in the American college curriculum, and financing early research about the inequities women faced in the workplace.

name: Margaret Thatcher
headline: Margaret Thatcher, ‘Iron Lady’ Who Set Britain on New Course, Dies at 87
abstract: Mrs. Thatcher, who set her country on a rightward economic path, held her nation’s top office longer than any other British politician in the 20th century.

name: Annette Funicello
profession: Beloved as a Mouseketeer and a Star of Beach Movies
headline: Annette Funicello, 70, Dies; Beloved as a Mouseketeer and a Star of Beach Movies
abstract: Ms. Funicello won America’s heart on television in “The Mickey Mouse Club” and later captivated adolescent baby boomers in slightly spicy beach movies.

name: Harold M. Schmeck
headline: Harold M. Schmeck, 89, Times Science Writer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Schmeck covered medical research for The New York Times, where he worked for more than 30 years.

name: Peter Workman
profession: Book Publisher With an Eye for Hits
headline: Peter Workman, Book Publisher With an Eye for Hits, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Workman was known for working closely with authors and editors, and it was his knack for marketing that helped propel books like “What to Expect When You’re Expecting.”

name: Ed Fisher
headline: Ed Fisher, New Yorker Cartoonist, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Fisher created cartoons that managed to be erudite without being pretentious, requiring a general recognition of the world’s history and a healthy appreciation of irony.

name: McCandlish Phillips
headline: McCandlish Phillips, Who Exposed a Jewish Klansman, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Phillips, associated with The Times for more than 20 years, wrote a 1965 exposé of a man in Queens with an Orthodox Jewish background who was a senior Ku Klux Klan official.

name: Marty Blake
headline: Marty Blake, Sharp Judge of N.B.A. Talent, Dies at 86
abstract: In a basketball career that lasted nearly 60 years, Blake had a knack for finding talented players that nearly anyone else would have overlooked.

name: Bigas Luna
headline: Bigas Luna Dies at 67; Spanish Film’s Shepherd
abstract: Mr. Luna’s films featured outlandish situations and were influenced by surrealist artists; he helped discover stars including Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem.

name: Paolo Soleri
headline: Paolo Soleri, Architect of Counterculture, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Soleri was best known as the designer of Arcosanti, a settlement in Arizona.

name: Robert G. Edwards
profession: Changed Rules of Conception With First Test Tube Baby
headline: Robert G. Edwards Dies at 87; Changed Rules of Conception With First ‘Test Tube Baby’
abstract: Dr. Edwards, a physiologist working out of the University of Cambridge in England, changed the prospects for infertile couples and forged a brand-new industry.

name: Martyl Langsdorf
headline: Martyl Langsdorf, Doomsday Clock Designer, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Langsdorf drew the Doomsday Clock for the June 1947 cover of the Bulletin of Atomic Scientists as a way to evoke the potential devastation of nuclear weapons.

name: Stan Isaacs
headline: Stan Isaacs, Cheeky Columnist, Dies at 83
abstract: Isaacs was one of the Chipmunks, a group of young reporters, mainly in New York, who brought irreverence and daring to sports coverage beginning in the early 1960s.

name: Helena Carroll
headline: Helena Carroll, 84, Actress of Stage and Screen, Dies
abstract: Ms. Carroll, an Irish actress known for her stage, film and television appearances in the United States, was a founder of the Irish Players repertory company in New York.

name: Zao Wou-ki
headline: Zao Wou-ki, Abstract Painter, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Zao, a Chinese émigré in Paris who merged Eastern and Western aesthetic traditions, helped to shape avant-garde art in postwar Europe and became a commercially successful artist.

name: Franco Biondi Santi
headline: Franco Biondi Santi, Brunello Winemaker, Dies at 91
abstract: The popularity of Mr. Biondi Santi’s Tuscan red wine, which was invented by his grandfather in Italy, skyrocketed in the last half-century.

name: Jonathan Winters
profession: Unpredictable Comic and Master of Improvisation
headline: Jonathan Winters, Unpredictable Comic and Master of Improvisation, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Winters shone as a guest on TV talk shows and kept audiences in stitches with characters like Maude Frickert, a sweet-seeming grandmother with a barbed tongue.

name: Maria Tallchief
profession: Dazzling Ballerina and Muse for Balanchine
headline: Maria Tallchief, a Dazzling Ballerina and Muse for Balanchine, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Tallchief achieved renown as an early prima ballerina with the New York City Ballet, dancing for George Balanchine and entertaining audiences with her speed, energy and fire.

name: Patricia McCormick
headline: Patricia McCormick, Bullfighter Who Defied Convention, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Ms. McCormick, the first woman from North America to be a professional bullfighter, performed in hundreds of bullfights in the 1950s and received top billing in stadiums worldwide.

name: Mickey Rose
profession: TV Writer and Woody Allen Collaborator
headline: Mickey Rose, TV Writer and Woody Allen Collaborator, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Rose worked with Mr. Allen on “Take the Money and Run” and “Bananas,” and wrote jokes for Sid Caesar, Johnny Carson and the Smothers Brothers.

name: Robert Byrne
headline: Robert Byrne, Chess Grandmaster, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Byrne analyzed top-flight matches and wrote a chess column for The New York Times from 1972 to 2006.

name: Daniel Reich
headline: Daniel Reich, 39, Resourceful Art Dealer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Reich put on exhibitions of emerging artists in his tiny studio apartment in Chelsea before moving to a commercial space.

name: Carmen Weinstein
headline: Carmen Weinstein, Who Led the Jews of Cairo, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Weinstein was the driving force behind the restoration of Maimonides’s yeshiva and other monuments of Egyptian Jewish history.

name: David Burge
headline: David Burge, Pianist, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. Burge was an American pianist and composer known as an indefatigable champion of 20th-century music.

name: Besedka Johnson
headline: Besedka Johnson, Late-Blooming Actress, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Johnson, who starred in the critically acclaimed “Starlet,” was discovered when she was 85.

name: Colin Davis
profession: British Conductor Known for His Exuberant Approach
headline: Colin Davis, a British Conductor Known for His Exuberant Approach, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Davis, the longest-serving principal conductor of the London Symphony Orchestra, brought enthusiasm and authority to his music-making.

name: Nathan Azrin
profession: Changed the Field of Behavioral Psychology
headline: Nathan Azrin Dies at 82; Changed the Field of Behavioral Psychology
abstract: Dr. Azrin, an author of “The Token Economy,” a foundational text, helped alter the way psychologists approached behavior-modifying techniques.

name: Bob Perry
profession: Big Backer of Swift Boat Ads
headline: Bob Perry, Big Backer of ‘Swift Boat’ Ads, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Perry gave $4.4 million to a group for its attack ads accusing John Kerry, the 2004 Democratic presidential nominee, of overstating his military accomplishments.

name: Carl Williams
headline: Carl Williams, Champ Who Ducked No One, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Williams, who was 6-foot-4 and nicknamed the Truth, was known for a rock-solid jab and for taking on the best fighters of his era.

name: Frank Bank
profession: Lumpy on Leave It to Beaver
headline: Frank Bank, Lumpy on ‘Leave It to Beaver,’ Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Bank’s character on the 1950s-’60s hit television series was the closest thing the show had to a bad guy, but even he was lovable.

name: Pat Summerall
profession: Star Kicker With Giants and a Calm Voice on TV
headline: Pat Summerall, Star Kicker With Giants and a Calm Voice on TV, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Summerall was a place-kicker who later went on to a career in broadcasting, forming a famous team with John Madden.

name: Dorothy Taubman
headline: Dorothy Taubman, Therapist for Pianists, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Taubman’s methods, known as the Taubman Technique, aided notable pianists who suffered injuries and whose careers were severely curtailed.

name: George Beverly Shea
profession: Stirring Singer at Billy Graham Revivals
headline: George Beverly Shea Dies at 104; Stirring Singer at Billy Graham Revivals
abstract: Mr. Shea, a Grammy Award-winning gospel singer, performed live for an estimated 200 million people on Billy Graham’s evangelistic crusades.

name: Gerald W. Lynch
profession: Fought to Save John Jay College
headline: Gerald W. Lynch, Who Fought to Save John Jay College, Dies at 76
abstract: After New York City proposed closing or merging several colleges in the CUNY system in 1975, Dr. Lynch supported student protests and found savings in the budget.

name: Pedro Ramírez Vázquez
headline: Pedro Ramírez Vázquez, Architect, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Mr. Ramírez designed a series of monuments to Mexican culture, including museums, a sports stadium and the Basilica of Guadalupe shrine.

name: Henry A. Prunier
headline: Henry A. Prunier, 91, U.S. Soldier Who Trained Vietnamese Troops, Dies
abstract: Mr. Prunier, originally recruited by the Army as a translator, was part of a clandestine mission to teach 200 Viet Minh guerrillas how to use American weapons.

name: Dean Drummond
headline: Dean Drummond, Musician and Instrument Maker, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Drummond, a protégé of Harry Partch’s, shared Mr. Partch’s affinity for microtonality and creating outlandish instruments.

name: Pentti Lund
profession: First Finn to Star in the N.H.L
headline: Pentti Lund, First Finn to Star in the N.H.L., Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Lund, a native of Finland, played in the N.H.L. long before the league began to attract the best ice hockey players in the world.

name: Dwike Mitchell
headline: Dwike Mitchell, Zealous Jazz Pianist, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Mitchell and his playing partner, Willie Ruff, played thousands of concerts at schools and colleges and in foreign countries where jazz was taboo.

name: Jimmy Dawkins
headline: Jimmy Dawkins, Chicago Blues Guitarist, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Dawkins, who did most of his touring in Europe and Japan, counted Buddy Guy and Eric Clapton among his fans.

name: Al Neuharth
headline: Al Neuharth, News Executive Who Built Gannett and USA Today, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Neuharth’s business model, characterized by stripped-down costs and generous margins, reshaped the industry, tilting the balance between profits and public service.

name: Andy Johns
profession: Rolling Stones and Led Zeppelin Engineer
headline: Andy Johns, 62, Rolling Stones and Led Zeppelin Engineer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Johns helped piece together one of the Stones’ most acclaimed albums, “Exile on Main St.” and was a producer of Television’s “Marquee Moon.”

name: Storm Thorgerson
headline: Storm Thorgerson, Album Designer, Dies at 69
abstract: In addition to that of “The Dark Side of the Moon,” Mr. Thorgerson also produced semi-surreal designs for recordings by Led Zeppelin, Genesis, the Cranberries and Phish.

name: Hilary Koprowski
headline: Hilary Koprowski, Who Developed First Live-Virus Polio Vaccine, Dies at 96
abstract: A pioneering researcher who also helped develop a vaccine for rabies, Dr. Koprowski never won much recognition for his polio breakthrough, since it was not widely used in the United States.

name: Anna Merz
headline: Anna Merz, Rhino Guardian and Champion, Dies at 81
abstract: Mrs. Merz founded a wildlife reserve in Kenya that has helped the black rhinoceros come back from the brink of extinction.

name: Alfredo Guevara Valdés
profession: Steward of Cuban Cinema and Castro Ally
headline: Alfredo Guevara Valdés, 87, Steward of Cuban Cinema and Castro Ally, Dies
abstract: Mr. Guevara was a Marxist intellectual and ally of Fidel Castro’s who presided over Cuba’s powerful state-financed film industry for much of the Castro era.

name: Robert Earl Holding
headline: Robert Earl Holding, Wide-Ranging Entrepreneur, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Holding’s far-flung assets, including oil refineries, cattle, hotels and ski slopes, made him a billionaire.

name: Richie Havens
headline: Richie Havens, Folk Singer Who Riveted Woodstock, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Havens marshaled a craggy voice and a percussive guitar to play his way into immortality at Woodstock in 1969, improvising “Freedom” on the fly.

name: E. L. Konigsburg
headline: E. L. Konigsburg, Author, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Ms. Konigsburg twice received the nation’s highest award in children’s literature, the American Library Association’s John Newbery Medal.

name: Allan Arbus
headline: Allan Arbus, Psychiatrist With Zingers on ‘M*A*S*H,’ Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Arbus played Maj. Sidney Freedman on the popular TV series. He worked with his first wife, Diane Arbus, as a photographer before taking up acting.

name: Edward de Grazia
headline: Edward de Grazia, Lawyer Who Fought Censorship of Books, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Grazia, who taught at the Benjamin N. Cardozo School of Law at Yeshiva University in New York, defined his life’s work as defending “morally defiant artists” against “reactionary politicians and judges.”

name: Shakuntala Devi
headline: Shakuntala Devi, ‘Human Computer’ Who Bested the Machines, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Devi’s lightning calculations amazed audiences and supported her family, even when she was a child.

name: Howard J. Phillips
headline: Howard J. Phillips, Stalwart Conservative, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Phillips could be a thorn in the side even of fellow Republicans for his devotion to ideological principles such as limited government and traditional family values.

name: Bob Edgar
headline: Bob Edgar, Lawmaker and Liberal Leader, Dies at 69
abstract: A six-term Pennsylvania congressman, Mr. Edgar was also a general secretary of the National Council of Churches and the president of the lobbying group Common Cause.

name: François Jacob
headline: François Jacob, Geneticist Who Pointed to How Traits Are Inherited, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Jacob was a French war hero whose combat wounds forced him to change his career paths from surgeon to scientist, a pursuit that led to a Nobel Prize in 1965.

name: Cordell Mosson
headline: Cordell Mosson, Funk Guitarist, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Mosson played bass, drums and rhythm guitar in George Clinton’s group, Parliament-Funkadelic, for more than 40 years.

name: George Jones
headline: His Life Was a Country Song
abstract: George Jones’s baritone singing, universally respected, found vulnerability and doubt behind the cheerful drive of honky-tonk.

name: Kathryn Davis
headline: Kathryn Davis, Donor Who Made the Hudson Her Cause, Dies at 106
abstract: After taking up kayaking in her 90s near her home in Tarrytown, N.Y., Ms. Davis donated millions to clean up the Hudson.

name: Leo Branton Jr.
headline: Leo Branton Jr., Activists’ Lawyer, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Branton successfully defended the activist and academic Angela Davis in 1972, and also argued cases on behalf of the Black Panthers and the Communist Party.

name: Shamshad Begum
headline: Shamshad Begum, Unseen Singer of Indian Film, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Begum was one of the first female playback singers in Hindi cinema — she was heard but not seen on screen, as other actresses lip-synced her work.

name: Mary Thom
headline: Mary Thom, an Editor Who Shaped Feminist Voices, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. Thom, who was renowned for her sharp pen, was a former executive editor at Ms. magazine.

name: Kenneth I. Appel
headline: Kenneth I. Appel, Mathematician Who Harnessed Computer Power, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Appel and a colleague solved a century-old problem concerning colors on a map with the help of an I.B.M. computer making billions of decisions.

name: Adolph Herseth
headline: Adolph Herseth, 91, Trumpeter With Chicago Symphony, Dies
abstract: Mr. Herseth was the principal trumpeter of the symphony for 53 years and one of the most accomplished and influential orchestral trumpeters of his time.

name: Donald Shirley
headline: Donald Shirley, a Pianist With His Own Genre, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Shirley, who was discouraged from pursuing a career in classical music because he was black, gathered many types of music under one umbrella.

name: Janos Starker
headline: Janos Starker, Master of the Cello, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Starker was widely known through his more than 150 recordings, including one of Bach’s six suites for solo cello for which he won a Grammy Award in 1998.

name: Tim Taylor
headline: Tim Taylor, Yale and ’94 Olympic Coach, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Taylor became Yale’s winningest hockey coach and the leader of four national teams in the world championships and one in the Lillehammer Olympics.

name: Deanna Durbin
profession: Plucky Movie Star of the Depression Era
headline: Deanna Durbin, Plucky Movie Star of the Depression Era, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Ms. Durbin was a teenage actress whose radiant voice and wholesome personality brought box-office gold to Universal Pictures before she vanished from Hollywood.

name: Bob Brozman
headline: Bob Brozman, Guitarist, Is Dead at 59
abstract: Mr. Brozman was a self-described “roving guitar anthropologist” who collaborated with musicians from Northern Ireland to Papua New Guinea.

name: Orville Slutzky
headline: Orville Slutzky, a Founder of a Ski Resort, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Slutzky and his brother founded the Hunter Mountain ski resort in upstate New York, which was known for its celebrity clientele and snow-making cannons.

name: Chris Kelly
headline: Chris Kelly, of Hip-Hop Duo Kris Kross, Dies at 34
abstract: Mr. Kelly was barely in his teens when he became a star who helped bridge hip-hop to pop.

name: Henry Hope Reed
headline: Henry Hope Reed, Architectural Historian, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Mr. Reed, a writer and critic, was known for being a fierce opponent of modern architecture.

name: Jeff Hanneman
headline: Jeff Hanneman, Guitarist, Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. Hanneman, who was a founder of the band Slayer while still in his teens, helped to create some of the darkest music and imagery in metal.

name: Mike Gray
headline: Mike Gray, ‘China Syndrome’ Writer, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Gray dealt with contemporary issues in his work, including race relations and American drug policy.

name: Tom Knapp
headline: Tom Knapp, Crowd-Pleasing Sure Shot, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Knapp broke world records by picking off flocks of airborne clay targets with the flair of a western movie hero.

name: John Williamson
headline: John Williamson, Co-Founder of the Sandstone Retreat, Dies at 80
abstract: Sandstone, which Mr. Williamson and his wife always insisted was about more than sex, at one point had a handful of couples who were full-time residents and about 500 paying members.

name: John Williamson
headline: John Williamson, 83, Dies; Economist Defined the ‘Washington Consensus’
abstract: A careful pragmatist, he regretted the way his term, aimed at developing countries, was misinterpreted by free-market ideologues and anti-globalization activists.

name: Emil Frei III
headline: Emil Frei III, Who Put Cancer Cures in Reach, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Frei was an oncologist whose trailblazing use of combination chemotherapy helped make certain cancers curable for the first time.

name: Frederic Franklin
headline: Frederic Franklin, Inventive and Charismatic Ballet Star, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Mr. Franklin, a British-born dancer and ballet master who performed into his 90s, was known for his stylistic versatility and inexhaustible energy.

name: Eleanor R. Adair
headline: Eleanor R. Adair, Microwave Proponent, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Adair became an increasingly prominent and firm voice of assurance that microwave radiation posed no health risk.

name: Giulio Andreotti
headline: Giulio Andreotti, Premier of Italy 7 Times, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Andreotti, who epitomized postwar Italy’s contradictions, helped usher the country into wealth but also played a part in the spread of cronyism.

name: Christian de Duve
headline: Christian de Duve, 95, Dies; Nobel-Winning Biochemist
abstract: Dr. de Duve, a Belgian biochemist whose discoveries shed light on genetic disorders like Tay-Sachs disease, shared the 1974 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with two others.

name: Otis R. Bowen
headline: Otis R. Bowen, Governor and Health Secretary, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Bowen, who worked as a family practitioner before becoming Indiana’s governor, was secretary of health and human services during the Reagan administration’s second term.

name: Ray Harryhausen
headline: Ray Harryhausen, Whose Creatures Battled Jason and Sinbad, Dies at 92
abstract: From sword fights to swooping pterodactyls, Mr. Harryhausen created and photographed many of the most memorable fantasy-adventure sequences in movie history.

name: Herbert Blau
headline: Herbert Blau, Pioneering Theater Director, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Blau, a champion of the new and avant-garde, was a founder of the seminal Actor’s Workshop in San Francisco.

name: Brad Drewett
headline: Brad Drewett, President of Men’s Tennis Tour, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Drewett was a former professional tennis player who became president of the ATP last year and won a greater share of Grand Slam tournament revenue for players.

name: Jeanne Cooper
headline: Jeanne Cooper, ‘Young and the Restless’ Star, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Cooper played the fabulously wealthy matriarch Katherine Chancellor for four decades and was the longest-serving cast member of the television soap opera.

name: Bryan Forbes
headline: Bryan Forbes, ‘Stepford Wives’ Director, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Forbes had a string of screenwriting credits and was also an actor and an author, but he was best remembered for the film that endures as an artifact of high camp and even as a quasi-feminist document.

name: Ottavio Missoni
profession: Made Zigzags a Symbol of High Fashion
headline: Ottavio Missoni, Who Made Zigzags a Symbol of High Fashion, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Missoni’s easily recognizable multicolored knits became an insider status symbol for the ultra-wealthy.

name: Merrill Brockway
profession: Producer of TVs Dance in America
headline: Merrill Brockway, Producer of TV’s ‘Dance in America,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Brockway, who was also a director, brought high art to millions of Americans though the PBS series.

name: Fredrick L. McKissack
headline: Fredrick L. McKissack, 73, Children’s Book Author, Dies
abstract: Mr. McKissack, with his wife, Patricia, wrote over 100 children’s books about African-American history.

name: Taylor Mead
headline: Taylor Mead, Bohemian and Actor, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Mead collaborated with Andy Warhol in the 1960s to make several curious films.

name: Joel A. Miele Sr.
headline: Joel A. Miele Sr., 78, Giuliani Appointee, Dies
abstract: Mr. Miele, an engineer, presided over an agency that in the 1990s undertook major initiatives to safeguard New York City’s water supply.

name: George Sauer
headline: George Sauer, Jets Receiver and Rebel, Is Dead at 69
abstract: Mr. Sauer, who was a wide receiver for the Jets, played a pivotal role in the team’s Super Bowl III win, but he grew to hate the life of a pro football player and retired at 27.

name: Alan Abelson
profession: at Barrons Was a Thorn in Wall Streets Side
headline: Alan Abelson, Who at Barron’s Was a Thorn in Wall Street’s Side, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Abelson was an editor and a columnist at Barron’s magazine who delivered sharp and influential commentary on the stock markets.

name: Al Fritz
headline: Al Fritz, Who Put Youngsters on Stylish, Colorful Bikes, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Fritz designed a rugged, compact bicycle, recognizable by its banana seat and high handlebars, which Schwinn sold in the millions.

name: Dean Jeffries
headline: Dean Jeffries, Car Customizer and Painter, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Jeffries was a virtual one-stop shop in the world of custom cars, and created the Monkeemobile and the “Bikini Beach” Mantaray.

name: Jacqueline Brookes
headline: Jacqueline Brookes, Actress and Teacher, Dies at 82
abstract: In a 60-year career, Ms. Brookes appeared in films and on television but drew her widest notice for performances in stage productions of Shakespeare, Pirandello and Edward Albee.

name: Jack Butler
headline: Jack Butler, an Undrafted Football Hall of Famer, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Butler, who in nine seasons with the Steelers intercepted 52 passes, was a first-team all-N.F.L. player three times and was elected to the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2012.

name: Joyce Brothers
headline: Dr. Joyce Brothers, On-Air Psychologist Who Made TV House Calls, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Brothers arrived at the exact historical moment when cold war anxiety, a greater acceptance of talk therapy and the widespread ownership of television sets converged.

name: Kenneth Battelle
headline: Kenneth Battelle, 86, Hairdresser to the Stars, Dies
abstract: Mr. Battelle, often called the first celebrity hairdresser, defined the styles of famous names like Audrey Hepburn, Marilyn Monroe and Jacqueline Kennedy.

name: Billie Sol Estes
headline: Billie Sol Estes, Texas Con Man Whose Fall Shook Up Washington, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Estes’s life captured America’s imagination, with its tales of business scams, political payoffs, covered-up killings and White House conspiracies.

name: Bob Sickinger
headline: Bob Sickinger, Chicago Stage Innovator, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Sickinger believed that theater wasn’t presented to a community but arose from it, and that was the model he followed in Chicago.

name: Chuck Muncie
headline: Chuck Muncie, Troubled N.F.L. Star, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Muncie blended speed and power to become one of the N.F.L.’s leading running backs of the late 1970s and early ’80s, but his career was cut short by drug abuse.

name: Robert Lindgren
headline: Robert Lindgren, 89, Ballet Dancer and College Dean, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Lindgren appeared with major American ballet companies before becoming the founding dean of the influential dance program at the North Carolina School of the Arts.

name: John LaMontaine
headline: John LaMontaine, Pulitzer-Winning Composer, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. LaMontaine, who won the Pulitzer Prize in 1959 and composed music for the Kennedy inauguration, had taken and passed a stockbrokers’ exam to support his career.

name: Thomas M. Messer
headline: Thomas M. Messer, Museum Director Who Gave Guggenheim Cachet, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Messer’s charm and diplomacy attracted donations of major collections and his leadership helped established the Guggenheim among the world’s great museums of modern art.

name: Geza Vermes
headline: Geza Vermes, Scholar of ‘Historical Jesus,’ Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Vermes, one of the scrolls’ essential translators, wrote several books that placed Jesus in the tradition of Jewish teachers.

name: Jorge Rafael Videla
headline: Jorge Rafael Videla, Jailed Argentine Military Leader, Dies at 87
abstract: General Videla was serving a life sentence for abuses in a campaign of political killings and forced disappearances during Argentina’s so-called Dirty War.

name: Albert Seedman
profession: Chief of Detectives in New York for Short
headline: Albert Seedman, Chief of Detectives in New York for Short, Tumultuous Time, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Seedman was the New York Police Department’s chief of detectives for only 13 months, but he helped modernize and restructure the way detectives and patrol officers did their jobs.

name: Kennett Love
headline: Kennett Love, Times Correspondent in 1950s, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Love was in Iran in 1953 when the C.I.A. plotted against the government, and he also reported on the Suez Canal crisis of 1956.

name: Ken Venturi
profession: U.S. Open Golf Champion and Broadcaster
headline: Ken Venturi, U.S. Open Golf Champion and Broadcaster, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Venturi won the 1964 United States Open, nearly collapsing from heat exhaustion. He later became a chief golf analyst for CBS Sports, where he worked for 35 years.

name: Kenneth Waltz
headline: Kenneth Waltz, Foreign-Relations Expert, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Waltz, who was a senior research scholar at Columbia, was a pre-eminent thinker who was known for his contrarian, debate-provoking ideas.

name: Christine White
profession: Actress in a Classic Twilight Zone
headline: Christine White, Actress in a Classic ‘Twilight Zone,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. White was seen in television roles from the 1950s through the mid-1970s, but was best remembered playing William Shatner’s loyal wife in “Nightmare at 20,000 Feet.”

name: Joseph Farman
headline: Joseph Farman, 82, Is Dead; Discovered Ozone Hole
abstract: Mr. Farman’s single-minded and at times officially derided study of atmospheric changes in the Antarctic led to one of the most important environmental discoveries of the 20th century.

name: William Miles
profession: Maker of Films About Black History
headline: William Miles, Maker of Films About Black History, Dies at 82
abstract: Among other topics, Mr. Miles, who specialized in unearthing lost material about forgotten subjects, made films about the history of Harlem and a black regiment that fought in World War I.

name: William M. Fine
headline: William M. Fine, Who Helped Shape Drug Laws, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Fine, a former magazine publisher and retailer, did research for Gov. Nelson A. Rockefeller that led to New York State’s stringent narcotics legislation.

name: J. Hyde Crawford
headline: J. Hyde Crawford, Fashion Illustrator, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Crawford redesigned the bouquet of violets that was Bonwit Teller’s symbol, and the ubiquitous logo became his signature.

name: Boruch Spiegel
headline: Boruch Spiegel, Fighter in Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Spiegel was one of the last surviving fighters of the 1943 uprising, in which 750 Jews held off German soldiers for over a month with crude arms and Molotov cocktails.

name: Barbara Brenner
headline: Barbara Brenner, Breast Cancer Iconoclast, Dies at 61
abstract: Ms. Brenner, who led Breast Cancer Action for 15 years, took on the medical establishment and industrial companies as she crusaded for research on the disease.

name: Lothar Schmid
profession: Chess Referee of the Match of the Century
headline: Lothar Schmid, Chess Referee of the ‘Match of the Century,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Schmid was a German grandmaster who negotiated a truce between Bobby Fischer and Boris Spassky that saved their 1972 world-championship match.

name: Ray Manzarek
profession: Keyboardist and a Founder of the Doors
headline: Ray Manzarek, 74, Keyboardist and a Founder of the Doors, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Manzarek played a key role in creating the group’s psychedelic sound, which could be haunted, meditative and circuslike, but which was also widely imitated.

name: Bernard Waber
headline: Bernard Waber, Children’s Author, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Waber’s most enduring creation was Lyle, a clever crocodile who lived on the Upper East Side.

name: Heinrich Rohrer
headline: Heinrich Rohrer, Physicist, Dies at 79; Helped Open Door to Nanotechnology
abstract: Dr. Rohrer helped invent the scanning tunneling microscope, which made it possible to see individual atoms and move them around.

name: Aleksei Balabanov
headline: Aleksei Balabanov, 54, Russian Film Director, Dies
abstract: Mr. Balabanov’s movies offered up hit men, corrupt government officials and plenty of corpses.

name: Harold Shapero
headline: Harold Shapero, American Neo-Classical Composer, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Shapero was a composer and a central figure of American Neo-Classicism, a school of composition that thrived in the 1940s and ’50s.

name: Mary Ward Brown
headline: Mary Ward Brown, Award-Winning Short Story Writer, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Brown resumed a literary career 25 years after putting it aside to run the family farm, producing award-winning short stories set in the Deep South.

name: Henri Dutilleux
headline: Henri Dutilleux, Modernist Composer, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Dutilleux, between Olivier Messiaen and Pierre Boulez in age, was little affected by either.

name: Vernon McGarity
headline: Vernon McGarity, Dies at 91, War Hero; Fought in the Battle of the Bulge
abstract: Mr. McGarity, who received the Medal of Honor, was a technical sergeant in the 99th Infantry Division in December 1944 when Hitler mounted his last offensive of the war.

name: Leonard Marsh
headline: Leonard Marsh, a Founder of Snapple, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Marsh was a longtime chief executive of the beverage company, now part of the Dr Pepper Snapple Group.

name: Bonnie Faubus Salcido
headline: Bonnie Faubus Salcido, Who Opposed Segregationist Brother, Dies at 93
abstract: Mrs. Salcido criticized her brother Gov. Orval E. Faubus’s attempt to block the integration of an Arkansas school in 1957, leading to years of hard feelings between the two.

name: Steve Forrest
profession: Performer on Film and TVs S.W.A.T
headline: Steve Forrest, Performer on Film and TV’s ‘S.W.A.T.,’ Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Forrest starred in films, onstage and in British television but was best known for ABC’s “S.W.A.T.,” in which he played Lt. Dan Harrelson.

name: Haynes Johnson
headline: Haynes Johnson, Journalist and Author, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Johnson was a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist, television commentator and author who spent most of his career at The Washington Post and won wide acclaim for his coverage of the capital.

name: Georges Moustaki
headline: Georges Moustaki, Poetic French Singer, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Moustaki, who wrote “Milord” for Édith Piaf, was known for his poetic sensibility and melancholy ballads.

name: Flynn Robinson
headline: Flynn Robinson, Scorer on Dominant N.B.A. Club, Dies at 72
abstract: Robinson was a 1970 All-Star, a seven-season N.B.A. player and a productive reserve guard on the first Los Angeles Lakers title team, which had a 33-game winning streak.

name: James L. Tolbert
headline: James L. Tolbert, 86, an Early Lawyer to Black Hollywood, Dies
abstract: Mr. Tolbert, a high school dropout, went on to play a central role in an early effort to improve the way that blacks were portrayed on film.

name: Alton T. Lemon
profession: Challenged State Aid to Religious Schools
headline: Alton T. Lemon, Who Challenged State Aid to Religious Schools, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Lemon was a civil rights activist whose objection to a 1968 Pennsylvania law gave rise to a watershed 1971 Supreme Court decision.

name: Morris Renek
headline: Morris Renek, a Novelist of Gift and Determination, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Renek was a critically admired New York writer who created comic tales about historical criminals and modern urban life but never achieved the commercial success many thought he deserved.

name: Wayne Miller
headline: Wayne Miller, Photographer of War and Peace, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Miller’s images, whether taken of the front lines, the streets of Chicago or the birth of his own son, intimately chronicled a world remaking itself.

name: Ed Shaughnessy
headline: Ed Shaughnessy, ‘Tonight’ Drummer, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Shaughnessy’s deft drumming anchored the “Tonight Show” orchestra for 29 years.

name: Kim Merker
headline: Kim Merker, Hand-Press Printer of Poets, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Merker, a native New Yorker, was a designer and typesetter who used presses he operated with his own inky hands to print beautiful books, often by emerging poets.

name: Mack Emerman
headline: Mack Emerman, Founder of Criteria Recording Studios, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Emerman founded the music-making studio in Miami, where artists like Eric Clapton, the Allman Brothers and James Brown made albums.

name: Angelo J. Errichetti
headline: Angelo J. Errichetti, 84, Camden Mayor Convicted of Bribery, Dies
abstract: Mr. Errichetti, a powerful Democrat, was caught in the Abscam sting, in which federal agents posed as wealthy Arabs offering bribes.

name: Marshall Lytle
headline: Marshall Lytle, 79, Bassist With Bill Haley, Dies
abstract: Mr. Lytle, one of the Comets, played on seminal rock ’n’ roll hits, including “Shake, Rattle and Roll” and “Rock Around the Clock.”

name: Jean Bach
headline: Jean Bach, Jazz Documentarian and Fan, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Bach’s first film told the story of “A Great Day in Harlem,” a legendary 1958 group portrait of jazz greats.

name: John C. Bierwirth
profession: Leader of Grumman in Time of Uneasy Transition
headline: John C. Bierwirth, Leader of Grumman in Time of Uneasy Transition, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Bierwirth’s company produced some of the Navy’s most renowned warplanes and won coveted aerospace contracts, but he failed to diversify the firm with civilian products, like the disastrous Flxible city buses.

name: Mulgrew Miller
headline: Mulgrew Miller, Influential Jazz Pianist, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Miller combined the bright precision of bebop with the clattering intrigue of modal jazz. His style influenced more than a generation of younger pianists.

name: Henry Morgentaler
headline: Henry Morgentaler, 90, Dies; Abortion Defender in Canada
abstract: Dr. Morgentaler, who was heralded and vilified for his work and his views, won the landmark Canadian Supreme Court decision that legalized abortion nationally in 1988.

name: Lewis A. Yocum
profession: Repaired Arms and Careers in Baseball
headline: Lewis A. Yocum Dies at 65; Repaired Arms and Careers in Baseball
abstract: Dr. Yocum performed Tommy John surgery on a number of major leaguers, saving the careers of many.

name: Clarence Burke Jr.
profession: Singer in the R&B Hit O-o-h Child
headline: Clarence Burke Jr., Singer in the R&B Hit ‘O-o-h Child,’ Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Burke was the lead singer of the Five Stairsteps, a sibling rhythm-and-blues group that had its best-known hit in 1970.

name: Otto Muehl
headline: Otto Muehl, Actionist Artist And Provocateur, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Muehl’s art was sometimes considered a threat to public morality; at other times it was simply considered a threat to public safety.

name: Andrew M. Greeley
headline: Andrew M. Greeley, Priest, Scholar and Scold, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Father Greeley’s outpouring of sociological research, contemporary theology, sexually frank novels and newspaper columns challenged reigning assumptions about American Catholicism.

name: Franca Rame
headline: Franca Rame, Italian Actress and Playwright, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Rame often collaborated with her husband, the playwright Dario Fo, and it was difficult to tease out who had written what.

name: Marvin Junior
profession: Robust, Earthy Baritone for the Dells
headline: Marvin Junior, 77, Robust, Earthy Baritone for the Dells
abstract: Mr. Junior’s voice was huge and powerful, and it held up through more than two dozen albums and 57 years of performing with the Dells.

name: Dean Brooks
headline: Dean Brooks, ‘Cuckoo’s Nest’ Doctor, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Brooks was the superintendent of an Oregon psychiatric hospital when he agreed to allow “One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest” to be filmed there.

name: Bill Austin
headline: Bill Austin, Pro Bowl Guard, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Austin played for the 1956 N.F.L. champion Giants, coached the Green Bay Packers’ offensive linemen for Vince Lombardi’s power sweep and was twice an N.F.L. head coach.

name: Don Oliver
headline: Don Oliver, NBC Correspondent, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Oliver covered major world events, like the conflicts in Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam, the Middle East peace talks in 1977 and the Civil War in El Salvador, for NBC News for more than 25 years.

name: William Demby
headline: William Demby, Author of Experimental Novels, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Demby spent much of his career in Italy writing subtitles for Fellini and Rossellini movies.

name: Jean Stapleton
headline: Jean Stapleton, Who Played Archie Bunker’s Better Angel, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Stapleton starred as the big-hearted and submissive — up to a point — housewife of Archie Bunker on the groundbreaking 1970s television series “All in the Family.”

name: Roger L. Shinn
headline: Rev. Dr. Roger L. Shinn, Theologian, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Shinn championed the ecumenical movement and argued for a sharper sense of ethical and social responsibility on the part of moderate Protestant churches.

name: Jack Vance
headline: Jack Vance, Novelist of the Fantastical, Is Dead at 96
abstract: Mr. Vance wrote fantasy and mysteries, sometimes pseudonymously. But he specialized in science fiction, a label he disdained, and wrote a number of book series.

name: Frank Lautenberg
profession: New Jersey Senator in His 5th Term
headline: Frank Lautenberg, New Jersey Senator in His 5th Term, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Lautenberg fought the alcohol and tobacco industries and promoted Amtrak while on Capitol Hill, after a successful business career.

name: Rituparno Ghosh
headline: Rituparno Ghosh, Bengali Film Director, Dies at 49
abstract: The movies made in India by Mr. Ghosh, an unabashed cross-dresser, took on sensitive subjects like divorce, widowhood, homosexuality and gender identity.

name: Viktor Kulikov
headline: Viktor Kulikov Dies at 91; Led Warsaw Pact Forces
abstract: Marshal Kulikov resisted efforts to slow the arms race and pressed Poland to squash the Solidarity protest movement.

name: Deacon Jones
