profession: Made Quarterback Sack Brutal and Enthralling
headline: Deacon Jones Dies at 74; Made Quarterback Sack Brutal and Enthralling
abstract: Mr. Jones, who was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1980 after a 14-year career, used his size and strength to glamorize defensive play and master the sack, mostly for the Los Angeles Rams.

name: Will D. Campbell
profession: Maverick Minister in Civil Rights Era
headline: Rev. Will D. Campbell, Maverick Minister in Civil Rights Era, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Campbell, a rare white cleric with an extensive field record as a civil rights activist, also wrote  books that explored the human costs of racism.

name: Richie Phillips
headline: Richie Phillips, Union Leader Who Helped and Hurt Umpires, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Phillips quintupled the salaries of major league baseball umpires as their representative, but caused many of them to lose their jobs by having them resign en masse.

name: Chen Xitong
headline: Chen Xitong, Beijing Mayor During Tiananmen Protests, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Chen’s stance on the Tiananmen Square protests of 1989 earned him promotion from the Communist Party and scorn from its opponents.

name: Vollis Simpson
headline: Vollis Simpson, Visionary Artist of the Junkyard, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Simpson made metal scraps into magnificent things that twirled and jangled and clattered when he set them out on his land.

name: Martin Arnold
headline: Martin Arnold, Former Times Journalist, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Arnold was an editor for The New York Times Magazine, earned a George Polk Award for his reporting, explored municipal corruption and wrote a column about the publishing industry.

name: Helen Hanft
profession: Master of Camp Way Off Broadway
headline: Helen Hanft, Master of Camp Way Off Broadway, Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. Hanft was an actress whose gift for camp humor, surreal scenarios and risqué roles made her the queen of Off Off Broadway during a golden age for experimental theater.

name: Bob Fletcher
headline: Bob Fletcher Dies at 101; Helped Japanese-Americans
abstract: Mr. Fletcher was thought of as an unsung hero for his efforts during World War II in California to manage the farms of Japanese families forced to live in internment camps.

name: Esther Williams
headline: Esther Williams, Swimming Champion Who Became a Movie Star, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Williams, a teenage swimming champion, became an enormous Hollywood star in a decade of watery MGM extravaganzas in the 1940s and ’50s.

name: Paul Olefsky
headline: Paul Olefsky, a Cellist and Educator, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Olefsky was a principal cellist of the Philadelphia Orchestra and a noted soloist, as well as a teacher at the Butler School of Music.

name: Pierre Mauroy
headline: Pierre Mauroy, Socialist Who Led Changes in France, Dies at 84
abstract: As France’s first Socialist prime minister after World War II, Mr. Mauroy pushed through what his party considered to be important reforms.

name: Joey Covington
headline: Joey Covington, Rock Drummer, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Covington was a replacement drummer for Jefferson Airplane and a founding member of Hot Tuna.

name: Richard Ramirez
headline: Richard Ramirez, the ‘Night Stalker’ Killer, Dies at 53
abstract: Most of the killings were committed by Mr. Ramirez before dawn during residential burglaries, and all were markedly coldblooded, involving savage beatings, mutilations and sexual assaults.

name: Joseph M. Sullivan
headline: Bishop Joseph M. Sullivan, Advocate for the Poor, Dies at 83
abstract: Bishop Sullivan testified before Congress in the 1980s about the effect of AIDS and poverty on communities in Brooklyn and Queens.

name: Abigail Heyman
headline: Abigail Heyman, Feminist Photojournalist, Dies at 70
abstract: In books like “Growing Up Female,” Ms. Heyman chronicled women’s lives in the 1970s and ’80s to document their traditional roles.

name: Tom Sharpe
headline: Tom Sharpe, Darkly Satirical British Novelist, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Sharpe, whose books included “Porterhouse Blue” and the Henry Wilt series, used crudity and excess to  take on targets like racism, the aristocracy and academia.

name: Mott Green
headline: Mott Green, a Free-Spirited Chocolatier, Dies at 47
abstract: Born David Friedman, Mr. Green started the Grenada Chocolate Company, an environmentally minded operation in the Caribbean.

name: Charlie Coles
profession: Led Underdog to a Stirring N.C.A.A. Run
headline: Charlie Coles, Who Led Underdog to a Stirring N.C.A.A. Run, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Coles coached Miami University in Ohio and Wally Szczerbiak to a memorable N.C.A.A. basketball tournament run in 1999.

name: Edward Hotaling
headline: Edward Hotaling, 75, TV Reporter Who Shed Light on Black History, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Hotaling offered tales about African-American jockeys and a White House built by slaves, and his question in 1988 about race ended the career of Jimmy (the Greek) Snyder at CBS.

name: Arnold Eidus
headline: Arnold Eidus, 90, Adman With Stradivarius, Dies
abstract: Mr. Eidus, an advertising executive, began his career as an internationally acclaimed concert violinist who made it to Carnegie Hall as a soloist at age 13.

name: Yoram Kaniuk
headline: Yoram Kaniuk, Maverick Israeli Novelist, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Kaniuk, a nonconformist with a sometimes morbid sense of humor, was a celebrated author and journalist who became disenchanted with his homeland.

name: Arturo Vega
headline: Arturo Vega, Shepherd for the Ramones, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Vega was often called the fifth Ramone for serving as the punk band’s spokesman and logo designer.

name: Robert W. Fogel
headline: Robert W. Fogel, Nobel-Winning Economist, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Fogel was widely known for work that aroused objections if not open hostility through his pioneering use of cliometrics, which applies economic theory and statistic methods to history.

name: Miller Barber
headline: Miller Barber, 82, Golf Champion With Odd Swing, Dies
abstract: Barber was a popular and successful player on the P.G.A. Tour in the 1960s and went on to dominate in the early years of senior tournament play.

name: Iain Banks
profession: Novelist of Crime and Science Fiction
headline: Iain Banks, Novelist of Crime and Science Fiction, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Banks, a best-selling Scottish author, churned out 28 books in just under 30 years on subjects ranging from violent crime to interstellar conflicts.

name: Barbara Vucanovich
headline: Barbara Vucanovich, 91, Dies; Served Nevada in Congress
abstract: Ms. Vucanovich traveled to Reno in 1949 to get a quick divorce and ended up staying and becoming the first woman to be sent to Congress from Nevada.

name: Bruno Bartoletti
headline: Bruno Bartoletti, Maestro Who Shaped Lyric Opera of Chicago, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Bartoletti was considered a superb interpreter of the 19th- and early-20th-century music of Italian masters.

name: Harold J. Cromer
headline: Harold J. Cromer, Vaudeville Duo’s Stumpy, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Cromer, who was in his 90s, was part of Stump and Stumpy, a comedy team that played the black theater and nightclub circuit from the 1930s to the ’50s, including the Apollo Theater in Harlem.

name: Joan H. Parker
headline: Joan H. Parker, 80, Mystery Writer’s Muse, Dies
abstract: Ms. Parker, the widow of Robert B. Parker, was a fund-raiser and an educator.

name: Doug Bailey
headline: Doug Bailey, G.O.P. Political Consultant, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Bailey founded The Hotline, a digest of political news, distributed by fax, that became an indispensable tool of the political trade in the pre-Web 1980s and ’90s.

name: Jerome Karle
headline: Jerome Karle, Nobelist for Crystallography, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Karle shared the 1985 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with a former college classmate for creating what is now an essential tool in the development of new drugs.

name: Joseph A. Unanue
profession: Former Chief Executive of Goya Foods
headline: Joseph A. Unanue, Former Chief Executive of Goya Foods, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Unanue is credited with coining the company’s well-known advertising slogan, “Goya — oh boya!”

name: Ralph Graves
profession: Strove to Keep Life Magazine Afloat
headline: Ralph Graves, Who Strove to Keep Life Magazine Afloat, Dies at 88
abstract: As the last managing editor of the weekly Life magazine, Mr. Graves strove to keep an American institution afloat in its turbulent final years.

name: Paul Soros
headline: Paul Soros, Shipping Innovator, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Soros built Soros Associates, which has dominated the port-building industry and shifted international trade and production patterns through its shipping innovations.

name: Walt Arfons
profession: Pioneer With Cars Using Jet Engines
headline: Walt Arfons, a Pioneer With Cars Using Jet Engines, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Arfons, with his half brother, Art Arfons, built some of the fastest racecars of the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Thomas Penfield Jackson
headline: Thomas Penfield Jackson, Outspoken Judge, Dies at 76
abstract: Judge Jackson ruled that Microsoft was a predatory monopoly and must be split in half, only to see an appeals court reverse his order because he discussed it with journalists.

name: Niels Diffrient
headline: Niels Diffrient, Industrial Designer Who Blended Form and Function, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Diffrient combined elegance and efficiency in everyday objects, and even office chairs like the award-winning Freedom Chair.

name: Gene Mako
headline: Gene Mako, Tennis Champion, Dies at 97
abstract: Mako and Don Budge teamed up to win two U.S. and two Wimbledon titles, and they met in the 1938 Open singles final, with Budge beating Mako to complete the sport’s first Grand Slam.

name: Bernard Sahlins
headline: Bernard Sahlins, Patriarch of Sketch Comedy, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Sahlins was the last survivor of the three founders of Second City, the Chicago nightclub that nurtured generations of comedians.

name: Maxine Stuart
profession: Acted on Stage, Film and TV
headline: Maxine Stuart, 94, Dies; Acted on Stage, Film and TV
abstract: Ms. Stuart had a recurring role on the soap opera “The Edge of Night” and starred in two nonfiction books by the writer Helene Hanff.

name: Bob Meistrell
headline: Bob Meistrell, Who Revolutionized Wet Suits, Dies at 84
abstract: With his twin brother, Mr. Meistrell began making wet suits for surfers and scuba divers in the 1950s and founded the company Body Glove, which produced some of the first custom-made wet suits.

name: Johnny Smith
headline: Johnny Smith, Venerable Jazz Guitarist, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Smith’s biggest hit, “Walk Don’t Run,” became famous in covers by other bands, notably the Ventures. Mr. Smith, the writer of “Walk, Don’t Run,” gave up his career in 1958 to care for his daughter.

name: Sherwood Ross
headline: Sherwood Ross, President of Ross Bicycles, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Ross became president of the company his father founded and turned it into the third-largest American bicycle maker.

name: James Gandolfini
profession: Complex Mob Boss in The Sopranos
headline: James Gandolfini Is Dead at 51; a Complex Mob Boss in ‘The Sopranos’
abstract: Mr. Gandolfini won three Emmy Awards for his lead role as a New Jersey mob kingpin on the HBO drama.

name: Slim Whitman
profession: Yodeling Country Singer With a Regular-Guy Image
headline: Slim Whitman, Yodeling Country Singer With a Regular-Guy Image, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Whitman recorded more than 500 songs, made more than 100 albums and sold more than 70 million records.

name: Dave Jennings
headline: Dave Jennings, All-Pro Punter for Giants, Dies at 61
abstract: Jennings, known for kicks that lingered in the air, angled toward the sideline and pinned opposing teams inside their 20-yard line, was often the best player on some dreadful teams.

name: Stephen Porter
headline: Stephen Porter, Theater Director, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Porter was a theater director who dusted off classic plays by the likes of Molière and Shaw and honed them as “the realism of another time.”

name: David Wall
headline: David Wall, a Prince Among Dancers, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Mr. Wall, a handsome redhead widely known as Ginger, became the youngest principal dancer in the history of the Royal Ballet in 1966.

name: Gyula Horn
headline: Gyula Horn, Who Helped Part Iron Curtain, Dies at 80
abstract: As Moscow’s grip on Eastern Europe slipped, Mr. Horn proved nimble as a newly minted, nonideological, pragmatic reformer in helping to lead Hungary away from Communism.

name: Vince Flynn
headline: Vince Flynn, Wrote Best-Selling Thrillers, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. Flynn, author of Mitch Rapp killer-for-hire thrillers, got his start selling a self-published book out of the trunk of his car.

name: Kenneth Wilson
headline: Kenneth Wilson, Nobel Physicist, Dies at 77
abstract: Dr. Wilson was known for showing how to calculate tricky moments in physics, like when ice melts or an iron bar loses magnetism.

name: Sam Farber
headline: Sam Farber, Creator of Oxo Utensils, Dies at  88
abstract: Mr. Farber got the idea for the hand-friendly utensils when his wife, who has mild arthritis in her hands, was peeling apples.

name: Martin Bernal
headline: Martin Bernal, ‘Black Athena’ Scholar, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Bernal’s work ignited a debate by arguing that the African and Semitic lineage of Western civilization had been scrubbed from the record of ancient Greece by 18th- and 19th-century historians.

name: Sam Most
profession: Helped Bring the Flute Into the Jazz Mainstream
headline: Sam Most, Who Helped Bring the Flute Into the Jazz Mainstream, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Most’s “Undercurrent Blues” helped introduce the flute into the modern jazz mainstream, inspiring Herbie Mann, Rahsaan Roland Kirk and others.

name: Michael Baigent
headline: Michael Baigent, Writer Who Sued Over ‘Da Vinci Code,’ Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Baigent, an author of “The Holy Blood and the Holy Grail,” contended that Dan Brown had stolen his ideas, using them in “The Da Vinci Code.”

name: Chet Flippo
headline: Chet Flippo, Journalist Who Championed Country Music, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Flippo, a dean of pop music journalism who wrote for Rolling Stone, insisted on profiling musicians like Willie Nelson and Dolly Parton during an era of rock celebrity mania.

name: Bobby Bland
headline: Bobby (Blue) Bland, Soul and Blues Balladeer, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Bland never achieved the popular acclaim enjoyed by contemporaries like B. B. King, but his emotionally fraught vocals helped modernize the blues.

name: Gary David Goldberg
profession: Television Writer And Creator of Family Ties
headline: Gary David Goldberg, Television Writer And Creator of ‘Family Ties,’ Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Goldberg, a writer and producer, created warmhearted television shows, most notably the 1980s comedy that propelled Michael J. Fox to stardom.

name: William Hathaway
headline: William Hathaway, Senator From Maine, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Hathaway’s 1972 election ended the career of his Republican opponent, Margaret Chase Smith, the first woman elected to both houses of Congress.

name: John L. Dotson Jr.
headline: John L. Dotson Jr., Publisher of Beacon Journal, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Dotson led The Akron Beacon Journal to a Pulitzer Prize for a series on race relations.

name: Richard Matheson
profession: Writer of Haunted Science Fiction and Horror
headline: Richard Matheson, Writer of Haunted Science Fiction and Horror, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Matheson’s novels, short stories, screenplays and teleplays drew the blueprints for dozens of science fiction and horror movies and television shows.

name: Filip Topol
profession: Rock Musician of the Czech Revolution
headline: Filip Topol, a Rock Musician of the Czech Revolution, Dies at 48
abstract: Mr. Topol and his band, Psi Vojaci, were Prague dissidents in their country’s heroic recent history.

name: Elliott Reid
headline: Elliott Reid, Sleuth in ‘Gentlemen Prefer Blondes,’ Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Reid played Ernie Malone, a private detective hired to investigate Lorelei Lee, played by Marilyn Monroe.

name: Marc Rich
headline: Marc Rich, Financier and Famous Fugitive, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Rich, who made billions in commodities as founder of Glencore International, was a fugitive on charges of tax evasion and trading with Iran until he was pardoned by President Bill Clinton.

name: Bert Stern
profession: Elite Photographer Known for Images of Marilyn Monroe
headline: Bert Stern, Elite Photographer Known for Images of Marilyn Monroe, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Stern helped redefine advertising and fashion art in the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Harry Parker
headline: Harry Parker Dies at 77; Guiding Hand in Rowing
abstract: Mr. Parker was an omnipresent figure in rowing at the collegiate and national levels for decades, coaching Harvard rowers with unrivaled success and men’s and women’s Olympic medal-winning crews.

name: Milorad Miskovitch
headline: Milorad Miskovitch, 85, Luminary in French Ballet, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Miskovitch became one of French ballet’s leading male stars in the 1940s and ’50s.

name: Frank Stranahan
profession: Top Amateur Golfer and Ardent Fitness Advocate
headline: Frank Stranahan, Top Amateur Golfer and Ardent Fitness Advocate, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Stranahan was a fervent advocate of bodybuilding and healthy living well before it became the rage. Arnold Palmer called him “muscles.”

name: Jim Hudson
profession: Intercepted Pass to Help Jets Win Title
headline: Jim Hudson, Who Intercepted Pass to Help Jets Win Title, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Hudson, whose interception helped defeat the Baltimore Colts in the 1969 Super Bowl, requested that his brain and spine be given to researchers studying sports-related trauma.

name: Frank B. Kelso
headline: Adm. Frank B. Kelso Dies at 79; Tied to Tailhook Scandal
abstract: Admiral Kelso held top naval commands and oversaw the capture of terrorists on the cruise ship Achille Lauro, but his career was tarnished after a sexual harassment scandal known as Tailhook.

name: David Rogers
headline: David Rogers, Stage Adapter of Offbeat Material, Dies at 85
abstract: Among the works Mr. Rogers produced was the book for a musical based on “Flowers for Algernon” and plays based on “Brave New World” and “The Sting.”

name: David Rogers
profession: Took on New Yorks School Board
headline: David Rogers, 88, Took on New York’s School Board
abstract: His condemnation of the educational bureaucracy, in a book published during a dispute over decentralization in 1968, fueled the movement that led to mayoral control.

name: Curtis W. Tarr
headline: Curtis W. Tarr, Innovative Leader of the Draft, Dies at 88
abstract: As director of the Selective Service System during the Vietnam War, Mr. Tarr initiated changes intended to make the draft lottery fairer.

name: Rena Price
headline: Rena Price Is Dead at 97; Catalyst for the Watts Riots
abstract: Ms. Price had a seminal role in the riots that gripped Los Angeles in the summer of 1965, the biggest uprising by blacks in the United States since the slave revolts.

name: Philip E. Slater
headline: Philip E. Slater, Social Critic Who Renounced Academia, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Slater’s best-selling book, “The Pursuit of Loneliness,” was published in 1970. The following year, he resigned from Brandeis University.

name: Alain Mimoun
headline: Alain Mimoun, a Top Runner, Dies at 92
abstract: Mimoun was a French Olympian and a brilliant distance runner who was hailed for the grandeur of his achievements and for embodying the amateur ideal.

name: Norman Eddy
headline: The Rev. Norman Eddy, a Minister in East Harlem, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Eddy, a Yale-educated minister from Connecticut, settled in East Harlem in 1951 and helped start myriad organizations that have sustained his work.

name: Sarah Charlesworth
headline: Sarah Charlesworth, Artist of Deconstructed Photographs, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Charlesworth, a contemporary of Cindy Sherman and Richard Prince, questioned photography’s role in culture and subverted the medium’s conventions.

name: Elías Querejeta
headline: Elías Querejeta, 78, Producer of Major Spanish Films, Dies
abstract: Mr. Querejeta produced the essential works of many of his nation’s most challenging filmmakers, including “The Hunt” (1966), by Carlos Saura, which ushered in the so-called New Spanish Cinema.

name: Donald Bevan
headline: Donald Bevan, 93, Sardi’s Artist and ‘Stalag 17’ Writer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Bevan, who was a longtime caricaturist for the Broadway bistro, and Edmund Trzcinski were inspired by their incarceration in a Nazi camp to write a play about the search for a spy.

name: Jim Kelly
headline: Jim Kelly, Star of Martial Arts Movies, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Kelly added an Afro, swagger and a few memorable one-liners to martial arts movies in the 1970s.

name: Emilio Colombo
headline: Emilio Colombo, Former Italian Premier, Dies at 93
abstract: A self-described technocrat, Mr. Colombo curbed roaring inflation, battled political extremism and legalized divorce in his country while helping to build an integrated Europe.

name: James Martin
headline: James Martin, Technology Consultant and Oxford Benefactor, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Martin was an influential figure in information technology who used his fortune to study the problems and opportunities confronting the 21st-century world.

name: James Martin
profession: Spurred G.O.P. Gains in the South
headline: James Martin, Who Spurred G.O.P. Gains in the South, Dies at 99
abstract: His close Senate race in 1962 and election to Congress in 1964 portended a Republican sweep in what had long been a Democratic bastion.

name: William H. Gray III
headline: William H. Gray III, Pastor and Lawmaker, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Gray was a third-generation Baptist minister from Philadelphia who won a seat in Congress in 1978 and rose to become the highest-ranking black lawmaker in the country.

name: William M. Gray
profession: Hurricane Predictor and Climate Change Skeptic
headline: William M. Gray, Hurricane Predictor and Climate Change Skeptic, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Gray aggregated measures of atmospheric conditions, water current and water temperature to predict the number and intensity of tropical storms.

name: Rawleigh Warner Jr.
headline: Rawleigh Warner Jr., Brash Chairman of Mobil, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Warner steered the company through the Arab oil embargo of 1973, lurches in the oil market and ever more delicate dealings with oil-producing nations.

name: Douglas Engelbart
headline: Computer Visionary Who Invented the Mouse
abstract: Dr. Engelbart’s 1968 demonstration of interactive computing astounded scientists and the technology was later refined for Apple and Microsoft.

name: Paul Smith
headline: Paul Smith, Jazz Pianist, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Smith played with many well-known singers but was best known for accompanying Ella Fitzgerald, leading the trio that backed her in concert.

name: Jim Nayder
headline: Jim Nayder, Specialist in ‘Annoying Music,’ Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Nayder’s epiphany that people were attracted to “train-wreck” music led him to become the Chicago-based founder and host of “The Annoying Music Show” on NPR.

name: Hans Hass
headline: Hans Hass, Early Undersea Explorer, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Hass, a marine scientist from Austria with an affinity for sharks, was known for the many commercial films he made between 1948 and 1960.

name: Ted Hood
profession: Champion of Americas Cup and Innovator in Yachting
headline: Ted Hood, Champion of America’s Cup and Innovator in Yachting, Dies at 86
abstract: Hood was a yachtsman, sailmaker, rigging builder and boat designer who captained Courageous, the 1974 America’s Cup winner.

name: Snoo Wilson
headline: Snoo Wilson, Surrealistic British Playwright, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Wilson’s plays often had a satirical edge and included real people from history, like Darwin, Eichmann and Aleister Crowley.

name: Theodore Reed
headline: Theodore Reed, Who Lifted National Zoo’s Profile, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Reed was the keeper of the celebrity pandas Ling-Ling and Hsing-Hsing, among other creatures, while he was the director of the National Zoo from 1958 to 1983.

name: F. D. Reeve
headline: F. D. Reeve, Poet and Translator, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Reeve, father of the actor Christopher Reeve, wrote highly regarded poetry and other works, translated Russian authors and founded The Poetry Review.

name: Lo Hsing Han
headline: Lo Hsing Han, Myanmar Drug Kingpin, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Lo was an opium and heroin trafficker who became one of Myanmar’s richest men and a potent symbol of the ability of the country’s drug warlords to operate with impunity.

name: Michael Mastromarino
headline: Michael Mastromarino, Dentist Guilty in Organ Scheme, Dies at 49
abstract: The former dental surgeon pleaded guilty in 2008 to illegally harvesting organs and tissues from cadavers in funeral homes without the survivors’ consent.

name: Arthur Rosenthal
headline: Arthur Rosenthal, Academic Book Publisher, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Rosenthal led Basic Books in the 1950s and ’60s and led Harvard University Press to solvency in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Edmund S. Morgan
headline: Edmund S. Morgan, Historian Who Shed Light on Puritans, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Morgan was drawn to the Puritans’ intellectual world, but also explored the paradox of freedom and slavery in colonial Virginia and wrote a best-seller about Benjamin Franklin.

name: Masao Yoshida
profession: Nuclear Engineer and Chief at Fukushima Plant
headline: Masao Yoshida, Nuclear Engineer and Chief at Fukushima Plant, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Yoshida won praise for his effort to minimize the damage at the power plant as multiple reactors spiraled out of control after a tsunami.

name: Douglas J. Dayton
headline: Douglas J. Dayton, First President of Target, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Dayton, whose family ran Dayton’s department stores, used a strategy of low prices and fashionable goods to build a profitable discount chain.

name: Austin Goodrich
headline: Austin Goodrich, Spy Who Posed as Journalist, Dies at 87
abstract: In the 1950s and ’60s, numerous secret agents for the United States used journalism as a cover. Mr. Goodrich, unlike some, considered himself primarily a spy.

name: Leland Mitchell
profession: Defied Racism on the Basketball Court
headline: Leland Mitchell, Who Defied Racism on the Basketball Court, Dies at 72
abstract: A decision by Mitchell and his teammates to play in a N.C.A.A. tournament despite opposition was widely seen as the beginning of the end of segregation in college sports.

name: Anton Antonov-Ovseyenko
headline: Anton Antonov-Ovseyenko, Who Exposed Stalin Terror, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Antonov-Ovseyenko’s books cracked through the shell of Soviet censorship, offering readers at home and in the West a vivid portrait of tyranny and violence.

name: Philip Caldwell
profession: First Nonfamily Member to Head Ford
headline: Philip Caldwell, First Nonfamily Member to Head Ford, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Outsiders were stunned when Henry Ford II dismissed Lee Iacocca as president of Ford Motor in 1977 and elevated Mr. Caldwell, who was nearly unknown outside the company.

name: Layhmond Robinson Jr.
headline: Layhmond Robinson Jr., Who Paved Way for Black Journalists, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Robinson, one of the first black reporters at The New York Times in the 1950s and a local television news correspondent, inspired the next generation of black journalists.

name: Alan Rosenthal
headline: Alan Rosenthal, Who Reshaped Legislatures, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Rosenthal was a political scientist and champion of the idea that government can be a positive force.

name: Toshi Seeger
headline: Toshi Seeger, Wife of Folk-Singing Legend, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Seeger married Pete Seeger in 1943, and he credited her with figuring out how to turn his artistic concepts into commercial successes, calling her “the brains of the family.”

name: Chuck Foley
headline: Chuck Foley, Co-Creator of the Game Twister, Dies at 82
abstract: Originally manufactured by Milton Bradley, Mr. Foley’s game was introduced in 1966 and has gone on to sell tens of millions of copies.

name: Amar G. Bose
headline: Amar G. Bose, Acoustic Engineer and Inventor, Dies at 83
abstract: Dr. Bose’s namesake company became synonymous with high-quality audio systems and speakers for home users, auditoriums and automobiles.

name: Jim Buck
headline: Jim Buck, Who Made Walking Dogs a Job, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Buck, a thin man who commanded the leashes of a half-dozen charges at a time, is considered the person who professionalized dog walking in New York City.

name: Robert L. Hardesty
headline: Robert L. Hardesty, Speechwriter for Johnson, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Hardesty also helped write and edit President Lyndon B. Johnson’s memoirs and served as president of Johnson’s alma mater.

name: John Hightower
headline: John Hightower, Besieged Art Museum Director, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Hightower was named director of the Museum of Modern Art at 37. His firing 19 months later made him a symbol of the fleeting of wunderkind success.

name: Barbara Robinson
headline: Barbara Robinson, Children’s Book Author, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Robinson, wrote several whimsical titles for a young audience, including “The Best Christmas Pageant Ever.”

name: Cory Monteith
headline: Cory Monteith, a Star of TV’s ‘Glee,’ Is Dead at 31
abstract: Mr. Monteith, who won global fame in Fox’s TV series and battled with substance abuse problems, was found dead in a hotel room in Canada on Saturday, the police said.

name: Nadezhda Popova
headline: Nadezhda Popova, WWII ‘Night Witch,’ Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Popova was a member of a renowned unit of deadly female Soviet pilots called the “Night Witches” by German invaders because of the sound their plywood planes made.

name: Leonard Garment
profession: Lawyer and Nixon Adviser During Watergate
headline: Leonard Garment, Lawyer and Nixon Adviser During Watergate, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Garment discouraged President Richard M. Nixon from destroying White House tapes and pushed unsuccessfully for the president’s early resignation. He also recommended to Gerald R. Ford that Mr. Nixon be pardoned.

name: Eugene P. Wilkinson
headline: Eugene P. Wilkinson, Who Steered First Nuclear Submarine, Dies at 94
abstract: Admiral Wilkinson commanded the Nautilus, the military’s first machine to harness atomic fission for propulsion rather than weaponry.

name: Herbert M. Allison Jr.
headline: Herbert M. Allison Jr. Dies at 69; Led Bailout Efforts
abstract: Mr. Allison, a former Merrill Lynch president, was appointed to lead and help rescue a troubled Fannie Mae in 2008 and then ran a federal bank bailout program.

name: Pran Sikand
headline: Pran Sikand, Villain of the Bollywood Screen, Dies at 93
abstract: During the height of Mr. Sikand’s fame, his sneers and snarls on film had such an indelible influence that mothers in India were said to be reluctant to name their sons Pran.

name: Marc Simont
headline: Marc Simont, Classic Children’s Book Illustrator, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Simont, a recipient of the Caldecott Medal, was admired for his delicately spare, but expressive, style.

name: Sidney Berry
headline: Lt. Gen. Sidney Berry, West Point Chief, Dies at 87
abstract: A decorated combat veteran and a military assistant to Robert S. McNamara, General Berry’s most notable role was overseeing the transition to coeducation at West Point.

name: Laurie Frink
profession: Trumpeter and Brass Instructor to Many
headline: Laurie Frink,Trumpeter and Brass Instructor to Many, Dies at 61
abstract: Ms. Frink was an accomplished trumpeter who became a brass instructor of widespread influence and high regard.

name: Bill Warner
headline: Bill Warner,  Who Set Speed Record on Motorcycle, Dies at 44
abstract: Mr. Warner set a world land speed record, 311.945 miles per hour in 1.5 miles, in 2011.

name: Lindy Hess
profession: Matchmaker to Publishers and Their Staff
headline: Lindy Hess, Matchmaker to Publishers and Their Staff, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Hess revamped an educational program that had lost touch with the publishing industry and helped its graduates get jobs.

name: T-Model Ford
headline: T-Model Ford, Late-Blooming Bluesman, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Ford, who released his first album in 1997, began his musical life in the 1980s in Mississippi juke joints.

name: Curtis Harnack
headline: Curtis Harnack, Writer and President of Yaddo, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Harnack wrote of his life growing up on an Iowa farm and was president of Yaddo, the artists’ retreat in Saratoga Springs, N.Y., from 1971 to 1987.

name: Tony Metcalf
headline: Tony Metcalf, Editor of Free City Newspapers, Dies at 50
abstract: Mr. Metcalf led Metro US, a newspaper that offers a quick read to young bus and subway riders in New York, Philadelphia and Boston.

name: Nobuyuki Aihara
headline: Nobuyuki Aihara, Olympic Champion, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Aihara won two gold medals at the 1960 Olympics in Rome and helped usher in an era of Japanese gymnastic dominance.

name: Bert Trautmann
profession: Won Iron Cross and F.A. Cup
headline: Bert Trautmann, Who Won Iron Cross and F.A. Cup, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Trautmann, who once played with a broken neck, said that his training as a paratrooper had made it easy to perform acrobatic dives as a goalkeeper.

name: Helen Thomas
headline: 50 Years of Tough Questions and ‘Thank You, Mr. President’
abstract: Ms. Thomas covered every president from John F. Kennedy to Barack Obama, but her career ended ignominiously over remarks she made about Israeli Jews.

name: Ashton Springer
headline: Ashton Springer, Producer of Broadway Shows, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Springer went from owning a laundromat to producing nearly a dozen shows on Broadway.

name: John Casablancas
headline: John Casablancas, Modeling Visionary, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Casablancas was the founder of the Elite Model Management agency and brought about the supermodel era in the fashion world.

name: Elmer T. Lee
headline: Elmer T. Lee, Whose Premium Bourbon Revived an Industry, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Lee created Blanton’s Single Barrel for Buffalo Trace Distillery in 1984 and is credited with reviving Kentucky whiskey’s reputation.

name: Phil Woosnam
headline: Phil Woosnam, Pioneer of North American Soccer, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Woosnam played professionally in Britain before becoming the commissioner of the North American Soccer League.

name: Alex Colville
headline: Alex Colville, Leading Canadian Artist, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Colville, a figurative painter, revealed emotional and cultural tension in his spare and precise depictions of moments that might otherwise seem mundane.

name: Marv Rotblatt
headline: Marv Rotblatt, Pitcher Celebrated Through Softball Marathon, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Rotblatt appeared in only 35 major league games, but a small college memorialized him with an annual softball game that now lasts nearly 150 innings.

name: Dennis Farina
headline: Dennis Farina, Detective in Life and TV, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Farina spent 20 years as a police officer in Chicago before he starred as a detective on the television shows “Law & Order” and “Crime Story.”

name: Page Morton Black
headline: Page Morton Black, Who Sang Heavenly Jingle, Dies at 97
abstract: Mrs. Black was a cabaret singer known for her sprightly rendition of the Chock Full o’Nuts song in radio and television ads.

name: Emile Griffith
headline: Emile Griffith, Boxer Who Unleashed a Fatal Barrage, Dies at 75
abstract: Griffith, a welterweight and middleweight champion, fought professionally for 20 years. He famously won a 1962 bout in which his opponent died 10 days later.

name: Mel Smith
headline: Mel Smith, TV Actor, Director and Producer, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Smith performed in TV and movies, directed films like “The Tall Guy” and helped found a production company with successful comedy shows.

name: Willie Louis
profession: Named the Killers of Emmett Till at Their Trial
headline: Willie Louis, Who Named the Killers of Emmett Till at Their Trial, Dies at 76
abstract: After walking through the thicket of Klansmen massed outside the courthouse, Mr. Louis testified in the murder of Emmett Till, a watershed moment in the civil rights movement.

name: Virginia Johnson
profession: Widely Published Collaborator in Sex Research
headline: Virginia Johnson, Widely Published Collaborator in Sex Research, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Johnson and William H. Masters helped make the frank discussion of sex in postwar America possible if not downright acceptable.

name: Ronnie Cutrone
headline: Ronnie Cutrone, a Warhol Assistant, Dies at 65
abstract: An artist, Mr. Cutrone’s associations made him a player in the New York art world.

name: George Mitchell
headline: George Mitchell, a Pioneer in Hydraulic Fracturing, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Mitchell, who on a hunch began drilling shale rock formations, is credited with creating an unexpected natural gas boom in the United States.

name: Walter De Maria
headline: Walter De Maria, Artist on Grand Scale, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. De Maria, whose art helped give rise to earthworks, Conceptual Art and Minimal art, was best known for large-scale outdoor works, including “The Lightning Field” in New Mexico.

name: Lindy Boggs
profession: Longtime Representative and Champion of Women
headline: Lindy Boggs, Longtime Representative and Champion of Women, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Mrs. Boggs succeeded her husband in Congress after his plane crashed in Alaska. She went on serve nine terms and to champion women’s rights.

name: J. J. Cale
headline: J. J. Cale, 74, Musician and Songwriter, Dies
abstract: Mr. Cale’s blues-inflected rock influenced some of the genre’s biggest names, and his songs were recorded by Eric Clapton and Johnny Cash among others.

name: James Gordon
headline: James Gordon, Who Paved Way for Lasers, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Gordon was a 25-year-old graduate student in physics when he helped develop the maser, which would lead to the building of the first laser.

name: Carline Ray
headline: Carline Ray, an Enduring Pioneer Woman of Jazz, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Ray, an instrumentalist and vocalist who began performing in the 1940s, worked steadily for seven decades and released her first recording as a lead singer this year.

name: Steve Berrios
profession: Master of Latin Jazz and Drums
headline: Steve Berrios, Master of Latin Jazz and Drums, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Berrios, a fixture of the New York jazz scene for 40 years, was a founding member of the Fort Apache Band.

name: Bud Day
headline: Col. Bud Day, Heroic Pilot in Vietnam War, Dies at 88
abstract: Colonel Day, an Air Force fighter pilot, earned the Medal of Honor for enduring more than five years of brutality without divulging sensitive information to his captors.

name: Garry Davis
headline: Garry Davis, Man of No Nation Who Saw One World of No War, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Davis was a self-declared world citizen who tirelessly advocated to erase national borders and to end wars as part of the One World movement.

name: William W. Scranton
headline: William W. Scranton, 96, G.O.P. Prodigy Who Led Pennsylvania, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Scranton, heir to a fortune in railroads and utilities, was a congressman and governor before running unsuccessfully for the Republican Party’s presidential nomination in 1964.

name: Herb Kaplow
profession: Voice of ABC and NBC News
headline: Herb Kaplow, Voice of ABC and NBC News, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Kaplow’s resonant voice and craggy face were familiar to generations of viewers of the nightly news broadcast.

name: G. W. Stocking
headline: G. W. Stocking, 84; Studied Anthropologists
abstract: Professor Stocking was a historian of science who chronicled the norms, customs and tribal beliefs of modern anthropologists, documenting a history of racial bias and ethnocentrism.

name: Eileen Brennan
headline: Eileen Brennan, Stalwart of Film and Stage, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Brennan’s performance  as the gleefully tough Army captain in the  1980 film “Private Benjamin” earned her an Academy Award nomination.

name: Juan David Ochoa Vásquez
headline: Juan David Ochoa Vásquez, Co-Founder of Medellín Cartel, Dies at 65
abstract: The cocaine trafficker, who started the brutal organization with his brothers and Pablo Escobar, served about five years in prison and then returned to raising horses.

name: Ossie Schectman
headline: Ossie Schectman, N.B.A.’s First Scorer, Dies at 94
abstract: The 6-foot Knicks guard and captain made history on a layup a minute or so into a game against the Toronto Huskies on Nov. 1, 1946.

name: Harry F. Byrd
headline: Harry F. Byrd, Virginia Senator, Dies at 98
abstract: The son of a senator and originally appointed to his seat, Mr. Byrd was a conservative Democrat turned independent.

name: León Ferrari
headline: León Ferrari, Provocative Argentine Conceptual Artist, Dies at 92
abstract: A conceptualist who spent years in exile in Brazil, Mr. Ferrari won international honors for his often polemical artwork.

name: Peter M. Flanigan
headline: Peter M. Flanigan, Banker and Nixon Aide, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Flanigan became one of President Richard M. Nixon’s most trusted, influential and well-connected aides on business and economic matters.

name: Mick Farren
profession: British Rock n Roll Renaissance Man
headline: Mick Farren, British Rock ’n’ Roll Renaissance Man, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Farren was a singer, songwriter, rock critic and historian, and science-fiction author.

name: Bernadette Lafont
headline: Bernadette Lafont, 74, Actress and Muse
abstract: Ms. Lafont was a French actress whose sensuality and ebullience made her a muse of French New Wave films in the late 1950s and early ’60s.

name: John Graves
headline: John Graves, Author Beloved by Fellow Texans, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Graves’s Brazos River excursion in 1957 resulted in “Goodbye to a River,” then two other books, “Hard Scrabble” and “From a Limestone Ledge,” completed the noted trilogy.

name: Dick Kazmaier
headline: Dick Kazmaier, a Heisman Winner Who Passed on the N.F.L., Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Kazmaier, a Princeton halfback who won the Heisman in 1951, was drafted by the Bears but declined to join the team, or any other, saying he had achieved all he wanted in the sport.

name: Berthold Beitz
headline: Berthold Beitz, German Steel Industrialist Who Saved Jews, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Beitz was well known for his efforts to save hundreds of Jews and Poles from the Nazis while stationed in Poland during World War II.

name: Fernando Alonso
headline: Fernando Alonso, a Founder of Cuban Ballet, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Alonso, who with his brother and then-wife, Alicia Alonso, began the Ballet Nacional de Cuba, was a dancer and teacher who mixed classical rigor with Latin physicality.

name: Michael Ansara
headline: Michael Ansara, Actor Who Played Cochise and Kang, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Ansara had a busy career as a guest star on many of the best-known television series in the 1950s, ’60s and ’70s, everything from “Broken Arrow” to “Star Trek” to “I Dream of Jeannie” to “Kojak.”

name: Leighton Gage
headline: Leighton Gage, Crime Novelist, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Gage was an advertising professional before his first book was published when he was 66.

name: Gene Wettstone
headline: Gene Wettstone, Record-Setting Gymnastics Coach, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Wettstone led Penn State University to a record nine N.C.A.A. championships in the sport, and also coached the U.S. men’s teams in the 1948 and 1956 Olympic Games.

name: Kongar-ol Ondar
headline: Kongar-ol Ondar, a Master of a Vocal Art, Dies at 51
abstract: Kongar-ol Ondar, a renowned master of Tuvan throat singing, was a superstar in his country and well-respected by musicians worldwide.

name: Charles Varnadore
headline: Charles Varnadore, Whistle-Blower at Lab, Dies at 71
abstract: In the 1990s Mr. Varnadore publicized questionable safety practices at Oak Ridge National Laboratory in Tennessee, which led to stronger laws protecting workers who complain about employers.

name: Paul Szilard
profession: Impresario Of Ballet and Modern Dance
headline: Paul Szilard, 100, Impresario Of Ballet and Modern Dance
abstract: Mr. Szilard’s colorful career in and out of dance included managing tours for the Ailey company.

name: Jean-Claude Suares
headline: Jean-Claude Suares, 71, a Daring Times Op-Ed Artist
abstract: Mr. Suares, the first Op-Ed page art director at The New York Times, began a visual era for editorial illustrations that influenced many other publications.

name: Michael J. Morwood
headline: Michael J. Morwood, Archaeologist Who Helped Find ‘New Human,’ Dies at 62
abstract: In 2003, Dr. Morwood and his team dug up remains of Homo floresiensis, or the little people of Flores who were nicknamed the hobbits, in an Indonesian island cave.

name: Art Donovan
headline: Art Donovan, a Behemoth of Modesty, Dies at 89
abstract: Donovan, a 300-pound tackle on the Baltimore Colts’ championship teams in 1958 and 1959, was known for his self-deprecating modesty.

name: George Duke
headline: George Duke, Keyboardist Who Crossed Genre Boundaries, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Duke started as a jazz pianist and later, at Frank Zappa’s request, took up the synthesizer, the instrument that became his hallmark.

name: Robert Bellah
headline: Robert Bellah, Sociologist of Religion Who Mapped the American Soul, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Bellah was widely credited with helping usher the study of religion — a historically marginalized subject in the social sciences — into the sociological fold.

name: Julius Chambers
headline: Julius Chambers, a Fighter for Civil Rights, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Chambers was a civil rights lawyer who endured firebombings of his house, office and car in winning case after case against racial segregation.

name: Jerry Wolman
headline: Jerry Wolman, Eagles and Flyers Owner, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Wolman, a real estate developer, fulfilled his childhood dream of owning the N.F.L.’s Philadelphia Eagles in 1963, at age 36, and also was a co-founder of the N.H.L.’s Philadelphia Flyers in the 1960s.

name: John Woodward
profession: Leader of British Navy in Falkland Islands War
headline: John Woodward, Leader of British Navy in Falkland Islands War, Dies at 81
abstract: Admiral Woodward, as commander of a Royal Navy battle group in 1982, gave the order to sink the Argentine cruiser General Belgrano.

name: Cosmo Allegretti
headline: Cosmo Allegretti, ‘Captain Kangaroo’ Actor and Puppeteer, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Allegretti commanded puppets like Bunny Rabbit and Mr. Moose and played Dancing Bear and Grandfather Clock on the popular CBS children’s show.

name: Lloyd Moss
headline: Lloyd Moss, 86, WQXR Host and Author
abstract: Mr. Moss, after ad-libbing on the radio, wrote the award-winning children’s book “Zin! Zin! Zin! A Violin” about orchestra instruments.

name: Gail Levin
headline: Gail Levin, Documentary Filmmaker for ‘American Masters,’ Dies at 67
abstract: Ms. Levin’s work included pieces on Marilyn Monroe, James Dean and Jeff Bridges for PBS’s “American Masters” series.

name: Elisabeth Maxwell
headline: Elisabeth Maxwell, Expert on Holocaust, Dies at 92
abstract: After Dr. Maxwell’s life was turned upside down by the death of her husband, Robert Maxwell, in 1991, she focused on being a Holocaust scholar, writer and lecturer.

name: Margaret Pellegrini
headline: Margaret Pellegrini, 89, Munchkin From Land of Oz
abstract: Ms. Pellegrini danced in a flowerpot hat in the classic 1939 film and was a regular at “Oz” events in later years.

name: Karen Black
headline: Karen Black, Versatile Character Actress, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Black, who was nominated for an Academy Award for best supporting actress, later seemed to specialize in horror movies and thrillers.

name: Jack Clement
headline: Jack Clement, Producer and Country Songwriter, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Clement worked with stars like Johnny Cash and Waylon Jennings, and had a long association with Charley Pride.

name: Marilyn King
headline: Marilyn King, Last of Singing Sisters’ Group, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. King was the youngest of the sisters in the family. The King Sisters started as a trio and at one point included six members, all but one of them actual sisters, but for most of their career they were a quartet.

name: Bill Lynch
headline: Bill Lynch, 72, Democratic Strategist in New York, Dies
abstract: Mr. Lynch was known as the “rumpled genius” behind David N. Dinkins’s victory as the first black mayor of New York City in 1989.

name: Regina Resnik
headline: Regina Resnik, Metropolitan Opera Star, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Resnik, a Bronx native who made a mid-career switch from soprano to mezzo-soprano, sang more than 300 performances at the Met.

name: Roy Rubin
headline: Roy Rubin, Who Led Record-Losing 76ers, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Rubin became the coach of the 1972-73 Philadelphia 76ers after a former assistant recommended him. He was fired after a 4-47 start, and the team finished 9-73.

name: Dixie Evans
headline: Dixie Evans, Who Brought ‘Monroe’ to Burlesque Houses, Dies at 86
abstract: In an act that played at burlesque houses across the country, Ms. Evans mimicked the speech, shimmy and look of Marilyn Monroe.

name: Sean Sasser
profession: Was Half of One of TVs First Gay Couples
headline: Sean Sasser, Who Was Half of One of TV’s First Gay Couples, Dies at 44
abstract: Mr. Sasser, a chef whose romance with Pedro Zamora on MTV’s “The Real World” was among the first real-life gay relationships on television, helped publicize issues about AIDS.

name: John Billingham
headline: John Billingham, Seeker of Extraterrestrials, Dies at 83
abstract: As a NASA official in the 1970s, Dr. Billingham helped persuade the federal government to use radio telescopes to scour the universe for evidence of extraterrestrial intelligence.

name: Eydie Gorme
headline: Eydie Gorme, Voice of Sophisticated Pop, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Gorme had a long-running “tux and gown” act with her husband, Steve Lawrence.

name: William P. Clark
profession: Influential Adviser in Reagan White House
headline: William P. Clark, Influential Adviser in Reagan White House, Is Dead at 81
abstract: As one of President Ronald Reagan’s most trusted advisers, Mr. Clark nudged him toward more hard-line positions on military spending, arms control and involvement in Central America.

name: Shirley Herz
profession: Press Agent for Broadway and Beyond
headline: Shirley Herz, Press Agent for Broadway and Beyond, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Herz publicized shows for almost 65 years, among “La Cage aux Folles,” and her client list included dance troupes, TV shows and even the Moscow Circus.

name: Simeon Golar
headline: Simeon Golar, Who Fought for Public Housing, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Golar was the first New York City Housing Authority chairman to have grown up in public housing, which he championed in the face of fierce neighborhood opposition in the early 1970s.

name: Barbara Mertz
headline: Barbara Mertz, Egyptologist and Mystery Writer, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Mertz, who wrote under the pen names Elizabeth Peters and Barbara Michaels, set many of her works in the Middle East.

name: Pauline Maier
headline: Pauline Maier, Historian Who Described Jefferson as ‘Overrated,’ Dies at 75
abstract: In her book “American Scripture: Making the Declaration of Independence,” Professor Maier chipped away at mythology.

name: Joseph M. McLaughlin
headline: Joseph M. McLaughlin, Judge and Fordham Law Dean, Dies at 80
abstract: Judge McLaughlin was known for his erudite rulings and a lightning wit with which he sometimes disarmed lawyers and delighted juries.

name: Jack Germond
profession: Political Reporter of the Old School
headline: Jack Germond, Political Reporter of the Old School, Dies at 85
abstract: A newspaper reporter, syndicated columnist and TV pundit who was one of the “Boys on the Bus” for 10 presidential elections.

name: Tompall Glaser
headline: Tompall Glaser, Country Artist in Outlaw Movement, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Glaser was one of four Nashville performers featured on the 1976 compilation “Wanted! The Outlaws,” the first album in the history of country music to be certified platinum for sales of one million copies.

name: Mark Sutton
headline: Parachutist From Olympics Dies in a Jump
abstract: Mark Sutton, 42, a stuntman who portrayed James Bond in last year’s opening Olympic ceremony, hit a mountainside in the Alps while wingsuit-flying.

name: Lisa Robin Kelly
headline: Lisa Robin Kelly, Actress on ‘That ’70s Show’ Sitcom, Dies at  43
abstract: Ms. Kelly, who played a humorous promiscuous character on the popular Fox TV series, had struggled with substance abuse.

name: Jean Bethke Elshtain
profession: Guiding Light for Policy Makers After 9/11
headline: Jean Bethke Elshtain, a Guiding Light for Policy Makers After 9/11, Dies at 72
abstract: Dr. Elshtain was a philosopher of politics and religion who wrote influentially about good and evil, war and peace, and the moral imperative of American global military engagement.

name: Lewis Kornfeld
profession: Made Radio Shack an Early Player in PCs
headline: Lewis Kornfeld, Made Radio Shack an Early Player in PCs, Dies at 97
abstract: In 1977, with Mr. Kornfeld as president, Radio Shack introduced the TRS-80, one of the first mass-market computers for consumers.

name: Bert Lance
headline: Bert Lance, Carter Adviser, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Lance, a pre-eminent adviser and tennis-playing confidant to Jimmy Carter, was forced to resign as director of the Office of Management and Budget because of accusations that he had personally traded on his ties with the president.

name: Marty Adler
profession: Curator of the Brooklyn Dodgers Legacy
headline: Marty Adler, Curator of the Brooklyn Dodgers’ Legacy, Dies at 76
abstract: Adler, the founder of the Brooklyn Dodgers Hall of Fame, helped keep alive the legacy of Jackie Robinson.

name: Ruth Asawa
headline: Ruth Asawa, an Artist Who Wove Wire, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Asawa learned to draw in an internment camp for Japanese-Americans, then went on to find renown for her wire sculptures.

name: Haji
profession: Actress Featured in Cult Films by Russ Meyer
headline: Haji, an Actress Featured in Cult Films by Russ Meyer, Dies at 67
abstract: Haji played a homicidal go-go dancer in “Faster, Pussycat! Kill! Kill!” and a bartender in “Supervixens,” among other roles.

name: John Hollander
profession: Poet at Ease With Intellectualism and Wit
headline: John Hollander, Poet at Ease With Intellectualism and Wit, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Hollander branched out with ambitious work after making a name for himself with traditional forms.

name: David Howard
headline: David Howard, Revered Teacher of Dancers, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Howard’s school in New York was frequented by the likes of Gelsey Kirkland, Patricia McBride and Mikhail Baryshnikov.

name: Penelope Casas
headline: Penelope Casas, Spanish Food Author, Dies at 70
abstract: The 1985 cookbook by Mrs. Casas was among the first to chronicle for American readers the culinary tradition of tapas bars.

name: Albert Murray
headline: Albert Murray, Scholar Who Saw a Multicolored American Culture, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Murray, whose prose style was influenced by jazz and the blues, wrote about black culture as inextricable from American culture.

name: Lee Thompson Young
headline: Lee Thompson Young, Detective on TV, Dies at 29
abstract: Mr. Young was an actor who played a child star on the Disney Channel show “The Famous Jett Jackson” and a detective on the hit TNT series “Rizzoli & Isles.”

name: Elmore Leonard
headline: A Novelist Who Made Crime an Art, and His Bad Guys ‘Fun’
abstract: Mr. Leonard’s louche characters, deadpan dialogue and immaculate prose style in novels like “Get Shorty” secured his status as a modern master of American genre writing.

name: Mario Richard
headline: Mario Richard, BASE Jumper and Sky Diver, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. Richard was a veteran BASE jumper and the husband of the rock climber Steph Davis who estimated last year that he had performed 2,000 BASE jumps and 7,000 sky dives.

name: Jane Harvey
profession: Jazz Singer With Long and Varied Career
headline: Jane Harvey, 88, Jazz Singer With Long and Varied Career, Dies
abstract: Ms. Harvey, who halted her career several times, recorded with Benny Goodman and Duke Ellington.

name: James Sterling Young
headline: James Sterling Young, Oral Historian, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Young was an award-winning historian of 19th-century American politics.

name: Cedar Walton
headline: Cedar Walton, Pianist and Composer, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Walton often said he preferred the role of accompanist to that of bandleader.

name: Marian McPartland
profession: Jazz Pianist and NPR Radio Staple
headline: Marian McPartland, Jazz Pianist and NPR Radio Staple, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. McPartland, an articulate spokeswoman for music, was on the radio for more than 30 years. She recorded for labels like Savoy and Capitol before forming her own company, Halcyon.

name: Rosalia Mera
headline: Rosalia Mera, Co-Founder of Zara, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Mera was a Spanish entrepreneur who helped start the Zara fashion empire, becoming the world’s richest self-made woman.

name: Sid Bernstein
headline: Sid Bernstein, Who Helped Import the Beatles, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Bernstein was a soft-spoken impresario whose long career included bringing the Beatles to Carnegie Hall in 1964 and Shea Stadium in 1965.

name: C. Gordon Fullerton
headline: C. Gordon Fullerton, Early Space Shuttle Pilot, Dies at 76
abstract: A pilot who tested 130 different types of aircraft for the Air Force and NASA, and flew two shuttle missions, as the commander on the Challenger and one of two pilots on the Columbia.

name: Leslie Land
headline: Leslie Land, a Food Writer Who Liked What Grew Nearby, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Land, with the British horticulturist Roger Phillips, wrote “The 3,000 Mile Garden,” which became a PBS series.

name: Ron Motley
headline: Ron Motley, Who Tackled Big Tobacco, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Motley helped lead litigation in the early 1990s on the health consequences of smoking, leading to the largest civil settlement in American history: $246 billion.

name: Dean Meminger
headline: Dean Meminger, Who Helped Knicks to a Title, Dies at 65
abstract: The speedy point guard and tenacious defender had long battled drug problems.

name: Tom Christian
headline: Tom Christian, Descendant of Bounty Mutineer, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Christian, whose great-great-great-grandfather led the mutiny on the Bounty in 1789 and sought refuge on Pitcairn Island, kept the isle connected to the world.

name: José Sarria
headline: José Sarria, Gay Advocate and Performer, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Sarria was a drag performer and gay rights advocate who many historians contend was the first openly gay person to campaign for public office in the United States.

name: Ted Post
headline: Ted Post, Director for Film and Television, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Post had a long, busy career making episodes of “Gunsmoke” and “Rawhide,” directing Clint Eastwood in two hit films, and winning praise for a Vietnam War movie, “Go Tell the Spartans.”

name: Charles Pollock
headline: Charles Pollock, Designer of Popular Office Chair, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Pollock was an industrial designer whose crowning achievement was an office chair characterized by a single aluminum band that held it together, structurally and visually.

name: Julie Harris
profession: Celebrated Actress of Range and Intensity
headline: Julie Harris, Celebrated Actress of Range and Intensity, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Harris had a lengthy résumé as an actress, with dozens of movie and television credits, including the 1955 film adaptation of John Steinbeck’s novel of brotherly rivalry, “East of Eden.”

name: Muriel Siebert
profession: Determined Trailblazer for Women on Wall Street
headline: Muriel Siebert, a Determined Trailblazer for Women on Wall Street, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Siebert, who cultivated the same brash attitude as Wall Street’s most successful men, donated millions of dollars to help other women get started in finance, and fought the old-boy network all her life.

name: Louisa Jo Killen
headline: Louisa Jo Killen, English Folk Singer, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Killen, a bearded pioneer of the 1950s British folk revival known for songs starring miners and sailors, became Louisa Jo at age 76.

name: Red Burns
headline: Red Burns, ‘Godmother of Silicon Alley,’ Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Burns helped to lead the movement for public access to cable television and started a New York University program to foster Internet wizards.

name: Gilbert Taylor
headline: Gilbert Taylor, Celebrated Cinematographer, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Taylor brought a cinéma vérité sensibility to black-and-white pictures like “Dr. Strangelove,” and also masterminded the bright, clean shots for “Star Wars.”

name: Peter Huttenlocher
headline: Peter Huttenlocher, Explorer of the Brain, Dies at 82
abstract: Dr. Huttenlocher counted synapses, observing how much of the information coming to the brain was discarded as the mind became more efficient.

name: Slawomir Mrozek
headline: Slawomir Mrozek, Leading Polish Playwright, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Mrozek’s plays were periodically banned in Poland for ridiculing the postwar Eastern bloc’s political and social climate. He had plays produced in cities worldwide, including New York.

name: Stephenie McMillan
headline: Stephenie McMillan, Film Set Decorator, Dies at 71
abstract: Ms. McMillan created the look of all eight Harry Potter films and won an Oscar for the 1996 romance “The English Patient.”

name: Anthony Pawson
headline: Anthony Pawson, Biologist in Cell-Protein Breakthrough, Dies at 60
abstract: In 1990, Dr. Pawson and his research team in Toronto identified the SH2 domain, which offered insights about how cells communicate with one another and resolved one of science’s oldest mysteries.

name: Frank Pulli
headline: Frank Pulli, First Umpire to Use Replay, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Pulli spent nearly 30 years as an umpire for Major League Baseball, and he became the first to use instant replay to verify a call in 1999.

name: Sathima Bea Benjamin
headline: Sathima Bea Benjamin, Jazz Singer and Activist, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Benjamin found fame after she left South Africa. She lived in exile in Manhattan for many years and raised money to fight apartheid.

name: Bruce C. Murray
headline: Bruce C. Murray, Who Helped Earth Learn of Mars, Dies at 81
abstract: As director of the Jet Propulsion Laboratory from 1976 to 1982, Dr. Murray faced shrinking budgets as the space agency focused on the emerging shuttle program.

name: Seamus Heaney
profession: Irish Poet of Soil and Strife
headline: Seamus Heaney, Irish Poet of Soil and Strife, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Heaney, a widely celebrated Irish poet who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1995, is recognized as one of the major poets of the 20th century.

name: Matthew Shear
headline: Matthew Shear, Book Publisher, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Shear, the publisher of St. Martin’s Press, helped writers like Janet Evanovich and Augusten Burroughs climb the best-seller lists.

name: David Frost
headline: David Frost, Interviewer Who Got Nixon to Apologize for Watergate, Dies at 74
abstract: A longtime broadcaster, Mr. Frost was best known for incisive interviews with public figures, including talks with former President Richard M. Nixon, which he called the highlight of his career.

name: Lotfi Mansouri
headline: Lotfi Mansouri, 84, Opera Troupe Director, Dies
abstract: Mr. Mansouri, who ran the San Francisco Opera and Canadian Opera Company in Toronto, introduced a system of showing the works’ translations on video screens during performances.

name: Gilmar
headline: Gilmar, Pelé’s Last Line of Defense, Dies at 83
abstract: Gilmar dos Santos Neves, with his teammate Pelé, helped lead Brazil to World Cup titles in 1958 and 1962.

name: Paul Poberezny
headline: Paul Poberezny, Pilot Who Founded Popular Fly-In, Dies at 91
abstract: At 15, Mr. Poberezny flew the first aircraft he ever traveled in and later founded the Experimental Aircraft Organization.

name: Janusz Lewandowski
headline: Janusz Lewandowski, 82, Polish Peace Envoy in Vietnam, Dies
abstract: In Operation Marigold, Mr. Lewandowski, then a diplomat from Poland, was given the task of trying to initiate talks between Washington and Hanoi in 1966.

name: Tommy Morrison
profession: Boxer and Co-Star in Rocky V
headline: Tommy Morrison, Boxer and Co-Star in ‘Rocky V,’ Dies at 44
abstract: Mr. Morrison defeated George Foreman for the heavyweight title and starred as a boxing protégé of Rocky Balboa’s in “Rocky V.”

name: Ronald H. Coase
headline:
Ronald H. Coase, ‘Accidental’ Economist
Who Won a Nobel Prize, Dies at 102
abstract: Professor Coase was a law professor whose papers on why companies work and when government regulation is unnecessary influenced modern economics.

name: Frederik Pohl
headline: Frederik Pohl, Science Fiction Master Who Vaporized Utopias, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Pohl, who grew up in Brooklyn, edited magazines and books before finding renown as a writer. Perhaps the most famous of his novels was “The Space Merchants.”

name: Ray Grebey
headline: Ray Grebey, Negotiator in ’81 Baseball Strike, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Grebey was hired by Major League Baseball in 1978, and some thought he pushed too hard and provoked a strike that could have been avoided.

name: Tatyana I. Zaslavskaya
headline: Tatyana I. Zaslavskaya, Adviser to Gorbachev, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Zaslavskaya, a Russian sociologist who founded a center to study public opinion, influenced Mikhail S. Gorbachev’s economic policies.

name: Martin L. Gross
headline: Martin L. Gross, Critic of Big Government, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Gross, who was embraced by supporters of the Tea Party, took aim at spending and taxation with books like “The Government Racket: Washington Waste From A to Z.”

name: Judith Daniels
headline: Judith Daniels, Editor of Savvy Magazine, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Daniels, who saw a big gap in the magazine industry, was the first to focus on the emerging class of high-earning professional women.

name: William Glasser
headline: William Glasser, 88, Doctor Who Said One Could Choose Happiness, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Glasser, through “choice theory,” posited that people were in much more control of their lives than they realized in solving emotional and mental problems.

name: Zvonko Busic
headline: Zvonko Busic, 67, Croatian Hijacker, Dies
abstract: Mr. Busic was a Croatian nationalist who in 1976 hijacked a Trans World Airlines flight out of La Guardia Airport and planted a bomb beneath Grand Central Terminal that killed a police officer.

name: Johnny Logan
profession: Shortstop for World Champion Milwaukee Braves
headline: Johnny Logan, Shortstop for World Champion Milwaukee Braves, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Logan, a four-time All-Star, helped the Braves win Milwaukee’s only title, a 4-3 World Series victory over the Yankees in 1957.

name: Rochus Misch
headline: Rochus Misch, Bodyguard of Hitler, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Misch was widely described as the last living witness to the Führer’s final days in his underground bunker and remained a devoted admirer of the man he called “the boss.”

name: Stephen Antonakos
headline: Stephen Antonakos, Sculptor of Neon, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Antonakos made illumination an essential component of his work, using electrified neon gas as a painter uses paint.

name: David S. Landes
headline: David S. Landes, Historian and Author, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Professor Landes, a distinguished Harvard scholar of economic history, was preoccupied by the importance of culture in shaping economic and social progress or stagnation.

name: Murray Gershenz
profession: Record Store Owner and Character Actor
headline: Murray Gershenz, Record Store Owner and Character Actor, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Gershenz, a merchant of used music who became an archivist of 300,000 albums, had a late-blooming career in films and television.

name: Jack Beal
headline: Jack Beal, Optimistic New Realist Painter, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Beal made minutely detailed portraits and narrative works, including large murals in the Times Square subway station.

name: Manson Whitlock
headline: Manson Whitlock, Typewriter Repairman, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Whitlock, often described as America’s oldest typewriter repairman, had a shop near Yale and fixed more than 300,000 machines — but never a computer.

name: Paul Scoon
headline: Paul Scoon, Who Invited Grenada Invaders, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Scoon was appointed to the ceremonial post of governor general of Grenada before playing the role of power broker when the United States invaded his Caribbean nation.

name: Cal Worthington
headline: Cal Worthington, Car Dealer With Manic Ads, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Worthington owned a string of car dealerships and ran dozens of outlandish commercials daily on California television for more than half a century.

name: Kenneth Wallis
profession: British Pilot of Bombers and Odder Flying Machines
headline: Kenneth Wallis, British Pilot of Bombers and Odder Flying Machines, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Wallis was an enthusiastic maker, flier and promoter of autogyros, buglike vehicles similar to helicopters.

name: Zelmo Beaty
headline: Zelmo Beaty, All-Star Center in Pro Basketball, Dies at 73
abstract: Beaty was probably about 6 feet 8 inches, but he excelled as a scorer and as a rebounder in his battles with bigger opponents.

name: Donal O’Brien
headline: Donal O’Brien, Audubon Leader, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. O’Brien, who served as the Rockefeller family’s lawyer for five decades, was a member of the National Audubon Society’s board for 25 years and its chairman for 15.

name: Alvin Eisenman
headline: Alvin Eisenman, Graphic Design Educator, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Eisenman enlisted Walker Evans as an instructor and persuaded Steve Jobs to donate early-generation computers to the program.

name: Saul Landau
profession: Maker of Films With Leftist Edge
headline: Saul Landau, Maker of Films With Leftist Edge, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Landau’s passion for asking what he called “the most intrusive questions” yielded penetrating cinematic profiles of leaders like Fidel Castro and Salvador Allende.

name: Fred Katz
headline: Fred Katz, Who Married Cello to Jazz, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Katz was a classically trained cellist who quite by accident helped elevate his instrument to unlikely stardom in jazz.

name: Godfrey Sperling
headline: Godfrey Sperling, Who Made Eggs for Press, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Sperling, a journalist with The Christian Science Monitor, organized breakfast meetings that became a Washington institution, bringing newsmakers together with news reporters.

name: Ray Dolby
profession: Put Moviegoers in the Middle of It
headline: Ray Dolby, Who Put Moviegoers in the Middle of It, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Dr. Dolby, who founded Dolby Laboratories, transformed cinema and home entertainment with the development of Dolby digital surround sound.

name: Sunila Abeysekera
headline: Sunila Abeysekera, Sri Lankan Human Rights Activist, Dies at 61
abstract: Ms. Abeysekera ran the Inform Human Rights Documentation Center, bringing attention to the violence in Sri Lanka as well as to women’s rights issues throughout South Asia.

name: Frank Tripucka
headline: Frank Tripucka, 85, a Star at Notre Dame, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Tripucka’s seven children were all athletes; his son Kelly was an all-American basketball player for the Fighting Irish.

name: Robert F. Capon
headline: Robert F. Capon, Who Wrote of God and Food, Dies at 87
abstract: The author of “The Supper of the Lamb: A Culinary Reflection” was the vicar of an Episcopal church on Long Island until his divorce.

name: Stephen Crohn
headline: Stephen Crohn, Who Furthered AIDS Study, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Crohn, a New York artist and editor who had a resistance to the virus that causes AIDS, helped scientists learn more about the disease simply by staying alive.

name: Marshall Berman
headline: Marshall Berman, Philosopher Who Praised Marx and Modernism, Dies at 72
abstract: In “All That Is Solid Melts Into Air,” Dr. Berman, an enthusiastic New Yorker, critiqued modernity.

name: Dick Newick
headline: Dick Newick, Sailboat Design Visionary, Dies at  87
abstract: Mr. Newick designed boats with two and three hulls that would beat conventional yachts in major races. The AC72 catamarans competing for the America’s Cup descend from concepts he helped develop.

name: Lansing Lamont
profession: Journalist and Historian of Atomic Bomb
headline: Lansing Lamont, Journalist and Historian of Atomic Bomb, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Lamont, who wrote and edited several other books, was a longtime correspondent for Time.

name: Lee Tanner
headline: Lee Tanner, Jazz Performance Portraitist, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Tanner’s often ethereal images, which graced album covers, magazines, exhibitions and books, included subjects like Duke Ellington, Dizzy Gillespie and Thelonious Monk.

name: Shalom Yoran
headline: Shalom Yoran, Jewish Resistance Fighter, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Yoran and his brother escaped their occupied town in Poland, days before their parents were killed, to wreak vengeance on the Nazis.

name: Chin Peng
headline: Chin Peng, Malaysian Rebel, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Peng pitted himself against Japanese invaders, British colonialists and his own government in a bloody struggle for an independent Communist country.

name: Reiko Douglas
headline: Reiko Douglas, Entertainer on TV Talk Shows, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Douglas was a Japanese-born entertainer who became a popular guest on American talk shows in the 1960s and ’70s even though she appeared to speak little English.

name: Sheldon Hackney
headline: Sheldon Hackney, Leader in Humanities, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Hackney was an educator and chairman of the National Endowment for the Humanities who organized  “national conversations” during the culturally fractious 1990s.

name: Rick Casares
headline: Rick Casares, 82, a Bear Who Got Yards With Grit, Dies
abstract: Casares led the National Football League in rushing in 1956 and is third on the Chicago Bears’ career rushing list.

name: Eiji Toyoda
profession: Promoter of the Toyota Way and Engineer of Its Growth
headline: Eiji Toyoda, Promoter of the Toyota Way and Engineer of Its Growth, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Toyoda, the nephew of the Toyota group’s founder, was the architect of the company’s “lean manufacturing” method, which helped turn the automaker into a global powerhouse.

name: Marcel Reich-Ranicki
headline: Marcel Reich-Ranicki, Literary Critic, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Mr. Reich-Ranicki, a Polish Jew who grew up in Berlin, became a powerful cultural figure in postwar Germany as a literary critic and a television talk show host.

name: Joseph E. Granville
headline: Joseph E. Granville, Stock Market Predictor, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Granville was a famous market forecaster who made his own fortune in the less risky newsletter business.

name: Stephen E. Malawista
headline: Stephen E. Malawista, Lyme Disease Researcher, Dies at 79
abstract: Dr. Malawista and his team were credited with defining an ailment that was causing distress in Connecticut.

name: Albert Taylor
headline: Albert Taylor, Tracker Whose Work Helped Children, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Taylor, a former Border Patrol agent, was regarded as a legend in the art of tracking people in the wild and helped develop a program to teach children how to increase their chances of being found.

name: Ken Norton
headline: Ken Norton, a Championship Fighter Who Broke Ali’s Jaw, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Norton fought three memorable fights with Muhammad Ali, winning once, and went on to become the World Boxing Council heavyweight champion.

name: Jackie Lomax
profession: British Rock Singer Recorded With Members of Beatles
headline: Jackie Lomax Dies at 69; British Rock Singer Recorded With Members of Beatles
abstract: Mr. Lomax, who played with the Undertakers and the Lomax Alliance, never made it as big as his fellow Liverpool rockers, the Beatles, did.

name: Hiroshi Yamauchi
headline: Hiroshi Yamauchi, Who Steered Nintendo to Dominance, Dies at 85
abstract: At 22, Mr. Yamauchi became president of his family’s playing-card company and later steered it into the growing game business, developing hits like Donkey Kong and the original Mario Brothers franchises.

name: Candace Pert
headline: Candace Pert, 67, Explorer of the Brain, Dies
abstract: As a Johns Hopkins graduate student, Dr. Pert helped discover a key to brain chemistry. She went on to become a neuroscientist and a major proponent of alternative medicine.

name: D. J. R. Bruckner
headline: D. J. R. Bruckner, Columnist and Critic, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Bruckner, who was a longtime editor for The New York Times Book Review, landed on Nixon’s enemies list over his syndicated columns for The Los Angeles Times.

name: Peter K. Leisure
headline: Peter K. Leisure, Judge Who Oversaw Football Antitrust Case, Dies at 84
abstract: Judge Leisure also presided over a Gambino crime family trial and ordered the release of secret grand jury testimony in the investigation of Alger Hiss, which included testimony by Richard M. Nixon.

name: Philip Berg
headline: Rabbi Philip Berg, Who Updated Jewish Mysticism, Dies at 86
abstract: Rabbi Berg’s Kabbalah Center International attracted celebrities like Madonna and Britney Spears but also drew criticism over spiritual and financial matters.

name: Bonita Spence
headline: Bonita Spence, a Referee Who Had a Cheering Section, Dies at 52
abstract: Well known in the world of basketball, Ms. Spence also worked as an investigator in the public defender’s office in Newark, N.J.

name: Marvin Rainwater
headline: Marvin Rainwater, 88, Twangy Country Singer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Rainwater was a classically trained pianist who turned to country music, then wrote and recorded the hits “Gonna Find Me a Bluebird” and “Whole Lotta Woman.”

name: John Kennell
headline: John Kennell, Advocate of Infant Bonding, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Kennell’s research in the 1960s helped end a common practice of keeping newly born infants and their parents apart in the first hours of life.

name: Robert McCabe Jr.
headline: Robert McCabe Jr., a Kidney Donation Specialist, Dies at 88
abstract: After having a donor kidney flown to Moscow in 1979 when no domestic recipients were found, Dr. McCabe used the episode to improve the transplant donor system.

name: Ruth Patrick
profession: Pioneer in Science and Pollution Control Efforts
headline: Ruth Patrick, a Pioneer in Science and Pollution Control Efforts, Is Dead at 105
abstract: Dr. Patrick, one of the country’s leading experts in the study of freshwater ecosystems, or limnology, was an innovator of a number of environmental practices and principles.

name: Carolyn Cassady
headline: Carolyn Cassady, Beat Writer and Muse, Dies at 90
