abstract: Ms. Cassady was the former wife of Neal Cassady and a character in Jack Kerouac’s “On the Road.” She later chronicled her life in the Beat Generation.

name: Christopher Koch
profession: Writer of Year of Living Dangerously
headline: Christopher Koch, Writer of ‘Year of Living Dangerously,’ Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Koch was widely regarded as one of Australia’s finest novelists. His best known book became even better known as a film.

name: David Hubel
headline: David Hubel, Nobel-Winning Scientist, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Hubel was half of a team that studied how the brain processed information from the retina. The findings led to a better understanding of how to treat certain birth defects.

name: Paul Dietzel
headline: Paul Dietzel, Coach Who Led L.S.U. to Its First National Title, Dies at 89
abstract: In Louisiana State’s 1958 championship season, Dietzel  used a platoon system famous for a scrappy defensive unit known as the Chinese Bandits.

name: Luciano Vincenzoni
headline: Luciano Vincenzoni, Screenwriter, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Vincenzoni, who worked with prominent filmmakers like Billy Wilder and Dino De Laurentiis, was most associated with “For a Few Dollars More” and “The Good, the Bad and the Ugly.”

name: Jane Connell
headline: Jane Connell, Agnes Gooch of ‘Mame,’ Is Dead at 87
abstract: Ms. Connell appeared in musicals, TV and movies, but was best known for her Agnes Gooch in the musical “Mame,” on Broadway and on screen.

name: Oscar Espinosa Chepe
headline: Oscar Espinosa Chepe, Cuban Economist and Castro Critic, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Espinosa Chepe, who advocated the limited restoration of capitalist principles, remained in Cuba despite enduring harassment and imprisonment.

name: Marta Heflin
headline: Marta Heflin, Actor, Dies at 68; Waif Seen in Altman Films
abstract: Ms. Heflin appeared in New York stage musicals like “Fiddler on the Roof” and “Jesus Christ Superstar,” and later in a string of Robert Altman movies that capitalized on her waifishness.

name: James van Sweden
profession: His Designs Urged Lawns to Grow
headline: James van Sweden Dies at 78; His Designs Urged Lawns to Grow
abstract: Mr. van Sweden helped lead a revolt against the well-manicured lawn, creating naturalistic, colorful gardens inspired by master painters.

name: Gates Brown
headline: Gates Brown, Tigers’ Clutch Pinch-Hitter, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Mr. Brown hit .370, including .450 as a pinch-hitter, to help lead Detroit to the World Series in 1968.

name: Álvaro Mutis
headline: Álvaro Mutis, Novelist Who Created a Rambling, Ruminative Soul, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Mutis’s best-known character, Maqroll, wandered the world unwillingly, but always with a book.

name: Robert Barnard
profession: Award-Winning Writer of British Crime Cozies
headline: Robert Barnard, Award-Winning Writer of British Crime ‘Cozies,’ Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Barnard, the author of 40 novels, was an accomplished creator of the “cozy” genre, murder mysteries that feature picturesque settings, colorful characters and minimal violence.

name: Jean Anyon
headline: Jean Anyon Dies at 72; Wrote ‘Ghetto Schooling’
abstract: Professor Anyon, who taught at the City University of New York, asserted that the problems that plague urban schools are inextricably linked to larger social ills.

name: Marcella Hazan
headline: Marcella Hazan, Author Who Changed the Way Americans Cook Italian Food, Dies at 89
abstract: Even people who have never heard of Mrs. Hazan cook and shop differently because of her, and the six cookbooks she wrote.

name: James Vaught
headline: James Vaught, Who Led Iran Hostage Mission, Dies at 86
abstract: General Vaught, a combat veteran of the Korean and Vietnam Wars, was the commander of the Carter administration’s failed 1980 mission to free 50 hostages held in Iran.

name: James Street
headline: James Street Dies at 65; Led Texas to Title
abstract: Street became an instant legend for fueling a 15-14 victory over Arkansas in 1969, which gave Texas the national crown, as declared by President Richard M. Nixon.

name: Bob Kurland
headline: Bob Kurland, 88, Pioneer for Basketball’s Big Men, Dies
abstract: Kurland, a three-time all-American who was elected to the Basketball Hall of Fame, was known for his athleticism in an era when tall players were considered oddities.

name: L. C. Greenwood
headline: L. C. Greenwood, Member of ‘Steel Curtain,’ Dies at 67
abstract: Greenwood, a left defensive end who was a master of the quarterback sack, helped lead the Pittsburgh Steelers to four Super Bowl victories in the 1970s.

name: Patricia Blair
headline: Patricia Blair Dies at 80; Starred in Television’s  ‘Daniel Boone’
abstract: Ms. Blair played the hotel owner Lou Mallory in the 1960s television western “The Rifleman” and Rebecca Boone, Daniel’s wife, in the NBC series “Daniel Boone.”

name: Harold M. Agnew
profession: Physicist Present at Birth of the Nuclear Age
headline: Harold M. Agnew, Physicist Present at Birth of the Nuclear Age, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Agnew, who helped build the world’s first reactor and atomic bombs, flew on the first atomic strike against Japan and filmed the mushroom cloud.

name: Israel Gutman
headline: Israel Gutman, Who Survived and Documented Holocaust, Dies at 90
abstract: Professor Gutman took part in the Warsaw ghetto uprising, survived three Nazi concentration camps and wrote about the Jews of Poland, the Jewish resistance and Auschwitz.

name: Arnold Burns
headline: Arnold Burns, Who Left Justice Dept. in Protest, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Burns, a top Justice Department official under President Ronald Reagan, resigned over what he and others viewed as improper acts by Attorney General Edwin Meese III.

name: Tom Clancy
headline: Tom Clancy, Best-Selling Master of Military Thrillers, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Clancy’s books were successfully transformed into blockbuster Hollywood films, including “Patriot Games,” “The Hunt for Red October” and “Clear and Present Danger.”

name: Lee Thornton
headline: Lee Thornton, Ex-White House Reporter, Dies at 71
abstract: The first black woman to cover the White House for CBS News, Ms. Thornton also was a co-host of “All Things Considered” on NPR, a news program producer for CNN and a teacher of journalism.

name: Ruth Maleczech
headline: Ruth Maleczech, Beacon of Stage Avant-Garde, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Maleczech, a fearless performer and director, was a founder of the experimental theater troupe Mabou Mines.

name: Albert D. Wheelon
headline: Albert D. Wheelon, Architect of Aerial Spying, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Wheelon’s work on satellites for the C.I.A. in the 1960s helped lay the foundation for a vast American arsenal of aerial surveillance systems.

name: Leonard Kerpelman
headline: Leonard Kerpelman, Who Led School Prayer Case, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Kerpelman successfully argued a landmark Supreme Court case in 1963 that led to a ban on state-supported prayer in public schools.

name: Elvin R. Heiberg III
headline: Elvin R. Heiberg III, General Who Took Blame for Hurricane Katrina Failures, Dies at 81
abstract: General Heiberg, as head of the Army Corps of Engineers, regretted his decision to stop fighting for barriers to protect New Orleans.

name: Mario Montez
headline: Mario Montez, a Warhol Glamour Avatar, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Montez was considered Andy Warhol’s first drag “superstar” and became a fixture in his films.

name: Sergei Belov
headline: Sergei Belov, Star Guard Who Led Soviet Upset of U.S., Dies at 69
abstract: A player called the Jerry West of Russia, Belov scored 20 points in the Soviets’ 51-50 victory over the United States in the 1972 Summer Games in Munich.

name: Vo Nguyen Giap
headline: Gen. Vo Nguyen Giap, Who Ousted U.S. From Vietnam, Is Dead
abstract: General Giap, whose victory at Dien Bien Phu forced France from Vietnam, later waged a long battle with the United States military that eventually sapped America’s political will to fight.

name: Lawrence Goodwyn
headline: Lawrence Goodwyn, Historian of Populism, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Goodwyn’s experience building cross-racial political coalitions in the 1960s led him to write an authoritative history of the rise of American populism in the 19th century.

name: Herman Wallace
headline: Herman Wallace, Freed After 41 Years in Solitary, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Wallace had only days earlier been released by a judge, who ruled that his indictment in the killing of a prison guard had been unconstitutional.

name: Bill Eppridge
headline: Bill Eppridge, Who Captured Powerful ’60s Images, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Eppridge made his most enduring mark with a historic image of a mortally wounded Senator Robert F. Kennedy lying on the floor of a Los Angeles hotel in June 1968.

name: Sidney Lanier
headline: Sidney Lanier, 90, Experimental Stage Producer, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Lanier, then an Episcopal priest, made his church a home for the American Place Theater in 1963.

name: Nicholas Oresko
profession: Hero of the Battle of the Bulge
headline: Nicholas Oresko, 96, a Hero of the Battle of the Bulge, Dies
abstract: Mr. Oresko single-handedly wiped out two machine-gun positions at the Battle of the Bulge in 1945, storming the hill alone when his platoon would not budge.

name: Abraham Nemeth
profession: Creator of a Braille Code for Math
headline: Abraham Nemeth, Creator of a Braille Code for Math, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Told that blind people could not do math, Dr. Nemeth developed a customized code that even captured the complexities of differential calculus.

name: A. C. Lyles
headline: A. C. Lyles, Prolific Producer of Westerns, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Lyles rose from the mailroom to a lucrative niche at Paramount Pictures, employing underused stars in profitable low-budget westerns.

name: Ovadia Yosef
profession: Spiritual Leader of Israels Sephardic Jews
headline: Rabbi Ovadia Yosef, Spiritual Leader of Israel’s Sephardic Jews, Dies at 93
abstract: Rabbi Yosef was a fiery figure in Israeli politics who, as the leader of the Shas Party, fought for the interests of Jews of North African and Middle Eastern origin.

name: Ruth Benerito
headline: Ruth Benerito, Who Made Cotton Cloth Behave, Dies at 97
abstract: Dr. Benerito, long affiliated with the United States Department of Agriculture, helped perfect modern wrinkle-free cotton in work that she and her colleagues began in the late 1950s.

name: Patrice Chéreau
headline: Patrice Chéreau, Opera, Stage and Film Director, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Chéreau’s iconoclastic theater, opera and film productions sometimes offered broad social critiques that made them both deeply provocative and widely influential.

name: Robert C. Stebbins
profession: Chronicler of Western Reptiles and Amphibians
headline: Robert C. Stebbins, Chronicler of Western Reptiles and Amphibians, Dies at 98
abstract: Professor Stebbins’s 1966 field guide — written in longhand and typed by his wife, Annarose — is considered an indispensable tool in a herpetologist’s field pack.

name: Ralph A. Dungan
headline: Ralph A. Dungan, Aide in Kennedy White House, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Dungan, who specialized in Latin American affairs as a presidential aide, later increased the size and prestige of New Jersey’s higher education system.

name: Stanley Kauffmann
profession: Spent a Half-Century at the Movies
headline: Stanley Kauffmann, Critic, Dies at 97; Spent a Half-Century at the Movies
abstract: Mr. Kauffmann’s reflective movie reviews appeared for 55 years in The New Republic, until his last months.

name: Andy Pafko
headline: Andy Pafko, Who Watched Thomson’s Shot, Dies at 92
abstract: Pafko, whose career spanned 17 seasons, was playing left field for Brooklyn in the Polo Grounds in 1951 when Bobby Thomson’s ninth-inning home run lifted the New York Giants to the National League pennant.

name: Paul Desmarais
headline: Paul Desmarais, Canadian Magnate, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Desmarais transformed a bankrupt bus line in Canada into an international conglomerate.

name: Wilfried Martens
headline: Wilfried Martens, Belgian Statesman, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Martens, a longtime prime minister, is credited with helping to keep together his linguistically divided country.

name: Scott Carpenter
profession: One of the Original Seven Astronauts
headline: Scott Carpenter, One of the Original Seven Astronauts, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Carpenter’s flight into space was in May 1962. Before the first mission to orbit the Earth, in February that same year, he famously told another astronaut, “Godspeed, John Glenn.”

name: Imero Fiorentino
headline: Imero Fiorentino, Lighting Designer Who Mastered Television, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Fiorentino had a major role in some of the biggest events in TV history, including three Kennedy-Nixon debates.

name: Erich Priebke
headline: Erich Priebke, Nazi Who Carried Out Massacre of 335 Italians, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Priebke, who was under house arrest in Rome, helped organize the execution of 335 men and boys at the Ardeatine Caves in 1944.

name: James A. Emanuel
headline: James A. Emanuel, Poet Who Wrote of Racism, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Emanuel, a poet, educator and critic frustrated by racism in the United States, moved to France permanently after the death of his only child.

name: Donald Cabana
headline: Donald Cabana, Warden Who Loathed Death Penalty, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Cabana, who worked in corrections for more than 25 years, argued that capital punishment was ineffectual, expensive and inhumane.

name: Oscar Hijuelos
profession: Won Pulitzer for Tale of Cuban-American Life
headline: Oscar Hijuelos, Who Won Pulitzer for Tale of Cuban-American Life, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Hijuelos’s 1989 book, “The Mambo Kings Play Songs of Love,” was his best-known work. His characters faced the conundrums of assimilation while holding on to an ethnic and national identity.

name: Chuck Smith
headline: Chuck Smith, Minister Who Preached to Flower Children, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Smith, a Southern California minister, preached fire-and-brimstone theology to Jesus Movement hippies.

name: Tommy Scott
profession: Country Singer With a Traveling Medicine Show
headline: Tommy Scott, Country Singer With a Traveling Medicine Show, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Scott, who wrote country and bluegrass hits, sang and performed comedy in a traveling medicine show long after such productions had become a rarity.

name: Mark B. Read
headline: Mark B. Read, Criminal Turned Author, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Read, known as Chopper, based top-selling books and stand-up performance on his violent and varied life of crime.

name: Kumar Pallana
headline: Kumar Pallana, Who Went From Yoga to Film, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Pallana, who spent decades on the vaudeville circuit as a plate spinner and was a Texas yoga instructor,  became a sought-after character actor  in his late 70s in films by Wes Anderson, Steven Spielberg and others.

name: Hans Riegel
headline: Hans Riegel, Marketer of Gummi Bears, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Riegel made the teddy bear-shaped gelatin sweets known as gummi bears a global favorite, and Haribo, his family-owned company, into an internationally recognized brand.

name: Maxine Powell
headline: Maxine Powell, Motown’s Maven of Style, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Powell was the director of the label’s in-house finishing school in the 1960s and was considered in no small part responsible for its early success.

name: Larry Benoit
headline: Larry Benoit, ‘Babe Ruth for Hunters,’ Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Benoit tracked whitetail deer through northern New England and southern Canada for more than seven decades and became one of the nation’s most revered deer hunters.

name: Bruno Metsu
headline: Bruno Metsu, 59, Dies; Led Senegal at World Cup
abstract: Metsu, a Frenchman, was a midfielder on European teams for nearly two decades, but he achieved his biggest success working in Africa.

name: John Grange
headline: Rev. John Grange, Who Welcomed Bronx’s Latinos, Dies at 73
abstract: Father Grange helped rebuild the impoverished South Bronx parish where he was raised into a more hospitable place for Hispanic immigrants in New York City.

name: William F. Niehous
headline: William F. Niehous, Survivor of Abduction in Venezuela, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Niehous, an American businessman thought dead after his 1976 abduction in Venezuela, was rescued more than three years later and went on to become Owens-Illinois’s vice president for technology.

name: Thomas Foley
headline: Thomas Foley, House Speaker, Dies at 84; Democrat Urged Parties to Collaborate
abstract: Mr. Foley, a Democrat from Washington State, became speaker in June 1989 and urged “our friends on the Republican side to come together and put away bitterness and division and hostility.”

name: Roger Richman
headline: Roger Richman, 69, Dies; Lobbied for Stars’ Heirs
abstract: Mr. Richman is widely credited with helping to invent a multimillion-dollar industry built on licensing the rights to images of dead celebrities.

name: Anthony Hinds
headline: Anthony Hinds, Who Scared British Moviegoers, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Hinds revived Hammer Films after World War II with monsters and werewolves, bankable stars and plenty of sex and gore.

name: Gloria Lynne
profession: Singer of I Wish You Love
headline: Gloria Lynne, Singer of ‘I Wish You Love,’ Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Lynne had a long career, performing on more than 25 albums, but fell on hard times.

name: Ralph Cook
headline: Ralph Cook, a Pioneer of Off Off Broadway, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Cook had a conversation with a co-worker named Sam Shepard at a West Village club in 1964, and a theater career was born.

name: Bum Phillips
headline: Bum Phillips, Homespun Coach Behind Oilers’ Rise, Dies at 90
abstract: Phillips took over a downtrodden Houston team and took it to two consecutive American Football Conference championship games.

name: Jamalul Kiram III
headline: Jamalul Kiram III, Self-Proclaimed Sultan, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Kiram led a quixotic military effort to regain part of the island of Borneo for his family this year, proclaiming: “I’m the poorest sultan in the world.”

name: Antonia Brenner
headline: Antonia Brenner, ‘Prison Angel’ Who Took Inmates Under Her Wing, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Ms. Brenner left a comfortable life in Beverly Hills to minister to inmates in a notorious Mexican prison, eventually becoming a nun.

name: Bud Adams
headline: Bud Adams, Founding Owner of N.F.L.’s Titans, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Adams, son of a prominent oil executive, helped start the American Football League and founded the Houston Oilers, which he moved to Tennessee in 1997.

name: Lawrence R. Klein
headline: Lawrence R. Klein, Economic Theorist, Dies at 93
abstract: Professor Klein was widely regarded for his statistical models used to predict global economic trends, for which he was awarded the 1980 Nobel in economic science.

name: Lou Scheimer
headline: Lou Scheimer, Whose Cartoon Studio Entertained Generation X, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Scheimer’s company, Filmation, produced “Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids,” “The Archie Show” and “He-Man and the Masters of the Universe,” among other cartoon series.

name: Don James
headline: Don James, Longtime Washington Huskies Football Coach, Dies at 80
abstract: During his 18-season tenure as the coach, James, known as the Dawgfather, led Washington to 10 bowl victories, 6 conference titles and a share of the 1991 national championship with Miami.

name: Paul Dickstein
profession: Kochs Budget Chief in New York City
headline: Paul Dickstein, Koch’s Budget Chief in New York City, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Dickstein enforced fiscal discipline during the administration of former Mayor Edward I. Koch. He acknowledged that he was the anointed voice of doom as the city’s budget director.

name: Ronald Shannon Jackson
headline: Ronald Shannon Jackson, Composer and Avant-Garde Drummer, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Jackson, known for his muscular style, led the band Decoding Society.

name: Bill Mazer
headline: Bill Mazer, Sports Fixture in New York, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Mazer, who spent more than 60 years in broadcasting, earned the nickname “The Amazin’ ” for his encyclopedic recall of sports facts.

name: Butch Warren
headline: Butch Warren, 74, Prominent Jazz Bassist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Warren performed and recorded with Thelonious Monk, Herbie Hancock and others before his career was derailed by mental illness and substance abuse.

name: Noel Harrison
profession: Actor and Singer of Windmills of Your Mind
headline: Noel Harrison, Actor and Singer of ‘Windmills of Your Mind,’ Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Harrison was best known for his role on “The Girl From U.N.C.L.E.” and his rendition of the song “The Windmills of Your Mind” for the soundtrack of “The Thomas Crown Affair.”

name: Allan Stanley
profession: Helped Maple Leafs Win 4 N.H.L. Titles
headline: Allan Stanley, 87, Dies; Helped Maple Leafs Win 4 N.H.L. Titles
abstract: Stanley, who played 21 seasons and was noted for a lumbering skating style, won four Stanley Cups with Toronto in the 1960s, including the team’s last championship, in 1967.

name: Anthony Caro
profession: Followed Sculpture on a Path to Abstraction
headline: Anthony Caro, Who Followed Sculpture on a ‘Path to Abstraction,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Caro drew praise from art aficionados and critics in Britain and the United States for his brightly colored, horizontal assemblages of welded steel.

name: Bob Greene
headline: Bob Greene, Jazz Pianist, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Greene’s love of the jazz legend Jelly Roll Morton’s music was such that he left his writing career to perform the Jelly Roll canon.

name: Bill Sharman
headline: Bill Sharman, Two-Time Basketball Hall of Famer, Dies at 87
abstract: A guard for the Boston Celtics in the 1950s, Sharman went on to lead the Lakers to their first N.B.A. title in Los Angeles, in 1971-72, and is credited with introducing the morning shootaround.

name: Paul Reichmann
profession: Helped Develop the World Financial Center
headline: Paul Reichmann, Who Helped Develop the World Financial Center, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Reichmann took enormous business risks, made and lost billions of dollars and built extensively in Toronto, New York and London.

name: Deborah Turbeville
headline: Deborah Turbeville, Fashion Photographer, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Turbeville took fashion photography from sedate to shocking, with stylized imagery steeped in decay that were commentaries all their own.

name: Mary Finch Hoyt
headline: Mary Finch Hoyt, Aide to Rosalynn Carter, Dies at 89
abstract: Before serving as Rosalynn Carter’s press secretary, Mrs. Hoyt worked on several Democratic presidential campaigns.

name: Sid Yudain
headline: Sid Yudain, 90, Dies; Created Congress’s Community Newspaper
abstract: Mr. Yudain created what he called a community newspaper for “the most important community in the world, probably.”

name: Jovanka Broz
headline: Jovanka Broz, Tito’s Widow, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Ms. Broz was a peasant girl who married Josip Broz Tito, Yugoslavia’s supreme leader, and became a glamorous symbol of Yugoslav unity: she was an ethnic Serb; he, a Croat.

name: Hans Ephraimson-Abt
headline: Hans Ephraimson-Abt, Air-Crash Victims’ Crusader, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Ephraimson-Abt became an internationally known advocate after the death of his daughter on Korean Air Lines Flight 007, which was shot down by Soviet fighter planes in 1983.

name: Hal Needham
profession: Stuntman and Director of Action Films
headline: Hal Needham, Stuntman and Director of Action Films, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Needham performed and designed stunts in many television episodes and movies before directing “Smokey and the Bandit,” “The Cannonball Run” and other films.

name: Lou Reed
profession: Lyrical Vision Helped Shape Rock n Roll
headline: Outsider Whose Dark, Lyrical Vision Helped Shape Rock ’n’ Roll
abstract: Mr. Reed was a singer, songwriter and guitarist whose work with the Velvet Underground in the 1960s had an impact on generations of rock musicians.

name: Arthur C. Danto
headline: Arthur C. Danto, a Philosopher of Art, Is Dead at 89
abstract: An encounter with Andy Warhol’s “Brillo Box” inspired Mr. Danto to link the concepts of art and meaning.

name: Robinson Risner
headline: Robinson Risner, Ace Fighter Pilot, Dies at 88
abstract: Brig. Gen. Robinson Risner shot down eight MIG-15 fighters during the Korean War and was held captive at the “Hanoi Hilton” for seven and a half years.

name: Marcia Wallace
headline: Marcia Wallace, Comic Actress on ‘The Simpsons,’ Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Wallace was a bubbly comic actress who greeted doctors and group-therapy patients on “The Bob Newhart Show” and was the Emmy Award-winning voice of Edna Krabappel on “The Simpsons.”

name: William H. Sullivan
profession: U.S. Ambassador to Volatile Laos and Iran
headline: William H. Sullivan, U.S. Ambassador to Volatile Laos and Iran, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Sullivan oversaw a secret bombing campaign in Laos and was the last United States ambassador to Iran before the 1979 hostage crisis.

name: William C. Lowe
profession: Oversaw the Birth of  IBMs PC
headline: William C. Lowe, Who Oversaw the Birth of  IBM’s PC, Dies at 72
abstract: In 1980, Mr. Lowe persuaded the company to let him form a team that would create the IBM Personal Computer with uncharacteristic speed.

name: Tadeusz Mazowiecki
headline: Tadeusz Mazowiecki, Ex-Premier of Poland, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Mazowiecki helped form the Solidarity trade union movement and became the first non-Communist to head an Eastern bloc nation since the late 1940s.

name: Ike Skelton
headline: Ike Skelton, Former Congressman From Missouri, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Skelton, a 17-term Democrat, was chairman of the House Armed Services Committee.

name: Augusto Odone
headline: Augusto Odone, Father Behind ‘Lorenzo’s Oil,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Odone, who had no medical training, helped concoct an experimental medicine that extended the life of his son and inspired a Hollywood film.

name: Lawrence G. Foster
profession: Helped Lead Tylenol Out of Cyanide Crisis
headline: Lawrence G. Foster Dies at 88; Helped Lead Tylenol Out of Cyanide Crisis
abstract: Mr. Foster, the former vice president of public relations at Johnson & Johnson, helped formulate the company’s response to the multiple deaths related to cyanide-laced capsules of Tylenol.

name: Manna Dey
profession: Voice of Many a Bollywood Star
headline: Manna Dey, 94, the Voice of Many a Bollywood Star, Dies
abstract: Mr. Dey was an acclaimed playback singer for Bengali as well as Bollywood films, but like most Bollywood singers, he was not seen onscreen.

name: Johnny Kucks
headline: Johnny Kucks, Who Pitched Yanks to Title, Dies at 81
abstract: Kucks had a mostly undistinguished six-season career in baseball, except when he helped the Yankees clinch the seventh game of the 1956 World Series with a shut out of the Brooklyn Dodgers.

name: Robert Rheault
profession: Green Beret Ensnared in Vietnam Murder Case
headline: Robert Rheault, Green Beret Ensnared in Vietnam Murder Case, Dies at 87
abstract: Colonel Rheault inspired two disparate Vietnam-related narratives: Brando’s Kurtz character in “Apocalypse Now” and Daniel Ellsberg’s leak of the Pentagon Papers.

name: Allan Block
profession: Sandal Shop Was Folk Music Hub
headline: Allan Block, Whose Sandal Shop Was Folk Music Hub, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Block helped popularize open-toed footwear, and his store in Greenwich Village drew musicians like Doc Watson and Bob Dylan during the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Srdja Popovic
headline: Srdja Popovic, 76, Serbian Champion of Rights, Dies
abstract: Mr. Popovic was a Serbian lawyer and celebrated human rights advocate who pressed for reform and free speech for five decades.

name: Gérard de Villiers
headline: Gérard de Villiers, 83, French Spy Writer, Dies
abstract: Mr. de Villiers was a French popular novelist whose long-running spy-thriller series, S.A.S., sold more than 100 million copies.

name: Frank Wess
profession: Saxophonist and Flutist With the Basie Band
headline: Frank Wess, 91, Saxophonist and Flutist With the Basie Band, Dies
abstract: Mr. Wess was not the first flutist in jazz, but his deft flute solos enjoyed a prominent platform: the front row of the Basie ensemble.

name: Walt Bellamy
profession: Hall of Famer Traded by the Knicks
headline: Walt Bellamy, Hall of Famer Traded by the Knicks, Dies at 74
abstract: Bellamy was a Hall of Fame center who was among the leading N.B.A. scorers and rebounders of his time, but he was overshadowed in his 14-year N.B.A. career by Wilt Chamberlain and Bill Russell.

name: Chana Mlotek
headline: A Yiddishe Momme of Music, Chana Mlotek, Dies at 91
abstract: Mrs. Mlotek was a sleuth and archivist of Yiddish music whose song collections allowed thousands to imbibe the mirthful and mournful melodies of the shtetl, ghetto and Yiddish theater.

name: Nalini Ambady
headline: Nalini Ambady, Psychologist of Intuition, Is Dead at 54
abstract: Professor Ambady was a social psychologist whose research on the surprising accuracy of first impressions was popularized by Malcolm Gladwell in his 2005 best seller, “Blink.”

name: Chris Chase
headline: Chris Chase, Actress Who Turned to Writing, Dies
abstract: Ms. Chase appeared on the New York stage, on television and in film under the name Irene Kane, before finding her voice in writing.

name: Charlie Trotter
headline: Charlie Trotter Dies at 54; Chef Made Chicago a Must
abstract: With his flagship restaurant, Mr. Trotter helped establish Chicago as a serious dining city and helped raise the standards of American cooking through books and television.

name: Tato Laviera
headline: Tato Laviera, 63, Poet of Nuyorican School
abstract: Mr. Laviera’s acclaimed poems and plays captured the rhythms and language of Puerto Rico and the Lower East Side.

name: Editta Sherman
profession: Celebrity Portraitist and Doyenne of Carnegie Hall Studios
headline: Editta Sherman, Celebrity Portraitist and Doyenne of Carnegie Hall Studios, Dies at 101
abstract: Ms. Sherman was a free-spirited photographer who worked, raised four children and lived for 61 years in a studio penthouse above Carnegie Hall — until she was forced out in 2010.

name: Doug Ireland
headline: Doug Ireland, an Acerbic Activist and Left-Wing Writer, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Mr. Ireland managed the congressional campaigns of Allard K. Lowenstein and Bella Abzug and wrote about politics, the media and gay issues.

name: Ace Parker
profession: Pro Football Hall of Famer From Leather-Helmet Days
headline: Ace Parker, Pro Football Hall of Famer From Leather-Helmet Days, Dies at 101
abstract: Parker, a star running back in the N.F.L. who also passed, caught passes, punted and place-kicked, was the oldest living member of the Pro Football Hall of Fame.

name: Clifford Nass
headline: Clifford Nass, Who Warned of a Data Deluge, Dies at 55
abstract: Dr. Nass, a professor a Stanford, studied the effects of technology and in one pioneering study showed the deleterious effects of multitasking.

name: Michael Palmer
headline: Michael Palmer, Doctor Who Became Top Author, Dies at 71
abstract: Dr. Palmer sold about five million books worldwide, including “Extreme Measures” and “Natural Causes,” after going through years of alcohol and drug addiction.

name: Eugene Callender
headline: Rev. Eugene Callender, Who Saw Potential of School Dropouts, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Callender ministered in Harlem, served in the Lindsay and Mario Cuomo administrations and started a chain of “street academies” that became a model for programs nationwide.

name: Ed Pincus
headline: Ed Pincus, Documentary Filmmaker, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Pincus’s intent, his son said, was to “make this statement that the documentarian’s job was to be subjective.”

name: John Hawk
headline: John Hawk, Hero of Normandy Battle, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Hawk, who received the Medal of Honor for action as an Army sergeant in World War II that led to the capture of more than 500 German troops in northern France, later became a school principal.

name: Walter H. Stern
headline: Walter H. Stern, Who Coined the Term ‘Fiscal Cliff,’ Dies at 88
abstract: Decades before the term was used for a potentially catastrophic federal budget situation, Mr. Stern connected the two words in an article about property taxes.

name: Dan Lurie
headline: Dan Lurie, 90, Star and Promoter of Bodybuilding, Dies
abstract: Mr. Lurie’s chiseled physique and feats of strength made him a cover model for fitness magazines and a walking promoter for both the sport and the business of bodybuilding.

name: Bobby Thomason
headline: Bobby Thomason, Pro Bowl Quarterback, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Thomason, a three-time Pro Bowler, set a record for the Eagles in 1953 by surpassing 400 passing yards.

name: Manfred Rommel
headline: Manfred Rommel, Son of German Field Marshal, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Rommel, a three-term mayor of Stuttgart, was a liberal voice in postwar West Germany, supporting immigrant rights and strengthening the city’s Jewish population.

name: Richard Witkin
profession: Witness to the History of Aviation
headline: Richard Witkin, 95, Witness to the History of Aviation, Dies
abstract: Mr. Witkin worked for The Times for three decades and was part of the team that won a Pulitzer for coverage of the Challenger disaster.

name: Jack Mitchell
headline: Jack Mitchell, Photographer of the Arts, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Mitchell, who took thousands of portraits of dancers, musicians, writer and other artists, was known for his ability to tease character studies from his photo sessions.

name: Leonard Herzenberg
headline: Leonard Herzenberg, 81, Immunologist Who Revolutionized Research, Dies
abstract: Dr. Herzenberg, who developed a device to better examine cells, helped facilitate stem cell research and advance the treatment of cancer and other illnesses.

name: Kermit Moore
headline: Kermit Moore, Cellist, Conductor and Composer, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Moore was concerned with music rooted in the black experience and renowned for championing the work of 20th-century composers.

name: Penn Kimball
headline: Penn Kimball, Journalist Who Sued U.S., Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Kimball successfully sued the federal government after he discovered that secret files had identified him as a national security risk.

name: William Pollack
headline: William Pollack Dies at 87; His Vaccine Saved Infants
abstract: Dr. Pollack, a medical researcher, helped develop a vaccine for a blood disorder commonly called Rh disease.

name: John Tavener
headline: John Tavener Dies at 69; Composer With Eye on God
abstract: Mr. Tavener, a composer informed by Orthodox Christianity, was heard throughout the world in his elegy, performed at the funeral of Diana, Princess of Wales.

name: Kjell Qvale
headline: Kjell Qvale Dies at 94; Married U.S. to Sports Cars
abstract: Mr. Qvale imported the MG from England in the late 1940s and helped start an American sports car craze that he later nurtured by bringing in Aston Martins, Austin-Healeys, Jaguars and even Rolls-Royce.

name: Eliot H. Lumbard
headline: Eliot H. Lumbard, 88, Dies; Pursued Mob Leaders
abstract: Mr. Lumbard drew new attention to organized crime after pursuing mob figures who were found to be meeting together in a rural New York town in 1957.

name: Todd Christensen
headline: Todd Christensen, Record-Setting Tight End, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Christensen was a tight end for the Oakland and Los Angeles Raiders who made five Pro Bowl teams and played on two Super Bowl champions.

name: Kalaparusha Maurice McIntyre
headline: Kalaparusha Maurice McIntyre, Tenor Saxophonist, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. McIntyre was a founding member of the Association for the Advancement of Creative Musicians and occasionally performed in face paint and tribal costume.

name: Saul Kagan
headline: Saul Kagan, Who Won Holocaust Restitution, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Kagan was the founding director of the Conference on Jewish Material Claims Against Germany, which sought reparations for the Nazi genocide against European Jews.

name: Bobbie Handman
headline: Bobbie Handman, a Medal of Arts Winner, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Handman was a behind-the-scenes force in Democratic politics, a theater preservationist and the first person to be awarded the National Medal of Arts for advocacy.

name: Glafkos Clerides
headline: Glafkos Clerides, Greek Cypriot Leader Who Sought Unification, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Mr. Clerides, the president of Cyprus from 1993 to 2003, was a frustrated peacemaker in futile talks with Turkish Cypriots to reunify their long-divided island.

name: Mike McCormack
headline: Mike McCormack, Hall of Fame Browns Lineman, Dies at  83
abstract: Mr. McCormack helped take the Browns to N.F.L. championships in 1954 and 1955 and became a league coach and executive.

name: Elmer Lokkins
headline: Elmer Lokkins, Symbol of Same-Sex Marriage Cause, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Lokkins married his longtime partner when both were in their 80s and became a symbol of gay rights.

name: Alex Calderwood
profession: Creator and Face of the Unconventional Ace Hotel Chain
headline: Alex Calderwood, Creator and Face of the Unconventional Ace Hotel Chain, Dies at 47
abstract: The quirky vintage interiors of Mr. Calderwood’s hotels influenced the industry and became the backdrop for countless Instagram pictures.

name: William Weaver
profession: Influential Translator of Modern Italian Literature
headline: William Weaver, Influential Translator of Modern Italian Literature, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Weaver’s work embraced the highest echelons of modern Italian fiction, nonfiction, poetry, prose and opera librettos, translating relatively obscure works along with international best sellers.

name: Joaquín Hernández Galicia
headline: Joaquín Hernández Galicia, Oil Workers Chief, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Hernández Galicia led a union of 200,000 workers employed by Mexico’s huge state-owned oil company, Pemex, and they revered him for the generous benefits he won for them.

name: Aleksandr Serebrov
headline: Aleksandr Serebrov, 69, Dies; Cosmonaut Who Persevered
abstract: Mr. Serebrov, who once held a spacewalk record, flew four missions for a program that abandoned Soviet ambitions for Russian spare parts.

name: Doris Lessing
headline: Doris Lessing, Author Who Swept Aside Convention, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Ms. Lessing was an uninhibited and outspoken novelist who produced dozens of novels, short stories, essays and poems, embarking on dizzying and at times stultifying literary experiments.

name: Suzanne Bianchi
headline: Suzanne Bianchi, 61, Who Analyzed Family Time, Dies
abstract: Professor Bianchi, a social scientist, upended conventional wisdom suggesting that working women were shortchanging their children.

name: Syd Field
profession: Wrote the Book on Writing Screenplays
headline: Syd Field, Who Wrote the Book on Writing Screenplays, Dies at 77
abstract: Thanks to Mr. Field, a teacher who wrote the definitive guide to screenwriting, the term “plot points” is in the filmmaking vocabulary.

name: Barbara Park
profession: Author of Junie B. Jones Series
headline: Barbara Park, Author of Junie B. Jones Series, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Park’s best-selling books starred a sassy grade schooler with an imperfect grasp of English grammar who always found herself in some sort of predicament.

name: Billy Hardwick
headline: Billy Hardwick, Hall of Fame Bowler, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Hardwick, the first of only six bowlers to win the sport’s triple crown, was a right-handed bowler with a fluid style, far smoother than many of today’s power players.

name: Charlotte Zolotow
profession: Author of Books on Childrens Real Issues
headline: Charlotte Zolotow, Author of Books on Children’s Real Issues, Dies at 98
abstract: The more than 70 books written by Ms. Zolotow, an editor as well as an author, were highlighted by pictures from some of the 20th century’s finest illustrators.

name: Jane Pratt Fitzpatrick
headline: Jane Pratt Fitzpatrick, 89, Savior of Pre-Revolutionary Inn, Dies
abstract: Mrs. Fitzpatrick kept the Red Lion Inn from being torn down to make way for a gas station in Stockbridge, Mass.

name: Frederick Sanger
profession: Twice a Nobel Laureate and a Genetics Pioneer
headline: Frederick Sanger, 95, Twice a Nobel Laureate and a Genetics Pioneer, Dies
abstract: Dr. Sanger, a British biochemist, showed how amino acids link together to form insulin in 1958, and invented a method of “reading” molecular letters that make up the genetic code in 1980.

name: Robert Bowie
profession: Adviser to Truman, Eisenhower, Johnson and Carter
headline: Robert Bowie, 104, Adviser to Truman, Eisenhower, Johnson and Carter, Dies
abstract: Robert R. Bowie, a Harvard foreign policy expert, was an analyst on the Cold War, national security and conflicts around the globe.

name: Diane Disney Miller
headline: Diane Disney Miller, 79, Keeper of Walt’s Flame, Dies
abstract: Mrs. Miller, the last surviving child of Walt Disney, co-founded a museum dedicated to the memory of her father as a human being rather than a brand.

name: Herbert Mitgang
headline: Herbert Mitgang, Wide-Ranging Author and Journalist, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Mitgang, a longtime reporter and editor for The New York Times, told of mountains of F.B.I. and C.I.A. records squirreled away on America’s most well-known writers.

name: James H. Steele
headline: James H. Steele, Pioneer in Veterinary Public Health, Dies at 100
abstract: Dr. Steele helped establish mass vaccination and prevention programs in the United States and abroad for diseases that pass from animals to people.

name: Michael Weiner
headline: Michael Weiner, Peacemaking Leader of Baseball Union, Dies at 51
abstract: Mr. Weiner forged agreements with baseball club owners that enhanced drug testing and brought years of labor peace to the game after decades of strife.

name: Sylvia Browne
headline: Sylvia Browne Dies at 77; Self-Proclaimed Psychic
abstract: Ms. Browne, who appeared on “Larry King Live” and other shows, said she could speak to the dead and claimed to have helped police find murder suspects and their victims.

name: Louis D. Rubin Jr.
headline: Louis D. Rubin Jr., Publisher, Scholar and Champion of Southern Writers, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Rubin, a man of letters who helped found Algonquin Books, was devoted to the practice and promotion of American Southern writing.

name: Thomas Rees
headline: Thomas Rees, Plastic Surgeon Who Treated Africa, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Rees, an innovative New York practitioner, helped found the Flying Doctors Service of East Africa, which helps provide medical care and save lives in the African bush.

name: Mavis Batey
profession: Allied Code Breaker in World War II
headline: Mavis Batey, Allied Code Breaker in World War II, Dies at 92
abstract: Mrs. Batey volunteered to be an army nurse after Britain declared war on Germany in 1939, but was instead assigned to the top-secret Allied effort to decipher codes.

name: Vern Mikkelsen
headline: Vern Mikkelsen, Hall of Famer Who Won Four Titles With the Lakers, Dies at 85
abstract: Mikkelsen, a six-time N.B.A. All-Star known for his tough defense and rebounding, helped pioneer the position of power forward.

name: John Egerton
headline: John Egerton, Who Lent Spice to Social Justice, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Egerton, a Southern writer, used Southern cooking both as a means to understand the culture and to achieve racial reconciliation.

name: T. J. Jemison
headline: Rev. T. J. Jemison, Civil Rights Leader Who Organized Early Boycott, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Jemison organized what is considered the civil rights movement’s first large-scale bus boycott, and was a founding member of the Southern Christian Leadership Conference.

name: Adrienne Asch
profession: Bioethicist and Pioneer in Disability Studies
headline: Adrienne Asch, Bioethicist and Pioneer in Disability Studies, Dies at 67
abstract: Professor Asch was a vocal opponent of prenatal testing and abortion to select children free of disabilities.

name: Fred Kavli
headline: Fred Kavli, Benefactor of Science Prizes, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Kavli, a California physicist raised in Norway, established $1 million awards and 17 institutes that finance university research.

name: Conrad Susa
headline: Conrad Susa, 78, Composer and Teacher, Dies
abstract: Mr. Susa, the writer of five operas, showed wide range even while hewing to the classical.

name: Peter B. Lewis
headline: Peter B. Lewis, Philanthropist Who Led Progressive Auto Insurance, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Lewis turned the small insurance firm co-founded by his father into one of the nation’s largest auto insurance companies by insuring high-risk drivers and high-end sports cars.

name: Jean Banchet
headline: Jean Banchet, Chef Who Translated French Cuisine, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Banchet’s traditional French cooking helped turn the Chicago suburbs into a global destination for food-lovers in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Alec Reid
headline: Alec Reid, Northern Ireland Priest Who Helped Broker Peace Accord, Dies at 82
abstract: Father Reid served as a secret peace broker between Gerry Adams, the leader of Sinn Fein, and contacts in the British and Irish governments.

name: James Rensenbrink
headline: James Rensenbrink, 81, Dies; Founded Aquarian Weekly
abstract: Mr. Rensenbrink’s Aquarian Weekly claimed to be one of the last independent alternative papers in the country and one of the oldest continuously published ones.

name: Chico Hamilton
headline: Chico Hamilton, Drummer, Bandleader and Exponent of Cool Jazz, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Hamilton, from the Los Angeles area, had a subtle and melodic approach that made him ideally suited for the refined, understated style that came to be known as cool jazz.

name: Lou Brissie
headline: Lou Brissie, an All-Star and War Hero, Dies at 89
abstract: Brissie achieved his dream and inspired people with disabilities by making the major leagues after suffering devastating leg injuries in World War II.

name: Georges Lautner
headline: Georges Lautner Dies at 87; Prolific French Film Director
abstract: Mr. Lautner made over 40 films starring Jean-Paul Belmondo, Alain Delon and others, and specialized in comedy and crime.

name: Merrell Williams Jr.
headline: Merrell Williams Jr., Paralegal Who Bared Big Tobacco, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Williams leaked mountains of internal documents in 1994, fueling lawsuits that resulted in an industry payout of billions of dollars to pay smokers’ medical bills.

name: Saul Leiter
headline: Saul Leiter, Photographer Who Captured New York’s Palette, Dies at 89
abstract: Where other eminent photographers in midcentury captured the city most often in sharp-edged black and white, Mr. Leiter was one of the first professionals to photograph it regularly in color.

name: Arik Einstein
headline: Arik Einstein, 74, Beloved Israeli Singer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Einstein’s blend of folk and rock helped shape a new Hebrew popular culture and his ballads became modern Israeli anthems.

name: Tony Musante
profession: Actor Known for Role in Toma
headline: Tony Musante, Actor Known for Role in ‘Toma,’ Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Musante acted on stage and in many films in the United States and Europe, working with Gene Hackman, Meryl Streep and George C. Scott.

name: Bill Foulkes
profession: Soccer Star Survived Teams Plane Crash
headline: Bill Foulkes Dies at 81; Soccer Star Survived Team’s Plane Crash
abstract: Sustaining only minor injuries in the crash in Munich in February 1958 that killed eight starting players, the rugged defender went on to help Manchester United rebuild.

name: Matthew Bucksbaum
headline: Matthew Bucksbaum, Mall Developer, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Bucksbaum started General Growth Properties in 1954 with his brothers in small cities throughout the Midwest and expanded the company in concert with the growth of American suburbs.

name: Paul Mayer
headline: Paul Mayer, 82, Ex-Priest and Peace Activist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Mayer was a Jewish-born former Roman Catholic priest who was at the forefront of peace and social justice campaigns for five decades.

name: Peter Kaplan
headline: Peter Kaplan, Editor of New York Observer, Dies at 59
abstract: In his 15 years as editor, Mr. Kaplan was credited with making The New York Observer both pertinent and impertinent as it gleefully chronicled the every move and shake of the city’s movers and shakers.

name: Peter B. Kaplan
headline: Peter B. Kaplan, a Photographer With Altitude, Is Dead at 79
abstract: He overcame his fear of heights to capture unique views, from the Statue of Liberty’s torch and the antennas of the Empire State and World Trade Center.

name: Al Plastino
headline: Al Plastino, 91, Dies; Drew Many Superheroes
abstract: Mr. Plastino took his greatest pride in “Superman’s Mission for President Kennedy,” which he began before the assassination.

name: Paul F. Crouch
headline: Paul F. Crouch, Who Built Evangelical TV Network, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Crouch and his wife were the faces of one of the largest Christian television empires, drawing tens of millions of dollars in donations annually.

name: William Stevenson
headline: William Stevenson, 89, Dies; Author With Ties to Spies
abstract: Mr. Stevenson, who wrote “A Man Called Intrepid” and “90 Minutes at Entebbe,” spent much of his career straddling the worlds of espionage and journalism.

name: André Schiffrin
profession: Publishing Force and a Founder of New Press
headline: André Schiffrin, Publishing Force and a Founder of New Press, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Schiffrin championed the work of Jean-Paul Sartre, Günter Grass, Studs Terkel, Michel Foucault, Simone de Beauvoir, Noam Chomsky and many others.

name: Paul Walker
profession: Star of Fast and Furious Movies
headline: Paul Walker, 40, Star of ‘Fast and Furious’ Movies, Dies in Crash
abstract: Mr. Walker, who was killed in a car crash, was best known for the “Fast and the Furious” movie series about street racing.

name: Natalya Gorbanevskaya
headline: Natalya Gorbanevskaya, Soviet Dissident and Poet, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Gorbanevskaya was arrested after protesting the Soviet Union’s 1968 invasion of Czechoslovakia, and later confined to a psychiatric hospital for her writings.

name: Willis Ware
profession: Engineer at Dawn of Computer Age
headline: Willis Ware, 93, Engineer at Dawn of Computer Age, Dies
abstract: As part of a group of engineers developing an early computer, Mr. Ware was first to try to engineer many of the components that would be essential for modern computers.

name: T.R. Fehrenbach
headline: T.R. Fehrenbach, Historian, Dies at 88; Chronicler of Larger-Than-Life Texas
abstract: A member of the Sons of Texas, Mr. Fehrenbach said he had never claimed to be a historian; he once characterized his writing as “political science fiction.”

name: Andro Linklater
headline: Andro Linklater, Who Re-Examined American Frontierism, Dies at 68
abstract: The Scottish historian wrote “Measuring America,” which stressed government surveying of the westward expansion, rather than the lone-wolf perception of pioneers.

name: Judy Rodgers
headline: Judy Rodgers, Chef of Refined Simplicity, Dies at 57
abstract: The influential chef at San Francisco’s Zuni Café was known for presenting dishes that were simultaneously rustic and urbane.

name: Peter Graf
headline: Peter Graf, Volatile Father of Tennis Great, Dies at 75
abstract: The man nicknamed Papa Merciless was accused of mismanaging the millions his daughter, Stefi Graf, had won.

name: Dick Dodd
headline: Dick Dodd, Lead Singer of the Standells, Dies at 68
abstract: The Standells’ most famous song, “Dirty Water,” became a hit in the mid-1960s and the anthem of Boston sports teams decades later.

name: Vincent A. Marchiselli
headline: Vincent A. Marchiselli, Ex-New York Legislator From Bronx, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Marchiselli, elected in 1974 as a reformer, was a defiant voice against his borough’s scandal-scarred Democratic organization.

name: Paul Aussaresses
headline: Paul Aussaresses, 95, Who Tortured Algerians, Dies
abstract: General Aussaresses stunned France in 2000 when he asserted that he had tortured and executed dozens of prisoners during his country’s war in Algeria four decades earlier.

name: Nelson Mandela
profession: South Africas Liberator as Prisoner and President
headline: Nelson Mandela, South Africa’s Liberator as Prisoner and President, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Mandela’s quest for freedom in South Africa’s system of white rule took him from the court of tribal royalty to the liberation underground to a prison cell to the presidency.

name: Mary Nerney
headline: Sister Mary Nerney, Advocate for Women in Prison, Dies at 75
abstract: Sister Mary founded an organization that helps women imprisoned for killing their batterers, as well as a program to teach female ex-convicts construction trades.

name: Christopher Evan Welch
headline: Christopher Evan Welch, 48, a Versatile, Busy Actor, Dies
abstract: Mr. Welch’s New York debut in “Scapin” led to many roles on New York stages, as well as high-profile film work.

name: Martin Sharp
headline: Martin Sharp, 71, an Artist Who Shaped Imagery of Rock, Dies
abstract: Mr. Sharp’s posters, paintings and collages included depictions of Tiny Tim and Marilyn Monroe.

name: Colin Eglin
headline: Colin Eglin, 88, Key White Opponent of Apartheid, Dies
abstract: Mr. Eglin, a South African politician, was at the forefront of his country’s white, liberal opposition to apartheid and helped draft the Constitution that ended it in 1993.

name: Jean-Claude Beton
headline: Jean-Claude Beton, Who Sent Orangina Around the World, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Beton used imaginative marketing techniques to popularize a sophisticated citrus soft drink.

name: Ahmed Fouad Negm
headline: Ahmed Fouad Negm, Dissident Poet of Egypt’s Underclass, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Negm’s fearless and often mocking critiques of power made him a folk hero, but also earned him a total of 18 years in jail.

name: Art Kaminsky
profession: Clients Won the Miracle on Ice
headline: Art Kaminsky, Whose Clients Won the ‘Miracle on Ice,’ Dies at 66
abstract: At one point, Mr. Kaminsky represented about one-third of the players in the N.H.L., and he branched out to handle broadcasters.

name: Michael Kammen
headline: Michael Kammen, Historian of U.S. Psyche, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Kammen, a Pulitzer Prize-winning author, helped cast the form of the modern scholarly field known as memory studies.

name: Robert Wachs
headline: Robert Wachs Dies at 73; Promoted Comedy, Including Eddie Murphy’s
abstract: Mr. Wachs, a founder of the Comic Strip nightclub, also managed Eddie Murphy for more than a decade.

name: Tabu Ley Rochereau
headline: Tabu Ley Rochereau Dies; Spread the Sound of Soukous
abstract: Global influences could be heard in the music of Mr. Tabu, a Congolese singer, songwriter and politician.

name: Delbert Tibbs
profession: Left Death Row and Fought Against It
headline: Delbert Tibbs, Who Left Death Row and Fought Against It, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Tibbs, sentenced to death in 1974 for a murder and rape in Florida, was one of six people whose stories of wrongful conviction and near execution were told in the play “The Exonerated.”

name: Edouard Molinaro
profession: Oscar Nominee for Directing La Cage
headline: Edouard Molinaro, Oscar Nominee for Directing ‘La Cage,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Molinaro had many television shows and movies to his credit, but “La Cage aux Folles” is his best-known work.

name: Fred Scherer
profession: Diorama Painter Mastered Even Illusion of Air
headline: Fred Scherer, 98, Dies; Diorama Painter Mastered Even Illusion of Air
abstract: Mr. Scherer helped create scenes for people in New York who otherwise might never see a flock of cormorants nesting on a cliff.

name: Bill Porter
headline: Bill Porter, an Exceptional Salesman Who Inspired a Film, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Porter, who had cerebral palsy, was the inspiration for “Door to Door,” a 2002 TV film starring William H. Macy.

name: Eleanor Parker
profession: Oscar Nominee Was in Sound of Music
headline: Eleanor Parker, 91, Dies; Oscar Nominee Was in ‘Sound of Music’
abstract: Ms. Parker, an elegant, ladylike film actress, had her most recognizable role as the Baroness who loves Christopher Plummer’s character in “The Sound of Music.”

name: Joseph Napolitan
headline: Joseph Napolitan, Pioneering Campaign Consultant, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Napolitan’s use of polling and advertising heralded the rise of independent political strategists like himself and the waning power of party organizations in managing campaigns.

name: Stan Tracey
profession: Helped British Jazz Emerge From American Shadow
headline: Stan Tracey Dies at 86; Helped British Jazz Emerge From American Shadow
abstract: Mr. Tracey’s inspirations for some of his compositions were distinctly British in origin.

name: Louis Waldon
profession: Actor in Warhol Films Seized for Obscenity
headline: Louis Waldon, Actor in Warhol Films Seized for Obscenity, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Waldon, one of the few Warhol Superstars who had acting experience, starred in “Lonesome Cowboys” and “Blue Movie.”

name: Jim Hall
headline: Jim Hall, Master Jazz Guitarist Who Played With the Greats, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Hall was distinguished by his simplicity of style and a warm, lush sound.

name: Joe Bihari
headline: Joe Bihari, Who Put Early R&B on Record, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Bihari created Modern Music Records with his two brothers, Jules and Saul, recording B.B. King, Etta James, John Lee Hooker and other blues legends.

name: Colin Wilson
profession: Author Acclaimed at 24 for The Outsider
headline: Colin Wilson, Author Acclaimed at 24 for ‘The Outsider,’ Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Wilson shot to international acclaim with his first book, which in 1956 touched a deep nerve in postwar Britain. He went on to write more than 100 others.

name: Allen Rosenberg
headline: Allen Rosenberg, Olympic Rowing Coach Who Transformed the Sport, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Rosenberg led the American rowing team to gold in the 1964 Olympics and brought an analytical approach to what was a sport of brute strength.

name: Don Mitchell
headline: Don Mitchell, a Co-Star on TV’s ‘Ironside,’ Dies
abstract: Besides playing Mark Sanger, the title character’s bodyguard-assistant on “Ironside,” Mr. Mitchell also appeared in the 1973 film “Scream Blacula, Scream” and on other TV series.

name: Honey Waldman
headline: Honey Waldman, 87, Dies; Created Theaters From Old Buildings
abstract: Ms. Waldman was a stage producer who teamed up with her husband to convert a dilapidated movie house in the Hudson Valley and a bank in the East Village into distinguished theaters.

name: Jack Fishman
headline: Jack Fishman Dies at 83; Saved Many From Overdose
abstract: Dr. Fishman worked on a drug that counters the addictive and potentially fatal use of narcotics.

name: Peter O’Toole
profession: Acclaim Began With Lawrence of Arabia
headline: Peter O’Toole, Whose Acclaim Began With ‘Lawrence of Arabia,’ Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. O’Toole’s performance in the epic 1962 film earned him overnight fame and established him as one of his generation’s most charismatic actors.

name: Charles M. Vest
profession: President of M.I.T. and a Leader in Online Education
headline: Charles M. Vest, 72, President of M.I.T. and a Leader in Online Education, Dies
abstract: Dr. Vest was trained as a mechanical engineer and became a champion of women in science and engineering.

name: Abraham Briloff
headline: Abraham Briloff, Accounting Professor, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Briloff practiced accounting, but it was the articles he wrote for Barron’s that turned him into something of a celebrity.

name: Joan Fontaine
profession: Won an Oscar for Hitchcocks Suspicion
headline: Joan Fontaine, Who Won an Oscar for Hitchcock’s ‘Suspicion,’ Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Fontaine was 24 when she took home an Academy Award in 1942, the youngest best-actress winner at the time.

name: Ray Price
headline: Ray Price, Groundbreaking, Hit-Making Country Singer, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Price placed more than 100 singles on the country charts, including hits like “Make the World Go Away,” and helped change the genre.

name: Tom Laughlin
profession: Star of Billy Jack Movie Series
headline: Tom Laughlin, 82, Star of ‘Billy Jack’ Movie Series, Dies
abstract: Mr. Laughlin wrote, directed and starred in all four of the films, based on an amalgam of cowboy archetypes, Asian martial-arts film archetypes and his image of himself.

name: Hugh Nissenson
headline: Hugh Nissenson, Who Pushed the Novel’s Boundaries, Dies at 80
abstract: A thorough researcher, Mr. Nissenson took years to create alternative worlds in pursuing questions of faith in books like “The Tree of Life.”

name: Audrey Totter
headline: Audrey Totter, Femme Fatale of ’40s Film Noir, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Totter is most remembered for her work in the 1940s in movies like “The Postman Always Rings Twice” and “Lady in the Lake.”

name: Harold Camping
profession: Dogged Forecaster of the End of the World
headline: Harold Camping, Dogged Forecaster of the End of the World, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Camping, who founded the Family Radio network, repeatedly prophesied the date of the apocalypse, and apologized when it turned out to be wrong.

name: George L. Shinn
headline: George L. Shinn, a Wall Street Chief Who Turned to Teaching, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Shinn, a former president of Merrill Lynch, also led the First Boston Corporation as chairman and chief executive, but left unexpectedly to pursue teaching.

name: Janet Dailey
headline: Janet Dailey, 69, Dies; Romance Author Who Sold in Hundreds of Millions
abstract: Ms. Dailey wrote her first novel on something of a dare and went on to sell as many as 300 million copies of her romance novels, many for Harlequin.

name: George Hambrick
headline: George Hambrick, 91, Leader in Dermatology, Dies
abstract: Dr. Hambrick founded the American Skin Association in 1987 with two colleagues and was its president from its inception to his death.

name: Ronnie Biggs
profession: Longtime Fugitive After the Great Train Robbery
headline: Ronnie Biggs, Longtime Fugitive After the Great Train Robbery, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Biggs gained international fame for his role in one of Britain’s best-known crimes, the Great Train Robbery of 1963, and his subsequent life on the run.

name: Cynthia Eagle Russett
headline: Cynthia Eagle Russett, Chronicler of Women’s History, Dies at 76
abstract: Professor Russett’s best-known book, “Sexual Science,” published in 1989, explored attempts by Victorian thinkers, including Darwin, to scientifically “prove” women’s inferiority.

name: George Rodrigue
headline: George Rodrigue, Painter of Blue Dog, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Rodrigue celebrated Louisiana culture in his earliest works but achieved a following with his paintings of Blue Dog.

name: Eyad El-Sarraj
headline: Eyad El-Sarraj, Psychiatrist Who Fought for Palestinians’ Rights, Dies at 70
abstract: Dr. Sarraj pioneered mental health care in Gaza and became an internationally recognized human rights advocate, criticizing both the Israeli and Palestinian authorities.

name: Günther Förg
headline: Günther Förg, German Artist Who Made Modernism His Theme, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Förg was a painter, sculptor and photographer whose work exemplified, toyed with, tweaked and commented on modernism.

name: Graham Mackay
headline: Graham Mackay, Who Built Beer Empire, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Mackay helped transform South Africa’s biggest brewer into SABMiller, one of the world’s biggest beer conglomerates.

name: Al Goldstein
headline: Al Goldstein, a Publisher Who Took the Romance Out of Sex, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Goldstein, the publisher of Screw magazine, was first to present sex to his audience without the slightest attempt at classiness or subtlety.

name: Fred Benjamin
profession: Exacting and Inventive Teacher of Jazz Dance
headline: Fred Benjamin, Exacting and Inventive Teacher of Jazz Dance, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Benjamin was part of the creative wave of young black modern-dance choreographers who came to prominence in the 1970s.

name: John W. Cornforth
headline: John W. Cornforth, 96, Nobel-Winning Chemist, Dies
abstract: Dr. Cornforth, who was born in Australia, shared the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1975 and could trace that achievement to his discovery as a child that he was becoming deaf.

name: Richard D. Heffner
headline: Richard D. Heffner, Host of ‘The Open Mind,’ Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Heffner’s background as a historian helped him carve out careers in education, broadcasting and in rating films.

name: Bernard Shaw
profession: Husband and Bodyguard of Patty Hearst
headline: Bernard Shaw, Husband and Bodyguard of Patty Hearst, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Shaw, a former police officer, met Ms. Hearst in the aftermath of her crime-ridden affiliation with a guerrilla group, and married her after her release from prison.

name: Bernard Shaw
headline: Bernard Shaw, CNN’s Lead Anchor for 20 Years, Dies at 82
abstract: He covered the Gulf War, anchored convention coverage and asked a revealing question of Gov. Michael Dukakis during a presidential debate in 1988.

name: Ned Vizzini
headline: Ned Vizzini, 32, Dies; Wrote Teenage Novels
abstract: Mr. Vizzini addressed depression and other adolescent issues in works like “It’s Kind of a Funny Story.”

name: Janet D. Rowley
headline: Janet D. Rowley, Who Discovered Cancer Can Be Genetic, Dies at 88
abstract: In 1972, Dr. Rowley became the first person to show a conclusive link between certain genetic abnormalities and certain cancers.

name: Kelly Clark
headline: Kelly Clark, Lawyer Who Won Boy Scouts Abuse Case, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Clark’s successful child molestation lawsuit against the Boy Scouts of America in Oregon led to the release of a trove of documents containing thousands of accusations of sexual abuse.

name: Kenneth A. Schechter
headline: Kenneth A. Schechter, 83, Dies; With Help, He Flew Blind
abstract: Mr. Schechter, then Ensign Schechter, a Navy pilot during the Korean War, was at the heart of one of the most electrifying air rescues in American military history.

name: Michiaki Takahashi
headline: Michiaki Takahashi, 85, Who Tamed Chickenpox, Dies
abstract: Dr. Takahashi, a researcher of measles and polio viruses, was spurred to action when his 3-year-old son fell ill.

name: Edgar M. Bronfman
headline: Edgar M. Bronfman, Who Built a Bigger, More Elegant Seagram, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Bronfman helped the liquor company acquire other businesses and make a stake in Hollywood, and he championed the rights of Jews as president of the World Jewish Congress.

name: John Eisenhower
profession: Military Historian and Son of the President
headline: John Eisenhower, Military Historian and Son of the President, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Eisenhower, the son of Dwight D. Eisenhower, the five-star general turned president, forged his own career in the Army and then chronicled the history of the military in numerous books.

name: Lawrence O. Kitchen
headline: Lawrence O. Kitchen, Steady Hand for Lockheed, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Kitchen rose through the ranks of the aerospace company during a 30-year career and led the company through rocky tussles with governments during the 1980s.

name: Mikhail Kalashnikov
headline: Mikhail Kalashnikov, Creator of AK-47, Dies at 94
abstract: General Kalashnikov sometimes lamented the weapon’s unchecked distribution but took pride in having invented the rifle, the most abundant firearm ever made.

name: Stan Brooks
headline: Stan Brooks, a Familiar Voice on 1010 WINS, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Brooks’s tenure and prolific output on New York’s first all-news radio station made him one of the most recognized voices on the radio for more than 40 years.

name: Larry Lujack
headline: Larry Lujack, a Cranky Radio Voice That Carried, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Lujack was a longtime Chicago disc jockey whose curmudgeonly attitude influenced current radio personalities like Rush Limbaugh.

name: Edwin A. Shuman III
headline: Edwin A. Shuman III, Former Prisoner of War Who Defied Hanoi Hilton Guards, Dies at 82
abstract: Commander Shuman, a Navy pilot whose plane was shot down in 1968, led an effort by prisoners to conduct church services in the North Vietnamese camp known as the Hanoi Hilton.

name: Yusef Lateef
headline: Yusef Lateef, Innovative Jazz Saxophonist and Flutist, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Lateef crossed musical boundaries, playing world music before world music had a name.

name: Rodolfo Hernandez
headline: Rodolfo Hernandez, 82, Dies; Awarded Medal of Honor
abstract: Mr. Hernandez received the award for charging at the enemy in a daring assault while wounded and armed with an inoperable rifle and a bayonet when he was an Army corporal during the Korean War.

name: Marv Wolfenson
profession: Led an N.B.A. Rebirth in Minnesota
headline: Marv Wolfenson, 87, Dies; Led an N.B.A. Rebirth in Minnesota
abstract: Mr. Wolfenson and his partner, Harvey Ratner, returned N.B.A. basketball to Minnesota in 1989, nearly 30 years after the Lakers had departed for California.

name: Barbara Branden
headline: Barbara Branden, Biographer of Ayn Rand, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Branden, once a member of Ms. Rand’s inner circle, wrote an unauthorized biography, “The Passion of Ayn Rand,” published in 1986, that angered some Rand followers.

name: Mike Hegan
headline: Mike Hegan, 71, Player Who Made Long Journey Home
abstract: Mr. Hegan, who played for several teams in the major leagues, including the Yankees, returned to his Cleveland and became a broadcaster.

name: Frederick Fox
headline: Frederick Fox, Milliner to Royals, Dies at 82
abstract: Beginning in 1970, Mr. Fox designed more than 350 hats for Queen Elizabeth. His trademark skill, admirers said, was to mix whimsy and propriety.

name: Paul Blair
headline: Paul Blair, Center Fielder for Champions, Dies at 69
abstract: Perhaps the finest outfielder of his era, Mr. Blair was known for his speed and grace, and for his ability to read a hitter’s swing and make a quick break on a fly ball.

name: Joseph Santo
headline: Joseph Santo Dies at 84; Restaurateur of Romance
abstract: Over the years, Dr. Santo opened a number of restaurants — Yellowfingers, Arizona 206 and Contrapunto among them — near the corner of Third Avenue and East 60th Street.

name: Andy Granatelli
headline: Andy Granatelli Dies at 90; Revved Businesses and Cars
abstract: Mr. Granatelli turned STP oil treatment into a national institution and shook up auto racing’s establishment with his innovations.

name: Vito Rizzuto
headline: Vito Rizzuto, Reputed Mafia Boss of Canada, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Rizzuto’s dapper outfits and his ability to avoid prison led the authorities to call him the John Gotti of Montreal.

name: Harold Simmons
headline: Harold Simmons Dies at 82; Backed Swift Boat Ads
abstract: Mr. Simmons, who built a billion-dollar empire starting with a Dallas drugstore, gave $26.9 million to “super PACs” opposing President Obama in the 2012 presidential election.

name: Robert Neuwirth
headline: Dr. Robert Neuwirth, a Pioneering Gynecologist, Dies at 80
abstract: Dr. Neuwirth developed minimally invasive procedures that allowed many women to avoid hysterectomies.

name: Kenneth C. Edelin
profession: Doctor at Center of Landmark Abortion Case
headline: Kenneth C. Edelin, Doctor at Center of Landmark Abortion Case, Dies at 74
abstract: Dr. Edelin became a hero of the women’s movement after his conviction and eventual acquittal for performing a legal abortion in 1973.

name: Marta Eggerth
headline: Marta Eggerth, the ‘Callas of Operetta,’ Dies at 101
abstract: A coloratura soprano, Miss Eggerth was often compared to Maria Callas for her vocal facility, charm and ubiquity — in opera houses, on the concert stage, in the movies and on Broadway.

name: John Dominis
headline: John Dominis, a Star Photographer for Life Magazine, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Dominis was known for capturing celebrities, wild animals and presidents at their unguarded best.

name: Patricia Ryan
headline: Patricia Ryan, a Managing Editor at Time Inc., Dies at 75
abstract: Initially making her mark as a secretary at Sports Illustrated who knew horses, Ms. Ryan was among the first women to lead major publications.

name: Mike O’Connor
headline: Mike O’Connor, Journalists’ Advocate, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. O’Connor, a veteran war correspondent, became an advocate for threatened journalists in Mexico, one of the world’s most dangerous countries for the press.

name: James Avery
headline: James Avery, ‘Fresh Prince’ Actor, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Avery, who played the surrogate father to Will Smith’s character on the 1990-96 NBC sitcom, also appeared in movies and was a popular voice-over actor.

name: James Avery
profession: Creator of a Southern Jewelry Empire
headline: James Avery, Creator of a Southern Jewelry Empire, Dies at 96
abstract: His company grew from a one-man operation in Texas to 80 stores across the South, gaining particular renown for its religiously inspired creations.

name: Alfred Marshall
headline: Alfred Marshall, Founder of Stores That Bear His Name, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Marshall parlayed a grocery store into a worldwide discount clothing retailer.

name: Bob Grant
profession: Combative Personality on New York Talk Radio
headline: Bob Grant, a Combative Personality on New York Talk Radio, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Grant, long a dominant voice on the airwaves, took advantage of the repeal of the Fairness Doctrine and thrived on the radio despite racist remarks.

name: George Jacobs
headline: George Jacobs, Memoirist and Valet for Sinatra, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Jacobs had a close-up of Frank Sinatra’s inner circle in the 1950s and ’60s and wrote about it in a 2003 book.

name: Micky Lay
headline: Micky Lay, a Source for ‘Jerusalem,’ Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Lay’s hard-drinking, rebel persona was an inspiration for Mark Rylance’s Tony- and Olivier-winning performance in Jez Butterworth’s play “Jerusalem.”

name: Johnny Orr
headline: Johnny Orr, Coach Who Turned Iowa State Into Contender, Dies at 86
abstract: Orr, who led Michigan to the N.C.A.A. men’s final in 1976, left for Iowa State in 1980 and turned around a moribund program by emphasizing speed over size.

name: Susan Rasky
headline: Susan Rasky, Award-Winning Reporter for The Times, Dies at 61
abstract: She shared a Polk Award for national reporting for coverage of Congress in 1990 and most recently taught at the University of California, Berkeley.

name: George Goodman
headline: George Goodman, Who Demystified the World of Money, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Goodman was probably best known as the amiable but intellectually rigorous host of “Adam Smith’s Money World,” seen on PBS from 1984 to 1997.

name: Juanita Moore
headline: Juanita Moore, Oscar-Nominated Actress, Dies at 99
abstract: Ms. Moore found only limited work after becoming the fifth African-American performer nominated for an Academy Award.

name: W.V. Cordice Jr.
headline: Dr. W.V. Cordice Jr., 94, a Surgeon Who Helped Save Dr. King, Dies
abstract: Dr. Cordice was part of a team of surgeons who operated on the civil rights leader after he was stabbed in Harlem in 1958.

name: Phil Everly
profession: Half of a Pioneer Rock Duo
headline: Phil Everly, Half of a Pioneer Rock Duo That Inspired Generations, Dies at 74
abstract: Songs by Mr. Everly and his older brother, Don Everly, carried the close fraternal harmonies of country tradition into pioneering rock ‘n’ roll.

name: Harvey K. Littleton
profession: Pioneer in the Art of Glass
headline: Harvey K. Littleton, a Pioneer in the Art of Glass, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Littleton, whose work has been acquired by the Metropolitan Museum of Art, founded what is considered to be the nation’s first college-level course in his field.

name: Saul Zaentz
headline: Saul Zaentz, Producer of Oscar-Winning Movies, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Zaentz, an independent film producer, won best-picture Academy Awards for “One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest,” “Amadeus” and “The English Patient.”

name: Donald H. Forst
headline: Donald H. Forst, Feisty Newspaper Editor, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Forst was the former top editor of New York Newsday, The Village Voice and The Boston Herald.

name: Eusébio
headline: Eusébio, 71, Legend of Portuguese Soccer, Dies
abstract: Eusébio, a Portuguese soccer star of the 1960s and 1970s, died on Sunday at the age of 71.

name: Anna E. Crouse
headline: Anna E. Crouse, 97, Dies; Championed Discount Tickets for Broadway
abstract: Ms. Crouse, a force behind the creation of the 40-year-old TKTS booth, also helped revitalize the struggling Lincoln Center Theater.

name: Jerry Coleman
profession: Yankee Infielder, Fighter Pilot and Voice of the Padres
headline: Jerry Coleman, 89, Yankee Infielder, Fighter Pilot and Voice of the Padres
abstract: A pilot in World War II and Korea, he was the most valuable player of the 1950 World Series when the Yankees swept the Phillies.

name: Run Run Shaw
profession: Chinese-Movie Giant of the Kung Fu Genre
headline: Run Run Shaw, Chinese-Movie Giant of the Kung Fu Genre, Dies at 106
abstract: Mr. Shaw and his older brother, Run Me, were movie pioneers in Asia, producing and sometimes directing films like “Five Fingers of Death.”

name: Halton Arp
headline: Halton Arp, 86, Dies; Astronomer Challenged Big Bang Theory
abstract: Mr. Arp was a provocative son of American astronomy whose dogged insistence that astronomers had misread the distance to quasars led to his exile from his peers.

name: Bronson Binger
profession: Saved New York Parks and Buildings
headline: Bronson Binger, 83, Who Saved New York Parks and Buildings, Dies
abstract: Mr. Binger helped wrest Union Square Park in Manhattan from drug dealers but was stymied in an effort to rebuild Wollman Rink in Central Park.

name: Richard N. Cohen
headline: Richard N. Cohen, 90, Dies; Was Director of Times Co.
abstract: Mr. Cohen, who worked in the insurance industry, was on the board of The New York Times Company from 1960 into the early 1970s.

name: Richard M. Cohen
headline: Richard M. Cohen, 76, News Producer Who Wrote of Health Challenge, Dies
abstract: When he was 25, he learned that he had multiple sclerosis. He coped with the disease throughout a long career at several networks, recalled in a best-selling memoir.

name: Elizabeth Jane Howard
headline: Elizabeth Jane Howard, Novelist of Mid-Century British Life, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Howard’s five-part series, The Cazalet Chronicles, traces a British family before, during and after World War II.

name: Carter Camp
headline: Carter Camp, Leader in Wounded Knee Uprising, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Camp was a leader of the American Indian Movement who led the first wave of the 1973 operation to seize Wounded Knee in South Dakota.

name: Al Porcino
profession: First Trumpeter With Leading Jazz Bands
headline: Al Porcino, First Trumpeter With Leading Jazz Bands, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Porcino held the first trumpet chair in bands led by Count Basie, Woody Herman, Stan Kenton, Buddy Rich and others.

name: C. T. Hsia
profession: Brought Chinese Literature to the West
headline: C. T. Hsia, Who Brought Chinese Literature to the West, Dies at 92
