abstract: Dr. Hsia helped introduce modern Chinese literature to the West in the 1960s while teaching at Columbia University.

name: Amiri Baraka
headline: Amiri Baraka, Polarizing Poet and Playwright, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Baraka’s work was widely anthologized, and he was also long famous as a political firebrand, with critical opinion divided in every arena.

name: Robert Nugent
headline: Rev. Robert Nugent, Priest Who Counseled Gay Catholics, Dies at 76
abstract: Before being silenced by the Vatican, he was a founder of New Ways Ministry, which advocated full acceptance of gay people in the church and society.

name: Vincent J. Termine
headline: Rev. Vincent J. Termine, Pastor Who Fought Racism in His Parish, Dies at 93
abstract: Father Termine angered members of his predominantly white flock in Brooklyn when he let black youths participate in organized basketball at his parish in the mid-1970s.

name: Robert Hess
headline: Robert Hess, 57, Dies; Led Homeless Services Under Bloomberg
abstract: Mr. Hess presided over a gradual decline in the homeless population in New York City until the recession of 2009 caused the problem to spike.

name: Nelson Ned
headline: Nelson Ned, Florid Brazilian Balladeer, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Ned’s records and his sentimental style brought him a large following throughout Latin America.

name: Larry Speakes
headline: Larry Speakes, Public Face of Reagan Era, Dies at 74
abstract: He became the press spokesman for President Reagan after his boss, the press secretary James Brady, was wounded in an attempt on the life of the president.

name: Dale T. Mortensen
headline: Dale T. Mortensen, Labor Economist and Nobel Laureate, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Mortensen was one of three economists who shared the 2010 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences for their work on a line of economic thinking known as search theory.

name: Bill Conlin
headline: Bill Conlin, Sportswriter Who Quit After Molestation Claims, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Conlin was honored by Baseball’s Hall of Fame in 2011, the same year a newspaper article detailed several accounts of sexual abuse he was accused of committing.

name: Franklin McCain
profession: Fought for Rights at All-White Lunch Counter
headline: Franklin McCain, Who Fought for Rights at All-White Lunch Counter, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. McCain helped fuel the civil rights movement in 1960 when he and three friends from their all-black college requested, and were refused, coffee and doughnuts at a whites-only lunch counter in Greensboro, N.C.

name: Ariel Sharon
headline: Ariel Sharon, Israeli Hawk Who Sought Peace on His Terms, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Sharon was both vilified and admired for his belief that Jews must assert and defend their collective needs without embarrassment or fear of censure.

name: Judy Protas
profession: Writer of Slogan for Levys Real Jewish Rye
headline: Judy Protas, Writer of Slogan for Levy’s Real Jewish Rye, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Protas knew that a campaign spent selling rye bread to Jews would be a campaign squandered in preaching to the converted.

name: Madeline Arakawa Gins
headline: Madeline Arakawa Gins, Visionary Architect, Is Dead at 72
abstract: Ms. Gins and her husband, the artist Arakawa, advanced theories of design they believed could make mortality a thing of the past.

name: Ian Barbour
profession: Found a Balance Between Faith and Science
headline: Ian Barbour, Who Found a Balance Between Faith and Science, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Barbour embraced the notion of evolution and the Big Bang theory but was also a devoted churchgoer who in 1999 won the Templeton Prize for his progress in the field of religion.

name: Vugar Gashimov
headline: Vugar Gashimov, a Bold Grandmaster of Chess, Dies at 27
abstract: Mr. Gashimov, an Azerbaijani, was renowned for his aggressive play and risky openings.

name: Sam Berns
profession: Public Face of a Rare Illness
headline: Sam Berns, 17, Public Face of a Rare Illness, Is Dead
abstract: Sam’s life with progeria, a genetic disorder resulting in rapid premature aging, was the subject of a documentary film shortlisted for an Academy Award.

name: Robert Pastor
headline: Robert Pastor, 66, Dies; Guided Panama Treaty for Carter
abstract: Mr. Pastor, an aide under President Jimmy Carter, shepherded the 1977 Panama Canal treaties and was punished for it years later, when conservatives defeated his nomination to be an ambassador.

name: Burton R. Lifland
headline: Burton R. Lifland, Bankruptcy Judge in Big Cases, Dies at 84
abstract: One of Judge Lifland’s biggest challenges was sifting through the wreckage of Bernard L. Madoff’s multibillion-dollar Ponzi scheme.

name: Thomas L. Chrystie
profession: Bank Services Innovator on Wall St
headline: Thomas L. Chrystie, Bank Services Innovator on Wall St., Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Chrystie created the cash management account, a one-stop-shopping convenience for the brokerage business.

name: Sheila Guyse
profession: Singer and Star in Race Movies
headline: Sheila Guyse, Singer and Star in ‘Race Movies,’ Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Guyse appeared on Broadway and in so-called race movies of the 1940s and ’50s. She also recorded an album of standards for MGM.

name: Ken Landwehr
profession: Played Key Role in Capture of Serial Killer
headline: Ken Landwehr, Who Played Key Role in Capture of Serial Killer, Dies at 59
abstract: Lieutenant Landwehr, a homicide detective in Wichita, Kan., played a pivotal role in the capture of the serial killer known as B.T.K.

name: Mae Young
headline: Mae Young, Unladylike Wrestler Who Loved to Be Hated, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Young, who pulled hair and took cheap shots, was a Hall of Famer who rose to prominence in the 1940s and fought her last round in 2010.

name: Hiroo Onoda
headline: Hiroo Onoda, Soldier Who Hid in Jungle for Decades, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Onoda was one of World War II’s last holdouts, a Japanese Imperial Army officer who guarded his post for 29 years, returning home in 1974.

name: Suchitra Sen
headline: Suchitra Sen, Actress Famed in Bengali Cinema, Dies at 82
abstract: After more than 50 films, Ms. Sen retired and became a recluse.

name: Arnold R. Pinkney
headline: Arnold R. Pinkney Dies at 83; Steered 1984 Jesse Jackson Run
abstract: Mr. Pinkney, a strategist who ran the campaigns in landmark races for black politicians, also advised Hubert H. Humphrey in his second bid for the Democratic presidential nomination.

name: Chryssa
headline: Chryssa, Artist Who Saw Neon’s Potential as a Medium, Dies at 79
abstract: Chryssa, a Greek-born sculptor, began incorporating neon into her constructions in America in the 1960s, in time mastering the technical difficulties of the medium.

name: Roy Campbell Jr.
headline: Roy Campbell Jr., Avant-Garde Jazz Trumpeter, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Campbell combined a pugnacious, hard-bop sound with an open-minded approach, working with a variety of free jazz musicians and becoming a fixture at avant-garde events like the Vision Festival.

name: Chris Chataway
headline: Chris Chataway, British Runner and Politician, Dies at 82
abstract: Chataway helped Roger Bannister, a fellow Oxford graduate, achieve the first sub-four-minute mile in 1954, and he later became a member of Parliament and a Cabinet minister.

name: Juan Gelman
headline: Juan Gelman, Argentine Poet Who Challenged Junta, Dies at 83
abstract: Social commentary, some of it born of personal tragedy, was just one hallmark of Mr. Gelman’s work.

name: Donald Morton
profession: Melanoma Expert Pioneered a Cancer Technique
headline: Dr. Donald Morton Dies at 79; Melanoma Expert Pioneered a Cancer Technique
abstract: Dr. Morton, who was known as one of the last physicians to treat the actor John Wayne, was at the forefront of cancer research and treatment.

name: Claudio Abbado
profession: Italian Conductor With a Global Reach
headline: Claudio Abbado, an Italian Conductor With a Global Reach, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Mr. Abbado led some of the world’s most revered musical institutions, including La Scala, the Vienna State Opera and the Berlin Philharmonic.

name: Otis G. Pike
profession: Long Island Congressman Took On C.I.A
headline: Otis G. Pike, 92, Dies; Long Island Congressman Took On C.I.A.
abstract: Mr. Pike was a long-term congressman from Long Island who spearheaded an inquiry in the 1970s into accusations that the intelligence establishment had abused its power.

name: John Dobson
headline: John Dobson, an Inventive Itinerant Guide to Stargazing, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Dobson, who developed the first high-powered, inexpensive, telescope for amateur astronomers, wanted others to see phenomena previously visible only to professional astronomers.

name: Martha Beck
profession: Founded the Drawing Center in New York
headline: Martha Beck, Who Founded the Drawing Center in New York, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Beck established the small alternative museum the Drawing Center in SoHo in 1977, and marshaled modest grants to organize exhibitions of major-museum quality.

name: Douglas Davis
headline: Douglas Davis, Newsweek Critic and Internet Artist, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Davis was a critic, an author and an artist, whose work explored the possibilities of video and the Internet as creative and interactive mediums.

name: Leslie Lee
headline: Leslie Lee, Playwright Who Enlarged Black Life Onstage, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Lee wrote more than a dozen stage works, but his best-known play was “The First Breeze of Summer,” which was nominated for a Tony Award.

name: John J. McGinty III
profession: Gave Away His Medal of Honor
headline: John J. McGinty III, Who Gave Away His Medal of Honor, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. McGinty, a retired Marine Corps officer, received the Medal of Honor for saving the lives of dozens of his men during an enemy attack in Vietnam.

name: Michael Sporn
profession: Film Animator Adapted Beloved Childrens Books
headline: Michael Sporn, 67, Dies; Film Animator Adapted Beloved Children’s Books
abstract: His work focused on adaptations of children’s books and included an Emmy-winning collaboration with Ntozake Shange.

name: Chet Curtis
headline: Chet Curtis, Half of Married News Team Whose Divorce Made News, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Curtis and his wife and co-anchor on WCVB, Channel 5, Natalie Jacobson, delivered the news nightly to Bostonians for 18 years before they split up.

name: Shulamit Aloni
headline: Shulamit Aloni, Outspoken Israeli Lawmaker, Dies at 86
abstract: Mrs. Aloni was an early champion of civil liberties, challenger of religious hegemony and outspoken opponent of Israel’s occupation of the Palestinian territories.

name: Ed Hookstratten
headline: Ed Hookstratten, Forceful Advocate for the Stars, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Hookstratten was an unapologetically aggressive lawyer and agent for entertainers and sports figures including Elvis Presley, Johnny Carson, Tom Brokaw and the football coach George Allen.

name: Sarah Marshall
profession: Actress in Twilight Zone and Star Trek
headline: Sarah Marshall, Actress in ‘Twilight Zone’ and ‘Star Trek’, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Marshall also appeared in films like “The Long, Hot Summer” and was nominated for a Tony for “Goodbye, Charlie.”

name: Alex Shear
headline: Alex Shear, Owner of 100,000 Pieces of American Kitsch, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Shear described his collection of pop-culture artifacts, which once spanned 11 storage facilities in three states, as a window into the American soul.

name: Millard L. Midonick
headline: Millard L. Midonick, Surrogate to Children and Auden, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Midonick was a Manhattan Family Court judge in the ’60s who pressed for the rights of children and then later, as a surrogate judge, decided the estates of the poet W. H. Auden and the painter Mark Rothko.

name: Herbert L. Haber
profession: Labor Negotiator in a Strike-Torn Era
headline: Herbert L. Haber, 89, Dies; Labor Negotiator in a Strike-Torn Era
abstract: Mr. Haber was the chief labor negotiator for the City of New York from 1966 to 1973, when labor strikes tested the balance of power between the city and its municipal unions.

name: Martin S. Bergmann
headline: Martin S. Bergmann, Psychoanalyst and an On-Screen Philosopher, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Bergmann became known to a wide general audience for his unplanned, much-praised role as a philosopher in Woody Allen’s 1989 film, “Crimes and Misdemeanors.”

name: Irving Milchberg
headline: Irving Milchberg, Who Smuggled Guns Under Nazis’ Noses, Dies at 86
abstract: As a street urchin in Warsaw, Mr. Milchberg managed to escape being sent to concentration camps while he smuggled guns and food to the resistance.

name: Tom Gola
headline: Tom Gola, a Philadelphia Basketball Legend, Dies at 81
abstract: Gola, still the Division I record-holder in career rebounds, led La Salle to the National Invitation Tournament title in 1952 and the N.C.A.A. title in 1954 before helping the Philadelphia Warriors to the N.B.A. title in 1956.

name: Luis Ávalos
headline: Luis Ávalos, Actor on ‘The Electric Company,’ Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Ávalos, a Cuban-born actor, began a long tenure on the PBS children’s program “The Electric Company” in 1972, when there were few Hispanic faces on television.

name: José Emilio Pacheco
headline: José Emilio Pacheco, Honored Writer Who Wrote of Social Ills, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Pacheco, who emerged as a poet of note in the 1960s, won many awards.

name: Pete Seeger
profession: Champion of Folk Music and Social Change
headline: Pete Seeger, Champion of Folk Music and Social Change, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Seeger, who spearheaded the folk revival that transformed popular music in the 1950s, spent a long career championing song as both a vital heritage and a catalyst for political action.

name: Morrie Turner
headline: Morrie Turner Dies at 90; Broke Race Barriers in Comics
abstract: Mr. Turner was the first African-American cartoonist to be widely syndicated, and his “Wee Pals” comic strip featured a group of racially mixed characters.

name: Bernard Perlin
profession: New York Painter of Varied Styles
headline: Bernard Perlin, a New York Painter of Varied Styles, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Perlin was an American painter who displayed a mastery of light and line across a wide range of work, including wartime propaganda posters, street scenes of New York and effervescent views of Italy.

name: Thomas M. Sherak
profession: Head of the House of Oscar
headline: Thomas M. Sherak, Head of the House of Oscar, Dies at 68
abstract: During a three-year term as president of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, Mr. Sherak sought younger and more diverse members and began a drive to build a museum of world film.

name: John R. Huizenga
profession: Physicist at Fore of Nuclear Era
headline: John R. Huizenga, Physicist at Fore of Nuclear Era, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Huizenga was drafted into the Manhattan Project to help build the world’s first atom bomb and was part of the scientific team that discovered two elements in the periodic table.

name: Riz Ortolani
headline: Riz Ortolani, Film Composer Who Wrote a Love Anthem, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Ortolani was among Italy’s busiest film composers for almost half a century and his music set the tone for everything from erotic films to spaghetti westerns.

name: Pete Burns
headline: Pete Burns, Rodeo Cowboy Who Coached Champions, Dies at 85
abstract: Burns also owned a company that supplied one of the meanest bucking bulls in the history of the sport.

name: Pete Burns
headline: Pete Burns, Frontman for the Band Dead or Alive, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Burns gained fame for the 1985 hit “You Spin Me Round (Like a Record)” and later became known for his plastic surgery.

name: Gary Arlington
headline: Gary Arlington, a Force in Underground Comic Books, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Mr. Arlington was a young man armed with thousands of comics when he opened his San Francisco Comic Book Company.

name: Donald S. Engel
profession: Persistent Contract Lawyer to the Stars
headline: Donald S. Engel, Persistent Contract Lawyer to the Stars, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Engel represented many famous entertainers, including singers, actors and authors, in contract disputes.

name: Theodore Millon
headline: Theodore Millon, Psychologist and Student of Personality, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Millon was a crucial figure in shaping the understanding of personality disorders, and a self-described exemplar of “secure narcissism.”

name: Harold Shaw
headline: Harold Shaw, Manager of Major Classical Artists, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Shaw’s clients included Jessye Norman, Nathan Milstein, John Williams and Jacqueline du Pré.

name: Maximilian Schell
headline: Maximilian Schell, Oscar-Winning Actor in ‘Nuremberg,’ Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Schell was an Austrian-born actor who won an Academy Award for his role in “Judgment at Nuremberg.”

name: Richard Grossman
headline: Richard Grossman, Crusading Publisher of 1960s, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Grossman published Ralph Nader’s “Unsafe at Any Speed,” the 1965 book that helped jump-start the modern consumer movement.

name: Miklos Jancso
profession: Made Stylized Films of War and Tyranny in Hungary
headline: Miklos Jancso Dies at 92; Made Stylized Films of War and Tyranny in Hungary
abstract: Mr. Jancso built an international reputation with a handful of early works, including “The Round-Up” and “Red Psalm,” that were distinct in both style and substance.

name: Philip Seymour Hoffman
headline: Philip Seymour Hoffman, Actor of Depth, Dies at 46
abstract: Mr. Hoffman was among his generation’s most ambitious and admired American actors, playing sidekicks, villains and lead roles on stage and in film.

name: Raymond Weil
profession: Swiss Watches Told More Than Time
headline: Raymond Weil, Whose Swiss Watches Told More Than Time, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Weil started his watch company at a time when most Swiss watchmakers were going bust, and he helped redefine the nation’s signature product.

name: Joan Mondale
headline: Joan Mondale, Who Merged Politics With Art, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Mondale learned the role of traditional political wife early in her marriage, but she expanded her reputation as a supporter of the arts throughout Walter F. Mondale’s career.

name: Jean Babilée
headline: Jean Babilée, Rebel of World Ballet, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Babilée was a French ballet star and choreographer who rejected conventions in dance and life.

name: James J. Gallagher
profession: Educator Focused on Disabled and Gifted
headline: James J. Gallagher Dies at 87; Educator Focused on Disabled and Gifted
abstract: Dr. Gallagher’s work expanded educational opportunities for disabled and gifted children nationwide, and he championed the education of both groups as a civil rights issue.

name: Arthur Ortenberg
headline: Arthur Ortenberg, a Liz Claiborne Founder, Dies at 87
abstract: With a third partner, Mr. Ortenberg and his wife, Liz Claiborne, met the apparel needs of women who streamed into the work force in the 1970s.

name: Russell Hemenway
headline: Russell Hemenway, Champion of Reformist Politics, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Hemenway led a progressive group that developed advanced systems for sorting electoral data and pinpointing areas where it might devote its efforts.

name: Arthur Rankin
profession: His Puppet Animation Was a Holiday Hallmark
headline: Arthur Rankin, 89, Dies; His Puppet Animation Was a Holiday Hallmark
abstract: Mr. Rankin created a canon of children’s holiday television using stop-motion puppet animations, including “Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer,” and “Frosty the Snowman.”

name: Louise Brough Clapp
headline: Louise Brough Clapp, Tennis Champion at Midcentury, Dies at 90
abstract: The former teenage star from Southern California won six singles titles, including four at Wimbledon, as well as 21 doubles championships and 8 mixed-doubles titles in Grand Slam events.

name: Gloria Leonard
headline: Gloria Leonard, Publisher, Pornography Star and Advocate, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Leonard was a pornographic film star, and, later, a publisher of High Society magazine and a spokeswoman for the industry.

name: Ralph Kiner
headline: Ralph Kiner, Slugger Who Became a Voice of the Mets, Dies at 91
abstract: Kiner led the National League in home runs every year from 1946 to 1952, spent half a century broadcasting Mets games and was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame in 1975.

name: Richard Hayman
profession: Pops Concert Figure in St. Louis and Boston
headline: Richard Hayman, a Pops Concert Figure in St. Louis and Boston, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Hayman was an American arranger of pops concerts in Boston, a harmonica player and a conductor.

name: Rene Ricard
headline: Rene Ricard, Art Arbiter With Wildean Wit, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Ricard, a regular in Andy Warhol’s Factory universe, helped popularize the work of Jean-Michel Basquiat and Julian Schnabel, among other artists.

name: Vasil Bilak
headline: Vasil Bilak, 96, Dies; Czech Communist Encouraged 1968 Soviet Invasion
abstract: Mr. Bilak was a former hard-line communist leader who paved the way for Soviet invasion of Czechoslovakia in 1968.

name: Maxine Kumin
profession: Pulitzer-Winning Poet With a Naturalists Precision
headline: Maxine Kumin, Pulitzer-Winning Poet With a Naturalist’s Precision, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Kumin, an author of essays, novels and children’s books, was best known for her volumes of sharply observed poetry, one of which, “Up Country,” won the Pulitzer Prize in 1973.

name: Robert A. Dahl
profession: Yale Scholar Defined Politics and Power
headline: Robert A. Dahl Dies at 98; Yale Scholar Defined Politics and Power
abstract: Professor Dahl, who taught at Yale for 40 years, was a political scientist who was widely regarded as his profession’s most distinguished student of democratic government.

name: Anne Heyman
headline: Anne Heyman, Who Rescued Rwandan Orphans, Dies at 52
abstract: Ms. Heyman found in Israel’s system of youth villages a model for assisting the young survivors of the Rwandan genocide.

name: Christopher Jones
headline: Christopher Jones, Rising Star Actor Who Quit the Field, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Jones, who made only a handful of films, including “Wild in the Streets” and “Ryan’s Daughter,” was often compared with James Dean.

name: K. Lamar Alsop
headline: K. Lamar Alsop, Violinist in a Musical Family, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Alsop, the longtime concertmaster for the New York City Ballet Orchestra, was also the father of Marin Alsop, the music director of the Baltimore Symphony Orchestra.

name: Walter Cottle Lester
profession: Spurned a Fortune in Donating Land
headline: Walter Cottle Lester, 88, Dies; Spurned a Fortune in Donating Land
abstract: Mr. Lester owned 300 acres near San Jose, Calif., and instead of selling it to the highest-bidding developer, he sought to preserve the farmland and open space.

name: Gerd Albrecht
headline: Gerd Albrecht, German Conductor and Lightning Rod, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Albrecht, a German, had a volatile run as the first non-Czech to lead the Czech Philharmonic Orchestra.

name: John J. Cali
profession: Leader in New Jersey Real Estate
headline: John J. Cali, a Leader in New Jersey Real Estate, Dies at 95
abstract: The company he co-founded in 1949 went public as a REIT in 1994, and merged in 1997 to become the Mack-Cali Corporation.

name: Erik Blegvad
profession: Childrens Book Artist With a Subversive Wit
headline: Erik Blegvad, Children’s Book Artist With a Subversive Wit, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Blegvad, a prolific illustrator, possessed a style that was comfortingly Old World; he worked primarily in meticulous pen and ink, with some forays into watercolor.

name: Paul Ash
headline: Paul Ash, Who Made Music Store a Chain, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Ash and his brother, Jerome, developed the music shop their father founded into a chain of 46 stores nationwide.

name: Robert E. Cooke
headline: Robert E. Cooke, Pediatrician Who Helped Create Head Start, Dies at 93
abstract: An adviser to Presidents John F. Kennedy and Lyndon B. Johnson, Dr. Cooke was instrumental in major initiatives to benefit children.

name: Shirley Temple Black
headline: Shirley Temple Black, Hollywood’s Biggest Little Star, Dies at 85
abstract: Mrs. Black, who rose to the height of Hollywood stardom as a precocious little girl in the 1930s, returned to the spotlight in the surprising role of a diplomat in the 1960s.

name: Marty Plissner
headline: Marty Plissner, 87, Is Dead; Led Political Coverage at CBS
abstract: Mr. Plissner was a reporter and writer known for his ability to cultivate sources and for a dexterity in covering primaries that contributed to increased competition among television networks.

name: Nancy Holt
headline: Nancy Holt, Outdoor Artist, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Holt was one of the few women to be a leader in the land-art movement, which places objects for natural settings.

name: Gabriel Axel
headline: Gabriel Axel Dies at 95; Directed ‘Babette’s Feast’
abstract: Mr. Axel’s 1987 film, about a Parisian chef who transforms a Danish village, helped expand popular interest in haute cuisine.

name: Sid Caesar
profession: Comedian of Comedians From TVs Early Days
headline: Sid Caesar, Comedian of Comedians From TV’s Early Days, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Caesar was a force of nature who starred on “Your Show of Shows” in the early 1950s and influenced generations of comedians and comedy writers.

name: Maggie Estep
headline: Maggie Estep, Who Brought Slam Poetry to TV, Dies at 50
abstract: Ms. Estep, a novelist and spoken-word poet, helped popularize slam poetry on MTV, HBO and PBS in the 1990s.

name: Doug Mohns
headline: Doug Mohns, N.H.L. All-Star Who Played for 22 Seasons, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Mohns was a stalwart of the old six-team league, playing half of his seasons with the Boston Bruins and having his most productive period with the Chicago Black Hawks.

name: William Zeckendorf Jr.
headline: William Zeckendorf Jr., 84, Dies; Developer Put Stamp on Skyline
abstract: Mr. Zeckendorf made big bets on big projects that helped refashion neighborhoods from the Upper West Side to Union Square.

name: Ralph Waite
headline: Ralph Waite, Depression-Era Patriarch in ‘The Waltons,’ Dies at 85
abstract: An acting assignment to “pick up a couple of bucks” turned into a nine-year job for Mr. Waite on one of America’s most popular television series.

name: Jim Fregosi
profession: Angel Was Traded for Nolan Ryan
headline: Jim Fregosi, All-Star, Dies at 71; Angel Was Traded for Nolan Ryan
abstract: Mr. Fregosi was a baseball lifer who made six All-Star teams as a player and managed the 1993 Philadelphia Phillies to the National League pennant.

name: Alice Babs
headline: Alice Babs, Who Sang for Ellington, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Babs was already an established pop singer in Sweden when she drew praise for her appearances on Duke Ellington’s “Sacred Concerts.”

name: Pete Camarata
headline: Pete Camarata, Who Fought Fellow Teamsters for Reforms, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Camarata headed the dissident group Teamsters for a Democratic Union, which grew to more than 8,000 members.

name: Hudson
headline: Hudson, Gallerist and Nurturer of Artists, Dies at 63
abstract: Hudson was an art dealer and mentor who ignored trends and kept a mysterious air.

name: Jacques le Sourd
headline: Jacques le Sourd, Theater Critic, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. le Sourd was syndicated nationally in Gannett Company newspapers for three decades.

name: Chad Kellogg
headline: Chad Kellogg, a Speed Climbing Pioneer, Dies in Rock Fall at 42
abstract: Kellogg was one of a small but growing number of climbers who had begun to make speed a priority in ascending a mountain. He died while descending the Patagonian peak Fitz Roy.

name: Stuart Hall
profession: Trailblazing British Scholar of Multicultural Influences
headline: Stuart Hall, Trailblazing British Scholar of Multicultural Influences, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Hall was a Jamaican-born British academic who focused on societal division and blending.

name: Mavis Gallant
profession: Her Stories Told of Uprooted Lives and Loss
headline: Mavis Gallant, 91, Dies; Her Stories Told of Uprooted Lives and Loss
abstract: Ms. Gallant, abandoned as a child, left Canada for Europe to make her name writing about the dislocated and the dispossessed.

name: Alison Jolly
headline: Alison Jolly, Who Found Female Dominance in Lemurs, Dies at 76
abstract: Dr. Jolly, who did not receive as much attention as her contemporary Jane Goodall, found that male primates are not always dominant, upending a bedrock assertion in evolutionary biology.

name: Bob Casale
headline: Bob Casale, Guitarist in Devo, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Casale was a guitarist who was an original member of the influential rock band Devo.

name: James Cahill
headline: James Cahill, Influential Authority on Chinese Art, Dies at 87
abstract: Professor Cahill, a scholar of Chinese painting, interpreted China’s great masters to the West.

name: Paul Colby
profession: Club Helped Fuel Greenwich Villages Rise
headline: Paul Colby, Whose Club Helped Fuel Greenwich Village’s Rise, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Colby was a longtime owner of the Bitter End, a music club where young performers like Bob Dylan, Joni Mitchell, Billy Crystal and countless others were first showcased.

name: Robert M. Fresco
headline: Robert M. Fresco, Oscar-Winning Documentary Filmmaker, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Fresco won an Academy Award with Denis Sanders for their documentary short “Czechoslovakia 1968.”

name: Toshiko
profession: Gritty Runner Was Champion in an Age Group
headline: Toshiko d’Elia Dies at 84; Gritty Runner Was Champion in an Age Group
abstract: A powerful and resilient runner who took up the sport at age 44, d’Elia emerged from the destitution of postwar Japan to achieve renown in the United States.

name: Garrick Utley
headline: Garrick Utley, a Mainstay at NBC News, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Utley was one of a rare breed in television news, a full-time foreign correspondent. He reported from some 75 countries in a career that included 30 years at NBC.

name: Walter Ehlers
profession: Last of Medal of Honor Recipients in D-Day Attack
headline: Walter Ehlers, Last of Medal of Honor Recipients in D-Day Attack, Dies at 92
abstract: The World War II veteran said he remained haunted by the Omaha Beach death of his older brother, who enlisted in the Army in 1940 alongside his younger sibling.

name: Richard Cabela
headline: Richard Cabela, Who Sold the Great Outdoors, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Mr. Cabela founded Cabela’s after he had bought $45 worth of hand-tied fishing flies while on a business trip to Chicago for the family’s furniture store near the Colorado border.

name: Horst Rechelbacher
headline: Horst Rechelbacher, ‘Father of Safe Cosmetics,’ Dies at 72
abstract: He started as a hairdresser making organic hair-care products with herbs and other plants, eventually beginning the company that made natural cosmetics popular in the United States.

name: Terry Adkins
headline: Terry Adkins, Composer of Art, Sculptor of Music, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Adkins brought genres together to create multidimensional works about historic figures and cultural themes.

name: Maria von Trapp
headline: Maria von Trapp, ‘Sound of Music’ Daughter, Dies at 99
abstract: Ms. von Trapp was the last survivor of the singing Austrian siblings made famous by Broadway and Hollywood.

name: Marty Thau
profession: Manager in Early New York Punk Scene
headline: Marty Thau, Manager in Early New York Punk Scene, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Thau, a promoter of bubble gum hits, later managed the New York Dolls. His label released albums by Suicide and the Fleshtones, among others.

name: Harold Ramis
headline: Harold Ramis, Director, Actor and Alchemist of Comedy, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Ramis’s hilarious and sometimes absurd comedy constructs appear in “Groundhog Day,” “Ghostbusters” and other classic movies of the 1980s and ’90s.

name: Simón Díaz
headline: Simón Díaz, Venezuelan Folk Musician Heard Worldwide, Dies at 85
abstract: For over 50 years Mr. Díaz was a presence in the cultural life of Venezuela and surrounding countries, “Uncle Simón” to fans of his cuatro music, radio and television shows and movies.

name: Roy Simmons
headline: Roy Simmons, 57, Lineman Who Later Came Out as Gay, Dies
abstract: Simmons, who played three years for the Giants and went to the 1984 Super Bowl with the Redskins, kept his sexuality a secret until 1992 despite a raucous social life.

name: Ivan Nagy
headline: Ivan Nagy, Star of American Ballet Theater, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Mr. Nagy was especially celebrated as a partner of the world’s leading ballerinas.

name: Paco de Lucía
headline: Paco de Lucía, Master Flamenco Guitarist, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. de Lucía was born into a musical family and became one of the world’s greatest guitarists, finding new audiences for flamenco by blending it with jazz and other genres.

name: Peter Rona
profession: Explorer Found Hot Springs on Ocean Floor
headline: Peter Rona, 79, Dies; Explorer Found Hot Springs on Ocean Floor
abstract: Discoveries made by Dr. Rona, a professor at Rutgers, piqued interest in deep-sea mining and the origins of life on earth.

name: Chokwe Lumumba
headline: Chokwe Lumumba, 66, Dies; Activist Who Became Mayor in Mississippi
abstract: Mr. Lumumba, a civil rights lawyer who once called for an independent black-majority country in the American Southeast, handily won a race for mayor of Jackson, Miss., last year.

name: Alice Herz-Sommer
profession: Found Peace in Chopin Amid Holocaust
headline: Alice Herz-Sommer, Who Found Peace in Chopin Amid Holocaust, Dies at 110
abstract: Mrs. Herz-Sommer, considered the oldest known Holocaust survivor and a distinguished musician in Europe before the war, credited her devotion to Chopin with saving her life.

name: Jim Lange
headline: Jim Lange, Genial Host of ‘Dating Game,’ Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Lange, an affable presence clad in a velvet tuxedo, presided over a hit TV game show that coyly played matchmaker between bachelors and bachelorettes.

name: Dale Gardner
headline: Dale Gardner, Astronaut Who Helped Corral Wayward Satellites, Dies at 65
abstract: Commander Gardner helped lead the first salvage operation in space, steering a jet-propelled backpack to bring the satellites aboard the space shuttle Discovery.

name: Huber Matos
headline: Huber Matos, Comrade of Castro, Then Adversary, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Matos, a commander in Mr. Castro’s army, broke from the Cuban revolution in 1959 over its tilt toward Communism and was imprisoned for 20 years.

name: Valery Kubasov
headline: Valery Kubasov, 79, Russian Who Helped Bring Cold War Thaw to Space, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Kubasov was a cosmonaut when a Soyuz spaceship linked with an Apollo capsule in 1975, some 140 miles above the earth.

name: Phyllis Krasilovsky
headline: Phyllis Krasilovsky Dies at 87; Wrote Children’s Books
abstract: Ms. Krasilovsky wrote several books, including one about a little girl “smaller than a rose bush,” and another about a man who wouldn’t wash his dirty dishes.

name: Lee Lorch
headline: Lee Lorch, Desegregation Activist Who Led Stuyvesant Town Effort, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Lorch’s leadership in the campaign to desegregate Stuyvesant Town, the gargantuan housing development in Manhattan, helped make housing discrimination illegal nationwide.

name: Carlos Gracida
profession: Celebrated Member of a Family Dynasty in Polo
headline: Carlos Gracida, a Celebrated Member of a Family Dynasty in Polo, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Gracida was one of the most accomplished players in the history of polo and a member of a legendary Mexican family in the so-called sport of kings.

name: Lewis Yablonsky
headline: Lewis Yablonsky, 89, Sociologist Who Learned From the Streets, Is Dead
abstract: A rough childhood in Newark informed his academic work, which combined analysis, experiential research and sometimes direct, unconventional efforts to solve social problems.

name: Alain Resnais
headline: Alain Resnais, Acclaimed Filmmaker Who Defied Conventions, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Resnais helped introduce literary modernism to the movies and became an international art-house star with nonlinear narrative films like “Hiroshima Mon Amour.”

name: Eddie O’Brien
profession: Played for Pirates With His Twin
headline: Eddie O’Brien, Who Played for Pirates With His Twin, Dies at 83
abstract: Though only 5 feet 9 inches, O’Brien and his brother Johnny were also basketball stars at Seattle University.

name: Tennent H. Bagley
headline: Tennent H. Bagley, Who Aided, Then Mistrusted a Soviet Spy, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Bagley’s case caused a war within the national security complex over whether the defector he encouraged, Yuri Ivanovich Nosenko, was a Soviet agent sent to trick the Americans.

name: Ralph Bahna
profession: Travel Industry Innovator in Air and on Sea
headline: Ralph Bahna, Travel Industry Innovator in Air and on Sea, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Bahna created one of the first luxury business classes on an airline, turned around the fortunes of the Cunard Line and was the chairman of Priceline.com.

name: Bill Adler
headline: Bill Adler, Author, Editor and Compiler, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Adler collected and published letters children had written to President John F. Kennedy and helped popularize novels written by political, entertainment and sports celebrities.

name: Don Singleton
headline: Don Singleton, 77, Dies; Daily News Reporter Examined Corruption
abstract: Mr. Singleton, who worked for The Daily News in New York for four decades, wrote about gamblers and tax evaders as well as corruption in the Fire Department and its unions.

name: Justin Kaplan
headline: Justin Kaplan, Prize-Winning Literary Biographer, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Kaplan was a biographer of Mark Twain, Walt Whitman and Lincoln Steffens, and an editor of Bartlett’s Familiar Quotations.

name: Sherwin B. Nuland
headline: Sherwin B. Nuland, Author of ‘How We Die,’ Is Dead at 83
abstract: Dr. Nuland’s book, which won the National Book Award in 1994, depicted death as messy and often humiliating, and it urged readers to approach late-life care with tempered expectations.

name: Sean Potts
profession: Master of the Tin Whistle and a Founder of the Chieftains
headline: Sean Potts, 83, Master of the Tin Whistle and a Founder of the Chieftains, Dies
abstract: Mr. Potts learned to play the tin whistle from his grandfather in the 1930s and took stirring solos onstage as a member of the traditional Irish band.

name: Alejandro Zaffaroni
headline: Alejandro Zaffaroni, Entrepreneur on Biotech Frontier, Dies at 91
abstract: The Uruguayan-born biochemist started more than a dozen companies and had a role in the development of the birth control pill, the nicotine patch and the DNA chip.

name: David Barrett
headline: David Barrett, Dogged Graft Investigator in Washington, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Barrett led an inquiry concerning Henry G. Cisneros, who was accused of lying about payments to a former mistress while he was mayor of San Antonio.

name: Robert Ashley
headline: Robert Ashley, Opera Composer Who Painted Outside the Lines, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Ashley stretched the boundaries of opera, choosing not to hew too closely to tradition in his work.

name: Frank Jobe
headline: Frank Jobe, Surgeon Who Saved Pitchers’ Careers, Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Jobe was renowned as the father of Tommy John surgery, a procedure that has been duplicated thousands of times in sports medicine.

name: Ned O’Gorman
headline: Ned O’Gorman, 84, Dies; Poet Founded Innovative Harlem School
abstract: Mr. O’Gorman started his “liberation camp,” the Children’s Storefront, on a dare in 1966 because he wanted to stir students’ imaginations.

name: Martin Gottfried
headline: Martin Gottfried, 80, Theater Critic and Scholar
abstract: Mr. Gottfried was a defender of nontraditional plays, a biographer of figures like Bob Fosse, George Burns and Arthur Miller, and an influential historian of the Broadway musical.

name: Carmen Berra
headline: Carmen Berra, Yogi’s Wife, Dies at 85
abstract: The two met in 1947 — early in the Yankees career of the beloved catcher Yogi Berra — when she was working as a waitress in St. Louis.

name: Richard Boone
profession: Johnson Aide and Advocate on Poverty
headline: Richard Boone, Johnson Aide and Advocate on Poverty, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Boone led private liberal groups pursuing political and social change.

name: Sheila MacRae
headline: Sheila MacRae, Wife in ’60s ‘Honeymooners’ Sketches, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. MacRae, an actress, singer and dancer, was best known for portraying a long-suffering Alice Kramden opposite Jackie Gleason.

name: Gerard Mortier
profession: Opera Visionary and Patron of New Work
headline: Gerard Mortier, Opera Visionary and Patron of New Work, Dies at 70
abstract: His bold theatricality and updating of classical works marked his four-decade career as the leader of some of the world’s most important opera companies.

name: William Clay Ford
profession: Auto Family Scion and Detroit Lions Owner
headline: William Clay Ford, Auto Family Scion and Detroit Lions Owner, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Ford, who never got to run the Ford Motor Company, was the last family member to be a confidant of Henry Ford, the American legend who made the automobile accessible to the masses.

name: Jack Belliveau
profession: Explorer of the Brain Using M.R.I
headline: Jack Belliveau, Explorer of the Brain Using M.R.I., Dies at 55
abstract: Dr. Belliveau was a Harvard scientist whose quest to capture the quicksilver flare of thought inside a living brain led to the first magnetic resonance image of human brain function.

name: Kurt Chew-Een Lee
headline: Kurt Chew-Een Lee, Singular Marine, Dies at 88
abstract: Believed to have been the first Asian-American officer in the Marine, Major Lee led troops into battle against the Chinese in Korea and was cited for bravery.

name: Joseph Sax
headline: Joseph Sax, Who Pioneered Environmental Law, Dies at 78
abstract: Professor Sax formulated a far-reaching legal doctrine that recognized the environment as a public trust and helped fuel the movement in the 1970s.

name: William Pogue
headline: William Pogue, Astronaut Who Staged a Strike in Space, Dies at 84
abstract: Colonel Pogue, the pilot for Skylab’s last manned mission in 1973, went on strike while in orbit to demand more free time to enjoy the view and to think.

name: Roger Hilsman
headline: Roger Hilsman, Adviser to Kennedy on Vietnam, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Hilsman helped draft a cable giving tacit American support to a coup against President Ngo Dinh Diem of South Vietnam, angering some military officials.

name: Wendy Hughes
headline: Wendy Hughes, 61, Actress in Australian Film Surge, Dies
abstract: Ms. Hughes, a film, stage and television star in Australia, was known in the United States and elsewhere for her role in “My Brilliant Career” and other movies.

name: Joe McGinniss
headline: Joe McGinniss, 71, Dies; Chronicled Politics and Sensational Crime
abstract: Mr. McGinniss’s books examined political figures like Sarah Palin and Richard M. Nixon and, in ‘Fatal Vision,’ a notorious criminal case.

name: Bill McLaughlin
headline: Bill McLaughlin, CBS News Correspondent, Dies at 76
abstract: In a 27-year television career, he covered the shooting of Pope John Paul II and conflicts in the Middle East and Vietnam, among other pivotal events.

name: Hunein Maassab
headline: Hunein Maassab, Who Developed FluMist Vaccine, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Maassab’s spray used a live version of the influenza virus that had been attenuated, or weakened, so as not to cause the flu.

name: Hal Douglas
headline: Hal Douglas, 89, Superstar of Movie Trailer Narrators, Dies
abstract: Mr. Douglas was a voice-over artist who narrated thousands of movie trailers in a gravelly baritone.

name: Ophelia DeVore-Mitchell
headline: Ophelia DeVore-Mitchell, 92, Dies; Redefined Beauty
abstract: Mrs. DeVore-Mitchell, a former model, agent, charm-school director and newspaper publisher, was a force in opening modeling to African-Americans.

name: Reubin Askew
profession: Progressive Governor of Florida in the 70s
headline: Reubin Askew, a Progressive Governor of Florida in the ’70s, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Askew, a “New South” Democrat who once sought the presidency, was part of a wave of moderate Southern governors in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Robert Rickel
headline: Robert Rickel, a Founder of Hardware Supermarkets, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Rickel and his brothers opened a chain of home-repair stores that offered supermarket-style shopping before Home Depot existed.

name: Joel Brinkley
headline: Joel Brinkley, a Times Washington and Mideast Reporter, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Brinkley won a Pulitzer Prize for The Louisville Journal-Courier and had an admired career as a correspondent for The New York Times.

name: Bob Crow
profession: Firebrand at Helm of British Union
headline: Bob Crow, Firebrand at Helm of British Union, Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. Crow, who led the National Union of Rail, Maritime and Transport Workers, was that rare thing in post-Thatcher Britain: a working-class hero.

name: Mae Keane
profession: Job Brought Radium to Her Lips
headline: Mae Keane, Whose Job Brought Radium to Her Lips, Dies at 107
abstract: Mrs. Keane, one of the so-called radium girls, was employed at the Waterbury Clock Company in the 1920s when a relatively new material, radium, was used.

name: Matthew Power
headline: Matthew Power, Wide-Roving Journalist, Dies at 39
abstract: Mr. Power’s writing took readers from a journey down the Mississippi with modern-day hobos to the scenes of international disasters.

name: Peter Callander
profession: Lyricist of Pop Hits in 60s and 70s
headline: Peter Callander, Lyricist of Pop Hits in ’60s and ’70s, Dies at 74
abstract: Songs that Mr. Callander wrote or co-wrote include “Billy, Don’t Be a Hero,” “The Night Chicago Died” and “The Ballad of Bonnie and Clyde.”

name: Tony Benn
profession: Preferred Politics to an Aristocrats Title
headline: Tony Benn, Who Preferred Politics to an Aristocrat’s Title, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Benn, a passionate figure in the Labour Party, renounced a hereditary peerage to remain in the House of Commons.

name: Jack Kinzler
headline: Jack Kinzler, Whose Ingenuity Saved Skylab, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Kinzler, known as NASA’s Mr. Fix-It, drew on umbrellas and fishing rods to preserve a mission. He also designed a 6-iron for lunar golf.

name: Iola Brubeck
profession: Collaborator and Wife of Jazz Pianist
headline: Iola Brubeck, Collaborator and Wife of Jazz Pianist, Dies at 90
abstract: Mrs. Brubeck was an effective promoter of her husband, Dave Brubeck, and went on to work with him as a lyricist and librettist.

name: Melba Hernández
profession: Confidante of Castro From First Volley
headline: Melba Hernández, a Confidante of Castro From First Volley, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Ms. Hernández became one of the first four members of Fidel Castro’s general staff and helped him during the Cuban revolution.

name: Charlie Porter
profession: Adventurer Scaling Rock and Sailing Seas
headline: Charlie Porter, an Adventurer Scaling Rock and Sailing Seas, Is Dead at 63
abstract: Mr. Porter, a self-taught adventurer and climate scientist, was most famous for the climbing routes he devised up El Capitan in Yosemite National Park in the early 1970s.

name: David Brenner
profession: Stand-up Comic of the Little Things in Life
headline: David Brenner, Stand-up Comic of the Little Things in Life, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Brenner, a stand-up comic and occasional host of “The Tonight Show With Johnny Carson” whose brand of humor focused on the annoying little details of everyday life, had been a mentor to many rising comedians.

name: Mitch Leigh
headline: Mitch Leigh, Who Composed ‘Man of La Mancha,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Leigh had been a writer of incidental music for Broadway comedies when he was given the break of a lifetime, going on to win a Tony Award for “La Mancha,” though he never had another Broadway hit.

name: Ola L. Mize
profession: Honored for Heroics in Korean War
headline: Ola L. Mize, Honored for Heroics in Korean War, Dies at 82
abstract: He initially refused the Medal of Honor, the nation’s highest military award for valor, but finally accepted it on behalf of his men, a recognition presented to him by President Dwight D. Eisenhower in September 1954.

name: Larry Scott
headline: Larry Scott, Bodybuilder Who Inspired Schwarzenegger, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Scott, who won the first and second Mr. Olympia competitions in the 1960s, also became Mr. America and Mr. Universe while influencing a generation of weight lifters.

name: L’Wren Scott
headline: L’Wren Scott, Whose Designs Melded Daring and Sophistication, Dies at 49
abstract: Ms. Scott, who had a romantic partnership with Mick Jagger, designed fashion suitable for the kind of leggy, statuesque woman she was herself.

name: Rachel Mellon
profession: Heiress Known for Her Green Thumb
headline: Rachel Mellon, an Heiress Known for Her Green Thumb, Dies at 103
abstract: A banker’s wife and a drug magnate’s daughter, Mrs. Mellon helped finance John Edwards’s presidential campaign.

name: Clarissa Dickson Wright
profession: Rebel TV Chef in Two Fat Ladies
headline: Clarissa Dickson Wright, Rebel TV Chef in ‘Two Fat Ladies,’ Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Dickson Wright, a former lawyer, became a middle-aged celebrity on a BBC cooking show that was picked up by the Food Network.

name: Samuel W. Lewis
profession: Shuttling Diplomat in Mideast Peace Pact
headline: Samuel W. Lewis, Shuttling Diplomat in Mideast Peace Pact, Dies at 83
abstract: After being instrumental in the accords during the Carter administration, Mr. Lewis was asked to stay on when President Ronald Reagan took office in 1981.

name: Joseph Fan Zhongliang
headline: Joseph Fan Zhongliang, ‘Underground’ Bishop of Shanghai, Dies at 95
abstract: Bishop Fan was arrested in 1955 during a crackdown on Christianity in China and spent more than two decades in prison and labor camps.

name: Sam Lacey
profession: Top Center in N.B.A. and the 1970 Final Four
headline: Sam Lacey, Top Center in N.B.A. and the 1970 Final Four, Dies at 66
abstract: Lacey spent most of his 13 pro seasons with the Cincinnati Royals and the Kansas City Kings, after leading New Mexico State deep into the N.C.A.A. tournament.

name: Randolph Thrower
headline: Randolph Thrower, I.R.S. Chief Who Resisted Nixon, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Thrower lost his job heading the Internal Revenue Service when he balked at Nixon administration efforts to punish its enemies through tax audits.

name: Scott Asheton
headline: Scott Asheton, Drummer in the Stooges, Is Dead at 64
abstract: Mr. Asheton was a founder of the band, which also included Iggy Pop and had a second life when it re-formed in 2003 and toured the world.

name: James E. Stowers Jr.
headline: James E. Stowers Jr., Benefactor of Medical Research, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Stowers founded the company that became American Century Investments and devoted much of his fortune to starting a Kansas City medical institute.

name: David Sive
profession: Father of Environmental Law and Advocacy
headline: David Sive, a Father of Environmental Law and Advocacy, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Sive argued precedent-setting cases and helped establish a string of environmental advocacy groups when such issues had barely penetrated public consciousness.

name: Robert S. Strauss
headline: Robert S. Strauss, Presidential Confidant and Deal Maker, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Strauss was an influential Washington insider and lobbyist, who led the Democratic Party and hopscotched among White House posts.

name: Fred Phelps
headline: Fred Phelps, Anti-Gay Preacher Who Targeted Military Funerals, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Phelps’s Westboro Baptist Church drew scornful attention for proclaiming in rallies that God was punishing America for tolerating homosexuality.

name: Lawrence E. Walsh
headline: Lawrence E. Walsh, Prosecutor in Iran-Contra Scandal, Dies at 102
abstract: As an independent counsel, Mr. Walsh exposed the lawbreaking in the administration of President Ronald Reagan that gave rise to the Iran-contra scandal.

name: Khushwant Singh
headline: Khushwant Singh, Provocative Indian Journalist, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Singh, a diplomat, journalist and a chronicler of the bloody sectarian strife in India, was also known for his wit and bawdy stories.

name: Charlotte Brooks
headline: Charlotte Brooks, a Photographer for Look Magazine, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Brooks gave complexity to the “women’s features” she was assigned to in the postwar years.

name: Jack Fleck
profession: Stole Hogans Moment at 1955 U.S. Open
headline: Jack Fleck, Who Stole Hogan’s Moment at 1955 U.S. Open, Dies at 92
abstract: Fleck, little known until he defeated Ben Hogan in a playoff at Olympic Club in San Francisco, went on to win only two more events on the regular PGA Tour.

name: Murray L. Weidenbaum
headline: Murray L. Weidenbaum, Reagan Economist, Dies at 87
abstract: As chief economic adviser, Mr. Weidenbaum championed a wave of deregulation but quit after a year and a half, unhappy about White House budget-making.

name: Howard H. Callaway
headline: Howard H. Callaway, Strategist Who Helped G.O.P. Rise in South, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Callaway played leading roles in the presidential campaigns of Richard M. Nixon and Gerald R. Ford and served as secretary of the Army under both.

name: Gene Feist
headline: Gene Feist, Founder of Roundabout Theater Company, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Feist was a playwright and director who worked as a public-school teacher when he started the nonprofit organization.

name: Vera Chytilova
profession: Made Daring Films in Czech New Wave
headline: Vera Chytilova Dies at 85; Made Daring Films in Czech New Wave
abstract: Ms. Chytilova was known for films that were formally rigorous even by the standards of the Czech New Wave movement.

name: Adolfo Suárez
headline: Adolfo Suárez Dies at 81; Led Spain Back to Democracy
abstract: Mr. Suárez, who helped fill a power vacuum left by the death of Gen. Francisco Franco in 1975, was a key figure in the country’s transition back to democracy.

name: James Rebhorn
profession: Actor Often Playing a Man in a Suit
headline: James Rebhorn, an Actor Often Playing a Man in a Suit, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Rebhorn appeared in dozens of popular movies and television shows and recently starred on the Showtime hit “Homeland.”

name: Patrick McGovern
headline: Patrick McGovern Dies at 76; Founded Publishing Empire
abstract: The company he founded in 1964, now called International Data Group, or IDG, developed the “For Dummies” instructional reference books and organized technology events, including the Macworld trade shows.

name: Patrick McGovern
headline: Patrick McGovern, the ‘Indiana Jones of Ancient Alcohol,’ Dies at 80
abstract: An archaeologist, he discovered and analyzed the residue of beverages imbibed by long-vanished civilizations and then figured out how to recreate them.

name: Wu Tianming
headline: Wu Tianming, Who Shaped Chinese Cinema in 1980s, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Wu was a movie director and former studio chief known as the godfather of contemporary Chinese cinema.

name: Joseph Kerman
headline: Joseph Kerman, Colorful Critic of Musicology, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Kerman, who disliked the lag of critical thought in music, expressed his opinions vividly, once describing Puccini’s “Tosca” as “a shabby little shocker.”

name: Ralph Wilson
profession: Founding Owner of the Buffalo Bills
headline: Ralph Wilson, Founding Owner of the Buffalo Bills, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Wilson founded the Bills as an original member of the A.F.L. in 1960 and took them to four Super Bowls in the 1990s as the team’s only owner.

name: Jonathan Schell
profession: Author on War in Vietnam and Nuclear Age
headline: Jonathan Schell, 70, Author on War in Vietnam and Nuclear Age, Dies
abstract: Mr. Schell came to public notice in his early 20s with his first book, “The Village of Ben Suc” in 1967. He came to greater prominence in 1982 with “The Fate of the Earth.”

name: Oswald Morris
headline: Oswald Morris, Artful Cinematographer, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Mr. Morris, a British cinematographer, helped redefine the color in Technicolor with filters, fog machines and makeshift devices.

name: Zbigniew Romaszewski
headline: Zbigniew Romaszewski, Physicist Who Resisted Poland’s Communists, Dies at 74
abstract: He played an early role in a seminal workers’ rights group founded in the 1970s, which helped establish the Solidarity movement.

name: James R. Schlesinger
headline: James R. Schlesinger, Willful Aide to Three Presidents, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Schlesinger, a tough strategist, served in posts that included the secretary of defense and energy, as well as head of the C.I.A.

name: Jeremiah A. Denton Jr.
profession: Blinks, Vietnam P.O.W. Told of Torture
headline: Jeremiah A. Denton Jr., 89, Dies; With Blinks, Vietnam P.O.W. Told of Torture
abstract: A Navy pilot who endured years in North Vietnamese captivity, he was later prompted by what he saw as America’s moral decline to become a proponent of right-wing Christian groups.

name: Felix Fibich
headline: Felix Fibich, Dancer and Choreographer, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Fibich, at first an actor, went on to specialize in Jewish dance traditions.

name: Howard Schmertz
headline: Howard Schmertz, Millrose Games Director, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Schmertz, a Bronx native, began attending the Millrose Games at the age of 7 and succeeded his father as the meet’s director in 1975.

name: Don Reitz
profession: Made Dirt and Salt Into Art
headline: Don Reitz, Who Made Dirt and Salt Into Art, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Reitz was one of a small cadre of midcentury artisans who expanded the medium to include immense, intellectually provocative works of abstract art.

name: Leo Bretholz
headline: Leo Bretholz, 93, Dies; Escaped Train to Auschwitz
abstract: Mr. Bretholz testified in Congress in 2011, asking that Holocaust survivors be allowed to sue the French railway S.N.C.F. for its role in Nazi deportations to death camps.

name: Eddie Lawrence
headline: Eddie Lawrence Dies at 95; Comedy’s ‘Old Philosopher’
abstract: Mr. Lawrence, an actor, writer and director, was famous for the Old Philosopher, a character and routine he performed on records, commercials and talk shows.

name: Kate O’Mara
headline: Kate O’Mara, a Schemer on ‘Dynasty,’ Dies at 74
abstract: The British actress often played beautiful but devious characters, including Caress, the sister of Joan Collins’s character on the 1980s ABC soap opera “Dynasty.”

name: Hobie Alter
headline: Hobie Alter, Innovator of Sailing and Surfing, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Alter used a production line and polyurethane foam in surfboard manufacturing, then created the popular Hobie Cat sailboat in the late 1960s.

name: Lorenzo Semple Jr.
headline: Lorenzo Semple Jr., Creator of TV’s ‘Batman,’ Dies at 91
abstract: It seemed as though ABC had a drama in mind, but Mr. Semple immediately saw the absurdity in the character of a wealthy bachelor who enjoyed dressing up as a bat to fight crime.

name: Marc Platt
headline: Marc Platt, 100, Stage and Screen Dancer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Platt was a lively and versatile dancer who had standout roles onstage and in films, including in the original 1943 Broadway production of “Oklahoma!”

name: Frankie Knuckles
headline: Frankie Knuckles, 59, Pioneer House D.J., Dies
abstract: Mr. Knuckles was often called the “godfather of house” for helping that percussive genre of dance music spread from Chicago nightclubs to global popularity and influence.

name: Irene Fernandez
profession: Champion of the Oppressed in Malaysia
headline: Irene Fernandez, Champion of the Oppressed in Malaysia, Dies at 67
abstract: Ms. Fernandez’s indefatigable advocacy for better treatment of foreign workers prompted her government to denounce her and human rights groups to shower her with awards.

name: Charles Keating
profession: Key Figure in 80s Savings and Loan Crisis
headline: Charles Keating, 90, Key Figure in ’80s Savings and Loan Crisis, Dies
abstract: Mr. Keating was a businessman who later went to prison after fleecing thousands of depositors with help from a group of United States senators dubbed the Keating Five.

name: Charles Keating
headline: Charles Keating, Actor on TV and Stage, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Keating’s long and broad career won him a Tony nomination and a Daytime Emmy Award.

name: Jerry Roberts
headline: Jerry Roberts, 93, Code Breaker for Britain
abstract: Mr. Roberts, a German linguist, was part of a top-secret team gathered to decipher messages between Hitler and his field commanders.

name: Hank Lauricella
headline: Hank Lauricella, 83, Last of a Football Breed
abstract: Mr. Lauricella, known as Mr. Everything for his all-around play, was runner-up in 1951 for the Heisman Trophy while leading Tennessee to a national title, then became a Louisiana state legislator.

name: Richard Black
headline: Richard Black, 92, Artist Who Conjured ‘Mr. Clean,’ Dies
abstract: Mr. Black, a commercial artist, drafted the original rendering of Procter & Gamble’s trademark “genie in a bottle.”

name: Robert Slater
headline: Robert Slater, 70, Journalist Covering Israel and Author
abstract: Mr. Slater covered Israel for Time for two tumultuous decades and wrote more than two dozen books.

name: Mon Levinson
headline: Mon Levinson, 88, Op Art Sculptor, Dies
abstract: Mr. Levinson was a prominent Op Art sculptor who used plexiglass and other nontraditional materials in creating work that actively affects the viewer’s perception.

name: Priscilla Morgan
headline: Priscilla Morgan, Cultural Matchmaker, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Morgan was a doyenne of international culture, longtime official of the Spoleto arts festival and all-around facilitator for artists of many stripes.

name: Joan Miller
headline: Joan Miller, Modern-Dance Champion, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Miller’s signature works included social commentary and wit, often about the African-American experience.

name: Sandy Grossman
headline: Sandy Grossman, Maestro of N.F.L. on TV, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Grossman was an Emmy-winning director of football broadcasts who worked with John Madden and Pat Summerall and orchestrated live shows from a production truck.

name: Roger Fessaguet
profession: Wizard of Haute Cuisine in New York
headline: Roger Fessaguet, a Wizard of Haute Cuisine in New York, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Fessaguet, a chef whose influence extended beyond La Caravelle in Manhattan, was known for attracting A-list celebrities and presidents with his approach to classic French cuisine.

name: Philip W. Brickner
profession: Made House Calls to the Vulnerable
headline: Dr. Philip W. Brickner Dies at 85; Made House Calls to the Vulnerable
abstract: Dr. Brickner preached the virtues of home care, but his biggest accomplishment was helping to develop ways to treat people who do not have homes.

name: Curtis Bill Pepper
headline: Curtis Bill Pepper, Author, Reporter and Traveler, Is Dead at 96
abstract: Mr. Pepper, a prolific journalist and author, excelled at finding anecdotes that revealed greater truths about his subjects.

name: James Benkard
profession: Defended Inmates in Death Penalty Cases
headline: James Benkard Dies at 76; Defended Inmates in Death Penalty Cases
abstract: Mr. Benkard was a corporate lawyer who was honored for his work in cases involving the death penalty and prisoners with mental illness.

name: Peter Matthiessen
headline: Peter Matthiessen, Lyrical Writer and Naturalist, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Matthiessen’s nonfiction explored the remote endangered wilds of the world, and his fiction often placed his protagonists in the heart of them.

name: Richard Brick
profession: Drew Films Back to New York
headline: Richard Brick, Who Drew Films Back to New York, Dies at 68
abstract: Named New York City’s commissioner of film, theater and broadcasting in 1992, Mr. Brick worked to bring movie crews back to the city for films like “Last Action Hero,” “Carlito’s Way,” and “Six Degrees of Separation.”

name: Barbara Gibbons
headline: Barbara Gibbons, 79, Writer of ‘Slim Gourmet’ Cookbooks, Dies
abstract: Ms. Gibbons made low-calorie recipes like macaroni-and-cheese, pizza, pancakes, chocolate pudding cake and what she called “man-pleasing beef stew.”

name: Lucy Hood
headline: Lucy Hood, Innovative TV Executive, Dies at 56
abstract: Ms. Hood, president and chief operating officer of the Academy of Television Arts and Sciences, was known for her efforts to expand the purview of television.

name: Mickey Rooney
profession: Master of Putting On a Show
headline: Mickey Rooney, Master of Putting On a Show, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Rooney led a roller-coaster life: the world’s top box-office star at 19, a bankrupt has-been in his 40s and a comeback kid on Broadway as he neared 60.

name: Thomas Polgar
profession: Helped Lead U.S. Evacuation of Saigon
headline: Thomas Polgar, C.I.A. Officer, Dies at 91; Helped Lead U.S. Evacuation of Saigon
abstract: Mr. Polgar, the C.I.A.’s Saigon station chief, urged Americans, in a final dispatch, to learn from their defeat in Vietnam.

name: John Pinette
headline: John Pinette, 50, Stand-Up Comic and Actor, Dies
abstract: A former accountant turned comedian, Mr. Pinette, who was a guest on “The Tonight Show” and “The View,” often dealt in comedy rooted in his own life.

name: Chuck Stone
headline: Chuck Stone, a Fiery, Trusted Columnist in Philadelphia, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Stone was a passionate voice against racism, police brutality and political corruption, with credibility at both the statehouse and street levels.

name: Arthur Smith
headline: Arthur Smith, Musician Who Wrote ‘Dueling Banjos,’ Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Smith had to fight for credit for his best-known composition two decades after it was appropriated for the film “Deliverance.”

name: Zeituni Onyango
headline: Zeituni Onyango, Obama’s Aunt From Kenya, Dies at 61
abstract: Ms. Onyango, who received asylum in the United States after years of living illegally in Boston, had served as Mr. Obama’s guide when he visited Kenya in the 1980s.

name: Edwin F. Kagin
headline: Edwin F. Kagin Dies at 73; Battled Religious Displays
abstract: Mr. Kagin’s many lawsuits included one challenging plans to install a cross-shaped remnant of the World Trade Center at the Sept. 11 Memorial.

name: Ken Forsse
profession: Brought a Toy Bear to Life
headline: Ken Forsse, Who Brought a Toy Bear to Life, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Forsse’s creation was almost impossible for harried parents to find when it burst on the scene in 1985, and it remained wildly popular through the next year.

name: Carl E. Mundy Jr.
headline: Gen. Carl E. Mundy Jr., Outspoken Marine Corps Leader, Dies at 78
abstract: General Mundy opposed allowing openly gay people to serve in the armed forces and helped shape the “don’t ask, don’t tell” policy.

name: Massimo Tamburini
headline: Massimo Tamburini, Sculptor of Shapely Motorcycles, Dies at 70
abstract: An admirer of motorcycles, Mr. Tamburini designed two of the most desirable motorcycles, the Ducati 916 and MV Agusta F4.

name: Wayne Henderson
headline: Wayne Henderson, a Founder of the Jazz Crusaders, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Henderson, a trombonist and composer, was a founding member of the Jazz Crusaders, which blurred the lines between jazz, funk and pop.

name: Mary Cheever
profession: Central Figure in a Literary Family
headline: Mary Cheever, a Central Figure in a Literary Family, Dies at 95
abstract: Mrs. Cheever was part of a tumultuous, complicated and well-chronicled suburban world.

name: James Hellwig
headline: James Hellwig, Wrestling’s Ultimate Warrior, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Hellwig, a star of the late 1980s and early ’90s, was inducted into the World Wrestling Entertainment Hall of Fame three days before his death.

name: Steven A. Shaw
profession: Founder of an Early Blog About Food
headline: Steven A. Shaw, 44, Founder of an Early Blog About Food, Dies
abstract: Mr. Shaw’s open-forum websites became online hubs for chefs, serious home cooks, gourmands and people just looking for a new restaurant.

name: Leee Black Childers
headline: Leee Black Childers, Portraitist of a Downtown Demimonde, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Childers fell in with the Warhol crowd in the late 1960s, capturing images of artists, drag queens, punk musicians and other late-night characters.

name: Jesse Winchester
profession: Writer and Singer of Thoughtful Songs
headline: Jesse Winchester, Writer and Singer of Thoughtful Songs, Dies at 69
abstract: His music celebrated his Southern roots, even though he could not tour in the United States for years after moving to Canada as a draft resister.

name: ‘Sweet’ Lou Hudson
profession: Jump Shot Master With the Hawks
headline: ‘Sweet’ Lou Hudson, Jump Shot Master With the Hawks, Dies at 69
abstract: A reliable scorer in the N.B.A., Hudson was a six-time All-Star and named humanitarian of the year in 2003 by an association of retired players.

name: Rivka Haut
profession: Championed Rights of Orthodox Jewish Women
headline: Rivka Haut, Dies at 71; Championed Rights of Orthodox Jewish Women
abstract: Ms. Haut fought to make it easier to obtain divorces in rabbinical courts and organized prayers at the Western Wall in Jerusalem.

name: Carol Grimaldi
headline: Carol Grimaldi, Co-Founder of Lauded Brooklyn Pizzeria, Dies at 76
abstract: Her good-natured enforcement of the customer code — no slices, no deliveries, no credit cards — became part of the lore of Grimaldi’s Pizzeria.

name: Fred Ho
profession: Composer and Musician in Popular Avant-Gard
headline: Fred Ho, Composer and Musician in ‘Popular Avant-Gard,’ Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Ho, who considered himself a “popular avant-gardist,” mixed jazz with popular and traditional elements of what he called Afro-Asian culture.

name: Ron Pundak
headline: Ron Pundak, a Key Israeli in Oslo Accords, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Pundak was an academic enlisted to take part in the secret negotiations with Palestinian officials that led to a historic agreement.

name: Charles Fager
profession: Lent Name to a Racetrack Champion
headline: Dr. Charles Fager, Dies at 90; Lent Name to a Racetrack Champion
abstract: Dr. Fager, who saved a trainer’s life, advanced the understanding and treatment of spinal disorders.

name: Gregory White Smith
headline: Gregory White Smith, Pollock Biographer, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Smith was co-author of a controversial 1990 biography of Pollock that asserted the artist had homosexual relationships.

name: Phyllis Frelich
headline: Phyllis Frelich, Tony-Winning Actress and Deaf Activist, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Frelich starred on Broadway in 1980 in “Children of a Lesser God,” a play she had inspired Mark Medoff to write.

name: Zander Hollander
headline: Zander Hollander, Sports Trivia Shepherd, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Hollander found a niche by annually providing statistics, team rosters, records, schedules and predictions for the coming season.

name: Sue Townsend
headline: Sue Townsend, Creator of Adrian Mole Books, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. Townsend beat the odds of a difficult early life to become one of Britain’s most popular writers.

name: Otto Petersen
headline: Otto Petersen, the Voice of Vulgarity, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Petersen was the flesh-and-blood half of Otto and George, a comedy team whose act was so scurrilous that it once proved too much for a historically thick-skinned crowd.

name: Alan Davie
headline: Alan Davie, Painter With a Global Bent, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Davie appropriated mythical and mystical imagery from various cultures, including Navajo, Celtic, Caribbean, aboriginal Australian and ancient Egyptian.

name: F. Reid Buckley
headline: F. Reid Buckley, Novelist and Columnist, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Buckley, brother to former Senator James L. Buckley and the conservative commentator William F. Buckley Jr., preferred the South to New York’s literary scene.

name: Warren Forma
headline: Warren Forma, Documentary Filmmaker, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Forma profiled nearly two dozen artists on “Artists at Work,” a series of television programs. Some of his films were screened at museums.

name: Basil A. Paterson
profession: Power in Harlem With Statewide Reach
headline: Basil A. Paterson, 87, a Power in Harlem With Statewide Reach, Dies
abstract: Mr. Paterson, the father of former Gov. David A. Paterson, influenced black political power in New York City and the state for decades.

name: Gabriel García Márquez
headline: Gabriel García Márquez, Conjurer of Literary Magic, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. García Márquez, who received the Nobel Prize for Literature in 1982, wrote fiction rooted in a mythical Latin American landscape of his own creation.

name: Nina Cassian
profession: Romanian Poet Exiled for Skewering Regime
headline: Nina Cassian, Romanian Poet Exiled for Skewering Regime, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Cassian sought refuge in the United States after her poems satirizing the regime of President Nicolae Ceausescu fell into the hands of the secret police.

name: Jacques Servier
profession: Accused of Hiding the Risks of Drugs
headline: Jacques Servier, 92, Dies; Accused of Hiding the Risks of Drugs
abstract: Laboratoires Servier, the pharmaceutical company founded by Mr. Servier, was hailed as a champion of French business until its diabetes drug was withdrawn.

name: Lois Wallace
headline: Lois Wallace, a Respected Agent of Prominent Authors, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Wallace formed a small but prestigious literary agency that represented Erich Segal, William F. Buckley Jr., Joan Didion and Don DeLillo.

name: Cheo Feliciano
headline: Cheo Feliciano, Debonair Salsa Singer, Dies at 78
abstract: The Puerto Rican-born musician helped introduce Latin music to mainstream America.

name: Michael Janeway
profession: Former Editor of The Boston Globe
headline: Michael Janeway, Former Editor of The Boston Globe, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Janeway was also executive editor of The Atlantic Monthly and the author of two books on the decline of democracy and journalism.

name: Adrianne Wadewitz
headline: Adrianne Wadewitz, 37, Wikipedia Editor, Dies in Rock Climbing Fall
abstract: Ms. Wadewitz, a literature scholar, completed more than 49,000 edits on the online encyclopedia, focusing on women’s biographies.

name: Gene Estess
profession: Left Wall Street to Aid the Poor
headline: Gene Estess, Who Left Wall Street to Aid the Poor, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Estess left the financial world to lead the Jericho Project, which serves homeless, mentally ill and addicted people in Harlem and the South Bronx.

name: Jacob Birnbaum
profession: Civil Rights Champion of Soviet Jews
headline: Jacob Birnbaum, Civil Rights Champion of Soviet Jews, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Birnbaum sought to improve the lives of Soviet Jews and contributed to legislation that liberalized Moscow’s emigration policies.

name: Rubin Carter
headline: Rubin (Hurricane) Carter, Boxer Found Wrongly Convicted, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Carter, whose case gained international attention, was twice convicted of murder and imprisoned for 19 years before the charges were dismissed.

name: John Shirley-Quirk
headline: John Shirley-Quirk, a Bass-Baritone and Specialist in Britten, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Shirley-Quirk was a British chemistry teacher who almost by accident became a renowned bass-baritone, making 30 appearances at the Met.

name: Doris Pilkington Garimara
headline: Doris Pilkington Garimara, Aboriginal Novelist, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Garimara’s 1996 novel, “Follow the Rabbit-Proof Fence,” helped awaken Australians to the plight of the Aborigines and was made into a film.

name: Harris Goldsmith
headline: Harris Goldsmith, Critic and Classical Pianist, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Goldsmith, a contributor to High Fidelity magazine, among other publications, was best known for his recordings of the Beethoven sonatas.

name: Hamish Maxwell
headline: Hamish Maxwell, Philip Morris Empire Builder, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Maxwell’s acquisitions helped Philip Morris become a consumer products giant.

name: U Win Tin
profession: Writer Jailed and Tortured in Myanmar for 19 Years
headline: U Win Tin, Writer Jailed and Tortured in Myanmar for 19 Years, Dies
abstract: An opponent of his country’s junta, Mr. Win Tin helped found the political party led by the Nobel laureate Daw Aung San Suu Kyi.

name: Phillip Hayes Dean
headline: Phillip Hayes Dean, the Playwright of Divisive ‘Paul Robeson,’ Dies at 83
abstract: “Paul Robeson,” which starred James Earl Jones and opened on Broadway in 1978, was considered by black intellectuals to be insufficiently complex and eventually derailed the writer’s career.

name: L. Jay Oliva
profession: Led the Rise of N.Y.U. in the 90s
headline: L. Jay Oliva, Who Led the Rise of N.Y.U. in the ’90s, Dies at 80
abstract: Professor Oliva, the first N.Y.U. faculty member to rise to the presidency, began a marketing campaign that helped triple the number of applicants.

name: Connie Marrero
profession: Pitcher Starred in Cuba and the Majors
headline: Connie Marrero, 102, Dies; Pitcher Starred in Cuba and the Majors
abstract: Mr. Marrero was 39 when he reached the major leagues with the 1950 Washington Senators and the oldest former major leaguer before he died.

name: Richard H. Hoggart
headline: Richard H. Hoggart, ‘Lady Chatterley’s’ Savior, Dies at 95
abstract: In a landmark obscenity case, Professor Hoggart testified in defense of a novel censored in Britain for more than three decades.

name: Steve Backer
profession: Force for Jazz at Major Labels
headline: Steve Backer, a Force for Jazz at Major Labels, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Backer, who ran jazz programs at major record labels, shaped the careers of musicians like Anthony Braxton and Henry Threadgill, as well as crossover bands like the Brecker Brothers.

name: Alistair MacLeod
headline: Alistair MacLeod, a Novelist in No Hurry, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. MacLeod, a Canadian author, won the International Impac Dublin Literary Award in 2001 for his novel “No Great Mischief.”

name: Robert Gray
headline: Robert Gray, a Powerhouse in Washington, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Gray, a Washington lobbyist and public relations expert, was a regular on the capital’s social scene and well known for his powerful connections.

name: Michael Glawogger
headline: Michael Glawogger, Who Filmed Lives of Desperation, Dies at 54
abstract: An Austrian documented the world’s grimmer corners, where prostitutes and scavengers and the grindingly poor live.

name: Earl Morrall
headline: Earl Morrall Is Dead at 79; Led 2 Teams to Super Bowl
abstract: Replacing Johnny Unitas and then Bob Griese, Morrall led the Baltimore Colts and the Miami Dolphins to Super Bowls in the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Daniel Anker
headline: Daniel Anker, Maker of Powerful Documentaries, Dies at 50
abstract: Mr. Anker was known for documentaries that he directed or produced, including those about the “Scottsboro boys” and Hollywood’s response to the Holocaust.

name: Chen Yizi
profession: Top Adviser Forced to Flee China
headline: Chen Yizi, a Top Adviser Forced to Flee China, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Chen, a close ally of Zhao Ziyang, sought to rally intellectuals and party moderates to support the student protests at Tiananmen Square.
