name: Douglas L. Coleman
profession: Found a Genetic Cause of Obesity
headline: Douglas L. Coleman, 82, Dies; Found a Genetic Cause of Obesity
abstract: Dr. Coleman upset scientific dogma by discovering that genes — not willpower, eating habits or other behaviors — could cause obesity in some people.

name: Hans Hollein
headline: Hans Hollein, Inventive Architect Who Designed With Wit, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Hollein, a Pritzker Prize winner, used not just line but unusual surfaces to make his artistic points.

name: George McDonald
profession: Union Leader Helped Save Newspaper Jobs
headline: George McDonald, 90, Dies; Union Leader Helped Save Newspaper Jobs
abstract: Mr. McDonald helped navigate organized labor’s orderly retreat from its peak of power in the industry in New York and, by some accounts, helped preserve the city’s surviving tabloids.

name: George McDonald
headline: George McDonald, Power Broker for the Powerless, Dies at 76
abstract: He went from an impoverished activist to the president of the Doe Fund, which has helped thousands of homeless people and ex-convicts in New York City find shelter and employment.

name: David W. Burke
headline: David W. Burke, Trusted Aide to Powerful Men, Dies at 78
abstract: An adviser to politicians and businessmen, Mr. Burke became president of CBS News and was appointed chairman of the Broadcasting Board of Governors by President Bill Clinton.

name: John Houbolt
headline: John Houbolt, NASA Innovator Behind Lunar Module, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Houbolt argued for a smaller and less expensive option for a moon shot — a Chevrolet, not a Cadillac, he liked to say — called a lunar orbit rendezvous.

name: Michael Heisley
headline: Michael Heisley, Who Rebuilt N.B.A.’s Grizzlies, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Heisley, a co-founder and chairman of the Heico Companies, bought the floundering Vancouver Grizzlies in 2000 and soon moved them to Memphis.

name: Paul Robeson Jr.
headline: Paul Robeson Jr., Activist and Author, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Robeson aimed to teach new generations about his father’s radical politics and criticized those he thought misrepresented his life.

name: Anthony Marriott
headline: Anthony Marriott, Author of ‘No Sex Please, We’re British’, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Marriott was best known for farcical work, like the long-running play “No Sex Please, We’re British.”

name: Jack Ramsay
headline: Jack Ramsay, Who Led Blazers to 1977 N.B.A. Title, Dies at 89
abstract: One of pro basketball’s keenest coaching minds, Ramsay, who was known as Dr. Jack, spent more than 60 years in basketball as a player, head coach and broadcast analyst.

name: Edgar Laprade
profession: Center and Gentleman on the Ice
headline: Edgar Laprade, Center and Gentleman on the Ice, Dies at 94
abstract: Laprade was the N.H.L.’s rookie of the year in 1945-46 and was inducted into the Hall of Fame.

name: DJ Rashad
headline: DJ Rashad, Chicago Dance Music Producer, Dies at 34
abstract: Rashad Harden helped bring footwork, a style of Chicago dance music, to a global audience.

name: William H. Honan
headline: William H. Honan, Journalist and Author, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Honan was a culture editor for The New York Times and the author of several books.

name: Frederic Schwartz
headline: Frederic Schwartz, 63, Dies; Designed Sept. 11 Memorials
abstract: Mr. Schwartz was on a street corner near his home in Manhattan, just 10 blocks away, when he watched the trade center’s towers collapse in 2001.

name: Bob Hoskins
headline: Bob Hoskins, Actor Who Combined Charm and Menace, Dies at 71
abstract: The bullet-shaped film star played the hero in “Who Framed Roger Rabbit’' and ruthless British gangsters in “The Long Good Friday” and “Mona Lisa.”

name: Walter R. Walsh
headline: Walter R. Walsh Dies at 106; Terrorized Gangsters and Targets
abstract: Mr. Walsh, an F.B.I. legend in the 1930s who joined the Marines during World War II, was still winning handgun awards and coaching Olympic marksmen at 90.

name: Stefanie Zweig
headline: Stefanie Zweig, Author Who Fled Nazis to Kenya, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Zweig wrote “Nowhere in Africa,” a best-selling autobiographical novel that became the inspiration for an Oscar-winning film.

name: Al Feldstein
headline: Al Feldstein, the Soul of Mad Magazine, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Feldstein took over a fledgling humor magazine called Mad in 1956 and made it a popular, profitable and enduring wellspring of American satire.

name: Frank Budd
profession: Once Known as Worlds Fastest Human
headline: Frank Budd, Once Known as World’s Fastest Human, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Budd, a senior at Villanova University, set the record for the 100-yard dash at 9.2 seconds in 1961, a year after competing at the Rome Olympics.

name: Dennis Kamakahi
headline: Dennis Kamakahi, 61, Hawaiian Guitarist and Composer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Kamakahi, a Grammy Award-winning virtuoso of the slack-key guitar tradition, composed roughly 500 songs, many of which have become beloved Hawaiian standards.

name: Nan Rosenthal
headline: Nan Rosenthal, Curator Who Championed Modern Art, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Rosenthal helped bring the 20th century to the National Gallery of Art in Washington and the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York.

name: Juan Formell
headline: Juan Formell, 71, Cuban Dance-Band Leader, Dies
abstract: Mr. Formell, the founder of Los Van Van, created an infectious, popular hybrid of Afro-Cuban music that influenced salsa performers like Ruben Blades.

name: Anthony Drexel Duke
headline: Anthony Drexel Duke, 95, Dies; Scion of Wealth Aided Underprivileged
abstract: Determined to open a camp for disadvantaged youth, Mr. Duke established Boys & Girls Harbor, which has served more than 50,000 children over the years.

name: Assi Dayan
profession: Celebrated Actor and Filmmaker in Israel
headline: Assi Dayan, a Celebrated Actor and Filmmaker in Israel, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Dayan, recognized for his contributions to Israeli culture, was also the son of Moshe Dayan, a charismatic figure in the Israeli military and government.

name: Marsha Mehran
headline: Marsha Mehran, Writer of Iranians’ Irish Experience, Dies at 36
abstract: Ms. Mehran, who wrote “Pomegranate Soup” and “Rosewater and Soda Bread,” planned a series of seven novels depicting the life of Iranians in Ireland.

name: Nicholas Martin
profession: Stage Director in New York and New England
headline: Nicholas Martin, 75, Stage Director in New York and New England, Dies
abstract: Mr. Martin was an artistic director of Huntington Theater Company in Boston and also brought productions to Broadway, including “The 39 Steps” and “Vanya and Sonia and Masha and Spike.”

name: Efrem Zimbalist Jr.
profession: Star of 77 Sunset Strip and The F.B.I
headline: Efrem Zimbalist Jr., Star of ‘77 Sunset Strip’ and ‘The F.B.I.’, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Zimbalist was an actor whose mellifluous voice and air of European sophistication left a distinctive stamp on two popular television crime series.

name: Gerald Guralnik
headline: Gerald Guralnik, a ‘God Particle’ Pioneer, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Guralnik is one of six pioneering physicists who in the 1960s came up with a theory that would lead to the discovery of a subatomic particle.

name: Myer Kripke
headline: Rabbi Myer Kripke, Early Buffett Friend and Investor, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Kripke lived modestly in a $900-a-month apartment despite making more than $25 million through investments.

name: Gary Becker
headline: Gary Becker, 83, Nobel Laureate, Dies; Applied Economics to Everyday Life
abstract: Professor Becker, the 1992 Nobel winner in economics, was original and provocative in research on marriage, crime, addiction and racial discrimination.

name: James Oberstar
profession: Congressman Ousted in Tea Party Tide
headline: James Oberstar, 79, Congressman Ousted in Tea Party Tide, Dies
abstract: Mr. Oberstar, a Democrat, served in the House for 36 years and led the Transportation Committee before a Tea Party-backed candidate defeated him in 2010.

name: George H. Heilmeier
headline: George H. Heilmeier, an Inventor of LCDs, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Heilmeier in the 1960s helped invent a kind of screen display that used liquid crystals to project images — technology that is now ubiquitous in telephones, digital watches, computer monitors and flat-screen televisions.

name: Jack Agüeros
headline: Jack Agüeros, a Champion of El Barrio, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Agüeros went from a childhood in East Harlem to defending its Puerto Rican people as an antipoverty official as well as celebrating its culture by expanding and moving El Museo del Barrio.

name: Roy Thompson Jr.
headline: Roy Thompson Jr., War Hero Who Played Himself in Movie, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Thompson was a decorated officer during the Korean War who, while still on duty, starred as himself in a Hollywood movie that was shot entirely on location.

name: Alan J. Friedman
profession: Revived Hall of Science in Queens
headline: Alan J. Friedman, Who Revived Hall of Science in Queens, Dies at 71
abstract: A physicist, Dr. Friedman was an advocate for museums of all types, arguing for their importance and independence and standing up to Mayor Rudolph W. Giuliani.

name: Glen Stassen
headline: Glen Stassen, Theologian, Dies at 78; Championed Nuclear Disarmament
abstract: Dr. Stassen helped define the social-justice wing of the evangelical movement in the 1980s and advance disarmament talks in the Cold War’s last years.

name: Kenneth Tomlinson
headline: Kenneth Tomlinson, Conservative Voice in Broadcast Oversight, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Tomlinson was a journalist who used his leadership role in federal communications agencies to counter what he regarded as liberal bias.

name: Farley Mowat
headline: Farley Mowat, Author, Dies at 92; a Champion of the Far North
abstract: Mr. Mowat was widely known for a 1963 book, “Never Cry Wolf,” in which he recounted his adventures as a biologist on a solo mission to study Arctic wolves.

name: Tatiana Samoilova
profession: Movie Star Behind the Iron Curtain
headline: Tatiana Samoilova, a Movie Star Behind the Iron Curtain, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Samoilova, a doe-eyed beauty who was compared to Audrey Hepburn, discovered the limitations of working within Moscow’s film bureaucracy.

name: Bill H. Dana
headline: Bill H. Dana, Pilot Who Outflew Bullets and Touched Space for NASA, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Dana flew the X-15 rocket plane at record supersonic speeds and tested many of the most innovative and dangerous aircraft ever developed.

name: Bill Dana
profession: Comic Best Known for José Jiménez Character
headline: Bill Dana, Comic Best Known for José Jiménez Character, Dies at 92
abstract: The comedian and comedy writer provoked anger as well as laughter with his English-mangling character, but insisted that it was not an ethnic caricature.

name: Billy Frank Jr.
profession: Defiant Fighter for Native Fishing Rights
headline: Billy Frank Jr., 83, Defiant Fighter for Native Fishing Rights
abstract: Mr. Frank fought Washington State to honor treaties written in the 1850s giving Native Americans the right to fish.

name: William Ash
headline: William Ash, Danger-Loving Escape Artist, Dies at 96
abstract: Before World War II ended, Mr. Ash had attempted 13 escapes from Nazi P.O.W. camps and made it outside the barbed wire a half dozen times.

name: Maria Lassnig
profession: Painter of Self From the Inside Out
headline: Maria Lassnig, Painter of Self From the Inside Out, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Lassnig’s portraits reflected “body awareness,” a Surrealist-influenced method of painting only her mental perception of herself and her feelings.

name: Bill Nunn
headline: Bill Nunn, Scout Who Shaped Steelers’ Super Bowl Teams, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Nunn parlayed his knowledge of football at historically black colleges into a job with the Pittsburgh Steelers and helped them win four Super Bowls from 1975 to 1980.

name: Bill Nunn
profession: Played Radio Raheem in Do the Right Thing
headline: Bill Nunn, Who Played Radio Raheem in ‘Do the Right Thing,’ Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Nunn starred in several movies by the director Spike Lee, but he made his greatest mark in the 1989 role as Radio Raheem.

name: Ben Hoberman
headline: Ben Hoberman, 91, Pioneer of All-Talk Radio, Is Dead
abstract: In 1960, Mr. Hoberman transformed the music station KABC in Los Angeles into what is generally considered the country’s first 24-hour all-talk station.

name: Joe Wilder
headline: Joe Wilder, Horn Player, Dies at 92; Elegance Was His Theme Song
abstract: Mr. Wilder worked with Count Basie, Lionel Hampton and Dizzy Gillespie and helped integrate Broadway, radio and television orchestras.

name: Lem Johns
headline: Lem Johns, Who Guarded Johnson in Dallas, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Johns, a Secret Service agent, received an award for his actions in responding to the sound of gunfire when President John F. Kennedy was assassinated.

name: Charles Marowitz
headline: Charles Marowitz, Iconoclastic Director and Playwright, Dies at 82
abstract: Irrepressible and opinionated, Mr. Marowitz led an unusual theatrical life in England and the United States as a director, playwright, teacher and critic.

name: Patrick J. Lucey
headline: Patrick J. Lucey, Governor and Vice-Presidential Candidate, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Lucey, of Wisconsin, ran on an independent ticket with John B. Anderson in 1980 and was an ambassador to Mexico.

name: Lynn Williams
headline: Lynn Williams, 89, Who Led Steelworkers Union, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Williams added 100,000 new members to the ranks of the United Steel Workers union and pioneered strategies for obtaining lasting benefits for workers.

name: William Coughlin
headline: William Coughlin, 91, Editor, Dies; His Newspaper Exposed Fouled Water
abstract: Mr. Coughlin, the editor of a small North Carolina paper, oversaw coverage that earned a Pulitzer Prize for public service in 1990.

name: George Christie
profession: Steward of His Familys Opera Legacy
headline: George Christie Dies at 79; Steward of His Family’s Opera Legacy
abstract: Mr. Christie inherited the Glyndebourne Opera Festival and squired it to modern international renown, broadening its audience and building a new opera house.

name: Malik Bendjelloul
profession: Oscar Winner for Sugar Man Film
headline: Malik Bendjelloul, Oscar Winner for ‘Sugar Man’ Film, Dies at 36
abstract: Mr. Bendjelloul’s debut feature documentary told of Rodriguez, an all-but-forgotten American singer-songwriter who unwittingly achieved fame in South Africa.

name: H. R. Giger
headline: H. R. Giger, Artist Who Gave Life to ‘Alien’ Creature, Dies at 74
abstract: With a phantasmagorical vision, Mr. Giger fused the human form and the machine in work for films, books and album covers.

name: Colin Pillinger
headline: Colin Pillinger, Who Set Europe’s Eye on Space, Dies at 70
abstract: Dr. Pillinger led a shoestring effort to put a European lander on Mars. It failed to reach the planet, but the mission elevated space exploration in Europe.

name: Judith Cummings
profession: Chief of a Bureau for The Times
headline: Judith Cummings, Chief of a Bureau for The Times, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. Cummings was a participant in a federal lawsuit that accused The New York Times of racial discrimination in hiring and promotional practices.

name: Lorenzo H. Zambrano
headline: Lorenzo H. Zambrano, Head of Cement Giant Cemex, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Zambrano turned a family-owned company into a global enterprise, exemplifying a generation of Mexican business leaders who embraced world markets.

name: William Bender
headline: William Bender, Time Editor and Music Critic, Is Dead at 83
abstract: In a career at the magazine that lasted from 1967 to 1978, he covered the full range of musical styles but considered himself primarily a classical music critic.

name: Mel Patton
profession: Shattered a Leg and Then Sprinting Records
headline: Mel Patton, 89, Who Shattered a Leg and Then Sprinting Records, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Patton, a five-time N.C.A.A. champion at U.S.C., won the 200 meters and anchored the team that won the 4x100-meter relay at the London Games in 1948.

name: Mary Stewart
headline: Mary Stewart, British Writer Who Spanned Genres, Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Stewart was an author of suspense novels early on, but then she became much better known for her fanciful Merlin trilogy.

name: Nancy Malone
headline: Nancy Malone, Actress and TV Director, Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. Malone had success in front of the camera, but turned to producing and directing to stretch her limits.

name: David Balding
headline: David Balding, Producer Who Adopted an Elephant, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Balding staged Broadway and Off Broadway plays but may have been best known for Circus Flora, which starred an orphaned baby African elephant.

name: Elaine Sturtevant
headline: Elaine Sturtevant, Who Borrowed Others’ Work Artfully, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Ms. Sturtevant, an American in Paris, made deliberately inexact likenesses of work by Andy Warhol, George Segal and Jasper Johns, among others.

name: Clyde Snow
headline: Clyde Snow, Sleuth Who Read Bones From King Tut’s to Kennedy’s, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Snow was a master of extracting the secrets of the dead from skeletal remains and a leader in using forensic anthropology in human rights cases.

name: Jeb Magruder
headline: Jeb Magruder, 79, Nixon Aide Jailed for Watergate, Dies
abstract: Years later, Mr. Magruder asserted that Nixon himself had ordered the break-in that set the Watergate scandal — and his own downfall — in motion.

name: Jean-Luc Dehaene
headline: Jean-Luc Dehaene, Former Prime Minister of Belgium, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Mr. Dehaene was blocked from becoming president of the European Union by one vote, Britain’s.

name: William Worthy
headline: William Worthy, a Reporter Drawn to Forbidden Datelines, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Worthy defied borders and the United States government while seeking the truth with his pen and a notepad.

name: Betty Sherrill
profession: Decorator to the White-Shoed and Wealthy
headline: Betty Sherrill, Decorator to the White-Shoed and Wealthy, Dies at 91
abstract: Mrs. Sherrill, a socialite from the South, was an arbiter of taste for New York’s bygone elite, known for her artful but conservative decorating.

name: Don Meyer
headline: Don Meyer, a Coach With 923 Victories, Is Dead at 69
abstract: Don Meyer came back from a near fatal car accident and liver cancer before ending his basketball coaching career with 923 victories.

name: Robert F. Erburu
headline: Robert F. Erburu, Who Led Times Mirror Company, Dies at 83
abstract: During Mr. Erburu’s 35 years at the company, Times Mirror acquired The Baltimore Sun, The Denver Post and the Long Island paper Newsday, as well as television stations, a book publisher and magazines.

name: Sidney J. Blatt
profession: Developed Double Helix Theory of Depression
headline: Sidney J. Blatt Dies at 85; Developed ‘Double Helix’ Theory of Depression
abstract: Dr. Blatt’s theory about two distinct origins of depression — one focused on identity and the other on relationships — guided treatment decisions for a generation of psychotherapists.

name: Jerry Vale
headline: Jerry Vale, Who Crooned Smoothly of Love, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. Vale was a fixture at Columbia Records, where he recorded more than 50 albums and popularized romantic Italian songs in the 1950s and early ’60s.

name: Gordon Willis
headline: Gordon Willis, ‘Godfather’ Cinematographer, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Willis’s work on seminal movies of the 1970s, like ‘Annie Hall,’ made his name synonymous with that pathbreaking decade in American moviemaking.

name: Jack Brabham
profession: Raced and Built Formula One Winners
headline: Jack Brabham, 88, Who Raced and Built Formula One Winners, Dies
abstract: Brabham won three world championships as a driver and four as a car builder in London.

name: Viktor M. Sukhodrev
headline: Viktor M. Sukhodrev, Soviet Leaders’ Trusted Interpreter, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Sukhodrev, often the sole translator during Cold War summit meetings, could shift seamlessly between flawless British and American accents depending on whether he was in London or Washington.

name: Robert Stuart Jr.
profession: Quaker Oats Chief and War Foe in 1940
headline: Robert Stuart Jr., 98, Quaker Oats Chief and War Foe in 1940, Dies
abstract: Mr. Stuart was an heir to the Quaker Oats business and as a law student in 1940 helped found the America First Committee.

name: Leslie Thomas
profession: Author of the Novel The Virgin Soldiers
headline: Leslie Thomas, Author of the Novel ‘The Virgin Soldiers,’ Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Thomas, a best-selling author, used his experience as a soldier to write his biggest success.

name: Arthur Gelb
headline: Arthur Gelb, Critic and Editor Who Shaped The Times, Dies at 90
abstract: By force of personality, Mr. Gelb was a dominant figure in the newsroom at The New York Times, lifting its metropolitan and arts coverage to new heights.

name: Tony Palladino
headline: Tony Palladino, Designer of ‘Psycho’ Lettering, Dies at 84
abstract: While advertising was his bread and butter, Mr. Palladino used his eye and pen to great effect in a broad range of projects.

name: Tadeusz Rozewicz
profession: Fierce Poetic Voice of Postwar Poland
headline: Tadeusz Rozewicz, Fierce Poetic Voice of Postwar Poland, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Rozewicz, whose youth was spent in war, survived to become one of Poland’s most distinguished literary voices.

name: Sante Kimes
headline: Sante Kimes Dies in Prison at 79; Killed and Swindled With Her Son
abstract: Ms. Kimes was serving a 120-year sentence for her role in a pair of gruesome murders that turned her and her son, Kenneth Kimes Jr., into vivid subjects for television writers and newspaper reporters.

name: Vincent Harding
profession: Civil Rights Author and Associate of Dr. King
headline: Vincent Harding, 82, Civil Rights Author and Associate of Dr. King, Dies
abstract: Dr. Harding was a historian, author and activist who wrote one of the most polarizing speeches ever given by the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., in which Dr. King expressed ardent opposition to the Vietnam War.

name: Dobrica Cosic
profession: First Friend Then Foe of Serbias Milosevic
headline: Dobrica Cosic, First Friend Then Foe of Serbia’s Milosevic, Dies at 92
abstract: A novelist and nationalist who served briefly as president of Yugoslavia as its breakup in the midst of sectarian war was already underway.

name: Ernesto Butcher
headline: Ernesto Butcher, Who Managed Port Authority After 9/11, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Butcher, a career civil servant at the authority, took charge of closing the gateways to the city on Sept. 11, 2001, and two days later, gave the signal to reopen the system.

name: Rupert zu Loewenstein
headline: Prince Rupert zu Loewenstein, Rolling Stones Money Manager, Dies at 80
abstract: The Bavarian aristocrat helped the band with matters as varied as financial oversight, divorces, drug charges and tours.

name: Gerald M. Edelman
headline: Gerald M. Edelman, Nobel Laureate and ‘Neural Darwinist,’ Dies at 84
abstract: After receiving the 1972 Nobel for a breakthrough in immunology, Dr. Edelman studied “how the brain gives rise to the mind.”

name: Allan Folsom
headline: Allan Folsom, Whose First Novel Sold for $2 Million, Dies at 72
abstract: It took three decades, but Mr. Folsom’s career finally caught fire beginning with the thriller “The Day After Tomorrow.”

name: Catherine M. Abate
headline: Catherine M. Abate, 66, a State Senator and Corrections Chief, Dies
abstract: Ms. Abate’s campaign for attorney general was derailed by questions about her father’s connection to organized crime. She then became a leader in community health care.

name: André Popp
profession: French Composer of Love Is Blue
headline: André Popp, French Composer of ‘Love Is Blue,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Popp was also known for film scores and for his collaboration on “Piccolo, Sax & Co.” (1957), a popular introduction to the symphony for children.

name: Cornelia G. Kennedy
headline: Cornelia G. Kennedy, a Pioneering Federal Judge, Dies at 90
abstract: Judge Kennedy, whom three presidents considered for Supreme Court openings, drew criticism for what some saw as conservative leanings.

name: Jaime Lusinchi
headline: Jaime Lusinchi, Ex-Leader of Venezuela, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Lusinchi, who was president during economic and political crises from 1984 to 1989, gave his mistress a position of power in his government.

name: Shirley Walton Fischler
headline: Shirley Walton Fischler, Hockey Writer Who Broke a Barrier, Dies at 74
abstract: In 1971, Ms. Fischler became the first woman allowed to report on hockey games from the Madison Square Garden press box.

name: Francis T. Purcell
headline: Francis T. Purcell, Three-Term Nassau County Executive, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Purcell, who was a three-term Nassau County Executive, promoted the development of downtown business areas and the transformation of Mitchel Field.

name: Robert J. Flynn
profession: Shot Down in Vietnam War and Held in China
headline: Robert J. Flynn, Shot Down in Vietnam War and Held in China, Dies at 76
abstract: Downed over southern China, a badly injured Lieutenant Flynn spent five and a half years in a Chinese prison, mostly in solitary confinement.

name: Wojciech Jaruzelski
headline: Gen. Wojciech Jaruzelski, Solidarity’s Foil, Dies at 90
abstract: General Jaruzelski earned a villainous place in history when he suppressed Poland’s powerful Solidarity labor movement, but was later consoled by the idea that his reputation would improve.

name: Bunny Yeager
headline: Bunny Yeager, Pinup Portraitist, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Yeager, a former model herself, produced famed innocently sexual images of the pinup era.

name: Frank M. Woods
headline: Frank M. Woods, Vintner and Ambassador for Sonoma, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Woods, a marketer and lifelong entrepreneur, put Sonoma County grapes on the map with his Clos du Bois winery.

name: Herb Jeffries
profession: Bronze Buckaroo of Song and Screen
headline: Herb Jeffries, ‘Bronze Buckaroo’ of Song and Screen, Dies at 100 (or So)
abstract: Mr. Jeffries sang with Duke Ellington and starred in early black westerns using a nickname that evoked his malleable racial identity.

name: Massimo Vignelli
headline: Massimo Vignelli, Visionary Designer Who Untangled the Subway, Dies at 83
abstract: A self-styled “information architect,” Mr. Vignelli gave Modernist shape to book covers, shopping bags, furniture, corporate logos and, famously, a subway map.

name: Radu Florescu
headline: Radu Florescu, Scholar Who Linked Dracula and Vlad the Impaler, Dies at 88
abstract: Professor Florescu wrote books that sought to identify Vlad, the 15th-century monarch, as the historical inspiration for Bram Stoker’s antihero.

name: Matthew Saad Muhammad
headline: Matthew Saad Muhammad, Boxing Champion, Is Dead
abstract: Saad Muhammad was a fighter known for his bruising style who was abandoned as a child and later escaped homelessness.

name: Maya Angelou
profession: Lyrical Witness of the Jim Crow South
headline: Maya Angelou, Lyrical Witness of the Jim Crow South, Dies at 86
abstract: The memoirist and poet’s landmark book, “I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings,” was among the first autobiographies by a 20th-century black woman to reach a wide readership.

name: Malcolm Glazer
profession: Owner of Buccaneers and Manchester United
headline: Malcolm Glazer, Owner of Buccaneers and Manchester United, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Glazer’s teams won championships in the N.F.L. and the English Premier League.

name: Oscar Dystel
headline: Oscar Dystel, Who Saved Bantam Books, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Dystel, the longtime publishing executive, succeeded by finding books with a shot at popularity and selling them vigorously.

name: Harold Baer Jr.
headline: Harold Baer Jr., Judge Whose Civil Liberties Rulings Drew Fire, Dies at 81
abstract: In 1996, Judge Baer ruled that $4 million worth of cocaine found in a car was inadmissible because the police search of the trunk had not been justified.

name: Storme DeLarverie
profession: Early Leader in the Gay Rights Movement
headline: Storme DeLarverie, Early Leader in the Gay Rights Movement, Dies at 93
abstract: For decades, Ms. DeLarverie roamed Greenwich Village and areas nearby, looking for any form of intolerance as a self-appointed guardian of lesbians.

name: Diego Cordovez
headline: Diego Cordovez, U.N. Envoy and Conflict Mediator, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Cordovez, an Ecuadorean, negotiated the withdrawal of Soviet troops from Afghanistan in the 1980s.

name: Sam Greenlee
headline: Sam Greenlee, Writer, Producer, Government Agent, Dies at 83
abstract: “The Spook Who Sat by the Door,” a film based on Mr. Greenlee’s novel about a black power revolution, was pulled from theaters after three weeks.

name: Melvin J. Glimcher
headline: Dr. Melvin J. Glimcher, Prosthetics Innovator, Dies at 88
abstract: His insights from the fields of orthopedics and engineering led to major scientific breakthroughs, including an artificial limb called the “Boston Arm.”

name: Robert Sallee
headline: Robert Sallee, Who Survived Smoke Jumping Disaster, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Sallee was one of three parachutists to escape a blaze in Montana’s Mann Gulch that killed 12 colleagues and changed Forest Service practices.

name: Bob Bailey
headline: Bob Bailey, Entertainer Who Helped Integrate Las Vegas, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Bailey worked at the Moulin Rouge, the first integrated hotel and casino in Las Vegas, and was named the first chairman of the Nevada Equal Rights Commission.

name: Terry Robinson
profession: Chiropractor and Fitness Trainer to the Stars
headline: Terry Robinson, Chiropractor and Fitness Trainer to the Stars, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Robinson parlayed a chiropractic session with MGM’s Louis B. Mayer into a career keeping Clark Gable, Spencer Tracy, Tyrone Power and other actors in shape.

name: Lewis Katz
profession: Victor in Fight to Own Philadelphia Inquirer
headline: Lewis Katz, Victor in Fight to Own Philadelphia Inquirer, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Katz, a prominent figure in Philadelphia political circles, agreed on Tuesday with his business partner to pay $88 million for The Inquirer, Philly.com and The Philadelphia Daily News.

name: Lee Chamberlin
headline: Lee Chamberlin, ‘Electric Company’ Actress, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Chamberlin, whose career took off when she joined Bill Cosby and Rita Moreno on the funky 1970s show, jumped from children’s television to Shakespeare.

name: Ann B. Davis
profession: Comic Actress Played Maid on Brady Bunch
headline: Ann B. Davis, 88, Dies; Comic Actress Played Maid on ‘Brady Bunch’
abstract: Her Alice Nelson, housekeeper for a blended family, was Ms. Davis’s best-known plain-Jane character. Schultzy, on ‘The Bob Cummings Show,’ was another.

name: Ciro de Quadros
profession: Leader in Ridding Latin America of Polio
headline: Ciro de Quadros, 74, Dies; Leader in Ridding Latin America of Polio
abstract: Dr. de Quadros navigated war zones to lead a successful immunization campaign in Latin America and the Caribbean.

name: Edward Finkelstein
profession: Took Macys to Its Highs and Lows
headline: Edward Finkelstein, 89, Dies; Took Macy’s to Its Highs and Lows
abstract: Mr. Finkelstein turned Macy’s into one of the nation’s smartest, fastest-growing department store chains, only to see it wind up in bankruptcy court.

name: Marilyn Beck
headline: Marilyn Beck, Hollywood Columnist Without the Gush, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Beck was a widely read newspaper columnist and broadcast figure who helped bring an impartial style to the world of celebrity gossip.

name: Roy Goodman
profession: Liberal Republican Stalwart in New York
headline: Roy Goodman, Liberal Republican Stalwart in New York, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Goodman was longtime state senator from the Upper East Side whose ambitions for higher office were thwarted.

name: Anna Berger
profession: Actress With a Gift for Matriarchs
headline: Anna Berger, an Actress With a Gift for Matriarchs, Dies at 91
abstract: Woody Allen and producers of “The Sopranos,” among others, cast Ms. Berger for her specialty: the older ethnic woman.

name: Mary Soames
profession: Daughter of Churchill and Chronicler of History
headline: Mary Soames, Daughter of Churchill and Chronicler of History, Dies at 91
abstract: After wartime service in uniform and as an aide to her father, Lady Soames became an acclaimed writer of books about her family.

name: Don Zimmer
headline: Don Zimmer, Who Lived Baseball for 66 Years, Dies at 83
abstract: As player, coach and manager, Zimmer was variously associated with the Brooklyn Dodgers, the Mets, the Red Sox and the Yankees. He was even married on a baseball diamond.

name: Yuri Kochiyama
headline: Yuri Kochiyama, Rights Activist Who Befriended Malcolm X, Dies at 93
abstract: Mrs. Kochiyama, a Harlem activist who was interned with other Japanese-Americans in World War II, cradled a dying Malcolm X after he was shot.

name: Maxine Greene
profession: Education Theorist Saw Arts as Essential
headline: Maxine Greene, 96, Dies; Education Theorist Saw Arts as Essential
abstract: A public intellectual and author, Dr. Greene was also a kind of Pied Piper at Teachers College, Columbia University, where she taught for a half century.

name: Karlheinz Böhm
headline: Karlheinz Böhm, Actor-Turned-Humanitarian, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Böhm was typecast as heartthrob counts and princes until he starred in “Peeping Tom,” a controversial horror film. He later started an Ethiopian charity.

name: Susan Spencer-Wendel
profession: Memoirist About Living and Losing Life
headline: Susan Spencer-Wendel, Memoirist About Living and Losing Life, Dies at 47
abstract: After learning she had an incurable muscle-wasting disease, she wrote “Until I Say Good-Bye: My Year of Living With Joy” mostly on a smartphone with one thumb.

name: Mary Anthony
profession: Choreographer and Teacher of Modern Dance
headline: Mary Anthony, Choreographer and Teacher of Modern Dance, Dies at 97
abstract: Students of Ms. Anthony included some of American dance’s leading figures, like Donald McKayle and Arthur Mitchell.

name: Peter Glaser
headline: Peter Glaser, Who Envisioned Space Solar Power, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Glaser’s concept for harnessing solar energy was deemed credible enough for the government to spend $20 million studying it, only to conclude it was too expensive.

name: Steven H. Scheuer
profession: He Put the TV Review Before the Show
headline: Steven H. Scheuer Is Dead at 88; He Put the TV Review Before the Show
abstract: Mr. Scheuer provided guidance to viewers with the “TV Key” column and the “TV Movie Almanac & Ratings.”

name: Chester Nez
profession: Navajo Words Washed From Mouth Helped Win War
headline: Chester Nez, 93, Dies; Navajo Words Washed From Mouth Helped Win War
abstract: Mr. Nez helped fashion from his Navajo language a military code so impervious that it helped the United States secure victory in the Pacific in the summer of 1945.

name: George J. Armelagos
headline: George J. Armelagos, Anthropologist Who Told Skeletons’ Tales, Dies at 77
abstract: Professor Armelagos was one of the founders of paleopathology, a discipline at the nexus of biology, medicine, evolution, archaeology and culture.

name: Karen DeCrow
profession: Feminist Lawyer and Author Led NOW
headline: Karen DeCrow Dies at 76; Feminist Lawyer and Author Led NOW
abstract: Ms. DeCrow led the National Organization for Women during the 1970s, fighting for the Equal Rights Amendment and Title IX.

name: Andrei N. Mironov
headline: Andrei N. Mironov, Soviet-Era Political Prisoner and Activist, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Mironov caught on early to the absurdities of Soviet life and later became active in the samizdat movement.

name: Alexander Shulgin
headline: Alexander Shulgin, Psychedelia Researcher, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Shulgin, a chemist who specialized in the creation of mind-altering substances, and who introduced the drug known as Ecstasy for potential therapeutic use, died on Monday.

name: Morris A. Adelman
headline: Morris A. Adelman Dies at 96; Saw Oil as Inexhaustible
abstract: He argued that the world’s supply of oil would never be exhausted because the technology to extract it would continue to improve.

name: David Nadien
headline: David Nadien, Philharmonic Concertmaster, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Although Mr. Nadien’s background was as a studio musician and not an orchestral player, Leonard Bernstein appointed him as concertmaster of the New York Philharmonic in 1966.

name: Rik Mayall
headline: Rik Mayall, British Alternative Comic, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Mayall was an actor, comedian and writer whose work on “The Young Ones” and other television series helped define alternative comedy in Britain in the 1980s.

name: Mona Freeman
headline: Mona Freeman, First ‘Miss Subways,’ Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Freeman was just 14 when she was named Miss Subways, a title bestowed on about 200 young women before the competition was retired 35 years later.

name: Myles J. Ambrose
headline: Myles J. Ambrose, Nixon Drug Czar, D.E.A. Midwife, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Ambrose was President Richard M. Nixon’s first drug czar, but resigned before he could take the helm of the new government arm he had helped shepherd into being, the Drug Enforcement Administration.

name: Martha Hyer
headline: Martha Hyer, Oscar-Nominated Actress, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Hyer, who married the producer Hal B. Wallis, played supporting roles but still enjoyed Hollywood’s high life.

name: Elodie Lauten
profession: Wove Opera From Allen Ginsbergs Poetry
headline: Elodie Lauten, Who Wove Opera From Allen Ginsberg’s Poetry, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Lauter’s compositions defied handy categorization but were performed widely in New York and beyond.

name: Bob Welch
profession: Pitching Ace and Prototype for Todays Power Arms
headline: Bob Welch, Pitching Ace and Prototype for Today’s Power Arms, Dies at 57
abstract: Welch overcame alcoholism in becoming one the hardest throwers of his era, winning a Cy Young Award and pitching in four World Series for the Dodgers and the A’s.

name: Michael Schmidt
headline: Michael Schmidt, 68, Maker of Photographic Narratives, Dies
abstract: Mr. Schmidt worked in black and white and made painstaking studies of subjects like the food industry and the life of his native city, Berlin.

name: Gabriel Kolko
headline: Gabriel Kolko, Left-Leaning Historian of U.S. Policy, Dies at 81
abstract: Professor Kolko, a prolific author, argued that business interests, rather than public priorities, have long been the essential driver of government action.

name: Phyllis Patterson
headline: Phyllis Patterson, Who Revived 16th Century, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Patterson, with her husband, Ron, created the first modern Renaissance fair in an effort “to bring history to life.”

name: Glenn Britt
headline: Glenn Britt, Cable Chief Who Saw Broadband’s Future, Dies at 65
abstract: He was a longtime executive with Time Warner Cable, eventually earning the titles of chairman and chief executive before he retired in 2012.

name: Rafael Frühbeck
profession: Conductor Made the World a Podium
headline: Rafael Frühbeck, 80, Dies; Conductor Made the World a Podium
abstract: A life that began in Franco’s Spain led Mr. Frühbeck to a career conducting dozens of major orchestras.

name: Ruby Dee
headline: Ruby Dee, a Ringing Voice for Civil Rights, Onstage and Off, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Dee, who earned acclaim in “A Raisin in the Sun” and “American Gangster,” sought roles that addressed racial issues and campaigned for civil rights with her husband, Ossie Davis.

name: Jimmy Scott
headline: Jimmy Scott, Singer Whose Star Rose Late, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Scott, whose plaintive delivery earned him a following that included other vocalists like Madonna, Marvin Gaye and Frankie Valli, spent most of his career in relative obscurity before gaining wider appreciation in recent years.

name: John A. Hamilton
profession: Host of Public Affairs TV Programs
headline: John A. Hamilton, Host of Public Affairs TV Programs, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Hamilton was a member of the editorial board of The New York Times before turning to radio and television work.

name: Eric Hill
profession: Created Spot, a Pup Beloved by Toddlers
headline: Eric Hill, 86, Dies; Created Spot, a Pup Beloved by Toddlers
abstract: Mr. Hill’s children’s books have sold 60 million copies in 60 languages and inspired a TV cartoon show.

name: Chuck Noll
headline: Chuck Noll, Coach of Steelers’ 1970s Dynasty, Dies at 82
abstract: Noll took a Pittsburgh team that had been a perennial doormat and turned it into a powerhouse.

name: Lee Hyla
profession: Mixed Rock and Jazz Into Classical Works
headline: Lee Hyla, 61, Who Mixed Rock and Jazz Into Classical Works, Dies
abstract: Critics said that Mr. Hylas’s works captivated audiences with its eclectic originality, propulsive rhythmic force, companionable combination of dissonance and consonance.

name: Alan Douglas
headline: Alan Douglas, Who Mined Hendrix Archive, Dies at 82
abstract: Whether Mr. Douglas’s decision to add new material to posthumous releases of Jimi Hendrix’s music was right or wrong is a matter of debate.

name: Frank Schirrmacher
headline: Frank Schirrmacher, German Newspaper Publisher, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Schirrmacher was co-publisher of the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung, one of Germany’s most respected publications.

name: Casey Kasem
headline: Casey Kasem, Wholesome Voice of Pop Radio, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Kasem, the longtime host of “American Top 40,” was known for his homey sentiment and an optimism that ran headlong into the prevailing spirit of rebellion in 1970s music culture.

name: Ultra Violet
headline: Ultra Violet, Warhol Superstar, Dies at 78
abstract: Isabelle Collin Dufresne, the French-born artist, actress and author known as Ultra Violet, was the beauty among the superstars of Andy Warhol’s glory days at his studio, the Factory.

name: Tony Gwynn
headline: Tony Gwynn, Hall of Fame Batting Champion, Dies at 54 of Cancer
abstract: In his 20-year major league career, all with the San Diego Padres, Gwynn had a batting average of .338, including .394 in 1994. He was inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame in 2007.

name: Frances Foster
profession: Childrens Book Editor With an Imprint
headline: Frances Foster, Children’s Book Editor With an Imprint, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Foster published award-winning authors like Roald Dahl, Peter Sis, Philip Pullman and Louis Sachar.

name: Moise Safra
headline: Moise Safra, Banker and Philanthropist, Dies at 79
abstract: A member of the prominent banking family, Mr. Safra recently invested in several real estate ventures in New York and London.

name: Julian Koenig
profession: Sold Americans on Beetles and Earth Day
headline: Julian Koenig, Who Sold Americans on Beetles and Earth Day, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Koenig, who developed the original campaign for the Volkswagen Beetle, is widely regarded as one of the 20th century’s most innovative advertising writers.

name: Daniel Keyes
headline: Daniel Keyes, Author of ‘Flowers for Algernon,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Keyes’s best-known novel tells of a man who gains and then loses his intelligence. It became the film “Charly,” with Cliff Robertson.

name: John Devens
headline: John Devens, Valdez Mayor During Exxon Spill, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Devens was the mayor of Valdez, an obscure coastal town in Alaska, when it was rocked by the wreck of the Exxon Valdez oil tanker in Prince William Sound.

name: Horace Silver
headline: Horace Silver, 85, Master of Earthy Jazz, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Silver, a pianist, composer and bandleader, wrote and performed music that was both sophisticated and accessible.

name: Stuart Vaughan
headline: Stuart Vaughan, Director and Shakespeare Expert, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Vaughan, who got his start directing the first productions of the New York Shakespeare Festival in 1956, professed a loyalty to the text and an aversion to “revisionist approaches.”

name: Carla Laemmle
headline: Carla Laemmle, Actress Since the 1920s, Dies at 104
abstract: Ms. Laemmle, who was reared on the Universal Studios lot, became a fan favorite at autograph shows and horror-film conventions in recent years.

name: Gerry Goffin
headline: Gerry Goffin, Hitmaking Songwriter With Carole King, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Goffin collaborated with Carole King to write some of the biggest hits of the 1960s.

name: Avraham Shalom
headline: Avraham Shalom, 86, Israeli Spy Chief Who Hunted Eichmann, Dies
abstract: Mr. Shalom led Israel’s internal security agency in a long spying career before resigning under a cloud over the killing of two Palestinian hijackers.

name: Lorna Wing
headline: Dr. Lorna Wing, Who Broadened Views of Autism, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Wing, a British psychiatrist, recognized autism as a mental disorder of many gradations, and she coined the term Asperger’s syndrome for its mildest form.

name: Charles Barsotti
profession: Cartoonist With Humor Both Simple and Absurd
headline: Charles Barsotti, Cartoonist With Humor Both Simple and Absurd, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Barsotti made New Yorker readers laugh for more than 40 years with imaginative drawings that often had no punch line.

name: Stephanie L. Kwolek
headline: Stephanie L. Kwolek, Inventor of Kevlar, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Ms. Kwolek, a DuPont chemist who invented the technology behind Kevlar, a virtually bulletproof fiber that has saved thousands of lives, spent 15 years in the laboratory without a promotion before her breakthrough.

name: Carlton A. Sherwood
headline: Carlton A. Sherwood, Reporter Behind 2004 Kerry Film, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Sherwood was an investigative journalist and former Marine who made “Stolen Honor,” a 2004 film about Vietnam War veterans’ opposition to John Kerry.

name: Arnold Relman
profession: Journal Editor and Health System Critic
headline: Dr. Arnold Relman, 91, Journal Editor and Health System Critic, Dies
abstract: A longtime editor of The New England Journal of Medicine, Dr. Relman used it to warn of a “new medical-industrial complex.”

name: Gustave Tassell
headline: Gustave Tassell Dies at 88; Clothed Leading Women of the ’60s
abstract: Mr. Tassell was a fashion designer whose urbane creations were favored by some of the most glamorous, socially prominent women of the era.

name: Fouad Ajami
profession: Commentator and Expert in Arab History
headline: Fouad Ajami, Commentator and Expert in Arab History, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Ajami, an academic and commentator on Middle East affairs, strove to put Arab history into a larger perspective and often said terrorism was one result of Muslim rage over losing power to the West in the 17th century.

name: Gerry Conlon
profession: Imprisoned in I.R.A. Attack and Freed After 15 Years
headline: Gerry Conlon, 60, Imprisoned in I.R.A. Attack and Freed After 15 Years, Dies
abstract: Mr. Conlon was a member of the so-called Guildford Four, whose convictions in deadly 1974 bombings in the London area were later quashed.

name: Steve Rossi
headline: Steve Rossi, Singer Who Found Fame in Comedy Duo, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Rossi was a suave crooner who rose to fame teaming with Marty Allen in one of the most successful comedy teams of the 1960s.

name: Stanley Marsh
headline: Stanley Marsh, Cadillac Rancher, Dies at 76, Shadowed by Charges
abstract: Mr. Marsh was known as an eccentric millionaire who commissioned the Cadillac Ranch outside Amarillo, Tex., until he was accused of sexually abusing teenage boys.

name: Felix Dennis
headline: Felix Dennis, 67, Flamboyant Builder of Magazine Empire, Dies
abstract: A roaring lover of money, women, drugs, trees, cars and later in life, poetry, Mr. Dennis built a magazine empire and fortune on being able to spot and exploit budding trends.

name: Johnny Mann
headline: Johnny Mann, Leader of Easy-Listening Singers, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Mann’s singers were the old-fashioned musical answer to the rumblings of rock ’n’ roll.

name: John McClure
headline: John McClure Dies at 84; Produced Classic Records
abstract: Mr. McClure was a producer and engineer who helped shape some of the most celebrated classical recordings of the 20th century, including acclaimed sessions with Bruno Walter, Igor Stravinsky and Leonard Bernstein.

name: Eli Wallach
profession: Multifaceted Actor on Stage and Screen
headline: Eli Wallach, Multifaceted Actor on Stage and Screen, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Wallach was one of his generation’s most prominent and prolific character actors in film, onstage and on television for more than 60 years.

name: Paula Kent Meehan
headline: Paula Kent Meehan, Co-Founder of a Hair-Care Giant, Dies at 82
abstract: With her hairdresser, she founded Redken, a company that changed the way shampoos and rinses were made and marketed.

name: Teenie Hodges
headline: Teenie Hodges, Soul Guitarist and Songwriter, Dies at 68
abstract: The musician, who worked with Al Green and others, helped shape the sound of Memphis soul in the 1970s.

name: Johnnie M. Walters
headline: Johnnie M. Walters, I.R.S. Chief Who Resisted Nixon’s Pressure, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Walters was a commissioner of the Internal Revenue Service under President Richard M. Nixon who left office after refusing to prosecute people on Nixon’s notorious “enemies list.”

name: Julius Rudel
profession: Longtime Impresario and Conductor of City Opera
headline: Julius Rudel, Longtime Impresario and Conductor of City Opera, Dies at 93
abstract: The Austrian-born conductor had led the organization, called “the people’s opera,” for 22 years and continued to be its backer.

name: John Harney
headline: John Harney, Missionary Who Spread the ‘Gospel of Tea,’ Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Harney barnstormed the country in the 1980s to acquaint the public with the dying art of tea appreciation.

name: Howard H. Baker Jr.
headline: Howard H. Baker Jr., ‘Great Conciliator’ of the Senate, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Baker, the Senate Republican leader for eight years, was a forceful figure on the chamber’s Watergate committee and helped President Ronald Reagan weather the Iran-Contra scandal.

name: John Tull
headline: John Tull, Lawyer Whose Illness Created a Bioterrorism Scare, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Tull’s diagnosis of bubonic plague during a visit from New Mexico caused alarm in New York, where the disease had not been seen in more than 100 years.

name: Mary Rodgers
profession: Author and Composer in a Musical Family
headline: Mary Rodgers, Author and Composer in a Musical Family, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Rodgers, born into American musical theater royalty, composed the music for “Once Upon a Mattress” and wrote the novel “Freaky Friday.”

name: Bobby Womack
headline: Bobby Womack, Royalty of the Soul Era, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Womack was nicknamed the Preacher for his authoritative, church-trained voice and the way he introduced songs with long discourses on life.

name: Leslie Manigat
profession: Overthrown in a Coup in Haiti
headline: Leslie Manigat, Overthrown in a Coup in Haiti, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Manigat was overthrown in a bloodless military coup after serving less than six months in office.

name: Robert Gardner
headline: Robert Gardner Dies at 88; Filmed Cultural Practices
abstract: Mr. Gardner’s career took him around the world to observe societies and film their rituals and customs.

name: Rollin King
headline: Rollin King, Texas Pilot Who Helped Start Southwest, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. King was a San Antonio businessman and pilot who sketched out an idea with his lawyer for a low-cost airline for Texas businessmen.

name: Mira Slovak
headline: Mira Slovak, a Daring Pilot Who Won Freedom, Then Races, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Slovak, known as the Flying Czech, lived a life of high-speed adventure, including hydroplane championships, after escaping Communist Czechoslovakia by hijacking his own commercial plane.

name: Meshach Taylor
headline: Meshach Taylor, an Actor on TV’s ‘Designing Women,’ Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Taylor was nominated for an Emmy Award in 1989 for the role of Anthony Bouvier, an ex-convict who became a partner at an Atlanta design firm with four women.

name: Allen Grossman
headline: Allen Grossman, a Poet’s Poet and Scholar, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Grossman was typically referred to as a poet’s poet for his brainy and lyrical poems that were proudly high-minded and often written in a voice described as conversationally academic.

name: Michael Brown
profession: Industrial Musicals Gave Wings to Mockingbird
headline: Michael Brown, 93, Dies; Industrial Musicals Gave Wings to ‘Mockingbird’
abstract: Mr. Brown wrote industrial musicals for American corporations, which were meant to rally employees, and used some of his earnings to support Harper Lee while she wrote “To Kill a Mockingbird.”

name: R. Michael Brown
profession: Defender of Notable New York City Interiors
headline: R. Michael Brown, Defender of Notable New York City Interiors, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Brown led efforts to protect the spaces inside Radio City Music Hall and Grand Central Terminal, among other buildings.

name: G. Michael Brown
headline: G. Michael Brown, Who Regulated and Then Ran Casinos, Dies at 82
abstract: He was a watchdog over casinos when they were introduced in New Jersey. He went on to run the nation’s most profitable one, in Connecticut.

name: Diana McLellan
profession: Gossip Columnist With an Ear to Washington
headline: Diana McLellan, Gossip Columnist With an Ear to Washington, Dies at 76
abstract: The British-born Mrs. McLellan, who wrote for three Washington papers, gained a devoted readership by skewering the powerful in the nation’s capital.

name: Frank Cashen
profession: Turned Lowly Mets Into Swaggering Champions
headline: Frank Cashen, Who Turned Lowly Mets Into Swaggering Champions, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Cashen assembled World Series champions in Baltimore and New York by nurturing farm systems and making shrewd trades.

name: Ana María Matute
profession: Spanish Novelist Marked by Civil War
headline: Ana María Matute, Spanish Novelist Marked by Civil War, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Matute’s explorations of alienation and the loss of innocence that children experienced during and after the Spanish Civil War made her one of Spain’s most acclaimed writers.

name: Nancy Garden
headline: Nancy Garden Dies at 76; Wrote Young-Adult Novel of Lesbians
abstract: In 2000, School Library Journal named “Annie on My Mind,” for which Ms. Garden remained best known, to its list of 100 books that shaped the 20th century.

name: Paul Mazursky
profession: Director Showed Me Eras Strength and Foibles
headline: Paul Mazursky Dies at 84; Director Showed ‘Me’ Era’s Strength and Foibles
abstract: Mr. Mazursky traced an era of moral shifts and uncertainties in films like “Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice” (1969) and “An Unmarried Woman” (1978).

name: Anatoly Kornukov
headline: Anatoly Kornukov, Who Led Russian Air Force, Dies at 72
abstract: Gen. Anatoly Kornukov ordered Korean Air Lines Flight 007, a commercial jet with 269 people aboard, shot down in 1983 after it strayed into Soviet airspace.

name: Lloyd Garrison
profession: Journalist; Covered Africa for The Times
headline: Lloyd Garrison, 83, Journalist; Covered Africa for The Times
abstract: Mr. Garrison covered conflicts in Nigeria, Congo and Angola for The Times in the 1960s, and later taught African history.

name: Lillian B. Rubin
profession: Wrote of Crippling Effects of Gender and Class Norms
headline: Lillian B. Rubin, 90, Is Dead; Wrote of Crippling Effects of Gender and Class Norms
abstract: Dr. Rubin explored identity crises of middle-aged women, life in a working-class family and why marriages often fail.

name: Christian Führer
headline: Christian Führer, East German Whose Prayers Inspired Protests, Dies at 71
abstract: Pastor Führer’s “prayers for peace” meetings in Leipzig grew into mass demonstrations that helped bring about the fall of Communism in East Germany.

name: Stephen Gaskin
headline: Stephen Gaskin, Hippie Who Founded an Enduring Commune, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Gaskin was a Marine veteran and hippie leader who founded the Farm, an archetypical hippie commune that has lasted longer than its counterparts while accepting elements of capitalism.

name: Louis Zamperini
headline: Louis Zamperini, Olympian and ‘Unbroken’ War Survivor, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Zamperini’s experiences as an airman who crashed into the Pacific and spent 47 days adrift before his capture by the Japanese were told in a best-selling biography.

name: Walter Dean Myers
profession: Wrote of Black Youth for the Young
headline: Walter Dean Myers Dies at 76; Wrote of Black Youth for the Young
abstract: Mr. Myers’s fiction for young readers often centered on African-Americans struggling in tough environments.

name: Paul S. Amos
headline: Paul S. Amos, a Co-Founder of Aflac, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Amos pushed the company to market its insurance policies at companies, not door to door.

name: Jim Brosnan
headline: Jim Brosnan, Who Threw Literature a Curve, Dies at 84
abstract: Brosnan’s 1960 book, “The Long Season,” a candid account of his experience as a pitcher, helped change the way baseball was chronicled.

name: Richard Mellon Scaife
headline: Richard Mellon Scaife, Influential U.S. Conservative, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Scaife, an heir to the Mellon banking fortune, laid the foundations for modern conservatism and fueled the impeachment of President Bill Clinton.

name: Bruno Zumino
profession: Sought to Tie Together Laws of Universe
headline: Bruno Zumino Dies at 91; Sought to Tie Together Laws of Universe
abstract: Mr. Zumino proposed a theory called supersymmetry that promised to help tie together the fundamental laws of the universe but that has yet to be borne out in experiments.

name: Gerald Robinson
profession: Priest Convicted of Killing Ohio Nun
headline: Gerald Robinson, Priest Convicted of Killing Ohio Nun, Dies at 76
abstract: Father Robinson was convicted in 2006 of murdering a nun more than 20 years earlier in the hospital where they worked together in Toledo, Ohio.

name: Emilio Álvarez Montalván
headline: Emilio Álvarez Montalván, Nicaragua’s Pro-Democracy Sage, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Álvarez was an ophthalmologist, former guerrilla, political prisoner, diplomat and trenchant critic of dictatorship, and he was often called the wisest man in Nicaragua.

name: Frank M. Robinson
profession: Author and Adviser to Harvey Milk
headline: Frank M. Robinson Dies at 87; Author and Adviser to Harvey Milk
abstract: Mr. Robinson made his mark in science fiction, film and politics.

name: Frank Robinson
profession: Hall of Fame Slugger and First Black Manager
headline: Frank Robinson, Hall of Fame Slugger and First Black Manager, Dies at 83
abstract: An intense player at the plate, he hit 586 home runs and made history when he took the helm of the Cleveland Indians in 1975.

name: David Truong
headline: David Truong, Figure in U.S. Wiretap Case, Dies at 68
abstract: His conviction on espionage charges in 1978 raised alarms about the federal government’s use of wiretaps without court orders and spurred passage of the 1978 Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act.

name: Louis Brown Jr.
headline: Louis Brown Jr., Nicole Simpson’s Father, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Brown was a familiar presence at the murder trial of O.J. Simpson and became a public voice against domestic violence.

name: Eduard Shevardnadze
headline: Eduard Shevardnadze, Foreign Minister Under Gorbachev, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Shevardnadze helped hone the “new thinking” that transformed the Soviet Union, and then led his native Georgia through its turbulent start as an independent state.

name: Alfredo Di Stéfano
headline: Alfredo Di Stéfano, Soccer Great for Real Madrid, Dies at 88
abstract: Di Stéfano, an Argentine, built a legendary career when he moved to Europe in the 1950s and led Real Madrid to five straight Continental club championships.

name: Alan J. Dixon
headline: Alan J. Dixon, 86, Is Dead; U.S. Senator Who Championed Illinois
abstract: Mr. Dixon was a two-term United States senator from Illinois in the 1980s and early ’90s who was known for keen attention to constituents’ needs.

name: Umaru Dikko
headline: Umaru Dikko, Ex-Nigerian Official Who Was Almost Kidnapped, Dies
abstract: In 1984, Mr. Dikko was found in a shipping crate at a London airport along with three kidnappers who had planned to ship him back to Lagos to stand trial.

name: Anne Hollander
headline: Anne Hollander, Scholar Who Linked Art and Style, Dies at 83
abstract: Through groundbreaking research, Ms. Hollander argued that clothing revealed far more about us than it concealed.

name: Zalman Schachter-Shalomi
headline: Zalman Schachter-Shalomi, Jewish Pioneer, Dies at 89
abstract: Rabbi Zalman Schachter-Shalomi was considered the spiritual father of the Jewish Renewal movement, an influential camp of religious pioneers who reintroduced to synagogue services ancient Judaic traditions.

name: Kenny Kingston
headline: Kenny Kingston, ‘Psychic to the Stars,’ Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Kingston said that he held readings for John Wayne, Whoopi Goldberg and the Duke and Duchess of Windsor, among others, and that some kept in contact after they died.

name: Dick Jones
headline: Dick Jones, Who Gave Voice to Disney’s Pinocchio, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Jones, who as a boy actor infused the animated Pinocchio with charm, went on to many other roles in film and TV, especially westerns.

name: Paul Horn
profession: Founding Father of New Age Music
headline: Paul Horn, a Founding Father of New Age Music, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Horn, a flutist and saxophonist, departed from mainstream jazz to create mellow, meditative recordings.

name: Rosemary Murphy
headline: Rosemary Murphy, 89, Emmy Winner Familiar to Broadway, Dies
abstract: Ms. Murphy appeared in classic works by Tennessee Williams, Edward Albee and Thomas Wolfe as well as the film “To Kill a Mockingbird.’

name: Seymour Barab
headline: Seymour Barab, 93, Composer of Playful Operas, Dies
abstract: Mr. Barab wrote whimsical chamber operas and championed contemporary music.

name: Eileen Ford
profession: Grande Dame of the Modeling Industry
headline: Eileen Ford, Grande Dame of the Modeling Industry, Dies at 92
abstract: Ford Models, founded by Mrs. Ford and her husband, Jerry, in 1947, elevated modeling to a serious business and created a market for “supermodels.”

name: Errie Ball
headline: Errie Ball, Welshman Who Played in First Masters, Dies at 103
abstract: Samuel Henry Ball, known since childhood as Errie, was the last survivor of the 72 players from the first Augusta National Invitational Tournament in 1934.

name: Ted Steeg
profession: Found Big Audience With Jury Duty Films
headline: Ted Steeg, Who Found Big Audience With Jury Duty Films, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Steeg was a maker of educational and industrial films. His best-known works have been seen by millions of prospective jurors in New York State.

name: John Seigenthaler
headline: John Seigenthaler, Editor and Aide to Politicians, Dies at 86
abstract: The longtime editor of The Tennessean also worked on John F. Kennedy’s presidential campaign in 1960 and at the Justice Department.

name: Charlie Haden
headline: Charlie Haden, Influential Jazz Bassist, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Mr. Haden, a seminal force in jazz, worked with Ornette Coleman, Keith Jarrett and Pat Metheny, among many others.

name: P. N. Furbank
headline: P. N. Furbank, Biographer of E. M. Forster, Dies at 94
abstract: Professor Furbank, who wrote widely, produced an account of Forster’s life that is regarded as one of the 20th century’s best biographies.

name: Zohra Sehgal
headline: Zohra Sehgal, Beloved and Prolific Indian Actress, Dies at 102
abstract: Ms. Sehgal was also a dancer and choreographer who continued making movies into her 90s.

name: Tommy Ramone
profession: He Gave Punk Rock Its Pulse
headline: Tommy Ramone Dies at 65; He Gave Punk Rock Its Pulse
abstract: The founding drummer and last surviving original member of the Ramones cut a much more easygoing figure than his bandmates.

name: Lorin Maazel
headline: Lorin Maazel, an Intense and Enigmatic Conductor, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Maazel, who directed the New York Philharmonic, the Cleveland Orchestra and the Vienna State Opera among others, was known for his incisive, sometimes extreme, interpretations.

name: Frederick I. Ordway III
profession: NASA Official Helped Shape Space Odyssey
headline: Frederick I. Ordway III Dies at 87; NASA Official Helped Shape ‘Space Odyssey’
abstract: Mr. Ordway spent two years in the 1960s as an adviser to the director Stanley Kubrick, whom he met through his friend, the science-fiction writer Arthur C. Clarke.

name: Nadine Gordimer
headline: Nadine Gordimer, Novelist Who Took On Apartheid, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Ms. Gordimer found her themes in the injustices and cruelties of South Africa’s policies of racial division, and she left no quarter of the society unexplored.

name: Red Klotz
profession: Beloved Foil for the Harlem Globetrotters
headline: Red Klotz, Beloved Foil for the Harlem Globetrotters, Dies at 93
abstract: Klotz was the founder and owner of the Washington Generals, the Globetrotters’ hapless, perennial opponent. But he had one moment of glory as their two-handed-set-shot artist.

name: Alice Coachman
profession: First Black Woman to Win Olympic Gold
headline: Alice Coachman, 90, Dies; First Black Woman to Win Olympic Gold
abstract: Coachman captured the high jump for the United States at the 1948 London Games, then returned home to a segregated South.

name: James MacGregor Burns
headline: James MacGregor Burns, Scholar of Presidents and Leadership, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Burns, a Pulitzer Prize-winning biographer and political scientist, wrote voluminously about the nature of leadership in general and the presidency in particular.

name: On Kawara
headline: On Kawara, Artist Who Found Elegance in Every Day, Dies at 81
abstract: The Japanese-born conceptual artist was known for works that emphasized the incremental passage of time, and for his lifelong self-effacement.

name: Robert Roe
profession: New Jersey Congressman Called Mr. Jobs
headline: Robert Roe, New Jersey Congressman Called ‘Mr. Jobs,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Roe was an advocate for public works who helped finance the expansion of the nation’s highway system and efforts to combat water pollution.

name: Paul Gibson Jr.
profession: New York Citys First Black Deputy Mayor
headline: Paul Gibson Jr., New York City’s First Black Deputy Mayor, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Gibson, a lawyer and vice president of American Airlines, was the deputy mayor for planning under Mayor Abraham D. Beame.

name: Randall Stout
headline: Randall Stout, Architect Tied to Nature, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Stout explored the relationship between architecture and energy in holistic designs that were no less sculptural and humane for being ecologically responsible.

name: Robert Stein
profession: Led McCalls and Redbook for Decades
headline: Robert Stein, Who Led McCall’s and Redbook for Decades, Dies at 90
abstract: As editor of the two women’s magazines, Mr. Stein ran articles about race and politics, and introduced feminists like Betty Friedan and Gloria Steinem.

name: Elaine Stritch
headline: Elaine Stritch, Broadway’s Enduring Dame, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Stritch, a brassy, tart-tongued actress and singer, became perhaps the leading interpreter of Stephen Sondheim’s acrid musings on aging.

name: Johnny Winter
headline: Johnny Winter, Virtuosic Blues Guitarist, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Winter rose to fame in the late 1960s and early ’70s for his energetic performances and musical collaborations, including with a childhood hero, Muddy Waters.

name: Elaine M. Brody
headline: Elaine M. Brody, Expert on Elderly Who Grew Into the Role, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Brody’s research on the elderly revealed increasing stress on women trying to build careers while caring for children and aging parents — “women in the middle,” she called them.

name: Tom Tierney
profession: Made Paper Dolls an Art Form
headline: Tom Tierney, Who Made Paper Dolls an Art Form, Dies at 85
abstract: A spate of diminutive two-dimensional figures sprang to life on Mr. Tierney’s drawing board, including American presidents, monarchs and silver-screen stars.

name: Otto Piene
headline: Otto Piene, German Artist of New Modes, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Piene was a founder of the Zero Group, which explored new methods of painting and anticipated developments in land art and Minimalism.

name: Yehuda Nir
headline: Yehuda Nir, a Psychiatrist and Holocaust Survivor, Dies at 84
abstract: As a child, Dr. Nir had to masquerade as a Roman Catholic in German-occupied Poland, an ordeal that he turned into a well-received memoir and that guided him in treating victims of trauma.

name: James Garner
headline: James Garner, Witty, Handsome Leading Man, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Garner was best known as the amiable gambler Bret Maverick in the 1950s western “Maverick” and the cranky sleuth Jim Rockford in the 1970s series “The Rockford Files.”

name: Bill Mulliken
headline: Bill Mulliken, Who Swam to Olympic Gold in 1960, Dies at 74
abstract: Mulliken was a little-known college swimmer when he outpaced the world-record holder in the 200-meter breaststroke in the 1960 Summer Games.

name: Curt Gentry
headline: Curt Gentry, 83, Co-Author of ‘Helter Skelter,’ Dies
abstract: Mr. Gentry’s books ranged from the Manson murders to J. Edgar Hoover to the madams of San Francisco.

name: Albert J. Stunkard
headline: Dr. Albert J. Stunkard, Destigmatizer of Fat, Dies at 92
abstract: The scientist discovered genetic predispositions for obesity through studies of adoptees, but took pains to keep his findings from being used an excuse for surrender.

name: Karl Albrecht
headline: Karl Albrecht, a Founder of Aldi Stores, Dies at 94
abstract: The German billionaire and his brother built their mother’s World War II-era corner shop into a global grocery empire known for bare-bones ambience enlivened by cut-rate prices.

name: Thomas Berger
headline: Thomas Berger, ‘Little Big Man’ Author, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Berger was known as the author of “Little Big Man” and books that explored the American West, but his body of work was broader than that.

name: Madeline Amgott
headline: Madeline Amgott, Television Producer, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Amgott was one of the few women to produce news programs in the male-dominated television universe of the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Henry Hartsfield Jr.
headline: Henry Hartsfield Jr. Is Dead at 80; Flew, With Fortune, on 3 Shuttles
abstract: Mr. Hartsfield, who logged 483 hours in space, flew on the Columbia and the Challenger before they met disaster.

name: Kenneth Noble
headline: Kenneth Noble, Ex-Times Reporter, Is Dead at 60
abstract: Mr. Noble covered a variety of topics for the newspaper, including business, the Los Angeles area and Africa.

name: Robert Newhouse
headline: Robert Newhouse, 64, Rusher Whose Pass Secured a Title, Dies
abstract: Mr. Newhouse, who played 12 seasons in the N.F.L., mostly as a fullback, threw a touchdown pass on a trick play in the Super Bowl in 1978.

name: Anthony Smith
headline: Anthony Smith, Explorer With Zest for Land, Sea and Air, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Smith’s many adventures included a late-life, 66-day odyssey across the Atlantic on a raft.

name: Martin Tahse
headline: Martin Tahse, TV and Broadway Producer, Dies at 84
abstract: Shows Mr. Tahse produced included a revival of “Kukla, Fran and Ollie” for syndication.

name: Alan C. Greenberg
profession: Led Bear Stearns in Good Times and Bad
headline: Alan C. Greenberg, 86, Dies; Led Bear Stearns in Good Times and Bad
abstract: A risk-taking trader at heart, Mr. Greenberg began at the brokerage as a $32.50-a-week clerk and emerged unscathed after its collapse.

name: Bel Kaufman
profession: Told What School Was Really Like
headline: Bel Kaufman, Who Told What School Was Really Like, Dies at 103
abstract: Ms. Kaufman’s first novel, “Up the Down Staircase,” portrayed the topsy-turvy world of a New York City public school and was based on her experience as a teacher.

name: Gene I. Maeroff
headline: Gene I. Maeroff, Education Reporter and Author, Dies at 75
abstract: A former education reporter for The Times, Mr. Maeroff found a second career working as an author, a researcher and an adviser on education issues.

name: Martin R. Hoffmann
headline: Martin R. Hoffmann, Army Secretary in 1970s, Dies at 82
abstract: As secretary of the Army in the 1970s, Mr. Hoffmann presided over a cheating scandal at West Point and helped usher in the all-volunteer Army.

name: Augie Rodriguez
headline: Augie Rodriguez, 86, Half of a Mambo Team, Dies
abstract: Mr. Rodriguez and his wife, Margo, were often accompanied by renowned bandleaders like Xavier Cugat.

name: Carlo Bergonzi
profession: Operatic Tenor of Subtlety and Emotional Acuity
headline: Carlo Bergonzi, 90, an Operatic Tenor of Subtlety and Emotional Acuity, Dies
abstract: Mr. Bergonzi, small and admittedly without leading-man looks or acting skills, was considered to have a vocal elegance that more than compensated for perceived shortcomings.

name: Peter Marler
headline: Peter Marler, Graphic Decoder of Birdsong, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Marler showed that certain songbirds not only learned their songs, but also learned to sing in a dialect peculiar to the region in which they were born.

name: Karen Walter Goodwin
headline: Karen Walter Goodwin, Producer of Broadway Hits, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Goodwin became a theater producer at a time when few women were associated with finding sources of capital.

name: Wah Wah Jones
headline: Wah Wah Jones, Versatile Kentucky Athlete, Dies at 88
abstract: Jones is the only University of Kentucky athlete to have his number, 27, retired in two sports, football and basketball. He became known as Wah Wah because that was how his younger sister pronounced his given name, Wallace.

name: Louise Shivers
headline: Louise Shivers, Conjurer of Rural South, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Shivers was startled by the critical success of her first novella, “Here to Get My Baby Out of Jail” (1983), published when she was in her 50s.

name: John W. Mazzola
headline: John W. Mazzola, Former President of Lincoln Center, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Mazzola expanded the reach of the performing arts center, helping to start free outdoor events and the “Live From Lincoln Center” television series.

name: Theodore Van Kirk
headline: Theodore Van Kirk, 93, Enola Gay Navigator, Dies
abstract: Mr. Van Kirk, a navigator, guided a flight that, six-and-a-half hours after takeoff, reached Hiroshima with its atomic bomb just seconds behind schedule.

name: Margot Adler
headline: Margot Adler, 68, Journalist and Priestess, Dies
abstract: Ms. Adler, a longtime reporter for NPR on myriad subjects, was a Wiccan high priestess and the author of “Drawing Down the Moon,” a 1979 survey of contemporary pagan movements.

name: M. Caldwell Butler
headline: M. Caldwell Butler, a Key Vote Against Nixon, Dies at 89
abstract: As a freshman Republican representative and a member of the House Judiciary Committee, Mr. Butler voted to impeach President Richard M. Nixon, then wept.

name: James Shigeta
profession: Leading Man in Flower Drum Song
headline: James Shigeta, 85, Leading Man in ‘Flower Drum Song,’ Dies
abstract: The Hawaii-born actor, who first found fame in Japan, helped break Hollywood clichés about Asian-American performers.

name: Arthur Shafman
headline: Arthur Shafman, 75, Importer of Mummenschanz Troupe, Dies
abstract: Mr. Shafman, who also managed artists, worked with many prominent performers over his long career, helping to stage well-received late-career appearances by Red Skelton at Carnegie Hall.

name: Jay Maeder
headline: Jay Maeder, 67, Newspaperman Who Wrote ‘Annie’ Comic Strip, Dies
abstract: A witty provocateur who also wrote the updated “Little Orphan Annie” strip, Mr. Maeder wrote columns for The Daily News and The Miami Herald, and he was a historian of the comics pages.

name: Dick Smith
headline: Dick Smith, Oscar-Winning Makeup Artist, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Smith’s handiwork could be seen in the “Godfather” films as well as “Amadeus,” “The Exorcist” and more, using plaster masks and liquid foam latex.

name: Julio Grondona
headline: Julio Grondona, Argentine Power in World Soccer, Dies at 82
abstract: Combative and iron-handed, Mr. Grondona led Argentina’s soccer association for 35 years, helping to shape World Cup teams, and was FIFA’s second in command.

name: Ed Sprinkle
profession: Defensive End Known for Violent Play
headline: Ed Sprinkle, Defensive End Known for Violent Play, Dies at 90
abstract: Sprinkle, a member of the Chicago Bears in the 1940s and ’50s under George Halas, was a prototype for pass-rushing defensive ends.

name: Robert L. Drew
headline: Robert L. Drew, Pioneer in Documentary Filmmaking, Dies at 90
abstract: In the 1950s and 1960s, Mr. Drew’s efforts helped cinéma vérité become a common storytelling device.

name: Noel Black
headline: Noel Black, 77, Dies; Directed Dark Comedy Cult Hit
abstract: Mr. Black’s first feature film, the black comedy “Pretty Poison,” was pulled from theaters before becoming a cult hit, even among some critics.

name: Warren G. Bennis
headline: Warren G. Bennis, Scholar on Leadership, Dies at 89
abstract: After serving as a 19-year-old lieutenant in World War II, Professor Bennis devoted his life to studying how leaders are made and became an adviser to the powerful.

name: Robert Halmi
headline: Robert Halmi, 90, Producer of TV Films, Dies
abstract: Mr. Halmi had already had a career as a photographer for Life magazine when he became a producer of TV mini-series like “Lonesome Dove,” “In Cold Blood” and “Don Quixote.”

name: Manny Roth
headline: Manny Roth, 94, Impresario of Cafe Wha?, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Roth presided over Cafe Wha?, a large, plain basement room at 115 Macdougal Street, during a lively and fertile period in the Village’s history.

name: Harun Farocki
headline: Harun Farocki, Filmmaker of Modern Life, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Farocki’s subject matter as an artist and filmmaker was the unexamined absurdities of the corporate and military world.

name: Charles R. Larson
headline: Adm. Charles R. Larson, 77, Dies; Twice Led Naval Academy
abstract: Admiral Larson was appointed superintendent of the academy for a second time in 1994 when the Navy sought his help in changing the ethical atmosphere after 134 midshipmen were accused of cheating on an exam.

name: Jon Cavaiani
headline: Jon Cavaiani, Medal of Honor Recipient in 1974, Dies at 70
abstract: Staff Sgt. Cavaiani, a member of a Special Forces unit, was severely wounded while holding off a much larger enemy force so his platoon could escape.

name: Wilfred Feinberg
profession: Federal Appeals Court Judge and Mentor
headline: Wilfred Feinberg, Federal Appeals Court Judge and Mentor, Dies at 94
abstract: Judge Feinberg, appointed by President Lyndon B. Johnson to the United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit, served for 45 years and ruled in major cases involving the Vietnam War and labor rights.

name: Joshu Sasaki
headline: Joshu Sasaki, 107, Tainted Zen Master
