abstract: Mr. Sasaki was one of the most influential and charismatic Zen masters in America but a tide of sex-abuse allegations emerged to cast his character and his legacy in a harsh light.

name: Taking a Bullet
profession: Gaining a Cause: James S. Brady
headline: Taking a Bullet, Gaining a Cause: James S. Brady Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Brady, the White House press secretary who was wounded in an assassination attempt on President Ronald Reagan, championed tighter regulations from his wheelchair.

name: Billie Letts
headline: Billie Letts, ‘Where the Heart Is’ Novelist, Dies at 76
abstract: The late-blooming writer was the mother of Tracy Letts, the playwright who won a Pulitzer Prize for the drama “August: Osage County.”

name: Steve Post
headline: Steve Post, Sardonic Wit on WNYC, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Mr. Post was a public radio personality known for mocking himself, his employers, his sponsors and the conventions of broadcasting.

name: Edward M. Joyce
profession: CBS News Leader During Era of Cost-Cutting
headline: Edward M. Joyce, CBS News Leader During Era of Cost-Cutting, Dies at 81
abstract: A former president of CBS News, he helped steer the network through a $120 million libel suit by Gen. William C. Westmoreland.

name: Jesse L. Steinfeld
headline: Jesse L. Steinfeld, Surgeon General and Tobacco Foe, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Steinfeld, the surgeon general in Nixon’s first term, brought new attention to the risks cigarettes posed to women and to people exposed to secondhand smoke.

name: Dorothy Salisbury Davis
headline: Dorothy Salisbury Davis, Suspense Novelist, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Davis promoted female mystery writers and explored the dark side of human nature in her award-winning career.

name: Jim Frederick
headline: Jim Frederick, Journalist Who Wrote Book About Iraq War Crime, Dies at 42
abstract: Mr. Fredrick, a former editor and correspondent for Time Inc., explored the rape and murder of an Iraqi girl by four American soldiers and the psychological state of the men involved.

name: Idris Muhammad
headline: Idris Muhammad, Drummer Whose Beat Still Echoes, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Muhammad was there at the intersection of jazz, R&B and funk, especially in the pivotal 1970s and for the original Broadway production of “Hair.”

name: Chapman Pincher
headline: Chapman Pincher, Fleet St. Scoop Specialist, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Pincher was a journalist whose career was spent unearthing exclusive stories from the world of double agents and secret weapons.

name: J. W. Hastings
headline: J. W. Hastings, 87, a Pioneer in Bioluminescence Research, Dies
abstract: Mr. Hastings was a Harvard biochemist whose discovery of how bacteria communicate became the foundation for groundbreaking research in the development of more effective antibiotics.

name: June Krauser
headline: June Krauser Dies at 88; Set 154 Records in the Pool
abstract: Ms. Krauser, who won national titles in her teens and in her 70s, helped to organize the adult racing program U.S. Masters Swimming

name: Menahem Golan
headline: Menahem Golan, Passionate Auteur of the B-Movie, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Golan’s films were based on everything from martial arts to Brecht to “King Lear.” He introduced audiences to Jean-Claude Van Damme and directed action stars like Sylvester Stallone and Chuck Norris.

name: Robin Williams
headline: Robin Williams, Oscar-Winning Comedian, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Williams imbued a lifetime of performances with a wild inventiveness and energy. The death was later ruled a suicide.

name: Fabian G. Palomino
profession: Legal Counsel to Democratic New York Governors
headline: Fabian G. Palomino, 90, Legal Counsel to Democratic New York Governors, Dies
abstract: W. Averell Harriman, Hugh L. Carey and both Mario M. Cuomo and Andrew M. Cuomo used Mr. Palomino’s counsel.

name: Dotty Lynch
headline: Dotty Lynch, Pollster Who Saw the Gender Gap, Is Dead at 69
abstract: Ms. Lynch was the first woman to be chief pollster for a presidential campaign and one of the first to recognize the benefit of developing themes aimed at winning female voters.

name: Ed Nelson
headline: Ed Nelson, a Star of ‘Peyton Place,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Nelson appeared in scores of television shows as well some films.

name: Lauren Bacall
profession: in a Bygone Hollywood, She Purred Every Word
headline: Lauren Bacall Dies at 89; in a Bygone Hollywood, She Purred Every Word
abstract: Ms. Bacall's provocative glamour elevated her to stardom in Hollywood’s golden age, and her lasting mystique put her on a plateau in American culture that few stars reach.

name: Henry Stone
headline: Henry Stone, 93, Dies; Produced the Miami Sound
abstract: Mr. Stone produced early Ray Charles and James Brown recordings, and later disco and what came to be called the Miami sound.

name: Earl Cheit
headline: Earl Cheit, Prescient Educator, Dies at 87
abstract: In 1970, Dr. Cheit wrote an influential report that said two-thirds of U.S. colleges and universities were in or near grave financial difficulty.

name: Mary MacCracken
headline: Mary MacCracken, Who Wrote About Disabilities, Dies at 88
abstract: Mrs. MacCracken wrote memoirs about her work with disabled children that inspired TV movies.

name: Pierre Ryckmans
headline: Pierre Ryckmans, 78, Dies; Exposed Mao’s Hard Line
abstract: He challenged the prevailing romantic view of Mao harbored by many Western intellectuals by writing about the cruelties of the Cultural Revolution.

name: Arthur G. Cohen
headline: Arthur G. Cohen, Real Estate Developer, Is Dead at 84
abstract: It was said that Mr. Cohen, who helped populate Manhattan with skyscrapers, had his hand in one in seven real estate deals in New York City.

name: Robert Richards
headline: Robert Richards, Marine Guilty in Taliban Desecration, Dies at 28
abstract: Mr. Richards was a sergeant who was demoted after video footage surfaced of him and his colleagues urinating on corpses of Taliban fighters in Afghanistan.

name: Licia Albanese
headline: Licia Albanese, Exalted Soprano, Is Dead at 105
abstract: One of the most admired operatic sopranos of the mid-20th century, she was revered for a soaring top range and a passionate intensity on the stage.

name: Leonard Fein
headline: Leonard Fein, Provocative Writer on Jewish Affairs, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Fein wrote voluminously about contemporary Jews, Judaism and “the often stormy relationship between Jews and Judaism,” and founded groups to combat hunger and illiteracy.

name: Eroni Kumana
profession: Saved Kennedy and His Shipwrecked Crew
headline: Eroni Kumana, Who Saved Kennedy and His Shipwrecked Crew, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Kumana and a fellow boatman were credited with spotting and rescuing Navy Lt. John F. Kennedy and members of his PT-109 crew after their boat had been destroyed in the Solomon Islands.

name: Jay Adams
headline: Jay Adams, Who Revolutionized Skateboarding, Dies at 53
abstract: Adams, who started surfing at age 4, joined a group of skateboarders who transformed what had been a childish activity by infusing it with aggression and attitude.

name: Sophie Masloff
headline: Sophie Masloff, Ex-Mayor of Pittsburgh, Dies at 96
abstract: She was named interim mayor in 1988, succeeding the popular Mayor Richard S. Caliguiri, who died of a rare blood disorder before the end of his third term.

name: Jim Jeffords
headline: Jim Jeffords, Who Altered Power in Senate, Dies at 80
abstract: Once a Republican who supported abortion rights, gay rights and the National Endowment for the Arts, Senator Jeffords shook up the political landscape when he left the party in 2001.

name: Jerry Lumpe
profession: Infielder for Yankees in 2 World Series
headline: Jerry Lumpe, Infielder for Yankees in 2 World Series, Dies at 81
abstract: Lumpe, who was signed by the same scout who signed Mickey Mantle, made his Yankee debut in 1956 and went on to be an All-Star second baseman for the Tigers.

name: Don Pardo
headline: Don Pardo, the Voice of ‘SNL,’ Is Dead at 96
abstract: An announcer whose career began with radio and grew with popular game shows like “The Price Is Right,” Mr. Pardo was best known for decades of introducing stars on the sketch comedy.

name: James Schiro
headline: James Schiro, Goldman’s Lead Director, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Schiro was also a veteran financial insider who led PricewaterhouseCoopers and, more recently, Zurich Financial Services.

name: John Blake Jr.
headline: John Blake Jr., Versatile Jazz Violinist, Dies at 67
abstract: He combined strong classical technique with the expressive power of African-American spirituals, folk music and blues.

name: Edward G. Leffingwell
headline: Edward G. Leffingwell, Curator, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Leffingwell brought avant-garde artists to the attention of the public in New York, Los Angeles and Latin America.

name: B. K. S. Iyengar
profession: Helped Bring Yoga to the West
headline: B. K. S. Iyengar, Who Helped Bring Yoga to the West, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Iyengar, who practiced his asanas, or postures, well into his 90s, established yoga institutes on six continents.

name: Terence Todman
headline: Terence Todman, an Envoy to 6 Nations, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Todman became the senior African-American member of the Foreign Service during his four decades in diplomacy.

name: Sylvia Hassenfeld
headline: Sylvia Hassenfeld, Philanthropist From Hasbro’s Founding Family, Dies at 93
abstract: Mrs. Hassenfeld became one of the first women to lead a major international Jewish aid organization.

name: Albert Reynolds
headline: Albert Reynolds Dies at 81; Peacemaking Irish Premier
abstract: His leadership in the early 1990s paved the way for a cease-fire with the Irish Republican Army and Loyalists, and ultimately to a peace accord.

name: Hashim Khan
headline: Hashim Khan, Patriarch of a Squash Dynasty, Is Dead
abstract: Khan, a champion and teacher of the sport, which he learned as a ball boy at a British officers’ club in Pakistan, was believed to be 100.

name: Fernand St Germain
headline: Fernand St Germain, Legislator Tied to S.&L. Crisis, Dies at 86
abstract: The Rhode Island Democrat’s legacy was marred when savings and loan associations, emboldened by deregulation he sponsored, became overextended and went under, at a huge cost to taxpayers.

name: Simin Behbahani
headline: Simin Behbahani, Outspoken Iranian Poet, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Behbahani touched on sensitive topics in her poems, often upsetting Iranian authorities.

name: Deborah Sussman
profession: Dressed Buildings in Vivid Colors and Shapes
headline: Deborah Sussman Dies at 83; Dressed Buildings in Vivid Colors and Shapes
abstract: Known for a bold use of color, Ms. Sussman was an early advocate of applying print elements to campuses, buildings and cityscapes.

name: Robert Sherrill
headline: Robert Sherrill, Author Who Skewered Right and Left, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Sherrill rose to prominence in the 1960s and ’70s for his provocative assessments of gun culture, military justice, Lyndon B. Johnson and other political topics.

name: Jean Redpath
headline: Jean Redpath, Prolific Scottish Folk Singer, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Redpath’s repertoire of contemporary tunes, ancient ballads and Robert Burns poems filled some 40 albums.

name: Chung Eun-yong
profession: Helped Expose U.S. Killings of Koreans
headline: Chung Eun-yong,Who Helped Expose U.S. Killings of Koreans, Dies at 91
abstract: He amassed evidence that American troops had systematically killed more than 100, and possibly as many as 400, civilian refugees early in the Korean War near a railroad bridge.

name: John F. Akers
headline: John F. Akers, 79, Dies; Led IBM as PCs Ascended
abstract: Mr. Akers became chief executive in 1985, as smaller, less expensive computers started to undercut the company’s lucrative mainframe computer business.

name: Richard Attenborough
headline: Richard Attenborough, Actor, Director and Giant of British Film, Dies at 90
abstract: A distinguished actor whose career spanned more than 60 years, Mr. Attenborough found his greatest success behind the camera with the monumental biographical film “Gandhi.”

name: Frans Brüggen
headline: Frans Brüggen, Pioneer in Early Music, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Brüggen, who began his career as a recorder soloist, was a founder of the Orchestra of the 18th Century.

name: Sam Hunter
headline: Sam Hunter, Curator and Museum Founder, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Hunter was founding curator of the Rose Art Museum at Brandeis and a prolific writer specializing in 20th-century art.

name: John G. Sperling
headline: John G. Sperling, For-Profit College Pioneer, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Sperling founded a multibillion-dollar enterprise in the University of Phoenix, and became “an unintentional entrepreneur and an accidental C.E.O.”

name: William Greaves
headline: William Greaves, a Documentarian and Pioneering Journalist, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Greaves was a co-host of “Black Journal,” the only national TV program on black issues in the 1960s.

name: Enrique Zileri
headline: Enrique Zileri, Stalwart Publisher in Peru, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Zileri was the former publisher of the nation’s top newsmagazine, and was deported several times for his criticisms of the government.

name: Philippine de Rothschild
headline: Philippine de Rothschild, Wine Nobility, Dies at 80
abstract: The baroness moved from a career as an actress into the lead role in her family business, producing some of the world’s most renowned Bordeaux.

name: Mervyn Susser
headline: Mervyn Susser, 92, Dies; Studied Illness and Society
abstract: Dr. Susser and his wife, Dr. Zena Stein, promoted some of the earliest educational and treatment programs for AIDS in South Africa.

name: Walter Mazzone
headline: Walter Mazzone Dies at 96; Directed Navy Underwater Feats
abstract: Captain Mazzone kept a waterlogged submarine from going belly up during a World War II rescue mission and later organized the first Sealab tests of human endurance at crushing ocean depths.

name: Helen Bamber
headline: Helen Bamber, Therapist to Torture Victims, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Bamber’s method involved revisiting victims’ worst horrors and letting her clients work them out.

name: David Rosand
headline: David Rosand, an Art History Scholar Whose Heart Was in Venice, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Rosand, who began teaching at Columbia in the mid-’60s, specialized in Venetian painting but had wide art knowledge beyond his immediate field.

name: Jeremiah Healy
headline: Jeremiah Healy, Who Created Boston Private Eye, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Healy wrote multiple books starring John Francis Cuddy, a widower and Vietnam veteran whose cases often touched on social issues.

name: Ahmed Seif
profession: Was Tortured in Egypt and Became Rights Defender
headline: Ahmed Seif, Who Was Tortured in Egypt and Became Rights Defender, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Seif, a leading human rights lawyer, defended leftists, Islamists, atheists and gays.

name: Werner Franz
headline: Werner Franz, Survivor of the Hindenburg’s Crew, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Franz was a 14-year-old cabin boy when the immense German zeppelin erupted into flames. He was believed to be the last surviving member of the crew.

name: Jack Kraft
headline: Jack Kraft, Villanova Basketball Coach, Dies at 93
abstract: Kraft, who spent 12 seasons as the Wildcats’ head coach, took them to the N.C.A.A. tournament six times.

name: Hal Finney
headline: Hal Finney, Cryptographer and Bitcoin Pioneer, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Finney made advancing online privacy his life’s work, and he took part in the first Bitcoin transaction, when Satoshi Nakamoto sent him 10 Bitcoins.

name: Arthur H. White
profession: Gauged Public Opinion and Encouraged Reading
headline: Arthur H. White Dies at 90; Gauged Public Opinion and Encouraged Reading
abstract: Mr. White was a co-founder of the research firm Yankelovich, Skelly & White, who went on to help start many nonprofits, including Reading Is Fundamental.

name: John Edwin Mroz
headline: John Edwin Mroz, Clandestine Envoy to Arafat, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Mroz was a co-founder and the chief executive of the EastWest Institute, a New York-based group specializing in international conflict resolution.

name: John A. Walker Jr.
headline: John A. Walker Jr., Ringleader of Spy Family, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Walker was a Navy communications specialist when he began spying for the Soviets at the height of the Cold War in 1967.

name: John Walker
headline: John Walker, Tech Executive Who Popularized AutoCAD, Dies at 74
abstract: He avoided the spotlight, but he helped bring to market an explosively popular computer program that revolutionized the architecture and design industries.

name: George Barrett
headline: George Barrett, Tennessee Lawyer Who Fought for Desegregation, Dies at 86
abstract: Representing a professor from Tennessee State University, Mr. Barrett — who said he aspired to be a “social engineer” — took on a case that lasted 38 years.

name: Glenn Cornick
headline: Glenn Cornick, Original Bassist in Jethro Tull, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Cornick was a founding member of a British band that began with a blues sound and expanded steadily in scope.

name: Sandy Wilson
profession: Composer and Writer of The Boy Friend
headline: Sandy Wilson, Composer and Writer of ‘The Boy Friend,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Wilson wrote the book and composed the score for the musical “The Boy Friend,” Julie Andrews’s Broadway debut and later a Ken Russell movie.

name: Yves Carcelle
headline: Yves Carcelle, Empire Builder at Louis Vuitton, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Carcelle, who led the Louis Vuitton brand and later ran LVMH’s fashion division, was the main architect of an expansion into Asia and other international markets.

name: Carol Vadnais
profession: All-Star and Stalwart on the Rangers
headline: Carol Vadnais, All-Star and Stalwart on the Rangers, Dies at 68
abstract: Vadnais, who began his career when the N.H.L. had six teams, won Stanley Cup titles with Montreal in 1968 and Boston in 1972 before playing with the Rangers.

name: A. J. Langguth
headline: A. J. Langguth, Author and Former Times Correspondent, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Langguth covered the trial of Jack Ruby and the Vietnam War for The Times, and later became an author and a journalism professor.

name: Lida Moser
headline: Lida Moser, Photographer With an Urban Eye, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Moser’s photography captured the reality of life in New York City and she also created a classic series on rural Quebec in 1950.

name: Bernard F. Fisher
headline: Bernard F. Fisher, Honored for Bold Vietnam Rescue, Dies at 87
abstract: Despite warnings, the aviator landed on an embattled airstrip where another flier had crashed, taxied under heavy fire to find him, and got his comrade and himself out alive.

name: Bernard Fisher
headline: Dr. Bernard Fisher, Who Revolutionized Breast Cancer Treatment, Dies at 101
abstract: He brought an end to the routine use of the debilitating radical mastectomy. He later battled false allegations of scientific misconduct.

name: Andrew Madoff
headline: Andrew Madoff, Who Told of His Father’s Swindle, Dies at 48
abstract: Mr. Madoff, the last surviving son of the convicted swindler Bernard L. Madoff, had mantle-cell lymphoma.

name: Andrew McLaglen
profession: Director in the Heyday of TV Westerns
headline: Andrew McLaglen, Director in the Heyday of TV Westerns, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. McLaglen directed stars like John Wayne, Clint Eastwood, James Arness and James Stewart, as well as many western television shows.

name: Charles Bowden
profession: Author With Unblinking Eye on Southwest
headline: Charles Bowden, Author With Unblinking Eye on Southwest, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Bowden’s work explored the brutality of life along the border between the United States and Mexico, underscoring the complexities of the drug trade.

name: Stephen D. Isaacs
headline: Stephen D. Isaacs, Journalist and Educator, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Isaacs grew up in a newspaper family and worked in print and broadcast journalism before joining Columbia’s Graduate School of Journalism.

name: Stan Goldberg
headline: Stan Goldberg, Who Drew Archie for Decades, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Goldberg, who drew Archie comics for more than 40 years, also worked closely with artists like Steve Ditko, Jack Kirby and Stan Lee.

name: Sergio Rodrigues
headline: Sergio Rodrigues, Father of Brazilian Furniture Design, Dies at 86
abstract: His tables, chairs and other living accessories were said to reflect the sociable, witty nature of the Brazilian national character.

name: Michael Katz
headline: Michael Katz, Who Challenged View of Poverty, Dies at 75
abstract: Professor Katz, who taught at the University of Pennsylvania and was a founder of its urban studies program, challenged the prevailing view in the 1980s and ’90s that poverty stemmed from the bad habits of the poor.

name: Michael Katz
profession: Wrote About Boxing With Passion and Humor
headline: Michael Katz, 85, Dies; Wrote About Boxing With Passion and Humor
abstract: Reporting, and opining, for The New York Times and The Daily News, he was known for his combative style and relished tweaking the powerful people in the sport.

name: Joan Rivers
headline: Joan Rivers, a Comic Stiletto Quick to Skewer, Is Dead at 81
abstract: From the stage and the red carpet, Ms. Rivers reveled in skewering the rich and famous with cutting remarks and a caustic wit.

name: Joseph Persico
headline: Joseph Persico, Rockefeller Speechwriter and Best-Selling Author, Dies at 84
abstract: He wrote 12 books, including a 2001 best seller in which he portrayed President Franklin D. Roosevelt as having a Machiavellian, secrecy-obsessed side.

name: Andrew Kay
headline: Andrew Kay, Pioneer in Computing, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Kay’s company Kaypro produced the Kaypro II computer, a hit in the 1980s, but fell into bankruptcy after being left behind by an industry coalescing around the MS-DOS operating system.

name: Charlie Powell
headline: Charlie Powell, a Standout Regardless of the Sport, Dies at 82
abstract: Described by a San Diego newspaper as “arguably the greatest athlete ever to come out of San Diego County,” Powell excelled at pro football, baseball and boxing.

name: Bruce Morton
headline: Bruce Morton, Veteran CBS News Reporter, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Morton, who covered major news events such as the Vietnam War and the space program, gained a reputation as a solid reporter of expansive breadth and expertise.

name: Marjorie Strider
headline: Marjorie Strider Dies at 83; Pop Artist Satirized Men’s Magazines
abstract: Ms. Strider slyly subverted her male counterparts’ takes on consumerism and the female form.

name: Lillian Gobitas Klose
headline: Lillian Gobitas Klose, 90, Dies; Stood Against Mandatory Pledge
abstract: In 1935 Ms. Klose heeded a Jehovah’s Witnesses leader’s call to refuse to recite the pledge in compliance with biblical commands against idolatry.

name: Penelope Niven
headline: Penelope Niven, Carl Sandburg Biographer, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Niven’s groundbreaking books helped revive public interest in Carl Sandburg, Edward Steichen and Thornton Wilder.

name: Peter Sculthorpe
headline: Peter Sculthorpe, Composer Steeped in Australia’s Sounds, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Sculthorpe, named a National Living Treasure in 1987, wrote music influenced by Australia’s landscapes and employing indigenous instruments like the didgeridoo.

name: Gustavo Cerati
profession: Star of South Americas Pop Scene
headline: Gustavo Cerati, a Star of South America’s Pop Scene, Dies at 55
abstract: Mr. Cerati had platinum success in the Spanish rock and pop world and worked with artists like Shakira.

name: S. Truett Cathy
headline: S. Truett Cathy, Chick-fil-A Founder, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Cathy ran his fast-food empire according to his conservative Christian principles, and it became a flash point in the debate over same-sex marriage.

name: Magda Olivero
headline: Magda Olivero, Frenzy-Inspiring Soprano, Dies at 104
abstract: Miss Olivero inspired deep devotion, as well as bootleg recordings and thundering ovations.

name: Gerald Wilson
headline: Gerald Wilson, Versatile Jazz Arranger, Is Dead at 96
abstract: Mr. Wilson’s career started in the 1930s and included work with jazz greats like Duke Ellington, Dizzy Gillespie, Ella Fitzgerald and Sarah Vaughan.

name: Marvin Barnes
headline: Marvin Barnes, Enigmatic Basketball Player, Dies at 62
abstract: Barnes helped Providence College reach the N.C.A.A. Final Four in 1973 and played in the A.B.A. and N.B.A.

name: Mildred Friedman
headline: Mildred Friedman, 85, Dies; Curator Elevated Design and Architecture
abstract: Ms. Friedman helped bring international acclaim to the Walker Art Center in Minneapolis as she lifted contemporary design’s profile.

name: Bob Suter
headline: Bob Suter, Defenseman for ‘Miracle on Ice,’ Dies at 57
abstract: Suter, the father of the Minnesota Wild star Ryan Suter, returned from a broken ankle to help the United States hockey team win the gold medal in 1980.

name: Herbert Lottman
headline: Herbert Lottman, American Biographer of French Figures, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Lottman wrote about giants of French culture, commerce and politics, including Camus, Flaubert and Colette.

name: Noel W. Hinners
profession: Voice for Scientific Research at NASA
headline: Noel W. Hinners, Voice for Scientific Research at NASA, Dies at 78
abstract: Dr. Hinners helped NASA launch some of its farthest-reaching scientific probes into space — to retrieve moon rocks, map the surface of Mars and peer beyond intergalactic dust to where stars are born.

name: Richard Kiel
headline: Richard Kiel Dies at 74; Played Jaws in Bond Films
abstract: Mr. Kiel, at more than seven feet tall, was a natural as a thug, giant, alien or other villain.

name: Ian Paisley
headline: Ian Paisley Dies at 88; Longtime Voice of Hard-Line Ulster Who Then Made Peace
abstract: The Protestant leader who vowed never to compromise with Irish Catholic nationalists accepted in his twilight a power-sharing agreement after decades of sectarian violence.

name: Bob Crewe
profession: Songwriter for Frankie Valli and Four Seasons
headline: Bob Crewe, Songwriter for Frankie Valli and Four Seasons, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Crewe, who wrote for other music acts as well, was perhaps best known for “Can’t Take My Eyes Off You,” a No. 1 hit for Mr. Valli.

name: Donald Sinden
profession: British Actor of Stage and Screen for 60 Years
headline: Donald Sinden, British Actor of Stage and Screen for 60 Years, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Sinden appeared in “Mogambo,” was nominated for a Tony for his role in Alan Bennett’s “Habeas Corpus,” and starred in long-running British television comedies.

name: Cosimo Matassa
profession: Studio Created a Rock n Roll Sound
headline: Cosimo Matassa, Whose Studio Created a Rock ’n’ Roll Sound, Dies at 88
abstract: Recording performers like Little Richard and Fats Domino as if they were playing for live audiences, Mr. Matassa was an engineer who became known for “the New Orleans sound.”

name: Riva Castleman
headline: Riva Castleman, Curator Who Promoted Printmaking, Dies at 84
abstract: As an art historian and curator with the Museum of Modern Art, Ms. Castleman organized exhibitions placing contemporary prints in a larger context.

name: Rashi Fein
headline: Rashi Fein, Economist Who Urged Medicare, Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Fein’s ethical and humanitarian perspectives on national health care were influential from the Truman administration to President Obama’s Affordable Care Act.

name: Frank Torre
headline: Frank Torre, Inspiration to a Yankees Manager, Dies at 82
abstract: Torre is best remembered by New Yorkers for cheering from his hospital bed as the Yankees, led by his younger brother Joe Torre, won the 1996 World Series.

name: Joe Sample
headline: Joe Sample, Crusaders Pianist Who Went Electric, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Sample became a jazz star as a pianist in the 1960s and an even bigger star a decade later when he began playing electric keyboards.

name: Andy Stapp
headline: Andy Stapp, Who Tried to Unionize the Military, Dies at 70
abstract: As antiwar protester determined to challenge the military from within, Mr. Stapp faced court-martial twice and a discharge for what his superiors deemed subversive activity.

name: Thomas Hale Boggs Jr.
headline: Thomas Hale Boggs Jr., 73, Lobbying Giant, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Boggs, the son of two prominent members of Congress, used his familiarity with the levers of power to build a firm that became synonymous with Washington lobbying.

name: Tony Auth
headline: Tony Auth, Pulitzer-Winning Cartoonist, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Auth was an anchor of The Philadelphia Inquirer’s editorial page, a witty whistle-blower in what he depicted as a complicated and often corrupt culture.

name: Tibor Rudas
profession: Brought the World the Three Tenors
headline: Tibor Rudas Dies at 94; Brought the World the Three Tenors
abstract: Mr. Rudas took classical music from concert halls to casinos and from there to baseball stadiums and the Eiffel Tower.

name: Terrance Paul
headline: Terrance Paul, Developer of Teaching Software, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Paul with his wife, Judi, created computerized teaching programs like Accelerated Reader that were widely adopted in American schools over the last 25 years.

name: Elizabeth Whelan
headline: Elizabeth Whelan, Who Challenged Food Laws, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Whelan was an epidemiologist who started a national organization to question conventional wisdom on food, chemicals and the environment.

name: Jack Wayman
headline: Jack Wayman, Impresario of Consumer Electronics Show, Dies at 92
abstract: In an era of only televisions, radios and phonographs, he was the industry’s top salesman and spread electronics fever.

name: Theodore J. Flicker
profession: Director and a Creator of Barney Miller
headline: Theodore J. Flicker, Director and a Creator of ‘Barney Miller,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Flicker also led an influential improvisational theater troupe and directed James Coburn in the comedy “The President’s Analyst.”

name: Jackie Cain
headline: Jackie Cain, of the Jazz Duo Jackie and Roy, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Cain teamed with her husband, Roy Kral, to form probably the most famous vocal duo in jazz history, melding popular tunes and sophisticated harmonies for more than half a century.

name: George Hamilton IV
headline: George Hamilton IV, Singer Who Gave Up Pop for Country, Dies at 77
abstract: After scoring some pop hits, finding a true home at the Grand Ole Opry and a big audience in Canada.

name: Angus Lennie
headline: Angus Lennie, Actor in ‘The Great Escape,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Lennie was also known for his television work, which included episodes of “Doctor Who,” “Rumpole of the Bailey” and “The Saint,” as well as a long-running role in “Crossroads.”

name: Guinter Kahn
headline: Guinter Kahn, Inventor of Baldness Remedy, Dies at 80
abstract: After a long, fierce legal battle, Dr. Kahn gained recognition for helping discover a baldness remedy that is sold under the brand name Rogaine.

name: Polly Bergen
headline: Polly Bergen Dies at 84; Emmy-Winning Actress
abstract: Ms. Bergen won an Emmy in 1958 for her portrayal of the alcoholic torch singer Helen Morgan and was nominated for another 50 years later for her recurring role on the television show “Desperate Housewives.”

name: Terence Moakley
headline: Terence Moakley, Advocate for Disabled, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Moakley, a quadriplegic, was not above staging public stunts to show how difficult it could be for the disabled to get around.

name: Robert E. Poli
profession: Leader of Pivotal Strike by Air Traffic Controllers
headline: Robert E. Poli, Leader of Pivotal Strike by Air Traffic Controllers, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Poli received harsh criticism after the Professional Air Traffic Controllers Organization went on strike in 1981 as President Ronald Reagan responded by dismissing 11,500 controllers in what is now viewed as a seminal moment in the decline of organized labor.

name: Kenny Wheeler
headline: Kenny Wheeler, Influential Sound in Jazz, Dies at 84
abstract: Critics hailed the ingenuity of Mr. Wheeler’s compositions, which were unfailingly melodic but often veered in unexpected directions, and the understated grace of his playing style.

name: Will Radcliff
headline: Will Radcliff, 74, Creator of the Slush Puppie, Dies
abstract: In the 1960s, he began studying the aesthetics of flavored ice drinks and reviewed the options on texture and flavoring, as well as drinking containers.

name: Yoshiko Yamaguchi
headline: Yoshiko Yamaguchi, 94, Actress in Propaganda Films, Dies
abstract: Ms. Yamaguchi starred in Japanese propaganda films during the occupation of China in the 1930s and ’40s. After escaping execution after the war, she helped normalize relations between the nations.

name: Oleg Ivanovsky
headline: Oleg Ivanovsky, Soviets’ Space-Age Designer, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Ivanovsky worked on the first satellite to orbit Earth and the craft that carried the first man into space.

name: Caldwell Jones
headline: Caldwell Jones, Shot-Blocking Basketball Star, Dies at 64
abstract: Caldwell Jones, who helped the Philadelphia 76ers to three N.B.A. finals appearances, was a top defender who also had smooth, slithery move to the basket, a fluid hook shot and a reliable short-range jumper.

name: Pati Hill
profession: Author Turned Artist of the Photocopier
headline: Pati Hill, Author Turned Artist of the Photocopier, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms.Hill began as a model, then wrote books and then became an artist, using the IBM photocopier as her medium.

name: Deborah Cavendish
profession: Last Mitford Sister and Savior of Estate
headline: Deborah Cavendish, Last Mitford Sister and Savior of Estate, Dies at 94
abstract: The dowager duchess of Devonshire was an author and businesswoman who helped turned her husband’s ancestral estate into one of England’s successful grand country houses.

name: Joseph D. McNamara
headline: Joseph D. McNamara, Father of Community Policing, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. McNamara, a former police chief in San Jose, Calif., and in Kansas City, Mo., was known for the farsighted policies he implemented and for his iconoclastic outspokenness.

name: Christopher Hogwood
headline: Christopher Hogwood, Early-Music Devotee, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Hogwood, a conductor and scholar, was consumed with making music that sounded as their long-ago composers intended.

name: J. California Cooper
headline: J. California Cooper, Award-Winning Writer, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Cooper was forthright in using novels, plays and short stories to explore the African-American woman.

name: John Slattery
headline: John Slattery, a Longtime TV Newsman, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Slattery covered New York City news for 35 years, including the terrorist attack on Sept. 11, 2001, and the murder of John Lennon in 1980.

name: Alastair Reid
headline: Alastair Reid, a Restless Poet and Essayist, Is Dead at 88
abstract: The Scottish-born Mr. Reid wrote of far-flung places for The New Yorker over more than half a century.

name: Milton Cardona
profession: Keeper of New York Salsas Beat
headline: Milton Cardona, Keeper of New York Salsa’s Beat, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Cardona played percussion on hundreds of albums ranging from Latin and Santeria music to fusions by the likes of David Byrne, Paul Simon and Herbie Hancock.

name: Don Keefer
profession: Had Bad Thoughts on Twilight Zone
headline: Don Keefer, Actor, Dies at 98; Had Bad Thoughts on ‘Twilight Zone’
abstract: Mr. Keefer was in the original Broadway cast of “Death of a Salesman” and had a long career in television and movies.

name: John Mack Carter
headline: John Mack Carter, 86, Is Dead; Led ‘Big 3’ Women’s Magazines
abstract: Mr. Carter is believed to be the only person to edit all of the so-called Big Three women’s magazines: McCall’s, Ladies’ Home Journal and Good Housekeeping.

name: James A. Traficant Jr.
profession: Cast Out by Congress in Bribery Case
headline: James A. Traficant Jr., Cast Out by Congress in Bribery Case, Dies at 73
abstract: A colorful Democrat from Ohio, Mr. Traficant became the second member of the House of Representatives to be ousted since the Civil War.

name: Michael Harari
profession: Israeli Agent Likened to James Bond
headline: Michael Harari, Israeli Agent Likened to James Bond, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Harari led the hit squad sent to avenge the murders of 11 Israeli athletes by Palestinian terrorists at the 1972 Olympic Games in Munich.

name: Gerald Larue
profession: Early Advocate of Right to Die
headline: Gerald Larue Dies at 98; Early Advocate of Right to Die
abstract: The family of Professor Larue, the first president of the Hemlock Society, who taught for decades at U.S.C., respected his wishes and declined to put him on a ventilator.

name: Gaby Aghion
headline: Gaby Aghion, Founder of Chloé Fashion House, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Aghion was a designer who played a pivotal role in creating less formal ready-to-wear fashions and brought a working woman’s sensibility to the industry.

name: Sheldon Patinkin
headline: Sheldon Patinkin, Force in Chicago Theater, Dies at 79
abstract: As a director at Second City and Steppenwolf and a department chairman at Columbia College, Mr. Patinkin helped to develop Chicago’s robust theatrical scene.

name: George Shuba
profession: Handshake Heralded Racial Tolerance in Baseball
headline: George Shuba, 89, Dies; Handshake Heralded Racial Tolerance in Baseball
abstract: Shuba, a Dodgers outfielder, is remembered for a welcoming gesture to Jackie Robinson on the day that Robinson, as a minor leaguer, broke baseball’s color barrier.

name: Ray Lambrecht
headline: Ray Lambrecht, Dealer Who Held Onto 500 Chevrolets, Is Dead at 96
abstract: Mr. Lambrecht, who sold hundreds, maybe thousands, of cars and trucks in his career, had an eccentricity or two built into his business plan.

name: U. Shrinivas
profession: Indian Mandolin Virtuoso With Global Reach
headline: U. Shrinivas, 45, Indian Mandolin Virtuoso With Global Reach, Dies
abstract: Mr. Shrinivas performed around the world, often blending the Indian classical style that was his specialty with the work of Western musicians.

name: William Lopez
headline: William Lopez, Prisoner Exonerated After 23 Years, Dies at 55
abstract: His 1989 conviction in the murder of a drug dealer in Brooklyn was overturned in 2013.

name: Wally Hergesheimer
profession: Small Big Scorer for the Rangers
headline: Wally Hergesheimer, a Small Big Scorer for the Rangers, Dies at 87
abstract: At only 5-7 and 145 pounds, Hergesheimer led the Rangers in goal-scoring his first three seasons in the N.H.L.

name: Otto Paparazzo
headline: Otto Paparazzo, Developer of Clustered Housing, Dies at 88
abstract: In his best-known project, Mr. Paparazzo sought to limit driving, preserve trees and arrange homes close together to increase open space and reduce infrastructure costs.

name: Gerry Neugebauer
headline: Gerry Neugebauer, Pioneer in Space Studies, Dies at 82
abstract: Dr. Neugebauer’s biggest achievement was in detecting and interpreting infrared radiation emanating from outer space to provide insights about the universe that radio waves or X-rays cannot.

name: Martin Perl
headline: Martin Perl, 87, Dies; Nobel Laureate Discovered Subatomic Particle
abstract: Dr. Perl was awarded the Nobel Prize in 1995 for discovering the tau lepton, a subatomic particle that is one of the building blocks of the universe.

name: Lily McBeth
headline: Lily McBeth, a Focal Figure for Transgender Rights, Dies at 80
abstract: A substitute teacher drew national attention after wanting to return to the classroom following a sex-change operation.

name: Mary Lea Bandy
headline: Mary Lea Bandy, Film Preservationist for MoMA, Dies at 71
abstract: Ms. Bandy, a film curator, raced to find and restore early prints and vastly expanded the Museum of Modern Art’s collection.

name: Jean-Claude Duvalier
profession: Ruled Haiti in Fathers Brutal Fashion
headline: Jean-Claude Duvalier Dies at 63; Ruled Haiti in Father’s Brutal Fashion
abstract: Mr. Duvalier returned to Haiti in 2011 after a 25-year exile and continued to defend what human rights workers called one of the most oppressive governments in the Western Hemisphere.

name: Jerrie Mock
profession: First Solo Female Pilot to Circumnavigate the Globe
headline: Jerrie Mock, First Solo Female Pilot to Circumnavigate the Globe, Dies at 88
abstract: When asked why she had undertaken such a treacherous journey alone, Ms. Mock replied, “It was about time a woman did it.”

name: Morris Collen
headline: Morris Collen, Pioneer in Computerized Medicine, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Collen worked with Kaiser Permanente for more than 70 years and started one of the first computer databases for tracking patients’ health.

name: Yuri Lyubimov
headline: Yuri Lyubimov, Experimental Director of Russian Stage, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Lyubimov, who founded the experimental Taganka Theater in Moscow in 1964, led productions that once prompted the Soviet government to send him into exile.

name: Geoffrey Holder
headline: Geoffrey Holder, Dancer, Actor, Painter and More, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Holder used his manifold talents to infuse the arts with the flavor of his native West Indies — and in television ads for “the Uncola” in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Fred Branfman
headline: Fred Branfman, Who Exposed Bombing of Laos, Dies at 72
abstract: During the Vietnam War, Mr. Branfman made public a secret bombing campaign by the United States and lobbied Congress to stop financing the war.

name: Steve Curry
headline: Steve Curry, Actor Who Was on ‘Hair’ Poster, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Curry played the naïve, sexually adventurous Woof in the Broadway musical “Hair” and posed for the photo that became the show’s poster and cast-album cover.

name: Marian Seldes
headline: Marian Seldes, a Ruler of the Broadway Stage, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Seldes was seldom offstage in a career that spanned six decades, and she was especially known for her performances of Edward Albee’s work.

name: Benedict Groeschel
profession: Priest Aided Poor and Drew a TV Flock
headline: Benedict Groeschel, 81, Dies; Priest Aided Poor and Drew a TV Flock
abstract: Father Groeschel was known in New York for his efforts on behalf of the poor, and worldwide as a television personality who denounced modernism and news reporting on sexual abuse by priests.

name: Vic Braden
headline: Vic Braden, Tennis’s Pied Piper, Dies at 85
abstract: Through instructional television, books, camps and clinics, Mr. Braden became “the patron saint of the weekend hacker.”

name: Robert Mangum
headline: Robert Mangum, a City and Civil Rights Leader, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Mangum, who was New York City’s youngest deputy police commissioner, helped found One Hundred Black Men.

name: Iva Withers
profession: Standby to the Rescue on Broadway
headline: Iva Withers, a Standby to the Rescue on Broadway, Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Withers made a career as a backup for actresses like Julie Harris and Carol Channing.

name: Peter Peyser
headline: Peter Peyser, Legislator Who Defied the G.O.P., Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Peyser rose from mayor of a Westchester County village to Congress, then defied the Republican leadership by challenging Senator James L. Buckley in a 1976 primary.

name: Jan Hooks
headline: Jan Hooks of ‘Saturday Night Live’ Fame Is Dead at 57
abstract: Ms. Hooks joined “S.N.L.” in 1986 and was part of a cast that is widely regarded as one of the best in the show’s history. Most recently, she appeared on “30 Rock.”

name: Carolyn Kizer
headline: Carolyn Kizer, Pulitzer-Winning Poet, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Kizer was known for political and satirical works that, she said, came with “a sting in the tail.”

name: Ray K. Metzker
headline: Ray K. Metzker, Art Photographer, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Metzker, who experimented with photographic forms for six decades, is perhaps best known for his cityscapes and landscapes.

name: Siegfried Lenz
headline: Siegfried Lenz, Novelist of Germany’s Past, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Lenz, a best-selling writer whose stories examined his country’s role in the rise of Nazism, insisted that the past be recounted accurately.

name: Comer Cottrell
headline: Comer Cottrell, Who Got Rich on Hair Curling, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Cottrell helped break color barriers in Dallas’s business community after his company found success with an inexpensive treatment that replicated the Jheri curl hairstyle.

name: Andrea de Cesaris
profession: Driver Known for Wrecks and Losses
headline: Andrea de Cesaris, Driver Known for Wrecks and Losses, Dies at 55
abstract: Mr. Cesaris, a Formula One driver who never won a Grand Prix event in 208 tries, was known for crashes early in his career.

name: Rita Shane
profession: Met Soprano Known for Range and Intensity
headline: Rita Shane, a Met Soprano Known for Range and Intensity, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Shane made her Metropolitan Opera debut in 1973 as the Queen of the Night in Mozart’s “The Magic Flute,” a role she sang some 250 times in her career.

name: Stanley Chase
headline: Stanley Chase Dies at 87; Gave New York Macheath
abstract: Mr. Chase went on to become a prolific producer of theater, film and television drama, with credits including a vast roster of popular series like “The Fugitive” and “Peyton Place.”

name: Zilpha Keatley Snyder
headline: Zilpha Keatley Snyder, Author of Eerie Children’s Tales, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Snyder had three Newbery Honor Books in the early 1970s, but she was probably best known for the dystopian utopia in the Green Sky Trilogy.

name: Pavel Landovsky
headline: Pavel Landovsky, Actor and Vocal Czech Dissident, Dies at 78
abstract: A colleague of Vaclav Havel who went into exile, Mr. Landovsky appeared in “The Unbearable Lightness of Being.”

name: David Greenglass
headline: David Greenglass, the Brother Who Doomed Ethel Rosenberg, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Greenglass, whose testimony against his sister and brother-in-law, Ethel and Julius Rosenberg, in a 1951 spy trial helped send them to the electric chair, later admitted to lying.

name: Norward Roussell
profession: Leader of Selma Schools in Turbulent Time
headline: Norward Roussell, Leader of Selma Schools in Turbulent Time, Dies at 80
abstract: As the first black superintendent of schools in Selma, Ala., Dr. Roussell aspired to equalize educational opportunity, only to be fired amid racial animosities, protests and a school boycott.

name: Elizabeth Peña
profession: Actress on the Big and Small Screens
headline: Elizabeth Peña, Actress on the Big and Small Screens, Dies at 55
abstract: Ms. Peña played everything from love interest to comedic sidekick in movies and on television for 35 years.

name: Anita Cerquetti
headline: Anita Cerquetti, Opera Fill-In Who Soared, Dies at 83
abstract: Miss Cerquetti stepped in for Maria Callas in Rome in 1958, but her fame was relatively short-lived.

name: William J. Ronan
headline: William J. Ronan, Architect of the M.T.A., Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Ronan, chairman of the transit authority and the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, was one of the most powerful officials in the modern history of New York State.

name: James M. LaRossa
profession: Defender of Mob Bosses in Court
headline: James M. LaRossa, Defender of Mob Bosses in Court, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. LaRossa numbered himself among “the last of the gladiators,” his characterization of defense lawyers, and proved it in decades of spirited courtroom battles.

name: Robert W. Fri
profession: Energy Adviser and Director at Smithsonian
headline: Robert W. Fri, Energy Adviser and Director at Smithsonian, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Fri, who nearly doubled attendance at the Smithsonian Institution’s National Museum of Natural History during his tenure, also served in posts at the Environmental Protection Agency.

name: Tim Hauser
headline: Tim Hauser, the Founder of the Manhattan Transfer, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Hauser, a singer and showman, founded the Grammy-winning vocal group that brought four-part harmonies to several decades’ worth of American popular songs.

name: Judith Edelman
headline: Judith Edelman, Architect, 91, Is Dead; Firebrand in a Male-Dominated Field
abstract: Ms. Edelman became the first woman elected to the executive committee of the New York chapter of the American Institute of Architects.

name: Edward V. Regan
headline: Edward V. Regan, Longtime New York State Comptroller, Dies at 84
abstract: As politicians go, Mr. Regan, known as Ned, was as unflashy as they come: a reserved watchdog of the public cash box known for fiscal competence and political reticence.

name: Park Honan
headline: Park Honan, a Biographer of Authors, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Honan’s groundbreaking books included biographies of Matthew Arnold, Robert Browning, Jane Austen and Shakespeare.

name: Peter Daland
headline: Peter Daland, Who Coached Swimming Champions, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Daland became one of the world’s most successful swimming coaches, leading Southern California to nine N.C.A.A. team championships and 20 unbeaten dual-meet seasons in 35 years.

name: Oscar de la Renta
headline: Oscar de la Renta, Who Clothed Stars and Became One, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. de la Renta dressed the wives of American presidents and socialites, but it was Hollywood glitz that defined him for a new age and a new customer.

name: Ali Mazrui
headline: Ali Mazrui, Scholar of Africa Who Divided U.S. Audiences, Dies at 81
abstract: Professor Mazrui, who had taught since 1989 at Binghamton University, set off national criticism with his 1986 television documentary, “The Africans: A Triple Heritage.”

name: Gough Whitlam
headline: Gough Whitlam, Leader of Australia Who Built Ties to China, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Whitlam, who introduced free university education and national health care as prime minister in the 1970s, was noted for his early recognition of China’s government.

name: Christophe de Margerie
headline: Christophe de Margerie, Swashbuckling Chief of Total Oil, Is Dead at 63
abstract: Mr. de Margerie, who was called Big Mustache by colleagues for his exceptional facial hair, was a charismatic French oil executive known for speaking his mind.

name: Ben Bradlee
headline: Ben Bradlee, Washington Editor and Watergate Warrior, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Bradlee, a quintessential newspaper editor, supervised The Washington Post’s exposure of the Watergate scandal that led to the resignation of President Richard M. Nixon.

name: Paul Craft
headline: Paul Craft, Witty Country Music Songwriter, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Craft’s hits included “Brother Jukebox” and “Dropkick Me, Jesus.”

name: Stephen Paulus
headline: Stephen Paulus, Classical Composer Rich in Lyricism, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Paulus’s warmly received musical output was prodigious, including 13 operas and some 400 choral works.

name: Nelson Bunker Hunt
profession: Oil Tycoon With a Texas-Size Presence
headline: Nelson Bunker Hunt, 88, Oil Tycoon With a Texas-Size Presence, Dies
abstract: The eccentric scion of a prominent Dallas family that made a fortune in oil, Mr. Hunt tried and failed to corner the world’s silver market in 1980.

name: Carolyn Rovee-Collier
headline: Carolyn Rovee-Collier, Who Said Babies Have Clear Memories, Is Dead at 72
abstract: Dr. Rovee-Collier, a developmental psychologist at Rutgers University, showed in a series of papers in the early 1980s that babies remembered plenty.

name: René Burri
headline: René Burri, Photographer of Picasso and Che, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Burri was a globe-trotting photographer who documented figures like Pablo Picasso and Che Guevara, as well as urban scenes and war.

name: Rick Piltz
profession: Quit Bush White House Over Climate Policy
headline: Rick Piltz Dies at 71; Quit Bush White House Over Climate Policy
abstract: Mr. Piltz, a climate policy analyst, resigned from the administration of George W. Bush in 2005, accusing it of distorting scientific findings for political reasons and then releasing internal White House documents to support his contention.

name: Donald Pels
headline: Donald Pels, 86, Dies; Media Executive Saw Cellphone Future
abstract: Mr. Pels, whose early investment in cellphone networks paid off for his company and for himself, had become a major philanthropist in his later years.

name: Frank Mankiewicz
profession: Press Aide to Robert Kennedy and NPR Chief
headline: Frank Mankiewicz, 90, Press Aide to Robert Kennedy and NPR Chief, Dies
abstract: After growing up amid Hollywood royalty, Mr. Mankiewicz became a writer and Democratic strategist who drew the sad task of announcing Mr. Kennedy’s death in 1968.

name: Joan Quigley
headline: Joan Quigley, Astrologer to a First Lady, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Miss Quigley, a Vassar-educated socialite, made celestial recommendations through phone calls to Nancy Reagan, often two or three a day.

name: Alfred Wertheimer
headline: Alfred Wertheimer, Early Photographer of Elvis Presley, Dies at 84
abstract: Assigned by a record label to take publicity shots, Mr. Wertheimer photographed rock ‘n’ roll’s earliest superstar in his earliest days.

name: John-Roger
profession: New Age Spiritual Leader in California
headline: John-Roger, New Age Spiritual Leader in California, Dies at 80
abstract: The founder of the Movement of Spiritual Inner Awareness gained a following among the Hollywood crowd, though some former adherents accused him of various misdeeds.

name: Chen Ziming
headline: Chen Ziming, Dissident in China, Is Dead at 62
abstract: A reform-minded intellectual, Mr. Chen, was accused by the government of fomenting the Tiananmen Square protests in 1989 and spent more than a decade in prison and under house arrest.

name: Msgr. William O’Brien
headline: Msgr. William O’Brien, 90, Dies; Innovator in Treating Drug Abuse
abstract: The monsignor helped start the Daytop Village network and was a fierce critic of the war on drugs.

name: Jack Bruce
headline: Jack Bruce, Cream’s Adventurous Bassist, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Bruce’s adventurous approach to his instrument influenced two generations of rock bassists.

name: Doris Hering
headline: Doris Hering, 94, Dies; Critic Championed Regional Dance
abstract: Ms. Hering, immersed in the New York dance world, eventually used her leverage to promote regional scenes around the country.

name: Stan M. Jay
profession: Seller of Strings to the Stars
headline: Stan M. Jay, Seller of Strings to the Stars, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Jay was the owner and co-founder of Mandolin Brothers, a Staten Island musical instrument store well known by world-famous and ordinary musicians alike.

name: Efua Dorkenoo
headline: Efua Dorkenoo, Who Campaigned Against Genital Cutting, Dies at 65
abstract: Ms. Dorkenoo led a successful 30-year campaign against the tradition of genital cutting of girls and women, mainly in Africa and the Middle East, by casting the practice as a human rights violation.

name: L. M. Kit Carson
profession: Actor and Writer in Independent Film
headline: L. M. Kit Carson, Actor and Writer in Independent Film, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Carson earned a following among devotees of independent film with his magazine journalism about movies and his own quirky films.

name: Zambia
headline: Zambia’s Acerbic Leader, Michael Sata, Dies at 77
abstract: After years working in the opposition and three failed election bids, Mr. Sata became president in 2011, promising to reduce inequality.

name: Zambia
headline: Zambia’s Former President Edgar Lungu Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Lungu, who was recently barred by a court ruling from running for president again, left a checkered legacy, with allegations that he eroded freedoms while in office.

name: Galway Kinnell
headline: Galway Kinnell, Plain-Spoken Poet, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Kinnell’s works could encompass celebrations of Manhattan street life and meditations on mortality. In 1983, he won a Pulitzer and a National Book Award.

name: Jack Broughton
profession: Pilot in Vietnam Turned Critic of Leaders
headline: Jack Broughton, 89, Dies; Pilot in Vietnam Turned Critic of Leaders
abstract: The Air Force accused him of covering up the strafing of a Soviet freighter in the North Vietnamese port of Cam Pha by a pilot under his command.

name: Susan Sollins
headline: Susan Sollins, a Creator of PBS’s ‘Art21’ Series, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Sollins organized art shows for small communities then produced Art21, a groundbreaking television series focusing on significant contemporary artists.

name: Terry Keenan
headline: Terry Keenan, Populist Finance Reporter, Dies at 53
abstract: Ms. Keenan, who was known for her straightforward vocabulary, worked for several media outlets, including CNN and Fox News.

name: Thomas M. Menino
headline: Thomas M. Menino, Mayor Who Led Boston’s Renaissance, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Mr. Menino was Boston’s longest-serving mayor, and helped transform it from a gritty parochial town to an economic and cultural hub of New England.

name: Roderick M. Hills
profession: Counsel to Gerald Ford and S.E.C. Chairman
headline: Roderick M. Hills, Counsel to Gerald Ford and S.E.C. Chairman, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Hills was a deputy counsel to President Gerald R. Ford and former chairman of the Securities and Exchange Commission.

name: David Armstrong
headline: David Armstrong, Photographer of Subcultures, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Armstrong photographed the often overlapping worlds of gay men, drug addicts, transvestites, fashion models and creative artists.

name: Herb Schapiro
profession: Playwright Behind The Me Nobody Knows
headline: Herb Schapiro, Playwright Behind ‘The Me Nobody Knows,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Inspired by essays by urban children, Mr. Schapiro had the idea for what became a “dark and lovely” Broadway musical.

name: Alagappa Alagappan
headline: Alagappa Alagappan, 88, Dies; Founded Hindu Temples Across U.S.
abstract: Mr. Alagappan, a native of India, began a movement in 1970 to build Hindu temples in the United States.

name: Bernard Mayes
headline: Bernard Mayes, 85, Dies; Started First U.S. Suicide Hotline
abstract: Mr. Mayes, a multifaceted Anglican priest, started the first suicide hotline in the United States and a decade later became the founding chairman of National Public Radio.

name: Bernard Spitzer
headline: Bernard Spitzer, New York Developer and Philanthropist, Dies at 90
abstract: He long supported his son Eliot’s political career and at times became entangled in it, as well as built a real estate empire over more than five decades.

name: Jonathan P. Hicks
profession: Former Reporter for The New York Times
headline: Jonathan P. Hicks, Former Reporter for The New York Times, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Hicks covered big business and all levels of New York politics for over 24 years as a reporter for The Times.

name: Beverly Blossom
headline: Beverly Blossom, Solo Dancer With a ‘Voice,’ Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Blossom was influenced by the work of Bertolt Brecht and studied in Germany with a dance teacher of the expressionist tradition.

name: Brittany Maynard
headline: Brittany Maynard, ‘Death With Dignity’ Ally, Dies at 29
abstract: Ms. Maynard became a public face for the “death with dignity” movement after she was found to have terminal brain cancer. She ended her life on Saturday at her home in Portland, Ore.

name: David M. Abshire
headline: David M. Abshire, Who Helped Reagan Through Iran-Contra Scandal, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Abshire also served as United States ambassador to NATO, held other high-level government posts and led respected research groups.

name: Tom Magliozzi
profession: One Half of the Jovial Brothers on Car Talk
headline: Tom Magliozzi, One Half of the Jovial Brothers on ‘Car Talk,’ Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Magliozzi hosted the popular NPR show “Car Talk” for more than 30 years with his younger brother, Ray, in which they bantered with callers through an automotive prism.

name: Thomas Sneddon
headline: Thomas Sneddon, 73, Dies; Prosecuted Michael Jackson Case
abstract: Mr. Sneddon was a district attorney who failed twice to convict Mr. Jackson on child molestation charges and became the target of a bitter song on one of the pop star’s albums.

name: Lorenzo Albacete
headline: Lorenzo Albacete, Theologian and Confidant of Popes, Dies at 73
abstract: Msgr. Albacete, a former aerospace researcher turned Roman Catholic priest, became one of the Vatican’s most articulate, unofficial defenders in the United States.

name: Donald Saddler
headline: Donald Saddler, Dancer, and a Choreographer on Broadway, Dies at 96
abstract: A soloist with Ballet Theater, Mr. Saddler made his Broadway musical theater debut in 1947, and he went on to win two Tonys as a Broadway choreographer.

name: Hubert de Montille
headline: Hubert de Montille, French Winemaker, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. de Montille was known for his insistence that wine should speak clearly of the place and the culture that produced it.

name: Jo Ann Harris
headline: Jo Ann Harris, 81, Dies; Prosecuted Headline Cases
abstract: Ms. Harris investigated a confrontation between government lawyers and Monica Lewinski, and helped prosecute Imelda Marcos on corruption charges.

name: David Redfern
profession: British Photographer of Jazz and Pop
headline: David Redfern, British Photographer of Jazz and Pop, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Redfern’s images of greats like Miles Davis, the Beatles and Jimi Hendrix became the basis for an important picture archive.

name: Manitas de Plata
headline: Manitas de Plata, Superstar of the Flamenco Guitar, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Mr. de Plata, considered a crowd pleaser rather than an observer of the music’s formal ritual traditions, picked up his distinct style of play as a young boy.

name: Richard Schaal
profession: TV Actor and Second City Veteran
headline: Richard Schaal, TV Actor and Second City Veteran, Dies at 86
abstract: Best known for his recurring appearances on hit shows like “The Dick Van Dyke Show” and “The Mary Tyler Moore Show,” Mr. Schaal was also a writer and an early member of Second City in Chicago.

name: S. Donald Stookey
headline: S. Donald Stookey, Scientist, Dies at 99; Among His Inventions Was CorningWare
abstract: By accident, Dr. Stookey discovered a highly versatile material that could be used in everything from guided missiles to cookware.

name: Larry Agenbroad
headline: Larry Agenbroad, Paleontologist at Mammoths’ Graveyard, Dies at 81
abstract: Dr. Agenbroad presided over a decades-long excavation in South Dakota that gave rise to the Mammoth Site museum and continues to yield fossils.

name: Clement A. Price
headline: Clement A. Price, a Cheerleader for Newark, Dies at 69
abstract: Professor Price was a Rutgers scholar with a deep affection for Newark, a city he wrote about, taught about, promoted and defended.

name: Ina Ginsburg
headline: Ina Ginsburg, Arts Patron and Washington Hostess, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Ginsburg, who fled to the United States from Austria during World War II, went on to champion the works of modern artists and actors, including Andy Warhol and Arnold Schwarzenegger.

name: Philip M. Crane
profession: Former Illinois Congressman and Conservative Leader
headline: Philip M. Crane, Former Illinois Congressman and Conservative Leader, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Crane, a Republican, was best known as leader of the American Conservative Union, leading its unsuccessful fight against the treaties turning the Panama Canal over to Panama.

name: Ernie Vandeweghe
headline: Ernie Vandeweghe, Knick and Physician, Dies at 86
abstract: A leading Knicks player of the early 1950s, Vandeweghe was also the patriarch of a three-generation family of athletes that includes the current professional tennis player Coco Vandeweghe.

name: John V. Shields Jr.
profession: Turned Trader Joes Into National Chain
headline: John V. Shields Jr., Who Turned Trader Joe’s Into National Chain, Dies at 82
abstract: Taking over in 1989, Mr. Shields opened stores in college towns and gentrifying communities, raising annual sales to $2 billion, from $132 million, by the time he retired in 2001.

name: Jerry Tallmer
headline: Jerry Tallmer, Critic Who Created the Obies, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Tallmer, the first theater critic for The Village Voice, also conceived its award for Off Broadway theater, the Obie.

name: H. Gary Morse
headline: H. Gary Morse, Who Built Mecca for Retirees, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Mr. Morse turned a small mobile home park in Central Florida into large and politically influential development that drew retirees from around the country.

name: John Doar
profession: Federal Lawyer on Front Lines Against Segregation
headline: John Doar, Federal Lawyer on Front Lines Against Segregation, Dies at 92
abstract: A Republican, Mr. Doar prosecuted some of the most notorious cases of murder in the South in the ’60s and was chief counsel to the House panel investigating Watergate.

name: Big Bank Hank
headline: Big Bank Hank, an Early Star of Rap, Dies at 58
abstract: Big Bank Hank was one of the three members of the Sugarhill Gang, whose “Rapper’s Delight” put rap on the commercial map.

name: Marge Roukema
headline: Marge Roukema, Congresswoman, Dies at 85; Backed Family Leave
abstract: Mrs. Roukema was a Republican whose moderate views often put her at odds with her party, most notably in her support of the Family and Medical Leave Act.

name: Daniel Meltzer
headline: Daniel Meltzer, Protector of the Beacon Theater, Dies at 74
abstract: A writer and teacher with a varied career, Mr. Meltzer led the successful fight to rescue one of New York City’s most grandiose showplaces from being turned into a discothèque.

name: Carol Ann Susi
profession: Unseen Actress on Big Bang Theory
headline: Carol Ann Susi, Unseen Actress on ‘Big Bang Theory,’ Is Dead at 62
abstract: Ms. Susi was a character actress best known for the off-screen role of a haranguing mother on the CBS sitcom “The Big Bang Theory.”

name: Harry Pearson
headline: Harry Pearson, Founder of Absolute Sound, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Pearson was a journalist and audiophile who founded a magazine for connoisseurs of high-fidelity audio in the 1970s.

name: Alvin Dark
profession: Led Giants to Pennants as Captain and Manager
headline: Alvin Dark, 92, Dies; Led Giants to Pennants as Captain and Manager
abstract: A top shortstop, Dark led the New York Giants’ pennant-winning teams in the 1950s, then managed them into the World Series in San Francisco. But his comments about minority players shadowed him.

name: Gisèle Masson
profession: Fed the Famous at La Grenouille
headline: Gisèle Masson Dies at 89; Fed the Famous at La Grenouille
abstract: Mme. Masson was known to visit tables, especially during dessert, at her classic French restaurant on the East Side of Manhattan.

name: Delford Smith
headline: Delford Smith, Founder of Aviation Company, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Smith, whose company flew military support missions during several wars, was known for his determination to preserve the Spruce Goose, the world’s largest flying boat, which remains an attraction at the Evergreen Aviation and Space Museum.

name: Gus Vlahavas
headline: Gus Vlahavas, 76, Who Ran a Brooklyn Culinary Haven, Dies
abstract: The ice cream parlor was a family institution, opened in 1936 by Mr. Vlahavas’s grandfather.

name: Jane Byrne
headline: Jane Byrne, Only Woman to Lead Chicago, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Byrne stunned Chicago’s Democratic machine in 1979 when she was elected mayor after sharply criticizing the incumbent for his handling of a devastating winter.

name: James A. Lebenthal
headline: James A. Lebenthal, Muni Bond Expert, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Lebenthal turned the tax-free financial instruments called munis into household words with radio and television ads.

name: Ernest Kinoy
headline: Ernest Kinoy, a Writer of TV’s ‘Roots,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Kinoy wrote television scripts that ranged from “Playhouse 90” presentations to “Victory at Entebbe.”

name: Alexander Grothendieck
headline: Alexander Grothendieck, Math Enigma, Dies at 86
abstract: His gift for abstraction excavated new ground in algebraic geometry and supplied a theoretical foundation for the solving of some of the most vexing conundrums of modern mathematics.

name: Dorian Paskowitz
headline: Dorian Paskowitz Dies at 93: Doctor and Surfer Lived an Endless Summer
abstract: Mr. Paskowitz gave up a lucrative medical practice to embark, with his family, on a peripatetic and celebrated surfing life.

name: Kakha Bendukidze
headline: Kakha Bendukidze Dies at 58; Pushed Post-Soviet Market Change
abstract: Mr. Bendukidze, a biologist and later a wealthy businessman in the final years of the Soviet Union, became an architect of economic and governmental changes in his native Georgia.

name: Carl Schlesinger
headline: Carl Schlesinger, 88, Dies; Helped Usher Out Hot Type
abstract: Mr. Schlesinger, a former typesetter at The New York Times, helped make a documentary about the last night the newspaper was made using hot-metal type.

name: Tomas Young
profession: Critic of Iraq War in Film
headline: Tomas Young, Army Veteran, Dies at 34; Critic of Iraq War in Film
abstract: Mr. Young was the subject of a film that showed the devastating human cost of the war and argued that it should have never been fought.

name: Saud bin Mohammed al-Thani
headline: Saud bin Mohammed al-Thani, Big-Spending Art Collector, Is Dead
abstract: Sheikh Saud, as Qatar’s culture minister, spent an estimated $1.5 billion on world art and objects.

name: Irving Peress
headline: Dr. Irving Peress, Target of McCarthy Crusade, Dies at 97
abstract: When Dr. Peress, a dentist serving in the Army, was promoted to major, Senator Joseph R. McCarthy said he was convinced it was part of “special treatment for Communists.”

name: Bill Frenzel
profession: Key Voice on Economics in House
headline: Bill Frenzel, Key Voice on Economics in House, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Frenzel had been appointed to governmental panels by presidents of both parties since ending his 20-year career in Congress, and he was a guest scholar at the Brookings Institution.

name: Carl Sanders
headline: Carl Sanders, 89, Dies; Led Georgia in ’60s
abstract: In his single term as governor, Mr. Sanders cautiously navigated the racial turmoil of the time, promoting Georgia as a region of relative calm amid the storms of the South.

name: Charles Champlin
headline: Charles Champlin, Critic and Memoirist, Dies at 88
abstract: Known as a graceful, knowledgeable writer with a gentlemanly respect for the art of film, Mr. Champlin was the lead movie critic for The Los Angeles Times from 1967 until 1980 and reviewed books thereafter.

name: Willy Burgdorfer
headline: Willy Burgdorfer, Who Found Bacteria That Cause Lyme Disease, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Dr. Burgdorfer’s familiar finding while conducting tick surgery solved the mysteries of an ailment that had affected scores of people.

name: Jimmy Ruffin
profession: Singer of a Memorable Motown Hit
headline: Jimmy Ruffin, Singer of a Memorable Motown Hit, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Ruffin was best known for the plaintive “What Becomes of the Brokenhearted,” a hit in 1966.

name: John T. Downey
profession: Held Captive in China for 20 Years
headline: John T. Downey Dies at 84; Held Captive in China for 20 Years
abstract: Mr. Downey became the longest-serving American prisoner of war by surviving more than 20 years in Chinese prisons after being shot down over Manchuria in 1952.

name: Mike Nichols
profession: Urbane Director Loved by Crowds and Critics
headline: Mike Nichols, Urbane Director Loved by Crowds and Critics, Dies at 83
abstract: One of America’s most decorated directors, Mr. Nichols had a protean résumé of critic- and crowd-pleasing work, including “The Graduate” in film and “The Odd Couple” on stage.

name: of Alba
headline: The Duchess of Alba, an Unconventional Aristocrat, Dies at 88
abstract: The flamboyant Spanish aristocrat was head of the five-century-old House of Alba. Her outspokenness and unconventional choices of marriage partners made her a media sensation.

name: Harland Stonecipher
headline: Harland Stonecipher, Insurance Pioneer, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Stonecipher, an insurance salesman, started Pre-Paid Legal Services after his difficulties with legal costs from an auto accident.

name: William Spoor
profession: Turned Pillsbury Into a Food Industry Giant
headline: William Spoor Dies at 91; Turned Pillsbury Into a Food Industry Giant
abstract: Mr. Spoor grew up in poverty and worked his way to becoming chief executive and chairman of Pillsbury, where he was known as a demanding and abrasive leader.

name: Donald F. Steiner
headline: Dr. Donald F. Steiner, Diabetes Researcher, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Steiner, whose discoveries were used by insulin manufacturers to improve their products, wrote hundreds of articles as a professor at the University of Chicago.

name: Richard Eder
headline: Richard Eder, Arts Critic and Foreign Correspondent, Dies at 82
abstract: A journalist with a literary bent, Mr. Eder wrote with an easy grace and a practiced eye for detail.

name: Raleigh Trevelyan
headline: Raleigh Trevelyan, Chronicler of a Notable Family, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Trevelyan’s books included a biography of Walter Raleigh and a look at the experiences of his many relatives in British India.

name: Victor Elmaleh
headline: Victor Elmaleh, 95, Builder and Entrepreneur, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Elmaleh imported the first Volkswagens to the United States, developed $7 billion worth of real estate and won national championships in handball and squash.

name: Marion Barry
headline: Marion Barry, Washington’s ‘Mayor for Life,’ Even After Prison, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Barry was a flamboyant and polarizing mayor of the nation’s capital who went to prison on a cocaine charge and then made one of the most improbable comebacks in the history of American politics.

name: William H. Scheide
headline: William H. Scheide, 100, Philanthropist, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Scheide devoted his life to philanthropic and artistic pursuits striking in their range and depth.

name: Ray Sadecki
headline: Ray Sadecki, Who Helped Cardinals Win World Series, Dies at 73
abstract: Sadecki, a left-handed pitcher, won 135 games in his 18 seasons in the major leagues, finishing his career with the Mets.

name: Leslie Feinberg
headline: Leslie Feinberg, Writer and Transgender Activist, Dies at 65
abstract: Feinberg’s 1993 novel, “Stone Butch Blues,” is considered a landmark in the contemporary literature of gender complexity.

name: Pat Quinn
headline: Pat Quinn, Coach Who Led Canada to Olympic Gold, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Quinn followed up a bruising career as a hockey player by steering Canada to its first Olympic gold medal in 50 years and twice winning coach-of-the-year honors in the National Hockey League.

name: Viktor Tikhonov
headline: Viktor Tikhonov Dies at 84: Soviet Hockey Coach in ‘Miracle on Ice’
abstract: Tikhonov was the domineering coach of the powerful Soviet national hockey team that won three Olympic gold medals and one devastating silver — when the Soviets lost to the United States in the 1980 Lake Placid Games.

name: Paul Katz
headline: Paul Katz, Big-Picture Architect, Dies at 57
abstract: As president and managing principal of one of the world’s leading architectural firms, Kohn Pedersen Fox Associates, Mr. Katz was the mastermind of many of its major projects in Japan, Shanghai, London and New York.

name: Lewis Baltz
headline: Lewis Baltz, Photographer of American Landscapes, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Baltz was part of the New Topographics movement, known for a seemingly dispassionate, affectless presentation of its subjects.

name: Nancy H. Teeters
profession: First Woman on Federal Reserve Board
headline: Nancy H. Teeters, First Woman on Federal Reserve Board, Dies at 84
abstract: A liberal economist, Mrs. Teeters often criticized actions by her fellow governors.

name: Dodo Cheney
headline: Dodo Cheney, a Tennis Champion for Decades, Dies at 98
abstract: She won 391 tennis championships in the United States, most of them after she turned 55.

name: Bunny Briggs
headline: Bunny Briggs, Tap Dancing Virtuoso, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Briggs’s career bridged the history of tap from Bill (Bojangles) Robinson to Savion Glover.

name: Francis Fraser
headline: Francis Fraser, Who Cashed In on His Cruelty, Dies at 90
abstract: Known as a British underworld enforcer and once suspected in as many as 40 deaths, Mr. Fraser turned his life of crime into a lucrative retirement by chronicling his own deeds in books and films.

name: Lucien Clergue
profession: Master and Promoter of Art Photography
headline: Lucien Clergue, Master and Promoter of Art Photography, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Clergue enjoyed a national stature in France for his modernist work, famous patrons and photography festival in Arles.

name: P. D. James
profession: Creator of the Adam Dalgliesh Mysteries
headline: P. D. James, Creator of the Adam Dalgliesh Mysteries, Dies at 94
abstract: A consummate stylist, the British author and baroness accumulated numerous awards for the 18 crime novels produced during her 49-year writing career.

name: Lester Bernstein
headline: Lester Bernstein, 94, Dies; Wide-Ranging Journalist Edited Newsweek
abstract: Mr. Bernstein, who also wrote for The New York Times and Time magazine, helped arrange America’s first televised presidential debates when he was an NBC vice president in 1960.

name: Denham Harman
headline: Denham Harman, 98, Dies; Sought Leverage on Aging
abstract: Dr. Harman’s ideas about free radical cell damage and the aging process were well ahead of his time.

name: Mary Hinkson
headline: Mary Hinkson, a Star for Martha Graham, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Hinkson, known for her dramatic power, was one of the first two black dancers to join the company.

name: Frank Yablans
headline: Frank Yablans, Paramount Executive in Fertile ’70s, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Yablans spent time as president of Paramount Pictures while it released some of the most acclaimed movies of the 1970s and led MGM/UA in the 1980s.

name: Roberto Gómez Bolaños
headline: Roberto Gómez Bolaños, Mexico’s Comedic Artist ‘Chespirito,’ Dies at 85
abstract: The actor, writer and director was known around the Spanish-speaking world for his iconic characters and widely viewed television shows.

name: Sabah
profession: Enduring Star in Arab World Entertainment
headline: Sabah, Enduring Star in Arab World Entertainment, Dies at 87
abstract: Her fame in the Arab world as an entertainer endured for six decades.

name: Mark Strand
headline: Mark Strand, 80, Dies; Pulitzer-Winning Poet Laureate
abstract: To critics who said Mr. Strand’s poems were too dark he replied, “I find them evenly lit.”

name: Claire Barry
headline: Claire Barry, Half of Yiddish Singing Duo, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Barry and her sister Merna were Yiddish singers who rose to international fame and appeared numerous times on “The Ed Sullivan Show.”

name: Anthony D. Marshall
headline: Anthony D. Marshall, Astor Son Who Was Convicted in Swindle, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Marshall, along with one of Brooke Astor’s former lawyers, was found guilty of criminal charges that they swindled millions from her after she was stricken with Alzheimer’s disease.

name: Bobby Keys
headline: Bobby Keys, Hard-Living Saxophonist for Rolling Stones, Dies at 70
