abstract: Mr. Keys was a self-taught musician who never learned to read music but recorded with a Who’s Who of rock. One of his most memorable moments was a howling solo on “Brown Sugar.”

name: Patrick Suppes
headline: Patrick Suppes, Pioneer in Computerized Learning, Dies at 92
abstract: In 1966, almost a decade before the invention of the personal computer, he predicted that children would have access to personal tutors “as well informed and as responsive as Aristotle.”

name: Kent Haruf
headline: Kent Haruf, Acclaimed Novelist of Small-Town Life, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Mr. Haruf’s breakthrough novel was “Plainsong,” which was nominated for the National Book Award.

name: Brumsic Brandon Jr.
headline: Brumsic Brandon Jr., Creator of ‘Luther’ Strip, Dies at 87
abstract: “Luther” was one of the first nationally syndicated comic strips set in a black urban neighborhood.

name: Jean Béliveau
profession: Leader of Canadiens and a Hero to Canadians
headline: Jean Béliveau, Leader of Canadiens and a Hero to Canadians, Dies at 83
abstract: Béliveau, one of the greatest centers in N.H.L. history, was an icon in Canada, and he led Montreal to 10 Stanley Cups in his playing career.

name: Herman Badillo
profession: Congressman and Fixture of New York Politics
headline: Herman Badillo, Congressman and Fixture of New York Politics, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Badillo, whose political odyssey spanned Kennedy liberalism in the 1960s to Giuliani conservatism in the 1990s, became the first Puerto Rico-born congressman.

name: Ian McLagan
headline: Ian McLagan, Keyboardist With the Faces, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. McLagan was a keyboardist with the Small Faces and later the Faces, and a sideman who traveled widely in rock circles, working with Bob Dylan, the Rolling Stones and Bruce Springsteen.

name: Brian Macdonald
headline: Brian Macdonald, Eclectic Choreographer and Director, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Macdonald worked with classical, contemporary and regional material, from Bach to Gilbert and Sullivan and on to Leonard Cohen.

name: Ian Player
headline: Ian Player Is Dead at 87; Helped to Save Rhinos
abstract: As a young game warden in South Africa, Mr. Player devised a plan to capture rhinos and ship them to other reserves, parks and game farms throughout Africa, and zoos and safari parks around the world.

name: Jeremy Thorpe
headline: Jeremy Thorpe, M.P. Accused in Scandal, Dies at 85
abstract: The British politician revived the fortunes of the Liberal Party, but his career was destroyed by allegations of a murder conspiracy conceived to cover up a homosexual relationship.

name: Arthur Leipzig
profession: Photographer of Everyday Life in New York
headline: Arthur Leipzig, Photographer of Everyday Life in New York, Dies at 96
abstract: Known for his crisp, emotionally provocative images, Mr. Leipzig was of a generation of socially minded photographers who took to the streets to record life as they encountered it.

name: Claudia Emerson
headline: Claudia Emerson, Pulitzer-Winning Poet, Dies at 57
abstract: Ms. Emerson, who won the Pulitzer Prize for poetry in 2006, found meaning and metaphor in the landscapes of her native South.

name: Martin Litton
headline: Martin Litton, Fighter for Environment, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Litton, a former director of the Sierra Club, was unrelenting in his efforts to preserve what was left of the wilderness in the American West, most notably the Grand Canyon and the Colorado River.

name: Wynn Chamberlain
headline: Wynn Chamberlain, an Artist in Paint, on Screen and in Novels, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Chamberlain, whose friends included the poet Allen Ginsberg and the pop artist Andy Warhol, was also an author and a producer.

name: Ralph H. Baer
profession: Inventor of First System for Home Video Games
headline: Ralph H. Baer, Inventor of First System for Home Video Games, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Baer, who worked as an engineer at a military contractor, became obsessed with building a “game box” that would allow people to play games on a standard television set.

name: Alla Sizova
headline: Alla Sizova, a Star Ballerina With the Kirov, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Sizova’s talent was so great she went directly from school to soloist for the Kirov Ballet, often partnering with Rudolf Nureyev.

name: Ernest Brace
profession: Civilian Pilot Held as P.O.W. in Vietnam
headline: Ernest Brace, Civilian Pilot Held as P.O.W. in Vietnam, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Brace, a C.I.A. contract flier, was held in a Hanoi prison cell next to that of a future senator, John McCain.

name: Nathaniel Branden
profession: Partner in Love and Business With Ayn Rand
headline: Nathaniel Branden, a Partner in Love and Business With Ayn Rand, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Branden, a devotee of the author Ayn Rand, became her lover and business associate, before going on to write a series of books about self-esteem.

name: Dollree Mapp
profession: Defied Police Search in Landmark Case
headline: Dollree Mapp, Who Defied Police Search in Landmark Case, Is Dead
abstract: When officers in Cleveland could not prove they had a warrant, Ms. Mapp’s objections led to a 1961 Supreme Court ruling that extended limits on police power and evidence.

name: Juan Flores
profession: Scholar of Puerto Rican Culture in New York
headline: Juan Flores, a Scholar of Puerto Rican Culture in New York, Dies at 71
abstract: Professor Flores, a pioneer in studying “Nuyorican” culture, was the director of Latino studies at New York University and an advocate for Puerto Rican writers.

name: Mary Ann Mobley
profession: Midcentury Miss America and an Actress
headline: Mary Ann Mobley, a Midcentury Miss America and an Actress, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Mobley, who was crowned in 1958, starred in two films with Elvis Presley and appeared in television shows and on Broadway.

name: Jane Freilicher
profession: Lyrical Painter of Long Island Landscapes
headline: Jane Freilicher, 90, a Lyrical Painter of Long Island Landscapes, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Freilicher was a stubbornly independent painter whose light-saturated yet recognizable images made her an anomaly in an era dominated by abstraction.

name: Gil Marks
profession: Historian of Jewish Food and Culture
headline: Gil Marks, Historian of Jewish Food and Culture, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Marks wrote five books that chronicled kosher menus through the centuries and examined the role of food in the establishment and growth of cultural traditions.

name: Karl Otto Pöhl
profession: Former President of the German Central Bank
headline: Karl Otto Pöhl, a Former President of the German Central Bank, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Pöhl had a fixation on price stability that still guides eurozone monetary policy and was an anti-inflation hawk.

name: Ann Marcus
headline: Ann Marcus, Writer for ‘Mary Hartman,’ Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Marcus wrote many episodes of shows like “Peyton Place” as well as the soap-opera parody “Mary Hartman, Mary Hartman.”

name: Kathleen O’Keefe
headline: Kathleen O’Keefe, a Newspaper Pioneer in Cambodia, Dies at 54
abstract: In founding The Phnom Penh Post in 1992, Ms. O’Keefe introduced objective journalism in a still-tumultuous Cambodia.

name: Michel du Cille
headline: Michel du Cille, 58, Photographer Who Won 3 Pulitzer Prizes, Dies
abstract: For The Miami Herald and then The Washington Post, Mr. du Cille captured people in dire circumstances, including a natural disaster and drugs and poverty.

name: Mary Burke Nicholas Washington
profession: Led New York Police Review Board
headline: Mary Burke Nicholas Washington Dies at 88; Led New York Police Review Board
abstract: As Mary Burke Nicholas, the name by which she was known before 1994, Mrs. Washington held prominent government posts in New York throughout the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Rose Cochran
profession: Figure in a Campaign Attack Video
headline: Rose Cochran, a Figure in a Campaign Attack Video, Dies at 73
abstract: Mrs. Cochran, a former teacher, was in a nursing home when she became part of an unsuccessful attack ad against her husband, Senator Thad Cochran.

name: Robert B. Oakley
headline: Robert B. Oakley, Envoy Deft at Tackling Crises, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Oakley was best known for negotiating the release of an American pilot held by Somali militiamen in 1993 in what was known as the “Black Hawk Down” crisis.

name: Sy Berger
profession: Turned Baseball Heroes Into Brilliant Rectangles
headline: Sy Berger, Who Turned Baseball Heroes Into Brilliant Rectangles, Dies at 91
abstract: During the 1950s with the Brooklyn-based Topps company, Mr. Berger was credited with creating the modern baseball card, adding color, statistics and facsimiles of stars’ signatures.

name: Neil Reshen
headline: Neil Reshen, 75, Dies; Manager Won ‘Outlaw’ Singers’ Freedom
abstract: Mr. Reshen, who started out doing music executives’ taxes, made deals for Willie Nelson, Waylon Jennings and others.

name: Phil Stern
profession: Photographed War, Movie Stars and a President
headline: Phil Stern, 95, Dies; Photographed War, Movie Stars and a President
abstract: Mr. Stern was a combat cameraman in World War II, and also captured intimate photographs of Sinatra, Bogart, Brando and Monroe, as well as the new President Kennedy.

name: David Garth
profession: Consultant Was an Innovator of Political TV Ads
headline: David Garth, 84, Dies; Consultant Was an Innovator of Political TV Ads
abstract: Mr. Garth helped elect governors, senators and four mayors of New York.

name: Fuzzy Thurston
profession: Big Broom in the Packers Great Sweep Play
headline: Fuzzy Thurston, Big Broom in the Packers’ Great Sweep Play, Dies at 80
abstract: The Green Bay left guard paved the way for the likes of the Hall of Famers Bart Starr, Paul Hornung and Jim Taylor.

name: Norman Bridwell
profession: Creator of Clifford the Big Red Dog Books
headline: Norman Bridwell, Creator of ‘Clifford the Big Red Dog’ Books, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Bridwell’s “Clifford” books, about a dog as big as a house, became an international favorite for parents to read aloud to their children.

name: Dick Rich
headline: Dick Rich, Who Helped Redefine TV Advertising, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Rich’s whimsical and sardonic commercials for clients like Alka-Seltzer helped introduce a more freewheeling approach to TV advertising in the 1960s.

name: Richard C. Hottelet
profession: CBS Newsman and Last of Murrow Boys
headline: Richard C. Hottelet, CBS Newsman and Last of ‘Murrow Boys,’ Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Hottelet, only 26 when he was hired by Edward R. Murrow, covered the invasion of Normandy and the Battle of the Bulge for CBS News.

name: Irene Dalis
headline: Irene Dalis, Opera Singer and Company Founder, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Dalis was a mezzo-soprano who starred at the Metropolitan Opera for two decades before building a second career as the founder and director of Opera San José.

name: Ernie Terrell
headline: Ernie Terrell, Heavyweight Champion, Dies at 75; Lost Grudge Match to Ali
abstract: In 55 bouts, Terrell had 21 knockouts and a record of 46-9. He briefly shared the heavyweight championship with Muhammad Ali.

name: Lee W. Wattenberg
headline: Lee W. Wattenberg, Who Saw Cancer Fighters in Foods, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Wattenberg, a University of Minnesota researcher hailed as the “father of chemoprevention,” found weapons in chemical compounds in broccoli, cabbage, coffee and garlic.

name: Virna Lisi
headline: Virna Lisi, Italian Actress Lured to Hollywood, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Lisi, an Italian who had her breakthrough Hollywood role in “How to Murder Your Wife” in 1965, had an award-winning revival in the 1990s.

name: Mandy Rice-Davies
headline: Mandy Rice-Davies, Figure in Profumo Scandal, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Rice-Davies achieved notoriety in 1963 in one of Britain’s most spectacular sex scandals, which brought down a government minister.

name: Rock Scully
headline: Rock Scully, Grateful Dead’s Manager Who Put the Band on Records, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Scully became the manager of the psychedelic rock band shortly after seeing them perform at an Acid Test in 1965.

name: Laszlo Varga
profession: Cellist for the New York Philharmonic
headline: Laszlo Varga, Cellist for the New York Philharmonic, Is Dead at 89
abstract: After escaping a Nazi work camp, Mr. Varga became principal cellist for the New York Philharmonic in 1951 and remained in the post for 11 years.

name: Joe Cocker
profession: Raspy-Voiced Rock Star With Distinctive Moves
headline: Joe Cocker Is Dead at 70; Raspy-Voiced Rock Star With Distinctive Moves
abstract: Mr. Cocker was known for his passionate, idiosyncratic takes on songs like the Beatles’ “With a Little Help From My Friends.”

name: Udo Jürgens
headline: Udo Jürgens, Austrian Singer and Songwriter, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Jürgens, known as the Frank Sinatra of Europe, sold more than 100 million records over five decades.

name: Billie Whitelaw
headline: Billie Whitelaw, Longtime Beckett Muse, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Whitelaw, an English actress, first encountered Samuel Beckett’s work at the National Theater in London in 1964.

name: Larry Smith
headline: Larry Smith, Hip-Hop Producer, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Smith’s work with the pioneering group Run-DMC pushed hip-hop out of disco’s orbit with a signature recorded sound and helped move it closer to the mainstream.

name: J. Robert Beyster
headline: J. Robert Beyster, Scientist and Entrepreneur, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Dr. Beyster founded the company, the Science Applications International Corporation, to focus on projects for the United States government.

name: Brandon Stoddard
headline: Brandon Stoddard, 77, ABC Executive Who Brought ‘Roots’ to TV, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Stoddard shepherded the production of multipart dramas like “Rich Man, Poor Man” and “The Winds of War” that helped popularize the mini-series.

name: Carleton Mabee
headline: Carleton Mabee, Biographer of Morse, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Mabee, a history professor, won a Pulitzer Prize 70 years ago for his unsparing biography of the inventor and painter Samuel F. B. Morse.

name: Harold M. Schulweis
headline: Harold M. Schulweis, Progressive Rabbi, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Rabbi Schulweis was an influential rabbi and theologian who focused his sermons, books and social activism on connecting the Jewish community with the wider world — and vice versa.

name: Buddy DeFranco
headline: Buddy DeFranco, 91, Versatile Jazz Clarinetist, Dies
abstract: Mr. DeFranco started in the swing era and continued for decades, changing his style to suit the times.

name: James B. Edwards
profession: Long-Shot as Governor of South Carolina
headline: James B. Edwards, a Long-Shot as Governor of South Carolina, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Edwards, a dentist turned Republican politician, was governor of South Carolina in the 1970s and energy secretary under President Ronald Reagan.

name: Jeremy Lloyd
headline: Jeremy Lloyd, Creator of British TV Comedies, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Lloyd was a creator of the long-running BBC comedy series “ ’Allo ’Allo!” and “Are You Being Served?”

name: Per-Ingvar Branemark
headline: Per-Ingvar Branemark, Dental Innovator, Dies at 85
abstract: The Swedish physician and research professor made an accidental discovery that turned him into the father of the modern dental implant.

name: Janis Martin
headline: Janis Martin, Opera Star Who Stretched Her Range, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Martin, a mezzo-soprano who became a soprano, gained international recognition for her performances in Wagner and Strauss operas.

name: Claude Frank
headline: Claude Frank, Pianist Admired for Performing Beethoven, Dies at 89
abstract: In addition to his concert and recording career, Mr. Frank was also an influential teacher of generations of pianists.

name: Timothy Dowd
headline: Timothy Dowd, Detective Who Led Son of Sam Manhunt, Dies at 99
abstract: Under Inspector Dowd’s direction, over 300 police officers scoured New York City for the serial killer, David Berkowitz, in a search described as a needle-in-a-haystack endeavor.

name: Ricardo Porro
headline: Ricardo Porro, Exiled Cuban Architect, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Porro’s architecture gave lyrical expression to a hopeful young Cuban revolution in the early 1960s before he himself fell victim to its ideological hardening.

name: Gleb Yakunin
headline: Gleb Yakunin, Russian Priest and Dissident, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Father Yakunin challenged the Soviet government for its restrictions on religious liberty and accused the hierarchy of his own church of collaborating with the K.G.B.

name: Luise Rainer
profession: Won Best Actress Oscars for Two Years Running
headline: Luise Rainer Dies at 104; Won Best Actress Oscars for Two Years Running
abstract: Ms. Rainer, who was born in Germany, left the pressures of Hollywood after winning Oscars in consecutive years in the 1930s.

name: Paul Sprenger
headline: Paul Sprenger, Lawyer Who Fought Discrimination, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Sprenger won victories for minorities, older workers and women, including a landmark sexual harassment case on behalf of female miners, on which the film “North Country” was based.

name: Edward Herrmann
headline: Edward Herrmann, Actor With a Noble Air, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Herrmann could be formidable or friendly and was often cast in movies and on television in affluent roles as a lawyer, judge or millionaire.

name: Ben Ammi
headline: Ben Ammi Ben-Israel Dies at 75: Led Black Americans in Migration to Israel
abstract: Mr. Ben-Israel, a former metal worker from Chicago, became known as a holy father to members of the African Hebrew Israelites of Jerusalem.

name: Bob Hall
headline: Bob Hall, Harlem Globetrotter Who Relished the Showman Role, Dies at 87
abstract: A dazzling ball handler who was built like a Sherman tank, Hall would launch one-handed, no-look, behind-the-back passes that mesmerized universal crowds, even in the Soviet Union.

name: Bob Hall
profession: First Wheelchair Champion of the Boston Marathon
headline: Bob Hall, First Wheelchair Champion of the Boston Marathon, Dies at 74
abstract: His accomplishment in 1975 inspired thousands of disabled athletes to participate in races around the world.

name: John I. Goodlad
headline: John I. Goodlad, Progressive Educator, Dies at 94
abstract: Many of the views put forth by Professor Goodlad, whose study of American public schools involved more than 27,000 students, remain central to educational improvement efforts.

name: Mario Cuomo
profession: Ex-New York Governor and Liberal Beacon
headline: Mario Cuomo, Ex-New York Governor and Liberal Beacon, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Cuomo, a spellbinding orator and colorful personality who flirted with running for the presidency, lived to see his son Andrew follow in his footsteps as governor.

name: Donna Douglas
headline: Donna Douglas, the Fairest ‘Beverly Hillbilly,’ Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Douglas played the shapely daughter of the mountaineer Jed Clampett on the wildly popular television sitcom “The Beverly Hillbillies.”

name: Jimmy Dickens
headline: Jimmy Dickens, an Outsize Country Singer, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Dickens, who was small in stature but had a big voice, sang about rural life.

name: Miller Williams
headline: Miller Williams, Plain-Spoken Arkansas Poet, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Williams, the father of the singer Lucinda Williams, was a man of economical speech whose admirers included Richard Yates and Flannery O’Connor.

name: Serge Hochar
headline: Serge Hochar, Producer of Lebanese Wines, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Hochar made his Chateau Musar much admired, in part for having operated even as civil war raged in Lebanon.

name: Stanislaw Baranczak
headline: Stanislaw Baranczak, 68, Polish Underground Poet, Dies
abstract: Mr. Baranczak defied state censors to write about living under Communist oppression and later emigrated to the United States, where he taught at Harvard.

name: Edward W. Brooke III
headline: Edward W. Brooke III, 95, Senate Pioneer, Is Dead
abstract: A liberal Republican from Massachusetts, Mr. Brooke in 1966 became the first African-American popularly elected to the Senate.

name: Stuart Scott
headline: Stuart Scott, ESPN’s Voice of Exuberance, Dies at 49
abstract: The popular Mr. Scott, who was the network’s most prominent black anchor and made “Booyah!” his signature expression, had been ill with cancer.

name: Ulrich Beck
headline: Ulrich Beck, Sociologist Who Warned of Technology, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Beck shot to fame in 1986 with his book “Risk Society: Towards a New Modernity,” which argued that technology had also created new risks in spheres ranging from ecology to finance.

name: Michio Kushi
profession: Advocate of Natural Foods in the U.S
headline: Michio Kushi, Advocate of Natural Foods in the U.S., Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Kushi, a Japanese scholar who popularized the macrobiotic diet in the United States, helped to change the way health-conscious Americans eat.

name: Bess Myerson
headline: Bess Myerson, New Yorker of Beauty, Wit, Service and Scandal, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Myerson, the only Jewish Miss America, was one of a select group of American figures to parlay pop culture celebrity into positions of influence in government.

name: Allie Sherman
headline: Allie Sherman Dies at 91; Led Giants to Title Games
abstract: Mr. Sherman, an early master of the T-formation, led the Giants to N.F.L. title games in his first three seasons as coach. He played quarterback for Brooklyn College and the Philadelphia Eagles.

name: Martin Anderson
headline: Martin Anderson, White House Adviser to Reagan, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Anderson, a conservative economist, served three other presidents in addition to Reagan.

name: Sacvan Bercovitch
headline: Sacvan Bercovitch, Scholar Who Traced America’s Self-Image, Dies at 81
abstract: Dr. Bercovitch argued that the Puritans regarded New England not as an extension of European societies but as something new and exceptional.

name: Leo Tindemans
profession: Belgian Prime Minister and Voice for European Unity
headline: Leo Tindemans, 92, Dies; Belgian Prime Minister and Voice for European Unity
abstract: Mr. Tindemans saw European integration and a single currency as a means of overcoming the virulent nationalism of the past.

name: Hank Peters
profession: Built Baseball Winners in Baltimore and Cleveland
headline: Hank Peters, 90, Dies; Built Baseball Winners in Baltimore and Cleveland
abstract: Mr. Peters won a World Series as general manager of the Baltimore Orioles and helped rejuvenate the Cleveland Indians.

name: James Hester
profession: Guided N.Y.U. to Become a Major University
headline: James Hester, 90, Dies; Guided N.Y.U. to Become a Major University
abstract: Dr. Hester steered New York University through campus unrest in the 1960s and helped chart its evolution from a commuter school on the brink of bankruptcy to a highly selective institution with national academic stature.

name: Ruth Popkin
profession: Hadassah Leader Worked to Resettle Refugees
headline: Ruth Popkin Dies at 101; Hadassah Leader Worked to Resettle Refugees
abstract: Ms. Popkin, the former president of Hadassah, the Jewish National Fund and the World Zionist Congress, assisted immigrants and environmental projects in Israel.

name: Philip E. Converse
headline: Prof. Philip E. Converse, Expert on How Voters Decide, Dies at 86
abstract: Professor Converse, in “The American Voter,” concluded with three co-authors in 1960 that most voters were remarkably uninformed and based their preferences largely on party affiliation.

name: Lee Israel
profession: Writer Proudest of Her Literary Forgeries
headline: Lee Israel, a Writer Proudest of Her Literary Forgeries, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Israel composed and sold hundreds of letters that she said had been written by Dorothy Parker, Noël Coward, Lillian Hellman and others.

name: Arch Moore
headline: Arch Moore, Trailblazing West Virginia Governor, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Moore was the only governor of the state to serve three four-year terms, and the first sitting governor to be formally charged with a crime.

name: Jethro Pugh
profession: Unsung Pillar for Cowboys on the Doomsday Defense
headline: Jethro Pugh, Unsung Pillar for Cowboys on the Doomsday Defense, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Pugh played in four Super Bowls and was involved in the key play in the 1967 N.F.C. championship game known as the Ice Bowl.

name: Walter Kühr
headline: Walter Kühr, Performer, Bandleader and Accordion Evangelist, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Kühr was for decades an evangelist of the accordion, as a performer, bandleader and owner of the Main Squeeze, a shop on the Lower East Side that he founded.

name: J. P. Parise
profession: Goal Scorer in Milestone Win by Islanders
headline: J. P. Parise, Goal Scorer in Milestone Win by Islanders, Dies at 73
abstract: Parise, who appeared in All-Star Games in 1970 and 1973, helped the Islanders win their first playoff series, arriving in a trade from the Minnesota North Stars in 1975.

name: Rod Taylor
profession: Star of The Birds and The Time Machine
headline: Rod Taylor, Star of ‘The Birds’ and ‘The Time Machine,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Taylor made more than 50 films, including “The Birds” and “The Time Machine,” and acted alongside Debbie Reynolds, Elizabeth Taylor, Maggie Smith and Jane Fonda.

name: Julio Scherer García
headline: Julio Scherer García, Investigative Journalist in Mexico, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Scherer, the founder of the magazine Proceso, created a school of critical journalism that unmasked political corruption in Mexico and helped lay the groundwork for its democratic transition.

name: Samuel Goldwyn Jr.
headline: Samuel Goldwyn Jr., 88, Dies; Hollywood Scion and Film Influence
abstract: Mr. Goldwyn was an early champion of stylized independent films that most major studios thought would never sell a ticket.

name: He Zhenliang
headline: He Zhenliang Dies at 85; China’s Olympic Crusader
abstract: The sports executive was credited with making the communist nation more accessible to the world after politics interrupted its participation in the Games for nearly 30 years.

name: David H. Marlowe
profession: Helped Army Nurture Bands of Brothers
headline: David H. Marlowe Dies at 83; Helped Army Nurture Bands of Brothers
abstract: His studies among soldiers drove home the importance of group cohesion in combat and led to changes in how the military disciplines, organizes and cares for its troops.

name: Andraé Crouch
headline: Andraé Crouch, 72, Who Infused Gospel With Soul, Dies
abstract: Mr. Crouch won seven Grammys for his mix of faith and pop genres, and was nominated for an Oscar for his work on “The Color Purple” score.

name: Maher Hathout
headline: Maher Hathout, a Powerful Voice for American Muslims, Dies at 79
abstract: Dr. Hathout, who helped found the Islamic Center of Southern California, called on American Muslims to embrace their dual identity, and preached interfaith comity and understanding in the aftermath of the Sept. 11 attacks.

name: Jeff Golub
profession: Guitarist at Home in Several Genres
headline: Jeff Golub, a Guitarist at Home in Several Genres, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Golub worked with Rod Stewart and Billy Squier and had a genre-crossing solo career as well.

name: Carl N. Degler
profession: Scholarly Champion of the Oppressed in America
headline: Carl N. Degler, Scholarly Champion of the Oppressed in America, Dies at 93
abstract: Professor Degler, a Stanford historian, was a Pulitzer Prize-winning author who illuminated the role of women, the poor and minorities in the nation’s evolution.

name: Anita Ekberg
headline: Anita Ekberg, International Screen Beauty, Dies at 83
abstract: The Swedish actress, best known for her role in “La Dolce Vita,” was frequently quoted as saying that it was Federico Fellini, the director, who owed his success to her, and not the other way around.

name: Taylor Negron
headline: Taylor Negron, of ‘Fast Times at Ridgemont High,’ Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Negron brought a funereal, straight-faced sensibility to a career’s worth of character roles in cult comedies like “Fast Times at Ridgemont High” and “One Crazy Summer.”

name: Harry V. Jaffa
headline: Harry V. Jaffa, Conservative Scholar and Goldwater Muse, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Jaffa, a prolific author, helped shape modern politics by suggesting two lines about extremism and moderation at the 1964 Republican National Convention.

name: Francesco Rosi
headline: Francesco Rosi, Italian Filmmaker With Political Bent, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Rosi’s commitment to social issues made him a direct heir to the traditions of Italian neorealist cinema of the postwar years.

name: Joan Peters
headline: Joan Peters, Journalist Who Wrote on Israeli-Palestinian Conflict, Dies at 78
abstract: In a 1984 book, both widely hailed and criticized, she cited historical documents showing that Arab settlers had flocked to Palestine beginning in the late 1800s; they had not, she wrote, inhabited the land “from time immemorial.”

name: Al Bendich
profession: Defender of Howl and Lenny Bruces Comedy
headline: Al Bendich, Defender of ‘Howl’ and Lenny Bruce’s Comedy, Is Dead at 85
abstract: As a young lawyer, Mr. Bendich argued the two landmark obscenity cases, providing the legal rationales for the judge to find in favor of the defense both times.

name: G.G. Michelson
headline: G.G. Michelson, Macy’s Executive Who Broke Glass Ceilings, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Michelson was an executive at R. H. Macy for more than 40 years and served as the only female director on a number of corporate boards.

name: Thomas Graboys
headline: Thomas Graboys, Doctor Who Wrote of Parkinson’s Fight, Dies at 70
abstract: While still at the apex of a stellar medical career, Dr. Graboys was found to have Parkinson’s disease. He detailed the stages of his illness in his autobiography.

name: Walter Berns
headline: Walter Berns, Whose Ideas Fueled Neoconservative Movement, Dies at 95
abstract: Professor Berns’s dissatisfaction with Cornell’s response to a takeover of a campus building by black students in 1969 fueled a group of intellectuals who blamed liberalism for many ills.

name: Jake Berthot
profession: Painter Inspired by the Natural World
headline: Jake Berthot, a Painter Inspired by the Natural World, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Berthot made a name for himself with abstract paintings and later with work that was heavily influenced by nature.

name: Lowell W. Paxson
headline: Lowell W. Paxson Dies at 79; Started Home Shopping Network
abstract: In addition to the network now called HSN, which grew out of a shopping feature on a Florida cable station, Mr. Paxson founded the broadcast network Ion.

name: Jean-Claude Baker
headline: Jean-Claude Baker Dies at 71; Restaurateur Honored a Chanteuse
abstract: Mr. Baker created the Manhattan restaurant Chez Josephine in memory of Josephine Baker, who had befriended him as a child and whose biography he wrote.

name: Milton Hebald
headline: Milton Hebald, Whose Sculptures Are in Plain View, Dies at 97
abstract: Though his name may not be familiar to many, Mr. Hebald’s work is — in Central Park and in other public spaces around the world.

name: Elaine Summers
headline: Elaine Summers, Who Meshed Dance and Film, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Summers was a dancer, choreographer and multimedia artist whose work sought to blur the boundaries between dance and film.

name: Ray Lumpp
profession: Played for Knicks and Ran a Track Meet
headline: Ray Lumpp, Who Played for Knicks and Ran a Track Meet, Dies at 91
abstract: Lumpp had a notable career as a basketball player, and he also was the athletic director of the New York Athletic Club, whose track and field meets faced accusations of discrimination.

name: Ervin Drake
headline: Ervin Drake, Composer of Pop Songs, Dies at 95
abstract: Among Mr. Drake’s many songs are “It Was a Very Good Year,” a hit for Frank Sinatra, and “I Believe,” sung by Frankie Laine.

name: Dorothy Thomas
headline: Dorothy Thomas, the ‘Mother’ of Bone Marrow Transplants, Dies at 92
abstract: She was a partner in the research into bone marrow transplants that won her husband a Nobel Prize.

name: Tadeusz Konwicki
headline: Tadeusz Konwicki, Leading Polish Novelist and Filmmaker, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Konwicki’s novel “A Minor Apocalypse,” about a despairing writer preparing to die, is required reading for Polish high school students.

name: Vernon B. Mountcastle
headline: Vernon B. Mountcastle, Brain Explorer, Dies at 96
abstract: At the dawn of modern neuroscience, Dr. Mountcastle showed how cylinders of neurons, dedicated to specific tasks, work together to process perception.

name: Bob Boyd
headline: Bob Boyd, Who Battled a Basketball Giant, Dies at 84
abstract: As basketball coach at Southern California, Boyd had a 216-131 record, with 11 winning teams in 13 seasons, but he went 2-25 against John Wooden’s U.C.L.A. teams.

name: Elena Obraztsova
headline: Elena Obraztsova, Jewel of the Bolshoi Opera, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Ms. Obraztsova, a mezzo-soprano, survived the siege of Leningrad to become one of the Soviet Union’s greatest opera singers with theatrical triumphs around the world.

name: ASAP Yams
headline: ASAP Yams, Creative Force in Hip-Hop, Dies at 26
abstract: A New York City native, Yams, whose real name was Steven Rodriguez, was an owner of the ASAP Worldwide label and a founder of the ASAP Mob collective.

name: Yoko Nagae Ceschina
profession: Countess and Fairy Godmother to the Arts
headline: Yoko Nagae Ceschina, Countess and Fairy Godmother to the Arts, Dies at 82
abstract: Countess Ceschina was one of the world’s foremost patrons of classical music, if also one of the least publicly known.

name: Jane Wilson
headline: Jane Wilson, Artist of the Ethereal, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Wilson, a founding member of the Hansa Gallery artists’ cooperative, turned away from pure abstraction to pursue the natural and evanescent.

name: Kim Fowley
headline: Kim Fowley, Rock Producer and Svengali, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Fowley made hundreds of records in doo-wop, surf, psychedelia, country, glam, punk and metal, but is best known for managing the all-girl group the Runaways.

name: Peter Wallenberg
headline: Peter Wallenberg, Patriarch of a Swedish Dynasty, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Wallenberg was the unlikely successor to lead his family’s business, expanding it far beyond Sweden’s big companies to become an international force.

name: Faith Seidenberg
profession: Took On McSorleys, an All-Male Haven
headline: Faith Seidenberg, 91, Dies; Took On McSorley’s, an All-Male Haven
abstract: Ms. Seidenberg, a civil rights lawyer, is best known for successfully suing McSorley’s Old Ale House in a case in which a judge found that sex discrimination in public accommodations is unconstitutional.

name: Tony Verna
profession: Started Instant Replay and Remade Sports Television
headline: Tony Verna, Who Started Instant Replay and Remade Sports Television, Dies at 81
abstract: Before the Army-Navy football game of 1963, Mr. Verna, the inventor of instant replay, puzzled out a method to rewind videotape and immediately run it again.

name: Melvin J. Gordon
headline: Melvin J. Gordon, Who Ran Tootsie Roll Industries, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Gordon expanded the product line, buying brands like Charleston Chew and Junior Mints, and running the company with an iron grip.

name: Alan J. Hirschfield
profession: Led Film Studio Through Financial Scandal
headline: Alan J. Hirschfield, Who Led Film Studio Through Financial Scandal, Dies at 79
abstract: At Columbia Pictures, Mr. Hirschfield fought board members in an attempt to fire an executive who had embezzled money, and both were forced out.

name: John Bayley
headline: John Bayley, Oxford Don Who Wrote of His Wife, Iris Murdoch, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Bayley was an Oxford don and literary critic who found an international readership with his memoir “Elegy for Iris,” a moving account of his life with the novelist Iris Murdoch, his wife.

name: Faten Hamama
profession: Actress Hailed as Lady of the Arabic Screen
headline: Faten Hamama, Actress Hailed as ‘Lady of the Arabic Screen,’ Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Hamama appeared in nearly 100 films but was best known to American audiences as the wife of Omar Sharif, whose career she had helped start.

name: Wendell Ford
headline: Wendell Ford, 90, Dies; Kentucky Senator Pushed Voting Rights
abstract: Mr. Ford, who rose to become the Democratic whip in the Senate, was best known for defending the tobacco industry and for pushing voter-registration laws.

name: Abdullah
headline: King Abdullah, a Shrewd Force Who Reshaped Saudi Arabia, Dies at 90
abstract: Abdullah was one of the world’s wealthiest and most powerful men, but a cautious reformer amid great changes in the Middle East.

name: Peggy Charren
headline: Peggy Charren, Children’s TV Crusader, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Charren, whose work ultimately led to the Children’s Television Act, received a Peabody Award for public service and, later, a Presidential Medal of Freedom.

name: Jean Lindenmann
headline: Jean Lindenmann, Who Made Interferon His Life’s Work, Is Dead at 90
abstract: As a postdoctoral student working with Dr. Alick Isaacs in 1957, Dr. Lindenmann discovered interferon, the powerful antiviral substance used to treat some cancers, hepatitis C and multiple sclerosis.

name: Jackie Selebi
profession: South Africa Police Head Convicted in Bribery Case
headline: Jackie Selebi, South Africa Police Head Convicted in Bribery Case, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Selebi, South Africa’s first black national police commissioner, was found guilty of taking bribes from a drug trafficker in a trial that drew immense international attention.

name: Vince Camuto
headline: Vince Camuto Dies at 78; Shoe Mogul Founded Nine West
abstract: Colleagues say Mr. Camuto was tuned in to the ever-changing tastes of his customers.

name: Ralph Morse
headline: Ralph Morse, Life Photographer of Big Events, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Mr. Morse, a Bronx native, was, at 24, the weekly magazine’s youngest war photographer and later covered the Mercury space program.

name: Dallas Taylor
headline: Dallas Taylor, Drummer for Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Taylor, who later became a drug counselor, was ejected from the band because of his drinking and drug use.

name: Ward Swingle
headline: Ward Swingle, Who Made Classical Music Jazzy, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Swingle was a conductor and arranger whose group, the Swingle Singers, combined scat vocals with classical music.

name: Ernie Banks
headline: Ernie Banks, the Eternally Hopeful Mr. Cub, Dies at 83
abstract: Banks, known for his sunny mantra, “Let’s play two,” hit 512 home runs in 19 seasons and won consecutive M.V.P. awards, but he never reached the postseason.

name: Alice K. Turner
headline: Alice K. Turner Dies at 75; Playboy Editor Kept Fiction Alive
abstract: Ms. Turner helped keep literary short fiction on life support in the late 20th century, when few other publishers would or could.

name: Joe Franklin
profession: Talk Show Institution in New York
headline: Joe Franklin, a Talk Show Institution in New York, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Franklin, a pioneer of local talk shows, was on the air in New York from 1951 to 1993 as the host of a compellingly low-rent parade of has-beens and yet-to-bes.

name: Chitresh Das
profession: Influential Performer and Educator of Indian Dance
headline: Chitresh Das, Influential Performer and Educator of Indian Dance, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Das helped popularize kathak, one of the most prominent forms of classical Indian dance and the only one that has roots in both Muslim and Hindu traditions.

name: Toller Cranston
headline: Toller Cranston, ‘the Nureyev’ of Figure Skating, Dies at 65
abstract: A flamboyant Canadian figure skater with a style often likened to dancing, Mr. Cranston played a major role in popularizing his sport.

name: Marcus Borg
headline: Marcus Borg, Liberal Scholar on Historical Jesus, Dies at 72
abstract: Professor Borg was among a group of scholars, known as the Jesus Seminar, who set out to discern which of Jesus’ acts and utterances could be confirmed as historically true, and which were merely myths.

name: Sal Polisi
profession: Master Woodcarver at South Street Seaport Museum
headline: Sal Polisi, Master Woodcarver at South Street Seaport Museum, Dies at 79
abstract: For more than 30 years, Mr. Polisi volunteered his skills turning wood into sculptures and ships’ figureheads, while explaining his craft to visitors.

name: Edgar Froese
headline: Edgar Froese, Adventurous Leader of Tangerine Dream, Dies at 70
abstract: In Tangerine Dream, a band that evolved through many incarnations and spanned decades, Mr. Froese is the musician who stayed the longest.

name: Bill Monbouquette
profession: Pitching Ace When Red Sox Struggled
headline: Bill Monbouquette, 78, Dies; Pitching Ace When Red Sox Struggled
abstract: Mr. Monbouquette was a stalwart right-handed pitcher for the Boston Red Sox during one of the leaner periods in the history of the franchise.

name: Leon Brittan
profession: Quit Thatcher Cabinet in Leak Case
headline: Leon Brittan, 75, Dies; Quit Thatcher Cabinet in Leak Case
abstract: Mr. Brittan was a British politician who rose fast and far in the Margaret Thatcher government, only to see his career crash over a leaked letter in a dispute over a helicopter company.

name: Reies Tijerina
headline: Reies Tijerina, 88, Dies; Led Chicano Property Rights Movement
abstract: Mr. Tijerina led efforts in the 1960s to seize land for Mexicans, Indians and descendants of the original Spanish settlers of what became the American Southwest.

name: Charles H. Townes
profession: Paved Way for the Laser in Daily Life
headline: Charles H. Townes, Who Paved Way for the Laser in Daily Life, Dies at 99
abstract: Dr. Townes shared the Nobel Prize in 1964 for his work on lasers, in a career that included advising on lunar landings, verifying Einstein’s theories and creating an atomic clock.

name: Robert Pirie
profession: Lawyer and Banker in Mergers and Takeovers
headline: Robert Pirie, 80, Lawyer and Banker in Mergers and Takeovers, Dies
abstract: Mr. Pirie was a combative lawyer when the risky but lucrative field of mergers and acquisitions was emerging and later a prominent investment banker on Wall Street.

name: Richard McBrien
headline: Rev. Richard McBrien, Dissenting Catholic Theologian, Dies at 78
abstract: Father McBrien was a champion of Vatican II reforms and often criticized the Roman Catholic Church for its stances on birth control, celibacy and the infallibility of the pope.

name: Don Harron
profession: Actor on Broadway and in Hee Haw
headline: Don Harron, Actor on Broadway and in ‘Hee Haw,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Harron, a busy stage actor in the 1950s and 1960s, became best known for playing Charlie Farquharson, a wisecracking hayseed on “Hee Haw.”

name: Margaret Bloy Graham
headline: Margaret Bloy Graham, ‘Harry the Dirty Dog’ Illustrator, Dies at 94
abstract: Two other works that Ms. Graham illustrated were named Caldecott Honor Books by the American Library Association.

name: Colleen McCullough
headline: Colleen McCullough, Author of ‘The Thorn Birds,’ Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. McCullough’s novel, set against the sweeping panorama of her native Australia, became one of the most-watched mini-series of all time.

name: Lotte Hass
profession: Pioneering Diver Known for Beauty and Bravery
headline: Lotte Hass, Pioneering Diver Known for Beauty and Bravery, Dies at 86
abstract: Often called the first lady of diving, Ms. Hass helped shatter the glass floor that had long kept women from the ocean’s depths.

name: David Landau
profession: Mideast Journalist and Biographer of Sharon
headline: David Landau, Mideast Journalist and Biographer of Sharon, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Landau was affiliated with The Jerusalem Post, Haaretz and The Economist, and wrote a recent biography of former Prime Minister Ariel Sharon.

name: Rod McKuen
profession: Poet and Lyricist With Vast Following
headline: Rod McKuen, Poet and Lyricist With Vast Following, Dies at 81
abstract: The author of dozens of books whose work met with immense commercial success if little critical esteem, Mr. McKuen was once described as “the unofficial poet laureate of America.”

name: Demis Roussos
headline: Demis Roussos Dies at 68; Greek Singer Was Internationally Known
abstract: In addition to his musical career, Mr. Roussos was a passenger on TWA Flight 847, from Athens to Rome, which was hijacked to Beirut in 1985.

name: R. K. Laxman
headline: R. K. Laxman, Cartoonist Who Amused India for Decades, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Laxman’s comic strip, featuring a character he called the Common Man, appeared daily on the front page of The Times of India for more than five decades.

name: Martha A. Derthick
headline: Martha A. Derthick, Analyst Who Untangled Public Policy, Dies at 81
abstract: Dr. Derthick’s work on Social Security, federalism, deregulation and welfare was said to vividly bring life to impenetrable subjects.

name: Jack Leggett
headline: Jack Leggett, Who Cultivated Writers in Iowa, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Leggett was a longtime director of the University of Iowa Writers’ Workshop and a mentor to many well-known authors.

name: Bernice Gordon
headline: Bernice Gordon, Crossword Creator for The Times, Dies at 101
abstract: For more than six decades, Ms. Gordon created crossword puzzles known for their wit and finesse.

name: Yves Chauvin
headline: Yves Chauvin, ‘Green’ Chemist and Nobel Laureate, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Chauvin helped unlock the secret of “green chemistry” to produce less hazardous waste in manufacturing.

name: Charlie Williams
headline: Charlie Williams, a Met Traded for Mays, Dies at 67
abstract: Williams played eight seasons in the majors, but was best known as the trade bait that brought Willie Mays back to New York.

name: Craig Ramini
headline: Craig Ramini, Whose Heart Led to Buffalo Mozzarella, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Ramini, a software consultant, stopped to ask himself what he really wanted to do, then doggedly pursued the answer despite great odds.

name: Edward J. Saylor
profession: Took Fight to Japan With Doolittle Raiders
headline: Edward J. Saylor, 94, Dies; Took Fight to Japan With Doolittle Raiders
abstract: Mr. Saylor was a member of a band of World War II airmen who bombed Japan in early 1942, stunning the enemy at a time when its army and navy were racking up victories across Asia.

name: Stig Bergling
profession: Cold War Spy Known for His Escape
headline: Stig Bergling, a Cold War Spy Known for His Escape, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Bergling, sentenced to life in prison in 1979 for selling military secrets to the Soviet Union, fled from custody during a conjugal visit with his wife.

name: Carl Djerassi
profession: Creator of the Birth Control Pill
headline: Carl Djerassi, 91, a Creator of the Birth Control Pill, Dies
abstract: Dr. Djerassi was one of two chemists working with a student assistant who in 1951 first synthesized a hormone that became the key ingredient of the contraceptive pill.

name: Richard von Weizsäcker
headline: Richard von Weizsäcker, 94, Dies: First President of Reunited Germany
abstract: Mr. Weizsäcker became West Germany’s head of state in 1984 and served through the merger of East Germany into the Federal Republic of Germany before stepping down in 1994.

name: Kel Nagle
profession: Staved Off Palmer to Win 60 British Open
headline: Kel Nagle, Who Staved Off Palmer to Win ’60 British Open, Dies at 94
abstract: Nagle, an Australian, staved off a rally at St. Andrews in Scotland to deny Arnold Palmer’s attempt to capture his third straight major title, and lost to Gary Player in a memorable playoff at the 1965 United States Open.

name: Rose Marie McCoy
headline: Rose Marie McCoy, a Songwriter for Rock, Pop and Jazz Legends, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. McCoy composed or collaborated on some 850 songs, which were recorded by artists including Aretha Franklin, Bette Midler and Nat King Cole.

name: Carroll Petrie
headline: Carroll Petrie, a New York Philanthropist, Dies at 90
abstract: Mrs. Petrie and her husband, Milton, a retailing mogul who died in 1994, gave to a number of causes that included the Museum of Modern Art and NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital.

name: Ann Mara
headline: Ann Mara, Matriarch of the Football Giants, Dies at 85
abstract: Mrs. Mara owned part of the Giants with her family and was regarded as the team’s matriarch.

name: Leon Silverman
profession: Lawyer Led Inquiry of Labor Secretary
headline: Leon Silverman, 93, Dies; Lawyer Led Inquiry of Labor Secretary
abstract: Mr. Silverman was appointed to investigate a Reagan labor secretary accused of ties to organized crime.

name: Sherry Arden
profession: Publisher With a Passion for Best Sellers
headline: Sherry Arden, Publisher With a Passion for Best Sellers, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Arden, whose exuberance as a publisher invigorated the book industry, promoted countless best sellers, including “Mommie Dearest” and “The Peter Principle.”

name: Sandy Socolow
headline: Sandy Socolow, CBS Newsman During Heady Days, Dies at 86
abstract: A longtime executive for CBS, Mr. Socolow contributed to shaping stories that defined history in the 1960s and 1970s.

name: Monty Oum
headline: Monty Oum, Web-Series Animator, Dies at 33
abstract: Mr. Oum was the director of animation for Rooster Teeth Productions, a company best known for repurposing avatars from the Halo video games into angst-ridden slackers in the popular web series “Red vs. Blue.”

name: Aldo Ciccolini
headline: Aldo Ciccolini Dies at 89; Pianist Interpreted Satie
abstract: Mr. Ciccolini said he had no delusions about whose legacy would be longer: Satie’s or his own.

name: Charlie Sifford
profession: Shattered a Barrier of Race in Golf
headline: Charlie Sifford, Who Shattered a Barrier of Race in Golf, Dies at 92
abstract: By the time Mr. Sifford was allowed to compete against the world’s best golfers, he was almost 40. But he won the PGA Tour’s Greater Hartford Open in 1967 and its Los Angeles Open in 1969.

name: Mary Healy
headline: Mary Healy, Actress and Singer, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Healy and Peter Lind Hayes were a husband-and-wife comedy team on TV in the 1950s and ’60s and portrayed their New Rochelle, N.Y., suburban life on radio.

name: Walter Liedtke
profession: Curator at Metropolitan Museum of Art
headline: Walter Liedtke, Curator at Metropolitan Museum of Art, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Liedtke, a curator of European paintings at the Met for 35 years and a Vermeer scholar, was killed in Tuesday’s crash of a Metro-North train.

name: Martin Gilbert
profession: Churchill Biographer With a Populist Bent
headline: Martin Gilbert, Churchill Biographer With a Populist Bent, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Gilbert wrote many books about a range of historical topics, but Winston Churchill was a favorite subject.

name: Ike Schambelan
headline: Ike Schambelan, Director Who Brought Disabled Artists to the Stage, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Schambelan started the company Theater Breaking Through Barriers as a vehicle for vision-impaired actors to perform their craft.

name: Carl J. Rubino
headline: Carl J. Rubino, Lawyer in Quiz-Show Scandal, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Rubino accompanied Charles Van Doren, his legal client, to Washington in 1959, when he admitted before a congressional subcommittee that he was fed answers on the NBC show “Twenty-One.”

name: Don Covay
profession: Performer and Writer of R&B Hits
headline: Don Covay, Performer and Writer of R&B Hits, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Covay wrote soul standards for his own use, but other musicians did even better with them, including Chubby Checker with “Pony Time” and Aretha Franklin with “Chain of Fools.”

name: Lizabeth Scott
headline: Lizabeth Scott, Film Noir Siren, Dies at 92
abstract: In films like “Dead Reckoning” and “Too Late for Tears,” Ms. Scott played unsympathetic yet seductive schemers convincingly.

name: Anita Darian
headline: Anita Darian, a Singer With an Eclectic Range, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Darian appeared not only in operettas and musicals, but also sang on pop hits including “The Lion Sleeps Tonight” and “Love Is Strange.”

name: André Brink
headline: André Brink, South African Literary Lion, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Brink’s work was often cited alongside that of Nadine Gordimer and J.M. Coetzee as an exemplar of South Africa’s ability to transform the experience of harsh racial politics into literature with a global reach.

name: Norm Drucker
headline: Norm Drucker, Referee Who Felled N.B.A. Giants, Dies at 94
abstract: Drucker gave Wilt Chamberlain a technical foul that caused his ejection from a game in 1962, accounting for the only minutes the star center missed that season.

name: Alex Vraciu
profession: Indestructible Ace of World War II
headline: Alex Vraciu, ‘Indestructible’ Ace of World War II, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Vraciu, a Navy pilot, downed 19 Japanese planes in all, including six in eight minutes during the “Great Marianas Turkey Shoot” in the Philippine Sea.

name: Stewart Stern
profession: Screenwriter of Rebel Without a Cause
headline: Stewart Stern, 92, Screenwriter of ‘Rebel Without a Cause,’ Dies
abstract: Mr. Stern was nominated for Oscars for his work on two other films, “Rachel Rachel” and “Teresa,” and won an Emmy for the mini-series “Sybil.”

name: Christine Valmy
headline: Christine Valmy, Builder of U.S. Skin-Care Business, Dies at 88
abstract: Forbidden to practice law in Communist Romania, Ms. Valmy took up dermatology and brought European ideas of skin care to a beauty market largely unaware of exfoliation and clogged pores.

name: John C. Whitehead
headline: John C. Whitehead, Who Led Effort to Rebuild After 9/11, Dies at 92
abstract: A Navy veteran, Mr. Whitehead became a chairman of Goldman Sachs, deputy secretary of state and head of the corporation charged with rebuilding the World Trade Center site.

name: Billy Casper
headline: Billy Casper, Overlooked Titan of Golf, Dies at 83
abstract: A superb putter, Casper also claimed a Masters title and finished with 51 PGA Tour victories, but he was overshadowed in his prime by other stars.

name: Dean Smith
profession: Champion of College Basketball and of Racial Equality
headline: Dean Smith, Champion of College Basketball and of Racial Equality, Dies at 83
abstract: Smith built the Tar Heels into a perennial national power in his 36 years at Chapel Hill and became one of the game’s most respected figures.

name: Ed Sabol
headline: Ed Sabol, Who Elevated Football Founding NFL Films, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Sabol and his son marshaled exquisite photography, rhapsodic music and poetry to elevate pro football to the realm of myth.

name: Robert Herzstein
headline: Robert Herzstein, Historian Who Linked a U.N. Leader to Nazi War Crimes, Dies at 74
abstract: A historian whose prodigious archival research on behalf of the World Jewish Congress helped uncover Kurt Waldheim’s veiled ties to Nazi war crimes.

name: Helen Eustis
headline: Helen Eustis, Mystery Author and Translator, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Eustis also wrote for magazines and newspapers in her early career and later translated books from French.

name: Kenji Ekuan
profession: Gave Soy Sauce Its Graceful Curves
headline: Kenji Ekuan, Who Gave Soy Sauce Its Graceful Curves, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Ekuan’s work included some of the products most closely associated with postwar Japan, including Yamaha motorcycles and bullet trains.

name: Val Fitch
profession: Discovered Universe to Be Out of Balance
headline: Val Fitch, Who Discovered Universe to Be Out of Balance, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Dr. Fitch shared the 1980 Nobel Prize in Physics for work that helped explain why the collision of matter and antimatter has not destroyed everything in the cosmos.

name: Jerry Tarkanian
profession: N.C.A.A. Foe and College Basketball Force
headline: Jerry Tarkanian, 84, N.C.A.A. Foe and College Basketball Force, Dies
abstract: Tarkanian, one of college basketball’s most successful coaches in his 19 seasons at Nevada-Las Vegas, had a long-running feud with the N.C.A.A.

name: Christophe Gbenye
headline: Christophe Gbenye, Radical Nationalist in Congo, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Gbenye, a Belgian-trained civil servant, was briefly one of several pivotal players in the seesawing civil wars waged by superpower proxies after the Belgian colonial regime left in 1960.

name: Rose E. Frisch
headline: Rose E. Frisch, Scientist Who Linked Body Fat to Fertility, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Frisch’s work showed that women without enough body fat would have trouble becoming pregnant but also had a lower risk of breast cancer.

name: Bob Simon
headline: Bob Simon, ‘60 Minutes’ Correspondent, Dies at 73 in Manhattan Car Crash
abstract: Mr. Simon, who covered most major news events over the past five decades, was in a livery cab that sideswiped a car and then veered into a median on 12th Avenue.

name: Deng Liqun
headline: Deng Liqun, Who Battled China’s Liberals, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Deng, a senior propaganda and ideology official in China, was once called as stubborn as a “Hunan mule” by Deng Xiaoping.

name: David Carr
profession: Times Critic and Champion of Media
headline: David Carr, Times Critic and Champion of Media, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Carr, a shrewd and well-informed skeptic, wriggled away from the demon of drug addiction to become an unlikely name-brand media columnist at The New York Times.

name: Harvey Goldschmid
headline: Harvey Goldschmid, Ally of Ordinary Shareholders, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Mr. Goldschmid, a commissioner at the Securities and Exchange Commission from 2002 to 2005, was a strong advocate of corporate responsibility to shareholders.

name: Gary Owens
headline: Gary Owens, Droll Announcer on ‘Laugh-In,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Owens, who was a disc jockey and writer as well, also voiced characters in thousands of cartoon broadcasts.

name: Assia Djebar
headline: Assia Djebar, Novelist Who Wrote About Oppression of Arab Women, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Djebar, frequently mentioned as a contender for the Nobel Prize in Literature, often focused on gender inequality.

name: Koos van de
headline: Koos van den Akker Dies at 75; Designed Bill Cosby’s Vivid Sweaters
abstract: The Dutch-born designer was called the “master of couture collage” for his creations, most notably the sweaters popularized by Bill Cosby on his long-running sitcom.

name: Marvin David Levy
headline: Marvin David Levy, Composer Who Rose, Fell and Rose Again, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Levy’s career went into a spiral after the failure of “Mourning Becomes Electra,” and he was imprisoned for two years for his role in a drug ring.

name: Philip Levine
headline: Philip Levine, a Poet of Grit, Sweat and Labor, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Levine’s work was vibrantly, angrily and often painfully alive with the sound, smell and sinew of heavy manual labor.

name: Michele Ferrero
headline: Michele Ferrero, Tycoon Who Gave the World Nutella, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Ferrero was widely regarded as the richest man in Italy and he presided over a vast international confectionary empire.

name: Louis Jourdan
profession: Suave Star in Europe and Hollywood
headline: Louis Jourdan, Suave Star in Europe and Hollywood, Dies at 93
abstract: In the 1940s and ’50s, Mr. Jourdan embodied Hollywood’s idea of the cultured, worldly European man.

name: Richard Meryman
headline: Richard Meryman, Journalist and Wyeth Biographer, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Meryman conducted the last interview with Marilyn Monroe and collaborated with Joan Rivers on her memoir.

name: Irving Singer
headline: Irving Singer, M.I.T. Professor Who Wrote ‘The Nature of Love,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Singer was a writer and professor of philosophy for 65 years, nearly 55 of them at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.

name: Lesley Gore
headline: Lesley Gore, Teenage Voice of Heartbreak, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. Gore’s hits included “It’s My Party,” “Judy’s Turn to Cry” and “You Don’t Own Me,” which became a feminist anthem.

name: Arnaud de Borchgrave
headline: Arnaud de Borchgrave, Journalist Whose Life Was a Tale Itself, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. de Borchgrave was the son of a Belgian count and a storied foreign correspondent who covered, by his estimate, at least 18 wars.

name: Sam Andrew
profession: Guitarist for Big Brother and the Holding Company
headline: Sam Andrew, Guitarist for Big Brother and the Holding Company, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Andrew, a musician who played a key role in Janis Joplin’s early career, was a founder of the band, part of the San Francisco sound.

name: Lorena Rojas
headline: Lorena Rojas, Actress in Spanish-Language Soap Operas, Dies at 44
abstract: Ms. Rojas, from Mexico, was an international presence on telenovelas like “El Cuerpo del Deseo” and “Rosario.”

name: Anne Moody
profession: Author of Coming of Age in Mississippi
headline: Anne Moody, Author of ‘Coming of Age in Mississippi,’ Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Moody’s memoir powerfully described growing up black in the Jim Crow era and taking part in the civil rights movement as a young woman.

name: John P. Craven
headline: John P. Craven, 90, Pioneer of Spying at Sea, Dies
abstract: Dr. Craven turned submarines into machines that could reach down miles to inspect and retrieve lost enemy matériel, including nuclear arms.

name: Jon Jerde
headline: Jon Jerde, Architect of Merging Visions, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Jerde’s designs seized on the human yen to shop, merging the mall and downtown, commercial and public space, and faux environments and real experiences.

name: Herald Price Fahringer
headline: Herald Price Fahringer, a Defender of Free Speech, Dies at 87
abstract: The court victories of Mr. Fahringer, a lawyer who represented Larry Flynt and Al Goldstein when they were accused of distributing pornography, often reverberated beyond the individual client.

name: Jerome Kersey
profession: Stalwart of Top Trail Blazers Teams
headline: Jerome Kersey, Stalwart of Top Trail Blazers Teams, Dies at 52
abstract: Kersey was a hard-working forward from a small college who overachieved in pro ball, spending 11 of his 17 seasons in the N.B.A. with Portland.

name: Harris Wittels
headline: Harris Wittels, Television Comedy Writer, Is Dead at 30
abstract: Along with writing for “Parks and Recreation” and “The Sarah Silverman Program,” Mr. Wittels was known for popularizing the term “humblebrag.”

name: Raul Rodriguez
profession: Showered Rose Parade With Bouquets on Wheels
headline: Raul Rodriguez, Who Showered Rose Parade With Bouquets on Wheels, Dies at 71
abstract: In addition to designing floats, Mr. Rodriguez also illustrated children’s books, created facades for casinos and made installations for stores and restaurants.

name: Ernest Sternglass
headline: Ernest Sternglass, Physicist and Nuclear Critic, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Sternglass, whose research in radiation physics laid the foundation for important technological advances, became a prominent critic of nuclear weapons and power.

name: Herman Rosenblat
headline: Herman Rosenblat, 85, Dies; Made Up Holocaust Love Story
abstract: Mr. Rosenblat, a survivor of Nazi camps, wrote a tale of a kind girl and an apple that turned out to be false.

name: Clark Terry
headline: Clark Terry, Master of Jazz Trumpet, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Terry, an alumnus of Count Basie and Duke Ellington ensembles and the “Tonight Show” band, was also a fervent jazz educator.

name: Harold Johnson
headline: Harold Johnson, Boxing’s Tough-Luck Champion, Dies at 87
abstract: Once the undisputed light-heavyweight titleholder, Johnson spent much of his career in the shadow of his bitter rival, Archie Moore.

name: John C. Willke
headline: John C. Willke, Doctor Who Led Fight Against Abortion, Dies at 89
abstract: The doctor and his wife, Barbara, wrote a book presenting the claim that a rape victim’s body would resist pregnancy.

name: Ben Woolf
headline: Ben Woolf, Actor in ‘American Horror Story,’ Dies at 34
abstract: Mr. Woolf, who was known for his roles on two seasons of the television show “American Horror Story,” was struck by a car on Thursday, his publicist said.

name: Yutaka Katayama
headline: Yutaka Katayama, Father of the Datsun ‘Z,’ Dies at 105
abstract: In 1960, Mr. Katayama was sent to California — the perfect habitat for the sporty, two-seat Datsun 240Z, which mesmerized drivers and helped him set up a nationwide network of dealers.

name: Bruce Sinofsky
headline: Bruce Sinofsky, Lauded Documentary Filmmaker, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Sinofsky and his collaborator Joe Berlinger examined sensational crimes in “Brother’s Keeper” and the “Paradise Lost” trilogy, about the West Memphis Three, and profiled the heavy metal band Metallica.

name: Donald R. Keough
profession: Led Coca-Cola Through New Coke Debacle
headline: Donald R. Keough, Who Led Coca-Cola Through New Coke Debacle, Dies at 88
abstract: When the company introduced the sweeter New Coke, it did not anticipate the “depth of feeling” for the original taste, Mr. Keough said in announcing a return to the regular formula.

name: Tonya Gonnella Frichner
headline: Tonya Gonnella Frichner, Advocate for Indigenous Peoples, Dies at 67
abstract: Ms. Frichner, a lawyer and professor from upstate New York, became a global voice for Native Americans in forging common ground with the world’s indigenous peoples.

name: Dori J. Maynard
headline: Dori J. Maynard, Who Sought Diversity in Journalism, Dies at 56
abstract: Ms. Maynard led a journalism education institute named for her publisher father, Robert C. Maynard, and explored how race, class and ethnicity appeared in news coverage.

name: Anthony B. Herbert
profession: Decorated War Hero Turned Army Whistleblower
headline: Anthony B. Herbert, Decorated War Hero Turned Army Whistleblower, Dies at 84
abstract: With four Silver Stars, four Bronze Stars and four Purple Hearts, the Army poster boy was relieved of his command in April 1969 after reporting he witnessed war crimes in South Vietnam.

name: Eugenie Clark
headline: Eugenie Clark, Scholar of the Life Aquatic, Dies at 92
abstract: Long before “Jaws,” Dr. Clark rode a 40-foot whale shark, met great whites while scuba diving, studied “sleeping” sharks in undersea caves and witnessed a shark’s birth.

name: Ariel Camacho
profession: Lead Singer of Los Plebes del Rancho
headline: Ariel Camacho, Lead Singer of Los Plebes del Rancho, Dies at 22
abstract: Mr. Camacho, who played guitar and wrote songs as well as singing, was idolized by youngsters in rural Mexico and had begun amassing a fan base on the other side of the border.

name: Irving Kahn
headline: Irving Kahn, Oldest Active Wall Street Investor, Dies at 109
abstract: Mr. Kahn was a contrarian adherent who left Lehman Brothers in 1978 to open Kahn Brothers Group with two of his sons.

name: Theodore Hesburgh
profession: Lifted Notre Dame and Advised Presidents
headline: Rev. Theodore Hesburgh, 97, Dies; Lifted Notre Dame and Advised Presidents
abstract: He stood up to the White House and the Vatican as he transformed Catholic higher education in America and raised a powerful moral voice in national affairs.

name: Don Johnson
headline: Don Johnson, a Yankees Sensation Who Fizzled Out, Dies at 88
abstract: Johnson, a hard-throwing pitcher who showed flashes of greatness in 1947, struggled with injuries and off-the-field troubles, finishing his major league career with only 27 wins.

name: Earl Lloyd
headline: Earl Lloyd, N.B.A.’s First Black Player, Dies at 86
abstract: Lloyd, who made his debut for the Washington Capitols in October 1950, played in the N.B.A. for nine seasons and was inducted into the Basketball Hall of Fame in 2003.

name: Leonard Nimoy
headline: Leonard Nimoy, Spock of ‘Star Trek,’ Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Nimoy won a worshipful global following as Mr. Spock, the resolutely logical human-Vulcan first officer in the television and movie juggernaut “Star Trek.”

name: Robert Benmosche
headline: Robert Benmosche, Rescuer of A.I.G. After Bailout, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Benmosche came out of retirement in 2009 to turn around the company, the worst casualty of the global financial crisis, which the American taxpayers spent $182 billion to bail out.

name: John Fairchild
profession: Made Womens Wear Daily a Must-Read
headline: John Fairchild, Who Made Women’s Wear Daily a Must-Read, Dies at 87
abstract: As publisher and editor, Mr. Fairchild transformed his family’s fusty trade publication into a must-read among fashion elites.

name: Anthony Mason
headline: Anthony Mason, Bruising Knicks Forward in the ‘90s, Dies at 48
abstract: Mason, whose muscular play and fearsome court persona helped the Knicks reach the N.B.A. finals in 1994, was an unlikely success story.

name: Henry T. Segerstrom
headline: Henry T. Segerstrom, California Developer and Arts Patron, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Segerstrom turned his family’s lima bean farm into Orange County’s cultural and commercial downtown.

name: Yasar Kemal
profession: Master Turkish Novelist and Strident Political Critic
headline: Yasar Kemal, Master Turkish Novelist and Strident Political Critic, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Kemal repeatedly clashed with the Turkish state while emerging as his country’s first novelist of global stature.

name: William Thomas McKinley
headline: William Thomas McKinley, Jazz-Loving Composer, Dies at 76
abstract: A hallmark of Mr. McKinley’s music was his acute sensitivity to the tonal possibilities of each instrument.

name: Minnie Minoso
profession: Helped Integrate Baseball With White Sox
headline: Minnie Minoso, Helped Integrate Baseball With White Sox, Dies at 89
abstract: Minoso, the major leagues’ first black player out of Latin America, was often cited as the only modern major leaguer to play in five decades.

name: Orrin Keepnews
profession: Record Executive and Producer of Jazz Classics
headline: Orrin Keepnews, Record Executive and Producer of Jazz Classics, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Keepnews, a four-time Grammy winner, produced classic albums from the likes of Sonny Rollins, Thelonious Monk and Bill Evans, and helped found Riverside Records.

name: Anthony R. Cucci
headline: Anthony R. Cucci, Combative Jersey City Mayor, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Cucci, a Jersey City guy through and through, won a bruising campaign in 1985 but later lost a re-election bid to the same opponent, Gerald McCann.

name: Malcolm Boyd
headline: Rev. Malcolm Boyd, an Author, Activist and Counterculture Rebel, Dies at 91
abstract: Father Boyd was among a handful of white clergymen who became nationally known for civil rights and protesting war, and — after disclosing in 1976 that he was gay — fought for women and homosexuals in the church.

name: Monroe Freedman
headline: Monroe Freedman, Influential Voice on Legal Ethics, Dies at 86
abstract: Professor Freedman, who was credited with inventing legal ethics as a serious academic subject, was especially concerned with lawyers’ responsibilities toward their clients and with access to justice.

name: Ernie Hemmings
profession: Founder of a Bible of Classic Cars
headline: Ernie Hemmings, Founder of a Bible of Classic Cars, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Hemmings turned an auto parts mail-order catalog into the popular magazine Hemmings Motor News.

name: Charlotte Spiegel
profession: Created New Yorks Window Guard Program
headline: Charlotte Spiegel, 92, Dies; Created New York’s Window Guard Program
abstract: Ms. Spiegel, a civic leader and politician, turned a publicity campaign into a formal health code requirement that landlords provide the guards in apartments occupied by children age 10 and under.

name: Jerome Kurtz
profession: Leader of I.R.S. During Carter Era
headline: Jerome Kurtz, Leader of I.R.S. During Carter Era, Dies at 83
abstract: As the I.R.S. commissioner, Mr. Kurtz, considered one of the leading tax policy experts of his time, was known for cracking down on tax shelters.

name: M. Stanton Evans
headline: M. Stanton Evans, Who Helped Shape Conservative Movement, Is Dead at 80
abstract: At 26, Mr. Evans drafted the statement of principles upon which Young Americans for Freedom, the first substantial national conservative organization, was created.

name: Bettina Graziani
headline: Bettina Graziani Dies at 89; Supermodel of Fashion’s ‘New Look’
abstract: Ms. Graziani, who was ubiquitous in the 1940s and ’50s, became an avatar of the postwar style built around full skirts, cinched waists and elegant silhouettes.

name: Natalia Revuelta Clews
profession: Fidel Castro Ally And Mother of His Daughter
headline: Natalia Revuelta Clews, Fidel Castro Ally And Mother of His Daughter, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Revuelta, who was born into Havana society, provided refuge and money to Cuban rebels and fell in love with their leader.

name: Ezra Laderman
headline: Ezra Laderman,Weaver of Eclectic ‘Marilyn’ Opera, Dies at 90
abstract: A prolific composer of symphonic, chamber and vocal music, Mr. Laderman won public notice thanks to his work about Marilyn Monroe for the New York City Opera.

name: Alex Johnson
profession: Deft Batter Won a Key Ruling
headline: Alex Johnson Dies at 72; Deft Batter Won a Key Ruling
abstract: Johnson captured a batting title in 1970 and later won an arbitration decision establishing that major league teams must treat emotional issues the same as physical ailments.

name: Bertrice Small
headline: Bertrice Small, 77, Writer of Risqué Romance Novels, Dies
abstract: Ms. Small, who was educated in a convent, was called “Lust’s Leading Lady” for her many bodice-ripping books.

name: Edward M. Egan
profession: Led New York Archdiocese in Trying Time
headline: Cardinal Edward M. Egan, 82, Dies; Led New York Archdiocese in Trying Time
abstract: Cardinal Egan was a stern defender of Roman Catholic orthodoxy who presided over the New York archdiocese for nine years.

name: Ed Modzelewski
profession: Fullback for Maryland and the Browns
headline: Ed Modzelewski, Fullback for Maryland and the Browns, Dies at 86
abstract: A fullback known as Big Mo, he starred with his brother Dick, the defensive tackle called Little Mo, on an undefeated University of Maryland team, then collided with him in the N.F.L. in the 1950s.

name: Robert G. Dean
headline: Robert G. Dean, Whose Theories on Sand Saved Beaches, Dies at 84
abstract: The techniques he advanced are routine today almost everywhere on developed coastlines; without them, many beach towns would be without beaches.

name: Daniel Von Bargen
profession: Actor in Seinfeld and Malcolm in the Middle
headline: Daniel Von Bargen, Actor in ‘Seinfeld’ and ‘Malcolm in the Middle,’ Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Von Bargen, who had a long career in film and TV, was perhaps best known for his part as a boss of George Costanza on “Seinfeld.”

name: Albert Maysles
headline: Albert Maysles, Pioneering Documentarian, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Maysles and his brother, David, made notable films like “Gimme Shelter” and “Grey Gardens,” and received a National Medal of Arts in July.

name: Brian Carman
headline: Brian Carman, Surf Rocker, Dies at 69
abstract: As a member of the Chantays, Mr. Carman helped write the instrumental hit “Pipeline.”

name: Harve Bennett
profession: Quiz Kid and Star Trek Producer
headline: Harve Bennett, Quiz Kid and ‘Star Trek’ Producer, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Bennett started out as a young radio star then went on to produce four “Star Trek” films and television movies.

name: Dean Hess
headline: Dean Hess, Preacher and Fighter Pilot, Dies at 97
abstract: Colonel Hess unwittingly bombed a German orphanage during World War II and later helped rescue hundreds of Korean orphans. He recorded his exploits in an autobiography that was made into a film.

name: Dirk Shafer
headline: Dirk Shafer, Playgirl Centerfold Who Revealed He Was Gay, Dies at 52
abstract: In a mock documentary called “Man of the Year,” Mr. Shafer explored the ramifications of being a closeted gay man who is a sex symbol for straight women.

name: Lawrence R. Scanlon Jr.
headline: Lawrence R. Scanlon Jr., Union Leader, Dies at 65
abstract: A behind-the-scenes power, Mr. Scanlon was the political director of the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees from 1995 until he retired in 2012.

name: Sam Simon
profession: Guided The Simpsons, Then Shared His Profits
headline: Sam Simon, 59, Dies; Guided ‘The Simpsons,’ Then Shared His Profits
abstract: Mr. Simon left the show after its fourth season in a lucrative arrangement that allowed him to spend much of the rest of his life giving his money away.

name: Lew Soloff
headline: Lew Soloff, Trumpeter for Blood, Sweat and Tears, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Soloff played across many genres, but he reached his broadest audience as a member of one of the first jazz-rock bands.

name: Lisa Bonchek Adams
headline: Lisa Bonchek Adams Dies at 45; Chronicled Fight With Breast Cancer
abstract: Ms. Adams was known for her thousands of blog posts, Facebook updates and Twitter messages detailing her struggle with breast cancer.

name: Claude Sitton
headline: Claude Sitton, 89, Acclaimed Civil Rights Reporter, Dies
abstract: A son of the South, Mr. Sitton delivered unwavering and perceptive coverage of the tumultuous civil rights movement and was hailed as a benchmark of 20th-century journalism.

name: Jonell Nash
headline: Jonell Nash, Who Cut Fat, Not Flavor, Out of Soul Food, Dies at 72
abstract: Ms. Nash wrote two cookbooks about lowering the fat content in traditional African-American cooking and was food editor of the magazine Essence for 25 years.

name: James H. Molyneaux
headline: James H. Molyneaux, Who Led Unionists in Northern Ireland, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Molyneaux, who described himself as the “dull old dog of Ulster politics,” symbolized Protestant resolve to keep Northern Ireland British.

name: Isaac Heller
profession: Co-Founder of Remco and Toymaker to a Generation
headline: Isaac Heller, Co-Founder of Remco and Toymaker to a Generation, Dies at 88
abstract: Remco’s walkie-talkies, rifles and battleships made Mr. Heller’s company one of the country’s leading toy manufacturers in the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Frei Otto
headline: Frei Otto, Architect, Dies at 89; the Soap Bubble Was an Inspiration
abstract: A lack of construction materials after World War II forced Mr. Otto to innovate; he created dazzling tensile structures while minimizing the use of material.

name: Florence Arthaud
headline: Florence Arthaud, Celebrated Solo Sailor, Dies at 57 in Helicopter Crash
abstract: Arthaud, a French sailor, is the only woman to have won the Route du Rhum, a grueling solo trans-Atlantic 3,500-mile race.

name: John D. Arras
headline: John D. Arras, Medical Care Philosopher, Is Dead at 69
abstract: Professor Arras, who taught bioethics at the University of Virginia, urged doctors to consider fairness and morality in their decisions.

name: Richard Glatzer
headline: Richard Glatzer, Co-Director of ‘Still Alice,’ Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Glatzer worked on the 2014 film, for which the actress Julianne Moore won an Academy Award, while he had amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.

name: Terry Pratchett
headline: Terry Pratchett, Novelist, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Pratchett, an accomplished British satirist, was known for his Discworld series. He created wildly imaginative alternative realities in his more than 70 books.

name: Michael Graves
headline: Michael Graves, 80, Dies; Postmodernist Designed Towers and Teakettles
