abstract: Mr. Graves, one of the most prominent and prolific American architects of the latter 20th century, was perhaps best known for his teakettle and pepper mill.

name: Jenna McMahon
headline: Jenna McMahon Dies at 89; Created Popular Sitcoms
abstract: Ms. McMahon wrote for many series, including “Diff’rent Strokes” and “The Mary Tyler Moore Show.”

name: Yoshihiro Tatsumi
headline: Yoshihiro Tatsumi, Formative Manga Artist, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Tatsumi, an innovator in the manga subgenre he called “gekiga,” helped establish the adult comic and graphic novel genres.

name: Dell Williams
headline: Dell Williams, Founder of Sex Boutique, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Williams started Eve’s Garden, widely described as the nation’s first sex shop catering to women, after an embarrassing experience buying a vibrator at a department store.

name: Willie T. Barrow
headline: Rev. Willie T. Barrow, a Fighter for Civil Rights, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Barrow campaigned on behalf of minorities, women, gays and other groups, as well as serving as a mentor to activists, including Barack Obama.

name: Brian Sutton-Smith
headline: Brian Sutton-Smith, Scholar of What’s Fun, Dies at 90
abstract: Professor Sutton-Smith sought to answer fundamental questions: What is play? Why do human beings engage in it? What psychological, cognitive and cultural functions does it serve?

name: Al Rosen
profession: Missed Triple Crown by a Step
headline: Al Rosen, Who Missed Triple Crown by a Step, Dies at 91
abstract: Rosen was a slugging third baseman for the Indians best remembered for his 1953 season, when his .336 batting average left him just shy of the batting triple crown.

name: Irwin Hasen
profession: Comic Book Artist and Dondi Illustrator
headline: Irwin Hasen, Comic Book Artist and ‘Dondi’ Illustrator, Dies at 96
abstract: The cartoonist helped create the popular comic strip about a wide-eyed World War II orphan, which appeared in newspapers for 31 years.

name: Curtis Gans
headline: Curtis Gans, 77, Is Dead; Worked to Defeat President Johnson
abstract: Mr. Gans mobilized thousands of college students to join Senator Eugene J. McCarthy’s challenge against Lyndon B. Johnson, who eventually quit the race.

name: Daevid Allen
profession: Guitarist and Singer in Progressive Rock
headline: Daevid Allen, Guitarist and Singer in Progressive Rock, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Allen, an Australian-born guitarist, singer and poet, was an innovator of the progressive rock genre.

name: William B. Ewald Jr.
headline: William B. Ewald Jr., Eisenhower Aide and Revisionist Author, Dies at 89
abstract: He found the former president to be a meticulous editor and unusually sparing in personal invective — in print — because he rarely carried a grudge for long. One exception was Senator Joseph R. McCarthy.

name: Valentin Rasputin
headline: Valentin Rasputin, Russian Writer Who Led ‘Village Prose’ Movement, Dies at 77
abstract: Conservatives praised Mr. Rasputin as a keeper of the Russian soul, while liberals expressed concern about his nationalist views.

name: Patrick McDarby
headline: Patrick McDarby, Sport Logo Designer, Is Dead at 57
abstract: Mr. McDarby’s designs included images for Major League Soccer, the New York Rangers, the Jacksonville Jaguars and the Villanova Wildcats.

name: Samuel Charters
headline: Samuel Charters, Foundational Scholar of the Blues, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Charters’s field research and books, including “The Country Blues” and “The Roots of the Blues,” established a field of musical history to study and celebrate.

name: Arthur A. Hartman
headline: Arthur A. Hartman, U.S. Ambassador to Soviet Union, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Hartman, who was appointed envoy to the Soviet Union by Ronald Reagan, filled a dozen or so economic and diplomatic Foreign Service posts over four decades.

name: Allen Jerkens
headline: Allen Jerkens, ‘Giant Killer’ of Horse Racing, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Jerkens, a Hall of Fame thoroughbred trainer who was renowned for pulling upsets, trained colts that beat Secretariat twice in 1973 after his Triple Crown victory.

name: Buddy Elias
profession: Cousin of Anne Frank and Guardian of Her Legacy
headline: Buddy Elias, Cousin of Anne Frank and Guardian of Her Legacy, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Elias was the closest living relative of Anne Frank, and his house yielded a cache of long-forgotten letters from Anne and her family that formed the basis of a recent book.

name: Charles N. Shaffer Jr.
headline: Charles N. Shaffer Jr., Lawyer Who Bolstered Case Against Nixon, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Shaffer’s detailed defense of John W. Dean III, the White House counsel, helped cost Richard M. Nixon the presidency during the Watergate scandal.

name: Malcolm Fraser
profession: Leader Given Power During Crisis in Australia
headline: Malcolm Fraser, a Leader Given Power During Crisis in Australia, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Fraser became prime minister of Australia during a constitutional crisis but later won three elections and led his country for eight years.

name: Robert Kastenmeier
profession: Liberal Voice in House for 32 Years
headline: Robert Kastenmeier, Liberal Voice in House for 32 Years, Dies at 91
abstract: A Wisconsin Democrat was an early opponent of the Vietnam War and in 1976 earned the gratitude of authors when he managed the first general revision of copyright law since 1909.

name: Walter Channing Jr.
headline: Walter Channing Jr., Vintner and Sculptor, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Channing combined careers as a venture capitalist, a sculptor in wood and a maker of well-regarded wines on the South Fork of Long Island, N.Y.

name: Izola Ware Curry
headline: Izola Ware Curry, Who Stabbed King in 1958, Dies at 98
abstract: In 1958, she stabbed the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. at a Harlem book signing — an episode that a decade later would become a rhetorical touchstone in the last oration of his life.

name: Chuck Bednarik
headline: Chuck Bednarik, Eagles’ Man of Concrete, Dies at 89
abstract: Bednarik, the Philadelphia Eagles’ Hall of Fame center and linebacker, was one of the last N.F.L. players to commonly play on both offense and defense.

name: Lee Kuan Yew
profession: Founding Father and First Premier of Singapore
headline: Lee Kuan Yew, Founding Father and First Premier of Singapore, Dies at 91
abstract: As prime minister for 31 years, Mr. Lee transformed the tiny island outpost into a modern, affluent city-state admired for its efficiency and low level of corruption.

name: Howard H. Guttenplan
profession: Nurtured Art Films in New York
headline: Howard H. Guttenplan, Who Nurtured Art Films in New York, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Guttenplan, who was also a photographer and graphic artist, transformed an antipoverty program into a leading workshop and showcase for experimental filmmakers.

name: Jerry Warren
profession: Editor and Press Aide to Nixon and Ford
headline: Jerry Warren, Editor and Press Aide to Nixon and Ford, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Warren, who served as deputy White House press secretary, returned to newspaper work after being disillusioned by the Watergate scandal and its aftermath.

name: Sashimani Devi
profession: Last of Indias Jagannath Temple Dancers
headline: Sashimani Devi, Last of India’s Jagannath Temple Dancers, Dies at 92
abstract: Initiated into service at the temple when she was a small girl, she was the last dancer in a centuries-old tradition that was condemned as exploitative by social reformers.

name: A. James Clark
headline: A. James Clark, ‘King of Concrete’ Who Built Arenas, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Clark’s contracting company transformed the District of Columbia and built sports stadiums and convention centers across the country.

name: Danny Schechter
profession: News Dissector and Human Rights Activist
headline: Danny Schechter, ‘News Dissector’ and Human Rights Activist, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Schechter was an author, filmmaker and award-winning television producer who infused almost all his work with his deep-rooted advocacy, whether it was for alternative or mainstream media.

name: Eva Burrows
headline: Eva Burrows, Salvation Army’s ‘People’s General,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Named for the first woman to run the organization, General Burrows became the second and led the Salvation Army into Eastern Europe after the Communist era.

name: Lyle Gramley
profession: Inflation Tamer in White House and at the Fed
headline: Lyle Gramley, 88, Inflation Tamer in White House and at the Fed, Dies
abstract: Mr. Gramley served as an economic adviser to President Carter from 1977 to 1980 and as a Federal Reserve governor from 1980 to 1985.

name: Gregory Walcott
profession: Actor in Plan 9 From Outer Space
headline: Gregory Walcott, Actor in ‘Plan 9 From Outer Space,’ Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Walcott had a career’s worth of screen and television credits in roles much different from the sci-fi B-movie that he couldn’t shed.

name: Steven Smith
headline: Steven Smith, a ‘Marco Polo’ of American Tea, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Smith, who helped found the Stash and Tazo tea companies, brought back novel varieties from his global travels and developed a wide following.

name: William King
profession: His Pointed Wit Was a Tool
headline: William King, Sculptor, Dies at 90; His Pointed Wit Was a Tool
abstract: Mr. King’s work is in the collections of the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Museum of Modern Art in New York and the Smithsonian American Art Museum in Washington.

name: Francis C. Rooney Jr.
profession: Turned Melville Into a Retail Giant
headline: Francis C. Rooney Jr. Dies at 93; Turned Melville Into a Retail Giant
abstract: As chief executive of the Melville Corporation, Mr. Rooney transformed it from a shoe company into a retail behemoth embracing CVS, Thom McAn and Marshall’s.

name: Lyle E. Schaller
profession: Helped Protestant Churches Survive and Grow
headline: Rev. Lyle E. Schaller Dies at 91; Helped Protestant Churches Survive and Grow
abstract: Mr. Schaller had published 55 books since 1964, edited 41 more and visited about 6,000 churches, offering advice on how to grow congregations.

name: Tomas Transtromer
headline: Tomas Transtromer, Swedish Poet Who Won Nobel, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Transtromer was known for his spare yet evocative imagery and his explorations of identity.

name: George Spitz
headline: George Spitz, Civic Gadfly Who Helped Transform Marathon, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Spitz, who was a perennial, if not quixotic, candidate for public office, is credited with recasting the New York City Marathon from a Central Park race into a citywide event.

name: John Renbourn
headline: John Renbourn, Eclectic Guitarist Who Founded the Pentangle, Dies at 70
abstract: As part of the folk-jazz group the Pentangle, Mr. Renbourn played Carnegie Hall and opened for the Grateful Dead; he was also a scholar of medieval music.

name: Rod Hundley
profession: Outsize Personality on and Off the Court
headline: Rod Hundley, an Outsize Personality on and Off the Court, Dies at 80
abstract: Hundley, known as Hot Rod, parlayed showmanship on the court with flair at the microphone to become a fan favorite for more than half a century, including many years as a broadcaster for the N.B.A.’s Jazz.

name: Gene Saks
profession: Tony-Winning Director of Neil Simon Hits
headline: Gene Saks, Tony-Winning Director of Neil Simon Hits, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Saks, who switched from acting to directing in midcareer, won three Tony Awards and became the leading interpreter of the plays of Neil Simon.

name: Roger L. Mayer
headline: Roger L. Mayer, Pioneer of Film Preservation, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Mayer was honored for rescuing movies that were in danger of disintegration, but criticized for supporting colorizing classics.

name: Miriam Bienstock
headline: Miriam Bienstock, Co-Founder of Atlantic Records, Dies at 92
abstract: Miriam Bienstock ran the business side in the early years of a record company that would later become a giant in the industry, with artists like Aretha Franklin and Ray Charles.

name: Robert Hite
profession: Survivor of Doolittle Raid and Japanese Imprisonment
headline: Robert Hite, 95, Survivor of Doolittle Raid and Japanese Imprisonment, Dies
abstract: Lt. Col. Hite was the last survivor among eight crewmen who were captured by the Japanese when American bombers brought World War II home to Japan in 1942.

name: Gary Dahl
headline: Gary Dahl, Inventor of the Pet Rock, Dies at 78
abstract: The 1975 fad made Mr. Dahl, a down-at-the-heels advertising copywriter when he hit on the idea, a millionaire practically overnight, but he came to regret the brainstorm that gave rise to it in the first place.

name: Carlos Falchi
profession: Turned Exotic Animal Skins Into Coveted Handbags
headline: Carlos Falchi, 70, Dies; Turned Exotic Animal Skins Into Coveted Handbags
abstract: A self-taught artisan from Brazil built a fashion empire from hand-sewn leather clothing and handbags made from the skins of exotic animals, including anacondas, caimans and ostriches.

name: Janet Norwood
headline: Janet Norwood Dies at 91; Led Labor Statistics Bureau
abstract: Dr. Norwood was appointed commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics by Jimmy Carter and held the position, where she oversaw the measurement of economic data, until 1991.

name: John D. States
profession: Doctor Helped Create New Yorks Seatbelt Law
headline: John D. States Dies at 89; Doctor Helped Create New York’s Seatbelt Law
abstract: Dr. States’s research and advocacy persuaded New York in 1984 to enact the nation’s first state law requiring automobile drivers and front-seat passengers to use seatbelts.

name: Klaus Tschira
headline: Klaus Tschira, Business Software Trailblazer, Dies at 74
abstract: He and three colleagues formed a company that developed an off-the-shelf software package to integrate all of a company’s business operations.

name: Cynthia Lennon
headline: Cynthia Lennon, the First Beatles Wife, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Lennon, who was the mother of John Lennon’s son Julian, wrote two memoirs about her former husband.

name: Tom Koch
headline: Tom Koch, 89, Dies; Comedy Writer Invented a 43-Man Game
abstract: Mr. Koch, a creator of the vexingly convoluted game 43-Man Squamish for Mad magazine, was the unheralded author of thousands of comedy scripts for Bob and Ray’s radio shows.

name: Robert Schuller
headline: Rev. Robert Schuller, 88, Dies; Built an Empire Preaching Self-Belief
abstract: Dr. Schuller was an apostle of positive thinking and a symbol of success for decades, before his Crystal Cathedral Ministries ran into financial troubles amid a changing religious broadcast industry.

name: Manoel de Oliveira
headline: Manoel de Oliveira, Pensive Filmmaker Who Made Up for Lost Time, Dies at 106
abstract: The Portuguese director was known for his ruminations on grand subjects and his extraordinary productivity in his old age.

name: Eddie LeBaron
headline: Eddie LeBaron, a Star in the N.F.L. at 5-Foot-7, Dies at 85
abstract: LeBaron, a scrambling quarterback, was 11-0 as a senior at Pacific before playing 11 seasons in the N.F.L., for Washington and Dallas.

name: John Paul Hammerschmidt
headline: John Paul Hammerschmidt, 92, Dies; Congressman Defeated Clinton
abstract: Mr. Hammerschmidt won his first race for Congress in 1966, making him the first Republican in Arkansas to win a federal election in the 20th century.

name: Miroslav Ondricek
headline: Miroslav Ondricek, Cinematographer for ‘Amadeus’ and ‘Ragtime,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Ondricek worked frequently with his countryman Milos Forman and was twice nominated for an Academy Award.

name: Rudolph Perz
headline: Rudolph Perz, Creator of Pillsbury’s Doughboy, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Perz was the creative director of the Leo Burnett advertising agency when he designed Poppin’ Fresh, the cute and pudgy marketing mascot, in 1965.

name: Sarah Brady
headline: Sarah Brady, Gun Control Activist, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Mrs. Brady campaigned side by side with her husband against the gun lobby, often pushing him in his wheelchair, but she was propelled into action when her 5-year-old son found a loaded .22 pistol and pointed it at her.

name: Andrew Porter
headline: Andrew Porter, New Yorker Classical Music Critic, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Porter, who also pieced together a restored version of ““Don Carlos,” directed operas as well, and translated librettos from the many languages he knew.

name: Elmer Lach
headline: Elmer Lach, a Small but Tough Canadien, Dies at 97
abstract: Lach was a member of the team’s fabled Punch Line, named for its scoring power, though he was an unapologetically aggressive player.

name: Robert Burns Jr.
headline: Robert Burns Jr., First Lynyrd Skynyrd Drummer, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Burns helped form Lynyrd Skynyrd, the Southern rock band, in 1964 as a drummer in high school but left 10 years later, overwhelmed by life on the road.

name: Evelyn Starks Hardy
headline: Evelyn Starks Hardy, Founder of the Gospel Harmonettes, Dies at 92
abstract: The Harmonettes, one of the first African-American female gospel groups to sign with a major label, made its voice heard in the civil rights movement.

name: Phyllis R. Klotman
headline: Phyllis R. Klotman, Archivist of African-American Cinema, Dies at 90
abstract: Professor Klotman, an emeritus professor in the department of African American and African Diaspora Studies at Indiana University in Bloomington, established the Black Film Center/Archive.

name: Victor Gotbaum
profession: Labor Leader Helped Rescue New York City in 1970s
headline: Victor Gotbaum, 93, Dies; Labor Leader Helped Rescue New York City in 1970s
abstract: In 1975, New York was on the brink of default, and Mr. Gotbaum, as the main negotiator for the city’s unions, helped City Hall and creditors reach a compromise.

name: Gardner C. Taylor
headline: Rev. Gardner C. Taylor, Powerful Voice for Civil Rights, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Taylor, the former senior pastor of the Concord Baptist Church of Christ in Brooklyn, had an impact as a political force that reached far beyond his 10,000-member congregation.

name: Julie Wilson
headline: Julie Wilson, Sultry Cabaret Legend and Actress, Dies at 90
abstract: The singer, who made a comeback in New York clubs after retiring from musical acting to raise her sons, was 90.

name: Fredric Brandt
headline: Dr. Fredric Brandt, 65, Celebrity ‘Baron of Botox,’ Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Brandt, a dermatologist, provided age-defying treatments for clients including supermodels, industrial titans and Madonna.

name: Ralph Sharon
headline: Ralph Sharon, Jazz Pianist Who Accompanied Tony Bennett, Dies at 91
abstract: Just before a 1961 concert tour, Mr. Sharon offered Mr. Bennett a piece of sheet music that he had forgotten about: “I Left My Heart in San Francisco.”

name: Peter Diamandopoulos
headline: Peter Diamandopoulos, Divisive Adelphi University President, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Diamandopoulos’s 12-year tenure at the Long Island institution culminated in his unceremonious ouster over lavish spending and conflicts of interest involving university trustees.

name: James Best
profession: Bumbling Sheriff of The Dukes of Hazzard
headline: James Best, Bumbling Sheriff of ‘The Dukes of Hazzard,’ Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Best’s Southern twang and rugged good looks made him a natural on westerns like “Gunsmoke” and rural series like “The Andy Griffith Show.”

name: Stan Freberg
headline: Stan Freberg, Madcap Adman and Satirist, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Freberg, who was called the father of the funny commercial, was a fount of irreverence and a purveyor of advertising sales pitches that employed extreme reverse psychology.

name: Paul Jeffrey
headline: Paul Jeffrey, Saxophonist Who Played With Monk and Mingus, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Jeffrey was a prominent jazz educator, teaching at Hartt College and Rutgers before spending 20 years as the director of jazz studies at Duke.

name: John E. Walsh
headline: John E. Walsh, Who Distilled the Bible, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Walsh was not trained as a scholar, but he became a prodigious researcher and prolific author.

name: John W. Walsh
profession: Fought for Cure for Lung Disease
headline: John W. Walsh, Who Fought for Cure for Lung Disease, Dies at 68
abstract: He was the co-founder of three groups whose mission was to heighten public awareness of the illness, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and develop a cure.

name: Anne-Claude Leflaive
headline: Anne-Claude Leflaive, Vintner in Burgundy, Dies at 59
abstract: Under Ms. Leflaive’s leadership, the reputation of her wine estate, Domaine Leflaive, soared, as Burgundy evolved from a connoisseur’s passion to a worldwide luxury good.

name: David Laventhol
headline: David Laventhol, Publisher on Both Coasts, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Laventhol, a former publisher of The Los Angeles Times and Newsday, tried to break into the New York newspaper market by starting New York Newsday in 1985.

name: Malli Mastan Babu
headline: Malli Mastan Babu, Who Scaled the World’s Tallest Mountains, Dies at 40
abstract: Mr. Babu, who was known as one of the world’s fastest summiteers, had been missing in the Andes since late March.

name: Richard Dysart
headline: Richard Dysart, 86, of ‘L.A. Law,’ Dies; Familiar as Authority Figure
abstract: Mr. Dysart specialized in playing doctors, presidents and lawyers, notably as head of the firm in ‘L.A. Law.’

name: Bernice Tannenbaum
headline: Bernice Tannenbaum, Who Fought U.N. Resolution on Zionism, Dies at 101
abstract: Ms. Tannenbaum, a former president of Hadassah, persuaded President Ronald Reagan and the United States Senate to condemn a United Nations resolution equating Zionism with racism.

name: Kayahan
headline: Kayahan, Turkish Singer-Songwriter, Dies at 66
abstract: Kayahan, best known for his love songs and his duets with Nilufer, another Turkish musician, represented Turkey at Eurovision in 1990.

name: Geoffrey Lewis
headline: Geoffrey Lewis, Actor in Clint Eastwood Films, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Lewis, who was the father of the actress Juliette Lewis, appeared in several films with Mr. Eastwood, including “High Plains Drifter.”

name: Richie Benaud
headline: Richie Benaud, Commentator Whose Native Tongue Was Cricket, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Benaud, a former captain of Australia, was a uniquely authoritative television voice, explaining the action with dry wit, perception and economy.

name: Judith Malina
headline: Judith Malina, Founder of the Living Theater, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Malina, with her husband, Julian Beck, created a troupe that advanced the idea of political theater in America.

name: Ivan Doig
headline: Ivan Doig, Author Who Lived the Western Life, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Doig traveled the West with his ranch hand father as a young boy and referred to himself as a product of the “lariat proletariat.”

name: Stanley I. Kutler
headline: Stanley I. Kutler, Historian Who Got Nixon Tapes Released, Dies at 80
abstract: Professor Kutler’s 1992 lawsuit against the National Archives for access to White House recordings led to the release of more than 500 additional hours.

name: Eugene Louis Faccuito
headline: Eugene Louis Faccuito, Creator of Jazz Dance Style, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Faccuito was a dancer and choreographer whose physical reawakening after a paralyzing accident became the wellspring of an internationally renowned jazz dance technique.

name: Barbara Bergmann
profession: Trailblazer for Study of Gender in Economics
headline: Barbara Bergmann, Trailblazer for Study of Gender in Economics, Is Dead at 87
abstract: The author and professor of economics wrote presciently about women in the workplace and served on the White House Council of Economic Advisers.

name: Milton Delugg
headline: Milton Delugg, 96, Dies; Accordionist, Composer, ‘Tonight Show’ Bandleader
abstract: Mr. Delugg accompanied Al Jolson, worked with the game show producer Chuck Barris and was a longtime musical director for the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade.

name: Richard L. Bare
headline: Richard L. Bare, Prolific TV Director for Decades, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Bare, who became a Hollywood mainstay in the early days of television, directed the hit sitcom “Green Acres” and several episodes of “The Twilight Zone” and was credited with discovering James Garner.

name: Günter Grass
profession: Writer Pried Open Germanys Past but Hid His Own
headline: Günter Grass Dies at 87; Writer Pried Open Germany’s Past but Hid His Own
abstract: Mr. Grass was the novelist, social critic and Nobel Prize winner whom many called his country’s moral conscience but who stunned Europe when he revealed in 2006 that he had been in the Waffen-SS.

name: Jin Youzhi
headline: Jin Youzhi, Sibling of China’s Last Emperor, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Jin, the half brother of Henry Pu Yi, the last of the Manchu dynasty to rule China, lived a simple life as a primary school educator.

name: Sheila Kitzinger
headline: Sheila Kitzinger, Childbirth Revolutionary, Dies at 86
abstract: Mrs. Kitzinger was a British anthropologist who encouraged women around the world to reclaim from doctors their natural prerogative over pregnancy and childbirth.

name: Eduardo Galeano
headline: Eduardo Galeano, Uruguayan Voice of Anti-Capitalism, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Mr. Galeano was a Uruguayan writer who blended literature, journalism and political satire in reflecting on the vagaries, injustices and small victories of history.

name: Percy Sledge
profession: Smooth Wailer in When a Man Loves a Woman
headline: Percy Sledge, Smooth Wailer in ‘When a Man Loves a Woman,’ Is Dead at 74
abstract: Sometimes called the King of Slow Soul, Mr. Sledge was one of the South’s first soul stars.

name: Bill Arhos
headline: Bill Arhos, Founder of ‘Austin City Limits,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Arhos convinced public broadcasting stations in 1975 that the nation was ready for a TV show devoted to the non-Nashville variety of country.

name: Paul Almond
headline: Paul Almond, Who Directed First ‘Seven Up!,’ Dies at 83
abstract: The Canadian director oversaw the beginning of what became a series tracking British children into adulthood.

name: Joel Spira
headline: Joel Spira, Physicist Who Softened the Lights in Homes Everywhere, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Spira invented the first lighting dimmer suitable for home use, and founded Lutron Electronics with his wife in 1961.

name: Homaro Cantu
headline: Homaro Cantu, Science-Minded Chicago Chef, Dies at 38
abstract: Mr. Cantu used chemical-laboratory techniques in his cooking, and his restaurant Moto held a Michelin star.

name: Barbara Strauch
profession: Science and Health Editor at The Times and Author
headline: Barbara Strauch, 63, Science and Health Editor at The Times and Author, Dies
abstract: Ms. Strauch, who wrote two books about the brain, worked for Newsday before The Times hired her in 1995. She became science editor in 2011.

name: Raul H. Castro
headline: Raul H. Castro, Arizona’s Only Hispanic Governor, Dies at 98
abstract: Arizona’s first and only Hispanic governor, Mr. Castro was also an American ambassador to three Latin American countries.

name: Art Powell
headline: Art Powell, Star Receiver Who Protested Segregation, Dies at 78
abstract: The star receiver for the New York Titans and the Oakland Raiders in the 1960s was a persistent voice protesting the segregation encountered by the pro football players of his time.

name: Levi Watkins
profession: Pioneering Heart Surgeon Pushed Civil Rights
headline: Levi Watkins, 70, Dies; Pioneering Heart Surgeon Pushed Civil Rights
abstract: Dr. Watkins was the first surgeon to successfully implant an automatic heart defibrillator in a human.

name: Ira Lewis
headline: Ira Lewis, Actor and Playwright, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Lewis turned out scripts that attracted the likes of Al Pacino and Jerry Orbach.

name: Thelma Coyne Long
headline: Thelma Coyne Long, Australian Tennis Champion, Dies at 96
abstract: Long won most of her titles in her native country, and received awards for her service to Australia during World War II.

name: Dan Farrell
headline: Dan Farrell, Photographer Who Captured Kennedy Funeral Salute, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Farrell photographed the Beatles’ first American visit and Bing Crosby on the subway while working at The Daily News in New York, but his most memorable image was of the slain president’s son.

name: Robert P. Griffin
profession: Michigan Senator Urged Nixon to Quit
headline: Robert P. Griffin Dies at 91; Michigan Senator Urged Nixon to Quit
abstract: Mr. Griffin, a former Republican senator and congressman from Michigan, championed a law to fight corruption in labor unions.

name: Francis E. George
profession: Urged Zero Tolerance in Abuse Scandal
headline: Cardinal Francis E. George, 78, Dies; Urged ‘Zero Tolerance’ in Abuse Scandal
abstract: Cardinal George, who was the Roman Catholic archbishop of Chicago for 17 years, helped shape the American Catholic bishops’ response to the child sexual abuse scandal.

name: Stanislav Gross
headline: Stanislav Gross, Czech Leader Who Erred on Iraq Link to 9/11, Dies at 45
abstract: A claim by Mr. Gross was the basis of the so-called Prague connection, an unsubstantiated allegation that linked the Sept. 11 attackers to Saddam Hussein’s regime, bolstering the case for invading Iraq.

name: Vivian Nicholson
headline: Vivian Nicholson, 79, Dies; A Rags-to-Riches Story Left in Tatters
abstract: Mrs. Nicholson was just 25 when she won a sports bet that paid more than £150,000, the equivalent today of about $4.5 million, and her life inspired a musical and a BBC television film.

name: Irwin Schatz
profession: Rare Critic of Tuskegee Syphilis Study
headline: Irwin Schatz, 83, Rare Critic of Tuskegee Syphilis Study, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Schatz was a young cardiologist in 1965 when, objecting to experiments on uneducated black men, he wrote the U.S. Public Health Service a letter whose moral force came to light seven years later.

name: A. Alfred Taubman
profession: Developer, Sothebys Owner and Focus of Scandal
headline: A. Alfred Taubman, 91, Dies; Developer, Sotheby’s Owner and Focus of Scandal
abstract: The retail tycoon, who turned Sotheby’s into a global power for art sales, went to prison in a price-fixing scandal involving Christie’s that, prosecutors said, cheated buyers and sellers out of $100 million.

name: Jonathan Crombie
profession: Romantic Lead in Anne of Green Gables
headline: Jonathan Crombie, Romantic Lead in ‘Anne of Green Gables,’ Dies at 48
abstract: At 17, Mr. Crombie was chosen for the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation’s adaptation of the book after a casting director saw him perform in a school play.

name: T.H. Tsien
profession: Scholar of Chinese Books Rescued 30,000 of Them
headline: T.H. Tsien, 105, Dies; Scholar of Chinese Books Rescued 30,000 of Them
abstract: Professor Tsien risked his life in 1941 to smuggle tens of thousands of rare volumes to safety at the Library of Congress amid the Japanese occupation of Shanghai.

name: Joseph Phelps
headline: Joseph Phelps Dies at 87; Brought Innovation to California Wines
abstract: Mr. Phelps brought a restless, entrepreneurial spirit to wine country that was evolving from a sleepy agricultural community into a modern engine of fine-wine production

name: Elio Toaff
headline: Elio Toaff, Spiritual Leader of Italian Jews, Dies at 99
abstract: Rabbi Toaff, the chief rabbi of Rome for half a century, helped forge more amicable relations between Jews and the Vatican after World War II.

name: Bob St. Clair
profession: Towering 49ers Tackle in the Hall of Fame
headline: Bob St. Clair, Towering 49ers Tackle in the Hall of Fame, Dies at 84
abstract: He was strong, he was fast and he blocked for the million-dollar backfield: Hugh McElhenny, John Henry Johnson, Joe Perry and Y. A. Tittle.

name: Frederic Morton
headline: Frederic Morton, Author Who Chronicled the Rothschilds, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Morton, who as a child fled Austria and the Nazis with his family, often wrote about his homeland, in both fiction and nonfiction books.

name: James Venture
profession: Resistance Fighter Survived Nazi Death Train
headline: James Venture, 93, Dies; Resistance Fighter Survived Nazi Death Train
abstract: Mr. Venture worked to ensure that the riders on the train to concentration camps in Germany in 1944, were not forgotten.

name: M.H. Abrams
profession: Shaped Romantic Criticism and Literary Bible
headline: M.H. Abrams, 102, Dies; Shaped Romantic Criticism and Literary ‘Bible’
abstract: Professor Abrams edited the first seven editions of “The Norton Anthology of English Literature” and was a leading figure in the study of Romanticism.

name: Betty Willis
headline: Betty Willis, Whose ‘Fabulous’ Sign Defined Las Vegas, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Willis’s 25-foot-high neon sign blazingly and irrevocably linked Las Vegas with fabulousness.

name: Bernard Stollman
headline: Bernard Stollman, Founder of Adventurous Record Label, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Stollman, a lawyer, created the independent record label ESP-Disk and chronicled the free jazz of the 1960s.

name: Lois Lilienstein
headline: Lois Lilienstein, of the Children’s Trio Sharon, Lois & Bram, Dies at 78
abstract: Her sunny personality and tuneful, bell-clear voice were central to the live and televised performances of the Canadian singing group.

name: Robert Patterson Jr.
headline: Robert Patterson Jr., Lawyer and Judge Who Fought for the Accused, Dies at 91
abstract: Judge Patterson helped to protect the rights of Attica inmates after the prison riot in 1971 and later served on the Federal District Court in Manhattan.

name: Mary Keefe
profession: Model for Rockwells Rosie the Riveter
headline: Mary Keefe, Model for Rockwell’s ‘Rosie the Riveter,’ Dies at 92
abstract: Mrs. Keefe never wielded a rivet gun before the 1990s, but her image encouraged women to pinch-hit in military plants in World War II.

name: Richard Corliss
headline: Richard Corliss, 71, Longtime Film Critic for Time, Dies
abstract: Mr. Corliss was known for his firm opinions and punchy prose, melding the forthright Time style and its compact format to a joy in deadline invention.

name: William Price Fox
headline: William Price Fox, Admired Southern Novelist and Humorist, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Fox, known for his well-honed countrified voice, wrote about things dear to South Carolina and won over Yankee critics.

name: Ellen Turner
profession: Opened Kitchen to Feed the Needy of Knoxville
headline: Ellen Turner Dies at 87; Opened Kitchen to Feed the Needy of Knoxville
abstract: Ms. Turner and her twin sister founded the Love Kitchen in 1986 in a church basement in Knoxville, Tenn., and it continues to provide clothing and meals.

name: Gilbert Haroche
profession: Builder of an Economy Travel Empire
headline: Gilbert Haroche, Builder of an Economy Travel Empire, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Haroche was a founder of Liberty Travel, which grew from a two-man operation to the largest leisure travel operation in the United States.

name: Harvey R. Miller
headline: Harvey R. Miller, Renowned Bankruptcy Lawyer, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Miller, of the firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges, represented companies including Lehman Brothers, General Motors and American Airlines, and mentored many of the top Chapter 11 practitioners today.

name: Jayne Meadows
profession: Actress and Steve Allens Wife and Co-Star
headline: Jayne Meadows, Actress and Steve Allen’s Wife and Co-Star, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Meadows was the older sister of Audrey Meadows, who played Alice Kramden on “The Honeymooners.”

name: Wladyslaw Bartoszewski
headline: Wladyslaw Bartoszewski, 93, Dies; Polish Auschwitz Survivor Aided Jews
abstract: Mr. Bartoszewski was given honorary Israeli citizenship for his work to save Jews during World War II and later surprised even himself by being instrumental in reconciling Poland and Germany.

name: Elizabeth Brown Pryor
profession: Biographer of Clara Barton and Robert E. Lee
headline: Elizabeth Brown Pryor, Biographer of Clara Barton and Robert E. Lee, Dies at 64
abstract: Ms. Pryor, who served more than two decades in the State Department, was the author of well-regarded biographies of the founder of the American Red Cross and the Confederate commander.

name: Don Mankiewicz
profession: Screenwriter in a Family Film Tradition
headline: Don Mankiewicz, Screenwriter in a Family Film Tradition, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Mankiewicz, an Oscar-nominated screenwriter for “I Want to Live!,” also wrote episodes of television shows such as “Star Trek” and “Marcus Welby, M.D.”

name: Andrew Lesnie
profession: Cinematographer of Lord of the Rings
headline: Andrew Lesnie, Cinematographer of ‘Lord of the Rings,’ Dies at 59
abstract: The magical quality Mr. Lesnie created in shooting the “Babe” films caught the eye of the director Peter Jackson, who chose him to film the fantasy epic.

name: Bruce Alger
profession: Led Mink Coat Protest Against Lyndon Johnson
headline: Bruce Alger, 96, Dies; Led ‘Mink Coat’ Protest Against Lyndon Johnson
abstract: Mr. Alger, who served five terms from Texas, led Republican women in a confrontation with Lyndon B. Johnson that may have cost Richard M. Nixon the 1960 presidential election.

name: Marcel Pronovost
profession: Hall of Famer Shared in Five N.H.L. Titles
headline: Marcel Pronovost, 84, Dies; Hall of Famer Shared in Five N.H.L. Titles
abstract: Pronovost, who played for the Red Wings, was not a prolific scorer, but he was a consummate team player with bruising checks and fearless bursts up the ice that could puncture a defense.

name: Jean Nidetch
headline: Jean Nidetch, a Founder of Weight Watchers, Dies at 91
abstract: A 214-pound Queens housewife struggled with a lifelong addiction to food until she shed 72 pounds and became the public face of the worldwide weight-control empire.

name: François Michelin
headline: François Michelin, Head of Tire Company, Dies at 88
abstract: Under Mr. Michelin’s leadership, which ended when he left the company in 2002, the Michelin Group became the world’s biggest tire maker, establishing a big presence in the United States and other major markets overseas.

name: Gene Fullmer
headline: Gene Fullmer, a Brawling Middleweight Champion, Dies at 83
abstract: Fullmer, who reigned when fight clubs abounded and Friday night fights were a television staple, was known for his title bouts with Sugar Ray Robinson and Carmen Basilio.

name: Betsy von Furstenberg
headline: Betsy von Furstenberg, Baroness and Versatile Actress, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. von Furstenberg made her debut in the movies and on the Broadway stage in the early 1950s as a teenager and later reinvented herself as a television actress, writer and philanthropist.

name: Jack Ely
headline: Jack Ely, Who Sang the Kingsmen’s ‘Louie Louie’, Dies at 71
abstract: A 2-minute-42-second demo recording captured in one take turned out to be a one-hit wonder for Mr. Ely, who was 19 when he sang the garage-band classic.

name: Sid Tepper
profession: Delivered Red Roses for a Blue Lady and Other Songs
headline: Sid Tepper Dies at 96; Delivered ‘Red Roses for a Blue Lady’ and Other Songs
abstract: Mr. Tepper was not a musical child and had no formal training, but he grew up to write both lyrics and tunes, trading off duties with the other member of the team, Roy C. Bennett.

name: Calvin Peete
profession: Racial Pioneer on the PGA Tour
headline: Calvin Peete, 71, a Racial Pioneer on the PGA Tour, Is Dead
abstract: With 12 tournament victories in his career, Mr. Peete was the most successful black professional golfer before Tiger Woods.

name: Richard Suzman
profession: Researcher Influenced Global Surveys on Aging
headline: Richard Suzman, 72, Dies; Researcher Influenced Global Surveys on Aging
abstract: At the National Institutes of Health, Dr. Suzman’s signature accomplishment was the central role he played in creating a global network of surveys on aging.

name: Jozef Paczynski
headline: Jozef Paczynski, Inmate Barber to Auschwitz Commandant, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Paczynski was one of the concentration camp’s longest surviving inmates and served as the personal barber to its Nazi commandant Rudolf Höss.

name: Verne Gagne
headline: Verne Gagne, Wrestler Who Grappled Through Two Eras, Dies at 89
abstract: Gagne wrestled professionally from the late 1940s until the 1980s and was a transitional figure between the early 20th century barnstormers and the steroidal sideshows of today.

name: Ben E. King
profession: Soulful Singer of Stand by Me
headline: Ben E. King, Soulful Singer of ‘Stand by Me,’ Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. King sang for the Drifters and found success as a solo performer with hits like “Spanish Harlem.”

name: Rolf Smedvig
headline: Rolf Smedvig, Trumpeter in the Empire Brass, Dies at 62
abstract: A former member of the Boston Symphony Orchestra, Mr. Smedvig helped found the wide-ranging Empire Brass quintet.

name: William Pfaff
headline: William Pfaff, Critic of American Foreign Policy, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Pfaff was an international affairs columnist and author who found Washington’s intervention in world affairs often misguided.

name: Marty Napoleon
profession: Jazz Pianist Played With Louis Armstrong
headline: Marty Napoleon, 93, Dies; Jazz Pianist Played With Louis Armstrong
abstract: Mr. Napoleon was a self-taught musician whose career began in earnest with the orchestra led by Chico Marx of the Marx Brothers.

name: Edward Chambers
headline: Edward Chambers, Early Leader in Community Organizing, Dies at 85
abstract: A lapsed seminarian, Mr. Chambers succeeded Saul Alinsky as leader of the social justice umbrella group Industrial Areas Foundation.

name: Dave Goldberg
profession: Half of a Silicon Valley Power Couple
headline: Dave Goldberg, Half of a Silicon Valley Power Couple, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. Goldberg was a serial Silicon Valley entrepreneur and venture capitalist who was married to Sheryl Sandberg, the chief operating officer of Facebook.

name: Maya Plisetskaya
headline: Maya Plisetskaya, Ballerina Who Embodied Bolshoi, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Plisetskaya, renowned for her fluidity of movement, expressive acting and willful personality, danced on the Bolshoi stage well into her 60s, but her life was shadowed by Stalinism.

name: Ruth Rendell
headline: Ruth Rendell, Novelist Who Thrilled and Educated, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Rendell was a prolific writer of intricately plotted mystery novels that combined psychological insight, social conscience and teeth-chattering terror.

name: William Sokolin
headline: William Sokolin, Wine Seller Who Broke Famed Bottle, Dies at 85
abstract: The bottle Mr. Sokolin famously broke was a Château Margaux said to have belonged to Thomas Jefferson. Mr. Sokolin had been hoping to sell it for $519,750.

name: Joseph Lechleider
profession: Father of the DSL Internet Technology
headline: Joseph Lechleider, a Father of the DSL Internet Technology, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Lechleider helped invent DSL technology, which enabled phone companies to offer high-speed web access over their infrastructure of copper wires.

name: Joshua Ozersky
headline: Joshua Ozersky, Food Writer Who Extolled Meat, Is Dead at 47
abstract: The 47-year-old Mr. Ozersky, a blogger, critic and author of several books, was in Chicago for an awards ceremony presented by the James Beard Foundation.

name: Michael Blake
profession: Won Oscar for Dances With Wolves
headline: Michael Blake, 69, Writer, Dies; Won Oscar for ‘Dances With Wolves’
abstract: Mr. Blake turned his 1988 novel into a script for the western epic of the same name that starred Kevin Costner.

name: Robert Rietti
profession: Movies Man With a Thousand Voices
headline: Robert Rietti, Movies’ ‘Man With a Thousand Voices,’ Dies at 92
abstract: In the film “Waterloo,” Mr. Rietti said he was responsible for the voices of 98 characters after a soundtrack issue required copious redubbing.

name: Thomas R. Shepard Jr.
headline: Thomas R. Shepard Jr., Look Magazine’s Last Publisher, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Shepard oversaw the popular magazine from 1965 to its demise in 1971 after a rapid descent from record ad revenue and circulation.

name: Benjamin F. Logan
profession: Engineer by Day and Bluegrass Fiddler by Night
headline: Benjamin F. Logan, Engineer by Day and Bluegrass Fiddler by Night, Dies at 87
abstract: Balancing these two seemingly mismatched passions, Dr. Logan wrote songs covered by the likes of Bob Dylan and Johnny Cash, and devised methods and devices at AT&T Bell Laboratories.

name: Alexander Rich
headline: Alexander Rich Dies at 90; Confirmed DNA’s Double Helix
abstract: Dr. Rich, a molecular biologist, spent nearly 60 years investigating DNA and RNA and helping puzzle out the structure of collagen.

name: Ellen Albertini Dow
headline: Ellen Albertini Dow, Actress, Dies at 101; Rapping Granny in ‘Wedding Singer’
abstract: Ms. Dow found acting success in her 70s, turning to film and television after retiring as a drama and acting teacher in the mid-1980s.

name: Patachou
profession: French Singer With a Habit of Snipping Neckties
headline: Patachou, French Singer With a Habit of Snipping Neckties, Dies at 96
abstract: One of the most renowned French singers of the postwar period, Patachou was known for her deep voice and amiably irreverent stage persona.

name: Jim Wright
profession: House Speaker Resigned Amid Ethics Charges
headline: Jim Wright Dies at 92; House Speaker Resigned Amid Ethics Charges
abstract: Mr. Wright, a driven Texas Democrat who led the 100th Congress, resigned after he had been accused of improperly accepting $145,000 in gifts from a Fort Worth developer.

name: Lynn Grefe
profession: Advocate for Those With Eating Disorders
headline: Lynn Grefe, Advocate for Those With Eating Disorders, Dies at 65
abstract: After her daughter came forward with an eating disorder, Ms. Grefe organized a national campaign to convince women that being too thin can be fatal.

name: Marcia Brown
profession: Book Illustrator Won Three Caldecott Medals
headline: Marcia Brown, 96, Dies; Book Illustrator Won Three Caldecott Medals
abstract: Ms. Brown won three Caldecott Medals for her children’s books, including “Once a Mouse” and “Shadow,” one of only two artists to do so.

name: Errol Brown
profession: Wrote and Sang Disco Hit You Sexy Thing
headline: Errol Brown, 71, Dies; Wrote and Sang Disco Hit ‘You Sexy Thing’
abstract: Mr. Brown, the lead vocalist for the British disco band Hot Chocolate, also wrote the song, which gained new popularity when featured in “The Full Monty” in 1997.

name: Thomas A. Constantine
profession: Led N.Y. State Police and U.S. Drug Agency
headline: Thomas A. Constantine Dies at 76; Led N.Y. State Police and U.S. Drug Agency
abstract: Mr. Constantine resigned from the Drug Enforcement Administration in protest of the United States’ foreign policy on Mexico.

name: Guy Carawan
profession: Taught a Generation to Overcome, in Song
headline: Guy Carawan Dies at 87; Taught a Generation to Overcome, in Song
abstract: With his performance of “We Shall Overcome” at the inaugural meeting of the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee in 1960, Mr. Carawan turned a little-known folk song into an anthem.

name: Louis Nuñez
headline: Louis Nuñez, Champion of Puerto Ricans, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Nuñez worked to advance educational and economic opportunity for Puerto Ricans in the United States for more than three decades.

name: Dianne White Clatto
headline: Dianne White Clatto, Weathercaster Who Broke a Color Barrier, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Clatto, who transitioned from radio host to a television “weathergirl” in St. Louis, became the first full-time black television weathercaster in the country in 1962.

name: Maurice Flanagan
profession: Made Dubai a Hub With Emirates Airline
headline: Maurice Flanagan, 86, Dies; Made Dubai a Hub With Emirates Airline
abstract: Mr. Flanagan was a founding manager of Emirates, the airline that brought Dubai to the world’s attention.

name: Denise McCluggage
headline: Denise McCluggage, Auto Racing Pacesetter, Dies at 88
abstract: A racer and a journalist, Ms. McCluggage shattered stereotypes about women as professional drivers.

name: Kenan Evren
profession: After Coup, Led Turkey With Iron Hand
headline: Kenan Evren, 97, Dies; After Coup, Led Turkey With Iron Hand
abstract: General Evren imposed the harshest repression in his country’s history, leading to his trial and conviction more than 30 years later.

name: Elizabeth Wilson
profession: Tony Winner With a Foot in Hollywood
headline: Elizabeth Wilson, Tony Winner With a Foot in Hollywood, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Wilson, a Tony Award winner who appeared in the films “The Graduate” and “9 to 5,” specialized in supporting roles that were often meaty but rarely glamorous.

name: Frank DiPascali Jr.
headline: Frank DiPascali Jr., Madoff Aide Who Pleaded Guilty in Fraud, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. DiPascali was a top aide to Bernard L. Madoff who cooperated with prosecutors, and was to be sentenced in September.

name: Kim Kyok-sik
profession: North Korean General Tied to Attacks
headline: Kim Kyok-sik, North Korean General Tied to Attacks, Dies at 77
abstract: General Kim was the commander of a North Korean Army corps accused by South Korea of sinking a naval ship, killing 46 sailors in March 2010.

name: Alexandre Lamfalussy
headline: Alexandre Lamfalussy, a Euro Founder, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Lamfalussy, an economist and banker, was the founding president of the European Monetary Institute, which became the European Central Bank.

name: Mira Rothenberg
headline: Mira Rothenberg, Pioneer in Therapy for Children, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Rothenberg, a clinical psychologist, helped change the public perception of mental illness.

name: Chris Burden
headline: Chris Burden, a Conceptualist With Scars, Dies at 69
abstract: One of the foremost performance artists of the 1970s, Mr. Burden was perhaps the single best-known practitioner of the subgenre of body art.

name: Richard Bartlett
headline: Richard Bartlett, Legislator Who Fought New York’s Death Penalty, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Bartlett oversaw a reorganization of the state’s courts and led a commission that virtually abolished capital punishment in 1965.

name: Gertrude Schimmel
profession: First Female New York Police Chief
headline: Gertrude Schimmel, First Female New York Police Chief, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Schimmel joined the department in 1940, decades before women were allowed to go on patrol, and helped prepare a lawsuit in the 1960s to be able to take the promotional exam for sergeant.

name: William Zinsser
headline: William Zinsser, Author of ‘On Writing Well,’ Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Zinsser was a prolific author, editor and teacher, but it was his role as an arbiter of good writing that resonated widely and deeply.

name: Ed Fouhy
profession: TV Newsman and Promoter of Civic Journalism
headline: Ed Fouhy, TV Newsman and Promoter of Civic Journalism, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Fouhy worked for all three major networks as a producer and executive before becoming a critic of news organizations he viewed as out of step with their audience.

name: Johnny Gimble
headline: Johnny Gimble, Who Fiddled His Way to Fame, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Gimble, a virtuoso Texas fiddler who played with a roster of country superstars, won the Country Music Association award for best musician/instrumentalist five times.

name: Rachel Rosenthal
headline: Rachel Rosenthal, Bold Performance Artist, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Rosenthal’s work melded dance, theater, dramatic monologues, improvisation and visual art to illuminate her abiding concerns: feminism, environmentalism and animal rights.

name: Jerome Cooper
headline: Jerome Cooper, a Multitextured Jazz Percussionist, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Cooper, known for rigorous precision and layers of sound, was a member of the influential jazz trio the Revolutionary Ensemble.

name: Tony Ayala Jr.
headline: Tony Ayala Jr., Boxer Convicted of Rape, Dies at 52
abstract: Part of a celebrated San Antonio boxing family, Ayala was a rising middleweight contender before a rape conviction sent him to prison.

name: Audree Norton
headline: Audree Norton, Who Paved Way for Deaf Actors, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Norton, a deaf actress, sacrificed her own career in a fight that demonstrably helped the careers of the generation that followed, including Marlee Matlin.

name: Stan Cornyn
headline: Stan Cornyn, Creative Record Executive, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Cornyn was associated with Warner Bros. Records and had a hand in the careers of acts like Frank Sinatra and the Grateful Dead.

name: Franz Wright
headline: Franz Wright, Pulitzer Prize Winner for Poetry, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Wright, who published about a dozen volumes of his work, wrote of beatings and suicide, and of his difficult relationship with his father, the poet James Wright.

name: Garo Yepremian
headline: Garo Yepremian, Whose Kicks Outshined One Pass, Dies at 70
abstract: Yepremian’s ill-advised pass after a blocked field goal led to a Redskins touchdown in Super Bowl VII, but the Dolphins survived to cap a perfect season.

name: Francis Fleetwood
headline: Francis Fleetwood, Architect Who Transformed the Hamptons, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Fleetwood designed more than 200 homes in the Hamptons, many of them costing tens of millions of dollars and commissioned by clients who did not blink at the price.

name: Elisabeth Bing
profession: Mother of Lamaze Helped Change Childbirth
headline: Elisabeth Bing Dies at 100; ‘Mother of Lamaze’ Helped Change Childbirth
abstract: Ms. Bing helped to popularize the natural childbirth movement, reducing the need for anesthesia and giving mothers more control over the process of childbirth.

name: Sam Ciccone
headline: Sam Ciccone, a Champion of Gay Police Officers, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Ciccone, a former sergeant in the Fairview, N.J., police department, was a co-founder of the Gay Officers Action League, known as GOAL, in New York City in 1982.

name: Alfred DelBello
headline: Alfred DelBello, Ex-Lieutenant Governor of New York, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. DelBello was the first Democrat to serve as Westchester County executive and the lieutenant governor of New York for two years under Gov. Mario M. Cuomo.

name: Moshe Levinger
profession: Contentious Leader of Jewish Settlers in Hebron
headline: Moshe Levinger, Contentious Leader of Jewish Settlers in Hebron, Dies at 80
abstract: Rabbi Levinger, a polarizing figure in Israeli society, led a controversial and successful Jewish movement to settle Hebron after the Six-Day War in 1967.

name: Prashant Bhargava
headline: Prashant Bhargava, Filmmaker of ‘Patang (The Kite),’ Dies at 42
abstract: The film won critical praise for Mr. Bhargava, a graffiti virtuoso who progressed into commercial campaigns for television series as well as film and music videos.

name: Happy Rockefeller
headline: Happy Rockefeller, 88, Dies; Marriage to Governor Scandalized Voters
abstract: She and Gov. Nelson A. Rockefeller of New York married soon after both had been divorced, kicking up a political storm that may have cost him the Republican presidential nomination in 1964.

name: John Lo Schiavo
headline: Rev. John Lo Schiavo Dies at 90; University President Barred Basketball
abstract: Father Lo Schiavo, who spent 14 years as president of the University of San Francisco, made headlines when he suspended the men’s basketball program after repeated violations of N.C.A.A. rules.

name: David Sackett
profession: Proved Aspirin Helps Prevent Heart Attacks
headline: Dr. David Sackett, Who Proved Aspirin Helps Prevent Heart Attacks, Dies at 80
abstract: Within his profession, Dr. Sackett was known for helping to develop evidence-based medicine, which uses statistical data to treat patients.

name: Bruce Lundvall
headline: Bruce Lundvall, Who Revived Blue Note Jazz Label, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Lundvall, who led Blue Note for 25 years, added some of the greatest jazz musicians of the age to the label while expanding its success into other genres with artists like Willie Nelson, Al Green and Norah Jones.

name: Maggie Black
profession: Teacher to the Stars of Ballet and Modern Dance
headline: Maggie Black, Teacher to the Stars of Ballet and Modern Dance, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Black taught stars including Twyla Tharp, Eliot Feld and Gelsey Kirkland and received the nickname Black Magic from George Balanchine.

name: Jacob Jensen
headline: Jacob Jensen, Designer in Danish Modern Style, Dies at 89
abstract: A longtime designer for Bang & Olufsen, Mr. Jensen created sleek, modern objects for the home. The Museum of Modern Art devoted an entire exhibition to his work in 1978.

name: Ira Harkavy
headline: Ira Harkavy, Common-Sense New York Judge, Dies at 84
abstract: Judge Harkavy was best known for sentencing a bad landlord to spend time in a dilapidated building he owned with his unhappy tenants.

name: Bob Belden
headline: Bob Belden, Jazz Saxophonist, Composer and Historian, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Belden, a musician, composer, arranger, bandleader and record producer, was part reformist and part conservationist in the world of jazz.

name: Marques Haynes
profession: Dribbled as a Globetrotter and Dazzled Worldwide
headline: Marques Haynes, 89, Dies; Dribbled as a Globetrotter and Dazzled Worldwide
abstract: Haynes was a stellar cog on the Globetrotter squads of the late 1940s and early ’50s, and was later inducted into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame.

name: Victor Salvi
profession: Played Harps and Made Them Too
headline: Victor Salvi, Who Played Harps and Made Them Too, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Salvi, a former New York Philharmonic member, founded a company that became the world’s foremost harp producer.

name: T.K. Jones
profession: Arms Official Saw Nuclear War as Survivable
headline: T.K. Jones, 82, Dies; Arms Official Saw Nuclear War as Survivable
abstract: Mr. Jones had such faith in civil defense that he once said, “If there are enough shovels to go around, everybody’s going to make it.”

name: K.C. Jones
profession: Celtics Standout as Player and Coach
headline: K.C. Jones, Celtics Standout as Player and Coach, Dies at 88
abstract: As a defense-minded guard, he played on eight consecutive championship teams. He later found success leading the team from the sidelines.

name: L.Q. Jones
profession: Played Heavies With a Light Touch
headline: L.Q. Jones, Who Played Heavies With a Light Touch, Dies at 94
abstract: His face was familiar, mostly in westerns, during a career that spanned five decades. He also directed the cult film “A Boy and His Dog.”

name: John F. Nash Jr.
profession: Math Genius Defined by a Beautiful Mind
headline: John F. Nash Jr., Math Genius Defined by a ‘Beautiful Mind,’ Dies at 86
abstract: The narrative of Dr. Nash’s brilliant rise, the lost years of severe mental illness, and the eventual awarding of a Nobel captured the public mind.

name: Anne Meara
headline: Anne Meara, Comedian and Actress, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Meara began her comedy career as the partner of her husband, Jerry Stiller; won an Obie Award for her stage work; earned four Emmy nominations; and became a playwright in her 60s.

name: Martin Sheets
headline: Martin Sheets, Who Shone at the Special Olympics, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Sheets participated for more than 40 years in the Special Olympics, going back to its first international summer games at Chicago’s Soldier Field in 1968.

name: McNeil Robinson II
headline: McNeil Robinson II, 72, Organist and Composer, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Robinson, who was the chairman of the organ department at the Manhattan School of Music, was also the organist for several houses of worship.

name: Mary Ellen Mark
headline: Mary Ellen Mark, Photographer Who Documented Difficult Subjects, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Mark was known for her unflinching yet compassionate depictions of her subjects, who included prostitutes in Mumbai and homeless teenagers in Seattle.

name: Marcus Belgrave
profession: Trumpeter and Mentor in Detroits Jazz Scene
headline: Marcus Belgrave, Trumpeter and Mentor in Detroit’s Jazz Scene, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Belgrave, who also played the fluegelhorn, became a coach and conscience for the city’s jazz musicians.

name: Hugh Ambrose
headline: Hugh Ambrose, Historian Who Wrote ‘The Pacific,’ Dies at 48
abstract: The historian began his career as a researcher for his father, Stephen E. Ambrose; his best-selling history became an Emmy Award-winning mini-series.

name: Walter Byers
headline: Walter Byers, Ex-N.C.A.A. Leader Who Rued Corruption, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Byers forged a moneymaking colossus built on student-athletes but ultimately decried the college sports world as corrupt and unfair.

name: Robert S. Wistrich
headline: Robert S. Wistrich, Scholar of Anti-Semitism, Dies at 70
abstract: The professor at Hebrew University in Jerusalem was the author or editor of 29 books, including the encyclopedic “Antisemitism: The Longest Hatred.”

name: Anthony C. Yu
profession: Translator of the Saga of a Chinese Pilgrimage
headline: Anthony C. Yu, Translator of the Saga of a Chinese Pilgrimage, Dies at 76
abstract: Professor Yu’s four-volume tale of a monk and his entourage, including the Monkey King, is based on a work from 1592.

name: Morris Wilkins
headline: Morris Wilkins, Who Lured Honeymooners to Poconos, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Wilkins marketed his once nondescript northeastern Pennsylvania hotel as a libidinous Land of Love.

name: Michael King
headline: Michael King, Builder of a TV Empire, Dies at 67
abstract: With his brother Roger, Mr. King built King World Productions into a huge syndicator of some of television’s best known shows, including “The Oprah Winfrey Show,” “Wheel of Fortune” and “Jeopardy!”

name: S. Parker Gilbert
profession: Led and Later Shook Up Morgan Stanley
headline: S. Parker Gilbert, 81, Dies; Led and Later Shook Up Morgan Stanley
abstract: Mr. Gilbert was instrumental in taking the Wall Street firm public and later, in retirement, pushing for a management shake-up.

name: Edward P. Gilligan
headline: Edward P. Gilligan, American Express Executive, Dies at 55
abstract: Mr. Gilligan was largely seen as the likely successor to Kenneth Chenault, the chief executive.

name: Reynaldo Rey
headline: Reynaldo Rey, 75, Actor and Comedian, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Rey appeared in the Ice Cube hit film “Friday” and long worked with the comic Redd Foxx.

name: Jerry Dior
profession: Designer of Major League Baseballs Logo
headline: Jerry Dior, Designer of Major League Baseball’s Logo, Dies at 82
abstract: The logo was a routine assignment for Mr. Dior, completed in one afternoon, while he was working for Sandgren & Murtha, a New York City marketing concern.

name: Vladimir Katriuk
profession: Beekeeper Accused of Nazi War Crimes
headline: Vladimir Katriuk, Beekeeper Accused of Nazi War Crimes, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Mr. Katriuk, No. 2 on a list of most wanted Nazi war criminals, had been at the center of a dispute between Russia and Canada over an extradition demand.

name: Dave Sweet
headline: Dave Sweet, a Quiet Pioneer of Surfboarding, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Sweet’s obsessive tinkering 60 years ago in search of a better way to ride a wave resulted in a surfboard revolution.

name: Beau Biden
headline: Beau Biden, Vice President Joe Biden’s Son, Dies at 46
abstract: Joseph R. Biden III, the former Delaware attorney general who was known as Beau, had been planning to run for governor in 2016, but had been battling brain cancer.

name: Lennie Merullo
profession: Last Cub to Play in a World Series
headline: Lennie Merullo, the Last Cub to Play in a World Series, Dies at 98
abstract: Merullo enjoyed a distinction that would elude hundreds of other Cubs: he was the last surviving ballplayer to have worn a Cubs uniform in a World Series.

name: Doris Hart
headline: Doris Hart, a Tennis Star Who Deftly Overcame Leg Ailments, Dies at 89
abstract: Although leg and knee conditions left her bowlegged and relatively slow — a leg infection when she was a child led a specialist to recommend amputation — Hart became one of the world’s best players.

name: Louis Johnson
profession: Bassist and Singer for the Brothers Johnson
headline: Louis Johnson, Bassist and Singer for the Brothers Johnson, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Johnson, who collaborated with his brother George on 1970s funk hits, was also in demand as a session musician for Quincy Jones and others.

name: Louis Johnson
headline: Louis Johnson, 90, Genre-Crossing Dancer and Choreographer, Dies
abstract: His career spanned Broadway (“Damn Yankees”), film (“The Wiz”), opera (“Aida”) and the stages of the Alvin Ailey and Dance Theater of Harlem companies.

name: Tanith Lee
headline: Tanith Lee, Fantasy and Horror Novelist, Dies at 67
abstract: Ms. Lee became the first woman to win the British Fantasy Award for best novel with “Death’s Master” in 1980.

name: Betsy Palmer
profession: From TV Panelist to Friday the 13th Villainess
headline: Betsy Palmer, 88, Dies; From TV Panelist to ‘Friday the 13th’ Villainess
abstract: Ms. Palmer is bound to be remembered by different generations for different career incarnations — as a live television performer, a game show panelist and a bloodthirsty camp cook.

name: Jean Ritchie
headline: Jean Ritchie, Lyrical Voice of Appalachia, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Ritchie brought hundreds of traditional songs from her native Appalachia to a wide audience and performed with major names in folk music, including Pete Seeger and Doc Watson.

name: Rochelle Shoretz
headline: Rochelle Shoretz, Founder of Cancer Support Group, Dies at 42
abstract: Ms. Shoretz, a lawyer who clerked for Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg of the Supreme Court, founded Sharsheret in 2001 after learning she had breast cancer.

name: Jim Bailey
headline: Jim Bailey, Character Actor in Drag, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Bailey, who performed in the guise of pop divas like Judy Garland and Barbra Streisand, was a Las Vegas favorite, but he also played supper clubs, cabarets, Carnegie Hall and the London Palladium.

name: Irwin A. Rose
headline: Irwin A. Rose, Nobel-Winning Biochemist, Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Rose’s early interest in the problem of protein disposal helped lead to the development of a new class of cancer-fighting drugs.

name: Dudley Williams
headline: Dudley Williams, Eloquent Dancer Who Defied Age, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Williams was an East Harlem prodigy who dazzled Alvin Ailey company audiences as a leading dancer for more than four decades, performing into his 60s.

name: Jacques Parizeau
headline: Jacques Parizeau, Who Led Second Quebec Separatist Movement, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Parizeau wanted Quebec to secede from Canada to help it realize its potential, but after a second failed vote in 1995, he damaged his reputation with a speech explaining why the separatists lost.

name: Nico Castel
profession: Tenor and Diction Coach at the Met
headline: Nico Castel, Tenor and Diction Coach at the Met, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Castel, who guided generations of the world’s foremost singers through the oohs and aahs of their craft, appeared in nearly 800 performances with the Metropolitan Opera.

name: Mario Cooper
profession: Nexus Between AIDS Activists and Black Leaders
headline: Mario Cooper, Nexus Between AIDS Activists and Black Leaders, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Cooper was a former Democratic political operative who pressed civil rights groups to confront H.I.V.’s effect.

name: Günther Schneider-Siemssen
headline: Günther Schneider-Siemssen Dies at 88; Envisioned Elaborate Opera Stage Sets
abstract: Mr. Schneider­-Siemssen originally studied to be a conductor until he was persuaded to use his artistic ability to interpret music visually instead.

name: Margaret Juntwait
profession: Voice of the Met on Radio
headline: Margaret Juntwait, the Voice of the Met on Radio, Dies at 58
abstract: Ms. Juntwait, who became the Met’s third radio host in 2004, hosting 229 Saturday radio broadcasts, also presided over 898 broadcasts on the Met’s satellite-radio channel.

name: Bevo Francis
profession: Scored 116 and 113 Points in College Basketball Games
headline: Bevo Francis Dies at 82; Scored 116 and 113 Points in College Basketball Games
abstract: In 1954, Francis scored 113 points in a single college basketball game, setting an N.C.A.A. record that stood for nearly six decades.

name: Will Holt
profession: Wrote Lemon Tree and for the Musical Stage
headline: Will Holt, Who Wrote ‘Lemon Tree’ and for the Musical Stage, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Holt spent much of his musical career creating theater projects.

name: Tariq Aziz
profession: Top Aide and Fervent Ally of Saddam Hussein
headline: Tariq Aziz, Top Aide and Fervent Ally of Saddam Hussein, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Aziz, the Iraqi foreign minister and deputy prime minister, was for decades the most public face of Mr. Hussein’s government.

name: Leonid Plyushch
profession: Soviet Dissident Punished in an Asylum
headline: Leonid Plyushch, Soviet Dissident Punished in an Asylum, Dies
abstract: Mr. Plyushch, a Ukrainian mathematician, became a leading political dissident, prompting the Kremlin to commit him to a mental asylum for a nightmarish three years of drugs and deprivation.

name: Ruth Feldman
profession: Quiz Kid Told What It Was Like in a Book
headline: Ruth Feldman, 80, Dies; Quiz Kid Told What It Was Like in a Book
abstract: Mrs. Feldman made her entrance to the radio quiz world in 1941 as Ruthie Duskin, age 7.

name: Irving Mondschein
headline: Irving Mondschein, Decathlete, Coach and Track Patriarch, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Mondschein was a national champion in the decathlon and high jump in the 1940s, a college and Olympic coach and the patriarch of three generations of track and field stars.

name: Ronnie Gilbert
headline: Ronnie Gilbert, Bold-Voiced Singer With the Weavers, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Ms. Gilbert, as a member of the Weavers, helped propel folk music to wide popularity and establish its power as an agent of social change.

name: Henry Carr
profession: Olympic Sprinter and a Football Giant
headline: Henry Carr, Olympic Sprinter and a Football Giant, Dies at 73
abstract: Carr, a sprinter, captured two gold medals in the 1964 Tokyo Olympics before he became a defensive back for the New York Giants.

name: Roger Vergé
headline: Roger Vergé, a Founder of Nouvelle Cuisine, Dies at 85
abstract: His adaptation of Provençal cooking incorporated the flavors of Africa and the Caribbean.

name: Alan Bond
headline: Alan Bond, Yachting Hero and Convict, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Bond funded Australia’s victory in the 1983 America’s Cup, but several of his other business ventures led to convictions of misconduct and the largest corporate fraud in Australian history.

name: Dolores Spikes
profession: Trailblazer as President of Southern University
headline: Dolores Spikes, Trailblazer as President of Southern University, Dies at 78
abstract: As president of the Southern University and A&M College System in Louisiana, Ms. Spikes opposed court-ordered desegregation of the state’s colleges to protect Southern’s identity as a black institution.

name: Vincent T. Bugliosi
headline: Vincent T. Bugliosi, Manson Prosecutor and True-Crime Author, Dies at 80
abstract: After successfully prosecuting the cult leader Charles Manson and several of his followers, Mr. Bugliosi wrote “Helter Skelter,” the best-selling true-crime book ever.

name: Vincent Musetto
profession: Wrote Headless Headline of Ageless Fame
headline: Vincent Musetto, 74, Dies; Wrote ‘Headless’ Headline of Ageless Fame
abstract: Mr. Musetto, as an editor at The New York Post, wrote the most anatomically evocative headline in the history of American journalism.

name: Marie-Louise Carven
headline: Marie-Louise Carven, Designer of Accessible Chic, Dies at 105
abstract: The brand Mrs. Carven built has become synonymous with the rise of “contemporary,” midprice, accessible clothing with runway credibility, in French fashion.

name: Hermann Zapf
headline: Hermann Zapf, 96, Dies; Designer Whose Letters Are Found Everywhere
abstract: Mr. Zapf found expression in subtly inventive typefaces that have brought words to readers on paper, on signposts, on monuments and on computer screens for more than half a century.

name: Manuel Camacho Solís
profession: Once on Path to Mexican Presidency
headline: Manuel Camacho Solís, Once on Path to Mexican Presidency, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Camacho, who served as mayor of Mexico City and held other offices, was expected to be selected to be a presidential candidate but was passed over.

name: Ludvik Vaculik
headline: Ludvik Vaculik, Influential Czech Writer and Dissident, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Vaculik not only wrote some great books, one expert said, but he also “influenced events and spearheaded political changes” in Czechoslovakia, especially the “Prague Spring” of 1968.

name: Horst Brandstätter
headline: Horst Brandstätter, Who Introduced Playmobil, Dies at 81
abstract: Frugality led to the development of small movable figures inspired by children’s drawings and crèche figurines.

name: Paul Bacon
profession: Book Jackets Drew Readers and Admirers
headline: Paul Bacon, 91, Whose Book Jackets Drew Readers and Admirers, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Bacon designed the covers of “Slaughterhouse-Five” and “Jaws” in a style that came to be known as the “Big Book Look,” a bold, minimalist design with prominent lettering and a small conceptual image.

name: Eugene Kennedy
profession: Voice for Change in the Catholic Church
headline: Eugene Kennedy, a Voice for Change in the Catholic Church, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Kennedy, who left the priesthood in 1977, was a teacher, writer and social scientist who believed the hierarchical structure of the church put it out of touch with the modern world.

name: Marguerite Patten
profession: Tutored Food-Rationed Britons in Home Cooking
headline: Marguerite Patten, 99, Dies; Tutored Food-Rationed Britons in Home Cooking
abstract: Starting out during the rationing years of the 1940s and 1950s, Ms. Patten, who wrote more than 170 books, was one of Britain’s first television chefs.

name: Ornette Coleman
headline: Ornette Coleman, Saxophonist Who Rewrote the Language of Jazz, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Coleman was a leader in making jazz less beholden to rules of harmony and rhythm.

name: Christopher Lee
profession: Actor Breathed Life Into Nightmarish Villains
headline: Christopher Lee Dies at 93; Actor Breathed Life Into Nightmarish Villains
abstract: Mr. Lee, “tall, dark and gruesome” in his own words, made an indelible mark in roles like Count Dracula, Frankenstein’s monster and Saruman in the “Lord of the Rings” movies.

name: Fred Anton Maier
headline: Fred Anton Maier, 76, Speedskating Champion and Record Setter, Dies
abstract: Maier won the Olympic gold medal in the 5,000 meters at Grenoble in 1968 but lost the 10,000 in a surprising upset.

name: Ron Moody
profession: Actor Best Known as Fagin in Oliver!
headline: Ron Moody, Actor Best Known as Fagin in ‘Oliver!,’ Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Moody, a British character actor, flared to prominence in the role of Dickens’s guru of thievery, in the stage and screen adaptation of “Oliver!”.

name: Mervin Field
profession: Took Pulse of California as Pollster
headline: Mervin Field Dies at 94; Took Pulse of California as Pollster
abstract: Mr. Field, who started a research company in 1945, was an institutional memory of public opinion in an opinionated state.

name: James Last
headline: James Last, Bandleader Known for ‘Happy Sound,’ Dies at 86
abstract: The internationally renowned German bandleader purveyed music that was considered staggeringly accessible, even by the standards of easy listening.

name: Jim Ed Brown
profession: Smooth Voice on The Three Bells and Other Hits
headline: Jim Ed Brown, Smooth Voice on ‘The Three Bells’ and Other Hits, Dies at 81
abstract: A Grand Ole Opry star, Mr. Brown had a long string of songs on the country charts, both as part of the Browns, with Helen Cornelius, and as a solo act.

name: Jane Hart
headline: Jane Hart, Activist and Nearly an Astronaut, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Hart passed NASA’s astronaut training program while married to Philip A. Hart, a Democratic senator from Michigan who often found himself defending his wife’s liberal views.

name: Robert Chartoff
profession: Producer of Raging Bull and Rocky
headline: Robert Chartoff, Producer of ‘Raging Bull’ and ‘Rocky,’ Dies at 81
abstract: For two decades, beginning in 1967, Mr. Chartoff and his partner, Irwin Winkler, produced many of the signature Hollywood films of the era.

name: Ronald A. Wilford
profession: Manager to a Host of Legendary Maestros
headline: Ronald A. Wilford, Manager to a Host of Legendary Maestros, Dies at 87
abstract: By orchestrating the careers of leading conductors, he became one of the most powerful figures in classical music in the second half of the 20th century.

name: Frank Zachary
headline: Frank Zachary, Editor and Art Director, Dies at 101
abstract: Former colleagues remember Mr. Zachary as one of the last great editors and art directors from a golden age of magazines.

name: John Carroll
headline: John Carroll, Editor Who Reinvigorated The Los Angeles Times, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Mr. Carroll, a widely admired newspaper editor, restored the reputation and credibility of The Los Angeles Times in the early 2000s even as he fought bitterly with the paper’s corporate parent.

name: Nek Chand
profession: Creator of a Sculpture Kingdom in India
headline: Nek Chand, Creator of a Sculpture Kingdom in India, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Chand’s life work was the Rock Garden of Chandigarh, which comprises fountains and sculptures, many of them made from found objects.

name: Monica Lewis
profession: Her Apple-Pie Appeal Sold Chiquita Bananas
headline: Monica Lewis, 93, Dies; Her Apple-Pie Appeal Sold Chiquita Bananas
abstract: Miss Lewis began her career as a singer and actress at an early age and was still performing near the end of her life.

name: Blaze Starr
headline: Blaze Starr, Burlesque Queen Who Was Linked to a Governor, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Starr’s affair with Gov. Earl K. Long of Louisiana was the basis of her memoir and a 1989 movie.

name: Kirk Kerkorian
profession: Billionaire Investor in Film Studios and Casinos
headline: Kirk Kerkorian, Billionaire Investor in Film Studios and Casinos, Dies at 98
abstract: A son of Armenian immigrants, Mr. Kerkorian was known for his large purchases of stock in Las Vegas and Hollywood companies, and his private lifestyle.

name: Anne Gaylor
profession: Guarded Wall Between Church and State
headline: Anne Gaylor, 88, Dies; Guarded Wall Between Church and State
abstract: Ms. Gaylor was the principal founder of the Freedom From Religion Foundation, the nation’s largest group of atheists and agnostics.

name: Suleyman Demirel
headline: Suleyman Demirel, Seven Times Turkey’s Prime Minister, Dies at 90
abstract: A remarkable political survivor, Mr. Demirel dominated his country’s affairs for almost 50 years.

name: Ron Clarke
profession: Australian Runner Known for World Records
headline: Ron Clarke, Australian Runner Known for World Records, Dies at 78
abstract: A middle- and long-distance runner who broke 17 world records, some by huge margins, in the mid-1960s but never won an Olympic gold medal.

name: Jimmy Lee
headline: Jimmy Lee, Investment Banking Force, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Lee was a vice chairman at JPMorgan Chase and was widely credited with developing the leveraged loan market in the United States.
