name: Nelson Doubleday Jr.
headline: Nelson Doubleday Jr., Publisher Who Owned the Mets, Dies at 81
abstract: He expressed his love for baseball on a grand scale when his family’s publishing business became majority owner of the last-place Mets in 1980 and committed millions to rebuilding the team.

name: Elisabeth Elliot
profession: Tenacious Missionary in Face of Tragedy
headline: Elisabeth Elliot, Tenacious Missionary in Face of Tragedy, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Elliot inspired generations of evangelical Christians by returning to preach the Gospel to the Indian tribe that had killed her husband.

name: Hilary Masters
profession: Novelist and Son of American Poet
headline: Hilary Masters, Novelist and Son of American Poet, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Masters, the son of Edgar Lee Masters, taught at Carnegie Mellon University for 32 years. His writing won praise for a keen sensitivity to ordinary life.

name: Jack Rollins
profession: Managed Comedy Greats Like Woody Allen
headline: Jack Rollins Dies at 100; Managed Comedy Greats Like Woody Allen
abstract: Mr. Rollins, whose clients also included Robin Williams, Billy Crystal, David Letterman and Lenny Bruce, scouted talent and helped develop acts.

name: Joyce Ann Brown
profession: Shackled by Her Name to Anothers Crime
headline: Joyce Ann Brown, Shackled by Her Name to Another’s Crime, Dies at 68
abstract: After her name was tied to a 1980 robbery and murder, the police learned of another woman with the same name. Yet Ms. Brown was wrongly jailed for the crime.

name: Ralph Roberts
headline: Ralph Roberts, Cable TV Pioneer Who Built Comcast, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Roberts turned a small cable service in Tupelo, Miss., into the largest cable television company in the nation.

name: James Salter
profession: Writers Writer Short on Sales but Long on Acclaim
headline: James Salter, a ‘Writer’s Writer’ Short on Sales but Long on Acclaim, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Salter wrote slowly, exactingly and, by almost every critic’s estimation, beautifully. But he never achieved the broad popularity he craved.

name: Carl Nesjar
headline: Carl Nesjar, Sculptor Who Added Dimension to Picasso, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Nesjar was for nearly two decades Picasso’s chosen fabricator — the artist who took the master’s drawings and scale models and gave them physical form as immense public sculptures.

name: Allen Weinstein
headline: Allen Weinstein, Historian of Alger Hiss Case, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Weinstein set out to write a book proving that Mr. Hiss did not pass government documents to the Soviet Union when he worked for the State Department in the 1930s, only to reverse his judgment in the face of the evidence.

name: Frederick P. Li
headline: Frederick P. Li, Who Proved a Genetic Cancer Link, Dies at 75
abstract: Dr. Li helped show a skeptical medical establishment that a dominant gene, passed from parent to child, was predisposing family members to various cancers.

name: Charles Correa
profession: Architect Fused Indias History With Modernism
headline: Charles Correa, 84, Is Dead; Architect Fused India’s History With Modernism
abstract: Mr. Correa, whose works were notable for their imagination and breadth, created striking museums and university buildings in India and abroad and was deeply invested in India’s urban future.

name: Gunther Schuller
headline: Gunther Schuller Dies at 89; Composer Synthesized Classical and Jazz
abstract: Mr. Schuller, who won a Pulitzer Prize for his orchestral work in 1994, coined the term Third Stream to describe music that drew on the forms and resources of both classical and jazz.

name: Colette Marchand
headline: Colette Marchand, Glamorous International Ballet Star, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Marchand played a highly visible role in the postwar creative ferment of French ballet and she was nominated for an Oscar for her role in John Huston’s “Moulin Rouge.”

name: Walter Scheib
headline: Walter Scheib, Innovative Former White House Chef, Is Dead at 61
abstract: Mr. Scheib, who ran the mansion’s kitchen during the administrations of Bill Clinton and George W. Bush, had been missing for about a week after going on a hike.

name: Laura Antonelli
headline: Laura Antonelli Dies at 73; Popular, and Seductive, Italian Actress
abstract: Ms. Antonelli appeared in more than 40 films, often with matinee idols like Marcello Mastroianni.

name: Daniel Villanueva
headline: Daniel Villanueva, a Creator of Univision, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Villanueva was a former kicker for the Los Angeles Rams and Dallas Cowboys who built a Spanish-language broadcasting empire spanning the United States.

name: James Horner
profession: His Score for Titanic Was a Hit, Too
headline: James Horner, Film Composer, Dies at 61; His Score for ‘Titanic’ Was a Hit, Too
abstract: Mr. Horner, a multiple Oscar and Grammy winner, was flying solo in a single-turboprop plane that crashed and burned in Southern California.

name: Dick Van Patten
profession: Harried Father on Eight Is Enough
headline: Dick Van Patten, Harried Father on ‘Eight Is Enough,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Van Patten was best known for his role as the patriarch on the 1977-81 ABC drama, based on a memoir by Tom Braden.

name: Don Featherstone
profession: Inventor of the Pink Flamingo (in Plastic)
headline: Don Featherstone, Inventor of the Pink Flamingo (in Plastic), Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Featherstone’s first pink plastic flamingo came off the assembly line in 1957.

name: Frances Kroll Ring
headline: Frances Kroll Ring, Secretary to F. Scott Fitzgerald, Dies at 99
abstract: Ms. Ring was a sounding board for Fitzgerald and after his death was a longtime source of information for biographers, filmmakers and fans.

name: Harvey Pollack
profession: Inventive Statistician in N.B.A. From Day 1
headline: Harvey Pollack, Inventive Statistician in N.B.A. From Day 1, Dies at 93
abstract: Pollack, who was associated mostly with the Philadelphia 76ers, was a mastermind of N.B.A. statistical innovation dating to the league’s creation in 1946.

name: Miriam Schapiro
headline: Miriam Schapiro, 91, a Feminist Artist Who Harnessed Craft and Pattern, Dies
abstract: When one of her works was criticized as sentimental, Ms. Schapiro said in an interview that sentiment was powerful to her although it was devalued by men.

name: Albert Evans
headline: Albert Evans, Ebullient City Ballet Dancer, Is Dead at 46
abstract: Mr. Evans, a muscular and elegant performer, was only the second black dancer to be named a principal with the company.

name: Mario Biaggi
headline: Mario Biaggi, 97, Popular Bronx Congressman Who Went to Prison, Dies
abstract: Mr. Biaggi had been a highly decorated police officer and a popular House member when he fell from grace in corruption scandals.

name: Patrick Macnee
profession: Dapper and Unflappable in The Avengers
headline: Patrick Macnee, 93, Dapper and Unflappable in ‘The Avengers,’ Dies
abstract: Mr. Macnee played many roles over the decades but was best known as John Steed on “The Avengers,” the 1960s British series.

name: Harold Battiste
headline: Harold Battiste, Musician, Mentor and Arranger, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Battiste lent his expertise to a long list of future stars, founded a collective record company and taught at universities.

name: George Winslow
headline: George Winslow, Child Actor Who Had a Moment With Marilyn, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Winslow made his film debut as Teenie in “Room for One More,” with Cary Grant, but his most memorable scene was in “Gentlemen Prefer Blondes.”

name: Phil Austin
headline: Phil Austin (a.k.a. Nick Danger) of Firesign Theater Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Austin was not only a voice-over artist but a writer, producer and guitarist for the comedy troupe, which was popular starting in the late 1960s.

name: Yevgeny Primakov
headline: Yevgeny Primakov, Former Russian Premier and Spymaster, Dies at 85
abstract: A former prime minister and intelligence chief, Mr. Primakov was also the Kremlin’s top expert on Middle Eastern affairs.

name: Red Mascara
profession: His Im From New Jersey Almost Became State Song
headline: Red Mascara, 92, Dies; His ‘I’m From New Jersey’ Almost Became State Song
abstract: Mr. Mascara’s persistent lobbying once came a veto pen away from succeeding, but always remained out of reach.

name: Walter Shawn Browne
headline: Walter Shawn Browne, Fast-Moving Chess Grandmaster, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Browne was an aggressive, animated grandmaster and six-time United States champion who dazzled spectators with his world-class ability at speed chess.

name: Chris Squire
profession: Founding Bassist With the Rock Band Yes
headline: Chris Squire, Founding Bassist With the Rock Band Yes, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Squire was the only member to have played on every one of Yes’s albums and participated in every one of its tours.

name: Marva Collins
headline: Marva Collins, Educator Who Aimed High for Poor, Black Students, Dies at 78
abstract: At Westside Preparatory School in Chicago, which she opened in 1975, Ms. Collins set high academic standards, emphasized discipline and promoted a nurturing environment.

name: Magali Noël
profession: French Singer and Actress and Muse to Fellini
headline: Magali Noël, a French Singer and Actress and Muse to Fellini, Dies at 83
abstract: The Turkish Ms. Noël, a favorite of the director Federico Fellini, sang a rendition of “Fais-Moi Mal, Johnny” (“Hurt Me, Johnny”) that proved scandalous because of its masochistic lyrics.

name: Ben Wattenberg
headline: Ben Wattenberg, Neoconservative Author and PBS Host, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Wattenberg was a self-professed neoconservative and PBS commentator who was wary of a Democratic move to the left.

name: Jack Carter
headline: Jack Carter, Comedian Who Brought His Rapid-Fire Delivery to TV, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Carter was a comic and an actor possessing a rapid-fire delivery, a barrage of one-liners and impressions, a dancer’s light-footedness and a more than passable singing voice.

name: Harold Feinstein
profession: Froze New York Moments in Black and White
headline: Harold Feinstein Dies at 84; Froze New York Moments in Black and White
abstract: Although Mr. Feinstein immortalized a period in the history of Coney Island, especially, he turned his lens on a wide variety of subjects.

name: Theodore Weesner
headline: Theodore Weesner, Author of ‘The Car Thief,’ Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Weesner, whose celebrated first novel was inspired in part by his wayward youth, earned plaudits for his patient, realistic narratives and humanely considered characters.

name: Nicholas Winton
headline: Nicholas Winton, Rescuer of 669 Children From Holocaust, Dies at 106
abstract: A London stockbroker in 1938, he rescued the youngsters from Czechoslovakia but then said nothing about his deeds for 50 years.

name: Donald Wexler
headline: Donald Wexler, Architect Who Gave Shape to Palm Springs, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Wexler’s innovative steel houses and soaring glass-fronted terminal at the Palm Springs International Airport helped make the desert city a showcase for midcentury modernism.

name: Kathryn Barnard
profession: Innovator in Care and Development of Newborns
headline: Kathryn Barnard, Innovator in Care and Development of Newborns, Dies at 77
abstract: Dr. Barnard conducted studies of infants and their parents that helped illustrate the connection between early stimulation of the senses and social, emotional and behavioral growth.

name: Charls Walker
headline: Charls Walker, Treasury Official and Business Lobbyist, Is Dead at 91
abstract: As a Treasury Department official, Mr. Walker oversaw federal revenue-sharing. As a lobbyist, he helped preserve write-offs for the three-martini lunch.

name: Sonny Madrid
profession: Illuminated Chicano Life in Lowrider Magazine
headline: Sonny Madrid, 70, Dies; Illuminated Chicano Life in Lowrider Magazine
abstract: He helped spread Chicano political activism by pairing it with coverage of the tricked-out cars that found popularity among Mexican-Americans in the 1970s.

name: Val Doonican
profession: Top-Selling Irish Singer and TV Host
headline: Val Doonican, Top-Selling Irish Singer and TV Host, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Doonican hosted a variety show for two decades, but was also known for knocking the Beatles out of the top spot on the British album charts.

name: Charles Harbutt
profession: Photojournalist With an Eye for Art
headline: Charles Harbutt, Photojournalist With an Eye for Art, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Harbutt infused his work with evocative imagery and as an art photographer he transformed conventional scenes into surreal metaphors.

name: John Whitman
profession: Investment Banker and Husband of Governor
headline: John Whitman, Investment Banker and Husband of Governor, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Whitman took on an ambassadorial role of sorts for state government when his wife, Christie Whitman, was governor of New Jersey during the 1990s.

name: Lawrence Herkimer
headline: Lawrence Herkimer, Grandfather of Modern Cheerleading, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Herkimer elevated cheerleading into an aspirational goal for generations of youths and a highly successful business for himself.

name: Charlie Sanders
profession: Hall of Fame Tight End With Lions
headline: Charlie Sanders, Hall of Fame Tight End With Lions, Dies at 68
abstract: Sanders, a tight end for the Lions from 1968 to 1977, helped redefine a position that had been traditionally reserved for stolid blockers.

name: Boyd K. Packer
headline: Boyd K. Packer, Advocate of Conservative Mormonism, Dies at 90
abstract: Next in line to become president of the Mormon Church, Mr. Packer spoke for those in the church who resisted social change.

name: Jane Aaron
profession: Her Film Animation Sprouted on Sesame Street
headline: Jane Aaron Dies at 67; Her Film Animation Sprouted on ‘Sesame Street’
abstract: Ms. Aaron’s films have been shown in museums around the world, but her work found its widest audience on the popular children’s education program.

name: Burt Shavitz
headline: Burt Shavitz, Scruffy Face of Burt’s Bees, Dies at 80
abstract: After Mr. Shavitz sold his share in the company, he returned to his hermit’s existence in a 400-square-foot converted turkey coop in Parkman, Me.

name: Jerry Weintraub
headline: Jerry Weintraub, a Force in Film and Music, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Weintraub’s career touched musical entertainers as grandly diverse as Elvis Presley and Led Zeppelin, and films like “The Karate Kid” and the “Ocean’s Eleven” casino heist trilogy.

name: Scot Breithaupt
headline: Scot Breithaupt, Who Blazed a Trail in BMX, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Breithaupt helped found and became the pre-eminent early promoter of bicycle motocross racing. He also manufactured BMX bikes and became a television commentator on BMX.

name: Juli Soler
headline: Juli Soler, the El Bulli Restaurateur Who Changed Dining, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Soler and Ferran Adrià turned El Bulli in Spain into the most daring and influential restaurant of its time.

name: John Maxtone-Graham
headline: John Maxtone-Graham, an Authority on Ocean Liners, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Maxtone-Graham made hundreds of crossings, spending more time at sea than on land, and recreated the glory days of luxury liners in books and lectures.

name: Ron Pollard
headline: Ron Pollard, Oddsmaker on Just About Everything, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Pollard was widely credited with introducing betting on British politics, extending the bookmaking business beyond horse and dog racing..

name: Helen Harrison
profession: Authority on the Trials of Premature Births
headline: Helen Harrison, Authority on the Trials of Premature Births, Dies at 68
abstract: After her own son was born two and a half months ahead of schedule, she wrote a popular manual, “The Premature Baby Book,” to help other parents in similar situations.

name: Saud al-Faisal
headline: Saud al-Faisal of Saudi Arabia, Quiet Force in Middle East, Dies at 75
abstract: Prince Saud, who served for four decades as Saudi Arabia’s foreign minister, was known for his behind-the-scenes, conservative diplomacy in a time of major changes.

name: Bonard Fowler
headline: Bonard Fowler, Alabama Officer in Shooting That Led to Selma March, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Fowler waited four decades to publicly acknowledge his role in Jimmie Lee Jackson’s death, considered an impetus for the 1965 voting-rights marches from Selma to Montgomery.

name: James Marcus
headline: James Marcus, Opera Benefactor and Ex-Goldman Partner, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Marcus served as a managing director of the Metropolitan Opera beginning in 1976. Ten years later he was named chairman, a position he held until 1993.

name: Masabumi Kikuchi
headline: Masabumi Kikuchi, Jazz Pianist Who Embraced Individualism, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Kikuchi’s playing had a cloistered originality and a style of free improvisation he described as “floating.”

name: Ken Stabler
headline: Ken Stabler, Quarterback Who Led Raiders to Title, Dies at 69
abstract: Stabler, a star quarterback under Bear Bryant at Alabama and under John Madden for the Raiders, was the National Football League’s most valuable player in 1974 and led Oakland to a Super Bowl victory in 1977.

name: Omar Sharif
profession: Star in Lawrence of Arabia and Doctor Zhivago
headline: ​Omar Sharif, 83, a Star in ‘Lawrence of Arabia’ and ‘Doctor Zhivago,’ Dies
abstract: Mr. Sharif was a commanding presence onscreen, multilingual and comfortable in almost any role or cultural setting.

name: James Tate
headline: James Tate, Prolific Pulitzer-Winning Poet, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Tate, a writer fond of wordplay and wild flights of surrealism, also won the National Book Award.

name: Roger Rees
headline: Roger Rees, Actor Who Won Tony as Nicholas Nickleby, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Rees, a lanky, Welsh-born actor and director, was known for roles on “Cheers” and “The West Wing,” but made his biggest mark as Nicholas Nickleby in the early 1980s.

name: William Conrad Gibbons
headline: William Conrad Gibbons, Dogged Writer About Vietnam War, Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Gibbons conducted interviews and analyzed a mass of material for his multivolume work about the relationship between Congress and the executive branch during the Vietnam War.

name: Blaine Gibson
profession: Sculptor of Figures in Disney Parks
headline: Blaine Gibson, Sculptor of Figures in Disney Parks, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Gibson created hundreds of sculptures for Disney’s Audio-Animatronic robotic figures, including those of Pirates of the Caribbean and Abraham Lincoln.

name: Paul Lioy
headline: Paul Lioy, Scientist Who Analyzed 9/11 Dust and Its Health Effects, Dies at 68
abstract: Dr. Lioy was an environmental scientist who was widely known for his analysis of the dust spawned by the Sept. 11 attacks on the World Trade Center, and for his studies of its health effects over time.

name: Jon Vickers
profession: Opera Star Known for His Raw Power and Intensity
headline: Jon Vickers, Opera Star Known for His Raw Power and Intensity, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Vickers brought a colossal voice to legendary portrayals of Wagner’s Tristan, Verdi’s Otello, Beethoven’s Florestan and Britten’s Peter Grimes.

name: Roy C. Bennett
headline: Roy C. Bennett, Part of Midcentury Songwriting Duo, Dies at 96
abstract: With his partner, Sid Tepper, Mr. Bennett wrote “Red Roses for a Blue Lady” and “Kiss of Fire.”

name: Roy Bennett
profession: White Zimbabwean With Black Political Base
headline: Roy Bennett, White Zimbabwean With Black Political Base, Dies in U.S. Helicopter Crash
abstract: Mr. Bennett, 60, was a coffee grower whose farm was seized as part of the land redistribution program of Robert G. Mugabe. He was a formidable leader of Zimbabwe’s main opposition party.

name: Charles Winick
headline: Charles Winick, Author Who Challenged Views on Drugs and Gender, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Winick, a professor of anthropology and sociology, was known for his research into the blurring of lines between the sexes and for his controversial views on drug addiction.

name: Satoru Iwata
headline: Satoru Iwata, Nintendo Chief Executive, Dies at 55
abstract: Under Mr. Iwata’s watch, Nintendo surged ahead of rival game companies with the release of the Nintendo DS, a hand-held system, and the popular Wii home console.

name: Christian Audigier
headline: Christian Audigier, Fashion Designer, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Audigier licensed the designs of Don Ed Hardy, a once obscure tattoo artist, and put tattoo prints of skulls, tigers, roses and other images on clothes and a wide variety of licensed products.

name: Michael Masser
headline: Michael Masser, Composer Who Wrote Whitney Houston Hits, Dies at 74
abstract: After leaving a career as a stockbroker, Mr. Masser wrote songs recorded by Ms. Houston, Diana Ross, Roberta Flack and many other star vocalists.

name: D’Army Bailey
headline: D’Army Bailey, 73, Activist Who Founded Museum Where Dr. King Was Shot, Dies
abstract: Mr. Bailey campaigned to transform the Lorraine Motel in Memphis, site of the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.’s assassination, into a civil rights museum.

name: Joan Sebastian
headline: Joan Sebastian, Mexican Singer and Songwriter, Is Dead at 64
abstract: Mr. Sebastian, who won four Grammy Awards and seven Latin Grammys, was nicknamed the People’s Poet and King of the Mexican Rodeo.

name: David Aronson
headline: David Aronson, Expressionist Artist, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Aronson, who had an Orthodox Jewish upbringing, made vivid paintings, charcoal drawings and sculptures that animated Old and New Testament allegories to convey universal human emotions.

name: Marlene Sanders
headline: Marlene Sanders, Pathbreaking TV Journalist, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Sanders compiled a stellar résumé as a reporter in the field, including Vietnam, and was an Emmy-winning writer and producer of documentaries.

name: Robert Broadbent
profession: Force Behind Rock Hall of Fame
headline: Robert Broadbent, Force Behind Rock Hall of Fame, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Broadbent, a retail executive, joined a group that lobbied for making Cleveland the site of the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and Museum.

name: David M. Raup
headline: David M. Raup, Who Transformed Field of Paleontology, Dies at 82
abstract: Viewed as a singular thinker, Dr. Raup challenged accepted tenets by raising ambitious questions about extinction patterns and biodiversity.

name: Hans H. Angermueller
profession: Banker Helped Free U.S. Hostages in Iran
headline: Hans H. Angermueller, 90, Dies; Banker Helped Free U.S. Hostages in Iran
abstract: Mr. Angermueller, a Citicorp executive in the 1970s and ’80s who was on the short list for the chief position, worked to devise a financial deal that helped free Americans held in Iran.

name: Wan Li
profession: Helped Chinas Farmers Emerge From Mao Era
headline: Wan Li, Who Helped China’s Farmers Emerge From Mao Era, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Wan, a party secretary in a rural province, instituted agricultural reforms adopted throughout China after discovering that people were starving.

name: Ettore Stratta
headline: Ettore Stratta, Music Producer and Conductor, Dies at 82
abstract: Classically trained, Mr. Stratta was known for crossing genres in his work.

name: Gary Mack
headline: Gary Mack, Kennedy Assassination Expert, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Mack was a Dallas broadcaster whose fascination with the event led him to become a widely consulted expert on the subject.

name: William Diamond
headline: William Diamond, Designer of Wildly Colored Interiors, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Diamond, with his design partner Anthony Baratta, created vividly hued rooms that married antiques and contemporary pieces; their creations were often featured in home design magazines.

name: Bill Arnsparger
headline: Bill Arnsparger, Architect of Feared Dolphins Defenses, Dies at 88
abstract: Arnsparger led N.F.L. defensive units to six Super Bowls, but his New York teams struggled.

name: Yoichiro Nambu
headline: Yoichiro Nambu, Nobel-Winning Physicist, Dies at 94
abstract: Professor Nambu contributed to the prediction of the Higgs boson, or “God particle.”

name: Helen F. Holt
profession: Elevated Elder Care Across the U.S
headline: Helen F. Holt, Who Elevated Elder Care Across the U.S., Dies at 101
abstract: Ms. Holt led the federal government’s effort to establish and standardize modern long-term care facilities for the elderly in the pre-Medicare era.

name: Lezly Ziering
headline: Lezly Ziering, Dancer Who Rescued Roller-Skating in Central Park, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Ziering, a professional dancer who reinvented himself as a skate dancer, was best known for his fight in keeping skating alive in Central Park.

name: Philipp Missfelder
headline: Philipp Missfelder, Rising Politician in Germany, Dies at 35
abstract: Mr. Missfelder, foreign affairs spokesman for the governing Christian Democrats, was known for his commitment to the trans-Atlantic partnership and to Israel.

name: Alex Rocco
profession: Played Moe Greene in The Godfather
headline: Alex Rocco, Who Played Moe Greene in ‘The Godfather,’ Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Rocco played Moe Greene, the cocky, bespectacled Las Vegas casino owner who made the mistake of talking back to Michael Corleone in the 1972 film.

name: Claudia Alexander
headline: Claudia Alexander, NASA Manager Who Led Jupiter Mission, Dies at 56
abstract: Dr. Alexander, who played a pioneering role in NASA’s Galileo mission to Jupiter, also served as a project scientist on the international Rosetta space-exploration project.

name: Buddy Buie
headline: Buddy Buie, Producer and Hit-Making Songwriter, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Buie helped propel the Classics IV and the Atlanta Rhythm Section to pop prominence with melodic soft-rock hits including “Spooky” and “So Into You.”

name: Robert Spillane
headline: Robert Spillane, Who Retooled Boston’s Schools, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Spillane helped revive Boston’s troubled schools as superintendent in the 1980s and went on to become a leading national education innovator.

name: Theodore Bikel
headline: Theodore Bikel, Master of Versatility in Songs, Roles and Activism, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Bikel sang in 21 languages, from medieval Spanish to Zulu, in addition to his roles in theater, television and films.

name: Richard Leone
profession: Port Authority Chairman and Force in N.J. Politics
headline: Richard Leone, 75, Dies; Port Authority Chairman and Force in N.J. Politics
abstract: Mr. Leone, who was the youngest state treasurer for New Jersey at 33, served as president of the Twentieth Century from 1989 to 2011 and worked for progressive policy changes.

name: E. L. Doctorow
profession: Literary Time Traveler Stirred Past Into Fiction
headline: E. L. Doctorow Dies at 84; Literary Time Traveler Stirred Past Into Fiction
abstract: Mr. Doctorow’s popular, critically admired and award-winning novels, including “Ragtime,” “Billy Bathgate” and “The March,” situated fictional characters in recognizable historical contexts.

name: Elio Fiorucci
profession: Disco-Era Temple of Fashion Changed Retail
headline: Elio Fiorucci, Whose Disco-Era Temple of Fashion Changed Retail, Dies at 80
abstract: Restlessly inventive, Mr. Fiorucci’s stores in Milan, London and New York anticipated many later innovations.

name: Paul Gebhard
headline: Paul Gebhard, Sex Researcher Who Worked With Kinsey, Dies at 98
abstract: Dr. Gebhard, who trained as an anthropologist, wrote the groundbreaking “Sexual Behavior in the Human Female” with Dr. Alfred C. Kinsey in 1953.

name: Patricia Crone
headline: Patricia Crone, Questioning Scholar of Islamic History, Dies at 70
abstract: Professor Crone challenged conventional views of the roots and evolution of Islam and her numerous books and articles shed new light on the history of the religion.

name: Vera Stern
headline: Vera Stern, Arts Advocate Who Helped Save Carnegie Hall, Dies at 88
abstract: Mrs. Stern, who once served as the president for the America-Israel Cultural Foundation, is remembered for having been the behind-the-scenes force that helped save Carnegie Hall from demolition.

name: U Aung Thaung
headline: U Aung Thaung, Burmese Politician Accused of Abuses, Dies at 74
abstract: He was the industry minister from 1997 to 2011, a position that he was said to have manipulated to financially benefit himself, his family and aides.

name: Owen Chadwick
headline: Owen Chadwick, Eminent Historian of Christianity, Dies at 99
abstract: “The Reformation” (1964), one of two volumes Professor Chadwick wrote for The Penguin History of the Church, was required reading in colleges for decades.

name: Nova Pilbeam
profession: Early but Brief Star for Hitchcock
headline: Nova Pilbeam, an Early but Brief Star for Hitchcock, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Pilbeam’s career was highlighted by her work as a teenager in Hitchcock thrillers in the 1930s.

name: Rosanne Klass
profession: Writer and Advocate for the Afghan People
headline: Rosanne Klass, Writer and Advocate for the Afghan People, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Klass, a writer and human rights advocate, taught English in rural Afghan schools and later became the director of the Afghanistan Information Center.

name: Chenjerai Hove
headline: Chenjerai Hove, Chronicler of Zimbabwean Struggles, Dies at 59
abstract: The plight of Mr. Hove’s home country comes through in his poems and novels.

name: Arvid Anderson
profession: New York Citys First Collective Bargaining Chief
headline: Arvid Anderson, New York City’s First Collective Bargaining Chief, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Anderson, a low-key Midwesterner, resolved volatile contract disputes calmly and methodically as chairman of the city’s collective bargaining board under three mayors.

name: Yasuo Minagawa
headline: Yasuo Minagawa, a Master Framer for Exacting Artists, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Minagawa, born in Tokyo, left Japan for Paris in pursuit of new developments in art and music and eventually settled in New York.

name: Sally Gross
headline: Sally Gross, Choreographer of Minimalist Dances, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Gross, whose work was the subject of an Albert Maysles documentary, favored repeated movements drawn from daily life.

name: George Coe
profession: Actor and Director of a Bergman Parody
headline: George Coe, Actor and Director of a Bergman Parody, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Coe was also a grown-up presence in the cast of “Saturday Night Live,” appearing in the very first episode.

name: Ingrid Sischy
headline: Ingrid Sischy, Doyenne of Art and Fashion, Dies at 63
abstract: In a career spanning 40 years, she brought artists like Joseph Beuys and designers like Miuccia Prada to the pages of Artforum, Interview magazine, Vanity Fair and others.

name: Howard Rumsey
profession: Musician Invigorated West Coast Jazz Scene
headline: Howard Rumsey, 97, Dies; Musician Invigorated West Coast Jazz Scene
abstract: As leader of the Lighthouse All-Stars in Hermosa Beach, Calif., Mr. Rumsey helped popularize the notion of a progressive West Coast jazz scene in the 1950s.

name: Bobbi Kristina Brown
headline: Bobbi Kristina Brown, Daughter of Whitney Houston, Dies at 22
abstract: Ms. Brown, who was found unconscious in a bathtub in her townhouse on Jan. 31 and placed into a medically induced coma, had been in hospice care since late June.

name: Peg Lynch
profession: Writer and Star of Early Situation Comedy
headline: Peg Lynch, Writer and Star of Early Situation Comedy, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Lynch was a pioneering woman in broadcast entertainment, writing nearly 11,000 scripts, creating original characters and performing her own written work.

name: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
headline: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam, Ex-President Who Pushed a Nuclear India, Dies at 83
abstract: Nicknamed “the Missile Man of India,” Dr. Kalam was one of his country’s most beloved figures for his role in advancing its nuclear program.

name: Shigeko Kubota
headline: Shigeko Kubota, a Creator of Video Sculptures, Dies at 77
abstract: A central figure in the anti-art Fluxus movement, Ms. Kubota integrated her videos physically and conceptually into works of sculpture.

name: Don Oberdorfer
profession: Top Diplomatic Reporter for Washington Post
headline: Don Oberdorfer, 84, Top Diplomatic Reporter for Washington Post, Dies
abstract: Mr. Oberdorfer, who also wrote books on Korea and the Cold War, covered stories from Vietnam to the fall of the Soviet Union with a firm grasp of foreign policy issues.

name: Ann Rule
headline: Ann Rule, 83, Dies: Wrote About Ted Bundy (a Friend) and Other Killers
abstract: Ms. Rule’s first book, “The Stranger Beside Me,” the 1980 study of the serial killer Ted Bundy, became an instant top seller.

name: Vic Firth
headline: Vic Firth, Who Gave Drummers Their Sticks, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Firth spent more than 40 years as the principal tympanist of the Boston Symphony Orchestra, and a company with his name now turns out some 12 million drumsticks and mallets annually.

name: Samuel Pisar
profession: Lawyer and Adviser Survived Nazi Camps
headline: Samuel Pisar Dies at 86; Lawyer and Adviser Survived Nazi Camps
abstract: Mr. Pisar survived the Holocaust to create a life of accomplishment, including becoming an adviser to John F. Kennedy, whom he met at Harvard, and as a lawyer to corporate executives and movie stars.

name: Van Alexander
headline: Van Alexander, Composer of ‘A-Tisket, A-Tasket,’ Dies at 100
abstract: The composer and arranger, whose adaptation of a nursery rhyme became Ella Fitzgerald’s breakout hit, also wrote for movies and television.

name: Jules Hirsch
headline: Jules Hirsch, Pioneer in Obesity Studies, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Dr. Hirsch found evidence that weight is at least partly determined by the body’s own processes.

name: Henry B. Platt
headline: Henry B. Platt, Scion Who Gave Tiffany Sparkle, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Platt, the great-great-grandson of Tiffany & Company’s founder, helped steer the business for 34 years and named two newly discovered gemstones.

name: Mullah Muhammad Omar
headline: Mullah Muhammad Omar, Enigmatic Leader of Afghan Taliban, Is Dead
abstract: The Afghan mullah kept his grip on power through cunning and ruthlessness, but was toppled by the United States when he refused to hand over Osama bin Laden.

name: Vasily Pichul
profession: Skewered Soviet Life in Little Vera
headline: Vasily Pichul, Director, Dies at 54; Skewered Soviet Life in ‘Little Vera’
abstract: Mr. Pichul’s 1988 film, written by his wife, captured international attention.

name: Ivan Moravec
headline: Ivan Moravec, Pianist, Dies at 84; His Music Penetrated Iron Curtain
abstract: Mr. Moravec was a renowned interpreter of Chopin, heard largely through recordings.

name: Richard D. Bass
headline: Richard D. Bass, Ski Resort Developer Who Climbed Tallest Peaks, Dies at 85
abstract: A book about the Texas rancher’s climbs and its attendant publicity were often given credit, and blame, for a flood of amateur attempts on Mount Everest.

name: Mike Pyle
profession: Captain of 9-0 Yale Team and Champion Bears in 63
headline: Mike Pyle, Captain of 9-0 Yale Team and Champion Bears in ’63, Dies at 76
abstract: Pyle was among the many former N.F.L. players who brought suit against the league for disregarding cognitive dangers resulting from football collisions.

name: Billy Pierce
profession: White Sox Power Pitcher in the 1950s
headline: Billy Pierce, White Sox Power Pitcher in the 1950s, Dies at 88
abstract: Pierce, a Chicago White Sox left-hander with a blazing fastball, became one of baseball’s leading pitchers of the 1950s.

name: Howard W. Jones Jr.
headline: Howard W. Jones Jr., a Pioneer of Reproductive Medicine, Dies at 104
abstract: Dr. Jones opened the first sex-change clinic in an American hospital and helped achieve the first birth through in vitro fertilization in the United States.

name: Jerome Kohlberg Jr.
profession: Pioneer of the Private Equity Industry
headline: Jerome Kohlberg Jr., Pioneer of the Private Equity Industry, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Kohlberg, who founded K.K.R., shunned hard-edged tactics, focusing on smaller, friendly deals.

name: Lynn Anderson
headline: Lynn Anderson, Singer of ‘Rose Garden,’ Dies at 67
abstract: Ms. Anderson recorded her signature song, “(I Never Promised You a) Rose Garden,” on a fluke.

name: Roddy Piper
headline: Roddy Piper, a Master Villain of Professional Wrestling, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Piper helped raise the profile of World Wrestling Entertainment and was a foil to Hulk Hogan in the 1980s.

name: Aja Zanova
headline: Aja Zanova, Top Czech Skater Who Defected to West, Dies at 84
abstract: Zanova was a world champion figure skater whose defection from Czechoslovakia as a teenager in 1950 made headlines around the world.

name: James Jude
headline: Dr. James Jude, Who Helped Develop Use of CPR, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Jude was a resident at Johns Hopkins University School of Medicine when he recognized that external manual pressure could revive a stalled heart, a discovery that led to the widespread use of CPR.

name: Buddy Emmons
headline: Buddy Emmons, Virtuoso of the Steel Guitar, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Emmons, an in-demand and influential performer, was also responsible for the evolution of his instrument.

name: Jerry Berrigan
headline: Jerry Berrigan, a Catholic Peace Activist, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Berrigan was arrested so many times, for protesting the Vietnam War and other conflicts, that he lost count.

name: Robin Phillips
headline: Robin Phillips, Director, Dies at 75; Revitalized Canada’s Stratford Festival
abstract: Mr. Phillips, a British theater director, added productions and brought in stars like Maggie Smith during his tenure as artistic director in the ’70s.

name: Donald L. Rasmussen
headline: Dr. Donald L. Rasmussen, Crusader for Coal Miners’ Health, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Rasmussen set off a grass-roots movement that reduced the spread of black lung disease and enhanced the treatment of afflicted workers.

name: John Gibbons
headline: John Gibbons, 86, Clinton Science Aide, Dies; Pushed Cooperation in Space
abstract: Mr. Gibbons argued for more efficient cars, a nuclear test ban and global cooperation in space while serving as a longtime science adviser to Congress and President Bill Clinton.

name: John Gibbons
profession: Argued for Rights for Guantánamo Detainees
headline: John Gibbons Dies at 94; Argued for Rights for Guantánamo Detainees
abstract: As a lawyer, he put his faith in equal access to the courts for all, including rioters in Newark in the 1960s; he also served as a federal appellate judge.

name: Forrest Bird
profession: Inventor of Medical Respirators and Ventilators
headline: Dr. Forrest Bird, Inventor of Medical Respirators and Ventilators, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Bird, who built his first prototype from shortcake tins and a doorknob in 1953, developed four generations of widely used cardiopulmonary devices.

name: Richard S. Schweiker
headline: Richard S. Schweiker, Former Senator and Reagan Confidant, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Schweiker, a Pennsylvania Republican, served for two decades in Congress and two more years in the White House in an era of assassinations, war and sweeping social changes.

name: Vincent Marotta Sr.
headline: Vincent Marotta Sr., a Creator of Mr. Coffee, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Marotta, who once played football professionally and signed with an M.L.B. team, created a coffee maker that knocked the percolator from its perch.

name: John Leslie Munro
profession: Last of the World War II Dambuster Pilots
headline: John Leslie Munro, Last of the World War II ‘Dambuster’ Pilots, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Munro, a New Zealander, took part in raids on heavily fortified dams in Germany in 1943, using bombs that bounced on the water before exploding.

name: Arnold Scaasi
profession: Dressed Stars and Socialites, His Scaasi Girls
headline: Arnold Scaasi Dies at 85; Dressed Stars and Socialites, His ‘Scaasi Girls’
abstract: Mr. Scaasi was known for bringing the techniques of the French couture to prominent American women, including first ladies, socialites and Hollywood stars.

name: Robert Conquest
headline: Robert Conquest, Historian Who Documented Soviet Horrors, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Conquest chronicled the Stalinist purges and the Ukrainian famine of the 1930s with original findings and gripping narratives.

name: Cilla Black
profession: Top Pop Star in Swinging Sixties Britain
headline: Cilla Black, Top Pop Star in Swinging Sixties Britain, Dies at 72
abstract: Ms. Black, who was closely associated with the Beatles, was considered a national treasure in Britain, a working-class girl who made good.

name: Alan Cheuse
profession: Late-Blooming Author and NPR Book Critic
headline: Alan Cheuse, Late-Blooming Author and NPR Book Critic, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Cheuse, a late-blooming author, assimilated his wide range of experiences to give authentic first-person voices to his characters.

name: Charles Goldstein
headline: Charles Goldstein, Lawyer Who Helped Find Looted Art, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Goldstein was a high-stakes New York real estate lawyer who transformed himself into a tenacious advocate for recovering art stolen from Holocaust victims.

name: Bob Timmons
headline: Bob Timmons, 91, a Demanding Coach Who Developed a Star Runner, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Timmons, whose most famous athlete was the Olympian and world-record holder Jim Ryun, enjoyed great success in more than two decades at the University of Kansas.

name: Louis Sokoloff
headline: Louis Sokoloff, Pioneer of PET Scan, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Sokoloff won the Albert Lasker Clinical Medical Research Award in 1981 for his role in developing the vivid color images that map brain function.

name: Johanna Quandt
headline: Johanna Quandt, Matriarch of Family That Controls BMW, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Quandt, who ranked 77th on Forbes magazine’s 2015 list of the world’s richest people, owned a 16.7 percent stake in the automaker and once served as its deputy chairwoman.

name: Jemera Rone
headline: Jemera Rone, Investigator Who Bared Human Rights Abuses, Dies at 71
abstract: Ms. Rone left a legal career on Wall Street to focus on exposing and seeking justice for human rights violations in El Salvador and Sudan.

name: George Cole
profession: Played a Young Scrooge in 51 Film
headline: George Cole, 90, British TV Star, Dies; Played a Young Scrooge in ’51 Film
abstract: Mr. Cole, who was mentored by Alastair Sim, played a young Scrooge in 1951, then went on to gain fame for his role in “Minder,” an ITV series.

name: Carol Brown Janeway
headline: Carol Brown Janeway, Translator and Executive, Dies at 71
abstract: Ms. Janeway published Nobel laureates and translated books for Knopf.

name: Frances Oldham Kelsey
headline: Frances Oldham Kelsey, Who Saved U.S. Babies From Thalidomide, Dies at 101
abstract: Dr. Kelsey became a 20th-century American heroine for sparing the United States from widespread birth deformities, and for inspiring laws that made drugs safer.

name: Coleen Gray
headline: Coleen Gray, Who Played Film Noir Naïfs, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Gray’s films included “The Killing,” “Kiss of Death,” “Nightmare Alley” and “Red River.”

name: Louise Suggs
profession: Helped Found the Womens Pro Tour
headline: Louise Suggs, Golf Pioneer, Dies at 91; Helped Found the Women’s Pro Tour
abstract: Born in Georgia, Suggs turned professional in 1948, the same year she was the reigning United States and British amateur champion.

name: Manuel Contreras
headline: Manuel Contreras, Chilean Spy Chief Under Pinochet, Dies at 86
abstract: Gen. Contreras, Chile’s intelligence chief during the dictatorship of Gen. Augusto Pinochet, was serving 526 years of multiple prison terms for human rights violations.

name: Douglas LeVien
headline: Douglas LeVien, New York Detective Who Infiltrated the Mafia, Dies at 68
abstract: An expert on organized crime, Detective LeVien was a 20-year veteran of the New York Police Department.

name: Benton Becker
headline: Benton Becker, Ford Aide, Dies at 77; Negotiated Nixon Pardon
abstract: Mr. Becker pushed for an acknowledgment of guilt from Richard M. Nixon and sought to keep records out of the hands of the disgraced president after his resignation.

name: Frank Gifford
profession: Star for Giants and in the Broadcast Booth
headline: Frank Gifford, Star for Giants and in the Broadcast Booth, Dies at 84
abstract: Gifford was a Hall of Fame running back and receiver who personified the Giants’ glory years of the late 1950s and early ’60s and then became a mainstay on television.

name: Tyler Drumheller
headline: Tyler Drumheller, Ex-C.I.A. Official Who Disputed Bush, Dies at 63
abstract: After his retirement, Mr. Drumheller said publicly that the Bush administration had knowingly hyped fabricated evidence of Iraqi weapons to justify the 2003 invasion.

name: Carolyn Kaelin
headline: Carolyn Kaelin, Breast Cancer Surgeon, Patient Advocate and Patient, Dies at 54
abstract: In addition to running a breast health center, Dr. Kaelin performed surgery and did research on breast cancer patients’ quality of life during and after treatment.

name: Sean Price
headline: Sean Price, Rapper With Deep Brooklyn Roots, Dies at 43
abstract: In the mid-1990s, under the name Ruck, Mr. Price was part of the duo Heltah Skeltah, which in turn was part of the extended Brooklyn crew Boot Camp Clik.

name: Gus Mortson
profession: Scrappy All-Star for Toronto N.H.L. Champions
headline: Gus Mortson, Scrappy All-Star for Toronto N.H.L. Champions, Dies at 90
abstract: Mortson teamed with Jim Thomson in a Maple Leafs pairing that was among the league’s toughest.

name: Billy Sherrill
headline: Billy Sherrill, Producer, Dies at 78; Promoted a ‘Countrypolitan’ Sound
abstract: Mr. Sherrill helped kick-start the career of Tammy Wynette, breathed new life into a declining George Jones and helped infuse country music with the spirit of 1960s pop.

name: David Nobbs
profession: Novelist and Creator of Reginald Perrin
headline: David Nobbs, Novelist and Creator of Reginald Perrin, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Nobbs, a British novelist and comedy writer, was best known for “The Fall and Rise of Reginald Perrin,” the dark BBC sitcom of the 1970s.

name: John Riggi
headline: John Riggi, Who Led New Jersey Crime Family, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Riggi was chief of the DeCavalcante family, New Jersey’s only indigenous mob group, but not, as some said, an inspiration for “The Sopranos.”

name: Ann McGovern
profession: She Made Stone Soup a School Staple
headline: Ann McGovern, Author, Is Dead at 85; She Made ‘Stone Soup’ a School Staple
abstract: Ms. McGovern, who worked at Little Golden Books and Scholastic, broke into children’s literature by writing about Roy Rogers after overhearing an editor wishing someone would write one.

name: J. Wallace LaPrade
headline: J. Wallace LaPrade, New York F.B.I. Chief in ’70s, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. LaPrade was fired as head of the New York bureau after being threatened with prosecution for refusing to cooperate with an investigation of illegal F.B.I. break-ins.

name: Fred Otnes
headline: Fred Otnes, Illustrator and Collage Artist, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Otnes, known for images he made for magazines, movie posters and postage stamps, embraced abstraction well before most other commercial illustrators.

name: John A. Nerud
headline: John A. Nerud, Hall of Fame Thoroughbred Trainer, Dies at 102
abstract: Nerud saddled more than 1,000 winners, including 27 in stakes races, and named his greatest horse, Dr. Fager, after the neurosurgeon who saved his life.

name: Biff Liff
headline: Biff Liff, Broadway Manager and Powerhouse Agent, Dies at 96
abstract: After making his mark backstage on shows like “My Fair Lady,” Mr. Liff became an agent whose clients included Julie Andrews, Angela Lansbury and Chita Rivera.

name: Richard S. Ross
profession: Johns Hopkins Dean and Watergate Walk-On
headline: Richard S. Ross, Johns Hopkins Dean and Watergate Walk-On, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Ross pushed for broader education for prospective doctors and earlier helped assess Richard M. Nixon’s health during the Watergate investigation.

name: Edward Thomas
headline: Edward Thomas, Policing Pioneer Who Wore a Burden Stoically, Dies at 95
abstract: The first African-American to build a career with the Houston Police Department could not walk through the front door when he reported for work in 1948. Now Police Headquarters is named for him.

name: Jerome G. Miller
profession: Emptied Reformatories to Better Juvenile Justice
headline: Jerome G. Miller, 83, Dies; Emptied Reformatories to Better Juvenile Justice
abstract: ‘What do we do with these bad kids’ became ‘What do we do with these bad institutions?’

name: Susan Newhouse
headline: Susan Newhouse, Who Guided Fresh Air Fund, Dies at 80
abstract: Mrs. Newhouse was the longtime chairwoman of the Fresh Air Fund, which pays for poor children from New York City to go summer camp upstate or to stay with host families in rural and suburban areas.

name: Bernard d’Espagnat
headline: Bernard d’Espagnat, 93, Physicist, Dies; Sought Implications of Quantum Theory
abstract: Dr. d’Espagnat was one of a handful of scientists in the 1960s and ’70s who urged their colleagues to look into the deeper meaning of quantum mechanics.

name: Julian Bond
headline: Julian Bond, Charismatic Civil Rights Leader, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Bond was also a lightning rod of the anti-Vietnam War campaign and a former chairman of the N.A.A.C.P.

name: Hamid Gul
profession: Backed Militants in Leading Pakistan Spy Agency
headline: Hamid Gul, 78, Dies; Backed Militants in Leading Pakistan Spy Agency
abstract: Mr. Gul, a three-star general, was deeply involved in the country’s policy toward neighboring Afghanistan during the Soviet withdrawal.

name: Warren Braren
profession: Urged Ban on Broadcast Tobacco Ads
headline: Warren Braren, 82, Dies; Urged Ban on Broadcast Tobacco Ads
abstract: Testifying before Congress, Mr. Braren, a reformed smoker, blew the whistle on broadcasters’ lax self-regulation on tobacco advertising.

name: Bob Johnston
profession: Produced Bob Dylan and Johnny Cash Albums
headline: Bob Johnston, 83, Dies; Produced Bob Dylan and Johnny Cash Albums
abstract: Mr. Johnston was behind “Blonde on Blonde,” “At Folsom Prison” and some classic albums by Simon and Garfunkel.

name: Rogelio Livieres Plano
headline: Rogelio Livieres Plano, Bishop Ousted by Pope Francis, Dies at 69
abstract: Bishop Livieres, a conservative clergyman in Paraguay, sheltered a priest accused of molestation and made him vicar general, responsible for handling accusations of sexual abuse.

name: Howard Brody
profession: Expert in the Physics of Tennis
headline: Howard Brody, an Expert in the Physics of Tennis, Dies at 83
abstract: Professor Brody began his professional life as a particle physicist before a chance encounter in the 1970s caused him to train his eye on tennis.

name: Melva Bucksbaum
headline: Melva Bucksbaum, Art Collector and Curator, Dies at 82
abstract: One of the country’s leading collectors, Ms. Bucksbaum was a Whitney trustee and established the Bucksbaum Award, which grants an artist $100,000 and an invitation to exhibit at the museum.

name: Tony Gleaton
headline: Tony Gleaton, 67, Dies, Leaving Legacy in Pictures of Africans in the Americas
abstract: Mr. Gleaton traveled light, by bus, without assistants, complex equipment or luxury lodgings, to document the lives of black cowboys and create images of the African diaspora in Latin America.

name: Bud Yorkin
profession: Writer and Producer of All in the Family
headline: Bud Yorkin, Writer and Producer of ‘All in the Family,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Yorkin and his partner, Norman Lear, followed “All in the Family” with hits including “The Jeffersons,” “Sanford and Son” and “Maude.”

name: Yvonne Craig
headline: Yvonne Craig, Actress Who Played Batgirl, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Ms. Craig added a scrappy girl-power element to the campy hit 1960s TV series “Batman.”

name: Louis Stokes
profession: Congressman From Ohio and Champion of the Poor
headline: Louis Stokes, Congressman From Ohio and Champion of the Poor, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Stokes, a Democrat, served in the House for 30 years, and led a special investigation into the assassinations of President John F. Kennedy and the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr.

name: William Jay Smith
headline: William Jay Smith, Poet and Craftsman of Rhythm, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Smith, whose work was praised for its lyrical diction and deceptive simplicity, was the author of many volumes of poems, as well as criticism, memoirs, translations and children’s verse.

name: John Henry Holland
headline: John Henry Holland, Who Computerized Evolution, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Holland developed computer codes, which he called genetic algorithms, that mimicked evolutionary processes by mating and mutating possible solutions.

name: Egon Bahr
headline: Egon Bahr, Who Laid Groundwork for German Reunification, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Bahr, an architect of Ostpolitik, West Germany’s Cold War policy of rapprochement, believed the best way to narrow Germany’s division was through negotiations.

name: George Houser
profession: Freedom Rides Pioneer and a Founder of CORE
headline: George Houser, Freedom Rides Pioneer and a Founder of CORE, Dies at 99
abstract: The Rev. Houser was a Methodist minister whose contributions to the civil rights movement went largely unheralded.

name: Frederick Payne
profession: Decorated Fighter Ace in the Pacific
headline: Frederick Payne, Decorated Fighter Ace in the Pacific, Dies at 104
abstract: Mr. Payne, a retired Marine Corps brigadier general, received the Navy Cross and other awards as World War II fighter ace in the Pacific.

name: Karen Stives
headline: Karen Stives, Acclaimed Olympic Equestrian, Dies at 64
abstract: Ms. Stives, riding Ben Arthur, won an individual silver medal and led the American team to a gold medal in three-day eventing at the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics.

name: Jacob Bekenstein
headline: Jacob Bekenstein, Physicist Who Revolutionized Theory of Black Holes, Dies at 68
abstract: Dr. Bekenstein, whose proposition on entropy and space eventually won over a skeptical Stephen Hawking, was considered one of the few giants in the study of quantum gravity.

name: John Correnti
headline: John Correnti, Steel Industry Executive, Dies at 68
abstract: At various times in his life, Mr. Correnti led Nucor, Big River Steel, Birmingham Steel and Severstal Columbus — and built steel mills from scratch, embracing new technologies.

name: Sasha Petraske
profession: Bar Owner Restored Luster to Cocktail Culture
headline: Sasha Petraske, 42, Dies; Bar Owner Restored Luster to Cocktail Culture
abstract: The founder of the influential New York cocktail bar Milk & Honey was found dead on Friday.

name: Liz Perle
headline: Liz Perle, Writer and Former Publishing Executive, Dies at 59
abstract: Ms. Perle was co-founder of Common Sense Media, a nonprofit that helps children engage with the digital world responsibly.

name: Ieng Thirith
headline: Ieng Thirith, Khmer Rouge Minister in Cambodia, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Ieng Thirith, the most powerful woman in a brutal regime and Pol Pot’s sister-in-law, was found unfit for trial in 2012 because of dementia.

name: Svetlana Boym
headline: Svetlana Boym, 56, Scholar of Myth and Memory, Dies
abstract: Ms. Boym, a Harvard professor who emigrated from the Soviet Union in her 20s, wrote of two types of nostalgia, one that clings to the past and another that realizes it is gone.

name: Doudou N’diaye Rose
headline: Doudou N’diaye Rose, 85, Senegalese Drummer and ‘Human Treasure,’ Dies
abstract: Mr. Rose became an emissary of his native culture’s joyous and complex rhythms, touring with percussion orchestras in Europe, Asia and the United States.

name: Merl Reagle
headline: Merl Reagle, Whose Crossword Puzzles Delighted Clued-In Solvers, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Reagle contributed devilishly inventive puzzles to numerous publications, relishing his roles as a wisecracker, provocateur and tease.

name: Cynthia Macdonald
profession: Poet Known for Humor and Ability to Shock
headline: Cynthia Macdonald, Poet Known for Humor and Ability to Shock, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Macdonald’s idiosyncratic blend of humor and the grotesque made her a distinctive voice on the American poetry scene.

name: Anna Kashfi
headline: Anna Kashfi, Actress Who Was Brando’s First Wife, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Kashfi, whose background was much disputed, was married to Brando for just two years and was the mother of their son, Christian.

name: Augusta Chiwy
headline: Augusta Chiwy, ‘Forgotten’ Wartime Nurse, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Chiwy, a Belgian nurse, was not recognized until 2011 for her bravery in saving countless American soldiers wounded in the Battle of the Bulge.

name: Joseph F. Traub
headline: Joseph F. Traub, 83, Dies; Early Advocate for Computer Science
abstract: Mr. Traub, who founded the computer science department at Columbia, helped the emerging academic discipline garner respectability and resources.

name: Marcy Borders
headline: Marcy Borders, ‘Dust Lady’ Who Survived 9/11, Dies at 42
abstract: Ms. Borders became known as the “dust lady” from a defining photograph of her covered in ash and grime on Sept. 11, 2001.

name: Frank E. Petersen
headline: Frank E. Petersen, First Black General in Marines, Dies at 83
abstract: He overcame bruising racial indignities to forge a long and distinguished career in the military, retiring as a three-star lieutenant general.

name: Amelia Boynton Robinson
profession: Pivotal Figure at the Selma March
headline: Amelia Boynton Robinson, a Pivotal Figure at the Selma March, Dies at 104
abstract: Images of Mrs. Boynton Robinson being left for dead by the police during the march in 1965 were seen worldwide and played a part in winning popular support for the Voting Rights Act.

name: Francis Sejersted
profession: Steered Nobel Peace Prize Into Controversy
headline: Francis Sejersted, 79, Dies; Steered Nobel Peace Prize Into Controversy
abstract: Mr. Sejersted led a committee that angered many by giving the awards to Shimon Peres, Yitzhak Rabin and Yasir Arafat, and to F. W. de Klerk and Nelson Mandela.

name: James H. Duke Jr.
headline: Dr. James H. Duke Jr., Texas Trauma Surgeon, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Duke was famous for his health reports on NBC and for having attended to President Kennedy and Gov. John Connally in Dallas after the deadly shooting in 1963.

name: James Duke
headline: James Duke, 88, Globe-Trotting Authority on Healing Plants, Is Dead
abstract: As a scholar and government researcher, he did field work in remote spots, finding indigenous remedies, trying them himself and pouring them into books.

name: Melody Patterson
headline: Melody Patterson, Wrangler Jane on ‘F Troop,’ Dies at 66
abstract: The actress played the scrappy postmistress and storekeeper at a military fort in the Old West staffed by bumblers.

name: Darryl Dawkins
profession: Lovable N.B.A. Figure and Fierce Dunker
headline: Darryl Dawkins, Lovable N.B.A. Figure and Fierce Dunker, Dies at 58
abstract: Dawkins arrived in professional basketball as a gigantic teenager and became one of the game’s fiercest dunkers and most notoriously lovable characters.

name: Al Arbour
headline: Al Arbour, Coach of Islanders’ 1980s Dynasty, Dies at 82
abstract: Arbour, who played in the N.H.L. as a defenseman, took over the Islanders in 1973, after they lost 60 games, and led them to four consecutive Stanley Cup titles, from 1980 to 1983.

name: Ruth Sivard
headline: Ruth Sivard, Economist Who Scrutinized Military Spending, Dies at 99
abstract: Ms. Sivard drew attention to the disparity between social and military spending for more than three decades.

name: Paul Royle
profession: Fled Nazis in a Great Escape
headline: Paul Royle, Who Fled Nazis in a ‘Great Escape,’ Dies at 101
abstract: Paul Royle briefly escaped from Stalag Luft III in 1944 with 75 other Allied soldiers, an episode that inspired the 1963 Steve McQueen movie “The Great Escape.”

name: Johan Renvall
headline: Johan Renvall, American Ballet Theater Principal, Dies at 55
abstract: Born in Stockholm, Mr. Renvall was a figure-skating champion before joining the Royal Swedish Ballet at the age of 18.

name: George Cleve
headline: George Cleve, Conductor Who Interpreted Mozart, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Cleve, who was born in Vienna, fled with his family to the United States and spent most of his American career on the West Coast.

name: Kyle Jean-Baptiste
headline: Kyle Jean-Baptiste, Actor in ‘Les Misérables,’ Dies at 21
abstract: Mr. Jean-Baptiste, who fell off a fourth-floor fire escape in Brooklyn, was the first black actor to play the lead role of Jean Valjean in the Broadway musical.

name: Oliver Sacks
headline: Oliver Sacks, Neurologist Who Wrote About the Brain’s Quirks, Dies at 82
abstract: Dr. Sacks explored some of the brain’s strangest pathways in best-selling case histories like “The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat,” achieving a level of renown rare among scientists.

name: Gary Keys
headline: Gary Keys, Filmmaker Who Documented Duke Ellington, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Keys produced concerts at Carnegie Hall and Lincoln Center by Stan Getz, Dionne Warwick, the Supremes, Simon and Garfunkel, Judy Garland and Stevie Wonder.

name: James L. Flanagan
headline: James L. Flanagan, Who Helped Make Computers Talk, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Flanagan’s groundbreaking acoustics research paved the way for digital speech, whether welcomed or not.

name: Marvin Mandel
profession: Progressive Maryland Governor Convicted of Fraud
headline: Marvin Mandel, Progressive Maryland Governor Convicted of Fraud, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Mandel’s record of modernizing Maryland’s state government was overshadowed by a racetrack scandal and a messy divorce.

name: Wes Craven
headline: Wes Craven, Whose Slasher Films Terrified Millions, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Craven, a proponent of the slasher genre, was best known for creating Freddy Krueger of “A Nightmare on Elm Street” fame and the “Scream” franchise.

name: Nelson Shanks
headline: Nelson Shanks, Who Painted the Prominent, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Shanks, known for his portraits of political leaders and figures in the arts, this year revealed that he had included a visual reference to the Monica Lewinsky affair in a portrait of Bill Clinton.

name: Wayne W. Dyer
headline: Wayne W. Dyer, Prolific Author of Self-Help Books, Dies at 75
abstract: Dr. Dyer, author of the best-selling “Your Erroneous Zones” and more than two dozen books, was a popular lecturer and talk-show guest.

name: Blondell Cummings
headline: Blondell Cummings, Dancer of Life’s Everyday Details, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Cummings danced on prominent stages and created works that embraced multiple disciplines.

name: Nikolaus Lehnhoff
headline: Nikolaus Lehnhoff, German Opera Director, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Lehnhoff staged “Salome” at the Metropolitan Opera in New York and Wagner’s “Ring” cycle in San Francisco in the 1980s, but was best known for his productions in Europe.

name: Noah Davis
profession: Artist and Founder of Underground Museum in Los Angeles
headline: Noah Davis, 32, Artist and Founder of Underground Museum in Los Angeles, Dies
abstract: Mr. Davis founded the Underground Museum, which provides free art shows in a working-class neighborhood, in Los Angeles.

name: William McCormick Blair Jr.
profession: Envoy and Confidant of Adlai Stevenson
headline: William McCormick Blair Jr., Envoy and Confidant of Adlai Stevenson, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Blair, a lawyer, ambassador and adviser to Stevenson, once approached John Steinbeck to write a derogatory novel based on Richard Nixon.

name: Dean Jones
profession: Affable Star in Love Bug and a Disney Fixture
headline: Dean Jones, Affable Star in ‘Love Bug’ and a Disney Fixture, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Jones appeared on television and Broadway but made his name in films playing a clean-cut Everyman contending with preternaturally intelligent animals or, in one case, a car.

name: Barbara Brecht-Schall
headline: Barbara Brecht-Schall, Guardian of Father’s Plays, Dies at 84
abstract: Mrs. Brecht-Schall managed the works of Bertolt Brecht and performed with the Berliner Ensemble, the troupe founded by him.

name: Gerry Hayden
profession: Took Farm-to-Table Dining to Long Island
headline: Gerry Hayden, Who Took Farm-to-Table Dining to Long Island, Dies at 50
abstract: Mr. Hayden worked at noted Manhattan restaurants before promoting New American cuisine at his and his wife’s North Fork Table and Inn in Southold.

name: Endre A. Balazs
headline: Endre A. Balazs, Doctor Who Found a Lubricant for Arthritic Knees, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Balazs transformed a syrupy natural substance from rooster combs into a palliative for arthritis and a skin protectant that made eye surgery routine.

name: Leon A. Gorman
profession: Made L. L. Bean a Household Name
headline: Leon A. Gorman, Who Made L. L. Bean a Household Name, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Gorman, a grandson of L. L. Bean’s founder, led the company for 34 years and oversaw the beginning of its online operations.

name: J. Donald Millar
headline: Dr. J. Donald Millar, 81, Dies; Led C.D.C. Mission That Helped Eradicate Smallpox
abstract: Dr. Millar oversaw the training, deployment and support of dozens of health workers in some 20 countries in Africa in the 1960s when the disease remained an urgent international health concern.

name: Thomas Sobol
profession: Education Advocate as New York State Commissioner
headline: Thomas Sobol, 83, Dies; Education Advocate as New York State Commissioner
abstract: Dr. Sobol supported the establishment of broad academic standards, subsidizing poor school districts, promoting a multicultural curriculum and empowering parents and teachers in policy-making.

name: Alberta Wright
headline: Alberta Wright, Restaurateur and Soul-Food Pioneer, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Wright, owner of the restaurant Jezebel, which opened in 1983, was a precursor of today’s upscale soul food eateries like Red Rooster in Harlem.

name: T. Eugene Thompson
headline: T. Eugene Thompson Dies at 88; Crime Stunned St. Paul
abstract: Mr. Thompson was convicted of first-degree murder in 1963 for hiring a bungling hit man to kill his wife, Carol, in their Minnesota home, but he always insisted he was innocent.

name: Joy Golden
headline: Joy Golden, Who Made Ads With Punch Lines, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Golden, who won five Clio Awards, rose from the steno pool to write copy for firms large and small. But she discovered her true calling by using humor to sell cheese in the 1980s.

name: Rhoda Lerman
headline: Rhoda Lerman, Writer Who Defied Labels, Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. Lerman was a difficult writer to categorize, but she had a feminist bent, a Jewish sensibility and a taste for ribaldry.

name: Ben Kuroki
profession: Japanese-American Overcame Bias to Fight for U.S
headline: Ben Kuroki Dies at 98; Japanese-American Overcame Bias to Fight for U.S.
abstract: Mr. Kuroki, a decorated member of the Army Air Forces of World War II, was hailed on the American homeland at a time when tens of thousands of Japanese-Americans were confined to internment camps.

name: Lynn Walker Huntley
profession: Lawyer in Prominent Civil Rights Issues
headline: Lynn Walker Huntley, Lawyer in Prominent Civil Rights Issues, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Huntley was a lawyer whose cases and causes involved issues including capital punishment, race relations and employment discrimination.

name: Jean Darling
profession: Child Actress in Our Gang Series
headline: Jean Darling, Child Actress in ‘Our Gang’ Series, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Darling appeared in the comedy series as a child and performed in the original Broadway production of “Carousel” in 1945.

name: Sara Little
headline: Sara Little, Peripatetic Product Designer, Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Little, who consulted for three decades for companies like 3M, General Mills and Coca-Cola, took inspiration from sources as varied as geishas, burglars and cheetahs.

name: Martin Milner
profession: Clean-Cut Star of Route 66 and Adam-12
headline: Martin Milner, Clean-Cut Star of ‘Route 66’ and ‘Adam-12,’ Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Milner had a successful run in late-1950s movies (including “Sweet Smell of Success”) before finding stardom on television.

name: Judy Carne
profession: Sock It to Me Girl on Laugh-In
headline: Judy Carne, ‘Sock It to Me’ Girl on ‘Laugh-In,’ Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Carne rocketed to pop culture fame on “Rowan & Martin’s Laugh-In,” before her career was derailed by drug arrests and a near-fatal accident.

name: Andrew Kohut
headline: Andrew Kohut, Pew Pollster Who Shed Light on Public Opinion, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Kohut was widely respected for his nonpartisanship, expertise and clarity in understanding the findings of national and global surveys.

name: Joaquin Andujar
headline: Joaquin Andujar, All-Star Who Pitched ’82 Cardinals to Title, Dies at 62
abstract: Andujar pitched for three teams in the 1970s and ’80s and won two games for the St. Louis Cardinals in the 1982 World Series triumph.

name: Brad Anderson
headline: Brad Anderson, Creator of ‘Marmaduke,’ Dies at 91
abstract: At its pinnacle, Mr. Anderson’s comic strip about a mischievous but lovable Great Dane appeared in more than 500 newspapers in the United States and in other countries.

name: John Perreault
headline: John Perreault, Art Critic (and Artist) Who Championed the New, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Perreault, a Village Voice art critic, poet and later a curator, made the case for feminist art, photorealism, art with gay content and other movements.

name: Charles S. Hallac
headline: Charles S. Hallac, Co-President of BlackRock, Dies at 50
abstract: Mr. Hallac, the first official employee to be hired by the fledgling asset management firm in 1988, developed its computerized investment platform, Aladdin.

name: Stanton R. Cook
headline: Stanton R. Cook, a Chief of the Tribune Company, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Cook rose from an engineer post in the production department of The Chicago Tribune to chief executive of the Tribune Company, taking it public in 1983.

name: Dennis Greene
headline: Dennis Greene, a Singer With Sha Na Na, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Greene, who left the band after 15 years, went on to become a vice president of Columbia Pictures and then a law professor.

name: Gabrielle Burton
headline: Gabrielle Burton, Feminist Novelist and Screenwriter, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Burton considered conventional marriage lopsided but identified with the pioneering Donner Party wife who perished protecting her husband.

name: Irving Harper
headline: Irving Harper, Creator of the Marshmallow Sofa, Dies at 99
abstract: The industrial designer was a pioneer of mid-20th-century Pop Art furniture designs, which included ball clocks and sunburst clocks.

name: Merv Adelson
headline: Merv Adelson, Las Vegas Developer-Turned-Daring TV Producer, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Adelson, a personable world-class schmoozer, built malls and supermarkets before co-founding Lorimar, producer of ‘The Waltons,’ ‘Eight Is Enough,’ ‘Knots Landing’ and a string of other popular TV series.

name: Candida Royalle
headline: Candida Royalle, 64, Dies; Filmed Erotica for Women
abstract: Ms. Royalle, a former star of pornographic films, also wrote “How to Tell a Naked Man What to Do: Sex Advice From a Woman Who Knows.”

name: Dickie Moore
profession: Child Actor Known for a Screen Kiss
headline: Dickie Moore, Child Actor Known for a Screen Kiss, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Moore’s first Hollywood role occurred before his first birthday.

name: Dickie Moore
profession: Feisty Piece of a Canadiens Dynasty
headline: Dickie Moore, a Feisty Piece of a Canadiens Dynasty, Dies at 84
abstract: Moore, who was a part of six Stanley Cup championship teams in Montreal, was a two-time N.H.L. scoring champion and played in six All-Star Games.

name: William H. Grier
headline: William H. Grier, Psychiatrist Who Delved Into ‘Black Rage’ in 1960s, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Grier and his co-author opened the eyes of a broad audience to the psychological rather than the economic consequences of racism.

name: Moses Malone
headline: Moses Malone, 76ers’ ‘Chairman of the Boards,’ Dies at 60
abstract: Malone, a three-time league M.V.P., was the first modern player to go straight from high school to the pros when he made his A.B.A. debut in 1974.

name: Frank D. Gilroy
profession: Had Smash Debut With Subject Was Roses
headline: Frank D. Gilroy, Who Had Smash Debut With ‘Subject Was Roses,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Gilroy won a Pulitzer Prize, a Tony and a Drama Critics’ Circle Award for that play, his 1964 Broadway debut, but it was his only major theatrical success.

name: Stanley Hoffmann
profession: Brought Passion to Foreign Policy Analysis
headline: Stanley Hoffmann, Who Brought Passion to Foreign Policy Analysis, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Hoffmann taught at Harvard for more than half a century and wrote a series of influential books that explored international relations.

name: Fred DeLuca
profession: Hands-on Co-Founder of Subway Sandwich Chain
headline: Fred DeLuca, Hands-on Co-Founder of Subway Sandwich Chain, Dies at 67
abstract: While Mr. DeLuca’s success was often portrayed as inspirational, Subway’s growth was achieved with aggressive tactics and sometimes unflattering publicity.

name: Norman L. Farberow
profession: Took Study of Suicide to Academic Fore
headline: Norman L. Farberow Is Dead at 97; Took Study of Suicide to Academic Fore
abstract: Dr. Farberow was a founder of the nation’s first comprehensive suicide prevention center and helped upend longstanding notions about the nature of suicide.

name: Melvin Bernhardt
headline: Melvin Bernhardt, Tony-Winning Director Who Helped Stars Shine, Dies at 84
abstract: Known for his astute casting and skillful work with actors, Mr. Bernhardt directed many leading stage performers on Broadway and won a Tony for “Da.”

name: Deborah Asnis
profession: Sounded Alert on West Nile Virus Outbreak
headline: Dr. Deborah Asnis, Who Sounded Alert on West Nile Virus Outbreak, Dies at 59
abstract: Dr. Asnis was credited with limiting the spread of the Western Hemisphere’s first outbreak of the virus by promptly reporting puzzling symptoms in two Queens patients.

name: Lawrence S. Phillips
headline: Lawrence S. Phillips, 88, Dies; Clothier Founded Jewish Aid Agency
abstract: Mr. Phillips, a longtime executive with Phillips-Van Heusen, also founded the aid organization American Jewish World Service and was particularly proud of his place on Nixon’s “enemies list.”

name: Lawrence Phillips
headline: Lawrence Phillips, Volatile Football Star, Dies at 40
abstract: A gifted running back for Nebraska and the St. Louis Rams, Phillips derailed his career with a series of violent criminal acts off the field.

name: Einar Ingman
profession: Soldier Lauded for Valor in Korean War
headline: Einar Ingman, Soldier Lauded for Valor in Korean War, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Ingman destroyed two machine gun nests in South Korea in 1951 despite suffering severe injuries, leading to the loss of an eye and hearing in one ear.

name: Max Beauvoir
profession: Gave Up Science to Be High Priest of Voodoo
headline: Max Beauvoir, Who Gave Up Science to Be High Priest of Voodoo, Dies at 79
abstract: American-educated, Mr. Beauvoir was planning a career in biochemistry when his dying grandfather anointed him a houngan.

name: Carl E. Schorske
profession: Pulitzer-Winning Historian Saw Vienna as Pivotal
headline: Carl E. Schorske, 100, Dies; Pulitzer-Winning Historian Saw Vienna as Pivotal
abstract: For Professor Schorske, a revered teacher at Princeton, the modern cultural age began in turn-of-the-century Vienna.

name: Milo Hamilton
profession: Brought Baseball, Including Aarons Homer, to Life
headline: Milo Hamilton, 88, Dies; Brought Baseball, Including Aaron’s Homer, to Life
abstract: Hamilton called baseball for seven major league teams over 60 years and was best known for calling Henry Aaron’s 715th home run.

name: Warren Murphy
profession: Writer and Creator of Remo Williams
headline: Warren Murphy, Writer and Creator of Remo Williams, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Murphy, who co-authored the gritty thriller “Created the Destroyer” with Dick Sapir in 1963, wrote many more novels and had credits for movies like “Lethal Weapon 2.”

name: Everett C. Parker
profession: Won Landmark Fight Over Media Race Bias
headline: Everett C. Parker, Who Won Landmark Fight Over Media Race Bias, Dies at 102
abstract: Dr. Parker won a landmark broadcasting case and led a civil rights crusade to hold stations accountable for presenting racially biased programming.

name: Roger Adelman
profession: Prosecutor in Reagan Attackers Insanity Trial
headline: Roger Adelman, Prosecutor in Reagan Attacker’s Insanity Trial, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Adelman’s unsuccessful prosecution of John W. Hinckley Jr. in the shooting of President Ronald Reagan and his press secretary led to a new law governing the insanity defense in criminal trials.

name: Adrian Frutiger
profession: His Type Designs Show You the Way
headline: Adrian Frutiger Dies at 87; His Type Designs Show You the Way
abstract: From the Paris Métro to Kennedy Airport, signs over the years have borne Mr. Frutiger’s imprint.

name: Mitchell L. Gaynor
profession: Oncologist and Author on Alternative Treatments
headline: Mitchell L. Gaynor, 59, Dies; Oncologist and Author on Alternative Treatments
abstract: Dr. Gaynor, a popular author and the founder of a Manhattan cancer clinic, incorporated music, diet and meditation in his treatments of patients.

name: Jackie Collins
headline: Jackie Collins, Best-Selling Novelist of Hollywood, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Collins’s sex-filled, escapist (and even once banned) fiction was devoured by tens of millions of readers.

name: Noël Verset
headline: Noël Verset, Vigneron Who Helped Save a Wine Tradition, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Verset’s perseverance laboring in vineyards in the Rhône Valley of France, helped the Cornas appellation survive to be discovered by a new generation of wine lovers.

name: Mamdouha Bobst
headline: Mamdouha Bobst, Philanthropist and Public Health Advocate, Dies at 90
abstract: Mrs. Bobst donated to institutions like N.Y.U., the American Cancer Society and the American Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals, and served as the Lebanese delegate to the United Nations.

name: Jack Larson
headline: Jack Larson, a TV Jimmy Olsen Turned Playwright, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Larson, who went on to write plays and librettos, predicted that he would be best remembered as the eager cub reporter for The Daily Planet on ‘Superman.’

name: Esmail Kiram II
headline: Esmail Kiram II, Self-Proclaimed Sultan of Sulu, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Kiram, whose title several others claim as well, encouraged a violent effort to regain part of the island Borneo for the Philippines in 2013.

name: Robert E. Simon Jr.
headline: Robert E. Simon Jr., Who Created a Town, Reston, Va., Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Simon, a New York real estate developer, planned the town in the 1960s as an alternative to postwar commuter towns with cookie-cutter homes.

name: Daniel Thompson
profession: Bagel Machine Altered the American Diet
headline: Daniel Thompson, Whose Bagel Machine Altered the American Diet, Dies at 94
