abstract: Bound up in the Thompson bagel machine is the story of Jewish assimilation, gastronomic homogenization, the decline of trade unionism and the rise of franchise retailing.

name: Carmen Balcells
profession: Agent to Latin Americas Literary Lions
headline: Carmen Balcells, Agent to Latin America’s Literary Lions, Dies at 85
abstract: Nicknamed “La Mamá Grande” after a story by Gabriel García Márquez, Ms. Balcells rewrote the rules of Spanish-language publishing.

name: David Willcocks
headline: Sir David Willcocks, Conductor Who Influenced British Choral Music, Dies at 95
abstract: Long considered Britain’s most esteemed choir director, Mr. Willcocks also led ensembles in the United States and even worked with the Rolling Stones.

name: Georges de Paris
headline: Georges de Paris, Tailor to Nine Presidents, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. de Paris had made suits for every American leader since Lyndon B. Johnson, and he crafted his own life story, as well.

name: William E. Paul
profession: Helped AIDS Research Save Millions of Lives
headline: Dr. William E. Paul, Who Helped AIDS Research Save Millions of Lives, Dies at 79
abstract: As the director of the Office of AIDS Research at the National Institute of Health, Dr. Paul focused the government’s research programs to develop innovative therapies.

name: Leon Root
headline: Dr. Leon Root, Orthopedic Surgeon Who Wrote Advice Books, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Root was chief of pediatric orthopedics for 27 years at the Hospital for Special Surgery in Manhattan, and he created a program to screen New York City children for disorders of the bones and joints.

name: Yogi Berra
headline: Yogi Berra, Yankee Who Built His Stardom 90 Percent on Skill and Half on Wit, Dies at 90
abstract: A mainstay player on 10 Yankee championship teams who as a manager led the Yankees and Mets to the World Series, Berra may have been better known for his bumbling yet wise way with words.

name: Jeremy P. Tarcher
headline: Jeremy P. Tarcher, Publisher of Nonfiction Best Sellers, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Tarcher founded the publishing house that bears his name in the 1970s and specialized in books on health, psychology and New Age spirituality.

name: Phil Patton
headline: Phil Patton, Design Writer Who Scrutinized the Everyday, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Patton’s keen eye for objects and their hidden significance made him a sought-after contributor to magazines including Art in America, Esquire, Smithsonian and Wired.

name: Elizabeth M. Fink
profession: Lawyer for Attica Inmates and Radicals
headline: Elizabeth M. Fink, a Lawyer for Attica Inmates and Radicals, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Fink, a self-described revolutionary, represented criminals and radicals pro bono for more than four decades.

name: Daniel Levins
profession: Dancer in Classical Ballet and Films
headline: Daniel Levins, Dancer in Classical Ballet and Films, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Levins joined Eliot Feld’s American Ballet Company as a teenager, was a principal at American Ballet Theater and had a memorable role in ‘The Turning Point.’

name: John McNeill
headline: John McNeill, Priest Who Pushed Catholic Church to Welcome Gays, Dies at 90
abstract: Father McNeill was a champion of gay rights long before the Catholic church opened the issue to debate, and he was expelled from his order as a result.

name: Terry Rosenbaum
headline: Terry Rosenbaum, Teacher Who Was Fired After Defying McCarthy, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Rosenbaum’s career in education was cut short after he helped in an attempt to indict a police officer in 1951 and attracted Senator Joseph R. McCarthy’s attention.

name: Marla Krolikowski
headline: Marla Krolikowski, Transgender Teacher Fired for Insubordination, Dies at 62
abstract: In a well-publicized lawsuit, Ms. Krolikowski sued St. Francis Preparatory School in Queens for dismissing her over her appearance.

name: Richard E. Rainwater
headline: Richard E. Rainwater, Billionaire Texas Dealmaker, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Rainwater made lucrative deals in real estate, entertainment and oil and was a family friend to the Bushes who helped George W. Bush make a modest fortune.

name: Sheri M. Goldhirsch
headline: Sheri M. Goldhirsch, Who Nurtured Young Playwrights, Dies at 55
abstract: Ms. Goldhirsch, the artistic director of Young Playwrights Inc., was responsible for helping along the careers of generations of American dramatists.

name: Catherine Coulson
profession: Enigmatic Log Lady of Twin Peaks
headline: Catherine Coulson, the Enigmatic Log Lady of ‘Twin Peaks,’ Dies at 71
abstract: Ms. Coulson acted for 22 seasons with the Oregon Shakespeare Festival, but it was her performance as one of the more eccentric residents of Twin Peaks, Wash., that made her a cult favorite.

name: Phil Woods
profession: Saxophonist Revered in Jazz and Heard on Hits
headline: Phil Woods, Saxophonist Revered in Jazz and Heard on Hits, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Woods was a disciple of Charlie Parker and was widely heard on songs by Billy Joel, Paul Simon and others.

name: Phyllis Tickle
profession: Energized a Market for Books on Religion
headline: Phyllis Tickle, Who Energized a Market for Books on Religion, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Tickle, the founding religion editor at Publishers Weekly, wrote dozens of books on spirituality, and was a leading voice in the Emergence Christianity movement.

name: Ionel Talpazan
profession: U.F.O. Art Had Sightings All Over
headline: Ionel Talpazan, Whose U.F.O. Art Had Sightings All Over, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Talpazan, who said he had an encounter with a U.F.O. in Romania when he was young, sold his visionary works on the sidewalks of Manhattan before being discovered in the late 1980s.

name: Doug Kendall
headline: Doug Kendall, Liberal Who Challenged Supreme Court’s Conservatives, Dies at 51
abstract: Mr. Kendall founded the Constitutional Accountability Center, where he sought to use conservatives’ own judicial strategy to advance liberal causes.

name: Robert Curvin
headline: Robert Curvin, Scholar Who Fought Bias and Poverty in Newark, Dies at 81
abstract: Dr. Curvin, a co-founder of the Newark chapter of the Congress of Racial Equality, helped make Kenneth A. Gibson the first black mayor of a major Northeast city.

name: Carole Little
headline: Carole Little, Fashion Designer for Working Women, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Little’s sportswear found an eager audience among working women who sought affordable style, and her clothing adorned stars like Lauren Hutton and Jane Fonda.

name: John Galvin
headline: Gen. John Galvin, a NATO Supreme Allied Commander, Dies at 86
abstract: General Galvin oversaw the North Atlantic military alliance from 1987 to 1992, retooling it into a more mobile, flexible multinational force after the collapse of the Soviet Union.

name: John Guillermin
headline: John Guillermin, ‘Towering Inferno’ Director, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Guillermin, a prolific British director, was known for big-budget extravaganzas and a raging temper.

name: Yuri N. Afanasyev
headline: Yuri N. Afanasyev, Historian Who Repudiated Communism, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Afanasyev, a Russian historian and former Communist loyalist, became a leading democratic politician in the late Soviet era.

name: Joseph Coffey
headline: Joseph Coffey, Detective Who Took Son of Sam’s Confession, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Coffey’s exploits included arresting the gangster John J. Gotti, uncovering fraud at the Vatican Bank and investigating the Lufthansa heist.

name: Brian Friel
headline: Brian Friel, Playwright Called the Irish Chekhov, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Friel’s distinctive blend of melancholy and humor infused plays that dealt with cultural identity, loss and disillusion, and the meaning of home.

name: Paul Reed
headline: Paul Reed, of the Washington Color School, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Reed, a painter and the last surviving member of the group, was known for his technique of staining the canvas and for hard-edge form.

name: Don Edwards
headline: Don Edwards, Congressman Who Championed Civil Rights, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Edwards, who once led the California Young Republicans, became one of the most liberal Democrats in Congress, drafting every civil rights bill in the House for two decades.

name: Bruce Wennerstrom
profession: Founder of Yearly Beauty Contest for Classic Cars
headline: Bruce Wennerstrom, Founder of Yearly Beauty Contest for Classic Cars, Dies at 88
abstract: “In their teens, a guy’s hormones and gasoline all get mixed up together,” Mr. Wennerstrom liked to say. “Most outgrow it. I never did.”

name: Wilton Felder
headline: Wilton Felder, Saxophonist for the Crusaders, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Felder was a founder of the Crusaders, whose sound evolved from hard bop to jazz funk, and was a busy session bass player.

name: Denis Healey
profession: Feisty Labour Leader in a Downsized Britain
headline: Denis Healey, 98, Dies; Feisty Labour Leader in a Downsized Britain
abstract: The British socialist politician and intellect used his various leadership roles to tell his party “hard truths about Britain having to live within her means.”

name: Henning Mankell
headline: Henning Mankell, Writer Whose Wallander Patrolled a Gritty Sweden, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Mankell was considered the dean of the so-called Scandinavian noir writers who gained fame for novels that mixed suspense with flawed, compelling protagonists and strong social themes.

name: Grace Lee Boggs
headline: Grace Lee Boggs, Human Rights Advocate for 7 Decades, Dies at 100
abstract: Ms. Boggs pursued revolutionary justice for causes like civil rights, labor, feminism and the environment.

name: Neal Walk
headline: Neal Walk, Who Rebounded Coast to Coast, Dies at 67
abstract: Walk grabbed more rebounds at the University of Florida than anyone else in the basketball program’s history and became an effective center for the Phoenix Suns in the early years of the franchise.

name: Vivian Stromberg
headline: Vivian Stromberg, Who Worked to Aid Women, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Stromberg, who taught elementary school in the South Bronx in the early 1980s, helped create Madre, an aid and human rights organization that supported women’s groups around the world.

name: Chantal Akerman
headline: Chantal Akerman, Whose Films Examined Women’s Inner Lives, Dies at 65
abstract: Ms. Akerman, a Belgian whose latest work is at the New York Film Festival, created ruminative observations of women, sometimes punctuated by violence.

name: Olga Hirshhorn
profession: Modern Art Collector and Museum Benefactor
headline: Olga Hirshhorn, Modern Art Collector and Museum Benefactor, Dies at 95
abstract: Mrs. Hirshhorn began buying modern art while married to Joseph H. Hirshhorn, the founder of the Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden in Washington.

name: Arpad Goncz
profession: Writer and Hungarys First Post-Communist President
headline: Arpad Goncz, Writer and Hungary’s First Post-Communist President, Dies at 93
abstract: Though his post was largely ceremonial, Mr. Goncz, a playwright and translator, eased his country through a transition with his widespread popularity.

name: Joker Arroyo
profession: Challenged Martial Law in the Philippines
headline: Joker Arroyo, Who Challenged Martial Law in the Philippines, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Arroyo, a politician and lawyer who was a trusted adviser to Corazon C. Aquino, counseled, bedeviled and helped topple Philippine presidents.

name: Sue Petersen Lubow
profession: Athletic Director at Merchant Marine Academy
headline: Sue Petersen Lubow, Athletic Director at Merchant Marine Academy, Dies at 61
abstract: Petersen Lubow, an all-American in swimming at Springfield College, in 1989 became the first female athletic director at a United States military service academy.

name: Billy Joe Royal
profession: His Down in the Boondocks Was a Hit
headline: Billy Joe Royal, Singer, Dies at 73; His ‘Down in the Boondocks’ Was a Hit
abstract: Mr. Royal, whose biggest hits were songs written and produced by Joe South, was best known for the 1965 record “Down in the Boondocks.”

name: Kevin Corcoran
headline: Kevin Corcoran, a Child Actor Mainstay for Disney, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Corcoran appeared in numerous Disney films and television shows, including “Old Yeller,” before moving to the production side of the business.

name: Harry Gallatin
profession: Rugged and Durable Hall of Famer With the Knicks
headline: Harry Gallatin, Rugged and Durable Hall of Famer With the Knicks, Dies at 88
abstract: Gallatin was a ferocious rebounder who played nine seasons for the Knicks in the 1950s, appearing in 746 consecutive games when pro basketball was a low-paid game for smaller, thinner men.

name: Donald R. Seawell
headline: Donald R. Seawell Dies at 103, Leaving His Stamp on Denver
abstract: After years as a New York lawyer and producer, Mr. Seawell led The Denver Post and founded Denver’s performing arts center.

name: Paul Prudhomme
headline: Paul Prudhomme, Chef Who Put Cajun Cooking on National Stage, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Prudhomme combined Deep South tradition with fresh, local ingredients, opening restaurants, marketing spice mixes and hosting popular TV shows.

name: Frank Albanese
profession: Tonys Uncle Pat on The Sopranos
headline: Frank Albanese, Tony’s Uncle Pat on ‘The Sopranos,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Albanese, who was born on Staten Island, also appeared in “Goodfellas” and “Honor Thy Father.”

name: Gail Zappa
profession: Keeper of Her Rock Star Husbands Legacy
headline: Gail Zappa, Keeper of Her Rock Star Husband’s Legacy, Dies at 70
abstract: Mrs. Zappa was a model and a performer before she became the manager of a career and guardian of an image.

name: Lindy Infante
headline: Lindy Infante, Head Coach Who Led Packers’ Revival, Dies at 75
abstract: Infante, the N.F.L.’s coach of the year in 1989 with Green Bay, was also the victim of bad timing, losing both his head-coaching jobs in the seasons before his teams obtained superstars.

name: Anna Pump
profession: Chef and Author Famed for Hamptons Store
headline: Anna Pump, Chef and Author Famed for Hamptons Store, Dies at 81
abstract: Trained by James Beard, Ms. Pump owned Loaves & Fishes, devoted to simple, well-prepared (and often pricey) fare. She died after being struck by a pickup truck.

name: Ravindra Jain
headline: Ravindra Jain, Bollywood Film Composer, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Jain, who was born blind, had a string of hits in India in the 1970s and ’80s and turned out hundreds of film scores.

name: Jerry Parr
headline: Jerry Parr, Secret Service Agent Who Helped Save Reagan, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Parr was just feet away from the president when John W. Hinckley Jr. opened fire on March 30, 1981.

name: Geoffrey Howe
headline: Geoffrey Howe, Cabinet Minister Who Hastened Thatcher’s Fall, Dies at 88
abstract: A Conservative British cabinet member who advanced Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher’s economic policies, Mr. Howe resigned and hastened her downfall in 1990.

name: Larry Brezner
headline: Larry Brezner, Hollywood Manager of Star Comics, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Mr. Brezner helped propel the careers of Robin Williams and Billy Crystal and produced more than a dozen feature films.

name: Dean Chance
profession: Cy Young Award Winner and Yankees Nemesis
headline: Dean Chance, Cy Young Award Winner and Yankees Nemesis, Dies at 74
abstract: Chance was a right-hander whose Cy Young Award-winning year, 1964, ranks among the great season-long performances in the history of the game.

name: John Berg
headline: John Berg, Art Director Who Made Album Covers Sing, Dies at 83
abstract: A four-time Grammy Award winner, Mr. Berg was midwife to some of the most emblematic album covers of the late 20th century, for artists including Bob Dylan, Bruce Springsteen and Barbra Streisand.

name: Sandra Spuzich
headline: Sandra Spuzich, 78, L.P.G.A. Record-Setter, Dies
abstract: Ms. Spuzich’s first pro victory came in the 1966 United States Women’s Open, and at 45 she became the tour’s oldest player to win two tournaments in one season.

name: Robert Leuci
profession: Exposed Graft Among Fellow Detectives in 70s
headline: Robert Leuci, 75, Who Exposed Graft Among Fellow Detectives in ’70s, Dies
abstract: Mr. Leuci was a rogue cop turned informer who exposed endemic corruption among fellow detectives in an elite New York City narcotics unit in the 1970s.

name: Kenneth Koe
headline: Kenneth Koe, an Inventor Behind Zoloft, Dies at 90
abstract: The Pfizer chemist helped create the antidepressant that has been used to treat more than 100 million people and has generated sales of more than $3 billion.

name: Rosalyn Baxandall
headline: Rosalyn Baxandall, Feminist Historian and Activist, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Baxandall was an author of “America’s Working Women: A Documentary History, 1600 to the Present,” a key text for students of American labor history and gender studies.

name: Henry Krystal
headline: Henry Krystal, Holocaust Trauma Expert, and Survivor, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Krystal, who was forced into slave labor by the Nazis, focused his psychiatric career on the emotional scars carried by concentration camp survivors.

name: Hilla Becher
headline: Hilla Becher, Photographer Who Chronicled Industrial Scenery, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Becher and her husband, Bernd, documented coal mines, steel mills and other features of the industrial landscape, straddling the worlds of archival documentation and conceptual art.

name: Diepreye Alamieyeseigha
headline: Diepreye Alamieyeseigha, Nigerian Notorious for Corruption, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Alamieyeseigha, a former governor of an oil-rich Nigerian state, embezzled as much as $55 million in oil ministry revenue, acquiring luxuries and homes around the world.

name: Larry Rosen
profession: Digital-Audio Pioneer and Force in Pop-Jazz
headline: Larry Rosen, Digital-Audio Pioneer and Force in Pop-Jazz, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Rosen, who started the label GRP with Dave Grusin, produced one of the earliest digitally recorded nonclassical albums.

name: Sybil Stockdale
profession: Fierce Advocate for P.O.W.s and Their Families
headline: Sybil Stockdale, Fierce Advocate for P.O.W.s and Their Families, Dies at 90
abstract: Mrs. Stockdale became a spokeswoman for the families of Americans missing in action after getting coded notes from her husband, a Navy flier, revealing his torture in a North Vietnamese prison.

name: Joan Leslie
headline: Joan Leslie, a Hollywood Girl Next Door, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Leslie played fresh-faced ingénue roles in movies of the 1940s, including “High Sierra,” “Sergeant York” and “Yankee Doodle Dandy.”

name: Richard F. Heck
headline: Richard F. Heck, Chemist, Dies at 84; Revolutionized Drug Development
abstract: Dr. Heck shared the 2010 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for creating techniques to synthesize complex carbon molecules that are now used to make drugs, electronics and other products.

name: Mathieu Kérékou
headline: Mathieu Kérékou, Dictator Who Ushered In Democracy in Benin, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Kérékou seized control of Benin in a military coup in 1972 but presided over a peaceful transition to democracy 20 years later.

name: Alvin P. Adams Jr.
headline: Alvin P. Adams Jr., Ambassador Who Helped Haiti Pursue Democracy, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Adams, a three-time ambassador, persuaded a Haitian military ruler in 1990 to abdicate. That move paved the way for Haiti’s first freely elected president.

name: Skip Yowell
headline: Skip Yowell, JanSport Co-Founder Who Blazed Trail for Backpacks, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Yowell’s passion for the outdoors inspired a multimillion-dollar business that catered originally to campers and hikers, and eventually to students.

name: Julien Studley
headline: Julien Studley, a Refugee Who Built a Commercial Real Estate Empire, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Studley, who came to New York in 1943 as a young refugee from Europe, started what became a commercial real estate empire by sending postcards to prospective tenants from his fourth-floor walk-up.

name: Irwin Schiff
profession: Fervent Opponent of Federal Income Taxes
headline: Irwin Schiff, Fervent Opponent of Federal Income Taxes, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Schiff, who was serving his third prison term, considered income tax unconstitutional, and he pressed his cause in six self-published books.

name: George Mueller
headline: George Mueller, Engineer Who Helped Put Man on Moon, Dies at 97
abstract: As a NASA official, Dr. Mueller saw the space program’s potential and played a critical role in fulfilling President John F. Kennedy’s vision.

name: Lennart Anderson
headline: Lennart Anderson, Painter Who Put Modern Twist on the Masters, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Anderson brought an understanding of painters like Degas to his still lifes, portraits, landscapes and streetscapes, while lifting them from the common run of academic realism.

name: Vera B. Williams
profession: Brought Working Class to Childrens Books
headline: Vera B. Williams, 88, Dies; Brought Working Class to Children’s Books
abstract: Ms. Williams broke new ground by broadening the scope of children’s books to include working-class families and others with struggles.

name: Gamal al-Ghitani
profession: Egyptian Novelist With a Political Bent
headline: Gamal al-Ghitani, Egyptian Novelist With a Political Bent, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Ghitani, whose work was frequently published in English translations, was most famous for “Zayni Barakat” (1974), a scorching allegorical critique of totalitarianism.

name: Gerald Gross
profession: Published Memoirs of a Hitler Associate
headline: Gerald Gross, Who Published Memoirs of a Hitler Associate, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Mr. Gross, a longtime book editor and publishing executive, was instrumental in bringing the memoirs of Adolf Hitler’s close associate Albert Speer to an English-speaking readership.

name: Paul West
headline: Paul West, Writer Who Shoveled Absurdity Into His Books, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. West, who managed to write again after a stroke reduced his once-Shakespearean vocabulary to a single syllable, wrote quirky novels with unusual themes and even more unusual protagonists.

name: Cory Wells
headline: Cory Wells, Singer With Three Dog Night, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Wells was one of three lead singers in the band, a signature pop group of the late 1960s and ’70s.

name: Walter Gerken
headline: Walter Gerken, Who Helped Found Pimco, Is Dead at 93
abstract: The former chairman and chief executive of Pacific Life Insurance, he decided to turn the company’s investment arm into a separate subsidiary that would manage outside money.

name: Marty Ingels
profession: Actor Funny Onscreen and Outrageous Off
headline: Marty Ingels, Actor Funny Onscreen and Outrageous Off, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Ingels held jobs as a talking peanut, an agent and the voice of Pac-Man.

name: Thomas G. Stemberg
profession: Joined a Rival to Found Staples
headline: Thomas G. Stemberg, Who Joined a Rival to Found Staples, Dies at 66
abstract: Inspired by his inability to buy a printer ribbon on the Fourth of July, Mr. Stemberg and a former rival in the grocery industry, Leo Kahn, teamed up to found Staples in 1986.

name: Richard Cardamone
headline: Richard Cardamone, Judge, Dies at 90; Doomed Westway Project in Manhattan
abstract: Perhaps Mr. Cardamone’s greatest legacy on a federal appeals court was his 1985 decision that blocked a $2.1 billion replacement for the derelict West Side Highway because of environmental concerns.

name: Beny Primm
profession: Pioneer in Addiction and AIDS Prevention
headline: Dr. Beny Primm, Pioneer in Addiction and AIDS Prevention, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Primm was a so-so student who went on to became a physician intent on fighting drug addiction and H.I.V.

name: Jerome Kass
headline: Jerome Kass, Writer for Broadway, Film and TV, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Kass was nominated for a Tony for the 1978 musical “Ballroom,” based on his Emmy-nominated teleplay about a Bronx widow who visits a dance hall.

name: Maureen O’Hara
headline: Maureen O’Hara, Irish-Born Star Who Played Strong-Willed Beauties, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. O’Hara became a star in escapist movies of the 1940s and ’50s, appearing in “How Green Was My Valley,” “Miracle on 34th Street” and “The Quiet Man.”

name: Mark Murphy
headline: Mark Murphy, an Unconventional Jazz Vocalist, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Murphy drew inspiration from such varied sources as the sound of his hometown factory whistle and the words of the Beat novelist Jack Kerouac.

name: Flip Saunders
headline: Flip Saunders, Coach and Executive Who Led Timberwolves’ Ascent, Dies at 60
abstract: The Minnesota team had recently rehired its former coach in the hope that he could once again turn the franchise around.

name: E. Virgil Conway
headline: E. Virgil Conway, Former M.T.A. Chairman, Dies at 85
abstract: A lawyer and banker, Mr. Conway presided over the system’s first fare abatement and the retirement of the iconic subway token.

name: Leon Bibb
headline: Leon Bibb, Actor, Folk Singer and Civil Rights Activist, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Bibb, an actor turned folk singer, made his Broadway debut in 1946 in “Annie Get Your Gun,” and earned a Tony nomination for “A Hand Is on the Gate” from 1967.

name: Bill Keith
headline: Bill Keith, Who Uncovered Banjo’s Melodic Potential, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Keith turned a largely percussive instrument into one with unforeseen melodic potential, bridging the traditional stylists of the mid-20th century and more freewheeling latter-day players.

name: Peter Dougherty
headline: Peter Dougherty, Who Brought Rap to MTV, Dies at 59
abstract: A behind-the-scenes downtown fixture of the 1970s and ’80s, Mr. Dougherty helped shape the network’s early identity, most notably as a creator of “Yo! MTV Raps.”

name: Murphy Anderson
headline: Murphy Anderson, Longtime Artist for DC Comics, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Anderson would pencil or ink nearly every major series the company published, including Superman and Hawkman.

name: John Backe
profession: Put CBS Back Atop Prime Time
headline: John Backe Dies at 83; Put CBS Back Atop Prime Time
abstract: Mr. Backe led CBS in the 1970s, helping the network take back first place in prime time, with bold programming like “Dallas.” He was ousted after a power struggle.

name: Sheldon S. Wolin
profession: Political Theorist Saw Limits of Popular Democracy
headline: Sheldon S. Wolin, 93, Dies; Political Theorist Saw Limits of Popular Democracy
abstract: Mr. Wolin galvanized political science by gathering key political philosophers, beginning with the Greeks, and examining their ideas as a way to criticize current political structures.

name: Alvin Bronstein
headline: Alvin Bronstein, Lawyer Who Fought Prison Abuse, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Bronstein spent the early part of his career as a civil rights lawyer seeking to defy Jim Crow culture, and he later directed the American Civil Liberties Union’s National Prison Project for 25 years.

name: David Cesarani
headline: David Cesarani, Holocaust Historian and Eichmann Biographer, Dies at 58
abstract: Professor Cesarani challenged Hannah Arendt’s view of a Nazi war criminal as just a cog in a vast machine of murder.

name: Jan Wallman
headline: Jan Wallman, Village Cabaret Owner, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Wallman provided the first rung in the career ladder for performers like Joan Rivers, Barbra Streisand, Woody Allen and Rodney Dangerfield.

name: Steve Gebhardt
headline: Steve Gebhardt, Who Made Films With Rock Stars, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Gebhardt, a filmmaker, worked with Yoko Ono and John Lennon on more than a dozen experimental films.

name: Al Molinaro
headline: Al Molinaro, Diner Owner on ‘Happy Days,’ Dies at 96
abstract: On “Happy Days,” Mr. Molinaro played Al Delvecchio, the owner of a diner where the show’s teenagers congregated.

name: George Germon
profession: Founder of Rhode Island Dining Gem
headline: George Germon, Founder of Rhode Island Dining Gem, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Germon and Johanne Killeen created Al Forno, a restaurant that drew international attention as a pillar of the ascendant dining scene in Providence, R.I.

name: Robert Neugeboren
headline: Robert Neugeboren, Survivor of Psychiatric Abuses, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Neugeboren was hauled away in a straitjacket in his late teens and spent most of his adult life in institutions.

name: Mel Daniels
profession: Prolific Rebounder on the Indiana Pacers in the 1970s
headline: Mel Daniels, Prolific Rebounder on the Indiana Pacers in the 1970s, Dies at 71
abstract: Daniels, the Hall of Fame center, led the Pacers to three American Basketball Association championships and became the leading rebounder in the league’s history.

name: Patricia Canning Todd
profession: Tennis Champion Refused to Play on Side Court
headline: Patricia Canning Todd, 93, Dies; Tennis Champion Refused to Play on Side Court
abstract: Todd, playing as a young mother, won four Grand Slam tennis tournaments in 1947 and 1948 but lost the chance for another in 1948 when she took a stand.

name: Willis Carto
headline: Willis Carto, Far-Right Figure and Holocaust Denier, Dies at 89
abstract: The Anti-Defamation League called Mr. Carto “one of the most influential American anti-Semitic propagandists” and “the mastermind of the hate network.”

name: Leo P. Kadanoff
headline: Leo P. Kadanoff, Physicist Who Explored How Matter Changes, Dies at 78
abstract: Dr. Kadanoff, a physicist, “won basically every prize except the Nobel Prize,” a colleague said.

name: Fred Thompson
headline: Fred Thompson, Former Senator, Actor and Presidential Candidate, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Thompson, a former Republican lawmaker, had an unusual career that bridged the worlds of national politics and mass-market entertainment.

name: Fred Thompson
headline: Fred Thompson, Who Championed Women in Track, Dies at 85
abstract: A former assistant attorney general, he gave up his law career to coach young athletes in Brooklyn and to run the Colgate Women’s Games for 40 years.

name: Günter Schabowski
profession: Gaffe Helped Burst the Berlin Wall
headline: Günter Schabowski, Whose Gaffe Helped Burst the Berlin Wall, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Schabowski’s bumbling answer to a reporter’s question inadvertently led to the opening of the Cold War’s most notorious closed border.

name: Thomas Blatt
headline: Thomas Blatt, Who Escaped Death Camp During Revolt, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Blatt was one of the few survivors of a rare revolt and mass escape from a Nazi death camp in occupied Poland in October 1943, during World War II.

name: Ahmad Chalabi
headline: Ahmad Chalabi, Iraqi Politician Who Pushed for U.S. Invasion, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Chalabi is perhaps the Iraqi most associated with President George W. Bush’s decision to invade the country and topple its longtime dictator, Saddam Hussein.

name: Ticky Burden
headline: Ticky Burden, Former All-American and Knick Who Fell Into Crime, Dies at 62
abstract: Luther Burden starred for the University of Utah and played for the Knicks in the 1970s. He was convicted of robbing a Long Island bank in 1980.

name: Norm Siebern
headline: Norm Siebern, All-Star Who Left Yankees in Trade for Maris, Dies at 82
abstract: Siebern, a three-time All-Star in the American League, may be best known as part of the trade that brought Roger Maris to the Yankees.

name: Colin Welland
profession: Oscar-Winning Writer of Chariots of Fire
headline: Colin Welland, Oscar-Winning Writer of ‘Chariots of Fire,’ Dies at 81
abstract: The Oscar-winning screenwriter, who had wanted to be an actor, eventually did have several roles, including a continuing spot in a British TV show, “Z-Cars.”

name: Charles Herbert
profession: Mid-Century Child Star on TV and in Movies
headline: Charles Herbert, Mid-Century Child Star on TV and in Movies, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Herbert, a top earner in his youth, appeared in more than 20 films (including “The Fly” and “Houseboat”) and 50 television episodes (including “The Twilight Zone”).

name: Howard Green
profession: Found a Way to Grow Skin and Saved Lives
headline: Howard Green, Who Found a Way to Grow Skin and Saved Lives, Dies at 90
abstract: From a failed experiment, Dr. Green discovered how to regenerate skin that could be grafted onto burn victims, and inspired future stem cell research.

name: Melissa Mathison
headline: Melissa Mathison, the Screenwriter Behind a Classic, ‘E.T.,’ Dies at 65
abstract: Ms. Mathison, who shared a screenplay credit on “The Black Stallion” (1979), met Steven Spielberg, the director of “E.T.,” in Tunisia, where he started to persuade her to write the script.

name: George Barris
headline: George Barris, California King of Customized Cars, Dies at 89
abstract: The man behind the Batmobile, immortalized in a Tom Wolfe essay, was a pioneer and master of car customization.

name: George Barris
headline: George Barris, Photographer Who Captured the Last Images of Marilyn Monroe, Dies at 94
abstract: Monroe and Mr. Barris had been friends for almost a decade. He told numerous interviewers over the years that he did not believe her death was a suicide.

name: Czeslaw Kiszczak
headline: Gen. Czeslaw Kiszczak, Poland’s Last Communist Prime Minister, Dies at 90
abstract: General Kiszczak helped crush the Solidarity movement in Poland in 1981 and eight years later presided briefly over the country’s transition to democracy.

name: Robert P. DeVecchi
headline: Robert P. DeVecchi, Who Led International Rescue Committee, Dies at 85
abstract: During Mr. DeVecchi’s 22 years with the committee, the last five as chief executive, it created emergency aid programs in nearly 30 countries and resettled more than 200,000 refugees in the United States.

name: Thomas S. Marvel
headline: Thomas S. Marvel, Architect of the Tropical, Dies at 80
abstract: An American who went to the Caribbean and stayed forever.

name: Yitzhak Navon
headline: Yitzhak Navon, 94, Israeli Ex-President, Dies; Part of Founding Generation
abstract: The scion of an old Jerusalem family, Mr. Navon served as Israel’s fifth president and was one of the fading generation of Israeli state builders.

name: Brookie Maxwell
headline: Brookie Maxwell, an Artist and Curator, Dies at 59
abstract: Ms. Maxwell, a painter, sculptor and curator, immersed herself in social causes and viewed art as a spiritual haven for homeless children.

name: Don Gregory
headline: Don Gregory, Theater Producer of Solo Shows, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Gregory worked with Richard Burton as King Arthur, Rex Harrison as Henry Higgins and many others.

name: Wojciech Fangor
headline: Wojciech Fangor, Painter Who Emerged From Postwar Poland, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Fangor, whose work was perched between Color Field painting and Op Art, enjoyed a career resurgence late in his life.

name: Hank Penza
profession: Owner of Mars Bar in the East Village
headline: Hank Penza, Owner of Mars Bar in the East Village, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Penza presided over the dive bar, one of the neighborhood’s last holdouts in the face of gentrification, until it closed in 2011.

name: Allen Toussaint
headline: Allen Toussaint, New Orleans R&B Mainstay, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Toussaint, a versatile producer and songwriter, was taken to a hospital after appearing in a concert in Madrid on Monday.

name: Helmut Schmidt
headline: Helmut Schmidt, Assertive West German Chancellor, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Schmidt, elected in 1974, often appeared to disregard diplomacy, but he pushed his country into a forceful international role during the waning Cold War years.

name: Vito J. Lopez
profession: Ex-New York Assemblyman Tainted by Scandal
headline: Vito J. Lopez, Ex-New York Assemblyman Tainted by Scandal, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Lopez, a former community organizer and legislator, was a power broker in New York City and Albany until he was brought down by a sexual harassment scandal.

name: Pat Eddery
headline: Pat Eddery, Prolific and Steely Jockey, Dies at 63
abstract: Eddery had three victories in the Epsom Derby and four in the Arc de Triomphe to his credit.

name: René Girard
profession: French Theorist of the Social Sciences
headline: René Girard, French Theorist of the Social Sciences, Dies at 91
abstract: Professor Girard’s explorations of literature and myth helped establish influential ideas about how people are motivated to want things.

name: Michael Leonard
headline: Michael Leonard, Whose Songs From Failed Musicals Endured, Dies at 84
abstract: The composer and arranger’s tunes for “The Yearling” were covered by Barbra Streisand, Nancy Wilson and many others.

name: André Glucksmann
headline: André Glucksmann, French Philosopher Who Renounced Marxism, Dies at 78
abstract: After publishing his most influential work, “The Master Thinkers,” Mr. Glucksmann became one of France’s most prominent public intellectuals.

name: Betsy Drake
headline: Betsy Drake, 92, Actress Who Starred With (and Wed) Cary Grant, Dies
abstract: Ms. Drake, a stage actress at the time, bumped into Grant on the Queen Mary, eloped with him and appeared with him in “Every Girl Should Be Married” and “Room for One More.”

name: Jacqueline Berrien
headline: Jacqueline Berrien, Head of E.E.O.C., Is Dead at 53
abstract: Ms. Berrien was a civil rights lawyer who was President Obama’s chairwoman of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission from 2010 to 2014.

name: Carol Doda
headline: Carol Doda, Pioneer of Topless Entertainment, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Doda, who started a topless revolution as a 26-year-old go-go dancer in 1964, had injected her breasts with enough silicone to expand her bra size to 44DD from 34B.

name: Richard Horowitz
profession: Timpanist and Craftsman of Conductors Batons
headline: Richard Horowitz, Timpanist and Craftsman of Conductors’ Batons, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Horowitz, who spent 66 years and some 10,000 performances with the Metropolitan Opera Orchestra, had stumbled into a second career making the directors’ sticks.

name: Gene Amdahl
headline: Gene Amdahl, Pioneer of Mainframe Computing, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Amdahl played a crucial role in developing the IBM System/360 series, which influenced computer design for years.

name: Nathaniel Marston
headline: Nathaniel Marston, ‘One Life to Live’ Actor, Dies at 40
abstract: Mr. Marston was known for playing a character who was brought back after he was killed off.

name: Fred McNeill
headline: Fred McNeill, Who Played in Two Super Bowls, Dies at 63
abstract: The Vikings linebacker went on to become a lawyer and a spokesman for former players who suffer from early onset dementia and other cognitive problems, as he did.

name: Phil Taylor
headline: Phil Taylor, Motorhead Drummer Who Helped Shape a Genre, Dies at 61
abstract: The “Philthy Animal” was credited with a drumming style that inspired some of the top metal bands of the 1980s and ’90s.

name: Rena Wolner
headline: Rena Wolner, Who Led 3 Major Paperback Publishers, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Wolner, president and publisher of Berkley, Pocket and Avon Books, helped lead the way in negotiating combined hardback and paperback deals with notable authors.

name: Abdul Karim al-Eryani
profession: Yemeni Politician Brokered Arab Spring Peace
headline: Abdul Karim al-Eryani, 81, Dies; Yemeni Politician Brokered Arab Spring Peace
abstract: A former prime minister and diplomat, Mr. Eryani helped bring about a peaceful change of government in 2011.

name: Gene Norman
profession: Music Producer With an Ear for Jazz
headline: Gene Norman, Music Producer With an Ear for Jazz, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Norman’s portfolio spread to the far corners of contemporary recording, with releases including a spoken-word album by Orson Welles and a Canadian easy-listening polka band.

name: Gene Norman
headline: Gene Norman, Who Helped Landmark Broadway Theaters, Dies at 85
abstract: As chairman of New York’s preservation commission, he also oversaw the preservation of St. Bartholomew’s Church, the Coney Island Cyclone and Ladies’ Mile.

name: Andy White
profession: Drummer on the Beatles Love Me Do
headline: Andy White, Drummer on the Beatles’ ‘Love Me Do,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. White, a studio musician renowned for his stylistic flexibility, sat in for the song at the band’s third recording session, while Ringo Starr played the tambourine.

name: Jack Yufe
headline: Jack Yufe, a Jew Whose Twin Was a Nazi, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Yufe became a celebrity after he and his brother were subjects in a study of nature versus nurture.

name: Tim Valentine
profession: 6-Term Democrat in Congress From North Carolina
headline: Tim Valentine, 89, 6-Term Democrat in Congress From North Carolina, Dies
abstract: Mr. Valentine was a moderate Democrat who supported the Voting Rights Act, though race was an underlying issue in his first House campaign.

name: Bruce B. Dayton
headline: Bruce B. Dayton, Minnesota Retailer and Arts Patron, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Dayton inherited what became the Dayton-Hudson Corporation from his grandfather and father.

name: Robert Craft
headline: Robert Craft, Stravinsky Adviser and Steward, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Craft’s close relationship with Stravinsky included sustaining and interpreting the composer’s legacy.

name: Aaron Shikler
profession: Portrait Artist Known for Images of Americas Elite
headline: Aaron Shikler, Portrait Artist Known for Images of America’s Elite, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Shikler was known for painting everyone from clowns and ballerinas to presidents, movie stars and socialites.

name: Hans Mommsen
profession: Documented Volkswagen Slave Labor in Nazi Era
headline: Hans Mommsen, 85, Dies; Documented Volkswagen Slave Labor in Nazi Era
abstract: Mr. Mommsen, a scholar of the Holocaust, was commissioned by Volkswagen to explore the company’s complicity in the crimes of the Third Reich.

name: P. F. Sloan
profession: Enigmatic Writer of 60s Hit Eve of Destruction
headline: P. F. Sloan, Enigmatic Writer of ’60s Hit ‘Eve of Destruction,’ Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Sloan wrote the apocalyptic anthem “Eve of Destruction” when he was 19. It became a No. 1 hit for Barry McGuire. He also wrote, with Steve Barri, “Secret Agent Man.”

name: Joel Elkes
profession: Cast Light on Brain Chemistry and Behavior
headline: Joel Elkes, Who Cast Light on Brain Chemistry and Behavior, Dies at 101
abstract: Dr. Elkes, a foundational figure in the study of psychosis, published the first scientific trial of a medication for schizophrenia as he explored the chemical underpinnings of being human.

name: Patrick Fallon
profession: Midwest Ad Agency Had National Reach
headline: Patrick Fallon, Whose Midwest Ad Agency Had National Reach, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Fallon’s Minneapolis version of Madison Avenue helped lift the fortunes of Rolling Stone magazine and Porsche and drew laughs with its “Cat Herders” Super Bowl commercial in 2000.

name: Robert F. Dall
headline: Robert F. Dall, Mastermind of Mortgage-Backed Bonds, Dies at 81
abstract: While at Salomon Brothers in the 1970s, Mr. Dall oversaw the first sale of bonds backed by American home mortgages to large private investors.

name: Jonah Lomu
profession: Rugby Superstar Melded Power and Speed
headline: Jonah Lomu, 40, Dies; Rugby Superstar Melded Power and Speed
abstract: Mr. Lomu’s size and strength made him a nearly unstoppable scorer for the New Zealand national team until a kidney disorder forced him into early retirement.

name: Stephen Birmingham
profession: Chronicler of the Rich and Other Elites
headline: Stephen Birmingham, Chronicler of the Rich and Other Elites, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Birmingham was the author of best sellers about a range of social strata and places like the Dakota apartment building.

name: Michael Gross
headline: Michael Gross, Who Designed the ‘Ghostbusters’ Logo, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Gross, a graphic designer and film producer, created several famous covers for National Lampoon magazine.

name: Seymour Lipkin
headline: Seymour Lipkin, Understated Pianist and Conductor, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Lipkin was often described as a Beethoven specialist, but his pianistic compass ranged from the Baroque era to the present day.

name: Beth Curry
headline: Beth Curry, Who Co-Founded Investment Firm and Philanthropy, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Curry and her husband, Ravenel Boykin Curry III, founded Eagle Capital Management in 1988.

name: Mal Whitfield
profession: Olympic Gold Medalist and Tuskegee Airman
headline: Mal Whitfield, Olympic Gold Medalist and Tuskegee Airman, Dies at 91
abstract: Whitfield was an orphan who went on to set six world records and win three Olympic gold medals for the United States in running.

name: Henry S. Rowen
headline: Henry S. Rowen, 90, RAND Chief Who Quit in Pentagon Papers Case, Dies
abstract: Mr. Rowen, a leading policy intellectuals for decades, resigned from RAND in 1971 after one of its two copies of the Pentagon Papers was leaked to the press.

name: John E. Zuccotti
headline: John E. Zuccotti, Urbanist, Financier and Would-Be Mayor, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Zuccotti was a street-smart urbanist and an unsung hero of New York City’s fiscal crisis in the 1970s.

name: Tom Buckley
headline: Tom Buckley, Versatile and Colorful Times Reporter, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Buckley, who worked at The New York Times from 1953 to 1982, covered a multitude of subjects including the United Nations and the war in Vietnam, and later wrote the column “About New York.”

name: Paul Laffoley
profession: Painter Inspired by Time Travel and Aliens
headline: Paul Laffoley, Painter Inspired by Time Travel and Aliens, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Laffoley, an outsider artist whose work was exhibited at Woodstock, said an extraterrestrial encouraged him to move the universe into the fifth dimension.

name: Bert Olmstead
profession: Hall of Fame Passer in Canadiens Dynasty
headline: Bert Olmstead, Hall of Fame Passer in Canadiens Dynasty, Dies at 89
abstract: Olmstead, with pinpoint passing, helped Montreal win five Stanley Cups in the 1950s. He did the same with the Toronto Maple Leafs in 1962.

name: Herbert Scarf
headline: Herbert Scarf, an Economist’s Mathematician, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Scarf, a Yale mathematician, never took an economics class, but his theories were accepted by businesses and governments.

name: Kim Young-sam
headline: Kim Young-sam, South Korean President Who Opposed Military, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Kim, an outspoken critic of military dictators, became the first civilian leader in South Korea in more than three decades when he was elected in 1992.

name: Saeed Jaffrey
profession: Actor in Gandhi and The Man
headline: Saeed Jaffrey, Actor in ‘Gandhi’ and ‘The Man Who Would Be King,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Jaffrey, best known in his native India for roles he characterized as “the naughty uncle,” had a career in radio, film, TV and onstage encompassing three continents.

name: Bob Foster
profession: Left Hook Decimated All but the Heavyweights
headline: Bob Foster, Whose Left Hook Decimated All but the Heavyweights, Dies at 76
abstract: Foster became a light-heavyweight champion in 1968 and went on to fight the legendary heavyweights Joe Frazier and Muhammad Ali, but he was knocked out by both.

name: Austin Kiplinger
profession: Co-Founder of a Personal Finance Magazine
headline: Austin Kiplinger, Co-Founder of a Personal Finance Magazine, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Kiplinger co-founded what is now Kiplinger’s Personal Finance magazine and expanded its parent company into a $100-million-a-year enterprise.

name: Ken Johnson
headline: Ken Johnson, Only Loser of 9-Inning No-Hitter, Dies at 82
abstract: The Houston Colt .45s pitcher threw a brilliant game against the Cincinnati Reds on April 23, 1964, only to lose in the ninth.

name: Adele Mailer
headline: Adele Mailer, Artist Who Married Norman Mailer, Dies at 90
abstract: Mrs. Mailer embraced the downtown arts scene and a bohemian lifestyle. In 1960, her husband stabbed her in the heart.

name: Douglass C. North
headline: Douglass C. North, Maverick Economist and Nobel Laureate, Dies at 95
abstract: In a seven-decade teaching career and in many books and articles, Mr. North became known for challenging traditional market-based methods of economic analysis.

name: Rex Reason
profession: Star of Sci-Fi Classic This Island Earth
headline: Rex Reason, Star of Sci-Fi Classic ‘This Island Earth,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Reason was known for roles like a heroic scientist in that film and a newspaperman in “The Roaring Twenties” TV series.

name: Charles M. Cawley
headline: Charles M. Cawley, Credit Card Pioneer, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Cawley’s MBNA Corporation introduced affinity credit cards, which are tied to sports teams, universities, professional associations and other organizations that inspire consumer loyalty.

name: Jim Perry
profession: Bustling Host of a Range of Game Shows
headline: Jim Perry, 82, Bustling Host of a Range of Game Shows, Dies
abstract: Mr. Perry was a mainstay of a broad range of such shows in the United States and Canada.

name: Mack McCormick
headline: Mack McCormick, Student of Texas Blues, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. McCormick, a folklorist who spent a lifetime searching out forgotten or unrecorded singers all over Texas, traveled thousands of miles to amass a blues archive.

name: David Canary
headline: David Canary, Star of ‘All My Children,’ Dies at 77
abstract: After first appearing on the soap opera in 1984, Mr. Canary won five Daytime Emmy Awards and received 16 nominations in the outstanding lead actor category.

name: Guy Lewis
profession: Coach of Houstons Phi Slama Jama Teams
headline: Guy Lewis, Coach of Houston’s Phi Slama Jama Teams, Dies at 93
abstract: Lewis coached the Cougars for 30 years, and to five Final Fours, but he is best remembered for his squads of the 1980s and their thunderous style of play.

name: Cynthia Robinson
profession: Sly and the Family Stone Trumpet Player
headline: Cynthia Robinson, Sly and the Family Stone Trumpet Player, Dies at 71
abstract: Ms. Robinson was part of the band’s biggest hits in the late 1960s and early ’70s.

name: Joseph Silverstein
headline: Joseph Silverstein, Violinist and Boston Symphony Concertmaster, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Silverstein, a conductor and violinist, joined the orchestra as its youngest player in 1955 before becoming its ninth concertmaster in 1962.

name: Setsuko Hara
profession: Japanese Star of Films by Ozu and Kurosawa
headline: Setsuko Hara, Japanese Star of Films by Ozu and Kurosawa, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Ms. Hara was lauded for her portrayal of tragic heroines torn between duty and desire. Her abrupt retirement in the 1960s shocked Japan.

name: Eldzier Cortor
profession: Painter of Scenes From African-American Social Life
headline: Eldzier Cortor, Painter of Scenes From African-American Social Life, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Cortor was perhaps best known for elegant paintings of nude black women in an era when they were rare in mainstream art.

name: Joan Duddy
profession: Nurtured Dance and Joyce SoHo in Manhattan
headline: Joan Duddy, Nurtured Dance and Joyce SoHo in Manhattan, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Duddy was an influential curator and advocate for new dance as the founder and director of the dance program at the Dia Center for the Arts (now Joyce SoHo) in Manhattan.

name: Norman C. Pickering
headline: Norman C. Pickering, Who Refined the Record Player, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Pickering, an engineer and musician, devised the Pickering pickup, a lightweight mechanism that reduced sound distortion and made records last longer.

name: Josephine Chaus
profession: Co-Founder and Re-Inventor of Fashion Brand
headline: Josephine Chaus, Co-Founder and Re-Inventor of Fashion Brand, Dies at 64
abstract: After her husband died and her company, Bernard Chaus Inc., faltered, Mrs. Chaus was able to rescue it from the brink of collapse in a way that surprised industry veterans.

name: James Prideaux
profession: Writer for Stage and for Television
headline: James Prideaux, Writer for Stage and for Television, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Prideaux wrote television movies that starred Katharine Hepburn and Elizabeth Taylor and a play for which Julie Harris won a Tony for best actress.

name: Yolanda Sonnabend
headline: Yolanda Sonnabend, Designer Who Influenced Choreographer, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Sonnabend had a long and successful collaboration with the British choreographer and Royal Ballet director Kenneth MacMillan.

name: Robert Ford
headline: Gen. Sir Robert Ford Is Dead at 91; British Commander on ‘Bloody Sunday’
abstract: General Ford was exonerated after two inquiries into the massacre, in which British paratroopers in Northern Ireland fatally shot 13 unarmed Roman Catholic civil rights protesters in 1972.

name: Robert Ford Jr.
headline: Robert Ford Jr., an Early Force in Hip-Hop, Is Dead at 70
abstract: He chronicled the scene when it was new, then went on to mentor some of its most important early figures, including Kurtis Blow and Russell Simmons.

name: Eldar Ryazanov
profession: Russian Film Director Known for His Satire
headline: Eldar Ryazanov, Russian Film Director Known for His Satire, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Ryazanov used the absurdities of everyday life in the Soviet Union and in the post-Gorbachev era to become one of Russia’s most popular directors and screenwriters.

name: Shigeru Mizuki
headline: Shigeru Mizuki, Influential Japanese Cartoonist, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Mizuki was known for his Kitaro manga series, the adventures of a one-eyed ghost-boy, and his depictions of the barbarities of war.

name: Maurice Strong
headline: Maurice Strong, Environmental Champion, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Strong was a former industrialist and confessed ecological sinner who was in the vanguard of placing environmentalism on the world’s agenda as a high-ranking United Nations official.

name: Luc Bondy
headline: Luc Bondy, Swiss-Born Theater and Opera Director, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Bondy’s productions were known for their probing of human behavior and were featured in Europe’s most prestigious theaters and opera houses.

name: Samuel Berger
headline: Samuel Berger, Adviser to Clinton Who Shaped Foreign Ties, Dies at 70
abstract: A political confidant of President Bill Clinton who held the foreign policy post at a moment when the U.S. was viewed as the world’s sole superpower.

name: Msgr. Richard Albert
profession: Fought for the Poor in Jamaica
headline: Msgr. Richard Albert, Who Fought for the Poor in Jamaica, Dies at 69
abstract: Through various philanthropies, Monsignor Albert established centers to provide food, education, health care and other services for drug addicts and people with H.I.V.

name: Mickey Corcoran
headline: Mickey Corcoran, Mentor to Bill Parcells, Dies at 93
abstract: A prominent figure in New Jersey athletics, Corcoran coached Parcells in high school basketball and then mentored him throughout Parcells’s N.F.L. coaching career.

name: Joseph F. Engelberger
headline: Joseph F. Engelberger, a Leader of the Robot Revolution, Dies at 90
abstract: A force in the early days of robotics, in the 1960s, Mr. Engelberger fostered the use of robots in auto plants and later hospitals.

name: Marcus Klingberg
profession: Highest-Ranking Soviet Spy Caught in Israel
headline: Marcus Klingberg, Highest-Ranking Soviet Spy Caught in Israel, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Klingberg, an Israeli scientist, was a Soviet spy whose activities were regarded as so damaging that he was imprisoned in secret for years under a false identity.

name: Joseph F. Girzone
profession: Created Christlike Figure in Joshua Novels
headline: Joseph F. Girzone, Who Created Christlike Figure in ‘Joshua’ Novels, Dies at 85
abstract: Father Girzone sold his first books about Joshua, a modern-day Christlike figure, from the trunk of his car.

name: George Sakato
profession: Awarded Medal of Honor Long After It Was Denied
headline: George Sakato, 94, Dies; Awarded Medal of Honor Long After It Was Denied
abstract: Mr. Sakato was the last survivor of the seven living Japanese-American veterans to whom tribute was paid more than a half a century after they fought gallantly for a nation that feared and loathed their people.

name: Steven Vogel
headline: Steven Vogel, Biologist Who Studied How Things Move, Dies at 75
abstract: Professor Vogel’s research and writing on how living things move in air and water helped define and popularize a new scientific field, comparative biomechanics.

name: Scott Weiland
headline: Scott Weiland, Singer Who Helped Found Stone Temple Pilots, Dies at 48
abstract: Mr. Weiland’s mercurial vocal style was a signature of the rock band he helped start, Stone Temple Pilots, and later of Velvet Revolver.

name: M. Roland Nachman
profession: Lawyer in Times v. Sullivan Libel Case
headline: M. Roland Nachman, Lawyer in Times v. Sullivan Libel Case, Dies at 91
abstract: The Alabama lawyer opposed The New York Times in a case that resulted in a Supreme Court decision establishing greater leeway for criticism of government officials and other public figures.

name: Melvin Williams
headline: Melvin Williams, an Inspiration for ‘The Wire,’ Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Williams, a drug kingpin in Baltimore, also played a role on the HBO show after he got out of prison.

name: Robert Loggia
headline: Robert Loggia, Rugged but Versatile Character Actor, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Loggia had a high-profile role as a drug lord in “Scarface.”

name: John Rassias
headline: John Rassias, Who Pioneered Foreign Language Teaching, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Rassias’s immersive approach to teaching foreign languages rapidly, known as the Rassias Method, has been used by thousands of teachers around the world since the 1960s.

name: Chuck Williams
headline: Chuck Williams, Founder of Williams-Sonoma, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Williams made kitchenware stylish and helped transform kitchens into gleaming, efficient refectories, making it possible for ordinary cooks to get serious.

name: Holly Woodlawn
headline: Holly Woodlawn, Transgender Star of 1970s Underground Films, Dies at 69
abstract: The actress, immortalized in the 1972 Lou Reed song “Walk on the Wild Side,” claimed a place in the Andy Warhol pantheon of stars.

name: Ray Gandolf
headline: Ray Gandolf, Sportscaster and ‘Our World’ Co-Anchor, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Gandolf, known for his genial manner in reporting for CBS and ABC, was co-anchor of the acclaimed but short-lived “Our World” on ABC in the 1980s.

name: Janet Wolfe
profession: Gothamite on a First-Name Basis With Her Era
headline: Janet Wolfe, Gothamite on a First-Name Basis With Her Era, Dies at 101
abstract: Known to readers of The New Yorker’s “Talk of the Town” department simply as “our friend Janet,” the longtime executive director of the New York City Housing Authority Symphony was equal parts Holly Golightly, Auntie Mame and Mehitabel.

name: Mariuccia Mandelli
headline: Mariuccia Mandelli, Italian Fashion Designer, Dies at 90
abstract: The designer, who founded the fashion house Krizia in the mid-1950s, reigned for decades as “the godmother of classic Milanese fashion.”

name: Amir Aczel
headline: Amir Aczel, Author of Scientific Cliffhanger, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Aczel sought out scientific topics with a colorful narrative behind them, including “Fermat’s Last Theorem,” a mathematical mystery published in 1996.

name: Timothy Seldes
headline: Timothy Seldes, Agent Who Championed Literary Stars, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Seldes was an editor and agent for some of the biggest names in literature, including notables like the Pulitzer winner Anne Tyler.

name: Douglas Tompkins
headline: Douglas Tompkins, 72, North Face Founder, Dies in Kayaking Accident
abstract: A hitchhiking encounter led to marriage and a store in San Francisco. Mr. Tompkins also founded the Esprit clothing brand before becoming a wealthy conservationist in South America.

name: Tibor Rubin
profession: Medal of Honor Was Delayed by Anti-Semitism
headline: Tibor Rubin Is Dead at 86; Medal of Honor Was Delayed by Anti-Semitism
abstract: Corporal Rubin was a Hungarian-born American hero, who joined the United States Army to thank the nation and the troops that rescued him from a Nazi concentration camp.

name: Arthur R. Taylor
headline: Arthur R. Taylor, Ex-CBS President Who Sold Yankees to Steinbrenner, Dies at 80
abstract: After he was fired from the network, Mr. Taylor became the founding president of a premium cable channel that was the predecessor of A&E.

name: C. Gerald Fraser
headline: C. Gerald Fraser, Longtime Reporter for The Times, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Fraser, one of the first black reporters hired by The Times, covered courts, culture and the landmark presidential campaign of Shirley Chisholm.

name: John Trudell
headline: John Trudell, Outspoken Advocate for American Indians, Is Dead at 69
abstract: Mr. Trudell was a leading advocate of Native American rights who channeled his message of righteous defiance into poetry and songwriting.

name: Fatema Mernissi
headline: Fatema Mernissi, a Founder of Islamic Feminism, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Mernissi, a Moroccan sociologist whose work included studies of the sexual politics of Islamic scripture and a memoir of her childhood in a domestic harem, published and lectured worldwide.

name: Arthur T. Hadley
profession: Writer of Critiques on U.S. Military
headline: Arthur T. Hadley, Writer of Critiques on U.S. Military, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Hadley, a journalist and author, learned about the armed forces firsthand as a veteran of World War II and as a consultant to the Joint Chiefs of Staff.

name: Dolph Schayes
headline: Dolph Schayes, a Bridge to Modern Basketball, Is Dead at 87
abstract: A 6-foot-8 forerunner of the power forward in today’s game, Schayes was the first N.B.A. player to score 15,000 points, a 12-time All-Star and a league champion with the 1955 Syracuse Nationals.

name: Gloria Contreras
headline: Gloria Contreras, Choreographer Mentored by Balanchine, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Contreras created more than 260 ballets for companies she directed in New York and Mexico, her native country.

name: Mattiwilda Dobbs
headline: Mattiwilda Dobbs, Soprano and Principal at Met, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Dobbs was the third African-American principal at the Metropolitan Opera. She also sang for Queen Elizabeth II and at the mayoral inauguration of her nephew Maynard Jackson of Atlanta.

name: Bonnie Lou
profession: Country and Rockabilly Star of the 1950s
headline: Bonnie Lou, Country and Rockabilly Star of the 1950s, Dies at 91
abstract: The singer began her career in the 1940s on radio in Ohio and then became a regular on the NBC music variety show “Midwestern Hayride.”

name: Charles S. Moffett
headline: Charles S. Moffett, Curator Who Focused on Impressionists, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Moffett redefined Monet and other artists with the exhibitions he organized at the Metropolitan Museum, the National Gallery and the Phillips Collection.

name: Bryony Brind
headline: Bryony Brind Dies at 55; Nureyev Lifted Ballerina’s Career
abstract: After the famous dancer discovered her, Ms. Brind rose to become a principal dancer for the Royal Ballet in London.

name: Marjorie Lord
profession: Actress on The Danny Thomas Show
headline: Marjorie Lord, Actress on ‘The Danny Thomas Show,’ Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Lord played many parts in television, film and theater after her breakthrough role as the dutiful wife on the Emmy-winning sitcom, but she always struggled against being typecast.

name: John Eaton
headline: John Eaton, Composer and Electronic Innovator, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Eaton, who was also an academic and inventor, was a creator of operas large and small.

name: Henry M. Rowan
headline: Henry M. Rowan, Industrialist Who Gave $100 Million Gift to University, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Rowan and his wife, Betty, made a $100 million donation to Glassboro State College in New Jersey in 1992, which was then the biggest individual cash gift to any public college or university.

name: Benedict Anderson
headline: Benedict Anderson, Scholar Who Saw Nations as ‘Imagined,’ Dies at 79
abstract: Dr. Anderson, an expert on Southeast Asia, transformed the study of nationalism with his book “Imagined Communities” and other works.

name: Lillian Vernon
profession: Creator of a Bustling Catalog Business
headline: Lillian Vernon, Creator of a Bustling Catalog Business, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Vernon’s company, started in 1951, once had revenues near $300 million and was the first owned by a woman to be listed on the American Stock Exchange.

name: Phil Pepe
headline: Phil Pepe, Longtime New York Sportswriter, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Pepe was best known for his baseball articles in New York newspapers and for his many books on the Yankees.

name: Evelyn Lieberman
profession: Aide Moved Lewinsky From White House
headline: Evelyn Lieberman, 71, Dies; Aide Moved Lewinsky From White House
abstract: As the first woman to serve as deputy chief of staff to a president, she worried about a onetime intern’s maturity and the potential for damaging rumors in the Clinton White House.

name: Glen Sonmor
headline: Glen Sonmor, 86, a Brawling N.H.L. Coach
abstract: Sonmor guided a young Minnesota North Stars team to the Stanley Cup finals.

name: Luigi Creatore
profession: Songwriter and Producer for Presley and Sam Cooke
headline: Luigi Creatore, Songwriter and Producer for Presley and Sam Cooke, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Creatore teamed with his cousin Hugo Peretti to create hits for stars like Perry Como, Little Peggy Marsh (“I Will Follow Him”) and the disco artist Van McCoy.

name: Walter J. Leonard
profession: Pioneer of Affirmative Action in Harvard Admissions
headline: Walter J. Leonard, Pioneer of Affirmative Action in Harvard Admissions, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Leonard was the architect of an influential affirmative-action formula at Harvard that was emulated across the country and also served as president of Fisk University.

name: Alfred C. Snider
headline: Alfred C. Snider, Who Promoted Healthy Debate as Just That, Dies at 65
abstract: Professor Snider was a scholar, rhetorician and evangelist who sought to heal the world through debate and in the process turned Vermont into the argumentative center of the world.

name: Peter Dickinson
profession: Master Plotter Relished a Good Puzzle
headline: Peter Dickinson, Author, Dies at 88; Master Plotter Relished a Good Puzzle
abstract: Mr. Dickinson was an award-winning British mystery writer whose books for adults and children often crossed the boundaries between crime, adventure, science fiction, fantasy and suspense.

name: Terry Backer
headline: Terry Backer, 61, Legislator Who Helped Clean Up Long Island Sound
abstract: Mr. Backer, a 12-term state representative in Connecticut, played a major role in largely successful efforts to clean up one of the country’s biggest estuaries.

name: Licio Gelli
headline: Licio Gelli, Italian Financier and Cabal Leader, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Gelli was a self-professed fascist accused of being the grandmaster of a secret society that plotted a right-wing coup, among other crimes and scandals.

name: George Ortman
headline: George Ortman, Artist Whose Works Presaged Minimalism, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Ortman’s creations included geometric designs that sought to surmount the limits of the flat canvas.

name: Alden Amos
profession: Spinning Wheels Gave Craft a Brighter Fate
headline: Alden Amos, Whose Spinning Wheels Gave Craft a Brighter Fate, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Amos, a big, bearded, overall-clad craftsman and teacher whom admirers called “the best curmudgeon in the world,” helped spur the modern revival of handspinning.

name: Kurt Masur
headline: Kurt Masur, Conductor Who Transformed New York Philharmonic, Dies at 88
abstract: When Mr. Masur took the helm, the orchestra was roundly considered to be a world-class ensemble in name only. He restored it to renown.

name: Anthony Muto
headline: Anthony Muto, Designer Who Dressed Three First Ladies, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Muto had his own labels, Marita by Anthony Muto and A.M./P.M., and was known in particular for his relaxed, unfussy evening wear.

name: Rick Curry
profession: Used Stagecraft to Help the Wounded and Disabled
headline: Rev. Rick Curry, 72, Dies; Used Stagecraft to Help the Wounded and Disabled
abstract: Father Curry, who was born without a right forearm, embraced stagecraft as his vehicle to overcome what others viewed as a handicap.

name: Robert Kobayashi
headline: Robert Kobayashi, Artist of Whimsy, Dies at 90
abstract: In 1977, Mr. Kobayashi bought the building on Elizabeth Street housing Moe’s Meat Market, a butcher shop, and turned it into his personal gallery with whimsical displays that delighted passers-by for decades.

name: Charles F. Harris
profession: Led Effort to Publish Work by Black Writers
headline: Charles F. Harris, 81, Dies; Led Effort to Publish Work by Black Writers
abstract: He spent much of his career chipping away at the prevailing notion in the industry that writing by black authors or aimed at black readers belonged to a niche market.

name: Patricia Elliott
profession: Tony Winner and Soap Opera Star
headline: Patricia Elliott, 77, Tony Winner and Soap Opera Star, Dies
abstract: Ms. Elliott won a Tony for best featured actress in a musical (and a Drama Desk Award) in 1973 for playing a Swedish countess in the original production of Stephen Sondheim’s “A Little Night Music.”

name: Joe Jamail
headline: Joe Jamail, Flamboyant Texas Lawyer Who Won Billions for Clients, Dies at 90
abstract: Jamail, a spirited courtroom performer, found national fame when, representing Pennzoil, he won a $10.5 billion judgment against Texaco in 1994 — a record then.

name: Fernande Grudet
profession: Ran High-Society Call-Girl Ring as Madame Claude
headline: Fernande Grudet, 92, Dies; Ran High-Society Call-Girl Ring as ‘Madame Claude’
abstract: In her heyday, Madame Claude presided over 500 women she called her swans; she claimed her clients included John F. Kennedy and the shah of Iran.

name: Snuff Garrett
headline: Snuff Garrett, Record Producer Who Made a String of Hits, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Garrett, a former disc jockey, produced records for Bobby Vee, Del Shannon, Gary Lewis & the Playboys, Cher and others.

name: Angela McEwan
headline: Angela McEwan, Late-Blooming Actress in ‘Nebraska,’ Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. McEwan was about 70 when she began acting. She was the former flame of Bruce Dern’s hapless old man in “Nebraska” and had a role in the TV series “Parks and Recreation.”

name: Noboru Ando
headline: Noboru Ando, Mobster Film Star in Japan, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Ando drew on his extensive gang experience to become a major player in the yakuza genre.

name: Peggy Say
headline: Peggy Say, Voice for Hostages in Lebanon, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Say waged a nearly seven-year campaign to draw attention to a hostage situation in Lebanon, where her brother was held for nearly seven years.

name: Alfred G. Gilman
profession: Work on Proteins Won Nobel Prize
headline: Dr. Alfred G. Gilman, Whose Work on Proteins Won Nobel Prize, Dies at 74
abstract: Dr. Gilman, whose research advanced the understanding of cancer, diabetes and other diseases, died Wednesday in Dallas.

name: Arlin Adams
profession: Federal Judge Three Times on Supreme Court Short List
headline: Arlin Adams, Federal Judge Three Times on Supreme Court Short List, Dies at 94
abstract: Known for deep Republican political ties in Pennsylvania and respected legal scholarship, Judge Adams led investigations into two former Reagan administration cabinet members.

name: Vonette Z. Bright
profession: Founder of Campus Crusade for Christ
headline: Vonette Z. Bright, a Founder of Campus Crusade for Christ, Dies at 89
abstract: Mrs. Bright began the evangelical organization, now called Cru in the United States, with her husband, Dr. William R. Bright, in 1951 in Los Angeles.

name: Robert D. Douglas Jr.
headline: Robert D. Douglas Jr., Eagle Scout Elder and Adventurer, Dies at 103
abstract: One of the nation’s oldest Eagle Scouts, Mr. Douglas had shot a lion on safari in Africa, hunted whales and grizzly bears in Alaska and written two books on his travels by age 17.

name: Robert S. Douglas
profession: Founder of the Black Dog Apparel Company
headline: Robert S. Douglas, Founder of the Black Dog Apparel Company, Dies at 93
abstract: The logo for his tavern on Martha’s Vineyard transformed a black Labrador-boxer mix into an international emblem for summertime.

name: Lewis M. Dabney
profession: Devoted Lifes Work to Edmund Wilson
headline: Lewis M. Dabney, Who Devoted Life’s Work to Edmund Wilson, Dies at 83
abstract: Professor Dabney, who taught at the University of Wyoming, spent more than 40 years immersed in Wilsoniana.

name: Robert Spitzer
profession: Psychiatrist Set Rigorous Standards for Diagnosis
headline: Robert Spitzer, 83, Dies; Psychiatrist Set Rigorous Standards for Diagnosis
abstract: Dr. Spitzer issued the first set of rigorous standards to describe mental disorders, providing a framework for diagnosis, research and legal judgments.

name: Haskell Wexler
headline: Haskell Wexler, Oscar-Winning Cinematographer, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Wexler was known for being outspoken during a career that included films like “Medium Cool” and “Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf?”

name: George Clayton Johnson
headline: George Clayton Johnson, Science Fiction Writer, Dies at 86
abstract: Often addressing issues of aging and mortality, Mr. Johnson was co-author of “Logan’s Run” and also wrote episodes of “The Twilight Zone” and the first televised episode of “Star Trek.”

name: Ellsworth Kelly
profession: Shaped Geometries on a Bold Scale
headline: Ellsworth Kelly, Who Shaped Geometries on a Bold Scale, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Kelly, who shaped his distinctive style of American painting in the years after World War II, showed influences of Picasso and Byzantine mosaics.

name: Meadowlark Lemon
headline: Meadowlark Lemon Dies at 83; Harlem Globetrotters’ Dazzling Court Jester
abstract: Known for his charismatic clowning and his halfcourt hook shots, Lemon was the Globetrotters’ top showman for more than two decades.

name: John Duffy
headline: John Duffy, a Composer Who Gave His Peers a Platform, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Duffy, a prolific writer of symphonic music and operas, was the founder and longtime director of the organization Meet the Composer.

name: Lemmy Kilmister
headline: Lemmy Kilmister, the Hard-Living, Jagged Voice of Motörhead, Dies at 70
abstract: Ian Fraser Kilmister, a heavy metal singer known as Lemmy, led the loud, fast British rock band Motörhead for decades, becoming an emblem of rock ‘n’ roll endurance.

name: Jocelyn Cooper
profession: Helped Pave Way for First Black Congresswoman
headline: Jocelyn Cooper Dies at 86; Helped Pave Way for First Black Congresswoman
abstract: Ms. Cooper and her husband, Andrew Cooper, sued in the early 1960s to challenge racially gerrymandered congressional district lines, which were redrawn under court order.

name: Stein Eriksen
headline: Stein Eriksen, Olympic Ski Champion Who Heralded Freestyle, Dies at 88
abstract: Eriksen was an Olympic ski champion whose competitive triumphs, elegant style and innovative acrobatics made him one of the sport’s first superstars.

name: Sidney Mintz
headline: Sidney Mintz, Father of Food Anthropology, Dies at 93
abstract: Professor Mintz was often described as the father of food anthropology, after the critical and popular success of his 1985 book, “Sweetness and Power: The Place of Sugar in Modern History.”

name: Donald Weinstein
headline: Donald Weinstein, Influential Historian on the Renaissance, Dies at 89
abstract: Professor Weinstein’s 1970 book about Savonarola overturned long-held assumptions about 15th-century Florence and redrew the contours of Renaissance scholarship.

name: Doug Atkins
profession: Feared Hall of Fame Pass Rusher
headline: Doug Atkins, a Feared Hall of Fame Pass Rusher, Dies at 85
abstract: Atkins, a 6-foot-8 defensive end mostly associated with the Chicago Bears and the University of Tennessee, terrified quarterbacks in the days before sacks were an official statistic.

name: Murray Weissman
profession: Publicist With a Focus on Oscar Campaigning
headline: Murray Weissman, Publicist With a Focus on Oscar Campaigning, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Weissman, who started at a time when publicity meant hot tips for newspaper reporters, worked on behalf of at least 38 best-picture nominees.

name: Edward Hugh
headline: Edward Hugh, Economist Who Foresaw Eurozone’s Struggles, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Hugh’s blog, which pointed out flaws at the root of Europe’s ambition to bind together disparate economies with a single currency, attracted a wide following.

name: Frank Malzone
profession: Star Fielder for Boston Red Sox
headline: Frank Malzone, Star Fielder for Boston Red Sox, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Malzone was a six-time All-Star third baseman and remarkably durable, playing in more than 150 games in seven consecutive seasons.

name: Allen Lacy
headline: Allen Lacy, a Professor Turned Gardening Columnist, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Lacy, a philosophy professor who sowed his cultivated wit and wisdom for The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal, wrote or edited 10 books on gardening.

name: Howard Davis Jr.
profession: Beat Grief to Win Boxing Gold
headline: Howard Davis Jr., Who Beat Grief to Win Boxing Gold, Dies at 59
abstract: Davis, who was mourning his mother when he earned a gold medal at the 1976 Montreal Olympics, had more than 100 victories as an amateur but never won a world title.

name: Wayne Rogers
headline: Wayne Rogers, Who Played Trapper John in ‘M*A*S*H,’ Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Rogers was on the show for just the first three of its 11 seasons as the army surgeon Trapper John, but his run, and his character, are especially revered by show devotees.

name: Gina DePalma
headline: Gina DePalma, Acclaimed Pastry Chef at Babbo, Dies at 49
abstract: Ms. DePalma, a chef who prized flavor above eye appeal, helped make Babbo one of Manhattan’s most beloved and admired restaurants.

name: Natalie Cole
headline: Natalie Cole, ‘Unforgettable’ Voice and Million-Selling Hitmaker, Dies at 65
abstract: Ms. Cole was a Grammy winner whose biggest hit was “Unforgettable,” a virtual duet with her father, Nat King Cole, that topped the 1991 charts.

name: Dale Bumpers
headline: Dale Bumpers, Liberal Stalwart of Arkansas Politics, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Bumpers, a four-term United States senator, was part of a generation of moderate Southern Democrats to emerge in the late 1960s and ’70s.

name: Hocine Aït-Ahmed
headline: Hocine Aït-Ahmed, a Pro-Democracy Algerian Leader, Dies at 89
abstract: After freedom from France, Mr. Aït-Ahmed remained an influential figure in Algerian politics, pushing for democracy and opposing successive governments.

name: John Holm
profession: Opened Linguistics to Creole and Pidgin Tongues
headline: John Holm, 72, Dies; Opened Linguistics to Creole and Pidgin Tongues
abstract: Mr. Holm studied creole and pidgin languages spoken by millions of people around the world, especially the English-derived creoles of the Caribbean.

name: John Angelo
profession: Investor and Co-Founder of Angelo Gordon
headline: John Angelo, Investor and Co-Founder of Angelo Gordon, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Angelo started Angelo Gordon with Michael Gordon in 1988, and helped build it into an investment firm with $26 billion in assets.

name: Woody Hochswender
