headline: Woody Hochswender, Fashion Reporter, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Hochswender wrote a column about the garment industry for The New York Times and popular books on Buddhism.

name: Jason Wingreen
headline: Jason Wingreen, Actor Who Voiced Boba Fett, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Wingreen’s long list of television roles included that of Harry the bartender on “All in the Family” and “Archie Bunker’s Place.”

name: Vilmos Zsigmond
profession: Gave Hollywood Films a New Look
headline: Vilmos Zsigmond, Cinematographer, Dies at 85; Gave Hollywood Films a New Look
abstract: Mr. Zsigmond lent a hyper-real glow to the arrival of space aliens and won an Oscar for Steven Spielberg’s 1977 “Close Encounters of the Third Kind.”

name: Robert Stigwood
headline: Robert Stigwood, Impresario of Rock, Film and Stage, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Stigwood’s name was attached to films, albums and theatrical productions that identified an era in music.

name: Richard Sapper
headline: Richard Sapper, Designer of Sleek Housewares, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Sapper was especially revered by coffee connoisseurs for his lustrous stovetop Coban 9090 espresso maker, sold by Alessi, the Italian housewares manufacturer.

name: Igor D. Sergun
headline: Igor D. Sergun, Chief of Russian Military Intelligence, Dies at 58
abstract: General Sergun managed Russia’s military intelligence service, known as the G.R.U., which has been accused of playing a crucial role in the 2014 takeover of Crimea.

name: Paul Bley
headline: Paul Bley, Adventurous Jazz Pianist, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Bley’s style of playing was melodic, measured, bluesy, often polytonal and seemingly effortless.

name: Eugenie Schwartz
headline: Eugenie Schwartz, Artist From New Orleans, Dies at 64
abstract: Ms. Schwartz, who was known as Ersy, found popularity and renown in her native New Orleans for her surreal, darkly humorous pieces.

name: Elizabeth Swados
headline: Elizabeth Swados, Creator of Socially Conscious Musicals, Is Dead at 64
abstract: The composer, writer and director worked on numerous productions, including “Runaways” and “Kasper Hauser,” that, she said, “should reflect what and how we are now.”

name: Pierre Boulez
headline: Pierre Boulez, Composer and Conductor Who Pushed Modernism’s Boundaries, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Boulez belonged to an extraordinary generation of European composers who, while in their 20s, came to the forefront during the decade or so after World War II.

name: Gilbert E. Kaplan
headline: Gilbert E. Kaplan, Publisher and Improbable Conductor, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Kaplan, the founder of Institutional Investor magazine, turned his obsession with Mahler’s Second Symphony into a vocation, leading international orchestras in its performance.

name: Robert H.B. Baldwin
headline: Robert H.B. Baldwin, Transformer of Morgan Stanley, Dies at 95
abstract: As president and chairman, Mr. Baldwin expanded the investment bank into a full-service financial brokerage and changed its long-entrenched culture.

name: Alan S. Gordon
profession: Colorful Union Leader in Opera and Ballet
headline: Alan S. Gordon, Colorful Union Leader in Opera and Ballet, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Gordon, who was the executive director of the American Guild of Musical Artists, represented singers, dancers and stage managers at major companies.

name: Judith S. Kaye
profession: First Woman to Serve as New Yorks Chief Judge
headline: Judith S. Kaye, First Woman to Serve as New York’s Chief Judge, Dies at 77
abstract: Judge Kaye was the first woman named to New York’s highest court and held the job of chief judge longer than any of her 21 male predecessors.

name: Kitty Kallen
profession: Big Band Singer of Bésame Mucho
headline: Kitty Kallen, Big Band Singer of ‘Bésame Mucho,’ Dies at 94
abstract: Her voice, sweet and clear, welcomed the troops home from World War II, singing, “Kiss me one, kiss me twice, kiss me once again.”

name: Pat Harrington
profession: Super on One Day at a Time
headline: Pat Harrington, the Super on ‘One Day at a Time,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Harrington was best known for his award-winning role as Schneider on the CBS sitcom.

name: Ashraf Pahlavi
profession: Twin Sister of Irans Last Shah
headline: Ashraf Pahlavi, Twin Sister of Iran’s Last Shah, Dies at 96
abstract: The princess was a close ally and staunch defender of her brother, Shah Mohammed Reza Pahlavi.

name: Ted Stanley
headline: Ted Stanley, Whose Son’s Illness Inspired Philanthropy, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Stanley, who made his fortune selling collectibles, gave hundreds of millions of dollars to biomedical research on psychiatric disorders.

name: Ted Stanley
headline: Ted Stanley, Whose Fentanyl Lollipop Treated Chronic Pain, Dies at 77
abstract: His invention, a palatable means of delivering a synthetic opioid analgesic, was a breakthrough for cancer patients young and old.

name: Stephen W. Bosworth
headline: Stephen W. Bosworth, U.S. Diplomat Who Helped Oust Ferdinand Marcos, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Bosworth persuaded the Philippine dictator to allow free elections, then delivered Washington’s pink slip to him when he refused to accept defeat.

name: André Courrèges
headline: André Courrèges, Fashion Designer Who Redefined Couture, Dies at 92
abstract: His ‘Space Age’ collection upended the little black dress.

name: George Elsey
profession: One of the Last Survivors of World War II White House
headline: George Elsey, One of the Last Survivors of World War II White House, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Elsey worked in the White House Map Room under Presidents Roosevelt and Truman, and later became an assistant to Truman, writing policy papers and speeches.

name: Florence King
headline: Florence King, Writer Who Wielded an Acerbic Wit, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. King, who wrote “Misanthrope’s Corner” for National Review, could sting her targets even as she made them laugh.

name: Rick Cluchey
headline: Rick Cluchey Dies at 82; Prison Theater Was His Redemption
abstract: After his release from prison, Mr. Cluchey spent time in Europe with Samuel Beckett.

name: Ellen Stovall
headline: Ellen Stovall, Three-Time Cancer Survivor and Advocate, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Stovall led a grass-roots campaign to make cancer treatment and prevention, and the search for a cure, the top health care and research priorities in the United States.

name: Billie Allen
headline: Billie Allen, Actress Who Bridged a Racial Gap, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Allen appeared on and off Broadway when New York theater was not especially welcoming to black performers, and she helped integrate network television.

name: Harry F. Mariani
headline: Harry F. Mariani, Who Introduced Americans to Lambrusco, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Mariani was a wine importer who, with his brother, made a fortune, first with Riunite, a sparkling, sweet red product of Italy.

name: David Bowie
profession: Star Transcended Music, Art and Fashion
headline: David Bowie Dies at 69; Star Transcended Music, Art and Fashion
abstract: Mr. Bowie taught generations of musicians about the power of drama, images and personas. He had been treated for cancer for the last 18 months.

name: Richard Libertini
profession: Had Memorable Turn in The In-Laws
headline: Richard Libertini, Actor, Dies at 82; Had Memorable Turn in ‘The In-Laws’
abstract: Mr. Libertini, a ubiquitous presence on stage, screen and television, was best known for his antic turn as the deranged General Garcia in the 1979 film comedy.

name: Bill Foster
headline: Bill Foster, Coach Who Set Duke on Winning Track, Dies at 86
abstract: Mike Krzyzewski has become associated with Duke’s rise as a basketball power, but it was his predecessor, Foster, who re-energized the program after it had languished in mediocrity.

name: Monte Irvin
headline: Monte Irvin, Star Outfielder Who Lost His Prime to Racism, Dies at 96
abstract: Irvin, among the most talented players in the Negro leagues, was already 30 when he joined the New York Giants in 1949. “I was way past my peak then,” he later said.

name: David Margulies
profession: Ghostbusters Mayor and Tony Sopranos Lawyer
headline: David Margulies, ‘Ghostbusters’ Mayor and Tony Soprano’s Lawyer, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Margulies, a versatile character actor, performed in scores of supporting stage, film and television roles.

name: Michael W. Davidson
headline: Michael W. Davidson, a Success in Microscopes and Neckwear, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Davidson created psychedelic images of crystallized substances like DNA and hormones. Many of those images ended up on ties, millions of which were sold.

name: Michael Davidson
headline: Dr. Michael Davidson, Who Studied Infectious Disease, Dies at 77
abstract: He told a friend that he would have relished the chance to help end the coronavirus pandemic had he still been active in the field. The virus claimed him instead.

name: Stanley Siegel
headline: Stanley Siegel, TV Host Who Made Career on Candor, Dies at 79
abstract: The New York broadcaster’s unscripted interviews coupled Jack Paar’s raw candor with Oscar Wilde’s credo that nothing succeeds like excess.

name: Red Simpson
profession: Made Trucks a Vehicle for the Bakersfield Sound
headline: Red Simpson, Who Made Trucks a Vehicle for the Bakersfield Sound, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Simpson, who wrote songs recorded by Buck Owens, Merle Haggard and others, had his first Top 10 country hit with 1971’s “I’m a Truck.”

name: Brian Bedford
headline: Brian Bedford, Stage Actor Who Brought the Classics to Life, Dies at 80
abstract: The versatile Mr. Bedford gained renown at Stratford in Canada and on Broadway portraying dozens of characters, most notably in works by Shakespeare, Molière and Chekhov.

name: Chocolate Armenteros
headline: Chocolate Armenteros, Trumpeter in Afro-Cuban Tradition, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Armenteros could often be found at the center of the genre’s changes, playing with innovators and popularizers including Arsenio Rodríguez, Cachao Lopez, Benny Moré and Eddie Palmieri.

name: Sylvan Barnet
headline: Sylvan Barnet, Scholar, Is Dead at 89; Edited Signet Shakespeare Paperbacks
abstract: A Tufts University professor introduced generations of college students to the bard through the Signet Classic Shakespeare series.

name: Myra Carter
profession: Dying Mother in Albees Three Tall Women
headline: Myra Carter, Dying Mother in Albee’s ‘Three Tall Women,’ Dies at 86
abstract: The actress was closely associated with the Albee canon, starting with her performance of this unpleasant character in the 1990s.

name: Alan Rickman
profession: Watchable Villain in Harry Potter and Die Hard
headline: Alan Rickman, Watchable Villain in ‘Harry Potter’ and ‘Die Hard,’ Dies at 69
abstract: The British actor brought an erudite dignity to film roles like the nefarious mastermind of “Die Hard” and the dour master of potions in the “Harry Potter” series.

name: Luis Arroyo
headline: Luis Arroyo, Baseball’s Best Reliever in ’61, Dies at 88
abstract: A left-hander with a baffling screwball, he pitched in two World Series and as a reliever helped Whitey Ford achieve his finest season with the Yankees.

name: Giorgio Gomelsky
headline: Giorgio Gomelsky, Impresario Who Gave the Rolling Stones Their Start, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Gomelsky, who was born on a ship going from Ukraine to Italy, also worked with the Yardbirds early in their career.

name: René Angélil
profession: Discovered and Then Married Celine Dion
headline: René Angélil, Who Discovered and Then Married Celine Dion, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Angélil recognized Ms. Dion’s singing talent when she was 12 and guided her career for more than 30 years.

name: Dan Haggerty
headline: Dan Haggerty, Who Played Grizzly Adams, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Haggerty parlayed a beard and a bear into a role that endeared him to viewers of a film and television series both titled “The Life and Times of Grizzly Adams.”

name: Dave Sime
profession: Worlds Fastest Sprinter, but Far From Its Luckiest
headline: Dave Sime Dies at 79; World’s Fastest Sprinter, but Far From Its Luckiest
abstract: An injury kept Sime out of the 1956 Olympics and bad luck cost him a gold medal in 1960; he became an ophthalmologist whose patients included Richard Nixon and Ted Williams.

name: C. D. Wright
headline: C. D. Wright, Poet of Ozarks and Beyond, Dies at 67
abstract: Ms. Wright, whose work mixes the commonplace and the fantastic and was informed by her Arkansan heritage, considered poetry writing an act of social responsibility.

name: Maria Teresa de Filippis
headline: Maria Teresa de Filippis, Pioneer of Auto Racing, Dies at 89
abstract: De Filippis, an Italian aristocrat who helped reopen a sport to women, drove in Formula 1 world championship grands prix.

name: Leonid Zhabotinsky
headline: Leonid Zhabotinsky, Strongman for the Ages, Dies at 77
abstract: The Big Zhabo, as he was known, set his first of 19 world superheavyweight weight-lifting records in 1963.

name: Peggy Anderson
headline: Peggy Anderson, Chronicler of the Nursing Profession, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Anderson wrote the 1978 best seller “Nurse,” which was based on interviews with a nurse. It was adapted into a TV movie and a TV series.

name: Richard G. Hendrickson
headline: Richard G. Hendrickson, Who Recorded the Weather for 85 Years, Dies at 103
abstract: Mr. Hendrickson took his first weather reading from the family farm in 1930 and only retired, reluctantly, last year.

name: Ted Marchibroda
headline: Ted Marchibroda, Who Led Colts and Ravens, Dies at 84
abstract: The N.F.L. coach turned around struggling Colts teams in Baltimore and in Indianapolis, then returned to Baltimore as the first head coach of the Ravens.

name: Noreen Corcoran
headline: Noreen Corcoran, ‘Bachelor Father’ Actress, Dies at 72
abstract: Ms. Corcoran grew up before television viewers in the 1950s and ’60s as a teenager during five seasons of the sitcom that also starred John Forsythe.

name: Glenn Frey
headline: Glenn Frey, Singer-Songwriter and Eagles Founding Member, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Frey teamed up with Don Henley in founding the Eagles, whose melodic, country-tinged rock was enormously popular in the 1970s, selling more records than any other band then.

name: George Jonas
profession: Book Was the Basis of the Film Munich
headline: George Jonas, Whose Book Was the Basis of the Film ‘Munich,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Jonas was a prominent Canadian newspaper columnist whose controversial book about Israeli counterterrorists was the basis of the 2005 film.

name: Leila Alaoui
profession: Photographer Wounded in Burkina Faso Siege
headline: Leila Alaoui, Photographer Wounded in Burkina Faso Siege, Dies at 33
abstract: Ms. Alaoui, a French-Moroccan whose photographs chronicled the themes of migration and cultural identity, was injured during the assault in the capital, Ouagadougou.

name: Marie Garibaldi
profession: First Woman on New Jersey Supreme Court
headline: Marie Garibaldi, First Woman on New Jersey Supreme Court, Dies at 81
abstract: Justice Garibaldi voted to uphold the death penalty and wrote decisions that defined sexual harassment in the workplace and declared Princeton’s all-male eating clubs discriminatory.

name: George Weidenfeld
profession: British Publisher of Lolita and London Fixture
headline: George Weidenfeld, British Publisher of ‘Lolita’ and London Fixture, Dies at 96
abstract: Penniless, Mr. Weidenfeld escaped the Nazi annexation of Austria and built a reputation as an international networker, party-giver and raconteur. Last year he created a fund to help persecuted Christian refugees from Syria.

name: Wilkes Bashford
headline: Wilkes Bashford, Clothier to Affluent San Franciscans, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Bashford’s clothing emporium catered to elegance-conscious San Franciscans for a half-century.

name: Ettore Scola
profession: Italian Film Director of Satire and Farce
headline: Ettore Scola, Italian Film Director of Satire and Farce, Dies at 84
abstract: In more than 40 films directed over 40 years, Mr. Scola focused on people always haplessly swept along by the tides of their times.

name: Michel Tournier
headline: Michel Tournier, French Novelist Who Fused Myth and Philosophy, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Tournier’s “Ogre,” the story of a French prisoner of war who procured boys for an elite Hitler youth camp, won the Prix Goncourt, in 1970.

name: Mustafa Koc
headline: Mustafa Koc, Leader of Turkish Conglomerate, Dies at 55
abstract: Since 2003, Mr. Koc had been chairman of Koc Holding, the vast enterprise founded by his grandfather, then led by his father.

name: Edmonde Charles-Roux
profession: Novelist and Editor of French Vogue
headline: Edmonde Charles-Roux, Novelist and Editor of French Vogue, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Charles-Roux’s first novel, “To Forget Palermo,” won the Prix Goncourt, France’s biggest literary prize, in 1966, four months after the magazine ousted her.

name: Lou Michaels
headline: Lou Michaels, All-Purpose Player, Dies at 80; Missed Kicks in ‘69 Super Bowl
abstract: The former All-American, all-purpose football player missed two field-goal attempts during the New York Jets’ upset of the Baltimore Colts.

name: Forrest McDonald
headline: Forrest McDonald, Historian Who Punctured Liberal Notions, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. McDonald, a conservative who opposed intrusive government, lionized the founding fathers as uniquely intellectual and wrote over a dozen books.

name: Bill Johnson
headline: Bill Johnson, U.S. Olympic Downhill Skiing Champion, Dies at 55
abstract: Johnson, a brash competitor, delivered on his promise to win gold in 1984, at Sarajevo, but was severely injured in a 2001 comeback at age 40 aimed at winning back his ex-wife.

name: Lois Weisberg
headline: Lois Weisberg, Chicago’s Cultural Connector, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Weisberg spent decades as a city administrator responsible for organizing public arts projects, earning recognition as a “type of person who seems to know everybody.”

name: Clarence Reid
profession: Singer and Songwriter Also Known as Blowfly
headline: Clarence Reid, Singer and Songwriter Also Known as Blowfly, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Reid and his Blowfly alter ego had success on two different fronts: soul and pre-rap music.

name: David Stoliar
profession: Survivor of World War II Disaster
headline: David Stoliar, Survivor of World War II Disaster, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Stoliar was the only survivor among nearly 800 Jews fleeing Romania’s Holocaust aboard a ship that was barred from Palestine, interned by Turkey, set adrift and torpedoed by a Soviet submarine.

name: Bobby Wanzer
profession: Hall of Fame Player From N.B.A.s Early, Patient Days
headline: Bobby Wanzer, 94, Hall of Fame Player From N.B.A.’s Early, Patient Days, Dies
abstract: Mr. Wanzer, a guard, led the Rochester Royals to the 1951 N.B.A. championship, the only league title of that much-traveled team, whose modern-day successor are the Sacramento Kings.

name: Henry Worsley
profession: British Adventurer Trying to Cross Antarctica
headline: Henry Worsley, a British Adventurer Trying to Cross Antarctica, Dies at 55
abstract: Mr. Worsley abandoned his 1,000-mile trek only 30 miles from his goal after suffering from exhaustion and dehydration.

name: Marvin Minsky
headline: Marvin Minsky, Pioneer in Artificial Intelligence, Dies at 88
abstract: Professor Minsky laid the foundation for the field by demonstrating the possibilities of imparting common-sense reasoning to computers.

name: Abe Vigoda
headline: Abe Vigoda, of ‘Godfather’ and ‘Barney Miller,’ Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Vigoda was reported dead 34 years ago — erroneously — a story that stuck with him and helped make him a cult figure.

name: Thornton Dial
headline: Thornton Dial, Outsider Artist Whose Work Told of Black Life, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Dial was a self-taught artist whose paintings and assemblages fashioned from scavenged materials found their way to the permanent collections of major museums.

name: John Jay Hooker Jr.
headline: John Jay Hooker Jr., Political Gadfly and Perennial Litigant, Dies at 85
abstract: Although Mr. Hooker repeatedly lost his races for elective office in Tennessee, he managed to advance a progressive agenda through his candidacies and as a plaintiff.

name: Mrinalini Sarabhai
headline: Mrinalini Sarabhai, Indian Classical Dancer and Choreographer, Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Sarabhai brought ancient South Indian dance forms into the 20th century and infused her work with social commentary.

name: Robert Tuggle
profession: Longtime Archivist of the Metropolitan Opera
headline: Robert Tuggle, Longtime Archivist of the Metropolitan Opera, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Tuggle helped create a digital database that includes details from every performance since the Met opened with Gounod’s “Faust” on Oct. 22, 1883.

name: Anna Laerkesen
headline: Anna Laerkesen, Danish Ballerina With Poetic Originality, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Laerkesen had huge success in the title role of “La Sylphide,” in which she was partnered by Erik Bruhn, Peter Martins and Rudolf Nureyev.

name: Concepcion Picciotto
profession: Kept Vigil by White House for Three Decades
headline: Concepcion Picciotto, Who Kept Vigil by White House for Three Decades, Dies
abstract: Ms. Picciotto maintained a peace vigil in Lafayette Park for more than 30 years in what is considered the longest political protest in American history.

name: Marvin Lipofsky
headline: Marvin Lipofsky, Ceramist Who Elevated Blown Glass to Fine Art, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Lipofsky worked glass into small-scale biomorphic shapes with a dazzling array of surface textures produced by cutting, grinding and sandblasting.

name: Walt Williams
headline: Walt Williams, Outfielder Known as No Neck, Dies at 72
abstract: Williams, a free-swinging outfielder who played most of his career with the White Sox, was probably best known for the unusual physique that earned him an unusual nickname.

name: Herbert L. Abrams
headline: Dr. Herbert L. Abrams, Who Worked Against Nuclear War, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Abrams, an expert in cardiovascular radiology, was a founder of International Physicians for the Prevention of Nuclear War, which won a Nobel Peace Prize for its work.

name: Vincent A. Cianci Jr.
profession: Celebrated and Scorned Ex-Mayor of Providence
headline: Vincent A. Cianci Jr., Celebrated and Scorned Ex-Mayor of Providence, R.I., Dies at 74
abstract: Known as “Buddy,” Mr. Cianci was known for protracted troubles with the law as well as for unfailing devotion to his city.

name: Michael J. Kennedy
headline: Michael J. Kennedy, Lawyer for Underdogs and Pariahs, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Kennedy defended John Gotti Sr., Huey P. Newton and Timothy Leary and won freedom for Jean S. Harris, who killed the Scarsdale Diet doctor.

name: Paul Kantner
headline: Paul Kantner, a Founder of Jefferson Airplane, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Kantner wrote or helped write many of the songs that defined the San Francisco psychedelic sound of the 1960s.

name: Sahabzada Yaqub Khan
headline: Sahabzada Yaqub Khan, Pakistani Diplomat, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Yaqub Khan had a role in facilitating President Richard Nixon’s overture to China in 1972 and helped negotiate the Soviet withdrawal from Afghanistan.

name: Jacques Rivette
profession: French New Wave Director of Enigmatic Films
headline: Jacques Rivette, French New Wave Director of Enigmatic Films, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Rivette may not have been as well known as his colleagues François Truffaut and Jean-Luc Godard, but his work was revered by film aficionados.

name: Yvonne Chouteau
headline: Yvonne Chouteau, Native American Ballerina, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Chouteau, a former principal dancer of the Ballet Russe de Monte Carlo, was one of five celebrated Native American dancers from Oklahoma.

name: Kenny Sailors
headline: Kenny Sailors, a Pioneer of the Jump Shot, Dies at 95
abstract: A number of players can claim to be the one who created the shot that revolutionized basketball, but many students of the game give the distinction to Sailors.

name: John Romas
profession: Leader of Greek Church at Ground Zero
headline: The Rev. John Romas, Leader of Greek Church at Ground Zero, Dies at 86
abstract: Father Romas was appointed pastor of St. Nicholas Greek Orthodox Church in 1987, and took his small congregation to Brooklyn after the church was destroyed during the terror attacks of Sept. 11, 2001.

name: Myron Beldock
headline: Myron Beldock, Civil Rights Lawyer Who Fought for Lost Causes, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Beldock was known for defending and winning freedom for people who had been convicted and imprisoned, including the boxer Rubin “Hurricane” Carter and a defendant in the Central Park Jogger case.

name: Denise Duval
headline: Denise Duval, French Soprano and Poulenc Interpreter, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Duval, a foremost interpreter of Francis Poulenc’s works, was also known for her performances of compositions by other French masters.

name: Howard Koslow
headline: Howard Koslow Dies at 91; Artist Designed Stamps for 40 Years
abstract: Mr. Koslow was a painter and illustrator who for more than four decades designed many of the most recognizable stamps issued by the United States Postal Service.

name: Murray Louis
headline: Murray Louis, Choreographer With a Comic Flair, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Louis was notable for his quick directional shifts, tiny darting gestures and unexpected contrasts between rigidity and stillness.

name: Francisco Flores
headline: Francisco Flores, Tainted Ex-President of El Salvador, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Flores was facing charges of diverting $15 million in contributions for earthquake victims to his personal and political party accounts.

name: Gordon Goody
profession: Leader of the Gang in the Great Train Robbery
headline: Gordon Goody, a Leader of the Gang in the Great Train Robbery, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Goody, who finished a 12-year prison term (and a life of crime) to become a beachfront bar owner in Spain, had been one of three surviving gang members.

name: David G. Hartwell
headline: David G. Hartwell, Literary-Minded Editor of Science Fiction, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Hartwell brought a literary sensibility to genres like horror, fantasy and science fiction, working with authors like Frank Herbert and Philip K. Dick.

name: Bob Elliott
profession: Half of the Deadpan Bob and Ray Comedy Team
headline: Bob Elliott, Half of the Deadpan Bob and Ray Comedy Team, Dies at 92
abstract: The comedian and his partner, Ray Goulding, specialized in low-key humor that debunked gasbags.

name: Jack Riley
profession: U.S. Coach of 1960 Gold Medal Hockey Team
headline: Jack Riley, U.S. Coach of 1960 Gold Medal Hockey Team, Dies at 95
abstract: Riley, who coached at Army from 1950 to 1986, transformed his team of bickering amateurs into Olympic champions at the Squaw Valley Games.

name: Maurice White
headline: Maurice White, Founder and Leader of Earth, Wind & Fire, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. White and his band were award-winning hit makers for much of the 1970s.

name: Mary Fiumara
profession: Mother in Indelible Prince Spaghetti Ad
headline: Mary Fiumara, Mother in Indelible Prince Spaghetti Ad, Dies at 88
abstract: Mrs. Fiumara played the devoted mother who shouted “Anthony! Anthony!” from her apartment window in a commercial for Prince spaghetti that ran for 13 years.

name: Alice Denham
profession: Kissed and Told About Literary New York
headline: Alice Denham, Who Kissed and Told About Literary New York, Dies at 89
abstract: In “Sleeping With Bad Boys,” Ms. Denham, a former Playboy centerfold, chronicled her years of literary striving and sexual adventure.

name: David Mirra
headline: David Mirra, BMX Bike Star, Dies in an Apparent Suicide
abstract: Mirra was found dead at age 41 with what the police said was an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound.

name: Lorna Jorgenson Wendt
profession: Defender of Rights of Corporate Ex-Wives
headline: Lorna Jorgenson Wendt, 72, Defender of Rights of Corporate Ex-Wives
abstract: Married to Gary Wendt, chief of GE Capital, she turned down a $10 million settlement, instead wanting half of what she believed to be $100 million in assets.

name: Edgar D. Mitchell
headline: Edgar D. Mitchell, Sixth Moonwalking Astronaut, Dies at 85
abstract: Commander Mitchell, a member of NASA’s first lunar mission devoted exclusively to scientific research, Apollo 14, spent just over nine hours on the moon on two moonwalks.

name: Marlow W. Cook
headline: Marlow W. Cook, Senator Who Groomed Mitch McConnell, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Cook, a moderate Republican from Kentucky, made Mr. McConnell his assistant in Washington but later criticized him for moving sharply to the right.

name: John L. Tishman
headline: John L. Tishman, Builder Who Shaped American Skylines, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Tishman’s company oversaw the construction of the John Hancock Center in Chicago and the twin towers of the World Trade Center in Manhattan.

name: Miriam Cedarbaum
headline: Miriam Cedarbaum, U.S. Judge, Dies at 86; Sentenced Martha Stewart
abstract: Judge Cedarbuam oversaw thousands of cases since 1986, including the 2004 trial of Martha Stewart that brought wide public attention.

name: Frank Finlay
headline: Frank Finlay, 89, Is Dead; Was Iago to Olivier’s Othello
abstract: Mr. Finlay, an English actor, was often cast as a rogue or villain and was nominated for an Academy Award for his role in the 1965 film version of “Othello.”

name: Robin Chandler Duke
headline: Robin Chandler Duke, Philanthropist Who Championed Women’s Rights, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Duke, a former reporter, executive and ambassador, was a prominent voice for health and education initiatives in Africa, Asia and elsewhere.

name: Dan Hicks
headline: Dan Hicks, of the Hot Licks, Dies at 74; Countered the ’60s Sound
abstract: A singer-songwriter’s band countered the psychedelic sound of late 1960s San Francisco with proudly eccentric and catchy music that he came to call “folk swing.”

name: Michael Brick
headline: Michael Brick, Former Times Reporter, Dies at 41
abstract: Mr. Brick helped cover the collapse of Enron, the aftermath of Hurricane Katrina and offbeat sports for The Times.

name: Gregg Feinstein
profession: Head of Mergers at Houlihan Lokey
headline: Gregg Feinstein, 54, Dies; Head of Mergers at Houlihan Lokey
abstract: Mr. Feinstein was one of the rare bankers who publicly advised shareholder activists on their campaigns for change at corporations.

name: Richard P. Von Herzen
headline: Richard P. Von Herzen, Explorer of Earth’s Undersea Furnaces, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Von Herzen, an oceanographer, uncovered thousands of miles of interconnected volcanoes where the planet’s oceanic plates pull apart and ooze molten rock.

name: Paul Aiken
headline: Paul Aiken, Who Championed Authors in Digital Era, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Aiken fought for copyrights and royalties in the early days of the digital age, defending the principle that creators should be rewarded for their work..

name: Artur Fischer
profession: Inventor With More Patents Than Edison
headline: Artur Fischer, Inventor With More Patents Than Edison, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Fischer, an obsessive tinkerer, created a wall anchor that’s used by millions and the first synchronized camera flash, an idea that came to him when trying to photograph his newborn daughter.

name: Sam Spence
profession: Set the Fierce Dance of the N.F.L. to Music in Film
headline: Sam Spence, Who Set the Fierce Dance of the N.F.L. to Music in Film, Dies at 88
abstract: Spence’s compositions were used to set the mood for NFL Films, and he was the last survivor of the four men credited with popularizing the football highlight genre.

name: Violette Verdy
profession: Theatrical Star of Balanchines City Ballet
headline: Violette Verdy, a ‘Theatrical’ Star of Balanchine’s City Ballet, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Verdy made her inflected dancing style work with multiple choreographers, including the more straightforward George Balanchine.

name: Arnold Lubasch
headline: Arnold Lubasch, Who Covered Crime for The Times, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Lubasch, who wrote about a multitude of federal trials, worked at The New York Times for more than 30 years.

name: Margaret Forster
profession: Author of Georgy Girl and More
headline: Margaret Forster, Author of ‘Georgy Girl’ and More, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Forster turned away from writing light and entertaining novels to biographies and works that grappled with history and social issues.

name: Zdravko Tolimir
headline: Zdravko Tolimir, General Tied to Srebrenica Massacre, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Tolimir, a Bosnian Serb former general, was serving a life sentence for his role in the massacre of more than 7,000 Muslim prisoners in 1995.

name: Leslie Bassett
headline: Leslie Bassett, Pulitzer Prize-Winning Composer, Dies at 93
abstract: Known for his lush sonorities and ecumenical instrumentation, Mr. Bassett wrote for orchestras, chamber and choral ensembles and solo instruments.

name: Sushil Koirala
headline: Sushil Koirala, Ex-Premier of Nepal Who Fought for Democracy, Dies at 77
abstract: As prime minister, Mr. Koirala last year presided over the adoption of Nepal’s first democratic Constitution written by an elected assembly.

name: Giacomo Tachis
profession: Brought French Influence to Italian Wine
headline: Giacomo Tachis, Who Brought French Influence to Italian Wine, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Tachis, an oenologist by training, helped develop top-quality wines that used French grape varieties, an approach that proved transformative for the world of Italian wine.

name: Willie Richardson
headline: Willie Richardson, Baltimore Colts’ All-Pro Receiver, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Richardson was an All-Pro receiver for the Baltimore Colts and their leading pass-catcher in Super Bowl III, when the Jets otherwise stymied their offense in a huge upset victory.

name: Tommy Kelly
headline: Tommy Kelly, Who Played a Hollywood Tom Sawyer, Dies at 90
abstract: A Bronx boy picked by David O. Selznick to star in “The Adventures of Tom Sawyer,” Mr. Kelly later left the movies for a career in education.

name: Drew Lewis
profession: Transportation Secretary During Air Controllers Strike
headline: Drew Lewis, Transportation Secretary During Air Controllers’ Strike, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Lewis, who was also an executive known for rescuing failing companies, put together a temporary system to keep planes in the air during the 1981 strike.

name: Jake Page
headline: Jake Page, Editor Who Made Science Accessible, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Page worked for book publishers and Smithsonian magazine and wrote books on several areas of science, natural history and the American Indian.

name: Antonin Scalia
headline: Antonin Scalia, Justice on the Supreme Court, Dies at 79
abstract: Justice Scalia, whose legal theories, vivid writing and outsize personality made him a conservative leader, was found dead on Saturday in Texas.

name: Warren Manzi
profession: Author of New Yorks Longest-Running Play
headline: Warren Manzi, Author of New York’s Longest-Running Play, Dies at 60
abstract: “Perfect Crime” logged its 11,824th performance, despite the fact that critics often did not like it and theatergoers often did not understand it.

name: Johnny Lattner
headline: Johnny Lattner, Heisman-Winning Halfback With Notre Dame, Dies at 83
abstract: Lattner, who was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1979, was an all-around talent who excelled at both offense and defense.

name: Steven Stucky
headline: Steven Stucky, Composer Who Won a Pulitzer, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Stucky was associated with the Los Angeles Philharmonic as composer in residence for more than 20 years.

name: Leo Van Munching Jr.
headline: Leo Van Munching Jr., Empire Builder for Heineken, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Van Munching went to work for his father’s company in the 1950s and expanded the Heineken brand, and by 1971, it accounted for 41 percent of all imported beer sales in the country.

name: Denise Matthews
headline: Denise Matthews, Pop Singer Known as Vanity, Dies at 57
abstract: Ms. Matthews toured with Prince in the 1980s before eschewing her wild persona for life as a minister.

name: Boutros Boutros-Ghali
headline: Boutros Boutros-Ghali, Former U.N. Secretary General, Dies at 93
abstract: The Egyptian diplomat led the United Nations in a chaotic period that began with hopes for peace after the Cold War but ended after a single term.

name: John J. Riccardo
headline: John J. Riccardo, Former Chairman of Chrysler, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Riccardo, who took over at a time of turmoil in 1975, recruited Lee Iacocca to succeed him, a bet that paid off when it helped win government aid.

name: Jerome Weinrib
headline: Jerome Weinrib, ABC Carpet’s Old-School Proprietor, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Weinrib helped build a business started by his grandfather in 1897 into a string of stores that generate $150 million in annual sales.

name: George Gaynes
headline: George Gaynes, a Versatile Character Actor, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Gaynes appeared in hundreds of episodes of sitcoms and dramas on television, 35 Hollywood and made-for-television films, and many plays, musical comedies and operas in New York and Europe.

name: Acel Moore
headline: Acel Moore, Founder of Black Journalists’ Organization, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Moore awakened his white colleagues and their readers in Philadelphia to everyday life in black communities.

name: Andrzej Zulawski
headline: Andrzej Zulawski, Rebellious Film Director, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Zulawski, known primarily to a small art-house and film festival audience, made no concessions to logic, ordinary human motivations or audience squeamishness.

name: William H. Tankersley
headline: William H. Tankersley, Watchdog for CBS Taste Standards, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Tankersley was in effect the network’s main censor from the mid-1950s to 1972, a time of envelope-pushing, though he saw his job as guarding CBS’s reputation.

name: Angela Raiola
profession: Big Ang of TVs Mob Wives
headline: Angela Raiola, ‘Big Ang’ of TV’s ‘Mob Wives,’ Dies at 55
abstract: Ms. Raiola was the formidable but lovable reality TV star who attracted a cult following as a cast member of the VH1 show.

name: Mohamed Hassanein Heikal
headline: Mohamed Hassanein Heikal, Prominent Egyptian Journalist, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Heikal’s career was defined by his close partnership with President Gamal Abdel Nasser, whom he helped write landmark speeches and a political manifesto.

name: Harper Lee
profession: Author of To Kill a Mockingbird
headline: Harper Lee, Author of ‘To Kill a Mockingbird,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Lee’s novel about racial injustice in a small Alabama town became one of the most beloved works of fiction ever written by an American.

name: Umberto Eco
headline: Umberto Eco, 84, Best-Selling Academic Who Navigated Two Worlds, Dies
abstract: Mr. Eco was an expert in the arcane field of semiotics whose seven works of fiction included the blockbuster medieval mystery “The Name of the Rose.”

name: Tony Phillips
headline: Tony Phillips, Whose Play Sealed 1989 World Series, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Phillips spent half of his 18-year major league career with the Oakland Athletics, finding glory with them in a World Series delayed by an earthquake.

name: Msgr. Thomas J. Hartman
headline: Msgr. Thomas J. Hartman, Half of ‘God Squad,’ Dies at 69
abstract: Monsignor Hartman wrote a syndicated column and appeared on radio and on a cable television show as part of an interfaith duo with Rabbi Marc Gellman beginning in 1987.

name: Dana Raphael
profession: Proponent of Breast-Feeding and Use of Doulas
headline: Dana Raphael, Proponent of Breast-Feeding and Use of Doulas, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Raphael, a medical anthropologist and protégée of Margaret Mead, was among the first scientists to challenge milk formula manufacturers.

name: Jim Davenport
headline: Jim Davenport, an Original San Francisco Giant, Dies at 82
abstract: Davenport, an infielder who started with the Giants in 1958, their first season in California, won a Gold Glove in 1962, the year the team lost to the Yankees in the World Series.

name: Renato Bialetti
headline: Renato Bialetti, the Mr. Coffee of Italy, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Bialetti created a marketing campaign that popularized the Moka Express, and led to it becoming a fixture in nearly every kitchen in Italy with sales around the world.

name: Rosario Ferré
headline: Rosario Ferré, Writer Who Examined Puerto Rican Identity, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Ferré, who wrote novels in both Spanish and English, was a finalist for the National Book Award in 1995 for “A House on the Lagoon.”

name: Douglas L. Inman
headline: Douglas L. Inman, Coastal Science Pioneer, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Inman helped change the understanding of the processes that shape the beach and trained generations of scientists who followed in his footprints.

name: Michael Jaharis
headline: Michael Jaharis, Pharmaceutical Executive and Philanthropist, Dies at 87
abstract: For nearly half a century, Mr. Jaharis navigated the industry, tinkering with existing drugs to create and sell a series of more refined products.

name: Eric Brown
profession: Record-Breaking British Aviator and World War II Combat Pilot
headline: Eric Brown, Record-Breaking British Aviator and World War II Combat Pilot, Dies at 97
abstract: In a career spanning the era of biplanes to the threshold of spaceflight, Captain Brown flew 487 types of aircraft, more than any pilot in history.

name: John E. Reinhardt
profession: Ambassador and Head of U.S. Information Agency
headline: John E. Reinhardt, Ambassador and Head of U.S. Information Agency, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Reinhardt was the first black American ambassador to Nigeria, and the first career diplomat and first university educator to lead the information agency.

name: Peter Mondavi
profession: Helped Put Napa Valley on Wine Industry Map
headline: Peter Mondavi, Who Helped Put Napa Valley on Wine Industry Map, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Mondavi introduced ideas like cold fermentation to produce crisp whites, but he and his brother, Robert, clashed over the years.

name: Fernando Cardenal
headline: Fernando Cardenal, Nicaraguan Priest Who Defied Pope, Dies at 82
abstract: Steeped in a movement committed to a Marxist agenda of promoting social justice and easing poverty, Father Cardenal joined the revolutionary Sandinista cabinet.

name: Barbara M. Clark
headline: Barbara M. Clark, New York Assemblywoman, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Clark, a Democrat and the Assembly’s deputy majority whip, made public education her signature issue over three decades in Albany.

name: Sonny James
profession: Country Singer Known for Young Love
headline: Sonny James, Country Singer Known for ‘Young Love,’ Dies at 87
abstract: A genial crooner of the 1960s and ’70s nicknamed the Southern Gentleman, Mr. James had 26 No.­1 country hits to his credit.

name: Ramón Castro
headline: Ramón Castro, Brother to Cuban Revolutionaries, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Castro, a rancher and the elder brother of Fidel and Raúl, took a smaller role in the country’s Communist revolution and government.

name: Henry Diamond
profession: Lawyer at Forefront of Conservation Movement
headline: Henry Diamond, Lawyer at Forefront of Conservation Movement, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Diamond hitched his political star to the Rockefellers and was New York State’s first conservation commissioner in 1970; he also served on presidential advisory committees.

name: Alisa Bellettini
profession: Creator of MTVs House of Style
headline: Alisa Bellettini, Creator of MTV’s ‘House of Style,’ Dies at 61
abstract: “House of Style” was both glamorous and approachable, an attempt to mix the worlds of style and music in a way that would appeal to young viewers.

name: Elizabeth Eisenstein
headline: Elizabeth Eisenstein, Trailblazing Historian of Movable Type, Dies at 92
abstract: In “The Printing Press as an Agent of Change,” Professor Eisenstein argued that the proliferation of print shops had a seismic effect on civilization.

name: Edward T. Foote
profession: Led and Lifted University of Miami
headline: Edward T. Foote, Who Led and Lifted University of Miami, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Foote sought to dispel the university’s reputation as Suntan U., and presided over a nearly tenfold increase in the university’s endowment.

name: Yolande Betbeze Fox
headline: Yolande Betbeze Fox, Miss America Who Defied Convention, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Fox helped set new standards for beauty pageants by refusing to tour the country in revealing bathing suits as Miss America of 1951.

name: John Gagnon
headline: John Gagnon, Who Linked Sexuality to Social Influences, Dies at 84
abstract: Professor Gagnon shifted the ground in sex research, proposing that sexuality is shaped in the world, not in the psyche.

name: Sarah Kershaw
headline: Sarah Kershaw, Former Times Reporter, Dies at 49
abstract: Ms. Kershaw joined The New York Times in 1995 as a news clerk. She became known for her ability to spot trends and write offbeat feature articles.

name: Tony Burton
profession: Apollo Creeds Trainer in Rocky Movies
headline: Tony Burton, Apollo Creed’s Trainer in ‘Rocky’ Movies, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Burton, who played Duke in six Rocky films, was a former boxing champion himself.

name: George C. Nichopoulos
headline: George C. Nichopoulos, Elvis’s Last Doctor, Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Nichopoulos, who lost his medical license for overprescribing addictive drugs, was the singer’s personal physician in the decade before his death.

name: Andy Bathgate
headline: Andy Bathgate, Standout on Dismal 1950s Rangers, Dies at 83
abstract: Bathgate set a team record for goals and was elected to the Hockey Hall of Fame, but he won the Stanley Cup only after being traded to Toronto.

name: Elias Demetracopoulos
profession: Journalist Linked Greek Junta to Nixon
headline: Elias Demetracopoulos, 87, Dies; Journalist Linked Greek Junta to Nixon
abstract: The enigmatic Mr. Demetracopoulos often exasperated the State Department, once sued the C.I.A. and was honored in his homeland as a champion of freedom.

name: Eddie Einhorn
profession: Creator of College Basketball on TV
headline: Eddie Einhorn, a Creator of College Basketball on TV, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Einhorn, who created a sports network that propelled national interest in college basketball, was also an owner and team president of the Chicago White Sox.

name: Sam Beall
profession: Farm-to-Table Restaurateur Right on His Farm
headline: Sam Beall, Farm-to-Table Restaurateur Right on His Farm, Dies at 39
abstract: Mr. Beall turned Blackberry Farm, his parents’ country inn in eastern Tennessee, into a national destination and was a leader in the farm-to-table movement.

name: Wesley A. Clark
headline: Wesley A. Clark, Who Designed First Personal Computer, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Clark’s designs built a bridge from the era of mainframe systems that were programmed with stacks of punch cards to personal computers that respond interactively to a user.

name: George Kennedy
profession: Versatile Actor Won Oscar for Cool Hand Luke
headline: George Kennedy Dies at 91; Versatile Actor Won Oscar for ‘Cool Hand Luke’
abstract: With the exception of his Academy Award performance in 1967 and his work in about a dozen other films, Mr. Kennedy was most often a peripheral player.

name: Claude Parent
headline: Claude Parent, Visionary Architect of the Oblique, Dies at 93
abstract: The French architect broke rule after rule on his way to developing a radical aesthetic that was all his own.

name: Alice Arlen
profession: Screenwriter and Collaborator With Nora Ephron
headline: Alice Arlen, Screenwriter and Collaborator With Nora Ephron, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Arlen and Ms. Ephron were Oscar nominees for their screenplay for “Silkwood.” Ms. Arlen, scion of a prominent journalism family, also wrote “Alamo Bay,” directed by Louis Malle, and other films.

name: Craig Windham
headline: Craig Windham, Top-of-the-Hour Voice of NPR, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Windham, a veteran NPR reporter, was known for delivering bite-size news reports in a warm, familiar tone to millions of Americans.

name: Holbrook Kohrt
headline: Dr. Holbrook Kohrt, Hemophiliac Who Made Condition a Crusade, Dies at 38
abstract: Inspired by his own body’s ability to suppress disease, Dr. Kohrt pursued a medical career that coupled basic science with a clinical practice.

name: Nabil Maleh
headline: Nabil Maleh, Giant of Syrian Cinema, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Maleh’s best-known films pushed the envelope in his country, challenging a rigid government and strict social mores.

name: Stuart J. Beck
profession: American Champion of a Pacific Island Nation
headline: Stuart J. Beck, American Champion of a Pacific Island Nation, Dies at 69
abstract: A lawyer and television executive, Mr. Beck persuaded Palau to claim a U.N. seat and then occupied it as its ambassador.

name: Jim Kimsey
profession: AOL Co-Founder Influenced Generation of Net Providers
headline: Jim Kimsey Dies at 76; AOL Co-Founder Influenced Generation of Net Providers
abstract: Long before Facebook or Twitter, Mr. Kimsey was a co-founder of AOL, connecting a nascent online audience with news and information as never before.

name: Aubrey McClendon
headline: Aubrey McClendon, Chesapeake Energy Ex-Chief, Dies Day After Indictment
abstract: Authorities said Mr. McClendon, who built a fortune in shale gas across the country, was killed when his car drove into a bridge.

name: William H. Schaap
profession: Radical Lawyer and Critic of C.I.A
headline: William H. Schaap, Radical Lawyer and Critic of C.I.A., Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Schaap counseled war resisters, exposed covert C.I.A. activities, and published Jim Garrison’s book on the John F. Kennedy assassination.

name: Delmer Berg
profession: Last of American Volunteers in Spanish Civil War
headline: Delmer Berg, Last of American Volunteers in Spanish Civil War, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Berg was one of nearly 3,000 Americans who, as the Abraham Lincoln Brigade, fought Franco’s fascist forces in the late 1930s.

name: Dick Bradsell
headline: Dick Bradsell, Bartender Who Helped Revive London Cocktail Scene, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Bradsell’s influence was felt throughout Britain and as far away as Australia thanks to bartenders trained by him or inspired by his creations.

name: Edward Lammer
headline: Edward Lammer, Doctor Who Linked Acne Drug to Birth Defects, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Lammer was among the first to establish a link between the acne medicine Accutane and human birth defects, and who became an advocate for the families of affected children.

name: John Chilton
headline: John Chilton, Jazz Musician and Historian, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Chilton, a trumpet-playing fixture on the British jazz scene, wrote a survey of Billie Holiday’s career, definitive biographies and a memoir.

name: Louise Rennison
profession: Wrote Adolescent Novels With a Personal Touch
headline: Louise Rennison, Who Wrote Adolescent Novels With a Personal Touch, Dies at 64
abstract: Ms. Rennison’s semi-autobiographical young-adult books were written in the form of a diary of a British teenager named Georgia Nicolson.

name: Bud Collins
profession: Covered Tennis With Authority and Flash
headline: Bud Collins, Who Covered Tennis With Authority and Flash, Dies at 86
abstract: In nearly half a century of covering the sport, Mr. Collins broadcast from Wimbledon for NBC and wrote extensively for The Boston Globe.

name: Robert Palladino
headline: Rev. Robert Palladino, Scribe Who Shaped Apple’s Fonts, Dies at 83
abstract: Father Palladino was a world-renowned master of calligraphy who taught Steve Jobs the importance — and aesthetics — of scripts.

name: Ralph Baruch
headline: Ralph Baruch, Who Shaped Viacom’s Rise, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Baruch, the first president and chief executive of Viacom, transformed it from a small cable and syndication company into a communications and entertainment giant.

name: Pat Conroy
profession: Author of The Prince of Tides and The Great Santini
headline: Pat Conroy, Author of ‘The Prince of Tides’ and ‘The Great Santini,’ Dies at 70
abstract: The writer’s troubled relationship with his father, as well as the lush coastal landscapes of the South, were perennial subjects of his fiction and memoirs.

name: Tom Knight
headline: Tom Knight, Brooklyn’s Baseball Sage, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Knight was the first and only official baseball historian of Brooklyn, and though it was not certain that he had any official duties, his qualifications were indisputable.

name: Tony Dyson
headline: Tony Dyson, Who Brought R2-D2 to Rolling, Beeping Life, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Dyson originally built eight models of the robot for the first “Star Wars” film, some operated by remote control and two fitted with a seat inside for the actor Kenny Baker.

name: Myron G. Schultz
headline: Dr. Myron G. Schultz, Who Helped Identify AIDS Crisis, Dies at 81
abstract: Dr. Schultz, an infectious disease epidemiologist, detected a cluster of pneumonia cases that proved “the opening salvo for the AIDS epidemic,” he later recalled.

name: Nancy Reagan
headline: Nancy Reagan, an Influential and Protective First Lady, Dies at 94
abstract: Mrs. Reagan was a fierce guardian of her husband’s image, sometimes at the expense of her own, and a trusted adviser to Ronald Reagan.

name: Nikolaus Harnoncourt
headline: Nikolaus Harnoncourt, Conductor and Early-Music Specialist, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Harnoncourt, who was also a cellist, founded the period-instrument ensemble Concentus Musicus Wien and worked regularly with many of Europe’s major orchestras.

name: Robert Del Tufo
headline: Robert Del Tufo, Former New Jersey Attorney General, Dies at 82
abstract: As a United States attorney for New Jersey, Mr. Del Tufo challenged the federal Abscam investigation, arguing that the F.B.I. had entrapped a senator.

name: Al Wistert
profession: Tenacious All-Pro Tackle for Champion Eagles Teams
headline: Al Wistert, a Tenacious All-Pro Tackle for Champion Eagles Teams, Dies at 95
abstract: Wistert was named a first-team All-Pro six times and was considered one of the finest players to miss out on election to the Pro Football Hall.

name: Raymond Tomlinson
headline: Raymond Tomlinson, Who Put the @ Sign in Email, Is Dead at 74
abstract: The computer programmer chose the “at” sign to separate a user name from a destination address in his new messaging program.

name: Thanat Khoman
profession: Thai Statesman and Co-Founder of Asian Alliance
headline: Thanat Khoman, Thai Statesman and Co-Founder of Asian Alliance, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Thanat helped the United States gain military bases in Thailand during the Vietnam War and helped start the Association of Southeast Asian Nations.

name: Elizabeth Garrett
headline: Elizabeth Garrett, First Female President of Cornell, Dies at 52
abstract: Ms. Garrett, who started the position last summer, announced a month ago that she had learned she had colon cancer.

name: Margaret Lavigne
headline: Margaret Lavigne, Advocate for People With Disabilities, Dies at 44
abstract: In a 2014 New York Times documentary, Ms. Lavigne spoke on living with a disability caused by muscular dystrophy and meeting her husband in a long-term care hospital.

name: Kathryn Popper
profession: Last Surviving Actor in Citizen Kane
headline: Kathryn Popper, Last Surviving Actor in ‘Citizen Kane,’ Dies at 100
abstract: Mrs. Popper was Orson Welles’s assistant and played a photographer in the 1941 film who asked, “What’s Rosebud?”

name: Harold H. Saunders
headline: Harold H. Saunders, Mideast Peace Broker, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Saunders helped draft the Camp David peace accords in 1978 and helped negotiate the release of American hostages from the United States embassy in Tehran in 1981.

name: George Martin
headline: George Martin, Redefining Producer Who Guided the Beatles, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Martin, who signed the band to a recording contract in 1962 after every other British label refused to, helped redefine a producer’s role in pop music.

name: Martha Wright
profession: Played Leading Roles in Beloved Musicals
headline: Martha Wright, Who Played Leading Roles in Beloved Musicals, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Wright replaced Mary Martin in “South Pacific” and “The Sound of Music,” logging more than 1,200 performances, yet not becoming a household name.

name: John Gutfreund
profession: Ran Wall Street Investment Firm at Its Apex
headline: John Gutfreund, 86, Dies; Ran Wall Street Investment Firm at Its Apex
abstract: Mr. Gutfreund transformed Salomon Brothers into one of the world’s largest securities traders, but left the industry in disgrace.

name: Bill Gadsby
profession: N.H.L. Star With Scars to Prove It
headline: Bill Gadsby, N.H.L. Star With Scars to Prove It, Dies at 88
abstract: The Hall of Fame defenseman played in the rough and tough Original Six era of the N.H.L., when skaters went without helmets and goalies shunned masks.

name: Clyde Lovellette
headline: Clyde Lovellette, Hall of Famer Who Brought Size and Skill to Basketball, Dies at 86
abstract: One of the game’s early big men, Lovellette was the first player to win N.C.A.A., Olympic and N.B.A. titles.

name: Charles Granby
profession: Coached Future N.B.A. Players in Queens
headline: Charles Granby, Who Coached Future N.B.A. Players in Queens, Dies at 81
abstract: At Campus Magnet High School in Queens, Granby coached generations of players, including future N.B.A. stars like Chris Mullin, with a combination of brashness and fatherly love.

name: David M. Gates
profession: Sounded Early Alarm on Environmental Perils
headline: David M. Gates Dies at 94; Sounded Early Alarm on Environmental Perils
abstract: Dr. Gates was in the vanguard of scientists who warned early on that fossil fuels, fertilizers and pesticides posed a dire threat to the environment.

name: Ben H. Bagdikian
profession: Reporter of Broad Range and Conscience
headline: Ben H. Bagdikian, Reporter of Broad Range and Conscience, Dies at 96
abstract: He covered stories from the Suez crisis to segregation, then trained his sharp eye on journalism itself, and its increasingly corporate character.

name: Naná Vasconcelos
headline: Naná Vasconcelos, Daring Brazilian Percussionist, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Vasconcelos was an award-winning talent, collaborating with artists as varied as the Talking Heads and Pat Metheny.

name: Gary Jeter
headline: Gary Jeter, 61, Giants Draftee Who Starred as Rams Lineman
abstract: A promising rookie who did not immediately live up to expectations, Jeter later thrived, particularly after a trade to the Rams.

name: Keith Emerson
profession: 70s Rock Showman With a Taste for Spectacle
headline: Keith Emerson, ’70s Rock Showman With a Taste for Spectacle, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Emerson was also an early innovator who incorporated the Moog synthesizer into his work in Emerson, Lake & Palmer.

name: Lawrence Van Gelder
profession: Critic and Editor at The Times
headline: Lawrence Van Gelder, Critic and Editor at The Times, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Van Gelder accumulated more than 5,200 bylines as a reporter, film critic and obituary writer and also worked as an editor on the culture and metropolitan desks.

name: Ralph S. Larsen
headline: Ralph S. Larsen, Builder of Giant Johnson & Johnson, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Larsen rose through the ranks to serve as chairman and chief executive of Johnson & Johnson from 1989 to 2002, expanding the company into a multinational giant.

name: Ken Adam
profession: Dreamed Up the Lairs of Movie Villains
headline: Ken Adam, Who Dreamed Up the Lairs of Movie Villains, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Adam, a production designer, is best known for creating futuristic sets for seven James Bond films and Stanley Kubrick’s “Dr. Strangelove.”

name: Peter Maxwell Davies
headline: Peter Maxwell Davies, Contrarian British Composer, Dies at 81
abstract: Although Mr. Davies was anti-establishment, anti-monarchist and avant-garde, he was named Queen Elizabeth II’s official Master of Music.

name: Lloyd S. Shapley
profession: Nobel Laureate and a Father of Game Theory
headline: Lloyd S. Shapley, 92, Nobel Laureate and a Father of Game Theory, Is Dead
abstract: A father of game theory, which tries to explain the choices that competitors make in situations that require strategic thinking.

name: Robert Horton
headline: Robert Horton, Handsome ‘Wagon Train’ Star Who Wanted More, Dies at 91
abstract: Resisting being typecast in westerns, Mr. Horton sought more complex roles and pursued a career as a singer.

name: Anita Brookner
profession: Bleak Fiction Won the Booker Prize
headline: Anita Brookner, Whose Bleak Fiction Won the Booker Prize, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Brookner, an art historian as well, was called the “mistress of gloom” for her stories of disappointed lives, usually of women.

name: Barbara Almond
headline: Dr. Barbara Almond, Who Examined Maternal Ambivalence, Dies at 77
abstract: Dr. Almond was a psychiatrist whose 2010 book looked at women’s difficult, and sometimes guilty, feelings about childbearing and motherhood.

name: Ernestine Anderson
headline: Ernestine Anderson, Grammy Nominated Jazz Singer, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Anderson was well known to jazz aficionados and praised by critics for her approach, which combined sophisticated jazz phrasing with an earthy blues sensibility.

name: Gogi Grant
profession: Knocked Elvis Off Top of Chart
headline: Gogi Grant, Who Knocked Elvis Off Top of Chart, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Grant’s rendition of “The Wayward Wind” a B-side afterthought, overtook “Heartbreak Hotel” at No. 1 in 1956.

name: Elwyn L. Simons
headline: Elwyn L. Simons, Who Discovered Early Human Forebears, Dies at 85
abstract: As the father of modern primate paleontology he braved sandstorms, dodged land mines and crawled through caves as a fossil hunter.

name: Frank Sinatra Jr.
headline: Frank Sinatra Jr., Singer Who Followed in His Father’s Footsteps, Dies at 72
abstract: Unlike his sister Nancy, Mr. Sinatra never had a hit of his own. “I was trying to sell antiques in a modern appliance store,” he said.

name: Meir Dagan
headline: Meir Dagan, Israeli Spymaster, Dies at 71; Disrupted Iran’s Nuclear Program
abstract: Mr. Dagan was credited with setting back Iran’s nuclear program through covert and daring operations while heading Mossad, Israel’s intelligence agency.

name: Quentin D. Young
profession: Public Health and Civil Rights Advocate
headline: Dr. Quentin D. Young, Public Health and Civil Rights Advocate, Dies at 92
abstract: The doctor was a personal physician to the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. and Barack Obama, and fought for universal health care.

name: James Sheldon
headline: James Sheldon, Director, Dies at 95; Career Reflected TV’s Evolution
abstract: Over 40 years, he directed episodes of some 100 series in most every genre, including classic episodes of “The Twilight Zone” and “The Millionaire.”

name: Hilary Putnam
headline: Hilary Putnam, Giant of Modern Philosophy, Dies at 89
abstract: He was known for the breadth of his thinking, the vividness of his arguments and his penchant for self-questioning and willingness to change his mind.

name: Guido Westerwelle
profession: German Foreign Minister Opposed Libya Incursion
headline: Guido Westerwelle Dies at 54; German Foreign Minister Opposed Libya Incursion
abstract: A former leader of the Free Democratic Party, Mr. Westerwelle became the highest-ranking openly gay person in the German government.

name: Elliot Gant
headline: Elliot Gant, Marketer of the Button-Down Shirt, Dies at 89
abstract: The Gant brothers transformed the button-down into a fashion must, as noted by the comedian Bob Newhart and his “button-down mind.”

name: Joe Santos
headline: Joe Santos, a Mainstay of ‘The Rockford Files,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Santos, an actor with many television and film credits, often played characters who were tough but stressed, including an overworked detective on “Rockford.”

name: Kathryn Reed Altman
headline: Kathryn Reed Altman, Film Director’s Widow and Archivist, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Altman often spoke at retrospectives of Robert Altman’s work, was co-author of a book about him and was part of the 2014 documentary “Altman.”

name: Sergio Arellano Stark
headline: Sergio Arellano Stark, Chilean General Who Led Death Squad, Dies at 94
abstract: He helped install Augusto Pinochet as president in a 1973 coup and was implicated in the murder or disappearance of more than 75 Chileans.

name: Larry Drake
headline: Larry Drake, Lovable Clerk on ‘L.A. Law,’ Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Drake’s role as Benny Stulwicz on “L.A. Law” began as a minor one but was expanded and earned him two Emmy Awards.

name: Geoffrey H. Hartman
headline: Geoffrey H. Hartman, Scholar Who Saw Literary Criticism as Art, Dies at 86
abstract: Long associated with the Yale School of criticism, Professor Hartman examined a wide range of subjects, including Wordsworth, Judaica and trauma.

name: Roger Agnelli
headline: Roger Agnelli, ‘Iron Man’ Who Led a Global Mining Giant, Dies at 56
abstract: As chief executive of Vale, Mr. Agnelli helped the Brazilian company become one of the world’s largest mining companies.

name: Bob Adelman
profession: Vivid Photos Captured Civil Rights Struggle
headline: Bob Adelman, Whose Vivid Photos Captured Civil Rights Struggle, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Adelman’s images of brutality and despair brought segregation and the civil rights movement home to Americans in the 1960s.

name: Andrew S. Grove
headline: Andrew S. Grove Dies at 79; Intel Chief Spurred Semiconductor Revolution
abstract: The semiconductor chip was a development as momentous as hydrocarbon fuels, electricity and telephones were in earlier eras.

name: Jack Masey
profession: Exhibitions Showed American Culture to World
headline: Jack Masey, Whose Exhibitions Showed American Culture to World, Dies at 91
abstract: A designer whose model American kitchen was the stage for a 1959 argument between Nikita S. Khrushchev and Vice President Richard M. Nixon.

name: Rob Ford
headline: Rob Ford, Blustery Ex-Mayor of Toronto Whose Struggles Went Public, Dies at 46
abstract: His admission that he used crack cocaine in one of his “drunken stupors” brought Mr. Ford international notoriety.

name: Leon H. Charney
headline: Leon H. Charney, Investor, Cable TV Host and Peace Broker, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Mr. Charney helped bring about the Camp David peace accords in 1978 by arranging secret talks between the Egyptian president, Anwar el-Sadat, and the Israeli prime minister, Menachem Begin.

name: Jan Nemec
profession: Czech Filmmaker Known for Works of Dream Realism
headline: Jan Nemec, Czech Filmmaker Known for Works of ‘Dream Realism,’ Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Nemec’s surreal and parable-like films made him one of the leading lights of the country’s new wave in the 1960s.

name: Charles Kaufman
profession: Transformative Leader of Mannes College of Music
headline: Charles Kaufman, Transformative Leader of Mannes College of Music, Dies at 87
abstract: In his 16 years as the dean, Dr. Kaufman staved off bankruptcy, bolstered programming and oversaw a partnership with the New School.

name: Malik Taylor
profession: Phife Dawg of A Tribe Called Quest
headline: Malik Taylor, Phife Dawg of A Tribe Called Quest, Dies at 45
abstract: He was a wry and agile rapper from Queens who would refer frequently to his home base, Linden Boulevard and 192nd Street, throughout his career.

name: Joe Garagiola
headline: Joe Garagiola, a Catcher Who Called a Better Game on TV, Is Dead at 90
abstract: A player in the majors for nine forgettable seasons, he went on to become a colorful broadcaster for NBC, which also made him a host of the “Today” show.

name: Rita Gam
headline: Rita Gam, Midcentury Hollywood Actress, Dies at 88
abstract: In addition to her films, Ms. Gam was known for having been Sidney Lumet’s first wife and one of Grace Kelly’s bridesmaids.

name: Ken Howard
headline: Ken Howard, 71, Actor and SAG-Aftra Union President, Dies
abstract: Mr. Howard presided over the merger of the screen actors’ and television and radio actors’ unions, giving members a greater voice.

name: Johan Cruyff
headline: Johan Cruyff, the High Priest of Dutch Soccer, Dies at 68
abstract: One of the architects of Total Football, Cruyff electrified the sport in the 1970s and is considered one of the game’s greatest players.

name: Garry Shandling
headline: Garry Shandling, Star of Groundbreaking Sitcoms, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Shandling was known for walking the tightrope between comedic fiction and show-business reality on two sitcoms.

name: Nicholas Scoppetta
headline: Nicholas Scoppetta, Former Foster Child Who Led Child Welfare Agency, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Scoppetta, who served under four New York City mayors, was the first commissioner of Children’s Services and also led the fire and investigation departments.

name: Henri Bonneau
headline: Henri Bonneau, Wine Producer Known for Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Bonneau, a 12th-generation French vigneron, rejected modern methods to issue powerful wines that recalled how they might have tasted a century or two ago.

name: Peter Brown
profession: Star in TV Westerns and Soap Opera
headline: Peter Brown, Star in TV Westerns and Soap Opera, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Brown acted in “Lawman” and “Laredo” and later played a doctor in the daytime drama “Days of Our Lives.”

name: Earl Hamner Jr.
headline: Earl Hamner Jr., Who Created ‘The Waltons,’ Dies at 92
abstract: Also a novelist, Mr. Hamner wrote episodes of “The Twilight Zone” before CBS picked up the series about a mountain family that was based on his own.

name: Robert Ebeling
headline: Robert Ebeling, Challenger Engineer Who Warned of Disaster, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Ebeling, who lobbied alongside his colleagues for the postponement of the shuttle’s launch, carried the burden of the disaster throughout his life.

name: Santiago Erevia
profession: Once Denied Medal of Honor Over Ethnicity
headline: Santiago Erevia, Once Denied Medal of Honor Over Ethnicity, Dies at 69
abstract: After a Pentagon investigation, Mr. Erevia, a Vietnam veteran, was eventually bestowed the nation’s highest award for valor by President Obama in 2014.

name: Jim Harrison
headline: Jim Harrison, Poet, Novelist and Essayist, Is Dead at 78
abstract: A darkly comic master of the novella, Mr. Harrison was also known for his poems and essays on food.

name: Mary Angelica
headline: Mother Mary Angelica, Who Founded Catholic TV Network, Dies at 92
abstract: She was a popular and influential host on the Eternal Word Television Network, where she criticized liberalizing trends in the Catholic Church.

name: Peter Stanford
profession: Steward of New Yorks Maritime History
headline: Peter Stanford, Steward of New York’s Maritime History, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Stanford left an advertising career to found the South Street Seaport Museum in Lower Manhattan.

name: James Noble
headline: James Noble, Absent-Minded Governor on ‘Benson,’ Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Noble, who began as a stage actor before rising to national fame on TV, played Gov. Eugene Gatling on the hit series from 1979 to 1986.

name: Patty Duke
headline: Patty Duke, Child Star and Oscar Winner, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Duke came to wide public notice when she starred as Helen Keller in “The Miracle Worker.”

name: Lester C. Thurow
headline: Lester C. Thurow, Economist Who Seized the Spotlight, Is Dead at 77
abstract: A prolific writer and popular public speaker, Mr. Thurow sounded an early alarm about the growing income gap between rich and poor Americans.

name: Vince Boryla
headline: Vince Boryla, an N.B.A. Jack of All Trades, Dies at 89
abstract: Boryla buoyed two franchises three decades apart — the Knicks as a player and coach in the 1950s and the Denver Nuggets as the general manager in the 1980s.

name: Harriet Mills
profession: Scholar Held in Brainwashing Prison in China
headline: Harriet Mills, Scholar Held in ‘Brainwashing Prison’ in China, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Mills, imprisoned as an American spy in Communist China in the 1950s, later made clear to her sister that she had been indoctrinated.

name: Adrienne Corri
profession: Actress Known for A Clockwork Orange
headline: Adrienne Corri, Actress Known for ‘A Clockwork Orange,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Over almost five decades Ms. Corri acted in a wide range of roles for directors like Stanley Kubrick, David Lean and Jean Renoir.

name: Paul Pontallier
profession: Gave New Life to a Bordeaux Estate
headline: Paul Pontallier, Who Gave New Life to a Bordeaux Estate, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Pontallier helped restore Château Margaux, a celebrated name in the history of wine, to pre-eminence and served as its passionate embodiment.

name: Shannon Bolin
headline: Shannon Bolin, 99, Actress Who Starred in ‘Damn Yankees,’ Dies
abstract: Ms. Bolin played Meg Boyd in both the Broadway and film version of the 1950s musical.

name: Imre Kertesz
headline: Imre Kertesz, Nobel Laureate Who Survived Holocaust, Dies at 86
abstract: What set the Hungarian writer apart from others was his insistence on describing Auschwitz and Buchenwald without outrage, especially in his definitive work, “Fateless.”

name: Zaha Hadid
headline: Zaha Hadid, Groundbreaking Architect, Dies at 65
abstract: Ms. Hadid, the first woman to win the Pritzker Prize, was renowned for her theoretical work that left a mark on skylines around the world.

name: Shirley Hufstedler
profession: Judge and Cabinets First Education Secretary
headline: Shirley Hufstedler, Judge and Cabinet’s First Education Secretary, Dies at 90
abstract: At the newly established Education Department, she set as her goal giving more help to the disadvantaged and the disabled.

name: Hans-Dietrich Genscher
headline: Hans-Dietrich Genscher, an Architect of German Reunification, Dies at 89
abstract: As the country that he helped create grew into a flourishing nation and a force in the European Union, Mr. Genscher became a living political legend.

name: Ronnie Corbett
headline: Ronnie Corbett, of ‘The Two Ronnies’ British Comedy Team, Dies at 85
abstract: “All those who believe in psychokinesis, raise my right hand,” Mr. Corbett would say in his routine with Ronnie Barker.

name: Eric Engberg
headline: Eric Engberg, CBS Newsman, Dies at 74; Pioneered Political Fact-Checking
abstract: “Reality Check,” Mr. Engberg’s segment on the “CBS Evening News,” was a precursor to websites like Politifact.com and Factcheck.org.

name: Frank De Felitta
profession: Audrey Rose Horror Novelist and Documentarian
headline: Frank De Felitta, ‘Audrey Rose’ Horror Novelist and Documentarian, Dies at 94
abstract: His tale of reincarnation sold 3.5 million copies. His documentary for NBC about the Deep South had tragic consequences.

name: Harold Morowitz
headline: Harold Morowitz, 88, Biophysicist, Dies; Tackled Enigmas Big and Small
abstract: Trained in philosophy and physics, no topic was too trivial for Professor Morowitz to tease profound meaning from, including the thermodynamics of pizza.

name: Coca Crystal
headline: Coca Crystal, Avatar of Counterculture and Provocateur, Dies at 68
abstract: With an anarchist past that included a well-aimed apple pie and lab rats at a luncheon, Ms. Crystal hosted the public-access channel variety show “If I Can’t Dance, You Can Keep Your Revolution.”

name: Gato Barbieri
profession: Latin Jazz Trailblazer With a Saxophone
headline: Gato Barbieri, Latin Jazz Trailblazer With a Saxophone, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. Barbieri, whose career began in Argentina in the 1940s, recorded dozens of albums and received a Latin Grammy lifetime award in 2015.

name: Joseph Medicine Crow
headline: Joseph Medicine Crow, Tribal War Chief and Historian, Dies at 102
abstract: A member of the Crow Tribe, he was the last living person to have heard direct oral testimony from people who were present before the Battle of the Little Bighorn in 1876.

name: Winston Moseley
headline: Winston Moseley, Who Killed Kitty Genovese, Dies in Prison at 81
abstract: Ms. Genovese’s 1964 murder in New York, while neighbors failed to act on her cries for help, came to symbolize urban apathy in America.

name: Frankie Michaels
headline: Frankie Michaels, Who Won a Tony Award at 11, Dies at 60
abstract: He was the youngest Tony winner, and “Mame” was his only Broadway credit. As an adult, he was a lounge singer, voice and piano teacher and electronics repairman.

name: Kazuko Hirabayashi
headline: Kazuko Hirabayashi, Choreographer and Dancers’ Mentor, Dies at 82
abstract: A Japanese-born modern-dance choreographer, Ms. Hirabayashi was even more widely known as a teacher to many leading dancers, at Juilliard and elsewhere.

name: Mike Sandlock
headline: Mike Sandlock Dies at 100; Was Oldest Living Big Leaguer
abstract: A catcher and infielder for three National League teams, Sandlock achieved his foremost baseball distinction decades after his playing days were over.

name: Inge Hardison
headline: Inge Hardison, Actress and Sculptor of Heroes, Dies at 102
abstract: Ms. Hardison immortalized African-American historical figures as well as ordinary black citizens in her sculptures.

name: Merle Haggard
headline: Merle Haggard, Country Music’s Outlaw Hero, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Haggard wrote about his scuffling early life and defied the conventions of the Nashville establishment in building the twangy Bakersfield sound.

name: Seymour Lazar
headline: Seymour Lazar, 88, Dies; Flamboyant Entertainment Lawyer, and More
abstract: Mr. Lazar, a swashbuckling renegade, represented Lenny Bruce and Miles Davis, associated with Timothy Leary and Allen Ginsberg and became involved in a huge fraud case.

name: Carlo Mastrangelo
profession: Doo-Wop Voice for Dion and the Belmonts
headline: Carlo Mastrangelo, a Doo-Wop Voice for Dion and the Belmonts, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Mastrangelo, an original member of the Belmonts, provided baritone vocals for hits including “A Teenager in Love” and “Where or When.”

name: Joel Kurtzman
headline: Joel Kurtzman, Economist of Gloom Who Shifted to Optimism, Dies at 68
abstract: Credited with coining the term”economic headwinds,” Mr. Kurtzman originally projected the crash of American markets but eventually predicted a bright future.

name: Yvette Fay Francis-McBarnette
profession: Pioneer in Treating Sickle Cell Anemia
headline: Yvette Fay Francis-McBarnette, a Pioneer in Treating Sickle Cell Anemia, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Francis was credited with successfully using antibiotics to treat children with the disease 15 years before the effectiveness of those drugs was confirmed.

name: Toni Grant
profession: Her Couch Was on AM Radio
headline: Toni Grant, Psychotherapist, Dies at 73; Her Couch Was on AM Radio
abstract: Dr. Grant, who described her show as “a soap opera that educates,” was on the air for almost 20 years.

name: Ogden Mills Phipps
profession: Horseman From a Leading Racing Family
headline: Ogden Mills Phipps, Horseman From a Leading Racing Family, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Phipps, the longtime chairman of the Jockey Club, was an old-fashioned owner who resisted buying from commercial breeders.

name: Peggy Fortnum
profession: Illustrator Gave Shape to the Paddington Bear
headline: Peggy Fortnum, 96, Dies; Illustrator Gave Shape to the Paddington Bear
