abstract: Ms. Fortnum was the first to draw Michael Bond’s beloved fictional bear, giving the character his floppy hat and duffle coat.

name: Robert MacCrate
headline: Robert MacCrate, Lawyer in My Lai Inquiry, Dies at 94
abstract: He served as civilian counsel for the Army panel investigating the 1968 massacre, and later oversaw a landmark report calling for an overhaul of legal education.

name: Tony Conrad
headline: Tony Conrad, Experimental Filmmaker and Musician, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Conrad’s first film, “The Flicker,” warned audiences it could induce epileptic seizures, but it was still shown at the New York Film Festival.

name: Duane R. Clarridge
headline: Duane R. Clarridge, Brash Spy Who Fought Terror Networks, Dies at 83
abstract: He was a champion of a brawny U.S. foreign policy and of the C.I.A.’s clandestine service, which he likened to a secret army that “marches for the president.”

name: Charles S. Hirsch
profession: New Yorks Chief Medical Examiner on 9/11
headline: Charles S. Hirsch, New York’s Chief Medical Examiner on 9/11, Dies at 79
abstract: Dr. Hirsch worked tirelessly to identify the 2,753 victims of the World Trade Center attack and restore what had distinguished them.

name: Howard Marks
headline: Howard Marks, Drug Smuggler Turned Author, Dies at 70
abstract: The Welshman wrote “Mr. Nice,” a best-selling autobiography, after his release from a United States prison.

name: Ed Snider
headline: Ed Snider, Flyers Owner Who Made Philadelphia a Hockey Town, Dies at 83
abstract: In 1967, Mr. Snider and his partners introduced hockey to Philadelphia. Soon the Flyers turned the City of Brotherly Love into a town that loved bare-knuckle fights on the ice.

name: Getatchew Mekurya
headline: Getatchew Mekurya, 81, Ethiopian Saxophonist With Global Reach, Dies
abstract: Mr. Mekurya, who had an imposing jazz sound and presence, collaborated with musicians from far beyond his home country.

name: David Gest
profession: Music Producer and Reality TV Star
headline: David Gest, Music Producer and Reality TV Star, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Gest, who was briefly married to Liza Minnelli, was a constant presence on British television, as a guest in a reality series and as the star of his own show.

name: J. Thomas Rosch
profession: Fought for and Against Antitrust Actions
headline: J. Thomas Rosch, Lawyer, Dies at 76; Fought for and Against Antitrust Actions
abstract: President George W. Bush made Mr. Rosch an F.T.C. commissioner after he spent years defending companies from government antitrust actions.

name: Vladimir Kagan
headline: Vladimir Kagan, Designer Whose Furniture Evoked Sensuality, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Kagan was one of the 20th century’s most successful designers, creating sofas and chairs with swoops, swivels and swooshes.

name: Arthur Anderson
profession: Voice of Lucky Charms Cereals Leprechaun
headline: Arthur Anderson, Voice of Lucky Charms Cereal’s Leprechaun, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Anderson performed on radio as a teenager with Orson Welles’s Mercury Theater and appeared on Broadway, in films and on television.

name: Joe Freeman Britt
headline: Joe Freeman Britt, Called America’s ‘Deadliest D.A.,’ Dies at 80
abstract: The North Carolina prosecutor oversaw cases that led to more than 40 death sentences, and Guinness World Records named him the “deadliest prosecutor” in 1978.

name: Joe Patten
profession: Theater Caretaker Known as Phantom of the Fox
headline: Joe Patten, Theater Caretaker Known as ‘Phantom of the Fox,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Patten became smitten with the theater on a visit to Atlanta in the 1940s and lived there for more than 35 years.

name: Arnold Wesker
headline: Arnold Wesker, 83, Writer of Working-Class Dramas, Dies
abstract: Mr. Wesker, drawing on his childhood in a leftist Jewish family, was among British playwrights called the “angry young men,” though he disliked the label.

name: Anne Jackson
headline: Anne Jackson, Stage Star With Her Husband, Eli Wallach, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Jackson, half of one of America’s best-known acting couples, was nominated for a Tony for her performance in Paddy Chayefsky’s “Middle of the Night.”

name: Fred Hayman
profession: Giorgio Boutique Led Gilding of Rodeo Drive
headline: Fred Hayman, Whose Giorgio Boutique Led Gilding of Rodeo Drive, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Hayman realized a vision to transform Rodeo Drive in Los Angeles into a luxury shopping destination to rival New York’s Fifth Avenue.

name: Peter J. Jannetta
headline: Dr. Peter J. Jannetta, Pioneering Neurosurgeon on Facial Pain, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Jannetta, a specialist in cranial nerve disorders, developed a microsurgery procedure to relieve facial pain associated with trigeminal neuralgia.

name: James Cross Giblin
profession: Wide-Ranging Author of Books for Children
headline: James Cross Giblin, 82, Wide-Ranging Author of Books for Children, Dies
abstract: Knives and forks, windows, milk, Hitler, George Washington and AIDS were just some of Mr. Giblin’s subjects.

name: Hector A. Cafferata
profession: Given Medal of Honor for Korea Heroics
headline: Hector A. Cafferata, 86, Dies; Given Medal of Honor for Korea Heroics
abstract: A Marine private, he single-handedly held off an enemy regiment, protected comrades from a live grenade and was felled by a sniper.

name: Walter Rosen
headline: Walter Rosen, Longtime Steward of Junior’s Restaurant, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Rosen ran the restaurant, a New York City staple famous for its signature cheesecake, for around two decades before handing the reins to his sons.

name: Phil Sayer
profession: Voice Behind Mind the Gap on London Underground
headline: Phil Sayer, Voice Behind ‘Mind the Gap’ on London Underground, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Sayer, an English voice actor, first recorded messages for the London Underground in 2005. “Mind the gap” has been in use since 1969.

name: Malick Sidibé
profession: Photographer Known for Social Reportage in Mali
headline: Malick Sidibé, Photographer Known for Social Reportage in Mali, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Sidibé’s 1960s black-and-white photos of young partygoers in his native country captured the exuberance of new freedom.

name: Richard K. Ransom
profession: Founder of Hickory Farms Specialty Foods Chain
headline: Richard K. Ransom, Founder of Hickory Farms Specialty Foods Chain, Dies at 96
abstract: From selling cheeses and meats at local fairs, Mr. Ransom went on to build an empire of specialty food stores, one sample at a time.

name: John Ferrone
profession: Editor of Eclectic Stable of Writers
headline: John Ferrone, Editor of Eclectic Stable of Writers, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Ferrone counted among his authors Alice Walker, Anaïs Nin and James Beard.

name: Nera White
profession: Hall of Fame Basketball Star of 1950s and 60s
headline: Nera White, Hall of Fame Basketball Star of 1950s and ’60s, Is Dead at 80
abstract: White, who was 6 feet 1 inch and could dunk, was an A.A.U. all-American for 15 straight years and one of the first two women to enter the Naismith Hall of Fame.

name: Doris Roberts
headline: Doris Roberts, Mother on ‘Everybody Loves Raymond,’ Dies at 90
abstract: The Emmy-winning character actress was best known for her role as Ray Romano’s tart-tongued, interfering mother on the hit CBS series.

name: Bill Campbell
headline: Bill Campbell, Coach of Silicon Valley Stars, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Campbell, who advised the likes of Steve Jobs at Apple and Larry Page at Google, helped shape the technology industry.

name: Harold Wood
headline: Harold Wood, Westchester County Legislator and Justice, Dies at 96
abstract: As the county’s first black supervisor, Justice Wood warned of racial unrest and called for better opportunities for blacks.

name: Milt Pappas
profession: Cagey All-Star Traded for Hall of Famer
headline: Milt Pappas, Cagey All-Star Traded for Hall of Famer, Dies at 76
abstract: Pappas won 209 games in his major league career, but he was best known for being traded for Frank Robinson.

name: Ronit Elkabetz
profession: Acclaimed Israeli Film Star and Director
headline: Ronit Elkabetz, Acclaimed Israeli Film Star and Director, Dies at 51
abstract: Her searing and spellbinding performances earned her three Ophir Awards, the Israeli equivalent of Oscars. Her range drew comparisons to Meryl Streep.

name: Patricio Aylwin
headline: Patricio Aylwin, President Who Guided Chile to Democracy, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Aylwin, the first civilian elected after the Pinochet dictatorship, created a truth commission to investigate human rights abuses.

name: Jackie Carter
profession: Pushed for Racial Diversity in Childrens Books
headline: Jackie Carter, Who Pushed for Racial Diversity in Children’s Books, Dies at 62
abstract: A publishing executive and writer, she devoted her career to editing and releasing books that might captivate minority children and also reflect their lives.

name: Pearl Washington
profession: Dazzling Guard Put Syracuse on Basketball Map
headline: Pearl Washington, 52, Dies; Dazzling Guard Put Syracuse on Basketball Map
abstract: A charismatic point guard who achieved legend status as a Brooklyn schoolboy, he helped lift Syracuse University to national prominence in basketball and went on to play in the N.B.A.

name: Frederick Mayer
headline: Frederick Mayer, Jew Who Spied on Nazis After Fleeing Germany, Dies at 94
abstract: Seven years after leaving Germany with his family, Mr. Mayer parachuted into Austria as an American spy and helped to hasten the Nazi surrender.

name: Chyna
profession: Pro Wrestler Turned Reality TV Star
headline: Chyna, Pro Wrestler Turned Reality TV Star, Is Dead at 46
abstract: Born Joanie Laurer, she was initially not a fan of the sport but joined a wrestling school led by Killer Kowalski, a dominant figure from the 1950s to the 1970s.

name: Guy Hamilton
headline: Guy Hamilton, Director of ‘Goldfinger,’ Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Hamilton’s first Bond film was the third in the franchise and the first to be a blockbuster at the box office.

name: Bettye Caldwell
headline: Bettye Caldwell, Educator Who Helped Pave Way for Head Start, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Caldwell, a longtime advocate for what she called educare, collaborated on a pilot project that helped prepare poor children for elementary school.

name: Rod Daniel
headline: Rod Daniel, Whose Crowd-Pleasing Films Lined Pockets, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Daniel said he had no illusions of greatness as a filmmaker, but that he believed in his work.

name: Lonnie Mack
headline: Lonnie Mack, Singer and Guitarist Who Pioneered Blues-Rock, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Mack was a seminal influence on a long list of British and American artists.

name: Robert Price
headline: Robert Price, Strategist for Lindsay and Rockefeller, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Price successfully managed John V. Lindsay’s first mayoral campaign and delivered Gov. Nelson A. Rockefeller a crucial victory in a contested presidential primary.

name: Brian Asawa
profession: Celebrated Countertenor and Pathbreaker at the Met
headline: Brian Asawa, Celebrated Countertenor and Pathbreaker at the Met, Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. Asawa was one of only a handful of countertenors to enjoy international renown.

name: Elton Spitzer
profession: Helped Turn WLIR Into a Radio Destination
headline: Elton Spitzer, 84, Who Helped Turn WLIR Into a Radio Destination, Dies
abstract: Mr. Spitzer, who operated 92.7 FM on Long Island, dared to be different by introducing listeners to new wave music most Americans hadn’t heard before.

name: Banharn Silpa-archa
headline: Banharn Silpa-archa, Former Prime Minister of Thailand, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Banharn’s brief tenure, in 1995 and 1996, was marked by allegations of corruption and economic mismanagement.

name: Walter Kohn
headline: Walter Kohn, Who Won Nobel in Chemistry, Dies at 93
abstract: A chemist and physicist who fled Nazi-occupied Vienna as a teenager and built a distinguished academic career in the United States, becoming an American citizen in 1957.

name: Qi Benyu
profession: Mao Aide Unrepentant About Cultural Revolution
headline: Qi Benyu, Mao Aide Unrepentant About Cultural Revolution, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Qi, a propagandist in the Chinese Communist Party, expressed no remorse about the brutalities under Mao Zedong and remained a steadfast admirer of him.

name: Papa Wemba
headline: Papa Wemba, Congolese King of ‘Rumba Rock,’ Is Dead at 66
abstract: A supple tenor who sang danceable fusions of African pop and world music, Papa Wemba performed in his native Lingala and in French.

name: Billy Paul
profession: Singer of the Hit Me and Mrs. Jones
headline: Billy Paul, Singer of the Hit ‘Me and Mrs. Jones,’ Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Paul’s 1972 ballad about an illicit romance was a success that he was unable to repeat in his later career.

name: Maurice Kenny
profession: Explored His Mohawk Heritage in Poetry
headline: Maurice Kenny, Who Explored His Mohawk Heritage in Poetry, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Kenny gave voice in his verse to historical figures of New York State, both white and Native American.

name: Madeleine Sherwood
profession: Actress on Stage, Film and Flying Nun
headline: Madeleine Sherwood, 93, Actress on Stage, Film and ‘Flying Nun,’ Dies
abstract: A Canadian who originated the Broadway role of Abigail in Arthur Miller’s “The Crucible,” she also starred in stage and film versions of Tennessee Williams plays.

name: Les Waas
headline: Les Waas, Adman, Dies at 94; Gave Mister Softee a Soundtrack
abstract: His jingle, a herald of summer in the city, and of the ice cream man down the block, is the textbook embodiment of an earworm: once heard, never forgotten.

name: Horace Ward
headline: Horace Ward, U.S. Judge Who Triumphed Over Bias, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Ward sued the University of Georgia after it rejected his law school application because of his race. He became Georgia’s first black federal judge.

name: Harry Wu
profession: Told World of Abuses in China
headline: Harry Wu, Who Told World of Abuses in China, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Wu was brutalized for 19 years in Communist labor camps, and later returned to his homeland undercover to expose prison conditions.

name: Robert J. Cooper
headline: Robert J. Cooper, 39, Creator of Popular Elderflower Liqueur, Dies
abstract: Mr. Cooper’s 2007 concoction, St-Germain, was so embraced by the cocktail crowd that it became known as “bartender’s ketchup.”

name: Ozzie Silna
headline: Ozzie Silna, Savvy A.B.A Owner Who Got Rich Off the N.B.A., Dies at 83
abstract: A businessman who made millions off N.B.A. television contracts long after the team he co-owned with his brother, Daniel, was dissolved.

name: Winston Hill
headline: Winston Hill, Durable Lineman for ’69 Champion Jets, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Hill made eight All-Pro teams and protected the blindside of quarterback Joe Namath during the team’s only Super Bowl victory.

name: Robert Linton
headline: Robert Linton, Steadfast ’80s Wall Street Banker, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Linton’s Drexel firm pioneered the junk bond industry and came to symbolize the era’s “greed is good” mentality, until it was swept into a federal inquiry.

name: Jenny Diski
headline: Jenny Diski, Author Who Wrote of Madness and Isolation, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. Diski’s novels included “Skating to Antarctica,“ “Stranger on a Train: Daydreaming and Smoking Around America With Interruptions” and “Rainforest.”

name: Philip Kives
headline: Philip Kives, Pitchman Who Perfected ‘As Seen on TV’ Infomercials, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Kives’s company, K-tel, saturated airwaves for decades with ads for gadgets like the Veg-O-Matic and compilation albums like “Hit Machine.”

name: Tommy Kono
profession: Weight-Lifting Champion Raised in Internment Camp
headline: Tommy Kono, Weight-Lifting Champion Raised in Internment Camp, Dies at 85
abstract: Kono learned to lift as a child in a Japanese-American detention camp during World War II and went on to win two Olympic gold medals in the sport.

name: George Weymouth
headline: George Weymouth, Conservationist, Horse Enthusiast and Bon Vivant, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Weymouth, a member of the du Pont family, was a longtime fixture in fox-hunting, polo, steeplechase and carriage-driving circles.

name: Remo Belli
profession: Developed Synthetic Drumhead and Changed Music
headline: Remo Belli, Who Developed Synthetic Drumhead and Changed Music, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Belli’s Weather King, so named because it was impervious to humid conditions, largely replaced animal hides and helped feed rock ’n’ roll fever.

name: Blackie Sherrod
profession: Wrote About Sports With a Texas Swagger
headline: Blackie Sherrod, 96, Who Wrote About Sports With a Texas Swagger, Dies
abstract: Mr. Sherrod, voted the state’s best 16 times, was admired for his lively style and for mentoring Dan Jenkins and other younger writers.

name: Samuel Billy Kyles
headline: Samuel Billy Kyles, Witness to King’s Last Moments, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Kyles was on the balcony of a Memphis motel with the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. when the civil rights leader was gunned down.

name: Daniel J. Berrigan
headline: Daniel J. Berrigan, Defiant Priest Who Preached Pacifism, Dies at 94
abstract: Father Berrigan, a Jesuit priest and poet, defiantly protested the Vietnam War and served time for his acts of civil disobedience.

name: Conrad Burns
headline: Conrad Burns, Former U.S. Senator of Montana, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Burns was a plain-spoken former livestock auctioneer who had a meteoric rise in politics that was sometimes overshadowed by derogatory comments he made.

name: Marisol
profession: Artist Known for Blithely Shattering Boundaries
headline: Marisol, an Artist Known for Blithely Shattering Boundaries, Dies at 85
abstract: Marisol brought folk art traditions to Pop Art and added political commentary and sharp humor.

name: Afeni Shakur
headline: Afeni Shakur, Guidepost for Slain Rapper Son, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Shakur had been the driving force in continuing the legacy of Tupac Shakur, who was gunned down at age 25.

name: Bob Fitch
headline: Bob Fitch, Photojournalist of Civil Rights Era, Dies at 76
abstract: His images chronicled America’s enduring ambivalence over race and the passions inspiring other protest movements.

name: Ned Miller
headline: Ned Miller, a Country Songwriter Who Gave Up Singing, Dies at 90
abstract: His biggest hit, “From a Jack to a King,” endured in covers by Elvis Presley and Bobby Darin long after Mr. Miller stopped performing because of shyness.

name: Thomas Libous
profession: Powerful New York Senator Felled by Scandal
headline: Thomas Libous, Powerful New York Senator Felled by Scandal, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Libous, a Republican, earned a reputation as a reliably reasonable lawmaker over nearly three decades in Albany, but his tenure ended with a federal conviction.

name: Jean-Baptiste Bagaza
profession: Deposed Leader of a Troubled Burundi
headline: Jean-Baptiste Bagaza, Deposed Leader of a Troubled Burundi, Is Dead at 69
abstract: As president of the small Central African nation, Mr. Bagaza invested in infrastructure but did little to make his country a stable democracy.

name: Charles Gatewood
headline: Charles Gatewood, Photographer of Extremes, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Gatewood‘s subjects included rock stars, strippers, exhibitionists, cross-dressers, fetishists, protesters and drunks. Just right for an anthropology major.

name: Harold Kroto
headline: Harold Kroto, Nobel Prize-Winning Chemist, Is Dead at 76
abstract: He shared the prize in 1996 for discovering a new form of carbon, nicknamed the buckyball.

name: Carl Fredrik Reutersward
headline: Carl Fredrik Reutersward, Known for Knotted-Gun Sculpture, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Reutersward, a Swedish artist who did not conform to any particular art movement, created his “Non-Violence” sculpture after the murder of John Lennon.

name: Robert Bennett
profession: Former Senator from Utah and Tea Party Casualty
headline: Robert Bennett, Former Senator from Utah and Tea Party Casualty, Dies at 82
abstract: A conservative stalwart, Mr. Bennett was nevertheless ousted in a Tea Party wave in 2010 for his willingness to compromise on the bank bailout, immigration and other big issues.

name: Robert Bennett
headline: Robert Bennett, Broadcaster Who Charted a New Course, Dies at 89
abstract: At a time when most local TV stations made big profits by airing reruns, Mr. Bennett executed an ambitious vision to create hours of original programming.

name: Robert S. Bennett
profession: Washingtons Go-to Lawyer in a Scandal
headline: Robert S. Bennett, Washington’s Go-to Lawyer in a Scandal, Dies at 84
abstract: He was a robust defender of a host of high-profile clients, including Bill Clinton over the president’s relationship with an intern.

name: Kaname Harada
headline: Kaname Harada, Pearl Harbor Fighter Pilot and, Later, a Pacifist, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Harada said it was not until the 50th anniversary of the airstrike that he learned the raid had been a sneak attack and that Japan had not declared war on the United States.

name: James Haughton
profession: Fought Racial Barriers in Building Trades
headline: James Haughton, Who Fought Racial Barriers in Building Trades, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Haughton was best known for breaking with more moderate proponents of equal opportunity in hiring and housing to form a group that became known as Fight Back.

name: Donald W. Duncan
profession: Ex-Green Beret and Early Critic of Vietnam War
headline: Donald W. Duncan, 79, Ex-Green Beret and Early Critic of Vietnam War, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Duncan, who died in obscurity in 2009, wrote in 1966 of witnessing atrocities by American troops and helped organize antiwar protests.

name: Nicolas Noxon
headline: Nicolas Noxon, Emmy-Winning National Geographic Filmmaker, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Noxon worked on a wide range of projects, often concerning nature, including “Secrets of the Titanic” and “The Dragons of Galápagos.”

name: Margot Honecker
profession: East German Hard-Liner and Widow of Ruler
headline: Margot Honecker, East German Hard-Liner and Widow of Ruler, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Honecker, who served as the minister of education in her husband Erich Honecker’s Communist regime in East Germany, had been living in exile in Chile.

name: Ursula Mamlok
headline: Ursula Mamlok, Avant-Garde Composer, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Mamlok, a German who fled the Nazis and became a fixture of the New York music scene, was known for chamber music, piano pieces and vocal works.

name: Harold Cohen
headline: Harold Cohen, a Pioneer of Computer-Generated Art, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Cohen, an abstract painter, developed Aaron, a software program that learned to create art in a manner similar to freehand drawing.

name: Irwin Weinberg
headline: Irwin Weinberg, Collector of Rare, Precious Stamps, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Weinberg drummed up notoriety for his travels to exhibit a one-of-a-kind 1856 stamp with public displays featuring handcuffs and armored cars.

name: Howard Garfinkel
profession: Discovered and Groomed Top Basketball Talent
headline: Howard Garfinkel, Who Discovered and Groomed Top Basketball Talent, Dies at 86
abstract: Garfinkel’s scouting reports helped widen college coaches’ recruiting boundaries, and his instructional camp helped develop players like Michael Jordan and LeBron James.

name: Ret Turner
headline: Ret Turner, Award-Winning Costume Designer, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Turner won five Emmys and worked with many of television’s biggest stars in the 1970s and ’80s, including Lucille Ball, Carol Burnett and Cher.

name: Mel Bartholomew
headline: Mel Bartholomew, an Engineer Who Popularized Square Foot Gardening, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Bartholomew’s innovation saved water and space by folding traditional rows of vegetables into a raised bed that could fit on porches, patios, decks or roofs.

name: William Schallert
profession: Prolific Actor Was Father on The Patty Duke Show
headline: William Schallert, 93, Dies; Prolific Actor Was Father on ‘The Patty Duke Show’
abstract: For a time Mr. Schallert seemed to be everywhere on TV, usually as an authority figure, as he was in the popular “Tribbles” episode of “Star Trek.”

name: Sylvia Kauders
headline: Sylvia Kauders, Late-Blooming Actress Who Found Her Niche, Dies
abstract: Ms. Kauders, who started auditioning at about 60, appeared in “Witness,” “American Splendor,” “The Sopranos” and more in “old lady” roles.

name: Ramón Carlín
headline: Ramón Carlín, Casual Sailor Who Won a Round-the-World Race, Dies at 92
abstract: A Mexican washing-machine magnate, Mr. Carlín was a a 50-year-old skipper of scant experience when he entered — and unaccountably won — the first Whitbread race.

name: Michael S. Harper
headline: Michael S. Harper, Poet With a Jazz Pulse, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Harper, who taught at Brown University for over 40 years, embraced an idiom interwoven with music, history and his experiences as a black man.

name: Anne Deborah Atai-Omoruto
profession: Leader in the Ebola Fight in Liberia
headline: Anne Deborah Atai-Omoruto, 59, a Leader in the Ebola Fight in Liberia, Dies
abstract: Dr. Atai-Omoruto trained more than 1,000 Liberian health workers for treating patients with the virus at a time of international panic.

name: Joan Helpern
headline: Joan Helpern, Joan & David Shoes Co-Founder, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Helpern and her husband, David, started a business to make shoes for women running through airports.

name: Michael Ratner
headline: Michael Ratner, Lawyer Who Won Rights for Guantánamo Prisoners, Dies at 72
abstract: As head of the Center for Constitutional Rights, Mr. Ratner also oversaw litigation that effectively voided New York City’s wholesale stop-and-frisk policing strategy.

name: John Young
profession: Promoter of Baseball for the Underprivileged
headline: John Young, Promoter of Baseball for the Underprivileged, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Young, who played two games for the Detroit Tigers, became their director of scouting and later founded the Reviving Baseball in Inner Cities program.

name: John Young
headline: John Young, Who Led First Space Shuttle Mission, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Young also walked on the moon and was the only astronaut to fly in the Gemini, Apollo and shuttle programs.

name: John L. Young
headline: John L. Young, 89, Dies; Pioneered Posting Classified Documents Online
abstract: His site, Cryptome, was a precursor to WikiLeaks, and in some ways bolder in its no-holds-barred approach to exposing government secrets.

name: Isao Tomita
headline: Isao Tomita Dies at 84; Combined Electronic and Classical Music
abstract: Mr. Tomita’s work was reported to have influenced musicians around the world, among them Stevie Wonder and the Japanese techno-pop group Yellow Magic Orchestra.

name: James D. Travis
headline: James D. Travis, Whose TV Ad Helped Re-elect Reagan, Dies at 83
abstract: Under Mr. Travis’s direction, the highly successful 1984 “Morning in America” commercial served up apple-pie slices of Middle American prosperity.

name: Kwame Somburu
headline: Kwame Somburu, Perennial Socialist Candidate, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Somburu, who sought office nine times, embraced a Trotskyite scientific socialism forged in anti-imperialism and class-conscious black nationalism.

name: Mark Lane
headline: Mark Lane, Early Kennedy Assassination Conspiracy Theorist, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Lane, a longtime activist and lawyer, ridiculed the findings of the Warren Commission and inspired hundreds of books on the assassination.

name: John Bradshaw
headline: John Bradshaw, Self-Help Evangelist Who Called to the ‘Inner Child,’ Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Bradshaw found fame with books and television shows proposing that emotional and psychological damage experienced in childhood was the root of adult ills.

name: François Morellet
headline: François Morellet, French Abstract Artist, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Morellet, who used unorthodox materials and incorporated kinetics in his sculptures, sought to make art that would “make it possible for the observer to find what he wants.”

name: Daniel P. Tully
profession: Led Merrill Lynch in Its Halcyon 90s
headline: Daniel P. Tully Dies at 84; Led Merrill Lynch in Its Halcyon ’90s
abstract: Mr. Tully, who stepped down in 1997, was a staunch believer in “Mother Merrill,” an ideal of devotion to the greater good of the firm.

name: Martin Friedman
headline: Martin Friedman, Whose Vision Shaped Walker Art Center, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Friedman remade a Minnesota landmark into a cultural destination, and after retirement delighted Manhattan with art at Madison Square Park.

name: Christy O’Connor Sr.
headline: Christy O’Connor Sr., Irish Golfer Who Played on 10 Ryder Cup Teams, Dies at 91
abstract: O’Connor, who played in an era when top British and Irish golfers did not have as much access to the American majors as they do now, won 24 times on the European Tour.

name: Ernest Michel
profession: Bore Witness to the Holocaust and Led Charities
headline: Ernest Michel, Who Bore Witness to the Holocaust and Led Charities, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Michel was spared when the Nazis conscripted him to falsify prisoner death certificates. He later wrote a memoir and headed up Jewish philanthropic causes.

name: Katherine Dunn
headline: Katherine Dunn, Author of ‘Geek Love,’ Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Dunn’s third novel, “Geek Love,” which revolves around a married couple who breed mutant children as sideshow freaks, has sold hundreds of thousands of copies.

name: Julius La Rosa
headline: Julius La Rosa, Singer Who Found Success After a Public Firing, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. La Rosa surged to fame in the 1950s under Arthur Godfrey, who fired him during a live broadcast, forcing Mr. La Rosa to reinvent his career.

name: Bill Backer
profession: Taught the World (and Don Draper) to Sing
headline: Bill Backer, Who Taught the World (and Don Draper) to Sing, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Backer created the classic 1971 commercial for Coca-Cola with singers on an Italian hilltop proclaiming Coke as “the real thing.”

name: Louisa Chase
profession: Painter of Geometric Shapes and Body Parts
headline: Louisa Chase, Painter of Geometric Shapes and Body Parts, Dies at 65
abstract: Ms. Chase was given a solo show at Artists Space in 1975, the same year she received her master’s degree from Yale.

name: Sammy Ellis
headline: Sammy Ellis, All-Star Starter Who Later Made Dave Righetti a Reliever, Dies at 75
abstract: Ellis won 20 games for Cincinnati in 1965 before arm troubles derailed his playing career. As a coach, he arranged Righetti’s successful move to the bullpen a year after he had thrown a no-hitter.

name: David M. Durst
headline: David M. Durst, Developer of Manhattan Towers, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Durst oversaw construction of eight skyscrapers over the course of three decades, and combined his talent as an engineer with his love of art to create whimsical sculptures.

name: Madeleine Lebeau
headline: Madeleine Lebeau, Jilted by Bogart in ‘Casablanca,’ Dies at 92
abstract: A patriotic, tear-stained scene made Ms. Lebeau a symbol of French resistance. She made two more American films before working in France through the 1950s.

name: Romaldo Giurgola
headline: Romaldo Giurgola, Architect of Australia’s Parliament House, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Giurgola combined a Modernist aesthetic with a keen sense of the site-specific in his projects, from office buildings to Australia’s 1988 seat of government in Canberra.

name: Tony Barrow
headline: Tony Barrow, Beatles Publicist Who Coined the Term ‘Fab Four,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Barrow played a central role in shaping the public’s perception of a nascent band in the early 1960s.

name: Darwyn Cooke
profession: Comic Book Artist With a Retro Take
headline: Darwyn Cooke, Comic Book Artist With a Retro Take, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Cooke rebelled against the increasingly dark nature comic book superheroes took on in the post-millennial years.

name: Guy Clark
headline: Guy Clark, a King of the Texas Troubadours, Is Dead at 74
abstract: A narrative-rich singer-songwriter whose works became hits for many country stars, he is known for “Desperados Waiting for a Train” and “L.A. Freeway.”

name: Dick McAuliffe
headline: Dick McAuliffe, Stalwart of ’68 Tigers, Dies at 76
abstract: A hard-nosed All-Star infielder who played 14 seasons with Detroit and was known to teammates as Mad Dog, he starred on the 1968 championship team.

name: David King
profession: Graphic Designer Amassed Trove of Soviet Political Art
headline: David King, 73, Dies; Graphic Designer Amassed Trove of Soviet Political Art
abstract: Mr. King, a graphic designer, drew on his collection for books on Trotsky and the Stalin era. He also produced album covers for the Who and the Jimi Hendrix Experience.

name: Yukio Ninagawa
headline: Yukio Ninagawa, 80, Director Who Fused Japanese and Western Theater, Dies
abstract: Mr. Ninagawa mounted original versions of Greek and Shakespearean tragedies in Japan, Europe and the United States.

name: Fritz Stern
headline: Fritz Stern, a Leading Historian on Modern Germany, Dies at 90
abstract: German-born and a longtime professor at Columbia University, Mr. Stern identified themes and intellectual currents that led to Germany’s drift toward totalitarianism.

name: Julia Meade
profession: Actress Found Leading Role as TV Pitchwoman
headline: Julia Meade Dies at 90; Actress Found Leading Role as TV Pitchwoman
abstract: Beginning in the early 1950s, Ms. Meade was the elegant public face of products including Lincoln cars, Kodak cameras and Hudnut hair products.

name: Robert W. Gutman
headline: Robert W. Gutman, Biographer of Wagner and Mozart, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Gutman upended misconceptions about the composers’ lives, including the notion that a rival composer played a role in Mozart’s death.

name: Morley Safer
headline: Morley Safer, Mainstay of ‘60 Minutes,’ Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Safer was on the CBS show for 46 years, and as a TV correspondent brought the horrors of the Vietnam War into America’s living rooms.

name: Joe Temperley
profession: Velvety Baritone Saxophonist in Big Bands
headline: Joe Temperley, Velvety Baritone Saxophonist in Big Bands, Dies at 86
abstract: The musician’s seven-decade career began with Scottish dance bands and included several American ensembles, among them the Jazz at Lincoln Center Orchestra.

name: Susan Tolchin
headline: Susan Tolchin, Political Scientist Who Foresaw Voter Anger, Dies at 75
abstract: Many of Ms. Tolchin’s books were written in collaboration with her husband, a journalist.

name: Marlene Marder
profession: Guitarist for Influential Post-Punk Band Liliput
headline: Marlene Marder, Guitarist for Influential Post-Punk Band Liliput, Dies at 61
abstract: Ms. Marder brought a distinctive sound to the group, a four-woman Swiss band whose admirers included Kurt Cobain.

name: Alan Young
headline: Alan Young, the Affable Owner on ‘Mister Ed,’ Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Young was an established radio and television personality when he began playing “Wilburrrr,” who could talk to a horse, of course.

name: Patricia Derian
headline: Patricia Derian, Diplomat Who Made Human Rights a Priority, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Derian, an assistant secretary of state under President Jimmy Carter, is credited with saving lives by standing up to dictators.

name: Marco Pannella
headline: Marco Pannella, Italian Champion of Civil Liberties, Dies at 86
abstract: As the co-founder of Italy’s Radical Party, Mr. Pannella campaigned to legalize abortion, divorce and marijuana in his predominantly Catholic country.

name: Jane Little
headline: Jane Little, Atlanta’s Venerable Bassist, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Little played 71 years to become the musician longest serving in a single orchestra.

name: Bill Herz
profession: Last of War of the Worlds Broadcast Crew
headline: Bill Herz, Last of ‘War of the Worlds’ Broadcast Crew, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Herz, a stage manager and casting director for Orson Welles’s Mercury Theater Company, was part of a shrinking cadre of Broadway originals.

name: Emilio Navaira
profession: Tejano Star on Both Sides of Border
headline: Emilio Navaira, Tejano Star on Both Sides of Border, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Navaira recorded in Spanish and English, won a Grammy and even found success on Billboard’s country music charts.

name: Kang Sok-ju
profession: Key Nuclear Negotiator for North Korea
headline: Kang Sok-ju, Key Nuclear Negotiator for North Korea, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Kang, a top foreign policy aide of Kim Jong-il, was known for a 1994 agreement with the United States that fell apart after accusations that North Korea was secretly pursuing uranium enrichment.

name: Fred Papert
profession: Innovative Ad Man and Champion of Grand Central
headline: Fred Papert, Innovative Ad Man and Champion of Grand Central, Dies at 89
abstract: After a stellar career in advertising, Mr. Papert rallied prominent New Yorkers in a successful campaign to save the railroad terminal from demolition.

name: Michael Mariotte
headline: Michael Mariotte, a Leading Antinuclear Activist, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Mariotte succeeded in preventing the repeal of a federal ban on interstate shipment of radioactive waste and barred the construction of new nuclear plants in Maryland and Louisiana.

name: Luis Álvarez
profession: Leading Figure in Mexicos National Action Party
headline: Luis Álvarez, Leading Figure in Mexico’s National Action Party, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Álvarez dedicated his life to the fight for democracy in Mexico and was steadfast in his efforts to end the long rule of the Institutional Revolutionary Party.

name: Luis Alvarez
headline: Luis Alvarez, Champion of 9/11 Responders, Dies at 53
abstract: A former New York City police officer, he developed cancer 16 years after spending three months seeking survivors and victims’ remains in Lower Manhattan in 2001.

name: Beth Howland
profession: Accident-Prone Waitress From the Sitcom Alice
headline: Beth Howland, Accident-Prone Waitress From the Sitcom ‘Alice,’ Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Howland made high anxiety an art form as the ditsy, accident-prone waitress Vera Louise Gorman on the 1970s and ’80s sitcom.

name: Donn Chappellet
headline: Donn Chappellet, Napa Pioneer Who Tired of Coffee Vending, Dies at 84
abstract: After becoming bored with his food services company, a hobbyist became a pioneer in Napa Valley, creating Chappellet Vineyard, now known for its cabernets.

name: Mell Lazarus
profession: Cartoonist of Miss Peach and Momma
headline: Mell Lazarus, Cartoonist of ‘Miss Peach’ and ‘Momma,’ Dies at 89
abstract: A past president of the National Cartoonists Society and a Reuben Award winner, Mr. Lazarus helped secure ownership rights for comic strip creators.

name: Loris Francesco Capovilla
profession: Pope Johns Aide and Spiritual Son
headline: Loris Francesco Capovilla, Pope John’s Aide and ‘Spiritual Son,’ Dies at 100
abstract: Cardinal Capovilla, Pope John XXIII’s personal secretary, helped prepare the Roman Catholic hierarchy for the opening of Vatican II in 1962.

name: Yang Jiang
profession: Revered Writer Witnessed Chinas Cultural Revolution
headline: Yang Jiang Dies at 104; Revered Writer Witnessed China’s Cultural Revolution
abstract: Ms. Yang’s popular memoir told of the forced rural labor she and her novelist husband endured. Her translation of “Don Quixote” is regarded as the definitive one in Chinese.

name: Suzanne Corkin
headline: Suzanne Corkin, Who Helped Pinpoint Nature of Memory, Dies at 79
abstract: Among many other contributions, Dr. Corkin’s work helped settle a debate about the function of the hippocampus in retrieving and reliving past experiences.

name: Marcus D. Gordon
headline: Marcus D. Gordon, Judge in ‘Mississippi Burning’ Case, Dies at 84
abstract: Four decades after three civil rights workers were kidnapped and killed, the judge sentenced an acquaintance accused of orchestrating the killings.

name: Jane Fawcett
headline: Jane Fawcett, British Decoder Who Helped Doom the Bismarck, Dies at 95
abstract: As an eagle-eyed staffer at Bletchley Park, home to Britain’s wartime code-breakers, Ms. Fawcett identified a message that led to the sinking of the fearsome German warship.

name: Hedy Epstein
headline: Hedy Epstein, Rights Activist and Holocaust Survivor, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Epstein’s parents died in Auschwitz and she devoted her life to social justice, telling audiences, “Remember the past, don’t hate, don’t be a bystander.”

name: Frank Modell
headline: Frank Modell, Longtime New Yorker Cartoonist, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Modell’s contributions to the magazine for more than 50 years evoked for readers their everyday vexations.

name: Ronald C. Davidson
headline: Ronald C. Davidson, Pioneer of Fusion Power, Dies at 74
abstract: During Dr. Davidson’s tenure, the Princeton Plasma Physics Laboratory made major advances toward harnessing fusion, which powers the sun.

name: Charles M. Harper
headline: Charles M. Harper, Who Made ConAgra a Food Giant, Dies at 88
abstract: As chief executive he grew the company from a faltering $600 million operation to a $20 billion juggernaut, but he had less success at RJR Nabisco.

name: Michael Dann
headline: Michael Dann, TV Programmer, Dies at 94; Scheduled Horowitz and Hillbillies
abstract: He brought “The Defenders,” “The Smothers Brothers Comedy Hour,” “The Mary Tyler Moore Show” and “The Beverly Hillbillies” to the screen, along with recitals by Vladimir Horowitz.

name: Connie Kopelov
profession: First Same-Sex Couple Legally Married in New York
headline: Connie Kopelov, of First Same-Sex Couple Legally Married in New York, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Kopelov and her partner of 23 years, Phyllis Siegel, were the first couple through the door of the marriage bureau the day the law took effect.

name: Rick MacLeish
profession: One of the Flyers Broad Street Bullies
headline: Rick MacLeish, One of the Flyers’ Broad Street Bullies, Dies at 66
abstract: MacLeish helped Philadelphia’s fledgling N.H.L. franchise win two Stanley Cups during the 1970s, including the first one not claimed by any of the league’s original six teams.

name: Helen Keller
headline: Helen Keller’s Obituary
abstract: The New York Times obituary of Helen Keller.

name: Nanette Rainone
profession: Early Creator of Feminist Radio Shows
headline: Nanette Rainone, Early Creator of Feminist Radio Shows, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Rainone made her mark during the late 1960s and early ’70s at the New York station WBAI, where she worked as a reporter and programmer.

name: Janice Crouch
headline: Janice Crouch, ‘Gospel of Prosperity’ Disciple, Dies at 78
abstract: The Trinity Broadcasting Network and its “gospel of prosperity” reached millions of viewers around the world and had lately been fighting multiple lawsuits.

name: Lou Gehrig
headline: Lou Gehrig’s Obituary
abstract: The New York Times obituary of Lou Gehrig.

name: Roger Enrico
headline: Roger Enrico, PepsiCo Chief During 1980s ‘Cola Wars,’ Dies at 71
abstract: He made marketing deals with celebrities like Michael Jackson, Madonna, Cindy Crawford and Michael J. Fox to try to gain market share from Coca-Cola.

name: John Margolies
headline: John Margolies, Photographer of Whimsical Architecture, Dies at 76
abstract: For decades, Mr. Margolies went out of his way to capture images of unusual sites like the Donut Hole in La Puente, Calif.

name: Jeremy Steig
headline: Jeremy Steig, Flutist Who Bridged Jazz and Rock, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Steig was the leader of one of the first jazz-rock bands, Jeremy & the Satyrs.

name: Mohammed Abdelaziz
profession: Advocate of an Independent Western Sahara
headline: Mohammed Abdelaziz, Advocate of an Independent Western Sahara, Dies at 68
abstract: The Polisario Front, led for four decades by Mr. Abdelaziz, has tried to establish a sovereign state for the disputed region’s Berber tribesmen.

name: Ruhollah Khomeini
profession: A Man Who Shook the World
headline: Iran’s Ruhollah Khomeini, a Man Who Shook the World
abstract: Mourning Ruhollah Khomeini, the founder of the Islamic republic, required every Iranian’s complete attention.

name: Hugh Honour
headline: Hugh Honour, Art Historian and Author, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Honour wrote and edited with John Fleming, his life partner, from a base in italy.

name: Dave Swarbrick
profession: British Folk Fiddler With Fairport Convention
headline: Dave Swarbrick, British Folk Fiddler With Fairport Convention, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Swarbrick was a prime mover in trad-rock, which connected the ferment of folk-rock and psychedelia to a deep British heritage of storytelling ballads and dance tunes.

name: Muhammad Ali
headline: Muhammad Ali Dies at 74: Titan of Boxing and the 20th Century
abstract: Ali was the most thrilling if not the best heavyweight boxer of all time, a towering figure with an agile mind who was both admired and vilified for his religious, political and social stances.

name: T. Marshall Hahn Jr.
headline: T. Marshall Hahn Jr., Who Remade Virginia Tech as President, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Hahn transformed a regional military college with a mostly white, male student body into a diverse, internationally renowned research university.

name: Bobby Williams
profession: Led Undefeated Notre Dame to a Title in 1949
headline: Bobby Williams Dies at 86; Led Undefeated Notre Dame to a Title in 1949
abstract: The Irish finished 10-0 after Williams became the starter his junior year.

name: Thomas Schaefer
profession: Ranking Officer Among American Hostages in Iran
headline: Thomas Schaefer, 85, Ranking Officer Among American Hostages in Iran, Dies
abstract: Mr. Schaefer endured death threats, a hunger strike and three months of solitary confinement during 444 days as a hostage in Tehran.

name: Robert F. Kennedy
headline: On One California Night, Triumph and Tragedy
abstract: “In many ways, the personal characteristics of Robert Kennedy are very much like the dominant characteristics of the American people,” The New York Times wrote on June 6, 1968, the day he died.

name: Peter Shaffer
profession: Playwright Won Tonys for Equus and Amadeus
headline: Peter Shaffer Dies at 90; Playwright Won Tonys for ‘Equus’ and ‘Amadeus’
abstract: Movie versions of Mr. Shaffer’s ambitious plays helped elevate his status at home in Britain and in the United States.

name: David Lamb
profession: Author and War Correspondent in Vietnam
headline: David Lamb, Author and War Correspondent in Vietnam, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Lamb covered the war in Vietnam and later opened a news bureau there; his work as a foreign correspondent led to books on the Arabs and Africans.

name: Phyllis Curtin
headline: Phyllis Curtin, American Soprano Who Championed New Music, Dies at 94
abstract: A mainstay of the New York City Opera in the 1950s and ‘60s, Ms. Curtin sang many leading roles yet operatic superstardom eluded her.

name: Viktor Korchnoi
headline: Viktor Korchnoi, Chess Giant Who Drew Soviet Ire, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Korchnoi was widely considered one of the best players in history, though he never won a world championship. He defected from the Soviet Union in the 1970s.

name: Kimbo Slice
headline: Kimbo Slice, Street Brawler and M.M.A. Fighter, Dies at 42
abstract: Slice parlayed fighting videos on YouTube into a mixed martial arts career.

name: Summer Obits
headline: The Eternally Quotable Dorothy Parker
abstract: Dorothy Parker was famous for her bons mots. Here are some of our favorites.

name: Aileen Ward
headline: Aileen Ward, Author of Award-Winning Keats Biography, Dies at 97
abstract: Professor Ward spent nine years researching “John Keats: The Making of a Poet,” which won the National Book Award in 1964.

name: Patti Grace Smith
headline: Patti Grace Smith, Champion of Private Space Travel, Dies at 68
abstract: As a federal aviation official, Ms. Smith set policies that allowed private space companies to flourish and planned to travel to space herself one day.

name: Boyce F. Martin Jr.
profession: Liberal U.S. Judge in Seminal Cases
headline: Boyce F. Martin Jr., Liberal U.S. Judge in Seminal Cases, Dies at 80
abstract: Judge Martin’s rulings on affirmative action in college admissions and President Obama’s health care law were affirmed by the Supreme Court.

name: William Wright
headline: William Wright, Biographer of Lillian Hellman, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Wright’s 1986 “Lillian Hellman: The Image, the Woman,” the first full treatment of her life, was written despite Hellman’s fierce opposition.

name: Antonio Imbert Barrera
headline: Antonio Imbert Barrera, Who Helped Assassinate Dominican Dictator Trujillo, Dies at 95
abstract: General Imbert, who had been a businessman became a national hero and for a short time, president, after he and a group of plotters disposed of Rafael L. Trujillo Molina.

name: Walter Curley
headline: Walter Curley, Venture Capitalist and U.S. Ambassador, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Curley, the ambassador to Ireland and France and New York City’s official greeter under two mayors, was a prodigious fund-raiser for President George Bush.

name: Dennis McCullough
profession: Pioneer of Slow Medicine in End-of-Life Care
headline: Dennis McCullough, Pioneer of ‘Slow Medicine’ in End-of-Life Care, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. McCullough’s movement, which advocates palliative care over invasive regimens for older patients, has been increasingly available in nursing homes.

name: Jerome S. Bruner
profession: Shaped Understanding of the Young Mind
headline: Jerome S. Bruner, Who Shaped Understanding of the Young Mind, Dies at 100
abstract: Dr. Bruner’s writings, which helped reduce the influence of behaviorism on psychology, were vastly influential on education policy.

name: Theresa Saldana
headline: Theresa Saldana, Actress and Attack Survivor, Dies at 61
abstract: Ms. Saldana appeared in “Raging Bull” and “I Wanna Hold Your Hand,” and in a TV movie that documented her near-fatal knife attack by a stalker.

name: Thomas J. Perkins
profession: Pioneering Venture Capitalist in Silicon Valley
headline: Thomas J. Perkins, Pioneering Venture Capitalist in Silicon Valley, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Perkins, a co-founder of Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers, nurtured both the venture capital industry and a generation of technology.

name: Manohar Aich
profession: 4-Foot-11 Bodybuilder Known as the Pocket Hercules
headline: Manohar Aich, 4-Foot-11 Bodybuilder Known as the Pocket Hercules, Dies at 103
abstract: Mr. Aich, who won the Mr. Universe title in 1952, built his physique while in prison for protesting Britain’s colonization of India.

name: Gordie Howe
profession: Mr. Hockey for the Red Wings
headline: Gordie Howe, Mr. Hockey for the Red Wings, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Howe, who only fully retired from his playing career at age 52, was regarded as one of the sport’s best all-around players.

name: Morton White
headline: Morton White, Philosopher of Holistic Pragmatism, Dies at 99
abstract: Professor White said his intellect awoke in college. Before that he was a “child of the streets” more conversant with baseball players than books.

name: Steve Wolfe
profession: Painter of Books by Their Covers
headline: Steve Wolfe, a Painter of Books by Their Covers, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Wolfe was best known for creating trompe l’oeil portraits of well-loved titles by Chandler, Proust and Joyce.

name: Kenneth Axelson
profession: Troubleshot New York Citys Fiscal Crisis
headline: Kenneth Axelson, Who Troubleshot New York City’s Fiscal Crisis, Dies at 93
abstract: The city enlisted Mr. Axelson, an executive of J. C. Penney, as a deputy mayor in 1975 to help balance its budget and stave off bankruptcy.

name: Margaret Heldt
headline: Margaret Heldt, Hairdresser Who Built the Beehive, Dies at 98
abstract: A Chicago beautician redefined coiffure for women of the 1960s and decades beyond, thanks to aerosol spray and a favorite hat.

name: Anatol Kovarsky
headline: Anatol Kovarsky, New Yorker Cartoonist for Decades, Dies at 97
abstract: A master of the wordless visual gag, Mr. Kovarsky produced nearly 40 covers for the magazine and 300 cartoons, each with a subtle, intellectual twist.

name: Janet Waldo
headline: Janet Waldo, Voice of Judy Jetson, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Waldo, a voice-over actress, played sprightly teenagers for decades on popular cartoon shows, most notably “The Jetsons.”

name: Jorge Luis Borges
headline: Not Forgotten: Jorge Luis Borges, Master of the Mystical
abstract: The mystical, enigmatic and paradoxical imbued the writing of Jorge Luis Borges, an Argentine author whose concise, intricate work overflowed with wonder.

name: Rhoda Blumberg
profession: Childrens Books Brought History to Life
headline: Rhoda Blumberg, Whose Children’s Books Brought History to Life, Dies at 98
abstract: Turning to history in her mid-50s, Ms. Blumberg infused her nonfiction with enlightening nuggets that tantalized young readers.

name: Chips Moman
headline: Chips Moman, Hit-Making Producer and Songwriter, Dies at 79
abstract: He helped define the Memphis sound in soul music in the 1960s and helped revive Elvis Presley’s career in the late ’60s.

name: Philip Majerus
headline: Dr. Philip Majerus, Who Discerned Aspirin’s Heart Benefits, Dies at 79
abstract: Dr. Majerus is credited with recognizing that small doses of aspirin taken daily can help to prevent heart attacks and strokes.

name: Ella Fitzgerald
headline: Not Forgotten: The Surprisingly Quiet Ella Fitzgerald
abstract: A listener would not have realized it hearing her crooning, belting or scatting, but Ella Fitzgerald was a quiet person in private.

name: Richard Selzer
headline: Richard Selzer, Who Fictionalized Medicine’s Absurdity and Gore, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Selzer, who spent years as a surgeon, turned his operating-room experiences into fictional stories about modern medicine.

name: Gregory Rabassa
profession: Premier Translator of Spanish and Portuguese Fiction
headline: Gregory Rabassa, a Premier Translator of Spanish and Portuguese Fiction, Dies at 94
abstract: Professor Rabassa was known in particular for making the wave of dynamic and powerful fiction that emerged in Latin America in the 1960s accessible in English.

name: Wernher von Braun
profession: Rocket Pioneer With a Dark Past
headline: Not Forgotten: Wernher von Braun, Rocket Pioneer With a Dark Past
abstract: Wernher von Braun played a key role in Hitler’s rocket program before turning to space exploration.

name: Melvin Dwork
profession: Once Cast From Navy for Being Gay
headline: Melvin Dwork, Once Cast From Navy for Being Gay, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Dwork became a renowned interior designer and, in 2011, won his fight to have his 1944 dishonorable discharge deemed honorable.

name: Kenneth Walton
profession: F.B.I.s Bold New York Face in the 80s
headline: Kenneth Walton, F.B.I.’s Bold New York Face in the ’80s, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Walton, who mixed the flair of a central-casting G-man with the nerve to defy rigid protocol, was the bureau’s public face in cases involving a Tylenol poisoning scare and a Brink’s truck robbery.

name: Gene Cavallero Jr.
headline: Gene Cavallero Jr., Who Ran the Colony Restaurant, Dies at 92
abstract: The Colony occupied a lofty perch in New York City’s dining scene, becoming a destination for boldface names like Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis and Frank Sinatra.

name: Robert Paine
headline: Robert Paine, Ecologist Who Found ‘Keystone Species,’ Dies at 83
abstract: Dr. Paine identified certain species, like sea otters and starfish, that if removed, could disproportionately affect their ecosystems and neighboring species.

name: Michelle Cliff
headline: Michelle Cliff, Who Wrote of Colonialism and Racism, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Cliff, the partner of the poet Adrienne Rich, who died in 2012, devoted herself to giving voice to suppressed histories, starting with her own.

name: Desmond Heeley
headline: Desmond Heeley, an ‘Alchemist’ of Theater Design, Dies at 85
abstract: At home in theater, opera and ballet, Mr. Heeley created costumes for the likes of Laurence Olivier, Beverly Sills and Margot Fonteyn and imaginative sets for productions throughout the world.

name: Lois Duncan
profession: Author Knew What You Did Last Summer
headline: Lois Duncan, 82, Dies; Author Knew ‘What You Did Last Summer’
abstract: Though her books had their share of violence, Ms. Duncan said she was “utterly horrified” when she saw the film adaptation of “I Know What You Did Last Summer.”

name: Anton Yelchin
headline: Anton Yelchin, ‘Star Trek’ Actor, Dies at 27
abstract: Mr. Yelchin had roles in independent films and on TV before landing the part of Chekov, which he reprised in the coming “Star Trek Beyond.”

name: Be
headline: Prince Be, Who Infused Rap With Mysticism, Dies at 46
abstract: The singer’s psychedelic pop-rap group, P.M. Dawn, which had hits in the early 1990s, was both popular and maligned.

name: Donald Shea
headline: Donald Shea, Officer Who Captured Infamous Bank Robber, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Shea arrested Willie Sutton, known as Slick Willie for carrying out robberies in disguise, in a highly publicized 1952 case.

name: Benjamin “Bugsy” Siegel
headline: Not Forgotten: Benjamin “Bugsy” Siegel, Las Vegas Visionary
abstract: Benjamin “Bugsy” Siegel is mainly remembered as a vicious mobster, but he also helped turn Las Vegas from a sleepy desert town into a grown-up playground.

name: Richard Linke
headline: Richard Linke, Andy Griffith’s Talent Manager, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Linke brought some clients, who included actors like Andy Griffith and Jim Nabors, from relative obscurity to mainstream success.

name: Lorna Kelly
profession: Left the Sothebys Rostrum to Help the Poor
headline: Lorna Kelly Dies at 70; Left the Sotheby’s Rostrum to Help the Poor
abstract: Ms. Kelly, one of the first female fine-art auctioneers in the world, grew discontented with her profession and embarked on a series of charitable endeavors.

name: Jack Fuller
headline: Jack Fuller, 69, Chicago Tribune Journalist Who Led Expansion, Dies
abstract: Mr. Fuller joined the paper at 16 and went on to win a Pulitzer Prize and to preside over Tribune Company’s $8 billion acquisition of Times Mirror.

name: David T. Morgenthaler
headline: David T. Morgenthaler, Who Shaped Venture Capitalism, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Morgenthaler founded his first venture capital firm in 1968 and pushed legislative agendas that shaped the industry.

name: Benoîte Groult
headline: Benoîte Groult, French Feminist and Writer, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Groult’s 1988 novel, ‘Salt on Our Skin,’ was branded by some as pornographic for its depiction of an extramarital affair.

name: Victor Stanculescu
headline: Victor Stanculescu, 88, Romanian General Who Turned Against Ceausescu, Dies
abstract: General Stanculescu helped the Communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu escape after he was toppled in 1989, then engineered his trial and execution.

name: Judy Garland
headline: Not Forgotten: The Rainbow That Judy Garland Never Got Over
abstract: Fame and fortune could never quite fill the void Judy Garland felt in her life.

name: Bill Berkson
profession: Poet and Art Critic of 60s Manhattan In-Crowd
headline: Bill Berkson, Poet and Art Critic of ’60s Manhattan In-Crowd, Dies at 76
abstract: His friends were legion, an endless roll call of the geniuses, provocateurs and poseurs who gave the decade its distinctive cultural tang.

name: Nicholas Clinch
headline: Nicholas Clinch, Who Took On Unclimbed Mountains, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Clinch led the first ascent of Hidden Peak, in northeast Pakistan, in 1958, and of Mount Vinson, in Antarctica, in 1966.

name: Robert Cox
profession: Man Behind the Just Say No Antidrug Campaign
headline: Robert Cox, Man Behind the ‘Just Say No’ Antidrug Campaign, Dies at 78
abstract: He was also responsible for the Amtrak “All aboard” slogan, and Ford’s “Quality is Job 1.”

name: Bill Richmond
headline: Bill Richmond, Longtime Collaborator With Jerry Lewis, Dies at 94
abstract: As a writer Mr. Richmond teamed up with Mr. Lewis on raft of films, including “The Nutty Professor,” before switching to TV and working with Carol Burnett.

name: David Thatcher
profession: Part of 42 Doolittle Raid on Japan
headline: David Thatcher, Part of ’42 Doolittle Raid on Japan, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Thatcher helped save the lives of four wounded fellow crewmen in the raid, America’s first strike against the Japanese homeland in World War II.

name: Paul Cox
headline: Paul Cox, Independent Filmmaker Who Explored Postmodern Life, Dies at 76
abstract: The Dutch-born Australian director was considered a father of Australian art cinema. He said he chose filmmaking not out of ambition, but because it was “pure compulsion.”

name: Wayne Jackson
headline: Wayne Jackson, Memphis Horns Trumpeter, Dies at 74
abstract: With the tenor saxophonist Andrew Love, Mr. Jackson helped define the soul sound of Stax Records.

name: John Ashe
profession: Ex-Diplomat Accused in U.N. Corruption Case
headline: John Ashe, Ex-Diplomat Accused in U.N. Corruption Case, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Ashe, a former president of the General Assembly, was accused in a bribery scheme that involved more than $1 million in payments from sources in China.

name: Jonas Salk
headline: Not Forgotten: Dr. Jonas Salk and the Continuing Battle Against Polio
abstract: Dr. Jonas Salk created the first successful vaccine against poliomyelitis, a debilitating illness that has proved difficult to eradicate.

name: Dan Daniel
profession: AM Radio D.J. and One of the Good Guys
headline: Dan Daniel, AM Radio D.J. and One of the Good Guys, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Daniel joined WMCA in 1961 becoming known among his rock ’n’ roll fans as “America’s most adequate swinging disc jockey,” a line he had coined.

name: Ralph Stanley
profession: Mountain Music Gave Rise to Bluegrass
headline: Ralph Stanley, Whose Mountain Music Gave Rise to Bluegrass, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Stanley was a singer, banjo player and guardian of unvarnished mountain music whose staple, updated for “O Brother, Where Art Thou?,” introduced him to a new generation of listeners.

name: Bernie Worrell
profession: Keyboards Left an Imprint on Funk and Hip-Hop
headline: Bernie Worrell, Whose Keyboards Left an Imprint on Funk and Hip-Hop, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Worrell created indelible signatures on Parliament and Funkadelic songs while showing that synthetic sounds could be earthy and untamed.

name: Goro Hasegawa
headline: Goro Hasegawa, Creator of Othello Board Game, Dies at 83
abstract: Similar to the ancient Go and Britain’s Reversi, Othello — played with black-and-white discs — has sold tens of millions of copies since its introduction in the 1970s.

name: Michael Herr
headline: Michael Herr, Author of a Vietnam Classic, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Herr, a war correspondent best known for his book “Dispatches,” was also a writer on the films “Full Metal Jacket” and “Apocalypse Now.”

name: Frank Chapot
profession: Olympic Show Jumper and Mainstay of the Sport
headline: Frank Chapot, Olympic Show Jumper and Mainstay of the Sport, Dies at 84
abstract: Chapot competed in six Olympic Games and coached the United States Equestrian Team’s show-jumping squad in six more.

name: Bill Cunningham
headline: Bill Cunningham, Legendary Times Fashion Photographer, Dies at 87
abstract: In nearly 40 years working for The New York Times, Mr. Cunningham operated both as a chronicler of fashion and as an unlikely cultural anthropologist.

name: Jim Hickman
profession: Slugger for Expansion Mets and All-Star with Cubs
headline: Jim Hickman, Slugger for Expansion Mets and All-Star with Cubs, Dies at 79
abstract: Hickman set milestones on the expansion Mets team of the early ’60s with his power hitting before reaching his peak with the Chicago Cubs.

name: John Santucci
profession: Prosecutor in High-Profile Cases in New York
headline: John Santucci, Prosecutor in High-Profile Cases in New York, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Santucci, a former Queens district attorney, drew praise and controversy in trials involving municipal corruption, police conduct and a racial attack.

name: Gerald Walpin
headline: Gerald Walpin, Watchdog Fired Over AmeriCorps Inquiry, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Walpin was a staunch conservative appointed by President George W. Bush as inspector general of the Corporation for National and Community Service.

name: Peter Hutton
headline: Peter Hutton, Filmmaker With Austerely Romantic Worldview, Dies at 71
abstract: All of Mr. Hutton’s films were silent. Generally devoid of camera movement and montage, they suggest sketchbooks or photographic albums.

name: Sam Bell
headline: Sam Bell, Exacting Mentor of College Runners, Dies at 88
abstract: Bell coached track and field and cross-country at Indiana for nearly three decades, producing several Olympic athletes in the process.

name: Pat Summitt
headline: Pat Summitt, Tennessee Basketball Coach Who Emboldened Women’s Sports, Dies at 64
abstract: Summitt led the Tennessee women’s basketball team to eight national titles in 38 seasons, winning more games than any other Division I coach, male or female.

name: Franz Ferdinand
headline: Not Forgotten: Franz Ferdinand, Whose Assassination Sparked a World War
abstract: World War I began with the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand by an 18-year-old student in Bosnia.

name: Buddy Ryan
profession: Combative Defensive Genius in the N.F.L
headline: Buddy Ryan, Combative Defensive Genius in the N.F.L., Dies at 85
abstract: His shifting and blitzing alignments helped propel the Jets and the Bears to Super Bowl titles.

name: Mack Rice
headline: Mack Rice, Who Wrote ‘Mustang Sally,’ Dies at 82
abstract: Detroit became his home, but Memphis and Stax Records were Mr. Rice’s muse.

name: Barbara Goldsmith
headline: Barbara Goldsmith, Author of ‘Little Gloria,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Goldsmith wrote “Little Gloria … Happy at Last,” a best-selling account of the bitter 1934 custody battle over Gloria Vanderbilt, published in 1980.

name: Scotty Moore
headline: Scotty Moore, Hard-Driving Guitarist Who Backed Elvis Presley, Dies at 84
abstract: His terse, bluesy licks on Presley’s early hits virtually created the rockabilly guitar style and established the guitar as a lead instrument in rock ’n’ roll.

name: Phil Parker
headline: Phil Parker, Who Helped Homeless Alcoholics, Dies at 86
abstract: After he stopped drinking, Mr. Parker founded a supported work program and later became a social worker in New York City.

name: Stanley Meisler
headline: Stanley Meisler, Foreign Correspondent Who Pivoted to Art History, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Meisler, a longtime foreign correspondent for The Los Angeles Times, made a second career as a writer on art and art history.

name: Alvin Toffler
headline: Alvin Toffler, Author of ‘Future Shock,’ Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Toffler wrote the prophetic 1970 best seller and other books anticipating how people would deal with runaway change and an explosion of information.

name: Jerome Fisher
headline: Jerome Fisher, a Founder of Nine West, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Fisher and Vince Camuto produced fashionable shoes at reasonable prices.

name: Simon Ramo
profession: Helped Develop ICBMs in the Cold War
headline: Simon Ramo Dies at 103; Helped Develop ICBMs in the Cold War
abstract: Dr. Ramo advised presidents on science and technology, and was a postwar force in the aerospace and electronics industries.

name: Frank Whipple
headline: Frank Whipple, Whose Nun Paintings Drew Hollywood Fans, Dies at 93
abstract: Over more than half a century, he turned out thousands of whimsical nun paintings. His celebrity patrons included Frank Sinatra, Cary Grant and John Wayne.

name: Upton Sinclair
headline: Not Forgotten: Upton Sinclair, Whose Muckraking Changed the Meat Industry
abstract: Sinclair’s novel “The Jungle” spurred public outrage that led to legislation in 1906 aimed at regulating the food and drug industries.

name: Oh Se-jong
headline: Oh Se-jong, Olympic Speedskater Who Won Relay Gold, Dies at 33
abstract: Oh was a member of star-studded South Korean teams that won titles at the Olympic Games and world championships.

name: Anahid Ajemian
headline: Anahid Ajemian, Violinist and New-Music Champion, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Ajemian was known for her extensive solo work but also for performing with her sister, Maro Ajemian, a pianist.

name: Wassyl Slipak
profession: Left Paris Opera for Ukraine War
headline: Wassyl Slipak, Who Left Paris Opera for Ukraine War, Dies at 41
abstract: Mr. Slipak quit his baritone position in Paris to join nationalist fighters in his native Ukraine.

name: Dave Heath
headline: Dave Heath, Photographer of Isolation, Dies at 85
abstract: The artist went through many years of obscurity before being rediscovered.

name: Geoffrey Hill
headline: Geoffrey Hill, Dense and Allusive British Poet, Is Dead at 84
abstract: His poems ranged from dark meditations on political violence to rapturous evocations of the English countryside.

name: Irving Morris
headline: Irving Morris, Who Fought for Justice Pro Bono, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Morris, a lawyer, wrote a book about his decade-long effort to overturn the convictions of three men in a Delaware rape case, earning the praise of a Supreme Court justice.

name: Medgar Evers
profession: Assassination Reverberated Through the Civil Rights Movement
headline: Not Forgotten: Medgar Evers, Whose Assassination Reverberated Through the Civil Rights Movement
abstract: “You can kill a man, but you can’t kill an idea,” he once said. Evers championed school integration, encouraged blacks to vote and staged daring protests against racial inequality in the South.

name: Elie Wiesel
profession: Auschwitz Survivor and Nobel Peace Prize Winner
headline: Elie Wiesel, Auschwitz Survivor and Nobel Peace Prize Winner, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Wiesel, the author of “Night,” seared the memory of the Holocaust on the world’s conscience.

name: Michael Cimino
profession: Director of The Deer Hunter and Heavens Gate
headline: Michael Cimino, Director of ‘The Deer Hunter’ and ‘Heaven’s Gate,’ Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Cimino won an Academy Award for the 1978 war drama “The Deer Hunter,” just his second film, but his next film, “Heaven’s Gate,” was panned and bombed at the box office.

name: Jack Taylor
headline: Jack Taylor, Founder of Enterprise Rent-A-Car, Dies at 94
abstract: Starting with a two-person office with seven cars in 1957, Mr. Taylor built a $19.4 billion company with 1.7 million vehicles.

name: Jack Taylor
profession: Scourge of the Wrecking Ball in Manhattan
headline: Jack Taylor, Scourge of the Wrecking Ball in Manhattan, Dies at 93
abstract: An amateur landmark preservationist, Mr. Taylor had a legacy including the Ladies’ Mile Shopping District and Tammany Hall. But there were also defeats.

name: Donald Jelinek
headline: Donald Jelinek, Lawyer for Attica Prisoners, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Jelinek also represented civil rights workers in the South and Native Americans who seized Alcatraz Island to air their grievances against the government.

name: Michel Rocard
headline: Michel Rocard, Former Prime Minister of France, Dies at 85
abstract: The politician was known for his efforts as a pragmatic reformer of the Socialist Party and for his struggles with President François Mitterrand.

name: Abbas Kiarostami
headline: Abbas Kiarostami, Acclaimed Iranian Filmmaker, Dies at 76
abstract: Associated with the Iranian New Wave of the late 1960s, Mr. Kiarostami was known for his parablelike dramas of ordinary people.

name: Robin Hardy
profession: Set The Wicker Man Cult Alight
headline: Robin Hardy, Who Set ‘The Wicker Man’ Cult Alight, Dies at 86
abstract: Sex and human sacrifice are the core of a pagan society in Scotland in “The Wicker Man,” Mr. Hardy’s best-known film.

name: Noel Neill
profession: Lois Lane to George Reevess Superman
headline: Noel Neill, the Lois Lane to George Reeves’s ‘Superman,’ Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Neill had roles in movies including “The Blue Dahlia,” “The Sky Dragon,” “Henry Aldrich’s Little Secret,” and “Junior Prom,” among many others.

name: Abner Mikva
headline: Abner Mikva, Lawmaker, Judge and Mentor to Obama, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Mikva was one of the nation’s leading liberal politicians for decades, having served in Congress, as a federal judge and as counsel in the Clinton White House.

name: Yves Bonnefoy
headline: Yves Bonnefoy, Pre-Eminent French Poet, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Bonnefoy was also regarded as France’s leading translator of Shakespeare and a wide-ranging art critic in the spirit of Baudelaire.

name: Roscoe C. Brown Jr.
profession: Tuskegee Airman and Confidant to New York Politicians
headline: Roscoe C. Brown Jr., Tuskegee Airman and Confidant to New York Politicians, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Brown had few political aspirations himself but was an adviser to black elected officials and a calm voice during the city’s racial strife.

name: Louis Armstrong
headline: Not Forgotten: Louis Armstrong, the Entertainer Who Epitomized Jazz
abstract: Was Louis Armstrong the world’s most beloved entertainer, or was he the single most important musician in the history of jazz? The answer is yes.

name: Lou Fontinato
headline: Lou Fontinato, N.H.L. Enforcer Who Battled Gordie Howe, Dies at 84
abstract: Fontinato had 1,247 penalty minutes in a nine-year career with the Rangers and the Canadiens, and his hockey fight with Gordie Howe in 1959 was memorialized by Life magazine.

name: Stanley Gault
headline: Stanley Gault, Who Led Rubbermaid and Goodyear, Dies at 90
abstract: After a long career at General Electric, Stanley C. Gault led turnarounds at Rubbermaid and Goodyear.

name: Robert Nye
headline: Robert Nye, Novelist Who Imagined Falstaff’s Memoirs, Dies at 77
abstract: The rollicking writer also wrote poetry and children’s books.

name: Irving Gottesman
headline: Irving Gottesman, Pioneering Psychologist on Schizophrenia, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Gottesman was perhaps best known for a study of twins that found a genetic link to mental illness, changing how people thought about its origins.

name: Baldev Duggal
headline: Baldev Duggal, Film Processing Innovator, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Duggal turned a $200 grubstake into Duggal Visual Solutions, and helped transform the area around the Flatiron Building into a center of fashion and photography.

name: C.D. Brooks
headline: C.D. Brooks Is Dead at 85; Preached Seventh-Day Adventist Message
abstract: For six decades, Mr. Brooks used the “Breath of Life” to help convert tens of thousands and establish 15 congregations in cities across the country.

name: Arthur Conan Doyle
profession: Spiritualist Behind the Rational Sherlock Holmes
headline: Not Forgotten: Arthur Conan Doyle, the Spiritualist Behind the Rational Sherlock Holmes
abstract: Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, remembered for creating the staunchly rational Sherlock Holmes, was also a devoted spiritualist.

name: Peter Powers
headline: Peter Powers, Mayor Giuliani’s Steady Right Hand, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Powers was a high school friend whom Rudolph W. Giuliani recruited to impose order on his chaotic novice mayoral campaign and later installed as his even-tempered alter ego in City Hall.

name: John McMartin
profession: Versatile Mainstay on Broadway and TV
headline: John McMartin, Versatile Mainstay on Broadway and TV, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. McMartin starred in “Sweet Charity” on stage and screen and was a favorite of Bob Fosse, Harold Prince and Stephen Sondheim.

name: Don Friedman
headline: Don Friedman, Versatile Jazz Pianist, Dies at 81
abstract: Over a six-decade career, Mr. Friedman worked with the likes of Clark Terry, Ornette Coleman, Booker Little and Herbie Mann.

name: Alison Bernstein
headline: Alison Bernstein, Educator and Ford Foundation Executive, Dies at 69
abstract: At the Ford Foundation, Ms. Bernstein allocated tens of millions of dollars to programs for the arts and education at all levels.

name: Abdul Sattar Edhi
headline: Abdul Sattar Edhi, Pakistan’s ‘Father Teresa,’ Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Edhi set up a foundation that runs nursing homes, orphanages, soup kitchens and family planning centers — all free of charge — as well as Pakistan’s largest ambulance service.

name: Sydney H. Schanberg
profession: Times Reporter Chronicled Khmer Rouge Terror
headline: Sydney H. Schanberg Dies at 82; Times Reporter Chronicled Khmer Rouge Terror
abstract: Mr. Schanberg won a Pulitzer Prize for covering the fall of the Lon Nol regime to the Khmer Rouge in 1970s Cambodia. His account of a colleague’s survival during the genocide of millions inspired the film “The Killing Fields.”

name: Carl Haas
profession: Builder of a Formidable IndyCar Racing Team
headline: Carl Haas, Builder of a Formidable IndyCar Racing Team, Dies at 87
abstract: After a driving career in the 1950s, Mr. Haas worked with Paul Newman to operate a racing team that won more than 100 IndyCar races.

name: Laurence Olivier
headline: Not Forgotten: Laurence Olivier: Scene-Stealer Extraordinaire
abstract: He was one of the great theatrical performers — some say the greatest of all — of the 20th century, equally adept at comedy and tragedy.

name: John Brademas
headline: John Brademas, Indiana Congressman and N.Y.U. President, Dies at 89
abstract: A gregarious leader with voluminous contacts, Mr. Brademas transformed the university from a commuter school into a premier residential research and teaching institutions.

name: Vaughn Harper
headline: Vaughn Harper, Silky-Voiced D.J., Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Harper was the host of the WBLS radio show “Quiet Storm,” a nightly staple for New Yorkers.

name: William H. McNeill
headline: William H. McNeill, Professor and Prolific Author, Dies at 98
abstract: Professor McNeill’s catholic exploration of world history widened the traditional Eurocentric approach to the subject.

name: Bill Jones
headline: Bill Jones, Photographer of the Black Glitterati, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Jones first picked up a camera in the Air Force and later trained his lens on black actors and musicians whom the white media often ignored.

name: Frida Kahlo
headline: Not Forgotten: Frida Kahlo, Whose Self-Portraits Spoke to the Soul
abstract: She defined herself by her painting, especially when she painted herself. Kahlo died on this day 62 years ago.

name: Maralin Niska
profession: Lyric Soprano at New York City Opera
headline: Maralin Niska, Lyric Soprano at New York City Opera Who Won Hearts, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Niska, who appeared in 29 lead roles with City Opera, was known for her supple voice, her mesmerizing stage presence and her movie-star looks.

name: Bernardo Provenzano
headline: Bernardo Provenzano, Who Led Sicilian Mafia Clan, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. Provenzano managed to elude the Italian police for four decades before being captured in 2006.

name: Howard Raiffa
headline: Howard Raiffa, Mathematician Who Studied Decision Making, Dies at 92
abstract: He was co-founder of the Kennedy School of Government at Harvard and a professor at the university for 37 years who pioneered decision science.

name: Billy the Kid
headline: Not Forgotten: An Outlaw by Any Name: Billy the Kid
abstract: The Times branded the violent cattle rustler Billy the Kid “one of the worst characters this country has produced” shortly after his death in 1881.

name: Alfred G. Knudson
headline: Dr. Alfred G. Knudson, the ‘Mendel of Cancer Genetics,’ Dies at 93
