abstract: A 1971 theory on the inheritable nature of retinoblastoma in children, proved in 1986, is credited with helping advance the framework of how cancers are studied.

name: Michael Crawford
headline: Michael Crawford, Wiseacre With a Pen, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Crawford was a student of habits, trends and human interaction, most of which he exploited for gentle ridicule or defiant amusement.

name: Hector Babenco
profession: Director of Kiss of the Spider Woman
headline: Hector Babenco, Director of ‘Kiss of the Spider Woman,’ Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Babenco, one of Latin America’s most visible directors, established himself as a filmmaker unafraid to push boundaries.

name: Edmond L. Browning
headline: Edmond L. Browning, an Episcopal Church Presiding Bishop, Dies at 87
abstract: A leader who declared the church “open to all,” emphasizing women’s ordination, gay and lesbian congregants and civil rights.

name: Sally Beauman
headline: Sally Beauman, Author Whose Advance Set a Record, Dies at 71
abstract: Ms. Beauman was unknown in the publishing world when her steamy romance novel, “Destiny,” sold for more than $1 million.

name: Judy Feiffer
headline: Judy Feiffer, Who Helped Develop Two Top Memoirs, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Feiffer urged Maya Angelou to write “I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings” and worked with Christina Crawford on “Mommie Dearest.”

name: Xu Jiatun
headline: Xu Jiatun, Chinese Official Who Opposed Tiananmen Crackdown, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Xu, who was expelled from the Communist Party, fled to the United States in 1990.

name: Gregg Smith
headline: Gregg Smith, Choral Leader Who Elevated Standards, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Smith founded the Gregg Smith Singers in 1955 when he was still a graduate student and most choruses were made up of amateur singers.

name: John F. Kennedy Jr.
headline: Not Forgotten: John F. Kennedy Jr.: A Life Under a Microscope, Cut Short
abstract: John Fitzgerald Kennedy Jr. was as close to a prince du sang as an American can be, and like his father he came to an untimely and tragic end.

name: Nate Thurmond
headline: Nate Thurmond, Warriors Center and Defensive Wall, Dies at 74
abstract: A seven-time All-Star and Hall of Fame player went toe-to-toe with the N.B.A.’s dominant big men.

name: Alan Vega
headline: Alan Vega, Punk Music Pioneer and Artist, Dies at 78
abstract: Suicide, Mr. Vega’s band, was one of the first bands to bill themselves as “punk music.” In the 2000s, he resumed his career as a visual artist.

name: Wendell Anderson
headline: Wendell Anderson, Governor Behind the ‘Minnesota Miracle,’ Dies at 83
abstract: A popular, two-term governor who was also an Olympic silver medalist, Mr. Anderson oversaw reforms in education financing and local property taxes.

name: Michael Elliott
headline: Michael Elliott, Newsmagazine Editor and Humanitarian, Dies at 65
abstract: A longtime journalist who left the industry to lead an advocacy group founded by the rock star Bono.

name: Carolyn See
headline: Carolyn See, Novelist Who Portrayed Quirks of Southern California, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. See often put portraits of intimate relationships and sociological observations of the lives of Angelenos together with grander fictional ideas.

name: John Gruen
headline: John Gruen, Cultural Renaissance Man, Dies at 89
abstract: As a composer, critic, biographer and photographer, Mr. Gruen excelled at an unusually diverse set of talents.

name: Tom Kibble
headline: Tom Kibble, Physicist Who Helped Discover the Higgs Mechanism, Dies at 83
abstract: Although Dr. Kibble was not awarded the Nobel Prize for his contributions to the discovery of the Higgs boson, his work sowed the seeds for other discoveries.

name: Bruce Lee
headline: Not Forgotten: A Fighter’s Fighter, Bruce Lee
abstract: The indomitable martial artist died at 32 before the release of his first Hollywood film, “Enter the Dragon.”

name: Garry Marshall
headline: Garry Marshall, ‘Pretty Woman’ Director, Dies at 81; a TV and Film Comedy Mastermind
abstract: Mr. Marshall’s work in TV and movies fattened the archive of romantic, family and buddy comedies and found a sweet spot in the middle of the mainstream.

name: Betsy Bloomingdale
headline: Betsy Bloomingdale, Socialite and Friend of Influencers, Dies at 93
abstract: Mrs. Bloomingdale was a fashion leader who, with her department store heir husband, maintained friendships with politicians and entertainers, keeping diaries of parties she hosted.

name: Karl Case
headline: Karl Case, Economist Who Developed Home Price Index, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Case, a professor at Wellesley College, worked with a Yale economist to develop the Case-Shiller Index to track home values in an opaque market.

name: Billy Name
headline: Billy Name, Who Glazed Warhol’s Factory in Silver, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Name was a photographer, a muse and a lover of Warhol who captured the Factory coterie in black-and-white pictures.

name: Dennis Green
profession: Pioneering Coach of the Vikings and the Cardinals
headline: Dennis Green, Pioneering Coach of the Vikings and the Cardinals, Dies at 67
abstract: Green was only the second black head coach in the modern era of the N.F.L. when he took over at Minnesota.

name: William Gaines
headline: William Gaines, Prizewinning Investigative Reporter, Dies at 82
abstract: A longtime journalist whose reporting on corruption in Chicago won two Pulitzer Prizes.

name: Gary S. Paxton
profession: Mixed Bag of a Life Was Filled With Music
headline: Gary S. Paxton, Whose Mixed Bag of a Life Was Filled With Music, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Paxton began performing on or producing hits like “Monster Mash” and “Cherry Pie,” saw hard times and ended up with a Grammy-winning gospel album.

name: David Horowitz
profession: Helped Make Bill Clinton a Media Darling
headline: David Horowitz, Who Helped Make Bill Clinton a Media Darling, Dies at 86
abstract: After a long convention speech in 1988, Mr. Clinton, then the governor of Arkansas, got a boost from Mr. Horowitz: a spot with his saxophone on “Johnny Carson.”

name: David Horowitz
profession: TV Consumer Advocate Cried, Fight Back!
headline: David Horowitz, 81, Dies; TV Consumer Advocate Cried, ‘Fight Back!’
abstract: On a nationally syndicated TV show, he put products to the test to see if they measured up to their claims. Johnny Carson spoofed him.

name: David Horowitz
headline: David Horowitz, Leftist Turned Trump Defender, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Once a Marxist, he came to embrace hard-right positions, including the falsehood that Mr. Trump won in 2020, and to mentor Stephen Miller, later the Trump adviser.

name: Thomas Sutherland
headline: Thomas Sutherland, Lebanon Hostage Who Was Freed After 6 Years, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Sutherland, an agriculture professor who was among dozens of Westerners kidnapped by Islamic militants in Beirut in the 1980s, was released in 1991.

name: Marni Nixon
headline: Marni Nixon, the Singing Voice Behind the Screen, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Nixon was the ghost singer for actresses in many of Hollywood’s most famous musicals, from “The King and I” to “West Side Story” to “My Fair Lady.”

name: Tim LaHaye
profession: Fundamentalist Leaders Grisly Novels Sold Millions
headline: Tim LaHaye Dies at 90; Fundamentalist Leader’s Grisly Novels Sold Millions
abstract: Dr. LaHaye, an evangelical minister and prolific writer, was co-author of the apocalyptic “Left Behind” novels and promoted traditional conservative organizations.

name: Robert Fano
headline: Robert Fano, 98, Dies; Engineer Who Helped Develop Interactive Computers
abstract: In the early 1960s, Dr. Fano and others developed a time-sharing operating system, which signaled a shift to a more interactive computing world.

name: Youree Dell Harris
headline: Youree Dell Harris, the TV Psychic Miss Cleo, Dies at 53
abstract: Ms. Harris’s Jamaican-accented character entered America’s pop culture zeitgeist in the late ’90s with the catchphrase, “Call me now!”

name: Mohamed Khan
headline: Mohamed Khan, Egyptian Filmmaker, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Khan drew popular and critical acclaim for his neorealist films, which focused on social ills and often featured feminist protagonists.

name: Sandy Pearlman
headline: Sandy Pearlman, Producer, Manager and Lyricist for Blue Öyster Cult, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Pearlman was also one of the first serious rock critics, writing and editing for the pioneering rock-culture magazine Crawdaddy.

name: James Nederlander
profession: Theater Owner Known as Broadways Last Patriarch
headline: James Nederlander, Theater Owner Known as Broadway’s Last Patriarch, Dies at 94
abstract: The man who built a theater empire was frequently a producer of shows as well.

name: Forrest E. Mars Jr.
headline: Forrest E. Mars Jr., Scion of a Candy Empire, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Mars played an early role in the company’s global expansion and became co-president with his brother in 1975.

name: James Alan McPherson
headline: James Alan McPherson, Pulitzer Prize-Winning Writer, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. McPherson grew up in the South, overcoming segregation to graduate from Harvard Law School and become the first black writer to win the Pulitzer Prize for fiction.

name: Otto Hahn
headline: Not Forgotten: Otto Hahn, the Nobel-Winning Chemist Whose Discovery Was Used in Hiroshima
abstract: The German chemist discovered that the atom could be split, paving the way for a nuclear bomb and changing the course of the 20th century.

name: Jack Davis
profession: Part of Mad Magazines Usual Gang of Idiots
headline: Jack Davis, Part of Mad Magazine’s Usual Gang of Idiots, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Davis poked fun at celebrities and politicians in Mad magazine for decades. His work also appeared on the covers of Time and TV Guide.

name: Denis Dubourdieu
headline: Denis Dubourdieu, Who Elevated Bordeaux White Wines, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Dubourdieu, a scientist, professor and winemaker, owned and managed several estates and educated a generation of French vineyard managers.

name: Dwight Jones
profession: Big Man Ejected in First U.S. Olympic Loss
headline: Dwight Jones, 64, Big Man Ejected in First U.S. Olympic Loss, Dies
abstract: Jones was thrown out near the end of the 1972 Olympic basketball championship game, contributing to the American team’s controversial 51-50 loss to the Soviet Union.

name: Matilda Rapaport
headline: Matilda Rapaport, an Extreme Skier, Is Dead at 30
abstract: A Swedish champion skied peaks that could be reached only by helicopter and appeared in many hair-raising ski films and videos.

name: Zelda Fichandler
headline: Zelda Fichandler, a Matriarch of Regional Theater, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Fichandler was a founder of the Arena Stage in Washington in 1950, building it into a professional force that helped spur the growth of theater companies around the country.

name: Robert Carswell
profession: Treasury Negotiator in Iran Hostage Crisis
headline: Robert Carswell, Treasury Negotiator in Iran Hostage Crisis, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Carswell was instrumental in choreographing the delicate financial talks that coaxed Tehran into freeing 52 American hostages in 1981.

name: Frank Hodsoll
headline: Frank Hodsoll, Who Navigated Arts Funding Under Reagan, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Hodsoll, an unlikely choice for the post, successfully lobbied against deep cuts in the National Endowment for the Arts during his tenure.

name: Dave Schwartz
headline: Dave Schwartz, 63, Dies; Was Weather Channel Meteorologist
abstract: Mr. Schwartz, known for an easygoing manner and gentle sense of humor, spoke on camera this year about his third bout with cancer.

name: Gloria DeHaven
profession: Sweetheart in Many a Movie Musical
headline: Gloria DeHaven, Sweetheart in Many a Movie Musical, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. DeHaven starred with June Allyson in “Two Girls and a Sailor,” Frank Sinatra in “Step Lively” and Judy Garland in “Summer Stock” before turning to TV roles.

name: Seymour Papert
headline: Seymour Papert, 88, Dies; Saw Education’s Future in Computers
abstract: Dr. Papert was a co-director of an artificial intelligence lab at M.I.T.; some considered him the foremost expert on technology and learning.

name: Suzanne Wright
headline: Suzanne Wright, a Founder of Autism Speaks, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Wright help found the advocacy group in 2005 after her grandson, Christian, stopped speaking and she struggled to find information about the disorder.

name: Marta Marzotto
headline: Marta Marzotto, Italian Designer and Socialite, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Marzotto was a countess and former model known for her boldly colorful garments and eye-catching accessories as well as her glittering parties.

name: Elio Guaitolini
headline: Elio Guaitolini, Restaurateur to New York’s Elite, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Guaitolini’s namesake restaurant on the Upper East Side has been an informal clubhouse for an A-list of writers, actors, producers and political heavyweights.

name: Alexander Graham Bell
profession: Sparked a New Era of Communication
headline: Not Forgotten: Alexander Graham Bell, Who Sparked a New Era of Communication
abstract: Alexander Graham Bell’s contraption of receivers connected to a series of wires forever changed the way people communicated.

name: Franciszek Macharski
profession: Archbishop Succeeded John Paul II in Krakow
headline: Franciszek Macharski, 89, Dies; Archbishop Succeeded John Paul II in Krakow
abstract: Cardinal Macharski, a close friend of the pope, was known for his work with the poor.

name: Forbes Carlile
headline: Forbes Carlile, Innovative Coach Who Studied Science of Swimming, Dies at 95
abstract: Carlile introduced a two-beat kick that saved energy, encouraged interval training and championed tapering training before major competitions.

name: James Baldwin
profession: Wrote for Equality at All Costs
headline: Not Forgotten: James Baldwin, Who Wrote for Equality at All Costs
abstract: The great African-American writer and activist, remembered through his own words.

name: Mahasweta Devi
headline: Mahasweta Devi, Bengali Writer and Activist Who Fought Injustice, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Devi’s work, which has been translated into many languages, reflected her time spent documenting India’s tribal communities.

name: James Houghton
headline: James Houghton, Founder of Signature Theater, Showcase for Playwrights, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Houghton also served as artistic director of the troupe, which presents season-long programs featuring the work of just one playwright.

name: Einojuhani Rautavaara
profession: His Lush Music Found Wide Appeal
headline: Einojuhani Rautavaara, Composer, Dies at 87; His Lush Music Found Wide Appeal
abstract: Many called him the greatest Finnish composer since Sibelius. Esa-Pekka Salonen and Magnus Lindberg were among his students.

name: Mary Ann Madden
headline: Mary Ann Madden, Creator of Wordplay Contests, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Madden created the magazine’s wordplay competition, which attracted an average of 1,500 readers every week. She retired in 2000.

name: Elena Doria
profession: Director of Metropolitan Operas Childrens Chorus
headline: Elena Doria, Director of Metropolitan Opera’s Children’s Chorus, Dies at 90
abstract: Equal parts den mother, wrangler and benevolent despot, Ms. Doria took the helm of the chorus in 1986 and presided over it for the next 23 years.

name: Jim Northrup
headline: Jim Northrup, Vietnam Veteran Who Wrote About Reservation Life, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Northrup, a published author, columnist, playwright, poet, performer and commentator, had crossover appeal beyond Indian country.

name: Hans Christian Andersen
headline: Not Forgotten: Sprung From Poverty, the Tales of Hans Christian Andersen Endure
abstract: Hans Christian Andersen’s stories, which were at least partly rooted in his difficult childhood, endure more than a century after his death.

name: Fred Tomlinson
headline: Fred Tomlinson, Singer Who Led a ‘Monty Python’ Troupe, Dies at 88
abstract: The arranger and his spoofing vocalists sang about Spam, lumberjacks and more for the comedy show.

name: Robert Rosencrans
headline: Robert Rosencrans, Who Helped Propel C-Span, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Rosencrans saw the broad potential of cable television when fewer than one in five homes was wired for it.

name: Steven LaTourette
headline: Steven LaTourette, Congressman Who Despised Gridlock, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. LaTourette, a centrist Ohio Republican, retired after nine terms in Congress because he was disgusted with Tea Party insurgents.

name: Chris Costner Sizemore
profession: Patient Behind The Three Faces of Eve
headline: Chris Costner Sizemore, Patient Behind ‘The Three Faces of Eve,’ Dies at 89
abstract: The woman whose story of dissociative identity disorder was made into the 1957 Oscar-winning movie was eventually treated and became a mental health advocate.

name: David Huddleston
profession: Title Lebowski in The Big Lebowski
headline: David Huddleston, the Title Lebowski in ‘The Big Lebowski,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Huddleston, a character actor with a gift for the cantankerous role, also played the blowhard Mayor Olson Johnson in “Blazing Saddles.”

name: Ahmed H. Zewail
headline: Ahmed H. Zewail, Nobel-Prize-Winning Chemist, Dies at 70
abstract: Dr. Zewail, a naturalized American citizen, was the first Arab to win a Nobel in any of the sciences, and he championed science in Egypt and the Middle East.

name: Pete Fountain
profession: Clarinetist Popularized Spirited New Orleans Jazz
headline: Pete Fountain, 86, Dies; Clarinetist Popularized Spirited New Orleans Jazz
abstract: Mr. Fountain brought the traditional jazz of his native New Orleans to a national audience through frequent appearances on the Lawrence Welk and Johnny Carson television shows.

name: Ivo Pitanguy
profession: Plastic Surgeon to the Stars and a Celebrity Himself
headline: Ivo Pitanguy, Plastic Surgeon to the Stars and a Celebrity Himself, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Pitanguy established himself in Brazil as one of the world’s most famous plastic surgeons, as much through his marketing savvy as through his surgical skills.

name: Elliot Tiber
profession: With a Permit Brought Forth Woodstock
headline: Elliot Tiber, Who With a Permit Brought Forth Woodstock, Dies at 81
abstract: As the head of a Chamber of Commerce, Mr. Tiber, an unlikely counterculture hero, offered a home for the music festival. He wrote two memoirs.

name: Jesse Owens
headline: Not Forgotten: Jesse Owens’s Chilly Reception in Nazi Germany, Then Olympic Glory
abstract: Owens faced a moral tug of war and ultimately decided to participate in the 1936 Games in Hitler’s Berlin. He won four gold medals.

name: Edward Daly
profession: Peace-Seeking Bishop in Northern Irelands Troubles
headline: Edward Daly, Peace-Seeking Bishop in Northern Ireland’s ‘Troubles,’ Dies at 82
abstract: As a priest and later as bishop, he argued relentlessly for peace during the three decades of sectarian violence.

name: Johnny Nicholson
profession: Midtown Cafe Drew the New Bohemians
headline: Johnny Nicholson, Whose Midtown Cafe Drew the ‘New Bohemians,’ Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Nicholson, with the chef Edna Lewis, served Southern cuisine in Manhattan to the likes of Frank Sinatra, Gore Vidal and Tennessee Williams.

name: Bryan Clauson
headline: Bryan Clauson, Champion Sprint Car Racer, Dies at 27 After Crash
abstract: Clauson, who unlike other drivers did not specialize in one style of car, was a four-time United States Auto Club champion and raced in the Indianapolis 500 three times.

name: Robert Kiley
headline: Robert Kiley, Mass Transit Chief in Boston, London and New York, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Kiley, a former C.I.A. agent, oversaw the revival of long-neglected subway and bus lines carrying millions of commuters. In New York he introduced the MetroCard.

name: Fred Schwartz
headline: Fred Schwartz, 84, Furrier, Philanthropist and Television Pitchman, Dies
abstract: Mr. Schwartz starred as Fred the Furrier in commercials in the 1970s and ’80s for the Fur Vault, retail outlets that offered mink coats at relatively modest prices.

name: Seena Hamilton
headline: Seena Hamilton, a Pioneer in Youth Tennis, Is Dead at 92
abstract: A relentless publicist and marketer for junior tennis, she started the Easter Bowl, which became perhaps the nation’s pre-eminent tennis event for junior players.

name: John Saunders
headline: John Saunders, a Measured Voice at ESPN, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Saunders, who had been with ESPN since 1986, was a familiar presence on fall Saturdays as the host of ABC’s studio coverage of college football and ESPN’s “College Football Live.”

name: Bernard Farrelly
headline: Bernard Farrelly, Surfing’s First World Champion, Dies at 71
abstract: As one of the top surfers of the 1960s, Farrelly was a pop-culture figure in his native Australia, but he could be an outsider in the surfing world.

name: Patrice Munsel
profession: Soprano Became a Star at the Met as a Teenager
headline: Patrice Munsel Dies at 91; Soprano Became a Star at the Met as a Teenager
abstract: Ms. Munsel was 17 when, in 1943, she won a Metropolitan Opera contract after tying for first place in the Metropolitan Auditions of the Air. She later sang on TV and in musical theater.

name: Hanif Mohammad
headline: Hanif Mohammad, Pakistani Cricket’s Little Master, Dies at 81
abstract: Mohammad’s technique was founded on durability, and his approach reached its peak in 1958 in a 16-hour turn at the crease, the longest innings in Test cricket’s history.

name: Gordon T. Danby
headline: Gordon T. Danby, Who Helped Invent Magnetic-Levitation Trains, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Danby invented the trains with a colleague, James R. Powell, then spent decades in largely futile efforts to get them built.

name: Frank Palopoli
headline: Frank Palopoli, Who Aided Fertility With Clomid Drug, Dies at 94
abstract: Millions of women have become pregnant because of the drug Mr. Palopoli and his team of researchers developed in the 1950s.

name: John Vaccaro
profession: Playhouse of the Ridiculous Gave Anarchy a Stage
headline: John Vaccaro, Whose Playhouse of the Ridiculous Gave Anarchy a Stage, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Vaccaro created so-called ridiculous works that sought to reveal the uncensored chaos that exists in people’s minds.

name: Glenn Yarbrough
headline: Glenn Yarbrough, Folk Singer With the Limeliters, Dies at 86
abstract: The trio met with runaway success during the 1960s folk revival. But, restless, Mr. Yarbrough quit, became a solo performer and later took to a life at sea.

name: Louis Herman
headline: Louis Herman, Who Talked With Dolphins, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Herman led his field of research in demonstrating dolphins’ ability to understand language, and taught two dozen words to two bottlenose dolphins.

name: Thomas Steinbeck
profession: Novelist and Son of John Steinbeck
headline: Thomas Steinbeck, Novelist and Son of John Steinbeck, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Steinbeck, the author of a short-story collection and two novels, drew attention for a legal battle for rights to his father’s literary output.

name: Susan M. Baer
headline: Susan M. Baer, Transportation Pioneer Who Ran New York’s Airports, Dies at 65
abstract: Ms. Baer, a longtime official for the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, also was the first woman named as its aviation director and the first woman to run the Lincoln Tunnel.

name: Philip Bialowitz
profession: Escaped a Nazi Death Camp and Testified in Court
headline: Philip Bialowitz, Who Escaped a Nazi Death Camp and Testified in Court, Dies at 90
abstract: Believed to be the last Polish Jew to survive the Sobibor extermination camp, Mr. Bialowitz wrote a memoir about his escape in a prisoner uprising.

name: Fyvush Finkel
headline: Fyvush Finkel, Pillar of Yiddish Theater Who Crossed Into TV, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Finkel won an Emmy for his portrayal of a cantankerous lawyer on the 1990s show “Picket Fences.”

name: Michel Richard
headline: Michel Richard, Acclaimed Chef at Citronelle, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Richard, a pastry chef by training, brought a playful, French twist to his food, and headed some of the United States’ most beloved restaurants.

name: Choo Choo Coleman
headline: Choo Choo Coleman, a Catcher With the Original, Woeful Mets, Dies
abstract: Mr. Coleman had a brief big league career but he had the good (or ill) fortune of playing for the Mets in their history-making first two seasons.

name: Gerald Grosvenor
headline: Gerald Grosvenor, British Duke and Billionaire, Dies at 64
abstract: The sixth Duke of Westminster was the country’s richest landowner, worth an estimated $12 billion, and a friend of the royal family.

name: Bobby Hutcherson
profession: Vibraphonist With Coloristic Range of Sound
headline: Bobby Hutcherson, Vibraphonist With Coloristic Range of Sound, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Hutcherson was one of the first jazz musicians to adapt his instrument to a freer postbop language, often playing chords with a pair of mallets in each hand.

name: Babe Ruth
headline: Not Forgotten: Babe Ruth, the Slugger Who Went From Boyhood Chaos to Baseball Stardom
abstract: Before Babe Ruth tantalized fans with hundreds of home runs he had to survive a tough childhood in an orphanage.

name: João Havelange
profession: Built and Ruled World Soccer With Firm Hand
headline: João Havelange, Who Built and Ruled World Soccer With Firm Hand, Dies at 100
abstract: As the head of FIFA for 24 years, the Brazilian businessman built soccer into a multibillion-dollar powerhouse. He was also implicated in a lucrative kickback scandal.

name: John McLaughlin
headline: John McLaughlin, TV Host Who Made Combat of Punditry, Dies at 89
abstract: A Jesuit priest who served in the Nixon White House, he turned to a new vocation that brought a sharp edge to the Sunday morning political talk show.

name: John F. Timoney
headline: John F. Timoney, Police Official Who Pushed Innovative Tactics to Curb Crime, Dies at 68
abstract: In New York, Philadelphia and Miami, Mr. Timoney plotted innovative strategies that reversed years of skyrocketing crime.

name: Arthur Hiller
profession: Love Story Director and Box-Office Magnet
headline: Arthur Hiller, ‘Love Story’ Director and Box-Office Magnet, Dies at 92
abstract: For a time he was one of Hollywood’s most commercially successful directors, piloting nearly 70 feature films, television movies and series episodes.

name: Ernst Neizvestny
headline: Ernst Neizvestny, a Russian Sculptor Who Clashed With Khrushchev, Dies at 91
abstract: Though his ventures into modernism put him at odds with Soviet cultural authorities in the post-Stalin era, the artist later created a monument for Khrushchev’s grave.

name: Harry Briggs Jr.
profession: Catalyst for Brown v. Board of Education
headline: Harry Briggs Jr., a Catalyst for Brown v. Board of Education, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Briggs’s parents originated the lawsuit that struck down public school segregation in 1954, though his name became a forgotten legal footnote.

name: Thomas Cholmondeley
profession: Scion Implicated in Killings of 2 Kenyans
headline: Thomas Cholmondeley, Scion Implicated in Killings of 2 Kenyans, Dies at 48
abstract: A descendant of British settlers, Mr. Cholmondeley was known as an eccentric outdoorsman who liked fast horses, speedy bikes and guns. He had been hospitalized for hip-replacement surgery.

name: John W. Vessey Jr.
headline: John W. Vessey Jr., Who Was Chairman of Joint Chiefs, Dies at 94
abstract: General Vessey was regarded as a leader of proven courage and integrity who inspired confidence, and he was also an old-fashioned patriot.

name: Ernst Nolte
headline: Ernst Nolte, Historian Whose Views on Hitler Caused an Uproar, Dies at 93
abstract: Professor Nolte, a respected German scholar of fascism, suggested in a 1986 essay that Nazism had been a logical response to the “existential threat” of the Russian Revolution.

name: Ronald DeLuca
headline: Ronald DeLuca, Ad Man Who Helped Revive Iacocca’s Chrysler, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. DeLuca was an ad man who had a crucial part in persuading Congress to approve a $1.5 billion federal loan guarantee package for the automaker in 1980.

name: Pramukh Swami Maharaj
profession: Hindu Sect Became Largest in U.S
headline: Pramukh Swami Maharaj, Whose Hindu Sect Became Largest in U.S., Dies at 94
abstract: He established more than a thousand temples around the world for BAPS, the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha sect.

name: D.A. Henderson
headline: D.A. Henderson, Doctor Who Helped End Smallpox Scourge, Dies at 87
abstract: Starting in 1966, Dr. Henderson, known as D.A., led the World Health Organization’s war on the smallpox virus, and achieved success astonishingly quickly.

name: Connie Crothers
headline: Connie Crothers, Jazz Pianist, Composer and Instructor, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Crothers, an acolyte of Lennie Tristano who maintained equal allegiance to the avant-garde and jazz tradition, recorded more than two dozen albums.

name: Toots Thielemans
profession: Won Jazz Renown With the Harmonica
headline: Toots Thielemans, Who Won Jazz Renown With the Harmonica, Dies at 94
abstract: The Belgian-American also developed a signature style by playing a guitar and whistling in unison, and his music has been part of the “Sesame Street” theme song.

name: Lou Pearlman
profession: Svengali Behind Backstreet Boys and NSync
headline: Lou Pearlman, Svengali Behind Backstreet Boys and ’NSync, Dies at 62
abstract: The music producer helped pioneer the boy-band phenomenon before he was convicted of running a $300 million Ponzi scheme and sentenced to 25 years in federal prison.

name: Dick Assman
headline: Dick Assman, Briefly a ‘Late Show’ Celebrity, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Assman, a Saskatchewan gas station owner made famous by David Letterman, soon saw his name on T-shirts and bumper stickers. It was always about the name.

name: Irving Fields
headline: Irving Fields, Composer Who Infused Songs With Latin Rhythms, Dies at 101
abstract: The composer of “Miami Beach Rhumba” and other hits spent the last decades of his life as a New York City lounge pianist.

name: Joyce Carol Thomas
headline: Joyce Carol Thomas, Who Wrote of African-American Life, Dies at 78
abstract: The award-winning children’s author portrayed complexities seldom seen in books created for young readers.

name: Doris Bohrer
profession: World War II Spy for Allies
headline: Doris Bohrer, World War II Spy for Allies, Dies at 93
abstract: She helped plan the Allied invasion of Sicily and traced the movement of German trains transporting prisoners to concentration camps.

name: George Curry
profession: Journalist With a Mission to Serve Black Readers
headline: George Curry, Journalist With a Mission to Serve Black Readers, Dies at 69
abstract: As editor in chief of Emerge, Mr. Curry shifted the emphasis from entertainment to news and came up with a motto: “Black America’s Newsmagazine.”

name: Steven Hill
profession: Starred on Law & Order and Mission: Impossible
headline: Steven Hill, Who Starred on ‘Law & Order’ and ‘Mission: Impossible,’ Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Hill appeared in feature films and originated imposing lead roles on television series in the 1960s and in the 1990s.

name: Nina Ponomareva
headline: Nina Ponomareva, Soviet Olympian Who Set Off a Diplomatic Crisis, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Ponomareva led a strong women’s discus contingent in the 1952 Helsinki Games, but years later she caused a stir when she shoplifted five hats in a London store.

name: Walter Scheel
profession: Leading Figure in West German Thaw With the East
headline: Walter Scheel, Leading Figure in West German Thaw With the East, Dies at 97
abstract: As foreign minister and deputy chancellor under Willy Brandt, Mr. Scheel fostered closer ties with Communist East Germany.

name: Morton Schindel
profession: Turned Childrens Books Into Animated Films
headline: Morton Schindel, Who Turned Children’s Books Into Animated Films, Dies at 98
abstract: Inspired by a trip to the children’s room of the New York Public Library, the filmmaker sought to preserve the books’ lush illustrations when animating them.

name: Sonia Rykiel
headline: Sonia Rykiel, Fashion Designer for the ‘Fragile, but Strong,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Based in Paris, she made fashions for women, like herself, who were proud of their pregnancies, sophisticated about sex and too busy to fuss over the latest fads.

name: Warren Hinckle
headline: Warren Hinckle, 77, Ramparts Editor Who Embraced Gonzo Journalism, Dies
abstract: Mr. Hinckle, the flamboyant editor who made Ramparts magazine a voice for the radical left, championed the work of Hunter S. Thompson.

name: Jay Fishman
profession: Led Travelers Safely Through the Financial Crisis
headline: Jay Fishman, Who Led Travelers Safely Through the Financial Crisis, Dies at 63
abstract: He weathered the recession by investing Travelers’ insurance premiums in stable vehicles, like fixed-income securities.

name: Rudy Van Gelder
headline: Rudy Van Gelder, 91, Audio Engineer Who Helped Define Jazz Sound on Records, Dies
abstract: The many albums he engineered for Blue Note and other labels in the 1950s and ’60s included acknowledged classics like Coltrane’s “A Love Supreme” and Miles Davis’s “Walkin.’”

name: Friedrich Nietzsche
headline: Not Forgotten: Friedrich Nietzsche, a Renegade Philosopher Whose Ideas Endured
abstract: Friedrich Nietzsche, a singular philosopher with the style of a romantic poet, influenced the past century in ways he could never have imagined and might not have countenanced.

name: Esther Jungreis
headline: Esther Jungreis, ‘the Jewish Billy Graham,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Jungreis, who founded the outreach organization Hineni, staged rallies with theatrical lighting and musical accompaniment at which she urged secular Jews to embrace their faith.

name: Max Ritvo
headline: Max Ritvo, Poet Who Chronicled His Cancer Fight, Dies at 25
abstract: The writer talked about his work and illness on radio, and had his poetry published in The New Yorker and elsewhere.

name: John Ellenby
headline: John Ellenby, Visionary Who Helped Create Early Laptop, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Ellenby founded Grid Systems, where the Compass was produced. It went on to become a tool for big corporations, government spies, White House officials and astronauts.

name: Jane Thompson
headline: Jane Thompson, Designer Who Helped Transform Waterfronts, Dies at 89
abstract: She joined her husband, Benjamin C. Thompson, in planning festival marketplaces including Faneuil Hall, the South Street Seaport, and Harborplace in Baltimore.

name: Josephine Del Deo
profession: Fought to Preserve Cape Cod Shoreline
headline: Josephine Del Deo, Who Fought to Preserve Cape Cod Shoreline, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Del Deo, a bohemian writer nicknamed the Muse of True History, helped ensure that Provincetown, Mass., would continue to appear much as it did in the days of Thoreau.

name: Jeremiah O’Keefe
profession: Ace in His First World War II Battle
headline: Jeremiah O’Keefe, Ace in His First World War II Battle, Dies at 93
abstract: In his first aerial battle, Mr. O’Keefe downed five Japanese planes over Okinawa; he later entered Mississippi politics as a staunch opponent of segregation.

name: Emmett Till
profession: Martyrdom Launched the Civil Rights Movement
headline: Not Forgotten: Emmett Till, Whose Martyrdom Launched the Civil Rights Movement
abstract: Emmett Till was just 14 when he was murdered for allegedly whistling at a white woman. Outrage at his death and the acquittal of his killers helped spark the civil rights movement.

name: Juan Gabriel
headline: Juan Gabriel, a Pop Music ‘Icon’ in Mexico, Dies at 66
abstract: A prolific singer and songwriter, he was nominated for six Grammys and received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

name: Gene Wilder
profession: Star of Willy Wonka and Young Frankenstein
headline: Gene Wilder Dies at 83; Star of ‘Willy Wonka’ and ‘Young Frankenstein’
abstract: Mr. Wilder’s neurotic comic persona added a special edge to numerous hits, including “Blazing Saddles” and “Stir Crazy.”

name: Daniel Z. Nelson
headline: Daniel Z. Nelson, Who Put Classrooms in High-Rises, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Nelson presided over the New York City Educational Construction Fund, a public benefit corporation that helped create classrooms in partnership with developers.

name: Antony Jay
profession: Machiavelli Scholar and a Creator of Yes Minister
headline: Antony Jay, a Machiavelli Scholar and a Creator of ‘Yes Minister,’ Dies at 86
abstract: A writer and producer who, drawing parallels between kings and business leaders, highlighted the machinations of government.

name: Harry Fujiwara
headline: Harry Fujiwara, Wrestling Villain Mr. Fuji, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Fuji, whose signature move was hurling a handful of salt into opponents’ eyes, won several tag-team titles with Professor Toru Tanaka.

name: Christopher McCandless
headline: Not Forgotten: Christopher McCandless, Whose Alaskan Odyssey Ended in Death
abstract: Christopher McCandless broke from his past and died of starvation in the Alaskan backcountry. Jon Krakauer wrote “Into the wild,” a best-selling book, about his life.

name: Jaime Davidovich
headline: Jaime Davidovich, Artist Whose Videos Bypassed the ‘Gatekeepers of Culture,’ Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Davidovich helped create “The Live! Show” on a Manhattan cable channel and later constructed temporary video theaters within museums and galleries.

name: James Cronin
profession: Explained Why Matter Survived the Big Bang
headline: James Cronin, Who Explained Why Matter Survived the Big Bang, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Cronin shared a Nobel Prize for discovering, with Val Fitch, “a fundamental asymmetry between matter and antimatter,” repudiating a basic principle of physics.

name: Marc Riboud
headline: Marc Riboud, Photojournalist Who Found Grace in the Turbulent, Dies at 93
abstract: A protégé of Henri Cartier-Bresson, Mr. Riboud routinely traveled to restive places throughout Asia and Africa in the 1950s and ’60s as part of his decades-long career.

name: Princess Diana
headline: Not Forgotten: Princess Diana, Who Was Beloved, Yet Troubled by Her Crown
abstract: Princess Diana, whose title and troubles made her a symbol of a nation’s emotional and generational conflicts, died on Aug. 31, 1997.

name: Vera Caslavska
headline: Vera Caslavska, Gymnast Who Faced Off With Soviets, Dies at 74
abstract: Caslavska won seven Olympics gold medals as a gymnast in the 1960s. Her public opposition to the Soviet invasion of her homeland, Czechoslovakia, ended her competitive career.

name: Joy Browne
headline: Dr. Joy Browne, Long-Running Psychologist of the Airwaves, Dies at 71
abstract: Dr. Browne, the syndicated radio and television therapist, dispensed advice, earnest inspiration and gentle goading for nearly four decades.

name: Joe Sutter
profession: Led an Army in Building Boeings Jumbo 747
headline: Joe Sutter, Who Led an Army in Building Boeing’s Jumbo 747, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Sutter headed a team of 4,500 engineers that in only 29 months designed and built the 747, a 20th-century answer to the luxury ocean liner.

name: Bill Etra
headline: Bill Etra, Inventor Who Helped Make Video an Art Form, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Etra and a colleague created the Rutt/Etra synthesizer, which let a user manipulate video more easily to make it a more expressive art form.

name: Nathan Lyons
profession: Influential Photographer and Advocate of the Art
headline: Nathan Lyons, Influential Photographer and Advocate of the Art, Dies at 86
abstract: Not only was Mr. Lyons known for his photographic work, he was an organizer who helped lay the foundations of contemporary photography as an art form.

name: Islam Karimov
headline: Islam Karimov Dies at 78, Ending a Long, Ruthless Rule of Uzbekistan
abstract: Mr. Karimov’s nearly three-decade reign was often described as one of the most brutal to emerge after the collapse of the Soviet Union.

name: Reinhard Selten
profession: Strides in Game Theory Led to a Nobel
headline: Reinhard Selten, Whose Strides in Game Theory Led to a Nobel, Dies at 85
abstract: Professor Selten shared the Nobel Prize with John C. Harsanyi and John F. Nash Jr. for their pioneering advances in strategic decision-making.

name: Fred Hellerman
profession: Last of the Weavers Folk Group
headline: Fred Hellerman, Last of the Weavers Folk Group, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Hellerman, a pillar of the quartet that helped build a folk music revival, also played on the debut albums of Joan Baez and Judy Collins and produced Arlo Guthrie’s first two albums.

name: Jon Polito
headline: Jon Polito, a Favorite in Coen Brothers Films, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Polito had more than 200 roles in film and television and appeared on Broadway as well.

name: Jerry Heller
headline: Jerry Heller, Music Manager Who Promoted N.W.A and Gangsta Rap, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Heller was a founder of Ruthless Records, which released N.W.A’s album “Straight Outta Compton” in 1988.

name: Roger Y. Tsien
profession: Nobel Winner for Use of Glowing Proteins
headline: Roger Y. Tsien, Nobel Winner for Use of Glowing Proteins, Dies at 64
abstract: The biochemist at the University of California, San Diego, transformed a green fluorescent protein from jellyfish into a ubiquitous biological tool.

name: Michel Butor
headline: Michel Butor, French Novelist Who Shattered Conventions, Dies at 89
abstract: His experiments with narrative and structure in the late 1950s and early ’60s put him at the forefront of the literary trend known as le nouveau roman.

name: Hugh O
profession: Dashing TV Star of Wyatt Earp Was 91
headline: Hugh O’Brian Dies; Dashing TV Star of ‘Wyatt Earp’ Was 91
abstract: Mr. O’Brian played the title role in the western “The Life and Legend of Wyatt Earp” from 1955 to 1961.

name: Namon Hoggle
profession: Accused in a Civil Rights Killing
headline: Namon Hoggle, 81, Accused in a Civil Rights Killing, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Hoggle was the last surviving defendant in the fatal beating of James J. Reeb, a white minister who had marched with civil rights advocates, in Selma, Ala., in 1965.

name: Phyllis Schlafly
profession: First Lady of a Political March to the Right
headline: Phyllis Schlafly, ‘First Lady’ of a Political March to the Right, Dies at 92
abstract: Angered by the cultural transformations of the 1960s, Mrs. Schlafly led grass-roots campaigns against Communism, abortion and the Equal Rights Amendment.

name: Leslie H. Martinson
profession: Director of Prime-Time TV for Four Decades
headline: Leslie H. Martinson, Director of Prime-Time TV for Four Decades, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Martinson’s long list of credits is a veritable capsule history of prime-time television through the postwar decades and beyond.

name: Richard Neville
headline: Richard Neville, 74, a Founder of ’60s Counterculture Magazine Oz, Dies
abstract: The Australian iconoclast, who stood trial for obscenity, challenged mores and societal taboos with magazines in his country and in Britain.

name: Vertamae Smart-Grosvenor
headline: Vertamae Smart-Grosvenor Dies at 79; Celebrated Gullah Food and Culture
abstract: A South Carolina native, who liked to call herself a “culinary griot,” she was heard on NPR for three decades. She also was an author, an actress and a singer.

name: Anna Dewdney
profession: Author of Llama Llama Books Was 50
headline: Anna Dewdney Dies; Author of ‘Llama Llama’ Books Was 50
abstract: Ms. Dewdney’s hugely successful picture-book series was inspired by car rides, passing farms, with her own young daughters.

name: Philip Kingsley
headline: Philip Kingsley, Who Dispensed Hair-Care Products and Expertise, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Kingsley, who owned clinics in London and Manhattan, counted celebrities among his clients and wrote books about hair and scalp health.

name: Johan Botha
headline: Johan Botha, Operatic Tenor in Difficult Roles, Dies at 51
abstract: Mr. Botha, who was born in South Africa, performed for decades in daunting parts by Wagner, Strauss and Verdi.

name: Chablis
profession: Sassy Eccentric in Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil
headline: The Lady Chablis, Sassy Eccentric in ‘Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil,’ Dies at 59
abstract: Ms. Chablis was a standout character in the book and movie that introduced the world to Savannah, Ga., and the sometimes unconventional people who live there.

name: Isabelle Dinoire
profession: Recipient of First Partial Facial Transplant
headline: Isabelle Dinoire, Recipient of First Partial Facial Transplant, Dies at 49
abstract: Her 2005 operation paved the way for dozens of other patients to receive this complicated surgery.

name: Sam Iacobellis
profession: B-1 Bomber Recast the Cold War
headline: Sam Iacobellis, Whose B-1 Bomber Recast the Cold War, Dies at 87
abstract: His development and lightning delivery of 100 stealth bombers to President Reagan in the 1980s was credited with speeding the Soviet Union’s collapse.

name: John R. Coleman
headline: John R. Coleman, Haverford President Who Explored Blue-Collar Life, Dies at 95
abstract: A labor economist, he was a strong voice at the Philadelphia-area college in the 1960s for the admission of women and against the Vietnam War.

name: John S. Coleman
headline: John S. Coleman, Weather Channel Co-Founder, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Coleman was the original meteorologist on “Good Morning America” and pioneered green-screen news and round-the-clock weather reporting.

name: Nora York
headline: Nora York, Singer Who Fused Forms, Dies at 60
abstract: A performance artist as well, Ms. York layered philosophy, poetry, politics and song when she appeared before an audience.

name: Daniel H. Cohen
headline: Daniel H. Cohen, Former Times Executive Who Led Advertising Growth, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Cohen, a great-grandson of Adolph Ochs, who bought The Times in 1896, was an executive in circulation and advertising before he left the company in 1999.

name: Daniel Cohen
profession: Sought Justice for Pan Am Bombing Victims
headline: Daniel Cohen, 82, Dies; Sought Justice for Pan Am Bombing Victims
abstract: Mr. Cohen and his wife, Susan, lost their daughter over Scotland when terrorists attacked Flight 103 in 1988. The couple became voices of the bereaved.

name: Norbert Schemansky
profession: Won Weight-Lifting Gold but Little Applause Back Home
headline: Norbert Schemansky, Who Won Weight-Lifting Gold but Little Applause Back Home, Dies at 92
abstract: In competition largely outside the sports world spotlight, he awed crowds and was the first to win medals in four Olympics but felt unappreciated in his hometown.

name: Jonathan Rinehart
headline: Jonathan Rinehart, Founder of Public Relations Firm, Dies at 86
abstract: His firm helped develop the specialty of handling communications about corporate mergers and acquisitions.

name: Bobby Chacon
headline: Bobby Chacon, Boxing Champion Hounded by Misfortune, Dies at 64
abstract: Chacon earned the first of two world titles less than two years into his career in 1974. As debilitating drug use and family tragedy took their toll, he refused to quit.

name: Greta Friedman
profession: Claimed to Be Nurse in V-J Day Photo
headline: Greta Friedman, Who Claimed to Be Nurse in V-J Day Photo, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Friedman was one of several women who said they were photographed kissing a sailor in Times Square at the end of World War II.

name: Buster
headline: Prince Buster, Trailblazer of Ska, Dies at 78
abstract: The performer and producer transformed Jamaican music in the 1960s, generating hundreds of songs with an emphasis on the backbeat.

name: Cary Blanchard
headline: Cary Blanchard, Journeyman Kicker Who Delivered in the Clutch, Dies at 47
abstract: Blanchard’s career was not particularly stable, taking him to several N.F.L. teams, but he often had a decisive impact on key games and made a Pro Bowl as a Colt.

name: Eddie Antar
headline: Eddie Antar, Retailer and Felon Who Created Crazy Eddie, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Antar expanded his business from a single Brooklyn store, founded in 1969, into the largest consumer electronics chain in the New York metropolitan area.

name: Albert Kumin
profession: Pastry Chef for Carter White House and Top New York Restaurants
headline: Albert Kumin, Pastry Chef for Carter White House and Top New York Restaurants, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Kumin’s dessert creations included the signature chocolate velvet cake at the Four Seasons and a lemon cream tart at Windows on the World atop the World Trade Center.

name: Jutta Limbach
profession: First Woman to Lead Germanys Highest Court
headline: Jutta Limbach, First Woman to Lead Germany’s Highest Court, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Limbach, who was 11 when World War II ended, also led a commission to mediate disputes about the restitution of art seized by the Nazis.

name: Robert Timberg
headline: Robert Timberg, Who Chronicled the Scars of Vietnam, Dies at 76
abstract: A Marine combat veteran who became an author and journalist, he is known for the books “The Nightingale’s Song” and “Blue-Eyed Boy.”

name: Stanley K. Sheinbaum
headline: Stanley K. Sheinbaum, Economist and Liberal Crusader, Dies at 96
abstract: Among other efforts abroad, Mr. Sheinbaum led a delegation of American Jewish leaders in 1988 to persuade the Palestinian leader, Yasir Arafat, to recognize Israel.

name: Jack Hofsiss
profession: Stage Director of The Elephant Man
headline: Jack Hofsiss, Stage Director of ‘The Elephant Man,’ Dies at 65
abstract: After becoming the youngest director to win a Tony, at 28, he went on to direct films and other plays, even after being paralyzed in an accident.

name: Julio Gonzalez
headline: Julio Gonzalez, Arsonist Who Killed 87 at New York Club in ’90, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Gonzalez was sentenced to 87 concurrent terms of 25 years for starting the fire, which prompted the city to renew its scrutiny of safety measures at nightclubs.

name: Frank J. Barbaro
headline: Frank J. Barbaro, Liberal New York Lawmaker, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Barbaro, who won election 12 times as a legislator, challenged Edward I. Koch for re-election to a second term as mayor of New York in 1981.

name: Rose Mofford
profession: First Woman to Serve as Arizonas Governor
headline: Rose Mofford, First Woman to Serve as Arizona’s Governor, Dies at 94
abstract: A Democrat in a historically Republican state, Ms. Mofford was governor from 1988 to 1991, culminating 50 years in state government.

name: Edward Albee
headline: Edward Albee, Trenchant Playwright Who Laid Bare Modern Life, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Albee, the Pulitzer-winning playwright of “Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf?” and “Three Tall Women,” among other dramas, charted the contentiousness of intimacy and the gap between self-delusion and truth in contemporary life.

name: Don Buchla
headline: Don Buchla, Inventor, Composer and Electronic Music Maverick, Dies at 79
abstract: The instruments Mr. Buchla built represented what became known as the West Coast philosophy of electronic music: more experimental and less commercial.

name: Howard E. Butt Jr.
headline: Howard E. Butt Jr., Grocery Empire Heir Who Spread a Gospel, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Butt left the day-to-day operation of a business to focus on Christian outreach, philanthropy and a message of marrying spiritual and professional lives.

name: Duane Graveline
headline: Duane Graveline, Doctor Who Was Forced Out as an Astronaut, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Graveline resigned after two months because he was getting divorced and NASA was worried about its image; his later career as a doctor was marred by scandal.

name: W.P. Kinsella
headline: W.P. Kinsella, Author of ‘Shoeless Joe,’ Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Kinsella’s award-winning novel was the inspiration for the 1989 movie “Field of Dreams,” starring Ray Liotta, James Earl Jones and Kevin Costner.

name: James Stacy
headline: James Stacy, Actor Who Kept Working After a Disabling Crash, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Stacy played specialized roles after losing an arm and a leg when his motorcycle was struck by a drunken driver.

name: Michel C. Bergerac
headline: Michel C. Bergerac, Who Made Over Revlon, Dies at 84
abstract: The French-born deal maker expanded Revlon beyond cosmetics, transforming it into a major player in health care before a hostile takeover by Ronald O. Perelman.

name: Dorothy Cann Hamilton
headline: Dorothy Cann Hamilton, Founder of French Culinary Institute, Dies in Crash at 67
abstract: Ms. Hamilton, a big influence on New York chefs, was driving in Nova Scotia, where she had a home.

name: D. Keith Mano
headline: D. Keith Mano, Novelist Who Tackled Christianity, Sex and More, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Mano wrote a stack of books, a National Review column and numerous articles in Playboy, Esquire and other magazines.

name: Allister Sparks
headline: Allister Sparks, South African Journalist Who Challenged Apartheid, Dies at 83
abstract: As the editor of The Rand Daily Mail, Mr. Sparks exposed a covert government propaganda campaign that led South Africa’s president to resign.

name: Rose Pak
profession: Brash Force for San Franciscos Chinatown
headline: Rose Pak, a Brash Force for San Francisco’s Chinatown, Dies at 68
abstract: Although she never held office, Ms. Pak helped turn her city’s Asian-American population into a substantial political power through outspoken style.

name: Curtis Hanson
profession: Director of Wicked Noir L.A. Confidential
headline: Curtis Hanson, Director of Wicked Noir ‘L.A. Confidential,’ Dies at 71
abstract: The director’s 1997 adaptation of a tough James Ellroy novel earned him an Academy Award, and introduced American moviegoers to Russell Crowe.

name: Deborah S. Jin
profession: Physicist Studied Matter in Extreme Cold
headline: Deborah S. Jin Dies at 47; Physicist Studied Matter in Extreme Cold
abstract: A MacArthur fellow and the second-youngest woman ever elected to the National Academy of Sciences.

name: Victor Scheinman
headline: Victor Scheinman, Assembly Line Robot Inventor, Dies at 73
abstract: The Scheinman Stanford Arm, developed in 1969, was adapted by manufacturers to become the leading robot in assembling and spot-welding products.

name: Teodoro González de León
headline: Teodoro González de León, Evocative Mexican Architect, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. González de León, in various settings, reimagined the tenets of Modernism in a Mexican context.

name: John D. Loudermilk
profession: Wrote Tobacco Road and Indian Reservation
headline: John D. Loudermilk, Who Wrote ‘Tobacco Road’ and ‘Indian Reservation,’ Dies at 82
abstract: The country singer and songwriter wrote dozens of hits in the 1960s and ’70s, performed by artists including Eddie Cochran and Paul Revere and the Raiders.

name: Ed Temple
headline: Ed Temple, Track Coach Who Produced Olympians and National Titles, Dies at 89
abstract: Temple, who coached at Tennessee State University from 1950 to 1993, mentored female runners who won 23 Olympic medals and 34 national titles.

name: Karl Dietrich Bracher
headline: Karl Dietrich Bracher, German Historian of Nazi Era, Dies at 94
abstract: Professor Bracher, who was born in 1922, refused to absolve his own generation of complicity in the horrors of Nazism.

name: Jack Garman
headline: Jack Garman, Whose Judgment Call Saved Moon Landing, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Garman was at a back-room console on July 20, 1969, when Neil Armstrong told mission control of a possible computer systems overload. “As long as it doesn’t reoccur, it’s fine,” Mr. Garman said.

name: Bobby Breen
headline: Bobby Breen, a Child Star Who Hit a High Note in the 1930s, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Breen arrived on the scene as an 8-year-old boy with an angelic face, and was described as “the most alarming vocal phenomenon of the day.”

name: Stanley Dural Jr.
headline: Stanley Dural Jr., Founder of Buckwheat Zydeco, Dies at 68
abstract: Founded in 1979, Buckwheat Zydeco mixed Louisiana Creole traditions with R&B and rock to become one of the world’s great party bands.

name: Richard P. Cooley
headline: Richard P. Cooley, Former Wells Fargo C.E.O., Dies at 92
abstract: For decades, Mr. Cooley was a prominent figure in West Coast banking, helping to turn Wells Fargo into a major regional bank.

name: Arnold Palmer
profession: Magnetic Face of Golf in the 60s
headline: Arnold Palmer, the Magnetic Face of Golf in the ’60s, Dies at 87
abstract: Palmer, who won seven major titles, captivated fans with his ferocious swing and fearless attitude, helping to inspire an American golf boom.

name: Jean Shepard
profession: Female Country Voice With Muscle and Ambition
headline: Jean Shepard, a Female Country Voice With Muscle and Ambition, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Shepard, also an expert yodeler, joined the Grand Ole Opry in 1955.

name: Charles L. Schultze
headline: Charles L. Schultze, 91, Dies; Advised Presidents on Economic Policy
abstract: Mr. Schultze spent most of his career working on national economic and fiscal policy, as a government economic adviser, university professor and research fellow.

name: Peter L. Gerety
headline: Peter L. Gerety, Oldest Archbishop Who Preached Social Justice, Dies at 104
abstract: Archbishop Gerety, who led the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Newark, preached for social justice and sought to give voice to women, the laity and lapsed churchgoers.

name: Herschell Gordon Lewis
headline: Herschell Gordon Lewis, a Pioneer of Gore Cinema, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Lewis set the bar for low-budget horror in movies like “Blood Feast” that went on to inspire filmmakers like Wes Craven and Quentin Tarantino.

name: Max Mannheimer
headline: Max Mannheimer, a Keeper of Holocaust Memory, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Mannheimer visited hundreds of schools and other institutions, advocating democracy and helping ensure that Germany’s World War II horrors were never repeated.

name: Shimon Peres
profession: Enduring Pillar From Israels Founding Era
headline: Shimon Peres, an Enduring Pillar From Israel’s Founding Era, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Peres helped build up his country’s military might, then worked as hard to establish peace with Israel’s Arab neighbors.

name: Joe Browder
headline: Joe Browder, a Guardian of the Florida Everglades, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Browder put together an eclectic bloc that prevented the construction of a jetport near Everglades National Park that would have been the world’s largest.

name: Agnes Nixon
profession: Infused Her Soap Operas With Social Relevance
headline: Agnes Nixon, Who Infused Her Soap Operas With Social Relevance, Dies at 93
abstract: Her “All My Children” and “One Life to Live” tackled drug addiction, abortion, child abuse and AIDS along with the usual soap tales of infidelity.

name: Ronald P. Stanton
headline: Ronald P. Stanton, Trammo Founder Who Shared His Fortune, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Stanton, who escaped from Nazi Germany with his mother when he was 9, made his money in petrochemicals and gave more than $300 million of it away.

name: Joseph Harmatz
profession: Led Jewish Plot to Kill Germans After World War II
headline: Joseph Harmatz, Who Led Jewish Plot to Kill Germans After World War II, Dies at 91
abstract: Harmatz, a survivor of the Vilnius ghetto in Lithuania, was the leader of a group that poisoned 2,200 imprisoned Germans by lacing their bread with arsenic.

name: Mary Weber Novak
headline: Mary Weber Novak, Top California Vintner, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Novak took over Spottswoode, her family’s vineyard, and turned it into a top producer of cabernet sauvignon and sauvignon blanc.

name: Richard D. Trentlage
profession: Wrote The Oscar Mayer Wiener Song
headline: Richard D. Trentlage, 87, Who Wrote ‘The Oscar Mayer Wiener Song,’ Dies
abstract: Mr. Trentlage’s may not be a household name, but generations know his work writing advertising jingles for companies such as Oscar Mayer and McDonald’s.

name: Curtis Roosevelt
profession: White House Charmer as a Child
headline: Curtis Roosevelt, a White House Charmer as a Child, Dies at 86
abstract: He and his sister were well known to Americans when they lived with their mother and grandparents in the White House in the 1930s.

name: Shirley Jaffe
headline: Shirley Jaffe, Geometric Artist of Joyful Forms, Dies at 92
abstract: An American who settled in Paris, Ms. Jaffe moved from Abstract Expressionism to a style rich in color and energy, finding a new audience in the 1990s.

name: Suzanne Mitchell
profession: Made Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders a Global Brand
headline: Suzanne Mitchell, 73, Dies; Made Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders a Global Brand
abstract: Working for Tex Schramm in the 1970s, Ms. Mitchell replaced a squad of high school bobby-soxers with a scantily clad chorus line.

name: David Budbill
headline: David Budbill, a Poet of Small-Town Vermont, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Budbill’s fictional creation Judevine, Vt., raised some hackles locally.

name: Oscar Brand
headline: Oscar Brand, Folk Singer Whose Radio Show Twanged for Decades, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Brand wrote books and scores for musicals and films, but was best known for WNYC’s “Folksong Festival,” the longest-running radio show in history with a single host.

name: Carroll Wainwright Jr.
headline: Carroll Wainwright Jr., ‘Silk-Stockinged Stowaway,’ Dies at 90
abstract: An 8-year-old Mr. Wainwright, a scion of one of the wealthiest families in the United States, made headlines after he sneaked aboard a ship from Bermuda to New York.

name: Kashif
headline: Kashif, R&B Singer, Songwriter and Producer, Dies at 59
abstract: A deft experimentalist, Kashif was in the stylistic vanguard of R&B in the 1980s and played a key role in the creation of Whitney Houston’s earliest recordings.

name: Neville Marriner
headline: Neville Marriner, Prolific Musician and Acclaimed Conductor, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Marriner, who established the Academy of St. Martin in the Fields, was honored three times for his service to music in Britain.

name: Gloria Naylor
profession: Honored Novel Was Set in a Housing Project
headline: Gloria Naylor, Whose Honored Novel Was Set in a Housing Project, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Naylor’s “The Women of Brewster Place” won a National Book Award and was adapted for a mini-series.

name: Gordon Davidson
profession: Artistic Director of Mark Taper Forum
headline: Gordon Davidson, Artistic Director of Mark Taper Forum, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Davidson helped establish Los Angeles as a West Coast capital of regional theater.

name: Trinh Thi Ngo
profession: Broadcaster Called Hanoi Hannah in Vietnam War
headline: Trinh Thi Ngo, Broadcaster Called ‘Hanoi Hannah’ in Vietnam War, Dies
abstract: The soft-spoken radio announcer both entertained and reproached American forces.

name: Joseph Verner Reed Jr.
profession: Envoy Became White House Chief of Protocol
headline: Joseph Verner Reed Jr., 78, Dies; Envoy Became White House Chief of Protocol
abstract: While under President George Bush, Mr. Reed was part of ‘the talking hat’ affair, a slip-up that entered the annals of diplomatic history.

name: Jack Kirrane
profession: Captain of U.S. Gold Medal Hockey Team in 1960
headline: Jack Kirrane, Captain of U.S. Gold Medal Hockey Team in 1960, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Kirrane also played on the 1948 American Olympic team, which did not win a medal, and he had the longest span between appearances on United States Olympic hockey teams as a result.

name: Richard J. Schwartz
headline: Richard J. Schwartz, Who Expanded Jonathan Logan’s Dress Empire, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Schwartz expanded his father’s business, Jonathan Logan, and later turned to philanthropy and the arts, including the New York State Council on the Arts.

name: Allen Roses
profession: Upset Common Wisdom on Cause of Alzheimers
headline: Allen Roses, Who Upset Common Wisdom on Cause of Alzheimer’s, Dies at 73
abstract: Dr. Roses and his colleagues concluded that Alzheimer’s resulted from a gene variation, and he was testing a drug that he hoped would delay symptoms.

name: Phyllis Creore
headline: Phyllis Creore, ‘Canteen Girl’ on Wartime Radio, Dies at 100
abstract: Ms. Creore told uplifting stories and sang musical numbers to American soldiers far and wide in the 1940s.

name: Rod Temperton
profession: Wrote Thriller for Michael Jackson and Boogie Nights
headline: Rod Temperton, Who Wrote ‘Thriller’ for Michael Jackson and ‘Boogie Nights,’ Dies
abstract: A British keyboardist and songwriter, he was a member of the disco-funk group Heatwave and went on to compose some of Jackson’s biggest hits.

name: Bing Thom
profession: Daring Architect With a Sense of Place
headline: Bing Thom, Daring Architect With a Sense of Place, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Thom‘s swooping, playful design for the Arena Stage company enlivened Washington’s dreary southwestern waterfront.

name: Bertrand M. Bell
profession: Strove to Reduce Medical Trainees Grueling Shifts
headline: Bertrand M. Bell, Who Strove to Reduce Medical Trainees’ Grueling Shifts, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Bell was a key voice in limiting medical school graduates’ workloads after an 18-year-old’s death at a Manhattan hospital in 1984 led to calls for reform.

name: Brock Yates
headline: Brock Yates, Writer and Rebel Who Created the Cannonball Run, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Yates wrote more than a dozen books about cars and motor sports, and during the 1970s, began a cross-country race that inspired a movie starring Burt Reynolds.

name: Jim Kilroy
profession: Real Estate Developer Renowned as a Yachtsman
headline: Jim Kilroy, Real Estate Developer Renowned as a Yachtsman, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Kilroy, a former aviation executive, applied aerodynamic principles in winning five Maxi Yacht World Championships.

name: Elaine Lustig Cohen
headline: Elaine Lustig Cohen, Designer Who Left Her Mark Everywhere, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Cohen’s design career began almost accidentally when she inherited the job of creating the signs for the Seagram Building.

name: Dale Schenk
profession: Saw Immune System as Weapon Against Alzheimers
headline: Dale Schenk, Who Saw Immune System as Weapon Against Alzheimer’s, Dies at 59
abstract: Dr. Schenk tested the novel idea that the immune system, which fights infection, might be enlisted to fight Alzheimer’s through vaccines and other immune-based treatments.

name: Walter Darby Bannard
profession: Artist of the Color Field Movement
headline: Walter Darby Bannard, Artist of the Color Field Movement, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Bannard spent his career exploring color, form and the physicality of paint.

name: Austin Kalish
headline: Austin Kalish, a Writer of ‘Maude’ Abortion Episode, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Kalish, a TV writer who wrote extensively for comedy series in the 1960s and ’70s, took on sensitive social issues when working with Norman Lear.

name: Joan Marie Johnson
headline: Joan Marie Johnson, of the Singing Trio the Dixie Cups, Dies at 72
abstract: A founder of the group, Ms. Johnson helped catapult it to the top of the charts in 1964 with “Chapel of Love,” supplanting the Beatles’ “Love Me Do.”

name: Roslyn Litman
profession: Antitrust Lawyer and Civil Liberties Advocate
headline: Roslyn Litman, Antitrust Lawyer and Civil Liberties Advocate, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Litman’s major court victories included the removal of a holiday Nativity display from a Pittsburgh courthouse and an antitrust settlement for the professional basketball player Connie Hawkins.

name: Wolfgang Suschitzky
headline: Wolfgang Suschitzky, Photographer and Cinematographer, Dies at 104
abstract: Mr. Suschitzky, who was also a documentary filmmaker, was the director of photography for the 1971 film “Get Carter,” starring Michael Caine.

name: Lyn Wilde
profession: Half of a Twin Act in Movies
headline: Lyn Wilde, 93, Half of a Twin Act in Movies, Is Dead
abstract: In the 1940s, Lyn and Lee Wilde played roles in films with story lines that capitalized on their similar looks. Later, Lyn went on to appear in several films by herself.

name: Theodore Anderson
headline: Theodore Anderson, Mathematician Who Advanced Data Analysis, Dies at 98
abstract: Professor Anderson’s postwar work involved equations that would reveal underlying patterns in the economy.

name: Peter Allen
profession: Voice on the Radio for the Met Opera
headline: Peter Allen, a Voice on the Radio for the Met Opera, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Allen, who presided over 29 seasons of broadcasts, said introducing performances was, except for his marriage, “the richest experience of my life.”

name: Andrzej Wajda
headline: Andrzej Wajda, Towering Auteur of Polish Cinema, Dies at 90
abstract: Among Mr. Wajda’s best-known films are a war trilogy made in the 1950s, along with “Man of Marble” and its sequel, “Man of Iron.” He won an honorary Oscar in 2000.

name: Reginald K. Brack Jr.
profession: Led Time Inc. Into Entertainment Era
headline: Reginald K. Brack Jr., 79, Dies; Led Time Inc. Into Entertainment Era
abstract: Over almost four decades, Mr. Brack introduced lifestyle magazines like Discover and InStyle and broke down walls between the business and editorial sides of publications.

name: Jacob Neusner
headline: Jacob Neusner, Judaic Scholar Who Forged Interfaith Bonds, Dies at 84
abstract: Professor Neusner, a leading historian of Jewish rabbinical texts, published over 900 books devoted to comparative religion, history and legal theory.

name: Elizabeth F. Rohatyn
profession: Supporter of Education and the Arts
headline: Elizabeth F. Rohatyn, Supporter of Education and the Arts, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Rohatyn was a former chairwoman of the New York Public Library and a board member of Lincoln Center, and helped low-income students go on to higher education.

name: Herbert Irving
profession: Sysco Co-Founder and $300 Million Hospital Donor
headline: Herbert Irving, Sysco Co-Founder and $300 Million Hospital Donor, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Irving co-founded the food services giant Sysco in 1969 and, with his wife, donated heavily for cancer care and research.

name: Aaron Pryor
headline: Aaron Pryor, Boxing Champion Who Defeated Addiction, Dies at 60
abstract: Pryor, a junior welterweight, was 39-1 professionally, and memorably battled Alexis Argüello. He later overcame a career-ending addiction to cocaine.

name: Morton Silverstein
headline: Morton Silverstein, Documentarian Who Explored Social Ills, Dies at 86
abstract: An Emmy Award winner, Mr. Silverstein said he was driven by a “sense of outrage at people being exploited and people without voices.”

name: Donn Fendler
profession: Was Lost in Wilds of Maine as a Boy
headline: Donn Fendler, Who Was Lost in Wilds of Maine as a Boy, Dies at 90
abstract: The 12-year-old’s tale of survival gained him fame and honors and was turned into a book that became required reading for schoolchildren in the state.

name: Benjamin Payton
headline: Benjamin Payton, Transformative Leader of Tuskegee University, Dies at 83
abstract: Dr. Payton turned the Tuskegee Institute in Alabama into a prominent historically black university over nearly three decades as its president.

name: Thomas Mikal Ford
profession: Known for His Role in 90s Sitcom Martin
headline: Thomas Mikal Ford, Known for His Role in ’90s Sitcom ‘Martin,’ Dies at 52
abstract: He played the pragmatic yet charming Tommy, a friend of the title character, played by Martin Lawrence, who was often the subject of the jokes in the show.

name: Jack Greenberg
profession: Courthouse Pillar of the Civil Rights Movement
headline: Jack Greenberg, a Courthouse Pillar of the Civil Rights Movement, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Greenberg, a member of a legal team assembled by Thurgood Marshall, was involved in more than 40 civil rights cases before the Supreme Court.

name: Dario Fo
headline: Dario Fo, Whose Plays Won Praise, Scorn and a Nobel, Dies at 90
abstract: The Nobel-Prize-winner is best known for the “Accidental Death of an Anarchist” and his one-man show “Mistero Buffo” (“Comic Mystery”).

name: Bhumibol Adulyadej
headline: Bhumibol Adulyadej, 88, People’s King of Thailand, Dies After 7-Decade Reign
abstract: The king, one of history’s longest-reigning monarchs, was a unifying figure in a deeply polarized country.

name: Patricia Barry
profession: Actress on TV Since Its Early Days
headline: Patricia Barry, Actress on TV Since Its Early Days, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Barry’s career’s was dominated by appearances on soap operas and shows like “The Twilight Zone.”

name: Stephen Bollenbach
profession: Spared Donald Trump From Personal Bankruptcy
headline: Stephen Bollenbach, Who Spared Donald Trump From Personal Bankruptcy, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Bollenbach was long praised for his financial skills, having been the first Hilton Hotels chief executive outside of the Hilton family.

name: James F. Colaianni
headline: James F. Colaianni, a Theologian Opposed to Priest Celibacy, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Colaianni, who was an editor at Ramparts magazine in the 1960s, also campaigned against the use of napalm during the Vietnam War.

name: Yutaka Yoshida
profession: U.S. War Hero of Japanese Descent
headline: Dr. Yutaka Yoshida, a U.S. War Hero of Japanese Descent, Dies at 104
abstract: Dr. Yoshida, who became a surgeon after earning a Silver Star during World War II, had been a police officer tasked with rounding up Japanese in Hawaii after the attack on Pearl Harbor.

name: Joseph L. Birman
headline: Joseph L. Birman, Physicist Who Aided Dissident Scientists, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Birman was instrumental in the creation of a program that helped refugee scientists restart their careers in the United States in the 1990s.

name: Louis Stettner
profession: Photographed the Everyday New York and Paris
headline: Louis Stettner, Who Photographed the Everyday New York and Paris, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Stettner, who considered the two cities his “spiritual mothers,” chronicled the poetry of daily life, with his subjects unaware of his presence.

name: Pierre Étaix
headline: Pierre Étaix, Director and Slapstick Actor, Dies at 87
abstract: Legal issues prevented the films of Mr. Étaix from being screened for decades.

name: Klaus Kertess
profession: Curator and Gallerist Gave Major Artists a Start
headline: Klaus Kertess Dies at 76; Curator and Gallerist Gave Major Artists a Start
abstract: Mr. Kertess was known for having an eye, and a nose, for developing talent, like Brice Marden and Chuck Close.

name: Anthony Foley
profession: Carried a Rugby Club and Raised a Cup
headline: Anthony Foley, 42, Dies; Carried a Rugby Club and Raised a Cup
abstract: Foley achieved international renown by leading his underdog Munster rugby club to a European championship, then became the team’s coach.

name: Leo Beranek
headline: Leo Beranek, Acoustics Designer and Internet Pioneer, Dies at 102
abstract: Bolt, Beranek & Newman, the company he helped found, built the first computer-based network, which paved the way for the creation of the internet.

name: Irwin Smigel
profession: New York Dentist Behind Cosmetic Techniques
headline: Irwin Smigel, New York Dentist Behind Cosmetic Techniques, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Smigel, who founded the American Society for Dental Aesthetics, built on processes used for laser whitening and bonding to improve the appearance of teeth.

name: David Antin
profession: Poet Created a New Performance Style
headline: David Antin Dies at 84; Poet Created a New Performance Style
abstract: At 16, Mr. Antin made a career decision and bought a rhyming dictionary, a thesaurus and a portable typewriter.

name: John Good
profession: Architect of F.B.I.s Abscam Sting Operation
headline: John Good, Architect of F.B.I.’s Abscam Sting Operation, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Good’s two-year inquiry resulted in bribery and conspiracy charges against a senator, six representatives and a dozen others.

name: Ted V. Mikels
headline: Ted V. Mikels, Master of Low-Budget Cult Favorites, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Mikels cranked out an endless stream of bloody shockers, sci-fi thrillers, action films and jiggle-fests.

name: Thom Jones
headline: Thom Jones, Janitor Turned Acclaimed Author, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Jones was working as a school janitor when he mailed an unsolicited, fictionalized war story to The New Yorker. In short time he became a literary sensation.

name: Eddie Applegate
profession: Sweetheart on The Patty Duke Show
headline: Eddie Applegate, a Sweetheart on ‘The Patty Duke Show,’ Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Applegate was best known for playing the boyfriend of the show’s character Patty Lane.

name: Phil Chess
profession: Record Label Elevated Unknown Blues Musicians
headline: Phil Chess, Whose Record Label Elevated Unknown Blues Musicians, Dies at 95
abstract: Chess Records, the label founded by Mr. Chess and his brother, became successful by finding little-known performers and persuading radio stations to play their music.

name: Yvette Chauviré
profession: Ballerina and Symbol of French Culture
headline: Yvette Chauviré, Ballerina and Symbol of French Culture, Dies at 99
abstract: Ms. Chauviré began as a child prodigy and went on to become one of the 20th century’s outstanding dancers.

name: Edgar Munhall
profession: First Curator of the Frick Collection
headline: Edgar Munhall, First Curator of the Frick Collection, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Munhall was known for a keen eye and prolific writing during his pivotal tenure at the venerable Upper East Side institution.

name: William G. Bowen
headline: William G. Bowen, Princeton Educator Who Championed Poor and Minority Students, Dies at 83
abstract: Dr. Bowen was president of the Andrew W. Mellon Foundation and also served as provost and president of Princeton, overseeing the admission of women and expanding the university academically.

name: Fashion Designer Richard Nicoll
headline: Fashion Designer Richard Nicoll Dies at 39
abstract: The London-born Central Saint Martins graduate was known for his distinctive, Modernist approach, candy-colored palettes and sculptured designs.

name: David Bunnell
headline: David Bunnell, Whose Magazines Were Tech World Must-Reads, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Bunnell rode the early wave of personal computers, establishing PC Magazine, Macworld and other magazines and contributing to the industry’s explosive growth.

name: Nicole Haran
profession: Helped Create a Theater Troupe and Web Series
headline: Nicole Haran, 47, Who Helped Create a Theater Troupe and Web Series, Dies
abstract: Ms. Haran directed her first film, “Dive,” last year and was still in graduate school when she and three classmates founded the Barefoot Theater Company.

name: Kigeli V
headline: Kigeli V, the Last King of Rwanda, Dies at 80
abstract: The monarch, who reigned for less than two years and spent over 50 in exile, ended up a pauper in Washington.

name: Annemarie Huste
headline: Annemarie Huste, a Kennedy Chef Who Said Too Much, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Huste, Jacqueline Kennedy’s personal cook, was fired for disclosing details about the family to the press.

name: Kevin Meaney
headline: Kevin Meaney, Veteran Stand-Up Comedian, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Meaney, who impersonated famous singers from the charity hit song “We Are the World,” also appeared regularly on television shows, including “Saturday Night Live” and “30 Rock.”

name: Steve Dillon
headline: Steve Dillon, Comic Artist Who Helped Create ‘Preacher,’ Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Dillon also worked on the character Judge Dredd for the British comic book 2000 AD and the Marvel character The Punisher.

name: Sandra Lee Bartky
