profession: at the Vanguard of Feminist Philosophy
headline: Sandra Lee Bartky, at the Vanguard of Feminist Philosophy, Dies at 81
abstract: Professor Bartky argued that women subconsciously submitted to men’s unnatural standards for their bodies, what she called the “tyranny of slenderness.”

name: Tom Hayden
profession: Civil Rights and Antiwar Activist Turned Lawmaker
headline: Tom Hayden, Civil Rights and Antiwar Activist Turned Lawmaker, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Hayden, one of the nation’s most visible radicals in the 1960s and early ’70s, was a founder of Students for a Democratic Society and a former husband of Jane Fonda.

name: Gordon Hamilton
headline: Gordon Hamilton, Climate Scientist, Dies at 50 in Antarctica Accident
abstract: Dr. Hamilton, who was studying changes in sea levels, died when his snowmobile went into a crevasse.

name: Khalifa bin Hamad al-Thani
headline: Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad al-Thani, Former Emir of Qatar, Dies at 84
abstract: As the Gulf nation’s leader from 1972 to 1995, Sheikh Khalifa oversaw Qatar’s independence from Britain and the rapid modernization of its economy.

name: Bobby Vee
profession: Pop Idol Known for Take Good Care of My Baby
headline: Bobby Vee, Pop Idol Known for ‘Take Good Care of My Baby,’ Dies at 73
abstract: One of a crop of dreamboat singers promoted in the late 1950s and early ’60s, he got his first big break when he filled in for Buddy Holly and others after their plane crashed.

name: Lucia Perillo
headline: Lucia Perillo, Whose Illness Shaped Her Poetry, Dies at 58
abstract: When asked about her multiple sclerosis, Ms. Perillo, who wrote piercingly about mortality, said: “I don’t battle M.S. I relent to its humiliations.”

name: Bob Hoover
headline: Bob Hoover, Aviator Whose Aerobatic Stunts Are Legend, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Hoover, a pilot who escaped Nazi captivity in a stolen plane, forged a career studded with aeronautical achievements and feats of derring-do.

name: Stanley Silverstein
headline: Stanley Silverstein, Co-Founder of Nina Footwear, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Silverstein, a designer of women’s shoes that were both fashionable and affordable, started Nina Footwear with his brother Mike in 1953.

name: Junko Tabei
headline: Junko Tabei, First Woman to Conquer Everest, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Tabei, a Japanese alpinist, was the first woman to reach the top of Mount Everest and the rest of the Seven Summits.

name: Howard Davies
profession: Theater Director in Britain and on Broadway
headline: Howard Davies, Theater Director in Britain and on Broadway, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Davies won awards in Britain and enthusiastic reviews on Broadway, where he mounted “Les Liaisons Dangereuses” and “The Iceman Cometh,” among other productions.

name: Jack T. Chick
headline: Jack T. Chick, Cartoonist Whose Tracts Preached Salvation, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Chick’s tracts were said to have sold more than 900 million copies while being attacked as instruments of hate speech.

name: Jorge Batlle
headline: Jorge Batlle, Political Scion Who Led Uruguay, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Batlle was the first Latin American leader to propose the partial legalization of drugs as a way to reduce trafficking, money laundering and profiteering by cartels.

name: Gavin MacFadyen
profession: Mentor and Defender of WikiLeaks Founder
headline: Gavin MacFadyen, 76, Mentor and Defender of WikiLeaks Founder, Dies
abstract: The American investigative journalist and documentarian was a core supporter of WikiLeaks and Julian Assange and provided support of whistle-blowers.

name: Ewen Whitaker
headline: Ewen Whitaker, Who Guided NASA to the Moon, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Whitaker had no formal training as an astronomer, but he used his unparalleled knowledge of the lunar surface to select landing sites for spacecraft.

name: Michael Massee
profession: Screen Villain Haunted by the Accidental Death of Brandon Lee
headline: Michael Massee, 64, Screen Villain Haunted by the Accidental Death of Brandon Lee, Dies
abstract: Mr. Massee, a character actor, took a long sabbatical after the deadly shooting on the set of “The Crow” in 1993 and then appeared in many TV and film roles.

name: John Zacherle
headline: John Zacherle, Host With a Ghoulish Perspective, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Zacherle was one of early television’s horror-movie hosts, playing an undertaker and other characters on stations in Philadelphia and New York in the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Sophia Cranshaw
headline: Sophia Cranshaw, MTV Producer of Social-Issue Campaigns, Dies at 45
abstract: Ms. Cranshaw won awards for public service announcements and campaigns that dealt with everything from genocide in Darfur to depression on campus.

name: Susan Lindquist
headline: Susan Lindquist, Scientist Who Made Genetic Discoveries Using Yeast, Dies at 67
abstract: The conceptually daring work of Dr. Lindquist, a National Medal of Science recipient, opened new paths to understanding Parkinson’s and other diseases.

name: Richard Pittman
headline: Richard Pittman, Marine Who Fended Off Vietnam Ambush, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Pittman earned the Medal of Honor for charging into heavy North Vietnamese fire to aid wounded fellow Marines.

name: W. Dudley Johnson
headline: W. Dudley Johnson, Heart Bypass Surgery Pioneer, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Johnson, who applied crocheting and needlecraft skills, went on to perform more than 8,500 bypass operations over four decades.

name: James Galanos
headline: James Galanos, Fashion Designer for the Elite, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Galanos, who outfitted Nancy Reagan for inaugural events, earned numerous accolades even as he evaded celebrity and shunned the fashion establishment.

name: Tammy Grimes
headline: Tammy Grimes, the Original ‘Unsinkable Molly Brown,’ Dies at 82
abstract: The throaty actress and singer won a Tony Award for her performance in “The Unsinkable Molly Brown” at age 26 and went on to a distinguished stage career.

name: Norman Brokaw
profession: Agent to Marilyn Monroe and Elvis Presley
headline: Norman Brokaw, Agent to Marilyn Monroe and Elvis Presley, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Brokaw rose from teenage mail clerk to top mogul at the William Morris talent agency, where he broke ground in the fledgling television industry.

name: Curly Putman
headline: Curly Putman, Writer of ‘The Green, Green Grass of Home,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Putman turned out hundreds of songs, many of them country chart-toppers, after moving to Nashville and signing with Tree Publishing in the early 1960s.

name: David H. Brooks
headline: David H. Brooks, 61, Dies Serving Time for Insider Trading
abstract: The founder of the military armor maker DHB Industries was serving 17 years for insider trading and fraudulently enriching himself.

name: Natalie Babbitt
profession: Took On Immortality in Tuck Everlasting
headline: Natalie Babbitt, 84, Dies; Took On Immortality in ‘Tuck Everlasting’
abstract: Ms. Babbitt’s book (one of many) about a family that cannot die found a fervent readership and inspired two films and a Broadway musical.

name: Robert Weber
profession: His New Yorker Cartoons Twitted the Overprivileged
headline: Robert Weber Dies at 92; His New Yorker Cartoons Twitted the Overprivileged
abstract: The people Mr. Weber drew over 45 years for the magazine were nothing if not entitled, going about with what some might see as skewed expectations.

name: Stanford Lipsey
headline: Stanford Lipsey, 89, Publisher Whose Nebraska Weeklies Won Pulitzer, Dies
abstract: Mr. Lipsey’s Omaha chain, the Sun Newspapers, won in 1973 for exposing fund-raising excesses by Boys Town, the charity for orphaned children.

name: Don Marshall
profession: Made Casting History in Land of the Giants
headline: Don Marshall, Who Made Casting History in ‘Land of the Giants,’ Is Dead at 80
abstract: Mr. Marshall, one of the first black actors to have a starring role on an American network television series, also appeared in television movies and feature films.

name: E. Lee Hennessee
headline: E. Lee Hennessee, a Leading Woman in Hedge Funds, Dies at 64
abstract: Ms. Hennessee created one of the first indexes to track the hedge fund industry’s secretive transactions.

name: Miriam Weinstein
profession: Mother and Backbone of Original Miramax
headline: Miriam Weinstein, Mother and Backbone of Original Miramax, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Weinstein had no plans to stop contributing (advice or pastries), even after Miramax grew in fame and value.

name: Kay Starr
headline: Kay Starr, Hillbilly Singer With Crossover Appeal, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Starr found fame in the big-band era, hit it big as a pop and country artist, and continued her career well into her later years.

name: David Seeley
headline: David Seeley, Educator Who Fought Against Segregation, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Seeley worked to provide equal opportunity to young people, through political actions and community alliances, for more than 50 years.

name: Rick Steiner
headline: Rick Steiner, Producer of Broadway Hits, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Steiner worked a broad variety of jobs and was, among other things, a poker champion.

name: Gene La Rocque
headline: Gene La Rocque, Decorated Veteran Who Condemned Waste of War, Dies at 98
abstract: After retiring from the Navy, Admiral La Rocque founded a think tank to promote peace and to monitor the influence of the military-industrial complex.

name: Jean-Jacques Perrey
headline: Jean-Jacques Perrey, Electronic Music Pioneer, Dies at 87
abstract: He created some of the earliest electronic pop albums and was one of the first musicians to use the Moog synthesizer after it appeared in the 1960s.

name: Janet Reno
profession: First Woman to Serve as U.S. Attorney General
headline: Janet Reno, First Woman to Serve as U.S. Attorney General, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Reno’s eight years in the office placed her in the middle of some of the most divisive episodes of the Clinton presidency.

name: Ralph Cicerone
headline: Ralph Cicerone, Scientist Who Sounded Climate Change Alarm, Dies at 73
abstract: Dr. Cicerone, who had a reputation for nonpartisan civility, pursued the activist agenda as president of the National Academy of Sciences.

name: E. Barrett Prettyman Jr.
headline: E. Barrett Prettyman Jr., Lawyer Who Fortified Desegregation Ruling, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Prettyman had the ear of several Supreme Court justices, but his sway was perhaps never more significant than in an opinion that wasn’t published.

name: Arnold Mesches
headline: Arnold Mesches, Artist Who Was Recorded by the F.B.I., Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Mesches was a scenic artist in Hollywood when his work for the Communist Party came to the attention of the bureau in 1945.

name: Yaffa Eliach
headline: Yaffa Eliach, Historian Who Captured Faces of the Holocaust, Dies at 79
abstract: Professor Eliach, who survived the Nazi massacres of Jews in her Lithuanian town, went on to document their lives in a canyon of photographs at the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum.

name: Zoltan Kocsis
headline: Zoltan Kocsis, Pianist and Conductor, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Kocsis revamped the Hungarian National Philharmonic Orchestra and played with orchestras in New York, Berlin, Chicago, London, San Francisco and elsewhere.

name: Raoul Coutard
profession: Cinematographer of the French New Wave
headline: Raoul Coutard, Cinematographer of the French New Wave, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Coutard, known for his mobile camera on films like “Breathless,” was said to have had the “rare ability to realize the very different objectives of each of the major directors he has worked with.”

name: Bob Cranshaw
profession: Bassist From Jazz to Pop to Broadway
headline: Bob Cranshaw, Bassist From Jazz to Pop to Broadway, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Cranshaw’s credits included classic recordings, late-night TV gigs, and even “Sesame Street.”

name: Rosamond Bernier
headline: Rosamond Bernier, Art Insider Who Turned Lectures Into Theater, Dies at 100
abstract: Ms. Bernier’s long life of journalism, famous friends and other encounters gave her talks an uncommonly wide sweep.

name: Charles Wolf Jr.
headline: Charles Wolf Jr., Who Clashed With Pentagon Papers Leaker, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Wolf, who worked at the RAND Corporation, was the supervisor of Daniel Ellsberg and tried to oust him in 1969 before he leaked the secret documents.

name: Leonard Cohen
headline: Leonard Cohen, Epic and Enigmatic Songwriter, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Cohen was an unlikely and reluctant pop star, but his lyrics captivated other artists and gave him a reputation as “the master of erotic despair.”

name: Clarence M. Ditlow III
headline: Clarence M. Ditlow III, Auto Safety Crusader, Dies at 72
abstract: As head of the Center for Auto Safety, Mr. Ditlow exposed hundreds of automotive defects and was instrumental in forcing the recall of millions of vehicles.

name: Robert Vaughn
profession: Starred as Napoleon Solo in Man From U.N.C.L.E
headline: Robert Vaughn, Who Starred as Napoleon Solo in ‘Man From U.N.C.L.E.,’ Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Vaughn reached the peak of his fame in the 1960s playing a debonair international agent.

name: Aileen Mehle
profession: Gossips Grande Dame Known as Suzy
headline: Aileen Mehle, Gossip’s Grande Dame Known as ‘Suzy,’ Dies at 98
abstract: Millions of people read her column in newspapers across the country and knew her face from her regular appearances on the game show “What’s My Line.”

name: Cella Irvine
headline: Cella Irvine, Digital Media Pioneer Who Led About.com, Dies at 59
abstract: She broke ground in a male-dominated field in corporate roles and as a founding board member and chairwoman of the nonprofit New York New Media Association.

name: Leon Russell
headline: Leon Russell, Hit Maker and Musicians’ Musician, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Russell went from being one of the top studio musicians in Los Angeles to a celebrated songwriter for himself and other acts.

name: Gwen Ifill
profession: Political Reporter and Co-Anchor of PBS NewsHour
headline: Gwen Ifill, Political Reporter and Co-Anchor of ‘PBS NewsHour,’ Dies at 61
abstract: Ms. Ifill reported for The Washington Post, The New York Times and NBC News before becoming a PBS presence and debate moderator.

name: Billy Miller
profession: Curator and Historian of Fringe Music
headline: Billy Miller, Curator and Historian of Fringe Music, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Miller and his wife, Miriam Linna, revived the reputations of several bands through their efforts to distribute rockabilly and garage band music.

name: Claire Labine
profession: Soap Opera Writer and Co-Creator of Ryans Hope
headline: Claire Labine, Soap Opera Writer and Co-Creator of ‘Ryan’s Hope,’ Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Labine’s story lines on “General Hospital” heightened public awareness about breast cancer, cardiac transplants and the AIDS epidemic.

name: Gardnar Mulloy
headline: Gardnar Mulloy, a Tennis Champion Who Later Championed Senior Tennis, Dies at 102
abstract: Mulloy, a brilliant doubles player inducted into the Hall of Fame in 1972, was ranked No. 1 in the U.S. in 1952 and won more than 125 national tournaments, most of them in senior play.

name: Mose Allison
headline: Mose Allison, a Fount of Jazz and Blues, Dies at 89
abstract: The influential musician tapped his voice, instrumental skill and Mississippi upbringing to convey wisdom and worldliness.

name: Dick Oliver
profession: Reporter for Good Day New York
headline: Dick Oliver, Reporter for ‘Good Day New York,’ Dies at 77
abstract: A longtime reporter and editor who was at the scene as planes hit the World Trade Center on 9/11.

name: Dwayne O. Andreas
profession: Turned Archer Daniels Midland Into Food Giant
headline: Dwayne O. Andreas, Who Turned Archer Daniels Midland Into Food Giant, Dies at 98
abstract: With business acumen and political ties, he pushed the food products company to the front of American industry.

name: Holly Dunn
headline: Holly Dunn, 59, Country Singer-Songwriter, Dies; ‘Daddy’s Hands’ Was a Hit
abstract: The wistful “Daddy’s Hands” won two Grammy nominations, and Ms. Dunn’s song “Maybe I Mean Yes” provoked a national conversation about date rape.

name: Ruth Baron Ziff
headline: Ruth Baron Ziff Dies at 92; Added Sociological Insight to Ads
abstract: A sociologist with a knack for market research, she contributed to the “Please don’t squeeze the Charmin” toilet paper ad.

name: Howard Ruff
headline: Howard Ruff, Quirky Conservative Economist and Author, Dies at 85
abstract: An idiosyncratic figure whose roller-coaster career included stockbroker, singer, investment adviser, publisher and television host.

name: Jules Eskin
headline: Jules Eskin, Cellist With Boston Symphony Orchestra, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Eskin performed with the ensemble for more than half a century.

name: Theodore F. Twardzik
headline: Theodore F. Twardzik, Founder of Mrs. T’s Pierogies, Dies at 89
abstract: He left a job as an accountant when he saw a future in creating a frozen food company that was named for his mother and used her recipe.

name: Melvin Laird
headline: Melvin Laird, Defense Secretary Who Challenged Vietnam Policy, Dies at 94
abstract: By late 1968, Mr. Laird believed that diplomacy was the only way to end the war, and later pressed the Nixon White House to wind down troop involvement.

name: Jay W. Forrester
headline: Jay W. Forrester Dies at 98; a Pioneer in Computer Models
abstract: In addition to developing system dynamics modeling, Mr. Forrester, an M.I.T. professor, was an inventor of magnetic core memory for computers.

name: Diana Balmori
profession: Landscape Architect With a Blending Philosophy
headline: Diana Balmori, Landscape Architect With a Blending Philosophy, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Balmori’s projects included buildings, gardens and master plans that emanated from “very clear human engineering with ecology and with landscape.”

name: Leon G. Billings
profession: Architect of Clean Air and Clean Water Acts
headline: Leon G. Billings, Architect of Clean Air and Clean Water Acts, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Billings was the first staff director of the Senate environment subcommittee and an alter ego of Senator Edmund S. Muskie, Democrat of Maine.

name: Ruth Gruber
profession: Fearless Chronicler of the Jewish Struggle
headline: Ruth Gruber, a Fearless Chronicler of the Jewish Struggle, Dies at 105
abstract: Ms. Gruber, a photojournalist and writer whose career spanned seven decades, often crossed the line from journalist to human rights advocate.

name: Denton Cooley
profession: Pioneering Heart Surgery Set Off a 40-Year Medical Feud
headline: Dr. Denton Cooley, Whose Pioneering Heart Surgery Set Off a 40-Year Medical Feud, Dies at 96
abstract: Working at the Houston cardiology center he founded, Dr. Cooley, in 1969, implanted the first totally artificial heart. His mentor and partner, the renowned surgeon Dr. Michael E. DeBakey, felt betrayed.

name: David Mancuso
profession: New York Loft Was a Hub of 70s Night Life
headline: David Mancuso, Whose New York Loft Was a Hub of ’70s Night Life, Dies at 72
abstract: With an eclectic musical mix, Saturday night parties at Mr. Mancuso’s loft provided the model for dozens of clubs to come.

name: Sharon Jones
profession: Powerful Voice of Soul With the Dap-Kings
headline: Sharon Jones, Powerful Voice of Soul With the Dap-Kings, Dies at 60
abstract: Ms. Jones recorded and performed at an unrelenting pace, and a documentary film chronicled her battle with pancreatic cancer.

name: Lupita Tovar
headline: Lupita Tovar, Star of Spanish-Language ‘Dracula,’ Dies at 106
abstract: Ms. Tovar, known as the “Sweetheart of Mexico,” also performed in silent films and Westerns and helped to promote Mexican cinema.

name: Houston Conwill
headline: Houston Conwill, Whose Sculptures Celebrated Black Culture, Dies at 69
abstract: Among Mr. Conwill’s best-known works are a memorial for the poet Langston Hughes in Harlem and one for the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. in San Francisco.

name: Milt Okun
profession: Turned John Denver Into a Pop Star
headline: Milt Okun, Who Turned John Denver Into a Pop Star, Dies at 92
abstract: A music producer and arranger who founded Cherry Lane Music Publishing, Mr. Okun also worked with Peter, Paul and Mary, Plácido Domingo and Harry Belafonte.

name: Patricia Kutteles
profession: Driven by Tragedy to End Dont Ask
headline: Patricia Kutteles, Driven by Tragedy to End ‘Don’t Ask, Don’t Tell,’ Dies at 67
abstract: Mrs. Kutteles’s relentless efforts helped reverse the policy against gay soldiers serving openly, a decade after her son was beaten to death by a fellow soldier.

name: William Trevor
headline: William Trevor, Writer Who Evoked the Struggles of Ordinary Life, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Irish by birth and upbringing but a longtime resident of Britain, Mr. Trevor focused his mournful, darkly funny short stories and novels on “the sadness of fate.”

name: Whitney Smith
profession: Passion for Flags Became a Career
headline: Whitney Smith, Whose Passion for Flags Became a Career, Dies at 76
abstract: Fascinated by the banners from an early age, Mr. Smith went on to coin a term for the study of flags, vexillology, and even designed one for Guyana.

name: Peter Binzen
profession: Dean of Philadelphia Journalism for Half a Century
headline: Peter Binzen, Dean of Philadelphia Journalism for Half a Century, Dies at 94
abstract: At The Evening and Sunday Bulletin and later The Philadelphia Inquirer, he wrote about education, urban affairs and business, and his books covered workers, mayors and railroads.

name: Ralph Branca
profession: Gave Up Shot Heard Round the World
headline: Ralph Branca, Who Gave Up ‘Shot Heard Round the World,’ Dies at 90
abstract: The Brooklyn Dodgers pitcher threw the ninth-inning pitch that Bobby Thomson drove into baseball legend with a pennant-clinching home run in 1951.

name: Edgar Chase Jr.
headline: Edgar Chase Jr., Purveyor of Creole Cuisine, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Chase, a jazz trumpeter known as Dooky, ran his family’s Creole restaurant, which also served as a gathering place for civil rights activists.

name: Ben Zion Shenker
headline: Ben Zion Shenker, Rabbi Who Wrote Prayer Melodies, Dies at 91
abstract: The rabbi’s music flavored the religious life of Orthodox Jews and influenced klezmer bands.

name: Al Caiola
headline: Al Caiola, Guitarist With Top 40 Instrumental Hits, Dies at 96
abstract: He played with Buddy Holly, Frank Sinatra and others and reached the top of the charts with themes from “The Magnificent Seven” and “Bonanza.”

name: Florence Henderson
profession: Upbeat Mom of The Brady Bunch
headline: Florence Henderson, Upbeat Mom of ‘The Brady Bunch,’ Dies at 82
abstract: Her career began with stage musicals, but Ms. Henderson’s touchstone role as the perky matriarch of a 1970s blended family made her an enduring TV presence for decades.

name: Cliff Barrows
headline: Cliff Barrows, Billy Graham’s Longtime Musical Director, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Barrows and Mr. Graham met by chance in 1945 and began a professional association that lasted more than 70 years.

name: Paul Sylbert
headline: Paul Sylbert, Oscar-Winner Who Gave Movies Their Look, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Sylbert, whose twin brother was in the same field, began his career painting backdrops for the Metropolitan Opera.

name: Stan Huntsman
profession: Track and Fields Mentor and Passionate Defender
headline: Stan Huntsman, Track and Field’s Mentor and Passionate Defender, Dies at 84
abstract: Huntsman coached at the college level, led United States Olympic teams and fought financial reductions that threatened the very existence of the sport.

name: Fidel Castro
headline: Fidel Castro, Cuban Revolutionary Who Defied U.S., Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Castro brought the Cold War to the Western Hemisphere, bedeviled 11 American presidents and briefly pushed the world to the brink of nuclear war.

name: Fritz Weaver
headline: Fritz Weaver, Tony-Winning Character Actor, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Weaver won a Tony for his role in Robert Marasco’s “Child’s Play” about the malevolent environment at an exclusive Roman Catholic school for boys.

name: Pauline Oliveros
headline: Pauline Oliveros, Composer Who Championed ‘Deep Listening,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Oliveros also addressed the theme of gender inequality repeatedly and tenaciously.

name: Ron Glass
profession: Played a Dapper Detective on Barney Miller
headline: Ron Glass, Who Played a Dapper Detective on ‘Barney Miller,’ Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Glass was nominated for an Emmy Award for supporting actor in 1982 for his performance on the series. He also played a mysterious preacher on “Firefly.”

name: Mark Taimanov
headline: Mark Taimanov, World-Class Chess and Piano Player, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Taimanov was a classical pianist and former Soviet chess champion whose lopsided loss to Bobby Fischer in 1971 cost him his government salary.

name: Joe Esposito
headline: Joe Esposito Dies at 78; Spent 20 Years Assisting Elvis Presley
abstract: Mr. Esposito met Elvis Presley when they were serving in the Army on a base in Germany and went on to be a friend and personal organizer.

name: David Hamilton
profession: Photographer Known for Nude Images of Girls
headline: David Hamilton, Photographer Known for Nude Images of Girls, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Hamilton, whose soft dreamy style defined his photographs fashion and advertising assignments in the 1960s, was the target of rape allegations.

name: Harry Flournoy Jr.
profession: Captain of First All-Black Starting Five to Win N.C.A.A. Title
headline: Harry Flournoy Jr., 72, Dies; a Captain of First All-Black Starting Five to Win N.C.A.A. Title
abstract: The 1965-66 Miners were the first team to win the national championship with five black starting players, defeating an all-white Kentucky team.

name: Russell Oberlin
profession: Led Renaissance of Countertenor in U.S
headline: Russell Oberlin, 88, Dies; Led Renaissance of Countertenor in U.S.
abstract: Lauded for his sensitive phrasing, crystalline diction and vibrato-rich tone, Mr. Oberlin helped spur the modern renaissance of the countertenor.

name: Al Brodax
profession: Steered the Beatles Yellow Submarine to the Screen
headline: Al Brodax, Who Steered the Beatles’ ‘Yellow Submarine’ to the Screen, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Brodax, a television producer, sold the Beatles’ manager, Brian Epstein, on the idea of a cartoon series and struck a deal for the animated film, a psychedelic classic.

name: Bruce Mazlish
profession: Fused Psychoanalysis and History in His Books
headline: Bruce Mazlish, Who Fused Psychoanalysis and History in His Books, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Mazlish created controversy with psychoanalytic biographies of living world leaders, including one about Richard M. Nixon.

name: Grant Tinker
headline: Grant Tinker, Former Chairman of NBC, Dies at 90; Made Network a Ratings Powerhouse
abstract: Mr. Tinker, whose MTM Enterprises produced hit shows in the 1970s, revamped NBC’s prime-time lineup in the 1980s with series like “Cheers” and “Hill Street Blues.”

name: Erich Bloch
headline: Erich Bloch, Who Helped Develop IBM Mainframe, Dies at 91
abstract: In 1964, he transformed computing with the System/360, the foundation for the modern operating system that would host various software programs.

name: Keo Woolford
headline: Keo Woolford, a Detective on ‘Hawaii Five-0,’ Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. Woolford, an actor and filmmaker, also starred in a one-man show that explored his Hawaiian heritage.

name: Michael James Delligatti
headline: Michael James Delligatti, Creator of the Big Mac, Dies at 98
abstract: He modeled the first McDonald’s double-decker on burgers at a Big Boy and introduced it in 1967 in Uniontown, Pa. A year later, it was on the menu nationwide.

name: Sebastian Leone
headline: Sebastian Leone, Borough President Who Championed Brooklyn, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Leone was borough president from 1970 to 1976, when Brooklyn did not enjoy the renown as a cultural center and thriving place to live that it has today.

name: Nancy Meehan
headline: Nancy Meehan, 85, Evocative Dancer and Choreographer, Dies
abstract: Tall and striking, combining sensuous grace with nuanced force, Ms. Meehan came to notice as a leading soloist in the Erick Hawkins troupe in the 1960s.

name: William A. Christenberry
headline: William A. Christenberry, Photographer of Rural South, Dies at 80
abstract: Few artists have been so identified with one small patch of terrain as Mr. Christenberry, who used Hale County, Ala., as the inspiration for many of his works.

name: Burton J. Lee
profession: Reagan AIDS Panelist and Bushs White House Physician
headline: Dr. Burton J. Lee, 86, Reagan AIDS Panelist and Bush’s White House Physician, Dies
abstract: Dr. Lee diagnosed the elder Mr. Bush’s thyroid condition, treated him after he vomited at a state dinner and earlier recommended government support for AIDS patients.

name: Ousmane Sow
headline: Ousmane Sow, Sculptor of Larger-Than-Life Figures, Dies at 81
abstract: In his art, the Senegal-born Mr. Sow relied on his knowledge of the human anatomy from his years working as a physical therapist.

name: Milt Moss
headline: Milt Moss, Actor in Classic Alka-Seltzer Ad, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Mr. Moss, who appeared in nightclubs and on TV, was best known for saying “I can’t believe I ate that whole thing” in an antacid commercial.

name: Andrew Sachs
profession: Hapless Waiter on the BBC Sitcom Fawlty Towers
headline: Andrew Sachs, Hapless Waiter on the BBC Sitcom ‘Fawlty Towers,’ Dies at 86
abstract: His earnest yet bumbling character, Manuel, was regularly recruited into the schemes of the hotel owner Basil Fawlty, played by John Cleese.

name: Irving Fradkin
profession: Founder of Dollars for Scholars Program
headline: Irving Fradkin, Founder of Dollars for Scholars Program, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Fradkin started the program on a card table in the 1950s. Since then it has provided more than $3.5 billion to over 2.2 million students and evolved into Scholarship America.

name: Peng Chang-kuei
headline: Peng Chang-kuei, Chef Behind General Tso’s Chicken, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Peng, whose chicken has been called “the most famous Hunanese dish in the world,” left a lasting mark on the food scene.

name: Alice Drummond
headline: Alice Drummond, Character Actress, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Drummond, a regular in Broadway and off Broadway productions in the 1960s and ’70s, had roles in films like “Ghostbusters,” “Awakenings” and “Doubt.”

name: C. Wyatt Dickerson
headline: C. Wyatt Dickerson, Businessman and Man About Washington, Is Dead at 92
abstract: In the 1960s and 1970s, Mr. Dickerson and his wife, Nancy, were a powerful couple, hosting politicians and Hollywood stars.

name: Sammy Lee
profession: First Asian-American Man to Earn Olympic Gold
headline: Sammy Lee, First Asian-American Man to Earn Olympic Gold, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Lee battled racial discrimination even after he became a physician, won three Olympic medals in diving and served in the Korean War.

name: Raynoma Gordy Singleton
headline: Raynoma Gordy Singleton, an Early Motown Force, Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. Singleton, Berry Gordy’s second wife and his partner in the label, helped run some operations, wrote arrangements, produced records and even signed Stevie Wonder.

name: Leonard B. Sand
profession: Judge in Landmark Yonkers Segregation Case
headline: Leonard B. Sand, Judge in Landmark Yonkers Segregation Case, Dies at 88
abstract: The case in which the federal judge found that city officials had segregated public housing and schools along racial lines stretched 27 years.

name: Jack Rudin
profession: Patriarch of Family of New York Developers
headline: Jack Rudin, Patriarch of Family of New York Developers, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Rudin was in the vanguard of a partnership of groups that helped spare the city from bankruptcy in the mid-1970s and figured prominently in its revival.

name: Margaret Whitton
headline: Margaret Whitton, ‘Major League’ Actress, Dies at 67
abstract: Ms. Whitton, who shifted to directing late in her career, was best known for her role as the owner of the Cleveland Indians, which played to her love of baseball.

name: Van Williams
headline: Van Williams, TV’s Green Hornet, Dies at 82
abstract: Before his most memorable television role as a masked vigilante, Mr. Williams played the detective Kenny Madison on two ABC series.

name: Robert R. Douglass
headline: Robert R. Douglass, Longtime Adviser to Rockefeller Family, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Douglass was counsel and secretary to Gov. Nelson A. Rockefeller of New York and worked closely with the family for decades, including as an executive at Chase Bank.

name: Rashaan Salaam
headline: Rashaan Salaam, Heisman Trophy Winner With Colorado, Dies at 42
abstract: Salaam, who was selected by the Chicago Bears in the first round of the 1995 N.F.L. draft, was plagued by injuries, fumbles and marijuana use.

name: Peter Vaughan
profession: Maester Aemon in Game of Thrones
headline: Peter Vaughan, Maester Aemon in ‘Game of Thrones,’ Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Vaughan had an acting career in films and British television for more than 50 years before his turn as the blind mentor to Jon Snow in the HBO series.

name: Luis Carlos Montalván
headline: Luis Carlos Montalván, Advocate for Soldiers With PTSD, Dies at 43
abstract: Mr. Montalván was an Iraq war veteran and best-selling author who toured the country with his service dog, Tuesday.

name: Nancy Mairs
profession: Wrote About Her Mental Illness and Multiple Sclerosis
headline: Nancy Mairs, Who Wrote About Her Mental Illness and Multiple Sclerosis, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Mairs chronicled her fears and hopes in intensely personal essays and memoirs, looking at her life, and her infirmities, with an unblinking eye.

name: Nguyen Ngoc Luong
headline: Nguyen Ngoc Luong, Times Guide in Vietnam War, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Luong’s small credits on photographs belied his other vital but unheralded journalistic contributions in bringing home the brutality of the war.

name: Doyle Owens
profession: Founder of the Unclaimed Baggage Center
headline: Doyle Owens, Founder of the Unclaimed Baggage Center, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Owens built his business on a traveler’s nightmare, selling the contents of lost luggage at his retail and tourist attraction in Scottsboro, Ala.

name: Dave Edwards
profession: Part of Dallas Cowboys Doomsday Defense
headline: Dave Edwards, Part of Dallas Cowboys’ ‘Doomsday Defense,’ Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Edwards, a linebacker known for his speed and aggressiveness, helped the team reach three Super Bowls and win the game in 1972.

name: Dave Edwards
headline: Dave Edwards, College Basketball Assist Wizard, Dies at 48
abstract: Edwards holds the single-season assist record for Texas A&M, where he starred for three years.

name: John Glenn
profession: American Hero of the Space Age
headline: John Glenn, American Hero of the Space Age, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Glenn was a symbol of the space age as the first American to orbit Earth, then became a national political figure representing Ohio in the Senate.

name: Greg Lake
headline: Greg Lake, of King Crimson and Emerson, Lake and Palmer, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Lake was instrumental in founding the band King Crimson, which is widely regarded as having produced the first progressive-rock album.

name: Paul Elvstrom
headline: Paul Elvstrom, 88, Olympian Who Powered Sailing by Leaning Over Waves
abstract: Elvstrom won four consecutive Olympic gold medals and popularized the sport’s technique.

name: Adolf Burger
profession: Forced by the Nazis to Counterfeit Cash
headline: Adolf Burger, Forced by the Nazis to Counterfeit Cash, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Burger was put to work in a concentration camp operation to create fake pound notes in a Nazi effort to destabilize the British economy.

name: Herb Hardesty
profession: Fats Dominos Saxophonist at Dawn of Rock n Roll
headline: Herb Hardesty, Fats Domino’s Saxophonist at Dawn of Rock ‘n’ Roll, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Hardesty played on the sessions that created hits like “I’m Walkin’,” “My Blue Heaven,” “Ain’t It a Shame” and “Let the Four Winds Blow.”

name: Mika Kurosawa
headline: Mika Kurosawa, ‘Godmother’ of Japanese Contemporary Dance, Dies at 59
abstract: Ms. Kurosawa, who was born into a dance family, was rebelliously devoted to her art, but not to the trappings of fame or popularity.

name: Ken Hechler
profession: West Virginia Populist and Coal Miners Champion
headline: Ken Hechler, West Virginia Populist and Coal Miners’ Champion, Dies at 102
abstract: First elected in 1958, Mr. Hechler, a Long Island native, fought to improve miners’ safety and health benefits while trying to curb strip mining as an environmental threat.

name: A. A. Gill
headline: A. A. Gill, Who Gleefully Skewered Britain’s Restaurants, Dies at 62
abstract: As an essayist and cultural critic for The Sunday Times, Mr. Gill laid stylishly malicious waste to superstar chefs, trendy restaurants and food fads.

name: Esma Redzepova
profession: Sang of Her Roma Heritage to Generations
headline: Esma Redzepova Dies at 73; Sang of Her Roma Heritage to Generations
abstract: Ms. Redzepova, who sang in 10 languages, helped to bring wider recognition and respect to Romany music.

name: E. R. Braithwaite
headline: E. R. Braithwaite, Author of ‘To Sir, With Love,’ Dies at 104
abstract: A Guyanese writer and diplomat, he recalled teaching in the East End of London in this memoir, which was the basis for a film starring Sidney Poitier.

name: Shirley Hazzard
headline: Shirley Hazzard, Novelist Who Charted Storm-Tossed Lives, Dies at 85
abstract: Australian-born, Ms. Hazzard spent decades in New York, writing award-winning fiction “stuffed with description so intellectually active as to be sometimes exhausting,” one critic said.

name: Thomas C. Schelling
headline: Thomas C. Schelling, Master Theorist of Nuclear Strategy, Dies at 95
abstract: The Nobel laureate used game theory to shed light on U.S. and Soviet actions and developed the theory of the “tipping point” to explain white flight.

name: Bob Krasnow
headline: Bob Krasnow, Revitalizer of Elektra Records, Dies at 82
abstract: The well-traveled music executive is credited with refreshing the label in the ’80s and ’90s, with acts like Metallica, Anita Baker and Björk.

name: Alan Thicke
headline: Alan Thicke, Reassuring Father on ‘Growing Pains,’ Dies at 69
abstract: In addition to acting, Mr. Thicke was a singer and songwriter who composed theme songs for numerous game shows and sitcoms.

name: Jim Lowe
headline: Jim Lowe, Radio D.J. and Singer, Dies at 93
abstract: On WNEW-AM and other stations, Mr. Lowe brought the American songbook to generations of listeners. He also had a No. 1 hit of his own in 1956.

name: Joe Ligon
profession: Gospel Singer With the Mighty Clouds of Joy
headline: Joe Ligon, Gospel Singer With the Mighty Clouds of Joy, Dies at 80
abstract: The group, aided by Mr. Ligon’s throbbing vocals, became one of the most successful gospel quartets of all time.

name: Javier Echevarría
headline: Bishop Javier Echevarría, Leader of Opus Dei, Dies at 84
abstract: Bishop Echevarría was the prelate of Opus Dei, the disciplined and influential global Roman Catholic organization, since 1994.

name: Rodney Smith
headline: Rodney Smith, Whimsical Photographer, Dies at 68
abstract: The people in his works often carried umbrellas and wore hats, or kissed atop taxi cabs. “I perceive my pictures as playing with time and space,” he said.

name: Halfdan Mahler
profession: Shifted W.H.O.s Focus to Primary Care
headline: Halfdan Mahler, Who Shifted W.H.O.’s Focus to Primary Care, Dies at 93
abstract: The director general of the World Health Organization from 1973 to 1988, Dr. Mahler acknowledged the group’s slowness in responding to AIDS.

name: Craig Sager
headline: Craig Sager, Colorful N.B.A. Sideline Reporter, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Sager was known as much for his outlandish outfits as for his brief interviews with basketball coaches and players on N.B.A. broadcasts.

name: Bill Usery
profession: Settled Wide Range of Labor Disputes
headline: Bill Usery, Who Settled Wide Range of Labor Disputes, Dies at 92
abstract: A welder and union official who became a mediator under two presidents, Mr. Usery reached deals for railway and postal workers, coal miners and football players.

name: Larry Colburn
headline: Larry Colburn, Who Helped Stop My Lai Massacre, Dies at 67
abstract: He intervened with two comrades to halt the massacre of unarmed Vietnamese civilians by United States soldiers in 1968.

name: Rose Evansky
headline: Rose Evansky, a Pioneer in Women’s Hairstyling, Dies at 94
abstract: Mrs. Evansky, a Jewish refugee from Nazi Germany, developed blow-dry styling in the 1960s at her London salon, and inadvertently created a revolution in hairdressing.

name: Henry J. Heimlich
headline: Dr. Henry J. Heimlich, Famous for Antichoking Technique, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Heimlich entered the pantheon of medical history with his maneuver but in later years often found himself at odds with a medical establishment skeptical of his claims.

name: Benjamin Gilman
headline: Benjamin Gilman, a New York Congressman for 30 Years, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Gilman was a chairman of the House International Relations Committee and a leading Republican critic of the Clinton administration’s foreign policy strategies.

name: Zsa Zsa Gabor
profession: Actress Famous for Her Glamour (and Her Marriages)
headline: Zsa Zsa Gabor, Actress Famous for Her Glamour (and Her Marriages), Dies at 99
abstract: Ms. Gabor put a luster on American celebrity with her self-parodying glamour and revolving-door millionaire marriages. She was 99.

name: William Hudnut
headline: William Hudnut, Mayor Who Transformed Indianapolis, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Under Mr. Hudnut, Indianapolis went from a sleepy Midwestern town to a thriving city, a transformation driven largely by a focus on professional sports.

name: Paulo Evaristo Arns
headline: Cardinal Paulo Evaristo Arns Dies at 95; Fought Torture in Brazil
abstract: The cardinal’s advocacy of human rights placed him in opposition to a military dictatorship; his leftist views put him at odds with the Vatican.

name: Louis Harris
profession: Pollster at Forefront of American Trends
headline: Louis Harris, Pollster at Forefront of American Trends, Dies at 95
abstract: From the 1950s into the ’90s, Mr. Harris not only gauged opinions, but sometimes helped make them, with his marketing advice to politicians and companies.

name: China Machado
headline: China Machado, Breakthrough Model Until the End, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Machado was the first nonwhite supermodel, and it’s a legacy the fashion industry has to wrestle with.

name: Esther Wilkins
headline: Esther Wilkins, Who Set Standards for Dental Hygienists, Dies at 100
abstract: Dr. Wilkins, who studied dentistry at a time when few women did, wrote an influential textbook in 1959 that is still used worldwide.

name: Gina Quattrochi
profession: Helped Provide Housing for AIDS Patients
headline: Gina Quattrochi, Who Helped Provide Housing for AIDS Patients, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Quattrochi served for 25 years as the AIDS Resource Center’s chief executive and was instrumental in building what became the nation’s largest housing resource for people living with AIDS.

name: Fran Jeffries
headline: Fran Jeffries, an Actress Who Performed a Sexy Samba in ‘The Pink Panther,’ Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. Jeffries was well known on the cabaret and Las Vegas circuit as the singing partner of Dick Haymes, her husband, when she got her first film role.

name: Dick Latessa
profession: Winner of a Tony for Hairspray
headline: Dick Latessa, Winner of a Tony for ‘Hairspray,’ Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Latessa appeared in several Broadway shows — like “Follies,” “Brighton Beach Memoirs” and “Damn Yankees” — as well as on television and in films.

name: Howard L. Bingham
headline: Howard L. Bingham, Muhammad Ali’s Longtime Photographer, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Bingham chronicled the boxer’s life for more than 50 years and displayed a particular flair for showing him away from the ring.

name: Sidney Drell
headline: Sidney Drell, Who Advised Presidents on Nuclear Weapons, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Drell served on a series of advisory groups that helped advance the technology of nuclear detection and shape the policy of nuclear deterrence.

name: Jens Risom
headline: Jens Risom, Modernist Designer Whose Furniture Still Has Legs, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Risom, a Danish immigrant, fused Scandinavian and rustic American influences in a celebrated armless chair that’s still selling 74 years later, and other modernist pieces for Knoll Studio.

name: Franca Sozzani
profession: Gave Italian Vogue a Daring Look and Voice
headline: Franca Sozzani Dies at 66; Gave Italian Vogue a Daring Look and Voice
abstract: In her 28-year direction of the magazine, she nurtured the careers of a generation of top fashion photographers, and didn’t shy from serious issues.

name: Michèle Morgan
headline: Michèle Morgan, the First ‘Best Actress’ at Cannes, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Morgan was just 26 when she starred as a blind woman in Jean Delannoy’s “Pastoral Symphony.” She and the film won honors at the first Cannes festival.

name: Marion Pritchard
profession: Risked Her Life to Rescue Jews From Nazis
headline: Marion Pritchard, Who Risked Her Life to Rescue Jews From Nazis, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Pritchard said that by the end of the war she had “lied, stolen, cheated, deceived and even killed” to shelter Jews in the Netherlands.

name: Kenneth Snelson
headline: Kenneth Snelson, Sculptor Who Fused Art, Science and Engineering, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Snelson applied a fascination with geometric forms to create works that, he said, examined the “wondrous essence of elementary structure.”

name: Piers J. Sellers
profession: Climate Scientist and Space Station Astronaut
headline: Piers J. Sellers, Climate Scientist and Space Station Astronaut, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Sellers was a leading figure in NASA’s scientific research programs, flying to the International Space Station on the space shuttle Atlantis in 2002 and 2010, and on Discovery in 2006.

name: Miruts Yifter
headline: Miruts Yifter, Ethiopian Who Ran to Two Olympic Golds, Dies at 72
abstract: He was known as Yifter the Shifter for the sudden bursts of speed that propelled him to wins in the 5,000- and 10,000-meter races at the 1980 Games in Moscow.

name: S. Newman Darby
headline: S. Newman Darby, Inventor of the Sailboard, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Darby created his invention, widely acknowledged as the first windsurfing craft, out of frustration because the waves on lakes were not big enough to surf on.

name: Léo Marjane
profession: Music Hall Star in Occupied France
headline: Léo Marjane, a Music Hall Star in Occupied France, Dies at 104
abstract: Ms. Marjane made the ballad “Alone Tonight” a signature song of the period.

name: Heinrich Schiff
headline: Heinrich Schiff, Master Cellist and Conductor, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Schiff held a revered place among the instrument’s leading players. “Schiff is a true cello animal,” the British cellist Natalie Clein, who studied with him, wrote.

name: Carrie Fisher
profession: Child of Hollywood and Star Wars Royalty
headline: Carrie Fisher, Child of Hollywood and ‘Star Wars’ Royalty, Dies at 60
abstract: Ms. Fisher channeled her struggles with depression and substance abuse into fiercely comic works, including the novel “Postcards From the Edge.”

name: Vera Rubin
profession: Opened Doors in Astronomy, and for Women
headline: Vera Rubin, 88, Dies; Opened Doors in Astronomy, and for Women
abstract: Dr. Rubin, who was awarded the National Medal of Science in 1993, ushered in the cosmic realization that most of the universe is invisible.

name: Gordie Tapp
profession: Hee Haw Regular of Pfft! You Was Gone Fame
headline: Gordie Tapp, ‘Hee Haw’ Regular of ‘Pfft! You Was Gone’ Fame, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Tapp seemed very much at home in the rural setting of “Hee Haw,” which was taped in Nashville, but he was from Canada.

name: Willa Kim
headline: Willa Kim, Designer of Fanciful Costumes, Dies at 99
abstract: Ms. Kim won Tony Awards for her designs in “Sophisticated Ladies” and “The Will Rogers Follies,” and worked in dance and opera as well.

name: Lella Vignelli
headline: Lella Vignelli, a Designer With a Spare, Elegant Style, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Vignelli and her husband, Massimo Vignelli, brought a bold, modernist aesthetic to a wide range of products and corporate brands.

name: Hans Tietmeyer
headline: Hans Tietmeyer, Banker Who Led German Transition to Euro, Dies at 85
abstract: As president of the Bundesbank, the central bank in Germany, Mr. Tietmeyer was a proponent of policies that prized price stability above all else.

name: Alphonse Mouzon
headline: Alphonse Mouzon, Jazz and Fusion Drummer, Dies at 68
abstract: The musician played in the first edition of the band Weather Report, and was a charter member of the Eleventh House.

name: Vesna Vulovic
headline: Vesna Vulovic, Flight Attendant Who Survived Jetliner Blast, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Vulovic, who wasn’t scheduled to be on the flight from Copenhagen to Belgrade in 1972, was the only one of 28 people to survive after plummeting thousands of feet onto a snowy hill.

name: Debbie Reynolds
headline: Debbie Reynolds, Wholesome Ingénue in 1950s Films, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Reynolds starred in “Singin’ in the Rain,” the classic MGM musical about 1920s moviemaking, in which she held her own with Gene Kelly and Donald O’Connor.

name: Edwin Goldwasser
headline: Edwin Goldwasser, Physicist Who Co-Founded Fermilab, Dies at 97
abstract: Dr. Goldwasser helped build one of the world’s most powerful particle accelerators and make Fermilab a leader in scientific advancements and collaborations.

name: Ed Reinecke
headline: Ed Reinecke, Lieutenant Governor Ensnared by Watergate, Dies at 92
abstract: The political career of Mr. Reinecke, a California congressman and a lieutenant governor under Ronald Reagan, was derailed by a 1974 perjury conviction.

name: George S. Irving
profession: Tony Winner and Voice of Heat Miser
headline: George S. Irving, Tony Winner and Voice of Heat Miser, Dies at 94
abstract: The actor appeared in many musicals and plays, and was a spokesman for White Owl cigars.

name: LaVell Edwards
headline: LaVell Edwards, Coach Who Led B.Y.U. to a Football Title, Dies at 86
abstract: Edwards, a onetime defensive coordinator, developed standout quarterbacks and innovative offensive schemes as a head coach and led Brigham Young to the 1984 national title.

name: Walter E. Mattson
profession: Former President of New York Times
headline: Walter E. Mattson, Former President of New York Times, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Mattson, a production executive who had once been a printer, helped transform the newspaper with innovative labor agreements and new technologies.

name: Cyril D. Tyson
profession: Fought Poverty in a Turbulent Era
headline: Cyril D. Tyson Dies at 89; Fought Poverty in a Turbulent Era
abstract: Mr. Tyson led antipoverty programs from inside and outside government in New York City and Newark during the racially tense 1960s.

name: Arthur H. Cash
headline: Arthur H. Cash, Writer of British Biographies, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Cash wrote about the English novelist Laurence Sterne, and his biography of the 18th-century English radical John Wilkes was a Pulitzer finalist.

name: Robert L. Hulseman
headline: Robert L. Hulseman, Inventor of the Solo Cup, Dies at 84
abstract: In addition to creating the popular plastic cup, Mr. Hulseman helped to invent a coffee cup lid that may be just as prevalent.

name: Tyrus Wong
profession: Bambi Artist Thwarted by Racial Bias
headline: Tyrus Wong, ‘Bambi’ Artist Thwarted by Racial Bias, Dies at 106
abstract: A Hollywood studio artist, painter, printmaker, calligrapher and maker of fantastical kites, Mr. Wong was one of the most celebrated Chinese-American artists of the 20th century.

name: F. Ross Johnson
headline: F. Ross Johnson, Symbol of ’80s Corporate Excess, Dies at 85
abstract: As chief executive of RJR Nabisco, Mr. Johnson instigated the era-defining takeover struggle chronicled in the best-selling book “Barbarians at the Gate.”

name: Allan Williams
headline: Allan Williams, First Manager of the Beatles, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Williams booked a long series of shows in Germany in 1960, forcing the band to expand its repertoire and sharpen its stagecraft.

name: Huston Smith
headline: Huston Smith, Author of ‘The World’s Religions,’ Dies at 97
abstract: Professor Smith, whose work has been a college fixture for decades, pursued enlightenment in churches, monasteries and even Timothy Leary’s living room.

name: Michel Déon
headline: Michel Déon, Novelist Who Tapped the French Experience, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Déon was complicated and contrarian, his wit and depth coming through in works like “A Purple Taxi” and “The Foundling Boy.”

name: William Christopher
headline: William Christopher, Father Mulcahy on ‘M*A*S*H,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Christopher, who started his career on and Off Broadway, was best known for playing a soft-spoken chaplain at an Army hospital during the Korean War.

name: Joyce Appleby
profession: Historian of Capitalism and American Identity
headline: Joyce Appleby, Historian of Capitalism and American Identity, Is Dead at 87
abstract: She put liberalism at the center of understanding the ideology of the revolutionary generation.

name: John Berger
headline: John Berger, Provocative Art Critic, Dies at 90
abstract: The British essayist, novelist and screenwriter’s book and TV series “Ways of Seeing” declared war on traditional ways of thinking about art.

name: Hilarion Capucci
profession: Archbishop Jailed for Aiding Palestinian Militants
headline: Hilarion Capucci, Archbishop Jailed for Aiding Palestinian Militants, Dies at 94
abstract: As the head of the Greek Catholic Church in Jerusalem, he was charged with smuggling arms to help Palestinians. The Vatican helped secure his release.

name: Anthony B. Atkinson
headline: Anthony B. Atkinson, Economist Who Pioneered Study of Inequality, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Atkinson developed new ways to measure disparities in income and wealth using historical records, long before inequality became the major issue it is today.

name: Jean Vuarnet
headline: Jean Vuarnet, a Downhill Skiing Innovator, Dies at 83
abstract: At the 1960 Winter Olympics, Mr. Vuarnet unveiled the tuck — a radical new skiing position that now seems obvious — and rode it to a gold medal.

name: Karel Husa
headline: Karel Husa, Pulitzer Prize-Winning Composer, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Husa also won the Grawemeyer Award for Music Composition, and was perhaps best known for “Music for Prague 1968.”

name: Georges Prêtre
headline: Georges Prêtre, French Conductor Known for Interpretation, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Prêtre, who led many of the world’s leading orchestras in a 70-year career, developed a strong rapport with Maria Callas and was a favorite in Vienna.

name: Frances Ann Carr
profession: One of the Last Three Shakers
headline: Sister Frances Ann Carr, One of the Last Three Shakers, Dies at 89
abstract: Sister Frances was a pillar of a Christian group whose members, who practice celibacy, have lived communally in the United States since the late 1700s.

name: Milt Schmidt
profession: Hall of Fame Center for Bruins
headline: Milt Schmidt, Hall of Fame Center for Bruins, Dies at 98
abstract: The N.H.L.’s points leader in 1939-40 and most valuable player in 1950-51, he was Boston’s career leader in goals and a two-time Stanley Cup winner when he retired in 1954.

name: Derek Parfit
headline: Derek Parfit, Philosopher Who Explored Identity and Moral Choice, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Parfit, who was associated with All Souls College at Oxford for his entire career, published seldom, but his works were ambitious and influential.

name: Jeremy Stone
profession: Influenced Arms Control During Cold War
headline: Jeremy Stone, Who Influenced Arms Control During Cold War, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Stone argued that if the Soviets could be persuaded not to build a missile defense system, then the United States could be persuaded to do the same.

name: Jill Saward
profession: Advocate for Victims of Sexual Assault
headline: Jill Saward, Advocate for Victims of Sexual Assault, Dies at 51
abstract: Ms. Saward was a British survivor of rape who waived her right to anonymity and called on other victims to come forward to share their ordeal.

name: Willie Evans
profession: Was Barred From a Bowl Game Because of His Color
headline: Willie Evans, Who Was Barred From a Bowl Game Because of His Color, Dies at 79
abstract: Evans, a star halfback, was one of two University of Buffalo players turned down for the Tangerine Bowl after an 8-1 season in 1958. The team rejected the bid.

name: Albert P. Brewer
headline: Albert P. Brewer, a Former Governor of Alabama, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Brewer took over as governor after the death of Gov. Lurleen Wallace, who had been elected as a proxy for her husband, the segregationist George C. Wallace.

name: Mário Soares
headline: Mário Soares Dies at 92; Guided Portugal’s Shift to Democracy
abstract: Mr. Soares, a Socialist who served as Portugal’s prime minister and president, played a central role in reshaping the country after its dictatorship fell in the 1970s.

name: Nat Hentoff
headline: Nat Hentoff, Journalist and Social Commentator, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Hentoff was an author, journalist, jazz critic and civil libertarian who called himself a troublemaker and proved it with a shelf of books and a mountain of essays.

name: Om Puri
headline: Om Puri, a Film Actor Who Rose With the Indian New Wave, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Puri appeared in some 300 films, most of them in India. He was known in the West mainly for his roles in British productions.

name: Michael Chamberlain
profession: Father of Baby Killed by a Dingo in Australia
headline: Michael Chamberlain, Father of Baby Killed by a Dingo in Australia, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Chamberlain and his first wife fought for decades to prove that the animal was responsible for their daughter’s disappearance.

name: Clare Hollingworth
headline: Clare Hollingworth, Reporter Who Broke News of World War II, Dies at 105
abstract: In 1939, Ms. Hollingworth was less than a week into her first job as a correspondent when she spotted troops and tanks concealed in a valley.

name: Roman Herzog
headline: Roman Herzog, Germany’s President in 1990s, Is Dead at 82
abstract: A former judge, Mr. Herzog encouraged economic overhauls and a remembrance of the Holocaust during his presidency, the second since reunification.

name: Roy Innis
profession: Black Activist With a Right-Wing Bent
headline: Roy Innis, Black Activist With a Right-Wing Bent, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Innis, the leader of CORE, took a go-it-alone approach to black empowerment and had no use for desegregation and affirmative action.

name: Steven McDonald
headline: Steven McDonald, Paralyzed Officer Who Championed Forgiveness, Dies at 59
abstract: The New York City police officer publicly forgave the 15-year-old boy who shot him in Central Park in 1986 and stayed in the public eye for his spirit in the face of adversity.

name: Peter Nowell
headline: Dr. Peter Nowell, Who Helped Transform Cancer Research, Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Nowell and a colleague discovered the first genetic defect proven to cause cancer, which led to major advances by other scientists decades later.

name: Vo Quy
profession: Father of Environmental Conservation in Vietnam
headline: Vo Quy, Father of Environmental Conservation in Vietnam, Dies at 87
abstract: Dr. Quy helped create Vietnam’s first national park in the 1960s and served as an intermediary as the country and the United States moved to address the effects of Agent Orange.

name: Jewel Plummer Cobb
headline: Jewel Plummer Cobb, 92, Dies; Led a California Campus
abstract: Dr. Cobb, the first black female president of Cal State, Fullerton, had been denied a New York college post in a move that led to bias accusations.

name: Christopher Byron
profession: Financial Writer and Author of Martha Inc
headline: Christopher Byron, Financial Writer and Author of ‘Martha Inc.,’ Dies at 72
abstract: Long before movies like “The Wolf of Wall Street” were popular fare, Mr. Byron was revealing the seamy underside of business in books about Martha Stewart and Time Inc.

name: Oliver Smithies
headline: Oliver Smithies, Tinkerer Who Transformed Genetics and Won a Nobel, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Smithies discovered a powerful tool for identifying the roles of individual genes in health and disease.

name: Martha Swope
profession: Etched Dance and Theater History in Photographs
headline: Martha Swope, 88, Who Etched Dance and Theater History in Photographs, Dies
abstract: Ms. Swope produced hundreds of thousands of images of performers in action, and by the time she retired, her studio contained more than a million images.

name: Leslie W. Dunbar
headline: Leslie W. Dunbar, White Civil-Rights Leader of the ’60s, Dies at 95
abstract: Historians compared him to other leading white liberals like Ralph McGill, the anti-segregation publisher of The Atlanta Constitution.

name: John M. Richman
headline: John M. Richman, Chief of Kraft Who Oversaw Merger With Philip Morris, Dies at 89
abstract: He turned what he considered an unacceptable offer of $11.5 billion into a $13.1 billion takeover to create the world’s largest consumer goods producer at the time.

name: Victor Lownes
headline: Victor Lownes, 88, Playboy Executive Who Shaped Company’s Libertine Ethic
abstract: A professed rake and a friend of Hugh Hefner’s, Mr. Lownes helped to develop the chain of Playboy Clubs.

name: Laurie Carlos
headline: Laurie Carlos, Actress in ‘For Colored Girls,’ Dies at 67
abstract: The inner lives of black women was often the focus of Ms. Carlos, a multifaceted award winner who was also a writer and director.

name: Levi Felix
headline: Levi Felix, a Proponent of Disconnecting From Technology, Dies at 32
abstract: Mr. Felix championed the virtues of unplugging from smartphones and co-founded Digital Detox retreats and camps to help people reconnect in real life.

name: Antony Armstrong-Jones
headline: Antony Armstrong-Jones, Photographer and Earl of Snowdon, Dies at 86
abstract: He married Princess Margaret, the sister of Queen Elizabeth II, in 1960, and plunged into a life of privileges, parties, quarrels and infidelities that ended in divorce 18 years later.

name: William Peter Blatty
headline: William Peter Blatty, Author of ‘The Exorcist,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Blatty’s novel about a girl possessed by a demon created the theological-horror genre, became a hit movie and destroyed its author’s hopes of ever writing comedy again.

name: Buddy Greco
headline: Buddy Greco, Singer Who Had That Swing, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Greco, who started with Benny Goodman, came into his own as a Las Vegas lounge singer with a propulsive, swinging style.

name: Zhou Youguang
profession: Made Writing Chinese as Simple as ABC
headline: Zhou Youguang, Who Made Writing Chinese as Simple as ABC, Dies at 111
abstract: Mr. Zhou created the Pinyin system of Romanized Chinese, which vastly increased literacy in China and eased the agonies of foreigners studying the language.

name: Tony Rosato
headline: Tony Rosato, of 1981-82 ‘Saturday Night Live’ Cast, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Rosato’s comedy career, which began in Toronto with the Second City troupe, ground to a halt because of mental illness and his incarceration.

name: Conservationist Bud Lilly
headline: Conservationist Bud Lilly, ‘a Trout’s Best Friend,’ Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Lilly, a fly fisherman, outfitter and retailer, came to embrace catch and release in order to protect the fish population in his native Montana.

name: Jimmy Snuka
headline: Jimmy Snuka, Ex-Pro Wrestler Known as Superfly, Dies at 73
abstract: An acrobatic performer in the ring, he was charged with murder late in life, but the case was thrown out shortly before his death because he was declared mentally unfit.

name: Kevin Starr
headline: Kevin Starr, Prolific Chronicler of California’s History, Dies at 76
abstract: In an eight-part opus about his home state, Mr. Starr showed how “the California of fact and the California of imagination shape and reshape each other.”

name: Dick Gautier
profession: Played a Rock Star in Bye Bye Birdie
headline: Dick Gautier, Who Played a Rock Star in ‘Bye Bye Birdie,’ Is Dead
abstract: The comic actor, who was also known for his role as a robot on the TV show “Get Smart,” was 85.

name: Hans Berliner
headline: Hans Berliner, Master Chess Player and Programmer, Dies at 87
abstract: The ex-computer science professor, a correspondence chess champion, won what has been called one of the greatest games ever. It lasted three years.

name: Eugene Cernan
profession: Last Human to Walk on Moon
headline: Eugene Cernan, Last Human to Walk on Moon, Dies at 82
abstract: A ferocious competitor, Mr. Cernan rocketed into space three times, went to the moon twice and shattered aerospace records on the Earth and the moon.

name: James S. Ackerman
profession: Author of Enduring Books on Architecture
headline: James S. Ackerman, Author of Enduring Books on Architecture, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Ackerman’s passion for architecture was kindled while serving in Italy with the Army. His studies of Michelangelo and Palladio are classics in the field.

name: Nicky Scarfo
headline: Nicky Scarfo, Mob Boss Who Plundered Atlantic City in the ’80s, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Scarfo purged two dozen fellow mobsters during his reign in Philadelphia and South Jersey and milked casino profits in Atlantic City.

name: Lois Dickson Rice
headline: Lois Dickson Rice, Trailblazing Executive Behind Pell Grants, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Rice, who started life as a janitor’s daughter, helped persuade Congress to provide federal subsidies to tens of millions of needy college students.

name: George Beall
headline: George Beall, Prosecutor Who Brought Down Agnew, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Beall, as United States attorney for Maryland, led the prosecution on bribery charges of Vice President Spiro T. Agnew that led to Mr. Agnew’s resignation in 1973.

name: Roberta Peters
headline: Roberta Peters, Soprano With a Dramatic Entrance, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Peters, who sang with the Metropolitan Opera for 35 years, was 20 when she was catapulted to stardom as a last-minute substitute in “Don Giovanni.”

name: William Onyeabor
headline: William Onyeabor, Reclusive African Electro-Funk Pioneer, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Onyeabor, whose music reached a new audience decades after he created it, composed, played and produced hypnotic electronic tracks infused with unmistakably African elements.

name: Wayne Barrett
profession: Fierce Muckraker at The Village Voice
headline: Wayne Barrett, Fierce Muckraker at The Village Voice, Dies at 71
abstract: In 37 years at The Village Voice, Mr. Barrett took on New York’s builders, landlords and politicians, among them Donald J. Trump and Rudolph W. Giuliani.

name: Henry J. Foner
profession: Labor Leader Accused of Communist Ties
headline: Henry J. Foner, Labor Leader Accused of Communist Ties, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Foner, who was the uncle of the historian Eric Foner, led the fur and leather workers union in New York. He and his brothers were accused of belonging to subversive groups.

name: James S. Vlasto
headline: James S. Vlasto, Adviser to New York Politicians, Dies at 82
abstract: Over six decades, Mr. Vlasto worked for both Democrats and Republicans, including Gov. Hugh L. Carey, Senator Jacob K. Javits and Representative Richard L. Ottinger.

name: William A. Hilliard
headline: William A. Hilliard, 89, Pioneering Black Journalist, Dies
abstract: Having faced racial discrimination, Mr. Hilliard, who climbed the ranks at The Oregonian to become editor in chief, made it a focus to not perpetuate stereotypes in news writing.

name: Paula Dell
headline: Paula Dell, Pioneering Movie Stuntwoman, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Ms. Dell worked as a stunt double in films like “Thoroughly Modern Millie” and “The Poseidon Adventure” and in the TV series “Charlie’s Angels.”

name: Charles Bobo Shaw
headline: Charles Bobo Shaw, Avant-Garde Jazz Drummer, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Shaw, from St. Louis, became a vital part of New York’s jazz vanguard, leading the Human Arts Ensemble and playing with Cecil Taylor and Anthony Braxton.

name: Brenda Barnes
headline: Brenda Barnes, Pepsi Chief Who Spurred a Work-Life Debate, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Barnes was a two-time corporate chief executive whose decision to leave a top job at Pepsi-Cola inspired a national debate about women juggling career and family.

name: Miguel Ferrer
profession: Celebrated as a Film and TV Tough Guy
headline: Miguel Ferrer, Celebrated as a Film and TV Tough Guy, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Ferrer had recently reprised his role as the F.B.I. forensics expert Albert Rosenfield in a revival of “Twin Peaks,” which is to start in May.

name: Maggie Roche
headline: Maggie Roche, Who Harmonized With Her Singing Sisters, Dies at 65
abstract: Best known for her work with her siblings Terre and Suzzy, she wrote songs that could be droll or diaristic, full of unexpected melodic turns.

name: Peter Abrahams
headline: Peter Abrahams, a South African Who Wrote of Apartheid and Identity, Dies at 97
abstract: The journalist and novelist’s moral center of gravity was located in the country he left at age 20. His 1946 novel, “Mine Boy,” drew global attention.

name: Ronald Webster
headline: Ronald Webster, Leader Who Plotted Anguilla Revolution, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Webster demanded to be severed from a three-island federation created by Britain in 1967 and insisted on embracing the mother country rather than breaking with it.

name: Charlie Liteky
profession: Returned Medal of Honor in Protest
headline: Charlie Liteky, 85, Dies; Returned Medal of Honor in Protest
abstract: Awarded the medal for bravery in Vietnam, Mr. Liteky later left it in an envelope addressed to President Ronald Reagan in protest of American policy in Central America.

name: Harold Hayes
profession: Survivor of Secret World War II Odyssey
headline: Harold Hayes, Survivor of Secret World War II Odyssey, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Hayes was among a group of noncombatants stranded behind enemy lines in Albania in 1943, hiding in caves, near starvation and hunted by German patrols.

name: Vicki Lansky
profession: Author of Advice Books for Parents
headline: Vicki Lansky, Author of Advice Books for Parents, Dies at 75
abstract: She wrote more than 30 books, including a healthful cookbook and a divorce guide, in addition to newspaper and magazine columns and a newsletter.

name: Eddie Kamae
profession: Innovator and a Historian on Four Strings
headline: Eddie Kamae, an Innovator and a Historian on Four Strings, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Kamae was one of the most influential Hawaiian musicians of the second half of the 20th century, at once an innovator and a diligent steward of folkloric customs.

name: Anthony Colombo
profession: Helped Get Mafia Out of The Godfather
headline: Anthony Colombo Dies at 71; Helped Get ‘Mafia’ Out of ‘The Godfather’
abstract: As vice president of the Italian-American Civil Rights League, the son of a mobster worked to keep Italian organized crime references out of the movie.

name: Byron Dobell
headline: Byron Dobell, Whose Editing Helped Change Journalism, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Dobell — an editor at Time-Life, Esquire and New York magazine — played a pivotal role in the careers of Tom Wolfe, Mario Puzo and other writers.

name: Lee O’Denat
headline: Lee O’Denat, Whose Hip-Hop Website Caught Many Eyes, Dies at 43
abstract: Mr. O’Denat’s WorldStarHipHop.com became one of the 250 most-visited sites in the United States, driven by its raw footage of street life.

name: Mary Tyler Moore
profession: Incarnated the Modern Woman on TV
headline: Mary Tyler Moore, Who Incarnated the Modern Woman on TV, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Moore was best known as the spunky professional Mary Richards on “The Mary Tyler Moore Show” and as Laura Petrie, the wife of a comedy writer, on “The Dick Van Dyke Show.”

name: Harry Middleton
headline: Harry Middleton, Ex-Speechwriter Who Led L.B.J. Library, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Middleton, the first director of Johnson’s presidential library, encouraged Lady Bird Johnson to let the public to hear her husband’s secret White House tapes.

name: Jaki Liebezeit
headline: Jaki Liebezeit, Influential Drummer for Can, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Liebezeit’s playing was a foundation of a stripped-down movement eventually categorized as krautrock.

name: Phyllis Harrison-Ross
headline: Phyllis Harrison-Ross, Mental Health Pioneer, Dies at 80
abstract: Dr. Harrison-Ross was an early leader in designing therapies for children with a combination of severe developmental, emotional and physical disabilities.

name: Robert Garcia
headline: Robert Garcia Dies at 84; Bronx Congressman Undone by Scandal
abstract: Mr. Garcia was an advocate for poor Hispanic and black people, but his political career was toppled in the Wedtech corruption case.

name: Stephen P. Cohen
profession: Secret Broker of Mideast Peace Talks
headline: Stephen P. Cohen, Secret Broker of Mideast Peace Talks, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Cohen arranged the first direct and informal talks between the Israeli government and Yasir Arafat, the Palestine Liberation Organization leader.

name: Stephen F. Cohen
headline: Stephen F. Cohen, Influential Historian of Russia, Dies at 81
abstract: He chronicled Stalin’s tyrannies and the collapse of the Soviet Union, and he was an enthusiastic admirer of Mikhail Gorbachev.

name: Mike Connors
headline: Mike Connors, Long-Running TV Sleuth in ‘Mannix,’ Dies at 91
abstract: The actor was best known for his role in “Mannix,” which started in 1967 and drew criticism for its violent content but became the most popular crime series of its era.

name: Arthur Rosenfeld
headline: Arthur Rosenfeld, Zealous Champion of Energy Efficiency, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Rosenfeld’s work, first embraced in California in the 1970s, gained national attention and helped lay the foundation for federal rules in place today.

name: J.S.G. Boggs
headline: J.S.G. Boggs, Artist, Dies at 62; He Made Money. Literally.
abstract: A man who used art as currency and hoped bills would be appreciated for their artistic merit. Law enforcement agencies in several countries took a different view.

name: Chuck Stewart
headline: Chuck Stewart, Jazz Photographer, Dies at 89; You’ve Seen His Album Covers
abstract: Mr. Stewart created an archive of some 800,000 negatives, and by his count his photographs appeared on the covers of at least 2,000 albums.

name: Barbara Hale
headline: Barbara Hale, Who Played Perry Mason’s Loyal Secretary, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Hale won an Emmy for her portrayal of the intrepid Della Street on the “Perry Mason” courtroom series, a role that defined her career.

name: John Hurt
profession: British Actor Hailed for His Shape-Shifting Roles
headline: John Hurt, British Actor Hailed for His Shape-Shifting Roles, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Hurt was nominated for an Academy Award for his portrayal of the title role in the 1980 film “The Elephant Man.”

name: Allan Steinfeld
headline: Allan Steinfeld, Who Modernized New York City Marathon, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Steinfeld used his scientific background to modernize the technical operations of the race and eventually became head of its parent organization.

name: Emma Tennant
profession: Wrote Beyond the Fringe of Realism
headline: Emma Tennant, Who Wrote Beyond the Fringe of Realism, Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. Tennant said she found her footing after discovering writers whose anti-realist qualities dovetailed with her love of myth, magic and dream.

name: Brunhilde Pomsel
profession: Goebbelss Secretary and Witness to Nazis Fall
headline: Brunhilde Pomsel, Goebbels’s Secretary and Witness to Nazis’ Fall, Dies at 106
abstract: Ms. Pomsel was the private secretary of the propaganda minister Joseph Goebbels and was one of Adolf Hitler’s retinue in his final days in a Berlin bunker.

name: Masaya Nakamura
headline: Masaya Nakamura, Whose Company Created Pac-Man, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Nakamura made a business of amusement, starting with wooden horses and culminating with the creation of a company that developed one of the most successful video games ever.

name: Paul Ornstein
headline: Paul Ornstein, 92, Psychoanalyst and Holocaust Survivor, Dies
abstract: Mr. Ornstein and his wife, whom he met as a teenager in Hungary, were leading proponents of a psychoanalytic theory called self-psychology.

name: Max Wilcox
headline: Max Wilcox, Grammy-Winning Record Producer, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Wilcox was called a musical collaborator by the pianist Arthur Rubinstein.

name: Emmanuelle Riva
profession: Star of Hiroshima Mon Amour and Amour
headline: Emmanuelle Riva, Star of ‘Hiroshima Mon Amour’ and ‘Amour,’ Dies at 89
abstract: A French New Wave star who a half-century later was the oldest person nominated for an Oscar for best lead actor or actress.

name: John Wetton
profession: Rocker With King Crimson and Asia
headline: John Wetton, Rocker With King Crimson and Asia, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Wetton, a technically adept bassist with a smooth tenor voice, adapted the progressive rock of his earlier bands into later mainstream hits.

name: Bernard Redmont
profession: Told World of North Vietnams Call for Peace
headline: Bernard Redmont Dies at 98; Told World of North Vietnam’s Call for Peace
abstract: Mr. Redmont, blacklisted during the McCarthy period, was a journalist in Paris in 1968 when he broke the news about the willingness to begin talks.

name: Lennart Nilsson
headline: Lennart Nilsson, Photographer Who Unveiled the Invisible, Dies at 94
abstract: An innovative Swede, his micro-cameras traced the development of an embryo in a celebrated 1965 photo spread in Life magazine.

name: Bharati Mukherjee
headline: Bharati Mukherjee, Writer of Immigrant Life, Dies at 76
abstract: Her award-winning collection “The Middleman and Other Stories” and several of her novels explored internal culture clashes with characters who asked “Who am I?”

name: Frank Pellegrino Sr.
profession: Proudly Rebuffed Would-Be Diners at Raos
headline: Frank Pellegrino Sr., 72, Is Dead; Proudly Rebuffed Would-Be Diners at Rao’s
abstract: Mr. Pellegrino is said to have denied Warren Buffett entry to the East Harlem restaurant by crooning, “I’ve got all the riches, baby, one man can claim.”

name: Herb Oscar Anderson
headline: Herb Oscar Anderson, Crooning D.J. for WABC-AM, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Anderson, who worked for a Top 40 station during the 1960s, was known for his signature style and singing “Hello Again” each morning to his listeners.

name: Étienne Tshisekedi
headline: Étienne Tshisekedi, Congo Opposition Leader for Decades, Dies at 84
abstract: He was the most powerful opposition figure still operating inside the Democratic Republic of Congo, a nation plagued by violence and staggering corruption.

name: Harold Rosen
profession: Ushered in the Era of Communication Satellites
headline: Harold Rosen, Who Ushered in the Era of Communication Satellites, Dies at 90
