abstract: Mr. Rosen’s legacy as an electrical engineer and inventor is the roughly 600 geostationary satellites that handle TV signals and other data.

name: Harry Mathews
headline: Harry Mathews, Idiosyncratic Writer, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Mathews was a novelist, poet and essayist who was confounding and captivating in whatever language he was working in.

name: Kevin Geer
headline: Kevin Geer, Known for Stage Roles, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Geer had an outsize persona onstage and a more contained presence in films.

name: H. Boyd Woodruff
headline: H. Boyd Woodruff, Microbiologist Who Paved Way for Antibiotics, Dies at 99
abstract: Dr. Woodruff was instrumental in isolating microbes that led to the development of streptomycin, the miracle cure used to treat tuberculosis and other diseases.

name: Dore Ashton
headline: Dore Ashton, Art Critic Who Embraced and Inhabited Modernism, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Ashton wrote sweeping histories and intimate studies devoted to individual artists, especially those in the world of Abstract Expressionism.

name: Marta Becket
headline: Marta Becket, Dancer Who Built a Theater in the Desert, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Becket, a ballerina and Broadway dancer, stopped in 1967 at the tiny town of Desert Valley Junction, Calif., and stayed, building a performance center in the Mojave.

name: Walter Hautzig
headline: Walter Hautzig, Pianist Whose Talent Helped Him Flee Nazis, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Hautzig, who settled in the United States, went on to perform around the world as a good-will ambassador.

name: Lorenzo Servitje
profession: Founder of the Worlds Biggest Bakery
headline: Lorenzo Servitje, a Founder of the World’s Biggest Bakery, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Servitje helped build Grupo Bimbo, a Mexican conglomerate whose trademarks include Wonder Bread, Sara Lee and Entenmann’s.

name: John Platt
headline: John Platt, C.I.A. Officer Who Befriended K.G.B. Agent, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Platt, trying to recruit a Cold War foe to spy for the United States, succeeded only in becoming friends with him, only to see their friendship betrayed by a Russian mole.

name: Irwin Corey
headline: Irwin Corey, Comedian and ‘Foremost Authority,’ Dies at 102
abstract: Mr. Corey inhabited many characters but was best known for his alter ego, a zany “professor,” and for his left-wing politics.

name: Joost van der Westhuizen
headline: Joost van der Westhuizen, South African Rugby Legend, Dies at 45
abstract: Van der Westhuizen, who played scrumhalf and retired in 2003, scored 38 tries for South Africa, still the scoring record for his position.

name: Alec McCowen
headline: Alec McCowen, British Actor Who Played Saint and Fool, Dies at 91
abstract: In a half-century career that spanned film, TV and theater, Mr. McCowen’s greatest triumphs were on the stage. But movie audiences knew him as well.

name: Howard Frank Mosher
headline: Howard Frank Mosher, Whose Novels Evoked Hardscrabble Vermont, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Mosher’s fictional Kingdom County, home to whiskey runners and farmers, was a fertile setting for his works, some of which were made into movies.

name: Tzvetan Todorov
profession: Literary Theorist and Historian of Evil
headline: Tzvetan Todorov, Literary Theorist and Historian of Evil, Dies at 77
abstract: A prolific Bulgarian-French scholar, Mr. Todorov published widely on the moral consequences of colonialism, racism and genocide.

name: Richard Hatch
headline: Richard Hatch, Who Starred in ‘Battlestar Galactica,’ Dies at 71
abstract: He played Captain Apollo, a fighter pilot, in the original 1970s television series and later a political leader, Tom Zarek, in a reboot of the series in 2004.

name: William Melvin Kelley
headline: William Melvin Kelley, Who Explored Race in Experimental Novels, Is Dead at 79
abstract: The author of “A Different Drummer” and “Dunfords Travels Everywheres” was compared to Faulkner and Joyce.

name: Henry-Louis de La Grange
headline: Henry-Louis de La Grange, Mahler Authority, Is Dead at 92
abstract: A Parisian educated in France and the United States, Professor de La Grange was inspired to pursue his life’s work after a Carnegie Hall concert in 1945.

name: Barbara Gelb
headline: Barbara Gelb, Author, Playwright and Journalist, Dies at 91
abstract: Mrs. Gelb wrote several books, the best known being a weighty biography of Eugene O’Neill on which she collaborated with her husband.

name: Hans Rosling
headline: Hans Rosling, Swedish Doctor and Pop-Star Statistician, Dies at 68
abstract: Inviting animated visualizations and prosaic props (like apples and Lego plastic blocks) defined him as a funky philosopher rather than a geeky professor.

name: Barbara Harlow
profession: Scholar on Perils of Resistance Writing
headline: Barbara Harlow, Scholar on Perils of Resistance Writing, Dies at 68
abstract: Professor Harlow believed that imaginative writing was a way to gain control over “the historical and cultural record.”

name: Lev Navrozov
headline: Lev Navrozov, Literary Translator and Soviet Dissident, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Navrozov, pugnacious and passionate, was allowed to emigrate to the United States, where he wrote prolifically on Soviet affairs and American politics.

name: Svend Asmussen
headline: Svend Asmussen, an Early Master of Jazz Violin, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Asmussen, among the first to carve a place for the violin in the jazz catalog, played with, among other musicians, Duke Ellington, Benny Goodman and David Grisman.

name: Ljubisa Beara
headline: Ljubisa Beara, Who Oversaw Massacre at Srebrenica, Dies at 77
abstract: Colonel Beara, a Bosnian Serb military officer, was serving a life sentence for his part in the murders of up to 8,000 Muslim men and boys over a five-day period in 1995.

name: Mike Ilitch
profession: Little Caesars Founder and Detroit Sports Owner
headline: Mike Ilitch, Little Caesars Founder and Detroit Sports Owner, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Ilitch, who founded the Little Caesars pizza chain in 1959, went on to purchase the Detroit Red Wings of the N.H.L. and the Detroit Tigers of M.L.B.

name: Nicolai Gedda
headline: Nicolai Gedda, Celebrated Opera Tenor, Dies at 91
abstract: The Swedish singer rose from a poor childhood to become a renowned opera star in Europe and the United States.

name: Buchi Emecheta
headline: Buchi Emecheta, Nigerian Novelist, Dies at 72
abstract: In novels like “Second-Class Citizen” and “The Bride Price,” Ms. Emecheta described the difficulties African women faced in negotiating traditional roles in a modern age.

name: Leonard Perroots
headline: Leonard Perroots, General Who Defused Nuclear Crisis With Soviets, Dies at 83
abstract: He saw the signs of an elevated Soviet military alert in Eastern Europe but decided not to respond, perhaps preventing a spiral into nuclear war.

name: Raymond Smullyan
headline: Raymond Smullyan, Puzzle-Creating Logician, Dies at 97
abstract: Whether it was in books or in conversation, Mr. Smullyan had a knack for adding a dash of whimsy to the logic puzzles he devised.

name: Peter Mansfield
headline: Peter Mansfield, M.R.I. Pioneer and Nobel Laureate, Dies at 83
abstract: Dr. Mansfield’s discoveries enabled doctors to diagnose and examine injuries without exposing the patient to radiation or cutting open the body.

name: Miles Cahn
headline: Miles Cahn, Co-Founder of Coach Handbags, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Cahn founded the company with his wife, Lillian, in New York City in 1961. They sold the upscale handbag business in 1985 for a reported $30 million.

name: Harvey Lichtenstein
profession: Led Brooklyn Academy of Musics Rebirth
headline: Harvey Lichtenstein, Who Led Brooklyn Academy of Music’s Rebirth, Dies at 87
abstract: Serving 32 years as its president and executive producer, Mr. Lichtenstein reorganized BAM, and gave it a renewed purpose as a center for the performing arts.

name: Al Jarreau
headline: Al Jarreau, Singer Who Spanned Jazz, Pop and R&B Worlds, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Jarreau’s eclectic vocal talents created a personal style that won him six Grammy Awards across three categories.

name: Harold Moore
profession: Vietnam Heroism Was Depicted in Film
headline: Lt. Gen. Harold Moore, Whose Vietnam Heroism Was Depicted in Film, Dies at 94
abstract: General Moore wrote of the bloody 1965 battle in a best-selling book, “We Were Soldiers Once ... and Young,” and was played by Mel Gibson in the movie.

name: Bobby Freeman
profession: Do You Want to Dance Singer
headline: Bobby Freeman, ‘Do You Want to Dance’ Singer, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Freeman was 18 when he wrote and recorded the 1950s pop hit that became his signature. Artists from the Beach Boys to Bette Midler covered it.

name: Barbara Carroll
headline: Barbara Carroll, Pioneering Jazz Pianist and Singer, Dies at 92
abstract: For seven decades a beloved fixture of Manhattan night life, Ms. Carroll was a devotee of the American songbook who never forsook her jazz roots.

name: Stanley Bard
profession: Ran Chelsea Hotel as a Bohemian Sanctuary
headline: Stanley Bard, Who Ran Chelsea Hotel as a Bohemian Sanctuary, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Bard, a Robin Hood of innkeepers, nurtured talented writers and artists and tolerated assorted deadbeats as manager and part-owner of the famed Manhattan hotel.

name: Max Ferrá
headline: Max Ferrá, a Trailblazer for Latino Theater, Dies at 79
abstract: The Cuban-born Mr. Ferrá was the first artistic director of the Intar Hispanic American Arts Center, an Off Broadway theater company that nurtures Latino playwrights.

name: Adele Smithers
headline: Adele Smithers, Who Empowered Charity Benefactors, Dies at 83
abstract: In an advance in philanthropy, Adele Smithers sued St. Luke’s-Roosevelt Hospital Center over its administration of an endowment her husband had left.

name: David Axelrod
headline: David Axelrod, Music Producer Who Bridged Genres, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Axelrod’s influence can be heard in the work of Lou Rawls, Cannonball Adderley, Lauryn Hill and many others.

name: E. Clinton Bamberger
profession: Lawyer With a Fire for Justice
headline: E. Clinton Bamberger, Lawyer With a ‘Fire for Justice,’ Is Dead at 90
abstract: His court challenge on behalf of a convicted murderer led to a precedent-setting Supreme Court ruling in 1963 that protected criminal defendants.

name: Ren Xinmin
headline: Ren Xinmin, Pioneering Chinese Satellite Designer, Dies at 101
abstract: Dr. Ren, best known for designing China’s first satellite to be successfully launched, was the chief designer for six major space projects, according to the state news media.

name: Irwin Stambler
profession: Reference Book Writer With Songs in His Heart
headline: Irwin Stambler, 92, Dies; Reference Book Writer With Songs in His Heart
abstract: Mr. Stambler wrote “The Encyclopedia of Pop, Rock and Soul,” a tome that established a standard for its breadth, accuracy and readability.

name: Robert Michel
headline: Robert Michel Dies at 93; House G.O.P. Leader Prized Conciliation
abstract: Mr. Michel was the longest-serving Republican leader in the history of the House of Representatives. He retired right before his party won control.

name: Stuart McLean
headline: Stuart McLean, Who Created Radio’s ‘The Vinyl Cafe,’ Dies at 68
abstract: The Canadian humorist’s show was heard on the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation and on many public radio stations in the United States.

name: Abba Tor
profession: Engineered T.W.A. Terminal at Kennedy Airport
headline: Abba Tor, Who Engineered T.W.A. Terminal at Kennedy Airport, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Tor helped the architect Eero Saarinen design a structure of reinforced concrete that reminded viewers of a bird in flight.

name: Saloua Raouda Choucair
profession: Early Exponent of Abstract Arabian Art
headline: Saloua Raouda Choucair, Early Exponent of Abstract Arabian Art, Dies at 100
abstract: Ms. Choucair, who worked in obscurity outside her native Lebanon for decades, contributed an Arab idiom to modernism with her sense of line and form.

name: George Steele
headline: George Steele, ‘the Animal’ Wrestler and Mild-Mannered Teacher, Dies at 79
abstract: A World Wrestling Federation mainstay known for his wild antics and his signature green tongue, Steele was a hated villain but was described as “truly nice.”

name: Michael Rainey
headline: Michael Rainey, Boutique Owner in Swinging London, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Rainey opened his London boutique, Hung on You, in 1965 and his designs became popular with rock stars like the Beatles and the Rolling Stones.

name: James Nichols
headline: James Nichols, Linked to Oklahoma City Bombing, Dies at 62
abstract: The brother of conspirator Terry Nichols once hosted the bomber, Timothy McVeigh, at his Michigan farm, and was detained for more than a month during the investigation.

name: Norma McCorvey
headline: Norma McCorvey, ‘Roe’ in Roe v. Wade, Is Dead at 69
abstract: Ms. McCorvey, the anonymous plaintiff in the landmark Roe v. Wade ruling, was a symbol for abortion rights, though she later changed her views.

name: Omar Abdel Rahman
profession: Blind Cleric Found Guilty of Plot to Wage War of Urban Terrorism
headline: Omar Abdel Rahman, Blind Cleric Found Guilty of Plot to Wage ‘War of Urban Terrorism,’ Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Abdel Rahman was convicted of a 1993 plot to destroy New York landmarks, kill hundreds of people and force the United States to abandon its support for Israel and Egypt.

name: Clyde Stubblefield
headline: Clyde Stubblefield, the ‘Funky Drummer’ for James Brown, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Stubblefield was best known for a drum solo near the end of a 1969 Brown song he “didn’t like” that became the ubiquitous breakbeat of hip-hop’s sampling era.

name: Michael Novak
headline: Michael Novak, Catholic Scholar Who Championed Capitalism, Dies at 83
abstract: A Roman Catholic social philosopher, Mr. Novak abandoned liberal politics to make the theological and moral case for capitalism in a series of books.

name: Charles L. Bartlett
headline: Charles L. Bartlett, Journalist and a Kennedy Matchmaker, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Bartlett won a Pulitzer Prize for his national reporting but was remembered especially for hosting a dinner party in 1951 in which he introduced John F. Kennedy to Jacqueline Bouvier.

name: Junie Morrison
headline: Junie Morrison, a Funk Mastermind, Dies at 62
abstract: He was an architect of hits by two pre-eminent 1970s funk outfits, the Ohio Players and Parliament-Funkadelic, and had a prolific career on his own.

name: Ivor Noël Hume
headline: Ivor Noël Hume, Archaeologist of Colonial America, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Noël Hume, a self-taught scholar, was the director of Colonial Williamsburg’s archaeological mission from 1957 to 1988.

name: Vitaly Churkin
headline: Vitaly Churkin, Russia’s U.N. Ambassador, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Churkin, something of a legend in diplomatic circles with a caustic, wry wit, served at a time of mounting tensions between Washington and the Kremlin.

name: Dick Bruna
headline: Dick Bruna, Author of Miffy Books, Is Dead at 89
abstract: The Dutch writer and illustrator was known for children’s books depicting a sparely drawn round white rabbit who gained a worldwide following.

name: Richard Schickel
headline: Richard Schickel, Movie Critic, Author and Filmmaker, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Schickel reviewed films for Life magazine and wrote 37 books about the movies.

name: Kaci Kullmann Five
profession: Head of Nobel Peace Prize Committee
headline: Kaci Kullmann Five, Head of Nobel Peace Prize Committee, Dies at 65
abstract: A former member of the Norwegian Parliament, she presided over honors awarded to Tunisian pro-democracy organizations and to the president of Colombia.

name: Jamie Fox
profession: Backstage Force in New Jersey State Politics
headline: Jamie Fox, a Backstage Force in New Jersey State Politics, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Fox was a chief of staff or an adviser to four governors and a senator and was credited with legislative overhauls but was also charged after the George Washington Bridge scandal.

name: Larry Coryell
profession: Guitarist of Fusion Before It Had a Name
headline: Larry Coryell, Guitarist of Fusion Before It Had a Name, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Coryell favored dipping into different genres and international musical traditions to augment his work.

name: Jannis Kounellis
headline: Jannis Kounellis, Leader in ’60s ‘Poor Art’ Movement, Dies at 80
abstract: The Greek-born Italian artist worked with materials of every description, including live parrots and cockroaches, ground coffee, doors, meat and more.

name: Kenneth Arrow
headline: Kenneth Arrow, Nobel-Winning Economist Whose Influence Spanned Decades, Dies at 95
abstract: Professor Arrow, one of the most brilliant minds in his field during the 20th century, became the youngest economist ever to earn a Nobel at the age of 51.

name: Seijun Suzuki
headline: Seijun Suzuki, Director Who Inspired Tarantino and Jarmusch, Dies at 93
abstract: The filmmaker’s low-budget movies used surrealist humor and experimentation; he’s perhaps best known for “Branded to Kill,” a 1967 gangster story.

name: Thomas Lux
headline: Thomas Lux, Poet Who Wrote of Life’s Absurdities, Dies at 70
abstract: The writer blended comedy and surrealist images in his early collections, before moving toward precise realism.

name: Doug Coe
headline: Doug Coe, Influential Evangelical Leader, Dies at 88
abstract: He gained esteem among powerful world figures as head of the Fellowship Foundation, a secretive group that sponsors the National Prayer Breakfast.

name: Frank Delaney
headline: Frank Delaney, 74, Author Whose Passion Was Deconstructing Joyce’s ‘Ulysses,’ Dies
abstract: Mr. Delaney, who initially dismissed the book as unreadable, spent his career making that elusive novel about ordinary people accessible to ordinary readers.

name: Ed Garvey
headline: Ed Garvey, Leader of N.F.L. Players’ Union, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Garvey led two strikes in an effort to loosen teams’ grip on players. He later became a progressive activist in Wisconsin.

name: Alan Colmes
profession: Sean Hannitys Liberal Partner on Fox News
headline: Alan Colmes, Sean Hannity’s Liberal Partner on Fox News, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Colmes and Mr. Hannity sparred for 12 years in Fox News Channel’s most tangible effort to fulfill its “fair and balanced” credo.

name: Gary Cartwright
headline: Gary Cartwright, Acclaimed Texas Writer, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Cartwright practiced the “gonzo journalism” made famous by another larger-than-life storyteller: Hunter S. Thompson.

name: Mildred Dresselhaus
headline: Mildred Dresselhaus, the Queen of Carbon, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Dresselhaus, who helped transform carbon into the superstar of modern materials science, was renowned for her efforts to promote the cause of women in science.

name: James Stevenson
headline: James Stevenson, Longtime New Yorker Cartoonist, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Stevenson’s work shifted easily from light social commentary to silliness for more than half a century.

name: Harold R. Denton
profession: Voice of Comfort at Three Mile Island
headline: Harold R. Denton, Voice of Comfort at Three Mile Island, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Denton, President Jimmy Carter’s crisis manager for the 1979 nuclear reactor accident in Pennsylvania, averted panic and calmed an anxious nation.

name: Desmond Connell
headline: Cardinal Desmond Connell, 90, Dies; Dublin Archbishop During Abuse Scandal
abstract: The cardinal, a stalwart defender of church doctrine, later expressed regret for his handling of the scandal.

name: Jerome Tuccille
headline: Jerome Tuccille, Libertarian Author and Trump Biographer, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Tuccille was a disaffected Roman Catholic looking for a new faith when he discovered the writings of Ayn Rand.

name: Theodore Lowi
profession: Zealous Scholar of Presidents and Liberalism
headline: Theodore Lowi, Zealous Scholar of Presidents and Liberalism, Dies at 85
abstract: Coupling academic expertise with charisma, Professor Lowi popularized his theories with an evangelical zeal and a Southern drawl in lectures, television appearances and books.

name: Bill Paxton
profession: Star of Big Love and Movie Blockbusters
headline: Bill Paxton, Star of ‘Big Love’ and Movie Blockbusters, Dies at 61
abstract: After playing a small part in “Aliens,” Mr. Paxton later starred in “Twister,” “Titanic” and “Apollo 13.”

name: Joseph A. Wapner
headline: Joseph A. Wapner, Judge on ‘The People’s Court,’ Dies at 97
abstract: Judge Wapner sat on the bench in the syndicated television show from its debut in 1981 to the end of its original run in 1993.

name: Stanislaw Skrowaczewski
headline: Stanislaw Skrowaczewski, Conductor Who Fled Poland, Dies at 93
abstract: After Mr. Skrowaczewski defected in 1960 (Communist rule “was impossible for musicians and composers”), he led the Minnesota Orchestra for 19 years.

name: Stanley Dearman
headline: Stanley Dearman, Editor Who Sought Justice in 1964 Murders, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Dearman’s editorials helped set the stage for the belated conviction of a former Klansman for organizing the murders of three civil rights workers in Mississippi.

name: Fritz Koenig
headline: Fritz Koenig, Sculptor of Trade Center ‘Sphere,’ Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Koenig knew that his most important sculpture would return to its intended site in Lower Manhattan. But he did not live to see the day.

name: Ward Chamberlin Jr.
headline: Ward Chamberlin Jr., Architect of Nation’s Public Broadcasting, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Chamberlin pioneered an enduring decentralized network model of independent public stations and supported documentaries like Ken Burns’s “The Civil War.”

name: Mostafa el-Abbadi
headline: Mostafa el-Abbadi, 88, Champion of Alexandria’s Resurrected Library, Dies
abstract: Professor Abbadi was a historian of Greco-Roman antiquity and the visionary behind the revival of the Great Library of Alexandria in Egypt.

name: Ned Garver
headline: Ned Garver, 20-Game Winner for the 102-Loss Browns, Dies at 91
abstract: The pitcher was 20-12 in 1951 for last-place St. Louis, finishing second in voting for the league’s Most Valuable Player Award.

name: Emmanuelle Khanh
headline: Emmanuelle Khanh, Who Reinvigorated French Fashion, Dies at 79
abstract: Frustrated with the rigidity of haute couture and the lack of spontaneity in French fashion, Ms. Khanh designed quirky, fluid clothes for young, active women.

name: Aileen Hernandez
headline: Aileen Hernandez, 90, Ex-NOW President and Feminist Trailblazer, Dies
abstract: Ms. Hernandez was one of the first African-American women to battle sex discrimination from inside the government and in the top ranks of the feminist movement.

name: William Liebenow
headline: William Liebenow, 97, Dies; PT Boat Skipper Rescued Kennedy
abstract: Lieutenant Liebenow was sent to pick up John Kennedy and his surviving crew members from an island behind enemy lines after their boat was rammed by the Japanese.

name: Edward E. David Jr.
headline: Edward E. David Jr., Who Elevated Science Under Nixon, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. David sought to make science more relevant and accessible to presidents and to the public, saying, “We can’t leave science and technology to the experts.”

name: Horace Parlan
headline: Horace Parlan, Jazz Pianist, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Parlan, who despite a partly disabled hand, forged a style that impressed critics. He also collaborated with acclaimed musicians like Charles Mingus and Archie Shepp.

name: Jerry Birbach
profession: Leader of Fight to Block Poor Tenants in Queens
headline: Jerry Birbach, Leader of Fight to Block Poor Tenants in Queens, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Birbach’s battle against a low-income housing project in Forest Hills in 1972 augured a white middle-class backlash to the liberal urban agenda and helped propel Mario Cuomo’s political rise.

name: Marian Javits
profession: Proto-Feminist and Widow of New York Senator
headline: Marian Javits, Proto-Feminist and Widow of New York Senator, Dies at 92
abstract: Mrs. Javits, the wife of Jacob K. Javits, a United States senator from 1957 to 1981, was a bon vivant who once said, “I’m my husband’s wife, and I’m striving to be my own person.”

name: David Rubinger
headline: David Rubinger, 92, Photographer Who Chronicled Israeli History, Dies
abstract: Mr. Rubinger, an Austria native who fought in 1948 for Israel’s independence, is known for a photo of paratroopers gazing at the Western Wall during the 1967 Arab-Israeli war.

name: Paul Kangas
headline: Paul Kangas, 79, Anchor Who Brought Stocks Into Living Rooms, Dies
abstract: When Mr. Kangas joined “Nightly Business Report” on public television as a stock commentator in 1979, there was nothing like it on the air.

name: Boaz Vaadia
headline: Boaz Vaadia, Sculptor Who Worked in Street Stone, Dies at 65
abstract: His earlier work used natural materials in abstract pieces, but after he moved to SoHo he turned to figural art.

name: Leon Ware
headline: Leon Ware, Producer Who Worked With Marvin Gaye, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Ware helped popularize the “quiet storm” sound, a mix of jazz and R&B, through collaborations with Gaye, Quincy Jones and other notables.

name: Paula Fox
headline: Paula Fox, Novelist Who Chronicled Dislocation, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Fox wrote for all ages, offering closely observed portraits of loss and abandonment. It was terrain she knew all too well.

name: Ren Hang
headline: Ren Hang, Provocative Chinese Photographer, Dies at 29
abstract: Mr. Ren, who was known for erotic images of naked young models, jumped from the 28th floor of a building, according to a report by The Beijing News.

name: Nicholas Mosley
headline: Nicholas Mosley, Novelist and Biographer, Dies at 93
abstract: While his experimental fiction brought him success, he also wrote unsparingly of his father, the fascist leader Sir Oswald Mosley.

name: Spencer Hays
headline: Spencer Hays, Business Magnate and Art Collector, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Hays, who once worked as a Bible salesman, arranged last year to leave his and his wife’s more than 600 masterwork paintings to France.

name: René Préval
headline: René Préval, President of Haiti in 2010 Quake, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Préval was the first — and so far only — Haitian president to be elected, serve out his term and hand over power to an elected successor.

name: Dorothy Rice
headline: Dorothy Rice, Pioneering Economist Who Made Case for Medicare, Dies at 94
abstract: Mrs. Rice was an analyst at the Social Security Administration when its study on aging highlighted how about half the population 65 and over had no health insurance.

name: Howard Schmidt
headline: Howard Schmidt, Cybersecurity Adviser to Two Presidents, Dies at 67
abstract: A computer crime expert, Mr. Schmidt was recruited by Presidents George W. Bush and Barack Obama and drafted safeguards that were approved by Congress.

name: Helen M. Marshall
profession: First Black Borough President of Queens
headline: Helen M. Marshall, First Black Borough President of Queens, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Marshall was remembered as a champion of public libraries and her borough’s culture.

name: Lester Tenney
profession: Faced Japans Brutality and Won Its Apologies
headline: Lester Tenney, 96, Dies; Faced Japan’s Brutality and Won Its Apologies
abstract: Mr. Tenney survived the Bataan Death March, followed by three and a half years of slave labor as a prisoner during World War II.

name: Thomas E. Starzl
headline: Dr. Thomas E. Starzl, Pioneering Liver Surgeon, Dies at 90
abstract: In the 1960s, Dr. Starzl performed the first successful liver transplant on a human patient and later helped advance drugs that made organ transplants more survivable.

name: Miriam Colón
profession: Actress and Founder of Puerto Rican Traveling Theater
headline: Miriam Colón, 80, Actress and Founder of Puerto Rican Traveling Theater, Dies
abstract: Among her many roles, Ms. Colón played Al Pacino’s Cuban mother in “Scarface.” She founded the Puerto Rican Traveling Theater in 1967.

name: Robert Osborne
headline: Robert Osborne, Turner Classic Movies Host, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Osborne, a film historian, was the congenial prime time host of the movie channel since its inception in 1994.

name: Simon Hobday
headline: Simon Hobday, Offbeat U.S. Senior Open Champion, Dies at 76
abstract: Hobday, a leading player on the African and European pro golf tours, won five senior events in the United States, including the Open in 1994.

name: Thomas Platt
headline: Thomas Platt, 91, Dies: Fined Air Traffic Controllers $100,000 an Hour
abstract: Judge Platt also presided over suits against Libya and Pan American World Airways in the terrorist bombing of a jet over Lockerbie, Scotland, in 1988.

name: Nancy Willard
headline: Nancy Willard, Prolific Children’s Book Author, Dies at 80
abstract: Her fiction and poems — including the first volume of poetry to win the Newbery Medal — charmed audiences with their mix of fanciful illusion and stark reality.

name: George Blackburn
profession: Worked to Help You Eat Better
headline: Dr. George Blackburn, Who Worked to Help You Eat Better, Dies at 81
abstract: Dr. Blackburn, a pre-eminent scholar on nutrition and obesity, advocated lower-fat diets and was a pioneer in developing gastric bypass surgery and nutritional liquid diets.

name: Joseph W. Rogers
headline: Joseph W. Rogers, a Founder of Waffle House, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Rogers and a neighbor started with one restaurant in the Atlanta area in 1955. Today, the no-frills, 24-hour chain has nearly 1,900.

name: Fred Weintraub
profession: Showcased Future Greats at the Bitter End
headline: Fred Weintraub, 88, Dies; Showcased Future Greats at the Bitter End
abstract: The Greenwich Village impresario advanced the careers of Bob Dylan, Woody Allen, Lenny Bruce and others, and later became a Hollywood producer who worked with Bruce Lee.

name: Lynne Stewart
headline: Lynne Stewart, Lawyer Imprisoned in Terrorism Case, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Stewart, who was convicted of aiding terrorism in her representation of Omar Abdel Rahman, was also known for defending a member of the Weather Underground and other violent activists.

name: Bill Webb
headline: Bill Webb, Tailor of TV Baseball Excitement, Dies at 70
abstract: Webb, who directed programming from a mobile production truck for Fox Sports and the Mets, relied on close-ups and pacing to enrapture his viewers.

name: Gustav Metzger
headline: Gustav Metzger, ‘Auto-Destructive Art’ Provocateur, Dies at 90
abstract: A political radical whose entire career consisted of pointed attacks on the capitalist system, Mr. Metzger inspired Pete Townshend to smash his guitars and amps.

name: Lou Duva
headline: Lou Duva, Boxing Promoter, Manager and Trainer, Dies at 94
abstract: Duva, who had ties to more than a dozen world champions, was the patriarch of boxing’s first family in the 1980s and ’90s through Main Events promoters.

name: Dave Valentin
headline: Dave Valentin, a Grammy Award-Winning Latin Jazz Flutist, Dies at 64
abstract: He won a Grammy for best Latin jazz album in 2003 for “The Gathering,” by the Caribbean Jazz Project.

name: Clayton Yeutter
profession: Blunt Negotiator of Intricate Trade Deals
headline: Clayton Yeutter, Blunt Negotiator of Intricate Trade Deals, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Yeutter, a Nebraska farmer who became United States trade representative and secretary of agriculture, oversaw negotiations that became the backbone of Nafta.

name: Stephen Ross
headline: Stephen Ross, Economist Who Developed Arbitrage Pricing Theory, Dies at 73
abstract: Professor Ross, who taught at the M.I.T. Sloan School of Management, was a seminal theorist whose work reshaped the field of financial economics.

name: Marilyn Young
headline: Marilyn Young, Historian Who Challenged U.S. Foreign Policy, Dies at 79
abstract: A longtime professor at New York University, she remarked in 2012 that the United States had been at war in one form or another since her childhood.

name: Howard Hodgkin
headline: Howard Hodgkin, Whose Paintings Were Coded With Emotion, Dies at 84
abstract: The British painter, who won the Turner Prize in 1985, was one of the most admired artists of the postwar period.

name: Kurt Moll
headline: Kurt Moll, German Basso Profundo, Dies at 78
abstract: He was his generation’s pre-eminent Baron Ochs in “Der Rosenkavalier,” mixing humor with a tinge of menace. His Ochs is preserved on many recordings.

name: Anthony Beilenson
headline: Anthony Beilenson, Congressman Who Fought for Abortion Rights, Dies at 84
abstract: As a Democratic state legislator in California, he persuaded Gov. Ronald Reagan to approve progressive abortion rights bill years before Roe v. Wade was decided.

name: Robert James Waller
profession: Author of The Bridges of Madison County
headline: Robert James Waller, Author of ‘The Bridges of Madison County,’ Dies at 77
abstract: Millions of readers found Mr. Waller’s story of reawakened love deeply moving and the novel topped best seller lists and was made into a movie.

name: Carol Field
headline: Carol Field, Italian Food Expert, Dies at 76
abstract: She was one of the new wave of cookbook writers who put as much emphasis on fine writing and context as on the recipes themselves.

name: Anne Friedman Glauber
headline: Anne Friedman Glauber, Champion of Social Causes, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Glauber, who worked as a public relations executive in New York, co-founded an initiative to reduce domestic violence and a council to help women in Rwanda and Afghanistan.

name: Lloyd Conover
headline: Lloyd Conover, Inventor of Groundbreaking Antibiotic, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Conover, a chemist, developed tetracycline, a powerful chemically altered antibiotic with fewer side effects than the drug from which it was derived.

name: George A. Olah
headline: George A. Olah, Carbon Compounds Pathfinder, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Olah’s advances in the understanding of hydrocarbons have been used in an array of applications, including the development of gasoline that burns more cleanly.

name: John Surtees
headline: John Surtees, Two- and Four-Wheel Racing Champion, Dies at 83
abstract: Surtees, active in the 1960s and ’70s, was the only driver to hold world titles in motorcycle and auto racing.

name: Joni Sledge
profession: Singer in the We Are Family Group Sister Sledge
headline: Joni Sledge, Singer in the ‘We Are Family’ Group Sister Sledge, Dies at 60
abstract: Ms. Sledge rose to stardom along with her three sisters in the late 1970s in the family quartet Sister Sledge.

name: Jay Lynch
headline: Jay Lynch, Underground Comics Creator, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Lynch was an artist, writer and satirist employing a retro style and deadpan humor. He was also an archivist of underground comics history.

name: Amy Krouse Rosenthal
headline: Amy Krouse Rosenthal, Children’s Author and Filmmaker, Dies at 51
abstract: Her death came 10 days after a “Modern Love” column in The Times about her illness titled, “You May Want to Marry My Husband.”

name: Igor Shafarevich
profession: Russian Mathematician With a Mixed Political Legacy
headline: Igor Shafarevich, Russian Mathematician With a Mixed Political Legacy, Dies at 93
abstract: His work was internationally renowned, but Professor Shafarevich’s reputation as an anti-Soviet dissident was later tarnished by accusations of anti-Semitism.

name: Christopher Gray
headline: Christopher Gray, Architecture Writer and Researcher, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Gray wrote extensively in books, magazines and newspapers, including the Streetscapes column for The New York Times, and acted as an architectural detective in documenting buildings’ histories.

name: Divine
headline: Mother Divine, Who Took Over Her Husband’s Cult, Dies at 91
abstract: Mother Divine led the International Peace Mission Movement after the death of her husband, Father Divine, who was regarded as God incarnate by his disciples.

name: Misha Mengelberg
headline: Misha Mengelberg, Bold and Spirited Jazz Pianist, Dies at 81
abstract: As both a musician and a composer, Mr. Mengelberg approached the jazz tradition with an antic sense of humor.

name: Jonathan Moore
profession: Academic and Public Servant for 6 Presidents
headline: Jonathan Moore, Academic and Public Servant for 6 Presidents, Dies at 84
abstract: His ability to circumvent bureaucracies and build coalitions was an asset in an eclectic career that straddled government and academia.

name: Ed Whitlock
profession: Oldest Marathoner to Break Four Hours
headline: Ed Whitlock, Oldest Marathoner to Break Four Hours, Dies at 86
abstract: A masters running champion, Mr. Whitlock, then 85, finished the 2016 Toronto Waterfront Marathon in 3 hours 56 minutes 34 seconds.

name: John Andariese
profession: Knicks Broadcaster Known as Johnny Hoops
headline: John Andariese, Knicks Broadcaster Known as ‘Johnny Hoops,’ Dies at 78
abstract: Andariese, who appeared in the N.I.T. twice with Fordham but never played or coached in the N.B.A., said he was driven to spread his love of the game.

name: Henry S. Lodge
profession: Author of Younger Next Year Books
headline: Henry S. Lodge, Author of ‘Younger Next Year’ Books, Dies at 58
abstract: Dr. Lodge’s guide to youthfulness involved regular workouts, abstaining from junk food, and connecting.

name: Ron Drever
headline: Ron Drever, Physicist Who Helped Confirm Einstein Theory, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Drever, a Scotsman long associated with Caltech, played a key role in the detection of gravitational waves — space-time ripples predicted by Einstein.

name: Fiora Corradetti Contino
headline: Fiora Corradetti Contino, Opera Maestra, Dies at 91
abstract: An acclaimed conductor, she specialized in the visceral, unsentimental realism of Italian verismo opera and was also a music professor and vocal coach.

name: Tommy LiPuma
headline: Tommy LiPuma, Record Producer and Grammy Winner, Dies at 80
abstract: The producer and music executive began his career after quitting a job as a barber, and went on to work with Diana Krall, Natalie Cole and others.

name: Kika de la Garza
headline: Kika de la Garza, Texas Congressman and Farmers’ Ally, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. de la Garza, a conservative Democrat, helped found the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and spent 32 years in the House representing South Texas.

name: Royal Robbins
headline: Royal Robbins, Conscience of Rock Climbers, Dies at 82
abstract: Robbins made several first ascents, and he urged those who followed him up the rocks to leave few traces of their path, setting an example that is still heeded.

name: Ben Jobe
headline: Ben Jobe, Southern University Basketball Coach, Dies at 84
abstract: Jobe transformed Southern into a scoring powerhouse during his 12 seasons as head coach and led the team to the N.C.A.A. tournament four times.

name: James Cotton
headline: James Cotton, Blues Harmonica Legend, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Cotton worked on his own, and with stars like Muddy Waters and Howlin’ Wolf, but he treasured his apprenticeship with Sonny Boy Williamson most.

name: Joseph Nicolosi
profession: Advocate of Conversion Therapy for Gays
headline: Joseph Nicolosi, Advocate of Conversion Therapy for Gays, Dies at 70
abstract: Dr. Nicolosi was an influential voice in the “ex-gay” movement, but his contentious views marginalized him within the mental-health profession.

name: Derek Walcott
profession: Poet and Nobel Laureate of the Caribbean
headline: Derek Walcott, Poet and Nobel Laureate of the Caribbean, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Walcott’s intricately metaphorical poetry captured the physical beauty of the Caribbean, the harsh legacy of colonialism and the complexities of living and writing in two cultural worlds.

name: Frederic Nathan
headline: Frederic Nathan, New York City Legal Officer, Dies at 94
abstract: A city lawyer who was in charge of enforcing the Public Employees Fair Employment Act, which prohibited strikes by state and municipal workers.

name: George Braziller
headline: George Braziller, Publisher of Fresh Literary Voices, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Braziller searched the world for promising writers — bringing the work of Jean-Paul Sartre to America — and gave new life to historic manuscripts.

name: Dave Stallworth
profession: Bulwark for Knicks First N.B.A. Title
headline: Dave Stallworth, Bulwark for Knicks’ First N.B.A. Title, Dies at 75
abstract: Stallworth, an all-American forward at Wichita State, helped the Knicks slow Wilt Chamberlain in the 1970 N.B.A. finals after an injury to Willis Reed.

name: Norbert W. Sander Jr.
headline: Norbert W. Sander Jr., Champion of New York Running, Dies at 74
abstract: After Dr. Sander won the New York City Marathon in 1974, he helped turn the Fort Washington Armory into a track-and-field mecca.

name: John Van de Kamp
headline: John Van de Kamp, Former Prosecutor in California, Dies at 81
abstract: As district attorney in Los Angeles, Mr. Van de Kamp prosecuted the Hillside Strangler case; he was also the state’s attorney general and ran for governor in 1990.

name: Hugh Hardy
headline: Hugh Hardy, Architect Who Lent Pizazz to New York Landmarks, Dies at 84
abstract: With showmanship and affection for the past, Mr. Hardy breathed new life into storied theaters like Radio City Music Hall.

name: John Herbers
profession: Vividly Covered the Civil Rights Era for The Times
headline: John Herbers, Who Vividly Covered the Civil Rights Era for The Times, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Herbers reported on national affairs including racial violence in the Deep South, protests against the Vietnam War, the assassination of Senator Robert F. Kennedy and the Watergate scandal.

name: Chuck Berry
headline: Chuck Berry, Rock ’n’ Roll Pioneer, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Berry was rock’s master theorist and conceptual genius, a songwriter who understood what the kids wanted before they knew themselves.

name: Jimmy Breslin
profession: Legendary New York City Newspaper Columnist
headline: Jimmy Breslin, Legendary New York City Newspaper Columnist, Dies at 88
abstract: With prose that was savagely funny, deceptively simple and poorly imitated, Mr. Breslin created his own distinct rhythm in the hurly-burly music of newspapers.

name: David Rockefeller
profession: Philanthropist and Head of Chase Manhattan
headline: David Rockefeller, Philanthropist and Head of Chase Manhattan, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Rockefeller was influential in foreign affairs, helped resolve New York’s fiscal crisis in the 1970s and was chairman of the Museum of Modern Art for many years.

name: Trisha Brown
profession: Choreographer and Pillar of American Postmodern Dance
headline: Trisha Brown, Choreographer and Pillar of American Postmodern Dance, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Brown’s choreography, showcased primarily in New York, helped shape generations of modern dance creators into the 21st century.

name: Robert Silvers
profession: Founding Editor of New York Review of Books
headline: Robert Silvers, a Founding Editor of New York Review of Books, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Silvers brought to The Review’s pages a self-effacing sense of devotion that made him indistinguishable from the publication, and it from him.

name: Richard Wagamese
headline: Richard Wagamese, Whose Writing Explored His Ojibwe Heritage, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Wagamese said the forced assimilation of his parents in Canada caused their negligence with their children.

name: Martin McGuinness
headline: Martin McGuinness, an I.R.A. Leader Turned Peacemaker, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. McGuinness helped negotiate peace in Northern Ireland after decades of sectarian violence and became a senior official in its power-sharing government.

name: Morton Deutsch
headline: Morton Deutsch, Expert on Conflict Resolution, Dies at 97
abstract: Professor Deutsch, who founded the International Center for Cooperation and Conflict Resolution, was known for his theory of cooperation and competition.

name: Jerry Krause
profession: Gave Michael Jordan His Supporting Cast
headline: Jerry Krause, Who Gave Michael Jordan His Supporting Cast, Dies at 77
abstract: The former Bulls general manager orchestrated the team’s dynasty of the 1990s, assembling the rosters that Jordan led to six N.B.A. championships.

name: Colin Dexter
profession: Creator of Inspector Morse, a Sleuth on Page and Screen
headline: Colin Dexter, 86, Dies; Creator of Inspector Morse, a Sleuth on Page and Screen
abstract: The British mystery writer indulged in the art for fun and never expected his character to attain such fame.

name: Chuck Barris
profession: Producer and Personality of Gong Show Fame
headline: Chuck Barris, Producer and Personality of ‘Gong Show’ Fame, Dies at 87
abstract: The creative force and host of TV hits — as well as a songwriter, novelist and even an assassin, to hear him tell it — Mr. Barris knew there was an audience for lowbrow.

name: Mary Maples Dunn
headline: Mary Maples Dunn, Advocate of Women’s Colleges, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Dunn spent most of her career at women’s colleges, which had been established long before women were admitted to many universities throughout the United States.

name: George Weinberg
profession: Coined Homophobia After Seeing Fear of Gays
headline: George Weinberg Dies at 87; Coined ‘Homophobia’ After Seeing Fear of Gays
abstract: Among Dr. Weinberg’s books were “Society and the Healthy Homosexual,” which rejected the prevalent idea that homosexuality was a psychological disorder.

name: Skip Williamson
headline: Skip Williamson, Underground Cartoonist, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Williamson, whose comics in the 1960s and ’70s reflected his radical politics, included savage caricatures and characters like Snappy Sammy Smoot.

name: Dallas Green
profession: Led the Phillies to Their First Title
headline: Dallas Green, Who Led the Phillies to Their First Title, Dies at 82
abstract: Green was a hot-tempered baseball lifer who, in his later years, struggled to recover from the shooting death of his 9-year-old granddaughter.

name: Peter Kwong
headline: Peter Kwong, Authority on Chinese Immigration, Dies at 75
abstract: Professor Kwong was a scholar, journalist, documentary filmmaker and author, charting the history of Chinese newcomers in the United States.

name: Lewis Rowland
profession: Leading Neurologist on Nerve and Muscle Diseases
headline: Dr. Lewis Rowland, Leading Neurologist on Nerve and Muscle Diseases, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Rowland, who had a special interest in A.L.S., or Lou Gehrig’s disease, refused to be interrogated by investigators in the McCarthy era.

name: Anatoly S. Chernyaev
profession: Key Aide and Gorbachevs Alter Ego
headline: Anatoly S. Chernyaev, Key Aide and Gorbachev’s ‘Alter Ego,’ Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Chernyaev advised Mikhail S. Gorbachev on foreign and domestic affairs and played a central role in his attempt to liberalize and modernize the Soviet Union.

name: Gershon Kekst
profession: Leader in Wall St. Public Relations
headline: Gershon Kekst, Leader in Wall St. Public Relations, Dies at 82
abstract: For more than five decades in public relations, Mr. Kekst forged relationships with business moguls and the bankers and lawyers who advised them on takeovers.

name: Boris V. Shekhtman
profession: Taught Russian to Journalists and Diplomats
headline: Boris V. Shekhtman, Who Taught Russian to Journalists and Diplomats, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Shekhtman was instrumental in recasting the way foreign languages were taught.

name: Don Hunstein
headline: Don Hunstein, Who Photographed Great Musicians, Dies at 88
abstract: As a staff photographer for Columbia Records, Mr. Hunstein shot Bob Dylan, Duke Ellington, Billie Holiday and many others.

name: Bernie Wrightson
profession: Artist and a Creator of Swamp Thing
headline: Bernie Wrightson, Artist and a Creator of Swamp Thing, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Wrightson, who learned his craft by studying comics and taking correspondence courses, loved to meet fans and attend conventions.

name: William Keeler
headline: William Keeler, Cardinal Who Championed Sexual Abuse Victims, Dies at 86
abstract: The former archbishop of Baltimore spoke up for victims of sexual abuse by priests, and is credited with improving Catholic-Jewish relations.

name: Robin O’Hara
headline: Robin O’Hara, Producer of Independent Films, Dies at 62
abstract: Ms. O’Hara got her start as a producer in the mid-1980s at the Kitchen, the experimental performance space in Chelsea.

name: Roger Wilkins
headline: Roger Wilkins, Champion of Civil Rights, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Wilkins waged a decades-long war against racism as a government official, a foundation executive, a journalist, an author and a professor.

name: Santiago Barberi Gonzalez
headline: Santiago Barberi Gonzalez, a Colombian Fashion Star, Dies at 40
abstract: The designer was the charismatic president of one of the largest purveyors of crocodile handbags in the world.

name: David Storey
profession: Novelist and Playwright Lauded on Both Sides of Atlantic
headline: David Storey, Novelist and Playwright Lauded on Both Sides of Atlantic, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Storey’s plays often reflected Britain’s class tensions but resonated with audiences around the world and with people of all backgrounds.

name: Christina Vella
profession: Author of Sizzling Works of Narrative History
headline: Christina Vella, 75, Author of Sizzling Works of Narrative History, Dies
abstract: The writer recounted the story of the Baroness de Pontalba, a New Orleans-born heiress shot by her French father-in-law in a dowry dispute.

name: Paul Novograd
headline: Paul Novograd, Who Owned Manhattan’s Last Public Livery, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Novograd reluctantly closed his family’s Claremont Riding Academy in 2007. Opened in 1892, it was billed as the oldest continuously operating stable in New York City.

name: Ahmed Kathrada
headline: Ahmed Kathrada, Anti-Apartheid Activist in South Africa, Dies at 87
abstract: He spent 26 years in prison, many alongside his close friend Nelson Mandela, for resisting white minority rule.

name: Bill Minor
headline: Bill Minor, Journalist Who Was Called Conscience of Mississippi, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Minor was already known for exposing corrupt Mississippi politicians when he became one of the South’s leading news voices on the civil rights movement.

name: William McPherson
headline: William McPherson, Book Critic and Novelist, Dies at 84
abstract: The Pulitzer Prize winner wrote for The Washington Post and was the author of the acclaimed novel “Testing the Current.”

name: William Powell
headline: William Powell, ‘Anarchist Cookbook’ Writer, Dies at 66
abstract: The author was an angry teenager when he began research on the book, which outlined weapon use, bomb-building techniques and drug manufacturing.

name: Arthur Blythe
headline: Arthur Blythe, Jazz Saxophonist Who Mixed Sultry and Strident, Dies at 76
abstract: A standard-bearer of the New York jazz avant-garde in the late ’70s, he had a vibrato-thickened style and was a spokesman for jazz’s Afrocentric vanguard.

name: Noreen Fraser
profession: Led a Public Fight Against Cancer
headline: Noreen Fraser, Who Led a Public Fight Against Cancer, Dies at 63
abstract: The television producer helped raise millions of dollars in a national campaign against breast cancer after learning she had the disease.

name: Deane Hinton
headline: Deane Hinton, Envoy Who Denounced Salvadoran ‘Death Squads,’ Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Hinton served as American ambassador to five countries for four Republican presidents, including Reagan during El Salvador’s civil war.

name: Brian Oldfield
headline: Brian Oldfield, Brash Shot-Putting Superstar, Dies at 71
abstract: ‘When God invented man, he wanted him to look like me.’

name: Donald Harvey
headline: Donald Harvey, Who Killed Dozens of Hospital Patients, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Harvey, among the most prolific mass murderers in United States history, confessed to killing 37 people, mostly hospital patients, over two decades in Ohio and Kentucky.

name: William T. Coleman Jr.
profession: Broke Racial Barriers in Court and Cabinet
headline: William T. Coleman Jr., Who Broke Racial Barriers in Court and Cabinet, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Coleman’s experiences with bigotry informed his efforts in three major civil rights cases before the United States Supreme Court.

name: Francine Hughes Wilson
headline: Francine Hughes Wilson, 69, Domestic Violence Victim Who Took Action, Dies
abstract: Her case, which was the subject of “The Burning Bed,” a book and a television movie, helped transform the public’s understanding of domestic abuse.

name: Jack Ziegler
headline: Jack Ziegler, Cartoonist at The New Yorker, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Ziegler set his cartoons nearly anywhere — in courtrooms or boardrooms, backyards or stadiums, barrooms or churches.

name: Alex Tizon
headline: Alex Tizon, Journalist Who Wrote of Alienation as Asian-American, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Tizon, who shared a Pulitzer Prize as a reporter, wrote the 2014 memoir “Big Little Man” in which he he asked, ‘When did this shame inside me begin?’

name: Pamela Edstrom
headline: Pamela Edstrom, Who Helped Shape Microsoft’s Public Image, Dies at 71
abstract: Ms. Edstrom, who joined Microsoft as its first director of public relations in 1982, became one of Bill Gates’s closest outside advisers.

name: Gilbert Baker
headline: Gilbert Baker, Gay Activist Who Created the Rainbow Flag, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Baker’s emblem, which he created in 1978, came to symbolize the gay rights movement. He described himself as the “gay Betsy Ross.”

name: James Rosenquist
headline: James Rosenquist, Pop Art Pioneer, Dies at 83
abstract: Working as a sign painter by day and an abstract artist by night, Mr. Rosenquist imported elements of outdoor advertising into the realm of fine art.

name: Yevgeny Yevtushenko
headline: Yevgeny Yevtushenko, Poet Who Stirred a Generation of Soviets, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Yevtushenko’s defiant verse inspired a generation of young Russians in their fight against Stalinism during the Cold War.

name: Richard Bolles
profession: Wrote What Color Is Your Parachute?
headline: Richard Bolles Dies at 90; Wrote ‘What Color Is Your Parachute?’
abstract: Mr. Bolles studied science but became an Episcopal minister, and then he lost his job, leaving him well prepared to write a guide to changing careers.

name: Alexei Abrikosov
headline: Alexei Abrikosov, Nobel Laureate in Physics, Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Abrikosov’s work with two other physicists offered insights on superconductors, or materials that conduct electricity without resistance.

name: Leonard Litwin
headline: Leonard Litwin, New York Real Estate Mogul, Dies at 102
abstract: Mr. Litwin’s imprint is on the Manhattan skyline in dozens of buildings he built, owned and operated with high-end amenities and lofty rents.

name: Gary Austin
headline: Gary Austin, Who Founded the Groundlings Improv Troupe, Dies at 75
abstract: A sought-after teacher, Mr. Austin helped change the shape of American comedy and gave many big names in comedy their start.

name: Ikutaro Kakehashi
headline: Ikutaro Kakehashi, Engineer Behind Revolutionary Drum Machine, Dies at 87
abstract: The founder of the Roland Corporation, Mr. Kakehashi made the beloved 808 drum machine and hundreds of other instruments.

name: Joe Harris
profession: Illustrator Behind Underdog and Trix Rabbit
headline: Joe Harris, Illustrator Behind Underdog and Trix Rabbit, Dies at 89
abstract: Besides drawing cartoon characters (also Tennessee Tuxedo and King Leonardo), Mr. Harris wrote ad copy, like the catchphrase “Silly rabbit! Trix are for kids!”

name: Joe Harris
profession: Thought to Be the Oldest World War II Paratrooper
headline: Joe Harris, 108, Dies; Thought to Be the Oldest World War II Paratrooper
abstract: He was a member of a segregated unit in the Pacific Northwest that fought forest fires set off by Japanese balloon bombs.

name: Amy Moritz Ridenour
headline: Amy Moritz Ridenour, Conservative Think Tank Founder, Dies at 57
abstract: Mrs. Ridenour, chairwoman of the National Center for Public Policy Research, had been an influential backer of the military and free markets since the Reagan administration.

name: Radley Metzger
headline: Radley Metzger, Whose Artful Erotica Turned Explicit, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Metzger was a serious student of film who changed course when his less-graphic films lost out to the more explicit competition.

name: Ronald G. Witt
profession: Gave the Renaissance a New Birthdate
headline: Ronald G. Witt, Who Gave the Renaissance a New Birthdate, Dies at 84
abstract: His work led him to identify the first stirrings of Italian humanism well before the time of its traditional father, Petrarch, in the 14th century.

name: Roy Sievers
headline: Roy Sievers, Slugging Washington Senator in the ’50s, Dies at 90
abstract: The winner of the American League’s first Rookie of the Year Award eventually became a favorite of Vice President Richard M. Nixon’s.

name: Lolis Elie
headline: Lolis Elie, Lawyer Who Helped Desegregate New Orleans, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Elie’s unstinting advocacy for civil rights as an organizer and a negotiator raised the consciousness of blacks and whites alike.

name: Arthur Bisguier
headline: Arthur Bisguier, Brash, Self-Taught Bronx Chess Champion, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Bisguier learned to play chess when he was 5 by watching games between his older sister and a cousin. He was frustrated by failures against Bobby Fischer.

name: Ruben Amaro Sr.
headline: Ruben Amaro Sr., Infielder for Star-Crossed ’64 Phillies, Dies at 81
abstract: Amaro, a superb fielder, won a Gold Glove at shortstop for a team that endured one of baseball’s most stunning collapses.

name: Don Rickles
headline: Don Rickles, Comedy’s Equal Opportunity Offender, Dies at 90
abstract: For over half a century, Mr. Rickles made outrageously derisive comments about people’s looks, their ethnicity or anything else he could think of.

name: Joanne Kyger
headline: Joanne Kyger, Zen-Infused Beat Generation Poet, Dies at 82
abstract: A Buddhist and author and one of the few female members of the male-dominated post-World War II cultural movement.

name: Lorraine Pearce
profession: First White House Curator, Hired by the Kennedys
headline: Lorraine Pearce Dies at 82; First White House Curator, Hired by the Kennedys
abstract: Ms. Pearce, a decorative arts scholar, helped Jacqueline Kennedy restore the presidential mansion to its 19th-century historic splendor.

name: Masha Leon
headline: Masha Leon, Society Columnist and Holocaust Survivor, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Leon survived harrowing childhood escapes from grim pre-ghetto Warsaw and Communist Siberia to mingle years later with New York’s glitterati as a writer for the world’s oldest Yiddish newspaper.

name: Chelsea Brown
headline: Chelsea Brown, of ‘Laugh-In,’ Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Brown, and actor and dancer, had a memorable role in “The Thing With Two Heads.”

name: Glenn O’Brien
headline: Glenn O’Brien, Writer and Editor Who Gained Fame With Warhol, Dies at 70
abstract: After Mr. O’Brien was invited to work on Andy Warhol’s magazine, his 15 minutes in the New York spotlight lasted more than 40 years.

name: Tim Pigott-Smith
headline: Tim Pigott-Smith, Actor Who Put Prince Charles on the Throne, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Pigott-Smith was playing Willy Loman in a production of “Death of a Salesman” that was about to open.

name: Eugene Lang
headline: Eugene Lang, Investor Who Made College Dreams a Reality, Dies at 98
abstract: One of Mr. Lang’s many acts of generosity came in a spur-of-the-moment promise to an East Harlem sixth-grade class that he would pay for their college educations.

name: Hans Dehmelt
headline: Hans Dehmelt, Nobel Laureate for Isolating Electrons, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Dehmelt shared the 1989 Nobel Prize in Physics for developing methods to trap a single ion or electron, allowing for a more precise way to measure their properties.

name: David Peel
headline: David Peel, Downtown Singer and Marijuana Evangelist, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Peel’s best-known song was “I Like Marijuana.” His best-known friends were John Lennon and Yoko Ono.

name: Mary Anderson
profession: Founder of the Outdoor Cooperative REI
headline: Mary Anderson, a Founder of the Outdoor Cooperative REI, Dies at 107
abstract: Dissatisfaction with ice axes available in the United States led Mrs. Anderson and her husband to start the Recreational Equipment Cooperative in 1938.

name: Louis Sarno
profession: Moved to Africa to Preserve Ancestral Music
headline: Louis Sarno Dies at 62; Moved to Africa to Preserve Ancestral Music
abstract: An American who became a cultural go-between for generations of Bayaka people.

name: Carme Chacón
headline: Carme Chacón, Spain’s First Female Defense Minister, Dies at 46
abstract: Ms. Chacón, a leading Socialist politician, became a symbol of the country’s progress toward gender equality.

name: Julian Stanczak
headline: Julian Stanczak, Abstract Painter, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Stanczak, a leading figure in the Op Art movement, once said that creating art was his attempt to forget about war traumas in a Soviet labor camp.

name: Linda Hopkins
headline: Linda Hopkins, a Tony-Winning Actress and Singer, Dies at 92
abstract: Her soaring, gospel-rooted voice was heard on Broadway in “Inner City,” “Black and Blue” and her long-running one-woman show, “Me and Bessie.”

name: Joseph Rascoff
profession: Had Rolling Stones Tours Under His Thumb
headline: Joseph Rascoff, Who Had Rolling Stones’ Tours Under His Thumb, Dies at 71
abstract: He preferred classical music, but Mr. Rascoff became a business manager and tour producer for powerhouse rock ’n’ roll acts including U2 and Paul Simon.

name: Frederick B. Lacey
headline: Frederick B. Lacey, Who Prosecuted Corruption in New Jersey, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Lacey won convictions against mayors, other public officials and Mafia members before becoming a judge whose cases included the French Connection trial.

name: J. Geils
profession: Bands Catchy Pop Hits Colored the 1980s
headline: J. Geils, Whose Band’s Catchy Pop Hits Colored the 1980s, Dies at 71
abstract: “Centerfold,” “Freeze-Frame” and “Love Stinks” were among the band’s most popular songs.

name: Dorothy Mengering
profession: David Lettermans Mother and Comic Foil
headline: Dorothy Mengering, David Letterman’s Mother and Comic Foil, Dies at 95
abstract: A white-haired avatar of small-town values who became a beloved regular on her son’s shows, she showed off her pies and interviewed Hillary Clinton.

name: Patricia McKissack
headline: Patricia McKissack, Prolific Author Who Championed Black Heroes, Dies at 72
abstract: Ms. McKissack looked for children’s literature about black history and saw a void. So she filled it, writing more than 100 books.

name: Charlie Murphy
profession: Chappelles Show Star and Eddies Brother
headline: Charlie Murphy, ‘Chappelle’s Show’ Star and Eddie’s Brother, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Murphy is best known for a skit in which he would spoof himself, regaling viewers with stories of his encounters with celebrities like Rick James.

name: Joan See
profession: Acted in TV Ads and Helped Others Do
headline: Joan See, Who Acted in TV Ads and Helped Others Do That, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. See’s success in commercials for products like American Express, Thomas’s English Muffins and Tide led her to start the Actors in Advertising School.

name: Steelers Chairman Dan Rooney
profession: N.F.L. Force and Link to Footballs Past
headline: Steelers Chairman Dan Rooney, 84, Dies; N.F.L. Force and Link to Football’s Past
abstract: Rooney began his time with the team as a water boy at age 9 and helped build one of the most successful franchises in N.F.L. history.

name: Bob Cerv
headline: Bob Cerv, Three-Time Yankee and One-Time All-Star, Dies at 91
abstract: Cerv, an outfielder and slugger who was a backup in three stints with the Mickey Mantle-era Yankees, also played for the Athletics, with whom he was an All-Star in 1958; the Angels; and the Colt .45s.

name: Christopher Morahan
profession: Producer and Director of The Jewel in the Crown
headline: Christopher Morahan, a Producer and Director of ‘The Jewel in the Crown,’ Dies at 87
abstract: Beyond that heralded TV series and plays for television, Mr. Morahan’s career spanned the stage and film.

name: Wayne Hardin
profession: Hall of Fame Football Coach at Navy
headline: Wayne Hardin, Hall of Fame Football Coach at Navy, Dies at 91
abstract: Hardin led the Midshipmen to five straight victories over Army and later helped Temple to its first bowl-game win. He joined the College Football Hall of Fame in 2013.

name: Mark Wainberg
headline: Dr. Mark Wainberg, Who Identified a Key AIDS Drug, Dies at 71
abstract: As a microbiologist, he found that the drug Lamivudine was effective against H.I.V., and he later became a global champion of AIDS treatment and awareness.

name: Al Golin
headline: Al Golin, PR Man Whose Vision Helped Make McDonald’s a Success, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Golin was a young press agent when he made a cold call to Ray Kroc in 1957 that began a 60-year relationship and helped turn the fast-food restaurant with the golden arches into a household word.

name: Michael Ballhaus
headline: Michael Ballhaus, an Oscar-Nominated Cinematographer, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Ballhaus, who was nominated for three Academy Awards, was a favorite of Martin Scorsese, Rainer Werner Fassbinder and other notable directors.

name: Bruce Langhorne
headline: Bruce Langhorne, Guitarist Who Inspired ‘Mr. Tambourine Man,’ Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Langhorne played on many influential folk-rock albums, most notably Bob Dylan’s landmark “Bringing It All Back Home.”

name: Frederick Borsch
headline: Frederick Borsch, Bishop Who Worked to Empower Minorities, Dies at 81
abstract: As leader of the Episcopal Diocese of Los Angeles from 1988 to 2002, he elevated female and Hispanic clergy. And he championed the ordination of gay men and lesbians.

name: Sylvia Moy
headline: Sylvia Moy, Motown Songwriter Who Worked With Stevie Wonder, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Moy was a Motown record producer who helped write hits like “My Cherie Amour” and “Uptight (Everything’s Alright).”

name: Allan Holdsworth
headline: Allan Holdsworth, Virtuoso Guitarist Who Amazed His Peers, Dies at 70
abstract: Endlessly exploring his instrument, Mr. Holdsworth played in seminal bands, including Soft Machine, before making a series of solo albums.

name: Ruth Sulzberger Holmberg
profession: Newspaper Publisher Born for the Job
headline: Ruth Sulzberger Holmberg, Newspaper Publisher Born for the Job, Dies at 96
abstract: A member of the family that controls The New York Times, Mrs. Holmberg challenged racial barriers, political skulduggery and environmental adversaries as publisher of The Chattanooga Times.

name: Trish Vradenburg
headline: Trish Vradenburg, Crusader Against Alzheimer’s, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Vradenburg, a sitcom writer whose mother died of complications of the disease, and her husband raised millions for research and established their own organization to generate greater awareness.

name: Harry Huskey
headline: Harry Huskey, Pioneering Computer Scientist, Is Dead at 101
abstract: One of the last surviving scientists in the forefront of the computer revolution, Dr. Huskey helped develop what was once billed as the first personal computer.

name: Robert Sadoff
headline: Robert Sadoff, Psychiatrist Who Assessed Murder Defendants, Dies at 81
abstract: A founder of modern forensic psychiatry, Dr. Sadoff once estimated that he had evaluated as many as 10,000 defendants in criminal cases.

name: John T. Curtin
headline: John T. Curtin, Judge Who Desegregated Buffalo Schools, Dies at 95
abstract: Judge Curtin wrote that the defendants had violated the right to equal protection under the laws “by intentionally causing and maintaining a segregated school system.”

name: Magdalena Abakanowicz
headline: Magdalena Abakanowicz, Sculptor of Brooding Forms, Dies at 86
abstract: The Polish artist’s works ranged from woven shrouds and tree trunks to mythic human figures that evoked the dark forces at work in the 20th century.

name: John Noonan
headline: John Noonan, Federal Judge Who Served for Three Decades, Dies at 90
abstract: Judge Noonan wrote opinions as a jurist on the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals on contentious issues such as assisted suicide and illegal immigration.

name: Barkley L. Hendricks
profession: Portraitist of a New Black Pride
headline: Barkley L. Hendricks, Portraitist of a New Black Pride, Dies at 72
abstract: Having seen virtually no black subjects among the portraits he admired in Europe, Mr. Hendricks painted friends, family and strangers who conveyed a culture of assertiveness.

name: Sandy Gallin
headline: Sandy Gallin, 76, Talent Manager Adored by Stars, Dies
abstract: Among Mr. Gallin’s clients were Dolly Parton, Richard Pryor, Cher, Michael Jackson and Joan Rivers, and he became a role model for gays and lesbians in entertainment.

name: Elizabeth Sargent
profession: Poet and Last Tenant Above Carnegie Hall
headline: Elizabeth Sargent, 96, Poet and Last Tenant Above Carnegie Hall, Dies
abstract: When Ms. Sargent, whose work was known for its frank description of sexuality and its slant rhymes, moved in 2010, it marked the end of an artist enclave.

name: Tom Fleming
headline: Tom Fleming, 65, New York City Marathon Winner, Dies
abstract: Mr. Fleming, a contemporary of Frank Shorter and Bill Rodgers who preferred to train 140 to 150 miles a week, won New York in 1973 and 1975.

name: Albert Freedman
headline: Albert Freedman, Producer of Rigged 1950s Quiz Show, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Freedman sought higher ratings for the show “Twenty-One” by giving questions to contestants in advance, in the hopes of creating more dramatic competition.

name: Erin Moran
headline: Erin Moran, Who Played Joanie on ‘Happy Days,’ Dies at 56
abstract: Ms. Moran’s biggest role was as the sweet but mischievous Joanie, who became a major character on the show and earned a spinoff, “Joanie Loves Chachi.”

name: Jay Dickey
headline: Jay Dickey, Arkansas Lawmaker Who Blocked Gun Research, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Dickey prevented the government from investigating the public health effects of gun violence, but long after leaving office, he did an about-face.

name: Robert M. Pirsig
profession: Author of Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance
headline: Robert M. Pirsig, Author of ‘Zen and the Art of Motorcycle Maintenance,’ Dies at 88
abstract: The novel became an unlikely publishing phenomenon in the mid-1970s and a touchstone in the waning days of the counterculture.

name: Kate O’Beirne
headline: Kate O’Beirne, National Review Editor and Columnist, Dies at 67
abstract: A stalwart of the neoconservative movement who was Washington editor of National Review and wrote its “Bread and Circuses” column.

name: Michael Bogdanov
headline: Michael Bogdanov, Shakespearean Stage Director, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Bogdanov also directed plays by Molière, Goethe, Chekhov, Gogol and Dylan Thomas, as well as musicals and operas. But a contemporary play nearly put him in jail.

name: Dennis Edwards
headline: Dennis Edwards, Judge Who Presided Over Trial of Lennon’s Killer, Dies at 95
abstract: Judge Edwards was serving as an acting Supreme Court justice in New York when he sentenced Mark David Chapman in the 1980 murder of John Lennon.

name: Dennis Edwards
headline: Dennis Edwards, Former Temptations Lead Singer, Dies at 74
abstract: His resonant voice was an essential part of the group’s success when it embraced psychedelic funk on songs like “Papa Was a Rollin’ Stone.”

name: Greg Marius
headline: Greg Marius, Impresario of Harlem Street Ball, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Marius’s Entertainers Basketball Classic at Rucker Park in Harlem featured playground legends, professional basketball players, corporate sponsors and exuberant crowds.

name: Benjamin R. Barber
headline: Benjamin R. Barber, Author of ‘Jihad vs. McWorld,’ Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Barber’s 1995 book presciently analyzed the forces leading to the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks and the rise in tribalism around the world.

name: Chuck Wielgus
profession: Empowered U.S. Swimming and Apologized in a Scandal
headline: Chuck Wielgus, 67, Dies; Empowered U.S. Swimming and Apologized in a Scandal
abstract: Mr. Wielgus oversaw great Olympic success but was criticized for his response to accusations of sexual abuse by coaches.

name: Jonathan Demme
headline: Jonathan Demme, Oscar-Winning Director, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Mr. Demme, an auteur whose films included documentaries and narrative features, won an Academy Award for “The Silence of the Lambs.”

name: Agustín Edwards
headline: Agustín Edwards, Conservative Media Tycoon in Chile, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Edwards was heir to the company that published El Mercurio, an influential right-wing publication that helped overthrow Salvador Allende in 1973.

name: Leonard Reiffel
headline: Leonard Reiffel, Who Studied Lunar Nuclear Bomb, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Reiffel revealed that the Air Force had been interested in staging a surprise explosion on or near the moon, and that its goal was propaganda.

name: Martha Lavey
headline: Martha Lavey, a Leading Lady of Chicago Theater, Dies at 60
abstract: An actress by training, Ms. Lavey was artistic director of Steppenwolf Theater during a period of great expansion.

name: Gary Steigman
profession: Teased Out the Universes Dark Secrets
headline: Gary Steigman, Who Teased Out the Universe’s Dark Secrets, Dies at 76
abstract: Dr. Steigman helped show that most matter in the universe was not made of atoms, a finding that led to modern conceptions of dark matter and dark energy.

name: Joseph Lifschutz
headline: Dr. Joseph Lifschutz, 92, Dies; Asserted Confidentiality Right for Therapists
abstract: Dr. Lifschutz spent a weekend in jail in 1969 defending his position that a privilege of confidentiality should be extended to psychotherapists.

name: Vito Acconci
headline: Vito Acconci, Performance Artist and Uncommon Architect, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Acconci made a radical career turn in the 1970s, when he abandoned the gallery world and remade himself as an architect.

name: Florence Finch
headline: Florence Finch, Unsung War Hero Who Took On Japanese, Dies at 101
abstract: During World War II, Mrs. Finch quietly undermined Japan when it occupied the Philippines, and was tortured for it. Then she quietly raised a family in the United States.

name: Thomas Forkner
headline: Thomas Forkner, Waffle House Co-Founder, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Forkner met his future business partner, Joseph W. Rogers, by selling him a house. They went on to build a chain of restaurants on all-night service and filling fare.

name: Norman T. Hatch
profession: Filmed Grisly World War II Combat
headline: Norman T. Hatch, Who Filmed Grisly World War II Combat, Dies at 96
abstract: He won a 1945 Academy Award for vivid documentary footage of combat between the United States and Japan on Tarawa Atoll.

name: Richard Haynes
headline: Richard Haynes, Flashy and Successful Houston Lawyer, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Haynes inherited the mantle of the legendary Texas lawyer Percy Foreman when he began compiling a spectacular record of acquittals in seemingly unwinnable cases

name: Shobha Nehru
profession: Escaped Holocaust and Married Into Indian Politics
headline: Shobha Nehru Dies at 108; Escaped Holocaust and Married Into Indian Politics
abstract: After marrying B.K. Nehru in 1935 and moving to India, Mrs. Nehru saw religious and ethnic violence convulse both her native and adopted countries.

name: Dick Contino
headline: Dick Contino, Accordion Heartthrob, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Contino, the inspiration for a notable novella, had been a sensation until changing times and resentment over draft evasion hurt his career.

name: Malcolm Toon
profession: but His Death Went Largely Unreported
headline: Malcolm Toon Made Waves as a Diplomat, but His Death Went Largely Unreported
abstract: The news of his death in 2009 circulated in and around his North Carolina hometown, but did not make headlines the way he himself had during his Foreign Service career.

name: William M. Hoffman
profession: Wrote the Pioneering AIDS Play As Is
headline: William M. Hoffman, Who Wrote the Pioneering AIDS Play ‘As Is,’ Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Hoffman began his career as a book editor and also wrote the groundbreaking libretto for John Corigliano’s opera “The Ghosts of Versailles.”

name: Vinod Khanna
headline: Vinod Khanna, Bollywood Movie Idol, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Khanna, one of the most well-known stars in India, also had a career in public service and at one point became a follower of the guru known as Osho.

name: Kenny Sears
headline: Kenny Sears, Knicks’ Two-Time Leading Scorer, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Sears, a 6-foot-9 forward who was with the Knicks for six full seasons, starting in 1955, was the first basketball player to appear on the cover of Sports Illustrated.

name: Hubert L. Dreyfus
profession: Philosopher of the Limits of Computers
headline: Hubert L. Dreyfus, Philosopher of the Limits of Computers, Dies at 87
abstract: Professor Dreyfus’s 1972 book “What Computers Can’t Do” made him a scourge and eventually an inspiration to researchers in artificial intelligence.

name: Luis Olmo
headline: Luis Olmo, a Pioneering Puerto Rican Baseball Player, Dies at 97
abstract: Olmo broke in with the Brooklyn Dodgers in 1943 and became the first position player in the major leagues from Puerto Rico.

name: June LeBell
headline: June LeBell, Pioneering Radio Announcer, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. LeBell became a familiar voice on WQXR, hosting “Kitchen Classics” and “IBM’s Salute to the Arts.”

name: Jean Stein
headline: Jean Stein, Who Chronicled Wealth, Fame and Influence, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Stein used oral histories to sketch vivid accounts of Edie Sedgwick, Robert Kennedy and powerful families of Los Angeles.

name: Bruce Hampton
headline: Bruce Hampton, 70, Jam Scene Patriarch, Dies After Collapsing Onstage
abstract: The career of an eclectic musician spanned decades before what turned out to be a final show in Atlanta, a concert in honor of his birthday.

name: Sam Mele
headline: Sam Mele, Major League Player, Manager and Scout, Dies at 95
abstract: Mele played for six teams from 1947 to 1956, managed the Twins to the 1965 pennant and had a long association with the Red Sox.

name: Leo Thorsness
profession: Decorated Veteran Held Captive With McCain
headline: Leo Thorsness, Decorated Veteran Held Captive With McCain, Dies at 85
abstract: Colonel Thorsness received the Medal of Honor. After his plane was shot down, he was brutalized for years at the notorious prison known as the Hanoi Hilton.

name: Burton Watson
profession: Influential Translator of Classical Asian Literature
headline: Burton Watson, 91, Influential Translator of Classical Asian Literature, Dies
abstract: Mr. Watson opened up the world of Japanese and Chinese texts to generations of English-speaking readers, with dozens of his works still in print.

name: Ann Sneed
profession: Brought Jazz to Schools and Concert Halls
headline: Ann Sneed, 87, Dies; Brought Jazz to Schools and Concert Halls
abstract: Ms. Sneed founded the nonprofit International Art of Jazz, which for 35 years promoted the music and fostered a love of the art.

name: Gustave Newman
headline: Gustave Newman, Defense Lawyer in Sensational Cases, Dies at 90
