abstract: A lion of New York’s white-collar criminal defense bar, Mr. Newman had a reputation for tackling the toughest cases.

name: Solly Walker
headline: Solly Walker, Trailblazing St. John’s Basketball Player, Dies at 85
abstract: Walker, St. John’s first black basketball player, was also the first black player to play on Kentucky’s home court, in 1951.

name: Julius Youngner
headline: Julius Youngner, Polio Vaccine Pioneer, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Youngner was the last surviving member of the original three-man research team assembled by Dr. Jonas Salk to address the American polio scourge.

name: Daliah Lavi
profession: Actress in Both Dramas and Spoofs
headline: Daliah Lavi, Actress in Both Dramas and Spoofs, Dies at 74
abstract: The Israeli actress appeared in “Lord Jim,” the 1967 “Casino Royale” and other movies before a career as a singer and actress in Germany.

name: Adolph Kiefer
profession: Gold Medal Backstroker in the 1936 Olympics
headline: Adolph Kiefer, a Gold Medal Backstroker in the 1936 Olympics, Dies at 98
abstract: Kiefer won 58 United States championships in backstroke, individual medley and freestyle from 1935 to 1945, but World War II limited him to one Olympics.

name: A.R. Penck
headline: A.R. Penck, German Neo-Expressionist of Cold-War Era, Dies at 77
abstract: Ralf Winkler adopted the name Penck, and other aliases, to confuse the East German authorities.

name: Peter Spier
headline: Peter Spier, Illustrator of Children’s Books, Dies at 89
abstract: His “Noah’s Ark,” which won the Caldecott Medal, showed Noah’s toils, like pulling a donkey onto the ark and trying to snatch two bees out of a swarm.

name: Richard Basciano
headline: Richard Basciano, Times Square Pornography Magnate, Dies at 91
abstract: One of Mr. Basciano’s businesses gave way to Times Square redevelopment and rising property values, but one, Show World, still functions.

name: Don Gordon
profession: Steve McQueens Sidekick Onscreen and in Life
headline: Don Gordon, Steve McQueen’s Sidekick Onscreen and in Life, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Gordon starred on television and in film for decades, often playing tough-guy roles.

name: Steven Holcomb
headline: Steven Holcomb, Gold Medal Bobsledder Who Beat Vision Problems, Dies at 37
abstract: Holcomb, overcoming a degenerative eye disease, piloted a four-man team in 2010 to the first American Olympic gold medal in the event in 62 years.

name: Heinz Kessler
headline: Heinz Kessler, Who Led East Germany’s Military, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Kessler was one of the very few leading Communists sentenced and jailed for crimes committed before the Berlin Wall fell in 1989.

name: Edwin Sherin
headline: Edwin Sherin, Theater and ‘Law & Order’ Director, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Sherin directed James Earl Jones on Broadway in “The Great White Hope” and enjoyed a successful career in television.

name: C. Jackson Grayson
headline: C. Jackson Grayson, 93, Nixon’s Anti-Inflation Overseer, Dies
abstract: Dr. Grayson was dean of a business school in 1971 when President Nixon named him to lead the first peacetime price control program in the country.

name: Anne Morrissy Merick
headline: Anne Morrissy Merick, a Pioneer From Yale to Vietnam, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Morrissy Merick, the first woman admitted to the press box of the Yale Bowl, later helped get a restriction against women covering the Vietnam War reversed.

name: Mario Maglieri
headline: Mario Maglieri, Who Coddled Rockers at His Clubs, Dies at 93
abstract: At Whisky a Go Go and the Rainbow Bar & Grill, Mr. Maglieri fed, encouraged and, when necessary, punched his famous patrons.

name: Hugh Thomas
headline: Hugh Thomas, Prodigious Author of Spanish History, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Thomas is best known for magisterial works on Spain’s past. He was also an ally of Margaret Thatcher’s during her years at 10 Downing Street.

name: Jack Tilton
profession: Art Dealer With an Eye for the New
headline: Jack Tilton, Art Dealer With an Eye for the New, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Tilton, who began his career at the Betty Parsons Gallery and saw art dealing as exploring, had a thirst for discovery.

name: Christopher Boykin
profession: Half of the MTV Odd Couple Rob & Big
headline: Christopher Boykin, Half of the MTV Odd Couple ‘Rob & Big,’ Dies at 45
abstract: Mr. Boykin, known as Big Black, was the skateboarder Rob Dyrdek’s bodyguard and buddy on their reality show “Rob & Big,” and later appeared on “Rob Dyrdek’s Fantasy Factory.”

name: Robert H. Phelps
profession: Editor at The Times and Boston Globe
headline: Robert H. Phelps, Editor at The Times and Boston Globe, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Phelps missed a scoop on the Watergate scandal but oversaw the coverage in major series on school desegregation and abuses at a transit agency that won Pulitzer Prizes.

name: William J. Baumol
profession: One of the Great Economists of His Generation
headline: William J. Baumol, 95, ‘One of the Great Economists of His Generation,’ Dies
abstract: A Princeton and N.Y.U. professor, he identified Baumol’s cost disease, which explains why the cost of services rises faster than the cost of goods.

name: Qian Qichen
headline: Qian Qichen, Pragmatic Chinese Envoy, Dies at 89
abstract: As foreign minister and vice premier, Mr. Qian shaped a foreign policy that helped China chip away at its isolation from the West after the Tiananmen Square massacre.

name: Stan Weston
profession: Sent G.I. Joe Marching Into Childhoods of Millions
headline: Stan Weston, 84, Dies; Sent G.I. Joe Marching Into Childhoods of Millions
abstract: Mr. Weston, inspired by the success of the Barbie doll, introduced a line of rugged heroes. Hundreds of millions of the action figures have been sold.

name: Judith Stein
headline: Judith Stein, Author on Liberalism and Economics, Dies at 77
abstract: Professor Stein, who taught history at City College for 50 years, was known for her analysis of the black nationalist Marcus Garvey.

name: Nicholas Sand
headline: Nicholas Sand, Chemist Who Sought to Bring LSD to the World, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Sand earned a reputation in the 1960s for making some of the purest LSD on the market, including Orange Sunshine, before the law finally caught up with him.

name: Eddie N. Williams
profession: Ran Leading Black Think Tank for Decades
headline: Eddie N. Williams, Who Ran Leading Black Think Tank for Decades, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Williams transformed the Joint Center for Political and Economic Studies into an unrivaled source of research on the state of black America.

name: Allan H. Meltzer
headline: Allan H. Meltzer, Conservative Economist, Dies at 89
abstract: He was an opponent of government bailouts who was credited with coining the phrase, “Capitalism without failure is like religion without sin.”

name: Henry Chung
profession: Helped Bring Hunans Flavors to America
headline: Henry Chung, Who Helped Bring Hunan’s Flavors to America, Dies at 98
abstract: Driven by his grandmother’s teachings, Mr. Chung opened San Francisco restaurants that focused on the garlic, spice and ginger of Hunanese cooking.

name: Yale Lary
profession: Force on the Detroit Lions Title-Winning Teams of the 1950s
headline: Yale Lary, a Force on the Detroit Lions’ Title-Winning Teams of the 1950s, Dies at 86
abstract: Lary, a Hall of Famer, was a safety and a punter. Although he was small, his “speed and quickness made him a real ballhawk,” said Raymond Berry, a Hall of Fame receiver for the Baltimore Colts.

name: Chuck Davis
profession: Brought African Dance Traditions to America
headline: Chuck Davis, Who Brought African Dance Traditions to America, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Davis, founder of the DanceAfrica festival, lived by the mantra “Peace, love and respect for everybody.”

name: Powers Boothe
profession: Actor Known for Deadwood and Other Dark Roles
headline: Powers Boothe, Actor Known for ‘Deadwood’ and Other Dark Roles, Dies at 68
abstract: The actor had lent his burly frame and Texas drawl to TV and films since the 1970s.

name: Steve Palermo
headline: Steve Palermo, Umpire Whose Career Was Ended by a Bullet, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Palermo was shot in 1991 while defending two waitresses from an attack outside a Dallas restaurant. He lived in chronic pain but had no regrets.

name: Thomas V. Daily
profession: Bishop With Legacy Tarnished by Response to Abuse
headline: Thomas V. Daily, Bishop With Legacy Tarnished by Response to Abuse, Dies at 89
abstract: Bishop Daily raised tens of millions of dollars to repair schools and churches, but his last years were marred by criticism of how he had handled allegations of sexual abuse.

name: Brad Grey
headline: Brad Grey, Former Chairman of Paramount Pictures, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Grey, who played a pivotal role in the creation of television hits like “The Sopranos,” helped blend the art of talent management with TV and film production.

name: Ian Brady
headline: Ian Brady, Unrepentant Killer of British Children, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Brady and his lover, Myra Hindley, were known as the Moors Murderers. He tortured and killed children, then buried them in a remote area.

name: Jerry Canterbury
profession: Paralysis Led to Informed Consent Laws
headline: Jerry Canterbury, Whose Paralysis Led to Informed Consent Laws, Is Dead at 78
abstract: A surgery left Mr. Canterbury partly paralyzed at 19 led to a ruling that transformed how doctors deal with patients in evaluating the risks of treatment.

name: Thomas A. Bolan
profession: Understated Force in New York Law
headline: Thomas A. Bolan, Understated Force in New York Law, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Bolan was, next to Roy M. Cohn, the quieter half of an odd couple at a potent law firm and a major player in Republican politics in New York.

name: Lee Hall
headline: Lee Hall, Artist and de Kooning Biographer, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Hall was an abstract landscape painter who also served as president of the Rhode Island School of Design during a difficult period there.

name: Jean Fritz
headline: Jean Fritz, Who Wrote History Books for Children, Dies at 101
abstract: Her works were full of human narratives and quirks, backed by engaging prose and deep archival research.

name: Lloyd Cotsen
profession: Collector of the Ordinary and the Odd
headline: Lloyd Cotsen, Collector of the Ordinary and the Odd, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Cotsen, who sold Neutrogena for $924 million, amassed diverse treasures like children’s books or bamboo baskets in finding “the extraordinary in the ordinary.”

name: Chris Cornell
headline: Chris Cornell, Soundgarden and Audioslave Frontman, Dies at 52
abstract: The musician’s death in Detroit was “sudden and unexpected,” his representative said in a statement. The medical examiner’s office said the cause of death was suicide.

name: Roger Ailes
profession: Built Fox News Into an Empire
headline: Roger Ailes, Who Built Fox News Into an Empire, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Ailes exerted wide influence on American politics with his conservative Fox News, only to be undone by sexual harassment allegations.

name: Beatrice Trum Hunter
headline: Beatrice Trum Hunter, ‘Natural Foods Cookbook’ Author, Dies at 98
abstract: Mrs. Hunter’s book, her first of 38, was heralded as the nation’s first healthful natural foods cookbook.

name: Jeanne Button
headline: Jeanne Button, Designer of Whimsical Costumes, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Button helped define hundreds of characters in Broadway and Off Broadway plays.

name: David Levin
headline: David Levin, the Only Triple Crown Balloonist, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Levin, who passed up a law career, won ballooning’s three top events: the hot-air and gas balloon world championships, and the Gordon Bennett Cup.

name: Elinor Bunin Munroe
profession: Film and TV Graphic Designer With a Theater in Her Name
headline: Elinor Bunin Munroe, Film and TV Graphic Designer With a Theater in Her Name, Dies
abstract: Known for the film complex at Lincoln Center that bears her name, Ms. Munroe was an Emmy-winning graphic designer whose movie work included “The Producers.”

name: Anne R. Dick
headline: Anne R. Dick, Memoirist and Writer’s Muse, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Her second husband, Philip K. Dick, used their marriage and her persona in books like “The Man in the High Castle” and “Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?”

name: William Brohn
headline: William Brohn, Who Made Broadway Orchestras Sing, Dies at 84
abstract: “The central focus for you is to help the composer say what he wants to say,” Mr. Brohn said of his work as an orchestrator.

name: Stanley Greene
headline: Stanley Greene, Whose Camera Captured War’s Brutality, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Greene, one of the leading war photographers of his generation, was a founding member of Noor Images who covered global conflicts with unblinking honesty.

name: Roxcy Bolton
headline: Roxcy Bolton, Feminist Crusader for Equality, Including in Naming Hurricanes, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Bolton founded the nation’s first rape treatment center and helped persuade national weather forecasters not to name hurricanes after only women.

name: Dina Merrill
headline: Dina Merrill, Actress and Philanthropist, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Merrill’s upper-class roles often reflected her own privileged background.

name: Roger Moore
headline: Roger Moore, Who Played James Bond 007 Times, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Moore was 45 when he inherited the role and had the longest run with it.

name: Cortez Kennedy
headline: Cortez Kennedy, Hall of Fame Defensive Tackle, Dies at 48
abstract: Mr. Kennedy, who played his entire 11-year career with the Seahawks, weighed 300 pounds but possessed surprising quickness. He became the prototype for defensive linemen in the 1990s.

name: Rand Castile
headline: Rand Castile, Who Opened Doors for Asian Art, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Castile worked on both the East and West Coasts, organizing artistic and cultural programs at Japan Society in Manhattan and the Asian Art Museum of San Francisco.

name: Barbara Smith Conrad
profession: Singer at Center of Integration Dispute
headline: Barbara Smith Conrad, Singer at Center of Integration Dispute, Dies at 79
abstract: As a 19-year-old University of Texas student in 1957, Ms. Conrad became the focus of attention when a state legislator objected to her casting in a mixed-race production of “Dido and Aeneas.”

name: Jacque Fresco
headline: Jacque Fresco, Futurist Who Envisioned a Society Without Money, Dies at 101
abstract: A self-taught industrial designer, Mr. Fresco promoted an alternative society where resources would be distributed equitably by computers.

name: Amy Reed
headline: Amy Reed, Doctor Who Fought a Risky Medical Procedure, Dies at 44
abstract: Dr. Reed and her husband turned a personal calamity into a crusade to spare other women from the medical procedure that harmed her.

name: Nora Mae Lyng
profession: Actress at the Heart of Forbidden Broadway
headline: Nora Mae Lyng, Actress at the Heart of ‘Forbidden Broadway,’ Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Lyng not only inspired the show and starred in its original cast; she also invested her comic talent and meager financial resources in it.

name: Michael Bliss
headline: Michael Bliss, Historian Who Dispelled Myths of Insulin’s Discovery, Dies at 76
abstract: Professor Bliss unraveled the story behind the discovery of the hormone, which transformed diabetes from a death sentence into a manageable condition.

name: Jerry Perenchio
headline: Jerry Perenchio, Entertainment Mogul Who Advised ‘Think Big,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Perenchio promoted the first Ali-Frazier fight, produced television shows with Norman Lear and turned Univision into the dominant Hispanic TV network in the United States.

name: John Mace
profession: Voice Coach and Campaigner for Same-Sex Marriage
headline: John Mace, 97, Voice Coach and Campaigner for Same-Sex Marriage, Dies
abstract: Mr. Mace lived with his partner, known professionally as Richard Adrian Dorr, for decades, and noted Broadway performers studied at the vocal studio they ran.

name: Denis Johnson
profession: Wrote of the Failed and the Desperate
headline: Denis Johnson, Who Wrote of the Failed and the Desperate, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Johnson, the author of “Jesus’ Son,” peopled his novels, stories and poems with drifters, addicts, inmates and spies.

name: Zbigniew Brzezinski
profession: National Security Adviser to Jimmy Carter
headline: Zbigniew Brzezinski, National Security Adviser to Jimmy Carter, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Brzezinski, who guided Mr. Carter during the Iran hostage crisis and the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, had decades of influence in global affairs.

name: Ronald D. Croatti
profession: Uniform Company Chief and Undercover Boss
headline: Ronald D. Croatti, Uniform Company Chief and Undercover Boss, Dies at 74
abstract: The family business he took over from his father now supplies uniforms to nearly two million people at 300,000 businesses worldwide.

name: Jim Bunning
profession: Hall of Fame Pitcher and Blunt-Spoken Senator
headline: Jim Bunning, Hall of Fame Pitcher and Blunt-Spoken Senator, Dies at 85
abstract: After a 17-season career in the major leagues, mostly with the Tigers and the Phillies, Mr. Bunning became a fervently conservative politician in Kentucky.

name: Gregg Allman
profession: Influential Force Behind the Allman Brothers Band
headline: Gregg Allman, Influential Force Behind the Allman Brothers Band, Dies at 69
abstract: The singer, keyboardist and songwriter was a founder of the Allman Brothers Band and a composer of songs like “Whipping Post” and “Midnight Rider.”

name: John Severson
headline: John Severson, Surfer Who Illustrated Allure of Waves, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Severson founded Surfer magazine in 1962 and created paintings, films and photographs depicting the surfing lifestyle.

name: Ann Birstein
headline: Ann Birstein, Memoirist and Novelist, Dies at 89
abstract: Her difficult marriage to Alfred Kazin arose in some of her writings.

name: Frank Deford
headline: Frank Deford, a Literary Storyteller of Sport, Dies at 78
abstract: A longtime contributor to NPR, Sports Illustrated and HBO, Mr. Deford was the only sportswriter to receive a National Humanities Medal.

name: Manuel Noriega
profession: Dictator Ousted by U.S. in Panama
headline: Manuel Noriega, Dictator Ousted by U.S. in Panama, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Noriega, known for drug ties and double-dealing with Washington, was unseated in 1989 in what was then the largest American military action since Vietnam.

name: Alistair Horne
profession: War Historian and Onetime British Spy
headline: Alistair Horne, War Historian and Onetime British Spy, Dies at 91
abstract: During the Iraq war, President George W. Bush read Mr. Horne’s book on the French-Algerian war and invited the author to the White House.

name: Raymond J. Pfeifer
headline: Raymond J. Pfeifer, 9/11 Firefighter Who Sought Care for Survivors, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Pfeifer went to the World Trade Center to help the day of the terrorist attack and remained for months, clearing debris. He then led a fight for benefits for emergency workers.

name: Bill Woods
profession: New York Urban Planner and Hero of the Harbor
headline: Bill Woods, New York Urban Planner and ‘Hero of the Harbor,’ Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Woods mobilized public and private constituencies to revitalize New York’s waterfront, helping to coordinate various transportation, recreation and housing projects.

name: Frances Sliwa
headline: Frances Sliwa, the Guardian Angels’ One-Woman Kitchen Cabinet, Dies at 93
abstract: Mrs. Sliwa became the bookkeeper, administrator and publicist for the red-beret-wearing neighborhood patrol group her son, Curtis, formed in New York in 1979.

name: Laura Biagiotti
profession: Designer Called the Queen of Cashmere
headline: Laura Biagiotti, Designer Called the Queen of Cashmere, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Biagiotti, who abandoned her early plans to be an archaeologist to join her mother’s tailoring studio, was an entrepreneur known for elegant fashions made from goat’s wool.

name: David Lewiston
profession: Recorded Indigenous Music Far and Wide
headline: David Lewiston, Who Recorded Indigenous Music Far and Wide, Dies at 88
abstract: No sound was alien to Mr. Lewiston, whose work on albums for the Nonesuch label took him from Indonesia to Tibet to Guatemala to Kashmir.

name: Stanley F. Whitman
profession: Saw Luxury as a Shopping Center Lure
headline: Stanley F. Whitman, Who Saw Luxury as a Shopping Center Lure, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Whitman was hailed as a visionary in the mid-1960s when he built an open-air shopping center near Miami Beach for luxury retailers.

name: Fred A. Kummerow
headline: Fred A. Kummerow, an Early Opponent of Trans Fats, Dies at 102
abstract: Artificial trans fats were ruled unsafe by the Food and Drug Administration partly in response to a lawsuit that Professor Kummerow filed against the agency.

name: Roberto De Vicenzo
profession: Golf Champion Remembered More for a Gaffe
headline: Roberto De Vicenzo, a Golf Champion Remembered More for a Gaffe, Dies at 94
abstract: Signing an incorrect scorecard cost De Vicenzo a chance at a playoff for the 1968 Masters title.

name: Jiri Belohlavek
profession: Conductor and Leading Interpreter of Czech Music
headline: Jiri Belohlavek, Conductor and Leading Interpreter of Czech Music, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Belohlavek led the Czech Philharmonic and was associated with some of the world’s greatest orchestras, specializing in the music of Dvorak, Janacek and other countrymen.

name: Reinhold Hanning
profession: Former Auschwitz Guard Convicted a Year Ago
headline: Reinhold Hanning, Former Auschwitz Guard Convicted a Year Ago, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Hanning was sentenced to five years in jail as an accessory to 170,000 murders while he worked at the camp, but he never spent time behind bars.

name: E. L. Woody
headline: E. L. Woody, ‘King of the Paparazzi,’ Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Woody, who gave himself the title, scrambled to the top of the celebrity photography profession, chronicling the after-hours exploits of Hollywood stars for a tabloid market.

name: Chandraswamy
profession: Fell From Favor as a Guru to Celebrities
headline: Chandraswamy, Who Fell From Favor as a Guru to Celebrities, Dies at 66
abstract: He was a counselor to Elizabeth Taylor and the Sultan of Brunei who built a vast network of political connections and faced many criminal investigations.

name: Eric Broadley
headline: Eric Broadley, Acclaimed Designer of Championship Racecars, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Broadley, a onetime cabinetmaker from Britain, created Lola cars and similarly speedy machines that won the Indianapolis 500 and numerous other races.

name: Elliot Martin
headline: Elliot Martin, Prolific Theater Producer, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Martin developed a knack for discovering new talent and for redeeming scripts that fellow producers had rejected as potential flops.

name: Marie Cosindas
profession: Photographs Brought Color to the Fore
headline: Marie Cosindas, Whose Photographs Brought Color to the Fore, Dies at 93
abstract: At a time when black-and-white images dominated photography, Ms. Cosindas used Polaroid film to make portraits and still lifes that opened up the medium to color.

name: Jack McCloskey
profession: Architect of Detroit Pistons Bad Boys Teams
headline: Jack McCloskey, Architect of Detroit Pistons’ ‘Bad Boys’ Teams, Dies at 91
abstract: By drafting and trading for rugged players like Dennis Rodman and Bill Laimbeer, Mr. McCloskey built a pugnacious squad that won two N.B.A. titles.

name: Sara Ehrman
profession: Outspoken Feminist With Deep Ties to Clintons
headline: Sara Ehrman, Outspoken Feminist With Deep Ties to Clintons, Dies at 98
abstract: Mrs. Ehrman counseled President Bill Clinton on the Israeli-Arab conflict but was best known as for advising a young Hillary Rodham not to move to Arkansas to marry Mr. Clinton.

name: Jean Sammet
profession: Co-Designer of a Pioneering Computer Language
headline: Jean Sammet, Co-Designer of a Pioneering Computer Language, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Sammet was a software engineer on COBOL, a programming language that was written in the 1950s but still underpins basic business operations today.

name: Jimmy Piersall
profession: Mental Illness Was Portrayed in Fear Strikes Out
headline: Jimmy Piersall, Whose Mental Illness Was Portrayed in ‘Fear Strikes Out,’ Dies at 87
abstract: The often outrageous player and broadcaster was a top center fielder and a two-time All-Star, but a breakdown almost ended his career as it was starting.

name: Wendell Burton
headline: Wendell Burton, Actor and Megachurch Minister, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Burton was cast opposite Liza Minnelli in the 1969 film “The Sterile Cuckoo.”

name: Jack O’Neill
headline: Jack O’Neill, Surfer Who Made the Wetsuit Famous, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. O’Neill changed the surfing industry with suits that were advanced enough to defy frigid waters, and he helped surfers be recognized as serious athletes.

name: Neil Gordon
profession: Academic and Author of Cerebral Political Novels
headline: Neil Gordon, Academic and Author of Cerebral Political Novels, Dies at 59
abstract: His novels about radical politics, including “The Company You Keep,” challenged readers with biblical parables and ethical dilemmas.

name: Jeffrey Tate
headline: Jeffrey Tate, Conductor Whose Life Was a Worldwide Whirlwind, Dies at 74
abstract: An English maestro who ultimately arrived at his calling after detouring to a medical degree.

name: Peter Sallis
profession: Voice of Wallace and Gromit Cartoons
headline: Peter Sallis, Voice of ‘Wallace and Gromit’ Cartoons, Dies at 96
abstract: The British actor played the cheese-loving inventor Wallace in the cartoons and was a star in the sitcom “Last of the Summer Wine.”

name: Adnan Khashoggi
headline: Adnan Khashoggi, High-Living Saudi Arms Trader, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Khashoggi rose to spectacular wealth in the 1970s and ’80s and was involved in many of his era’s highest-profile scandals, including Iran-contra.

name: Donald J. Vidrine
profession: Supervisor on Ill-Fated Deepwater Horizon Rig
headline: Donald J. Vidrine, Supervisor on Ill-Fated Deepwater Horizon Rig, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Vidrine took a plea bargain in a devastating oil rig explosion that killed 11 workers and spilled millions of gallons of crude into the Gulf of Mexico.

name: Sergei Vikharev
headline: Sergei Vikharev, Russian Ballet Master Who Revived the Past, Dies at 55
abstract: Mr. Vikharev sought to replace shorter, streamlined versions of “The Sleeping Beauty” with stagings that more closely resembled the original choreography.

name: Alois Mock
headline: Alois Mock, Austrian Who Helped Tear Down Iron Curtain (Literally), Dies at 82
abstract: In 1989, Mr. Mock, the Austrian foreign minister, helped his Hungarian counterpart to cut open the wire fence between the countries just months before the Berlin Wall fell.

name: Jack Trout
profession: Fought for Consumers Minds and Money
headline: Jack Trout, Who Fought for Consumers’ Minds and Money, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Trout developed the marketing strategy of positioning with Al Ries and advised, among others, the casino mogul Donald Trump and David Axelrod.

name: Charles Simmons
headline: Charles Simmons, Novelist Who Satirized His Other Job, Book Reviewing, Dies at 92
abstract: The writer, who once worked at the The New York Times Book Review, published a sendup of his former employer in the novel “The Belle Lettres Papers.”

name: Elena Verdugo
headline: Elena Verdugo, Who Lifted Latina Image on TV, Dies at 92
abstract: Portraying the astute nurse on “Marcus Welby, M.D.,” Ms. Verdugo was credited with inspiring Hispanic women to strive for greater self-respect.

name: Juan Goytisolo
headline: Juan Goytisolo, Novelist Who Took Aim at Spanish Conservatism, Dies at 86
abstract: One of Spain’s most celebrated writers, Mr. Goytisolo authored experimental novels and stories that savaged his country’s religious and sexual conservatism.

name: Juliana Young Koo
headline: Juliana Young Koo, Chinese Immigrant Who Published Her Life Story at 104, Dies at 111
abstract: A long, eventful life of positive thinking, tragedy, travel, good works, glamour and moving in diplomatic circles.

name: Samuel D. Cook
headline: Samuel D. Cook, Educator Who Pierced Campus Color Barriers, Dies at 88
abstract: The first black professor to hold a tenure-track appointment at a mostly white Southern university, and a childhood friend of Martin Luther King Jr.

name: William Krisel
headline: William Krisel, Architect Who Found a Midcentury Niche, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Krisel coupled elegance with frugality, and avoided cookie-cutter looks, as he designed mass-produced homes in the Sun Belt.

name: Isabelle Rapin
profession: Advanced Concept of an Autism Spectrum
headline: Isabelle Rapin, Who Advanced Concept of an Autism Spectrum, Dies at 89
abstract: The Swiss-born neurologist is credited with modernizing the understanding of autism’s causes and popularizing use of the term “autism spectrum disorder.”

name: Chana Bloch
headline: Chana Bloch, Poet and Hebrew Translator, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Ms. Bloch, who helped turn the Song of Solomon into erotic English, wrote poems about love, sex, family, illness and the end of her first marriage.

name: Glenne Headly
headline: Glenne Headly, a Versatile and Scene-Stealing Actress, Dies at 62
abstract: After Ms. Headly’s career took shape with the Steppenwolf theater group, she appeared in Hollywood films like “Dick Tracy” and “Dirty Rotten Scoundrels.”

name: Vic Gold
headline: Vic Gold, Hard-Charging G.O.P. Spokesman and Campaigner, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Gold helped pave the way for modern conservatism with his work for Barry Goldwater and Spiro Agnew and his criticism of what he called media bias.

name: Adam West
headline: Sad Day for Gotham: Adam West, Who Played Batman, Dies at 88
abstract: The classically handsome baritone actor turned a comic-book superhero into live-action Pop Art in the 1960s television series “Batman.”

name: Andimba Toivo ya Toivo
headline: Andimba Toivo ya Toivo, Namibian Independence Leader, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. ya Toivo, who was jailed alongside Nelson Mandela at Robben Island, became a symbol of Namibians’ struggle for independence from South Africa.

name: Edith Shiffert
profession: Poet Inspired by Nature and Her Life in Japan
headline: Edith Shiffert, a Poet Inspired by Nature and Her Life in Japan, Dies at 101
abstract: The American author of nearly two dozen volumes of poetry was known for having an affinity with the natural world.

name: Ed Victor
headline: Ed Victor, a Stylish and Frenetic Book Agent, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Victor, a 6-foot-4 bon vivant who was born in the Bronx, put together a star-studded client roster in England.

name: Rosalie Sorrels
headline: Rosalie Sorrels, a Folk Singer Who Transported Her Audience, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Ms. Sorrels never rose to fame and fortune, but she influenced a generation of musicians with her songwriting style and her intimate performances.

name: Charles P. Thacker
headline: Charles P. Thacker Dies at 74; Helped Design Early Personal Computer
abstract: Mr. Thacker, an electrical engineer, was part of a group at the Palo Alto Research Center that in the 1970s created the Alto, featuring a graphical user interface.

name: Anita Pallenberg
profession: Actress and Muse of Rolling Stones
headline: Anita Pallenberg, Actress and Muse of Rolling Stones, Dies at 75
abstract: Best known for her relationships with Keith Richards and Brian Jones of the Stones, Ms. Pallenberg appeared in quirky films like “Barbarella” and “Candy.”

name: A.R. Gurney
headline: A.R. Gurney, Playwright Who Explored Upper-Crust Anxieties, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Gurney, whose plays included “The Cocktail Hour,” “Love Letters” and “The Middle Ages,” leavened his astute social analysis with tart humor.

name: Patricia Knatchbull
headline: Patricia Knatchbull, a Grande Dame of Britain’s Elite, Dies at 93
abstract: Her life embraced a fabled childhood and personal tragedy after her father and a son were killed by the Irish Republican Army in a bomb attack at sea.

name: Ronald Markman
headline: Ronald Markman, an Artist Who Conjured His Own Kingdom, Dies at 86
abstract: The artist worked to break free of the confines of classical art, and wasn’t afraid to poke fun at society.

name: Robert S. Leiken
headline: Robert S. Leiken, Political Scientist Who Defied Labels, Dies at 78
abstract: The title of his unfinished memoir reflected the frustration of his ideological soul mates, first liberals and later conservatives: “How I Lost All My Friends.”

name: Helen Dunmore
headline: Helen Dunmore, Who Wrote About Legacy and Loss, Dies at 64
abstract: Ms. Dunmore, an Englishwoman, found much success writing novels, poetry, short stories and children’s books.

name: Philip Gossett
headline: Philip Gossett, Scholar Who Brought Operas Back to Life, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Gossett rediscovered lost works, created new editions of Rossini and Verdi scores and helped revive them onstage.

name: Hein Verbruggen
headline: Hein Verbruggen, Who Raised Cycling’s Profile, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Verbruggen helped to bring the sport to new countries but was accused of failing to confront widespread doping.

name: David Fromkin
headline: David Fromkin, Professor and Author on Mideast, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Fromkin was a lawyer as well as the founding director of the Frederick S. Pardee Center for the Study of the Longer-Range Future at Boston University.

name: Helmut Kohl
headline: Helmut Kohl, Chancellor Who Reunited Germany, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Kohl held the post for 16 years, from 1982 to 1998, longer than any German leader since Bismarck.

name: John Avildsen
profession: Director of Rocky and The Karate Kid
headline: John Avildsen, Director of ‘Rocky’ and ‘The Karate Kid,’ Dies at 81
abstract: The Oscar-winning filmmaker, over a career that spanned nearly five decades, told stories of down-and-out characters finding triumph.

name: William J.L. Sladen
headline: William J.L. Sladen, Expert on Penguin Libidos, Is Dead at 96
abstract: Dr. Sladen, a British zoologist whose work was the basis of the 1996 movie “Fly Away Home,” also helped teach young birds to safely migrate.

name: Ben Finney
headline: Ben Finney, Anthropologist Who Debunked Theory on Island Settlement, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Finney supervised the building of the Hokulea, which sailed from Hawaii to Tahiti and discredited the “accidental settlement” theory of Polynesia.

name: Ernestina Herrera de Noble
headline: Ernestina Herrera de Noble, Media Mogul in Argentina, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Herrera de Noble, the publisher of Clarín, was instrumental in creating one of the largest media conglomerates in the Spanish-speaking world.

name: Stephen Furst
headline: Stephen Furst, Who Played Flounder in ‘Animal House,’ Dies at 63
abstract: The fraternity pledge nicknamed Flounder was a role Mr. Furst remained proud of all his career, which encompassed TV series and movies.

name: Larry Grantham
headline: Larry Grantham, Defensive Captain of Champion Jets, Dies at 78
abstract: Grantham, an undersize linebacker, played 13 seasons with the New York Titans and the Jets, whom he helped upset the Colts in the 1969 Super Bowl.

name: Prodigy
profession: Forged Sound of New York Rap
headline: Prodigy of Mobb Deep Dies at 42; Forged Sound of New York Rap
abstract: Half of the duo Mobb Deep, Prodigy, born Albert Johnson, had been hospitalized in Las Vegas suffering from complications of sickle-cell anemia.

name: Tony DiCicco
profession: Popular Coach of the U.S. Womens Soccer Team
headline: Tony DiCicco, Popular Coach of the U.S. Women’s Soccer Team, Dies at 68
abstract: DiCicco, an easygoing and accommodating presence, led the team to a gold medal at the 1996 Olympics and a victory in the 1999 Women’s World Cup final.

name: Paul Zukofsky
headline: Paul Zukofsky, Prodigy Who Became, Uneasily, a Virtuoso Violinist, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Zukofsky, a musician of immense talent and exacting standards, had a life marked by strained relationships.

name: Carla Fendi
profession: Fashion Pioneer in a Female Dynasty
headline: Carla Fendi, Fashion Pioneer in a Female Dynasty, Dies at 79
abstract: Part of fashion’s best-known sister act, Ms. Fendi was an instrumental force in the evolution of her small family business into a luxury powerhouse.

name: Jerry Nelson
headline: Jerry Nelson, Designer of the Segmented Telescope, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Nelson’s design, made decades after the size limit was thought to have been reached, allowed scientists to peer farther into the universe than ever before.

name: Lawrence Weed
headline: Dr. Lawrence Weed, Pioneer in Recording Patient Data, Dies at 93
abstract: Dr. Weed created a system for organizing medical data that is used all over the world, and helped develop a computerized method for aiding diagnosis and treatment.

name: Phyllis Kravitch
headline: Phyllis Kravitch, Judge Who Opened Doors for Herself, Dies at 96
abstract: Judge Kravitch embarked on her legal career in Savannah, Ga., her hometown, in 1944, more than a decade before women were allowed to sit on juries in the state.

name: Robert Campeau
headline: Robert Campeau, Flamboyant Canadian Who Owned Bloomingdale’s, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Campeau, a developer, built a department store empire in the United States in the 1980s, but it swiftly drowned in a sea of debt.

name: Frédérick Leboyer
headline: Frédérick Leboyer, Who Saw Childbirth Through Baby’s Eyes, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Leboyer, a French physician, advocated natural birth methods that focused on easing suffering for the baby.

name: Edit DeAk
headline: Edit DeAk, a Champion of Outsider Artists, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. DeAk was a critic and a player on the downtown Manhattan scene in the 1970s and 1980s.

name: Paulus Berensohn
headline: Paulus Berensohn, a Dancer Who Pivoted to Pottery, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Berensohn argued for a slower, quieter and more mindful approach to pottery.

name: Pete Flynn
headline: Pete Flynn, Mets Groundskeeper for Almost 50 Years, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Flynn helped tend three homes of the Mets — the Polo Grounds, Shea Stadium and Citi Field — beginning with the club’s founding in 1962.

name: Gabe Pressman
profession: Dean of New York TV Journalism
headline: Gabe Pressman, a Dean of New York TV Journalism, Dies at 93
abstract: To generations of mayors, governors and ordinary New Yorkers, Mr. Pressman, WNBC’s senior correspondent, seemed always on the scene.

name: Frank Kush
profession: Hall of Fame Coach of Arizona State
headline: Frank Kush, Hall of Fame Coach of Arizona State, Dies at 88
abstract: Kush led the Sun Devils to six bowl victories, but his career was derailed in an assault investigation.

name: Hans Breder
headline: Hans Breder, Who Broke Artistic Boundaries, Dies at 81
abstract: The German-born Mr. Breder left New York for the University of Iowa to establish the first interdisciplinary art program of its kind.

name: John Sarno
profession: Best-Selling Author Tied Pain to Anxieties
headline: Dr. John Sarno, 93, Dies; Best-Selling Author Tied Pain to Anxieties
abstract: Dr. Sarno was both hailed and dismissed for his contention that most chronic pain could be traced to deep within the psyche.

name: Marion Goldin
headline: Marion Goldin, Award-Winning ‘60 Minutes’ Producer, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Goldin, a trailblazer as a TV newswoman, was long paired with Mike Wallace on memorable investigative pieces.

name: Elias Burstein
headline: Elias Burstein, Pioneer in Semiconductors, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Burstein was one of the first scientists to use lasers to do research on semiconductors and insulators, and held patents for a method to increase the semiconducting capacity of silicon.

name: Samuel V. Wilson
headline: Samuel V. Wilson, Ex-Director of Defense Intelligence Agency, Dies at 93
abstract: A decorated military man, Mr. Wilson helped develop wartime practices that emphasize understanding the culture of the countries where fighting is taking place.

name: Hope Ryden
headline: Hope Ryden, Wildlife Protector and Photographer, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Ryden developed a passion for photography during breaks abroad as a flight attendant, and became a full-time naturalist and animal-rights advocate.

name: Meir Zlotowitz
profession: Made Jewish Prayer Books Clear to All
headline: Rabbi Meir Zlotowitz, Who Made Jewish Prayer Books Clear to All, Dies at 73
abstract: His company, ArtScroll Mesorah, provides prayer books and volumes of the Torah and Talmud for the Orthodox Jewish community written in everyday English.

name: Richard Benson
headline: Richard Benson, Photographer and Printer, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Benson believed in the painterly impact of reproducing the work of photographers like Irving Penn, Lee Friedlander and Helen Levitt on an offset printing press.

name: Alain Senderens
headline: Alain Senderens, a Chef Who Modernized French Food, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Senderens, one of the most adventurous of the founding fathers of nouvelle cuisine, produced dishes that could entice and, on occasion, shock.

name: Margaux Fragoso
headline: Margaux Fragoso, Memoirist Who Wrote Hauntingly of Sexual Abuse, Dies at 38
abstract: “Tiger, Tiger,” Ms. Fragoso’s graphic account of her relationship with a much older man, was considered one of the more notable books of the year when it was released in 2011.

name: Michael Nyqvist
profession: Star in John Wick and the Swedish Dragon Tattoo
headline: Michael Nyqvist, a Star in ‘John Wick’ and the Swedish ‘Dragon Tattoo,’ Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Nyqvist was a star in Swedish movies and television before playing villains in Hollywood thrillers. He also wrote about his search for his biological parents.

name: Geri Allen
headline: Geri Allen, Pianist Who Reconciled Jazz’s Far-Flung Styles, Dies at 60
abstract: Ms. Allen’s dense but agile piano playing formed a bridge between jazz’s midcentury past and its stylistically diffuse present.

name: Michael Bond
headline: Michael Bond, Paddington Bear Creator, Is Dead at 91
abstract: The character — disaster-prone but good-natured and always polite — was the hero of children’s novels, picture books and animated television series.

name: Anthony Young
headline: Anthony Young, Who Lost 27 Consecutive Decisions for Mets, Dies at 51
abstract: The pitcher maintained his dignity after breaking the major league record for futility, which made him a national celebrity in the early 1990s.

name: Herve Filion
profession: for Many Years Harness Racings Top Driver
headline: Herve Filion, for Many Years Harness Racing’s Top Driver, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Filion would have won even more races were it not for a seven-year suspension that resulted from charges that were ultimately dropped.

name: Ketumile Masire
profession: Shaped and Led a Vibrant Botswana
headline: Ketumile Masire, Who Shaped and Led a Vibrant Botswana, Dies at 91
abstract: President Masire was instrumental in transforming his arid, destitute country into the envy of other African nations.

name: Gary DeCarlo
profession: Sang Na Na Hey Hey Kiss Him Goodbye
headline: Gary DeCarlo, Who Sang ‘Na Na Hey Hey Kiss Him Goodbye,’ Is Dead
abstract: Mr. DeCarlo saw the song reach No. 1 on the pop charts in 1969 and live on as an indelible sports stadium taunt.

name: Roger D. Abrahams
headline: Roger D. Abrahams, Folklorist Who Studied African-American Language, Dies at 84
abstract: Professor Abrahams cast a wide net, from folk songs to street rhymes, chants, proverbs and other oral traditions, in the United States and the Caribbean.

name: Peter Berger
headline: Peter Berger, Theologian Who Fought ‘God Is Dead’ Movement, Dies at 88
abstract: Professor Berger was known for his work in what is called the sociology of knowledge — understanding how humans experience everyday reality.

name: Edward Kline
profession: Silent Partner in Aiding Soviet Dissidents
headline: Edward Kline, ‘Silent Partner’ in Aiding Soviet Dissidents, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Kline helped to shepherd Andrei D. Sakharov’s memoirs into worldwide distribution and set up a publishing house in New York to print books that were banned by the Soviet authorities.

name: Simone Veil
headline: Simone Veil, Ex-Minister Who Wrote France’s Abortion Law, Dies at 89
abstract: An Auschwitz survivor, Mrs. Veil was a vocal advocate for women’s rights who served as health minister and later as president of the European Parliament.

name: Suzanne Wasserman
profession: Historian of New York City and Filmmaker
headline: Suzanne Wasserman, Historian of New York City and Filmmaker, Dies at 60
abstract: Ms. Wasserman became intrigued by the Lower East Side after moving to New York from Chicago.

name: Herma Hill Kay
profession: First Woman to Lead Berkeley Law Faculty
headline: Herma Hill Kay, First Woman to Lead Berkeley Law Faculty, Dies at 82
abstract: Appointed as dean while California voters were seeking to end affirmative action in the 1990s, Ms. Kay championed the rights of women and minorities.

name: Doug Peterson
profession: Trailblazer in the Design of Racing Yachts
headline: Doug Peterson, Trailblazer in the Design of Racing Yachts, Dies at 71
abstract: Peterson had his breakthrough when he borrowed money from his grandmother to build a boat that finished second in a premier international race in 1973.

name: Norman Dorsen
headline: Norman Dorsen, Tenacious Civil Rights Advocate, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Dorsen spent a long legal career focused on fighting for human rights, including before the Supreme Court, and led the A.C.L.U. for 15 years.

name: Darrall Imhoff
headline: Darrall Imhoff, a Decorated Basketball Center, Dies at 78
abstract: Imhoff led California to the 1959 N.C.A.A. title, won an Olympic gold medal and had a long career in the N.B.A., including two seasons with the Knicks.

name: Jan Fontein
headline: Jan Fontein, Scholar of Asian Art, Is Dead at 89
abstract: The Dutch-born Mr. Fontein led the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, through major expansion as its director in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Kelan Philip Cohran
headline: Kelan Philip Cohran, a Musician Who Invigorated Chicago With Education and Activism, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Cohran helped found the Association for the Advancement of Creative Musicians, which raised public consciousness through performances.

name: Morton Cohen
profession: Scholar of Lewis Carroll and His Wonderland
headline: Morton Cohen, Scholar of Lewis Carroll and His Wonderland, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Cohen tracked down many of the women Carroll had corresponded with when they were young.

name: Denys Johnson-Davies
headline: Denys Johnson-Davies, Translator of Arab Writers, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Mr. Johnson-Davies translated more than 30 Arabic novels, short-story collections and anthologies. He was best known for his work with Naguib Mahfouz.

name: Heathcote Williams
headline: Heathcote Williams, Radical British Poet Who Helped Form Anarchist Nation, Dies at 75
abstract: Outraged at conformity and drawn to theatricality, Mr. Williams aimed to effect change with language.

name: Gene Conley
profession: Dual-Sport Threat With World Series and N.B.A. Titles
headline: Gene Conley, Dual-Sport Threat With World Series and N.B.A. Titles, Dies at 86
abstract: Very few athletes have won championships in two major American professional sports. Conley was one.

name: John R. Quinn
profession: Archbishop and Liberal Voice in Church
headline: John R. Quinn, Archbishop and Liberal Voice in Church, Dies at 88
abstract: As leader of the San Francisco archdiocese in the 1980s and 1990s, Archbishop Quinn had a powerful voice on social and political issues.

name: Sheila Michaels
headline: Sheila Michaels, Who Brought ‘Ms.’ to Prominence, Dies at 78
abstract: Dissatisfied with other honorifics for women, Ms. Michaels undertook “a timid eight-year crusade” to usher the term back into being after decades of disuse.

name: David Vincent
headline: David Vincent, the Sultan of Swat Stats, Dies at 67
abstract: Want to know the heaviest player to hit an inside-the-park homer? Mr. Vincent could tell you that and many other often-esoteric home run facts.

name: Spencer Johnson
headline: Spencer Johnson, ‘Who Moved My Cheese?’ Author, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Johnson wrote pithy best-sellers, including one about the benefits of embracing change and another defining effective management.

name: Pierre Henry
headline: Pierre Henry, Composer Who Found the Music in Sounds, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Henry abandoned notes in favor of ambient sounds — dripping water, car horns, bird calls, locomotive engines — which he manipulated with a tape recorder in surprising ways.

name: José Luis Cuevas
headline: José Luis Cuevas, a Dark Master of Mexican Art, Dies at 83
abstract: One of Mexico’s most celebrated artists, Mr. Cuevas brought an existentialist vision, influenced by Goya and Breughel, to unsparing depictions of human suffering.

name: Nelsan Ellis
headline: Nelsan Ellis, ‘True Blood’ Actor, Dies at 39
abstract: Mr. Ellis starred in “True Blood” from 2008 to 2014 as a scene-stealing diner cook and dealer of addictive vampire blood in rural Louisiana.

name: Joaquín Navarro-Valls
headline: Joaquín Navarro-Valls, Ex-Vatican Spokesman, Dies at 80
abstract: A fierce loyalist to Pope John Paul II, Mr. Navarro-Valls oversaw an extensive renovation of the Vatican’s press office and served as the pope’s wingman on foreign trips.

name: Kenneth Silverman
headline: Kenneth Silverman, Pulitzer-Winning Author, Dies at 81
abstract: Professor Silverman, a specialist in Colonial American literature, also wrote biographies of Edgar Allan Poe, Harry Houdini, Samuel F.B. Morse and John Cage.

name: Elsa Martinelli
headline: Elsa Martinelli, Italian Model and Actress, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Martinelli, described as “a kind of Audrey Hepburn with sex appeal,” was well known for starring opposite Kirk Douglas in “The Indian Fighter.”

name: Yuri Drozdov
headline: Yuri Drozdov, Soviet Superspy Who Planted ‘Illegals’ in Other Countries, Dies at 91
abstract: General Drozdov also played a key role in a famous exchange of captive spies between the Soviet Union and the United States.

name: Jon Underwood
headline: Jon Underwood, Founder of Death Cafe Movement, Dies at 44
abstract: Mr. Underwood encouraged Britons to discuss, over tea and cake, their fear of death, and his efforts have spread to more than a dozen countries.

name: Jim Bush
headline: Jim Bush, Title-Winning Track Coach at U.C.L.A., Dies at 90
abstract: Bush’s outspoken comments sometimes threatened to overshadow his accomplishments.

name: Neil Welch
profession: F.B.I. Mastermind in Abscam Sting Operation
headline: Neil Welch, F.B.I. Mastermind in Abscam Sting Operation, Dies at 90
abstract: The political investigation ensnared a senator and seven congressmen. He also negotiated the surrender of the escaped killer of Kitty Genovese.

name: Jack Shaheen
profession: Resisted and Cataloged Stereotyping of Arabs
headline: Jack Shaheen, Who Resisted and Cataloged Stereotyping of Arabs, Dies at 81
abstract: Dr. Shaheen began his campaign against xenophobia in films and on television in 1974, documenting and mitigating negative images of Arabs and Muslims.

name: Ilya Glazunov
headline: Ilya Glazunov, Painter Entranced by Russia’s Past, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Glazunov ran afoul of both Socialist Realist practitioners and progressives, but won a devoted following after the collapse of Communism.

name: Chuck Blazer
headline: Chuck Blazer, Central Figure in FIFA Scandal, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Blazer was a gregarious American soccer official who pleaded guilty to a range of charges as part of a federal investigation.

name: Liu Xiaobo
headline: Liu Xiaobo, Chinese Dissident Who Won Nobel While Jailed, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Liu, who was convicted in 2009 of inciting subversion and sentenced to prison, was given medical parole recently to be treated for late-stage cancer.

name: Meechy Monroe
profession: YouTube Star for Her Natural Hair Lessons
headline: Meechy Monroe, a YouTube Star for Her Natural Hair Lessons, Dies at 32
abstract: Ms. Monroe achieved online fame with style tutorials that empowered black women to forgo harsh chemicals and embrace the natural hair movement.

name: Keith Conners
headline: Keith Conners, Psychologist Who Set Standard for Diagnosing A.D.H.D., Dies at 84
abstract: After devising a scale for treating attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, Dr. Conners later expressed dismay over how loosely the label was being applied.

name: Irina Ratushinskaya
headline: Irina Ratushinskaya, Soviet Dissident and Writer, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Ratushinskaya composed some 250 poems in prison, many drafted with burned matchsticks on bars of soap.

name: Gus Trowbridge
profession: Turned Kings Integration Dream Into a School
headline: Gus Trowbridge, Turned King’s Integration Dream Into a School, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Trowbridge and his wife, Marty, followed Martin Luther King Jr.’s ideals in founding Manhattan Country School in 1966.

name: Jean-Jacques Susini
headline: Jean-Jacques Susini, Right-Wing Extremist in Algeria, Dies at 83
abstract: He opposed Algerian independence from France, plotted to assassinate President Charles de Gaulle, and belonged to a group that used terrorism tactics.

name: Ray Phiri
headline: Ray Phiri, ‘Graceland’ Guitarist and Anti-Apartheid Bandleader, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Phiri, who led Stimela, a long-running South African band, worked with Paul Simon on the albums “Graceland” and “The Rhythm of the Saints.”

name: Babe Parilli
headline: Babe Parilli Dies at 87; Standout Quarterback With ‘Houdini Hands’
abstract: A two-time all-American under Coach Bear Bryant at the University of Kentucky, Parilli also played for 15 years in the National Football League and the American Football League.

name: Maryam Mirzakhani
profession: Only Woman to Win a Fields Medal
headline: Maryam Mirzakhani, Only Woman to Win a Fields Medal, Dies at 40
abstract: Dr. Mirzakhani, a mathematician at Stanford University, was the only woman and only Iranian ever to win what is often described as the Nobel Prize of mathematics.

name: Hootie Johnson
profession: Opposed Letting Women Into Augusta National
headline: Hootie Johnson, Who Opposed Letting Women Into Augusta National, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Johnson’s clash with a women’s rights activist underscored how social discrimination could affect women’s professional ambitions.

name: Charles W. Bachman
headline: Charles W. Bachman, Business Software Innovator, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Bachman was a pioneer in the field of database management software, and modern digital commerce sites like Amazon and eBay owe an intellectual debt to his work.

name: Bob Wolff
headline: Bob Wolff, Sports Broadcaster for Nearly 80 Years, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Wolff called Don Larsen’s perfect game, the Giants-Colts 1958 N.F.L. title game, baseball’s Game of the Week in the ’60s and the Knicks’ N.B.A. championship runs.

name: George Romero
headline: George Romero, Father of the Zombie Movie, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Romero created the modern zombie genre with his 1968 cult film, “Night of the Living Dead.”

name: Martin Landau
headline: Martin Landau, Actor Who Won an Oscar for ‘Ed Wood,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Landau, who gained fame in the 1960s TV series “Mission: Impossible,” but then struggled to find work, enjoyed a career revival in film decades later.

name: Wm. Theodore de Bary
headline: Wm. Theodore de Bary, Renowned Columbia Sinologist, Dies at 97
abstract: Professor de Bary, an authority in particular on Confucius, was awarded the National Humanities Medal by President Barack Obama.

name: S. Allen Counter
headline: S. Allen Counter, Who Championed an Unsung Black Explorer, Dies at 73
abstract: An explorer himself, Dr. Counter reclaimed the reputation of Matthew Henson, who reached the North Pole with Robert Peary.

name: Frances Gabe
profession: Creator of the Only Self-Cleaning Home
headline: Frances Gabe, Creator of the Only Self-Cleaning Home, Dies at 101
abstract: Equal parts quixotic dreamer and accomplished visionary, Ms. Gabe made the house do its own scrubbing.

name: Bracha Graber
profession: Spurred Changes in New York Foster Care
headline: Bracha Graber, Who Spurred Changes in New York Foster Care, Dies at 68
abstract: Rebuffed by her bosses at a city child welfare agency, Ms. Graber filed a lawsuit that led to a bureaucratic overhaul.

name: Betty Dukes
headline: Betty Dukes, Greeter Whose Walmart Lawsuit Went to Supreme Court, Dies at 67
abstract: Ms. Dukes, who filed suit on behalf of 1.5 million female workers, was portrayed as the epitome of a low-paid worker taking on a huge corporation.

name: Sam Glanzman
profession: Comic-Book Artist Inspired by His War Service
headline: Sam Glanzman, Comic-Book Artist Inspired by His War Service, Dies at 92
abstract: A writer and artist whose richly detailed work recreated the battles, camaraderie and down times of war in the Pacific.

name: Raymond Sackler
headline: Raymond Sackler, Psychopharmacology Pioneer and Philanthropist, Dies at 97
abstract: Purdue Pharma, a company led by Dr. Sackler and his brothers, made the painkiller OxyContin. His donations put his name on schools, museum galleries and a planet.

name: Chester Bennington
headline: Chester Bennington, Linkin Park Singer, Is Dead at 41
abstract: The frontman was known for his piercing scream and free-flowing anguish. His death is being investigated as a possible suicide.

name: Kenneth Jay Lane
headline: Kenneth Jay Lane, Jewelry Designer Who Made a Fortune Faking It, Dies at 85
abstract: Over six decades, Mr. Lane built a global business by making it acceptable and chic for women to wear glittering jewelry of unabashed deception.

name: Wall Street
headline: Wall Street Journal Editorial Writer Is Found Dead
abstract: The writer, Joseph Rago, 34, won a Pulitzer Prize in 2011 for his editorials challenging President Barack Obama’s health care law. Foul play is not suspected.

name: C. Weston Houck
headline: C. Weston Houck, Judge Who Ended Citadel’s Male-Only Policy, Dies at 84
abstract: Judge Houck, an appointee of President Jimmy Carter, declared that the college’s refusal to admit Shannon Faulkner was a violation of the 14th Amendment’s equal protection clause.

name: Clancy Sigal
headline: Clancy Sigal, Novelist Whose Life Was a Tale in Itself, Dies at 90
abstract: Jailed at 5, blacklisted in Hollywood, the author of “Going Away” fell in with R.D. Laing and Doris Lessing.

name: Scharlette Holdman
profession: Force for the Defense on Death Row
headline: Scharlette Holdman, a Force for the Defense on Death Row, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Holdman was a pioneer in unearthing legal reasons to spare the lives of the convicted, often working on the cases of those convicted of heinous crimes.

name: John Heard
headline: John Heard, the Frazzled Father in ‘Home Alone,’ Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Heard played pained characters in dramas but was best known as the dad who embarked on a family trip to Paris without his youngest son.

name: John Kundla
headline: John Kundla, Winning Coach of Fledgling Lakers, Dies at 101
abstract: Kundla led the Minneapolis team to five titles in the N.B.A. and its immediate precursor.

name: Bo Pilgrim
profession: Founder of Pilgrims Pride Poultry Products
headline: Bo Pilgrim, Founder of Pilgrim’s Pride Poultry Products, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Pilgrim joined a brother in taking over a Texas feed store owned by their father and transformed it into a company with 35,000 employees and operations in 17 states and Mexico.

name: Margaret Bergmann Lambert
profession: Jewish Athlete Excluded From Berlin Olympics
headline: Margaret Bergmann Lambert, Jewish Athlete Excluded From Berlin Olympics, Dies at 103
abstract: She was a dominant, German-born world-class athlete, but the Nazis said she had not qualified for the 1936 Games.

name: Shigeaki Hinohara
headline: Dr. Shigeaki Hinohara, Longevity Expert, Dies at (or Lives to) 105
abstract: The advice of Dr. Hinohara, who cautioned against early retirement and advocated climbing stairs regularly, helped make Japan the world leader in longevity.

name: Keith Baird
headline: Keith Baird, Linguist Who Fought the Use of ‘Negro,’ Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Baird, a native of Barbados who became a teacher and administrator in New York City schools and at various colleges, argued for the term Afro-American.

name: Marina Ratner
headline: Marina Ratner, Émigré Mathematician Who Found Midlife Acclaim, Dies at 78
abstract: Dr. Ratner defied the notion that the brightest in her field do their best work when they are young.

name: G. Yunupingu
headline: Dr. G. Yunupingu, Australian Aboriginal Singer, Dies at 46
abstract: The blind, largely self-taught musician produced the best-selling Indigenous album in Australian history and played in concert halls around the world.

name: Thomas Fleming
headline: Thomas Fleming, Historian of the Revolution, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Fleming wrote prolifically about powerful men, including Washington, Jefferson, Franklin and Hamilton, and pivotal moments like the battles of Bunker Hill, Lexington and Concord.

name: Andrew Paulson
headline: Andrew Paulson, Chess Impresario and Serial Entrepreneur, Dies at 58
abstract: Besides his numerous ventures in the arts and media, Mr. Paulson also strove to make chess a popular spectator sport on television.

name: June Foray
headline: June Foray, Virtuoso of Cartoon Voices, Notably Rocky’s, Dies at 99
abstract: Ms. Foray cackled, chirped, meowed and sometimes sang her way through nearly 300 productions. Rocky the flying squirrel was among her most popular characters.

name: Robert Farmer
headline: Robert Farmer, Resourceful Fund-Raiser for Democrats, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Farmer found a way to get around spending limits on his way to raising $800 million for candidates.

name: Herbert Needleman
profession: Saw Leads Wider Harm to Children
headline: Dr. Herbert Needleman, Who Saw Lead’s Wider Harm to Children, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Needleman studied lost baby teeth to show that any level of absorbed lead can damage young brains.

name: Bill Collings
headline: Bill Collings, Maker of Sought-After Guitars, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Collings’s company made guitars for Keith Richards, Pete Townshend, Joni Mitchell, Eddie Van Halen, Paul Simon, Lou Reed, Bill Frisell and Emmylou Harris.

name: Mervyn Rose
headline: Mervyn Rose, 7-Time Grand Slam Champion in Tennis, Dies at 87
abstract: Rose had a Hall of Fame career in the 1950s and later coached Billie Jean King and Margaret Smith Court.

name: D.L. Menard
headline: D.L. Menard, ‘the Cajun Hank Williams,’ Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Menard’s song “The Back Door” is ubiquitous in Cajun music and has sold an estimated one million records.

name: Jeanne Moreau
profession: Femme Fatale of French New Wave
headline: Jeanne Moreau, Femme Fatale of French New Wave, Is Dead at 89
abstract: The sensual, gravel-voiced Parisian actress starred in Louis Malle’s 1958 drama “The Lovers” and in François Truffaut’s 1962 film “Jules and Jim.”

name: Sam Shepard
headline: Sam Shepard, Actor and Pulitzer-Winning Playwright, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Mr. Shepard, one of the most important and influential writers of his generation, specialized in capturing the darker sides of American family life.

name: Lee May
headline: Lee May, the Big Bopper for the Reds, Dies at 74
abstract: May, a slugging first baseman, was traded to the Astros before Cincinnati’s Big Red Machine really got rolling. The move felt like being “kicked out of the house,” he said.

name: Lawrence Pezzullo
profession: Broker of Somozas Abdication in Nicaragua
headline: Lawrence Pezzullo, Broker of Somoza’s Abdication in Nicaragua, Dies at 91
abstract: He was sent to persuade Anastasio Somoza DeBayle to stop the bloodshed in Nicaragua’s civil war with the Sandinistas by relinquishing power.

name: Carl E. Reichardt
profession: Leader of Wells Fargo in the 1980s and 90s
headline: Carl E. Reichardt, Leader of Wells Fargo in the 1980s and ’90s, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Reichardt introduced a leaner approach to commercial banking that served as a model for the industry.

name: Ara Parseghian
headline: Ara Parseghian, Coach Who Returned Notre Dame Football to Greatness, Dies at 94
abstract: Parseghian took over a program that had been in decline for years, and led it to national titles in 1966 and 1973.

name: Judith Jones
profession: Editor of Literature and Culinary Delight
headline: Judith Jones, Editor of Literature and Culinary Delight, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Jones discovered Julia Child and other venerated culinary writers, and pushed for the American publication of Anne Frank’s diary.

name: Rula Quawas
profession: Champion of Womens Advancement in Jordan
headline: Rula Quawas, Champion of Women’s Advancement in Jordan, Dies at 57
abstract: The professor helped her students create a video that exposed the sexual harassment they endured on campus.

name: Jeff Brotman
headline: Jeff Brotman, Founder of Retail Juggernaut Costco, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Brotman grew the company into one of the world’s largest retailers by advertising rock-bottom prices on household goods.

name: Denis Mack Smith
headline: Denis Mack Smith, Chronicler of Modern Italy, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Smith rankled many when he wrote that the Risorgimento, the movement that forged a unified Italian state, was not a glorious chapter.

name: Gösta Peterson
headline: Gösta Peterson, Barrier-Breaking Fashion Photographer, Dies at 94
abstract: Among Mr. Peterson’s most notable subjects in the 1960s were the black model Naomi Sims and the English sensation Twiggy.

name: Michael Bradfield
headline: Michael Bradfield, Lawyer Who Helped Shape U.S. Economic Policy, Dies at 83
abstract: A longtime public servant, Mr. Bradfield helped steer the economy through a series of financial crises while at the Federal Reserve and elsewhere.

name: Marty Sklar
headline: Marty Sklar, Longtime Disney Aide and Executive, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Sklar started editing Disneyland’s newspaper as a college student and later oversaw designs of the company’s parks.

name: Bobby Taylor
headline: Bobby Taylor, Soul Singer Who Helped the Jackson 5, Dies
abstract: Upon encountering the Jackson 5, Mr. Taylor was especially taken with the lead singer, a child phenomenon named Michael.

name: Robert Hardy
profession: Frequent Churchill and a Potter Wizard
headline: Robert Hardy, a Frequent Churchill and a ‘Potter’ Wizard, Dies at 91
abstract: An actor who became a familiar face to a new generation of fans when he was cast, in his late 70s, as Cornelius Fudge in the Harry Potter films.

name: Richard Dudman
profession: Reporter at Center of Historys Churn
headline: Richard Dudman, Reporter at Center of History’s Churn, Dies at 99
abstract: The journalist for The St. Louis Post-Dispatch spent over a month in Cambodia as a captive of the Vietcong, met Pol Pot and published excerpts from the Pentagon Papers.

name: Fred Leighton
headline: Fred Leighton, a Jeweler Who Made Stars Glitter, Dies at 85
abstract: The earrings and necklaces from Mr. Leighton’s Manhattan store seemed to shine brightest on Hollywood’s red carpets.

name: Mark White
headline: Mark White, Texas Governor Who Championed Public Education, Dies at 77
abstract: As governor from 1983 to 1987, Mr. White limited class sizes, increased teachers’ pay and required high school athletes to pass their classes.

name: Ty Hardin
headline: Ty Hardin, Star of ‘Bronco’ Western, Dies at 87
abstract: In the late 1950s and early ’60s, Mr. Hardin made a name for himself in a TV landscape full of gunslinging heroes.

name: Jack Rabinovitch
headline: Jack Rabinovitch, Founder of Canadian Literary Award, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Rabinovitch, a real estate developer, set up the Giller Prize, Canada’s leading literary award, as a memorial for his second wife.

name: Betty Cuthbert
profession: Australias Golden Girl of Track and Field
headline: Betty Cuthbert, Australia’s ‘Golden Girl’ of Track and Field, Dies at 79
abstract: Cuthbert burst onto the scene at the 1956 Melbourne Olympics, where she became the first Australian to win three gold medals.

name: Darren Daulton
headline: Darren Daulton, Catcher for the 1993 Pennant-Winning Phillies, Dies at 55
abstract: Daulton, a three-time All-Star, was a no-nonsense figure who battled through numerous injuries to become an everyday player.

name: Martin Roth
headline: Martin Roth, German Who Led Britain’s Victoria and Albert Museum, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Roth was a pathbreaking curator in London who stepped down in protest over the “Brexit” vote.

name: Ernst Zündel
profession: Holocaust Denier Tried for Spreading His Message
headline: Ernst Zündel, Holocaust Denier Tried for Spreading His Message, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Zündel spewed anti-Semitic propaganda from his house in Toronto and twice saw his convictions overturned.

name: Don Baylor
profession: Slugging M.V.P. in the American League
headline: Don Baylor, Slugging M.V.P. in the American League, Dies at 68
abstract: A veteran of six teams, Baylor had a talent for being hit by a pitch — 267 times, in all.

name: Haruo Nakajima
headline: Haruo Nakajima, the First Actor to Play Godzilla, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Nakajima starred as the movie monster 12 times from 1954 to 1972, turning Japan’s postwar nuclear anxieties into an international phenomenon.

name: Barbara Cook
headline: Barbara Cook, Broadway Star Who Became a Cabaret Mainstay, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Cook, a Tony Award-winning leading lady in Broadway musicals of the 1950s and ’60s, grappled with alcoholism and obesity before reinventing herself.

name: Christian Millau
headline: Christian Millau, 88, Co-Founder of Lively Restaurant Guide, Dies
abstract: Mr. Millau, with Henri Gault, took aim at the Michelin Guide, which he called stodgy and as terse as “a telephone book.”

name: Glen Campbell
profession: Hit Songs Bridged Country and Pop
headline: Glen Campbell, Whose Hit Songs Bridged Country and Pop, Dies at 81
abstract: A sharecropper’s son who became a recording, television and movie star, Mr. Campbell also battled alcohol and drugs and became a public face of Alzheimer’s disease.

name: George Bundy Smith
profession: Wrote Ruling Voiding New York Death Penalty
headline: Judge George Bundy Smith, 80, Dies; Wrote Ruling Voiding New York Death Penalty
abstract: A liberal but independent-minded judge who had fought for civil rights in the South.

name: Alan Peckolick
headline: Alan Peckolick, a Leading Logo Designer, Dies at 76
abstract: GM, Revlon and Mercedes-Benz were just some of Mr. Peckolick’s clients.

name: Angel Nieto
headline: Angel Nieto, Motorcyclist Who Won 13 Grand Prix Championships, Dies at 70
abstract: Nieto rose from poverty to hobnob with a king, while doing for motorcycle racing in Spain what Seve Ballesteros did for golf there.

name: Marshall I. Goldman
headline: Marshall I. Goldman, Expert on Russian Economy, Dies at 87
abstract: As early as 1987, Professor Goldman painted a grim picture of the consequences of perestroika and glasnost.

name: Arlene Gottfried
headline: Arlene Gottfried, Photographer Who Found the Extraordinary in the Ordinary, Dies at 66
abstract: She roamed the streets of New York, camera in hand, finding opportunity at every corner.

name: Cathleen Morawetz
headline: Cathleen Morawetz, Mathematician With Real-World Impact, Dies at 94
abstract: In one case, Dr. Morawetz’s work helped aerospace engineers minimize shock waves around the wings of airplanes flying below the speed of sound.

name: U.R. Rao
headline: U.R. Rao, Pioneer of India’s Space Program, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Rao helped India propel its first satellites into space, providing television signals and weather forecasting data to the most rural parts of the country.

name: Eduardo del Río
headline: Eduardo del Río, Cartoonist Who Mocked Politics and Religion, Dies at 83
abstract: Not even being kidnapped and excommunicated were enough to stop a prolific caricaturist who wielded a mighty pen against Mexico’s establishment.

name: Ken Kaiser
profession: Colorful and Imposing Big League Umpire
headline: Ken Kaiser, Colorful and Imposing Big League Umpire, Dies at 72
abstract: “Kenny was big, boisterous, tough and arrogant. He walked with a strut. And he took nothing from nobody — never.”

name: Bryan Murray
headline: Bryan Murray, Who Turned Around Losing Hockey Teams, Dies at 74
abstract: Murray led the Florida Panthers, the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim and the Ottawa Senators to the Stanley Cup Finals and was named coach of the year in 1984.

name: Joseph Bologna
profession: Onscreen Tough Guy With a Sense of Humor
headline: Joseph Bologna, Onscreen Tough Guy With a Sense of Humor, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Bologna couldn’t seem to resist writing and playing sensitive male characters in films like “Lovers and Other Strangers” and “Made for Each Other.”

name: Frank Broyles
headline: Frank Broyles, Football Coach Who Put Arkansas on Map, Dies at 92
abstract: Broyles led the Razorbacks to a national title and, as athletic director, lifted Arkansas in basketball and track.

name: Milton Mollen
profession: Investigated Police Corruption in New York
headline: Milton Mollen, 97, Dies; Investigated Police Corruption in New York
abstract: In the 1990s, he led a commission that uncovered a “deep-rooted institutional reluctance to uncover corruption” in the city’s police department.

name: Ruth Pfau
headline: Dr. Ruth Pfau, Savior of Lepers in Pakistan, Dies at 87
abstract: A German-born medical missionary who discovered her life’s calling by chance was hailed as “the Mother Teresa of Pakistan.”

name: Neil Chayet
profession: Host of Looking at the Law on Radio
headline: Neil Chayet, Host of ‘Looking at the Law’ on Radio, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Chayet, a pun-loving Massachusetts lawyer, reached a national audience from his base in Boston.

name: Marian C. Diamond
headline: Marian C. Diamond, 90, Student of the Brain, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Diamond, a neuroscientist, challenged the long-held assumption that the brain is a static and unchangeable entity and examined Albert Einstein’s.

name: Gunnar Birkerts
headline: Gunnar Birkerts, Architect, Dies at 92; Gave Shape to the Unexpected
abstract: The Latvian-born Mr. Birkerts was inspired by Scandinavian masters of Modernism.

name: Paul Oliver
headline: Paul Oliver, Pre-eminent Authority on the Blues, Dies at 90
abstract: The author of “The Story of the Blues” and other books, he was a respected British architectural historian better known for his sideline as a student of black music.

name: Fadwa Suleiman
profession: Actress and Voice of Syrian Opposition in Exile
headline: Fadwa Suleiman, Actress and Voice of Syrian Opposition in Exile, Dies at 47
abstract: Ms. Suleiman, who fled to France, defied gender and sectarian stereotypes to protest the regime’s repression and propaganda about the civil war.

name: Roy Lunn
headline: Roy Lunn, Pioneering Engineer of Celebrated Cars, Dies at 92
abstract: The British-born Mr. Lunn oversaw development of the Mustang, GT40 and Jeep Cherokee and helped build an almost impregnable presidential limousine.

name: Edward Allcard
profession: Solo Sailor on the High Seas
headline: Edward Allcard, Solo Sailor on the High Seas, Dies at 102
abstract: Mr. Allcard was said to be the first to sail across the Atlantic and back singlehandedly (the stowaway aside). He also circled the globe on a solo trip.

name: Jo Walker-Meador
headline: Jo Walker-Meador, 93, Dies; Raised Country Music’s Profile
abstract: Mrs. Walker-Meador was the first employee of the Country Music Association and its longtime executive director.

name: Stuart J. Thompson
headline: Stuart J. Thompson, Award-Winning Broadway Producer, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Thompson, whose productions were nominated for 20 Tony Awards and won six, helped mount hits like “The Book of Mormon.” “He elevated me,” said Patti LuPone.

name: Arthur Finkelstein
headline: Arthur Finkelstein, Innovative, Influential Conservative Strategist, Dies at 72
abstract: He fundamentally transformed political polling and financing and perfected virulent campaigns that toppled liberal incumbents.

name: Dick Gregory
profession: Found Humor in the Civil Rights Struggle
headline: Dick Gregory, 84, Dies; Found Humor in the Civil Rights Struggle
abstract: A black satirist who gave white audiences a deeper feel for the nation’s shameful racial history, Mr. Gregory was a national sensation in the early 1960s.

name: Jerry Lewis
headline: Jerry Lewis, a Jester Both Silly and Stormy, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Lewis rose to fame as Dean Martin’s comedy partner but went on to a major solo career with films like “The Bellboy” and “The Nutty Professor.”

name: Jerry Lewis
headline: Jerry Lewis, Master of the Congressional Earmark, Dies at 86
abstract: A powerful legislator, he became chairman of the House Appropriations Committee in 2005 but faced scrutiny from the Justice Department for his ties to a lobbyist.

name: Sonny Burgess
headline: Sonny Burgess, Rockabilly Wild Man, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Burgess, who recorded for the storied Sun label, was a full-tilt rocker capable of whipping audiences into a frenzy.

name: Leo Hershkowitz
headline: Leo Hershkowitz, 92, Dies; Unearthed New York City History
abstract: Professor Hershkowitz’s salvage operations earned him a reputation as a highly regarded archival scavenger.

name: Colin Meads
headline: Colin Meads, Revered New Zealand Rugby Star, Dies at 81
abstract: For many New Zealanders, Meads epitomized his nation’s rugged image of itself. As he put it, “Heads down, bottoms up and drive, drive for 80 minutes.”

name: Janusz Glowacki
profession: Polish Playwright of Terror and Dark Humor
headline: Janusz Glowacki, Polish Playwright of Terror and Dark Humor, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Glowacki, whose plays were produced at the Public and other New York theaters, used dark humor to comment on turbulent times.

name: Tony de Brum
profession: Voice of Pacific Islands on Climate Change
headline: Tony de Brum, Voice of Pacific Islands on Climate Change, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. de Brum championed independence for the Marshall Islands and its preservation in the face of rising seas.

name: Thomas Meehan
profession: Wrote the Books for Broadway Hits
headline: Thomas Meehan, Who Wrote the Books for Broadway Hits, Dies at 88
abstract: “Annie,” “Hairspray” and “The Producers” won Tony Awards for Mr. Meehan.

name: M.T. Liggett
headline: M.T. Liggett, 86, Folk Artist and Provocateur, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Liggett’s sculptures, signs and whirligigs have been described as “the gospel according to Rush Limbaugh rendered in wood and steel.”

name: John Abercrombie
headline: John Abercrombie, Lyrical Jazz Guitarist, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Abercrombie had a knack for understatement and was an expert at finding the moments of opportunity in a band’s interplay.

name: Jack Rosenthal
headline: Jack Rosenthal, Times Journalist and Civic Leader, Is Dead at 82
abstract: An aide to Robert F. Kennedy, he later led the editorial page and the Sunday magazine at The New York Times.

name: Brian Aldiss
profession: Author of Science Fiction and Much More
headline: Brian Aldiss, Author of Science Fiction and Much More, Dies at 92
