abstract: Mr. Aldiss wrote scores of novels, memoirs and short stories, including the inspirations for the films “A.I.” and “Frankenstein Unbound.”

name: Bea Wain
profession: Star Singer of the Big Band Era
headline: Bea Wain, Star Singer of the Big Band Era, Dies at 100
abstract: Among the tunes Ms. Wain helped make famous on radio and records was “My Reverie,” based on a melody by Debussy.

name: Felo Ramirez
profession: Enduring Voice of Baseball in Latin America
headline: Felo Ramirez, Enduring Voice of Baseball in Latin America, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Ramirez reached more than 200 radio stations over 72 years, the last 24 announcing Miami Marlins games.

name: Jay Thomas
profession: Actor on Murphy Brown and Cheers
headline: Jay Thomas, Actor on ‘Murphy Brown’ and ‘Cheers,’ Is Dead at 69
abstract: Mr. Thomas, who won two Emmy Awards, was best known for his role as Eddie LeBec, an ice hockey player who was married to the character Carla Tortelli.

name: Cecil D. Andrus
headline: Cecil D. Andrus, 85, Carter’s Preservationist Interior Secretary, Dies
abstract: With Mr. Andrus leading the way, the Carter administration set aside more than 100 million acres in Alaska for federal protection.

name: Marshall H. Klaus
headline: Dr. Marshall H. Klaus, Maternity-Ward Reformer, Dies at 90
abstract: Dr. Klaus’s research led many hospitals to allow closer contact between parents and babies immediately after birth.

name: Vernon Ehlers
headline: Rep. Vernon Ehlers, Who Put Science Before Politics, Dies at 83
abstract: A nuclear physicist before he entered politics, Dr. Ehlers often disagreed with his fellow Republicans on education and the environment.

name: Charles R. Bentley
headline: Charles R. Bentley, 87, Pioneer of Polar Science, Is Dead
abstract: His answer to the question “Would anybody like to go to the Antarctic?” led him to go where no one else had gone and measure what no one else had measured.

name: Tobe Hooper
profession: Director of The Texas Chain Saw Massacre
headline: Tobe Hooper, Director of ‘The Texas Chain Saw Massacre,’ Dies at 74
abstract: Finding little to scare him in most horror films, Mr. Hooper was inspired to create a low-budget movie that became an influential classic of the genre.

name: Fredell Lack
headline: Fredell Lack, Admired Violinist and Teacher, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Lack began touring the world as a teenager, cited for a warm and intimate style. She later elevated music studies at the University of Houston.

name: George A. Keyworth II
headline: George A. Keyworth II, Reagan Science Adviser, Dies at 77
abstract: In the face of stiff opposition, Dr. Keyworth was a strong advocate of the antimissile plan known as Star Wars.

name: Alan Root
headline: Alan Root, Oft-Bitten Wildlife Filmmaker, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Root, often working with his first wife, Joan, came up with inventive ways to capture striking images of African animals and their ecosystems.

name: Jeannie Rousseau de Clarens
headline: Jeannie Rousseau de Clarens, Valiant World War II Spy, Dies at 98
abstract: Using charm and guile, she uncovered Hitler’s rocket program and was held in three concentration camps.

name: Bernard Pomerance
headline: Bernard Pomerance, Who Wrote ‘The Elephant Man,’ Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Pomerance won a Tony Award in 1979 for his play about a deformed man who became a celebrity in Victorian England.

name: Howard Kaminsky
headline: Howard Kaminsky, Publisher With a Best-Seller Sense, Dies at 77
abstract: In top publishing jobs, Mr. Kaminsky steered Richard Simmons, Xaviera Hollander, Richard Nixon and Donald Trump into print while writing his own novels.

name: Ibrahim Yazdi
headline: Ibrahim Yazdi, Leading Iranian Dissident, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Yazdi’s calls for moderation were tolerated because of his early kinship with Ayatollah Khomeini, the father of the Iranian revolution.

name: David Tang
headline: David Tang, Fashion Retailer and Raconteur, Dies at 63
abstract: A lifelong entrepreneur from a wealthy family, he founded a succession of businesses catering to the affluent but also backed democracy for Hong Kong.

name: Jud Heathcote
profession: Coached Michigan State to Basketball Title
headline: Jud Heathcote, 90, Dies; Coached Michigan State to Basketball Title
abstract: Coaching Magic Johnson and his teammates to the N.C.A.A. championship in 1979 was the “euphoric” height of Heathcote’s long career.

name: Rollie Massimino
profession: Rode Dark Horse Villanova to Basketball Glory
headline: Rollie Massimino, 82, Dies; Rode Dark Horse Villanova to Basketball Glory
abstract: For a coach who won more than 800 games, none was sweeter than the 1985 N.C.A.A. final against Georgetown.

name: Sumiteru Taniguchi
headline: Sumiteru Taniguchi, 88, Who Survived Nagasaki to Become Activist, Dies
abstract: Painfully wounded in the atomic bombing when he was 16, he went on to become a prominent campaigner for the abolition of nuclear weapons.

name: Syd Silverman
headline: Syd Silverman, 85, Who Kept Variety Boffo for 30 Years, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Silverman’s grandfather started the show-business bible, known for its headlines and for coining slang expressions, in 1905. He took over in 1957.

name: Elaine Ford
headline: Elaine Ford, Writer of Spare, Detailed Novels, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Ford, whose works included “The Playhouse” and “Monkey Bay,” found her stories in ordinary lives.

name: Larry Elgart
headline: Larry Elgart, Who Kept Swing Up to Date, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Elgart’s recordings included the “American Bandstand” theme and “Hooked on Swing,” a surprise Top 40 hit with a disco beat.

name: Richard Anderson
profession: Six Million Dollar Man and Bionic Woman
headline: Richard Anderson, of ‘Six Million Dollar Man’ and ‘Bionic Woman,’ Dies at 91
abstract: A familiar face to both TV and film audiences, Mr. Anderson was typically cast as an upright authority figure.

name: Shelley Berman
headline: Shelley Berman, Stand-Up Comic Who Skewered Modern Life, Dies at 92
abstract: Along with Mort Sahl, Lenny Bruce and others, Mr. Berman redefined comedy in the mid-20th century while also carving out a notable acting career.

name: Janine Charrat
headline: Janine Charrat, Ballerina and Choreographer, Dies at 93
abstract: A child star as a dancer, Ms. Charrat went on to create important dances at a time when few women were doing so and survived an accident that left her burned.

name: Michael Cromartie
headline: Michael Cromartie, Who Guided Journalists on Religion, Dies at 67
abstract: A former conscientious objector to the Vietnam War, he became an influential evangelical thinker in Washington.

name: Louise Hay
headline: Louise Hay, Widely Read Self-Help Author, Dies at 90
abstract: From a 1984 best seller, Ms. Hay built a publishing empire emphasizing the power of positive thoughts.

name: Karoly Makk
headline: Karoly Makk, Acclaimed Hungarian Filmmaker, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Makk’s “Love” won a prize at the Cannes Film Festival. His “Cats’ Play” was nominated for an Academy Award.

name: Walter Becker
headline: Walter Becker, Guitarist, Songwriter and Co-Founder of Steely Dan, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Becker and Donald Fagen developed a sophisticated, adventurous sound, producing hits like “Do It Again” and “Rikki Don’t Lose That Number” and a raft of acclaimed albums.

name: John Ashbery
profession: Poetic Voice Often Echoed, Never Matched
headline: John Ashbery Is Dead at 90; a Poetic Voice Often Echoed, Never Matched
abstract: Among his many honors, Mr. Ashbery was the first poet to win the Pulitzer, the National Book Award and the National Book Critics Circle Award.

name: Susan Vreeland
profession: Novelist With a Passion for Art
headline: Susan Vreeland, Novelist With a Passion for Art, Dies at 71
abstract: A former high school teacher, Ms. Vreeland was best known for her novel “Girl in Hyacinth Blue,” which traces the history of a fictional painting.

name: Murray Lerner
headline: Murray Lerner, Who Filmed Music’s Biggest Stars, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Lerner’s documentaries about the Newport Folk Festival and the Isle of Wight Festival captured performances by Bob Dylan, the Who and more.

name: Stephen Fybish
profession: Had Much to Say About the Weather
headline: Stephen Fybish, Who Had Much to Say About the Weather, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Fybish carved out a unique amateur niche in meteorological circles as an ardent hoarder and disseminator of weather data.

name: Sugar Ramos
profession: Boxer Remembered for a Fatal Fight
headline: Sugar Ramos, 75, Boxer Remembered for a Fatal Fight, Dies
abstract: The death of Davey Moore three days after Ramos knocked him down led to calls for legislation that would outlaw boxing.

name: Simeon Wright
profession: Witness to Abduction of Emmett Till
headline: Simeon Wright, Witness to Abduction of Emmett Till, Dies at 74
abstract: Two young cousins, one visiting from Chicago, shared a bedroom on the night of a murder in 1955 that shook the nation and galvanized the civil rights movement.

name: Kate Millett
headline: Kate Millett, Ground-Breaking Feminist Writer, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Ms. Millett’s 1970 book, “Sexual Politics,” was revolutionary in its analysis of gender roles in society and provoked a backlash in some quarters.

name: Gene Michael
headline: Gene Michael, Whose Yankee Teams Won 4 World Series, Dies at 79
abstract: A former shortstop, Michael rose to general manager under a mercurial George Steinbrenner and built powerful teams starting in the mid-’90s.

name: Novella Nelson
headline: Novella Nelson, 78, Dies; Brought Authority to Myriad Roles
abstract: An actress whose face was more familiar than her name, Ms. Nelson was seen onstage, in movies and on television for a half-century.

name: Pierre Bergé
profession: Transformative Fashion Executive and Opera Czar
headline: Pierre Bergé, Transformative Fashion Executive and Opera Czar, Dies at 86
abstract: He was the managerial genius behind Yves Saint Laurent, his former lover, and had a stormy run as the head of Paris’s opera houses.

name: Jeffrey Tuchman
profession: Directed Clinton Man From Hope Film
headline: Jeffrey Tuchman, 62, Dies; Directed Clinton ‘Man From Hope’ Film
abstract: An award-winning documentarian, Mr. Tuchman introduced Bill Clinton to many Americans in a film nationally broadcast from the 1992 Democratic convention.

name: Jack Keil
profession: Creator of the Crime-Fighting Dog McGruff
headline: Jack Keil, Creator of the Crime-Fighting Dog McGruff, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Keil spearheaded a campaign to educate Americans on how to “take a bite out of crime,” and provided the voice for its cartoon spokesman.

name: Rick Stevens
headline: Rick Stevens, Funk-Soul Singer Convicted of Murder, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Stevens’s promising career with the band Tower of Power was derailed when he was sentenced to life in prison. He was paroled after 36 years.

name: Don Williams
headline: Don Williams, Singer of Plain-Spoken Country Songs, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Williams, whose admirers included Pete Townshend and Eric Clapton, was best known for ballads extolling the virtues of romantic commitment.

name: Halim El-Dabh
headline: Halim El-Dabh, Composer of Martha Graham Ballets, Dies at 96
abstract: An Egyptian-American composer, Mr. El-Dabh was best known for the haunting, Eastern-inflected scores for “Clytemnestra” and other ballets by Ms. Graham.

name: Holger Czukay
headline: Holger Czukay, 79, Influential Rock Experimenter, Is Dead
abstract: As the bassist and primary sound architect of the German band Can, Mr. Czukay made music that, he said, “creates a certain sort of vision.”

name: Troy Gentry
headline: Troy Gentry of the Country Music Duo Montgomery Gentry Dies at 50
abstract: Mr. Gentry made dynamism out of country hollers and recorded three platinum albums with Eddie Montgomery.

name: Jim McDaniels
profession: Led Western Kentucky to Final Four
headline: Jim McDaniels, 69, Dies; Led Western Kentucky to Final Four
abstract: An all-American in college, McDaniels got off to a tangled start in his professional career because of contract disputes.

name: Michael Friedman
profession: Co-Creator of Bloody Bloody Andrew Jackson
headline: Michael Friedman, Co-Creator of ‘Bloody Bloody Andrew Jackson,’ Dies at 41
abstract: A versatile, cerebral and witty composer and lyricist, Mr. Friedman had a particular fascination with politics, which informed much of his work.

name: Nancy Hatch Dupree
headline: Nancy Hatch Dupree, Scholar of Afghanistan, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mrs. Dupree, who arrived in Afghanistan in 1962, devoted decades to preserving the country’s heritage in its darkest days.

name: Don Ohlmeyer
headline: Don Ohlmeyer, ‘Monday Night Football’ Producer, Dies at 72
abstract: Two decades after Mr. Ohlmeyer managed diverse personalities on the football program, he guided NBC in an era of prime-time hits like “Seinfeld” and “ER.”

name: Len Wein
headline: Len Wein, Influential Comic Book Writer, Dies at 69
abstract: Through characters like Wolverine and Swamp Thing, he helped bring a new depth to his art form.

name: Lotfi Zadeh
headline: Lotfi Zadeh, Father of Mathematical ‘Fuzzy Logic,’ Dies at 96
abstract: Professor Zadeh sought to apply mathematics to the ambiguous ways people talk, think and interact with the world.

name: Nicolaas Bloembergen
profession: Shared Nobel for Advances With Laser Light
headline: Nicolaas Bloembergen, Who Shared Nobel for Advances With Laser Light, Dies at 97
abstract: Dr. Bloembergen, who began his studies in the Nazi-occupied Netherlands, showed how laser light transformed the properties of the material it passed through.

name: Jeremiah Goodman
headline: Jeremiah Goodman, Portraitist of Gilded Homes, Dies at 94
abstract: In paintings, he captured bold interiors by the best designers at the homes of luminaries like Greta Garbo, Ronald and Nancy Reagan, and Wallis Simpson, the duchess of Windsor.

name: Edith Windsor
profession: Same-Sex Marriage Fight Led to Landmark Ruling
headline: Edith Windsor, Whose Same-Sex Marriage Fight Led to Landmark Ruling, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Windsor’s case struck down the Defense of Marriage Act in 2013 and granted same-sex married couples federal recognition for the first time.

name: Douglas Dowd
profession: Antiwar Activist and Critic of Capitalism
headline: Douglas Dowd, 97, Antiwar Activist and Critic of Capitalism Is Dead
abstract: Professor Dowd’s views were largely shaped by his disappointment that the United States had, as he saw it, failed to live up to its ideals.

name: Pete Domenici
profession: Long a Powerful Senate Voice on Fiscal Policy
headline: Pete Domenici, Long a Powerful Senate Voice on Fiscal Policy, Dies at 85
abstract: An influential six-term senator from New Mexico, Mr. Domenici was a plain-spoken master of budget, tax and nuclear power issues.

name: J.P. Donleavy
profession: Acclaimed Author of The Ginger Man
headline: J.P. Donleavy, Acclaimed Author of ‘The Ginger Man,’ Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Donleavy’s first novel, which he called a celebration of “resolutely careless mayhem,” provoked controversy but came to be regarded as a classic.

name: Gary Wadler
headline: Gary Wadler, Expert on Doping in Sports, Dies at 78
abstract: Dr. Wadler was among the doctors and scientists who emerged in the 1980s and ’90s as sports organizations struggled to keep pace with athletes’ illicit drug use.

name: Frank Vincent
profession: Mobster on The Sopranos and in Goodfellas
headline: Frank Vincent, Mobster on ‘The Sopranos’ and in ‘Goodfellas,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Vincent, a character actor who specialized in tough-guy roles, had a particularly memorable scene in “Goodfellas.”

name: Grant Hart
headline: Grant Hart, Hüsker Dü Drummer and Singer, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Hart, along with Bob Mould and Greg Norton, started Hüsker Dü, an early member of the hardcore movement, in the late 1970s in Minnesota.

name: Gastone Moschin
profession: Played a Doomed Don in Godfather Part II
headline: Gastone Moschin Dies at 88; Played a Doomed Don in ‘Godfather Part II’
abstract: Mr. Moschin, an Italian character actor, had the role of Don Fanucci, a dapper crime boss gunned down by Vito Corleone, in Francis Ford Coppola’s “The Godfather Part II.”

name: Hal Tulchin
headline: Hal Tulchin, Who Documented a ‘Black Woodstock,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Tulchin shot an estimated 40 hours of footage of a landmark Harlem event in 1969, most of which the public has never seen.

name: Maurice Bluestein
headline: Maurice Bluestein, Who Modernized the Wind Chill Index, Dies at 76
abstract: While shoveling his daughter’s driveway one winter day, Dr. Bluestein, a scientist, realized something: The wind chill index was wrong.

name: René Laurentin
headline: René Laurentin, Investigator of Celestial Visions, Dies at 99
abstract: A theologian honored by the Vatican, Father Laurentin assessed reports of sightings of the Virgin Mary, from Lourdes to a Texas backyard.

name: Greg Escalante
headline: Greg Escalante, Champion of ‘Lowbrow’ Art, Dies at 62
abstract: As a collector, gallery owner and general enthusiast, Mr. Escalante helped put the brash art of comics and California car culture into galleries.

name: Jerry Pournelle
profession: Science Fiction Novelist and Computer Guide
headline: Jerry Pournelle, Science Fiction Novelist and Computer Guide, Dies at 84
abstract: An aerospace consultant, advice columnist, blogger and best-selling author. (And maybe the first to write a novel on a word-processor.)

name: Harry Dean Stanton
headline: Harry Dean Stanton, Character Actor Who Became a Star, Dies at 91
abstract: The gaunt, hollow-eyed Mr. Stanton had his breakthrough in “Paris, Texas.” As one critic wrote, he was able “to make everything he does seem immediately authentic.”

name: Brenda Lewis
headline: Brenda Lewis, Versatile American Soprano, Is Dead at 96
abstract: A singing actress known for performing work by contemporary composers, Ms. Lewis originated signal roles in the opera house and on the Broadway stage.

name: Penny Chenery
profession: Owner of the Triple Crown Winner Secretariat
headline: Penny Chenery, Owner of the Triple Crown Winner Secretariat, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Chenery knew little about horse racing when she took over her father’s thoroughbred farm, but she became a major figure in the racing industry.

name: Gin Wong
profession: Designed Futuristic Buildings in Los Angeles
headline: Gin Wong, Who Designed Futuristic Buildings in Los Angeles, Dies at 94
abstract: Perhaps best known for a Union 76 gas station in Beverly Hills, Mr. Wong also did design work for the Los Angeles airport and CBS Television City.

name: Stanislav Petrov
headline: Stanislav Petrov, Soviet Officer Who Helped Avert Nuclear War, Is Dead at 77
abstract: After a Soviet computer system warned that the Americans had launched a nuclear missile attack, he decided — correctly — that it was a false alarm.

name: Bobby Heenan
headline: Bobby Heenan, Professional Wrestling Personality, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Heenan, known as the Brain, managed some of wrestling’s top stars and was one of the most colorful commentators the business has seen.

name: Allan J. MacEachen
profession: Force in Bringing Public Health Care to Canada
headline: Allan J. MacEachen, a Force in Bringing Public Health Care to Canada, Dies at 96
abstract: “Canadians are living in a country that Allan J. built, and they like it,” Prime Minister Justin Trudeau said.

name: Joyce Matz
headline: Joyce Matz, Fervid Voice for Historic Preservation, Dies at 92
abstract: St. Bartholomew’s Church, Lever House and the Town Hall were among the sites she helped protect against developers, including Donald J. Trump.

name: Charles Owens
headline: Charles Owens, Golfer, Dies at 85; Novel Putter Brought Late Success
abstract: Owens overcame segregation, severe injuries and, with a long putter, the “yips” to win on the Senior PGA Tour.

name: Jake LaMotta
profession: Raging Bull in and Out of the Ring
headline: Jake LaMotta, ‘Raging Bull’ in and Out of the Ring, Dies at 95
abstract: LaMotta, who learned to box in a reformatory, won the middleweight championship and inspired an acclaimed film in which he was played by Robert De Niro.

name: Lillian Ross
profession: Acclaimed Reporter for The New Yorker
headline: Lillian Ross, Acclaimed Reporter for The New Yorker, Dies at 99
abstract: One of her rules of journalism was, “Do not call attention to yourself.” Yet she did just that in a memoir about her long affair with her celebrated editor.

name: Edmond Eger II
profession: Found Way to Make Anesthesia Safer
headline: Dr. Edmond Eger II, 86, Dies; Found Way to Make Anesthesia Safer
abstract: Dr. Eger and colleagues developed a technique to determine the proper dosage of anesthesia in operating rooms all over the world, saving an untold number of lives.

name: Bernie Casey
headline: Bernie Casey, Who Glided From Football to Hollywood, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Casey was known for roles in “Revenge of the Nerds” and “I’m Gonna Git You Sucka” after eight years as an N.F.L. wide receiver. He was also an accomplished painter.

name: Liliane Bettencourt
profession: LOréal Heiress Vexed by Swindling Case
headline: Liliane Bettencourt, L’Oréal Heiress Vexed by Swindling Case, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Mrs. Bettencourt, ranked as the world’s richest woman, tried to live down her family’s fascist associations, and her final years were overtaken by scandal.

name: Katherine M. Bonniwell
headline: Katherine M. Bonniwell, Life Magazine Publisher, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Bonniwell held a number of top positions at Time Inc. at a heady time for magazine publishing, paving the way for future female managers.

name: Albert Speer Jr.
profession: Architect and Son of Hitler Confidant
headline: Albert Speer Jr., Architect and Son of Hitler Confidant, Dies at 83
abstract: The younger Mr. Speer ultimately had more influence on urban landscapes than his notorious father, from whom he sought to distance himself.

name: Daniel Yankelovich
headline: Daniel Yankelovich, Master of Public Opinion Research, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Yankelovich demonstrated that psychology, sociology and statistical analysis could be harnessed in the service of business, government and the masses.

name: Pete Turner
headline: Pete Turner, Whose Color Photography Could Alter Reality, Dies at 83
abstract: With saturated colors, often on global assignments, Mr. Turner created spectacular images, some for the covers of record albums.

name: Johnny Sandlin
headline: Johnny Sandlin, 72, Allman Brothers Band Producer, Is Dead
abstract: A onetime band mate of Duane and Gregg Allman, Mr. Sandlin worked with their band and many other artists in a career that began at Capricorn Records.

name: Marian Horosko
profession: Dancer and Advocate for the Art
headline: Marian Horosko, Dancer and Advocate for the Art, Dies at 92
abstract: After a performing career that included eight years with New York City Ballet, Ms. Horosko wrote books and championed the health and other needs of dancers.

name: Myrna Lamb
profession: Feminist Playwright in an Unwelcoming Era
headline: Myrna Lamb, Feminist Playwright in an Unwelcoming Era, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Lamb’s works, staged at the Public Theater and elsewhere, often came under attack from male critics.

name: Ritha Devi
headline: Ritha Devi, Indian Classical Dancer and Teacher, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Devi was a specialist in the Odissi form of dance, a once-neglected style that she helped popularize in America in the 1970s.

name: Edgar Smith
headline: Edgar Smith, Killer Who Duped William F. Buckley, Dies at 83
abstract: Sentenced to the electric chair for killing a 15-year-old girl in New Jersey, Mr. Smith won his freedom with help from the conservative commentator.

name: Charles Bradley
headline: Charles Bradley, a Late-in-Life Soul Music Star, Dies at 68
abstract: The singer, once a small-time James Brown impersonator called Black Velvet, was known for his beleaguered rasp and passionate live performances.

name: David Shepherd
headline: David Shepherd, Who Both Painted and Preserved Wildlife, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Shepherd, enraged by poaching and other abuses he witnessed while painting wild animals, formed his own conservation foundation.

name: David Shepherd
headline: David Shepherd, 94, Dies; Nurtured Improvisational Theater
abstract: As a founder of the Compass Players in Chicago, he helped create the world of improvisational comedy that is best known in the work of Second City

name: Barbara Blaine
headline: Barbara Blaine, Who Championed Victims of Priests’ Abuse, Dies at 61
abstract: Ms. Blaine, who had been molested by a priest as a teenager, founded a national network of abuse survivors and became a voice for them.

name: Joseph M. McDade
headline: Joseph M. McDade, 18-Term Pennsylvania Congressman, Dies at 85
abstract: A Republican champion of the coal industry, he delivered for his Scranton-area constituents and survived ethics charges, of which he was acquitted.

name: Basil Gogos
headline: Basil Gogos, Who Painted Monsters With Love, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Gogos made penetrating portraits of Dracula, the Wolf Man and the Phantom of the Opera, and imbued Frankenstein’s monster with notable compassion.

name: Paul Horner
headline: Paul Horner, Fake News Writer Who Took Credit for Trump Victory, Dies at 38
abstract: The cause was an apparent drug overdose. His hoaxes included articles about paid protesters and claims that President Obama was gay and a Muslim.

name: Norman Dyhrenfurth
profession: Led First U.S. Team to Reach Top of Everest
headline: Norman Dyhrenfurth, 99, Dies; Led First U.S. Team to Reach Top of Everest
abstract: Though he did not reach the summit himself, he made it possible for others to plant the flag in 1963 and be honored by President Kennedy

name: Albert Tomei
headline: Albert Tomei, Judge Who Doomed New York Executions, Dies at 77
abstract: He ruled in 1997 that a law reinstating the capital punishment had prodded defendants to plead guilty rather than risk a death sentence by going to trial.

name: Albert Innaurato
headline: Albert Innaurato, Playwright Who Lit Up Broadway in ’70s, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Innaurato had a long stretch of success with “Gemini” and “The Transfiguration of Benno Blimpie” and made a comeback in 2014.

name: Hugh Hefner
profession: Built the Playboy Empire and Embodied It
headline: Hugh Hefner, Who Built the Playboy Empire and Embodied It, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Hefner, the magazine’s very public avatar, styled himself as an emblem of the sexual revolution.

name: Kit Reed
headline: Kit Reed, Author of Darkly Humorous Fiction, Dies at 85
abstract: In novels and stories that hopscotched across genres, happy endings were no more likely than they are in life.

name: Anne Jeffreys
headline: Anne Jeffreys, Glamorous Ghost of ’50s TV, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Ms. Jeffreys, who had a long career in film, on television and on Broadway, was best known for playing the otherworldly Marion Kerby on “Topper.”

name: Red Miller
profession: Coached Broncos to Their First Super Bowl
headline: Red Miller Dies at 89; Coached Broncos to Their First Super Bowl
abstract: Perennial losers since 1960, Denver found glory under Miller, powered by its defensive unit, the Orange Crush.

name: Vann Molyvann
headline: Vann Molyvann, Architect Who Shaped Cambodia’s Capital, Dies at 90
abstract: He returned from years in exile only to watch as his buildings and urban planning were dismantled by unbridled capitalism, corruption and urban sprawl.

name: Lucan
profession: Last Witness to a Murder Most Lurid
headline: Lady Lucan, Last Witness to a Murder Most Lurid, Dies at 80
abstract: Lord Lucan, the first peer indicted in a killing since 1760, disappeared after the 1974 slaying of his children’s nanny. Did he mistake her for his wife?

name: Herbert Kalmbach
headline: Herbert Kalmbach, Who Figured in Watergate Payoffs, Dies at 95
abstract: Nixon’s personal lawyer was the conduit for hush money to the defendants who bungled the break-in. He pleaded guilty in an illegal fund-raising scheme and served time in jail.

name: Reggie Lavong
headline: Reggie Lavong, Smooth-Voiced D.J., Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Lavong helped bring rhythm and blues to New York radio listeners in the 1960s and promoted the genre as a vice president of Capitol Records.

name: Monty Hall
profession: Co-Creator and Host of Lets Make a Deal
headline: Monty Hall, Co-Creator and Host of ‘Let’s Make a Deal,’ Dies at 96
abstract: A smooth-talking personality and ad-libber, he presided over a rollicking game show that, with some interruptions, would last more than 50 years.

name: S.I. Newhouse Jr.
profession: Turned Condé Nast Into a Magazine Powerhouse
headline: S.I. Newhouse Jr., Who Turned Condé Nast Into a Magazine Powerhouse, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Newhouse owned The New Yorker, Vogue, Vanity Fair and other magazines associated with the golden age of publishing.

name: Digby Diehl
profession: Collaborator on Memoirs of the Famous
headline: Digby Diehl, Collaborator on Memoirs of the Famous, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Diehl, a prolific journalist and critic in his own right, wrote autobiographical books with Natalie Cole, Esther Williams, Patti LuPone and more.

name: CeDell Davis
headline: CeDell Davis, Bluesman Who Played Guitar With a Knife, Dies at 91
abstract: His hands were constricted by polio, so Mr. Davis used a knife along his guitar’s fretboard. A critic helped him gain international attention.

name: Ludmila Belousova
headline: Ludmila Belousova, Russian Who Skated With Husband to Olympic Gold, Dies at 81
abstract: She and Oleg Protopopov dominated pairs competition in figure-skating in the 1960s, winning Olympic gold medals with a balletic style.

name: Tom Paley
profession: Drove a Folk Revival With Banjo
headline: Tom Paley, Who Drove a Folk Revival With Banjo, Guitar and Voice, Dies at 89
abstract: Best known for his work with the New Lost City Ramblers, Mr. Paley helped introduce urban audiences to Depression-era rural music.

name: Robert Delpire
headline: Robert Delpire, Champion of Photography as Art, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Delpire, who created his own photographic universe in Paris, didn’t just publish photography books; as one admirer put it, “he reinvented them.”

name: Arthur Janov
profession: Psychologist Caught Worlds Attention With Primal Scream
headline: Arthur Janov, 93, Dies; Psychologist Caught World’s Attention With ‘Primal Scream’
abstract: The father of primal scream therapy, Dr. Janov maintained, not without controversy, that it could cure an array of ills, from alcoholism to asthma.

name: Tom Petty
profession: Mainstay of Rock With the Heartbreakers
headline: Tom Petty, a Mainstay of Rock With the Heartbreakers, Dies at 66
abstract: A singer, songwriter and guitarist, Mr. Petty melded California rock with a Southern heritage in hits like “American Girl” and “Free Fallin’.”

name: Jalal Talabani
profession: Kurdish Leader and Iraqs First Postwar President
headline: Jalal Talabani, Kurdish Leader and Iraq’s First Postwar President, Is Dead at 83
abstract: He used the largely ceremonial position as a bridge-builder during an intensely violent period in the years after the American-led invasion that toppled Saddam Hussein.

name: Zuzana Ruzickova
headline: Zuzana Ruzickova, Leading Harpsichordist and War Survivor, Dies at 90
abstract: She endured death camps, slave labor and Communist dictatorship to become her instrument’s first soloist to record all of Bach’s keyboard works.

name: Paul S. Otellini
profession: Led Intel and Saw It Grow Even More
headline: Paul S. Otellini, Who Led Intel and Saw It Grow Even More, Dies at 66
abstract: As chief of the Silicon Valley giant from 2005 to 2013, he solidified its position in PCs but missed the mobile phone boom.

name: M. Cherif Bassiouni
profession: War-Crimes Jurist and Human Rights Champion
headline: M. Cherif Bassiouni, War-Crimes Jurist and Human Rights Champion, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Bassiouni was an architect of the modern idea of international criminal justice, investigating war crimes and teaching others how to do so.

name: Iulian Vlad
profession: Ex-Chief of Romanias Feared Secret Police
headline: Iulian Vlad, Ex-Chief of Romania’s Feared Secret Police, Dies at 86
abstract: General Vlad’s role in the violent suppression of dissent led to four years in prison for “favoring genocide.”

name: Robert Yates
profession: Nascar Team Owner and Master Engine Builder
headline: Robert Yates, Nascar Team Owner and Master Engine Builder, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Yates’s clients included Junior Johnson, Richard Petty and Bobby and Davey Allison, and his team won 57 races.

name: Anne Wiazemsky
headline: Anne Wiazemsky, Film Star, Wife of Godard and Author, Dies at 70
abstract: She appeared in seven New Wave movies directed by Jean-Luc Godard, her husband of 12 years, and wrote memoirs and novels.

name: Vladimir Voevodsky
headline: Vladimir Voevodsky, Revolutionary Mathematician, Dies at 51
abstract: A once-restless student who flunked out of college went on to found entirely new fields of mathematics. “He has given us a new constitution,” a colleague said.

name: Jim Walrod
profession: Sought-After Guide to Worlds of Design
headline: Jim Walrod, Sought-After Guide to Worlds of Design, Dies at 56
abstract: A sometime interior designer himself, Mr. Walrod knew a lot about a lot and shared it with those outfitting restaurants, hotels and homes.

name: Tom Alter
headline: Tom Alter, Blue-Eyed Star of Bollywood Films, Dies at 67
abstract: Born to missionaries in India, Mr. Alter went on to act in more than 300 films, often as Western diplomats, colonials, priests and police officers.

name: Jack Good
profession: Put Rock n Roll on TV With Shindig
headline: Jack Good, Who Put Rock ’n’ Roll on TV With ‘Shindig,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Good made pop music a television staple, recruiting acts like the Beatles, the Rolling Stones and James Brown as well as go-go girls.

name: Ralphie May
profession: Comedian Who Happens to Be Fat
headline: Ralphie May, 45, Comedian ‘Who Happens to Be Fat,’ Dies
abstract: Mr. May was in residence at Harrah’s casino in Las Vegas when he suffered cardiac arrest. He toured widely and was seen in Netflix specials.

name: Joseph Schmitt
headline: Joseph Schmitt, 101, Spacesuit Technician for Early Astronauts, Dies
abstract: As an equipment specialist, or “suit tech,” Mr. Schmitt was responsible for hooking up Alan Shepard, John Glenn and other astronauts before blastoff.

name: Connie Hawkins
profession: Electrifying N.B.A. Forward Barred in His Prime
headline: Connie Hawkins, Electrifying N.B.A. Forward Barred in His Prime, Dies at 75
abstract: Hawkins, a playground legend in New York, did not make his N.B.A. debut until age 27 because of unfounded connections to a point-shaving scandal.

name: Y.A. Tittle
headline: Y.A. Tittle, Quarterback Who Led Giants to 3 Title Games, Dies at 90
abstract: Tittle endeared himself to New York not as a golden boy but as a muddied, grass-stained scrapper who had been discarded by the 49ers as too slow and too old.

name: Hervé Leroux
profession: Creator of the Hervé Léger Bandage Dress
headline: Hervé Leroux, Creator of the Hervé Léger Bandage Dress, Dies at 60
abstract: At the height of his fame Mr. Leroux dressed celebrities and jet-setters in his figure-hugging creations. Then he lost control of the name that had made him famous.

name: Liam Cosgrave
headline: Liam Cosgrave, Irish Premier Who Helped End Violence, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Cosgrave, who helped break his country’s cycle of violence, had a devotion to political stability steeped in his family’s protracted revolt against British domination.

name: Armando Calderón Sol
headline: Armando Calderón Sol, Who Led El Salvador After War, Dies at 69
abstract: In a five-year term in the 1990s, he began privatizing government-owned utilities, lowered trade barriers and sought to integrate former guerrillas into society.

name: Nora Johnson
profession: Author of The World of Henry Orient
headline: Nora Johnson, Author of ‘The World of Henry Orient,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Johnson, a novelist, essayist and memoirist, had early success with “Henry Orient,” a satire involving private school girls in Manhattan. It was adapted for film and the stage.

name: Jim Landis
profession: Defensive Star for Pennant-Winning White Sox
headline: Jim Landis, Defensive Star for Pennant-Winning White Sox, Dies at 83
abstract: A speedy centerfielder whose fielding — sometimes compared to that of Willie Mays — was a big reason his Chicago team won the 1959 American League title.

name: Holly Block
headline: Holly Block, Director of the Bronx Museum, Dies at 58
abstract: Ms. Block moved just outside the white-hot center of the New York art world, where alternative spaces and smaller museums overlap and cross-fertilize.

name: Michel Jouvet
headline: Michel Jouvet, Who Unlocked REM Sleep’s Secrets, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Jouvet’s research, he wrote, showed that dreaming was “the third state of the brain, as different from sleep as sleep was from waking.”

name: Vincent La Selva
profession: Dauntless Founder of New York Grand Opera
headline: Vincent La Selva, Dauntless Founder of New York Grand Opera, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. La Selva’s loftily named troupe, though intended as a people’s opera company, brought masterworks to Carnegie Hall as well as Central Park.

name: Bob Schiller
headline: Bob Schiller, Writer on Beloved TV Comedies, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Schiller, often teamed with Bob Weiskopf, had to his credit numerous episodes of “I Love Lucy,” “Maude” and “All in the Family,” among others.

name: Grady Tate
headline: Grady Tate, Jazz Drummer Turned Vocalist, Dies at 85
abstract: Celebrated for his versatility as a percussionist, Mr. Tate “never thought of singing as a career,” but somehow it happened.

name: Lawrence Argent
headline: Lawrence Argent, Sculptor Who Was Big on Whimsy, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Argent was especially known for “I See What You Mean,” a 40-foot-tall blue bear peering into the Colorado Convention Center.

name: Terry Downes
headline: Terry Downes Dies at 81; Middleweight Champion Was Britain’s Pride
abstract: Downes was a middleweight champion who fought all but two of his bouts in Britain, defeating a fading Sugar Ray Robinson in 1962.

name: William Lombardy
headline: William Lombardy, Chess Grandmaster Turned Priest, Dies at 79
abstract: The Bronx-born Mr. Lombardy was among the top players of his generation, but he gave up chess almost entirely to join the priesthood, which he later renounced.

name: Mary Cochran
headline: Mary Cochran, Dancer Who ‘Lit Up the Stage,’ Dies at 54
abstract: Ms. Cochran, the daughter of a dancer, performed with the Paul Taylor Dance Company for 12 years, then led the influential dance department at Barnard College for 10.

name: Richard Wilbur
headline: Richard Wilbur, Poet Laureate and Pulitzer Winner, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Wilbur’s poems were praised for their beauty but were criticized for their “mildness.” He was named the nation’s second poet laureate.

name: Roy Dotrice
profession: Nimble British Actor Familiar on Both Sides of Atlantic
headline: Roy Dotrice, Nimble British Actor Familiar on Both Sides of Atlantic, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Dotrice, who began acting in a P.O.W. camp, had a long career in movies, on TV and onstage, winning his Tony in “A Moon for the Misbegotten.”

name: Sima Wali
headline: Sima Wali, Champion of Afghan Women’s Rights, Is Dead at 66
abstract: She wrote of women oppressed by the Taliban, “I carried with me their pleading voices and ultimately their screams, while the world looked away.”

name: Arthur Cinader
headline: Arthur Cinader, Who Started J. Crew, Avatar of Preppy Style, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Cinader created a retail success story by catering to affluent consumers eager to signal a certain Ivy League pedigree in what they wear.

name: Marian Cannon Schlesinger
headline: Marian Cannon Schlesinger, Author and Eyewitness to History, Dies at 105
abstract: A painter, memoirist and daughter of an early feminist, she wrote frankly of the Kennedy White House, where her husband, Arthur Schlesinger Jr., was an adviser.

name: Gord Downie
headline: Gord Downie, a Distinctly Canadian Rock Star, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Downie, who fronted the band the Tragically Hip, announced last year that he had brain cancer.

name: Cornelia Bailey
profession: Champion of African-Rooted Culture in Coastal Georgia
headline: Cornelia Bailey, Champion of African-Rooted Culture in Coastal Georgia, Dies at 72
abstract: Ms. Bailey fought to preserve the traditions of Gullah-Geechee communities on isolated islands, where descendants of slaves have lived for generations.

name: Michele Marsh
headline: Michele Marsh, Longtime New York TV Anchor, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Marsh was the youngest of the women who by 1980 had swept into what was once an exclusively male position on New York newscasts.

name: William Turnage
headline: William Turnage, Who Reinvented the Wilderness Society, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Mr. Turnage turned the organization into an advocacy group and did battle against President Ronald Reagan’s environmental policies.

name: Danielle Darrieux
headline: Danielle Darrieux, French Film Star Over 8 Decades, Is Dead at 100
abstract: Ms. Darrieux’s career of sophisticated roles spanned indelible incarnations as ingénue, coquette, femme fatale and grande dame.

name: Harriette Thompson
headline: Harriette Thompson, Marathon Runner Into Her 90s, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Thompson, a classical pianist and cancer survivor, was 76 when she started running marathons and completed a half-marathon in June.

name: Federico Luppi
profession: Actor Known for del Toro Films
headline: Federico Luppi, 83, Actor Known for del Toro Films, Dies
abstract: A slim and stately Argentine with a shock of white hair, Mr. Luppi endowed his characters with complexity and a sense of gravity.

name: Creighton Hale
headline: Creighton Hale, 93, Inventor of Little League Helmet, Dies
abstract: A physiologist and longtime Little League executive, Mr. Hale worked hard to make baseball safer for young players.

name: Diana Hutchins Angulo
headline: Diana Hutchins Angulo, Western Witness to Chinese History, Dies at 98
abstract: As a child, Ms. Angulo enjoyed “privileged opulence” and had a front-row seat to upheaval in China, decades before the Communist takeover.

name: Robert de Zafra
headline: Robert de Zafra, Who Made Key Findings on Ozone, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. de Zafra was part of a team in Antarctica that helped define the role of aerosol sprays and refrigerants in depleting the protective ozone layer.

name: Jon Lester
profession: Convicted in Howard Beach Race Attack
headline: Jon Lester, Convicted in Howard Beach Race Attack, Dies at 48
abstract: At 17, he was called a ringleader in the 1986 assault by whites in Queens that left a black man dead and another badly beaten. The family said he committed suicide.

name: Marina Sturdza
headline: Marina Sturdza, Romanian Princess and Humanitarian, Dies at 73
abstract: She and her family fled the Communist takeover after World War II. When she returned in the 1990s, she supported child protection and palliative care.

name: Robert Guillaume
headline: Robert Guillaume, Emmy-Winning Star of ‘Benson,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Guillaume won awards for playing a character who began as a caustic butler on one sitcom and ended up as a candidate for governor on another.

name: Al Hurricane
headline: Al Hurricane, Influential New Mexico Balladeer, Dies at 81
abstract: In the 1970s and ’80s, Mr. Hurricane forged a new musical style by blending New Mexico folk music with the rhythms of rock, jazz and country.

name: Fats Domino
profession: Early Rock n Roller With a Boogie-Woogie Piano
headline: Fats Domino, Early Rock ’n’ Roller With a Boogie-Woogie Piano, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Known for his two-fisted piano playing and nonchalant vocals, he had more than three dozen hits, including “Blueberry Hill” and “I’m Walkin’.”

name: Rita Henley Jensen
headline: Rita Henley Jensen, Founder of Women’s eNews, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Jensen, who furthered the journalism careers of numerous women, overcame a lot, including a brush with a notorious robbery.

name: Dennis Wayne
headline: Dennis Wayne, 72, Charismatic Dancer With Leading Troupes, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Wayne had matinee idol looks that made teenage girls scream and a rebellious streak that earned him the nickname the Bad Lad of Ballet.

name: Paul Weitz
headline: Paul Weitz, Astronaut on Skylab and Challenger, Dies at 85
abstract: Captain Weitz commanded the shuttle Challenger on its maiden voyage, and after it later exploded, he was among NASA officials who examined why.

name: Isabella L. Karle
profession: Findings on Molecules Helped Husband Win Nobel
headline: Isabella L. Karle Dies at 95; Findings on Molecules Helped Husband Win Nobel
abstract: Her husband was disappointed that her work, which aided in the development of drugs for illnesses, was not cited by the Nobel committee.

name: Donald Bain
headline: Donald Bain, Widely Read Author (but Not by That Name), Dies at 82
abstract: Whodunit? If you’re asking about a Margaret Truman or a Jessica Fletcher book (or “Coffee, Tea or Me”?), here’s your answer.

name: Tom Mathews
profession: Promoter of Liberal Causes and Candidates
headline: Tom Mathews, Promoter of Liberal Causes and Candidates, Dies at 96
abstract: A former journalist, Mr. Mathews raised the profile of groups like the Peace Corps and was the spokesman for Robert F. Kennedy’s presidential campaign in 1968.

name: Walter Lassally
headline: Walter Lassally, Cinematographer Who Won Oscar for ‘Zorba,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Lassally, whose Academy Award came in 1964, also worked for Tony Richardson, the Merchant Ivory group and many others.

name: Fay Chiang
headline: Fay Chiang, 65, Poet Who Championed Asian-American Culture, Dies
abstract: Ms. Chiang’s poetry reflected her anxieties as a first-generation Chinese-American and her work as a community activist in New York City.

name: Robert Blakeley
profession: Created a Sign of the Cold War
headline: Robert Blakeley, Who Created a Sign of the Cold War, Dies at 95
abstract: Robert Blakeley’s yellow-and-black placards reflected Americans’ anxieties about nuclear war while pointing the way to where they might be saved from it.

name: Terry Laughlin
headline: Terry Laughlin, Who Taught Swimmers Not to Struggle, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Laughlin developed Total Immersion Swimming, which emphasized form over speed and helped thrashing swimmers learn to glide through the water.

name: Wopo Holup
headline: Wopo Holup, Who Adorned Public Spaces With Art, Dies at 80
abstract: At Battery Park in Manhattan and many other places, countless people have seen her works, which often incorporated images from the natural world.

name: Dennis Banks
headline: Dennis Banks, American Indian Civil Rights Leader, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Banks, a Chippewa, led often-violent insurrections to protest the treatment of Native Americans and to call attention to a history of injustices against them.

name: Iona Opie
headline: Iona Opie, 94, Authority on Childish Things, Is Dead
abstract: Mrs. Opie worked with her husband, Peter, to produce major studies of nursery rhymes, games and jokes. She continued the work after his death in 1982.

name: Fred Beckey
headline: Fred Beckey, Conqueror of North American Peaks, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Beckey rarely ventured into the Himalayas or the Andes, instead roaming Alaska, British Columbia and the Pacific Northwest to establish new routes.

name: June Robles Birt
headline: June Robles Birt, Whose Abduction at 6 Gripped the Nation, Is Dead at 87
abstract: After “Little June” was rescued from a coffinlike cage in Arizona in 1934, she vanished again, this time deliberately into an inconspicuous life.

name: Muhal Richard Abrams
headline: Muhal Richard Abrams, 87, Individualistic Pianist and Composer, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Abrams was known both for his diverse, unclassifiable music and for helping to found a long-running Chicago-based musicians’ collective.

name: David Vaughan
headline: David Vaughan, Chronicler of Dance History, Dies at 93
abstract: He was the Merce Cunningham company’s archivist and wrote definitive biographies of choreographers. He also did some dancing and choreography himself.

name: Peter Schutz
headline: Peter Schutz, Executive Who Saved a Signature Porsche, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Schutz, whose family had fled the Nazis, returned to Germany to be the only American to lead the sports car maker. He stopped it from killing the 911 model.

name: Linda Nochlin
headline: Linda Nochlin, 86, Groundbreaking Feminist Art Historian, Is Dead
abstract: She earned a place of honor in art-historical and art-world circles with her provocatively titled 1971 essay “Why Have There Been No Great Women Artists?”

name: Jane Juska
profession: Drew Notice Writing of Late-Life Sex
headline: Jane Juska, 84, Who Drew Notice Writing of Late-Life Sex, Dies
abstract: “Before I turn 67,” she wrote in a personal ad, “I would like a lot of sex with a man I like.” Her encounters were the basis of a well-received book.

name: Joan Tisch
profession: Patron of the Arts and AIDS Fight
headline: Joan Tisch, Patron of the Arts and AIDS Fight, Dies at 90
abstract: A matriarch of a philanthropic family, Mrs. Tisch was a conscientious benefactor who also inherited a half-stake in the New York Giants.

name: Virginia Thoren
headline: Virginia Thoren, Artful Fashion Photographer, Dies at 97
abstract: An advertising designer with no formal training in photography, Ms. Thoren chased beauty with a camera using natural light and realistic settings.

name: Richard Hambleton
headline: Richard Hambleton, ‘Shadowman’ of the ’80s Art Scene, Dies at 65
abstract: His spectral silhouettes appeared mysteriously on buildings in Manhattan — “I painted the town black,” he said — but his work also drew notice abroad.

name: John Mollo
profession: Costumes Made Star Wars Seem Real
headline: John Mollo, Whose Costumes Made ‘Star Wars’ Seem Real, Dies at 86
abstract: An authority on military uniforms, Mr. Mollo was adept at creating verisimilitude in worlds both imagined and remembered.

name: Salvador Minuchin
headline: Salvador Minuchin, a Pioneer of Family Therapy, Dies at 96
abstract: His work with teenagers shifted the focus from individual symptoms to their social environment.

name: Nancy Friday
headline: Nancy Friday, 84, Best-Selling Student of Gender Politics, Dies
abstract: In books like “My Secret Garden: Women’s Sexual Fantasies,” Ms. Friday helped establish what one commentator called “a confessional feminism.”

name: Joe Taub
headline: Joe Taub, Basketball Fan Who Became Part Owner of the Nets, Dies at 88
abstract: With his brother and a future senator, he helped build ADP, but his passion was basketball, and for three decades he was involved with the Nets.

name: Mel Rosenthal
headline: Mel Rosenthal, Photographer Who Captured the Bronx, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Rosenthal’s images of the South Bronx from the 1970s and ’80s documented an area in distress, but they emphasized the survival of the human spirit.

name: Richard Gordon
headline: Richard Gordon, Astronaut Who Reached for Moon and Very Nearly Made It, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Gordon undertook a harrowing spacewalk in 1966 and orbited the moon in 1969, but he never achieved his dream of walking on the lunar surface.

name: Irv Refkin
profession: Brash Accidental Spy in World War II
headline: Irv Refkin, Brash Accidental Spy in World War II, Dies at 96
abstract: By the time the British realized he wasn’t Canadian and the Americans discovered he was missing, he had already parachuted into occupied France.

name: Arjay Miller
headline: Arjay Miller, Who Led a Resurgence at Ford, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Miller was president of the car company in the 1960s, then became dean of Stanford’s Graduate School of Business.

name: Tzipora Jochsberger
profession: Founder of a Jewish Arts School
headline: Tzipora Jochsberger, Founder of a Jewish Arts School, Dies at 96
abstract: Eager for American Jews to appreciate their heritage, Ms. Jochsberger, who left Nazi Germany in 1939, started what is now the Kaufman Music Center.

name: Henry Christensen III
headline: Henry Christensen III, Key Lawyer in Astor Case, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Christensen, who represented Brooke Astor, was esteemed but largely unknown outside his field until her son was accused of defrauding her.

name: Ray Robinson
headline: Ray Robinson, Who Wrote of Gehrig the Man, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Robinson’s sports biographies, which mixed careful research with personal recollections, were more realistic than reverential.

name: John Hillerman
headline: John Hillerman, Snooty Sidekick on ‘Magnum, P.I.,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Hillerman, an Emmy Award-winning actor, also had roles in classic movies like “The Last Picture Show,” “Blazing Saddles” and “Chinatown.”

name: Gilbert Rogin
profession: Magazine Editor and Writer of Droll Fiction
headline: Gilbert Rogin, 87, Magazine Editor and Writer of Droll Fiction, Dies
abstract: Mr. Rogin worked at Sports Illustrated and Discover and had a run of short stories in The New Yorker, until a rejection led him to abandon the form abruptly.

name: Karl Katz
profession: Museum Director in New York and Israel
headline: Karl Katz, Museum Director in New York and Israel, Dies at 88
abstract: Among many other accomplishments, Mr. Katz expanded the Metropolitan Museum of Art’s audience by showcasing its collection on film and television.

name: Katie Lee
headline: Katie Lee, Folk Singer Who Fought to Protect a Canyon, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Lee never forgave the builders of the Glen Canyon Dam and said the only thing that prevented her from blowing it up was that she did not know how.

name: Robert De Cormier
profession: Arranger for Folk and Pop Stars
headline: Robert De Cormier, Arranger for Folk and Pop Stars, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. De Cormier had a musical double life, as a choral director and composer and as an arranger for the likes of Harry Belafonte and Peter, Paul and Mary.

name: Fred Cole
headline: Fred Cole, Leader of Garage-Rock Band Dead Moon, Dies at 69
abstract: A singer and guitarist who became a hero of the Northwest music scene of the 1990s, he set a standard for do-it-yourself perseverance.

name: Liz Smith
profession: Longtime Queen of Tabloid Gossip Columns
headline: Liz Smith, Longtime Queen of Tabloid Gossip Columns, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Smith’s column ran for more than three decades, and she offered a gentler view of movie stars and moguls than many other gossip writers.

name: Patrick Nagatani
headline: Patrick Nagatani, Photographer Famous for Collages, Dies at 72
abstract: His constructions captured the legacies of nuclear weaponry and his parents’ internment in camps for Japanese-Americans during World War II.

name: Thomas Hudner
profession: War Hero in a Civil Rights Milestone
headline: Thomas Hudner, War Hero in a Civil Rights Milestone, Dies at 93
abstract: Lieutenant Hudner defied expectations when he tried to rescue the Navy’s first black aviator during the Korean War. He was awarded the Medal of Honor.

name: Frank Corsaro
headline: Frank Corsaro, Director Who Shook Up Opera World, Dies at 92
abstract: In dozens of productions, many for New York City Opera, Mr. Corsaro sought to energize the form, refusing to let his singers just stand and deliver.

name: Bobby Doerr
profession: Red Sox Hall of Fame Second Baseman
headline: Bobby Doerr, 99, Red Sox Hall of Fame Second Baseman, Is Dead
abstract: An immensely popular player during his 14 seasons with Boston, he had been the oldest living former major leaguer.

name: Debra Chasnoff
headline: Debra Chasnoff, Whose Films Redefined Gay Families, Dies at 60
abstract: An Oscar-winning documentarian, she addressed subjects including parenting, sexuality, bullying, nuclear power and affordable housing.

name: Vanu Bose
profession: Brought Cellular Service to Remote Areas
headline: Vanu Bose, Who Brought Cellular Service to Remote Areas, Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. Bose, whose father founded the Bose Corporation, was an innovator in his own right, developing wireless networks that helped Puerto Rico after Hurricane Maria.

name: Sid Catlett
profession: Star of a Classic High School Basketball Game
headline: Sid Catlett, 69, Star of a Classic High School Basketball Game, Dies
abstract: In 1965 he led his school against the team led by Lew Alcindor, soon to be known as Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, and ended its 71-game winning streak.

name: Paul Buckmaster
profession: Arranger on Hits by Bowie and More
headline: Paul Buckmaster, 71, Arranger on Hits by Bowie and More, Dies
abstract: Mr. Buckmaster worked on classic songs by Elton John and dozens of others, melding rich orchestrations with rock, pop, jazz and country.

name: Uwe Reinhardt
profession: Listened-to Voice on Health Care Policy
headline: Uwe Reinhardt, 80, Dies; a Listened-to Voice on Health Care Policy
abstract: A Princeton economics professor, he was an adviser to Washington policymakers and an advocate of Obamacare.

name: Lil Peep
headline: Lil Peep, Rapper Who Blended Hip-Hop and Emo, Is Dead at 21
abstract: Gustav Ahr was a bright young musical talent who built a rabid following online with songs recorded in a bedroom on Skid Row in Los Angeles.

name: Eric Newman
headline: Eric Newman, Whose Coins Told of America’s History, Dies at 106
abstract: Mr. Newman, a numismatist for nearly a century, was one of the country’s most distinguished authorities on the art and history of coinage and paper money.

name: Ferdie Pacheco
headline: Ferdie Pacheco, ‘Fight Doctor’ for Muhammad Ali, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Pacheco, a physician, provided medical assistance to boxers for four decades and later became a ringside analyst on television.

name: Salvatore Riina
headline: Salvatore Riina, Italian Mafia’s ‘Boss of Bosses,’ Dies at 87
abstract: Known as the Beast, the brutal and murderous leader of the Sicilian Cosa Nostra was serving 26 life sentences.

name: Girish Bhargava
headline: Girish Bhargava, Film Editor Who Captured Dance, Dies at 76
abstract: Whether in “Dance in America” or “Dirty Dancing,” Mr. Bhargava’s eye and sense of musicality were highly prized in translating dance to film.

name: John Raines
profession: Evaded Capture in an F.B.I. Break-in
headline: John Raines, 84, Who Evaded Capture in an F.B.I. Break-in, Dies
abstract: Dr. Raines and his wife were among the antiwar protesters who broke into a field office in 1971 and stole hundreds of files, which they gave to journalists.

name: Jeremy Hutchinson
headline: Jeremy Hutchinson, a Top Lawyer in High-Profile Cases, Dies at 102
abstract: As a leading British barrister he defended Penguin Books for publishing D.H. Lawrence’s “Lady Chatterley’s Lover,” which had been banned as indecent.

name: Gemze de Lappe
profession: Keeper of the Agnes de Mille Flame
headline: Gemze de Lappe, 95, Dies; Keeper of the Agnes de Mille Flame
abstract: She performed de Mille’s choreography and later became and expert at restaging it. She was, one admirer said, “the potter’s clay for Agnes.”

name: Bobby Baker
headline: Bobby Baker, String-Puller Snared in Senate Scandal, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Baker was a significant behind-the-scenes player in the 1950s and early ’60s for Lyndon Johnson, until an investigation felled him.

name: Azzedine Alaïa
headline: Azzedine Alaïa, Fashion’s Most Independent Designer, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Alaïa insisted on his freedom and worked, argued and cooked on his own schedule.

name: Malcolm Young
profession: Guitar Riffs Helped Propel AC/DC to Fame
headline: Malcolm Young, Whose Guitar Riffs Helped Propel AC/DC to Fame, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Young, who was a founder of the band, was known for his raucous energy. A family statement said he had had dementia for several years.

name: Steve Mostyn
headline: Steve Mostyn, Texas Democratic Fund-Raiser, Dies at 46
abstract: Mr. Mostyn was at the center of a long effort to wrest political power from Republicans. Texas Democrats have not won a statewide office since 1994.

name: Mel Tillis
profession: Country Star Known for His Songs and His Stutter
headline: Mel Tillis, Country Star Known for His Songs and His Stutter, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Tillis found a way to turn his speech impediment into an asset by getting audiences to laugh along with him.

name: Pancho Segura
headline: Pancho Segura, Tennis Great of the ’40s and ’50s, Dies at 96
abstract: A crowd-pleaser on the court, Segura flourished as a player for two decades and then coached Jimmy Connors in Grand Slam events in the 1970s.

name: Shannon Michael Cane
headline: Shannon Michael Cane, Who Transformed Art Book Fairs, Dies at 43
abstract: Mr. Cane, an exuberant Australian expatriate, helped foster the growing popularity of fairs focusing on art books.

name: Earle Hyman
profession: Bill Cosbys Father on The Cosby Show
headline: Earle Hyman, Bill Cosby’s Father on ‘The Cosby Show,’ Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Hyman, an accomplished stage actor, was just 11 years older than his television son, but he proved to be an authoritative father figure.

name: Charles Manson
profession: Wild-Eyed Leader of a Murderous Crew
headline: Charles Manson Dies at 83; Wild-Eyed Leader of a Murderous Crew
abstract: Mr. Manson became one of the most notorious killers of the 20th century after his followers brutally murdered seven people in 1969, including the actress Sharon Tate.

name: Jana Novotna
headline: Jana Novotna, Czech Winner of Wimbledon, Dies at 49
abstract: Novotna won a total of 17 Grand Slam titles, 16 of them in doubles and mixed doubles. The tribulations of her singles career, however, came to define her.

name: Della Reese
profession: Singer and Touched by an Angel Star
headline: Della Reese, Singer and ‘Touched by an Angel’ Star, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Reese, who first sang in church, segued from a successful recording career to a long tenure on one of prime-time television’s top-rated shows.

name: Edward Herman
profession: Critic of U.S. Media and Foreign Policy
headline: Edward Herman, 92, Critic of U.S. Media and Foreign Policy, Dies
abstract: An economist, he described a “propaganda model” of newspaper and TV network complicity with a government whose foreign policy was hypocritical.

name: Albert Ledner
headline: Albert Ledner, Architect With a Quirky Sense, Dies at 93
abstract: Three porthole-filled buildings in New York and many unique homes in New Orleans testify to Mr. Ledner’s adventurousness.

name: Pat Hutchins
headline: Pat Hutchins, 75, Dies; Wrote and Illustrated Children’s Books
abstract: Ms. Hutchins, whose best-known book was “Rosie’s Walk,” also wrote stories about a boy named Titch that were adapted for British television.

name: Lilli Hornig
profession: A-Bomb Researcher Lobbied for Women in Science
headline: Lilli Hornig, 96, Dies; A-Bomb Researcher Lobbied for Women in Science
abstract: An alumna of Los Alamos, she became a chemistry professor and urged universities to recruit more women as students, professors and administrators.

name: David Cassidy
headline: David Cassidy, Heartthrob and ‘Partridge Family’ Star, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Cassidy was beloved by fans during the 1970s and continued to perform for decades, but he struggled with his early exposure to fame.

name: Dmitri Hvorostovsky
headline: Dmitri Hvorostovsky, Silver-Maned Baritone From Siberia, Dies at 55
abstract: Mr. Hvorostovsky escaped the street-gang life as a teenager in a grim Siberian city to become an international star.

name: Ann Wedgeworth
profession: Tony-Winning Actress Known for Threes Company
headline: Ann Wedgeworth, 83, Dies; Tony-Winning Actress Known for ‘Three’s Company’
abstract: Ms. Wedgeworth’s characters were often flirtatious, maternal or a combination of both in plays like “Chapter Two” and films like “Steel Magnolias.”

name: Nancy Zieman
headline: Nancy Zieman, Host of Long-Running Sewing Show, Dies at 64
abstract: “Sewing With Nancy” was seen on numerous public television outlets over the last 35 years.

name: George Avakian
headline: George Avakian, Record Producer and Talent Scout, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Avakian was a longtime force in the recording industry, helping the careers of Miles Davis, Dave Brubeck, Keith Jarrett and the comedian Bob Newhart.

name: Jon Hendricks
profession: Brought a New Dimension to Jazz Singing
headline: Jon Hendricks, 96, Who Brought a New Dimension to Jazz Singing, Dies
abstract: His work with the vocal trio Lambert, Hendricks & Ross established him as a master of adding words to jazz instrumentals.

name: Naim Suleymanoglu
headline: Naim Suleymanoglu, 50, Dies; Weight Lifting’s ‘Pocket Hercules’
abstract: At 4-foot-10, he won three consecutive Olympic gold medals in weight lifting, emerging as a national hero in Turkey.

name: Maurice D. Hinchey
headline: Maurice D. Hinchey, Congressman and Environmental Advocate, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Hinchey, a Democrat from New York who served 10 terms in Congress, built a reputation as a champion of the environment and blue-collar workers.

name: C.E. Meyer Jr.
profession: as T.W.A. Chief, He Fought a Takeover
headline: C.E. Meyer Jr., 89, Dies; as T.W.A. Chief, He Fought a Takeover
abstract: Mr. Meyer tried unsuccessfully to thwart the corporate raider Carl Icahn’s bid to take over the troubled airline in 1985.

name: Mary Adelman
headline: Mary Adelman, 89, Fixer of Broken Typewriters, Is Dead
abstract: For decades, her shop on the Upper West Side of Manhattan was a fixture in the lives of writers desperate to keep the words flowing.

name: Eric Salzman
headline: Eric Salzman, Composer Who Championed Avant-Garde, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Salzman, who was also a music critic and book author, was a founder of the American Music Theater Festival in Philadelphia.

name: Pete Moore
profession: Original Miracle and Co-Writer of Hits
headline: Pete Moore, an Original Miracle and Co-Writer of Hits, Dies at 79
abstract: As an integral member of the group led by his childhood friend Smokey Robinson, Mr. Moore played an important role in Motown Records’ origin story.

name: Wayne Cochran
profession: Singer With High Energy and Big Hair
headline: Wayne Cochran, Singer With High Energy and Big Hair, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Cochran wrote a classic song of doomed love, “Last Kiss,” then changed styles to become “the White Knight of Soul.”

name: Vera Shlakman
headline: Vera Shlakman, Professor Fired During Red Scare, Dies at 108
abstract: She had taught economics at Queens College and written a groundbreaking book when she refused to say if she was a Communist. An apology came years later.

name: Neil Gillman
headline: Rabbi Neil Gillman, Theologian of Conservative Judaism, Dies at 84
abstract: Rabbi Gillman sought new ways to talk about God, death and the afterlife. He also championed the ordination of women and gays.

name: Carol Neblett
profession: Soprano at the Met and City Opera
headline: Carol Neblett, Soprano at the Met and City Opera, Dies at 71
abstract: Ms. Neblett performed numerous roles over many years but may have drawn the most attention for one in New Orleans in which she shed her clothes.

name: Harry Pregerson
headline: Harry Pregerson, Judge Guided by Conscience, Dies at 94
abstract: Named by Presidents Johnson and Carter, he served on the Ninth Circuit bench in California as a liberal whose priority was equal protection.

name: Ken Shapiro
headline: Ken Shapiro, Whose ‘Groove Tube’ Satirized TV, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Shapiro’s film, with a cast that included Chevy Chase, anticipated “Saturday Night Live” by a year. But he stopped making movies before he turned 40.

name: Armando Hart
headline: Armando Hart, Who Revolutionized Cuban Schools, Dies at 87
abstract: An early confidant of Fidel Castro, he was credited with greatly improving the nation’s literacy rate as the regime’s first minister of education.

name: W. Marvin Watson
headline: W. Marvin Watson, Johnson’s Unofficial Chief of Staff, Dies at 93
abstract: He spurned several job offers from Lyndon Johnson before finally accepting the role of White House gatekeeper, though without the chief of staff title.

name: Jim Nabors
headline: Jim Nabors, 87, TV’s Gomer Pyle, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Nabors found fame as an amiable bumpkin while pursuing as a second career as a singer with a booming baritone voice.

name: Jerry A. Fodor
headline: Jerry A. Fodor, Philosopher Who Plumbed the Mind’s Depths, Dies at 82
abstract: Dr. Fodor brought the workings of 20th-century computer technology to bear on ancient questions about the structure of human cognition.

name: Jack Doroshow
headline: Jack Doroshow, 78, Drag Pageant Impresario, Dies
abstract: Mr. Doroshow organized pageants in the 1960s, before the gay- and transgender-rights movements had gotten rolling. He hosted them as Flawless Sabrina.

name: Vincent Scully
headline: Vincent Scully, 97, Influential Architecture Historian, Dies
abstract: “I think he probably did more than anyone else over the last 60 years to affect not just architecture but architecture culture as well,” one disciple said.

name: Mitch Margo
headline: Mitch Margo, an Original Member of the Tokens, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Margo helped write a number of songs for the group (although not its biggest hit, “The Lion Sleeps Tonight”). he later wrote music for television.

name: Norman Baker
headline: Norman Baker, Adventurer, Dies at 89; Crossed Atlantic on Reed Raft
abstract: He joined Thor Heyerdahl in 1970 on the Ra II, just one of the adventures that turned a Brooklyn boy into an unconventional world traveler.

name: Leon Cooper
profession: Carried on a Battle for Tarawa
headline: Leon Cooper, Who Carried on a Battle for Tarawa, Dies at 98
abstract: A veteran of the fight to take a Pacific atoll in World War II, he fought for the return of Marines’ remains and to restore a beach as “hallowed ground.”

name: Leon Cooper
headline: Leon Cooper Dies at 94; Nobelist Unlocked Secrets of Superconductivity
abstract: He shared the 1972 physics prize for showing how some materials could convey electricity without resistance. He also did pioneering research in neuroscience.

name: William Mayer
headline: William Mayer, Wide-Ranging Composer, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Mayer produced orchestral works, operas, chamber pieces, music for children and more, sometimes displaying a whimsical streak.

name: John Anderson
profession: Ran Against Reagan and Carter in 1980
headline: John Anderson, Who Ran Against Reagan and Carter in 1980, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Drawing support from moderate to liberal Republicans and liberal Democrats, Mr. Anderson held the spotlight for a while before voters turned to candidates who they believed could actually win.

name: Shashi Kapoor
headline: Shashi Kapoor, Indian Film Star in ’70s and ’80s, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Kapoor, who appeared in scores of Hindi films as well as Merchant Ivory productions, broke a taboo in 1978 with an onscreen kiss.

name: Surin Pitsuwan
profession: Envoy and Voice of Southeast Asia
headline: Surin Pitsuwan, Envoy and Voice of Southeast Asia, Dies at 68
abstract: As secretary general of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, Mr. Surin sought to promote democracy and human rights in a fractious region.

name: Ali Abdullah Saleh
headline: Ali Abdullah Saleh, Strongman Who Helped Unite Yemen, and Divide It, Dies at 75
abstract: A former president who left a legacy of corruption, he re-emerged to play a major role in his country’s civil war.

name: Gillian Rolton
headline: Gillian Rolton, Australian Who Won Gold Despite Broken Bones, Dies at 61
abstract: In 1996 in Atlanta, she fell off her horse twice and broke her collarbone, but she completed her ride and helped her country win a gold medal.

name: Ivan Chermayeff
headline: Ivan Chermayeff, 85, Eminent Designer of Familiar Logos, Dies
abstract: One of the first to convey corporate identity by means of abstraction, Mr. Chermayeff created logos for Showtime, the Smithsonian, Pan Am and more.

name: Michael
headline: King Michael of Romania, Who Ousted a Hitler Puppet, Dies at 96
abstract: First becoming king at age 5, Michael, at just 22, may have shortened World War II by arresting his country’s fascist dictator. He later went into exile.

name: Christine Keeler
profession: Central Figure in British Scandal of the Century
headline: Christine Keeler, Central Figure in British ‘Scandal of the Century,’ Is Dead at 75
abstract: Ms. Keeler’s affair with the government minister John Profumo and other revelations set England abuzz in the early 1960s.

name: Christine Keeler
profession: Central Figure in British Scandal of the Century
headline: Christine Keeler, Central Figure in British ‘Scandal of the Century,’ Is Dead at 75
abstract: News of her affair with the government minister John Profumo and other revelations set England abuzz in the early 1960s.

name: Johnny Hallyday
headline: Johnny Hallyday, the Elvis Presley of France, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Although he was little known outside the French-speaking world, Mr. Hallyday sold more than 100 million records and starred in numerous movies.

name: Jean d’Ormesson
headline: Jean d’Ormesson, ‘Immortal’ French Man of Letters, Dies at 92
abstract: Once the youngest of the Académie Française’s 40 “immortals,” he became a national figure through his writings and television appearances.

name: Maurice Carroll
headline: Maurice Carroll, Political Reporter and Pollster, Dies at 86
abstract: Mickey Carroll, as he was known, was a fixture in the pages of New York-area newspapers and afterward helped raise the profile of the Quinnipiac poll.

name: William H. Gass
headline: William H. Gass, Acclaimed Postmodern Author, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Gass never scored a best seller, but his ideas and his inventive use of language were influential.

name: Ernest Finney Jr.
headline: Ernest Finney Jr., Rights Lawyer in ‘Jail, Not Bail’ Case, Dies at 86
abstract: He represented the Friendship Nine, who chose jail rather than fines after a 1961 sit-in. He went on to become South Carolina’s first black chief justice.

name: Bill Steinkraus
headline: Bill Steinkraus, Equestrian Who Made Olympic History, Dies at 92
abstract: One of the sport’s most celebrated riders, Steinkraus was the first American to win an individual gold medal in equestrian events.

name: Perry Wallace
headline: Perry Wallace, College Basketball Pioneer, Is Dead at 69
abstract: As the first black varsity basketball player in Southeastern Conference history, he distinguished himself on the court while battling racism.

name: Les Whitten
headline: Les Whitten, Muckraking Columnist and Novelist, Dies at 89
abstract: He shared a byline with Jack Anderson and was arrested in 1973 in a First Amendment controversy involving his possession of stolen government files.

name: Ron Meyer
profession: Coached S.M.U. to a Football Title
headline: Ron Meyer, Who Coached S.M.U. to a Football Title, Dies at 76
abstract: Under Meyer, the Mustangs reigned in 1981 but were soon stained by a recruiting scandal. He later coached the Patriots and Colts in the N.F.L.

name: Mickey Gurdus
headline: Mickey Gurdus, Who Eavesdropped on the World, Dies at 73
abstract: An Israeli, Mr. Gurdus monitored private and public communications over the air to create his own journalistic niche and score reportorial scoops.

name: Tracy Stallard
headline: Tracy Stallard, Who Gave Up Historic Maris Homer, Dies at 80
abstract: On the last day of the 1961 season, Roger Maris hit a Stallard fastball into Yankee Stadium’s right-field seats, breaking Babe Ruth’s record of 60 home runs.

name: Leslie Wolfe
headline: Leslie Wolfe, Who Pursued Equality for Women, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Wolfe sought AIDS treatment for women in the 1980s and researched gender and racial bias on the SAT exam as head of a think tank.

name: Simeon Booker
headline: Simeon Booker, Pioneering Reporter on Race Issues, Dies at 99
abstract: The first black reporter at The Washington Post, Mr. Booker left to become a Jet magazine columnist and Washington bureau chief for its parent company.

name: Roy Reed
headline: Roy Reed, Times Reporter Who Covered the Civil Rights Era, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Reed was with Martin Luther King when he was released from jail in Selma, Ala., and with protesters on Bloody Sunday at the Pettus Bridge.

name: Marshall Loeb
headline: Marshall Loeb, Editor Who Shaped Money and Fortune Magazines, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Loeb turned a floundering Money into one of the nation’s most successful publications in the 1980s and led a similar revival at Fortune.

name: Charles Jenkins
headline: Charles Jenkins, 77, U.S. Soldier Who Regretted Fleeing to North Korea, Dies
abstract: Patrolling the zone between North and South Korea in 1965, he fled his post to avoid combat in Vietnam. He was kept in North Korea for almost 40 years.

name: Ed Lee
headline: Ed Lee, San Francisco’s First Asian-American Mayor, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Lee was long an advocate for affordable housing in a city that in recent years has seen housing costs soar amid an explosion of economic growth.

name: Bruce Brown
headline: Bruce Brown, 80, Dies; His ‘Endless Summer’ Documented Surfing
abstract: Mr. Brown’s movie became an unlikely hit when it was released nationally in 1966 and helped change the way surfers are perceived.

name: Enrico Castellani
headline: Enrico Castellani, Artist in the Postwar Avant-Garde, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Castellani, from Italy, was part of a swirl of movements and groups that rejected emotion and subjectivity and flourished on both sides of the Atlantic.

name: Macon Brock Jr.
headline: Macon Brock Jr., Co-Founder of Dollar Tree, Dies at 75
abstract: Years in the toy business gave Mr. Brock the merchandising skills that sent him around the world looking for products for his discount stores.

name: Anthony Harvey
profession: Lion in Winter Director and Kubrick Editor
headline: Anthony Harvey, ‘Lion in Winter’ Director and Kubrick Editor, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Harvey began as a film editor, filling that role on “Dr. Strangelove,” but ended up directing Katharine Hepburn in several movies.

name: Clarence Beavers
profession: Last of a Black Paratroop Unit
headline: Clarence Beavers, Last of a Black Paratroop Unit, Dies at 96
abstract: The unit, known as the Triple Nickels, was trained for combat but assigned in 1945 to fight fires ignited by Japanese balloon bombs in the Northwest.

name: Vera Katz
headline: Vera Katz, Mayor Who Oversaw Portland’s Flowering, Dies at 84
abstract: A feminist force and lawmaker in Oregon, she served three terms in Portland as it grew into a liberal bastion of visionary urban planning.

name: Aharon Leib Shteinman
headline: Aharon Leib Shteinman, Ultra-Orthodox Leader in Israel, Dies at 104
abstract: The rabbi’s influence was particularly felt when he reluctantly agreed that some ultra-Orthodox adherents should be eligible for Israel’s military conscription.

name: Anthony Scaduto
headline: Anthony Scaduto, an Early Biographer of Dylan, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Scaduto, a journalist with a long tenure at The New York Post, also wrote a book challenging the verdict in the kidnapping of the Lindbergh baby.

name: Pat DiNizio
profession: Singer and Songwriter for the Smithereens
headline: Pat DiNizio, Singer and Songwriter for the Smithereens, Dies at 62
