abstract: He and three others from New Jersey formed the group in 1980 and attracted a loyal following with songs like “Blood and Roses” and “A Girl Like You.”

name: Vincent Nguini
headline: Vincent Nguini, Guitarist With Paul Simon, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Simon called the Cameroonian-born Mr. Nguini, a member of his band for 30 years, “the most creative musician I’ve ever worked with.”

name: Sunny Murray
headline: Sunny Murray, Influential Free-Jazz Drummer, Is Dead at 81
abstract: In his work with Cecil Taylor and Albert Ayler, Mr. Murray treated the drum set as a palette of textures more than a percussion instrument.

name: Stuart Evey
headline: Stuart Evey, a Founding Force at ESPN, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Evey persuaded his bosses at Getty Oil to invest in the start-up sports network and then helped manage it as it took wing.

name: Marina Popovich
headline: Marina Popovich, Record-Breaking Soviet Test Pilot, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Popovich broke the sound barrier in 1964. But despite speculation, she did not become the first Soviet woman to travel in space.

name: Model
headline: Model, Countess, Author, Spy: Aline Griffith Is Dead
abstract: An American espionage agent in Madrid in World War II, she went on to recount daring adventures (embroidered or not) in a raft of books.

name: Kevin Robinson
headline: Kevin Robinson, Soaring BMX Star, Dies at 45
abstract: He was the first BMX rider to land an incredibly difficult move called the double flair. He also set two world records.

name: Howard Gottfried
headline: Howard Gottfried, 94, Producer of ‘Network,’ Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Gottfried was a calming, levelheaded influence on the talented but ornery screenwriter Paddy Chayefsky for more than a decade.

name: Bette Howland
headline: Bette Howland, Author and Protégée of Bellow’s, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Howland wrote three well-regarded books and in 1984 won a MacArthur grant. But then she largely disappeared, to be rediscovered only recently.

name: Bob Seidemann
profession: Photographer of Rock Stars and Aviators
headline: Bob Seidemann, 75, Photographer of Rock Stars and Aviators, Dies
abstract: He became famous for his shots of Janis Joplin and the Grateful Dead. His later subjects included Chuck Yeager and Gen. James Doolittle.

name: Martin Ransohoff
headline: Martin Ransohoff, Producer of TV and Film, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Ransohoff was a force behind both light television fare like “Mister Ed” and substantive movies like “The Americanization of Emily.”

name: Lones Wigger Jr.
headline: Lones Wigger Jr., ‘Best Ever’ Rifle Marksman, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Wigger won Olympic gold medals and broke dozens of world records on the rifle range. One magazine called him “the greatest shooter in history.”

name: Keely Smith
profession: Torch Singer With a Deadpan Role
headline: Keely Smith, Torch Singer With a Deadpan Role, Is Dead at 89
abstract: As the calm half of a lounge act with the ebullient Louis Prima, Ms. Smith had hit records and won a Grammy. She went on to a successful solo career.

name: Johnny Fox
headline: Johnny Fox, Sword-Swallowing Showman, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Fox was a mainstay at the Maryland Renaissance Festival and for a time operated a quirky museum called the Freakatorium on the Lower East Side.

name: Kevin Mahogany
headline: Kevin Mahogany, Masterly Jazz Singer, Is Dead at 59
abstract: His style drew on Kansas City’s tradition of bluesy male vocals, while also reflecting the influence of R&B and jazz from the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Robert G. Wilmers
headline: Robert G. Wilmers, Bank Chief and Buffalo Philanthropist, Dies at 83
abstract: He steered M&T Bank through the 2008 financial crisis without so much as reducing its stock dividend and had been at the helm for almost 35 years.

name: Bernard Law
profession: Powerful Cardinal Disgraced by Priest Abuse Scandal
headline: Bernard Law, Powerful Cardinal Disgraced by Priest Abuse Scandal, Dies at 86
abstract: His stature as archbishop of Boston and America’s senior Roman Catholic prelate was shattered by revelations that he had protected child molesters for years.

name: Yu Guangzhong
headline: Yu Guangzhong, Exiled Poet Who Longed for China, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Yu’s poem “Nostalgia” symbolized the aching separation felt by a generation of homesick Chinese who lived in Taiwan.

name: Clifford Irving
profession: Author of a Notorious Literary Hoax
headline: Clifford Irving, Author of a Notorious Literary Hoax, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Irving’s “Autobiography of Howard Hughes” was one of the biggest literary scandals of the 20th century and landed him in jail.

name: Mamie Johnson
headline: Mamie Johnson, Trailblazer in the Negro Leagues, Dies at 82
abstract: Johnson, known as Peanut, was the only woman known to pitch in the leagues, playing for the Indianapolis Clowns and compiling an impressive record.

name: Janet Elder
headline: Janet Elder, a Top Editor at The Times, Dies at 61
abstract: For years Ms. Elder reported the results of CBS News/Times polls assessing the public’s views on politicians, social issues and even driving habits.

name: Combat Jack
headline: Combat Jack, Hip-Hop Lawyer Turned Podcast Pioneer, Dies at 53
abstract: Reggie Ossé captured lightning in a bottle twice, first as a lawyer in the 1990s and later as a podcaster as rap had moved online.

name: Janet Benshoof
profession: Womens Champion on a Global Scale
headline: Janet Benshoof, Women’s Champion on a Global Scale, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Benshoof, a lawyer, defended abortion and contraceptive rights in American courts and took on cases of sexual violence, war crimes and genocide abroad.

name: Edward Rowny
headline: Edward Rowny, Outspoken Treaty Negotiator, Dies at 100
abstract: General Rowny advised presidents from Richard Nixon to George H.W. Bush during talks with the Soviet Union about nuclear arms. He could be blunt.

name: Dick Enberg
headline: Dick Enberg, Veteran Sportscaster, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Few sportscasters were as versatile as Mr. Enberg, whose signature “Oh, my!” rang out during countless sporting events over a 60-year career.

name: Diane Straus
headline: Diane Straus, Publisher of Liberal Policy Magazines, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Straus led The American Prospect before taking the reins of Washington Monthly and leading its revival. She was also a platform tennis champion.

name: Bruce McCandless
profession: First to Fly Untethered in Space
headline: Bruce McCandless, First to Fly Untethered in Space, Dies at 80
abstract: A photograph of Mr. McCandless floating above Earth captured the imagination of millions. He also played a role in Neil Armstrong’s moonwalk.

name: Arseny Roginsky
headline: Arseny Roginsky, Russian Human Rights Leader, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Leading the organization Memorial, Mr. Roginsky, a former political prisoner, documented state persecution during the Soviet period and after.

name: Hiep Thi Le
headline: Hiep Thi Le, Vietnamese Refugee Who Became Film Star, Dies at 46
abstract: Ms. Le was merely accompanying friends when she went to an open casting call for Oliver Stone’s “Heaven and Earth.” She landed the central role.

name: Jerry Yellin
profession: Flew the Last World War II Combat Mission
headline: Jerry Yellin, 93, Dies; Flew the Last World War II Combat Mission
abstract: He led an attack on Japan the day Emperor Hirohito surrendered. He later fought a battle against what is now known as post-traumatic stress disorder.

name: Lou Adler
profession: Fixture of New York Radio News
headline: Lou Adler, a Fixture of New York Radio News, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Adler spent much of his career at WCBS-AM, where he anchored the news and also served as the station’s news director.

name: William Agee
headline: William Agee, ’70s C.E.O. Whose Star Was Dimmed, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Agee’s relationship with a female subordinate, Mary Cunningham, raised issues of gender and behavior in the workplace that resonate today.

name: William Agee
headline: William Agee, Leading Art Curator and Teacher, Dies at 86
abstract: His exhibitions and his writings expanded the view of American Modernism, and his decades of teaching shaped future scholars and curators.

name: Don Hogan Charles
profession: Lauded Photographer of Civil Rights Era
headline: Don Hogan Charles, Lauded Photographer of Civil Rights Era, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Charles, the first black photographer to be hired by The New York Times, took pictures of Malcolm X, Coretta Scott King and Muhammad Ali.

name: Thomas P. Griesa
headline: Judge Thomas P. Griesa, Who Ruled Against Westway, Dies at 87
abstract: He presided over two of the most ambitious development proposals in New York City history: a superhighway in Manhattan and revival of Times Square.

name: Simonetta Puccini
headline: Simonetta Puccini, Keeper of the Composer’s Flame, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Puccini went to court to get herself recognized as a granddaughter of Giacomo Puccini. She then worked to foster his legacy.

name: Z’ev
headline: Z’ev, Percussionist and Industrial Music Pioneer, Dies at 66
abstract: An explorer of sound’s visceral and mystical dimensions, Z’ev was a performer, composer and theorist for whom “cacophonous” was a compliment.

name: Roswell Rudd
headline: Roswell Rudd, 82, Trombonist With a Wide-Open Approach, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Rudd helped to establish a place for his instrument on the free-jazz scene of the 1960s. He later explored a broad array of other styles.

name: Johnny Bower
headline: Johnny Bower, Oldest Full-Time N.H.L. Goalie, Dies at 93
abstract: Bower was 45 when he played his last game in the National Hockey League. He won four Stanley Cups with the Toronto Maple Leafs in a Hall of Fame career.

name: Jerold F. Lucey
headline: Jerold F. Lucey, Innovator in Premature Births, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Lucey helped introduce new treatments for fragile newborns and edited the journal Pediatrics for 35 years.

name: Ralph Carney
profession: Saxophonist for Tom Waits and Many Others
headline: Ralph Carney, Saxophonist for Tom Waits and Many Others, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Carney, who also played dozens of other instruments, was a versatile musician with a distinct sensibility who recorded widely, and wildly.

name: Larry Harris
profession: Promoter of a Risk-Taking Record Label
headline: Larry Harris, Promoter of a Risk-Taking Record Label, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Harris helped Neil Bogart found Casablanca, which in the ’70s was known for its wildness and a roster that included Donna Summer and Kiss.

name: Yehoshua Hershkowitz
profession: Founder of a Kosher Meal Program
headline: Yehoshua Hershkowitz, 92, Founder of a Kosher Meal Program, Dies
abstract: He founded Tomche Shabbos out of his kitchen in Brooklyn to bring food to people in need. It now distributes meals to 600 families every week.

name: Marcus Raskin
headline: Marcus Raskin, Co-Founder of Liberal Think Tank, Dies at 83
abstract: He and Richard Barnet provided research on war, draft resistance, economic inequality and civil rights and had a role in the Pentagon Papers episode.

name: Rose Marie
profession: Showbiz Veteran and Dick Van Dyke Show Star
headline: Rose Marie, Showbiz Veteran and ‘Dick Van Dyke Show’ Star, Dies at 94
abstract: Originally known as Baby Rose Marie, she became a star as a toddler and again on one of television’s most beloved comedies.

name: Recy Taylor
profession: Fought for Justice After a 1944 Rape
headline: Recy Taylor, Who Fought for Justice After a 1944 Rape, Dies at 97
abstract: The crime was never prosecuted because two all-white grand juries refused to indict her attackers. Alabama lawmakers apologized in 2011.

name: Ben Barres
headline: Ben Barres, Neuroscientist and Equal-Opportunity Advocate, Dies at 63
abstract: Dr. Barres, who in 1997 transitioned from female to male, drew on his experiences as a woman to highlight the obstacles women in science face.

name: Sue Grafton
headline: Sue Grafton, Whose Detective Novels Spanned the Alphabet, Dies at 77
abstract: Her popular series about a female private eye began in 1982 with “A Is for Alibi” and continued through “Y Is for Yesterday” this year.

name: Kenichi Yamamoto
headline: Kenichi Yamamoto, Father of Mazda’s Rotary Engine, Is Dead at 95
abstract: He led the engineering team that produced an innovative answer to the conventional piston automotive engine. He later led the company.

name: John Portman
headline: John Portman, Architect Who Made Skylines Soar, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Portman, who was also a developer, built futuristic office complexes and hotels with towering atriums, transforming cityscapes across the world.

name: Dan Talbot
headline: Dan Talbot, Impresario of Art Films, Is Dead at 91
abstract: As an operator of Lincoln Plaza Cinemas and the New Yorker Theater, Mr. Talbot introduced Americans to a whole universe of European filmmaking.

name: Maura Jacobson
headline: Maura Jacobson, Creator of Witty Crosswords, Dies at 91
abstract: A superstar to crossword fans, Ms. Jacobson made more than 1,400 puzzles for New York magazine, filling them with puns and sparkling thematic clues.

name: Calestous Juma
headline: Calestous Juma, 64, Dies; Sought Innovation in African Agriculture
abstract: Professor Juma believed that science, particularly biotechnology, could play a major role in improving life in Africa.

name: Lawrence Stager
headline: Lawrence Stager, Creative Biblical Archaeologist, Dies at 74
abstract: A Harvard professor, he led excavations in Ashkelon, Israel, that discovered a “golden calf” and a rare Philistine cemetery.

name: LeRoy Jolley
headline: LeRoy Jolley, Who Trained Two Derby Winners, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Jolley, who learned at the side of his father, also a trainer, won the Kentucky race with Foolish Pleasure in 1975 and Genuine Risk in 1980.

name: Rick Hall
profession: Architect of the Muscle Shoals Sound
headline: Rick Hall, Architect of the Muscle Shoals Sound, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Hall, a producer and engineer and the founder of FAME Studios, turned small-town Alabama into a crucible of soul, country, rock and pop music.

name: Thomas Monson
headline: Thomas Monson, President of the Mormon Church, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Monson enlarged the ranks of female Mormon missionaries, but he stood firm against ordaining women as priests and against same-sex marriage.

name: Fred Bass
profession: Made the Strand Bookstore a Mecca
headline: Fred Bass, Who Made the Strand Bookstore a Mecca, Dies at 89
abstract: Building on what his father began, Mr. Bass ultimately oversaw a bustling emporium housing “18 miles of books” in Lower Manhattan, with outposts here and there.

name: Ulrich Wegener
headline: Ulrich Wegener, German Commando Who Ended 1977 Hijacking, Is Dead
abstract: After a massacre at the Munich Olympics in 1972, Mr. Wegener created and led an elite counterterrorism squad known as GSG-9.

name: Aharon Appelfeld
profession: Israeli Novelist Haunted by the Holocaust
headline: Aharon Appelfeld, Israeli Novelist Haunted by the Holocaust, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Appelfeld, a survivor himself, made the plight of Jews during World War II his great subject, but in stories told obliquely, from a seemingly naïve viewpoint.

name: Maurice Peress
headline: Maurice Peress, Conductor Who Worked With Ellington, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Peress also had a long association with Leonard Bernstein, for whom he was an assistant conductor in the early 1960s.

name: Carmen Cozza
profession: Hall of Fame Football Coach at Yale
headline: Carmen Cozza, Hall of Fame Football Coach at Yale, Dies at 87
abstract: In one stretch, Cozza’s Bulldogs won seven of eight Ivy League titles and in an unbeaten season played a memorable finale against Harvard.

name: Jimmie Holland
profession: Cared for the Cancer Patients Mind
headline: Jimmie Holland, Who Cared for the Cancer Patient’s Mind, Dies at 89
abstract: In a groundbreaking field, Dr. Holland addressed patients’ depression and anxiety and rejected what she called “the tyranny of positive thinking.”

name: Brendan Byrne
headline: Brendan Byrne, Former New Jersey Governor, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Mr. Byrne helped lure professional sports teams to New Jersey and risked his political future by winning passage of the state’s first income tax.

name: Eugene V. Thaw
headline: Eugene V. Thaw, Influential Art Collector and Dealer, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Thaw’s collection contained more than 400 drawings by European old masters, and he helped produce a monumental compendium on Jackson Pollock.

name: Jerome Lefkowitz
profession: Force in New York Labor Law
headline: Jerome Lefkowitz, a Force in New York Labor Law, Dies at 86
abstract: He helped draft the Taylor Law, which gives public employees bargaining rights but bars them from striking. He also led the agency that enforces it.

name: Peggy Cummins
profession: Seductive Star of a Cult Film
headline: Peggy Cummins, Seductive Star of a Cult Film, Dies at 92
abstract: The slender, blond Ms. Cummins had mostly played innocents until being cast in her best-known role, as a bloodthirsty sharpshooter in “Gun Crazy.”

name: Betty Woodman
headline: Betty Woodman, Who Spun Pottery Into Multimedia Art, Dies at 87
abstract: Her evolution from artisan to fine artist culminated in a retrospective at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, its first for a living female artist.

name: Jerry Van Dyke
profession: Coach Actor and Foil for His Brother
headline: Jerry Van Dyke, ‘Coach’ Actor and Foil for His Brother, Dick, Dies at 86
abstract: After decades in show business, Mr. Van Dyke emerged from his older brother’s shadow with an Emmy-nominated role in the long-running ABC sitcom “Coach.”

name: Horace Ashenfelter
profession: Olympic Victor of a Cold War Showdown
headline: Horace Ashenfelter, Olympic Victor of a Cold War Showdown, Dies at 94
abstract: Ashenfelter, an F.B.I. agent, won gold at the 1952 Games by passing a favored Soviet runner on the final water obstacle of the 3,000-meter steeplechase.

name: Tatsuro Toyoda
headline: Tatsuro Toyoda, Who Led Toyota’s Global Expansion, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Toyoda led Toyota’s first factory in North America, bringing with him a Japanese approach to manufacturing and labor relations.

name: Ray Thomas
profession: Founding Member of the Moody Blues
headline: Ray Thomas, Founding Member of the Moody Blues, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Thomas sang, wrote songs and played flute, most notably on “Nights in White Satin,” which became the group’s signature song.

name: Alan Sagner
headline: Alan Sagner, Who Revitalized the Port Authority, Dies at 97
abstract: A Democratic fund-raiser, he ran the New York-New Jersey agency from 1977 to 1985 and later headed the Corporation for Public Broadcasting.

name: Tim Rollins
profession: Turned Bronx Teenagers Into Art Stars
headline: Tim Rollins Dies at 62; Turned Bronx Teenagers Into Art Stars
abstract: Mr. Rollins devoted almost all of his career to an unusual combination of art-making and teaching, and to the group known as Tim Rollins + K.O.S.

name: France Gall
headline: France Gall, Adaptable French Singing Star, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Ms. Gall had big hits in the 1960s in the pop genre known as ye-ye, then embraced more mature styles in a recording career that stretched into the 1980s.

name: Karin von Aroldingen
headline: Karin von Aroldingen, a Major Dancer for Balanchine, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Whether exuding power or poignancy, she left a lasting impact at City Ballet on roles that he choreographed expressly for her.

name: Anna Mae Hays
headline: Anna Mae Hays, 97, U.S. Military’s First Female General, Dies
abstract: She served on the front lines during World War II and Korea and, as chief of the Army Nurse Corps, sought to contain casualties in Vietnam.

name: James Melius
headline: Dr. James Melius, Advocate for Workers’ Health, Dies at 69
abstract: His expertise was essential to the creation of the law that authorized billions to help those whose health was affected by the 9/11 terrorist attacks.

name: Odvar Nordli
headline: Odvar Nordli, a Cold War Leader of Norway, Dies at 90
abstract: As a Labor prime minister, he pressed a social-democratic agenda. But he resigned under fire for letting the U.S. stockpile weapons near the Soviet border.

name: Denise LaSalle
profession: Singer and Writer of Earthy Songs
headline: Denise LaSalle, Singer and Writer of Earthy Songs, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. LaSalle had a career that lasted almost half a century and reached the top of the R&B charts in 1971 with “Trapped by a Thing Called Love.”

name: Donnelly Rhodes
headline: Donnelly Rhodes, Prolific Character Actor, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Rhodes’s numerous roles included a dimwitted escaped convict on “Soap” and a brusque doctor on the reboot of “Battlestar Galactica.”

name: Fast Eddie Clarke
headline: Fast Eddie Clarke, Motörhead Guitarist, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Clarke was the last surviving member of the British rock band’s best-known lineup.

name: Carole Hart
profession: Producer and Writer of Childrens TV
headline: Carole Hart, Producer and Writer of Children’s TV, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Hart worked on the earliest episodes of “Sesame Street” and helped Marlo Thomas create the groundbreaking “Free to Be ... You and Me.”

name: Cy Young
profession: Only American to Win Gold in Javelin
headline: Cy Young, Only American to Win Gold in Javelin, Is Dead at 89
abstract: He did it in Helsinki in 1952 — a banner Olympic year for the United States — breaking a Finn’s record as well as Finland’s grip on the sport.

name: José Molina
profession: Brought Spanish Dance to U.S. Audiences
headline: José Molina, 81, Who Brought Spanish Dance to U.S. Audiences, Dies
abstract: Mr. Molina’s striking flamenco skills took him to stages all over America and made him a “Tonight Show” regular.

name: Edgar Ray Killen
profession: Convicted in 64 Killings of Rights Workers
headline: Edgar Ray Killen, Convicted in ’64 Killings of Rights Workers, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Killen, who died in prison, drew a 60-year sentence in 2005 after evading conviction 41 years earlier in the murders of three civil rights campaigners.

name: Kynaston McShine
headline: Kynaston McShine, Curator of Historic Art Exhibitions, Dies at 82
abstract: A West Indian in a largely white profession, he cut a dynamic figure in the art world, mounting memorable shows that disturbed the status quo.

name: Ronald Fieve
profession: Pioneered Lithium to Treat Mood Swings
headline: Dr. Ronald Fieve, 87, Dies; Pioneered Lithium to Treat Mood Swings
abstract: Dr. Fieve and a colleague identified lithium as the first naturally occurring medication to prevent and control a specific psychiatric disorder.

name: Thomas Luken
headline: Thomas Luken, Veteran Ohio Democrat, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Known for his confrontational style, Mr. Luken was a major force in Cincinnati for more than 30 years, as a prosecutor, the mayor and a member of Congress.

name: David Toschi
headline: David Toschi, 86, Detective Who Pursued the Zodiac Killer, Dies
abstract: A San Francisco police investigator, he worked on the case, which remains unsolved, for nine years — until he was removed in 1978 for “a foolish thing.”

name: John V. Tunney
headline: John V. Tunney, Boxer’s Son Who Lasted One Term in the Senate, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Tunney seemed to be a rising star in the Democratic Party until a Senate re-election loss sent him into early political exile because of turbulent times.

name: Keith Jackson
headline: Keith Jackson, Voice of College Football, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Jackson was synonymous with Saturday college football for millions of fans through five decades.

name: Doug Harvey
profession: Hall of Fame Umpire Players Called God
headline: Doug Harvey, Hall of Fame Umpire Players Called God, Dies at 87
abstract: Harvey was considered firm and fair during a 31-season career spent entirely in the National League. He worked five World Series and six All-Star Games.

name: Dolores O’Riordan
headline: Dolores O’Riordan, Lead Singer of the Cranberries, Dies at 46
abstract: Ms. O’Riordan’s voice, high and breathy but more determined than fragile, lent an unmistakable sound to songs like the hits “Linger” and “Zombie.”

name: Dan Gurney
headline: Dan Gurney, Driver and Builder of Racecars, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Gurney was the first driver to win races in all four of the major motor sports categories: Grand Prix, Indy car, Nascar and sports cars.

name: Edwin Hawkins
profession: Known for the Hit Oh Happy Day
headline: Edwin Hawkins, Known for the Hit ‘Oh Happy Day,’ Is Dead at 74
abstract: His catchy song of praise, recorded on a two-track machine and “never intended for commercial purposes,” became a Top 10 hit in 1970.

name: Mathilde Krim
profession: Mobilizing Force in an AIDS Crusade
headline: Mathilde Krim, Mobilizing Force in an AIDS Crusade, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Krim raised awareness of the scourge and money to fight it while lobbying governments and enlisting a broad spectrum of powerful allies.

name: Keorapetse Kgositsile
headline: Keorapetse Kgositsile, 79, South African Poet and Activist, Dies
abstract: He received acclaim while living in the United States; when he returned to South Africa after the fall of apartheid, he was welcomed as a hero.

name: Joseph Rice
headline: Joseph Rice, Bank Chief Who Fought Hostile Takeover, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Rice led the Irving Bank Corporation, which was acquired by Bank of New York after a corporate fight unusual for what had been a staid industry.

name: Jo Jo White
headline: Jo Jo White, Deadeye Shooter for Boston Celtics, Dies at 71
abstract: White played 10 seasons for the Celtics and helped lead the team to N.B.A. championships in 1974 and 1976.

name: Gualtiero Marchesi
headline: Gualtiero Marchesi, Renowned (and Feisty) Chef, Dies at 87
abstract: His Milan restaurant became the first in Italy to receive a Michelin guide’s three stars, but later, feeling slighted, he repudiated rating systems.

name: Hugh Wilson
headline: Hugh Wilson, Who Created ‘WKRP in Cincinnati,’ Dies at 74
abstract: In addition to writing TV comedies, Mr. Wilson directed films, including “Police Academy” and “The First Wives Club.”

name: Geoffrey Hazard
headline: Geoffrey Hazard, Influential Arbiter of Legal Ethics, Dies at 88
abstract: Professor Hazard, a scholar who taught a Supreme Court justice, was “one of the law’s wise men,” a former federal judge said.

name: Peter Mayle
profession: Wrote of A Year in Provence
headline: Peter Mayle, Who Wrote of ‘A Year in Provence,’ Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Mayle, an Englishman, spawned a genre in 1989 with his travel memoir about renovating a house in Southern France.

name: Terence Marsh
headline: Terence Marsh, Who Gave Memorable Films Their Look, Dies at 86
abstract: He won Oscars for his art direction of “Dr. Zhivago” and “Oliver!” and was production designer of films ranging from “Basic Instinct” to “Spaceballs.”

name: Paul Booth
headline: Paul Booth, Antiwar Organizer and Union Stalwart, Dies at 74
abstract: A chief architect of the 1965 march on Washington against the Vietnam War, he later became a key adviser to the nation’s largest public employee union.

name: William Bain Jr.
headline: William Bain Jr., 80, Business Consultant and Romney Mentor, Dies
abstract: He made Bain & Company, in Boston, a fierce competitor to some of the country’s leading firms. Mitt Romney was one of his most significant hires.

name: Stansfield Turner
headline: Stansfield Turner, C.I.A. Director Who Confronted Communism Under Carter, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Turner, who led the Central Intelligence Agency under President Jimmy Carter, started small covert actions that grew into some of the biggest battles of the Cold War.

name: Christine Beshar
headline: Christine Beshar, Trailblazing Lawyer, Dies at 88
abstract: She was one of the first female partners at a Wall Street law firm and, in another first, persuaded it to provide on-site emergency child-care.

name: Dorothy Malone
headline: Dorothy Malone Dies at 93; Star of TV’s ‘Peyton Place’
abstract: She won an Oscar for “Written on the Wind” but found her greatest fame on the small screen.

name: Joe Frank
headline: Joe Frank, Spinner of Strange Radio Tales, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Delivered in a measured baritone, Mr. Frank’s monologues trod the line between fact and fiction and brought listeners into unusual territory.

name: Julius Lester
headline: Julius Lester, Chronicler of Black America, Is Dead at 78
abstract: A captivating and often polarizing writer, Mr. Lester traveled through a labyrinth of religious and ethnic identities, including a conversion to Judaism.

name: Herbert Schmertz
headline: Herbert Schmertz, Innovative Public-Relations Man, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Schmertz promoted “advertorials” for Mobil Oil during the 1970s oil shortages and was instrumental in arranging its sponsorship of PBS programs.

name: Paul Bocuse
headline: Paul Bocuse, Celebrated French Chef, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Bocuse was a leading figure in the pathbreaking culinary movement known as nouvelle cuisine.

name: Harry Selby
headline: Harry Selby, Renowned Hunter and Safari Guide, Is Dead at 92
abstract: He shot his first antelope at 8, his first elephant at 14. Mr. Selby was a protégé of the East Africa hunter Philip Hope Percival, who took Theodore Roosevelt and Ernest Hemingway on safari.

name: Bradford Dillman
headline: Bradford Dillman, Star of Broadway and Hollywood, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Dillman had at least 140 film and television credits to his name, but he was best known for his roles in “Long Day’s Journey Into Night” and “Compulsion.”

name: Naomi Parker Fraley
headline: Naomi Parker Fraley, the Real Rosie the Riveter, Dies at 96
abstract: Mrs. Fraley’s connection to Rosie was made public in 2016, ending years of speculation over who was the model for the fictional 1940s war worker.

name: Valery Chalidze
headline: Valery Chalidze, Soviet Dissident Forced Into Exile, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Chalidze had campaigned for human rights alongside Andrei Sakharov when he was allowed to visit the United States and then barred from returning.

name: John Barton
headline: John Barton, Revelatory Shakespeare Director, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Barton was there at the founding of the Royal Shakespeare Company and directed numerous productions for it across 40 years.

name: Hugh Masekela
headline: Hugh Masekela, Trumpeter and Anti-Apartheid Activist, Dies at 78
abstract: The pioneer of South African jazz came to the forefront of the country’s music in the 1950s as a member of the Jazz Epistles, gaining international fame after moving to the United States in 1960.

name: Wyatt Tee Walker
profession: Dr. Kings Strategist and a Harlem Leader
headline: Wyatt Tee Walker, Dr. King’s Strategist and a Harlem Leader, Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Walker played a key role in civil rights protests that turned the tide against racial injustice in the Deep South.

name: Ursula K. Le Guin
headline: Ursula K. Le Guin, Acclaimed for Her Fantasy Fiction, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Ms. Le Guin brought literary elegance and a feminist sensibility to science fiction and fantasy tales, drawing millions of readers around the world.

name: Jack Whitten
headline: Jack Whitten, Artist of Wide-Ranging Curiosity, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Whitten began as an Abstract Expressionist but was always eager to explore other genres and ways of painting.

name: Nicanor Parra
profession: Chilean Voice in an Anti-Poet Movement
headline: Nicanor Parra, Chilean Voice in an ‘Anti-Poet’ Movement, Dies at 103
abstract: With everyday language, Mr. Parra and others defied high-flown poetic conventions with a directness that evoked the humor and absurdity of modern life.

name: Olivia Cole
headline: Olivia Cole, Award-Winning ‘Roots’ Actress, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Ms. Cole won an Emmy for her role in the acclaimed 1977 mini-series. She was also in “Backstairs at the White House” and “The Women of Brewster Place.”

name: Bernadine Morris
headline: Bernadine Morris, Veteran Observer of Fashion, Dies at 92
abstract: She uncovered the latest trends for more than five decades, including 32 years at The New York Times, where she became the chief fashion writer.

name: Mark E. Smith
headline: Mark E. Smith, Uncompromising Leader of the Fall, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Smith led the bristling and influential post-punk band for four decades with an intransigent voice and anarchically caustic lyrics.

name: Allison Shearmur
profession: Star Wars and Hunger Games Producer
headline: Allison Shearmur, 54, ‘Star Wars’ and ‘Hunger Games’ Producer, Dies
abstract: Ms. Shearmur helped bring to the screen a number of box-office hits as an executive for major studios, and later as an independent producer.

name: Warren Miller
headline: Warren Miller, Ski Bum Turned Filmmaker, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Skiing was a niche pursuit when he began filming it in the 1940s. His movies popularized the sport and helped create a multibillion-dollar industry.

name: Wendell Castle
profession: Blurred the Line Between Furniture and Art
headline: Wendell Castle, 85, Dies; Blurred the Line Between Furniture and Art
abstract: Trained as an industrial designer and sculptor, Mr. Castle fashioned whimsical furnishings from wood and metal. But his favorite tool was a pencil.

name: Elizabeth Hawley
headline: Elizabeth Hawley, Who Chronicled Everest Treks, Dies at 94
abstract: An American, Ms. Hawley spent decades grilling mountaineers and compiling records for climbing expeditions in Nepal.

name: Marlene VerPlanck
headline: Marlene VerPlanck, Singer of Jazz and Jingles, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. VerPlanck brought a clear and disciplined voice to the American songbook. But millions knew that voice best from commercials.

name: William McDonough
profession: Guided New York Fed Through Crises
headline: William McDonough, Who Guided New York Fed Through Crises, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. McDonough’s 10 years as the Federal Reserve Bank of New York’s president included guiding it through the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks and limiting the damage of a major hedge fund’s failure.

name: Mort Walker
profession: Creator of Beetle Bailey Comic Strip
headline: Mort Walker, Creator of ‘Beetle Bailey’ Comic Strip, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Walker, who created “Beetle Bailey” in 1950, had the longest tenure of any cartoonist on an original creation, according to the comic’s distributor.

name: Ingvar Kamprad
profession: Founder of Ikea and Creator of a Global Empire
headline: Ingvar Kamprad, Founder of Ikea and Creator of a Global Empire, Dies at 91
abstract: The Swedish entrepreneur practiced thrift and diligence, and he portrayed those traits as the basis for Ikea’s success.

name: Arno Motulsky
headline: Arno Motulsky, a Founder of Medical Genetics, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Motulsky narrowly escaped the Nazis as a teenager and went on to become what one scientist called “a maestro of human genetics.”

name: Robert Parry
headline: Robert Parry, Investigative Reporter in Washington, Dies at 68
abstract: His exposés for The Associated Press on the Iran-contra scandal earned him a Polk Award. He also worked for “Frontline” and started a journalism website.

name: Dennis Peron
headline: Dennis Peron, Early Medical Marijuana Advocate, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Peron campaigned to change the California laws that criminalized the possession of marijuana for medical use. He succeeded.

name: Bénédicte Pesle
profession: Introduced American Stage Artists to France
headline: Bénédicte Pesle Dies at 90; Introduced American Stage Artists to France
abstract: Ms. Pesle championed the choreographer Merce Cunningham, the experimental director Robert Wilson and many others, but the public rarely knew her name.

name: Connie Sawyer
headline: Connie Sawyer, Film’s Oldest Working Actress, Dies at 105
abstract: Ms. Sawyer performed in vaudeville and acted on stages and screens for more than eight decades. “Just keep me workin’,” she said.

name: Robert Pincus-Witten
headline: Robert Pincus-Witten, Art Critic and Historian, Is Dead at 82
abstract: His writing in Artforum and elsewhere helped make sense of the tempestuous 1960s and ’70s and gave art a new term, Post-Minimalism.

name: Oscar Gamble
headline: Oscar Gamble, Power Hitter With Prodigious Hair, Dies at 68
abstract: In addition to his home runs, he was known for his formidable Afro — until, that is, he was traded to George Steinbrenner’s Yankees.

name: Nicholas von Hoffman
headline: Nicholas von Hoffman, Provocative Journalist and Author, Dies at 88
abstract: In columns and books, Mr. von Hoffman examined American politics and culture from a left-wing perspective over five decades.

name: Haim Gouri
profession: Poetic Voice of a Rising Israel
headline: Haim Gouri, Poetic Voice of a Rising Israel, Is Dead at 94
abstract: A journalist and author as well, Mr. Gouri was called the last of Israel’s national poets and the conscience of the founding generation.

name: Andre Surmain
profession: Fed the Elite in Luxe Style at Lutèce
headline: Andre Surmain, Who Fed the Elite in Luxe Style at Lutèce, Dies at 97
abstract: His restaurant was one of the last bastions of grand dining in New York, an oasis of elegance defined by haute cuisine, high prices and a lofty clientele.

name: Pierre Godé
profession: Top Adviser to Frances Richest Man
headline: Pierre Godé, Top Adviser to France’s Richest Man, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Godé spent 30 years at the side of the LVMH chief, Bernard Arnault. His vision was instrumental in the creation of one of the world’s largest luxury groups.

name: Louis Zorich
profession: Familiar Actor on TV and Stage
headline: Louis Zorich, Familiar Actor on TV and Stage, Dies at 93
abstract: He was known for “Mad About You” and other shows. But his first love was the theater, where he often appeared alongside his wife, Olympia Dukakis.

name: Gene Sharp
headline: Gene Sharp, Global Guru of Nonviolent Resistance, Dies at 90
abstract: An apostle of peaceful protest, he inspired insurrections against dictators around the world and the “occupy” movement in the United States.

name: Arnold Gold
headline: Dr. Arnold Gold, 92, Dies; Made Compassionate Care a Cause
abstract: In a medical world ever more reliant on technology, Dr. Gold insisted on teaching, and rewarding, a human touch at the bedside.

name: Jon Huntsman Sr.
headline: Jon Huntsman Sr., Billionaire Businessman and Philanthropist, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Huntsman was an industrialist who made a fortune, gave millions to cancer research and left a legacy of public service.

name: Lin Bolen
headline: Lin Bolen, a Trailblazing TV Executive, Dies at 76
abstract: Rising to a vice presidency at NBC in the early 1970s, Ms. Bolen energized the network’s daytime lineup.

name: Melvyn Weiss
headline: Melvyn Weiss, Lawyer Who Fought Corporate Fraud, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Weiss used class-action suits to reap billions in settlements and legal safeguards for investors and consumers. Then the government prosecuted him.

name: Romana Acosta Bañuelos
headline: Romana Acosta Bañuelos, U.S. Treasurer Under Nixon, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Acosta Bañuelos, a Mexican-American who got her start running a tortilla business, was chosen at a time when the president was seeking more Latino voters.

name: Peter Colapietro
headline: Peter Colapietro, ‘Saloon Priest’ Who Ministered to Lowly and Mighty, Dies at 69
abstract: A longtime pastor of Holy Cross on 42nd Street in Manhattan who was also a beloved regular at Elaine’s.

name: John Mahoney
headline: John Mahoney, Actor Best Known for ‘Frasier,’ Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Mahoney was born in England, but he came to embody all-American grass-roots fatherhood on TV. He also appeared on Broadway and won a Tony Award.

name: Claribel Alegría
headline: Claribel Alegría, 93, Poet for Central America’s Voiceless, Dies
abstract: With roots in both Nicaragua and El Salvador, she wrote eloquently of sorrow and struggle.

name: Leon Chancler
headline: Leon (Ndugu) Chancler, Versatile Drummer, Is Dead at 65
abstract: Mr. Chancler played on hundreds of jazz, pop, funk, disco and country albums, including Michael Jackson’s “Thriller.”

name: Joseph Polchinski
headline: Joseph Polchinski, 63, Leading Theorist on Multiple Universes, Dies
abstract: He helped lay the mathematical foundation for the startling idea that our universe is not alone.

name: Victor Sidel
headline: Dr. Victor Sidel, Public Health Champion, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Dr. Sidel linked the health of populations to social and economic conditions and political choices, like putting nuclear arms ahead of medical care.

name: Isadore Rosenfeld
headline: Dr. Isadore Rosenfeld, High-Profile Cardiologist, Dies at 91
abstract: When not practicing on the Upper East Side, he wrote best-selling books, had his own television program and led a medical research advocacy group.

name: Mickey Jones
headline: Mickey Jones, Drummer Turned Character Actor, Is Dead at 76
abstract: In the 1960s, Mr. Jones toured with Bob Dylan. In the 1990s, he played a recurring role on the hit sitcom “Home Improvement.”

name: John Perry Barlow
headline: John Perry Barlow, 70, Dies; Championed an Unfettered Internet
abstract: In a multifaceted life, he fought for free expression on the web, wrote lyrics for the Grateful Dead, ran a ranch and was a Republican leader in Wyoming.

name: Lovebug Starski
headline: Lovebug Starski, Hip-Hop Trailblazer, Is Dead at 57
abstract: A versatile D.J. and rapper, in the 1970s he was a key figure in the development and evolution of a new kind of music in the South Bronx.

name: Arkady Wajspapir
headline: Arkady Wajspapir, 96, Is Dead; Escaped Death Camp in Uprising
abstract: Having endured the horrors of the Holocaust, he fled Sobibor, in Poland, in a mass insurrection after killing a Nazi officer with an ax.

name: Sonia Gechtoff
headline: Sonia Gechtoff, Acclaimed Abstract Expressionist, Dies at 91
abstract: With technique emphasizing the palette knife, Ms. Gechtoff came to prominence in the 1950s in a genre then dominated by men.

name: John Gavin
profession: Actor and Ambassador to Mexico Under Reagan
headline: John Gavin, Actor and Ambassador to Mexico Under Reagan, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Gavin played romantic leads in the 1950s and 1960s and served in Mexico City for a rocky five-year tenure.

name: Reg E. Cathey
profession: Actor on House of Cards and The Wire
headline: Reg E. Cathey, Actor on ‘House of Cards’ and ‘The Wire,’ Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Cathey won an Emmy for his portrayal of a barbecue pit owner and confidant to Francis Underwood on “House of Cards.” He also played a political operative on “The Wire.”

name: Wesla Whitfield
headline: Wesla Whitfield, Singer Who Reinvigorated Standards, Dies at 70
abstract: Unmoved by opera, Ms. Whitfield chose to apply her classical training to songs by Cole Porter, Irving Berlin, Rodgers and Hart, and many others.

name: Asma Jahangir
headline: Asma Jahangir, Fearless Pakistani Rights Activist, Dies at 66
abstract: She gained international acclaim as the voice of conscience in a country where liberal, secular voices have been under threat.

name: Frederieke Taylor
headline: Frederieke Taylor, Gallery Owner With Eclectic Taste, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Taylor’s gallery, founded in 1993, was known for exploring the intersection between art and architecture.

name: Wally Moon
profession: Homers Helped the Dodgers Win a World Series
headline: Wally Moon, Whose Homers Helped the Dodgers Win a World Series, Dies at 87
abstract: The National League rookie of the year in 1954, he became known for his “moon shot” home runs in the Dodgers’ second season in Los Angeles.

name: Vic Damone
profession: Crooned His Way to Postwar Popularity
headline: Vic Damone, Who Crooned His Way to Postwar Popularity, Dies at 89
abstract: In an era dominated by Sinatra, Como and Bennett, Mr. Damone built his own following on records and television and in nightclubs.

name: Jan Maxwell
headline: Jan Maxwell, Celebrated Stage Actress, Is Dead at 61
abstract: Ms. Maxwell, a longtime favorite of critics, earned five Tony Award nominations in seven years, including two in one season.

name: Johann Johannsson
headline: Johann Johannsson, Award-Winning Movie Composer, Dies at 48
abstract: With an indie-rock past, he blended elements of electronic and classical music in his scores for “The Theory of Everything,” “Sicario” and “Arrival.”

name: Marty Allen
headline: Marty Allen, Wild-Eyed Comedy Star, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Teamed with the singer Steve Rossi, Mr. Allen — with his signature “Hello dere!” — brought a childlike mix of innocence and insanity to TV and top nightclubs.

name: Ben Agajanian
headline: Ben Agajanian, Square-Shoed Kicking Star, Dies at 98
abstract: Though missing four toes because of an accident, he was pro football’s first career kicking specialist, playing for nine teams until he was 45.

name: Anne Treisman
headline: Anne Treisman, Who Studied How We Perceive, Dies at 82
abstract: Her theories on how the brain sorts the avalanche of sensory input it receives to focus on a particular thing have been foundational in the field.

name: Donald Lynden-Bell
headline: Donald Lynden-Bell, Quasar and Black Hole Expert, Dies at 82
abstract: An astrophysicist, he joined six colleagues in suggesting that the universe is expanding sideways, and not evenly, challenging conventional theories.

name: Sam Bloch
headline: Sam Bloch, Champion of Holocaust Survivors, Is Dead at 93
abstract: A longtime executive of the World Zionist Organization, Mr. Bloch organized numerous gatherings that offered mass witness to the horrors of Nazism.

name: Ruth Ann Koesun
headline: Ruth Ann Koesun, Versatile Ballet Theater Dancer, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Koesun epitomized the company’s early eclectic profile as a lyrical Romantic ballerina who could also surprise with dramatic ferocity.

name: Morgan Tsvangirai
profession: Longtime Foe of Mugabe in Zimbabwe
headline: Morgan Tsvangirai, Longtime Foe of Mugabe in Zimbabwe, Dies at 65
abstract: A former labor leader and prime minister, he seemed on the cusp of defeating Mr. Mugabe in 2008, only to be subjected to bloody intimidation.

name: Tom Rapp
headline: Tom Rapp, the Voice of Pearls Before Swine, Is Dead at 70
abstract: His band became a favorite in the underground-music scene of the 1960s and early ’70s. Then came a career as a civil rights lawyer.

name: Kenneth Haigh
profession: Angry Young Man of British Stage
headline: Kenneth Haigh, 86, ‘Angry Young Man’ of British Stage, Dies
abstract: A coal miner’s son, he had a long theater, film and TV career, but he was best known as the rebellious antihero in John Osborne’s “Look Back in Anger.”

name: Ruud Lubbers
headline: Ruud Lubbers, Former Dutch Prime Minister, Is Dead at 78
abstract: As his country’s longest-serving leader, he helped revive the economy and pave the way for the European Union. But his later career was marred by scandal.

name: Patricia Frustaci
headline: Patricia Frustaci, 63, Dies; Septuplets Put Her in Spotlight
abstract: Her multiple births set a record in 1985, and they led to a medical ordeal, early deaths, a lawsuit and a flood of media attention.

name: André Harvey
headline: André Harvey, Sculptor of the Natural World, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Mr. Harvey was renowned for his intricately detailed, realistic bronze representations of pigs, frogs, turtles and even the occasional human.

name: Lerone Bennett Jr.
headline: Lerone Bennett Jr., Historian of Black America, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Bennett, the author of “Before the Mayflower” and other books, was also a top editor at Ebony magazine for decades.

name: Jim Bridwell
headline: Jim Bridwell, Mountaineering Maverick, Is Dead at 73
abstract: With a go-for-broke style, Mr. Bridwell conquered countless peaks, many in Yosemite, where he led the 1970s climbers known as the Stonemasters.

name: Günter Blobel
headline: Günter Blobel, Nobel Laureate Who Found Cell ‘ZIP Codes,’ Dies at 81
abstract: Dr. Blobel, at Rockefeller University, discovered that proteins in any given cell carry signals that guide them to where they can do their beneficial job.

name: Lydia Ratcliff
headline: Lydia Ratcliff, Writer Who Found a Farmer’s Calling, Dies at 84
abstract: She gave up ghostwriting for the financial columnist Sylvia Porter to help pioneer the farm-to-table movement, delivering her meats to top restaurants.

name: David Poindexter
profession: Used Media to Preach Family Planning
headline: David Poindexter, 89, Who Used Media to Preach Family Planning, Dies
abstract: A Methodist minister, he saw TV and radio programming — soap operas, in particular — as effective tools to teach the world about population control.

name: Jeffrey Bell
headline: Jeffrey Bell, G.O.P. Giant-Killer and Supply-Sider, Dies at 74
abstract: He upset Senator Clifford P. Case in New Jersey’s 1978 Republican primary, lost to Bill Bradley, but became an effective advocate of tax cuts.

name: Billy Graham
profession: Pastor Filled Stadiums and Counseled Presidents
headline: Billy Graham, 99, Dies; Pastor Filled Stadiums and Counseled Presidents
abstract: Mr. Graham spread the Gospel around the world through a combination of religious conviction, commanding stage presence and shrewd use of advanced communication technologies.

name: Nini Theilade
headline: Nini Theilade, Dancer in Reinhardt’s ‘Dream,’ Dies at 102
abstract: She later performed with the Ballet Russe de Monte Carlo, and was also well known as a dance teacher.

name: Catherine Wolf
profession: Studied How People and Computers Interact
headline: Catherine Wolf, 70, Dies; Studied How People and Computers Interact
abstract: A leader in IBM’s development of a speech-recognition system, she relied on her laptop to communicate after Lou Gehrig’s disease left her paralyzed.

name: David Zwick
headline: David Zwick, a Leading Clean-Water Advocate, Dies at 75
abstract: His work as one of “Nader’s raiders” helped bring about the Clean Water Act of 1972, and he helped found the advocacy group Clean Water Action.

name: Peggy Cooper Cafritz
headline: Peggy Cooper Cafritz, Patron of Black Artists, Dies at 70
abstract: Also a civil rights activist and educator, she championed African and African-American art, building a collection and then rebuilding it after a fire.

name: Idrissa Ouedraogo
headline: Idrissa Ouedraogo, Lauded African Filmmaker, Dies at 64
abstract: His movies, featuring simple, compelling stories set in Burkina Faso, his home country, and elsewhere in Africa, won accolades at Cannes.

name: Nanette Fabray
profession: Star of TV and Stage Comedies
headline: Nanette Fabray, Star of TV and Stage Comedies, Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Fabray won a Tony for a performance on Broadway in the 1940s and three Emmys for her work with Sid Caesar in the 1950s.

name: Rick McKay
headline: Rick McKay, Who Documented Memories of Broadway, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. McKay filmed the reminiscences of dozens of theater luminaries for the 2004 documentary “Broadway: The Golden Age, by the Legends Who Were There.”

name: Lee Harris Pomeroy
headline: Lee Harris Pomeroy, 85, Dies; Architect Revived Subway Stations
abstract: With a passion for historic preservation, Mr. Pomeroy saw restoring a century-old railroad building as “a significant gesture of respect to the Bronx.”

name: Sridevi Kapoor
headline: Sridevi Kapoor, Bollywood’s First Female Superstar, Dies at 54
abstract: Sridevi, a veteran of some 300 films in five languages, was one of the only Bollywood actresses to headline box-office hits without a man beside her in a leading role.

name: George S. Kaufman
headline: George S. Kaufman, Who Revived Astoria Studios, Dies at 89
abstract: A third-generation real estate owner and manager, he was instrumental in a public-private partnership in Queens that spurred filmmaking in New York.

name: Eido Shimano
headline: Eido Shimano, Buddhist Leader Who Resigned in Scandal, Dies at 85
abstract: He led a New York group and built a monastery in the Catskills, but for years rumors circulated that he was having sex with his female followers.

name: Lewis Gilbert
headline: Lewis Gilbert, Director of ‘Alfie’ and 007 Movies, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Best known for his work with Michael Caine and Sean Connery, Mr. Gilbert also made action films (“Sink the Bismarck!”) and quieter ones (“Educating Rita”).

name: Jack Hamilton
headline: Jack Hamilton, Who Hurled a Fateful Pitch, Dies at 79
abstract: A fastball that struck the Red Sox All-Star Tony Conigliaro in 1967 was so damaging that it shortened a potential Hall of Fame career and haunted the man who threw it.

name: Cynthia Heimel
headline: Cynthia Heimel, Irreverent Writer About Sex, Dies at 70
abstract: In newspaper and magazine advice columns, many collected in books, Ms. Heimel was blunt and breezy about men, women, feminism, lingerie and much else.

name: Arthur J. Moss
headline: Arthur J. Moss, Who Pioneered Heart Treatments, Dies at 86
abstract: He successfully conducted research into fatal cardiac disorders, including a rare genetic malfunction called long QT syndrome.

name: Quini
headline: Quini, Soccer Player Who Was Celebrated and Kidnapped, Dies at 68
abstract: Quini, a prolific goal scorer for two Spanish clubs, was seized at gunpoint after a match in 1981, unsettling an entire nation.

name: Raymond Danowski
headline: Raymond Danowski, Stockpiler of Poetry, Is Dead at 74
abstract: A son of the Bronx amassed 75,000 books, believed to be the largest private library of 20th-century poetry in English. He gave it all to Emory University.

name: Sean Lavery
profession: Ballet Star in a Shortened Career
headline: Sean Lavery, Ballet Star in a Shortened Career, Dies at 61
abstract: He was one of New York City Ballet’s main dancers until a spinal tumor sidelined him.

name: Luciano Menéndez
profession: Army Chief in Brutal Argentine Era
headline: Luciano Menéndez, Army Chief in Brutal Argentine Era, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Menéndez, who received 14 life sentences, was implicated in homicides, torture, kidnapping and forced disappearances. He was unrepentant to the end.

name: Boyd Jarvis
headline: Boyd Jarvis, Whose Synthesizer Fueled Dance Music, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Jarvis played a synthesizer alongside dance music DJs in New York in the early 1980s, building a sound that anticipated house music.

name: Barry Crimmins
profession: Comic and Warrior Against Sex Abuse
headline: Barry Crimmins, Comic and Warrior Against Sex Abuse, Dies at 64
abstract: A caustic cornerstone of Boston’s comedy scene, Mr. Crimmins became a crusader against online child pornographers early in the internet age.

name: Richard E. Taylor
headline: Richard E. Taylor, Nobel Winner Who Plumbed Matter, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Dr. Taylor, of Stanford, shared the 1990 physics prize for the discovery of quarks, one of the fundamental particles in the universe.

name: William Borders
headline: William Borders, Former Times Reporter and Editor, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Borders covered Nigeria, Canada, India and Britain before taking senior editing positions at the newspaper in a 46-year career there.

name: Richard Weinstein
headline: Richard Weinstein, Public-Minded Urban Planner, Dies at 85
abstract: Seeking more livable cities, he sought to preserve neighborhoods’ historic character, leaving his mark on New York and Los Angeles.

name: Penny Vincenzi
headline: Penny Vincenzi, Best-Selling British Author, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Her novels, with many pages and many characters, featured strong women and plots full of glamour, romance and family secrets.

name: Harvey Schmidt
headline: Harvey Schmidt, Co-Creator of ‘The Fantasticks,’ Is Dead at 88
abstract: He wrote the music. A former college friend, Tom Jones, wrote the words. What resulted was the world’s longest-running musical (and a lasting partnership).

name: Charles Wilson
headline: Charles Wilson, Top Brain Surgeon and Researcher, Dies at 88
abstract: Dr. Wilson was a deft, busy neurosurgeon in San Francisco but still found time to establish a leading center for the study of tumors.

name: Barbara Lekberg
headline: Barbara Lekberg, Artist With a Blowtorch, Dies at 92
abstract: Her welded-metal sculptures were known for their grace and sense of motion.

name: Roger Bannister
profession: First Athlete to Break the 4-Minute Mile
headline: Roger Bannister, First Athlete to Break the 4-Minute Mile, Dies at 88
abstract: The Briton ran a mile in 3:59.4, becoming the first man ever to do so, breaking through a mystical barrier and creating a seminal moment in sports history.

name: David Ogden Stiers
headline: David Ogden Stiers, Major Winchester on ‘M*A*S*H,’ Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Stiers appeared on stage in New York in the 1970s, had roles in four Woody Allen movies, and voiced characters in two dozen Disney animated films.

name: Sonja Bata
profession: Museum of Shoes Tells a Story
headline: Sonja Bata, Whose Museum of Shoes Tells a Story, Dies at 91
abstract: The Bata Shoe Museum, which she founded in Toronto, contains thousands of items spanning 4,500 years of footwear history.

name: Russ Solomon
headline: Russ Solomon, Founder of Tower Records, Dies at 92
abstract: A pioneer of superstore hangouts for music lovers, he built a global retail empire that became obsolete and finally went bankrupt.

name: Barbara Alston
headline: Barbara Alston, Who Sang With the Crystals, Dies at 74
abstract: Ms. Alston was just a teenager when she and four high school friends formed a vocal group that released a string of hits produced by Phil Spector.

name: Alan Gershwin
headline: Alan Gershwin, Who Claimed a Famous Father, Is Dead at 91
abstract: For decades he insisted that he was the illegitimate (and look-alike) son of George Gershwin, and despite the skeptics, he made a career out of that claim.

name: Sammy Stewart
headline: Sammy Stewart, Pitcher Whose Life Took a Downturn, Dies at 63
abstract: His career got off to a stellar start and he became an effective, hard-working reliever. But he later descended into drug abuse and homelessness.

name: Anatoly Lein
headline: Anatoly Lein, an Émigré Chess Grandmaster, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Lein was a star in the Soviet Union before leaving for the United States, where he remained a top competitor.

name: Trevor Baylis
profession: Inventor of a Radio Powered by Muscle
headline: Trevor Baylis, Inventor of a Radio Powered by Muscle, Dies at 80
abstract: His signature creation was inspired by an interest in making sure information about AIDS could reach parts of Africa without electricity.

name: Kalman Aron
profession: Art Spared Him in the Holocaust
headline: Kalman Aron, Whose Art Spared Him in the Holocaust, Dies at 93
abstract: A former child prodigy and a future painter, Mr. Aron, as a teenager, survived seven Nazi camps on scraps of food from guards whose portraits he drew.

name: Jesús López-Cobos
headline: Jesús López-Cobos, Internationally Known Conductor, Dies at 78
abstract: He led the Cincinnati Symphony Orchestra, among others, and was known for both orchestral works and opera.

name: Lillias Campbell Davidson
headline: Overlooked No More: Lillias Campbell Davidson, an Early Advocate for Women’s Cycling
abstract: Davidson encouraged women to bicycle at a time when they were told they were “by nature physically unfit.”

name: Charlotte Brontë
headline: Overlooked No More: Charlotte Brontë, Novelist Known for ‘Jane Eyre’
abstract: She was fearless — so fearless that she paid to have a volume of poems by her and her younger sisters published under pseudonyms, an unusually ambitious act for a woman of her era.

name: Belkis Ayón
profession: Cuban Printmaker Inspired by a Secret Male Society
headline: Overlooked No More: Belkis Ayón, a Cuban Printmaker Inspired by a Secret Male Society
abstract: She worked by applying materials to a printing plate rather than carving into its surface, in a palette of grays, to express the disquiet within.

name: Emily Warren Roebling
headline: Emily Warren Roebling, the Woman Behind the Man Who Built the Brooklyn Bridge
abstract: She was not an engineer. But she was instrumental to the construction of the great engineering feat.

name: Madhubala
headline: Madhubala, a Bollywood Legend Whose Tragic Life Mirrored Marilyn Monroe’s
abstract: In her 36 years, Madhubala starred in more than 70 movies, often portraying modern young women testing the limits of traditions.

name: Diane Arbus
headline: Diane Arbus Called Her Portraits ‘A Secret About a Secret’
abstract: A daughter of privilege, she photographed those on the outside, and her work has been hailed as brave and reviled as freakish.

name: Qiu Jin
headline: Qiu Jin, Beheaded by Imperial Forces, Was ‘China’s Joan of Arc’
abstract: She unbound her feet, wrote poetry and fought against the government, believing that women’s rights and political revolution naturally went hand in hand.

name: Ida B. Wells
profession: Took on Racism in the Deep South With Powerful Reporting on Lynchings
headline: Ida B. Wells, Who Took on Racism in the Deep South With Powerful Reporting on Lynchings
abstract: Wells is considered by historians to have been the most famous black woman in the United States during her lifetime, even as she was dogged by prejudice.

name: Margaret Abbott
headline: Margaret Abbott, an Unwitting Olympic Trailblazer
abstract: She was the first American woman to win the equivalent of Olympic gold, but at a time when the Games were scattershot, her achievement was not recognized.

name: Ada Lovelace
headline: Ada Lovelace, Mathematician Who Wrote the First Computer Program
abstract: Lovelace thought of math and logic as creative and imaginative, and her writings about computing in the mid-1800s earned her recognition as the first computer programmer.

name: Nella Larsen
headline: Nella Larsen Wrestled With Race and Sexuality in the Harlem Renaissance
abstract: The writer’s novels were celebrated and helped her become the first African-American woman to receive a Guggenheim Fellowship. Then she disappeared.

name: Henrietta Lacks
profession: Cells Led to a Medical Revolution
headline: Henrietta Lacks, Whose Cells Led to a Medical Revolution
abstract: Lacks, a former tobacco farmer, died of cancer at 31, but her endlessly renewable cancer cells have been at the core of advances in treatment for many ailments.

name: Sylvia Plath
profession: Postwar Poet Unafraid to Confront Her Own Despair
headline: Sylvia Plath, a Postwar Poet Unafraid to Confront Her Own Despair
abstract: As she grappled with the rejection of editors and her husband, Plath spent her last months writing the poems that would secure her literary reputation.

name: Marsha P. Johnson
headline: Marsha P. Johnson, a Transgender Pioneer and Activist
abstract: Johnson was part of the Stonewall uprising, helped transgender youths and was an AIDS activist. She died at 46 under murky circumstances.

name: Mary Ewing Outerbridge
profession: Helped Bring Tennis to the United States
headline: Mary Ewing Outerbridge, Who Helped Bring Tennis to the United States
abstract: Outerbridge set up a tennis court in Staten Island in the 1870s. It may have been the first in America.

name: Nitin Vadukul
headline: Nitin Vadukul, Innovative Photographer of Hip-Hop, Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. Vadukul departed from depicting rappers as street toughs, taking a cinematically surreal approach with subjects like Eminem and Dr. Dre.

name: Shammi
profession: Bollywood Actress Known for Comedic Roles
headline: Shammi, Bollywood Actress Known for Comedic Roles, Dies at 89
abstract: In some 200 films and several popular sitcoms, she played doting sisters, mothers and grandmothers.

name: Helmut Maucher
headline: Helmut Maucher, Executive Who Transformed Nestlé, Dies at 90
abstract: A German, Mr. Maucher rose from a milk production job to chief executive, then expanded Nestle’s global reach while cutting its work force.

name: Paul Magriel
profession: Was Called the Best in Backgammon
headline: Paul Magriel, Who Was Called the Best in Backgammon, Dies at 71
abstract: A onetime chess prodigy became “probably the best backgammon player in the world,” one newspaper said. With a gambler’s passion, he then switched to poker.

name: Hayden White
headline: Hayden White, Who Explored How History Is Made, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. White’s ideas about how we shape the past have been fueling discussion in history and other fields for half a century.

name: Ursula Marvin
headline: Ursula Marvin, Geologist of the Extraterrestrial, Dies at 96
abstract: Dr. Marvin, who had an asteroid and a mountain named after her, analyzed a chunk of a Soviet satellite and moon rocks retrieved by Apollo astronauts.

name: Reynaldo Bignone
headline: Reynaldo Bignone, Argentina’s Last Military Dictator, Dies at 90
abstract: At his death Mr. Bignone was under house arrest, having been found guilty of crimes against humanity in multiple trials.

name: William Pulte
headline: William Pulte, Pathbreaking Home Builder, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Pulte was part of a postwar generation of builders who turned a mom-and-pop industry into a giant one traded on the New York Stock Exchange.

name: Charles Campion
headline: Charles Campion, Campaign Adviser to Democrats, Dies at 62
abstract: Known as Chuck, he was sought out by the presidential campaigns of Walter Mondale, Michael Dukakis, Al Gore, John Kerry and Hillary Clinton.

name: Lucie Brock-Broido
headline: Lucie Brock-Broido, Inventive Poet, Is Dead at 61
abstract: Ms. Brock-Broido called her work “feral” and said she wrote poetry “because I felt I couldn’t live properly in the real world.”

name: Hubert de Givenchy
headline: Hubert de Givenchy Dies at 91; Fashion Pillar of Romantic Elegance
abstract: Over more than 40 years, Mr. Givenchy dressed the likes of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, Grace Kelly and memorably Audrey Hepburn in “Breakfast at Tiffany’s.”

name: Oskar Gröning
headline: Oskar Gröning, the ‘Bookkeeper of Auschwitz,’ Is Dead at 96
abstract: A former member of Hitler’s Waffen SS, he was among the last Germans to face war-crime charges arising from the Holocaust.

name: John Buchanan
profession: Once a Deep South Centrist in Congress
headline: John Buchanan, Once a Deep South Centrist in Congress, Dies at 89
abstract: He was one of the first Republicans elected to Congress from Alabama in the 20th century, but he became too progressive for his constituents.

name: Ethel Stein
headline: Ethel Stein, Who Created Intricate Textile Art, Dies at 100
abstract: Ms. Stein studied historical weaving techniques, sometimes with a microscope, to create her art. She also had a noteworthy sock-puppet sideline.

name: Sala Kirschner
profession: Trove of Letters Told of the Holocaust
headline: Sala Kirschner, 94, Whose Trove of Letters Told of the Holocaust, Dies
abstract: For 50 years, she kept secret a cache of letters she had squirreled away from Nazi guards. The collection later inspired a book and a play.

name: Togo West Jr.
profession: Army Secretary in Time of Transition
headline: Togo West Jr., 75, Dies; Army Secretary in Time of Transition
abstract: He worked to grant women in the Army more combat roles and shield them from sexual abuse. He later ran the Department of Veterans Affairs.

name: Craig Mack
headline: Craig Mack, ‘Flava in Ya Ear’ Rapper, Is Dead at 47
abstract: Mr. Mack’s biggest hit was one of the most important rap songs of the 1990s and helped build the foundation for Sean Combs’s Bad Boy Records.

name: Stephen Hawking
headline: Stephen Hawking Dies at 76; His Mind Roamed the Cosmos
abstract: A physicist and best-selling author, Dr. Hawking did not allow his physical limitations to hinder his quest to answer “the big question: Where did the universe come from?”

name: T. Berry Brazelton
headline: Dr. T. Berry Brazelton, Who Explored Babies’ Mental Growth, Dies at 99
abstract: In hospitals, clinics and books, he revolutionized our understanding of how children develop psychologically.

name: Lefty Kreh
headline: Lefty Kreh, a Fly Fisherman With Few Peers, Is Dead at 93
abstract: A pre-eminent sport fisherman, he circled the world teaching, writing, speaking and appearing on TV — when he wasn’t reeling in his quarry.

name: Alison Hargreaves
profession: Conquered Everest Solo and Without Bottled Oxygen
headline: Overlooked No More: Alison Hargreaves, Who Conquered Everest Solo and Without Bottled Oxygen
abstract: Hargreaves sent her children a message from the apex: “I am on the highest point of the world, and I love you dearly.” She perished months later while descending Earth’s second-highest peak, K2.

name: Joaquin Avila
headline: Joaquin Avila, Advocate of Hispanic Voting Rights, Dies at 69
abstract: The son of immigrants, he challenged discriminatory laws and practices as president of the Mexican American Legal Defense and Educational Fund.

name: Michael Getler
profession: Journalist Turned Watchdog of the Press
headline: Michael Getler, Journalist Turned Watchdog of the Press, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Getler was a former reporter and high-ranking editor who became the first internal monitor of an American TV network when he joined PBS in 2005.

name: John E. Sulston
profession: Found Clues to Genes in a Worm
headline: John E. Sulston, 75, Dies; Found Clues to Genes in a Worm
abstract: After putting a roundworm under a microscope, Dr. Sulston shared a Nobel Prize in 2002 for discoveries on how organisms develop.

name: Ed Charles
profession: Infield Sage of the Miracle Mets
headline: Ed Charles, Infield Sage of the Miracle Mets, Is Dead at 84
abstract: He was the clubhouse wise man for a team of upstarts who surprised the baseball world with a championship in 1969.

name: Tom Benson
headline: Tom Benson, Tycoon Who Danced With His Saints, Dies at 90
abstract: A colorful self-made billionaire, Mr. Benson was alternately revered and reviled in New Orleans, where he also owned the N.B.A.’s Pelicans.

name: Louise Slaughter
headline: Louise Slaughter, 88, Liberal Congresswoman in 16th Term, Is Dead
abstract: A House member from upstate New York, Ms. Slaughter championed women’s rights, food safety and the Affordable Care Act.

name: Gary Burden
headline: Gary Burden, Designer of Famous Album Covers, Dies at 84
abstract: His work on records by Joni Mitchell, the Doors, Neil Young and numerous others provided visual reference points for music that defined an era.

name: Mordechai Hager
headline: Rabbi Mordechai Hager, Leader of Large Hasidic Sect, Dies at 95
abstract: He settled many of his followers in an upstate New York enclave to escape the decadence and temptations of the city.

name: Anthony Acevedo
headline: Anthony Acevedo, Who Documented His Holocaust Ordeal, Dies at 93
abstract: Imprisoned in a slave labor camp, he kept a diary that alternated accounts of Nazi atrocities with quotidian observations and biting humor.

name: Wilson Harris
headline: Wilson Harris, Guyanese Writer of Intricate Novels, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Harris used his experience as a surveyor in unexplored areas of his native country to fashion dense stories full of history, metaphor and myth.

name: Kate Wilhelm
headline: Kate Wilhelm, Prolific Science Fiction Writer, Dies at 89
abstract: She wrote some 50 works of imaginative fiction, with plots one admirer called “haunting, hypnotic, incommensurable and strange.” She also wrote mysteries.

name: Emily Nasrallah
headline: Emily Nasrallah, Lebanese Novelist and Activist, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Nasrallah defied a civil war to remain in Beirut, where she campaigned for women’s rights and illuminated the vacuum left by immigration to other countries.

name: David Wyman
headline: David Wyman, Scholar of America’s Holocaust Response, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Wyman’s 1984 book, “The Abandonment of the Jews,” minced no words in concluding that the United States had failed to do its humanitarian duty.

name: Nokie Edwards
headline: Nokie Edwards, Whose Guitar Drove the Ventures, Dies at Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Edwards’s “twangy tone, wang-bar glides and staccato riffing,” one admirer wrote, “paved the way for the California surf bands of the 1960s.”

name: Adrián Lamo
headline: Adrián Lamo, Hacker Who Reported Chelsea Manning to the F.B.I., Dies at 37
abstract: Mr. Lamo, who was also known for hacking into the computer network of The New York Times, was reviled and revered for turning in Ms. Manning to the authorities.

name: Keith O’Brien
headline: Keith O’Brien, Cardinal Ousted in Sex Scandal, Dies at 80
abstract: Cardinal O’Brien was removed from office after acknowledging that he had engaged in the sort of homosexual behavior that he had earlier denounced.

name: Robert Grossman
headline: Robert Grossman, Illustrator With a Brash Touch, Dies at 78
abstract: On hundreds of magazine covers and in newspaper pages, Mr. Grossman caricatured all manner of politicians and made puns on their names.

name: Larry Kwong
profession: N.H.L.s First Player of Asian Descent
headline: Larry Kwong, 94, Dies; N.H.L.’s First Player of Asian Descent
abstract: Known as the China Clipper, he played only one shift of one game for the Rangers in 1948. But that was enough to earn him a place in hockey history.

name: Matt Dike
headline: Matt Dike, Hit-Making Founder of Hip-Hop Label, Dies at 56
abstract: His label, Delicious Vinyl, released crossover hits by Tone-Loc and Young M.C., and he helped the Beastie Boys make the groundbreaking “Paul’s Boutique.”

name: Peter G. Peterson
profession: Power From Wall St. to Washington
headline: Peter G. Peterson, a Power From Wall St. to Washington, Dies at 91
abstract: Captain of business, financier, philanthropist and public-policy watchdog, Mr. Peterson rose from humble Nebraska roots to be a force in American life.

name: Francis Bator
headline: Francis Bator, Influential White House Economist, Dies at 92
abstract: His proposals found their way into Lyndon B. Johnson’s overtures to the Soviet Union, his collaboration with Western Europe and his War on Poverty.

name: Katherine Westphal
headline: Katherine Westphal, Creator of Unusual Textile Art, Dies at 99
abstract: Ms. Westphal devoted her life to, in her words, “the patterning of cloth on any surface available” — including quilts, kimonos, dresses and baskets.

name: Les Payne
headline: Les Payne, Journalist Who Exposed Racial Injustice, Dies at 76
abstract: A Pulitzer Prize-winning reporter, a passionate columnist and a mentoring editor at Newsday, he was a pioneer for fellow blacks in the profession.

name: Barbara Wersba
profession: Wrote Candid Books for Young Adults
headline: Barbara Wersba, 85, Dies; Wrote Candid Books for Young Adults
abstract: Her books left more sanitized subjects behind and were among the first to explore topics like alcoholism and same-sex relationships.

name: Lisa Garcia Quiroz
headline: Lisa Garcia Quiroz, Magazine Publisher, Is Dead at 57
abstract: At Time Inc., Ms. Quiroz launched People en Español and Time for Kids and spearheaded the company’s diversity and arts philanthropy initiatives.

name: Millie Veasey
profession: Part of Trailblazing Unit in WWII
headline: Millie Veasey, Part of Trailblazing Unit in WWII, Dies at 100
abstract: She served in an all-black, all-women’s battalion tasked with untangling a mail-delivery nightmare, and later led the Raleigh chapter of the N.A.A.C.P.

name: Ruth Wakefield
headline: Overlooked No More: Ruth Wakefield, Who Invented the Chocolate Chip Cookie
abstract: Legend has it that Wakefield was trying a variation on a butterscotch dessert when she decided to let the chocolate chips fall where they may.

name: Julie Yip-Williams
profession: Writer of Candid Blog on Cancer
headline: Julie Yip-Williams, Writer of Candid Blog on Cancer, Dies at 42
abstract: More than chronicling her colon cancer, she wrote about hope, love and family and recalled being born blind in Vietnam and her family’s escape in a boat.

name: Sammy Williams
profession: Tony Winner in A Chorus Line
headline: Sammy Williams, Tony Winner in ‘A Chorus Line,’ Dies at 69
abstract: As a tormented young gay man aspiring to be a Broadway dancer, he delivered a wrenching monologue. But his career soon took a downturn.

name: Charles P. Lazarus
headline: Charles P. Lazarus, Toys ‘R’ Us Founder, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Lazarus parlayed a single store in Washington, D.C., into the world’s leading toy chain, but the company liquidated last week, burdened by debt.

name: Hazel Smith
headline: Hazel Smith, 83, Matriarch of Country Music, Is Dead
abstract: A freewheeling songwriter, journalist, confidante and more, she was credited with coining the phrase “outlaw country” to describe a raw new sound.

name: Robert S. Rubin
headline: Robert S. Rubin, Banker Who Defended Brooklyn Museum, Dies at 86
abstract: As chairman of the Brooklyn Museum, he refused to capitulate when Mayor Giuliani tried to censor an exhibit he considered scandalous.

name: Phan Van Khai
profession: First Vietnamese Prime Minister to Visit Washington
headline: Phan Van Khai, First Vietnamese Prime Minister to Visit Washington, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Khai pushed for strengthened economic and security ties with the United States.

name: H. Wayne Huizenga
profession: Owner of Teams and a Business Empire
headline: H. Wayne Huizenga, Owner of Teams and a Business Empire, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Huizenga built a business empire with the Blockbuster and AutoNation chains and owned three South Florida teams, the Marlins, Dolphins and Panthers.

name: Zell Miller
headline: Zell Miller, Feisty Democrat Who Sided With G.O.P., Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Miller rose to governor of Georgia, then filled a Senate seat, where he showed his independence with a tart convention speech backing George W. Bush.

name: Eli Leon
headline: Eli Leon, 82, Dies; Champion of African-American Quilt Makers
abstract: A collector and self-taught scholar, Mr. Leon was best known for his devotion to the work of the artist Rosie Lee Tompkins.

name: Oleg Tabakov
headline: Oleg Tabakov, Revered Russian Actor and Teacher, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Mr. Tabakov was well known for scores of films, but his biggest impact was in the theater, as an actor, director and mentor of future stars.

name: Olly Wilson
profession: Composer Meshed African and Western Music
headline: Olly Wilson, 80, Dies; Composer Meshed African and Western Music
abstract: A scholar and musician as well, he drew on jazz and West African traditions as well as Stravinsky, and once played with Chuck Berry in a St. Louis bar.

name: Gary Lincoff
profession: Spread the Joy of Mushrooms Far and Wide
headline: Gary Lincoff, 75, Dies; Spread the Joy of Mushrooms Far and Wide
abstract: Mr. Lincoff, a self-taught mycologist, led mushroom hunts from Siberia to Central Park, where he found more than 400 species just blocks from his apartment.

name: Betty Ann Bowser
headline: Betty Ann Bowser, Versatile TV Newswoman, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Ms. Bowser was one of television’s most prominent newswomen, reporting for CBS and then for the “PBS NewsHour,” covering a wide range of issues.

name: Lawrence K. Grossman
profession: Head of PBS and Then NBC News
headline: Lawrence K. Grossman, Head of PBS and Then NBC News, Dies at 86
abstract: At PBS he expanded the “MacNeil/Lehrer Report” and started “Frontline,” but early successes at NBC News were overtaken by cuts imposed by new corporate bosses.

name: Buell Neidlinger
headline: Buell Neidlinger, Acclaimed Genre-Crossing Bassist, Dies at 82
