abstract: He had a founding role in free jazz, played alongside Cecil Taylor, performed in a Stravinsky premiere and recorded with Dolly Parton and the Eagles.

name: Li Ao
profession: Writer and Political Firebrand in Taiwan
headline: Li Ao, Writer and Political Firebrand in Taiwan, Dies at 82
abstract: Known affectionately as the “madman” of Taiwan, Mr. Li vigorously defended freedom of speech and called for reunification with mainland China.

name: Linda Brown
headline: Linda Brown, Symbol of Landmark Desegregation Case, Dies at 75
abstract: She was a child whose exclusion from a whites-only school led to the 1954 Supreme Court case Brown v. Board of Education.

name: José Antonio Abreu
headline: José Antonio Abreu, Venezuelan Musical Visionary, Dies at 78
abstract: His widely imitated program, El Sistema, taught classical music to some of Venezuela’s poorest children and gave the conductor Gustavo Dudamel his start.

name: John Cacioppo
headline: John Cacioppo, Who Studied Effects of Loneliness, Is Dead at 66
abstract: He helped link a lack of social connections to physiological damage. And while conducting his research he married a fellow neuroscientist.

name: Mel Rosen
profession: Coach of Powerful 92 Olympics Track Team
headline: Mel Rosen, Coach of Powerful ‘92 Olympics Track Team, Dies at 90
abstract: After making Auburn a track and field power, Rosen led a United States team to glory at the Barcelona Games.

name: James F. Holland
headline: James F. Holland, Trailblazing Cancer Researcher, Dies at 92
abstract: Dr. Holland was called a founding father of chemotherapy, collaborating on drug combinations to contain childhood leukemia and other tumors.

name: Philip Kerr
headline: Philip Kerr, 62, Author of ‘Gunther’ Crime Novels, Is Dead
abstract: Though wary of being typecast as a one-note author, Mr. Kerr, to keep his fans satisfied, ended up writing 13 novels about a detective in Nazi-era Berlin.

name: Delores Taylor
profession: Writer and Star in Billy Jack Films
headline: Delores Taylor, 85, Dies; Writer and Star in ‘Billy Jack’ Films
abstract: On both sides of the camera, Ms. Taylor was a driving force behind a surprise 1971 hit action-film and its two sequels.

name: Stéphane Audran
headline: Stéphane Audran, Star in Oscar-Winning ‘Babette’s Feast,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Her turn in an Oscar-winning film was one highlight among numerous credits, many in the films of Claude Chabrol, her husband for 16 years.

name: Arnold R. Hirsch
headline: Arnold R. Hirsch, Historian of Housing Segregation, Dies at 69
abstract: An inquiry into urban unrest led to “Making the Second Ghetto,” a chronicle of systemic bias in the wake of the second Great Migration of Southern blacks.

name: Liam O’Flynn
profession: Master Irish Piper in a Folk Revival
headline: Liam O’Flynn, Master Irish Piper in a Folk Revival, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. O’Flynn “could move your heart” playing the uilleann pipes. He was best known as a founding member of the acclaimed folk band Planxty.

name: Saba Mahmood
profession: Traced Intersection of Feminism and Islam
headline: Saba Mahmood, 57, Dies; Traced Intersection of Feminism and Islam
abstract: In one book, Professor Mahmood, a scholar at Berkeley, examined a grass-roots women’s movement in Egypt focused on moral reform.

name: Nancy McFadden
profession: Adviser to Bill Clinton and Jerry Brown
headline: Nancy McFadden, 59, Adviser to Bill Clinton and Jerry Brown, Dies
abstract: A campaign aide to Mr. Clinton in 1992, she joined his administration before becoming Governor Brown’s right hand in Sacramento.

name: Yu Gwan-sun
headline: Overlooked No More: Yu Gwan-sun, a Korean Independence Activist Who Defied Japanese Rule
abstract: When a call for peaceful protests came in spring 1919, a schoolgirl became the face of a nation’s collective yearning for freedom.

name: Rusty Staub
headline: Rusty Staub, Durable Batter Who Won Pennant With Mets, Dies at 73
abstract: Nicknamed Le Grand Orange while playing for Montreal — he was 6-foot-2 and had curly red hair — Staub made six All-Star teams in his 23-year major league career.

name: Barbara Lewalski
headline: Barbara Lewalski, 87, Milton Scholar and Barrier Breaker, Is Dead
abstract: A Renaissance authority, she was the first woman to hold tenured, endowed professorships in the English departments at Brown and Harvard.

name: Deborah Carrington
headline: Deborah Carrington, 58, Dies; Actress and Stuntwoman
abstract: Her dwarfism allowed her to play Ewoks and Geex, and she was admired as a stunt double, but she was happiest to get work as a character actress.

name: Russell Freedman
profession: Writer of History for Young Readers
headline: Russell Freedman, 88, Writer of History for Young Readers, Dies
abstract: His more than 60 books were acclaimed for their clear prose, thorough research and generous use of photographs and illustrations.

name: Anita Shreve
headline: Anita Shreve, 71, Best-Selling Novelist Who Wrote ‘Weight of Water,’ Is Dead
abstract: Her career took off in 1999 when Oprah Winfrey chose “The Pilot’s Wife” for Oprah’s Book Club.

name: Andrew Balducci
profession: Turned a Market Into a Food Mecca
headline: Andrew Balducci, Who Turned a Market Into a Food Mecca, Dies at 92
abstract: From his father’s pushcart, he and his family built Balducci’s into an emporium that dominated the specialty-foods business in New York for decades.

name: Mel Gordon
headline: Mel Gordon, Drama Scholar of the Fringe, Is Dead at 71
abstract: An insatiable curiosity led him to contemplate Jewish superheroes, bad acting, the sexualized worlds of Weimer Berlin and Risqué Paris, and more.

name: Peter Munk
profession: Built Worlds Biggest Gold Mining Company
headline: Peter Munk, 90, Dies; Built World’s Biggest Gold Mining Company
abstract: After a notable failure in making stereo equipment, Mr. Munk turned to gold, originally striking it rich in Nevada.

name: Anne Forer Pyne
headline: Anne Forer Pyne, a Feminist Who Opened Eyes, Dies at 72
abstract: Her use of the phrase “consciousness raising” in a New York gathering in the 1960s helped awaken in women a sense of solidarity against oppression.

name: Samuel Belzberg
profession: Corporate Raider in a Family Dynasty
headline: Samuel Belzberg, Corporate Raider in a Family Dynasty, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Belzberg was a Canadian who, with his brothers, amassed a fortune using the “greenmail” takeover tactic and later reinvented himself as a private-equity investor.

name: Johan van Hulst
profession: Helped Save 600 Children From the Nazis
headline: Johan van Hulst, Who Helped Save 600 Children From the Nazis, Dies at 107
abstract: ‘You know for a fact that the children you leave behind are going to die. I took 12 with me. Later on, I asked myself, “Why not 13?”’

name: Efraín Ríos Montt
headline: Efraín Ríos Montt, Guatemalan Dictator Convicted of Genocide, Dies at 91
abstract: General Ríos Montt began his political career as a reformer but was later found guilty of trying to exterminate a Mayan Indian community.

name: Elizabeth Ebert
headline: Elizabeth Ebert, ‘Grand Dame of Cowboy Poetry,’ Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Ebert, who wrote in secret for most of her life, later rose to queenly prominence within the chivalrous ranks of cowboy poetry.

name: Steven Bochco
profession: Producer of Hill Street Blues and NYPD Blue
headline: Steven Bochco, Producer of ‘Hill Street Blues’ and ‘NYPD Blue,’ Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Bochco’s gritty dramas forever changed the genre and shattered what had been the norms for hourlong prime-time shows.

name: Winnie Madikizela-Mandela
headline: Winnie Madikizela-Mandela Is Dead at 81; Fought Apartheid
abstract: She was hailed as a liberator, only to see that stature overshadowed by corruption, kidnapping, murder and the implosion of her marriage to Nelson Mandela.

name: Stephen Reinhardt
headline: Stephen Reinhardt, Liberal Lion of Federal Court, Dies at 87
abstract: Judge Reinhardt, a Carter appointee to the Ninth Circuit in California, was a target of conservatives and often overruled by the Supreme Court.

name: Martin Luther King Jr.
headline: Martin Luther King Jr.’s Original New York Times Obituary
abstract: The obituary, which was published on April 5, 1968, celebrated the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. as a prophet of a crusade for racial equality and a voice of anguish for millions of people.

name: Michael Tree
headline: Michael Tree, a Founder of the Guarneri Quartet, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Tree, a violist, helped create the group in 1964. With only one change in its lineup, it performed for the next 45 years.

name: Anna Chennault
headline: Anna Chennault, Behind-the-Scenes Force in Washington, Dies at 94
abstract: A writer, executive and Republican fund-raiser who dabbled in Cold War foreign intrigue after the death of her husband, a famous general in World War II.

name: Connie Lawn
headline: Connie Lawn, Independent White House Reporter, Dies at 73
abstract: Ms. Lawn built her nearly 50-year career at the White House without the consistent support of a major media company.

name: Bob Beattie
profession: Olympic Ski Coach and ABC Sports Analyst
headline: Bob Beattie, 85, Olympic Ski Coach and ABC Sports Analyst, Dies
abstract: A commentator brought an intense knowledge of Olympic and World Cup skiing to the early days of “Wide World of Sports.”

name: Janka Nabay
profession: Carried an African Dance Music Worldwide
headline: Janka Nabay, 54, Dies; Carried an African Dance Music Worldwide
abstract: A musician fled war-torn Sierra Leone for the United States, formed a band and introduced an ancient music, bubu, to a broad audience.

name: William Prochnau
headline: William Prochnau, Journalist and Author, Is Dead at 80
abstract: His lauded book “Once Upon a Distant War” profiled a group of young, skeptical Vietnam War reporters. Other projects inspired movies.

name: Herbert Kaiser
profession: Health Care Champion in South Africa
headline: Herbert Kaiser, 94, Health Care Champion in South Africa, Dies
abstract: A former diplomat there, he and his wife started an initiative that nurtured 10,000 black medical professionals in a system that heavily favored whites.

name: Drue Heinz
profession: Patron of Literature and Host of Authors
headline: Drue Heinz, Patron of Literature and Host of Authors, Dies at 103
abstract: She created a castle retreat for writers in Scotland, endowed literary prizes, started a publishing house and was publisher of The Paris Review.

name: Alfred Crosby
headline: Alfred Crosby, ‘Father of Environmental History,’ Is Dead at 87
abstract: A historian who added the sciences to the historian’s toolkit in investigating the impact of European culture on the world, starting with Columbus.

name: Bessie B. Stringfield
headline: Overlooked No More: Bessie B. Stringfield, the ‘Motorcycle Queen of Miami’
abstract: In the 1950s, when women were relegated to housework, Stringfield revved and roared through Florida’s palm-tree-lined streets on her Harley-Davidson.

name: Amsale Aberra
headline: Amsale Aberra, Trendsetting Bridal Gown Designer, Is Dead at 64
abstract: With her own brand, Ms. Aberra eschewed the elaborate tulle-and-lace dresses of the 1980s and introduced a simple, modern wedding dress.

name: Robert Haas
headline: Robert Haas, Wine Importer and California Vintner, Dies at 90
abstract: Over nearly 70 years, a Brooklyn-born entrepreneur introduced French brands to Americans and cultivated Rhone Valley vines in a West Coast winery.

name: Robert Haas
headline: Robert Haas, Financier and Aerial Photographer, Dies at 74
abstract: He specialized in leveraged buyouts in the 1980s, shot distant landscapes and wildlife from helicopters, then collected so many motorcycles that he opened a museum.

name: Carl Scheib
profession: Youngest Player in American League History
headline: Carl Scheib, Youngest Player in American League History, Dies at 91
abstract: A star pitcher in high school, Scheib had never seen a major league baseball game. But in 1943, at 16, he began playing for the Philadelphia A’s.

name: Susan Anspach
headline: Susan Anspach, 75, Dies; Daring Actress in Maverick Films
abstract: She personified the counterculture in the Off Broadway run of “Hair” in the ’60s and in films like “Five Easy Pieces” and “Play It Again, Sam” in the ’70s.

name: Cecil Taylor
headline: Cecil Taylor, Pianist Who Defied Jazz Orthodoxy, Is Dead at 89
abstract: An uncompromising artist, Mr. Taylor argued against reductive definitions of what a musician of his training and background could or should do.

name: Sheila Link
headline: Sheila Link, Sportswoman and Firearms Authority, Dies at 94
abstract: A former New Jersey music major, she hunted, camped and shared her adventures and advice as an author and a columnist for Women & Guns magazine.

name: La Wilson
headline: La Wilson, 93, Dies; Made Art in Elaborate Assemblages
abstract: She took ordinary objects, from alphabet blocks to bullet casings, and arranged them in boxes, giving them extraordinary new life.

name: Daniel Akaka
headline: Daniel Akaka, Former Democratic Senator From Hawaii, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Akaka, a 36-year veteran of Capitol Hill, fought for the belated recognition of Asian-American servicemen in World War II.

name: Isao Takahata
headline: Isao Takahata, Leader in Japanese Animation, Dies at 82
abstract: With Hayao Miyazaki, Mr. Takahata founded Japan’s premier anime studio, Ghibli, and directed sophisticated films like “Grave of the Fireflies.”

name: Eric Bristow
headline: Eric Bristow, the First Superstar of Darts, Is Dead at 60
abstract: Described as “brash and arrogant,” Mr. Bristow won more than 70 darts tournaments, and his colorful personality helped fuel the game’s popularity.

name: Chuck McCann
profession: Zany Comic in Early Childrens TV
headline: Chuck McCann, Zany Comic in Early Children’s TV, Dies at 83
abstract: He acted onscreen, was the voice of Cocoa Puff’s Cuckoo Bird and greeted his neighbor with “Hi, guy!” through a shared medicine chest in a deodorant ad.

name: Ivor Guest
headline: Ivor Guest, 97, Dies; Transformed Study of Dance History
abstract: A lawyer by training, Mr. Guest became a leading authority on the period from 1750 to 1900 and contributed to a well-loved 20th-century ballet.

name: Keith Murdoch
headline: Keith Murdoch, Rugby Bruiser Who Vanished in the Outback, Is Dead at 74
abstract: While on tour, he was sent home to New Zealand over a hotel fracas. But he “went bush” instead, disappearing into remotest Australia and into legend.

name: Yvonne Staples
profession: Member and Manager of the Staple Singers
headline: Yvonne Staples, Member and Manager of the Staple Singers, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Staples was a background voice and business manager for her family’s pop and soul group, whose 1970s hits included “I’ll Take You There.”

name: Donald McKayle
headline: Donald McKayle, 87, Broadway and Modern Dance Choreographer, Dies
abstract: He wove the African-American experience, including the pain of discrimination, into modern dance and directed and choreographed the musical “Raisin.”

name: Marcia Thompson
headline: Marcia Thompson, Prudent Promoter of the Arts, Dies at 94
abstract: From her unheralded role at the Ford Foundation, she gave cultural groups with artistic potential the financial incentives to close their budget gaps.

name: Fran Bera
headline: Fran Bera, Competitive, Record-Breaking Aviator, Is Dead at 93
abstract: She earned her pilot’s license at 16 and kept flying until she was 91, winning more than a dozen air competitions and breaking a world record.

name: Ruth Nussenzweig
headline: Ruth Nussenzweig, Who Pursued Malaria Vaccine, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Nussenzweig’s research into one of the world’s most deadly diseases laid the groundwork for an approach once thought beyond reach.

name: J.D. McClatchy
headline: J.D. McClatchy, Poet of the Body, in Sickness and Health, Dies at 72
abstract: A prolific man of letters — he was a critic, translator and librettist as well — he later turned his poet’s eye on his struggle with cancer.

name: Lois Wheeler Snow
profession: Critic of Human Rights Abuses in China
headline: Lois Wheeler Snow, Critic of Human Rights Abuses in China, Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Snow was an actress and writer whose outspoken criticism was amplified by the legacy of her husband, the journalist Edgar Snow.

name: Lin Huiyin
headline: Overlooked No More: Lin Huiyin and Liang Sicheng, Chroniclers of Chinese Architecture
abstract: In the 1930s, the couple began surveying and recording the country’s overlooked ancient buildings in an effort to begin preserving them.

name: Liang Sicheng
headline: Overlooked No More: Lin Huiyin and Liang Sicheng, Chroniclers of Chinese Architecture
abstract: In the 1930s, the couple began surveying and recording the country’s overlooked ancient buildings in an effort to begin preserving them.

name: Mitzi Shore
headline: Mitzi Shore, Whose Comedy Store Fostered Rising Stars, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Shore was a critic, confidante and caretaker for comics like Richard Pryor, Robin Williams, George Carlin, Sandra Bernhard and Jim Carrey.

name: John Ehle
headline: John Ehle, Who Rooted His Novels in Appalachia, Is Dead at 92
abstract: His fiction was praised for giving dignity to mountain people too often stereotyped as hillbillies. He was also an innovator in arts education.

name: Peter Grünberg
headline: Peter Grünberg, 78, Winner of an ‘iPod Nobel,’ Is Dead
abstract: Discovering how to store vast amounts of data by manipulating magnetic and electrical fields paved the way for devices like the smartphone.

name: Pierre Sioufi
profession: Sheltered the Kids of the Arab Spring
headline: Pierre Sioufi, Who Sheltered ‘the Kids’ of the Arab Spring, Is Dead at 56
abstract: A kindhearted bohemian in Cairo opened his home overlooking Tahrir Square as a refuge to the protesters who were risking their lives.

name: John Melcher
profession: Montana Democrat in House and Senate
headline: John Melcher, Montana Democrat in House and Senate, Dies at 93
abstract: He embraced both economic development and environmental protections for a state rich in natural resources and pristine wilderness.

name: William Beinecke
profession: Patron of Central Park and Yale
headline: William Beinecke, Patron of Central Park and Yale, Dies at 103
abstract: A former chief of S&H (dispenser of Green Stamps), he was the first chairman of the park conservancy and helped create the Yale School of Management.

name: Charles McDew
profession: Tactician for Student Civil Rights Group
headline: Charles McDew, 79, Tactician for Student Civil Rights Group, Dies
abstract: A founder of the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee, he helped organize direct-action protests and looked beyond integration to voting rights.

name: Jean Marzollo
profession: Her I Spy Books Challenged Children
headline: Jean Marzollo, 75, Dies; Her ‘I Spy’ Books Challenged Children
abstract: The books, among more than 150 she wrote, sent millions of young readers searching for objects in elaborate photo collages.

name: Helen Mayer Harrison
headline: Helen Mayer Harrison, Leader in Eco-Art Movement, Dies at 90
abstract: With her husband, Newton, she formed an artistic team that examined ecosystems, global warming and related subjects in innovative ways.

name: Tim O’Connor
headline: Tim O’Connor, Complex Resident of ‘Peyton Place,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. O’Connor, a familiar face on TV for decades, had his longest run as a convict-turned-newspaperman on an ABC prime-time soap opera.

name: Milos Forman
profession: Won Oscars for Cuckoos Nest and Amadeus
headline: Milos Forman, 86, Dies; Won Oscars for ‘Cuckoo’s Nest’ and ‘Amadeus’
abstract: A witness to turmoil in his Czech homeland, he was in the front rank of directors struggling to make commercial films with countercultural sensibilities.

name: Gillian Ayres
headline: Gillian Ayres, Abstract Artist Besotted by Paint, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Ayres had little patience for people seeking the meaning of her bold, colorful works. “I wish they’d just look. It’s visual.”

name: R. Lee Ermey
profession: Harsh Drill Instructor in Full Metal Jacket
headline: R. Lee Ermey, Harsh Drill Instructor in ‘Full Metal Jacket,’ Dies at 74
abstract: He drew on his service as a Marine drill instructor, carrying shrapnel in his back, in playing a foulmouthed sergeant in Stanley Kubrick’s 1987 film.

name: Hal Greer
profession: Hall of Fame Jump Shooter for 76ers
headline: Hal Greer, Hall of Fame Jump Shooter for 76ers, Is Dead at 81
abstract: In the era of Oscar Robertson and Jerry West, Greer was a brilliant and prolific star guard in his own right, leading Philadelphia to the 1967 title.

name: Mary Regula
profession: Founder of Library Saluting First Ladies
headline: Mary Regula, Founder of Library Saluting First Ladies, Dies at 91
abstract: She recruited her husband, an Ohio congressman, along with Hillary Clinton and others to help create a National Parks site in Canton, Ohio.

name: David Edgerton
headline: David Edgerton, a Founder of Burger King, Is Dead at 90
abstract: He and a partner created a flourishing fast-food chain only to sell it, for what proved to be a bargain price, just as the industry was about to soar.

name: Harry Anderson
headline: Harry Anderson, 65, ‘Night Court’ Actor Who Bottled Magic Onscreen and Off, Dies
abstract: As the zany Judge Harry Stone, Mr. Anderson spent nine seasons presiding over a fictional Manhattan courtroom and was nominated for three consecutive Emmys.

name: Harry Anderson
headline: Harry Anderson, ‘M.V.P. of American Sailing,’ Is Dead at 98
abstract: A scion of a patrician family familiar to yacht clubs, he devoted his life to racing and its rules, with a hand in the America’s Cup, the Olympics and training the young.

name: Karen Dawisha
headline: Karen Dawisha, 68, Dies; Traced Roots of Russian Corruption
abstract: A Russia scholar, she delved into Vladimir V. Putin’s circle of friends in 1990s St. Petersburg and found the blueprint for a “kleptocracy.”

name: Bill Nack
profession: Covered the Horses From Up Close
headline: Bill Nack, Who Covered the Horses From Up Close, Dies at 77
abstract: In articles for Sports Illustrated and in a biography of Secretariat, he observed horse racing with a literary eye from the stable to the track.

name: Daphne Sheldrick
headline: Daphne Sheldrick, 83, Who Saved Orphaned Elephants, Is Dead
abstract: A wildlife trust she established in Kenya took in young animals, including many who had lost their mothers to poachers.

name: Carl Kasell
headline: Carl Kasell, NPR Newsman Who Discovered Laughs, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Kasell started off as an anchorman and later in his career became an absurdist comedian on the popular quiz show “Wait Wait ... Don’t Tell Me.”

name: Ronald Dunbar
headline: Ronald Dunbar, 78, Producer and Grammy-Winning Songwriter, Dies
abstract: Mr. Dunbar was credited for soul hits like “Band of Gold,” “Give Me Just a Little More Time” and “Patches,” which became a hit for Clarence Carter.

name: Art Bell
headline: Art Bell, Radio Host Who Tuned In to the Dark Side, Dies at 72
abstract: Reaching a nationwide audience from a home studio in the desert, he listened to callers’ accounts of the paranormal deep into the early hours.

name: Barbara Bush
profession: Wife of 41st President and Mother of 43rd
headline: Barbara Bush, Wife of 41st President and Mother of 43rd, Dies at 92
abstract: Mrs. Bush avoided controversial issues while in the White House and became known for her straight talk, lack of pretension and self-deprecating humor.

name: Nathan Davis
headline: Nathan Davis, Jazz Saxophonist and Educator, Is Dead at 81
abstract: The founding director of the University of Pittsburgh’s jazz studies program, he helped establish a place for African-American music in the academy.

name: Bruno Sammartino
profession: Durable Champ in WWE Hall of Fame
headline: Bruno Sammartino, Durable Champ in WWE Hall of Fame, Dies at 82
abstract: A popular, Verdi-loving Italian immigrant who dominated the ring for a record 11 years in the 1960s and ′70s and insisted that he never took a dive.

name: Vittorio Taviani
headline: Vittorio Taviani, 88, Dies; Made Acclaimed Films With Brother
abstract: His and Paolo Taviani’s movies drew notice in their native Italy and beyond; one, “Padre Padrone,” won the Palme d’Or at Cannes in 1977.

name: Jean McFaddin
profession: Made the Macys Parade What It Is
headline: Jean McFaddin, Who Made the Macy’s Parade What It Is, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. McFaddin transformed a Thanksgiving tradition into a spectacular, then turned her hand to Santaland, a flower extravaganza and fireworks on the Fourth.

name: Harriott Daley
headline: Overlooked No More: Harriott Daley, the Capitol’s First Telephone Operator
abstract: Daley, who became a switchboard operator in 1898, made sure members of Congress were just a phone call away from their constituents.

name: Beatrix Hamburg
headline: Beatrix Hamburg, Barrier-Breaking Scholar, Is Dead at 94
abstract: At Vassar and then at Yale’s Medical School, Dr. Hamburg blazed trails for black women. Then came a distinguished career in child development.

name: Daedra Charles
profession: Hall of Fame Center for Tennessee
headline: Daedra Charles, 49, Hall of Fame Center for Tennessee, Dies
abstract: With Charles, the Lady Vols won two national championships under coach Pat Summitt. She went on to play on the Olympic team and in the pros.

name: Rob Matthews
headline: Rob Matthews, 56, Blind Paralympian Who Won 8 Gold Medals, Dies
abstract: A British runner competed at six Games for the disabled and broke 22 world records. “Running turned back the fear,” he said.

name: Sergio Pitol
headline: Sergio Pitol, Inventive and Honored Mexican Author, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Pitol won the prestigious Cervantes Prize for a body of work that blended genres. King Juan Carlos I of Spain said it “seduced us with the truth.”

name: Lee Holley
profession: Cartoonist of Teenage Life in Ponytail
headline: Lee Holley, Cartoonist of Teenage Life in ‘Ponytail,’ Dies at 85
abstract: He was helping with “Dennis the Menace” when he created “Ponytail,” about a spirited girl in a postwar suburban world of boys, burgers and phone chats.

name: Earle Bruce
profession: Winning Football Coach at Ohio State
headline: Earle Bruce, Winning Football Coach at Ohio State, Dies at 87
abstract: Bruce had the unenviable task of following the revered Woody Hayes, but he compiled 81 victories over eight seasons before being fired.

name: Carolyn Jacobson
headline: Carolyn Jacobson, Champion of Women’s Union Rights, Dies at 67
abstract: She helped place equal rights and health and social issues of particular concern to women workers on the agenda of organized labor.

name: Avicii
profession: Electronic Dance Music Producer and D.J
headline: Avicii, Electronic Dance Music Producer and D.J., Is Dead at 28
abstract: Tim Bergling, who worked with pop stars like Madonna and Coldplay under the stage name Avicii, was found dead in Muscat, Oman.

name: Joan Konner
headline: Joan Konner, 87, TV Producer and Journalism Dean, Dies
abstract: Ms. Konner worked for NBC and PBS, teamed up with Bill Moyers, won 16 Emmys and was the first woman to lead Columbia’s graduate school.

name: Kirk Simon
headline: Kirk Simon, 63, Oscar-Winning Documentarian, Dies
abstract: Mr. Simon won an Academy Award for “Strangers No More,” about a diverse school in Israel, and directed HBO’s “Masterclass,” in which luminaries became teachers.

name: Richard Oldenburg
profession: Led MoMAs Expansion and Drew Crowds
headline: Richard Oldenburg, Who Led MoMA’s Expansion and Drew Crowds, Dies at 84
abstract: A director brought blockbuster exhibitions of Picasso, Matisse and Cézanne — along with a steady hand — to a Museum of Modern Art that doubled its size.

name: Verne Troyer
headline: Verne Troyer, Mini-Me in Austin Powers Movies, Dies at 49
abstract: At 2 feet 8 inches, Mr. Troyer was a versatile actor who was widely recognizable from the movies he appeared in.

name: Richard Jenrette
profession: Wall St. Power and Preserver of Homes
headline: Richard Jenrette, 89, Wall St. Power and Preserver of Homes, Dies
abstract: He helped found a groundbreaking firm, nursed an insurance giant back to health and created a trust devoted to restoring historic American homes.

name: Eugene Leff
profession: Fought for New York in Love Canal Case
headline: Eugene Leff Dies at 73; Fought for New York in Love Canal Case
abstract: Mr. Leff was the state’s lead lawyer in a toxic-waste suit against a chemical company that led to a record $98 million settlement in 1994.

name: Charles Zwick
headline: Charles Zwick, Who Balanced Budget Under Johnson, Dies at 91
abstract: As the president’s last budget director, he helped engineer the only federal surplus to be recorded over a span of almost 40 years.

name: Bob Dorough
profession: Jazzman With a Hit Kid-Music Series
headline: Bob Dorough, Jazzman With a Hit Kid-Music Series, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Dorough worked with Miles Davis and many others, but he’s best known for his songs for the educational cartoon series “Schoolhouse Rock!”

name: Vel Phillips
headline: Vel Phillips, Housing Rights Champion in the ′60s, Is Dead at 95
abstract: She broke racial and gender barriers on her way to spearheading open-housing legislation in Milwaukee and was a voice in Democratic national politics.

name: Samuel Epstein
headline: Dr. Samuel Epstein, 91, Cassandra of Cancer Prevention, Dies
abstract: He blamed greedy manufacturers, lax regulators, misguided researchers and complicit charitable groups for what he saw as a coming cancer epidemic.

name: Soon-Tek Oh
headline: Soon-Tek Oh, Actor Who Chafed at Asian Stereotypes, Dies at 85
abstract: He was among the founders of East West Players, a theater troupe that sought better roles for Asian-American actors and more representative stories.

name: Maria Bochkareva
profession: Led Women Into Battle in WWI
headline: Overlooked No More: Maria Bochkareva, Who Led Women Into Battle in WWI
abstract: “My heart yearned to be there, in the boiling caldron of war, to be baptized in its fire and scorched in its lava,” Bochkareva wrote in her 1919 autobiography.

name: Sachio Kinugasa
headline: Sachio Kinugasa, Japanese Baseball’s Iron Man, Is Dead at 71
abstract: In 1987 he broke Lou Gehrig’s record for consecutive games played, only to see his testament to durability exceeded nine years later by Cal Ripken Jr.

name: Gertrude Jeannette
headline: Gertrude Jeannette, Actor, Director and Cabdriver, Dies at 103
abstract: Believed to be the first woman to drive a taxi in New York City, she also overcame a speech impediment to work on Broadway, in film and on television.

name: Sam Hamill
headline: Sam Hamill, Poet, Publisher and War Protester, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Hamill, the founder of Copper Canyon Press, expressed his opposition to the Iraq war by collecting and publishing thousands of antiwar poems.

name: Jean Gump
headline: Jean Gump, Tireless Fighter for Social Justice, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Gump served four years in prison for disabling a missile silo, one of her many arrests as a political activist, all while raising 12 children.

name: Polixeni Papapetrou
headline: Polixeni Papapetrou, Photographer With an Eerie Eye, Dies at 57
abstract: Her photographs often featured her own children in startling costumes, but the most attention-getting one involved no clothes at all.

name: Charles Neville
headline: Charles Neville of the Neville Brothers Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Neville, a saxophonist, joined with his brothers in 1977 to form a New Orleans supergroup that mingled a party spirit with social consciousness.

name: Michael Healy
headline: Maj. Gen. Michael Healy, Paragon Among Green Berets, Dies at 91
abstract: General Healy served for decades and helped lift morale when he took command of Special Forces in Vietnam after a scandalous murder case in 1969.

name: Nelson Pereira dos Santos
headline: Nelson Pereira dos Santos, 89, Dies; Lifted Brazilian Film
abstract: Mr. dos Santos was a leader of the Cinema Novo movement, which emphasized grit and struggle, and fought for a uniquely Brazilian cinema.

name: Larry Harvey
headline: Larry Harvey, the Man Behind Burning Man, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Mr. Harvey’s anti-establishment festival evolved from a modest affair on a San Francisco beach to a globally celebrated phenomenon in the Nevada desert.

name: James H. Cone
headline: James H. Cone, a Founder of Black Liberation Theology, Dies at 79
abstract: Dr. Cone argued for racial equality and an understanding of the Christian Gospel that elevated the voices of the oppressed.

name: Judith Leiber
headline: Judith Leiber, 97, Dies; Turned Handbags Into Objets d’Art
abstract: Her imaginative evening bags were sought after by celebrities and royalty. She died only hours after the death of her husband, the painter Gerson Leiber.

name: Steven Marcus
headline: Steven Marcus, Columbia Scholar and Literary Critic, Dies at 89
abstract: An author and professor for more than four decades, he made criticism a prism on history and society, from pornography to psychoanalysis.

name: Abbas Attar
headline: Abbas Attar, Who Photographed Iran’s Revolution, Dies at 74
abstract: He took pictures in troubled areas all over the world, but he was more interested in the causes and aftermath of war than in the killing.

name: Gerson Leiber
profession: Artist Created Museum With Designer Wife
headline: Gerson Leiber, 96, Dies; Artist Created Museum With Designer Wife
abstract: Mr. Leiber’s paintings ranged from abstract to stylized representational. His and Judith Leiber’s collection features his art and her celebrated handbags.

name: Everett Fahy
headline: Everett Fahy, Museum Authority on European Painting, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Mr. Fahy ran the Frick Collection and then oversaw a reorganization at the Metropolitan Museum of Art that was hailed as groundbreaking.

name: Donald Seldin
profession: Put a Medical School on the Map
headline: Dr. Donald Seldin, Who Put a Medical School on the Map, Dies at 97
abstract: A kidney specialist born in Brooklyn, he gambled that an old Army barracks in Dallas could grow into a national leader in biomedicine.

name: Jabo Starks
headline: Jabo Starks, Drummer for James Brown, Dies at 79
abstract: During Brown’s heyday in the 1960s and ’70s, Mr. Starks and Clyde Stubblefield were the drum team behind some big hits.

name: Luis García Meza
headline: Luis García Meza, Bolivian Dictator Jailed for Genocide, Dies at 88
abstract: In a brief but bloody rule in the 1980s, he jailed and tortured hundreds of dissidents. He had been serving a 30-year prison term at his death.

name: Marcia Hafif
headline: Marcia Hafif, Painter of Monochromatic Works, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Ms. Hafif didn’t want you to wonder what a work was a painting of; she wanted you to see the color, the brush strokes, the play of light.

name: Art Paul
headline: Art Paul, Art Director Who Gave Playboy Its Look, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Paul, who was with the magazine from the beginning, created its rabbit-head logo and hired great illustrators to lend worldliness to its pages.

name: Julia de Burgos
headline: Overlooked No More: Julia de Burgos, a Poet Who Helped Shape Puerto Rico’s Identity
abstract: De Burgos, a literary foremother of the Nuyorican movement, defied societal norms and advocated for the island’s independence.

name: Joan Chase
profession: Drew Acclaim With First Novel at 46
headline: Joan Chase, Who Drew Acclaim With First Novel at 46, Dies at 81
abstract: Margaret Atwood called Ms. Chase’s book “a Norman Rockwell painting gone bad, the underside of the idyllic hometown” in American society.

name: Alice Provensen
headline: Alice Provensen, a Star in the Children’s-Book World, Dies at 99
abstract: She illustrated dozens of books beginning in the 1940s, many with her husband, and as her career progressed she also wrote quite a few.

name: Bill Torrey
profession: Brought the Stanley Cup to Long Island
headline: Bill Torrey, Who Brought the Stanley Cup to Long Island, Is Dead at 83
abstract: The original general manager of the Islanders, he built four consecutive N.H.L. championships in the early 1980s.

name: Lester James Peries
headline: Lester James Peries, 99, Visionary Sri Lankan Filmmaker, Dies
abstract: Shunning traditional dance and fantasy fare, he made psychologically rich stories that brought wide recognition to an island nation’s film industry.

name: Joel Kovel
headline: Dr. Joel Kovel, a Founder of Ecosocialism, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Dr. Kovel abandoned Freudian psychiatry to further a radical school of “green and red” thought that envisioned an unpolluted world without capitalism.

name: Thom DeVita
headline: Thom DeVita, 85, Dies; Revolutionized the Art of Tattooing
abstract: Working from his Lower East Side apartment, Mr. DeVita was one of the few artists tattooing in New York City after the practice was banned in 1961.

name: Wanda Wilkomirska
headline: Wanda Wilkomirska, Famed Polish Violinist, Is Dead at 89
abstract: She was one of her country’s most popular cultural exports, until the Solidarity movement disrupted her life.

name: Ninalee Allen Craig
profession: at the Center of a Famous Photograph
headline: Ninalee Allen Craig, at the Center of a Famous Photograph, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Craig reveled in her starring role in Ruth Orkin’s “American Girl in Italy” and said she wasn’t the least bit offended by the men ogling her.

name: Jhoon Rhee
headline: Jhoon Rhee, Athletic Ambassador of Taekwondo, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Rhee‘s many pupils included Bruce Lee, Muhammad Ali, Chuck Norris, Tony Robbins and more than 250 members of congress, like Joe Biden.

name: Aaron Panken
headline: Rabbi Aaron Panken, Reform Seminary President, Dies in Plane Crash at 53
abstract: Rabbi Panken had a degree in electrical engineering, but chose the clergy over a career in a laboratory.

name: Afonso Dhlakama
headline: Afonso Dhlakama, Mozambique’s Opposition Leader, Dies at 65
abstract: With backing from white-controlled African nations, Mr. Dhlakama’s youthful soldiers engaged in a civil war that claimed up to a million lives, mostly civilians.

name: Edwin G. Burrows
headline: Edwin G. Burrows, Historian and Co-Author of ‘Gotham,’ Dies at 74
abstract: He and a fellow college professor, Mike Wallace, spent almost 20 years producing their epic history of New York City, winning the Pulitzer Prize.

name: Ronald Wolk
headline: Ronald Wolk, Innovator in Covering Education News, Dies at 86
abstract: He helped found both The Chronicle of Higher Education and Education Week, two national publications that helped set an agenda academic agenda.

name: Pierre Rissient
headline: Pierre Rissient, 81, Behind-the-Scenes Force of Cinema, Dies
abstract: Mr. Rissient scouted movies for the Cannes Film Festival, and in that role gave a boost to the careers of Jane Campion, Clint Eastwood and many more.

name: Christiane Collins
headline: Christiane Collins, Scholar Who Fought a Columbia Gym, Dies at 92
abstract: An author and architectural historian, she figured in the struggle to preserve West Harlem’s Morningside Park against encroachment by a growing campus.

name: Gayle Shepherd
headline: Gayle Shepherd of the Singing Shepherd Sisters Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Shepherd and her three siblings rode their harmonious style to chart success in 1957 with “Alone (Why Must I Be Alone).”

name: Ermanno Olmi
headline: Ermanno Olmi, Whose Films Captured Humble Lives, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Olmi was more famous at home in Italy than abroad, but he won international acclaim for films like “The Tree of Wooden Clogs” and “Il Posto.”

name: George Deukmejian
headline: George Deukmejian, 2-Term California Governor in the ’80s, Dies at 89
abstract: A fiscally conservative Republican, he was admired for his bipartisanship and popular with voters as a foe of apartheid and assault rifles.

name: Anne V. Coates
headline: Anne V. Coates, Admired Editor of Acclaimed Movies, Dies at 92
abstract: In a six-decade career working for top directors, she was nominated for five Oscars, winning one for “Lawrence of Arabia.”

name: Brooks Kerr
headline: Brooks Kerr, Piano Prodigy and Ellington Expert, Dies at 66
abstract: He started playing the piano when he was 2. As a teenager, he toured with the Ellington band and helped celebrate Ellington’s birthday at the White House.

name: Leticia Ramos Shahani
headline: Overlooked No More: Leticia Ramos Shahani, a Philippine Women’s Rights Pioneer
abstract: Shahani, who died in 2017, worked to advance women’s causes in her native Philippines and around the world.

name: Robert N. Hall
headline: Robert N. Hall, 96, Whose Inventions Are Everywhere, Is Dead
abstract: He came up with a semiconductor laser used in supermarket scanners, printers and remote controls. His magnetron was adapted for the microwave oven.

name: Art Shay
profession: Camera Captured the Famous and the Everyday
headline: Art Shay, Whose Camera Captured the Famous and the Everyday, Dies at 96
abstract: For Life, Time and other magazines, Mr. Shay photographed Marlon Brando, Elizabeth Taylor, Muhammad Ali and nine presidents, as well as the streets of Chicago.

name: Stanley Falkow
headline: Stanley Falkow, Who Saw How Bacteria Cause Disease, Dies at 84
abstract: He found resistance to antibiotics spreading among bacteria and was hailed for his discoveries, though a Nobel Prize eluded him. (Not that he wanted one.)

name: Charlie Russell
headline: Charlie Russell, Who Befriended Bears, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Russell challenged conventional, fear-based ideas of bear management by going to live among black bears in a remote part of Russia.

name: Davida Coady
headline: Dr. Davida Coady, Medical Missionary, Is Dead at 80
abstract: She helped eradicate smallpox in India and reduce malnutrition in Africa, aided refugees in Latin America and later focused on drug and alcohol addictions.

name: Evgeni Vasiukov
headline: Evgeni Vasiukov, Russian Chess Grandmaster, Is Dead at 85
abstract: He was among the world’s best chess players for more than 15 years, but his career was eclipsed by better-known and more talented contemporaries.

name: David Pines
headline: David Pines, 93, Insightful and Influential Physicist, Dies
abstract: He helped explain the electric flow of superconductors and the churning matter inside collapsed stars, work that led to Nobel Prizes (but not for him).

name: Peter Mayer
profession: Publisher of the Incendiary Satanic Verses
headline: Peter Mayer, Publisher of the Incendiary ‘Satanic Verses,’ Dies at 82
abstract: As head of the Penguin Group, he weathered threats over the Salman Rushdie novel. Later, with his father, he had success publishing out-of-print books.

name: Doreen Simmons
headline: Doreen Simmons, Unlikely Voice of Sumo Wrestling, Dies at 85
abstract: Born in England and educated at Cambridge, she found her true calling on Japanese television analyzing the quintessential Japanese sport.

name: Ernest Medina
profession: Army Captain Acquitted in My Lai Massacre
headline: Ernest Medina, Army Captain Acquitted in My Lai Massacre, Dies at 81
abstract: Charged with involuntary manslaughter of at least 100 civilians, Captain Medina denied ordering the killings and was acquitted at a court-martial.

name: Chuck Knox
headline: Chuck Knox, 3-Time N.F.L. Coach of the Year, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Knox was so passionate about the running game he was called Ground Chuck, but he fought to bring Joe Namath to the New York Jets.

name: Margot Kidder
headline: Margot Kidder, Actress Who Found Movie Stardom in ‘Superman,’ Dies at 69
abstract: Best known for playing the role of Lois Lane in four films, Ms. Kidder was a sought-after actress in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Jerrold Meinwald
headline: Jerrold Meinwald, 91, Dies; Studied Creatures’ Chemical Signals
abstract: He examined the chemistry behind secreted substances that can attract a mate or repel a predator, helping to establish a new field, chemical ecology.

name: Adam Parfrey
headline: Adam Parfrey, Publisher of the Provocative, Dies at 61
abstract: His books drew conspiracists and cultists as well as the director Tim Burton, who adapted two of them into the films “Ed Wood” and “Big Eyes.”

name: Tom Wolfe
profession: New Journalist With Electric Style and Acid Pen
headline: Tom Wolfe, 88, ‘New Journalist’ With Electric Style and Acid Pen, Dies
abstract: He wrote “The Electric Kool-Aid Acid Test,” “Bonfire of the Vanities” and “The Right Stuff,” and pioneered a novelistic form of journalism in the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Glenn Branca
headline: Glenn Branca, Composer Who Blended Genres, Loudly, Dies at 69
abstract: One fellow composer said Mr. Branca, who often wrote for massed amplified guitars, was among the few “who put a clearly defined stamp on their music.”

name: Mary Sansone
headline: Mary Sansone, a Grass-Roots Political Godmother, Dies at 101
abstract: A Brooklyn social worker and civic leader who was colorblind to race, she could deliver votes and was courted by political candidates.

name: Matt Marks
headline: Matt Marks, Cutting-Edge Composer and Musician, Dies at 38
abstract: As a founder of the chamber orchestra Alarm Will Sound, he was at the epicenter of a community of open-minded artists.

name: Doug Ford
headline: Doug Ford, Oldest Masters Champion, Dies at 95
abstract: A top golfer in the 1950s who had honed his game in the Bronx, he won at Augusta in 1957 after taking the P.G.A. Championship two years earlier.

name: Harold Guskin
headline: Harold Guskin, Acting Coach Who Nurtured Stars, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Find the character in the words on the page, he instructed Kevin Kline, Glenn Close, James Gandolfini, Rachel Weisz and others.

name: Leah Napolin
headline: Leah Napolin, Whose ‘Yentl’ Adaptation Made Broadway, Dies at 83
abstract: The play, based on an Isaac Bashevis Singer story, was a tale of empowerment in the midst of feminism’s second wave.

name: Lara Saint Paul
headline: Lara Saint Paul, Italian Singer and Aerobics Promoter, Dies at 73
abstract: Born in Eritrea and raised in Italy, she sang with Louis Armstrong and other American idols and, inspired by Jane Fonda, kindled a fitness craze.

name: Fulvia Visconti Ferragamo
headline: Fulvia Visconti Ferragamo, 67, Luxury House Executive, Dies
abstract: One of four generations of Ferragamo women, she bridged the creative and management sides of a venerable Italian purveyor of clothing and accessories.

name: Michael Slive
profession: Led Southeastern Conference to New Heights
headline: Michael Slive, 77, Dies; Led Southeastern Conference to New Heights
abstract: He led the conference from 2002 to 2015 and helped it to navigate a period mired by N.C.A.A. sanctions and become a college football powerhouse.

name: Margarita Xirgu
headline: Overlooked No More: Margarita Xirgu, Theater Radical Who Staged Lorca’s Plays
abstract: The Spanish film star and theater director was known for taking chances in her politics, in her private life and on the stage.

name: Richard Pipes
profession: Historian of Russia and Reagan Aide
headline: Richard Pipes, Historian of Russia and Reagan Aide, Dies at 94
abstract: The author of monumental works, he achieved renown in government as a “cold warrior” skeptic about détente with the Soviet Union.

name: Joseph Campanella
headline: Joseph Campanella, 93, Ubiquitous Character Actor, Dies
abstract: Mr. Campanella found his stride on television as a frequent guest star, playing doctors, lawyers, criminals, cops and judges.

name: Bobbie Louise Hawkins
headline: Bobbie Louise Hawkins, Beat Poet and Author, Dies at 87
abstract: Her writing pulsed with her hardscrabble Texas childhood and, refusing to be his “muse,” her liberation from an overbearing poet husband.

name: Lucian Pintilie
headline: Lucian Pintilie, Authority-Defying Romanian Director, Dies at 84
abstract: His films and stage work angered Communist officials, but he was embraced abroad and seen as an inspiration for the Romanian New Wave.

name: Patricia Morison
profession: Broadways First Kate to Be Kissed
headline: Patricia Morison, 103, Dies; Broadway’s First Kate to Be Kissed
abstract: Ms. Morison was a star of the musical stage in “Kiss Me, Kate” and “The King and I.”

name: Per Kirkeby
headline: Per Kirkeby, Painter Inspired by Nature, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Mr. Kirkeby’s paintings could evoke flattened stones, small boulders, skeins of vines and flowing water emerging from darkness.

name: Reggie Lucas
headline: Reggie Lucas, Versatile Guitarist and Producer, Dies at 65
abstract: In the 1970s, Mr. Lucas worked with Miles Davis. In the 1980s, he produced Madonna’s first album and wrote her hit song “Borderline.”

name: Will Alsop
headline: Will Alsop, Architectural Provocateur, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Mr. Alsop, one of whose designs was called “courageous, bold and just a little insane,” believed that architects had a calling to inspire the public.

name: Bill Gold
headline: Bill Gold, 97, Whose Posters Captured Movie Magic, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Gold was a behind-the-scenes superstar whose artwork offered moviegoers tantalizing glimpses of the raptures awaiting in the cinema darkness.

name: Billy Cannon
profession: Football Star With a Troubled Life
headline: Billy Cannon, Football Star With a Troubled Life, Dies at 80
abstract: He won the 1959 Heisman Trophy and played professionally for 11 years. Then his involvement in a counterfeiting operation landed him in prison.

name: Bernard Lewis
headline: Bernard Lewis, Influential Scholar of Islam, Is Dead at 101
abstract: Mr. Lewis’s views on the connection between Islam and terrorism inspired controversy but also helped shape American foreign policy under George W. Bush.

name: Dovey Johnson Roundtree
headline: Dovey Johnson Roundtree, Barrier-Breaking Lawyer, Dies at 104
abstract: Though little recognized, Ms. Roundtree won advances for black people and women at the bar of justice, challenging the Jim Crow society she knew too well.

name: Robert Indiana
headline: Robert Indiana, 89, Who Turned ‘Love’ Into Enduring Art, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Indiana’s depiction of the letters L, O, V and E was one of the best-known images of the 20th century, widely reproduced but also widely imitated.

name: Zhao Kangmin
profession: Restorer of Chinas Ancient Terra-Cotta Warriors
headline: Zhao Kangmin, Restorer of China’s Ancient Terra-Cotta Warriors, Dies at 81
abstract: The reconstruction of an underground army, one of China’s greatest treasures, would become an archaeologist’s crowning achievement.

name: Geoffrey Hendricks
headline: Geoffrey Hendricks, 86, Attention-Getting Fluxus Artist, Dies
abstract: Mr. Hendricks, known for both his sky paintings and his experiments in art as performance, was also a longtime teacher at Rutgers.

name: Clint Walker
profession: Western Star Tall in the Saddle
headline: Clint Walker, Western Star Tall in the Saddle, Is Dead at 90
abstract: The 6-foot-6 Mr. Walker played the title role in the long-running ABC series “Cheyenne” and was also seen in movies like “The Dirty Dozen.”

name: Carol Mann
headline: Carol Mann, Golf Star and L.P.G.A. Leader, Is Dead at 77
abstract: One of the leading female golfers of the 1960s and ’70s, she later became president of the Ladies Professional Golf Association.

name: Darío Castrillón Hoyos
headline: Cardinal Darío Castrillón Hoyos, Vatican Conservative, Dies at 88
abstract: A Colombian, he held top posts in the Vatican, figuring in controversies on sexual abuse and liberation theology and favoring the Latin Mass.

name: Philip Roth
headline: Philip Roth, Towering Novelist Who Explored Lust, Jewish Life and America, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Roth won almost all the major literary awards and published an exceptional sequence of historical novels in his 60s, an age when many writers are winding down.

name: Joan Wile
profession: Grandmother Against the War in Iraq
headline: Joan Wile, a Grandmother Against the War in Iraq, Dies at 86
abstract: She and other contemporaries held weekly curbside protests in New York for nearly nine years and was arrested twice when they took on Times Square military recruiters.

name: Luis Posada Carriles
headline: Luis Posada Carriles, Who Waged Quest to Oust Castro, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Posada was linked to bombings and plots, worked for the C.I.A., survived an assassination attempt and was jailed in at least three countries.

name: Esther Morris
headline: Overlooked No More: She Followed a Trail to Wyoming. Then She Blazed One.
abstract: The Western territory made history in 1869 by giving women the right to vote. When Esther Morris became justice of the peace a few months later, she made history as well.

name: Laszlo Tabori
headline: Laszlo Tabori, Celebrated Hungarian Runner Who Bolted to U.S., Dies at 86
abstract: Tabori became the third man to run the mile in under four minutes before defecting from his native Hungary to the United States.

name: Dave Garcia
profession: M.L.B. Manager and Minor League Mainstay
headline: Dave Garcia, M.L.B. Manager and Minor League Mainstay, Dies at 97
abstract: Garcia played more than 14 seasons in the minors and hung on as a coach, manager and sage in the majors, doggedly loyal to baseball to the end.

name: Faith Whittlesey
headline: Faith Whittlesey, Conservative Voice and Reagan Aide, Dies at 79
abstract: The only woman on the president’s senior staff, she courted the religious right in helping to build a Reagan coalition and alienated feminists.

name: Michael Goldstein
headline: Michael Goldstein, Publicist Who Started SoHo Weekly News, Dies at 79
abstract: After representing Jimi Hendrix, Sly Stone and other music stars, he challenged The Village Voice, covering Lower Manhattan in a grittier era.

name: Glenn Snoddy
profession: Accidental Inventor of the Fuzz Tone
headline: Glenn Snoddy, 96, Accidental Inventor of the Fuzz Tone, Dies
abstract: A Nashville recording engineer, he earned a place in music history when a studio malfunction created an influential guitar sound.

name: Angelo Falcón
profession: Advocate for Latinos in New York
headline: Angelo Falcón, Advocate for Latinos in New York, Dies at 66
abstract: The outspoken Mr. Falcón was the founder of a one-man research operation that wielded hard data to argue for greater public commitment to Hispanics’ needs.

name: Alan Bean
profession: 4th Person to Walk on the Moon
headline: Alan Bean, 4th Person to Walk on the Moon, Dies at 86
abstract: After leaving NASA, Mr. Bean, a former Navy test pilot, became a full-time artist, creating images of space exploration.

name: Herman D. Farrell Jr.
headline: Herman D. Farrell Jr., a Fixture of New York Politics, Dies at 86
abstract: A longtime Democratic assemblyman, Mr. Farrell was a trusted, gentlemanly party leader in New York and once ran for mayor.

name: Richard Peck
headline: Richard Peck, Acclaimed Author for Young Readers, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Peck used historical fiction, horror and other genres to tell stories about rape, unwanted pregnancy, suicide and other difficult subjects.

name: Stewart Lupton
headline: Stewart Lupton, Singer for ’90s Band Jonathan Fire*Eater, Is Dead at 43
abstract: The songwriter and poet fronted an electric, volatile band that helped inspire a rock revival in New York in the early 2000s.

name: Camilla Dietz Bergeron
headline: Camilla Dietz Bergeron, Stockbroker Turned Jeweler, Dies at 76
abstract: After a successful career on Wall Street, she became a leading buyer and seller of antique and estate baubles on Madison Avenue.

name: Fred Kovaleski
profession: Once a Spy in a Tennis Disguise
headline: Fred Kovaleski, Once a Spy in a Tennis Disguise, Dies at 93
abstract: After he was recruited by the C.I.A. during the Cold War, his international tennis career became a cover for espionage.

name: Dick Tuck
headline: Dick Tuck, Democrats’ Political Prankster in Chief, Dies at 94
abstract: He bedeviled Goldwater, Nixon and other Republican candidates with campaign-trail tomfoolery as a consultant and advance man for the Democratic Party.

name: Josh Greenfeld
headline: Josh Greenfeld, Who Chronicled His Son’s Autism, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Greenfeld, also a screenwriter, wrote the powerful “A Child Called Noah” and then two more books about his son and family.

name: Mildred Council
headline: Mildred Council, a Pillar of Southern Cooking, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Known as Mama Dip, Ms. Council turned an 18-seat diner in North Carolina into a culinary career and never strayed from her food-to-table roots.

name: Sophia Perovskaya
headline: Overlooked No More: The Russian Icon Who Was Hanged for Killing a Czar
abstract: Sophia Perovskaya, an aristocrat, was executed for a political crime after leading the 1881 assassination of Czar Alexander II.

name: Romana Raffetto
headline: Romana Raffetto, Pasta Matriarch in New York, Dies at 85
abstract: She ruled the sauce pot in the kitchen of the family-run factory and store that her father-in-law founded in Greenwich Village in 1906.

name: Ted Dabney
profession: Founder of Atari and a Creator of Pong
headline: Ted Dabney, a Founder of Atari and a Creator of Pong, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Dabney helped lay the groundwork for the modern video game industry by developing the technology behind an electronic version of table tennis that was an instant hit.

name: José Hawilla
headline: José Hawilla, 74, Central Figure in Soccer Scandal, Dies
abstract: A prominent Brazilian sports marketing executive, he admitted bribing soccer officials to buy the media and marketing rights to major tournaments.

name: Elaine Markson
headline: Elaine Markson, Literary Agent for Feminist Authors, Dies at 87
abstract: One of the few women to own an agency in the 1970s, she built a client roster that included Grace Paley and Andrea Dworkin as well as Salman Rushdie and Abbie Hoffman.

name: Connie Kurtz
headline: Connie Kurtz, Gay Rights Advocate, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Kurtz and her wife, Ruth Berman, were plaintiffs in a New York City lawsuit that helped extend health benefits to domestic partners.

name: Serge Dassault
headline: Serge Dassault, French Aviation Magnate, Is Dead at 93
abstract: He led a vast family-owned business empire that was best known for making civilian and military aircraft. His later years were marred by scandal.

name: Jens Christian Skou
headline: Jens Christian Skou, Nobel Winner for Chemistry, Dies at 99
abstract: Dr. Skou is best known for his discovery in 1957 of a key mechanism in cells that forms the basis for many important functions of the body.

name: Allyn Ann McLerie
headline: Allyn Ann McLerie, Veteran of Broadway, TV and Film, Dies at 91
abstract: She starred in the Broadway hit “Where’s Charley?” in 1948 and went on to TV fame on “The Tony Randall Show” and “The Days and Nights of Molly Dodd.”

name: Ella Brennan
profession: Grande Dame Restaurateur of New Orleans
headline: Ella Brennan, Grande Dame Restaurateur of New Orleans, Dies at 92
abstract: She could not cook and never wanted to, but she was the matriarch of restaurant royalty in a city famous for its food.

name: Irving Sandler
headline: Irving Sandler, Art Historian Who Was Close to Artists, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Sandler drew on his relationships with artists in the New York City scene of the 1950s and ′60s in compiling authoritative histories.

name: Miguel Obando y Bravo
headline: Cardinal Miguel Obando y Bravo, Key Figure in Nicaraguan Turmoil, Dies at 92
abstract: Cardinal Obando initially supported the Sandinista junta, then opposed it, and later had another change of heart, backing President Daniel Ortega.

name: Frank C. Carlucci
profession: Diplomat and Defense Secretary to Reagan
headline: Frank C. Carlucci, Diplomat and Defense Secretary to Reagan, Dies at 87
abstract: In his wide-ranging government career, Mr. Carlucci was an expert budget-whacker and, to presidents and cabinet secretaries, an indispensable No. 2 man.

name: Russell Nype
headline: Russell Nype, Two-Time Tony-Winning Actor, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Nype sang with an ebullient baritone and won Tony Awards for performing alongside Elaine Stritch in “Goldilocks” and Ethel Merman in “Call Me Madam.”

name: Bernard E. Trainor
headline: Bernard E. Trainor, 89, General Turned Military Analyst, Is Dead
abstract: A Marine combat veteran of the Korean and Vietnam Wars, he collaborated on three books that took a critical view of American policy in the wars with Iraq.

name: Jill Ker Conway
headline: Jill Ker Conway, 83, Feminist Author and Smith President, Dies
abstract: Dr. Conway wrote three acclaimed memoirs, starting with her childhood on a sheep ranch in Australia and ending in American academia.

name: Kate Spade
headline: Kate Spade, Whose Handbags Carried Women Into Adulthood, Is Dead at 55
abstract: Ms. Spade built a brand on the appeal of clothes and accessories that made women smile. Her name became a shorthand for the cute, clever bags that were an instant hit.

name: Barbara Kafka
headline: Barbara Kafka, Cookbook Author and Food Writer, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Kafka helped popularize the microwave oven and the food processor for a new generation that wanted speed and convenience in the kitchen.

name: Dwight Clark
profession: Made a Touchdown Catch for the Ages
headline: Dwight Clark, 61, Dies; Made a Touchdown Catch for the Ages
abstract: His last-minute leaping reception in 1982 propelled the San Francisco 49ers toward the first of four N.F.L. championships they would win in the 1980s.

name: Eddy Clearwater
headline: Eddy Clearwater, Chicago Bluesman, Is Dead at 83
abstract: He billed himself as “The Chief” and played music that merged his rural Mississippi upbringing with the aggressive attack of West Side Chicago blues.

name: Mel Weinberg
profession: F.B.I.s Lure in the Abscam Sting
headline: Mel Weinberg, 93, the F.B.I.’s Lure in the Abscam Sting, Dies
abstract: A swindler facing jail, Mr. Weinberg helped snare politicians in the biggest corruption scandal of the 1970s, a case dramatized in “American Hustle.”

name: Joe Pintauro
headline: Joe Pintauro, Playwright Who Had Been a Priest, Dies at 87
abstract: His works on topical subjects like the AIDS crisis and suburban sprawl were widely staged, including by Circle Repertory Company and the Bay Street Theater.

name: Jerry Maren
profession: Sang and Danced as a Munchkin in Oz
headline: Jerry Maren, Who Sang and Danced as a Munchkin in Oz, Dies at 98
abstract: He led the Lollipop Guild in the 1939 classic movie and was the cast’s last surviving dwarf. Behind the scenes, he fought for the dignity of dwarfs.

name: Clarence Fountain
profession: Led the Blind Boys of Alabama
headline: Clarence Fountain, 88, Dies; Led the Blind Boys of Alabama
abstract: Mr. Fountain’s gospel group, which embraced secular sounds without straying from the spiritual, performed all over the world and won multiple Grammys.

name: Gordon M. Ambach
headline: Gordon M. Ambach, New York Education Chief in ’80s, Dies at 83
abstract: He persuaded the New York State Regents to pass more rigorous academic standards for high school graduation.

name: Alexander Askoldov
headline: Alexander Askoldov, Whose Banned Film Was Found, Dies at 85
abstract: Soviet censors refused to release “The Commissar” because of its sympathetic portrayal of a Jewish family, but it resurfaced two decades later to much acclaim.

name: Mary Ann
headline: Overlooked No More: How Mary Ann Shadd Cary Shook Up the Abolitionist Movement
abstract: “We should do more and talk less.” With that statement Shadd Cary questioned the anti-slavery establishment and helped define a new role for black women. But her work didn’t end there.

name: Red Schoendienst
profession: Cardinals Star and Oldest Hall of Famer
headline: Red Schoendienst, Cardinals Star and Oldest Hall of Famer, Dies at 95
abstract: The epitome of a baseball lifer, Schoendienst was a key figure for St. Louis and managed the team for 14 seasons.

name: Philip George
headline: Philip George, Designer of Elegant Restaurants, Dies at 94
abstract: He also helped construct the site of the model American kitchen in Moscow where Richard Nixon had an impromptu debate with Nikita Khrushchev in 1959.

name: Malcolm Morley
headline: Malcolm Morley, Genre-Crossing Artist, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Morley, who discovered his artistic talent while in prison, became a founding figure in both Photorealism and Neo-Expressionism.

name: David Douglas Duncan
headline: David Douglas Duncan, 102, Who Photographed the Reality of War, Dies
abstract: Among the most influential photographers of the 20th century, he was also known for his extensive pictorial record of Pablo Picasso’s life.

name: Anthony Bourdain
headline: Anthony Bourdain, Renegade Chef Who Reported From the World’s Tables, Is Dead at 61
abstract: Mr. Bourdain, who began his career as a chef, redefined the staid genres of food writing and food-tourism shows.

name: Homer A. Neal
headline: Homer A. Neal, Leader in Physics Who Explored Matter, Dies at 75
abstract: Dr. Neal became a particle physicist when few African-Americans entered the field; he went on to lead two large University of Michigan research teams.

name: Ira Berlin
headline: Ira Berlin Is Dead at 77; Groundbreaking Historian of Slavery
abstract: Dr. Berlin’s deeply researched books showed that slavery and its aftermath were far more complex than most people realized.

name: Charlotte Fox
headline: Charlotte Fox, 61, Trailblazing Alpinist and Everest Survivor, Dies
abstract: She defied the fatal blizzard chronicled in “Into Thin Air” and was credited as the first American woman to climb three peaks more than 26,000 feet high.

name: Robert Mandan
headline: Robert Mandan, Philandering Husband on ‘Soap,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Mandan was best known as the patriarch Chester Tate on ABC’s soap-opera satire. But he also played many other roles, including King Lear.

name: Jerry Hopkins
headline: Jerry Hopkins, Biographer of Jim Morrison, Is Dead at 82
abstract: A music writer for Rolling Stone, he had a best seller with “No One Here Gets Out Alive,” which inspired Oliver Stone’s film “The Doors.”

name: Mikhail Ugarov
headline: Moscow Theater Rebels, Husband and Wife, Are Dead
abstract: Mikhail Ugarov and Elena Gremina, who died this spring, founded Teatr.doc, a company that addressed society’s ills and took the Putin government to task.

name: Elena Gremina
headline: Moscow Theater Rebels, Husband and Wife, Are Dead
abstract: Mikhail Ugarov and Elena Gremina, who died this spring, founded Teatr.doc, a company that addressed society’s ills and took the Putin government to task.

name: Lorraine Gordon
profession: Keeper of the Village Vanguard Flame
headline: Lorraine Gordon, Keeper of the Village Vanguard Flame, Dies at 95
abstract: A lifelong jazz fan, Ms. Gordon took over New York’s most venerated jazz nightclub when her husband died in 1989 and had run it ever since.

name: Maria Bueno
headline: Maria Bueno, Brazilian Tennis Star Who Reigned Over 1960s, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Bueno won 19 total Grand Slam titles and, with a pink underskirt and matching underwear at Wimbledon, is said to have prompted the tournament’s all-white clothing rule.

name: Danny Kirwan
profession: Guitarist in Fleetwood Macs Early Years
headline: Danny Kirwan, Guitarist in Fleetwood Mac’s Early Years, Dies at 68
abstract: A thoughtful composer and a talented musician, Mr. Kirwan played a role in the band’s transition from blues to pop-rock before he was fired in 1972.

name: Eunice Gayson
headline: Eunice Gayson, the First Bond Girl, Dies at 90
abstract: The British actress, a star in film and television who was trained to sing, may be best remembered for her role in “Dr. No.”

name: Michael Vollbracht
headline: Michael Vollbracht, Fashion Designer and Illustrator, Dies at 70
abstract: Dressing a host of celebrity clients in his creations, Mr. Vollbracht represented the giddy extravagance and glamour of the late 1970s and early ’80s.

name: Murray Fromson
headline: Murray Fromson, Champion of Press Freedom, Dies at 88
abstract: A well-traveled print and broadcast reporter, he covered the biggest stories of his day, including the Vietnam War and the civil rights movement.

name: Nick Meglin
headline: Nick Meglin, 82, a Mad Magazine Mainstay, Is Dead
abstract: In his half-century at Mad, Mr. Meglin became the chief barometer of whether the magazine’s humor had gone too far — or not far enough.

name: Jon Hiseman
headline: Jon Hiseman, 73, Drummer Who Melded Rock, Jazz and Blues
abstract: A composer and progressive-rock innovator, he led the bands Colosseum and Tempest in a career that began in London in the late 1960s.

name: Maya Jribi
headline: Maya Jribi, Tunisian Fighter for Democracy, Is Dead at 58
abstract: Ms. Jribi, the first woman to lead a Tunisian political party, opposed the influence of Islamists after the revolution that began the Arab Spring.

name: Jalal Mansur Nuriddin
headline: Jalal Mansur Nuriddin, ‘Grandfather of Rap,’ Is Dead at 73
abstract: With the Last Poets, he recited rhythmic verses over conga drumming, speaking to disaffected black youth and helping lay the foundation for hip-hop.

name: Gena Turgel
profession: Holocaust Survivor With a Love Story
headline: Gena Turgel, Holocaust Survivor With a Love Story, Dies at 95
abstract: Among the British soldiers who liberated her and others at the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp was her future husband.

name: Douglas Bennet
headline: Douglas Bennet, Who Led NPR and Wesleyan, Dies at 79
abstract: In his 10 years at National Public Radio, Mr. Bennet brought financial stability to the organization, which had been on shaky fiscal ground.

name: Fannie Farmer
headline: Overlooked No More: Fannie Farmer, Modern Cookery’s Pioneer
abstract: She brought a scientific approach to cooking, taught countless women marketable skills and wrote a cookbook that defined American food for the 20th century.

name: Dorothy Cotton
profession: Rights Champion and Close Aide to King
headline: Dorothy Cotton, Rights Champion and Close Aide to King, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Cotton was a leading campaigner for voting rights in the Deep South and was with Dr. King in Memphis during his final hours.

name: D.J. Fontana
headline: D.J. Fontana, 87, Elvis Presley’s Longtime Drummer, Is Dead
abstract: He was the first drummer in Presley’s band, helping to shape the early sound of rock ’n’ roll, and played with him for 14 years.

name: D.C. Fontana
headline: D.C. Fontana, First Female ‘Star Trek’ Writer, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Fontana, who was part of the “Star Trek” universe from its early days, was best known for her work on Spock, the half-human, half-Vulcan Starfleet officer portrayed by Leonard Nimoy.

name: Anne Donovan
headline: Anne Donovan, a Power in Women’s Basketball, Dies at 56
abstract: A dominating college player in the early 1980s, she went on to win championships as a coach in the W.N.B.A. and the Summer Olympics.

name: Ed Sadlowski
headline: Ed Sadlowski, Fiery Steelworkers Insurgent, Dies at 79
abstract: The Chicagoan became leader of a local when he was 26 but failed to defeat the union brass to win the organization’s national presidency.

name: Yvette Horner
headline: Yvette Horner, France’s Star Accordionist, Is Dead at 95
abstract: She came to fame entertaining in the caravan that accompanies the Tour de France. In recent decades she achieved a kitschy cool.

name: Stephen Reid
headline: Stephen Reid, Gentleman Bank Robber Turned Writer, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Reid, a member of the Stop Watch Gang, later found success as a writer, but he was never able to fully leave his past behind.

name: George N. Leighton
headline: George N. Leighton, Lawyer Who Fought Segregation, Dies at 105
abstract: Mr. Leighton overcame systemic discrimination to serve as a state and federal judge, eventually becoming a fixture in Chicago’s legal community.

name: William Reese
headline: William Reese, Leading Seller of Rare Books, Is Dead at 62
abstract: For nearly 40 years, Mr. Reese shaped tastes, cultivated collectors and advised museums and libraries from his by-appointment-only store in New Haven.

name: Clemens Kalischer
headline: Clemens Kalischer, 97, Refugee Photographer of Humanity, Dies
abstract: He escaped war-torn Europe, had a lucky break in New York and then defined himself by remaining invisible behind the camera.

name: Reinhard Hardegen
headline: Reinhard Hardegen, Who Led U-Boats to America’s Shore, Dies at 105
abstract: “We were the first to be here, and for the first time in this war a German soldier looked upon the coast of the U.S.A.”

name: Martin Bregman
headline: Martin Bregman, Producer of ‘Scarface’ and ‘Serpico,’ Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Bregman was a personal manager to stars like Barbra Streisand and Al Pacino. Later, he worked with the directors Sidney Lumet and Brian De Palma.

name: Gennady Rozhdestvensky
headline: Gennady Rozhdestvensky, a Leading Russian Conductor, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Rozhdestvensky was a tireless promoter of Shostakovich, Schnittke, Gubaidulina and others at home and abroad as one of the best-known Russian conductors.

name: Myrtle Allen
headline: Myrtle Allen, Who Elevated Irish Cooking, Dies at 94
abstract: Using local ingredients, she defined modern Irish cuisine at a restaurant she created in an imposing Georgian house on a 300-acre farm in County Cork.

name: James H. Tully Jr.
profession: Former New York State Tax Chief
headline: James H. Tully Jr., Former New York State Tax Chief, Dies at 87
abstract: He signed a tax pact with Connecticut, sued New Jersey and oversaw New York City’s sales tax revenue in the depths of the fiscal crisis.

name: Walter Bahr
profession: Star of a World Cup Upset
headline: Walter Bahr, a Star of a World Cup Upset, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Later a successful college coach, in 1950 he was a key to what many consider the greatest upset in the history of international soccer.

name: Adel Mahmoud
profession: Was Credited With HPV and Rotavirus Vaccines
headline: Dr. Adel Mahmoud, Who Was Credited With HPV and Rotavirus Vaccines, Dies at 76
abstract: As president of Merck Vaccines, Dr. Mahmoud overcame doubts in developing vaccines against two threats to women and babies: HPV and rotavirus.

name: Bonaldo Giaiotti
headline: Bonaldo Giaiotti, Stalwart Operatic Bass, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Giaiotti, known for his a resonant, majestic sound, appeared on the Met stage more than 400 times in his 30-year-career.

name: Matt Murphy
headline: Matt Murphy, Master of Blues Guitar, Is Dead at 88
abstract: He was best known for his work with the Blues Brothers, but he had established himself as a mainstay of the Chicago scene long before then.

name: Frances Walker-Slocum
headline: Frances Walker-Slocum, 94, Pioneering Pianist and Teacher, Dies
abstract: The first black woman granted tenure at Oberlin College, she was a champion of black composers as well as a celebrated concert performer.

name: Richard Valeriani
headline: Richard Valeriani, Veteran NBC News Correspondent, Dies at 85
abstract: A familiar presence on the “Nightly News,” he covered the civil rights movement, the assassination of John F. Kennedy and Kissinger’s shuttle diplomacy.

name: Peter Thomson
profession: Australian Golfer With 5 British Open Wins
headline: Peter Thomson, 88, Australian Golfer With 5 British Open Wins, Dies
abstract: Thomson emerged in the 1950s as a leading player at a time when Australians had made little impact on international golf.

name: Kazuo Kashio
headline: Kazuo Kashio, a Founder of Casio Computer, Dies at 89
abstract: One of four brothers who organized the company in postwar Japan, he marketed the mini-calculator, the G-Shock watch and other innovations.

name: Stanley Cavell
headline: Stanley Cavell, Prominent Harvard Philosopher, Dies at 91
abstract: Professor Cavell, an expert in so-called ordinary language philosophy, found deep thoughts in popular areas like movies and plays.

name: Amrita Sher-Gil
headline: Overlooked No More: Amrita Sher-Gil, a Pioneer of Indian Art
abstract: With her paintbrush, Sher-Gil explored the sadness felt by people, especially women, in 1930s India, giving voice and validity to their experiences.

name: Hubert Green
profession: Won Golfs U.S. Open Under a Threat
headline: Hubert Green, Who Won Golf’s U.S. Open Under a Threat, Dies at 71
abstract: Green, with 19 tour victories, had an unorthodox style and an unusual story: Winning a major tournament under armed guard after receiving a death threat.

name: Charles Krauthammer
headline: Charles Krauthammer, Prominent Conservative Voice, Dies at 68
abstract: A former liberal, he abandoned psychiatry for journalism and overcame tragedy to become an independent-minded political commentator.

name: Billy Connors
headline: Billy Connors, Yankee Pitching Guru, Is Dead at 76
abstract: In his long career as a coach with the Yankees and other teams, Connors was known for teaching new pitches and rebuilding pitchers’ mechanics.

name: James Gips
profession: Extended Computer Use to the Disabled
headline: James Gips, Who Extended Computer Use to the Disabled, Dies at 72
abstract: He helped develop two technologies that allowed people who could not use a mouse to communicate with a computer, and thus with the world.

name: Diana King
headline: Diana King, a Leading Teacher in Overcoming Dyslexia, Dies at 90
abstract: An author of 15 books, Ms. King founded a summer camp and school to help children with learning disabilities that had often gone undiagnosed.

name: Rebecca Parris
headline: Rebecca Parris, Jazz Singer, Is Dead at 66
abstract: In a four-decade career, Ms. Parris, hailed as Boston’s first lady of jazz, recorded 10 albums and performed with Dizzy Gillespie and Gary Burton.

name: Nina Baym
profession: Brought Novels by Women to Light
headline: Nina Baym, Who Brought Novels by Women to Light, Dies at 82
abstract: Professor Baym was a key early figure in feminist literary history and criticism, excavating forgotten works by female writers.

name: Chuck Vinci
headline: Chuck Vinci, Olympic Champion Weight Lifter, Dies at 85
abstract: Considered one of the greatest weight lifters ever, he won gold medals at the 1956 and 1960 Summer Games, the last to be won by an American man.

name: Dick Leitsch
profession: Sip-In Was a Gay Rights Milestone
headline: Dick Leitsch, Whose ‘Sip-In’ Was a Gay Rights Milestone, Dies at 83
abstract: In 1966, he led an act of civil disobedience in Manhattan that paved the way for the legalization of openly gay bars in New York State.

name: Kim Jong-pil
headline: Kim Jong-pil, Political Kingmaker in South Korea, Dies at 92
abstract: A two-time prime minister who helped three presidents come to power, Mr. Kim never managed to win the top job himself.

name: Vinnie Paul
profession: Pantera Drummer and Heavy Metal Innovator
headline: Vinnie Paul, Pantera Drummer and Heavy Metal Innovator, Is Dead at 54
abstract: A drummer who was “totally capable of hitting hard and rumbling thunder,’’ Mr. Paul also loved food and would invite fans to dine at his home.

name: Donald Hall
profession: Poet Laureate of the Rural Life
headline: Donald Hall, a Poet Laureate of the Rural Life, Is Dead at 89
abstract: The prolific Mr. Hall was also a memoirist, an essayist and a children’s book author, not to mention a passionate Red Sox fan who wrote two books on baseball.

name: Donald J. Hall
headline: Donald J. Hall, 96, Dies; Expanded Hallmark Beyond Greeting Cards
