abstract: After succeeding his father as the company’s top executive, he added new product lines and increased its focus on family-friendly TV shows.

name: Frank Heart
headline: Frank Heart, Who Linked Computers Before the Internet, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Heart’s team built the gateway device for the Arpanet, the precursor to the internet. Data networking was so new then, they made it up as they went.

name: David Goldblatt
headline: David Goldblatt, Acclaimed South African Photographer, Dies at 87
abstract: His pictures, often subtle and reflective, captured the era of apartheid and beyond.

name: Dan Ingram
headline: Dan Ingram, Irreverent Disc Jockey, Is Dead at 83
abstract: In a career that began in the early 1960s at the powerful Top 40 station WABC-AM, Mr. Ingram gleefully mocked songs, singers, sponsors and the weather.

name: Kathy Shaw
headline: Kathy Shaw, Watchdog on Clergy Sexual Abuse, Dies at 72
abstract: As a reporter and blogger, she monitored reports of molestation and uncovered a Vatican document that victims’ advocates said had condoned cover-ups.

name: Joe Jackson
profession: Domineering Father of a Musical Dynasty
headline: Joe Jackson, Domineering Father of a Musical Dynasty, Dies at 89
abstract: His son Michael called him “a managerial genius,” but his abusive behavior alienated Michael, Janet and the rest of his children.

name: Emma Gatewood
profession: First Woman to Conquer the Appalachian Trail Alone
headline: Overlooked No More: Emma Gatewood, First Woman to Conquer the Appalachian Trail Alone
abstract: What the woman known as Grandma Gatewood accomplished in 1955 was remarkable. So is the untold story of what she overcame before that.

name: Daisy Kadibil
headline: Daisy Kadibil, 95, Whose Australia Trek Inspired a Film, Dies
abstract: Seized under an assimilation program, she and two other Aboriginal girls made their way home across hundreds of miles, a feat depicted in “Rabbit-Proof Fence.”

name: Willie Lee Rose
headline: Willie Lee Rose, Historian of Reconstruction, Dies at 91
abstract: Her research undermined the prevailing theory that Northern Republicans and newly enfranchised former slaves created a tragedy for the South.

name: Constance Adams
headline: Constance Adams, Architect of Space Habitats, Is Dead at 53
abstract: She gave up designing skyscrapers to develop structures that would help travelers live on the International Space Station, Mars or the moon.

name: Anne Tolstoi Wallach
profession: Her Advertising Novel Caused a Stir
headline: Anne Tolstoi Wallach, 89, Dies; Her Advertising Novel Caused a Stir
abstract: “Women’s Work,” published in 1981, drew an enormous advance for a first-time novelist. It told of an adwoman who was not unlike its author.

name: Harlan Ellison
headline: Harlan Ellison Dies at 84; Prolific, Irascible (Science) Fiction Writer
abstract: Mr. Ellison’s body of popular literary work — novels, short stories, scripts and much more — was as outsize as his fast-talking, polymathic personality.

name: Miriam Bockman
headline: Miriam Bockman, Groundbreaking Manhattan Democrat, Dies at 86
abstract: The first woman to lead the New York County party, she hailed from the reform wing, serving in the 1970s after Tammany Hall bosses were no more.

name: Jamsheed Marker
headline: Jamsheed Marker, Leading Pakistani Diplomat, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Marker played an important role in negotiations over the Soviet Union’s withdrawal from Afghanistan and was the U.N. envoy to East Timor.

name: Donald Ritchie
headline: Donald Ritchie, Record-Breaking Ultrarunner, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Ritchie set more than a dozen records in grueling runs much longer than a standard marathon, including one that took him the length of the Britain.

name: Arvid Carlsson
headline: Arvid Carlsson, Who Discovered a Treatment for Parkinson’s, Dies at 95
abstract: Dr. Carlsson determined the critical role of the brain chemical dopamine, leading to drugs for Parkinson’s disease and a Nobel Prize.

name: Miriam Griffin
profession: Put Nero in a New Light
headline: Miriam Griffin, Who Put Nero in a New Light, Dies at 82
abstract: A leading classical scholar, Dr. Griffin examined how figures like Nero and Seneca interacted with the political and social systems of their time

name: Liliane Montevecchi
headline: Liliane Montevecchi, Tony Winner for ‘Nine,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Frank Rich called Ms. Montevecchi “a glorious amalgam of music-hall feistiness and balletic grace, with Toulouse-Lautrec shadows about the eyes.”

name: Gillian Lynne
headline: Gillian Lynne, Choreographer of ‘Cats,’ Is Dead at 92
abstract: After a long and successful career as a ballerina, Ms. Lynne found greater fame creating dances for Andrew Lloyd Webber and others.

name: Philippe de Baleine
headline: Philippe de Baleine, Editor and Worldly Writer, Dies at 96
abstract: A war reporter in Indochina, a travel writer in West Africa, a magazine editor, a novelist and said to be the inspiration for a “Tintin” character.

name: Irena Szewinska
headline: Irena Szewinska, Champion Polish Sprinter, Is Dead at 72
abstract: An indefatigable runner and long jumper, “the first lady of Polish sport,” as she was called, set multiple world records and won seven Olympic medals.

name: Alfred Alberts
profession: Unsung Father of a Cholesterol Drug
headline: Alfred Alberts, Unsung Father of a Cholesterol Drug, Dies at 87
abstract: His discovery led to lovastatin, but he shunned the limelight — until he was a patient himself and doctors, learning who he was, treated him “like a rock star.”

name: Henry Butler
headline: Henry Butler, Quintessential New Orleans Pianist, Is Dead at 69
abstract: His music was rooted, encyclopedic, precise and wild as he carried the two-fisted keyboard traditions of his native city to the brink of the avant-garde.

name: Max Fuchs
profession: G.I. Cantor in Historic Battlefield Service
headline: Max Fuchs, G.I. Cantor in Historic Battlefield Service, Is Dead at 96
abstract: On an emotional day in October 1944, Mr. Fuchs sang Sabbath hymns at the first Jewish service to be broadcast on German soil since the rise of Hitler.

name: Claude Lanzmann
headline: Claude Lanzmann, Epic Chronicler of the Holocaust, Dies at 92
abstract: His obsession with the Nazi genocide brought forth “Shoah,” a film recognized as both an important historical record and an original work of art.

name: Eugene Pitt
headline: Eugene Pitt, Doo-Wop Singer With Staying Power, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Pitt was the lead singer of the Jive Five, a group that lasted decades after their 1961 hit “My True Story” by adopting their sound to new genres.

name: Michelle Musler
headline: Michelle Musler, Courtside Perennial in the Garden, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Her four-decade devotion to the Knicks was legend — she’d even straighten Jeff Van Gundy’s tie — though she wasn’t too happy about those ticket prices.

name: Ed Schultz
headline: Ed Schultz, Blunt-Spoken Political Talk-Show Host, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Schultz was the host of a conservative radio show before moving to the left and joining MSNBC in 2009. In recent years his politics shifted again.

name: Gudrun Burwitz
headline: Gudrun Burwitz, Ever-Loyal Daughter of Himmler, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Though her father was an architect of the Holocaust, she sought to rehabilitate his name while providing aid to former Nazis in postwar Germany.

name: Ralph Paige
headline: Ralph Paige, Champion of Black Farmers, Dies at 74
abstract: As head of the Federation of Southern Cooperatives, Mr. Paige fought to save black farmers’ land and win compensation to redress government discrimination.

name: Steve Ditko
headline: Steve Ditko, Influential Comic-Book Artist Who Helped Create Spider-Man, Dies at 90
abstract: Best known for his role in the creation of Spider-Man and noted for his cinematic storytelling, he had a mystique rare among industry superstars.

name: Frank Ramsey
profession: First Among Sixth Men in the N.B.A
headline: Frank Ramsey, First Among ‘Sixth Men’ in the N.B.A., Dies at 86
abstract: Playing with the Boston Celtics, Ramsey pioneered a versatile role in pro basketball while with seven championship teams, earning him a place in the sport’s Hall of Fame.

name: Tab Hunter
headline: Tab Hunter, 86, 1950s Hollywood Heartthrob, Is Dead
abstract: One of the last products of the studio system, Mr. Hunter made an unlikely comeback in 1981 in the quirky and very un-Hollywood “Polyester.”

name: Oliver Knussen
profession: Where the Wild Things Are Composer
headline: Oliver Knussen, ‘Where the Wild Things Are’ Composer, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Knussen was 15 when he led the London Symphony Orchestra in his First Symphony. He matured into a major composer, conductor and mentor.

name: Carrington
headline: Lord Carrington, 99, Former British Foreign Secretary, Dies
abstract: He held senior posts under Conservative prime ministers from Churchill to Thatcher, and led NATO in the last years of the Cold War.

name: Robert D. Ray
headline: Robert D. Ray, Centrist G.O.P. Governor of Iowa, Dies at 89
abstract: In his five terms, Mr. Ray embraced progressive policies. In 1975 invited thousands of Southeast Asian refugees to settle in his state.

name: Price Cobbs
headline: Price Cobbs, Who Helped Define ‘Black Rage,’ Is Dead at 89
abstract: Dr. Cobbs, a psychiatrist, co-wrote a high-profile 1968 book that linked the anger of that decade to the lingering effects of slavery.

name: Robby Müller
headline: Robby Müller, Inventive Cinematographer, Is Dead at 78
abstract: His distinctive use of lighting and artful approach to composition were consistent elements of films by Wim Wenders, Jim Jarmusch and other directors.

name: Hans Günter Winkler
headline: Hans Günter Winkler, Olympic Champion Equestrian, Dies at 91
abstract: Winkler, a dominant force in show jumping for decades, won seven Olympic medals. His best performances were astride a singular mare named Halla.

name: Bradford Smith
headline: Bradford Smith, Who Showed Postcards From Outer Space, Dies at 86
abstract: As head of the camera team for the Voyager mission, Dr. Smith was humanity’s tour guide to the solar system.

name: Bill Watrous
headline: Bill Watrous, Trombonist and Bandleader, Is Dead at 79
abstract: In addition to being a busy studio musician, Mr. Watrous released more than a dozen albums under his own name and for a while led a jazz-rock big band.

name: Patricia Schiller
headline: Patricia Schiller, a Sex-Education Pioneer, Dies at 104
abstract: Switching from a law career, she founded a professional association for sex counselors and therapists.

name: Bette Nesmith Graham
headline: Overlooked No More: Bette Nesmith Graham, Who Invented Liquid Paper
abstract: A struggling secretary created a concoction that relieved her and others around the world from the pressure of perfection.

name: Alan Johnson
headline: Alan Johnson, 81, ‘Springtime for Hitler’ Choreographer, Dies
abstract: A former dancer, Mr. Johnson collaborated with Mel Brooks on several movies and once asked him, “‘Oh my God, are we allowed to show this?”

name: Lindy Remigino
headline: Lindy Remigino, Olympic Champion Runner, Is Dead at 87
abstract: In a monumental upset, Remigino won the 1952 gold medal in the 100-meter dash with no more than six inches separating first place from fourth.

name: Tom Gallagher
headline: Tom Gallagher, Diplomat Who Became a Gay Activist, Dies at 77
abstract: He began his career having to hide the fact that he was gay. He ended it celebrated as a pioneer.

name: Jeremy Gold
headline: Jeremy Gold, Actuary Who Warned of Pension Crisis, Dies at 75
abstract: Concluding that actuarial standards for pensions were flawed, Mr. Gold embarked on a 30-year mission “to save my profession.”

name: Nathaniel Reed
headline: Nathaniel Reed, 84, Champion of Florida’s Environment, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Reed, a Republican, helped turn the Endangered Species Act into law while serving as an assistant secretary of the Interior in the 1970s.

name: Richard Elden
headline: Richard Elden, Innovative Hedge Fund Investor, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Elden adopted a diversified approach to investing in hedge funds, opening a new area of American finance.

name: Nancy Barbato Sinatra
profession: Idols First Wife and Lasting Confidante
headline: Nancy Barbato Sinatra, 101, an Idol’s First Wife and Lasting Confidante, Dies
abstract: For nearly half a century after her divorce from Frank Sinatra, she remained his cherished and devoted friend.

name: William McBride
headline: William McBride, Who Warned About Thalidomide, Dies at 91
abstract: Proclaimed a hero, Dr. McBride was later embroiled in lengthy controversies over faulty research.

name: Len Chappell
headline: Len Chappell, 77, College All-American and N.B.A. All-Star, Dies
abstract: Chappell led Wake Forest to the Final Four in 1962 and was the top scorer for the Knicks in 1963-64, averaging more than 17 points per game.

name: Les Lieber
profession: Served Jazz to the Lunch Crowd
headline: Les Lieber, Who Served Jazz to the Lunch Crowd, Dies at 106
abstract: His Jazz at Noon series, which ran for more than 45 years, featured skilled amateur players alongside well-known guest professionals.

name: Annabelle Neilson
headline: Annabelle Neilson, Muse of Alexander McQueen, Dies at 49
abstract: The former model and reality TV personality was a fixture of the 1990s celebrity party scene in Britain, and a confidante to some of its biggest stars.

name: Ann Hopkins
profession: Struck an Early Blow to the Glass Ceiling
headline: Ann Hopkins, Who Struck an Early Blow to the Glass Ceiling, Dies at 74
abstract: Her bosses at the office saw her as too “macho” and “aggressive” to be made a partner. The Supreme Court saw her as a victim of gender stereotyping.

name: Alan S. Rabson
headline: Dr. Alan S. Rabson, Influential Cancer Researcher, Is Dead at 92
abstract: A longtime leader of the National Cancer Institute, he was known for his willingness to help anyone with a cancer diagnosis seeking advice or a referral.

name: Marcia Chambers
headline: Marcia Chambers, 78, Who Exposed Discrimination in Golf, Dies
abstract: A longtime legal affairs reporter, Ms. Chambers turned her attention in the 1990s to exclusionary practices at private country clubs.

name: John Stormer
profession: None Dare Call It Treason Author
headline: John Stormer, ‘None Dare Call It Treason’ Author, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Stormer’s self-published 1964 book, warning of a Communist conspiracy threatening America, became a grass-roots phenomenon for the right wing.

name: Beatrice Tinsley
headline: Overlooked No More: Beatrice Tinsley, Astronomer Who Saw the Course of the Universe
abstract: An insurgent who challenged the academic establishment and became a foremost expert on the aging of galaxies, she was eventually forced to choose between family and career.

name: Robert Keating
headline: Robert Keating, Judge Who Backed Jail Alternatives, Dies at 76
abstract: As a New York court administrator, he oversaw the introduction of the Midtown Community Court, a way to avoid sending low-level offenders to jail.

name: Yvonne Blake
headline: Yvonne Blake, Award-Winning Costume Designer, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Ms. Blake won an Oscar for “Nicholas and Alexandra,” but her most recognizable work was the superhero and supervillain ensembles she created for “Superman.”

name: Manny Ycaza
headline: Manny Ycaza, Hall of Fame Jockey, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Known for an aggressive style that earned him several suspensions, he was among the first Latin American jockeys to have success in the United States.

name: Gary Beach
headline: Gary Beach, Tony Winner for ‘The Producers,’ Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Beach’s many Broadway roles also included Lumière, the genial candelabra, in the original cast of “Beauty and the Beast.”

name: Marion Woodman
headline: Marion Woodman, Explorer of the Feminine Mind, Dies at 89
abstract: A Jungian psychoanalyst, she wrote popular books and lectured on mythical feminine archetypes and the primal, unconscious elements of feminine identity.

name: Auguste Clape
headline: Auguste Clape, Whose Hillside Vineyards Rose to Fame, Dies at 93
abstract: Growing syrah grapes in the Rhône Valley wine country of France, he helped elevate the little-known appellation Cornas, named after a nearby village.

name: Adrian Cronauer
headline: Adrian Cronauer, ‘Good Morning, Vietnam’ D.J., Dies at 79
abstract: Although the character embodied by Robin Williams was largely a fictional construct, Mr. Cronauer’s signature wake-up line was real.

name: Jean-Louis Tauran
headline: Jean-Louis Tauran, Vatican’s Interfaith Point Man, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Cardinal Tauran championed dialogue among religions and spoke of a “clash of forms of ignorance and radicalism.”

name: Barry Mills
profession: Brutal Leader of Racist Prison Gang
headline: Barry Mills, Brutal Leader of Racist Prison Gang, Dies at 70
abstract: The head of the Aryan Brotherhood, he was linked to murders, drug dealing, prostitution, racial warfare and more in a life spent mostly behind bars.

name: Shinobu Hashimoto
headline: Shinobu Hashimoto, Writer of Towering Kurosawa Films, Is Dead at 100
abstract: His first film, “Rashomon,” became a touchstone of world cinema. He went on to collaborate on celebrated pictures like “Ikiru” and “Seven Samurai.”

name: Stephen Saban
profession: Chronicler (and Arbiter) of New York Night Life
headline: Stephen Saban, Chronicler (and Arbiter) of New York Night Life, Dies at 72
abstract: In his column-writing heyday in the late 1970s and ’80s, Mr. Saban was a star maker who became a star himself among the underground cognoscenti.

name: Madeleine Kamman
profession: Gave Americans a Taste of France
headline: Madeleine Kamman, 87, Who Gave Americans a Taste of France, Dies
abstract: Schooled in Paris, she was a strong-willed teacher of traditional French cuisine for modern tastes and an influential chef and restaurateur.

name: Jonathan Gold
headline: Jonathan Gold, Food Critic Who Celebrated L.A.’s Cornucopia, Dies at 57
abstract: A gourmand who explored Los Angeles’s immigrant communities, taco carts and chic restaurants, Mr. Gold won renown in the culinary world and a Pulitzer Prize for criticism.

name: Angela Bowen
headline: Angela Bowen, Dance Teacher and Gay Activist, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Her dance school in New Haven influenced many, and her outspokenness as a black lesbian feminist influenced many more.

name: Robert Blizzard
headline: Robert Blizzard, Who Gave Children Hormones to Grow, Dies at 94
abstract: A pediatric pioneer, he liked to say he had added 11 miles to the height of the U.S. population. But growth hormones were later banned and replaced.

name: Burton Richter
headline: Burton Richter, a Nobel Winner for Plumbing Matter, Dies at 87
abstract: He shared the 1976 physics prize for the discovery of an unexpected particle, a building block of the universe, in a high-speed accelerator he had designed.

name: Rene Portland
headline: Rene Portland, 65, Longtime Penn State Basketball Coach, Dies
abstract: She won more than 600 games over 27 seasons. But her reputation was tarnished when she was accused of discriminating against lesbian players.

name: Aiko Herzig Yoshinaga
headline: Aiko Herzig Yoshinaga, Critic of Wartime Internment, Is Dead at 93
abstract: An amateur researcher, she discovered evidence that evacuating Japanese-Americans was motivated by “race prejudice,” not by military necessity.

name: Lincoln Brower
headline: Lincoln Brower, Champion of the Monarch Butterfly, Dies at 86
abstract: Dr. Brower was a leading expert on the monarch and its awe-inspiring migratory journey, which could cover thousands of miles.

name: Christine Nöstlinger
headline: Christine Nöstlinger, Clear-Eyed Children’s Book Author, Dies at 81
abstract: An author who avoided sentimentality and took on contemporary issues of social justice in books that were translated into 30 languages.

name: Anne Olivier Bell
headline: Anne Olivier Bell, Editor of Virginia Woolf Diaries, Dies at 102
abstract: Married to Woolf’s nephew, she was a last link to the famed Bloomsbury Group, and also part of the wartime art-preservation unit known as the Monuments Men.

name: Sergio Marchionne
headline: Sergio Marchionne, Who Revived Fiat and Chrysler, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Marchionne, who merged the two carmakers, pulling them back from the brink of collapse, led the combined Fiat Chrysler until just a few days ago.

name: Guy V. Molinari
profession: Power Broker in New York and Beyond
headline: Guy V. Molinari, Power Broker in New York and Beyond, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Congressman, assemblyman, Staten Island borough president: Even more, he was a Republican kingpin with wide reach in a largely Democratic city.

name: Cindy Joseph
headline: Cindy Joseph, a Model Who Embraced Her Age, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Ms. Joseph became a model at 49, after decades as a makeup artist, and in 2010 she started a cosmetics company to complement, not conceal, a woman’s age.

name: Raymond Hunthausen
headline: Raymond Hunthausen, Liberal Archbishop Rebuked by Rome, Dies at 96
abstract: He was temporarily stripped of some powers by the Vatican in a struggle with conservatives that deepened a rift with American bishops.

name: Edmonia Lewis
headline: Overlooked No More: Edmonia Lewis, Sculptor of Worldwide Acclaim
abstract: As an artist she transcended constraints, and as a woman of color, she confronted a society that wished to categorize her.

name: Oksana Shachko
headline: Oksana Shachko, a Founder of Feminist Protest Movement, Dies at 31
abstract: She was a key member of Femen, whose members held topless demonstrations against authoritarian leaders and the exploitation of women.

name: Kimishige Ishizaka
headline: Dr. Kimishige Ishizaka, Who Found Allergy Link, Dies at 92
abstract: Working with his wife, he identified an antibody that, in allergic individuals, produces excess amounts of histamine, which makes them sneeze.

name: Elbert Howard
headline: Elbert Howard, a Founder of the Black Panthers, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Howard often acted as spokesman for the party during incendiary events. But he was also adept at organizing community programs.

name: Franz Beyer
headline: Franz Beyer, Who Revised Mozart’s Requiem, Is Dead at 96
abstract: In restoring a work left unfinished at the composer’s death, he sought to achieve “a closer and more conscious understanding of the Mozartean spirit.”

name: Alene Duerk
headline: Alene Duerk, Navy’s First Female Rear Admiral, Is Dead at 98
abstract: She enlisted in the nursing corps during World War II, not expecting to make a career out of the Navy. But in 1972, she broke a barrier.

name: Bill Loud
profession: Father of TVs An American Family
headline: Bill Loud, the Father of TV’s ‘An American Family,’ Is Dead at 97
abstract: In 1973, the real-life domestic dramas of Mr. Loud and his family were presented in 12 hourlong episodes now considered the genesis of reality television.

name: Mai Skaf
headline: Mai Skaf, Syrian Actress Who Defied Assad Regime, Dies at 49
abstract: Ms. Skaf fled to Paris after being arrested and harassed and receiving death threats when she spoke out against the Syrian government.

name: Hatidza Mehmedovic
profession: Spoke Out for Bosnia Massacre Victims
headline: Hatidza Mehmedovic, 65, Dies; Spoke Out for Bosnia Massacre Victims
abstract: She helped found Mothers of Srebrenica, seeking justice for the 8,000 men and boys — her husband and sons among them — killed by Serb forces in 1995.

name: Maryon P. Allen
profession: Made a Senator by Husbands Death
headline: Maryon P. Allen, Made a Senator by Husband’s Death, Dies at 92
abstract: One of only two female U.S. senators from Alabama, she was picked to fill a suddenly vacant seat but lost a bid to keep it, undone perhaps by her outspokenness.

name: Judith Appelbaum
headline: Judith Appelbaum, a Guide for Would-Be Authors, Dies at 78
abstract: A long career in the publishing world was highlighted by her influential and enduring book “How to Get Happily Published.”

name: Doris Arndt
headline: Doris Arndt, Celebrated Animal Trainer, Is Dead at 88
abstract: A rare female performer in a field dominated by men, she topped European circus bills in the 1950s and ’60s with an act that featured a dozen polar bears.

name: Ron Dellums
profession: Unrelenting in Congress, He Upheld Lefts Ideals
headline: Ron Dellums, 82, Dies; Unrelenting in Congress, He Upheld Left’s Ideals
abstract: Arriving in Washington as an antiwar firebrand, he became a House leader as head of the Armed Services Committee and the Congressional Black Caucus.

name: Kathy Kriger
profession: Madame Rick at Her Casablanca Cafe
headline: Kathy Kriger, ‘Madame Rick’ at Her Casablanca Cafe, Is Dead at 72
abstract: A former American diplomat, she created a real Rick’s Cafe, evoking the cinematic Moroccan gin joint made famous by Bogart and Bergman.

name: Herman Shine
profession: One of the Few to Escape Auschwitz
headline: Herman Shine, One of the Few to Escape Auschwitz, Dies at 95
abstract: He and his best friend fled a death camp with the help of a Polish civilian and the woman he would marry. He was one of the last surviving escapees.

name: Pat de Groot
profession: Seascape Painter and Doyenne of the Dunes
headline: Pat de Groot, Seascape Painter and Doyenne of the Dunes, Dies at 88
abstract: In Provincetown, at Cape Cod’s tip, John Waters called her “bohemian royalty,” a barefooted artist, party giver, salon host and emblem of a bygone day.

name: Maureen Turlish
headline: Sister Maureen Turlish, a Voice for Sex Abuse Victims, Dies at 79
abstract: Galvanized by scandal in the Catholic Church, she sought compensation for survivors, the ouster of abusive clergymen and accountability by the hierarchy.

name: Tony Cloninger
headline: Tony Cloninger, Pitcher Remembered for His Bat, Dies at 77
abstract: He was the only pitcher ever to hit two grand slams in a single game, for the Braves in 1966. He later won four World Series rings as a Yankees coach.

name: Mary Jane McCaffree Monroe
headline: Mary Jane McCaffree Monroe, Protocol Authority, Dies at 106
abstract: As a top aide to Mamie Eisenhower, she kept the White House social scene organized. Then, with a co-author, she wrote the book on the subject.

name: Patricia Cohen
headline: Patricia Cohen, Who Tracked Mental Health of Children, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Cohen oversaw one of the longest-running studies of its kind, tracing the mental well-being of youngsters as they grew into adolescence.

name: Nikolai Volkoff
profession: Soviet Villain in the Wrestling Ring
headline: Nikolai Volkoff, Soviet Villain in the Wrestling Ring, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Volkoff, played by Josip Peruzovic, would belt out the Soviet Union’s national anthem before matches, though he had detested life under Communist rule.

name: Howard Felsher
headline: Howard Felsher, Game Show Whiz Who Overcame Scandal, Dies at 90
abstract: After admitting to Congress that he had rigged a quiz show, he found redemption as a game show doctor, lifting ratings of daytime fare like “Family Feud.”

name: Clara Lemlich Shavelson
headline: Overlooked No More: Clara Lemlich Shavelson, Crusading Leader of Labor Rights
abstract: Shavelson ignited a huge strike by women garment workers that helped galvanize the labor movement. She went on to fight for suffrage and tenants’ rights.

name: Vladimir Voinovich
headline: Vladimir Voinovich, Dissident Russian Writer, Dies at 85
abstract: His satires were not well received by the Soviet authorities, and in 1980 he thought it best to live in the West until things thawed out.

name: Charles Hamlen
profession: Classical Music Manager With a Cause
headline: Charles Hamlen, Classical Music Manager With a Cause, Dies at 75
abstract: He co-founded one of the leading classical music management agencies, IMG Artists, and then left it behind to raise money to help people with AIDS.

name: Jacques Wirtz
headline: Jacques Wirtz, Innovative Landscape Designer, Dies at 93
abstract: From Paris to Japan, he transformed gardens and grounds with the eye of a sculptor and the insight of a horticulturalist.

name: Michael Sheehan
headline: Michael Sheehan, Prescient Counterterrorism Expert, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Sheehan was said to have urged the Clinton White House in 1998 to focus on thwarting Osama bin Laden. His warning, an official said, went unheeded.

name: Betty Miles
headline: Betty Miles, Whose Children’s Books Tackled Sexism, Dies at 90
abstract: As a woman of the 1950s, she said, she felt “presumptuous” about wanting a writing career, but overcame her qualms to carve out a successful one.

name: Art Lee
headline: Art Lee, Fly-Fishing Virtuoso and Writer, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Lee was a Catskills fixture whose reputation as an angler spread far and wide. He once took Jimmy Carter fishing and wrote a whole book on a knot.

name: Rick Genest
profession: Tattooed Zombie Boy in Lady Gaga Video
headline: Rick Genest, Tattooed ‘Zombie Boy’ in Lady Gaga Video, Dies at 32
abstract: Mr. Genest, whose tattoos covered his entire body, participated in the 2011 Lady Gaga music video “Born This Way.”

name: Christopher Gibbs
headline: Christopher Gibbs, Avatar of ‘Swinging London,’ Dies at 80
abstract: An antiques dealer and arbiter of eclectic taste, he popularized the 1960s Peacock Revolution in fashion and “distressed bohemian” in interior design.

name: Mary Carlisle
headline: Mary Carlisle, Depression-Era Movie Ingénue, Is Dead at 104
abstract: Discovered at 14 in a Hollywood commissary, she went on to appear in 50 movies, including three with Bing Crosby, and was a darling of the press.

name: Patricia Hermes
headline: Patricia Hermes, Whose Children’s Books Had Serious Side, Dies at 82
abstract: No fairy tales, thank you: Her many books dealt with death, war, slavery and other harsh realities and looked at history from contrasting viewpoints.

name: Douglas Grindstaff
headline: Douglas Grindstaff, ‘Star Trek’ Sound Whiz, Dies at 87
abstract: He helped create the beeps, clinks and whooshes of the original 1960s series on his way to an Emmy-winning career.

name: Nancy Tuckerman
profession: Trusted Aide of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis
headline: Nancy Tuckerman, 89, Trusted Aide of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, Dies
abstract: An old friend, she was White House social secretary in tragic times, then continued to advise the family for decades, after Mrs. Kennedy became Mrs. Onassis.

name: Winston Ntshona
headline: Winston Ntshona, Tony-Winning South African Actor, Dies at 76
abstract: After a Broadway run, Mr. Ntshona was jailed in his home country for performing in a play he had written with Athol Fugard and the actor John Kani.

name: Tomasz Stanko
headline: Tomasz Stanko, Ruminative Jazz Trumpeter, Dies at 76
abstract: A bandleader who played with a melancholic air, he was Poland’s leading jazz musician, honored across Europe and included in a Smithsonian anthology.

name: H.F. Lenfest
profession: Philanthropist and Owner of Philadelphias Newspapers
headline: H.F. Lenfest, Philanthropist and Owner of Philadelphia’s Newspapers, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Lenfest made $1 billion in the cable industry and gave most of it away to arts, education and journalism institutions.

name: Charlotte Rae
headline: Charlotte Rae of ‘The Facts of Life’ and ‘Diff’rent Strokes’ Dies at 92
abstract: A fixture on Broadway and television for six decades, the actress found her greatest success as a warmhearted, wisecracking housemother in two sitcoms.

name: Joël Robuchon
headline: Joël Robuchon, a French Chef Festooned With Stars, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Classically trained but always inventive, he dazzled the culinary world, sweeping up Michelin stars wherever he set foot with a new restaurant.

name: Amy Meselson
headline: Amy Meselson, Lawyer Who Defended Young Immigrants, Dies at 46
abstract: She intervened to save an 18-year-old Senegalese student who had won a prize for robotics in East Harlem but was facing deportation.

name: Antonio Dias
headline: Antonio Dias, Brazilian Artist Who Poked the Generals, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Dias took aim at the 1960s ruling junta with trenchant works of bright colors, graphic immediacy and world weariness. He later went into exile.

name: Paul Laxalt
profession: Senator From Nevada and Reagan Confidant
headline: Paul Laxalt, Senator From Nevada and Reagan Confidant, Dies at 96
abstract: Known for a firm conservatism conveyed courteously, Mr. Laxalt developed a relationship with Ronald Reagan when they were governors of neighboring states.

name: Margaret Heckler
headline: Margaret Heckler, Lawmaker and Reagan Health Secretary, Dies at 87
abstract: She championed women’s rights in Congress and ran the Department of Health and Human Services until she was forced out and appointed ambassador to Ireland.

name: Tony Bullimore
headline: Tony Bullimore, Saved in Dramatic Ocean Rescue, Dies at 79
abstract: In 1997, he spent four days in an air pocket of his overturned boat after encountering a storm during an around-the-world race.

name: Robert Silman
headline: Robert Silman, Engineer Who Saved Fallingwater, Dies at 83
abstract: He was involved in many major restoration and salvation projects, including Carnegie Hall, the Ellis Island museum and the World Trade Center staircase.

name: Stan Mikita
profession: Hockey Hall of Famer Lifted Blackhawks
headline: Stan Mikita, 78, Dies; Hockey Hall of Famer Lifted Blackhawks
abstract: A nine-time All-Star, he spend his entire 22-season career with Chicago and teamed with Bobby Hull to revive the floundering franchise in the 1960s.

name: Julia Sand
headline: Overlooked No More: Julia Sand, Whose Letters Inspired a President
abstract: A housebound New York woman sought to influence the heart of Chester A. Arthur at a time when no one believed in him.

name: Alan Rabinowitz
headline: Alan Rabinowitz, Conservationist of Wild Cats, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Rabinowitz made it his life’s mission to preserve lions, tigers, leopards and cheetahs after childhood encounters with a jaguar at the Bronx Zoo

name: Glen Roven
headline: Glen Roven, Emmy-Winning Composer and Conductor, Dies at 61
abstract: With little formal training, he made his debut on Broadway when he was 19 and became a prolific presence on TV and in concert halls around the world.

name: Lorrie Collins
headline: Lorrie Collins, Dynamic Rockabilly Singer, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Ms. Collins and her brother, Larry, billed as the Collins Kids, were stars before they were teenagers, regularly featured on television variety shows.

name: Richard Jarecki
headline: Richard Jarecki, Doctor Who Conquered Roulette, Dies at 86
abstract: He found a million-dollar edge by closely observing and identifying slight biases in roulette wheels, becoming “a menace to every casino in Europe.”

name: Robert Newman
headline: Dr. Robert Newman, Apostle of Methadone Treatment, Dies at 80
abstract: Since 1970, when he established a major treatment program in New York, Dr. Newman emerged as a global expert on opioid addiction.

name: Jarrod Lyle
headline: Jarrod Lyle, Golfer Who Played On Despite Cancer, Dies at 36
abstract: An Australian who competed in more than 120 P.G.A. tournaments, he was recognized for his persistence in returning to golf after bouts with leukemia.

name: Takeshi Onaga
profession: Critic of U.S. Bases as Okinawa Governor
headline: Takeshi Onaga, Critic of U.S. Bases as Okinawa Governor, Dies at 67
abstract: A conservative who defied Japan’s ruling party, he opposed not just the relocation of a Marine base on the island but the entire American military presence there.

name: Anita Miller
headline: Anita Miller, Who Battled John Cheever’s Family, Dies at 91
abstract: An author and publisher with an eclectic bent, she was a founder of Academy Chicago, which sold feminist, mystery, literary and children’s books.

name: Burt Britton
profession: Book Lover if Ever There Was One
headline: Burt Britton, a Book Lover if Ever There Was One, Dies at 84
abstract: He had intimate knowledge of every shelf at the Strand, was a partner in another bookstore and, when not reading, collected celebrities’ self portraits.

name: A.W. Richard Sipe
profession: Leading Expert on Clergy Sex Abuse
headline: A.W. Richard Sipe, a Leading Expert on Clergy Sex Abuse, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Sipe spent decades researching priestly celibacy and the roots of the sexual abuse of minors by clergymen. He became a powerful advocate for victims.

name: Patrick Williams
profession: Composer as Heard on TV (and Beyond)
headline: Patrick Williams, 79, Composer as Heard on TV (and Beyond), Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Williams, whose approach blended jazz, classical and pop elements, provided music for film, television and his own award-winning records.

name: Arvonne Fraser
headline: Arvonne Fraser, Who Spoke Out on Women’s Issues, Dies at 92
abstract: Whether in her home state of Minnesota or in Washington, Ms. Fraser urged women to fight for their rights.

name: Anya Krugovoy Silver
headline: Anya Krugovoy Silver, Poetic Voice on Mortality, Dies at 49
abstract: “My joy exists with pain,” Ms. Silver wrote. Her poems moved in a new direction after she received a diagnosis of breast cancer in 2004.

name: V.S. Naipaul
headline: V.S. Naipaul, Who Explored Colonialism Through Unsparing Books, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Naipaul, who was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2001, wrote about the liberation movements that swept across Africa and the Caribbean, where he was born.

name: Bui Tin
headline: Bui Tin, Colonel Who Accepted South Vietnam’s Surrender, Dies at 90
abstract: He had a prominent role in the Vietnam War’s final moments, but he later fled the country and became an unlikely critic of its ruling Communist Party.

name: Melanie Kaye/Kantrowitz
headline: Melanie Kaye/Kantrowitz, Feminist, Activist and Author, Dies at 72
abstract: She helped shape new ways of thinking about Jewish identity, including challenging the Zionist notion that Israel must be honored as the homeland.

name: Muthuvel Karunanidhi
headline: Muthuvel Karunanidhi, 94, Screenwriter Turned Politician, Dies
abstract: India’s longest-serving legislator, he challenged the caste system’s hold on his country, first in cinema and later in politics.

name: Fakir Musafar
headline: Fakir Musafar, Whose ‘Body Play’ Went to Extremes, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Musafar, a performance artist, practiced rituals like piercing and branding, believing they expanded consciousness and led to catharsis.

name: Larry Meachum
headline: Larry Meachum, Prison Reformer Who Led Prisons, Dies at 79
abstract: He oversaw corrections systems in three states, promoting programs to improve life for inmates while being accused in some quarters of “coddling” them.

name: Amber Tatro
profession: Suit Gave Rights to Disabled Students
headline: Amber Tatro, Whose Suit Gave Rights to Disabled Students, Dies at 42
abstract: Born with spina bifida, she was at the heart of a case seeking services that it said school districts were required to provide. The Supreme Court agreed.

name: Katie Cannon
profession: Lifted Black Womens Perspective in Theology
headline: Katie Cannon, 68, Dies; Lifted Black Women’s Perspective in Theology
abstract: In her teaching and in books like “Black Womanist Ethics,” Dr. Cannon sought to escape the white- and male-centered views of religion.

name: Moshe Mizrahi
profession: Won an Oscar for Madame Rosa
headline: Moshe Mizrahi, 86, Who Won an Oscar for ‘Madame Rosa,’ Is Dead
abstract: Born to a Jewish family in Egypt, Mr. Mizrahi was the first Israeli filmmaker to win an Academy Award and is still the only one.

name: Herbert Sperling
profession: Drug Kingpin Tied to French Connection Case
headline: Herbert Sperling, Drug Kingpin Tied to French Connection Case, Dies at 79
abstract: He was serving a life sentence for his role in importing heroin and was accused of plotting to murder the mastermind of the theft of drugs from the police.

name: Sissieretta Jones
headline: Overlooked No More: Sissieretta Jones, a Soprano Who Shattered Racial Barriers
abstract: She was the first African-American woman to headline a concert at Carnegie Hall, but she didn’t care for her stage name, “the Black Patti,” which compared her to a white diva.

name: John Smyth
profession: Christian Camp Leader Accused of Beatings
headline: John Smyth, Christian Camp Leader Accused of Beatings, Dies at 77
abstract: He left Britain after an inquiry found he had brutally beaten young men at elite camps. But he was never prosecuted and went on to open similar camps in Africa.

name: Morgana King
headline: Morgana King, Jazz Singer and ‘Godfather’ Actor, Is Dead at 87
abstract: A well-regarded singing career brought her some fame, but probably not as much as her small part as Vito Corleone’s wife.

name: Atal Bihari Vajpayee
headline: Atal Bihari Vajpayee, Former Prime Minister of India, Dies at 93
abstract: As India’s leader from 1998 to 2004, Mr. Vajpayee ended a long moratorium on nuclear tests but also eased tensions with Pakistan and built closer ties with United States.

name: Aretha Franklin
headline: Aretha Franklin, Indomitable ‘Queen of Soul,’ Dies at 76
abstract: With hits like “Respect” and “Chain of Fools,” she defined a female archetype: sensual and strong, long-suffering but ultimately indomitable.

name: Isamu Shibayama
headline: Isamu Shibayama Dies at 88, His Quest for Reparations Unfulfilled
abstract: His family was deported from Peru to an American wartime internment camp, setting him on a mission to have the wrongs redressed. He died still waiting.

name: Johnny Kline
headline: Johnny Kline, Globetrotter Turned Advocate, Is Dead at 86
abstract: After overcoming a heroin addiction, he became a drug abuse counselor and founded an organization to help long-forgotten black basketball players.

name: John Glines
profession: Helped Bring Torch Song to Broadway
headline: John Glines, Who Helped Bring ‘Torch Song’ to Broadway, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Glines was a producer who was committed to plays with gay themes and instrumental in bringing them into the mainstream.

name: Miriam Nelson
headline: Miriam Nelson, 98, Golden Age Dancer and Choreographer, Dies
abstract: A Broadway hoofer who went to Hollywood to tutor William Holden, Kim Novak, Ingrid Bergman, Jerry Lewis, Tuesday Weld and Jane Fonda, to name a few.

name: Louis Gignac
profession: Styles Took the Fuss Out of Hair
headline: Louis Gignac, Whose Styles Took the Fuss Out of Hair, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Gignac, promoting wash-and-wear styles, ran a New York salon that attracted clients like Gloria Vanderbilt, Elizabeth Taylor and Catherine Deneuve.

name: Kofi Annan
headline: Kofi Annan, Who Redefined the U.N., Dies at 80
abstract: Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2001, he projected himself and his organization as the world’s conscience and moral arbiter, despite a series of failures and scandals.

name: David McReynolds
headline: David McReynolds, Socialist Activist Who Ran for President, Dies at 88
abstract: His pacifist work spanned decades and several wars, and he twice ran for the White House as an openly gay man on the Socialist Party USA ticket.

name: Rita Borsellino
profession: Murder Made Her an Anti-Mafia Crusader
headline: Rita Borsellino, 73, Dies; a Murder Made Her an Anti-Mafia Crusader
abstract: After her brother, a prosecutor, was killed in a bombing, she campaigned against Cosa Nostra influence in Sicily.

name: John Calder
headline: John Calder, British Publisher Who Fought Censorship, Dies at 91
abstract: His authors included Samuel Beckett and Henry Miller, and he fought in court to publish “Last Exit to Brooklyn,” which had been ruled obscene.

name: Uri Avnery
headline: Uri Avnery, Israeli Journalist and Peace Activist, Is Dead at 94
abstract: A left-wing thorn in the government’s side, he called for a Palestinian state and challenged the notion of a strictly Jewish nationality.

name: Vivian Matalon
headline: Vivian Matalon, Tony-Winning Director, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Best known for a revelatory staging of “Morning’s at Seven,” he also directed Noël Coward in his final West End stage performance.

name: Don Cherry
profession: Singer by Night and Golfer by Day
headline: Don Cherry, Singer by Night and Golfer by Day, Is Dead at 94
abstract: He was a top amateur player and a nightclub headliner in the 1950s and ’60s, scoring a hit record with “Band of Gold.” He was also the voice of Mr. Clean.

name: Thomas Hofeller
headline: Thomas Hofeller, Republican Master of Political Maps, Dies at 75
abstract: He had a crucial role in the Republican Party’s resurgence in Congress and state legislatures. In the South, he helped upend decades of Democratic rule.

name: Hanna Mina
headline: Hanna Mina, Syrian Novelist Who Chronicled the Poor, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Mina wrote dozens of books that portrayed the oppressed in a career that spanned half a century, although only two have been translated into English.

name: Barbara Harris
headline: Barbara Harris, Stage, Screen and Improv Actress, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Harris got her start with the Second City and went on to win a Tony Award and to appear in films like “A Thousand Clowns” and “Nashville.”

name: Barbara Harris
profession: First Woman Ordained an Episcopal Bishop
headline: Barbara Harris, First Woman Ordained an Episcopal Bishop, Dies at 89
abstract: Her groundbreaking election angered many conservatives. She even received death threats.

name: Brian Murray
headline: Brian Murray, an Acclaimed Veteran of Broadway, Dies at 80
abstract: South African-born, Mr. Murray went to Broadway by way of the Royal Shakespeare Company. In a busy career, he was nominated for three Tony Awards.

name: Robert H. Ferrell
headline: Robert H. Ferrell, 97, Truman Authority Inspired by Diaries, Dies
abstract: The consummate Truman scholar wrote or edited a dozen books about the 33rd president, including collections of long-buried diaries and letters.

name: Doria Shafik
headline: Overlooked No More: Doria Shafik, Who Led Egypt’s Women’s Liberation Movement
abstract: Her hunger strikes and demonstrations made her one of the most influential women in the history of the Arab world. Yet few Egyptians today know her name.

name: Khaira Arby
profession: Outspoken Malian Singer With Global Reach
headline: Khaira Arby, Outspoken Malian Singer With Global Reach, Dies at 58
abstract: The “Nightingale of Timbuktu” spoke out against Islamist oppression and sang out again female genital cutting, reaching audiences far beyond Africa.

name: Hilary Lister
headline: Hilary Lister, a Quadriplegic Who Sailed Solo, Dies at 46
abstract: Ms. Lister was the first quadriplegic to cross the English Channel and the first disabled woman to circumnavigate Britain solo.

name: George Andrie
headline: George Andrie, Pillar of Cowboys’ Doomsday Defense, Dies at 78
abstract: Andrie played right end for Dallas from 1962 to 1972 and scored an unlikely touchdown in the 1967 N.F.L. championship game in frigid Green Bay.

name: Craig Zadan
profession: Produced Musicals for Stage, Screen and TV
headline: Craig Zadan, 69, Dies; Produced Musicals for Stage, Screen and TV
abstract: A showman who helped put “The Sound of Music” on television, “Chicago” on movie screens and “How to Succeed in Business” back on Broadway.

name: Mary Pratt
headline: Mary Pratt, Realist Painter of Household Scenes, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Pratt, defying early advice that only her husband could become a painter, became a popular artist in Canada and something of feminist champion.

name: María Isabel Chorobik de Mariani
headline: María Isabel Chorobik de Mariani, Crusading Argentine Grandmother, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Mariani’s long search for her abducted granddaughter drew attention to the crimes of Argentina’s military junta in the 1970s. She never found the girl.

name: Alex Storm
profession: Found a Long-Lost Treasure at Sea
headline: Alex Storm, Who Found a Long-Lost Treasure at Sea, Dies at 80
abstract: In 1965, with two partners, he located thousands of coins in the water off Nova Scotia from the wreck of the Chameau in 1725.

name: Robin Leach
profession: Lifestyles of the Rich and Famous Host
headline: Robin Leach, 76, ‘Lifestyles of the Rich and Famous’ Host, Dies
abstract: His syndicated TV show was omnipresent during the 1980s and ’90s, and his instantly recognizable voice and delivery were widely parodied.

name: Lazy Lester
headline: Lazy Lester, Luminary of Swamp Blues, Is Dead at 85
abstract: A leading figure in a subgenre that combines traditional blues with Cajun, country and other styles, he got his nickname for his relaxed vocal style.

name: Costas Kondylis
profession: Go-To Architect in a High-Rise Town
headline: Costas Kondylis, Go-To Architect in a High-Rise Town, Dies at 78
abstract: Donald Trump and many more developers hired him again and again as they made the Manhattan skyline soar even more.

name: Tom Clark
headline: Tom Clark, 77, Is Dead; Poet, Biographer, Baseball Bard
abstract: He hitchhiked with Ginsberg, studied under Donald Hall, worked for George Plimpton and wrote prolifically, whether on love, cosmology or the Oakland A’s.

name: Tom Clark
profession: Private Equity Investor Turned Sheep Farmer
headline: Tom Clark, Private Equity Investor Turned Sheep Farmer, Dies at 85
abstract: On more than 500 acres in upstate New York, he kept a small herd of East Friesian ewes, producing award-winning cheeses and running a high-end restaurant and hotel.

name: John McCain
headline: John McCain, War Hero, Senator, Presidential Contender, Dies at 81
abstract: A naval aviator who endured torture in Vietnam, Mr. McCain rose to the heights of power in Washington until cancer felled him.

name: Neil Simon
headline: Neil Simon, Broadway Master of Comedy, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Simon started out writing for television and later wrote for the movies, but his plays were his biggest successes, among them “The Odd Couple” and “Barefoot in the Park.”

name: Jack Costanzo
headline: Jack Costanzo, Musician Known as Mr. Bongo, Dies at 98
abstract: He played with top bandleaders like Stan Kenton, as well as with celebrities like Marlon Brando, and helped fuel the Latin jazz genre.

name: Queeneth Ndaba
headline: Queeneth Ndaba, Champion of South African Jazz, Dies at 81
abstract: She managed Johannesburg’s most influential home of art and culture during the darkest days of apartheid and invested heavily in the music she staged there.

name: George Walker
headline: George Walker, Barrier-Breaking Composer, Is Dead at 96
abstract: He was the first black composer to be awarded a Pulitzer Prize. Earlier, as a pianist, he had felt deprived of concert opportunities because of his race.

name: Inge Borkh
headline: Inge Borkh, Opera Diva of Passionate Portrayals, Dies at 97
abstract: She inhabited some of the most daunting roles in the operatic repertoire and was best known for her depictions of two Strauss heroines, Salome and Elektra.

name: Sterling Stuckey
headline: Sterling Stuckey, 86, Dies; Charted African Culture in Slavery
abstract: Mr. Stuckey, inspired by Frederick Douglass and Paul Robeson, was critical of white academics whom he accused of hijacking African studies.

name: Heidi Morawetz
headline: Heidi Morawetz, Creative Force in Makeup Industry, Is Dead at 79
abstract: She worked with Yves St. Laurent and oversaw Chanel’s beauty line for three decades, creating nail polish colors that became international hits.

name: Henry Arnhold
profession: Patriarch of a Storied Banking Family
headline: Henry Arnhold, Patriarch of a Storied Banking Family, Dies at 96
abstract: After his family fled Nazi Germany, he helped re-establish its business, dating to 1864, in New York. He also had a hand in rebuilding his native Dresden.

name: James Villas
headline: James Villas, Sharp-Tongued Food Critic, Dies at 80
abstract: His cookbooks and magazine articles championed Southern fare, and he eschewed the contrived and trendy mix of ingredients in gastronomic innovation.

name: Lindsay Kemp
headline: Lindsay Kemp, Dancer Who Taught David Bowie, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Another student, Kate Bush, said Mr. Kemp was “astonishingly inspirational.” But his boundary-pushing work often divided critics.

name: Ruby Payne-Scott
headline: Overlooked No More: Ruby Payne-Scott, Who Explored Space With Radio Waves
abstract: Payne-Scott helped establish the field of radio astronomy by using radio waves to detect solar bursts, but she was forced to resign after she got married.

name: Ted Achilles
profession: Gave Afghan Girls Access to Education
headline: Ted Achilles, Who Gave Afghan Girls Access to Education, Died at 82
abstract: Mr. Achilles and Shabana Basij-Rasikh founded the School of Leadership Afghanistan, a boarding school in Kabul that provides a safe education for Afghan girls.

name: Paul Taylor
profession: Brought Poetry and Lyricism to Modern Dance
headline: Paul Taylor Dies at 88; Brought Poetry and Lyricism to Modern Dance
abstract: Mr. Taylor’s poignant and exuberant works entered the repertory of numerous dance companies. His own company has been one of the world’s superlative troupes.

name: Russ Heath
headline: Russ Heath, Whose Comics Caught Lichtenstein’s Eye, Dies at 91
abstract: In a long and prolific career, Mr. Heath drew countless comic books. He was known for his viscerally illustrated combat stories.

name: Ruth Finley
profession: Put Fashion Shows on a Schedule
headline: Ruth Finley, Who Put Fashion Shows on a Schedule, Dies at 98
abstract: Ms. Finley plotted out a checkerboard of cat-walking for generations of designers jockeying for time slots in the New York show season.

name: Lawrence Rubin
profession: Art Dealer and Supporter of Frank Stella
headline: Lawrence Rubin, Art Dealer and Supporter of Frank Stella, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Rubin helped restore the fortunes of the Knoedler Gallery, the troubled New York dealer, well before it was engulfed by a more recent scandal.

name: Martin Shubik
headline: Martin Shubik, Economist and Game Theory Pioneer, Dies at 92
abstract: In the mid-1960s, he predicted that there would be “computing machines” in homes and schools. In the 1970s, he conducted a serious study of pastrami.

name: Bobby Lynn Maslen
headline: Bobby Lynn Maslen, Who Found Young Readers’ Wavelength, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Maslen created Bob Books, simple stories simply illustrated, and thereby helped teach countless youngsters to read.

name: Elizabeth Connell
headline: Dr. Elizabeth Connell, Authority on Contraception, Is Dead at 92
abstract: An activist as well as a scientist, Dr. Connell helped open a clinic in East Harlem and promoted women’s health around the world.

name: Ellie Mannette
profession: Father of the Modern Steel Drum
headline: Ellie Mannette, Father of the Modern Steel Drum, Dies at 90
abstract: A Trinidadian musician and drum maker, he was captivated by steel-pan bands as a child. He sought to elevate the craft and share it with the world.

name: Krishna Reddy
headline: Krishna Reddy, Master Printmaker and Indian Modernist, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Reddy, who apprenticed with the sculptor Henry Moore, was an expert in intaglio printing who applied sculptural techniques to paper.

name: Rachel Cowan
headline: Rachel Cowan, Innovative Rabbi, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Rabbi Cowan helped couples navigate mixed-faith marriages, designed “healing services” and injected contemplative practices into religious life.

name: Peter Frame
headline: Peter Frame, Ballet Dancer and Instructor, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Frame was a member of the New York City Ballet for 14 years. He was known for resurrecting a rare piece of George Balanchine choreography as a soloist in 1986.

name: Randy Weston
headline: Randy Weston, Pianist Who Traced Roots of Jazz to Africa, Dies at 92
abstract: Whether it be jazz, blues, samba or salsa, Mr. Weston said, “If you take out the African elements of our music, you would have nothing.”

name: Iosif Kobzon
profession: Known as the Russian Frank Sinatra
headline: Iosif Kobzon, Known as the ‘Russian Frank Sinatra,’ Dies at 80
abstract: After a career as one of Russia’s most popular singers, Mr. Kobzon served in the nation’s parliament and became a strong ally of Vladimir Putin.

name: Marie Severin
headline: Marie Severin, Versatile Comic Book Artist, Dies at 89
abstract: Beginning in the 1960s, when women rarely drew comics, Ms. Severin depicted the greatest Marvel heroes, like the Hulk, Dr. Strange and Spider Man.

name: Carole Shelley
profession: Tony Winner and a Pigeon Sister
headline: Carole Shelley, a Tony Winner and a Pigeon Sister, Dies at 79
abstract: A Broadway stalwart (“Elephant Man,” “Wicked”), she also appeared in all three versions of “The Odd Couple” (stage, film and TV) as a giggly neighbor.

name: James Mirrlees
headline: James Mirrlees, Whose Tax Model Earned a Nobel, Dies at 82
abstract: A British social democrat, he was surprised by his own conservative findings — that more progressive rates on high earners can cost governments revenue.

name: Kenny Shopsin
profession: Brash Owner of a Quirky Restaurant
headline: Kenny Shopsin, Brash Owner of a Quirky Restaurant, Dies at 76
abstract: His sprawling menu was legendary, and so was his penchant for tossing out potential customers who didn’t get the concept of his neighborhood eatery.

name: Jan Ellen Lewis
headline: Jan Ellen Lewis, Expert on Jefferson’s Other Family, Dies at 69
abstract: A historian, she organized a groundbreaking conference on Jefferson’s legacy after DNA tests showed that he had fathered children with Sally Hemings, a slave.

name: Melitta Bentz
headline: Overlooked No More: Melitta Bentz, Who Invented the Coffee Filter
abstract: Trial and error prevailed in a German woman’s kitchen. And when she got the system she wanted, she put her name on it.

name: Gloria Jean
headline: Gloria Jean, Child Singing Sensation in 1940s Films, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Jean warbled in a slew of popular musicals for Universal Studios. She also starred alongside W.C. Fields in “Never Give a Sucker an Even Break.”

name: Christopher Kennedy Lawford
headline: Christopher Kennedy Lawford, Actor and Author Who Battled Addiction, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Lawford turned his struggle with addiction into a career speaking and writing about his recovery and public health.

name: Richard M. DeVos
headline: Richard M. DeVos, Amway Co-Founder and G.O.P. Stalwart, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. DeVos turned the marketing company into a global enterprise and used his wealth to strengthen the Republican Party and buy the Orlando Magic basketball team.

name: Stan Brock
profession: Intrepid Provider of Health Care in Remote Areas
headline: Stan Brock, 82, Intrepid Provider of Health Care in Remote Areas, Dies
abstract: A British-born former cowboy in South America and a “Wild Kingdom” TV star, he went on to deploy mobile clinics to treat the underserved and uninsured.

name: Burt Reynolds
profession: Made Hearts Throb and Audiences Laugh
headline: Burt Reynolds Dies at 82; Made Hearts Throb and Audiences Laugh
abstract: Mr. Reynolds carried on a long love affair with moviegoers even though his performances were often more memorable than the films that contained them.

name: Ward Hall
headline: Ward Hall, Who Kept the Sideshow Going, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Withstanding decades of cultural change, his World of Wonders presented oddities and amazements at carnivals and fairs all over the United States.

name: Erich Lessing
headline: Erich Lessing, 95, Photographer Who Chronicled Postwar Europe, Dies
abstract: He fled Europe in 1939 but returned to Austria after the war as a self-taught photojournalist and chronicler of modern history and culture.

name: Irving Petlin
headline: Irving Petlin, Artist Who Recorded Injustice, Dies at 83
abstract: In his paintings and pastels, Mr. Petlin reimagined brutal events with subtlety and surrealism in a style neither realistic nor abstract.

name: Mac Miller
headline: Mac Miller, Rapper Who Wrestled With Fame and Addiction, Dies at 26
abstract: The musician, who released five albums, began his career as a mischievous party-starter but turned toward darker themes.

name: Amanda Kyle Williams
headline: Amanda Kyle Williams, Crime Novelist Who Was Dyslexic, Dies at 61
abstract: Ms. Williams, who was dyslexic, didn’t read her first novel until she was 23. Then she landed a $1 million contract to write a mystery series.

name: Will Jordan
headline: Will Jordan, Who Mimicked the Famous, Is Dead at 91
abstract: A gifted impressionist, he was best known for his full-body imitation of the television host Ed Sullivan — an impression that was itself widely imitated.

name: Wakako Yamauchi
headline: Wakako Yamauchi, Playwright on Japanese-American Life, Dies at 93
abstract: Her works, drawn from her own experiences, including time in an internment camp, focused on dislocation and assimilation.

name: Bill Daily
profession: Regular on I Dream of Jeannie and The Bob Newhart Show
headline: Bill Daily, a Regular on ‘I Dream of Jeannie’ and ‘The Bob Newhart Show,’ Dies at 91
abstract: His character on “I Dream of Jeannie” was initially scripted as “Man in Uniform.” After he tried out for the role, he became the show’s second banana.

name: Adam Clymer
headline: Adam Clymer, Veteran Political Reporter and Pollster, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Clymer reported from around the world, the halls of Congress and the campaign trail, in one instance eliciting an open-mic vulgarism by George W. Bush.

name: Tito Capobianco
headline: Tito Capobianco, Assertive Opera Director, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Capobianco created major productions featuring Beverly Sills at the New York City Opera and was the longterm general director of the Pittsburgh Opera.

name: Jeff Lowe
profession: Pathfinder Up the Face of Mountains
headline: Jeff Lowe, Pathfinder Up the Face of Mountains, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Lowe completed more than 1,000 daunting first ascents, wrote books on ice-climbing and used his fortitude to face a debilitating illness.

name: Henry Bawnik
profession: Survivor of Death Camps and an Inferno at Sea
headline: Henry Bawnik, Survivor of Death Camps and an Inferno at Sea, Dies at 92
abstract: In the final days of World War II, after being held in four concentration camps, he found himself on board a German ship that was bombed by the British.

name: Barbara Gould
profession: Model in a Famously Long-Lived TV Spot
headline: Barbara Gould, Model in a Famously Long-Lived TV Spot, Dies at 81
abstract: She was already a successful cover girl in 1975 when a TV commercial showing her buying a used fur hit the air — and continued to run for 14 years.

name: Tom Frost
headline: Tom Frost, Mountaineer Who Designed a Cleaner Climb, Dies at 82
abstract: Frost was known for his harrowing first ascents up El Capitan in Yosemite and for designing climbing tools to protect rock surfaces from being scarred.

name: Marthe McKenna
headline: Overlooked No More: Marthe McKenna, Nurse Who Spied for the British in World War I
abstract: Her nursing skills gave her the perfect cover for espionage. She later produced a thrilling memoir that Winston Churchill couldn’t put down.

name: Diane Leather
profession: First Woman to Run Mile in Under 5 Minutes
headline: Diane Leather, 85, First Woman to Run Mile in Under 5 Minutes, Dies
abstract: She broke the barrier in 1954, a feat — like women’s distance running in general at the time — that was not recognized by the track and field establishment.

name: Marin Mazzie
headline: Marin Mazzie, Broadway Musical Star, Is Dead at 57
abstract: In a long career cut short by cancer, she earned three Tony nominations in just six years, for performances in “Passion,” “Ragtime” and “Kiss Me, Kate.”

name: Andre Blay
headline: Andre Blay, Who Put Movies on Videotape, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Overcoming the studios’ initial reluctance, Mr. Blay in effect redefined the term “home movie” with a product that made him a multimillionaire.

name: John Wilcock
headline: John Wilcock, Pioneer of the Underground Press, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Wilcock led two lives: as a prolific travel writer and a provocateur at The Village Voice, The East Village Other and the Underground Press Syndicate.

name: Janet Weinberg
profession: Advocate for Gay Causes and the Disabled
headline: Janet Weinberg, 63, Dies; Advocate for Gay Causes and the Disabled
abstract: Ms. Weinberg’s fund-raising work for the Gay Men’s Health Crisis led to her being named chief operating officer and then chief executive.

name: David Yallop
headline: David Yallop, Writer Who Saw a Deadly Vatican Conspiracy, Dies at 81
abstract: An investigative journalist, he was best known for “In God’s Name,” a best seller that claimed that Pope John Paul I was murdered in a Vatican plot.

name: Walter Mischel
headline: Walter Mischel, 88, Psychologist Famed for Marshmallow Test, Dies
abstract: Dr. Mischel’s experiments with preschoolers and sweets zeroed in on the importance of delayed gratification, and his insights changed the study of personality.

name: Nancy Blomberg
headline: Nancy Blomberg, Champion of Native American Art, Dies at 72
abstract: As a curator at the Denver Art Museum, she valued American Indian works as art, not as ethnographic specimens.

name: Rachid Taha
headline: Rachid Taha, 59, Algerian Rocker Who Spoke for Immigrants, Dies
abstract: Mr. Taha, who led the group Carte de Séjour before beginning a solo career, melded his Arabic heritage with punk, funk and electronic beats.

name: Peter Donat
headline: Peter Donat, Actor Who Played a Panoply of Roles, Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Donat acted often on the screen and had a recurring role on “The X Files.” But he said he was most gratified by theatrical work.

name: Shan Tianfang
headline: Shan Tianfang, a Superstar of Chinese Storytelling, Dies at 83
abstract: When Mr. Shan first brought his storytelling to radio in 1980, an estimated 100 million people tuned in.

name: Big Jay McNeely
headline: Big Jay McNeely, 91, Dies; R&B’s ‘King of the Honkers’
abstract: At the dawn of rock ’n’ roll, he put the saxophone front and center, sometimes while lying on his back, kicking his legs, or jumping off the stage.

name: Alan Abel
headline: Alan Abel, Hoaxer Extraordinaire, Is (on Good Authority) Dead at 94
abstract: A professional trickster, Mr. Abel gleefully hoodwinked the American public time and again, even convincing The Times in 1980 that he had died.

name: John Pritchard III
headline: John Pritchard III, Tenacious Law Enforcement Leader, Dies at 75
abstract: Rising from beat cop to high-ranking posts in New York, he had a hand in investigations of the mob, Abscam, corruption scandals and a child-killer case.

name: Ira Sabin
headline: Ira Sabin, Founder of JazzTimes Magazine, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Originally a drummer, he channeled his passion for jazz into a publication that began as a four-page newspaper to promote his record store in Washington.

name: Ehsan Yarshater
profession: Iran Scholar With a Monumental Vision
headline: Ehsan Yarshater, Iran Scholar With a Monumental Vision, Dies at 98
abstract: He worked on his magnum opus, an encyclopedia of Iranian history and culture, for more than 40 years, retiring at the letter “K.” The work goes on.

name: Annette Michelson
profession: Film Studies Pioneer and Journal Founder
headline: Annette Michelson, Film Studies Pioneer and Journal Founder, Dies at 95
abstract: Through the influential arts journal October and her own writings, Ms. Michelson helped turn cinema into an academic discipline.

name: Mary Nooter Roberts
headline: Mary Nooter Roberts, Champion of African Art, Is Dead at 58
abstract: She helped alter standard institutional presentations of African art by acknowledging its spiritually, socially and physically interactive character.

name: Ruth Clark
profession: Helped the Jobless Get a Foothold
headline: Ruth Clark, Who Helped the Jobless Get a Foothold, Dies at 76
abstract: A key-punch operator herself, she opened an agency in 1974 to meet a demand for data processors and to relieve unemployment in minority neighborhoods.

name: Thad Mumford
headline: Thad Mumford, Pathbreaking Television Writer, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Mr. Mumford forged a writing career on shows like “M*A*S*H” and “Maude” at a time when African-Americans were rare in network writing rooms.

name: Arthur Mitchell
profession: Showed the Way for Black Dancers
headline: Arthur Mitchell Is Dead at 84; Showed the Way for Black Dancers
abstract: Mr. Mitchell, the first black ballet dancer to achieve international stardom, was also the founding director of the groundbreaking Dance Theater of Harlem.

name: Luigi Cavalli-Sforza
headline: Luigi Cavalli-Sforza, 96, Who Tracked Genes Through History, Dies
abstract: Before 23andMe and Ancestry.com, he did groundbreaking work exploring how genes reveal where people come from and whom they’re related to.

name: Robert Venturi
headline: Robert Venturi, Architect Who Rejected Modernism, Dies at 93
abstract: To the modernist notion of “less is more,” he retorted, “Less is a bore,” arguing for ornament, historical references and even humor in architecture.

name: Ana Mendieta
headline: Overlooked No More: Ana Mendieta, a Cuban Artist Who Pushed Boundaries
abstract: Mendieta’s art, sometimes violent, often unapologetically feminist and usually raw, left an indelible mark before her life was cut short.

name: Micheline Rozan
headline: Micheline Rozan, a Force Behind a Theater Master, Dies at 89
abstract: She helped the famed director Peter Brook start an influential theater group in Paris and mount major productions like “The Mahabharata.”

name: Marceline Loridan-Ivens
headline: Marceline Loridan-Ivens, 90, Dies; Wrote of Holocaust’s Enduring Toll
abstract: An author and filmmaker, she examined the long-term anguish of surviving the death camps as a teenager and challenged attitudes about Jews in France.

name: Stephen Jeffreys
headline: Stephen Jeffreys, Playwright Known for ‘The Libertine,’ Dies at 68
abstract: His 1994 play about a hedonistic 17th-century nobleman became a vehicle for Johnny Depp and John Malkovich.

name: Jon Burge
profession: Ex-Commander in Chicago Police Torture Cases
headline: Jon Burge, 70, Ex-Commander in Chicago Police Torture Cases, Dies
abstract: His reported torture of criminal suspects, by shocking them with cattle prods or pointing guns in their mouths, led to pardons, reparations and to the abolition of the death penalty in Illinois.

name: Perry Miller Adato
headline: Perry Miller Adato, a Filmmaker Focused on Artists, Dies at 97
abstract: At a time when relatively few women were documentarians, Ms. Adato won awards for films about Dylan Thomas, Georgia O’Keeffe, Picasso and others.

name: Tran Dai Quang
headline: Tran Dai Quang, Hard-Line Vietnamese President, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Quang, whose role was largely ceremonial, was a former chief of the country’s powerful Ministry of Public Security.

name: David DiChiera
profession: Gave Opera a Home in Detroit
headline: David DiChiera, Who Gave Opera a Home in Detroit, Dies at 83
abstract: Dr. DiChiera built an opera company that presented world-class talent at a time when Detroit’s population was dwindling and its future looked bleak.

name: Beat Richner
headline: Beat Richner, Doctor to Cambodia’s Needy Young, Dies at 71
abstract: Dr. Richner turned a war-ravaged pediatric hospital in Phnom Penh into a network of five medical centers that now serve one million patients a year.

name: Anne Russ Federman
profession: Scion of a Royal Family of Smoked Fish
headline: Anne Russ Federman, Scion of a Royal Family of Smoked Fish, Dies at 97
abstract: The last of three sisters who inherited the venerable Lower East Side appetizing store Russ & Daughters, a temple of lox, herring and so much more.

name: Lawrence Martin-Bittman
headline: Lawrence Martin-Bittman, 87, Master of Disinformation, Dies
abstract: He was a dirty trickster for Czechoslovakia during the Cold War. Then he defected to the West and taught the perils of propaganda to journalism students.

name: Marilyn Lloyd
headline: Marilyn Lloyd, 89, Tennessee Trailblazer in Congress, Dies
abstract: A conservative Democrat, she replaced her husband on the ballot when he was killed in a plane crash in 1974. She went on to serve 10 terms.

name: Charles Kao
headline: Charles Kao, Nobel Laureate Who Revolutionized Fiber Optics, Dies at 84
abstract: In the 1960s, Dr. Kao outlined the potential capacity of fiber optic cables for transmitting information, laying the technical groundwork for modern communications.

name: Tommy McDonald
profession: Fleet Hall of Famer for the Eagles
headline: Tommy McDonald, Fleet Hall of Famer for the Eagles, Dies at 84
abstract: What he lacked in size — he was 5 feet 9 and 175 pounds — he made up for in speed and durability, lasting 12 N.F.L. seasons and scoring 84 touchdowns.

name: Henry Wessel
profession: Lens Captured Life in the West
headline: Henry Wessel, Whose Lens Captured Life in the West, Is Dead at 76
abstract: He was a New Jersey native enthralled by California. “The light had such physical presence; it looked as though you could lean against it,” he said.

name: Madeleine Yayodele Nelson
headline: Madeleine Yayodele Nelson, 69, Percussion Group’s Founder, Dies
abstract: Trained as an educator, Ms. Nelson spent 40 years performing music from across the African diaspora as the leader of Women of the Calabash.

name: Freddie Oversteegen
headline: Freddie Oversteegen, Gritty Dutch Resistance Fighter, Dies at 92
abstract: She was only 14 when she joined her sister and a law student as an all-female underground trio of saboteurs and assassins in German-occupied Holland.

name: Joshua Roth
headline: Joshua Roth, Who Brought Agents to Visual Artists, Dies at 40
abstract: Mr. Roth founded United Talent Agency’s fine arts division in 2015 to tap into a new revenue source and help artists broker deals beyond the art world.

name: Mel Elfin
headline: Mel Elfin, Newsman Who Built Up College Ranking Guide, Dies at 89
abstract: He oversaw the expansion of U.S. News & World Report’s annual college rankings, a boon to high school seniors but also a target of criticism.

name: John Putnam
profession: Melville of the South Street Seaport
headline: John Putnam, the Melville of the South Street Seaport, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Putnam spent decades bringing New York’s maritime history to life as a resident museum historian and an impersonator of the author of “Moby-Dick.”

name: Frances Edelstein
profession: Queen of the Polish Tea Room
headline: Frances Edelstein, Queen of the Polish Tea Room, Is Dead at 92
abstract: With her husband, she turned a former hotel ballroom in Midtown Manhattan into a dining hangout for actors, directors, playwrights, producers — and tourists.

name: Katherine Hoover
headline: Katherine Hoover, Flutist and Composer, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Ms. Hoover, whose “Kokopeli” is a frequently performed piece for flute, made significant inroads into the male-dominated world of classical composition.

name: Constance Sutton
headline: Constance Sutton, Feminist Anthropologist, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Margaret Mead urged her to do field work, even though to do so as a married woman “was not heard of.” She became an expert on gender in the Caribbean.

name: Voltairine de Cleyre
headline: Overlooked No More: Voltairine de Cleyre, America’s ‘Greatest Woman Anarchist’
abstract: At a time of rampant income inequality, stifling social roles for women and church-mandated morality, de Cleyre rebelled against the accepted order.

name: David Wolkowsky
profession: Developer Hailed as Mr. Key West
headline: David Wolkowsky, Developer Hailed as Mr. Key West, Dies at 99
abstract: He led the island’s preservation and its transformation into an artists’ colony and vacation spot, befriending literary figures and hiring Jimmy Buffett along the way.

name: Jack McKinney
profession: N.B.A. Coach Trailed by a What if?
headline: Jack McKinney, 83, Dies; N.B.A. Coach Trailed by a ‘What if?
abstract: With Magic Johnson he brought “Showtime” to the Lakers in 1979, but he missed their glory years after a calamitous bicycle accident.

name: Merle Debuskey
headline: Merle Debuskey, Renowned Theatrical Press Agent, Dies at 95
abstract: He represented hundreds of shows on Broadway and off and had a long association with Joseph Papp, whom he helped battle to keep Shakespeare free.

name: David Wong Louie
headline: David Wong Louie, Who Probed Ethnic Identity in Fiction, Dies at 63
abstract: In a writing career hampered by illness, Mr. Louie created acclaimed stories that drew on his experiences as an American son of Chinese immigrants.

name: Lois Jovanovic
headline: Dr. Lois Jovanovic, 71, Dies; Helped Diabetic Women Have Babies
abstract: A third-generation diabetic herself, she upset conventional wisdom in finding that women whose blood sugar level was controlled could safely give birth.

name: Inge Feltrinelli
profession: Publishing Titan Started With a Camera
headline: Inge Feltrinelli Dies at 87; Publishing Titan Started With a Camera
abstract: Early on she photographed Hemingway, Garbo, Picasso and others. Then she married a publisher and later took over the house, one of Italy’s most important.

name: Geta Bratescu
headline: Geta Bratescu, Adventuresome Romanian Artist, Is Dead at 92
abstract: The creator of experimental, often humorous works, she had been a prolific artist for decades in her own country. But the West discovered her only recently.

name: Joe Masteroff
headline: Joe Masteroff, Playwright of ‘Cabaret’ Fame, Is Dead at 98
abstract: The winner of a Tony for his evocation of decadent prewar Berlin, he is also remembered for another acclaimed Broadway musical, “She Loves Me.”

name: Pam Henry
headline: Pam Henry, the Last Poster Child for Polio, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. Henry was part of the last March of Dimes publicity campaign against the disease. She later became one of the first female TV reporters in Oklahoma.

name: Marty Balin
headline: Marty Balin, a Founder of Jefferson Airplane, Dies at 76
abstract: A guitarist, singer and songwriter for a San Francisco band that defined the psychedelic rock era of the late 1960s, then morphed into Jefferson Starship.

name: Otis Rush
headline: Otis Rush, Influential Blues Singer and Guitarist, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. Rush was part of a circle of late-1950s performers whose music heralded a new era for Chicago blues and influenced a generation of rock musicians.

name: George Kolombatovich
profession: Fencing Coach at Columbia and the Met
headline: George Kolombatovich, Fencing Coach at Columbia and the Met, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Kolombatovich taught sword fighting to the casts of “Otello,” “Carmen” and “Don Giovanni,” and led Columbia to five N.C.A.A. fencing championships.

name: Charles Aznavour
profession: Enduring French Singer of Global Fame
headline: Charles Aznavour, 94, Enduring French Singer of Global Fame, Dies
abstract: With his ballads of love found and love lost, he was said to have sold almost 200 million records and appeared in scores of films.

name: Walter Laqueur
profession: Scholar of Terrorism and the Holocaust
headline: Walter Laqueur, Scholar of Terrorism and the Holocaust, Dies at 97
abstract: After fleeing Nazi Germany, he steeped himself in world affairs, from the Middle East to the Soviet Union, running think tanks and writing prodigiously.

name: Jerry González
headline: Jerry González, Innovator of Latin Jazz, Is Dead at 69
