abstract: A trumpeter and percussionist, he melded Cuban, African, Puerto Rican and other influences in the Fort Apache Band and other ensembles.

name: Do Muoi
headline: Do Muoi, Vietnam’s Leader in Economic Transition, Dies at 101
abstract: He was called “a prime example of a steadfast communist.” But he also pushed through reforms as Vietnam opened its markets and encouraged free enterprise.

name: Lois Gray
headline: Lois Gray, Mentor to Unions and Women Who Work, Dies at 94
abstract: At Cornell she taught and nurtured women, immigrants and minority group members as she broke ground in the field of labor and industrial relations.

name: Jane Fortune
headline: Jane Fortune, Champion of Florence’s Female Artists, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Fortune, an Indiana philanthropist, found a late-in-life purpose in restoring Renaissance art by women, earning her the nickname “Indiana Jane.”

name: Gary Kurtz
headline: Gary Kurtz, Hands-On ‘Star Wars’ Producer, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Mr. Kurtz worked closely with George Lucas on the first two films in one of the most successful franchises in history.

name: Leon Lederman
profession: Explorer (and Explainer) of the Subatomic World
headline: Leon Lederman, 96, Explorer (and Explainer) of the Subatomic World, Dies
abstract: A Nobel laureate who deepened science’s understanding of the building blocks of matter, he was called “the best ambassador of physics to the general public since Einstein.”

name: Minnie Mae Freeman Penney
headline: Overlooked No More: Minnie Mae Freeman Penney, Nebraska’s ‘Fearless Maid’
abstract: In one of America’s deadliest blizzards, a schoolteacher used quick thinking and resourcefulness to save more than a dozen students.

name: Geoff Emerick
profession: Recorded the Beatles in Their Prime
headline: Geoff Emerick, 72, Dies; Recorded the Beatles in Their Prime
abstract: A Grammy Award-winning engineer, he played a key role in the making of “Revolver,” “Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band” and other important albums.

name: David P. Schippers
headline: David P. Schippers, 88, House Counsel in Clinton Impeachment, Dies
abstract: A Chicago lawyer and a lifelong Democrat, he worked for the Republicans at the behest of his friend Henry Hyde, the House Judiciary Committee chairman.

name: Dave Anderson
headline: Dave Anderson, Award-Winning Times Sportswriter, Dies at 89
abstract: Rare for a sports journalist, he won a Pulitzer Prize, crowning a long career as a columnist and author that began when he was a teenager in Brooklyn.

name: Warrington Colescott
headline: Warrington Colescott, Who Etched With a Satirical Edge, Dies at 97
abstract: In his etchings, Mr. Colescott, a renowned printmaker, made biting and witty commentaries on history, politics, civil rights and, satisfyingly, the I.R.S.

name: Bernard J. Carroll
headline: Dr. Bernard J. Carroll, ‘Conscience of Psychiatry,’ Dies at 77
abstract: After early work on the biological basis of depression, Dr. Carroll became a relentless campaigner against corruption among academic researchers.

name: Rosa Bouglione
profession: Doyenne of a French Circus Family
headline: Rosa Bouglione, Doyenne of a French Circus Family, Dies at 107
abstract: After Rosa Van Been married Joseph Bouglione in a lion cage, the Bouglione family bought the Cirque d’Hiver in Paris, still standing more than 80 years later.

name: C. Payne Lucas
headline: C. Payne Lucas, Leader in Aid to Africa, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Lucas helped found Africare and, with help from African-Americans, built it into a leading nonprofit promoting economic development.

name: Peggy Sue Gerron Rackham
headline: Peggy Sue Gerron Rackham, Who Inspired a Hit Song, Dies at 78
abstract: The girlfriend of Buddy Holly’s drummer in the Crickets, she was the “pretty, pretty, pretty, pretty Peggy Sue” immortalized in a 1957 rock ’n’ roll record.

name: Roger Robinson
headline: Roger Robinson, Who Tackled August Wilson Roles, Dies at 78
abstract: He won a Tony Award for his work in the 2009 revival of Mr. Wilson’s “Joe Turner’s Come and Gone,” his seventh and final Broadway appearance.

name: Vladimir Radunsky
headline: Vladimir Radunsky, 64, Dies; Protean Children’s Book Illustrator
abstract: Mr. Radunsky harnessed a multitude of artistic styles for different narrative effects in books about subjects including Albert Einstein and a rapping dog.

name: Richard Kaplan
headline: Richard Kaplan, Acclaimed Documentarian, Is Dead at 93
abstract: His films included an Oscar-winning study of Eleanor Roosevelt and a portrait of the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. that one critic called a “genuine spiritual epic.”

name: Sydney Goldstein
headline: Sydney Goldstein, Maestro of Public Conversation, Dies at 73
abstract: She founded City Arts & Lectures, which showcases conversation as entertainment and is broadcast on more than 100 public radio stations nationwide.

name: William Helfand
headline: William Helfand, a Collector Intrigued by Quackery, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Helfand’s collection of posters and prints for dubious medical cures was formidable. It is now spread among assorted museums.

name: Montserrat Caballé
headline: Montserrat Caballé, Opera Star With ‘Ethereal’ Voice, Is Dead at 85
abstract: One of the 20th century’s most renowned sopranos, the Spanish-born Ms. Caballé inspired delirious adulation on both sides of the Atlantic.

name: Audrey Wells
profession: Screenwriter Behind The Hate U Give
headline: Audrey Wells, Screenwriter Behind ‘The Hate U Give,’ Dies at 58
abstract: Audrey Wells, whose work included “Under the Tuscan Sun,” had been privately battling cancer for five years. She died the day before her latest film hit theaters.

name: Hamiet Bluiett
headline: Hamiet Bluiett, Baritone Saxophone Trailblazer, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Bluiett, a charter member of the World Saxophone Quartet and a leading light of the jazz avant-garde, expanded the possibilities of his instrument.

name: Scott Wilson
headline: Scott Wilson, 76, ‘Walking Dead’ and ‘In Cold Blood’ Actor, Dies
abstract: Mr. Wilson’s breakout part was as one of two murderers in “In Cold Blood.” He played a kinder figure on several seasons of “The Walking Dead.”

name: Will Vinton
headline: Will Vinton, Revolutionary Animator With Claymation, Dies at 70
abstract: He and a partner won an Oscar with a stop-motion technique using clay figures, the likes of which found a wide audience in the California Raisins commercials.

name: David Wise
headline: David Wise, Journalist Who Exposed C.I.A. Activity, Dies at 88
abstract: The C.I.A. tried to quash one book, to the point of buying up all the copies. But the publisher said it would just print more. It became a best seller.

name: Marie Runyon
headline: Marie Runyon, a Liberal Firebrand Into Her 90s, Dies at 103
abstract: Her long fight as a tenant against eviction by Columbia University led to decades of protests for peace and racial justice and even arrests.

name: Phyllis Kind
headline: Phyllis Kind, Art Dealer Who Took In Outsiders, Dies at 85
abstract: In New York and Chicago galleries she expanded the narrative of 20th-century art to include artists known as the Hairy Who and then as the Chicago Imagists.

name: Thomas A. Steitz
profession: Illuminated a Building Block of Life
headline: Thomas A. Steitz, 78, Dies; Illuminated a Building Block of Life
abstract: A Nobel laureate, he discovered the structure of a huge molecule crucial to translating genetic information into the proteins that make up living matter.

name: George Taliaferro
headline: George Taliaferro, First Black Drafted by N.F.L., Is Dead at 91
abstract: A running back who also passed, kicked and played defensive back, Taliaferro was drafted by the Chicago Bears but signed with a rival league.

name: Annemarie Schwarzenbach
headline: Overlooked No More: Annemarie Schwarzenbach, Author, Photographer and ‘Ravaged Angel’
abstract: A Swiss heiress, she was an adventurous traveler whose writings, along with her androgynous glamour and troubled life, made her a gay cult figure after her death.

name: Tex Winter
headline: Tex Winter, Brain Behind Basketball’s Triangle Offense, Dies at 96
abstract: Winter, who was inducted into the Basketball Hall of Fame in 2011, spent 60 years in the sport and helped propel Phil Jackson’s teams to nine N.B.A. titles.

name: Donald E. Moore
headline: Donald E. Moore, Who Expanded Brooklyn Botanic Garden, Dies at 90
abstract: As the garden’s president in the 1980s, he doubled its indoor exhibition space, tripled the membership and raised funds for the Steinhardt Conservatory.

name: Angela Maria
headline: Angela Maria, 89, Brazilian Singer Who Inspired a Generation, Dies
abstract: Her unique voice — at times piercing, sometimes hoarse, often loaded with melancholy — powered a wildly successful recording career.

name: Helena Almeida
headline: Helena Almeida, Experimental Portuguese Artist, Dies at 84
abstract: In photographs, drawings and paintings, she bent the boundaries between genres, using her body as an artistic tool.

name: Robert Pitofsky
headline: Robert Pitofsky, Champion of Consumer Protection, Dies at 88
abstract: As chairman of the Federal Trade Commission in the Clinton administration, he looked beyond traditional views of antitrust enforcement.

name: Natan Wekselbaum
headline: Natan Wekselbaum, 83, Dies; Built a Cornucopia of Housewares
abstract: A Cuban immigrant, he and his brother started a tiny hardware store on the Upper East Side that grew into the sprawling Gracious Home emporium.

name: Betty Grissom
headline: Betty Grissom, Who Sued in Astronaut Husband’s Death, Dies at 91
abstract: She was shunned by the space community after she sued North American Rockwell in the launchpad death of Gus Grissom. She won a settlement.

name: Joseph Tydings
headline: Joseph Tydings, Ex-Democratic Senator and Nixon Target, Dies at 90
abstract: He had an active single term as what the White House called a “liberal radical” from Maryland. He later objected to Trump’s appropriating his family seal.

name: Cindy R. Lobel
profession: Traced New York History Through Food
headline: Cindy R. Lobel, Who Traced New York History Through Food, Dies at 48
abstract: Professor Lobel was among the first historians to explore the economic and social elements of city life in the 19th century through the lens of eating.

name: Sidney Shachnow
headline: Sidney Shachnow, 83, Is Dead; Holocaust Escapee and U.S. General
abstract: After leaving a forced labor camp in Lithuania under his uncle’s coat, he found his way to America, where he eventually commanded the Special Forces.

name: Pik Botha
profession: South Africas Last Apartheid Foreign Minister
headline: Pik Botha, South Africa’s Last Apartheid Foreign Minister, Dies at 86
abstract: A defender of apartheid, he also showed a moderate streak rarely found among hard-liners, predicting that the country would one day have a black president.

name: Carol Hall
headline: Carol Hall, ‘Best Little Whorehouse’ Composer, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Ms. Hall was a moderately successful songwriter until she and two collaborators came up with one of the biggest Broadway hits of the 1970s.

name: Jeanne Ashworth
headline: Jeanne Ashworth, Pioneering Speedskating Olympian, Dies at 80
abstract: After learning to skate on a small pond in Massachusetts, she went on to become the first U.S. woman to win a speedskating medal in the Winter Olympics.

name: Jim Taylor
profession: Hall of Fame Fullback for the Green Bay Packers
headline: Jim Taylor, Hall of Fame Fullback for the Green Bay Packers, Dies at 83
abstract: Taylor ran for more than 1,000 yards in five consecutive seasons and was named to the N.F.L.’s all-decade team for the ’60s.

name: William Coors
headline: William Coors, Brewery Chief and Ultraconservative Voice, Dies at 102
abstract: Mr. Coors built a regional brewery into the nation’s third largest, but critics called his speeches and policies racist, sexist and homophobic.

name: Herbert D. Kleber
headline: Herbert D. Kleber, Pioneer in Addiction Treatment, Dies at 84
abstract: A professional detour to the federal prison hospital in Lexington, Ky., known as the “narcotics farm,” would set the course of his life’s work.

name: Mary Midgley
profession: Moral Philosopher for the General Reader
headline: Mary Midgley, 99, Moral Philosopher for the General Reader, Is Dead
abstract: Writing into her 90s — her last book was published last month — Dr. Midgley challenged with wit and verve the primacy of science as arbiter of reality.

name: Irving Like
profession: Foe of Power Plant and Friend of Fire Island
headline: Irving Like, 93, Dies; Foe of Power Plant and Friend of Fire Island
abstract: Mr. Like, an environmental lawyer, waged a long and ultimately successful fight against the Shoreham nuclear generator on Long Island.

name: Alfred Hubay
headline: Alfred Hubay, Met Opera’s Box Office Prognosticator, Dies at 93
abstract: In a lifetime of working at the Met, he developed an ability to project ticket sales with uncanny accuracy.

name: Paul G. Allen
headline: Paul G. Allen, Microsoft’s Co-Founder, Is Dead at 65
abstract: Mr. Allen and Bill Gates started the company in 1975, helping to usher in the personal computing revolution. He died after a recurrence of cancer.

name: Karl Mildenberger
headline: Karl Mildenberger, German Heavyweight Who Fought Ali, Dies at 80
abstract: He was not seen as a serious threat to the champion, but after lasting 12 rounds against Ali, he saw the fight, though he lost, as a capstone to his career.

name: Mario Buatta
profession: Interior Designer and Prince of Chintz
headline: Mario Buatta, Interior Designer and ‘Prince of Chintz,’ Dies at 82
abstract: He made exuberant use of pillows, fringes, swags, tassels, bows and ruffles for a list of clients that included the famous as well as the merely rich.

name: Dennis Hof
headline: Dennis Hof, the Pimp Who Won a Nevada State Primary, Dies at 72
abstract: A brothel owner and a Republican, he likened himself to President Trump and was weeks away from general election when he was found dead by a pornographic film star.

name: Ian Kiernan
headline: Ian Kiernan, Australian Sailor Who Battled Pollution, Dies at 78
abstract: Appalled by the trash he saw in the world’s oceans, he began a cleanup campaign in Sydney that went global.

name: Felix Smith
headline: Felix Smith, Who Piloted Covert Flights Over Asia, Is Dead at 100
abstract: Recruited by Lt. Gen. Claire Chennault, Captain Smith flew over China, Vietnam and Laos on stealth Cold War missions for the American government.

name: Yamei Kin
headline: Overlooked No More: Yamei Kin, the Chinese Doctor Who Introduced Tofu to the West
abstract: Long before veggie burgers and soy lattes were fashionable, Kin was sent on a mission by the United States government to uncover the benefits of the soybean for Americans.

name: Walter Huddleston
headline: Walter Huddleston, Senator Toppled by Mitch McConnell, Dies at 92
abstract: A two-term Democrat from Kentucky, he was narrowly defeated by Mr. McConnell, then a county judge and executive, in a Republican campaign engineered by Roger Ailes.

name: Takehisa Kosugi
headline: Takehisa Kosugi, Composer for Merce Cunningham, Dies at 80
abstract: In a long career on the cutting edge, Mr. Kosugi found music everywhere — in bicycle parts, in crumpled paper, even in silence.

name: William Shearer
profession: Doctor (Like Another Dad) to Boy in Bubble
headline: William Shearer, Doctor (‘Like Another Dad’) to Boy in Bubble, Dies at 81
abstract: “What he gave us was a powerful lesson in many areas of medicine,” Dr. Shearer said of his young patient, who lived in a sterile plastic cocoon.

name: Raye Montague
headline: Raye Montague, the Navy’s ‘Hidden Figure’ Ship Designer, Dies at 83
abstract: Despite facing racism and sexism, she became the first person to design a Navy ship using a computer program. She was recognized nationally only later in life.

name: Ara Guler
headline: Ara Guler, Poetic Photographer of Istanbul, Dies at 90
abstract: One of the greatest Turkish photographers of his generation, Mr. Guler depicted the city with poignancy. He also photographed the famous worldwide.

name: Sue Hubbell
headline: Sue Hubbell, Who Wrote of Bees and Self-Reliance, Dies at 83
abstract: In well-reviewed books like “A Country Year” and “A Book of Bees,” she described adjusting to a midlife divorce and keeping 300 hives in the Ozarks.

name: Cy Adler
headline: Cy Adler, Pied Piper of Manhattan’s Piers, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Adler, an environmentalist, started the Great Saunter, an annual 32-mile walk that reawakens New York City residents to the greenbelt that encircles them.

name: Anthea Bell
headline: Anthea Bell, Translator of Freud, Kafka and Comics, Dies at 82
abstract: Translating is “like acting,” said Ms. Bell, the rare practitioner who became a well-known name in her own right.

name: Shirin Aliabadi
profession: Iranian Artist With a Focus on Women
headline: Shirin Aliabadi, Iranian Artist With a Focus on Women, Dies at 45
abstract: Her work depicted young women negotiating their modern, slightly rebellious impulses within the strictures of the Islamic Republic.

name: Evelyn Anthony
headline: Evelyn Anthony, Writer of Spy Thrillers, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Anthony was one of the few women to explore the espionage genre. “I am basically an entertainer, and I’m very proud of it,” she said.

name: Lisbeth Palme
headline: Lisbeth Palme, Witness to an Assassination, Dies at 87
abstract: A noted advocate for children, she was also a key part of long-running efforts to find the killer of her husband, Sweden’s prime minister.

name: Dick Modzelewski
profession: Key Lineman in a Vaunted Giants Defense
headline: Dick Modzelewski, Key Lineman in a Vaunted Giants Defense, Dies at 87
abstract: He played tackle in a unit that transformed defensive players into glamorous football figures during the team’s glory years of the late 1950s and early ’60s.

name: David Posner
profession: Senior Rabbi of Flagship Reform Synagogue
headline: David Posner, Senior Rabbi of Flagship Reform Synagogue, Dies at 70
abstract: A scholar and a pastor, Rabbi Posner served for 40 years at Temple Emanu-El in Manhattan, giving succor to the sick and reaching out to other faiths.

name: Walter Kwok
headline: Walter Kwok, Hong Kong Developer Who Survived Kidnapping, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Kwok led the development giant Sun Hung Kai Properties with his brothers, but was later ousted from the family business.

name: Joachim Ronneberg
headline: Joachim Ronneberg, Leader of Raid That Thwarted a Nazi Atomic Bomb, Dies at 99
abstract: The Norwegian resistance fighter commanded a daring World War II mission to blow up a heavy-water plant and help sabotage Hitler’s nuclear program.

name: Wen C. Fong
profession: Shaper of Met Museums Asian Collection
headline: Wen C. Fong, Shaper of Met Museum’s Asian Collection, Dies at 88
abstract: In building a world-renowned collection, Professor Fong counseled collectors, philanthropists and curators. He also taught at Princeton for 40 years.

name: Robert Faurisson
headline: Robert Faurisson, Holocaust Denier Prosecuted by French, Dies at 89
abstract: A former literature professor, he was an obscure anti-Semitic propagandist until a respected newspaper published an article by him, causing an uproar.

name: Cornelius E. Gallagher
headline: Cornelius E. Gallagher, 7-Term New Jersey Congressman, Dies at 97
abstract: A champion of civil liberties and privacy, he wound up shadowed by corruption charges and was jettisoned by the Democratic Party.

name: Charles B. Wang
profession: Software Entrepreneur and New York Islanders Owner
headline: Charles B. Wang, Software Entrepreneur and New York Islanders Owner, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Wang was an entrepreneur and deal-maker who built a multibillion-dollar software business, then was a majority owner of the New York Islanders.

name: Gertrude Mokotoff
headline: Gertrude Mokotoff, Ex-Mayor and a Bride at 98, Is Dead at 100
abstract: A Vows article in The Times about her wedding to Alvin Mann, then 94, drew a wide readership. They had met at the gym.

name: Todd Bol
profession: Creator of Little Free Library Movement
headline: Todd Bol, Creator of Little Free Library Movement, Dies at 62
abstract: He built a wooden box, filled it with books and stuck it in his front yard; today there are more than 75,000 like it in 88 countries, run under the honor system.

name: Eugene H. Peterson
headline: Eugene H. Peterson, 85, Scholar Turned Homespun Pastor, Dies
abstract: Mr. Peterson produced 30 books, including a wildly popular colloquial version of the Bible, and eschewed megachurches and televised preaching.

name: Tom Jago
profession: in the Spirits Industry, a Maker of Best Sellers
headline: Tom Jago Dies at 93; in the Spirits Industry, a Maker of Best Sellers
abstract: His hand could be found in Baileys Irish Cream, Malibu Rum and Johnnie Walker Blue. He was so revered, Scotch lovers named him a Master of the Quaich.

name: Tony Hoagland
headline: Tony Hoagland, Poet With a Wry Outlook, Is Dead at 64
abstract: Though he took poetry seriously, he wasn’t afraid to go for a laugh.

name: Danny Leiner
headline: Danny Leiner, Director Known for Stoner Films, Is Dead at 57
abstract: His breakout movie was “Dude, Where’s My Car?” It was followed, four years later, by the first “Harold & Kumar” film.

name: Annapurna Devi
headline: Annapurna Devi, Acclaimed but Reclusive Indian Musician, Dies at 91
abstract: Her performances with her husband at the time, Ravi Shankar, were acclaimed, but there were only a few of them.

name: Rose Zar
headline: Overlooked No More: Rose Zar, a Holocaust Survivor Who Hid in Plain Sight
abstract: Zar worked in the home of a Nazi commander and saved dozens of Jewish orphans, then moved to the United States and shared her life story.

name: Osamu Shimomura
profession: Won Nobel for Finding a Glowing Protein
headline: Osamu Shimomura, 90, Dies; Won Nobel for Finding a Glowing Protein
abstract: Dr. Shimomura isolated a green-glowing protein from jellyfish. It became a major element of biological research, lighting up the inner workings of cells.

name: Albert K. Smiley III
headline: Albert K. Smiley III, 74, Keeper of Mohonk Mountain House, Dies
abstract: He nudged the hotel, which had been in the family for generations, into the modern world while maintaining its Victorian traditions and its commitment to conservation.

name: Wanda Ferragamo
profession: Reigned Over Familys Luxury Goods Empire
headline: Wanda Ferragamo, 96, Dies; Reigned Over Family’s Luxury Goods Empire
abstract: Taking over her husband’s shoe business after his death in 1960, she and her children transformed it into a billion-dollar global enterprise.

name: James Karen
headline: James Karen, Veteran Actor and ‘Pathmark Man,’ Dies at 94
abstract: A classic character actor, he had some 200 film and television credits but may have been best known in the Northeast for supermarket commercials.

name: Dorcas Reilly
profession: Creator of the Classic American Green-Bean Casserole
headline: Dorcas Reilly, Creator of the Classic American Green-Bean Casserole, Dies at 92
abstract: Mrs. Reilly invented the dish when she worked at the Campbell Soup Company test kitchen in the 1950s.

name: Earl E. Bakken
headline: Earl E. Bakken, Pacemaker Inventor and Medtronic Founder, Dies at 94
abstract: Starting in a garage, where he invented the battery-powered pacemaker, he and a brother-in-law created the world’s largest medical device company.

name: Msgr. Thomas P. Leonard
profession: Priest With Feet on the Ground
headline: Msgr. Thomas P. Leonard, 90, Priest With Feet on the Ground, Dies
abstract: He ministered in Manhattan to AIDS patients and the homeless and revitalized a struggling Upper West Side parish where he presided for 14 years.

name: Cicely Berry
headline: Cicely Berry, Who Taught Actors Shakespeare’s Sound, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Using unorthodox methods (walk around a room, speak it together), she helped actors find their voices by feeling the weight and rhythms of the words.

name: Gilberto Benetton
headline: Gilberto Benetton, 77, Dies; Expanded Family Clothing Company
abstract: Starting with a brand known for colors and provocative ads, he helped build a $13.6 billion holding company comprising infrastructure, real estate and more.

name: Tyrone Gayle
profession: Spokesman for Senators and Hillary Clinton
headline: Tyrone Gayle, 30, Spokesman for Senators and Hillary Clinton, Dies
abstract: Mr. Gayle, Senator Kamala Harris’s press secretary, had worked on Mrs. Clinton’s 2016 presidential campaign and Tim Kaine’s 2012 Senate campaign.

name: Thomas Keating
headline: Rev. Thomas Keating, Pioneer in Contemplative Movement, Dies at 95
abstract: He willingly went from riches to rags, walking away from privilege to a monastic life, only to be rewarded with spiritual riches.

name: Ntozake Shange
headline: Ntozake Shange, Who Wrote ‘For Colored Girls,’ Is Dead at 70
abstract: Ms. Shange’s play featured seven black female characters named for the colors of the rainbow and inspired generations of playwrights.

name: Ana González
headline: Ana González, Campaigner for Chile’s Missing, Dies at 93
abstract: After four members of her family disappeared under the Pinochet dictatorship, she crusaded tirelessly on behalf of other families who lost loved ones.

name: Rico J. Puno
profession: Soul Music Pioneer in the Philippines
headline: Rico J. Puno, Soul Music Pioneer in the Philippines, Dies at 65
abstract: Known as Macho Gwapito, or Little Handsome, Mr. Puno helped create a distinctive brand of soul music in the Philippines.

name: Whitey Bulger
headline: Whitey Bulger Is Dead in Prison at 89; Long-Hunted Boston Mob Boss
abstract: One of America’s most wanted gangsters for 16 years, he was beaten to death by fellow inmates in West Virginia. His murderous life inspired books and films.

name: Dionisio Lind
headline: Dionisio Lind, Whose Voice Was a Mighty Carillon, Dies at 87
abstract: For decades, Mr. Lind played at the Riverside Church and at St. Martin’s Episcopal in Harlem, sounding their bells far and wide.

name: Horacio Cardo
headline: Horacio Cardo, Illustrator With a Political Edge, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Mr. Cardo’s phantasmagorical paintings and collages offered compelling commentary on war, social issues and Freudian psychoanalysis.

name: William Wheeler
headline: William Wheeler, New York Mass Transit Visionary, Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Wheeler oversaw the strategic planning that led to, among other things, the MetroCard and countdown clocks for subways and buses.

name: María Irene Fornés
headline: María Irene Fornés, Writer of Spare, Poetic Plays, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Fornés won acclaim and awards for her experimental works. But her fellow playwrights often said her achievements far outstripped her fame.

name: Mel Ramos
profession: Painter of Female Nudes and Comic Heroes
headline: Mel Ramos, Painter of Female Nudes and Comic Heroes, Dies at 83
abstract: In his precisely painted portraits of unclothed women, Mr. Ramos tiptoed on the line between Pop Art and smut.

name: Phylis Bamberger
headline: Phylis Bamberger, Who Challenged Brutality at Attica, Dies at 79
abstract: As a Legal Aid lawyer, she won a suit to protect inmates who faced reprisals from guards after the deadly 1971 prison uprising. She later became a judge.

name: Miki Gorman
headline: Overlooked No More: Miki Gorman, the Unlikely Marathon Winner
abstract: Gorman at 40, was self-conscious about her body and had recently given birth when she entered the New York City Marathon. Her win made her that much more of a pioneer for women in the sport.

name: Victor Marchetti
profession: Book Was First to Be Censored by C.I.A
headline: Victor Marchetti, 88, Dies; Book Was First to Be Censored by C.I.A.
abstract: A former employee of the agency, he ran afoul of it as co-author of a book about its inner workings. It led to a landmark First Amendment fight.

name: Willie McCovey
profession: Hall of Fame Slugger With the Giants
headline: Willie McCovey, 80, Dies; Hall of Fame Slugger With the Giants
abstract: A revered figure in San Francisco who hit 521 home runs in 22 seasons.

name: Bernard Bragg
profession: Showed the Way for Deaf Actors
headline: Bernard Bragg, Who Showed the Way for Deaf Actors, Dies at 90
abstract: His achievements included helping to found the National Theater of the Deaf. The actress Marlee Matlin was one of his protégés.

name: Sonny Fortune
headline: Sonny Fortune, Saxophonist of Urgency and Grace, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Fortune was an essential member of bands led by Miles Davis, Elvin Jones, McCoy Tyner and Mongo Santamaria as well as a gifted bandleader.

name: Cot Campbell
headline: Cot Campbell, Colorful Horse Racing Innovator, Is Dead at 91
abstract: A dapper raconteur in racing world, he established a system of shared ownership of thoroughbreds, bringing a bit of democracy to the sport of kings.

name: Teodoro Petkoff
headline: Teodoro Petkoff, Reconstructed Venezuelan Rebel, Is Dead at 86
abstract: He evolved from Marxist guerrilla to government minister to fiercely independent critic of his country’s authoritarian president, Hugo Chavez.

name: Wah Wah Watson
headline: Wah Wah Watson, Guitarist Whose Sound Was Everywhere, Dies at 67
abstract: He worked the wah-wah pedal with prodigious and playful subtlety on songs by the Temptations, Marvin Gaye, Maxwell, Herbie Hancock and many others.

name: Lodi Gyari
profession: Top Envoy for the Dalai Lama
headline: Lodi Gyari, Top Envoy for the Dalai Lama, Dies at 69
abstract: For decades, Mr. Gyari led fruitless negotiations with China over the status of Tibet and promoted his homeland’s cause in Washington.

name: Jun Ashida
headline: Jun Ashida, Who Dressed Japanese Royalty, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Ashida, a self-effacing designer, synthesized Western styles and traditional Japanese sensibilities in creating his clothing collections.

name: Jin Yong
profession: Lionized Author of Chinese Martial Arts Epics
headline: Jin Yong, 94, Lionized Author of Chinese Martial Arts Epics, Dies
abstract: He created widely popular panoramic fictional universes that inspired movies and video games and that have led some to compare him to J.R.R. Tolkien.

name: Mario Segale
headline: Mario Segale, Developer Who Inspired Nintendo to Name Super Mario, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Segale rented a warehouse near Seattle to Nintendo in the company’s early days, and once berated its president about unpaid rent.

name: Milton Gendel
profession: Art Critic and Photographer Took Root in Rome
headline: Milton Gendel, 99, Dies; Art Critic and Photographer Took Root in Rome
abstract: An American in Rome, he became a force in the art world and a photographer who captured la dolce vita Italy and Queen Elizabeth II feeding her dogs.

name: Carlene Roberts Lawrence
headline: Carlene Roberts Lawrence, Air Industry Pioneer, Dies at 105
abstract: In 1951, at a time when few women were being admitted into the executive suites of any industry, she became a vice president of American Airlines.

name: Paul Zimmerman
headline: Paul Zimmerman (Dr. Z) Dies at 86; Chronicled Football’s Complexity
abstract: For almost 30 years at Sports Illustrated, he gained a national voice dissecting play-calling and writing revealing profiles of players and coaches.

name: Hardy Fox
headline: Hardy Fox, of the Avant-Garde Band the Residents (Maybe), Dies at 73
abstract: He never admitted that he performed with the group, whose members remained anonymous behind masks as they playfully subverted rock conventions for decades.

name: Roy Hargrove
headline: Roy Hargrove, Trumpeter Who Gave Jazz a Jolt of Youth, Dies at 49
abstract: With virtuosic creative power, Mr. Hargrove retooled and reinvigorated jazz traditions for a new generation, earning wide respect and acclaim.

name: Raymond Chow
headline: Raymond Chow, Movie Producer Who Popularized Kung Fu Stars, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Chow, who co-founded the Golden Harvest studio, helped propel Bruce Lee and Jackie Chan to global fame.

name: Judith Kazantzis
headline: Judith Kazantzis, British Feminist Poet and Activist, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Kazantzis found freedom from the drudgery of being a housewife by breaking down patriarchal norms and writing about people who faced injustices.

name: William J. Murtagh
headline: William J. Murtagh, Lion of Historic Preservation, Dies at 95
abstract: Trained in architecture, he became the first “keeper” of the National Register of Historic Places, created teaching programs and wrote a leading text book.

name: Ruth Gates
profession: Made Saving Coral Reefs Her Mission
headline: Ruth Gates, Who Made Saving Coral Reefs Her Mission, Is Dead at 56
abstract: A marine biologist, Dr. Gates worked to develop a “super coral” to resist the deadening effects of warming ocean waters.

name: Kitty O’Neil
headline: Kitty O’Neil, Stuntwoman and Speed Racer, Is Dead at 72
abstract: Her deafness was no hindrance as she broke the land-speed record for women, one highlight of a life in daredevilry. “Deaf people,” she said, “can do anything.”

name: Muriel Manings
profession: Dancer in a Politically Charged Era
headline: Muriel Manings, Dancer in a Politically Charged Era, Dies at 95
abstract: She was part of the New Dance Group, which infused its dances with left-leaning ideas and sought to bring movement to the people.

name: Evelyn Y. Davis
headline: Evelyn Y. Davis, Shareholder Scourge of C.E.O.s, Dies at 89
abstract: For more than 50 years she harangued executives, sometimes wearing a costume to make a point. And sometimes this gadfly got results.

name: Christopher Lehmann-Haupt
headline: Christopher Lehmann-Haupt, 84, Long-Serving Times Book Critic, Dies
abstract: Over three decades he wrote some 4,000 reviews and essays that influenced literary careers and book sales nationally. He later wrote obituaries of authors.

name: Barbara Jonas
headline: Barbara Jonas, Who Traded Art Collecting for Philanthropy, Dies at 84
abstract: She and her husband began a family foundation to improve nursing, help veterans and protect children from environmental hazards.

name: Jackie Mitchell
headline: Overlooked No More: Jackie Mitchell, Who Fanned Two of Baseball’s Greats
abstract: Mitchell was a 17-year-old pitcher in 1931 when she struck out Babe Ruth and Lou Gehrig in an exhibition game, but questions about that exploit linger.

name: Dave Pickerell
headline: Dave Pickerell, Master of Whiskey and Rye, Is Dead at 62
abstract: Once nicknamed the Johnny Appleseed of American whiskey, Mr. Pickerell played a central role in the growth of Maker’s Mark bourbon.

name: Devah Pager
profession: Documented Race Bias in Job Market
headline: Devah Pager, Who Documented Race Bias in Job Market, Dies at 46
abstract: Her research established that a white man, even if he had a felony conviction, fared better when applying for a job than a black man with no criminal record.

name: Jean Mohr
headline: Jean Mohr, Photographer Who Found Heart Amid Bleakness, Dies at 93
abstract: He toured the world, often to record the aftermath of calamity, and collaborated on books with acclaimed writers.

name: Raymond Plank
headline: Raymond Plank, 96, Coal Miner’s Son Who Became an Oil Tycoon, Dies
abstract: An eyewitness to atomic warfare as a combat pilot, he returned home to help found Apache, one of the nation’s largest independent oil and gas concerns.

name: John Maguire
profession: Early Promoter of Diversity in Education
headline: John Maguire, 86, Early Promoter of Diversity in Education, Dies
abstract: As a Southern youth he was “a white oppressor,” he said. But he had an awakening, and became a pioneer in making a racial mix a college admissions goal.

name: Juris Jurjevics
headline: Juris Jurjevics, Enterprising Publisher and Novelist, Dies at 75
abstract: A Latvian refugee, he helped found Soho Press, a champion of emerging authors, and edited James Baldwin’s last novel. His own writing career came later.

name: Gérald Bloncourt
headline: Gérald Bloncourt, Haitian Photographer and Activist, Dies at 91
abstract: “I am protesting against poverty,” Mr. Bloncourt said of his pictures of Portuguese immigrants who lived in squalor in France.

name: Ron Johnson
headline: Ron Johnson, Record-Setting Giants Running Back, Dies at 71
abstract: Johnson twice rushed for more than 1,000 yards in the 1970s, when the Giants struggled to win. He is tied for the team record of four touchdowns in a game.

name: Oskar Rabin
headline: Oskar Rabin, Defiant Artist During Soviet Era, Dies at 90
abstract: He was an organizer of what became known as the Bulldozer Exhibition, after the authorities used heavy equipment to sweep away forbidden art.

name: Louise DeSalvo
headline: Louise DeSalvo, Memoirist and Virginia Woolf Scholar, Dies at 76
abstract: She initially avoided writing about the traumas in her life, focusing instead on the food. “Life is too short for even one bad meal,” she wrote.

name: Stan Lee
headline: Stan Lee Is Dead at 95; Superhero of Marvel Comics
abstract: Mr. Lee helped create Spider-Man, the X-Men, the Fantastic Four, Iron Man and others while overseeing his company’s emergence as a media behemoth.

name: Douglas Rain
profession: Shakespearean and Voice of Computer Named HAL
headline: Douglas Rain, 90, Shakespearean and Voice of Computer Named HAL, Dies
abstract: Mr. Rain was a regular on the stage at the Stratford Festival for decades, but he was perhaps best known for his chilly voice in “2001: A Space Odyssey.”

name: Herbert London
headline: Herbert London, Conservative Savant and Social Critic, Dies at 79
abstract: A New York University dean and professor, he also advanced his views running for governor and comptroller of New York State and heading think tanks.

name: David Pearson
profession: Silver Fox of Stock Car Racing
headline: David Pearson, ‘Silver Fox’ of Stock Car Racing, Dies at 83
abstract: A low-key Nascar Hall of Famer who won more races than any driver except Richard Petty.

name: Barry Rand
headline: Barry Rand, Barrier-Breaking Chief Executive, Is Dead at 74
abstract: After being passed over at Xerox, he became one of the few African-American chief executives of a Fortune 500 company when he took control of Avis.

name: John Marttila
headline: John Marttila, Strategist Who Helped Biden and Kerry, Dies at 78
abstract: A refugee from Republican politics in Detroit, he plotted the campaigns of progressive Democrats, black mayors and anti-Vietnam War candidates.

name: Naomi Breslau
headline: Naomi Breslau, Who Studied Post-Traumatic Stress, Dies at 86
abstract: She also investigated links between various disorders, like depression and smoking, and suggested that migraines could cause mental problems — and vice versa.

name: Caroline Rose Hunt
headline: Caroline Rose Hunt, 95, Dies; Turned Inheritance Into Vast Wealth
abstract: An heiress to a Texas oil fortune, she protected her assets as her brothers went bust trying to corner silver, and she quietly built a real fortune.

name: Dorothy Cheney
headline: Dorothy Cheney, Who Studied Primates Up Close, Dies at 68
abstract: Her research with her husband, Robert Seyfarth, found that baboons and vervet monkeys had more complex social relationships than previously thought.

name: Pandita Ramabai
headline: Overlooked No More: Pandita Ramabai, Indian Scholar, Feminist and Educator
abstract: Ramabai traveled around India in the 19th century to give lectures on women’s emancipation and established one of the country’s first women’s shelters and schools.

name: Roy Clark
profession: Face of Country Music on Hee Haw
headline: Roy Clark Is Dead at 85; a Face of Country Music on ‘Hee Haw’
abstract: He and Buck Owens were hosts of a long-running prime-time TV variety show that helped bring country music into mainstream American pop culture.

name: Herbert Fingarette
headline: Herbert Fingarette, Contrarian Philosopher on Alcoholism, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Fingarette concluded that heavy drinking was willful behavior, not a disease, and that moderate use of alcohol was an acceptable treatment goal.

name: H. Peter Stern
profession: Co-Founder of Storm King Art Center
headline: H. Peter Stern, 90, Co-Founder of Storm King Art Center, Dies
abstract: “Works of art should not be seen in isolation,” said Mr. Stern, who joined with his father-in-law to create a vast outdoor sculpture garden.

name: William Goldman
headline: William Goldman, Screenwriting Star and Hollywood Skeptic, Dies at 87
abstract: He won Oscars for “Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid” and “All the President’s Men.” But his jaundiced view of the movie business was well known.

name: Jerry Ohlinger
headline: Jerry Ohlinger, Colorful Dealer in Film Memorabilia, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Ohlinger’s Movie Material Store in Manhattan was famous for its whimsical clutter and its vast collection of posters and stills.

name: Zhores Medvedev
headline: Zhores Medvedev, 93, Dissident Scientist Who Felt Moscow’s Boot, Is Dead
abstract: A biologist and writer who dared to challenge Soviet pseudoscience, he was declared insane, confined to an institution and stripped of his citizenship.

name: Mayra Langdon Riesman
headline: Mayra Langdon Riesman, Movie Website Creator, Dies at 64
abstract: The Film Scouts website let Ms. Riesman indulge her love of movies but also showed her early prescience about the power of the internet.

name: Linda Tarnay
headline: Linda Tarnay, Dancer and Teacher of Generations, Dies at 75
abstract: She was seen frequently in modern dance works in New York beginning in the 1960s and taught at N.Y.U. for 38 years.

name: Ramona Ripston
headline: Ramona Ripston, California Civil Liberties Champion, Dies at 91
abstract: She expanded the A.C.L.U’s mission to encompass civil rights, including matters of racial, social and economic justice.

name: Aldyr Schlee
profession: Created Brazil Soccer Teams Iconic Jersey
headline: Aldyr Schlee, 83, Dies; Created Brazil Soccer Team’s Iconic Jersey
abstract: Mr. Schlee won a contest, though he was skeptical about the rules: The jersey design had to use the blue, green, white and yellow of Brazil’s flag.

name: Andrew Fitzgerald
profession: Saved Men From a Storm-Sundered Ship
headline: Andrew Fitzgerald, Who Saved Men From a Storm-Sundered Ship, Dies at 87
abstract: He was the last surviving member of a four-man Coast Guard crew who braved monstrous seas off Cape Cod in 1952 to save 32 seamen clinging to half a tanker.

name: Fernando del Paso
headline: Fernando del Paso, Expansive Mexican Writer, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. del Paso, whose novels were rife with digressions, allusions and metaphors stacked on metaphors, won the prestigious Miguel de Cervantes Prize in 2015.

name: Jerry Frankel
headline: Jerry Frankel, Prolific Broadway Producer, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Frankel, a former dress manufacturer, produced more than 50 plays and musicals with various partners and won nine Tony Awards.

name: Blanche Burton-Lyles
headline: Blanche Burton-Lyles, Pianist and Flame Keeper, Dies at 85
abstract: After her own performing career, which began when she was a child, she promoted the legacy of the woman who had encouraged her, Marian Anderson.

name: Dennis Wrong
profession: One of the Last of the New York Intellectuals
headline: Dennis Wrong, 94, One of the Last of the ‘New York Intellectuals,’ Dies
abstract: Part of a mid-20th-century cadre of sophists, he wrote prodigiously, and iconoclastically, in left-leaning journals while earning distinction as a sociologist.

name: Michael O’Neal
headline: Michael O’Neal, Civic-Minded Manhattan Restaurateur, Dies at 82
abstract: With his brother, the actor Patrick O’Neal, he ran the Ginger Man and O’Neal’s Baloon near Lincoln Center and popularized the American bistro.

name: James H. Billington
profession: Led Library of Congress Into Digital Age
headline: James H. Billington, 89, Dies; Led Library of Congress Into Digital Age
abstract: Overseeing the nation’s treasure house of knowledge for three decades, he almost doubled its holdings but resigned in 2015, stung by cries of mismanagement.

name: Pablo Ferro
headline: Pablo Ferro, Who Energized Films’ Opening Credits, Dies at 83
abstract: Beginning with “Dr. Strangelove,” he found attention-getting ways to make title sequences more than just a list of names.

name: Lilian Rice
headline: Overlooked No More: Lilian Rice, Architect Who Lifted a Style in California
abstract: In the 1920s, Rice brought her design aesthetic to a small village north of San Diego. Those who live there continue to respect her vision.

name: Jane Maas
headline: Jane Maas, a Pioneer for Women in Advertising, Dies at 86
abstract: A product of the “Mad Men” era who was once called “the real Peggy Olson,” she handled the revivifying “I Love New York” campaign and held top agency jobs.

name: Tommy Rowles
headline: Tommy Rowles, 78, Dies; Bartender to the Prominent (and Others)
abstract: For 53 years, Mr. Rowles served drinks at Bemelmans Bar in the Carlyle hotel. His drink menu eventually included one named after him.

name: Janet Paisley
headline: Janet Paisley, Scottish Writer Who Drew on Family Abuse, Dies at 70
abstract: Many Ms. Paisley’s poems, plays and fiction plumbed the depths of domestic violence, a subject she knew all too well.

name: Donald McCaig
profession: Followed Up Gone With the Wind
headline: Donald McCaig, Who Followed Up ‘Gone With the Wind,’ Dies at 78
abstract: His book, “Rhett Butler’s People,” was a best seller. He was also known for titles inspired by the Border collies on his sheep ranch in Virginia.

name: José Peralta
profession: First Dominican-American Elected to New York State Senate
headline: José Peralta, First Dominican-American Elected to New York State Senate, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. Peralta served 16 years in the State Legislature but lost in a September primary as part of a breakaway group of Democrats who caucused with Republicans.

name: Olivia Hooker
profession: Witness to an Ugly Moment in History
headline: Olivia Hooker, 103, Dies; Witness to an Ugly Moment in History
abstract: She was a child in Tulsa, Okla., during an attack on a black section of the city in 1921. She later broke a racial barrier for the Coast Guard.

name: Lucho Gatica
headline: Lucho Gatica, ‘the King of Bolero,’ Is Dead at 90
abstract: A star throughout Latin America, Mr. Gatica helped enshrine a style of romantic balladry from the 19th century as a 20th-century pop craze.

name: Wolfgang Zuckermann
headline: Wolfgang Zuckermann, Harpsichord Do-It-Yourselfer, Dies at 96
abstract: Tired of tuning people’s harpsichords, he created a kit that let them build their own, placing himself in the middle of the instrument’s postwar renaissance.

name: Bernard Glassman
headline: Bernard Glassman, Zen Master and Social Activist, Dies at 79
abstract: A practitioner of “Engaged Buddhism,” he hired the unemployable; provided job training, child care and housing; and developed retreats at Auschwitz.

name: Bob McNair
headline: Bob McNair, Energy Mogul Who Brought the N.F.L. Back to Houston, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. McNair, who was awarded the franchise that became the Texans, gave to many charitable causes. More recently, he was criticized for remarks about national anthem protests.

name: Nicolas Roeg
headline: Nicolas Roeg, Director of ‘The Man Who Fell to Earth,’ Dies at 90
abstract: He liked to put music stars in his films, including David Bowie and Mick Jagger. Among his other admired 1970s movies were “Don’t Look Now” and “Walkabout.”

name: Betty Bumpers
headline: Betty Bumpers, Campaigner for Childhood Vaccinations, Dies at 93
abstract: Using her influence as an Arkansas first lady and senator’s wife, she earned national recognition for her efforts to promote immunizations.

name: Ricky Jay
headline: Ricky Jay, Gifted Magician, Actor and Author, Is Dead at 72
abstract: Mr. Jay, described as “the most gifted sleight-of-hand artist alive,” also acted in 40 or so films and television shows, including “Boogie Nights.”

name: Willie Naulls
headline: Willie Naulls, Knicks All-Star and Celtics Champion, Dies at 84
abstract: Naulls was an All-American at U.C.L.A. and one of pro basketball’s early black stars, playing on three championship teams.

name: Bernardo Bertolucci
profession: Director of Last Tango in Paris
headline: Bernardo Bertolucci, Director of ‘Last Tango in Paris,’ Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Bertolucci’s early work reflected the revolutionary spirit of the 1960s and ’70s, in particular the shifting social and sexual mores of the times.

name: Meena Alexander
headline: Meena Alexander, Poet Who Wrote of Dislocation, Dies at 67
abstract: Born in India and later a resident of Africa, Europe and the United States, she explored themes of feminism, post-colonialism and the search for identity.

name: Stephen Hillenburg
headline: Stephen Hillenburg, ‘SpongeBob SquarePants’ Creator, Dies at 57
abstract: His cartoon show, loved by the 12-and-under crowd and by many much older fans as well, spawned two movies and a Tony-nominated Broadway musical.

name: Tom Margittai
headline: Tom Margittai, Who Revitalized the Four Seasons, Dies at 90
abstract: He and his business partner, Paul Kovi, converted a struggling Manhattan restaurant into a 20th-century culinary landmark and home of the power lunch.

name: Trumpington
headline: Lady Trumpington, Code Breaker and Irreverent Politician, Dies at 96
abstract: A Bletchley Park worker during World War II and a New York socialite in the 1950s, she became a government minister and a celebrity in her 90s.

name: Harold O. Levy
profession: Progressive New York City Schools Chief
headline: Harold O. Levy, Progressive New York City Schools Chief, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Levy, who was the chancellor of New York City’s vast public school system from 2000 to 2002, attracted thousands of new teachers by insisting on higher starting wages.

name: Randolph Braham
headline: Randolph Braham, 95, Holocaust Scholar Who Saw a Whitewash, Dies
abstract: A survivor himself, he was an expert on the persecution of Jews in Hungary, his homeland, and defied nationalist efforts to play down that country’s role.

name: Mujahid Farid
headline: Mujahid Farid, 69, Ex-Prisoner Who Advocated for Older Inmates, Dies
abstract: He was denied parole nine times. Once released, he helped push New York State to take prisoners’ age into account when considering parole.

name: Nancy Cappello
headline: Nancy Cappello, Breast Cancer Activist, Is Dead at 66
abstract: A survivor of the disease, she fought for fuller disclosure of mammogram results — something she did not get. She died from complications of her treatment.

name: Noor Inayat Khan
headline: Overlooked No More: Noor Inayat Khan, Indian Princess and British Spy
abstract: Khan, who was recently suggested as the new face of the £50 note, was an unlikely candidate to engage in espionage in World War II, but she did so with a “steely strength of will.”

name: Gerald Berenson
headline: Dr. Gerald Berenson, 96, Dies; Traced Heart Disease to Childhood
abstract: He was the chief researcher of the marathon Bogalusa Heart Study, which found that reducing childhood risk factors could allay cardiac conditions in adults.

name: Patricia Quintana
headline: Patricia Quintana, Champion of Mexican Cuisine, Dies at 72
abstract: She pushed back against stereotypes in her cooking, her books and her destination restaurant, drawing on indigenous ingredients and her training in Paris.

name: Gloria Katz
headline: Gloria Katz, a Writer of ‘American Graffiti,’ Is Dead at 76
abstract: She and her husband, Willard Huyck, also worked on “Indiana Jones and the Temple of Doom” and “Howard the Duck,” and did uncredited work on “Star Wars.”

name: Harry Leslie Smith
headline: Harry Leslie Smith, ‘World’s Oldest Rebel,’ Is Dead at 95
abstract: He survived the Great Depression. He fought the Nazis in World War II. And at 87 he turned to writing and agitating, and acquired a loyal following.

name: Nina Beilina
headline: Nina Beilina, Soviet Violinist and Festival Founder, Dies at 81
abstract: Concerned about diminishing opportunities for Jews in her homeland, she emigrated to the United States and started over.

name: Aaron Klug
profession: His 3-D Images of Bodily Molecules Won a Nobel
headline: Aaron Klug, 92, Dies; His 3-D Images of Bodily Molecules Won a Nobel
abstract: Born in Lithuania, raised in South Africa and working in Britain, he made large strides in understanding the structure of proteins, DNA and more.

name: George Bush
headline: George Bush, Who Steered Nation in Tumultuous Times, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Mr. Bush, a Republican, was a transitional figure in the White House, where he served from 1989 to 1993. He was the last of the World War II generation to occupy the Oval Office.

name: Cyril Pahinui
headline: Cyril Pahinui, Who Carried a Hawaiian Guitar Legacy, Dies at 68
abstract: The son of a pioneer of slack-key guitar, he preserved and extended the tradition, carrying secrets of a family style to the world.

name: Thomas Altizer
headline: Thomas Altizer, 91, Proponent of ‘God Is Dead’ Theology, Dies
abstract: “He was one of the country’s most hated, misunderstood, radical and prophetic voices of the past century,” one scholar said.

name: Ken Berry
profession: Star of F Troop and Mamas Family
headline: Ken Berry, Star of ‘F Troop’ and ‘Mama’s Family,’ Dies at 85
abstract: He aspired to be in movie musicals, but made a television career of playing nice guys who were often bumblers.

name: Robert Plotnik
headline: Robert Plotnik, ‘Bleecker Bob’ of Record-Store Fame, Dies at 75
abstract: His Greenwich Village shop, which he opened with a partner in Manhattan in 1967, helped to nurture punk rock and became a haven for fans and musicians alike.

name: Ruth Haring
headline: Ruth Haring, Top Chess Player Who Led Federation, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Haring played for the national women’s team in five consecutive Olympiads and was later a rare woman to lead the United States Chess Federation.

name: Paul Gregory
profession: Risk-Taking Showman in a Golden Age
headline: Paul Gregory, Risk-Taking Showman in a Golden Age, Is Dead at 95
abstract: His star rose in the 1950s and ’60s, when Broadway was ripe for experimentation. But he died in 2015 far from the limelight, and little notice was taken.

name: Philip Bosco
headline: Philip Bosco, Tony-Winning Character Actor, Is Dead at 88
abstract: A familiar face for years in movies, on television and especially on Broadway, he had a particular affinity for the work of George Bernard Shaw.

name: Charley Parkhurst
profession: Gold Rush Legend With a Hidden Identity
headline: Overlooked No More: Charley Parkhurst, Gold Rush Legend With a Hidden Identity
abstract: A swashbuckling, one-eyed stagecoach driver lived her life disguised as a man. After her death, the revelation that she was a woman provoked widespread astonishment.

name: Charles Harrison
headline: Charles Harrison, 87, Designer Who Reshaped the View-Master, Dies
abstract: He was part of the postwar golden age of industrial design, when newly prosperous families realized they needed the products they saw on television.

name: Robert Rainwater
headline: Robert Rainwater, Influential Art Curator, Is Dead at 75
abstract: He oversaw a vast expansion of the New York Public Library’s holdings in modern and contemporary prints, artist-made books and printed ephemera.

name: Sy Kattelson
profession: Photographer Made Art From Street Life
headline: Sy Kattelson Dies at 95; Photographer Made Art From Street Life
abstract: A member of the Photo League, he captured New York City life in its unguarded moments, creating nuanced, intimate pictures that brought him acclaim.

name: Andrei Bitov
headline: Andrei Bitov, Russian Writer Who Chose Not to Flee, Dies at 81
abstract: At a time when many of the Soviet Union’s greatest authors left the country, he stayed, despite sometimes incurring official wrath.

name: World’s Oldest Celebrity Chef
headline: World’s Oldest Celebrity Chef, an Indian Great-Grandma, Dies at 107
abstract: She presided over a spectacularly popular video channel, cooking emu eggs and pizza. Fans also loved her salt-of-the-earth sense of humor.

name: Paul Sherwen
profession: Became a Voice of the Tour de France
headline: Paul Sherwen, 62, Who Became a Voice of the Tour de France, Dies
abstract: For English-speaking television viewers, Mr. Sherwen, a former cyclist, and Phil Liggett provided the soundtrack of the sport’s biggest event.

name: Lisa Schwartz
headline: Dr. Lisa Schwartz, Critic of Medical Excess, Is Dead at 55
abstract: She and her husband, also a doctor, waged a campaign against “the medicalization of everyday life” and an “epidemic of diagnoses.”

name: Amanda Swimmer
profession: Potter and Keeper of Cherokee Traditions
headline: Amanda Swimmer, Potter and Keeper of Cherokee Traditions, Dies at 97
abstract: The recipient of numerous honors, Mrs. Swimmer was deeply respected by members of the Eastern Band of the Cherokee: “Everyone called her grandmother.”

name: P.M. Forni
headline: P.M. Forni, Who Argued for ‘Choosing Civility,’ Dies at 67
abstract: In two books he wrote about rudeness and how to avoid it. He also started a program to encourage the practice of good manners.

name: Albert Frère
headline: Albert Frère, 92, Belgian Master of Multinational Mergers, Dies
abstract: He parlayed the profits of his father’s nail factory into an investment portfolio worth billions.

name: Dawn Clements
profession: Put Her Life Into Her Panoramas
headline: Dawn Clements, Who Put Her Life Into Her Panoramas, Dies at 60
abstract: Ms. Clements recorded detailed scenes from her own life and from old movies, often in extremely large artworks in ink or paint.

name: Pete Shelley
headline: Pete Shelley, Leader of the Punk-Rock Buzzcocks, Dies at 63
abstract: His melodic and energetic songs, a fellow rocker said, influenced “multiple generations of lonesome hearts and weirdos.”

name: Palden Gyatso
headline: Palden Gyatso, Monk Who Suffered for a Free Tibet, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Gyatso said he endured decades of brutality in Chinese prisons. Once he escaped, he told the world his story and championed Tibetan independence.

name: Belisario Betancur
headline: Belisario Betancur, 95, Colombia President During Rebel Siege, Dies
abstract: Gabriel García Márquez described Mr. Betancur, a writer and professor who promoted peace, as “a poet on whom fate imposed the penance of power.”

name: Selma Engel
profession: Escaped Death Camp and Revealed Its Horror
headline: Selma Engel, 96, Dies; Escaped Death Camp and Revealed Its Horror
abstract: Speaking to Russian reporters in 1944, she helped provide the first public, detailed account of Sobibor, where most Jews were instantly gassed or shot.

name: Rosanell Eaton
headline: Rosanell Eaton, Fierce Voting Rights Advocate, Dies at 97
abstract: Calling her an unsung hero, President Barack Obama praised her and others for refusing “to accept anything less than a full measure of equality.”

name: Bob Bergland
headline: Bob Bergland, Agriculture Secretary Under Carter, Dies at 90
abstract: Raised in northern Minnesota, he was forced, as a young man, to leave his farm to find work, served in Congress and became an advocate for consumers as well as farmers.

name: Lyudmila Alexeyeva
profession: Grandmother of Russias Human Rights Movement
headline: Lyudmila Alexeyeva, ‘Grandmother’ of Russia’s Human Rights Movement, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Alexeyeva, who had been the most prominent surviving dissident of the Soviet era, spent a lifetime challenging abusive leaders.

name: Evelyn Berezin
profession: Built the First True Word Processor
headline: Evelyn Berezin, 93, Dies; Built the First True Word Processor
abstract: Her device freed secretaries from the typewriter. But as word processing became ubiquitous, it helped eliminate their jobs.

name: Sidney Horenstein
headline: Sidney Horenstein, 82, Geologist Who Wrung Stories From Stone, Dies
abstract: Working full-time for the American Museum of Natural History in New York, he was an author and tour guide whose exuberance brought fossils to life.

name: Alvin Epstein
headline: Alvin Epstein, Actor, Director and Master of Beckett, Dies at 93
abstract: In a long stage career that took him from Yale to Broadway, he was steeped in the author of “Waiting for Godot,” acting in its Broadway premiere in 1956.

name: Lothar Baumgarten
headline: Lothar Baumgarten Dies at 74; Artist Explored Collision of Cultures
abstract: Many of his conceptual pieces drew on the months he spent living with a tribe in the Amazon.

name: William Blum
profession: U.S. Policy Critic Cited by bin Laden
headline: William Blum, U.S. Policy Critic Cited by bin Laden, Dies at 85
abstract: He railed in relative obscurity against what he viewed as United States imperialism, until he received an unexpected endorsement from the founder of Al Qaeda.

name: Helen Klaben Kahn
headline: Helen Klaben Kahn, Survivor of a 49-Day Yukon Ordeal, Dies at 76
abstract: She was a 20-year-old Brooklynite seeking adventure when her plane crashed. But she and the pilot, both injured, endured in subzero weather until rescued.

name: Elizabeth Keckly
profession: Dressmaker and Confidante to Mary Todd Lincoln
headline: Overlooked No More: Elizabeth Keckly, Dressmaker and Confidante to Mary Todd Lincoln
abstract: Keckly was born a slave but bought her freedom and began working for the first lady. Her memoir offered a rare look inside the Lincoln White House.

name: Monique Pillard
headline: Monique Pillard, a Power in the Modeling World, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Working at two of the industry’s pre-eminent agencies, Ms. Pillard helped guide the careers of Cindy Crawford, Naomi Campbell and other supermodels.

name: Peter Boizot
headline: Peter Boizot, Founder of the PizzaExpress Chain, Dies at 89
abstract: He grew up on a limited diet, but in Italy he discovered pizza and took that love home to England, where an international success was born.

name: Melvin Dummar
profession: Claimed Howard Hughes Left Him Millions
headline: Melvin Dummar, 74, Who Claimed Howard Hughes Left Him Millions, Dies
abstract: As depicted in the film “Melvin and Howard,” he said he helped the billionaire out in the desert one night and that Hughes rewarded him handsomely.

name: William J. Conklin
headline: William J. Conklin, Architect With a Broad Stamp, Dies at 95
abstract: He worked on the planned community of Reston, Va., the Navy Memorial in Washington, the restoration of Brooklyn Borough Hall and what became Battery Park City.

name: Riccardo Giacconi
profession: Explorer of the Universe Through X-Rays
headline: Riccardo Giacconi, 87, Explorer of the Universe Through X-Rays, Dies
abstract: A Nobel laureate, he traced the X-rays emitted by black holes, exploding stars and other violent actors to help understand the workings of the cosmos.

name: Michael Paul Smith
profession: Founder of a Beloved Imaginary Town
headline: Michael Paul Smith, 67, Founder of a Beloved Imaginary Town, Dies
abstract: In carefully staged photographs made with miniature cars, tiny model buildings and a cheap camera, he created Elgin Park on Flickr. Millions have visited.

name: Sondra Locke
headline: Sondra Locke, 74, Is Dead; Oscar-Nominated Actress
abstract: Ms. Locke, who received an Academy Award nomination for her first film, “The Heart Is a Lonely Hunter,” starred in several movies with Clint Eastwood, with whom she had a turbulent relationship.

name: Nancy Wilson
headline: Nancy Wilson, Singer Who Bridged Jazz and Pop, Is Dead at 81
abstract: A three-time Grammy winner, Ms. Wilson liked to turn songs into stories, telling them through jazz ballads, Broadway show tunes and R&B torch songs.

name: Andrew Frierson
headline: Andrew Frierson, Pioneering Black Opera Singer, Dies at 94
abstract: A bass-baritone, he made his professional debut with the New York City Opera and later encouraged other black opera singers, especially men.

name: Joan Steinbrenner
headline: Joan Steinbrenner, 83, Yankees Vice-Chairwoman and Owner’s Widow, Dies
abstract: She held a front-office title and had an active philanthropic career. Her four children with George Steinbrenner are now general partners of the team.

name: Fred Greenstein
headline: Fred Greenstein, 88, Dies; Political ‘Psychologist’ Assessed Presidents
abstract: He identified six qualities in evaluating performance in the Oval Office. (No. 1: emotional intelligence.) And as a scholar of Eisenhower, he liked Ike.

name: Irwin Hollander
headline: Irwin Hollander, 90, Master Lithographer Who Revived Fine Art, Dies
abstract: Mr. Hollander persuaded Willem de Kooning, Robert Motherwell and other Abstract Expressionists to try their hands at lithography at his Manhattan workshop. Their proofs became some of his best work.

name: Meng Lang
headline: Meng Lang, Poet Who Promoted Dissident Writers, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Meng co-founded the Independent Chinese PEN Center, a nonprofit organization formed in 2011 to promote freedom of expression and publication.

name: Oribe Canales
profession: Celebrity Stylist in the Big Hair Era
headline: Oribe Canales, Celebrity Stylist in the Big Hair Era, Dies at 62
abstract: Known simply as Oribe, he helped define an ’80s and ’90s era of big hair, outsize glamour and downtown fun.

name: Lee Leonard
headline: Lee Leonard, TV Sports Show Host Who Ushered in ESPN, Dies at 89
abstract: A former disc jockey, Mr. Leonard brought a sophisticated style to hosting TV sports programs in New York (“Sports Extra”) and on ESPN and CNN.

name: Penny Marshall
profession: Laverne & Shirley Star and Movie Director
headline: Penny Marshall, ‘Laverne & Shirley’ Star and Movie Director, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Marshall made a mark in “Laverne & Shirley” and went on to direct “Big,” “Awakenings” and “A League of Their Own.”

name: Galt MacDermot
profession: Composer of the Rock Musical Hair
headline: Galt MacDermot, Composer of the Rock Musical ‘Hair,’ Dies at 89
abstract: He cut an unlikely figure in the 1960s milieu of “Hair,” not smoking pot and never having met a hippie. But his rock style and beat-driven sound fit right in.

name: John Ford Noonan
headline: John Ford Noonan, ‘Coupla White Chicks’ Playwright, Dies at 77
abstract: His plays, produced frequently in the 1970s, ’80s and ’90s, often threw polar opposites together to explore themes both comic and serious.

name: Gertrude Beasley
headline: Overlooked No More: Gertrude Beasley, Who Wrote an Uncompromising Memoir, Then Vanished
abstract: “Thirty years ago, I lay in the womb of a woman, conceived in a sexual act of rape,” the memoir begins. It disappeared, and so did Beasley.

name: Jerry Chesnut
headline: Jerry Chesnut, 87, Country Songwriter With Blue-Collar Hits, Dies
abstract: His songs have been sung by Loretta Lynn, Willie Nelson, George Jones, Johnny Cash, Dolly Parton, Jerry Lee Lewis and two Elvises: Presley and Costello.

name: Donald Moffat
headline: Donald Moffat, 87, a Top Actor Who Thrived in Second Billings, Dies
abstract: For a half-century Mr. Moffat, a transplanted Briton, was a lauded figure on stages and screens, whether performing Shakespeare or Tom Clancy.

name: Charles Weldon
headline: Charles Weldon, Who Led the Negro Ensemble Company, Dies at 78
abstract: An “accidental actor,” he found himself on Broadway almost immediately after his career began and went on to appear frequently onstage.

name: Raven Wilkinson
headline: Raven Wilkinson, 83, Is Dead; Black Ballerina Braved Segregated South
abstract: Ms. Wilkinson was one of the first African-Americans to dance with a major ballet company, joining Ballet Russe de Monte Carlo in the 1950s.

name: Shan Goshorn
headline: Shan Goshorn, Whose Cherokee Art Was Political, Dies at 61
abstract: A multimedia artist who was best known for weaving calls for human rights into her imaginative basketry — work that now resides in many museums.

name: Peter Masterson
headline: Peter Masterson, 84, a ‘Best Little Whorehouse’ Creator, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Masterson helped turn a magazine article about a bordello into a hit Broadway musical. He later directed the movie “The Trip to Bountiful.”

name: James Rogers
profession: Utility Chief and Clean Energy Advocate
headline: James Rogers, 71, Dies; Utility Chief and Clean Energy Advocate
abstract: As chief executive of Duke Energy, Mr. Rogers emerged as one of the industry’s most passionate supporters of sustainable energy.

name: Timothy C. May
headline: Timothy C. May, Early Advocate of Internet Privacy, Dies at 66
abstract: As the rabble-rousing leader of the Cypherpunks, his writings foreshadowed concerns about privacy and government control and movements like WikiLeaks.

name: Mel Hutchins
headline: Mel Hutchins, B.Y.U. All-American and N.B.A. All-Star, Dies at 90
abstract: He led Brigham Young to a championship in 1951, raising the university’s profile before turning pro. He was also part of a formidable sports family.

name: Audrey Geisel
profession: Dr. Seuss Widow and Keeper of His Flame
headline: Audrey Geisel, 97, Dies; Dr. Seuss’ Widow and Keeper of His Flame
abstract: She was deeply involved in marketing her husband’s works and managing his legacy, overseeing multiple commercial ventures. “You use it or you lose it,” she said.

name: Eleanor Maccoby
profession: Pathbreaker on How Boys and Girls Differ
headline: Eleanor Maccoby, Pathbreaker on How Boys and Girls Differ, Dies at 101
abstract: An eminent psychologist, she focused on various factors in the development of the sexes, finding that social settings magnified differences.

name: Justin Cartwright
headline: Justin Cartwright, Lauded South African Expatriate Novelist, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Cartwright garnered several of Britain’s most important literary recognitions, including the Whitbread Book Award and Hawthornden Prize.

name: Roberto Suazo Córdova
headline: Roberto Suazo Córdova, Ex-President of Honduras, Dies at 91
abstract: The first civilian president after a decade of military rule, he was seen by critics as too willing to serve the interests of the United States.

name: Yuan Mu
profession: Face of Chinas Tiananmen Square Crackdown
headline: Yuan Mu, Face of China’s Tiananmen Square Crackdown, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Yuan is remembered as the government spokesman who said that “not one person” died in the 1989 assault on protesters. Hundreds were reported killed.

name: Deborah Zall
headline: Deborah Zall, 84, Dies; Depicted Extraordinary Women in Dance
abstract: After studying with Martha Graham, Ms. Zall went on to create solo works praised for their intense theatricality.

name: Ricardo Barber
headline: Ricardo Barber, Cuban Actor Who Succeeded in New York, Dies at 81
abstract: He became a core member of the Spanish-language troupe Repertorio Español after leaving Cuba, where he had spent time in a forced-labor camp.

name: Wendy Beckett
headline: Sister Wendy Beckett, Nun Who Became a BBC Star, Dies at 88
abstract: She interrupted a cloistered life of prayer in England and soared to international stardom as one of the most improbable art critics in television history.

name: Larry Eisenberg
headline: Larry Eisenberg, 99, Dead; His Limericks Were Very Well Read
abstract: Given the chance, Dr. Eisenberg, a prolific and clever commenter on the news on The Times’s website, would undoubtedly have set this obituary to rhyme.

name: Jane Langton
headline: Jane Langton, Author of New England Mysteries, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Ms. Langton, who believed that a novel’s meaning “comes from an organic relationship with its setting,” also wrote children’s books and often did her own illustrations.

name: Sono Osato
headline: Sono Osato, Japanese-American Ballet Star, Is Dead at 99
abstract: She toured the world with the Ballets Russes de Monte Carlo, danced with the Ballet Theater and gained acclaim in two Broadway musicals.

name: Faith Hope Consolo
headline: Faith Hope Consolo, a Force in Retail Real Estate, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Ms. Consolo was known for brash self-promotion and for brokering deals that lured luxury retailers to Manhattan.

name: Amos Oz
headline: Amos Oz, Israeli Author and Peace Advocate, Dies at 79
abstract: One of Israel’s most prolific writers, he published numerous works of both fiction and nonfiction, and his writing was translated into more than 35 languages.

name: David Austin
headline: David Austin, Who Breathed Life Into the Rose, Is Dead at 92
abstract: He combined the strong aromas of old roses with the color and repeated flowerings of newer types, and upended the market by creating more than 200 varieties.

name: Ralph Koltai
headline: Ralph Koltai, Innovative Stage Designer, Is Dead at 94
abstract: His work in opera, theater and ballet cast aside traditional ideas of what sets should be — realistic and utilitarian — in favor of abstract designs that made a statement.

name: David M. O’Brien
headline: David M. O’Brien, Who Studied Supreme Court Politics, Dies at 67
abstract: His legal knowledge was extensive, but he never lost sight of the role played by politics in shaping the court’s decisions and, ultimately, the law.

name: Liza Redfield
headline: Liza Redfield, Who Broke a Broadway Barrier, Is Dead at 94
abstract: When she led the orchestra for “The Music Man” in 1960, she became the first woman to be hired as a full-time conductor for a Broadway show.

name: Shehu Shagari
headline: Shehu Shagari, Nigerian President During ’80s Oil Crisis, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Shagari sought to revive democratic rule, but military officers deposed him during a 1983 economic crisis caused by plummeting oil prices.

name: Lawrence Roberts
headline: Lawrence Roberts, Who Helped Design Internet’s Precursor, Dies at 81
abstract: Dr. Roberts worked with other engineers to create the underpinnings of the Arpanet, making many crucial decisions. But his work did not make him rich.

name: Nancy Roman
headline: Nancy Roman, ‘Mother of the Hubble’ Telescope, Dies at 93
abstract: As NASA’s chief of astronomy, Dr. Roman was the first woman in a leadership position at the agency and oversaw planning for the Hubble Space Telescope.

name: Bre Payton
profession: Conservative Writer and Fox News Commentator
headline: Bre Payton, Conservative Writer and Fox News Commentator, Dies at 26
abstract: She started writing for The Federalist in April 2015. The site said she quickly became a “rising star” who was regularly featured on Fox News.

name: June Whitfield
headline: June Whitfield, a Star of ‘Absolutely Fabulous,’ Dies at 93
abstract: As Mother, she looked like a proper London granny, but she liked to steal things. “She appears more grounded, but she’s as mad as the rest of them.”

name: Héctor Timerman
profession: Argentine Ex-Foreign Minister Indicted in Iran Deal
headline: Héctor Timerman, 65, Argentine Ex-Foreign Minister Indicted in Iran Deal, Dies
abstract: He was charged with treason over a pact with Iran involving the bombing of a Jewish community center in Buenos Aires. Prosecutors said it was a cover-up.

name: Warren Wells
profession: Star Receiver With a Derailed Career
headline: Warren Wells, Star Receiver With a Derailed Career, Dies at 76
abstract: Wells was a deep threat for the vaunted Oakland offenses of the late 1960s, but his playing days ended after he served a seasonlong prison sentence.

name: Norman Gimbel
headline: Norman Gimbel, 91, Grammy and Oscar-Winning Lyricist, Is Dead
abstract: He wrote lyrics for “The Girl From Ipanema” and “Killing Me Softly” and for the themes to the TV sitcoms “Happy Days” and “Laverne and Shirley.”

name: Aldo Parisot
profession: Eminent Cello Teacher and Yale Fixture
headline: Aldo Parisot, Eminent Cello Teacher and Yale Fixture, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Parisot went from a major solo career to a long teaching tenure. “The best cello teacher I have met in my life,” the great Janos Starker said.

name: Judith Rich Harris
profession: Author Played Down the Role of Parents
headline: Judith Rich Harris, 80, Dies; Author Played Down the Role of Parents
abstract: Genes and peer groups play a greater role than parents in how children turn out, Ms. Harris wrote in the best-selling “The Nurture Assumption.”

name: Karen Sparck Jones
profession: Established the Basis for Search Engines
headline: Overlooked No More: Karen Sparck Jones, Who Established the Basis for Search Engines
abstract: A pioneer of computer science for work combining statistics and linguistics, and an advocate for women in the field.

name: Gene Okerlund
headline: Gene Okerlund, Serious Voice of Pro Wrestling, Is Dead at 76
abstract: A straight man to the outsize personalities who fill the ring, he had a resonant voice that lent a certain gravitas to an enterprise hardly known for it.

name: Bob Einstein
profession: a.k.a. Super Dave Osborne and Larry David Pal
headline: Bob Einstein, 76, a.k.a. Super Dave Osborne and Larry David Pal, Dies
abstract: Mr. Einstein first gained fame in the 1970s by playing an accident-prone daredevil. He later had a recurring role on “Curb Your Enthusiasm.”

name: Ray Sawyer
headline: Ray Sawyer, ‘Cover of Rolling Stone’ Singer, Dies at 81
abstract: Thanks to an eye patch, he was the most recognizable member of Dr. Hook and the Medicine Show, which had several hits in the 1970s.

name: Daryl Dragon
headline: Daryl Dragon, of the Captain and Tennille Pop Duo, Dies at 76
abstract: He and his wife, Toni Tennille, were one of the most successful hit-making combinations of the 1970s. Their “Love Will Keep Us Together” went to No. 1.

name: Geoffrey Langlands
headline: Geoffrey Langlands, Lauded British Educator in Pakistan, Dies at 101
abstract: A British officer who stayed for six decades after his service ended, Mr. Langlands, known as “the Major,” taught at least two future prime ministers.

name: Edgar Hilsenrath
headline: Edgar Hilsenrath, 92, Writer of Unvarnished Holocaust Novels, Dies
abstract: A German Jew who survived the war, he wrote “The Nazi and the Barber” and other satirical portrayals of Nazi horrors and the miseries of the ghetto.

name: William C. Thompson
headline: William C. Thompson, Pioneering Black Legislator and Judge, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Thompson was Brooklyn’s first black state senator, an appeals court justice and a politician who urged a larger role for black Democrats in New York.

name: Blake W. Nordstrom
headline: Blake W. Nordstrom, Scion of Retail Family, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Nordstrom and his two brothers ran the Seattle-based clothing and shoe retailer, which was co-founded by their great-grandfather in 1901.

name: Mrinal Sen
headline: Mrinal Sen, One of India’s Leading Directors, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Sen was among the leaders in a type of small-scale, realistic filmmaking that was an alternative to Bollywood.

name: Herb Kelleher
headline: Herb Kelleher, Whose Southwest Airlines Reshaped the Industry, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Kelleher built Southwest into one of the nation’s most successful and admired companies by combining low fares with good customer service.

name: Ringo Lam
profession: Director of Hong Kong Classic City on Fire
headline: Ringo Lam, Director of Hong Kong Classic ‘City on Fire,’ Dies at 63
abstract: He achieved renown with a string of crime dramas, including a 1987 thriller that influenced Quentin Tarantino’s “Reservoir Dogs.”

name: Rosalyn Terborg-Penn
headline: Rosalyn Terborg-Penn, 77, Dies; Historian Recognized Black Suffragists
