abstract: She found that the role of black women in winning the vote for all women had virtually been erased from the history books by white movement leaders.

name: Christine McGuire
headline: Christine McGuire, Eldest of the Singing Sisters, Is Dead at 92
abstract: With hits like “Sincerely” and “Sugartime,” the McGuire Sisters embodied the postwar popular culture of the 1950s.

name: Honey Lantree
profession: Rarity as a Female 60s Rock Drummer
headline: Honey Lantree, 75, Rarity as a Female ’60s Rock Drummer, Is Dead
abstract: Performing with the British group the Honeycombs, she powered the hit single “Have I the Right?” despite claims that she was hired as a gimmick.

name: Dean Ford
headline: Dean Ford, Singer on Marmalade’s ‘Reflections,’ Is Dead at 72
abstract: After quick fame thanks to a big international hit and tours with the Who and others, Mr. Ford confronted the challenge of alcoholism.

name: Georges Loinger
headline: Georges Loinger, Wartime Rescuer of Jewish Children, Dies at 108
abstract: A French Jew, he saved hundreds from deportation or death by smuggling them into Switzerland, often by means of daring ruses under the Germans’ noses.

name: Pegi Young
headline: Pegi Young, 66, Musician Who Started a School for Disabled, Dies
abstract: The mother of a child with cerebral palsy, she helped start the Bridge School, whose star-studded benefit concerts included her ex-husband, Neil Young.

name: Harold Brown
headline: Harold Brown, Defense Secretary in Carter Administration, Dies at 91
abstract: The first scientist to become defense secretary, Mr. Brown brought technical knowledge and a background in weapons research.

name: Harold Brown
headline: Harold Brown, Tuskegee Airman Who Faced a Lynch Mob, Dies at 98
abstract: One of the last surviving Black pilots from that celebrated group, he was surrounded by an angry mob after parachuting from his P-51 over Austria during World War II.

name: Joe Casely-Hayford
headline: Joe Casely-Hayford, Iconoclastic Fashion Designer, Dies at 62
abstract: One of the first black designers to win international acclaim, Mr. Casely-Hayford alternately embraced and rejected the norms of the fashion establishment.

name: Brian Garfield
headline: Brian Garfield, Prolific Author of ‘Death Wish,’ Dies at 79
abstract: A writer whose best-known novel became a hit movie for Charles Bronson. He wrote a follow-up, “Death Sentence,” to atone for the earlier book’s violence.

name: Peter Meldrum
profession: Lost a Fight to Patent Genes
headline: Peter Meldrum, Who Lost a Fight to Patent Genes, Dies at 71
abstract: He led Myriad Genetics, whose patents on the BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes, associated with breast cancer, were invalidated by the Supreme Court.

name: Moshe Arens
headline: Moshe Arens, Israeli Statesman and Ex-Defense Minister, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Arens, who also served as foreign minister and ambassador to the United States, remained until his last days a beacon of Israel’s ideological right.

name: Babs Simpson
headline: Babs Simpson, Taste-Making Fashion Editor at Vogue, Is Dead at 105
abstract: She worked with titans of fashion photography and magazine grande dames, dressed Marilyn Monroe in one shoot and mingled in cafe society.

name: Howell Begle
headline: Howell Begle, Defender of R&B Artists’ Rights, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Mr. Begle’s efforts on behalf of performers like Ruth Brown led to royalty reform and the creation of the charitable Rhythm and Blues Foundation.

name: Rosenda Monteros
headline: Rosenda Monteros, Actress in ‘The Magnificent Seven,’ Dies
abstract: Ms. Monteros, one of the few women in John Sturges’s testosterone-fueled 1960 western, had a long career in Mexican film, theater and television.

name: Sylvia Chase
headline: Sylvia Chase, Pioneering Television Newswoman, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Ms. Chase was at the forefront of a generation of women who took themselves seriously and demanded that the industry and viewers did, too.

name: Roy J. Glauber
profession: Nobel Laureate Explored Behavior of Light
headline: Roy J. Glauber, 93, Dies; Nobel Laureate Explored Behavior of Light
abstract: Dr. Glauber, the New York-born son of a traveling salesman, developed theories that helped lay the basis for quantum computers and quantum cryptography.

name: Mary Kay Stearns
profession: Star of One of TVs Earliest Shows
headline: Mary Kay Stearns, 93, a Star of One of TV’s Earliest Shows, Dies
abstract: In 1947, with her real-life husband, she starred in “Mary Kay and Johnny,” a show that anticipated “I Love Lucy” and other domestic comedies of the 1950s.

name: Bernice Sandler
headline: Bernice Sandler, ‘Godmother of Title IX,’ Dies at 90
abstract: She changed the landscape for women in academic settings, prompting investigations into female admissions and in faculty hiring, promotions and salaries.

name: Larry Langford
headline: Larry Langford, Convicted Former Birmingham Mayor, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Langford, who was released from federal prison in December, was known for grandiose ideas and for the corruption case that ended his political career in 2009.

name: Carlos Sánchez
profession: Embodied Colombian Coffee as Juan Valdez
headline: Carlos Sánchez, 83, Dies; Embodied Colombian Coffee as Juan Valdez
abstract: Mr. Sánchez played Valdez, a humble but hard-working farmer and one of the world’s most recognizable pitchmen, from 1969 until 2006.

name: Dennis Johnson
profession: Creator of a Rediscovered Minimalist Score
headline: Dennis Johnson, 80, Creator of a Rediscovered Minimalist Score, Dies
abstract: Mr. Johnson’s 1959 composition “November,” a six-hour work for piano, was a landmark in the Minimalist movement, but it went unheard for 50 years.

name: Laura De
headline: Overlooked No More: Laura de Force Gordon, Suffragist, Journalist and Lawyer
abstract: Gordon was speaking from experience when, in 1893, she described in a speech how “society has sneered at learned women.” She spent decades trying to change that.

name: Mungau Dain
profession: Villager Star in Pacific Island Film
headline: Mungau Dain, Villager Star in Pacific Island Film, Dies at 24
abstract: Mr. Dain starred in the Oscar-nominated “Tanna,” which portrayed his village in the remote island nation of Vanuatu. An infection led to his death.

name: Lewis L. Judd
headline: Dr. Lewis L. Judd, 88, Dies; Oversaw ‘Decade of the Brain’
abstract: At the National Institute of Mental Health, he helped put in place an ambitious research agenda focused on biology as the key to understanding psychiatric problems.

name: Jakiw Palij
profession: Former Nazi Guard Deported After Decades in U.S
headline: Jakiw Palij, Former Nazi Guard Deported After Decades in U.S., Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Palij had lived for decades in Queens. Although ordered deported in 2004, no country agreed to take him for 14 years.

name: Luis Garden Acosta
headline: Luis Garden Acosta, Resuscitator of a Brooklyn Neighborhood, Dies at 73
abstract: He was a founder of El Puente, which bridged political and ethnic divides in Williamsburg to curb gang violence and instill a collaborative spirit.

name: Eugeniu Iordachescu
headline: Eugeniu Iordachescu, Who Saved Bucharest’s Churches, Dies at 89
abstract: A civil engineer, he helped rescue dozens of buildings from destruction in the 1980s by literally rolling them to safety.

name: Michael Atiyah
headline: Michael Atiyah, Mathematician in Newton’s Footsteps, Dies at 89
abstract: One of the 20th century’s leading mathematical theorists, he revealed a connection between math and physics not seen since the 17th century.

name: Lamin Sanneh
headline: Lamin Sanneh, Scholar of Islam and Christianity, Dies at 76
abstract: Born on a river island in West Africa and inspired by Helen Keller, he wound up teaching at Yale and writing about the spread of religions in Africa.

name: Jessica Tcherepnine
headline: Jessica Tcherepnine, Exacting Botanical Artist, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Ms. Tcherepnine painted blossoms from her family garden in England and became a world-renowned botanical artist after moving to the United States.

name: Joseph Jarman
profession: Mainstay of the Art Ensemble of Chicago
headline: Joseph Jarman, 81, Dies; Mainstay of the Art Ensemble of Chicago
abstract: Mr. Jarman, who played numerous reed and woodwind instruments, drew inspiration not only from jazz and blues but also from world music, ritual and folklore.

name: John Falsey
headline: John Falsey, Creator of Acclaimed TV Series, Is Dead at 67
abstract: He and Joshua Brand were behind “St. Elsewhere” and “Northern Exposure,” among other shows.

name: Verna Bloom
profession: Amorous Deans Wife in Animal House
headline: Verna Bloom, 80, Amorous Dean’s Wife in ‘Animal House,’ Dies
abstract: She was best known for wildly different roles, in a frat house comedy and in the 1960s drama “Medium Cool.” She was also in films by Clint Eastwood and Martin Scorsese.

name: Patricia Wald
profession: First Woman to Preside Over D.C. Appeals Court
headline: Patricia Wald, First Woman to Preside Over D.C. Appeals Court, Dies at 90
abstract: A recipient of the Presidential Medal of Freedom, she was the first woman to serve on the Court of Appeals in Washington. She was soon joined by Ruth Bader Ginsburg.

name: John Burningham
headline: John Burningham, Author Who Piqued Young Imaginations, Dies at 82
abstract: A prolific writer and illustrator of children’s books — “a picture-book pioneer” — whose titles include “Avocado Baby” and “Whaddayamean.”

name: Mel Stottlemyre
headline: Mel Stottlemyre, Yankees’ Ace During Lean Years, Dies at 77
abstract: Stottlemyre was an anchor for the pitching staff during the late 1960s and early ’70s. He was later the pitching coach for Yankees and Mets teams that won the World Series.

name: Lester Wunderman
headline: Lester Wunderman, Father of Direct Marketing, Dies at 98
abstract: He was even credited with coining the term as a co-founder of the world’s largest direct-marketing ad agency, long before there were internet cookies.

name: Nicholas Heyward Sr.
headline: Nicholas Heyward Sr., 61, Dies; Spoke Out Against Police Brutality
abstract: Mr. Heyward became an activist after his 13-year-old son, who was playing with a toy gun, was killed by a police officer in Brooklyn in 1994.

name: Francine du Plessix Gray
headline: Francine du Plessix Gray, Searching Novelist and Journalist, Is Dead at 88
abstract: She explored the obstacles confronting women seeking their place in the world as well as her own privileged but unsettled life under the sway of daunting parents.

name: Elias M. Stein
headline: Elias M. Stein, Mathematician of Fluctuations, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Arriving from Europe with diamonds in his shoes (hidden there), he found renown in his field with real-world applications, like charting a stock market.

name: Clydie King
profession: Top-Tier Backup Singer on Big Hits
headline: Clydie King, Top-Tier Backup Singer on Big Hits, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Ms. King sang on hits by the Rolling Stones, Linda Ronstadt and even Lynyrd Skynyrd. Bob Dylan called her his “ultimate singing partner.”

name: Carol Channing
headline: Carol Channing Dies at 97; a Larger-Than-Life Broadway Star
abstract: Her performances as the gold-digging Lorelei Lee in “Gentlemen Prefer Blondes” and the matchmaker Dolly Gallagher Levi in “Hello, Dolly!” made her a Broadway legend.

name: Alan R. Pearlman
headline: Alan R. Pearlman, Synthesizer Pioneer, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Pearlman’s ARP synthesizers were once ubiquitous in pop and electronic music. By the mid-1970s, they commanded 40 percent of the market.

name: Theo Adam
headline: Theo Adam, Acclaimed in Wagner Operas, Is Dead at 92
abstract: A German bass-baritone who was called one of the 20th century’s most important interpreters of his countryman. He was also prized for his acting.

name: Jean Bourgain
headline: Jean Bourgain, Problem-Conquering Mathematician, Is Dead at 64
abstract: Dr. Bourgain, a recipient of some of his field’s most prestigious awards, was undaunted by even the most intractable of challenges.

name: Bob Kuechenberg
headline: Bob Kuechenberg, 71, Dies; Gritty Guard With Champion Dolphins
abstract: Playing through injuries, he was a critical part of a daunting offensive line that helped Miami win back-to-back Super Bowls and achieve a perfect season.

name: Isabelle Kelley
profession: Developed a Food Stamp Program to Feed Millions
headline: Overlooked No More: Isabelle Kelley, Who Developed a Food Stamp Program to Feed Millions
abstract: At a time when many needy families lacked adequate nutrition, Kelley helped develop a program to improve the well being of Americans. Today, more than 38 million people receive food stamps.

name: Jo Andres
headline: Jo Andres, Innovative Choreographer and Filmmaker, Dies at 64
abstract: In her dances and short films, she created dreamlike, surreal tapestries. “I describe my aesthetic style as ‘perceptual mischief,’” she once said.

name: John C. Bogle
headline: John C. Bogle, Founder of Financial Giant Vanguard, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Beginning in 1974, Mr. Bogle built Vanguard Group into one of the world’s largest mutual fund companies, attracting investors in droves.

name: Mary Oliver
profession: Prize-Winning Poet of the Natural World
headline: Mary Oliver, 83, Prize-Winning Poet of the Natural World, Is Dead
abstract: With its plain language and minute attention to flora and fauna, her uplifting verse was widely popular and her readings drew throngs. But critics were divided.

name: Bonnie Guitar
headline: Bonnie Guitar, Music Industry Trailblazer, Is Dead at 95
abstract: She was best known for her hit record “Dark Moon,” but her greatest achievement may have been her success as a businesswoman.

name: Barbara Gardner Proctor
headline: Barbara Gardner Proctor, Barrier-Breaking Ad Executive, Dies at 86
abstract: After growing up poor in North Carolina, she opened, in Chicago, what is believed to be the first advertising agency founded by a black woman.

name: Mark Urman
headline: Mark Urman, Champion of Independent Films, Is Dead at 66
abstract: As a distributor, Mr. Urman helped documentaries and other art-house fare reach more and more moviegoers instead of fading into obscurity.

name: John Mendelsohn
headline: Dr. John Mendelsohn, 82, Researcher Who Led Top Cancer Center, Dies
abstract: After pioneering a targeted cancer therapy, he oversaw MD Anderson in Houston as it gained a reputation as the nation’s top cancer hospital.

name: Walter Chandoha
headline: Walter Chandoha, Photographer Whose Specialty Was Cats, Dies at 98
abstract: A stray kitten appropriately named Loco started Mr. Chandoha on an unexpected career. By the time he died, he had taken some 90,000 cat pictures.

name: John E. Merow
headline: John E. Merow, Former Head of Sullivan & Cromwell, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Merow, who oversaw the expansion of one of Wall Street’s major law firms, died along with his wife, Mary Alyce, in a fire in their Manhattan home.

name: Lorna Doom
profession: Bassist in the Punk Band Germs
headline: Lorna Doom, Bassist in the Punk Band Germs, Is Dead at 61
abstract: She and Belinda Carlisle, later of the Go-Go’s, answered an ad looking for “two untalented girls” and ended up in one of the first punk groups in Los Angeles.

name: Nathan Glazer
headline: Nathan Glazer, Urban Sociologist and Outspoken Intellectual, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Glazer often waded into heated debates over contentious issues about race, ethnicity, immigration and education.

name: Henry Sy
profession: Philippines Richest Man and a Shopping Mall Tycoon
headline: Henry Sy, 94, Dies; Philippines’ Richest Man and a Shopping Mall Tycoon
abstract: Mr. Sy, who started out selling surplus boots in Manila after World War II, has been called the “father of modern Philippine retail.”

name: Reggie Young
profession: Guitarist Heard on Hundreds of Hits
headline: Reggie Young, Guitarist Heard on Hundreds of Hits, Dies at 82
abstract: A studio mainstay first in Memphis and later in Nashville, Mr. Young recorded with Elvis Presley and countless others.

name: Tony Mendez
profession: C.I.A. Officer Celebrated in the Film Argo
headline: Tony Mendez, 78, Dies; C.I.A. Officer Celebrated in the Film ‘Argo’
abstract: Mr. Mendez orchestrated one of the most audacious covert operations in the agency’s history: the rescue of six American diplomats from Iran in 1980.

name: Tony Mendez
profession: David Lettermans Oddball Cue Card Boy
headline: Tony Mendez, David Letterman’s Oddball ‘Cue Card Boy,’ Dies at 76
abstract: For more than 20 years, he wrote and flipped cards for Mr. Letterman’s “Late Show.” He was also a member of the show’s troupe of quirky onscreen characters.

name: Brandon Truaxe
headline: Brandon Truaxe, Visionary Beauty Entrepreneur, Is Dead at 40
abstract: He founded Deciem, owners of The Ordinary.

name: Harris Wofford
headline: Harris Wofford, 92, Ex-Senator Who Pushed Volunteerism, Is Dead
abstract: A Pennsylvania lawyer, he was instrumental in the Peace Corps and AmeriCorps, advised Martin Luther King Jr. and headed two colleges.

name: Kaye Ballard
headline: Kaye Ballard, Indefatigable Comedian and Actress, Dies at 93
abstract: Best known for the 1960s sitcom “The Mothers-in-Law,” she also had memorable turns in Broadway musicals and rode the nightclub circuit for years.

name: Joseph Howze
headline: Joseph Howze Is Dead at 95; Groundbreaking African-American Bishop
abstract: As head of the mostly white Diocese of Biloxi, Miss., he was the first African-American bishop appointed to preside over a Roman Catholic diocese in the 20th century.

name: Russell Baker
headline: Russell Baker, Pulitzer-Winning Times Columnist and Humorist, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Baker, a backwoods-born Virginian who became one of America’s most celebrated writers, spent decades at The New York Times and hosted “Masterpiece Theater” for years.

name: Andy de Groat
headline: Andy de Groat, 71, Downtown Choreographer, Is Dead
abstract: Best known for his work with Robert Wilson, he later formed his own company and built a distinctive choreographic identity through his use of spinning.

name: Jonas Mekas
headline: Jonas Mekas, ‘Godfather’ of American Avant-Garde Film, Is Dead at 96
abstract: Lithuanian-born, he arrived in New York in 1949 and became a prolific filmmaker, curator, critic and evangelist for independent movies, especially experimental ones.

name: Mabel Stark
headline: Overlooked No More: Mabel Stark, Fearless Tiger Trainer
abstract: Stark was one of the most celebrated animal trainers in a field dominated by men. She performed with tigers until she was nearly 80, then took her own life when she was separated from them.

name: Bernardo Benes
headline: Bernardo Benes, Cuban Exile Who Negotiated With Castro, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Benes helped engineer the release of 3,600 political prisoners from Cuba, but he earned the wrath of fellow exiles in Miami.

name: Edward Morrison
headline: Edward Morrison, Deputy Mayor Who Helped John Lennon, Dies at 85
abstract: Serving in the Lindsay administration, he argued that Lennon was a cultural asset when the Nixon administration tried to deport him in the early 1970s.

name: Mary Boyd Higgins
headline: Mary Boyd Higgins, Wilhelm Reich’s Devoted Trustee, Is Dead at 93
abstract: She volunteered for the job with a father of the sexual revolution, even though she had never met him. She protected his legacy and republished his books.

name: Diana Athill
profession: Wrote Cleareyed Memoirs of Love and Sex
headline: Diana Athill Dies at 101; Wrote Cleareyed Memoirs of Love and Sex
abstract: The English author, whose critically lauded autobiographies chronicled her romantic and sexual liaisons, attained literary celebrity in her 90s.

name: Douglas Costle
profession: Helped Create the E.P.A. and Then Ran It
headline: Douglas Costle, Who Helped Create the E.P.A. and Then Ran It, Dies at 79
abstract: He helped conceive the environmental agency that President Nixon created in 1970 and oversaw it through crises in the Carter administration.

name: Rita Vidaurri
headline: Rita Vidaurri, Ranchera Singer Who Reclaimed Her Career, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Vidaurri became famous in Latin America for belting out songs in the 1950s but stopped at her peak, only to return to the limelight as she neared 80.

name: Norman Goodman
profession: Summoned Manhattanites to Jury Duty, Like It or Not
headline: Norman Goodman, 95, Dies; Summoned Manhattanites to Jury Duty, Like It or Not
abstract: Yes, he existed. For generations, this clerk of New York County’s printed signature in the upper-left-hand corner of a mailed summons was something to dread.

name: Nicola L
profession: Feminist Art Had a Useful Side
headline: Nicola L, Whose Feminist Art Had a Useful Side, Is Dead
abstract: A multimedia fixture of the New York scene, belatedly celebrated as a Pop Artist, she made works that could function as furniture or even be worn.

name: Frank Blaichman
profession: Led Jewish Fighters in World War II
headline: Frank Blaichman, 96, Dies; Led Jewish Fighters in World War II
abstract: He took charge of a band of Jewish partisans in occupied Poland who disrupted supply lines and rooted out Nazi collaborators.

name: Florence Knoll Bassett
profession: Designer of the Modern American Office
headline: Florence Knoll Bassett, 101, Designer of the Modern American Office, Dies
abstract: The mid-20th-century furnishings she fashioned were profoundly influential, and they still resonate.

name: Lamia Al-Gailani Werr
headline: Lamia Al-Gailani Werr, 80, Dies; Archaeologist Rescued Iraqi Art
abstract: One of the few Iraqi women in the field, she pushed to excavate ancient sites and helped a national museum recover from looting in the Iraq war.

name: Michel Legrand
headline: Michel Legrand, Pianist and Film Composer, Dies at 86
abstract: The winner of three Oscars and five Grammys, he collaborated with musicians from John Coltrane to Kiri Te Kanawa over a career that spanned seven decades.

name: Fatima Ali
headline: Fatima Ali, Fan Favorite on ‘Top Chef,’ Dies of Cancer at 29
abstract: Ms. Ali publicly battled a rare form of cancer for a year while she sought to fulfill her final wish of eating at the best restaurants in the world.

name: Meshulam Riklis
headline: Meshulam Riklis, Financier Who Wed Pia Zadora, Is Dead at 95
abstract: He was one of the first corporate raiders to acquire companies with leveraged buyouts. But he was probably best known for his marriage.

name: Charles Kettles
profession: Rescued Dozens of Troops in Vietnam
headline: Charles Kettles, Who Rescued Dozens of Troops in Vietnam, Dies at 89
abstract: “A soldier who was there said, ‘That day, Major Kettles became our John Wayne.’ With all due respect to John Wayne, he couldn’t do what Chuck Kettles did.”

name: Thomas L. Phillips
headline: Thomas L. Phillips, C.E.O. Who Diversified Raytheon, Has Died
abstract: Carrying his born-again faith into the executive suite, he transformed a weapons manufacturer into a maker of refrigerators, aircraft and more as well.

name: Clark B. Olsen
profession: Witness to a Civil Rights Killing
headline: Clark B. Olsen, Witness to a Civil Rights Killing, Dies at 85
abstract: In Selma, Ala., in 1965, he saw a fellow minister, James Reeb, take a fatal blow to the head, a murder with national consequences.

name: Patricia McBride Lousada
headline: Patricia McBride Lousada, One of Balanchine’s Originals, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Lousada was one of the first ballerinas chosen for what became New York City Ballet. Later in life she became a successful cookbook author.

name: Stanley Hill
profession: Led New York Citys Biggest Public Union
headline: Stanley Hill, 82, Dies; Led New York City’s Biggest Public Union
abstract: He was the first black leader of District Council 37, from 1987 to 1999. But he was forced to resign amid charges of mismanagement and overspending.

name: Frances Grill
profession: Founder of an Inclusive Modeling Agency
headline: Frances Grill, 90, Founder of an Inclusive Modeling Agency, Dies
abstract: At Click there have been white models (Elle Macpherson, Isabella Rossellini, Uma Thurman), black (Whitney Houston, Gail O’Neill) and transgender (Teri Toye).

name: Peter Magowan
headline: Peter Magowan, Giants Fan Turned Giants’ Owner, Is Dead at 76
abstract: While running Safeway Stores, Mr. Magowan headed a group that bought the team and kept it from moving from San Francisco to Florida.

name: Kim Bok-dong
headline: Kim Bok-dong, Wartime Sex Slave Who Sought Reparations for Koreans, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Kim, one of the thousands of women forced to work in Japanese brothels during World War II, was among the first to break decades of silence about their ordeal.

name: Oliver Mtukudzi
headline: Oliver Mtukudzi, Renowned Zimbabwean Musician, Is Dead at 66
abstract: His music, a kind of soundtrack to his country’s life in the late 20th century, became its own idiom, called “Tuku music,” after his nickname.

name: Edwin Birdsong
headline: Edwin Birdsong, Whose Music Was Reborn in Hip-Hop, Dies at 77
abstract: His blend of funk, jazz and disco from the 1970s and ′80s has been sampled by a later generation of artists, including Daft Punk and De La Soul.

name: James Ingram
headline: James Ingram, a Hitmaking Voice of ’80s R&B, Is Dead at 66
abstract: In romantic duets with other stars and as a solo act, he sang his way onto the music charts, won Grammys and performed on movie soundtracks.

name: Charles J. Hynes
profession: Brooklyn D.A. in a Tumultuous Era
headline: Charles J. Hynes, Brooklyn D.A. in a Tumultuous Era, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Hynes took the office after prosecuting the Howard Beach case and won convictions against corrupt officials, but controversy dogged his final years on the job.

name: Morton Sobell
profession: Last Defendant in Rosenberg Spy Case
headline: Morton Sobell, Last Defendant in Rosenberg Spy Case, Is Dead at 101
abstract: Convicted in the Cold War spy trial that delivered Julius and Ethel Rosenberg to their deaths and divided the nation, he later admitted that he had been a spy.

name: Dumisani Kumalo
headline: Dumisani Kumalo Dead at 71; Helped Turn Tide Against Apartheid
abstract: After incurring the wrath of the South African authorities, he came to America and advocated divestment, putting extra pressure on them.

name: Erik Olin Wright
profession: Marxist Sociologist With a Pragmatic Approach
headline: Erik Olin Wright, 71, Dies; Marxist Sociologist With a Pragmatic Approach
abstract: Dr. Wright offered practical alternatives to capitalism, promoting ideas like a universal basic income.

name: Forough Farrokhzad
headline: Overlooked No More: Forough Farrokhzad, Iranian Poet Who Broke Barriers of Sex and Society
abstract: An author unafraid to defy midcentury attitudes about her gender. “What is important is humanity,” she said, “not being a man or a woman.”

name: Leonard Dinnerstein
headline: Leonard Dinnerstein, 84, Dies; Scholar of Anti-Semitism in U.S.
abstract: He began his academic work with a seminal account of the 1915 lynching of Leo Frank, a Jewish factory manager in Georgia who was convicted of murder.

name: Harold Bradley
headline: Harold Bradley, a Nashville Studio Master, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Mr. Bradley’s work on six-string bass and guitar was featured on records by Hank Williams, Elvis Presley, Buddy Holly, Loretta Lynn and numerous others.

name: Jean Guillou
headline: Jean Guillou, Organ Maestro Who Broke Traditions, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Guillou charted his own path in organ performance, composition and even design — attracting controversy but leaving a legacy of more than 100 recordings.

name: Margo Rodriguez
profession: Half of an Innovative Mambo Duo
headline: Margo Rodriguez, 89, Half of an Innovative Mambo Duo, Dies
abstract: As the dance team Augie and Margo, Mrs. Rodriguez and her husband helped mambo evolve from a nightclub craze into popular mainstream entertainment.

name: Dusan Makavejev
headline: Dusan Makavejev, 86. Eyebrow-Raising Serbian Director, Dies
abstract: His films, among them “WR: Mysteries of the Organism,” were full of sex and metaphor. They were celebrated on the festival circuit but also sometimes reviled.

name: Major Taylor
headline: Major Taylor, World Champion Bicyclist
abstract: The first African-American cycling champion, fans called him the Black Cyclone. He blew past terrifying threats, setting records with an elegant grace.

name: Moses Fleetwood Walker
headline: Moses Fleetwood Walker
abstract: It turns out Jackie Robinson was not the first big league baseball player known to be African-American. That distinction belongs to Moses Fleetwood Walker.

name: Philip Payton
headline: Philip Payton, the Real Estate Mogul Who Made Harlem a Black Mecca
abstract: An African-American entrepreneur seized the chance to draw black New Yorkers from slums to a comfortable white enclave.

name: Elizabeth Jennings
headline: Elizabeth Jennings, Who Desegregated New York’s Trolleys
abstract: She had been primed, by temperament and family ties, to fight for racial equality. Her moment came on a streetcar ride to church.

name: Mary Ellen Pleasant
headline: The Many Chapters of Mary Ellen Pleasant
abstract: Born into slavery, Mary Ellen Pleasant became a Gold Rush-era millionaire, defying conventions of what a black woman could be in the 19th century.

name: Oscar Micheaux
profession: Intrepid Creator of Films on Race
headline: Oscar Micheaux, Intrepid Creator of Films on Race
abstract: Micheaux’s movies gave black America something they had never seen — their loves and lives on the big screen.

name: Granville T. Woods
headline: Granville T. Woods, Inventor Known as ‘Black Edison’
abstract: Woods was the most prolific black inventor at the turn of the 19th century, but when he died, he was all but forgotten, buried in an unmarked grave.

name: Nina Mae McKinney
profession: Defied the Barriers of Race to Find Stardom
headline: Nina Mae McKinney, Who Defied the Barriers of Race to Find Stardom
abstract: McKinney was hailed in 1929 as “an honest-to-goodness screen star,” but she couldn’t find good roles in the United States. So she carved a niche in Europe.

name: Alfred Hair
profession: Collective Created a Path for Black Artists
headline: Alfred Hair, Whose Collective Created a Path for Black Artists
abstract: Part artist, part businessman and all charisma, Hair started a movement that would allow African-American artists to make a living in the South.

name: Zelda Wynn Valdes
headline: Zelda Wynn, Fashion Designer to the Stars
abstract: She worked her way up from a stockroom worker to specializing in accentuating the curves of performers like Dorothy Dandridge, Mae West and Eartha Kitt.

name: Margaret Garner
headline: Margaret Garner, a Runaway Slave Who Killed Her Own Daughter
abstract: In one soul-chilling moment, Garner committed a desperate act, raising the question: Is slavery worse than death? Her life inspired a Toni Morrison novel.

name: Scott Joplin
headline: Scott Joplin, Ragtime Master Who Wrote ‘The Entertainer’
abstract: Scott Joplin elevated ragtime, composed one of the first African-American operas and laid the groundwork for jazz.

name: Gladys Bentley
profession: Gender-Bending Blues Performer and 20s Harlem Royalty
headline: Gladys Bentley, Gender-Bending Blues Performer and ’20s Harlem Royalty
abstract: In her top hat and tuxedo, Bentley loosened social mores as she swept through a Harlem speakeasy, soliciting the audience for dirty lyrics.

name: Dick Miller
profession: Character Actor and Roger Corman Mainstay
headline: Dick Miller, 90, Dies; Character Actor and Roger Corman Mainstay
abstract: He appeared in dozens of low-budget films for Mr. Corman and later in “The Terminator,” “Gremlins” and other movies directed by Corman acolytes.

name: Sanford Sylvan
headline: Sanford Sylvan, Baritone Who Created Major Opera Roles, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Sylvan brought to life characters in John Adams’s “Nixon in China” and “The Death of Klinghoffer” during a career as a sensitive, eloquent singer.

name: Andy Hebenton
headline: Andy Hebenton, N.H.L. Ironman with 630 Consecutive Games, Dies at 89
abstract: A stalwart with the New York Rangers, he extended his streak even when he was sent down to the minors. It only ended when he went to his father’s funeral.

name: Bob Friend
headline: Bob Friend, 88, Mainstay of Pirates Team That Stunned Yanks, Dies
abstract: Mr. Friend was a dependable arm and league standout on losing teams until the 1960 World Series thriller, won by Bill Mazeroski’s walk-off home run.

name: John O. Marsh Jr.
headline: John O. Marsh Jr., Ex-Army Chief and Presidents’ Adviser, Dies at 92
abstract: He liked to call himself a country lawyer, but in Washington, serving three presidents, he was known as a master of military and political affairs.

name: Julie Adams
profession: Seized by Creature in Black Lagoon
headline: Julie Adams, Seized by Creature in ‘Black Lagoon,’ Dies at 92
abstract: Her Hollywood career stretched across six decades, but it was her 1954 role as the love interest of a reptilian monster that gave her lasting fame.

name: Theodore Rabb
headline: Theodore Rabb, Resourceful Renaissance Historian, Dies at 81
abstract: Based at Princeton, Professor Rabb brought a fresh eye to analyzing historical records in producing books, articles and a PBS series.

name: Kristoff St. John
headline: Kristoff St. John, a Fixture of Daytime TV, Is Dead at 52
abstract: Mr. St. John won two Daytime Emmy Awards for playing a cosmetics executive on “The Young and the Restless.” He was haunted by his son’s suicide.

name: Jacqueline Steiner
headline: Jacqueline Steiner, 94, Lyricist Who Left Charlie on the M.T.A., Dies
abstract: In a song that became a hit for the Kingston Trio in 1959, she conjured up an Everyman who is trapped by Boston’s subway system. He still hasn’t returned.

name: Albert J. Dunlap
profession: Tough Executive Known as Chainsaw Al
headline: Albert J. Dunlap, Tough Executive Known as Chainsaw Al, Dies at 81
abstract: Viewing himself as a corporate doctor who knew what ailed troubled companies, Mr. Dunlap was known for his outspokenness and big layoffs.

name: Izzy Young
headline: Izzy Young, Who Presided Over the Folk Revival, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Bob Dylan, whose first formal concert Mr. Young produced, called his Greenwich Village shop, the Folklore Center, “the citadel of Americana folk music.”

name: William Van Alstyne
headline: William Van Alstyne, 84, Dies; Often-Cited Constitutional Scholar
abstract: An enrolled Republican and a civil libertarian, he said the Bill of Rights guaranteed both the freedom to have an abortion and the freedom to own a gun.

name: Christine Kay
headline: Christine Kay, Editor on Prizewinning Times Projects, Dies at 54
abstract: Ms. Kay helped shepherd Pulitzer-winning series, including the celebrated “Portraits of Grief” remembrances of the victims of 9/11.

name: Ron Joyce
profession: Force Behind Tim Hortons Doughnut Shops
headline: Ron Joyce, Force Behind Tim Hortons Doughnut Shops, Dies at 88
abstract: After the death of its namesake co-founder, Mr. Joyce made the chain an inescapable part of Canadian life.

name: Alice Dye
headline: Alice Dye, Innovative Golf Course Designer, Is Dead at 91
abstract: A promoter of the women’s game as well, she and her husband, Pete Dye, were a team, creating some of the most admired golf courses in the world.

name: Mabel Grammer
profession: Brown Baby Plan Found Homes for Hundreds
headline: Overlooked No More: Mabel Grammer, Whose Brown Baby Plan Found Homes for Hundreds
abstract: Grammer’s self-run adoption agency made it possible for unwanted mixed-race children in Germany to find homes after World War II.

name: John Mason
headline: John Mason, Who Expanded Ceramics’ Boundaries, Dies at 91
abstract: His large wall reliefs and other sculptures explored the artistic possibilities of clay.

name: Doris Wethers
profession: on Front Lines Against Sickle Cell
headline: Dr. Doris Wethers, 91, on Front Lines Against Sickle Cell, Dies
abstract: Breaking racial barriers in New York’s medical world, she earned renown for research and advocacy that led to mandatory testing for sickle cell anemia.

name: Lili Wronker
headline: Lili Wronker, Calligrapher and Illustrator, Is Dead at 94
abstract: A German refugee, she brought her expertise in lettering to Hebrew calligraphy. She also illustrated hundreds of books, many of them for children.

name: Rosamunde Pilcher
headline: Rosamunde Pilcher, Author of ‘The Shell Seekers,’ Dies at 94
abstract: After the success of what her publisher called “the quintessential word-of-mouth book,” many of her novels were made into TV movies or mini-series.

name: Yechiel Eckstein
headline: Rabbi Yechiel Eckstein Dies at 67; Fostered Israeli-Evangelical Ties
abstract: His organization has raised more than $1.5 billion from evangelical Christian contributors abroad, though the effort has left some Jews uncomfortable.

name: John Dingell Jr.
headline: John Dingell Jr., a House ‘Bull’ Who Served the Longest, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Representing a Michigan district for a record 59 years, he was one of the last of a group of powerful Democratic committee chairmen on Capitol Hill.

name: Albert Finney
headline: Albert Finney, 82, ‘Angry Young Man’ Who Became a Hollywood Star, Is Dead
abstract: He was known for roles in the movies “Tom Jones,” “Murder on the Orient Express,” “Under the Volcano” and “Erin Brockovich,” as well as on the London stage.

name: Barbra Siperstein
headline: Barbra Siperstein, Crusader for Transgender Rights, Dies at 76
abstract: Married with three children, she became a vigorous advocate after her wife died. Her name is on a new New Jersey law on gender identity.

name: Nehanda Abiodun
headline: Nehanda Abiodun, 68, Black Revolutionary Who Fled to Cuba, Dies
abstract: A freedom fighter to some and a terrorist to others, she became a fugitive after she was charged in connection with a deadly botched robbery in 1981.

name: Jan Wahl
headline: Jan Wahl, Children’s Writer Who Attracted Top Artists, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Wahl published more than 100 lucidly written books, some illustrated by the likes of Maurice Sendak, Norman Rockwell and Edward Gorey.

name: John Gunderson
headline: Dr. John Gunderson, 76, Dies; Defined Borderline Personality Disorder
abstract: “He was the first person to look systematically at the data and figure out what the heck this diagnosis really meant,” a colleague said.

name: Walter H. Munk
headline: Walter H. Munk, Scientist-Explorer Who Illuminated the Deep, Dies at 101
abstract: One of the 20th century’s leading oceanographers, he was called the “Einstein of the oceans,” in one case predicting the surf on D-Day and saving lives.

name: Robert Ryman
headline: Robert Ryman, Minimalist Painter Who Made the Most of White, Dies at 88
abstract: Self-taught after discovering art as a museum guard, he became one of America’s most important postwar artists, reaching beyond Abstract Expressionism.

name: Pierre Nanterme
headline: Pierre Nanterme, Former C.E.O. of Accenture, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Nanterme, who capped a 36-year career at the global consulting giant with eight years as chief executive, transformed the company by sharpening its focus on new technologies.

name: Joe Sirola
headline: Joe Sirola, Actor Who Found Riches in Commercials, Dies at 89
abstract: He made countless commercials; at one point it was said that people who listened to the radio or watched TV heard his voice every single day.

name: Ron Hutchinson
headline: Ron Hutchinson, Restorer of Early Sound Films, Is Dead at 67
abstract: For years, he hunted down the discs containing the soundtracks to short films from as early as 1926 that featured comedians, opera singers and others.

name: Nancy B. Reich
headline: Nancy B. Reich, Scholarly Champion of Clara Schumann, Dies at 94
abstract: Her research raised the profile of a composer too often overshadowed by her husband and established her as a major figure of German Romanticism.

name: Tomi Ungerer
profession: Brash Illustrator for Young and Older
headline: Tomi Ungerer, Brash Illustrator for Young and Older, Dies at 87
abstract: His children’s books brought a refreshing jolt to the genre, but his erotica made him an outcast in some circles.

name: C.Y. Lee
headline: C.Y. Lee, ‘Flower Drum Song’ Author, Is Dead at 102
abstract: His novel of generational and cultural conflict among Chinese immigrants became a hit Broadway musical and then a film that earned five Oscar nominations.

name: K.W. Lee
headline: K.W. Lee, 96, Dies; Journalist Who Gave Voice to Immigrant Communities
abstract: His reporting sought to humanize and unite Asian Americans. It also led to the release of a Korean immigrant on death row.

name: Edward F. Zigler
headline: Edward F. Zigler, an Architect of Head Start, Dies at 88
abstract: The Yale psychologist helped design the preschool program in the 1960s and was the first permanent head of the Office of Child Development.

name: Heidi Toffler
headline: Heidi Toffler, Unsung Force Behind Futurist Books, Dies at 89
abstract: With her husband, Alvin Toffler, she was half of a team that produced global best-sellers, including “Future Shock.” Recognition was belated.

name: Ron Miller
profession: Rose to the Top at Disney
headline: Ron Miller, Who Rose to the Top at Disney, Then Fell, Dies at 85
abstract: A former football player, he spent three decades working for Walt Disney, his father-in-law, and had notable successes — until things turned sour.

name: Manfred Eigen
headline: Manfred Eigen, 91, Nobel Winner Who Put a Clock to Chemicals, Dies
abstract: He shared the 1967 prize for finding a way to time “immeasurably fast” chemical reactions. His research advanced the study of enzymes, among other things.

name: Roderick MacFarquhar
headline: Roderick MacFarquhar, Eminent China Scholar, Dies at 88
abstract: With a three-volume study of the Cultural Revolution and lively lectures at Harvard, he influenced how people around the world understood China.

name: Anne Firor Scott
headline: Anne Firor Scott, Scholar of Women’s History, Dies at 97
abstract: Studying diaries, letters and more, she found that women, in the South and beyond, were not just passive observers of the vital events of their time.

name: Mel A. Tomlinson
headline: Mel A. Tomlinson, 65, Ballet Star and ‘Agon’ Interpreter, Dies
abstract: Mr. Tomlinson, who danced with New York City Ballet, Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater and Dance Theater of Harlem, was a rangy, powerful presence on the stage.

name: Lyndon LaRouche
headline: Lyndon LaRouche, Cult Figure Who Ran for President 8 Times, Dies at 96
abstract: A quixotic leader who began his political career on the far left and ended it on the far right, railing against a host of groups.

name: Carol F. Reich
headline: Carol F. Reich, Charter School Innovator, Is Dead at 83
abstract: The success that she and her husband achieved with the experimental school they opened in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, helped inspire a movement.

name: Dudley Randall
profession: Broadside Press Gave a Voice to Black Poets
headline: Overlooked No More: Dudley Randall, Whose Broadside Press Gave a Voice to Black Poets
abstract: Randall, a poet and librarian, started the press out of his home, eventually publishing the work of about 200 writers amid Detroit’s flowering Black Arts Movement.

name: Walter B. Jones
headline: Walter B. Jones, 76, Dies; Republican Turned Against Iraq War
abstract: A staunch war supporter, he rebranded French fries as “freedom fries,” but then opposed the war and sought to atone for his earlier support.

name: Pedro Morales
profession: First to Win Three Major Wrestling Titles
headline: Pedro Morales, 76, First to Win Three Major Wrestling Titles, Dies
abstract: A hard-punching star of the 1970s and ’80s, he was known as much for his kindness outside the ring as for his ferocity within it.

name: David Forden
profession: C.I.A. Handler in Cold War Intrigue
headline: David Forden, C.I.A. Handler in Cold War Intrigue, Dies at 88
abstract: He cultivated a colonel in the Polish high command whose warnings may have staved off a Soviet incursion. They were later neighbors in Florida.

name: Frederick Douglass
headline: Frederick Douglass’s Original New York Times Obituary From 1895
abstract: Douglass, who was described as an adviser to President Lincoln, a skillful writer and orator and an activist for abolition and women’s suffrage, died suddenly.

name: Mable Lee
headline: Mable Lee, Tap-Dancing ‘Queen of the Soundies,’ Dies at 97
abstract: A professional entertainer from the age of 9, Ms. Lee was seen in numerous short musical films as well as in nightclubs and on Broadway.

name: Raymond K. Price Jr.
headline: Raymond K. Price Jr., 88, a Key Nixon Speechwriter, Is Dead
abstract: A former newsman, Mr. Price wrote drafts for the president’s Inaugural Addresses and his resignation speech, lending a moderate voice.

name: A. Ernest Fitzgerald
headline: A. Ernest Fitzgerald, Exposer of Pentagon Waste, Dies at 92
abstract: Fired for testifying about a major Air Force project that far exceeded its budget, he got his job back and never stopped trying to trim Pentagon costs

name: Andrea Levy
headline: Andrea Levy, Author Who Spoke for a Generation of Immigrants, Dies at 62
abstract: Her books were praised for their witty, honest portraits of the immigrant experience, especially of those who moved to Britain from the West Indies after World War II.

name: Tom Cade
headline: Tom Cade, a Savior of the Peregrine Falcon, Dies at 91
abstract: After DDT had wiped the bird out on the East Coast, he led the effort to bring it back. It was eventually removed from the federal endangered species list.

name: Patricia Nell Warren
headline: Patricia Nell Warren, Novelist of Gay Romance, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Warren’s 1974 book, “The Front Runner,” portrayed a positive, open relationship between two men and sold millions of copies.

name: Luis M. Neco
headline: Luis M. Neco, 87, Dies; Barrier-Breaking Puerto Rican Police Official
abstract: He became the highest-ranking official of his heritage that the New York City police had ever appointed when he was named a deputy commissioner.

name: Sharon Mattes
profession: Central Figure in a Gay Custody Case
headline: Sharon Mattes, 48, Dies; Central Figure in a Gay Custody Case
abstract: When she entered into a same-sex relationship, her mother sued for custody of her young son, and won.

name: Betty Ballantine
headline: Betty Ballantine, Who Helped Introduce Paperbacks, Dies at 99
abstract: As a publishing team, she and her husband, Ian, set out in 1939 “to change the reading habits of America,” and to a large extent they did.

name: Li Rui
headline: Li Rui, a Mao Confidant Who Turned Party Critic, Dies at 101
abstract: Once one of Mao Zedong’s personal secretaries, Mr. Li became a revisionist historian and a standard-bearer for liberal values in China.

name: Bruno Ganz
headline: Bruno Ganz, Who Played an Angel and Hitler, Is Dead at 77
abstract: “Wings of Desire” and “Downfall” were among the highlights of Mr. Ganz’s long film career, which he spent mostly in Europe.

name: Patrick Caddell
headline: Patrick Caddell, Self-Taught Pollster Who Helped Carter to White House, Dies at 68
abstract: Decades after aiding the Democratic presidential campaigns of George McGovern and Jimmy Carter, he began advising conservatives like Stephen Bannon.

name: Lee Radziwill
profession: Ex-Princess and Sister of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis
headline: Lee Radziwill, Ex-Princess and Sister of Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, Dies at 85
abstract: She shared the qualities of wealth, social status and ambition with her older sister, but she struggled to achieve professional recognition.

name: Gene Littler
headline: Gene Littler, Golfer With a Gorgeous Swing, Dies at 88
abstract: Littler won 29 tournaments on the PGA Tour, including the United States Open in 1961. He was unassuming in an era dominated by Arnold Palmer, Jack Nicklaus and Gary Player.

name: Kiyoshi Koyama
headline: Kiyoshi Koyama, Prominent Japanese Jazz Journalist, Dies at 82
abstract: As the editor of his country’s leading jazz magazine, he documented the music’s development. As a producer of archival albums, he helped document its past.

name: U Tin
headline: U Tin, Burmese Slide Guitar Master, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Tin adapted a Western instrument to express the richness of Burmese music, including folk tunes, royal court music and movie songs.

name: Don Bragg
headline: Don Bragg, Olympic Pole-Vault Champion, Is Dead at 83
abstract: His dream of playing Tarzan in the movies went unfulfilled, but he set records and won a gold medal at the 1960 Games in Rome.

name: George Mendonsa
profession: Most Likely the Sailor in a Famous Photo
headline: George Mendonsa, 95, Most Likely the Sailor in a Famous Photo, Dies
abstract: Mr. Mendonsa made the most credible claim to being the man captured kissing a woman in Times Square on V-J Day in a picture that became a national emblem.

name: Karl Lagerfeld
headline: Karl Lagerfeld, Designer Who Defined Luxury Fashion, Is Dead
abstract: “He represents the soul of fashion,” said Anna Wintour of Vogue, “restless, forward-looking and voraciously attentive to our changing culture.”

name: Guy Webster
profession: Master of the Album Cover Photograph
headline: Guy Webster, Master of the Album Cover Photograph, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Webster captured memorable images of the Rolling Stones, the Doors, Simon & Garfunkel, the Mamas & the Papas and numerous others.

name: Albert Vorspan
profession: Rallied Reform Judaism for Social Justice
headline: Albert Vorspan, 95, Is Dead; Rallied Reform Judaism for Social Justice
abstract: He was a catalyst in the movement’s embrace of the struggles for civil rights and against the Vietnam War, apartheid and continuing anti-Semitism.

name: Don Newcombe
profession: Dodger Pitcher Helped Break Racial Barrier
headline: Don Newcombe Dies at 92; Dodger Pitcher Helped Break Racial Barrier
abstract: Newcombe, a teammate of Jackie Robinson’s, was an overpowering righty as a rookie of the year, an M.V.P. and the first Cy Young Award winner.

name: Bibi Ferreira
headline: Bibi Ferreira, Grande Dame of Brazilian Stage, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Ferreira, who kept singing well into her 90s, brought Broadway musicals to Brazil and made the music of Édith Piaf and Frank Sinatra her own.

name: Wallace Broecker
profession: Sounded Early Warning on Climate Change
headline: Wallace Broecker, 87, Dies; Sounded Early Warning on Climate Change
abstract: Called by some “the grandfather of climate science,” he wrote a 1975 paper that asked, “Are We on the Brink of a Pronounced Global Warming?”

name: Jeffrey Hart
headline: Jeffrey Hart, Influential and Iconoclastic Conservative, Is Dead at 88
abstract: He was an author, Republican speechwriter, National Review polemicist, Dartmouth Review provocateur and, to many, an antiwar apostate when he defected to Obama.

name: Theodore Isaac Rubin
headline: Theodore Isaac Rubin Is Dead at 95; Popularized Psychotherapy
abstract: Dr. Rubin was a public face of psychotherapy and a prolific author. One of his novels was the basis of the 1962 movie “David and Lisa.”

name: Dorothy Bolden
profession: Started a Movement for Domestic Workers
headline: Overlooked No More: Dorothy Bolden, Who Started a Movement for Domestic Workers
abstract: Bolden adapted the organizing techniques she learned as a civil rights activist to secure protections for domestic workers, a largely unregulated part of the work force.

name: Norman Orentreich
headline: Norman Orentreich, 96, Force Behind Hair Transplants, Dies
abstract: In the 1950s, Dr. Orentreich took hair from the back of the head and planted it in the scalp, and lo, it grew. He also helped establish the Clinique skin-care line.

name: Peter Tork
headline: Peter Tork, Court Jester of the Monkees, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Mr. Tork was an accomplished musician, but he became famous for his comedic role as the goofy member of a made-for-television band.

name: Seweryn Bialer
headline: Seweryn Bialer, 92, Defector and Soviet Union Scholar, Dies
abstract: An author who knew his subject firsthand from his years as an official in Communist Poland, he became a sought-after voice on Soviet affairs.

name: W.E.B. Griffin
headline: W.E.B. Griffin, 89, Dies; a Best-Selling Novelist Dozens of Times
abstract: He estimated that he published more than 150 books — including dozens about soldiers, spies and cops — using numerous pseudonyms (including W.E.B. Griffin).

name: Ken Nordine
profession: Surreal Poet With a Jazz Beat
headline: Ken Nordine, Surreal Poet With a Jazz Beat, Is Dead at 98
abstract: His improvisational poetry, which he called “word jazz,” attracted admiring collaborators like Fred Astaire, Jerry Garcia, Tom Waits and Laurie Anderson.

name: Fred Foster
headline: Fred Foster, Nashville Champion of Talent, Is Dead at 87
abstract: As a producer, a music publisher and the founder of Monument Records, he nurtured the early careers of Roy Orbison, Dolly Parton and Kris Kristofferson.

name: Toni Myers
headline: Toni Myers, Who Turned Astronauts Into Filmmakers, Dies at 75
abstract: She directed Imax space documentaries known for their eye-popping imagery.

name: Ethel Ennis
headline: Ethel Ennis, Singer Who Walked Away From Fame, Is Dead at 86
abstract: She was praised by Billie Holiday, Ella Fitzgerald and Frank Sinatra. But she preferred to stay home and became Baltimore’s “First Lady of Jazz.”

name: Jackie Shane
headline: Jackie Shane, Transgender Pioneer of 1960s Soul Music, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Shane grew up black and transgender in the Jim Crow South, became a star in Canada, then left the stage, returning in 2017 with a Grammy-nominated album.

name: Marella Agnelli
profession: Societys Last Swan and a Passionate Gardener
headline: Marella Agnelli, Society’s ‘Last Swan’ and a Passionate Gardener, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mrs. Agnelli, descended from Neapolitan nobility and married into the Fiat empire, became a subject of high society fascination.

name: Stanley Donen
headline: Stanley Donen, ‘Master of the Musical’ Who Directed ‘Singin’ in the Rain,’ Dies at 94
abstract: He worked on the musical with Gene Kelly, with whom who he also co-directed another famous production, “On the Town.”

name: Donald Keene
headline: Donald Keene, Famed Translator of Japanese Literature, Dies at 96
abstract: The longtime Columbia professor had a passionate interest in Japanese writing and history, making him a celebrity in Japan, where he became a citizen after a nuclear disaster there in 2011.

name: Hilde Zadek
profession: Mainstay of the Vienna State Opera
headline: Hilde Zadek, Mainstay of the Vienna State Opera, Dies at 101
abstract: She made her debut in Vienna in 1947, a Jew who had fled Hitler, and feared onetime Nazis would disrupt her performance. Instead, they applauded.

name: Mac Wiseman
headline: Mac Wiseman, Bluegrass Star Who Was Much More Than That, Dies at 93
abstract: His hallmark was crossing genre lines, recording versions of pop, folk and country tunes, rhythm and blues numbers, a Fleetwood Mac song and more.

name: Bisi Silva
profession: Bold Curator of Contemporary African Art
headline: Bisi Silva, 56, Bold Curator of Contemporary African Art, Dies
abstract: In Nigeria and around the world, Ms. Silva worked to bring wide recognition to African artists and to nurture their careers.

name: Dominick Argento
headline: Dominick Argento, ‘Traditionalist’ Composer of Operas, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Argento, a Pulitzer winner, won acclaim for orchestral and chamber works but was best-known for his accessible and stylistically diverse operas.

name: Perry Wolff
headline: Perry Wolff, Award-Winning TV News Documentarian, Dies at 97
abstract: For CBS News, he oversaw “Hunger in America,” “The Selling of the Pentagon” and, shown on three networks, Jacqueline Kennedy’s “A Tour of the White House.”

name: Brody Stevens
headline: Brody Stevens, Comic Who Explored His Darker Side, Dies at 48
abstract: His subject matter included his own struggles with depression, although he said he didn’t want to be known as “the guy who had this breakdown.”

name: Mark Bramble
headline: Mark Bramble, Book Writer of Broadway’s ‘Barnum,’ Dies at 68
abstract: A Broadway jack-of-all-trades, Mr. Bramble also collaborated on the book for the 1980s blockbuster “42nd Street” and directed its Broadway revival.

name: Dick Churchill
profession: Last Survivor of The Great Escape
headline: Dick Churchill, Last Survivor of ‘The Great Escape,’ Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Churchill took part in the daring breakout from a Nazi prison camp in 1944 that inspired the 1963 film starring Steve McQueen.

name: Jeraldine Saunders
headline: Jeraldine Saunders, Whose Book Begat ‘The Love Boat,’ Dies at 95
abstract: She wrote a memoir about her work as a cruise director. The resulting TV series ran for 250 episodes and became a cultural touchstone.

name: Dorothy Masuka
headline: Dorothy Masuka, South African Singer and Activist, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Masuka was also a prolific songwriter, and many of her songs squarely addressed the racist policies of her country’s government.

name: Ira Gitler
headline: Ira Gitler, Influential Jazz Critic and Historian, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Gitler conveyed an outsize passion for jazz, especially bebop, in reviews, articles, books and liner notes for more than 700 albums.

name: Dondi Donald
headline: Overlooked No More: The Underground Graffiti Adventures of Dondi
abstract: Donald Joseph White, considered a legend before “street art” became popular, turned New York City’s subways into rolling canvases of color, humor and social commentary.

name: Carrie Ann Lucas
headline: Carrie Ann Lucas, Champion for Disabled Parents, Dies at 47
abstract: Ms. Lucas, who lived with multiple disabilities, met resistance when she sought to adopt her niece from foster care. So she helped change the law.

name: Mark Hollis
headline: Mark Hollis, Leader of ’80s Band Talk Talk, Is Dead
abstract: After recording some synth-pop hits, Mr. Hollis’s group veered into an experimental sound that influenced a generation of musicians.

name: André Previn
headline: André Previn, Whose Music Knew No Boundaries, Dies at 89
abstract: A composer, conductor and pianist, he made a career of crossing from classical music to pop, from movie scores to jazz, winning Oscars and Grammys.

name: Edward Nixon
headline: Edward Nixon, 88, President’s Brother and Champion, Is Dead
abstract: A geologist and last surviving Nixon brother, he served in two of Richard Nixon’s campaigns and testified in a Watergate-era conspiracy trial.

name: John O’Neal
profession: Champion of Theater in the Deep South
headline: John O’Neal, 78, Champion of Theater in the Deep South, Dies
abstract: A founder of the Free Southern Theater in 1963, he was as eager to hear his audiences’ stories as he was to perform.

name: Patrick McCarthy
headline: Patrick McCarthy Dies at 67; Ran a Fashion Publishing Empire
abstract: Although he knew little about fashion when he started, Mr. McCarthy rose to run Fairchild, the company that for many years published Women’s Wear Daily and W.

name: Li Xueqin
profession: Key Historian in Chinas Embrace of Antiquity
headline: Li Xueqin, Key Historian in China’s Embrace of Antiquity, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Li walked a fine line between scholarship and serving the Communist Party as he sought the truth about his country’s distant past.

name: Theodore Bayless
headline: Theodore Bayless, Pathbreaker on Dairy Intolerance, Dies at 87
abstract: His research led to commercial innovations for people whose bodies reject milk products, and to better treatments for other gastrointestinal diseases.

name: Jean Fairfax
profession: Unsung but Undeterred in Integrating Schools
headline: Jean Fairfax, Unsung but Undeterred in Integrating Schools, Dies at 98
abstract: At the NAACP Legal Defense and Educational Fund, she was an organizer in the civil rights struggle, in one case escorting a brave 6-year-old to school.

name: Katherine Helmond
profession: Soap and Whos the Boss? Star
headline: Katherine Helmond, ‘Soap’ and ‘Who’s the Boss?’ Star, Dies at 89
abstract: Before she found fame on two long-running television series, Ms. Helmond was a well-regarded stage actress.

name: Charles McCarry
headline: Charles McCarry, 88, Spy Turned Master Spy Novelist, Is Dead
abstract: What Mr. McCarry learned as a Cold War C.I.A. operative served him well as a writer. His fiction was compared to John le Carré’s.

name: Zhores Alferov
profession: Nobel Winner Paved Way for Laser Technology
headline: Zhores Alferov, 88, Dies; Nobel Winner Paved Way for Laser Technology
abstract: A Russian who shared the 2000 physics prize with Americans after they had engaged in a Cold War “laser race.” The work led to DVDs and cellphones.

name: Kevin Roche
headline: Kevin Roche, Architect Who Melded Bold With Elegant, Dies at 96
abstract: A favorite of corporations, museums and government, he was given wide leeway in expressing his restless imagination in refined but daring ways.

name: Ogden R. Reid
headline: Ogden R. Reid, 93, Herald Tribune Editor and Congressman, Dies
abstract: The scion of a newspaper publishing family, he later served in the House representing Westchester County, N.Y., switching from Republican to Democrat.

name: Keith Flint
headline: Keith Flint, 49, Mohawked Frontman of the Prodigy, Dies
abstract: The “Firestarter” and “Breathe” singer, who frightened parents worldwide, took his own life, according to a bandmate.

name: Ted Lindsay
headline: Ted Lindsay, Hall of Fame Scorer Who Powered Red Wings, Dies at 93
abstract: Lindsay, Gordie Howe and Sid Abel were known as hockey’s Production Line as they led Detroit to four Stanley Cup titles in the 1950s.

name: Luke Perry
headline: Luke Perry, ‘Beverly Hills, 90210’ Star, Is Dead at 52
abstract: Starting in 1990, he played the heartthrob Dylan McKay on the long-running Fox drama “90210.” More recently he was Archie’s dad on “Riverdale.”

name: Juan Corona
profession: Convicted as Killer of 25 Farm Workers
headline: Juan Corona, 85, Convicted as Killer of 25 Farm Workers, Dies
abstract: The migrants’ bodies were found in 1971 buried in orchards. He had had a history of mental problems, but why he killed them has never been clear.

name: Kong Bundy
headline: King Kong Bundy, Gargantuan Professional Wrestler, Dies at 63
abstract: Bundy, who was massive even by pro wrestler standards, used his bulk and surprising agility to wrangle with stars like Hulk Hogan and the Undertaker.

name: Eusebio Pedroza
headline: Eusebio Pedroza, Fighter Who Held Title for Seven Years, Dies
abstract: Pedroza, one of the most successful featherweight boxers ever, successfully defended his title 19 times before losing to Barry McGuigan.

name: Joseph Flummerfelt
headline: Joseph Flummerfelt, a Force Behind Mighty Choruses, Dies at 82
abstract: When there were requiems, masses and choral symphonies to conduct, star maestros and leading orchestras called Mr. Flummerfelt and the choirs he led.

name: Julia Morgan
headline: Overlooked No More: Julia Morgan, Pioneering Female Architect
abstract: Morgan, who was the first woman to earn an architect’s license in California, was a prolific designer of hundreds of buildings, namely the Hearst Castle at San Simeon.

name: Hugh Fordin
headline: Hugh Fordin, Writer and Record Producer, Is Dead at 83
abstract: His DRG label specialized in the American songbook, cast albums and artists like Barbara Cook.

name: Marcia Dale Weary
headline: Marcia Dale Weary, Heartland Ballet Teacher, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Ms. Weary’s school in rural Pennsylvania produced an enormous number of professional dancers and stars at major companies.

name: Don Nice
profession: Painter of Pop Art and River Scenes
headline: Don Nice, Painter of Pop Art and River Scenes, Dies at 86
abstract: In a varied career, Mr. Nice broke free of the traditional rectangular canvas and was often inspired by the Hudson River.

name: John Shafer
headline: John Shafer, 94, Who Made Triumphant Leap Into Winemaking, Dies
abstract: At 48, knowing nothing about grape-growing, he gave up his job as a Chicago publishing executive and became a celebrated Napa Valley vintner.

name: Jerry Merryman
headline: Jerry Merryman, Co-Inventor of the Pocket Calculator, Dies at 86
abstract: A self-taught electrical engineer, he joined with two others at Texas Instruments to revolutionize the way people handled everyday mathematics.

name: Carmine Persico
headline: Carmine Persico, Colombo Crime Family Boss, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Persico, nicknamed the Snake, died in prison. He was serving a combined 139-year sentence after being convicted of leading a vast and violent criminal enterprise.

name: Dan Jenkins
profession: Chronicler of Sports in Raucous Prose
headline: Dan Jenkins, 90, Chronicler of Sports in Raucous Prose, Dies
abstract: Mr. Jenkins, an early star at Sports Illustrated, pressed the limits of irreverence in novels often about good old boys.

name: George Stade
headline: George Stade, Scholar-Novelist Partial to the Popular, Dies at 85
abstract: While teaching Joyce and Faulkner (and also Stephen King and Dashiell Hammett), he published “Confessions of a Lady-Killer,” drawing feminist scorn.

name: Robert DeProspero
headline: Robert DeProspero, 80, Innovative Secret Service Agent, Dies
abstract: “If you made a wrong move or did not do what you were supposed to do,” he said of protecting the president, “it would ruin your life.”

name: Gillian Freeman
profession: Groundbreaking Novelist on a Gay Theme
headline: Gillian Freeman, Groundbreaking Novelist on a Gay Theme, Dies at 89
abstract: She drew notice for a story of a gay attraction that threatens a marriage and a fictional diary of a woman in Nazi Germany that some took to be true.

name: Jan-Michael Vincent
headline: Jan-Michael Vincent, Troubled Star of ‘Airwolf,’ Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Vincent was seen frequently in movies and on TV in the 1970s and ’80s. But his career later foundered, in part because of drug and alcohol abuse.

name: Sidney Sheinberg
headline: Sidney Sheinberg, a Force Behind Universal and Spielberg, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Mr. Sheinberg helped turn the studio into a behemoth with theme parks, record companies, television production and, above all, movie blockbusters.

name: Peter Hurford
profession: Organist Noted for His Complete Bach
headline: Peter Hurford, Organist Noted for His Complete Bach, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Hurford, who was also a composer and choir director, was known for the simplicity, clarity and rhythmic vitality of his organ playing.

name: Barbara Winslow Grant
headline: Barbara Winslow Grant, Mother of Times Chairman, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Grant, who was the wife of one Times publisher, mother of another and grandmother of a third, devoted much of her life to volunteerism.

name: Julia Ruth Stevens
headline: Julia Ruth Stevens, Babe Ruth’s Daughter, Dies at 102
abstract: The Babe’s adopted daughter was a tireless promoter of baseball, and of her father’s legacy.

name: Carolee Schneemann
headline: Carolee Schneemann, Visionary Feminist Performance Artist, Dies at 79
abstract: In one performance piece, she stood nude on a table, posing like a studio model, while reading from a book of her collected writings.

name: Harry Howell
profession: Star Defenseman With Rangers for 17 Years
headline: Harry Howell, Star Defenseman With Rangers for 17 Years, Dies at 86
abstract: He played 1,160 regular-season games with the Rangers, a team record that still stands, and was a seven-time All-Star.

name: Mel Miller
headline: Mel Miller, Assembly Speaker With Tarnished Career, Dies at 79
abstract: He rose to the highest ranks of New York State government but left politics after a fraud conviction, even though it was later overturned on appeal.

name: Joseph Boardman
headline: Joseph Boardman, 70, Amtrak Chief During Record Growth, Dies
abstract: During Mr. Boardman’s tenure as overseer of the nation’s passenger railroads, from 2008 to 2016, he presided over increases in ridership and revenue.

name: John Richardson
headline: John Richardson, Art Historian and Picasso Biographer, Is Dead at 95
abstract: A protean citizen of the art world — artist, curator, dealer, collector and more — he wrote a monumental four-volume life of a 20th-century giant.

name: Jacques Loussier
headline: Jacques Loussier, Pianist Who Jazzed Up Bach, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Loussier’s trio, formed in 1959, played Bach’s music with jazz inflections, selling millions of albums and performing around the world.

name: Hal Blaine
headline: Hal Blaine, Wrecking Crew Drummer, Is Dead at 90
abstract: One of the busiest session musicians of all time, he brought percussive drama to records by Frank Sinatra, Elvis Presley and countless others.

name: Edda Goering
headline: Edda Goering, Unrepentant Daughter of Hermann, Dies at 80
abstract: The only daughter of the leader of the Luftwaffe and Hitler’s potential successor, she defended her father’s legacy after his death.

name: Michael Gielen
headline: Michael Gielen, Uncompromising German Maestro, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Mr. Gielen, who also composed, was animated by the music of the 20th century and brought daring opera productions to Frankfurt.

name: Isabella Goodwin
profession: New York Citys First Female Police Detective
headline: Overlooked No More: Isabella Goodwin, New York City’s First Female Police Detective
abstract: Goodwin, a police matron overseeing female inmates, earned her detective shield for going undercover as a scrubwoman to expose a bank robber.

name: Sidney Verba
headline: Sidney Verba, Innovative Scholar of Democracies, Dies at 86
abstract: His pioneering research compared civic participation and democracy in five countries. In a parallel career, he headed, and digitized, Harvard’s library.

name: Barbara Low
profession: Research Identified the Shape of Penicillin
headline: Barbara Low, Whose Research Identified the Shape of Penicillin, Dies at 98
abstract: Her work with Dorothy Hodgkin unleashed a bonanza of lifesaving antibiotics and gave other female scientists a foothold in a male-dominated field.

name: William C. Powers Jr.
headline: William C. Powers Jr., 72, Author of Scathing Enron Report, Is Dead
abstract: In investigating one of the nation’s largest corporate scandals, he called Enron’s actions “absolutely appalling.” He also led the University of Texas.

name: Birch Bayh
profession: Senator Drove Title IX and 2 Amendments
headline: Birch Bayh, 91, Dies; Senator Drove Title IX and 2 Amendments
abstract: Mr. Bayh, from Indiana, was a force in laws barring sex discrimination, giving 18-year-olds the vote and providing for the removal of a president.

name: Vivian Cherry
headline: Vivian Cherry, 98, Socially Aware Street Photographer, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Cherry was originally a dancer, but she abandoned the “fantasy world” of dance as a young woman to document the reality of life in New York.

name: Harry Hughes
headline: Harry Hughes, Governor Who Brought Change to Maryland, Dies at 92
abstract: Delivering a rebuke to his state’s culture of corruption, he promised voters an honest and understated administration — and largely delivered.

name: Marian Sulzberger Heiskell
profession: Civic Leader in New York City
headline: Marian Sulzberger Heiskell, Civic Leader in New York City, Dies at 100
abstract: Mrs. Heiskell, a member of the family that controls The New York Times, was an influential leader in urban recreation spaces and helped restore the grandeur to theaters near Times Square.

name: Milton Moskowitz
headline: Milton Moskowitz, ‘Best Companies’ List Maker, Is Dead at 91
abstract: He and a colleague first wrote about the 100 best places to work in 1984. The list they created has appeared annually in Fortune magazine since 1998.

name: Al Silverman
headline: Al Silverman, Writer Behind ‘Brian’s Song,’ Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Silverman collaborated with Gale Sayers on his memoir, a chapter of which was later adapted into one of the most popular TV movies of all time.

name: W.S. Merwin
headline: W.S. Merwin, Poet of Life’s Damnable Evanescence, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Merwin, one of the world’s most decorated poets, sang of silence and nature with an oracular voice. Later in life he became an ardent conservationist.

name: Johnny Jones
headline: Johnny (Lam) Jones, Texas Track and Football Star, Dies at 60
abstract: Jones won a gold medal at the 1976 Olympics and signed pro football’s first million-dollar contract, with the Jets. But N.F.L. stardom eluded him.

name: Edith Iglauer
headline: Edith Iglauer, Journalist and Bard of Canada, Dies at 101
abstract: Ms. Iglauer, an American, came to Canada to portray it for the rest of the world. But she made it her home and wrote with an insider’s perspective.

name: Marjorie Weinman Sharmat
headline: Marjorie Weinman Sharmat, 90, ‘Nate the Great’ Author, Dies
abstract: Her detective hero, who loved pancakes and his dog, Sludge, helped children learn how to read — and how to sleuth.

name: Helen Miller
headline: Helen Miller, 82, Labor Champion of Home-Care Workers, Dies
abstract: A home-care worker who believed in the dignity of helping sick, elderly and disabled people, Ms. Miller became a respected union leader

name: Dick Dale
headline: Dick Dale, 81, King of the Surf Guitar, Dies
abstract: Mr. Dale was known for “Misirlou,” which Quentin Tarantino used as the opening anthem to his film “Pulp Fiction.”

name: Alan B. Krueger
profession: Economic Aide to Clinton and Obama
headline: Alan B. Krueger, Economic Aide to Clinton and Obama, Is Dead at 58
abstract: A labor economist, Princeton scholar, Treasury official and chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers. The police said the cause was suicide.

name: Okwui Enwezor
headline: Okwui Enwezor, Curator Who Remapped Art World, Dies at 55
abstract: In large shows like Documenta and the Venice Biennale, he put art from around the globe on an equal footing with that of Europe and the United States.

name: Johnny Thompson
headline: Johnny Thompson, a Magician’s Magician, Is Dead at 84
abstract: As the Great Tomsoni, he made audiences laugh and gasp. As a consultant, he showed other magicians how to get the most out of a trick.

name: J.H. Kwabena Nketia
headline: J.H. Kwabena Nketia, 97, Pre-eminent Scholar of African Music, Dies
abstract: Dr. Nketia, who had an international presence, documented, analyzed and championed traditional music of the continent until his final days.

name: James Dapogny
headline: James Dapogny, Who Resurrected Jazz of the Past, Dies at 78
abstract: He was especially known for bringing renewed appreciation to Jelly Roll Morton.

name: Rachel Ingalls
headline: Rachel Ingalls, 78, Rediscovered Author of ‘Mrs. Caliban,’ Dies
abstract: Her 1982 tale of a lonely woman who falls in love with a sea creature had a revival, dovetailing with the release of the 2017 film “The Shape of Water.”

name: Bernard Krisher
headline: Bernard Krisher, Free Press Champion in Cambodia, Dies at 87
abstract: A former Newsweek reporter, he founded the country’s first English-language newspaper and, as a philanthropist, established a hospital and hundreds of schools.

name: Jake Phelps
profession: as Thrasher Editor, a Skateboarding Guru
headline: Jake Phelps Dies at 56; as Thrasher Editor, a Skateboarding Guru
abstract: From his perch, Mr. Phelps set the caustic but funny tone for the magazine, making him both loved and hated in the skateboarding world.

name: Andre Williams
profession: Sang of Bacon Fat and Tail Feathers
headline: Andre Williams, 82, Dies; Sang of Bacon Fat and Tail Feathers
abstract: An earthy R&B performer, he began his career in the 1950s, was sidelined by addiction, then was rediscovered in the ’90s by punk and garage rockers.

name: Barbara Hammer
headline: Barbara Hammer, Filmmaker of Lesbian Sexuality, Dies at 79
abstract: After Ms. Hammer came out in the 1970s, her films took a provocative and influential turn. “One of my goals,” she said, “was to put a lesbian on camera.”

name: Elizabeth Peratrovich
headline: Overlooked No More: Elizabeth Peratrovich, Rights Advocate for Alaska Natives
abstract: Peratrovich and her husband rallied Natives to ensure the passage of the 1945 Anti-Discrimination Act, the first anti-discrimination law in the United States.

name: Randy Jackson
headline: Randy Jackson, a Fence-Clearing Footnote to Baseball History, Dies at 93
abstract: In the next-to-last game of the 1957 season, he became the last Brooklyn Dodger to hit a home run before the team moved to Los Angeles.

name: Antonia Rey
profession: Latin Actress of Stage and Screen
headline: Antonia Rey, Latin Actress of Stage and Screen, Dies at 92
abstract: She and her husband fled Cuba under Castro, giving up their prominence in theater there. In the North, she had a steady diet of ethnic roles.

name: Anita Silvers
headline: Anita Silvers, an Authority on Disability Rights, Dies at 78
abstract: A well-regarded philosophy professor, Dr. Silvers knew the subject firsthand, having had polio as a child.

name: Maya Turovskaya
headline: Maya Turovskaya, Russian Critic and Documentarian, Dies at 94
abstract: Called “the Susan Sontag of Soviet aesthetic thought,” she wrote about movies and theater and helped make a film that drew parallels between Nazism and Stalin.

name: Rafi Eitan
headline: Rafi Eitan, 92, Israeli Spymaster Who Caught Eichmann, Is Dead
abstract: He led the team that seized the Nazi architect of the Final Solution in Argentina and later handled the American spy Jonathan Jay Pollard.

name: Godfried Danneels
profession: Liberal Cardinal Tainted by Sex Scandal
headline: Godfried Danneels, Liberal Cardinal Tainted by Sex Scandal, Dies at 85
abstract: He was considered a progressive in Roman Catholic leadership. But his reputation was hurt when it was learned that he had urged a victim of abuse not to talk.

name: Alessandro Mendini
headline: Alessandro Mendini, Designer Known for Splash, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Whether a crazy quilt of a museum in the Netherlands or a whimsical corkscrew that looked like his friend Anna, Mr. Mendini’s work drew attention.

name: Robert W. Sweet
headline: Robert W. Sweet, Mayor’s Deputy Turned Federal Judge, Is Dead at 96
abstract: He was John Lindsay’s voice in tense labor talks. On the bench, he deemed panhandling free speech and said McDonald’s can’t be blamed for obesity.

name: Cal Ramsey
headline: Cal Ramsey, Knicks Broadcaster and Community Representative, Dies at 81
abstract: A standout player at N.Y.U., he had a brief N.B.A. career but made his mark as a color commentator and the team’s link to the youth of New York.

name: Scott Walker
headline: Scott Walker, Pop Singer Who Turned Experimental, Dies at 76
abstract: Forsaking the music that made his group, the Walker Brothers, a 1960s sensation, he veered toward the avant-garde, influencing David Bowie and Radiohead.

name: Larry Cohen
headline: Larry Cohen, Director of Garish Horror Classics, Dies at 82
abstract: His films, which featured killer babies and desserts, offered suspense and horror bordering on satire. He was also a prolific creator of television shows.

name: Mike Greco
profession: Salami King of Bronxs Little Italy
headline: Mike Greco, Salami King of Bronx’s Little Italy, Dies at 89
