abstract: The “Mayor of Arthur Avenue” came from Calabria in 1947 and opened a deli that endures as a magnet for locals, politicians and Bronx expatriates.

name: Andrew Marshall
headline: Andrew Marshall, Pentagon’s Threat Expert, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Marshall led a little-known office that has helped shape American military thinking, and kept his focus on China even when that was out of fashion.

name: Linda Gregg
headline: Linda Gregg, Poet of Taut, Vivid Verse, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Ms. Gregg found poems in nature and loss, matters of the heart and matters of the spirit.

name: Janet Lieberman
headline: Janet Lieberman, 97, a Force in Community College Education, Dies
abstract: From its inception she was a guiding spirit at LaGuardia Community College in Queens with national influence in helping underserved students.

name: Ranking Roger
headline: Ranking Roger, a Star of the Ska Revival, Is Dead at 56
abstract: He was one of two frontmen for the British group the Beat 40 years ago, and he was still releasing new music this year.

name: Fred Malek
headline: Fred Malek, 82, Republican Fund-Raiser and Presidential Adviser, Dies
abstract: Mr. Malek spurred the party from its slump after 2008, helping Republicans to capture 84 governorships over the next decade.

name: Bessie Blount
headline: Overlooked No More: Bessie Blount, Nurse, Wartime Inventor and Handwriting Expert
abstract: Blount invented a feeding device and taught amputee veterans to write with their teeth and their feet. She later became a forensic handwriting analyst.

name: Henry J. Stern
headline: Henry J. Stern, Whose Vast Urban Domain Was Green, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Only Robert Moses surpassed Mr. Stern, New York City’s longtime parks commissioner, in ensuring that a teeming population had places to breathe.

name: Michel Bacos
profession: Hero Pilot of Jet Hijacked to Entebbe
headline: Michel Bacos, Hero Pilot of Jet Hijacked to Entebbe, Dies at 94
abstract: An Air France commander, he insisted on remaining with his Jewish and Israeli hostages until they were rescued by Israeli commandos in a daring raid.

name: Victoria Ruvolo
headline: Victoria Ruvolo, Who Forgave Her Attacker, Is Dead at 59
abstract: She was severely injured when a teenager threw a frozen turkey that smashed through her car’s windshield. But she argued against a harsh sentence.

name: Agnès Varda
headline: Agnès Varda Is Dead at 90; Influential French New Wave Filmmaker
abstract: Ms. Varda was closely associated with the movement known as the New Wave, although her reimagining of cinematic conventions actually predated it.

name: Michael Lynne
profession: Key Figure at New Line Cinema
headline: Michael Lynne, a Key Figure at New Line Cinema, Dies at 77
abstract: He helped turn the small studio into a major player responsible for hits like the “Lord of the Rings” trilogy. He was also known for his winemaking.

name: Mary Warnock
headline: Mary Warnock, Who Offered Guidance on Embryo Use, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Warnock a British moral philosopher, oversaw a committee that examined how to regulate the creation of human life in laboratories.

name: Genevieve Oswald
headline: Genevieve Oswald, the Soul of a Dance Archive, Is Dead at 97
abstract: As the curator for 43 years of the New York Public Library’s dance collection, which she founded, Ms. Oswald helped preserve a fragile art form’s history.

name: Tejshree Thapa
profession: Defender of Human Rights in South Asia
headline: Tejshree Thapa, Defender of Human Rights in South Asia, Dies at 52
abstract: Her investigations sought to establish mass rape and sexual enslavement as crimes against humanity. She also spent time in the field with survivors.

name: David White
profession: Hitmaker With Danny and the Juniors
headline: David White, Hitmaker With Danny and the Juniors, Dies at 79
abstract: He co-wrote the No. 1 hit “At the Hop” and wrote its follow-up, “Rock and Roll Is Here to Stay.” He later helped write hits for Lesley Gore and others.

name: Kenneth Gibson
profession: Newark Mayor Broke Race Barrier in Northeast
headline: Kenneth Gibson, 86, Dies; Newark Mayor Broke Race Barrier in Northeast
abstract: He pledged to make Newark a model city, saying, “If we solve the urban problem here, we can export our solution to other areas.”

name: Charles Sanna
headline: Charles Sanna, Man Behind Swiss Miss Cocoa, Dies at 101
abstract: A surplus of perishable powdered milk was the mother of invention for the popular instant drink made with hot water and formulated in the early 1960s.

name: Gerry Stickells
headline: Gerry Stickells, Who Helped Make Rock Shows Big, Dies at 76
abstract: His skills as production manager were invaluable to Queen, Paul McCartney and others as the logistics of touring and performing grew increasingly elaborate.

name: S.N. Goenka
headline: Overlooked No More: S.N. Goenka, Who Brought Mindfulness to the West
abstract: He gave up life as a successful Burmese businessman to teach meditation in India, and played a significant role in the explosion of interest in meditation as we know it today.

name: Natalia Fileva
headline: Natalia Fileva, Leader in Russia’s ‘Babyflot’ Airlines, Dies at 55
abstract: Ms. Fileva, who died in a plane crash, was the rare woman to hold an executive post in Russia. She helped consolidate the post-Soviet airline industry.

name: Lyle Tuttle
profession: Recast Tattooings Image Pore by Pore
headline: Lyle Tuttle, Who Recast Tattooing’s Image Pore by Pore, Dies at 87
abstract: Tattooed almost head to foot himself, he helped move the art form “out of the back alley” and into the mainstream, finding fame with a celebrity clientele.

name: David Fechheimer
headline: David Fechheimer, a Reserved but Adroit Sam Spade, Dies at 76
abstract: A practitioner of old-fashioned investigative techniques, he was inconspicuous compared with many of his colleagues and high-profile clients.

name: Joe Bellino
profession: Navy Star and Heisman Trophy Winner
headline: Joe Bellino, 81, Navy Star and Heisman Trophy Winner, Dies
abstract: A fleet running back, he was the overwhelming choice for the 1960 Heisman, but his pro career, delayed by military service, fell short of expectations.

name: Ralph Metzner
headline: Ralph Metzner, LSD and Consciousness Researcher, Dies at 82
abstract: After participated in controversial studies by Timothy Leary involving hallucinogens, he continued researching alternate states of consciousness.

name: Mona Lee Brock
headline: Mona Lee Brock, Farmers’ ‘Angel’ on the Line, Dies at 87
abstract: She cautioned suicidal farmers to think what it would be like for their children “if they sat down at the supper table and there would be an empty chair.”

name: Rapper Who
headline: A Rapper Who Came Back for His Neighborhood
abstract: The son of an Eritrean father, Nipsey Hussle grew up in Los Angeles, joined a gang and dropped out of school before hearing “wake-up calls.”

name: Sydel Silverman
headline: Sydel Silverman, 85, Dies; Defended Anthropology in Academia
abstract: As a scholar, teacher and historian at the City University of New York, she was an ardent preservationist and an inclusive ethnographer.

name: Sydney Brenner
headline: Sydney Brenner, a Decipherer of the Genetic Code, Is Dead at 92
abstract: A Nobel Prize winner, he was a central player in the golden age of molecular biology, beginning with the discovery of the structure of DNA.

name: Jonathan Baumbach
headline: Jonathan Baumbach, Novelist With an Experimental Bent, Dies at 85
abstract: Concerned about the limited interests of conventional publishers, Mr. Baumbach also helped found a publishing collective run by writers.

name: Kim English
headline: Kim English, Who Blended Gospel With Dance Music, Dies at 48
abstract: Ms. English had more than a dozen house-music hits. But her songs, her longtime manager said, were “all related to God.”

name: Vonda N. McIntyre
profession: Champion of Women in Science Fiction
headline: Vonda N. McIntyre, 70, Champion of Women in Science Fiction, Dies
abstract: Ms. McIntyre won three Nebula Awards for her writing and inspired other female authors. She also wrote five novels set in the “Star Trek” universe.

name: Dan Robbins
headline: Dan Robbins, Who Made Painting as Easy as 1-2-3 (and 4-5-6), Dies at 93
abstract: But was it art? No, Mr. Robbins said, but paint-by-numbers kits — all the rage among young baby boomers — gave the inartistic the “experience” of art.

name: Yisroel Avrohom Portugal
headline: Yisroel Avrohom Portugal, Revered Orthodox Rabbi, Dies at 95
abstract: He drew long lines to his home in Brooklyn, but he chose not to translate that veneration into a community of acolytes on a grand scale.

name: Ly Tong
headline: Ly Tong, Vietnamese Pilot Who Hijacked Planes to Fight Communism, Dies at 74
abstract: A South Vietnam Air Force veteran, Mr. Ly Tong dropped leaflets over Ho Chi Minh City in 1992 and 2000. His actions made him a hero to many Vietnamese refugees.

name: Ernest Hollings
headline: Ernest Hollings, 97, a South Carolina Senator Who Evolved, Is Dead
abstract: Once a foe of civil rights legislation, he came to support a more liberal social agenda after a tour of poor, black areas of his state shocked him.

name: Bob Slade
headline: Bob Slade, Distinguished Voice on Black Radio, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Slade was a host of “Open Line,” a call-in show that dedicated to the African-American community that conveyed a perspective lacking in news media.

name: Cho Yang-ho
headline: Cho Yang-ho, 70, Dies; Expanded Korean Air Amid Scandals
abstract: Recently stripped of a board seat in his family’s empire, Mr. Cho had been caught up in corruption investigations and a daughter’s “nut rage” incident.

name: Marilynn Smith
headline: Marilynn Smith, an L.P.G.A. Founder and Tour Champion, Is Dead at 89
abstract: She was one of 13 women who started a league of their own, having so little money at first that they traveled to tournaments in highway caravans.

name: Richard Cole
profession: Last Survivor of Doolittle Raid on Japan
headline: Richard Cole, 103, Last Survivor of Doolittle Raid on Japan, Dies
abstract: He was Jimmy Doolittle’s co-pilot in the first airstrike against the Japanese homeland, an event that buoyed Americans still reeling from Pearl Harbor.

name: Ed Westcott
profession: Singular Eye at the Dawn of the Atomic Age
headline: Ed Westcott, a Singular Eye at the Dawn of the Atomic Age, Dies at 97
abstract: He was the government’s official photographer at Oak Ridge, Tenn., a secret city where uranium was enriched for the bomb that fell on Hiroshima.

name: Charles Van Doren
headline: Charles Van Doren, a Quiz Show Whiz Who Wasn’t, Dies at 93
abstract: A charismatic and well-pedigreed contestant, he confessed to Congress that his ballyhooed TV performances in the 1950s had been scandalously rigged.

name: Lawrence Rhodes
headline: Lawrence Rhodes, Celebrated Dancer and Renowned Teacher, Dies at 79
abstract: His performances in both classical ballet and modern existential works were widely hailed. “He was my hero,” American Ballet Theater’s director said.

name: Jean-Louis David
profession: French Hairstylist for the Modern Woman
headline: Jean-Louis David, French Hairstylist for the Modern Woman, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. David, who created looks that emphasized practicality as well as style, founded a worldwide chain of salons that bear his name.

name: Rose Morgan
headline: Overlooked No More: Rose Morgan, a Pioneer in Hairdressing and Harlem
abstract: From 1945 on, her Rose Meta House of Beauty drew black women around the country to the famed enclave of Sugar Hill and “the biggest Negro beauty parlor in the world.”

name: Ralph Solecki
headline: Ralph Solecki, Who Found Humanity in Neanderthals, Dies at 101
abstract: Dr. Solecki’s archaeological research at Shanidar Cave in Iraq found that Neanderthals cared for the ailing and buried their dead with flowers.

name: Lorraine Branham
headline: Lorraine Branham, Journalism Dean and Mentor, Dies at 66
abstract: As the first woman and first person of color to lead the Newhouse School at Syracuse, she helped students and faculty embrace the future — and diversity.

name: Jacob A. Stein
headline: Jacob A. Stein, an Eminence Among Washington Lawyers, Dies at 94
abstract: He won a rare Watergate acquittal, gained immunity for Monica Lewinsky to testify against President Clinton and, in the Reagan years, investigated Edwin Meese.

name: Kitty Tucker
profession: Raised Awareness of the Silkwood Case
headline: Kitty Tucker, 75, Who Raised Awareness of the Silkwood Case, Dies
abstract: She saw the whistle-blower Karen Silkwood as a feminist hero in the movement against nuclear power and helped organize the legal effort on her behalf.

name: Earl Thomas Conley
headline: Earl Thomas Conley, Country Star of the 1980s, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Singing in a smoky baritone about the complexity of romantic relationships, Mr. Conley topped the country charts 24 times, often with a flavor of soul.

name: Joan Jones
profession: Force Against Racism in Nova Scotia
headline: Joan Jones, 79, Force Against Racism in Nova Scotia, Dies
abstract: In the 1960s, she and her husband galvanized black residents, who were underrepresented in politics and saw high rates of incarceration and unemployment.

name: Forrest Gregg
profession: Iron Man Lineman for Lombardis Packers
headline: Forrest Gregg, Iron Man Lineman for Lombardi’s Packers, Dies at 85
abstract: An All-Pro on championship teams and a Hall of Famer, he powered Green Bay’s turf-churning “sweep.” He was later a head coach of three N.F.L. teams.

name: Donald Stewart
profession: Took Over the College Board at a Crucial Time
headline: Donald Stewart, 80, Dies; Took Over the College Board at a Crucial Time
abstract: He favored high standards for college applicants and programs to help minority students meet those standards. Earlier he had helped revive Spelman College.

name: Sam Pilafian
headline: Sam Pilafian, Tuba Maestro of Multiple Genres, Dies at 69
abstract: Considered one of the world’s best tuba players, he forged a successful career as a soloist and was a founding member of the quintet Empire Brass.

name: James Winn
profession: Dryden Biographer and a Skilled Flutist
headline: James Winn, 71, Dryden Biographer and a Skilled Flutist, Dies
abstract: Whether he was writing a Restoration period biography or a book on war poetry, his background in music informed his approach.

name: Paul Greengard
headline: Paul Greengard, 93, Nobel Prize-Winning Neuroscientist, Is Dead
abstract: His 15-year quest to understand how brain cells communicate provided the underlying science for many antipsychotic drugs.

name: Bibi Andersson
headline: Bibi Andersson, Luminous Presence in Bergman Films, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Andersson, a Swedish actress, personified first purity and youth, then complexity and disillusionment, in 13 Ingmar Bergman films.

name: David Brion Davis
headline: David Brion Davis, Prizewinning Historian of Slavery, Dies at 92
abstract: In a revelatory trilogy, Professor Davis, called “one of the most influential historians of his generation,” placed slavery at the center of American history.

name: Mirjana Markovic
headline: Mirjana Markovic, the ‘Lady Macbeth’ of War-Torn Serbia, Dies at 76
abstract: She and her husband, Slobodan Milosevic, led their country into catastrophic wars. Accused of genocide, he died while awaiting trial; she fled to Russia.

name: Georgia Engel
headline: Georgia Engel, Gentle-Voiced ‘Mary Tyler Moore’ Actress, Is Dead at 70
abstract: After gaining fame as the blustery newsman Ted Baxter’s love interest, Ms. Engel went on to “Everybody Loves Raymond” and more.

name: Stanley Plumly
headline: Stanley Plumly, Lyrical Poet Influenced by Keats, Dies at 79
abstract: “Keats, for me, represents the integrity of the mission of the poet,” said Mr. Plumly, whose books included a “personal biography” called “Posthumous Keats.”

name: Owen Garriott
headline: Owen Garriott, 88, an Early Scientist-Astronaut, Is Dead
abstract: He was the science pilot on the record-breaking 59-day mission to Skylab in 1973. Ten years later, he returned to space on the shuttle Columbia.

name: Barbara Schultz
profession: Produced Serious Drama in a Sitcom Era
headline: Barbara Schultz, 92, Dies; Produced Serious Drama in a Sitcom Era
abstract: At a time when comedies and variety shows dominated TV (and few women held executive jobs), she gave viewers “CBS Playhouse” and, later, “Visions” on PBS.

name: Aloha Wanderwell
headline: Overlooked No More: Aloha Wanderwell, Explorer and Filmmaker
abstract: By 16, she was traveling around the world behind the wheel of a Model T in a life of adventure that was interrupted only by a murder mystery.

name: Claude Lalanne
headline: Claude Lalanne, Whimsical (and Sought-After) Sculptor, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Her works, like a metal cabbage with chicken legs, weren’t taken seriously at first but now command lofty prices.

name: James W. McCord Jr.
headline: James W. McCord Jr., Who Led the Watergate Break-In, Is Dead at 93
abstract: He was the first to expose the White House crimes and cover-ups that led to President Nixon’s downfall. His death, almost two years ago, went unreported.

name: Gene Wolfe
headline: Gene Wolfe, Acclaimed Science Fiction Writer, Dies at 87
abstract: His four-book series “The Book of the New Sun” is considered one of the major works of the genre.

name: Lyra McKee
profession: Journalist; Killed Covering Northern Ireland Unrest
headline: Lyra McKee, 29, Journalist; Killed Covering Northern Ireland Unrest
abstract: An author, speaker and gay-rights activist, she was shot during rioting on Thursday just after tweeting: “Derry tonight. Absolute madness.”

name: Warren Adler
headline: Warren Adler, ‘The War of the Roses’ Author, Is Dead at 91
abstract: A late-blooming novelist, he had his greatest success with a comedy about a couple in a domestic free-for-all. It became a hit movie.

name: Sally O’Neill
headline: Sally O’Neill, Rights Worker in Central America, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. O’Neill and a colleague, Ana Paula Hernandez, were killed in a car crash while gathering information on the political crisis in Guatemala.

name: Lorraine Warren
profession: Paranormal Investigator Portrayed in The Conjuring
headline: Lorraine Warren, Paranormal Investigator Portrayed in ‘The Conjuring,’ Dies at 92
abstract: She and her husband looked into that famed house of spookiness in Amityville, and their cases turned into films.

name: Geraldyn M. Cobb
profession: Found a Glass Ceiling in Space
headline: Geraldyn M. Cobb, 88, Who Found a Glass Ceiling in Space, Dies
abstract: She was as qualified as any man to be an astronaut and passed all the tests, but NASA wasn’t interested in sending women into space in 1961.

name: Jayne Wrightsman
profession: Arts Benefactor and Doyenne of High Society
headline: Jayne Wrightsman, Arts Benefactor and Doyenne of High Society, Dies at 99
abstract: Mrs. Wrightsman, who had no formal training, became a connoisseur of 18th-century French art and a significant donor to the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

name: David Thouless
profession: Nobel Laureate Cast Light on Matter
headline: David Thouless, 84, Dies; Nobel Laureate Cast Light on Matter
abstract: Using math to explain strange states of matter, like superconductivity, he had a “transformational” impact on physics, with real-world applications.

name: David V. Picker
headline: David V. Picker, Film Executive Behind Many Hits, Dies at 87
abstract: He was crucial to the James Bond franchise, the Beatles movies, “Midnight Cowboy” and more.

name: Henry W. Bloch
headline: Henry W. Bloch, Tax-Preparation Pioneer (and Pitchman), Is Dead at 96
abstract: With his brother Richard, Mr. Bloch founded H&R Block, one of the most recognizable brands in American business.

name: David Hamburg
headline: Dr. David Hamburg, Leader in Conflict Resolution, Dies at 93
abstract: As a behavioral scientist and president of the Carnegie Corporation, he took on policy issues that bring about “hatred and violence and ignorance.”

name: Verena Lafferentz
headline: Verena Lafferentz, 98, Last of Wagner Grandchildren, Is Dead
abstract: Unlike the other grandchildren, she had no musical ambitions. She was rumored to be romantically involved with Hitler and married a high-ranking Nazi.

name: Mark Medoff
profession: Children of a Lesser God Playwright
headline: Mark Medoff, ‘Children of a Lesser God’ Playwright, Is Dead at 79
abstract: The work, featuring a central character who is deaf, won the Tony Award for best play in 1980 and was turned into an Oscar-winning 1986 movie.

name: Grand Duke Jean
headline: Grand Duke Jean of Luxembourg Is Dead at 98
abstract: A decorated combat veteran of World War II, he reigned for 36 years, many of them coinciding with a period of great prosperity for his small country.

name: Heather Harper
headline: Heather Harper, Beloved Soprano and Britten Interpreter, Dies at 88
abstract: The Northern Irish-born Ms. Harper moved from lighter opera roles to Wagner and Strauss and took part in the premiere of Britten’s “War Requiem.”

name: Martin Sostre
profession: Reformed Americas Prisons From His Cell
headline: Overlooked No More: Martin Sostre, Who Reformed America’s Prisons From His Cell
abstract: The lawsuits he filed from behind bars in the 1960s and ’70s challenging harsh prison conditions laid the groundwork for prisoners to defend their rights even today.

name: Fay McKenzie
profession: Almost the Length of Her Screen Career
headline: Fay McKenzie Dies at 101, Almost the Length of Her Screen Career
abstract: Five 1940s movies with Gene Autry were high points of her century-spanning run, which began in silent films as an infant. She shot her last role last year.

name: Marilyn Mason
headline: Marilyn Mason, Globe-Trotting Organist and Teacher, Dies at 93
abstract: Championing living composers, Dr. Mason commissioned more than 70 pieces for the king of instruments while teaching for a record 67 years.

name: Nils Nilsson
profession: Scientist Helped Robots Find Their Way
headline: Nils Nilsson, 86, Dies; Scientist Helped Robots Find Their Way
abstract: He was part of a Stanford team whose work in artificial intelligence has found its way into smartphones, Siri and other hallmarks of the algorithmic age.

name: John L’Heureux
headline: John L’Heureux, Whose Novels Wrestled With Faith, Dies at 84
abstract: “God is not dead in L’Heureux stories,” one critic wrote. “He’s simply absent, joking or malicious.” A former priest, L’Heureux wrote more than 20 books.

name: John Havlicek
profession: Dynamo in Two Eras of Celtics Glory
headline: John Havlicek, a Dynamo in Two Eras of Celtics Glory, Dies at 79
abstract: “Hondo,” as he was called, was a relentless, clutch and consistently proficient player on eight championship teams in a 16-season Hall of Fame career.

name: Steve Golin
profession: Producer Built a Small Hollywood Empire
headline: Steve Golin Is Dead at 64; Producer Built a Small Hollywood Empire
abstract: His company, Anonymous Content, produced TV series, music videos and two candidates for the 2016 best-picture Oscar, including the winner, “Spotlight.”

name: Michael Koskoff
headline: Michael Koskoff, Fierce Litigator in Momentous Fights, Dies at 77
abstract: He sued hospitals for malpractice, helped integrate police and fire departments and sought to hold gunmakers liable in the Sandy Hook massacre.

name: Michael Fesco
headline: Michael Fesco, Whose Gay Clubs Were Trendsetters, Dies at 84
abstract: His Ice Palace on Fire Island and Flamingo in Manhattan gave gay men the opportunity to meet, dance and perhaps find a sense of empowerment.

name: Michael Wolf
headline: Michael Wolf, Who Photographed Skyscrapers Minus the Sky, Dies at 64
abstract: Framing buildings in disorienting fashion, he created images of Hong Kong’s density. He also recorded the minutiae of its everyday life.

name: Ira Neimark
headline: Ira Neimark, Bergdorf Executive Who Put Fashion First, Dies at 97
abstract: As president, Mr. Neimark helped transform what had been seen as a safe, dull and expensive store into an avatar of luxurious shopping.

name: Manuel Luján Jr.
headline: Manuel Luján Jr., Ex-Congressman and Interior Secretary, Dies at 90
abstract: Under George H.W. Bush, he often angered environmentalists over the use of federal land as he sought to balance conservation and development.

name: Richard Lugar
profession: G.O.P. Senator and Foreign Policy Force
headline: Richard Lugar, G.O.P. Senator and Foreign Policy Force, Dies at 87
abstract: His most notable accomplishment: helping to create a program to destroy surplus stocks of nuclear weapons around the world.

name: Damon Keith
headline: Damon Keith, Federal Judge Who Championed Civil Rights, Dies at 96
abstract: As a judge, he attacked racial segregation in education, housing and employment, and efforts to limit African-American voting.

name: Monir Farmanfarmaian
profession: Artist Melded Islam and the Abstract
headline: Monir Farmanfarmaian, 96, Dies; Artist Melded Islam and the Abstract
abstract: A Persian sculptor, she was known for abstract compositions of mirrors and glass. In her 10th decade she received a Guggenheim retrospective.

name: Jo Sullivan Loesser
profession: Singer and Guardian of a Legacy
headline: Jo Sullivan Loesser, Singer and Guardian of a Legacy, Dies at 91
abstract: She married the composer Frank Loesser and stopped performing after starring in his “Most Happy Fella.” Resuming her career after he died, she emphasized his music.

name: John Singleton
headline: John Singleton, ‘Boyz N the Hood’ Director, Dies at 51
abstract: His first film, which he began shooting when he was in his early 20s, earned an Oscar nomination for best director — the first for an African-American.

name: H. Johannes Witteveen
headline: H. Johannes Witteveen, 97, Dies; Steered I.M.F. Through Turbulent Era
abstract: As its managing director, he inherited a dispirited International Monetary Fund in 1973 but revived it, in part by tapping into a surge of oil wealth.

name: Mavis Pusey
headline: Mavis Pusey, Under-the-Radar Abstract Artist, Is Dead at 90
abstract: She favored bold geometric forms, especially in works inspired by urban construction and demolition in New York City.

name: Gino Marchetti
headline: Gino Marchetti, Baltimore Colts Defensive Star, Dies at 93
abstract: A member of the Pro Football Hall of Fame, he had a knack for knowing where a play was going and made one of the most famous tackles in N.F.L. history.

name: Martin Kilson
profession: Scholar and Racial Pathbreaker at Harvard
headline: Martin Kilson, Scholar and Racial Pathbreaker at Harvard, Dies at 88
abstract: A leader in African-American studies and a follower of W.E.B. Du Bois, he was the university’s first tenured black professor and a mentor to many.

name: Annie Edson Taylor
profession: Tumbled Down Niagara Falls Into Fame
headline: Overlooked No More: Annie Edson Taylor, Who Tumbled Down Niagara Falls Into Fame
abstract: She was the only person to survive going over Niagara in a barrel, but the glamour that followed was short-lived.

name: Quentin Fiore
headline: Quentin Fiore, Who Made the Medium His Message, Dies at 99
abstract: A graphic designer, he interpreted Marshall McLuhan’s famous phrase in a visual way, amplifying its message.

name: Phil Solomon
headline: Phil Solomon, Leading Experimental Filmmaker, Is Dead at 65
abstract: He subjected found footage to what a colleague called “a chemical and optical alchemy,” creating haunting films that he thought of as a form of painting.

name: Ellen Tauscher
headline: Ellen Tauscher, Congresswoman and Diplomat, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Ms. Tauscher had a career on Wall Street before being elected to the House as a Democrat. She later helped negotiate a nuclear arms treaty.

name: Michael Doyle
headline: Michael Doyle, 78, Surfing Champion of the 1960s, Dies
abstract: Doyle was runner-up at the World Surfing Championships in 1964. “He was one of the standouts,” said PT Townend, another former surfing star.

name: Corinne Cobson
profession: Designer With a Rock n Roll Edge
headline: Corinne Cobson, Designer With a Rock ’n’ Roll Edge, Dies at 62
abstract: Ms. Cobson’s clothes, which gained acclaim in the 1980s and ’90s, were known for their spunk but were also comfortable to wear.

name: Les Murray
headline: Les Murray, Australia’s Unofficial Poet Laureate, Is Dead at 80
abstract: A prolific poet who some said deserved a Nobel Prize, he courted controversy and was always, his biographer said, “on the side of the outcast.”

name: Red Kelly
profession: Gentleman Stalwart in a Run of Stanley Cups
headline: Red Kelly, Gentleman Stalwart in a Run of Stanley Cups, Is Dead at 91
abstract: A fierce but seldom penalized Hall of Famer, he helped capture eight N.H.L. titles — four with the Red Wings and four with the Maple Leafs.

name: Doreen Spooner
headline: Doreen Spooner, Trailblazer on Fleet Street, Dies at 91
abstract: Recognized as the first woman to become a full-time photographer on a British national newspaper, she earned her male colleagues’ respect “just by getting on with my job.”

name: Peter Mayhew
profession: Actor Behind Chewbaccas Mask in Star Wars
headline: Peter Mayhew, Actor Behind Chewbacca’s Mask in ‘Star Wars,’ Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Mayhew played Han Solo’s menacing-seeming yet cuddly sidekick and co-pilot in the original “Star Wars” trilogy and two later films in the franchise.

name: Giuliano Bugialli
headline: Giuliano Bugialli, Champion of Italian Cuisine, Dies at 88
abstract: In his books and his cooking classes, he extolled traditional recipes. His 1977 cookbook, “The Fine Art of Italian Cooking,” is a standard in the field.

name: Rafael Hernández Colón
headline: Rafael Hernández Colón, 82, Ex-Governor of Puerto Rico, Is Dead
abstract: While others called for statehood or independence, Mr. Hernández Colón maintained that commonwealth status was best.

name: Wayson Choy
profession: Books Are Windows on Chinese-Canadian Life
headline: Wayson Choy, 80, Whose Books Are Windows on Chinese-Canadian Life, Dies
abstract: In books like “The Jade Peony,” he was one of the first writers to explore an Asian immigrant experience, discovering his own hidden past along the way.

name: David Winters
headline: David Winters, Energetic Dancer Turned Choreographer, Dies at 80
abstract: Inspired by Jerome Robbins, who cast him in the stage and film versions of “West Side Story,” he went on to create dances for Ann-Margret and others.

name: Ben Heller
headline: Ben Heller, Powerhouse Collector of Abstract Art, Dies at 93
abstract: An early advocate of Abstract Expressionism, Mr. Heller sold or donated many major works. He also wrote about art and advised artists and museums.

name: Rachel Held Evans
headline: Rachel Held Evans, Voice of the Wandering Evangelical, Dies at 37
abstract: Ms. Evans’s spiritual journey and writing fostered a community of believers who challenged conservative Christian groups they felt were exclusionary.

name: Menachem Mendel Taub
headline: Menachem Mendel Taub, Grand Rabbi and Holocaust Survivor, Dies at 96
abstract: A victim of experiments by Dr. Josef Mengele, Rabbi Taub helped reconstitute a community of Hungarian Hasidic Jews in Israel.

name: Terry Allen Kramer
headline: Terry Allen Kramer, Tony-Winning Producer, Is Dead at 85
abstract: She won five Tony Awards as a Broadway producer, but was just as well known as the grande dame of Palm Beach, Fla., socialites.

name: Norma Miller
headline: Norma Miller, Lindy-Hopping ‘Queen of Swing,’ Is Dead at 99
abstract: As a child, she danced the Lindy Hop on Harlem sidewalks before becoming a Savoy Ballroom sensation and an international stage and screen star.

name: Beth Carvalho
headline: Beth Carvalho, Brazil’s ‘Godmother of Samba,’ Is Dead at 72
abstract: A singer with a smoky, rough-edged voice, she championed generations of songwriters and modernized samba without succumbing to pop trends.

name: Jean Vanier
profession: Savior of People on the Margins
headline: Jean Vanier, Savior of People on the Margins, Dies at 90
abstract: His organization, L’Arche, which ministers to people with developmental disabilities, has evolved into a worldwide movement.

name: Nurit Karlin
profession: Found Her Voice in Wordless Cartoons
headline: Nurit Karlin, Who Found Her Voice in Wordless Cartoons, Dies at 80
abstract: Whimsical, thoughtful and caption-less was her style when The New Yorker took her on in 1974. At the time, she was the magazine’s only female cartoonist.

name: Robert Pear
profession: Authoritative Times Reporter on Health Care
headline: Robert Pear, Authoritative Times Reporter on Health Care, Dies at 69
abstract: An understated but tenacious journalist who mastered national issues with in-depth coverage that became a must-read in the capital and beyond.

name: Art Kunkin
headline: Art Kunkin, Counterculture Newspaper Publisher, Dies at 91
abstract: The Los Angeles Free Press, which he founded in 1964, strove to cover stories and communities that mainstream publications ignored.

name: Gloria Schiff
profession: Fashion Editor and Glamorous Twin Model
headline: Gloria Schiff, Fashion Editor and Glamorous Twin Model, Dies at 90
abstract: She and her sister caught the eye of a fashion photographer at 15. She later worked at Harper’s Bazaar and Vogue and became a fixture of New York society.

name: John Lukacs
headline: John Lukacs, Iconoclastic Historian and Author, Dies at 95
abstract: His heroes: Churchill, Orwell and Tocqueville. His targets: Hitler, Stalin, populism, nationalism and the degeneration of morality and truth.

name: Barbara Johns
headline: Overlooked No More: Barbara Johns, Who Defied Segregation in Schools
abstract: At 16, Johns led a strike by the student body that ultimately became one of five court cases consolidated into Brown v. Board of Education.

name: Max Azria
headline: Max Azria, Designer Who Sold Couture for Less, Has Died
abstract: Mr. Azria founded BCBG Max Azria in 1989 to “give fashion to more people.” It became a global concern, and celebrities like Beyoncé wore his clothes.

name: Chuck Kinder
headline: Chuck Kinder, Novelist Who Inspired ‘Wonder Boys,’ Dies at 76
abstract: His struggles to complete a book caught the eye of one of his students, Michael Chabon. Some years later, he finished the book, “Honeymooners.”

name: Chris Albertson
headline: Chris Albertson, Biographer of Bessie Smith, Is Dead at 87
abstract: His “Bessie” was praised as “provocative and enlightening” and shattered many myths. He also produced an acclaimed multivolume reissue of her recordings.

name: Jim Fowler
profession: Naturalist and a Face of TVs Wild Kingdom
headline: Jim Fowler, Naturalist and a Face of TV’s ‘Wild Kingdom,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Fowler and Marlin Perkins formed a long-running duo on the documentary series filmed in the wild and sponsored by Mutual of Omaha.

name: Susan Beschta
headline: Susan Beschta, Punk Rocker Turned Judge, Is Dead at 67
abstract: It was, at first glance, an unlikely journey: A guitarist and vocalist known as Susan Springfield performed at CBGB before turning to human rights law.

name: Verna Hart
profession: Art Expressed the Rhythms of Jazz
headline: Verna Hart, Whose Art Expressed the Rhythms of Jazz, Dies at 58
abstract: Gifted since she was 5, she found inspiration in music improvisation and admirers in Spike Lee, Branford Marsalis and the M.T.A.

name: Hannelore Elsner
headline: Hannelore Elsner, Compelling German Actress, Is Dead at 76
abstract: She played the first female detective at the center of a German television series. On TV and in film, she was a role model for independent modern women.

name: Warren H. Phillips
headline: Warren H. Phillips, Longtime Wall Street Journal Publisher, Dies at 92
abstract: Starting as a $40-a-week proofreader, he rose through the newsroom and corporate ranks, becoming chairman and chief executive of Dow Jones.

name: Michel Roux
headline: Michel Roux, Whose Vodka Success Was Absolut, Is Dead at 78
abstract: With the help of Andy Warhol, Kurt Vonnegut and others, Mr. Roux turned a little-known Swedish brand into the top imported vodka in the United States.

name: Michel Roux
profession: Helped Bring French Cuisine to London
headline: Michel Roux, 78, Dies; Helped Bring French Cuisine to London
abstract: He was appalled by English food, particularly peas. With his brother, he established the first British restaurant to win three Michelin stars.

name: Andrei Kramarevsky
headline: Andrei Kramarevsky, Influential Ballet Teacher, Is Dead at 90
abstract: After a successful dance career in the Soviet Union, he turned up at the School of American Ballet looking for work. He taught there for more than 40 years.

name: Alvin Sargent
headline: Alvin Sargent, Oscar-Winning Hollywood Screenwriter, Dies at 92
abstract: He won an Oscar for his gripping portrayal of breakdowns lurking under the surface of an affluent family in Robert Redford’s 1980 film “Ordinary People,” and for 1977’s “Julia.”

name: Fleming Begaye
profession: Navajo Code Talker Honored at White House
headline: Fleming Begaye, Navajo Code Talker Honored at White House, Dies at 97
abstract: At the 2017 ceremony meant to honor code talkers, President Trump angered many by mocking Senator Elizabeth Warren as “Pocahontas.”

name: Peggy Lipton
profession: Mod Squad and Twin Peaks Actress
headline: Peggy Lipton, ‘Mod Squad’ and ‘Twin Peaks’ Actress, Dies at 72
abstract: Two decades after starring in “The Mod Squad,” winning a Golden Globe for her role, Ms. Lipton recaptured viewers’ attention in “Twin Peaks.”

name: Arthur Zitrin
headline: Dr. Arthur Zitrin, Bioethicist and Death Penalty Foe, Dies at 101
abstract: An authority on bioethics at New York University for decades, Dr. Zitrin sought to discipline physicians who assisted in executions by lethal injection.

name: Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba
headline: Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba, 67, Dies; Helped End Basque Terrorism
abstract: Mr. Rubalcaba, a chemist by training, was a leader of Spain’s Socialist Party and led the effort to dismantle ETA, the violent Basque separatist group.

name: Lenora Lapidus
headline: Lenora Lapidus, A.C.L.U. Advocate for Women’s Rights, Dies at 55
abstract: She was a summer intern at the A.C.L.U.’s Women’s Rights Project and returned as its director, giving her the life “I was dreaming of living.”

name: Doris Day
headline: Doris Day, Movie Star Who Charmed America, Dies at 97
abstract: From the perky girl next door in the 1950s to the woman next door in 1960s sex comedies, Ms. Day was the most popular film actress since Shirley Temple.

name: Goro Shimura
headline: Goro Shimura, 89, Mathematician With Broad Impact, Is Dead
abstract: His insights provided the foundation for the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem and led to tools widely used in modern cryptography.

name: Eva de La O
headline: Eva de La O, Soprano Who Promoted Hispanic Composers, Dies at 88
abstract: She established Musica de Camara, a chamber ensemble, in 1979 to support classical artists and composers and expose new audiences to their works.

name: Jenna Welch
headline: Jenna Welch, Laura Bush’s Mother, Dies at 99
abstract: Her $8,000 loss in the Enron scandal was cited by George W. Bush in distancing himself from campaign contributors in the energy industry.

name: Robert Maxwell
headline: Robert Maxwell, World War II Hero Who Fell on a Grenade, Dies at 98
abstract: Germans had attacked an American headquarters in France when he absorbed the blast, saving lives. Maimed, he was awarded the Medal of Honor.

name: Tim Conway
headline: Tim Conway, Beloved TV Bumbler, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Best known for his long tenure on “The Carol Burnett Show,” Mr. Conway was a leading non-leading man and an enduringly popular clown.

name: Alice M. Rivlin
headline: Alice M. Rivlin, 88, a Leading Government Economist, Is Dead
abstract: She was the founding director of the Congressional Budget Office, budget director under Bill Clinton and vice chairwoman of the Federal Reserve.

name: Bert Cooper
headline: Bert Cooper, Boxer Who Knocked Down Holyfield, Dies at 53
abstract: Cooper fought many of the top boxers of his day but was better known for his losses than for his victories. He also fought a serious drug problem.

name: Harold Lederman
headline: Harold Lederman, Boxing Judge and HBO Personality, Dies at 79
abstract: As HBO Sports’ ringside fight scorer and rules expert, Mr. Lederman exuberantly explained the fine points of fights, usually off camera.

name: Sergei Dorenko
headline: Sergei Dorenko, Maverick Russian Broadcast Journalist, Dies at 59
abstract: A former vocal supporter of Putin, he was also unafraid to challenge the authorities in a career in which he was alternately in and out of favor.

name: Jörg Demus
headline: Jörg Demus, Pianist Known for His Expressivity, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Demus, widely respected for the refinement of his playing, accompanied many of the great singers of his time and championed the four-hand piano literature.

name: Nasrallah Sfeir
headline: Cardinal Nasrallah Sfeir, 98, a Voice for Lebanese Christians, Dies
abstract: Cardinal Sfeir, the Maronite Catholic patriarch, supported a compromise that ended Lebanon’s 15-year civil war but resulted in 15 years of Syrian occupation.

name: Dax Cowart
headline: Dax Cowart, Who Suffered for Patients’ Rights, Dies at 71
abstract: Doctors forced Mr. Cowart to undergo treatment after he was severely burned in an explosion. He spent the rest of his life arguing for patient autonomy.

name: Grace Banker
profession: Hello Girls Decoded Calls in World War I
headline: Overlooked No More: Grace Banker, Whose ‘Hello Girls’ Decoded Calls in World War I
abstract: Though she was on the front lines helping to lead Signal Corps switchboard operators, she was not designated a veteran until after her death.

name: Barbara Marx Hubbard
headline: Barbara Marx Hubbard, 89, Futurist Who Saw ‘Conscious Evolution,’ Dies
abstract: In her writings and lectures, she postulated that the human race was on the brink of an enhanced way of existing and could bring about great things.

name: George L. Kelling
headline: George L. Kelling, a Father of ‘Broken Windows’ Policing, Is Dead at 83
abstract: His seminal 1982 article, with James Q. Wilson, revolutionized law enforcement. It was also misinterpreted and led to “zero tolerance” strategies.

name: Bob Hawke
profession: Led Australia Into a New Era as Prime Minister
headline: Bob Hawke, Who Led Australia Into a New Era as Prime Minister, Dies at 89
abstract: A highly popular prime minister from 1983 to 1991, he was an ally of Presidents Ronald Reagan and George H.W. Bush and revolutionized the Australian economy.

name: Gianni De Michelis
headline: Gianni De Michelis, Italian Politician Tarnished by Scandal, Dies at 78
abstract: He flew high in the 1980s as a top member of the Socialist Party and a celebrated disco dancer. But he was later found guilty of corruption.

name: I.M. Pei
headline: I.M. Pei, Master Architect Whose Buildings Dazzled the World, Dies at 102
abstract: Mr. Pei, a committed modernist, was one of the few architects equally attractive to real estate developers, corporate chieftains and art museum boards.

name: Herman Wouk
profession: Best-Selling Novelist With a Realists Touch
headline: Herman Wouk, Best-Selling Novelist With a Realist’s Touch, Dies at 103
abstract: His critics could be brutal, but he enthralled millions of readers with novels like “The Winds of War,” “The Caine Mutiny” and “Marjorie Morningstar.”

name: Machiko Kyo
profession: Star of Rashomon and Other Films
headline: Machiko Kyo, Star of ‘Rashomon’ and Other Films, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Kyo, whose dedication to her craft left Akira Kurosawa “speechless,” rose to fame during an extraordinarily creative period in Japanese filmmaking.

name: Thomas Nozkowski
headline: Thomas Nozkowski, Painter of Bold (if Small) Abstractions, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Nozkowski rejected the grandiose Abstract Expressionism of his youth and created modest, colorful and self-contained abstract works with his own stamp.

name: Bobbie Raymond
headline: Bobbie Raymond, 80, Visionary on Racially Integrated Housing, Dies
abstract: In Oak Park, bordering Chicago’s West Side, she fought for a fair housing law and helped curb white flight using a strategy that became a model.

name: Unita Blackwell
profession: Rights Crusader and Winner of Historic Election
headline: Unita Blackwell, 86, Dies; Rights Crusader and Winner of Historic Election
abstract: A sharecropper’s daughter, she joined the voter-registration fight before becoming the first black woman elected a mayor in Mississippi.

name: Edwin Drummond
headline: Edwin Drummond, 73, Who Turned Climbing Into Activism, Dies
abstract: A poet as well as a mountaineer, he climbed the Statue of Liberty and Nelson’s Column in London to draw attention to causes.

name: Georgie Anne Geyer
headline: Georgie Anne Geyer, Foreign Correspondent and Columnist, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Geyer, who broke into the business when few women reported from overseas, traveled the world and interviewed Castro and other often elusive leaders.

name: Niki Lauda
headline: Niki Lauda, Formula One Champion Who Pushed Limits, Dies at 70
abstract: While driving Porsches, Ferraris, McLarens and other high-tech torpedoes, Lauda won three world championships and survived a devastating crash.

name: Stanton T. Friedman
headline: Stanton T. Friedman, Scientist Who Tracked U.F.O.s, Dies at 84
abstract: He was a nuclear physicist until reports of Earth visits by space aliens seized his imagination. He never met one, but he believed, gaining renown.

name: Neus Català
headline: Neus Català, Dogged Anti-Fascist and Camp Survivor, Dies at 103
abstract: She fought Franco in Spain and joined the French Resistance against Hitler. She survived two death camps, and told the stories of other survivors.

name: Thomas Silverstein
headline: Thomas Silverstein, Killer and Most Isolated Inmate, Dies at 67
abstract: Convicted of murdering a guard and two fellow prisoners, he had been in solitary confinement since 1983, personifying, to some, cruel and unusual punishment.

name: Nancy Wigginton
profession: First Woman to Read National News on BBC
headline: Nancy Wigginton, First Woman to Read National News on BBC, Dies at 93
abstract: Known on TV as Nan Winton, she presented bulletins for a few months in 1960, when prejudices against female anchors ran deep.

name: Larry J. Hanley
profession: Helped Rid Transit Union of Corruption
headline: Larry J. Hanley, 62, Dies; Helped Rid Transit Union of Corruption
abstract: A former bus driver, he won the presidency of the Amalgamated Transit Union after accusing the incumbent of failing to discipline a local linked to the mob.

name: Louis Osteen
headline: Louis Osteen, Chef Who Championed Southern Food, Dies at 77
abstract: His stylish restaurant helped start the rise of Charleston, S.C., as a culinary destination.

name: Binyavanga Wainaina
headline: Binyavanga Wainaina, Pioneering Voice in African Literature, Dies at 48
abstract: Mr. Wainaina, winner of the Caine Prize for African Writing, came out in 2014, becoming one of the most prominent Africans ever to publicly identify as gay.

name: Debra Hill
headline: Overlooked No More: Debra Hill, Producer Who Parlayed ‘Halloween’ Into a Cult Classic
abstract: Hill rose through Hollywood’s ranks, setting an example as a successful Hollywood producer at a time when there were few women in the industry.

name: Leonard Bailey
profession: Gave a Baby a Baboons Heart
headline: Dr. Leonard Bailey, Who Gave a Baby a Baboon’s Heart, Dies at 76
abstract: The case of Baby Fae, the recipient of Dr. Bailey’s experimental transplant in 1984, generated worldwide headlines — along with criticism, demonstrations and threats.

name: Jake Black
headline: Jake Black, a Composer of the ‘Sopranos’ Theme, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Black was a founder of Alabama 3, whose 1997 song “Woke Up This Morning” provided the memorable soundtrack for the opening of a memorable HBO hit.

name: Karol Modzelewski
headline: Karol Modzelewski, Inspiring Voice of Poland’s Solidarity, Is Dead at 81
abstract: A historian and a leading dissident against a Communist regime, he coined the name of the Solidarity movement and was its first spokesman.

name: Judith Kerr
profession: Beloved Childrens Book Author and Illustrator
headline: Judith Kerr, Beloved Children’s Book Author and Illustrator, Dies at 95
abstract: The author of “The Tiger Who Came to Tea” and many other books, she had fled Nazi Germany with her family before World War II.

name: Sol Yaged
headline: Sol Yaged, a Joyful New York Jazz Mainstay, Is Dead at 96
abstract: A clarinetist solidly in the Benny Goodman mold, Mr. Yaged began performing in the early 1940s and continued to play well into the 21st century.

name: Murray Gell-Mann
profession: Peered at Particles and Saw the Universe
headline: Murray Gell-Mann, Who Peered at Particles and Saw the Universe, Dies at 89
abstract: A Nobel winner, he found hidden patterns in the subatomic matter that forms the universe, evoking James Joyce in calling one kind of particle “quarks.”

name: André Lurton
headline: André Lurton, Vintner of Choice Bordeaux, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Lurton came from a family of chateau owners and managers and specialized in elevating distressed vineyards.

name: June Dobbs Butts
headline: June Dobbs Butts, Sex Therapist Who Preached Frankness, Dies at 90
abstract: By many accounts the first African-American to train with William Masters and Virginia Johnson, she brought their uninhibited view of sex therapy to black patients.

name: Baby Jane Dexter
headline: Baby Jane Dexter, Singer Who Knew Heartbreak, Dies at 72
abstract: A fixture of the New York cabaret scene, she took a long hiatus in the 1980s to deal with depression but, she said, “was able to take my life back through music.”

name: Geneviève Waïte
profession: Star of the Swinging-60s Film Joanna
headline: Geneviève Waïte, 71, Star of the Swinging-’60s Film ‘Joanna,’ Dies
abstract: Her role as a waifish art student who has an interracial affair brought her fame and notoriety. But her time in the spotlight proved to be short.

name: Prem Tinsulanonda
profession: Former Thai Premier and Adviser to King
headline: Prem Tinsulanonda, Former Thai Premier and Adviser to King, Dies at 98
abstract: The prime minister from 1980 to 1988, Mr. Prem survived two coup attempts and weakened the influence of political parties and the military.

name: Bart Starr
headline: Bart Starr, Quarterback Who Led the Packers to Greatness, Dies at 85
abstract: The son of a strict military man, he became the fierce in-the-huddle incarnation of Coach Vince Lombardi.

name: Lutz Bacher
headline: Lutz Bacher, Conceptual Artist Who Hid Much About Herself, Dies at 75
abstract: Her insistent anonymity appeared to be part of career-long strategy to present herself as a Conceptual work.

name: Edmund Morris
headline: Edmund Morris, Reagan Biographer Who Upset Conventions, Dies at 78
abstract: The author of an acclaimed biography of Theodore Roosevelt inserted himself as a fictional narrator in his book on Reagan, a device that some critics scorned.

name: Bill Buckner
profession: All-Star Shadowed by World Series Error
headline: Bill Buckner, All-Star Shadowed by World Series Error, Dies at 69
abstract: A veteran of the Cubs and Dodgers, he was at first base for the Red Sox when Mookie Wilson of the Mets hit a grounder to him. Disaster came next.

name: Robert L. Bernstein
headline: Robert L. Bernstein, Publisher and Champion of Dissent, Dies at 96
abstract: The founder of Human Rights Watch, Mr. Bernstein led Random House when it became the world’s largest publisher of general interest books.

name: Dumiso Dabengwa
headline: Dumiso Dabengwa, a Force in Zimbabwe’s Liberation, Is Dead at 79
abstract: He was feared as the K.G.B.-trained “Black Russian,” but he became a unifying figure among the rival guerrilla armies that had opposed white minority rule.

name: Tony Horwitz
headline: Tony Horwitz Dies at 60; Prize-Winning Journalist and Best-Selling Author
abstract: A Pulitzer Prize winner at The Wall Street Journal, he wrote the best sellers “Blue Latitudes” and “Confederates in the Attic” and seven other books.

name: Roger Hirson
headline: Roger Hirson, Who Wrote the Book for ‘Pippin,’ Dies at 93
abstract: For more than a decade, Mr. Hirson was known for writing for television, but meeting the composer Stephen Schwartz led to the hit musical “Pippin.”

name: Richard P. Matsch
headline: Richard P. Matsch, 88, Judge in Oklahoma Bombing Case, Is Dead
abstract: He presided over two trials stemming from the worst act of domestic terrorism, which killed 168 at a federal building, until the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks.

name: Emma Stebbins
profession: Sculpted an Angel of New York
headline: Overlooked No More: Emma Stebbins, Who Sculpted an Angel of New York
abstract: Though her Angel of the Waters at the Bethesda Fountain in Central Park was initially met with negative reviews, it eventually became all but synonymous with the city.

name: Edward Seaga
profession: Led Jamaica on a Conservative Path
headline: Edward Seaga, Who Led Jamaica on a Conservative Path, Dies at 89
abstract: Promising “deliverance is near” amid economic turmoil, Mr. Seaga ousted Michael Manley to become prime minister and grew close to the U.S. and Britain.

name: Thad Cochran
headline: Thad Cochran, 81, Lawmaker Who Brought Largess to Mississippi, Dies
abstract: In 45 years as a representative and senator, he combined homespun politics and a canny skill at producing billions of dollars for his home state.

name: Claus von Bülow
headline: Claus von Bülow, Society Figure in High-Profile Case, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. von Bülow was cleared of trying to kill his wife, the wealthy heiress Martha von Bülow. The case was one of the most sensational of the 1980s and became a movie.

name: Leon Redbone
headline: Leon Redbone, Idiosyncratic Throwback Singer, Is Dead at 69
abstract: He drew songs from Tin Pan Alley, the Delta blues and other sources. In the late 1970s, he introduced them to the “Saturday Night Live” crowd.

name: Curtis Blake
headline: Curtis Blake, a Founder of the Friendly’s Chain, Dies at 102
abstract: Mr. Blake and his brother, S. Prestley Blake, opened the first Friendly ice cream shop in 1935. With an expanded menu, it grew into an East Coast staple.

name: Virginia Zabriskie
headline: Virginia Zabriskie, 91, Art Dealer Who Promoted the Overlooked, Dies
abstract: Ms. Zabriskie supported legions of painters and sculptors who did not have celebrity status but were vital contributors to American art.

name: Everett Raymond Kinstler
headline: Everett Raymond Kinstler, Prolific Portraitist, Dies at 92
abstract: He painted celebrities and politicians, including several presidents, and has dozens of works in the National Portrait Gallery collection.

name: Marc Okkonen
profession: Baseball Maven of a Sartorial Bent
headline: Marc Okkonen, Baseball Maven of a Sartorial Bent, Dies at 85
abstract: His painstaking research on 20th-century major league uniforms, and his artist’s hand, led to the definitive book on the subject.

name: Frank Lucas
profession: Drug Kingpin Depicted in American Gangster
headline: Frank Lucas Dies at 88; Drug Kingpin Depicted in ‘American Gangster’
abstract: His rise from poverty to riches through a drug-smuggling enterprise was a larger-than-life tale of ambition, organization and ruthless brutality.

name: LaSalle Leffall Jr.
headline: LaSalle Leffall Jr., 89, Dies; Cancer Society’s First Black Leader
abstract: A prominent surgeon and Howard University professor, he promoted awareness of the risks of cancer, particularly among African-Americans.

name: Leah Chase
headline: Leah Chase, 96, Creole Chef Who Fed Presidents and Freedom Riders, Dies
abstract: In New Orleans, Dooky Chase’s was the only upscale restaurant that welcomed African-Americans, and it became a gathering place for civil rights leaders.

name: Leann Birch
profession: Knew How to Get a Child to Eat Peas
headline: Leann Birch, Who Knew How to Get a Child to Eat Peas, Dies at 72
abstract: Her research into childhood nutrition and obesity shed new light on not just what children eat, but also why.

name: Donald M. Fraser
headline: Donald M. Fraser, Lawmaker Who Bared a South Korea Plot, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Fraser, who later served as mayor of Minneapolis, led House hearings that exposed a bribery conspiracy by South Korean intelligence agents and the Rev. Sun Myung Moon.

name: Juliann Bluitt Foster
headline: Juliann Bluitt Foster, Trailblazer in Dentistry, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Just 2 percent of dentists were women when she joined their ranks, and “maybe 2 percent of that 2 percent” were black. She made it her goal to change that.

name: James Ketchum
headline: James Ketchum, Who Conducted LSD Experiments on Soldiers, Dies at 87
abstract: An Army psychiatrist, he spearheaded a Cold War project to test whether recreational drugs could be used in chemical attacks to disable enemy troops.

name: Roky Erickson
headline: Roky Erickson, 71, Revered Figure of Psychedelic Rock, Dies
abstract: He fronted the influential group the 13th Floor Elevators with his scream-inflected vocals, but struggled with mental illness for much of his life.

name: Maryetta Dussourd
profession: Raised Early Alarm on Abusive Priests
headline: Maryetta Dussourd, 74, Dies; Raised Early Alarm on Abusive Priests
abstract: The church initially ignored a mother’s complaints about a pedophile priest. Decades later, she helped force the resignation of Boston’s archbishop.

name: Le Anne Schreiber
headline: Le Anne Schreiber, 73, Dies; a First Among Sports Editors
abstract: She was the first woman to run a major American daily newspaper’s sports section — that of The New York Times. She was later an ombudswoman for ESPN.

name: Ellen Bree Burns
headline: Ellen Bree Burns, Barrier-Breaking Connecticut Judge, Dies at 95
abstract: She was the first woman to serve on the state’s major criminal court. She presided until she was 91.

name: Stanley Tigerman
headline: Stanley Tigerman, Architect of Puckish Postmodernism, Dies at 88
abstract: He departed from the pristine monoliths spawned by followers of Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, challenging the idea that they defined Chicago architecture.

name: Patricia Bath
profession: Took On Blindness and Earned a Patent
headline: Dr. Patricia Bath, 76, Who Took On Blindness and Earned a Patent, Dies
abstract: An ophthalmologist, she was the first black woman doctor to receive a patent, for a technique used in cataract surgery. And she promoted eye care for those in need.

name: Louis Levi Oakes
profession: Last of the Mohawk Code Talkers
headline: Louis Levi Oakes, Last of the Mohawk Code Talkers, Dies at 94
abstract: Native American soldiers like Mr. Oakes helped Allied forces prevail in World War II with an impenetrable code based on indigenous languages.

name: Alan Turing
profession: Condemned Code Breaker and Computer Visionary
headline: Overlooked No More: Alan Turing, Condemned Code Breaker and Computer Visionary
abstract: His ideas led to early versions of modern computing and helped win World War II. Yet he died as a criminal for his homosexuality.

name: Terese Hayden
headline: Terese Hayden, Whose Guide Helped Actors Get Cast, Dies at 98
abstract: A struggling performer herself, she began publishing The Players’ Guide, a compendium of names, photographs, credits and phone numbers, in 1944.

name: Tony Glover
headline: Tony Glover, Master of the Blues Harmonica, Is Dead at 79
abstract: With his fellow blues aficionados John Koerner and Dave Ray, Mr. Glover played an important role in the folk music revival of the 1960s.

name: Patricia Battin
profession: Lightning Rod in a Library War
headline: Patricia Battin, Lightning Rod in a Library War, Dies at 89
abstract: A leading librarian who championed high tech, she dueled with preservationists like Nicholson Baker over how best to protect the written word for posterity.

name: Semyon Rozenfeld
profession: Last Known Survivor of Death Camp Escape
headline: Semyon Rozenfeld, Last Known Survivor of Death Camp Escape, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Rozenfeld escaped the Sobibor camp in Poland in 1943 along with about 300 other prisoners. He was among fewer than 60 who survived the war.

name: Murray Polner
headline: Murray Polner, Antiwar Editor and Author, Is Dead at 91
abstract: An outspoken pacifist, Mr. Polner founded the progressive public affairs journal Present Tense in 1973 and was its only editor until it closed in 1990.

name: Herb Sandler
headline: Herb Sandler, Banker Who Financed ProPublica, Dies at 87
abstract: The investigative journalism group was just one cause backed by Mr. Sandler and his wife, Marion, who built a banking giant and then gave millions away.

name: Lowell North
profession: World Champion Sailor and Innovative Sailmaker
headline: Lowell North, World Champion Sailor and Innovative Sailmaker, Dies at 89
abstract: He won five world sailing championships and an Olympic gold medal. He also founded North Sails, which became the largest sailmaker in the world.

name: John
headline: Dr. John, of Voodoo Beads, Feathers and New Orleans Sound, Dies at 77
abstract: Born Malcolm Rebennack Jr., he was part of a pantheon of New Orleans keyboard wizards that also included Professor Longhair, James Booker and Fats Domino.

name: Rudolf von Ribbentrop
headline: Rudolf von Ribbentrop, Son of Top Nazi Diplomat, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. von Ribbentrop spent nearly six years in combat. His father, Germany’s foreign minister, was hanged as a war criminal.

name: Maida Heatter
profession: Cookbook Writer and the Queen of Cake
headline: Maida Heatter, Cookbook Writer and the ‘Queen of Cake,’ Dies at 102
abstract: Her many cookbooks were full of sinful recipes, not only for cakes but also for cookies, pies, tortes and more.

name: Robert Earle
headline: Robert Earle, 93, Moderator of TV’s ‘College Bowl,’ Is Dead
abstract: In the 1960s he was the man asking tough questions to teams of college students in a fast-paced test of knowledge.

name: Lewis B. Cullman
profession: Patron of the Arts and Education
headline: Lewis B. Cullman, Patron of the Arts and Education, Dies at 100
abstract: Resisting his father’s pleas to join the family tobacco business, Mr. Cullman made a fortune on his own, and, with his wife, proceeded to give it away.

name: Nicky Barnes
headline: Nicky Barnes, ‘Mr. Untouchable’ of Heroin Dealers, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Sentenced to life in prison, he informed on former associates, disappeared into the witness protection program and died in 2012 — a death unnoticed until now.

name: Camille Billops
headline: Camille Billops, Who Filmed Her Mother-Daughter Struggle, Dies at 85
abstract: A sculptor, painter and filmmaker, she gave up her daughter for adoption and documented the reunion they had 20 years later — only to reject her again.

name: Bushwick Bill
headline: Bushwick Bill, Rapper Who Told Harrowing Tales in Geto Boys, Is Dead at 52
abstract: The rapper, who helped inject Southern hip-hop storytelling with vivid horror and morbid comedy, announced he had pancreatic cancer in May.

name: Jiggs Kalra
headline: Jiggs Kalra, Food Writer Who Elevated Indian Fine Dining, Dies at 72
abstract: Through his newspaper columns and cookbooks, Mr. Kalra became a pioneer in Indian food writing and put the spotlight on little known chefs.

name: Joe Overstreet
headline: Joe Overstreet, Painter and Activist, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Like many of his fellow African-American artists, he infused his work with burning political issues of the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Lee Hee-ho
profession: Fought for Women as South Korea First Lady
headline: Lee Hee-ho, Who Fought for Women as South Korea First Lady, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Lee, an early campaigner for women’s rights, also inspired her late husband, President Kim Dae-jung, in his pro-democracy struggle against the country’s military dictatorship.

name: Yannick Bellon
headline: Yannick Bellon, French Director With Feminist Bent, Dies at 95
abstract: “I have treated several aspects of the feminine reality,” Ms. Bellon, whose films included a feature that graphically depicted a gang rape, once said.

name: John Gunther Dean
headline: John Gunther Dean, U.S. Ambassador as Cambodia Fell, Dies at 93
abstract: He was evacuated just before Phnom Penh fell to the Khmer Rouge, clutching the American flag that had flown over the U.S. Embassy.

name: Gabriele Grunewald
headline: Gabriele Grunewald, Runner Who Chronicled Journey With Cancer, Dies at 32
abstract: Grunewald competed in middle distances, reaching the Olympic trials multiple times, despite facing a rare metastatic cancer.

name: Ma Rainey
headline: Overlooked No More: Ma Rainey, the ‘Mother of the Blues’
abstract: With her unapologetic lyrics, Rainey proudly proclaimed her bisexuality and helped to mainstream black female narratives in a musical style that later became a nationwide craze.

name: Velvel Pasternak
headline: Velvel Pasternak, Preserver of Hasidic Music, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Pasternak recorded and transcribed melodies that had historically been passed along by tradition, saving them from possible extinction.

name: Martin Feldstein
headline: Martin Feldstein, 79, a Chief Economist Under Reagan, Dies
abstract: He took a leave from Harvard to be chairman of the Council of Economic Advisers and, as a deficit hawk, never shied from challenging his White House colleagues.

name: Sylvia Miles
profession: Actress With a Flair for the Flamboyant
headline: Sylvia Miles, Actress With a Flair for the Flamboyant, Dies at 94
abstract: She won Oscar nominations for “Midnight Cowboy” and “Farewell, My Lovely” and gossip-column attention for her indefatigable partygoing.

name: Kenneth Forde
headline: Dr. Kenneth Forde, Surgeon Who Fostered Cancer Screening, Dies at 85
abstract: Long the only black faculty member at Columbia’s medical college, he — with Katie Couric — promoted regular colonoscopies, which are now routine.

name: Bill Wittliff
profession: Lonesome Dove Screenwriter and Son of Texas
headline: Bill Wittliff, ‘Lonesome Dove’ Screenwriter and Son of Texas, Dies at 79
abstract: His screenplays displayed an affinity for the mythology and history of his native state, and he and his wife started an archive devoted to Texas writers.

name: Teruko Ishizaka
headline: Dr. Teruko Ishizaka, Who Advanced Allergy Treatment, Dies at 92
abstract: She and her husband identified an antibody that triggers wheezing and rashes. Monitoring it can help prevent and remedy allergic reactions.

name: Henry Lynch
headline: Dr. Henry Lynch, 91, Dies; Found Hereditary Link in Cancer
abstract: To a doubting medical world, he found compelling evidence that some cancers are passed along genetically. His work was ultimately widely embraced.

name: Pat Bowlen
profession: Influential Owner of the Denver Broncos
headline: Pat Bowlen, Influential Owner of the Denver Broncos, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Bowlen, known for his personal flair, had one of the most successful runs of any team owner in American professional sports.

name: Anthony Price
profession: Author of Cold War Spy Thrillers
headline: Anthony Price, Author of Cold War Spy Thrillers, Dies at 90
abstract: His 19-book series featuring an intelligence analyst named David Audley drew comparisons to John le Carré.

name: Keith Botsford
profession: Man of Letters and Saul Bellow Associate
headline: Keith Botsford, Man of Letters and Saul Bellow Associate, Dies at 90
abstract: He was an uncontainable writer (novelist, essayist, biographer and more), started magazines with Bellow and died almost a year ago, to little public notice.

name: Edwin Kosik
profession: Firm Judge in Kids for Cash Case
headline: Edwin Kosik, Firm Judge in ‘Kids for Cash’ Case, Dies at 94
abstract: Judge Kosik gave long prison sentences to two judges charged with accepting kickbacks from a developer of youth detention centers in Pennsylvania.

name: Lil’ Buck Sinegal
headline: Lil’ Buck Sinegal, Noted Louisiana Guitarist, Dies at 75
abstract: He worked with Allen Toussaint, Buckwheat Zydeco, Clifton Chenier and more. He has been called “the best guitar slinger South Louisiana has to offer.”

name: Franco Zeffirelli
profession: Italian Director With Taste for Excess
headline: Franco Zeffirelli, Italian Director With Taste for Excess, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Zeffirelli’s opera productions sometimes drew critical ire, but audiences generally loved them. He worked in film, too.

name: Susannah Hunnewell
headline: Susannah Hunnewell, Publisher of The Paris Review, Dies at 52
abstract: She had been a member of its literary circles since joining it as an intern under its editor George Plimpton.

name: Dale Greig
headline: Dale Greig, Early Women’s Marathoner, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Confounding the notion that long-distance running was too rigorous for women, she finished her first marathon in 1964; 19 of the men in that race didn’t.

name: Alan Brinkley
headline: Alan Brinkley, Leading Historian of 20th-Century America, Dies at 70
abstract: A National Book Award winner, he explored the seminal political events of the last century, including the Depression and World War II.

name: Gloria Vanderbilt
headline: Gloria Vanderbilt Dies at 95; Built a Fashion Empire
abstract: An illustrious family name became synonymous with designer jeans, as Ms. Vanderbilt became a celebrity in her own right.

name: Charles Reich
headline: Charles Reich, Who Saw ‘The Greening of America,’ Dies at 91
abstract: He was a Yale Law School professor when he embraced the counterculture in a 1970 book that became a best seller and brought him rock-star-level fame.

name: Molly O’Neill
headline: Molly O’Neill, Writer Who Explored and Celebrated Food, Is Dead at 66
abstract: She was a keen observer of what she called the “essential tension in the American appetite,” a reflection of the country’s cultural conflicts.

name: Elizabeth Barrett-Connor
headline: Dr. Elizabeth Barrett-Connor, Scrutinizer of Aging, Dies at 84
abstract: Dr. Barrett-Connor founded and led an important long-term study on aging, using both men and women as subjects — an unusual method at the time.

name: William Loverd
headline: William Loverd, Who Promoted Literary Giants, Dies at 78
abstract: He chaperoned the works of dozens of writers at Alfred A. Knopf for almost 40 years. “Bill and Knopf,” a colleague said, “were entirely synonymous.”

name: Peter Whitehead
headline: Peter Whitehead, 82, Swinging-’60s Filmmaker, Is Dead
abstract: He captured the Rolling Stones on tour and both captured and helped define an era with “Tonite Let’s All Make Love in London.”

name: Claude Cahun
headline: Overlooked No More: Claude Cahun, Whose Photographs Explored Gender and Sexuality
abstract: Society generally considered women to be women and men to be men in early-20th-century France. Cahun’s work protested gender and sexual norms, and has become increasingly relevant.

name: Philippe Zdar
headline: Philippe Zdar, Influential French Music Producer, Dies at 52
abstract: A major figure in the electro scene, Mr. Zdar fell out of a window in an accident in Paris on Wednesday night.

name: Gary Burrell
profession: Helped People Find Their Way (With GPS)
headline: Gary Burrell, Who Helped People Find Their Way (With GPS), Dies at 81
abstract: He and Min Kao built the world’s largest maker of consumer navigation devices, relying on the global positioning system for planes, boats and people.

name: Jeanne O’Laughlin
profession: Voice in Cuban Boys Custody Fight
headline: Sister Jeanne O’Laughlin, 90, Voice in Cuban Boy’s Custody Fight, Dies
abstract: She sought to keep Elian Gonzalez from being returned to his father in Cuba after the boy had been rescued at sea off Florida, his mother having drowned.

name: Suzan Pitt
headline: Suzan Pitt, 75, Wildly Inventive Animation Filmmaker, Dies
abstract: Ms. Pitt’s short films were vivid, immersive fantasies influenced by her dreams, underground comics and the cartoons of Max Fleischer.

name: David Esterly
profession: Master Carver Steeped in History and Nature
headline: David Esterly, 75, Master Carver Steeped in History and Nature, Dies
abstract: A self-taught artist’s muse was a 17th-century master woodcarver for the English crown.

name: Michael Jaffee
headline: Michael Jaffee, Who Co-Founded Early-Music Group, Dies at 81
abstract: With his wife, he created the Waverly Consort, which brought medieval and Renaissance music back to life and spurred new interest in the field.

name: Dimitris Christofias
profession: Cyprus President for One Ill-Fated Term
headline: Dimitris Christofias, 72, Cyprus President for One Ill-Fated Term, Dies
abstract: Elected amid hopes he could reunify the divided island, his tenure was marked by financial crisis and a devastating munitions accident.

name: Dave Bartholomew
headline: Dave Bartholomew, Mainstay of New Orleans R&B, Dies at 100
abstract: Mr. Bartholomew, a producer, arranger, composer, trumpet player and bandleader, was best known for his long collaboration with Fats Domino.

name: George Rosenkranz
profession: Developer of the Birth Control Pill
headline: George Rosenkranz, 102, a Developer of the Birth Control Pill, Is Dead
abstract: Dr. Rosenkranz also had a key role in the first practical synthesis of cortisone and was a contract bridge champion whose wife was kidnapped during a tournament.

name: Judith Krantz
profession: Tales of Sex and Shopping Sold Millions
headline: Judith Krantz, Whose Tales of Sex and Shopping Sold Millions, Dies at 91
abstract: She published her first novel at 50, and her heroines were invariably rich, savvy, ambitious and preternaturally beautiful.

name: Elliot Roberts
headline: Elliot Roberts, Manager of Rock Stars, Is Dead at 76
abstract: He guided the careers of Joni Mitchell, David Crosby, Jackson Browne, Tom Petty and Tracy Chapman but was best known for his many years with Neil Young.

name: Robert Therrien
headline: Robert Therrien, Sculptor, Dies at 71; He Made the Mundane Monumental
abstract: Mr. Therrien’s dining room table was the model for his best-known work: a 10-foot-high replica that let viewers see it from below, as a child might.

name: Mitchel Levitas
profession: Editor in Leading Posts at The Times
headline: Mitchel Levitas, Editor in Leading Posts at The Times, Dies at 89
abstract: A Polk Award winner, he edited the Op-Ed page, The Book Review, The Week in Review and also oversaw coverage of the New York area.

name: Joyce Pensato
headline: Joyce Pensato, Who Made Cartoon Characters Complex, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Pensato, who found art-world success relatively late, transformed the likes of Mickey Mouse and Batman into ambiguous and sometimes scary creatures.

name: Jan Meyers
headline: Jan Meyers, a Kansas Republican ‘First’ in Congress, Dies at 90
abstract: The first woman from her party to be elected to the House from her state, Ms. Meyers was a moderate who backed abortion rights and gun control.

name: Charles Ginnever
headline: Charles Ginnever, Sculptor on a Grand Scale, Dies at 87
abstract: His steel geometric forms are in parks and other public spaces all over the United States.

name: Steve Dunleavy
headline: Steve Dunleavy, Brash Face of Murdoch Journalism, Dies at 81
abstract: An Australian with sartorial dash, he was a reporter, columnist, editor and TV correspondent who practiced a feisty brand of tabloid journalism.

name: Philip H. Geier Jr.
headline: Philip H. Geier Jr., Who Built an Advertising Giant, Dies at 84
abstract: Over 20 years as Interpublic’s chief executive, Mr. Geier acquired 200 companies to provide clients with an enormous breadth of services.

name: Robert J. Friend
headline: Robert J. Friend, Tuskegee Pilot Who Led U.F.O. Project, Is Dead at 99
abstract: His death leaves 11 survivors of the all-black Red Tail flying unit in World War II. He studied flying objects with the Air Force’s Project Blue Book.

name: Bill Larson
profession: Became a Symbol of Gay Loss in New Orleans
headline: Overlooked No More: Bill Larson, Who Became a Symbol of Gay Loss in New Orleans
abstract: Larson died in the city’s deadliest fire ever, at a gay bar called the Up Stairs Lounge, but his death — and those of the 31 other victims — was treated with indifference.

name: Brenda Maddox
headline: Brenda Maddox, Biographer Who Revealed Joyce’s Muse, Dies at 87
abstract: Her “Nora” shed new light on the writer’s overlooked wife. A later book did the same for a woman of science.

name: Peter Ball
profession: Anglican Bishop Jailed for Sex Abuse
headline: Peter Ball, Anglican Bishop Jailed for Sex Abuse, Dies at 87
abstract: A protégé of Prince Charles, he was convicted of abusing boys and young men and stood at the center of a case study in impunity within the church.

name: John Shearer
headline: John Shearer, Who Photographed Tumultuous 1960s, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Shearer joined the staff of Look magazine at the age of 20, becoming one of the few black photographers at a major national publication.

name: Jerry Carrigan
headline: Jerry Carrigan, Prolific Studio Drummer, Is Dead at 75
abstract: First in Muscle Shoals, Ala., and then in Nashville, he became known for his fertile imagination and an approach that valued feeling over flash.

name: Min Hogg
headline: Min Hogg, World of Interiors Editor, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Hogg turned a fledgling operation into a respected publication that would become a touchstone in the design world and beyond.

name: Peter Selz
profession: Art Museum Force on Two Coasts
headline: Peter Selz, an Art Museum Force on Two Coasts, Dies at 100
abstract: After fleeing Nazi Germany as a youth, he became a top curator at the Museum of Modern Art, then the founding museum director at Berkeley.

name: Isabel Sarli
profession: Popular Star of Racy Argentine Films
headline: Isabel Sarli, Popular Star of Racy Argentine Films, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Sarli reached international audiences in dozens of movies that were the bane of censors, starting with one in which she appeared fully nude.

name: Barbara Hunt McLanahan
headline: Barbara Hunt McLanahan, Influential Arts Administrator, Dies at 55
abstract: She championed emerging artists and, as executive director of the Children’s Museum of the Arts, sought to make art available to all types of youngsters.

name: Billy Drago
profession: Villain in Movies and on TV
headline: Billy Drago, a Villain in Movies and on TV, Is Dead at 73
abstract: He was memorably Frank Nitti in Brian De Palma’s “The Untouchables” and a lowdown deputy in Clint Eastwood’s “Pale Rider.”

name: Whitney North Seymour Jr.
headline: Whitney North Seymour Jr., Former U.S. Prosecutor Who Fought Corruption, Dies at 95
abstract: He was a patrician Republican who was prominent in New York civic, social and legal circles, the scion of a lawyer who championed unpopular causes.

name: Ken Behring
headline: Ken Behring, Former Seattle Seahawks Owner, Dies at 91
abstract: A real estate developer and philanthropist, he tried unsuccessfully to move the Seahawks to Southern California. He sold the team in 1997.

name: Susan Bernard
profession: Actress and Keeper of a Photographic Legacy
headline: Susan Bernard, 71, Dies; Actress and Keeper of a Photographic Legacy
abstract: The daughter of Bernard of Hollywood, photographer to the stars, she exhibited and marketed his work, notably his images of Marilyn Monroe.

name: David Binder
