profession: Chronicled the Cold War and Its Aftermath
headline: David Binder, 88, Dies; Chronicled the Cold War and Its Aftermath
abstract: Mr. Binder’s thousands of reports for The Times included coverage of the Berlin Wall’s construction in 1961 and its destruction in 1989.

name: Bob Dorian
profession: Genial Guide to Old Films on AMC
headline: Bob Dorian, Genial Guide to Old Films on AMC, Is Dead at 85
abstract: A movie buff since childhood, Mr. Dorian was an actor, a magician and a disc jockey before joining the channel as prime-time host in 1984.

name: Max Wright
profession: Went From Theater Roles to ALF
headline: Max Wright, Who Went From Theater Roles to ‘ALF,’ Dies at 75
abstract: He was best known for playing a suburban father who lives with a furry alien. But he preferred the stage, and he said he had been “hugely eager” for the show to end.

name: Lee Iacocca
headline: Lee Iacocca, Visionary Automaker Who Led Both Ford and Chrysler, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Mr. Iacocca helped create the Ford Mustang, brought out the minivan saved the failing Chrysler Corporation and came to personify the American auto industry.

name: Ralph Lazo
profession: Voluntarily Lived in an Internment Camp
headline: Overlooked No More: Ralph Lazo, Who Voluntarily Lived in an Internment Camp
abstract: About 115,000 Japanese-Americans on the West Coast were incarcerated after Pearl Harbor, and Lazo, who was Mexican-American, joined them in a bold act of solidarity.

name: Gary Duncan
headline: Gary Duncan, San Francisco Psychedelic Rocker, Dies at 72
abstract: A guitarist, singer and songwriter, Mr. Duncan was, a former bandmate said, the “engine” of the group Quicksilver Messenger Service.

name: Arte Johnson
headline: Arte Johnson, ‘Very Interesting’ Comic Actor, Is Dead at 90
abstract: He became a star on “Rowan & Martin’s Laugh-In” playing a range of characters, most notably a German soldier with a memorable catchphrase.

name: Robert Levine
headline: Robert Levine, Who Studied Kindness, Identity and Time, Dies at 73
abstract: His social experiments explored how people around the world spend time, whether kindness varies by city and what compels us to buy things we may not need.

name: Stewart Greene
headline: Stewart Greene, Who Helped Shape TV Advertising, Dies at 91
abstract: In the 1960s, Mr. Greene created ad campaigns that, among other things, made indigestion entertaining and airplanes visually appealing.

name: Spiro Malas
profession: Dependable Bass and a Most Happy Fella
headline: Spiro Malas, Dependable Bass and a ‘Most Happy Fella,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Malas’s resonant voice and sly comic timing served him well in numerous secondary roles. A starring role, and acclaim, came late in his career on Broadway.

name: Ben Barenholtz
headline: Ben Barenholtz, Midnight-Movie Innovator, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Mr. Barenholtz created a cult hit and started a trend in 1970 with late-night showings of the bloody, surreal film “El Topo” at his Manhattan theater.

name: Sid Ramin
profession: West Side Story Orchestrator and a Composer
headline: Sid Ramin, ‘West Side Story’ Orchestrator and a Composer, Dies at 100
abstract: A childhood friend of Leonard Bernstein, he won an Oscar and a Grammy for his work on the film “West Side Story” and 12 Clio Awards for his work in TV advertising.

name: Barry Kowalski
headline: Barry Kowalski, Prosecutor in Rodney King Case, Is Dead at 74
abstract: “He’s been called the Justice Department’s pit bull,” a colleague said of Mr. Kowalski, who prosecuted many high-profile civil rights cases.

name: Paul Benjamin
profession: Corner Man in Do the Right Thing
headline: Paul Benjamin, a ‘Corner Man’ in ‘Do the Right Thing,’ Is Dead
abstract: In a career that lasted almost half a century, he also appeared onscreen opposite Clint Eastwood and other stars and was frequently seen on television.

name: Gene Pingatore
headline: Gene Pingatore, ‘Hoop Dreams’ Documentary Coach, Dies at 82
abstract: He won 1,035 basketball games at St. Joseph High School, near Chicago. But he was best known for his role in an acclaimed documentary.

name: Mickey Kapp
headline: Mickey Kapp, Who Made Mixtapes for Astronauts, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Kapp, a record producer, became the unofficial music provider to the space-bound after forging an unlikely connection with members of the Mercury 7 crew.

name: João Gilberto
headline: João Gilberto, an Architect of Bossa Nova, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Gilberto was the quintessential transmitter of the harmonically and rhythmically complex, lyrically nuanced Brazilian music, including a version of “The Girl From Ipanema.”

name: Marie Ponsot
headline: Marie Ponsot, Poet of Love, Divorce and Family, Dies at 98
abstract: Her poetry — some of it stashed in a drawer for years — was tempered by years of being a single mother and her Roman Catholic faith.

name: Eva Kor
profession: Survivor of Twin Experiments at Auschwitz
headline: Eva Kor, Survivor of Twin Experiments at Auschwitz, Dies at 85
abstract: She lost her parents and two sisters in the death camp. She and her twin, Miriam, were spared so that Dr. Josef Mengele could use them as “human guinea pigs.”

name: Jack Renner
profession: Recording Master and a Founder of Telarc
headline: Jack Renner, Recording Master and a Founder of Telarc, Dies at 84
abstract: At his record label, Mr. Renner created carefully engineered classical and jazz recordings that were beloved by audiophiles.

name: Janne E. Nolan
headline: Janne E. Nolan, Principled Adviser on World Affairs, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Sought out by the White House and the State Department, she stressed the importance of ethics in policymaking and of heeding one’s conscience.

name: Martin Charnin
headline: Martin Charnin, Who Brought ‘Annie’ to the Stage, Dies at 84
abstract: He turned the comic strip “Little Orphan Annie” into a long-running Broadway musical and wrote the memorable lyrics to a score that included “Tomorrow.”

name: Ross Perot
headline: Ross Perot, Brash Texas Billionaire Who Ran for President, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Perot made a fortune in computer services, mounted bizarre paramilitary missions in Asia and was a strong third-party hopeful in the 1990s.

name: Vivian Perlis
headline: Vivian Perlis, Oral Historian of American Music, Dies at 91
abstract: She was the founding director of a Yale project that preserved the voices of Duke Ellington, Aaron Copland and many more. It has been called “incomparable.”

name: Michael Colgrass
headline: Michael Colgrass, Composer Who Transcended Genres, Dies at 87
abstract: A Pulitzer Prize winner, he refused to align himself with any new-music style, drawing on jazz, world music and even bird calls.

name: Rip Torn
headline: Rip Torn, an Outsize Presence Onstage and Off, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Torn won an Emmy for “The Larry Sanders Show” and acclaim for his theater work. But he was dogged by his reputation as a troublemaker.

name: Valentina Cortese
headline: Valentina Cortese, a Leading Italian Film Actress, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Cortese, who starred in over 50 films, was perhaps best known for her role as a fading, tippling movie diva in François Truffaut’s “Day for Night.”

name: Else Ury
headline: Overlooked No More: Else Ury’s Stories Survived World War II. She Did Not.
abstract: Ury’s books about a German girl were so beloved, readers clung to them through the upheaval of World War II and passed them on to their children. But few knew that the author had died at Auschwitz.

name: Philip Freelon
headline: Philip Freelon, African-American Museum Architect, Dies at 66
abstract: He worked on numerous museums, libraries and other cultural projects, many of them devoted to the black experience.

name: Jim Bouton
profession: Author of Tell-All Baseball Memoir Ball Four
headline: Jim Bouton, Author of Tell-All Baseball Memoir ‘Ball Four,’ Dies at 80
abstract: A pitcher who had modest success with the Yankees in the 1960s, Bouton revealed the seamier side of baseball in a book that was a best seller.

name: Francine Shapiro
headline: Francine Shapiro, Developer of Eye-Movement Therapy, Dies at 71
abstract: Dr. Shapiro’s technique for dealing with trauma was initially met with some skepticism. But it has attracted devotees worldwide.

name: Andrew Dibner
headline: Andrew Dibner, Medical Alert Pioneer, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Concerned about what happens when people fall and can’t reach a telephone to call an ambulance, Mr. Dibner, a psychologist, developed a system to help.

name: David Koloane
profession: Art Was a Weapon Against Apartheid
headline: David Koloane, Whose Art Was a Weapon Against Apartheid, Dies at 81
abstract: At a time when black South African artists were banned from art schools and museums, his art fused abstraction with polemical themes.

name: Colin Palmer
headline: Colin Palmer, Historian of the African Diaspora, Is Dead at 75
abstract: He emphasized that diaspora meant more than just the American slave trade. It began in prehistoric times, he said, and continues to this day.

name: Walt Michaels
headline: Walt Michaels, Outspoken Coach of the Jets, Is Dead at 89
abstract: An old-school, temperamental coach whose players feared and respected him, he led the Jets to the 1982 American Football Conference championship.

name: Elka Gilmore
headline: Elka Gilmore, Chef Who Blended the Old and the New, Dies at 59
abstract: “I don’t really know what ‘fusion’ means,” she said, but at restaurants in California and New York she displayed a knack for combining flavors.

name: Jerry Lawson
headline: Jerry Lawson, Lead Singer of the Persuasions, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Mr. Lawson and his colleagues revived the lost art of a cappella singing and attracted a loyal following that included Joni Mitchell and Frank Zappa.

name: Fernando Corbató
profession: Father of Your Computer (and Your Password)
headline: Fernando Corbató, a Father of Your Computer (and Your Password), Dies at 93
abstract: In a breakthrough in the 1960s, he showed that computers could be used interactively with quick results, and also made secure from others’ using them.

name: Fernando de la Rúa
headline: Fernando de la Rúa, Ill-Fated President of Argentina, Dies at 81
abstract: He was elected easily in 1999. But he resigned two years later amid a spectacular economic collapse, leaving the presidential palace by helicopter.

name: Hector Figueroa
headline: Hector Figueroa, Union Leader With Impact, Dies at 57
abstract: As head of New York’s Service Employees union, he successfully campaigned for better pay and working conditions for more than 170,000 people.

name: Alex Navab
headline: Alex Navab, Prominent Wall Street Dealmaker, Is Dead at 53
abstract: He was once considered to be in line to run the private equity giant KKR and had recently started his own ambitious firm.

name: Douglas Crimp
headline: Douglas Crimp, Scholar, Curator and Art World Disrupter, Dies at 74
abstract: He insisted on viewing art through a social prism as he moved in two cultures, the alternative-art world and the Lower Manhattan gay community.

name: Michael Seidenberg
headline: Michael Seidenberg, Who Ran a Not-So-Secret Bookstore, Dies at 64
abstract: Those who knew where to look on East 84th Street could find an apartment stuffed with literature and a literary salon to go with it.

name: Pernell Whitaker
headline: Pernell Whitaker, Champion in Four Boxing Classes, Dies at 55
abstract: A defensive master, Whitaker “could stand in front of you and you couldn’t find him,” one boxing announcer said. He died after being struck by a car in Virginia.

name: Steve Cannon
profession: Townhouse Was an East Village Salon
headline: Steve Cannon, Whose Townhouse Was an East Village Salon, Dies at 84
abstract: A writer and publisher who had lost his sight, he opened his door to a revolving cast of painters, poets, musicians and others for meandering conversation.

name: Jerry Seltzer
profession: Revived Roller Derby, Elbows and All
headline: Jerry Seltzer Dies at 87; Revived Roller Derby, Elbows and All
abstract: His father invented a sport in which roller-skating players muscle and shove one another on a banked track. He used television to expand its audience.

name: E. Katherine Kerr
headline: E. Katherine Kerr, Actress and Playwright, Is Dead at 82
abstract: She appeared onscreen with Meryl Streep, won an award for her Off Broadway work, and later distinguished herself as a writer and a teacher.

name: Johnny Clegg
headline: Johnny Clegg, South African Singer Who Battled Apartheid With Music, Is Dead at 66
abstract: With the bands Juluka and Savuka and as a solo artist, Mr. Clegg fused Western and African cultural influences and defied racial separation.

name: William Dannemeyer
headline: William Dannemeyer, 89, California Archconservative, Dies
abstract: A seven-term Orange County congressman, he favored curbs on people with AIDS and laws against sodomy and opposed abortion rights and environmentalists.

name: John Paul Stevens
headline: Supreme Court Justice John Paul Stevens, Who Led Liberal Wing, Dies at 99
abstract: On the Supreme Court, John Paul Stevens transformed from a Republican antitrust lawyer into the leader of the court’s liberal wing.

name: Andrea Camilleri
headline: Andrea Camilleri, Author of Inspector Montalbano Novels, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Camilleri was a late-blooming novelist whose series about a Sicilian police officer became wildly popular in Italy and the basis for a television series.

name: Lucette Lagnado
profession: Memoirist of Jews in Old Cairo
headline: Lucette Lagnado, Memoirist of Jews in Old Cairo, Dies at 62
abstract: She and her family, whom she later wrote about, were among the last Jews to flee what she called a “cultural holocaust” and ended up in Brooklyn in the early 1960s.

name: Alan Rogan
headline: Alan Rogan, Keeper of Rock Guitars, Smashed Ones Included, Dies at 68
abstract: Of all his clients — the Rolling Stones, Eric Clapton and Paul McCartney among them — Pete Townshend of the Who posed the biggest challenge: repairing what he deliberately wrecked.

name: Maty Ezraty
profession: Yoga Methods Have Had Global Reach
headline: Maty Ezraty, Whose Yoga Methods Have Had Global Reach, Dies at 55
abstract: If you’ve ever taken a yoga class in the United States, the chances are you were influenced by Ms. Ezraty’s techniques.

name: Florence Merriam Bailey
headline: Overlooked No More: Florence Merriam Bailey, Who Defined Modern Bird-Watching
abstract: Her pioneering approach involved quietly examining birds in their natural habitat, rather than shooting them, as people had previously done.

name: Pumpsie Green
profession: First Black Player for Boston Red Sox
headline: Pumpsie Green, First Black Player for Boston Red Sox, Dies at 85
abstract: Green, who played mostly at second base and shortstop, broke the color barrier for the last major league franchise that had remained all white.

name: Mitchell Feigenbaum
headline: Mitchell Feigenbaum, Physicist, Dies at 74; He Made Sense of Chaos
abstract: His discovery of what seemed at first a mathematical curiosity led to what is known as the Feigenbaum constant, a pattern of chaos found in nature.

name: Mortimer Caplin
headline: Mortimer Caplin, Tactful but Tough Tax Collector, Dies at 103
abstract: As I.R.S. commissioner in the Kennedy administration, Mr. Caplin promised to be “both reasonable and vigorous” and largely succeeded.

name: Aaron Rosand
profession: Renowned Violinist With a Famous Fiddle
headline: Aaron Rosand, Renowned Violinist With a Famous Fiddle, Dies at 92
abstract: For decades he played a 1741 instrument. Then he sold it and gave $1.5 million of the proceeds to his alma mater.

name: John Tanton
headline: Dr. John Tanton, Quiet Catalyst in Anti-Immigration Drive, Dies at 85
abstract: A small-town eye doctor, he founded and fostered advocacy groups whose warnings on demographic change have reached the Trump White House.

name: L. Bruce Laingen
headline: L. Bruce Laingen, Senior Hostage During Iran Crisis, Dies at 96
abstract: A career diplomat, he had only recently arrived in Tehran for a temporary diplomatic posting when the embassy was seized in 1979.

name: Arthur Ryan
profession: Founded the Low-Cost Fashion Chain Primark
headline: Arthur Ryan, Who Founded the Low-Cost Fashion Chain Primark, Dies at 83
abstract: By keeping costs down and prices affordable, Mr. Ryan grew the company from one store in Dublin into an international retail behemoth.

name: Ida Wyman
headline: Ida Wyman, Whose Camera Captured Ordinary People, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Wyman photographed for Life, Business Week and her own enjoyment, satisfying “an immense curiosity to learn and understand the lives of others.”

name: Marylou Whitney
profession: Social Queen of the Racing World
headline: Marylou Whitney, Social Queen of the Racing World, Dies at 93
abstract: A fixture in Saratoga and Lexington, she was a prominent hostess, a patron of the arts and, not least, a sportswoman and a thoroughbred breeder.

name: Angus McQueen
headline: Angus McQueen, the N.R.A.’s Image Maker, Dies at 74
abstract: He was a principal architect of the N.R.A.’s modern image, until an astonishing legal battle between his firm and the gun group broke out.

name: Cesar Pelli
profession: Designer of Iconic Buildings Around the World
headline: Cesar Pelli, Designer of Iconic Buildings Around the World, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Pelli, whose many distinctive projects include the Petronas Twin Towers in Malaysia, tried to reconcile modernism with his interest in shape, texture and the architecture of the past.

name: Hugh Southern
headline: Hugh Southern, a Creator of the TKTS Booth, Dies at 87
abstract: He held high-profile positions at the Metropolitan Opera and the National Endowment for the Arts, battling critics who wanted to abolish the agency.

name: Russell Smith
profession: Amazing Rhythm Aces Singer and Songwriter
headline: Russell Smith, Amazing Rhythm Aces Singer and Songwriter, Dies at 70
abstract: His most enduring composition was “Third Rate Romance,” a Top 20 pop and country hit that was later recorded by Rosanne Cash, Elvis Costello and others.

name: Paul Krassner
headline: Paul Krassner, Anarchist, Prankster and a Yippies Founder, Dies at 87
abstract: His circle included Abbie Hoffman and Jerry Rubin. When People magazine called him the “father of the underground press” — he founded The Realist — he demanded a paternity test.

name: Robert Morgenthau
headline: Robert Morgenthau, Longtime Manhattan District Attorney, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Morgenthau was the bane of mobsters and crooked politicians and a confidant of mayors and governors, who came and went while he stayed on for decades.

name: Yukiya Amano
profession: Head of the I.A.E.A. Nuclear Watchdog Group
headline: Yukiya Amano, Head of the I.A.E.A. Nuclear Watchdog Group, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Amano led the agency for nearly a decade, including a critical period during which it monitored Iran’s nuclear activities under a deal signed in 2015.

name: Leon Kossoff
headline: Leon Kossoff, 92, Who Painted Portraits of Urban Life, Dies
abstract: His primary subjects were his family and friends, the many glories of London, and old master paintings in the National Gallery.

name: George Hodgman
profession: Wrote Best Seller on Caring for His Mother
headline: George Hodgman, 60, Dies; Wrote Best Seller on Caring for His Mother
abstract: He was a leading magazine and book editor who found his own measure of fame with “Bettyville,” in which he also delved into growing up gay in a small town.

name: Christopher Kraft
headline: Christopher Kraft, NASA Mission Control’s Founding Father, Dies at 95
abstract: He directed the first piloted orbital flights, orchestrated spacewalks, oversaw the first lunar landing and led the space center in Houston.

name: Li Peng
profession: Chinese Leader Derided for Role in Tiananmen Crackdown
headline: Li Peng, Chinese Leader Derided for Role in Tiananmen Crackdown, Dies at 90
abstract: For decades, critics called for Mr. Li, who became known as the “butcher of Beijing,” to face trial or a public reckoning for his role in the 1989 bloodshed.

name: David Hedison
headline: David Hedison, Actor Who Found Fame in a Submarine, Dies at 92
abstract: The science fiction TV series “Voyage to the Bottom of the Sea” made him a star. His résumé also included two James Bond movies and “The Fly.”

name: Joel Filártiga
profession: Won Human Rights Ruling in Sons Death
headline: Dr. Joel Filártiga, 86, Dies; Won Human Rights Ruling in Son’s Death
abstract: After the brutal death of his teenage son in Paraguay, he won a landmark case in the United States that extended universal law against torture.

name: Francesco Saverio Borrelli
headline: Francesco Saverio Borrelli, Scourge of Italy’s Corrupt, Dies at 89
abstract: With 1,281 convictions, his landmark investigation, popularly known as Clean Hands, swept away the ruling class and helped transform Italian politics.

name: Art Neville
headline: Art Neville, a New Orleans Funk Fixture, Is Dead at 81
abstract: In the Neville Brothers and other groups, most notably the Meters, he was an influential musical force for decades.

name: Edith Irby Jones
headline: Edith Irby Jones, Barrier-Breaking Doctor in the South, Dies at 91
abstract: Watching her sister die of typhoid inspired her to become a doctor focused on treating poor people. She blazed a trail along the way.

name: Daniel Callahan
headline: Daniel Callahan, 88, Dies; Bioethics Pioneer Weighed ‘Human Finitude’
abstract: At the Hastings Center, which he co-founded, he explored ethical issues raised by medical advances and questioned the wisdom of prolonging life.

name: Gertrude Benham
profession: Climbed the World One Mountain at a Time
headline: Overlooked No More: Gertrude Benham, Who Climbed the World One Mountain at a Time
abstract: Benham climbed more than 300 peaks in her lifetime to satisfy a “spirit of wanderlust that has entered my soul.”

name: Julia Farron
headline: Julia Farron, Acclaimed Ballerina From Age 14, Is Dead at 96
abstract: Over four decades with the Royal Ballet, she created roles for a host of eminent choreographers. She then shaped notable careers as a teacher.

name: Rutger Hauer
headline: Rutger Hauer, Memorable Antagonist in ‘Blade Runner,’ Dies at 75
abstract: He enjoyed “the freedom you have as a bad guy,” which he was in scores of movie and television shows. But he branched out as his career advanced.

name: Béji Caïd Essebsi
headline: Béji Caïd Essebsi, President Who Guided Tunisia to Democracy, Dies at 92
abstract: In office at his death, he came out of retirement to lead his country after an Arab Spring uprising ousted a dictator, then won a free election.

name: Mark Kleiman
profession: Fought to Lift Ban on Marijuana
headline: Mark Kleiman, Who Fought to Lift Ban on Marijuana, Dies at 68
abstract: A sought-after drug policy expert, and often a maverick, he favored decriminalizing pot but remained wary of full-scale commercial legalization.

name: P. Rajagopal
headline: P. Rajagopal, Restaurant Mogul Convicted of Murder, Dies at 71
abstract: His restaurant chain, Saravana Bhavan, known for tasty vegetarian food at low prices, continued to expand into more than 20 countries even after his conviction.

name: Yao Li
headline: Yao Li, ‘Silver Voice’ of Shanghai, Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Yao was a celebrated singer in Shanghai and Hong Kong starting in the 1930s. One of her songs appeared on the soundtrack of the film “Crazy Rich Asians.”

name: Ben Johnston
headline: Ben Johnston, Who Made Microtonal Music Melodic, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Johnston’s compositions had complex theoretical underpinnings but were also, a former student said, “grounded in the real world.”

name: Lois Wille
profession: Twice a Pulitzer Winner in Her Beloved Chicago
headline: Lois Wille, Twice a Pulitzer Winner in Her Beloved Chicago, Dies at 87
abstract: A hard-hitting reporter, she won two of the prizes, one for a series on how poor women were denied birth control and a second for editorial writing.

name: Jaime Ortega
headline: Cardinal Jaime Ortega, a Cuban Bridge to the U.S., Dies at 82
abstract: He was a go-between for Pope Francis and Presidents Obama and Raúl Castro as they thawed Cold War relations between the two countries.

name: M. Owen Lee
headline: M. Owen Lee (Father Lee to His Met Opera Radio Fans) Dies at 89
abstract: A Roman Catholic priest whose avocation for 23 years was offering commentaries and quiz answers in broadcasts during intermissions.

name: Ben Kinchlow
headline: Rev. Ben Kinchlow, Co-Host of TV’s ‘The 700 Club,’ Dies at 82
abstract: A self-described reprobate turned evangelical minister, he found a global congregation beside Pat Robertson on the Christian Broadcasting Network.

name: Bryan Magee
headline: Bryan Magee, Who Brought Philosophy to British TV, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Magee was a philosopher, writer and politician who challenged the idea that television could not “make serious demands on viewers.”

name: Russi Taylor
profession: Voice of Minnie Mouse and Simpsons Characters
headline: Russi Taylor, the Voice of Minnie Mouse and ‘Simpsons’ Characters, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Taylor had done work for numerous animated series and also voiced Donald Duck’s nephews, Huey, Dewey and Louie.

name: Harlan Lane
headline: Harlan Lane, Vigorous Advocate for Deaf Culture, Dies at 82
abstract: Dr. Lane saw the deaf as part of a distinct ethnic group with their own vibrant culture, and he opposed the use of cochlear implants for deaf children.

name: Arthur McGee
headline: Arthur McGee, Fashion Designer Who Broke Racial Barrier, Dies at 86
abstract: Thought to be the first black designer to run a Seventh Avenue design room, he worked ancient influences into contemporary styles.

name: Keith Lincoln
profession: San Diego Chargers Star in the A.F.L
headline: Keith Lincoln, San Diego Chargers Star in the A.F.L., Dies at 80
abstract: In a stunning performance, Lincoln accounted for 349 yards as a runner, receiver and passer in the team’s only championship victory in its history.

name: Neil Estern
headline: Neil Estern, Sculptor of Monumental Public Works, Is Dead at 93
abstract: With his renderings of Franklin and Eleanor Roosevelt, Fiorello La Guardia, John F. Kennedy and others, he strove for realism (as he once did with a doll).

name: Paul F. Markham
headline: Paul F. Markham, 89, Kennedy Friend at Chappaquiddick, Dies
abstract: He had recently stepped down as a United States attorney when he dived into the water to try to find Mary Jo Kopechne, who had been riding in Mr. Kennedy’s car.

name: Agnes Heller
headline: Agnes Heller, 90, Hungarian Philosopher and Outspoken Dissident, Is Dead
abstract: Since the 1950s, she had been a thorn in the side of authoritarian governments on the left and the right, including Viktor Orban’s today.

name: Hal Prince
profession: Giant of Broadway and Reaper of Tonys
headline: Hal Prince, Giant of Broadway and Reaper of Tonys, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Prince helped bring to life a stunning lineup of shows: “Cabaret,” “Sweeney Todd,” and Broadway’s longest-running spectacle, “The Phantom of the Opera.”

name: Ras G
profession: Hip-Hop Producer and Force in L.A. Music Scene
headline: Ras G, 40, Hip-Hop Producer and Force in L.A. Music Scene, Dies
abstract: The experimental, kaleidoscopic beats he made and called “ghetto sci-fi” channeled a wide spectrum of black musical history.

name: Nick Buoniconti
headline: Nick Buoniconti, 78, Dies; All-Pro Linebacker Championed Medical Research
abstract: He won two Super Bowls with the Dolphins and later fought to find a cure for his son’s paralysis. Struggling with dementia, he donated his brain to science.

name: Georgia Gilmore
profession: Fed and Funded the Montgomery Bus Boycott
headline: Overlooked No More: Georgia Gilmore, Who Fed and Funded the Montgomery Bus Boycott
abstract: Gilmore started the Club From Nowhere, a clandestine group that prepared and sold meals to raise money for the 381-day resistance action.

name: Dorothy Toy
headline: Dorothy Toy, 102, Half of Asian-American Dance Team, Dies
abstract: Beginning in the 1930s, she and Paul Wing lit up stages, until war intervened.

name: Mario Gonzalez
headline: Mario Gonzalez, Father of Golf in Brazil, Is Dead at 96
abstract: A master teacher, he was content to stay in Brazil. “If he had played more on the PGA Tour,” one golfer said, “I am sure he would be in the Hall of Fame.”

name: Corbin Gwaltney
headline: Corbin Gwaltney, Chronicle of Higher Education Founder, Dies at 97
abstract: He saw a void in the 1950s and filled it with coverage of colleges and universities. Today the publication reaches a wide readership online and in print.

name: Martin Mayer
profession: Prolific and Protean Author and Critic
headline: Martin Mayer, Prolific and Protean Author and Critic, Dies at 91
abstract: In dozens of books and a torrent of articles, writing into the wee hours, he demystified lawyers, banking, advertising, builders, classical music and much more.

name: Vivian Paley
headline: Vivian Paley, Educator Who Promoted Storytelling, Dies at 90
abstract: Her methods helped children “join a complex and diverse social world,” a colleague said, but they met resistance from advocates of standardized testing.

name: Richard Rosenbaum
headline: Richard Rosenbaum, 88, Loyal Rockefeller Republican, Is Dead
abstract: As the New York State G.O.P. chairman, he was vital in persuading the Ford administration to enlist the former New York governor as vice president.

name: Carlos Cruz-Diez
headline: Carlos Cruz-Diez, Whose Art Made Color Move, Is Dead at 95
abstract: One of Latin America’s greatest postwar artists, he wanted shifting and shimmering color to be experienced as intensely as cold or heat.

name: Phil Hymes
headline: Phil Hymes, Who Lit ‘Saturday Night Live,‘ Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Hymes was a lighting director and designer at “Saturday Night Live” for over 40 years and was known as a gruff and outsize character behind the scenes.

name: D.A. Pennebaker
profession: Pioneer of Cinéma Vérité in America
headline: D.A. Pennebaker, Pioneer of Cinéma Vérité in America, Dies at 94
abstract: With films that observed political and pop cultural figures — including, notably, Bob Dylan — Mr. Pennebaker “invented nothing less than the modern documentary.”

name: Nuon Chea
headline: Nuon Chea, Khmer Rouge’s Chief Ideologist, Dies at 93
abstract: Pol Pot’s deputy, who was known as Brother No. 2, was convicted of directly overseeing the torture and killing of more than 14,000 people in a Cambodian prison.

name: Arthur Lazarus Jr.
headline: Arthur Lazarus Jr., Champion of Native American Rights, Dies at 92
abstract: He won a landmark victory for the Sioux Nation after 57 years of litigation, believed to be the longest court case in U.S. history.

name: Cliff Branch
headline: Cliff Branch, Raiders’ Elusive All-Pro Receiver, Dies at 71
abstract: One of the N.F.L.’s fastest players, he made defenses “afraid that he’d blow by them,” a former teammate said, “and, ultimately, he would blow by them.”

name: Toni Morrison
profession: Towering Novelist of the Black Experience
headline: Toni Morrison, Towering Novelist of the Black Experience, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Morrison, who wrote “Beloved” and “Song of Solomon,” was the first African-American woman to win the Nobel in literature.

name: Harley Race
profession: Wrestler Known as King of the Ring
headline: Harley Race, Wrestler Known as ‘King of the Ring,’ Dies at 76
abstract: He was old-school tough but knew how to create a character. “What you create in your mind is what makes people get behind you or go against you,” he said.

name: Morton Bahr
profession: Led Communications Workers Into Digital Age
headline: Morton Bahr, 93, Dies; Led Communications Workers Into Digital Age
abstract: As head of the C.W.A. for 20 years, he helped workers survive technological changes and corporate revamping that threatened thousands of jobs.

name: Marisa Merz
profession: Bold Explorer When Art Was a Mans World
headline: Marisa Merz, Bold Explorer When Art Was a Man’s World, Dies at 93
abstract: She was the lone and often overshadowed woman among the central figures of the avant-garde movement in Italy known as Arte Povera. But her day did come.

name: Harvey Frommer
profession: Historian of Sports and New York
headline: Harvey Frommer, Historian of Sports and New York, Dies at 83
abstract: He wrote prolifically, with a focus on the Yankees, while teaching at Dartmouth and collaborating with his wife on New York oral histories.

name: J. Robert Schrieffer
profession: Nobel Winner Inspired on the Subway
headline: J. Robert Schrieffer, 88, Nobel Winner Inspired on the Subway, Dies
abstract: He came up with the last piece of a puzzle to explain how some materials can convey electricity without resistance. It came to him on the subway.

name: William Byron Rumford
headline: Overlooked No More: William Byron Rumford, a Civil Rights Champion in California
abstract: As the first black person elected to the California Legislature from the Bay Area, Rumford was at the forefront of the struggle to desegregate the promise and opportunity of the West Coast.

name: Steve Sawyer
headline: Steve Sawyer, Greenpeace Activist and Leader, Dies at 63
abstract: He was there when the ship the Rainbow Warrior was bombed in an antinuclear protest and helped evacuate an atoll contaminated by radioactive fallout.

name: Thomas S. Gulotta
headline: Thomas S. Gulotta, 75, Republican Who Led Nassau County, Dies
abstract: He was a popular hands-on public servant until a fiscal crisis cost him his job and pried loose his party’s grip on one of the nation’s wealthiest counties.

name: David Berman
profession: Silver Jews Leader and Indie-Rock Poet
headline: David Berman, Silver Jews Leader and Indie-Rock Poet, Dies at 52
abstract: With wry songs full of black humor, his band became an underground favorite in the 1990s, and a new group, Purple Mountains, was set to tour.

name: Anner Bylsma
profession: Eminent Cellist With an Ear for the Past
headline: Anner Bylsma, Eminent Cellist With an Ear for the Past, Dies at 85
abstract: He was a key part of the early music movement, which uses period techniques and instruments. His recordings of six Bach suites for cello were seminal.

name: Rosie Ruiz
headline: Rosie Ruiz, Who Faked Victory in Boston Marathon, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Ruiz “won” the 1980 Boston Marathon after bursting through the crowd about a mile from the finish line. She was later disqualified.

name: Sushma Swaraj
profession: Popular Indian Minister and Modi Ally
headline: Sushma Swaraj, 67, Popular Indian Minister and Modi Ally, Dies
abstract: Ms. Swaraj, a right-wing politician and the second woman to serve as India’s external affairs minister, was known for her good-humored social media presence.

name: Dorothy Olsen
profession: Pioneering Pilot in World War II
headline: Dorothy Olsen, a Pioneering Pilot in World War II, Dies at 103
abstract: She was one of 38 surviving members of the WASPs, who freed men for combat duty by ferrying military planes to domestic embarkation points.

name: Bob Wilber
headline: Bob Wilber, Champion of Jazz’s Legacy, Is Dead at 91
abstract: He was a devoted disciple of the pioneering New Orleans soprano saxophonist and clarinetist Sidney Bechet. But he developed his own take on Bechet’s style.

name: Sherm Poppen
headline: Sherm Poppen, a Dad Who Fathered the Snowboard, Dies at 89
abstract: He was trying to entertain his daughters on a snowy Christmas Day in Michigan when he invented his Snurfer, a prototype of the modern snowboard.

name: Ann Snitow
headline: Ann Snitow, Feminist Teacher and Activist, Dies at 76
abstract: Neither a polemicist nor an ideologue, she thrived on complexities generated by doubt and uncertainty.

name: Lee Bennett Hopkins
headline: Lee Bennett Hopkins, Champion of Poetry for Children, Dies at 81
abstract: In the scores of anthologies he compiled and in his own writing, he sought to teach and expand young imaginations through verse.

name: Henri Belolo
headline: Henri Belolo, a Founder of the Village People, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Belolo and his business partner, Jacques Morali, assembled a colorful group of singers dressed as macho archetypes and created a disco phenomenon.

name: Carl Weiss Jr.
profession: His Father, He Said, Didnt Kill Huey Long
headline: Dr. Carl Weiss Jr., 84, Dies; His Father, He Said, Didn’t Kill Huey Long
abstract: Doubting the official account — that Carl Sr. had killed the Louisiana senator before being gunned down himself — a son sought to clear his father’s name.

name: John Hansen
headline: Dr. John Hansen, Who Made Marrow Transplants Safer, Dies at 76
abstract: His research expanded the pool of donors whose bone marrow was less likely to be rejected by patients with leukemia and other blood disorders.

name: Paul Findley
headline: Paul Findley, Congressman Behind War Powers Act, Dies at 98
abstract: The main author of the resolution that limited a president’s ability to wage war, he also made overtures to the Arab world and earned the opposition of the pro-Israel lobby.

name: Paco Navarro
profession: Seductive Voice of Disco on New York Radio
headline: Paco Navarro, 82, Seductive Voice of Disco on New York Radio, Dies
abstract: He became one of the city’s highest-rated disc jockeys when he moved from Spanish-language radio to WKTU in 1978, when the station adopted a disco format.

name: Alla Verber
profession: Gave Russia a Taste for Luxury
headline: Alla Verber, Who Gave Russia a Taste for Luxury, Dies at 61
abstract: In the wake of the dowdy Soviet era, she was called the most powerful woman in Russian fashion, ushering in Western brands and modernizing top department stores.

name: Laxmibai Rani
headline: Overlooked No More: Rani of Jhansi, India’s Warrior Queen Who Fought the British
abstract: When the British tried to take control of the northern Indian town of Jhansi, Queen Laxmibai trained and led her own army, and was killed in battle.

name: Piero Tosi
headline: Piero Tosi, Who Outfitted Stars of Italian Films, Dies at 92
abstract: A favorite of the director Luchino Visconti, he was nominated for five Oscars for costume design and received an honorary award in 2013.

name: Gerry Murray
headline: Gerry Murray, Stalwart Roller Derby Star, Dies at 98
abstract: A speedy skater and tough brawler, she played for 22 years, then returned in her 50s for a bruising final hurrah.

name: Kary B. Mullis
profession: Found a Way to Analyze DNA and Won Nobel
headline: Kary B. Mullis, 74, Dies; Found a Way to Analyze DNA and Won Nobel
abstract: His discovery created a new world of possibilities in diagnosing disease, unearthing the past and assisting in criminal cases, including O.J. Simpson’s murder trial.

name: Barbara Crane
profession: Photographer Found Abstract in the Ordinary
headline: Barbara Crane, 91, Dies; Photographer Found Abstract in the Ordinary
abstract: A master of illusion, Ms. Crane transformed the quotidian into the quirky by distorting images through a variety of formats.

name: Donald Klein
headline: Donald Klein, Who Expanded the Psychiatric Toolbox, Dies at 90
abstract: His studies of the use of drugs to treat disorders led many to consider him “the father of psychopharmacology.”

name: Ernie Colón
headline: Ernie Colón, Comic Book Artist Who Drew 9/11, Dies at 88
abstract: His art captured the whimsy of Richie Rich, the fantasy realms of Amethyst and the horror of the terrorist attacks.

name: Danny Cohen
profession: Helped Set the Stage for a Digital Era
headline: Danny Cohen, Who Helped Set the Stage for a Digital Era, Dies at 81
abstract: A computer scientist who devised the first flight simulator and paved the way for internet voice calls, cloud computing and online dating. (He married her.)

name: Peter Fonda
headline: Peter Fonda, ‘Easy Rider’ Actor and Screenwriter, Is Dead at 79
abstract: A member of a celebrated Hollywood family, he was nominated for an Oscar in a seminal film of the 1960s.

name: Jean-Pierre Mocky
headline: Jean-Pierre Mocky, Iconoclastic French Film Director, Dies at 90
abstract: He found a following making unapologetically raw films that challenged what he saw as hypocrisies in society.

name: Paule Marshall
headline: Paule Marshall, Influential Black Novelist, Dies at 90
abstract: A child of Barbadian immigrants, Ms. Marshall drew on her upbringing to animate the lives of her characters, many of them strong women.

name: Katreese Barnes
headline: Katreese Barnes, a Musical Force Behind the Scenes, Dies at 56
abstract: She worked with Roberta Flack and other stars. But she probably made her biggest splash by helping write a risqué song for “Saturday Night Live.”

name: Richard Williams
headline: Richard Williams, Who Brought Roger Rabbit to Life, Dies at 86
abstract: A three-time Oscar winner, he worked in film and television and wrote a book on animation that became an essential industry reference.

name: Liane Russell
headline: Liane Russell, Who Studied Radiation’s Effects on Embryos, Dies at 95
abstract: Her findings led to cautions against X-rays for pregnant women. She also discovered that the presence of the Y chromosome meant a mammalian embryo was male.

name: Jack Whitaker
headline: Jack Whitaker, Emmy-Winning Sportscaster, Dies at 95
abstract: He covered all areas of sport, from baseball and football to golf and the Olympics, but he was perhaps best known for his graceful essays.

name: Kathleen Blanco
headline: Kathleen Blanco, Louisiana Governor During Hurricane Katrina, Dies at 76
abstract: She was the first female governor of her state, and won mixed reviews for her response to the devastating storm.

name: Gina Lopez
profession: Led Crackdown on Mines in the Philippines
headline: Gina Lopez, Who Led Crackdown on Mines in the Philippines, Dies at 65
abstract: Ms. Lopez was forced from her job as environment secretary after she halted the operations of many of the country’s mining companies.

name: Myrna Katz Frommer
profession: Oral Historian of Catskills and Brooklyn
headline: Myrna Katz Frommer, 80, Dies; Oral Historian of Catskills and Brooklyn
abstract: She collaborated with her husband, Harvey, on “It Happened in the Catskills” and other histories told in the voices of the people who were there.

name: Al Jackson
headline: Al Jackson, Pitching Star of Woeful 1960s Mets, Is Dead at 83
abstract: He lost 20 games and won only eight in 1962 for a legendarily bad team. But among his wins were four shutouts, including a one-hitter.

name: Shelby Lyman
profession: Unlikely Star of a Fischer-Spassky Broadcast
headline: Shelby Lyman, 82, Dies; Unlikely Star of a Fischer-Spassky Broadcast
abstract: Mr. Lyman was a high-ranked player who was drafted to provide live commentary of the celebrated chess match in 1972. The show became an improbable hit.

name: Ugo Sansonetti
headline: Ugo Sansonetti, 100, Dies; Won Track Medals Into His 90s
abstract: He began running after retiring from his job and racked up dozens of gold medals and two world records in masters competitions.

name: Jack Perkins
headline: Jack Perkins, NBC Reporter and ‘Biography’ Host, Dies at 85
abstract: He was a familiar face on TV for more than two decades, covering the civil rights movement, the Vietnam War and other big stories.

name: Timothy Means
headline: Timothy Means, Whose Ecotourism Made a Difference, Dies at 75
abstract: He loved the Baja Peninsula and helped preserve it, introducing people to the region and convincing them that it was worth protecting.

name: Lau Sing Kee
profession: War Hero Jailed for Helping Immigrants
headline: Overlooked No More: Lau Sing Kee, War Hero Jailed for Helping Immigrants
abstract: Kee was awarded for his bravery in World War I, but later became a convicted criminal when he skirted discriminatory laws to help immigrants move to America from China.

name: Ann Gish Phillips
headline: Ann Gish Phillips Dies at 70; Designed and Sold Luxury Bedding
abstract: She saw a void in the home furnishings market and decided to fill it, opening a large emporium in Manhattan and reaching a global customer base.

name: Nancy Reddin Kienholz
headline: Nancy Reddin Kienholz, Whose Art Challenged and Disturbed, Dies at 75
abstract: With her husband and artistic partner, the sculptor Edward Kienholz, she created installations that denounced societal ills like sexism, racism and child-abuse.

name: Felice Gimondi
profession: Cyclist With a Career Triple Crown and a Rival
headline: Felice Gimondi, Cyclist With a Career Triple Crown and a Rival, Dies at 76
abstract: He was one of the rare competitors to win the Tour de France, the Vuelta a España and the Giro d’Italia. But he was stymied by the great Eddy Merckx.

name: David Koch
headline: David Koch, Billionaire Who Fueled Right-Wing Movement, Dies at 79
abstract: A man-about-town philanthropist, he and his brother Charles ran a business colossus while furthering a libertarian agenda that reshaped American politics.

name: Russ Conway
profession: His Reporting Led to a Hockey Bosss Downfall
headline: Russ Conway, 70, Dies; His Reporting Led to a Hockey Boss’s Downfall
abstract: He detailed the corrupt acts of the head of the N.H.L. players’ union, laying the groundwork for successful prosecutions in the United States and Canada.

name: Werner Kramarsky
headline: Werner Kramarsky, Rights Official and Arts Patron, Dies at 93
abstract: He played prominent roles in both city and state government in New York. He wore another hat as well, supporting artists and building a vast drawing collection.

name: Charles Santore
headline: Charles Santore Dies at 84; Illustrated Classic Children’s Books
abstract: He began his career creating magazine advertisements and covers for TV Guide, and later focused on vibrant new versions of classic children’s tales.

name: Gerard O’Neill
headline: Gerard O’Neill, Boston Globe Investigative Reporter, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. O’Neill’s biggest quarry was Whitey Bulger, Boston’s most notorious mobster, whom he helped expose as an F.B.I. informant.

name: Sidney Rittenberg
headline: Sidney Rittenberg, Idealistic American Aide to Mao Who Evolved to Counsel Capitalists, Dies at 98
abstract: Once a dedicated Communist, Mr. Rittenberg became disillusioned after 16 years in prison in China and returned to the United States to forge a lucrative career helping companies do business in China.

name: Isabel Toledo
headline: Isabel Toledo Dies at 59; Designed Michelle Obama’s Inaugural Outfit
abstract: She described her work as “romantic mathematics” and was happy that her designs could find a wider audience through her work with Anne Klein and Lane Bryant.

name: Ann Nelson
headline: Ann Nelson, Expert on Particle Physics, Is Dead at 61
abstract: Dr. Nelson was celebrated for helping to address flaws in the Standard Model, the longtime basis for explaining how particles interact.

name: Pal Benko
headline: Pal Benko, Who Stepped Aside for Bobby Fischer, Dies at 91
abstract: In 1970 Mr. Benko qualified for the world chess championship cycle but, past his peak as a competitive player, ceded his place to the much younger Mr. Fischer.

name: Ferdinand Piëch
headline: Ferdinand Piëch, Domineering Volkswagen Chief, Dies at 82
abstract: The grandson of the designer of the Beetle, he rescued Volkswagen from near bankruptcy but was blamed for creating a company culture that bred scandal.

name: Arun Jaitley
headline: Arun Jaitley, Bold Indian Finance Minister, Is Dead at 66
abstract: Working alongside Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Mr. Jaitley oversaw major economic experiments and earned respect in a fractured political landscape.

name: Orlando Suero
headline: Orlando Suero, 94, Dies; Photographed Notables, Including the Kennedys
abstract: He captured the newlyweds John and Jacqueline Kennedy in their Georgetown home and, later, Brigitte Bardot, Paul Newman and numerous other movie stars.

name: Richard Booth
headline: Richard Booth, Self-Crowned King of Used Books, Dies at 80
abstract: He transformed a fading Welsh town into a tourist magnet by buying books in bulk from colleges, libraries, defunct wholesalers and collectors’ estates.

name: Wang Guodong
headline: Wang Guodong, Who Painted Mao Year After Year, Dies at 88
abstract: He received one of China’s highest — and most intimidating — honors: responsibility for creating the huge portrait that gazes down on Tiananmen Square.

name: Tim Bell
profession: Brazen P.R. Man for Thatcher and Other Leaders
headline: Tim Bell, 77, Dies; Brazen P.R. Man for Thatcher and Other Leaders
abstract: His clients included dictators and people accused of crimes. “Morality,” he once said, “is a job for priests, not P.R. men.”

name: Frances Crowe
headline: Frances Crowe, Peace Activist and War Resister, Dies at 100
abstract: The bombing of Hiroshima led her to devote her life to antiwar protests. She was arrested often, but when asked how often, she said, “Not enough.”

name: Elizabeth Rona
profession: Pioneering Scientist Amid Dangers of War
headline: Overlooked No More: Elizabeth Rona, Pioneering Scientist Amid Dangers of War
abstract: Rona moved from lab to lab — and country to country — and in the process made important findings about the behavior of atoms and radioactivity.

name: Mario Davidovsky
headline: Mario Davidovsky, Composer Who Made Electronics Sing, Dies at 85
abstract: In the early 1960s, Mr. Davidovsky was a groundbreaker in creating music that coupled acoustic instruments with electronic sounds.

name: Ningali Lawford-Wolf
headline: Ningali Lawford-Wolf, Indigenous Australian Actress, Dies
abstract: Known for her role in the movie “Rabbit-Proof Fence,” she also had a rich stage career, including a critically praised one-woman show.

name: Kay Ann Johnson
headline: Kay Ann Johnson, 73, Who Studied China’s One-Child Policy, Dies
abstract: After adopting an abandoned infant from an orphanage in China, she began researching the lives of birth parents who had been forced to give up their children.

name: Donnie Fritts
headline: Donnie Fritts, Who Bridged Soul and Country Music, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Fritts, who was probably best known for his long tenure in Kris Kristofferson’s band, was a force in Southern popular music for more than two decades.

name: James R. Leavelle
profession: Detective at Lee Harvey Oswalds Side
headline: James R. Leavelle, Detective at Lee Harvey Oswald’s Side, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Leavelle’s reaction to Lee Harvey Oswald’s shooting by Jack Ruby in 1963 was captured in an indelible photograph that won the Pulitzer Prize.

name: Vince Naimoli
profession: Brought Major League Baseball to Tampa
headline: Vince Naimoli, 81, Dies; Brought Major League Baseball to Tampa
abstract: He succeeded in luring an expansion team to the Tampa-St. Petersburg area. But the team never had a winning season during his time as owner.

name: Takis
headline: Takis, Sculptor Who Made Art From Moving Parts, Dies at 93
abstract: His Kinetic works could resemble science projects or unfinished constructions. When they were activated, their movements could startle, educate and entertain.

name: Pedro Bell
headline: Pedro Bell, Whose Wild Album Covers Defined Funkadelic, Dies at 69
abstract: His vivid imagery, hypersexualized and full of futuristic themes, helped create the mythology of George Clinton’s groundbreaking group.

name: Brunilda Ruiz
headline: Brunilda Ruiz, Original Joffrey and Harkness Dancer, Dies at 83
abstract: A student of Robert Joffrey, she was celebrated for her classical form and dramatic presence and viewed as a role model by other Hispanic ballet dancers.

name: Bobby Dillon
profession: Packer With One Eye and Team Record
headline: Bobby Dillon, Packer With One Eye and Team Record, Dies at 89
abstract: An All-American defensive back at the University of Texas and a four-time Pro Bowl safety, he holds Green Bay’s lifetime interception mark with 52.

name: Valerie Harper
profession: Won Fame and Emmys as Rhoda
headline: Valerie Harper, Who Won Fame and Emmys as ‘Rhoda,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Originally a theater actress, she parlayed a role as a wisecracking sidekick on “The Mary Tyler Moore Show” into her own sitcom.

name: Leslie H. Gelb
profession: Former Diplomat and New York Times Journalist
headline: Leslie H. Gelb, 82, Former Diplomat and New York Times Journalist, Dies
abstract: He was an editor, columnist and Pulitzer Prize-winning correspondent for The Times and served in a variety of government posts.

name: Clora Bryant
profession: Trumpeter and Pillar of L.A. Jazz Scene
headline: Clora Bryant, Trumpeter and Pillar of L.A. Jazz Scene, Dies at 92
abstract: Dizzy Gillespie called her his protégé. But faced with sexist discrimination, she did not establish herself as a bandleader until middle age.

name: Edda Servi Machlin
headline: Edda Servi Machlin, 93, Champion of Italian Jewish Cuisine, Dies
abstract: Friends urged her to write down her recipes, and in 1981 she brought a little-known side of Jewish food to the public

name: Nicolás Leoz
profession: FIFA Official Charged in Corruption Scandal
headline: Nicolás Leoz, FIFA Official Charged in Corruption Scandal, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Leoz, once the most powerful man in South American soccer, spent years fighting extradition to the United States to face charges of taking bribes.

name: Barbara Probst Solomon
headline: Barbara Probst Solomon, Who Wrote of Spain Under Franco, Dies at 90
abstract: Admired for her observations on culture and politics, she was best known for a memoir about her involvement with the anti-Franco resistance movement.

name: Sogyal Rinpoche
profession: Tibetan Buddhist Lama Felled by Abuse Accusations
headline: Sogyal Rinpoche Dies; Tibetan Buddhist Lama Felled by Abuse Accusations
abstract: A friend of the Dalai Lama’s, he wrote a popular book about life, death and the afterlife that updated “The Tibetan Book of the Dead.”

name: Donald Lindberg
profession: Opened Medical Research to the World
headline: Dr. Donald Lindberg, 85, Dies; Opened Medical Research to the World
abstract: As director of the National Library of Medicine, the world’s largest medical library, he digitized its holdings to make them available to experts globally.

name: Franco Columbu
headline: Franco Columbu, Bodybuilder and Schwarzenegger Friend, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Columbu held titles like Mr. Universe and Mr. Olympia, and helped bodybuilding broaden its audience by appearing in action films and “Pumping Iron.”

name: Martin Weitzman
headline: Martin Weitzman, Virtuoso Climate Change Economist, Dies at 77
abstract: A pathfinder in environmental economics who insisted on factoring in the worst-case scenarios of global warming.

name: Peter Lindbergh
headline: Peter Lindbergh, Photographer Who Captured Rise of the Supermodel, Dies at 74
abstract: He was known for cinematic and naturalistic portraits of models in black and white.

name: Rosemary Kuhlmann
headline: Rosemary Kuhlmann, Singer in a TV Breakthrough, Dies at 97
abstract: In 1951 she sang a pivotal role in Gian Carlo Menotti’s made-for-TV opera, ‘Amahl and the Night Visitors,’ which became a classic.

name: Dawda Jawara
headline: Dawda Jawara, Founding Father of Gambia, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Jawara led Gambia to independence from the British, then presided over the country as it became one of the region’s longest-running democracies.

name: Sally Floyd
headline: Sally Floyd, Who Helped Things Run Smoothly Online, Dies at 69
abstract: In the early 1990s, Dr. Floyd was one of the inventors of Random Early Detection, which continues to play a vital role in the stability of the internet.

name: Marita Lorenz
profession: Told Tales of Castro and Kennedy
headline: Marita Lorenz, Who Told Tales of Castro and Kennedy, Dies at 80
abstract: She was romanced by revolutionaries. She was called “a patron saint of conspiracy buffs.” At least some of her stories appear to be true.

name: James Atlas
headline: James Atlas, an Ambassador for Biographies, Dies at 70
abstract: His own books on Saul Bellow and Delmore Schwartz were acclaimed, as was the series of biographies by other authors that he edited.

name: Tom Collins
profession: Promoter of Elite Figure Skating Tours
headline: Tom Collins, Promoter of Elite Figure Skating Tours, Dies at 88
abstract: For nearly 40 years, his Champions on Ice showcased Olympic stars like Michelle Kwan, Brian Boitano, Dorothy Hamill and Johnny Weir.

name: Terrance Dicks
headline: Terrance Dicks, ‘Doctor Who’  Mainstay, Dies at 84
abstract: He wrote numerous episodes of the long-running show, as well as dozens of novels for young readers based on its scripts.

name: LaShawn Daniels
headline: LaShawn Daniels, Grammy-Winning Songwriter, Dies at 41
abstract: He wrote songs for superstars like Lady Gaga, Michael Jackson and Jennifer Lopez and was honored for his work on the Destiny’s Child hit “Say My Name.”

name: Carol Lynley
profession: Star of Blue Denim and The Poseidon Adventure
headline: Carol Lynley, Star of ‘Blue Denim’ and ‘The Poseidon Adventure,’ Dies at 77
abstract: An actress whose career mirrored America’s shift from the Eisenhower era to the sexually frank 1960s.

name: Robert Mugabe
headline: Robert Mugabe, Strongman Who Cried, ‘Zimbabwe Is Mine,’ Dies at 95
abstract: Until 2017, he was the only leader his country had known since independence in 1980. He presided over its long decline.

name: Steven Gubser
profession: Bright Star in the Physics Universe
headline: Steven Gubser, a Bright Star in the Physics Universe, Dies at 47
abstract: He did groundbreaking work toward finding a “theory of everything.” He died in an Alpine rock-climbing accident.

name: Alice Guy Blaché
headline: Overlooked No More: Alice Guy Blaché, the World’s First Female Filmmaker
abstract: Even before women had the right to vote, Blaché, in her actions and in her films, expressed female drives, desires and self-determination.

name: Francisco Toledo
profession: Celebrated Mexican Artist and Arts Philanthropist
headline: Francisco Toledo, Celebrated Mexican Artist and Arts Philanthropist, Dies at 79
abstract: He drew on his indigenous Zapotec heritage in his art and used his prestige to preserve the culture of his native Oaxaca.

name: Patty Abramson
profession: Supporter of Businesses Owned by Women
headline: Patty Abramson, 74, Supporter of Businesses Owned by Women, Dies
abstract: She helped create the Women’s Growth Capital Fund to overcome a barrier. But, she said, “We wouldn’t have done this if money wasn’t to be made.”

name: Hans Rausing
headline: Hans Rausing, Swedish Packaging Magnate, Is Dead at 93
abstract: One of the wealthiest people in Europe, he took over his father’s company and helped bring Tetra Pak to supermarkets and breakfast tables around the world.

name: Jimmy Johnson
profession: Studio Staple of Southern Soul and Pop
headline: Jimmy Johnson, Studio Staple of Southern Soul and Pop, Dies at 76
abstract: As a guitarist and a recording engineer, he contributed to hit records by Aretha Franklin, Paul Simon, Wilson Pickett and many others.

name: Ciaran McKeown
headline: Ciaran McKeown Dies at 76; Sought Peace in Northern Ireland
abstract: Mr. McKeown was inspired by the deaths of three children to help found the Peace People, a grass-roots organization that campaigned for an end to violence.

name: Elaine La Roche
profession: Power on Wall Street Despite Its Barriers
headline: Elaine La Roche, a Power on Wall Street Despite Its Barriers, Dies at 70
abstract: She was one of the most influential women in investment banking in the ’90s, helping to orchestrate a landmark partnership with China.

name: Stanley Love
headline: Stanley Love, Choreographer Who Celebrated Joy, Dies at 49
abstract: With his own company, he created works for dancers of all skill levels, embracing spectacle, pop music and social dancing.

name: Dorothea Benton Frank
headline: Dorothea Benton Frank, Whose Novels Depicted Strong Women, Dies at 67
abstract: She had been a fashion buyer and executive before declaring, “I’m going to write a book and I’m going to sell a million copies and I’m going to buy Momma’s house back.’’

name: Marca Bristo
headline: Marca Bristo, Influential Advocate for the Disabled, Dies at 66
abstract: Paralyzed in an accident at 23, she devoted her life to changing perceptions of the disabled and was a key player in passing the Americans With Disabilities Act.

name: Camilo Sesto
headline: Camilo Sesto, Spain’s Romantic Hitmaker, Is Dead at 72
abstract: With more than 2 dozen albums and more than 50 No. 1 hits worldwide, he was a pop superstar, singing about love and heartache.

name: Peter Nichols
headline: Peter Nichols, Playwright Who Found Comedy in Desperation, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Nichols drew on his life for acerbic but humor-filled works like “A Day in the Death of Joe Egg,” and “Forget-Me-Not Lane.”

name: Neil Montanus
headline: Neil Montanus, a Kodak Colorama Photographer, Dies at 92
abstract: His colossal pictures, depicting an idealized American life, greeted travelers at Grand Central Terminal for decades.

name: Robert Frank
headline: Robert Frank Dies; Pivotal Documentary Photographer Was 94
abstract: Mr. Frank, best known for his groundbreaking book, “The Americans,” had a visually raw and personally expressive style that made him one of the most influential photographers of the 20th century.

name: Immanuel Wallerstein
headline: Immanuel Wallerstein, Sociologist With Global View, Dies at 88
abstract: His doctrine of the world-system, an influential theory in the field, went beyond tribes, nations and ethnic groups.

name: Chris March
headline: Chris March, Over-the-Top Fashion Designer, Dies at 56
abstract: He dressed celebrities like Lady Gaga and Beyoncé, but he found his most outlandish inspirations in vegetables, Martha Stewart, even a martini.

name: Susan Kamil
headline: Susan Kamil, a Top Book Editor and Publisher, Dies at 69
abstract: Salman Rushdie, Ta-Nehisi Coates, Lena Dunham, Elizabeth Strout, Gary Shteyngart and Prince were among the authors she nurtured.

name: Charlie Silvera
headline: Charlie Silvera, Seldom-Seen Yankees Catcher, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Capable at the plate and solid behind it, he had one good reason for toiling in obscurity: being No. 2 to Yogi Berra. (But the money was good.)

name: Joan Johnson
headline: Joan Johnson, Whose Company Broke a Racial Barrier, Dies at 89
abstract: With her husband, George, she founded the hair-care and cosmetics company Johnson Products, the first black-owned business on the American Stock Exchange.

name: Jan Ruff-O’Herne
profession: Told of Wartime Rape by the Japanese
headline: Jan Ruff-O’Herne, Who Told of Wartime Rape by the Japanese, Dies at 96
abstract: As many as 200,000 “comfort women” were treated as the Imperial Army’s sex slaves. She was the first European to speak up about it — 50 years later.

name: Frederic Pryor
profession: Player in Bridge of Spies Case
headline: Frederic Pryor, Player in ‘Bridge of Spies’ Case, Dies at 86
abstract: Arrested and jailed on an espionage charge in East Berlin in 1961, Mr. Pryor, an economics student, became part of a famous prisoner exchange.

name: Diet Eman
profession: Risked Her Life to Rescue Dutch Jews
headline: Diet Eman, Who Risked Her Life to Rescue Dutch Jews, Dies at 99
abstract: It took 50 years for her to write of her exploits in the Dutch Resistance, rescuing pilots, sheltering fugitives and enduring capture.

name: Kiran Nagarkar
headline: Kiran Nagarkar, Novelist Who Chronicled Mumbai Life, Dies at 77
abstract: His writing was bawdy, irreverent and joyous but also held up a mirror to uncomfortable truths.

name: T. Boone Pickens
profession: Oil Magnate and Corporate Raider Was 91
headline: T. Boone Pickens Is Dead; Oil Magnate and Corporate Raider Was 91
abstract: He made big oil companies quake by threatening to take them over. His targets included Gulf Oil, Unocal and Phillips Petroleum.

name: Richard Conrad
headline: Richard Conrad, Briefly a Bel Canto Star, Dies at 84
abstract: Discovered as a young tenor by Joan Sutherland, he went on to a career in Europe and overcame a throat injury from a mugging to return as a baritone.

name: Daniel Johnston
headline: Daniel Johnston Dies; Gifted and Enigmatic Songwriter Was 58
abstract: He was admired by Kurt Cobain and Tom Waits and earned comparisons to William Blake. But his career was cut short by his struggles with mental illness.

name: Mary Lyerly Alexander
headline: Mary Lyerly Alexander, Keeper of the Coltrane Flame, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Celebrated in song by John Coltrane as “Cousin Mary,” she helped preserve his legacy and keep the jazz scene vibrant in Philadelphia.

name: Alison Cheek
headline: Alison Cheek, Pioneering Episcopal Priest, Is Dead at 92
abstract: In a controversial 1974 ceremony, she and 10 other women became priests. Then she became the first to celebrate the Eucharist in an Episcopal church.

name: Mihri Rassim
profession: Feminist Artist in the Ottoman Empire
headline: Overlooked No More: Mihri Rassim, Feminist Artist in the Ottoman Empire
abstract: In conservative Turkey, she sought the same artistic freedoms that men were granted, championed art education for women and ultimately left for the United States to pursue her ambitions.

name: B.J. Habibie
headline: B.J. Habibie Dies at 83; Ushered in Democracy in Indonesia
abstract: Though he served as the country’s president for only 17 months, he played a crucial role in ending a harsh 32-year dictatorship.

name: Chester Williams
headline: Chester Williams, Rugby Champion Who Signaled Apartheid’s Defeat, Dies at 49
abstract: Williams was the only nonwhite on the Springboks when it won the 1995 World Cup and was embraced by Nelson Mandela in a message of reconciliation.

name: Roger Etchegaray
headline: Cardinal Roger Etchegaray Dies at 96; Skilled Papal Emissary
abstract: He was in charge of the Vatican department that dealt with peace efforts, and was sent by Pope John Paul II to Cuba, Iraq and China.

name: William Y. Chang
profession: Newspaper Spoke to Chinatown in English
headline: William Y. Chang, Whose Newspaper Spoke to Chinatown in English, Dies at 103
abstract: For 17 years, his aim was to help the children of Chinese immigrants acquire an American identity as they adapted to life in the United States.

name: Eddie Money
headline: Eddie Money, ‘Two Tickets to Paradise’ Singer, Is Dead at 70
abstract: He burst on the scene in the late 1970s and went on to have a string of rock hits that also included “Baby Hold On.”

name: Mardik Martin
headline: Mardik Martin, Collaborator With Scorsese, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Known for gritty realism, he had screenwriting credits including “Mean Streets,” “New York, New York” and  “Raging Bull.”

name: Jean Edward Smith
headline: Jean Edward Smith, Biographer of the Underrated, Dies at 86
abstract: His books helped restore the reputations of Grant and Eisenhower and return John Marshall to the forefront of the American story.

name: Anne Rivers Siddons
headline: Anne Rivers Siddons, Novelist Whose Muse Was the New South, Dies at 83
abstract: She found inspiration in her Georgia upbringing and in Atlanta’s evolution into a major postwar city.

name: Juanita Abernathy
profession: Force in the Civil Rights Movement
headline: Juanita Abernathy, a Force in the Civil Rights Movement, Dies at 87
abstract: The wife of the Rev. Dr. Ralph Abernathy, she was an activist in her own right in the struggle to end segregation and to secure the vote.

name: Ric Ocasek
profession: New Wave Rock Visionary and Cars Co-Founder
headline: Ric Ocasek, New Wave Rock Visionary and Cars Co-Founder, Dies at 75
abstract: A Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductee, he wrote songs that updated classic sounds and managed to please both punk-rock fans and a broader pop audience.

name: Phyllis Newman
headline: Phyllis Newman, Tony Award-Winning Star, Is Dead at 86
abstract: She was also a familiar face on television and raised millions of dollars to help women in entertainment deal with health problems.

name: Paul Ingrassia
headline: Paul Ingrassia, Prizewinning Auto Industry Reporter, Dies at 69
abstract: He went inside the boardrooms and executive suites in winning a Pulitzer for The Wall Street Journal, then traced the industry’s fortunes in books.

name: Cokie Roberts
headline: Cokie Roberts Dies; Veteran Broadcast Journalist Was 75
abstract: She was known to millions for her pioneering work for ABC News and NPR.

name: John Cohen
headline: John Cohen, Champion of Old-Time Music, Is Dead at 87
abstract: As a founder of the New Lost City Ramblers and as a photographer, filmmaker and musicologist, he devoted his life to the traditional music of the rural South.

name: Sander Vanocur
headline: Sander Vanocur, TV Newsman Who Covered Kennedy, Dies at 91
abstract: A veteran correspondent, he was the last surviving journalist who questioned Nixon and Kennedy in the first televised presidential debate.

name: Betty Corwin
headline: Betty Corwin, Who Preserved Theater’s Legacy, Dies at 98
abstract: By definition, live theater vanishes in the moment; Ms. Corwin pushed to have shows videotaped and deposited in a library collection, which she ran for decades.

name: Marina Schiano
profession: Distinctive Presence in the Fashion World
headline: Marina Schiano, Distinctive Presence in the Fashion World, Dies at 77
abstract: Leaving home in Italy as a teenager, she modeled for Vogue and other magazines before carving out a high-profile career as an executive and stylist.

name: Luigi Colani
profession: Designer of Fanciful and Futuristic Objects
headline: Luigi Colani, 91, Designer of Fanciful and Futuristic Objects, Dies
abstract: Better known for far-out prototypes than actual products, he was seen by his admirers as a visionary in an unimaginative world.

name: Elizabeth A. Gloucester
profession: Richest Black Woman and Ally of John Brown
headline: Overlooked No More: Elizabeth A. Gloucester, ‘Richest’ Black Woman and Ally of John Brown
abstract: She ran boardinghouses whose lodgers included members of New York’s elite, raised money for an orphan asylum and was active in the abolitionists’ cause.

name: Lee Salem
headline: Lee Salem, Champion of Quirky Cartoonists, Is Dead at 73
abstract: He nurtured an empire of influential comic strips, including “Cathy,” “Doonesbury,” “Calvin and Hobbes,” “The Boondocks” and “For Better or for Worse.”

name: Richard Abrons
profession: Patron of the Henry Street Settlement
headline: Richard Abrons, Patron of the Henry Street Settlement, Dies at 92
abstract: As a boy, he met the famed institution’s founder, Lillian Wald, and became a benefactor. In midcareer, he traded Wall Street investing for writing short stories and plays.

name: James Robertson
headline: Judge James Robertson, Who Quit FISA Court Over Wiretapping, Dies at 81
abstract: He took a stand to protest warrantless domestic eavesdropping under George W. Bush. On the federal bench, he ruled against trying a Guantánamo detainee in a military court.

name: James I. Robertson Jr.
headline: James I. Robertson Jr., Exacting Civil War Historian, Dies at 89
abstract: Dr. Robertson, who wrote or edited dozens of books, was best known for his monumental biography of Stonewall Jackson.

name: Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali
profession: Tunisia Autocrat Ousted in Arab Spring
headline: Zine el-Abidine Ben Ali, 83, Tunisia Autocrat Ousted in Arab Spring, Dies
abstract: His oppressive rule set off uprisings that spread throughout the Arab world. He died in exile in Saudi Arabia, which had refused to extradite him.

name: Maurice Ferré
headline: Maurice Ferré, Miami’s First Hispanic Mayor, Dies at 84
abstract: He led the city through a defining period of growth and tumult for 12 years. But he could ultimately not withstand its demographic transformation.

name: Mark von Hagen
headline: Mark von Hagen, Critic of Times’s Stalin Coverage, Dies at 65
abstract: A historian, he was asked by the paper to judge whether a correspondent’s Pulitzer Prize should be revoked because of biased reporting. He said it should be.

name: Barron Hilton
profession: Hotel Magnate and Founding A.F.L. Owner
headline: Barron Hilton, Hotel Magnate and Founding A.F.L. Owner, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Hilton successfully expanded the hotel chain founded by his father, but he said his happiest days were when he owned the Chargers football team.

name: Steve Dalachinsky
headline: Steve Dalachinsky, Avant-Garde Poet, Is Dead at 72
abstract: A familiar sight in downtown New York clubs as both a spectator and a performer, he often read his poems to jazz accompaniment.

name: Annette Kolodny
headline: Annette Kolodny, Feminist Critic and Scholar, Dies at 78
abstract: She was a pioneer in the field of ecofeminism, in which she drew parallels between the ravaging of the environment and the ravaging of women.

name: Howard Cassady
headline: Howard (Hopalong) Cassady, Speedy Heisman Winner, Dies at 85
abstract: Twice an All-American, he scored 37 touchdowns in 36 games at Ohio State, then won an N.F.L. title with the Lions.

name: Ascensión Mendieta
profession: Symbol of Justice for Franco Victims
headline: Ascensión Mendieta, 93, Dies; Symbol of Justice for Franco Victims
abstract: She fought for decades to recover the remains of her father, who had been executed by a firing squad in 1939. Finally, when she was 92, she found him.

name: Davo Karnicar
profession: Made First Full Ski Descent of Everest
headline: Davo Karnicar Dies at 56; Made First Full Ski Descent of Everest
abstract: A Slovenian adventurer, Karnicar needed less than five hours to ski 12,000 feet from the summit of Mount Everest to its base camp.

name: John L. Keenan
profession: Led the Son of Sam Manhunt
headline: John L. Keenan, Who Led the ‘Son of Sam’ Manhunt, Dies at 99
abstract: At one point, Chief Keenan put 300 people on the case, and he was the one who took the confession from the killer, David Berkowitz, who had slain six young people.

name: John F. Keenan
profession: U.S. Judge in Myerson and Marcos Trials
headline: John F. Keenan, U.S. Judge in Myerson and Marcos Trials, Dies at 94
abstract: He was impatient with courtroom theatrics, and the Manhattan trials of the commissioner and ex-beauty queen Bess Myerson and the former Philippines first lady Imelda Marcos had plenty.

name: Harold Mabern
profession: Jazz Pianist With a Lush Sound
headline: Harold Mabern, Jazz Pianist With a Lush Sound, Dies at 83
abstract: A bandleader, composer and educator, he was sought after by top musicians to record with them, drawn by his harmonic sophistication and feel for the blues.

name: Sid Haig
headline: Sid Haig, Horror Actor and Cult Figure, Dies at 80
abstract: A veteran character actor, he had roles in more than 70 movies, including the murderous clown Captain Spaulding in Rob Zombie’s “House of 1000 Corpses.”

name: Michael Edwardes
profession: Hard-Nosed Rescuer of British Car Giant
headline: Michael Edwardes, Hard-Nosed Rescuer of British Car Giant, Dies at 88
abstract: A union scourge, he brought British Leyland (maker of Jaguar, MG, Mini, Land Rover and more) back from the brink in the 1970s and was knighted for it.

name: Christopher Rouse
headline: Christopher Rouse, Composer of Rage and Delicacy, Dies at 70
abstract: He was influenced by the energy of rock music and became a favorite of orchestras for his intense, kinetic works.

name: A. Alvarez
profession: Poet Elevated Both Sylvia Plath and Poker
headline: A. Alvarez Dies at 90; Poet Elevated Both Sylvia Plath and Poker
abstract: He was pivotal in bringing the work of poets like Plath and Ted Hughes to the wider public and wrote acclaimed books on poker in Las Vegas and suicide.

name: Robert Hunter
headline: Robert Hunter, Grateful Dead Lyricist, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Hunter wrote some of the band’s signature songs, including “Uncle John’s Band,” “Scarlet Begonias” and “Dark Star.”

name: Robert McClelland
headline: Dr. Robert McClelland, Who Tried to Save President Kennedy, Dies at 89
abstract: He assisted in an emergency tracheotomy in Dallas and saw close up the gravity of the president’s head wound.

name: Sigmund Jähn
profession: First German in Space and a Hero Back Home
headline: Sigmund Jähn, First German in Space and a Hero Back Home, Dies at 82
abstract: He spent almost eight days aboard a space station in 1978 and was hailed by East Germans as a symbol of socialist achievement.

name: Alfred Haynes
headline: Alfred Haynes, Pilot Who Saved Scores in Crash Landing, Dies at 87
abstract: In 1989, he defied the odds in bringing his crippled United Flight 232 in for a crash landing; more than 180 people survived.

name: Robert Johnson
headline: Overlooked No More: Robert Johnson, Bluesman Whose Life Was a Riddle
abstract: Johnson gained little notice in his life, but his songs — quoted by the Rolling Stones, Eric Clapton and Led Zeppelin — helped ignite rock ‘n’ roll.

name: Sol Stein
headline: Sol Stein, Publisher, Author and Champion of James Baldwin, Dies at 92
abstract: A founder of the publishing house Stein and Day, he also worked with Dylan Thomas, Budd Schulberg and David Frost and wrote more than a dozen books.

name: Ruth Abrams
headline: Ruth Abrams, Judge Who Broke a Glass Ceiling Installed in 1692, Dies at 88
abstract: In Massachusetts she wrote landmark decisions on family law and gender equality that were widely cited across the country. And she quietly recruited many women to the bench.

name: Robert Boyd
headline: Robert Boyd, Journalist Whose Reporting Shifted an Election, Dies at 91
abstract: He shared a Pulitzer for detailing how George McGovern’s initial running mate in 1972 had undergone electroshock therapy for depression.

name: Jacques Chirac
headline: Jacques Chirac, Who Led France Envisioning European Unity, Is Dead at 86
abstract: As president he opposed the Iraq war, sought a ‘United Europe of States’ and cultivated comity between the left and the right. But an embezzlement conviction damaged him.

name: Plato Cacheris
profession: Washington Super Lawyer in Headline Cases
headline: Plato Cacheris, Washington ‘Super Lawyer’ in Headline Cases, Dies at 90
abstract: If there was a national scandal — Watergate, Iran-contra, “Monica-gate,” the Snowden affair — he got the call. His deal making was legend.

name: Anthony Mancinelli
headline: Anthony Mancinelli, World’s Oldest Working Barber, Dies at 108
abstract: A barber who spent nearly a century of cutting hair in upstate New York “didn’t know the meaning of the word retired.”

name: George Lardner Jr.
headline: George Lardner Jr., 85, Dies; Reported on His Daughter’s Murder
abstract: She was shot to death by a former boyfriend. He wrote about it for The Washington Post. His article won a Pulitzer Prize.

name: Joachim Messing
profession: Charted the DNA of Viruses and Plants
headline: Joachim Messing, 73, Who Charted the DNA of Viruses and Plants, Dies
abstract: His “shotgun sequencing” helped decode genetic information faster, transforming agriculture, medicine and the basic sciences. One result: engineered corn.

name: Gianfranco Gorgoni
headline: Gianfranco Gorgoni, Artistic Photographer of Art, Dies at 77
abstract: He captured masters at work and documented the creation of Land Art like Robert Smithson’s “Spiral Jetty.” For one book, he teamed with Fidel Castro.

name: Joseph Wilson
headline: Joseph Wilson, Who Challenged Iraq War Narrative, Dies at 69
abstract: He contradicted a statement in President George W. Bush’s State of the Union address. A week later, his wife at the time, Valerie Plame, was outed as a C.I.A. agent.

name: Ira Lipman
