headline: Ira Lipman, Security Man Who Spoke Out for Air Safety, Dies at 78
abstract: He founded one of the largest privately held security companies, was prescient about safeguarding airports and favored stripping most guards of guns.

name: Jimmy Nelson
profession: Star of the Golden Age of Ventriloquism
headline: Jimmy Nelson, Star of the Golden Age of Ventriloquism, Dies at 90
abstract: With his dummies Danny O’Day and Farfel, he was a familiar presence on TV. He also inspired future ventriloquists with his instructional records.

name: Myron Bloom
headline: Myron Bloom, Revered French Horn Player, Is Dead at 93
abstract: He was principal horn in the Cleveland Orchestra for George Szell and in the Orchestre de Paris for Daniel Barenboim. But his first love was the cello.

name: Napoleon Chagnon
headline: Napoleon Chagnon, 81, Controversial Anthropologist, Is Dead
abstract: His studies of an Amazon people made them famous, and put him at the center of a scholarly storm.

name: Shuping Wang
profession: Helped Expose Chinas Rural AIDS Crisis
headline: Shuping Wang, Who Helped Expose China’s Rural AIDS Crisis, Dies at 59
abstract: She braved ostracism, assault and the loss of her job to expose the spread of the disease in rural China. A play about her has opened in London.

name: Huguette Caland
profession: Celebrated Freedom in Art and Life
headline: Huguette Caland, 88, Dies; Celebrated Freedom in Art and Life
abstract: She left her husband and children in Beirut to flex her artistic muscles in Paris. Her desire to live without restrictions was her defining theme.

name: Jimmy Spicer
headline: Jimmy Spicer, Influential Early Rapper, Is Dead at 61
abstract: Mr. Spicer’s career was brief but consequential. In just a few songs he introduced phrases and tropes that would become part of hip-hop’s core catalog.

name: Jessye Norman
headline: Jessye Norman, Regal American Soprano, Is Dead at 74
abstract: A multiple Grammy Award winner, she was a towering figure on operatic, concert and recital stages.

name: Mary Abbott
headline: Mary Abbott, Abstract Expressionist, Is Dead at 98
abstract: She traveled in the same circles as Pollock and de Kooning, but recognition in a male-dominated genre often eluded her.

name: John Rothman
headline: John Rothman, Who Made The Times’s Archives Accessible, Dies at 95
abstract: Long before Google, he helped create The New York Times Information Bank, an electronic repository of content from The Times and other publications.

name: James Robinson
profession: Filled an Ambulance Gap in Brooklyn
headline: James Robinson, 79, Dies; Filled an Ambulance Gap in Brooklyn
abstract: Frustrated that responses to emergency calls took too long in Bedford-Stuyvesant, he started a volunteer ambulance corps, and it’s been nimble.

name: James D. Robinson III
headline: James D. Robinson III, Transformative Head of American Express, Dies at 88
abstract: He led the company from 1977 to 1993 and helped turn Wall Street into a more competitive financial marketplace.

name: Martin Bernheimer
headline: Martin Bernheimer, Tartly Eloquent Music Critic, Dies at 83
abstract: He minced no words when he wrote about classical music, which for most of his career he did for The Los Angeles Times.

name: Bill Bidwill
headline: Bill Bidwill, Dynastic Owner of N.F.L.’s Cardinals, Dies at 88
abstract: He moved the team from St. Louis to Arizona and presided over five playoff appearances, but never won a Super Bowl.

name: Kim Shattuck
headline: Kim Shattuck, Musician Who Fronted the Muffs, Is Dead at 56
abstract: A singer, songwriter and guitarist, she was in the vanguard of punk bands crashing into the mainstream in the 1990s.

name: Wayne Fitzgerald
headline: Wayne Fitzgerald, Master of Films’ Opening Moments, Dies at 89
abstract: His title sequences for “Bonnie and Clyde,” “Footloose” and countless others, as well as for TV, helped elevate the art form.

name: Mac Conner
headline: Mac Conner, Illustrator Who Captured a Postwar World, Dies at 105
abstract: In the 1950s and ’60s, Mr. Conner’s art helped sell airlines and overalls and accompanied short stories in The Saturday Evening Post and elsewhere.

name: Jerome Facher
profession: Won Acquittal in Noted Pollution Case
headline: Jerome Facher, 93, Dies; Won Acquittal in Noted Pollution Case
abstract: After children died from toxic water, he defended the conglomerate Beatrice Foods in a case that became the basis of the book and movie “A Civil Action.”

name: Larry Willis
headline: Larry Willis, Pianist Who Crossed Genres, Is Dead at 76
abstract: In a career that began in the early 1960s, he worked with a long and varied list of musicians and groups including Hugh Masekela, Carla Bley and Blood, Sweat and Tears.

name: Diahann Carroll
headline: Diahann Carroll, Actress Who Broke Barriers With ‘Julia,’ Dies at 84
abstract: In addition to being a sitcom pioneer, she sang on television, in nightclubs, on recordings and on Broadway, where she won a Tony Award.

name: Mordicai Gerstein
headline: Mordicai Gerstein, Illustrator of Magical Worlds, Dies at 83
abstract: He wrote and illustrated more than 40 children’s books, many of which dealt with the messy business of being human.

name: Su Beng
headline: Su Beng, a Father of Taiwan Independence, Dies at 100
abstract: He ran underground operations to liberate the island from colonial rule and wrote the foundational book “Taiwan’s 400-Year History.”

name: Karel Gott
profession: Pop Singer Called Sinatra of the East
headline: Karel Gott, Pop Singer Called ‘Sinatra of the East,’ Dies at 80
abstract: His crooning in Czech and several other languages brought him great popularity, especially in countries behind the Iron Curtain.

name: Pierre Le-Tan
headline: Pierre Le-Tan, Illustrator With a Quiet Touch, Dies at 69
abstract: His work appeared in galleries, museums and books, in collaborations with fashion brands, and, 18 times, on the cover of The New Yorker.

name: Paul Badura-Skoda
headline: Paul Badura-Skoda, Who Could Make a Piano Sing, Dies at 91
abstract: With an admired tone, he excelled at the heart of the classical repertory and was, with more than 200 discs, one of the most-recorded pianists.

name: Elaine Feinstein
headline: Elaine Feinstein, Poet, Novelist and Biographer, Dies at 88
abstract: Prolific and multifaceted, she took inspiration from her Jewish heritage and the Russian women whose work she translated.

name: Ginger Baker
headline: Ginger Baker, Superstar Rock Drummer With Cream, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Teamed with the guitarist Eric Clapton and the bassist Jack Bruce in the band Cream, Mr. Baker helped redefine the role of the drums in rock.

name: Marcello Giordani
headline: Marcello Giordani, Tenor Who ‘Sang Like a God,’ Dies at 56
abstract: A former bank employee, the Italian singer appeared more than 240 times with the Metropolitan Opera, in 27 roles.

name: Rip Taylor
headline: Rip Taylor, Flamboyant Comedian, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Known as the ‘King of Confetti,’ he was a familiar face on television during his more than 50 years in show business.

name: Günter Kunert
headline: Günter Kunert, 90, Searingly Satirical German Author, Dies
abstract: In his poems, essays, short stories and novels, he highlighted the differences between East and West Germany, even after the Berlin Wall fell.

name: Stephen Lukasik
headline: Stephen Lukasik, 88, Who Pushed Tech in National Defense, Is Dead
abstract: He oversaw the Defense Department’s research division in the 1960s and ’70s, when it made great early strides in nuclear-device detection, artificial intelligence and computer networking.

name: Beverly Watkins
headline: Beverly Watkins, Fiery Blues Guitarist, Is Dead at 80
abstract: She performed in relative obscurity for many years, but she made up for lost time after recording her first solo album at the age of 60.

name: Michael Coe
headline: Michael Coe, Maya Scholar and Codebreaker, Is Dead at 90
abstract: He authenticated the oldest written manuscript in the Americas and proved that the Maya written language was surprisingly complex.

name: Marshall Efron
profession: Funny Cog in the PBS Dream Machine
headline: Marshall Efron, Funny Cog in the PBS ‘Dream Machine,’ Dies at 81
abstract: In the 1970s he was part of a much-talked about prime-time TV series as well as a somewhat subversive Sunday morning Bible show for children.

name: Mitsuye Endo
profession: Name Linked to Justice for Japanese-Americans
headline: Overlooked No More: Mitsuye Endo, a Name Linked to Justice for Japanese-Americans
abstract: She was the lead plaintiff in a Supreme Court case that successfully challenged mass internment of American citizens during World War II.

name: Ciaran Carson
headline: Ciaran Carson, Versatile Belfast Poet, Is Dead at 70
abstract: In his poetry, as well as in his prose, he conveyed the complexities of his city and his country.

name: Jill Freedman
headline: Jill Freedman, Photographer Who Lingered in the Margins, Dies at 79
abstract: She immersed herself in the rougher precincts of American life for months at a time, portraying their denizens as noble but not necessarily heroic.

name: Deborah Marrow
headline: Deborah Marrow, a Getty Leader With Global Reach, Dies at 70
abstract: As a top executive of the J. Paul Getty Trust and its only female president, she spread its wealth around the world while promoting multiculturalism.

name: Karen Pendleton
headline: Karen Pendleton, an Original Mouseketeer, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Along with Annette Funicello and others, she was in the cast of “The Mickey Mouse Club” from its debut in 1955.

name: Francis Currey
headline: Francis Currey, a Hero in Battle at 19, Dies at 94
abstract: Days after a massacre of G.I.s, he was a one-man onslaught in the face of German tanks, earning a Medal of Honor. Only two other honorees from World War II now survive.

name: Stephen Swid
headline: Stephen Swid, Music Licensing Innovator, Is Dead at 78
abstract: After acquiring a series of businesses, including the “21” Club, he turned the obscure licensing organization Sesac into a force in the music industry.

name: Bjorn Thorbjarnarson
profession: Surgeon to Warhol and the Shah
headline: Bjorn Thorbjarnarson, Surgeon to Warhol and the Shah, Dies at 98
abstract: Warhol’s death in New York after undergoing surgery put him at the center of a lawsuit, but a later investigation suggested he and a hospital had not been at fault.

name: Aleksei Leonov
headline: Aleksei Leonov, First to Walk in Space, Dies at 85
abstract: The Russian cosmonaut’s thrilling feat in 1965 nearly cost him his life, but raised Soviet prestige during the Cold War space race against the United States.

name: Robert Goelet
headline: Robert Goelet, New York Grandee and Naturalist, Dies at 96
abstract: The scion of a 17th-century New York family, he headed major cultural institutions and became a steward of Gardiners Island, which his wife’s family had owned since 1639.

name: Anna Quayle
headline: Anna Quayle, British Character Actress, Is Dead at 86
abstract: She bantered with John Lennon in “A Hard Day’s Night” and won a Tony for playing four women in “Stop the World — I Want to Get Off.”

name: Masaichi Kaneda
headline: Masaichi Kaneda, Japan’s ‘Emperor’ of Baseball, Dies at 86
abstract: A swaggering player with a quirky warm-up routine, he set pitching records for wins (400), strikeouts (4,490), innings (5,526⅔) — and losses (298).

name: Carlos Celdran
headline: Carlos Celdran, 46, Philippine Activist and Performance Artist, Dies
abstract: He received widespread attention for his dramatic protest against the Roman Catholic Church after it blocked the passage of a reproductive health bill.

name: Philip Gips
headline: Philip Gips, Creator of Celebrated Film Posters, Dies at 88
abstract: In the imagery he devised to promote “Alien,” “Rosemary’s Baby” and other movies, he strove to capture their essence without giving too much away.

name: Robert Forster
headline: Robert Forster, Oscar Nominee for ‘Jackie Brown,’ Dies at 78
abstract: Before his 1997 comeback, his career was at a low point. “I went 21 months without a job. I had four kids. I took any job I could get.”

name: Richard Jackson
profession: Had an Ear for Childrens Books
headline: Richard Jackson, Who Had an Ear for Children’s Books, Dies at 84
abstract: As an editor he championed writers, like Judy Blume, who changed the landscape of literature for young people. He later became a writer himself.

name: Bruce LeFavour
headline: Bruce LeFavour, ‘a Good Cook,’ Dies at 84
abstract: As a restaurateur, he was in the vanguard of moving from rich French fare to more fish and seasonal, locally sourced fresh produce.

name: John Giorno
profession: Moved Poetry Beyond the Printed Page
headline: John Giorno, Who Moved Poetry Beyond the Printed Page, Dies at 82
abstract: He starred in an Andy Warhol movie, “Sleep,” but was best known for his efforts to bring poetry into the modern age.

name: Harold Bloom
headline: Harold Bloom, Critic Who Championed Western Canon, Dies at 89
abstract: Called the most notorious literary critic in America, Professor Bloom argued for the superiority of giants like Shakespeare, Chaucer and Kafka.

name: Sally Soames
headline: Sally Soames, Fearless Photographer With Personal Touch, Dies at 82
abstract: In taking portraits of the famous — Margaret Thatcher, Sean Connery and Rudolf Nureyev among them — she made them relax. In war zones she was unflinching.

name: Dana Fradon
headline: Dana Fradon, Prolific New Yorker Cartoonist, Is Dead at 97
abstract: In the nearly 1,400 cartoons he published between 1948 and 2003, he cast a wide and whimsical net on American society and skewered pomposity.

name: Beverly Sackler
headline: Beverly Sackler, 95, Dies; Philanthropist and Purdue Pharma Director
abstract: Ms. Sackler was the matriarch of the company whose drug OxyContin has been blamed for the opioid epidemic.

name: Sophia Kokosalaki
profession: Gave London Fashion a Grecian Spin
headline: Sophia Kokosalaki, Who Gave London Fashion a Grecian Spin, Dies at 46
abstract: One of the leading Greek designers of her generation, she balanced a cutting-edge feminine look with ancient motifs and dressed thousands for the Athens Olympics.

name: Lotte Reiniger
headline: Overlooked No More: Lotte Reiniger, Animator Who Created Magic With Scissors and Paper
abstract: Even before Disney, Reiniger told fanciful stories in animated films with her hand-cut paper silhouettes.

name: Elijah Cummings
headline: Elijah Cummings, Powerful Democrat Who Investigated Trump, Dies at 68
abstract: A son of sharecroppers, he fought tirelessly for his hometown, Baltimore, and became a key figure in the impeachment investigation of President Trump.

name: Alicia Alonso
headline: Alicia Alonso, Star of Cuba’s National Ballet, Dies at 98
abstract: A ballerina of unusual range and power, she continued to dance into her 70s despite chronic vision problems.

name: Charles Jencks
headline: Charles Jencks, 80, Dies; Helped Define Postmodern Architecture
abstract: His writings announced the death of Modernism, and the public spaces he designed were full of adventurous shapes and ideas.

name: Lee Botts
headline: Lee Botts, Champion of the Great Lakes, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Her environmental work touched practically every drop of water and every mile of shoreline in the Great Lakes basin and educated numerous people in its ecology.

name: Ginny NiCarthy
profession: Author of Guide for Battered Women
headline: Ginny NiCarthy, 92, Author of Guide for Battered Women, Dies
abstract: Her book became a standard reference for women suffering abuse in the home. “What did you do right today?” it asked, calling for a daily checklist.

name: Sara Danius
profession: First Woman to Head Nobel Literature Committee
headline: Sara Danius, 57, Dies; First Woman to Head Nobel Literature Committee
abstract: She led the deliberations to grant Bob Dylan the Nobel. When she was ousted after a sex scandal in which she was not involved, thousands rallied to her defense.

name: Mark Hurd
headline: Mark Hurd, Co-Chief Executive of Oracle, Is Dead at 62
abstract: Mr. Hurd, who previously ran Hewlett-Packard and other technology businesses, had stepped aside last month from Oracle for health reasons.

name: Bill Macy
headline: Bill Macy, a Memorable Sitcom Foil on ‘Maude,’ Dies at 97
abstract: After years of stage roles, Mr. Macy became a TV star in the 1970s as Walter, the harried husband of Bea Arthur’s larger-than-life title character.

name: Dorothea Buck
profession: Nazi Victim and Voice for Mentally Ill
headline: Dorothea Buck, 102, Dies; Nazi Victim and Voice for Mentally Ill
abstract: After a forced sterilization at 19, she became first a sculptor and then an advocate for more humane psychiatric care in modern Germany and beyond.

name: Samuel Hynes
headline: Samuel Hynes, Professor Whose Books Taught Lessons of War, Dies at 95
abstract: He wrote about Yeats and Auden, but as a former pilot in World War II, he was best known for exploring the reality of battle.

name: Kate Braverman
profession: Wrote of Women on the Margins
headline: Kate Braverman, Who Wrote of Women on the Margins, Dies at 70
abstract: Her novels, short stories and poetry were dense with lush and spellbinding imagery. As a teacher, one former student said, “She lived and died by the word.”

name: William G. Milliken
profession: Michigan Governor in a Transformative Era
headline: William G. Milliken, Michigan Governor in a Transformative Era, Dies at 97
abstract: A moderate Republican and the longest-serving governor in the state’s history, he led Michigan, an ailing industrial bastion, as it embraced technology and environmental quality.

name: Nick Tosches
headline: Nick Tosches, 69, Fiery Music Writer and Biographer, Dies
abstract: He brought a brash style to coverage of the rock world in the late 1960s and ’70s, then applied similar skills to novels and books on Dean Martin and Sonny Liston.

name: Paul Polak
profession: Entrepreneur for Those Living on $2 a Day
headline: Paul Polak, Entrepreneur for Those Living on $2 a Day, Dies at 86
abstract: A former psychiatrist and real-estate speculator turned to helping the poor make money by selling foot pumps, charcoal and clean water.

name: Thomas D’Alesandro
profession: Ex-Mayor of Baltimore and Pelosis Brother
headline: Thomas D’Alesandro, 90, Ex-Mayor of Baltimore and Pelosi’s Brother, Dies
abstract: He was elected president of the Baltimore City Council in 1963 before serving as mayor from 1967 to 1971.

name: Scotty Bowers
profession: Wrote of Providing Sex to Stars
headline: Scotty Bowers, Who Wrote of Providing Sex to Stars, Dies at 96
abstract: His 2012 book, “Full Service,” told scandalous tales about Katharine Hepburn, Spencer Tracy and countless others using his sexual referral business.

name: Sam Bobrick
headline: Sam Bobrick, ‘Saved by the Bell’ Creator, Is Dead at 87
abstract: A television mainstay, he was also a playwright. His best-known play, “Norman, Is That You?,” flopped on Broadway but went on to international success.

name: Andrés Gimeno
headline: Andrés Gimeno, Who Broke French Open Age Mark, Dies at 82
abstract: With an aggressive forehand and an arsenal of lobs, drop shots and slices, he was one of Spain’s most prominent tennis players and the oldest man to win a singles title at the French Open.

name: Matthew Wong
headline: Matthew Wong, Painter on Cusp of Fame, Dies at 35
abstract: Mr. Wong, who had Tourette’s syndrome and depression, drew wide acclaim for his first solo show in New York just last year.

name: Michael Armstrong
profession: Led Knapp Probe of Police Corruption
headline: Michael Armstrong, 86, Dies; Led Knapp Probe of Police Corruption
abstract: He was chief counsel to the New York commission formed after Frank Serpico’s revelations about systemic graft and the department’s lax response.

name: Michael Armstrong
headline: Michael Armstrong, Who Published a Local Brooklyn Paper, Dies at 79
abstract: Active in politics, he was best known as publisher of The Phoenix Newspaper. He and his wife, Dnynia Armstrong, 80, died of the coronavirus a month apart.

name: Raymond Leppard
headline: Raymond Leppard, Versatile Maestro Who Led Baroque Revival, Dies at 92
abstract: After beginning as a 17th-century specialist, Mr. Leppard became a conductor with a broad repertory, leading the Indianapolis Symphony for 14 years.

name: Willie Brown
profession: Hall of Fame Defensive Back With Raiders
headline: Willie Brown, Hall of Fame Defensive Back With Raiders, Dies at 78
abstract: Named to nine Pro Bowls, he helped the Raiders win Super Bowl XI in 1977 with a memorable interception that became a 75-yard touchdown.

name: Georgette Elgey
profession: Wrote Epic History of Postwar France
headline: Georgette Elgey, 90, Dies; Wrote Epic History of Postwar France
abstract: A former journalist, she spent nearly 50 years producing an acclaimed six-volume work on the Fourth Republic. Her own life held plenty of drama of its own.

name: Ray Santos
headline: Ray Santos, a Pillar of Latin Jazz, Is Dead at 90
abstract: After playing saxophone with Machito, Tito Puente and Tito Rodriguez, he wrote arrangements for Linda Ronstadt and the movie “The Mambo Kings.”

name: Sanmao
headline: Overlooked No More: Sanmao, ‘Wandering Writer’ Who Found Her Voice in the Desert
abstract: Her book, “Stories of the Sahara,” has endured for generations of young Taiwanese and Chinese women yearning for independence from conservative social norms.

name: Hildegard Bachert
profession: Championed Klimt, Schiele and Grandma Moses
headline: Hildegard Bachert, 98, Dies; Championed Klimt, Schiele and Grandma Moses
abstract: In her 78 years at the Galerie St. Etienne in Manhattan, she promoted German and Austrian Expressionists as well as the celebrated American folk artist.

name: Ingo Maurer
profession: Designer Known as a Poet of Light
headline: Ingo Maurer, Designer Known as a Poet of Light, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Maurer’s wonky fascination with technology led to lamps he made out of scribbled memos, tea strainers and incandescent bulbs with feathered wings.

name: Woodie Flowers
headline: Woodie Flowers, Who Made Science a Competitive Sport, Dies at 75
abstract: His hands-on methods of teaching mechanical engineering at M.I.T. made him a star on campus (and on PBS) and led to student contests on a global scale.

name: Nene Pimentel
profession: Filipino Politician Stood Up to Marcos
headline: Nene Pimentel, 85, Dies; Filipino Politician Stood Up to Marcos
abstract: Aquilino Pimentel Jr. helped end the dictatorship of Ferdinand Marcos as an organizer of the 1986 People Power Revolution.

name: John Mbiti
headline: John Mbiti, 87, Dies; Punctured Myths About African Religions
abstract: A theologian and an Anglican priest, he argued that traditional African religions deserved the same respect as Christianity, Islam, Judaism and Buddhism.

name: Leyna Gabriele
headline: Leyna Gabriele, 95, Dies; Soprano Who Sang in the First ‘Baby Doe’
abstract: Her performance in an opera about greed in the Old West won her a loyal following. She also sang for celebrities’ suppers at a nightclub in Manhattan.

name: Marta Kurtag
headline: Marta Kurtag Dies at 92, Sundering a Profound Musical Partnership
abstract: She worked closely with her husband, the composer Gyorgy Kurtag, as a performer, muse and critic and was also deeply involved in his writing.

name: Maurice Nadjari
headline: Maurice Nadjari Dies at 95; Crusading, and Criticized, Prosecutor
abstract: He was hailed by many for zealously pursuing corruption in New York’s criminal justice system, but others, including the courts, said he often went too far.

name: Emilio Nicolas Sr.
headline: Emilio Nicolas Sr., 88, a Creator of Univision, Dies
abstract: Mr. Nicolas and four other investors expanded a single San Antonio television station into what became a Spanish-language broadcasting juggernaut.

name: Bernie Parrish
headline: Bernie Parrish, All-Pro Cornerback Who Took on the N.F.L., Dies at 83
abstract: A hard-hitting player who defended players’ rights, Parrish suffered from a cognitive decline late in life, presumably from concussions.

name: Leroy Johnson
headline: Leroy Johnson, Barrier-Breaking Georgia Politician, Dies at 91
abstract: In 1962, he became the first black candidate elected to the State Senate since Reconstruction. But his influence extended farther, as Muhammad Ali found out.

name: E.A. Carmean
profession: Forsook a Life in Art for the Church
headline: E.A. Carmean,Who Forsook a Life in Art for the Church, Dies at 74
abstract: An expert on European and American modernism, he was most notably the founding curator of the National Gallery’s department of 20th-century art.

name: Don Valentine
headline: Don Valentine, Founder of Sequoia Capital, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Valentine’s venture capital firm, established in 1972, helped cement Silicon Valley as a hub for technology companies.

name: Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi
profession: ISIS Leader Known for His Brutality
headline: Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, ISIS Leader Known for His Brutality, Is Dead at 48
abstract: President Trump announced the death of al-Baghdadi, who transformed the Islamic State into a global terrorist network that conquered territory the size of Britain and directed horrific attacks in the West.

name: John Conyers Jr.
headline: John Conyers Jr., Longest-Serving African-American in Congressional History, Dies at 90
abstract: One of the most liberal members of Congress, he resigned after two women accused him of making unwelcome sexual advances.

name: Robert Evans
headline: Robert Evans, a Maverick Producer of Hollywood Classics, Dies at 89
abstract: He was a force behind masterworks like “The Godfather” and “Chinatown,” and his own story — of unlikely success and drug-fueled decline — was the stuff of legend.

name: Kay Hagan
headline: Kay Hagan, Former North Carolina Senator, Dies at 66
abstract: A Democrat, she served one term after defeating Elizabeth Dole. She was found to have a tick-borne virus in 2016.

name: John T. Tate
profession: Familiar Name in the World of Numbers
headline: John T. Tate, Familiar Name in the World of Numbers, Dies at 94
abstract: Many of his explanations of fundamental ideas now bear his name, a much-honored one among mathematicians.

name: Vladimir Bukovsky
profession: Revered Soviet Dissident and Putin Critic
headline: Vladimir Bukovsky, Revered Soviet Dissident and Putin Critic, Dies at 76
abstract: Even in exile, a former Soviet prisoner kept up his attacks on the Kremlin under both the Communists and Putin. But disputed child pornography charges marred his reputation.

name: Robert Provine
headline: Robert Provine, an Authority on Laughter, Is Dead at 76
abstract: A psychology professor, he set about trying to understand what triggers giggles and guffaws and wrote a definitive book on the subject. He could also make you laugh.

name: Paul Barrere
profession: Longtime Member of the Band Little Feat
headline: Paul Barrere, Longtime Member of the Band Little Feat, Dies at 71
abstract: A guitarist and singer, Mr. Barrere also wrote or co-wrote some of the critically acclaimed band’s best-known songs.

name: Sadako Ogata
profession: First Woman to Lead U.N. Refugee Agency
headline: Sadako Ogata, First Woman to Lead U.N. Refugee Agency, Dies at 92
abstract: Appointed to the position in 1991, she oversaw refugee operations at a time of ravaging conflict in the former Yugoslavia, Rwanda, Iraq and other regions.

name: Meyer Ackerman
headline: Meyer Ackerman, 96, Whose Theaters Were Loved by Cinephiles, Dies
abstract: His single-screen cinemas in and around New York brought foreign and other hard-to-find films to hungry audiences.

name: Al Bianchi
profession: Pro Basketball Coach and Knicks G.M
headline: Al Bianchi, Pro Basketball Coach and Knicks G.M., Dies at 87
abstract: He made his N.B.A. debut as a player in 1956, oversaw a promising but short-lived revival of the Knicks in the 1980s and remained active into the 21st century.

name: Chou Wen-chung
headline: Chou Wen-chung, Composer and Calligrapher in Sound, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Chou taught the leading Chinese composers of the day and was an assistant to the modernist master Edgard Varèse, whose legacy he tended.

name: Huang Yong Ping
profession: His Art Saw a World of Power Struggles
headline: Huang Yong Ping, 65, Dies; His Art Saw a World of Power Struggles
abstract: His startling conceptual pieces (in one case using live creatures) commented on humanity, challenged conventional notions of art and sought to erase the artist’s ego.

name: John Witherspoon
profession: Actor in Friday and Other Movies
headline: John Witherspoon, Actor in ‘Friday’ and Other Movies, Dies at 77
abstract: Mr. Witherspoon, who started out as a stand-up comedian, was best known for his role as Ice Cube’s father in the “Friday” franchise. He was also seen on “The Wayans Bros.” and many other TV shows.

name: Rolando Panerai
headline: Rolando Panerai, Renowned Baritone and Callas Collaborator, Dies at 95
abstract: In a career that spanned more than six decades, he appeared in landmark performances and made classic recordings with Maria Callas and other opera legends.

name: Ed Cray
profession: Biographer of Woody Guthrie and Earl Warren
headline: Ed Cray, Biographer of Woody Guthrie and Earl Warren, Dies at 86
abstract: A folklorist and journalism professor at U.S.C., he also profiled George C. Marshall, Levi Strauss and the serial killer Juan Corona.

name: Olive Morris
headline: Overlooked No More: How Olive Morris Fought for Black Women’s Rights in Britain
abstract: In the 27 years she was alive, Morris raised awareness of inequalities by traveling, writing, organizing protests and setting up support groups.

name: Jonathan Gradess
headline: Jonathan Gradess, Legal Defender of the Poor, Dies at 72
abstract: For nearly 40 years, he opposed the death penalty and headed a New York group of lawyers that protected indigent suspects and fought for veterans.

name: Kadri Gopalnath
profession: Brought the Saxophone to Indian Music
headline: Kadri Gopalnath, 69, Dies; Brought the Saxophone to Indian Music
abstract: Drawn to an instrument that sounded exotic to him, he became one of the most prominent classical musicians in India.

name: Ron Fairly
headline: Ron Fairly, Dodger Star Turned Broadcaster, Dies at 81
abstract: In his 20-year playing career, he was on three World Series championship teams. After his playing days, he spent more than 20 years at the microphone.

name: Jennifer Davis
headline: Jennifer Davis, 85, Dies; Led Divestment Effort Over Apartheid
abstract: After leaving South Africa, she pressed colleges, churches, unions, philanthropies and others to unload their stock in companies profiting from a racist system.

name: Bernard Slade
headline: Bernard Slade, 89, Dies; ‘Partridge Family’ Creator and Playwright
abstract: His “Same Time, Next Year” ran for years on Broadway, was made into a movie and is often described as one of the most-produced plays in the world.

name: Barry Frank
headline: Barry Frank Dies at 87; Sports Agent, Negotiator and Programmer
abstract: Mr. Frank juggled several roles in a long career: He represented sportscasters, created TV shows and negotiated rights deals.

name: Sheldon Breiner
headline: Sheldon Breiner, 82, Dies; Used Magnetism for Explorations
abstract: He developed the techniques he used to help locate sunken submarines and enormous stone heads, as well as early applications for artificial intelligence.

name: Victoria Braithwaite
headline: Victoria Braithwaite, Researcher Who Said Fish Feel Pain, Dies at 52
abstract: In two papers and a book, Dr. Braithwaite made the case that fish react to unpleasant stimuli and argued that they be treated humanely.

name: Joseph Flannery
headline: Joseph Flannery, Who Turned Uniroyal Around, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Flannery took over as chief executive in 1980, when the company was in its “darkest hour.” He then fended off a hostile takeover bid by Carl Icahn.

name: Enriqueta Basilio
profession: First Woman to Light Olympic Flame
headline: Enriqueta Basilio, 71, Dies; First Woman to Light Olympic Flame
abstract: She was a 20-year-old sprinter when she made history by lighting the caldron at the Summer Games in Mexico City in 1968.

name: Azam Taleghani
headline: Azam Taleghani, Defiant Would-Be President of Iran, Dies at 76
abstract: A dissident politician and women’s rights advocate, she sought repeatedly to be accepted as a presidential candidate but each time was denied.

name: Walter Mercado
profession: Celebrity Astrologer for Millions of Latinos
headline: Walter Mercado, Celebrity Astrologer for Millions of Latinos, Dies
abstract: For years, he kept Latino families glued to their televisions as he dramatically revealed their futures, as foretold by the stars.

name: Brian Tarantina
profession: Actor on The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel
headline: Brian Tarantina, Actor on ‘The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel,’ Dies at 60
abstract: He played a comedy club M.C. on the Emmy-winning show. A New York-bred actor, he also had roles on the stage, in movies and in a soap opera.

name: Ann Crumb
headline: Ann Crumb, Who Starred in ‘Aspects of Love,’ Is Dead at 69
abstract: She was also nominated for a Tony for her performance in the title role of “Anna Karenina” and was a member of the original cast of “Les Misérables.”

name: Al Burton
profession: Sitcom Producer With an Eye for Youth Culture
headline: Al Burton, 91, Dies; Sitcom Producer With an Eye for Youth Culture
abstract: He began his career with a show about teenagers, then helped get “Mary Hartman, Mary Hartman” and “The Facts of Life” onto the air.

name: Rudy Boesch
headline: Rudy Boesch, SEAL and ‘Survivor’ Star, Is Dead at 91
abstract: An ex-Navy man, he was the oldest, and probably bluntest, castaway ever to appear on CBS’s popular reality show, becoming a Season 1 fan favorite.

name: William B. Branch
headline: William B. Branch, Playwright of the Black Experience, Dies at 92
abstract: An ill-treated war veteran, Frederick Douglass, colonial oppression: Mr. Branch’s Off Broadway work on race ranged widely. He also made a mark in TV.

name: Marya Columbia
headline: Marya Columbia, Whose Music Soothed on 9/11, Dies at 63
abstract: She performed at St. Paul’s Chapel but was told she could not collect health benefits as a “responder” after developing cancer years later.

name: Ernest J. Gaines
profession: Author of The Autobiography of Miss Jane Pittman
headline: Ernest J. Gaines, Author of ‘The Autobiography of Miss Jane Pittman,’ Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr. Gaines chronicled the lives and struggles of black people in the South before the civil rights era; “The Autobiography of Miss Jane Pittman” is his best-known work.

name: Jerome Wilson
profession: Key in Revamping New York Divorce Law
headline: Jerome Wilson, Key in Revamping New York Divorce Law, Dies at 88
abstract: As a legislator in 1966, he led a commission that pushed to broaden the legal grounds for divorce. New York had been the last state to recognize only adultery.

name: U Tun Lwin
headline: U Tun Lwin, Who Warned of Deadly Myanmar Cyclone, Dies at 71
abstract: “The people’s weatherman” said his forecasts had been played down by the government. At least 140,000 people perished in one of the most calamitous storms in recorded history.

name: Narayana Reddy
headline: Narayana Reddy, YouTube Star as ‘Grandpa Kitchen,’ Has Died
abstract: Mr. Reddy, a cook in India, started a YouTube channel in 2017 featuring videos of him preparing huge portions of food for children. His channel has more than six million subscribers.

name: Marie Laforêt
headline: Marie Laforêt, French Actress and Singer, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Known as “the girl with the golden eyes,” she was seen in dozens of feature films and on television and sold more than 35 million records.

name: Annie Londonderry
headline: Overlooked No More: Annie Londonderry, Who Traveled the World by Bicycle
abstract: She cycled away from her Boston home and into stardom, leaving a husband and three small children for a journey that came to symbolize women’s independence.

name: James Stern
headline: James Stern, Who Disrupted a Racist Group, Dies at 55
abstract: A black former preacher with an eventful past, Mr. Stern talked a virulent neo-Nazi into signing his organization over to him.

name: Ray Jenkins
headline: Ray Jenkins, Newspaperman Who Covered Civil Rights Era, Dies at 89
abstract: He had a “ringside seat to history” in the South, befriending Martin Luther King Jr. and triggering a landmark First Amendment case that went to the Supreme Court.

name: Gert Boyle
profession: Sportswear Chief Billed as One Tough Mother
headline: Gert Boyle, 95, Dies; Sportswear Chief Billed as ‘One Tough Mother’
abstract: She took over her family’s company, Columbia Sportswear, when her husband died and saw it flourish, becoming its flinty public face in ads.

name: Gay Byrne
profession: Tackled Taboos as Irelands TV Host
headline: Gay Byrne, Who Tackled Taboos as Ireland’s TV Host, Dies at 85
abstract: A revered figure, he mixed serious discussion on matters like sex abuse and contraception with lighter fare on his long-running “Late Late Show.”

name: Louis Eppolito
profession: Police Officer Turned Mob Hit Man
headline: Louis Eppolito, Police Officer Turned Mob Hit Man, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Eppolito and his partner, Stephen Caracappa, were convicted of taking part in eight gangland murders in New York’s “Mafia Cop” scandal.

name: Marcelle Ninio
profession: Spy for Israel Imprisoned in Egypt
headline: Marcelle Ninio, Spy for Israel Imprisoned in Egypt, Dies at 89
abstract: She was the only woman in an espionage ring of about a dozen Egyptians that engineered bombings. Their mission did not go well.

name: Gillian Jagger
headline: Gillian Jagger, Sculptor Whose Medium Was Nature, Dies at 88
abstract: Her sculptures, which often incorporated tree trunks and animal carcasses, emphasized commonality and connection between humans, animals and the earth.

name: Peter Collier
headline: Peter Collier, Author and Leading Conservative Voice, Dies at 80
abstract: He and David Horowitz wrote well-regarded biographies of prominent families. They also drew attention for their ideological shift from left to right.

name: Norman Myers
headline: Norman Myers Dies at 85; Sounded Early Alarm on Environment
abstract: He lobbied governments and wrote books, papers and articles to alert the public to looming disasters like mass extinction well before they were common knowledge.

name: Maria Perego
headline: Maria Perego, Topo Gigio’s Creator, Dies at 95
abstract: The mouse puppet that she made in the late 1950s in Italy became a worldwide phenomenon, with the help of “The Ed Sullivan Show.”

name: Robert Norris
headline: Robert Norris, Marlboro Man Who Didn’t Smoke, Dies at 90
abstract: He gave up his role in the popular tobacco advertising campaign after 14 years, saying he was setting a bad example for his children.

name: William Hughes
headline: William Hughes, Congressman and Ambassador, Dies at 87
abstract: He represented New Jersey’s Second District for 20 years, then was ambassador to Panama in a crucial period.

name: Stephen Dixon
headline: Stephen Dixon, Prolific Writer of Experimental Fiction, Dies at 83
abstract: The author of 18 novels and hundreds of short stories, he never found fame or big sales. But his idiosyncratic storytelling drew praise.

name: Bernard J. Tyson
headline: Bernard J. Tyson, Chairman of Health Care Giant, Dies at 60
abstract: After rising up its ladder, he ran Kaiser Permanente, the admired California organization that integrates hospitals, clinics and health insurance.

name: Robert Freeman
headline: Robert Freeman, Photographer of Beatles Albums, Dies at 82
abstract: His covers for “With the Beatles,” “Rubber Soul” and other records helped define the group’s imagery early in their career.

name: Frank Giles
profession: Editor Snared in Hitler Diaries Hoax
headline: Frank Giles, 100, Editor Snared in ‘Hitler Diaries’ Hoax, Is Dead
abstract: At The Sunday Times of London, he learned at the last minute that the diaries were fake, but the paper’s owner, Rupert Murdoch, ordered them published.

name: Jan Erik Kongshaug
headline: Jan Erik Kongshaug, Maestro of Recorded Sound, Dies at 75
abstract: The techniques he developed with Manfred Eicher, the founder of the ECM label, had a major influence on the recordings of Pat Metheny, Keith Jarrett and many others.

name: Zeke Bratkowski
profession: Packer Quarterback but Not a Starr
headline: Zeke Bratkowski, Packer Quarterback but Not a Starr, Dies at 88
abstract: He had all the tools to lead a team and often excelled on the field, but he was fated to serve as the understudy to the future Hall of Famer Bart Starr.

name: Rick Ludwin
headline: Rick Ludwin, NBC Executive Who Championed ‘Seinfeld,’ Dies at 71
abstract: He was also a veteran of the late-night wars and presided over the difficult changeover of “Tonight Show” hosts from Johnny Carson to Jay Leno.

name: Shoji Sadao
headline: Shoji Sadao, Quiet Hand Behind Two Visionaries, Dies at 92
abstract: An architect, Mr. Sadao translated the ideas of Buckminster Fuller and Isamu Noguchi to the real world.

name: Wayne Bardin
headline: Dr. Wayne Bardin, 85, Innovative Researcher on Birth Control, Dies
abstract: He helped develop long-acting implanted contraceptive devices — like Norplant, Jadelle and Mirena — used by millions of women around the world.

name: Noel Ignatiev
headline: Noel Ignatiev, 78, Persistent Voice Against White Privilege, Dies
abstract: In the journal Race Traitor and in a provocative book, Dr. Ignatiev argued that the white race should, in a sense, be abolished.

name: Carrie Saxon Perry
headline: Carrie Saxon Perry, Barrier-Breaking Mayor, Dies at 87
abstract: The first African-American woman to run a major New England city, Hartford, she died a year ago, but the death was reported only recently.

name: Carol Brightman
profession: Profiled a Notable Writer and a Notable Band
headline: Carol Brightman, 80, Dies; Profiled a Notable Writer and a Notable Band
abstract: After publishing a biography of Mary McCarthy, she changed course and plunged into the world of the Grateful Dead and the group’s devoted fans.

name: Irv Noren
headline: Irv Noren, a Bridge Between DiMaggio and Mantle, Dies at 94
abstract: After two strong seasons with the Washington Senators, he joined the Yankees to fill an outfield gap. He won three World Series rings with the team.

name: Werner G. Doehner
headline: Werner G. Doehner, Last Survivor of the Hindenburg, Dies at 90
abstract: He was 8 and traveling with his family when the German airship caught fire and crashed in New Jersey.

name: Harrison Dillard
headline: Harrison Dillard, World’s Best Hurdler in the 1940s, Dies at 96
abstract: A four-time Olympic gold medal winner, he failed to qualify in the hurdles at the 1948 Olympic trials, but won gold in the 100-meter dash.

name: Bogaletch Gebre
headline: Bogaletch Gebre, Foe of Female Genital Mutilation, Dies at 66
abstract: Called “the woman who began the rebellion of Ethiopian women,” she helped thwart a barbaric practice that she had suffered and that had cost her sister’s life.

name: Terry O’Neill
headline: Terry O’Neill, Photographer of the Famous, Is Dead at 81
abstract: On an early assignment he shot a new group called the Beatles. He went on to photograph, among many others, Faye Dunaway — whom he later married.

name: Kehinde Lijadu
headline: Kehinde Lijadu, 71, Outspoken Nigerian Songwriter, Is Dead
abstract: As the Lijadu Sisters, she and her identical twin, Taiwo, sang about injustice and hope and had a string of hit records in the 1970s.

name: Vera Clemente
headline: Vera Clemente, Flame-Keeping Widow of Baseball’s Roberto, Dies at 78
abstract: After her husband’s death in a plane crash in 1972, she carried on his humanitarian and philanthropic legacy.

name: Mustapha Matura
headline: Mustapha Matura, Caribbean Playwright in London, Dies at 79
abstract: His often satirical plays spoke for an alienated West Indian population in postwar Britain and for the people he left behind in Trinidad and Tobago.

name: Raymond Poulidor
headline: Raymond Poulidor, Cycling’s ‘Eternal Second,’ Is Dead at 83
abstract: He never won the Tour de France, cycling’s most important race, but a series of near misses made him a favorite of French fans.

name: Pauline Boty
headline: Overlooked No More: Pauline Boty, Rebellious Pop Artist
abstract: With her daring feminist art and freewheeling lifestyle, Boty personified the cultural scene known as Swinging London.

name: Walter J. Minton
headline: Walter J. Minton, Publisher Who Defied Censors, Dies at 96
abstract: As president of Putnam’s, he broke ground with sexually explicit works like “Lolita” and “Fanny Hill,” worked with top authors and scored many best sellers.

name: Thich Tri Quang
headline: Thich Tri Quang, 95, Galvanizing Monk in South Vietnam, Dies
abstract: An orator with “eyes of a tiger,” he helped bring down American-backed governments in Saigon during the Vietnam War and pressed for democratic reforms.

name: William Loren Katz
headline: William Loren Katz, Historian of African-Americans, Dies at 92
abstract: He documented the often overlooked contributions of black people in books for young adults, helping to refashion social studies curriculums across the country.

name: Branko Lustig
headline: Branko Lustig, 87, Dies; Holocaust Survivor Turned Film Producer
abstract: Mr. Lustig’s experiences as a concentration camp inmate informed his work on “Schindler’s List,” for which he won an Academy Award.

name: Tom Spurgeon
headline: Tom Spurgeon, Who Surveyed the Comic Book World, Dies at 50
abstract: A reporter, editor and author, he co-wrote a biography of Stan Lee, oversaw a comics festival and started an award-winning website.

name: Wat Misaka
profession: First Nonwhite in Modern Pro Basketball
headline: Wat Misaka, 95, First Nonwhite in Modern Pro Basketball, Dies
abstract: A son of Japanese immigrants, he starred for the University of Utah on national championship teams before joining the Knicks for a short but history-making run.

name: Jake Burton Carpenter
profession: Ushered in Snowboarding as a Sport
headline: Jake Burton Carpenter, Who Ushered in Snowboarding as a Sport, Dies at 65
abstract: After his fascination with the Snurfer, a crude version of a snowboard created in the 1960s, he built the first successful snowboard company.

name: Michael J. Pollard
profession: Character Actor in Bonnie and Clyde
headline: Michael J. Pollard, Character Actor in ‘Bonnie and Clyde,’ Dies at 80
abstract: A familiar face in movies and on television, he rose to fame in 1967 as the outlaw couple’s dimwitted accomplice, earning an Oscar nomination.

name: Guido Badano
profession: Officer in the Andrea Doria Crash
headline: Guido Badano, Officer in the Andrea Doria Crash, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Badano scrambled to rescue passengers and fellow crew members when two ocean liners collided in 1956, resulting in the deaths of 51 people.

name: Gahan Wilson
headline: Gahan Wilson, Vividly Macabre Cartoonist, Dies at 89
abstract: His work — seen in National Lampoon, Playboy, The New Yorker and other magazines — was full of visual surprises and black humor.

name: Fred Cox
profession: Vikings Kicker and an Inventor of Nerf Football
headline: Fred Cox, Vikings Kicker and an Inventor of Nerf Football, Dies at 80
abstract: He was a mainstay of a Vikings team that lost four Super Bowls and, while playing, helped create a squeezable foam toy that brought him decades of royalties.

name: Mary Previte
profession: Grateful Survivor of a Concentration Camp
headline: Mary Previte, Grateful Survivor of a Concentration Camp, Dies at 87
abstract: Rescued in Japanese-occupied China, she sought out her saviors a half-century later. In New Jersey, she turned a youth detention center into a national model.

name: Dorothy Seiberling
headline: Dorothy Seiberling, Influential Arts Editor, Dies at 97
abstract: She championed Jackson Pollock and Georgia O’Keeffe and helped shape public opinion about the 20th century’s foremost avant-garde artists.

name: Alfred E. Smith IV
headline: Alfred E. Smith IV, 68, M.C. of Catholic Charity Roast, Dies
abstract: A great-grandson of a New York governor, he hosted an annual fund-raising dinner that draws the state’s power elite and White House hopefuls.

name: Ethel Johnson
headline: Ethel Johnson, Early Black Wrestling Star, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Beginning in the 1950s, she and her two athletic sisters helped expand the demographics of the ring.

name: Henry Sobel
headline: Rabbi Henry Sobel, 75, Dies; Defied Brazil’s Military Rulers
abstract: The leader of the largest liberal Jewish congregation in Latin America, he took a stand when a journalist was killed by his torturers in 1975.

name: Barbara Hillary
profession: Trailblazer on Top (and Bottom) of the World
headline: Barbara Hillary, 88, Trailblazer on Top (and Bottom) of the World, Dies
abstract: A retired nurse, she was the first black woman to reach both poles, doing so in her 70s after deciding that she wanted a little adventure in her life.

name: Ethel Paley
headline: Ethel Paley, Champion of Nursing Home Patients, Dies at 99
abstract: Well into her own advanced age, she guided nursing home residents and their surrogates in navigating a labyrinthine and sometimes abusive health care system.

name: Dorothy Seymour Mills
headline: Dorothy Seymour Mills, Uncredited Baseball Historian, Dies at 91
abstract: She collaborated with her first husband on an acclaimed three-volume history of the game. But it took 50 years for her contribution to be fully acknowledged.

name: Jonathan Miller
profession: Bold Director of Theater and Opera
headline: Jonathan Miller, Bold Director of Theater and Opera, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Known for his radical restagings of classic works, Mr. Miller was also a doctor who periodically left the stage to practice medicine.

name: Clive James
profession: Literary Critic Took His Wit to TV
headline: Clive James Dies at 80; Literary Critic Took His Wit to TV
abstract: A transplanted Australian, he had a zest for the knockout punch as he sparred with all things cultural, creating a pungent comic persona on British television.

name: Japanese Maple
headline: ‘Japanese Maple’ by Clive James
abstract: Clive James’s 2014 poem is a poignant meditation on his impending death. He has died at 80 in England.

name: George Clements
headline: George Clements, Priest and Activist, Is Dead at 87
abstract: He worked to advance black causes within the Catholic Church. In 1981 he drew national coverage and consternation in the church when he adopted a child.

name: William Ruckelshaus
headline: William Ruckelshaus, Who Quit in ‘Saturday Night Massacre,’ Dies at 87
abstract: As deputy attorney general he refused Nixon’s order to fire the special prosecutor Archibald Cox in the Watergate scandal. He was earlier the E.P.A.’s first leader.

name: Lillian Harris Dean
profession: Culinary Entrepreneur Known as Pig Foot Mary
headline: Overlooked No More: Lillian Harris Dean, Culinary Entrepreneur Known as ‘Pig Foot Mary’
abstract: From a baby carriage on a Manhattan street corner, she sold Southern food to African-Americans who, like her, had moved to New York during the Great Migration.

name: Evelyne Daitz
headline: Evelyne Daitz Dies at 83; Ran a Vital Photography Gallery
abstract: She took over the Witkin in Manhattan after the death of its founder and kept it going for 15 years.

name: Frank Biondi
headline: Frank Biondi Dies at 74; Headed Major Entertainment Companies
abstract: Over his career Mr. Biondi was chief executive at HBO, Viacom, Universal Studios and the television and movie division of Coca-Cola.

name: Marilyn Yalom
headline: Marilyn Yalom, Feminist Author and Historian, Is Dead at 87
abstract: In books about the history of wives, the history of the breast and other subjects, she examined how cultural forces led over time to feminist thinking.

name: James Holloway III
headline: James Holloway III, 97, Dies; Navy Chief Under Three Presidents
abstract: A combat veteran of three wars, he led an inquiry that criticized the planning behind a failed 1980 mission to rescue hostages in Iran.

name: Garth C. Reeves
headline: Garth C. Reeves, 100, Activist Newspaper Publisher, Is Dead
abstract: He advanced the cause of civil rights through the venerable Miami Times, the city’s most influential black newspaper, which his father founded in 1923.

name: Robert F.X. Sillerman
headline: Robert F.X. Sillerman Dies at 71; Built Entertainment Empires
abstract: A brash figure in the financial pages, he bought and sold lucrative radio and concert businesses and controlled the Elvis Presley estate.

name: Marion McClinton
headline: Marion McClinton, Interpreter of August Wilson, Dies at 65
abstract: He directed numerous productions of Wilson plays, including two on Broadway, but some of his best work was done in regional theaters.

name: Yasuhiro Nakasone
headline: Yasuhiro Nakasone, Assertive Prime Minister of Japan, Dies at 101
abstract: He called for a stronger military and a larger global role for Japan and was one of the few Japanese leaders to win recognition on the world stage.

name: Janette Sherman
headline: Dr. Janette Sherman, 89, Early Force in Environmental Science, Dies
abstract: In one case, discovering that autoworkers shared the same diseases, she pinpointed the cause as chemicals in the factories — not, as was thought, cigarettes.

name: Seymour Siwoff
headline: Seymour Siwoff, Master of Sports Statistics, Is Dead at 99
abstract: As head of the Elias Sports Bureau, which he took over in 1952, he supervised record-keeping for baseball, football and other professional sports.

name: Irving Burgie
profession: Wrote Calypso Hits for Harry Belafonte
headline: Irving Burgie, Who Wrote Calypso Hits for Harry Belafonte, Dies at 95
abstract: He and Mr. Belafonte were behind the calypso craze of the 1950s. Mr. Burgie was also a singer, under the name Lord Burgess.

name: Marilyn Saviola
headline: Marilyn Saviola, Disability Rights Advocate, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Polio left her in a wheelchair. It also started her on a lifelong fight to change perceptions and break down real-world obstacles.

name: Michael Howard
headline: Michael Howard, Eminent British Military Historian, Dies at 97
abstract: A decorated soldier in World War II, he helped reshape the study of war and was knighted in 1986 for his academic work.

name: Shelley Morrison
headline: Shelley Morrison, ‘Will & Grace’ Actress, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Morrison’s portrayal of the memorable maid Rosario, who stood up to her socialite boss, made her a fan favorite.

name: Mariss Jansons
headline: Mariss Jansons, Who Led Top Orchestras, Dies at 76
abstract: He drew memorable performances from symphonies in Munich, Amsterdam, Oslo, Pittsburgh and elsewhere.

name: Robert K. Massie
headline: Robert K. Massie, Narrator of Russian History, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Mr. Massie wrote readable and respected biographies of Russian royals, including “Nicholas and Alexandra,” which became a movie.

name: Perry Hoffman
profession: Saw Family Support as Key to Psychiatric Care
headline: Perry Hoffman, 75, Dies; Saw Family Support as Key to Psychiatric Care
abstract: Dr. Hoffman established a family network to help people with borderline personality disorder, a support system that become a model for other conditions.

name: André Daguin
profession: Chef Made Gascony (and a Dish) Famous
headline: André Daguin Dies at 84; Chef Made Gascony (and a Dish) Famous
abstract: His menu, most notably the grilled duck breast, made a region of southwest France a required stop for traveling food lovers.

name: Gary Regan
profession: Maestro of Mixology and Cocktail Culture
headline: Gary Regan, Maestro of Mixology and Cocktail Culture, Dies at 68
abstract: A British-born son of publicans, he became a bartender in New York, a saloonkeeper, an author of 18 books and a columnist and commentator.

name: Wayne Merry
headline: Wayne Merry, Climber Who Conquered El Capitan, Dies at 88
abstract: In 1958 he and two others became the first to scale a 2,900-foot granite wall in Yosemite National Park in California that many considered practically unclimbable.

name: Allan Gerson
headline: Allan Gerson, Who Sought Justice for Terror Victims, Dies at 74
abstract: A lawyer and the son of Jewish refugees from Poland, he helped families of those killed in the Lockerbie bombing hold Libya accountable.

name: Carolyn Konheim
headline: Carolyn Konheim, Foe of All That Befouled a City, Dies at 81
abstract: Finding her sons’ clothes speckled with soot, a history teacher was transformed into an influential New York environmentalist with pollution in her sights.

name: Joe Smith
headline: Joe Smith, Career-Making Record Executive, Is Dead at 91
abstract: He spanned musical eras in presiding, all told, over three major labels, nurturing acts from Peter, Paul and Mary to the Grateful Dead to Queen.

name: Howard Cruse
headline: Howard Cruse Dies at 75; His Cartoons Explored Gay Life
abstract: He described his experiences as a gay man in a comic strip and an acclaimed semi-autobiographical graphic novel, influencing many other cartoonists.

name: Josie Rubio
profession: Wrote of Dating While Terminally Ill
headline: Josie Rubio, 42, Dies; Wrote of Dating While Terminally Ill
abstract: Her essay in The New York Times drew a wide readership; she also chronicled her life with terminal cancer in a blog, finding humor amid despair.

name: Stephen Cleobury
headline: Stephen Cleobury, Longtime Leader of Fabled Choir, Dies at 70
abstract: He led the King’s College Choir of England for 37 years, including during its famous Christmas Eve performances.

name: William E. Macaulay
headline: William E. Macaulay, 74, Booster of Tuition-Free Education, Dies
abstract: A billionaire energy investor, he gave opportunities to thousands of select City University of New York students with a $30 million gift.

name: Raeanne Rubenstein
headline: Raeanne Rubenstein, Versatile Celebrity Photographer, Dies at 74
abstract: She had a knack for capturing her subjects, whether Andy Warhol in New York or Dolly Parton in Nashville, in ways that caught their essence.

name: Jay Kriegel
headline: Jay Kriegel, a ‘New York City Patriot,’ Is Dead at 79
abstract: A former whiz kid in Lindsay’s City Hall, he became a knows-everybody “process broker” with wide reach in civic affairs, broadcasting and real estate.

name: Rose Mackenberg
headline: Overlooked No More: Rose Mackenberg, Houdini’s Secret ‘Ghost-Buster’
abstract: Working undercover for the illusionist, Mackenberg exposed phony psychics who claimed they could connect people to their dead loved ones.

name: Winston Lawson
profession: Secret Service Agent With Kennedy in Dallas
headline: Winston Lawson, 91, Secret Service Agent With Kennedy in Dallas, Dies
abstract: The advance man for the Texas trip, he rode ahead of Kennedy’s limo, helped lift the president onto a stretcher and then lived a half-century with regrets.

name: Ron Leibman
headline: Ron Leibman, Tony Winner for ‘Angels,’ Is Dead at 82
abstract: In addition to his acclaimed turn as Roy Cohn on Broadway, he was known for his work in “Norma Rae,” “Slaughterhouse-Five” and other films.

name: Juice WRLD
headline: Juice WRLD Dies at 21; Chicago Rapper Whose Star Was on the Rise
abstract: He began posting songs online while in high school. On hits like “Lucid Dreams,” he combined melodic hip-hop instincts with heavy-hearted angst.

name: Caroll Spinney
profession: Big Birds Alter Ego on Sesame Street
headline: Caroll Spinney, Big Bird’s Alter Ego on ‘Sesame Street,’ Is Dead at 85
abstract: Besides the sweet-natured giant yellow bird, he also played the misanthropic bellyacher Oscar the Grouch.

name: Marvin Goodfriend
profession: Trump Nominee to the Federal Reserve
headline: Marvin Goodfriend, Trump Nominee to the Federal Reserve, Dies at 69
abstract: He was a conservative monetary economist and a Carnegie Mellon professor who took on policy roles. His nomination lapsed after he failed to win Senate support.

name: Bump Elliott
headline: Bump Elliott, College Football Star and Coach, Dies at 94
abstract: An All-American halfback at the University of Michigan, he later coached the team and then became athletic director at the University of Iowa.

name: Donald B. Marron
headline: Donald B. Marron, Financier, Art Collector and Philanthropist, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Marron began his Wall Street career as a teenager before leading some of its most powerful firms and becoming a force at the Museum of Modern Art.

name: Margaret Lawrence
headline: Margaret Lawrence, 105, Dies; Pioneering Black Female Psychoanalyst
abstract: She overcame many hurdles, including rejection by Cornell’s medical school, which told her a black man before her “didn’t work out.” (He had died.)

name: René Auberjonois
headline: René Auberjonois, a ‘Deep Space Nine’ Star, Dies at 79
abstract: The busy character actor was also known for “Benson,” “Boston Legal” and several Broadway roles.

name: Paul A. Volcker
headline: Paul A. Volcker, Fed Chairman Who Waged War on Inflation, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Mr. Volcker helped shape American economic policy for decades, notably by leading the Federal Reserve’s brute-force campaign to subdue inflation in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Pete Frates
headline: Pete Frates, Who Promoted the Ice Bucket Challenge, Dies at 34
abstract: The former college baseball player’s involvement in the viral trend helped raise more than $100 million toward fighting A.L.S.

name: Roxette Singer Marie Fredriksson
headline: Roxette Singer Marie Fredriksson Is Dead at 61
abstract: As half of the Swedish duo, which gained fame in the 1980s and ’90s, Ms. Fredriksson was known for her powerful voice and dynamic onstage presence.

name: Fitzhugh Mullan
headline: Fitzhugh Mullan, Foe of Health Care Disparities, Dies at 77
abstract: As a doctor, he saw the inequities in the system at first hand; as a writer and administrator, he called them out.

name: Johann Baptist Metz
headline: Johann Baptist Metz, Theologian of Compassion, Dies at 91
abstract: One of the most influential Catholic theologians of the 20th century, he challenged his fellow German Catholics to face the reality of Auschwitz.

name: Yuri M. Luzhkov
profession: Mayor at Dawn of Post-Soviet Moscow
headline: Yuri M. Luzhkov, 83, Dies; Mayor at Dawn of Post-Soviet Moscow
abstract: An energetic leader, he steered the Russian capital out of its gloom, dominating Moscow’s political system while his wife became the richest woman in the country.

name: Kim Woo-choong
profession: Strove to Be Automotive Genghis Khan
headline: Kim Woo-choong, Who Strove to Be ‘Automotive Genghis Khan,’ Dies at 82
abstract: The Daewoo founder’s mad-rush corporate expansion symbolized South Korea’s rise as an Asian tiger. Daewoo’s collapse offered a bracing reality check.

name: Reinhard Bonnke
headline: Reinhard Bonnke, the ‘Billy Graham of Africa,’ Dies at 79
abstract: He was a German-born evangelist whose open-air Christian revivals drew millions of followers, many of them hoping to be healed of their afflictions.

name: Bessie Coleman
headline: Overlooked No More: Bessie Coleman, Pioneering African-American Aviatrix
abstract: In 1921 Coleman became the first black woman in the United States to earn a pilot’s license, then barnstormed around the country thrilling audiences and inspiring later generations.

name: Leonard Goldberg
headline: Leonard Goldberg, Producer of Hit TV Shows, Is Dead at 85
abstract: His partnership with Aaron Spelling gave the world “Charlie’s Angels,” “Fantasy Island” and many other series. On his own, he created “Blue Bloods.”

name: Terry de Havilland
headline: Terry de Havilland, Cobbler to the Stars, Is Dead at 81
abstract: He made python boots for Nureyev, black leather thigh-high boots for Jacqueline Onassis and platforms for Kate Moss that spelled out a vulgarity in crystals.

name: George Laurer
headline: George Laurer, Who Developed the Bar Code, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Every purchase evokes his design of the rectangular Universal Product Code. But although it became ubiquitous, he received no royalties.

name: Edna Smith Primus
headline: Edna Smith Primus, Lawyer in Pivotal Rights Case, Dies at 75
abstract: She successfully challenged a professional reprimand and in the process helped redefine free speech rights for lawyers and advocacy groups.

name: Danny Kronenfeld
headline: Danny Kronenfeld, Champion of the Homeless, Is Dead at 87
abstract: He founded a groundbreaking shelter for families and later spent 16 years in charge of the historic Henry Street Settlement.

name: William Luce
headline: William Luce, Playwright, Dies at 88; Wrote ‘Belle of Amherst’
abstract: He specialized in one-character dramas, portraying luminaries like Emily Dickinson, John Barrymore, Lillian Hellman, Zelda Fitzgerald and Isak Dinesen.

name: Richard Easton
headline: Richard Easton, Stage Veteran and Tony Winner, Dies at 86
abstract: He won theater’s top prize for his performance in “The Invention of Love,” one of numerous Broadway roles.

name: Danny Aiello
profession: Actor in Do the Right Thing
headline: Danny Aiello, Actor in ‘Do the Right Thing,’ Dies at 86
abstract: A memorable character actor on both stage and screen, Mr. Aiello won an Academy Award nomination for his role in Spike Lee’s 1989 film.

name: Elisabeth Sifton
profession: Editor and Tamer of Literary Lions
headline: Elisabeth Sifton, Editor and Tamer of Literary Lions, Dies at 80
abstract: She was also a publisher and an author whose memoir affirmed that her father, the theologian Reinhold Niebuhr, had popularized the Serenity Prayer.

name: Don McDonagh
headline: Don McDonagh, Dance Critic and Author, Dies at 87
abstract: In his reviews in The New York Times, he championed experimental choreographers emerging in the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Tony Brooker
headline: Tony Brooker, Pioneer of Computer Programming, Dies at 94
abstract: After meeting Alan Turing, Mr. Brooker went to work at the University of Manchester and wrote the programming language for the first commercial computer.

name: William McFeely
headline: William McFeely, Pulitzer-Winning Historian, Dies at 89
abstract: The author of acclaimed biographies of Ulysses S. Grant and Frederick Douglass, he also helped establish Yale’s black studies department.

name: Felix G. Rohatyn
headline: Felix G. Rohatyn, Financier Who Piloted New York’s Rescue, Dies at 91
abstract: An immigrant from war-ravaged Europe, Mr. Rohatyn reached the apex of Wall Street and the inner circles of government and commerce.

name: Richard G. Hatcher
headline: Richard G. Hatcher, Ex-Mayor of Gary, Ind., and Champion of Urban and Black Issues, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Hatcher was one of the first two black people elected in 1967 as mayor of a large American city.

name: Anna Karina
profession: Star of French New Wave Cinema
headline: Anna Karina, Star of French New Wave Cinema, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Best known for her work with Jean-Luc Godard, she also appeared in films by Visconti, Fassbinder and others, as well as pursuing a singing career and writing four novels.

name: Andrew Clements
headline: Andrew Clements, 70, Dies; Wrote Best-Selling Children’s Books
abstract: His best-known book, “Frindle,” posed a question about the nature of words: What would happen if you called a pen a frindle?

name: Goar Vartanyan
headline: Goar Vartanyan, Celebrated Soviet Spy, Dies at 93
abstract: Without her and her husband, also a Soviet spy, “the history of our world could have been different,” the Kremlin said. But her exact role remains a secret.

name: Gershon Kingsley
headline: Gershon Kingsley, Master of Electronic Sounds, Dies at 97
abstract: One of the first composers to embrace the Moog synthesizer, he gave the world the enduring instrumental hit “Pop Corn,” among many other works.

name: Frederick B. Dent
headline: Frederick B. Dent, 97, Commerce Secretary and Nixon Ally, Dies
abstract: He was a staunch defender of the president amid the administration’s Watergate crisis and later served as Gerald Ford’s trade representative.

name: Heidi Hynes
headline: Heidi Hynes, Transplanted Crusader for the Poor, Dies at 51
abstract: Dismayed by inequality and injustice, a white woman from the Midwest devoted her abbreviated career to helping poor blacks and Latinos in the Bronx.

name: Peter Snell
headline: Peter Snell, Record-Breaking Runner in the 1960s, Dies at 80
abstract: A middle-distance runner from New Zealand, he set world records in five events and won three Olympic gold medals.

name: Ken Heyman
profession: Collaborative Photographer With a Singular Eye
headline: Ken Heyman, 89, Dies; Collaborative Photographer With a Singular Eye
abstract: He traveled with the anthropologist Margaret Mead, teamed up with President Lyndon Johnson and shot for Life and Look, creating revelatory pictures.

name: Larry Heinemann
headline: Larry Heinemann, Novelist of the Vietnam War, Dies at 75
abstract: His “Paco’s Story” was the surprise winner of the National Book Award for fiction in 1987, beating books by Toni Morrison and Philip Roth.

name: John Robbins
headline: Dr. John Robbins, Developer of a Meningitis Vaccine, Dies at 86
abstract: His method of boosting immune protection in babies helped save seven million lives. But he never profited from it.

name: John Robbins
profession: Author of Diet for a New America
headline: John Robbins, Author of ‘Diet for a New America,’ Dies at 77
abstract: He walked away from his family’s hugely successful ice cream business to crusade for a plant-based diet and against cruelty to animals.

name: Earl Tucker
headline: Overlooked No More: Earl Tucker, a Dancer Known as ‘Snakehips’
abstract: Tucker was a name attraction in Harlem nightclubs in the 1920s, and his moves were echoed by Elvis Presley and Michael Jackson.

name: Rina Lazo
headline: Rina Lazo, Muralist Who Worked With Diego Rivera, Dies at 96
abstract: She got her start in the 1940s as one of Rivera’s assistants. She went on to become a celebrated artist in both Mexico and her native Guatemala.

name: Ruth Anderson
headline: Ruth Anderson, Pioneering Electronic Composer, Dies at 91
abstract: The electronic music studio Ms. Anderson founded at the City University of New York in 1968 was among the very few anywhere established by a woman.

name: Herman Boone
profession: Coach Portrayed in Remember the Titans
headline: Herman Boone, Coach Portrayed in ‘Remember the Titans,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Boone led the T.C. Williams High School Titans to a state championship in 1971. Denzel Washington portrayed him.

name: Christine Chambers
profession: Her Photos Empowered Actors of Color
headline: Christine Chambers, 39, Dies; Her Photos Empowered Actors of Color
abstract: As a photographer and a playwright, she helped document the rise of a generation of theater artists who wanted to tell their own stories their own way.

name: Thomas Elsaesser
profession: Film Scholar With a Broad View
headline: Thomas Elsaesser, Film Scholar With a Broad View, Dies at 76
abstract: An erudite German-born essayist, Mr. Elsaesser was as enthusiastic about the films of Fassbinder as he was about Hollywood melodramas.

name: Ward Just
profession: Ex-Journalist Found Larger Truths in Fiction
headline: Ward Just, 84, Dies; Ex-Journalist Found Larger Truths in Fiction
abstract: After covering the Vietnam War and Washington, Mr. Just turned to writing novels that probed American society.

name: Robert Moir
profession: His Research Changed Views on Alzheimers
headline: Robert Moir, 58, Dies; His Research Changed Views on Alzheimer’s
abstract: Dr. Moir’s radical and iconoclastic theories defied conventional views of the disease. But some scientists were ultimately won over.

name: Phase 2
headline: Phase 2, an Aerosol Art Innovator, Is Dead at 64
abstract: In the early 1970s, the dawn of what became known as hip-hop, he helped shape the art of graffiti on New York City subways. But he hated the word.

name: Randy Suess
headline: Randy Suess, Computer Bulletin Board Inventor, Dies at 74
abstract: The messaging system that he and a friend created in 1978 was a forerunner of social media services like Twitter, Facebook and YouTube.

name: Junior Johnson
headline: Junior Johnson, Good-Old-Boy Auto Racing Star, Is Dead at 88
abstract: He competed on the NASCAR circuit for 12 seasons, became a successful team owner and was one of the first inductees in the organization’s Hall of Fame.

name: Abbey Simon
headline: Abbey Simon, Masterly Pianist, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Simon, light of touch yet breathtakingly pyrotechnic, was known for his interpretations of the Romantic literature.

name: Claudine Auger
headline: Claudine Auger, James Bond’s First French Co-Star, Dies at 78
abstract: “Thunderball” was her breakthrough, and she went on to appear in movies with Alain Delon and Giancarlo Giannini. But Hollywood stardom eluded her.

name: Jeanne Guillemin
headline: Jeanne Guillemin, Who Exposed Soviet Anthrax Lab, Dies at 76
abstract: After an outbreak killed scores of people in 1979, she showed how even a tiny amount of a biological warfare agent could threaten a population.

name: Johanna Lindsey
headline: Johanna Lindsey, Best-Selling Romance Novelist, Dies at 67
abstract: Over more than 40 years, Ms. Lindsey turned out hot-blooded historical romances set around the world. “Romance,” she said, “is what comes out of me.”

name: Baba Ram Dass
profession: Proponent of LSD Turned New Age Guru
headline: Baba Ram Dass, Proponent of LSD Turned New Age Guru, Dies at 88
abstract: Born Richard Alpert, he first gained notice as a colleague of Timothy Leary and later became even better known as the author of “Be Here Now.”

name: Karl E. Meyer
headline: Karl E. Meyer, 91, Reporter, Editorialist and Author, Dies
abstract: He reported on Castro’s rise and the Bay of Pigs invasion and, as an opinion writer, criticized, in retrospect, a Times reporter’s Stalin-era dispatches.

name: Elizabeth Spencer
profession: Author of The Light in the Piazza
headline: Elizabeth Spencer, Author of ‘The Light in the Piazza,’ Dies at 98
abstract: A writer of novels and short stories, many set in her native South, she was best known for a 1960 novella, set in Italy, that was adapted for film and stage.

name: Emanuel Ungaro
headline: Emanuel Ungaro, Adventurous Fashion Designer, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Mr., Ungaro’s clothes could be both chic and surprising. Fashion, he believed, should be “disturbing to the eye.”

name: Chuck Peddle
profession: His $25 Chip Helped Start the PC Age
headline: Chuck Peddle Dies at 82; His $25 Chip Helped Start the PC Age
abstract: His invention brought digital technology to a new breed of consumer devices and powered early Apple and Commodore computers.

name: Joseph Fallek
headline: Joseph Fallek, Lawyer Who Defended Police Officers, Dies at 93
abstract: A onetime New York officer himself, he made a career of representing former colleagues accused of misconduct and corruption.

name: Hayden Fry
headline: Hayden Fry, Who Made Iowa a Football Powerhouse, Dies at 90
abstract: The Hawkeyes had foundered for nearly two decades when he took over in 1979. It took him three seasons to turn the team around.

name: Dalton Baldwin
headline: Dalton Baldwin, an Eminence Among Accompanists, Dies at 87
abstract: Often described as an equal partner to the singers he performed with, he preferred to be called simply a pianist.

name: Allee Willis
headline: Allee Willis, 72, Dies; ‘Friends’ Theme and ‘September’ Songwriter
abstract: She also wrote or co-wrote “Neutron Dance” for the Pointer Sisters, “What Have I Done to Deserve This?” for the Pet Shop Boys and Dusty Springfield, and other hits.

name: Joseph Segel
profession: Founder of the QVC Shopping Network
headline: Joseph Segel, Founder of the QVC Shopping Network, Dies at 88
abstract: The chief executive of QVC’s parent company said it “changed the way the world shops.” Mr. Segel’s many other ventures included the Franklin Mint.

name: May Stevens
headline: May Stevens, Who Turned Activism Into Art, Is Dead at 95
abstract: “The reason I’m an artist,” she once said, “is because it’s a place where you can be totally free.”

name: Kate Figes
headline: Kate Figes, Feminist Author on Family Life, Dies at 62
abstract: She explored life after childbirth, marriage, infidelity and other topics, and recalled a difficult relationship with her mother, also a feminist author.

name: Diane Terman Felenstein
headline: Diane Terman Felenstein, 79, Dies; Financial Guru to Women
abstract: She helped start an investment club for women, then helped write “The Money Club,” a best-selling financial advice guide.

name: Peter Wollen
headline: Peter Wollen, Who Wrote a Film Theory Bible, Is Dead at 81
abstract: His “Signs and Meaning in the Cinema,” part of a varied career that also included making his own movies, re-energized film studies.

name: William Greider
headline: William Greider, Journalist Who Focused on Economy, Dies at 83
abstract: In interviews with Reagan’s budget director, David Stockman, he exposed doubts about the supply-side economics that the administration had embraced.

name: Jerry Herman
headline: Jerry Herman, Composer of ‘Hello, Dolly!’ and Other Broadway Hits, Dies at 88
abstract: His rich melodies and powerful lyrics, also heard in “Mame” and “La Cage aux Folles,” dazzled critics and kept audiences returning for more.

name: Bentley Kassal
profession: Lawyer and Jurist for Nearly 80 Years
headline: Bentley Kassal, 102, Lawyer and Jurist for Nearly 80 Years, Dies
abstract: As a lawyer, he represented Lenny Bruce in an obscenity arrest. As a judge, he ruled in the self-defense case of the subway shooter Bernard Goetz.

name: George Sakheim
headline: George Sakheim, Interpreter at Nuremberg Trials, Dies at 96
abstract: A German refugee, he translated during the interrogations of Nazi leaders like Hermann Göring and Rudolf Höss, the commandant at Auschwitz.

name: Don Imus
headline: Don Imus, Radio Host Who Pushed Boundaries, Dies at 79
abstract: On the air, he was an irascible, confrontational growler who led pranks and parodies that could be tasteless, obscene and sometimes racist, sexist or homophobic.

name: Sue Lyon
headline: Sue Lyon, Star of ‘Lolita,’ Is Dead at 73
abstract: She was 14 when she was cast in the title role of Stanley Kubrick’s 1962 film of the Nabokov novel. It remained her best-known credit.

name: Arthur Singer Jr.
profession: Set the Stage for Public TV
headline: Arthur Singer Jr., Who Set the Stage for Public TV, Dies at 90
abstract: He played a key behind-the-scenes role in the Carnegie Commission report that led to the Corporation for Public Broadcasting and federal funding.

name: Neal R. Peirce
headline: Neal R. Peirce, Who Put Spotlight on Urban Innovation, Dies at 87
abstract: As a columnist and author he turned local affairs into a national subject, focusing on how alliances among leaders produced showcase projects.

name: Lee Mendelson
profession: Producer Behind A Charlie Brown Christmas
headline: Lee Mendelson, Producer Behind ‘A Charlie Brown Christmas,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Mendelson, who worked on dozens of animated projects, also wrote the enduring lyrics to the song “Christmas Time Is Here.”

name: Fred P. Graham
profession: Legal Affairs Reporter and Court TV Anchor
