headline: Fred P. Graham, Legal Affairs Reporter and Court TV Anchor, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Graham covered the Supreme Court for The New York Times during an era of intense political upheaval and racial tension before becoming CBS’s law correspondent in 1972.

name: Sleepy LaBeef
headline: Sleepy LaBeef, a Rockabilly Mainstay, Is Dead at 84
abstract: He never had what would be considered a hit record. But he gained a following for his ever-changing live shows and constant touring.

name: Neil Innes
headline: Neil Innes, a Master of Musical Humor, Is Dead at 75
abstract: He worked with the Monty Python troupe and was known for his own projects, including the Beatles parody band the Rutles.

name: Barbara Testa
profession: Her Discovery Rocked the Literary World
headline: Barbara Testa Dies at 91; Her Discovery Rocked the Literary World
abstract: Scholars had been searching for the manuscript for the first part of “Huckleberry Finn” for decades. Ms. Testa found it in her attic.

name: Sonny Mehta
headline: Sonny Mehta, Venerable Knopf Publisher, Is Dead at 77
abstract: A voracious reader and an instinctive decision maker, Mr. Mehta could spot great books and, coming from a paperback world, had no qualms about pushing them.

name: Gertrude Himmelfarb
headline: Gertrude Himmelfarb, Conservative Historian of Ideas, Dies at 97
abstract: Her arguments that a little more virtuousness trumps any number of government social programs made her a hero to some and a bête noire to others.

name: Peter Schreier
headline: Peter Schreier, 84, Elegant German Tenor Who Also Conducted, Dies
abstract: He made a mark singing in Bach oratorios and Mozart operas. But he also forged a career on the podium — sometimes singing roles in productions he led.

name: Paul X. Kelley
profession: Top Marine Tested by a Bombing
headline: Gen. Paul X. Kelley, Top Marine Tested by a Bombing, Dies at 91
abstract: As commandant from 1983 to 1987, he came to be viewed by many as an embodiment of the Marine Corps. But the deadly attack on a barracks in Lebanon proved personally traumatic.

name: Woody Vasulka
headline: Woody Vasulka, Whose Video Art Extended Boundaries, Dies at 82
abstract: He deftly manipulated electronic images to produce otherworldly, sometimes jarring visions. He also founded, with his wife, a landmark performance space.

name: Fazle Abed
profession: Founder of a Leading Relief Agency
headline: Fazle Abed, Founder of a Leading Relief Agency, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Abed gave up a job as a senior executive at a multinational company to start BRAC after he saw his native land, Bangladesh, devastated by war.

name: David Stern
headline: David Stern, Transformative N.B.A. Commissioner, Dies at 77
abstract: His marketing vision turned the world’s premier professional basketball league into a global brand with its biggest stars as its ambassadors.

name: Don Larsen
headline: Don Larsen, Yankee Who Pitched Only Perfect Game in World Series History, Dies at 90
abstract: He retired after 14 seasons with a losing record for his career, but for one day in 1956 he was the picture of perfection.

name: Qassim Suleimani
headline: Qassim Suleimani, Master of Iran’s Intrigue, Built a Shiite Axis of Power in Mideast
abstract: The commander helped direct wars in Iraq, Syria, Lebanon and Yemen, and he became the face of Iran’s efforts to build a regional bloc of Shiite power.

name: Syd Mead
profession: Maker of Future Worlds in Blade Runner and More
headline: Syd Mead, 86, Maker of Future Worlds in ‘Blade Runner’ and More, Dies
abstract: In a wide-ranging career, he designed cars, restaurants and, most notably, the otherworldly look of science-fiction movies.

name: Vaughan Oliver
profession: His Designs Gave Indie Rock Physical Dimension
headline: Vaughan Oliver, 62, Dies; His Designs Gave Indie Rock ‘Physical Dimension’
abstract: Mr. Oliver’s album covers for the 4AD label were a fitting complement to music by influential alternative bands like Pixies and the Breeders.

name: Sam Wyche
profession: Led Cincinnati to the Super Bowl
headline: Sam Wyche, Who Led Cincinnati to the Super Bowl, Dies at 74
abstract: He was praised as a hard-driving coach willing to go against the grain. He was also fined for keeping a female reporter out of the team’s locker room.

name: Jack Sheldon
headline: Jack Sheldon, Trumpeter and ‘Schoolhouse Rock!’ Singer, Is Dead at 88
abstract: He played with leading jazz musicians. He bantered with Merv Griffin. But his best-known work may have been on a children’s cartoon series.

name: Harry Kupfer
profession: Director and Opera King of Berlin
headline: Harry Kupfer, Director and ‘Opera King of Berlin,’ Dies at 84
abstract: He reimagined Wagner for the modern world, including a “Ring” focused on ecological destruction.

name: Heather Ashton
headline: Dr. Heather Ashton, 90, Dies; Helped People Quit Anxiety Drugs
abstract: Her “Ashton Manual,” published in 1999, has become a cornerstone for people all over the world dealing with benzodiazepine dependence.

name: John Baldessari
profession: Gave Conceptual Art a Dose of Wit
headline: John Baldessari, Who Gave Conceptual Art a Dose of Wit, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Through his hybrid works and teaching, he helped build the Los Angeles art scene, mentoring a who’s who of contemporary artists.

name: Elizabeth Wurtzel
headline: Elizabeth Wurtzel, ‘Prozac Nation’ Author, Is Dead at 52
abstract: Her startling 1994 memoir won praise for opening a dialogue about clinical depression and helped introduce an unsparing style of confessional writing that remains influential.

name: James Parks Morton
headline: James Parks Morton, Dean Who Brought a Cathedral to Life, Dies at 89
abstract: Leading the Cathedral Church of St. John the Divine for 25 years, he sought to make it central to urban life.

name: Jack Garfein
headline: Jack Garfein, Director From Actors Studio’s Heyday, Dies at 89
abstract: His family perished in the Holocaust. He survived and went to the United States, where he worked with Ben Gazzara, George Peppard, Samuel Beckett and Arthur Miller.

name: June Bacon-Bercey
headline: June Bacon-Bercey, 90, Pathbreaking Meteorologist, Is Dead
abstract: She is widely believed to have been the first African-American female meteorologist to forecast weather on television.

name: Bob Wade
headline: Bob Wade, Sculptor of the Outlandishly Large, Dies at 76
abstract: Known as Daddy-O, he created roadside, streetside and top-of-the-roof attractions in Texas and elsewhere.

name: Adela Holzer
headline: Adela Holzer, Whose Fall From Grace Was Theatrical, Is Dead
abstract: She went from being “Broadway’s hottest producer” to “one of the cleverest and most successful white-collar criminals in the history of this state.”

name: Peter Kirstein
headline: Peter Kirstein, Father of the European Internet, Is Dead at 86
abstract: He was crucial to the spread of the protocols that underpin today’s internet (and gave Queen Elizabeth her own email address).

name: Margaret McFarland
headline: Overlooked No More: Margaret McFarland, Mentor to Mister Rogers
abstract: Behind the scenes of “Mister Rogers’ Neighborhood,” McFarland, a child psychologist, helped shape the groundbreaking show.

name: Buck Henry
profession: Helped Create Get Smart and Adapt The Graduate
headline: Buck Henry, Who Helped Create ‘Get Smart’ and Adapt ‘The Graduate,’ Dies at 89
abstract: An unassuming screenwriter and actor, Mr. Henry thought up quirky characters with Mel Brooks and inhabited many more on “Saturday Night Live.”

name: Frederick Richmond
headline: Frederick Richmond, 96, Dies; Congressman Undone by Corruption
abstract: A wealthy House member and a champion of liberal causes as a New York civic leader, he was forced to quit Congress in 1982 in a corruption scandal.

name: Mamie Kirkland
profession: Witness to an Era of Racial Terror
headline: Mamie Kirkland, Witness to an Era of Racial Terror, Dies at 111
abstract: She endured the horrors of the African-American experience — lynchings, riots, the Ku Klux Klan — and worked to ensure that they never slipped from collective memory.

name: Edd Byrnes
profession: Combed His Way to TV Stardom
headline: Edd Byrnes, Who Combed His Way to TV Stardom, Dies at 86
abstract: He became one of television’s first teen idols as Kookie, the hair-combing, jive-talking youth on the hit series “77 Sunset Strip.”

name: Pete Dye
headline: Pete Dye, ‘Picasso’ of Golf Course Design, Is Dead at 94
abstract: “His courses built for tournaments are hard,” Tiger Woods once said, “ but there’s a good reason for everything.”

name: Marian Finucane
headline: Marian Finucane, 69, Dies; Influential Voice in Irish Radio
abstract: She took on sensitive subjects like homosexuality and contraception in a society dominated at the time by restrictive Roman Catholic teachings.

name: J. Charles Jones
headline: J. Charles Jones, Civil Rights Activist, Is Dead at 82
abstract: He was a participant in many pivotal events of the 1960s, beginning with lunch-counter protests in Charlotte, N.C.

name: Charles O. Jones
profession: Expert on Congress and the Presidency
headline: Charles O. Jones, Expert on Congress and the Presidency, Dies at 92
abstract: As a professor of political science and an author, he displayed a distinctive gift for simplifying the complexities of the American political system.

name: Harold Burson
headline: Harold Burson, a Giant in Public Relations, Dies at 98
abstract: His skills were called upon in a Tylenol-tampering case and a devastating gas leak in India. In 1999, he was named the century’s most influential P.R. figure.

name: Neil Peart
headline: Neil Peart, Drummer and Lyricist for Rush, Dies at 67
abstract: His drumming was at once intricate and explosive, expanding Rush’s power-trio dynamics. His lyrics transformed the band’s songs into elaborate suites.

name: Georges Duboeuf
profession: Creator of the Beaujolais Nouveau Craze
headline: Georges Duboeuf, Creator of the Beaujolais Nouveau Craze, Dies at 86
abstract: He almost single-handedly started the rush for the first wines of the Beaujolais harvest.

name: Alasdair Gray
headline: Alasdair Gray, Scottish Author of Daring Prose, Dies at 85
abstract: He didn’t publish his first novel (which he illustrated himself) until he was 46. But his impact, as both a writer and an artist, has lasted.

name: John Rothchild
profession: Wrote About Personal Finance With Wit
headline: John Rothchild, 74, Dies; Wrote About Personal Finance With Wit
abstract: He worked with Peter Lynch on several guides to stock trading. He also wrote a guidebook that offered no advice at all.

name: Courtney Everts Mykytyn
headline: Courtney Everts Mykytyn, Crusader for School Integration, Dies at 46
abstract: She challenged privileged white parents to send their children to schools with predominantly black and Latino student bodies.

name: Qaboos
profession: Built Oman Into Prosperous Oasis of Peacemaking
headline: Sultan Qaboos, 79, Is Dead; Built Oman Into Prosperous Oasis of Peacemaking
abstract: The longest-serving Arab ruler, Qaboos pulled his nation from poverty and brokered quiet talks between global foes.

name: Ronald Melzack
headline: Ronald Melzack, Cartographer of Pain, Is Dead at 90
abstract: The theory that he and a colleague devised deepened medicine’s understanding of pain and how it is best measured and treated.

name: Nelson Bryant
headline: Nelson Bryant, ‘Supreme Chronicler’ of Outdoor Life, Dies at 96
abstract: For nearly four decades, his lyrical columns for The Times brought readers to the banks of clear-running streams and the hushed glades of majestic forests.

name: Nancy Lewis
headline: Nancy Lewis, the Pythons’ Ticket to America, Dies at 76
abstract: The British troupe wasn’t well known in the United States until she began promoting its records and pushing to get “Monty Python’s Flying Circus” on PBS.

name: John Pawasarat
profession: Used Data to Address Social Ills
headline: John Pawasarat Dies at 70; Used Data to Address Social Ills
abstract: His research on driver’s licenses — who had them, who didn’t — was cited in voting rights disputes over whether requiring picture IDs was discriminatory.

name: Matty Maher
headline: Matty Maher, an Institution at an Institution, McSorley’s, Dies at 80
abstract: As bartender, manager and owner, he helped the East Village saloon survive neighborhood blight and change its ways by admitting women and banning smoking.

name: Ed Filipowski
headline: Ed Filipowski, 58, Pioneer of Fashion Public Relations, Dies
abstract: “He was not emotional about fashion,” a colleague said. “He was steady.” He was also influential.

name: Gladys Bourdain
profession: Helped Her Son Reach an Audience
headline: Gladys Bourdain, Who Helped Her Son Reach an Audience, Dies at 85
abstract: A Times copy editor, she kick-started Anthony Bourdain’s career when she helped him get a tell-all article about the restaurant world published in The New Yorker.

name: Ivan Passer
headline: Ivan Passer, Noted Czech Director Who Went to Hollywood, Dies at 86
abstract: A contemporary and friend of Milos Forman, he was part of the Czech New Wave before resettling in the United States.

name: Betty Pat Gatliff
headline: Betty Pat Gatliff, 89, Whose Forensic Art Solved Crimes, Dies
abstract: She used clay to reconstruct the faces of the missing and the murdered, in the hope of helping police departments learn who they were.

name: Ana Orantes
profession: Gruesome Murder Brought Change to Spain
headline: Overlooked No More: Ana Orantes, Whose Gruesome Murder Brought Change to Spain
abstract: In 1997, Orantes was killed by her husband after she went on television to describe his abuse. Her story led to major legal reforms to protect women from domestic violence.

name: Gary Starkweather
headline: Gary Starkweather, Inventor of the Laser Printer, Dies at 81
abstract: He originally received pushback from his employer, Xerox. But his invention eventually became nearly ubiquitous in every office and home.

name: Sylvia Jukes Morris
headline: Sylvia Jukes Morris, Biographer of Clare Boothe Luce, Dies at 84
abstract: She spent 33 years on the two-volume biography, examining 460,000 items at the Library of Congress that stretched 319 linear feet.

name: Rocky Johnson
headline: Rocky Johnson, Pro Wrestler Who Trained His Son the Rock, Dies at 75
abstract: Johnson battled racism early on and introduced Dwayne Johnson to professional wrestling years before he became a famous actor.

name: Marion Chesney
headline: Marion Chesney, a.k.a. Mystery Writer M.C. Beaton, Dies at 83
abstract: Her popular crime solvers Hamish Macbeth and Agatha Raisin were the focus of dozens of books, as well as TV series.

name: George Nicolau
headline: George Nicolau, Arbitrator in Baseball’s Collusion Cases, Dies at 94
abstract: He found that team owners had twice conspired to impede the market for free agents in the 1980s. As a result of his rulings, owners had to pay $280 million.

name: Roger Scruton
headline: Roger Scruton, a Provocative Public Intellectual, Dies at 75
abstract: A philosopher, author and columnist, he was an outspoken hero to conservatives in Britain and recently at the center of, in his words, a “hate storm.”

name: Christopher Tolkien
headline: Christopher Tolkien, Keeper of His Father’s Legacy, Dies at 95
abstract: As literary executor of the estate of his father, J.R.R. Tolkien, Mr. Tolkien compiled and edited such works as “The Silmarillion.”

name: Lorenza Mazzetti
headline: Lorenza Mazzetti, Wartime Survivor and Seminal Filmmaker, Dies at 92
abstract: She was spared by German soldiers seeking her uncle and protector, a cousin of Albert Einstein. She went on to help start the British New Wave in cinema.

name: Ninez Cacho-Olivares
headline: Ninez Cacho-Olivares, Journalist and Critic of Marcos, Dies at 78
abstract: She was among a cadre of newswomen who faced down the Philippine dictator. But she later unexpectedly turned around to support President Rodrigo Duterte.

name: Norma Tanega
profession: Sang About a Cat Named Dog
headline: Norma Tanega, Who Sang About a Cat Named Dog, Dies at 80
abstract: She had only one hit record, but it was a memorable one: a quirkily titled song about freedom, dreaming and her cat, who really was named Dog.

name: Peter Larkin
profession: Stage Designer With a Funky Asterisk
headline: Peter Larkin, Stage Designer With a Funky Asterisk, Dies at 93
abstract: His Broadway work won him four Tony Awards. A different audience knew another of his designs: the Parliament-Funkadelic Mothership.

name: Barry Tuckwell
headline: Barry Tuckwell, French Horn Virtuoso, Is Dead at 88
abstract: He was widely considered to be the finest player of his era and was said to have “inspired every generation of horn player for the past 70 years.”

name: Edith Kunhardt Davis
profession: Author of Pat the Bunny Sequels
headline: Edith Kunhardt Davis, Author of ‘Pat the Bunny’ Sequels, Dies at 82
abstract: She also wrote about the death of her son at 27, for which she blamed herself because she had been an alcoholic when she was pregnant with him.

name: Jimmy Heath
headline: Jimmy Heath, 93, Jazz Saxophonist and Composer, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Heath, whose compositions became part of the midcentury jazz canon, found new prominence in middle age as a co-leader of a band with his two brothers.

name: Lotte Shin
headline: ‘Chewing Gum Tycoon’ of Lotte Group, Shin Kyuk-ho, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Shin transformed a small business in postwar Tokyo into ​a ​corporate giant spanning South Korea and Japan.

name: David Olney
headline: David Olney, 71, Singer-Songwriter, Dies Onstage
abstract: He wasn’t as famous as those who sang his songs, but he was revered by them. After apparently suffering a heart attack, mid-song, he stopped and said, “I’m sorry.”

name: David Glass
profession: Walmart Boss and K.C. Royals Owner
headline: David Glass, Walmart Boss and K.C. Royals Owner, Dies at 84
abstract: He introduced selling groceries alongside general merchandise in Supercenters, positioning Walmart to compete with Amazon today. His Royals won a World Series.

name: Egil Krogh
headline: Egil Krogh, 80, Nixon Aide, Dies; Authorized an Infamous Break-In
abstract: He regretted his role in the burglary of Daniel Ellsberg’s psychiatrist’s office and said he thought it had set the stage for Watergate.

name: Morgan Wootten
headline: Morgan Wootten, Acclaimed High School Basketball Coach, Dies at 88
abstract: He had one of the best winning streaks, and was inducted into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame.

name: Terry Jones
headline: Terry Jones, Monty Python Founder and Scholar, Is Dead at 77
abstract: In addition to being a charter member of the celebrated British sketch troupe, he was a director, a screenwriter and an authority on Chaucer.

name: Michael I. Sovern
headline: Michael I. Sovern, Who Led Columbia in Eventful Era, Dies at 88
abstract: During his tenure, 1980-93, the university was restored to financial health, divested from companies tied to South Africa and admitted women to its college.

name: Lee Gelber
profession: Dean of New York Tour Guides
headline: Lee Gelber, Dean of New York Tour Guides, Dies at 81
abstract: “He knew our city better than anyone else,” a colleague said, “and made it his goal for everyone else to know it, too.”

name: Tom Railsback
headline: Tom Railsback, Who Reconciled G.O.P. to Oust Nixon, Dies at 87
abstract: A moderate Republican congressman from Illinois, he forged a compromise on two articles of impeachment that passed the House Judiciary Committee in 1974.

name: Jack Van Impe
headline: Jack Van Impe, End Times Preacher on TV, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Known for his prodigious memorization of the Bible, he mingled scripture with commentary on public affairs.

name: Judee Sill
headline: Overlooked No More: Judee Sill, Singer Whose Life Was Cut Short
abstract: The story that runs parallel to Sill’s rising stardom was one of misfortune and adversity that culminated in her death at the age of 35.

name: Jim Lehrer
headline: Jim Lehrer, Longtime PBS News Anchor, Is Dead at 85
abstract: For 36 years, mostly teaming with Robert MacNeil, he offered an alternative to network evening news programs with in-depth reporting, interviews and news analysis.

name: Carol Serling
profession: Rods Wife and Tender of Twilight Zone Flame
headline: Carol Serling, Rod’s Wife and Tender of ‘Twilight Zone’ Flame, Dies at 90
abstract: Rod Serling, who created “The Twilight Zone,” died in 1975. His wife — in publishing, academic and screen ventures — helped keep his spirit alive.

name: Frederic Berman
profession: Protector of Renters in New York
headline: Frederic Berman, Protector of Renters in New York, Dies at 92
abstract: He helped institute safeguards for tenants of 1.4 million rent-controlled apartments in the ’60s and was a key player behind the Rent Stabilization Law.

name: Sonny Grosso
headline: Sonny Grosso, Detective Who Severed ‘French Connection,’ Dies at 89
abstract: He and his partner broke the heroin case that inspired that 1971 film. After he retired, he became a movie and television producer and consultant.

name: Claudio Roditi
headline: Claudio Roditi, Lyrical Jazz Trumpeter, Is Dead at 73
abstract: The Brazilian-born Mr. Roditi fused in his playing the gentle lilt of samba with the drive of the post-bop trumpet tradition.

name: Frieda Caplan
headline: Frieda Caplan, Who Enlivened the Produce Aisle, Dies at 96
abstract: She helped introduce kiwi, jicama and countless other unfamiliar fruits and vegetables to American consumers.

name: Margo Lion
headline: Margo Lion, Producer of ‘Hairspray’ and More, Dies at 75
abstract: In an era when big-budget theater was an increasingly corporate affair, Ms. Lion was a proudly independent producer.

name: Clayton Christensen
headline: Clayton Christensen, Guru of ‘Disruptive Innovation,’ Dies at 67
abstract: He broke ground with his assertion that the factors that helped the best companies succeed were also the reasons some of those same companies failed.

name: Nina Griscom
headline: Nina Griscom, Model, Entrepreneur and ‘It Girl’ of the ’80s, Dies at 65
abstract: At home in high society and gossip columns, she also worked regularly as a TV host, designer, writer and home décor entrepreneur.

name: Rhona Wurtele
profession: One of Canadas Flying Twins Ski Champions
headline: Rhona Wurtele, One of Canada’s ‘Flying Twins’ Ski Champions, Dies at 97
abstract: With her sister, Rhoda, she won many American and Canadian competitions, and later the two taught thousands of people to ski.

name: Jason Polan
headline: Jason Polan, Fast-Drawing Artist of the Offbeat, Dies at 37
abstract: His projects included a quixotic quest to sketch everyone in New York City.

name: Seamus Mallon
profession: Advocate for Peace in Northern Ireland
headline: Seamus Mallon, Advocate for Peace in Northern Ireland, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Mallon spent his life campaigning for an end to killings and abuses by all sides in the conflict known as the Troubles.

name: Bill Ray
headline: Bill Ray, Photographer of Indelible Moments, Dies at 83
abstract: He captured Marilyn Monroe singing “Happy birthday, Mr. President,” Elvis Presley as an Army private, scenes of war and urban unrest, and much more.

name: Michou
profession: Drag Cabaret Was the Toast of Paris
headline: Michou, Whose Drag Cabaret Was the Toast of Paris, Dies at 88
abstract: Since 1956, his jewel box of a club in storied Montmartre has drawn a host of luminaries, turning the proprietor himself into one.

name: Pete Stark
profession: Fighter in Congress for Health Care
headline: Pete Stark, Fighter in Congress for Health Care, Dies at 88
abstract: Hailing from a liberal corner of California, he was a major voice in health care debates, but an acid tongue may have scuttled his advancement.

name: Bob Shane
profession: Last of the Original Kingston Trio
headline: Bob Shane, Last of the Original Kingston Trio, Dies at 85
abstract: The group spearheaded a commercially successful folk revival in the late 1950s and early ’60s, with Mr. Shane singing lead most of the time.

name: Arnold Aronson
headline: Arnold Aronson, Who Revitalized Saks in the ’80s, Dies at 85
abstract: He transformed a venerable retail chain with a “dowager image” by courting baby boomers, renovating its flagship store and expanding its national reach.

name: Harriet Frank Jr.
headline: Harriet Frank Jr., Writer of Challenging Screenplays, Dies at 96
abstract: She and her husband, Irving Ravetch, were among Hollywood’s most successful and literate script writers, collaborating on movies like “Hud” and “Norma Rae.”

name: Franz Mazura
headline: Franz Mazura, 95, Opera Singer Whose Specialty Was Villains, Dies
abstract: An imposing Austrian bass-baritone, his first major international appearance came in his early 40s. He continued to perform nearly until the end.

name: Lina Ben Mhenni
headline: Lina Ben Mhenni, 36, ‘a Tunisian Girl’ Who Confronted Regime, Dies
abstract: Ms. Ben Mhenni used her blog to expose violence against protesters in the revolt that led to the government’s overthrow, and then to the Arab Spring.

name: Chris Doleman
profession: Hall of Fame Scourge of Quarterbacks
headline: Chris Doleman, Hall of Fame Scourge of Quarterbacks, Dies at 58
abstract: In 15 N.F.L. seasons, mostly with the Vikings, Doleman was a 290-pound juggernaut, recording 150½ sacks. He died of brain cancer.

name: Leila Janah
headline: Leila Janah, Entrepreneur Who Hired the Poor, Dies at 37
abstract: A child of Indian immigrants, she created digital jobs that pay a living wage to thousands in Africa and India, believing that the intellect of the poor was “the biggest untapped resource” in the world.

name: Wes Wilson
headline: Wes Wilson, Psychedelic Poster Pioneer, Dies at 82
abstract: His work announced concerts by the Grateful Dead, Jefferson Airplane and more — to those who could read them.

name: Fred Silverman
profession: TV Power When Three Networks Ruled
headline: Fred Silverman, 82, Is Dead; a TV Power When Three Networks Ruled
abstract: A top executive at CBS, ABC and then NBC, he shepherded series like “All in the Family,” “Laverne & Shirley” and “Hill Street Blues.”

name: Anne Cox Chambers
headline: Anne Cox Chambers, Media Heiress and Ex-Ambassador, Dies at 100
abstract: Mrs. Chambers, whose stake in Cox Enterprises was once worth billions, campaigned for Jimmy Carter, who gave her a diplomatic post in Belgium.

name: Homer Plessy
profession: Sat on a Train and Stood Up for Civil Rights
headline: Overlooked No More: Homer Plessy, Who Sat on a Train and Stood Up for Civil Rights
abstract: He boarded a whites-only train car in New Orleans with the hope of getting the attention of the Supreme Court. But it would be a long time before he got justice.

name: Jack Burns
profession: Comic Force on Camera and Off
headline: Jack Burns, a Comic Force on Camera and Off, Is Dead at 86
abstract: He paired with George Carlin, was the pompous half of a memorable comedy team with Avery Schreiber and had a second career as a producer and writer.

name: Del Pitt Feldman
headline: Del Pitt Feldman, Who Made Crocheting Hip, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Her designs captured the freewheeling spirit of the 1960s counterculture. Among her clients were Janis Joplin, Grace Slick and Cher.

name: Louis Nirenberg
headline: Louis Nirenberg, ‘One of the Great Mathematicians,’ Dies at 94
abstract: Winner of the math world’s equivalent of a Nobel, he puzzled out equations describing the vibrating of strings, the flow of heat and the movement of water.

name: Hester Diamond
headline: Hester Diamond, Passionate Art Collector, Is Dead at 91
abstract: A self-taught art expert, she always insisted that her first criterion for a purchase — maybe her only one — was loving the piece.

name: Bonnie Burstow
headline: Bonnie Burstow, Psychotherapist Who Rejected Psychiatry, Dies at 74
abstract: A self-described feminist therapist, she was a prominent voice in the anti-psychiatry movement, contending that the field is patriarchal.

name: Mary Higgins Clark
headline: Mary Higgins Clark, Best-Selling Queen of Suspense, Dies at 92
abstract: She became a world-renowned author writing about “nice people whose lives are invaded.”

name: Monique Van Vooren
headline: Monique Van Vooren, Actress With a Diverse Résumé, Dies at 92
abstract: Her filmography ranged from “Tarzan and the She-Devil” to “Wall Street.” She also appeared on “Batman” and on game shows and sang in cabarets.

name: Frank Press
headline: Frank Press, White House Science Adviser, Is Dead at 95
abstract: After serving as President Jimmy Carter’s chief aide on scientific matters, he led the National Academy of Sciences for 12 years.

name: Peter Serkin
headline: Peter Serkin, 72, Dies; Pianist With Pedigree Who Forged a New Path
abstract: Descended from two eminent musical families, he became a maverick, questioned the establishment and fostered a career on his own terms.

name: Andy Gill
profession: Radical Guitarist With Gang of Four
headline: Andy Gill, Radical Guitarist With Gang of Four, Dies at 64
abstract: “You could tell by listening to Gang of Four music that punk had happened,” he once said. “But it definitely wasn’t punk music.”

name: Bernard J. Ebbers
headline: Bernard J. Ebbers, WorldCom Chief Jailed in Fraud, Dies at 78
abstract: Once hailed as an entrepreneurial success story, the “telecom cowboy,” he presided over one of the biggest scandals in American corporate history.

name: George Steiner
headline: George Steiner, Prodigious Literary Critic, Dies at 90
abstract: He ranged over subjects like the origins of speech, the moral power of literature and the future of truth — and sometimes drew criticism himself.

name: ‘Mad Mike’ Hoare
headline: ‘Mad Mike’ Hoare, Irish Mercenary Leader in Africa, Dies at 100
abstract: His exploits included fighting in wars, rescuing hostages, searching for a lost city and staging a farcical aborted coup.

name: Xana Antunes
headline: Xana Antunes, Business Journalist and Top Editor, Dies at 55
abstract: She led The New York Post and the business news site Quartz.

name: Willie Wood
profession: Star Defensive Back With the Green Bay Packers
headline: Willie Wood, Star Defensive Back With the Green Bay Packers, Dies at 83
abstract: A Hall of Famer, he was a key figure in Vince Lombardi’s dynasty and played on five championship teams in the 1960s.

name: Daniel arap Moi
headline: Daniel arap Moi, Autocratic and Durable Kenyan Leader, Dies at 95
abstract: He oversaw an island of political stability in Africa for decades. But it was a democracy in name only, as the economy stagnated and corruption flourished.

name: Alice Mayhew
headline: Alice Mayhew, Who Edited a Who’s Who of Writers, Dies at 87
abstract: At Simon & Schuster, best sellers were her stock in trade. She popularized the nonfiction political page turner, starting with “All the President’s Men.”

name: Leonard Shengold
headline: Dr. Leonard Shengold, 94, Psychoanalyst Who Studied Child Abuse, Dies
abstract: He said mistreating and neglecting children amounted to “soul murder” — a deliberate attempt to crush or eradicate the personality of a vulnerable young person.

name: Nathaniel R. Jones
headline: Nathaniel R. Jones, Rights Lawyer and Federal Judge, Dies at 93
abstract: As a voice of the N.A.A.C.P., he challenged school segregation in the North and racial bias in the military. But, he cautioned, the struggle is not over.

name: Lucy Jarvis
profession: Took TV Viewers Far and Wide
headline: Lucy Jarvis, Who Took TV Viewers Far and Wide, Dies at 102
abstract: In an era when few if any producers were women, she got access to the Kremlin, China and more.

name: Gene Reynolds
headline: Gene Reynolds, 96, an Architect of ‘M*A*S*H,’ Is Dead
abstract: He also helped bring another acclaimed series, “Lou Grant,” to television.

name: Beverly Pepper
headline: Beverly Pepper, Sculptor of Monumental Lightness, Dies at 97
abstract: An American artist who long worked in Italy, she created towering forms whose evanescence belied their giant scale.

name: Ivan Kral
profession: Rocker With Patti Smith and Others
headline: Ivan Kral, Rocker With Patti Smith and Others, Is Dead at 71
abstract: A key figure in New York’s creative underground of the 1970s, he was also a filmmaker who chronicled the early days of the punk scene.

name: Joseph Bartholomew
headline: Overlooked No More: Joseph Bartholomew, Golf Course Architect
abstract: He designed and built some of the best-known courses in segregated Louisiana. But though he loved the game, he was never permitted to play those courses.

name: Kirk Douglas
headline: Kirk Douglas, a Star of Hollywood’s Golden Age, Dies at 103
abstract: His rugged good looks and muscular intensity made him a commanding presence in films like “Lust for Life,” “Spartacus” and “Paths of Glory.”

name: Deborah A. Batts
headline: Deborah A. Batts, First Openly Gay Federal Judge, Dies at 72
abstract: Another gay judge said Judge Batts “literally broke down the closet door and allowed the rest of us to walk through it.”

name: Nello Santi
profession: Conductor With His Heart in Italian Opera
headline: Nello Santi, Conductor With His Heart in Italian Opera, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Santi, who led hundreds of performances at the Metropolitan Opera, was a renowned interpreter of Puccini and, especially, Verdi.

name: Greta Beer
profession: Fought Swiss Banks for Family Assets
headline: Greta Beer, Who Fought Swiss Banks for Family Assets, Dies at 98
abstract: Rebuffed by the banks, she pressed her fight and her testimony in Congress helped bring about a billion-dollar settlement over accounts of Holocaust victims that were long hidden.

name: Roger Kahn
profession: Lifted Sportswriting With Boys of Summer
headline: Roger Kahn, Who Lifted Sportswriting With ‘Boys of Summer,’ Dies at 92
abstract: His 1972 book about his beloved Brooklyn Dodgers, acknowledged as a classic, was, like many of his 20 or so other books, steeped in memories of his boyhood.

name: Terry DeCarlo
profession: Gay Leader in the Wake of a Shooting
headline: Terry DeCarlo, Gay Leader in the Wake of a Shooting, Dies at 57
abstract: After 49 people were killed at the Pulse nightclub in Orlando, Fla., in 2016, he spoke for the city’s L.G.B.T.Q. community on the national stage.

name: Stephen Joyce
headline: Stephen Joyce Dies at 87; Guarded Grandfather’s Literary Legacy
abstract: The last direct descendant of the author of “Ulysses” and “Finnegans Wake” was a fierce protector of James Joyce’s estate, to the frustration of scholars.

name: Emily Mason
headline: Emily Mason, Who Created Colorful Canvases, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Part of a family of artists, she was known for creating abstract works by a process she liked to call “letting a painting talk to you.”

name: Stanley Cohen
headline: Stanley Cohen, Nobelist, Dies at 97; Made Breakthrough on Cell Growth
abstract: He shared the prize with Rita Levi-Montalcini for research that opened the door to a clearer understanding of dementia, cancer and other maladies.

name: Kevin Conway
profession: Elephant Man Actor Known for Intensity
headline: Kevin Conway, ‘Elephant Man’ Actor Known for Intensity, Dies at 77
abstract: In a wide-ranging career, he appeared onstage, on TV and in films and was the voice of Mark Twain for a Ken Burns film and of an “Outer Limits” reboot.

name: Jhon Jairo Velásquez
headline: Jhon Jairo Velásquez, 57, Dies; Escobar Henchman Turned YouTube Star
abstract: Mr. Velásquez, who boasted of murdering hundreds of people for Pablo Escobar, in recent years had built a business around the memories of his criminal activities.

name: Orson Bean
profession: Free-Spirited Actor of Stage and Screen
headline: Orson Bean, Free-Spirited Actor of Stage and Screen, Dies at 91
abstract: After finding success on television and Broadway, he established a progressive school and later wandered around America as a late-blooming hippie.

name: Paul Farnes
profession: Last R.A.F. Ace of Battle of Britain
headline: Paul Farnes, Last R.A.F. Ace of Battle of Britain, Dies at 101
abstract: He was one of the last of “The Few,” the Royal Air Force airmen who defended Britain against the powerful Luftwaffe.

name: Robert Conrad
profession: Two-Fisted TV Star of Wild Wild West
headline: Robert Conrad, Two-Fisted TV Star of ‘Wild Wild West,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Conrad, known for tough guy roles, played a secret agent in a mid-1960s television series that transplanted James Bond-style plots into an Old West setting.

name: Mirella Freni
headline: Mirella Freni, Matchless Italian Prima Donna, Dies at 84
abstract: Ms. Freni was acclaimed for her exquisite singing in lighter lyric roles. In midcareer she also dared to explore weightier ones.

name: Bruce McEwen
profession: Found Stress Can Alter the Brain
headline: Bruce McEwen, 81, Is Dead; Found Stress Can Alter the Brain
abstract: A neuroscientist, he showed how an unrelenting barrage of stress hormones can break down the body, leading to disease, depression, obesity and more.

name: Terry Hands
profession: Director Known for Hits and Carrie
headline: Terry Hands, Director Known for Hits and ‘Carrie,’ Dies at 79
abstract: While at the Royal Shakespeare Company, he took several shows to Broadway. One didn’t go so well.

name: Joseph Shabalala
headline: Joseph Shabalala, Ladysmith Black Mambazo Founder, Dies at 78
abstract: His choral group acquired an international following and won Grammys after collaborating with Paul Simon on the album “Graceland.”

name: Santu Mofokeng
headline: Santu Mofokeng, Photographer of Apartheid Life, Dies at 63
abstract: His sublime black-and-white images of everyday life in South Africa both during and after white rule capture hope and unfulfilled expectations.

name: Lyle Mays
headline: Lyle Mays, 66, Pat Metheny Group Keyboardist, Is Dead
abstract: His synthesizers gave depth and color to the ensemble’s sound. He soloed gracefully on grand piano. And he helped write many staples of the group’s repertoire.

name: Paula Kelly
profession: Danced From Stage Onto the Screen
headline: Paula Kelly, Who Danced From Stage Onto the Screen, Dies at 77
abstract: She was one of the first black women to make the transition, propelled by the musical “Sweet Charity.” She also broke ground playing a black lesbian on TV.

name: Katherine W. Phillips
headline: Katherine W. Phillips, 47, Dies; Taught the Value of Difference
abstract: A business school professor who studied the benefits of diversity in the workplace and spoke to companies about it.

name: Lawrence Pierce
headline: Lawrence Pierce, Judge in Contraceptives Case, Dies at 95
abstract: On the federal bench, he voided a New York law banning the sale of birth-control products to minors. He considered himself a Republican civil libertarian.

name: Katsuya Nomura
headline: Katsuya Nomura, 84, Enduring Star of Japanese Baseball, Dies
abstract: His 657 home runs and 1,988 runs batted in were second in the nation’s history, as were his 2,901 hits and 3,017 games. He also had success as a manager.

name: Dyanne Thorne
headline: Dyanne Thorne, 83, Star of Scandalous ‘Ilsa’ Films, Is Dead
abstract: She was a sadistic Nazi doctor in “Ilsa: She Wolf of the SS,” a 1975 sexploitation movie that has achieved cult status, then returned in several sequels.

name: Andrée Blouin
headline: Overlooked No More: Andrée Blouin, Voice for Independence in Africa
abstract: Politicized by her child’s death, she went on to counsel the first post-colonial leaders of Algeria, both Congos, Ivory Coast, Mali, Guinea and Ghana.

name: Elizabeth Cullinan
profession: Writer With an Eye for Detail
headline: Elizabeth Cullinan, Writer With an Eye for Detail, Dies at 86
abstract: Hiring her as a typist, The New Yorker wound up publishing many of her closely observed stories, which helped redefine Irish-American literature.

name: George Coyne
headline: George Coyne, 87, Vatican Astronomer and Galileo Defender, Dies
abstract: While seeking to reconcile science and religion, Father Coyne also vigorously supported Darwin and challenged believers in intelligent design.

name: Charles O’Brien
headline: Charles O’Brien, 86, Who Was Dogged by Hoffa Case, Is Dead
abstract: Suspicions that Chuckie O’Brien was involved in the union boss’s disappearance trailed him for 45 years.

name: Rajendra Pachauri
headline: Rajendra Pachauri, 79, Dies; Led Nobel-Winning Climate Agency
abstract: Sharing the prize with Al Gore, his U.N. organization was recognized for its work on global warming, but his career was undone by harassment accusations.

name: Nedda Casei
headline: Nedda Casei, Mezzo-Soprano Turned Labor Leader, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Casei was an energetic and exciting presence on the Met stage in the 1960s and ’70s before becoming president of a performers’ union.

name: A. E. Hotchner
profession: Writer and Friend of the Famous
headline: A. E. Hotchner, Writer and Friend of the Famous, Dies at 102
abstract: His diverse body of work included novels, plays and a memoir about Ernest Hemingway. He was also a partner with his friend Paul Newman in business and charity.

name: Barbara Remington
headline: Barbara Remington, Illustrator of Tolkien Book Covers, Dies at 90
abstract: Her work for the 1965 paperback editions of “The Lord of the Rings” and “The Hobbit” achieved mass-cult status. But she hadn’t read the books when she got the job.

name: Kamau Brathwaite
headline: Kamau Brathwaite, Poet Who Celebrated Caribbean Culture, Dies at 89
abstract: The peoples of the Caribbean needed to rediscover their heritage, he said, adding, “Instead of developing a sense of ourselves, we developed a false sense of Europe.”

name: Owen Bieber
profession: Auto Workers President During Period of Decline
headline: Owen Bieber, Auto Workers’ President During Period of Decline, Dies at 90
abstract: Faced with automation and competition from foreign car companies, he was forced to make concessions in an effort to preserve jobs.

name: Charles Portis
headline: Charles Portis, Elusive Author of ‘True Grit,’ Dies at 86
abstract: The publicity-shy Mr. Portis earned a modest but devoted readership and accolades as America’s “least-known great writer.”

name: Dawn Mello
headline: Dawn Mello, Who Revived Bergdorf Goodman and Gucci, Dies at 88
abstract: She was one of the first women to rise to leadership in retailing, and her aesthetic helped shift the landscape of American fashion.

name: Mickey Wright
profession: One of the Greatest Players in Womens Golf
headline: Mickey Wright, One of the Greatest Players in Women’s Golf, Dies at 85
abstract: She won 82 L.P.G.A. tournaments, 13 of them majors, dominating the tour in the late 1950s and much of the 1960s.

name: Clayton Williams
headline: Clayton Williams, Oilman Whose Gaffes Cost an Election, Dies at 88
abstract: Leading Ann Richards in 1990, he was undone by a spate of blunders. He was the last Republican to date to lose a race for governor of Texas.

name: Buzzy Linhart
headline: Buzzy Linhart, Eccentric and Eclectic Singer-Songwriter, Dies at 76
abstract: A prominent figure on the Greenwich Village folk scene of the 1960s, he wrote songs performed by Bette Midler, Carly Simon and the Muppets.

name: Zoe Caldwell
headline: Zoe Caldwell, Winner of Four Tony Awards, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Her signature performances included the title role in “The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie” and Maria Callas in “Master Class.”

name: Janet Dubois
headline: ‘Good Times’ Actress Ja’Net DuBois Dies
abstract: Ms. DuBois played Willona Woods on the 1970s TV show, and composed and wrote the theme song to “The Jeffersons.”

name: Kellye Nakahara
headline: Kellye Nakahara, a Memorable Nurse on ‘M*A*S*H,’ Dies at 73
abstract: Originally an extra, she ended up appearing in 167 episodes. “I put myself in every scene,” she once said, “and nobody told me to get out.”

name: Frank Anderson
headline: Frank Anderson, Former Spy Who Supplied Afghan Insurgents, Dies at 78
abstract: He supervised operations in Afghanistan and the Middle East and oversaw a top-secret link with a high official of the Palestine Liberation Organization.

name: Esther Scott
headline: Esther Scott, ‘Boyz N the Hood’ Actress, Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Scott made a career of small, powerful roles in which she portrayed sharp but nurturing characters.

name: Jean Daniel
headline: Jean Daniel, Leading French Journalist and Humanist, Dies at 99
abstract: In France, where news and opinion are blurred, Mr. Daniel, a self-described non-Communist leftist, used journalism as a means of advocacy.

name: Sy Sperling
profession: Founder of Hair Club for Men (and Also a Client)
headline: Sy Sperling, Founder of Hair Club for Men (and Also a Client), Dies at 78
abstract: A star in the era of TV pitchmen, Mr. Sperling rose to fame with ubiquitous late-night ads in the 1980s and ’90s.

name: Lawrence Tesler
headline: Lawrence Tesler, Who Made Personal Computing Easier, Dies at 74
abstract: When you’re cutting and pasting, dragging the cursor over selected text and performing other common computer tasks, you can thank him.

name: Bonnie MacLean
headline: Bonnie MacLean, Psychedelic Poster Artist, Is Dead at 80
abstract: The posters she made for concerts at the Fillmore in San Francisco helped define the 1960s.

name: Jack Youngerman
headline: Jack Youngerman, Distinctively Abstract Artist, Dies at 93
abstract: He was a leading member of the generation that sought to recast abstraction in cooler, more analytic terms after the turmoil of Abstract Expressionism.

name: Julius Montgomery
headline: Julius Montgomery, Who Broke a Space-Age Race Barrier, Dies at 90
abstract: In the Jim Crow South, he was the first black professional to be hired at Cape Canaveral, then made a sacrifice so that a technology school might open.

name: Tobi Tobias
headline: Tobi Tobias, Longtime Dance Critic, Dies at 81
abstract: She wrote for New York and Dance magazines, pulling no punches. She was also the author of a number of children’s books.

name: Reinbert de Leeuw
headline: Reinbert de Leeuw, Dutch Champion of Contemporary Music, Dies at 81
abstract: He pushed conservative institutions to program the new, and was a noted conductor of major avant-garde works.

name: Andrew Weatherall
headline: Andrew Weatherall, D.J. Who Broke Down Genre Barriers, Dies at 56
abstract: Also a record producer, he shaped London’s fertile club scene in the late 1980s and ’90s and helped meld rock and dance music.

name: Charles Hobson
profession: Helped Break a TV Color Line
headline: Charles Hobson, Who Helped Break a TV Color Line, Dies at 83
abstract: He produced programs, like “Inside Bedford-Stuyvesant” and “Like It Is,” that exposed a wide audience to the black experience.

name: José Zalaquett
profession: Leader in Chiles Search for Truth
headline: José Zalaquett, Leader in Chile’s Search for Truth, Dies at 77
abstract: He incurred the wrath of the dictator Augusto Pinochet, was exiled, and became an expert in how to heal traumatized countries.

name: Lynn Cohen
profession: Magda on Sex and the City
headline: Lynn Cohen, Magda on ‘Sex and the City,’ Is Dead at 86
abstract: She had a long career onstage and on film and TV. But she found her greatest fame late in life, as a stern housekeeper on a hit HBO series.

name: Johni Cerny
profession: Helped the Famous Find Their Roots
headline: Johni Cerny Dies at 76; Helped the Famous Find Their Roots
abstract: Fascinated by family trees since childhood, she became, Henry Louis Gates Jr. said, “the proverbial dean of American genealogical research.”

name: Valaida Snow
headline: Overlooked No More: Valaida Snow, Charismatic ‘Queen of the Trumpet’
abstract: She was not just a master musician, singer and dancer; she was also a teller of tall tales whose interviews could be as much a performance as her stage act.

name: Philip Leder
headline: Philip Leder, Who Helped Decipher the Genetic Code, Dies at 85
abstract: Dr. Leder, who also discovered a genetic cause of cancer, said he got his best scientific ideas while listening to classical music.

name: B. Smith
profession: Model Turned Restaurateur and Lifestyle Guru
headline: B. Smith, Model Turned Restaurateur and Lifestyle Guru, Dies at 70
abstract: Often called the black Martha Stewart, Ms. Smith wrote books on cooking and entertaining, had a syndicated television show, and created a line of products.

name: L.J. Smith
profession: Author of Vampire Diaries Book Series
headline: L.J. Smith, Author of ‘Vampire Diaries’ Book Series, Dies at 66
abstract: She wrote seven books in a series that went on to be a hit TV show. After she was replaced by ghostwriters, she reclaimed her characters online in fan fiction.

name: Katherine Johnson
headline: Katherine Johnson Dies at 101; Mathematician Broke Barriers at NASA
abstract: She was one of a group of black women mathematicians at NASA and its predecessor who were celebrated in the 2016 movie “Hidden Figures.”

name: John Franzese
headline: John Franzese, Mafioso Who Consorted With Celebrities, Dies at 103
abstract: Prosecutors said Sonny Franzese, a No. 2 in the Colombo organization, was a fearsome killer and an enduring mob “earner,” remaining active into his 90s.

name: Thich Quang Do
headline: Thich Quang Do, Defiant Rights Champion in Vietnam, Dies at 91
abstract: As the patriarch of a banned Buddhist church, he endured prison, house arrest and internal exile but refused to bend to the Communist authorities.

name: Diana Serra Cary
headline: Diana Serra Cary, ‘Baby Peggy’ of Silent Films, Dies at 101
abstract: Ms. Cary, who endured poverty and heartbreak after her parents squandered her fortune, went on to become an author and film historian as an adult.

name: Hosni Mubarak
profession: Egyptian Leader Ousted in Arab Spring
headline: Hosni Mubarak, Egyptian Leader Ousted in Arab Spring, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Mubarak, who had been likened to a modern-day pharaoh, was deposed in 2011 by the popular unrest in the Arab world that came to be called the Arab Spring.

name: Anne Marion
headline: Anne Marion, Texas Rancher, Heiress and Arts Patron, Dies at 81
abstract: A fourth-generation owner of one of the biggest ranches in Texas, she helped build museums, including the Georgia O’Keeffe Museum in Santa Fe.

name: Michael Hertz
headline: Michael Hertz — You’ve Surely Seen His Subway Map — Dies at 87
abstract: In 1979 his firm came up with the New York City subway map that is the basis for the one still used.

name: Clive Cussler
headline: Clive Cussler, Best-Selling Author and Adventurer, Is Dead at 88
abstract: His literary fantasies and larger-than-life exploits swirled together for decades. He wrote 85 books, selling no fewer than 100 million copies, and located scores of shipwrecks.

name: Claire Bretécher
headline: Claire Bretécher, Satirical French Cartoonist, Dies at 79
abstract: She was so incisive about the human condition that in 1976 the philosopher Roland Barthes called her the “best sociologist of the year.”

name: David Roback
profession: Founder of the Band Mazzy Star
headline: David Roback, 61, a Founder of the Band Mazzy Star, Is Dead
abstract: The group, which he formed with Hope Sandoval, had a haunting, ethereal sound and a surprise hit with “Fade Into You.”

name: Stanley Dudrick
headline: Dr. Stanley Dudrick, Who Saved Post-Surgical Patients, Dies at 84
abstract: Why were they dying after “successful” operations? He discovered the cause and came up with a remedy:  intravenous nutrition — a technique that has saved millions of lives.

name: Louis A. Craco
headline: Louis A. Craco, Who Recruited Lawyers for Poor, Dies at 86
abstract: He was a founder of Volunteers of Legal Service, which enlisted private firms and corporations. He also helped streamline New York City’s bureaucracy.

name: Linda Wolfe
profession: Wrote of Preppie Murder and Other Crimes
headline: Linda Wolfe, 87, Dies; Wrote of ‘Preppie Murder’ and Other Crimes
abstract: She probed the psychology of mostly upper-class perpetrators, saying their personal histories interested her more than the crimes themselves.

name: Lisel Mueller
headline: Lisel Mueller, Pulitzer-Winning Poet, Dies at 96
abstract: Her themes included language, nature and history, including her own flight from Nazi Germany.

name: Freeman Dyson
headline: Freeman Dyson, Math Genius Turned Technological Visionary, Dies at 96
abstract: After an early breakthrough on light and matter, he became a writer who challenged climate science and pondered space exploration and nuclear warfare.

name: Charles Friedgood
headline: Dr. Charles Friedgood, Paroled Wife Killer, Is Dead at 99
abstract: Terminally ill with cancer, he was released from prison in 2007 after serving 31 years, then lived another decade. His death, in 2018, went unnoticed.

name: Lynn Evans Mand
profession: Voice on Mr. Sandman and Lollipop
headline: Lynn Evans Mand, 95, Dies; a Voice on ‘Mr. Sandman’ and ‘Lollipop’
abstract: With Ms. Mand on lead vocals, the Chordettes reached the top of the pop charts in the 1950s

name: Johnny Antonelli
headline: Johnny Antonelli, Star Pitcher for the Giants, Dies at 89
abstract: He helped them win the World Series in 1954, when they played in New York, and remained an essential part of the team after they moved to San Francisco.

name: Gerald Krone
headline: Gerald Krone, a Negro Ensemble Company Founder, Dies at 86
abstract: He provided the administrative know-how that got the theater troupe off the ground in 1967. That he was white drew some criticism.

name: Lee Phillip Bell
profession: Soap Opera Creator and Talk Show Host
headline: Lee Phillip Bell, Soap Opera Creator and Talk Show Host, Dies at 91
abstract: She and her husband developed “The Young and the Restless” and “The Bold and the Beautiful” while she also worked as a broadcast journalist in Chicago.

name: Joe Coulombe
headline: Joe Coulombe, Who Founded Trader Joe’s, Dies at 89
abstract: “Equal parts gourmet shop, discount warehouse and Tiki trading post,” his stores caught on in Southern California and, eventually, beyond.

name: Ernesto Cardenal
headline: Ernesto Cardenal, Nicaraguan Priest, Poet and Revolutionary, Dies at 95
abstract: Father Cardenal defied the Roman Catholic Church in the 1980s by serving as a minister in the revolutionary government of Nicaragua.

name: Jack Welch
headline: Jack Welch, G.E. Chief Who Became a Business Superstar, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Welch was named “manager of the century” after General Electric’s revenue jumped nearly fivefold during his tenure.

name: James Lipton
headline: James Lipton, ‘Inside the Actors Studio’ Host, Dies at 93
abstract: His in-depth conversations with celebrities on the program focused on craft, not gossip, and made the show a hit on Bravo.

name: Ulay
headline: Ulay, Boundary-Pushing Performance Artist, Dies at 76
abstract: He made his name during a 12-year creative and romantic partnership with Marina Abramovic.

name: Matvey Natanzon
headline: Matvey Natanzon, a.k.a. Falafel the Backgammon King, Dies at 51
abstract: A Russian-born émigré by way of Israel, he made a gambler’s living taking on challengers, and often hustling them, in becoming the world’s ranking player.

name: Bobbie Battista
headline: Bobbie Battista, a Mainstay Anchor at CNN, Dies at 67
abstract: She covered world events in the 1980s and ’90s and was the host of “TalkBack Live,” a program in which the audience posed questions to guest newsmakers.

name: Stanislaw Kania
headline: Stanislaw Kania, 92, Polish Leader During Solidarity’s Rise, Dies
abstract: Mr. Kania walked a tightrope between demands for reform within Poland and the Soviet threat of intervention.

name: Rafael Cancel Miranda
headline: Rafael Cancel Miranda, Gunman in ’54 Attack on Congress, Dies at 89
abstract: He and three others opened fire on a crowded House chamber in the cause of Puerto Rican independence. Some saw him as a terrorist, others as a hero.

name: Henry Cobb
profession: Courtly Architect of Bostons Hancock Tower
headline: Henry Cobb, Courtly Architect of Boston’s Hancock Tower, Dies at 93
abstract: He was I.M. Pei’s unsung partner for nearly four decades but was responsible for a celebrated body of work in his own right, including New England’s tallest building.

name: Rosalind P. Walter
profession: First Rosie the Riveter and a PBS Funder
headline: Rosalind P. Walter, 95, First ‘Rosie the Riveter’ and a PBS Funder, Dies
abstract: A daughter of privilege who worked on an assembly line during World War II, she became a principal benefactor of public television, her name intoned on a host of programs.

name: Nexhmije Hoxha
headline: Nexhmije Hoxha, ‘Lady Macbeth’ of Albania, Dies at 99
abstract: A political partner with her Communist dictator husband, they isolated their small Balkan nation, executed dissidents and drove the economy to collapse.

name: Nick Apollo Forte
profession: Has-Been Singer in Broadway Danny Rose
headline: Nick Apollo Forte, 81, Has-Been Singer in ‘Broadway Danny Rose,’ Is Dead
abstract: In a very brief acting career, Mr. Forte played a small-time lounge singer opposite Woody Allen as his bottom-feeding agent in a hit 1984 comedy.

name: Ann Grifalconi
headline: Ann Grifalconi, Whose Children’s Books Bridged Cultures, Dies at 90
abstract: Her books, notably “The Village of Round and Square Houses,” set in Central Africa, introduced young readers to stories from different cultures.

name: Javier Pérez de Cuéllar
headline: Javier Pérez de Cuéllar Dies at 100; U.N. Chief Brokered Peace Pacts
abstract: A cultured diplomat from Peru, Mr. Pérez de Cuéllar was a reluctant compromise choice for secretary general but proved remarkably successful in the war-torn 1980s and ‘90s.

name: Zara Steiner
headline: Zara Steiner, Historian Who Explored World War I’s Roots, Dies at 91
abstract: Following history’s paper trail, she wrote about the failures of diplomacy and the period between the world wars.

name: Amory Houghton Jr.
headline: Amory Houghton Jr., Who Went From Corning to Congress, Dies at 93
abstract: He led his family’s venerable glass works company before entering the House from upstate New York and becoming a voice of moderation in a hard-right Republican Party.

name: Joyce Gordon
profession: Broke the Glasses Ceiling on TV
headline: Joyce Gordon, Who Broke the Glasses Ceiling on TV, Dies at 90
abstract: As a bespectacled pitchwoman, she defied a stereotype. She was also a screen actors’ labor leader and a familiar voice (“The number you have reached is no longer in service”).

name: Henri Richard
profession: Hall of Fame Center for Montreal Canadiens
headline: Henri Richard, Hall of Fame Center for Montreal Canadiens, Dies at 84
abstract: Richard played on 11 Stanley Cup-winning teams — five of them with his illustrious brother Maurice — and holds the record for game appearances with the Canadiens.

name: McCoy Tyner
headline: McCoy Tyner, Jazz Piano Powerhouse, Is Dead at 81
abstract: With his rich, percussive playing, he gained notice with John Coltrane’s groundbreaking quartet, then went on to influence virtually every pianist in jazz.

name: Alan Turner
profession: Artist of the Evocative and the Odd
headline: Alan Turner, Artist of the Evocative and the Odd, Dies at 76
abstract: Some of his paintings were of shimmering forests. Others were of disarranged body parts.

name: Audrey Sutherland
headline: Overlooked No More: Audrey Sutherland, Paddler of Her Own Canoe
abstract: Long before solo adventure travel became a trend among women, Sutherland was a pioneer, traveling around the world in her inflatable kayak.

name: Alexei Botyan
headline: Alexei Botyan, Soviet Spy Hailed as ‘Hero,’ Dies at 103
abstract: The Russians say he saved the Polish city of Krakow from being destroyed by the Nazis, but historians say that is a fiction of the Putin era.

name: Eva Szekely
profession: Survived Holocaust to Win Olympic Gold
headline: Eva Szekely Dies at 92; Survived Holocaust to Win Olympic Gold
abstract: Szekely, a Hungarian, became an Olympic champion after she was nearly killed during the Nazi occupation of Hungary.

name: Troy Collings
headline: Troy Collings, 33, Who Took Travelers Into North Korea, Dies
abstract: His company takes travelers to “destinations your mother would rather you stay away from.” One client was Otto Warmbier, who was imprisoned and fell into a coma.

name: Gray Kunz
profession: Four-Star Chef Fused France and Asia
headline: Gray Kunz, 65, Dies; Four-Star Chef Fused France and Asia
abstract: Raised in Singapore, trained in Hong Kong and apprenticed in Switzerland, he made a celebrated mark in New York at Lespinasse.

name: Steve Weber
profession: Founder of an Influential Folk Band
headline: Steve Weber, 76, a Founder of an Influential Folk Band, Dies
abstract: Mr. Weber and Peter Stampfel were the heart of the Holy Modal Rounders, a group born of the folk revival. It then detoured into a mischievous, “zany” style.

name: Max von Sydow
profession: Star of Seventh Seal and Exorcist
headline: Max von Sydow, Star of ‘Seventh Seal’ and ‘Exorcist,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Widely hailed as one of the finest actors of his generation, Mr. von Sydow formed a close relationship with the director Ingmar Bergman and became an elder pop culture star.

name: Mart Crowley
headline: Mart Crowley, ‘Boys in the Band’ Playwright, Dies at 84
abstract: When it opened in 1968, the play broke new ground in its depiction of gay characters.

name: Charles Urstadt
headline: Charles Urstadt, Who Eased N.Y. Rent Controls, Dies at 91
abstract: As state housing commissioner, he pushed a law that let landlords charge market rates when apartments became vacant. He also shepherded Battery Park City.

name: Anton Coppola
headline: Anton Coppola, Opera Conductor in Filmmaking Clan, Dies at 102
abstract: A seemingly ageless composer and maestro, he completed Puccini’s unfinished “Turandot,” wrote the opera “Sacco and Vanzetti” and led a concert of his music at 100.

name: Jamey Gambrell
profession: Made Russian Writing Sing, in English
headline: Jamey Gambrell Dies at 65; Made Russian Writing Sing, in English
abstract: A pre-eminent translator of contemporary Russian authors like Tatyana Tolstaya and Vladimir Sorokin, she won a prestigious prize for translation in 2016.

name: Barbara Neely
headline: Barbara Neely, Activist Turned Mystery Writer, Dies at 78
abstract: Her creation Blanche White was probably the first fictional black maid to solve a murder while working for a wealthy white family.

name: Peregrine Pollen
headline: Peregrine Pollen, Who Livened Up Auctions, Dies at 89
abstract: Running Parke-Bernet in New York in the 1960s after a merger with Sotheby’s, Mr. Pollen injected fun into the proceedings while expanding the business.

name: Keith Olsen
profession: Rock Hitmaker With a Broad Résumé
headline: Keith Olsen, Rock Hitmaker With a Broad Résumé, Dies at 74
abstract: He worked on albums by the Grateful Dead, Santana, Pat Benatar and Whitesnake. He also brought Stevie Nicks and Lindsey Buckingham to Fleetwood Mac.

name: J. Seward Johnson Jr.
headline: J. Seward Johnson Jr., Sculptor of the Hyper-Real, Dies at 89
abstract: His works often caught passers-by unawares. One was so lifelike that, after 9/11, firefighters are said to have tried to rescue it.

name: Del Shofner
profession: Master Pass Receiver With the Giants
headline: Del Shofner, Master Pass Receiver With the Giants, Dies at 85
abstract: The long-distance throws he caught from Y.A. Tittle thrilled fans and led the team to three straight league championship games in the ’60s.

name: Dana Zatopkova
headline: Dana Zatopkova, Champion Javelin Thrower, Is Dead at 97
abstract: She is best remembered for winning the gold medal at the 1952 Helsinki Olympics, just an hour after her husband, Emil Zatopek, won the men’s 5,000-meter run.

name: Ni Gusti Ayu Raka Rasmi
headline: Overlooked No More: Ni Gusti Ayu Raka Rasmi, Balinese Dancer
abstract: At the age of 12 she was the star of a troupe that performed in 1952 at theaters in the United States and Europe.

name: Andreas Brown
profession: Longtime Owner of Gotham Book Mart
headline: Andreas Brown, Longtime Owner of Gotham Book Mart, Dies at 86
abstract: An appraiser and archivist, he bought the celebrated mid-Manhattan shop in 1967 from its founder, Frances Steloff and ran it for 40 years.

name: Charles Wuorinen
headline: Charles Wuorinen, Uncompromising Modernist Composer, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Wuorinen won a Pulitzer Prize at 31 and went on to write a large body of mainly atonal works, including the opera “Brokeback Mountain.”

name: Tom Turnipseed
headline: Tom Turnipseed, a ‘Reformed Racist’ After Backing Wallace, Dies at 83
abstract: He supported George Wallace’s 1968 presidential bid. But after a change of heart, he worked for civil rights and other progressive causes.

name: Herb Goldsmith
profession: Man Behind the Members Only Jacket
headline: Herb Goldsmith, the Man Behind the Members Only Jacket, Dies at 92
abstract: An aggressive marketer, he used celebrities to promote his brand. Frank Sinatra, Johnny Carson and two presidents wore his jackets.

name: Genesis Breyer P-Orridge
headline: Genesis Breyer P-Orridge, Musician, Artist and Provocateur, Dies at 70
abstract: Genesis achieved cult notoriety leading the British rock bands Throbbing Gristle and Psychic TV, and later pushed the limits of gender in a surgical project to merge identities with her wife.

name: Eric Taylor
headline: Eric Taylor, Poetic Texas Singer-Songwriter, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Revered by peers like Lyle Lovett, he fused a brooding yet tender melodicism with evocative stream-of-consciousness narration, to hypnotic effect.

name: Betsy Byars
headline: Betsy Byars, Who Wrote of Deserted Children, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Ms. Byars’s award-winning children’s books, including “The Summer of the Swans” and “The Night Swimmers,” often dealt with abandonment.

name: Vittorio Gregotti
headline: Vittorio Gregotti, Modernist Architect, Dies in Pandemic at 92
abstract: With works like Barcelona’s Olympic Stadium, he combined a respect for older traditions with bold expressions of the new. He had contracted the coronavirus in his native Italy.

name: Elinor Ross
headline: Elinor Ross, Met Soprano With Illness-Shortened Career, Dies at 93
abstract: In 1970 she stepped in on short notice at the Metropolitan Opera. Nine years later, Bell’s palsy sidelined her.

name: Stuart Whitman
profession: Leading Man on Big and Small Screens
headline: Stuart Whitman, Leading Man on Big and Small Screens, Dies at 92
abstract: Known for his studied portrayals of complex characters, he earned an Oscar nomination for his role as a convicted child molester in “The Mark.”

name: Lyle Waggoner
profession: TV Star as Actor and Announcer
headline: Lyle Waggoner, a TV Star as Actor and Announcer, Dies at 84
abstract: He first achieved fame as both a voice and a sketch performer on “The Carol Burnett Show.” He later became even more famous on “Wonder Woman.”

name: Tonie Marshall
headline: Tonie Marshall Dies at 68; French Filmmaker Took On Sexism
abstract: A French-American actress and director, she helped open up a male-dominated movie industry to more women.

name: Eduard Limonov
headline: Eduard Limonov, Russian Writer and Dissident, Dies at 77
abstract: He wrote colorful books based on his time in exile in New York. His politics were just as colorful.

name: Alfred Worden
profession: Orbited Moon and Walked in Deep Space
headline: Alfred Worden, 88, Dies; Orbited Moon and Walked in Deep Space
abstract: While two Apollo 15 crewmen roamed the lunar surface on a scientific mission, he took valuable photographs from the space capsule.

name: Richard Hanna
headline: Richard Hanna, Republican Who Opposed Trump, Dies at 69
abstract: A New York Congressman, he broke with his party in 2016 and endorsed Hillary Clinton for president, saying Trump was “unfit” for office.

name: Catherine Hamlin
headline: Catherine Hamlin, 96, Dies; Pioneering Doctor Treated Childbirth Injury
abstract: She helped develop reconstructive surgery techniques to treat tens of thousands of women in Ethiopia with a condition called obstetric fistula.

name: Mal Sharpe
headline: Mal Sharpe, Groundbreaker in Street-Level Pranking, Dies at 83
abstract: Long before late-night talk show hosts began doing it, he conducted absurd interviews with gullible passersby with his comedic partner, Jim Coyle.

name: Molly Brodak
profession: Poet and Memoirist of Her Fathers Crimes
headline: Molly Brodak, Poet and Memoirist of Her Father’s Crimes, Dies at 39
abstract: Her father robbed 11 banks in and around Detroit when she was a teenager to pay off debts. But his sprees were just the jumping off point for her unsparing memoir.

name: Doriot Anthony Dwyer
headline: Doriot Anthony Dwyer, Flutist and Orchestral Pathbreaker, Dies at 98
abstract: Related to Susan B. Anthony, Ms. Dwyer was only the second woman to win a principal chair in a major American orchestra.

name: Boris Yaro
headline: Boris Yaro, Whose Photo of an Assassination Endures, Dies at 81
abstract: In June 1968, Mr. Yaro took one of the seminal images of the killing of Robert F. Kennedy.

name: Charles Trimble
headline: Charles Trimble, Advocate for Native American Rights, Dies at 84
abstract: He dedicated his life to advancing the tribal causes of self-determination, sovereignty and human rights.

name: Danny Ray Thompson
profession: Mainstay of Sun Ras Otherworldly Band
headline: Danny Ray Thompson, 72, Dies; Mainstay of Sun Ra’s Otherworldly Band
abstract: For the better part of five decades, he was the baritone saxophonist and linchpin of one of the most idiosyncratic and influential ensembles in jazz.

name: Maggie Griffin
profession: Kathys Mother and a D-List Celebrity
headline: Maggie Griffin, Kathy’s Mother and a ‘D-List’ Celebrity, Dies at 99
abstract: Ms. Griffin was a co-star on her daughter’s reality show, “My Life on the D-List,” and became something of a colorful celebrity herself.

name: Suzy Delair
profession: French Star of Movies and Music Halls
headline: Suzy Delair, French Star of Movies and Music Halls, Dies at 102
abstract: Her career included a long association with the director Henri-Georges Clouzot and a starring role in Laurel and Hardy’s last film.

name: James Hatch
headline: James Hatch, Archivist of Black Theater, Dies at 91
abstract: A scholar and historian, he amassed an invaluable trove of interviews and other material with his wife, the filmmaker Camille Billops.

name: Kenny Rogers
profession: Brought Country Music to a Pop Audience
headline: Kenny Rogers, Who Brought Country Music to a Pop Audience, Dies at 81
abstract: One of the first country artists to sell out arenas, Mr. Rogers sold more than 100 million records in a career that spanned decades.

name: Betty Williams
headline: Betty Williams, Peace Laureate From Northern Ireland, Dies at 76
abstract: She and Mairead Corrigan shared the 1976 Nobel Prize for galvanizing a mass movement to protest sectarian violence during the time known as the Troubles.

name: Bill Smith
headline: Bill Smith, Master of Two Musical Worlds, Is Dead at 93
abstract: As Bill Smith, he was a jazz clarinetist who played with Dave Brubeck. As William O. Smith, he was a composer who pioneered unorthodox techniques for his instrument.

name: Eli Miller
headline: Eli Miller, a Sultan of Seltzer, Is Dead at 86
abstract: He began delivering sparkling water in 1960, when hundreds of seltzer men plied the streets. He continued until 2017, when there were almost none.

name: Daniel S. Greenberg
headline: Daniel S. Greenberg, Science Journalist and Iconoclast, Dies at 88
abstract: He challenged peers who acted as “cheerleaders” for science, and influenced government science policy with a Washington-based newsletter.

name: Lorenzo Sanz
headline: Lorenzo Sanz, Who Led Comeback of Real Madrid, Dies at 76
abstract: He helped the soccer club win its first European Cup in 32 years. He is the most prominent Spaniard to die of the coronavirus.

name: Jeremy Marre
headline: Jeremy Marre, Documentarian of World Music, Is Dead at 76
abstract: With a minimal camera and sound crew, Mr. Marre traveled the world to film music and musicians on home turf that was often gritty and unglamorous.

name: Aurlus Mabele
headline: Aurlus Mabele, Congolese King of Soukous Music, Dies at 66
abstract: His up-tempo hits and high-wattage performances were highlighted by spectacular dance moves. He contracted the coronavirus and died in Paris.

name: Boris Stankovic
profession: Paved Way for N.B.A.s Dream Team
headline: Boris Stankovic, Who Paved Way for N.B.A.’s ‘Dream Team,’ Dies at 94
abstract: As the longtime head of FIBA, the international game’s governing body, he successfully lobbied to let pros play in the Olympics.

name: Eric Weissberg
headline: Eric Weissberg, ‘Dueling Banjos’ Musician, Dies at 80
abstract: His melodic banjo work on a 1973 hit single (heard in the movie “Deliverance”) helped usher bluegrass music into the cultural mainstream.

name: Manu Dibango
headline: Manu Dibango, Soulful Ambassador of African Music, Dies at 86
abstract: His 1972 hit “Soul Makossa” arrived at the dawn of the disco era and made its way to dance floors across the United States, Europe and Africa.

name: Wolf Kahn
headline: Wolf Kahn, Who Painted Vibrant Landscapes, Is Dead at 92
abstract: He played with color, creating scenes both calming and arresting. He said he wanted his colors “to be surprising to people without being offensive.”

name: Terrence McNally
headline: Terrence McNally, Tony-Winning Playwright of Gay Life, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. McNally, who died of coronavirus complications, introduced audiences to characters and situations that most mainstream theater had previously shunted into comic asides.

name: Nashom Wooden
headline: Nashom Wooden, Downtown Denizen, Is Dead at 50
abstract: He had survived every iteration of gay nightlife. Then came a sudden illness, believed to be the novel coronavirus.

name: Michael Broadbent
profession: Put Wine on the Auction Block
headline: Michael Broadbent, Who Put Wine on the Auction Block, Dies at 92
abstract: At Christie’s in London, he essentially created the notion that wine could be auctioned like furniture or art. He was also an influential wine writer.

name: Stanley Sporkin
headline: Stanley Sporkin, Bane of Corporate Corruption, Dies at 88
abstract: As the S.E.C.’s enforcer, he targeted firms that made illegal campaign contributions in the U.S. and bribed officials to gain business in other countries.

name: Albert Uderzo
profession: Co-Creator of French Comic Series Asterix
headline: Albert Uderzo, 92, Co-Creator of French Comic Series Asterix, Dies
abstract: He teamed up with the writer René Goscinny to create the mustachioed Gaul, whose adventures have sold hundreds of millions of comic books worldwide.

name: Richard Marek
headline: Richard Marek, Editor of Hemingway, Baldwin and Ludlum, Dies at 86
abstract: He shepherded more than 300 books into print, including James Baldwin’s “If Beale Street Could Talk” and Robert Ludlum’s “The Bourne Identity.”

name: Julia Miles
profession: Pushed for Gender Parity in the Theater
headline: Julia Miles, 90, Dies; Pushed for Gender Parity in the Theater
abstract: Concerned that female directors and playwrights were underrepresented in New York theaters, she founded Women’s Project in 1978 to cultivate their work.

name: Floyd Cardoz
profession: Gave American Fine Dining an Indian Flavor
headline: Floyd Cardoz, 59, Dies; Gave American Fine Dining an Indian Flavor
abstract: He was the first chef born and raised in India to lead an influential New York City kitchen, at Tabla. He died in the coronavirus pandemic.

name: Richard Reeves
headline: Richard Reeves, Columnist and Author on Presidents, Dies at 83
abstract: His books on Kennedy, Nixon, Clinton and others could be as unsparing as his syndicated column. He was also a familiar face on PBS public-affairs programs.

name: Maurice Berger
headline: Maurice Berger, Curator Outspoken About Race, Is Dead at 63
abstract: An influential art historian, he called out racism in the museum world, and in the broader culture as well.

name: Curly Neal
headline: Curly Neal, Globetrotters’ Dazzling Dribbler, Dies at 77
abstract: He admitted he “didn’t know anything about being funny” when he joined the comedic basketball team, but he became one of its biggest stars.

name: Mark Blum
headline: Mark Blum, a Familiar Face Off Broadway, Is Dead at 69
abstract: Mr. Blum, who died of coronavirus complications, was also seen on Broadway; in “Crocodile Dundee” and other movies; and on numerous television shows.

name: Kate Worley
headline: Overlooked No More: Kate Worley, a Pioneer Writer of Erotic Comics
abstract: Worley, who wrote Omaha the Cat Dancer, about a feline stripper, “injected a woman’s point of view” that helped the comic stand out from others in the 1980s.

name: Arnold Obey
headline: Arnold Obey, 73, Educator and Marathoner, Dies
abstract: Mr. Obey was a veteran school principal who took to marathoning and kept at it — 38 times in a row in the New York City Marathon.

name: Jenny Polanco
profession: Fashion Designer with a Caribbean Palette
headline: Jenny Polanco, Fashion Designer with a Caribbean Palette, Dies at 62
abstract: A breakthrough Dominican designer of clothing, jewelry and accessories, she worked across the Caribbean and in Paris and New York.

name: Dez-Ann Romain
headline: Dez-Ann Romain, Educator with Grit and Heart, Dies at 36
abstract: Ms. Romain ran a school for young people who fared better in a smaller setting; she was the first school employee in New York City to die of the coronavirus

name: Romi Cohn
headline: Romi Cohn Saved 56 Jewish Families. Coronavirus Took His Life
abstract: Mr. Cohn was only 15 when he began rescuing Jewish families in Czechoslovakia in 1944.

name: Alan Finder
headline: Alan Finder, 72, Unflappable Newspaper Journalist, Dies
abstract: At The Times, he vitalized what in lesser hands might have been benumbing explications of property tax assessments and revisions of the City Charter.

name: Stuart Gordon
headline: Stuart Gordon, Whose Films Reanimated Horror, Dies at 72
abstract: His low-budget movies, notably the cult favorite “Re-Animator,” combined grisly body horror with a mordant sense of humor.

name: Sol Kerzner
headline: Sol Kerzner, South African Casino Tycoon, Is Dead at 84
abstract: His Sun City resort let black and white people mingle in the apartheid era, but some saw it as an emblem of all that was wrong with that racial system.

name: Lucia Bosé
headline: Lucia Bosé, Whose Acting Was Interrupted by Marriage, Dies at 89
abstract: She appeared in films by Antonioni and Buñuel before marrying the bullfighter Luis Miguel Dominguín, then resumed her career after they split up.

name: John Sears
headline: John Sears, Strategist for Nixon and Reagan, Dies at 79
abstract: Some thought he was “Deep Throat,” the secret source who helped The Washington Post unravel Watergate. He was not.

name: Joseph E. Lowery
profession: Civil Rights Leader and King Aide
headline: Rev. Joseph E. Lowery, Civil Rights Leader and King Aide, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Lowery helped found the Southern Christian Leadership Conference and gave the benediction at President Barack Obama’s inauguration.

name: Tom Coburn
headline: Tom Coburn, the ‘Dr. No’ of Congress, Is Dead at 72
abstract: His prolific use of a bill-blocking measure earned him his nickname, but he also won grudging respect on Capitol Hill as a political maverick.

name: Ray Mantilla
headline: Ray Mantilla, Percussionist Who Transcended Genres, Dies at 85
