abstract: He was adept at a range of instruments, particularly the congas and timbales, and he could make himself at home in almost any ensemble.

name: Mike Longo
headline: Mike Longo, Jazz Pianist, Composer and Educator, Dies at 83
abstract: Best known for his long association with Dizzy Gillespie, Mr. Longo, who died of the coronavirus, also led a big band and promoted the work of other musicians.

name: Krzysztof Penderecki
headline: Krzysztof Penderecki, Polish Composer With Cinematic Flair, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Penderecki’s modernist compositions turned up in films like “The Exorcist” and influenced a generation of edgy rock musicians.

name: Michael Sorkin
profession: Saw Architecture as a Vehicle for Change
headline: Michael Sorkin, 71, Dies; Saw Architecture as a Vehicle for Change
abstract: Mr. Sorkin, who died of the coronavirus, promoted social justice in his prodigious output of essays, lectures and designs.

name: David Schramm
headline: David Schramm, Blustery Comic Foil in ‘Wings,’ Dies at 73
abstract: Though known from his TV role, he did much of his work on the stage, starting as an original Acting Company member.

name: Philip W. Anderson
headline: Philip W. Anderson, Nobel Laureate in Physics, Is Dead at 96
abstract: His work at Princeton and Bell Labs deepened science’s understanding of magnetism, superconductivity and the structure of matter.

name: Alan Merrill
profession: Songwriter of I Love Rock n Roll
headline: Alan Merrill, a Songwriter of ‘I Love Rock ’n’ Roll,’ Dies
abstract: The musician, who died of the coronavirus, had an early rock career in Japan before helping write the song that became Joan Jett’s breakthrough hit.

name: William Helmreich
profession: Sociologist and a Walker in the City
headline: William Helmreich, Sociologist and a Walker in the City, Dies at 74
abstract: A scholar of Judaism as well, he walked every block in New York — totaling 6,163 miles — and wrote a book about his odyssey. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Edward Tarr
headline: Edward Tarr, Renowned Trumpeter Who Delved Into Past, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Tarr was a scholar, teacher and performer who helped revive the natural trumpet, a sweet-sounding, valveless version of the modern instrument.

name: Zororo Makamba
headline: Zororo Makamba, 30, Dies; Zimbabwean Television Host
abstract: His death from the coronavirus was the first to be recorded in his southern African nation.

name: Joe Diffie
headline: Joe Diffie, Grammy-Winning Country Music Star, Dies at 61
abstract: He was known for his ballads and honky-tonk singles, like “Home” and “Pickup Man.” On Friday, he announced that he had tested positive for the coronavirus.

name: Tomie dePaola
headline: Tomie dePaola, ‘Strega Nona’ Author and Illustrator, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. dePaola wrote or illustrated more than 270 books, notably the beloved stories of a “grandma witch” with an eternally full pasta pot.

name: Chloe Aaron
headline: Chloe Aaron, a Top PBS Executive, Is Dead at 81
abstract: As one of TV’s highest-ranking women in the 1970s, she worked to broaden the audience for public television.

name: Kious Kelly
headline: Kious Kelly, a Nurse in the Covid Fight, Dies at 48
abstract: He may have been the first New York City nurse to be claimed by the virus. His death has been a rallying cry.

name: Steven Dick
headline: Steven Dick, British Diplomat in Hungary, Dies at 37
abstract: Mr. Dick, the deputy British ambassador to Hungary, always dreamed of working for the Foreign Office.

name: Jan Howard
profession: Singer and Writer of Country Hits
headline: Jan Howard, Singer and Writer of Country Hits, Dies at 91
abstract: A female star in Nashville when there weren’t many others, she found success as Bill Anderson’s duet partner and as a solo artist singing about the heartache she knew all too well.

name: April Dunn
headline: April Dunn, Louisiana Fighter for Disability Rights, Dies at 33
abstract: Ms. Dunn, who succumbed to the coronavirus, successfully pushed for legislation that provided alternative ways to gain a high school degree.

name: Roberto Stella
profession: Regional Doctor with a National Presence
headline: Roberto Stella, Regional Doctor with a National Presence, Dies at 67
abstract: Dr. Stella was listed as the first Italian physician to die of the coronavirus.

name: Hellmut Stern
profession: Violinist Returned to Germany After Fleeing
headline: Hellmut Stern, 91, Dies; Violinist Returned to Germany After Fleeing
abstract: He joined the Berlin Philharmonic after years in exile, setting what a colleague called “a unique example of reconciliation and forgiveness.”

name: Wallace Roney
headline: Wallace Roney, Jazz Trumpet Virtuoso, Is Dead at 59
abstract: Initially dismissed by some as a Miles Davis imitator, Mr. Roney, who has died of coronavirus complications, emerged as a major musician in his own right.

name: George Preti
profession: Studied Bodily Odors as Biological Clues
headline: George Preti, 75, Dies; Studied Bodily Odors as Biological Clues
abstract: In his “bizarre niche” of science, he sought to weaponize odors as a means to sniff out disease, even using dogs to do so.

name: James T. Goodrich
headline: Dr. James T. Goodrich, Who Operated on Conjoined Twins, Dies at 73
abstract: Dr. Goodrich led teams that did a series of celebrated surgeries. He was a victim of the coronavirus.

name: Joseph O’Hare
headline: The Rev. Joseph O’Hare, Resourceful President of Fordham, Dies at 89
abstract: He transformed the university into a national institution and played a major civic role as the overseer of New York City’s public campaign finance law.

name: Hilda Churchill
headline: Hilda Churchill, 108, Dies; Survived Wars and the 1918 Pandemic
abstract: The Spanish flu struck her entire family and killed her baby sister a century ago. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Manolis Glezos
profession: Tore Down Nazi Flag Over Athens
headline: Manolis Glezos Dies at 97; Tore Down Nazi Flag Over Athens
abstract: He became a national hero in the Greek resistance for a daring feat atop the Acropolis. He later endured prison and exile and pursued a leftist political career.

name: Lorena Borjas
headline: Lorena Borjas, Transgender Immigrant Activist, Dies at 59
abstract: She helped transgender women in Queens contend with human trafficking, health issues and possible deportation. Her death was attributed to the coronavirus.

name: Adam Schlesinger
headline: Adam Schlesinger, Songwriter for Rock, Film and the Stage, Dies at 52
abstract: He made suburban characters shine in Fountains of Wayne songs and brought pop-rock perfection to the film “That Thing You Do!” He died of coronavirus complications.

name: Kevin Thomas Duffy
headline: Kevin Thomas Duffy, U.S. Judge in Terrorism Cases, Dies at 87
abstract: An independent-minded jurist, he oversaw the World Trade Center bombing trial and another involving a plot to down jetliners. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Ellis Marsalis
profession: Jazz Pianist and Music Family Patriarch
headline: Ellis Marsalis, Jazz Pianist and Music Family Patriarch, Dies at 85
abstract: The father of Wynton and Branford Marsalis and a prominent performer and educator, he succumbed to complications of the coronavirus.

name: Bucky Pizzarelli
headline: Bucky Pizzarelli, Master of the Jazz Guitar, Is Dead at 94
abstract: He became a mainstay of the New York jazz scene, often performing with his celebrated son John. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Gerald Freedman
headline: Gerald Freedman, Prolific Stage Director, Dies at 92
abstract: Among his credits were musicals, operas and the original production of “Hair.” He influenced numerous actors’ careers as an educator.

name: John Murray
headline: Dr. John Murray, Pioneering Lung Expert, Dies at 92
abstract: Internationally recognized in pulmonology, he helped define acute respiratory distress syndrome, a condition that led to his death, attributed to the coronavirus.

name: Pape Diouf
profession: Former President of Marseille Soccer Club
headline: Pape Diouf, Former President of Marseille Soccer Club, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Diouf, who died of the coronavirus, was the first black president of Marseille, a notoriously difficult club to run. He was also a gifted orator and a defender of the club’s passionate fan base.

name: Arianne Caoili
headline: Arianne Caoili, Chess Master, Is Dead at 33
abstract: A former model, she stood out in the chess world for her glamour in what is often thought of as an unglamorous game.

name: Ken Shimura
headline: Ken Shimura, Comedian Whose Sketches Delighted Japan, Dies at 70
abstract: His slapstick humor, physical comedy and naïve persona made him a household name in the country for decades.

name: William Frankland
headline: William Frankland, Pioneering Allergist, Dies at 108
abstract: One of the top allergists of the 20th century, Dr. Frankland, who died of the coronavirus, helped legions of hay fever sneezers by publicizing pollen counts. Among his patients was Saddam Hussein.

name: Bill Withers
profession: Sang Lean on Me and Aint No Sunshine
headline: Bill Withers, Who Sang ‘Lean on Me’ and ‘Ain’t No Sunshine,’ Dies at 81
abstract: A three-time Grammy Award winner, he had a string of much-covered hits in the 1970s but had not released an album since 1985.

name: Gita Ramjee
headline: Gita Ramjee, a Leading AIDS Researcher, Dies at 63
abstract: Working in South Africa, she led studies and drug trials, hoping to overcome not only H.I.V. but also cultural barriers to stopping its spread. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Patricia Bosworth
headline: Patricia Bosworth, Actress-Turned-Author, Dies at 86
abstract: She gave up the stage for the writing life, publishing biographies of some famous friends and two powerful memoirs. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Nur Hassan Hussein
headline: Nur Hassan Hussein, Former Prime Minister of Somalia, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Hussein, who died after testing positive for coronavirus, led his country’s government during a crucial transitional period.

name: Harriet Glickman
profession: Pushed Peanuts to Add a Black Character
headline: Harriet Glickman, Who Pushed ‘Peanuts’ to Add a Black Character, Dies at 93
abstract: In 1968, at her urging, Charles M. Schulz added Franklin Armstrong to his enormously popular comic strip as a way to promote racial equality.

name: Edward Feightner
profession: Test Pilot and World War II Ace
headline: Edward Feightner, Test Pilot and World War II Ace, Dies at 100
abstract: Admiral Feightner played a leading role in the development of the Navy’s postwar jets.

name: Suellen Rocca
headline: Suellen Rocca, Founding Member of the Hairy Who, Dies at 76
abstract: She and five other Chicago artists came together in the 1960s to form a group whose rambunctious style tacked hard against prevailing art orthodoxies.

name: Michael McKinnell
profession: Architect of a Monumental City Hall
headline: Michael McKinnell, 84, Dies; Architect of a Monumental City Hall
abstract: His and Gerhard Kallmann’s sculptural and public-minded design for Boston helped spur the cityscape’s revival in the late 1960s. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Wilhelm Burmann
headline: Wilhelm Burmann, Teacher of Ballet’s Brightest, Dies at 80
abstract: For decades, he presided over a dance class in Manhattan, guiding stars with a sharp wit and a grand aim: instilling discipline and excellence.

name: Rafael Gómez Nieto
headline: Rafael Gómez Nieto, Last Member of Unit That Helped Liberate Paris, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Gómez, a veteran of the Spanish Civil War who served in a French unit that entered Paris in 1944, was infected by the coronavirus.

name: Mary Roman
headline: Mary Roman, City Clerk Who Set Senior Shot Put Records, Dies at 84
abstract: Mrs. Roman excelled at many field events, as well as local government. She succumbed to the coronavirus.

name: Cristina
headline: Cristina, Cult Downtown New York Singer, Dies at 64
abstract: A fixture in New York’s dance-music nightlife of the late ’70s and early ’80s, she gained new attention in 2004 when her albums were reissued.

name: Tom Dempsey
headline: Tom Dempsey, Record-Setting Kicker, Dies at 73
abstract: He was born without toes on his right foot, but spent 11 seasons in the N.F.L. and kicked 159 field goals. He died of complications of the coronavirus.

name: Bobby Mitchell
profession: Hall of Famer and the Redskins First Black Star
headline: Bobby Mitchell, Hall of Famer and the Redskins’ First Black Star, Dies at 84
abstract: He played four seasons with the Cleveland Browns and seven with the Redskins, the last N.F.L. team of his time to integrate.

name: Honor Blackman
headline: Honor Blackman, a Memorable James Bond Adversary, Dies at 94
abstract: In a long career she was best known for an early role: Pussy Galore, who declared herself immune to Agent 007’s charms before judo-flipping him.

name: Leïla Menchari
headline: Leïla Menchari, Who Turned Store Windows Into Art, Dies at 93
abstract: A longtime Hermès window dresser, she created fantastical worlds that held the gaze of passers-by. She died of the novel coronavirus.

name: E. Margaret Burbidge
headline: E. Margaret Burbidge, Astronomer Who Blazed Trails on Earth, Dies at 100
abstract: She was denied access to a telescope because of her sex, but Dr. Burbidge forged ahead anyway, going on to make pathbreaking discoveries about the cosmos.

name: Sergio Rossi
headline: Sergio Rossi, Italian Shoemaker and Ready-to-Wear Ally, Dies at 84
abstract: Known for his spindly heels and designer collaborations, Mr. Rossi was part of the postwar generation that transformed Italian fashion

name: Marguerite Derrida
headline: Marguerite Derrida, French Psychoanalyst and Translator, Dies at 87
abstract: A clinician by training, she translated major works in the field of psychoanalysis. She was the wife of Jacques Derrida, the French philosopher, for more than 40 years.

name: John G. Davies
profession: Rodney King Judge and Olympic Medalist
headline: John G. Davies, Rodney King Judge and Olympic Medalist, Dies at 90
abstract: A record-breaking swimmer, he was credited with helping to prevent further rioting for his handling of the second trial of four police officers.

name: Al Kaline
headline: Al Kaline, Tigers’ Perennial All-Around All-Star, Is Dead at 85
abstract: One of baseball’s finest hitters, he was also one of its best defensive outfielders, playing 22 seasons in Detroit. To Billy Martin, he was Mr. Perfection.

name: James Drury
headline: James Drury, Taciturn Star of ‘The Virginian,’ Dies at 85
abstract: A product of New York City and an Oregon ranch, he played the title character, a ranch foreman who is never named, for its entire nine-season run.

name: Vincent Lionti
headline: Vincent Lionti, Violist and Youth Orchestra Conductor, Dies at 60
abstract: He was a member of the Metropolitan Opera Orchestra for three decades, and also led an ensemble of young players in Westchester County.

name: Albert Petrocelli
headline: Albert Petrocelli, Fire Chief Who Lost a Son on 9/11, Dies at 73
abstract: He and a firefighter son answered the call when terrorists attacked the World Trade Center; another son died there. Mr. Petrocelli had the novel coronavirus.

name: Robert Barth
headline: Robert Barth, a Pioneer of Deep-Sea Diving, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Barth was the sole “aquanaut” to play a major role in all four stages of the Navy’s landmark program to open the depths to long-term habitation.

name: Sandra Santos-Vizcaino
headline: Sandra Santos-Vizcaino, Beloved Brooklyn Teacher, Dies at 54
abstract: The longtime educator is believed to be the first public-school teacher in New York City, the nation’s largest school district, to die of the coronavirus.

name: Judy Drucker
headline: Judy Drucker, Who Brought Miami Top-Notch Music, Dies at 91
abstract: She presented musicians, opera singers and dancers. “I don’t think of Judy as” an impresario, Itzhak Perlman said. “I think of her as a friend.”

name: Anita Fial
profession: Carried the Banner of Exotic Food
headline: Anita Fial, Who Carried the Banner of Exotic Food, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Fial worked to burnish the reputation of mangoes, avocados, radishes and celery, among other produce.

name: Idelle Weber
profession: Stretched the Meaning of Pop Art
headline: Idelle Weber, Who Stretched the Meaning of Pop Art, Dies at 88
abstract: One of the few women involved in the Pop Art movement, she captured the anonymity of corporate life in silhouettes. She later turned to realism.

name: David Driskell
headline: David Driskell, 88, Pivotal Champion of African-American Art, Dies
abstract: An artist himself, Professor Driskell recognized the role of black artists in the broader story of American art. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Ira Einhorn
headline: Ira Einhorn, Counterculture Guru and Murderer, Dies in Prison at 79
abstract: He preached peace, love and environmentalism. Then he killed his girlfriend, stuffed her body in a steamer trunk and fled to Europe.

name: John Prine
profession: Chronicled the Human Condition in Song
headline: John Prine, Who Chronicled the Human Condition in Song, Dies at 73
abstract: A singer and songwriter with a raspy voice and a gift for offbeat humor, he was revered by his peers, including Bob Dylan. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Anne Bass
headline: Anne Bass, 78, Arts Patron and Peerless Gardener, Dies
abstract: A leading philanthropist, she championed, without fanfare, the New York City Ballet and numerous art museums. She also loved her dahlias.

name: Hal Willner
headline: Hal Willner, Music Producer Who Melded Styles, Dies at 64
abstract: He was best known for assembling diverse casts of performers to play a slightly off-center body of work, and for obliterating the lines between genres.

name: Linda Tripp
headline: Linda Tripp, Key Figure in Clinton Impeachment, Dies at 70
abstract: She gave over her secretly recorded conversations with Monica Lewinsky to an independent prosecutor, a pivot point in his investigation of the president.

name: Ahmed Ismail Hussein
headline: Ahmed Ismail Hussein, Venerable Somali Musician, Dies at 91
abstract: Famously known as the “King of Oud,” Mr. Hussein was considered one of the giants of modern Somali music. He had the novel coronavirus.

name: Paul Kasmin
headline: Paul Kasmin, Gallerist Who Ruled a Mini-Empire of Art, Dies at 60
abstract: With his eclectic range and loyalty to living artists, one didn’t know what to expect on walking into one of his New York galleries.

name: Chynna
headline: Chynna, Model-Turned-Hip-Hop Artist, Dies at 25
abstract: The rapper, whose full name was Chynna Rogers, performed with ASAP Rocky’s hip-hop collective ASAP Mob.

name: Aileen Baviera
headline: Aileen Baviera, Leading Philippines Scholar of China, Dies at 60
abstract: Dr. Baviera studied in Beijing in the early 1980s, at the start of her lifelong fascination with China.

name: Mort Drucker
headline: Mort Drucker, Master of the Mad Caricature, Is Dead at 91
abstract: His illustrations of celebrities for Mad magazine’s movie and television satires inspired countless cartoonists. Actors, politicians and others knew they had made it when he drew them.

name: Ricardo Castaneda
headline: Ricardo Castaneda, Psychiatrist With Many Talents, Dies at 64
abstract: He was a writer and caricaturist who planned to treat his patients even after he was admitted to the hospital, where he died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Laneeka Barksdale
headline: Laneeka Barksdale, 47, a Detroit Ballroom Dancing Star, Is Dead
abstract: She was known for the glide and other challenging steps in a scene that has been hit hard by the coronavirus.

name: Greg Farrell
headline: Greg Farrell, Civic Reformer and Schools Innovator, Dies at 84
abstract: He applied the teamwork and confidence-building techniques of Outward Bound to the challenges of urban classroom education.

name: Ronald Lewis
profession: Preserver of New Orleans Black Culture
headline: Ronald Lewis, Preserver of New Orleans Black Culture, Dies at 68
abstract: His colorful museum, the House of Dance and Feathers, was a monument to the rich street culture of African-Americans. Mr. Lewis died of the coronavirus.

name: F.N. Souza
headline: Overlooked No More: F.N. Souza, India’s Anti-Establishment Artist
abstract: Souza, who started a collective of renegade artists in 1947, embraced the sacred and profane in erotically charged images. Several of his paintings fetched record auction prices for Indian art.

name: Zhang Lifa
headline: Zhang Lifa, Veteran Who Worked on China’s Nuclear Program, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Zhang, like his father, felt an impulse to serve his country from a young age, but he paid a price from long-term exposure to radiation.

name: Alan T. Ortiz
profession: Veteran of Philippine Government and Business
headline: Alan T. Ortiz, a Veteran of Philippine Government and Business, Dies at 66
abstract: Mr. Ortiz traveled to Paris in March for an international conference and was exposed there to the coronavirus.

name: Michael C. Cooper
headline: Michael C. Cooper, Convicted in Tax Scam, Dies a Prisoner at 66
abstract: Seeing an opportunity to profit off widespread resentment over the tax system, he ensnared 50,000 Americans who sought to dodge the I.R.S.

name: Earl G. Graves Sr.
headline: Earl G. Graves Sr., a Voice for Black Entrepreneurs, Dies at 85
abstract: In 1970 he founded Black Enterprise magazine to encourage his fellow African-American professionals. He later collected his advice in a best-selling book.

name: Jean-Laurent Cochet
headline: Jean-Laurent Cochet, Actor Who Taught France’s Stars, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Cochet, who had the coronavirus, was a major figure in French theater. His students included Gérard Depardieu and Isabelle Huppert.

name: Victor Skrebneski
headline: Victor Skrebneski, Who Captured Stars in Striking Photos, Dies at 90
abstract: His career began when he found a camera in a park as a boy. A famous campaign for Estée Lauder followed, as did images of celebrities in black turtlenecks.

name: Yaakov Perlow
profession: Head of Hasidic Dynasty in Brooklyn
headline: Rabbi Yaakov Perlow, Head of Hasidic Dynasty in Brooklyn, Dies at 89
abstract: He was the third Novominsker Rebbe and also led Agudath Israel of America, an umbrella organization for Haredi Jews.

name: William R. Polk
headline: William R. Polk, Historian and Middle East Envoy, Dies at 91
abstract: He wrote and edited many books, but he was no armchair academic — he crossed a desert by camel in part to understand a poem.

name: Phyllis Lyon
profession: Lesbian Activist and Gay Marriage Trailblazer
headline: Phyllis Lyon, Lesbian Activist and Gay Marriage Trailblazer, Dies at 95
abstract: When Ms. Lyon married her partner of 55 years in 2008, they formed the first legal gay union in California.

name: Bruce Baillie
headline: Bruce Baillie, ‘Essential’ Avant-Garde Filmmaker, Dies at 88
abstract: He became known in the mid-1960s for his lyrical landscape films. His most extraordinary work is a simple, single panning shot.

name: Andy González
headline: Andy González, Prolific Latin Jazz Bassist, Is Dead at 69
abstract: A busy studio musician, he was also a key part of two influential groups: the Fort Apache Band, which he founded with his brother Jerry, and Libre.

name: Dario Gabbai
headline: Dario Gabbai, a Final Witness to Auschwitz, Is Dead at 97
abstract: He was among the last Sonderkommandos, prisoners forced by the Nazis to herd fellow inmates into the gas chambers.

name: S. Fred Singer
headline: S. Fred Singer, a Leading Climate Change Contrarian, Dies at 95
abstract: Derided as a “Merchant of Doubt,” he spent decades trying to refute the evidence of global warming and other environmental risks.

name: Ruth B. Mandel
headline: Ruth B. Mandel, a Voice for Women in Politics, Dies at 81
abstract: Her experience fleeing the Nazis on the doomed “Voyage of the Damned” informed her faith in democracy as head of the Eagleton Institute of Politics.

name: Stirling Moss
profession: One of the Greatest Drivers of All Time
headline: Stirling Moss, One of the Greatest Drivers of All Time, Dies at 90
abstract: Known for his brash, puckish persona, he won 212 of his 529 races, including 16 Grand Prix victories, but never won the Grand Prix Championship title.

name: Rafael Callejas
profession: Honduran Ex-President Convicted in FIFA Case
headline: Rafael Callejas, Honduran Ex-President Convicted in FIFA Case, Dies at 76
abstract: Unlike many others, he admitted his guilt in the global soccer corruption scandal and was awaiting sentencing.

name: Doug Sanders
headline: Doug Sanders, ‘Peacock of the Fairways,’ Dies at 86
abstract: A colorful dresser who was a fan favorite on the PGA Tour, he won 20 events but no major tournaments, missing a crucial putt at the British Open.

name: Israel Sauz
headline: Israel Sauz, Gas-Station Worker and New Father, Dies at 22
abstract: He graduated from high school in Tulsa, Okla., four years ago. He worked at QuikTrip and his son was born a month ago. Then he died of the coronavirus.

name: Lila Fenwick
profession: Broke a Barrier at Harvard Law
headline: Lila Fenwick, Who Broke a Barrier at Harvard Law, Dies at 87
abstract: She was the first black female graduate of the school and went on to a career at the United Nations; she also was a major supporter of sickle cell research. She was a victim of the coronavirus.

name: Onaje Allan Gumbs
headline: Onaje Allan Gumbs, Musically Ecumenical Pianist, Is Dead at 70
abstract: As a musician, composer and arranger, Mr. Gumbs was a close collaborator with stars across musical styles.

name: Sam Clayton Jr.
profession: Sound Engineer With a Global Ear
headline: Sam Clayton Jr., Sound Engineer With a Global Ear, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Clayton, who died of the coronavirus, worked with reggae musicians from Jamaica and countries far from the music’s birthplace.

name: Richard Brodsky
headline: Richard Brodsky, Legislator Known as Albany’s Conscience, Dies at 73
abstract: A 14-term Assemblyman from Westchester County, he was instrumental in empowering New York State to monitor its 700 quasi-public authorities.

name: Craig Gilbert
headline: Craig Gilbert, 94, Dies; Created Groundbreaking ‘American Family’
abstract: Airing in 1973 and making national stars out of the Loud family, it is now considered the first reality TV show. It had people buzzing then, and fighting.

name: Irene Inouye
headline: Irene Inouye, 71, Fund-Raising Champion of Japanese-Americans, Dies
abstract: She headed two major foundations, established a Japanese-American museum and, the widow of a senator, quietly helped lift Detroit out of bankruptcy.

name: Irena Chalmers
headline: Irena Chalmers, 84, Is Dead; Writer Anticipated a Food Revolution
abstract: She wrote her first cookbook, “Fondue Cook-In,” to help sell pots. She went on to discover chefs who would become well-known cooking authorities.

name: Hank Steinbrenner
headline: Hank Steinbrenner, an Heir to the Yankees, Is Dead at 63
abstract: After the death of their father, George, in 2010, he and his younger brother, Hal, took over the franchise. But Hal was given the bigger role.

name: Wynn Handman
headline: Wynn Handman, Influential Director and Teacher, Dies at 97
abstract: At the American Place Theater, he championed new works. In his acting classes, he nurtured countless future stars. His death was related to the coronavirus.

name: Antonio Checo
headline: Antonio Checo, Episcopal Priest Who Stressed Service, Dies at 67
abstract: His years as a social worker led him to preach community engagement as the rector of St. Mark’s Church in Jackson Heights, Queens.

name: Darius Swann
headline: Darius Swann, Plaintiff in Landmark Busing Case, Dies at 95
abstract: A former missionary, he sued the local school system in North Carolina when his 6-year-old son could not attend class two blocks away.

name: Albert K. Webster
profession: Built Up the New York Philharmonic
headline: Albert K. Webster, Who Built Up the New York Philharmonic, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Webster, who had the coronavirus, lived and breathed the Philharmonic as a career orchestra administrator and consultant.

name: Robby Browne
headline: Robby Browne, Real Estate Player and Philanthropist, Dies at 72
abstract: As a top agent in New York City, he socialized with celebrities and the business elite. He also contributed to numerous AIDS- and gay-related charities.

name: Joseph Migliucci
headline: Joseph Migliucci, Fixture at Storied Bronx Restaurant, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Migliucci’s family-owned restaurant on Arthur Avenue, Mario’s, celebrated its 100th anniversary last year. He fell victim to the coronavirus.

name: Michael Angel Bastiaans
headline: Michael Angel Bastiaans, Beloved Indonesian Teacher, Dies at 31
abstract: He was the kind of teacher who gave his lunch to a hungry student and dug into his own pocket to help others in need.

name: Kimarlee Nguyen
headline: Kimarlee Nguyen, Writer Who Explored Cambodian Roots, Dies at 33
abstract: Ms. Nguyen’s writing career was budding; she was also an inspiring teacher of first-generation Americans. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Stuart Cohen
headline: Stuart Cohen, Cabdriver Thirsty for Knowledge, Dies at 73
abstract: Collecting used books, he read voraciously when not having lively conversations with his passengers. He died in the coronavirus pandemic.

name: Henry F. Graff
headline: Henry F. Graff, Columbia Historian of Presidents, Dies at 98
abstract: A professor and author, he had translated decrypted Japanese messages in World War II that revealed German defenses for D-Day and Tokyo’s imminent capitulation.

name: John Horton Conway
headline: John Horton Conway, a ‘Magical Genius’ in Math, Dies at 82
abstract: He made profound contributions to number theory, coding theory, probability theory, topology, algebra and more — and created games from it all. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Hailey Herrera
headline: Hailey Herrera, 25, Dies; Therapy Student Focused on Families
abstract: She was especially dedicated to working with Latino patients — and to organizing social events for friends.

name: Lee Konitz
headline: Lee Konitz, Jazz Saxophonist Who Blazed His Own Trail, Dies at 92
abstract: He was a pioneer of the cool school, but he resisted pigeonholing and focused on “making a personal statement.” He died of complications of the coronavirus.

name: Richard Passman
headline: Richard Passman, Space-Age Engineer Who Kept His Secrets, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Passman had a leadership role in many of the technologies that gave the United States strength in aircraft, spy satellites and missiles.

name: Thomas Miller
headline: Thomas Miller, Hit-Making TV Producer, Is Dead at 79
abstract: “Happy Days,” “Laverne & Shirley” and “Full House” were among his shows. And he found the right guy to play the Fonz.

name: Brian Dennehy
headline: Brian Dennehy, Tony Award-Winning Actor, Dies at 81
abstract: A versatile star, he had scores of television and film credits and made a searing impression on Broadway in “Death of a Salesman.”

name: Nora Illi
headline: Nora Illi, Swiss Muslim Convert Who Sparked Controversy, Dies at 35
abstract: When the first Swiss canton banned full-body veils for Muslim women, Ms. Illi showed up wearing one, prompting the police to get involved.

name: Cedric Dixon
headline: Cedric Dixon, Towering Detective in Harlem, Dies at 48
abstract: His death in March is believed to be the first of a sworn New York City police officer caused by the coronavirus.

name: Glenna Goodacre
headline: Glenna Goodacre, Created Vietnam Women’s Memorial, Dies at 80
abstract: A sculptor and one of the few women to make large public monuments, she also commemorated the Irish famine in a massive bronze piece in Philadelphia.

name: Jimmy Webb
headline: Jimmy Webb, Purveyor of Punk Fashion, Is Dead at 62
abstract: He wasn’t a rocker himself, but as the manager of the East Village clothing emporium Trash and Vaudeville, he was a proud bearer of the punk-glam torch.

name: Raymond Copeland
headline: Raymond Copeland, Sanitation Worker Who Hit His Stride, Dies at 46
abstract: He raised three girls as a single father. He was engaged and just coming into his stride in midlife. Then he got the coronavirus.

name: Fernando Miteff
profession: Graffiti Artist With a Generous Spirit
headline: Fernando Miteff, 60, Graffiti Artist With a Generous Spirit, Dies
abstract: He brought graffiti back to the subway, only this time his work would last for only the length of a ride.

name: Stanley Chera
headline: Stanley Chera, Developer and Friend of Trump, Dies at 77
abstract: As his friend lay dying of the coronavirus, President Trump spoke of him from the White House podium.

name: Ferdi German
headline: Ferdi German, M.T.A. Subway Car Inspector, Dies at 41
abstract: Mr. German, who worked for more than 12 years at the M.T.A.’s 207th street overhaul shop, was one of the thousands of transit workers who have fallen sick or self-quarantined.

name: Leilani Jordan
headline: Leilani Jordan, 27, Dies; Disabled, but Helping Shoppers
abstract: A victim of the coronavirus, she had been hired under a supermarket program for disabled people, but took care of customers less able than herself.

name: Tarlach MacNiallais
profession: Fought for Gay and Disability Rights
headline: Tarlach MacNiallais, Who Fought for Gay and Disability Rights, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. MacNiallais helped organize the St. Pat’s For All Parade in Queens, a more inclusive version of the annual parade on Fifth Avenue.

name: Moraes Moreira
profession: Brazilian Songwriter and Cowboy of Sound
headline: Moraes Moreira, 72, Dies; Brazilian Songwriter and ‘Cowboy of Sound’
abstract: His songs, written with a shifting assortment of lyricists, forged musical hybrids with his Bahian roots and celebrated Brazil’s multicultural vitality.

name: Norman Platnick
headline: Norman Platnick, the ‘Real Spider-Man,’ Is Dead at 68
abstract: A renowned expert on arachnids, he traveled the world to identify unknown species. He also showed that Tobey Maguire wasn’t afraid of them.

name: Paul O’Neill
headline: Paul O’Neill, Treasury Secretary Who Clashed With Bush, Dies at 84
abstract: He was “fearless,” a former colleague said, in pressing ideas based on facts and evidence. His independence cost him his job.

name: Liyna Anwar
profession: Publicized Inequities in Stem Cell Registry
headline: Liyna Anwar, 30, Dies; Publicized Inequities in Stem Cell Registry
abstract: She was a journalist of South Asian descent whose struggle to find a matching donor to treat her leukemia became a cri de coeur and encouraged more people of color to register.

name: Nobuhiko Obayashi
headline: Nobuhiko Obayashi, Unpredictable Japanese Director, Dies at 82
abstract: He made a splash in 1977 with a horror movie about a house full of furniture that eats schoolgirls. His later movies explored a range of themes.

name: Peter Beard
profession: Wildlife Photographer on the Wild Side
headline: Peter Beard, Wildlife Photographer on the Wild Side, Dies at 82
abstract: Called “the last of the adventurers,” Mr. Beard photographed African fauna at great personal risk, and well into old age could party till dawn. He had been missing for 19 days.

name: Luis Sepúlveda
headline: Luis Sepúlveda, Chilean Writer Exiled by Pinochet, Dies at 70
abstract: His best-known work was “The Old Man Who Read Love Stories.” Mr. Sepúlveda was among the first people in Spain hospitalized with the new coronavirus.

name: Sirio Maccioni
headline: Sirio Maccioni, Whose Le Cirque Drew Manhattan’s Elite, Dies at 88
abstract: Dash, charm and matinee-idol looks helped make Mr. Maccioni an unusual sort of celebrity in New York City’s restaurant scene.

name: Richard Teitelbaum
headline: Richard Teitelbaum, Electronic Composer and Improviser, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Teitelbaum, whose sonic vocabulary emphasized otherworldly sounds and textures, worked with everyone from Karlheinz Stockhausen to Anthony Braxton.

name: Nina Balducci
headline: Nina Balducci, Who Shaped a Famed Grocery Store, Dies at 91
abstract: She gave Balducci’s its polish and weathered an operatic family battle over the store’s ownership.

name: Beryl Bernay
profession: Childrens TV Host With a Varied Career
headline: Beryl Bernay, Children’s TV Host With a Varied Career, Dies at 94
abstract: Also an actor and painter, she assisted Margaret Mead and was an expert on Bali. She died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Rubem Fonseca
headline: Rubem Fonseca, Giant of Brazilian Literature, Dies at 94
abstract: A former police official, he wrote crime stories that titillated and shocked Brazilians and earned him prestigious awards.

name: Robert Loomis
headline: Robert Loomis, Old-School Editor of Big-Name Books, Dies at 93
abstract: He wielded his pencil at Random House for more than 50 years, nurturing the work of Maya Angelou, William Styron and other literary lights.

name: Noach Dear
headline: Noach Dear, Combative Brooklyn Councilman and Judge, Dies at 66
abstract: In pursuing his constituents’ Orthodox Jewish agenda, he opposed abortion rights and legislation to ban discrimination against gay people.

name: Walentyna Janta-Polczynska
headline: Walentyna Janta-Polczynska, Polish War Heroine, Dies at 107
abstract: She was a confidante of the prime minister of the Polish government in exile. In Queens, she was nicknamed the first lady of Polish Americans.

name: Abigail Thernstrom
headline: Abigail Thernstrom, Scholarly Foe of Affirmative Action, Dies at 83
abstract: She supported civil rights, but later, with her husband, Stephan, concluded that colorblind policies worked better than preferential treatment.

name: Liu Ouqing
headline: Liu Ouqing, Civil Servant Who Helped Feed Wuhan, Dies at 78
abstract: As China was opening up its centrally planned economy, Mr. Liu was party secretary of the Wuhan Grain Bureau, and he later helped establish Wuhan Business University.

name: Heherson Alvarez
headline: Heherson Alvarez, Fierce Opponent of Marcos Dictatorship, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Alvarez escaped the brutal regime by fleeing to the United States, where he helped organize the opposition Movement for a Free Philippines.

name: Jaroslava Brychtova
headline: Jaroslava Brychtova, Creator of Monumental Glass Art, Dies at 95
abstract: Working with her husband, Stanislav Libensky, she made sculptures that pushed the boundaries of glass, winning international acclaim.

name: Deirdre Bair
headline: Deirdre Bair, Beckett and de Beauvoir Biographer, Dies at 84
abstract: She was an unknown writer with no experience in biographies when she wrote to the elusive Samuel Beckett. To her surprise, he wrote back.

name: Martin Douglas
headline: Martin Douglas, Who Set Tone for Steel-Pan Brooklyn, Dies at 71
abstract: A deft musician and beloved mentor, he helped keep steel-pan music — his bridge to the Caribbean — a vibrant part of New York life. He had the coronavirus.

name: Ann Sullivan
headline: Ann Sullivan, Animator of Disney Hits, Dies at 91
abstract: She contributed to modern favorites like “The Little Mermaid” and “The Lion King.” She succumbed to complications of Covid-19.

name: Cheryl A. Wall
headline: Cheryl A. Wall, 71, Dies; Champion of Black Literary Women
abstract: An author and longtime professor at Rutgers, she pressed for the inclusion of black authors in curriculums and was an expert on Zora Neale Hurston.

name: Eunice Foote
headline: Overlooked No More: Eunice Foote, Climate Scientist Lost to History
abstract: Foote’s ingenious experiment more than 150 years ago yielded a remarkable discovery that could have helped shape modern climate science had she not been overshadowed.

name: Virginia Savage McAlester
headline: Virginia Savage McAlester, ‘Queen of Dallas Preservation,’ Dies at 76
abstract: Her book “A Field Guide to American Houses,” published in 1984 and revised in 2013, made her a household name among preservationists and architecture buffs.

name: Bennie G. Adkins
headline: Bennie G. Adkins, 86, Dies; Honored for Vietnam Heroics
abstract: He was awarded the Medal of Honor in 2014 for bravery in battle and aided veterans in his later years. He died of the new coronavirus.

name: Orlando Moncada
headline: Orlando Moncada, a Building Foreman in Manhattan, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Moncada, who died of the coronavirus, left Peru 40 years ago in pursuit of the American dream. He grabbed it with both hands.

name: Carole Brookins
headline: Carole Brookins, a Rare Woman on 1970s Wall Street, Dies at 76
abstract: She was an expert in the global political economy, with a specialty in agriculture, and served as executive director of the World Bank. She fell victim to the novel coronavirus.

name: Joseph Feingold
headline: Joseph Feingold, Holocaust Survivor and Documentary Star, Dies at 97
abstract: His donation of a violin to a 12-year-old Bronx girl spawned an Oscar-nominated documentary. He died from complications of the new coronavirus.

name: Shirley Knight
headline: Shirley Knight, Tony- and Emmy-Winning Actress, Dies at 83
abstract: She burst onto the scene with an Oscar-nominated performance in the 1960 film “The Dark at the Top of the Stairs” and went on to a long career in film, on television and on the stage.

name: Ketty Herawati Sultana
headline: Ketty Herawati Sultana, Tireless Indonesian Physician, Dies at 60
abstract: One of Dr. Ketty’s last patients was a top government official who tested positive for the coronavirus.

name: Donald Kennedy
headline: Donald Kennedy, Who Led Stanford in 1980s, Dies at 88
abstract: As president, he expanded the university and battled a government inquiry into its research expenses. He also headed the F.D.A. under President Carter.

name: Richard Sobol
profession: Civil Rights Lawyer in the South
headline: Richard Sobol, Civil Rights Lawyer in the South, Dies at 82
abstract: Unlike other Northern lawyers who joined the struggle in the South, he stayed, and won a landmark case.

name: John Pfahl
headline: John Pfahl, Photographer Who Played With Landscapes, Dies at 81
abstract: Long before Photoshop, he manipulated landscapes with everyday objects, and found beauty in compost piles and other peculiar places.

name: Abba Kyari
headline: Abba Kyari, Nigerian President’s Right-Hand Man, Dies
abstract: As chief of staff to President Muhammadu Buhari, Mr. Kyari was a “gatekeeper” and “loyal friend.”

name: Iris Love
headline: Iris Love, Stylish Archaeologist and Dog Breeder, Dies at 86
abstract: She was once known as the archaeologist in a miniskirt, a scion of old New York whose second career was raising Westminster Kennel Club champions.

name: John Houghton
headline: John Houghton, Who Sounded Alarm on Climate Change, Dies at 88
abstract: He led the United Nations panel on global warming that won a Nobel Peace Prize; he died from complications of the coronavirus

name: Don Campbell
headline: Don Campbell, Hip-Hop Dance Innovator, Is Dead at 69
abstract: He invented the Campbellock, better known as locking, an idiosyncratic style that became one of the first street dances to gain widespread attention.

name: Fred
headline: Fred the Godson, Nimble New York Rapper, Dies at 41
abstract: The Bronx musician was a forceful presence on mixtapes, filling his rhymes with clever punch lines.

name: Henry Geller
profession: Helped Rid TV of Cigarette Ads
headline: Henry Geller, Who Helped Rid TV of Cigarette Ads, Dies at 96
abstract: While at the F.C.C., he used the fairness doctrine to challenge the tobacco industry. He also helped pave the way for televised presidential debates.

name: Mario César Romero
headline: Mario César Romero, 78, Art Historian of East Harlem, Dies
abstract: He celebrated the neighborhood’s artists, including Alice Neel and James de la Vega.

name: Kenneth Saunders III
profession: Civic Leader with a Mediating Touch
headline: Kenneth Saunders III, Civic Leader with a Mediating Touch, Dies at 43
abstract: He joined his first local board at 18 and never stopped trying to improve his suburban Atlanta community. Mr. Saunders died of the coronavirus.

name: Philip Kahn
profession: Spanish Flu Took His Twin a Century Ago
headline: Philip Kahn, 100, Dies; Spanish Flu Took His Twin a Century Ago
abstract: Aware of the irony of dying during a pandemic, he said history repeats itself. A family member called the brothers “pandemic bookends.”

name: Gene Deitch
headline: Gene Deitch, Prolific Animator, Is Dead at 95
abstract: In a six-decade career, he created Tom Terrific, revived Tom and Jerry and won an Academy Award for a cartoon based on a Jules Feiffer story.

name: Michael Cogswell
headline: Michael Cogswell, 66, Dies; Sustained Louis Armstrong’s Legacy
abstract: He turned the jazz giant’s trove of memorabilia into a scholarly archive and created a popular museum at Armstrong’s house in Queens.

name: Bertha Laforest
headline: Bertha Laforest, Canadian Nun Who Found Refuge in Her Convent, Dies At 94
abstract: Sister Laforest was one of at least 36 of the 47 nuns in her Quebec convent to become infected with the coronavirus. Three others have died.

name: Richard Hake
profession: Longtime WNYC Radio Reporter and Host
headline: Richard Hake, Longtime WNYC Radio Reporter and Host, Dies at 51
abstract: Mr. Hake produced and created live radio feature segments that focused on breaking news, culture and artistic sound portraits.

name: Betsy Wyeth
headline: Betsy Wyeth, Andrew Wyeth’s Widow and Collaborator, Dies at 98
abstract: She was just 17 when she met her future husband. She went on to guide his career and became an avid preservationist of vernacular architecture.

name: Steve Dalkowski
profession: Model for Erratic Pitcher in Bull Durham
headline: Steve Dalkowski, Model for Erratic Pitcher in ‘Bull Durham,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Known for his extraordinary fastball, Dalkowski never made it to the major leagues, walking batters almost as often as he struck them out.

name: Harland Svare
profession: Giants Linebacker and Young Head Coach
headline: Harland Svare, 89, Giants Linebacker and Young Head Coach, Dies
abstract: Brainy more than brawny, he helped put New York in three title games, then became, with the Rams, the youngest head coach in modern N.F.L. history at the time.

name: Bernard Gersten
headline: Bernard Gersten, Offstage Star of Nonprofit Theater, Dies at 97
abstract: He helped run Joseph Papp’s Public Theater (shepherding “A Chorus Line”) and the New York Shakespeare Festival, then helped revive Lincoln Center Theater.

name: Francisco Mendez
headline: Francisco Mendez, Boxing Gym Owner and Mentor, Dies at 61
abstract: Arriving from Mexico, he found his calling outside the ring and attracted a following of clients with different backgrounds and goals.

name: Bruce Myers
profession: Actor With Voice of a Stradivarius
headline: Bruce Myers, Actor With Voice of a ‘Stradivarius,’ Dies at 78
abstract: He was a stalwart member of the group of actors who worked with the director Peter Brook. Mr. Myers died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Harold Reid
profession: Bedrock Voice of the Statler Brothers
headline: Harold Reid, Bedrock Voice of the Statler Brothers, Dies at 80
abstract: With his resonant bass, comic timing and business acumen, he was the Statlers’ de facto leader as they climbed the country music charts for decades.

name: Corliss Henry
headline: Corliss Henry, Trailblazing New Jersey Nurse, Dies at 95
abstract: She was the first black staff nurse at Muhlenberg Hospital and went on to become a nursing professor.

name: Tina Girouard
headline: Tina Girouard, Experimental Artist in 1970s SoHo, Dies at 73
abstract: She was a founder of Food, an influential artist-run kitchen in Manhattan, and a member of the alternative art space 112 Greene Street.

name: Mel Baggs
headline: Mel Baggs, Blogger on Autism and Disability, Dies at 39
abstract: Candid blog posts and a widely viewed short film sought to expand the very definition of what it means to be human.

name: Norman Gulamerian
headline: Norman Gulamerian, Artist With a Grand Passion, Dies at 92
abstract: He fell in love with a young widow with five children, and after years of courtship by mail, he persuaded her to marry him. He died of the coronavirus.

name: James Beggs
headline: James Beggs, 94, Is Dead; NASA Chief Championed Space Shuttle
abstract: He was on leave during the Challenger disaster in 1986 and resigned shortly after what critics called a leadership vacuum.

name: Eavan Boland
headline: Eavan Boland, ‘Disruptive’ Irish Poet, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Her work addressed domestic themes seldom found in the male-dominated world of Irish poetry and won her many accolades.

name: Irrfan Khan
profession: Bollywood Star at Home in Hollywood
headline: Irrfan Khan, Bollywood Star at Home in Hollywood, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Khan, whose films include “The Namesake,” “Life of Pi” and “Slumdog Millionaire,” was comfortable in both mainstream and art-house roles.

name: Arlene Saunders
headline: Arlene Saunders, Soprano With a Dramatic Flair, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Saunders, who had the coronavirus, was a charismatic performer who could sing “as easily as if she were conversing.”

name: Tadashi Tsufura
profession: Internment Survivor and New York Principal
headline: Tadashi Tsufura, Internment Survivor and New York Principal, Dies at 89
abstract: During World War II, he and his family were forcibly relocated to Arizona. He later became a beloved educator in New York City.

name: Terry Lenzner
headline: Terry Lenzner, Sleuth With a Wide-Ranging Career, Dies at 80
abstract: He prosecuted civil rights violators, investigated the Nixon administration during the Watergate scandal and worked for Bill Clinton.

name: Milena Jelinek
headline: Milena Jelinek, Screenwriter and Educator, Dies at 84
abstract: She was thrown out of her film school in Prague for a movie called “An Easy Life.” After landing in New York, she became a tough-love screenwriting professor at Columbia University.

name: Barney Ales
headline: Barney Ales, Indispensable Motown Executive, Is Dead at 85
abstract: In the 1960s, he promoted the black-owned company’s music to the white-dominated music industry, helping to make it a ubiquitous force in American pop culture.

name: Ricardo Brennand
headline: Ricardo Brennand, Brazilian Entrepreneur and Collector, Dies at 92
abstract: He amassed a vast trove of art and artifacts and built a castle-like repository so the public could see it, partly because his family wasn’t happy with his collecting.

name: Samuel Hargress Jr.
profession: Owner of a Beloved Harlem Bar
headline: Samuel Hargress Jr., Owner of a Beloved Harlem Bar, Dies at 84
abstract: He ran Paris Blues, a throwback to the ’60s that attracted locals and tourists alike and seemed to be an extension of himself. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Rishi Kapoor
profession: Leading Man From a Bollywood Dynasty
headline: Rishi Kapoor, Leading Man From a Bollywood Dynasty, Dies at 67
abstract: Best known as a romantic hero, he had a charm and charisma that made him one of India’s most popular actors of the 1970s and ’80s.

name: David Toren
headline: David Toren, Who Fought to Recover Nazi-Looted Art, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Toren, who died of the coronavirus, was a patent lawyer who recovered a relative’s stolen painting amid a large cache of works discovered in Germany.

name: Madeline Kripke
headline: Madeline Kripke, Doyenne of Dictionaries, Is Dead at 76
abstract: A woman of many words, mostly unspoken, she amassed a lexicographic trove of some 20,000 books, much of it crammed into her Greenwich Village apartment.

name: Valentina Blackhorse
headline: Valentina Blackhorse, Navajo Pageant Winner With Dreams, Dies at 28
abstract: She nurtured political aspirations while raising her 1-year-old daughter. Then she tested positive for the novel coronavirus. The next day she was dead.

name: Tim Brooke-Taylor
headline: Tim Brooke-Taylor, a Mainstay of British Comedy, Dies at 79
abstract: The humor on the BBC sketch show “The Goodies,” of which he was a creator and star, was visual, anarchic and very silly. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Patricia McGowan
headline: Sister Patricia McGowan, Dedicated Teacher, Dies at 80
abstract: She joined the Sisters of Charity in New York in 1956 and taught at her alma mater, the College of Mount Saint Vincent, until 2019. She died from complications of the coronavirus.

name: Willie Levi
profession: He Escaped a Life of Servitude
headline: Willie Levi, 73, Dies; He Escaped a Life of Servitude
abstract: He was one of a group of men with disabilities who worked for substandard wages at a turkey plant but found justice. He succumbed to the new coronavirus.

name: Idris Bey
headline: Idris Bey, an N.Y.C. Emergency Worker, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Bey, who died of the coronavirus, was a popular instructor at the Fire Department’s Emergency Medical academy.

name: Germano Celant
headline: Germano Celant, Curator Behind Italy’s Arte Povera, Dies at 79
abstract: He identified the “poor art” avant-garde movement and was an internationally renowned curator at the Guggenheim Museum in New York and the Fondazione Prada in Milan.

name: Helen McGehee
headline: Helen McGehee, a Martha Graham Dancer and Teacher, Dies at 98
abstract: She was known as a fierce and powerful dancer. Her teaching style was similarly demanding.

name: Matty Simmons
headline: Matty Simmons, a Force Behind ‘Animal House,’ Is Dead at 93
abstract: He helped get National Lampoon off the ground and was a producer of the Lampoon franchise’s hit movies.

name: Lynn Harrell
headline: Lynn Harrell, Acclaimed American Cellist, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Critics called him a “gentle giant,” a 6-foot-4 internationally renowned musician and frequent soloist whose playing could be sensitive and subtle.

name: Zev Buffman
headline: Zev Buffman, Prolific Theatrical Producer, Is Dead at 89
abstract: He brought both Elizabeth Taylor (in “The Little Foxes”) and Muhammad Ali (in a memorable flop) to Broadway. He was even busier in Florida.

name: Takuo Aoyagi
headline: Takuo Aoyagi, an Inventor of the Pulse Oximeter, Dies at 84
abstract: The medical device, which clips onto a patient’s finger, has saved millions of lives and is a vital tool in the fight against the novel coronavirus.

name: Marvin Schick
headline: Marvin Schick, Advocate for the Orthodox Community, Dies at 85
abstract: Because of his work, society began to accommodate those who kept kosher and observed the Sabbath.

name: Peter Jonas
headline: Peter Jonas, Innovative Opera Impresario, Is Dead at 73
abstract: He ran first the English National Opera and then the Bavarian State Opera, emphasizing vibrant theatrical interpretations as well as high musical values.

name: Hamilton Bohannon
headline: Hamilton Bohannon, Driving Disco Drummer, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Bohannon’s steady four-on-the-floor beat kept dancers moving, and many of his tracks became hip-hop samples long after disco’s heyday.

name: Tony Allen
headline: Tony Allen, Drummer Who Created the Beat of Afrobeat, Dies at 79
abstract: With the Nigerian bandleader Fela and later on his own, he merged West African styles with American jazz and funk, reaching listeners worldwide.

name: Sam Lloyd
headline: Sam Lloyd, ‘Scrubs’ Actor, Dies at 56
abstract: Mr. Lloyd appeared in dozens of television shows and films in his career, including “Seinfeld,” “Modern Family” and “The West Wing.”

name: Ronan O’Rahilly
headline: Ronan O’Rahilly, Pioneer of Pirate Radio, Is Dead at 79
abstract: He said he was in the “why-not” business. And his Radio Caroline became the soundtrack of British and European youth in the 1960s.

name: Don Shula
headline: Don Shula, N.F.L. Coach Who Won, and Won, and Won, Dies at 90
abstract: He had more victories than any other coach in the league and the only perfect season in its history, all while helping to shape pro football’s modern era.

name: Richard Friedman
headline: Dr. Richard Friedman, Who Debunked Homosexuality Myth, Dies at 79
abstract: In an important book, he challenged the widely held Freudian notion that same-sex attraction was curable, finding it instead rooted in biology.

name: Per Olov Enquist
headline: Per Olov Enquist, Literary Lion of Sweden, Dies at 85
abstract: His novels and plays used history to investigate life’s deeper questions. “One of the world’s most underrated great writers,” Kirkus Reviews once said.

name: Linda Yang
headline: Linda Yang, Who Offered Advice for Urban Gardeners, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Yang grew trees, flowers and herbs on a 19th-floor terrace. She was a contributor to The New York Times from 1979 until 1995.

name: Sjowall
headline: Maj Sjowall, Godmother of Nordic Noir, Dies at 84
abstract: With her companion, Per Wahloo, Ms. Sjowall wrote 10 books starring Martin Beck, a laconic, flawed Swedish detective.

name: Daniel and Valerie Zane
headline: Daniel and Valerie Zane, Married 71 Years, Die 2 Days Apart
abstract: Both in their 90s, they lived together in a senior facility; he took care of his wife, who was in declining health. Then he got the coronavirus.

name: Liu Shouxiang
headline: Liu Shouxiang, Champion of Watercolor in China, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Liu helped expand the country’s art beyond the traditionally dominant disciplines.

name: Zarina Hashmi
profession: Artist of a World in Search of Home
headline: Zarina Hashmi, Artist of a World in Search of Home, Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Hashmi was of a generation of artists whose life and work were haunted by the 1947 partition of India.

name: Bana Ali
headline: Bana Ali, Who Championed Basketball in Somalia, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Ali, who had the novel coronavirus, dedicated his own time and finances to promoting basketball and sports among Somali youth.

name: William Haddad
headline: William Haddad, Crusader for Generic Drugs, Dies at 91
abstract: As head of an industry group, he fought Big Pharma to make treatments for AIDS and other diseases more affordable. And that was just one hat he wore.

name: Ji Chaozhu
profession: Interpreter for China During Nixons Trip
headline: Ji Chaozhu, Interpreter for China During Nixon’s Trip, Dies at 90
abstract: With his flawless English, he sometimes translated for both American and Chinese officials, making him the “indispensable man.”

name: Paul Marks
headline: Paul Marks, Who Pushed Sloan Kettering to Greatness, Dies at 93
abstract: A charismatic leader, Dr. Marks brought the fruits of a scientific revolution to an institution that, when he took over, was behind the times.

name: Jana Prince
headline: Jana Prince, a Selfless Social Worker, Dies at 43
abstract: She had cerebral palsy, but her interest was in helping others with their problems. She died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Stanley Moser
headline: Stanley Moser, Virtuoso Encyclopedia Marketer, Dies at 88
abstract: He spent 30 years at Funk & Wagnalls selling encyclopedias and other reference works, eventually becoming an owner of the company. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Avraham Rabby
headline: Avraham Rabby, Blind Diplomat and Advocate, Is Dead at 77
abstract: He waged a successful campaign to overturn a State Department rule prohibiting the blind from becoming Foreign Service officers.

name: Florian Schneider
headline: Florian Schneider, 73, Dies; Revolutionized Pop Music With Kraftwerk
abstract: The German band he helped found toyed with ideas about technology and society, leaving a profound mark on rock, dance music and hip-hop.

name: Heyward Dotson
headline: Heyward Dotson, 71, Dies; Lifted Columbia to Basketball Glory
abstract: He helped lead the Lions to its only Ivy League title, in 1968, then studied at Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar.

name: Barry Webber
headline: Dr. Barry Webber, Surgeon Who Stuck With His Patients, Dies at 67
abstract: A rock climber, tinkerer and musician, he was a general surgeon who died of the novel coronavirus after volunteering to help Covid-19 patients.

name: Jean Erdman
headline: Jean Erdman, a Dancer Moved by Myth, Is Dead at 104
abstract: Ms. Erdman, who first came to wide notice as a choreographer in the 1940s, often focused in her work on the inner lives of women.

name: Munir Mangal
headline: Munir Mangal, Afghan General and Police Commander, Dies at 70
abstract: He was a career military officer who rose through the ranks and became the highest-profile Afghan to die after infection by the novel coronavirus.

name: Rosalind Elias
headline: Rosalind Elias, a Popular American Mezzo-Soprano, Dies at 90
abstract: A Metropolitan Opera mainstay, she sang some 680 performances of more than 50 roles there, often in starry casts. She made her Broadway debut at 82.

name: Michael McClure
headline: Michael McClure, Present at Beat Poetry’s Birth, Dies at 87
abstract: He took part in the storied San Francisco reading where Allen Ginsberg unveiled a version of “Howl.” He went on to have his own moments of fame and notoriety.

name: Frederick Kroesen
headline: Gen. Frederick Kroesen, 97, Dies; Survived a Terrorist Attack
abstract: The commander of troops in Europe, he had faced enemy fire in three wars before emerging with only cuts from a rocket attack by radical West German leftists in 1981.

name: Dave Greenfield
headline: Dave Greenfield, Keyboardist of the Stranglers, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Greenfield’s sound helped his band transcend the British punk rock scene.

name: Barry Farber
headline: Barry Farber, Perennial Talk Radio Host, Dies at 90
abstract: He began broadcasting in New York in 1960, when he was 30, and he never stopped talking — even when he was briefly off the air to run for Congress and mayor.

name: Gil Schwartz
profession: CBS Spokesman With a Biting Alter Ego
headline: Gil Schwartz, CBS Spokesman With a Biting Alter Ego, Dies at 68
abstract: He was the network’s top communications executive, but to readers of Esquire and Fortune he was Stanley Bing, skewering corporate America in humor columns.

name: Elizabeth Scholtz
headline: Elizabeth Scholtz, Barrier-Breaking Garden Director, Dies at 98
abstract: The first female director of a major botanic garden in the U.S., she was a daily presence at the Brooklyn Botanic Garden even after she retired.

name: Alfredo
profession: Health Care Aides on the Front Lines
headline: Alfredo and Susana Pabatao Die; Health Care Aides on the Front Lines
abstract: Married for 44 years, they both fell ill of the coronavirus and died within four days of each other in the New Jersey hospital where Mr. Pabatao worked.

name: Yukio Okamoto
headline: Yukio Okamoto, Diplomat Who Nurtured Japan’s U.S. Ties, Dies at 74
abstract: While in government and in the private sector, he advised Japanese prime ministers on how to manage the relationship between the two economic giants.

name: Ian Whitcomb
headline: Ian Whitcomb, Rocker Turned Pop Music Historian, Dies at 78
abstract: After his 1965 single “You Turn Me On” became a Top 10 hit, he renounced rock stardom for older musical idioms like ragtime.

name: Paul Shelden
headline: Paul Shelden, Clarinetist and Classical Music Advocate, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Shelden, who had the coronavirus, played under Leonard Bernstein and was inspired by his Young People’s Concerts.

name: Myles Coker
profession: Freed From a Life Term in Prison
headline: Myles Coker, 69, Dies; Freed From a Life Term in Prison
abstract: A sentencing rule change, a spotless prison record and his standing as a “true father” to his sons led to his release after 23 years behind bars for selling heroin.

name: Denis Goldberg
headline: Denis Goldberg, South African Freedom Fighter, Is Dead at 87
abstract: He was the only white defendant to be convicted alongside Nelson Mandela and others in 1964 for resisting apartheid. He spent 22 years in prison.

name: Daisy Lucidi
profession: Radio Voice With a Telenovela Following
headline: Daisy Lucidi, a Radio Voice With a Telenovela Following, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Lucidi had a large following in Brazil for her radio show “Hello Daisy!,” a mix of gossip, recipes and urban muckraking. She died of Covid-19.

name: Millie Small
headline: Millie Small, ‘My Boy Lollipop’ Singer, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Her 1964 smash hit was a breakthrough for Jamaican music. But she later became “one of the most elusive performers in pop history.”

name: Satish Gujral
headline: Satish Gujral, Versatile Indian Artist, Is Dead at 94
abstract: After losing his hearing as a child, he became one of his country’s best-known painters, sculptors and architects.

name: Ben Benson
profession: Put Singles in a Bar and Steak on the Tables
headline: Ben Benson, Who Put Singles in a Bar and Steak on the Tables, Dies at 89
abstract: He got his start with TGI Fridays, a ’60s hit on the bar scene, helped start Smith & Wollensky, then opened his own Midtown steakhouse, drawing a tony crowd.

name: Motoko Fujishiro Huthwaite
headline: Motoko Fujishiro Huthwaite, 92, Last of the ‘Monuments Women,’ Dies
abstract: An American who was sent to Japan after Pearl Harbor, she was one of 345 people from 14 countries who helped preserve cultural treasures.

name: June Almeida
headline: Overlooked No More: June Almeida, Scientist Who Identified the First Coronavirus
abstract: In 1966, she used a powerful electron microscope to capture an image of a mysterious pathogen — the first coronavirus known to cause human disease.

name: Roy Horn
profession: Dazzled Audiences as Half of Siegfried & Roy
headline: Roy Horn, Who Dazzled Audiences as Half of Siegfried & Roy, Dies at 75
abstract: He and his partner mesmerized crowds for decades, using a stunning mix of magic, costumes and exotic animals. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Little Richard
profession: Flamboyant Wild Man of Rock n Roll
headline: Little Richard, Flamboyant Wild Man of Rock ’n’ Roll, Dies at 87
abstract: Delving deeply into the wellsprings of gospel music and the blues, and screaming as if for his very life, he created something new, thrilling and dangerous.

name: Andre Harrell
headline: Andre Harrell, Executive Who Bridged Hip-Hop and R&B, Dies at 59
abstract: He founded the influential label Uptown Records and gave a first break to Sean Combs, who would go on to become one of hip-hop’s signature moguls.

name: Jimmy Glenn
headline: Jimmy Glenn, Ex-Boxer Whose Times Square Bar Endures, Dies at 89
abstract: A fighter, trainer, cutman and manager, he once owned both a bar and a gym. Only the bar survives. He died of coronavirus complications.

name: Thomas Reppetto
headline: Thomas Reppetto, Crime Watchdog and Historian, Is Dead at 88
abstract: A former police officer with a Harvard Ph.D., he brought a street cop’s experience and a scholarly perspective to the Citizens Crime Commission in New York.

name: Betty Wright
headline: Betty Wright, Soul Singer Who Mentored a New Generation, Dies at 66
abstract: She had her first hit, “Clean Up Woman,” when she was only 17 and became a key player in the Miami funk sound of the 1970s.

name: Jaquelin Taylor Robertson
headline: Jaquelin Taylor Robertson, Architect and Passionate Urbanist, Dies at 87
abstract: Devoted to classical architecture, he was equally committed to design that benefits city life and helped establish a New York agency to promote it.

name: Jerry Stiller
headline: Jerry Stiller, Comedian With Enduring Appeal, Is Dead at 92
abstract: In the 1960s, he and his wife, Anne Meara, found success as a comedy team. In the 1990s, he found it again as Frank Costanza on “Seinfeld.”

name: Barbara Babcock
profession: Force for Women in the Law
headline: Barbara Babcock, a Force for Women in the Law, Dies at 81
abstract: She helped Ruth Bader Ginsburg win a federal judgeship. “I would not hold the good job I have today were it not for Barbara,” Justice Ginsburg said.

name: Robert May
headline: Robert May, an Uncontainable ‘Big Picture’ Scientist, Dies at 84
abstract: Trained as a physicist, he applied simple mathematical models to complex phenomena in ecology, epidemiology and financial systems.

name: Georgianna Glose
profession: Nun and Activist for the Poor
headline: Georgianna Glose, a Nun and Activist for the Poor, Dies at 73
abstract: Sister Glose, who died from complications of the novel coronavirus, ran a nonprofit in Brooklyn and was a whistle-blower in a sex abuse scandal.

name: Double Rainbow
headline: ‘Double Rainbow Guy’ Paul Vasquez Is Dead at 57
abstract: His unbridled joy at the sight of two concentric rainbows made him a YouTube star.

name: Edith Richemond
headline: Edith Richemond, a Haitian Bootstrap Success Story, Dies at 88
abstract: With an 8th-grade education, she emigrated to Brooklyn, where she invested her savings in real estate, rented out apartments and ran two laundromats.

name: Richard Fenno
headline: Richard Fenno, Who Studied Congress Close Up, Dies at 93
abstract: His books broke new ground in political science, emphasizing politicians’ interactions not in Washington but in their home districts.

name: Ann McBride Norton
profession: First Woman to Run Common Cause
headline: Ann McBride Norton, First Woman to Run Common Cause, Dies at 75
abstract: In leading a watchdog group, she championed campaign finance reform. John McCain called her “our general and our strategist” in pushing that fight in Congress.

name: Aimee Stephens
headline: Aimee Stephens, Plaintiff in Transgender Case, Dies at 59
abstract: Ms. Stephens was fired from her job after she announced that she would live as a woman. Her complaint is now before the Supreme Court.

name: Julie Butler
headline: Dr. Julie Butler, Vet Who Cared for Harlem and Its Pets, Dies at 62
abstract: She owned and operated the 145th Street Animal Hospital and lived by the principle that “if you have it to give, you give,” caring for animals and opening her home to friends in need.

name: Carolyn Reidy
headline: Carolyn Reidy, the Head of Simon & Schuster, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Taking the helm in 2008, she steered the publishing house, one of the Big Five, through a deep recession and a digital revolution.

name: Joel Kupperman
profession: Scarred by Success as a Quiz Kid
headline: Joel Kupperman, Scarred by Success as a ‘Quiz Kid,’ Dies at 83
abstract: As a philosophy professor in adulthood, he would not speak of the World War II-era radio show (later on TV) that had made him famous and left him embittered.

name: Thomas Sokolowski
profession: Put Art in the Service of AIDS Activism
headline: Thomas Sokolowski, 70, Dies; Put Art in the Service of AIDS Activism
abstract: The longtime director of the Andy Warhol Museum, he used his position as a museum professional to connect the art world and the gay community.

name: Mike Storen
profession: Ran a Basketball League and Three Teams
headline: Mike Storen, 84, Dies; Ran a Basketball League and Three Teams
abstract: He was commissioner of the upstart American Basketball Association and built the Indiana Pacers and the Kentucky Colonels into champions.

name: Jonathan Adewumi
headline: Jonathan Adewumi, Who Made Everyone Feel at Home, Dies at 57
abstract: Proud of his Nigerian heritage, he brought Africa to New York and, at his Brooklyn restaurant, united a community.

name: Jerzy Glowczewski
headline: Jerzy Glowczewski, Polish Pilot in a Spitfire, Dies at 97
abstract: He fled Warsaw when the Nazis invaded, flew 100 combat missions, and made a life as an architect in Poland, Egypt and the United States. He died of the coronavirus in New York.

name: Richard Gilder
headline: Richard Gilder, Donor to Parks, Museum and History, Dies at 87
abstract: A successful investor, he was a major benefactor of Central Park, the New-York Historical Society and the Museum of Natural History.

name: Martin Lovett
profession: Last Living Member of the Amadeus Quartet
headline: Martin Lovett, Last Living Member of the Amadeus Quartet, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Lovett played cello in the celebrated ensemble, which performed together for 40 years. He died of complications of the novel coronavirus.

name: Ralph W. McGehee
headline: Ralph W. McGehee, Agent Who Exposed the C.I.A., Dies at 92
abstract: A crisis of conscience in Vietnam led him to conclude that the agency was “a malevolent force” and to lay it bare in a memoir, “Deadly Deceits.”

name: Bob Watson
headline: Bob Watson, Baseball’s First Black General Manager, Dies at 74
abstract: A former major leaguer, he shattered a racial barrier in 1994 with the Houston Astros. Two years later, he was the Yankees’ G.M. as New York began a championship run.

name: Nick Kotz
headline: Nick Kotz, Crusading Journalist and Author, Dies at 87
abstract: He won a Pulitzer Prize for exposing unsafe conditions in meatpacking plants. He also wrote about hunger in America and the politics of the B-1 bomber.

name: Antonio González Pacheco
headline: Antonio González Pacheco, Accused Policeman in Franco’s Spain, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. González Pacheco was charged with torturing opponents of the Franco dictatorship but never stood trial. Reports said he died of complications of the novel coronavirus.

name: S. Roger Horchow
headline: S. Roger Horchow, Retailer Turned Broadway Producer, Dies at 91
abstract: He built a luxury catalog business, then sold it and used the proceeds to mount the Tony-winning hit musical “Crazy for You.”

name: Gil Loescher
headline: Gil Loescher, 75, Refugees Expert Who Survived Iraq Bombing, Dies
abstract: He lost his legs in a 2003 suicide attack but continued his scholarship and field work on behalf of the world’s displaced.

name: Ty
headline: Ty, British Rapper Who Bridged Generations and Genres, Dies at 47
abstract: His sound didn’t fit neatly into any hip-hop archetypes, and he pushed to make room for unconventional voices.

name: Louis Delsarte
headline: Louis Delsarte, a Muralist of the Black Experience, Dies at 75
abstract: His paintings and murals rendered the Harlem Renaissance, Martin Luther King Jr. and his Brooklyn neighbors in stunning color.

name: Tendol Gyalzur
headline: Tendol Gyalzur, Refugee Who Founded Orphanages in Tibet, Dies
abstract: After losing her parents during the failed 1959 Tibetan uprising, she fled to India, became a nurse in Germany and later worked with the Chinese government to aid needy children in her homeland.

name: Peter Brancazio
headline: Peter Brancazio, Who Explored the Physics of Sports, Dies at 81
abstract: He used science to demystify the myths of rising fastballs and Michael Jordan’s seemingly long hang time. He died of complications of the novel coronavirus.

name: David Carter
headline: David Carter, a Historian of Stonewall, Is Dead at 67
abstract: His research into the 1969 uprising that was a turning point in the gay rights movement helped get the site of that uprising recognized as a landmark.

name: Fred Willard
profession: Played Characters Gloriously Out of Their Depth
headline: Fred Willard, Who Played Characters ‘Gloriously Out of Their Depth,’ Dies at 86
abstract: He was nominated for Emmys for his roles on “Modern Family” and “Everybody Loves Raymond,” and was a frequent collaborator with the director Christopher Guest.

name: Astrid Kirchherr
headline: Astrid Kirchherr, Who Helped Create the Beatles’ Image, Dies at 81
abstract: The stark black-and-white photographs she took of the group in Hamburg, Germany, before the musicians were famous captured both their toughness and their sensitivity.

name: Lynn Shelton
headline: Lynn Shelton, Director of Intimate Comic Dramas, Dies at 54
abstract: She got a late start on her filmmaking career but won acclaim for a freewheeling style that made room for contributions from actors like Marc Maron, who survives her.

name: Phyllis George
headline: Phyllis George, Trailblazing Sportscaster, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Four years after being crowned Miss America, she became a celebrity, and drew criticism, as a co-host of the CBS show “The NFL Today.”

name: S. David Freeman
headline: S. David Freeman, 94, Tireless Advocate for Clean Energy, Dies
abstract: A folksy but forceful “Green Cowboy,” he helped shape energy policy in the White House and at local utilities for seven decades.

name: Frances Goldin
profession: Crusader for the Lower East Side
headline: Frances Goldin, a Crusader for the Lower East Side, Dies at 95
abstract: A neighborhood preservationist, she had significant victories as a protester, provocateur and voice for lost causes.

name: Michel Piccoli
profession: Star of French Stage and Screen
headline: Michel Piccoli, Star of French Stage and Screen, Dies at 94
abstract: A storied actor, he starred opposite Brigitte Bardot and Catherine Deneuve and worked with many of the giants of European filmmaking.

name: Gene Rossides
profession: Led Columbia to Historic Upset of Army
headline: Gene Rossides, 92, Dies; Led Columbia to Historic Upset of Army
abstract: A star quarterback, he helped snap West Point’s 32-game unbeaten streak in 1947. Instead of the N.F.L., he became a lawyer and served two presidents.

name: Cleon Boyd
profession: Vermont Twins Tied to the Land
headline: Cleon and Leon Boyd, Vermont Twins Tied to the Land, Die at 64
abstract: They boiled sap at the family farm, groomed the ski slopes and played country music. The brothers died of the novel coronavirus, which also sickened many in their extended family.

name: Leon Boyd
profession: Vermont Twins Tied to the Land
headline: Cleon and Leon Boyd, Vermont Twins Tied to the Land, Die at 64
abstract: They boiled sap at the family farm, groomed the ski slopes and played country music. The brothers died of the novel coronavirus, which also sickened many in their extended family.

name: Conrad Ifill
headline: Conrad Ifill, a Caribbean Baker in Brooklyn, Dies at 81
abstract: His Conrad’s Famous Bakery produced breads and a nine rum fruit cake  that reminded West Indians of home. He fell victim to the novel coronavirus.

name: Ken Osmond
headline: Ken Osmond, the Troublemaker Eddie Haskell on ‘Beaver’, Dies at 76
abstract: He was the memorably two-faced friend of Wally Cleaver, a perfect young gentleman in front of parents, a perfect devil when the adults weren’t around.

name: Marie Pino
headline: Marie Pino, Navajo Teacher Who Educated Generations, Dies at 67
abstract: A well-known teacher, she was mourning the loss of her son to the virus when she tested positive. Then she died as well, adding to the Navajo Nation’s toll.

name: Yu Lihua
profession: Writer Spoke to Rootless Chinese Émigrés
headline: Yu Lihua, 90, Dies; Writer Spoke to ‘Rootless’ Chinese Émigrés
abstract: In her fiction she depicted “the struggle of Chinese immigrants in American society” — not the “Oriental exoticism” preferred by many publishers in the ’60s.

name: Michael McCaskey
profession: Bears Boss in Their Glory Years
headline: Michael McCaskey, Bears’ Boss in Their Glory Years, Dies at 76
abstract: He was a business professor when he took the reins from his grandfather George Halas, then led the team as it flourished in the 1980s, winning a Super Bowl.

name: Annie Glenn
profession: Champion of Those With Speech Disorders
headline: Annie Glenn, Champion of Those With Speech Disorders, Dies at 100
abstract: Being an astronaut’s wife thrust her into the spotlight, but a stutter left her struggling for words until she found help.

name: Nita Pippins
headline: Nita Pippins, a Mother to AIDS Patients, Dies at 93
abstract: At 60, she moved to New York to care for her dying son. Instead of returning home, she dedicated herself to AIDS patients during the worst of the epidemic.

name: Cécile Rol-Tanguy
headline: Cécile Rol-Tanguy, French Resistance Fighter, Dies at 101
