abstract: Passing through Nazi checkpoints in disguise, she carried machine guns and hand grenades to members of the underground.

name: Melford Henson
headline: Melford Henson, Construction Foreman, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Henson fell ill from the coronavirus only months before he was to be released from California’s prison system.

name: Leonard Levitt
headline: Leonard Levitt, Reporter Who Riled N.Y.P.D. Brass, Dies at 79
abstract: His newspaper column, books and blog sought to hold the police accountable, and his reporting reopened a murder case against a Kennedy cousin in Connecticut.

name: Kamal Ahmed
headline: Kamal Ahmed, Who Helped Bangladeshi-Americans, Dies at 69
abstract: He was a banquet server at a hotel near the United Nations and leader of the Bangladesh Society of New York.

name: Francis Kennedy
headline: Francis Kennedy, War Hero and Restless Inventor, Dies at 95
abstract: After the violence in Korea, Mr. Kennedy sought to give something back to the world with his inventions. He succumbed to the novel coronavirus.

name: Else Blangsted
profession: Fled the Nazis and Found a Hollywood Ending
headline: Else Blangsted, Who Fled the Nazis and Found a Hollywood Ending, Dies at 99
abstract: A top movie music editor who worked with Dave Grusin and Michel Legrand, she was haunted by the fate of her first child.

name: Rolf Hochhuth
headline: Rolf Hochhuth, Who Challenged a Pope’s Wartime Silence, Dies at 89
abstract: His play “The Deputy,” from 1963, took issue with Pius XII’s stance toward Nazi atrocities and caused a furor. “The theater,” Susan Sontag wrote, “is courtroom.”

name: René Buch
headline: René Buch, a Force in Spanish-Language Repertory Theater, Dies at 94
abstract: As a founder of the venerable Manhattan company Repertorio Español, Mr. Buch reimagined works both classic and contemporary.

name: Susan Rothenberg
headline: Susan Rothenberg, Acclaimed Figurative Painter, Dies at 75
abstract: Her raw renditions of horses and other figures breathed new life into painting when the genre was under siege in 1970s SoHo.

name: Harold Blake
profession: Loyal to Robert Moses Until the End
headline: Harold Blake, Loyal to Robert Moses Until the End, Dies at 91
abstract: He was executive assistant to that imperious urban planner when Mr. Moses headed the 1964-65 World’s Fair in New York. He was later an executive with the city’s bridge and tunnel authority.

name: Lucky Peterson
profession: Bluesman Since He Was a Boy
headline: Lucky Peterson, a Bluesman Since He Was a Boy, Dies at 55
abstract: He cut a record at 5 and went on to a steady if somewhat under-the-radar career as a backing musician and solo artist.

name: Sally Rowley
headline: Sally Rowley, Jewelry Maker and Freedom Rider, Dies at 88
abstract: She fought for civil rights, learned to fly and sold her art on the streets of San Francisco. She died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Abdullah al-Hamid
headline: Abdullah al-Hamid, Saudi Dissident, Dies in Detention at 69
abstract: A tireless advocate for human rights and a thorn in the side of the monarchy, he spoke out for democratic reforms and was imprisoned seven times.

name: Wilson Jerman
headline: Wilson Jerman, Longtime White House Butler, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Jerman started working as a cleaner for President Dwight D. Eisenhower in 1957 and retired in 2012 as an elevator operator for President Barack Obama.

name: Bernice Silver
headline: Bernice Silver, Impish Puppeteer and Activist, Dies at 106
abstract: Trained in the political theater of the 1930s, Ms. Silver was a beloved figure in the puppetry, folk music and environmental worlds.

name: Hazel Ying
headline: Overlooked No More: When Hazel Ying Lee and Maggie Gee Soared the Skies
abstract: Lee and Gee never met, but as the only two Chinese-American women pilots during the war, their lives ran a strikingly similar course, and both thwarted layers of prejudice.

name: Rhody McCoy
profession: Key Figure in New Yorks School Wars
headline: Rhody McCoy, Key Figure in New York’s School Wars, Dies at 97
abstract: He headed the Brooklyn district where teacher transfers in 1968 sparked a bitter, racially-charged dispute over union seniority and community control.

name: Joel M. Reed
headline: Joel M. Reed, 86, Director of Horror Movies, Dies
abstract: He made the exploitation-splatter film “Blood Sucking Freaks,” which was widely reviled but achieved cult status. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Lloyd Porter
headline: Lloyd Porter, Cafe Owner Who Found Joy in Everyone, Dies at 49
abstract: An actor transplanted from California, he and his wife opened Bread Stuy, a bakery and cafe that became a local gathering spot.

name: Jerry Sloan
profession: Hall of Fame N.B.A. Guard and Coach
headline: Jerry Sloan, Hall of Fame N.B.A. Guard and Coach, Dies at 78
abstract: An All-Star with the Bulls, he became an immensely successful coach, turning the Utah Jazz into a powerhouse and a postseason perennial.

name: Walter Dallas
headline: Walter Dallas, ‘Heartbeat’ of Philadelphia Theater, Dies at 73
abstract: A man of many talents, he led Freedom Theater, one of the nation’s top African-American companies, for more than a decade.

name: Phil May
headline: Phil May, British Rocker of Unbridled Energy, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Mr. May’s snarling vocals and rebellious persona helped make his band, the Pretty Things, an influential part of the 1960s British scene.

name: Marcel Ospel
profession: Architect of the Swiss Bank UBS
headline: Marcel Ospel, Architect of the Swiss Bank UBS, Is Dead at 70
abstract: He built a global colossus that nearly toppled during the financial crisis of 2008, a plunge that required a bailout and led to his resignation.

name: John Driscoll
headline: John Driscoll, Scholar, Art Dealer and Collector, Dies at 70
abstract: He purchased and expanded Babcock Galleries, New York’s oldest art seller, while building a renowned pottery collection. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: John Macurdy
profession: Stalwart Bass in Roles Large and Small
headline: John Macurdy, Stalwart Bass in Roles Large and Small, Dies at 91
abstract: During a 38-year career with the Metropolitan Opera, he sang 1,001 performances, drawing notice for his performances in Wagner, Verdi and Mozart.

name: Rafael Leonardo Black
headline: Rafael Leonardo Black, Solitary and Self-Trained Artist, Dies at 71
abstract: After laboring for years in his small Brooklyn apartment, he had his first New York gallery show when he was 64. He died from complications of Covid-19.

name: June Willenz
profession: Champion of Women in the Military
headline: June Willenz, Champion of Women in the Military, Dies at 95
abstract: She didn’t serve in the military herself. But she saw the armed services denying equal benefits to female veterans, and she crusaded to make a difference.

name: Sal Capozucca
profession: Rock Drummer with a Real Estate Gig
headline: Sal Capozucca, Rock Drummer with a Real Estate Gig, Dies at 65
abstract: He had a day job as a broker specializing in townhouses, but his heart belonged with his rock ’n’ roll drum set and his local band. He died of Covid-19.

name: Mory Kante
headline: Mory Kante, Million-Selling African Singer and Bandleader, Dies at 70
abstract: Incorporating electric instruments and elements of Western pop, he gave many Western listeners an accessible introduction to African music.

name: Michael Halkias
profession: Promised Wish Fulfillment at Banquet Hall
headline: Michael Halkias, Who Promised Wish Fulfillment at Banquet Hall, Dies at 82
abstract: His Grand Prospect Hall in Brooklyn hosted four decades’ worth of events, and he and his wife, Alice, made the hall’s commercials a late-night TV staple.

name: Richard Anuszkiewicz
profession: Op Art Caught Eyes in the 60s
headline: Richard Anuszkiewicz, Whose Op Art Caught Eyes in the ’60s, Dies at 89
abstract: He was a pioneer in manipulating fundamental elements of art to create optical effects — and to make, as he put it, “something romantic out of a very, very mechanistic geometry.”

name: Eddie Sutton
profession: Winning Basketball Coach at Four Schools
headline: Eddie Sutton, 84, Winning Basketball Coach at Four Schools, Dies
abstract: Recently elected to the Hall of Fame, he led Creighton, Arkansas, Kentucky and Oklahoma State to the N.C.A.A. tournament as he piled up 806 victories.

name: Stanley Ho
profession: Turned Macau Into a Global Gambling Hub
headline: Stanley Ho, Who Turned Macau Into a Global Gambling Hub, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Ho led the tiny Chinese territory’s transformation into the world’s most lucrative gambling destination.

name: John von Sternberg
headline: John von Sternberg, Seller and Protector of Homes, Dies at 79
abstract: He was a pillar of the community in Mountain Lakes, N.J., a real estate agent and a 60-year volunteer firefighter. He fell victim to Covid-19.

name: Anthony Bailey
headline: Anthony Bailey, Biographer With Restless Literary Spirit, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Bailey was a longtime New Yorker magazine writer who wrote about Rembrandt, J. M. W. Turner and other artists. He died from the novel coronavirus.

name: Jimmy Cobb
profession: Drummer on Miles Daviss Kind of Blue
headline: Jimmy Cobb, Drummer on Miles Davis’s ‘Kind of Blue,’ Dies at 91
abstract: The last surviving member of that landmark album’s sextet, he was a master of understatement, propelling his bandmates with a quiet persistence.

name: José María Galante
profession: Dogged Pursuer of Justice for Francos Victims
headline: José María Galante, Dogged Pursuer of Justice for Franco’s Victims, Dies at 71
abstract: Despite an amnesty law, Mr. Galante continued to gather evidence and press for the prosecution of police officials. He died of Covid-19.

name: Nancy Stark Smith
headline: Nancy Stark Smith, a Founder of Contact Improvisation, Dies at 68
abstract: She helped develop and popularize a dance form that is both artful and athletic, focusing on touch, gravity and weight sharing.

name: Larry Kramer
headline: Larry Kramer, Playwright and Outspoken AIDS Activist, Dies at 84
abstract: He sought to shock the country into dealing with AIDS as a public-health emergency and foresaw that it could kill millions regardless of sexual orientation.

name: Ravi Zacharias
headline: Ravi Zacharias, Preacher Who Used Reason to Defend Faith, Dies at 74
abstract: He practiced an intellectual form of Christian theology called apologetics and sought to “connect the gospel with the life of the mind.”

name: Steve Hann
profession: Sidewalk Bookseller With a Brainy Following
headline: Steve Hann, Sidewalk Bookseller With a Brainy Following, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Hann, who tested positive for the novel coronavirus, drew customers from Columbia University and a NASA office to his folding tables covered with used books.

name: Oliver Williamson
headline: Oliver Williamson, 87, Dies; Nobel Laureate Studied Organizations
abstract: He shared the 2009 award in economic science for his theories on how business decisions are made, work whose influence reached into various sectors of the economy.

name: Barbara Sher
profession: Prescribed Self-Help With a Dose of Humor
headline: Barbara Sher, 84, Dies; Prescribed Self-Help With a Dose of Humor
abstract: After lifting herself up, she poked fun at the motivational industry while promoting her own brand of self-fulfillment in workshops and popular books.

name: Gabriel Bacquier
headline: Gabriel Bacquier, 95, Dies; Set Standard for French Baritones
abstract: He mastered both a broad range of opera roles and the art of the French song.

name: Eduardo L. Gancayco
headline: Eduardo L. Gancayco, Who Kept Hospital Workers Fed, Dies at 62
abstract: He was a cafeteria manager at Mount Sinai Medical Center in Manhattan, where he died of Covid-19, and a consummate host.

name: William J. Small
profession: Key Official During CBS Newss Heyday
headline: William J. Small, Key Official During CBS News’s Heyday, Dies at 93
abstract: As the network’s Washington bureau chief, Mr. Small built a journalistic all-star team that included Dan Rather, Lesley Stahl and many others.

name: Carvel H. Moore
profession: Found a Career in Bettering a City
headline: Carvel H. Moore, Who Found a Career in Bettering a City, Dies at 90
abstract: Ms. Moore, an early proponent of business improvement districts across New York City, died of complications of the coronavirus.

name: Margaret Maughan
headline: Margaret Maughan, Medal-Winning Wheelchair Athlete, Dies at 91
abstract: Paralyzed from the waist down, she won gold in archery and swimming at the first Paralympic Games in 1960 and became an advocate of sports as therapy.

name: Richard Herd
headline: Richard Herd, a Baffled Boss on ‘Seinfeld,’ Is Dead at 87
abstract: A busy character actor, he also appeared on several science-fiction shows, including “Star Trek: The Next Generation,” on which he played a Klingon.

name: Albert Krieger
profession: Bulldog of the Criminal Defense Bar
headline: Albert Krieger, a Bulldog of the Criminal Defense Bar, Dies at 96
abstract: His clients included John Gotti, Joseph Bonanno, Miami’s “cocaine cowboys” and the defendants in the Wounded Knee siege.

name: Gladys Cortes
profession: Miracle Baby Moved to Help Others
headline: Gladys Cortes, ‘Miracle Baby’ Moved to Help Others, Dies at 48
abstract: Ms. Cortes came to New York from Puerto Rico and hoped to be an artist. She died of complications of Covid-19

name: John E. Randall
headline: John E. Randall, Ichthyologist Extraordinaire, Dies at 95
abstract: He swam the world’s oceans, identified hundreds of new fish species and named 834 of them.

name: Emma Amos
headline: Emma Amos, Painter Who Challenged Racism and Sexism, Dies at 83
abstract: Early in her career she created brightly colored scenes of black middle-class domestic life. Her later work was increasingly personal and experimental.

name: Alberto Rottura
headline: Alberto Rottura, Stylist to Boldface Names, Dies at 77
abstract: A teenage immigrant from Italy, he opened salons in Manhattan and cut the hair of Mayor Bloomberg of New York and other prominent people.

name: Bobby Digital
headline: Bobby Digital Dies at 59; His Reggae Rhythms Spread Worldwide
abstract: The producer born Robert Dixon was responsible for hits like the Shabba Ranks song “Dem Bow,” which became a staple of global pop.

name: Harold and Marion Wernig
headline: Harold and Marion Wernig, Together Until the End, Die at 87 and 85
abstract: The Wernigs, married for 67 years, shared a “fierce” love. They died on the same day of the coronavirus.

name: Sam Johnson
headline: Sam Johnson, Congressman and Former P.O.W., Is Dead at 89
abstract: A much-decorated pilot held by the North Vietnamese for years, he would later criticize his fellow Republican Donald Trump for disparaging John McCain.

name: John Loengard
headline: John Loengard, Life Photographer and Chronicler, Dies at 85
abstract: He shot compelling portraits of the Beatles, Georgia O’Keeffe and many others and celebrated photography, and Life magazine, in books.

name: Herb Stempel
headline: Herb Stempel, Quiz Show Whistle-Blower, Is Dead at 93
abstract: After being instructed to give a wrong answer and lose to his golden-boy opponent, he played a key role in exposing a major television scandal.

name: Karen Blumenthal
headline: Karen Blumenthal, 61, Dies; Journalist Turned Young-Adult Author
abstract: After many years at The Wall Street Journal, she began writing books about the social forces that gave rise to hot-button issues in American culture.

name: Benjamin Smalls
headline: Benjamin Smalls, Jailhouse Lawyer and Prison Reformer, Dies at 72
abstract: To fellow inmates, he was known as the Elder Statesman, and his cell was cluttered with legal papers. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Norman Lamm
profession: Rescued Yeshiva U. From Brink of Bankruptcy
headline: Norman Lamm, 92, Dies; Rescued Yeshiva U. From Brink of Bankruptcy
abstract: He championed the idea that Orthodox Jews could maintain their faith while engaging with modern society.

name: Christo
headline: Christo, Artist Who Wrapped and Festooned on an Epic Scale, Dies at 84
abstract: Mountains, museums, bridges and Central Park were just some of what he used to make astonishing and popular art with his wife and collaborator, Jeanne-Claude.

name: Joel Revzen
headline: Joel Revzen, Conductor and Music Festival Leader, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Revzen, who had the coronavirus, held posts with regional companies and was on the staff of the Metropolitan Opera.

name: Pat Dye
headline: Pat Dye, Football Coach Who Elevated Auburn, Dies at 80
abstract: He reshaped the very architecture and culture of the Iron Bowl rivalry and led Auburn to four conference titles.

name: Ruben Varias Reyes
headline: Ruben Varias Reyes, Diplomat Who Questioned Marcos Spending, Dies at 79
abstract: Assigned to the Philippine Embassy in London, Mr. Reyes challenged expenditures on items like Persian rugs, perfume and real estate.

name: Wes Unseld
profession: Powerful Hall of Fame N.B.A. Center
headline: Wes Unseld, Powerful Hall of Fame N.B.A. Center, Dies at 74
abstract: A rock on the court known for his indefatigable rebounding, he helped turn the Baltimore Bullets around.

name: Federico Acerri
headline: Federico Acerri, Who Answered Students’ Questions, Dies at 81
abstract: He was an information specialist in the Michigan school system. He was also an artist who went by the alias Mad Monk. Mr. Acerri died of complications of the new coronavirus.

name: Patricia Reed Scott
profession: Cast New York as Hollywood East
headline: Patricia Reed Scott, Who Cast New York as Hollywood East, Dies at 86
abstract: Working for two mayors, she re-established the city as the prime East Coast outpost for movie and TV production, clearing out traffic more than once.

name: Robb Forman Dew
headline: Robb Forman Dew, Novelist Who Wrote of Families, Dies at 73
abstract: Her well-regarded books chronicled day-to-day life, spurning fast-paced gimmicks in favor of carefully built portraits.

name: Elsa Dorfman
headline: Elsa Dorfman, Who Made Art With Giant Polaroids, Dies at 83
abstract: She used a 200-pound camera for her natural portraits of everyday subjects and celebrities — even while Polaroid, outpaced by technology, was fast going out of business.

name: Mary J. Wilson
headline: Mary J. Wilson, Barrier-Smashing Zookeeper, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Wilson, who had the coronavirus, was the first African-American senior zookeeper at what is now the Maryland Zoo in Baltimore.

name: Mary Wilson
headline: Mary Wilson, an Original Member of the Supremes, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Wilson joined with Florence Ballard and Diana Ross — who later emerged as the lead singer — to form one of the biggest musical acts of the 1960s.

name: Charles Lippincott
headline: Charles Lippincott, Who Hyped ‘Star Wars,’ Is Dead at 80
abstract: In handling publicity for George Lucas’s 1977 blockbuster, he helped create a playbook for future science fiction movies.

name: Angelo Rottoli
headline: Angelo Rottoli, Boxer and Man About Town, Dies at 61
abstract: A five-time Italian heavyweight champion, he was a well-known figure in his northern Italian town. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Johnny Majors
profession: Winning Coach at Pittsburgh and Tennessee
headline: Johnny Majors, 85, Winning Coach at Pittsburgh and Tennessee, Dies
abstract: A former star for Tennessee, he led Pitt to a national championship and coached the Volunteers for 16 seasons, only to be ousted after heart surgery.

name: Bruce Jay Friedman
profession: Author With a Darkly Comic Worldview
headline: Bruce Jay Friedman, 90, Author With a Darkly Comic Worldview, Dies
abstract: An unusual case in American letters, he moved easily between literature and pop culture, including movies like “Stir Crazy" and “Splash,” to great acclaim.

name: Celine Fariala Mangaza
headline: Celine Fariala Mangaza, Congolese Heroine of Disabled People, Dies at 52
abstract: A survivor of polio, she created a place for disabled women to earn a little money, and find solidarity. Doctors believe she died because of Covid-19.

name: Hutton Gibson
profession: Extremist and Father of Mel Gibson
headline: Hutton Gibson, Extremist and Father of Mel Gibson, Dies at 101
abstract: His anti-Semitic, anti-Vatican views gained notoriety after his son directed the controversial film, “The Passion of the Christ.”

name: Jimmy Capps
headline: Jimmy Capps, Guitarist on Numerous Country Hits, Dies at 81
abstract: In addition to his prolific work as a studio musician, Mr. Capps was a member of the Grand Ole Opry’s house band for more than 50 years.

name: John McCormack
headline: John McCormack, a Nurturing Theater Producer, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. McCormack, who died of coronavirus-related causes, lifted the careers of Off Broadway actors and playwrights, even as he remained elusive.

name: Vladimir Lopukhin
profession: Held Key Post When U.S.S.R. Fell
headline: Vladimir Lopukhin, Who Held Key Post When U.S.S.R. Fell, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Lopukhin, who died of the novel coronavirus, was in charge of the energy ministry at a time of tumultuous change in Russia’s oil and gas industry.

name: Hecky Powell
headline: Hecky Powell, Barbecue Master and Civic Leader, Dies at 71
abstract: From his restaurant in Evanston, Ill., he fed hungry students and the Chicago Bulls, and counseled high schoolers, mayors, a governor and a young Barack Obama.

name: Bertram Brown
headline: Dr. Bertram Brown, Mental Health Advocate, Is Dead at 89
abstract: In the 1960s and ’70s, as head of the National Institute of Mental Health, he was instrumental in improving programs for intellectually disabled Americans.

name: Bobby Morrow
profession: Ran to Stardom at the 1956 Olympics
headline: Bobby Morrow, Who Ran to Stardom at the 1956 Olympics, Dies at 84
abstract: With three gold medals in sprints in Melbourne, he matched what Jesse Owens had memorably accomplished 20 years earlier in Berlin.

name: Roberta Cowell
headline: Overlooked No More: Roberta Cowell, Trans Trailblazer, Pilot and Auto Racer
abstract: Cowell is the first woman known to undergo sex reassignment surgery in Britain. But after a splash in the 1950s, she withdrew from public life and died in obscurity.

name: Charles Kleinberg
profession: Muted Prosecutor With a Sharp Calculus
headline: Charles Kleinberg, Muted Prosecutor With a Sharp Calculus, Dies at 71
abstract: The more than 70 cases he tried in Brooklyn included the prosecution of a college dean accused of embezzlement and forced labor. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Louis Sheldon
headline: Louis Sheldon, Anti-Gay Minister With Political Clout, Dies at 85
abstract: The founder of the Traditional Values Coalition, he railed against what he called the “homosexual agenda,” gaining the ear of national politicians.

name: Guy Bedos
headline: Guy Bedos, Who Made France Laugh at Itself, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Inspired by Lenny Bruce, he spared no one in his bitingly satirical sketches while becoming a fixture of French movies and TV.

name: Grace Edwards
headline: Grace Edwards, Harlem Mystery Writer, Dies at 87
abstract: A former director of the Harlem Writers Guild, she published her first novel when she was 55, and her first mystery, featuring a stylish female ex-cop turned sleuth, when she was 64.

name: Harry Hoffman
headline: Harry Hoffman Dies at 92; Led the Expansion of Waldenbooks
abstract: In a pre-Amazon world, Mr. Hoffman solidified his company’s stature as the No. 1 book retailer in the United States.

name: Stacey Milbern
headline: Stacey Milbern, a Warrior for Disability Justice, Dies at 33
abstract: Ms. Milbern, who identified as queer, called out the mainstream disability movement for marginalizing people of color and nontraditional gender identities.

name: Sandra Gaines
headline: Sandra Gaines, Unflagging Banquet Server, Is Dead at 75
abstract: A stalwart worker and a valued colleague, she was also known for the lush garden she cultivated in her rare free time. Her death was related to Covid-19.

name: Robert Northern a.k.a. Brother Ah
headline: Robert Northern a.k.a. Brother Ah, Jazz Explorer, Dies at 86
abstract: A master of the French horn, Mr. Northern was adept at both classical music and jazz. As a bandleader, he was devoted to what he called “sound awareness.”

name: Shigeru Yokota
profession: Fought for Return of Abducted Daughter
headline: Shigeru Yokota, 87, Dies; Fought for Return of Abducted Daughter
abstract: He became the head of a group that fought tirelessly for the return to Japan of more than a dozen people kidnapped by the North Korean government.

name: Kurt Thomas
headline: Kurt Thomas, Trailblazing Champion Gymnast, Dies at 64
abstract: The first American to win a world championship in men’s gymnastics, he captured many medals but missed out on his best chance to take Olympic gold.

name: Evelyn Caro
headline: Evelyn Caro, Nurse Who Realized a Lifelong Dream, Dies at 69
abstract: Nearing 50, with her children grown, she went back to school and became a nurse. She came out of retirement only to die of the coronavirus.

name: Bradley Fields
headline: Bradley Fields, Magician Who Favored Warmth Over Flash, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Fields was an actor, mime, illusionist and educator who equated magic with pure wonder, not trickery. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Mary Pat Gleason
profession: Actress With Many Credits and a Cause
headline: Mary Pat Gleason, Actress With Many Credits and a Cause, Dies at 70
abstract: She was seen on TV shows like “Mom” and movies like “A Cinderella Story.” She also shared her experience with bipolar disorder in a one-woman play she wrote.

name: Bonnie Pointer
headline: Bonnie Pointer, a Founder of Sisters’ Vocal Group, Dies at 69
abstract: She started the Pointer Sisters with her siblings but left them to pursue a solo career before they went on to score hit after hit in the 1980s.

name: Bert Bial
profession: Philharmonic Musician With an Insiders Lens
headline: Bert Bial, Philharmonic Musician With an Insider’s Lens, Dies at 93
abstract: When he wasn’t playing bassoon he was taking photos, capturing the orchestra’s most memorable moments as well as more subtle ones.

name: Julio Guzman
headline: Julio Guzman, Salvadoran Refugee Who Started a Church, Dies at 64
abstract: Mr. Guzman proclaimed his faith in God even as he lay dying of Covid-19 in the hospital. He started his church in New Jersey 30 years ago.

name: Albert Memmi
headline: Albert Memmi, a ‘Jewish Arab’ Intellectual, Dies at 99
abstract: His books and novels were consumed by identity, as a Tunisian-born Jew who fled to France, and as a left-wing Zionist who supported a Palestinian homeland.

name: Lennie Niehaus
headline: Lennie Niehaus, Who Set Eastwood’s Films to Music, Dies at 90
abstract: After a high-profile stint as a saxophonist and arranger with Stan Kenton’s big band, he found new opportunities in Hollywood as a film and television composer.

name: Yves-Emmanuel Segui
headline: Yves-Emmanuel Segui, Indomitable Bronx Pharmacist, Dies at 60
abstract: After immigrating from Ivory Coast with a pharmacy degree, he repeatedly took and finally passed the exam qualifying him to work in his field, only to die of Covid-19 soon afterward.

name: Roberto Faraone Mennella
headline: Roberto Faraone Mennella, Jewelry Innovator, Is Dead at 48
abstract: He made a splash with a hoop earring called the Stella, seen first on “Sex and the City” and soon worn by Hollywood A-listers and many others.

name: Claudell Washington
headline: Claudell Washington, a Rookie Baseball Sensation at 19, Dies at 65
abstract: He helped the Oakland A’s win their third consecutive championship in 1974 and had a solid 17-season career. But he never matched his early heroics.

name: Marny Xiong
headline: Marny Xiong, Progressive Dynamo in Minnesota, Dies at 31
abstract: A child of Hmong refugees, she was chair of the St. Paul school board. The coronavirus struck her and her father on the same day. He survived; she didn't.

name: Nicholas Rinaldi
headline: Nicholas Rinaldi, Writer of Character-Rich Novels, Dies at 86
abstract: He was compared to Heller, Mailer and Styron, and though he never achieved their celebrity, he was beloved by his students and readers. He died in the coronavirus pandemic.

name: Pete Rademacher
headline: Pete Rademacher, 1956 Olympic Boxing Champion, Dies at 91
abstract: After winning gold, Rademacher concocted a scheme to take on Floyd Patterson, the world heavyweight champion.

name: Eva Konrad Hawkins
headline: Eva Konrad Hawkins, Marine Scientist Who Fled Hungary, Dies at 90
abstract: She lived through the Holocaust, Communism and the Hungarian Revolution of 1956. She died of Covid-19.

name: Salvatore Scilanga
headline: Salvatore Scilanga, Who Rescued Migrants at Sea, Dies at 51
abstract: His quiet generosity made him popular in town in Italy and among his colleagues in his country’s Coast Guard. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Murray Olderman
profession: Both Wrote and Drew About Sports
headline: Murray Olderman, Who Both Wrote and Drew About Sports, Dies at 98
abstract: At a time when caricatures were a regular part of the nation’s sports pages, Mr. Olderman thrived as a cartoonist. He also wrote features and columns.

name: James Harvey
headline: James Harvey, Who Wrote About Hollywood’s Heyday, Is Dead at 90
abstract: His meticulous, capacious books on silver-screen love, romantic comedy and the mysteries of star quality are required reading for cinephiles.

name: Margaret Holloway
headline: Margaret Holloway, the ‘Shakespeare Lady’ of New Haven, Dies at 68
abstract: A once-promising director and actor who struggled with mental illness and drug addiction, she performed for years on the city’s streets. She died of Covid-19.

name: Carol Krieger
headline: Carol Krieger, Who Taught Emotionally Impaired Children, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Krieger said her work, often with survivors of severe trauma, defined her. It was retirement that was hard. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Vicki Wood
headline: Vicki Wood, Who Broke Car-Racing Gender Barriers, Dies at 101
abstract: A trailblazer in a macho world, she burned up the sand at Daytona Beach, clocking in at more than 150 miles per hour.

name: Oleh Hornykiewicz
headline: Oleh Hornykiewicz, Who Discovered Parkinson’s Treatment, Dies at 93
abstract: His research into dopamine led to the mainstay treatment still used today to treat millions of people with Parkinson’s.

name: William S. Sessions
profession: F.B.I. Director at a Turbulent Time
headline: William S. Sessions, F.B.I. Director at a Turbulent Time, Dies at 90
abstract: He was applauded for broadening the bureau’s ranks to include more black, Hispanic and female agents. But many of his other actions drew severe criticism.

name: Cynthia Navaretta
headline: Cynthia Navaretta, Who Promoted Female Artists, Is Dead at 97
abstract: At a time when the art world was dominated by men, her newsletter and publishing house provided a voice for change.

name: Harry Glickman
headline: Harry Glickman, Who Brought Basketball to Oregon, Dies at 96
abstract: A native of Portland, Mr. Glickman founded the Trail Blazers and helped shape them into one of the N.B.A.’s great success stories.

name: Ralph Caplan
profession: Design Critic Big on Sit-Ins but Not Chairs
headline: Ralph Caplan, Design Critic Big on Sit-Ins but Not Chairs, Dies at 95
abstract: A writer, editor and consultant, his views on American product design allowed him to stray into a wide range of cultural issues, including the battle for civil rights.

name: Baruch Haviv
headline: Baruch Haviv, Pilot, Landlord and Opera Fan, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Haviv, who came to the United States penniless, believed Hell’s Kitchen had a bright future. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Rupert Hine
headline: Rupert Hine, Synth-Pop Music Producer, Dies at 72
abstract: He was behind Tina Turner’s “Better Be Good to Me” and hits by the Fixx and Howard Jones. He also made a dozen albums of his own songs.

name: Alan Hurwitz
headline: Alan Hurwitz, Teacher and Activist Who Turned to Bank Heists, Dies at 79
abstract: Once a Detroit educator committed to social justice, he developed a crack addiction and robbed 18 banks in three months, earning the name the “Zombie Bandit.” He died of Covid-19.

name: Leota Dooley
profession: Music Lover in the Colorado Mountains
headline: Leota Dooley, a Music Lover in the Colorado Mountains, Dies at 97
abstract: As a member of a singing group, she kept the Salida, Colo., area tuneful. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Edén Pastora
headline: Edén Pastora, ‘Commander Zero’ in Nicaragua, Dies at 83
abstract: A hero of the 1979 Sandinista revolution, he later turned on his comrades in arms, mounting an international campaign of political pressure and later guerrilla attacks inside the country.

name: Thomas Freeman
headline: Thomas Freeman, Debate Coach With Broad Influence, Dies at 100
abstract: His Texas Southern University team rose to national prominence, and Martin Luther King Jr., Barbara Jordan and Denzel Washington all learned from him.

name: Kristin Linklater
headline: Kristin Linklater, Who Made Actors Their Vocal Best, Dies at 84
abstract: Her methods went beyond mere diction and emphasized getting the whole body (and inner self) involved in speaking the words.

name: Yisroel Friedman
headline: Yisroel Friedman, Yeshiva Teacher and Scholar, Dies at 83
abstract: As pious as he was learned, Rabbi Friedman taught at a Brooklyn yeshiva for Orthodox Jews of the Chabad-Lubavitch sect. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Eduardo Cojuangco
headline: Eduardo Cojuangco, Philippine Tycoon and Marcos Ally, Dies at 85
abstract: A cousin of one president and a friend to others, the chairman of the San Miguel Corporation built up a billion-dollar fortune with the help of his political ties.

name: Manuel Felguérez
headline: Manuel Felguérez, Mexican Abstract Artist, Is Dead at 91
abstract: He was part of a movement that broke from traditional Mexican muralists like Diego Rivera. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Ronald Tackmann
profession: Escape Artist Better at Art Than Escaping
headline: Ronald Tackmann, Escape Artist Better at Art Than Escaping, Dies at 66
abstract: Despite three attempts to flee, he spent most of his life in prison, where he became a self-taught painter and sculptor.

name: Tomisaku Kawasaki
headline: Dr. Tomisaku Kawasaki, Who Pinpointed a Mysterious Disease, Dies at 95
abstract: In 1967, he identified a disease that causes heart inflammation in children, one that Covid-19 has brought back into the news.

name: Frederick C. Tillis
headline: Frederick C. Tillis, Composer Who Straddled Genres, Dies at 90
abstract: He began his career at 12, playing jazz in nightclubs. He went on to become a prolific composer who merged European and African-American influences.

name: Vanee Sykes
headline: Vanee Sykes, Ex-Prisoner Who Helped Others Rejoin Society, Dies at 53
abstract: She eased the transition of scores of women back into society. She also helped raise three children of her own from behind bars. She died of Covid-19.

name: Yupadee Kobkulboonsiri
headline: Yupadee Kobkulboonsiri, Designer of Otherworldly Jewelry, Dies at 51
abstract: She made whimsical high-end jewelry and transformed everyday objects into artwork, too. She died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Delbert Africa
profession: Convicted in Radical Groups Clash With Police
headline: Delbert Africa, 74, Convicted in Radical Group’s Clash With Police, Dies
abstract: As a member of Move, he spent four decades in prison and was released in January. His beating by Philadelphia police officers in 1978 was broadcast nationwide.

name: Vera Lynn
headline: Vera Lynn, Singer Whose Wartime Ballads Lifted Britain, Dies at 103
abstract: Known as the “Forces’ Sweetheart,” Ms. Lynn performed sentimental songs that captured the affection of troops abroad and Britons at home.

name: Jean Kennedy Smith
profession: Helped Forge Peace in Northern Ireland
headline: Jean Kennedy Smith Dies at 92; Helped Forge Peace in Northern Ireland
abstract: The last surviving sibling in a family that wrote itself into U.S. history, she was the first Kennedy woman of her generation to take on a serious political role.

name: Mady Mesplé
profession: French Soprano With a Silvery Voice
headline: Mady Mesplé, French Soprano With a Silvery Voice, Dies at 89
abstract: She achieved distinction in Europe with French opera roles and songs, but audiences also cherished her performances of operetta and works by Debussy, Ravel, Poulenc and Satie.

name: Messias Kokama
headline: Messias Kokama, Indigenous Leader in the Amazon, Dies at 53
abstract: Chief Kokama sought better treatment and opportunities for Indigenous people in Manaus, a major Brazilian city. He died of Covid-19.

name: Denny O’Neil
headline: Denny O’Neil, Writer Who Left His Mark on Batman, Dies at 81
abstract: In a long career with both DC and Marvel, Mr. O’Neil became best known for writing superhero comics that addressed social issues.

name: Nemir Kirdar
profession: Middle East Financier With Foot in the West
headline: Nemir Kirdar, Middle East Financier With Foot in the West, Dies at 83
abstract: The private equity firm he founded, Investcorp, tapped into Persian Gulf oil money and once purchased Tiffany and Co., Gucci and other Western brands.

name: Ian Holm
headline: Ian Holm, Malleable Actor Who Played Lear and a Hobbit, Dies at 88
abstract: A character actor who eventually took leading roles, Mr. Holm had a range that went from the sweet-tempered to the psychotic.

name: Nikita Price
profession: Homeless Father Turned Advocate for Homeless
headline: Nikita Price, Homeless Father Turned Advocate for Homeless, Dies at 63
abstract: He united people in shelters with those living on the streets, and he negotiated with city officials for greater support.

name: Lynika Strozier
headline: Lynika Strozier, Who Researched Early Plant DNA, Dies at 35
abstract: She overcame a severe learning disability to become a scientist with “golden hands” and most recently a college instructor. She died of Covid-19.

name: Michael Drosnin
headline: Michael Drosnin, Who Found Clues in the Bible, Is Dead at 74
abstract: His best-selling “Bible Code” books claimed that historical and future events were encoded in the Old Testament, although he couldn’t explain how or why.

name: Mike McCormick
headline: Mike McCormick, Comeback Cy Young Award Winner, Dies at 81
abstract: He was an All-Star fastball pitcher with the Giants until he developed a sore arm. He salvaged his career by learning to throw a screwball.

name: Carlos Ruiz Zafón
profession: Author of The Shadow of the Wind
headline: Carlos Ruiz Zafón, Author of ‘The Shadow of the Wind,’ Dies at 55
abstract: A story within a story that begins in a mysterious place known as the Cemetery of Forgotten Books, it is one of the most successful Spanish novels ever published.

name: Paolo Giorgio Ferri
headline: Paolo Giorgio Ferri, Hunter of Looted Antiquities, Dies at 72
abstract: A prosecutor in Italy, he dismantled multinational trafficking rings, recovering tens of thousands of Greco-Roman artifacts worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

name: Sally Banes
headline: Sally Banes, Distinguished Dance Critic and Historian, Dies at 69
abstract: Her writing paired a vivid and inquisitive approach with a lack of agenda and a belief that dance was a crucial part of cultural history.

name: Jim Kiick
profession: Helped the Dolphins Win 2 Super Bowls
headline: Jim Kiick, Who Helped the Dolphins Win 2 Super Bowls, Dies at 73
abstract: With Larry Csonka and Mercury Morris, he transformed the hapless Dolphins into a dominant team in the early 1970s.

name: Stephan L. Kamholz
profession: Chair of Medicine at Maimonides Hospital
headline: Stephan L. Kamholz, Chair of Medicine at Maimonides Hospital, Dies at 72
abstract: Dr. Kamholz was working hard on the front lines of a Brooklyn hospital swamped by the coronavirus. Then the virus got him.

name: Joel Schumacher
headline: Joel Schumacher, Director of ‘St. Elmo’s Fire,’ Is Dead at 80
abstract: His movies, which also included “The Lost Boys” and “Batman & Robin,” were cinematic mileposts of the 1980s and ’90s.

name: Jean Raspail
profession: Immigration Novel Drew the Far Right
headline: Jean Raspail, Whose Immigration Novel Drew the Far Right, Dies at 94
abstract: White supremacists saw his 1973 novel, “The Camp of the Saints,” about a dark-skinned “invasion,” as portending the end of Western civilization.

name: John Rankin
headline: John Rankin, Grant Proposal Writer Who Loved Languages, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Rankin was a proposal writer working in the Washington area before a series of strokes beginning in 2013 left him disabled. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Brenda Ravenell
headline: Brenda Ravenell, Lawyer With a Compassionate Touch, Dies at 64
abstract: With her gentle personality, she practiced family law in New Jersey, while her partner worked on personal injury cases. She died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Shirley Siegel
profession: Leading New York Civil Rights Lawyer
headline: Shirley Siegel, Leading New York Civil Rights Lawyer, Dies at 101
abstract: Initially snubbed by 40 law firms, she went on to become the solicitor general of New York State and argued cases before the Supreme Court.

name: Eula Bingham
headline: Eula Bingham, Champion of Worker Safety, Dies at 90
abstract: As head of OSHA under President Carter, she dispensed with “nit-picking” regulations and went after serious health and safety violations.

name: Steve Bing
headline: Steve Bing, Hollywood Producer and Financier, Is Dead at 55
abstract: An heir to a New York real estate fortune, he was involved in a number of popular films. A police official said he had jumped from a high-rise balcony.

name: Paulinho Paiakan
headline: Paulinho Paiakan, Indigenous Defender of Rainforest, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Paiakan became celebrated internationally for his campaigns in Brazil, even appearing once with Sting. He died of Covid-19.

name: Paul Fortune
headline: Paul Fortune, L.A. Designer to the Stars, Dies at 69
abstract: He designed the interiors of the Tower Bar and the homes of Sofia Coppola, Marc Jacobs and other celebrities.

name: Robert Laughlin
headline: Robert Laughlin, Preserver of a Mayan Language, Dies at 85
abstract: His monumental dictionary, after years of field work, documented Tzotzil in southern Mexico. But that was just the start of his efforts to preserve the culture.

name: Dan Foster
profession: American-Born Big Dawg of Nigerian Radio
headline: Dan Foster, the American-Born ‘Big Dawg’ of Nigerian Radio, Dies at 61
abstract: Mr. Foster, a former U.S. Marine, pioneered a new style of on-air personality in his African home, becoming a top celebrity. He died after testing positive for the coronavirus.

name: Kirk Smith
headline: Kirk Smith, Towering Figure in Environmental Science, Dies at 73
abstract: Dr. Smith’s meticulous research established household pollution as one of the leading causes of disease and death in the developing world.

name: Sergei Khrushchev
headline: Sergei Khrushchev, Son of Former Soviet Premier, Dies at 84
abstract: A rocket scientist in the Soviet Union, he became a U.S. citizen long after the Cold War ended. “I’m not a defector,” he said. “I like this country.”

name: Michael Hawley
headline: Michael Hawley, Programmer, Professor and Pianist, Dies at 58
abstract: A man of manifold interests, his achievements ranged from developing ideas behind the so-called Internet of Things to publishing the world’s biggest book.

name: Dennis Nagle
profession: Free Spirit With an Engineers Mind
headline: Dennis Nagle, Free Spirit With an Engineer’s Mind, Dies at 78
abstract: He lived a life of sex, drugs and rock ’n’ roll before settling into a fulfilling job at M.I.T. late in life. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Chris Trousdale
profession: Boy Band Idol With a Broadway Past
headline: Chris Trousdale, Boy Band Idol With a Broadway Past, Dies at 34
abstract: He was scouted for the group Dream Street at 14 after appearing on Broadway in “Les Misérables.” He died of the coronavirus.

name: Elsa Joubert
headline: Elsa Joubert, 97, Dies; Afrikaans Writer Explored Black Reality
abstract: Her novel “The Long Journey of Poppie Nongena” was compared to Alan Paton’s “Cry, the Beloved Country” in arousing white opinion against apartheid. She had Covid-19.

name: Akbar Nurid-Din Shabazz
headline: Akbar Nurid-Din Shabazz, Texas Prison Chaplain, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Shabazz spent 40 years providing support to inmates in Texas prisons and was credited with expanding the practice of Islam there. He died of Covid-19.

name: Zeev Sternhell
headline: Zeev Sternhell, ‘Super Zionist’ Wary of Extremism, Dies at 85
abstract: A scholar of European fascism (and a bomb attack target), he feared ultranationalism in Israel and saw West Bank settlements as “a cancer.”

name: John J. Mooney
headline: John J. Mooney, an Inventor of the Catalytic Converter, Dies at 90
abstract: The device he developed with a colleague in the 1970s has prevented billions of tons of emissions from being spewed by cars, trucks and lawn mowers.

name: Li Zhensheng
headline: Li Zhensheng, Photographer of China’s Cultural Revolution, Dies at 79
abstract: With his camera and red arm band, he captured the dark side of Mao’s revolution at great personal risk. Many of the images were stashed under a floor, going undeveloped for years.

name: Valerie Solanas
headline: Overlooked No More: Valerie Solanas, Radical Feminist Who Shot Andy Warhol
abstract: She made daring arguments in “SCUM Manifesto,” her case for a world without men. But it was her attack on Warhol that came to define her life.

name: Lester Crystal
headline: Lester Crystal, Guiding Force Behind ‘NewsHour,’ Dies at 85
abstract: As executive producer, he expanded the PBS newscast to an hour and helped make it a distinctive voice in broadcast journalism.

name: Angela Marie Rooney
profession: Oldest Member of Her Order in New York
headline: Sister Angela Marie Rooney, 103, Dies; Oldest Member of Her Order in New York
abstract: Sister Angela was a teacher, secretary and, in her late decades, a whiz on the computer. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Kenneth Lewes
headline: Kenneth Lewes, Who Challenged Views of Homosexuality, Dies at 76
abstract: In an influential book, he defied the idea that being gay, as he was, is an illness, and took on psychiatry’s “history of homophobia.” He died of the coronavirus.

name: Thomas Blanton
headline: Thomas Blanton, Who Bombed a Birmingham Church, Dies at 82
abstract: He was the last survivor of three Klansmen who were convicted, years later, in the killing four black girls in 1963, a case that was a turning point in the civil rights struggle.

name: Milton Glaser
profession: Master Designer of I ♥ NY Logo
headline: Milton Glaser, Master Designer of ‘I ♥ NY’ Logo, Is Dead at 91
abstract: He was also a founder of New York magazine, created a memorable Bob Dylan poster and produced designs for everything from supermarkets to restaurants to “Mad Men.”

name: Elly Stone
profession: Distinctive Singer in Jacques Brel Revue
headline: Elly Stone, 93, Distinctive Singer in ‘Jacques Brel’ Revue, Dies
abstract: She performed some of the most powerful songs in that show, which ran for more than four years in Greenwich Village and became a theater staple.

name: William Dement
headline: Dr. William Dement, Leader in Sleep Disorder Research, Dies at 91
abstract: At Stanford, he created the world’s first successful sleep clinic and taught a popular class on sleep and dreams. (If he caught students dozing, he’d wake them with a water gun.)

name: Charles Webb
headline: Charles Webb, Elusive Author of ‘The Graduate,’ Dies at 81
abstract: His novel was turned into an era-defining movie, but he was never comfortable with its success, and he chose to live in poverty.

name: Linda Cristal
headline: Linda Cristal, Who Starred in ‘High Chaparral,’ Dies at 89
abstract: To win the role of the fiery Victoria Cannon, she said, she threw away the script and “made up stories showing love, hate, passion, envy, jealousy, etc.”

name: Mike East
profession: Lowered U.S. Flag in Havana in 1961
headline: Mike East, Who Lowered U.S. Flag in Havana in 1961, Dies at 81
abstract: Along with two fellow Marines, he was back in Cuba when a flag was hoisted again at the American Embassy in 2015.

name: Sérgio Sant’Anna
profession: Brazilian Master of the Short Story
headline: Sérgio Sant’Anna, Brazilian Master of the Short Story, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Sant’Anna wrote novels and poetry, but was most famous for stories that used a sardonic humor to skewer the fractures within Brazilian society. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Yvonne Sherwell
headline: Yvonne Sherwell, Actress, Author and Coat Checker, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Ms. Sherwell led an artistic existence in bohemian New York, appearing in plays, movies and cabaret. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Ruth Buchanan
headline: Ruth Buchanan, Philanthropist and Hostess Extraordinaire, Is Dead at 101
abstract: She and her husband, an ambassador who later served as White House chief of protocol, presided over grand gatherings in Washington and Newport, R.I.

name: Madeline McWhinney Dale
headline: Madeline McWhinney Dale, Trailblazing Banker, Is Dead at 98
abstract: She was the first female officer of the Federal Reserve Bank. Later, in another first, she ran a commercial bank largely owned and operated by women.

name: Carl Reiner
headline: Carl Reiner, Multifaceted Master of Comedy, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Mr. Reiner was a gifted comic actor, but he spent most of his career slightly out of the spotlight — writing, directing and letting others get the laughs.

name: Johnny Mandel
headline: Johnny Mandel, 94, Writer of Memorable Movie Scores, Is Dead
abstract: After composing and arranging for big bands, he gave the world melodies like “The Shadow of Your Smile,” “Emily” and “Suicide Is Painless.”

name: Angela Madsen
headline: Angela Madsen, Paralympian Rower, Dies on Solo Pacific Voyage at 60
abstract: With her legs paralyzed, she found freedom rowing across oceans. “It’s hopeless, it’s majestic, it’s exhilarating,” she said.

name: Lewis John Carlino
headline: Lewis John Carlino, Oscar-Nominated Screenwriter, Dies at 88
abstract: Remembered for his adaptations of “I Never Promised You a Rose Garden” and “The Great Santini,” he prided himself on knowing his characters inside and out.

name: Georg Ratzinger
headline: Rev. Georg Ratzinger, Choirmaster and a Pope’s Brother, Dies at 96
abstract: Father Ratzinger, a trained musician, pursued a career far away from the world of the Vatican and the future Pope Benedict XVI.

name: Tito Vértiz
headline: Tito Vértiz, Prison Therapist, Novelist and Painter, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Vértiz, a citizen of three countries, left Peru as a flight attendant in the 1960s and built friendships around the world. He died of Covid-19.

name: Gregory Katz
profession: Reporter at Home in War or Fashion
headline: Gregory Katz, Reporter at Home in War or Fashion, Dies at 67
abstract: As The Associated Press’s acting London bureau chief, Mr. Katz covered everything with gusto, including the Royal Family. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Anders Ericsson
headline: Anders Ericsson, Psychologist and ‘Expert on Experts,’ Dies at 72
abstract: His research helped inspire “Outliers,” Malcolm Gladwell’s best-selling book on the keys to excelling.

name: Karl Heinrich Ulrichs
headline: Overlooked No More: Karl Heinrich Ulrichs, Pioneering Gay Activist
abstract: Before the word “homosexuality” existed, he argued that same-sex attraction was innate, and that those who experienced it should be treated the same as anyone else.

name: Allen Lew
headline: Allen Lew, a Virtuoso Builder of Public Works, Dies at 69
abstract: He bypassed red tape and erected stadiums, schools, hospitals and convention centers in Washington and New York. Mr. Lew died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Nelson Henry
headline: Nelson Henry Dies at 96; Fought to Correct Military Slight
abstract: In World War II, he was given an insulting “blue discharge”; more than 70 years later, he was upgraded to “honorable.” He died of the coronavirus.

name: Hugh Downs
headline: Hugh Downs, Perennial Small-Screen Fixture, Is Dead at 99
abstract: A longtime host of both “Today” and “20/20,” for many years he held the Guinness-certified record for most total hours on commercial network television.

name: Lester Grinspoon
headline: Lester Grinspoon, Influential Marijuana Scholar, Dies at 92
abstract: He believed pot was dangerous until his research convinced him otherwise. He then became a leading proponent of legalization.

name: Freddy Cole
headline: Freddy Cole, Performer Who Emerged From Nat’s Shadow, Dies at 88
abstract: Like his famous older sibling, he played the piano and sang. But he used his music to insist, “I’m Not My Brother, I’m Me.”

name: Gay Culverhouse
headline: Gay Culverhouse,Who Helped Injured Football Players, Dies at 73
abstract: She navigated the league’s male-dominated world as a team president, then devoted her energy to fighting on behalf of players with brain disorders.

name: Gregori Armstrong
headline: Gregori Armstrong, a Chicago Ironworker, Dies at 66
abstract: He helped build his hometown for four decades. He also enjoyed fixing things and taking care of loved ones. He had tested positive for the coronavirus.

name: Maria de Sousa
headline: Maria de Sousa, Leading Portuguese Scientist, Dies at 80
abstract: She focused on the immune system and helped establish a major academic program in her field. She died after testing positive for the novel coronavirus.

name: James Sherwood
headline: James Sherwood, Who Revived the Orient Express, Dies at 86
abstract: A multimillionaire by 36, he also bought Cipriani in Venice, the “21” Club in New York, Harry’s Bar in London and dozens of grand hotels.

name: Margaret Morton
profession: Photographer at Home With the Homeless
headline: Margaret Morton, Photographer at Home With the Homeless, Dies at 71
abstract: For nearly two decades, she chronicled communities on the edge of society in elegant photographs that drew comparisons to the work of Jacob Riis.

name: Lenora Fay Garfinkel
headline: Lenora Fay Garfinkel, 90, Architect for Orthodox Jewish Communities, Dies
abstract: Ms. Garfinkel thrived in a field dominated by men, juggling a career while raising five children. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Saroj Khan
headline: Saroj Khan, Choreographer Who Made Bollywood Sparkle, Dies at 71
abstract: After entering the industry as a child actress, Ms. Khan went on to choreograph some of the most memorable performances of the 1980s and ’90s.

name: Tânio Mendonça
headline: Tânio Mendonça, Brazilian Carnaval Samba Composer, Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. Mendonça, who wrote music for Rio’s spectacular annual parades, was one of many victims of the novel coronavirus within the world of Carnaval.

name: Rudolfo Anaya
headline: Rudolfo Anaya, a Father of Chicano Literature, Dies at 82
abstract: His coming-of-age novel “Bless Me, Ultima” reframed the way many in New Mexico viewed their own history, even as school districts tried to ban it.

name: Lonnie Wheeler
headline: Lonnie Wheeler, 68, Dies; Helped Ballplayers Tell Their Stories
abstract: A longtime sportswriter, he collaborated with Hank Aaron, Bob Gibson and Mike Piazza on their autobiographies. “I was there,” he once said, “to make the subject more literary.”

name: Marc Fumaroli
headline: Marc Fumaroli, Defender of French Culture, Is Dead at 88
abstract: A leading historian, he wrote and taught in defense of the French language and its heritage and against “globish English.”

name: Nikolai Fadeyechev
headline: Nikolai Fadeyechev, Elegant Bolshoi Dancer, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Acclaimed for his noble style, he was also praised as a “self-deprecating” partner who showed off his ballerinas and did not compete with them.

name: Nick Cordero
profession: Nominated for Tony as Tap-Dancing Tough Guy
headline: Nick Cordero, Nominated for Tony as Tap-Dancing Tough Guy, Dies at 41
abstract: The Broadway actor’s battle with the coronavirus was followed closely by many as his wife chronicled his experience on social media.

name: Ennio Morricone
headline: Ennio Morricone, Oscar-Winning Composer of Film Scores, Dies at 91
abstract: His vast output included atmospheric music for spaghetti westerns in his native Italy and scores for some 500 movies by a Who’s Who of directors.

name: Charlie Daniels
profession: Fiddling Force in Country and Rock
headline: Charlie Daniels, Fiddling Force in Country and Rock, Dies at 83
abstract: He was a singer, songwriter, bandleader and a blazing fiddle player on hits like “The Devil Went Down to Georgia.” His politics swung, too, from left to right.

name: Dulce Nunes
headline: Dulce Nunes, Bossa Nova Star of the 1960s, Dies at 90
abstract: She was best-known for the 1964 album “Poor Little Rich Girl.” She died of Covid-19.

name: Richard di Liberto
headline: Richard di Liberto, Expert Photographer of Museum Art, Dies at 82
abstract: His photos of the Frick Collection’s artworks illustrate books and catalogs and helped create the museum’s visual identity. He died of Covid-19.

name: Emma Sanders
headline: Emma Sanders, 91, Dies; Challenged Segregating of Democrats
abstract: She was one of the “unofficial” slate of Black Mississippians who sought to displace the nonrepresentative all-white delegation at the 1964 Democratic National Convention.

name: Henry Martin
headline: Henry Martin, Wry New Yorker Cartoonist, Is Dead at 94
abstract: He defined his artistic mission as finding humor in the mundane and everyday — and he found it for 35 years.

name: Kevin Rafferty
headline: Kevin Rafferty, ‘Atomic Cafe’ Co-Director, Dies at 73
abstract: In that acclaimed Cold War documentary and other films, he often let archival footage do the talking.

name: Mary Kay Letourneau
headline: Mary Kay Letourneau, Teacher Who Raped Student and Then Married Him, Dies at 58
abstract: A tabloid fixture in the 1990s, she defended the relationship as consensual, as did he.

name: Santiago Manuin
headline: Santiago Manuin, Indigenous Leader in Peru, Dies at 63
abstract: Mr. Manuin fought for the rights of Indigenous people and the protection of the Amazon. He survived a gunshot wound from a 2009 police crackdown, but died last week of Covid-19.

name: Brad Lomax
headline: Overlooked No More: Brad Lomax, a Bridge Between Civil Rights Movements
abstract: A member of the Black Panthers, he helped lead a historic, and successful, sit-in in San Francisco as part of a nationwide anti-discrimination campaign on behalf of people with disabilities.

name: Ida Haendel
profession: Violin Virtuoso With Fire and Ice in Her Playing
headline: Ida Haendel, Violin Virtuoso With ‘Fire and Ice’ in Her Playing, Dies
abstract: A link to the early-20th-century school of violin playing, Ms. Haendel was a noted champion of the concertos of Britten, Walton and Sibelius.

name: James Harrison
headline: James Harrison, Music Professor and Piano Lover, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Harrison was a longtime teacher of music theory and a dean of fine arts and humanities at Hunter College in Manhattan. He has died of complications of Covid-19.

name: James Harrison
headline: James Harrison, Whose Antibodies Helped Millions, Dies at 88
abstract: James Harrison earned the nickname “The Man With the Golden Arm” because his blood had a rare antibody that may have helped more than two million babies in Australia.

name: Ola Mae Spinks
headline: Ola Mae Spinks, Who Helped Preserve a Slave Archive, Dies at 106
abstract: In 1972, she and another librarian went to the Library of Congress to bring order to a sprawling collection of interviews with former slaves.

name: Helen O’Hagan
headline: Helen O’Hagan, Fashion Executive Who Personified Saks, Dies at 89
abstract: As the store’s head of publicity, she promoted top designers. She also lived a glamorous life as the friend and caregiver of the actress Claudette Colbert.

name: Adrian Gomez
headline: Adrian Gomez, Who Cared for Migrant Youth, Is Dead at 52
abstract: He worked at a shelter in Texas and as a juvenile probation officer; he wanted, his daughter said, to make a difference. He died of complications of the novel coronavirus.

name: Martha Rocha
profession: to Brazil, a Beauty Queen Denied a Crown
headline: Martha Rocha, 87, Dies; to Brazil, a Beauty Queen Denied a Crown
abstract: Popular opinion has held that she came in second in the 1954 Miss Universe pageant because she didn’t conform to a North American standard of beauty.

name: Herman Benson
headline: Herman Benson, Who Fought Union Corruption, Dies at 104
abstract: A machinist and Socialist from the Bronx, he pushed trade unions to be more democratic and to depose crooked labor leaders.

name: Earl Cameron
headline: Earl Cameron, Barrier-Breaking British Actor, Is Dead at 102
abstract: In the 1950s and ’60s, when Black leading men and women were virtually nonexistent on British screens, he became a star. He continued to make movies into his 90s.

name: Everton Weekes
headline: Everton Weekes, Cricket Star and Racial Pioneer, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Along with his fellow Barbados batsmen Frank Worrell and Clyde Walcott — together they were “the three Ws” — he broke the sport’s longstanding color barrier.

name: Marga Richter
headline: Marga Richter, Composer in a Male-Dominated Era, Dies at 93
abstract: During a career that began in the 1940s and stretched into this century, she often felt she and other women were slighted.

name: Edward Kleinbard
headline: Edward Kleinbard, Tax Lawyer Turned Reformer, Dies at 68
abstract: After advising multinationals for 30 years, he began teaching and writing, criticizing corporate tax dodging and pressing for higher taxes to combat inequality.

name: Jack Charlton
profession: Soccer Hero in England and Ireland
headline: Jack Charlton, Soccer Hero in England and Ireland, Dies at 85
abstract: A towering defender, he won the World Cup with his home country in 1966 and went on to coach the Irish national team to memorable runs in 1990 and 1994.

name: Paik Sun-yup
profession: Lightning Rod General in South Korea
headline: ​Paik Sun-yup, Lightning Rod General in South Korea, Dies at 99
abstract: The country’s first four-star general, he was a war hero to the U.S. and South Korean militaries. But many saw him as a traitor who had collaborated with the Japanese.

name: Ragaa el-Gedawy
headline: Ragaa el-Gedawy, Cherished Star of Egyptian Cinema, Dies at 85
abstract: She endeared herself to audiences with her grace, naturalism and comic skill. She fell ill after filming a TV series in May and died from Covid-19 in July.

name: Lucius Barker
profession: Expert on Race in American Politics
headline: Lucius Barker, Expert on Race in American Politics, Dies at 92
abstract: He was a passionate Jesse Jackson delegate at the 1984 Democratic National Convention and, later, a mentor to future politicians like Senator Cory Booker.

name: Rex Robles
headline: Rex Robles, Plotter of Philippine Coups, Is Dead at 77
abstract: He was seen as the chief theorist and propaganda expert of a group of ambitious military officers who worked to oust two presidents.

name: Marlo
profession: Rising Atlanta Rapper With Big Connections
headline: Marlo, a Rising Atlanta Rapper With Big Connections, Is Shot and Killed at 30
abstract: A local favorite who came up alongside Lil Baby and Migos, Marlo was found dead after a highway shooting on Saturday night.

name: Kelly Preston
headline: Kelly Preston, ‘Jerry Maguire’ Star, Dies at 57
abstract: Ms. Preston, who was married to John Travolta, was known for her role in “Jerry Maguire” as the hardhearted fiancée of the Tom Cruise character.

name: Jose Morón
headline: Jose Morón, Whose Metal Creations Adorned Chicago, Dies at 54
abstract: An immigrant from Mexico, Mr. Morón established a metalwork company and earned the loyalty of clients and employees. He has died of Covid-19.

name: Louis Colavecchio
headline: Louis Colavecchio, Master Counterfeiter, Is Dead at 78
abstract: A former jewelry maker, he crafted fake slot machine coins that even officials had a hard time telling from legitimate ones under a microscope.

name: Judy Dyble
profession: Singer in Fairport Convention and Beyond
headline: Judy Dyble, Singer in Fairport Convention and Beyond, Dies at 71
abstract: Her crystalline soprano drew on folk tradition, but she also embraced psychedelia and progressive rock.

name: Michael Lewis
profession: Forged a New Life After Prison
headline: Michael Lewis, Who Forged a New Life After Prison, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Lewis counseled newly released inmates on how to adjust to life on the outside, using a simple orange bag to make his point. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Zindzi Mandela
profession: Activist in South Africa and Ambassador
headline: Zindzi Mandela, Activist in South Africa and Ambassador, Dies at 59
abstract: She was ambassador to Denmark after years as a voice against apartheid (sometimes in poetry) alongside her parents, Nelson Mandela and Winnie Madikizela-Mandela.

name: Grant Imahara
headline: Grant Imahara, Engineer Who Co-Hosted ‘MythBusters,’ Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. Imahara also worked behind the scenes on the “Matrix” sequels, among other films, and operated the robot R2-D2 in the “Star Wars” prequels.

name: Thereza de Orléans e Bragança
headline: Thereza de Orléans e Bragança, Brazilian Society Doyenne, Dies at 91
abstract: Once called “the best dressed woman in Rio de Janeiro” by Life magazine, she was an “old money” style-setter in the 1950s and ’60s before marrying into Brazilian royalty.

name: Jay Riffe
headline: Jay Riffe, Spearfishing King, Is Dead at 82
abstract: He became a champion in sport fishing while in his 20s and went on to found a leading company in the manufacture of spearfishing and diving gear.

name: Abraham Vega
headline: Abraham Vega, 48, ‘Peacemaking’ Texas Sheriff, Dies
abstract: Remarried, likely to win re-election in November, he was embarking on a second act when he died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Blaine Kern
profession: Architect of Lavish Mardi Gras Floats
headline: Blaine Kern, Architect of Lavish Mardi Gras Floats, Dies at 93
abstract: The work of Mr. Kern, known as “Mr. Mardi Gras,” has delighted visitors to Carnival in New Orleans for decades.

name: Molly Neptune Parker
headline: Molly Neptune Parker, Basket Maker and Tribal Elder, Dies at 81
abstract: Ms. Parker was the matriarch of four generations of basket makers and one of the first female lieutenant governors of the Passamaquoddy Tribe.

name: Vickey Gibbs
headline: Rev. Vickey Gibbs, Activist in a Progressive Church, Dies at 57
abstract: Ms. Gibbs used her pulpit in Houston to treat broken parishioners in a broken social world. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Leonardo Villar
headline: Leonardo Villar, Venerated Brazilian Actor, Dies at 96
abstract: From telenovelas to a winner of the Palme d’Or, this member of Brazil’s cinematic royalty devoted himself entirely to his work.

name: David Kaiser
headline: David Kaiser, Rockefeller Heir Who Fought Exxon Mobil, Dies at 50
abstract: A great-great grandson of John D. Rockefeller, he steered one of his family’s philanthropies to a feisty stance on the oil giant’s role in climate change.

name: Hillary Gregg
headline: Hillary Gregg, Line Cook at Top-Shelf Restaurants, Dies at 73
abstract: He was the Quilted Giraffe’s longtime “walking cookbook” and later cooked at another Manhattan restaurant, March. He died of Covid-19.

name: Joanna Cole
headline: Joanna Cole, Who Imagined Fantastical Bus Rides, Dies at 75
abstract: Her “Magic School Bus” children’s books were wild, and wildly popular. They were also educational.

name: Eddie Gale
headline: Eddie Gale, Deeply Spiritual Jazz Trumpeter, Dies at 78
abstract: He drew notice in the 1960s for his provocative playing with Cecil Taylor and Sun Ra and on his own records. He later devoted most of his time to teaching.

name: Christopher Dickey
headline: Christopher Dickey, Renowned Foreign Correspondent, Dies at 68
abstract: He reported from Paris and from war zones and published seven books, including a pained memoir about growing up with his father, the poet James Dickey.

name: C.T. Vivian
headline: C.T. Vivian, Martin Luther King’s Field General, Dies at 95
abstract: A disciplined advocate of nonviolence, he was on the front lines in the 1960s movement for racial justice.

name: Nancy Green
headline: Overlooked No More: Nancy Green, the ‘Real Aunt Jemima’
abstract: A nanny and cook, she played the part as the pancake flour company that employed her perpetuated a racial stereotype. She died 97 years ago in Chicago.

name: Brandis Kemp
headline: Brandis Kemp, Character Actress and ‘Fridays’ Original, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Kemp told comically gruesome fortunes on “Fridays” and made doctors’ lives miserable on “AfterMASH.” She died of a brain tumor and complications of Covid-19.

name: Emily Howell Warner
headline: Emily Howell Warner, Who Broke a Sky-High Glass Ceiling, Dies at 80
abstract: She was the first woman hired to command the cockpit for a major American airline on scheduled flights and the first woman to achieve the airline rank of captain.

name: Flossie Wong-Staal
headline: Flossie Wong-Staal, Who Unlocked Mystery of H.I.V., Dies at 73
abstract: A molecular biologist, she helped establish the virus as the cause of AIDS, then cloned it and took it apart to understand how it evades the immune system.

name: Jane Walentas
headline: Jane Walentas, Who Planted a Carousel in Dumbo, Dies at 76
abstract: With her husband, David, Ms. Walentas helped develop the Brooklyn waterfront neighborhood into a desirable address — and gave it an unusual gift.

name: Gabriella Tucci
profession: Italian Soprano and Met Opera Mainstay
headline: Gabriella Tucci, 90, Dies; Italian Soprano and Met Opera Mainstay
abstract: Ms. Tucci’s voice had luster, and she brought refinement to her singing. She sang 20 roles at the Met, where her heyday was the 1960s.

name: Frans Nieuwendam
headline: Frans Nieuwendam, Who Knew Style and Had It, Dies at 60
abstract: He was a quiet force in fashion, though others knew him as the guy to try to impress on the rope line. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Brigid Berlin
headline: Brigid Berlin, Socialite Who Joined Warhol’s World, Dies at 80
abstract: Born into privilege, she rejected her upbringing to become a fixture on the New York underground art scene of the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Luther Price
headline: Luther Price, Experimental Artist and Filmmaker, Dies at 58
abstract: He explored family, sexuality and death, using found footage, emulsion scraps and dust bunnies as his medium. And he kept his real name a secret.

name: Gordon Bower
headline: Gordon Bower, Inventive Memory Researcher, Is Dead at 87
abstract: In a long career at Stanford, he was known for elegant experiments that explored how we learn and how we remember.

name: Nakotah LaRance
headline: Nakotah LaRance, Acclaimed Native American Hoop Dancer, Dies at 30
abstract: A nine-time winner at the World Championship of Hoop Dance, he also performed with Cirque du Soleil.

name: Emitt Rhodes
headline: Emitt Rhodes, 70, Dies; Singer-Songwriter Vanished After a Splash
abstract: He resurfaced a decade ago, after having built a fan base that compared him to Paul McCartney.

name: Zizi Jeanmaire
headline: Zizi Jeanmaire, French Star of Ballet, Cabaret and Film, Dies at 96
abstract: She was celebrated for her artistic range, androgynous sexiness and husky-voiced charm.

name: Cosmas Magaya
profession: Musician and Teacher of African Traditions
headline: Cosmas Magaya, Musician and Teacher of African Traditions, Dies at 66
abstract: A virtuoso of the mbira, a plucked instrument, he shared his knowledge with the wider world to preserve wisdom handed down orally. He died of Covid-19.

name: Paul Fusco
headline: Paul Fusco, Photographer on a Funeral Train, Dies at 89
abstract: The pictures he took after Robert Kennedy’s assassination are among his many photographs that captured the human side of important events.

name: Dick Buerkle
headline: Dick Buerkle, Master of the Indoor Mile, Dies at 72
abstract: After running the 5,000 meters, Buerkle, a former Villanova walk-on, devoted himself to the mile and set a record. He regretted missing the 1980 Moscow Olympics.

name: Andrew Mlangeni
profession: Ally of Mandela in Anti-Apartheid Struggle
headline: Andrew Mlangeni, Ally of Mandela in Anti-Apartheid Struggle, Dies at 95
abstract: He was a convicted co-defendant with Mr. Mandela at the Rivonia Trial of 1964, which exposed to the world the injustices of South Africa’s segregationist policies.

name: Annie Ross
headline: Annie Ross, Jazz Vocalist of ‘Twisted’ Renown, Dies at 89
abstract: She rose to fame with the vocal group Lambert, Hendricks and Ross and, after personal struggles, found success as both an actress and a cabaret mainstay.

name: Samantha Diaz
headline: Samantha Diaz, Florida Health Care Worker, Dies at 29
abstract: She left behind three children — two of whom have the novel coronavirus — in the care of her parents. “Our world came crashing down,” her mother said after Ms. Diaz died of Covid-19.

name: Tony Elliott
headline: Tony Elliott, Whose Time Out Clued Readers In, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Elliott said, “I had one idea, but it was a good one.” On it he built a global publishing empire.

name: Constance Curry
profession: Author and Ally in Civil Rights Fight
headline: Constance Curry, 86, Author and Ally in Civil Rights Fight, Dies
abstract: She was a bridge between Black activists and white Southerners, worked for Andrew Young and chronicled a Black Mississippi family’s struggle against racism.

name: Phyllis Somerville
headline: Phyllis Somerville, Busy Stage and Screen Actress, Dies at 76
abstract: She specialized in supporting roles, including an attention-getting recurring character in “The Big C.”

name: Charles Evers
headline: Charles Evers, Businessman and Civil Rights Leader, Dies at 97
abstract: Galvanized by the assassination of his brother, Medgar, he helped transform Mississippi politics, running for Congress, becoming a mayor and gaining wide attention.

name: Ronald L. Graham
headline: Ronald L. Graham, Who Unlocked the Magic of Numbers, Dies at 84
abstract: He was pre-eminent in the field of discrete mathematics, coming up with “some really pretty cool stuff.” (He was also a world-class juggler.)

name: Gerald Williams
headline: Gerald Williams, Poet, Essayist and Editor, Dies at 85
abstract: Bronx-born and Boston-educated, he also worked as a translator in Paris and Amsterdam before settling in New York in the late 1960s. He died of Covid-19.

name: Samantha Hickey
profession: Nurse With a Gift for Diagnosis
headline: Samantha Hickey, Nurse With a Gift for Diagnosis, Dies at 45
abstract: Ms. Hickey trained dozens of junior colleagues and exercised rare skills as a diagnostician over more than 20 years as a nurse in southwestern Idaho. She died of Covid-19.

name: Juan Marsé
headline: Juan Marsé, Who Wrote of Spain’s Dark Years, Is Dead at 87
abstract: His novels chronicled the difficult days after the Spanish Civil War. He was, his biographer, said, “the reference writer of the anti-Franco movement.”

name: Keith Sonnier
headline: Keith Sonnier, Playful Sculptor in Neon, Dies at 78
abstract: He tweaked the solemnity of Post-Minimalism with a sense of poetry and fun, using functional everyday materials.

name: Anthony Terlato
profession: Brought Pinot Grigio to the U.S
headline: Anthony Terlato, Who Brought Pinot Grigio to the U.S., Dies at 86
abstract: In a 60-year career as a wine importer and marketer, he introduced Americans to lesser-known labels and shaped tastes.

name: Cheryl Marie Wade
headline: Overlooked No More: Cheryl Marie Wade, a Performer Who Refused to Hide
abstract: Going public with her disability helped her cope with the pain and hardship she felt.

name: Benjamin Mkapa
headline: Benjamin Mkapa, Ex-President of Tanzania, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Mkapa served two terms, from 1995 to 2005. The third president of his country since independence, he was the first democratically elected leader after its transition to multiparty politics.

name: Nadine Taub
profession: Early Leader in Womens Rights Law
headline: Nadine Taub, Early Leader in Women’s Rights Law, Dies at 77
abstract: Along with other feminist lawyers like Ruth Bader Ginsburg, Ms. Taub made legal history in cases that argued that the Constitution protected women’s rights.

name: Marlene Sekaquaptewa
headline: Marlene Sekaquaptewa, Hopi Tribal Leader and Quiltmaker, Dies at 79
abstract: She played a major role in Hopi Tribal government for decades and was governor of the village of Bacavi when she died after testing positive for Covid-19.

name: Brad Watson
profession: His Southern Upbringing Animated His Books
headline: Brad Watson, 64, Dies; His Southern Upbringing Animated His Books
abstract: In his acclaimed novels and short stories, most of them set in his native Mississippi, he wrote about characters who had to transcend difficult moments.

name: Bruce Blair
headline: Bruce Blair, Crusader for Nuclear Arms Control, Dies at 72
abstract: A former Minuteman launch officer, he sounded alarms about how easy it was to start a nuclear attack, and about the lack of safeguards.

name: Rene Carpenter
headline: Rene Carpenter, Astronaut’s Wife Who Broke NASA Mold, Dies at 92
abstract: The last living member of the Mercury 7 couples who helped define America’s early space program, she went on to become a writer and television host.

name: Richard Gelles
headline: Richard Gelles, Scholar of Family Violence, Is Dead at 73
abstract: He believed in reuniting families even if parents had abused their children — until he saw how often that approach threatened children’s safety.

name: Milos Jakes
headline: Milos Jakes, Czech Communist Leader, Is Dead at 97
abstract: In 1987 he was made general secretary of the country’s Communist Party. Two years later he was swept aside by reform.

name: David Sackoff
headline: David Sackoff, 71, ‘Survivor’ Who Battled Mental Illness, Dies
abstract: He lived on the streets, in prison and in psychiatric facilities, but in the end achieved independence. He died of complications of the novel coronavirus.

name: Regis Philbin
headline: Regis Philbin, TV’s Enduring Everyman, Dies at 88
abstract: With patience, determination and folksy, spontaneous wit, Mr. Philbin climbed to pre-eminence relatively late in life on talk and game shows.

name: Olivia de Havilland
profession: Star of Gone With the Wind
headline: Olivia de Havilland, a Star of ‘Gone With the Wind,’ Dies at 104
abstract: She built an illustrious Hollywood career punctuated by a successful fight to loosen the studios’ grip on actors.

name: Peter Green
headline: Peter Green, Fleetwood Mac’s Founder, Is Dead at 73
abstract: One of England’s finest blues guitarists, he wrote most of the group’s early songs. But he left the group after taking LSD, saying he wanted to change his life.

name: Mason Gaffney
headline: Mason Gaffney, Who Argued for Taxing Only Land, Dies at 96
abstract: He was at the forefront of a tax-policy movement based on the ideas of Henry George, which helped spark the Progressive movement in the 19th century.

name: Kansai Yamamoto
profession: Designer With Ziggy Stardust as a Client
