headline: Kansai Yamamoto, Designer With Ziggy Stardust as a Client, Dies at 76
abstract: Unapologetically flamboyant, he shaped the look of David Bowie’s alter ego and also worked with Elton John and Stevie Wonder.

name: Darius Settles
headline: Darius Settles, Custom Suit-Designer to Ministers, Dies at 30
abstract: A son and grandson of Pentecostal ministers, he was at the time the youngest person in Nashville to die of the coronavirus.

name: Eddie Shack
profession: Feisty Wing for Powerful Maple Leafs
headline: Eddie Shack, Feisty Wing for Powerful Maple Leafs, Dies at 83
abstract: He helped Toronto win four Stanley Cups in the ’60s, his pugnacity earning love in Toronto (and, no surprise, hatred in rival Montreal).

name: Willie Doria
profession: Spanish American Baseball Star in Texas
headline: Willie Doria, Spanish American Baseball Star in Texas, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Doria was also a World War II and Air Force veteran, and an usher for the San Antonio Missions and Spurs. He died of Covid-19.

name: Reese Schonfeld
profession: Founder of CNN and Food Network
headline: Reese Schonfeld, a Founder of CNN and Food Network, Dies at 88
abstract: He joined Ted Turner to create the Cable News Network and oversaw its growth before being fired. Afterward he was critical of how CNN had changed.

name: John Saxon
headline: John Saxon, a Star of ‘Enter the Dragon,’ Is Dead at 83
abstract: A son of Brooklyn whose “smoldering” good looks got him to Hollywood, where he once starred with Marlon Brando and, by Mr. Saxon’s lights, outacted him.

name: Niels Lauersen
profession: Fallen Fertility Doctor to the Stars
headline: Niels Lauersen, Fallen Fertility Doctor to the Stars, Dies at 84
abstract: He treated celebrities like Celine Dion and Foxy Brown before he was undone by malpractice suits and a prison sentence for insurance fraud.

name: Bent Fabric
profession: Pianist and Composer Known for Alley Cat
headline: Bent Fabric, Pianist and Composer Known for ‘Alley Cat,’ Dies at 95
abstract: A simple tune with an old-time feel, it could embed itself in the listener’s ear as if on a continuous loop. In 1962, it became a worldwide hit.

name: Katherine Hoffman
headline: Katherine Hoffman, ‘Eternal’ Florida State Figure, Dies at 105
abstract: From the 1930s to the 2010s, as a student, professor and distinguished alumna, she was a model citizen in support of the school. She died of Covid-19.

name: Joseph Kernan
headline: Joseph Kernan, Vietnam P.O.W. and Indiana Governor, Dies at 74
abstract: He spent 11 months in a North Vietnamese prison after his plane was downed. He was later a long-serving mayor of South Bend.

name: Renada McGuire
headline: Renada McGuire, Resilient Home Health Aide, Dies at 39
abstract: She decided to work with adults with mental disabilities after giving birth to a child with challenges. She died of complications of the novel coronavirus.

name: Lou Henson
profession: Final Four Coach With Two Schools
headline: Lou Henson, Final Four Coach With Two Schools, Dies at 88
abstract: A genial “old school” leader, he took New Mexico State and then Illinois deep into the N.C.A.A. tournament. In a 42-year career, he won close to 800 games.

name: Lee Teng-hui
headline: Lee Teng-hui, 97, Who Led Taiwan’s Turn to Democracy, Dies
abstract: Its first popularly elected president, he transformed a police state into a vibrant country while angering Beijing by insisting that Taiwan be treated as a sovereign state.

name: Herman Cain
headline: Herman Cain, Former C.E.O. and Presidential Candidate, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Cain sought the 2012 Republican nomination and became an early supporter of Donald Trump’s 2016 bid. He had been hospitalized with the coronavirus.

name: Hugh Freyer
profession: Poker Player With Discretion of a Banker
headline: Hugh Freyer, Poker Player With Discretion of a Banker, Dies at 86
abstract: A son of immigrants, he became a private banker in New York and was also devoted to helping recovering alcoholics. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Waldemar Gonzalez
headline: Waldemar Gonzalez, Social Worker Who Drew on His Own Hard Life, Dies at 72
abstract: He grew up with an abusive father and carried that pain into adulthood before becoming ‘Dad 2.0.’ He died of the coronavirus.

name: Martha Nierenberg
headline: Martha Nierenberg, Entrepreneur Who Sought Art’s Return, Dies at 96
abstract: A co-founder of Dansk Designs, she fought to recover family masterpieces stolen by the Nazis when they invaded Hungary. The case, mired in a U.S. court, goes on.

name: Ben Jipcho
headline: Ben Jipcho, a Runner Who Sacrificed Himself for a Teammate, Dies at 77
abstract: At the 1968 Summer Olympics, he set a blistering early pace in the 1,500-meter race to help his teammate beat the American Jim Ryun. Jipcho finished 10th.

name: Malik B.
headline: Malik B., Longtime Member of the Roots, Is Dead at 47
abstract: He brought his understatedly gritty lyrics and cadence to the band during its formative years. After he went solo, he dropped in on a few Roots albums.

name: Dobby Dobson
headline: Dobby Dobson, Versatile Jamaican Singer and Songwriter, Dies at 78
abstract: Best known for his hit “I’m a Loving Pauper,” he was a significant figure in the evolution of Jamaican music. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Alan Parker
headline: Alan Parker, Versatile Film Director, Is Dead at 76
abstract: “Midnight Express” and “Mississippi Burning” brought him Oscar nominations, and many of his other films, including “Fame,” were acclaimed.

name: Roland Johnson
profession: Fought to Shut Down Institutions for the Disabled
headline: Overlooked No More: Roland Johnson, Who Fought to Shut Down Institutions for the Disabled
abstract: He survived 13 years of neglect and abuse, including sexual assault, at the notorious Pennhurst State School and Hospital outside Philadelphia before emerging as a champion for the disabled.

name: William English
headline: William English, Who Helped Build the Computer Mouse, Dies at 91
abstract: He was one of the computing pioneers who “showed what a computer interface could — and should — look like,” a colleague said.

name: Robert Gnaizda
headline: Robert Gnaizda, Lawyer Who Fought for Social Justice, Dies at 83
abstract: He challenged redlining banks, employers who discriminated in hiring and, early in his career, Southern counties that thwarted Black voters.

name: Eddie Negrón
headline: Dr. Eddie Negrón, a Physician Full of Fun, Is Dead at 69
abstract: Friends remember his jokes and his dancing as well as his medical care. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: James Silberman
headline: James Silberman, Editor Who Nurtured Literary Careers, Dies at 93
abstract: At Random House and elsewhere, including his own Summit imprint, he worked with James Baldwin, Marilyn French, Hunter S. Thompson and many others.

name: Connie Culp
profession: First Face Transplant Recipient in U.S
headline: Connie Culp, First Face Transplant Recipient in U.S., Dies at 57
abstract: Her near-total transplant in 2008 was at the time the most complex one ever performed. She was the fourth patient in the world to undergo such a procedure.

name: Víctor Víctor
profession: Known for the Hit Mesita de Noche
headline: Víctor Víctor, Known for the Hit ‘Mesita de Noche,’ Dies at 71
abstract: A singer, songwriter and producer, Mr. Víctor also worked to bring theater, music and dance lessons to underprivileged communities. He died of Covid-19.

name: Red Couture
profession: Mother Hen of a Drag Scene
headline: Lady Red Couture, ‘Mother Hen’ of a Drag Scene, Dies at 43
abstract: A fixture in Los Angeles clubs who stood 7-foot-2 in heels, she also co-hosted the L.G.B.T.Q. talk show “Hey Qween!”

name: Wilford Brimley
profession: Cocoon Star and Quaker Oats Pitchman
headline: Wilford Brimley, ‘Cocoon’ Star and Quaker Oats Pitchman, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Recognizable by his walrus mustache, the actor specialized in playing cantankerous characters in “Absence of Malice,” “The Natural” and other films.

name: Leon Fleisher
profession: Spellbinding Pianist Using One Hand or Two
headline: Leon Fleisher, 92, Dies; Spellbinding Pianist Using One Hand or Two
abstract: Unable to use his right hand, he performed pieces written for left hand only, conducted and taught. Years later, he made a triumphant two-handed comeback.

name: John Hume
profession: Nobel Laureate for Work in Northern Ireland
headline: John Hume, Nobel Laureate for Work in Northern Ireland, Dies at 83
abstract: The politician’s campaign for peace was seen as a driving force behind an end to 25 years of sectarian conflict in the territory.

name: John Eric Swing
headline: John Eric Swing, a Filipino-American Community Builder, Dies at 48.
abstract: Mr. Swing was a catalyst in the Historic Filipinotown neighborhood of Los Angeles, a new center of food start-ups. He died of complications of the coronavirus.

name: Bernaldina José Pedro
headline: Bernaldina José Pedro, Repository of Indigenous Culture, Dies at 75
abstract: Ms. Pedro was a leader of Brazil’s Macuxi people and carried a message of alarm for their fate to Pope Francis. She died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Adam Max
headline: Adam Max, Patron of Brooklyn Cultural Institutions, Dies at 62
abstract: He was chairman of the Brooklyn Academy of Music and a benefactor of St. Ann’s Warehouse. He and his wife also helped create a center for women’s history.

name: Helen Jones Woods
profession: Member of an All-Female Jazz Group
headline: Helen Jones Woods, Member of an All-Female Jazz Group, Dies at 96
abstract: She played trombone in the multiracial International Sweethearts of Rhythm, but later put down her horn forever. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Pete Hamill
headline: Pete Hamill, Quintessential New York Journalist, Dies at 85
abstract: He was a celebrated reporter and columnist, the top editor of The New York Post and The Daily News, and the author of numerous books.

name: Eric Bentley
headline: Eric Bentley, Critic Who Preferred Brecht to Broadway, Dies at 103
abstract: Mr. Bentley, who was also a playwright, was an early champion of modern European drama in the 1940s but had little use for American plays.

name: James Powers
headline: James Powers, Brooklyn Gallerist Who Nurtured Black Artists, Dies at 80
abstract: Openings at Mr. Powers’s Spiral Gallery on Vanderbilt Avenue were rollicking festivals of art and jazz featuring emerging artists from the neighborhood and beyond.

name: Kathleen Duey
headline: Kathleen Duey, a Mentoring Children’s Book Author, Dies at 69
abstract: A prolific writer, she published more than 75 books, including a Best Seller and a National Book Award finalist, all while encouraging aspiring authors.

name: Doris Buffett
headline: Doris Buffett, Her Family’s ‘Retail Philanthropist,’ Dies at 92
abstract: Her younger brother, Warren, entrusted her with vetting requests after he announced his intention to donate nearly his entire fortune. “Warren loves to make money and I love to give it away,” she said.

name: Hawa Abdi
headline: Hawa Abdi, Doctor Who Aided Thousands in Somalia, Dies at 73
abstract: Dr. Abdi turned her family’s land into a hospital and camp that treated and supported legions of people displaced during a civil war.

name: Diana Russell
headline: Diana Russell, Who Studied Violence Against Women, Dies at 81
abstract: She popularized the term “femicide,” to highlight the killing of women “because they are women” and to distinguish these killings from other homicides.

name: Enrico Navarra
headline: Enrico Navarra, Art World Visionary, Is Dead at 67
abstract: As a gallerist and publisher, he championed artists who weren’t yet fully appreciated, notably Jean-Michel Basquiat.

name: Horace Clarke
profession: Standout in a Dismal Yankee Era
headline: Horace Clarke, Standout in a Dismal Yankee Era, Dies at 82
abstract: He was a solid, dependable player, but he had the misfortune of joining the Yankees just as they tumbled from greatness.

name: Brent Scowcroft
profession: Force on Foreign Policy for 40 Years
headline: Brent Scowcroft, a Force on Foreign Policy for 40 Years, Dies at 95
abstract: He was a national security adviser to President Ford and the first President Bush and an influential voice in Washington for decades.

name: Lorenzo Wilson Milam
headline: Lorenzo Wilson Milam, Guru of Community Radio, Is Dead at 86
abstract: He helped start noncommercial stations in the 1960s and ’70s, offering an eclectic mix of music and talk. His goal: to change the world.

name: Barbara Costikyan
headline: Barbara Costikyan, New York Magazine Food Columnist, Dies at 91
abstract: Ms. Costikyan, who died of the coronavirus, once wrote that she couldn’t think about food “without thinking about the people who do it.”

name: Sharon Williams
headline: Sharon Williams, a Nurturer on the Police Force, Dies at 54
abstract: When Ms. Williams came across troubled young women while on the job in New Orleans, she saw them as potential “angels.” She died of Covid-19.

name: Jovita Idár
profession: Promoted Rights of Mexican-Americans and Women
headline: Overlooked No More: Jovita Idár, Who Promoted Rights of Mexican-Americans and Women
abstract: As a teacher, writer, editor and activist, Idár preserved Mexican culture in South Texas and encouraged women to pursue an education and push for equal rights.

name: Brent Carver
headline: Brent Carver, Versatile Tony-Winning Actor, Dies at 68
abstract: He played Hamlet, the wizard Gandalf and Tevye in “Fiddler on the Roof.” But he was probably best known for “Kiss of the Spider Woman.”

name: Bernard Bailyn
headline: Bernard Bailyn, Eminent Historian of Early America, Dies at 97
abstract: On topic after topic he shifted the direction of scholarly inquiry, winning two Pulitzers and a Bancroft Prize for his innovative research and groundbreaking works.

name: Frances Allen
headline: Frances Allen, Who Helped Hardware Understand Software, Dies at 88
abstract: One of the few women in the computer industry in its early days, she paved the way for the efficient, lightning-fast apps of today.

name: Richard Lapointe
headline: Richard Lapointe, Exonerated in a Murder Case, Dies at 74
abstract: Advocates worked for decades to free him in the murder of his wife’s grandmother in Connecticut; in 2015 a court finally agreed.

name: Robbie Waters
headline: Robbie Waters, an Old-School Cop and Legislator, Dies at 84
abstract: A Sacramento fixture, Mr. Waters drove a 1932 Ford and crossed paths with Patty Hearst and Squeaky Fromme. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Shirley Ann Grau
headline: Shirley Ann Grau, Writer Whose Focus Was the South, Dies at 91
abstract: In books like her novel “The Keepers of The House,” which won a Pulitzer Prize, Ms. Grau wrote unsparingly about race relations.

name: Terry Cannon
profession: Creator of an Alternative to Cooperstown
headline: Terry Cannon, Creator of an Alternative to Cooperstown, Dies at 66
abstract: His Baseball Reliquary collects quirky artifacts and honors people who wouldn’t ordinarily be elected to the august Baseball Hall of Fame.

name: Gloria DeNard
headline: Gloria DeNard, Who Educated Through Jazz, Is Dead at 93
abstract: She founded the East Harlem music school Manna House Workshops because, she said, “I wanted the people in the community to have a better feeling of self-worth.”

name: Adin Steinsaltz
headline: Adin Steinsaltz, 83, Dies; Created Epic Translation of Talmud
abstract: A rabbi and scholar, he wrote more than 60 books, but his crowning achievement (he called it his hobby) was his 45-year, 45-volume translation of a key Jewish text.

name: Steven dePyssler
headline: Col. Steven dePyssler, Who Aided Veterans’ Families, Dies at 101
abstract: He acquired everything from toilet paper to plane parts for Air Force squadrons. Later, he advised widows on veterans’ benefits. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Fay Chew Matsuda
headline: Fay Chew Matsuda, Steward of Chinese Immigrant Legacy, Dies at 71
abstract: A social worker turned preservationist, she directed the Museum of Chinese in America. “Sometimes it was literally dumpster-diving,” she said of rescuing artifacts.

name: Wayne Fontana
profession: Hitmaker With The Game of Love
headline: Wayne Fontana, Hitmaker With ‘The Game of Love,’ Dies at 74
abstract: The song brought him and his British Invasion band, the Mindbenders, a bit of success in the mid-1960s. Then he went solo, and the hits did not keep coming.

name: Trini Lopez
headline: Trini Lopez, Singing Star Who Mixed Musical Styles, Dies at 83
abstract: His blend of American folk, Latin and rockabilly music captivated listeners worldwide. His secret: arrangements that people could dance to. He died of Covid-19.

name: Bill Mack
profession: D.J. Beloved by Truckers and Country Fans
headline: Bill Mack, D.J. Beloved by Truckers and Country Fans, Dies at 91
abstract: With a signal that reached half the country, the “midnight cowboy” was one of radio’s first national personalities. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Matt Herron
headline: Matt Herron, Whose Camera Chronicled a Movement, Dies at 89
abstract: As a magazine photojournalist, he immersed himself in the South as a witness to civil rights marches and clashes. He was killed when the glider he was piloting crashed.

name: Sumner Redstone
profession: Built Media Empire and Long Reigned Over It
headline: Sumner Redstone Dies at 97; Built Media Empire and Long Reigned Over It
abstract: Starting with a chain of drive-in movie theaters, Mr. Redstone negotiated, sued and otherwise fought to amass a domain that included CBS and Viacom.

name: Carroll Hardy
headline: Carroll Hardy, Athlete With a Unique Distinction, Dies at 87
abstract: He was a college star in three sports and a successful N.F.L. executive. But he was better known as the only player who ever pinch-hit for Ted Williams.

name: Robert Ryland
headline: Robert Ryland, Who Broke a Tennis Barrier, Dies at 100
abstract: The first professional Black player, he also taught future tennis stars, as well as a few stars of show business.

name: Carol Brock
headline: Carol Brock, Who Pushed at a ‘Pyrex Ceiling,’ Dies at 96
abstract: A veteran food writer, she founded Les Dames d’Escoffier, a society for women in the male-dominated culinary world.

name: James Harris
headline: James Harris, Towering Wrestler Known as Kamala, Dies at 70
abstract: He became a top draw portraying a stereotypical menacing African warrior who was always supposed to lose to his white opponents. He died of Covid-19.

name: Kurt Luedtke
headline: Kurt Luedtke, Newspaperman Turned Screenwriter, Dies at 80
abstract: He led The Detroit Free Press at 33, then gave up journalism for Hollywood. “Absence of Malice” was one result; an Oscar for “Out of Africa” was another.

name: David Galante
headline: David Galante, Who Spoke Belatedly About Auschwitz, Dies at 96
abstract: It took him decades before he felt comfortable sharing the horrors he witnessed during the Holocaust. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Le Kha Phieu
headline: Le Kha Phieu, Vietnam Leader Who Was Pushed Out, Dies at 88
abstract: He served for less than four years as the country’s general secretary, losing his post after unusually public factional struggles.

name: Konrad Steffen
headline: Konrad Steffen, Who Sounded Alarm on Greenland Ice, Dies at 68
abstract: A renowned researcher on rising sea levels, he died after falling into the kind of crevasse that warming has created. “It looks like climate change actually claimed him as a victim,” a colleague said.

name: Luchita Hurtado
headline: Luchita Hurtado, Artist Who Became a Sensation in Her 90s, Dies at 99
abstract: For years she worked in the shadow of her artist husbands and more famous peers, painting at night when the children were asleep. Then a trove of her work was discovered.

name: Julian Bream
headline: Julian Bream, Maestro of Guitar and Lute, Dies at 87
abstract: It could be argued that he, even more than Andrés Segovia, established the guitar’s credibility as a serious solo instrument.

name: Eusebio Leal Spengler
headline: Eusebio Leal Spengler, Who Restored Old Havana, Dies at 77
abstract: His decades-long effort to preserve a capital’s colonial buildings turned a former slum into a tourist destination and capitalist success story.

name: Deborah Henson
headline: Deborah Henson, Church Member With Generous Spirit, Dies at 56
abstract: In Ocala, Fla., she counseled couples, donated clothing and aided women who suffered from domestic violence. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Billy Goldenberg
headline: Billy Goldenberg, TV, Movie and Stage Composer, Dies at 84
abstract: He worked with Steven Spielberg, Barbra Streisand and Elvis Presley, wrote the theme music to many familiar series and accompanied Nichols and May and Bea Arthur on Broadway.

name: Aritana Yawalapiti
headline: Aritana Yawalapiti, Revered Indigenous Leader in Brazil, Dies at 71
abstract: Known for his quiet dignity, he dedicated himself to protecting the environment and promoting the health of his people. He died of the coronavirus.

name: James R. Thompson
headline: James R. Thompson, Longest-Serving Governor of Illinois, Dies at 84
abstract: A relentless campaigner, he served for 14 years after winning an election to a special two-year term in 1976.

name: Robert S. Trump
headline: Robert S. Trump, the President’s Younger Brother, Dies at 71
abstract: A loyal spokesman for the family, he shunned the spotlight and had “zero sense of entitlement.”

name: Jay Galst
headline: Dr. Jay Galst, a Specialist in Eyes and Coins, Dies at 69
abstract: An ophthalmologist with a numismatic hobby, he combined those interests in an unusual book. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Charles Wetli
profession: Medical Examiner for T.W.A. Flight 800 Crash
headline: Charles Wetli, Medical Examiner for T.W.A. Flight 800 Crash, Dies at 76
abstract: Families blamed him for not identifying the victims fast enough, but in the end, he “put a name on every bit of human remains recovered.”

name: Claire Shulman
headline: Claire Shulman, First Woman to Lead Queens, Dies at 94
abstract: She became borough president in the wake of a corruption scandal in 1986, then won elections that kept her in office as an advocate for Queens for 16 years.

name: Marvin Creamer
headline: Marvin Creamer, a Mariner Who Sailed Like the Ancients, Dies at 104
abstract: No GPS for him, not even a sextant; the sun and the stars did nicely. He was the first recorded person to sail round the world without navigational instruments.

name: Barbara Caplan
headline: Barbara Caplan, Spotter of Consumer Trends, Dies at 93
abstract: After raising a family, she got a master’s degree in psychology and became an expert in what people would crave and buy. She tested positive for Covid-19.

name: Sixto Brillantes Jr.
headline: Sixto Brillantes Jr., Elections Lawyer in the Philippines, Dies at 80
abstract: He was a veteran insider who was praised as a reformer of the electoral system. He died of the coronavirus in a country besieged by it.

name: Gisèle Halimi
headline: Gisèle Halimi, Influential French Lawyer and Feminist, Dies at 93
abstract: Her cases were often precedent-setting and helped shift French laws and attitudes about abortion and women’s rights.

name: Amer Fakhoury
profession: Released From Jail in Lebanon After U.S. Pressure
headline: Amer Fakhoury, 57, Dies; Released From Jail in Lebanon After U.S. Pressure
abstract: Mr. Fakhoury, an American citizen, had been detained on charges related to the torture of Lebanese prisoners decades ago.

name: Peter V. Tytell
headline: Peter V. Tytell, a Typewriter Whisperer, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Raised in his parents’ repair shop, he was renowned for resolving disputes over the authenticity of documents, including one that put George W. Bush in a bad light.

name: Ben Cross
headline: Ben Cross, Star of ‘Chariots of Fire,’ Dies at 72
abstract: A long acting career bridged generations. He was a British Olympic runner in a 1981 Oscar-winning film and Spock’s father in a 2009 “Star Trek” reboot.

name: Slade Gorton
profession: Was Voted Out of Senate and Then Back In
headline: Slade Gorton, Who Was Voted Out of Senate and Then Back In, Dies at 92
abstract: A “passionate moderate” Republican from Washington State, he served three nonconsecutive terms as a friend to its industries, from logging to tech.

name: Mary Hartline
profession: TV Star When TV Was New
headline: Mary Hartline, a TV Star When TV Was New, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Often called television’s first sex symbol, she was a striking presence on “Super Circus” from 1949 to 1955 — and a master of promotion.

name: Stephen F. Williams
headline: Stephen F. Williams, U.S. Appeals Court Judge, Dies at 83
abstract: A Reagan appointee, he served on the District of Columbia bench for three decades. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Kenneth Bernard
headline: Kenneth Bernard, Convention-Shattering Playwright, Dies at 90
abstract: His experimental works, staged by the Playhouse of the Ridiculous and other groups, challenged audiences and sometimes baffled them.

name: Norman Carlson
headline: Norman Carlson, Forceful Head of U.S. Prisons, Dies at 86
abstract: He created the model for today’s super-maximum security prisons and oversaw a near doubling of federal facilities. He also insisted on cleanliness and decent food.

name: Beth Salamensky
headline: Beth Salamensky, Lawyer Who Found an L.G.B.T.Q. Community, Dies at 43
abstract: She moved from the Chicago area to Los Angeles, where she joined a lesbian and gay synagogue. But after falling destitute, she withdrew and died of the coronavirus.

name: Ann Syrdal
profession: Helped Give Computers a Female Voice
headline: Ann Syrdal, Who Helped Give Computers a Female Voice, Dies at 74
abstract: As a researcher at AT&T, she helped lay the groundwork for modern digital assistants like Siri and Alexa.

name: Christine Jahnke
profession: Speech Coach for Women in Politics
headline: Christine Jahnke, Speech Coach for Women in Politics, Dies at 57
abstract: A backstage fixture at Democratic conventions, she helped speakers work with the teleprompter, read the audience and sharpen their message.

name: Chi Chi DeVayne
headline: Chi Chi DeVayne, Popular ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race’ Contestant, Dies at 34
abstract: She made her name as a classically trained dancer who delighted audiences and charmed them with candor.

name: Ray Cave
headline: Ray Cave, Influential Time Magazine Editor, Is Dead at 91
abstract: After bringing big changes to Sports Illustrated in the 1960s and ’70s, Mr. Cave had an equally significant impact at Time.

name: Steve Grossman
profession: Hired as a Teenager by Miles Davis
headline: Steve Grossman, Hired as a Teenager by Miles Davis, Dies at 69
abstract: He was just 18 when Davis recruited him to play saxophone in his band. He went on to play with Elvin Jones and to lead his own groups.

name: Margaret and Jimmy Shaw
headline: Margaret and Jimmy Shaw, Married for 62 Years, Die Apart at 79 and 80
abstract: The couple, who eloped at 17, came from humble roots and were mainstays in their Miami church. They died of the coronavirus in separate hospital rooms.

name: Leonora O’Reilly
headline: Overlooked No More: Leonora O’Reilly, Suffragist Who Fought for Working Women
abstract: She was a charismatic and powerful public speaker who pushed for equal pay for equal work, better labor standards and overall empowerment for women.

name: Deidre Davis Butler
headline: Deidre Davis Butler, Who Fought for Disability Rights, Dies at 64
abstract: A wheelchair user herself, she helped draft a landmark law and held government posts championing people with disabilities, especially those of color.

name: Nina Popova
headline: Nina Popova, Dancer Who Fled Bolsheviks and Nazis, Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Popova, who grew up in Russia, toured the globe, danced on Broadway and became a teacher. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Elaine Roulet
profession: Aided Imprisoned Mothers and Their Children
headline: Sister Elaine Roulet, 89, Dies; Aided Imprisoned Mothers and Their Children
abstract: Changes Sister Elaine helped bring about at the Bedford Hills prison for women in New York State allowed inmates and their offspring to bond.

name: Geoffrey Nunberg
headline: Geoffrey Nunberg, Expert on How Language Works, Dies at 75
abstract: A widely respected linguist, he found popularity beyond academia with appearances on NPR and books like the intriguingly titled “Going Nucular.”

name: Alyce Gullattee
headline: Dr. Alyce Gullattee, Expert on Substance Abuse, Dies at 91
abstract: Dr. Gullattee, who died of the coronavirus, taught at Howard University and served on White House committees for Presidents Nixon, Ford and Carter.

name: Mercedes Barcha
profession: Gabriel García Márquezs Wife and Muse
headline: Mercedes Barcha, Gabriel García Márquez’s Wife and Muse, Dies at 87
abstract: For nearly 60 years, she was the Nobel Prize-winning novelist’s companion and inspiration, his sharp-witted foil and his chief of staff.

name: Dan Budnik
headline: Dan Budnik, Who Photographed History, Is Dead at 87
abstract: His assignments for leading magazines took him to pivotal events of the civil rights era. He was also known for his photographs of artists.

name: Justin Townes Earle
headline: Justin Townes Earle, Singer-Songwriter in Father’s Footsteps, Dies at 38
abstract: He released eight alt-country albums as a solo artist, seeking to emerge from the long shadow of the outlaw country star Steve Earle.

name: Frank Cullotta
headline: Frank Cullotta, Mobster Turned Memoirist and YouTuber, Dies at 81
abstract: He testified in organized-crime cases, wrote memoirs, gave tours and spoke about his life on his YouTube channel, “Coffee with Cullotta.” He died of Covid-19.

name: Gail Sheehy
headline: Gail Sheehy, Journalist, Author and Social Observer, Dies at 83
abstract: She looked at what makes public figures tick and, in her “Passages” books, how adults navigate life’s inevitable changes.

name: Joe Segal
profession: Impresario of Live Jazz for 70 Years
headline: Joe Segal, Impresario of Live Jazz for 70 Years, Dies at 94
abstract: His Jazz Showcase was a staple in Chicago since 1947, presenting a who’s who of artists, from Charlie Parker to Dee Dee Bridgewater. To the N.E.A., he was a Jazz Master.

name: Pandit Jasraj
headline: Pandit Jasraj, Master Indian Vocalist, Is Dead at 90
abstract: Known for his soulful voice and multi-octave range, he was one of the most famous performers in Hindustani classical music.

name: Alfredo Breitfeld
headline: Alfredo Breitfeld, Antiquarian Bookseller in Buenos Aires, Dies at 82
abstract: He was determined to attend this year’s antiquarian book fair in New York City. He sickened as he flew home and died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Istvan Rabovsky
headline: Istvan Rabovsky, Ballet Dancer Who Defected From Hungary, Dies at 90
abstract: A powerful dancer, he and his first wife, the ballerina Nora Kovach, were among the first highly-publicized defectors from the Soviet Bloc.

name: Hee Sook Lee
headline: Hee Sook Lee, Founder of BCD Tofu House, Dies at 61
abstract: She spent long nights developing her secret recipe for Korean tofu soup, a dish that became a phenomenon while her restaurant grew into a chain.

name: Bernard Fils-Aimé
headline: Bernard Fils-Aimé, Haitian Activist and Cellphone Mogul, Dies at 67
abstract: He ran Haiti’s first cellular network, which he saw as a way of raising the voices of ordinary citizens, in Haiti and the United States. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Angela Buxton
profession: Half of an Outcast Duo in Tennis History
headline: Angela Buxton, Half of an Outcast Duo in Tennis History, Dies at 85
abstract: She was Jewish, and the great Althea Gibson was Black, and in the segregated world of 1950s tennis they forged a remarkable friendship as champion doubles partners.

name: Anthony Martignetti
headline: Anthony Martignetti (‘Anthony!’), Who Raced Home for Spaghetti, Dies at 63
abstract: He was a 12-year-old Italian immigrant when a classic TV commercial for Prince, the Boston pasta company, gave him a lasting identity.

name: Bill Arnett
profession: Collector and Promoter of Little-Known Black Art
headline: Bill Arnett, Collector and Promoter of Little-Known Black Art, Dies at 81
abstract: In the 1980s and ’90s, he traveled Southern byways to find brilliant works by self-taught African-American artists who often used scavenged materials.

name: Walter Lure
profession: Guitarist for a Mythical Punk Band
headline: Walter Lure, Guitarist for a ‘Mythical’ Punk Band, Dies at 71
abstract: With the Heartbreakers, a shooting star in New York’s punk rock scene, he was a more proficient guitarist than many of his peers. Then came a very unpunk second act.

name: Douglas A.J. Latchford
headline: Douglas A.J. Latchford, Khmer Antiquities Expert, Dies at 88
abstract: A leading collector of Cambodian relics, he was credited with helping preserve Khmer culture. He was also charged with trafficking in looted treasures.

name: Charles Cook
headline: Charles Cook, Ground Zero Volunteer for Months, Dies at 79
abstract: After the planes hit on 9/11, he walked from his home in Harlem, against the tide of people fleeing, to help. After Hurricane Katrina, he lent a hand in New Orleans.

name: Gerald D. Hines
headline: Gerald D. Hines, Developer and Architects’ ‘Medici,’ Is Dead at 95
abstract: He transformed skylines around the world by recruiting blue-chip architects and holding to the credo that good design is good business.

name: Archbishop Oscar Cruz
profession: Philippine Critic of Graft and Gambling
headline: Archbishop Oscar Cruz, Philippine Critic of Graft and Gambling, Dies at 85
abstract: He made it his main mission to rid the Philippines of illegal gambling, drawing the ire of officials. He died of complications of the new coronavirus.

name: Linda Manz
profession: Young Star of Days of Heaven
headline: Linda Manz, Young Star of ‘Days of Heaven,’ Dies at 58
abstract: She was in her teens when she appeared in and narrated Terrence Malick’s 1978 masterpiece. Then came Dennis Hopper’s ‘Out of the Blue.’ And then she disappeared.

name: Ian McRae
profession: Brought Electricity to Black South Africa
headline: Ian McRae, Who Brought Electricity to Black South Africa, Dies at 90
abstract: As head of the state-owned utility, he defied apartheid laws by laying the groundwork for providing power to the nonwhite townships and by hiring Black people. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Dirk Mudge
profession: Played a Key Role in Namibian Independence
headline: Dirk Mudge, Who Played a Key Role in Namibian Independence, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Mudge was a pro-apartheid politician who later turned toward helping lay the foundations of multiracial democracy. He died of Covid-19 complications.

name: Alice Koller
headline: Alice Koller, Author of the Solitary Life, Dies at 94
abstract: Her book, “An Unknown Woman,” has been compared to a feminist’s Walden and has attracted fans inspired by her self-reckoning.

name: Larry Pardey
headline: Larry Pardey, Mariner Who Sailed the World Engineless, Dies at 80
abstract: With his wife, Lin, he circumnavigated the world twice on wooden boats he had built. And they always took their time.

name: Lute Olson
profession: Put Arizona on College Basketball Map
headline: Lute Olson, Who Put Arizona on College Basketball Map, Dies at 85
abstract: He led the Wildcats to 23 consecutive appearances in the N.C.A.A. tournament, winning the championship in 1997. Earlier, he took Iowa to the Final Four.

name: Chadwick Boseman
headline: ‘Black Panther’ Star Chadwick Boseman Dies of Cancer at 43
abstract: The actor also played groundbreaking figures like James Brown, Jackie Robinson and Thurgood Marshall, becoming one of his generation’s most sought-after leading men.

name: Jeanette Carlson
headline: Jeanette Carlson, Fighter Against Apartheid, Dies at 91
abstract: She was deported from South Africa in 1971 for her activity and vowed never to return. “It was disgusting to live in that kind of environment,” she said.

name: Jürgen Schadeberg
headline: Jürgen Schadeberg, Whose Photos Chronicled Apartheid, Dies at 89
abstract: He gained rare entree into segregated Black communities and took pictures that bookended the career of Nelson Mandela.

name: Nyameka Goniwe
profession: Sought Justice in Her Husbands Killing
headline: Nyameka Goniwe, 69, Dies; Sought Justice in Her Husband’s Killing
abstract: Her family became a target of South Africa’s security police, facing “constant surveillance, death threats, phone bugging,” but she fought on.

name: Cliff Robinson
headline: Cliff Robinson, UConn Star Who Played 18 N.B.A. Seasons, Dies at 53
abstract: He took the Huskies to the N.I.T. championship, and was the Sixth Man of the Year for the Trail Blazers. In 2017, he opened a marijuana dispensary.

name: Pranab Mukherjee
headline: Pranab Mukherjee, Indispensable Man of Indian Politics, Dies at 84
abstract: A journalist turned politician, he was India’s president from 2012 to 2017 and wore many hats during a career that spanned political generations.

name: Joe Ruby
headline: Joe Ruby, a Creator of ‘Scooby-Doo,’ Is Dead at 87
abstract: Charged with creating an animated mystery series, Mr. Ruby and his writing partner, Ken Spears, came up with a show that endures more than 50 years later.

name: Aldir Blanc
headline: Aldir Blanc, Lyricist Who Pushed Samba’s Boundaries, Dies at 73
abstract: His songs included “O Bêbado e a Equilibrista,” a popular call for the amnesty of political exiles during Brazil’s military dictatorship. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Tootie Robbins
headline: Tootie Robbins, Lineman With Cardinals and Packers, Dies at 62
abstract: An offensive lineman for a dozen years, he was popular with his teammates and never forgot his roots. He died of pneumonia related to Covid-19.

name: Barbara Judge
headline: Barbara Judge, Who Shattered Many Glass Ceilings, Dies at 73
abstract: She championed the advancement of women in business, and, in a career studded with precedent-setting appointments, she set her own example.

name: George Wolf
headline: George Wolf, Caring Neighbor Who Glimpsed the Face of Evil, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Wolf escaped the Nazi occupation of Czechoslovakia and built a life as a garment manufacturer and lover of music in New York City. He was infected with the novel coronavirus.

name: Wolfgang Uhlmann
headline: Wolfgang Uhlmann, East Germany’s Top Chess Player, Dies at 85
abstract: Supported by the Communist regime, he won major tournament after major tournament during the Cold War years and beat stars like Bobby Fischer.

name: Duch
headline: Duch, Prison Chief Who Slaughtered for the Khmer Rouge, Dies at 77
abstract: Under his watch at Tuol Sleng prison, Duch, whose real name was Kaing Guek Eav, said, “I considered it evil eating evil.”

name: Howell Binkley
headline: Howell Binkley, Who Sculpted Broadway Hits in Light, Dies at 64
abstract: An in-demand lighting designer, he won Tony Awards for “Hamilton” and “Jersey Boys.”

name: Hans A. Linde
headline: Hans A. Linde, Iconoclastic Legal Scholar, Dies at 96
abstract: As a justice on the Oregon Supreme Court, he was a proponent of the new judicial federalism of the 1970s, which grounded civil rights protections in state constitutions.

name: Sophia Farrar
profession: Belied Indifference to Kitty Genovese Attack
headline: Sophia Farrar Dies at 92; Belied Indifference to Kitty Genovese Attack
abstract: For decades, the conventional narrative that defined urban anomie overlooked a good Samaritan who heeded a dying woman’s cries for help.

name: Betty J. McBride
headline: Betty J. McBride, Georgia Teacher and Counselor, Dies at 71
abstract: She taught music and special-education classes, but found that she could be even more helpful as a mentor beyond the classroom. She died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Tom Seaver
headline: Tom Seaver, Pitcher Who Led ‘Miracle Mets’ to Glory, Dies at 75
abstract: A Hall of Famer, Seaver won 311 games for four different teams. But Mets fans called him Tom Terrific for turning around the club’s fortunes.

name: Seymour Schwartz
headline: Dr. Seymour Schwartz, Who Wrote the Book on Surgery, Dies at 92
abstract: His name is synonymous with his field: He was a founding editor of “Schwartz’s Principles of Surgery,” a seminal textbook for medical students.

name: Siah Armajani
headline: Siah Armajani, Sculptor of Communal Spaces, Dies at 81
abstract: “I am interested in the nobility of usefulness,” Mr. Armajani said. He kept a low profile, but his public installations garnered wide influence.

name: Irving Kanarek
headline: Irving Kanarek, Lawyer Who Defended Charles Manson, Dies at 100
abstract: The national spotlight that focused on Mr. Kanarek made his disruptive circus of courtroom tactics almost as fascinating as his bizarre clients.

name: Salome Bey
headline: Salome Bey, Soulful Singer, Actress and Playwright, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Bey, known as “Canada’s first lady of the blues,” broke ground in her adopted country by creating opportunities for Black people in the theater.

name: Angela Russell
profession: She Grew Up With a Love of Song
headline: Angela Russell Dies at 65; She Grew Up With a Love of Song
abstract: Ms. Russell, a blind and intellectually disabled woman, lived for the past 25 years in an adult-care community. She died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Charlotta Bass
profession: First Black Woman to Run for Vice President
headline: Overlooked No More: Before Kamala Harris, There Was Charlotta Bass
abstract: She was the first Black woman to run for vice president, in 1952. She was also a pioneering journalist.

name: David Graeber
headline: David Graeber, Caustic Critic of Inequality, Is Dead at 59
abstract: He wrote about crushing debt, pointless jobs and the negative effects of globalization. And he played a leading role in the Occupy Wall Street movement.

name: Cathy Smith
profession: Injected John Belushi With Fatal Drugs
headline: Cathy Smith, Who Injected John Belushi With Fatal Drugs, Dies at 73
abstract: After giving an interview to The National Enquirer, she was convicted in Mr. Belushi’s overdose death and served time in prison.

name: Conny Nxumalo
headline: Conny Nxumalo, Advocate for South Africa’s Poor, Dies at 53
abstract: Years after helping to draft legislation that reversed apartheid-era social policies, her work exposed her to the coronavirus. She died of complications of the disease.

name: Julia Reed
headline: Julia Reed, Chronicler of Politics, Food and the South, Dies at 59
abstract: In Ms. Reed’s writing for Newsweek, Vogue and other publications, her canvas included the follies of the powerful and the pleasures of Southern food.

name: Eleanor Jacobs
profession: Force Behind the Earth Shoe Phenomenon
headline: Eleanor Jacobs, 91, Dies; a Force Behind the Earth Shoe Phenomenon
abstract: After discovering a pair in Copenhagen that eased her back pain, she and her husband rebranded the funny-looking shoe and sold millions in the U.S.

name: Joseph Bartscherer
headline: Joseph Bartscherer, Rigorously Conceptual Photographer, Dies at 65
abstract: His work — including a project for which he collected three decades of front-page obituaries from The New York Times — often took years to complete.

name: Gerald Shur
headline: Gerald Shur, Architect of Witness Protection Program, Dies at 86
abstract: As a young Justice Department lawyer investigating the mob, he realized that more witnesses might talk if they weren’t afraid of being killed.

name: Lou Brock
profession: Baseball Hall of Famer Known for Stealing Bases
headline: Lou Brock, Baseball Hall of Famer Known for Stealing Bases, Dies at 81
abstract: The son of sharecroppers, Brock attended a one-room schoolhouse, but was inspired by possibilities beyond the poverty and segregation of the rural South.

name: Constance Weldon
headline: Constance Weldon, Pioneering Virtuoso of the Tuba, Dies at 88
abstract: When she joined the Boston Pops in 1955, she was believed to be the first woman to play tuba in a major American orchestra.

name: Neelanshu Shukla
headline: Neelanshu Shukla, Indian Television Journalist, Dies at 30
abstract: A reporter who was passionate about politics, he covered his home state of Uttar Pradesh for the TV Today network. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Cecilia Romo
profession: Mexican Actress With a Broad Range
headline: Cecilia Romo, Mexican Actress With a Broad Range, Dies at 74
abstract: She played rebellious types, witches and nuns, and she had a gift for comedy. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Tom Jernstedt
headline: Tom Jernstedt, an Architect of March Madness, Dies at 75
abstract: A former backup college quarterback, he helped transform the N.C.A.A. men’s basketball tournament into one of the biggest events in sports.

name: Ron Gorchov
headline: Ron Gorchov, Painter Who Challenged Viewers’ Perceptions, Dies at 90
abstract: Seeking “a new kind of visual space” and using a vivid palette, he stacked multiple canvases with gently curved, round-cornered tops.

name: George Bizos
headline: George Bizos, Anti-Apartheid Lawyer Who Defended Mandela, Dies at 92
abstract: A champion of human rights, he represented his client and friend in the so-called Rivonia trial of leaders of the African National Congress in the 1960s.

name: Gary Peacock
headline: Gary Peacock, Master Jazz Bassist, Is Dead at 85
abstract: He was a free-jazz pioneer early on before becoming part of Keith Jarrett’s enduring trio, where he infused American standards with a Zen sensibility.

name: Forrest Fenn
headline: Forrest Fenn, Who Enticed Thousands With Treasure Hunt, Dies at 90
abstract: An art dealer, he announced in a 2010 book that he had hidden a chest of gold nuggets and jewels somewhere in the Rocky Mountains. People headed for them.

name: Diana Rigg
profession: Stylish Emma Peel of The Avengers
headline: Diana Rigg, Stylish Emma Peel of ‘The Avengers,’ Dies at 82
abstract: Ms. Rigg also played many classic roles onstage in both New York and London and, late in her career, found new fans on “Game of Thrones.”

name: Marcia Sasser
headline: Marcia Sasser, Who Smiled Through Chronic Pain, Dies at 75
abstract: Despite suffering from rheumatoid arthritis for decades, she traveled frequently and became the star of her SilverSneakers exercise class in Georgia.

name: Joan Feynman
profession: Shined Light on the Aurora Borealis
headline: Joan Feynman, Who Shined Light on the Aurora Borealis, Dies at 93
abstract: Her mother told her that women’s brains “can’t do science.” She would prove her mother very wrong.

name: Ronald Khalis Bell
headline: Ronald Khalis Bell of Kool & the Gang Dies at 68
abstract: He was the chief force behind the feel-good song “Celebration” and wrote or co-wrote many of the group’s other hits.

name: Ronald Harwood
headline: Ronald Harwood, Oscar-Winning Screenwriter, Is Dead at 85
abstract: A prolific writer of books and plays as well as screenplays, he won an Academy Award in 2003 for “The Pianist.”

name: Felicia Campbell
headline: Felicia Campbell, Professor Who Studied Gambling and Pop Culture, Dies at 89
abstract: Ms. Campbell was the longest-serving professor at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas. She died of complications of the novel coronavirus.

name: Ken Robinson
headline: Ken Robinson, Who Preached Creativity in Teaching, Dies at 70
abstract: Dance, he said, is just as important as math. He was knighted for his work, and his TED Talk on schools and the arts was the most viewed of all time.

name: Shere Hite
headline: Shere Hite, Who Challenged Myths of Female Sexuality, Dies at 77
abstract: Her 1976 book, ‘The Hite Report,’ touched off ‘a revolution in the bedroom’ and has sold tens of millions of copies. But harsh criticism drove her to self-exile in Europe.

name: Hal Singer
headline: Hal Singer, Influential Saxophonist, Is Dead at 100
abstract: A Tulsa massacre survivor, he worked with Duke Ellington and others contributed to the birth of rhythm and blues and rock ’n’ roll.

name: Toots Hibbert
headline: Toots Hibbert, a Father of Reggae, Is Dead
abstract: The first to use the word reggae on a record, he sang in a soulful tone and wrote songs with subtle social commentary, helping bring the sounds of Jamaica to the world.

name: Terence Conran
headline: Terence Conran, Designer and Retail Magnate, Is Dead at 88
abstract: An entrepreneur of mercurial moods and missionary zeal, he created an empire to market his designs and later opened restaurants in London, Paris and New York.

name: Simeon Coxe
headline: Simeon Coxe, Whose Silver Apples Presaged Synth-Pop, Dies at 82
abstract: In the late 1960s, playing a homemade electronic instrument, he created “the mating call between a jackhammer and a Veg-O-Matic.”

name: Gene Budig
profession: Last President of the American League
headline: Gene Budig, Last President of the American League, Dies at 81
abstract: After a distinguished academic career, he brought his love of baseball to a position that he considered a dream job — but that was eliminated five years later.

name: Kevin Dobson
headline: Kevin Dobson, ‘Kojak’ and ‘Knots Landing’ Actor, Dies at 77
abstract: Starting out by working odd jobs while auditioning, he found his greatest success on television playing a detective and a lawyer.

name: Florence Howe
headline: Florence Howe, ‘Mother of Women’s Studies,’ Dies at 91
abstract: In 1970, she helped found the Feminist Press. It was hailed for making available “a legacy of writings by and about women.”

name: Vasilis Dimitriou
profession: Keeper of a Fading Movie Art
headline: Vasilis Dimitriou, Keeper of a Fading Movie Art, Dies at 84
abstract: He was one of Europe’s last Hollywood billboard painters, creating, by hand, giant film promotions for theaters since the end of World War II.

name: Nancy Dine
profession: Filmmaker and Muse of Artist Jim Dine
headline: Nancy Dine, Filmmaker and Muse of Artist Jim Dine, Dies at 83
abstract: In the 1960s, the Dines were an art-world force in New York and London. Ms. Dine went on to make films about her husband, earning her an Academy Award nomination.

name: Jack
headline: Jack ‘Murph the Surf’ Murphy, Heist Mastermind, Dies at 83
abstract: He stole the Star of India and other gems from the Museum of Natural History. Two days later he was under arrest.

name: Marion Moses
headline: Dr. Marion Moses, Top Aide to Cesar Chavez, Dies at 84
abstract: She tended to the health of poor farm workers and was at the forefront of a 1960s national grape boycott that brought his agricultural union triumph.

name: Jiri Menzel
headline: Jiri Menzel, Oscar-Winning Czech Director, Dies at 82
abstract: His 1966 feature, “Closely Watched Trains,” won an Academy Award and was part of a burst of creativity in Czech filmmaking.

name: Anthony M. Hopkins
profession: Fought in Vietnam and the Gulf
headline: Anthony M. Hopkins, Who Fought in Vietnam and the Gulf, Dies at 70
abstract: A tank commander, he earned a Purple Heart when he was badly wounded by shrapnel in an ambush in South Vietnam. Later a postal worker, he died of Covid-19.

name: Randall Kenan
headline: Randall Kenan, Southern Writer of Magical Realism, Dies at 57
abstract: His upbringing in North Carolina helped him create a fictional hamlet, Tims Creek, where a 3-year-old clairvoyant scares the neighbors and a pig talks.

name: Bruce Williamson Jr.
headline: Bruce Williamson Jr., a Latter-Day Temptation, Dies at 49
abstract: A gospel music prodigy as a child, Mr. Williamson went on to sing with the Motown group for nearly a decade. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Bill Gates Sr.
headline: Bill Gates Sr., Who Guided Billionaire Son’s Philanthropy, Dies at 94
abstract: He channeled support for campaigns to eradicate polio, reduce infant mortality, build schools and help find an AIDS vaccine — among other causes.

name: DJ Jaffe
profession: Ad Man Turned Mental Health Crusader
headline: DJ Jaffe, Ad Man Turned Mental Health Crusader, Dies at 65
abstract: He pushed for passage of Kendra’s Law in New York, which mandates outpatient psychiatric treatment for patients deemed dangerous. It became a model for similar programs nationwide.

name: Stanley Crouch
headline: Stanley Crouch, Critic Who Saw American Democracy in Jazz, Dies at 74
abstract: A prolific author, essayist, columnist and social critic, he challenged conventional thinking on race and helped found Jazz at Lincoln Center.

name: William Pursell
headline: William Pursell, Musician of the Nashville Sound, Dies at 94
abstract: The two-time Grammy nominee was a studio pianist for country stars. His performance of “Our Winter Love” in 1963 hit the Billboard singles and album charts. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Momcilo Krajisnik
profession: Bosnian Serb Convicted of War Crimes
headline: Momcilo Krajisnik, Bosnian Serb Convicted of War Crimes, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Krajisnik, the speaker of the Bosnian Serb Parliament during the 1992-95 Bosnian war and the right-hand man of Radovan Karadzic, has died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Steve Carter
profession: Playwright in a Black Theater World
headline: Steve Carter, Playwright in a Black Theater World, Dies at 90
abstract: He emerged from the Black Arts movement and the famed Negro Ensemble Company, writing dramas and satires about the Black and Caribbean-American experiences.

name: John Najarian
headline: John Najarian, Pioneering Transplant Surgeon, Dies at 92
abstract: He was known for taking on difficult cases, many involving children. An anti-rejection drug he developed led to a scandal, but he was vindicated.

name: Tyler Amburgey
headline: Tyler Amburgey, Devoted Hockey Player and Coach, Dies at 29
abstract: A physical defenseman, he loved hockey enough to be excited by the sight of a new pair of skates or shin guards. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Ricardo Valderrama
profession: Noted Anthropologist and Mayor in Peru
headline: Ricardo Valderrama, Noted Anthropologist and Mayor in Peru, Dies at 75
abstract: As a scholar, Mr. Valderrama put a new focus on the plight of Indigenous people; as mayor of Cusco, he led the response to Covid-19, which killed him.

name: Ann Getty
headline: Ann Getty, Publisher and Bicoastal Arts Patron, Is Dead at 79
abstract: She married into one of the world’s richest families but refused to let herself be marginalized as a socialite.

name: Ke’Lin Dillard
headline: Ke’Lin Dillard, Caregiver and Dedicated Mother, Dies at 29
abstract: Ms. Dillard died of the coronavirus after giving birth to a second child. She never got the chance to hold her newborn.

name: Christian Liaigre
headline: Christian Liaigre, Minimalist Interior Designer, Dies at 77
abstract: Known for his muscular and clean-lined furniture, Mr. Liaigre designed the influential Mercer hotel in SoHo, as well as the homes of Rupert Murdoch and others.

name: Henrietta Boggs
headline: Henrietta Boggs, Southerner Who Spread Her Wings, Dies at 102
abstract: Fleeing segregated Alabama, she found revolution in Costa Rica and married its future president. She then pushed him to grant women and minorities the right to vote.

name: Tommy Searcy
headline: Tommy Searcy, Veteran Texas Firefighter, Dies at 45
abstract: He and his twin brother volunteered when they were 18 and had remained on the job ever since. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Winston Groom
headline: Winston Groom, Author of ‘Forrest Gump,’ Dies at 77
abstract: He wrote the 1986 novel that inspired the Oscar-winning film starring Tom Hanks. Another book was a finalist for a Pulitzer.

name: Larry Wilson
headline: Larry Wilson, Who Made Safety an N.F.L. Threat, Dies at 82
abstract: A feared Hall of Famer for the St. Louis Cardinals, he was known — particularly by battered quarterbacks — for the safety blitz.

name: Ruth Bader Ginsburg
headline: Ruth Bader Ginsburg, Supreme Court’s Feminist Icon, Is Dead at 87
abstract: The second woman appointed to the Supreme Court, Justice Ginsburg’s pointed and powerful dissenting opinions earned her late-life rock stardom.

name: Mabel Ping-Hua Lee
headline: Overlooked No More: Mabel Ping-Hua Lee, Suffragist With a Distinction
abstract: Lee stood out as a Chinese immigrant, giving speeches, writing articles and helping to lead a 10,000-strong march through the streets of New York City when she was just a teenager.

name: Anne Stevenson
headline: Anne Stevenson, Poet and Plath Biographer, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Her poetry was acclaimed, but her take on her more famous contemporary caused controversy.

name: Robert S. Graetz
profession: Rare White Minister to Back Bus Boycott
headline: Robert S. Graetz, Rare White Minister to Back Bus Boycott, Dies at 92
abstract: Targeted by the Ku Klux Klan, he drove Black people to and from work during the Montgomery boycott and remained an unbowed voice for desegregation.

name: Roy Hammond
headline: Roy Hammond, Soul Singer Who Birthed a Hip-Hop Heartbeat, Dies at 81
abstract: He wrote and produced the Honey Drippers’ “Impeach the President,” which has been sampled countless times and changed the sound of New York rap.

name: Charles Peterson
profession: Veteran Minor Leaguer and M.L.B. Scout
headline: Charles Peterson, Veteran Minor Leaguer and M.L.B. Scout, Dies at 46
abstract: As a football player, he caught a pass to win the state title for his South Carolina high school. He was later a scout for the St. Louis Cardinals. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Edith Raymond Locke
headline: Edith Raymond Locke, Mademoiselle Editor in the 1970s, Dies at 99
abstract: With her magazine for “smart girls,” she championed designers like Donna Karan, Ralph Lauren and Betsey Johnson.

name: Bryan Fonseca
headline: Bryan Fonseca, Independent Voice in Indianapolis Theater, Dies at 65
abstract: He directed unconventional works and championed diversity, both in the material he staged and in the actors performing it. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Betty Bushman
headline: Betty Bushman, an Early Female Baseball Voice, Dies at 89
abstract: Hired in 1964 to provide the women’s perspective on radio broadcasts of the Kansas City Athletics’ games, she made history. But her tenure was brief.

name: Tommy DeVito
profession: Original Member of the Four Seasons
headline: Tommy DeVito, Original Member of the Four Seasons, Dies at 92
abstract: He sang behind Frankie Valli in a hit-making harmony group that gained a new audience when “Jersey Boys” stormed Broadway. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Gale Sayers
profession: Elusive Hall of Fame Running Back Was 77
headline: Gale Sayers Dies; Elusive Hall of Fame Running Back Was 77
abstract: Though his career was cut short by injuries, he was regarded as one of the N.F.L.’s greatest players. The movie “Brian’s Song” spread his name beyond the sports world.

name: Ron Cobb
headline: Ron Cobb, a Pioneer in Science Fiction Design, Dies at 83
abstract: An artist and movie production designer, he helped shape the aesthetics of science fiction with his work on movies including “Star Wars,” “Alien” and “Back to the Future.”

name: Jackie Stallone
headline: Jackie Stallone, Celebrity Astrologer and Sylvester’s Mother, Dies at 98
abstract: After running away with the circus, she promoted women’s wrestling and fitness before seeing signs of the future in a most unusual spot. (Hint: it’s not the palm.)

name: Juliette Gréco
headline: Juliette Gréco, Grande Dame of Chanson Française, Dies at 93
abstract: The muse of bohemian postwar Paris, she became an internationally known actress and singer.

name: Harold Evans
profession: Crusading Newspaperman With a Second Act
headline: Harold Evans Dies at 92; Crusading Newspaperman With a Second Act
abstract: In Britain, he helped redefine high-quality newspapers and challenged legal restrictions on the press. In America, he brought new scope and glitz to book publishing as the head of Random House.

name: Sterling Magee
headline: Sterling Magee, Bluesman Known as ‘Satan,’ Dies at 84
abstract: As half of the duo Satan and Adam, he played blues on the streets of Harlem and later on stages around the world. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Donald Kendall
profession: Pepsis Chief During the Cola Wars
headline: Donald Kendall, Pepsi’s Chief During the Cola Wars, Dies at 99
abstract: He faced off against Coke, wooed a ‘Pepsi generation’ and bought Frito-Lay and fast food chains. Ever loyal, he downed a Pepsi for breakfast.

name: Henry van Ameringen
headline: Henry van Ameringen, Friend of L.G.B.T.Q. Causes, Dies at 89
abstract: Heir to a family fortune in the fragrances industry, he was among the first openly gay major donors to fund L.G.B.T.Q. and AIDS-related organizations.

name: Christiane Eda-Pierre
headline: Christiane Eda-Pierre, Leading French Soprano, Dies at 88
abstract: Born in Martinique, Ms. Eda-Pierre was one of France’s first international Black opera stars.

name: Catharine Phanavong
profession: Expert Cook and Dinner Party Enthusiast
headline: Catharine Phanavong, Expert Cook and Dinner Party Enthusiast, Dies at 39
abstract: “Chefs would get off work and come to our place for late night dinners,” her boyfriend said. Ms. Phanavong died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Sam McBratney
profession: Wrote Guess How Much I Love You
headline: Sam McBratney Dies at 77; Wrote ‘Guess How Much I Love You’
abstract: His bedtime story of a hare and his son one-upping each other in declaring their love became a children’s classic, translated into 57 languages.

name: Robert Gore
headline: Robert Gore, Inventor of Gore-Tex, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Experiments with a polymer led him to create the breathable, waterproof material used in numerous applications, including ski jackets and medical implants.

name: Ang Rita
headline: Ang Rita, Who Conquered Everest Again and Again, Dies at 72
abstract: Earning the nickname Snow Leopard for his agility, he climbed the world’s highest mountain 10 times without supplemental oxygen between 1983 and 1996.

name: Pierre Troisgros
headline: Pierre Troisgros, Renowned French Restaurateur, Dies at 92
abstract: He was part of a generation of influential, game-changing chefs at the forefront of nouvelle cuisine.

name: Michael Lonsdale
headline: Michael Lonsdale, a Bond Villain and Much More, Dies at 89
abstract: He was best known to many as Hugo Drax in “Moonraker.” But he also worked with a Who’s Who of directors including Truffaut, Spielberg and Marguerite Duras.

name: Rebecca Shadowen
headline: Dr. Rebecca Shadowen, Expert in Infectious Diseases, Dies at 62
abstract: Dr. Shadowen, ill with the coronavirus, continued to attend meetings from her hospital bed. She eventually died of Covid-19.

name: Keith Hufnagel
headline: Keith Hufnagel, Pro Skateboarder and Entrepreneur, Dies at 46
abstract: He soared over treacherous streets on his board before opening a streetwear store that grew into the popular brand Huf.

name: Tony Tanner
headline: Tony Tanner, Who Brought ‘Joseph’ to Broadway, Dies at 88
abstract: A versatile writer and actor as well as a director, he was also Littlechap in a film version of “Stop the World, I Want to Get Off.”

name: Bette Dewing
headline: Bette Dewing, Columnist for a ‘Gentle City,’ Dies at 97
abstract: For more than 40 years, Ms. Dewing urged New Yorkers to reclaim civility in her column in Our Town, an Upper East Side weekly. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Arthur Ashkin
profession: Nobel Laureate Invented a Tractor Beam
headline: Arthur Ashkin, 98, Dies; Nobel Laureate Invented a ‘Tractor Beam’
abstract: It isn’t quite “Star Trek,” but his optical tweezers use the pressure of light in a laser beam to seize and manipulate microscopic objects, from atoms to living cells.

name: Swami Agnivesh
profession: Crusader Against Labor Abuses in India
headline: Swami Agnivesh, Crusader Against Labor Abuses in India, Dies at 80
abstract: A pacifist monk, he championed social justice causes, fighting against child labor, indentured servitude and a rising tide of Hindu fundamentalism.

name: Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah
headline: Sheikh Sabah al-Ahmad al-Sabah, Kuwait’s Leader, Dies at 91
abstract: The emir steered the tiny, oil-rich country through the tumultuous rivalries of the Middle East.

name: Lillian Brown
headline: Lillian Brown, Makeup Artist to Nine Presidents, Dies at 106
abstract: She did more than powder noses; she advised on diction and apparel and helped commanders in chief put their best selves forward for television.

name: Jay Johnstone
headline: Jay Johnstone, Major League Outfielder and Prankster, Dies at 74
abstract: He played in the World Series with the 1978 Yankees and the 1981 Dodgers, but he was best known for his imaginative stunts. He died of Covid-19 complications.

name: Meron Benvenisti
profession: Urged One State for Jews and Palestinians
headline: Meron Benvenisti Dies at 86; Urged One State for Jews and Palestinians
abstract: As a political scientist, columnist and ‘the last Zionist,’ he argued against a separate Palestinian state, saying the growth of West Bank settlements had precluded it.

name: Helen Reddy
headline: Helen Reddy Dies at 78; Sang ‘I Am Woman’
abstract: The Australian-born singer’s first No. 1 hit became a feminist anthem and propelled her to international stardom.

name: Mac Davis
headline: Mac Davis, Pop and Country Singing Star, Is Dead at 78
abstract: After writing hits for Elvis Presley and others, he became famous in his own right with songs like the No. 1 hit “Baby Don’t Get Hooked on Me.”

name: Norman Bernal
headline: Norman Bernal, Generation-Spanning Music Teacher, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Bernal, who had Covid-19, was a Peruvian-born violinist who established himself as a longtime player and pedagogue in the United States.

name: Timothy Ray Brown
headline: Timothy Ray Brown, First Patient Cured of H.I.V., Dies at 54
abstract: Known initially as the “Berlin Patient,” he underwent an experimental stem cell transplant 13 years ago that rid his body of the virus. He died of leukemia.

name: Robert Bechtle
headline: Robert Bechtle, Photorealist Painter of Suburbia, Dies at 88
abstract: He used photographs to guide his meticulously rendered paintings of everyday American landscapes, finding unexpected beauty.

name: Lucy Diggs Slowe
headline: Overlooked No More: Lucy Diggs Slowe, Scholar Who Persisted Against Racism and Sexism
abstract: Impelled by her vision of the modern Black woman, Slowe nurtured a post-World War I generation at Howard University to be empowered, self-aware and globally conscious.

name: Verne Edquist
headline: Verne Edquist, Virtuoso Piano Tuner, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Edquist ministered to Glenn Gould’s favorite piano, heard on dozens of recordings. The two men’s exacting approaches were well matched.

name: John Turner
profession: Briefly Its Leader but Long a Force in Canada
headline: John Turner, Briefly Its Leader but Long a Force in Canada, Dies at 91
abstract: He carried out Liberal Party reforms in top cabinet posts but was ousted as prime minister after just 79 days. He later led the opposition to free-trade deals with the U.S.

name: Renée C. Fox
headline: Renée C. Fox, Founding Figure of Medical Sociology, Dies at 92
abstract: She is credited with helping to create the field of bioethics and applying the methods of sociology to medical care.

name: Yuri Orlov
headline: Yuri Orlov, Bold Champion of Soviet Dissidents, Dies at 96
abstract: A prominent physicist, he founded the Moscow Helsinki Group to hold his government accountable after serving time in prison and in exile.

name: Grace Meo
profession: Skilled Seamstress and Serious Sinatra Fan
headline: Grace Meo, Skilled Seamstress and Serious Sinatra Fan, Dies at 93
abstract: Ms. Meo could sew anything, and she loved her family, but her heart belonged to the Voice. She died of Covid-19.

name: Joe Laurinaitis
headline: Joe Laurinaitis, a Star as Tag Team’s ‘Animal,’ Dies at 60
abstract: As one of the Road Warriors, he brought a muscled flamboyance to professional wrestling.

name: S. P. Balasubrahmanyam
headline: S. P. Balasubrahmanyam, Indian Singer With Huge Repertory, Dies at 74
abstract: Known as S.P.B., he sang in a number of languages and was known for his film work. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Murray Schisgal
profession: Brought the Absurd to the Mainstream
headline: Murray Schisgal, Who Brought the Absurd to the Mainstream, Dies at 93
abstract: With “Luv” on Broadway and “Tootsie” on the screen, he wrote with knowing, slightly askew humor about subjects like sex, family and failure.

name: Cat Bordhi
headline: Cat Bordhi, Who Challenged Traditional Ways of Knitting, Dies at 69
abstract: Confounded by the complicated instructions that had become the standard, she thought up whimsical new techniques to create socks, scarves and other items.

name: Jacques-Louis Monod
profession: Modernist Composer With a Lyrical Touch
headline: Jacques-Louis Monod, Modernist Composer With a Lyrical Touch, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Monod was an uncompromising champion of composers of the Second Viennese School, including Arnold Schoenberg and Anton Webern.

name: Soraya Santiago Solla
headline: Soraya Santiago Solla, Transgender Trailblazer, Dies at 72
abstract: She was the first in Puerto Rico to change a gender designation on a birth certificate and the first there to reveal that she’d had sex-reassignment surgery.

name: Terry Goodkind
headline: Terry Goodkind, Master of Fantasy Fiction, Is Dead at 72
abstract: His epic series “The Sword of Truth” spanned 17 books and sold more than 25 million copies worldwide. But his views angered some readers.

name: Joan Marks
headline: Joan Marks, Doyenne of Genetic Counselors, Dies at 91
abstract: She taught counselors to empower their patients to make informed medical decisions about genetic tests and inherited diseases.

name: Derek Mahon
headline: Derek Mahon, Popular Irish Poet, Is Dead at 78
abstract: He wove together history, personal demons and quiet contemplation in works that could be dark but also spoke of renewal.

name: Bob Gibson
headline: Bob Gibson, Feared Flamethrower for the Cardinals, Dies at 84
abstract: Gibson, who won two Cy Young Awards and threw 56 career shutouts, was one of baseball’s most dominating and intimidating pitchers.

name: Kenzo Takada
profession: Brought Japanese Fashion to the World
headline: Kenzo Takada, Who Brought Japanese Fashion to the World, Dies at 81
abstract: He planned to stay in Paris for six months but stayed 56 years, becoming known for bold, exuberant prints. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Thomas Jefferson Byrd
headline: Thomas Jefferson Byrd, Actor in Spike Lee Films, Dies at 70
abstract: The Tony-nominated actor, 70, was found by police with multiple gunshot wounds early Saturday morning.

name: Carter Williams
headline: Carter Williams, Who Unshackled Nursing Home Residents, Dies at 97
abstract: By closely describing the inner lives of older people, Ms. Williams altered legal regulations and clinical standards applied to nursing homes.

name: Mike Foster
headline: Mike Foster, Louisiana Governor During a Lull, Dies at 90
abstract: A two-term Republican convert, he served between the tumult of the scandalous Edwin Edwards era and the devastation of Hurricane Katrina.

name: James Helferich
profession: Artist in the Food World and Prison Chef
headline: James Helferich, Artist in the Food World and Prison Chef, Dies at 75
abstract: A classically trained cook, Mr. Helferich worked at marine theme parks in Florida, enthralling his co-workers with his skill as an ice and butter sculptor. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Quino
headline: Quino, Creator of Beloved ‘Mafalda’ Cartoon, Dies at 88
abstract: Joaquín Salvador Lavado drew the comic strip of the six-year-old Argentine girl, who was curious about the world and finely attuned to its injustices.

name: Ron Perranoski
headline: Ron Perranoski, Ace Reliever in Dodgers’ Storied ’60s, Dies at 84
abstract: A crafty left-hander, he appeared in three World Series for Los Angeles, backing up the likes of Koufax and Drysdale.

name: Peregrine Worsthorne
headline: Peregrine Worsthorne, Provocative Conservative British Editor, Dies at 96
abstract: From a newspaper perch, he championed the British “elite,” lamented the decline of “the gentleman” and made headlines himself with a word that can’t be quoted.

name: Edoardo Tamer
headline: The Rev. Edoardo Tamer, Who Ministered to Syrians in War, Dies at 83
abstract: Father Tamer, a Lebanese Franciscan, chose to remain behind when given the chance to leave Syria after fighting broke out. He died of Covid-19.

name: William Danforth
headline: William Danforth, Who Led Washington University, Dies at 94
abstract: Under Dr. Danforth, the St. Louis campus was transformed from a commuter school into a world-renowned institution.

name: Eddie Van Halen
headline: Eddie Van Halen, Virtuoso of the Rock Guitar, Dies at 65
abstract: His outpouring of riffs, runs and solos was hyperactive and athletic, making deeper or darker emotions feel irrelevant. The band he led was one of the most popular of all time.

name: Robert K. Ruskin
headline: Robert K. Ruskin, Who Targeted New York Corruption, Dies at 93
abstract: As investigation commissioner under Mayor Lindsay in the early 1970s, he went after police officers, building inspectors, parking ticket fixers and peep-show operators.

name: Johnny Nash
profession: Sang I Can See Clearly Now
headline: Johnny Nash, Who Sang ‘I Can See Clearly Now,’ Dies at 80
abstract: After only modest success as a romantic crooner, he played a key role in bringing reggae to a wider audience.

name: Joseph L. Bruno
profession: Power Broker in New York Senate
headline: Joseph L. Bruno, Power Broker in New York Senate, Dies at 91
abstract: As the Republican majority leader for 13 years, he was one of the “three men in a room” who decided things in Albany. Then came corruption charges and, ultimately, vindication.

name: Lyon Gardiner Tyler Jr.
headline: Lyon Gardiner Tyler Jr., Grandson of the 10th President, Dies at 95
abstract: He and his brother, grandsons of John Tyler, were the third of three generations that remarkably spanned almost the entire history of the American experience.

name: Mark Andrews
headline: Mark Andrews, North Dakota Farmer-Politician, Dies at 94
abstract: His support for agriculture helped him win nine elections to the House and one to the Senate, despite a moderate-to-liberal voting record as a Republican.

name: Jim Dwyer
headline: Jim Dwyer, Pulitzer Prize-Winning Journalist, Dies at 63
abstract: Working for New York Newsday, The Daily News and The Times, he covered the human stories of New York in dramatic prose and crusaded against injustice.

name: Maynard Solomon
headline: Maynard Solomon, Provocative Biographer of Composers, Dies at 90
abstract: Mr. Solomon probed the psyches of Mozart and Beethoven in critically acclaimed works; he was also a co-founder of an adventurous Vanguard record label.

name: Stephen Barnes
profession: Partner in Law Firm With Cellino
headline: Stephen Barnes, Partner in Law Firm With Cellino, Dies at 61
abstract: A jingle helped them transform a two-partner practice in Buffalo into a 50-lawyer personal injury behemoth in New York State and California. Mr. Barnes died in a plane crash.

name: Ardeth Platte
headline: Ardeth Platte, Dominican Nun and Antinuclear Activist, Dies at 84
abstract: Sister Ardeth spent years behind bars for her beliefs and was the inspiration for a character on the Netflix hit “Orange Is the New Black.”

name: Maurice Edwards
profession: Busy Figure in Theater and Music
headline: Maurice Edwards, Busy Figure in Theater and Music, Dies at 97
abstract: He was involved with the Brooklyn Philharmonic for many years and performed both on Broadway and off. He died of the novel coronavirus.

name: Giovanni D’Alise
headline: Bishop Giovanni D’Alise, Italian Bishop Who Defended South, Dies at 72
abstract: An amiable, down-to-earth priest, he was the first Italian bishop infected by the coronavirus to die.

name: Mohammad Reza Shajarian
headline: Mohammad Reza Shajarian, Iranian Master Singer and Dissident, Dies at 80
abstract: He popularized Persian classical music for a new generation and built a global following, only to be blacklisted by Iran for supporting antigovernment protests.

name: Whitey Ford
headline: Whitey Ford, Beloved Yankees Pitcher Who Confounded Batters, Dies at 91
abstract: An irrepressible son of New York City, Ford joined the pantheon of baseball legends who dominated the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Mario J. Aranda
headline: Mario J. Aranda, Advocate for Immigrant Rights, Dies at 79
abstract: A Mormon, he spent decades as an advocate for Latinos in Chicago before making a break with his old life. He died of Covid-19.

name: Gary Pettus
profession: Used Skills To Bless the Lives of People
headline: Gary Pettus Dies at 70; Used Skills ‘To Bless the Lives of People’
abstract: Mr. Pettus built a plumbing and heating business from scratch and grabbed opportunities to be a mentor and relief worker with his church. He died of Covid-19.

name: Carol Paumgarten
profession: Den Mother to a Dance Scene
headline: Carol Paumgarten, ‘Den Mother’ to a Dance Scene, Dies at 76
abstract: Her sprawling studio, Steps on Broadway, has been a mecca for professionals, celebrities, children and just everyday people who want to dance.

name: Domenic Parisi
headline: Domenic Parisi Dies at 76; He Sheared Nixon’s Locks
abstract: Born in Sicily, he trained as a farrier but became a barber in New Jersey, where his most famous client was the former president. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Joe Morgan
headline: Joe Morgan, Hall of Fame Second Baseman, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Morgan, who later became a well-known television commentator, was among the smallest great players in the history of the game and among the greatest second basemen.

name: Mitsuye Tanamachi
headline: Mitsuye Tanamachi, World War II Internee, Dies at 97
abstract: The Japanese-American daughter of a California farmer was confined to a camp in Arizona where she found her husband. She died of Covid-19.

name: Walter Ashcraft
headline: Walter Ashcraft, College Football Star Who Became a Coach, Dies at 91
abstract: He was an N.F.L. draftee, but an injury prevented him from playing. He devoted himself to coaching and hospitality work. He died of Covid-19.

name: Margaret Nolan
headline: Margaret Nolan, ‘Goldfinger’ Actress, Dies at 76
abstract: She drew attention at age 20 when she was seen painted gold in the Bond film’s opening credits. She also appeared in the Beatles movie “A Hard Day’s Night.”

name: Roberta McCain
profession: Mother of the Senator and His Beacon
headline: Roberta McCain Dies at 108; Mother of the Senator and His Beacon
abstract: John McCain credited to her his will to survive as a prisoner of war. She later campaigned for him in his 2008 bid for the presidency.

name: Monica Roberts
headline: Monica Roberts, Transgender Advocate and Journalist, Dies at 58
abstract: Ms. Roberts started her blog, TransGriot, in 2006, at a time when coverage of transgender issues by the mainstream media was limited.

name: Joyce Dinkins
profession: Wife of Former New York Mayor
headline: Joyce Dinkins, Wife of Former New York Mayor, Dies at 89
abstract: As the city’s first Black first lady, she transformed herself from a private person to a gracious public advocate for children.

name: Conchata Ferrell
profession: Memorable Maid on Two and a Half Men
headline: Conchata Ferrell, Memorable Maid on ‘Two and a Half Men,’ Dies at 77
