abstract: She first achieved acclaim on the stage. But she was best known for her Emmy-nominated role as Berta, Charlie Sheen’s gruff housekeeper.

name: Tom Kennedy
profession: Genial Journeyman of TV Game Shows
headline: Tom Kennedy, Genial Journeyman of TV Game Shows, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Kennedy brought gaiety and a dollop of schmaltz to his work as the host of 14 shows on multiple networks, and in syndication, over nearly 30 years.

name: Don Piccard
headline: Don Piccard, a Pioneer Who Soared, Is Dead at 94
abstract: He was balloon royalty, the son of scientist parents who reached the stratosphere. He went on to build balloons — and set records — of his own.

name: Mario Molina
profession: Sounded an Alarm on the Ozone Layer
headline: Mario Molina, 77, Dies; Sounded an Alarm on the Ozone Layer
abstract: He shared the Nobel Prize in Chemistry for research that showed how chemicals in hair spray and other products could cause grave environmental damage.

name: Herbert Kretzmer
headline: Herbert Kretzmer, Lyricist for ‘Les Misérables,’ Dies at 95
abstract: A London theater critic, he turned a little-known French musical into a global blockbuster, earning $20 million in royalties.

name: Erin Wall
profession: Acclaimed Soprano in Mozart and Strauss
headline: Erin Wall, 44, Dies; Acclaimed Soprano in Mozart and Strauss
abstract: Ms. Wall, who started her career at Lyric Opera of Chicago, had a silvery soprano voice that grew more opulent as it evolved.

name: Faith Stewart-Gordon
profession: Doyenne of the Russian Tea Room
headline: Faith Stewart-Gordon, Doyenne of the Russian Tea Room, Dies at 88
abstract: After her husband died in 1967, she was the sole owner of the festive Manhattan gathering and gossiping spot until she sold it in 1995.

name: Constance Buchanan
headline: Constance Buchanan Dies at 73; Gave Women Voice in Religion
abstract: At Harvard Divinity School, she ensured that women were represented in scholarship, in the curriculum, in the syllabus and in publications.

name: Stuart Bowyer
headline: Stuart Bowyer, Astronomer Who Lent His Ear to the Cosmos, Dies at 86
abstract: He was a scientist who succeeded in seeing the unseeable and hoped to tune in to extraterrestrial life.

name: Lulu Peyraud
headline: Lulu Peyraud, a French Wine Matriarch, Dies at 102
abstract: Her family ran Domaine Tempier, a wine estate in Provence known for its Bandol reds and rosés. She ran the kitchen.

name: Bob Shanks
headline: Bob Shanks, Influential TV Executive, Dies at 88
abstract: He helped create “Good Morning America” and “20/20” and had a role in the early careers of the Smothers Brothers, Barbra Streisand and many others.

name: Scott Lilienfeld
headline: Scott Lilienfeld, Psychologist Who Questioned Psychology, Dies at 59
abstract: Dr. Lilienfeld disturbed the order in his own field by questioning the science behind many of its conceits, therapies and tools.

name: Max Osceola Jr.
headline: Max Osceola Jr., Seminole Tribal Leader, Dies at 70
abstract: He helped his tribe go from operating roadside bingo games to owning the Hard Rock chain, ushering in an era of prosperity. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Eitan Haber
headline: Eitan Haber, Rabin Aide and Israeli Wordsmith, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Haber moved between journalism and service to the prime minister whose death he announced to the nation.

name: Ruth Kluger
profession: Author of a Haunting Holocaust Memoir
headline: Ruth Kluger, Author of a Haunting Holocaust Memoir, Dies at 88
abstract: Her “Still Alive” was an unforgiving view of anti-Semitism in Vienna and a feminist window on the war and the world beyond.

name: Eleanor Flexner
profession: Pioneering Feminist in an Anti-Feminist Age
headline: Overlooked No More: Eleanor Flexner, Pioneering Feminist in an Anti-Feminist Age
abstract: “Century of Struggle,” her 1959 history of the women’s rights movement, uncovered previously ignored narratives, like the contributions of African-American women.

name: Ed Benguiat
headline: Ed Benguiat, a Master of Typography, Is Dead at 92
abstract: A noted graphic designer, he was an expert in typefaces, developing many himself and “fixing” others. His work adorns this newspaper.

name: Rhonda Fleming
headline: Rhonda Fleming, 97, Movie Star Made for Technicolor, Is Dead
abstract: Ms. Fleming’s roles ranged from Wyatt Earp’s love interest to a princess in King Arthur’s court.

name: Fred Dean
headline: Fred Dean, Sack Specialist Who Ignited 49ers Dynasty, Dies at 68
abstract: Dean helped lead San Francisco to two Super Bowl victories, transforming the team into an N.F.L. powerhouse. He died of Covid-19.

name: Bess Abell
profession: Social Secretary in Johnson White House
headline: Bess Abell, Social Secretary in Johnson White House, Dies at 87
abstract: Averting last-minute crises is part of the job description; she was built for it, carried it out in style and had a good time doing it.

name: Alan S. Boyd
headline: Alan S. Boyd, Nation’s First Transportation Chief, Dies at 98
abstract: Lyndon B. Johnson chose him to lead a new department integrating vast air, sea and land systems. He also led Amtrak and the Illinois Central Railroad.

name: Jon Gibson
headline: Jon Gibson, Minimalist Saxophonist and Composer, Dies at 80
abstract: Best known for his long association with Philip Glass, Mr. Gibson also worked with Steve Reich, Terry Riley and La Monte Young as well as performing his own music.

name: Clark Middleton
headline: Clark Middleton, Actor With a Cause, Is Dead at 63
abstract: Known for his role on “The Blacklist,” he strove to convey the message that his juvenile rheumatoid arthritis was not a limitation.

name: John Vakulskas
headline: Rev. John Vakulskas Dies at 76; Carnivals Were His Parish
abstract: He ministered to generations of carnival workers, and his work was recognized by popes. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Rebecca Cryer
profession: Tribal Judge and Oklahoma City Bomb Survivor
headline: Rebecca Cryer, 73, Tribal Judge and Oklahoma City Bomb Survivor, Dies
abstract: Judge Cryer, who traced her ancestry to the Pottawatamie people, traveled the country to assist poorly funded native courts. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Spencer Davis
profession: Band Helped Power the Sound of the 60s
headline: Spencer Davis, Whose Band Helped Power the Sound of the ’60s, Dies at 81
abstract: Hits like “Gimme Some Lovin’” and “I’m a Man” made the Spencer Davis Group, based in Britain, famous worldwide and launched the career of its lead singer, Steve Winwood.

name: Anthony Chisholm
headline: Anthony Chisholm Dies at 77; Acclaimed in August Wilson Roles
abstract: He appeared in numerous productions of Wilson’s Pittsburgh Cycle plays, including four on Broadway.

name: Robert DeMora
profession: Helped Make Bette Midler Look Divine
headline: Robert DeMora Dies at 85; Helped Make Bette Midler Look Divine
abstract: His outlandish costumes embellished Ms. Midler’s elaborate extravaganzas. He also contributed to films like “Risky Business” and “The Birdcage.”

name: Ruth Falcon
headline: Ruth Falcon, Soprano Turned Master Teacher, Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Falcon had a career singing at major opera houses before becoming a much sought-after teacher. Her students included Deborah Voigt and Nadine Sierra.

name: J. Michael Lane
profession: General in the Rout of Smallpox
headline: J. Michael Lane, a General in the Rout of Smallpox, Dies at 84
abstract: At the C.D.C., he waged a 13-year campaign to vanquish a deadly infectious disease that had ravaged the world for centuries. Victory came in 1977.

name: James A. Johnson
headline: James A. Johnson, Democratic Power Broker, Dies at 76
abstract: Once called “the chairman of the universe,” he led Fannie Mae, the Kennedy Center and the Brookings Institution. He also aided in several presidential runs.

name: James Randi
headline: James Randi, Magician Who Debunked Paranormal Claims, Dies at 92
abstract: Known professionally as the Amazing Randi, he dedicated his life to exposing seers who did not see, healers who did not heal and many others.

name: Marge Champion
headline: Marge Champion, Dancer, Actor and Choreographer, Dies at 101
abstract: She was a model for Disney’s animated heroine in “Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs,” and she and her husband, Gower, epitomized the clean-cut, all-American dance team of Hollywood musicals.

name: James Redford
headline: James Redford, Documentarian and Environmentalist, Dies at 58
abstract: After two liver transplants, he founded an institute to increase awareness. He and his father, Robert Redford, also championed environmental films.

name: Lonnie Norman
headline: Mayor Lonnie Norman, Whose Town Hosts Bonnaroo, Dies at 79
abstract: He was dedicated to Manchester, the small city where he was born and raised. In 1991, he became the city’s first Black mayor. He died of Covid-19.

name: Alexandra Korry
profession: Pushed to End Solitary for Juveniles
headline: Alexandra Korry, 61, Dies; Pushed to End Solitary for Juveniles
abstract: A corporate lawyer who gave time for public service in New York, she also criticized police stop-and-frisk tactics and school funding that harmed Black and Hispanic people.

name: Tom Maschler
profession: Bold British Publisher and Booker Prize Founder
headline: Tom Maschler, Bold British Publisher and Booker Prize Founder, Dies at 87
abstract: He fostered the careers of more than a dozen Nobel laureates, including Gabriel García Márquez, Nadine Gordimer and Doris Lessing.

name: Harrison Johnson
profession: Pastor at Funeral in Mass Shooting
headline: Harrison Johnson, Pastor at Funeral in Mass Shooting, Dies at 65
abstract: A minister who doubled as a funeral director, he officiated at an El Paso service attended or livestreamed by thousands. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Charles Giambelluca
headline: Charles Giambelluca, Dedicated Youth Baseball Coach, Dies at 77
abstract: He owned a sporting goods store, but his passion was American Legion ball: He coached the same squad for 50 years. He died of Covid-19 complications.

name: Jerry Jeff Walker
headline: Jerry Jeff Walker, Who Wrote and Sang ‘Mr. Bojangles,’ Dies at 78
abstract: He never had a Top 40 pop hit. But his best-known composition became a standard, and he became a mainstay of the outlaw country movement.

name: Edith O’Hara
headline: Edith O’Hara, a Fixture of Off Off Broadway, Dies at 103
abstract: The theater she founded, the 13th Street Repertory Company, has been an eclectic presence on the New York scene for almost half a century.

name: Lee Kun-hee
profession: Built Samsung Into a Global Giant
headline: Lee Kun-hee, Who Built Samsung Into a Global Giant, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Lee was convicted — and pardoned — twice for white-collar crimes, in a sign of the ills in South Korea’s relationship with its business dynasties.

name: Virginia Mollenkott
profession: Feminist Found Liberation in the Bible
headline: Virginia Mollenkott, 88, Dies; Feminist Found Liberation in the Bible
abstract: A Christian evangelical who was shunned for her lesbianism, she became an influential scholar of the Bible, finding in it acceptance of L.G.B.T.Q. people.

name: Jeannette Williams-Parker
profession: Nurse in a Virus Hot Spot
headline: Jeannette Williams-Parker, Nurse in a Virus Hot Spot, Dies at 48
abstract: She was the first nurse in West Virginia to die of Covid-19. “She just never thought it would happen to her,” her mother said.

name: Susan Hendl
headline: Susan Hendl, Ballet Master and Dancer, Dies at 73
abstract: After dancing for George Balanchine and Jerome Robbins, she became a longtime teacher at the New York City Ballet.

name: Ming Cho Lee
headline: Ming Cho Lee, Fabled Set Designer, Is Dead at 90
abstract: His work in theater, dance and opera helped redefine American stage design.

name: Daniel Menaker
headline: Daniel Menaker, Book Editor Who Wrote With Wit, Dies at 79
abstract: After 26 years at The New Yorker, he became chief editor at Random House, overseeing works by a raft of luminaries. He wrote a half-dozen well-received books of his own.

name: Sharon Hunt
headline: Sharon Hunt, Teacher for a Quarter-Century, Dies at 65
abstract: After a career in the classroom, she died before she could spend her first retirement check. Her battle with Covid-19 taught family and friends a lesson in fortitude.

name: Robert Murray
headline: Robert Murray, Coal Baron With Clout, Dies at 80
abstract: The son of a coal miner, he built a sprawling company, fought government regulations and wielded considerable political influence as a Trump ally.

name: Joyce Wallace
headline: Dr. Joyce Wallace, Pioneering AIDS Physician, Dies at 79
abstract: Among the first to study the disease in the 1980s, she tried to stop its spread among thousands of New York City prostitutes.

name: Cecilia Chiang
profession: Brought Authentic Chinese Food to America
headline: Cecilia Chiang, Who Brought Authentic Chinese Food to America, Dies at 100
abstract: With her famed Mandarin restaurant in San Francisco, she enticed diners with the dishes she grew up with, leaving the American chop suey and chow mein era far behind.

name: Juan Torruella
headline: Juan Torruella, Groundbreaking U.S. Appeals Judge, Dies at 87
abstract: He was the only Hispanic to serve on the First Circuit court in Boston. In July he moved to overturn a death sentence in the Boston Marathon bombing.

name: Diane di Prima
profession: Poet of the Beat Era and Beyond
headline: Diane di Prima, Poet of the Beat Era and Beyond, Dies at 86
abstract: She traveled in the circles of Ginsberg and Ferlinghetti, a rare female voice in a male world, and went on to a long, prolific career in poetry.

name: Bob Biggs
headline: Bob Biggs, Los Angeles Punk-Rock Entrepreneur, Dies at 74
abstract: Slash Records, which Mr. Biggs founded in 1979, became one of the most successful independent record labels of its era.

name: Chris Pendergast
headline: Chris Pendergast, Who Fought A.L.S. Mile After Mile, Dies at 71
abstract: Living for 27 years with Lou Gehrig’s disease (and beating the odds), he started Ride for Life, an annual trek that has raised millions for A.L.S. research.

name: Billy Joe Shaver
headline: Billy Joe Shaver, Outlaw Singer and Songwriter, Dies at 81
abstract: Waylon Jennings put him on the musical map. Elvis Presley and Johnny Cash recorded his material. Bob Dylan sang admiringly of listening to his music.

name: Dan Baum
headline: Dan Baum, Journalist, Author and Long-Form Tweeter, Dies at 64
abstract: He was a Twitter pioneer in writing at length, 140 characters at a time, about losing his job at The New Yorker. He also wrote an admired book on New Orleans.

name: Choua Yang
headline: Choua Yang, Hmong Refugee and Educator, Dies at 53
abstract: With her husband, she founded Prairie Seeds Academy in Minneapolis, a charter school centered on Hmong language, culture and heritage. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Jimmy Orr
profession: Favorite Target of the Colts Unitas
headline: Jimmy Orr, a Favorite Target of the Colts’ Unitas, Dies at 85
abstract: He and Baltimore’s Hall of Fame quarterback were a top passing combination in the ’60s. But he may be best remembered for the pass that never came his way.

name: Travis Roy
profession: Inspired Millions After a Hockey Tragedy
headline: Travis Roy, Who Inspired Millions After a Hockey Tragedy, Dies at 45
abstract: After an awkward fall 11 seconds into his first Boston University game left him a quadriplegic, he dedicated his life to advocacy for similarly disabled people.

name: Rosa May Billinghurst
headline: Overlooked No More: Rosa May Billinghurst, Militant Suffragette
abstract: She was arrested multiple times but persisted in her activism, which ultimately helped women secure the right to vote in England.

name: Peter Secchia
headline: Peter Secchia, Confidant of Ford and Bush, Dies at 83
abstract: He was a Republican fund-raiser from Michigan who became a White House regular and an ambassador to Italy. He died of Covid-19.

name: Enzo Mari
headline: Enzo Mari, Industrial Designer Who Kept Things Simple, Dies at 88
abstract: He railed against material excess, consumerism and fame, but made poetic and useful objects that influenced generations of designers. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Herb Adderley
headline: Herb Adderley, a Packers Hall of Fame Cornerback, Dies at 81
abstract: A defensive star in Green Bay — he ran back seven interceptions for touchdowns — he played on five championship teams under Vince Lombardi and one in Dallas.

name: Sean Connery
headline: Sean Connery, Who Embodied James Bond and More, Dies at 90
abstract: To legions of fans who have watched a parade of actors play Agent 007, none played the part as magnetically or as indelibly as Mr. Connery.

name: Elvia Ramirez
profession: Youngest Covid-19 Victim in North Dakota
headline: Elvia Ramirez Dies at 17; Youngest Covid-19 Victim in North Dakota
abstract: Her mother watched her heartbreaking decline over three swift weeks, starting in mid-September, when Elvia began experiencing headaches.

name: Amanda Bouffioux
headline: Amanda Bouffioux, Alaska Native and ‘Amazing Mother,’ Dies at 44
abstract: Ms. Bouffioux’s death, of the coronavirus, was a reminder of the impact the pandemic has had on Alaska Natives, whose mortality rate has been more than four times higher than white Alaskans.

name: Joan Bingham
headline: Joan Bingham, Catalyst in a Publishing Merger, Dies at 85
abstract: She helped produce the Grove Atlantic publishing house, then oversaw prize winners as its executive editor.

name: Philip Lee
headline: Dr. Philip Lee Is Dead at 96; Engineered Introduction of Medicare
abstract: As a top health official for Lyndon Johnson and a fighter for social justice, he used government money as a cudgel to compel hospitals to desegregate in the ’60s.

name: Robert Fisk
headline: Robert Fisk, Intrepid War Correspondent, Dies at 74
abstract: “You cannot get near the truth without being there,” he said. Working for British newspapers, he ranged across the Middle East, Bosnia, Northern Ireland and elsewhere.

name: Betty Dodson
headline: Betty Dodson, Women’s Guru of Self-Pleasure, Dies at 91
abstract: She was a second-wave feminist who taught consciousness raising with a twist, and her workshops on masturbation, buoyed by the internet, have inspired millions.

name: Bobby Ball
profession: Half of a Hit British Comedy Duo
headline: Bobby Ball, Half of a Hit British Comedy Duo, Dies at 76
abstract: Their TV show “Cannon & Ball,” part goofy comedy and part earnest musical numbers, drew up to 20 million viewers on Saturday nights in the 1980s. Mr. Ball was infected with the coronavirus.

name: H. Jesse Arnelle
headline: H. Jesse Arnelle, Pathbreaker in Corporate Law, Dies at 86
abstract: Thirty years after he led the Penn State basketball team to the Final Four, he and a friend started one of the few Black-owned firms catering to blue-chip clients.

name: Johnny Meadows
profession: Pro Wrestler With a Tuneful Side
headline: Johnny Meadows, Pro Wrestler With a Tuneful Side, Dies at 59
abstract: John Condrone, as he was called in real life, left the ring for a different stage, becoming a songwriter and performer. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Helen Lachs Ginsburg
profession: Saw a Living Wage as a Right
headline: Helen Lachs Ginsburg, Who Saw a Living Wage as a Right, Dies at 91
abstract: A top authority on full employment, she said a job for all may seem unrealistic, but at one time so did the right of women to vote.

name: Wolman
headline: Baron Wolman, Whose Photos Helped Start Rolling Stone, Dies at 83
abstract: He was the magazine’s first photographer, capturing Frank Zappa, Janis Joplin, the Grateful Dead and many more in the days before image control.

name: Marylin Bender
headline: Marylin Bender Dies at 95; Journalist in a Male-Dominated Era
abstract: One of the few women with any editing authority at The Times, she felt resentment and, when asking for a raise, was told: “You’re married. You don’t need it.”

name: Arolde de Oliveira
headline: Arolde de Oliveira, Conservative Brazilian Senator, Dies at 83
abstract: Senator Oliveira, who had the support of evangelicals, played down the coronavirus before succumbing to it.

name: Tony Stempeck
headline: Tony Stempeck, Guardian of a Restaurant’s Legacy, Dies at 63
abstract: He spent much of his life training to run the venerable Nevada red-sauce joint founded by his grandparents. Weeks after taking over, he died of Covid-19.

name: Elsa Raven
profession: Back to the Future Character Actress
headline: Elsa Raven, ‘Back to the Future’ Character Actress, Dies at 91
abstract: She built a steady career of Everywoman roles. Perhaps none of them made a bigger impression than her performance as “Clocktower Lady.”

name: E.S. Reddy
headline: E.S. Reddy, Who Led U.N.’s Efforts Against Apartheid, Dies at 96
abstract: An Indian-born acolyte of Gandhi, he campaigned for boycotts, divestments and other protests against the South African government.

name: Gene Mater
headline: Gene Mater, Champion of Press Freedom, Dies at 93
abstract: As news director of Radio Free Europe, he saw the Berlin Wall go up and later worked for CBS and at the Newseum in Washington. He died in the pandemic.

name: Gigi Proietti
headline: Gigi Proietti, Actor Who Embodied the Roman Spirit, Dies at 80
abstract: Beloved in Italy, he was best known as the star of a TV series playing a small-town police chief. He also had a long film career and a popular one-man stage show.

name: Viola Smith
profession: Fastest Girl Drummer in the World
headline: Viola Smith, ‘Fastest Girl Drummer in the World,’ Dies at 107
abstract: She became a star as a percussionist and bandleader in the swing era. But her call for the big bands to hire women instrumentalists during World War II had little impact.

name: Eddie Johnson
headline: Eddie Johnson, N.B.A. Star Who Fell Into Crime, Dies at 65
abstract: Nicknamed Fast Eddie, he was an All-Star guard with the Atlanta Hawks. But he had drug problems, and after retiring he was convicted of sexual assault.

name: Marguerite Littman
headline: Marguerite Littman, the Inspiration for Holly Golightly, Dies at 90
abstract: She knew everyone, Truman Capote said. And she drew on her friends to contribute to her efforts in the fight against AIDS.

name: Robert Sam Anson
headline: Robert Sam Anson, ‘Bare-Knuckled’ Magazine Writer, Dies at 75
abstract: He covered wars, politics and brash, complicated men — like himself. His profile subjects included Oliver Stone, Tupac Shakur and David Geffen.

name: Seymour Topping
profession: Former Times Journalist and Eyewitness to History
headline: Seymour Topping, Former Times Journalist and Eyewitness to History, Dies at 98
abstract: He was one of the most accomplished foreign correspondents of his generation and a newsroom leader under the renowned executive editor A.M. Rosenthal.

name: Norm Crosby
headline: Norm Crosby, Comedian Who Had a (Wrong) Way With Words, Dies at 93
abstract: You might call him the Boston mangler. “I was doing everybody’s material,” he said, before discovering his own shtick and becoming the master of the malaprop.

name: Alex Trebek
headline: Alex Trebek, Longtime Host of ‘Jeopardy!,’ Dies at 80
abstract: A good host, he once said, could set his ego aside and let contestants be all they could be. But he let them know when he thought they missed easy answers.

name: Howie Meeker
headline: Howie Meeker, Hockey Star and Colorful Broadcaster, Dies at 97
abstract: Meeker was known for his candid remarks about players and the games. He came to television after a career as an All-Star for the Toronto Maple Leafs.

name: Dan Camp
headline: Dan Camp, Who Created a Mississippi Jewel, Dies at 79
abstract: He developed the trendy Cotton District from a run-down area next to Mississippi State, anticipating the New Urbanism movement. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Roger Ryman
headline: Roger Ryman, a ‘Real-Life’ Cowboy From Nebraska, Dies at 70
abstract: After working summers at the family ranch, he decided to saddle up as a job, turning to selling real estate later in life. He died of Covid-19.

name: Jonathan Sacks
headline: Jonathan Sacks, the U.K.’s Inclusive Former Chief Rabbi, Dies at 72
abstract: In writings and media appearances, he took a universalist view of religion in a multicultural world — a stance that could get him in hot water with conservatives.

name: Saeb Erekat
headline: Saeb Erekat, Palestinian Chief Negotiator Amid Turmoil, Dies at 65
abstract: A passionate champion of Palestinian statehood, his goal seemed to become less attainable with time. “I’m not finished with what I was born to do,” he said.

name: David Toole
profession: Disabled Dancer With Grace in His Hands
headline: David Toole, Disabled Dancer With Grace in His Hands, Dies at 56
abstract: He learned to dance expressively long after his legs were amputated. A premier disabled performer on stages around the world, he opened the 2012 London Paralympics.

name: Annie Feron
profession: Teacher and Host Mother to Foreign Students
headline: Annie Feron, Teacher and Host Mother to Foreign Students, Dies at 83
abstract: She left her home in Belgium and spent time in London as a young woman, then went on to foster a chain of foreign exchange student relationships that spanned generations. She died of Covid-19.

name: Tom Heinsohn
profession: Champion Celtic as Player and Coach
headline: Tom Heinsohn, Champion Celtic as Player and Coach, Is Dead at 86
abstract: His blood always ran green: eight titles with Boston as a Hall of Fame forward and two as head coach followed by a four-decade career as a die-hard Celtics broadcaster.

name: Amadou Toumani Touré
headline: Amadou Toumani Touré, Former Malian President, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Touré, who led Mali through a tumultuous transition from military rule in 1991, was the country’s second democratically chosen president. He was later ousted himself in a military coup.

name: Khalifa Bin Salman al-Khalifa
headline: Khalifa Bin Salman al-Khalifa, Leader of Bahrain’s Government, Dies at 84
abstract: During his tenure as the world’s longest-serving prime minister, he oversaw development in the Gulf kingdom, stood up for the monarchy and quashed dissent.

name: Israel Horovitz
headline: Israel Horovitz, Playwright Tarnished by Abuse Allegations, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Horovitz found success Off Broadway, working with actors who later became household names, but he was also accused by multiple women of a pattern of sexual misconduct and assault.

name: Natan Zach
headline: Natan Zach, Blunt and Cherished Israeli Poet, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Zach chafed at the formal structures and opaque Hebrew of poetry in the young Jewish state, and wrote in a looser and more direct language.

name: Sindika Dokolo
profession: Crusader for Return of African Art
headline: Sindika Dokolo, Crusader for Return of African Art, Dies at 48
abstract: He started a campaign to repatriate art stolen or removed during the colonial era. This year, he and his billionaire Angolan wife were embroiled in a corruption investigation.

name: Lucille Bridges
profession: Led Her Daughter Across a Color Line
headline: Lucille Bridges, 86, Dies; Led Her Daughter Across a Color Line
abstract: In 1960, Ms. Bridges escorted 6-year-old Ruby to an all-white school in New Orleans under the guard of federal marshals as protesters chanted and threw eggs.

name: Jerry Rawlings
headline: Jerry Rawlings, From Coup-Plotter to Ghanaian Statesman, Dies at 73
abstract: After leading the country with brutal crackdowns, he helped Ghana blossom into a stable democracy.

name: Anya Phillips
profession: Fashion Influencer in New Yorks Punk Scene
headline: Overlooked No More: Anya Phillips, Fashion Influencer in New York’s Punk Scene
abstract: She helped give pulse to the movement’s anti-establishment credo, dressing musicians like Debbie Harry of Blondie and James Chance and becoming a downtown “It girl.”

name: Aileen Passloff
headline: Aileen Passloff, Dancer, Choreographer and Teacher, Dies at 89
abstract: Ballet, modern, postmodern: She embraced all forms of dance, pushing students to find “the courage,” as one said, to know themselves through movement.

name: Pearl Chin
profession: Her Knitting Store Was a Haven and a Hub
headline: Pearl Chin Dies at 71; Her Knitting Store Was a Haven and a Hub
abstract: Knitty City was more than a Manhattan supply shop for yarn; it was an urban sanctuary and a springboard for social activism (or, as she and others called it, “craftivism”).

name: Rosanna Carteri
headline: Rosanna Carteri, Soprano Who Retired at Her Peak, Dies at 89
abstract: The graceful singer, celebrated in Verdi and Puccini, was only in her mid-30s when she left the stage to tend to her family.

name: David Easton
headline: David Easton, Architect for an American Gentry, Dies at 83
abstract: He was noted in the ’80s for his English-style manors, catering to an opulent clientele with a taste for grandeur.

name: Tom Metzger
headline: Tom Metzger, Notorious White Supremacist, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Metzger, a former Klansman and the founder of the White Aryan Resistance, was one of the most influential leaders of the white power movement.

name: Aldo Tambellini
headline: Aldo Tambellini, Avant-Garde Filmmaker and Video Artist, Dies at 90
abstract: A fixture of the Lower East Side’s ’60s art scene, he had an abiding interest in black. “‘Black,’” he wrote, “is not the opposite of white; it is a state of being.”

name: Peter Sutcliffe
profession: Murderer Known as the Yorkshire Ripper
headline: Peter Sutcliffe, Murderer Known as the ‘Yorkshire Ripper,’ Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Sutcliffe, who was convicted in 1981 in the deaths of 13 women and the attempted murders of seven more, had tested positive for the coronavirus, the authorities said.

name: Irvin Baxter
headline: Irvin Baxter, Who Preached the End Was Near, Dies at 75
abstract: He built a book, DVD and broadcasting business based on endtime prophecies he perceived in the Bible. He died of coronavirus, which he implied had been sent by God.

name: Paul Hornung
headline: Paul Hornung, Midcentury Football’s ‘Golden Boy,’ Is Dead at 84
abstract: His dazzling play at Notre Dame, a Hall of Fame Career with the Green Bay Packers, matinee-idol looks and a playboy image made him a national celebrity in the ’50s and ’60s.

name: Rance Allen
profession: Frontman of a New-Sounding Gospel Group
headline: Rance Allen, Frontman of a New-Sounding Gospel Group, Dies at 71
abstract: The Rance Allen Group was at the forefront of contemporary gospel, fusing traditional music with pop, rhythm and blues, jazz, even disco.

name: Lynn Kellogg
headline: Lynn Kellogg, Who Found the Spotlight in ‘Hair,’ Dies at 77
abstract: She had a leading role as a student protester in the original Broadway production. She died of Covid-19.

name: Lee Hyo-jae
profession: Champion of Womens Rights in South Korea
headline: Lee Hyo-jae, Champion of Women’s Rights in South Korea, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Lee was a prominent activist and a founder of women’s studies programs. She also stood up to the country’s dictators.

name: Joanna Harcourt-Smith
headline: Joanna Harcourt-Smith, 74, Dies; Lived a ‘Psychedelic Love Story’
abstract: For an adventurous globe-trotting time, she was by the side of the LSD guru Timothy Leary, only to be left traumatized by the experience.

name: Roger Jepsen
profession: Senator From Iowa and Reagan Ally
headline: Roger Jepsen, Senator From Iowa and Reagan Ally, Dies at 91
abstract: A voice for farmers, he lost a re-election bid after it was disclosed that he had joined a health spa that was shut down on prostitution charges.

name: Albert R. Jonsen
profession: Brought Medical Ethics to the Bedside
headline: Albert R. Jonsen, 89, Dies; Brought Medical Ethics to the Bedside
abstract: A former Jesuit priest and leader in bioethics, he believed that an ethicist should be part of a patient’s medical team when hard decisions have to be made.

name: David Andahl
headline: David Andahl, 55, Dies; Elected Posthumously in North Dakota
abstract: He caught Covid-19 as the virus surged across the state. How to fill his vacant seat in the state legislature remained in dispute.

name: Lindy McDaniel
headline: Lindy McDaniel, Ace Reliever for Mediocre Teams, Dies at 84
abstract: Over 21 seasons — including eight with the Cardinals and six with the Yankees — he was one of the game’s most dependable closers but never made the postseason.

name: Alexander Vedernikov
headline: Alexander Vedernikov, Conductor and Bolshoi Veteran, Dies at 56
abstract: A kinetic podium presence, he led performances at major opera houses and orchestras. He died of Covid-19.

name: Masatoshi Koshiba
headline: Masatoshi Koshiba, 94, Dies; Nobel Winner Tracked Ghostly Neutrinos
abstract: A physics teacher had flunked him, denigrating his abilities. Dr. Koshiba set out to prove the teacher was wrong.

name: Bruno Barbey
profession: Magnum Photographer of War and Peace
headline: Bruno Barbey, Magnum Photographer of War and Peace, Dies at 79
abstract: He was “a formidable visual architect” who captured the streets of Paris during the violent demonstrations in 1968 and documented the human experience in other parts of the world.

name: Eleanor Schano
headline: Eleanor Schano, Trailblazing Journalist in Pittsburgh, Dies at 88
abstract: Ms. Schano rose from “weather girl” to reporter to anchor in a series of firsts for the city, hiding three pregnancies along the way. She died of Covid-19.

name: Sheldon H. Solow
headline: Sheldon H. Solow, Manhattan Real Estate Mogul, Dies at 92
abstract: He built an empire from scratch, changing the skyline with high-end residential and office towers but leaving his crowning project unfinished.

name: Jill Paton Walsh
headline: Jill Paton Walsh, Multigenerational Writer, Dies at 83
abstract: Her books for young readers had won acclaim when, in 1994, one for adults made the Booker Prize shortlist — but only after she had resorted to publishing it herself.

name: Drew Days
profession: First Black Leader of Civil Rights Unit
headline: Drew Days, First Black Leader of Civil Rights Unit, Dies at 79
abstract: Born in the segregated South, Mr. Days, who later became solicitor general, knew from an early age that he wanted to work for civil rights.

name: LaTasha Benton
headline: LaTasha Benton, Who Pitched In Despite Obstacles, Dies at 43
abstract: She’d had strokes and two kidney transplants, but she remained active in social justice causes in Lexington, Ky. She died of the coronavirus.

name: François Catroux
headline: François Catroux, Decorator of Choice for Aristocrats, Dies at 83
abstract: Along with his wife, a muse of Yves Saint Laurent, he was at the center of Paris’s glittering 1970s-era social scene, where art, style and money collided.

name: Frederick Weston
headline: Frederick Weston, Outsider Artist Who Was Finally Let In, Dies at 73
abstract: For decades he made his art in dingy Manhattan hotel rooms, living hand-to-mouth, hoping for his big break. It finally arrived, just a few years before his death.

name: Archie Spigner
headline: Archie Spigner, ‘Godfather of Politics’ in Queens, Dies at 92
abstract: He launched the careers of fellow Black leaders and was a force on the New York City Council for decades, focusing on his home turf.

name: Ken Spears
headline: Ken Spears, Partner in an Animation Powerhouse, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Spears and Joe Ruby were best known for “Scooby-Doo, Where Are You!,” perhaps the most spun-off series in the history of television.

name: José Luiz da Silva
headline: José Luiz da Silva, Brazilian Social Media Star, Dies at 52
abstract: He acquired more than a million followers on Instagram and appeared in commercials and music videos and on TV variety shows. He died of Covid-19.

name: Nancy Darsch
headline: Nancy Darsch, Champion Coach of Women’s Basketball, Dies at 68
abstract: Darsch turned Ohio State into a powerhouse, helped two U.S. teams win Olympic gold and was one of the original coaches in the W.N.B.A., leading the New York Liberty.

name: Jan Myrdal
headline: Jan Myrdal, Swedish Author and Provocateur, Dies at 93
abstract: His father and mother were both Nobel winners. His most famous book was about how badly they had treated him.

name: Margaret Guilfoyle
headline: Margaret Guilfoyle, a Multiple ‘First’ in Australia Politics, Dies at 94
abstract: As a cabinet member from 1975 to 1983, she was the first woman to run an Australian government department. Her country’s news media called her “a mother with political ambitions.”

name: Soumitra Chatterjee
headline: Soumitra Chatterjee, Globally Acclaimed Indian Film Star, Dies at 85
abstract: His roles in classic movies directed by Satyajit Ray won him admiration from cinephiles and made him a hero to his fellow Bengalis.

name: Jan Morris
profession: Celebrated Writer of Place and History
headline: Jan Morris, Celebrated Writer of Place and History, Is Dead at 94
abstract: In more than four dozen books, Morris explored foreign lands, her own Britain and her experience as a transgender woman.

name: Gianni Bernardinello
headline: Gianni Bernardinello, Baker Who Fed Neighbors Amid Pandemic, Dies at 76
abstract: The Milanese baker would leave out baskets of bread for people hit hard economically by the coronavirus pandemic. Now the disease has claimed his life.

name: Andrew White
headline: Andrew White, Virtuoso Saxophonist and Coltrane Scholar, Dies at 78
abstract: A man of, in his words, “various artistic gifts of excess,” he amassed a trove of self-released recordings, books and musical transcriptions.

name: Tracey Davis
profession: Chronicler of Ups and Downs With Her Famous Father
headline: Tracey Davis, Chronicler of Ups and Downs With Her Famous Father, Dies at 59
abstract: In two books, she described Sammy Davis Jr.’s negligent parenting but also celebrated the intimate moments she shared with him toward the end of his life.

name: Len Barry
profession: Soulful Voice of Bristol Stomp and 1-2-3
headline: Len Barry, 78, Dies; Soulful Voice of ‘Bristol Stomp’ and ‘1-2-3’
abstract: He had success as the lead singer of the Dovells and later as a solo artist. But he was always a reluctant performer, most comfortable as a songwriter and producer.

name: Fred Hills
profession: Editor of Nabokov and Many Others
headline: Fred Hills, Editor of Nabokov and Many Others, Dies at 85
abstract: A longtime editor at Simon & Schuster, he brought to market both commercial hits and literary prizewinners and edited more than 50 New York Times best sellers.

name: Nelly Kaplan
headline: Nelly Kaplan, Whose Films Explored Female Strength, Dies at 89
abstract: An Argentine who relocated to France, she drew acclaim with “A Very Curious Girl” and other films about female characters who empowered themselves.

name: Arthur Imperatore
profession: Founder of a Critical Ferry Service
headline: Arthur Imperatore, Founder of a Critical Ferry Service, Dies at 95
abstract: He steered New York Waterway through financial straits. He also reveled in moments of glory, notably when his boats rode to the rescue on Sept. 11, 2001.

name: Cándido Camero
headline: Cándido Camero, Conga Master Who Transformed Jazz, Dies at 99
abstract: He brought Afro-Cuban influences to American ensembles and dazzled audiences with his virtuosic multiple-drum technique.

name: Bruce Swedien
headline: Bruce Swedien, a Shaper of Michael Jackson’s Sound, Dies at 86
abstract: In more than 60 years as a recording engineer, he worked with a wide range of artists. His most notable collaboration was with Mr. Jackson and the producer Quincy Jones.

name: Jake Scott
profession: Super Bowl M.V.P. for the Dolphins
headline: Jake Scott, Super Bowl M.V.P. for the Dolphins, Dies at 75
abstract: A fearless defender, he had 35 interceptions in six seasons in Miami and was named to five consecutive Pro Bowls in the 1970s.

name: Daniel Cordier
headline: Daniel Cordier, French Resistance Hero, Is Dead at 100
abstract: He parachuted into occupied France and became an assistant to the legendary Jean Moulin, though only later did he learn Moulin’s true identity.

name: Eric Hall
headline: Eric Hall, Extravagant British Soccer Agent, Dies at 73
abstract: After promoting bands like Queen and the Sex Pistols, Mr. Hall became one of the most colorful agents in England’s Premier League. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Elizabeth Anson
headline: Lady Elizabeth Anson, Party Planner to the Royals, Dies at 79
abstract: A daughter of British nobility, she knew instinctively how to make guests comfortable, the queen among them and even that table of dreadful bores.

name: David N. Dinkins
headline: David N. Dinkins, New York’s First Black Mayor, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Dinkins, who served in the early 1990s, was seen as a compromise selection for voters weary of racial unrest, crime and fiscal turmoil. The racial harmony he sought remained elusive during his years in office.

name: David Maas
profession: Half of Quick Change Magic Act
headline: David Maas, Half of ‘Quick Change’ Magic Act, Dies of Covid-19
abstract: Mr. Maas and his wife, who performed lightning-fast costume changes, often appeared on television and were a halftime fixture at N.B.A. and college basketball arenas.

name: Honestie Hodges
headline: Honestie Hodges, Whose Handcuffing Changed Police Policy, Is Dead at 14
abstract: Honestie’s handcuffing by the police in Grand Rapids, Mich., caused a national uproar and led to a new law enforcement policy on dealing with youths. Honestie died of Covid-19.

name: Priscilla Jana
headline: Priscilla Jana, Lawyer Who Battled Apartheid, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Representing Nelson and Winnie Mandela among many others, Ms. Jana fought for equality in South Africa both in and out of the courtroom.

name: Diego Maradona
headline: Diego Maradona, One of Soccer’s Greatest Players, Is Dead at 60
abstract: He was ranked with Pelé among the best, and his ability to surprise and startle won over fans and even critics. But his excesses and addictions darkened his legacy.

name: Ian Finkel
headline: Ian Finkel, ‘World’s Greatest Xylophonist,’ Dies at 72
abstract: He entertained from the borscht belt to the Philharmonic, playing an unconventional instrument with vaudevillian flair. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Dena Dietrich
profession: Found TV Fame as Mother Nature
headline: Dena Dietrich, Who Found TV Fame as Mother Nature, Dies at 91
abstract: In a long acting career she was best known for wreaking havoc in a series of margarine commercials, warning, “It’s not nice to fool Mother Nature.”

name: Edward P. Lazear
headline: Edward P. Lazear, Economist and Presidential Adviser, Dies at 72
abstract: He was a widely respected labor economist at Stanford who led President George W. Bush’s economic council during the financial crisis.

name: James D. Wolfensohn
profession: Led the World Bank for 10 Years
headline: James D. Wolfensohn, Who Led the World Bank for 10 Years, Dies at 86
abstract: He was a force on Wall Street before taking the reins of the bank in 1995, then proceeded to shake it up. He did the same at both Carnegie Hall and the Kennedy Center.

name: Betty Jones
headline: Betty Jones, Founding Member of Limón Troupe, Dies at 94
abstract: She created the Desdemona role in José Limón’s best-known dance, “The Moor’s Pavane,” and became a respected teacher.

name: Edward J. Perkins
profession: First Black U.S. Envoy to South Africa
headline: Edward J. Perkins, 92, Dies; First Black U.S. Envoy to South Africa
abstract: He also held ambassadorial postings in Liberia and Australia and, as director general, helped diversify the elite, mostly white Foreign Service.

name: Paolo Gabriele
headline: Paolo Gabriele, Pope’s Butler in ‘Vatileaks’ Scandal, Dies at 54
abstract: He admitted to stealing files and giving them to a journalist as a way to expose Vatican corruption and protect his boss, Benedict XVI.

name: Mary Fowkes
headline: Dr. Mary Fowkes, 66, Dies; Helped Science Understand the Pandemic
abstract: She performed autopsies in New York that found blood clots in vital organs, suggesting how much the virus spreads through the body.

name: Geoffrey Palmer
headline: Geoffrey Palmer, Judi Dench’s Sitcom Co-Star, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Their show “As Time Goes By” was a hit in Britain and had a following in the U.S. “When you acted with him,” Ms. Dench said, “you’d just feel very safe.”

name: Leonard Kamsler
headline: Leonard Kamsler, a Dissecting Golf Photographer, Dies at 85
abstract: He pioneered the use of strobe photography to break down a golfer’s swing. He was also innovative, even crafty, in documenting P.G.A. tournaments for decades.

name: Debra White Plume
headline: Debra White Plume, Defender of Her Tribe, Is Dead at 66
abstract: She championed the rights of the Oglala Lakota in South Dakota and was a leader in protests at Wounded Knee and oil pipeline sites.

name: Bruce Boynton
profession: Plaintiff in Landmark Civil Rights Case
headline: Bruce Boynton, Plaintiff in Landmark Civil Rights Case, Dies at 83
abstract: He was a Black man who wanted to sit in the white section of a bus terminal restaurant. The case reached the Supreme Court.

name: Tony Hsieh
headline: Tony Hsieh, Longtime Chief of Zappos, Is Dead at 46
abstract: In the early days of online retailing, he realized that the key to success was making people feel comfortable and secure shopping on the internet.

name: Dave Prowse
headline: Dave Prowse, Man Behind Darth Vader’s Mask, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Prowse went from being a weight lifting champion in Britain to helping portray one of the most memorable villains in movie history. But his voice did not make the edit.

name: Georgina Mace
headline: Georgina Mace, Who Shaped List of Endangered Species, Dies at 67
abstract: She rewrote the global Red List, which describes which species are in trouble, and warned that the world must restore its ecological balance or pay a steep price.

name: Rafer Johnson
headline: Rafer Johnson, Winner of a Memorable Decathlon, Is Dead
abstract: His triumphant performance at the 1960 Olympics was his farewell to track and field. He went on to become a good-will ambassador for the United States and a close associate of the Kennedy family.

name: Raja Mukhopadhyay
headline: Raja Mukhopadhyay, Poetry-Loving Police Officer, Dies at 50
abstract: His career was in the police force but his true passion was Bengali poetry. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Valéry Giscard d’Estaing
headline: Valéry Giscard d’Estaing, 94, Is Dead; Struggled to Transform France
abstract: As a conservative president, he sought to make government more responsive to the people but was thwarted by an economic slowdown, demographic shifts and an imperious bearing. He died of Covid-19.

name: Hamish MacInnes
headline: Hamish MacInnes, Scotland’s Man of the Mountains, Dies at 90
abstract: He scaled dangerous peaks all over the world. He also modernized rescue techniques that helped save countless lives.

name: Miguel Algarín
headline: Miguel Algarín, Force Behind Nuyorican Cafe, Dies at 79
abstract: His Lower East Side performance space has been an incubator for poets, playwrights and other artists, many of them not initially embraced by the mainstream.

name: Judith Jarvis Thomson
headline: Judith Jarvis Thomson, Philosopher Who Defended Abortion, Dies at 91
abstract: She wrote some of the most influential papers in contemporary American philosophy and prompted debates about urgent moral concerns in everyday life.

name: Alison Lurie
headline: Alison Lurie, Tart-Voiced Novelist of Manners, Dies at 94
abstract: Ms. Lurie wrote about academics and intellectuals, straying spouses, snobs and artists, in novels of close observation and sharp prose.

name: Lon Adams
profession: Gave the Slim Jim Its Flavor
headline: Lon Adams, Who Gave the Slim Jim Its Flavor, Dies at 95
abstract: Mr. Adams spent a quarter-century developing and refining the recipe for the beef jerky snack. He died of complications of Covid-19

name: Betsy Wade
profession: First Woman to Edit News at The Times
headline: Betsy Wade, First Woman to Edit News at The Times, Dies at 91
abstract: In a 45-year Times career, she also became the first woman to lead the Newspaper Guild of New York and fought a sex discrimination case against the paper.

name: Barbara Waxman Fiduccia
headline: Overlooked No More: Barbara Waxman Fiduccia, Reproductive Rights Advocate
abstract: A sexual health educator and counselor in Los Angeles, she challenged a dominant culture that viewed people with disabilities as asexual beings.

name: Frank Carney
headline: Frank Carney, Co-Founder of Pizza Hut, Dies at 82
abstract: When he was 19, Mr. Carney and his brother Dan borrowed $600 from their mother to start their business in Wichita, Kan. Before long it became the world’s largest pizza chain.

name: Irina Antonova
profession: Grande Dame of Russian Museum World
headline: Irina Antonova, Grande Dame of Russian Museum World, Dies at 98
abstract: During her decades-long reign at Moscow’s main fine arts museum, she provided a window on the outside world for the Soviet people. She died of complications of the coronavirus.

name: Fernando Solanas
headline: Fernando Solanas, Argentine Filmmaker and Politician, Dies at 84
abstract: He helped propel a new wave of politically charged moviemaking and served as a lawmaker. He died of complications of the coronavirus.

name: Naomi Long Madgett
headline: Naomi Long Madgett, Champion of Black Poets, Is Dead at 97
abstract: The longtime poet laureate of Detroit, she was as well known for publishing the work of others as she was for her own verse.

name: Walter E. Williams
headline: Walter E. Williams, 84, Dies; Conservative Economist on Black Issues
abstract: Skeptical of antipoverty programs, he was a scholar who reached a wide public through a newspaper column and books, and as a fill-in for Rush Limbaugh.

name: Cliff Joseph
headline: Cliff Joseph, Artist, Activist and Therapist, Dies at 98
abstract: After agitating for the inclusion of Black artists in New York museums, he helped introduce a multicultural perspective to the field of art therapy.

name: William Aronwald
profession: Target of a Botched Mob Hit
headline: William Aronwald, Target of a Botched Mob Hit, Dies at 79
abstract: He was a prominent prosecutor in the 1970s. A blunder by hit men left his father dead.

name: Suhaila Siddiq
headline: Suhaila Siddiq, Afghanistan’s First Female General, Is Dead
abstract: Also a renowned surgeon, she rose through the ranks of the Afghan Army and practiced medicine during the Soviet invasion and the Afghan civil war and under the Taliban’s rule.

name: Fred Sasakamoose
profession: One of the First Indigenous N.H.L. Players
headline: Fred Sasakamoose, One of the First Indigenous N.H.L. Players, Dies at 86
abstract: He played only 11 games in hockey’s top league, but he inspired generations of athletes from Canada’s First Nations. He died after suffering complications of the coronavirus.

name: Pamela Tiffin
headline: Pamela Tiffin, Movie Star Who Shone Brightly but Briefly, Dies at 78
abstract: Billy Wilder called her “the greatest film discovery since Audrey Hepburn,” and she made an immediate splash in two 1961 movies, when she was only 19.

name: David L. Lander
headline: David L. Lander, Squiggy on ‘Laverne & Shirley,’ Dies at 73
abstract: He appeared in more than 100 movies and TV projects, but was best known for his seven-year run on the popular 1970s sitcom.

name: Paul Sarbanes
headline: Paul Sarbanes, 87, Dies; Maryland Senator Fought Accounting Fraud
abstract: Early in his career, he introduced the first article of impeachment against Richard Nixon. Decades later, he co-wrote legislation in response to corporate scandals.

name: Pat Patterson
headline: Pat Patterson, a Wrestling Star Who Came Out, Dies at 79
abstract: He delighted his fans, especially in villain roles. When he announced in 2014 that he was gay, they remained loyal.

name: Elizabeth J. McCormack
headline: Elizabeth J. McCormack, Innovative Educator, Dies at 98
abstract: A former nun, she transformed Manhattanville College as its president before becoming a philanthropic adviser to major foundations and the Rockefellers.

name: Dick Allen
headline: Dick Allen, 78, Dies; Baseball Slugger Withstood Bigotry
abstract: One of the game’s best and most honored players in the 1960s and into the ’70s, he nevertheless felt racism’s sting early in his career in Philadelphia.

name: Chuck Yeager
headline: Chuck Yeager, Test Pilot Who Broke the Sound Barrier, Is Dead at 97
abstract: A World War II fighter ace and Air Force general, he was, according to Tom Wolfe, “the most righteous of all the possessors of the right stuff.”

name: Natalie Desselle
profession: Comedic Heart of BAPS and Eve
headline: Natalie Desselle, Comedic Heart of ‘BAPS’ and ‘Eve,’ Dies at 53
abstract: Her role as Halle Berry’s uproarious stardom-seeking sidekick helped define a decades-long career in film and TV.

name: Wilbert Robertson
headline: Rev. Wilbert Robertson, Native American Pastor, Dies at 86
abstract: A veteran of the Korean and Vietnam wars, he established Baptist congregations in the Dakotas. He died of Covid-19.

name: Tabaré Vázquez
headline: Tabaré Vázquez, Former President of Uruguay, Dies at 80
abstract: Dr. Vazquez was also a practicing physician who specialized in oncology and pushed some of the toughest anti-tobacco rules in the region.

name: Doug Scott
profession: Part of First Team to Summit Everest by Southwest Face
headline: Doug Scott, Part of First Team to Summit Everest by Southwest Face, Dies at 79
abstract: In recent decades, Mr. Scott directed and raised funds for Community Action Nepal, a charity he founded to improve the lives of people in Nepal.

name: Camilla Wicks
profession: Dazzling Violinist From a Young Age
headline: Camilla Wicks, Dazzling Violinist From a Young Age, Dies at 92
abstract: She was a rare female soloist in a male-dominated era, but cut back on performing to raise her children.

name: Helen LaFrance
headline: Helen LaFrance, Folk Artist of Rural Kentucky, Dies at 101
abstract: Her vibrant “memory paintings,” which drew comparisons to the work of Grandma Moses and other regional artists, brought her renown late in life.

name: Guido Goldman
headline: Guido Goldman, a U.S. Bridge to Germany, Dies at 83
abstract: A Kissinger protégé (and a pre-eminent textile art collector), his fingerprints can be found on many of the leading postwar institutions linking the two allies.

name: Lorraine Millar
profession: Resilient in the Face of Tragedy
headline: Lorraine Millar, Resilient in the Face of Tragedy, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Millar persevered through a series of deaths in her family, succeeding in multiple careers and finding joy in life. She died of Covid-19.

name: Sara Leland
headline: Sara Leland, Ballerina of Passion and Abandon, Dies at 79
abstract: She was a favorite of George Balanchine at New York City Ballet and staged his ballets worldwide even during her performing career.

name: Ray Perkins
profession: Coach at Alabama and in the N.F.L
headline: Ray Perkins, Coach at Alabama and in the N.F.L., Dies at 79
abstract: With the Crimson Tide, he had a tough act to follow, Bear Bryant, but he enjoyed some success. He didn’t fare so well with the Giants and the Buccaneers.

name: Arnie Robinson Jr.
headline: Arnie Robinson Jr., Olympic Long Jump Champion, Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Robinson won the gold medal at the 1976 Summer Olympics in Montreal and a bronze medal in Munich in 1972.

name: Lillian Blancas
headline: Lillian Blancas, Candidate for a Texas Judgeship, Dies at 47
abstract: Ms. Blancas, a widely respected lawyer, died days before a runoff election in El Paso but remained on the ballot and won. She died of Covid-19.

name: Deb Price
profession: First as a Columnist on Gay Life
headline: Deb Price, a First as a Columnist on Gay Life, Dies at 62
abstract: If she wrote for mainstream Americans about same-sex couples in everyday situations, she thought, society would have a harder time denying them equal rights.

name: Phil Linz
headline: Phil Linz, Unlikely Baseball Celebrity, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Never a star and rarely a starter as a Yankee in the 1960s, Linz made news not for playing baseball but for playing the harmonica.

name: Norman Abramson
headline: Norman Abramson, Pioneer Behind Wireless Networks, Dies at 88
abstract: His ALOHAnet, designed a half-century ago in Hawaii, was a precursor to the technology used in today’s smartphones and home WiFi networks.

name: Brittanya Karma
headline: Brittanya Karma, German-Vietnamese Social Media Star, Dies at 29
abstract: She used her social media clout to preach and model self-confidence. She died of complications of Covid-19 in a Hamburg hospital.

name: Tommy Lister
headline: Tommy Lister, Actor Who Menaced as Deebo in ‘Friday,’ Is Dead at 62
abstract: The actor was found dead in his California home on Thursday after friends and business associates could not reach him, the authorities said.

name: Othella Dallas
headline: Othella Dallas, Keeper of Katherine Dunham’s Flame, Dies at 95
abstract: Ms. Dallas taught the Afro-Caribbean-influenced Dunham dance technique in Europe well into her 90s. She also had a career as a blues, jazz and R&B singer.

name: Charley Pride
headline: Charley Pride, Country Music’s First Black Superstar, Dies at 86
abstract: He began his career amid the racial unrest of the 1960s and cemented his place in the country pantheon with hits like “Kiss an Angel Good Mornin’.”

name: Noah Creshevsky
headline: Noah Creshevsky, Composer of ‘Hyperreal’ Music, Dies at 75
abstract: He built his musical works from myriad sampled sounds, including noises from the street as well as voices and instruments. He was also a respected teacher.

name: Jerrold M. Post
headline: Jerrold M. Post, Specialist in Political Psychology, Dies at 86
abstract: He invented the field at the C.I.A., producing influential “psychobiographies” of world leaders. He later used the same methods to analyze Donald Trump.

name: Lawrence Byrne
profession: Former Lawyer for New York Police
headline: Lawrence Byrne, Former Lawyer for New York Police, Dies at 61
abstract: His younger brother, a police officer, was assassinated by a drug gang at 22, a key moment in the city’s crack epidemic of the 1980s.

name: Ben Bova
headline: Ben Bova, Science Fiction Editor and Author, Is Dead at 88
abstract: As editor of the magazines Analog and Omni, he was a champion of a new generation of authors, including George R.R. Martin.

name: Alex Olmedo
profession: Tennis Star Known for a Remarkable Year
headline: Alex Olmedo, 84, Dies; Tennis Star Known for a Remarkable Year
abstract: In 1959, Olmedo won the Australian and Wimbledon men’s single championships and reached the final of the United States Nationals.

name: Anthony Veasna So
profession: Author on the Brink of Stardom
headline: Anthony Veasna So, Author on the Brink of Stardom, Dies at 28
abstract: His darkly comedic stories explored the experiences of Cambodian-Americans. His first book, the subject of a bidding war, is to be published next August.

name: John le Carré
profession: Best-Selling Author of Cold War Thrillers
headline: John le Carré, Best-Selling Author of Cold War Thrillers, Dies at 89
abstract: Breaking from the James Bond mold, he turned the spy novel into high art as he explored the moral compromises of agents on both sides of the Iron curtain.

name: Lidia Menapace
headline: Lidia Menapace, Who Fought Fascists and Sexists, Dies at 96
abstract: She was a partisan in northern Italy during World War II and denounced efforts to discount the role of women in the Resistance. She had been hospitalized with Covid-19.

name: Carol Sutton
profession: Stage and Screen Actress Devoted to New Orleans
headline: Carol Sutton, a Stage and Screen Actress Devoted to New Orleans, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Sutton brought characters to life on the stage, on television and in movies like “Steel Magnolias.” She also mentored young people in her local theater community. She died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Ann Reinking
profession: Dancer, Actor, Choreographer and Fosse Muse
headline: Ann Reinking Dies at 71; Dancer, Actor, Choreographer and Fosse Muse
abstract: From the ensembles of “Cabaret” and “Pippin,” she stepped into the role of Roxie Hart in “Chicago,” and the rest is Tony-winning history.

name: Carlos Araujo Preza
profession: Doctor on the Pandemics Front Lines
headline: Carlos Araujo Preza, Doctor on the Pandemic’s Front Lines, Dies at 51
abstract: A pulmonologist, he tested positive for Covid-19 and was treated at the same hospital where he once saw patients. He died of the disease.

name: Richard Hinch
headline: Richard Hinch, Speaker of New Hampshire House, Dies at 71
abstract: A Republican, he had a staunchly conservative agenda as his party took control of the state government in the November election. He died of Covid-19.

name: Jack Steinberger
headline: Jack Steinberger, Nobel Winner in Physics, Dies at 99
abstract: Dr. Steinberger shared the prize in 1988 for expanding understanding of the neutrino, a staggeringly ubiquitous subatomic particle.

name: Joseph Safra
headline: Joseph Safra, Banker Who Was the Richest Brazilian, Dies at 82
abstract: An immigrant from Lebanon, he earned a reputation as a canny dealmaker overseeing a family banking empire reaching from São Paulo to Geneva to New York.

name: Dorothy Gill Barnes
headline: Dorothy Gill Barnes, 93, Artist Whose Raw Material Came From Trees, Dies
abstract: She created works from bark, wood and roots, sometimes carving patterns into trees and waiting years to see the scarring. She died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Harold Budd
headline: Harold Budd, Composer of Spaciousness and Calm, Dies at 84
abstract: Known for his collaborations with art-pop artists like Brian Eno and Cocteau Twins, he created a signature sound suspended in reverberation and drone.

name: Kim Ki-duk
headline: Kim Ki-duk, Award-Winning South Korean Filmmaker, Dies at 59
abstract: He was celebrated for movies centered on society’s underbelly, but he was later accused of sexual misconduct. He died of Covid-19.

name: Takashi Oka
headline: Takashi Oka, Journalist Who Interpreted Japan for U.S., Dies at 96
abstract: A former war crimes trial interpreter, he was the first native-born Tokyo bureau chief for The New York Times and a longtime correspondent for The Christian Science Monitor.

name: Jeremy Bulloch
profession: Played Boba Fett in Star Wars Movies
headline: Jeremy Bulloch, 75, Dies; Played Boba Fett in ‘Star Wars’ Movies
abstract: Mr. Bulloch said he based his performance as the menacing bounty hunter in part on Clint Eastwood’s performance as a laconic gunslinger.

name: Benny Napoleon
profession: Michigan Sheriff and Ex-Detroit Police Chief
headline: Benny Napoleon, Michigan Sheriff and Ex-Detroit Police Chief, Dies at 65
abstract: Sheriff Napoleon served for more than a decade in the Michigan county that includes Detroit, and ran unsuccessfully for the city’s mayor.

name: Ralph K. Winter Jr.
headline: Ralph K. Winter Jr., a Top Conservative Judicial Mind, Dies at 85
abstract: As a scholar and a federal appellate judge, he changed the shape of laws on campaign finance and corporate governance.

name: Clarice Lispector
headline: Overlooked No More: Clarice Lispector, Novelist Who Captivated Brazil
abstract: Critics lauded her stream-of-consciousness style and described her as glamorous and mysterious. But she didn’t always welcome the attention she received.

name: Barbara Windsor
profession: Beloved British TV and Film Star
headline: Barbara Windsor, Beloved British TV and Film Star, Dies at 83
abstract: She went from bubbly sex symbol in the “Carry On” films to working-class hero on “EastEnders.” Her private life was often as troubled as her “EastEnders” character’s.

name: Karen Killilea
headline: Karen Killilea, 80, Dies; Turned Disability Into Triumph
abstract: She refused to be limited by her cerebral palsy. Her story was the subject of two widely read books and became an inspiration to many.

name: Henry Haller
headline: Henry Haller, Chef for Five Presidents, Dies at 97
abstract: He had the high-level skills necessary for the job but also a welcome flexibility, allowing him to thrive in the, well, pressure-cooker that is the White House.

name: Jean Graetz
profession: White Supporter of Civil Rights in Alabama
headline: Jean Graetz, White Supporter of Civil Rights in Alabama, Dies at 90
abstract: With her husband, Robert, Mrs. Graetz became a friend of Rosa Parks and supported the Montgomery bus boycott, despite threats to her life.

name: Grace Knowlton
headline: Grace Knowlton, Sculptor Who Worked ‘in the Round,’ Dies at 88
abstract: A rare female modernist who broke into the masculine culture of outdoor sculpting, she exhibited her spheres at top museums and galleries.

name: Catie Lazarus
profession: Comedian With a Lot of Questions
headline: Catie Lazarus, Comedian With a Lot of Questions, Dies at 44
abstract: On her live show “Employee of the Month,” she got laughs by interrogating writers, artists, politicians, intellectuals and her fellow comics.

name: Stanley Cowell
profession: Jazz Pianist With a Wide Range
headline: Stanley Cowell, Jazz Pianist With a Wide Range, Dies at 79
abstract: His playing consolidated generations of musical history. He was also a composer, an educator and the founder of an important artist-run record label.

name: Rosendo Mendoza
headline: Rosendo and Rogelio Mendoza, Twins and Texas Welders, Die at 56
abstract: The Mendoza brothers, identical twins who worked together, died of complications of Covid-19 on the same day.

name: Rogelio Mendoza
headline: Rosendo and Rogelio Mendoza, Twins and Texas Welders, Die at 56
abstract: The Mendoza brothers, identical twins who worked together, died of complications of Covid-19 on the same day.

name: William Winter
headline: William Winter, Reform-Minded Mississippi Governor, Dies at 97
abstract: In his single term, he fought to improve his state’s education system. He later threw himself into civil rights work.

name: K.T. Oslin
headline: K.T. Oslin, Country Singer Known for ‘80’s Ladies,’ Dies at 78
abstract: Her song, the first of many hits, heralded the arrival of a songwriting voice whose sharply drawn miniatures conveyed domestic humor and pathos.

name: Chad Stuart
headline: Chad Stuart, of the Hit British Duo Chad & Jeremy, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Stuart’s wistful tunes of summer romance brought him and Jeremy Clyde an intense but brief burst of stardom during the British Invasion of the 1960s.

name: Kevin Greene
headline: Kevin Greene, Master of Sacking the Quarterback, Dies at 58
abstract: A charismatic player with seemingly inexhaustible energy, he recorded the third-most sacks in N.F.L. history and the most by a linebacker.

name: Jose Garcia
headline: Jose Garcia, New Mexico Farmworker, Dies at 68
abstract: One of Mr. Garcia’s nine children, a nurse at the hospital in Las Cruces where he died, was the only family member allowed to visit with him as he battled Covid-19.

name: Ezra F. Vogel
profession: Eminent Scholar of China and Japan
headline: Ezra F. Vogel, Eminent Scholar of China and Japan, Dies at 90
abstract: A longtime scholar at Harvard, Professor Vogel wrote books that helped shape how the world viewed the two ascendant economic powers.

name: Rebecca Luker
headline: Rebecca Luker, a Broadway Star for Three Decades, Dies at 59
abstract: Her Broadway career, fueled by her crystal-clear operatic soprano, brought her Tony Award nominations for “Show Boat,” “The Music Man” and “Mary Poppins.”

name: Virginia Shackles
headline: Virginia Shackles, Painter of Vivid Scenery, Dies at 99
abstract: Ms. Shackles loved to paint cliffs and ocean scenes in the coastal city of Monterey, Calif. She died of complications from Covid-19.

name: Jack Lenor Larsen
headline: Jack Lenor Larsen, Innovative Textile Designer, Dies at 93
abstract: He blended ancient techniques and modern technology to weave fabrics that are in the collections of MoMA and the Louvre, which gave him a one-man retrospective.

name: ‘Blue’ Gene Tyranny
headline: ‘Blue’ Gene Tyranny, Whose Music Melded Genres, Dies at 75
abstract: A creator of modern music as a teenager, he later juggled a breezy pop sensibility with conceptual rigor. He was an important collaborator with the composer Robert Ashley.

name: Stella Tennant
headline: Stella Tennant, Aristocratic British Model, Is Dead at 50
abstract: Noble lineage, classic beauty and punk attitude combined in a model who stood at fashion’s apex for three decades.

name: Leslie West
headline: Leslie West, ‘Mississippi Queen’ Rocker, Is Dead at 75
abstract: He rose to fame with Mountain, which Rolling Stone called a “louder version of Cream” — a band Mr. West idolized. One of the group’s first gigs was Woodstock.

name: Roger Berlind
headline: Roger Berlind, 90, Dies; Broadway Impresario Who Amassed 25 Tonys
abstract: He played a role in producing more than 100 plays and musicals. And while he kept an eye on the bottom line, he could be seduced by sheer artistry.

name: Jeannie Morris
headline: Jeannie Morris, Trailblazing Chicago Sportscaster, Dies at 85
abstract: She was a rare woman in broadcast sports journalism when she began her career in the late 1960s, but she helped pave the way for the many women who followed.

name: Minoru Makihara
headline: Minoru Makihara, Who Ran Mitsubishi After It Stumbled, Dies at 90
abstract: He steered the company, then the world’s largest, through the troubles of a collapsing economy, and dedicated himself to improving relations with the U.S.

name: Nancye Radmin
headline: Nancye Radmin, Pioneer of Plus-Size Fashion, Is Dead at 82
abstract: The Forgotten Woman boutique, which she opened in 1977, spoke directly to the nascent idea of body acceptance. It soon became a chain.

name: Robert Thacker
profession: Survived Pearl Harbor to Fly in 3 Wars
headline: Robert Thacker, 102, Dies; Survived Pearl Harbor to Fly in 3 Wars
abstract: His unarmed bomber was caught in the thick of Japan’s attack. He went on to fly some 80 missions in World War II and to become a record-setting test pilot.

name: George Blake
headline: George Blake, British Spy Who Betrayed the West, Dies at 98
abstract: He was caught spilling secrets to the Soviets in 1961 and imprisoned. Five years later, he escaped and fled to Moscow, where he was hailed as a hero.

name: Fanny Waterman
profession: Doyenne of the Leeds Piano Competition
headline: Fanny Waterman, Doyenne of the Leeds Piano Competition, Dies at 100
abstract: A British pianist and teacher, she helped establish one of the world’s most important piano showcases and then presided over it for decades.

name: Michael Alig
profession: Fixture of New York City Nightlife
headline: Michael Alig, Fixture of New York City Nightlife, Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Alig, who gained fame in the 1980s as a party promoter, was a tabloid celebrity who served 17 years in prison for manslaughter.

name: John Fletcher
profession: a.k.a. Ecstasy of the Group Whodini
headline: John Fletcher, a.k.a. Ecstasy of the Group Whodini, Dies at 56
abstract: He was, the executive who signed Whodini said, “truly one of the first rap stars” and a sex symbol “when they were very scarce in the early days of rap.”

name: Barry Lopez
headline: Barry Lopez, Lyrical Writer Who Was Likened to Thoreau, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Lopez spent five years in the Arctic, and his books, essays and short stories explored the kinship of nature and human culture.

name: Reginald Foster
headline: Reginald Foster, Vatican Latinist Who Tweeted in the Language, Dies at 81
abstract: One of the world’s foremost experts on Latin, Father Foster was a monk who looked like a stevedore, dressed like a janitor and swore like a sailor.

name: Barbara Rose
profession: Critic and Historian of Modern Art
headline: Barbara Rose, Critic and Historian of Modern Art, Dies at 84
abstract: She wrote a celebrated college textbook, but, extending her reach beyond academia, she preferred exploring the unfolding art of the present.

name: Phil Niekro
headline: Phil Niekro, Hall of Fame Knuckleball Pitcher, Dies at 81
abstract: A five-time all-star, he played in the major leagues for 24 seasons, but never made it to the World Series.

name: Betty Campbell-Adams
headline: Betty Campbell-Adams, Bronx Evangelist of Carrot Cake, Dies at 65
abstract: The bakery Ms. Campbell-Adams founded with her husband has won legions of fans all over the world for the Caribbean-infused delicacy that is its specialty.

name: Jackie Saccoccio
headline: Jackie Saccoccio, Painter of Explosive Abstraction, Dies at 56
abstract: She specialized in large canvases on which splashes of luminous color swirled and clashed. Her goal was to make her paintings seem as if they were moving.

name: H. Jack Geiger
headline: H. Jack Geiger, Doctor Who Fought Social Ills, Dies at 95
abstract: He used medicine to take on poverty, racism and the threat of nuclear destruction. Two groups he helped start won Nobel Peace Prizes.

name: Tony Rice
profession: Bluegrass Innovator With a Guitar Pick
headline: Tony Rice, Bluegrass Innovator With a Guitar Pick, Dies at 69
abstract: The nimble king of flatpicking had enormous influence on a host of prominent musicians. And he could sing, too, until he could no longer.

name: Joseph Bachelder III
headline: Joseph Bachelder III, Engineer of the Golden Parachute, Dies at 88
abstract: As a lawyer he used computerized statistical analyses when negotiating chief executives’ exit packages, to demonstrate why they deserved a gilded send-off.

name: Pierre Cardin
profession: Designer to the Famous and Merchant to the Masses
headline: Pierre Cardin, Designer to the Famous and Merchant to the Masses, Dies at 98
abstract: In a career spanning more than three-quarters of a century, he remained a futurist, reproducing fashions for ready-to-wear consumption and affixing his brand to an outpouring of products.

name: Bassam Saba
headline: Bassam Saba, Renowned Proponent of Arabic Music, Dies at 62
abstract: A skilled multi-instrumentalist, Mr. Saba co-founded the New York Arabic Orchestra and directed Lebanon’s national conservatory of music. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Scott Donaldson
headline: Scott Donaldson, Biographer of Literary Titans, Dies at 92
abstract: His subjects included Hemingway, Fitzgerald and Cheever, though he acknowledged that writing a definitive biography was an unattainable goal.

name: Ted DeLaney
headline: Ted DeLaney, Conscience of a Roiled University, Dies at 77
abstract: He worked his way up from custodian to department head at Washington and Lee, then led a reckoning with the Confederate general its very name honored, Robert E. Lee.

name: Howard J. Rubenstein
headline: Howard J. Rubenstein, Public Relations Impresario, Dies at 88
abstract: He polished the tarnished images of the rich, the famous and the flawed, with clients that included Donald J. Trump, Rupert Murdoch and George M. Steinbrenner.

name: Joe Clark
profession: Tough Principal at New Jersey High School
headline: Joe Clark, Tough Principal at New Jersey High School, Dies at 82
abstract: Bullhorn in hand, he roamed the hallways as he imposed discipline, expelling “miscreants” and restoring order. Morgan Freeman portrayed him in the film “Lean on Me.”

name: Dawn Wells
headline: Dawn Wells, Mary Ann on ‘Gilligan’s Island,’ Dies at 82
abstract: Her character on the ’60s sitcom radiated all-American wholesomeness and youthful charm. After her TV career cooled, she focused on theater acting.

name: Rita Houston
headline: Rita Houston, WFUV D.J. Who Lifted Music Careers, Dies at 59
abstract: From a studio in the Bronx, she introduced listeners to artists from a wide range of genres. She was also a mentor to the stars, and a sometime-confidante.

name: Fou Ts’ong
headline: Fou Ts’ong, Pianist Whose Family Letters Inspired a Generation, Dies at 86
abstract: Driven from China during Mao’s rule, Mr. Fou kept up a correspondence with his father that became a beloved book in the wake of the Cultural Revolution.

name: Phyllis McGuire
profession: Last of a Singing Sisters Act
headline: Phyllis McGuire, Last of a Singing Sisters Act, Dies at 89
abstract: Starting in the ’50s, the McGuire Sisters were one of America’s most popular vocal groups, their three-part harmonies a balm to audiences rattled by rock ’n’ roll.

name: Armando Manzanero
headline: Armando Manzanero, Influential Mexican Balladeer, Is Dead
abstract: He was known as one of the great romantic composers. His songs were performed by Elvis Presley, Andrea Bocelli, Christina Aguilera and many others.

name: Joan Micklin Silver
headline: Joan Micklin Silver, Director of ‘Crossing Delancey,’ Dies at 85
abstract: She broke barriers for women, directing seven feature films, including “Hester Street” and “Between the Lines,” as well as TV movies.

name: John Outterbridge
headline: John Outterbridge, Who Turned Castoffs Into Sculpture, Dies at 87
abstract: Leftover wood, rags, rusted metal — all were his materials, and pieced together as assemblages, they told stories about history, about culture and about him.

name: Adál Maldonado
headline: Adál Maldonado, Provocative ‘Nuyorican’ Photographer, Dies at 72
abstract: Adál, who moved from Puerto Rico to New York as a teenager, created art that was often bitingly satirical and politically subversive.

name: Tim Severin
headline: Tim Severin, Seafarer Who Replicated Explorers’ Journeys, Dies at 80
abstract: He and his crew sailed from Ireland to Newfoundland in a 36-foot boat like the one a sixth-century monk is believed to have used to cross the Atlantic.

name: Paul Westphal
profession: N.B.A. Hall of Famer and Coach
headline: Paul Westphal, N.B.A. Hall of Famer and Coach, Dies at 70
abstract: Drafted in the first round by the Celtics, he played for 12 seasons before leading teams in Phoenix, Seattle and Sacramento.

name: Paige Rense
headline: Paige Rense, Trendsetting Editor of Architectural Digest, Dies at 91
abstract: Showcasing the lavish homes of world leaders and celebrities, she and her magazine became powerful forces in interior design.

name: Kim Chernin
headline: Kim Chernin, Who Wrote About Women, Weight and Identity, Dies at 80
abstract: In a memoir, she also recounted her upbringing as the daughter of Rose Chernin, a Communist organizer convicted of trying to overthrow the government.

name: Brian Urquhart
headline: Brian Urquhart, Troubleshooter for the U.N., Dies at 101
abstract: He was best known for creating and directing the U.N.’s peacekeeping operations in conflict-filled areas around the world.

name: Shirley Young
profession: Businesswoman and Cultural Diplomat to China
headline: Shirley Young, Businesswoman and Cultural Diplomat to China, Dies at 85
abstract: Breaking barriers she rose in the advertising industry before General Motors took her onboard. She later used classical music to forge closer ties between Americans and the Chinese.

name: Floyd Little
profession: Star Running Back for Syracuse and Broncos
headline: Floyd Little, Star Running Back for Syracuse and Broncos, Dies at 78
abstract: Gen. Douglas MacArthur urged him to attend West Point, but he became an Orangeman to honor a promise to Ernie Davis.

name: Gerry Marsden
headline: Gerry Marsden, a Hitmaker With the Pacemakers, Dies at 78
