abstract: For a time in the early ’60s, with songs like“Ferry Cross the Mersey,” “Don’t Let the Sun Catch You Crying” and “You’ll Never Walk Alone,” the Pacemakers rivaled the Beatles.

name: Lee Breuer
headline: Lee Breuer, Adventurous Theater Director, Dies at 83
abstract: One of the founders of Mabou Mines, he reveled in being an outsider even when his celebrated “The Gospel at Colonus” reached Broadway.

name: Tanya Roberts
profession: Charlies Angel and a Bond Girl
headline: Tanya Roberts, a Charlie’s Angel and a Bond Girl, Is Dead at 65
abstract: After finding stardom in the 1980s, she fell out of the spotlight until re-emerging in 1998 in the sitcom “That ’70s Show.”

name: Julius Schachter
headline: Julius Schachter, Leading Expert on Chlamydia, Dies at 84
abstract: He played a major role in combating trachoma, a chlamydia-related disease. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: William Link
headline: William Link, Co-Creator of ‘Columbo’ and ‘Murder, She Wrote,’ Dies at 87
abstract: With his writing partner, Richard Levinson, Mr. Link helped shape the crime-drama genre on television for decades.

name: Isaac Shoshan
headline: Isaac Shoshan, Israeli Spy Who Posed as an Arab, Is Dead at 96
abstract: A Syrian-born Jew, he took part in early undercover operations, including bombings, and later taught “generations” of Israeli agents.

name: Gordon Stewart
headline: Gordon Stewart, Founder of Sandals Resorts, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Stewart turned a rundown beach hotel in Montego Bay, in his native Jamaica, into the flagship of a chain of luxury resorts.

name: Albert Roux
headline: Albert Roux, Chef Who Brought French Cuisine to London, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Roux and his brother, Michel, opened Le Gavroche in the late 1960s, raising the level of fine dining in the city and offering a training ground for some of the restaurant industry’s future stars.

name: Rosemary Collins
headline: Rosemary Collins, Singer and Choir Director, Dies at 51
abstract: Her tastes ran from Meat Loaf to Mozart and she brought that spirit of eclecticism to her jobs in schools and a church. She died of complications of the coronavirus.

name: Eric Jerome Dickey
headline: Eric Jerome Dickey, Best-Selling Novelist, Dies at 59
abstract: His fiction often featured strong Black women, and Black women were among his most enthusiastic readers.

name: Richard Means
profession: Fought for Access to the Ballot
headline: Richard Means, Who Fought for Access to the Ballot, Dies at 78
abstract: He was a premier election and campaign lawyer and a fixture in Chicago legal circles. He died of Covid-19.

name: Bryan Sykes
profession: Saw the Ancient Past in Genes
headline: Bryan Sykes, Who Saw the Ancient Past in Genes, Dies at 73
abstract: An Oxford scientist with a flair for the dramatic, he introduced millions of people to the secrets of their ancestry through his books and TV appearances.

name: Joanne Michaels
profession: Sketched the Hudson Valley in Words
headline: Joanne Michaels, Who Sketched the Hudson Valley in Words, Dies at 69
abstract: Ms. Michaels found material for her books and public access talk show in the region she loved. She died of Covid-19.

name: Sunil Kothari
headline: Sunil Kothari, Eminent Scholar of Indian Dance, Dies at 87
abstract: A critic for The Times of India and a teacher of youthful energy, he explored a country rich in dance traditions, interviewing hundreds of gurus.

name: Jean Valentine
headline: Jean Valentine, Minimalist Poet With Maximum Punch, Dies at 86
abstract: A former New York State Poet, she won the National Book Award and was a Pulitzer finalist for poems in which small details could accrue great power.

name: Shamsur Rahman Faruqi
headline: Shamsur Rahman Faruqi, Towering Figure in Urdu Literature, Dies at 85
abstract: A poet, scholar, historian, critic and novelist, he was credited with the revival of Urdu literature, especially from the 18th and 19th centuries. He died of Covid-19.

name: Narinder S. Kapany
headline: Narinder S. Kapany, ‘Father of Fiber Optics,’ Dies at 94
abstract: A physicist and entrepreneur who cut an imposing figure, he did more than anyone to make optical research a priority in government and corporate budgets.

name: Neil Sheehan
profession: Author and Times Reporter on the Pentagon Papers
headline: Neil Sheehan Dies at 84; Author and Times Reporter on the Pentagon Papers
abstract: His exhaustive coverage of the Vietnam War also led to the book “A Bright Shining Lie,” which won a National Book Award and a Pulitzer Prize.

name: John Muckler
headline: John Muckler, Coach of an N.H.L. Dynasty, Dies at 86
abstract: He was a co-head coach and then the sole head coach of the Edmonton Oilers, and, with a core of Hall of Famers, skated to five Stanley Cup championships from 1984 to ’90.

name: Tommy Lasorda
profession: Dodger From His Cleats to His Cap
headline: Tommy Lasorda, a Dodger From His Cleats to His Cap, Dies at 93
abstract: “Cut my veins, and I bleed Dodger blue,” said Lasorda, who managed the club to two World Series championships in a decades-long Hall of Fame career.

name: Eugene Wright
headline: Eugene Wright, Longtime Brubeck Quartet Bassist, Dies at 97
abstract: As a member of one of the most popular groups in jazz, he was a star. But as a Black musician in an otherwise all-white ensemble, he sometimes confronted racism.

name: Carol Johnson
headline: Carol Johnson, Leading Landscape Architect, Dies at 91
abstract: Her firm, one of the largest owned by a woman, was known for large-scale projects in Boston, Washington and elsewhere.

name: Michael Apted
profession: Versatile Director Known for Up Series
headline: Michael Apted, Versatile Director Known for ‘Up’ Series, Dies at 79
abstract: His output included “Coal Miner’s Daughter” and a James Bond film. But he was best known for his long-running documentary series about life in Britain.

name: Claude Bolling
headline: Claude Bolling, Jazzman With Crossover Appeal, Dies at 90
abstract: “Suite for Flute and Jazz Piano,” his 1975 collaboration with the flutist Jean-Pierre Rampal, spent a decade on the classical album chart.

name: Michael Cusack
headline: Michael Cusack, 64, Dies; Helped Inspire the Special Olympics
abstract: An athlete with Down syndrome, he won numerous medals over nearly 40 years at an event that one admirer said would not have happened without him.

name: Nancy Bush Ellis
headline: Nancy Bush Ellis, Sister and Aunt of Presidents, Dies at 94
abstract: Unlike most of her family, she was a liberal Democrat for a time, supporting the NAACP Legal Defense Fund and environmental causes.

name: Ved Mehta
headline: Ved Mehta, Writer Who Illuminated India, Is Dead at 86
abstract: He explored his country — and introduced it to American readers — in  The New Yorker and in many books, notably in his 12-volume memoir.

name: Pat Loud
profession: Reality Show Matriarch of An American Family
headline: Pat Loud, Reality Show Matriarch of ‘An American Family,’ Dies at 94
abstract: A mother of five, she unapologetically laid bare the drama of her family life as a star of the first reality show.

name: Thomas Verdillo
profession: Restaurateur Went from Red Sauce to Blue Ribbon
headline: Thomas Verdillo, 77, Dies; Restaurateur Went from Red Sauce to Blue Ribbon
abstract: He put a refined twist on traditional Italian-American cooking at his South Brooklyn restaurant, Tommaso. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Barry Goldsmith
headline: Barry Goldsmith, Who Escaped, Dropped Out and Came Back, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Goldsmith survived the Holocaust, immigrated to the United States and built a successful career as an architect, before abandoning his life for a commune — and then coming home. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Sheldon Adelson
profession: Billionaire Donor to G.O.P. and Israel
headline: Sheldon Adelson, Billionaire Donor to G.O.P. and Israel, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Mr. Adelson drew a cornucopia of cash from his empire of casinos and resort hotels and poured money into right-wing causes.

name: Alice Rose George
headline: Alice Rose George, a ‘Photographer’s Dream Editor,’ Dies at 76
abstract: Her unerring eye for visuals made her a fixture in New York’s magazine world, where she promoted scores of famous and unsung photographers.

name: Dee Rowe
headline: Dee Rowe, UConn Basketball Coach and Fund-Raiser, Dies at 91
abstract: He coached the Huskies for eight seasons, taking them to the N.C.A.A. tournament, before spending decades raising money for campus athletic facilities.

name: Frank Kimbrough
headline: Frank Kimbrough, Pianist With a Subtle Touch, Is Dead at 64
abstract: He could hold the spotlight in everything from a trio to Maria Schneider’s 18-piece big band. He was also a passionate educator.

name: Barbara Weisberger
headline: Barbara Weisberger, a Force in American Ballet, Dies at 94
abstract: She founded the Pennsylvania Ballet, with George Balanchine as an adviser, and turned it into a nationally acclaimed company.

name: Adolfo Quiñones
headline: Adolfo Quiñones, an Early Star of Street Dance, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Quiñones, also known as Shabba-Doo, rose to fame in the movie “Breakin’” and helped bring a distinctly urban kind of movement to the mainstream.

name: Lynn Gray
headline: Lynn Gray, Who Fought for Youths Left Behind, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Gray started or worked on programs designed to give young people a decent education in a troubled school system. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Dedé Mirabal
profession: Carried the Torch of Her Slain Sisters
headline: Overlooked No More: Dedé Mirabal, Who Carried the Torch of Her Slain Sisters
abstract: After they were murdered by Rafael Trujillo, the Dominican Republic’s ruthless dictator, Dedé Mirabal made sure that the world knew of their resistance to him.

name: Kathleen Heddle
headline: Kathleen Heddle, Rower Who Won 3 Olympic Gold Medals, Dies at 55
abstract: “I liked the balance between brute strength and power with finesse,” Heddle, a two-time Olympian for Canada, said of her sport.

name: Harold N. Bornstein
headline: Harold N. Bornstein, Trump’s Former Personal Physician, Dies at 73
abstract: He attested that President Trump would be the “healthiest president ever,” but he was later expelled from his orbit.

name: Siegfried Fischbacher
headline: Siegfried Fischbacher, Magician of Siegfried & Roy, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Fischbacher’s death came months after that of Roy Horn, his partner in one of the most spectacular shows in Las Vegas history.

name: Mary Catherine Bateson
headline: Mary Catherine Bateson Dies at 81; Anthropologist on Lives of Women
abstract: After a well-documented childhood as the daughter of Margaret Mead, she earned her own renown with a book on women’s lives that became a touchstone to feminists.

name: Ted Lumpkin Jr.
headline: Ted Lumpkin Jr., a Tuskegee Airman, Dies at 100
abstract: In World War II, he was among a barrier-shattering group of Black pilots and support personnel. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Helga Weyhe
headline: Helga Weyhe, Germany’s Oldest Bookseller, Dies at 98
abstract: She died above the bookstore, founded in 1840, where she had worked since the waning months of World War II. She locked it up for the last time in December.

name: Melvis Kwok
profession: Tireless Elvis Impersonator in Hong Kong
headline: Melvis Kwok, Tireless Elvis Impersonator in Hong Kong, Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Kwok, who busked in the Chinese territory for 28 years, was hardly the first Elvis Presley impersonator in Asia. But he may have been the most committed.

name: Shirley Abrahamson
headline: Shirley Abrahamson, Trailblazing Wisconsin Judge, Dies at 87
abstract: The first female chief justice of her state’s Supreme Court, she was on the short list for the U.S. Supreme Court seat that went to Ruth Bader Ginsburg.

name: Philip J. Smith
headline: Philip J. Smith, a Power on Broadway, Is Dead at 89
abstract: As head of the Shubert Organization, he was one of New York City’s most influential real estate and cultural entrepreneurs.

name: Debra Ivory
profession: Smiling Owner of a Barbecue Haven
headline: Debra Ivory, Smiling Owner of a Barbecue Haven, Dies at 62
abstract: In her mid-50s, she cashed out some retirement savings to buy an Oklahoma City eatery, revamping the menu with family recipes. She died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Tom Lankford
headline: Tom Lankford, 85, Dies; Southern Journalist With Divided Loyalties
abstract: He took memorable photographs of the civil rights movement for The Birmingham News. But behind the scenes he was building dubious relationships with law enforcement.

name: David Barclay
headline: David Barclay, Reclusive British Business Mogul, Dies at 86
abstract: With his twin brother, Frederick, he built a media and business empire that included the Ritz Hotel in London and The Daily Telegraph.

name: Kim Tschang-Yeul
profession: Painted Water Drops Swollen With Meaning
headline: Kim Tschang-Yeul, 91, Dies; Painted Water Drops Swollen With Meaning
abstract: Hailing from South Korea, he became an international art star with luminous images informed by Eastern philosophy and the trauma of war.

name: Joanne Rogers
headline: Joanne Rogers, Mister Rogers’s Mrs., Is Dead at 92
abstract: She worked to preserve the legacy of “Mister Rogers’ Neighborhood,” spreading her husband’s message of kindness. A friend said, “Her presence in my life made me never forget Fred.”

name: Marsha Zazula
profession: Metal Matriarch of Metallica and Others
headline: Marsha Zazula, ‘Metal Matriarch’ of Metallica and Others, Dies at 68
abstract: She and her husband founded Megaforce Records and introduced the world to heavy metal bands that became major stars.

name: Alan Canfora
headline: Alan Canfora, Who Carried Wounds From Kent State, Dies at 71
abstract: He devoted his life to pursuing the truth about the tragic events of May 4, 1970, and to keeping them in the public eye.

name: Sylvain Sylvain
headline: Sylvain Sylvain of the Proto-Punk New York Dolls Dies at 69
abstract: He was a core member of a group that had limited commercial success in the early 1970s and didn’t last long but proved hugely influential.

name: Phil Spector
profession: Famed Music Producer and Convicted Murderer
headline: Phil Spector, Famed Music Producer and Convicted Murderer, Dies at 81
abstract: Known for creating the ‘Wall of Sound,’ he scored hits with the Crystals, the Ronettes and the Righteous Brothers and was one of the most influential figures in popular music.

name: Nikolai Antoshkin
headline: Nikolai Antoshkin, Who Helped Halt Chernobyl Disaster, Dies at 78
abstract: He survived radiation as commander of the operation that extinguished the Chernobyl nuclear plant fire. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Martinus Veltman
headline: Martinus Veltman, Who Made Key Contribution in Physics, Dies at 89
abstract: He shared a Nobel Prize for research that helped explain the fundamental forces in the universe.

name: Deborah Rhode
profession: Transformed the Field of Legal Ethics
headline: Deborah Rhode, Who Transformed the Field of Legal Ethics, Dies at 68
abstract: A Stanford professor, she pushed the legal profession to confront the ways it failed clients and to be more inclusive of women.

name: Barbara Shelley
headline: Barbara Shelley, Leading Lady of Horror Films, Dies at 88
abstract: Sometimes the victim, sometimes the monster, she was a frequent presence in scary movies in the 1950s and ’60s. She died of underlying conditions following a bout with the coronavirus.

name: Roger Mandle
headline: Roger Mandle, Museum Director Who Helped Bring Art to Qatar, Dies at 79
abstract: From the Rhode Island School of Design to Doha, Mr. Mandle was a force in art and design for decades.

name: Don Sutton
headline: Don Sutton, Hall of Fame Right-Hander, Is Dead at 75
abstract: “When you gave him the ball, you knew one thing,” his former manager Tommy Lasorda once said. “Your pitcher was going to give you everything he had.”

name: Margo St. James
headline: Margo St. James, Advocate for Sex Workers, Dies at 83
abstract: She founded a group called COYOTE (Call Off Your Old Tired Ethics) and devoted her life to the cause of decriminalizing prostitution.

name: Joseph M. Scheidler
headline: Joseph M. Scheidler, ‘Godfather’ of the Anti-Abortion Movement, Dies at 93
abstract: A former ad executive, he pioneered a militant style of direct-action protest during the 1980s before winning a decades-long lawsuit that accused him of racketeering and extortion.

name: Patty Sakal
headline: Patty Sakal, A.S.L. Interpreter for Virus Updates, Dies of Covid at 62
abstract: Ms. Sakal had worked as an interpreter in Hawaii for nearly 40 years.

name: Antonio Sabàto
headline: Antonio Sabàto, Spaghetti Western Leading Man, Dies at 77
abstract: One of his biggest roles was as a racecar driver in John Frankenheimer’s “Grand Prix.” He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Elijah Moshinsky
profession: Met Opera Director With Fanciful Touch
headline: Elijah Moshinsky, Met Opera Director With Fanciful Touch, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Moshinsky, known for mixing traditional staging ideas with modern flourishes, also created productions for the Royal Opera and Opera Australia. He died of Covid-19.

name: Charles Saunders
headline: A Black Literary Trailblazer’s Solitary Death: Charles Saunders, 73
abstract: His speculative fiction was built on Black heroes and African themes. He died alone and unrecognized, but friends are trying to make amends.

name: Suhail Zaheer Lari
headline: Suhail Zaheer Lari, Force for Preservation in Pakistan, Dies at 84
abstract: After a corporate career, he devoted his time to chronicling the history of Sindh Province and preserving its cultural heritage. He died from complications of Covid-19.

name: Ron Levin
headline: Ron Levin, Sought-After New York Hair Colorist, Dies at 81
abstract: The self-described “most fabulous colorist in the world,” he tended to rich and famous clients like Anne Hearst, Nancy Sinatra, Farrah Fawcett — and Marilyn Monroe.

name: Hank Aaron
headline: Hank Aaron, Home Run King Who Defied Racism, Dies at 86
abstract: He held the most celebrated record in sports for more than 30 years.

name: Charlene Gehm
headline: Charlene Gehm, Protean Dancer With the Joffrey, Dies at 69
abstract: She could be combative in one duet, a picture of stillness in another and witty in still another role. On Broadway, she danced in “West Side Story.”

name: Mira Furlan
headline: Mira Furlan, Actress on ‘Lost’ and ‘Babylon 5,’ Dies at 65
abstract: The Croatian-born actress played Ambassador Delenn on the science fiction TV series “Babylon 5” throughout its five seasons and in two movies.

name: Lubomir Kavalek
headline: Lubomir Kavalek, Czech Who Became U.S. Chess Champion, Dies at 77
abstract: One of the first and most elite chess players to flee the Soviet bloc for the West, he was among the best players in the world for many years.

name: Jimmie Rodgers
headline: Jimmie Rodgers, Who Sang ‘Honeycomb’ and Other Hits, Dies at 87
abstract: His crossover appeal landed him on the charts often in the 1950s and ’60s, but a violent incident in 1967 derailed his career.

name: Bob Avian
headline: Bob Avian, Choreographer of Broadway Smashes, Dies at 83
abstract: His collaborations with Michael Bennett included “A Chorus Line.” He later worked on “Miss Saigon” and other hits.

name: Alice Hoagland
headline: Alice Hoagland, Grieving Inspiration in Gay Rugby, Dies at 71
abstract: She became a beloved figure in a movement that her son had helped spearhead before dying heroically aboard Flight 93 on 9/11.

name: Sharon Begley
headline: Sharon Begley, a Top Science Journalist, Is Dead at 64
abstract: Long at Newsweek, she was regarded as one of her generation’s pre-eminent science writers. An “Enlightenment-era figure,” Jon Meacham said.

name: George Carruthers
headline: George Carruthers, Whose Telescopes Explored Space, Dies at 81
abstract: At a time when there were few other Black astrophysicists, he developed a telescopic device that went to the moon on Apollo 16.

name: Gladdie Fowler
headline: Gladdie Fowler, Educator and Mental Health Advocate, Dies at 69
abstract: Nicknamed the “turnaround principal,” Ms. Fowler was entrusted with low-performing schools in southeast Texas. She died of Covid-19.

name: Walter Bernstein
headline: Walter Bernstein, Celebrated Screenwriter, Is Dead at 101
abstract: His movies included “Fail Safe,” “Paris Blues” and, perhaps most notably, “The Front,” based on his own experience of being blacklisted.

name: Ted Thompson
headline: Ted Thompson, Who Helped Revive the Packers, Is Dead at 68
abstract: As Green Bay’s general manager, he made the decision — contentious at the time but later consequential — to draft Aaron Rodgers in the first round.

name: Junior Mance
headline: Junior Mance, Jazz Pianist Who Played With Giants, Dies at 92
abstract: After working with Dizzy Gillespie and many others, he emerged as, in one critic’s words, “one of the most swinging and utterly delightful pianists in jazz.”

name: George Armstrong
profession: Led Toronto to 4 Stanley Cup Titles
headline: George Armstrong, Who Led Toronto to 4 Stanley Cup Titles, Dies at 90
abstract: A 7-time All-Star and the longtime captain of the Maple Leafs, he was the first player of Indigenous descent to score in the N.H.L.

name: Elias Rahbani
headline: Elias Rahbani, Lebanese Composer Who Sought New Sounds, Dies at 82
abstract: He was one of Lebanon’s most prolific composers, writing music for divas, TV ads, movies and underground bands. He died of Covid-19.

name: James R. Flynn
headline: James R. Flynn, Who Found We Are Getting Smarter, Dies at 86
abstract: A philosopher who moved into psychology and studied I.Q., he showed that as society grows more technical, human intellectual abilities expand to meet the challenge.

name: Diane Fillmore
headline: Diane Fillmore, Navy Veteran Who Found a New Course at 50, Dies at 59
abstract: She was the “cool mom” who loved old-school R&B and videos of people eating lots and lots of food. She died of Covid-19.

name: Juan Carlos Copes
headline: Juan Carlos Copes, Who Brought Tango to Broadway, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Copes, along with his partner María Nieves Rego, helped take tango out of the social club and make it an international craze. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Gregory Sierra
profession: Actor Known for His Sitcom Work
headline: Gregory Sierra, 83, Actor Known for His Sitcom Work, Is Dead
abstract: Often cast in ethnic roles, he saw his career take off in the 1970s as a recurring character on “Sanford and Son” and a regular on “Barney Miller.”

name: Harthorne Wingo
headline: Harthorne Wingo, 1970s Knick With Much-Chanted Name, Dies at 73
abstract: The bench player with the unusual name became a favorite of the team’s fans, who filled Madison Square Garden with cries of “Wing-o! Wing-o!”

name: Christina Crosby
profession: Feminist Scholar Wrote of Becoming Disabled
headline: Christina Crosby, 67, Dies; Feminist Scholar Wrote of Becoming Disabled
abstract: After a bicycle accident left her paralyzed, she wrote a memoir, “A Body, Undone,” which refused to draw tidy lessons about overcoming hardship.

name: Jay Jaxon
profession: Pioneering Black Designer of French Couture
headline: Overlooked No More: Jay Jaxon, Pioneering Black Designer of French Couture
abstract: He worked in fashion houses like Jean-Louis Scherrer, Yves Saint Laurent and Christian Dior and dressed Annie Lennox, Thelma Houston and other stars.

name: Jerry Brandt
headline: Jerry Brandt, Whose Music Clubs Captured a Moment, Dies at 82
abstract: Energizing Manhattan night life, he opened the Electric Circus in 1967 and the Ritz 13 years later. He died of Covid-19.

name: Jonas Gwangwa
headline: Jonas Gwangwa, Trombonist and Anti-Apartheid Activist, Dies at 83
abstract: He became a leading light on the South African jazz scene at a young age, and went on to lead the African National Congress’s flagship ensemble.

name: Sekou Smith
headline: Sekou Smith, Award-Winning N.B.A. Reporter and Analyst, Dies at 48
abstract: Mr. Smith, the creator and host of NBA.com’s “Hang Time” blog and podcast, covered professional basketball for more than two decades. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Debbie Hennessy
profession: Cal State Official Dubbed the Duchess
headline: Debbie Hennessy, Cal State Official Dubbed ‘the Duchess,’ Dies at 80
abstract: She was a longtime university administrator who was given an affectionate nickname in her husband’s newspaper columns. She died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Pauline Anna Strom
headline: Pauline Anna Strom, Composer of Enduring Electronic Sounds, Dies at 74
abstract: Her blindness, she said, enhanced her music, which included homemade recordings from the 1980s prized by aficionados.

name: Eleanor Torrey West
headline: Eleanor Torrey West, Preserver of Her Inherited Island, Dies at 108
abstract: Off Georgia’s coast, the lush 26,000-acre Ossabaw Island had been in her family since 1924. She dedicated her life to keeping it out of the hands of developers.

name: Cicely Tyson
headline: Cicely Tyson, an Actress Who Shattered Stereotypes, Dies at 96
abstract: In a remarkable career of many decades, she refused to take parts that demeaned Black people and won a Tony, Emmys and an honorary Oscar.

name: Bootee
headline: Duke Bootee, Whose ‘Message’ Educated Hip-Hop, Dies at 69
abstract: His 1982 hit about the “jungle” of urban poverty charted a new, grittier path for rap music in its early days.

name: John Chaney
profession: Hall of Fame Temple Basketball Coach
headline: John Chaney, Hall of Fame Temple Basketball Coach, Dies at 89
abstract: He won more than 500 games and six Atlantic 10 tournament championships with Temple, and he took his teams to the N.C.A.A. tournament’s regional finals five times.

name: Sharon Kay Penman
headline: Sharon Kay Penman, Whose Novels Plumbed Britain’s Past, Dies at 75
abstract: The author of best-selling books set in medieval England and Wales, she insisted that historical fiction had an obligation to the facts.

name: Corky Lee
headline: Corky Lee, Who Photographed Asian-American Life, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. Lee was determined to correct history that left out Asian-Americans, and to document their present-day lives and struggles. He died of Covid-19.

name: Isidore Torres
headline: Isidore Torres, Trailblazing Hispanic Judge in Michigan, Dies at 73
abstract: A child of migrant workers, he served more than 25 years in the Wayne County court system and advocated for other Latinos in the legal profession. He died of Covid-19.

name: Robert Cohan
headline: Robert Cohan, 95, Dies; Exported Contemporary Dance to Britain
abstract: A New York-born protégé of Martha Graham, he and a rich patron revolutionized dance in the U.K. with a cutting-edge new form.

name: Sophie
profession: Pushed the Boundaries of Pop Music
headline: Sophie, Who Pushed the Boundaries of Pop Music, Dies at 34
abstract: As a producer and performer, Sophie distilled speed, noise, melody and clarity, working simultaneously at the experimental fringes of dance music and the center of pop.

name: Sonny Fox
headline: Sonny Fox, Whose ‘Wonderama’ Mixed Fun and Learning, Dies at 95
abstract: He was not a comic or a clown, just a smart and genial TV host who for almost a decade spoke to children, not at them. He died of Covid pneumonia.

name: Sylvia Lieber
headline: Sylvia Lieber, Creative Kindergarten Teacher, Dies at 102
abstract: She gave 5- and 6-year-olds an early introduction to classical music and museum art — and taught them where milk comes from. She died of complications of Covid-19.,

name: Joseph Sonnabend
profession: Early Force in Fight Against AIDS
headline: Joseph Sonnabend, Early Force in Fight Against AIDS, Dies at 88
abstract: At the epicenter of the epidemic in New York City, he was a pioneer researcher who, as a clinician, also made house calls.

name: Andrew Brooks
headline: Andrew Brooks, Who Developed a Covid Spit Test, Dies at 51
abstract: His breakthrough helped millions get their results quickly in the early days of the pandemic, when tests were scarce and lines were long.

name: Dustin Diamond
profession: Actor on Saved by the Bell
headline: Dustin Diamond, Actor on ‘Saved by the Bell,’ Dies at 44
abstract: Mr. Diamond played Screech on the popular high school sitcom, but struggled to find work and reconcile with cast members in the decades after the show ended.

name: Sibongile Khumalo
profession: South Africas First Lady of Song
headline: Sibongile Khumalo, South Africa’s ‘First Lady of Song,’ Dies at 63
abstract: Proficient across a range of genres, she had the hall-filling power of an operatic mezzo-soprano and the directness of a pop singer.

name: Jamie Tarses
profession: Executive in a Hollywood Rise-and-Fall Story
headline: Jamie Tarses, Executive in a Hollywood Rise-and-Fall Story, Dies at 56
abstract: She broke barriers as a woman in the TV industry and turned out hit after hit, only to see it all fizzle under a very public spotlight.

name: Marc Wilmore
headline: Marc Wilmore, ‘In Living Color’ Writer, Dies at 57
abstract: Mr. Wilmore was also known for his work on “F Is for Family.” One of his elaborate pranks led to a more than decade-long stint on “The Simpsons.” He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Hal Holbrook
headline: Hal Holbrook, Actor Who Channeled Mark Twain, Is Dead at 95
abstract: He carved out a substantial career in television and film but achieved the widest acclaim with his one-man stage show, playing Twain for more than six decades.

name: John J. Sweeney
headline: John J. Sweeney, Crusading Labor Leader, Is Dead at 86
abstract: As head of the A.F.L.-C.I.O., he embraced immigrants, women, minority groups and low-wage workers in an effort to reverse organized labor’s long decline.

name: Barry Lewis
profession: Beloved Guide to New York City
headline: Barry Lewis, Beloved Guide to New York City, Dies at 75
abstract: His walking tours of the city’s neighborhoods made Mr. Lewis, an architectural historian, a local celebrity with a star spot on a PBS series.

name: Ricky Powell
profession: Chronicled Early Hip-Hop and Downtown New York
headline: Ricky Powell, 59, Dies; Chronicled Early Hip-Hop and Downtown New York
abstract: Prolific with his point-and-shoot camera, he captured essential images of the Beastie Boys, Jean-Michel Basquiat, Run-DMC, Andy Warhol and more.

name: Eugenio Martínez
headline: Eugenio Martínez, Last of the Watergate Burglars, Dies at 98
abstract: A hero to exiles from Castro’s Cuba, he was the only person other than Richard Nixon to receive a presidential pardon in the scandal.

name: Rennie Davis
headline: Rennie Davis, ‘Chicago Seven’ Antiwar Activist, Dies at 80
abstract: The trial arising from the “police riot” at the 1968 convention thrust him into the spotlight. He later became an unlikely spokesman for a teenage guru.

name: Allan Burns
profession: Creator of The Mary Tyler Moore Show
headline: Allan Burns, a Creator of ‘The Mary Tyler Moore Show,’ Dies at 85
abstract: He won Emmys for his work on that show and helped create the spinoffs “Rhoda” and “Lou Grant.” Among his other creations was the cereal mascot Cap’n Crunch.

name: June Rose Bellamy
headline: June Rose Bellamy, Adventurous Burmese Princess, Dies at 88
abstract: She traveled the world, hosted a TV show in the Philippines, married a dictator (out of patriotism, she said) and, among other things, opened a cooking school in Italy.

name: Richard Feigen
headline: Richard Feigen, Gallerist and Champion of Art, Dies at 90
abstract: He brought a hard-driving style to the showing and selling of art in New York and beyond. He died of Covid-19.

name: Wayne Terwilliger
headline: Wayne Terwilliger Dies at 95; Baseball Was His (Long) Life
abstract: He began his career as a minor league player in 1948. He played and coached in the majors. He ended his career as a minor league coach in 2010.

name: Eva Coutaz
headline: Eva Coutaz, a Record Label Force for Quality, Dies at 77
abstract: An executive with the respected label Harmonia Mundi, she shaped classical music careers and public tastes in turning out incomparable recordings from a French farmhouse.

name: Tony Trabert
headline: Tony Trabert, a Two-Time No. 1 in Men’s Tennis, Dies at 90
abstract: Trabert drew on a powerful serve-and-volley game and an outstanding backhand to win five Grand Slam tournament titles in a single year.

name: Ross Graham
profession: Tenacious Fighter for New York City
headline: Ross Graham Dies at 93; Tenacious Fighter for New York City
abstract: She died of Covid-19 after a lifetime of fighting to legalize abortion and preserve Chelsea and Hell’s Kitchen on Manhattan’s West Side.

name: Grant Jackson
headline: Grant Jackson, Relief Pitcher for Six Teams, Dies at 78
abstract: A left-hander, he had a 3-0 record in the postseason, including the victory in Game 7 of the World Series for the Pittsburgh Pirates. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Sandie Crisp
profession: Goddess Bunny of the Underground Scene
headline: Sandie Crisp, ‘Goddess Bunny’ of the Underground Scene, Dies at 61
abstract: She became a muse among the Hollywood avant-garde, appearing in movies, music videos and photographs. She died of Covid-19.

name: Paul Crutzen
headline: Paul Crutzen, Nobel Laureate Who Fought Climate Change, Dies at 87
abstract: He named our age the “Anthropocene” and warned the world of threats that certain chemicals posed to the ozone layer.

name: Margaret C. Snyder
headline: Margaret C. Snyder, the U.N.’s ‘First Feminist,’ Dies at 91
abstract: Inspired by her liberal Roman Catholic upbringing, she refocused the organization’s development efforts to include women’s empowerment.

name: Christopher Plummer
profession: Actor From Shakespeare to The Sound of Music
headline: Christopher Plummer, Actor From Shakespeare to ‘The Sound of Music,’ Dies at 91
abstract: His performance as Captain von Trapp in one of the most popular movies of all time propelled a steady half-century parade of television and film roles.

name: Carmen Vázquez
headline: Carmen Vázquez, a Force on L.G.B.T.Q. Issues, Dies at 72
abstract: Often outspoken, she was a fixture in advocacy groups in San Francisco and New York. She died of Covid-19.

name: Abraham Twerski
headline: Abraham Twerski, Who Merged 12 Steps and the Torah, Dies at 90
abstract: A noted psychiatrist, he looked outside his Orthodox tradition to meld an eclectic menu of addiction treatments, including the A.A. idea of a “higher power.”

name: Albert Hale
headline: Albert Hale, Former President of Navajo Nation, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Hale was a trailblazing lawyer and a vocal advocate for Indigenous rights and securing greater tax revenues for Arizona’s tribal nations. He died of Covid-19.

name: Frank Shankwitz
headline: Frank Shankwitz, a Founder of Make-a-Wish, Is Dead at 77
abstract: A state highway patrolman in Arizona, he helped a terminally ill boy become a motorcycle cop and then came up with a plan to help more children realize their dreams.

name: Leon Spinks
headline: Leon Spinks, Boxer Who Took Ali’s Crown and Lost It, Dies at 67
abstract: He was an Olympic champion with few pro fights under his belt when he surprised the world by beating the champ in 1978. Things did not go smoothly after that.

name: Emil Freireich
headline: Emil Freireich, Groundbreaking Cancer Researcher, Dies at 93
abstract: He helped devise a successful chemotherapy regimen for childhood leukemia, which had long been a death sentence.

name: George P. Shultz
profession: Top Cabinet Official Under Nixon and Reagan
headline: George P. Shultz, Top Cabinet Official Under Nixon and Reagan, Dies at 100
abstract: He carried one of Washington’s weightiest résumés — labor secretary, treasury secretary and budget director for Nixon and secretary of state under Reagan as the Cold War waned.

name: Naomi Levine
headline: Naomi Levine, Lawyer Who Helped Transform N.Y.U., Dies at 97
abstract: She thrived in a profession where she found herself mostly surrounded by men, taking on leadership roles and helping to turn New York University into a top-tier institution.

name: Cindy Nemser
headline: Cindy Nemser, Advocate for Women Artists, Is Dead at 83
abstract: In the 1970s she called out chauvinism and pushed back against the marginalization of women in the art world, in part by helping to create The Feminist Art Journal.

name: Robert L. Herbert
profession: Saw Impressionism With a Fresh Eye
headline: Robert L. Herbert, 91, Dies; Saw Impressionism With a Fresh Eye
abstract: A distinguished art historian at Yale, he illuminated the paintings of Seurat, Monet and others by regarding them through a social lens.

name: Maxine Cheshire
headline: Maxine Cheshire, Who Chronicled Beltway Scandals, Dies at 90
abstract: A star society reporter for The Washington Post, she was the scourge of presidents, foreign operatives and philandering politicians.

name: Joe Allen
headline: Joe Allen, Theater District Restaurateur, Is Dead at 87
abstract: His restaurant Joe Allen and another he opened next door, Orso, have been popular hangouts for celebrities and celebrity-watchers and the flagships of an international empire.

name: Anne Feeney
headline: Anne Feeney, Fierce and Tireless Protest Singer, Dies at 69
abstract: She quit her legal career to play music full time, performing more than 4,000 shows over 30 years in union halls and punk bars and on picket lines.

name: Karen Lewis
headline: Karen Lewis, Who Fought for Chicago’s Teachers, Dies at 67
abstract: As the resolute head of the city’s teachers union, she led a seven-day strike in 2012 and often butted heads with Mayor Rahm Emanuel.

name: Marty Schottenheimer
profession: Winning N.F.L. Coach With Four Teams
headline: Marty Schottenheimer, 77, Winning N.F.L. Coach With Four Teams, Dies
abstract: With a running attack known as Martyball, his teams won 200 regular season games and reached the playoffs 13 times but never made it to the Super Bowl.

name: S. Clay Wilson
headline: S. Clay Wilson, Taboo-Breaking Underground Cartoonist, Dies at 79
abstract: His drawings were so outrageous that, on first encountering them, his fellow cartoonist R. Crumb recalled feeling that “suddenly my own work seemed insipid.”

name: Lourdes Rivera
headline: Lourdes Rivera, Private High School’s Beating Heart, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. Rivera was Columbia Prep’s receptionist, and emanated empathy, tough love and comfort to students, faculty and parents alike at the New York City school. She died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Arianna Rosenbluth
headline: Arianna Rosenbluth Dies at 93; Pioneering Figure in Data Science
abstract: Dr. Rosenbluth, who received her physics Ph.D. at 21, helped create an algorithm that has become a foundation of understanding huge quantities of data. She died of complications of the coronavirus.

name: Ron Wright
headline: Ron Wright, Texas Conservative, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Wright contracted Covid-19 soon after the Capitol riot. A month later, he became the first sitting member of Congress to succumb to the disease.

name: Dianne Durham
headline: Dianne Durham, Barrier-Breaking Gymnast, Dies at 52
abstract: Though an injury derailed her career, she proved that Black women could reach the pinnacle of the sport, winning the 1983 national championship.

name: Helen Etuk
headline: Helen Etuk, Who Planned to Be a Pediatrician, Dies at 20
abstract: She was attending classes at the University of North Texas when she caught the coronavirus, her mother said. She died of complications of the virus.

name: Larry Flynt
profession: Built a Porn Empire With Hustler
headline: Larry Flynt, Who Built a Porn Empire With Hustler, Dies at 78
abstract: As the publisher of a notorious sexually explicit magazine, he found himself at the nexus of a cultural and legal war and became an unlikely free-speech hero.

name: Jean-Claude Carrière
profession: Prolific Writer of Screenplays and More
headline: Jean-Claude Carrière, 89, Dies; Prolific Writer of Screenplays and More
abstract: He was a favorite of Luis Buñuel and other top filmmakers. He also had a fruitful collaboration with the stage director Peter Brook.

name: Leslie Robertson
headline: Leslie Robertson, Who Engineered the World Trade Center, Dies at 92
abstract: He remained proud of the towers, which stood long enough for thousands to escape on 9/11, but carried with him “a troubled heart.”

name: James Gunn
headline: James Gunn, Prizewinning Science Fiction Author, Dies at 97
abstract: In short stories like “The Immortals” and novels like “The Listeners,” Mr. Gunn helped prepare readers for the future.

name: Jimmie McDaniel
headline: Overlooked No More: Jimmie McDaniel, Tennis Player Who Broke Barriers
abstract: More than 80 years ago he played what is believed to have been the first interracial tennis match, against Don Budge, the world champion. But he has become a forgotten footnote of the game’s storied past.

name: Ibrahim Idris
headline: Ibrahim Idris, a Guantánamo Bay Detainee on Day 1, Dies at 60
abstract: He was one of 20 men famously photographed on their knees the day the prison opened in the wake of 9/11. He was held for 11 years.

name: Chick Corea
headline: Chick Corea, Jazz Keyboardist and Innovator, Dies at 79
abstract: When jazz and rock fused in the 1970s, he was at the forefront of the movement. But he never abandoned his love of the acoustic piano.

name: Maria Guarnaschelli
headline: Maria Guarnaschelli, Book Editor Who Changed What We Cook, Dies at 79
abstract: She introduced Americans to new cuisines and helped transform cooking from a domestic chore to a cultural touchstone, inspiring her daughter, Alex, to be a chef.

name: Millie Hughes-Fulford
headline: Millie Hughes-Fulford, NASA Shuttle Scientist, Dies at 75
abstract: As the space agency’s first female payload specialist, she conducted experiments about the impact of weightlessness on astronauts’ immune systems and loss of bone mass.

name: John Bentson
headline: Dr. John Bentson, Who Invented a Better Brain-Imaging Tool, Dies at 83
abstract: He was a neuroradiologist who came up with an improved way to provide imaging of problems in the brain and spinal cord. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Danny Ray
headline: Danny Ray, James Brown’s ‘Original Hype Man,’ Dies at 85
abstract: He opened thousands of concerts for the “Godfather of Soul,” and closed them by draping a sequined velvet over his body just before the encore.

name: S. Prestley Blake
headline: S. Prestley Blake, a Founder of Friendly’s, Dies at 106
abstract: With a $547 loan from their parents, he and a brother opened the Friendly Ice Cream Shop in 1935, then built it into a chain of hundreds of restaurants.

name: Brenda Ballin
profession: Enlivened Tours of the Met Museum
headline: Brenda Ballin, Who Enlivened Tours of the Met Museum, Dies at 91
abstract: She was a guide at the museum for decades, bringing both knowledge and humor to the task. She died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Isadore Singer
profession: Bridged a Gulf From Math to Physics
headline: Isadore Singer, Who Bridged a Gulf From Math to Physics, Dies at 96
abstract: His unifying disparate theoretical realms helped revolutionize our understanding of the most basic structure of the universe.

name: David Katzenstein
profession: AIDS Researcher With Focus on Africa
headline: David Katzenstein, AIDS Researcher With Focus on Africa, Dies at 69
abstract: He honed methods of prevention, diagnosis and treatment, and made them accessible to underserved populations in sub-Saharan Africa. He died of Covid-19.

name: J. Hillis Miller
headline: J. Hillis Miller, 92, Dies; Helped Revolutionize Literary Studies
abstract: He was most closely associated with the Yale School, which took on the foundations of literary scholarship in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Brayden Smith
headline: Brayden Smith, Five-Time ‘Jeopardy!’ Champion, Dies at 24
abstract: Mr. Smith had appeared on some of the last shows hosted by Alex Trebek, earning $115,798 and the moniker “Alex’s Last Great Champion.”

name: Carlos Saúl Menem
headline: Carlos Saúl Menem, Who Led Argentina Through Economic Turmoil, Dies at 90
abstract: As president from 1989 to 1999, he helped restore the economy after a major crisis, but was later embroiled in corruption charges.

name: James Ridgeway
headline: James Ridgeway, Hard-Hitting Investigative Journalist, Dies at 84
abstract: Writing for many publications, he drew attention to neo-Nazis, corporate polluters, preening politicians and the practice of solitary confinement.

name: Reggie Jones
headline: Reggie Jones, Jones Beach’s Longest-Serving Lifeguard, Dies at 93
abstract: He began keeping an eye on beachgoers in 1944 and kept doing it for 64 summers. He made more than 1,000 ocean rescues in his career.

name: Albor Ruiz
headline: Albor Ruiz, a Journalistic Voice for Latinos, Is Dead at 80
abstract: As a columnist for The Daily News, he wrote passionately about the issues facing immigrants and lobbied for the U.S. to lift its trade embargo of his native Cuba.

name: Norman Golb
headline: Norman Golb, Dead Sea Scrolls Contrarian, Is Dead at 92
abstract: He challenged the conventional wisdom about a major archaeological discovery. He also led a successful effort to open it for study by a wide range of researchers.

name: Ruth Dayan
headline: Ruth Dayan, Who Built an Israeli Fashion Brand, Dies at 103
abstract: Fusing social activism with style, she helped Jewish immigrants and local Arabs sell traditional crafts, leading to the formation of a fashion house.

name: Kathleen Ham
profession: Met Her Rapist Twice in Court
headline: Kathleen Ham, Who Met Her Rapist Twice in Court, Dies at 73
abstract: “He’s been out there for 32 years,” she said in a voice turned gravelly by years of chain-smoking. “And I’ve been in my own private jail.”

name: Johnny Pacheco
profession: Helped Bring Salsa to the World
headline: Johnny Pacheco, Who Helped Bring Salsa to the World, Dies at 85
abstract: A Dominican-born bandleader and songwriter, he co-founded Fania Records, known as the Motown of Salsa.

name: Arne Sorenson
headline: Arne Sorenson, Marriott’s Chief Executive, Dies at 62
abstract: Mr. Sorenson, the company’s third-ever C.E.O., was the first person outside the Marriott family to lead the hotel company, which grew to be the world’s biggest during his tenure.

name: Bernard Lown
profession: Inventive Heart Doctor and Antiwar Activist
headline: Bernard Lown, Inventive Heart Doctor and Antiwar Activist, Dies at 99
abstract: He created the first effective heart defibrillator and co-founded a physicians group that campaigned against nuclear war, earning a Nobel Peace Prize.

name: Rush Limbaugh
profession: Turned Talk Radio Into a Right-Wing Attack Machine
headline: Rush Limbaugh Dies at 70; Turned Talk Radio Into a Right-Wing Attack Machine
abstract: With a following of 15 million and a divisive style of mockery, grievance and denigrating language, he was a force in reshaping American conservatism.

name: Leo Goodman
headline: Leo Goodman, Who Transformed Sociology With Stats, Dies at 92
abstract: He developed tools for researchers to analyze categorical data, revolutionizing the study of poverty, income inequality and social mobility. He died of Covid-19.

name: Barbara Ann Rowan
headline: Barbara Ann Rowan, Who Spurred Advances for Black Lawyers, Dies at 82
abstract: As a lawyer she protested a racial slur during a bar association speech after forging a trail as a federal prosecutor in Manhattan. She died of Covid-19.

name: Patricia Lynch
headline: Patricia Lynch, NBC Journalist Who Focused on Cults, Dies at 82
abstract: An investigative producer on “NBC Nightly News,” she won two Emmys and invoked the wrath of Lyndon LaRouche.

name: Lynn Stalmaster
headline: Lynn Stalmaster, Hollywood’s ‘Master Caster,’ Dies at 93
abstract: With his eye for talent, he was a godsend to directors and could make careers. Ask John Travolta, Jeff Bridges, Dustin Hoffman, Geena Davis and many more actors.

name: Bruce Blackburn
headline: Bruce Blackburn, Designer of Ubiquitous NASA Logo, Dies at 82
abstract: He was known for the NASA “worm,” which has become synonymous with space exploration. He also designed the 1976 American Revolution Bicentennial star.

name: Rupert Neve
headline: Rupert Neve, the Father of Modern Studio Recording, Dies at 94
abstract: His equipment became the industry standard and influenced the sound of groups like Nirvana, Fleetwood Mac, the Grateful Dead, Santana, Chicago and the Who.

name: Peter G. Davis
profession: Music Critic of Wide Knowledge and Wit
headline: Peter G. Davis, Music Critic of Wide Knowledge and Wit, Dies at 84
abstract: He wrote with passion and bite about classical music, and especially opera, over a 50-year career at The Times and New York magazine.

name: Jack Schwartz
profession: Key Cog at New York Newspapers
headline: Jack Schwartz, Key Cog at New York Newspapers, Dies at 82
abstract: His guiding hand shaped countless news stories and careers. He died of Covid-19.

name: Milford Graves
headline: Milford Graves, Singular Drummer and Polymath, Dies at 79
abstract: His free-jazz drumming style was unlike anything heard before, but his explorations and inventions went far beyond music.

name: U-Roy
headline: U-Roy, Whose ‘Toasting’ Transformed Jamaican Music, Dies at 78
abstract: He popularized the genre in which the D.J. adds a vocal and verbal layer to a recorded track, a precursor of rap.

name: Dianna Ortiz
headline: Dianna Ortiz, American Nun Tortured in Guatemala, Dies at 62
abstract: She became a champion of survivors of torture and helped compel the release of documents showing U.S. complicity in decades of human rights abuses in Guatemala.

name: Shlomo Hillel
headline: Shlomo Hillel, Who Helped 120,000 Jews Flee Iraq, Dies at 97
abstract: Working undercover, he used bribes, fake visas and a network of smugglers to bring refugees to Israel in the late 1940s and early ’50s.

name: Tom Konchalski
headline: Tom Konchalski, Dogged Basketball Scout, Dies at 74
abstract: He traveled to schools, camps and schoolyards to evaluate high school players, and his reports were essential to college coaches in their recruiting.

name: Arturo Di Modica
headline: Arturo Di Modica, Sculptor of the ‘Charging Bull’, Dies at 80
abstract: A Sicilian-born artist, he installed the artwork in Lower Manhattan without permission. The outpouring of public support persuaded the city to keep it.

name: Fernando Hidalgo
headline: Fernando Hidalgo, Cuban-Born TV Host, Dies at 78
abstract: For 14 years, “El Show de Fernando Hidalgo,” a racy variety show with a Cuban flair, was appointment viewing in Latino households across the United States.

name: Barry Le Va
headline: Barry Le Va, Whose Floor-Bound Art Defied Boundaries, Dies at 79
abstract: Extolling horizontality, he made sculptures from felt, flour, glass sheets and even meat cleavers. Elsewhere, in a performance piece, his body was a sprinting projectile.

name: Joy Kaiser
profession: Saw a Medical Need in South Africa
headline: Joy Kaiser, Who Saw a Medical Need in South Africa, Dies at 90
abstract: With her husband, she founded an organization devoted to increasing the number of Black medical professionals. She died of Covid-19.

name: Douglas Turner Ward
headline: Douglas Turner Ward, Pioneer in Black Theater, Dies at 90
abstract: A founder of the Negro Ensemble Company in New York in the 1960s, he was outspoken about limited opportunities for fellow Black actors and directors.

name: Ahmed Zaki Yamani
headline: Ahmed Zaki Yamani, Former Saudi Oil Minister, Dies at 90
abstract: As Saudi Arabia’s powerful oil minister, he was architect of the Arab world’s drive to control its own energy resources in the 1970s.

name: Elizabeth R. Duff
profession: First Woman to Drive a Nashville City Bus
headline: Elizabeth R. Duff, First Woman to Drive a Nashville City Bus, Dies at 72
abstract: A Black woman, Mrs. Duff broke gender and race barriers. She died of Covid-19.

name: Lawrence Ferlinghetti
headline: Lawrence Ferlinghetti, Poet Who Nurtured the Beats, Dies at 101
abstract: An unapologetic proponent of “poetry as insurgent art,” he was also a publisher and the owner of the celebrated San Francisco bookstore City Lights.

name: Lenore Janis
headline: Lenore Janis, Who Broke Construction Industry Barriers, Dies at 86
abstract: As a founder and president of an influential trade organization, she showed women how to make it in a field that had long excluded them.

name: Judy Wald
profession: Headhunter in the Mad Men Era
headline: Judy Wald, Headhunter in the ‘Mad Men’ Era, Dies at 96
abstract: She was a power broker in advertising’s glamour years, recruiting and fostering much of the industry’s biggest talent.

name: Fanne Foxe
profession: Plunged Into the Tidal Basin and Emerged Famous
headline: Fanne Foxe, Who Plunged Into the Tidal Basin and Emerged Famous, Dies at 84
abstract: A stripper known as “the Argentine Firecracker,” she was at the center of a political sex scandal that rocked Washington in the 1970s.

name: Luis Fernando Arias
headline: Luis Fernando Arias, Colombian Indigenous Leader, Dies at 41
abstract: Motivated by violence inflicted on his family by paramilitaries, he became the leading voice in a coalition of Indigenous peoples. Complications of the coronavirus contributed to his death.

name: Susan Feingold
profession: Helped Give New York Children a Head Start
headline: Susan Feingold Dies at 95; Helped Give New York Children a Head Start
abstract: Her Bloomingdale Family Program provided preschoolers with a haven where there hadn’t been one before. It became a model for similar efforts under Lyndon Johnson’s War on Poverty.

name: Florence Birdwell
headline: Florence Birdwell, Singing Teacher to Broadway Stars, Dies at 96
abstract: She was a tough yet empathetic voice professor at Oklahoma City University for 67 years. Two of her students, Kelli O’Hara and Kristin Chenoweth, won Tony Awards.

name: Patrick Filien
headline: Patrick Filien, Peripatetic Basketball Coach, Dies at 51
abstract: After assistant coaching jobs around the country, he found his dream job as the head coach at a small college in Albany, N.Y. He died of Covid-19.

name: Rajie Cook
profession: Helped Make Sense of Public Spaces
headline: Rajie Cook, Who Helped Make Sense of Public Spaces, Dies at 90
abstract: He and Don Shanosky developed the pictogram symbols used to identify airports, restrooms and more. He was also known for his sculptural assemblages.

name: Loretta Whitfield
profession: Black Doll Was Ahead of Its Time
headline: Loretta Whitfield, Whose Black Doll Was ‘Ahead of Its Time,’ Dies at 79
abstract: In the 1980s, amid the craze for Cabbage Patch Kids, she and her husband came up with an alternative: Baby Whitney, a doll with realistic Black features.

name: Bill Wright
profession: Broke a Color Barrier in Golf
headline: Bill Wright, Who Broke a Color Barrier in Golf, Dies at 84
abstract: In 1959, decades before Tiger Woods, Wright became the first Black golfer to win a United States Golf Association event.

name: Michael Somare
profession: Papua New Guineas Father of the Nation
headline: Michael Somare, Papua New Guinea’s ‘Father of the Nation,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Somare, who played a major role in leading the country to independence from Australia, was its longest-serving prime minister.

name: Shelia Washington
headline: Shelia Washington Dies at 61; Helped Exonerate Scottsboro Boys
abstract: She fought for decades to get their names cleared from an egregious injustice in the Jim Crow South, and created a museum in their honor.

name: Claudette White
headline: Claudette White, Innovative Tribal Judge, Dies at 49
abstract: Judge White was an advocate for her people, the Quechan of Southern California. She had been calling out injustice since the third grade. She died of Covid-19.

name: Aminah Brenda Lynn Robinson
headline: Overlooked No More: Aminah Brenda Lynn Robinson, Whose Art Chronicled Black Life
abstract: She believed that life for her people in America was an act of near-superhuman perseverance, and she was determined to capture that history in every medium she could.

name: Raymond Cauchetier
headline: Raymond Cauchetier, Whose Camera Caught the New Wave, Dies at 101
abstract: A self-taught photographer, he created indelible images on the sets of a French revolution in film, though he was not recognized for them for decades.

name: Antoine Hodge
profession: Opera Singer With a Powerful Work Ethic
headline: Antoine Hodge, Opera Singer With a Powerful Work Ethic, Dies at 38
abstract: Mr. Hodge, a bass-baritone, was recently a chorus member in “Porgy and Bess” at the Metropolitan Opera. He died of Covid-19.

name: Yuval Waldman
headline: Yuval Waldman, Bridge-Building Violinist, Is Dead at 74
abstract: A conductor as well as a skilled soloist, he liked to spotlight music composed in times of oppression, including the Holocaust.

name: Lawrence Otis Graham
profession: Explored Race and Class in Black America
headline: Lawrence Otis Graham, 59, Dies; Explored Race and Class in Black America
abstract: An Ivy League-trained lawyer, he rose to prominence in the 1990s by examining the tensions that surround Black achievement and wealth.

name: Fred Segal
headline: Fred Segal, Designer Who Commodified California Cool, Dies at 87
abstract: His laid-back style and namesake jeans made him a touchstone of 1960s fashion, drawing celebrities and tourists alike to his stores.

name: Derek Khan
headline: Derek Khan, Onetime Stylist for Hip-Hop Stars, Dies at 63
abstract: He was an architect of the over-the-top look known as “ghetto fabulous.” Later, unable to support his own lavish lifestyle, he fell from grace.

name: Norman Landsberg
headline: Norman Landsberg, Jeweler With a Friendly Touch, Dies at 94
abstract: He designed and sold jewelry for 72 years from a booth in the diamond district in Manhattan. He died of Covid-related pneumonia.

name: Irv Cross
profession: First Black Network TV Sports Analyst
headline: Irv Cross, First Black Network TV Sports Analyst, Dies at 81
abstract: After playing defensive back in the N.F.L., he made history when he joined CBS Sports’ pregame show, “The NFL Today.”

name: Vernon Jordan
profession: Civil Rights Leader and D.C. Power Broker
headline: Vernon Jordan, Civil Rights Leader and D.C. Power Broker, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Jordan, who was selected to head the National Urban League while still in his 30s, counseled presidents and business leaders.

name: John D. Pomfret
profession: Key Figure in Revamping The Times
headline: John D. Pomfret, Key Figure in Revamping The Times, Dies at 93
abstract: As a senior executive in the 1970s, he was part of a management team that expanded the paper’s format, boosted advertising and ushered in computer technology.

name: Margaret Maron
headline: Margaret Maron, Acclaimed Mystery Writer, Dies at 82
abstract: She was known for two book series centered on complex female characters, and for stories that illuminated her native North Carolina.

name: Bunny Wailer
headline: Bunny Wailer, Reggae Pioneer With the Wailers, Dies at 73
abstract: He was the last surviving original member of the group, which also featured Bob Marley and Peter Tosh. Together they helped spread the music of Jamaica worldwide.

name: Walter Chambers
headline: Walter Chambers, Birder Who Saw What Others Didn’t, Dies at 46
abstract: He worked night shifts as a pharmacist so that he could spend time scouring Georgia for unseen birds. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Toko Shinoda
headline: Toko Shinoda Dies at 107; Fused Calligraphy With Abstract Expressionism
abstract: One of the foremost Japanese artists of the 20th century, she was sought after by major museums and galleries worldwide for more than five decades.

name: Joseph D. Duffey
headline: Joseph D. Duffey, 88, Dies; Apostle of Liberalism and Humanities
abstract: His 1970 Senate race in Connecticut energized antiwar progressives. He later served two presidents and headed universities in Massachusetts and Washington.

name: Benedict J. Fernandez
headline: Benedict J. Fernandez, Photojournalist and Mentor, Dies at 84
abstract: He photographed Martin Luther King Jr. and produced classic images of the protest movements of the 1960s.

name: Moufida Tlatli
headline: Moufida Tlatli, Groundbreaker in Arab Film, Dies at 78
abstract: With “The Silences of the Palace,” a story of oppressed women in colonial Tunisia, she was first female director from the Arab world to achieve worldwide acclaim.

name: Rosalyn Koo
headline: Rosalyn Koo, 94, Dies; Fund-Raising Powerhouse for Chinese Communities
abstract: A scion of a wealthy Shanghai family, Ms. Koo helped older people in California and organized a program to educate girls in rural China.

name: Roger Englander
headline: Roger Englander, Producer of ‘Young People’s Concerts,’ Dies at 94
abstract: He collaborated with the charismatic conductor Leonard Bernstein and the New York Philharmonic for 14 years of programs aimed at educating children about the joys of music.

name: Erica Faye Watson
headline: Erica Faye Watson, Comedic ‘Hidden Gem of Chicago,’ Dies at 48
abstract: Best known as a regular on a local morning talk show, she also wrote plays and acted in movies. She died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Henry Goldrich
headline: Henry Goldrich, Gear Guru to Rock Stars, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Owning Manny’s Music in Manhattan, he brought wah-wah to Hendrix and Clapton and connected musicians with equipment that helped define their styles.

name: Tony Hendra
headline: Tony Hendra, a Multiplatform Humorist, Is Dead at 79
abstract: He took his British brand of satire to nightclubs, TV, film (“This Is Spinal Tap”) and National Lampoon. But a memoir led to a sex-abuse accusation.

name: Bill C. Davis
profession: Had a Hit Play With Mass Appeal
headline: Bill C. Davis, Who Had a Hit Play With ‘Mass Appeal,’ Dies at 69
abstract: He was an unknown playwright in his 20s when his comic drama about a priest and a seminarian drew raves off and on Broadway. It was turned into a movie.

name: Bill Davis
headline: Bill Davis, Pragmatic Ontario Premier, Dies at 92
abstract: A champion of education in his province, he helped his nation achieve sovereignty from Britain by brokering a 1982 compromise.

name: Naomi Rosenblum
headline: Naomi Rosenblum, Historian of Photography, Dies at 96
abstract: Her seminal works brought scholarship to the field and helped develop appreciation for it as a creative art form.

name: David Mintz
headline: David Mintz, Whose Tofutti Made Bean Curd Cool, Dies at 89
abstract: He set out to create an ice cream substitute for people who keep kosher. He created a phenomenon, also loved by vegans, diabetics and people with milk allergies.

name: Priscilla Read Chenoweth
headline: Priscilla Read Chenoweth, Who Won Freedom for a Stranger, Dies at 90
abstract: She spent seven years and much of her retirement savings to prove that a teenager had been wrongly convicted of murder.

name: Anna Majani
headline: Anna Majani, Grande Dame of Fine Chocolate, Dies at 85
abstract: She turned chocolates from her family company, founded in the 18th century, into design objects. She died of Covid-19.

name: Annmarie Reinhart Smith
headline: Annmarie Reinhart Smith, Who Battled for Retail Workers, Dies at 61
abstract: After nearly three decades with Toys “R” Us, she helped lead a fight by employees for severance pay from the bankrupt company. She died of Covid-19.

name: Bruce Meyers
profession: Built the First Fiberglass Dune Buggy
headline: Bruce Meyers, Who Built the First Fiberglass Dune Buggy, Dies at 94
abstract: His creation revolutionized off-road riding. But he fell victim to companies that knocked off his design for kits that turned Beetles into buggies.

name: Richie Tienken
headline: Richie Tienken, Whose Comedy Club Propelled Careers, Dies at 75
abstract: At the Comic Strip, which Mr. Tienken and two partners opened in 1976, Eddie Murphy, Jerry Seinfeld and many others made a lot of people laugh.

name: David Newhouse
profession: His Paper Broke the Sandusky Story
headline: David Newhouse, 65, Dies; His Paper Broke the Sandusky Story
abstract: A member of a powerful publishing family, he drove his Pennsylvania newspaper’s Pulitzer Prize-winning coverage of the child sex abuse scandal at Penn State.

name: Hershel Shanks
headline: Hershel Shanks, Whose Magazine Uncovered Ancient Israel, Dies at 90
abstract: For more than 40 years at Biblical Archaeology Review, Mr. Shanks simplified esoteric scholarly articles and crowned them with tantalizing headlines.

name: Ralph Peterson Jr.
headline: Ralph Peterson Jr., Jazz Drummer and Bandleader, Dies at 58
abstract: Probably the most prominent drummer of his generation to consistently front his own groups, he was also an insightful educator and mentor.

name: Monica Alexis
headline: Monica Alexis, Nurse’s Aide With a Calling, Dies at 83
abstract: Ms. Alexis worked in hospitals in New York and Pennsylvania, helping her patients with “the most important things.” She died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Carla Wallenda
profession: Surefooted Mainstay of a High-Wire Act
headline: Carla Wallenda, Surefooted Mainstay of a High-Wire Act, Dies at 85
abstract: The last surviving child of the Flying Wallendas’ founder, she was with the troupe for seven decades, performing heart-stopping aerial stunts into her 80s.

name: Norton Juster
headline: Norton Juster, Who Wrote ‘The Phantom Tollbooth,’ Dies at 91
abstract: “Tollbooth,” about a bored boy’s fantastical journey, became a beloved touchstone of children’s literature when it was first published in 1961.

name: Allan McDonald
profession: Tried to Stop the Challenger Launch
headline: Allan McDonald Dies at 83; Tried to Stop the Challenger Launch
abstract: An engineer for the maker of the shuttle’s booster rockets, he opposed letting it take off, worried that cold weather might affect them. He was right.

name: Roger Mudd
headline: Roger Mudd, Anchorman Who Stumped a Kennedy, Is Dead at 93
abstract: A staple of CBS, NBC and PBS, he was best known for his interview with Senator Edward M. Kennedy in 1979, when he asked a simple question: “Why do you want to be president?”

name: Barbara Ess
profession: Artist Blurred Lines Between Life and Art
headline: Barbara Ess, 76, Dies; Artist Blurred Lines Between Life and Art
abstract: An avant-garde musician and photographer, she was widely known for her large-scale ambient works shot with a pinhole camera.

name: Charles Hill
headline: Charles Hill, Detective Who Found ‘The Scream,’ Dies at 73
abstract: His investigations, often conducted under cover, led to the recovery of Munch’s masterpiece as well as stolen paintings by Vermeer and Titian.

name: Walter LaFeber
headline: Walter LaFeber, Historian Who Dissected Diplomacy, Dies at 87
abstract: Challenging convention from all political perspectives, he mesmerized his students at Cornell, many of whom went on to hold foreign policy posts or professorships.

name: Aruká Juma
headline: Aruká Juma, Last Man of His Tribe, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Juma, who used the name of his people in Brazil, was in his late 80s when he died of Covid-19.

name: Peter Semler
headline: Peter Semler, Career Diplomat During Cold War, Dies at 89
abstract: A well-traveled Foreign Service officer, he had posts across Europe from the 1950s through the collapse of the Soviet Union. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Wilhelmina Cole Holladay
headline: Wilhelmina Cole Holladay, Whose Art Museum Promoted Women, Dies at 98
abstract: She used her networking skills and social connections to establish the National Museum of Women in the Arts in Washington, the first of its kind.

name: Otto Dov Kulka
headline: Otto Dov Kulka, 87, Dies; Studied, and Witnessed, the Holocaust
abstract: As an Israeli historian, he examined the German people’s response to mass deportations. As a memoirist, he recalled the murders of family members.

name: Mike Pearl
headline: Mike Pearl, Innovative TV Sports Producer, Is Dead at 77
abstract: A winner of 16 Sport Emmy Awards, he produced the groundbreaking pregame show “The NFL Today” and the highest-rated Olympics ever, the 1994 Winter Games in Lillehammer, at CBS.

name: Aleksander Doba
headline: Aleksander Doba, Who Kayaked Across the Atlantic, Dies at 74
abstract: He hungered to paddle across an ocean so vast it seemed infinite. He did it three times, setting records and becoming a national hero in Poland.

name: Aaron Rose
headline: Aaron Rose, Photographer Whose Work Long Went Unseen, Dies at 84
abstract: Spurning commercialism, he made thousands of one-of-a-kind prints that for decades he largely kept to himself. Then came a show at the Whitney.

name: Lou Ottens
headline: Lou Ottens, Father of Countless Mixtapes, Is Dead at 94
abstract: He led the team at Philips that changed the audio world in 1963 by introducing a small, portable way to play and record: the cassette.

name: Fred Figa
headline: Fred Figa, Who Helped Expose a Drug’s Dangers, Is Dead at 65
abstract: He was the first hospital official to question the use of an unregulated vitamin injection linked to the deaths of 38 infants. He died of coronavirus complications.

name: Goodwill Zwelithini ka Bhekuzulu
headline: Goodwill Zwelithini ka Bhekuzulu, King of the Zulu Nation, Dies at 72
abstract: He led South Africa’s largest ethnic group through decades of change and political turmoil.

name: Paul Jones
headline: Paul Jones, a Hamptonite of Many Pursuits, Dies at 40
abstract: Real estate agent, bouncer, furniture maker, coach and also a new father, he was known all over Long Island’s East End. Engaged to be married, he died of Covid-19.

name: Leon Gast
profession: Director of When We Were Kings
headline: Leon Gast, Director of ‘When We Were Kings,’ Dies at 84
abstract: He spent 22 years making an Oscar-winning movie about the 1974 Ali-Foreman boxing match, considered one of the greatest sporting events of all time.

name: Patrick Dupond
headline: Patrick Dupond, French Ballet Virtuoso, Dies at 61
abstract: Renowned as both a star dancer and the director of the Paris Opera Ballet, he was a household name in France from an early age.

name: Luis Palau
headline: Luis Palau, the ‘Billy Graham of Latin America,’ Dies at 86
abstract: He rose from preaching on street corners in Argentina to ministering to millions around the world, then focused his ministry on liberal corners of the U.S.

name: Marvelous Marvin Hagler
headline: Marvelous Marvin Hagler, Middleweight Champion of the 1980s, Dies at 66
abstract: One of the most formidable boxers of his era, Hagler defended his title 12 times before losing to Sugar Ray Leonard in a 1987 split decision.

name: Carmel Quinn
headline: Carmel Quinn, Irish Singer and Storyteller, Dies at 95
abstract: A hit on the television variety-show circuit of the 1950s and ’60s, she also sang to packed crowds for many years at Carnegie Hall for St. Patrick’s Day

name: Flory Jagoda
headline: Flory Jagoda, Keeper of Sephardic Music Tradition, Dies at 97
abstract: A charismatic musician, she sang and wrote songs that linked her to Jewish ancestors who lived in Spain until their expulsion in 1492.

name: Rosalind Cartwright
headline: Rosalind Cartwright, Psychologist and ‘Queen of Dreams,’ Dies at 98
abstract: An early researcher of sleep disorders and the role of dreams in emotional health, she studied her subjects’ nights to help them turn their days around.

name: Mary Monahan
headline: Mary Monahan, Dedicated Preschool Teacher, Dies at 67
abstract: An Irish immigrant to the Bronx as a toddler, she had ample training for her job as the eldest of eight children. She died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Ronald DeFeo
profession: Murder Spree Inspired The Amityville Horror
headline: Ronald DeFeo, Whose Murder Spree Inspired ‘The Amityville Horror,’ Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. DeFeo confessed to killing his parents and four siblings in 1974 at their home in Amityville, N.Y. The house became the subject of books and movies.

name: Sally Grossman
profession: Immortalized on a Dylan Album Cover
headline: Sally Grossman, Immortalized on a Dylan Album Cover, Dies at 81
abstract: She picked out a red outfit and struck a relaxed pose on the cover of “Bringing It All Back Home,” leaving much for fans to guess about.

name: Stephen Bechtel Jr.
headline: Stephen Bechtel Jr., 95, Dies; Led Family’s Giant Engineering Firm
abstract: He modernized the Bechtel Group as it oversaw construction on scores of megaprojects, including the Bay Area transit system and Saudi Arabia’s Jubail Industrial City.

name: Yaphet Kotto
headline: Yaphet Kotto, Bond Villain and ‘Alien’ Star, Dies at 81
abstract: Well known for playing hardened personalities, he was also seen in movies like “Midnight Run” and the TV show “Homicide: Life on the Street.”

name: Steven Spurrier
profession: Upended Wine World With a Tasting
headline: Steven Spurrier, Who Upended Wine World With a Tasting, Dies at 79
abstract: In what came to be called the Judgment of Paris, he arranged for California and French wines to be compared in a blind tasting. The verdict was a shocker.

name: Edward C. Luck
profession: Architect of U.N. Code on Genocide
headline: Edward C. Luck, Architect of U.N. Code on Genocide, Dies at 72
abstract: He transformed vague ideals into a strategy on when the world should collectively intervene to stop mass atrocities.

name: Ion Mihai Pacepa
headline: Ion Mihai Pacepa, Key Cold War Defector, Dies at 92
abstract: A general in the Romanian intelligence service, he later revealed the corruption and cruelty behind his country’s Communist regime. He died of Covid-19.

name: Marie Mongan
headline: Marie Mongan, 86, Who Developed Hypnotherapy for Childbirth, Dies
abstract: Her natural childbirth techniques have been used by Kate Middleton, Jessica Alba and many other women around the world in search of a more gentle, unmedicated experience.

name: Nicola Pagett
headline: Nicola Pagett, ‘Upstairs, Downstairs’ Actress, Dies at 75
abstract: She preferred the stage, but she won praise for her work on television as the rebellious and thoroughly spoiled Elizabeth Bellamy, and later as Anna Karenina.

name: James Levine
headline: James Levine, Former Met Opera Maestro, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Mr. Levine was the longtime musical leader of the Met and orchestras in Boston and Munich. But his career ended in a scandal over allegations of sexual improprieties.

name: Sabine Schmitz
headline: Sabine Schmitz, Racing Driver and TV Personality, Dies at 51
abstract: She was the only woman to win the epic 24-hour race at the storied Nürburgring track in Germany. She became a spirited participant on the BBC show “Top Gear.”

name: John Magufuli
headline: John Magufuli, Tanzania Leader Who Played Down Covid, Dies at 61
abstract: “Vaccines don’t work,” he told a maskless crowd. First elected in 2015, he pushed his East African nation deeper into authoritarianism.

name: Christine Nofchissey McHorse
headline: Christine Nofchissey McHorse, Navajo Ceramist, Dies at 72
abstract: Ms. McHorse used micaceous clay, a tensile material flecked with mica, to make sensual, mysterious work that called to mind the shapes of Brancusi. She died of the coronavirus.

name: Dick Hoyt
profession: Ran Marathons While Pushing His Son
headline: Dick Hoyt, Who Ran Marathons While Pushing His Son, Dies at 80
abstract: He finished more than a thousand road races with his son Rick, who was in a wheelchair. They were best known for competing in the Boston Marathon.

name: Carola Eisenberg
profession: Helped Start Physicians for Human Rights
headline: Carola Eisenberg Dies at 103; Helped Start Physicians for Human Rights
abstract: She helped start the nonprofit after documenting atrocities in Latin America. She was also a pioneering educator at M.I.T. and Harvard.

name: Bhaskar Menon
headline: Bhaskar Menon, Who Turned Capitol Records Around, Dies at 86
abstract: After becoming the label’s chief in 1971, he oversaw the release of gargantuan hits like Pink Floyd’s album “The Dark Side of the Moon.”

name: Roger Baldwin
headline: Roger Baldwin, Groundbreaker in Blackjack Strategy, Dies at 91
abstract: He and three math-minded Army buddies — the “Four Horsemen of Aberdeen” — used calculators to figure out how to give players an edge against the casino.

name: Marianne Carus
profession: Created Cricket Magazine for the Young
headline: Marianne Carus, 92, Dies; Created Cricket Magazine for the Young
abstract: Her lively monthly publication, often called “The New Yorker for kids,” paired stories by the likes of John Updike with drawings of bugs and birds.

name: Dennis Mileti
headline: Dennis Mileti, Expert on Preparing for Disasters, Dies at 75
abstract: He was dismayed at the mixed messaging on Covid-19. The virus killed him.

name: Greg Steltenpohl
headline: Greg Steltenpohl, Pioneer in Plant-Based Drinks, Dies at 66
abstract: His first company, Odwalla, was crippled by a bacterial outbreak; he then started Califia Farms, now a leader in the beverage industry.

name: Cepillín
headline: Cepillín, a Clown Beloved Across Latin America, Is Dead at 75
abstract: Over a half-century, he hosted television shows, sold millions of albums and toured the Americas.

name: Kenneth Cooper
headline: Kenneth Cooper, Harpsichordist With Improviser’s Gift, Dies at 79
abstract: He excelled in the Baroque repertoire, but his interests were eclectic. He was also an accomplished musicologist.

name: George Bass
headline: George Bass, Archaeologist of the Ocean Floor, Dies at 88
abstract: He was called the father of underwater archaeology, finding treasures in shipwrecks around the world that illuminated ancient history.

name: Richard H. Driehaus
headline: Richard H. Driehaus, Champion of Classic Architecture, Dies at 78
abstract: A Chicago investor and philanthropist, he was an apostle of historic preservation and established an annual prize to celebrate traditional design.

name: Elsa Peretti
headline: Elsa Peretti, Star Designer of Elegant Jewelry, Dies at 80
abstract: Celebrities wore Ms. Peretti’s creations on the red carpet and in the movies. Some years her merchandise represented 10 percent or more of Tiffany’s sales.

name: Robina Asti
profession: Made History on the Ground and in the Air
headline: Robina Asti, Who Made History on the Ground and in the Air, Dies at 99
abstract: As a transgender veteran in her 90s, she challenged government bureaucracy. She then set out to be recognized as the oldest working flight instructor.

name: Nawal el Saadawi
profession: Advocate for Women in the Arab World
headline: Nawal el Saadawi, Advocate for Women in the Arab World, Dies at 89
abstract: An author, physician and champion of equal rights, she was jailed by Anwar Sadat for her activism against the Egyptian government.

name: Hugh Newell Jacobsen
headline: Hugh Newell Jacobsen, Famed Modernist Architect, Dies at 91
abstract: Mentored by Louis Kahn, he created designs for clients like Meryl Streep and Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis, as well as colleges and museums.

name: Elgin Baylor
profession: Acrobatic Hall of Famer in N.B.A
headline: Elgin Baylor, Acrobatic Hall of Famer in N.B.A., Dies at 86
abstract: Foreshadowing the likes of Michael Jordan, he was a star with the glamorous Lakers and was voted to the all-N.B.A. team for the league’s first 50 years.

name: Paul Brock
headline: Paul Brock, 89, Dies; Helped Found Black Journalists Group
