abstract: The National Association of Black Journalists was formed to promote more aggressive hiring practices in the news media and to improve how people of color were covered.

name: Amaranth Ehrenhalt
headline: Amaranth Ehrenhalt, Abstract Expressionist, Dies at 93
abstract: She was an under-the-radar figure in New York and Paris in the formative 1950s and for decades after. She died of Covid-19.

name: Jessica McClintock
profession: Dressed Generations in Lace and Satin
headline: Jessica McClintock, 90, Dies; Dressed Generations in Lace and Satin
abstract: She made calico granny dresses inspired by “flower children,” dressed a young Hillary Rodham and helped young women gussy up for their proms.

name: David McCabe
headline: David McCabe, Who Photographed Warhol Becoming Warhol, Dies at 80
abstract: In 1964, he began following the artist around New York and chronicling his exploits. His photographs finally saw the light of day four decades later.

name: Paul Jackson
headline: Paul Jackson, Funk Bassist With Herbie Hancock, Dies at 73
abstract: He was an integral member of Mr. Hancock’s jazz-funk band the Headhunters, whose albums reached millions in the 1970s.

name: Frances D. Horowitz
headline: Frances D. Horowitz, 88, Dies; Transformed CUNY Graduate Center
abstract: A distinguished child psychologist, she presided over the school’s move to a landmark building in Manhattan and expanded its capacity for research.

name: Daniel Wolf
profession: Helped Create a Market for Art Photography
headline: Daniel Wolf, 65, Dies; Helped Create a Market for Art Photography
abstract: In 1984, he quietly amassed 25,000 photos for the J. Paul Getty Museum, jump-starting collectors’ interest in the medium.

name: Adam Zagajewski
headline: Adam Zagajewski, Poet of the Past’s Presence, Dies at 75
abstract: A dissident in Communist Poland in the late 1960s — his writing was banned for a time — he found wider fame as an exile in Paris and taught in the U.S.

name: Tony Murray
profession: Moral Support for a Gay N.B.A. Player
headline: Tony Murray, Moral Support for a Gay N.B.A. Player, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Murray, along with his husband, helped their nephew Jason Collins become the first player in the league to come out publicly. He died of Covid-19.

name: Jessica Walter
headline: Jessica Walter, Tart-Tongued Matriarch of ‘Arrested Development,’ Dies at 80
abstract: An Emmy Award-winning actress, she gained early fame in Clint Eastwood’s “Play Misty for Me” and found a new audience in a cult TV hit.

name: Bobby Brown
headline: Bobby Brown, Yankee Infielder Turned Cardiologist, Is Dead at 96
abstract: He played in four World Series championships before opening a medical practice, then returned to baseball once more as the American League president.

name: Bill Brock
headline: Bill Brock, G.O.P. National Chairman After Watergate, Dies at 90
abstract: A former senator, he sought to broaden his demoralized party’s base by appealing to women and Black voters and was later labor secretary under Reagan.

name: Marianne Steiner
headline: Marianne Steiner, Refugee Who Found a New Life in New York, Dies at 101
abstract: She escaped Nazi Germany and recreated a comfortable life in Manhattan. She died of Covid-19.

name: Gail Slatter
profession: Helped Make the Times Newsroom Run
headline: Gail Slatter, Who Helped Make the Times Newsroom Run, Dies at 68
abstract: For 40 years she was a guide and gatekeeper, working in “the morgue” (the article and photo archive) and on the photo and culture desks. She died of Covid-19.

name: Bernadette Bartels Murphy
headline: Bernadette Bartels Murphy, Pioneering Wall Street Trader, Dies at 86
abstract: Starting out as a secretary, she became a sought-after financial adviser in a male world and found a national platform for her views on public television.

name: Bertrand Tavernier
headline: Bertrand Tavernier, 79, French Director With Wide Appeal, Dies
abstract: He was a regular on the world’s film festival circuit with movies like “Death Watch,” a science-fiction thriller, and “’Round Midnight,” about a jazz musician.

name: José Baselga
headline: José Baselga, Who Advanced Breast Cancer Treatments, Dies at 61
abstract: He was a top executive at Memorial Sloan Kettering before resigning over payments from health care companies. He went on to lead cancer research at AstraZeneca.

name: Janice McLaughlin
headline: Janice McLaughlin, Nun Who Exposed Abuse in Africa, Dies at 79
abstract: In a life dedicated to social justice, she was jailed in Rhodesia but later returned to a liberated Zimbabwe to help build its school system.

name: Larry McMurtry
headline: Larry McMurtry, Novelist of the American West, Dies at 84
abstract: In “Lonesome Dove,” “The Last Picture Show” and dozens more novels and screenplays, he offered unromantic depictions of a long mythologized region.

name: Bretton Sciaroni
headline: Bretton Sciaroni, Influential American in Cambodia, Dies at 69
abstract: After losing his White House job because of his role in the Iran-contra scandal, he reinvented himself as a business broker and government adviser in Phnom Penh.

name: Liesbeth Stoeffler
profession: Runner Kept Going by Rare Lung Treatment
headline: Liesbeth Stoeffler, 61, Runner Kept Going by Rare Lung Treatment, Dies
abstract: A machine that acted as an artificial lung kept her eligible for a transplant as she dealt with cystic fibrosis. She went on to compete again in marathons.

name: Kitty Cone
profession: Trailblazer of the Disability Rights Movement
headline: Overlooked No More: Kitty Cone, Trailblazer of the Disability Rights Movement
abstract: Shunned in school because of her disability, she devoted her life to the cause, organizing a historic sit-in that led to landmark federal legislation.

name: Beverly Cleary
headline: Beverly Cleary, Beloved Children’s Book Author, Dies at 104
abstract: Her funny stories about Henry Huggins and his dog Ribsy, the sisters Ramona and Beezus Quimby, and a motorcycling mouse named Ralph never talked down to readers.

name: Morris Dickstein
headline: Morris Dickstein, Critic and Cultural Historian, Dies at 81
abstract: He had a passion for reading, and for writing about what he was reading. “Criticism,” he once said, “plays a very important role in keeping people honest.”

name: Michael Bennett
headline: Michael Bennett, Small-Town Doctor Who Pushed for Masks, Dies at 52
abstract: His death leaves only one family physician in Greenfield, Mo. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Glynn S. Lunney
profession: Oversaw NASA Flights From Mission Control
headline: Glynn S. Lunney Dies at 84; Oversaw NASA Flights From Mission Control
abstract: He was hailed for leading the rescue of Apollo 13 astronauts when their spacecraft was rocked by an explosion en route to the moon, and for helping guide them home.

name: Howard Schnellenberger
headline: Howard Schnellenberger, College Coach Who Built Winners, Dies at 87
abstract: After assembling the formidable offense for the unbeaten 1972 Miami Dolphins, he breathed new life into football programs at two universities.

name: Craig muMs Grant
headline: Craig muMs Grant, Actor and Slam Poet, Dies at 52
abstract: He was a star of the HBO series “Oz” under the name muMs, which he also used on the poetry circuit both before and after finding success on television.

name: Jimmy Gamonet de
headline: Jimmy Gamonet de los Heros Dies at 63; Helped Ballet in Miami
abstract: He was Miami City Ballet’s resident choreographer before establishing his own company. He later returned to his native Peru to run the National Ballet. He died of Covid-19.

name: Edith Prentiss
profession: Fierce Voice for New Yorks Disabled
headline: Edith Prentiss, Fierce Voice for New York’s Disabled, Dies at 69
abstract: She was passionate — and relentless — about making the city she loved navigable for everyone.

name: Paul Laubin
profession: Master of Making Oboes the Old-Fashioned Way
headline: Paul Laubin, 88, Dies; Master of Making Oboes the Old-Fashioned Way
abstract: He learned the craft from his father and continued to make his instruments by hand. Laubin oboes are cherished for their dark and rich tone.

name: Sarah Onyango Obama
headline: Sarah Onyango Obama, Ex-President’s Stepgrandmother, Dies at 99
abstract: Known widely among Kenyans as Mama Sarah, Ms. Obama was seen as the matriarch of Barack Obama’s extended family in Africa.

name: Jack Bradley
headline: Jack Bradley, Louis Armstrong Photographer and Devotee, Dies at 87
abstract: His trove of pictures formed the foundation of a vast personal collection that is now part of the Louis Armstrong House Museum in Queens.

name: Alvin Sykes
profession: Self-Taught Legal Defender of Civil Rights
headline: Alvin Sykes, 64, Self-Taught Legal Defender of Civil Rights, Dies
abstract: After dropping out of high school, he studied law at the public library, then used his knowledge to reopen cold cases, including Emmett Till’s murder.

name: Freddie Redd
headline: Freddie Redd, Jazz Pianist and Composer, Is Dead at 92
abstract: He was best known for writing the music for “The Connection,” an Off Broadway play that depicted the lives of heroin-addicted musicians in New York.

name: Joan Walsh Anglund
headline: Joan Walsh Anglund, 95, Dies; Her Children’s Books Touched Millions
abstract: Her first in a prolific career, “A Friend Is Someone Who Likes You,” was a phenomenon. And her illustrations capturing childhood became a cottage industry.

name: Elena Malagodi
profession: Dedicated Her Last Years to Senegal
headline: Elena Malagodi Dies at 84; Dedicated Her Last Years to Senegal
abstract: Ms. Malagodi escaped the Nazis, married a famous Cuban sculptor and an Italian politician, then devoted her life to helping children and mothers in Senegal. She died of Covid-19.

name: Robert Hershon
headline: Robert Hershon, Artful Poet Who Published Poets, Dies at 84
abstract: He was a founder of Hanging Loose Press, which started as a loose-page poetry journal and became a book publisher as well.

name: G. Gordon Liddy
headline: G. Gordon Liddy, Mastermind Behind Watergate Burglary, Dies at 90
abstract: Unlike other defendants in the scandal that brought down Richard Nixon, Mr. Liddy refused to testify and drew the longest prison term.

name: Pat Collins
headline: Pat Collins, Tony Award-Winning Lighting Designer, Dies at 88
abstract: She sought to move audiences with her lighting in shows like “The Threepenny Opera,” “I’m Not Rappaport” and “Ain’t Misbehavin’.”

name: Bibian Mentel
headline: Bibian Mentel, Champion Paralympic Snowboarder, Dies at 48
abstract: After losing part of a leg to cancer, she dominated the sport for nearly two decades, winning three Paralympic gold medals.

name: Paul Feinman
profession: First Openly Gay Judge on N.Y. High Court
headline: Paul Feinman, First Openly Gay Judge on N.Y. High Court, Dies at 61
abstract: “I hope I add to the diversity of perspectives that the court considers,” he said before being unanimously confirmed to the Court of Appeals in 2017.

name: Michael Friedlander
headline: Michael Friedlander, Urban Architect of Offbeat Designs, Dies at 63
abstract: He was best known for the Spring Street Salt Shed, a crystalline structure that appears, with a little imagination, to form a coarse grain of salt.

name: Daniel Laske
headline: Daniel Laske, a ‘Social Justice Warrior,’ Dies at 21
abstract: He wanted to combine his passions for medicine and politics to make the world a better place. Then he tested positive for the coronavirus.

name: Constance Demby
headline: Constance Demby, New Age Composer, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Ms. Demby wrote ethereal, otherworldly music and played much of it on instruments of her own making, including one she called the Space Bass.

name: Malcolm Cecil
headline: Malcolm Cecil, Synthesizer Pioneer, Is Dead at 84
abstract: His massive machine, known as TONTO, helped transform the music in Stevie Wonder’s mind into classic albums like “Innervisions.”

name: Kenneth C. Kelly
headline: Kenneth C. Kelly, Champion of Desegregation in California, Dies at 94
abstract: When Mr. Kelly, an engineer, wasn’t designing ways to communicate with spacecraft, he was opening doors for Black families to move into the San Fernando Valley.

name: Arthur Kopit
profession: Oh Dad Shook Up the Theater
headline: Arthur Kopit, Whose ‘Oh Dad’ Shook Up the Theater, Dies at 83
abstract: A three-time Tony nominee, he first became known for avant-garde works, many of them christened with rambling titles, that sparked spirited reactions.

name: Kristofer Schipper
headline: Kristofer Schipper, Influential China Scholar, Dies at 86
abstract: A native of Holland, he helped change the understanding of Chinese religion and became a Taoist priest in the process.

name: Winfred Rembert
headline: Winfred Rembert, 75, Dies; Turned Painful Memories Into Art
abstract: Decades after nearly being lynched in rural Georgia, he began recreating vivid scenes from his life by carving figures into leather.

name: Martha Lou Gadsden
headline: Martha Lou Gadsden, Soul-Food Matriarch, Dies at 91
abstract: For 37 years she stirred the pot at Martha Lou’s Kitchen in Charleston, S.C., a modest restaurant that became known as a temple for Low Country cuisine.

name: Gloria Henry
headline: Gloria Henry, ‘Dennis the Menace’ Mother, Dies at 98
abstract: She was a prolific B-movie actress early in her career, but she became best known for her role as Alice Mitchell, the gentle mother of Dennis, on the CBS show.

name: Gianluigi Colalucci
headline: Gianluigi Colalucci, Who Showed Michelangelo’s True Colors, Dies at 91
abstract: The chief restorer of the Vatican Museums, he led the cleaning of the Sistine Chapel, a 14-year effort that revealed a new vision of Michelangelo’s complex work.

name: Robert A. Mundell
profession: Father of the Euro and Reaganomics
headline: Robert A. Mundell, a Father of the Euro and Reaganomics, Dies at 88
abstract: His insights on global finance earned him a Nobel, while his more iconoclastic theories fostered the adoption of a single European currency and supply-side economics.

name: Hans Küng
profession: Catholic Theologian Critical of the Church
headline: Hans Küng, Catholic Theologian Critical of the Church, Dies at 93
abstract: A prolific writer and a prominent speaker, he promoted dialogue among religions and challenged Vatican doctrine on many fronts, provoking its censure.

name: Lois Sasson
profession: Quiet Force in Gay and Womens Rights
headline: Lois Sasson, Quiet Force in Gay and Women’s Rights, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Sasson, a jewelry designer and the partner of the singer Lesley Gore, was an advocate for feminism, gay rights and more. She died of Covid-19.

name: Isamu Akasaki
profession: Nobel Winner Lit Up the World With LEDs
headline: Isamu Akasaki, 92, Dies; Nobel Winner Lit Up the World With LEDs
abstract: A physicist, he shared the prize with two others for their breakthrough in creating blue light-emitting diodes, succeeding “where everyone else had failed.”

name: Bill Gamson
headline: Bill Gamson, Sociologist and Inventor of Games, Dies at 87
abstract: He created a game of simulated baseball that was a precursor to today’s fantasy sports. As a professor, he devised a role-playing game to help students address societal problems.

name: Alcee Hastings
headline: Alcee Hastings, Longtime Florida Congressman, Dies at 84
abstract: As a federal judge, he was impeached and removed from the bench. He was then elected to the House, where he became known as a strong liberal voice.

name: Nemam Ghafouri
headline: Nemam Ghafouri, Doctor Who Aided Yazidis in Iraq, Dies at 52
abstract: Dr. Ghafouri helped survivors of an ISIS genocide and reunited formerly enslaved women with children taken from them. She died of Covid-19.

name: Lois Kirschenbaum
headline: Lois Kirschenbaum, the Ultimate Opera Superfan, Dies at 88
abstract: In New York opera circles, an autograph request from her, the mezzo-soprano Frederica von Stade said, was considered “a special type of approval.”

name: Charles Coolidge
headline: Charles Coolidge, Oldest Medal of Honor Recipient, Dies at 99
abstract: A harrowing World War II firefight in France brought him the nation’s highest decoration for valor. A park, a highway and a museum are named in his honor.

name: Phyllis Marchand
headline: Phyllis Marchand, Face of Disputed Deer-Culling Program, Dies at 81
abstract: She gained national attention as mayor of Princeton, N.J., when deer overran her suburban town and she hired sharpshooters to control the population.

name: Sharon Matola
profession: Opened a Zoo in the Jungle of Belize
headline: Sharon Matola, Who Opened a Zoo in the Jungle of Belize, Dies at 66
abstract: An Air Force veteran and former lion tamer, she helped her adopted country fall in love with tapirs, macaws and peccaries.

name: Granville Redmond
headline: Overlooked No More: Granville Redmond, Painter, Actor, Friend
abstract: He was known for his California landscapes. Deaf since childhood, he acted with Charlie Chaplin in silent films, an early example of deaf representation in Hollywood.

name: Anne Beatts
headline: Anne Beatts, Original ‘S.N.L.’ Writer, Dies at 74
abstract: Often writing with Rosie Shuster, she created memorable sketches in the show’s early years, including ones involving those nerds Lisa and Todd.

name: Philip
headline: Prince Philip, Husband of Queen Elizabeth II, Is Dead at 99
abstract: The Duke of Edinburgh, who married the future queen in 1947, brought the monarchy into the 20th century, but his occasional tactless comments hurt his image.

name: DMX
headline: DMX, Top-Selling but Troubled Rapper, Dies at 50
abstract: He released a string of No. 1 albums that reflected his gritty past and featured a gruff and unmistakable lyrical style.

name: Judy McGinn
profession: Librarian With a Love for Home
headline: Judy McGinn, Librarian With a Love for Home, Dies at 78
abstract: She was hyper-vigilant about keeping safe during the pandemic, but she caught Covid-19 after her first vaccine.

name: Peter Manso
headline: Peter Manso, Biographer of Brando and Mailer, Dies at 80
abstract: His relationship with his subjects and critics could be tempestuous. His interview with Mayor Edward I. Koch for Playboy may have cost Koch the governorship

name: Yehuda Ben-Yishay
headline: Yehuda Ben-Yishay, Pioneer in Treating Brain Injuries, Dies at 88
abstract: After working with wounded Israeli soldiers in the 1970s, he developed a holistic approach to helping patients regain some semblance of the life they had before.

name: Ethel Gabriel
profession: Rare Woman in the Record World
headline: Ethel Gabriel, a Rare Woman in the Record World, Dies at 99
abstract: For much of her more than 40 years at RCA, Ms. Gabriel was a producer, overseeing “Living Strings” and other profitable lines.

name: James Hampton
headline: James Hampton, Bumbling ‘F Troop’ Bugler, Dies at 84
abstract: A character actor, he was best known for comedic roles but also appeared in “The China Syndrome” and other dramas.

name: Martina Batan
profession: New York Art Dealer Consumed by a Cold Case
headline: Martina Batan, New York Art Dealer Consumed by a Cold Case, Dies at 62
abstract: Finding answers to the unsolved murder of her 14-year-old brother became a lifelong quest, ultimately chronicled in a documentary film.

name: Ramsey Clark
profession: Attorney General and Rebel With a Cause
headline: Ramsey Clark, Attorney General and Rebel With a Cause, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Clark oversaw the drafting of the Fair Housing Act in 1968 and went on to defend both the disadvantaged and the unpopular.

name: Marshall D. Sahlins
headline: Marshall D. Sahlins, Groundbreaking Anthropologist, Dies at 90
abstract: His work focused on the way cultures shape, and are shaped by, individuals — a framework he demonstrated through his passionate political activism.

name: John Topping
headline: John Topping, 77, Dies; Early Advocate for Climate Action
abstract: A former official of the Environmental Protection Agency, he was a Republican activist on global warming when it was an issue with bipartisan support

name: Benita Raphan
headline: Benita Raphan, Maker of Lyrical Short Films, Is Dead at 58
abstract: Her dreamlike “genius” films about figures like Emily Dickinson and Buckminster Fuller hovered between documentary and experimental cinema.

name: Howard Weitzman
headline: Howard Weitzman, Defense Lawyer for the Famous, Dies at 81
abstract: A master practitioner of the courthouse-steps news conference, he often made his case in the court of public opinion. He also made lawsuits disappear.

name: Gail Coburn
profession: Social Worker With a Gift for Solutions
headline: Gail Coburn, Social Worker With a Gift for Solutions, Dies at 71
abstract: After a divorce in her early 20s, Ms. Coburn raised her son and launched herself on a succession of careers. She died of Covid-19.

name: Mary Ellen Moylan
headline: Mary Ellen Moylan, Acclaimed Balanchine Dancer, Is Dead at 94
abstract: The celebrated choreographer George Balanchine created roles for her. The critics hailed her. Yet her death a year ago went unnoticed in the dance world.

name: Jeffrey Paley
headline: Jeffrey Paley, Journalist, Gallerist and Investor, Dies at 82
abstract: A son of the CBS founder, he wrote for newspapers from Europe, championed young artists in SoHo and became an investor. He died of complications of the coronavirus.

name: Bernard Madoff
profession: Architect of Largest Ponzi Scheme in History
headline: Bernard Madoff, Architect of Largest Ponzi Scheme in History, Is Dead at 82
abstract: His enormous fraud left behind a devastating human toll and paper losses totaling $64.8 billion.

name: Burt Pugach
profession: Protagonist of a Strange Tabloid Love Story
headline: Burt Pugach, Protagonist of a Strange Tabloid Love Story, Dies at 93
abstract: In 1959, he had his lover blinded. When he got out of prison, he married her. He called their relationship “a storybook romance.”

name: Donald P. Ryder
headline: Donald P. Ryder, Architect of Black Heritage Sites, Dies at 94
abstract: His firm, which he formed with J. Max Bond Jr., designed public works commemorating the civil rights movement as well as the Schomburg Center in Harlem.

name: John Naisbitt
profession: Business Guru and Author of Megatrends
headline: John Naisbitt, Business Guru and Author of ‘Megatrends,’ Dies at 92
abstract: His book, published in 1982 amid a brutal recession, foretold of a bountiful postindustrial information economy. He was half right.

name: Frank Jacobs
profession: Mad Magazine Writer With a Lyrical Touch
headline: Frank Jacobs, Mad Magazine Writer With a Lyrical Touch, Dies at 91
abstract: He deftly mocked pop culture, politics and more for 57 years. He also wrote new lyrics for familiar songs, which led to a lawsuit from Irving Berlin and others.

name: Anthony Audy
profession: Vermont Tattoo Artist With Whimsical Style
headline: Anthony Audy, Vermont Tattoo Artist With Whimsical Style, Dies at 44
abstract: A love for all things magical, spooky and cute informed the thousands of tattoos Mr. Audy inked in a 15-year career in Burlington. He died of Covid-19.

name: Giancarlo DiTrapano
headline: Giancarlo DiTrapano, Defiantly Independent Book Publisher, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. DiTrapano championed avant-garde work and relished taking chances on young, untested authors. His Tyrant Books produced some unexpected hits.

name: Bobby Leonard
headline: Bobby Leonard, Hall of Fame Basketball Coach, Dies at 88
abstract: He coached the Indiana Pacers for 12 seasons and took them to three A.B.A. titles. The governor of Indiana called him “the embodiment of basketball.”

name: Carol Prisant
headline: Carol Prisant, Elegant Design Writer, Dies at 82
abstract: She was a 51-year old former antiques dealer with no experience as a writer when she wrote to the editor of The World of Interiors magazine about a job. She was hired.

name: Shirley Williams
headline: Shirley Williams, Breakaway Political Force in Britain, Dies at 90
abstract: She was one of the “Gang of Four” who left Labour to start the more centrist Social Democratic Party in 1981, altering the country’s political landscape.

name: Shelia Smith
headline: Shelia Smith, Exuberant Teacher’s Aide, Dies at 61
abstract: At her rural Alabama school, she was beloved by students, especially those with special needs, and by her colleagues. She died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Vartan Gregorian
profession: Savior of the New York Public Library
headline: Vartan Gregorian, Savior of the New York Public Library, Dies at 87
abstract: A scholar, a university leader and a believer in libraries, he almost single-handedly rescued a grand but broken one in a time of municipal austerity.

name: Shawn G. Kennedy
headline: Shawn G. Kennedy, Times Reporter in a Vanguard, Dies at 73
abstract: She was part of a wave of recruited Black reporters who began changing the face of the paper in the ’70s. She also helped rebuild New Orleans after Katrina.

name: Joye Hummel
profession: First Woman to Write Wonder Woman
headline: Joye Hummel, First Woman to Write Wonder Woman, Dies at 97
abstract: For almost 70 years, her contributions to one of the comic-book world’s most enduring characters went largely unappreciated.

name: Helen McCrory
headline: Helen McCrory, British Star of Stage, Film and TV, Dies at 52
abstract: She was acclaimed for her work on the TV series “Peaky Blinders” and in three Harry Potter movies, but she first gained notice in the London theater.

name: Rusty Young
headline: Rusty Young, Country-Rock Pioneer, Is Dead at 75
abstract: As a founding member of the band Poco, he helped define a genre and establish the pedal steel guitar as an integral voice in West Coast rock.

name: Liam Scarlett
headline: Liam Scarlett, Choreographer Accused of Sexual Misconduct, Dies at 35
abstract: He won acclaim in the dance world with remarkable speed. His subsequent downfall, amid allegations of sexual misconduct, happened just as abruptly.

name: Denis Donoghue
headline: Denis Donoghue, Humanist Literary Critic, Dies at 92
abstract: He wrote prodigiously while teaching, first in Dublin and then in New York, and often clashed with critics he considered too political.

name: Marie Supikova
profession: Survivor of Nazi Terror in Czech Village
headline: Marie Supikova, Survivor of Nazi Terror in Czech Village, Dies at 88
abstract: The men of Lidice, including her father, were massacred and the women, including her mother, sent to a concentration camp. She later testified at the Nuremberg war-crimes trials.

name: LaDonna Allard
headline: LaDonna Allard Dies at 64; Led Dakota Pipeline Protests
abstract: She started a resistance camp that turned into a movement that opposed fossil fuels while it embraced tribal sovereignty and environmental justice.

name: Jerry Lee Albin
profession: Found Sobriety After a Hard Life
headline: Jerry Lee Albin, Who Found Sobriety After a Hard Life, Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Albin put drugs, prison and biker gangs behind him, started a construction business and counseled prisoners. He died of complications of the coronavirus.

name: Richard Rush
headline: Richard Rush, Who Directed ‘The Stunt Man,’ Dies at 91
abstract: He was nominated for an Oscar for the movie, about filmmaking stunts, perception and reality. His earlier films were aimed at the teenage market.

name: Walter Mondale
profession: Ex-Vice President and Champion of Liberal Politics
headline: Walter Mondale, Ex-Vice President and Champion of Liberal Politics, Dies at 93
abstract: Under Jimmy Carter, he was the first V.P. to serve as a genuine partner of a president. His own run for the top position ended in a crushing defeat.

name: Jeremiah Trusty
headline: Jeremiah Trusty, Singer, Model, Actor, Dies at 38
abstract: Of all his endeavors, singing was the most important. He had recently recorded a song that he hoped would be his breakthrough. He died of Covid-19.

name: Felix Silla
profession: Cousin Itt on The Addams Family
headline: Felix Silla, Cousin Itt on ‘The Addams Family’ Dies at 84
abstract: He made a strong impression in his best-known role, even though his face wasn’t seen and his voice wasn’t heard.

name: Chuck Geschke
headline: Chuck Geschke, Father of Desktop Publishing, Dies at 81
abstract: If you sent a PDF on your computer today, thank him. In 1980, he and a colleague created a way of sending digital documents to a printer, starting a company, Adobe.

name: Jim Steinman
headline: Jim Steinman, ‘Bat Out of Hell’ Songwriter, Dies at 73
abstract: The rocker Meat Loaf’s interpretations of Mr. Steinman’s songs became one of the biggest-selling albums of all time.

name: Idriss Déby
profession: Poor Herders Son Became Chads Longtime Autocrat
headline: Idriss Déby Dies at 68; Poor Herder’s Son Became Chad’s Longtime Autocrat
abstract: Mr. Déby, who was aiming for a fourth decade in power, died from what the government called wounds sustained at a battlefront with rebels.

name: Monte Hellman
headline: Monte Hellman, Cult Director of ‘Two-Lane Blacktop,’ Dies at 91
abstract: Originally part of Roger Corman’s army of hungry young actors and filmmakers, he made terse action movies and became a hero of the American independent film movement.

name: Tempest Storm
headline: Tempest Storm, Who Disrobed to Enduring Acclaim, Dies at 93
abstract: One of the most celebrated strippers of her time, she began her career in burlesque’s golden twilight and continued performing into her 80s.

name: Mariano Puig
profession: Scion of a Spanish Fashion House
headline: Mariano Puig, Scion of a Spanish Fashion House, Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Puig was instrumental in expanding his family’s company internationally and in acquiring famed brands.

name: Mao Ayuth
headline: Mao Ayuth, Filmmaker Who Survived the Khmer Rouge, Dies at 76
abstract: At a time when most artists were killed, he hid his background. Later he resumed his career and served in government. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: June Newton
headline: June Newton, Photographer and Muse, Dies at 97
abstract: The widow and inspiration of the provocative photographer Helmut Newton, she took pictures that were as tender as his were erotically charged.

name: Carl Spielvogel
headline: Carl Spielvogel, a Longtime Power in Advertising, Dies at 92
abstract: A former newspaper columnist, he climbed the ladder at one big firm, founded his own, then rose again through mergers to the top of a global  agency.

name: Peter Warner
headline: Peter Warner, 90, Seafarer Who Discovered Shipwrecked Boys, Dies
abstract: That story, which has sometimes been called a real-life “Lord of the Flies,” was just one episode in a life filled with adventure.

name: Bhanu Athaiya
headline: Overlooked No More: Bhanu Athaiya, Who Won India Its First Oscar
abstract: Athaiya, a costume designer on more than 100 films, won the award in 1983 for her work on “Gandhi.”

name: Thomas Brock
profession: Discovery Paved the Way for PCR Tests
headline: Thomas Brock, Whose Discovery Paved the Way for PCR Tests, Dies at 94
abstract: In 1966, he found heat-resistant bacteria in a hot spring at Yellowstone National Park. That led to the development of the chemical process behind the coronavirus test.

name: Bob Porter
headline: Bob Porter, Jazz Producer and Broadcaster, Dies at 80
abstract: Hundreds of albums bore his name, notably reissues of classic material. And he helped make WBGO the biggest jazz radio station in the New York area.

name: Richard K. Kim
headline: Richard K. Kim, Pioneering Korean-American Prosecutor, Dies at 76
abstract: He was appointed an assistant district attorney in Queens in 1985 and later became counsel to a cosmetics company. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Shock G
profession: Frontman for Hip-Hop Group Digital Underground
headline: Shock G, Frontman for Hip-Hop Group Digital Underground, Dies at 57
abstract: The group had a string of hits in the 1990s, including “The Humpty Dance,” and helped introduce a little-known rapper named Tupac Shakur.

name: Kathie Coblentz
headline: Kathie Coblentz, 73, Dies; Not Your Ordinary Librarian
abstract: A Yankees fan, marathon runner, cinephile, editor, and, yes, a cataloger, she was the New York Public Library’s third-longest serving employee.

name: Les McKeown
profession: Lead Singer of the Bay City Rollers
headline: Les McKeown, Lead Singer of the Bay City Rollers, Dies at 65
abstract: Known for their catchy pop songs and their distinctive tartan outfits, the Rollers attracted a fanatical teenage following after Mr. McKeown joined in 1973.

name: Allon Schoener
profession: Curator Caught in Furor Over Harlem Show
headline: Allon Schoener, 95, Dies; Curator Caught in Furor Over ‘Harlem’ Show
abstract: His “Harlem on My Mind” exhibit at the Met museum in 1969 drew protests for not including works by Black artists. But since then it’s been reconsidered.

name: Al Young
headline: Al Young, Poet With a Musical Bent, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Mr. Young, who served for three years as California’s poet laureate and also wrote about jazz, was known for his readings, which often incorporated music.

name: Penelope Laingen
headline: Penelope Laingen, 89, Dies; Her Yellow Ribbon Rallied Americans
abstract: As the wife of the highest-ranking American detained in the Iran hostage crisis in 1979, she started a nationwide movement with a symbol of support.

name: Nick Springer
headline: Nick Springer, Paralympic Gold Medalist, Dies at 35
abstract: A quadruple amputee, he was a relentless defender on the United States’ wheelchair rugby team, which won a gold medal at the 2008 Paralympics in Beijing.

name: Thelma Harper
headline: Thelma Harper, ‘Transformative’ Tennessee Legislator, Dies at 80
abstract: She was the first African-American woman elected to the State Senate, and she was its longest-serving female senator when she retired in 2018.

name: Alber Elbaz
headline: Alber Elbaz, Beloved Fashion Designer, Is Dead at 59
abstract: A favorite of celebrities like Meryl Streep and Natalie Portman, he rejuvenated Lanvin and had recently started his own brand. He died of Covid-19.

name: Bob Fass
headline: Bob Fass, Pioneer of Underground Radio, Dies at 87
abstract: His provocative “Radio Unnameable,” long a staple of the New York station WBAI, offered a home on the FM dial to everyone from Abbie Hoffman to Tiny Tim.

name: Christa Ludwig
headline: Christa Ludwig, Mezzo-Soprano of Velvety Hues, Is Dead at 93
abstract: She was a beloved interpreter of Strauss, Mozart and Wagner roles, but equally admired for her rendition of art songs.

name: Arlene Pieper Stine
profession: First Woman to Finish a Marathon
headline: Arlene Pieper Stine, 90, Dies; First Woman to Finish a Marathon
abstract: She ran the challenging Pikes Peak Marathon in Colorado in 1959. For the next 50 years she had no idea that she had made sports history.

name: Helen Weaver
profession: Chronicler of an Affair With Kerouac
headline: Helen Weaver, Chronicler of an Affair With Kerouac, Dies at 89
abstract: She was a respected translator from French and a writer on astrology, but her magnum opus was a memoir of her time with Kerouac and the Beats.

name: Hester Ford
headline: Hester Ford, Oldest American, Dies
abstract: She was believed to be either 115 or 116. She experienced two pandemics and two world wars and lived under 21 presidents.

name: Paul Oscher
profession: Blues Musician in Muddy Waterss Band
headline: Paul Oscher, Blues Musician in Muddy Waters’s Band, Dies at 74
abstract: He mainly played harmonica, but also guitar and piano — often all three instruments at the same time. He died of complications of the coronavirus.

name: W. Galen Weston
headline: W. Galen Weston, Who Transformed a Family Food Empire, Dies at 80
abstract: Faced with the task of turning around a nearly bankrupt supermarket chain, he made private-label merchandise fashionable.

name: Daniel Kaminsky
headline: Daniel Kaminsky, Internet Security Savior, Dies at 42
abstract: If you are reading this obituary online, you owe your digital safety to him.

name: Theodore Lambrinos
profession: Baritone With a Zest for the Road
headline: Theodore Lambrinos, Baritone With a Zest for the Road, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Lambrinos sang performances at the Metropolitan Opera and was a stalwart of New York Grand Opera. He died of Covid-related pneumonia.

name: Erica Chang
profession: Motivated by the Pandemic to Help
headline: Erica Chang, Motivated by the Pandemic to Help, Dies at 24
abstract: Armed with degrees in biomedicine and engineering, she wanted to administer health care. Her Covid-19 death came just five days before her father’s.

name: Ole Anthony
headline: Ole Anthony, Scourge of Televangelists, Dies at 82
abstract: After working as a well-paid Republican operative, he gave up a lavish lifestyle to live in poverty as a self-proclaimed Jeremiah, calling out fraud in the name of God.

name: John C. Martin
headline: John C. Martin, 69, Dies; Led Drugmaker in Breakthroughs
abstract: A chemist by training, he turned Gilead Sciences into a leading, and lucrative, innovator with single-pill treatments for H.I.V. and hepatitis C.

name: John Martin
headline: John Martin, Devoted Publisher of Literary Rebels, Dies at 94
abstract: Black Sparrow Press, a shoestring operation he ran out of his home, became one of the highest-profile small publishers in the U.S., championing writers like Charles Bukowski.

name: Wayne Peterson
headline: Wayne Peterson, Pulitzer Prize-Winning Composer, Dies at 93
abstract: His Pulitzer, in 1992, came amid controversy not of his making: A three-member jury had recommended a different work.

name: Michael Collins
profession: Third Man of the Moon Landing
headline: Michael Collins, ‘Third Man’ of the Moon Landing, Dies at 90
abstract: Orbiting dozens of miles above the lunar surface, he kept solitary watch of the Apollo command module as Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin embarked for the moon.

name: Charles Strum
headline: Charles Strum, Versatile Editor for The Times, Dies at 73
abstract: Whether overseeing the paper’s night operations, a regional bureau or the obituaries, he was known for his calmness under deadline pressure.

name: Valerie Cirillo-Bunch
headline: Valerie Cirillo-Bunch, a Child-Care Sage, Dies at 41
abstract: She worked with preschoolers, infants and their parents, “the mom that other moms looked up to.” She died of Covid-19.

name: Clara Lamore Walker
headline: Clara Lamore Walker, 94, Thwarted Olympian Redeemed in Her 50s, Dies
abstract: She gave up competitive swimming after the 1948 Games in London — until her doctor prescribed the pool for back pain. She staged an astonishing comeback.

name: Paul Kellogg
headline: Paul Kellogg, New York City Opera Impresario, Dies at 84
abstract: He had no opera experience when he was chosen to run the Glimmerglass Opera in upstate New York; 17 years later, he took on City Opera during a difficult period.

name: Rajan Mishra
headline: Rajan Mishra, Classical Indian Vocalist, Dies at 69
abstract: Part of a famous duet with his brother, he brought traditional ragas to generations of young musicians. He died of Covid 19-related complications.

name: Inji Efflatoun
headline: Overlooked No More: Inji Efflatoun, Egyptian Artist of the People
abstract: She was born into the aristrocacy but became an activist for commoners while depicting social injustices in her paintings.

name: Jill Corey
profession: Coal Miners Daughter Turned Singing Sensation
headline: Jill Corey, 85, Coal Miner’s Daughter Turned Singing Sensation, Dies
abstract: The subject of a Life magazine cover story, she found early fame as a star of ’50s era television and drew comparisons to Judy Garland.

name: Clotilda Douglas-Yakimchuk
headline: Clotilda Douglas-Yakimchuk, Pioneering Nurse, Dies at 89
abstract: Breaking color barriers, she devoted herself to social justice, the education of Black youth and the well-being of older people. She died of Covid-19.

name: Tomas Estes
headline: Tomas Estes, Who Put Tequila on a Pedestal, Dies at 75
abstract: Starting with a popular Mexican restaurant in Amsterdam, he helped place the drink on the same shelf as fine cognac and single-malt Scotch.

name: Al Schmitt
headline: Al Schmitt, Maestro of Recorded Sound, Is Dead at 91
abstract: The winner of multiple Grammys, he engineered or produced records by Frank Sinatra, Ray Charles, Paul McCartney, Bob Dylan, Jefferson Airplane and many others.

name: Eli Broad
headline: Eli Broad, Who Helped Reshape Los Angeles, Dies at 87
abstract: The businessman, who made a fortune in home-building and insurance, spent lavishly to try to make the city a cultural capital.

name: Jeff Fox
headline: Jeff Fox, 52, Dies; Balanced Baseball With Protecting Presidents
abstract: A star college athlete who later worked in the Secret Service, he played for decades in elite amateur leagues around Washington. He died of Covid-19.

name: John Konrads
headline: John Konrads, ‘Wonder Boy’ Olympian Swimmer, Dies at 78
abstract: A Hall of Famer, he was a sensation at the 1960 Games in Rome. He and his sister Ilsa, a champion in her own right, were known as “the Konrads Kids.”

name: James Prigoff
headline: James Prigoff, Who Documented Street Art, Dies at 93
abstract: In thousands of pictures, Mr. Prigoff captured the often ephemeral but complex works that were once dismissed as vandalism.

name: Olympia Dukakis
headline: Olympia Dukakis, Oscar Winner for ‘Moonstruck,’ Dies at 89
abstract: A veteran of the stage who also had a long list of film and TV credits, she was best known for playing characters who were worldly wise and world-weary.

name: Manisha Jadhav
headline: Manisha Jadhav, Key Administrator at Mumbai Hospital, Dies at 51
abstract: Dr. Jadhav took action when the pandemic hit last year, mustering personal protection equipment, food and transportation for the staff.

name: Fred Jordan
headline: Fred Jordan, Publisher of Taboo-Breaking Books, Dies at 95
abstract: At Grove Press, he and Barney Rosset challenged censors as they popularized D.H. Lawrence, Henry Miller, William S. Burroughs, Allen Ginsberg and others.

name: Jason Matthews
headline: Jason Matthews, C.I.A. Officer Turned Novelist, Dies at 69
abstract: After 33 years at the agency, he turned out three well-received novels that included realistic details of espionage — and appearances by Vladimir Putin.

name: Pete Lammons
profession: Helped the Jets Win 69 Super Bowl
headline: Pete Lammons, Who Helped the Jets Win ’69 Super Bowl, Dies at 77
abstract: After his football career, he bred racehorses and competed in professional fishing tournaments. He died after falling out of a boat in East Texas.

name: Bobby Unser
headline: Bobby Unser, Racing Clan’s Three-Time Indy 500 Winner, Dies at 87
abstract: Unser, who was afraid of heights, also captured the Pikes Peak climb race an unmatched 13 times.

name: Jacques d’Amboise
headline: Jacques d’Amboise, Charismatic Star of City Ballet, Is Dead at 86
abstract: He helped popularize ballet with an all-American style, combining the nonchalance of Fred Astaire with the nobility of a classic male dancer. Hollywood came calling, too.

name: Helen Murray Free
headline: Helen Murray Free Dies at 98; Chemist Developed Diabetes Test
abstract: She and her husband invented a dip-and-read paper strip that greatly simplified the diagnosis of the disease and paved the way for home test kits.

name: Patrick O’Connell
profession: Raised Awareness of AIDS With Art
headline: Patrick O’Connell, 67, Dies; Raised Awareness of AIDS With Art
abstract: As the founding director of Visual AIDS, he helped develop campaigns including “Day Without Art” and, most notably, the ubiquitous red ribbon.

name: Adam Kolton
profession: Led Fight to Protect Alaskan Refuge
headline: Adam Kolton, 53, Dies; Led Fight to Protect Alaskan Refuge
abstract: Through his work with environmental groups, he tried to prevent the introduction of oil and gas drilling in sensitive lands.

name: Tamara Press
headline: Tamara Press, Olympian Whose Feats Raised Questions, Dies at 83
abstract: She won three gold medals in the 1960s but was the focus of speculation about her gender. She retired after pulling out of a track meet that would have required a sex test.

name: Nancy Lassalle
headline: Nancy Lassalle, Longtime Promoter of Ballet, Dies at 93
abstract: In 1941 she studied at George Balanchine’s fledgling dance academy. She was not destined to be a ballerina, but she dedicated her life to Balanchine’s legacy.

name: Linda Love
profession: Crossing Guard With a Maternal Streak
headline: Linda Love, Crossing Guard With a Maternal Streak, Dies at 79
abstract: After decades on assembly lines, she brought the same affection she showed her family to the students she watched over as they headed to school. She died of Covid-19.

name: Vira Sathidar
headline: Vira Sathidar, Cultural Figure Who Fought India’s Caste System, Dies at 62
abstract: After a career of activism on behalf of the lower castes, Mr. Sathidar was cast in a movie that reflected his life. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Johnny Crawford
profession: Western Heros Son on The Rifleman
headline: Johnny Crawford, a Western Hero’s Son on ‘The Rifleman,’ Dies at 75
abstract: For five TV seasons he was at the side of Chuck Connors’s widowed sharpshooter. He also had some success as a pop singer, film actor and bandleader.

name: James Serritella
headline: James Serritella, Counselor in Church Sex-Abuse Crisis, Dies at 78
abstract: He advised four Chicago cardinals and advanced the U.S. bishops’ zero-tolerance policy toward clergy guilty of sex crimes.

name: William T. Wiley
headline: William T. Wiley, ‘Funk Artist’ Who Spurned Convention, Dies at 83
abstract: Rooted in the Bay Area, he disdained commerce (and the New York scene, mostly), produced an eclectic kind of figurative art and imparted his “Wiz-dumb” to disciples.

name: Lucinda Franks
headline: Lucinda Franks Dies at 74; Prize-Winning Journalist Broke Molds
abstract: She avoided covering beauty pageants by going to Northern Ireland on her own and was later the first woman to win a Pulitzer for national reporting.

name: David Swensen
headline: David Swensen, Who Revolutionized Endowment Investing, Dies at 67
abstract: At Yale, a colleague said, he showed “there was a way to compete hard and well in financial markets, but to have our lives be about something that mattered more.”

name: Sharon Pollock
headline: Sharon Pollock, Playwright Who Explored Canada’s Identity, Dies at 85
abstract: Ms. Pollock was best known for dramas inspired by historical events that examined racial tensions and other volatile issues.

name: Bob Abernethy
profession: Longtime Host of PBS Show on Religion
headline: Bob Abernethy, Longtime Host of PBS Show on Religion, Dies at 93
abstract: He conceived and produced “Religion & Ethics NewsWeekly” and was its face for 20 years, after four decades as an NBC News correspondent.

name: Milva
profession: Redheaded Italian Diva of Many Artistic Hues
headline: Milva, Redheaded Italian Diva of Many Artistic Hues, Dies at 81
abstract: One of Italy’s best-known singers, she sang pop songs and political anthems, and appeared at festivals and on theater stages.

name: Del Crandall
headline: Del Crandall, All-Star Catcher With Champion Braves, Dies at 91
abstract: In his 13 seasons with the team, first in Boston and then in Milwaukee, he helped lead them to two National League pennants and a World Series title.

name: Soli Sorabjee
profession: Eminent Indian Jurist and Jazz Lover
headline: Soli Sorabjee, Eminent Indian Jurist and Jazz Lover, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Sorabjee was a constitutional expert and free speech advocate who served two stints as the nation’s attorney general. He died of the coronavirus.

name: Michelangelo Lovelace
profession: Artist of Street Life in Cleveland
headline: Michelangelo Lovelace, Artist of Street Life in Cleveland, Dies at 60
abstract: His vibrant paintings of the urban Black experience, and his sketches of nursing home residents he cared for as an aide, drew increasing notice in his last years.

name: Paulo Gustavo
headline: Paulo Gustavo, Comedian Who Lampooned Brazilian Mothers, Dies at 42
abstract: Weeks before falling ill, he urged his countrymen to consider laughter “an act of resistance.” One of the country’s most beloved actors, he died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Pamela Kraft
profession: Arts Magnet and Champion of Indigenous Rights
headline: Pamela Kraft, 77, Dies; Arts Magnet and Champion of Indigenous Rights
abstract: She immersed herself in New York’s creative underground, then shifted to globetrotting activism for decades as the founder of Tribal Link.

name: Geoff Crowther
profession: Guided Travelers Looking to Get Lost
headline: Geoff Crowther, 77, Dies; Guided Travelers Looking to Get Lost
abstract: An early author for Lonely Planet, he tempted a generation of adventurers on journeys to exotic locales full of surprises.

name: Anita Lane
headline: Anita Lane, Rocker Who Was More Than a Muse, Is Dead at 61
abstract: Ms. Lane was Nick Cave’s collaborator and girlfriend during his formative period and helped define his sound. She also made records of her own.

name: Lyn Macdonald
profession: Preserved Voices of World War I
headline: Lyn Macdonald, Who Preserved Voices of World War I, Dies at 91
abstract: “The recording angel of the common soldier,” she chronicled the war in seven books from the soldiers’ perspective, drawing on 600 interviews with veterans.

name: Tawny Kitaen
headline: Tawny Kitaen, Star of 1980s Music Videos, Dies at 59
abstract: Ms. Kitaen gained fame for her carefree spirit and sultry dancing in music videos for bands like Whitesnake and Ratt and her role in the movie “Bachelor Party.”

name: Manzoor Ahtesham
headline: Manzoor Ahtesham, Writer Who Brought Bhopal to Life, Dies at 73
abstract: He focused with forensic precision on his native city, which was marked by an industrial tragedy in 1984. He was among the thousands in India to die of Covid-19 in the last few weeks.

name: Lloyd Price
headline: Lloyd Price, ‘Personality’ Hitmaker, Is Dead at 88
abstract: His “Lawdy Miss Clawdy” was a rhythm-and-blues smash that hooked white listeners in 1952, anticipating the rise of rock ’n’ roll. Even bigger records would follow.

name: Martin Bookspan
profession: Cultured Voice of Lincoln Center Telecasts
headline: Martin Bookspan, Cultured Voice of Lincoln Center Telecasts, Dies at 94
abstract: The longtime announcer for “Live From Lincoln Center,” he said he wanted his audience “to become involved, to love what they’re hearing.”

name: Ed Ward
headline: Ed Ward, Rock Critic and Historian, Is Dead at 72
abstract: His reviews for Crawdaddy, Rolling Stone and Creem were admired. But his tough criticism at The Austin American-Statesman inspired a “Dump Ed Ward” movement.

name: Pete du Pont
headline: Pete du Pont, Ex-Delaware Governor Who Ran for President, Dies at 86
abstract: Bored with working at his family’s chemical company, Mr. du Pont entered politics and led an economic turnaround of his debt-ridden home state.

name: George Jung
headline: George Jung, Who Made Millions Smuggling Cocaine, Dies at 78
abstract: Part of the Medellín drug cartel, he was imprisoned multiple times and was later played by Johnny Depp in the 2001 movie “Blow.”

name: Mohammad Ashraf Sehrai
headline: Mohammad Ashraf Sehrai, Kashmiri Separatist, Is Dead at 77
abstract: He was a close aide to the most powerful Kashmiri separatist leader for 50 years, but he was arrested a year ago and imprisoned. He died in a hospital of the coronavirus.

name: Helmut Jahn
headline: Helmut Jahn, ‘Convention-Busting’ Architect, Dies at 81
abstract: He helped redefine Chicago architecture with his postmodern designs of the Thompson Center and the United Airlines terminal at O’Hare International Airport. But he was also known worldwide.

name: Chandro Tomar
profession: Shot Her Way Through a Glass Ceiling
headline: Chandro Tomar, Who Shot Her Way Through a Glass Ceiling, Dies
abstract: Born in 1931, she found her calling late in life but inspired thousands of people, especially women and girls, through her passion for the sport of shooting.

name: Pat Bond
headline: Pat Bond, a Sexual-Subculture Pioneer, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Bond was a 44-year-old music teacher when he founded an organization for masochists. After a few meetings, sadists were also invited.

name: Robert Slavin
headline: Robert Slavin, Who Studied How Children Learn, Dies at 70
abstract: He favored phonics to teach reading and grouping students with different aptitudes rather than by age or grade.

name: Bill McCreary
profession: Blazed Trail for Black Journalists on TV
headline: Bill McCreary Dies at 87; Blazed Trail for Black Journalists on TV
abstract: He was hired at what became the Fox flagship station in New York in 1967, when there were few Black faces on the air, and became an Emmy-winning anchor.

name: Norman Lloyd
headline: Norman Lloyd, Associate of Welles, Hitchcock and Others, Dies at 106
abstract: He was seen in movies and on TV shows like “St. Elsewhere” and worked with some of the biggest names in show business, even though his own name was little known.

name: Lester L. Wolff
headline: Lester L. Wolff, Influential Former Congressman, Dies at 102
abstract: A Democrat from New York, he championed Great Society programs like Medicare, helped navigate U.S. relations in Asia and fought against drug trafficking.

name: Bibi Romeiza John
headline: Bibi Romeiza John, Home Health Aide in Queens, Dies at 48
abstract: She, her husband and one of his sons all contracted Covid at the same time; they recovered, but she did not.

name: Billie Hayes
headline: Billie Hayes, Memorable Witch on ‘H.R. Pufnstuf,’ Dies at 96
abstract: Ms. Hayes had quite a cackle, and it served her well in a number of witchy roles, beginning in 1969 on a short-lived but much remembered TV series.

name: Spencer Silver
headline: Spencer Silver, an Inventor of Post-it Notes, Is Dead at 80
abstract: He created the adhesive that lets the small, square notes stick to surfaces. They became one of the most ubiquitous office products ever conceived.

name: Eugene Webb
headline: Eugene Webb, Leading Harlem Real Estate Broker, Dies at 102
abstract: Raised in Alabama, he made his fortune in New York and became a banker, civic leader and developer.

name: Usha Mehta
profession: Freedom Fighter Against British Rule in India
headline: Overlooked No More: Usha Mehta, Freedom Fighter Against British Rule in India
abstract: At 22, she helped establish the underground station Congress Radio, which amplified Mahatma Gandhi’s message of rebellion.

name: William R. Harris
profession: Hoped to Curb Risks of Nuclear War
headline: William R. Harris Dies at 79; Hoped to Curb Risks of Nuclear War
abstract: A lawyer and policy analyst, he studied ways to forestall energy crises and other catastrophes. He died of Covid-19.

name: Curtis Fuller
headline: Curtis Fuller, a Powerful Voice on Jazz Trombone, Dies at 88
abstract: He was a fixture on the New York jazz scene since shortly after his arrival in 1957. He also made his mark as a composer.

name: Pervis Staples
headline: Pervis Staples, Who Harmonized With the Staple Singers, Dies at 85
abstract: He sang alongside his father and sisters as his family’s gospel group achieved renown in the late 1950s and ’60s.

name: Chad Kalepa Baybayan
headline: Chad Kalepa Baybayan, Seafarer Who Sailed Using the Stars, Dies at 64
abstract: He was a torchbearer for the celestial navigation art known as wayfinding, which ancestral Polynesian sailors used to navigate the Pacific Ocean.

name: Barbara Stone
headline: Barbara Stone, Modeling Agent to American Beauties, Dies at 87
abstract: At Stewart Models in the 1960s and ’70s, she specialized in fresh-faced American blondes and played a key role in the careers of Cheryl Tiegs and Cybill Shepherd.

name: Bob Koester
profession: Revered Figure in Jazz and Blues
headline: Bob Koester, Revered Figure in Jazz and Blues, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Koester’s Delmark Records and his Chicago record store were vital in preserving and promoting music the big labels tended to overlook.

name: Eula Hall
headline: Eula Hall, One-Woman Relief Agency in Appalachia, Dies at 93
abstract: Calling herself a “hillbilly activist,” she started a health care clinic and offered other services in chronically underserved eastern Kentucky.

name: Yitzhak Arad
profession: Led Holocaust Study Center in Israel
headline: Yitzhak Arad, Who Led Holocaust Study Center in Israel, Dies at 94
abstract: A survivor of the Nazis, Mr. Arad was an esteemed scholar and the longtime chairman of the Yad Vashem complex of museums and archives in Jerusalem.

name: Leigh Perkins
profession: Built Orvis Into a Lifestyle Brand
headline: Leigh Perkins, Who Built Orvis Into a Lifestyle Brand, Dies at 93
abstract: In 28 years at the company’s helm, he turned a small mail-order fishing tackle shop into a sporting brand with stores all over the country.

name: Damon Weaver
headline: Damon Weaver, Child Reporter Who Interviewed Obama, Dies at 23
abstract: At 11 years old, Mr. Weaver gained national attention when he scored an interview with President Barack Obama, making him one of the youngest people to interview a sitting president.

name: Jack Terricloth
profession: Punk Rocker With a Cabaret Air
headline: Jack Terricloth, Punk Rocker With a Cabaret Air, Dies at 50
abstract: As the devilishly smarmy vocalist and ringleader of the World/Inferno Friendship Society, he melded punk defiance with decadent theatricality.

name: Katherine Barber
headline: Katherine Barber, Who Defined Canadian English, Is Dead at 61
abstract: As the founding editor of the Canadian Oxford Dictionary, she turned to “trashy novels” and parliamentary debates to find Canada’s version of the language.

name: Art Gensler
headline: Art Gensler Dies at 85; Built a Global Architecture Firm
abstract: His buildings include China’s tallest skyscraper, in Shanghai, and the terminals at San Francisco International Airport.

name: Buddy Roemer
headline: Buddy Roemer, Reformer as a Louisiana Governor, Dies at 77
abstract: He came into office as the answer to the scandal-plagued Edwin Edwards administration but was nevertheless ousted by Mr. Edwards four years later.

name: Charles Grodin
profession: Star of Beethoven and Heartbreak Kid
headline: Charles Grodin, Star of ‘Beethoven’ and ‘Heartbreak Kid,’ Dies at 86
abstract: A familiar face who was especially adept at deadpan comedy, he also appeared on Broadway in “Same Time, Next Year,” wrote books and had his own talk show.

name: Jim Klobuchar
headline: Jim Klobuchar Dies at 93; Minnesota Newspaperman and Amy’s Father
abstract: He rose to folk hero status with his derring-do as a journalist and came to national attention when his daughter, Senator Amy Klobuchar, spoke openly about his struggles with alcoholism.

name: Aaron Stern
headline: Dr. Aaron Stern, Who Enforced the Movie Ratings Code, Dies at 96
abstract: He was a New York psychiatrist who went to Hollywood to help lay down guidelines for sex and violence in films. Not everyone was pleased.

name: Paul Mooney
profession: Trailblazing Comedian and Richard Pryor Collaborator
headline: Paul Mooney, Trailblazing Comedian and Richard Pryor Collaborator, Dies at 79
abstract: He was known for his boundary-pushing routines about racism and social justice and for his work with Pryor and on “In Living Color” and “Chappelle’s Show.”

name: Franco Battiato
headline: Franco Battiato, Pop Singer and Versatile Composer, Dies at 76
abstract: Though hugely popular as a singer-songwriter in Italy, he never stopped experimenting. He composed for movies, opera and ballet, directed films and painted.

name: Jim Clendenen
headline: Jim Clendenen, Santa Barbara Winemaking Pioneer, Dies at 68
abstract: With exuberant charisma and relentless traveling, he promoted his label, Au Bon Climat, and the region as a wine hub.

name: Lee Evans
headline: Lee Evans, Olympic Runner Who Protested Racism, Dies at 74
abstract: One of several Black athletes who had threatened to boycott the 1968 Summer Games, he won two gold medals, then raised his fist at the presentation ceremony.

name: David Wake
headline: David Wake, Expert on Salamanders and Evolution, Dies at 84
abstract: While on a college field trip to collect beetles, he found salamanders. He became an authority and later grew alarmed by the disappearance of many amphibians.

name: Margaret Rossi
profession: Gift Shop Matriarch in Little Italy
headline: Margaret Rossi, Gift Shop Matriarch in Little Italy, Dies at 72
abstract: Despite rising rents and the pandemic, “In her heart she wanted to keep it going,” her husband said of their business. She died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Rennie Stennett
headline: Rennie Stennett, Pirate Who Had Seven Hits in a Game, Dies at 72
abstract: A second baseman, he was part of baseball’s first all-minority lineup in 1971, along with the future Hall of Famers Roberto Clemente and Willie Stargell.

name: Mary Ahern
profession: Produced Early TV and Then Preserved It
headline: Mary Ahern, Who Produced Early TV and Then Preserved It, Dies at 98
abstract: She was a key behind-the-scenes figure in the landmark series “Omnibus” before becoming the Paley Center for Media’s first curator.

name: Paul Van Doren
profession: Built an Empire With Vans Shoes
headline: Paul Van Doren, 90, Dies; Built an Empire With Vans Shoes
abstract: The sneakers became a hit in the skateboard world and later a multibillion-dollar nationwide sensation thanks in part to a Sean Penn movie.

name: Rahul Vohra
headline: Rahul Vohra, Indian Actor and Video Blogger, Dies at 35
abstract: His YouTube posts dissected issues of Indian life, especially gender inequality. He died of complications of Covid-19 after lamenting his hospital treatment.

name: Roman Kent
profession: Reminded the World of the Holocaust
headline: Roman Kent, Who Reminded the World of the Holocaust, Dies at 92
abstract: He galvanized survivors into a movement to memorialize the Holocaust and spoke often of his experience. “I didn’t want our past to become our children’s future,” he said.

name: Arthur Pomposello
profession: Impresario for a Cabaret Swan Song
headline: Arthur Pomposello, Impresario for a Cabaret Swan Song, Dies at 85
abstract: He was the host at the Oak Room of the Algonquin Hotel during an improbable resurgence of cabaret from the 1980s to the early 2000s. He died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Jerome Kagan
headline: Jerome Kagan, Who Tied Temperament to Biology, Dies at 92
abstract: A Harvard psychologist, he originally attributed personality traits to nurturing only. Then he concluded, We’re largely born this way.

name: Joan Schenkar
headline: Joan Schenkar, Biographer of Patricia Highsmith, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Schenkar was also known for experimental plays. In one, a reimagining of the Red Riding Hood story, Grandma was a butcher.

name: Mark Levitan
profession: Measured the True Face of Poverty
headline: Mark Levitan, Who Measured the True Face of Poverty, Dies at 73
abstract: He came up with a more realistic threshold, changing the way New York City determines who is impoverished and persuading the Obama White House to follow suit.

name: Terence Riley
profession: Architectural Force in the Museum World
headline: Terence Riley, Architectural Force in the Museum World, Dies at 66
abstract: He was the chief architectural curator at MoMA, overseeing shows and the museum’s massive redesign, then moving on to the Miami art world.

name: Ruth Freitag
headline: Ruth Freitag, Librarian to the Stars, Dies at 96
abstract: An expert on astronomy, she spent nearly a half-century at the Library of Congress and helped Isaac Asimov and Carl Sagan with research.

name: Kathleen Andrews
profession: Helped Give Ziggy and Others Their Start
headline: Kathleen Andrews Dies at 84; Helped Give Ziggy and Others Their Start
abstract: As a top executive at the Andrews McMeel syndicate, she played a key role in the careers of Tom Wilson, Cathy Guisewite and Garry Trudeau.

name: Roger Hawkins
headline: Roger Hawkins, Drummer Heard on Numerous Hits, Is Dead at 75
abstract: An innately soulful musician, he recorded with Aretha Franklin, Wilson Pickett and many others and was an architect of what became known as the Muscle Shoals sound.

name: Paul J. Hanly Jr.
headline: Paul J. Hanly Jr., Top Litigator in Opioid Cases, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Hanly had been central to the current nationwide litigation against pharmaceutical companies, pharmacies and others in the opioid supply chain.

name: Yuan Longping
headline: Yuan Longping, Plant Scientist Who Helped Curb Famine, Dies at 90
abstract: His development of high-yield rice hybrids in the 1970s led to steeply rising harvests in Asia and Africa and made him a national hero in China, credited with saving countless lives.

name: Richard Nonas
profession: Explored Art and the Space It Inhabits
headline: Richard Nonas, Who Explored Art and the Space It Inhabits, Dies at 85
abstract: A part of the early-1970s art scene in SoHo and TriBeCa, he created Post-Minimalist sculptures out of steel, stone and wood.

name: Shirley Kost
headline: Shirley Kost, Baseball’s ‘Cookie Lady,’ Dies at 82
abstract: Mrs. Kost would bestow cookies on her beloved Texas Rangers — players, coaches and employees — at home games. She died of complications of the coronavirus.

name: Max Mosley
profession: Motor Racing Chief and Embattled Privacy Advocate
headline: Max Mosley, Motor Racing Chief and Embattled Privacy Advocate, Dies at 81
abstract: The son of Nazi sympathizers sought to separate himself from his parents, but was bogged down by a secretly recorded sex video later in life.

name: Mark York
headline: Mark York, Actor on ‘The Office,’ Dies at 55
abstract: An advocate for greater onscreen visibility for people with disabilities, he was seen on the hit NBC sitcom as Billy Merchant, who like him used a wheelchair.

name: Joel Chadabe
headline: Joel Chadabe, Explorer of Electronic Music’s Frontier, Dies at 82
abstract: As both a composer and an advocate, Mr. Chadabe devoted himself to what one music critic called the “marriage between humans and their computers.”

name: Kentaro Miura
headline: Kentaro Miura, Creator of Epic Manga ‘Berserk,’ Dies at 54
abstract: For more than 30 years he reached tens of millions of readers worldwide with a fantastical tale of vulnerable characters in an apocalyptic world.

name: Robbie McCauley
headline: Robbie McCauley, Stage Artist Who Explored Race, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. McCauley often put race at the center of plays and other works that sought to alter perspectives and foster dialogue.

name: John Warner
headline: John Warner, Genteel Senator From Virginia, Dies at 94
abstract: In his 30 years in the Senate, the former Navy secretary was a leading Republican voice on military policy. He was once married to Elizabeth Taylor.

name: Janine Brookner
headline: Janine Brookner, Punished C.I.A. Officer Who Got Revenge, Dies at 80
abstract: She had been a successful operative and station chief when staffers made dubious allegations that forced her from the field. She sued the C.I.A. — and won.

name: Anna Halprin
headline: Anna Halprin Dies at 100; Choreographer Committed to Experimenting
abstract: Her work, which stressed improvisation, attracted students, disciples and enthusiasts fascinated by the creative issues she explored and the way she explored them.

name: Eric Carle
profession: Author of The Very Hungry Caterpillar
headline: Eric Carle, Author of ‘The Very Hungry Caterpillar,’ Dies at 91
abstract: A self-described “picture writer,” he wrote and illustrated more than 70 books for young children, selling more than 170 million copies.

name: Mary Beth Edelson
headline: Mary Beth Edelson, Feminist Art Pioneer, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Her revision of “The Last Supper” was a defining image for the movement in the ’70s, and her ritualistic performances would be an influence for decades.

name: Samuel E. Wright
profession: Voice of Sebastian in The Little Mermaid
headline: Samuel E. Wright, the Voice of Sebastian in ‘The Little Mermaid,’ Dies at 72
abstract: Mr. Wright also worked on Broadway, earning a Tony nomination as Mufasa in the original cast of “The Lion King.”

name: Walter Kissinger
headline: Walter Kissinger, Businessman and Brother of Henry, Dies at 96
abstract: Walter shed his Bavarian accent while Henry notably did not. Asked why he lost his, Walter told interviewers, “Because I am the Kissinger who listens.”

name: Si-lan Chen
headline: Overlooked No More: Si-lan Chen, Whose Dances Encompassed Worlds
abstract: As a dancer and choreographer, she sought to represent a broad range of ethnic groups, but audiences often sexualized and exoticized her by focusing on her mixed race.

name: Kay Tobin Lahusen
headline: Kay Tobin Lahusen, Gay Rights Activist and Photographer, Dies at 91
abstract: She and her partner, Barbara Gittings, were on the front lines long before Stonewall, and Ms. Lahusen photographed protests during the movement’s earliest days.

name: Harvey Schlossberg
profession: Cop With a Ph.D. in Defusing a Crisis
headline: Harvey Schlossberg, Cop With a Ph.D. in Defusing a Crisis, Dies at 85
abstract: A psychologist who had worn the blue, he coached thousands of New York City police officers in hostage negotiations, creating a model for law enforcement.

name: Rusty Warren
profession: Brash Comic in a Strait-Laced Time
headline: Rusty Warren, Brash Comic in a Strait-Laced Time, Dies at 91
abstract: In the 1950s and ’60s, Ms. Warren made sex the central subject of her nightclub routines, and of popular comedy albums like “Knockers Up!”

name: Alix Dobkin
headline: Alix Dobkin, Who Sang Songs of Liberation, Dies at 80
abstract: She broke new ground in 1973 with her album “Lavender Jane Loves Women,” recorded and distributed by women for women, which sketched out a lesbian separatist utopia.

name: Faye Schulman
profession: Fought Nazis With a Rifle and a Camera
headline: Faye Schulman Dies; Fought Nazis With a Rifle and a Camera
abstract: She joined the Resistance brigade after her family was executed and used her photographs as proof of German barbarity and Jews’ determination to fight back.

name: Christopher Stone
headline: Christopher Stone, Who Proposed Legal Rights for Trees, Dies at 83
abstract: A law review article he wrote in 1972 kick-started a worldwide movement to grant nature the same rights enjoyed by human beings.

name: Carla Fracci
headline: Carla Fracci, Expressive Doyenne of Italian Ballet, Dies at 84
abstract: A major figure in 20th-century dance, she was acclaimed for her directness and emotional naturalness onstage, especially in the title role of “Giselle.”

name: Foster Friess
headline: Foster Friess, Big Donor to Republicans, Dies at 81
abstract: A conservative Christian and wealthy businessman, he gave millions to Rick Santorum and Donald Trump in their presidential bids.

name: Wimar Witoelar
headline: Wimar Witoelar, Puckish Spokesman for Indonesian President, Dies at 75
abstract: As a college student, he was briefly imprisoned for his activism. He later served President Abdurrahman Wahid and had a thriving career as a media figure.

name: Margherita Marchione
headline: Sister Margherita Marchione, Defender of Pius XII, Dies at 99
abstract: She spent decades arguing that the pope had helped the Jews during World War II, despite accusations that he had abdicated his moral responsibility.

name: Thomas Sullivan
headline: Thomas Sullivan Dies at 91; Investigated Corruption in Chicago’s Courts
abstract: He helped start an undercover sting that led to the convictions of judges, lawyers and sheriffs. As a renowned lawyer in high-profile cases he helped end capital punishment in Illinois.

name: Gavin MacLeod
profession: Mary Tyler Moore and Love Boat Actor
headline: Gavin MacLeod, ‘Mary Tyler Moore’ and ‘Love Boat’ Actor, Dies at 90
abstract: After years as a journeyman with a long list of credits but little name recognition, he found stardom on two of the biggest television hits of the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Chi Modu
headline: Chi Modu, Photographer Who Defined 1990s Hip-Hop, Dies at 54
abstract: His images of the Notorious B.I.G., Tupac Shakur, Dr. Dre and many more helped shape rap music’s visual identity.

name: B.J. Thomas
profession: Raindrops Keep Fallin on My Head Singer
headline: B.J. Thomas, ‘Raindrops Keep Fallin’ on My Head’ Singer, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Thomas, who won five Grammys, helped introduce a smooth, down-home sensibility to the AM radio airwaves in the 1960s and ’70s.

name: D.M. Thomas
profession: His White Hotel Was a Surprise Best Seller
headline: D.M. Thomas, 88, Dies; His ‘White Hotel’ Was a Surprise Best Seller
abstract: A former English teacher with a modest writing career in Britain, he found fame in 1981 with an inventive story of an opera singer, Freud and the Holocaust.

name: Lois Ehlert
profession: Creator of Boldly Colored Childrens Books
headline: Lois Ehlert, Creator of Boldly Colored Children’s Books, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Ehlert, whose best-known book was “Chicka Chicka Boom Boom,” made distinctive collage artwork for readers ranging in age from infancy to 10.

name: Mark Eaton
profession: Shot-Blocking Star for the Utah Jazz
headline: Mark Eaton, Shot-Blocking Star for the Utah Jazz, Dies at 64
abstract: At 7-foot-4, Eaton was a two-time N.B.A. defensive player of the year, and his career shot-blocking average was the best in league history.

name: Josep Almudéver
profession: Last Known Veteran of International Brigades
headline: Josep Almudéver, 101, Dies; Last Known Veteran of International Brigades
abstract: He was one of many of the Brigades’ volunteers who viewed Spain’s Civil War as a broader fight against the advance of Fascism across Europe.

name: Raimund Hoghe
headline: Raimund Hoghe, Choreographer of Strength and Frailty, Dies at 72
abstract: Born with a spinal deformity, he doubted he could ever dance, but he was able to incorporate his physical handicaps into his performances.

name: David Anthony Kraft
headline: David Anthony Kraft, Comic Book Writer and Chronicler, Dies at 68
abstract: He worked on The Defenders, Captain America and Man-Wolf early in his career. He died of complications of the coronavirus.

name: Dan Frank
headline: Dan Frank, Adventurous Book Editor, Is Dead at 67
abstract: As head of Pantheon, he nurtured prize winners and best sellers, rescued Joseph Mitchell from obscurity and helped establish graphic novels as a literary genre.

name: Jerome Hellman
headline: Jerome Hellman, Producer of ‘Midnight Cowboy,’ Dies at 92
abstract: His movie-producing career consisted of just seven films, but they earned him six Academy Awards, three for “Midnight Cowboy” and three for “Coming Home.”

name: Mike Marshall
profession: First Relief Pitcher to Win Cy Young Award
headline: Mike Marshall, 78, First Relief Pitcher to Win Cy Young Award, Dies
abstract: Dominant and durable, he appeared in a record 106 games for the 1974 pennant-winning Dodgers. His tools? A screwball and a doctorate in physiology.

name: Arthur Staats
profession: Called Time Out for Unruly Kids
headline: Arthur Staats Dies at 97; Called ‘Time Out’ for Unruly Kids
abstract: A behavioral psychologist, he advised that it was more productive to briefly isolate a misbehaving child than to spank or yell. Thus a household phrase was born.

name: Sophie Rivera
headline: Sophie Rivera, Photographer of Latin New York, Dies at 82
abstract: Her portraits of fellow Puerto Rican New Yorkers could be both majestic and tender. She was also a constant street photographer and later made herself her subject.

name: Ellen Vales
headline: Ellen Vales, a Caretaker in Many Forms, Dies at 73
abstract: She spent her life cooking and caring for others until she died of Covid-19.

name: Susan Cole
headline: Susan Cole, Advocate for Traumatized Children, Dies at 72
abstract: Ms. Cole examined the link between abuse at home and problems in the classroom, and sought to make schools “trauma sensitive.”

name: Friederike Mayröcker
headline: Friederike Mayröcker, Grande Dame in German Literature, Dies at 96
abstract: An Austrian, she was among the most decorated German-language poets of the postwar period, producing a large body of daring work.

name: Ganga Stone
headline: Ganga Stone, Who Gave Sustenance to AIDS Patients, Dies at 79
abstract: At the height of the AIDS epidemic, she started God’s Love We Deliver, a charity that brought hot meals to people who were too ill to cook.

name: Patrick Sky
profession: 60s Folk Star and Later a Piper
headline: Patrick Sky, ’60s Folk Star and Later a Piper, Dies at 80
abstract: He was a part of the folk revival emanating from Greenwich Village, mixing melodic songs and satire. Then he became infatuated with the uilleann pipes.

name: Yoshi Wada
headline: Yoshi Wada, Inventive Creator of Sound Worlds, Dies at 77
abstract: A member of the Fluxus performance art movement (and a contractor by trade), he incorporated bagpipes, electronics and, yes, plumber’s materials in his music.

name: Richard Rubenstein
headline: Richard Rubenstein, 97, Dies; Theologian Challenged Ideas of God
abstract: A rabbi, educator and author of a landmark book, he asked, “How can Jews believe in an omnipotent, beneficent God after Auschwitz?”

name: Raymond Donovan
profession: Labor Secretary Quit Under a Cloud
headline: Raymond Donovan, 90, Dies; Labor Secretary Quit Under a Cloud
abstract: He faced fraud charges when he left the Reagan administration, but a jury acquitted him, leaving him to ask, “Which office do I go to to get my reputation back?”

name: Graeme Ferguson
headline: Graeme Ferguson, Filmmaker Who Helped Create Imax, Dies at 91
abstract: He partnered with friends to produce stunning original technology that would give movie viewers an immersive, stadium-like experience.

name: Clarence Williams III
headline: Clarence Williams III, a Star of ‘Mod Squad,’ Is Dead at 81
abstract: He portrayed Linc Hayes, a hip undercover police officer who was teamed with Peggy Lipton and Michael Cole.

name: David Dushman
headline: David Dushman, Soviet Soldier Who Helped Liberate Auschwitz, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Dushman is believed to have been the last surviving liberator of the camp. He went on to become a decorated fencer.

name: Richard Robinson
headline: Richard Robinson Dies at 84; Turned Scholastic Into an Empire
abstract: With help from Harry Potter, the Magic School Bus and the Baby-Sitters Club, he created the largest publisher and distributor of children’s books.

name: Robert Hollander
headline: Robert Hollander, Who Led Readers Into ‘The Inferno,’ Dies at 87
abstract: He and his wife wrote an admired translation of Dante’s “Divine Comedy,” and he began an innovative project to digitize centuries of scholarly commentary.

name: Douglas Cramer
profession: Producer of Dynasty and The Love Boat
headline: Douglas Cramer, Producer of ‘Dynasty’ and ‘The Love Boat,’ Dies at 89
abstract: He had a hand in some of the biggest shows of the 20th century, often in partnership with Aaron Spelling. He was also a leading art collector.

name: Jim Fassel
headline: Jim Fassel Bridged Giants Eras With a Smile. And, Once, a Rant.
abstract: The Giants coach called Gentleman Jim was best known for smoothly transitioning the team out of the Bill Parcells era, but one uncharacteristic tirade stood out.

name: Cornelia Oberlander
