headline: Cornelia Oberlander, a Farsighted Landscape Architect, Dies at 99
abstract: Her acclaimed modernist but naturalist designs recognized the fragility of the climate and the social effects of parks and playgrounds.

name: Stuart Silver
headline: Stuart Silver, Designer of Museum Blockbusters, Dies at 84
abstract: He helped reinvigorate the Metropolitan and made its exhibitions into crowd-pleasing spectacles, providing a model for other fine-art museums across the country.

name: Michael Smith
headline: Michael Smith, a Voice for Justice Reform, Is Dead at 78
abstract: As head of the Vera Institute in New York, he spurred community policing and pressed for easing bail, profoundly influencing the law enforcement agenda.

name: Ron Hill
headline: Ron Hill, Marathoner Who Set Record in Boston, Dies at 82
abstract: In 1970 he shaved more than three minutes off the earlier mark. He later set another record: running at least a mile a day for 52 years and 39 days (even after surgery).

name: Jessica Morris
headline: Jessica Morris, Whose Brain Cancer Was Her Cause, Dies at 57
abstract: After her diagnosis of glioblastoma in 2016, she founded an organization that advocated for patients and research.

name: Violetta Elvin
headline: Violetta Elvin, Glamorous Royal Ballet Dancer, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Celebrated for her strong technique and natural grandeur, she was a star soloist with the Bolshoi Ballet before finding a new audience in London.

name: Gottfried Böhm
headline: Gottfried Böhm, Master Architect in Concrete, Dies at 101
abstract: A recipient of his field’s highest award, he was known for his Brutalist designs, of churches in particular, in a postwar Germany trying to rebuild itself.

name: Robert Katzmann
profession: U.S. Judge With Reach Beyond the Bench
headline: Robert Katzmann, U.S. Judge With Reach Beyond the Bench, Dies at 68
abstract: As chief of the Second Circuit in New York, he championed immigrants’ rights, judicial transparency and schooling the public on the law. In 2019 he dealt Trump a blow.

name: William Clinger Jr.
headline: William Clinger Jr., 92, Dies; Led House Inquiries on Clinton
abstract: A nine-term Pennsylvania Republican, he oversaw investigations into the so-called Travelgate and Filegate matters. The Clintons were exonerated in both.

name: Herb Sturz
profession: Quiet Force in the Life of New York City
headline: Herb Sturz, a Quiet Force in the Life of New York City, Dies at 90
abstract: His agenda and reach, in government and out, extended from criminal justice to urban planning, though his constituency — prisoners, the homeless, the elderly and more — hardly knew his name.

name: Jobriath
profession: Openly Gay Glam Rocker in the 70s
headline: Overlooked No More: Jobriath, Openly Gay Glam Rocker in the ’70s
abstract: His space alien persona and theatrical rock music drew comparisons to David Bowie’s Ziggy Stardust character. But American audiences seemed unwilling to accept his sexuality.

name: Martha White
profession: Before Rosa Parks, She Sparked a Bus Boycott
headline: Martha White, 99, Dies; Before Rosa Parks, She Sparked a Bus Boycott
abstract: The 1953 protest in Baton Rouge, triggered by her ejection from a bus for sitting in a “whites only” section, became a template for Martin Luther King.

name: Rezo Gabriadze
headline: Rezo Gabriadze, Who Created Magic Out of Puppetry, Dies at 84
abstract: His productions, vivid and fanciful, played all over the world, including at Lincoln Center.

name: Milton Moses Ginsberg
headline: Milton Moses Ginsberg, 85, Unconventional Filmmaker, Dies
abstract: His movies about a psychiatrist’s disintegration and a werewolf in the White House originally bombed, but they both drew favorable attention many years later.

name: Mudcat Grant
headline: Mudcat Grant, American League’s First Black 20-Game Winner, Dies at 85
abstract: After 14 major league seasons, he wrote a book about Black pitchers and sang in nightclubs. “I made way more money in music than I did in baseball,” he said.

name: Donald York
profession: Musical Director of Paul Taylor Company
headline: Donald York, Musical Director of Paul Taylor Company, Dies at 73
abstract: Mr. York, a former child prodigy who was raised on jazz and choral music, wrote scores that matched Mr. Taylor’s eclectic choreography.

name: Ned Beatty
profession: Actor Known for Network and Deliverance
headline: Ned Beatty, Actor Known for ‘Network’ and ‘Deliverance,’ Dies at 83
abstract: In a career that spanned more than four decades and more than 150 movie and TV roles, Mr. Beatty was rarely the star but almost always made a strong impression.

name: Karla Burns
profession: Broke a British Tonys Color Barrier
headline: Karla Burns, Who Broke a ‘British Tonys’ Color Barrier, Dies at 66
abstract: Her Olivier Award was for her signature role as Queenie in “Show Boat,” a part that once earned a Tony nomination. She later lost her voice in surgery and fought to regain it.

name: Carol Jarecki
headline: Carol Jarecki, Respected Chess Referee, Dies at 86
abstract: She was known for her practical, no-nonsense approach at scores of major tournaments. She was also a pilot and a nurse and, with her husband, conquered the game of roulette.

name: Richard Baron
headline: Richard Baron, Who Published Baldwin and Mailer, Dies at 98
abstract: As the risk-taking publisher of the Dial Press, he also released the satirical hoax “Report From Iron Mountain,” a “leaked” government report on the dangers of peace.

name: Lisa Banes
headline: Lisa Banes, Film and Stage Actress, Dies at 65
abstract: A mainstay of the New York stage, she also acted in films, including “Gone Girl.” She died 10 days after she was struck by a scooter as she was crossing a street in Manhattan.

name: William vanden Heuvel
headline: William vanden Heuvel, Diplomat and a Kennedy Confidant, Dies at 91
abstract: A lawyer, he was an adviser to Robert F. Kennedy, led Jimmy Carter’s New York campaign and targeted jail conditions as head of New York City’s corrections board.

name: Jack B. Weinstein
profession: U.S. Judge With an Activist Streak
headline: Jack B. Weinstein, U.S. Judge With an Activist Streak, Is Dead at 99
abstract: In 53 years on the bench and nearly a decade as the chief judge of the Eastern District of New York, he was known for his bold jurisprudence and his outsize personality.

name: Lee Ross
profession: Expert in Why We Misunderstand Each Other
headline: Lee Ross, Expert in Why We Misunderstand Each Other, Dies at 78
abstract: His argument about how social situations, not personality, can govern behavior took hold in modern psychology and inspired thinkers like Malcolm Gladwell.

name: Brigitte Gerney
headline: Brigitte Gerney, ‘Crane Lady’ Who Survived Collapse, Dies at 85
abstract: Her legs were crushed when she was trapped for six hours in Manhattan in 1985, touching off a media frenzy. Miraculously, she was able to walk again.

name: Richard R. Ernst
headline: Richard R. Ernst, Nobelist Who Paved Way for M.R.I., Dies at 87
abstract: His development of advanced analytical techniques formed the basis for M.R.I. technology used in hospitals and helped chemists determine the structure of complex molecules.

name: Janet Malcolm
profession: Provocative Journalist With a Piercing Eye
headline: Janet Malcolm, Provocative Journalist With a Piercing Eye, Dies at 86
abstract: Her subjects ranged widely, but she took special aim at journalism itself, writing that every journalist “knows that what he does is morally indefensible.”

name: Eva Sereny
headline: Eva Sereny, Who Photographed Film Stars at Work, Dies at 86
abstract: She captured De Niro, Streep, Eastwood and many others, often in unguarded moments. Working with directors like Fellini and Spielberg inspired her to make movies herself.

name: Kenneth Kaunda
headline: Kenneth Kaunda, Patriarch of African Independence, Is Dead at 97
abstract: As Zambia’s first president, he dominated his country, outliving many of the other frontline leaders who had sponsored southern Africa’s guerrilla wars.

name: Saul B. Cohen
headline: Saul B. Cohen, Who Helped Raise CUNY Standards, Dies at 95
abstract: As president of Queens College and a state regent, Dr. Cohen, a renowned geographer, brokered a compromise to end the open admissions policy.

name: Frank Bonner
profession: Brash Salesman on WKRP in Cincinnati
headline: Frank Bonner, Brash Salesman on ‘WKRP in Cincinnati,’ Dies at 79
abstract: He played the memorably obnoxious Herb Tarlek for all four seasons of the popular sitcom set at a radio station, and reprised the role on a sequel show a decade later.

name: Madeline Davis
profession: Spoke to the Nation as a Lesbian
headline: Madeline Davis, Who Spoke to the Nation as a Lesbian, Dies at 80
abstract: She was the first openly gay woman to speak to a major party’s national convention, asking Democrats in 1972 to include an anti-discrimination plank in their platform.

name: Allen Midgette
headline: Allen Midgette, an Ersatz Andy Warhol, Dies at 82
abstract: In a prank, or perhaps a piece of performance art, Mr. Midgette pretended to be the famed artist on a lecture tour in 1967.

name: Frances Stein
profession: Fashion Force at Chanel and Elsewhere
headline: Frances Stein, a Fashion Force at Chanel and Elsewhere, Dies at 83
abstract: Halston hired her to design his first collections. She worked with Calvin Klein. And she helped make Chanel newly relevant when it was floundering in the 1970s.

name: Edward Diener
headline: Edward Diener, Psychologist Known as Dr. Happiness, Dies at 74
abstract: Since the 1980s, he was recognized as a leader in measuring what he called “subjective well-being.” And, yes, he was very happy.

name: George Stranahan
profession: Benefactor of Physicists and Bar Flies
headline: George Stranahan, Benefactor of Physicists and Bar Flies, Dies at 89
abstract: A venturesome millionaire, he forged an only-in-America career in fields ranging from craft beer to free speech activism to scientific research.

name: Enrique Bolaños
headline: Enrique Bolaños, Former President of Nicaragua, Dies at 93
abstract: A conservative leader who fought corruption and pushed for economic progress, Mr. Bolaños believed that his country was in a time of crisis.

name: Karl Wirsum
headline: Karl Wirsum, Dynamic and Eclectic Chicago Artist, Dies at 81
abstract: A member of the small but influential group known as the Hairy Who, he built his art on a highly original synthesis of multiple sources.

name: Robert Quackenbush
headline: Robert Quackenbush, Creator of Animal Detective Stories, Dies at 91
abstract: His many characters included Detective Mole, Sherlock Chick and Miss Mallard, a crime-solving duck who got her own television series.

name: Mark Peel
profession: Helped Forge a New Culinary Path
headline: Mark Peel, Who Helped Forge a New Culinary Path, Dies at 66
abstract: A pillar of California’s pioneering food scene, he worked at Spago and was a founder of the renowned Campanile and La Brea Bakery.

name: Consuewella Africa
profession: Lost Two Daughters in MOVE Siege
headline: Consuewella Africa, 67, Dies; Lost Two Daughters in MOVE Siege
abstract: One of the girls’ remains from a 1985 police attack are believed to have ended up in a cardboard box for use in a university forensics course, provoking outrage.

name: Sylvia Deutsch
profession: Force in New York City Land Use
headline: Sylvia Deutsch, a Force in New York City Land Use, Dies at 96
abstract: The only person to lead two city land-use agencies and the first woman to head each, she expanded housing opportunities and promoted a revitalized Times Square.

name: Ei-ichi Negishi
headline: Ei-ichi Negishi, Nobel Prize Winner in Chemistry, Dies at 85
abstract: His work in creating a method to build complex organic molecules applied to everything from pharmaceutical manufacturing to electronics.

name: Richard Stolley
headline: Richard Stolley, Founding Editor of People Magazine, Dies at 92
abstract: He also scored a major journalistic coup by securing the rights to the Zapruder film of John F. Kennedy’s assassination for Life magazine.

name: Milkha Singh
headline: Milkha Singh, Track Star of Post-Colonial India, Is Dead
abstract: Through the late 1950s and early ’60s, the man known as the Flying Sikh blazed through tracks in India and abroad, representing the hopes of a young nation.

name: Leonard Crow Dog
headline: Leonard Crow Dog, Spiritual Leader at Wounded Knee, Dies at 78
abstract: He served time in prison after the 1973 occupation on the Pine Ridge reservation and dedicated his life to preserving the traditions of the Sicangu Lakota.

name: Gianna Rolandi
profession: Spirited Soprano With a Radiant Voice
headline: Gianna Rolandi, Spirited Soprano With a Radiant Voice, Dies at 68
abstract: Ms. Rolandi, an acclaimed Vixen and Lucia, made her mark at the New York City Opera and the Lyric Opera of Chicago.

name: Benigno S. Aquino III
headline: Benigno S. Aquino III, 61, Former President of the Philippines, Dies
abstract: A scion of the country’s most prominent pro-democracy political family, he was celebrated early in his administration for stabilizing the country’s faltering economy.

name: Diego Cortez
profession: Scene Shaper in Art and Music
headline: Diego Cortez, a Scene Shaper in Art and Music, Dies at 74
abstract: In ’70s and ’80s New York, he elevated Jean-Michel Basquiat in a huge show he curated. He also helped found the Mudd Club and worked with Laurie Anderson and, later, Patti Smith.

name: Stephen Graubard
headline: Stephen Graubard, 96, Journal Editor and Provocative Historian, Dies
abstract: He edited the scholarly journal Daedalus for decades and wrote books on the presidency, sparing neither Kennedy nor Clinton nor the Bushes.

name: Stephen Dunn
headline: Stephen Dunn, Poet Who Celebrated the Ordinary, Dies at 82
abstract: His work, one reviewer said, “has an out-of-time quality, like a conversation with your smartest friend during a long-distance road trip.” In 2001 he won the Pulitzer Prize.

name: Richard J. Meislin
profession: Times Editor and Web Journalism Pioneer
headline: Richard J. Meislin, Times Editor and Web Journalism Pioneer, Dies at 68
abstract: He was both a computer whiz and an accomplished newsman when he began prodding colleagues and the newspaper itself to begin adapting to the online world.

name: John Sacret Young
headline: John Sacret Young, Creative Force Behind ‘China Beach,’ Dies at 75
abstract: The series, about a Vietnam War hospital, was just one vehicle for him in his writing career to explore war and its aftershocks.

name: Jacques Barzaghi
headline: Jacques Barzaghi, a Former Fixture Beside Jerry Brown, Dies at 82
abstract: Whether as policy adviser, interior decorator or barber, he was a Zen-like presence in that California politician’s orbit, and always dressed in black.

name: Romulo Yanes
profession: Photographs Captured the Beauty of Food
headline: Romulo Yanes, Whose Photographs Captured the Beauty of Food, Dies at 62
abstract: Best known for his long tenure at Gourmet magazine, he brought a sense of elegant realism to his job and let his delectable subjects take center stage.

name: Paulo Mendes da Rocha
headline: Paulo Mendes da Rocha, Architect of ‘Concrete Acrobatics,’ Dies at 92
abstract: A Pritzker Prize winner, he was known for a muscular style often called Brazilian Brutalism, but he had a lighter touch than that label implies.

name: Jeanne Lamon
headline: Jeanne Lamon, Who Led an Early-Music Ensemble, Dies at 71
abstract: A violinist, she directed Tafelmusik for 33 years, striving not only to present centuries-old music as it was originally heard but also to reach modern audiences.

name: Mike Gravel
headline: Mike Gravel, Unconventional Two-Term Alaska Senator, Dies at 91
abstract: He made headlines by fighting for an oil pipeline and reading the Pentagon Papers aloud. After 25 years of obscurity, he re-emerged with a quixotic presidential campaign.

name: Jon Hassell
headline: Jon Hassell, Trumpeter and ‘Fourth World’ Composer, Dies at 84
abstract: Blending modern technology with traditional instruments, Mr. Hassell created a genre he described as “coffee-colored classical music of the future.”

name: Frederic Rzewski
headline: Frederic Rzewski, Politically Committed Composer and Pianist, Dies at 83
abstract: Known for his anti-establishment views, Mr. Rzewski created works inspired by the Attica prison uprising and a Chilean protest song.

name: John Clem Clarke
headline: John Clem Clarke, a Pop Art Perennial in SoHo, Dies at 83
abstract: He bought a loft in that Manhattan neighborhood and helped form its art scene in the 1970s, then remained even as the area’s bohemian character vanished.

name: John Langley
profession: Creator of the TV Series Cops
headline: John Langley, a Creator of the TV Series ‘Cops,’ Dies at 78
abstract: “You can be entertained by it, you can be disgusted,” he said of the popular reality show that embedded film crews with police officers in the streets for 31 years.

name: Frieda Fritzshall
profession: Survived to Create a Holocaust Museum
headline: Frieda Fritzshall, 91, Dies; Survived to Create a Holocaust Museum
abstract: Sent to Auschwitz as a girl, she settled in Chicago after the war and vowed not to let the world forget the atrocities. The museum, in Skokie, Ill., bears witness.

name: Ellen McIlwaine
profession: Slide Guitarist With a Power Voice
headline: Ellen McIlwaine, Slide Guitarist With a Power Voice, Dies at 75
abstract: Early in her career she played with Jimi Hendrix. She went on to record several well-regarded albums. But she remained under the radar.

name: Elizabeth Martínez
headline: Elizabeth Martínez, Voice of the Chicana Movement, Dies at 95
abstract: Through her writings, she inspired, provoked, educated, strategized, organized and built cross-racial and cross-ethnic alliances, all in pursuit of social justice.

name: Jack Downing
profession: C.I.A. Chief in Cold War Capitals
headline: Jack Downing, C.I.A. Chief in Cold War Capitals, Dies at 80
abstract: He was the agency’s only official to have served as station head in both Moscow and Beijing. Then he was drawn out of retirement in 1997 to save its espionage operations.

name: Donald Rumsfeld
headline: Donald Rumsfeld, Defense Secretary Under 2 Presidents, Is Dead at 88
abstract: Mr. Rumsfeld, who served under Gerald Ford and George W. Bush, was in charge of the invasion of Iraq and later said that the removal of Saddam Hussein had “created a more stable and secure world.”

name: Greg Noll
headline: Greg Noll, Surfing Superstar Who Tackled the Big Waves, Dies at 84
abstract: Known as ‘Da Bull,’ he caught waves in Hawaii, California, Australia and Mexico. One expert said he “could be the Babe Ruth of surfing.”

name: Robert Sacchi
headline: Robert Sacchi, Who Played Bogart Again and Again, Dies at 89
abstract: He was a hard-working actor and not merely a doppelgänger. But his claim to fame on film, TV and the stage was that he looked like Bogie.

name: Boryana Straubel
headline: Boryana Straubel, 38, Dies; Founded a ‘Green’ Jewelry Company
abstract: A former Tesla executive, she ran a family foundation that focuses on environmental sustainability. Her jewelry company uses recycled metals.

name: Patricia Reilly Giff
headline: Patricia Reilly Giff, ‘Polk Street’ Children’s Book Writer, Dies at 86
abstract: Ms. Giff wrote more than 100 books, ranging from an exploration of the Irish potato famine to a humorous series about the antics of second graders.

name: Louis Andriessen
headline: Louis Andriessen, Lionized Composer With Radical Roots, Dies at 82
abstract: After challenging the Dutch musical establishment as a young man, he went on to write a series of large and loud symphonic works that grappled with big ideas.

name: Mimi Stern-Wolfe
headline: Mimi Stern-Wolfe, Presenter of Socially Conscious Concerts, Dies at 84
abstract: The range of programs she staged on the Lower East Side and in nearby neighborhoods included an annual concert devoted to composers lost to AIDS.

name: Tran Thien Khiem
profession: Power in South Vietnam Before Its Fall
headline: Tran Thien Khiem, 95, Dies; a Power in South Vietnam Before Its Fall
abstract: For six years he was the nation’s second in command, a master of political intrigue who had plotted and thwarted coups before fleeing the Communist victory in 1975.

name: Eve Adams
headline: Overlooked No More: Eve Adams, Writer Who Gave Lesbians a Voice
abstract: Her 1925 book, “Lesbian Love,” is one of the earliest examples of American lesbian literature. She also ran Eve’s Hangout, a literary haunt in Manhattan.

name: Hash Halper
headline: Hash Halper, Street Artist Who Adorned New York With Hearts, Dies at 41
abstract: He was something of a downtown folk hero, bringing positivity to a harsh city with his humble shards of chalk. But he harbored his own struggles.

name: June Finch
profession: Virtuoso Dance Teacher With a Humane Touch
headline: June Finch, Virtuoso Dance Teacher With a Humane Touch, Dies at 81
abstract: A premier teacher of Merce Cunningham’s technique, she gave equal attention to everyone in her class, not just those destined for stardom with his company.

name: Lauren Berlant
headline: Lauren Berlant, Critic of the American Dream, Is Dead at 63
abstract: Professor Berlant’s book “Cruel Optimism” provided a popular term to describe false hopes in an increasingly unequal nation.

name: William Fagaly
headline: William Fagaly, Curator Who Focused on African Art, Dies at 83
abstract: In his 50 years at the New Orleans Museum of Art, he also made substantial contributions in the areas of Southern outsider art and contemporary art.

name: Barbara Murphy
headline: Dr. Barbara Murphy, Kidney Transplant Expert, Dies at 56
abstract: Her focus was on immunology and how to predict and diagnose the outcomes of transplants. She was, a colleague said, “a great researcher and a great mentor to many people.”

name: Delia Fiallo
headline: Delia Fiallo, Master of the Telenovela, Is Dead at 96
abstract: She wrote more than 40 telenovelas, the American soap opera’s addictive cousin, and was one of the most celebrated names in Spanish-language television.

name: Peter Zinovieff
headline: Peter Zinovieff, Composer and Synthesizer Innovator, Dies at 88
abstract: His powerful, affordable instruments made memorable sounds for Pink Floyd, Kraftwerk, David Bowie, King Crimson and many others.

name: Tom Reich
profession: Negotiated Big Deals for Baseball Stars
headline: Tom Reich, Who Negotiated Big Deals for Baseball Stars, Dies at 82
abstract: In the early days of free agency, he won multimillion-dollar salaries for players. Among his clients were Sammy Sosa, Ken Griffey and Dock Ellis.

name: Terry Donahue
headline: Terry Donahue, Who Led U.C.L.A. to Bowl Victories, Dies at 77
abstract: Over 20 years, he had more wins than any football coach in the school’s history, including seven consecutive bowl championships.

name: Richard Donner
profession: Director of Superman and Lethal Weapon Films
headline: Richard Donner, Director of ‘Superman’ and ‘Lethal Weapon’ Films, Dies at 91
abstract: The Bronx-born Mr. Donner was in his late 40s when he made his first megahit, about the Man of Steel, but others soon followed, including “The Goonies” and “Scrooged.”

name: Dilip Kumar
headline: Dilip Kumar, Film Star Who Brought Realism to Bollywood, Dies at 98
abstract: One of India’s earliest Method actors, he was the last survivor of a triumvirate of actors who ruled Hindi cinema in the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Suzzanne Douglas
headline: Suzzanne Douglas, Star of ‘The Parent ’Hood,’ Dies at 64
abstract: Her four-decade acting career also included roles in the films “Tap” and “Inkwell,” as well as appearances on Broadway.

name: Robert Downey Sr.
headline: Robert Downey Sr., Filmmaker and Provocateur, Is Dead at 85
abstract: His movies, most notably “Putney Swope,” didn’t make a lot of money. But they attracted a lot of attention and influenced a lot of younger directors.

name: Richard C. Lewontin
profession: Eminent Geneticist With a Sharp Pen
headline: Richard C. Lewontin, Eminent Geneticist With a Sharp Pen, Dies at 92
abstract: He demonstrated that differences in DNA between groups of people were far smaller than originally believed. He was also a noted opponent of aspects of sociobiology.

name: Dicky Maegle
profession: Football Star Remembered for a Bizarre Tackle
headline: Dicky Maegle Dies at 86; Football Star Remembered for a Bizarre Tackle
abstract: He’s in the College Football Hall of Fame, but he’s probably best known for the Cotton Bowl game in which an opposing player left the bench to take him down.

name: Rachmawati Sukarnoputri
headline: Rachmawati Sukarnoputri, 70, Sibling Rival in Indonesia Politics, Dies
abstract: A daughter of the founding president, Sukarno, she feuded with her older sister over who would inherit his mantle, losing that fight. She died of Covid-19.

name: Clare Peploe
headline: Clare Peploe, Film Director Who Jumbled Genres, Dies at 79
abstract: She contributed to the movies of her husband, Bernardo Bertolucci, but also made her own, including “Triumph of Love.”

name: Danny Shanahan
headline: Danny Shanahan, Cartoonist With an Absurd Touch, Dies at 64
abstract: He drew about 1,000 cartoons for The New Yorker, populated by clowns, snowmen, cats, dogs, Elvis and more. But his career with the magazine ended under a cloud.

name: James Kallstrom
profession: Led F.B.I. Review of T.W.A. Crash
headline: James Kallstrom Dies at 78; Led F.B.I. Review of T.W.A. Crash
abstract: As the F.B.I. chief in New York, he spent 16 months investigating why Flight 800 crashed 12 minutes after takeoff, killing all 230 people on board.

name: Yury Dokhoian
headline: Yury Dokhoian, Chess Coach Who Guided Kasparov, Dies at 56
abstract: A Russian grandmaster, he spent a decade working with the longtime world champion, who said Mr. Dokhoian gave him “stability and confidence.” He died of the coronavirus.

name: Haunani-Kay Trask
profession: Champion of Native Rights in Hawaii
headline: Haunani-Kay Trask, Champion of Native Rights in Hawaii, Dies at 71
abstract: She helped found the field of Hawaiian studies and pressed for Indigenous sovereignty. “We will die as Hawaiians,” she said. “We will never be Americans.”

name: Jehan Sadat
profession: Widow of Egypts President and Womens Advocate
headline: Jehan Sadat, 87, Widow of Egypt’s President and Women’s Advocate, Dies
abstract: Until her husband was assassinated in 1981, she pushed him to enact measures aimed at improving women’s rights and education.

name: Thomas Cleary
headline: Thomas Cleary, Prolific Translator of Eastern Texts, Dies at 72
abstract: His renderings of classic works of Buddhism, Taoism and more brought them to a general Western readership.

name: Athan Theoharis
headline: Athan Theoharis, Chronicler of F.B.I. Abuses, Dies at 84
abstract: He found his way through the formerly unobtainable files of J. Edgar Hoover, whom he called “an insubordinate bureaucrat in charge of a lawless organization.”

name: Henry Parham
profession: Fought in a Black Unit on D-Day
headline: Henry Parham, Who Fought in a Black Unit on D-Day, Dies at 99
abstract: He helped tell the story of the 320th Battalion, gaining recognition only late in his life. “I did what I was supposed to do as an American,” he said.

name: Byron Berline
headline: Byron Berline, Master of the Bluegrass Fiddle, Dies at 77
abstract: His updated version of an old-timey approach enhanced recordings by everyone from Bill Monroe to the Rolling Stones.

name: Jane Kaufman
headline: Jane Kaufman, Artist Who Celebrated Women’s Work, Dies at 83
abstract: A leader of what became known as the Pattern and Decoration movement, she made screens, wall hangings and quilts — a radical act in an age of minimalism.

name: Paul Orndorff
headline: Paul Orndorff, Wrestler Known as Mr. Wonderful, Dies at 71
abstract: The wrestler competed in the first WrestleMania, held in 1985 at Madison Square Garden.

name: Allan Reiver
profession: Built a Little Urban Oasis in New York
headline: Allan Reiver, Who Built a Little Urban Oasis in New York, Dies at 78
abstract: When he saw a vacant lot three decades ago, he said, “I thought I could make something beautiful out of it.” The result was the Elizabeth Street Garden.

name: Paul Huntley
profession: Hair Master of Broadway and Hollywood
headline: Paul Huntley, Hair Master of Broadway and Hollywood, Is Dead at 88
abstract: The many famous heads he worked on included those of Elizabeth Taylor and Carol Channing. Some actors requested him in their contracts.

name: Priscilla McMillan
headline: Priscilla McMillan, Who Knew Both Kennedy and Oswald, Dies at 92
abstract: A Cold War scholar, she met Lee Harvey Oswald four years before  President John F. Kennedy’s assassination and later wrote “Marina and Lee,” a book about him and his Russian wife.

name: Ahmed Jibril
headline: Ahmed Jibril, Militant Palestinian Leader Behind Attacks, Dies at 84
abstract: He was considered a top security threat to Israel in the 1970s and ’80s, and his hijackings, kidnappings and attacks had enduring political effects.

name: Charlie Robinson
profession: Actor Best Known for Night Court
headline: Charlie Robinson, Actor Best Known for ‘Night Court,’ Dies at 75
abstract: Mr. Robinson became a fan favorite as Mac, a levelheaded clerk surrounded by oddballs, on the long-running NBC courtroom comedy.

name: Bernette Ford
headline: Bernette Ford, Who Made Children’s Books More Diverse, Dies at 70
abstract: As a publishing executive and as an author, she sought to make sure that all children saw themselves in what they read.

name: Kristen Richards
headline: Kristen Richards, 69, Dies; Reshaped Architecture Journalism Online
abstract: Her ArchNewsNow website connected architects, designers and journalists with its curated list of must-read articles from around the world.

name: Esther Bejarano
profession: Auschwitz Survivor Fought Hate With Hip-Hop
headline: Esther Bejarano, 96, Dies; Auschwitz Survivor Fought Hate With Hip-Hop
abstract: She played the accordion in the camp’s orchestra. Decades later, she spoke out against fascism and racism, using music as well as words.

name: Oleg Briansky
headline: Oleg Briansky, Star Dancer Turned Star Teacher, Is Dead at 91
abstract: When his career was ended by a bad knee, he and his wife and fellow dancer opened what became one of the most prestigious ballet academies in America.

name: Raffaella Carrà
headline: Raffaella Carrà, Saucy Superstar of Italian TV, Dies at 78
abstract: Known for her energetic dancing and singing as well as for conducting serious interviews, she was beloved by Italians of all generations.

name: Christian Boltanski
headline: Christian Boltanski, Whose Art Installations Dazzled, Dies at 76
abstract: In often sprawling works that used old photos, discarded clothes and other found objects, he pondered loss, chance and memory.

name: Dennis Murphy
headline: Dennis Murphy, Impresario of Alternative Leagues, Dies at 94
abstract: He founded the American Basketball Association, which revolutionized the game, and participated in other imaginative, sometimes zany sports ventures.

name: Rebecca Lee Crumpler
headline: Overlooked No More: Rebecca Lee Crumpler, Who Battled Prejudice in Medicine
abstract: As the first Black woman to earn a medical degree in the United States, she persevered to make care accessible to women and Black communities, regardless of their ability to pay.

name: Frank Askin
headline: Frank Askin, Fierce Defender of Civil Liberties, Dies at 89
abstract: A late bloomer in law school, he founded a constitutional rights clinic to guard against government overreach and was a longtime general counsel at the A.C.L.U.

name: William H. Regnery II
profession: Bankrolled the Rise of the Alt-Right
headline: William H. Regnery II, 80, Dies; Bankrolled the Rise of the Alt-Right
abstract: The reclusive heir to a Midwestern textile fortune, he sought, through funding and organizing, to upgrade and update white supremacy.

name: William H. Pauley III
profession: Judge in Trump Hush Money Case
headline: William H. Pauley III, Judge in Trump Hush Money Case, Dies at 68
abstract: He sentenced Michael D. Cohen to three years in prison for breaking campaign finance laws by helping to buy the silence of two women who said they had affairs with Donald J. Trump.

name: Biz Markie
profession: Hip-Hops Just a Friend Clown Prince
headline: Biz Markie, Hip-Hop’s ‘Just a Friend’ Clown Prince, Dies at 57
abstract: An innovative yet proudly goofy rapper, he had an unlikely crossover hit with a tune that led one critic to call him (favorably) “the father of modern bad singing.”

name: Barbara J. Litrell
headline: Barbara J. Litrell, 77, Dies; Publisher of Magazines for Women Who Work
abstract: As publisher, Ms. Litrell focused not on telling woman what to wear or how to cook, but on how to integrate into the work force.

name: Erin Gilmer
headline: Erin Gilmer, Disability Rights Activist, Dies at 38
abstract: She fought for a more compassionate health care system, bringing an extensive knowledge of policy and even more extensive firsthand experience as a patient.

name: John Veronis
headline: John Veronis, Who Helped Start Psychology Today, Dies at 93
abstract: After working as a magazine executive, he helped broker major media transactions, including Rupert Murdoch’s $3 billion purchase of the company that owned TV Guide.

name: Shirley Fry Irvin
headline: Shirley Fry Irvin, Tennis Star of the ’40s and ’50s, Is Dead at 94
abstract: The fastest player of her day, she played down her own ability but admitted, “Billie Jean King said I was her idol.”

name: Gloria Richardson
headline: Gloria Richardson, Uncompromising Civil Rights Advocate, Dies at 99
abstract: Her efforts to refocus the movement on economic justice made her a bridge between more moderate leaders and Black Power activism.

name: John P. McMeel
headline: John P. McMeel, Newspaper Syndicator With a Difference, Dies at 85
abstract: He and his business partner started in a basement, recruited a Yale student cartoonist named Garry Trudeau, and built the largest company of its kind.

name: Paul Auerbach
headline: Dr. Paul Auerbach, Father of Wilderness Medicine, Dies at 70
abstract: He pioneered a new branch of emergency medicine — when emergency rooms are nowhere to be found — and helped compile the definitive textbook on health care in the wild.

name: Kurt Westergaard
headline: Kurt Westergaard, 86, Dies; His Muhammad Cartoon Sparked Outrage
abstract: A caricature that many Muslims considered blasphemous prompted a debate over free speech and a massacre at the offices of a Paris magazine.

name: Graham Vick
headline: Graham Vick, Director Who Opened Opera’s Doors, Dies at 67
abstract: The British director was no stranger to the prestige houses, but his calls to make opera more inclusive and available to everyone eventually found their moment.

name: Rick Laird
profession: Bassist at the Forefront of Fusion
headline: Rick Laird, Bassist at the Forefront of Fusion, Dies at 80
abstract: He played with jazz greats and helped make music history with the Mahavishnu Orchestra. But he gave it up in his 40s to become a photographer.

name: Gil Wechsler
profession: Illuminating Fixture at the Met Opera
headline: Gil Wechsler, an Illuminating Fixture at the Met Opera, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Wechsler, the first resident lighting designer at the Met, created lighting designs that helped bring numerous operas to life.

name: Marjorie Adams
profession: Went to Bat for a Baseball Pioneer
headline: Marjorie Adams, Who Went to Bat for a Baseball Pioneer, Dies at 72
abstract: Her great-grandfather is considered a founding father of the game, but his contributions were not well known. She campaigned to earn him a place in the Hall of Fame.

name: Josef Silverstein
headline: Josef Silverstein, Scholar and Critic of Myanmar, Dies at 99
abstract: He focused on democracy and human rights in a strife-torn country both as an academic and as an on-the-ground adviser to rebel groups.

name: Carol Easton
headline: Carol Easton, Biographer of Arts Figures, Dies at 87
abstract: Curious about creativity, she chronicled the lives of Agnes de Mille, Jacqueline du Pré, Samuel Goldwyn and Stan Kenton.

name: Kathy Andrade
headline: Kathy Andrade, Unionist Who Fought for Immigrant Workers, Dies at 88
abstract: Her work on behalf of garment workers helped prod organized labor to rethink its approach to an increasingly immigrant-based work force.

name: Harry deLeyer
profession: He Saved a Horse and Made Him a Legend
headline: Harry deLeyer, 93, Dies; He Saved a Horse and Made Him a Legend
abstract: A Dutch immigrant, he bought a plow horse for $80 in 1956 and named him Snowman. Two years later the pair won the show-jumping triple crown.

name: Harry Rosenfeld
profession: Saw News in a Third-Rate Burglary
headline: Harry Rosenfeld, Who Saw News in a ‘Third-Rate Burglary,’ Dies at 91
abstract: He assigned Woodward and Bernstein to follow the Watergate break-in for The Washington Post and fended off efforts to supplant them.

name: Vladimir Menshov
headline: Vladimir Menshov, Surprise Russian Oscar Winner, Dies at 81
abstract: His “Moscow Does Not Believe in Tears” was named best foreign-language film in 1980, beating Truffaut and Kurosawa. U.S. critics demurred.

name: Arturo Schwarz
headline: Arturo Schwarz, Refugee Who Became a Surrealism Tycoon, Dies at 97
abstract: After expulsion from Egypt left him penniless, he befriended André Breton and Marcel Duchamp and amassed an enormous collection of priceless art.

name: Bruce Kirby
headline: Bruce Kirby, Who Transformed Sailing With a ‘Doodle,’ Dies at 92
abstract: On yellow legal paper, Mr. Kirby, a self-taught designer and Olympic sailor, came up with an impromptu design for a lightweight craft that changed the face of sailing.

name: Alice Clark Brown
profession: Black Star in a White Circus
headline: Alice Clark Brown, Black Star in a White Circus, Dies at 68
abstract: At a time when Ringling Brothers had few Black performers, she dazzled with aerial ballet and balanced on galloping elephants.

name: Purnell Choppin
profession: Researcher Laid Groundwork for Pandemic Fight
headline: Purnell Choppin, 91, Dies; Researcher Laid Groundwork for Pandemic Fight
abstract: He explored how viruses multiply. An accomplished administrator, he also turned the Howard Hughes Medical Institute into a global biomedical powerhouse.

name: Jackie Mason
headline: Jackie Mason, 93, Dies; Turned Kvetching Into Comedy Gold
abstract: He kept the borscht belt style of comedy alive long after the Catskills resorts had closed and eventually brought it, triumphantly, to Broadway.

name: Bob Moses
profession: Crusader for Civil Rights and Math Education
headline: Bob Moses, Crusader for Civil Rights and Math Education, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Moses developed a reputation for extraordinary calm in the face of violence as he helped to register thousands of voters and trained a generation of activists in Mississippi in the early 1960s.

name: Steven Weinberg
headline: Steven Weinberg, Groundbreaking Nobelist in Physics, Dies at 88
abstract: His discoveries deepened understanding of the basic forces at play in the universe, and he took general readers back to its dawn in his book “The First Three Minutes.”

name: Yoel Kahn
profession: Oral Scribe for the Grand Rabbi
headline: Rabbi Yoel Kahn, Oral Scribe for the Grand Rabbi, Dies at 91
abstract: For decades he memorized virtually verbatim the speeches and discourses of Rabbi Menachem Schneerson and meticulously compiled them into about 150 volumes.

name: Elliot Lawrence
headline: Elliot Lawrence, Award-Winning Conductor, Dies at 96
abstract: He led a big band, conducted on Broadway, collected Emmys and for nearly 50 years led the orchestra on the annual Tony Awards broadcast.

name: Sally Miller Gearhart
headline: Sally Miller Gearhart, Lesbian Separatist and Activist, Dies at 90
abstract: She fought anti-gay policies alongside Harvey Milk, wrote influential books, including science fiction, and founded a women-only refuge in the woods.

name: Michael Enzi
headline: Michael Enzi, Long-Serving U.S. Senator From Wyoming, Dies at 77
abstract: A four-term senator, Mr. Enzi was a consistent conservative with a consensus-seeking style. He died after a bicycle accident in Gillette, Wyo., the city where he began his political career.

name: Jimmy Elidrissi
headline: Jimmy Elidrissi, Waldorf Bellhop for Five Decades, Dies at 74
abstract: A Moroccan immigrant’s goal was to make guests, including nine U.S. presidents, feel right at home amid the grandeur of a landmark Manhattan hotel.

name: J. Allan Hobson
headline: Dr. J. Allan Hobson, Who Studied the Dreaming Brain, Dies at 88
abstract: He disputed the Freudian view that dreams held encrypted codes of meaning, believing instead that they resulted from random firings of neurons in the brain.

name: Joey Jordison
headline: Joey Jordison, Slipknot Drummer, Dies at 46
abstract: Mr. Jordison’s explosive, virtuosic playing and elaborate solos, sometimes performed atop a hydraulic riser, made him a fan favorite.

name: Robert Ellison
profession: Ceramics Collector With a Giving Streak
headline: Robert Ellison, Ceramics Collector With a Giving Streak, Dies at 89
abstract: The more than 600 works he gave to the Met enriched the museum’s collection enormously.

name: George Rhoads
headline: George Rhoads, Designer of Fantastical ‘Ball Machines,’ Dies at 95
abstract: In his ingeniously conceived sculptures, balls seem to travel randomly and trigger various sounds. “Each pathway that the ball takes,” he said, “is a different drama.”

name: Dusty Hill
headline: Dusty Hill, Long-Bearded Bassist for ZZ Top, Dies at 72
abstract: The band, known for its hard-charging, blues-inflected rock, was one of the biggest acts of the 1980s, selling more than 50 million albums.

name: Ron Popeil
headline: Ron Popeil, Inventor and Ubiquitous Infomercial Pitchman, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Popeil became a well-known presence on TV, hawking products that people didn’t know they needed, including the Veg-O-Matic and the Inside-the-Shell Egg Scrambler.

name: Albert Bandura
headline: Albert Bandura, Leading Psychologist of Aggression, Dies at 95
abstract: He was most known for his Bobo doll experiment, in which children mimicked adults in attacking an inflatable doll. The work challenged basic tenets of psychology.

name: Floyd Cooper
profession: Illustrator of Black Life for Children
headline: Floyd Cooper, Illustrator of Black Life for Children, Dies at 65
abstract: He sought to revive and recount chapters of African American history that he felt weren’t taught enough in classrooms.

name: Johnny Ventura
profession: Created the Sound of Modern Merengue
headline: Johnny Ventura, Who Created the Sound of Modern Merengue, Dies at 81
abstract: The “Elvis of Merengue” released more than 100 albums and won six Latin Grammys. For a time, he was mayor of the capital of the Dominican Republic.

name: Carl Levin
headline: Carl Levin, the Senate Scourge of Corporate America, Dies at 87
abstract: The longest-serving U.S. senator in Michigan history, Mr. Levin was regarded by colleagues and Washington observers as a paragon of probity.

name: Ruth Pearl
profession: Mother of Murdered Reporter Daniel Pearl
headline: Ruth Pearl, Mother of Murdered Reporter Daniel Pearl, Dies at 85
abstract: A reluctant celebrity, she was thrust into the spotlight after his brutal death, and created a foundation in his memory to promote cultural understanding.

name: Janet Sobel
headline: Overlooked No More: Janet Sobel, Whose Art Influenced Jackson Pollock
abstract: With no formal art training, working in her Brooklyn apartment, she took up the drip style of painting that Pollock later made famous.

name: Chuck E. Weiss
headline: Chuck E. Weiss, Musician Who, in Love, Inspired a Hit Song, Dies at 76
abstract: He and Tom Waits and Rickie Lee Jones were inseparable in the late ’70s, and when Mr. Weiss’s romantic life took a turn, Ms. Jones memorialized it in “Chuck E.’s in Love.”

name: Roberto Calasso
headline: Roberto Calasso, Renaissance Man of Letters, Dies at 80
abstract: A Florentine by birth, he was a polymath as an author and publisher (Kafka, Vedic philosophy, Greek mythology) who reached a wide international readership.

name: Richard Lamm
profession: Governor and Early Abortion Rights Supporter
headline: Richard Lamm, Governor and Early Abortion Rights Supporter, Dies at 85
abstract: He spearheaded the passage of a liberal abortion law in Colorado before Roe v. Wade, and he helped stop the 1976 Winter Olympics from being held in the state.

name: Frenchy Cannoli
headline: Frenchy Cannoli, Ardent Evangelist for Hashish, Dies at 64
abstract: He left France at 18 for a nearly two-decade sojourn to India, Nepal, Mexico and Morocco to learn the secrets of making hash and became an authority.

name: Reynold Ruffins
headline: Reynold Ruffins, Push Pin Studios Graphic Artist, Dies at 90
abstract: With Milton Glaser, Ed Sorel and Seymour Chwast, he was part of a movement that upended the ’50s era advertising style with witty, faux-nostalgic imagery.

name: Jay Pickett
headline: Jay Pickett, Veteran Soap Opera Actor, Dies at 60
abstract: His credits included “General Hospital,” “Days of Our Lives” and “Port Charles.” He died while filming a western in Idaho, where he was raised.

name: George Forss
profession: Photographer Discovered on the Streets of N.Y
headline: George Forss, 80, Photographer Discovered on the Streets of N.Y., Dies
abstract: He was peddling his black-and-white photos of New York City’s majesty for $5 each in the 1980s — until a famous photographer came upon them in “astonishment.”

name: Paula Caplan
profession: Feminist Psychologist Took On Her Profession
headline: Paula Caplan, 74, Dies; Feminist Psychologist Took On Her Profession
abstract: She argued that categorizing premenstrual syndrome or feelings of guilt as disorders resulted from sexism in a field dominated by men.

name: Lynn C. Franklin
profession: Literary Agent and Memoirist on Adoption
headline: Lynn C. Franklin, Literary Agent and Memoirist on Adoption, Dies at 74
abstract: She represented Desmond Tutu and Deepak Chopra, but the book closest to her was the one she wrote about giving up her baby and then reuniting with him.

name: Willie Winfield
headline: Willie Winfield, Angelic-Voiced Doo-Wop Singer, Is Dead at 91
abstract: For more than 60 years, he sang with various incarnations of the Harptones. “His voice was unique,” one concert producer said, “and it lasted his whole life.”

name: Robert Dennison
profession: Parole Board Chief Turned Inmate Advocate
headline: Robert Dennison, Parole Board Chief Turned Inmate Advocate, Dies at 75
abstract: After growing disillusioned with the board he had run, he became, a colleague said, “a vocal critic of the arbitrary and arcane parole system.”

name: Joan Ullyot
headline: Joan Ullyot, Debunker of Limits on Women Who Run, Dies at 80
abstract: Dr. Ullyot argued in her research, and showed over miles and miles in competition herself, that, yes, women are built to run marathons. Olympic officials finally agreed.

name: Louise Fishman
profession: Gave Abstract Expressionism a New Tone
headline: Louise Fishman, Who Gave Abstract Expressionism a New Tone, Dies at 82
abstract: Her paintings infused a once-male-dominated genre with a feminist, lesbian sensibility.

name: Gilbert V. Levin
profession: Said He Found Signs of Life on Mars
headline: Gilbert V. Levin, Who Said He Found Signs of Life on Mars, Dies at 97
abstract: Most planetary scientists dismissed his conclusions, but he remained steadfast that the experiment he conducted in the mid-1970s had been a success.

name: Abebech Gobena
headline: Abebech Gobena, the ‘Mother Teresa’ of Africa, Dies at 85
abstract: She created one of Ethiopia’s largest orphanages and through it saved thousands from starvation and disease. She died of complications of Covid-19.

name: Patricia Kennealy-Morrison
headline: Patricia Kennealy-Morrison, Rock Journalist, Dies at 75
abstract: She took the music seriously at a time when not many writers did. Among her books was a memoir of her life with one of its biggest stars, Jim Morrison.

name: Dave Severance
headline: Col. Dave Severance, Commander at Iwo Jima, Dies at 102
abstract: He sent Marines to the top of Mount Suribachi to plant the flag. Captured in a photograph, the scene remains an enduring image of American men at war.

name: Richard Trumka
headline: Richard Trumka, A.F.L.-C.I.O. Chief, Dies at 72
abstract: A third-generation coal miner from Pennsylvania, he had led the labor federation since 2009, forging influential ties with leading Democrats.

name: Arthur French
headline: Arthur French, Negro Ensemble Company Pioneer, Dies at 89
abstract: He more or less stumbled into a career as an actor, but it proved to be a long and prolific one, on film, on television and especially on the stage.

name: Otelo Saraiva de Carvalho
headline: Otelo Saraiva de Carvalho, 84, Dies; Key Figure in Portugal Revolt
abstract: He became a national hero in the 1974 “Carnation Revolution,” which ousted a dictatorship. But he later landed in prison for links to a terrorist group.

name: Herbert Schlosser
headline: Herbert Schlosser, a Force Behind ‘S.N.L.’ and ‘Laugh-In,’ Dies at 95
abstract: As a top NBC executive, he wrote a memo envisioning the show that became “Saturday Night Live.” He also helped recruit Johnny Carson and oversaw a raft of hit shows.

name: Patricia Wilde
headline: Patricia Wilde, Ballerina Showcased by Balanchine, Dies at 93
abstract: Quick and daring with New York City Ballet, she was a favorite of its leader, who would throw her into a role with barely a rehearsal.

name: Ilona Royce Smithkin
profession: Improbable Muse in Fashion and Art
headline: Ilona Royce Smithkin, Improbable Muse in Fashion and Art, Dies at 101
abstract: After a troubling youth and a career teaching art, she sashayed into the roles of movie actress, cabaret singer, fashion model and artists’ mentor.

name: Paul Cotton
profession: Mainstay of the Country-Rock Band Poco
headline: Paul Cotton, Mainstay of the Country-Rock Band Poco, Dies at 78
abstract: He joined the band for its third album and expanded its emotional and stylistic palette with his sinewy, blues-inflected guitar work and brooding baritone vocals.

name: Jon Lindbergh
headline: Jon Lindbergh, Aviator’s Son Who Took to the Sea, Dies at 88
abstract: Family triumph (Charles Lindbergh’s trans-Atlantic flight) and tragedy (the kidnapping “crime of the century”) shaped his early life, but he made his mark in the depths.

name: Nach Waxman
profession: Founder of a Bookstore Where Foodies Flock
headline: Nach Waxman, Founder of a Bookstore Where Foodies Flock, Dies at 84
abstract: A “kitchen anthropologist,” he created a mecca in Manhattan for chefs, writers, scholars, everyday cooks and anyone else who is, well, hungry for culinary knowledge.

name: Gareth Hughes
profession: Sports Producer With a Human Touch
headline: Gareth Hughes, Sports Producer With a Human Touch, Dies at 41
abstract: A multiple Emmy winner, he created a specialty in crafting “teases,” short videos that precede major events like the Masters and N.F.L. playoff games.

name: Bobby Bowden
headline: Bobby Bowden, Coach Who Led Florida State to Greatness, Dies at 91
abstract: He transformed the Seminoles into a national powerhouse, and ended his career second only to Joe Paterno in major college football victories.

name: Karen Hastie Williams
headline: Karen Hastie Williams, Barrier-Breaking Lawyer, Dies at 76
abstract: She was the first Black woman to serve as a Supreme Court clerk and went on to break countless other glass ceilings, while helping others do the same.

name: Marc Lieberman
headline: Marc Lieberman, Who Brought Jews and Buddhists Together, Dies at 72
abstract: He called himself “a healthy mosaic” of the two faiths. An ophthalmologist, he also ran a clinic that brought sight back to Tibetans with cataracts.

name: Dennis ‘Dee Tee’ Thomas
headline: Dennis ‘Dee Tee’ Thomas, Saxophonist for Kool & the Gang, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Thomas was a co-founder of the band, which was known for its hits such as “Celebration,” “Get Down on It” and “Jungle Boogie.”

name: Markie Post
headline: Markie Post, ‘Night Court’ Actress, Dies at 70
abstract: Ms. Post played a bail bondswoman on the show “The Fall Guy” in the 1980s and starred opposite John Ritter in the sitcom “Hearts Afire” in the 1990s.

name: Jacob Desvarieux
headline: Jacob Desvarieux, Guitarist Who Forged Zouk Style, Dies at 65
abstract: His band, Kassav’, found millions of listeners as it held on to Caribbean roots while reaching out to the world. He died of Covid-19.

name: Jane Withers
headline: Jane Withers, Child Star Who Later Won Fame in Commercials, Dies at 95
abstract: As a girl, she landed leading roles that were the antidote to Shirley Temple’s. As an adult, she was known as Josephine the Plumber in ads for Comet cleanser.

name: Sergei Kovalev
headline: Sergei Kovalev, Longtime Kremlin Adversary, Dies at 91
abstract: He campaigned for human rights during the Soviet era and continued his activism in the post-Communist years under Boris A. Yeltsin and Vladimir V. Putin.

name: Trevor Moore
profession: Founder of The Whitest Kids U Know
headline: Trevor Moore, a Founder of ‘The Whitest Kids U’ Know,’ Dies at 41
abstract: In addition to the popular sketch show, his work included a solo comedy album, “Drunk Texts to Myself,” and the films “Miss March” and “The Civil War on Drugs.”

name: Kelli Hand
profession: Detroit D.J. and Music Industry Trailblazer
headline: Kelli Hand, Detroit D.J. and Music Industry Trailblazer, Dies at 56
abstract: In 2017, the Detroit City Council honored Ms. Hand as the “first lady of Detroit” for her contributions, which included breaking into a male-dominated techno music scene.

name: Walter Yetnikoff
headline: Walter Yetnikoff, Powerful but Abrasive Record Executive, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Yetnikoff led CBS Records during the boom years that included Michael Jackson’s “Thriller” album. Then he fell from grace.

name: Ying-shih Yu
headline: Ying-shih Yu, Renowned Scholar of Chinese Thought, Dies at 91
abstract: He believed that Chinese tradition was more varied and tolerant than critics thought it to be, and that it could be a vessel for enlightened values and democratic progress.

name: Brian Mulheren
profession: New York Polices Go-to Man in Emergencies
headline: Brian Mulheren, New York Police’s Go-to Man in Emergencies, Dies at 73
abstract: In the 1970s and ’80s, he was the police commissioner’s liaison with City Hall and became known as “Mr. Disaster.”

name: Toshihide Maskawa
profession: Nobelist Helped Unlock a Cosmic Mystery
headline: Toshihide Maskawa, 81, Dies; Nobelist Helped Unlock a Cosmic Mystery
abstract: Why did the universe not destroy itself in the Big Bang, in a collision of matter and antimatter? A eureka moment in the bathtub led to an answer.

name: Tony Esposito
profession: Nimble Hall of Fame Goalie Known as Tony O
headline: Tony Esposito, Nimble Hall of Fame Goalie Known as Tony O, Dies at 78
abstract: Esposito guarded the Chicago Blackhawks’ net for 15 seasons and was an early pioneer of the butterfly style of goaltending.

name: Elka Schumann
profession: Matriarch of the Bread and Puppet Theater
headline: Elka Schumann, Matriarch of the Bread and Puppet Theater, Dies at 85
abstract: She and her husband ran a Vermont-based troupe that has taken on social and political issues in productions featuring enormous puppets.

name: Neal Conan
profession: Talked (and Listened) to the Nation on NPR
headline: Neal Conan, Who Talked (and Listened) to the Nation on NPR, Dies at 71
abstract: In a broadcasting career that began when he was 17, he was a producer, editor and news director — and a voice listeners trusted.

name: Marcia Nasatir
profession: Broke a Glass Ceiling in Hollywood
headline: Marcia Nasatir, Who Broke a Glass Ceiling in Hollywood, Dies at 95
abstract: A former book editor and agent, she got her first movie studio job, at United Artists, when she was 48. She insisted on being hired as a vice president.

name: John Rizzo
headline: John Rizzo, C.I.A. Lawyer Who Sanctioned Waterboarding, Dies at 73
abstract: He defended the agency’s treatment of suspected terrorists, but he was later more reflective about it than most of his colleagues.

name: Leon Litwack
profession: Changed How Scholars Portray Black History
headline: Leon Litwack, 91, Dies; Changed How Scholars Portray Black History
abstract: One of Berkeley’s most popular professors, he brought passion and nuance — and a love for blues music — to his award-winning study of the marginalized and the oppressed.

name: Frank Torres
headline: Frank Torres, Judge Who Sought More Latinos on the Bench, Dies at 93
abstract: The son of one judge and the father of another, Justice Torres pressed for greater Hispanic representation in the legal profession and the New York courts.

name: Una Stubbs
headline: Una Stubbs, Veteran Actress Known for ‘Sherlock,’ Dies at 84
abstract: A fixture on British television for more than half a century, she was best known to American audiences as Sherlock Holmes’s cheerful landlady.

name: Hettie Anderson
headline: Overlooked No More: Hettie Anderson, Sculptors’ Model Who Evaded Fame
abstract: Her image has been rendered on gold coins and monuments around the United States. But little is known about this Gilded Age model.

name: Janice Mirikitani
profession: Poet and Crusader for People in Need
headline: Janice Mirikitani, Poet and Crusader for People in Need, Dies at 80
abstract: Interned with her family during World War II, she became San Francisco’s poet laureate and an activist on behalf of the city’s marginalized people.

name: Nanci Griffith
headline: Nanci Griffith, Singer Who Blended Folk and Country, Dies at 68
abstract: Her best-loved songs were closely observed tales of small-town life, sometimes with painful details in the lyrics, but typically sung with a deceptive prettiness.

name: Donald Kagan
headline: Donald Kagan, Leading Historian of Ancient Greece, Dies at 89
abstract: His studies of the Peloponnesian War and his impassioned teaching style inspired generations of scholars, as well as Washington strategists.

name: James Hormel
headline: James Hormel, America’s First Openly Gay Ambassador, Dies at 88
abstract: An outspoken advocate of L.G.B.T.Q. rights, he was nominated by President Bill Clinton and appointed despite fierce opposition from the right.

name: Pat Hitchcock O’Connell
headline: Pat Hitchcock O’Connell, Director’s Daughter and Cast Member, Dies at 93
abstract: She acted in three films directed by her father, Alfred Hitchcock,  including “Psycho.” She later wrote a book about her mother’s role as his cinematic partner.

name: Michael Thomas
profession: Writer and Bête Noire of the Moneyed Class
headline: Michael Thomas, Writer and Bête Noire of the Moneyed Class, Dies at 85
abstract: His early careers as an art historian and Wall Street financier informed his financial thrillers, which often savaged the rich and powerful.

name: Joe Walton
headline: Joe Walton, Giants Star Who Found Futility as Jets Coach, Dies at 85
abstract: He took them to the playoffs several times in the 1980s but was dismissed after a 53-57 record. He went on to achieve success as a college coach.

name: Maki Kaji
headline: Maki Kaji, the ‘Godfather of Sudoku,’ Is Dead at 69
abstract: Mr. Kaji, a university dropout, turned a numbers game into one of the world’s most popular logic puzzles.

name: Ellen Havre Weis
headline: Ellen Havre Weis, Whose Museum Put Pop Into Mythology, Dies at 64
abstract: The Museum of Modern Mythology, in San Francisco, which she helped found, posited that advertising figures have emerged as the pre-eminent mythical figures of our time.

name: Chucky Thompson
headline: Chucky Thompson, Hitmaking Producer, Is Dead at 53
abstract: He brought a range of musical influences to bear on the tracks he helped create for Mary J. Blige, the Notorious B.I.G. and many others.

name: Hiro
headline: Hiro, Fashion Photographer Who Captured the Surreal, Dies at 90
abstract: He juxtaposed the mundane and the exotic, transforming ordinary objects into the desirable — an approach he took in his still-life images as well as in fashion.

name: Glen Ford
headline: Glen Ford, Black Journalist Who Lashed the Mainstream, Dies at 71
abstract: Fiercely progressive and independent, he was a persistent critic of the liberal establishment, especially Black leaders like Barack Obama.

name: Peter Rehberg
headline: Peter Rehberg, a Force in Underground Music, Dies at 53
abstract: He released his own experiments with sound under the name Pita, and also ran the influential label Editions Mego.

name: Chuck Close
headline: Chuck Close, Artist of Outsized Reality, Dies at 81
abstract: He found success with his large-scale Photorealist portraits, becoming one of the leading artists of his generation. Late in life he faced allegations of sexual harassment.

name: Joe Galloway
headline: Joe Galloway, Decorated Vietnam War Correspondent, Dies at 79
abstract: He chronicled the first major battle of the war in “We Were Soldiers Once … and Young” and raised questions about the invasion of Iraq.

name: Sonny Chiba
profession: Japanese Star With a Kill Bill Connection
headline: Sonny Chiba, Japanese Star With a ‘Kill Bill’ Connection, Dies at 82
abstract: His martial arts movies appalled some with their extreme violence, but the director Quentin Tarantino was a fan and gave him a late-career boost.

name: Gustave M. Hauser
headline: Gustave M. Hauser, an Early Force in Cable TV, Dies at 91
abstract: The bold experiment Mr. Hauser undertook in Columbus, Ohio, in 1977 helped usher in the modern era of multichannel digital cable television.

name: Kaari Upson
profession: California Artist of Desire and Disturbance
headline: Kaari Upson, California Artist of Desire and Disturbance, Dies at 51
abstract: Known for her resin sculptures and her disquieting videos, she was one of the most significant artists to emerge from the vibrant 21st-century Los Angeles art scene.

name: Gino Strada
profession: Brought Health Care to the Desperate
headline: Dr. Gino Strada, Who Brought Health Care to the Desperate, Dies at 73
abstract: He was a force behind Emergency, which operates clinics, hospitals, trauma centers and other institutions throughout the world.

name: Evgeny Sveshnikov
headline: Evgeny Sveshnikov, Grandmaster and Theorist of Chess, Dies at 71
abstract: He made significant contributions to the theory of the game, particularly the openings, one of which is named for him.

name: James W. Loewen
headline: James W. Loewen, Who Challenged How History Is Taught, Dies at 79
abstract: In a dozen books, most famously “Lies My Teacher Told Me,” he attacked historical misconceptions, particularly concerning the Black struggle in the South.

name: Eloise Greenfield
headline: Eloise Greenfield, Who Wrote to Enlighten Black Children, Dies at 92
abstract: In nearly 50 books, written in poetry and prose, she described the lives of ordinary people and heroes like Rosa Parks and Paul Robeson.

name: Tom T. Hall
headline: Tom T. Hall, Country Music’s ‘Storyteller,’ Is Dead at 85
abstract: Mr. Hall, who wrote hits like “Harper Valley P.T.A.,” helped to imbue country lyrics with newfound depth and insight in the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Gerd Müller
profession: Soccer Star Known for His Scoring Prowess
headline: Gerd Müller, Soccer Star Known for His Scoring Prowess, Dies at 75
abstract: He scored 566 goals for Bayern Munich, helping the club to four German titles, four German Cup wins and three European Cup victories in 15 years.

name: Barbara Kannapell
headline: Barbara Kannapell, Activist Who Empowered Deaf People, Dies at 83
abstract: She gave them a sense of identity and culture and helped legitimize American Sign Language, which she considered her native language.

name: Stanley Aronowitz
headline: Stanley Aronowitz, Labor Scholar and Activist, Dies at 88
abstract: As a self-described “working-class intellectual,” he declared that direct action was more potent than collective bargaining or conventional politics.

name: Gary B. Nash
profession: Drew Ire for Trying to Update History Education
headline: Gary B. Nash, 88, Dies; Drew Ire for Trying to Update History Education
abstract: A respected scholar of early America, he became a central figure in the culture wars that enveloped the country in the 1990s.

name: Bill Freehan
headline: Bill Freehan, Champion Tigers’ Durable Centerpiece, Dies at 79
abstract: An 11-time All-Star catcher, he played a key role in Detroit’s 1968 World Series victory over the St. Louis Cardinals.

name: Don Everly
profession: Older Brother in Groundbreaking Rock Duo
headline: Don Everly, Older Brother in Groundbreaking Rock Duo, Dies at 84
abstract: The Everly Brothers, Don and Phil, were the most successful rock act to emerge from Nashville in the 1950s, rivaling Elvis Presley for radio airplay.

name: Lucille Times
headline: Lucille Times, Who Inspired the Montgomery Bus Boycott, Dies at 100
abstract: Six months before Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat, Mrs. Times had an altercation with a bus driver and stopped riding the city’s segregated buses.

name: Hung Liu
headline: Hung Liu, Artist Who Blended East and West, Is Dead at 73
abstract: An immigrant from China, she once said her goal was “to invent a way of allowing myself to practice as a Chinese artist outside of a Chinese culture.”

name: Rod Gilbert
profession: Hockey Hall of Famer Known as Mr. Ranger
headline: Rod Gilbert, Hockey Hall of Famer Known as Mr. Ranger, Dies at 80
abstract: Gilbert played his entire N.H.L. career with New York and is the franchise’s only player to score more than 400 goals.

name: Alan Heller
headline: Alan Heller, Who Made Plastic Housewares Beautiful, Dies at 81
abstract: For designers like Mario Bellini and Massimo and Lella Vignelli, Mr. Heller produced domestic objects that became models of modern design.

name: Anthony M. Scotto
profession: Former Union Power on the Docks
headline: Anthony M. Scotto, Former Union Power on the Docks, Dies at 87
abstract: He rose to leadership in the longshoremen’s union as a polished reformer, but the U.S. called him a Mafia boss, and he served prison time in a racketeering case.

name: R. Murray Schafer
headline: R. Murray Schafer, Composer Who Heard Nature’s Music, Dies at 88
abstract: He delved into the relationship between sound and the environment. Many of his compositions incorporated the music of the natural world.

name: Hissène Habré
profession: Ex-President of Chad Jailed for War Crimes
headline: Hissène Habré, Ex-President of Chad Jailed for War Crimes, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Habré, who received a life sentence for crimes against humanity including torture and sex offenses, was said to be out of prison for medical treatment at his death.

name: Buckie Leach
profession: Coach of U.S. Gold Medal Fencer in Tokyo
headline: Buckie Leach, Coach of U.S. Gold Medal Fencer in Tokyo, Dies at 62
abstract: Under his tutelage, Lee Kiefer became a first for the United States. Leach led the women’s national foil team in five Summer Olympics. He died in a motorcycle accident.

name: Charlie Watts
profession: Bedrock Drummer for the Rolling Stones
headline: Charlie Watts, Bedrock Drummer for the Rolling Stones, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Watts, who had no taste for the life of a pop idol, was an unflashy but essential presence with the band and brought to it a swinging style.

name: Rand V. Araskog
headline: Rand V. Araskog, Former Chief of ITT Corp., Dies at 89
abstract: Over two decades, during a tumultuous time for American business, he winnowed an unwieldy corporation and fended off corporate raids.

name: Jean Breeze
headline: Jean Breeze, First Woman of Dub Poetry, Dies at 65
abstract: She was known for the passion of her performances, the raw honesty of her stories and her use of Jamaica’s lyrical vernacular.

name: Micki Grant
headline: Micki Grant, Groundbreaking Broadway Composer, Dies at 92
abstract: With “Don’t Bother Me, I Can’t Cope,” she became the first woman to write the book, music and lyrics of a Broadway musical.

name: David Roberts
headline: David Roberts, Who Turned Adventure Writing Into Art, Dies at 78
abstract: He was an accomplished mountain climber with a literary gift to match, and the author of dozens of books.

name: Larry Harlow
headline: Larry Harlow, Influential Figure in Salsa, Dies at 82
abstract: He was born into a family of Jewish musicians, but he made his mark in Latin music, as a pianist, bandleader and producer.

name: Inge Ginsberg
profession: Holocaust Survivor With a Heavy Metal Coda
headline: Inge Ginsberg, Holocaust Survivor With a Heavy Metal Coda, Dies at 99
abstract: Her rich life, spanning three continents and 11 decades, entailed wartime espionage, volumes of poetry, songwriting and a late-career turn as a rock band’s frontwoman.

name: Michael Morgan
headline: Michael Morgan, Adventurous Oakland Maestro, Dies at 63
abstract: As music director of the Oakland Symphony, he sought diversity in his audiences as well as in his programming.

name: William G. Clotworthy
headline: William G. Clotworthy, ‘Saturday Night Live’ Censor, Dies at 95
abstract: A self-described “professional square,” he fell in love with the show, and worked with its writers to tweak questionable material. Cast members called him “Dr. No.”

name: Lila Gleitman
headline: Lila Gleitman, Who Showed How Children Learn Language, Dies at 91
abstract: Building on the work of Noam Chomsky, she designed elegant experiments to show that syntax is hard-wired into the human brain.

name: Donald Newlove
profession: Novelist Explored the Depths of Drink
headline: Donald Newlove, 93, Dies; Novelist Explored the Depths of Drink
abstract: His acclaimed fiction and a memoir had a common theme: alcoholism. After becoming sober, he called his former besotted muse “Drunkspeare.”

name: Lloyd Dobyns
profession: Co-Anchor of an Innovative TV Newscast
headline: Lloyd Dobyns, Co-Anchor of an Innovative TV Newscast, Dies at 85
abstract: He teamed with Linda Ellerbee on “NBC News Overnight” in 1982 to set an unusual tone for network news in an equally unusual time slot.

name: Jeanne Robertson
profession: Down-Home Humorist With a Pageant Past
headline: Jeanne Robertson, 77, Down-Home Humorist With a Pageant Past, Dies
abstract: She told family-friendly stories from everyday life, about things like family squabbles and sending a man to the grocery store. Her YouTube fans were legion.

name: Jerry Harkness
profession: Star of a Historic Integrated Basketball Team
headline: Jerry Harkness, 81, Dies; Star of a Historic Integrated Basketball Team
abstract: He was an All-American forward for Loyola University Chicago, which started four Black players against an all-white Mississippi State team in the 1963 N.C.A.A. tournament.

name: Randy Snow
headline: Overlooked No More: Randy Snow, Paralympic Champion of Wheelchair Tennis
abstract: He won gold medals in singles and doubles at the 1992 Games in Barcelona and was the first Paralympic athlete to be inducted into the Olympic Hall of Fame.

name: Stephen B. Oates
headline: Stephen B. Oates, Civil War Historian, Dies at 85
abstract: In a quartet of biographies, he explored how slavery and racial oppression could exist in a land based on the ideals of the Declaration of Independence.

name: Bob Diamond
headline: Bob Diamond, the ‘Tunnel King’ of Brooklyn, Dies at 61
abstract: First he discovered a long-forgotten rail tunnel. Then he spent decades trying — in vain — to revive Brooklyn’s trolley system.

name: Rebecca Wasserman-Hone
profession: Put Burgundy on the U.S. Map
headline: Rebecca Wasserman-Hone, Who Put Burgundy on the U.S. Map, Dies at 84
abstract: American born, she fell into the wine business and became a champion of the small vignerons of the Burgundy region and their ancient family farms.

name: Don Poynter
profession: Made Toilets Talk and Golf Balls Walk
headline: Don Poynter, Who Made Toilets Talk and Golf Balls Walk, Dies at 96
abstract: His line of novelty items was wide-ranging. Jayne Mansfield posed for him so that he could make a shapely, sexy hot-water bottle.

name: Ed Asner
profession: Emmy-Winning Star of Lou Grant and Up
headline: Ed Asner, Emmy-Winning Star of ‘Lou Grant’ and ‘Up,’ Dies at 91
abstract: Best known as the gruff newsman he first played on “The Mary Tyler Moore Show,” he was also a busy character actor and a political activist.

name: Kenny Malone
profession: Premier Drummer for Top Nashville Names
headline: Kenny Malone, Premier Drummer for Top Nashville Names, Dies at 83
abstract: He propelled hits by stars in country, folk and pop, including Dolly Parton, Crystal Gayle, Ray Charles, Waylon Jennings, Kenny Rogers and Bela Fleck.

name: Jacques Rogge
headline: Jacques Rogge, Who Led Olympic Committee, Dies at 79
abstract: Taking over in the wake of an ethics scandal, Dr. Rogge was credited with restoring stability and taking a hard line against doping.

name: Lee Perry
profession: Bob Marley Mentor and Reggae Innovator
headline: Lee (Scratch) Perry, Bob Marley Mentor and Reggae Innovator, Dies at 85
abstract: With a four-track tape recorder in his Jamaican home studio, he opened surreal sonic vistas and cultivated the image of a mad genius.

name: Gail Omvedt
profession: India Became Her Home, the Caste System Her Cause
headline: Gail Omvedt, 80, Dies; India Became Her Home, the Caste System Her Cause
abstract: An American-born sociologist, she moved to India in the 1970s, helped pioneer the study of castes and drew attention to the lives of the country’s most oppressed.

name: Robert Middlekauff
profession: Historian of Washington and His War
headline: Robert Middlekauff, Historian of Washington and His War, Dies at 91
abstract: He wrote what many believe to be the best single-volume history of the Revolutionary War and another work seeing the war through the eyes of George Washington.

name: Carolyn Shoemaker
headline: Carolyn Shoemaker, Hunter of Comets and Asteroids, Dies at 92
abstract: After her children left for college, she unexpectedly became astronomy’s record-setting spotter of unidentified objects hurtling through the cosmos.

name: Mikis Theodorakis
headline: Mikis Theodorakis, ‘Zorba’ Composer and Marxist Rebel, Dies at 96
abstract: Known for his film music, he also waged a war of words and music against a military junta that banned his work and imprisoned him during its rule of Greece.

name: Syed Ali Geelani
headline: Syed Ali Geelani, Separatist Leader in Kashmir, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Geelani was an uncompromising opponent of the Indian government’s control of the Kashmir valley and favored Pakistani sovereignty over the mostly Muslim region.

name: Mal Z. Lawrence
headline: Mal Z. Lawrence, Noted Catskill Quipster, Dies at 88
abstract: A popular comic in the Catskills’ heyday as a resort area, he brought borscht belt humor to audiences all over the country, including on Broadway.

name: Edmond H. Fischer
headline: Edmond H. Fischer, 101, Who Helped Discover How Cells Talk, Dies
abstract: He and a colleague identified a mechanism by which cells communicate, a Nobel-winning breakthrough that paved the way for disease-fighting drugs.

name: Edward J. Greenfield
headline: Edward J. Greenfield, Judge With a Writerly Touch, Dies at 98
abstract: He often luxuriated in the richness of the English language, going off on whimsical digressions and enlivening the law with colorful asides.

name: Ernst van de Wetering
headline: Ernst van de Wetering, Authority and Arbiter on Rembrandt, Dies at 83
abstract: His decisions on whether a painting was authentic, a copy or an outright fake could jolt the art market. “No one else alive knows as much as he did about Rembrandt.”

name: Robert L. James
headline: Robert L. James, Globally Minded Ad Man, Dies at 84
abstract: He took over a storied but struggling agency, McCann Erickson, in the early ’80s and pushed it to become the biggest in the world, with a foot in 99 countries.

name: Stephen Vizinczey
profession: In Praise of Older Women Author
headline: Stephen Vizinczey, ‘In Praise of Older Women’ Author, Dies at 88
abstract: His best-known work, somewhat scandalous for the mid-1960s, treated sex frankly and sold millions of copies.

name: Delores Custer
profession: Gave Star Turns to Cornflakes and Noodles
headline: Delores Custer, 79, Dies; Gave Star Turns to Cornflakes and Noodles
abstract: A longtime food stylist for big-name companies, she was a master of the craft and taught students all over the world how to sweat a glass or perfect the pizza cheese pull.

name: Patricia Maginnis
headline: Patricia Maginnis, Pioneering Abortion-Rights Activist, Dies at 93
abstract: In the years before Roe v. Wade, she helped shift the debate away from the rules governing abortion providers to women’s right to control their bodies.

name: Keith McCants
profession: Football Star Laid Low by Drugs
headline: Keith McCants, Football Star Laid Low by Drugs, Dies at 53
abstract: At one time the N.F.L.’s highest-paid defensive player, he left the league after six seasons and fell into a spiral of addiction, homelessness and desolation.

name: Jean-Paul Belmondo
profession: Magnetic Star of the French New Wave
headline: Jean-Paul Belmondo, Magnetic Star of the French New Wave, Dies at 88
abstract: He was compared to Marlon Brando and James Dean for his acclaimed portrayals of tough, alienated characters, most memorably in Godard’s “Breathless.”

name: Igor Oistrakh
profession: Soviet-Era Violinist (and a Son of One)
headline: Igor Oistrakh, Soviet-Era Violinist (and a Son of One), Dies at 90
abstract: His father, David, was one of the 20th century’s finest violinists, but Igor more than held his own as a musician and interpreter performing throughout the West.

name: Adlai E. Stevenson III
profession: Ex-Senator and Scion of Political Family
headline: Adlai E. Stevenson III, Ex-Senator and Scion of Political Family, Dies at 90
abstract: The Illinois Democrat served a decade in the United States Senate: “It was ordained at birth that I would go into a life of public service.”

name: Phil Schaap
headline: Phil Schaap, Grammy-Winning Jazz D.J. and Historian, Dies at 70
abstract: His radio programs, most notably on Columbia University’s WKCR, were full of minutiae he had accumulated during a lifetime immersed in the genre.

name: Joseph I. Kramer
headline: Joseph I. Kramer, the ‘Country Doctor’ of Avenue D, Dies at 96
abstract: Shunning the New Jersey suburbs in 1969, he set up a pay-what-you-can practice on the blighted Lower East Side and for three decades was a hero to the poor.

name: Alberto Vilar
headline: Alberto Vilar, Arts Patron Convicted of Fraud, Dies at 80
abstract: An opera fan, he used the riches from his investment business to fuel a spending spree at opera companies and other cultural organizations. But many of his pledges went unfulfilled.

name: Michael Constantine
profession: Father in My Big Fat Greek Wedding
headline: Michael Constantine, Father in ‘My Big Fat Greek Wedding,’ Dies at 94
abstract: He won an Emmy for his role on the TV series “Room 222” and played many other characters over the years before becoming known as the hit film’s patriarch.

name: Terry Brennan
headline: Terry Brennan, a Notre Dame Football Coach at 25, Dies at 93
