abstract: One of Frank Leahy’s Lads as a player on national championship teams, he succeeded his mentor but was fired at 30.

name: Sinn Sisamouth
headline: Overlooked No More: Sinn Sisamouth, ‘King’ of Cambodian Pop Music
abstract: He and his singing partner, Ros Serey Sothea, drew from a wide range of Western and local influences. They disappeared after the Khmer Rouge seized power in 1975.

name: Sunil Perera
profession: Outspoken Star of Sri Lankan Baila Music
headline: Sunil Perera, Outspoken Star of Sri Lankan Baila Music, Is Dead at 68
abstract: The frontman of his family’s popular band combined the country’s unique, Latin-influenced sound with politically biting lyrics.

name: Sam Cunningham
profession: Fostered Integration on the Football Field
headline: Sam Cunningham Dies at 71; Fostered Integration on the Football Field
abstract: As one of three Black players in the U.S.C. backfield, he led the team to a stunning win in 1970 over Coach Bear Bryant’s all-white Alabama. He would go on to star for the New England Patriots.

name: Elizabeth I. McCann
headline: Elizabeth I. McCann, Tony-Winning Broadway Producer, Is Dead at 90
abstract: In a career that began in 1976, she brought more than 60 productions to the New York stage, including “Equus,” “Amadeus” and the work of Edward Albee.

name: Michel Laclotte
headline: Michel Laclotte, Who ‘Created the Modern Louvre,’ Dies at 91
abstract: He championed two of the most debated architectural projects in recent Paris history: the Musée D’Orsay (in a former train station) and the Louvre pyramid.

name: Carl Bean
headline: Carl Bean, Gay Singer Who Turned to Preaching, Dies at 77
abstract: After recording “I Was Born This Way,” a club favorite, he entered the ministry and founded a church for the L.G.B.T.Q. community.

name: Nickolas Davatzes
profession: Force Behind A&E and the History Channel
headline: Nickolas Davatzes, Force Behind A&E and the History Channel, Dies at 79
abstract: He led the cable giant, whose eclectic mix of shows would include collaborations with the BBC and documentary-style series like “Hoarders.”

name: Abimael Guzmán
headline: Abimael Guzmán, Leader of Guerrilla Group That Terrorized Peru, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Guzmán’s Maoist movement, Shining Path, killed tens of thousands in the 1980s and ’90s. He sought to bring the world to a “higher stage of Marxism.”

name: Teresa Zylis-Gara
headline: Teresa Zylis-Gara, Plush-Voiced Polish Soprano, Is Dead at 91
abstract: She took on a wide range of roles in her long international career, which included a stretch as a stalwart of the Metropolitan Opera in the 1970s.

name: Gilbert Seltzer
profession: Soldier in the World War II Ghost Army
headline: Gilbert Seltzer, Soldier in the World War II ‘Ghost Army,’ Dies at 106
abstract: He was one of the last survivors of a band of Army con artists who duped German forces with their arsenal of fakery, including inflatable tanks and scripted radio transmissions.

name: Nino Castelnuovo
headline: Nino Castelnuovo, ‘The Umbrellas of Cherbourg’ Star, Dies at 84
abstract: Mr. Castelnuovo, who brought an incandescent charm to the screen, became famous during a golden age of Italian cinema. But his breakthrough role was in a French film.

name: Mick Tingelhoff
headline: Mick Tingelhoff, Vikings Hall of Fame Center, Dies at 81
abstract: He started in 240 consecutive games and played in four Super Bowls, providing pass protection for quarterback Fran Tarkenton.

name: George Wein
headline: George Wein, Newport Jazz Festival Trailblazer, Is Dead at 95
abstract: He brought jazz (and later folk music) to Rhode Island, and made festivals as important as nightclubs and concert halls on jazz musicians’ itineraries.

name: Kaycee Moore
profession: Actress in Black Directors Seminal Films
headline: Kaycee Moore, Actress in Black Directors’ Seminal Films, Dies at 77
abstract: She explored her characters’ inner lives in movies like “Killer of Sheep” and “Bless Their Little Hearts,” independent works that grew out of the L.A. Rebellion movement.

name: Art Metrano
profession: Actor and Comic Once Felled by an Accident
headline: Art Metrano, Actor and Comic Once Felled by an Accident, Dies at 84
abstract: He had built a career in stand-up comedy and in film and TV, but a fall from a ladder left him with a personal struggle.

name: Norm Macdonald
headline: Norm Macdonald, ‘Saturday Night Live’ Comedian, Dies at 61
abstract: Acerbic and sometimes controversial, he became familiar to millions as the show’s “Weekend Update” anchor from 1994 to 1998.

name: Cho Yong-gi
headline: Cho Yong-gi, Who Spread Christianity in South Korea, Dies at 85
abstract: His mammoth Yoido Full Gospel Church in Seoul symbolized the explosive growth of the religion in the once war-torn country.

name: Jean-Claude van Itallie
headline: Jean-Claude van Itallie, ‘America Hurrah’ Playwright, Dies at 85
abstract: He was a central figure in the experimental theater movement for decades. His best-known work, a trilogy of one-acts, opened in 1966 and ran for more than 630 performances.

name: Ruly Carpenter
profession: Owned the Phillies First Championship Team
headline: Ruly Carpenter, 81, Dies; Owned the Phillies’ First Championship Team
abstract: Distressed by soaring salaries, he sold the team a year after they beat Kansas City in the 1980 World Series. “We hoped common sense would prevail,’’ he said. “But it didn’t.”

name: Ida Nudel
profession: Angel to Soviet Jews Seeking to Flee
headline: Ida Nudel, ‘Angel’ to Soviet Jews Seeking to Flee, Dies at 90
abstract: During the Cold War, she fought for the rights of others and waged a 16-year fight of her own for an exit visa to Israel. She finally won in 1987.

name: Joan Washington
headline: Joan Washington, Dialect Coach to the Stars, Dies at 74
abstract: She taught Penélope Cruz, Jessica Chastain and countless other performers how to sound like someone else.

name: Jane Powell
headline: Jane Powell, Hollywood’s Girl Next Door, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Typecast from the outset, she was a star of movie musicals before she was out of her teens. But her big-screen career peaked when she was in her 20s.

name: Antony Hewish
profession: Astronomer Honored for the Discovery of Pulsars
headline: Antony Hewish, Astronomer Honored for the Discovery of Pulsars, Dies at 97
abstract: He received a Nobel Prize for his finding. Some criticized the prize because it was a graduate student in his lab who had first detected the signals.

name: Ralph Irizarry
headline: Ralph Irizarry, Innovative Latin Percussionist, Dies at 67
abstract: A colleague said Mr. Irizarry, who played timbales with Ray Barretto and Rubén Blades and led his own bands, expanded the instrument’s possibilities “to the nth degree.”

name: Abdelaziz Bouteflika
headline: Abdelaziz Bouteflika, Algeria’s Longest-Serving President, Dies at 84
abstract: He joined the country’s fight for independence in the 1950s and helped lead it out of a brutal civil war in the 1990s. He was ousted in 2019 after 20 years in office,

name: Bennie Pete
headline: Bennie Pete, Bandleader Who Kept the Beat After Katrina, Dies at 45
abstract: A tuba player and the leader of the Hot 8, one of New Orleans’s high-profile brass bands, he brought music to his fellow citizens in the difficult days after the storm.

name: Adalberto Álvarez
headline: Adalberto Álvarez, Latin Dance Music Maestro, Is Dead at 72
abstract: He was known as the “Gentleman of Son” because of his infectious enthusiasm for repopularizing the genre considered the bedrock of the Cuban sound.

name: Yolanda López
headline: Yolanda López, Artist Who Celebrated Working-Class Women, Dies at 78
abstract: She was celebrated for recasting the Virgin of Guadalupe in her own image as a feminist superhero — a young, strong, brown woman in running shoes.

name: Peter Williams
profession: His Art Evoked Black Lives, Including His
headline: Peter Williams, 69, Dies; His Art Evoked Black Lives, Including His
abstract: His colorful works could be quite personal, or they could be blunt responses to police brutality or other news of the day.

name: John Shelby Spong
profession: Sought to Open Up the Episcopal Church
headline: John Shelby Spong, 90, Dies; Sought to Open Up the Episcopal Church
abstract: Bishop Spong pushed for women in the clergy and same-sex marriage, and he called on his followers to reject “supernatural” aspects of Christianity.

name: Kenneth Schoen
headline: Kenneth Schoen, ‘Linchpin’ in Criminal Justice Reform, Dies at 89
abstract: In Minnesota, New York and nationally, he pushed for better conditions for prison inmates and more options for “community-based corrections.”

name: Anthony Johnson
headline: Anthony Johnson, Actor Known for ‘Friday,’ Dies at 55
abstract: Mr. Johnson, whose other film credits include “House Party” and “Menace II Society,” died on Sept. 6, his agent said.

name: Irma Kalish
headline: Irma Kalish, TV Writer Who Tackled Social Issues, Dies at 96
abstract: A female trailblazer in the TV industry, she and her husband took on topics like rape and abortion in writing for sitcoms like “All in the Family” and “Maude.”

name: Reuben Klamer
profession: Creator of the Game of Life
headline: Reuben Klamer, Creator of the Game of Life, Dies at 99
abstract: He developed an estimated 200 toys and other items, including a phaser rifle for “Star Trek.” But his best-known product was a game for “literally everyone on earth.”

name: Saadi Yacef
profession: Battle of Algiers Catalyst and Actor
headline: Saadi Yacef, ‘Battle of Algiers’ Catalyst and Actor, Dies at 93
abstract: At the center of the Algerian effort to throw off French rule, he re-created that role in Gillo Pontecorvo’s searing 1966 movie, based on a book by Mr. Yacef.

name: Sarah Dash
profession: Glue of the Vocal Trio Labelle
headline: Sarah Dash, the ‘Glue’ of the Vocal Trio Labelle, Is Dead at 76
abstract: She brought her church-rooted soprano and high harmonies to the rock and funk powerhouse best known for the No. 1 hit “Lady Marmalade.”

name: Willie Garson
headline: Willie Garson, ‘Sex and the City’ Actor, Dies at 57
abstract: Best known for his role as Carrie Bradshaw’s closest male friend, he was also the con man Mozzie on “White Collar” and appeared in more than 70 movies.

name: Barbara Campbell Cooke
profession: Widow of the Slain Sam Cooke
headline: Barbara Campbell Cooke, 85, Widow of the Slain Sam Cooke, Is Dead
abstract: They were teenage sweethearts, but their marriage turned tragic, and when she married the protégé singer Bobby Womack, the publicity was intense and the boos were loud.

name: George Holliday
profession: Taped Police Beating of Rodney King
headline: George Holliday, Who Taped Police Beating of Rodney King, Dies at 61
abstract: His shocking video, which played a key role in the prosecution of four officers, presaged the now-common use of cellphones to capture police abuse.

name: Carmen Balthrop
profession: Soprano Known for Joplin Opera Role
headline: Carmen Balthrop, Soprano Known for Joplin Opera Role, Dies at 73
abstract: After winning a vocal competition in 1975, she starred in “Treemonisha,” which ended up on Broadway. She also sang for a senator.

name: Melvin Van Peebles
headline: Melvin Van Peebles, Champion of New Black Cinema, Dies at 89
abstract: A fertile creative force, he wrote fiction and musicals but is best known for a breakthrough movie that heralded the genre known as blaxploitation.

name: Rudy Riska
headline: Rudy Riska, the Heisman Trophy’s Guiding Light, Dies at 85
abstract: For over 40 years he oversaw the awarding of the prestigious trophy to the nation’s top college football player and helped winners on their “magic carpet ride” in New York.

name: María Mendiola
profession: Half of a Chart-Topping Disco Duo
headline: María Mendiola, Half of a Chart-Topping Disco Duo, Dies at 69
abstract: “Yes Sir, I Can Boogie,” which she and a fellow ballet dancer recorded under the name Baccara, became one of the disco anthems of the 1970s.

name: Jimmy Greaves
headline: Jimmy Greaves, English Soccer Star, Is Dead at 81
abstract: He was the first player to lead scoring in England’s top league for three straight seasons, but he may be best known for one game he missed: the 1966 World Cup final.

name: Philip Caruso
headline: Philip Caruso, Former N.Y.P.D. Union President, Dies at 86
abstract: He took the reins of the P.B.A. in 1980, when morale was low after the city’s fiscal crisis. When he stepped down in ’95, the force was at peak strength.

name: Roger Michell
headline: Roger Michell, Director of ‘Notting Hill,’ Is Dead at 65
abstract: He was an accomplished theater director as well as a filmmaker. But he was best known for his blockbuster romantic comedy starring Julia Roberts and Hugh Grant.

name: Gira Sarabhai
headline: Gira Sarabhai, Designer Who Helped Shape Modern India, Dies at 97
abstract: The youngest daughter of an influential family of industrialists, she trained with Frank Lloyd Wright before returning to India and founding design institutions.

name: Sherwood Boehlert
headline: Sherwood Boehlert, a G.O.P Moderate in the House, Dies at 84
abstract: A champion of environmentalism who chided climate-change skeptics, he was among the last of the relatively progressive Rockefeller Republicans.

name: Remedios Varo
headline: Overlooked No More: Remedios Varo, Spanish Painter of Magic, Mysticism and Science
abstract: In the 1950s, and ’60s, she depicted women, artists and thinkers in intricate dreamlike canvases that now fetch high prices.

name: Doris Diether
headline: Doris Diether, Guardian of Greenwich Village, Dies at 92
abstract: She challenged Robert Moses to preserve Washington Square Park and helped save Shakespeare in the Park. In the process, she became a zoning expert.

name: Charles Sellers
headline: Charles Sellers, 98, Historian Who Upset the Postwar Consensus, Dies
abstract: A Southerner who became a radical at Berkeley, he argued that democracy developed in America as a response to the emergence of industrial capitalism.

name: Cliff Freeman
headline: Cliff Freeman, Adman Who Asked, ‘Where’s the Beef?,’ Dies at 80
abstract: His humorous touch was evident in commercials for Wendy’s, Little Caesars, Fox Sports and many other clients. “We have to win with wit,” he once said.

name: Penny Harrington
headline: Penny Harrington, Who Broke a Blue Ceiling, Dies at 79
abstract: Overcoming bias, she became the first woman to head a major city police department in the nation, in Portland, Ore. But a rocky tenure led her to resign 17 months later.

name: Cloyd Boyer
profession: Last of a Three-Brother Baseball Rarity
headline: Cloyd Boyer, Last of a Three-Brother Baseball Rarity, Dies at 94
abstract: His pitching career was cut short, but at one time he and his brothers Ken and Clete were all on the major league stage together. He ended up outliving them.

name: George Mraz
headline: George Mraz, Consummate Jazz Bassist, Dies at 77
abstract: For half a century, he was in constant demand, backing big names like Oscar Peterson as well as countless up-and-coming performers.

name: Bobby Zarem
headline: Bobby Zarem, ‘Superflack’ and Maker of Stars, Dies at 84
abstract: As a spirited impresario of public relations, he promoted entertainers, films and the “I Love New York” tourism campaign.

name: Théoneste Bagosora
headline: Théoneste Bagosora, a Mastermind of Rwanda Genocide, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Bagosora was convicted of genocide for ordering a massacre in the capital and the killing of top officials, including the prime minister.

name: Jonathan Mirsky
headline: Jonathan Mirsky, Journalist and Historian of China, Dies at 88
abstract: He brought a historian’s expertise to many decades of writing about China for The Observer of London, The New York Review of Books and other outlets.

name: Jay Sandrich
headline: Jay Sandrich, Emmy-Winning Sitcom Director, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Acclaimed for his work on “The Mary Tyler Moore Show” and “The Cosby Show,” he also made a crucial casting decision about “The Golden Girls.”

name: Mohamed Hussein Tantawi
headline: Mohamed Hussein Tantawi, 85, Dies; Led Egypt After Mubarak’s Fall
abstract: A general and defense minister, he took power after the Arab Spring uprising, overseeing a crackdown on pro-democracy protesters.

name: Frances T. Farenthold
profession: Liberal Force in Texas and Beyond
headline: Frances T. Farenthold, Liberal Force in Texas and Beyond, Dies at 94
abstract: Known as Sissy, she was an advocate for racial parity and women’s rights, and her name was placed in nomination for the vice presidency in 1972. Tragedy trailed her.

name: Pee Wee Ellis
headline: Pee Wee Ellis, James Brown’s Partner in Funk, Dies at 80
abstract: As musical director for the bands behind Mr. Brown and also Van Morrison, Mr. Ellis helped forge new hybrids, meshing pop, jazz, R&B and more.

name: Charles W. Mills
headline: Charles W. Mills, Philosopher of Race and Liberalism, Dies at 70
abstract: He argued that white supremacy was a feature of the Western political tradition, and that racism represented a political system as intentional as liberal democracy.

name: George Malkemus
headline: George Malkemus, Who Pushed Manolos to New Heights, Dies at 67
abstract: He successfully marketed Manolo Blahnik’s extravagantly heeled confections. Then a television character named Carrie Bradshaw brandished a pair in “Sex and the City.”

name: Alemayehu Eshete
profession: Singer Known as the Abyssinian Elvis
headline: Alemayehu Eshete, Singer Known as the ‘Abyssinian Elvis,’ Dies at 80
abstract: He became a swaggering star in the late 1960s, when Addis Ababa experienced a golden age of night life and music. Decades later, he was rediscovered.

name: Bob Moore
headline: Bob Moore, an Architect of the Nashville Sound, Dies at 88
abstract: He played bass on thousands of popular recordings, helping to create the uncluttered style that came to characterize the country music of the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Bob Moore
headline: Bob Moore, Who Founded Bob’s Red Mill, Is Dead at 94
abstract: A former gas station owner, he was learning to read the Bible in its original languages when he changed course and started what became an artisanal-grains powerhouse.

name: Marilyn Golden
headline: Marilyn Golden, Effective Voice for the Disabled, Dies at 67
abstract: “Radicalized” after an accident left her disabled, she became a “linchpin” in the fight for the Americans With Disabilities Act as a leading policy analyst.

name: Sue Thompson
profession: Sang of Norman and Sad Movies
headline: Sue Thompson, Who Sang of ‘Norman’ and Sad Movies, Dies at 96
abstract: She started out a country singer, but she found fame and pop-chart success in the early 1960s with catchy novelty songs, as well as the occasional ballad.

name: Clive Sinclair
headline: Clive Sinclair, Inventive Computer Pioneer, Dies at 81
abstract: His inexpensive Sinclair personal computer, one of many inventions, was an introduction to computing for young people in Britain and beyond.

name: Lonnie Smith
headline: Lonnie Smith, Soulful Jazz Organist, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Adept at blending the sophistication of jazz with the earthy appeal of rhythm and blues, he was later widely sampled by hip-hop artists.

name: Ruth Sullivan
headline: Ruth Sullivan, Advocate for People With Autism, Dies at 97
abstract: After her son was found to be autistic, she started organizations to help children and adults. She also consulted on the making of the movie “Rain Man.”

name: R. Allen Gardner
profession: Taught Sign Language to a Chimp Named Washoe
headline: R. Allen Gardner, 91, Dies; Taught Sign Language to a Chimp Named Washoe
abstract: He and his wife and collaborator made headlines with their finding that they could communicate with a young ape using the language of the deaf.

name: Teresa Miller
headline: Teresa Miller, Law Professor and Prison Reformer, Is Dead at 59
abstract: Her work on prisoner’s rights at Attica aimed to convey the humanity of incarcerated people. She later worked on diversity efforts for SUNY.

name: Takao Saito
profession: Created a Japanese Comic Book Superstar
headline: Takao Saito, 84, Dies; Created a Japanese Comic Book Superstar
abstract: Over a half-century and in more than 200 collected volumes, his manga tales of Golgo 13, a globe-trotting assassin, steered Japanese comics toward adults.

name: George Ferencz
headline: George Ferencz, Innovative Theater Director, Dies at 74
abstract: He directed works by Sam Shepard, Amiri Baraka and others at La MaMa and similar theaters known for experimentation.

name: Tommy Kirk
headline: Tommy Kirk, Young Star of ‘Old Yeller,’ Is Dead at 79
abstract: For a time, he was a Disney regular, seen in movies like “Swiss Family Robinson” and “The Shaggy Dog.” But his career derailed.

name: Pearl Tytell
headline: Pearl Tytell, Examiner of Dubious Documents, Dies at 104
abstract: For a half-century, she used her knowledge of handwriting, typewriters, paper and ink to investigate the veracity of checks, letters, contracts and other paperwork.

name: Richard H. Kirk
headline: Richard H. Kirk, Post-Punk Pioneer of Industrial Music, Dies at 65
abstract: Cabaret Voltaire, of which he was a founder, began as a band of experimental provocateurs and later moved to the dance floor.

name: Marcia Freedman
headline: Marcia Freedman, First American Woman in Knesset, Dies at 83
abstract: As a radical gay feminist in historically patriarchal Israel, Ms. Freedman was under constant criticism and was often dismissed by her colleagues.

name: Mohib Ullah
headline: Mohib Ullah, 46, Dies; Documented Ethnic Cleansing of Rohingya
abstract: Shot dead by gunmen, he had compiled a list of those who perished in the hope that the data could be used as evidence in international courts.

name: Angelo Codevilla
headline: Angelo Codevilla, Whose Writings Anticipated Trumpism, Dies at 78
abstract: A hawkish conservative, he believed that America was hamstrung at home and abroad by a progressive ruling class.

name: Todd Akin
profession: Senate Bid Collapsed After a Rape Remark
headline: Todd Akin, Whose Senate Bid Collapsed After a Rape Remark, Dies at 74
abstract: The former Republican representative from Missouri was widely criticized after saying in 2012 that women’s bodies could reject pregnancies that were the result of a sexual assault.

name: Kamla Bhasin
headline: Kamla Bhasin, a First-Wave South Asian Feminist, Dies at 75
abstract: An activist, poet and author, she spent most of her adult life fighting injustice and patriarchy and building bonds of solidarity with women across borders.

name: Debby King
profession: Backstage Aide Known as Soul of Carnegie Hall
headline: Debby King, 71, Backstage Aide Known as ‘Soul of Carnegie Hall,’ Dies
abstract: From Sinatra to Isaac Stern to Sting, she attended to the needs of the star performers in the Maestro Suite and helped calm their nerves.

name: David H. Komansky
headline: David H. Komansky, Global-Minded Chief of Merrill Lynch, Dies at 82
abstract: A postal worker’s son, he rose from financial adviser trainee to chairman of one of the world’s most powerful financial institutions, expanding it overseas.

name: Roberto Roena
headline: Roberto Roena, Salsa Percussionist and Bandleader, Dies at 81
abstract: His albums and performances with Apollo Sound brought new complexity to the genre in the 1970s. His group was still getting the crowds dancing decades later.

name: Alan Kalter
profession: Longtime Voice of Lettermans Late Show
headline: Alan Kalter, Longtime Voice of Letterman’s ‘Late Show,’ Dies at 78
abstract: Far more than just an announcer, he contributed all sorts of outlandish, incongruous comic bits to “Late Show With David Letterman.”

name: Msgr. John Powis
headline: Msgr. John Powis, Champion of Brooklyn’s Downtrodden, Dies at 87
abstract: His aggressive agenda as a pastor and civic leader in Brownsville and Bushwick laid the groundwork for a remarkable recovery.

name: Robert Schiffmann
headline: Robert Schiffmann, Inventive Guru of the Microwave, Dies at 86
abstract: As a scientist he saw the potential of microwave ovens when he observed one heating up a sandwich in the 1960s. Microwaveable oatmeal, among other advances, was in his future.

name: Marie Wilcox
profession: Saved Her Native Language From Extinction
headline: Marie Wilcox, Who Saved Her Native Language From Extinction, Dies at 87
abstract: The subject of a Times Op-Doc, she was, for a time, the last fluent speaker of Wukchumni and spent 20 years producing the first complete dictionary of its vocabulary.

name: Neal Sher
headline: Neal Sher, U.S. Government’s Leading Nazi Hunter, Dies at 74
abstract: He pursued former Nazis who had gotten into the United States illegally and become citizens. One target was John Demjanjuk, accused of being “Ivan the Terrible.”

name: Billy Apple
headline: Billy Apple, Artist Who Was His Own Life’s Work, Dies at 85
abstract: Born Barrie Bates in New Zealand, he became Billy Apple in London, embarking on a long career that marched through art explorations, from Pop to conceptual to self-branding.

name: Paula J. Clayton
headline: Paula J. Clayton Dies at 86; Helped Destigmatize Depression and Suicide
abstract: A clinical psychiatrist, she showed that suicide was often a result of mental illness, and that it could be avoided with the right treatment and public education.

name: Cynthia Harris
headline: Cynthia Harris, the Mother on ‘Mad About You,’ Dies at 87
abstract: She was a familiar, sometimes meddling, presence on a hit ’90s sitcom about a pair of newlyweds. Earlier she won acclaim as Wallis Simpson, who inspired a king to abdicate.

name: Budge Patty
headline: Budge Patty, Elegant Tennis Champion of the 1950s, Dies at 97
abstract: Known for his style as much as his forehand volley, he was one of only three Americans to win the French and Wimbledon men’s singles in the same year.

name: Violet Piercy
headline: Overlooked No More: Violet Piercy, Pioneering Marathoner
abstract: She established herself as one of the first known female endurance runners in Britain in 1926, a time when women were not permitted to compete in long-distance races.

name: Peter C. Bunnell
profession: Brought Academic Rigor to History of Photography
headline: Peter C. Bunnell, 83, Dies; Brought Academic Rigor to History of Photography
abstract: As a curator at MoMA and then a professor at Princeton, he pushed museums and art historians to take photography seriously.

name: Abolhassan Bani-Sadr
headline: Abolhassan Bani-Sadr, Former Iranian President, Dies at 88
abstract: He tried to resist the currents of Islamic radicalism, but was forced out of office when he lost the support of Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini.

name: Moshe Tendler
headline: Moshe Tendler, Authority on Jewish Medical Ethics, Dies at 95
abstract: His pronouncements — on sex, death, organ transplants and more — carried weight in no small part because he was both a master of Jewish scripture and a microbiologist.

name: Raymond T. Odierno
headline: Gen. Raymond T. Odierno Dies at 67; Oversaw Iraq Surge
abstract: The four-star general helped carry out the strategy to increase U.S. troop numbers, which was credited with turning the tide of sectarian killings.

name: Abdul Qadeer Khan
headline: Abdul Qadeer Khan, Father of Pakistan’s Nuclear Program, Dies at 85
abstract: Starting from scratch in 1976, he acquired the technology and knowledge that allowed Pakistan to detonate its first nuclear device in 1998.

name: Richard Schultz
headline: Richard Schultz, Designer Who Made the Outdoors Modern, Dies at 95
abstract: Working for Knoll, Mr. Schultz created furniture that became classics. One standout: a sleek mesh and aluminum chaise with wheels.

name: Dottie Dodgion
profession: Standout Drummer in More Ways Than One
headline: Dottie Dodgion, a Standout Drummer in More Ways Than One, Dies at 91
abstract: At a time when a female jazz percussionist was a rarity, she played with Benny Goodman and went on to work with Marian McPartland and other big names.

name: Iohan Gueorguiev
headline: Iohan Gueorguiev, ‘Bike Wanderer’ of the Wilderness, Dies at 33
abstract: He gained a following online for his lyrical appreciation of the open road while biking through remote landscapes and braving extreme conditions.

name: Bernard Tapie
headline: Bernard Tapie, French Tycoon, Actor and Politician, Dies at 78
abstract: His larger-than-life career, flamboyant personality and ongoing legal struggles made him one of the best-known personalities in France.

name: Anne Saxelby
headline: Anne Saxelby, Who Championed Fine American Cheeses, Dies at 40
abstract: When she opened her shop on the Lower East Side of Manhattan in 2006, she helped put American cheeses on the map, and on shopping lists.

name: Jimmy Neary
profession: Irish Pub Became a Power Brokers Hub
headline: Jimmy Neary, Whose Irish Pub Became a Power Brokers’ Hub, Dies at 91
abstract: Opening on St. Patrick’s Day, 1967, Neary’s attracted politicians, media players, archbishops and more, drawn as much by Mr. Neary himself as by the lamb chops.

name: Ruthie Tompson
profession: Breathed Animated Life Into Disney Films
headline: Ruthie Tompson Dies at 111; Breathed Animated Life Into Disney Films
abstract: One of a cadre of women who worked behind the scenes, she did indispensable but anonymous work on classics like “Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs” and “Pinocchio.”

name: Tony De Marco
headline: Tony De Marco, Welterweight Pride of Boston, Is Dead at 89
abstract: He was a North End hero “not because he’s the greatest prizefighter in the world, which he isn’t,” a sportswriter wrote, “but because he’s so damned courageous.”

name: Martin Sherwin
headline: Martin Sherwin, Prize-winning Biographer of Oppenheimer, Dies at 84
abstract: A historian of the nuclear age, he and his co-author, Kai Bird, won a 2006 Pulitzer for their book about the scientist behind the atom bomb.

name: Paddy Moloney
headline: Paddy Moloney, Piper Who Led Revival of Irish Music, Dies at 83
abstract: The Chieftains, the band he fronted for nearly 60 years, toured the world, collaborated with rock stars and helped spark a musical renaissance.

name: Albert J. Raboteau
headline: Albert J. Raboteau, Who Transformed Black Religious Studies, Dies at 78
abstract: Working in the 1970s and ’80s, his scholarship helped to cement African-American studies as an academic discipline.

name: Mary Bloom
headline: Mary Bloom, Photographer to the Dog Stars, Dies at 81
abstract: She was well known at the Westminster Kennel Club show for her ability to communicate with dogs. “I just understand who they are,” she said.

name: Myriam Sarachik
headline: Myriam Sarachik, Physicist Who Plumbed Magnetism, Dies at 88
abstract: She overcame bias against women in science and personal tragedy to perform groundbreaking work. She earned recognition for her achievements last year.

name: Raymond Gniewek
headline: Raymond Gniewek, 89, Met Orchestra’s Enduring Concertmaster, Dies
abstract: For 43 years he was a steadying force with the ensemble as he helped it become one of the world’s most esteemed.

name: Russ Kick
headline: Russ Kick, ‘Rogue Transparency Activist,’ Is Dead at 52
abstract: Working on his own, he used the Freedom of Information Act to publish suppressed documents, sometimes making front-page news.

name: Eric Cassell
headline: Dr. Eric Cassell, Bioethicist Who Put the Patient First, Dies at 93
abstract: A professor and prolific author, he cautioned that doctors too often focus on the disease instead of the overall well-being of the sufferer.

name: Mike Renzi
headline: Mike Renzi, a Jazz Singer’s Best Friend, Dies at 80
abstract: He was an in-demand accompanist and arranger for countless artists, including Mel Tormé, the duo of Lady Gaga and Tony Bennett, and the “Sesame Street” crew.

name: Gary Paulsen
headline: Gary Paulsen, Author of Young-Adult Adventures, Dies at 82
abstract: His 200 books, among them “Hatchet” and “Dogsong,” inspired generations with their tales of exploration, survival and the bloody reality of the natural world.

name: Andrea Martin
headline: Andrea Martin, R&B Songwriter, Dies at 49
abstract: She co-wrote hits for En Vogue, Toni Braxton and other artists in the 1990s and 2000s and was also a singer, releasing an album.

name: Brian Goldner
headline: Brian Goldner, Hasbro Executive With Hollywood Vision, Dies at 58
abstract: He turned a traditional maker of toys and games into an entertainment company with its own TV and movie studio.

name: David F. Kennedy
profession: Ad Agency Put Nike on the Map
headline: David F. Kennedy, Whose Ad Agency Put Nike on the Map, Dies at 82
abstract: Wieden+Kennedy, which he co-founded in Portland, Ore., broke from Madison Avenue tradition. Unlike many of its rivals, it has remained independent.

name: Timuel Black
profession: Strategist and Organizer for Black Chicago
headline: Timuel Black, Strategist and Organizer for Black Chicago, Dies at 102
abstract: He assembled attendees of the March on Washington, mentored a young Barack Obama and wielded the solidarity of the South Side as a tool for political power.

name: Anni Bergman
headline: Anni Bergman, Therapist Who Listened to Children, Dies at 102
abstract: She was part of a groundbreaking study that observed how very young children separated from their mothers. Late in life, she became a photographer’s muse.

name: Megan Rice
profession: Fierce Critic of U.S. Nuclear Arsenal
headline: Sister Megan Rice, Fierce Critic of U.S. Nuclear Arsenal, Dies at 91
abstract: Arrested more than 40 times, she was best known for her role in the 2012 break-in at the Oak Ridge nuclear complex in Tennessee.

name: Colin Powell
headline: Colin Powell, Who Shaped U.S. National Security, Dies at 84
abstract: A former chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, secretary of state and national security adviser, Mr. Powell died of complications of Covid-19, his family said.

name: Betty Lynn
profession: Thelma Lou on The Andy Griffith Show
headline: Betty Lynn, Thelma Lou on ‘The Andy Griffith Show,’ Dies at 95
abstract: She played Deputy Barney Fife’s girlfriend on the long-running sitcom and was remembered by fans with fondness more than 50 years later.

name: David Finn
profession: Co-Founder of a Public Relations Power
headline: David Finn, Co-Founder of a Public Relations Power, Dies at 100
abstract: While running Ruder Finn, with big clients like Philip Morris, Exxon and Coca-Cola, Mr. Finn pursued a parallel career as a painter, photographer and sculptor.

name: Nadia Chaudhri
headline: Nadia Chaudhri, Scientist With an End-of-Life Mission, Dies at 43
abstract: She documented her last months with ovarian cancer on Twitter while raising funds to support students from backgrounds that are underrepresented in the sciences.

name: Earl Old
headline: Earl Old Person, Chief of the Blackfeet Nation, Dies at 92
abstract: As the longest-serving elected tribal leader in the country, he pushed for self-sufficiency and greater respect from the federal government.

name: Leslie Bricusse
profession: Prolific Songwriter for Stage and Screen
headline: Leslie Bricusse, Prolific Songwriter for Stage and Screen, Dies at 90
abstract: His songs from “Stop the World,” “Willy Wonka,” “Goldfinger” and other shows and movies became hits for a range of performers.

name: Kim Hak-soon
profession: Broke the Silence for Comfort Women
headline: Overlooked No More: Kim Hak-soon, Who Broke the Silence for ‘Comfort Women’
abstract: Her public testimony about the horrors of sexual slavery that Japan had engineered for its World War II military encouraged other survivors to step forward.

name: Alan Lapidus
headline: Alan Lapidus, Architect of Hotels and Casinos, Dies at 85
abstract: He followed in the footsteps of his architect father, Morris, with glitzy landmarks in Times Square, Las Vegas and Atlantic City, where Donald Trump was a client.

name: Diane Weyermann
headline: Diane Weyermann, Executive Who Championed ‘An Inconvenient Truth,’ Dies at 66
abstract: A former public interest lawyer, she oversaw this and many other documentaries that addressed urgent social issues.

name: Jerry Pinkney
headline: Jerry Pinkney, Acclaimed Children’s Book Illustrator, Dies at 81
abstract: Adept at reimagining classic tales, he often made sure that his books included Black characters and themes.

name: Bernard Haitink
headline: Bernard Haitink, Conductor Who Let Music Speak for Itself, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Haitink, who was closely identified with the Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra in Amsterdam, drew direct, unaffected interpretations of symphonic works and opera.

name: Geert Jan van Oldenborgh
profession: Linked Weather Disasters to Climate Change
headline: Geert Jan van Oldenborgh, 59, Dies; Linked Weather Disasters to Climate Change
abstract: With a colleague, he founded a group that quickly analyzes heat waves and other extreme events for signs of global warming’s influence.

name: Tom Morey
headline: Tom Morey, Surfer Who Invented the Boogie Board, Dies at 86
abstract: He created a lightweight, flexible board out of a piece of foam in his backyard in Hawaii in 1971. It introduced millions to the pleasures of riding waves on their bellies.

name: Dorothy Steel
profession: Big-Screen Career Had a Late Start
headline: Dorothy Steel, Whose Big-Screen Career Had a Late Start, Dies at 95
abstract: She was cast in “Black Panther” at 90, not long after she began acting professionally. “As soon as we saw her,” the movie’s casting director said, “we wanted her.”

name: Edita Gruberova
headline: Edita Gruberova, Dazzling Soprano With Emotional Power, Dies at 74
abstract: A Slovak coloratura, she was a fixture at the opera houses of Vienna and Munich, artfully balancing technical brilliance with deep expression.

name: Peter Scolari
headline: Peter Scolari, ‘Newhart’ and ‘Girls’ Actor, Is Dead at 66
abstract: His first big break came as Tom Hanks’s co-star on the TV comedy “Bosom Buddies” in the early 1980s. He also worked on the stage, occasionally on Broadway.

name: Chuck Bundrant
headline: Chuck Bundrant, Pacific Fisheries’ ‘Henry Ford,’ Dies at 79
abstract: In 1961 he arrived in Seattle with no job, no skills and $80. Over the next 60 years, he built a seafood empire and transformed the industry.

name: Jay Black
profession: Soaring Lead Singer of the Americans
headline: Jay Black, Soaring Lead Singer of the Americans, Dies at 82
abstract: His majestic voice was the key to hits like “Only in America,” “Come a Little Bit Closer” and his signature song, “Cara, Mia.”

name: Paul Salata
headline: Paul Salata, Champion of the N.F.L.’s ‘Irrelevant,’ Dies at 94
abstract: He created an annual award to honor the player picked last in the college draft, because, he said, “they do their work and should be noticed.”

name: Dee Pop
profession: Drummer and Downtown New York Fixture
headline: Dee Pop, Drummer and Downtown New York Fixture, Dies at 65
abstract: Initially known for his tight and soulful playing with the celebrated post-punk band Bush Tetras, he later became an entrepreneur of avant-garde music.

name: James Michael Tyler
headline: James Michael Tyler, Who Played Gunther on ‘Friends,’ Dies at 59
abstract: A real barista who was cast as a Central Perk co-worker of his crush, Jennifer Aniston’s character, he appeared in 150 episodes of the hit show.

name: Gene Freidman
headline: Gene Freidman, ‘Taxi King’ Who Upended His Industry, Dies at 50
abstract: He bid up the price of medallions and borrowed against them. When their value plummeted, immigrant cabbies were left deep in debt.

name: Roh Tae-woo
profession: South Korean Leader in Move Toward Democracy
headline: Roh Tae-woo, 88, South Korean Leader in Move Toward Democracy, Dies
abstract: He played a role in a bloody crackdown on pro-democracy protesters in 1980, then oversaw his country’s winning 1988 Olympics bid. He was later mired in legal trouble.

name: Arnold Hano
profession: Author of a Bleachers View Baseball Classic
headline: Arnold Hano, Author of a Bleachers’ View Baseball Classic, Dies at 99
abstract: “A Day in the Bleachers” recalled what he saw, heard and felt at the Polo Grounds during a 1954 World Series game in which Willie Mays made “the Catch.”

name: Sonny Osborne
headline: Sonny Osborne, Bluegrass Innovator, Is Dead at 83
abstract: He and his brother, Bobby, pioneered a style of three-part harmony singing that broke with bluegrass tradition. He was also an influential banjo player.

name: Mort Sahl
headline: Mort Sahl, Whose Biting Commentary Redefined Stand-Up, Dies at 94
abstract: A self-appointed warrior against hypocrisy, he revolutionized comedy in the 1950s by addressing political and social issues.

name: Martha Henry
headline: Martha Henry, Indefatigable Stage Actress, Dies at 83
abstract: For decades her work at the Stratford Festival in Canada drew acclaim. She gave her last performance in a wheelchair while dying of cancer.

name: David DePatie
headline: David DePatie, Producer Behind the Pink Panther, Dies at 91
abstract: He and the animator Friz Freleng created the cool feline character he called “the James Bond of the animation world.” The character’s first cartoon won an Oscar.

name: Viktor Bryukhanov
headline: Viktor Bryukhanov, Blamed for the Chernobyl Disaster, Dies at 85
abstract: In charge of the plant in Ukraine, he was held responsible for the world’s worst nuclear-power disaster and imprisoned.

name: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi
headline: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi, the Father of ‘Flow,’ Dies at 87
abstract: His work as a psychologist on the benefits of intense focus led to a global best seller, a term that became a cultural touchstone and new ideas about the path to happiness.

name: Val Bisoglio
headline: Val Bisoglio, Oft-Cast Character Actor, Dies at 95
abstract: He was seen on “Quincy, M.E.” and “The Sopranos.” He also memorably played John Travolta’s father in “Saturday Night Fever.”

name: Eleonore von Trapp Campbell
headline: Eleonore von Trapp Campbell, of the ‘Sound of Music’ Family, Dies at 90
abstract: She was a member of the Trapp Family Singers, which toured internationally, though she herself was not depicted in the musical or the film.

name: Richard Hammer
headline: Richard Hammer, Who Illuminated the My Lai Massacre, Dies at 93
abstract: His books on that Vietnam episode drew acclaim, and he was an Edgar Award-winning author of nonfiction books about crime in its many manifestations.

name: Mimi Levin Lieber
profession: Her Focus Groups Shaped Postwar Marketing
headline: Mimi Levin Lieber, 93, Dies; Her Focus Groups Shaped Postwar Marketing
abstract: She helped Fortune 500 companies sell to women in the 1960s and ’70s, then became a stalwart promoter of early childhood literacy.

name: Rose Lee Maphis
profession: Early Star of Country Music TV
headline: Rose Lee Maphis, Early Star of Country Music TV, Dies at 98
abstract: She and her husband, Joe (“Mr. and Mrs. Country Music”), helped give birth to a West Coast music scene later associated with Buck Owens and Merle Haggard.

name: Bruce Gaston
headline: Bruce Gaston, American Maestro of Thai Music, Dies at 75
abstract: A transplanted Californian and former conscientious objector, he infused Thai music with Western sounds as a prominent composer and performer based in Bangkok.

name: Jo-Carroll Dennison
profession: Miss America During World War II
headline: Jo-Carroll Dennison, Miss America During World War II, Dies at 97
abstract: The oldest surviving former Miss America, she was among the first to object to wearing a swimsuit during her reign.

name: Pauline Bart
headline: Pauline Bart, Sociologist Who Mapped Women’s Challenges, Dies at 91
abstract: She researched the ways gender biases harmed women, and she wrote about her findings in studies laced with compassion and wry humor.

name: Louise Slade
headline: Louise Slade, Scientist Who Studied the Molecules in Food, Dies at 74
abstract: Her research focused on how to keep dough, bread, cookies and crackers tasting delicious even after weeks on a grocery store shelf.

name: Muriel Lezak
headline: Muriel Lezak, Leading Authority on Brain Injuries, Dies at 94
abstract: A neuropsychologist, she wrote a textbook that became an essential guide to describing and evaluating brain damage and dysfunction.

name: Aaron T. Beck
headline: Dr. Aaron T. Beck, Developer of Cognitive Therapy, Dies at 100
abstract: It was an answer to Freudian analysis: a pragmatic, thought-monitoring approach to treating anxiety, depression and other mental disorders, and it changed psychiatry.

name: Ronnie Tutt
headline: Ronnie Tutt, Drummer Who Backed Both Elvises, Dies at 83
abstract: He was a force in Elvis Presley’s TCB band and accompanied other big names like Elvis Costello, Jerry Garcia and Billy Joel.

name: Linwood Holton
headline: Linwood Holton, 98,Virginia Governor Who Pushed for Racial Equality, Dies
abstract: The first Republican governor of the state in almost a century, he seemed to herald a new, post-racial South. He later became disillusioned with his own party.

name: Manuel Neri
profession: Figurative Sculptor With a Modern Twist
headline: Manuel Neri, Figurative Sculptor With a Modern Twist, Dies at 91
abstract: Mr. Neri was a stalwart of the Bay Area art scene but exhibited widely, known for mixing artistic mediums and styles.

name: Pat Martino
headline: Pat Martino, Jazz Guitarist Who Overcame Amnesia, Dies at 77
abstract: He was one of the genre’s most acclaimed players when brain surgery left him with no memory. But he recovered and made music for another three decades.

name: Sunao Tsuboi
headline: Sunao Tsuboi, 96, Dies; Hiroshima Victim Who Lived to Tell His Story
abstract: After suffering through the agony of the attack and its aftermath, he devoted himself to spreading the message that nuclear weapons should be abolished.

name: Tony Downs
headline: Tony Downs, Economist Who Studied Why People Vote, Dies at 90
abstract: He explored democracy, traffic congestion, race relations and bureaucrats through the prism of an economist.

name: Richard M. Ohmann
profession: Brought Radical Politics to College English
headline: Richard M. Ohmann, 90, Dies; Brought Radical Politics to College English
abstract: Inspired by the antiwar movement of the 1960s, he helped transform humanities by making room for subjects like women’s studies and Marxist criticism.

name: Margaret York
headline: Margaret York, an L.A.P.D. Model for ‘Cagney & Lacey,’ Dies at 80
abstract: She became the police force’s highest ranking woman after she and a detective partner inspired a TV series fighting crime in the streets and sexism in the ranks.

name: Tom Matte
headline: Tom Matte, Emergency Quarterback for Baltimore Colts, Dies at 82
abstract: A gritty running back, he was enlisted to replace Johnny Unitas and his backup as quarterback in critical games in 1965. He wore a wristband to remember the plays.

name: Nelson Freire
profession: Piano Virtuoso of Warmth and Finesse
headline: Nelson Freire, Piano Virtuoso of Warmth and Finesse, Dies at 77
abstract: Hailing from Brazil as one of the great pianists of the last half of the 20th century, he recalled masters of the first half in his virtuosity. But he shunned the limelight.

name: Pamela McCorduck
headline: Pamela McCorduck, Historian of Artificial Intelligence, Dies at 80
abstract: She interviewed many of the scientists who were at the heart of the field through the end of the 1970s, and she compiled a groundbreaking history of its early years.

name: Louise Blanchard Bethune
headline: Overlooked No More: Louise Blanchard Bethune, Who Changed the Face of Buffalo
abstract: She is widely considered to have been the first American woman to become a certified architect, and she left her stamp throughout western New York and in New England.

name: Ivy Nicholson
headline: Ivy Nicholson, Model and Warhol Factory Star, Dies at 88
abstract: She blazed through 1950s Europe as a top fashion model and then became a part of the 1960s Warhol crowd in New York before falling on hard times.

name: Camille Saviola
profession: Deep Space Nine and Stage Actor
headline: Camille Saviola, ‘Deep Space Nine’ and Stage Actor, Dies at 71
abstract: She was known for her comic work in cabarets, for her performance in the musical “Nine” on Broadway and for her role in a “Star Trek” spinoff.

name: Ronnie Wilson
headline: Ronnie Wilson, Founder of the Gap Band, Dies at 73
abstract: After beginning his career as a teenager, he joined with his two younger brothers to record R&B hits like “You Dropped a Bomb on Me” and “Outstanding.”

name: Julie Green
headline: Julie Green, Artist Who Memorialized Inmates’ Last Suppers, Dies at 60
abstract: For more than two decades, she rendered death row prisoners’ requests for a last meal on a series of plates, bringing a human face to capital punishment.

name: William Conway
headline: William Conway, Who Reimagined America’s Zoos, Is Dead at 91
abstract: He sought to conserve wildlife and encouraged zoos to exhibit animals in their natural habitats. But he lost a battle to rename the Bronx Zoo.

name: Aaron Feuerstein
headline: Aaron Feuerstein, Mill Owner Who Refused to Leave, Dies at 95
abstract: After a fire devastated his Massachusetts factory in 1995, he kept paying his employees and spent hundreds of millions to rebuild.

name: JoAnna Cameron
headline: JoAnna Cameron, an Early Female Superhero on TV, Is Dead at 73
abstract: In addition to achieving Saturday morning fame as Isis, she was said to have appeared in more national television commercials than anyone in advertising history.

name: Mark Glaze
headline: Mark Glaze, Influential Gun Control Advocate, Dies at 51
abstract: As the executive director of Everytown for Gun Safety, he took on the National Rifle Association and helped make gun violence a winning issue.

name: Michael Rutter
headline: Michael Rutter, Pioneering Child Psychiatrist, Is Dead at 88
abstract: His wide-ranging research helped transform his field, a colleague said, by “insisting on using data to drive thinking about diagnosis and treatment.”

name: Stephen Karpiak
headline: Stephen Karpiak, Pathbreaking H.I.V. Researcher, Dies at 74
abstract: His work helped change people’s attitude toward older people living with the virus that causes AIDS.

name: Elaine Romagnoli
headline: Elaine Romagnoli, Longtime Fixture of Lesbian Nightlife, Dies at 79
abstract: The bustling downtown bars that Ms. Romagnoli created, beginning in 1972, became central to New York City’s gay community.

name: Earl A. Grollman
profession: Sought to Demystify Death and Grief
headline: Rabbi Earl A. Grollman, 96, Dies; Sought to Demystify Death and Grief
abstract: He wrote prolifically about grief, counseled the bereaved after 9/11 and the Oklahoma City bombing and paid particular attention to children. “Grief is the price we pay for love,” he’d say.

name: Max Cleland
headline: Max Cleland, Vietnam Veteran and Former Senator, Dies at 79
abstract: He lost both legs and an arm in the war. Republicans impugned his patriotism by linking him to Osama bin Laden in an infamous TV spot.

name: Dean Stockwell
profession: Child Actor Turned Quantum Leap Star
headline: Dean Stockwell, Child Actor Turned ‘Quantum Leap’ Star, Dies at 85
abstract: He appeared alongside Frank Sinatra and Gene Kelly when he was not yet 10. He later had signature roles in movies like “Married to the Mob” and “Blue Velvet.”

name: Ruth Ann Minner
headline: Ruth Ann Minner, Down-to-Earth Governor of Delaware, Dies at 86
abstract: The first woman in that position, she rose from being a receptionist in the governor’s office to claiming the top job herself.

name: Don Maddox
profession: Last Survivor of a Pioneering Country Band
headline: Don Maddox, Last Survivor of a Pioneering Country Band, Dies at 98
abstract: In the 1940s, he joined with his three brothers and his sister, Rose, to make exuberant music that anticipated rockabilly and rock ’n’ roll.

name: Peter L. Zimroth
headline: Peter L. Zimroth, Who Oversaw Stop-and-Frisk Reforms, Dies at 78
abstract: As New York City’s chief legal officer, he drafted a model public campaign financing law and fought bias against women in private clubs.

name: F.W. de Klerk
headline: F.W. de Klerk, South Africa President Who Ended Apartheid, Dies at 85
abstract: A prominent Afrikaner, he defended the separation of the races before helping to dismantle that system, leading to his sharing the Nobel Peace Prize with Nelson Mandela.

name: Jonathan Reynolds
headline: Jonathan Reynolds, Playwright and Food Columnist, Dies at 79
abstract: His plays tended to parody American institutions. His food writing tended to be full of humor.

name: Steven Mark Klein
headline: Steven Mark Klein, Fashion Archivist and Gadfly, Dies at 70
abstract: His collection of fashion ephemera now fills a museum, but he also chastised the industry, all while making a name as a brand adviser to hotels and restaurants.

name: Edward L. Sadowsky
profession: Lion of the New York City Council
headline: Edward L. Sadowsky, a Lion of the New York City Council, Dies at 92
abstract: A liberal legislator from Queens, he served for 24 years and polished the Council’s reputation as it prepared to inherit greater powers.

name: Quandra Prettyman
headline: Quandra Prettyman, Champion of Black Women’s Literature, Dies at 88
abstract: As Barnard’s first Black full-time faculty member, she broke ground in merging feminist literary studies with a study of Black writers.

name: Zuo Fang
headline: Zuo Fang, Chinese Journalist Who Challenged the Powerful, Dies at 86
abstract: When he helped start Southern Weekly, he charted a course for a freer era for the country’s press, which later became increasingly constrained by Beijing.

name: Pedro Feliciano
profession: Durable Relief Pitcher for the Mets
headline: Pedro Feliciano, Durable Relief Pitcher for the Mets, Dies at 45
abstract: He led the major leagues in appearances from 2008 to 2010, earning him the nickname Perpetual Pedro.

name: John Artis
headline: John Artis, Convicted With Rubin (Hurricane) Carter, Dies at 75
abstract: He was the “forgotten man” in the triple murder case that was eventually overturned and that exposed flaws in the criminal justice system.

name: Helene Fortunoff
headline: Helene Fortunoff, Who Built a Family Jewelry Empire, Dies at 88
abstract: A powerhouse female executive in a male-dominated industry, she hired a team of mostly women buyers who traveled the world to find unusual gems.

name: Graeme Edge
profession: Drummer and Co-Founder of the Moody Blues
headline: Graeme Edge, Drummer and Co-Founder of the Moody Blues, Dies at 80
abstract: Many of their songs incorporated his spoken-word poetry, making them pioneers in the prog-rock movement of the late-1960s and ’70s.

name: Jane Brown Grimes
headline: Jane Brown Grimes, Rare Female Force in Tennis, Dies at 80
abstract: She was a top executive at three organizations, including the International Tennis Hall of Fame, where she was later inducted.

name: Bettina Grossman
profession: Artistic Fixture at the Chelsea Hotel
headline: Bettina Grossman, an Artistic Fixture at the Chelsea Hotel, Dies at 94
abstract: Her apartment was so crowded with her artwork that she slept in the hallway. But she did not become widely known until near the end of her life.

name: Sam Huff
profession: Fearsome Hall of Fame Giants Linebacker
headline: Sam Huff, Fearsome Hall of Fame Giants Linebacker, Dies at 87
abstract: Huff, who became the epitome of the rough-and-tough football star with New York, was remembered for his head-on duels with two of the game’s greatest fullbacks.

name: Etel Adnan
headline: Etel Adnan, Lebanese American Author and Artist, Dies at 96
abstract: Her novel about a kidnapping in Lebanon has become a classic of war literature. She was in her 80s when her art started to draw international attention.

name: Lee Maracle
headline: Lee Maracle, Combative Indigenous Author, Dies at 71
abstract: She collected signatures to persuade publishers that people would buy her books. She became a foundational figure in Indigenous literature.

name: Alan Paller
headline: Alan Paller, a Mover on Cybersecurity Threat, Is Dead at 76
abstract: He made it his mission to find, recruit and develop the next generation of digital warriors to defend the nation against an onslaught of cyberattacks.

name: Terence Wilson
profession: Key Part of Reggae Band UB40
headline: Terence Wilson, Key Part of Reggae Band UB40, Dies at 64
abstract: As Astro with a popular racially diverse British group, he added rap vocals to hits like “Red Red Wine.”

name: Clarissa Eden
headline: Clarissa Eden, British Countess and Political Influencer, Dies at 101
abstract: The iconoclastic niece of Winston Churchill, she was married to Prime Minister Anthony Eden, who was at the helm during the Suez crisis.

name: Maureen Cleave
headline: Maureen Cleave, Pop Journalist and Beatles Confidante, Dies at 87
abstract: Ms. Cleave’s interview with John Lennon, in which he said the Beatles were “more popular than Jesus,” drew worldwide attention.

name: Bob Gill
headline: Bob Gill, Graphic Designer Who Elevated the ‘Message,’ Dies at 90
abstract: He was a groundbreaking master of the visual pun, part of a generation of designers for whom the aesthetic was in service to the idea.

name: Ed Lucas
headline: Ed Lucas, Blind Baseball Chronicler, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Sightless since 12, he became a baseball columnist and a radio reporter. He had a unique ability to know where a ball was hit by the sound of the crack of the bat.

name: Ed Bullins
profession: Leading Playwright of the Black Arts Movement
headline: Ed Bullins, Leading Playwright of the Black Arts Movement, Dies at 86
abstract: He wrote not for white or middle-class audiences, but for the strivers, hustlers and quiet sufferers whose struggles he sought to capture in searing works.

name: Raúl Rivero
profession: Disenchanted Poet of the Cuban Revolution
headline: Raúl Rivero, Disenchanted Poet of the Cuban Revolution, Dies at 75
abstract: A leading journalistic voice who broke with the Castro regime, he gained wide recognition for his protests, was jailed as a dissident and went into exile.

name: Philip Margo
headline: Philip Margo of the Tokens, Who Sang of a Snoozing Lion, Dies at 79
abstract: His baritone contributed to the 1961 hit “The Lion Sleeps Tonight,” which became one of the most recognizable American pop songs ever.

name: Justus Rosenberg
profession: Beloved Professor With a Heroic Past
headline: Justus Rosenberg, Beloved Professor With a Heroic Past, Dies at 100
abstract: As a teenager, he helped provide safe passage to artists and intellectuals out of Vichy France. He went on to teach literature at Bard College for six decades.

name: Jimmie Durham
headline: Jimmie Durham, Sculptor Who Explored Indigenous Themes, Dies at 81
abstract: He played with and challenged Native American stereotypes, then was criticized by Cherokee artists for tracing his ancestry to their tribe.

name: Dave Frishberg
profession: Writer of Songs Sardonic and Nostalgic
headline: Dave Frishberg, Writer of Songs Sardonic and Nostalgic, Dies at 88
abstract: A gifted jazz pianist and a singer with a limited range but a distinctive voice, he wrote mostly for grown-ups but reached his largest audience on “Schoolhouse Rock!”

name: Wilbur Smith
headline: Wilbur Smith, Best-Selling Author of Swashbuckling Novels, Dies at 88
abstract: His books were full of lovers, dysfunctional families, pirates and hunters, and set in locations from ancient Egypt to colonial Africa. They sold in the millions.

name: Ruth Polsky
headline: Overlooked No More: Ruth Polsky, Who Shaped New York’s Music Scene
abstract: She booked concerts at influential nightclubs in the 1980s, bringing exposure to up-and-coming artists like the Smiths and New Order.

name: Bettina Plevan
headline: Bettina Plevan, Litigator Who Shattered Glass Ceilings, Dies at 75
abstract: After her own meteoric rise to partner at Proskauer Rose, where she handled sexual harassment cases, she helped other women advance in the legal profession.

name: W. Sterling Cary
headline: Rev. W. Sterling Cary, Pioneering Black Churchman, Dies at 94
abstract: He embraced what became known as Black liberation theology and, in 1972, became the first Black leader of the National Council of Churches.

name: Bob Bondurant
headline: Bob Bondurant, Car Racer Who Tutored Actors on the Track, Dies at 88
abstract: After a racetrack accident put him in the hospital, he pivoted to open a driving school, where his students included Paul Newman, Tom Cruise and Christian Bale.

name: Bonnie Sherk
headline: Bonnie Sherk, Landscape Artist Full of Surprises, Dies at 76
abstract: Her artwork included transforming forlorn parcels, sometimes by planting them, other times just by sitting in them.

name: Caroline Todd
headline: Caroline Todd, Half of a Mystery-Writing Duo, Dies at 86
abstract: Writing under the pen name Charles Todd, she and her son published nearly 40 mystery novels, all of them set in rural England just after World War I.

name: Mick Rock
headline: Mick Rock, Sought-After Rock Photographer, Dies at 72
abstract: His images of David Bowie, Lou Reed, Queen and others helped define the 1970s. He was still shooting the stars decades later.

name: Jay Last
headline: Jay Last, One of the Rebels Who Founded Silicon Valley, Dies at 92
abstract: He and seven others left the Shockley Semiconductor Laboratory to create their own silicon company, Fairchild Semiconductor, which is now seen as ground zero for the West Coast tech industry.

name: Ardeshir Zahedi
headline: Ardeshir Zahedi, Irrepressible Iranian Diplomat, Dies at 93
abstract: While he enabled business deals worth billions of dollars, he also hosted lavish parties, led conga lines through his embassy and dated Elizabeth Taylor.

name: Robert Bly
headline: Robert Bly, Poet Who Gave Rise to a Men’s Movement, Dies at 94
abstract: His most famous, and most controversial, work was “Iron John,” which made the case that American men had grown soft and feminized. It made him a cultural phenomenon.

name: Nathan Johnson
headline: Nathan Johnson, Modernist Architect of Black Churches, Dies at 96
abstract: He opened his practice in Detroit in the 1950s, and his first commissions were to usher many of the city’s historic Black churches into the 20th century.

name: Sylvère Lotringer
headline: Sylvère Lotringer, Shape-Shifting Force of the Avant-Garde, Dies at 83
abstract: He succeeded in making French philosophy hip and provoking mainstream American culture, but he couldn’t vanquish his childhood memories of Nazi rule.

name: Chun Doo-hwan
headline: Chun Doo-hwan, Ex-Military Dictator in South Korea, Dies at 90
abstract: The country’s most vilified former military dictator, he seized power in a coup and ruled his country with an iron fist for most of the 1980s.

name: Ian Fishback
headline: Maj. Ian Fishback, Who Exposed Abuse of Detainees, Dies at 42
abstract: His letter to two senators about beatings by U.S. troops in Iraq led to legislation in 2005 prohibiting extreme mistreatment of military prisoners.

name: Bill Virdon
profession: Quiet Manager of Four M.L.B. Teams
headline: Bill Virdon, Quiet Manager of Four M.L.B. Teams, Dies at 90
abstract: As a player, mainly for the Pirates, he was an outstanding center fielder and hit a catalytic ground ball in the 1960 World Series against the Yankees.

name: Zena Stein
headline: Zena Stein, 99, Dies; Researcher Championed Women’s Health
abstract: She studied the impact of AIDS on women and explored the effects of famine and poverty on health with an “unwavering commitment to social justice.”

name: Peter Buck
profession: Co-Founder of the Subway Sandwich Chain
headline: Peter Buck, Co-Founder of the Subway Sandwich Chain, Dies at 90
abstract: The $1,000 loan he gave to a friend’s son was used to start a single sandwich shop. That shop grew into the world’s biggest fast-food chain.

name: Slide Hampton
headline: Slide Hampton, Trombonist, Composer and Arranger, Dies at 89
abstract: He began playing professionally as a child, worked with some of jazz’s biggest names in the 1950s and was a leading figure in the music for the next 60 years.

name: Margo Guryan
headline: Margo Guryan, Whose Album Drew Belated Acclaim, Dies at 84
abstract: She recorded “Take a Picture” in 1968, but it died when she declined to tour. Three decades later, adventurous listeners discovered it and gave it a new life.

name: Kariamu Welsh
headline: Kariamu Welsh, Pioneer of African Dance Studies, Dies at 72
abstract: Inspired by double Dutch jump rope moves she saw growing up in Brooklyn, she developed an influential dance technique based on archetypes found in African art.

name: Noah Gordon
profession: American Novelist With an Audience Overseas
headline: Noah Gordon, 95, Dies; American Novelist With an Audience Overseas
abstract: His first book, “The Rabbi,” was a best seller in the U.S. Almost all his other novels were best sellers, too — but in Western Europe.

name: Jakucho Setouchi
profession: Buddhist Priest Wrote of Sex and Love
headline: Jakucho Setouchi, 99, Dies; Buddhist Priest Wrote of Sex and Love
abstract: Her more than 400 novels often drew on her own romantic affairs, and her translation of an 11th-century romantic Japanese classic sold millions of copies.

name: Stephen Sondheim
headline: Stephen Sondheim, Titan of the American Musical, Is Dead at 91
abstract: He was the theater’s most revered and influential composer-lyricist of the last half of the 20th century and the driving force behind some of Broadway’s most beloved and celebrated shows.

name: Wakefield Poole
headline: Wakefield Poole, Pioneer in Gay Pornography, Dies at 85
abstract: He gave up a dance career to create a crossover, and now classic, hit film in 1971 that had both gay and straight audiences, and celebrities, lining up to see it.

name: Laszlo Z. Bito
headline: Laszlo Z. Bito, Scientist, Novelist and Philanthropist, Dies at 87
abstract: He fled communist rule in Hungary, discovered a treatment for glaucoma in the U.S., then became an author and a voice against authoritarianism in his homeland.

name: Sylvia Weinstock
headline: Sylvia Weinstock, the ‘da Vinci of Wedding Cakes,’ Dies at 91
abstract: She produced floral-draped architectural works in the shape of rose-studded topiaries, baskets of speckled lilies and bouquets of anemones.

name: Virgil Abloh
headline: Virgil Abloh, Path-Blazing Designer, Is Dead at 41
abstract: His expansive approach to design inspired comparisons to artists including Andy Warhol and Jeff Koons. For him, clothes were totems of identity.

name: Phil Saviano
headline: Phil Saviano, Survivor of Clergy Sex Abuse, Dies at 69
abstract: He played a pivotal role in helping The Boston Globe uncover the widespread scandal in the Catholic Church and was portrayed in the movie “Spotlight.”

name: Carrie P. Meek
headline: Carrie P. Meek, U.S. Lawmaker Who Made Racial History, Dies at 95
abstract: She was the first Black person to represent Florida in the House since Reconstruction, and in five terms she fought for programs to create jobs.

name: Lee Elder
headline: Lee Elder, Who Broke a Golf Color Barrier, Dies at 87
abstract: In his prime he played in a league for Black players, but in 1975, at 40, he became the first African American to take part in the Masters tournament.

name: Arlene Dahl
headline: Arlene Dahl, Movie Star Turned Entrepreneur, Is Dead at 96
abstract: She had already started branching out when her film career was at its height, writing a syndicated column and launching a fashion and cosmetics business.

name: Doyle Hamm
headline: Doyle Hamm, Who Survived a Bungled Execution, Dies in Prison at 64
abstract: The failed lethal injection for Mr. Hamm, who was terminally ill, amounted to what his lawyer said was a case of cruel and unusual punishment.

name: Adolfo
headline: Adolfo, Designer Who Dressed Nancy Reagan, Dies at 98
abstract: Adolfo, who began as a milliner and took inspiration from Chanel, was also a favorite of New York society women.

name: David Gulpilil
headline: David Gulpilil, Famed Aboriginal Actor, Dies at 68
abstract: In a career that began with the film “Walkabout” 50 years ago, he was acclaimed for changing the way Australia’s Indigenous people were portrayed and viewed.

name: Jim Warren
headline: Jim Warren, Early Influencer in Personal Computing, Dies at 85
abstract: He personified the blend of technical enthusiasm and counterculture values that shaped the industry, launching the West Coast Computer Faire in the 1970s.

name: Alvin Lucier
headline: Alvin Lucier, Probing Composer of Soundscapes, Is Dead at 90
abstract: His experimental music was rooted in the physics of sound and might yield unpredictable results — in one instance a Beatles song emanating from a teapot.

name: Don Demeter
headline: Don Demeter, a Dodger Star of the Future Who Wasn’t, Dies at 86
abstract: Groomed to replace Duke Snider, he broke his wrist in 1960 and never lived up to expectations. But he had a fine career with four other teams.

name: Marcus Lamb
headline: Marcus Lamb, Christian Broadcaster and Vaccine Skeptic, Dies of Covid at 64
abstract: Mr. Lamb, who co-founded the Daystar Television Network, repeatedly suggested on air that people pray instead of getting vaccinated.

name: Curley Culp
profession: Defensive Anchor of Two Football Teams
headline: Curley Culp, Defensive Anchor of Two Football Teams, Dies at 75
abstract: A bruising Hall of Famer, Culp helped lead the Kansas City Chiefs to an upset victory in Super Bowl IV. With the Houston Oilers, he revolutionized the role of nose tackle.

name: Lamine Diack
profession: Olympics Power Broker Convicted of Taking Bribes
headline: Lamine Diack, Olympics Power Broker Convicted of Taking Bribes, Dies at 88
abstract: The former head of the world governing body for track and field was convicted of accepting bribes to cover up a Russian doping scandal.

name: Stu Rasmussen
profession: First Openly Transgender Mayor in America
headline: Stu Rasmussen, 73, First Openly Transgender Mayor in America, Dies
abstract: The mayor, who served two terms in Silverton, Ore., defied many conventions, gender being just one of them.

name: Ralph E. Ablon
headline: Ralph E. Ablon, Pioneer of Corporate Conglomerates, Dies at 105
abstract: After expanding a family scrap metal business into a hodgepodge of some 55 companies, he then successfully focused on the service economy.

name: Almudena Grandes
headline: Almudena Grandes, Novelist of Spain’s Marginalized, Dies at 61
abstract: Beginning with an acclaimed erotic novel, she became what the prime minister called “one of the most important writers of our time.”

name: Franz Streitwieser
profession: Trumpet Maestro With a Trove of Brass
headline: Franz Streitwieser, Trumpet Maestro With a Trove of Brass, Dies at 82
abstract: He accumulated more than 1,000 items with provenances spanning centuries, all housed for a time in a converted barn in rural Pennsylvania.

name: LaMarr Hoyt
headline: LaMarr Hoyt, Pitcher Whose Star Shone Brightly but Briefly, Dies at 66
abstract: He won the 1983 Cy Young Award as the American League’s leading pitcher, but an injury and troubles with drugs and the law ended his career prematurely.

name: Susan Rosenblatt
headline: Susan Rosenblatt, Who Took On Big Tobacco, Dies at 70
abstract: She was the quieter half of a law partnership with her husband that pursued a suit against cigarette companies on behalf of Florida smokers.

name: Julia Tuttle
headline: Overlooked No More: Julia Tuttle, the ‘Mother of Miami’
abstract: She worked tirelessly to revitalize the area now known as Miami, and is widely recognized as the only woman to have founded a major American city.

name: Sherif R. Zaki
headline: Dr. Sherif R. Zaki, Acclaimed Disease Detective, Dies at 65
abstract: He helped identify numerous viruses, including Covid-19, as well as the bioterrorism attack that spread anthrax in 2001.

name: Lawrence Weiner
headline: Lawrence Weiner, Artist Whose Medium Was Language, Dies at 79
abstract: A pioneer of the Conceptual art movement, he used words as his métier more than any other artist of his generation.

name: Eddie Mekka
headline: Eddie Mekka, a Star of ‘Laverne & Shirley,’ Is Dead at 69
abstract: As Carmine Ragusa on the hit sitcom, he got to show off his singing, tap-dancing and gymnastic skills — and to croon “Rags to Riches” many times.

name: Stonewall Jackson
profession: Grand Ole Opry Star for Over 60 Years
headline: Stonewall Jackson, Grand Ole Opry Star for Over 60 Years, Dies at 89
abstract: His biggest record, “Waterloo,” topped the country music chart for five weeks in 1959 and became a crossover hit.

name: Constance Ahrons
headline: Constance Ahrons, Advocate of ‘Good Divorce,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Her efforts to reduce the stigma of divorce included coining the term “binuclear” to refer to families in two separate households.

name: Bob Dole
profession: Old Soldier and Stalwart of the Senate
headline: Bob Dole, Old Soldier and Stalwart of the Senate, Dies at 98
abstract: Mr. Dole, a son of the Kansas prairie who was left for dead on a World War II battlefield, became one of the longest-serving Republican leaders.

name: Ken Moffett
profession: Top Federal Mediator and Union Official
headline: Ken Moffett, Top Federal Mediator and Union Official, Dies at 90
abstract: In the busy summer of 1981, he mediated labor disputes involving baseball players, postal workers and air traffic controllers. He later briefly ran the players’ union.

name: Antony Sher
headline: Antony Sher, Actor Acclaimed for His Versatility, Dies at 72
abstract: In his long career, most of it with the Royal Shakespeare Company, he played everyone from King Lear to Primo Levi to Ringo Starr.

name: Norodom Ranariddh
headline: Norodom Ranariddh, Royal Player in Cambodian Politics, Dies at 77
abstract: He rode a wave of royalist sentiment to win a United Nations-sponsored election in 1993, but was later ousted in a power struggle with his co-prime minister.

name: Claude Humphrey
profession: Pillar of N.F.L. Falcons Grits Blitz
headline: Claude Humphrey, Pillar of N.F.L. Falcons’ ‘Grits Blitz,’ Dies at 77
abstract: He was belatedly inducted into the Hall of Fame, having played before sacks were an official statistic. He ended his career with a Super Bowl team, the Eagles.

name: Hyun Sook Han
profession: Korean Social Worker and Adoption Pioneer
headline: Hyun Sook Han, Korean Social Worker and Adoption Pioneer, Dies at 83
abstract: Over three decades, she placed thousands of Korean orphans with families in the Midwest and made sure the children never forgot their heritage.

name: Fred Hiatt
headline: Fred Hiatt, Washington Post Editorial Page Editor, Dies at 66
abstract: He used his powerful platform to champion human rights, caution against a Trump presidency and condemn the killing of a Saudi columnist for the paper.

name: Marie-Claire Blais
headline: Marie-Claire Blais, Acclaimed French Canadian Novelist, Dies at 82
abstract: Though largely unknown outside Canada, she was often ranked alongside Margaret Atwood and Alice Munro as one of the country’s greatest living writers.

name: Justo Gallego
headline: Justo Gallego, Who Built a Cathedral, Brick by Brick, Dies at 96
abstract: A former monk, he spent decades constructing a grand edifice as an act of faith and devotion, and did so almost single-handedly.

name: Greg Tate
headline: Greg Tate, Influential Black Cultural Critic, Dies at 64
abstract: His writing for The Village Voice and other publications helped elevate hip-hop and street art to the same planes as jazz and Abstract Expressionism.

name: Darlene Hard
profession: Strong-Willed Tennis Star Before Pro Era
headline: Darlene Hard, Strong-Willed Tennis Star Before Pro Era, Dies at 85
abstract: Hard, who was outspoken and independent minded, was the top-ranked American woman from 1960 to 1963.

name: Lina Wertmüller
headline: Lina Wertmüller, Italian Director of Provocative Films, Dies at 93
abstract: She established an idiosyncratic reputation for blending tragedy, farce, politics and sex. She was the first woman nominated for a best director Oscar.

name: Denis O’Brien
headline: Denis O’Brien, Force in Ex-Beatle’s Film Company, Dies at 80
abstract: He and George Harrison created Handmade Films to make “Monty Python’s Life of Brian.” Other successes followed, but the partnership ended badly.

name: William Hartmann
headline: William Hartmann, 63, Michigan Official Who Disputed Election, Dies
abstract: He refused to certify Joseph Biden’s victory over Donald Trump in Detroit but later relented. A foe of Covid vaccines, he was hospitalized with the virus.

name: Ernesta Procope
headline: Ernesta Procope, Pioneering Black Insurance Broker, Dies at 98
abstract: She broke ground in the business as a woman, too, and also in transplanting her firm from Brooklyn to Wall Street.

name: Barry Harris
profession: Pianist and Devoted Scholar of Bebop
headline: Barry Harris, Pianist and Devoted Scholar of Bebop, Dies at 91
abstract: For decades, he performed, taught and toured with unflagging devotion. He also helped to lay the foundation for the widespread academic study of jazz.

name: Robbie Shakespeare
headline: Robbie Shakespeare, Prolific Reggae Bassist, Is Dead at 68
abstract: As half of the duo Sly and Robbie, he performed or recorded with everyone from Peter Tosh and Grace Jones to Bob Dylan and Serge Gainsbourg.

name: Al Unser
headline: Al Unser, Four-Time Winner of the Indy 500, Dies at 82
abstract: He was part of one of auto racing’s most celebrated families, whose members won the Indianapolis 500 a combined nine times.

name: Michael Nesmith
headline: Michael Nesmith, the ‘Quiet Monkee,’ Is Dead at 78
abstract: He shot to fame as a member of a made-for-TV rock group, but he denied that he was the group’s only “real” musician. He went on to create some of the first music videos.

name: C. Herbert Oliver
headline: Rev. C. Herbert Oliver, Civil Rights Activist, Dies at 96
abstract: He helped focus the nation on bombings and police abuse in Alabama in the 1960s and, later, on problems with the education of Black students in Brooklyn.

name: Margaret Giannini
headline: Margaret Giannini, Champion of People With Disabilities, Dies at 100
abstract: After meeting the parents of children with a range of disabilities, she decided almost on the spot to start a clinic to treat such children exclusively.

name: Anne Rice
headline: Anne Rice, Who Spun Gothic Tales of Vampires, Dies at 80
abstract: She wrote more than 30 novels, including the best seller “Interview With the Vampire,” which became a hit movie starring Tom Cruise and Brad Pitt.

name: Robert Farris Thompson
headline: Robert Farris Thompson, ‘Guerrilla Scholar’ of African Art, Dies at 88
abstract: He revolutionized the study of the cultures of Africa and the Americas by combining art history with anthropology, sociology and ethnomusicology.

name: Mikio Shinagawa
headline: Mikio Shinagawa, Who Ran a Fashionable SoHo Haunt, Dies at 66
abstract: His earthy Japanese restaurant, Omen, became a downtown canteen for well-known patrons like Patti Smith, Yoko Ono and Richard Gere.

name: Marjorie Tallchief
headline: Marjorie Tallchief, Acclaimed Ballerina, Is Dead at 95
abstract: A versatile artist who performed with the Paris Opera Ballet, she was the younger sister of the famed dancer Maria Tallchief.

name: Vicente Fernández
profession: El Rey of Mexican Ranchera Music
headline: Vicente Fernández, ‘El Rey’ of Mexican Ranchera Music, Is Dead at 81
