abstract: A beloved Mexican singer, Mr. Fernández was known for his powerful operatic range and marathon performances, delivered in a signature charro outfit and intricately embroidered sombrero.

name: Suzette Winter
headline: Suzette Winter, Who Documented Hollywood’s Golden Age, Dies at 90
abstract: She and her husband produced more than 30 rosy biographical films for television about the era’s biggest stars.

name: Masayuki Uemura
headline: Masayuki Uemura, 78, Dies; Designed the First Nintendo Console
abstract: He developed the Nintendo Entertainment System in the 1980s, which laid the foundation for today’s enormous video game console market and franchises like Super Mario Brothers.

name: Humphrey Davies
headline: Humphrey Davies, Noted Translator of Arabic Literature, Dies at 74
abstract: He introduced numerous novels, including works by the Nobel laureate Naguib Mahfouz, to English language readers.

name: Nai-Ni Chen
headline: Nai-Ni Chen, Whose Dances Merged East and West, Dies at 62
abstract: Ms. Chen, who founded the Nai-Ni Chen Dance Company in 1988, died while swimming in Hawaii, where she was vacationing.

name: Charles R. Morris
headline: Charles R. Morris, Iconoclastic Author on Economics, Dies at 82
abstract: Resisting ideological labels, experienced in government and banking, he critiqued policymakers’ “good intentions” and the costs of health care and forecast the 2008 financial crisis.

name: Linda McAlister
profession: Philosopher and Founder of Feminist Journal
headline: Linda McAlister, Philosopher and Founder of Feminist Journal, Dies at 82
abstract: She was among a collective of philosophy professors who started Hypatia, the first major scholarly publication to view the discipline from a feminist lens.

name: Michael Gargiulo
headline: Michael Gargiulo Dies at 95; Documented the Moscow ‘Kitchen Debate’
abstract: Sent to the Soviet Union in 1959 to promote color television, he ended up taping what he later called a “turning point” in U.S.-Soviet relations.

name: Shirley McBay
headline: Shirley McBay, Pioneering Mathematician, Is Dead at 86
abstract: The first Black student to receive a doctorate from the University of Georgia, she devoted her life to advocating for diversity in science and math education.

name: Elfrida von Nardroff
profession: Won Big Money on a Fixed Quiz Show
headline: Elfrida von Nardroff, 96, Dies; Won Big Money on a Fixed Quiz Show
abstract: In 1958, she won more on “Twenty-One” than anyone else. But she became embroiled in a scandal that led to grand jury and congressional investigations.

name: Manuel Santana
headline: Manuel Santana, Influential Spanish Tennis Champion, Dies at 83
abstract: He won the French Open twice and captured the U.S. National Championships and Wimbledon, as well as winning at the 1968 Olympics.

name: bell hooks
headline: bell hooks, Pathbreaking Black Feminist, Dies at 69
abstract: She insisted that the fight for women’s rights had to take into account the diverse experiences of working-class and Black women.

name: Frances B. Johnston
headline: Overlooked No More: Frances B. Johnston, Photographer Who Defied Genteel Norms
abstract: Undaunted by obstacles facing her gender, she carved out a career taking portraits of celebrities and creating series on architecture and education.

name: Julius S. Scott
headline: Julius S. Scott, Influential Historian of the Caribbean, Dies at 66
abstract: In “The Common Wind,” he linked the Haitian Revolution to the spread of ideas by word of mouth as sailors and enslaved people navigated Atlantic commerce.

name: Ken Kragen
profession: Force Behind We Are the World
headline: Ken Kragen, a Force Behind ‘We Are the World,’ Dies at 85
abstract: Michael Jackson, Lionel Richie and Quincy Jones were among the public faces of that 1985 fund-raising record. But behind the scenes, Mr. Kragen made it all happen.

name: Donald Cozzens
headline: Donald Cozzens, Priest Who Pressed Church From Within, Dies at 82
abstract: He challenged the Roman Catholic Church on the culture of secrecy and denial that protected predator priests, and said celibacy should be optional.

name: Oriol Bohigas
headline: Oriol Bohigas, Architect Who Helped Transform Barcelona, Dies at 95
abstract: He was a mastermind of the city’s overhaul in preparation for the 1992 Summer Olympics, which helped turn it into a major tourist destination.

name: Allan Rechtschaffen
headline: Allan Rechtschaffen, Eminent Sleep Researcher, Dies at 93
abstract: He studied sleep deprivation, dreams, narcolepsy and insomnia. But he was puzzled by the ultimate question: Why do we sleep?

name: Rosalie Trombley
headline: Rosalie Trombley, Who Picked Hits and Made Stars, Dies at 82
abstract: As music director for CKLW, a major radio station in the Detroit market, she furthered the careers of Alice Cooper, Bob Seger, the Temptations and many others.

name: Shirley Zussman
headline: Shirley Zussman, Indefatigable Sex Therapist, Is Dead at 107
abstract: After she and her husband attended a Masters and Johnson lecture in 1966, they joined the burgeoning field of sexology. She remained active well into the 21st century.

name: Henry Orenstein
profession: Force Behind Transformers and Poker on TV
headline: Henry Orenstein, 98, Dies; Force Behind Transformers and Poker on TV
abstract: A Holocaust survivor, he started a successful toy company in the 1950s and later invented a method of showing poker players’ hole cards on televised tournaments.

name: Richard Rogers
headline: Richard Rogers, Architect Behind Landmark Pompidou Center, Dies at 88
abstract: A Pritzker Prize winner, he altered the skylines of Paris and London with colorful and striking designs that turned architecture not just inside out but also on its head.

name: Kangol Kid
headline: Kangol Kid, Early Rapper Who Sought ‘Roxanne,’ Dies at 55
abstract: As a member of the group UTFO, he was heard on one of the most influential and widely imitated songs of commercial hip-hop’s early years.

name: Johnny Isakson
headline: Johnny Isakson, 76, Longtime Senator From Georgia, Is Dead
abstract: He succeeded Newt Gingrich in the House. As a Republican U.S. senator, he was known for championing bipartisan cooperation.

name: Lucía Hiriart
headline: Lucía Hiriart, Powerful Wife of Chile’s Dictator, Dies at 98
abstract: Her husband, Augusto Pinochet, acknowledged that she had pushed him to participate in the 1973 coup that brought him to power in 1973.

name: Eve Babitz
headline: Eve Babitz, a Hedonist With a Notebook, Is Dead at 78
abstract: A child of Hollywood, she wrote of the sensuous pleasures of Los Angeles, and sampled them enthusiastically.

name: Carlos Marín
headline: Carlos Marín, of the Multinational Quartet Il Divo, Dies at 53
abstract: A Spanish baritone, he joined singers from France, Switzerland and the U.S. to become worldwide stars of the genre sometimes called popera.

name: Roman Kaplan
profession: Restaurateur and Host for Soviet Exiles
headline: Roman Kaplan, Restaurateur and Host for Soviet Exiles, Dies at 83
abstract: The Russian Samovar in Manhattan became a hub for artists and writers far from home, drawing eminent regulars like Joseph Brodsky and Mikhail Baryshnikov.

name: Alexander Garvin
headline: Alexander Garvin, Who Reimagined Ground Zero, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Architect, author, Yale academic and City Hall planner, he directed the rebuilding of the World Trade Center site and helped plan a New York City Olympics.

name: Darby Penney
headline: Darby Penney, Who Crusaded for Better Psychiatric Care, Dies at 68
abstract: She shed light on marginalized people’s lives by examining the contents of suitcases left in the attic of a psychiatric hospital. She went on to become a prominent activist.

name: Sally Ann Howes
profession: Star of Chitty Chitty Bang Bang
headline: Sally Ann Howes, Star of ‘Chitty Chitty Bang Bang,’ Dies at 91
abstract: The English-born actress captivated children in the 1968 film, which became a holiday favorite. It was one of around 140 productions she appeared in during a six-decade career.

name: Anne Emerman
headline: Anne Emerman, Champion of Disability Rights, Dies at 84
abstract: Insisting that buildings be wheelchair accessible, she never backed down, not even to Mother Teresa. She also founded a musical group called Disabled in Action.

name: Carlos Tejada
profession: Deputy Asia Editor for The Times
headline: Carlos Tejada, Deputy Asia Editor for The Times, Dies at 49
abstract: He was an editor in Asia for 13 years, including with The Wall Street Journal. One colleague said he had embodied the phrase, “Edit ferociously and with joy.”

name: Frederick Baldwin
headline: Frederick Baldwin, Whose Photography Told Stories, Dies at 92
abstract: He saw the camera as “a passport to the world” that helped him document nature, the civil rights movement and life in rural America.

name: Steve Bronski
headline: Steve Bronski, of the Pioneering Gay Band Bronski Beat, Dies at 61
abstract: He was part of a British trio whose songs often directly addressed gay themes and issues in a way few other pop music acts were doing.

name: Thomas Kinsella
headline: Thomas Kinsella, Evocative, and Debated, Irish Poet, Dies at 93
abstract: His work — difficult and often contentious — was likened to the prose of James Joyce for its sense of place. He was also a translator of ancient texts, including the Tain Bo Cuailnge.

name: Franklin A. Thomas
headline: Franklin A. Thomas, Pathbreaking Ford Foundation President, Dies at 87
abstract: He rose from working-class Brooklyn to become the first Black person to run a major American philanthropy, and he revitalized it, shifting its focus to poverty and education.

name: Joan Didion
headline: Joan Didion, ‘New Journalist’ Who Explored Culture and Chaos, Dies at 87
abstract: She established a distinctive voice in American fiction before turning to political reporting and screenplay writing. But it was California, her native state, that provided her with her richest material.

name: H. Jackson Brown Jr.
headline: H. Jackson Brown Jr., Best-Selling Giver of Fatherly Advice, Dies at 81
abstract: His “Life’s Little Instruction Book,” which counseled “take someone bowling” and “believe in love at first sight,” has sold over seven million copies.

name: Grace Mirabella
headline: Grace Mirabella, Who Brought Vogue Down to Earth, Dies at 92
abstract: In her 17 years at the helm of the fashion magazine, she took a more practical-minded approach, in line with a rise in women’s participation in the work force.

name: Dave Draper
headline: Dave Draper, Bodybuilding’s ‘Blond Bomber,’ Dies at 79
abstract: After being named Mr. America, Mr. Universe and Mr. World, he left competitive bodybuilding in 1970. But he kept lifting weights until a year before he died.

name: Robert H. Grubbs
profession: His Chemistry Breakthrough Led to a Nobel
headline: Robert H. Grubbs, 79, Dies; His Chemistry Breakthrough Led to a Nobel
abstract: He helped perfect the manufacturing of compounds that are now used to make everything from plastics to pharmaceuticals, marking an advance in “green chemistry.”

name: James F. Fries
profession: Studied the Good Life and How to Live It
headline: James F. Fries, Who Studied the Good Life and How to Live It, Dies at 83
abstract: He showed that while a healthy lifestyle won’t help us live much longer, it can stave off chronic disease and disability until our final years.

name: Edward D. Shames
profession: Last Living Band of Brothers Officer
headline: Edward D. Shames, Last Living ‘Band of Brothers’ Officer, Dies at 99
abstract: His company’s exploits in World War II were recounted in a best-selling book and later in an HBO mini-series.

name: Gordon Carey
profession: Force in the Civil Rights Movement
headline: Gordon Carey, a Force in the Civil Rights Movement, Dies at 89
abstract: An “unsung hero” of the era, he played important roles in two of its far-reaching events: the 1960 lunch-counter sit-ins and the 1961 Freedom Rides.

name: Wanda Young
headline: Wanda Young, Motown Hitmaker With the Marvelettes, Dies at 78
abstract: She was the lead voice on “Don’t Mess With Bill” and other songs written by Smokey Robinson, who said she “had this little voice that was sexy to me.”

name: Desmond Tutu
headline: Desmond Tutu, Whose Voice Helped Slay Apartheid, Dies at 90
abstract: The archbishop, a powerful force for nonviolence in South Africa’s anti-apartheid movement, was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1984.

name: Wayne Thiebaud
headline: Wayne Thiebaud, Playful Painter of the Everyday, Dies at 101
abstract: Mr. Thiebaud’s rich and luminous depictions of midcentury Americana separated him from the classic Pop Art of the time.

name: Jean-Marc Vallée
headline: Jean-Marc Vallée, Director of ‘Dallas Buyers Club,’ Dies at 58
abstract: Known for his naturalistic approach, the Canadian-born filmmaker transformed true stories into acclaimed dramas.

name: E.O. Wilson
headline: E.O. Wilson, a Pioneer of Evolutionary Biology, Dies at 92
abstract: A Harvard professor for 46 years, he was an expert on insects and explored how natural selection and other forces could influence animal behavior. He then applied his research to humans.

name: Jonathan Spence
headline: Jonathan Spence, Noted China Scholar, Dies at 85
abstract: His classes at Yale and well-regarded books explored China’s vast history through details that illuminated bigger pictures and themes.

name: Donald H. Elliott
headline: Donald H. Elliott, Innovative Urban Planner, Dies at 89
abstract: He preserved landmarks in New York through creative zoning, involved communities in decision-making and insisted on aesthetic standards for urban design.

name: Sarah Weddington
headline: Sarah Weddington, Who Successfully Argued Roe v. Wade, Dies at 76
abstract: She went before the U.S. Supreme Court at 26 with almost no legal experience and won one of the most consequential cases in American history.

name: J.D. Crowe
headline: J.D. Crowe, Banjo Virtuoso and Bluegrass Innovator, Dies at 84
abstract: Drawing on rock and R&B, Mr. Crowe recast the sound of bluegrass while helping launch the careers of some of the genre’s biggest stars.

name: Neil Marcus
headline: Neil Marcus, Whose Art Illuminated Disability, Dies at 67
abstract: A playwright and actor, he saw his life as performance art. He was best known for his play “Storm Reading.”

name: Thomas Lovejoy
headline: Thomas Lovejoy, Wide-Ranging Ecologist and Amazon Rescuer, Dies at 80
abstract: His ambitious, long-running project in Brazil explored the impact of deforestation on animals and plants — and how to deal with it.

name: John Madden
profession: Face and Voice of the N.F.L. on the Field and in the Broadcast Booth
headline: John Madden, Face and Voice of the N.F.L. on the Field and in the Broadcast Booth, Dies at 85
abstract: Mr. Madden coached the Oakland Raiders to a Super Bowl title before becoming one of football’s best-known broadcasters and a video game entrepreneur.

name: Harry M. Reid
profession: Senate Majority Leader Behind Landmark Democratic Victories
headline: Harry M. Reid, Senate Majority Leader Behind Landmark Democratic Victories, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Reid, who was from Nevada, displayed his pugilistic instincts as he steered an economic stimulus package and the Affordable Care Act to passage.

name: Keri Hulme
profession: New Zealands First Booker Prize Winner
headline: Keri Hulme, New Zealand’s First Booker Prize Winner, Dies at 74
abstract: The power Ms. Hulme drew from her Maori heritage shone through in her work, especially in “The Bone People,” which won the literary prize in 1985.

name: Beverly Russell
headline: Beverly Russell, Who Ran Design Magazines With Flair, Dies at 87
abstract: In the 1980s, she used her position as editor in chief of the trade magazine Interiors to advocate for women in media, design and architecture.

name: Lee Kaufman
profession: Cleaned Her Way to Late-Life Stardom
headline: Lee Kaufman, Who Cleaned Her Way to Late-Life Stardom, Dies at 99
abstract: When she and her husband, Morty, were featured in advertising spots for Swiffer products in their 90s, the public embraced them.

name: David Wagoner
headline: David Wagoner, Prolific Poet of the Northwest, Is Dead at 95
abstract: He found his subjects in nature, his childhood and many other realms. He also wrote novels full of lively dialogue.

name: Ben McFall
headline: Ben McFall, ‘the Heart of the Strand,’ Is Dead at 73
abstract: He was the longest-tenured bookseller in the history of New York’s most storied bookstore, and he perpetuated its bohemian character.

name: Karen Ferguson
headline: Karen Ferguson, Fighter for Pension Rights, Dies at 80
abstract: She started as one of Ralph Nader’s “Nader Raiders” and, after developing an expertise in retirement systems, became a leading advocate for workers’ rights.

name: Asma Khader
profession: Fighter for Womens Rights in Jordan
headline: Asma Khader, Fighter for Women’s Rights in Jordan, Dies at 69
abstract: A respected lawyer, she focused on the victims of domestic violence and also worked hard to change discriminatory laws.

name: Sam Jones
headline: Sam Jones, Sharpshooting Celtics Star of the 1960s, Dies at 88
abstract: A member of the Basketball Hall of Fame, he was named one of the 50 greatest players in N.B.A. history and played on 10 N.B.A. championship teams.

name: Betty White
headline: Betty White, a TV Fixture for Seven Decades, Is Dead at 99
abstract: Among the many highlights of a career that began in 1949 were star turns on “The Mary Tyler Moore Show” in the 1970s and “Saturday Night Live” in 2010.

name: Dan Reeves
headline: Dan Reeves, Coach Who Reached (but Lost) Four Super Bowls, Dies at 77
abstract: After years as a player and coach with the Dallas Cowboys, he went on to great success in Denver and Atlanta. He also coached the Giants, but less successfully.

name: James Cayne
headline: James Cayne, Who Ran the Ill-Fated Bear Stearns, Dies at 87
abstract: The first Wall Street chief to own a company stake worth more than $1 billion, he steered the company to five years of record profits before it suffered huge losses in 2007.

name: Richard Leakey
headline: Richard Leakey, Kenyan Fossil Hunter and Conservationist, Dies at 77
abstract: His discoveries of ancient human skulls and skeletons, including the famed “Turkana Boy,” helped cement Africa’s standing as the cradle of humanity.

name: April Ashley
headline: April Ashley, London Socialite and Transgender Pioneer, Dies at 86
abstract: She modeled for Vogue, partied with John Lennon and Mick Jagger, and married into minor nobility, all while fighting for legal recognition of her gender.

name: Sabine Weiss
profession: Last of the Humanist Street Photographers
headline: Sabine Weiss, Last of the ‘Humanist’ Street Photographers, Dies at 97
abstract: Like Robert Doisneau and Brassaï, she shot life in postwar Paris as it really was. But she also won fame for her reporting and fashion work.

name: Kathy Flores
headline: Kathy Flores, Pathbreaking Women’s Rugby Coach, Dies at 66
abstract: She was a gifted player and exacting coach who pushed for recognition of women in a historically male-dominated sport.

name: Lisa Brodyaga
headline: Lisa Brodyaga, Crusading Lawyer for Immigrants’ Rights, Dies at 81
abstract: She became a folk hero representing asylum seekers fleeing violence in Central America, setting up shop in the Rio Grande Valley and building a refuge camp.

name: Billy Turner
profession: Trainer of a Triple Crown Winner
headline: Billy Turner, Trainer of a Triple Crown Winner, Dies at 81
abstract: In 1977, under his guidance, Seattle Slew became only the 10th thoroughbred in history to win the Kentucky Derby, Preakness Stakes and Belmont Stakes.

name: Ronald Weinstein
headline: Dr. Ronald Weinstein, Telepathology Pioneer, Dies at 83
abstract: Decades ago, he demonstrated that cancer could be diagnosed remotely. It was a pivotal step in the evolution of telemedicine.

name: William M. Ellinghaus
headline: William M. Ellinghaus Dies at 99; Presided Over AT&T Breakup
abstract: He led the communications giant when it settled an antitrust suit in the 1980s, not long after he helped save New York City in the fiscal crisis of the ’70s.

name: Mary Alice Thatch
headline: Mary Alice Thatch, Publisher Who Won Pardon for the Wilmington 10, Dies at 78
abstract: At the helm of The Wilmington Journal, she pushed to cover issues affecting the Black community that had been ignored by the mainstream press.

name: Peter Bogdanovich
headline: Peter Bogdanovich, 82, Director Whose Career Was a Hollywood Drama, Dies
abstract: Within one decade, the ’70s, he was transformed from one of the most celebrated of filmmakers, notably for “The Last Picture Show,” into one of the most ostracized.

name: Judith Davidoff
headline: Judith Davidoff, Master of Long-Dormant Instruments, Dies at 94
abstract: A master of the viola da gamba and other stringed instruments, she was a central part of the early-music scene.

name: Harry Colomby
headline: Harry Colomby, Teacher Who Aided a Jazz Great’s Career, Dies at 92
abstract: A chance encounter with Thelonious Monk led to a 14-year stint as his manager. After seeing a young Michael Keaton at a stand-up club, he became his manager, too.

name: Sidney Poitier
profession: Paved the Way for Black Actors in Film
headline: Sidney Poitier, Who Paved the Way for Black Actors in Film, Dies at 94
abstract: The first Black performer to win the Academy Award for best actor, for “Lilies of the Field,” he once said he felt “as if I were representing 15, 18 million people with every move I made.”

name: Theresa Hak Kyung Cha
headline: Overlooked No More: Theresa Hak Kyung Cha, Artist and Author Who Explored Identity
abstract: She was murdered after the publication of her first novel, “Dictee,” a challenging exploration of Korean history and immigrant life that inspires Asian American writers today.

name: Grichka Bogdanoff
headline: Grichka and Igor Bogdanoff, Twins in an Uneasy Spotlight, Die at 72
abstract: In France they were science-loving TV celebrities (molded by plastic surgery) whose own research was suspect, maybe a hoax. They died within days of each other.

name: Igor Bogdanoff
headline: Grichka and Igor Bogdanoff, Twins in an Uneasy Spotlight, Die at 72
abstract: In France they were science-loving TV celebrities (molded by plastic surgery) whose own research was suspect, maybe a hoax. They died within days of each other.

name: F. Sionil Jose
headline: F. Sionil Jose, 97, Novelist Who Saw Heroism in Ordinary Filipinos, Dies
abstract: Mr. Jose’s writing, rich in themes drawn from his rural upbringing, amounted to a continuing morality play about poverty and class divisions in the Philippines.

name: Lani Guinier
profession: Legal Scholar at the Center of Controversy
headline: Lani Guinier, Legal Scholar at the Center of Controversy, Dies at 71
abstract: President Bill Clinton pulled her nomination as assistant attorney general in 1993 after she came under criticism for her views on voting rights.

name: Dan Reilly
headline: Dan Reilly, the Original Mr. Met, Is Dead at 83
abstract: For four seasons — at Shea Stadium, when the Mets were dreadful but beloved, he donned a giant head and roamed the stands greeting fans as the team’s mascot.

name: Marilyn Bergman
profession: Half of an Oscar-Winning Songwriting Duo
headline: Marilyn Bergman, Half of an Oscar-Winning Songwriting Duo, Dies at 93
abstract: With her husband, Alan, she wrote the lyrics to “The Way We Were” and “The Windmills of Your Mind,” as well as a number of memorable TV themes.

name: Robert Birnbaum
headline: Robert Birnbaum, Architect of Modern-Day Financial Markets, Dies at 94
abstract: He was renowned for his steady hand during the 1987 stock market crash. He later helped design circuit breakers to calm future panics.

name: Max Julien
profession: Star of a Cult Blaxploitation Film
headline: Max Julien, Star of a Cult Blaxploitation Film, Dies at 88
abstract: Black audiences flocked to see him in “The Mack,” and generations of cinephiles have paid homage to his star turn, his smooth delivery and his extraordinary costumes.

name: Stephen Lawrence
headline: Stephen Lawrence, Whose Music Enriched ‘Sesame Street,’ Dies at 82
abstract: He composed the title song of the landmark album “Free to Be … You and Me.” He then moved on to Big Bird and friends.

name: Dwayne Hickman
headline: Dwayne Hickman, TV’s Lovelorn Dobie Gillis, Is Dead at 87
abstract: He went on to appear in movies and other TV shows and to work as a television executive, but the role of Dobie would dog him for decades.

name: Bob Saget
headline: Bob Saget, Comic Who Starred in the Sitcom ‘Full House,’ Dies at 65
abstract: The actor, who had also hosted “America’s Funniest Home Videos,” was found dead in an Orlando hotel room while on tour.

name: Robert Durst
profession: Real Estate Scion Convicted as a Killer
headline: Robert Durst, Real Estate Scion Convicted as a Killer, Dies at 78
abstract: He was a suspect in three lurid murders and became a fugitive. In September, he was found guilty in the fatal shooting of a confidante and sentenced to life in prison.

name: Don Maynard
profession: Hall of Fame Receiver for Champion Jets
headline: Don Maynard, Hall of Fame Receiver for Champion Jets, Dies at 86
abstract: He teamed with the quarterback Joe Namath in a passing attack that took New York to an upset victory in Super Bowl III against the powerful Colts.

name: Carl Bennett
headline: Carl Bennett, Founder of Caldor Discount Stores, Dies at 101
abstract: He and his wife, Dorothy, turned a walk-up store in Westchester, N.Y., into a 100-outlet behemoth that reached $1 billion in annual sales.

name: Chris Dickerson
headline: Chris Dickerson, Who Broke Bodybuilding Barriers, Dies at 82
abstract: Nicknamed “Diamond Calves,” he was the first Black man to win the Mr. America contest. As a gay man, he said, he also felt bigotry over his sexual orientation.

name: David Sassoli
headline: David Sassoli, President of the European Parliament, Dies at 65
abstract: He was a well-known journalist in his native Italy before going into politics, and devoted his tenure to making the Parliament more prominent.

name: Michael Lang
headline: Michael Lang, a Force Behind the Woodstock Festival, Dies at 77
abstract: He and his partners hoped their weekend of “peace and music” would draw 50,000 attendees. It ended up drawing more than 400,000 — and making history.

name: Shirley McGreal
headline: Shirley McGreal, Champion of Primates Under Threat, Dies at 87
abstract: She exposed smuggling rings and research laboratories and built a sanctuary for gibbons in South Carolina.

name: Bob Falkenburg
profession: Tennis Hall of Famer Turned Entrepreneur
headline: Bob Falkenburg, Tennis Hall of Famer Turned Entrepreneur, Dies at 95
abstract: He won at Wimbledon in 1948 and took some doubles titles before decamping to Brazil and founding a fast-food chain.

name: James Mtume
profession: Juicy Fruit Became a Hip-Hop Beat
headline: James Mtume, Whose ‘Juicy Fruit’ Became a Hip-Hop Beat, Dies at 76
abstract: In a wide-ranging career, he went from playing percussion with Miles Davis to writing and producing sleek R&B to a long stint on political talk radio.

name: Bill Staines
headline: Bill Staines, Folk Music Mainstay, Dies at 74
abstract: Among his best-known songs were “River,” “The Roseville Fair” and a cross-generational classic, “A Place in the Choir.”

name: Dale Clevenger
headline: Dale Clevenger, Chicago Symphony’s Fearless Horn Master, Dies at 81
abstract: Mr. Clevenger, who played his notoriously treacherous instrument with daring, was an anchor of the Chicago orchestra’s famed brass section for 47 years.

name: Gerald Stern
headline: Gerald Stern, a Founding New York Judicial Watchdog, Dies at 86
abstract: He was the first head of a state commission that investigated misconduct by judges and meted out discipline in nearly 600 cases during his 29-year tenure.

name: Gerald Stern
headline: Gerald Stern, Poet of Wistfulness, Anger and Humor, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Stern, who drew on his own upbringing and the death of his sister, began writing late in life and earned the 1998 National Book Award, among other accolades.

name: Ronnie Spector
headline: Ronnie Spector, Who Brought Edge to Girl-Group Sound, Dies at 78
abstract: As a member of the Ronettes, she sang on the hits “Be My Baby” and “Baby, I Love You.”

name: Maria Ewing
headline: Maria Ewing, Dramatically Daring Opera Star, Dies at 71
abstract: She sought to incorporate acting techniques in her singing rather than settle for predictable staging. Uncertainty about her heritage inspired her daughter, the actress Rebecca Hall, to make the film “Passing.”

name: Beatrice Mintz
headline: Beatrice Mintz, Groundbreaking Cancer Researcher, Dies at 100
abstract: She found that nearby tissue could help tame tumor cells more gently than radiation or chemotherapy, paving the way for new therapies.

name: Clyde Bellecourt
profession: Founder of the American Indian Movement
headline: Clyde Bellecourt, a Founder of the American Indian Movement, Dies at 85
abstract: A leader of armed confrontations at Wounded Knee and in Washington, he later shifted his focus to education, jobs and cultural renewal.

name: Majid Al Futtaim
headline: Majid Al Futtaim, Who Helped Build Modern Dubai, Dies at 87
abstract: His real estate empire, including malls, grocery stores and luxury hotels, transformed the Persian Gulf city into a global tourism hub.

name: Eddie Basinski
profession: Played Both the Infield and the Fiddle
headline: Eddie Basinski, Who Played Both the Infield and the Fiddle, Dies at 99
abstract: Basinski, who spent time with the Dodgers and the Pirates, was a rare double threat: a major league ballplayer and a trained violinist.

name: Edward Kirkland
headline: Edward Kirkland, Who Helped Preserve Historic Chelsea, Dies at 96
abstract: He played a less public but powerful role in creating the High Line, Hudson River Park and landmark districts in the Manhattan neighborhood.

name: Ed Schoenfeld
headline: Ed Schoenfeld, Impresario of Chinese Cuisine, Dies at 72
abstract: He helped introduce New Yorkers to the breadth of Chinese regional food with a series of top-rated Manhattan restaurants in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: John Bowman
profession: Comedy Writer With a Knack for Crossing Over
headline: John Bowman, Comedy Writer With a Knack for Crossing Over, Dies at 64
abstract: A white writer who left a corporate job, he became known for working on series with Black stars like Keenen Ivory Wayans and Martin Lawrence.

name: Michael Parks
headline: Michael Parks, Reporter Who Rose to Lead The Los Angeles Times, Dies at 78
abstract: A Pulitzer winner, he covered the Vietnam War, the collapse of the Soviet Union and the end of apartheid in South Africa before running The Times’s newsroom.

name: Rosa Lee Hawkins
profession: Youngest Member of the Dixie Cups
headline: Rosa Lee Hawkins, Youngest Member of the Dixie Cups, Dies at 76
abstract: The singing group’s debut single, “Chapel of Love,” rose to the top of the charts in 1964, displacing the Beatles’ “Love Me Do.”

name: Terry Teachout
profession: Arts Critic With a Wide Range
headline: Terry Teachout, Arts Critic With a Wide Range, Is Dead at 65
abstract: He called himself a “well-informed amateur,” and he wrote about everything from bluegrass to ballet.

name: Paul Carter Harrison
headline: Paul Carter Harrison, Whose Ideas Shaped Black Theater, Dies at 85
abstract: In his essays and plays, he provided a framework that linked playwrights like August Wilson to African rituals and mythologies.

name: Joe B. Hall
headline: Joe B. Hall, Longtime Kentucky Men’s Basketball Coach, Dies at 93
abstract: Following Adolph Rupp, one of the greatest college coaches of all time, was a challenge. Hall rose to the occasion, taking the team to the Final Four three times.

name: Steve Jenkins
profession: His Childrens Books Brought Science to Life
headline: Steve Jenkins, 69, Dies; His Children’s Books Brought Science to Life
abstract: In plain language, he answered many burning questions: How do you catch a fly? What do animals do the day they’re born? How loud is a lion’s roar?

name: Dallas Frazier
headline: Dallas Frazier, Who Wrote Hits for Country Stars, Dies at 82
abstract: His songs included the novelty number “Alley Oop,” the Oak Ridge Boys’ hit “Elvira” and “Beneath Still Waters” for Emmylou Harris.

name: Ibrahim Boubacar Keita
headline: Ibrahim Boubacar Keita, Malian President Ousted in 2020, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Keita was elected in 2013 with a mandate to stem the country’s many crises. But during his tenure, they escalated.

name: Andrew Vachss
profession: Childrens Champion in Court and Novels
headline: Andrew Vachss, Children’s Champion in Court and Novels, Dies at 79
abstract: In hard-edged fiction and in the real-life courtrooms where he practiced law, he sought to shine a light on child sexual abuse.

name: Charles E. McGee
headline: Charles E. McGee, Honored Tuskegee Airman, Dies at 102
abstract: In three wars, he flew a total of 409 combat missions. “We shattered all the myths,” he said of the accomplishments of Black pilots in World War II.

name: Ralph Emery
headline: Ralph Emery, the Dick Clark of Country Music, Dies at 88
abstract: For six decades he promoted country performers on radio and television, earning a place in the Country Music Hall of Fame.

name: Ali Mitgutsch
headline: Ali Mitgutsch, Inventive Children’s Book Illustrator, Dies at 86
abstract: The father of a German genre called Wimmelbuch, he delighted readers with detailed, cartoonish tableaus crammed with jokes and anecdotes.

name: Yvette Mimieux
profession: Found Fame With The Time Machine
headline: Yvette Mimieux, Who Found Fame With ‘The Time Machine,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Playing fragile characters, she had success in the 1960s in “Where the Boys Are” and other movies before her acting career took a downturn.

name: André Leon Talley
headline: André Leon Talley, Editor and Fashion Industry Force, Dies at 73
abstract: Called “a creative genius,” he was the rare Black editor at the top of a field that was mostly white and notoriously elitist.

name: Laurel Cutler
headline: Laurel Cutler, a Power in Advertising’s Golden Age, Dies at 94
abstract: In her five decades on Madison Avenue, she cracked the glass ceiling at a time when women were rarely seen in the executive suite.

name: Gaspard Ulliel
profession: French Actor and Moon Knight Star
headline: Gaspard Ulliel, French Actor and ‘Moon Knight’ Star, Dies at 37
abstract: He gained fame as a young Hannibal Lecter and the designer Yves Saint Laurent. He died after a skiing accident weeks before he is to appear in a Disney+ series.

name: Ricardo Bofill
headline: Ricardo Bofill, Architect of Otherworldly Buildings, Dies at 82
abstract: His structures were so bold, they were the backdrops for TV shows and films, including “Westworld” and a “Hunger Games” movie. But they were also socially aware.

name: Sara McLanahan
headline: Sara McLanahan, Who Studied Single Motherhood, Dies at 81
abstract: A Princeton sociologist and a single mother herself, she brought her own experience to her wide body of scholarly work.

name: Hardy Kruger
headline: Hardy Kruger, German-Born Hollywood Star, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Escaping execution by the Nazis for “cowardice” as a soldier, he found success in films because he found ways to portray “the new, good German.”

name: Fred Parris
headline: Fred Parris, Creator of a Doo-Wop Classic, Is Dead at 85
abstract: His “In the Still of the Night” (originally “Nite”), recorded with his group the Five Satins, came to define a sort of dreamy 1950s nostalgia.

name: Everett Lee
profession: Broke Color Barriers on the Conductors Podium
headline: Everett Lee, Who Broke Color Barriers on the Conductor’s Podium, Dies at 105
abstract: He was known as the first Black conductor on Broadway and the first to conduct a white orchestra in the South. Mr. Lee went on to a successful career in Europe.

name: Deborah Nickerson
headline: Deborah Nickerson, Pioneering Genome Researcher, Dies at 67
abstract: Using the Human Genome Project as her guide, she helped find genes responsible for cardiovascular disease, autism and a rare disorder called Miller syndrome.

name: Lusia Harris
headline: Lusia Harris, ‘Queen of Basketball,’ Dies at 66
abstract: She was the only woman officially drafted by the N.B.A. and the first Black woman inducted into the Basketball Hall of Fame.

name: Elza Soares
profession: Pushed the Boundaries of Brazilian Music
headline: Elza Soares, 91, Who Pushed the Boundaries of Brazilian Music, Dies
abstract: She rose from a favela in Rio to samba stardom in the 1960s. But her career was later overshadowed by an affair with a famous soccer player that became a national scandal.

name: Meat Loaf
profession: Bat Out of Hell Singer and Actor
headline: Meat Loaf, ‘Bat Out of Hell’ Singer and Actor, Dies at 74
abstract: Born Marvin Lee Aday, he sold millions of albums, won a Grammy and acted in films including “The Rocky Horror Picture Show” and “Fight Club.”

name: Louie Anderson
headline: Louie Anderson, Genial Stand-Up Comic and Actor, Dies at 68
abstract: He won an Emmy Award for his work on the series “Baskets” and two Daytime Emmys for his animated children’s show, “Life With Louie.”

name: Ann Arensberg
profession: Insightful Novelist of Mysteries and Manners
headline: Ann Arensberg, Insightful Novelist of Mysteries and Manners, Dies at 84
abstract: Her debut novel, “Sister Wolf,” won a 1981 National Book Award. Her later books explored the Manhattan theater scene and the New England occult.

name: Lee Godie
headline: Overlooked No More: Lee Godie, Eccentric Chicago Street Artist
abstract: A self-described Impressionist, she hawked her art on Michigan Avenue in the 1970s and ’80s and lived mostly outdoors. But her work is in museums.

name: Bob Goalby
profession: Masters Champion Thanks to a Gaffe
headline: Bob Goalby, Masters Champion Thanks to a Gaffe, Dies at 92
abstract: He won at Augusta in 1968 after Robert De Vincenzo signed an incorrect scorecard. But to many, the victory was tainted, leaving Goalby feeling like the victim.

name: Thich Nhat Hanh
headline: Thich Nhat Hanh, Monk, Zen Master and Activist, Dies at 95
abstract: A monk with global influence and an ally of Martin Luther King, he championed what he called “engaged Buddhism,” applying its principles in pressing for peace.

name: Anatoly Kvashnin
profession: Russian General in a Pivotal Era
headline: Anatoly Kvashnin, Russian General in a Pivotal Era, Dies at 75
abstract: His brutal campaign in Chechnya left a legacy of embittered civilians and vengeful leaders. But he was also part of a warming toward the West after the Soviet Union fell.

name: Harvey G. Stack
headline: Harvey G. Stack, Leading Dealer in Rare Coins, Dies at 93
abstract: At the New York firm his father and uncle started in 1933, he was said to have personally conducted more auction sales than anyone else in the industry.

name: Lisa Goddard
headline: Lisa Goddard, 55, Dies; Brought Climate Data to Those Who Needed It
abstract: She helped show government agencies around the world how to predict upcoming droughts, flooding and other extreme weather events.

name: Dan Einstein
headline: Dan Einstein, Champion of Singer-Songwriters, Is Dead at 61
abstract: He operated independent record labels for John Prine and Steve Goodman that took a critically praised (and award-winning) artist-driven approach.

name: Badal Roy
headline: Badal Roy, Who Fused Indian Rhythms With Jazz, Is Dead at 82
abstract: He collaborated across cultures, playing tabla with Miles Davis, Ornette Coleman, John McLaughlin and others in the jazz world and beyond, including Yoko Ono.

name: Nino Cerruti
headline: Nino Cerruti, Designer Who Revolutionized Men's Wear, Dies at 91
abstract: He loosened up men’s suits with unstructured tailoring and supple fabrics. He also dressed generations of movie stars, onscreen and off.

name: Dennis Smith
headline: Dennis Smith, Firefighter Who Wrote Best Sellers, Dies at 81
abstract: “Report From Engine Co. 82” was the first of his 16 books. He also started Firehouse magazine and was the founding chairman of the New York City Fire Museum.

name: Clark Gillies
profession: Rugged Star on Islanders Championship Teams
headline: Clark Gillies, 67, Rugged Star on Islanders’ Championship Teams, Dies
abstract: He was part of the Trio Grande, along with Bryan Trottier and Mike Bossy, on teams that won the Stanley Cup four years in a row.

name: Thierry Mugler
headline: Thierry Mugler, Genre-Busting French Fashion Designer, Dies at 73
abstract: The dominatrix-loving couturier turned sex into a style weapon.

name: James Maraniss
headline: James Maraniss, Librettist of Long-Silent Opera, Dies at 76
abstract: A Spanish scholar who taught for more than four decades at Amherst College, he waited, along with the composer, 32 years for “Life Is a Dream” to be staged.

name: Sheldon Silver
profession: New York Power Broker Convicted of Corruption
headline: Sheldon Silver, 77, New York Power Broker Convicted of Corruption, Dies
abstract: A Democratic leader of the State Assembly, he held sway in New York politics for decades and died while serving a prison sentence.

name: Steve Schapiro
headline: Steve Schapiro, Photojournalist Who Bore Witness, Dies at 87
abstract: He documented the civil rights movement and subjects as diverse as narcotics users, migrant workers and movie stars, seeking to capture their emotional heart.

name: Frank Dutton
headline: Frank Dutton, Detective Who Took On Apartheid Crimes, Dies at 72
abstract: A lauded South Africa police official, he dug into cold cases from the days of white rule. “The finest detective that this country has ever produced.”

name: Olavo de Carvalho
headline: Olavo de Carvalho, Bolsonaro’s Far-Right Guru, Dies at 74
abstract: He was the intellectual leader of Brazil’s far-right movement and a conspiracy theorist who mocked the pandemic. He died days after announcing he had Covid.

name: John Arrillaga Sr.
headline: John Arrillaga Sr., Who Helped Build Silicon Valley, Dies at 84
abstract: Starting in the 1960s, he developed the area’s farmland into office parks that housed fast-growing technology companies.

name: Jana Bennett
headline: Jana Bennett, Former Director of BBC Television, Dies at 66
abstract: An American-born executive who transformed the presentation of science on TV and was considered one of the most influential women in her industry.

name: Lucy Rowan Mann
profession: Doyenne of a Classical Music Prize
headline: Lucy Rowan Mann, Doyenne of a Classical Music Prize, Dies at 100
abstract: With her husband, the violinist Robert Mann, she mentored young classical musicians and administered the Naumburg Foundation’s storied annual awards.

name: Don Wilson
profession: Gave the Ventures Their Distinctive Rhythm
headline: Don Wilson, Who Gave the Ventures Their Distinctive Rhythm, Dies at 88
abstract: He was a founder, with Bob Bogle, of what has been called the best-selling and most influential instrumental band in rock ’n’ roll history.

name: Israel Dresner
profession: Civil Rights Champion and King Ally
headline: Rabbi Israel Dresner, Civil Rights Champion and King Ally, Dies at 92
abstract: He was jailed multiple times in the South during the 1960s and made human rights his lifelong cause, following the Jewish doctrine of “tikkun olam” — to repair the world.

name: Johan Hultin
headline: Johan Hultin, Who Found Frozen Clues to 1918 Virus, Dies at 97
abstract: His discovery in the 1950s of the remains of a victim of the pandemic, in Alaska, gave scientists the opportunity to map the virus’s genetic material.

name: Edgar S. Cahn
profession: Legal Reformer in Defense of the Poor
headline: Edgar S. Cahn, Legal Reformer in Defense of the Poor, Dies at 86
abstract: He and his wife came up with the idea for federally funded legal services, then went on to found the first public-interest law school.

name: Peter Robbins
headline: Peter Robbins, Original Voice of Charlie Brown, Dies at 65
abstract: Mr. Robbins, who first gave voice to the “Peanuts” character in a 1965 Christmas special, had struggled with mental illness and addiction in recent years.

name: Ron Goulart
headline: Ron Goulart, Who Spanned Genres in 180 Books, Dies at 89
abstract: He wrote science fiction, mystery, fantasy and romance novels, collaborated with William Shatner on the “TekWar” books and turned Groucho Marx into a private eye.

name: Jonathan Brown
headline: Jonathan Brown, Influential Historian of Spanish Art, Dies at 82
abstract: He played a crucial role in reinvigorating a neglected area of Western art history, bringing figures from the past to life.

name: Carol Speed
headline: Carol Speed, Vixen of the Blaxploitation Era, Dies at 76
abstract: In the mid-70s, thanks to two beloved B movies, she had a moment in the spotlight and enjoyed celebrity status in the Black press.

name: Beegie Adair
profession: Jazz Master in Country Musics Capital
headline: Beegie Adair, a Jazz Master in Country Music’s Capital, Dies at 84
abstract: In a city defined by honky-tonks and string ties, she had a 60-year career as a jazz pianist and a mainstay of the local scene.

name: Tito Matos
profession: Virtuoso of a Puerto Rican Sound
headline: Tito Matos, Virtuoso of a Puerto Rican Sound, Dies at 53
abstract: A lifelong champion of the plena genre, he helped rejuvenate it for a new generation both in Puerto Rico and in New York.

name: Esteban Torres
headline: Esteban Torres, Congressional Advocate for Latinos, Dies at 91
abstract: A California Democrat who for a time served as chairman of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, he dedicated himself to fighting poverty.

name: Phyllis Oakley
profession: Female Pioneer at the State Department
headline: Phyllis Oakley, Female Pioneer at the State Department, Dies at 87
abstract: She had to quit the foreign service to marry. But she was reinstated 16 years later, when female employees challenged the department’s sexist traditions, and she thrived.

name: Jeremiah Stamler
profession: Found Ways to Curb Heart Disease
headline: Jeremiah Stamler, Who Found Ways to Curb Heart Disease, Dies at 102
abstract: He was at the forefront of studies that found links between salt, diet and other risk factors and cardiovascular ailments.

name: Hargus Robbins
headline: Hargus Robbins, Pianist on Country Music Hits, Dies at 84
abstract: A revered member of Nashville’s A-Team of studio musicians, he was a major contributor to Bob Dylan’s “Blonde on Blonde” album.

name: Howard Hesseman
profession: D.J. Johnny Fever in WKRP in Cincinnati
headline: Howard Hesseman, 81, the D.J. Johnny Fever in ‘WKRP in Cincinnati,’ Dies
abstract: Mr. Hesseman played a fallen radio star who landed in the Midwest on the popular sitcom, which captured the misadventures of a struggling station.

name: John K. Singlaub
headline: John K. Singlaub, 100, General Who Clashed With Jimmy Carter, Dies
abstract: After a career in military intelligence, waging war in Europe, Korea and Vietnam, he was forced out of the U.S. Army. He then aided the contras in Nicaragua.

name: Alan A. Stone
profession: Challenged Psychiatrys Use in Public Policy
headline: Alan A. Stone, 92, Dies; Challenged Psychiatry’s Use in Public Policy
abstract: An iconoclastic thinker, he greatly influenced the evolution of psychiatric ethics, and guided the decision to take homosexuality off the list of mental disorders.

name: Donald Mahler
headline: Donald Mahler, Prolific Ballet Choreographer, Dies at 88
abstract: After dancing with the Metropolitan Opera Ballet and other companies, he became its director. He was also well known for his staging of works by Antony Tudor.

name: Mel Mermelstein
headline: Mel Mermelstein, Holocaust Survivor Who Sued Deniers, Dies at 95
abstract: He accused a revisionist history group of reneging on its promise to give a reward to anyone who could prove that the Nazis gassed Jews. He won his case.

name: Shintaro Ishihara
headline: Shintaro Ishihara, Outspoken Nationalist Governor of Tokyo, Dies at 89
abstract: An author as well as a politician, he was known for feuding with China over disputed islands and calling for Japan to assert itself against the United States.

name: Monica Vitti
headline: Monica Vitti, ‘Queen of Italian Cinema,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Both sensual and cerebral, she made her mark on the international scene in the 1960s, when visionary directors like Michelangelo Antonioni were remaking the cinema landscape.

name: Birju Maharaj
headline: Birju Maharaj, Virtuoso of Classical Indian Dance, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Maharaj choreographed for Bollywood, but was chiefly known for carrying the torch of Kathak, one of India’s major dance traditions.

name: John C. Koss
headline: John C. Koss, Stereo Headphone Innovator, Is Dead at 91
abstract: The sound “was just bouncing in my ears,” he said of his first experience with the earliest version of the headphones he helped invent in 1958.

name: Robin Herman
profession: Pried Open Doors in the N.H.L
headline: Robin Herman, Who Pried Open Doors in the N.H.L., Dies at 70
abstract: When hockey teams barred female reporters from men’s locker rooms, she pushed back, breaking through a barrier and campaigning successfully for equal access for women.

name: Janet Mead
headline: Janet Mead, Nun Whose Pop-Rock Hymn Reached the Top of the Charts, Dies
abstract: Her upbeat version of “The Lord’s Prayer” was an instant hit in Australia, reached No. 4 in the U.S. and was nominated for a Grammy (it lost to Elvis Presley).

name: Jean-Jacques Beineix
headline: Jean-Jacques Beineix, ‘Cinema du Look’ Director, Dies at 75
abstract: His first feature, “Diva,” a visually unusual tale, is credited with starting a new, style-focused genre of filmmaking in France.

name: Bill Fitch
headline: Bill Fitch, Who Coached Celtics to the ’81 Title, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Hailed for reviving sagging teams, he was voted one of the top 10 coaches in the N.B.A.’s first half century and was twice named coach of the year.

name: Arnie Kantrowitz
headline: Arnie Kantrowitz, Pioneer of Gay Liberation, Dies at 81
abstract: A professor, author and activist, he fought against discrimination because of sexual orientation and for fairness from the media.

name: Jason Epstein
headline: Jason Epstein, Editor and Publishing Innovator, Is Dead at 93
abstract: His literary and marketing instincts brought quality paperbacks to American readers and led to the creation of The New York Review of Books.

name: David Gordon
headline: David Gordon, a Wizard of Movement and Words, Dies at 85
abstract: For this choreographer, director and pioneer of postmodern dance, life was art and art was life.

name: Ora Washington
headline: Overlooked No More: Ora Washington, Star of Tennis and Basketball
abstract: She was dominant in both sports over two decades and was in all likelihood the first Black star in women’s sports in the United States.

name: James Bidgood
headline: James Bidgood, a Master of Gay Photography, Dies at 88
abstract: In addition to his elaborately staged images of gay fantasies, he made the film “Pink Narcissus,” a cult classic released anonymously in 1971.

name: Yale Kamisar
profession: Known as the Father of the Miranda Rule
headline: Yale Kamisar, Known as the ‘Father’ of the Miranda Rule, Dies at 92
abstract: His legal scholarship, cited in more than 30 Supreme Court cases, shaped modern criminal procedure, including protections for the rights of the accused.

name: Jon Zazula
headline: Jon Zazula, Early Promoter of Heavy Metal, Dies at 69
abstract: With his wife, Marsha, he founded Megaforce, a label that released the first albums of Metallica and others.

name: Todd Gitlin
profession: Voice and Critic of the New Left
headline: Todd Gitlin, a Voice and Critic of the New Left, Dies at 79
abstract: He earned his stripes in the antiwar movement of the 1960s. In his later years, he was often critical of his erstwhile kindred spirits.

name: Sam Lay
headline: Sam Lay, Drummer Who Backed Blues Greats and Bob Dylan, Dies at 86
abstract: His distinctive double-shuffle groove, which he likened to “three different drummers playing the same beat,” enlivened records by Howlin’ Wolf and many others.

name: Martine Colette
headline: Martine Colette, Who Rescued Exotic Animals, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Her wildlife sanctuary just outside Los Angeles was among the first of its kind and was supported by Hollywood luminaries.

name: Lata Mangeshkar
headline: Lata Mangeshkar, Bollywood’s Most Beloved Voice, Dies at 92
abstract: Ms. Mangeshkar, a revered figure in India, recorded songs for countless films — not appearing onscreen herself, but providing characters’ singing voices.

name: Charles Vert Willie
headline: Charles Vert Willie, 94, Dies; Studied, and Defended, Racial Diversity
abstract: He devised a plan to desegregate Boston’s public schools. He also stood up against sexism in the Episcopal Church.

name: John Vinocur
headline: John Vinocur, Foreign Correspondent and Editor, Dies at 81
abstract: After decades as a reporter for The A.P. and The Times, he became executive editor of The International Herald Tribune and a columnist on world affairs.

name: George Crumb
headline: George Crumb, Eclectic Composer Who Searched for Sounds, Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Crumb wrote startling works, sometimes with political themes, and challenged musicians to employ new techniques, vocalize and move about the stage.

name: Kenneth H. Brown
profession: Playwright Best Known for The Brig
headline: Kenneth H. Brown, Playwright Best Known for ‘The Brig,’ Dies at 85
abstract: He drew on his own experiences in the Marines to depict brutality within the corps, drawing acclaim Off Off Broadway.

name: Norma Waterson
profession: Key Figure in Britains Folk Revival
headline: Norma Waterson, a Key Figure in Britain’s Folk Revival, Dies at 82
abstract: With her familial singing group, the Watersons, and later as a solo performer, she helped revitalize traditional music from the north of England.

name: Greta Ferusic
profession: Survived Auschwitz and Siege of Sarajevo
headline: Greta Ferusic Dies at 97; Survived Auschwitz and Siege of Sarajevo
abstract: She was the only one in her family to survive the Holocaust, then endured the shelling of her city during the Bosnian war. A documentary chronicled her story.

name: Syl Johnson
profession: Soul Singer With a Cult Following
headline: Syl Johnson, Soul Singer With a Cult Following, Dies at 85
abstract: He released dozens of records on an array of labels across five decades, and his work was heavily sampled by rappers. He enjoyed a career revival in his 70s.

name: Jerome Chazen
profession: Original Partner in Liz Claiborne Empire
headline: Jerome Chazen, Original Partner in Liz Claiborne Empire, Dies at 94
abstract: One of a core group, he helped the company outfit a generation of working women, marketing its lines to department stores in the shopping-mall era.

name: Trude Feldman
headline: Trude Feldman, White House Reporter Who Got Access, Dies at 97
abstract: She was known to lob softballs in interviews, but she was tireless in getting face time with officials, including every president from Lyndon Johnson to George W. Bush.

name: Irwin Young
headline: Irwin Young, Patron of Independent Filmmakers, Is Dead at 94
abstract: As the head of a prominent film processing laboratory, he helped directors like Spike Lee, Michael Moore and Frederick Wiseman early in their careers.

name: Hans Neuenfels
profession: Opera Director With a Pointed View
headline: Hans Neuenfels, Opera Director With a Pointed View, Dies at 80
abstract: A leading proponent of “director’s theater,” he was known for productions with a provocative stamp that often provoked outrage.

name: Ashley Bryan
headline: Ashley Bryan, Who Brought Diversity to Children’s Books, Dies at 98
abstract: A prolific and eclectic artist, he filled his books with Black characters and injected rhythm into African folk tales.

name: John Rice Irwin
headline: John Rice Irwin, Guardian of Appalachia’s Past, Dies at 91
abstract: He created the nation’s premier museum of Appalachian history by conserving the log cabins and heirlooms of the mountain folk in his native region.

name: Jeremy Giambi
headline: Jeremy Giambi, Who Played for the Oakland Athletics, Dies at 47
abstract: Giambi, who also played with the Royals, the Phillies and the Red Sox, hit 52 home runs in his career. A cause of death was not given.

name: Gloria Rojas
headline: Gloria Rojas, Trailblazing Latina Broadcaster, Dies at 82
abstract: “I remember thinking,” she once said, “that if they hire another Hispanic, they’ll have to let me go, since who needs two?” She helped change that.

name: Luc Montagnier
headline: Luc Montagnier, Nobel-Winning Co-Discoverer of H.I.V., Dies at 89
abstract: He helped find the virus that causes AIDS, fell into a feud over it and later turned controversial, taking an anti-vaccine stance during the Covid-19 crisis.

name: Marie-Claire Chevalier
headline: Marie-Claire Chevalier, Catalyst for French Abortion Law, Dies at 66
abstract: While in high school in 1972, she was raped and became pregnant. Her illegal abortion paved the way for France to decriminalize the procedure in 1975.

name: Betty Davis
headline: Betty Davis, Raw Funk Innovator, Is Dead at 77
abstract: “Nasty Gal” and her two other 1970s albums influenced generations of R&B and hip-hop.

name: Patricia Moreno
headline: Patricia Moreno, Spiritual Fitness Leader, Dies at 57
abstract: Ms. Moreno’s intenSati program helped bring positive psychology into the exercise world.

name: John Wesley
headline: John Wesley, an Artist Who Couldn’t Be Pinned Down, Dies at 93
abstract: With his cartoonlike work that seemed to plumb the American subconscious, he was celebrated as a Pop artist, a surrealist, an eroticist and more.

name: Bob Wall
headline: Bob Wall, Martial Arts Master Who Sparred With Bruce Lee, Dies at 82
abstract: He taught thousands of senseis how to run a dojo, all the while trading kicks onscreen with Lee and Chuck Norris.

name: Richard Christiansen
headline: Richard Christiansen, Influential Chicago Theater Critic, Dies at 90
abstract: His reviews for The Chicago Tribune, and his encouragement of playwrights, directors and actors, helped make Chicago one of the country’s leading theater cities.

name: Douglas Trumbull
headline: Douglas Trumbull, Visual Effects Wizard, Dies at 79
abstract: His technical savvy was on display in films like “2001: A Space Odyssey,” “Star Trek: the Motion Picture,” “Close Encounters of the Third Kind” and “Blade Runner.”

name: Lars Eighner
headline: Lars Eighner, Who Wrote Eloquently of Being Homeless, Dies at 73
abstract: His 1993 memoir, “Travels With Lizbeth,” is considered a classic of the genre and brought him fame, but not fortune.

name: Julie Saul
headline: Julie Saul, Effervescent Manhattan Gallerist, Is Dead at 67
abstract: She promoted photographers like Sally Gall and Arne Svenson, and she later broadened her gallery’s scope to include multimedia artists like Maira Kalman and Roz Chast.

name: Stephanie Selby
headline: Stephanie Selby, 56, ‘A Very Young Dancer’ Who Inspired Many, Dies
abstract: A 1976 book of photographs and text traced her year at the School of American Ballet and made her famous. But a darker story lay underneath.

name: Sigal Barsade
headline: Sigal Barsade, 56, Dies; Argued That It’s OK to Show Emotions at Work
abstract: Her pioneering research showed that feelings have a place in the office, and that good leaders should learn to embrace that fact.

name: Carmen Herrera
headline: Carmen Herrera, Cuban-Born Artist Who Won Fame at 89, Dies at 106
abstract: She painted in obscurity for decades, living on the earnings of her husband, an English teacher. Everything changed with a gallery show in 2004.

name: Ivan Reitman
headline: Ivan Reitman, Director of ‘Ghostbusters,’ Is Dead at 75
abstract: He injected giant marshmallow boogeymen and toga parties into popular culture with movies that also included “National Lampoon’s Animal House” and “Stripes.”

name: Simcha Krauss
headline: Rabbi Simcha Krauss, Advocate for Women’s Rights, Dies at 84
abstract: He drew criticism for his efforts to liberate Orthodox women from recalcitrant husbands who refused to grant a religious divorce. But he stood his ground.

name: Ian McDonald
headline: Ian McDonald, of the Bands King Crimson and Foreigner, Dies at 75
abstract: As a multi-instrumentalist and songwriter with King Crimson, he helped propel the progressive rock movement. He found more commercial success with Foreigner.

name: Kathryn Kates
headline: Kathryn Kates, Actress of ‘Seinfeld’ Babka Fame, Dies at 73
abstract: She had a long screen career but may be best remembered as the counterwoman who tells Jerry and Elaine the bad news that her bakery was out of chocolate babkas.

name: P.J. O’Rourke
headline: P.J. O’Rourke, Conservative Political Satirist, Dies at 74
abstract: In articles, in best sellers and as a talk show regular he was a voice from the right skewering whatever in government or culture he thought needed it.

name: Beverly Ross
profession: Teenage Songwriter in Rock n Rolls Youth
headline: Beverly Ross, Teenage Songwriter in Rock ’n’ Roll’s Youth, Dies at 87
abstract: With hits like “Lollipop,” she became a top woman songwriter in the early 1960s, but she quit the business in frustration over the theft of her work.

name: Harriet S. Shapiro
headline: Harriet S. Shapiro, Groundbreaker in Solicitor General’s Office, Dies at 93
abstract: She was the office’s first female lawyer, and the quality of her written Supreme Court briefs made her a name in Washington legal circles.

name: Hugo Torres
headline: Hugo Torres, Former Rebel Turned Political Prisoner, Dies at 73
abstract: Once a guerrilla commander who helped free President Daniel Ortega of Nicaragua from prison, Mr. Torres was jailed last year during a political crackdown.

name: Walter Dellinger
profession: Scholar and Top Legal Aide Under Clinton
headline: Walter Dellinger, 80, Scholar and Top Legal Aide Under Clinton, Dies
abstract: He served as head of the Office of Legal Counsel and acting solicitor general and remained a leading figure in liberal legal battles.

name: Rosalie Kunoth-Monks
headline: Rosalie Kunoth-Monks, Champion of Indigenous Peoples, Dies at 85
abstract: As a teenager, she was the star of a film about an Aboriginal girl raised by a white family. As an adult, she fought discrimination in Australia against her people.

name: Leslie Parnas
headline: Leslie Parnas, Celebrated Cellist and Musical Diplomat, Dies at 90
abstract: His success at a competition in Moscow in 1962 earned him global renown and gave him a platform as a musical emissary.

name: Gail Halvorsen
headline: Gail Halvorsen, ‘Candy Bomber’ in Berlin Airlift, Dies at 101
abstract: Lieutenant Halvorsen came up with the idea to drop candies, chocolate and chewing gum for the children of West Berlin during a tense Cold War standoff.

name: Herbert Benson
headline: Dr. Herbert Benson, Who Saw the Mind as Medicinal, Dies at 86
abstract: A cardiologist and best-selling author, he was initially a skeptic before finding that a person can influence bodily health through meditation.

name: Martin Tolchin
profession: Times Reporter Was a Founder of The Hill
headline: Martin Tolchin, 93, Dies; Times Reporter Was a Founder of The Hill
abstract: He covered Congress in the 1970s and ’80s before heading up a successful Capitol Hill newspaper.

name: Sidney Miller
headline: Sidney Miller, Who Championed Black Music, Dies at 89
abstract: He founded the influential trade magazine Black Radio Exclusive and presented a popular annual conference that featured unknowns and superstars.

name: Valerie Boyd
headline: Valerie Boyd, Biographer of Zora Neale Hurston, Is Dead at 58
abstract: In addition to writing an acclaimed biography, she encouraged a generation of young writers, predominantly women of color, to pursue careers in nonfiction.

name: Art Cooley
profession: Founder of the Environmental Defense Fund
headline: Art Cooley, 87, a Founder of the Environmental Defense Fund, Dies
abstract: He was part of a small group of scientists and citizens on Long Island that was instrumental in banning the toxic pesticide DDT, first locally and then nationally.

name: Jim Hagedorn
headline: Jim Hagedorn, a Trump Ally in the House, Dies at 59
abstract: A two-term Minnesota conservative, he backed efforts to overturn the election of Joseph Biden as president on spurious grounds of voter fraud.

name: Mary Eliza Mahoney
headline: Overlooked No More: Mary Eliza Mahoney, Who Opened Doors in Nursing
abstract: As the first trained Black nurse in America, Mahoney devoted her life to creating opportunities in the profession for people of all races.

name: Peter Earnest
headline: Peter Earnest, C.I.A. Veteran Who Ran a Spy Museum, Dies at 88
abstract: He ran secret agents and later served as the agency’s spokesman. Both roles prepared him well for his role as the International Spy Museum’s first director.

name: Emile Francis
profession: Rebuilt N.H.L.s Rangers as Coach and G.M
headline: Emile Francis Dies at 95; Rebuilt N.H.L.’s Rangers as Coach and G.M.
abstract: Known as “the Cat” when he was a nimble goaltender, he went on to lead the team to a winning record and coached stars like Eddie Giacomin, Rod Gilbert and Brad Park.

name: Charley Taylor
profession: Running Back Turned Hall of Fame Receiver
headline: Charley Taylor, Running Back Turned Hall of Fame Receiver, Dies at 80
abstract: After changing positions, he became the most prolific receiver in N.F.L. history and helped make Washington a force in the league.

name: Jamal Edwards
headline: Jamal Edwards, Force in British Rap, Dies at 31
abstract: Edwards set up SB.TV, one of the first YouTube channels dedicated to British rap music, and was also key to Ed Sheeran’s early success.

name: Paul Willen
headline: Paul Willen, Architect of Manhattan’s Waterfront, Dies at 93
abstract: His plan for a former rail yard became the template for a neighborhood created by a coalition of civic groups and a brash developer named Donald Trump.

name: Paul Farmer
headline: Paul Farmer, Pioneer of Global Health, Dies at 62
abstract: As a medical student, Dr. Farmer decided to build a clinic in Haiti. It grew into a vast network serving some of the world’s poorest communities.

name: Arthur Feuerstein
profession: Chess Player With a Comeback Gambit
headline: Arthur Feuerstein, Chess Player With a Comeback Gambit, Dies at 86
abstract: Once one of the country’s best young players, he became a top player again after a car crash left him slipping in and out of consciousness.

name: Mark Lanegan
profession: Screaming Trees and Queens of the Stone Age Singer
headline: Mark Lanegan, Screaming Trees and Queens of the Stone Age Singer, Dies at 57
abstract: Known for his deep, world-weary voice, he was part of a generation of Seattle musicians who put grunge music on the map.

name: Dennison Young
headline: Dennison Young, Inseparable Aide to Giuliani, Dies at 78
abstract: He was a calm, deliberate and thoughtful lifelong confidant, presenting an odd-couple contrast with the voluble, impulsive, sometimes operatic former mayor.

name: Iraj Pezeshkzad
profession: Author of a Classic Iranian Novel
headline: Iraj Pezeshkzad, Author of a Classic Iranian Novel, Dies at 94
abstract: The satirical “My Uncle Napoleon” became a cultural touchstone that held up a mirror to his country, before the 1979 revolution sent the author into exile in Paris.

name: John Szeles
profession: Comic Magician as the Amazing Johnathan
headline: John Szeles, Comic Magician as the Amazing Johnathan, Dies at 63
abstract: He called himself the “Freddy Kreuger of Comedy,” incorporating horror magic tricks into his Las Vegas act.

name: Gary Brooker
headline: Gary Brooker, Singer for Procol Harum, Dies at 76
abstract: The pianist and singer composed the band’s music for five decades, including the hit “A Whiter Shade of Pale.”

name: William Kuenzel
headline: William Kuenzel, Who Claimed Innocence From Death Row, Dies at 60
abstract: When evidence emerged that might have exonerated him, his case drew the support of prominent legal figures, but the Supreme Court twice declined to review it.

name: Bob Beckel
headline: Bob Beckel, Liberal Operative Who Became a Fixture on Fox, Dies at 73
abstract: He ran Walter Mondale’s 1984 presidential campaign, and later became a curmudgeonly pundit on conservative TV.

name: Sandy Nelson
headline: Sandy Nelson, Drummer Who Turned His Rhythms Into Hits, Dies at 83
abstract: His “Teen Beat” hit No. 4 in 1959. More than 30 albums followed.

name: Leonard Kessler
headline: Leonard Kessler, Colorful Children’s Book Author, Dies at 101
abstract: He crafted tales of everyday life for early readers. His “Mr. Pine’s Purple House,” first published in 1965, later inspired a new publishing company — and Jeff Bezos.

name: Sally Kellerman
headline: Sally Kellerman, Oscar-Nominated ‘MASH’ Actress, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Ms. Kellerman, who became a star in Robert Altman’s dark satire, was known for her self-effacing comedy, a velvety voice and an ability to toggle between sultry and silly.

name: Bappi Lahiri
headline: Bappi Lahiri, India’s ‘Disco King,’ Dies at 69
abstract: He helped popularize the genre with some of the country’s biggest hits of all time, including “I Am a Disco Dancer.”

name: John Landy
profession: Dueled Roger Bannister in Mile of the Century
headline: John Landy Dies at 91; Dueled Roger Bannister in ‘Mile of the Century’
abstract: The second man to run the mile in less than four minutes, he believed that he and his longtime rival, who was the first, had simply done the inevitable.

name: Demetrios Papademetriou
headline: Demetrios Papademetriou, Top Immigration Scholar, Dies at 75
abstract: He designed the “Grand Bargain,” an ambitious plan for Mexican immigrants to gain legal status in the U.S., but it collapsed after the terrorist attacks of 9/11.

name: Leo Bersani
profession: Literary Critic and Theorist on Gay Life
headline: Leo Bersani, Literary Critic and Theorist on Gay Life, Dies at 90
abstract: He had a long career as a scholar of French literature, but he was best known for his writings on gay identity at the height of the AIDS crisis.

name: David Boggs
headline: David Boggs, Co-Inventor of Ethernet, Dies at 71
abstract: Thanks to the invention he helped create in the 1970s, people can send email over an office network or visit a website through a coffee shop hot spot.

name: Richard Blum
profession: Political Donor and Husband of Senator Feinstein
headline: Richard Blum, Political Donor and Husband of Senator Feinstein, Dies at 86
abstract: As a financier, he amassed a fortune that he spent on Democrats, helping to propel his wife from San Francisco mayor to a long career in the Senate.

name: Sharon Wohlmuth
headline: Sharon Wohlmuth, Photographer of Best-Selling ‘Sisters,’ Dies at 75
abstract: Her images, paired with the words of Carol Saline, created a publishing sensation that led to the follow-up books “Mothers & Daughters” and “Best Friends.”

name: Michele McNally
headline: Michele McNally, Who Elevated Times Photography, Dies at 66
abstract: The paper won six Pulitzer Prizes for photography during her tenure as its director of photography and a member of the newsroom’s top management.

name: Dottie Frazier
profession: Pioneer in Diving the Deep Seas
headline: Dottie Frazier, a Pioneer in Diving the Deep Seas, Dies at 99
abstract: Famed in the diving world, she is thought to be the first woman certified as a scuba instructor in the U.S.

name: John Q. Trojanowski
headline: John Q. Trojanowski Dies at 75; Changed Understanding of Brain Diseases
abstract: He was able to combine pathology and biochemistry to help figure out how and why people get diseases as disparate as Alzheimer’s, Parkinson’s and A.L.S.

name: Connie Hogarth
headline: Connie Hogarth, Relentless Social Activist, Dies at 95
abstract: As leader of a group in Westchester County, N.Y., she was arrested more than 20 times for local and national protests, including ones against nuclear power plants.

name: Shirley Hughes
headline: Shirley Hughes, Whose Books Depicted Children’s Mini-Dramas, Dies at 94
abstract: Beloved in her native England, she wrote and illustrated more than 70 books for children of all ages, with millions of copies sold worldwide. She was honored by the queen.

name: Barry Bauman
headline: Barry Bauman, Restoration Artist and Detective, Dies at 73
abstract: A noted conservator, he peeled back paintings’ hidden layers and sometimes uncovered fakes, most notably a portrait wrongly thought to be of Mary Todd Lincoln.

name: Autherine Lucy Foster
profession: First Black Student at U. of Alabama
headline: Autherine Lucy Foster, First Black Student at U. of Alabama, Dies at 92
abstract: Her career there lasted only three days; attacked by mobs, she was suspended and then expelled. Today, a campus building is named in her honor.

name: Duvall Hecht
headline: Duvall Hecht, Founder of Books on Tape, Is Dead at 91
abstract: His desire to listen to something enriching on his daily commute led him to start the company whose success made audiobooks a commercial phenomenon.

name: Farrah Forke
profession: Played a Helicopter Pilot on Wings
headline: Farrah Forke, Who Played a Helicopter Pilot on ‘Wings,’ Dies at 54
abstract: Forke played Alex Lambert on three seasons of the popular sitcom, a fixture of the NBC schedule in the 1990s.

name: Ken Duberstein
headline: Ken Duberstein, a Former Reagan Chief of Staff, Dies at 77
abstract: He helped revive the Reagan presidency in its last years and became a respected lobbyist in Washington.

name: Alan Ladd Jr.
headline: Alan Ladd Jr., Hitmaking Film Executive, Dies at 84
abstract: When other studios didn’t want it, he took on the project that became “Star Wars.” He later guided “Chariots of Fire,” “Young Frankenstein” and numerous other movies.

name: Monique Hanotte
headline: Monique Hanotte, Savior of Allied Airmen, Dies at 101
abstract: Using her knowledge of the Belgium-France border and quick thinking, she guided dozens of downed Allied airmen to safety during World War II.

name: Joni James
headline: Joni James, 91, Heartfelt Chanteuse of the 1950s, Dies
abstract: A top-selling artist known as the “Queen of Hearts,” she had a voice tinged with longing and melancholy and was an early influence on Barbra Streisand.

name: Shane Warne
profession: One of Crickets Masters of Spin
headline: Shane Warne, One of Cricket’s Masters of Spin, Dies at 52
abstract: Warne’s management company said the Australian star died Friday of a suspected heart attack.

name: Andrei Belgrader
headline: Andrei Belgrader, 75, Dies; Director Influenced Future Stars
abstract: His Yale Rep and American Repertory Theater productions included early work by Cherry Jones, Mark Linn-Baker and more, and he directed starry Off Broadway shows.

name: Gary North
headline: Gary North, Apostle of Bible-Based Economics, Dies at 80
abstract: A prolific economic historian, he sought to infiltrate the conservative Christian and libertarian mainstream but never got too far from the fringe.

name: Dan Graham
headline: Dan Graham, Mind-Bending Conceptual Artist, Dies at 79
abstract: Best known for his large mirrored installations, he played with ideas about spectacle and perception in a vast array of genres.

name: Barbara Shermund
headline: Overlooked No More: Barbara Shermund, Flapper-Era Cartoonist
abstract: For two decades, she drew almost 600 cartoons for The New Yorker with female characters that commented on life with wit, intelligence and irony.

name: Lionel James
headline: Lionel James, Speedy Back Who Covered a Lot of Turf, Dies at 59
abstract: A diminutive player, he set a single-season record in 1985 for yardage gained in the N.F.L. as a running back, receiver and kick and punt returner.

name: Tim Considine
profession: Young Star of My Three Sons
headline: Tim Considine, Young Star of ‘My Three Sons,’ Is Dead at 81
abstract: He played the oldest son, Mike, after gaining fame in the “Spin and Marty” serial on Disney’s “The Mickey Mouse Club.” But after his 1960s heyday, he faded as an actor.

name: Maggy Hurchalla
headline: Maggy Hurchalla, Formidable Florida Environmentalist, Dies at 81
abstract: She fought to protect the wilderness she loved, tangling with developers. One case led to a $4.4 million judgment against her.

name: Alice von Hildebrand
headline: Alice von Hildebrand, Conservative Catholic Philosopher, Dies at 98
abstract: She was critical of abortion rights and gay rights, and called on women to change the world by embracing what she called feminine virtues.

name: Tony Walton
headline: Tony Walton, Award-Winning Stage and Screen Designer, Dies at 87
abstract: He worked with the directors Mike Nichols, Bob Fosse and Jerry Zaks, winning three Tony Awards and an Oscar for “All That Jazz.”

name: Mitchell Ryan
profession: Played the Villain in Lethal Weapon
headline: Mitchell Ryan, Who Played the Villain in ‘Lethal Weapon,’ Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Ryan, who appeared in the TV series “Dark Shadows,” played a brutal businessman in “Santa Barbara” and a wealthy father in the sitcom “Dharma & Greg.”

name: Dennis Cunningham
profession: Civil Rights Lawyer for Varied Causes
headline: Dennis Cunningham, Civil Rights Lawyer for Varied Causes, Dies at 86
abstract: He successfully represented the Black Panthers, environmentalists who accused the government of conspiracy and Attica prison inmates.

name: Walter R. Mears
profession: Boys on the Bus Campaign Reporter
headline: Walter R. Mears, ‘Boys on the Bus’ Campaign Reporter, Dies at 87
abstract: He won a Pulitzer while reporting on politics for The Associated Press, and in an enduring 1973 book he epitomized the virtues of wire service journalism.

name: Conrad Janis
profession: Father on Mork & Mindy and Much More
headline: Conrad Janis, Father on ‘Mork & Mindy’ and Much More, Dies at 94
abstract: His role on the hit sitcom was just one of more than 100 film and television credits; he was also a fine jazz trombonist and co-owner of an art gallery.

name: Edmund Keeley
profession: Shined a Light on Modern Greek Culture
headline: Edmund Keeley Dies at 94; Shined a Light on Modern Greek Culture
abstract: The pre-eminent translator of poets like C.P. Cavafy and George Seferis, he was also a well-regarded novelist and poet in his own right.

name: Kent Waldrep
headline: Kent Waldrep, Athlete Whose Injury Led to Advocacy, Dies at 67
abstract: Partly paralyzed as a college football player, he had a role in the inception of the Americans With Disabilities Act and raised money for spinal cord research.

name: Alain Graillot
headline: Alain Graillot, Influential Rhône Valley Winemaker, Dies at 77
abstract: Skilled, charismatic and energetic, he found success in a region that had not been esteemed for its wines, helping to raise its international reputation.

name: Fred Ferretti
headline: Fred Ferretti, Reporter Turned Writer on Food, Dies at 90
abstract: He covered every aspect of dining for The Times from 1969 to 1986 and then became a columnist for Gourmet magazine.

name: Charles E. Entenmann
profession: Last of a Storied Baking Family
headline: Charles E. Entenmann, Last of a Storied Baking Family, Dies at 92
