abstract: Working with his brothers and their mother, he helped turn the company that bore their name into a nationally known symbol of sweetness.

name: Evgeny Maslin
headline: Evgeny Maslin, Russian General Who Secured Nuclear Arsenal, Dies at 84
abstract: He persuaded Ukraine and other post-Soviet states to give up their weapons, then worked with the U.S. to safeguard and dismantle thousands of them.

name: Nelson W. Aldrich Jr.
headline: Nelson W. Aldrich Jr., 86, Dissector of Old Money, Dies
abstract: In books and articles, he unsparingly scrutinized an American aristocracy that he knew intimately.

name: Carlos Barbosa-Lima
headline: Carlos Barbosa-Lima, 77, Dies; Expanded Classical Guitar’s Reach
abstract: A virtuoso since his teenage years, he performed concerts that ranged from classical repertory to Brazilian music to the Beatles and Broadway.

name: Sally Schmitt
headline: Sally Schmitt, Trend-Setting Restaurateur, Is Dead at 90
abstract: She founded the French Laundry in the Napa Valley with her husband, Don, and is often cited as a pioneer in California cuisine.

name: Elsa Klensch
headline: Elsa Klensch, Face of Fashion on CNN, Is Dead at 89
abstract: She was one of the cable channel’s early stars, covering designers, models and trends in a weekly show that brought the industry to a mass television audience.

name: Emilio Delgado
profession: Luis on Sesame Street for Four Decades
headline: Emilio Delgado, Luis on ‘Sesame Street’ for Four Decades, Dies at 81
abstract: The actor was a fixture on the groundbreaking educational program. His character’s wedding to Maria on the show in 1988 captivated children and their parents.

name: Leo Marx
profession: Studied Clash of Nature and Culture in America
headline: Leo Marx, 102, Dies; Studied Clash of Nature and Culture in America
abstract: His landmark book, “The Machine in the Garden,” explored the contradiction of a “pastoral ideal” and helped define the field of American studies.

name: Rusty Mae Moore
headline: Rusty Mae Moore, Transgender Educator and Activist, Dies at 80
abstract: Ms. Moore, a business professor, sheltered numerous people, including the activist Sylvia Rivera, in her Park Slope home, which came to be known as Transy House.

name: Bruce Duffy
profession: Hailed for His Ambitious First Novel
headline: Bruce Duffy, Hailed for His Ambitious First Novel, Dies at 70
abstract: In “The World as I Found It,” he created a fictional biography of the philosopher Wittgenstein. But though acclaimed as an “emerging” star, he wrote only two more novels.

name: Johnny Grier
headline: Johnny Grier, N.F.L.’s First Black Referee, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Grier joined the league as a field judge in 1981 and was elevated to referee, or crew chief, seven years later, becoming a mentor to other Black officials.

name: Donald Pinkel
profession: Developed a Cure for Childhood Leukemia
headline: Donald Pinkel, Who Developed a Cure for Childhood Leukemia, Dies at 95
abstract: The disease was once a virtual death sentence for children. Today, his aggressive treatments mean that almost everyone survives it.

name: Bobbie Nelson
headline: Bobbie Nelson, Longtime Pianist for Brother Willie, Dies at 91
abstract: They grew up together playing music, and in 1973 she became a core member of the band that would take Mr. Nelson to worldwide fame.

name: Ron Miles
headline: Ron Miles, Understated Master of Jazz Cornet, Is Dead at 58
abstract: He enjoyed the admiration of his fellow musicians for decades, but he had just been starting to find his place in the spotlight.

name: Yuriko
headline: Yuriko, Keeper of Martha Graham’s Flame, Is Dead at 102
abstract: A choreographer and dancer, she was associated with Graham for more than 50 years, and founded and directed the Martha Graham Ensemble, a student company.

name: Tova Borgnine
headline: Tova Borgnine, Cosmetics Maven and QVC Star, Dies at 80
abstract: She turned a cactus-derived face mask into a multimillion-dollar beauty business. Her husband, the actor Ernest Borgnine, gave it a surprise assist.

name: Brent Renaud
headline: Brent Renaud, Crusading Filmmaker, Is Killed at 50
abstract: He traveled around the world and the United States making documentaries about urgent moral issues. He was shot to death while filming in Ukraine.

name: Renny Cushing
headline: Renny Cushing, Relentless Foe of Death Penalty, Dies at 69
abstract: Even after his father was murdered, he opposed capital punishment and led the effort to repeal it in New Hampshire. Three decades later, he succeeded.

name: William Hurt
headline: William Hurt, Oscar-Winning Leading Man of the 1980s, Dies at 71
abstract: A four-time Academy Award nominee, he starred in such films as “Body Heat,” “The Big Chill,” “Kiss of the Spider Woman” and “Broadcast News.”

name: Bernard W. Nussbaum
headline: Bernard W. Nussbaum, Clinton Counsel and Defender, Dies at 84
abstract: The president’s first White House lawyer, Mr. Nussbaum had a turbulent 14 months in the job weathering a rash of controversies.

name: Thomas Demakos
profession: Judge in Howard Beach Murder Case
headline: Thomas Demakos, Judge in Howard Beach Murder Case, Dies at 98
abstract: In a notorious 1987 trial over the death of a Black man in New York City, he ruled that defense lawyers could not exclude potential jurors on the basis of race.

name: Scott Hall
headline: Scott Hall, Wrestler Who Rose to Fame as Razor Ramon, Dies at 63
abstract: Called a “hugely influential superstar” by World Wrestling Entertainment, he was also a founding member of the villainous New World Order with Kevin Nash and Hulk Hogan.

name: Timmy Thomas
profession: Singers Big Hit Was an Antiwar Anthem
headline: Timmy Thomas, 77, Dies; Singer’s Big Hit Was an Antiwar Anthem
abstract: His “Why Can’t We Live Together” rose to the top of the Billboard charts in 1973. He could never match its success.

name: Maureen Howard
headline: Maureen Howard, 91, Novelist Who Traced Women’s Challenges, Dies
abstract: In well-reviewed works like “Natural History” and “A Lover’s Almanac,” she was intent, a fellow writer said, on “making the novel do and hold more.”

name: Annie Flanders
headline: Annie Flanders, Founder of Details Magazine, Dies at 82
abstract: Her idiosyncratic and fiercely independent magazine chronicled Downtown Manhattan in the 1980s, a combustible mix of art, music and fashion.

name: Jean Potvin
profession: Part of the 1980s Islanders N.H.L. Dynasty
headline: Jean Potvin, Part of the 1980s Islanders’ N.H.L. Dynasty, Dies at 72
abstract: He was traded to New York in 1973, when they were an awful expansion team, but became part of a fast-improving franchise that won its first two Stanley Cups in 1980 and ’81.

name: Hiram Maristany
headline: Hiram Maristany, 76, Dies; ‘People’s Photographer’ of Spanish Harlem
abstract: He sought to depict his community “from the inside out” and to challenge negative images of Puerto Ricans in New York.

name: Lauro Cavazos
headline: Lauro Cavazos, First Hispanic Cabinet Member, Dies at 95
abstract: A sixth-generation Mexican American and a Democrat, he was secretary of education, straddling the administrations of Ronald Reagan and George H.W. Bush.

name: Barrie R. Cassileth
headline: Barrie R. Cassileth, Who Transformed Cancer Care, Dies at 83
abstract: By advocating for acupuncture and other treatments, she helped countless patients weather the pain of chemotherapy and radiation.

name: Lynn Yeakel
profession: Spurred Into Politics by Anita Hill
headline: Lynn Yeakel, Spurred Into Politics by Anita Hill, Dies at 80
abstract: She nearly unseated Senator Arlen Specter after his aggressive grilling of Ms. Hill during Clarence Thomas’s 1991 Supreme Court confirmation hearings.

name: Ralph Terry
profession: Yankee Hurler Redeemed by One Pitch
headline: Ralph Terry, Yankee Hurler Redeemed by One Pitch, Dies at 86
abstract: In 1960 he gave up the home run that handed the Pittsburgh Pirates a World Series victory. Two years later he got the final out of the Series against the San Francisco Giants.

name: Eugene N. Parker
profession: Predicted the Existence of Solar Wind
headline: Eugene N. Parker, 94, Dies; Predicted the Existence of Solar Wind
abstract: At first, almost no one believed his findings on gigantic eruptions from the sun. Today, a NASA mission to fly through its outer atmosphere is named after him.

name: Jack Willis
headline: Jack Willis, TV Producer and Empathetic Filmmaker, Dies at 87
abstract: A survivor of a crippling accident, his documentaries and news coverage for public television focused on poverty, race and other social issues.

name: Jeanette Wagner
headline: Jeanette Wagner, Who Globalized the Estée Lauder Brand, Dies at 92
abstract: Meticulous in building relationships, she helped open new markets for the cosmetics company, notably in the Soviet Union, as head of its international operations.

name: Chaim Kanievsky
headline: Rabbi Chaim Kanievsky, Venerated Talmudic Scholar, Dies at 94
abstract: He initially insisted, “Canceling Torah study is more dangerous than the coronavirus.” But he had a change of heart, even before testing positive.

name: Peter Bowles
profession: Actor in To the Manor Born
headline: Peter Bowles, Actor in ‘To the Manor Born,’ Dies at 85
abstract: In a six-decade career in TV, film and onstage, he played comedy and drama, hapless heroes and villains, often with the air of the archetypal English gent.

name: Av Westin
headline: Av Westin, Newsman Behind ABC’s ‘20/20,’ Dies at 92
abstract: After nearly 20 years at CBS News, he went to a rival network and helped turn its answer to “60 Minutes” into a frequent Emmy Award winner.

name: Don Young
profession: Alaska Congressman and Dean of the House
headline: Don Young, Alaska Congressman and Dean of the House, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Young, who was first elected in 1973, during the Nixon administration, became the longest-serving Republican in House history in 2019.

name: Louise Little
profession: Activist and Mother of Malcolm X
headline: Overlooked No More: Louise Little, Activist and Mother of Malcolm X
abstract: She fought oppression in public and private spheres, and shaped her son’s education as he evolved into a powerful thinker and speaker.

name: Janet MacPherson
profession: Kind of First Wave Feminist in Surfing
headline: Janet MacPherson, a Kind of First Wave Feminist in Surfing, Dies at 84
abstract: She was the rare woman to pick up surfing in the 1950s. More remarkably, she continued to ride the waves into her 80s.

name: John Clayton
profession: N.F.L. Reporter Best Known for His ESPN Work
headline: John Clayton, N.F.L. Reporter Best Known for His ESPN Work, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Clayton, who was known as the Professor, combined substantive reporting and a crisp delivery during his on-air appearances.

name: Julian Heicklen
headline: Julian Heicklen, Cantankerous Civil Liberties Advocate, Dies at 90
abstract: A retired chemistry professor, he staged weekly protests in front of a Manhattan courthouse, angering prosecutors, who tried to send him to prison.

name: Sumy Sadurni
headline: Sumy Sadurni, Photojournalist Whose Focus Was East Africa, Dies at 32
abstract: She traveled the world, but she was best known for the photographs she took in Uganda, which brought pathos and humanity to charged subject matter.

name: Victor Fazio
profession: Longtime Democratic Leader in the House
headline: Victor Fazio, Longtime Democratic Leader in the House, Dies at 79
abstract: Known for his ability to work across the aisle, he represented the Sacramento area from 1979 to 1999 and rose to become chairman of the House Democratic caucus.

name: Chris Madden
headline: Chris Madden, Lifestyle Author and Personality, Dies at 73
abstract: An early HGTV host, she lent her name to furniture and housewares lines. In the late 1990s, her book on women’s private sanctuaries touched a nerve.

name: Yvan Colonna
profession: Corsican Jailed for French Prefects Murder
headline: Yvan Colonna, Corsican Jailed for French Prefect’s Murder, Dies at 61
abstract: A folk hero for Corsica’s nationalist movement, he evaded a long manhunt but was finally arrested in 2003. He died shortly after being brutally attacked in prison.

name: Madeleine Albright
profession: First Woman to Serve as Secretary of State
headline: Madeleine Albright, First Woman to Serve as Secretary of State, Dies at 84
abstract: She rose to power and fame as a brilliant analyst of world affairs before serving as an aggressive advocate of President Bill Clinton’s policies.

name: John Roach
headline: John Roach, Pioneer of the Personal Computer, Is Dead at 83
abstract: He helped make the home computer ubiquitous by introducing the fully assembled Tandy TRS-80, which was so novel at the time that it became a museum piece.

name: William Kraft
profession: Percussionist and Force in New Music
headline: William Kraft, Percussionist and Force in New Music, Dies at 98
abstract: A mainstay of the Los Angeles Philharmonic, he also composed music that elevated overlooked instruments like the timpani.

name: John Korty
headline: John Korty, Director of ‘Miss Jane Pittman,’ Is Dead at 85
abstract: He was best known for a series of ambitious television movies that examined racism, disability and other social issues.

name: Stephen Wilhite
headline: Stephen Wilhite, Creator of the GIF, Is Dead at 74
abstract: The looping animations known as graphics interchange format quickly became a staple of the internet, although the pronunciation of ‘GIF’ was a frequent subject of debate.

name: Edward C. Johnson III
headline: Edward C. Johnson III, 91, Dies; Made Fidelity an Investment Giant
abstract: Mr. Johnson’s exceptionally long tenure — he presided over Fidelity into his 80s — coincided with a huge expansion of his industry.

name: Edward Johnson
profession: C.I.A. Hero in Iran Hostage Crisis
headline: Edward Johnson, C.I.A. Hero in Iran Hostage Crisis, Dies at 81
abstract: He was a secret partner who helped rescue six American diplomats in 1980 by passing them off as a film crew. The caper inspired the movie “Argo.”

name: Vera Gissing
headline: Vera Gissing, Who Was Rescued by ‘Britain’s Schindler,’ Dies at 93
abstract: She was not quite 11 when train convoys organized by a London stockbroker carried her and hundreds of other Jewish children from Czechoslovakia on the eve of World War II.

name: Dagny Carlsson
headline: Dagny Carlsson, Centenarian Blogger, Dies at 109
abstract: She began posting about her daily life in Sweden at the age of 99. She went on to acquire a worldwide fan base.

name: Kip Hawley
headline: Kip Hawley, Transportation Security Administrator, Dies at 68
abstract: He sought to overhaul a much-maligned federal agency by enhancing security procedures, bolstering morale and taking a common-sense approach to the job.

name: Dirck Halstead
headline: Dirck Halstead, Photojournalist Who Captured History, Dies at 85
abstract: Shooting for Time magazine and United Press International, he documented presidents, the Vietnam War and more.

name: Taylor Hawkins
headline: Taylor Hawkins, Foo Fighters’ Drummer, Dies at 50
abstract: Hard-hitting and charismatic, he was direct about his hopes for the group’s future, even after two decades. “I want to be the biggest band in the world,” he said.

name: Lee E. Koppelman
headline: Lee E. Koppelman, Trailblazing Long Island Planner, Dies at 94
abstract: He was a pioneer in grappling with suburban sprawl and preserving open spaces, helping to shape the region.

name: Martin Pope
headline: Martin Pope, Whose Research Led to OLEDs, Dies at 103
abstract: The work done by the self-effacing Dr. Pope helped pave the way for the high-performance electronics displays that are so common today.

name: Sara Suleri Goodyear
headline: Sara Suleri Goodyear Dies at 68; Known for Memoir of Pakistan
abstract: Her 1989 book, “Meatless Days,” is viewed as an important work of postcolonial literature.

name: Marina Goldovskaya
headline: Marina Goldovskaya, 80, Dies; Filmmaker Documented Russian Life
abstract: In about 30 documentaries she looked at the people and history of her homeland, some of it brutally dark.

name: Christopher Alexander
headline: Christopher Alexander, Architect Who Humanized Urban Design, Dies at 85
abstract: A fierce anti-modernist, he championed vernacular structures, becoming a counterculture hero to many, from New Urbanists to software designers to Prince Charles.

name: Joan Joyce
headline: Joan Joyce, a Sensation in Softball and More, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Her pitching feats — including striking out Ted Williams — were legend. And her prowess in basketball, volleyball and golf as well spoke to her all-around athletic greatness.

name: Ashton Hawkins
profession: Curator of the Rich and Powerful at the Met Museum
headline: Ashton Hawkins, Curator of the Rich and Powerful at the Met Museum, Dies at 84
abstract: A top executive, he cultivated donors, then used his legal acumen to arrange their multimillion-dollar gifts of money and art.

name: Richard Lipez
headline: Richard Lipez, Who Reimagined the Gay Detective Novel, Dies at 83
abstract: Under the pen name Richard Stevenson, he sought to correct crime fiction’s portrayals of gay characters as freaks or villains with an entirely relatable protagonist.

name: Patrick Demarchelier
headline: Patrick Demarchelier, Fashion Photographer, Dies at 78
abstract: He was famous for his portraits of supermodels and his close relationship with Princess Diana. His images are part of the fashion canon.

name: Nancy Lane
profession: Spirit Behind Studio Museum in Harlem
headline: Nancy Lane, Spirit Behind Studio Museum in Harlem, Dies at 88
abstract: An art collector and the institution’s longest-serving board member, she was also a pioneering Black woman in the corporate world.

name: Ted Mooney
headline: Ted Mooney, Author of Inventive Novels, Is Dead at 70
abstract: His attention-getting first book, “Easy Travel to Other Planets,” began with dolphin-human sex. The three that followed were comparably offbeat.

name: Elizabeth Hayes
headline: Overlooked No More: Elizabeth Hayes, Coal Town Doctor Who Fought for Miners
abstract: “Dr. Betty” led 350 miners on a strike in Pennsylvania in 1945 demanding that the mining company that owned their town improve horridly unsanitary conditions.

name: Margaret M. McGowan
profession: Expanded the Field of Dance History
headline: Margaret M. McGowan, Who Expanded the Field of Dance History, Dies at 90
abstract: She took a unique interdisciplinary approach and created a new field of study by exploring the collision of politics, ballet, design and music.

name: Budi Tek
profession: His Fortune Built a Vast Trove of Asian Art
headline: Budi Tek, 65, Dies; His Fortune Built a Vast Trove of Asian Art
abstract: He was one of the world’s top collectors, and his immense Yuz Museum in Shanghai helped establish the region’s bustling art scene.

name: Charles G. Boyd
profession: Air Force General and Former P.O.W
headline: Charles G. Boyd, Air Force General and Former P.O.W., Dies at 83
abstract: He began his 36-year career in the military as a fighter pilot and was the only prisoner of war in the Vietnam conflict to become a four-star general.

name: Thomas F. Staley
headline: Thomas F. Staley, Dogged Pursuer of Literary Archives, Dies at 86
abstract: As head of the Harry Ransom Center in Texas, he enhanced its holdings by acquiring the papers of a host of literary lions, and of Woodward and Bernstein to boot.

name: Bill Fries
profession: Singer Known for 1970s Trucking Ballad Convoy
headline: Bill Fries, Singer Known for 1970s Trucking Ballad ‘Convoy,’ Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Fries, who performed under the stage name C.W. McCall, was an ad executive before he scored a hit with “Convoy,” a CB radio-inspired ode to renegade truckers.

name: Michelle Materre
headline: Michelle Materre, Champion of Black Independent Film, Dies at 67
abstract: Through her distribution company and an educational series, Ms. Materre was for decades a tireless advocate for underrepresented filmmakers.

name: Estelle Harris
headline: Estelle Harris, George’s Mother on ‘Seinfeld,’ Dies at 93
abstract: Employing a high-powered screech, she took maternal exasperation and paranoia to comedic heights as one of the show’s most frequently recurring characters.

name: Tabby Diamond
headline: Two Members of the Mighty Diamonds, Acclaimed Reggae Trio, Are Dead
abstract: Tabby Diamond, 66, was shot and killed Tuesday in Kingston, Jamaica. Bunny Diamond, 70, died three days later after a long illness.

name: Bunny Diamond
headline: Two Members of the Mighty Diamonds, Acclaimed Reggae Trio, Are Dead
abstract: Tabby Diamond, 66, was shot and killed Tuesday in Kingston, Jamaica. Bunny Diamond, 70, died three days later after a long illness.

name: Anne Parsons
headline: Anne Parsons, Who Revived the Detroit Symphony, Dies at 64
abstract: She shepherded the orchestra through a bitter six-month strike and then worked to ensure that it flourished after what many considered a near-death moment.

name: Gene Shue
headline: Gene Shue, All-Star and Longtime N.B.A. Coach, Dies at 90
abstract: He had a seven-decade pro career, starting as a guard with the Pistons before coaching for 22 years, leading the Bullets and the 76ers to the finals.

name: Tommy Davis
headline: Tommy Davis, Batting Star With the ’60s Dodgers, Dies at 83
abstract: A two-time batting champion, he helped power a dominant Los Angeles team, but a serious injury derailed his career, and he fell short of the Hall of Fame.

name: Lygia Fagundes Telles
headline: Lygia Fagundes Telles, Popular Brazilian Novelist, Dies at 98
abstract: One of her country’s first writers to address female sexuality from a woman’s perspective, she produced four novels and dozens of short stories that could be read as political allegories.

name: Roland White
headline: Roland White, a Shaper of Bluegrass and Country-Rock, Dies at 83
abstract: A mandolin player and singer, he made his mark with the Country Boys (later renamed the Kentucky Colonels), and his influence extended into the rock of the ’60s.

name: Alan J. Hruska
headline: Alan J. Hruska, a Founder of Soho Press, Dies at 88
abstract: A litigator for 44 years, he was also a novelist; a writer, director and producer of plays and films; and helped establish the independent publishing house Soho Press.

name: June Brown
headline: June Brown, a Mainstay of Britain’s ‘EastEnders,’ Dies at 95
abstract: As the memorable Dot Cotton, she appeared in thousands of episodes of the hugely popular soap opera over 35 years.

name: Terry Wallis
profession: Awoke 19 Years After a Traumatic Brain Injury
headline: Terry Wallis, 57, Dies; Awoke 19 Years After a Traumatic Brain Injury
abstract: Long after a car accident left him in a minimally conscious state in 1984, he woke up one day and said, “Mom.” Then he kept talking.

name: Bobby Rydell
headline: Bobby Rydell, Teenage Idol With Enduring Appeal, Dies at 79
abstract: He had his first hit in 1959. Six decades later, teamed with his fellow singers Frankie Avalon and Fabian, he was still drawing crowds.

name: Vladimir V. Zhirinovsky
headline: Vladimir V. Zhirinovsky Dies at 75; Ultranationalist Russian Politician
abstract: His antics kept him at center stage in Russia for three decades, and his once fringe views on imperial expansion had gone mainstream with the invasion of Ukraine.

name: June Shagaloff Alexander
headline: June Shagaloff Alexander, School Desegregation Leader, Dies at 93
abstract: She helped Thurgood Marshall prepare for his Supreme Court fight and later took on de facto school segregation across the North and West.

name: Doris Derby
headline: Doris Derby, Civil Rights Era Photographer, Dies at 82
abstract: She was an artist who was studying anthropology when she became an activist in the civil rights movement and a rare woman to document Black life in photos.

name: Nehemiah Persoff
profession: Actor With a Familiar Face (and Voice)
headline: Nehemiah Persoff, Actor With a Familiar Face (and Voice), Dies at 102
abstract: His most prominent roles included three tenderly caring parents, but he was most associated with the dapper gangsters he portrayed in the movies and on television.

name: Mira Calix
headline: Mira Calix, Iconoclastic Composer and Artist, Is Dead at 52
abstract: Her work spanned albums, public art installations, music for Shakespeare plays and touring with Radiohead.

name: Joseph Kalichstein
headline: Joseph Kalichstein, Pianist of Subtlety and Refinement, Dies at 76
abstract: An acclaimed exponent of Schumann, Brahms and Mendelssohn, he was best known for his work as a member of the Kalichstein-Laredo-Robinson Trio.

name: Nan Melville
profession: Photography Captured Dance in Many Forms
headline: Nan Melville, 72, Whose Photography Captured Dance in Many Forms, Dies
abstract: Over a long career, her pictures, whether of famed dance troupes or experimental works, reflected what one admirer called “her love affair with dance.”

name: Herb Turetzky
headline: Herb Turetzky, Nets’ Official Scorer for 54 Years, Dies at 76
abstract: He recorded the statistics of more than 2,200 home games for the team in both New York and New Jersey, and in both the American and National Basketball Associations.

name: Rae Allen
headline: Rae Allen, Tony Winner and TV Mainstay, Dies at 95
abstract: In a varied career, she had memorable roles in “Damn Yankees” and on “Seinfeld” and was nominated for three Tonys. She later became a director.

name: Gerda Weissmann Klein
headline: Gerda Weissmann Klein, Honored Holocaust Survivor, Dies at 97
abstract: Her story was told in an Oscar-winning documentary, and her message of hope and love in the face of overwhelming evil was an inspiration to millions.

name: Tony May
headline: Tony May, 84, Restaurateur Who Championed Italian Cuisine, Dies
abstract: A native of Italy, he was crucial in bringing Italian fine dining to New York and beyond, determined to break the stranglehold of French haute cuisine.

name: Marion Joseph
headline: Marion Joseph, Citizen Warrior on Reading Instruction, Dies at 95
abstract: Arguing for phonics as a learning tool and getting results, she exerted influence on educational policy in California and beyond.

name: Rayfield Wright
headline: Rayfield Wright, Cowboys’ Hall of Fame Lineman, Dies at 76
abstract: He was an All-Pro right tackle in the 1970s. But in retirement he was diagnosed with dementia, which he linked to repeated hits to the head.

name: Eleanor Munro
headline: Eleanor Munro, Who Profiled Women Artists, Is Dead at 94
abstract: Her 1979 book featured interviews with dozens of artists, but she also wrote on other subjects — pilgrimages, for instance.

name: Arthur D. Riggs
headline: Arthur D. Riggs, 82, Dies; Led Team That Invented Artificial Insulin
abstract: His research into recombinant DNA provided a foundation for the biotech revolution, leading to a long list of lifesaving treatments.

name: Jack Higgins
profession: Author of The Eagle Has Landed
headline: Jack Higgins, Author of ‘The Eagle Has Landed,’ Dies at 92
abstract: Under various pseudonyms, he wrote adventure novels that sold more than 250 million copies worldwide.

name: Jordan Mooney
headline: Jordan Mooney, an Avatar of Punk Style, Dies at 66
abstract: Swathed in rubber and glowering from spiked heels, she was a fearsome figurehead for a generation of disaffected English teenagers.

name: Patricia MacLachlan
headline: Patricia MacLachlan, ‘Sarah, Plain and Tall’ Author, Dies at 84
abstract: A best-selling children’s book writer, she focused on family life and its difficulties, earning acclaim for her gentle, spare prose.

name: Gilbert Gottfried
headline: Gilbert Gottfried, Comedian With a Distinctive Voice, Dies at 67
abstract: His credits ranged from the family-friendly “Aladdin” to the unfettered vulgarity of “The Aristocrats” and included a brief stint on “Saturday Night Live.”

name: Mimi Reinhard
headline: Mimi Reinhard, Who Typed Up Schindler’s List, Dies at 107
abstract: As a secretary in a forced-labor camp in World War II, she added her own name to the list of 1,100 Jews who would be spared from the gas chambers.

name: Shirley Spork
profession: Teaching Pro and a Founder of the L.P.G.A
headline: Shirley Spork, Teaching Pro and a Founder of the L.P.G.A., Dies at 94
abstract: She was one of 13 who started the Ladies Professional Golf Association in 1950, though her legacy lay in tutoring countless women, from duffers to pros.

name: Michel Bouquet
headline: Michel Bouquet, Award-Winning French Actor, Dies at 96
abstract: One of his country’s great theater performers, he went on to appear in more than 100 films playing ordinary men whose surface blandness masked complex lives.

name: Jerry Uelsmann
headline: Jerry Uelsmann, Surreal Image-Maker, Dies at 87
abstract: He did not believe that a photographer’s creativity ended with the click of the shutter; in his darkroom, he combined elements of multiple pictures to create something new.

name: Christopher Moore
profession: Preserver of Black New York History
headline: Christopher Moore, Preserver of Black New York History, Dies at 70
abstract: Mr. Moore, who was of African American and Native American descent, was committed to preserving the past as a curator, author and savior of city landmarks.

name: Franz Mohr
headline: Franz Mohr, Piano Tuner to the Stars, Is Dead at 94
abstract: “I play more in Carnegie Hall than anybody else,” he said of his career adjusting instruments for Horowitz, Gould and others, “but I have no audience.”

name: Marvin Chomsky
headline: Marvin Chomsky, Director of ‘Roots’ and ‘Holocaust,’ Dies at 92
abstract: A four-time Emmy Award winner, he directed landmark historical TV dramas and the movie “Inside the Third Reich.”

name: Mike Bossy
profession: Hall of Famer on Champion Islander Teams
headline: Mike Bossy, Hall of Famer on Champion Islander Teams, Dies at 65
abstract: He led the N.H.L. in goals twice as his team won four consecutive Stanley Cups in the early ’80s, but he felt it never got the recognition it deserved.

name: Christopher Coover
profession: Auction Expert on the Printed Word
headline: Christopher Coover, Auction Expert on the Printed Word, Dies at 72
abstract: At Christie’s, he managed sales of rare books, manuscripts and documents by the likes of da Vinci, Lincoln and Kerouac. On TV, he lent his eye to “Antiques Roadshow.”

name: Michael F. Neidorff
profession: His Company Was an Obamacare Stalwart
headline: Michael F. Neidorff, 79, Dies; His Company Was an Obamacare Stalwart
abstract: He transformed a small company into a corporation focused on providing health insurance under government programs. It now insures 25 million people.

name: Ann Hutchinson Guest
headline: Ann Hutchinson Guest, Who Fixed Dance on Paper, Dies at 103
abstract: She was a leading advocate of and expert on dance notation, helping to do for choreographed works what a score does for music.

name: Sidney Altman
profession: Stumbled on a Breakthrough in Genetics
headline: Sidney Altman, Who Stumbled on a Breakthrough in Genetics, Dies at 82
abstract: He shared a Nobel for finding that RNA was not just a carrier of genetic information but could also trigger life-changing chemical reactions in cells.

name: John Zaritsky
headline: John Zaritsky, Unflinching Oscar-Winning Documentarian, Dies at 78
abstract: He took on uncomfortable subjects like rape, cancer and assisted suicide. His account of a student’s murder on a cross-country trip won a 1983 Academy Award.

name: Liz Sheridan
headline: Liz Sheridan, Who Played Jerry Seinfeld’s Mom, Dies at 93
abstract: She was Helen Seinfeld on his sitcom and was seen on many other TV shows and on Broadway. She also wrote of her youthful romance with James Dean.

name: Art Rupe
profession: Brought Rhythm and Blues to the Mainstream
headline: Art Rupe, Who Brought Rhythm and Blues to the Mainstream, Dies at 104
abstract: As the founder of the independent label Specialty Records, he helped set the table for the rock ’n’ roll era by signing performers like Little Richard.

name: Peng Ming-min
headline: Peng Ming-min, Fighter for Democracy in Taiwan, Dies at 98
abstract: He endured Japanese imperial rule, a lost limb in World War II, Chinese martial law and decades in exile to become a leading force for Taiwanese self-determination.

name: Paul Siebel
headline: Paul Siebel, Singer Whose Career Was Notable but Brief, Dies at 84
abstract: He arrived on the Greenwich Village folk scene in the mid-1960s and drew comparisons to Dylan. But he left the music business not long after.

name: Jacqueline Shohet Kahanoff
headline: Overlooked No More: Jacqueline Shohet Kahanoff, Writer of Levantine Identity
abstract: In her books and essays, she developed a social model and a vision for how various groups could find their place in a modern Middle East.

name: Kevin Lippert
headline: Kevin Lippert, ‘Impresario’ of Architectural Books, Dies at 63
abstract: He began by selling reprints of classics from the trunk of his car and created what one architect called “a whole architectural universe.”

name: Harrison Birtwistle
headline: Harrison Birtwistle, Fiercely Modernist Composer, Dies at 87
abstract: His labyrinthine, theatrical works placed him in the first rank of 20th-century English composers, though his music was often tagged as “difficult.”

name: Kathryn Hays
headline: Kathryn Hays, Soap Star for Nearly 40 Years, Dies at 87
abstract: A string of TV credits, including a turn on “Star Trek,” led to an enduring role on “As the World Turns,” in which her character matured as Ms. Hays aged.

name: Letizia Battaglia
headline: Letizia Battaglia, Photographer of Mafia Brutality, Dies at 87
abstract: Her images of victims on the streets of Palermo were stamped on the nation’s consciousness as she challenged the grip mobsters had on her native Sicily.

name: Radu Lupu
headline: Radu Lupu, Pianist Who Awed Listeners, Is Dead at 76
abstract: Preferring the stage (and an office chair) to the recording studio, he enthralled audiences with ruminative performances that evoked the otherworldly.

name: Dede Robertson
profession: Wife and Partner of Pat Robertson
headline: Dede Robertson, Wife and Partner of Pat Robertson, Dies at 94
abstract: A founding board member of the Christian Broadcasting Network, she also campaigned for her husband when he ran for president in 1988.

name: Nicholas Angelich
headline: Nicholas Angelich, Ocean-Straddling Pianist, Dies at 51
abstract: American-born and Paris-based since he was 13, he performed on both sides of the Atlantic, winning acclaim specializing in Germanic repertory.

name: Rosario Ibarra de Piedra
headline: Rosario Ibarra de Piedra, 95, Dies; Fought for Mexico’s ‘Disappeared’
abstract: When her son vanished in 1975, she began a crusade on behalf of him and hundreds of others and became a voice of moral authority on the left.

name: Peter Swales
headline: Peter Swales, Who Startled Freud Scholarship, Dies at 73
abstract: He was not a traditional academic, but his eyebrow-raising research challenged received wisdom on Sigmund Freud.

name: Jimmy Wang Yu
profession: Seminal Figure in Kung Fu Films
headline: Jimmy Wang Yu, Seminal Figure in Kung Fu Films, Dies at 79
abstract: He changed the nature of Asian martial arts movies, which had been relying on sword fighting and fantasy, by bringing hand-to-hand combat to the fore.

name: Mikhail Vasenkov
profession: His Spy Ring Inspired The Americans
headline: Mikhail Vasenkov Dies at 79; His Spy Ring Inspired ‘The Americans’
abstract: He and his wife were among 10 Soviet sleeper agents who blended into American society before being exposed and deported in 2010. The TV series sprung from the episode.

name: Daryle Lamonica
headline: Daryle Lamonica, Hard-Throwing Quarterback, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Known as the Mad Bomber for his powerful arm, he led the Oakland Raiders to the Super Bowl and was among pro football’s top passers in the late 1960s and early ’70s.

name: Mwai Kibaki
headline: Mwai Kibaki, Kenya’s Third President, Dies at 90
abstract: He came to power promising to root out corruption and improve government transparency. But his tenure was blighted by widespread graft and a violent upheaval.

name: Guy Lafleur
profession: Dynamic Star of the Montreal Canadiens
headline: Guy Lafleur, Dynamic Star of the Montreal Canadiens, Dies at 70
abstract: He helped lead the team to five Stanley Cup titles and was the first player in N.H.L. history to score at least 50 goals and 100 points in six consecutive years.

name: Ursula Bellugi
profession: Pioneer in the World of Sign Language
headline: Ursula Bellugi, Pioneer in the World of Sign Language, Dies at 91
abstract: Her research advanced understanding of the brain and the origins of language — signed and spoken — and shed light on how humans communicate and socialize.

name: Umang Gupta
profession: Paved Way for Indian Tech Executives
headline: Umang Gupta, Who Paved Way for Indian Tech Executives, Dies at 73
abstract: He found success as an entrepreneur in Silicon Valley shortly after arriving there in 1978, then represented his fellow alumni from the Indian Institutes of Technology.

name: Laura Hales
headline: Laura Hales, Who Examined Her Church’s Tough Issues, Dies at 54
abstract: Her writings and her podcast on subjects like polygamy explored the history and doctrine of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

name: Hermann Nitsch
headline: Hermann Nitsch, an Artist With Guts, as Well as Blood, Dies at 83
abstract: He was a founding father of a group of radical artists who used their bodies and other elements to upend art-making at the dawn of the 1960s.

name: Orrin Hatch
profession: Seven-Term Senator and a Republican Force
headline: Orrin Hatch, Seven-Term Senator and a Republican Force, Dies at 88
abstract: Overcoming poverty and representing Utah, he became a powerful figure in Washington, helping to build a conservative majority on the Supreme Court.

name: Jim Hartz
profession: NBC Newsman and Former Today Co-Host
headline: Jim Hartz, NBC Newsman and Former ‘Today’ Co-Host, Dies at 82
abstract: He was Barbara Walters’s on-air partner for only two years, but viewers also knew him for three decades as a correspondent, anchor and TV host.

name: Chris Bailey
headline: Chris Bailey, Who Gave Australia Punk Rock, Dies at 65
abstract: His band, the Saints, introduced the country (and the world) to their raw sound just as the Sex Pistols were emerging in London and the Ramones in New York.

name: L. McCrae Dowless Jr.
profession: Operative at Heart of Election Scandal
headline: L. McCrae Dowless Jr., 66, Dies; Operative at Heart of Election Scandal
abstract: Federal prosecutors charged him with absentee-ballot tampering in North Carolina, and the state ordered a historic rerun of a federal election.

name: Donald Baechler
headline: Donald Baechler, Painter of Cartoonish Collages, Is Dead at 65
abstract: His works, depicting crudely-drawn images of balloon-like faces, beach balls, flowers, globes or ice cream cones, brought him fame in New York in the 1980s.

name: Geraldine Weiss
profession: Blazed a Trail for Women in Investing
headline: Geraldine Weiss Dies at 96; Blazed a Trail for Women in Investing
abstract: She published her stock market newsletter for nearly four decades — initially as “G. Weiss,” to conceal her identity as a woman in a male-dominated industry.

name: Sid Mark
profession: Disc Jockey Devoted to Sinatra for Six Decades
headline: Sid Mark, Disc Jockey Devoted to Sinatra for Six Decades, Dies at 88
abstract: He hosted four radio shows that focused on the singer, who at one concert singled him out in the audience and said, “I love him.”

name: Cynthia Albritton
headline: Cynthia Albritton, Rock’s ‘Plaster Caster,’ Is Dead at 74
abstract: She gained fame making sculptures of male rockers’ genitals, an attention-getting gimmick that she grew to regard as art and that became part of rock ’n’ roll lore.

name: Rolando Hinojosa-Smith
headline: Rolando Hinojosa-Smith, Award-Winning Hispanic Novelist, Dies at 93
abstract: A Texan raised in two cultures in the Rio Grande Valley border county, he wrote 15 novels about the area and became a major figure in Chicano literature.

name: Kenneth Tsang
headline: Kenneth Tsang, Veteran Hong Kong Actor, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Tsang, who was known for tough-guy supporting roles and ubiquitous hair dye advertisements, was found dead while in hotel quarantine.

name: John DiStaso
profession: Star Reporter of New Hampshire Primaries
headline: John DiStaso, Star Reporter of New Hampshire Primaries, Dies at 68
abstract: The dean of the state’s political press corps, he was well positioned to grill, vet and analyze a new crop of presidential candidates every four years.

name: Earl E. Devaney
headline: Earl E. Devaney, Scourge of Waste and Corruption, Dies at 74
abstract: A former football lineman, he pushed back against abuse in federal agencies as one of the government’s most aggressive internal watchdogs.

name: José Luis Cortés
headline: José Luis Cortés, Trailblazing Cuban Bandleader, Dies at 70
abstract: He was trained in the classics and jazz, but he helped popularize a new, danceable genre known as timba.

name: Jacques Perrin
headline: Jacques Perrin, Soft-Spoken Film Star and Producer, Is Dead at 80
abstract: A French actor, he was a heartthrob in the musical “The Young Girls of Rochefort,” a photojournalist in the thriller “Z” and a jaded director in the hit “Cinema Paradiso.”

name: Klaus Schulze
headline: Klaus Schulze, Pioneering Electronic Composer, Is Dead at 74
abstract: In a prolific career spanning five decades, he helped pave the way for ambient, techno and trance music.

name: Catherine Spaak
profession: Darling of Italian Cinema in the 60s
headline: Catherine Spaak, Darling of Italian Cinema in the ’60s, Dies at 77
abstract: Born in France, she moved to Italy as a teenager and began a long acting career, which extended to Hollywood in the movie “Hotel.”

name: Ady Fidelin
profession: Black Model Hidden in Plain Sight
headline: Overlooked No More: Ady Fidelin, Black Model ‘Hidden in Plain Sight’
abstract: She appeared in hundreds of Man Ray’s photos, was friends with Picasso and is believed to be the first Black model to appear in a major American fashion magazine.

name: Philip J. Hilts
headline: Philip J. Hilts, 74, Dies; Reporter Exposed a Big-Tobacco Cover-up
abstract: In one of many scoops for The Times, he revealed how the tobacco industry had kept secret its own research showing that nicotine was harmful and addictive.

name: Régine
profession: Discotheque Gave Nightlife a New Dawn
headline: Régine, Whose Discotheque Gave Nightlife a New Dawn, Dies at 92
abstract: Credited with opening the first disco, she built an empire of glittering playgrounds for the Beautiful People in Paris, New York and beyond.

name: Kathy Boudin
profession: Radical Imprisoned in a Fatal Robbery
headline: Kathy Boudin, Radical Imprisoned in a Fatal Robbery, Dies at 78
abstract: She had a role in the Brink’s heist by the Weather Underground that left two police officers dead. But she became a model prisoner and, after being freed, helped former inmates.

name: Ron Galella
headline: Ron Galella, Celebrity-Hounding Photographer, Dies at 91
abstract: He personified the paparazzi — brazen and relentless in chasing the famous, particularly Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis. But his pictures also came to be admired.

name: David Birney
profession: Starred on TVs Bridget Loves Bernie
headline: David Birney, Who Starred on TV’s ‘Bridget Loves Bernie,’ Dies at 83
abstract: The sitcom, about an interfaith marriage, drew criticism from Jewish groups and was canceled after one season. He fared better onstage than in television.

name: Norman Y. Mineta
headline: Norman Y. Mineta, First Japanese American Cabinet Member, Dies at 90
abstract: Interned during World War II, he went to Congress and later served in the cabinets of Presidents Bill Clinton and George W. Bush.

name: Rob Stein
headline: Rob Stein, Who Changed How Politics Is Funded, Dies at 78
abstract: In the wake of Republican electoral victories in 2002 and 2004, he convened major liberal donors to finance a network of political groups aligned with Democrats.

name: David Walden
profession: Computer Scientist at Dawn of Internet
headline: David Walden, Computer Scientist at Dawn of Internet, Dies at 79
abstract: In 1969, he was part of a team of young engineers who built the first machine to switch data among computers using the Arpanet, the precursor to the internet.

name: Erich Barnes
profession: Star Defensive Back for the 1960s Giants
headline: Erich Barnes, Star Defensive Back for the 1960s Giants, Dies at 86
abstract: A speedy cornerback who also played for the Chicago Bears and the Cleveland Browns, he was often matched against the league’s best wide receivers.

name: George D. Gould
profession: Pillar in New Yorks Fiscal Rescue
headline: George D. Gould, a Pillar in New York’s Fiscal Rescue, Dies at 94
abstract: As a Republican Wall Street financier recruited by the Democratic mayor, he helped make the city’s effort to restore stability more credible.

name: Judy Henske
profession: Distinctive Voice on the Folk Scene
headline: Judy Henske, a Distinctive Voice on the Folk Scene, Dies at 85
abstract: Her versatile vocals were a trademark, as was her comic stage patter. The character Annie Hall owed her a debt.

name: Marcus Leatherdale
headline: Marcus Leatherdale, Portraitist of Downtown Manhattan, Dies at 69
abstract: He was the Cecil Beaton of New York City’s demimonde during the AIDS years, making elegant portraits of Andy Warhol, Keith Haring and Madonna.

name: Neal Adams
headline: Neal Adams, Who Gave Batman a Darker Look, Dies at 80
abstract: He brought an earthy realism (and a new adversary or two) to the superhero characters he drew. He also championed the rights of comic book creators.

name: Stanislav Shushkevich
headline: Stanislav Shushkevich, First Leader of Post-Soviet Belarus, Dies at 87
abstract: He helped formalize the breakup of the Soviet Union in 1991, led his country until 1994, then became a vocal critic of his successor, Aleksandr G. Lukashenko.

name: Sheldon Krimsky
profession: Warned of Profit Motive in Science
headline: Sheldon Krimsky, Who Warned of Profit Motive in Science, Dies at 80
abstract: He delved into numerous scientific fields — stem-cell research, genetic modification of food and DNA privacy among them — and sought to pinpoint the dangers.

name: Ricardo Alarcon
headline: Ricardo Alarcon, Diplomat and Castro Confidant, Dies at 84
abstract: As Havana’s go-between with the U.S., he negotiated Elián González’s return to Cuba. He was also the country’s U.N. representative on two occasions.

name: Maria Marcus
headline: Maria Marcus, Public Interest Lawyer and Mentor, Dies at 88
abstract: She argued before the Supreme Court six times representing New York State, took on civil rights cases for the N.A.A.C.P. and taught at Fordham for decades.

name: Peter Moore
headline: Peter Moore, a Force in the 1980s Sneaker Revolution, Dies at 78
abstract: He was a key member of the team at Nike that changed sneaker culture by developing the enduringly popular Air Jordan.

name: Johnnie A. Jones Sr.
headline: Johnnie A. Jones Sr. Dies at 102; a Civil Rights Lawyer Early On
abstract: In 1953, he represented defendants in the Baton Rouge bus boycott, a model for later activism, after returning from World War II as a wounded veteran of D-Day.

name: Morton Mower
headline: Dr. Morton Mower, Inventor of Lifesaving Heart Device, Dies at 89
abstract: With a colleague, he created a miniaturized defibrillator that could be implanted inside patients suffering from potentially fatal arrhythmia.

name: Mickey Gilley
headline: Mickey Gilley, Country Star Whose Club Inspired ‘Urban Cowboy,’ Dies at 86
abstract: His records regularly made the charts for two decades. But he was ultimately best known for his Texas nightclub, which was at the heart of a country music revival.

name: Ric Parnell
profession: Real Drummer in a Famous Fake Band
headline: Ric Parnell, Real Drummer in a Famous Fake Band, Dies at 70
abstract: The central characters in the mockumentary “This Is Spinal Tap” were comic actors, but Mr. Parnell was an actual professional musician.

name: George Pérez
profession: Gave New Life to Wonder Woman
headline: George Pérez, Who Gave New Life to Wonder Woman, Dies at 67
abstract: Working for both Marvel and DC, he created comic book series that brought superheroes together, and was co-creator of The New Teen Titans.

name: Yuri Averbakh
headline: Yuri Averbakh, Chess’s First Centenarian Grandmaster, Dies at 100
abstract: A Russian, he was one of the world’s best players during the Cold War of the 1950s, joining other top competitors as the pride of the Soviet Union.

name: Midge Decter
headline: Midge Decter, an Architect of Neoconservatism, Dies at 94
abstract: As a writer and intellectual, she abandoned liberal politics, challenged the women’s movement and championed the Reagan Republican agenda.

name: Susan Jacks
profession: Sang Which Way You Goin Billy?
headline: Susan Jacks, Who Sang ‘Which Way You Goin’ Billy?,’ Dies at 73
abstract: Released in 1969, the song, by her group the Poppy Family, was one of the biggest hits to come out of Canada to that point.

name: Edward J. Bronson
headline: Edward J. Bronson, Who Fought for Fairer Trials, Dies at 91
abstract: In cases like the Oklahoma City and Boston Marathon bombings, he favored a greater willingness to change trial venues to overcome bias and impact of publicity.

name: Alfred Baldwin
headline: Alfred Baldwin, Lookout for Watergate Burglars, Dies at 83
abstract: A co-conspirator, he became an early witness for the government, which helped lead to the indictment of the burglars and linked them with the White House.

name: Leonid Kravchuk
profession: First President of an Independent Ukraine
headline: Leonid Kravchuk, First President of an Independent Ukraine, Dies at 88
abstract: Days after his election, he signed a multinational agreement that formally declared the dissolution of the Soviet Union.

name: Gloria Parker
headline: Gloria Parker, Maestra of the Musical Glasses, Dies at 100
abstract: She played many instruments and appeared on radio and television, but she was best known for the skill that led to a role in Woody Allen’s “Broadway Danny Rose.”

name: John Leo
headline: John Leo, Columnist Who Took Aim at Liberal Pieties, Dies at 86
abstract: With a deft wit and disarming sense of humor, he used his posts at Time and later U.S. News & World Report to criticize excesses on the left.

name: Bob Lanier
headline: Bob Lanier, a Dominant Center of the 1970s and ’80s, Dies at 73
abstract: Playing for the Detroit Pistons and the Milwaukee Bucks, he held his own against titans of the era like Wilt Chamberlain, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar and Willis Reed.

name: Bruce MacVittie
headline: Bruce MacVittie, Ubiquitous Character Actor, Dies at 65
abstract: A co-founder of the Naked Angels troupe in New York, he was a familiar face in Off Broadway theater, in movies and on TV, often playing tough guys with tormented souls.

name: Joanna Barnes
profession: Actress in The Parent Trap and Its Remake
headline: Joanna Barnes, Actress in ‘The Parent Trap’ and Its Remake, Dies at 87
abstract: In 1961, she played a vixenish fortune hunter. In 1998, she played the character’s mother. In between, she kept busy on TV and also wrote novels.

name: Gino Cappelletti
headline: Gino Cappelletti, Versatile Boston Patriots Star, Dies at 89
abstract: Playing wide receiver and kicking field goals and extra points, he played in all 10 years of the A.F.L.’s existence and scored a league-record 1,100 points.

name: Susan Nussbaum
profession: Pressed for Disability Rights in Her Plays
headline: Susan Nussbaum, 68, Who Pressed for Disability Rights in Her Plays, Dies
abstract: In a wheelchair after being hit by a car in her 20s, she became an advocate for people with disabilities in her writing for the stage and as a novelist.

name: Khalifa
headline: Sheikh Khalifa, U.A.E. Ruler, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan oversaw vast economic growth and built his country’s partnership with the United States in his 18 years as head of state.

name: Fred Ward
profession: Star of The Right Stuff and Henry and June
headline: Fred Ward, Star of ‘The Right Stuff’ and ‘Henry and June,’ Dies at 79
abstract: A versatile actor, he was best known throughout his long career for playing tough, resilient characters. But he also had a subtle side.

name: Robert C. McFarlane
profession: Top Reagan Aide in Iran-Contra Affair
headline: Robert C. McFarlane, Top Reagan Aide in Iran-Contra Affair, Dies at 84
abstract: As national security adviser, he pleaded guilty in an illegal scheme to aid Nicaraguan rebels in the 1980s. Guilt-ridden, he attempted suicide.

name: Henry Scott Stokes
headline: Henry Scott Stokes Dies at 83; Opened Japan to English Speakers
abstract: A biographer of the nationalist novelist Yukio Mishima, he was Tokyo bureau chief for three major newspapers and, afterward, was no stranger to controversy.

name: Junichi Arai
headline: Overlooked No More: Junichi Arai, Innovative Textile Designer
abstract: His experimentations with different materials and technology earned him widespread recognition as well as patents and awards.

name: Val Broeksmit
profession: Blew the Whistle on Deutsche Bank
headline: Val Broeksmit, 46, Who Blew the Whistle on Deutsche Bank, Dies
abstract: An itinerant musician, he leaked secret files to F.B.I. investigators looking at the bank’s ties to money laundering, the Trump Organization and Russia.

name: Randy Weaver
profession: Confronted U.S. Agents at Ruby Ridge
headline: Randy Weaver, Who Confronted U.S. Agents at Ruby Ridge, Dies at 74
abstract: The 1992 standoff left his wife, his son and a U.S. marshal dead, and made him a reluctant hero of the anti-government far right.

name: Richard C. Wald
profession: Leader in Print and Network News
headline: Richard C. Wald, Leader in Print and Network News, Is Dead at 92
abstract: He was the last managing editor of The New York Herald Tribune. When that newspaper folded, he went on to top jobs with NBC and ABC News.

name: Teresa Berganza
profession: Charismatic Star of the Opera Stage
headline: Teresa Berganza, Charismatic Star of the Opera Stage, Is Dead at 89
abstract: The Spanish mezzo-soprano was internationally acclaimed for her dramatic performances in the works of Mozart, Rossini and Bizet.

name: Carrie White
headline: Carrie White, Hair Stylist to the Stars, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Her Beverly Hills salon was a party scene where she roller-skated among her glamorous clientele, including Elizabeth Taylor and Warren Beatty.

name: Lil Keed
headline: Lil Keed, Up-and-Coming Atlanta Rapper, Dies at 24
abstract: The musician, a protégé of Young Thug, died on Friday in Los Angeles, his label said.

name: Jack Cakebread
headline: Jack Cakebread, Pioneering Napa Valley Winemaker, Dies at 92
abstract: He was an auto mechanic with a sideline in photography when he and his wife bought a cattle farm in 1972. They turned it into one of America’s leading wineries.

name: Larry Woiwode
headline: Larry Woiwode, Who Wrote of Family, Faith and Rural Life, Dies at 80
abstract: Raised in North Dakota and rural Illinois, he was a literary star in New York City in the 1970s. But he left the limelight to raise a family on a North Dakota farm.

name: Katsumoto Saotome
headline: Katsumoto Saotome, Who Preserved Stories of Tokyo Firebombing, Dies at 90
abstract: He compiled six books of survivors’ recollections of the 1945 attack. He also founded (without government support) a memorial museum.

name: Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma
headline: Pandit Shiv Kumar Sharma, Master of the Santoor, Dies at 84
abstract: He single-handedly elevated a 100-string instrument little known outside Kashmir into a prominent component of Hindustani classical music.

name: Jürgen Blin
headline: Jürgen Blin, Who Went 7 Rounds Against Ali, Dies at 79
abstract: In 1971, Blin was a working-class fighter from Hamburg and a top contender in Germany. Ali was coming off a loss to Joe Frazier and needed to get back in shape.

name: Maggie Peterson
headline: Maggie Peterson, a Memorable ‘Andy Griffith Show’ Guest, Dies at 81
abstract: As Charlene Darling, a member of the musical Darling family, she appeared in five episodes, beginning with one in which her character became smitten with Mr. Griffith’s.

name: Urvashi Vaid
headline: Urvashi Vaid, Pioneering L.G.B.T.Q. Activist, Is Dead at 63
abstract: Over a four-decade career, she profoundly shaped a range of progressive issues, including AIDS advocacy, prison reform and gay rights.

name: John L. Canley
headline: John L. Canley, Belated Medal of Honor Recipient, Dies at 84
abstract: He was the first living Black Marine to be awarded America’s highest military decoration — 50 years after he demonstrated valor in Vietnam.

name: Rosmarie Trapp
headline: Rosmarie Trapp, of the ‘Sound of Music’ Family, Dies at 93
abstract: She was the last surviving daughter of the baron and the would-be nun depicted in the stage musical and 1965 film.

name: Ray Scott
profession: Creator of the Super Bowl of Bass Fishing
headline: Ray Scott, Creator of the Super Bowl of Bass Fishing, Dies at 88
abstract: He turned bass fishing into a professional sport with the championship Bassmaster Classic and other tournaments, using his showmanship skills to excite fans.

name: Donald K. Ross
headline: Donald K. Ross, Leading Public Interest Lawyer, Dies at 78
abstract: A Ralph Nader acolyte, he galvanized students in the 1970s and promoted social change through legislation, legal action and political pressure.

name: Ben Roy Mottelson
profession: Shed Light on the Shape of Atoms
headline: Ben Roy Mottelson Dies at 95; Shed Light on the Shape of Atoms
abstract: He shared the 1975 Nobel Prize in Physics for discoveries of forces that can distort the shape of an atomic nucleus, with implications for human-made nuclear fission.

name: Alexander Toradze
headline: Alexander Toradze, 69, Idiosyncratic Pianist, Is Dead
abstract: A defector to the U.S., he was admired for his prowess in the Russian repertory, but his individualistic approach “was not for everyone — or for all repertoire.”

name: Kwaku Ohene-Frempong
headline: Kwaku Ohene-Frempong, Expert in Sickle Cell Disease, Dies at 76
abstract: When his baby boy was diagnosed with the illness, he made it his mission to combat it. He later took his expertise back to his native Ghana.

name: Elspeth Barker
profession: Author of a Beloved if Unsung Novel
headline: Elspeth Barker, Author of a Beloved if Unsung Novel, Dies at 81
abstract: Her “O Caledonia,” a Gothic coming-of-age story set in Scotland, has been called “one of the best least-known novels of the 20th century.”

name: Bob Neuwirth
headline: Bob Neuwirth, Colorful Figure in Dylan’s Circle, Dies at 82
abstract: He was a recording artist and songwriter himself, but he also played pivotal roles in the careers of Bob Dylan and Janis Joplin.

name: Robert Goolrick
profession: Became a Successful Novelist Late in Life
headline: Robert Goolrick Dies at 73; Became a Successful Novelist Late in Life
abstract: Being fired as an advertising executive freed him to write a blistering memoir about his Southern family and an erotic novel that became a best seller.

name: Suzi Gablik
headline: Suzi Gablik, Art Critic Who Took Modernism to Task, Dies at 87
abstract: As a collage artist and reviewer, she was an it-girl of avant-garde art. But she turned on that world in 1984 with her salvo of a book, “Has Modernism Failed?”

name: Roger Angell
headline: Roger Angell, Who Wrote About Baseball With Passion, Dies at 101
abstract: In elegantly winding articles for The New Yorker loaded with inventive imagery, he wrote more like a fan than a sports journalist.

name: Marshall Arisman
headline: Marshall Arisman, Illustrator Who Found Beauty in Violence, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Arisman, whose work appeared in The New York Times and other major periodicals, was a storyteller who mined his personal biography for inspiration.

name: Vangelis
profession: Composer Best Known for Chariots of Fire
headline: Vangelis, Composer Best Known for ‘Chariots of Fire,’ Dies at 79
abstract: A master of the synthesizer, he won an Oscar for that film’s score, and his memorable theme song became a No. 1 pop hit.

name: Robert J. Vlasic
profession: Made a Fortune by Making Pickles Funny
headline: Robert J. Vlasic Dies at 96; Made a Fortune by Making Pickles Funny
abstract: His company took a lighthearted approach to its products, with a wisecracking stork as its mascot, and became the market leader.

name: Frank Gilbert
profession: Preservationist in New York and Beyond
headline: Frank Gilbert, Preservationist in New York and Beyond, Dies at 91
abstract: He fought to spare Grand Central Terminal from the fate that befell Penn Station. He also helped draft a landmarks preservation law that became a model across the country.

name: Kenneth Welsh
profession: Memorable as a Villain on Twin Peaks
headline: Kenneth Welsh, Memorable as a Villain on ‘Twin Peaks,’ Dies at 80
abstract: In a long career onstage (including Broadway), in movies and on television, he ranged across genres, from sketch comedy to science fiction.

name: Amanda Claridge
headline: Amanda Claridge, Archaeologist of Ancient Rome, Dies at 72
abstract: Her 1998 guide took a detailed look at the city and its many ruins, examining who built what and why.

name: Simon Preston
headline: Simon Preston, Acclaimed Organist and Conductor, Dies at 83
abstract: A force in the world of choral music, he was considered one of the most important English church musicians of his generation.

name: Kristine Gebbie
headline: Kristine Gebbie, the First U.S. AIDS Czar, Dies at 78
abstract: She worked with President Bill Clinton to to make the disease a public health priority. But her office never achieved the stature or effectiveness that some had hoped for.

name: Colin Cantwell
headline: Colin Cantwell, ‘Star Wars’ Spacecraft Designer, Dies at 90
abstract: He created the look of the X-wing and the Death Star; he also worked on “2001: A Space Odyssey,” “Close Encounters of the Third Kind” and “WarGames.”

name: Julie Beckett
profession: Helped Disabled Children Live at Home
headline: Julie Beckett, Who Helped Disabled Children Live at Home, Dies at 72
abstract: A waiver named for her daughter, Katie, has allowed hundreds of thousands of children to receive medical care without having to live in a hospital.

name: E. Gerald Corrigan
headline: E. Gerald Corrigan, Who Helped Ease ’87 Stock Crash, Dies at 80
abstract: As president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, he favored flooding the financial system with cash to restore confidence among investors.

name: Joe Pignatano
profession: Met Coach Known for His Bullpen Farm
headline: Joe Pignatano, Met Coach Known for His Bullpen Farm, Dies at 92
abstract: After an undistinguished career as a catcher with the Brooklyn Dodgers and other teams, he cultivated vegetables as well as relief pitchers at Shea Stadium.

name: Morton L. Janklow
headline: Morton L. Janklow, Agent for Best-Selling Authors, Dies at 91
abstract: A bold, risk-taking negotiator, he numbered among his clients Danielle Steel, Judith Krantz, three presidents and Pope John Paul II.

name: Colin Forbes
headline: Colin Forbes, a ‘Designer’s Designer,’ Is Dead at 94
abstract: He was best known as the brain behind Pentagram, the influential partnership that has been a force in the design world for half a century.

name: Ray Liotta
headline: Ray Liotta, of ‘Goodfellas’ and ‘Field of Dreams,’ Dies at 67
abstract: He was known for his intensity, especially in crime dramas, but he was also adept at comedy. “You want to do as many different genres as you can,” he once said.

name: Hazel Henderson
headline: Hazel Henderson, Groundbreaking Environmentalist, Dies at 89
abstract: A self-taught apostle of the green economy and socially responsible investing, she taught her followers to act locally.

name: Margot Heuman
profession: Bore Witness to the Holocaust as a Gay Woman
headline: Margot Heuman, Who Bore Witness to the Holocaust as a Gay Woman, Dies at 94
abstract: She was a rare survivor who spoke — in recent years — of her same-sex relationship in the concentration camps, and how it sustained her.

name: Dervla Murphy
headline: Dervla Murphy, Travel Writer Who Preferred Her Bike, Dies at 90
abstract: A curious, intrepid loner from Ireland, she famously went from Dunkirk through Europe and then to Iran, Afghanistan, Pakistan and India — mostly on two wheels.

name: Rosemary Radford Ruether
headline: Rosemary Radford Ruether, Feminist Theologian, Dies at 85
abstract: She was a leading figure in a wave of progressive women who took on the Roman Catholic Church’s male-centered doctrines.

name: Andy Fletcher
headline: Andy Fletcher, a Founder of Depeche Mode, Dies at 60
abstract: With three others, he created the band in 1980 and rode its synthesizer-driven music to worldwide fame.

name: Ron Rice
headline: Ron Rice, Creator of Hawaiian Tropic Lotion, Is Dead at 81
abstract: A poor, pale mountain boy who became smitten with the beach, he mixed some ingredients in a garbage can and found his place in the sun.

name: Angelo Sodano
headline: Cardinal Angelo Sodano, Vatican Power Broker, Dies at 94
abstract: He rose to the second-highest-ranking position in the Roman Catholic Church, but his reputation was stained by his handling of sex-abuse cases.

name: E. Robert Wallach
headline: E. Robert Wallach, 88, Lawyer Linked to Reagan-Era Scandal, Dies
abstract: Convicted in a fraud case that took down an attorney general, he successfully appealed, and later defended himself in a retrial.

name: Alan White
headline: Alan White, Who Drummed With Yes and Ex-Beatles, Dies at 72
abstract: The invitation to perform with John Lennon, which he thought was a joke, led to almost 50 years with one of progressive rock’s foremost bands.

name: Heddy Honigmann
profession: Films Told of Loss and Love
headline: Heddy Honigmann, Whose Films Told of Loss and Love, Dies at 70
abstract: A documentarian, she liked to engage her subjects — Parisian subway buskers, Peruvian taxi drivers, survivors of genocide — in conversations.

name: Ronnie Hawkins
headline: Ronnie Hawkins, Rockabilly Road Warrior, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Besides performing, he mentored stars like Robbie Robertson, Levon Helm and Rick Danko, who went on to form one of the most influential groups of the rock era, the Band.

name: Kenny Moore
headline: Kenny Moore, Marathoner and Track Writer, Dies at 78
abstract: A three-time All-American, he began a long career at Sports Illustrated while still competing. A former top editor there said, “He was a guy with a real literary bent.”

name: KK
headline: KK, Singer of Bollywood Hits, Dies at 53 After a Concert
abstract: He had just concluded a performance when he was stricken. Nicknamed “the Mesmerizer,” he recorded hundreds of songs for some of India’s biggest movie stars.

name: David C. MacMichael
headline: David C. MacMichael, C.I.A. Whistleblower, Dies at 95
abstract: An expert on Latin America, he left the agency and called out the Reagan administration for overselling the Communist threat in Nicaragua.

name: George Shapiro
headline: George Shapiro, Talent Manager Who Pushed for ‘Seinfeld,’ Dies at 91
abstract: He left his job as an agent in the 1970s to guide the careers of Jerry Seinfeld, Carl Reiner and other comics.

name: Marion Barber III
headline: Marion Barber III, Bruising Running Back for Cowboys, Dies at 38
abstract: Nicknamed “Marion the Barbarian,” he had a nose for the end zone, leading the N.F.C. in touchdowns in 2006. But his post-playing years were troubled.

name: Paul Gunther
headline: Paul Gunther, Keeper of a Cultural Flame, Dies at 65
abstract: In New York City, he helped engineer behind-the-scenes rescues of monuments, murals and museums and the preservation of Times Square’s dazzling lights.

name: Gilberto Rodríguez Orejuela
headline: Gilberto Rodríguez Orejuela, Colombian Drug Lord, Dies at 83
abstract: Known as “the Chess Player,” he ran the Cali cartel’s cocaine empire with a businesslike approach until his extradition to the United States. He died in prison.

name: Sophie Freud
headline: Sophie Freud, Critic of Her Grandfather’s Gospel, Dies at 97
abstract: Sigmund Freud’s last surviving grandchild, she fled the Nazis in Vienna, became a professor in America and argued that psychoanalysis was a “narcissistic indulgence.”

name: Maureen Colquhoun
headline: Overlooked No More: Maureen Colquhoun, Pathbreaking Politician Waylaid by Bias
abstract: Colquhoun campaigned for women’s rights in Britain’s male-dominated Parliament. But her political career came to an end when she was outed as a lesbian.

name: Samella Lewis
profession: Artist and Activist for Art World Diversity
headline: Samella Lewis, Artist and Activist for Art World Diversity, Dies at 99
abstract: In addition to painting, she was a historian who pushed for a more inclusive definition of art, in part by founding her own museum devoted to Black artists.

name: Bill Walker
profession: Nashville Force as Conductor and Arranger
headline: Bill Walker, Nashville Force as Conductor and Arranger, Dies at 95
abstract: He scored chart-topping records for country stars and later served as the musical director of “The Johnny Cash Show.”

name: Ann Turner Cook
profession: Her Face Sold Baby Food by the Billions
headline: Ann Turner Cook Dies at 95; Her Face Sold Baby Food by the Billions
abstract: Her likeness as an infant has graced the labels on Gerber products for more than 90 years, though for decades her identity was not disclosed.

name: Barry Sussman
headline: Barry Sussman, Washington Post Watergate Editor, Dies at 87
abstract: He worked closely with the reporters Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein in covering the break-in and the subsequent scandal that doomed Richard Nixon.

name: Martha Myers
profession: Taught Dancers How to Move and More
headline: Martha Myers, Who Taught Dancers How to Move and More, Dies at 97
abstract: She was an institution at the American Dance Festival, and also made early television dance and exercise programs.

name: Paul Vance
profession: Lyricist Behind an Itsy Bitsy Bikini
headline: Paul Vance, Lyricist Behind an ‘Itsy Bitsy’ Bikini, Dies at 92
abstract: His daughter’s experience wearing a bikini on a beach in 1960 inspired him to write a novelty song that became a No. 1 hit.

name: Charlotte Frank
profession: Shaper of New York City Curriculums
headline: Charlotte Frank, Shaper of New York City Curriculums, Dies at 93
abstract: She pushed for universal kindergarten, modernized sex education and barred textbook teaching of creationism.

name: Jim Seals
profession: Half of a Popular 1970s Soft-Rock Duo
headline: Jim Seals, Half of a Popular 1970s Soft-Rock Duo, Dies at 79
abstract: Teamed with Dash Crofts, he hit it big with “Summer Breeze” in 1972. The two went on to have chart success with “Diamond Girl” and other songs.

name: Andrée Geulen
profession: Savior of Jewish Children in Wartime
headline: Andrée Geulen, Savior of Jewish Children in Wartime, Dies at 100
abstract: A Belgian teacher, she kept them out of the hands of Nazis, hiding them in convents, monasteries and farms. After the war, she reunited many with their parents.

name: Ken Bode
profession: Erudite Washington Week Host on PBS
headline: Ken Bode, Erudite ‘Washington Week’ Host on PBS, Dies at 83
abstract: Beginning in 1994, he brought to the moderator’s role credentials as a political activist, an academic and a national correspondent for NBC News.

name: Oris Buckner
headline: Oris Buckner, Detective Who Blew Whistle on Police Abuse, Dies at 70
abstract: The only Black man on the New Orleans homicide squad, he provided key testimony in one of the city’s most notorious civil rights cases.

name: Lawrence D. Ackman
headline: Lawrence D. Ackman, a Cityscape’s Financier, Dies at 83
abstract: A behind-the-scenes power in New York, he helped the city’s leading developers fulfill their skyscraping ambitions.

name: Jim Murphy
profession: Wrote Vivid Histories for the Young
headline: Jim Murphy, Who Wrote Vivid Histories for the Young, Dies at 74
abstract: His books on the Chicago fire, an 18th-century plague and wars drew on first-person accounts to re-create dramatic times.

name: Dave Smith
headline: Dave Smith, Whose Synthesizers Shaped Electronic Music, Dies at 72
abstract: His innovations included the first polyphonic, programmable synthesizer and the universal connectivity of MIDI.

name: Grachan Moncur III
headline: Grachan Moncur III, Trombonist Whose Star Shone Briefly, Dies at 85
abstract: He mixed free jazz and post-bop in notable 1960s and ’70s recordings. But he withdrew from the jazz scene, in part because of a dispute over publishing rights.

name: Dmitry Kovtun
headline: Dmitry Kovtun, Accused Killer of Russian Dissident, Dies at 56
abstract: He and another ex-spy were found by British authorities to have served polonium-laced tea in London to an intelligence agent who had defected.

name: Ingram Marshall
headline: Ingram Marshall, Minimalist Composer of Mystical Sounds, Dies at 80
abstract: An influential figure in American experimental music, he was part of a group of composers who stripped music down to basic elements and used digital sounds.

name: Ranan Lurie
profession: Political Cartoonist With a Global Pen
headline: Ranan Lurie, Political Cartoonist With a Global Pen, Dies at 90
abstract: Starting in the Air Force in Israel and later moving to the United States, he set a record as the world’s most widely syndicated in his field.

name: Sean Thackrey
headline: Sean Thackrey, Creator of Eccentric California Wines, Dies at 79
abstract: A polymath, he dismissed conventional wisdom about varietal wines, terroir and scientific management and won a global following.

name: Song Hae
profession: Survived War and Poverty to Become a Beloved TV Host
headline: Song Hae, Who Survived War and Poverty to Become a Beloved TV Host, Dies at 95
abstract: Born in what is now North Korea, he was known for his cheeky grin and folksy wisecracks as the host of South Korea’s weekly “National Singing Contest” for more than three decades.

name: Paula Rego
headline: Paula Rego, Artist Known for Unsettling Images, Dies at 87
abstract: Her paintings, many of which focused on women’s experiences and perspectives, might depict fear or menace. But it was up to the viewer to fill in the blanks.

name: Valery Ryumin
headline: Valery Ryumin, Who Set Endurance Record in Space, Dies at 82
abstract: A Soviet cosmonaut, he spent 362 days in flight on three missions. He returned 18 years later on a U.S. shuttle to the Mir space station.

name: Julee Cruise
headline: Julee Cruise, Vocalist of ‘Twin Peaks’ Fame, Dies at 65
abstract: In projects for the director David Lynch, she brought an eerie, otherworldly style to “Falling” and other songs.

name: Nancy Clark Reynolds
headline: Nancy Clark Reynolds, a Player in Reagan’s Washington, Dies at 94
abstract: A renowned political insider, she parlayed her connections to become one of the city’s most sought-after lobbyists in the 1980s.

name: John Merriman
headline: John Merriman, Eminent Historian of France, Is Dead at 75
abstract: An indefatigable researcher, he wrote books about terrorists, anarchists, leftists and ordinary people and spent a lot of time in France’s archives.

name: Peter Lamborn Wilson
headline: Peter Lamborn Wilson, Advocate of ‘Poetic Terrorism,’ Dies at 76
abstract: His concept of a “temporary autonomous zone” became an inspiration for protests like Occupy Wall Street and for gatherings like Burning Man.

name: Alexander Nikitin
headline: Alexander Nikitin, Who Coached a Chess Champion, Dies at 87
abstract: Garry Kasparov was just 10 when Mr. Nikitin took him on as a student. By age 17, with Mr. Nikitin as his coach, he was a grandmaster.

name: Philip Baker Hall
headline: Philip Baker Hall, Actor Familiar as Authority Figures, Dies at 90
abstract: He appeared in “Secret Honor,” “Boogie Nights,” “Seinfeld” and dozens of other movies and television shows.

name: Kenneth Dam
profession: Deputy in Reagan and George W. Bush Cabinets
headline: Kenneth Dam, Deputy in Reagan and George W. Bush Cabinets, Dies at 89
abstract: He served under George Shultz at the State Department as the Soviet Union began crumbling and later, at Treasury, led a crackdown on funding for terrorism after 9/11.

name: A.B. Yehoshua
headline: A.B. Yehoshua, Politically Engaged Israeli Writer, Dies at 85
abstract: In 11 novels, three short-story collections and four plays, he tackled a variety of narrative forms and delved into knotty and uncommon subjects.

name: Charles Kernaghan
headline: Charles Kernaghan, Scourge of Sweatshops, Is Dead at 74
abstract: He specialized in taking down high-profile brands that used low-wage labor, including a line of clothing licensed by Kathie Lee Gifford.

name: Sharon Oster
headline: Sharon Oster, Barrier-Breaking Economist, Dies at 73
abstract: She was the first woman to win tenure as a professor at the Yale School of Management and the first woman to be named its dean.

name: Duncan Hannah
headline: Duncan Hannah, Artist and ’70s Chronicler, Dies at 69
abstract: He immersed himself in the wild New York scene of Warhol and CBGB, then emerged in the ’80s as a respected painter.

name: Josh Jensen
headline: Josh Jensen, Visionary Vintner of Pinot Noir, Is Dead at 78
abstract: His belief in limestone soils led him on a two-year quest for the ideal site for what became the Calera Wine Company: a remote mountain south of San Francisco.

name: Shauneille Perry Ryder
headline: Shauneille Perry Ryder, Pioneering Theater Director, Dies at 92
abstract: As a Black woman, she blazed a path Off Broadway with an intuitive grasp of “how a story should be told, particularly a Black story,” Giancarlo Esposito said.

name: Dorothy E. Smith
headline: Dorothy E. Smith, Groundbreaker in Feminist Sociology, Dies at 95
abstract: Starting in the 1960s, she sought to re-center her discipline on the experiences of women, people of color and other marginalized groups.

name: William B. Gould
profession: Escaped Slave and Civil War Diarist
headline: Overlooked No More: William B. Gould, Escaped Slave and Civil War Diarist
abstract: He served nearly three years in the U.S. Navy and documented almost all of it, leaving an invaluable record of Black life during the war.

name: Jean-Louis Trintignant
headline: Jean-Louis Trintignant, Star of Celebrated European Films, Dies at 91
abstract: For 50 years, in movies like “A Man and a Woman” and “My Night at Maud’s,” his specialty was playing the flawed Everyman.

name: Claude Rutault
headline: Claude Rutault, Master of the Painted Word, Is Dead at 80
abstract: His paintings were actually instructions for making paintings. One of his signature “protocols” was to paint a canvas the same color as the wall on which it would hang.

name: Donald Pippin
headline: Donald Pippin, Conductor on Broadway and Beyond, Dies at 95
abstract: As music director, he contributed to the success of acclaimed shows including “Oliver!,” “Mame,” “La Cage aux Folles” and “A Chorus Line.”

name: Joel Whitburn
headline: Joel Whitburn, Tireless Researcher of Music Charts, Dies at 82
