abstract: His numerous books delved deeply into the Billboard charts, developing what an admirer called “the de facto history of recorded music.”

name: George Lamming
headline: George Lamming, Who Chronicled the End of Colonialism, Dies at 94
abstract: Born in Barbados, he was among the last of a generation of writers who traced the Caribbean’s transition to independence.

name: Tim Sale
headline: Tim Sale, Comic Book Artist Who Reimagined Batman, Dies at 66
abstract: Series like “Batman: The Long Halloween” influenced big-screen images of the hero, while “Superman for All Seasons” was another fan favorite.

name: Mark Shields
profession: TV Pundit Known for His Sharp Wit
headline: Mark Shields, TV Pundit Known for His Sharp Wit, Dies at 85
abstract: A former campaign strategist, he became a fixture in American political journalism and punditry and was seen on “PBS NewsHour” for 33 years.

name: Paul M. Ellwood Jr.
headline: Dr. Paul M. Ellwood Jr., Architect of the H.M.O., Is Dead at 95
abstract: Often called the father of the health maintenance organization, he coined the term in 1970, envisioning a system that would compete for patients by providing the best care at the lowest price.

name: Lennie Rosenbluth
profession: Led North Carolina to a Title
headline: Lennie Rosenbluth, Who Led North Carolina to a Title, Dies at 89
abstract: With a starting lineup of New Yorkers, the undefeated Tarheels beat a Kansas team led by Wilt Chamberlain in triple overtime to win the 1957 N.C.A.A. championship.

name: Clela Rorex
headline: Clela Rorex, Clerk Who Broke a Gay-Marriage Barrier, Dies at 78
abstract: In 1975 she issued a gay couple a license to marry in Colorado, becoming a hero to some and an object of hate for others.

name: Steven Gluckstern
headline: Steven Gluckstern, Who Pushed for Mortgage Relief, Dies at 71
abstract: A financial executive and sometime sports entrepreneur, he was thwarted in his quixotic quest to help homeowners with underwater mortgages during the Great Recession.

name: James Rado
headline: James Rado, Co-Creator of the Musical ‘Hair,’ Is Dead at 90
abstract: Working with his fellow writer and actor Gerome Ragni and the composer Galt MacDermot, he jolted Broadway into the Age of Aquarius.

name: Vivian Hewitt
profession: Amassed a Major Collection of Black Art
headline: Vivian Hewitt, Who Amassed a Major Collection of Black Art, Dies at 102
abstract: Ms. Hewitt, a librarian, and her husband used their keen eyes and connections in New York to buy works by Romare Bearden, Jacob Lawrence and others.

name: Meghan Stabile
headline: Meghan Stabile, Who Linked Jazz and Hip-Hop, Dies at 39
abstract: Shows that she produced on a shoestring sought to energize the jazz scene by connecting with younger audiences accustomed to D.J.s and turntables.

name: Hugh McElhenny
headline: Hugh McElhenny, Elusive Hall of Fame Halfback, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Known as the King, he was a thrilling figure on the field, twisting and turning as he frustrated defenders on his circuitous romps to the end zone.

name: Harry Gesner
headline: Harry Gesner, Architect of Soaring California Style, Dies at 97
abstract: His houses cantilevered from cliffs, straddled canyons and sprung from mountains; they would come to define the Southern California landscape.

name: Baxter Black
profession: Elevated Cowboy Poetry to Folk Art
headline: Baxter Black, Who Elevated Cowboy Poetry to Folk Art, Dies at 77
abstract: His wide-ranging work, including books, speeches and regular appearances on NPR, celebrated cowpokes, feed lots and life on the range.

name: Gloria Allen
headline: Gloria Allen, Transgender Activist Who Ran a Charm School, Dies at 76
abstract: She overcame a life of intolerance and abuse to teach style, etiquette and life lessons to young transgender people who were at risk.

name: Ken Knowlton
profession: Father of Computer Art and Animation
headline: Ken Knowlton, a Father of Computer Art and Animation, Dies at 91
abstract: His work at Bell Labs in the 1960s laid the groundwork for today’s computer-generated imagery in film and on TV.

name: Haleh Afshar
profession: Fought for Rights of Muslim Women
headline: Haleh Afshar, Who Fought for Rights of Muslim Women, Dies at 77
abstract: An Iranian-born British scholar and self-described “Muslim feminist,” she joined the House of Lords and advised the British government on women’s issues.

name: Michel David-Weill
headline: Michel David-Weill, Influential Lazard Banker, Dies at 89
abstract: A member of his firm’s family dynasty, he built Lazard into an elite player on Wall Street while keeping it a smaller operation than most of its competitors.

name: Jeffrey Escoffier
profession: Health Official and Scholar of Gay Theory
headline: Jeffrey Escoffier, Health Official and Scholar of Gay Theory, Dies at 79
abstract: He wrote extensively on gay identity and history, but New Yorkers knew a different side of his work: his campaigns on H.I.V. and other health issues.

name: Patrick Adams
profession: Master of New Yorks Underground Disco Scene
headline: Patrick Adams, Master of New York’s Underground Disco Scene, Dies at 72
abstract: He produced, arranged or engineered many of the era’s biggest nightclub hits, even if his records rarely got much play on the radio.

name: Sam Gilliam
headline: Sam Gilliam, Abstract Artist of Drape Paintings, Dies at 88
abstract: A brilliant colorist, he hung his canvases from ceilings in great curves and loops, or pinned them, gathered, to walls, taking his medium into three dimensions.

name: Leonardo Del Vecchio
headline: Leonardo Del Vecchio Dies at 87; Transformed Eyeglass Industry
abstract: He merged eyewear with fashion, turning a quotidian necessity into high style. He rose from poverty to become one of the world’s wealthiest men.

name: Marlin Briscoe
headline: Marlin Briscoe, Pioneering Black Quarterback, Dies at 76
abstract: He became the first Black starting quarterback of the Super Bowl era in the 1960s, but prejudiced thinking by coaches stifled his trajectory at the position.

name: Mary Fuller McChesney
headline: Mary Fuller McChesney, Bay Area Artist and Historian, Dies at 99
abstract: She documented California’s postwar art scene, and created Aztec-inspired sculptures of bears and goddesses.

name: Margaret Keane
headline: Margaret Keane, Painter of Sad-Eyed Waifs, Dies at 94
abstract: Her work was immensely popular and virtually ubiquitous. But until the matter was settled in court, her husband fraudulently claimed credit for it.

name: Deborah James
headline: Deborah James, British Cancer Campaigner and Podcaster, Dies at 40
abstract: She had chronicled her struggle with an incurable bowel tumor with candor and vivacity after the illness was diagnosed more than five years ago.

name: Bernard Stolar
headline: Bernard Stolar, Influential Video Game Executive, Dies at 75
abstract: He worked on the original PlayStation at Sony, then brought Sega’s Dreamcast to the market in the late 1990s.

name: Hershel Williams
profession: Hero in the Battle for Iwo Jima
headline: Hershel Williams, a Hero in the Battle for Iwo Jima, Dies at 98
abstract: He was the last of the 27 Marines and Navy servicemen who received Medals of Honor in the 36-day fight for the Japanese island.

name: Mary Mara
headline: Mary Mara, Actress on ‘ER,’ ‘Dexter’ and ‘Nash Bridges,’ Dies at 61
abstract: She appeared in dozens of movies and television shows in a career of more than 30 years. The police said they believed she died in a drowning accident.

name: Betty Rowland
headline: Betty Rowland, One of Burlesque's Last Queens, Dies at 106
abstract: Known as “the Red Headed Ball of Fire,” she began performing at age 14, became a headliner on two coasts, and outlived most of her peers.

name: Michael Stenger
headline: Michael Stenger, Ousted Senate Sergeant-at-Arms, Dies at 71
abstract: As the chief law enforcement officer of the Senate, he did not seek the National Guard’s help in advance of the Jan. 6 insurrection at the Capitol.

name: John Visentin
headline: John Visentin, Xerox C.E.O., Dies at 59
abstract: He had sought to broaden the company’s offerings beyond photocopying and printing. Xerox said he died of “complications from an ongoing illness.”

name: Sonny Barger
headline: Sonny Barger, Face of the Hells Angels, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Barger cultivated the motorcycle club’s outlaw image and was a pivotal figure in its rise from obscurity into a countercultural phenomenon in the 1960s.

name: Arnold Skolnick
headline: Arnold Skolnick, Whose Poster Embodied Woodstock, Dies at 85
abstract: On short notice, he created the bird-on-a-guitar design that advertised the 1969 festival — and became a symbol of the era.

name: Klaus Nomi
headline: Overlooked No More: Klaus Nomi, Singer With an Otherworldly Persona
abstract: His sound and look influenced everyone from Anohni to Lady Gaga. He also sang backup vocals for David Bowie.

name: Richard Taruskin
headline: Richard Taruskin, Vigorously Polemical Musicologist, Dies at 77
abstract: Author, critic, teacher and public intellectual, he was an unabashed flamethrower who challenged conventional thinking about classical music.

name: H.T. Chen
headline: H.T. Chen, Choreographer of the Asian Experience, Dies at 74
abstract: He merged Eastern and Western influences in his modern dance works, and his dance center was a cultural anchor in New York’s Chinatown.

name: Vladimir Zelenko
headline: Vladimir Zelenko, 48, Dies; Promoted an Unfounded Covid Treatment
abstract: A self-described “simple country doctor,” he won national attention in 2020 when the White House embraced his hydroxychloroquine regimen.

name: Bruce Katz
headline: Bruce Katz, Pioneer of the Walking Shoe, Is Dead at 75
abstract: A third-generation shoe manufacturer, he built Rockport with his father and, before selling it to Reebok, campaigned to turn walking into a fitness movement.

name: Peter Brook
profession: Celebrated Stage Director of Scale and Humanity
headline: Peter Brook, Celebrated Stage Director of Scale and Humanity, Dies at 97
abstract: He was called “the greatest innovator of his generation,” leaving an indelible mark with plays, musicals, opera and a relentless curiosity.

name: James Bardeen
headline: James Bardeen, an Expert on Unraveling Einstein’s Equations, Dies at 83
abstract: A scion of a renowned family of physicists, he helped set the stage for what has been called the golden age of black hole astrophysics.

name: Hunter Reynolds
headline: Hunter Reynolds, Artist Who Dressed Up AIDS, Dies at 62
abstract: After he learned he was H.I.V. positive, he began making art — often performing as his gown-wearing alter ego — that told stories about the condition.

name: Kurt Markus
headline: Kurt Markus, Photographer of Cowboys and Models, Is Dead at 75
abstract: He traveled the world and shot celebrities and fashion luminaries. But he never abandoned his roots in the open spaces of the American West.

name: Clifford L. Alexander
headline: Clifford L. Alexander, Adviser to Presidents, Is Dead at 88
abstract: He was the first Black secretary of the Army — just one of many jobs, both high- and low-profile, that he held over nearly 20 years in government.

name: Zhang Sizhi
headline: Zhang Sizhi, Lawyer Who Defended Chinese Dissidents, Dies at 94
abstract: He shed tears over the challenge of defending clients in a system stacked against them. But even in defeat, admirers said, he set a lasting example.

name: Joe Turkel
headline: Joe Turkel, the Spectral Bartender in ‘The Shining,’ Dies at 94
abstract: Also memorably seen in “Blade Runner,” he was a favorite among directors looking for someone who could bring zealous professionalism to even the smallest role.

name: Willie Lee Morrow
headline: Willie Lee Morrow, Barber Who Popularized the Afro Pick, Dies at 82
abstract: He built an empire around hair care products aimed at African American consumers, including a softener that inspired the Jheri curl.

name: Bradford Freeman
profession: Last of the Band of Brothers
headline: Bradford Freeman, Last of the ‘Band of Brothers,’ Dies at 97
abstract: The exploits of his World War II paratroop company were chronicled in a best-selling book and then in an acclaimed HBO mini-series.

name: Kazuki Takahashi
headline: Kazuki Takahashi, Yu-Gi-Oh! Creator, Dies at 60
abstract: The manga artist won international fame with a story that inspired a trading card game rivaling Pokemon as one of Japan’s most recognizable cultural exports.

name: Ni Kuang
profession: Prolific Hong Kong Novelist and Screenwriter
headline: Ni Kuang, Prolific Hong Kong Novelist and Screenwriter, Dies at 87
abstract: Best known for fantastical thrillers that doubled as political allegories, he also wrote hundreds of martial arts films for Bruce Lee and others.

name: James Caan
headline: James Caan, Actor Who Won Fame in ‘The Godfather,’ Dies at 82
abstract: A Bronx native, he starred in countless movies and TV shows, but was most closely identified with the volatile character Sonny Corleone.

name: Harvey Dinnerstein
headline: Harvey Dinnerstein, Proudly Realistic Painter, Is Dead at 94
abstract: He documented the early days of the civil rights movement in evocative drawings. Later, his paintings examined details of the everyday life around him.

name: Shinzo Abe
headline: Shinzo Abe, Japan’s Longest-Serving Prime Minister, Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Abe was shot on Friday during a campaign event. Before he left office in 2020, he helped pull his country out of economic malaise but fell short of his most cherished goal: to normalize Japan’s military after decades of postwar pacifism.

name: José Eduardo dos Santos
headline: José Eduardo dos Santos, Longtime Angolan Ruler, Dies at 79
abstract: As Angola’s president for 38 years, Mr. dos Santos ended the country’s civil war. He also launched an economic boom, but it mainly benefited his family and friends.

name: Kenward Elmslie
headline: Kenward Elmslie, Poet and Librettist, Dies at 93
abstract: He collaborated on operas with Jack Beeson and Ned Rorem and published numerous poetry books. Late in life, he was victimized by theft.

name: Larry Storch
profession: Comic Actor Best Known for F Troop
headline: Larry Storch, Comic Actor Best Known for ‘F Troop,’ Dies at 99
abstract: His well-honed comic timing, and the mimicry skills he had developed in nightclubs, served him well on one of the sillier sitcoms of the 1960s.

name: Joyce C. Lashof
headline: Joyce C. Lashof, Doctor Who Shattered Glass Ceilings, Dies at 96
abstract: In Illinois, she was the first woman to head a state public health department. She went on to become dean of the School of Public Health at Berkeley.

name: Susie Steiner
profession: Author of Acclaimed British Crime Novels
headline: Susie Steiner, Author of Acclaimed British Crime Novels, Dies at 51
abstract: Her books found a worldwide audience, but while she wrote them she had to contend with the loss of her sight and the diagnosis of a brain tumor.

name: Tony Sirico
headline: Tony Sirico, an Eccentric Gangster on ‘The Sopranos,’ Dies at 79
abstract: A familiar face in Woody Allen movies, he became widely known for his portrayal of Paulie Walnuts on the hit HBO series.

name: Bill J. Allen
profession: Alaska Businessman at the Center of Scandal
headline: Bill J. Allen, Alaska Businessman at the Center of Scandal, Dies at 85
abstract: He was one of the state’s most powerful figures, but his extensive corruption schemes brought him down — and took several politicians with him.

name: Luis Echeverría Alvarez
headline: Luis Echeverría Alvarez, Former President of Mexico, Dies at 100
abstract: He had faced accusations that, as interior secretary, he was responsible for repressing protests before the 1968 Olympics that ended in a massacre.

name: Hank Goldberg
profession: Betting Maven and Sports Radio Star
headline: Hank Goldberg, Betting Maven and Sports Radio Star, Dies at 82
abstract: A New Jersey fan of sports and gambling who became one of the country’s top television handicappers: What are the odds?

name: Mike Brito
headline: Mike Brito, Influential Dodger Scout in Mexico, Dies at 87
abstract: He opened the door to the major leagues for many Mexican players, most notably Fernando Valenzuela, who won the 1981 Rookie of the Year and Cy Young Awards.

name: Francis X. Clines
headline: Francis X. Clines, Lyrical Writer for The Times, Dies at 84
abstract: He brought a literary sensibility to his widely admired work as a reporter, columnist and editorial writer, whether covering the streets of New York or the Troubles of Northern Ireland.

name: Gerald W. McEntee
headline: Gerald W. McEntee, Union Leader With Political Clout, Dies at 87
abstract: He made the American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees an electoral force in a time of Republican hostility to organized labor.

name: Adam Wade
headline: Adam Wade, Network Game Show Pioneer, Is Dead at 87
abstract: As a singer, he had three Top 10 hits in 1961. As an actor, he had a long career in film and on television. As an M.C., he broke a racial barrier.

name: Spider Webb
profession: Tattoo Artist With a Defiant Streak
headline: Spider Webb, Tattoo Artist With a Defiant Streak, Dies at 78
abstract: Part of a generation that brought serious art credentials to tattooing, he campaigned to overturn a ban in New York and helped the form gain acceptance.

name: Cláudio Hummes
headline: Cardinal Cláudio Hummes, Close Ally of Pope Francis, Dies at 87
abstract: An advocate for the poor, he was a force behind the progressive turn taken by many Latin American Catholics in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Monty Norman
headline: Monty Norman, Who Wrote 007’s Memorable Theme, Dies at 94
abstract: He composed the instantly recognizable melody for the first James Bond film, “Dr. No.” It has accompanied the agent on his adventures ever since.

name: John R. Froines
profession: Chemist and Member of the Chicago Seven
headline: John R. Froines, Chemist and Member of the Chicago Seven, Dies at 83
abstract: After his acquittal for inciting a riot at the 1968 Democratic National Convention, he became a leading environmental toxicologist, shaping government safety standards.

name: Ivana Trump
profession: Ex-Wife of Donald Trump and Businesswoman
headline: Ivana Trump, Ex-Wife of Donald Trump and Businesswoman, Dies at 73
abstract: She helped build his real estate empire, though she was better known for being one half of the quintessential 1980s power couple.

name: Jerome M. Eisenberg
profession: Expert on Antiquities Both Real and Fake
headline: Jerome M. Eisenberg, Expert on Antiquities Both Real and Fake, Dies at 92
abstract: He saw himself as a leader in promoting the ethical acquisition of ancient art by museums and collectors, although he also called himself “both an idealist and a hypocrite.”

name: David Dalton
headline: David Dalton, Rock Writer Who Lived the Scene, Dies at 80
abstract: An early writer for Rolling Stone, he traveled in the same circles as the Beatles, Janis Joplin and other stars, witnessing and documenting a time of cultural transformation.

name: Mark Fleischman
headline: Mark Fleischman, the Last Impresario of Studio 54, Dies at 82
abstract: He took over the celebrated Manhattan club in the early 1980s and briefly became the self-described “ringleader” of an all-night circus.

name: Eugenio Scalfari
headline: Eugenio Scalfari, Leading Italian Journalist, Dies at 98
abstract: As a founder of La Repubblica, one of the country’s major newspapers, and later as a columnist, he left a mark on civic life.

name: Jak Knight
profession: Known for the Netflix Series Big Mouth
headline: Jak Knight, Known for the Netflix Series ‘Big Mouth,’ Dies at 28
abstract: Mr. Knight, who had been a successful stand-up comedian for several years, was also a writer for the ABC sitcom “Black-ish.”

name: Lily Safra
headline: Lily Safra, Star-Crossed Socialite and Philanthropist, Dies at 87
abstract: Her life was marked by tragedy, including the bizarre death of her fourth husband, but that did not stop her from giving away millions.

name: David Weiss Halivni
headline: David Weiss Halivni, Controversial Talmudic Scholar, Dies at 94
abstract: He was considered too radical by many Orthodox rabbis and too regressive by many Conservative Jewish leaders. But his work was widely praised.

name: Nikolai Krogius
profession: Adviser in Chess Match of the Century
headline: Nikolai Krogius, Adviser in Chess ‘Match of the Century,’ Dies at 91
abstract: A grandmaster and a sports psychologist, he was part of the support team for the world champion Boris Spassky in his 1972 loss to Bobby Fischer.

name: Gerald Shargel
profession: Criminal Defense Lawyer for the Mob
headline: Gerald Shargel, Criminal Defense Lawyer for the Mob, Dies at 77
abstract: He coupled legal scholarship with courtroom wit to decimate the prosecution’s cases against Mafia bosses.

name: Claes Oldenburg
profession: Pop Artist Made the Everyday Monumental
headline: Claes Oldenburg Dies at 93; Pop Artist Made the Everyday Monumental
abstract: Taking ordinary objects like hamburgers and household items, he sculpted them in unfamiliar, often imposing dimensions — what he called his “Colossal Monuments.”

name: Hobie Billingsley
headline: Hobie Billingsley, Coach of a Diving Dynasty, Dies at 95
abstract: A national champion diver himself, he led Indiana University to glory over 31 years and guided gold medal winners in the Olympics.

name: Ritzi Jacobi
headline: Ritzi Jacobi, Maker of Mind-Bending Textile Art, Dies at 80
abstract: Her monumental wall hangings and soft sculptures incorporated fiber-based materials, like goat hair, as part of a “new tapestry” movement.

name: Ann Shulgin
headline: Ann Shulgin, 91, Who Explored Psychedelics With Her Husband, Dies
abstract: The couple advocated the use of hallucinogens in psychotherapy and documented their experiences with hundreds of drugs in two widely read books.

name: Robert F. Curl Jr.
headline: Robert F. Curl Jr., Nobel Prize Winner in Chemistry, Dies at 88
abstract: He and three others discovered unexpectedly simple carbon molecules called buckyballs (think of a soccer ball), spurring explorations of nanotechnology.

name: Albert Vann
profession: Built a Black Power Base in Brooklyn
headline: Albert Vann, Who Built a Black Power Base in Brooklyn, Dies at 87
abstract: As a legislator for four decades, he led voter registration drives and challenges to redistricting that rattled the political establishment.

name: Sean Kelly
headline: Sean Kelly, Early National Lampoon Troublemaker, Dies at 81
abstract: He helped set the magazine’s irreverent tone with his pitch-perfect parodies. He also wrote lyrics for the Off Broadway Lampoon show “Lemmings.”

name: William Hart
headline: William Hart, Driving Force Behind the Delfonics, Dies at 77
abstract: With hits like “La-La (Means I Love You)” and “Didn’t I (Blow Your Mind This Time),” his group pioneered the soulful Philadelphia sound.

name: Lottie Brunn
headline: Overlooked No More: Lottie Brunn, the ‘Queen of Jugglers’
abstract: Known as the world’s fastest woman juggler, she assisted her brother before launching a three-decade solo career.

name: Werner Reich
headline: Werner Reich, Who Learned Magic in Auschwitz, Dies at 94
abstract: He was 16 when a fellow inmate, a magician, taught him a card trick in the barracks of the extermination camp. He called it a “miracle.”

name: Judith Schiff
headline: Judith Schiff, Who Roamed Yale’s Vast Archive, Dies at 84
abstract: An expert researcher, she helped put together a posthumous autobiography by Charles Lindbergh and ferreted out historical oddities.

name: Ronni Solbert
headline: Ronni Solbert, Children’s Book Illustrator, Dies at 96
abstract: She did the artwork for dozens of books, notably “The Pushcart War,” a parable about overcoming bullies, written by her partner, Jean Merrill.

name: Uwe Seeler
profession: One of Germanys Greatest Soccer Players
headline: Uwe Seeler, One of Germany’s Greatest Soccer Players, Dies at 85
abstract: He led West Germany to the 1966 World Cup, but his teams never won a title. Pele included him on his list of the world’s premier living players.

name: Shonka Dukureh
headline: Shonka Dukureh, Actress Who Sang ‘Hound Dog’ in ‘Elvis,’ Dies at 44
abstract: She made her Hollywood debut as Big Mama Thornton, giving a performance that one castmate called “a spiritual experience.”

name: Patrick J. Michaels
headline: Patrick J. Michaels, Vocal Outlier on Climate Change, Dies at 72
abstract: He thought the conversation around global warming was alarmist, and his scientific credentials made him a go-to expert for those who played down the threat.

name: Taurean Blacque
profession: Actor Best Known for Hill Street Blues
headline: Taurean Blacque, Actor Best Known for ‘Hill Street Blues,’ Dies at 82
abstract: He received an Emmy nomination for his work as Detective Neal Washington, a character he strove to portray as something other than “that hip, jive Black man.”

name: Perry Rubenstein
headline: Perry Rubenstein, Gallerist Convicted of Embezzlement, Dies at 68
abstract: He took his growing art business from Manhattan to Los Angeles, but it soon fell apart. Then, in 2016, he was arrested.

name: Michael Henderson
headline: Michael Henderson, Funk Bassist Turned Crooner, Dies at 71
abstract: He was a sideman with Stevie Wonder and Miles Davis before embarking on a successful second career as a singer of soulful, romantic ballads.

name: Carleton Varney
profession: Interior Designer Known as Mr. Color
headline: Carleton Varney, Interior Designer Known as Mr. Color, Dies at 85
abstract: He was trained by the maximalist decorator Dorothy Draper, who favored bold colors, and he inherited her aversion to the bland and the beige.

name: Diana Kennedy
headline: Diana Kennedy, Authority on Mexican Cooking, Dies at 99
abstract: Her books taught Americans about the regional nature of the cuisine. Also: “There is always someone who wants to know how to clean an iguana, so why not?”

name: Edward Feiner
headline: Edward Feiner, 75, Dies; Revolutionized Look of Federal Buildings
abstract: As the government’s chief architect, he prioritized good design in the construction of hundreds of courthouses and office buildings.

name: Bob Rafelson
headline: Bob Rafelson, Director of ‘Five Easy Pieces,’ Dies at 89
abstract: A central figure in the New Hollywood movement, he was also the co-creator of the TV pop group the Monkees and featured it in a movie, “Head.”

name: Michael R. Long
headline: Michael R. Long, N.Y. Conservative Party Stalwart, Dies at 82
abstract: His endorsement of George E. Pataki in 1994 helped elect the state’s only Republican governor in 50 years.

name: Paul Sorvino
headline: Paul Sorvino, Master of the Mild-Mannered Mobster, Dies at 83
abstract: A would-be singing star, he found success in Hollywood playing a variety of roles, but they were often quiet, dangerous men, like Paulie Cicero in “Goodfellas.”

name: David Trimble
profession: Peace Prize Winner in Ulster Strife
headline: David Trimble, Peace Prize Winner in Ulster Strife, Dies at 77
abstract: A onetime Protestant firebrand, he surprised adversaries when he helped broker peace in Northern Ireland with the Good Friday pact of 1998.

name: David Warner
headline: David Warner, Actor Who Played Villains and More, Dies at 80
abstract: He seemed destined for a major stage career but by the early 1970s was focused on film and TV. His credits included “TRON,” “Titanic” and hundreds more.

name: Tony Dow
profession: Big Brother Wally on Leave It to Beaver
headline: Tony Dow, Big Brother Wally on ‘Leave It to Beaver,’ Dies at 77
abstract: He was later a director, producer and sculptor, but he never shook his association with the sitcom. His death came a day after it was announced erroneously.

name: James Lovelock
profession: Gaia Theory Saw the Earth as Alive
headline: James Lovelock, Whose Gaia Theory Saw the Earth as Alive, Dies at 103
abstract: A British ecologist, he captured imaginations with his hypothesis and was essential to today’s understanding of man-made pollutants and their effect on the climate.

name: Lourdes Grobet
headline: Lourdes Grobet, Photographer of Mexico’s Masked Wrestlers, Dies at 81
abstract: In her innovative career, she found her ultimate subject in lucha libre wrestling: men and women who, to her, were members of an unexplored subculture.

name: Phyo Zeya Thaw
headline: Phyo Zeya Thaw, Burmese Pro-democracy Rapper, 41, Is Executed
abstract: A hip-hop star, he was a democracy activist in Myanmar and then a lawmaker. After a military coup, he joined the resistance and was hanged for it.

name: Bernard Cribbins
headline: Bernard Cribbins, British Actor Known for ‘Doctor Who,’ Is Dead at 93
abstract: Mr. Cribbins’s long career included roles on stage, film and television.

name: Tim Giago
headline: Tim Giago, Native American Newspaperman, Is Dead at 88
abstract: The founder of the first independent American Indian newspaper braved gunshots and firebombs to provide an unvarnished look at life on the reservation.

name: Charlotte Pomerantz
headline: Charlotte Pomerantz, Inventive Children’s Book Author, Dies at 92
abstract: Her imaginative use of words and lively rhymes entertained young readers, sometimes with a subtle message included, drawn from her own life.

name: Stuart Woods
headline: Stuart Woods, Prolific Best-Selling Thriller Author, Dies at 84
abstract: His mysteries featured extravagant characters like Stone Barrington, a libidinous New York lawyer who, like Mr. Woods, hung out at Elaine’s.

name: Larry Josephson
headline: Larry Josephson, Champion of Free-Form Radio, Dies at 83
abstract: His dyspeptic morning show helped make WBAI-FM in New York a vibrant, eccentric, alternative radio haven. “I was the first angry man in morning radio,” he said.

name: Mary Alice
profession: Tony Winner for Her Role in Fences
headline: Mary Alice, Tony Winner for Her Role in ‘Fences,’ Dies at 85
abstract: A former Chicago schoolteacher, she appeared on TV in ‘A Different World’ and ‘I’ll Fly Away,’ winning an Emmy in 1993.

name: Fidel Ramos
headline: Fidel Ramos, Philippine President Who Broke With Marcos, Dies at 94
abstract: Considered a ruthless Marcos henchman,  he was later hailed as a national hero for breaking with the dictator, and went on to preside over an economic boom.

name: Bill Russell
headline: Bill Russell, Who Transformed Pro Basketball, Dies at 88
abstract: A Hall of Famer who led the Celtics to 11 championships, he was “the single most devastating force in the history of the game,” his coach Red Auerbach said.

name: Nichelle Nichols
headline: Nichelle Nichols, Lieutenant Uhura on ‘Star Trek,’ Dies at 89
abstract: She was among the first Black women to have a leading role in a TV series. She later worked with NASA to recruit minorities for the space program.

name: Mick Moloney
profession: Musician and Champion of Irish Culture
headline: Mick Moloney, Musician and Champion of Irish Culture, Dies at 77
abstract: An Irish immigrant to the U.S., he was a recording artist, scholar and concert presenter who also encouraged women to join a male-dominated folk tradition.

name: Ayman al-Zawahri
profession: Ayman al-Zawahri Led a Life of Secrecy and Violence
headline: Killed at 71, Ayman al-Zawahri Led a Life of Secrecy and Violence
abstract: A radicalized physician, he was seen as the intellectual spine of Osama bin Laden’s terrorist organization and ran it after Bin Laden was killed in 2011.

name: Mo Ostin
headline: Mo Ostin, Music Powerhouse Who Put Artists First, Dies at 95
abstract: At the helm of Warner Bros. Records from the 1960s into the ’90s, he worked closely with some of the most successful and influential performers of his era.

name: Bernard Marson
headline: Bernard Marson, a Catalyst for SoHo’s Renaissance, Dies at 91
abstract: An architect and developer, he helped pioneer the neighborhood’s transition from manufacturing into lofts where artists could work and live.

name: Burt Metcalfe
headline: Burt Metcalfe, Who Left His Mark on ‘M*A*S*H,’ Is Dead at 87
abstract: He was the showrunner of the classic Korean War sitcom for its last six seasons, notably casting David Ogden Stiers as the pompous surgeon Winchester.

name: Eli N. Evans
profession: Wrote About Jews in American South
headline: Eli N. Evans, Who Wrote About Jews in American South, Dies at 85
abstract: His book “The Provincials” mixed memoir, travelogue and history to tell the story of a culture that many people never knew existed.

name: Vin Scully
profession: Voice of the Dodgers for 67 Years
headline: Vin Scully, Voice of the Dodgers for 67 Years, Dies at 94
abstract: The team has had many great players since World War II, but it was Mr. Scully, a gifted storyteller and a master of the graceful phrase, who became the enduring face of the franchise.

name: George Bartenieff
headline: George Bartenieff, Fixture of Downtown Theater, Dies at 89
abstract: A veteran actor, he was also a founder of Theater for the New City and Theater Three Collaborative, Manhattan groups known for experimental productions.

name: Richard Tait
profession: Co-Inventor of the Board Game Cranium
headline: Richard Tait, Co-Inventor of the Board Game Cranium, Dies at 58
abstract: His decidedly eclectic board game became a familiar part of American family life in the late 1990s and 2000s.

name: Terry Castro
profession: Proud Outsider in the Jewelry World
headline: Terry Castro, a Proud Outsider in the Jewelry World, Dies at 50
abstract: A self-taught designer, he started out selling necklaces on the streets of New York and battled stereotypes, racial and otherwise, throughout his career.

name: Robert E. Simanek
profession: Korean War Medal of Honor Recipient
headline: Robert E. Simanek, Korean War Medal of Honor Recipient, Dies at 92
abstract: He saved fellow Marines by falling on a live grenade. His death leaves only two surviving veterans of that war to have been honored with the medal.

name: Jennifer Bartlett
headline: Jennifer Bartlett, Conceptual Painter on Vast Scale, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Her landmark work, “Rhapsody,” inspired by New York City subway signs, comprises 987 enameled plates and stretches for 153 feet.

name: Georges Briguet
headline: Georges Briguet, Who Presided Over Le Périgord, Dies at 85
abstract: The owner of a classic French restaurant in Manhattan for a half-century, he welcomed his well-heeled guests by name, offering them a serene urban oasis on the far East Side.

name: Alda Merini
headline: Overlooked No More: Alda Merini, Poet Who Wrote of Life’s Joys and Struggles
abstract: Countless fans have been intrigued by her verses carrying erotic and sacred imagery, and by her life, from her childhood in Milan to her time spent in asylums.

name: Dee Hock
headline: Dee Hock, Credit Card Visionary, Is Dead at 93
abstract: As chief executive of Visa, he transformed a struggling company into a global powerhouse and the world’s leading credit card network.

name: Mary Ellin Barrett
profession: Daughter and Defender of Irving Berlin
headline: Mary Ellin Barrett, Daughter and Defender of Irving Berlin, Dies at 95
abstract: When the great American songwriter’s character came under attack after his death, Ms. Barrett sought to correct the record with a candid but tender memoir.

name: Ronald J. Sider
headline: Ronald J. Sider, 82, Who Urged Evangelicals to Social Action, Dies
abstract: He often bucked the rightward trend among some Christians, and in a popular 1977 book he argued that faith meant more than just personal salvation.

name: Melissa Bank
headline: Melissa Bank, Author Whose ‘Girls’ Guide’ Was a Phenomenon, Dies at 61
abstract: Her story collection “The Girls’ Guide to Hunting and Fishing,” her first book, has been translated into dozens of languages and has sold more than 1.5 million copies.

name: Leon E. Rosenberg
headline: Leon E. Rosenberg, Geneticist Who Wrote of His Depression, Dies at 89
abstract: After years of pioneering research into inherited disorders, mostly in children, he spoke openly about his struggle with mental illness.

name: Albert Woodfox
profession: Survivor of 42 Years in Solitary Confinement
headline: Albert Woodfox, Survivor of 42 Years in Solitary Confinement, Dies at 75
abstract: His term in solitary was perhaps the longest in American history. He described how he kept his sanity, and dignity, in an acclaimed memoir.

name: Sid Jacobson
headline: Sid Jacobson, Comic Book Writer With Range, Dies at 92
abstract: His portfolio included the adventures of Richie Rich and graphic treatments of 9/11 and torture by the C.I.A. He also wrote dozens of songs.

name: Clu Gulager
profession: Rugged Character Actor of Film and TV
headline: Clu Gulager, Rugged Character Actor of Film and TV, Dies at 93
abstract: On TV, he played Billy the Kid on “The Tall Man” and was seen on the long-running “The Virginian.” His movies ranged from “The Killers” to “The Last Picture Show.”

name: Christopher Meyer
profession: Vocal British Envoy to the U.S
headline: Christopher Meyer, Vocal British Envoy to the U.S., Dies at 78
abstract: He served loyally during the 9/11 attacks and Iraq invasion. But in a 2005 memoir, he faulted the “conception and execution” of the Iraq war.

name: David McCullough
headline: David McCullough, Best-Selling Explorer of America’s Past, Dies at 89
abstract: His research — on Adams, Truman and so much more — was deep, his writing was lively, and his narrator’s voice in documentary films was familiar to millions.

name: Bert Fields
headline: Bert Fields, Lawyer to the Hollywood Elite, Dies at 93
abstract: A master dealmaker, he had as clients Madonna, Michael Jackson, Tom Cruise, the Beatles and many others, becoming something of a celebrity himself.

name: Olivia Newton-John
headline: Olivia Newton-John, Pop Singer and ‘Grease’ Star, Dies at 73
abstract: She amassed No. 1 hits, chart-topping albums and four records that sold more than two million copies each. More than anything else, she was likable, even beloved.

name: Issey Miyake
profession: Opened a Door for Japanese Fashion
headline: Issey Miyake, Who Opened a Door for Japanese Fashion, Dies at 84
abstract: The first Japanese designer to show in Paris, he was known for his origami-like designs, creating pleated skirts, dresses and trousers that afforded freedom.

name: Lamont Dozier
headline: Lamont Dozier, Writer of Numerous Motown Hits, Dies at 81
abstract: With the brothers Brian and Eddie Holland, Mr. Dozier wrote dozens of singles that reached the pop or R&B charts, including “You Can’t Hurry Love,” by the Supremes.

name: Judith Durham
profession: Singer of Georgy Girl and Other Hits
headline: Judith Durham, Singer of ‘Georgy Girl’ and Other Hits, Dies at 79
abstract: A classically trained soprano, she became a chart-topping pop star in the 1960s with the folk-based Australian quartet the Seekers.

name: Chase Mishkin
headline: Chase Mishkin, Tony-Winning Producer of ‘Dame Edna,’ Dies at 85
abstract: She was nearly 60 when she began producing shows on Broadway. In 19 years, she had a hand (and her money) in 30 plays and musicals.

name: Raymond Briggs
headline: Raymond Briggs, Who Drew a Wordless ‘Snowman,’ Dies at 88
abstract: An author and illustrator of children’s books sensitive to emotions, he used comic-strip-like panels to explore the joys and struggles of workaday British life.

name: Gary Schroen
headline: Gary Schroen, Who Led the C.I.A. Into Afghanistan, Dies at 80
abstract: Weeks before the troops arrived, he took a small team into the country to prepare for an invasion and begin the hunt for Osama bin Laden.

name: Kamoya Kimeu
headline: Kamoya Kimeu, Fossil-Hunting ‘Legend’ in East Africa, Is Dead
abstract: Working closely with the Leakey family in Kenya, he discovered many of the bones that rewrote how we understand human evolution.

name: Paul Coker
profession: Cartoonist at Mad for Almost Six Decades
headline: Paul Coker, Cartoonist at Mad for Almost Six Decades, Dies at 93
abstract: The artist behind the magazine’s long-running feature “Horrifying Cliches,” he also created, for TV, the look of Frosty the Snowman and other animated characters.

name: Roger E. Mosley
headline: Roger E. Mosley, Actor Best Known for ‘Magnum, P.I.,’ Dies at 83
abstract: He played Leadbelly and Sonny Liston on the big screen. But his most high-profile role was a rugged, wry Vietnam War veteran opposite Tom Selleck on TV.

name: Jean-Jacques Sempé
headline: Jean-Jacques Sempé, Cartoonist of Droll Whimsy, Dies at 89
abstract: Beloved in France and popular around the world, he drew more than 100 covers for The New Yorker in an association that began in 1978.

name: Anne Heche
headline: Anne Heche, Actress Known for ’90s Film Roles, Dies at 53
abstract: Ms. Heche, who won a Daytime Emmy early in her career and whose films included “Donnie Brasco” and “Wag the Dog,” had been critically injured in a car crash.

name: Bill Pitman
headline: Bill Pitman, Revered Studio Guitarist, Is Dead at 102
abstract: As a versatile member of the loose association of musicians known as the Wrecking Crew, he was heard on many of the biggest pop and rock hits of the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Jan Longone
headline: Jan Longone, Influential Scholar of Food History, Dies at 89
abstract: The cookbook collection that began in the basement of her home became the Janice Bluestein Longone Culinary Archive at the University of Michigan.

name: Elana Dykewomon
headline: Elana Dykewomon, Author Who Explored Lesbian Lives, Dies at 72
abstract: In a five-decade career that began with the coming-of-age novel “Riverfinger Women,” she was outspoken in her fiction, her poetry and her life.

name: Zofia Posmysz
profession: Wrote of Life in Concentration Camps
headline: Zofia Posmysz, Who Wrote of Life in Concentration Camps, Dies at 98
abstract: Her radio play, “The Passenger in Cabin 45,” became a novel that was translated into 15 languages, a movie and an acclaimed opera.

name: Pete Carril
headline: Pete Carril, Princeton’s Textbook Basketball Coach, Dies at 92
abstract: Without athletic scholarships, he made outgunned teams winners by keeping them moving and unnerving opponents, leading to one of the biggest upsets in college basketball.

name: John L. Eastman
headline: John L. Eastman, McCartney’s Lawyer in Beatles’ Strife, Dies at 83
abstract: An entertainment attorney for high-profile clients, he was central to a battle over control of the Beatles’ business empire in the last days of the band.

name: Nicholas Evans
headline: Nicholas Evans, Author of ‘The Horse Whisperer,’ Dies at 72
abstract: He was a first-time novelist whose tale of a manly vocation and family trauma broke publishing and then movie rights records when Robert Redford bought them.

name: Frederick Buechner
headline: Frederick Buechner, Novelist With a Religious Slant, Dies at 96
abstract: He drew on his theological credentials in essays and memoirs, and his fiction, full of colorful characters, was admired for its elegance, wit and depth.

name: Wolfgang Petersen
headline: Wolfgang Petersen, Director of ‘Das Boot,’ Is Dead at 81
abstract: He made it big in Hollywood, but he’s best remembered for a harrowing, Oscar-nominated German film set inside a U-boat in World War II.

name: Carl Kabat
profession: Peace Activist and Fool for Christ
headline: Rev. Carl Kabat, Peace Activist and ‘Fool for Christ,’ Dies at 88
abstract: An associate of the Berrigan brothers, he spent nearly two decades in prison for his relentless protesting, often in a clown suit, against nuclear arms.

name: Cecile Pineda
profession: Latina Writer Known for a Novel of Identity
headline: Cecile Pineda, Latina Writer Known for a Novel of Identity, Dies at 89
abstract: She became a novelist after a theater career and won acclaim with her debut, “Face,” the story of a man who rebuilds his own face after a disfiguring accident.

name: Raymond Damadian
profession: Creator of the First M.R.I. Scanner
headline: Raymond Damadian, Creator of the First M.R.I. Scanner, Dies at 86
abstract: Incensed when two others won the Nobel Prize for the science behind the invention, he took out a newspaper ad that called his exclusion a “shameful wrong that must be righted.”

name: Anshu Jain
profession: Took Deutsche Bank to Wall Street
headline: Anshu Jain, Who Took Deutsche Bank to Wall Street, Dies at 59
abstract: As co-chief executive, he helped remake the German company into an investment banking power, but stepped down after the complex activities he pushed caused regulatory problems.

name: Hanae Mori
headline: Hanae Mori, Japanese Couturier Who Melded East-West Styles, Dies at 96
abstract: From a Tokyo dressmaking shop catering to the wives of American G.I.s, she climbed to global fame as the first Asian woman to join the ranks of French haute couture.

name: Norah Vincent
headline: Norah Vincent, Who Chronicled Passing as a Man, Is Dead at 53
abstract: Her best-selling 2006 book about that experience, “Self-Made Man,” made her a media darling. But it cost her psychologically.

name: Andrew J. Maloney
headline: Andrew J. Maloney, Prosecutor Who Took Down John Gotti, Dies at 90
abstract: A street-smart U.S. attorney, he won a conviction against the Mafia boss after several previous efforts failed.

name: Abdul Wadud
headline: Abdul Wadud, Cellist Who Crossed Musical Boundaries, Dies at 75
abstract: He performed with classical ensembles, but he was best known for his work with cutting-edge composers and improvisers like Anthony Davis and Julius Hemphill.

name: Regina Jonas
headline: Overlooked No More: Regina Jonas, Upon Whose Shoulders ‘All Female Rabbis Stand’
abstract: Jonas was officially ordained as a rabbi in Germany in 1935, just as conditions were worsening for Jews. She was killed at Auschwitz when she was 42.

name: Nafis Sadik
profession: U.N. Official and Proud Champion of Choice
headline: Nafis Sadik, U.N. Official and ‘Proud Champion of Choice,’ Dies at 92
abstract: An obstetrician, she led a groundbreaking effort to put women’s rights to control all aspects of their lives at the heart of the global population debate.

name: Dmitri Vrubel
profession: Planted a Kiss on the Berlin Wall
headline: Dmitri Vrubel, Who Planted a Kiss on the Berlin Wall, Dies at 62
abstract: A Russian-born painter, he created a mural of the Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev smooching the East German leader Erich Honecker — and with it a tourist attraction.

name: Gene LeBell
profession: Judo Champion, Wrestler and Star Stuntman
headline: Gene LeBell, 89, Judo Champion, Wrestler and Star Stuntman, Dies
abstract: A tough guy who got beaten up by the likes of John Wayne, he had a bottom-line view of his job: “The more you get hit in the nose, the richer you are.”

name: Ann McGuiness
headline: Ann McGuiness, Major Fund-Raiser for Women’s Health, Dies at 65
abstract: At Planned Parenthood and other organizations, she worked behind the scenes for reproductive rights and related causes.

name: Vadim V. Bakatin
headline: Vadim V. Bakatin, the Last Chairman of the K.G.B., Dies at 84
abstract: He led the spy agency for only a few months, promising to reduce its size and rein in its excesses. After he left, it bounced back under a new name.

name: Latisha Chong
headline: Latisha Chong, Hair Stylist Who Helped Change Fashion, Dies at 32
abstract: In work seen, among other places, on the cover of Vogue, she was part of a vanguard of Black talent that altered an industry and expanded the canon of beauty.

name: Tom Weiskopf
profession: British Open Winner and Golf Course Designer
headline: Tom Weiskopf, British Open Winner and Golf Course Designer, Dies at 79
abstract: A four-time runner-up at the Masters, he won 16 PGA Tour events starting in the late 1960s and later became a television commentator.

name: Donald Jonas
headline: Donald Jonas, Retail Magnate Who Sold Art to Help Nurses, Dies at 92
abstract: A founder of the Lechters housewares chain, he and his wife focused their philanthropy on a profession they felt had been largely ignored.

name: David A. Kay
profession: Searched for Nuclear Weapons in Iraq
headline: David A. Kay, Who Searched for Nuclear Weapons in Iraq, Dies at 82
abstract: He scoured the country for weapons of mass destruction after the U.S. invasion in 2003, but his search proved fruitless.

name: Archbishop Rembert Weakland
headline: Archbishop Rembert Weakland, Critic of Vatican Orthodoxy, Dies at 95
abstract: In his long career, he was an intellectual touchstone for progressive Catholic reformers. But he resigned after the disclosure of a long-ago love affair.

name: Julian Robertson
profession: Brought Hedge Funds Into the Mainstream
headline: Julian Robertson, 90, Dies; Brought Hedge Funds Into the Mainstream
abstract: His driving insight was that one could make money just as easily by betting that a company’s stock would fall as by betting that it would rise.

name: Joanne Koch
headline: Joanne Koch, Who Led Lincoln Center’s Film Society, Dies at 92
abstract: A lifelong film lover, she stood up to protesters, and to federal and church authorities, to bring challenging movies to the masses.

name: Tim Page
profession: Gonzo Photographer of the Vietnam War
headline: Tim Page, Gonzo Photographer of the Vietnam War, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Fearless and free-spirited, he pushed the boundaries of life and photography, recording intimate images of combat that helped shift the course of the war.

name: Len Dawson
profession: Took Kansas City to a Championship
headline: Len Dawson, Who Took Kansas City to a Championship, Dies at 87
abstract: After seeing little action for five seasons, he emerged as a star of the fledgling A.F.L. and one of the best quarterbacks in pro football.

name: Dorli Rainey
profession: Unlikely Face of the Occupy Movement
headline: Dorli Rainey, Unlikely Face of the Occupy Movement, Dies at 95
abstract: A picture taken of Ms. Rainey, who called herself an “old lady in combat boots,” after she was doused with pepper spray at a protest went viral.

name: Jerry Allison
headline: Jerry Allison, Who Played Drums With Buddy Holly, Dies at 82
abstract: An original Cricket, he was also a co-writer of two signature Holly songs, “That’ll Be the Day” and “Peggy Sue.”

name: Gary Gaines
profession: Coach of Friday Night Lights Fame
headline: Gary Gaines, Coach of ‘Friday Night Lights’ Fame, Dies at 73
abstract: He coached the Permian High School Panthers in Odessa, Texas, for four seasons in the 1980s, including the one that became the subject of a best-selling book.

name: Howard Slusher
profession: Sports Agent Known for His Toughness
headline: Howard Slusher, Sports Agent Known for His Toughness, Dies at 85
abstract: For years, his hardball tactics, including holding out players for as long as a year to win bigger contracts, made him the enemy of team owners.

name: Morgan Taylor
headline: Morgan Taylor, Inventive Children’s Performer, Dies at 52
abstract: His popular character Gustafer Yellowgold was aimed at youngsters and, more generally, “people who enjoy humor and absurdity and good pop music.”

name: E. Bryant Crutchfield
profession: Gave the World the Trapper Keeper
headline: E. Bryant Crutchfield, 85, Dies; Gave the World the Trapper Keeper
abstract: His ability to blend the fun and the functional with the binder he invented brought order to the chaos of grade-school life in the 1980s and ’90s.

name: Creed Taylor
headline: Creed Taylor, Producer Who Shaped Jazz for Decades, Dies at 93
abstract: He made scores of albums with artists who were well known and others who soon would be. He also founded two important record labels.

name: Howard Rosenthal
headline: Howard Rosenthal, Who Quantified Partisanship in Congress, Dies at 83
abstract: He took part in studies that found the widening ideological divide to be the largest since post-Civil War Reconstruction.

name: Steven Hoffenberg
headline: Steven Hoffenberg, Debt Baron Who Ran a Vast Fraud, Dies at 77
abstract: A onetime business associate of Jeffrey Epstein who briefly controlled The New York Post, he spent 18 years in prison for a $460 million Ponzi scheme.

name: Joe E. Tata
profession: Peach Pit Owner in Beverly Hills
headline: Joe E. Tata, Peach Pit Owner in ‘Beverly Hills, 90210,’ Dies at 85
abstract: As Nat Bussichio, Mr. Tata doled out fatherly advice to the students who frequented his diner on the hit series, which ran for 10 seasons on Fox.

name: Sy Johnson
headline: Sy Johnson, Arranger Who Worked Closely With Mingus, Dies at 92
abstract: A jazz Renaissance man, he arranged many of the bassist’s later works and also wrote reviews, took photographs and composed his own music.

name: Virginia Patton Moss
headline: Virginia Patton Moss, ‘It’s a Wonderful Life’ Actress, Dies at 97
abstract: The last surviving adult member of the film’s cast, she played the sister-in-law to James Stewart’s George Bailey. Three years later, she quit Hollywood.

name: Joey DeFrancesco
profession: Reigning King of the Jazz Organ
headline: Joey DeFrancesco, Reigning King of the Jazz Organ, Dies at 51
abstract: A prodigy whose playing had drawn raves since he was a teenager, he helped bring the Hammond B3 back into the jazz lineup.

name: Rick Reed
profession: G.O.P. Adman of Swift Boat Campaign
headline: Rick Reed, G.O.P. Adman of ‘Swift Boat’ Campaign, Dies at 69
abstract: In helping to create a series of ads attacking the Democratic presidential candidate John Kerry’s military record, he added a new term to the political lexicon.

name: Jaimie Branch
headline: Jaimie Branch, Trumpeter Who Crossed Genre Lines, Dies at 39
abstract: One of the most dynamic trumpet players in contemporary music, she forged a direct emotional, and even spiritual, connection with her listeners.

name: Carl Croneberg
headline: Carl Croneberg, Explorer of Deaf Culture, Dies at 92
abstract: He helped write the first comprehensive dictionary of American Sign Language and later identified the deaf as a part of society worth examining.

name: Uma Pemmaraju
headline: Uma Pemmaraju, an Original Fox News Channel Anchor, Dies at 64
abstract: She convinced her Indian parents to allow her to pursue journalism as a career, then went on to win three Emmy Awards.

name: Mikhail S. Gorbachev
headline: Mikhail S. Gorbachev, Reformist Soviet Leader, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Adopting principles of glasnost and perestroika, he weighed the legacy of seven decades of Communist rule and set a new course, presiding over the end of the Cold War and the dissolution of the U.S.S.R.

name: Ruby C. Williams
profession: Folk Artist With a Produce Stand
headline: Ruby C. Williams, Folk Artist With a Produce Stand, Dies at 94
abstract: Her colorful paintings started out as advertisements for her farm stand in Florida. Before long, her works found their way to art galleries.

name: Roland Mesnier
headline: Roland Mesnier, Pastry Chef to Five Presidents, Dies at 78
abstract: French born and French trained, he served up inventive and ambrosial desserts in the White House for more than two decades.

name: Robert Kime
profession: Decorator for Nobility and Other Notables
headline: Robert Kime, Decorator for Nobility and Other Notables, Dies at 76
abstract: A celebrated antiques lover with an understated, old-guard approach, his clients included Prince Charles and Andrew Lloyd Webber.

name: Esther Cooper Jackson
headline: Esther Cooper Jackson, Civil Rights Pioneer, Dies at 105
abstract: A feminist and a self-proclaimed revolutionary, she was in the forefront of the fledgling movement for economic and political equality in the 1940s.

name: Charlbi Dean
profession: Star of Top Winner at Cannes
headline: Charlbi Dean, Star of Top Winner at Cannes, Dies at 32
abstract: A South African-born actress and model, she had a breakout role in the satirical “Triangle of Sadness,” due in theaters in the fall.

name: Robert LuPone
headline: Robert LuPone, Actor Who Became a Behind-the-Scenes Force, Dies at 76
abstract: After playing a critical Broadway role in “A Chorus Line,” he helped start the vibrant Off Broadway MCC Theater. TV watchers knew him from “The Sopranos” and “Law and Order.”

name: Amy Stechler
headline: Amy Stechler, Documentarian Who Helped Define a Style, Dies at 67
abstract: She worked on early projects at Florentine Films, where Ken Burns, her husband for a time, would find fame with “The Civil War.”

name: Vera Menchik
headline: Overlooked No More: Vera Menchik, First Women’s Chess Champion
abstract: As the only woman in a tournament, she was often greeted with skepticism. She once responded by saying that she looked forward “to drinking some men’s blood.”

name: Barbara Ehrenreich
headline: Barbara Ehrenreich, Explorer of Prosperity’s Dark Side, Dies at 81
abstract: Her book “Nickel and Dimed,” an undercover account of the indignities of being a low-wage worker in the United States, is considered a classic in social justice literature.

name: Kazuo Inamori
headline: Kazuo Inamori, Major Industrialist in Postwar Japan, Dies at 90
abstract: Founding two giant companies, he helped turn his country into an economic giant while encouraging employees to approach work with an almost spiritual devotion.

name: Richard Roat
headline: Richard Roat, Seen on ‘Cheers,’ ‘Friends’ and ‘Seinfeld,’ Dies at 89
abstract: A familiar TV face for years, he appeared on many of the most popular prime-time shows of recent decades.

name: Archie Roach
profession: Lived and Sang the Aboriginal Blues
headline: Archie Roach, Who Lived and Sang the Aboriginal Blues, Dies at 66
abstract: His song “Took the Children Away,” inspired by his childhood, shook Australians into confronting a grim era when their government tore apart Aboriginal families.

name: Earnie Shavers
headline: Earnie Shavers, Hard-Punching Heavyweight, Is Dead at 78
abstract: He won 68 bouts by knockout and fought some of the biggest names in boxing. He lasted 15 rounds against Muhammad Ali. But he never won a championship.

name: Stanley Turkel
profession: Manager and Avid Historian of Hotels
headline: Stanley Turkel, Manager and Avid Historian of Hotels, Dies at 96
abstract: A hotelier, a history maven and a New York civic activist, he chronicled hotels in extraordinary detail both in books and on a blog.

name: Marilyn Loden
headline: Marilyn Loden, Who Championed a Feminist Metaphor, Dies at 76
abstract: She was asked to speak at a conference in 1978 about barriers faced by women in the workplace. She noted a barrier she called “the glass ceiling.”

name: Charlie Finch
profession: Caustic Chronicler of New Yorks Art Scene
headline: Charlie Finch, Caustic Chronicler of New York’s Art Scene, Dies at 69
abstract: He exposed what he saw as pretension and bad art with passion and, at times, viciousness, winning fans but offending many.

name: Sterling Lord
headline: Sterling Lord, Premier Literary Agent, Is Dead at 102
abstract: The list of well-known writers he represented is long. But his success began with an unknown named Jack Kerouac and his hard-to-sell novel “On the Road.”

name: Moon Landrieu
headline: Moon Landrieu, 92, Dies; New Orleans Mayor Championed Integration
abstract: He rose in local politics in the 1960s and ’70s by nurturing crosscultural connections, even as many other Southern leaders of his era exploited racial division.

name: Frank Drake
profession: Led Search for Life on Other Planets
headline: Frank Drake, Who Led Search for Life on Other Planets, Dies at 92
abstract: He was convinced that human beings would eventually connect with extraterrestrials, and he inspired others to share that belief.

name: Peter Straub
headline: Peter Straub, Literary Master of the Supernatural, Dies at 79
abstract: A fan of Henry James and John Ashbery, he brought a poet’s sensibility to stories about ghosts, demons and other things that go bump in the night.

name: Ronald Glasser
profession: Bard of the Vietnam War Wounded
headline: Dr. Ronald Glasser, Bard of the Vietnam War Wounded, Dies at 83
abstract: His “365 Days” offered unvarnished, vivid sketches of soldiers injured in the war. He said it was a book he felt compelled to write.

name: Don Gehrmann
profession: Victory in a Mile Took 314 Days
headline: Don Gehrmann, Whose Victory in a Mile Took 314 Days, Dies at 94
abstract: After a dead-heat finish in the 1950 Wanamaker Mile in New York and a series of yes-no-yes rulings, he was finally declared the winner almost a year later.

name: Anne Garrels
headline: Anne Garrels, Fearless NPR Correspondent, Dies at 71
abstract: She reported on conflicts around the world and for a time was the only American broadcast journalist reporting from Baghdad during the U.S. “shock and awe” bombing campaign in 2003.

name: Elizabeth II
headline: Queen Elizabeth II Dies at 96; Was Britain’s Longest-Reigning Monarch
abstract: She ruled for seven decades, unshakably committed to the rituals of her role amid epic social and economic change and family scandal.

name: Elizabeth Bailey
headline: Elizabeth Bailey, Who Helped Deregulate Airlines, Dies at 83
abstract: In a career full of firsts, she was the first woman to serve on the Civil Aeronautics Board as well as a distinguished economist and academic.

name: Kurt Gottfried
profession: Physicist and Foe of Nuclear Weapons
headline: Kurt Gottfried, Physicist and Foe of Nuclear Weapons, Dies at 93
abstract: As a founder of the Union of Concerned Scientists, he defended Soviet dissidents and advocated higher standards in government research.

name: Joseph Hazelwood
headline: Joseph Hazelwood, Captain of the Exxon Valdez, Is Dead at 75
abstract: The tanker spilled millions of gallons of oil when it ran aground, causing one of the nation’s worst environmental disasters. He accepted responsibility but was demonized.

name: Tina Ramirez
profession: Founder of a Leading Hispanic Dance Troupe
headline: Tina Ramirez, Founder of a Leading Hispanic Dance Troupe, Dies at 92
abstract: Her company, Ballet Hispánico, performed for audiences across the United States and beyond. It also trained countless dancers.

name: Thomas Carney
headline: Thomas Carney, Crusty Bartender at Elaine’s, Dies at 82
abstract: Cracking wise, keeping tabs and keeping order, the head barman of New York’s famous saloon was a supporting character in one of the city’s longest-running shows.

name: Lars Vogt
headline: Lars Vogt, Acclaimed Pianist and Conductor, Is Dead at 51
abstract: Piano technique for Mr. Vogt was a means to expression, not an end in itself. He avoided repertoire that called for mere virtuosity.

name: Sheila Tobias
headline: Sheila Tobias, Who Defined ‘Math Anxiety,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Feeling jittery about math — and altogether avoiding it — “is a serious handicap” that often affected women, she wrote in Ms. magazine in 1976, followed by a book on the subject.

name: Marc Lewitinn
headline: Marc Lewitinn, Covid Patient, Dies at 76 After 850 Days on a Ventilator
abstract: While no definitive statistics exist, doctors say Mr. Lewitinn, a retired Manhattan store owner, likely remained on the device longer than any other Covid patient.

name: Marsha Hunt
headline: Marsha Hunt, Actress Turned Activist, Is Dead at 104
abstract: She seemed well on her way to stardom until her career was derailed by the Hollywood blacklist. She then turned her attention to social causes.

name: Mable John
profession: Soul Singer With a Star-Studded Résumé
headline: Mable John, Soul Singer With a Star-Studded Résumé, Dies at 91
abstract: She was one of the first female acts signed to Motown, and her career later intersected with Isaac Hayes and Ray Charles. But she eventually heeded a higher calling.

name: James Stewart Polshek
headline: James Stewart Polshek, Quiet Giant of Modern Architecture, Dies at 92
abstract: He took a sensitive, socially conscious approach to projects including the Clinton library and the renovated entrance to the Brooklyn Museum.

name: Diane Noomin
profession: Gave Underground Comics a Feminist Voice
headline: Diane Noomin, 75, Is Dead; Gave Underground Comics a Feminist Voice
abstract: Her best-known creation was a sendup of a certain kind of female stock character. But Ms. Noomin rendered her with compassion, and used her to tell important stories.

name: Gwendolyn Midlo Hall
headline: Gwendolyn Midlo Hall, 93, Dies; Created Database of Enslaved People
abstract: A historian of colonial-era Louisiana, she dug deep into the archives to transform our understanding of the roots of American culture.

name: William Klein
profession: Photographed the Energy of City Life
headline: William Klein, Who Photographed the Energy of City Life, Dies at 96
abstract: He built his reputation with dreamlike images of New York, Rome, Moscow and Tokyo and cast a satirical eye on fashion in a decade of work for Vogue.

name: Javier Marías
profession: to Many the Greatest Living Spanish Novelist
headline: Javier Marías, to Many the Greatest Living Spanish Novelist, Dies at 70
abstract: A regular nominee for the Nobel, his books were as popular as they were lauded, filled with themes of mystery, betrayal and the moral weight of the past.

name: Ramsey Lewis
headline: Ramsey Lewis, Jazz Pianist Who Became a Pop Star, Dies at 87
abstract: His 1965 recording of “The ‘In’ Crowd” brought him to a place few jazz musicians reached in that era: the Top 10.

name: Jean-Luc Godard
profession: Bold Director Shaped French New Wave
headline: Jean-Luc Godard, 91, Is Dead; Bold Director Shaped French New Wave
abstract: The Franco-Swiss filmmaker and provocateur radically rethought motion pictures and left a lasting influence on the medium.

name: Susan L. Solomon
headline: Susan L. Solomon, Crusader for Stem Cell Research, Dies at 71
abstract: Vexed by lags in producing cures for diabetes and cancer, she helped raise $400 million to start a foundation that has made medical breakthroughs.

name: Ken Starr
headline: Ken Starr, Independent Counsel in Clinton Investigation, Dies at 76
abstract: Mr. Starr’s investigation into President Clinton’s affair with a former White House intern propelled issues of sex and morality to the center of American life for more than a year.

name: Irene Papas
headline: Irene Papas, Actress in ‘Zorba,’ ‘Z’ and Greek Tragedies, Is Dead at 96
abstract: She was best known for commanding movie roles in the 1960s but received the greatest plaudits for playing heroines of the ancient stage.

name: Rommy Hunt Revson
headline: Rommy Hunt Revson, Creator of the Scrunchie, Dies at 78
abstract: A former nightclub singer, she developed the simple ornamental hair tie that quickly became a ubiquitous accessory.

name: Lily Renée Phillips
headline: Lily Renée Phillips, Pioneering Comic Book Artist, Dies at 101
abstract: A refugee from Nazi-annexed Austria, she started a new life in New York drawing powerful, glamorous heroines and broke barriers in a male-dominated field.

name: Melvin Sokolsky
headline: Melvin Sokolsky, Surrealist Fashion Photographer, Dies at 88
abstract: Models flew over Paris or floated in a bubble in his arresting images, seen in Harper’s Bazaar and other fashion bibles in the experimental ’60s.

name: Art Rosenbaum
profession: Painter and Preserver of Folk Music
headline: Art Rosenbaum, Painter and Preserver of Folk Music, Dies at 83
abstract: As an artist and exponent of American traditional songs, he sought to blur the lines between outsider and insider art.

name: Paul T. Kwami
headline: Paul T. Kwami, Fisk Jubilee Singers’ Longtime Director, Dies at 70
abstract: He took the storied Black musical group to new heights, including its first Grammy win and a National Medal of Arts.

name: Fred Franzia
profession: Upended Wine Industry With Two-Buck Chuck
headline: Fred Franzia, 79, Dies; Upended Wine Industry With Two-Buck Chuck
abstract: An unorthodox businessman, he took on the wine industry and its high markups, selling wine at prices many families could afford every day.

name: Earl J. Silbert
headline: Earl J. Silbert, Lead Prosecutor of Watergate Break-In, Dies at 86
abstract: He worked to secure several convictions, making early inroads in the investigation of a scandal that would bring down a president.

name: Sylvia Rexach
headline: Overlooked No More: Sylvia Rexach, Puerto Rican Singer and Composer
abstract: She was especially known for reinventing boleros — songs of stringent, abiding love — amid Puerto Rico’s sexist and militaristic society in the mid-20th century.

name: Lowry Mays
headline: Lowry Mays, Who Revolutionized the Radio Industry, Dies at 87
abstract: He built his company, Clear Channel Communications, from a single struggling station into one of the world’s biggest media empires.

name: Jorja Fleezanis
headline: Jorja Fleezanis, Violinist and Pioneering Concertmaster, Dies at 70
abstract: “Being a concertmaster is terribly demanding,” she once said, “but women can handle the job as well as men can. I know that.”

name: Herbert Kohler
headline: Herbert Kohler, Plumbing Mogul Who Created a Golf Mecca, Dies at 83
abstract: The billionaire chief of a family company known for its bathtubs, toilets and faucets, he brought championship play to a tiny Wisconsin town.

name: Henry Silva
headline: Henry Silva, Actor Who Specialized in Menace, Dies at 95
abstract: He was forever cast as a thug, a hit man or some other nefarious character. But he took pride in his ability to play each bad guy differently.

name: Maximilian Lerner
profession: Espionage Skills Helped Win a War
headline: Maximilian Lerner, Whose Espionage Skills Helped Win a War, Dies at 98
abstract: An Austrian immigrant, he was one of the so-called Ritchie Boys, who were trained at a secret Army intelligence camp to serve in World War II.

name: Kevin M. Cahill
profession: Tropical Disease Expert With a Political Bent
headline: Kevin M. Cahill, 86, Dies; Tropical Disease Expert With a Political Bent
abstract: He treated celebrities, advised a governor and saved an Irish historical society. But he died under a cloud of sexual assault allegations.

name: Virginia Dwan
profession: Behind-the-Scenes Force in the Art World
headline: Virginia Dwan, Behind-the-Scenes Force in the Art World, Dies at 90
abstract: At her galleries and with her financial resources, she supported artists working on art’s frontiers and later donated works to museum collections.

name: Alain Tanner
profession: Leading Director in Swiss New Wave
headline: Alain Tanner, Leading Director in Swiss New Wave, Dies at 92
abstract: With his brainy works of neorealism, he made films that helped establish Switzerland as a film center in the 1970s.

name: Valery Polyakov
profession: Took the Longest Journey in Space
headline: Valery Polyakov, Who Took the Longest Journey in Space, Dies at 80
abstract: Seeking to demonstrate the safety of long space missions, he worked out on his trip and returned 437 days later looking “like he could wrestle a bear,” one astronaut said.

name: Maury Wills
headline: Maury Wills, Master of the Stolen Base, Is Dead at 89
abstract: His speed (and his bat) helped the Los Angeles Dodgers win four pennants and three championships. He was voted the National League’s M.V.P. in 1962.

name: Arnold Tucker
headline: Arnold Tucker, 95, Celebrated but Overshadowed Quarterback, Is Dead
abstract: Though he helped lead Army to three national titles, he was eclipsed by two storied running backs, and his death in 2019 was largely overlooked.

name: Jack Charles
headline: Jack Charles, Grandfather of Aboriginal Theater, Dies at 79
abstract: One of Australia’s leading Indigenous actors, he had a resonant voice, a charismatic personality and a troubled personal life that often landed him in jail.

name: John W. O’Malley
headline: John W. O’Malley, Leading Catholic Historian, Dies at 95
abstract: He wrote groundbreaking histories of the Second Vatican Council, the late medieval church and the Jesuits, of which he was a member.

name: John O’Malley
headline: John O’Malley, Bronx Detective and Federal Investigator, Dies at 73
abstract: As a detective with the N.Y.P.D., he helped prosecute violent crimes under federal law. At the U.S. attorney’s office, he was involved in high-profile exonerations.

name: John Train
profession: Paris Review Co-Founder and Cold War Operative
headline: John Train, Paris Review Co-Founder and Cold War Operative, Dies at 94
abstract: His career, ranging from literature to finance to war, and from France to Afghanistan, seemed to cover every interest and issue of his exalted social class.

name: Allan M. Siegal
headline: Allan M. Siegal, Influential Watchdog Inside The Times, Dies at 82
abstract: As a top editor who was both feared and revered at the newspaper for decades, he left a deep imprint as its arbiter of language, taste, tone and ethics.

name: Saul Kripke
headline: Saul Kripke, Philosopher Who Found Truths in Semantics, Dies at 81
abstract: A leading 20th-century thinker, he published a landmark work at 32. Known for lecturing extemporaneously without notes, he dazzled colleagues with the breadth of his ruminations.

name: Maarten Schmidt
profession: First Astronomer to Identify a Quasar
headline: Maarten Schmidt, First Astronomer to Identify a Quasar, Dies at 92
abstract: His 1963 breakthrough revealed one of the furthest objects from Earth and opened new questions about the evolution of the universe.

name: Hilary Mantel
headline: Hilary Mantel, Prize-Winning Author of Historical Fiction, Dies at 70
abstract: The two-time Booker Prize-winning author was known for “Wolf Hall” and two other novels based on the life of Thomas Cromwell.

name: Newton Harrison
headline: Newton Harrison, a Founder of the Eco-Art Movement, Dies at 89
abstract: He and his wife produced work that blended marine biology, agriculture, urban planning and activism and that tackled, early on, the effects of climate change.

name: Irwin Glusker
profession: Gave American Heritage Its Distinctive Look
headline: Irwin Glusker, 98, Dies; Gave American Heritage Its Distinctive Look
abstract: A veteran art director, he was best known for his work at the lavish magazine of U.S. history that became a fixture in dens across the country.

name: Ilse Nathan
headline: Ilse Nathan and Ruth Siegler, Sisters and Survivors Together, Die 11 Days Apart
abstract: They stood by each other at Birkenau, married other Holocaust survivors, lived near each other in Alabama and remained close into their 90s.

name: Ruth Siegler
headline: Ilse Nathan and Ruth Siegler, Sisters and Survivors Together, Die 11 Days Apart
abstract: They stood by each other at Birkenau, married other Holocaust survivors, lived near each other in Alabama and remained close into their 90s.

name: Donald Blinken
headline: Donald Blinken, Ambassador, Financier and Art Patron, Dies at 96
abstract: He co-founded a venture capital firm, championed Mark Rothko, served in Hungary during a pivotal period and raised a future U.S. secretary of state.

name: Louise Fletcher
profession: Oscar Winner for One Flew Over the Cuckoos Nest
headline: Louise Fletcher, 88, Dies; Oscar Winner for ‘One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest’
abstract: She was largely unknown to the public when she was cast as what the American Film Institute called one of cinema’s most memorable villains.

name: Pharoah Sanders
profession: Saxophone Was a Force of Nature
headline: Pharoah Sanders, Whose Saxophone Was a Force of Nature, Dies at 81
abstract: He first gained wide recognition for his work with John Coltrane. He went on to a fertile, prolific career, releasing dozens of albums as a leader.

name: Roxanne Lowit
profession: Fashion Photographer With a Backstage View
headline: Roxanne Lowit, Fashion Photographer With a Backstage View, Dies at 80
abstract: Her candid shots at fashion shows captured stars of the industry as themselves and showed that the spectacle behind the curtain often rivaled the main event.

name: Jim Post
profession: Known for a Memorably Groovy Hit Song
headline: Jim Post, Known for a Memorably ‘Groovy’ Hit Song, Dies at 82
abstract: He and his wife, Cathy Conn, had a Top 10 single with “Reach Out of the Darkness” as Friend & Lover in 1968. It’s still played today, but it was their only hit.

name: Just Jaeckin
headline: Just Jaeckin, Whose ‘Emmanuelle’ Was a Scandalous Success, Dies at 82
abstract: His first film, the story of a young woman’s erotic adventures, was initially blocked by French censors but became a runaway hit.

name: Greg Lee
profession: Key Member of Two U.C.L.A. Title-Winners
headline: Greg Lee, a Key Member of Two U.C.L.A. Title-Winners, Dies at 70
abstract: A master of the assist, he played alongside Bill Walton and Jamaal Wilkes on teams that John Wooden led to the N.C.A.A. championship in 1972 and 1973.

name: Nancy Hiller
profession: Broke a Glass Ceiling in Woodworking
headline: Nancy Hiller, Who Broke a Glass Ceiling in Woodworking, Dies at 63
abstract: One of the few women in her profession, she steadily built a quiet but forceful reputation as one of the best cabinetmakers in the country.

name: Jim Florio
profession: New Jersey Governor Undone by Tax Hike
headline: Jim Florio, New Jersey Governor Undone by Tax Hike, Dies at 85
abstract: A Democrat, he had successes on gun control, the environment and property-tax relief, but after raising income and sales taxes, he lost a bid for re-election.

name: Ray Edenton
headline: Ray Edenton, ‘A-Team’ Studio Guitarist in Nashville, Dies at 95
abstract: In a career that spanned four decades, he played on thousands of sessions and accompanied many of the biggest names in country music.

name: David Foreman
headline: David Foreman, Hard-Line Environmentalist, Dies at 75
abstract: As a co-founder of the group Earth First!, he advocated slashing tires and downing power lines in an effort to return vast swaths of the country to their natural state.

name: Sonia Handelman Meyer
headline: Sonia Handelman Meyer, Socially Conscious Photographer, Dies at 102
abstract: As a member of the Photo League in the 1940s and ’50s, she roved New York City, capturing the humanity of ordinary people. She was 87 when her work was rediscovered.

name: Valerie Maynard
headline: Valerie Maynard, Artist Who Celebrated Black Identity, Dies at 85
abstract: A sculptor and printmaker aligned with the Black Arts Movement, she tackled racism and oppression while reflecting on African American culture.

name: Rita Gardner
headline: Rita Gardner, an Original ‘Fantasticks’ Star, Is Dead at 87
abstract: In 1960 she originated the lone female role in an Off Broadway show that became part of theater history thanks to a record-setting run.

name: Hilaree Nelson
headline: Hilaree Nelson, 49, a Top Ski Mountaineer, Is Dead in Avalanche
abstract: The first woman to lead a global team of adventurers, she made dozens of first descents from peaks around the world. Her body was found in Nepal on Wednesday.

name: Bill Plante
profession: CBS Newss Man at the White House
headline: Bill Plante, CBS News’s Man at the White House, Dies at 84
abstract: He covered four presidencies in a 52-year career and never worried about “offending those in power in pursuit of answers,” one former White House press secretary said.

name: Coolio
headline: Coolio, ‘Gangsta’s Paradise’ Rapper, Dies at 59
abstract: From a bookish, asthmatic child to mainstream hitmaker, the West Coast M.C. charted a distinctive path to hip-hop stardom.

name: Maria Orosa
headline: Overlooked No More: Maria Orosa, Inventor of Banana Ketchup
abstract: As a food scientist, she sought to reduce the Philippines’ dependence on imported food, pioneering new ways to use local products. And that was before she became a war hero.

name: David Gottesman
profession: Wall St. Power and Warren Buffett Partner
