headline: David Gottesman, 96, Wall St. Power and Warren Buffett Partner, Dies
abstract: He founded the investment house First Manhattan and, after befriending him in the 1960s, pursued enormously lucrative deals with Mr. Buffett.

name: Leonard Cole
headline: Leonard Cole, Who Detailed Secret Army Germ Tests, Dies at 89
abstract: A dentist with a parallel career as a political scientist, he drew attention to a program that made millions of Americans unwitting guinea pigs.

name: Sue Mingus
profession: Promoter of Her Husbands Musical Legacy
headline: Sue Mingus, Promoter of Her Husband’s Musical Legacy, Dies at 92
abstract: Charles Mingus was among the greatest bassists in jazz. She worked tirelessly to ensure that he was known as a great composer as well.

name: Nick Holonyak Jr.
headline: Nick Holonyak Jr., Pioneer of LED Lighting, Is Dead at 93
abstract: He invented a visible red-light diode. His 41 patents also included lasers that enabled DVD and CD players.

name: Joe Bussard
headline: Joe Bussard, Obsessive Collector of Rare Records, Dies at 86
abstract: His life revolved around his massive hoard of fragile 78 r.p.m. disks of jazz, blues, country and gospel music recorded between the 1920s and ’50s.

name: Hector Lopez
headline: Hector Lopez, Who Broke a Baseball Color Barrier, Dies at 93
abstract: A utility player for the powerhouse Yankees of the 1960s, he later became the first Black manager at minor league baseball’s highest level.

name: Elias Theodorou
profession: Pioneer of Medical Marijuana in Sports
headline: Elias Theodorou, Pioneer of Medical Marijuana in Sports, Dies at 34
abstract: A Canadian mixed martial artist, he brought cerebral flair to the ring and a dogged determination to his campaign for changing the sport’s drug rules.

name: Antonio Inoki
headline: Antonio Inoki, Japanese Wrestler and Improbable Diplomat, Dies at 79
abstract: After gaining fame for an odd 1976 bout with Muhammad Ali, he became a politician and globe-traveling broker of peace.

name: Sacheen Littlefeather
headline: Sacheen Littlefeather, Activist Who Rejected Brando’s Oscar, Dies at 75
abstract: The actress was booed at the Academy Awards in 1973 after she refused the best actor award on Marlon Brando’s behalf in protest of Hollywood’s depictions of Native Americans.

name: Robert Ferrante
profession: News-Driven Producer at CBS and NPR
headline: Robert Ferrante, News-Driven Producer at CBS and NPR, Dies at 87
abstract: He raised the profiles of the news programs “Morning Edition” and “The World” on public radio, and created the overnight program “Nightwatch” on CBS.

name: Loretta Lynn
profession: Country Music Star and Symbol of Rural Resilience
headline: Loretta Lynn, Country Music Star and Symbol of Rural Resilience, Dies at 90
abstract: Her powerful voice, playful lyrics and topical songs were a model for generations of country singers and songwriters. So was her life story.

name: Theo Richmond
profession: Revived the Past in a Polish Shtetl
headline: Theo Richmond, Who Revived the Past in a Polish Shtetl, Dies at 93
abstract: For “Konin: A Quest,” Mr. Richmond, a filmmaker, conducted 200 interviews to memorialize the culture of his forebears that vanished once the Nazis arrived.

name: Charles Fuller
profession: Pulitzer Winner for A Soldiers Play
headline: Charles Fuller, Pulitzer Winner for ‘A Soldier’s Play,’ Dies at 83
abstract: He was the second Black playwright to win the award and later adapted the play into an Oscar-nominated film, “A Soldier’s Story.”

name: Jerzy Urban
headline: Jerzy Urban, Acerbic Communist Turned Free-Speech Hero, Dies at 89
abstract: He spent the 1980s as the Polish regime’s sarcastic spokesman, then transformed himself into a controversial media entrepreneur in the ’90s.

name: Kitten Natividad
profession: Movie Star in Russ Meyers Bawdy World
headline: Kitten Natividad, Movie Star in Russ Meyer’s Bawdy World, Dies at 74
abstract: She was top-billed in his final feature, “Beneath the Valley of the Ultra-Vixens.” She was also his paramour and, he said, his favorite leading lady.

name: Tiffany Jackson
profession: Texas Star Forward and W.N.B.A. Veteran
headline: Tiffany Jackson, Texas Star Forward and W.N.B.A. Veteran, Dies at 37
abstract: She was an All-American in college and spent nine years as a pro. “I don’t think I’ve seen a player as competitive,” her college coach said.

name: Laurence Silberman
headline: Laurence Silberman, Conservative Touchstone on the Bench, Dies at 86
abstract: From his powerful perch on the D.C. appeals court, he voided gun controls and challenged press freedoms but also upheld the Affordable Care Act.

name: Patricia Cloherty
headline: Patricia Cloherty, Trailblazing Venture Capitalist, Dies at 80
abstract: A logger’s daughter, she was among the first women to thrive in the high-risk, high-reward field and a key backer of fledgling Russian companies in the 1990s.

name: Meredith Tax
headline: Meredith Tax, Feminist Author, Historian and Activist, Dies at 80
abstract: An uncompromising voice in the women’s movement’s second wave, she focused on working-class women and later on women’s rights around the world.

name: Colin Alevras
profession: Inventive New York Chef and Restaurateur
headline: Colin Alevras, Inventive New York Chef and Restaurateur, Dies at 51
abstract: He popularized a farmers’ market cuisine at his and his wife’s tiny, quirky and acclaimed East Village establishment called the Tasting Room.

name: Judy Tenuta
headline: Judy Tenuta, Accordion-Playing ‘Love Goddess’ of Comedy, Dies at 72
abstract: She cracked comedy’s top ranks with a memorably outlandish act in the 1980s, when the stand-up scene was largely male.

name: Günter Lamprecht
headline: Günter Lamprecht, Star of ‘Berlin Alexanderplatz,’ Dies at 92
abstract: He drew acclaim as the central character in Rainer Werner Fassbinder’s 14-part 1980 television epic about Weimar Germany.

name: Robert Kalfin
headline: Robert Kalfin, Founder of an Adventurous Theater, Dies at 89
abstract: For two decades, his Chelsea Theater Center was on the cutting edge with productions that could be challenging, baffling or, sometimes, Broadway bound.

name: David Beckwith
profession: Scooped the Supreme Court on Roe
headline: David Beckwith, Who Scooped the Supreme Court on Roe, Dies at 79
abstract: His article on the landmark abortion-rights ruling gained renewed attention this year after a draft of the opinion overturning that decision was leaked.

name: Al Primo
profession: Creator of Local TVs Eyewitness News
headline: Al Primo, Creator of Local TV’s Eyewitness News, Dies at 87
abstract: At stations in Philadelphia and then New York, he relaxed the tone of news delivery, using two anchors, a diverse team of reporters and dollops of banter.

name: Anton Fier
headline: Anton Fier, Drummer Who Left Stamp on a Downtown Scene, Dies at 66
abstract: He worked with everyone from the Feelies to Herbie Hancock to Laurie Anderson, as well as leading the indie-rock supergroup the Golden Palominos. But there was a troubled side.

name: Billy Sothern
headline: Billy Sothern, Crusading New Orleans Defense Lawyer, Dies at 45
abstract: He was known for taking on some of Louisiana’s toughest cases, including the wrongful conviction of Albert Woodfox, who spent 42 years in solitary confinement.

name: Stephanie Dabney
headline: Stephanie Dabney, Electrifying Prima Ballerina, Dies at 64
abstract: A principal dancer with Dance Theater of Harlem, she was an international star, a memorable Firebird and an inspiration for dancers of color.

name: Grace Glueck
profession: Arts Writer Fought for Equality at The Times
headline: Grace Glueck, 96, Dies; Arts Writer Fought for Equality at The Times
abstract: She made the art world a distinct beat at the newspaper, inspiring other papers to make it an industry standard. She later helped bring a groundbreaking sex-discrimination suit against The Times.

name: Kevin Locke
headline: Kevin Locke, Who Worked to Preserve Lakota Culture, Dies at 68
abstract: Playing the wooden flute and performing hoop dances, he sought to introduce audiences throughout the nation to Native American traditions.

name: Douglas Kirkland
headline: Douglas Kirkland, Who Took Portraits of Movie Stars, Dies at 88
abstract: His many memorable shots included one of his earliest assignments and probably his most famous: Marilyn Monroe in bed, wrapped in a silk sheet.

name: Nikki Finke
headline: Nikki Finke, Caustic Hollywood Chronicler, Is Dead at 68
abstract: At newspapers and then at Deadline, the website she founded, she served up the opposite of fluff entertainment journalism.

name: Leonard Kriegel
headline: Leonard Kriegel, 89, Dies; Wrote Unflinchingly About His Disability
abstract: He was known for his scholarly and popular writings about historical phenomena. But he was best known for writing about losing the use of his legs.

name: Anita Kerr
headline: Anita Kerr, an Architect of the Nashville Sound, Dies at 94
abstract: She and her background vocalists were heard “oohing” and “aahing” on thousands of country and pop hits recorded in the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Angela Lansbury
headline: Angela Lansbury, Star of Film, Stage and ‘Murder, She Wrote,’ Dies at 96
abstract: She was a Hollywood and Broadway sensation, but she captured the biggest audience of her career as the TV sleuth Jessica Fletcher.

name: Eileen Ryan
headline: Eileen Ryan, Actress of Stage and Screen, Is Dead at 94
abstract: She put her career on hold for a time to raise her sons, the actors Sean and Chris Penn and the musician Michael Penn.

name: Walter Dean Burnham
headline: Walter Dean Burnham, Who Traced Political Parties’ Shifts, Dies at 92
abstract: A noted political scientist, he saw parties periodically realigning themselves in stark fashion, presaging the rise of Donald Trump.

name: Andy Detwiler
headline: Andy Detwiler, Armless Farmer Who Became a YouTube Star, Dies at 52
abstract: After a childhood accident, he learned how to drive tractors and feed farm animals with his feet. Then he started a popular farming channel on YouTube.

name: Sterling Johnson Jr.
profession: Prosecutor Turned U.S. Judge in Brooklyn
headline: Sterling Johnson Jr., Prosecutor Turned U.S. Judge in Brooklyn, Dies at 88
abstract: He closed a Guantánamo “H.I.V. prison camp” and castigated the city over its treatment of poor people with AIDS. A former detective, he had also been a narcotics prosecutor.

name: Bruno Latour
profession: Philosopher on the Social Basis of Scientific Facts
headline: Bruno Latour, 75, Philosopher on the Social Basis of Scientific Facts, Dies
abstract: A leading thinker of the postwar era, he became an ally of the science establishment in the face of attacks by climate deniers and conspiracy theorists.

name: Art Laboe
headline: Art Laboe, D.J. Who Popularized ‘Oldies but Goodies,’ Dies at 97
abstract: A familiar voice on the California airwaves for almost 80 years, he saw the appeal of old rock ’n’ roll records practically before they were old.

name: Jack Brogan
headline: Jack Brogan, Who Gave Substance to Artists’ Visions, Is Dead at 92
abstract: A master fabricator, he was a wizard at handling the new materials and technologies used by artists. But to the public, he remained a hidden gem.

name: Robert Toll
headline: Robert Toll, Who Mass-Produced ‘McMansions,’ Is Dead at 81
abstract: He and his brother, Bruce, founded a home-building company that found suburbia fertile ground to make hundreds of millions of dollars with roomy dwellings.

name: Dan Wieden
profession: Adman of Nike Just Do It Fame
headline: Dan Wieden, Adman of Nike ‘Just Do It’ Fame, Is Dead at 77
abstract: A mix of Norman Rockwell and Andy Warhol, the self-effacing co-founder of the advertising agency Wieden+Kennedy considered his success a “cosmic joke.”

name: Bernard McGuirk
profession: Famous and Infamous as Foil of Imus
headline: Bernard McGuirk, Famous and Infamous as Foil of Imus, Dies at 64
abstract: The two men were fired because of a racist exchange about the Rutgers women’s basketball team, marring, but not ending, their shared radio success.

name: Robbie Coltrane
profession: Hagrid in the Harry Potter Films
headline: Robbie Coltrane, Hagrid in the ‘Harry Potter’ Films, Dies at 72
abstract: The veteran Scottish actor and comedian also won acclaim for playing a gambling-addicted psychologist on the crime series “Cracker” in the 1990s.

name: Katharine Briggs
headline: Overlooked No More: Katharine Briggs and Isabel Myers, Creators of a Personality Test
abstract: Mother and daughter, they developed the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator, which has helped millions of people discover if they are introverts or extroverts or thinkers or feelers.

name: Isabel Myers
headline: Overlooked No More: Katharine Briggs and Isabel Myers, Creators of a Personality Test
abstract: Mother and daughter, they developed the Myers-Briggs Type Indicator, which has helped millions of people discover if they are introverts or extroverts or thinkers or feelers.

name: Vincent DiMaio
headline: Dr. Vincent DiMaio, Pathologist in Notorious Murder Cases, Dies at 81
abstract: A gunshot expert, he testified in the Trayvon Martin case, examined Lee Harvey Oswald’s remains and concluded that Vincent van Gogh’s death was a homicide, not a suicide.

name: Mary Adelia McLeod
profession: First Female Bishop of an Episcopal Diocese
headline: Mary Adelia McLeod, 84, Dies; First Female Bishop of an Episcopal Diocese
abstract: She began her seminary studies around the time the church approved the ordination of women. She was elected to lead the Vermont Diocese in 1993.

name: Charles Sherrod
profession: Civil Rights Pioneer in Rural Georgia
headline: Charles Sherrod, Civil Rights Pioneer in Rural Georgia, Dies at 85
abstract: He brought his deep Christian faith and his commitment to grass-roots organizing to the small town of Albany. He never left.

name: Bruce Sutter
headline: Bruce Sutter, Hall of Fame Relief Pitcher, Is Dead at 69
abstract: Relying on a single pitch, the split-fingered fastball, he made the All-Star team six times, won a Cy Young Award and saved 300 games.

name: Jim Redmond
profession: Aid to Son Was an Olympic Moment
headline: Jim Redmond, Whose Aid to Son Was an Olympic Moment, Dies at 81
abstract: Derek Redmond pulled a hamstring at the 1992 Games. His father rushed to the track, and they finished the race together.

name: Benjamin Civiletti
profession: Attorney General in Iran Hostage Crisis
headline: Benjamin Civiletti, 87, Attorney General in Iran Hostage Crisis, Dies
abstract: As Carter’s last attorney general, he fought for the release of Americans held by Iran and investigated allegations against two aides and the president’s brother.

name: James A. McDivitt
headline: James A. McDivitt, Commander in Early NASA Triumphs, Is Dead at 93
abstract: In the 1960s, he led the first spacewalk mission and took part in the first crewed orbital flight of a lunar module.

name: Ralph DeNunzio
headline: Ralph DeNunzio, Wall Street Chieftain, Is Dead at 90
abstract: He was chairman of the New York Stock Exchange and rose to lead the venerable securities firm Kidder, Peabody, but stepped down after it was caught up in a 1980s insider-trading scandal.

name: Charles W. Duncan Jr.
headline: Charles W. Duncan Jr., Energy Secretary in Oil Crisis, Is Dead at 96
abstract: Heir to a Houston coffee fortune and a former president of Coca-Cola, he joined President Jimmy Carter’s cabinet in 1979 as oil shortages roiled the nation.

name: Laura Anglin
profession: Leading New York State and City Official
headline: Laura Anglin, a Leading New York State and City Official, Dies at 57
abstract: She was budget director in Albany and “was one of the unsung heroes” in helping to shape the pandemic response as a deputy mayor under Bill de Blasio.

name: Jeff Weiss
headline: Jeff Weiss, an Unconventional Theatrical Force, Dies at 82
abstract: Downtown, he was known for sprawling works and vivid performances, but later in his career he drew praise as an actor in mainstream productions, too.

name: Charley Trippi
headline: Charley Trippi, Versatile Football Hall of Famer, Dies at 100
abstract: A star on offense and defense, he took Georgia to a Rose Bowl victory and the Chicago Cardinals to an N.F.L. title. “The greatest football player I’ve ever seen,” Jim Thorpe said.

name: Al Ries
headline: Al Ries, Adman Who Sought a Portal Into Consumers’ Brains, Dies at 95
abstract: Using the concept of “positioning,” he guided companies to market their products by creating hard-to-forget messages.

name: Roger Welsch
headline: Roger Welsch, ‘America’s Premier Storyteller,’ Is Dead at 85
abstract: Author, humorist and tractor buff, he quit academia and found fame as a correspondent from the Nebraska heartland for the CBS News program “Sunday Morning.”

name: Billy Al Bengston
headline: Billy Al Bengston, Painter Who Channeled California Cool, Dies at 88
abstract: A former motorcycle racer and stuntman, he helped put Los Angeles on the art world map with paintings inspired by the West Coast’s surf and car culture.

name: Mary McCaslin
headline: Mary McCaslin, 75, Folk Singer Who Lamented the Lost Old West, Dies
abstract: A songwriter in her own right, she was known for renditions of pop and rock songs, “Pinball Wizard” among them, that made them sound like mountain ballads.

name: Lenny Lipton
profession: Puff the Magic Dragon Lyricist and 3-D Film Pioneer
headline: Lenny Lipton, ‘Puff the Magic Dragon’ Lyricist and 3-D Film Pioneer, 82, Dies
abstract: He used the royalties earned from the hit folk song, based on a poem he wrote in college, to fund decades of research into stereoscopic projection.

name: Peter Schjeldahl
profession: New York Art Critic With a Poets Voice
headline: Peter Schjeldahl, New York Art Critic With a Poet’s Voice, Dies at 80
abstract: Writing for The New Yorker and The Village Voice, he was an indispensable guide to art on view, both old and new.

name: Joanna Simon
profession: Opera Singer from Famously Musical Family
headline: Joanna Simon, Opera Singer from Famously Musical Family, Dies at 85
abstract: A renowned mezzo-soprano, she grew up alongside her younger sisters, Carly and Lucy, both of whom became singer-songwriters.

name: Lucy Simon
headline: Lucy Simon, Singer and Broadway Composer, Is Dead at 82
abstract: She and her sister Carly Simon were a folk duo in the 1960s. Years later, she wrote the Tony-nominated music for “The Secret Garden.”

name: Beryl Benacerraf
profession: Pioneered the Use of Prenatal Ultrasound
headline: Beryl Benacerraf, 73, Dies; Pioneered the Use of Prenatal Ultrasound
abstract: A radiologist with an uncanny visual sense, she revolutionized the diagnosis of fetal abnormalities like Down syndrome.

name: Geoff Nuttall
profession: First Among Equals in Acclaimed Quartet
headline: Geoff Nuttall, First Among Equals in Acclaimed Quartet, Dies at 56
abstract: With the St. Lawrence Quartet, he played the violin with such enthusiasm that he often swept himself from his seat. At the Spoleto Festival USA, he was a shaping force.

name: Ngo Vinh Long
profession: Lightning Rod for Opposing the Vietnam War
headline: Ngo Vinh Long, Lightning Rod for Opposing the Vietnam War, Dies at 78
abstract: After escaping arrest in Vietnam for his antiwar views, he became the most prominent Vietnamese in the United States to campaign against the war.

name: Louis Gigante
headline: Louis Gigante, Priest Who Led South Bronx Revival, Dies at 90
abstract: The brother of a convicted Mafia boss, he became a Democratic Party leader and a city councilman, and helped build thousands of units of housing.

name: Leslie Jordan
headline: Leslie Jordan, Comic Actor and Instagram Star, Dies at 67
abstract: Shows like “Will & Grace” made him a familiar face, then the pandemic brought new fame. He was killed in a car crash in Hollywood.

name: Dietrich Mateschitz
profession: Creator of the Red Bull Empire
headline: Dietrich Mateschitz, Creator of the Red Bull Empire, Dies at 78
abstract: The Austrian salesman turned a Thai energy drink into a marketing juggernaut that owned sports teams, media outlets and a winning Formula 1 crew.

name: Ashton B. Carter
headline: Ashton B. Carter, Defense Secretary Under Obama, Dies at 68
abstract: Trained as a physicist, he opened the U.S. military to transgender service members and removed barriers to women in combat roles.

name: Ahmed Alshaiba
headline: Ahmed Alshaiba, Yemeni Music Master, Is Dead at 32
abstract: He taught himself to play the oud, a lutelike stringed instrument, and made a splash on social media with his cover versions of pop songs.

name: Pierre Soulages
headline: Pierre Soulages, Leading French Abstract Painter, Dies at 102
abstract: Once called “the world’s greatest living artist,” Mr. Soulages was best known for exploring the possibilities of the color black.

name: Jody Miller
profession: Singer of Queen of the House and More
headline: Jody Miller, Singer of ‘Queen of the House’ and More, Dies at 80
abstract: Best known for a 1965 homemaker’s reply to a hobo’s refrain, the Oklahoma native had a hit the same year with the very different “Home of the Brave.”

name: John Jay Osborn Jr.
headline: John Jay Osborn Jr., Author of ‘The Paper Chase,’ Dies at 77
abstract: His 1971 novel became a movie, with John Houseman giving an award-winning performance as the imperious Professor Kingsfield, and later a television series.

name: Lucianne Goldberg
headline: Lucianne Goldberg, Who Helped Expose Clinton Affair, Dies at 87
abstract: It was Ms. Goldberg, a literary agent, who suggested that Linda Tripp tape her conversations with Monica Lewinsky. She later fed revelations to the news media.

name: Robert Gordon
headline: Robert Gordon, Punk Rocker Turned Rockabilly Revivalist, Dies at 75
abstract: Weary of the angry and aggressive sound of New York’s musical underground of the late 1970s, he returned to rock’s roots and seeded a rockabilly revival.

name: Toshi Ichiyanagi
headline: Toshi Ichiyanagi, Avant-Garde Composer and Pianist, Dies at 89
abstract: A former protégé of John Cage who was once married to Yoko Ono, he was part of a lively experimental music scene in New York and became a leading modern composer in Japan.

name: Seymour Press
headline: Seymour Press, a Behind-the-Scenes Fixture on Broadway, Dies at 98
abstract: He started playing in Broadway orchestras in 1957, and eventually he began recruiting those orchestras as well.

name: Margo Feiden
headline: Margo Feiden, Hirschfeld’s Idiosyncratic Gallerist, Dies at 77
abstract: She handled the sales of the great caricaturist’s works and told stories of flying Diane Arbus in her plane and encountering the woman who shot Andy Warhol.

name: Jerry Lee Lewis
headline: Jerry Lee Lewis, a Rock ’n’ Roll Original, Dies at 87
abstract: With his pounding piano, his impassioned vocals and his incendiary performing style, Mr. Lewis lived up to his nickname, the Killer.

name: Calvin O. Butts III
display_name: The Rev. Calvin O. Butts III
headline: The Rev. Calvin O. Butts III, Dynamic Harlem Pastor, Dies at 73
abstract: He led Abyssinian Baptist Church and helped revitalize his community by building housing, some of which he reserved for existing residents.

name: Jules Bass
headline: Jules Bass, Co-Producer of TV Holiday Staples, Is Dead at 87
abstract: The animation company he ran with Arthur Rankin Jr. gave the world “Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer,” “Frosty the Snowman” and much more.

name: Dorothy Spencer
profession: Film Editor Sought Out by Big Directors
headline: Overlooked No More: Dorothy Spencer, Film Editor Sought Out by Big Directors
abstract: She worked with Alfred Hitchcock, Elia Kazan, Frank Capra and John Ford, and she was known for her deft touch, particularly with action movies.

name: Vince Dooley
profession: Hall of Fame Football Coach for Georgia
headline: Vince Dooley, Hall of Fame Football Coach for Georgia, Dies at 90
abstract: In a 25-year coaching career, he appeared in 20 bowl games and won 201 games, the fourth-highest total in Southeastern Conference history.

name: Carmen Callil
profession: Founder of the Feminist Press Virago
headline: Carmen Callil, Founder of the Feminist Press Virago, Dies at 84
abstract: She upended the clubby male landscape of British publishing, and expanded the literary canon, reintroducing works by forgotten women authors.

name: Thomas Cahill
headline: Thomas Cahill, Popular Writer of Ireland’s History, Dies at 82
abstract: His book “How the Irish Saved Civilization” became a best seller and helped open the door to a new appreciation of that country’s culture.

name: Msgr. John Meier
headline: Msgr. John Meier, Who Searched for ‘Historical Jesus,’ Dies at 80
abstract: For more than three decades, he worked on his multivolume series, “A Marginal Jew,” drawing praise from Pope Benedict XVI.

name: Sy Presten
profession: Press Agent So Old-Fashioned He Was News
headline: Sy Presten, Press Agent So Old-Fashioned He Was News, Dies at 98
abstract: He fed material to gossip columns, buttered up reporters and banged on typewriters from the heyday of the Copacabana to the rise of reality TV.

name: Roz Wyman
profession: Helped Bring the Dodgers to Los Angeles
headline: Roz Wyman, Who Helped Bring the Dodgers to Los Angeles, Dies at 92
abstract: As a City Council member, she vowed to bring Major League Baseball to the city and persuaded the team’s owner, Walter O’Malley, to move from Brooklyn.

name: Gael Greene
headline: Gael Greene, Who Shook Up Restaurant Reviewing, Dies at 88
abstract: She brought sass and sensuality to the job as a critic for New York magazine for four decades. She also helped create the charity Citymeals on Wheels.

name: Julie Powell
profession: Food Writer Known for Julie & Julia
headline: Julie Powell, Food Writer Known for ‘Julie & Julia,’ Dies at 49
abstract: She attempted to cook every recipe in a classic Julia Child cookbook and documented the effort in a popular blog that became a best-selling book and a hit movie.

name: Bernard Rosen
profession: Budget Brain for Four New York City Mayors
headline: Bernard Rosen, Budget Brain for Four New York City Mayors, Dies at 91
abstract: He knew how to find hidden pots of money. “There wasn’t a budget director in the last 50 years who didn’t rely on Bernie,” one of his acolytes said.

name: Daniel Smith
profession: Thought to Be the Last Child of an Enslaved Person
headline: Daniel Smith, 90, Dies; Thought to Be the Last Child of an Enslaved Person
abstract: He led a life marked by encounters with touchstone moments in Black history, from the March on Washington to Barack Obama’s first inauguration.

name: Christine Farnon
headline: Christine Farnon, ‘Guiding Light’ of the Grammys, Dies at 97
abstract: Present at the creation, she guarded the awards’ independence and integrity but, the Grammys’ longtime producer said, “never received the recognition she deserves.”

name: John McVay
profession: Key Figure in the Making of a 49ers Dynasty
headline: John McVay, Key Figure in the Making of a 49ers Dynasty, Dies at 91
abstract: He rebounded from the humiliation of “the fumble” as coach of the ’78 New York Giants to help San Francisco win five Super Bowls over 14 seasons as a top team executive.

name: Harry Bates
profession: Modernist Architect of Long Island Homes
headline: Harry Bates, Modernist Architect of Long Island Homes, Dies at 95
abstract: Withstanding “a tsunami of shingles” on houses going up on the East End, he stuck to an aesthetic of clean, elegant lines and simple materials.

name: George Booth
profession: New Yorker Cartoonist of Sublime Zaniness
headline: George Booth, New Yorker Cartoonist of Sublime Zaniness, Dies at 96
abstract: He depicted a quirky cast of people and pets — notably his mad-as-a-hatter bull terrier, which became a reader favorite and the magazine’s unofficial mascot.

name: Philip Hiat
headline: Philip Hiat, Rabbi Who Forged Bonds With Other Faiths, Dies at 95
abstract: His bridge-building efforts notably included a book and traveling exhibition of Jewish manuscripts from the Vatican’s archives.

name: Hannah Pick-Goslar
headline: Hannah Pick-Goslar, a Presence in Anne Frank’s Diary, Dies at 93
abstract: The two young women knew each other from kindergarten until their final encounter, on opposite sides of a barbed-wire fence in the Bergen-Belsen concentration camp.

name: Rodney Graham
headline: Rodney Graham, Conceptual Artist Who Starred in His Work, Dies at 73
abstract: As both an artist and a model, he created alternative worlds where ordinary characters seemed extraordinary.

name: Tony Isidore
headline: Tony Isidore, Galvanizing Adman, Is Dead at 89
abstract: With arresting ad campaigns, he helped promote the New York Urban Coalition (“Give a Damn”) and the re-election of Mayor John V. Lindsay (“I Made Mistakes”).

name: Ray Guy
profession: First N.F.L. Punter Named to the Hall of Fame
headline: Ray Guy, First N.F.L. Punter Named to the Hall of Fame, Dies at 72
abstract: A slender Georgia country boy with the outlaw Oakland Raiders of the 1970s, he proved that a punt could be a spectacle in its own right.

name: James Giffen
headline: James Giffen, Who Was Embroiled in ‘Kazakhgate,’ Dies at 81
abstract: The government charged him with funneling $78 million in bribes to Kazakhstan, but dropped the case after a judge decided he had acted with C.I.A. approval.

name: Rebecca Godfrey
profession: Author Found Humanity in Teenage Violence
headline: Rebecca Godfrey, 54, Dies; Author Found Humanity in Teenage Violence
abstract: She drew praise for the precision and compassion of “Under the Bridge,” her account of the beating and murder of a 14-year-old girl.

name: Katherine Duncan-Jones
headline: Katherine Duncan-Jones, Who Cast Shakespeare as a Boor, Dies at 81
abstract: A fearless scholar of English literature, she argued in books and interviews that the revered playwright was a narcissist, misogynist and social climber.

name: Douglas McGrath
headline: Douglas McGrath, Playwright, Filmmaker and Actor, Is Dead at 64
abstract: His one-man Off Broadway show, “Everything’s Fine,” directed by John Lithgow, had opened just weeks ago.

name: Freddy Rodríguez
headline: Freddy Rodríguez, 76, Artist Who Explored His Dominican Roots, Dies
abstract: His main medium was paint, but his most viewed work may have been the outdoor memorial in Queens to Flight 587.

name: Samuel L. Katz
headline: Samuel L. Katz, a Developer of the Measles Vaccine, Dies at 95
abstract: In 1956, when he began working with a small group in a Boston laboratory, measles was a major threat. Seven years later, lifesaving immunizations began.

name: Doris Grumbach
headline: Doris Grumbach, Author Who Explored Women’s Plight, Dies at 104
abstract: In novels, essays and literary criticism, she wrote about women trapped in repressive families or disintegrating marriages. She also wrote six memoirs.

name: Romano Mazzoli
headline: Romano Mazzoli, Who Oversaw Major Immigration Reform, Dies at 89
abstract: A House Democrat, he worked across the aisle with Senator Alan K. Simpson to enable a compromise allowing amnesty for millions of undocumented immigrants.

name: Aaron Carter
headline: Aaron Carter, Singer and Onetime Teenage Sensation, Dies at 34
abstract: Mr. Carter, who released his first album at age 9 and “Aaron’s Party” at age 12, was the younger brother of Nick Carter, a member of the Backstreet Boys.

name: Dow Finsterwald
profession: Golfer Known for Some Close Calls
headline: Dow Finsterwald, Golfer Known for Some Close Calls, Dies at 93
abstract: Finsterwald was one of the sport’s most consistent money winners. But he may be best known for twice narrowly missing out on winning the Masters.

name: Ela Bhatt
profession: Advocate for Women Workers in India
headline: Ela Bhatt, Advocate for Women Workers in India, Dies at 89
abstract: The cooperative she founded has helped millions of women who had never before had a safety net. “They were,” she said, “the poorest among the poor.”

name: Michael Basman
profession: Chess Master Known for Bad Openings
headline: Michael Basman, Chess Master Known for ‘Bad’ Openings, Dies at 76
abstract: He was known for playing some of the least respected openings, including the Grob, the Creepy Crawly or the St. George Defense. But he was often successful.

name: Ernie Lazar
headline: Ernie Lazar, Who Trawled for Secret Government Documents, Dies at 77
abstract: By pursuing his “unusual hobby” of filing as many as 10,000 Freedom of Information requests about extremist groups, he proved invaluable to historians and journalists.

name: Evelyn de Rothschild
headline: Evelyn de Rothschild, Scion of Banking Dynasty, Dies at 91
abstract: Initially showing little promise, he eventually joined the family firm and rose to chairman, wielding vast influence in Britain’s financial and political affairs.

name: Herman Daly
profession: Challenged the Economic Gospel of Growth
headline: Herman Daly, 84, Who Challenged the Economic Gospel of Growth, Dies
abstract: Perhaps the best-known ecological economist, he faulted his mainstream peers for failing to account for the environmental harm growth can bring.

name: Leslie Phillips
profession: Comic Actor Voiced Harry Potter Hat
headline: Leslie Phillips, 98, Dies; Comic Actor Voiced ‘Harry Potter’ Hat
abstract: He made a name for himself in British satires, then late in his career reached a different audience as the voice of the Sorting Hat in the Harry Potter movies.

name: Lee Bontecou
headline: Lee Bontecou, Acclaimed Creator of Unusual Sculptures, Dies at 91
abstract: Her use of what one critic called “a three-dimensional form that was neither painting nor sculpture” earned the kind of praise typically reserved in the 1960s for male art stars.

name: Elizabeth Stewart
headline: Elizabeth Stewart, Champion of Scotland’s Folk Music, Dies at 83
abstract: She was part of a musical family of Scottish Travellers that furthered the nation’s folk revival and influenced its American counterpart.

name: Paul Morantz
headline: Paul Morantz, Lawyer Who Campaigned Against Cults, Dies at 77
abstract: He took on sects and other fringe groups in California, as well as abusive psychotherapists and a self-help guru. At one point assassins tried to kill him with a rattlesnake.

name: Joe Tarsia
profession: Architect of the Sound of Philadelphia
headline: Joe Tarsia, an Architect of the Sound of Philadelphia, Dies at 88
abstract: His work as an engineer at Sigma Sound Studios left a sonic stamp on R&B hits by the O’Jays, the Delfonics, the Stylistics and many others.

name: Gal Costa
headline: Gal Costa Dies at 77; Singer Embodied Tropicália’s Innovative Spirit
abstract: Her graceful, flexible voice and ear for memorable songs sustained a five-decade career defining the sound of Brazilian pop.

name: Lewis Kuller
headline: Dr. Lewis Kuller, a Father of Preventive Cardiology, Dies at 88
abstract: His clinical studies focused largely on how to reduce the risk factors of cardiovascular disease. He also established a link between menopause and heart disease.

name: Lois Curtis
headline: Lois Curtis, Whose Lawsuit Secured Disability Rights, Dies at 55
abstract: The Supreme Court decided in Olmstead v. L.C. that warehousing people with disabilities in mental institutions was discriminatory.

name: Patrick Haggerty
profession: Lost Pioneer of Gay Country Music
headline: Patrick Haggerty, ‘Lost Pioneer’ of Gay Country Music, Dies at 78
abstract: In 1973, he put out a little-noticed album of songs about same-sex love and social protest. Forty-one years later, he became an unlikely star.

name: Jane Gross
headline: Jane Gross, Sportswriter Who Opened Locker Room Doors, Dies at 75
abstract: She made news by entering a pro basketball inner sanctum to do her job. Years later, her mother’s physical decline led her to write about aging for The Times and in a book.

name: Jeff Cook
profession: Founder of the Country Band Alabama
headline: Jeff Cook, a Founder of the Country Band Alabama, Dies at 73
abstract: His group had 32 No. 1 country singles, and his guitar and fiddle playing helped extend its reach to a generation raised on rock ’n’ roll.

name: Joyce Molyneux
headline: Joyce Molyneux, Noted British Chef, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Her restaurant in Dartmouth, England, received a Michelin star in the 1970s, a rare honor for a kitchen presided over by a woman.

name: Cléoma Falcon
headline: Overlooked No More: Cléoma Falcon, Queen of Cajun Music
abstract: She and her husband, Joe, recorded the first commercial recording of Cajun music ever made, giving voice to French-speaking Louisiana.

name: Mimi Parker
headline: Mimi Parker, Moody Alt-Rock Vocalist, Is Dead at 55
abstract: Her influential band, Low, emerged in the 1990s, but its minimalist sound stood in sharp contrast to the anthems of angst that came to define the grunge era.

name: Kevin Conroy
profession: Gave Voice to Batman for 3 Decades
headline: Kevin Conroy, Who Gave Voice to Batman for 3 Decades, Dies at 66
abstract: With a distinctively deep and raspy voice, Mr. Conroy spent more time playing Batman than any other actor, without ever showing his face.

name: Brian O’Doherty
headline: Brian O’Doherty, Art Critic and (Conceptual) Art Creator, Dies at 94
abstract: A restless Irish polymath who had trained as a doctor in Dublin, he found his way to New York and became a leading figure in the city’s bustling art scene.

name: Kevin O’Neill
profession: Comics Artist With a Taste for the Lurid
headline: Kevin O’Neill, Comics Artist With a Taste for the Lurid, Dies at 69
abstract: “Nobody drew like Kevin O’Neill,” said the writer Alan Moore, who collaborated with him from 1999 to 2019 on the series The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen.

name: Samuel Folsom
headline: Samuel Folsom, 102, Who Fought the Japanese Above Guadalcanal, Dies
abstract: He went to war at 22 with limited flying experience but dodged Zeros, knocked out bombers and won the Distinguished Flying Cross and a Purple Heart.

name: Paul Schrade
profession: Was Wounded When Robert Kennedy Was Slain
headline: Paul Schrade, 97, Who Was Wounded When Robert Kennedy Was Slain, Dies
abstract: A leader of the United Auto Workers and a Kennedy confidant, he remained convinced that a second gunman had been involved in the assassination.

name: Mehran Karimi Nasseri
headline: Mehran Karimi Nasseri, Who Inspired ‘The Terminal,’ Dies in Paris Airport
abstract: He slept on a bench in Charles de Gaulle Airport for 18 years, stuck in limbo as a refugee. His story inspired a Steven Spielberg film with Tom Hanks.

name: Dan McCafferty
headline: Dan McCafferty, Nazareth Frontman Who Sang ‘Love Hurts,’ Dies at 76
abstract: His Scottish band became known for hard-driving stadium rock, but its biggest hit was a cover of a country ballad about heartbreak.

name: John Aniston
headline: John Aniston, Veteran Television Actor, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Aniston, the father of the actor Jennifer Aniston, played a suave villain on the soap opera “Days of Our Lives” for more than three decades.

name: Ellen Levine
profession: Editor With Keen Sense of Women Readers
headline: Ellen Levine, 79, Dies; Editor With Keen Sense of Women Readers
abstract: She was Good Housekeeping’s first female top editor, earlier edited Woman’s Day and Redbook, and helped Oprah Winfrey create a newsstand sensation.

name: Virginia McLaurin
headline: Virginia McLaurin Dies; Sharecroppers’ Daughter Who Danced With the Obamas
abstract: “I thought I would never live to get in the White House,” the centenarian said during a 2016 meeting with the first couple. A video of the encounter made her famous.

name: Henry Rosovsky
profession: Builder of Black and Jewish Studies at Harvard
headline: Henry Rosovsky, 95, Builder of Black and Jewish Studies at Harvard, Dies
abstract: As dean of the faculty, he diplomatically persuaded his colleagues to tighten requirements for a degree and create a Black studies program.

name: Fred Hickman
headline: Fred Hickman, Longtime CNN Sports Anchor, Is Dead at 66
abstract: He was teamed memorably with Nick Charles for many years on “Sports Tonight” and gained praise early on for his interviews with sports figures.

name: Budd Friedman
profession: Built an Empire of Comedy Clubs
headline: Budd Friedman, Who Built an Empire of Comedy Clubs, Dies at 90
abstract: Starting with the original Improv in Midtown Manhattan, he gave Richard Pryor, Lily Tomlin and countless other comedians a launching pad to fame.

name: Michael J. Gerson
headline: Michael J. Gerson, Presidential Speechwriter and Columnist, Dies at 58
abstract: He composed many of George W. Bush’s signature addresses, and later, as a writer for The Washington Post, took a stand against Donald J. Trump.

name: Robert Clary
profession: Took a Tragic Journey to Hogans Heroes
headline: Robert Clary, Who Took a Tragic Journey to ‘Hogan’s Heroes,’ Dies at 96
abstract: After surviving concentration camps as a youth, he went on to star on the hit 1960s sitcom set in a German prisoner-of-war camp.

name: Alice Davis
headline: Alice Davis, Costume Designer for Disney Rides, Dies at 93
abstract: She created the costumes for more than 150 singing, dancing robotic children in It’s a Small World, and for the buccaneers of Pirates of the Caribbean.

name: Ned Rorem
profession: Composer Known for Both His Music and His Diaries
headline: Ned Rorem, Composer Known for Both His Music and His Diaries, Dies at 99
abstract: A Pulitzer Prize winner, he wrote many orchestral works but was most celebrated for his vocal pieces. He was also well known for writing candidly about his life.

name: Michael Butler
headline: Michael Butler, Who Brought ‘Hair’ to Broadway, Dies at 95
abstract: He came from a wealthy family, but he championed the ideas of the counterculture. Journalists called him “the hippie millionaire.”

name: Keith Levene
headline: Keith Levene, Public Image Ltd.’s Buzz-Saw Guitarist, Dies at 65
abstract: Considered a post-punk pioneer, he was also a founding member of the Clash but left before it became one of the biggest bands of its era.

name: Carol Leigh
profession: Sought a New View of Prostitution
headline: Carol Leigh, Who Sought a New View of Prostitution, Dies at 71
abstract: She was serious about issues related to sex for money. But she also spoke through an amusing persona she called Scarlot Harlot.

name: Staughton Lynd
profession: Historian and Activist Turned Labor Lawyer
headline: Staughton Lynd, Historian and Activist Turned Labor Lawyer, Dies at 92
abstract: After being blacklisted from academia for his antiwar activity, he became an organizer among steel workers in the industrial Midwest.

name: Ed Rudy
profession: Chronicler of the Beatles First Trip to America
headline: Ed Rudy, Chronicler of the Beatles’ First Trip to America, Dies at 93
abstract: He sent reports about the Fab Four’s travels to radio stations in February 1964. Then he turned the material into an album that rose to No. 20 on the Billboard chart.

name: Mitchell Rosenthal
headline: Dr. Mitchell Rosenthal, Phoenix House Founder, Dies at 87
abstract: A psychiatrist, he was an early apostle for treating drug and alcohol addiction with group therapy in a residential setting.

name: George Lois
headline: George Lois, Visionary Art Director, Is Dead at 91
abstract: He brought the counterculture to advertising and designed memorable covers for Esquire magazine, many of them wordless critiques of American society.

name: Danny Kalb
headline: Danny Kalb, Guitarist Who Gave Blues-Rock an Edge, Dies at 80
abstract: His 1960s band, the Blues Project, won a following with a driving, experimental approach to traditional material that was anything but purist.

name: Dagny Corcoran
profession: Bookselling Fixture of L.A. Art Scene
headline: Dagny Corcoran, Bookselling Fixture of L.A. Art Scene, Dies at 77
abstract: Her store, Art Catalogues, specialized in books for and about museum and gallery exhibitions and became a gathering place for artists and bibliophiles.

name: Jay Pasachoff
headline: Jay Pasachoff, Who Pursued Eclipses Across the Globe, Dies at 79
abstract: An astronomer at Williams College, he probably saw more solar eclipses than any other human in history.

name: Jason David Frank
headline: Jason David Frank, Who Starred in ‘Power Rangers’ Franchise, Dies at 49
abstract: Mr. Frank played the Green and White Rangers in the campy television show, which featured six teenage high school students who transformed into superheroes to defend Earth against evil aliens.

name: Bao Tong
profession: Top Chinese Official Imprisoned After Tiananmen
headline: Bao Tong, 90, Dies; Top Chinese Official Imprisoned After Tiananmen
abstract: He helped design China’s political reforms in the 1980s and tried to avert the bloodshed that ended the democracy protests. After prison, he became a critic of the party.

name: Robert D. Kern
headline: Robert D. Kern, 96, Whose Emergency Generators Produced Riches, Dies
abstract: Born in a garage, his company, Generac, thrived on the threat of power failures to corner the market on portable and backup sources of electricity.

name: Hebe de Bonafini
headline: Hebe de Bonafini, 93, Who Rallied Mothers of ‘the Disappeared,’ Dies
abstract: She was a key force behind a 1970s human rights movement demanding justice from Argentina’s brutal military dictatorship. Her extreme leftist views later made her a polarizing figure.

name: Edward C. Prescott
profession: Won Nobel for Studying Business Cycles
headline: Edward C. Prescott, 81, Dies; Won Nobel for Studying Business Cycles
abstract: He was among the leading thinkers to explain the economic shocks of the 1970s, and his work was critical to the supply-side economics of the ’80s.

name: Pablo Eisenberg
headline: Pablo Eisenberg, Fierce Critic of Aloof Philanthropies, Dies at 90
abstract: He fought for transparency, accountability, equity and support directed to grass-roots organizations.

name: Frederick P. Brooks Jr.
headline: Frederick P. Brooks Jr., Computer Design Innovator, Dies at 91
abstract: He was a lead designer of the computers that cemented IBM’s dominance for decades. He later wrote a book on software engineering that became a quirky classic.

name: Harriet Bograd
headline: Harriet Bograd, Champion of Jews in Africa, Dies at 79
abstract: She wanted them to feel connected to their origins by helping them start businesses and open synagogues and schools.

name: Cecilia Marshall
profession: Rights Advocate and Widow of Justice
headline: Cecilia Marshall, Rights Advocate and Widow of Justice, Dies at 94
abstract: A civil rights activist herself, she guarded Thurgood Marshall’s legacy as the first Black member of the Supreme Court.

name: Jean-Marie Straub
headline: Jean-Marie Straub, Uncompromising Filmmaker, Is Dead at 89
abstract: Emerging from the French New Wave, driven by artistic purity, he and his wife and directing partner, Danièle Huillet, didn’t care if audiences walked out on their films.

name: Pablo Milanés
headline: Pablo Milanés, Troubadour of the Cuban Revolution, Dies at 79
abstract: His music blended traditional idioms with pop inflections and social themes, earning him comparisons with Bob Dylan.

name: John Y. Brown Jr.
headline: John Y. Brown Jr., KFC Mogul and Kentucky Governor, Dies at 88
abstract: Though his political career was brief, after storming to victory with a former Miss America by his side, he made millions after selling the fried chicken chain.

name: Irene Cara
headline: Irene Cara, ‘Fame’ and ‘Flashdance’ Singer, Dies at 63
abstract: Ms. Cara was a child star from the Bronx who gained fame in the 1980s as a singer of pop anthems and as the star of the movie “Fame.”

name: Borje Salming
headline: Borje Salming, N.H.L.’s First Star From Sweden, Dies at 71
abstract: A Hall of Fame defenseman for the Toronto Maple Leafs, he led the way for other European hockey players in the league.

name: Louise Tobin
profession: Jazz Vocalist Made Comeback After a Hiatus
headline: Louise Tobin, 104, Dies; Jazz Vocalist Made Comeback After a Hiatus
abstract: She was a rising swing era star when she quit to raise children, at the request of her first husband, the bandleader Harry James. But her singing days weren’t over.

name: Eleanor Jackson Piel
headline: Eleanor Jackson Piel, Lawyer Who Fought Capital Convictions, Dies at 102
abstract: A renowned defender of the marginalized, she had many celebrated victories, including a Florida appeal known as the case of the Death Row Brothers.

name: Susan Kikuchi
profession: Staged Martha Graham Dances and King and I
headline: Susan Kikuchi, 74, Dies; Staged Martha Graham Dances and ‘King and I’
abstract: Like her mother, she became a Graham dancer, and then oversaw acclaimed productions of the choreographer’s works as well as Jerome Robbins’ musical.

name: Melody Miller
headline: Melody Miller, Trusted Aide to the Kennedys, Dies at 77
abstract: She worked with the family for over 40 years, mostly for Senator Ted Kennedy. But her duties went far beyond the office.

name: Michael Pertschuk
headline: Michael Pertschuk, Antismoking and Auto Safety Crusader, Dies at 89
abstract: As an obscure but muscular congressional staffer and chairman of the Federal Trade Commission, he helped usher into law a raft of consumer protections.

name: Charles Koppelman
profession: Force in the Music Industry and Beyond
headline: Charles Koppelman, Force in the Music Industry and Beyond, Dies at 82
abstract: A dealmaker and superstar matchmaker, he worked with artists like Barbra Streisand, Dolly Parton and Tracy Chapman. Later he was chairman of Martha Stewart Living.

name: Jiang Zemin
headline: Jiang Zemin, Leader Who Guided China Into Global Market, Dies at 96
abstract: Mr. Jiang, a wily and garrulous politician, presided over a decade of meteoric economic growth in the post-Tiananmen era.

name: Michael Feingold
headline: Michael Feingold, Forceful Drama Critic, Dies at 77
abstract: For decades he wrote about theater in The Village Voice, but he also was a dramaturge and a Tony-nominated translator.

name: Hiroshi Miyamura
profession: Given Medal of Honor in Korean War
headline: Hiroshi Miyamura, Given Medal of Honor in Korean War, Dies at 97
abstract: He was the first living Japanese American to receive the country’s highest military award for valor.

name: Gaylord Perry
profession: Hall of Fame Pitcher With a Doctoring Touch
headline: Gaylord Perry, Hall of Fame Pitcher With a Doctoring Touch, Dies at 84
abstract: He won 314 games and recorded 3,500 strikeouts, but he’s remembered as much for his acknowledged spitball, with saliva just one substance in his arsenal.

name: Art Brewer
headline: Art Brewer, Leading Photographer of Surfers, Is Dead at 71
abstract: A surfer from a young age, he began publishing his pictures when he was a teenager and became renowned for both his action shots and his portraits.

name: Barbara Love
profession: Fought for Lesbians to Have a Voice
headline: Barbara Love, Who Fought for Lesbians to Have a Voice, Dies at 85
abstract: As an activist and an author, she was determined to demystify and normalize the lesbian experience, and to integrate it into the women’s movement.

name: Frederick Swann
headline: Frederick Swann, Master of the Pipe Organ, Is Dead at 91
abstract: He drew the best from complex instruments at Riverside Church in Manhattan, at countless recitals and on the “Hour of Power” TV show.

name: Julia Reichert
headline: Julia Reichert, Documentarian of the Working Class, Dies at 76
abstract: She took home, to Ohio, a 2019 Oscar for “American Factory,” and in a long career teaching and making films, she paid special attention to working women.

name: Freddie Roman
headline: Freddie Roman, Who Brought Catskill Comedy to Broadway, Dies at 85
abstract: Bored with selling shoes, he became a comedian in the 1960s and later conceived the hit show “Catskills on Broadway.” He was also the longtime dean of the Friars Club.

name: Mary Shannon Little
headline: Mary Shannon Little, Who Prosecuted Wedtech Scandal, Dies at 65
abstract: She “brought moral force to her work” in a 1980s bribery and extortion case that took down two Bronx congressmen and a borough president.

name: Brad William Henke
headline: Brad William Henke, N.F.L. Player Who Turned to Acting, Dies at 56
abstract: A defensive lineman who played for the Denver Broncos, he later appeared in “Orange Is the New Black,” “Dexter” and “Lost.”

name: Allen Kay
profession: Coined If You See Something, Say Something
headline: Allen Kay, 77, Dies; Coined ‘If You See Something, Say Something’
abstract: He created many memorable commercials, including one featuring a monk who works miracles with a Xerox copier. His most notable slogan helped save lives.

name: Hans Magnus Enzensberger
headline: Hans Magnus Enzensberger, Leading Light in German Letters, Dies at 93
abstract: Poet, essayist, journalist and social critic, he held wide influence among a postwar literary generation with works as intellectual as they were political.

name: John Prados
headline: John Prados, Master of Uncovering Government Secrets, Dies at 71
abstract: An “archives rat,” he was expert at digging through declassified materials to tell new stories about America’s military history.

name: Ann Davison
headline: Overlooked No More: Ann Davison, Who Daringly Crossed the Atlantic Alone
abstract: She set sail in 1952 not to set a record or make a point about women and their abilities. Rather, her motivation was deeply personal.

name: Aline Kominsky-Crumb
headline: Aline Kominsky-Crumb, Pioneering Comics Memoirist, Dies at 74
abstract: Her autobiographical cartoons — confessional, sexualized and self-deprecating — were considered the first by a woman in underground comics.

name: John Corry
profession: Former Times Reporter and TV Critic
headline: John Corry, Former Times Reporter and TV Critic, Dies at 89
abstract: Among his best known articles were one that helped clear a man of killing his mother and one that disputed plagiarism charges against Jerzy Kosinski.

name: Bernadette Mayer
headline: Bernadette Mayer, Poet Who Celebrated the Ordinary, Dies at 77
abstract: A New York writer and artist who found inspiration in the countryside, she used experimental forms to celebrate mundane pleasures.

name: Werner Franke
headline: Werner Franke, Who Exposed East German Doping Program, Dies at 82
abstract: In the 1990s, he and his wife unearthed documentary evidence of the illicit, state-sponsored drug program that propelled the country to Olympic glory.

name: Bob McGrath
headline: Bob McGrath, Longtime ‘Sesame Street’ Star, Dies at 90
abstract: He was an original cast member who, for nearly half a century, played a sweater-clad and easygoing music teacher who dispensed advice.

name: Felipe Valls
profession: His Cuban Restaurant Became a Political Hub
headline: Felipe Valls, 89, Dies; His Cuban Restaurant Became a Political Hub
abstract: Politicians, protesters and celebrants of happy community news have known where to converge: Versailles, a Miami landmark for Cuban Americans.

name: Nick Bollettieri
headline: Nick Bollettieri, Nurturer of Tennis Champions, Dies at 91
abstract: At his training camps, he employed a tough style in developing 10 players who reached the No. 1 world ranking. “He yells at kids, insults them. And they work harder.”

name: Kirstie Alley
headline: Kirstie Alley, Emmy-Winning ‘Cheers’ Actress, Dies at 71
abstract: A virtual unknown when she joined the cast of the hit sitcom in 1987, she became a star and a decade later had her own show, “Veronica’s Closet.”

name: Don Luce
headline: Don Luce, Activist Who Helped End the Vietnam War, Dies at 88
abstract: His relentless campaigning and his exposure of South Vietnam’s “tiger cages” were instrumental in turning the American public and Congress against the war.

name: Jim Kolbe
headline: Jim Kolbe, Openly Gay Republican Congressman, Is Dead at 80
abstract: His vote for the Defense of Marriage Act in 1996 prompted a gay-interest magazine to prepare to out him. He later regretted his vote and celebrated coming out.

name: Sal Durante
profession: Caught a Bit of Baseball History
headline: Sal Durante, Who Caught a Bit of Baseball History, Dies at 81
abstract: At Yankee Stadium on Oct. 1, 1961, Mr. Durante, a 19-year-old truck driver, stood on his seat in right field and nabbed Roger Maris’s 61st home run one-handed.

name: Gaddis Smith
profession: Taught History to Generations at Yale
headline: Gaddis Smith Dies at 89; Taught History to Generations at Yale
abstract: One of his students became a president, another an actress. He also helped the university modernize during the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Joyce Bryant
headline: Joyce Bryant, Sensual Singer Who Changed Course, Dies at 95
abstract: In the 1940s and ’50s she was a glamorous Black star when there were few. Then she became a missionary.

name: George Newall
headline: George Newall, a Creator of ‘Schoolhouse Rock,’ Dies at 88
abstract: He was the last surviving member of the team that produced the educational cartoon for ABC-TV that informed Generation X.

name: Jule Campbell
profession: Architect of the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue
headline: Jule Campbell, 96, Dies; Architect of the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue
abstract: Be it objectification or celebration, the annual rite she created earned millions for the magazine and helped usher in the supermodel era.

name: Johnny Johnson
headline: Johnny Johnson, the Last World War II ‘Dambuster,’ Dies at 101
abstract: With the Royal Air Force, he took part in a morale-boosting strike on Nazi Germany’s industrial heartland, breaching dams and unleashing devastating floods.

name: Jim Stewart
headline: Jim Stewart, Unlikely Entrepreneur of Soul Music, Dies at 92
abstract: His background was in country music. But Stax, the label he founded with his sister, achieved a level of success with Black artists that rivaled Motown’s.

name: Dominique Lapierre
profession: Popular Author Wrote Is Paris Burning?
headline: Dominique Lapierre, 91, Dies; Popular Author Wrote ‘Is Paris Burning?’
abstract: His books, many co-written with the American journalist Larry Collins, were international best-sellers, among them “City of Joy,” based on his travels to India.

name: Hamish Kilgour
profession: New Zealand Cult Band Had Reach
headline: Hamish Kilgour, Whose New Zealand Cult Band Had Reach, Dies at 65
abstract: He was a powerful drummer and, most notably, a founding member of the Clean, which inspired indie bands like Pavement, Yo La Tengo and Superchunk.

name: Silver Saundors Friedman
headline: Silver Saundors Friedman, Who Helped Found the Improv, Dies at 89
abstract: She ran the famous New York comedy club with her husband for years as they launched the careers of many comic stars.

name: Eric Allison
headline: Eric Allison, Prison Reporter Who Knew the Beat All Too Well, Dies at 79
abstract: A career criminal in England for nearly a half-century, he was hired by The Guardian to report on injustices in prisons — work that led to exposés and honors.

name: Joseph Kittinger
headline: Joseph Kittinger, a Record-Setter High in the Skies, Dies at 94
abstract: He soared in a balloon to 102,800 feet and, with parachutes, plunged in a free fall for 16 miles, helping to set the stage for manned spaceflights.

name: Lee Lorenz
profession: Cartoonist and Gatekeeper at The New Yorker
headline: Lee Lorenz, 90, Cartoonist and Gatekeeper at The New Yorker, Dies
abstract: Over 40 years at the magazine he drew hundreds of cartoons and covers and served as art and cartoon editor, recruiting new talent and deciding who got published.

name: Alain Sailhac
headline: Alain Sailhac, a Celebrity Chef Who Never Sought the Title, Dies at 86
abstract: The mild-mannered, French-born chef cooked for presidents and stars at Le Cirque in New York and earned an early four-star rating at Le Cygne.

name: Mills Lane
headline: Mills Lane, Who Refereed Tyson Ear Bite Fight, Dies at 85
abstract: He was a referee for more than a hundred boxing title fights, but gained national renown for the 1997 bout between Mike Tyson and Evander Holyfield.

name: Paul Silas
profession: N.B.A. Defensive Star and Head Coach
headline: Paul Silas, N.B.A. Defensive Star and Head Coach, Dies at 79
abstract: Known for his rebounding, he spent 16 seasons as a player, most notably with the Celtics. He was also LeBron James’s first coach as a pro.

name: Marijane Meaker
headline: Marijane Meaker, 95, Who Took Lesbian Pulp Fiction Mainstream, Dies
abstract: Her 1952 novel “Spring Fire” was about a girl who falls in love with a sorority sister. As M.E. Kerr, she wrote popular young adult books.

name: Fernando Campana
headline: Fernando Campana, Provocateur of Furniture Design, Is Dead at 61
abstract: Working with his brother, he became a star of the design world, creating furniture and other objects and elevating the culture of his native Brazil.

name: Angelo Badalamenti
headline: Angelo Badalamenti, Composer for ‘Twin Peaks,’ Is Dead at 85
abstract: The filmmaker David Lynch turned to his haunting work again and again, for “Blue Velvet,” “Mulholland Drive” and other neo-noir films.

name: Don Lewis
headline: Don Lewis, Unsung Pioneer of Electronic Music, Dies at 81
abstract: He invented the first system for integrating multiple instruments using a single control panel, predating the MIDI controller by years.

name: Mike Leach
profession: Football Coach With an Air Raid Offense
headline: Mike Leach, Football Coach With an ‘Air Raid’ Offense, Dies at 61
abstract: At Mississippi State and earlier at Texas Tech and Washington State, he deployed a high-powered, pass-happy scheme, winning eight bowl games.

name: Curt Simmons
profession: Last of the Phillies Whiz Kids
headline: Curt Simmons, Last of the Phillies’ Whiz Kids, Dies at 93
abstract: A three-time All Star pitcher, he helped Philadelphia win the pennant in 1950 and was with the Cardinals when they won the 1964 World Series.

name: Lloyd Newman
headline: Lloyd Newman, Teenage Chronicler of ‘Ghetto Life,’ Dies at 43
abstract: He and LeAlan Jones recorded stories of life and death in a Chicago housing project for NPR, winning a Peabody Award and inspiring the birth of StoryCorps.

name: Stuart Margolin
profession: Emmy Winner for The Rockford Files
headline: Stuart Margolin, Emmy Winner for ‘The Rockford Files,’ Dies at 82
abstract: A sought-after character actor for decades, he worked frequently with James Garner. He also wrote and directed.

name: Dorothy Pitman Hughes
headline: Dorothy Pitman Hughes Dies at 84; Brought Black Issues to Feminism
abstract: A close friend of Gloria Steinem, she toured with her and spoke widely about the need for women to confront racism and classism in their ranks.

name: Abigail Kawananakoa
profession: Claimed to Be Last Hawaiian Princess
headline: Abigail Kawananakoa, 96, Dies; Claimed to Be Last Hawaiian Princess
abstract: She was the great-great niece of the last king as well as the heiress to one of the state’s largest fortunes.

name: Stephen Boss
profession: Dancer and Reality TV Star Known as tWitch
headline: Stephen Boss, Dancer and Reality TV Star Known as tWitch, Dies at 40
abstract: Mr. Boss spent nine years with “The Ellen DeGeneres Show” as D.J., guest host and, eventually, an executive producer.

name: Jay Goldberg
headline: Jay Goldberg, Tenacious Lawyer for Celebrities, Dies at 89
abstract: He defended Donald Trump, Sean Combs, Bono, the Rolling Stones, the Hells Angels and mob figures with wit and verve.

name: Billie Moore
profession: Coach of Champions in Womens Basketball
headline: Billie Moore, Coach of Champions in Women’s Basketball, Dies at 79
abstract: She was the first coach to lead two different schools to titles in the 1970s, when the women’s college game was new and struggling.

name: Alice Teirstein
headline: Alice Teirstein, Who Introduced Youths to Dance, Dies at 93
abstract: She taught for decades at the Fieldston School and founded a free summer dance program open to all students in New York.

name: Frances Hesselbein
profession: Progressive Leader of the Girl Scouts
headline: Frances Hesselbein, Progressive Leader of the Girl Scouts, Dies at 107
abstract: Widely cited as a model of leadership, she took the scouts out of “the Betty Crocker era,” halting a membership decline and recruiting minority girls.

name: Audrey Munson
headline: Overlooked No More: Audrey Munson, Forgotten but, Living On in Sculptures, Not Gone
abstract: Called “the American Venus,” she was a model immortalized by sculptors, her image remaining visible in monuments across New York City.

name: Beryl Grey
headline: Beryl Grey, Acclaimed British Ballerina, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Her versatility and theatricality brought her world renown and an appearance with the Bolshoi Ballet in Moscow. She later became a troupe’s artistic director.

name: Frank Shakespeare
profession: TV Executive Behind a New Nixon
headline: Frank Shakespeare, TV Executive Behind a New Nixon, Dies at 97
abstract: He helped dispel the candidate’s stiff image for the 1968 presidential campaign and then led U.S. government broadcasting efforts overseas under Nixon and Reagan.

name: Herbert Deutsch
headline: Herbert Deutsch, Co-Creator of the Moog Synthesizer, Dies at 90
abstract: An experimental composer, Mr. Deutsch collaborated with Robert Moog to create the first synthesizer to make a significant impact on popular music, launching a revolution in electronic music.

name: Marion Smith
headline: Marion Smith, the World’s Most Prolific Cave Explorer, Dies at 80
abstract: He was particularly fond of vertical caving, often dangling freely in a hundred-foot abyss on a rope no thicker than a thumb.

name: Milton Viorst
headline: Milton Viorst, Writer Who Chronicled the Middle East, Dies at 92
abstract: He wrote that the Six-Day War was a necessary prelude to peace, but he also warned that the conflict would continue without Palestinian statehood.

name: Dino Danelli
headline: Dino Danelli, Drummer Who Drove the Rascals, Is Dead at 78
abstract: His percussion virtuosity was a key to the band’s many hits of the late 1960s, including the chart-topping “Good Lovin’,” “Groovin’” and “People Got to Be Free.”

name: Philip Pearlstein
headline: Philip Pearlstein, Whose Realist Nudes Revived Portraiture, Dies at 98
abstract: His harshly lit studies of life models represented a major departure in American painting and shocked modernist critics.

name: Adrienne Mancia
headline: Adrienne Mancia, Influential Film Curator, Dies at 95
abstract: Her choices for exhibitions at the Museum of Modern Art and the Brooklyn Academy of Music gave foreign directors and newcomers valuable exposure in New York.

name: Ashley Bickerton
headline: Ashley Bickerton, Whose Art Evoked Humor and Wonder, Dies at 63
abstract: After achieving early fame, he abandoned the insular art world of New York and fled to Bali, producing work that was lush, provocative and often sharply satirical.

name: Louis Orr
profession: Syracuse Star, Knicks Forward and a Coach
headline: Louis Orr, 64, Dies; Syracuse Star, Knicks Forward and a Coach
abstract: He helped lead a dominant squad at Syracuse and won all-American honors. He later became a role player for the Knicks and a college coach.

name: Drew Griffin
headline: Drew Griffin, CNN Investigative Journalist, Dies at 60
abstract: His reporting on delayed care for military veterans at Veterans Affairs hospitals led to the resignation of the secretary of the department.

name: Jose Maria Sison
headline: Jose Maria Sison, Philippine Communist Party Founder, Dies at 83
abstract: He fielded a force of armed guerrillas, and the organization spread its revolution throughout the country. In exile, he claimed to “lead from abroad.”

name: Elena Xausa
headline: Elena Xausa, Illustrator With a Whimsical Style, Dies at 38
abstract: Her brightly colored work, often serving as visual metaphors, was sought after worldwide by major periodicals and advertisers like Apple and Nike.

name: Tom Browning
profession: Pitched a Perfect Game for the Reds
headline: Tom Browning, Who Pitched a Perfect Game for the Reds, Dies at 62
abstract: He had a reputation as a colorful character, but he was probably best known for the gem he threw against the Los Angeles Dodgers in 1988.

name: Kim Simmonds
profession: Key Figure in the British Blues Movement
headline: Kim Simmonds, a Key Figure in the British Blues Movement, Dies at 75
abstract: His band, Savoy Brown, never had a hit single, but it showcased his skills as a guitarist and songwriter and remained active for more than 50 years.

name: Stanley Drucker
profession: Ageless Clarinetist of the N.Y. Philharmonic
headline: Stanley Drucker, Ageless Clarinetist of the N.Y. Philharmonic, Dies at 93
abstract: He played in the orchestra for 60 years, performing under the baton of five music directors. He personified the orchestra’s brilliant, even brash, character.

name: Franco Harris
headline: Franco Harris, Steeler Who Caught ‘Immaculate Reception,’ Dies at 72
abstract: A Hall of Fame running back, he died days before the 50th anniversary of one of the most memorable plays in N.F.L. history.

name: Frank Salemme
profession: Onetime Head of the New England Mafia
headline: Frank Salemme, Onetime Head of the New England Mafia, Dies at 89
abstract: Known as Cadillac Frank, he took over the region’s top organized-crime outfit in the 1990s, then cooperated with prosecutors against his former ally Whitey Bulger.

name: Elayne Jones
headline: Elayne Jones, Pioneering Percussionist, Is Dead at 94
abstract: She challenged racial barriers when she joined the San Francisco Symphony in 1972. But she became embroiled in a legal battle when she was denied tenure two years later.

name: Albert Madansky
profession: Gauged Risk of Unwitting Atomic War
headline: Albert Madansky Dies at 88; Gauged Risk of Unwitting Atomic War
abstract: As a scholarly statistician, he also evaluated stock options, the best nonfiction books and the most mouthwatering pastrami sandwich.

name: Sonya Eddy
headline: Sonya Eddy, ‘General Hospital’ Actress, Dies at 55
abstract: Ms. Eddy played Epiphany Johnson, the head nurse on the long-running ABC daytime series, for 16 years.

name: Oscar White Muscarella
headline: Oscar White Muscarella, Museum ‘Voice of Conscience,’ Dies at 91
abstract: An archaeologist at the Met, he warned about plundered and fake antiquities and about the acquisition practices of collectors and museums, including his own.

name: Xi Xi
profession: Writing Defined a Changing Hong Kong
headline: Xi Xi, Whose Writing Defined a Changing Hong Kong, Dies at 85
abstract: Her work captured the unease of Hong Kong’s transition to Chinese rule, gave voice to the city’s children and working-class residents, and helped put it on the literary map.

name: Mike Hodges
headline: Mike Hodges, Director Acclaimed for ‘Get Carter,’ Dies at 90
abstract: He was best known for complex crime dramas like “Croupier.” But he also made the big-budget 1980 science-fiction yarn “Flash Gordon.”

name: Ali Ahmed Aslam
profession: Credited With Inventing Chicken Tikka Masala
headline: Ali Ahmed Aslam, 77, Dies; Credited With Inventing Chicken Tikka Masala
abstract: A Glasgow restaurateur, he was part of the rise of the British curry house — and played an essential part in its story.

name: Mimi Kilgore
profession: Arts Patron and de Kooning Muse
headline: Mimi Kilgore, Arts Patron and de Kooning Muse, Dies at 87
abstract: A well-connected Texan, she made a significant mark supporting the visual arts and theater, and a lasting one on a master of Abstract Expressionism.

name: Alberto Zamperla
headline: Alberto Zamperla, Amusement Park Impresario, Is Dead at 71
abstract: His family-friendly company revived historic Luna Park in Coney Island and built attractions for Disney and Six Flags.

name: Charlene Mitchell
profession: First Black Woman to Run for President
headline: Charlene Mitchell, 92, Dies; First Black Woman to Run for President
abstract: She was the Communist Party candidate in 1968 and later led the campaign to free Angela Davis. But she eventually split with the party.

name: Tshala Muana
headline: Tshala Muana, Congolese Singer With Danceable Messages, Dies at 64
abstract: A superstar in Africa, she sang in the language of her tribe and often addressed social concerns, insisting on women’s strength and decrying abuse.

name: Patricia Daly
profession: Took On Corporate Giants on Social Justice
headline: Sister Patricia Daly, 66, Dies; Took On Corporate Giants on Social Justice
abstract: A leader in the field of socially responsible investing, she used shareholder actions and private meetings to pressure big corporations, including G.E. and Ford.

name: Stuart Namm
profession: Judge Blew Whistle on Police and Prosecutors
headline: Stuart Namm, 89, Dies; Judge Blew Whistle on Police and Prosecutors
abstract: His complaints led to an investigation of egregious misconduct by the authorities on Long Island, but he paid a political price.

name: Thom Bell
profession: Force Behind the Philadelphia Soul Sound
headline: Thom Bell, a Force Behind the Philadelphia Soul Sound, Dies at 79
abstract: As a songwriter, arranger and producer, he brought sophistication and melodic inventiveness to hits by the Delfonics, the Spinners and others.

name: Don Christopher
profession: Turned Lowly Garlic Into a Staple
headline: Don Christopher, Who Turned Lowly Garlic Into a Staple, Dies at 88
abstract: Known as the Garlic King, he used his enthusiasm and a business acumen to build an empire around the once-lowly “stinking rose.”

name: Maya Ruiz-Picasso
headline: Maya Ruiz-Picasso, Artist’s Daughter and Inspiration, Dies at 87
abstract: As a girl she brought out a childlike quality in Picasso. As an adult she became an authority on his works.

name: Terry Hall
headline: Terry Hall, a Face of Britain’s Ska Revival, Is Dead at 63
abstract: The son of Coventry factory workers, he overcame a traumatic childhood to find fame in the Thatcher years as the frontman of the Specials.

name: Kathy Whitworth
headline: Kathy Whitworth, Record-Holder for U.S. Golf Wins, Dies at 83
abstract: She was a Hall of Famer who became the first women’s pro golfer to earn more than $1 million.

name: Menahem Schmelzer
headline: Menahem Schmelzer, Jewish Theological Seminary Librarian, Dies at 88
abstract: During his long tenure, the seminary’s collection was a primary destination for scholarly inquiry into the history and literature of the Jewish people.

name: Nélida Piñon
headline: Nélida Piñon, Provocative Brazilian Novelist, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Widely regarded as one of her country’s greatest contemporary writers, she was also the first woman elected president of the Brazilian Academy of Letters.

name: Daniel Brush
headline: Daniel Brush, Boundary-Defying Artist, Is Dead at 75
abstract: He worked in jewelry, sculpture and other genres, creating one-of-a-kind pieces and, for the most part, spurning the mainstream art world.

name: Pelé
headline: Pelé, the Global Face of Soccer, Dies at 82
abstract: Pelé, who was declared a national treasure in his native Brazil, achieved worldwide celebrity and helped popularize the sport in the United States.

name: Arata Isozaki
headline: Arata Isozaki, Prolific Japanese Architect, Dies at 91
abstract: In major structures in a dozen countries, including the Museum of Contemporary Art in Los Angeles, Mr. Isozaki absorbed and reinterpreted Eastern and Western traditions.

name: Dave Whitlock
headline: Dave Whitlock, a Star of the Fly-Fishing World, Dies at 88
abstract: Known for the flies he created and for the eloquent way he chronicled his adventures in streams and rivers, he was, one editor said, “Everyman’s fly-fishing mentor.”

name: Vivienne Westwood
profession: Brought Provocative Punk Style to High Fashion
headline: Vivienne Westwood, 81, Dies; Brought Provocative Punk Style to High Fashion
abstract: The London shop she ran with Malcolm McLaren defined an era. “I don’t think punk would have happened,” Chrissie Hynde said, “without Vivienne and Malcolm.”

name: Ian Tyson
headline: Ian Tyson, Revered Canadian Folk Singer, Dies at 89
abstract: A rancher for most of his life, he began his music career as half of the duo Ian and Sylvia and was also celebrated for his commitment to the culture of Canada’s ranch country.

name: Bridgette Wimberly
headline: Bridgette Wimberly, Playwright and Librettist, Dies at 68
abstract: She had success with a play about abortion in 2001, and in 2015 wrote the libretto for the opera “Charlie Parker’s Yardbird.”

name: Cara De Silva
headline: Cara De Silva, Food Historian Who Preserved Jewish Recipes, Dies at 83
abstract: She edited “In Memory’s Kitchen,” a collection compiled by prisoners in the Theresienstadt concentration camp. It was a surprise hit.

name: Tony Vaccaro
profession: Photographed War From a Soldiers Perspective
headline: Tony Vaccaro, 100, Dies; Photographed War From a Soldier’s Perspective
abstract: After carrying a camera across battlefields, he became a magazine photographer known for his images of famous subjects like Georgia O’Keeffe and Greta Garbo.

name: Albert Reichmann
profession: Patriarch of a Real Estate Empire
headline: Albert Reichmann, Patriarch of a Real Estate Empire, Dies at 93
abstract: He and his brothers built the World Financial Center in New York and the first phase of Canary Wharf in London. But their company was upended in 1992.

name: Barbara Walters
headline: Barbara Walters, a First Among TV Newswomen, Is Dead at 93
abstract: She broke barriers for women as a co-host of the “Today” show, a network evening news anchor and a creator of “The View,” all while gaining her own kind of celebrity.

name: Benedict XVI
headline: Benedict XVI, First Modern Pope to Resign, Dies at 95
abstract: He defined a conservative course for the Roman Catholic Church, but his papacy was noted for his struggle with the clergy sexual abuse scandal and for his unexpected resignation.

name: Walter ‘Wolfman’ Washington
headline: Walter ‘Wolfman’ Washington, New Orleans Musical Luminary, Dies at 79
abstract: A guitarist and singer, he was a quintessential local star, mixing blues, funk and jazz through six decades of club and festival gigs.

name: Jean Franco
profession: Pioneering Scholar of Latin American Literature
headline: Jean Franco, 98, Pioneering Scholar of Latin American Literature, Dies
abstract: She infused her work with political and feminist perspectives and insisted that art had to be understood within its social context.

name: Haim Druckman
headline: Rabbi Haim Druckman, a Leader of Religious Zionism, Dies at 90
abstract: An influential educator, he was a strong advocate of creating Jewish settlements in the West Bank, Gaza and East Jerusalem.

name: Edith Pearlman
headline: Edith Pearlman, Writer Who Won Acclaim Late in Life, Dies at 86
abstract: A short story writer for four decades, her own tale was a rare Cinderella story in publishing, centering on a septuagenarian and a young editor.

name: Jeremiah Green
headline: Jeremiah Green, Drummer for Modest Mouse, Dies at 45
abstract: Mr. Green was a founder of the group, an indie band that rose to mainstream success. He was also one of its most enduring members.

name: Anita Pointer
profession: Frequent Lead Singer of Famed Sister Act
headline: Anita Pointer, Frequent Lead Singer of Famed Sister Act, Dies at 74
abstract: She was the lead vocalist on all three of the Pointer Sisters’ Top 40 hits in the group’s early years, and she helped define its pop sound in the 1980s.

name: Ronald Feldman
