profession: Art Gallerist With an Eye for Politics
headline: Ronald Feldman, Art Gallerist With an Eye for Politics, Dies at 84
abstract: A former lawyer, he showcased artists who tackled issues like women’s rights, the environment, totalitarianism and war.

name: Gangsta Boo
profession: Memphis Rapper Formerly With Three 6 Mafia
headline: Gangsta Boo, Memphis Rapper Formerly With Three 6 Mafia, Dies at 43
abstract: Born Lola Chantrelle Mitchell, she was one of the first female rappers to build off the gangster rap image and sound that took off in the 1990s.

name: Fred White
headline: Fred White, Drummer for Earth, Wind & Fire, Dies at 67
abstract: He provided the beat on unforgettable hits like “September,” “Let’s Groove,” “Shining Star” and “Boogie Wonderland.”

name: Ken Block
headline: Ken Block, Rally Driver and YouTube Stuntman, Dies at 55
abstract: The acclaimed driver, best known for his “Gymkhana” videos, was killed in a snowmobile accident.

name: Walter Cunningham
profession: Helped Pave the Way to the Moon
headline: Walter Cunningham, Who Helped Pave the Way to the Moon, Dies at 90
abstract: In 1968 he was a member of the first manned Apollo mission, which buoyed an America shocked by a fatal capsule fire the previous year.

name: Fay Weldon
headline: Fay Weldon, ‘She-Devil’ Author Who Challenged Feminist Orthodoxy, Dies at 91
abstract: By turns elusive and confessional in public, she used dark satire to explore the divides between men and women.

name: James ‘Buster’ Corley
headline: James ‘Buster’ Corley, Co-Founder of Dave & Buster’s, Dies at 72
abstract: The chain appealed to adults by combining food, beverage, sports and gaming under one roof.

name: Frank Galati
headline: Frank Galati, Mainstay of Chicago Theater, Dies at 79
abstract: He brought his adaptation of “The Grapes of Wrath” to Broadway and won Tony Awards. He also directed the long-running hit “Ragtime.”

name: Henry Grossman
headline: Henry Grossman, Photographer of Celebrities and Beatles, Dies at 86
abstract: He was best known for his formal portraits of prominent politicians and entertainers. Less famously, he took thousands of candid shots of John, Paul, George and Ringo.

name: Kenneth Rowe
profession: Defected From North Korea With His Jet
headline: Kenneth Rowe, Who Defected From North Korea With His Jet, Dies at 90
abstract: Two months after the Korean War armistice, he handed America an intelligence bonanza with his headline-making flight in a Soviet-made MIG.

name: Nate Thayer
headline: Nate Thayer, Bold Reporter Who Interviewed Pol Pot, Dies at 62
abstract: The “mad genius” journalist scored an exclusive interview with the genocidal Cambodian leader and covered his show trial, another worldwide scoop.

name: Ken Balcomb
profession: Revealed the Hidden World of Killer Whales
headline: Ken Balcomb, 82, Dies; Revealed the Hidden World of Killer Whales
abstract: His annual orca survey helped transform the animals’ image from soulless predators to compassionate creatures worth protecting.

name: Dick Savitt
profession: Won Australian and Wimbledon Tennis Titles in 1951
headline: Dick Savitt Dies at 95; Won Australian and Wimbledon Tennis Titles in 1951
abstract: He was the second American to win both Grand Slam tournaments in the same year, and he was ranked among the world’s top 10 players four times.

name: Art McNally
headline: Art McNally, N.F.L.’s ‘Father of Instant Replay,’ Dies at 97
abstract: The first field official in the Pro Football Hall of Fame, he helped bring technology into the sport and kept his cool even in the face of angry coaches and players.

name: Michael Snow
headline: Michael Snow, Prolific and Playful Artistic Polymath, Is Dead at 94
abstract: He was a painter, a musician, a photographer and a sculptor. But he was best known for experimental (and often contentious) films like “Wavelength.”

name: Joseph Torg
headline: Joseph Torg, Doctor Who Fought to Lessen Football Injuries, Dies at 88
abstract: Concerned about spinal-cord damage caused by headfirst strikes with helmets, he became a vocal proponent of rules changes.

name: Tove Ditlevsen
headline: Overlooked No More: Tove Ditlevsen, Danish Writer of Confessional Autofiction
abstract: She wrote of her life in raw detail with emotional force. But she was not recognized internationally until after her death, when her memoirs were translated into English.

name: Willard Gaylin
headline: Willard Gaylin, a Pioneer in Bioethics, Is Dead at 97
abstract: A psychiatrist, he started the Hastings Center with Daniel Callahan, a leading Roman Catholic thinker, to explore the moral issues arising from medical advances.

name: Joyce Meskis
headline: Joyce Meskis, Bookseller Who Defended Readers’ Rights, Dies at 80
abstract: Her Denver bookstore, the Tattered Cover, was among the country’s best, and she often found herself in the midst of First Amendment fights.

name: Russell Banks
profession: Novelist Steeped in the Working Class
headline: Russell Banks, Novelist Steeped in the Working Class, Dies at 82
abstract: He brought his own sometimes painful blue-collar experiences to bear in acclaimed stories exploring issues of race, class and power in American life.

name: Adam Rich
profession: Child Star on Eight Is Enough
headline: Adam Rich, Child Star on ‘Eight Is Enough,’ Dies at 54
abstract: After gaining popularity as a symbol of innocence on TV in the 1970s, he struggled with drugs and depression. He later became a mental health advocate.

name: Phojanakong
profession: Pioneer of Filipino Food in New York
headline: King Phojanakong, Pioneer of Filipino Food in New York, Dies at 54
abstract: His first restaurant, Kuma Inn, became destination dining despite its location on what was then a quiet stretch of the Lower East Side.

name: Bernard Kalb
headline: Bernard Kalb, Veteran Foreign Correspondent, Is Dead at 100
abstract: He covered wars, revolutions and diplomatic breakthroughs for CBS, NBC and The New York Times. He also served, briefly and unhappily, as a State Department spokesman.

name: Naomi Replansky
headline: Naomi Replansky, Poet of Hopeful Struggle, Dies at 104
abstract: Her verse examined social history through individual lives, including her own, in which she later found love. Yet for all the admiration she inspired, she was unheralded.

name: Ruggero Deodato
headline: Ruggero Deodato, Whose ‘Cannibal Holocaust’ Enraged, Dies at 83
abstract: He directed a variety of movies in a variety of genres. But it was a gruesome found-footage film that brought him both fame and infamy.

name: Adolfo Kaminsky
profession: His Forgeries Saved Thousands of Jews
headline: Adolfo Kaminsky Dies at 97; His Forgeries Saved Thousands of Jews
abstract: His talent for creating realistic documents helped children, their parents and others escape deportation to concentration camps, and in many cases to flee Nazi-occupied territory.

name: Jean Paré
headline: Jean Paré, Best-Selling ‘Everyday’ Cookbook Author, Dies at 95
abstract: With easy-to-follow recipes developed in her native Canada, she became one of the world’s top cookbook authors, publishing more than 30 million copies.

name: Charles Simic
headline: Charles Simic, Pulitzer-Winning Poet and U.S. Laureate, Dies at 84
abstract: A Serbian-born American, he left the impression in his verse that he had “poked a hole into everyday life to reveal a glimpse of something endless.”

name: Robert Moller
profession: Mediated Between U.N. Envoys and the City
headline: Robert Moller Dies at 85; Mediated Between U.N. Envoys and the City
abstract: As the U.S. liaison to some 50,000 United Nations diplomats and staff, he sought to resolve disputes on issues ranging from fugitives hiding in U.N. missions to diplomats’ unpaid parking tickets.

name: Blake Hounshell
profession: On Politics Editor at The Times
headline: Blake Hounshell, ‘On Politics’ Editor at The Times, Dies at 44
abstract: He was managing editor of Foreign Policy magazine and a top editor at Politico before overseeing The Times’s popular political newsletter.

name: Lynette Hardaway
headline: Lynette Hardaway, of Pro-Trump Duo Diamond and Silk, Dies at 51
abstract: Ms. Hardaway rose to fame with one of her sisters as a conservative media celebrity.

name: George Pell
headline: George Pell, Cardinal Whose Abuse Conviction Was Overturned, Dies at 81
abstract: An adviser to Pope Francis and a prominent figure in Australia, Cardinal Pell went to prison on charges of abusing two boys in the 1990s, but a higher court later acquitted him.

name: Rehman Rahi
headline: Rehman Rahi, 97, Eminent Kashmiri Poet Who Restored a Language, Dies
abstract: Kashmir’s unofficial poet laureate, he gave voice to the rich culture of a bitterly divided territory and helped give his mother tongue a distinct literary identity.

name: Thomas Hughes
profession: Government Insider and Vietnam War Skeptic
headline: Thomas Hughes, 97, Dies; Government Insider and Vietnam War Skeptic
abstract: Among the last of the Kennedy era’s “best and brightest,” he later transformed the Carnegie Endowment into a leading think tank.

name: Jeff Beck
profession: Guitarist With a Chapter in Rock History
headline: Jeff Beck, Guitarist With a Chapter in Rock History, Dies at 78
abstract: His playing with the Yardbirds and as leader of his own bands brought a sense of adventure to their groundbreaking recordings.

name: Liz Robbins
profession: Broke Glass Ceiling as a Washington Lobbyist
headline: Liz Robbins Dies at 76; Broke Glass Ceiling as a Washington Lobbyist
abstract: She founded the first woman-owned lobbying firm in the country, and made her name by supporting social policy and nonprofit causes.

name: Paul Johnson
headline: Paul Johnson, Prolific Historian Prized by Conservatives, Dies at 94
abstract: He wrote outsize histories on a panoply of subjects, found renown in Britain as an indefatigable columnist and infuriated liberals with his outspoken Tory views.

name: William Consovoy
profession: Took Conservative Cases to Supreme Court
headline: William Consovoy Dies at 48; Took Conservative Cases to Supreme Court
abstract: He argued against affirmative action and the Voting Rights Act and represented former President Trump in fighting the release of his tax returns.

name: Norm Fruchter
profession: Champion of Equal Access to Education
headline: Norm Fruchter, Champion of Equal Access to Education, Dies at 85
abstract: A lawsuit he helped initiate to change how the state allocates aid to localities reaped a bonanza for New York City schools.

name: Scott Minerd
headline: Scott Minerd, a Force, and a Voice, on Wall Street, Dies at 63
abstract: He helped turn Guggenheim Partners into a global investing giant. He was also a CNBC and Bloomberg commentator and a philanthropist for human rights.

name: Lisa Marie Presley
headline: Lisa Marie Presley, Singer-Songwriter and Daughter of Elvis, Dies at 54
abstract: Her death in Los Angeles on Thursday, after a life tinged with tragedy, came after a medical emergency and brief hospitalization.

name: Constantine II
headline: Constantine II, the Last King of Greece, Dies at 82
abstract: An Olympic medalist, he was popular when he took the throne in 1964. But his efforts to intervene in Greek politics led to a coup and his ouster.

name: Russell Pearce
headline: Russell Pearce, Fiery Foe of Illegal Immigration, Dies at 75
abstract: As an Arizona state senator, he sponsored what came to be known as the “show me your papers” law, requiring the police to demand documentation from those they detained.

name: Robbie Knievel
headline: Robbie Knievel, a Motorcycle Daredevil Like His Father, Dies at 60
abstract: He followed his father, Evel Knievel, into the high-flying world of motorcycle stunts, jumping the Grand Canyon and the fountains at Caesars Palace.

name: Casey Hayden
profession: Force for Civil Rights and Feminism
headline: Casey Hayden, a Force for Civil Rights and Feminism, Dies at 85
abstract: While working for the Student Nonviolent Coordinating Committee in the early 1960s, she helped write two memos that spurred the modern women’s movement.

name: Hannes Keller
headline: Hannes Keller, Swiss Deep-Sea Diving Pioneer, Is Dead at 88
abstract: His 1,020-foot descent to the Pacific Ocean floor in a diving bell in 1962 made headlines and set a record. But it had disastrous consequences.

name: Peter Grose
headline: Peter Grose, Veteran Foreign Correspondent, Dies at 88
abstract: His career with The New York Times took him to Saigon and Moscow. He drew on that experience later to write several well-received books.

name: Tatjana Patitz
headline: Tatjana Patitz, a Star in the Supermodel Era, Dies at 56
abstract: With a few others, she epitomized glamour in the late 1980s and early ’90s — on the runway, in magazines and even in a much-viewed music video.

name: Alfred T. Goodwin
profession: Judge in Pledge of Allegiance Case
headline: Alfred T. Goodwin, Judge in Pledge of Allegiance Case, Dies at 99
abstract: He ruled the pledge unconstitutional because the words “under God” violated the separation of church and state. The Supreme Court reversed the ruling.

name: Ruth Adler Schnee
headline: Ruth Adler Schnee, Exuberant Designer of Modernist Textiles, Dies at 99
abstract: A refugee from Nazi Germany, she was among a group of designers who elevated fabric from decoration into a medium for midcentury modern design.

name: Charles White
profession: Heisman Winner With a Difficult Second Act
headline: Charles White, Heisman Winner With a Difficult Second Act, Dies at 64
abstract: A tough, bruising tailback, he set U.S.C.’s career rushing record. But he also dealt with drug and alcohol abuse and, later, dementia.

name: Edie Landau
profession: Film Producer Ahead of Her Time
headline: Edie Landau, Film Producer Ahead of Her Time, Dies at 95
abstract: She and her husband invented a model for faithfully adapting acclaimed literature, illuminating an alternate path for independent cinema.

name: Gina Lollobrigida
headline: Gina Lollobrigida, Movie Star and Sex Symbol, Is Dead at 95
abstract: She began her career in her native Italy, and although she achieved fame in America, she worked more often in Europe. She later had a second career as an artist and filmmaker.

name: Frank Thomas
headline: Frank Thomas, Power-Hitting Original Met, Dies at 93
abstract: His 34 home runs and 94 runs batted in were among the few accomplishments worth celebrating on a team that famously went nowhere in 1962.

name: Rosi Mittermaier
profession: as Olympic Skier, a German National Hero
headline: Rosi Mittermaier Dies at 72; as Olympic Skier, a German National Hero
abstract: She became known as Gold-Rosi after winning two Olympic gold medals and the Alpine Ski World Cup in 1976.

name: Lupe Serrano
headline: Lupe Serrano, Ballerina of Power and Fire, Is Dead at 92
abstract: She danced with Nureyev and dazzled audiences during her 18 years with American Ballet Theater. She later went on to a five-decade career as an admired teacher.

name: André
headline: Sister André, World’s Oldest Known Person, Is Dead at 118
abstract: A French nun, she lived through two world wars and the 1918 flu pandemic and, more than a century later, survived Covid-19. She enjoyed a bit of wine and chocolate daily.

name: K. Alex Müller
headline: K. Alex Müller, Innovator in Ceramic Superconductors, Dies at 95
abstract: His and a colleague’s breakthroughs in high-temperature superconductors were honored with a Nobel Prize in Physics and opened up a world of scientific possibilities.

name: Mary Kaye Richter
headline: Mary Kaye Richter, Florist Turned Medical Crusader, Dies at 77
abstract: From her kitchen table in rural Illinois, Ms. Richter started a global foundation for families who shared her son’s rare genetic disorder.

name: Carl Hahn
headline: Carl Hahn Dies at 96; Made the VW Beetle Ubiquitous
abstract: As president of Volkswagen of America, he pushed the “Think Small” ad campaign that helped create a counterculture icon.

name: Yukihiro Takahashi
headline: Yukihiro Takahashi, Pioneer of Electronic Pop Music, Dies at 70
abstract: A drummer and singer, he was best known as a member of Yellow Magic Orchestra, one of Japan’s most successful bands and a major influence on hip-hop, techno and New Wave.

name: Jonathan Raban
headline: Jonathan Raban, Adventurous Literary Traveler, Dies at 80
abstract: An expatriate Briton, he followed Huckleberry Finn’s Mississippi, sailed to Alaska and explored eastern Montana. But, he said, he was not a “travel writer.”

name: Arthur Duncan
headline: Arthur Duncan, Barrier-Breaking Tap Dancer, Is Dead at 97
abstract: One of the first Black regulars on a TV variety show, he brought tap to millions of viewers on “The Lawrence Welk Show” after Betty White gave him his first big break.

name: David Crosby
headline: David Crosby, Folk-Rock Voice of the 1960s Whose Influence Spanned Decades, Dies at 81
abstract: He was an original member of the Byrds and a founder of Crosby, Stills & Nash. But he was almost as well known for his troubled personal life as for his music.

name: Chris Ford
profession: Made a 3-Point Mark in the N.B.A
headline: Chris Ford, Who Made a 3-Point Mark in the N.B.A., Dies at 74
abstract: He helped the Celtics win a title and coached them in the ’90s, but he may be remembered more for sinking what was hailed as the league’s first 3-point shot. Or was it?

name: Gerrie Coetzee
headline: Gerrie Coetzee, 67, Afrikaner Boxing Champ Who Fought Apartheid, Dies
abstract: He won the World Boxing Association title in 1983, became a symbol of racial comity and showed a surprising gentleness in public.

name: Dick Polich
profession: Artists Ally in the Creation of Sculptures
headline: Dick Polich, Artists’ Ally in the Creation of Sculptures, Dies at 90
abstract: His cavernous Hudson Valley foundry helped Louise Bourgeois, Richard Serra, Jeff Koons and many others turn their large-scale visions into reality.

name: Betty Lee Sung
profession: Pioneering Scholar of Chinese in America
headline: Betty Lee Sung, Pioneering Scholar of Chinese in America, Dies at 98
abstract: U.S.-born, she lived for a time in China and then fled as Japan invaded. She later broke academic ground in New York in the study of the Asian American diaspora.

name: Gwen Knapp
headline: Gwen Knapp, Sportswriter Who Looked at the Big Picture, Dies at 61
abstract: She was well known in the San Francisco area for focusing on subjects like racism, sexism and drugs, in columns that sometimes angered sports stars.

name: Marion Meade
headline: Marion Meade, Biographer Behind Dorothy Parker Revival, Dies at 88
abstract: Her 1988 book put an Algonquin wit back in circulation. She also wrote about Eleanor of Aquitaine, the suffragist Victoria Woodhull and Woody Allen.

name: Edward Pressman
headline: Edward Pressman, Film Producer Who Bet on Unsung Talent, Dies at 79
abstract: He took on Oliver Stone, Terrence Malick, Kathryn Bigelow and other directors just starting out. His name was on “Hoffa,” “American Psycho,” “Conan the Barbarian” and many more films.

name: Sal Bando
headline: Sal Bando, Captain of Championship Oakland Athletics, Dies at 78
abstract: He was a calming presence on a volatile squad, one of the few teams in baseball history to win the World Series three years in a row.

name: Ginny Redington Dawes
headline: Ginny Redington Dawes, Composer of Memorable Ad Jingles, Dies at 77
abstract: She collaborated on the melodies for signature commercials that sang the praises of McDonald’s, Coca-Cola and other brands.

name: Eileen Yin-Fei Lo
profession: Taught Americans How to Cook Chinese Food
headline: Eileen Yin-Fei Lo, 85, Dies; Taught Americans How to Cook Chinese Food
abstract: She was committed to codifying traditional Chinese cooking techniques when most Americans thought of Chinese food as dishes like chop suey and chow mein.

name: Victor S. Navasky
headline: Victor S. Navasky, a Leading Liberal Voice in Journalism, Dies at 90
abstract: Witty and contrarian, he was the longtime editor and later publisher of The Nation and wrote an acclaimed book about the Hollywood blacklisting era.

name: Marilyn Stafford
headline: Marilyn Stafford, a Photojournalist Rediscovered, Dies at 97
abstract: She brought a narrative eye and a social consciousness to her work, whether covering refugee crises, celebrities or fashion. But much of it might have been lost.

name: Balkrishna Doshi
headline: Balkrishna Doshi, Modernist Indian Architect, Is Dead at 95
abstract: The first Indian to receive the Pritzker Prize, he developed a distinctive approach to building for his country.

name: Myrtle Witbooi
headline: Myrtle Witbooi, Who Fought for Domestic Workers’ Rights, Dies at 75
abstract: She experienced the inequities of the job firsthand in South Africa and helped build national and international unions to address them.

name: James G. Lowenstein
headline: James G. Lowenstein, Whose Reports Questioned Vietnam War, Dies at 95
abstract: His deeply researched studies, drawing on extensive reporting in Southeast Asia, helped undermine President Nixon’s war plans.

name: Paul La Farge
headline: Paul La Farge, Inventive Novelist, Is Dead at 52
abstract: He played with history and narrative techniques whether writing about 19th-century France or H.P. Lovecraft.

name: J. Richard Steadman
headline: J. Richard Steadman, 85, Dies; Saved Knees of Countless Skiers
abstract: A renowned orthopedic surgeon, he developed innovative techniques for alpine Olympians. He also treated soccer, tennis and baseball stars.

name: Lance Kerwin
profession: James at 15 and Salems Lot Star
headline: Lance Kerwin, ‘James at 15’ and ‘Salem’s Lot’ Star, Dies at 62
abstract: “James,” which followed the adventures of a sandy-haired teenager who moves with his family to Boston from Oregon, made him a teenage idol.

name: Lloyd Morrisett
headline: Lloyd Morrisett, a Founder of ‘Sesame Street,’ Dies at 93
abstract: His observations about his 3-year-old daughter’s viewing habits led him to join Joan Ganz Cooney in creating a program that revolutionized children’s television.

name: Everett Quinton
headline: Everett Quinton, a Force in Downtown Theater, Dies at 71
abstract: He took over the Ridiculous Theatrical Company after the death of his partner, Charles Ludlam, in 1987. His specialty was playing women, but his range was wide.

name: Álvaro Colom
headline: Álvaro Colom, Guatemalan President Who Fought for the Indigenous, Dies at 71
abstract: He expanded access to education and health care in Indigenous villages and provided aid to the poor in a country scarred by deep inequalities and decades of civil war.

name: Jerry Blavat
headline: Jerry Blavat, D.J. Who Channeled the Soul of Philadelphia, Dies at 82
abstract: A live-wire personality and an epic self-promoter, he got a generation of youth in the City of Brotherly Love on its feet with little-known R&B gems.

name: Yoshimitsu Yamada
headline: Yoshimitsu Yamada, Who Brought Aikido to the U.S., Dies at 84
abstract: He emphasized the basics of the Japanese martial art, and he encouraged his students to develop their own interpretations of it.

name: George Zimbel
profession: Photographer of Marilyn Monroe and J.F.K
headline: George Zimbel, Photographer of Marilyn Monroe and J.F.K., Dies at 93
abstract: He preferred to take pictures of ordinary people. But in events separated by six years, he took indelible pictures of two people who transcended celebrity.

name: Alfred Leslie
headline: Alfred Leslie, Artist Who Turned Away From Abstraction, Dies at 95
abstract: “The virtual banishment of figuration and narrative from the vocabulary of so many thoughtful artists was one of the legacies of the modernists,” he said. “I never accepted this.”

name: Billy Packer
headline: Billy Packer, Straight-Talking College Basketball Analyst, Dies at 82
abstract: With partners on NBC and then CBS, and with a rapid, opinionated style, he was heard during every N.C.A.A. men’s basketball tournament from 1975 to 2008.

name: Mary Barr
headline: Overlooked No More: Mary Barr, Who Fought Wildfires From Aloft
abstract: She relied on adamantine nerves and decades of flying experience as the first woman lead pilot for the U.S. Forest Service.

name: Tom Verlaine
headline: Tom Verlaine, Influential Guitarist and Songwriter, Dies at 73
abstract: He first attracted attention with the band Television, a fixture of the New York punk rock scene. But his music wasn’t so easily categorized.

name: Ray Cordeiro
profession: Voice on Hong Kongs Airwaves for 70 Years
headline: Ray Cordeiro, a Voice on Hong Kong’s Airwaves for 70 Years, Dies at 98
abstract: Late-night radio listeners in Hong Kong associated Mr. Cordeiro’s sonorous voice with easy-listening standards and early rock. He worked until he was 96.

name: Sylvia Syms
headline: Sylvia Syms, Versatile British Actress, Is Dead at 89
abstract: In a career that began in the 1950s, she had roles that ranged from the lead in the movie “Teenage Bad Girl” to Margaret Thatcher and the Queen Mother.

name: Barbara Stanley
headline: Barbara Stanley, Influential Suicide Researcher, Dies at 73
abstract: Her simple idea, for patients to write down a plan that would help them weather a suicidal crisis, rapidly spread in clinical settings.

name: Gregory Allen Howard
headline: Gregory Allen Howard, Screenwriter of ‘Remember the Titans,’ Dies at 70
abstract: After the success of that movie, he established a brand for writing Hollywood movies about inspiring episodes in Black history.

name: Annie Wersching
profession: Played Borg Queen on Star Trek: Picard
headline: Annie Wersching, Who Played Borg Queen on ‘Star Trek: Picard,’ Dies at 45
abstract: Ms. Wersching was best known for playing the Borg Queen on the Paramount+ “Star Trek” series. She was also on the television series “24,” “Bosch” and “Timeless.”

name: Bobby Hull
headline: Bobby Hull, Hockey Hall of Famer, Is Dead at 84
abstract: The third player in N.H.L. history to score at least 50 goals in a season, he spent 15 seasons with Chicago.

name: Lisa Loring
profession: Wednesday Addams in The Addams Family
headline: Lisa Loring, Wednesday Addams in ‘The Addams Family,’ Dies at 64
abstract: With her dark clothes and pigtailed hair framing a pale face, Ms. Loring played Wednesday as a young girl obsessed with death on the ABC series, which ran from 1964 to 1966.

name: Barrett Strong
headline: Barrett Strong, Whose ‘Money’ Helped Launch Motown, Dies at 81
abstract: As a singer he was a one-hit wonder. But teaming with Norman Whitfield, he wrote a string of hits for others, including “I Heard It Through the Grapevine.”

name: Cindy Williams
headline: Cindy Williams, Co-Star of ‘Laverne & Shirley,’ Dies at 75
abstract: From 1976 to 1983, she (Shirley) and Penny Marshall (Laverne) drew millions of viewers to a sitcom playing roommates who worked in a Milwaukee brewery.

name: Dave Durenberger
profession: Censured by Senate in Ethics Breach
headline: Dave Durenberger, Censured by Senate in Ethics Breach, Dies at 88
abstract: He was a Minnesota favorite son with a sterling reputation before the Ethics Committee found he had schemed to get around Senate financial rules.

name: Carin Goldberg
profession: Transformed Book and Album Cover Design
headline: Carin Goldberg, Who Transformed Book and Album Cover Design, Dies at 69
abstract: She was part of a vanguard of women designers who looked to the past to upend the cool modernism of the ’70s with a style that would become prominent in the ’80s.

name: Allan A. Ryan
headline: Allan A. Ryan, Dogged Pursuer of Nazi Collaborators, Dies at 77
abstract: As the director of the U.S. Office of Special Investigations, he identified and prosecuted dozens of former camp guards and other henchmen.

name: Bobby Beathard
headline: Bobby Beathard, Mastermind of N.F.L. Dynasties, Dies at 86
abstract: Using unconventional tactics, he built powerhouse teams in Washington and Miami and helped mold teams in Kansas City, Atlanta and San Diego, his hometown.

name: Mira Lehr
headline: Mira Lehr, Artist Who Explored Nature’s Distress, Dies at 88
abstract: She helped found a gallery for women artists in Miami Beach and, influenced by an early Buckminster Fuller experiment, focused her art on ecology.

name: Ann McLaughlin Korologos
headline: Ann McLaughlin Korologos, Former Labor Secretary, Dies at 81
abstract: Her brief tenure as only the second woman to run the department came after years of service within the Reagan administration.

name: Joyce Dopkeen
headline: Joyce Dopkeen, Barrier-Breaking News Photographer, Dies at 80
abstract: In 1973, she was the first woman hired by The New York Times to be a full-time staff photographer.

name: Paco Rabanne
headline: Paco Rabanne, Couturier of the Space Age, Dies at 88
abstract: He burst onto the French fashion scene in 1966 and, with dresses made from metal, plastic and paper, changed the definition of couture.

name: Linda Pastan
headline: Linda Pastan, Poet Who Plumbed the Ordinary, Dies at 90
abstract: In 15 collections, beginning in the early 1970s, she wrote of family, nature, loss and sometimes dogs.

name: Carol Sloane
headline: Carol Sloane, Jazz Singer Who Found Success Early and Late, Dies at 85
abstract: After seemingly being on the verge of stardom, she languished for decades, battered by changing tastes and bad luck, before enjoying a midlife comeback.

name: Bob Born
profession: Brought Marshmallow Peeps to the Masses
headline: Bob Born, Who Brought Marshmallow Peeps to the Masses, Dies at 98
abstract: By mechanizing and greatly expanding production, he made the gooey yellow chicks an Easter favorite and a pop-culture phenomenon.

name: Jackie Rogers
headline: Jackie Rogers, Jet-Setting Fashion Designer, Dies at 90
abstract: An outspoken American who became a model for Coco Chanel, she partied with Europe’s elite before starting her own clothing line for stars and socialites.

name: Fred Terna
headline: Fred Terna, Creator of Fiery Holocaust Paintings, Dies at 99
abstract: A prisoner at Auschwitz and three other camps, he dealt with his trauma in semiabstract works that depict crematories, ovens and chimneys and serve as testimony.

name: Pervez Musharraf
headline: Pervez Musharraf, Former Military Ruler of Pakistan, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Musharraf took power in a bloodless coup in late 1999 but resigned under threat of impeachment in 2008. He drew fire for his ties to Washington.

name: Charles Kimbrough
profession: Actor Best Known for Murphy Brown
headline: Charles Kimbrough, Actor Best Known for ‘Murphy Brown,’ Dies at 86
abstract: In a career that included a Tony nomination for “Company,” he specialized in playing uptight characters, notably Candice Bergen’s stuffy straight man.

name: Melinda Dillon
headline: Melinda Dillon, 2-Time Oscar Nominee, Is Dead at 83
abstract: She was a Broadway star at 23 and then quit acting, but later re-emerged in films like “Close Encounters of the Third Kind” and “A Christmas Story.”

name: Harry Whittington
headline: Harry Whittington, Texas Lawyer Shot by Cheney, Dies at 95
abstract: He drew headlines in 2006 when he was struck by birdshot from a shotgun fired by Vice President Dick Cheney in a hunting accident — then apologized himself for the incident.

name: Charlie Thomas
profession: Drifter in Song Nearly All His Life
headline: Charlie Thomas, a Drifter in Song Nearly All His Life, Dies at 85
abstract: He was heard on hits like “There Goes My Baby,” “Under the Boardwalk” and “Up on the Roof.” He kept singing them for decades.

name: Frances Ellen Watkins Harper
headline: Overlooked No More: Frances Ellen Watkins Harper, Poet and Suffragist
abstract: One of the best-known Black poets of the 19th century, she was also a renowned orator. “You white women speak here of rights,” she said. “I speak of wrongs.”

name: David Harris
profession: Leader of Vietnam Draft Resistance Movement
headline: David Harris, Leader of Vietnam Draft Resistance Movement, Dies at 76
abstract: An activist who went to jail for refusing to serve in the military, he teamed with and married Joan Baez and later became a journalist.

name: David E. Harris
headline: David E. Harris, Trailblazing Airline Pilot, Is Dead at 89
abstract: In 1964, at the height of the civil rights movement, he became the first Black pilot for a major commercial airline in the United States.

name: David Harris
profession: Actor in the Cult Classic The Warriors
headline: David Harris, Actor in the Cult Classic ‘The Warriors,’ Dies at 75
abstract: He played Cochise, a member of the Warriors gang who navigated a panoply of costumed aggressors in New York City.

name: Ted Bell
profession: Adman Turned Author of Best-Selling Thrillers
headline: Ted Bell, Adman Turned Author of Best-Selling Thrillers, Is Dead at 76
abstract: In midcareer, having worked for the biggest agencies, he quit to conjure up novels about a British spy named Alex Hawke, who was likened to James Bond.

name: Mukarram Jah
profession: Heir to an Opulent Throne He Abandoned
headline: Mukarram Jah, Heir to an Opulent Throne He Abandoned, Dies at 89
abstract: He descended from famed Islamic royalty in India and Turkey, but later fled to Australia and became a sheep farmer.

name: Charles Silverstein
headline: Charles Silverstein, 87, Dies; Helped Destigmatize Homosexuality
abstract: He was at the forefront in persuading the American Psychiatric Association to reassess its classification of homosexuality as a mental disorder.

name: Bob Orben
headline: Bob Orben, One-Man Gag Factory and Speechwriter, Dies at 95
abstract: He wrote tens of thousands of jokes in his career — told by, among others, Dick Gregory, Jack Paar, Red Skelton and, for a while, President Gerald R. Ford.

name: Ronald Blythe
headline: Ronald Blythe, Scribe of the English Countryside, Dies at 100
abstract: He was best known for his 1969 book “Akenfield,” but he was also beloved for his many essays and columns about rural life in his native Suffolk.

name: Burt Bacharach
headline: Burt Bacharach, Composer Who Added a High Gloss to the ’60s, Dies at 94
abstract: His sophisticated collaborations with the lyricist Hal David — “The Look of Love,” “Walk On By,” “Alfie” and many more hits — evoked a sleek era of airy romance.

name: Albert Okura
headline: Albert Okura, ‘Chicken Man’ Who Saved a Ghost Town, Dies at 71
abstract: He built a California fast-food chain, opened a McDonald’s museum and restored a historic town on Route 66, a road that was special to him.

name: Jean Anderson
headline: Jean Anderson, 93, Exacting and Encyclopedic Cookbook Author, Dies
abstract: Her 1,300-page “Doubleday Cookbook” was a rival to “The Joy of Cooking,” and her rigorously tested recipes taught generations of home cooks.

name: Ron Labinski
profession: Designed a Cozier Future for Stadiums
headline: Ron Labinski, Who Designed a Cozier Future for Stadiums, Dies at 85
abstract: An architect, he followed his hunch that teams would abandon ugly concrete multipurpose arenas for fan-friendly single-sport facilities, like Oriole Park at Camden Yards.

name: Marianne Mantell
profession: Helped Pave the Way for Audiobooks
headline: Marianne Mantell, Who Helped Pave the Way for Audiobooks, Dies at 93
abstract: In her early 20s she co-founded the groundbreaking spoken-word record label Caedmon, which had a hit with Dylan Thomas’s “A Child’s Christmas in Wales.”

name: Roslyn Pope
profession: Her Manifesto Helped Fuel Civil Rights Fight
headline: Roslyn Pope, 84, Dies; Her Manifesto Helped Fuel Civil Rights Fight
abstract: An activist leader in Atlanta, in 1960 she wrote, with Julian Bond’s help, “An Appeal for Human Rights,” which resonated in the struggle across the country.

name: Eugene Lee
profession: Set Designer for Broadway and S.N.L
headline: Eugene Lee, Set Designer for Broadway and ‘S.N.L.,’ Dies at 83
abstract: He won Tony Awards for “Wicked” and other shows while also overseeing the sets for the late-night franchise’s fast-paced sketch comedy.

name: Dennis O’Leary
profession: Voice of Calm After Reagan Was Shot
headline: Dr. Dennis O’Leary, Voice of Calm After Reagan Was Shot, Dies at 85
abstract: Thrust into the role of spokesman after the assassination attempt in 1981, he led televised medical briefings that reassured an anxious nation.

name: Master Hsing Yun
headline: Master Hsing Yun, Monk Who Spread Buddhism in China, Dies at 95
abstract: He established a modern brand of Buddhism in Taiwan and opened temples around the world, becoming the rare religious figure backed by Beijing.

name: Hazel McCallion
headline: Hazel McCallion, No-Nonsense Canadian Mayor for 36 Years, Dies at 101
abstract: Tough, pragmatic and brusque when she had to be, she helped transform Mississauga from a sleepy Toronto suburb into one of the country’s largest and most dynamic cities.

name: Solomon Perel
headline: Solomon Perel, Jew Who Posed as a Hitler Youth to Survive, Dies at 97
abstract: His masquerade — a tale recounted in a memoir and in the film “Europa Europa” — saved his life. But “to this day,” he said, “I have a tangle of two souls in one body.”

name: Jürgen Flimm
profession: Director of Festivals and Opera Houses
headline: Jürgen Flimm, Director of Festivals and Opera Houses, Dies at 81
abstract: He left his mark in Hamburg, Berlin, Salzburg and elsewhere. He also directed a memorable “Ring” cycle in Bayreuth.

name: Sandra Seacat
headline: Sandra Seacat, Much Admired Acting Coach, Dies at 86
abstract: She helped Laura Dern, Marlo Thomas, Mickey Rourke and many others overcome fears, find their characters and discover “the joy of acting.”

name: De La Soul’s David Jolicoeur
headline: De La Soul’s David Jolicoeur, Who Rapped as Trugoy the Dove, Dies at 54
abstract: The trio expanded the stylistic vocabulary of hip-hop in the 1980s and ’90s, but its early experiments with sampling led to legal troubles, and the group’s longtime exclusion from streaming.

name: Ted Lerner
profession: Developer Bought and Built Washington Nationals
headline: Ted Lerner, 97, Dies; Developer Bought and Built Washington Nationals
abstract: A billionaire and Washington native, he gave the city its first baseball championship in 95 years, along with 20 million square feet of shopping malls and housing.

name: Robert Geddes
headline: Robert Geddes, 99, Transformative Architecture Dean at Princeton, Dies
abstract: As an educator, he worked to put architecture on an equal footing with other disciplines. As an architect, he was known for buildings at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton.

name: Carlos Saura
headline: Carlos Saura, a Leading and Enduring Spanish Director, Dies at 91
abstract: Called “one of the fundamental filmmakers in the history of Spanish cinema,” he began making movies under Franco, often hiding his messages in allegory.

name: Hugh Hudson
headline: Hugh Hudson, Director of ‘Chariots of Fire,’ Dies at 86
abstract: His first film — about two runners, one Christian, one Jewish, who compete at the 1924 Summer Olympics — won four Oscars, including for best picture.

name: Julian Wasser
headline: Julian Wasser, the ‘Photographer Laureate’ of L.A., Dies at 89
abstract: In the 1960s and ’70s, he created indelible images of the city’s combustible mix of art, rock ’n’ roll, new Hollywood and social ferment.

name: Lawrence McKenna
profession: New York Judge in High-Profile Cases
headline: Lawrence McKenna, New York Judge in High-Profile Cases, Dies at 89
abstract: He ruled against the Giuliani administration on issues of homelessness and free speech and revoked the citizenship of a Brooklyn man who had aided Nazis.

name: Howard Bragman
headline: Howard Bragman, Publicist Who Helped Clients Come Out, Dies at 66
abstract: He was called in to do damage control for celebrities in a negative spotlight, but his specialty was working with gay stars, athletes and others.

name: Raquel Welch
headline: Raquel Welch, Actress and ’60s Sex Symbol, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Beginning with a doeskin bikini in “One Million Years B.C.,” she built a celebrated show business career around sex appeal and, sometimes, a comic touch.

name: Hans Modrow
profession: One of East Germanys Last Communist Leaders
headline: Hans Modrow, 95, Dies; One of East Germany’s Last Communist Leaders
abstract: He became prime minister less than two weeks after the fall of the Berlin Wall, and initially sought to preserve East Germany before accepting reunification.

name: Shoichiro Toyoda
profession: Helped Make Toyota a Global Force
headline: Shoichiro Toyoda, Who Helped Make Toyota a Global Force, Dies at 97
abstract: He pushed the company into North America and beyond, setting it on its path to becoming one of the world’s most powerful automakers.

name: Arne Treholt
profession: Diplomat Convicted of Spying for Soviets
headline: Arne Treholt, 80, Dies; Diplomat Convicted of Spying for Soviets
abstract: A Norwegian, he handed over NATO plans and other secrets in one of the Cold War’s biggest espionage scandals. He was sentenced to 20 years in prison.

name: Tim McCarver
profession: Catcher in the Hall of Fame as a Broadcaster
headline: Tim McCarver, Catcher in the Hall of Fame as a Broadcaster, Dies at 81
abstract: Twice an All-Star, he played on four teams over four decades and won two World Series titles. Then he took his baseball smarts and gift of gab into the TV booth.

name: Sandra Trehub
profession: Pioneer in the Psychology of Music
headline: Sandra Trehub, Pioneer in the Psychology of Music, Dies at 84
abstract: She showed that basic musical ability is present in infants across cultures, laying a foundation for a growing field of study.

name: Margaret Heagarty
profession: Champion for Childrens Health in Harlem
headline: Margaret Heagarty, 88, Champion for Children’s Health in Harlem, Dies
abstract: The first white woman to head the pediatrics unit at Harlem Hospital, she was challenged by the epidemics of crack cocaine and H.I.V.

name: Eileen Sheridan
headline: Eileen Sheridan, Who Dominated Cycling in Postwar Britain, Dies at 99
abstract: Known as “the Mighty Atom,” she excelled at long-distance time trials and set several records that still stand more than 70 years later.

name: Rena Gluck
profession: Helped Bring Modern Dance to Israel
headline: Rena Gluck, Who Helped Bring Modern Dance to Israel, Dies at 89
abstract: As a student of Martha Graham and a founding member of the Batsheva Dance Company, she helped lay the foundation for an art that has thrived in Israel.

name: Donald Spoto
profession: Biographer of Hitchcock and Many More
headline: Donald Spoto, Biographer of Hitchcock and Many More, Dies at 81
abstract: He wrote more than two dozen books, including richly detailed biographies of Marilyn Monroe, James Dean, Laurence Olivier and Jesus.

name: Friedrich Cerha
headline: Friedrich Cerha, 96, Who Finished Another Composer’s Masterpiece, Dies
abstract: His skill in completing Alban Berg’s “Lulu” almost 40 years after Berg’s death was considered one of the greatest operatic achievements of the 20th century.

name: Stella Stevens
headline: Stella Stevens, Hollywood Bombshell Who Yearned for More, Dies at 84
abstract: She starred alongside the likes of Elvis Presley and Jerry Lewis. But she wanted to direct and write, and she felt held back by industry sexism.

name: William Greenberg Jr.
headline: William Greenberg Jr., Baker Who Sweetened Manhattan, Dies at 97
abstract: He used poker winnings to open a modest bakery in 1946 that grew into an artisanal dessert empire, tempting New Yorkers of all ages.

name: Jerrold Schecter
headline: Jerrold Schecter, Who Procured Khrushchev’s Memoirs, Dies at 90
abstract: As a Time magazine bureau chief, he was pivotal in the publication of revelatory taped interviews with the ousted premier that had been smuggled out of the Soviet Union.

name: Istvan Banyai
headline: Istvan Banyai, Illustrator Who Mined the Surreal, Dies at 73
abstract: His fantastical work for The New Yorker, New York and Playboy made him a hot commodity in the last golden era for magazines and their illustrators.

name: Sal Piro
headline: Sal Piro, ‘Rocky Horror Picture Show’ Superfan, Dies at 72
abstract: Like many others, he was riveted by the film and attended numerous midnight showings. Unlike many others, he made it the focus of his life.

name: Richard Belzer
profession: Detective Munch on Law & Order: S.V.U
headline: Richard Belzer, Detective Munch on ‘Law & Order: S.V.U.,’ Dies at 78
abstract: A stand-up comic, he called his hard-boiled character on the long-running TV drama “Lenny Bruce with a badge.”

name: Huey ‘Piano’ Smith
profession: New Orleans Rock n Roll Cornerstone
headline: Huey ‘Piano’ Smith, New Orleans Rock ’n’ Roll Cornerstone, Dies at 89
abstract: With songs like “Don’t You Just Know It,” “Rocking Pneumonia and the Boogie Woogie Flu” and “Sea Cruise,” he put a firm backbeat behind joyful nonsense.

name: Roger C. Schank
headline: Roger C. Schank, Theorist of Artificial Intelligence, Dies at 76
abstract: He combined linguistics, cognitive science and computing with the goal of “trying to understand the nature of the human mind.”

name: Paul Berg
headline: Paul Berg, Nobel-Winning Pioneer of Genetic Engineering, Is Dead at 96
abstract: In 1971, he transferred material from one organism to another, creating the first recombinant DNA, or rDNA. He later helped lead a historic effort to write protocols for genetic research.

name: Red McCombs
headline: Red McCombs, Car Salesman Turned Media Mogul, Dies at 95
abstract: A Texas entrepreneur, he co-founded the media giant Clear Channel, owned pro sports teams and created more than 400 businesses in a variety of industries.

name: Adrian Hall
headline: Adrian Hall, Who Invigorated Regional Theater, Dies at 95
abstract: As founding artistic director, he made Trinity Rep in Rhode Island a leader in theatrical innovation. He then made his mark in Dallas as well.

name: Barbara Bosson
profession: Brought Family Drama to Hill Street Blues
headline: Barbara Bosson, 83, Dies; Brought Family Drama to ‘Hill Street Blues’
abstract: She received five consecutive Emmy nominations for her role as Fay Furillo, the frenetic ex-wife of a police precinct captain.

name: Glória Maria
headline: Glória Maria, Who Broke Barriers in Brazilian Television, Dies at 73
abstract: Thought to be Brazil’s first Black TV journalist and a rare female anchor, she was a trailblazer in a country with a long history of racism.

name: Rick Newman
headline: Rick Newman, Whose Comedy Club Made Careers, Dies at 81
abstract: Soon after he opened Catch a Rising Star in Manhattan in 1972, it became a showcase for emerging talents like Billy Crystal, Robin Williams and Pat Benatar.

name: John Motson
profession: BBCs Voice of Soccer for Five Decades
headline: John Motson, BBC’s Voice of Soccer for Five Decades, Dies at 77
abstract: The broadcaster was a commentator for English soccer’s biggest moments, including 10 World Cups.

name: Tom Whitlock
profession: Co-Writer of Top Gun Anthem Danger Zone
headline: Tom Whitlock, Co-Writer of ‘Top Gun’ Anthem ‘Danger Zone,’ Dies at 68
abstract: Mr. Whitlock wrote the words for that song and the chart-topping “Take My Breath Away,” central elements in the success of the hit 1986 movie.

name: John Macrae III
headline: John Macrae III, Eclectic Publisher and Rights Champion, Dies at 91
abstract: In addition to having a roster of authors that included Gail Sheehy, David Levering Lewis and Lech Walesa, he spoke out for the rights of writers worldwide.

name: Tony Earl
headline: Tony Earl, Progressive Former Governor of Wisconsin, Dies at 86
abstract: He served only one term, but he went on to make his mark as a champion of environmental causes, gay rights and election reform.

name: Clara Driscoll
profession: Designer of Visions in Glass for Tiffany
headline: Overlooked No More: Clara Driscoll, Designer of Visions in Glass for Tiffany
abstract: She oversaw the Tiffany girls, a group of glass cutters and artisans who created elaborate, colorful lamps that are still in demand.

name: Linda King Newell
headline: Linda King Newell, Feminist Scholar of Mormon History, Dies at 82
abstract: Her work exploring the idea of female subservience within the church won acclaim. But it also led to her being blacklisted by Mormon leaders.

name: Thomas H. Lee
headline: Thomas H. Lee, Pioneer in Leveraged Buyouts, Is Dead at 78
abstract: Born into wealth, he became a billionaire in founding an aggressive Boston private equity firm. He was remembered as a “kinder, gentler” corporate raider.

name: Raymond Trollat
profession: Took a Hilly Wine Region to New Heights
headline: Raymond Trollat, Who Took a Hilly Wine Region to New Heights, Dies at 91
abstract: Few knew the Northern Rhône Valley when he began growing grapes and making wine in the 1940s. By the time he retired, the region, and his wines, were world famous.

name: Robert Hébras
profession: Last Survivor of a 1944 Massacre in France
headline: Robert Hébras, Last Survivor of a 1944 Massacre in France, Dies at 97
abstract: Dead bodies shielded him as the Nazis killed 643 people in Oradour-sur-Glane. He spent his life keeping the memory of the slaughter alive.

name: Shinta Ratri
profession: Fighter for Transgender Rights in Indonesia
headline: Shinta Ratri, Fighter for Transgender Rights in Indonesia, Dies at 60
abstract: The Islamic boarding school she helped found offers a haven for transgender women in a country where discrimination can be acute.

name: Ward Stone
headline: Ward Stone, Wildlife Coroner Who Warned Against PCBs, Dies at 84
abstract: As New York State’s animal pathologist, he ventured far afield to investigate the impact of toxic chemicals on humans.

name: Tom Luddy
headline: Tom Luddy, a Behind-the-Scenes Force in Cinema, Dies at 79
abstract: Known for his association with Francis Ford Coppola, Werner Herzog and many others, he was also a founder of the Telluride Film Festival.

name: James Abourezk
headline: James Abourezk, the First Arab American Senator, Dies at 92
abstract: A Democrat from South Dakota, he found the freedom to act on principle in the House and Senate by choosing not to seek re-election.

name: Bob Richards
profession: Pole-Vaulting Hero of the Cold War Era
headline: Bob Richards, Pole-Vaulting Hero of the Cold War Era, Dies at 97
abstract: An ordained minister known as the Vaulting Vicar, he was an Olympic gold medal winner and the first athlete to appear on the front of Wheaties boxes.

name: Betty Boothroyd
profession: Britains First Female House of Commons Speaker
headline: Betty Boothroyd, Britain’s First Female House of Commons Speaker, Dies at 93
abstract: The speaker made Britain’s parliamentary proceedings must-see TV, even in other countries.

name: Ahmed Qurei
profession: Former Palestinian Premier and Peace Envoy
headline: Ahmed Qurei, Former Palestinian Premier and Peace Envoy, Dies at 86
abstract: A member of the old guard of Palestinian leaders, Mr. Qurei was a principal architect of the Oslo Accords, the first peace agreement with Israel.

name: Charles Pernasilice
profession: Haunted by the Violence at Attica
headline: Charles Pernasilice, Haunted by the Violence at Attica, Dies at 70
abstract: He was being held in the prison when inmates took it over in 1971. Murder charges against him were dropped, but he spent years trying to escape the memories.

name: Linda Kasabian
headline: Linda Kasabian, 73, Dies; Lookout Testified Against Charles Manson
abstract: She had been a Manson family member and was along on the nights of the infamous Tate-LaBianca murders, but she became the prosecution’s lead witness.

name: Maurizio Costanzo
headline: Maurizio Costanzo, Who Transformed Italian Talk Shows, Dies at 84
abstract: Praised by critics as the inventor of contemporary Italian television, he also used his position to take on the Sicilian Mafia, which tried to kill him.

name: Richard Anobile
headline: Richard Anobile, Chronicler of the Marx Brothers, Dies at 76
abstract: He produced many books about film. But Groucho Marx tried to stop distribution of one collaborative effort because he didn’t like seeing his salty and insulting remarks in print.

name: Wayne Shorter
profession: Innovator During an Era of Change in Jazz
headline: Wayne Shorter, Innovator During an Era of Change in Jazz, Dies at 89
abstract: His career as an influential tenor saxophonist and composer reached across more than half a century, tracking jazz’s complex evolution during that span.

name: Greta Andersen
headline: Greta Andersen, Champion Marathon Swimmer, Dies at 95
abstract: As a long-distance, open-water swimmer, she braved waves, sharks and darkness to break 18 world records.

name: Jesse Treviño
headline: Jesse Treviño, Chicano Artist Whose Muse Was San Antonio, Dies at 76
abstract: After losing his dominant right hand from a Vietnam War injury, he began chronicling Mexican American culture with his left.

name: Justin O. Schmidt
profession: Entomologist Known as King of Sting
headline: Justin O. Schmidt, Entomologist Known as ‘King of Sting,’ Dies at 75
abstract: Studying the venom of bees, wasps and ants, he was stung hundreds of times and famously ranked the stings in a colorful pain scale index.

name: Bernadette Carey Smith
profession: Black Reporter in Mostly White Newsrooms
headline: Bernadette Carey Smith, Black Reporter in Mostly White Newsrooms, Dies at 83
abstract: She was one of the first Black female journalists at The New York Times and The Washington Post. The Times put her on the staff of a women’s news section.

name: Rafael Viñoly
headline: Rafael Viñoly, Global Architect of Landmark Buildings, Dies at 78
abstract: Uruguayan-born and New York-based, he was responsible for major commercial and cultural buildings in nearly a dozen countries.

name: Steve Mackey
profession: Mainstay of the Britpop Band Pulp
headline: Steve Mackey, a Mainstay of the Britpop Band Pulp, Dies at 56
abstract: Shortly after he joined that long-running group in 1987, it rose from obscurity to chart-topping success in what came to be called the Cool Britannia era.

name: Pierre Apraxine
profession: Assembler of a Remarkable Trove of Photos
headline: Pierre Apraxine, 88, Assembler of a Remarkable Trove of Photos, Dies
abstract: Working with a paper magnate (and without a budget), he helped put together a collection that transformed the Metropolitan Museum of Art’s photography department.

name: Tom Sizemore
profession: Intense Actor With a Troubled Life
headline: Tom Sizemore, Intense Actor With a Troubled Life, Dies at 61
abstract: He earned praise for his work in films like “Saving Private Ryan” and “Black Hawk Down.” He also served prison time for drug possession and domestic abuse.

name: Gordon Pinsent
profession: Actor Known for Playing Twinkle-Eyed Rogues
headline: Gordon Pinsent, Actor Known for Playing Twinkle-Eyed Rogues, Dies at 92
abstract: Frustrated in Hollywood but celebrated in Canada, he drew widespread praise late in life for his performance opposite Julie Christie in “Away From Her.”

name: Ricou Browning
headline: Ricou Browning, Who Made the Black Lagoon Scary, Dies at 93
abstract: He helped bring “Flipper” to the movies and TV but was best known for his plunge in a monster suit in “Creature From the Black Lagoon.”

name: Jerry Richardson
headline: Jerry Richardson, Who Founded the Carolina Panthers, Dies at 86
abstract: He used the money he made playing for the Baltimore Colts to build the Hardee’s fast-food restaurant empire and then bought an N.F.L. expansion franchise.

name: Judy Heumann
profession: Led the Fight for Disability Rights
headline: Judy Heumann, Who Led the Fight for Disability Rights, Dies at 75
abstract: She successfully battled to become a teacher and went on to help bring about a revolution in the government’s treatment of the disabled.

name: David Lance Goines
headline: David Lance Goines, Who Shaped the Counterculture Aesthetic, Dies at 77
abstract: Starting with sensuous posters for Chez Panisse restaurant in Berkeley, his graphic work came to visually define the city and the bohemian ethos that took root there.

name: Gary Rossington
profession: Last of the Original Lynyrd Skynyrd
headline: Gary Rossington, Last of the Original Lynyrd Skynyrd, Dies at 71
abstract: He played the soaring slide guitar solo on “Free Bird,” co-wrote “Sweet Home Alabama” and survived the 1977 plane crash that killed three members of the band.

name: Joseph Zucchero
headline: Joseph Zucchero, Whose Sandwich Shop Inspired ‘The Bear,’ Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Beef, the Chicago restaurant he co-founded in the 1970s, specializes in the Italian beef, a classic American sandwich. The acclaimed FX series “The Bear” was filmed there.

name: Duong Tuong
profession: Opened Western Works to Vietnamese Readers
headline: Duong Tuong, Who Opened Western Works to Vietnamese Readers, Dies at 90
abstract: He translated works by Proust, Nabokov, Tolstoy and Emily Brontë into Vietnamese, and a classic Vietnamese poem, “The Tale of Kieu,” into English.

name: David Lindley
profession: Musicians Musician to the Rock Elite
headline: David Lindley, ‘Musician’s Musician’ to the Rock Elite, Dies at 78
abstract: He worked with a wide range of luminaries, most notably Jackson Browne, and there was seemingly no stringed instrument he couldn’t play.

name: Georgina Beyer
headline: Georgina Beyer, 65, Dies; Considered First Transgender Parliament Member
abstract: A New Zealand lawmaker, she fought for the rights of sex workers, L.G.B.T.Q. and Māori people, and won a battle to legalize civil unions for couples of any gender.

name: Ans Westra
profession: Her Photos Captured a Changing New Zealand
headline: Ans Westra, 86, Dies; Her Photos Captured a Changing New Zealand
abstract: She created a comprehensive record of the country’s social history, her focus often falling outside New Zealand’s white conservative mainstream.

name: Bert I. Gordon
headline: Bert I. Gordon, Auteur of Mutant Monster Movies, Dies at 100
abstract: Despite low budgets and years of mostly negative reviews, he gained a cult following for his giant villains, homemade effects and preposterous plotlines.

name: Ian Falconer
headline: Ian Falconer, Creator of Olivia, the Energetic Piglet, Dies at 63
abstract: He was a stage designer noted for his work in opera when he hit the best-seller list in 2000 with the first in a series of books for children.

name: Topol
profession: Star of Fiddler on the Roof Onscreen and Onstage
headline: Topol, Star of ‘Fiddler on the Roof’ Onscreen and Onstage, Dies at 87
abstract: Wide acclaim for his portrayal of Tevye helped make him, according to one newspaper, “Israel’s most famous export since the Jaffa orange.”

name: Rebecca Blank
headline: Rebecca Blank, Who Changed How Poverty Is Measured, Dies at 67
abstract: As an economics professor, she found serious flaws in how government determines who is poor in America. As under secretary of commerce, she fixed them.

name: Eugene Kohn
headline: Eugene Kohn, Architect of Skyscraping Reach, Dies at 92
abstract: His firm, Kohn Pedersen Fox, became an international force, merging the commercial with the creative in designing some of the world’s tallest buildings.

name: Jean Faut
profession: Star Pitcher in Womens Baseball League
headline: Jean Faut, Star Pitcher in Women’s Baseball League, Dies at 98
abstract: She threw two perfect games — something no major league pitcher has done — in the league that inspired the film “A League of Their Own.”

name: Robert Blake
profession: Baretta Star Acquitted in Wifes Murder
headline: Robert Blake, ‘Baretta’ Star Acquitted in Wife’s Murder, Dies at 89
abstract: His film and TV career began with “Our Gang” comedies and was highlighted by his performance as a killer in “In Cold Blood.” But he led a tempestuous life.

name: Barbara Bryant
profession: First Woman to Lead the Census Bureau
headline: Barbara Bryant, First Woman to Lead the Census Bureau, Dies at 96
abstract: When she took over in 1989, she found herself dealing with controversies over the 1990 count, including the problem of overlooked populations.

name: Traute Lafrenz
headline: Traute Lafrenz, Last Survivor of Anti-Hitler Group, Dies at 103
abstract: As a member of the White Rose, a small anti-Nazi resistance group, she used peaceful tactics to try persuading Germans to turn against Hitler.

name: Dilys Winn
profession: Brought Murder and Mystery to Manhattan
headline: Overlooked No More: Dilys Winn, Who Brought Murder and Mystery to Manhattan
abstract: She opened Murder Ink, believed to be the nation’s first mystery bookstore, and brought fans together through interactive whodunits and other events.

name: Suzy McKee Charnas
headline: Suzy McKee Charnas, Writer of Feminist Science Fiction, Dies at 83
abstract: She was best known for the Holdfast Chronicles, a series about a dystopic world in which once-enslaved women conquer their former male masters.

name: Otis Taylor
profession: Star Receiver for the Kansas City Chiefs
headline: Otis Taylor, Star Receiver for the Kansas City Chiefs, Dies at 80
abstract: An acrobatic player, he was the prototype for the big receivers who succeeded him. He caught a memorable touchdown in the Chiefs’ upset win in Super Bowl IV.

name: Spot
headline: Spot, Record Producer Who Captured the Fury of 1980s Punk, Dies at 71
abstract: A lifelong jazz aficionado, he changed course to produce bands like Black Flag and Hüsker Dü for the influential SST label.

name: Mary Bauermeister
headline: Mary Bauermeister, Avant-Garde Artist and Host, Dies at 88
abstract: She played a key role in the freewheeling performance art of the 1960s, and her biggest impact may have come from the open house she kept in an attic studio.

name: Bud Grant
headline: Bud Grant, Longtime Minnesota Vikings Coach, Dies at 95
abstract: He took his Vikings, with Fran Tarkenton at quarterback and the famed Purple People Eaters defensive line, to four Super Bowls — although he lost each time.

name: Jesus Alou
profession: Youngest in Trio of Baseball-Playing Brothers
headline: Jesus Alou, Youngest in Trio of Baseball-Playing Brothers, Dies at 80
abstract: He and his brothers, Felipe and Matty, were the only three brothers in major league history to play together in a single game.

name: Kenzaburo Oe
profession: Nobel Laureate and Critic of Postwar Japan
headline: Kenzaburo Oe, Nobel Laureate and Critic of Postwar Japan, Dies at 88
abstract: With his powerful novels and essays, Mr. Oe tried to ensure that Japan learned the lessons of its 20th-century militarism.

name: Masatoshi Ito
profession: King of Convenience Stores in Japan
headline: Masatoshi Ito, 98, the King of Convenience Stores in Japan, Dies
abstract: He introduced the American chain 7-Eleven to the country, covering the landscape with thousands of outlets and starting a retail revolution there.

name: Dick Fosbury
headline: Dick Fosbury, 76, Whose ‘Flop’ Transformed the High Jump, Is Dead
abstract: His back-first, neck-down leaping style struck many as a novelty act. After he won Olympic gold in 1968, it came to dominate his sport.

name: Joe Pepitone
profession: Rowdy Star When the Yankees Faded
headline: Joe Pepitone, Rowdy Star When the Yankees Faded, Dies at 82
abstract: He had All-Star years, won three Gold Gloves, hit with power and was a fan favorite, but as the team’s fortunes dimmed, his renegade lifestyle had its costs.

name: Patricia Schroeder
headline: Patricia Schroeder, Feminist Force in Congress, Dies at 82
abstract: In a long career in the House and armed with a barbed wit, she helped win legislation on family leave, pregnancy discrimination and other progressive causes.

name: Jiang Yanyong
headline: Jiang Yanyong, Who Helped Expose China’s SARS Crisis, Dies at 91
abstract: A retired military surgeon, he blew the whistle in 2003 on Beijing’s cover-up of the epidemic. He was later punished for denouncing the Tiananmen Square crackdown.

name: John Jakes
profession: Hit the Jackpot With Historical Novels
headline: John Jakes, Who Hit the Jackpot With Historical Novels, Dies at 90
abstract: His sagas of the Revolution and the Civil War sold tens of millions of copies, were adapted for TV and put him in the pantheon of big-name authors.

name: Amy Schwartz
profession: Captured Life as Viewed by a Child
headline: Amy Schwartz, Who Captured Life as Viewed by a Child, Dies at 68
abstract: The dozens of books for young readers that she wrote and illustrated had a knack for finding “the wondrous in the mundane.”

name: Richard Rosenberg
headline: Richard Rosenberg, Who Rejuvenated Bank of America, Dies at 92
abstract: As chief executive and chairman in the 1990s, he helped turn the bank into the nation’s second-largest through a series of acquisitions.

name: Frank T. Griswold III
headline: Frank T. Griswold III, Bridge-Building Bishop, Dies at 85
abstract: As head of the Episcopal Church in America, he consecrated the denomination’s first gay bishop, ordained women as priests and formed a communion with Lutherans.

name: Phyllida Barlow
headline: Phyllida Barlow, 78, Dies; Sculptor of Playful, Scale-Defying Works
abstract: After decades of teaching, the British-born Ms. Barlow found fame as an artist late in life, creating monumental sculptures that wryly commented on industrial society.

name: Lynn Seymour
profession: Acclaimed Ballerina and a Dramatic Force
headline: Lynn Seymour, Acclaimed Ballerina and a Dramatic Force, Dies at 83
abstract: Considered one of the greats of her era, she partnered with Nureyev, Baryshnikov and others, bringing a passionate style to roles in dance, both ballet and modern.

name: Bobby Caldwell
headline: Bobby Caldwell, Silky-Voiced R&B Crooner, Dies at 71
abstract: His much-covered 1978 hit “What You Won’t Do for Love” launched him on a prolific career that spanned decades and genres.

name: Lewis Spratlan
profession: Took Winding Route to Music Pulitzer
headline: Lewis Spratlan, 82, Is Dead; Took Winding Route to Music Pulitzer
abstract: His opera sat unproduced for decades. Then a piece of it garnered one of the field’s top prizes. Then it sat some more.

name: Simone Segouin
headline: Simone Segouin, Teenage Fighter in French Resistance, Dies at 97
abstract: Portrayed in Life magazine in 1944 as a simple farm girl brandishing a submachine gun, she became a symbol of the partisans who helped defeat the Nazis.

name: Jerry Samuels
headline: Jerry Samuels, Creator of a Novelty Hit, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Under the name Napoleon XIV, he recorded “They’re Coming to Take Me Away, Ha-Haaa!” and, to almost everyone’s surprise, it stormed the charts in 1966.

name: Jim Mellen
profession: Original Member of the Militant Weathermen
headline: Jim Mellen, an Original Member of the Militant Weathermen, Dies at 87
abstract: A former college professor among student revolutionaries, he brought a fiery Marxist sensibility to the group before it veered into violence.

name: Lance Reddick
profession: Star of The Wire and John Wick
headline: Lance Reddick, Star of ‘The Wire’ and ‘John Wick,’ Dies at 60
abstract: A prolific actor, he also starred in the Amazon series “Bosch” and had recently branched out into video games like Horizon Zero Dawn and the Destiny franchise.

name: Polito Vega
profession: Salsa King of New York Radio
headline: Polito Vega, Salsa ‘King’ of New York Radio, Dies at 84
abstract: In a career that began in 1960, the Puerto Rico-born Mr. Vega became, one admirer said, “the architect of Hispanic radio at a global level.”

name: Cruz Miguel Ortíz Cuadra
profession: Face of Puerto Rican Culinary History
headline: Cruz Miguel Ortíz Cuadra, ‌67, Face of Puerto Rican Culinary History, Dies
abstract: The island’s leading expert on its cuisine and its roots, he sought to educate the world about it through books, podcasts and teaching.

name: Stuart Hodes
headline: Stuart Hodes, Who Danced With Martha Graham, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Devoting his long life to dance, he was also a choreographer, an educator and an author, and was still onstage in his 90s.

name: Lilian Lindsay
headline: Overlooked No More: Lilian Lindsay, Britain’s First Female Dentist
abstract: The profession was considered unladylike in 1890s England, where she was refused admission to dental school. But she found one in Scotland, and became a notable figure in dentistry.

name: Patrick French
headline: Patrick French, Unsparing Biographer of V.S. Naipaul, Dies at 56
abstract: He was a historian of India and Tibet, but best known for his biography of Naipaul, which one reviewer described as “a portrait of the artist as a monster.”

name: Willis Reed
profession: Hall of Fame Center for Champion Knicks
headline: Willis Reed, Hall of Fame Center for Champion Knicks, Dies at 80
abstract: He was beloved by New York fans for his willingness to play hurt, as memorably exemplified in the decisive Game 7 of the 1970 N.B.A. finals at Madison Square Garden.

name: Virginia Zeani
headline: Virginia Zeani, Versatile and Durable Soprano, Dies at 97
abstract: A noted Violetta in Verdi’s “La Traviata,” she was “a woman blessed with beauty both physical and vocal,” Plácido Domingo said.

name: Warren Boroson
headline: Warren Boroson, Who Surveyed Psychiatrists on Goldwater, Dies at 88
abstract: The defeated Republican presidential candidate sued Mr. Boroson and the magazine he worked for, saying it had libeled him for suggesting that he was mentally unfit for the presidency.

name: John Jenrette Jr.
headline: John Jenrette Jr., Congressman Nabbed in Abscam Sting, Dies at 86
abstract: Once a rising star of the Democratic Party, he served 13 months in prison for bribery after being targeted in an F.B.I. scam involving a phony sheikh.

name: William A. Wulf
headline: William A. Wulf, Pioneering Computer Scientist, Dies at 83
abstract: One of the first people to receive a graduate degree in the field, Dr. Wulf helped to adapt an early Pentagon communications web into the network that eventually grew into the internet.

name: Raphael Mechoulam
headline: Raphael Mechoulam, ‘Father of Cannabis Research,’ Dies at 92
abstract: His work helped break down the chemical structures of THC, the psychoactive compound in marijuana, to figure out how cannabis makes users high.

name: Fuzzy Haskins
headline: Fuzzy Haskins, Who Helped Turn Doo-Wop Into P-Funk, Dies at 81
abstract: As a teenager, he joined forces with George Clinton. Their vocal group, the Parliaments, morphed into Parliament-Funkadelic, one of the wildest acts of the 1970s.

name: Marisol Malaret
headline: Marisol Malaret, First Puerto Rican Miss Universe, Dies at 73
abstract: Edging out Miss USA, Ms. Malaret — who was also the first winner from the Caribbean — brokered her fame to become a television host and magazine editor back home.

name: Howard Brandston
headline: Howard Brandston, Who Made His Mark With Light, Dies at 87
abstract: His lighting design company applied his art globally to landmarks, including the Statue of Liberty, as well as architecture, exhibitions and even penguins in a zoo.

name: Jacqueline Gold
profession: Executive Tapped Into the Female Libido
headline: Jacqueline Gold, 62, Dies; Executive Tapped Into the Female Libido
abstract: She made Britain’s Ann Summers shops a thriving source of lingerie and sex toys and became a role model for female entrepreneurs.

name: Greg Wittine
profession: Once a Hero for Disabled Boy Scouts
headline: Greg Wittine, Once a Hero for Disabled Boy Scouts, Dies at 67
abstract: As a young man with cerebral palsy, he gained notice for his quest to be an Eagle Scout, which changed Scouting. But his name was lost to popular memory.

name: John Woods
headline: John Woods, Masterly Translator of Thomas Mann, Dies at 80
abstract: Among the other German writers whose work he rendered into English was Arno Schmidt, whose Joycean wordplay presented a daunting challenge.

name: Gordon E. Moore
headline: Gordon E. Moore, Intel Co-Founder Behind Moore’s Law, Dies at 94
abstract: His prediction in the 1960s about rapid advances in computer chip technology charted a course for the age of high tech.

name: Scott Johnson
headline: Scott Johnson, Playfully Inventive Composer, Is Dead at 70
abstract: In works like “John Somebody,” he mixed the structural rigor of classical composition with the ebullient sound and attitude of rock.

name: Bobbi Ercoline
profession: Hug Became a Symbol of Woodstock
headline: Bobbi Ercoline, Whose Hug Became a Symbol of Woodstock, Dies at 73
abstract: Embracing her boyfriend, a blanket around them, she appeared on the cover of the ubiquitous soundtrack album of “Woodstock,” the 1970 documentary film about the music festival.

name: Gladys Kessler
headline: Gladys Kessler, Judge Who Curbed Deceptive Tobacco Ads, Dies at 85
abstract: In a landmark case, she ruled in 2006 that cigarette companies had been deceiving the public about the health hazards of smoking, violating racketeering laws.

name: Yang Bing-yi
profession: Brought Soup Dumplings to the World
headline: Yang Bing-yi, Who Brought Soup Dumplings to the World, Dies at 96
abstract: Starting with a modest shop in Taiwan in 1958, he built Din Tai Fung into a global dumpling and noodle empire, earning a Michelin star along the way.

name: Julie Anne Peters
headline: Julie Anne Peters, Whose Young-Adult Books Caused a Stir, Dies at 71
abstract: Her 2004 novel, “Luna,” broke new ground by having a transgender teenager as a main character. That book and others she wrote have been targets of conservatives.

name: Walter Cole
headline: Walter Cole, Who Dazzled as Darcelle, the World’s Oldest Drag Performer, Dies at 92
abstract: He turned a run-down tavern into a drag cabaret that became a hub and a fund-raising powerhouse for the L.G.B.T.Q. community as well as a beloved Portland, Ore., institution.

name: Mark Russell
headline: Mark Russell, Piano-Playing Political Satirist, Dies at 90
abstract: Washington was his main quarry. Did he have any writers? “Oh, yes — 100 in the Senate and 435 in the House of Representatives.”

name: Michael Blackwood
headline: Michael Blackwood, Who Captured 20th-Century Artists on Film, Dies at 88
abstract: He made cinéma vérité documentaries — more than 160 — about musicians (Thelonious Monk), architects (Frank Gehry), composers (Philip Glass) and sculptors (Isamu Noguchi).

name: Royston Ellis
profession: Bridge Between Beat Poets and the Beatles
headline: Royston Ellis, Bridge Between Beat Poets and the Beatles, Dies at 82
abstract: Making his name with a blend of poetry and rock ’n’ roll he called “rocketry,” he straddled two eras of British youth culture at the dawn of the 1960s.

name: Margot Stern Strom
headline: Margot Stern Strom, Anti-Bigotry Educator, Dies at 81
abstract: She started an organization whose curriculums challenge teenagers to understand the roots of the Holocaust, racism, apartheid and other human injustices.

name: Ryuichi Sakamoto
headline: Ryuichi Sakamoto, Oscar-Winning Composer, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Sakamoto, whose work with Yellow Magic Orchestra influenced electronic music, composed scores for “The Last Emperor” and “The Revenant.”

name: Seymour Stein
headline: Seymour Stein, Record Industry Giant Who Signed Big Names, Dies at 80
abstract: Steeped in music, he championed Madonna, the Ramones, Talking Heads, the Pretenders and more on his Sire label, and helped found the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame.

name: Raghavan Iyer
profession: Made Indian Cooking Accessible Across America
headline: Raghavan Iyer, 61, Dies; Made Indian Cooking Accessible Across America
abstract: He broke with traditions in writing cookbooks, teaching thousands of cooks, consulting for restaurants, leading tours, catering meals and creating frozen dinners.

name: Emahoy Tsegué-Maryam Guèbrou
headline: Emahoy Tsegué-Maryam Guèbrou, Nun With a Musical Gift, Dies at 99
abstract: Ethiopian-born, she was on track to be a concert pianist before choosing a monastic life. But her later piano recordings gained fans. Norah Jones called them “beautiful.”

name: Nigel Lawson
headline: Nigel Lawson, Economic Force Under Thatcher, Dies at 91
abstract: As chancellor of the Exchequer, he helped lift Britain with tax cuts and other Conservative measures — the “Lawson Boom” — but harder times followed, and he resigned in bitterness.

name: Bing Newcomb
headline: Bing Newcomb, Whose E*Trade Transformed Stock Trading, Dies at 79
abstract: He wrote a program that allowed people to buy and sell stocks on their home computers and co-founded a company that reaped its benefits.

name: Klaus Teuber
profession: Creator of the Board Game Catan
headline: Klaus Teuber, Creator of the Board Game Catan, Dies at 70
abstract: He created the strategy game about settling a new land in 1995. Millions of copies have been sold since then, and it’s played all over the world.

name: Neal Boenzi
profession: Top New York Times Photographer for Four Decades
headline: Neal Boenzi, 97, Top New York Times Photographer for Four Decades, Dies
abstract: He built a reputation for finding compelling subjects on the street. “Anyone can take a picture,” he liked to say, “but are you a journalist?”

name: Elizabeth de Cuevas
profession: Sculptor With a Flair for the Monumental
headline: Elizabeth de Cuevas, Sculptor With a Flair for the Monumental, Dies at 94
abstract: A Rockefeller heiress who was inspired by the monuments of Europe, she fashioned towering metal creations that channeled the cosmic.

name: Jane LaTour
profession: Fighter for Women in Labor Unions
headline: Jane LaTour, Fighter for Women in Labor Unions, Dies at 76
abstract: No stranger to blue-collar work herself, she pushed for equality in male-dominated unions and as a writer chronicled the struggles of “sisters in the brotherhoods.”

name: Mimi Sheraton
profession: Innovative New York Times Food Critic
headline: Mimi Sheraton, Innovative New York Times Food Critic, Dies at 97
abstract: Ms. Sheraton, who worked for many publications in a six-decade career, was the first restaurant reviewer to wear a disguise in order to get a normal diner’s experience.

name: Colin McCord
headline: Colin McCord, Who Helped Impose a Smoking Ban, Dies at 94
abstract: The indoors prohibition, in New York City, was just one public health accomplishment. His global efforts on behalf of woman and children saved countless lives.

name: Harry Lorayne
headline: Harry Lorayne, Dazzling Master of Total Recall, Is Dead at 96
abstract: A memory expert and magician who was a favorite guest of Johnny Carson’s, he astonished audiences by reeling off the names of hundreds of people he had only just met.

name: James Bowman
headline: James Bowman, Who Helped Resurrect the Countertenor, Dies at 81
abstract: He took up the repertory for the highest male voice at a time when few were performing it. He was particularly known for two roles in Britten operas.

name: Nora Forster
profession: Married (and Stayed Married to) a Sex Pistol
headline: Nora Forster, 80, Who Married (and Stayed Married to) a Sex Pistol, Dies
abstract: A German publishing heiress and music promoter, she settled in London in time for the 1970s punk-rock explosion and became the muse to its baddest boy.

name: Benjamin B. Ferencz
headline: Benjamin B. Ferencz, Last Surviving Nuremberg Prosecutor, Dies at 103
abstract: In addition to convicting prominent Nazi war criminals, he crusaded for an international criminal court and for laws to end wars of aggression.

name: Bill Butler
headline: Bill Butler, Cinematographer Best Known for ‘Jaws,’ Dies at 101
abstract: He came up with a mechanism that allowed Steven Spielberg to film underwater. His work on “One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest” earned him an Oscar nomination.

name: Mel King
