profession: Boston Mayoral Bid Eased Racial Tensions
headline: Mel King, Whose Boston Mayoral Bid Eased Racial Tensions, Dies at 94
abstract: The first Black finalist for mayor of the city, he was credited, along with the eventual winner, Raymond Flynn, with running a respectful, calming campaign.

name: Alice Ball
headline: Overlooked No More: Alice Ball, Chemist Who Created a Treatment for Leprosy
abstract: After she died — and just a year after her discovery — another scientist took credit for her work. It would be more than half a century until her story resurfaced.

name: María Kodama
headline: María Kodama, Keeper of the Borges Legacy, Dies at 86
abstract: She was a writer and translator but was best known as the widow of Jorge Luis Borges, one of Latin America’s great writers.

name: Hobie Landrith
headline: Hobie Landrith, the First New York Met, Dies at 93
abstract: A major league catcher for 14 seasons, he was the first player picked by the newly formed Mets in the expansion draft in 1961.

name: Craig Breedlove
profession: Once the Fastest Man on Earth
headline: Craig Breedlove, 86, Once the Fastest Man on Earth, Dies
abstract: A former firefighter, he broke the land-speed record repeatedly in the 1960s in jet-engine-powered vehicles, all called Spirit of America.

name: Myriam Ullens
headline: Myriam Ullens, 70, Philanthropic Baroness, Is Killed
abstract: A stepson was held on charges of shooting her over family money. She started institutions in Belgium, Nepal and China, including a major museum in Beijing.

name: Jennifer Muller
headline: Jennifer Muller, Choreographer Whose Dances Told Human Tales, Dies at 78
abstract: In a postmodern era dominated by minimalism and conceptual themes, her work focused on emotion and storytelling.

name: Michael Lerner
profession: Actor Seen in Elf and Barton Fink
headline: Michael Lerner, Actor Seen in ‘Elf’ and ‘Barton Fink,’ Dies at 81
abstract: “I am a chameleon,” Mr. Lerner, who was nominated for a supporting-actor Oscar in 1992, said of his long career as a character actor in movies and television.

name: Michael Lerner
profession: Founder of a Combative Jewish Magazine
headline: Michael Lerner, 81, Is Dead; Founder of a Combative Jewish Magazine
abstract: His publication, Tikkun, was a leading voice for left-wing American Jews. His ideas about “the politics of meaning” were embraced by Hillary Clinton.

name: Al Jaffee
headline: Al Jaffee, Inventive Cartoonist at Mad Magazine, Dies at 102
abstract: For 55 years he created the fold-in (as opposed to, say, Playboy’s fold-out), giving readers a satirical double-take on whatever was going on in the news.

name: Vivan Sundaram
profession: Pivotal, and Political, Figure in Indian Art
headline: Vivan Sundaram, 79, Dies; a Pivotal, and Political, Figure in Indian Art
abstract: Veering from European-inspired abstraction, he embraced multimedia forms to reflect the realities of a country torn by ethnic and religious violence.

name: Carl Fischer
headline: Carl Fischer, Who Shot Attention-Getting Esquire Covers, Dies at 98
abstract: Among his most famous photographs was one depicting Muhammad Ali as a martyr stuck full of arrows.

name: Kwame Brathwaite
profession: Photographer With a Lens on Black Pride
headline: Kwame Brathwaite, 85, Photographer With a Lens on Black Pride, Is Dead
abstract: Part of the “Black is beautiful” movement during the civil rights era, he trained his camera on athletes, musicians and models as well as everyday people.

name: Anne Perry
profession: Crime Writer With Her Own Dark Tale
headline: Anne Perry, Crime Writer With Her Own Dark Tale, Dies at 84
abstract: She was well into her career as a prolific author of historical crime fiction when a murderous past was publicly revealed and dramatized in a 1994 movie.

name: Alicia C. Shepard
profession: Ombudsman Defended NPR in Torture Debate
headline: Alicia C. Shepard, 69, Dies; Ombudsman Defended NPR in Torture Debate
abstract: In one of many jobs she held in a diverse journalism career, she dealt with charges that the network was “serving as right-wing apologists for waterboarding.”

name: Virginia Norwood
headline: Virginia Norwood, ‘Mother’ of Satellite Imaging Systems, Dies at 96
abstract: A pioneer in aerospace, she invented a technology that has enabled scientists to map and study the earth for more than 50 years.

name: Mary Quant
headline: Mary Quant, British Fashion Revolutionary, Dies at 93
abstract: Known as the mother of the miniskirt, clad in her signature play clothes and boots, with huge painted eyes, fake freckles and a bob, she epitomized London’s Swinging Sixties.

name: Rachel Pollack
profession: Transgender Activist and Authority on Tarot
headline: Rachel Pollack, Transgender Activist and Authority on Tarot, Dies at 77
abstract: Her science fiction writing won awards. Her tarot books won her a devoted following. And she created DC Comics’ first transgender superhero.

name: Meir Shalev
profession: Novels Found Humor in Israeli Life
headline: Meir Shalev, Whose Novels Found Humor in Israeli Life, Dies at 74
abstract: He focused mostly on the half-century before Israeli independence, finding the plight of the early Zionists ripe for affectionate satire.

name: Pierre Lacotte
headline: Pierre Lacotte, Choreographer Who Aided a Defection, Dies at 91
abstract: He befriended Rudolf Nureyev in 1961 while the Kirov Ballet was in Paris and witnessed his headline-making defection at the height of the Cold War.

name: Leonard Abrams
profession: Chronicler of 1980s East Village Art Boom
headline: Leonard Abrams, 68, Chronicler of 1980s East Village Art Boom, Dies
abstract: His newspaper, the East Village Eye, was as scrappy and iconoclastic as the young maverick stars its pages brought to life.

name: Billy Waugh
headline: Billy Waugh, 93, ‘Godfather of the Green Berets,’ Is Dead
abstract: He was a Special Forces soldier during the Vietnam War and then worked for the C.I.A., tracking Osama bin Laden in Sudan and fighting in Afghanistan after 9/11.

name: Edward Koren
profession: Cartoon Creatures Poked Fun at People
headline: Edward Koren, 87, Whose Cartoon Creatures Poked Fun at People, Dies
abstract: For six decades in The New Yorker and elsewhere, his hairy, toothy, long-nosed characters offered witty commentary on the foibles of the American middle class.

name: Keith Johnstone
headline: Keith Johnstone, Champion of Improvisational Theater, Dies at 90
abstract: The theatrical games and performance techniques Mr. Johnstone developed became a familiar part of the acting arsenal.

name: Hedda Kleinfeld Schachter
profession: Built an Empire of Tulle and Satin
headline: Hedda Kleinfeld Schachter Dies at 99; Built an Empire of Tulle and Satin
abstract: With her husband, Jack, she expanded I. Kleinfeld & Son into a bridal superstore that became a New York City institution.

name: Edward H. Meyer
headline: Edward H. Meyer, Who Created an Advertising Powerhouse, Dies at 96
abstract: Known for his iron resolve and his attention to detail, he transformed Grey Advertising from a midsize agency into a multinational powerhouse.

name: Ahmad Jamal
headline: Ahmad Jamal, Whose Spare Style Redefined Jazz Piano, Dies at 92
abstract: He was known for his laid-back style and for his influence on, among others, Miles Davis, who once said, “All my inspiration comes from Ahmad Jamal.”

name: Robert Trotman
profession: Opened Swimming Lanes to Minority Children
headline: Robert Trotman, 82, Dies; Opened Swimming Lanes to Minority Children
abstract: The club he started as a coach has helped young Black and Hispanic youths learn to swim and compete in the sport in urban areas not known as oases for it.

name: Bernice Rose
headline: Bernice Rose, Curator Who Elevated the Art of Drawing, Dies at 87
abstract: Her exhibitions, at the Museum of Modern Art in Manhattan and elsewhere, showed that drawings were far more than preliminary works executed on paper.

name: John J. Doherty
headline: John J. Doherty, Stalwart Sanitation Commissioner, Dies at 84
abstract: He ran New York City’s Sanitation Department, the world’s largest, longer than anyone else, disposing of three million tons of garbage a year and coping with snowstorms and hurricanes.

name: Freddie Scappaticci
profession: May Have Been British Spy Stakeknife
headline: Freddie Scappaticci, Who May Have Been British Spy ‘Stakeknife,’ Is Dead
abstract: He denied that he was Stakeknife, the code name of a high-ranking British mole in the Irish Republican Army during the Northern Ireland conflict.

name: Gloria Dea
headline: Gloria Dea, Magician Rediscovered Late in Life, Dies at 100
abstract: She had faded from public view in the last half-century, until some young magicians realized she was probably the first to perform a magic act at a Las Vegas casino.

name: Blair Tindall
headline: Blair Tindall, Whose Music Memoir Scandalized, Dies at 63
abstract: Her 2005 book, “Mozart in the Jungle,” lived up to its subtitle, “Sex, Drugs, and Classical Music,” and was later made into an Amazon TV series.

name: Otis Redding III
headline: Otis Redding III, Who Followed His Father Into Music, Dies at 59
abstract: He was grateful for Otis Redding’s enduring legacy, he said, even if it overshadowed his efforts to make music of his own.

name: Leon Levine
profession: Made a Billion One Dollar at a Time
headline: Leon Levine, Who Made a Billion One Dollar at a Time, Dies at 85
abstract: He created the discount chain retailer Family Dollar, which found success, and criticism, by catering to the poor.

name: Todd Haimes
headline: Todd Haimes, 66, Who Rebuilt the Roundabout Theater Company, Dies
abstract: After rescuing the company from bankruptcy, he turned it into a major player on Broadway and one of the largest nonprofit theater companies in the country.

name: Richard Riordan
profession: Mayor of an Uneasy Los Angeles
headline: Richard Riordan, Mayor of an Uneasy Los Angeles, Dies at 92
abstract: He was a successful businessman before taking office in 1993 amid civil unrest after the police beating of Rodney King. He became known for impolitic wisecracking.

name: Helen Barolini
headline: Helen Barolini, Chronicler of Italian American Women, Dies at 97
abstract: As a novelist, a poet and an editor, she sought to illuminate rarely told stories of her immigrant female forebears in a new land.

name: Loren Cameron
profession: His Camera Brought Transgender Men to Light
headline: Loren Cameron, 63, Dies; His Camera Brought Transgender Men to Light
abstract: Mr. Cameron’s groundbreaking portraits of himself and others, collected in his book, “Body Alchemy,” inspired a generation of transgender people.

name: Dave Wilcox
profession: Hall of Fame Linebacker for the 49ers
headline: Dave Wilcox, Hall of Fame Linebacker for the 49ers, Dies at 80
abstract: A seven-time Pro Bowl selection known for his physical style, he was one of the game’s best and most durable linebackers.

name: Jessica Burstein
headline: Jessica Burstein, Whose Camera Captured New York, Dies at 76
abstract: She photographed “Law & Order” and Elaine’s. And in 2006, she was given exclusive access to chronicle the construction of the new Yankee Stadium.

name: Bud Shuster
headline: Bud Shuster, Unabashed ‘Asphalt King’ of Congress, Dies at 91
abstract: A Pennsylvania Republican, he targeted a disproportionate share of federal highway funds to his Appalachian district during his 28 years in the House.

name: Valda Setterfield
profession: Star in the Postmodern Dance Firmament
headline: Valda Setterfield Dies at 88; a Star in the Postmodern Dance Firmament
abstract: A dancer with a singularly theatrical presence, she was best known for her long collaboration with her husband, the choreographer David Gordon.

name: Charles Stanley
headline: Charles Stanley, Atlanta Pastor Who Preached to the World, Dies at 90
abstract: He helped lead a conservative takeover of the Southern Baptist Convention, and he mastered the use of media to spread his message.

name: Barry Humphries
headline: Barry Humphries (Dame Edna to You, Possums) Is Dead at 89
abstract: Bewigged, bejeweled and bejowled, Mr. Humphries’s creation was one of the longest-lived characters ever channeled by a single performer.

name: Elizabeth Wagner Reed
profession: Resurrected Legacies of Women in Science
headline: Overlooked No More: Elizabeth Wagner Reed, Who Resurrected Legacies of Women in Science
abstract: Reed made several discoveries in genetics and dedicated her career toward supporting women scientists. Yet she herself fell into obscurity.

name: Gail Christian
headline: Gail Christian, Trailblazing News Correspondent, Dies at 83
abstract: An on-air career seemed unlikely for a Black woman in the 1970s. It didn’t help that she had been imprisoned for armed robbery. But she broke barriers.

name: Elisabeth Kopp
headline: Elisabeth Kopp, Swiss Politician Who Made History, Dies at 86
abstract: In 1984 she became the first woman elected to the country’s governing council, but a scandal prevented her from being the first woman to serve as president.

name: Bruce Haigh
headline: Bruce Haigh, Diplomat Who Helped Battle Apartheid, Dies at 77
abstract: An Australian, he assisted South African dissidents like the journalist Donald Woods, whose story was told in the movie “Cry Freedom.”

name: Len Goodman
headline: Len Goodman, ‘Dancing With the Stars’ Judge, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Goodman, who was also a longtime judge on the British show “Strictly Come Dancing,” was known for his wry humor, wit and colorful phrases.

name: Herb Douglas
profession: Olympic Medalist Inspired by Jesse Owens
headline: Herb Douglas, Olympic Medalist Inspired by Jesse Owens, Dies at 101
abstract: The oldest living U.S. Olympic medalist, he met Owens as a teenager, won bronze in the broad jump in 1948 and later created an award in his idol’s honor.

name: Megan Terry
profession: Feminist Playwright and Rock Musical Innovator
headline: Megan Terry, Feminist Playwright and Rock Musical Innovator, Dies at 90
abstract: She wrote 70 plays, won an Obie Award and wrote and directed “Viet Rock,” a musical that predated “Hair” and is considered the first U.S. stage work to address the Vietnam War.

name: H. Dale Hemmerdinger
headline: H. Dale Hemmerdinger, Who Led the M.T.A. Through Recession, Dies at 78
abstract: A developer, he steered the agency as its chairman in making progress on the L.I.R.R.-Grand Central connection project and in holding a fare increase to 25 cents in the 2000s.

name: Harry Belafonte
headline: Harry Belafonte, 96, Dies; Barrier-Breaking Singer, Actor and Activist
abstract: In the 1950s, when segregation was still widespread, his ascent to the upper echelon of show business was historic. But his primary focus was civil rights.

name: Alton H. Maddox Jr.
profession: Lawyer in Tawana Brawley Rape Hoax
headline: Alton H. Maddox Jr., 77, Lawyer in Tawana Brawley Rape Hoax, Dies
abstract: The case inflamed racial tensions, with Mr. Maddox later calling New York “the Mississippi of the ’90s.” After the fraud was revealed, he was unrepentant.

name: Michael Denneny
profession: Editor Created Outlets for Gay Literature
headline: Michael Denneny, 80, Dies; Editor Created Outlets for Gay Literature
abstract: In a largely closeted era, he was a founder of a magazine devoted to gay and lesbian writing and an imprint devoted to L.G.B.T. fiction and nonfiction.

name: Ken Potts
profession: Oldest Survivor of U.S.S. Arizona Sinking
headline: Ken Potts, Oldest Survivor of U.S.S. Arizona Sinking, Dies at 102
abstract: Only one other known veteran of the battleship bombed by the Japanese at Pearl Harbor remains alive, at 101.

name: Emily Meggett
headline: Emily Meggett, Matriarch of Gullah Geechee Cuisine, Is Dead at 90
abstract: She never used a recipe in cooking, but she published a best-selling cookbook that documented the Gullah Geechee food of the coastal South.

name: Karl Berger
profession: Opened Minds of Generations of Musicians
headline: Karl Berger, 88, Who Opened Minds of Generations of Musicians, Is Dead
abstract: A vibraphonist, pianist, educator and musical thinker, he co-founded the Creative Music Studio to bring musicians together to foster improvisation.

name: April Stevens
profession: Her Deep Purple Became a Surprise Hit
headline: April Stevens Dies at 93; Her ‘Deep Purple’ Became a Surprise Hit
abstract: Her unusual version of the standard, which she recorded with her brother, Nino Tempo, reached No. 1 on the Billboard chart in 1963 and won a Grammy.

name: Jerry Springer
profession: Host of a Raucous TV Talk Show
headline: Jerry Springer, Host of a Raucous TV Talk Show, Is Dead at 79
abstract: The confrontational “Jerry Springer Show” ran for nearly three decades and became a cultural phenomenon. Mr. Springer also had a career in politics.

name: Carolyn Bryant Donham
headline: Carolyn Bryant Donham Dies at 88; Her Words Doomed Emmett Till
abstract: She accused Emmett, 14, of accosting her, and her testimony led to the acquittals of her husband and his half brother in a murder that helped galvanize the civil rights movement.

name: Dick Groat
headline: Dick Groat, Hoops Whiz Who Became a Star Shortstop, Dies at 92
abstract: He insisted he was better at basketball, but as a shortstop he won a batting championship and an M.V.P. Award and was a five-time All-Star.

name: Jane Davis Doggett
profession: Graphic Designer Helped People Find Their Way
headline: Jane Davis Doggett, 93, Dies; Graphic Designer Helped People Find Their Way
abstract: She was a pioneer in making airports and other complex public spaces easier to navigate.

name: John Underwood
headline: John Underwood, Stylish Sportswriter and Author, Dies at 88
abstract: After fishing with Ted Williams in 1967, he collaborated with him on two books. He also helped the Alabama football coach Bear Bryant write his autobiography.

name: Stew Leonard Sr.
headline: Stew Leonard Sr. Dies at 93; Founded ‘Disneyland of Dairy Stores’
abstract: A former milkman, he combined attentive customer service, low prices, quality goods and gimmicks, like singing cows, into a retailing grocery phenomenon.

name: Mark Stewart
headline: Mark Stewart, Fiery British Rocker, Is Dead at 62
abstract: His band, the Pop Group, was anything but pop, blending anti-authoritarian fury with a ferocious mix of punk, funk and experimental jazz.

name: Charles Hull
headline: Charles Hull, Who Brought Theater to Young Audiences, Dies at 92
abstract: The award-winning company he co-founded, Theaterworks USA, went on the road to introduce millions of students to professional productions of plays and musicals.

name: James Harithas
headline: James Harithas, Maverick Museum Director and Founder, Dies at 90
abstract: Whether directing august art museums or scrappy upstarts, he championed art-world outsiders and socially conscious and political art. He gave Yoko Ono her first solo show.

name: Harold S. Kushner
headline: Rabbi Harold S. Kushner, Reassuring Best-Selling Author, Dies at 88
abstract: With a wide-reaching spiritual message in books like “When Bad Things Happen to Good People,” he drew on his own experience with grief and doubt.

name: John Stobart
headline: John Stobart, Celebrated Maritime Painter, Dies at 93
abstract: Dismissing modern art as “baloney,” he made millions as a master of historical harbor paintings.

name: Ralph Boston
profession: Leaped 27 Feet and Landed in History
headline: Ralph Boston, Who Leaped 27 Feet and Landed in History, Dies at 83
abstract: A dominant long jumper in the 1960s, he first shattered a 25-year-old record set by Jesse Owens before becoming the first to break the 27-foot mark.

name: Keshub Mahindra
headline: Keshub Mahindra, Billionaire Indian Industrialist, Dies at 99
abstract: He expanded a family steel and jeep business into an international leviathan, but his career was stained by a conviction in the 1984 Bhopal disaster.

name: Yvonne Jacquette
profession: Painter of Views From on High
headline: Yvonne Jacquette, Painter of Views From on High, Dies at 88
abstract: She was known to hire airplanes, hang out of helicopters and explore skyscrapers to get the towering perspectives required for her unusual landscapes.

name: Gordon Lightfoot
headline: Gordon Lightfoot, Hitmaking Singer-Songwriter, Is Dead at 84
abstract: His rich baritone voice and songs like “Sundown,” “The Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald” and “If You Could Read My Mind” made him a top artist of the 1970s.

name: Mike Shannon
headline: Mike Shannon, a St. Louis Cardinal for Life, Dies at 83
abstract: A St. Louis native, he devoted his entire career to the team — first as an outfielder and third baseman and then, for 50 years, as a radio announcer.

name: Robert Patrick
profession: Early and Prolific Playwright of Gay Life
headline: Robert Patrick, Early and Prolific Playwright of Gay Life, Dies at 85
abstract: He got his start at Caffe Cino, the birthplace of Off Off Broadway. His first of hundreds of plays, performed there in 1964, is a milestone of gay theater.

name: Tori Bowie
headline: Tori Bowie, World Champion Sprinter, Is Dead at 32
abstract: She won three Olympic medals in 2016 and the world championship the next year in an intense 100-meter dash.

name: Pamela Timmins
headline: Pamela Timmins, Press Secretary to Jacqueline Kennedy, Dies at 85
abstract: She was the first person to hold the post for an American first lady, helping Mrs. Kennedy navigate times both dazzling and tragic.

name: Wolfgang Schivelbusch
headline: Wolfgang Schivelbusch, Polymathic Cultural Historian, Dies at 81
abstract: His books covered an unusual range of subjects, including the trajectory of railroad tracks, why the South claimed a “moral” victory in the Civil War and the historical significance of beer soup.

name: Dorothy Bohm
headline: Dorothy Bohm, a Roving and Enduring Photographer, Dies at 98
abstract: In a peripatetic life, beginning with a flight from the Nazis, she found a kind of stability in making pictures for more than seven decades.

name: Katie Cotton
headline: Katie Cotton, Who Helped Raise Apple’s Profile, Dies at 57
abstract: As head of public relations, she worked closely with Steve Jobs, the company’s visionary chief executive, to spread the word about products like the iMac and the iPhone.

name: John Olsen
profession: Last of a Pivotal Group of Australian Artists
headline: John Olsen, Last of a Pivotal Group of Australian Artists, Dies at 95
abstract: The last surviving member of a generation that defined his country’s modern art, he painted exuberant landscapes that changed the way Australia saw its environment.

name: Laura Pels
headline: Laura Pels, Devoted Supporter of Nonprofit Theater, Dies at 92
abstract: She led a foundation that underwrote productions for numerous theater groups, as well as playwrights like Harold Pinter and Arthur Miller.

name: Roy Saltman
headline: Roy Saltman, Who Warned About Hanging Chads, Dies at 90
abstract: He foresaw the problems with punch-card ballots that benumbed the nation after Florida’s chaotic vote in the 2000 presidential election. His warnings went largely unheeded.

name: Bruce McCall
headline: Bruce McCall, Satirical Artist Who Conjured a ‘Retrofuture,’ Dies at 87
abstract: On New Yorker covers and elsewhere, he lampooned the rich by forecasting a plutocratic fantasyland — or, as he put it, “looking back to see how yesterday viewed tomorrow.”

name: Judith Miller
headline: Judith Miller, ‘Antiques Roadshow’ Mainstay, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Known for her many guidebooks, she helped determine what was trash and what was treasure on the BBC series that inspired the American show.

name: Newton N. Minow
profession: F.C.C. Chief Deemed TV a Vast Wasteland
headline: Newton N. Minow, 97, Dies; F.C.C. Chief Deemed TV a ‘Vast Wasteland’
abstract: His stunning declaration caused an instant sensation when he made it in 1961 and ignited a national debate over Americans’ viewing habits.

name: Don Sebesky
headline: Don Sebesky, Arranger Who Helped Broaden Jazz’s Audience, Dies at 85
abstract: He won Tonys for his orchestrations and Grammys for his compositions and arrangements. But he was best known for his genre-straddling work at CTI Records.

name: Menahem Pressler
headline: Menahem Pressler, Pianist Who Co-Founded Beaux Arts Trio, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Pressler, who fled Nazi Germany as a youth, was the anchor of a group that, with various lineups, performed all over the world for 53 years.

name: Adam Brace
profession: Put Stand-up Comedy in Front of Footlights
headline: Adam Brace, Who Put Stand-up Comedy in Front of Footlights, Dies at 43
abstract: He worked with comedians and other performers to develop one-person stage shows — one of which is headed for Broadway — that were more than just collections of jokes.

name: Don January
headline: Don January, Who Won the 1967 P.G.A. Title, Is Dead at 93
abstract: He won 10 tournaments in 10 different years on the PGA Tour and was an early star on the senior Champions Tour.

name: Vida Blue
profession: Pitching Sensation for Champion As Teams
headline: Vida Blue, Pitching Sensation for Champion A’s Teams, Dies at 73
abstract: In 1971, his first full season, he was an unstoppable fastball pitcher. Then he had a fight with the owner of the Athletics that left him embittered.

name: Ronald Steel
profession: Critic of American Cold War Policies
headline: Ronald Steel, Critic of American Cold War Policies, Dies at 92
abstract: In essays and books. he saw the U.S. postwar era as a series of misadventures spawning unwise wars. He also wrote the definitive biography of the journalist Walter Lippmann.

name: James Sakoda
profession: Wartime Internment Inspired a Social Science Tool
headline: Overlooked No More: James Sakoda, Whose Wartime Internment Inspired a Social Science Tool
abstract: After documenting his experience in Japanese American internment camps, Sakoda helped bring the study of human behavior to the computer age.

name: Stanley Deser
profession: Ideas on Gravity Help Explain the Universe
headline: Stanley Deser, Whose Ideas on Gravity Help Explain the Universe, Dies at 92
abstract: His theory of supergravity sought to bridge quantum mechanics and general relativity, a potential step toward a theory of everything.

name: Theodor Diener
profession: Discovered the Tiniest of Infectious Agents
headline: Theodor Diener, Who Discovered the Tiniest of Infectious Agents, Dies at 102
abstract: The cause of a potato disease bedeviled scientists for decades before Dr. Diener figured out that an impossibly small pathogen called a viroid was to blame.

name: Grace Bumbry
headline: Grace Bumbry, Barrier-Shattering Opera Diva, Is Dead at 86
abstract: A flamboyant mezzo-soprano (who could also sing meaty soprano roles), she overcame racial prejudice to become one of opera’s first, and biggest, Black stars.

name: Joe Kapp
headline: Joe Kapp, Quarterback Who Led Vikings to Super Bowl IV, Dies at 85
abstract: He found his way to the N.F.L. after playing eight seasons in Canadian football and was remembered for his toughness, playing through injury after injury.

name: John Roland
profession: Durable Anchor at Fox Flagship in N.Y
headline: John Roland, Durable Anchor at Fox Flagship in N.Y., Dies at 81
abstract: For a quarter-century, he was the face of the kinetic 10 p.m. news program that typically beat its rivals in the ratings.

name: Heather Armstrong
headline: Heather Armstrong, ‘Queen of the Mommy Bloggers,’ Is Dead at 47
abstract: Fired from a dot-com job for making indiscreet comments about her company online, she created, under the name Dooce, a hugely popular, moneymaking blog about parenthood and marriage.

name: David Miranda
profession: Gay Rights Activist and Snowden Ally in Brazil
headline: David Miranda, Gay Rights Activist and Snowden Ally in Brazil, Dies at 37
abstract: Emerging from Rio’s slums, he helped Edward Snowden reveal classified documents and lobbied for his asylum before rising to his country’s Congress.

name: Sam Gross
profession: Prolific Purveyor of Cartoons, Tasteful and Otherwise
headline: Sam Gross, 89, Dies; Prolific Purveyor of Cartoons, Tasteful and Otherwise
abstract: In his work for The New Yorker and especially National Lampoon, he was unafraid to offend people. But his primary goal was to make them laugh.

name: Rita Lee
headline: Rita Lee, Brazil’s Queen of Rock, Is Dead at 75
abstract: As a member the 1960s band Os Mutantes and later as a solo artist, she drew a following that included Kurt Cobain, Beck and the Prince of Wales.

name: Chris Strachwitz
profession: Dug Up the Roots of American Music
headline: Chris Strachwitz, Who Dug Up the Roots of American Music, Dies at 91
abstract: Traveling the nation to discover little-known performers for the Arhoolie label, which he founded in 1960, he earned a nickname: El Fanático.

name: Fred Siegel
profession: Urban Historian and a Former Liberal
headline: Fred Siegel, Urban Historian and a Former Liberal, Is Dead at 78
abstract: His books traced his ideological transformation from a Democratic Socialist in New York to neoconservative partisan for Rudolph Giuliani and Donald Trump.

name: Jacklyn Zeman
profession: a.k.a. Bobbie Spencer of General Hospital
headline: Jacklyn Zeman, a.k.a. Bobbie Spencer of ‘General Hospital,’ Dies at 70
abstract: One of the longest-lasting cast members of any soap opera, she earned four Daytime Emmy Award nominations for her portrayal of a loving but tough nurse.

name: Kemal Dervis
headline: Kemal Dervis, Who Eased Turkey’s Economic Crisis, Dies at 74
abstract: Changes he spearheaded in 2001 helped avert disaster. He later led the United Nations Development Program.

name: Hodding Carter III
profession: Crusading Editor and Jimmy Carter Aide
headline: Hodding Carter III, Crusading Editor and Jimmy Carter Aide, Dies at 88
abstract: As a journalist in Mississippi, he championed civil rights. He later became the face of the U.S. government during the Iranian hostage crisis.

name: Mike Pride
profession: Proved a Regional Newspaper Could Work
headline: Mike Pride, Who Proved a Regional Newspaper Could Work, Dies at 76
abstract: For 25 years he was editor of The Concord Monitor, an award-winning go-to source every four years for national reporters covering the New Hampshire presidential primary.

name: Bernadine Strik
headline: Bernadine Strik, Whose Insights Helped Blueberries Thrive, Dies at 60
abstract: A horticulturist, she discovered farming methods that increased yields of the fruit as its health benefits became widely understood and demand for it grew.

name: Thomas Stacy
headline: Thomas Stacy, Master of the English Horn, Dies at 84
abstract: Through his decades with the New York Philharmonic and his busy touring schedule, he helped make an unfamiliar instrument much less so.

name: Pema Tseden
headline: Pema Tseden, Pioneering Tibetan Filmmaker, Is Dead at 53
abstract: His films captured contemporary Tibetan life as Tibetans saw it, devoid of the stereotypes long associated with their homeland.

name: Slava Zaitsev
headline: Slava Zaitsev, Enduring Soviet-Era Fashion Designer, Dies at 85
abstract: He gave color, sparkle and opulence to a generation raised in drab Soviet gray and designed for pop stars, Olympic athletes, politicians and ballerinas.

name: Bill Oesterle
headline: Bill Oesterle, Co-Founder of Angie’s List, Dies at 57
abstract: What began as a company to review local contractors grew into a website with millions of subscribers looking to make home improvements.

name: Don Denkinger
profession: Top Umpire Remembered for Botched Call
headline: Don Denkinger, 86, Top Umpire Remembered for Botched Call, Dies
abstract: His reputation as a lauded, longtime major-league umpire was overshadowed by a pivotal wrong call he made during the 1985 World Series.

name: Owen Davidson
profession: Won 8 Grand Slams With Billie Jean King
headline: Owen Davidson, Who Won 8 Grand Slams With Billie Jean King, Dies at 79
abstract: In the 1960s and ’70s, he and King dominated mixed doubles tournaments. He was also known for his congeniality, sportsmanship and skill at the net.

name: Doyle Brunson
profession: Poker Champion Known as Texas Dolly
headline: Doyle Brunson, Poker Champion Known as ‘Texas Dolly,’ Dies at 89
abstract: In a lucrative career that began in Texas saloons, he won back-to-back World Series of Poker titles (and 10 in all) and wrote a definitive poker manual.

name: Amy Silverstein
profession: Chronicled a Life of Three Hearts
headline: Amy Silverstein, Who Chronicled a Life of Three Hearts, Dies at 59
abstract: In two memoirs, magazine articles and a Times essay, she recounted the joys and miseries of living as a double transplant recipient.

name: Bill Saluga
headline: Bill Saluga, a Memorable Comedic Wiseguy, Is Dead at 85
abstract: He played many characters in his career, but he was best known by far for the one who said, “You doesn’t have to call me Johnson.”

name: Marlene Bauer Hagge
headline: Marlene Bauer Hagge, Last of the L.P.G.A.’s Founders, Dies at 89
abstract: Emerging on the national scene at 13, she went on to win 26 pro tournaments, including the 1956 L.P.G.A. Championship. She and 12 other women started the league.

name: Robert E. Lucas Jr.
headline: Robert E. Lucas Jr., Nobel-Winning Conservative Economist, Dies at 85
abstract: Challenging the theories of John Maynard Keynes, he questioned the idea that government intervention could help steer the economy.

name: Sam Zell
headline: Sam Zell, 81, Tycoon Whose Big Newspaper Venture Went Bust, Dies
abstract: With a fortune made in real estate, he went into the media business in a landmark leveraged buyout of the Tribune Company in 2007. Bankruptcy ensued.

name: Gary Prado Salmón
headline: Gary Prado Salmón, Bolivian Captor of Che Guevara, Dies at 84
abstract: As an army captain, he led the operation that tracked down the Communist guerrilla who had helped lead the Cuban revolution and was trying to foment one in Bolivia.

name: Larry Mahan
headline: Larry Mahan, the Elvis of Rodeo, Is Dead at 79
abstract: His eight championships made him a legend to his fans. His mod style, swashbuckling lifestyle and flirtations with Hollywood made him a star.

name: Mark Gietzen
headline: Mark Gietzen, 69, Dies; Zealous Lieutenant in Anti-Abortion Movement
abstract: He helped make Kansas a staging ground in the abortion debate but failed to overturn the state’s vote in favor of abortion rights. He died in a plane crash.

name: Andy Rourke
headline: Andy Rourke, Bassist for the Smiths, Dies at 59
abstract: His sinewy bass lines were a vital — if, as one writer put it, “habitually unsung” — part of the influential British rock band’s success.

name: Robin Guenther
headline: Robin Guenther, Architect of Healthy Hospitals, Dies at 68
abstract: Supporting the use of nontoxic construction materials, she co-wrote the first guide to building green health care facilities and designed them to be less austere.

name: Bill Perkins
headline: Bill Perkins, Defender of His Harlem Constituents, Dies at 74
abstract: As a councilman and state senator, he fought for higher wages, health care, gay rights and sought justice for the Central Park Five.

name: Timothy Keller
headline: The Rev. Timothy Keller, Pioneering Manhattan Evangelist, Dies at 72
abstract: Shunning fire and brimstone, he became a best-selling author and founded Redeemer Presbyterian Church, which drew young New Yorkers.

name: Jim Brown
profession: Football Great and Civil Rights Champion
headline: Jim Brown, Football Great and Civil Rights Champion, Dies at 87
abstract: After a Hall of Fame career in the N.F.L., he pursued social activism and Hollywood stardom, but his image was stained by accusations of abuse toward women.

name: Shermane Billingsley
profession: Guardian of the Stork Clubs Legacy
headline: Shermane Billingsley, Guardian of the Stork Club’s Legacy, Dies at 78
abstract: The nightspot her father opened as a Prohibition-era speakeasy endured as a Manhattan institution until 1965. For decades she was “the keeper of the flame.”

name: Superstar Billy Graham
headline: Superstar Billy Graham, Model of the Buff, Blond Wrestler, Dies at 79
abstract: His spectacular physique, outrageous personality and blond dye job inspired Hulk Hogan and Jesse Ventura. But the steroids that built his body also destroyed it.

name: Martin Amis
profession: Acclaimed Author of Bleakly Comic Novels
headline: Martin Amis, Acclaimed Author of Bleakly Comic Novels, Dies at 73
abstract: In books like “Money” and “The Information,” he created “a high style to describe low things,” as he put it. He found more renown as a critic, and a measure of unease as his famous father’s son.

name: James de Jongh
headline: James de Jongh, Who Put Stories of Slavery Onstage, Dies at 80
abstract: His play “Do Lord Remember Me,” constructed from interviews with formerly enslaved people in the 1930s, was first staged in 1978 and has been revived multiple times since.

name: Gloria Molina
headline: Gloria Molina, Pioneering Latina Politician, Dies at 74
abstract: In three elections, she was a “first,” becoming one of the leading Latina politicians in California and the country.

name: Helmut Berger
profession: Actor Known for His Work With Visconti
headline: Helmut Berger, Actor Known for His Work With Visconti, Dies at 78
abstract: He first made his mark in “The Damned” as a character one critic said personified “the outright perversion” of Nazism. He and the director became lovers.

name: C. Boyden Gray
headline: C. Boyden Gray, Lawyer for the Republican Establishment, Dies at 80
abstract: A former Democrat, he served as White House counsel under George Bush and aided other presidents, including Ronald Reagan and Donald J. Trump.

name: Linda Lewis
headline: Linda Lewis, British Singer Whose Voice Knew Few Limits, Dies at 72
abstract: Inspired by Motown early in her career, she became an acclaimed singer-songwriter and backed the likes of David Bowie, Rod Stewart and Cat Stevens.

name: Rick Wolff
profession: Sports Radio Host and Much More
headline: Rick Wolff, Sports Radio Host and Much More, Is Dead at 71
abstract: As a psychological coach (and ex-player), he helped revive a woeful Cleveland baseball team. He had a WFAN show about youth sports and shepherded best sellers.

name: Buddy Melges
headline: Buddy Melges, American Sailing Champion, Dies at 93
abstract: A product of a Wisconsin lake region, he was the first sailor to win both Olympic gold and sailing’s top prize, the America’s Cup. And his colleagues revered him.

name: Rick Hoyt
profession: Competed in Races While Pushed by His Father
headline: Rick Hoyt, Who Competed in Races While Pushed by His Father, Dies at 61
abstract: Hoyt, who was in a wheelchair, regularly took part in the Boston Marathon with the help of his father, Dick. The two, he said, had “a special bond.”

name: Leon Ichaso
headline: Leon Ichaso, Whose Films Explored Latino Identity, Dies at 74
abstract: His first feature, “El Super,” was critically acclaimed. He continued to examine culture and exile in “Crossover Dreams,” “El Cantante” and “Piñero.”

name: Ray Stevenson
headline: Ray Stevenson, Actor in ‘Thor’ and ‘Rome,’ Is Dead at 58
abstract: His wide-ranging roles included fantasy characters, a knight, a Roman soldier and a Punisher.

name: Bill Lee
profession: Bassist and Composer of Son Spike Lees Films
headline: Bill Lee, Bassist and Composer of Son Spike Lee’s Films, Dies at 94
abstract: He accompanied a wide range of jazz and folk musicians and scored “She’s Gotta Have It,” “School Daze” “Do the Right Thing” and “Mo’ Better Blues.”

name: Kenneth Anger
profession: Experimental Filmmaker Left a Pop Culture Legacy
headline: Kenneth Anger, 96, Dies; Experimental Filmmaker Left a Pop Culture Legacy
abstract: His movie, “Scorpio Rising,” proved that sound and image could be combined to create something powerful, influencing the rise of music video.

name: Nicholas Gray
profession: Grays Papaya Became a Hot Dog Mecca
headline: Nicholas Gray, Whose Gray’s Papaya Became a Hot Dog Mecca, Dies at 86
abstract: His storefront eatery, a knockoff of a leading frankfurter grill, helped turn an unlikely culinary combination into a New York phenomenon.

name: Rolf Harris
headline: Rolf Harris, Disgraced British Entertainer, Dies at 93
abstract: His career as a musician and a painter over six decades ended abruptly when he was convicted of sexually abusing teenage girls.

name: Tina Turner
headline: Tina Turner, Magnetic Singer of Explosive Power, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Hailed in the 1960s for her dynamic performances with her first husband, Ike, she became a sensation as a recording artist, often echoing her personal struggles in her songs.

name: Robert J. Zimmer
headline: Robert J. Zimmer, Who Promoted Free Speech on Campus, Dies at 75
abstract: A mathematician, he was for many years the president of the University of Chicago, where he argued that civility was not a reason to silence discussion.

name: Pete Brown
profession: Put Words to Sunshine of Your Love
headline: Pete Brown, Who Put Words to ‘Sunshine of Your Love,’ Dies at 82
abstract: A British Beat poet, he wrote lyrics for the band Cream and, after it broke up, continued to collaborate with Jack Bruce, the group’s lead singer and bassist.

name: Tom Sawyer
headline: Tom Sawyer, Congressman Who Challenged Census Undercount, Dies at 77
abstract: A Democrat from Ohio, he said the 1990 population data missed more than two million Black Americans and shortchanged the nation’s older cities.

name: Ed Ames
headline: Ed Ames, Singing Star Who Became a Familiar Face on TV, Dies at 95
abstract: After more than a decade of hit records with his brothers, he found success as a solo performer and a star of the series “Daniel Boone.”

name: Mary Turner Pattiz
headline: Mary Turner Pattiz, Rock D.J. During FM’s Heyday, Dies at 76
abstract: She was known as “the Burner” for her seductive delivery, but off the air she was anything but a wild rock ’n’ roller. She later became an addiction counselor.

name: Ingrid Haebler
profession: Pianist Known for Her Mastery of Mozart
headline: Ingrid Haebler, Pianist Known for Her Mastery of Mozart, Is Dead
abstract: In concerts and on dozens of recordings, she applied a delicate touch that critics said set her apart from other performers.

name: Stanley Engerman
headline: Stanley Engerman, Revisionist Scholar of Slavery, Dies at 87
abstract: His two-volume study, written with Robert W. Fogel, used data to challenge commonly held ideas about American slavery, including that it was unprofitable and inefficient.

name: Ian Hacking
profession: Eminent Philosopher of Science and Much Else
headline: Ian Hacking, Eminent Philosopher of Science and Much Else, Dies at 87
abstract: Never limited by categories, his free-ranging intellect delved into physics, probability and anthropology, establishing him as a major thinker.

name: George Maharis
headline: George Maharis, TV Heartthrob of ‘Route 66,’ Is Dead at 94
abstract: He appeared in Off Broadway roles before starring on CBS as one of two young men who find adventure crossing the country in a Corvette convertible.

name: Brian Shul
headline: Brian Shul Dies at 75; Fighter Pilot Who Flew World’s Fastest Plane
abstract: He was near death after his plane was shot down in the Vietnam War but survived to fly the world’s fastest and highest-altitude jet.

name: Robin Wagner
headline: Robin Wagner, Set Designer Who Won Three Tony Awards, Dies at 89
abstract: He created sets for more than 50 of Broadway’s most celebrated productions, including “Hair,” “A Chorus Line,” “On the Twentieth Century” and “The Producers.”

name: Juan Carlos Formell
profession: Buoyant Heir of Cuban Musical Legacy
headline: Juan Carlos Formell, Buoyant Heir of Cuban Musical Legacy, Dies at 59
abstract: The son of Juan Formell, a giant of Cuban music, he found his own voice as a singer-songwriter. He died during a performance in New York.

name: Amitai Etzioni
profession: Envisioned a Society Built on the Common Good
headline: Amitai Etzioni, 94, Dies; Envisioned a Society Built on the Common Good
abstract: A sociologist, he advised U.S. presidents and other Western leaders while fathering communitarianism, a political middle ground between the left and the right.

name: Eusebius McKaiser
headline: Eusebius McKaiser, Acerbic South African Political Analyst, Dies at 44
abstract: Adamantly progressive, openly gay and politically fearless, he cast a sharp eye on the country’s post-apartheid politics and culture.

name: Ilya Kabakov
profession: Soviet-Born Artist Depicted Grimness With Wit
headline: Ilya Kabakov, 89, Dies; Soviet-Born Artist Depicted Grimness With Wit
abstract: In often fantastical paintings, drawings and immersive installations, he explored the privations and indignities of the Soviet life he would flee, landing on Long Island.

name: Kaija Saariaho
headline: Kaija Saariaho, 70, Pathbreaking Composer of Singular Colors, Is Dead
abstract: She brought new textures to modernist music, sometimes using electronics, and became the first female composer to have two operas staged by the Met.

name: Redd Holt
headline: Redd Holt, Drummer on ’60s Instrumental Pop Hits, Dies at 91
abstract: He was a member of the Ramsey Lewis Trio when it reached the Top 10 with “The ‘In’ Crowd,” and he later had a hit as a co-leader with the funky “Soulful Strut.”

name: Harvey Pitt
headline: Harvey Pitt, S.E.C. Chair Who Resigned Amid Scandals, Dies at 78
abstract: Mr. Pitt, who served under President George W. Bush, oversaw a swift reopening of stock exchanges after 9/11 but was tarnished by later missteps.

name: Don Bateman
headline: Don Bateman, Who Kept Airplanes From Crashing, Dies at 91
abstract: His cockpit warning system, which alerts the crew if an aircraft is heading toward a mountain, a building or the ocean, has saved thousands of lives.

name: Thomas Buergenthal
headline: Thomas Buergenthal, Holocaust Survivor and Judge, Dies at 89
abstract: He said his survival of the Holocaust at 10 years old allowed him to understand “what it is like to be a victim of human rights violations.”

name: Cynthia Weil
headline: Cynthia Weil, Who Put Words to That ‘Lovin’ Feeling,’ Dies at 82
abstract: With her husband and songwriting partner, Barry Mann, she wrote lyrics for timeless hits by the Righteous Brothers, the Animals and Dolly Parton.

name: Peter Simonischek
headline: Peter Simonischek, Beloved Austrian Actor, Is Dead at 76
abstract: He played a prankster and adoring father in “Toni Erdmann,” the Oscar-nominated 2016 comedy that made him an international star, but he had long been a celebrity at home.

name: Roger Craig
headline: Roger Craig, Teacher of an Era-Defining Pitch, Is Dead at 93
abstract: After winning three World Series as a player, Craig became a coach and spread the gospel of the split-fingered fastball, what one player of the time called “the pitch of the ’80s.”

name: Robert Hanssen
profession: F.B.I. Agent Exposed as Spy for Moscow
headline: Robert Hanssen, F.B.I. Agent Exposed as Spy for Moscow, Dies at 79
abstract: Mr. Hanssen was sentenced to life in prison in 2002, bringing to a close one of the most lurid and damaging espionage cases in American history.

name: Ama Ata Aidoo
headline: Ama Ata Aidoo, Groundbreaking Ghanaian Writer, Dies at 81
abstract: A playwright, novelist and poet, she was a leading African writer who explored the complexities faced by modern women living in the shadow of colonialism.

name: Andrew Bellucci
profession: Pizza Visionary With a Troubled Past
headline: Andrew Bellucci, Pizza Visionary With a Troubled Past, Dies at 59
abstract: His obsession with recreating the original New York pizza helped revive a classic and inspire a generation of chefs. But his ambitions led to conflicts and, once, prison.

name: Jim Hines
profession: First to Sprint 100 Meters in Under 10 Seconds
headline: Jim Hines, First to Sprint 100 Meters in Under 10 Seconds, Dies at 76
abstract: He ran a gold-medal-winning time of 9.95 seconds at the Mexico City Olympics in 1968, setting an official world record that held for 15 years.

name: Anna Shay
headline: Anna Shay, Star of Netflix’s ‘Bling Empire,’ Dies at 62
abstract: A Los Angeles socialite and heiress to a defense contractor, she lived most of her life in private before joining a reality show.

name: Astrud Gilberto
profession: Shot to Fame With The Girl From Ipanema
headline: Astrud Gilberto, 83, Dies; Shot to Fame With ‘The Girl From Ipanema’
abstract: It was the first song she ever recorded. And it played a key role in making the Brazilian sound known as bossa nova a phenomenon in the United States.

name: Françoise Gilot
profession: Artist in the Shadow of Picasso
headline: Françoise Gilot, Artist in the Shadow of Picasso, Is Dead at 101
abstract: An accomplished painter (and memoirist), she did what no other lover of his had ever done: She walked out.

name: Ronnie Cummins
headline: Ronnie Cummins, Scourge of Genetically Modified Food, Dies at 76
abstract: A lifelong protester, he became a leading promoter of organic food and a forceful critic of a food industry that genetically engineers what it produces and sells.

name: Pat Cooper
headline: Pat Cooper, Comedian of Outrage, Is Dead at 93
abstract: He built his act on making fun of his Italian American heritage. He later publicly insulted stars he had worked with, including Frank Sinatra and Howard Stern.

name: John Beasley
profession: Late-Blooming Actor Known for Playing Sages
headline: John Beasley, Late-Blooming Actor Known for Playing Sages, Dies at 79
abstract: A former railroad clerk, he didn’t became a full-time actor until his 40s, but he made up for lost time in films like “Rudy” and TV shows like “Everwood.”

name: George Winston
profession: Pianist With a Popular Soothing Sound
headline: George Winston, Pianist With a Popular Soothing Sound, Dies at 74
abstract: He won a Grammy in the new age category, and his top-selling records helped define the genre. But his interests also included Hawaiian guitar and the Doors.

name: The Iron Sheik
headline: The Iron Sheik, Villainous Hall of Fame Wrestler, Is Dead
abstract: Khosrow Vaziri drew on his Iranian heritage to create a caricature of a Middle Eastern villain and became one of the most memorable heels in wrestling history.

name: Pat Robertson
headline: Pat Robertson, Who Gave Christian Conservatives Clout, Is Dead at 93
abstract: A Baptist minister and a broadcaster, he turned evangelicals into a powerful constituency that helped Republicans capture Congress in 1994. He earlier ran for president.

name: Barry Newman
profession: Star of the Cult Film Vanishing Point
headline: Barry Newman, Star of the Cult Film ‘Vanishing Point,’ Dies at 92
abstract: Panned when it was released in 1971, the movie gained acclaim decades later. Mr. Newman also starred on TV in the legal drama “Petrocelli.”

name: Richard E. Snyder
profession: Drove Simon & Schuster to New Heights
headline: Richard E. Snyder, 90, Dies; Drove Simon & Schuster to New Heights
abstract: In two decades of leadership at the publishing house, he helped remold a clubby book industry into a diversified and highly profitable corporate enterprise.

name: Carroll Cooley
headline: Carroll Cooley, Detective in Landmark Miranda Case, Dies at 87
abstract: His interrogation helped lead to a Supreme Court ruling that established rights that protect criminal suspects from incriminating themselves while in custody.

name: James G. Watt
headline: James G. Watt, Polarizing Interior Secretary Under Reagan, Dies at 85
abstract: A friend of developers, he declared that department policies had swung too far toward conservation under the influence of “environmental extremists.”

name: Lou Sullivan
headline: Overlooked No More: Lou Sullivan, Author and Transgender Activist
abstract: In diaries, articles and letters, he pushed for the medical community’s acceptance of men who were assigned female at birth and identified as gay.

name: William E. Spriggs
headline: William E. Spriggs, Economist Who Pushed for Racial Justice, Dies at 68
abstract: An educator who served in the Obama administration, he championed workers, especially Black workers, and challenged his profession’s racial assumptions.

name: Harald zur Hausen
headline: Harald zur Hausen, 87, Nobelist Who Found Cause of Cervical Cancer, Dies
abstract: When he proposed that the human papillomavirus caused cervical cancer, he was ridiculed. He persevered, and today a vaccine exists.

name: Helen Thorington
profession: Brought Sonic Art to the Airwaves
headline: Helen Thorington, Who Brought Sonic Art to the Airwaves, Dies at 94
abstract: A pioneer in radio art and, later internet art, she created a blend of synthesizer compositions and found sounds that opened new artistic terrain.

name: Michael Batayeh
headline: Michael Batayeh, Comedian and ‘Breaking Bad’ Actor, Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. Batayeh starred in three episodes of the Emmy-winning series and performed stand-up comedy.

name: Ted Kaczynski
headline: Ted Kaczynski, ‘Unabomber’ Who Attacked Modern Life, Dies at 81
abstract: Alone in a shack in the Montana wilderness, he fashioned homemade bombs and launched a violent one-man campaign to destroy industrial society.

name: Edward Stack
profession: Longtime President of the Baseball Hall of Fame
headline: Edward Stack, 88, Longtime President of the Baseball Hall of Fame, Dies
abstract: He presided over the annual Hall induction ceremony in Cooperstown, N.Y., for many years. But he also helped keep one star, Pete Rose, from being part of it.

name: Jessie Maple
headline: Jessie Maple, Pathbreaking Filmmaker, Is Dead at 86
abstract: She was believed to be the first Black woman to produce, write and direct an independent feature film. She also broke ground as a union cinematographer.

name: Owen Gingerich
headline: Owen Gingerich, Astronomer Who Saw God in the Cosmos, Dies at 93
abstract: He wrote and lectured widely, often on the theme that religion and science were not incompatible. He also chased down 600 copies of Copernicus’s landmark book.

name: Silvio Berlusconi
headline: Silvio Berlusconi, a Showman Who Upended Italian Politics and Culture, Dies at 86
abstract: He introduced sex and glamour to Italian TV and then brought the same formula to politics, dominating the country and its culture for more than 20 years.

name: Franz Leichter
profession: Fighter in Albany for Progressive Causes
headline: Franz Leichter, a Fighter in Albany for Progressive Causes, Dies at 92
abstract: A legislator from Manhattan and a former refugee, he co-wrote a landmark abortion-rights law and pushed for same-sex marriage and legalized marijuana long before their time.

name: Treat Williams
profession: Actor Known for Hair and Everwood
headline: Treat Williams, Actor Known for ‘Hair’ and ‘Everwood,’ Dies at 71
abstract: His many other roles included a detective turned informant in “Prince of the City.” He was killed in a motorcycle accident in Vermont.

name: Cormac McCarthy
headline: Cormac McCarthy, Novelist of a Darker America, Is Dead at 89
abstract: “All the Pretty Horses,” “The Road” and “No Country for Old Men” were among his acclaimed books that explore a bleak world of violence and outsiders.

name: Jacques Rozier
profession: Last of the French New Wave Directors
headline: Jacques Rozier, Last of the French New Wave Directors, Dies at 96
abstract: Though he never achieved the fame of Jean-Luc Godard or François Truffaut, he was considered by many to be their equal.

name: John Romita Sr.
headline: John Romita Sr., Creative Force at Marvel Comics, Is Dead at 93
abstract: As an artist, he defined decades of Marvel storytelling and helped bring characters like Spider-Man and Wolverine to life.

name: Roger Payne
headline: Roger Payne, Biologist Who Heard Whales Singing, Dies at 88
abstract: His underwater microphones recorded “Songs of the Humpback Whale,” inspiring a movement that led to national and international bans on commercial whaling.

name: Ivan Menezes
profession: Head of Johnnie Walker and Other Liquor Giants
headline: Ivan Menezes, Head of Johnnie Walker and Other Liquor Giants, Dies at 63
abstract: As chief executive of Diageo for a decade, he presented alcohol as an attainable luxury and helped brands like Smirnoff and Guinness grow.

name: Robert Gottlieb
profession: Eminent Editor From le Carré to Clinton
headline: Robert Gottlieb, Eminent Editor From le Carré to Clinton, Dies at 92
abstract: At Simon & Schuster, Alfred A. Knopf and The New Yorker, he polished the work of a who’s who of mid-to-late 20th century writers.

name: Jim Turner
profession: Kicked the Jets Into Super Bowl History
headline: Jim Turner, Who Kicked the Jets Into Super Bowl History, Dies at 82
abstract: He was a reliable pro-football place-kicker for 16 years and had a moment of glory in the 1969 championship game.

name: Glenda Jackson
headline: Glenda Jackson, Oscar-Winning Actress Turned Politician, Dies at 87
abstract: She walked away from a successful acting career to enter the British Parliament, before returning to the stage as the title character in an acclaimed “King Lear.”

name: Homer Jones
profession: Wide Receiver Specialized in Bombs and Spikes
headline: Homer Jones Dies at 82; Wide Receiver Specialized in Bombs and Spikes
abstract: For a few years with the Giants, he was among the most feared pass catchers in the N.F.L. — and the acknowledged inventor of an end-zone celebration.

name: Irma Capece Minutolo
profession: Opera Singer and Partner to Exiled King
headline: Irma Capece Minutolo, Opera Singer and Partner to Exiled King, Dies at 87
abstract: A former Naples beauty queen, she became famous as the companion to the playboy Farouk I of Egypt, then carved out a successful opera career.

name: C. Welton Gaddy
headline: The Rev. C. Welton Gaddy, Defender of Church-State Divide, Dies at 81
abstract: He started out in the Southern Baptist Convention, but when that group took a sharp conservative turn he became a voice for tolerance and diversity.

name: Carol Higgins Clark
headline: Carol Higgins Clark, Mystery Writer, Is Dead at 66
abstract: She had a modest career as an actress but was best known for following in the footsteps of her mother, the best-selling author Mary Higgins Clark.

name: Richard Severo
profession: Times Reporter in Internal Clash Over Book
headline: Richard Severo, Times Reporter in Internal Clash Over Book, Dies at 90
abstract: He challenged a company’s prerogative to transfer an employee and a news organization’s ability to assert publishing rights when a reporter’s articles are used for a book.

name: Daniel Ellsberg
headline: Daniel Ellsberg, Who Leaked the Pentagon Papers, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Deeply disturbed by the accounting of American deceit in Vietnam, he approached The New York Times. The disclosures that followed rocked the nation.

name: Jack McNally
headline: Jack McNally, N.Y.P.D. Detective Turned Defense Sleuth, Dies at 89
abstract: After he helped collar the men behind New York City’s biggest jewel heist, he worked as a private investigator for defendants like O.J. Simpson and Patty Hearst.

name: Lisl Steiner
headline: Lisl Steiner, Photographer Who Glimpsed Luminaries Up Close, Dies at 95
abstract: A flamboyant photojournalist with the moxie to stand up to autocrats, she captured the intimate moments of leading figures of the 20th century.

name: Saskia Hamilton
headline: Saskia Hamilton, Poet Who Edited Another Poet’s Letters, Dies at 56
abstract: In addition to her prizewinning writing, she was known for editing the correspondence between the poet Robert Lowell and the writer Elizabeth Hardwick.

name: Donald Triplett
profession: Case 1 in the Study of Autism
headline: Donald Triplett, ‘Case 1’ in the Study of Autism, Dies at 89
abstract: He was widely considered the first person to be diagnosed with autism. His happy life later became the subject of a book and documentary.

name: Max Morath
headline: Max Morath, Pianist Who Staged a One-Man Ragtime Revival, Dies at 96
abstract: A student of both music and history, he entertained audiences in the 1960s and beyond while educating them about a genre whose heyday had ended decades earlier.

name: Magda Saleh
headline: Magda Saleh, Influential Egyptian Ballerina, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Trained at the Bolshoi, she became a star of the Cairo Ballet and played a key role in making ballet accessible to people of all classes.

name: Paxton Whitehead
headline: Paxton Whitehead, Actor Who Found Humor in the Stodgy, Dies at 85
abstract: An Englishman with a deep, cultured voice, he played uptight snobs in films like “Back to School” and on shows like “Friends” and “Mad About You.”

name: Haim Roet
headline: Haim Roet, Who Kept Holocaust Victims’ Names Alive, Dies at 90
abstract: Since he first read the names of people murdered by the Nazis at a protest in 1989, the practice has become a part of memorial ceremonies around the world.

name: Julie Garwood
headline: Julie Garwood, Best-Selling Romance Novelist, Dies at 78
abstract: She first became known for novels set in the distant past. She later wrote contemporary tales that involved computer hacking and Ponzi schemes.

name: Henry Petroski
headline: Henry Petroski, Whose Books Decoded Engineering, Dies at 81
abstract: He wrote extensively about the design of buildings and bridges and how they failed. He also examined the history of commonplace objects like the pencil.

name: Firouz Naderi
headline: Firouz Naderi, NASA Scientist Who Led Mars Missions, Dies at 77
abstract: In a career that was an inspiration to Iranians and Iranian Americans, he oversaw multiple missions to Mars, including two successful landings.

name: Teresa Taylor
profession: Butthole Surfers Drummer and a Face of Gen X
headline: Teresa Taylor, Butthole Surfers Drummer and a Face of Gen X, Dies at 60
abstract: In addition to playing with the audacious Texas band, she helped define the image of an aimless generation with her role in the 1990 film “Slacker.”

name: Hamish Harding
headline: Hamish Harding, an Explorer Who Knew No Bounds, Dies at 58
abstract: An aviation tycoon who pushed the limits, he went to the depths of the ocean and the blackness of space before his fateful dive to the Titanic on Sunday.

name: Stockton Rush
headline: Stockton Rush, Pilot of the Titan Submersible, Dies at 61
abstract: A lifelong adventure seeker, Mr. Rush said he took on the risk of deepwater travel because the “ocean is the universe. That’s where life is.”

name: Shahzada Dawood
headline: Shahzada Dawood, Executive, 48, and Son, 19, Die Aboard Submersible
abstract: Mr. Dawood, a British Pakistani businessman, was the vice chairman of Engro Corporation, a conglomerate owned by one of the richest families in Pakistan.

name: Bob Brown
headline: Bob Brown, Intimidator on N.F.L. Offensive Lines, Dies at 81
abstract: As an offensive tackle for three teams in a Hall of Fame career, he said he prided himself on being the “beater” and not the “beatee.”

name: Sheldon Harnick
headline: Sheldon Harnick, ‘Fiddler on the Roof’ Lyricist, Dies at 99
abstract: His collaborations with the composer Jerry Bock also included “Fiorello!” — which, like “Fiddler,” was a Tony winner — and “She Loves Me.”

name: Paul-Henri Nargeolet
headline: Paul-Henri Nargeolet, Known as ‘Mr. Titanic,’ Dies at 77
abstract: One of the five people aboard the Titan submersible when it imploded, he died near the Titanic wreckage that he had visited dozens of times.

name: Margaret Gilleo
profession: Made a Yard Sign a Free-Speech Beacon
headline: Margaret Gilleo, 84, Dies; Made a Yard Sign a Free-Speech Beacon
abstract: An antiwar sign she put up in 1990 led to a legal clash with a wealthy suburb of St. Louis. The case made it all the way to the Supreme Court.

name: H. Lee Sarokin
headline: H. Lee Sarokin, Federal Judge Who Freed Hurricane Carter, Dies at 94
abstract: In his 15 years on the U.S. District Court bench in Newark, he also ruled on high-profile cases involving the tobacco industry and the rights of homeless people.

name: Paul Ickovic
profession: Photographer at Home on the Street
headline: Paul Ickovic, Photographer at Home on the Street, Dies at 79
abstract: His camera captured the variety of the human experience, but changing tastes in photography kept him from the acclaim he sought — as did his own idiosyncrasies.

name: Dolores Alexander
headline: Overlooked No More: Dolores Alexander, Feminist Journalist and Activist
abstract: She was a reporter, executive director of the National Organization for Women and owner of the restaurant Mother Courage, which became a hub for women.

name: Harry Markowitz
profession: Nobel-Winning Pioneer of Modern Portfolio Theory
headline: Harry Markowitz, Nobel-Winning Pioneer of Modern Portfolio Theory, Dies at 95
abstract: He overturned the traditional approach to buying stocks by examining the relationship between risk and reward.

name: Rita Reif
headline: Rita Reif, Antiques and Auctions Columnist, Dies at 94
abstract: She worked at The Times for decades, and she made news herself when she challenged ownership of a painting thought to have been looted by the Nazis.

name: Don Harold
headline: Don Harold, Sneaky Subway Preservationist, Dies at 91
abstract: He played an essential role in the creation of the New York Transit Museum by helping to save vintage train cars — sometimes using subterfuge.

name: Jesse McReynolds
profession: Lead Singer in Long-Running Bluegrass Duo
headline: Jesse McReynolds, Lead Singer in Long-Running Bluegrass Duo, Dies at 93
abstract: Also a mandolinist, he performed alongside his brother, Jim, in an act that lasted 55 years. He continued performing after his brother’s death.

name: Richard Ravitch
profession: Rescuer of the Subways and New Yorks Finances
headline: Richard Ravitch, Rescuer of the Subways and New York’s Finances, Dies at 89
abstract: He helped New York City avoid bankruptcy in the mid-1970s, ran the Metropolitan Transportation Authority and later served as lieutenant governor.

name: John B. Goodenough
profession: Nobel-Winning Creator of the Lithium-Ion Battery
headline: John B. Goodenough, 100, Dies; Nobel-Winning Creator of the Lithium-Ion Battery
abstract: An unassuming professor who remained active into his 90s, he is credited with the breakthrough that gave rise to the batteries powering today’s electronic devices.

name: Robert Black
headline: Robert Black, Bass Virtuoso of the Avant-Garde, Is Dead at 67
abstract: As part of the influential Bang on a Can All-Stars, he helped popularize experimental music through international tours and well-regarded albums.

name: Frederic Forrest
profession: Actor Known for Apocalypse Now and The Rose
headline: Frederic Forrest, 86, Dies; Actor Known for ‘Apocalypse Now’ and ‘The Rose’
abstract: He appeared in a string of films directed by Francis Ford Coppola, and his performance as Bette Midler’s love interest earned him an Oscar nomination.

name: Julian Sands
profession: Actor Played Shelley, a Warlock and a King
headline: Julian Sands Dies at 65; Actor Played Shelley, a Warlock and a King
abstract: Over a 40-year screen career, the instantly recognizable Mr. Sands displayed great versatility onscreen. He died while hiking in the San Gabriel Mountains.

name: James Crown
headline: James Crown, Chicago Businessman and Avid Philanthropist, Dies at 70
abstract: He was a director of General Dynamics and served on the board of JPMorgan Chase. He was also a crucial early supporter of Barack Obama.

name: Bobby Osborne
headline: Bobby Osborne, 91, Mandolinist Who Flouted Bluegrass Convention, Dies
abstract: The band he led with his brother broke new ground with an unusually broad repertoire, unorthodox instrumentation and untraditional vocal harmonies.

name: Lowell Weicker
headline: Lowell Weicker, Senator Whose Star Rose During Watergate, Dies at 92
abstract: A liberal Republican who became a third-party governor, he was known for his fierce criticism of Nixon and later termed Donald Trump “a total con artist.”

name: Ben Helfgott
headline: Ben Helfgott, Holocaust Survivor Turned Weight Lifter, Dies at 93
abstract: He was one of more than 700 child survivors flown to Britain after World War II. He later became a leader in efforts to remember the Nazi horrors.

name: Chris Printup
profession: Founder of Streetwear Brand Born X Raised
headline: Chris Printup, Founder of Streetwear Brand Born X Raised, Dies at 42
abstract: Mr. Printup, known as “Spanto,” died on Wednesday morning in Albuquerque, N.M., from injuries sustained in a car accident on Sunday, the brand confirmed.

name: Marvin Kitman
headline: Marvin Kitman, Satirist Whose Main Target Was TV, Dies at 93
abstract: He twitted the networks for 35 years as a critic at Newsday. He also audited George Washington’s wartime expense account and wrote a biography of Bill O’Reilly.

name: April Kingsley
headline: April Kingsley, Curator Who Championed Unsung Artists, Dies at 82
abstract: In shows she organized, and in her writing, she highlighted women and Black artists at a time when they were seldom drawing mainstream attention.

name: Christine King Farris
profession: Last Sibling of Martin Luther King Jr
headline: Christine King Farris, Last Sibling of Martin Luther King Jr., Dies at 95
abstract: She supported him during the civil rights movement and promoted his legacy after he was assassinated.

name: Alan Arkin
profession: Comic Actor With a Serious Side
headline: Alan Arkin, Comic Actor With a Serious Side, Dies at 89
abstract: He got laughs and won awards on Broadway in “Enter Laughing” and in movies like “Little Miss Sunshine.” But he also had a flair for drama.

name: Darren Drozdov
headline: Darren Drozdov, Pro Wrestler Whose Career Was Cut Short, Dies at 54
abstract: A former professional football player, he had a promising career in the ring until an injury in 1999 left him quadriplegic.

name: Frank Field
headline: Frank Field, Who Brought Expertise to TV Weathercasting, Dies at 100
abstract: The first meteorologist to forecast the weather on New York television, he later became known for, among other things, publicizing the Heimlich maneuver.

name: Jon Haggins
headline: Jon Haggins, Designer Who Slipped Into and Out of Fashion, Dies at 79
abstract: He was a member of a cohort of Black designers celebrated in the late 1960s and early ’70s. But struggles with financing led to several changes in direction.

name: Paul Justman
profession: Shed Light on Motowns Unsung Heroes
headline: Paul Justman, Who Shed Light on Motown’s Unsung Heroes, Dies at 74
abstract: After establishing himself as a leading music video director in the 1980s, he found acclaim with his 2002 documentary about session musicians.

name: Anthony Bouza
headline: Anthony Bouza, Police Commander Who Ruffled Feathers, Dies at 94
abstract: A self-confessed maverick, he was praised by some and criticized by others for ideas that upset the law-enforcement status quo.

name: Susan Love
headline: Dr. Susan Love, Surgeon and Breast Health Advocate, Dies at 75
abstract: One of the world’s most visible public faces in the war on breast cancer, she helped reshape both the doctor’s role and the patient’s.

name: Peter Brötzmann
profession: His Thunderous Saxophone Shook Jazz Traditions
headline: Peter Brötzmann, 82, Dies; His Thunderous Saxophone Shook Jazz Traditions
abstract: One of Europe’s most influential free-jazz musicians, he played with “a kind of scream” to exorcise his demons, and those of German history.

name: Edward Fredkin
profession: Saw the Universe as One Big Computer
headline: Edward Fredkin, 88, Who Saw the Universe as One Big Computer, Dies
abstract: An influential M.I.T. professor and an outside-the-box scientific theorist, he gained fame with unorthodox views as a pioneer in digital physics.

name: Lewis Branscomb
headline: Lewis Branscomb, Champion of Science Across Fields, Dies at 96
abstract: He led scientific advances at IBM and within the federal government during a career that spanned the space race and the dawn of the internet.

name: Coco Lee
headline: Coco Lee, ‘Crouching Tiger’ and ‘Mulan’ Singer, Dies at 48
abstract: A pop star across Asia by her early 20s, Ms. Lee reached international recognition with an Oscar-nominated song in 2001.

name: Winnie Ewing
headline: Winnie Ewing, Who Transformed Scottish Politics, Dies at 93
abstract: Her charismatic nationalism made independence from Britain a mainstream idea. She championed that idea for her many decades in office.

name: Jack Goldstein
headline: Jack Goldstein, a Savior of Broadway Theaters, Dies at 74
abstract: He helped secure landmark status for more than two dozen theaters in the 1980s, then initiated the design competition that led to a new TKTS booth.

name: Lawrence Turman
profession: Producer Spotted a Winner in The Graduate
headline: Lawrence Turman, 96, Dies; Producer Spotted a Winner in ‘The Graduate’
abstract: He was relatively new to the business when he was struck by an obscure novel and turned it into the biggest film of 1967.

name: Yan Mingfu
profession: Tried to Defuse the Tiananmen Powder Keg
headline: Yan Mingfu, Who Tried to Defuse the Tiananmen Powder Keg, Dies at 91
abstract: As an envoy the to the pro-democracy protesters, Mr. Yan, who was also Mao’s interpreter, tried to find a peaceful way out of the crisis.

name: Sue Johanson
headline: Sue Johanson, Who Talked Sex With Aplomb, Dies at 92
abstract: A beloved radio and television host, first in Canada and then also in the U.S., she approached the hottest topic with compassion and humor.

name: Evva Hanes
headline: Evva Hanes, Who Made Moravian Cookies World Famous, Dies at 90
abstract: She made several varieties of the thin, crispy cookie in a factory next door to her North Carolina home, and sold 10 million of them a year.

name: Hannie Schaft
profession: Resistance Fighter During World War II
headline: Overlooked No More: Hannie Schaft, Resistance Fighter During World War II
abstract: She killed Nazis in the Netherlands and was known as “the girl with the red hair” on their most-wanted list. Then she was executed.

name: Nikki McCray-Penson
headline: Nikki McCray-Penson, Basketball Star and Coach, Dies at 51
abstract: After a standout college career at the University of Tennessee, she won two Olympic gold medals, played nine years in the W.N.B.A. and was the head coach at two universities.

name: Peter Nero
headline: Peter Nero, Pianist Who Straddled Genres, Is Dead at 89
abstract: He soared to popularity with a swinging hybrid of classics and jazz. He later conducted the Philly Pops, often with one hand while the other played piano.

name: James F. Dobbins
headline: James F. Dobbins, Leading Authority on Nation Building, Dies at 81
abstract: His Foreign Service career took him on a tour of world hot spots, including Somalia, Haiti, the Balkans and Afghanistan, where he led efforts to rebuild war-torn countries.

name: Henry Kamm
headline: Henry Kamm, Pulitzer-Winning New York Times Journalist, Dies at 98
abstract: In a 47-year career at The Times, he covered Cold War diplomacy in Europe, famine in Africa and genocide in Southeast Asia and was also an author.

name: James W. Lewis
headline: James W. Lewis, Suspect in the 1982 Tylenol Murders, Dies at 76
abstract: He was never charged with the deaths of seven people from cyanide-laced Tylenol, but he was convicted of extortion after he sent a letter to Johnson & Johnson demanding $1 million to “stop the killing.”

name: Benno Schmidt Jr.
profession: Reforming Leader at Yale and CUNY
headline: Benno Schmidt Jr., a Reforming Leader at Yale and CUNY, Dies at 81
abstract: A noted constitutional law scholar, he also led Columbia University Law School and two networks of for-profit private schools.

name: Ruth Fitzpatrick
profession: Crusader for Letting Women Be Priests
headline: Ruth Fitzpatrick, Crusader for Letting Women Be Priests, Dies at 90
abstract: Feeling called to the Roman Catholic priesthood but denied entry, she became a leader of a national group that has pushed the Vatican to ordain women.

name: Ellen Hovde
headline: Ellen Hovde, ‘Grey Gardens’ Documentarian, Dies at 97
abstract: She worked with the Maysles brothers on the groundbreaking film about two Long Island recluses, and she later shared an Emmy for a mini-series about Ben Franklin.

name: Milan Kundera
headline: Milan Kundera, Literary Star Who Skewered Communist Rule, Dies at 94
abstract: The author of “The Unbearable Lightness of Being,” he was known for sexually charged novels that captured the suffocating absurdity of life in his native Czechoslovakia.

name: Gerald C. Meyers
headline: Gerald C. Meyers, C.E.O. Who Paved Way for the S.U.V., Dies at 94
abstract: He led a struggling but innovative (if not quirky) American Motors to record profits and helped fuel an appetite for off-road vehicles with the Jeep Cherokee.

name: Mary Ann Hoberman
headline: Mary Ann Hoberman, 92, Dies; Her Rhymes Tantalized Young Readers
abstract: She wrote whimsical tales about the little things in a child’s life. “A House Is a House for Me” won a National Book Award.

name: Evelyn M. Witkin
headline: Evelyn M. Witkin, Who Discovered How DNA Repairs Itself, Dies at 102
abstract: Her findings led to breakthroughs in the treatment of cancer and in the understanding of the mechanics of evolution.

name: Minnie Bruce Pratt
headline: Minnie Bruce Pratt, Celebrated Poet of Lesbian Life, Dies at 76
abstract: Her collection “Crime Against Nature,” which recounts her losing custody of her children after she came out, made her a literary star — and a target of conservatives.

name: Carlo Vittorini
headline: Carlo Vittorini, Publisher Who Lifted Parade Magazine, Dies at 94
abstract: He spent two decades guiding a popular newspaper Sunday supplement as its revenue and circulation grew, reaching nearly 40 million readers at one point.

name: Rick Froberg
headline: Rick Froberg, Singer of Artful Intensity, Is Dead at 55
abstract: A longtime linchpin of a 1990s underground music scene, he built a devoted and enthusiastic following and was also a prolific visual artist.

name: John Uelses
headline: John Uelses, First to Pole-Vault 16 Feet, Is Dead at 85
abstract: In an era when track and field athletes could rise to national celebrity, Uelses became a newsreel idol and made the cover of Sports Illustrated.

name: André Watts
headline: André Watts, Pioneering Piano Virtuoso, Dies at 77
abstract: One of the first Black superstars in classical music, he awed audiences with his charisma and his technical powers.

name: Melvin Wulf
headline: Melvin Wulf, Transformative Civil Liberties Lawyer, Dies at 95
abstract: As legal director for 15 years, he made the A.C.L.U. a more aggressive organization and worked with Ruth Bader Ginsburg before she became a United States Supreme Court justice.

name: Carlos Alberto Montaner
headline: Carlos Alberto Montaner, Prominent Critic of Castro’s Cuba, Dies at 80
abstract: After fleeing the island in 1961, he became one of the leading voices of opposition against the country’s Communist dictatorship.

name: Everett Mendelsohn
headline: Everett Mendelsohn, Who Linked Science and Society, Dies at 91
abstract: A longtime professor at Harvard, he lectured on atom bombs, genetics and more, examining how science, culture and politics influence one another.

name: Marga Minco
headline: Marga Minco, Who Chronicled Jewish Life in Wartime, Dies at 103
abstract: Her best-known book, “Het Bittere Kruid” (“Bitter Herbs”), described her experiences as a young woman after the Nazi invasion of the Netherlands in 1940.

name: Jane Birkin
