headline: Jane Birkin, Singer, Actress and Fashion Inspiration, Dies at 76
abstract: She was a lithe beauty of 1960s European film, a famous musical collaborator and lover of Serge Gainsbourg, and the namesake of elegant Hermès handbags.

name: Sally Kempton
headline: Sally Kempton, Rising Star Journalist Turned Swami, Dies at 80
abstract: She was making her name in New York journalism in the footsteps of her famous father and becoming an outspoken feminist when she met an Indian guru.

name: C.R. Roberts
headline: C.R. Roberts, Scoring Sensation in Milestone Game, Dies at 87
abstract: In 1956, he starred for the University of Southern California in a signal victory over an all-white University of Texas team after withstanding racial threats.

name: Harry G. Frankfurt
profession: Philosopher With a Surprise Best Seller
headline: Harry G. Frankfurt, Philosopher With a Surprise Best Seller, Dies at 94
abstract: He spent his career exploring will and deceit. Then came a sudden success: a bluntly titled book that found that one strain of dishonesty with a barnyard name was worse than lying.

name: Beverly Moss Spatt
profession: Protector of Landmarks in New York
headline: Beverly Moss Spatt, Protector of Landmarks in New York, Dies at 99
abstract: Grand Central Terminal. Grand Army Plaza. The Queensboro Bridge. They, and more, were preserved as historic treasures under her fierce watch at the city’s landmarks commission.

name: Stephen M. Silverman
headline: Stephen M. Silverman, Biographer of Stage and Screen, Is Dead at 71
abstract: An entertainment journalist, he persuaded the publicity-shy director David Lean to let him write his story and died before seeing his final book, on Stephen Sondheim, published.

name: Angelo Mozilo
profession: Mortgage Giant Fell in Housing Bust
headline: Angelo Mozilo, Whose Mortgage Giant Fell in Housing Bust, Dies at 84
abstract: He built Countrywide Financial into the country’s largest mortgage lender, but its increasingly risky loans helped precipitate the 2008 financial crisis.

name: Dermot Doran
headline: Dermot Doran, Priest Who Rallied Aid for Biafran Airlift, Dies at 88
abstract: In 1968, Father Doran, who had been in Nigeria as an educator, became the linchpin of one of the largest civilian humanitarian efforts in history.

name: Steve Pieters
headline: Steve Pieters, Pastor Who Spoke of AIDS in Famed Interview, Dies at 70
abstract: He had the disease and was interviewed on the PTL network in 1985 by Tammy Faye Bakker, a broadcast that was said to have changed minds and hearts.

name: James Reston Jr.
profession: Author With a Hand in Nixon Apology
headline: James Reston Jr., Author With a Hand in Nixon Apology, Dies at 82
abstract: A historian and novelist, he provided a 96-page “interrogation” memo for David Frost’s TV interviews that prodded Nixon to admit, “I let the American people down” over Watergate.

name: Lilli Vincenz
profession: Lesbian Crusader When Few Dared to Be One
headline: Lilli Vincenz, Lesbian Crusader When Few Dared to Be One, Dies at 85
abstract: After being ousted from the U.S. military for being gay, she became an early fighter for gay rights and a prominent figure in the nascent L.G.B.T.Q. rights movement.

name: Jerry Bradley
headline: Jerry Bradley, Who Helped Remake Country Music, Dies at 83
abstract: A longtime Nashville executive, he was the driving force behind “Wanted! The Outlaws,” the 1976 album that sold a million copies and shook up the status quo.

name: Kevin Mitnick
profession: Once the Most Wanted Computer Outlaw
headline: Kevin Mitnick, Once the ‘Most Wanted Computer Outlaw,’ Dies at 59
abstract: Best known for an audacious hacking spree in the 1990s involving the theft of data and credit card numbers, he later became a security consultant and public speaker.

name: Martha Saxton
headline: Martha Saxton, Historian Who Explored Women’s Lives, Dies at 77
abstract: Her wide range of subjects included the actress Jayne Mansfield, the novelist Louisa May Alcott and Mary Washington, the mother of a president.

name: Dick Biondi
headline: Dick Biondi, Fast-Talking Star of Top 40 Radio, Dies at 90
abstract: “Wild, outrageous, goofy and uplifting,” as one fan put it, he was based in Chicago for most of his career but had fans all over the country.

name: Carlin Glynn
headline: Carlin Glynn, 83, Actress Whose Comeback Brought Her a Tony, Dies
abstract: After putting her career on hold to raise children, she won the part of the madam in “The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas” — and then a statuette hailing her performance.

name: Tony Bennett
profession: Jazzy Crooner of the American Songbook
headline: Tony Bennett, Jazzy Crooner of the American Songbook, Is Dead at 96
abstract: From his initial success at the Paramount in Times Square through his generation-spanning duets, his career was remarkable for both its longevity and its consistency.

name: James B. Zagel
headline: James B. Zagel, U.S. Judge Who Jailed Illinois Governor, Dies at 82
abstract: He sentenced Rod Blagojevich to 14 years to send a message about corruption in high places. As a prosecutor he helped put the mass murderer Richard Speck in prison.

name: João Donato
headline: João Donato, Innovative Brazilian Musician, Is Dead at 88
abstract: A prolific pianist, composer and arranger who began recording in the 1950s, he was a pioneer of bossa nova but didn’t confine himself to any genre.

name: Lily Parr
headline: Overlooked No More: Lily Parr, Dominant British Soccer Player
abstract: She persevered at a time when women were effectively banned from the sport, and was the first woman inducted into England’s National Football Hall of Fame.

name: Catherine Burks-Brooks
headline: Catherine Burks-Brooks, 83, Freedom Rider Who Had the Last Word, Dies
abstract: She was among a small group of students who restarted the Freedom Rides after the first attempt ended in violence and nearly destroyed the movement.

name: Mike Reynolds
headline: Mike Reynolds, 79, Dies; Champion of California’s Three-Strikes Law
abstract: The murder of his daughter sent him on a successful quest to push for tougher sentencing at a time when violent crime was a top concern nationwide.

name: Richard Barancik
profession: Last of the World War II Monuments Men
headline: Richard Barancik, Last of the World War II Monuments Men, Dies at 98
abstract: He played a role in the celebrated Allied operation to preserve European artworks and cultural treasures stolen by the Nazis.

name: Cheri Pies
headline: Cheri Pies, Who Guided Lesbian Couples in Parenthood, Dies at 73
abstract: She made her name with a watershed book for same-sex parents and later studied the impact of racial and economic inequality on health.

name: Reeves Callaway
headline: Reeves Callaway, Maker of Really, Really Fast Cars, Dies at 75
abstract: He turbocharged high-end vehicles for Alfa Romeo, Chevrolet and others, and in 1988 a Corvette he had modified reached over 254 miles per hour, breaking a record.

name: Ales Pushkin
headline: Ales Pushkin, Dissident Artist in Belarus, Is Dead in Prison at 57
abstract: A “holy fool,” in his words, he railed against the repressive Lukashenko government, once with a pile of manure. He died under mysterious circumstances.

name: Johnny Lujack
headline: Johnny Lujack, a Star Quarterback at Notre Dame, Dies at 98
abstract: He took the Irish to three national championships in the 1940s, won the Heisman Trophy in 1947 and then had a stellar (if brief) stint with the Chicago Bears.

name: Rocky Wirtz
headline: Rocky Wirtz, Owner of N.H.L.’s Chicago Blackhawks, Dies at 70
abstract: He assumed control of the team after his father’s death and helped bring it to prominence. But the mishandling of an assault accusation dimmed that success.

name: Simpson Kalisher
headline: Simpson Kalisher, Photographer Who Captured Urban Grit, Dies at 96
abstract: He emerged from a largely commercial background to join the towering figures who defined an art form — street photography — in the 1950s and ’60s.

name: Sinead O’Connor
headline: Sinead O’Connor, Evocative and Outspoken Singer, Is Dead at 56
abstract: She broke out with the single “Nothing Compares 2 U,” then caused an uproar a few years later by ripping up a photo of Pope John Paul II on “S.N.L.”

name: Bo Goldman
headline: Bo Goldman, Oscar-Winning Screenwriter, Dies at 90
abstract: He was a struggling writer when he won an Academy Award for “One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest.” He won another for “Melvin and Howard.”

name: Julian Barry
headline: Julian Barry, Who Made Lenny Bruce Into ‘Lenny,’ Dies at 92
abstract: Mr. Barry’s scripts for a hit Broadway play and later a Hollywood movie about that rule-breaking comic helped give Mr. Bruce a lasting place in pop culture lore.

name: Bill Geddie
headline: Bill Geddie, a Creator of ‘The View,’ Is Dead at 68
abstract: His partnership with Barbara Walters began when he produced her prime-time specials. He later helped turn her idea for an all-female talk show into a long-running hit.

name: Louise Levy
profession: Was Studied for Her Very Long Life
headline: Louise Levy, Who Was Studied for Her Very Long Life, Is Dead at 112
abstract: She was one of hundreds of people, all of them Ashkenazi Jews, whose good health and cognitive ability at extreme old age were the subject of genetic research.

name: Randy Meisner
headline: Randy Meisner, a Founding Member of the Eagles, Dies at 77
abstract: The group’s original bass player, he was a member from 1971 to 1977, but he was never one to jostle for the spotlight.

name: Jean Fagan Yellin
profession: Uncovered a Slavery Tales True Author
headline: Jean Fagan Yellin, Who Uncovered a Slavery Tale’s True Author, Dies at 92
abstract: Her research proved that a 19th-century book presumed to be a novel by a white woman was actually an autobiography by a formerly enslaved Black woman.

name: Mari Ruti
headline: Mari Ruti, Scholar of Gender, Sexuality and More, Dies at 59
abstract: Her books explored psychoanalytic theories and a range of other topics, including the enduring popularity of a Julia Roberts movie.

name: Pamela Blair
headline: Pamela Blair, an Original ‘Chorus Line’ Cast Member, Dies at 73
abstract: As Val, one of the dancers in the hit Broadway musical, she sang a memorable song explaining how she got work by enhancing her body through cosmetic surgery.

name: Hugh Carter Jr.
headline: Hugh Carter Jr., Who Pinched Pennies for a President, Dies at 80
abstract: While his cousin Jimmy was in the White House, his job was to make the Oval Office less imperial. Staffers called him “Cousin Cheap.”

name: SunRay Kelley
headline: SunRay Kelley, Master Builder of the Counterculture, Dies at 71
abstract: The go-to guru for those seeking their dream yurt, spiritual retreat or treehouse, he brought forth his handmade structures like a wizard with a chain saw.

name: Edward Sexton
profession: Bespoke Tailor of Rock n Roll
headline: Edward Sexton, Bespoke Tailor of Rock ’n’ Roll, Dies at 80
abstract: With his partner, Tommy Nutter, he outfitted London celebrities at the tail end of the Swinging Sixties — and beyond — in suits with swagger.

name: Alan Roland
headline: Alan Roland, 93, Psychoanalyst Who Cautioned Against Western Bias, Dies
abstract: In “In Search of Self” and other books, he emphasized the role of cultural influences in a patient’s life.

name: Lois Libien
profession: Found a Readership With Household Tips
headline: Lois Libien, Who Found a Readership With Household Tips, Dies at 87
abstract: As a journalist she covered issues affecting women, then turned to writing about housekeeping in handbooks and a syndicated newspaper column.

name: Roger Sprung
profession: Banjo Virtuoso of N.Y.C. Folk Scene
headline: Roger Sprung, Banjo Virtuoso of N.Y.C. Folk Scene, Dies at 92
abstract: The “godfather” of progressive bluegrass, he grew up in New York, honed his skills in the mountains and flourished in Greenwich Village in the ’60s.

name: Myron Goldfinger
headline: Myron Goldfinger, 90, Architect of Monumental Modernist Homes, Dies
abstract: His houses, which dot the Hamptons and other parts of the New York region, include a residence featured in “The Wolf of Wall Street.”

name: Richard O. Simpson
headline: Richard O. Simpson, First U.S. Product Safety Czar, Dies at 93
abstract: As Nixon’s choice to lead the Consumer Product Safety Commission, he protected the public from buying 25 million risky goods.

name: Seiichi Morimura
headline: Seiichi Morimura, 90, Who Exposed Japanese Wartime Atrocities, Dies
abstract: In a widely read book, he detailed gruesome biological experiments on people at a secret Imperial Army site in occupied China before and during World War II.

name: Jess Search
headline: Jess Search, a Force in the Documentary Genre, Dies at 54
abstract: As one of the leaders of Doc Society, she supported countless filmmakers, with an emphasis on underrepresented groups and unconventional stories.

name: Mark Margolis
headline: Mark Margolis, Scene-Stealing Actor in ‘Breaking Bad,’ Dies at 83
abstract: His ex-drug lord in a wheelchair was unable to speak, but Mr. Margolis, who also appeared in “Better Call Saul,” didn’t need dialogue to wield fearsome power.

name: Leny Andrade
headline: Leny Andrade, ‘First Lady of Brazilian Jazz,’ Dies at 80
abstract: With her soulful, cigarette-tinged contralto and emotive “bossa-jazz” stylings, she mesmerized audiences and critics alike.

name: William H. Dilday Jr.
profession: First Black TV Station Manager in U.S
headline: William H. Dilday Jr., First Black TV Station Manager in U.S., Dies at 85
abstract: Hired to run a troubled Mississippi affiliate of NBC, he turned it into a respected and highly profitable operation, with a more diverse staff.

name: Julia Scully
headline: Julia Scully, Influential Photography Editor and Memoirist, Dies at 94
abstract: She oversaw Modern Photography for 20 years and wrote an acclaimed book about her rough-and-tumble childhood, some of it spent in an orphanage and in remote Alaska.

name: Charles J. Ogletree Jr.
profession: at Harvard Law, a Voice for Equal Justice
headline: Charles J. Ogletree Jr., 70, Dies; at Harvard Law, a Voice for Equal Justice
abstract: A mentor to the Obamas and many others, he was renowned for his work in both the classroom and the courtroom, taking cases on behalf of the famous and the indigent alike.

name: Florence Berger
headline: Florence Berger, Who Helped People Find Enduring Love, Dies at 83
abstract: A tenured professor at Cornell with a feel for human chemistry, she found a second calling as a successful matchmaker. Almost all of her pairings lasted.

name: Henri Konan Bédié
profession: Ivory Coast President Deposed in a Coup
headline: Henri Konan Bédié, Ivory Coast President Deposed in a Coup, Dies at 89
abstract: As a longtime power broker he helped make his West African country an economic dynamo, but in office he fomented ethnic divisions and cracked down on dissent.

name: William Friedkin
profession: Director of French Connection and Exorcist
headline: William Friedkin, Director of ‘French Connection’ and ‘Exorcist,’ Dies at 87
abstract: He made his name with two of the biggest box-office hits of the 1970s. But despite some later successes, he never regained his early acclaim.

name: Rhoda Karpatkin
headline: Rhoda Karpatkin, Who Led Consumer Reports for Decades, Dies at 93
abstract: The first woman to be named executive director of Consumers Union, the publisher of Consumer Reports, she expanded its readership and its influence in Washington.

name: Michael Boyd
headline: Michael Boyd, 68, Who Invigorated the Royal Shakespeare Company, Dies
abstract: He is credited with stabilizing that venerable British troupe while energizing it with ambitious projects, including Broadway’s “Matilda the Musical.”

name: DJ Casper
profession: Hit Song Cha-Cha Slide Made You Dance
headline: DJ Casper, Whose Hit Song ‘Cha-Cha Slide’ Made You Dance, Dies at 58
abstract: The popular line dance, which gained international fame in the early 2000s, has been a staple at family functions, night clubs and more for more than 20 years.

name: Martin Walser
profession: Among Postwar Germanys Last Literary Titans
headline: Martin Walser, 96, Dies; Among Postwar Germany’s Last Literary Titans
abstract: He won critical and commercial acclaim, but drew censure for comments on the Holocaust and antisemitic tropes in one of his novels.

name: Alice K. Ladas
headline: Alice K. Ladas, Whose Book Popularized the G-Spot, Dies at 102
abstract: Working with collaborators, she wrote “The G Spot,” which became a cultural sensation and sold more than a million copies.

name: Amos Badertscher
headline: Amos Badertscher, Who Documented a Sexual Underground, Dies at 86
abstract: He took intimate photographic portraits of hustlers, prostitutes and drag queens on Baltimore’s streets and in gay bars.

name: Robbie Robertson
headline: Robbie Robertson, 80, Dies; Canadian Songwriter Captured American Spirit
abstract: As the chief songwriter and guitarist for the Band, he offered a rustic vision of his adopted country that helped inspire the genre that came to be known as Americana.

name: Rodriguez
headline: Rodriguez, Singer Whose Career Was Resurrected, Dies at 81
abstract: Two albums in the early 1970s went largely unnoticed in the United States, but not overseas. Then came the 2012 documentary “Searching for Sugar Man.”

name: Brice Marden
headline: Brice Marden, Who Rejuvenated Painting in the 1960s, Dies at 84
abstract: When conceptual art, Pop Art and minimalist sculpture were in the ascendancy and many were saying that painting was dead, Mr. Marden issued a powerful counterstatement.

name: Herbert J. Siegel
headline: Herbert J. Siegel, Investor in Major Media Deals, Dies at 95
abstract: As head of Chris-Craft Industries, he played a role in the Time-Warner merger and sold 10 television stations to Rupert Murdoch.

name: Jamie Reid
profession: His Anarchic Graphics Helped Define the Sex Pistols
headline: Jamie Reid, 76, Dies; His Anarchic Graphics Helped Define the Sex Pistols
abstract: He created some of the most controversial — and celebrated — artwork of the punk era, which outraged polite British society almost as much as the band’s music did.

name: Richard J. Whalen
headline: Richard J. Whalen, Biographer of Joseph P. Kennedy, Dies at 87
abstract: His book about the patriarch of the Kennedy political dynasty was a best seller. He later worked, briefly and not happily, for Richard M. Nixon.

name: W. Jason Morgan
headline: W. Jason Morgan, Who Developed Theory of Plate Tectonics, Dies at 87
abstract: His framework offered a new way to think about continental drift and revolutionized the study of earthquakes, volcanoes and evolution.

name: Joan Kaplan Davidson
headline: Joan Kaplan Davidson, Philanthropist Who Championed New York, Dies at 96
abstract: As president of a foundation established by her father, she focused her grant making on issues related to the city’s architecture, design and quality of life.

name: John Barrett
headline: John Barrett, Hairdresser for the Fashionable Elite, Dies at 66
abstract: His salon on the penthouse level of Bergdorf Goodman drew regulars like Martha Stewart, Princess Diana, Ethel Kennedy and Hillary Clinton.

name: Tom Jones
headline: Tom Jones, Half of Record-Setting ‘Fantasticks’ Team, Dies at 95
abstract: He wrote the book and lyrics to a little show that opened in 1960 in Greenwich Village and became “the longest-running musical in the universe.”

name: Keith Waldrop
headline: Keith Waldrop, Professor and Award-Winning Poet, Dies at 90
abstract: He won the National Book Award for poetry in 2009, having first been nominated 40 years earlier. He also taught at Brown University for four decades.

name: Nechama Tec
headline: Nechama Tec, Polish Holocaust Survivor and Scholar, Dies at 92
abstract: She wrote about heroic Jewish resisters in her book “Defiance,” which was later made into a film starring Daniel Craig and Liev Schreiber.

name: Frederick Eberstadt
headline: Frederick Eberstadt, Photographer of Socialites and Artists, Dies at 97
abstract: The son of a Wall Street lion, he charted his own course with a camera, chronicling uptown Manhattan society and the downtown cool crowd.

name: Clarence Avant
headline: Clarence Avant, Mighty Engine Behind Black Superstars, Dies at 92
abstract: Behind the scenes, he furthered the careers of numerous entertainers, as well as some athletes and politicians.

name: Magoo
headline: Magoo, Rapper and Former Timbaland Collaborator, Dies at 50
abstract: The man whose birth name was Melvin Barcliff was a teenager in Virginia when he joined a hip-hop scene that continues to influence music today.

name: Philip L. Sherman
headline: Philip L. Sherman, Who Circumcised Thousands of Babies, Dies at 67
abstract: A mohel who became a boldface name, he said his record in 45 years of performing the Jewish religious rite was 11 in a single day (including two pairs of twins).

name: Joan Meyer
profession: Longtime Editor of a Besieged Newspaper
headline: Joan Meyer, Longtime Editor of a Besieged Newspaper, Dies at 98
abstract: She collapsed a day after the police raided her home and the offices of The Marion County Record, a weekly paper in Kansas.

name: Renata Scotto
headline: Renata Scotto, Opera Diva Who Inhabited Roles, Dies at 89
abstract: A leading Italian soprano, she sang more than two dozen roles at the Metropolitan Opera and was known as a charismatic stage partner — and a demanding one.

name: Dorothy Casterline
headline: Dorothy Casterline, Who Codified American Sign Language, Dies at 95
abstract: She collaborated with two professors at Gallaudet University on the first ASL dictionary, laying the groundwork for a flourishing in Deaf identity over the last 50 years.

name: Robert H. Giles
headline: Robert H. Giles, Newspaper Editor and Nieman Curator, Dies at 90
abstract: He headed the journalism program at Harvard after overseeing Pulitzer Prize-winning coverage of the Kent State shootings and corruption in Michigan.

name: Carol Duvall
headline: Carol Duvall, a TV Queen of Crafting, Dies at 97
abstract: On Michigan television and then on national shows, she showed viewers how to make all sorts of decorative and practical items. The responses she got could be moving.

name: Aleksandar Matanovic
headline: Aleksandar Matanovic, 93, Dies; His Publishing Company Changed Chess
abstract: Largely self-taught, he became a grandmaster in his 20s and was later a founder of Chess Informant, which revolutionized how people studied the game.

name: Paul Brodeur
headline: Paul Brodeur, Reporter Who Exposed the Hazards of Asbestos, Dies at 92
abstract: In his long career at The New Yorker, he specialized in writing about this and other threats to people’s health, including chlorofluorocarbons.

name: Michael Parkinson
headline: Michael Parkinson, Famous for Interviewing the Famous, Dies at 88
abstract: A mainstay of British television, he was best known for a long-running BBC program that was called simply “Parkinson.”

name: Jerry Moss
headline: Jerry Moss, the ‘M’ of A&M Records, Is Dead at 88
abstract: In partnership with Herb Alpert, he turned a small independent label into a powerhouse with a roster full of superstars.

name: James L. Buckley
profession: Conservative Senator in Liberal New York
headline: James L. Buckley, Conservative Senator in Liberal New York, Dies at 100
abstract: In 1970, Mr. Buckley, the son of an oil tycoon and the brother of a leading force on the right, became the first third-party candidate elected to the U.S. Senate in 30 years.

name: John Devitt
profession: Champion Swimmer With a Tarnished Gold Medal
headline: John Devitt, Champion Swimmer With a Tarnished Gold Medal, Dies at 86
abstract: He won two Olympic gold medals for Australia, but the second was awarded after a disputed finish — one of the more freakish moments in sports history.

name: Ada Deer
profession: Native American Voice Inside Government and Out
headline: Ada Deer, Native American Voice Inside Government and Out, Dies at 88
abstract: A champion of tribal sovereignty, she was the first chairwoman of the Menominee in Wisconsin and the first Native American woman to lead the Bureau of Indian Affairs.

name: Jerome Hauer
profession: Manager of Catastrophes and Other Crises
headline: Jerome Hauer, 71, Manager of Catastrophes and Other Crises, Dies
abstract: Working for New York City, New York State and the U.S. government, he made a career of preparing for the worst and then dealing with it, from 9/11 to hurricanes.

name: Jean-Louis Georgelin
headline: Jean-Louis Georgelin, Face of the Notre-Dame Reconstruction, Dies at 74
abstract: A former army chief of staff, he was put in charge of the cathedral’s restoration and prided himself on keeping the project on track.

name: Rosemary S. Pooler
headline: Rosemary S. Pooler, Federal Judge and Consumer Defender, Dies at 85
abstract: Three decades after establishing herself as a civil rights lawyer, she became a trailblazer for women on the bench in two upstate New York districts.

name: Thierry Despont
headline: Thierry Despont, 75, Dies; Brought Elegance to Prestigious Properties
abstract: Whether helping refurbish the Statue of Liberty and the Carlyle hotel or decorating the homes of Bill Gates and Calvin Klein, he designed with a sense of heritage and place.

name: Inga Swenson
headline: Inga Swenson, Who Went From Stage to ‘Benson,’ Dies at 90
abstract: She had success on Broadway in “110 in the Shade” and other shows, but a later generation knew her from a sitcom.

name: Gus Solomons Jr.
profession: Rare Black Presence in Experimental Dance
headline: Gus Solomons Jr., 84, Dies; a Rare Black Presence in Experimental Dance
abstract: An uncompromising, charismatic dancer and choreographer, he was a towering (6-foot-3) figure who taught, wrote and had the ability, a colleague said, “to wake you up.”

name: Ron Cephas Jones
profession: Emmy Winner for This Is Us
headline: Ron Cephas Jones, Emmy Winner for ‘This Is Us,’ Dies at 66
abstract: After facing homelessness in his youth, he became an admired theater and television actor, playing tough and weathered but vulnerable characters.

name: Robert M. Budd
headline: Overlooked No More: Robert M. Budd, Whose Newsstand Was Like No Other
abstract: He built a thriving business in New York selling back numbers, or old issues of newspapers and magazines, recognizing their value and the history they contained.

name: Howard S. Becker
profession: Looked at Society With a Fresh Eye
headline: Howard S. Becker, Who Looked at Society With a Fresh Eye, Dies at 95
abstract: A sociologist, he challenged conventional thinking on matters as diverse as deviance, art making and marijuana use. He found a particular following in France.

name: Maxie Baughan
headline: Maxie Baughan, Feared Linebacker of the 1960s, Dies at 85
abstract: A star at Georgia Tech and later in the N.F.L., he dominated his way to nine Pro Bowl selections and could be inducted into the Hall of Fame next year.

name: Sliman Bensmaia
headline: Sliman Bensmaia, Who Enabled Prosthetic Limbs to Feel, Dies at 49
abstract: His work in the neuroscience of touch led to devices that allow amputees and quadriplegics not just to move about the world but also to sense temperature and pressure.

name: Tom Courtney
headline: Tom Courtney, Runner Who Lunged to Grab Olympic Gold, Dies at 90
abstract: In 1956 in Melbourne, he was dueling with another American when an English runner burst toward the finish line. But Courtney had one last surge in him.

name: Betty Tyson
headline: Betty Tyson, Who Was Wrongfully Imprisoned for Murder, Dies at 75
abstract: She was New York’s longest-serving female inmate when her conviction was overturned in 1998. She left prison 25 years to the day after her arrest.

name: Robert Paulson
headline: Robert Paulson, Long-Term A.L.S. Survivor, Is Dead at 86
abstract: He lived with the condition also known as Lou Gehrig’s disease much longer than most and spread the message, an admirer said, that disability was “just a different way of living.”

name: Toto Cutugno
headline: Toto Cutugno, Singer Whose ‘L’Italiano’ Struck a Chord, Dies at 80
abstract: The nostalgic ballads and catchy pop songs he wrote paved the way for an international career. He sold more than 100 million albums worldwide.

name: Warren Hoge
profession: Covered Wars and World Crises for The Times
headline: Warren Hoge, Who Covered Wars and World Crises for The Times, Dies at 82
abstract: A correspondent and bureau chief, he wrote vividly from all corners of the globe before rising in newsroom leadership as foreign editor and assistant managing editor.

name: Johaar Mosaval
profession: Broke Free of Apartheid for Ballet
headline: Johaar Mosaval, Who Broke Free of Apartheid for Ballet, Dies at 95
abstract: Of South Asian descent, he was discriminated against as “colored” in South Africa, but he flourished in London as a principal dancer with the Royal Ballet.

name: Terry Funk
headline: Terry Funk, Hard-Core Hall of Fame Wrestler, Dies at 79
abstract: A fierce fighter known for wielding improvised weapons, he brought his menacing image not just to the ring but also to Hollywood, in films like “Road House.”

name: Carol Robles-Román
headline: Carol Robles-Román, Latina Champion for Justice, Dies at 60
abstract: As a New York City deputy mayor and a lawyer for the city and state court systems, she fought for equal access and opportunity for women, immigrants and minorities.

name: John Warnock
headline: John Warnock, Inventor of the PDF, Dies at 82
abstract: As a founder of Adobe Systems, he oversaw the development of software and systems that made modern personal computing possible.

name: Albert Quie
headline: Albert Quie, Conservative Who Was Ahead of His Time, Dies at 99
abstract: As a Republican in the House of Representatives from Minnesota and as the state’s governor, he became identified with Christian piety and limited government.

name: Karol Bobko
profession: First to Pilot the Challenger Into Space
headline: Karol Bobko, First to Pilot the Challenger Into Space, Dies at 85
abstract: Almost three years before it exploded, he was aboard the shuttle on its maiden flight. He commanded two other shuttle missions and was the first New York City native to orbit the earth.

name: Howard Hubbard
profession: Longtime Albany Bishop Clouded by Scandal
headline: Howard Hubbard, Longtime Albany Bishop Clouded by Scandal, Dies at 84
abstract: The youngest American to be made a bishop, he died while still defending himself against allegations of sexual abuse.

name: Yevgeny Prigozhin
headline: Yevgeny Prigozhin, Renegade Mercenary Chief Who Rattled Kremlin
abstract: A tycoon and a Putin ally, he built a paramilitary force that fought by Russia’s side even as he castigated its military leaders. He died at 62 in a plane crash, Russian authorities said.

name: Léa Garcia
profession: Raised Black Actors Profile in Brazil
headline: Léa Garcia, Who Raised Black Actors’ Profile in Brazil, Dies at 90
abstract: Best known internationally for her breakout performance in the 1959 film “Black Orpheus,” she challenged racial stereotypes over a seven-decade career.

name: Dmitri Utkin
headline: Dmitri Utkin, a Leader of the Wagner Mercenaries
abstract: Mr. Utkin, 53, was a prominent commander in the private Russian military company and a longtime lieutenant to Yevgeny V. Prigozhin. He died in a plane crash, Russian authorities said.

name: Isabel Crook
profession: Her Life in China Spanned a Century of Change
headline: Isabel Crook, 107, Dies; Her Life in China Spanned a Century of Change
abstract: A noted educator and anthropologist, she spent almost her entire life in China, where she was a committed friend of the Communist government.

name: David Jacobs
profession: Turned Soap Opera Drama Into Prime-Time Gold
headline: David Jacobs, 84, Dies; Turned Soap Opera Drama Into Prime-Time Gold
abstract: As the creator of “Dallas” and its spinoff “Knots Landing,” he did more than anyone to change the landscape of nighttime TV.

name: Bob Barker
profession: Longtime Host of The Price Is Right
headline: Bob Barker, Longtime Host of ‘The Price Is Right,’ Dies at 99
abstract: The winner of numerous Emmy Awards, he was almost as well known for his advocacy of animal rights as he was for his half a century as a daytime television fixture.

name: David LaFlamme
headline: David LaFlamme, Whose ‘White Bird’ Captured a 1960s Dream, Dies at 82
abstract: As a founder of the San Francisco band It’s a Beautiful Day, he was at the center, if not in the forefront, of the Haight-Ashbury acid-rock explosion.

name: Claude Ruiz-Picasso
headline: Claude Ruiz-Picasso, Who Ran His Artist Father’s Estate, Dies at 76
abstract: He took charge of the estate after he and his sister Paloma successfully sued in court to be recognized as Pablo Picasso’ s legitimate heirs.

name: Samuel Wurzelbacher
headline: Samuel Wurzelbacher, Celebrated as ‘Joe the Plumber,’ Dies at 49
abstract: For Republicans in 2008, he briefly became a symbol of Middle America when he questioned the presidential candidate Barack Obama in a televised encounter.

name: Don Sundquist
headline: Don Sundquist, Two-Term Tennessee Governor, Is Dead at 87
abstract: A Republican, he never lost an election in 12 years in Congress and eight more as governor, but his party soured on him when he proposed a state income tax.

name: Nicholas Hitchon
profession: Aged 7 Years at a Time in Up Films
headline: Nicholas Hitchon, Who Aged 7 Years at a Time in ‘Up’ Films, Dies at 65
abstract: He was one of the original children profiled in “Seven Up!,” a 1964 British documentary, and reappeared in subsequent installments for more than a half-century.

name: Pat Corrales
profession: Manager of Three Major League Teams
headline: Pat Corrales, Manager of Three Major League Teams, Dies at 82
abstract: The first big league manager of Mexican descent and a former catcher, he led teams in Texas, Cleveland and Philadelphia.

name: Tina Howe
profession: Playwright Best Known for Coastal Disturbances
headline: Tina Howe, Playwright Best Known for ‘Coastal Disturbances,’ Dies at 85
abstract: She mixed insight and absurdity in a vast body of work that also included “Painting Churches” and “Pride’s Crossing,” both of which were Pulitzer finalists.

name: Laszlo Birinyi
profession: Leading Stock Picker and Market Forecaster
headline: Laszlo Birinyi, Leading Stock Picker and Market Forecaster, Dies at 79
abstract: His investment strategy, which tracked the flow of money, won him a reputation for prescience in the 1990s.

name: Richard Ekstract
profession: Magazine Publisher With Link to Warhol
headline: Richard Ekstract, Magazine Publisher With Link to Warhol, Dies at 92
abstract: He was promoting a new trade journal, Tape Recording, when he lent a video recorder to Andy Warhol, who used it to make a classic work with Edie Sedgwick.

name: Ray Hildebrand
profession: Paul of Hitmakers Paul and Paula
headline: Ray Hildebrand, the ‘Paul’ of Hitmakers Paul and Paula, Dies at 82
abstract: He wrote a romantic song for his friend’s girlfriend, Paula, and recorded it as a duet with Jill Jackson. It became a No. 1 hit.

name: Norman Pfeiffer
headline: Norman Pfeiffer, Bicoastal Architect of Civic Spaces, Dies at 82
abstract: His global portfolio was dominated by projects that helped revitalize downtown Los Angeles and restore landmarks in New York.

name: Gil Brandt
profession: Helped Make the Cowboys Americas Team
headline: Gil Brandt, 91, Dies; Helped Make the Cowboys ‘America’s Team’
abstract: As talent evaluator for nearly 30 years, he built Dallas into an N.F.L. powerhouse through the use of computer technology and other innovations.

name: Bill Pinkney
headline: Bill Pinkney, Globe-Circling Sailor Who Set a Racial Mark, Dies at 87
abstract: He was the first Black person to sail alone by way of the arduous southern route, rounding the perilous Cape Horn and withstanding storms and loneliness.

name: Mohamed al-Fayed
headline: Mohamed al-Fayed, Tycoon Whose Son Died With Diana, Is Dead at 94
abstract: An Egyptian businessman, he built an empire of trophy properties in London, Paris and elsewhere, but it was all overshadowed by a fatal car crash that stunned the world.

name: Franne Lee
headline: Franne Lee, Tony Winner Who Also Costumed Coneheads, Dies at 81
abstract: She worked on “Sweeney Todd” and “Candide” and also on the early seasons of “Saturday Night Live,” contributing to the look of the Blues Brothers and the Killer Bees.

name: Nancy Buirski
headline: Nancy Buirski, Award-Winning Documentary Filmmaker, Dies at 78
abstract: She won Emmy and Peabody Awards for “The Loving Story,” about a Virginia couple’s successful challenge to a ban on interracial marriage.

name: Jimmy Buffett
headline: Jimmy Buffett, Roguish Bard of Island Escapism, Is Dead at 76
abstract: With songs like “Margaritaville” and “Cheeseburger in Paradise,” he became a folk hero to fans known as Parrot Heads. He also became a millionaire hundreds of times over.

name: Bill Richardson
headline: Bill Richardson, Champion of Americans Held Overseas, Dies at 75
abstract: After serving in Congress and as governor of New Mexico, he practiced quasi-public and freelance diplomacy, often with considerable success.

name: Nathan Louis Jackson
profession: Writer for the Theater and TV
headline: Nathan Louis Jackson, Writer for the Theater and TV, Dies at 44
abstract: He wrote plays that tackled big issues like the death penalty and gun violence. He also wrote for series including the superhero saga “Luke Cage.”

name: Steve Harwell
profession: Voice of the Band Smash Mouth
headline: Steve Harwell, Voice of the Band Smash Mouth, Is Dead at 56
abstract: He was a founding member of the band, which broke out in the late 1990s with hit songs like “Walkin’ on the Sun” and “All Star.”

name: Douglas Lenat
profession: Tried to Make A.I. More Human
headline: Douglas Lenat, Who Tried to Make A.I. More Human, Dies at 72
abstract: He spent decades working on artificial intelligence, striving to create computers that could replicate common sense.

name: Marilyn Lovell
headline: Marilyn Lovell, Astronaut’s Wife in the Spotlight, Is Dead at 93
abstract: She embodied the glamour and the hardship of being married to an American hero. Her husband, Jim Lovell, was the commander of the ill-fated Apollo 13 mission in 1970.

name: Edith Grossman
headline: Edith Grossman, Who Elevated the Art of Translation, Dies at 87
abstract: “You are my voice in English,” Gabriel García Márquez told her. She insisted that her name appear on the covers of books she translated, including with that of Cervantes.

name: Gloria Coates
headline: Gloria Coates, Composer Who Defied Conventions, Is Dead at 89
abstract: A Wisconsin native, she was among the most prolific female composers of symphonies, 17 in all, finding particular prominence in Europe, where she lived.

name: Ferid Murad
headline: Ferid Murad, Nobelist Who Saw How a Gas Can Aid the Heart, Dies at 86
abstract: An American pharmacologist, he delved into the effects of nitric oxide, work that led to advances in treating heart disease, hypertension and erectile dysfunction.

name: Gary Wright
profession: Had a 70s Hit With Dream Weaver
headline: Gary Wright, Who Had a ’70s Hit With ‘Dream Weaver,’ Dies at 80
abstract: He was a pioneer in using synthesizers, and his friendship with George Harrison led to a spiritual awakening that also influenced another hit, “Love Is Alive.”

name: Sarah Wunsch
headline: Sarah Wunsch, Dogged Defender of Civil Liberties, Dies at 75
abstract: Her advocacy in New York and Massachusetts won protections for free speech, gender equality and access to birth control. And she was a voice on marital rape.

name: Arleen Sorkin
profession: Soap Opera Star With a Claim to Batman Fame
headline: Arleen Sorkin, Soap Opera Star With a Claim to Batman Fame, Dies at 67
abstract: Her “Days of Our Lives” character provided a rare burst of daytime-drama comedy. She was later the voice of Harley Quinn, the Joker’s henchwoman.

name: Patricia Caulfield
profession: Battled Warhol Over Use of Her Photograph
headline: Patricia Caulfield, 91, Dies; Battled Warhol Over Use of Her Photograph
abstract: She sued the pop artist while she was executive editor of Modern Photography. She later traveled the world as a nature photographer.

name: Sarah Young
profession: Created an Empire Around a Christian Devotional
headline: Sarah Young, 77, Dies; Created an Empire Around a Christian Devotional
abstract: Her book “Jesus Calling,” written in the voice of Jesus Christ, rose to the top of the Christian publishing best-seller lists. Sequels and spinoffs followed.

name: Shabtai Shavit
headline: Shabtai Shavit, Former Top Israeli Spymaster, Dies at 84
abstract: As director-general of the Mossad under three prime ministers, he helped orchestrate a treaty between Israel and Jordan. But he also showed an iron hand.

name: Mangosuthu Buthelezi
profession: Zulu Nationalist and a Mandela Rival
headline: Mangosuthu Buthelezi Dies at 95; Zulu Nationalist and a Mandela Rival
abstract: He was a powerful force as apartheid ended and bargaining over South Africa’s future began, emerging as a voice for tribal and ethnic rights, and powers for regional governments.

name: Marc Bohan
headline: Marc Bohan, Designer Who Oversaw the Dior Look for Decades, Dies at 97
abstract: As the creative force for Christian Dior longer than its founder, he maintained a reputation for playful elegance throughout fashion’s endless cycles.

name: Max Gomez
headline: Max Gomez, Longtime TV Medical Reporter, Dies at 72
abstract: Known as Dr. Max (he was not a medical doctor. but had a Ph.D. in neuroscience), he reported on health and science with an easygoing gravitas.

name: Richard Davis
headline: Richard Davis, Gifted Bassist Who Crossed Genres, Dies at 93
abstract: He was best known for his jazz work. But he was also heard on Van Morrison’s “Astral Weeks” and with orchestras conducted by Igor Stravinsky and Leonard Bernstein.

name: Ian Wilmut
profession: Scientist Behind Dolly the Cloned Sheep
headline: Ian Wilmut, Scientist Behind Dolly the Cloned Sheep, Is Dead at 79
abstract: He led a project in Scotland that, in 1996, cloned a mammal for the first time, a feat of genetic engineering that shocked the world.

name: Alfredo Martinez
headline: Alfredo Martinez, Who Fused Art World and Underworld, Dies at 56
abstract: He created hoopla around art made in prison — first in the early 2000s, with himself as the artist, then 20 years later with the scammer Anna Sorokin.

name: Nelia Sancho
profession: Beauty Queen Turned Defiant Rights Activist
headline: Nelia Sancho, Beauty Queen Turned Defiant Rights Activist, Dies at 71
abstract: She had been competing in pageants in the Philippines, but she found her calling when she observed the offenses of the Marcos regime firsthand.

name: Curtis Fowlkes
headline: Curtis Fowlkes, Avant-Jazz Pioneer of the 1980s, Dies at 73
abstract: A founder of the acclaimed Jazz Passengers, he was also a sought-after sideman who played trombone for both jazz and rock heavyweights.

name: Howard Safir
headline: Howard Safir, N.Y.P.D. Commissioner Under Giuliani, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Violent crime dropped under his sometimes contentious, sometimes innovative watch. But his response to the fatal police shootings of Black men drew criticism.

name: Len Chandler
profession: Early Fixture of the Folk Revival
headline: Len Chandler, an Early Fixture of the Folk Revival, Dies at 88
abstract: A singer who performed alongside Bob Dylan, Joan Baez and Pete Seeger, he was known for his topical songs, some of which he wrote in minutes.

name: Larry Chance
profession: Helped Keep Doo-Wop Alive for Decades
headline: Larry Chance, Who Helped Keep Doo-Wop Alive for Decades, Dies at 82
abstract: His career began in 1957, when he and some friends from the Bronx formed the vocal group that would become the Earls. He recorded his last song 65 years later.

name: Peter C. Newman
profession: Journalist and Scourge of Canadas Powerful
headline: Peter C. Newman, 94, Journalist and Scourge of Canada’s Powerful, Dies
abstract: A historian as well, he challenged, with a muckraker’s spirit, the political and corporate establishment of a country he adopted after fleeing Nazi-occupied Europe.

name: Éva Fahidi
headline: Éva Fahidi, Outspoken Holocaust Survivor, Dies at 97
abstract: She saw her family members marched off to their deaths while she went to a forced-labor camp. It took her almost 60 years to begin telling her story.

name: Lisa Lyon
headline: Lisa Lyon, Bodybuilding Pioneer and Mapplethorpe Muse, Dies at 70
abstract: She won the first Women’s World Pro Bodybuilding Championship. But she saw herself as an artist and posed for Robert Mapplethorpe and other photographers.

name: Hugo Blanco
headline: Hugo Blanco, Environment Activist Who Targeted Capitalism, Dies at 88
abstract: In Peru, he argued that global capitalism was at the root of the global ecological crisis, and he spent decades fighting for an alternative.

name: Molly Nelson
headline: Overlooked No More: Molly Nelson, Steward of Penobscot Culture
abstract: As a dancer, actress and storyteller also known as Molly Spotted Elk, she bridged her world and that of the West, captivating audiences along the way.

name: Lauch Faircloth
profession: Senator Targeted D.C. Home Rule in Crisis
headline: Lauch Faircloth Dies at 95; Senator Targeted D.C. Home Rule in Crisis
abstract: A North Carolina hog farmer and a Democrat-turned-Republican, he helped strip Mayor Marion Barry of his fiscal powers as Washington’s deficits swelled in the late ’90s.

name: Fernando Botero
headline: Fernando Botero, Artist of Whimsical Rotundity, Is Dead at 91
abstract: His voluptuous figures, both in paintings and in sculpture, portrayed the high and mighty as well as everyday people through an enlarging prism.

name: Bobby Schiffman
profession: Guiding Force of the Apollo Theater
headline: Bobby Schiffman, Guiding Force of the Apollo Theater, Dies at 94
abstract: Taking over for his father in 1961, he transformed a former vaudeville house in Harlem into a pre-eminent R&B showcase.

name: Erik Aschengreen
profession: Historian and Critic Illuminated Danish Dance
headline: Erik Aschengreen, 88, Dies; Historian and Critic Illuminated Danish Dance
abstract: In books, articles and lectures across Europe and America, he broadened an international appreciation of his native country’s rich dance tradition.

name: Charles Gayle
headline: Charles Gayle, Saxophonist of Fire and Brimstone, Dies at 84
abstract: An intense and uncompromising player, he made music that one critic said was more about “motion and spirit” than tonal centers, rhythms and melodies.

name: Tadaaki Kuwayama
headline: Tadaaki Kuwayama, 91, Dies; Painter Who Carved His Own Spare Path
abstract: Arriving in New York from Japan in 1958, he sought to “create works with no trace of touch” in cool but vivid monochromes.

name: Michael McGrath
headline: Michael McGrath, Tony Winner and ‘Spamalot’ Veteran, Dies at 65
abstract: He clanged coconuts in the Monty Python stage musical in 2005; seven years later, he won a Tony for “Nice Work if You Can Get It.”

name: Jules Melancon
headline: Jules Melancon, Oyster Farmer Who Tried Something New, Dies at 65
abstract: In the wake of hurricanes and the BP oil spill, he revolutionized his industry by turning from wild catches to cage farming his precious bivalves.

name: Irish Grinstead
headline: Irish Grinstead, Who Asked, ‘Where My Girls At?,’ Dies at 43
abstract: The song, from 1999, was the biggest hit for her, her sister and a friend, who made up the R&B trio 702.

name: Margaret Chung
headline: Overlooked No More: Margaret Chung, Doctor Who Was ‘Different From Others’
abstract: As the first known American woman of Chinese ancestry to earn a medical degree, she treated celebrities and opened a practice in San Francisco’s Chinatown.

name: Raymond Moriyama
headline: Raymond Moriyama, Designer of Humane Public Spaces, Dies at 93
abstract: His Japanese Canadian family was interned during World War II. That experience inspired him to create inviting buildings for all people.

name: Roger Whittaker
headline: Roger Whittaker, Balladeer With an International Reach, Dies at 87
abstract: A Briton with a rich baritone, he charmed audiences, mostly in Europe and America, with sentimental songs, like his signature hit, “The Last Farewell.”

name: James Hoge
headline: James Hoge, Who Led Two Big City Tabloids, Dies at 87
abstract: He was publisher of The Chicago Sun-Times, where he was also the top editor, and New York’s Daily News. He was later editor of Foreign Affairs magazine.

name: Michael Leva
headline: Michael Leva, Who Found Fashion Fame Early, Is Dead at 62
abstract: Known for sophisticated and wearable clothes, he was among a crop of young designers celebrated in the late 1980s. He went on to consult for fashion companies.

name: Robert Klane
headline: Robert Klane, Writer of ‘Weekend at Bernie’s,’ Dies at 81
abstract: He also adapted his best-known novel, “Where’s Poppa?,” into the script for a raw Carl Reiner comedy and directed the disco movie “Thank God It’s Friday.”

name: Jango Edwards
headline: Jango Edwards, Clown Who Challenged His Art Form, Dies at 73
abstract: More Frank Zappa than Ronald McDonald, he moved the field beyond red noses, infusing it with social commentary while breaking down walls of propriety.

name: Gita Mehta
headline: Gita Mehta, Whose Writing Shaped Perspectives of India, Dies at 80
abstract: Her novels and nonfiction provided alternatives to the Western- and male-centric views of modern India offered by writers like E.M. Forster.

name: Marvin Newman
profession: Photographer of Sports and the Streets
headline: Marvin Newman, Photographer of Sports and the Streets, Dies at 95
abstract: He captured people in shadow on Chicago sidewalks and under storefronts in wintry Coney Island. He also shot athletes like Muhammad Ali and Mickey Mantle.

name: Victor R. Fuchs
profession: Dean of American Health Care Economists
headline: Victor R. Fuchs, ‘Dean’ of American Health Care Economists, Dies at 99
abstract: He was among the first to offer a comprehensive explanation, and a possible solution, for the country’s rising health care costs.

name: Stephen Gould
profession: Tenor Best Known for Tackling Wagner
headline: Stephen Gould, Tenor Best Known for Tackling Wagner, Dies at 61
abstract: He was especially acclaimed for his performances at the Bayreuth Festival in Germany. As his voice developed, he once said, so did his view of how and why to deploy it.

name: Erwin Olaf
profession: Photographer With an Eye for the Theatrical
headline: Erwin Olaf, Photographer With an Eye for the Theatrical, Dies at 64
abstract: With exquisite precision, he used costumes and sets in staging many of his pictures, letting his subjects, whatever their social status, express themselves.

name: Giorgio Napolitano
headline: Giorgio Napolitano, Italian Post-Communist Pillar, Dies at 98
abstract: He served for 38 years in Parliament and, after being elected president at a critical moment in Italy’s fortunes, helped stabilize the country.

name: Buddy Teevens
headline: Buddy Teevens, Pioneering Dartmouth Football Coach, Dies at 66
abstract: He took the extraordinary step of banning tackling during all practices, which reduced concussions at a time when brain trauma in football had become a crisis.

name: Dick Clark
headline: Dick Clark, Iowan Who Walked 1,300 Miles for a Senate Seat, Dies at 95
abstract: After his unlikely win, in 1972, he spent his single term pushing for a more liberal foreign policy, particularly toward Africa.

name: Matteo Messina Denaro
headline: Matteo Messina Denaro, Long-Sought Italian Mafia Boss, Dies at 61
abstract: A high-ranking member of the Cosa Nostra, he was arrested in January after decades on the run. He was found through medical records related to his cancer treatment.

name: Barbara Mullen
profession: Rode Unorthodox Beauty to Modeling Fame
headline: Barbara Mullen, Who Rode Unorthodox Beauty to Modeling Fame, Dies at 96
abstract: With her 20-inch waist and gangly figure, she overcame early skepticism from editors to embody a new look in 1950s fashion.

name: David McCallum

name: Pearl Bowser

headline: Overlooked No More: Alice Anderson, Who Ran Australia’s First All-Woman Garage

headline: Brooks Robinson, Slick-Fielding Hall of Fame Third Baseman, Dies at 86
abstract: In his 23-year career, all of it with the Baltimore Orioles, he had 2,848 hits and 268 home runs. But he was best known for his unparalleled defense.

name: Endel Tulving
headline: Endel Tulving, Whose Work on Memory Reshaped Psychology, Dies at 96
abstract: He drew a distinction between the facts we learn and the experiences we remember, which he argued are part of what makes us human.

name: Nashawn Breedlove
headline: Nashawn Breedlove, Rapper Who Dueled Eminem in ‘8 Mile,’ Dies at 46
abstract: He drew praise for his scene in the film, in which he belittled Eminem’s character with sarcastic lyrics, a gruff voice and an imposing presence.

name: M. S. Swaminathan
headline: M. S. Swaminathan, Scientist Who Helped Conquer Famine in India, Dies at 98
abstract: Called the father of India’s Green Revolution, he served on agencies and boards around the world and developed a system of ecologically safe food production.

name: Michael Gambon

headline: Michael Gambon, Dumbledore in the ‘Harry Potter’ Films, Dies at 82
abstract: After he made his mark in London in the 1970s, he went on to play a wide range of roles, including Edward VII, Oscar Wilde and Winston Churchill.

name: Ed Fancher
headline: Ed Fancher, a Founder of The Village Voice, Is Dead at 100
abstract: When he started the alternative weekly with Dan Wolf and Norman Mailer in 1955, he later said, “We were crazy enough to think it would succeed.”

name: Dianne Feinstein
profession: Oldest Sitting Senator and Fixture of California Politics
headline: Dianne Feinstein, 90, Dies; Oldest Sitting Senator and Fixture of California Politics
abstract: She achieved remarkable political breakthroughs as a woman, becoming San Francisco’s first female mayor and the first woman elected to the Senate from California.

name: Lucy Morgan
headline: Lucy Morgan, Feared and Revered Florida Reporter, Dies at 82
abstract: Her investigations upended rural sheriffs’ departments, exposed state senators’ misdeeds and exemplified the power of a past era in American newspapering.

name: Tom Conway
headline: Tom Conway, Steelworkers President and Biden Ally, Dies at 71
abstract: A tough but pragmatic negotiator, he led his union through decades of tumult, then helped drive through the president’s infrastructure plans.

name: Robert Day
headline: Robert Day, Financier and Philanthropist, Dies at 79
abstract: An heir to an oil fortune, he built his own empire with TCW Group and was an influential California donor, including to his alma mater, Claremont McKenna College.

name: Lori Teresa Yearwood
profession: Journalist of Life on the Edge
headline: Lori Teresa Yearwood, Journalist of Life on the Edge, Dies at 57

name: Chris Snow
headline: Chris Snow, Hockey Executive Who Publicly Faced A.L.S., Dies at 42
abstract: The assistant general manager of the Calgary Flames, he was given a year to live in 2019. He and his wife used the time to document life with the disease.

headline: Tim Wakefield, Pitcher Who Helped Boston Break the Curse, Dies at 57
abstract: After surrendering a homer that ended the Red Sox run in 2003, he played a critical role in the team’s World Series victory a year later.

name: Alice Shalvi
profession: Hailed as a Mother of Feminism in Israel
headline: Alice Shalvi, Hailed as a Mother of Feminism in Israel, Dies at 96
abstract: She was an often defiant, galvanizing force in pressing for equal treatment for women in marriage, employment, education and more.

name: Horace Ové
headline: Horace Ové, Pioneering Black Filmmaker in Britain, Dies at 86

name: Echo Brown
headline: Echo Brown, Young Adult Author and Performer, Is Dead at 39
abstract: A one-woman show that used her date with a white hipster to talk about life, race, love and sex, led an editor to sign her to write two novels.

name: Beverly Willis
profession: Architect and Advocate for Women in the Field
headline: Beverly Willis, 95, Dies; Architect and Advocate for Women in the Field
abstract: With her own firm in San Francisco and a foundation in New York, she made it her mission to recognize the work of her female predecessors and contemporaries.

name: Ed Young

headline: Ed Young Dies at 91; Infused His Illustrations With Chinese Tradition
abstract: Over a 60-year career, he illustrated some 100 books of fairy tales, poetry and memoirs, and won a Caldecott Medal and two Caldecott Honors.

name: Harriet Pattison
profession: Landscape Architect With a Tie to Louis Kahn
headline: Harriet Pattison, 94, Dies; Landscape Architect With a Tie to Louis Kahn
abstract: After having a son with the famous architect, she built a career, often collaborating with Mr. Kahn on projects, including a New York memorial to Franklin D. Roosevelt.

name: James Jorden
profession: Creator of an Essential Opera Blog
headline: James Jorden, Creator of an Essential Opera Blog, Dies at 69
abstract: With Parterre Box, he brought together high culture, punk aesthetics and gleeful camp in an irreverent source for news, criticism and gossip.

name: Georgia Dullea

abstract: Writing for The Times with a gimlet eye, she examined the impact of no-fault divorces on women, the excesses of the Reagan years, the AIDS crisis, and more.

name: Joe Christopher
headline: Joe Christopher, an Original Met Who Was Amazin’ in ’64, Dies at 88

headline: Russell Sherman, Poetic Interpreter at the Piano, Is Dead at 93
abstract: He was a passionate, idiosyncratic performer of the classical canon in concerts and on recordings and admired as an educator.

name: Dick Butkus
headline: Dick Butkus, Fearsome Hall of Fame Linebacker, Is Dead at 80
abstract: He was both hard hitting against the run and fleet-footed in foiling pass plays in his eight seasons with the Chicago Bears. He later took up acting.

headline: Russell Batiste Jr., the Drumming Heartbeat of New Orleans, Dies at 57
abstract: A pyrotechnic funk and R&B mainstay, he was a vital figure in his home city as a member of one of its celebrated musical dynasties.

headline: Michael Bonallack, Britain’s Greatest Postwar Amateur Golfer, Dies at 88

name: Florence Fisher

profession: Top Model in a Segregated Era
headline: Helen Williams, Top Model in a Segregated Era, Is Dead at 87
abstract: She was one of the most photographed Black models of the 1950s and ’60s, seen mainly in magazines, like Ebony and Jet, aimed at the Black middle class.

name: Ken Mattingly
headline: Ken Mattingly, Astronaut Bumped From Apollo 13, Is Dead at 87
abstract: He later orbited the moon, but in 1970 he was scrubbed from the Apollo flight after being exposed to German measles. Then, from mission control, he helped it avert disaster.

name: William Pelham Jr.
headline: William Pelham Jr., Who Rethought How A.D.H.D. Is Treated, Dies at 75
abstract: A child psychologist, he argued that behavioral therapy had to come first in addressing attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, with drugs like Ritalin as a supplement.

name: Saleemul Huq
headline: Saleemul Huq, 71, Bangladeshi Spearhead on Climate Change, Dies
abstract: He pressed rich nations to compensate poorer ones for the disproportionate “loss and damage” they’ve endured because of greenhouse gas emissions.

name: Helen Marcus
headline: Helen Marcus, Prolific Photographer of the Famous, Dies at 97
abstract: One of the few women at the top of her field in book and magazine publishing, she was also a champion of her fellow professionals.

name: David Kirke
profession: Made the First Modern Bungee Jump
headline: David Kirke, Who Made the First Modern Bungee Jump, Dies at 78
abstract: An Oxford-educated prankster as colorful as he was daring, he accidentally helped invent a new extreme sport in the 1970s.

name: Jane Garrett
profession: Book Editor With a Prizewinning Touch
headline: Jane Garrett, Book Editor With a Prizewinning Touch, Dies at 88
abstract: In 44 years at Knopf, she shepherded history books that won a raft of Pulitzers — seven in all — as well as Bancrofts, although one recipient set off a furious debate.

name: Jeffrey A. Bader
profession: Helped Steer Obamas Pivot to Asia
headline: Jeffrey A. Bader, Who Helped Steer Obama’s ‘Pivot’ to Asia, Dies at 78
abstract: A veteran China expert, he advised Presidents Clinton and Obama as they navigated the complexities of Beijing’s rise to global power.

name: Robbin Bain
headline: Robbin Bain, Pageant Winner and ‘Today Girl,’ Is Dead at 87
abstract: After winning the annual Miss Rheingold beauty contest, in which millions voted, she covered fashion and beauty for the popular morning show.

name: Walter Davis
profession: Basketball Star With a Velvet Touch
headline: Walter Davis, Basketball Star With a Velvet Touch, Dies at 69
abstract: “Walter is a good shooter until the fourth period,” one coach said of Davis, a standout in both college and the N.B.A. “Then he becomes a great shooter.”

name: Zdenek Macal
headline: Zdenek Macal, Conductor With an International Reach, Dies at 87
abstract: Shuttling between Europe and the United States, he conducted the world’s great orchestras. He was music director of the New Jersey Symphony for 11 years.

name: Cody Dorman
profession: Forged a Close Bond With a Top Racehorse
headline: Cody Dorman, Who Forged a Close Bond With a Top Racehorse, Dies at 17
abstract: A boy with a rare genetic disorder inspired the name of the horse Cody’s Wish, who won at the Breeders’ Cup on Saturday.

name: Mortimer Downey
profession: Titan of Transit for New York and Nation
headline: Mortimer Downey, Titan of Transit for New York and Nation, Dies at 87
abstract: He devised innovative financing to revive New York City’s subway. In Washington, as a U.S. Transportation Department leader, he bolstered Amtrak and secured federal funds for public transit.

name: Mel Sembler
headline: Mel Sembler, Developer and G.O.P. Fund-Raiser, Is Dead at 93
abstract: He received ambassadorships after filling campaign coffers that led to two Bush presidencies. He later came around to backing Donald Trump.

name: Oleg Protopopov
profession: Skated With His Wife to Olympic Gold
headline: Oleg Protopopov, Who Skated With His Wife to Olympic Gold, Dies at 91
abstract: Twice Soviet champions at the Games, he and Ludmila Belousova revolutionized pairs figure skating in the 1960s with a balletic style before defecting to the West.

name: Philip Meyer
headline: Philip Meyer, Reporter Who Pioneered Data-Driven Journalism, Dies at 93
abstract: First as a correspondent and later as a professor, he pushed his industry to adopt more rigorous, quantitative methods.

name: Domenico Spano
profession: Clothier of Stars Found Fame of His Own
headline: Domenico Spano Dies at 79; Clothier of Stars Found Fame of His Own
abstract: Born in Italy, he dressed billionaires and film stars while turning heads for his own outfits in his adopted city, New York.

name: Elizabeth Moynihan
headline: Elizabeth Moynihan, Engine of the Senator’s Success, Dies at 94
abstract: She not only had an outsize role in New York and Washington politics as the wife of Daniel Patrick Moynihan; she also made a significant archaeological discovery in India.

name: Gary Winnick
profession: Won and Lost With Global Crossing
headline: Gary Winnick, Who Won and Lost With Global Crossing, Dies at 76
abstract: He masterminded the building of a transoceanic fiber-optics network to speed the internet and phone traffic. But in five years the company went bankrupt in a historic failure.

name: Alan Hevesi
headline: Alan Hevesi, New York Official Who Fell From Grace, Dies at 83
abstract: A state legislator from Queens and a city and state comptroller, he was forced to resign in a scandal and later imprisoned in a pay-to-play scheme.

name: Linda R. Hirshman
headline: Linda R. Hirshman, Who Challenged Stay-at-Home Mothers, Dies at 79
abstract: A feminist provocateur, she went on to write about the gay rights movement and transformative figures like the first two female Supreme Court justices.

name: Frank Borman
headline: Frank Borman, Astronaut Who Led First Orbit of the Moon, Dies at 95
abstract: He commanded the 1968 Apollo 8 mission that carried three astronauts farther from Earth than anyone had ever traveled. He later led Eastern Airlines.

name: Yuri Temirkanov
headline: Yuri Temirkanov, Conductor Who Celebrated Russia’s Music, Dies at 84
abstract: Immersed in his native land’s repertoire — Tchaikovsky, Rachmaninoff, Prokofiev — he drew bold, rich sounds from the world’s major orchestras. In Russia, he was adored.

name: Byron Wien
profession: Wall Street Seer of the Unexpected
headline: Byron Wien, Wall Street Seer of the Unexpected, Dies at 90
abstract: A widely read financial analyst, he was known for his annual forecast “Ten Surprises.” But he was fallible, as when he predicted a President Hillary Clinton.

name: Ángela Ruiz Robles
headline: Overlooked No More: Ángela Ruiz Robles, Inventor of an Early E-Reader
abstract: Long before Kindles and iPads became popular, Ruiz Robles, a teacher, created her Mechanical Encyclopedia to help lighten her students’ textbook load.

name: Marina Cicogna
profession: Italys First Major Female Film Producer
headline: Marina Cicogna, Italy’s First Major Female Film Producer, Dies at 89
abstract: A countess from an influential Italian family, she charted her own course and produced films by the likes of Pasolini and Zeffirelli.

name: Lara Parker
headline: Lara Parker, a Memorable Witch on ‘Dark Shadows,’ Dies at 84
abstract: Her three-dimensional portrayal of a character who was also a vampire helped the Gothic soap opera develop a cult following.

name: Peter S. Fischer
headline: Peter S. Fischer, Who Helped Create ‘Murder, She Wrote,’ Dies at 88
abstract: He spent many years as a writer and producer of the hit mystery series starring Angela Lansbury. He later wrote his own mystery novels, set in Hollywood.

name: David Ferry
headline: David Ferry, Poet and Translator Who Won Acclaim Late in Life, Dies at 99
abstract: After nearly 40 years as a professor, he began a new career writing poems and translating classics. He won a National Book Award when he was 86.

name: Karen Davis
profession: Battled for the Rights of Birds
headline: Karen Davis, Who Battled for the Rights of Birds, Dies at 79
abstract: A fierce campaigner, Ms. Davis expanded the reach of the animal rights movement by advocating for chickens, turkeys and other farmyard fowl.

name: Maryanne Trump Barry
profession: Retired Judge and Donald Trump Sister
headline: Maryanne Trump Barry, Retired Judge and Donald Trump Sister, Dies at 86
abstract: A former appellate federal judge in New Jersey, she supported her brother but, as audio recordings revealed in 2019, she could be scathingly critical of him.

name: Kevin Wynn
headline: Kevin Wynn, Choreographer of Complex Movement, Dies at 67
abstract: He became known for his “layered movement dialogue” and was an uncommonly dedicated teacher who mentored students over decades.

name: Shirley Jo Finney
headline: Shirley Jo Finney, 74, Dies; Addressed the Black Experience Onstage
abstract: After an acting career that included playing the Olympic sprinter Wilma Rudolph in a TV movie, she became known as a director for her work at regional theaters.

name: Roland Lajoie
profession: Army General at the Cold Wars Front Lines
headline: Roland Lajoie, Army General at the Cold War’s Front Lines, Dies at 87
abstract: Part officer, part diplomat, part spy, he led military inspections in East Germany and later oversaw the destruction of Soviet nuclear weapons.

name: Peter Seidler
headline: Peter Seidler, Big-Spending San Diego Padres Owner, Dies at 63
abstract: Under his leadership, the team’s payroll grew to one of the largest in Major League Baseball. But a championship proved elusive.

name: Joe Sharkey
headline: Joe Sharkey, Travel Writer Who Survived Midair Collision, Dies at 77
abstract: He offered advice to business travelers in hundreds of columns in The Times. His eyewitness account of a disaster was front-page news.

name: Sally Darr
headline: Sally Darr, Formidable Chef of ’80s-Era French Bistro, Dies at 100
abstract: A skilled and self-taught cook of homey French fare, she drew fans (including Julia Child) to her Greenwich Village restaurant for more than a decade.

name: Johnny Green
headline: Johnny Green, Jumpin’ Knicks All-Star, Dies at 89
abstract: An All-Star forward — and an all-American at Michigan State — he was known as Jumpin’ Johnny, able to soar over taller opponents for 14 seasons in the N.B.A.

name: Roger Kastel
headline: Roger Kastel, ‘Jaws’ Poster Artist, Dies at 92
abstract: A prolific illustrator, he was most closely associated with the image that made the “Jaws” paperback a runaway best seller, and the blockbuster film it inspired an enduring classic.

name: A.S. Byatt
headline: A.S. Byatt, Scholar Who Found Literary Fame With Fiction, Dies at 87
abstract: One of Britain’s most ambitious and intellectual novelists, she won the Booker Prize with “Possession,” her 1990 tale of illicit love spanning two centuries.

name: George Tscherny
headline: George Tscherny, Whose Graphic Designs Defined an Era, Is Dead at 99
abstract: With a bevy of corporate and institutional clients, he helped shape the visual language of the postwar American economy.

name: George Brown
headline: George Brown, Drummer With Kool & the Gang, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Brown kept time for a group that combined funk, disco, R&B and jazz to create some of the most memorable pop songs of the 1970s.

name: Brendan Sexton
headline: Brendan Sexton, a Pioneer of Recycling, Is Dead at 78
abstract: As New York City’s sanitation commissioner, he began the mandatory program to separate garbage. He also hired the department’s first uniformed women.

name: Don Walsh
headline: Don Walsh, Record-Breaking Deep Sea Explorer, Dies at 92
abstract: In 1960, aboard the submersible Trieste, he and a scientist made a historic dive of nearly seven miles into the ocean’s deepest spot.

name: Viktor Belenko
profession: Defected to the West in a Jet Fighter
headline: Viktor Belenko, Who Defected to the West in a Jet Fighter, Dies at 76
abstract: Among the highest-profile figures to flee the Soviet Union, he brought with him a secret weapon and firsthand experience behind the Iron Curtain.

name: David Del Tredici
headline: David Del Tredici, Who Set ‘Alice’ to Music, Dies at 86
abstract: A Pulitzer Prize-winning composer, he was an experimentalist who redefined himself, becoming identified with a lush style called the New Romanticism.

name: Karel Schwarzenberg
headline: Karel Schwarzenberg, Renegade Czech Prince and Politician, Dies at 85
abstract: Popular with the Czech public for quietly subverting the aristocracy, he served twice as foreign minister and ran for president in 2013.

name: Rosalynn Carter
profession: First Lady and a Political Partner
headline: Rosalynn Carter, First Lady and a Political Partner, Dies at 96
abstract: She helped propel Jimmy Carter from rural Georgia to the White House and became the most politically active first lady since Eleanor Roosevelt.

name: Bobby Ussery
headline: Bobby Ussery, Jockey Who Saw Triumph and Dismay, Dies at 88
abstract: In amassing 3,611 victories, he rode a long shot, Proud Clarion, to victory in the 1967 Kentucky Derby. The next year at Churchill Downs, he saw victory nullified.

name: Radcliffe Bailey
headline: Radcliffe Bailey, Artist Who Explored Black Migration, Dies at 54
abstract: His work blended family photographs with symbols of the African diaspora. The story he told, his gallerist said, is “not a ‘me’ thing, it’s a ‘we’ thing.”

name: Herbert Gold
profession: Postwar Novelist of Love and Marriage
headline: Herbert Gold, Postwar Novelist of Love and Marriage, Dies at 99
abstract: Part of the generation of Norman Mailer and Philip Roth, he explored the lives of ordinary men and women and the complexities of Jewish identity in America.

name: Carlton Pearson
profession: Pastor Deemed a Heretic for Denying Hell
headline: Carlton Pearson, Pastor Deemed a Heretic for Denying Hell, Dies at 70
abstract: He led a popular religious revival and a megachurch, but his peers and congregation abandoned him once he questioned core doctrine and advocated gay rights.

name: Peter Tarnoff
profession: Diplomat Helped Plot Argo Escape From Iran
headline: Peter Tarnoff Dies at 86; Diplomat Helped Plot ‘Argo’ Escape From Iran
abstract: A consummate man behind the scenes, he held top posts under Carter and Clinton, and in between ran the Council on Foreign Relations.

name: Elena Zelayeta
headline: Overlooked No More: Elena Zelayeta, Emissary for Mexican Cooking
abstract: Beginning the 1930s in San Francisco, she transformed the image of her native Mexican cuisine in the United States with a restaurant and popular cookbooks, all while overcoming a loss of sight.

name: Joan Jara
profession: Found Justice for Husband Slain After Coup
headline: Joan Jara, Who Found Justice for Husband Slain After Coup, Dies at 96
abstract: She sought accountability in the military killing of the leftist folk singer Victor Jara in the right-wing turmoil that carried Gen. Augusto Pinochet to power in Chile in 1973.

name: Bob Contant
headline: Bob Contant, Bohemian Bookseller Who Held On, Is Dead at 80
abstract: A founder of the St. Mark’s Bookshop in the East Village, he prided himself on stocking titles that were not “too popular” and stayed in business for four decades.

name: Joss Ackland
headline: Joss Ackland, Busy, Versatile Actor on Stage and Screen, Dies at 95
abstract: He was a villain in “Lethal Weapon 2,” C.S. Lewis on TV in “Shadowlands” and Falstaff onstage in “Henry IV” — and had a cameo in a Pet Shop Boys video.

name: Suzanne Shepherd
headline: Suzanne Shepherd, Actress Known for Playing Mothers, Dies at 89
abstract: After establishing herself as a teacher, she started a prolific screen acting career in her 50s that included roles in “Goodfellas” and “The Sopranos.”

name: Willie Hernández
headline: Willie Hernández, Relief Pitcher Who Had a Banner 1984, Dies at 69
abstract: He was voted the American League’s Most Valuable Player and won its Cy Young Award in a championship season with the Detroit Tigers. “It’s unbelievable,” he said.

name: Emmanuel Le Roy Ladurie
profession: Looked at History From the Bottom Up
headline: Emmanuel Le Roy Ladurie, Who Looked at History From the Bottom Up, Dies at 94
abstract: He led a movement that rejected historiography’s traditional emphasis on great events and leaders in favor of mining the “mental universe” of peasants, merchants and clergymen.

name: Charles Peters
headline: Charles Peters, Founder of The Washington Monthly, Dies at 96
abstract: His political journal challenged liberal and conservative orthodoxies for decades.

name: Audrey Salkeld
headline: Audrey Salkeld, Pioneering Historian of Everest, Dies at 87
abstract: She trawled 56 boxes of forgotten archives, bringing to life mysterious figures from early expeditions on the world’s highest peak.

name: Terry Taylor
profession: First Woman Named Sports Editor of The A.P
headline: Terry Taylor, First Woman Named Sports Editor of The A.P., Dies at 71
abstract: She brought a relentless management style to the wire service’s sports department for 21 years, supervising its coverage of sports around the world.

name: William Casey
headline: William Casey, Who Uncovered Police Corruption, Is Dead at 78
abstract: He was the unsung investigator whose dogged undercover probe exposed the “Dirty 30” scandal in a Harlem precinct.

name: Betty Rollin
profession: Wrote Candidly About Her Breast Cancer
headline: Betty Rollin, Who Wrote Candidly About Her Breast Cancer, Dies at 87
abstract: Coping with illness was the subject of a popular memoir, “First, You Cry.” In “Last Wish,” a best seller, she wrote about helping her mother end her life. She chose to end her own life as well.

name: Catherine Christer Hennix
headline: Catherine Christer Hennix, Spiritual Drone Musician, Dies at 75
abstract: She fused her mathematical knowledge with minimalist sounds and global spiritual traditions, most notably in her 1976 composition “The Electric Harpsichord.”

name: Marty Krofft
headline: Marty Krofft, 86, Dies: Created Fantastical TV Shows With Brother
abstract: With Sid Krofft, he produced children’s shows, like “H.R. Pufnstuf,” and prime time programs, including “Donny & Marie.”

name: Jean Knight
profession: Struck Platinum With Mr. Big Stuff
headline: Jean Knight, Who Struck Platinum With ‘Mr. Big Stuff,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Her anthem of female strength topped the Billboard R&B chart and reached No. 2 on the pop chart in 1971. Its appeal has endured.

name: Charles T. Munger
profession: Much More Than Warren Buffetts No. 2
headline: Charles T. Munger, Much More Than Warren Buffett’s No. 2, Dies at 99
abstract: A billionaire himself, he was the witty vice chairman of Mr. Buffett’s powerhouse investment firm Berkshire Hathaway. But he had far more influence than his title suggested.

name: Holly Maguigan
profession: Fought for the Rights of Battered Women
headline: Holly Maguigan, Who Fought for the Rights of Battered Women, Dies at 78
abstract: Through her scholarship and her teaching, she made it possible for women in abusive relationships to claim self-defense when fighting back.

name: Frances Sternhagen
headline: Frances Sternhagen, Actress Who Thrived in Mature Roles, Dies at 93
abstract: Her Tony-winning Broadway career included “Driving Miss Daisy,” “On Golden Pond” and “The Heiress.” On TV she had maternal roles in “Cheers” and “Sex and the City.”

name: Daisaku Ikeda
headline: Daisaku Ikeda, Who Led Influential Japanese Buddhist Group, Dies at 95
abstract: He grew Soka Gakkai International’s following over two decades and helped create a coalition partner for the country’s dominant Liberal Democratic Party.

name: Henry Kissinger
profession: Shaped the Nations Cold War History
headline: Henry Kissinger Is Dead at 100; Shaped the Nation’s Cold War History
abstract: The most powerful secretary of state of the postwar era, he was both celebrated and reviled. His complicated legacy still resonates in relations with China, Russia and the Middle East.

name: Shane MacGowan
headline: Shane MacGowan, Songwriter Who Fused Punk and Irish Rebellion, Is Dead at 65
abstract: As frontman for the Pogues, he romanticized whiskey-soaked rambles and hard-luck stories of emigration, while providing a musical touchstone for members of the Irish diaspora.

name: Sandra Day O’Connor
profession: First Woman on the Supreme Court
headline: Sandra Day O’Connor, First Woman on the Supreme Court, Is Dead at 93
abstract: During a crucial period in American law — when abortion, affirmative action, sex discrimination and voting rights were on the docket — she was the most powerful woman in the country.

name: Ronald Fischetti
headline: Ronald Fischetti, 87, Virtuoso Criminal Defense Lawyer, Dies
abstract: He had a client list that included a police officer accused of assault, a congressman caught up in a scandal, mobsters and former President Trump.

name: Henri Lopes
profession: Straddled Literature and Politics in Africa
