headline: Henri Lopes, 86, Who Straddled Literature and Politics in Africa, Dies
abstract: His lauded fiction satirized abuses of power in the continent, but as a high official for the Republic of Congo, he benefited from a much-criticized government.

name: Mica Ertegun
headline: Mica Ertegun, 97, Glamorous Interior Designer and Philanthropist, Dies
abstract: She and her longtime husband, the music magnate Ahmet Ertegun, were once called “the virtual definition of sophistication.”

name: Tim Dorsey
profession: Turned Floridas Quirks Into Comic Gold
headline: Tim Dorsey, Who Turned Florida’s Quirks Into Comic Gold, Dies at 62
abstract: Long before Florida Man became a meme, he mined the Sunshine State’s weirdness for enough material to fill 26 darkly funny crime novels.

name: John Nichols
profession: Author of The Milagro Beanfield War
headline: John Nichols, Author of ‘The Milagro Beanfield War,’ Dies at 83
abstract: After decamping from New York to New Mexico, he wrote what was, for a time, among the most widely read novels about Latinos.

name: Geordie Walker
headline: Geordie Walker, Guitarist for Killing Joke, Dies at 64
abstract: He helped define the look as well as the sound of the enduring British post-punk band, which influenced Nirvana, Metallica and others.

name: Robert H. Precht
profession: Producer of The Ed Sullivan Show
headline: Robert H. Precht, Producer of ‘The Ed Sullivan Show,’ Dies at 93
abstract: Among the highlights of his long tenure was supervising the Beatles’ appearances and filming their 1965 Shea Stadium concert.

name: Tim Rogers
profession: Hairstylist to the Stars and Moguls
headline: Tim Rogers, Hairstylist to the Stars and Moguls, Dies at 51
abstract: A native of Britain, he made his mark in his adopted city styling celebrities like Adele, Roger Federer and the Olsen twins.

name: Cobi Narita
headline: Cobi Narita, Tireless Jazz Promoter and Benefactor, Dies at 97
abstract: She produced concerts, helped musicians find work and started a women’s jazz festival. “Jazz in New York would not have been the same without Cobi,” one musician said.

name: Julius W. Becton Jr.
headline: Julius W. Becton Jr., Pathbreaking Army General, Dies at 97
abstract: A three-star general, he saw combat in three wars and was the first Black commander of an Army corps. He later led FEMA before focusing on education.

name: Norman Lear
profession: Comedies Changed the Face of TV
headline: Norman Lear, Whose Comedies Changed the Face of TV, Is Dead at 101
abstract: As the producer of “All in the Family” and many other shows, Mr. Lear showed that it was possible to be topical, funny and immensely popular.

name: Nguyen Qui Duc
headline: Nguyen Qui Duc, Whose Salon Became a Hanoi Hub, Dies at 65
abstract: A former refugee who found radio success in the U.S., he opened an exhibition space in his native Vietnam that drew artists and ambassadors. Anthony Bourdain dropped in.

name: Sandra Elkin
profession: Creator of a Pioneering Feminist Talk Show
headline: Sandra Elkin, Creator of a Pioneering Feminist Talk Show, Dies at 85
abstract: “Woman,” which she hosted, brought frank talk about issues like birth control, pay inequality and homosexuality into millions of homes in the 1970s.

name: Denny Laine
profession: Founding Member of the Moody Blues and Wings
headline: Denny Laine, Founding Member of the Moody Blues and Wings, Dies at 79
abstract: He wrote “Mull of Kintyre” with Paul McCartney and was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame with the Moody Blues.

name: Andrea Fay Friedman
headline: Andrea Fay Friedman, Who Built a Breakthrough Acting Career, Dies at 53
abstract: Ms. Friedman, who called Down syndrome her “up syndrome,” forged an unlikely path in acting by playing characters with developmental disabilities.

name: Isabella de la Houssaye
headline: Isabella de la Houssaye, Athlete Who Endured Against the Odds, Dies at 59
abstract: After being diagnosed with Stage 4 lung cancer, she continued to go on extreme adventures with her children, including an ascent of the tallest mountain in the Americas.

name: Benjamin Zephaniah
headline: Benjamin Zephaniah, Poet of Social Justice Issues, Dies at 65
abstract: He opened the door for future generations of poets of color to use their own voices.

name: Jane Wodening
profession: Experimental Film Star and Intrepid Writer
headline: Jane Wodening, Experimental Film Star and Intrepid Writer, Dies at 87
abstract: For 30 years she collaborated with the filmmaker Stan Brakhage, her husband, often appearing on camera. After they divorced, she lived off the grid and wrote about her life.

name: Colette Maze
headline: Colette Maze, Pianist Who Started Recording in Her 80s, Dies at 109
abstract: Born before the outbreak of World War I, she began making albums in the 1990s. She released her latest, “109 Ans de Piano,” this year.

name: Juanita Castro
headline: Juanita Castro, Who Turned Against Her Brother Fidel, Dies at 90
abstract: She was originally a supporter of the uprising that brought her brother to power. But she grew disillusioned, worked undercover for the C.I.A. and later fled the island.

name: Ellen Holly
profession: Challenged Racial Barriers on Daytime TV
headline: Ellen Holly, Who Challenged Racial Barriers on Daytime TV, Dies at 92
abstract: The first Black performer to play a lead role on a soap opera, she spurred controversy on “One Life to Live” in the late 1960s.

name: Janet Panetta
headline: Janet Panetta, 74, Dies; Admired Dancer, Choreographer and Teacher
abstract: She overcame childhood polio to become a dancer with American Ballet Theater, then taught contemporary dancers and members of Pina Bausch’s acclaimed company.

name: Ryan O’Neal
profession: Became a Star With Love Story
headline: Ryan O’Neal, Who Became a Star With ‘Love Story,’ Dies at 82
abstract: He was a familiar face on TV before his breakout performance opposite Ali MacGraw in the 1970 blockbuster movie. But it was overshadowed by years of personal problems.

name: Maria Emilia Martin
profession: Creator of Public Radios Latino USA
headline: Maria Emilia Martin, Creator of Public Radio’s ‘Latino USA,’ Dies at 72
abstract: As a radio journalist committed to the goal of representing all voices, she fought to tell the stories of Latino communities in the Americas.

name: Ada Blackjack
profession: Survivor of a Harrowing Arctic Expedition
headline: Overlooked No More: Ada Blackjack, Survivor of a Harrowing Arctic Expedition
abstract: She learned to fend for herself during a venture to Wrangel Island. By the time a rescue ship arrived, she was the last crew member standing.

name: John A. Talbott
profession: Champion of Care for the Mentally Ill
headline: Dr. John A. Talbott, Champion of Care for the Mentally Ill, Dies at 88
abstract: A psychiatrist and a prolific author, he criticized what he referred to as a “nonsystem” that left vulnerable people on the streets to fend for themselves.

name: Rick Ahearn
profession: Advance Man for Candidates and Presidents
headline: Rick Ahearn, Advance Man for Candidates and Presidents, Dies at 74
abstract: Renowned for his professionalism and attention to detail, he worked for Republicans from Nixon to Trump. He was by Ronald Reagan’s side when he was shot in 1981.

name: David Ellenson
profession: Guided a Generation of Reform Rabbis
headline: David Ellenson, 76, Who Guided a Generation of Reform Rabbis, Dies
abstract: A teacher and rabbi, he forged alliances across all branches of Judaism, and his scholarship confronted questions of Jewish tradition and modernity.

name: Gao Yaojie
profession: Exposed AIDS Epidemic in Rural China
headline: Dr. Gao Yaojie, Who Exposed AIDS Epidemic in Rural China, Dies at 95
abstract: Despite government efforts to silence her, she drew global attention to an epidemic that devastated rural China and killed tens of thousands.

name: Shlomo Avineri
headline: Shlomo Avineri, Israeli Scholar Skeptical About Peace, Dies at 90
abstract: A former liberal government official, he saw little chance of full reconciliation with Palestinians in “the foreseeable future” but nevertheless sought to ease tensions.

name: Celedonia Jones
headline: Celedonia Jones, Self-Educated New York Historian, Dies at 93
abstract: He served as Manhattan borough historian from 1997 to 2005. He also dug deeply into the history of Seneca Village, a mostly Black settlement in what became Central Park.

name: Glenys Kinnock
profession: Political Force in Britain and Europe
headline: Glenys Kinnock, Political Force in Britain and Europe, Dies at 79
abstract: The wife of the Labour leader Neil Kinnock, she carved her own leftist identity with a seat in the European Parliament and as a British government minister.

name: Zahara
profession: Acclaimed South African Singer and Guitarist
headline: Zahara, Acclaimed South African Singer and Guitarist, Dies at 36
abstract: A self-taught musician who sang in English and Xhosa, she was a prominent figure in contemporary Afro-soul known for her heartfelt voice.

name: George Cohon
headline: George Cohon, Who Brought Big Macs to Moscow, Dies at 86
abstract: He was chairman of McDonald’s in Canada and in Russia, where he opened the chain’s first restaurant in 1990, engaging in what he called “hamburger diplomacy.”

name: Michael Bishop
profession: Genre-Busting Writer Known for Science Fiction
headline: Michael Bishop, Genre-Busting Writer Known for Science Fiction, Dies at 78
abstract: His early work took readers to the stars, but his later work ventured into noir mystery and the back roads of the American South.

name: J. Michael Bishop
profession: Nobel Prize Winner for Cancer Research
headline: J. Michael Bishop, Nobel Prize Winner for Cancer Research, Dies at 90
abstract: He helped discover cancer-causing genes. Later, as chancellor of the University of California, San Francisco, he led a major expansion.

name: Sara Tavares
headline: Sara Tavares, Portuguese Singer Who Prized Her African Roots, Dies at 45
abstract: She drew on rhythms from across the African diaspora and sang in Portuguese, English, Cape Verdean Criolo and Angolan slang.

name: Lionel Dahmer
profession: Agonized About Raising a Serial Killer
headline: Lionel Dahmer, Who Agonized About Raising a Serial Killer, Dies at 87
abstract: The father of Jeffrey Dahmer, he wrote a memoir that one reviewer said sought to “peer not just into the soul of his son but into his own.”

name: Andre Braugher
profession: Actor on Homicide and Brooklyn Nine-Nine
headline: Andre Braugher, Actor on ‘Homicide’ and ‘Brooklyn Nine-Nine,’ Dies at 61
abstract: He was best known for playing stoic police officers on two acclaimed but very different television series — one an intense drama, the other a comedy.

name: Michael Blakemore
profession: Single-Season Double Tony Winner for Directing
headline: Michael Blakemore, a Single-Season Double Tony Winner for Directing, Dies at 95
abstract: Acclaimed in Britain, he had the unique distinction of winning awards for best musical and best play in 2000, for his Broadway revival of “Kiss Me, Kate” and “Copenhagen.”

name: Mort Engelberg
profession: Producer of Hit Films and Presidential Campaigns
headline: Mort Engelberg, Producer of Hit Films and Presidential Campaigns, Dies at 86
abstract: A celebrated “advance man” — responsible for logistics and camera-ready moments in campaigns — he forged a lasting bond with Bill Clinton.

name: Mary Cleave
profession: Glimpsed a Blighted Earth From Space
headline: Mary Cleave, Who Glimpsed a Blighted Earth From Space, Dies at 76
abstract: After flying on two shuttle missions and viewing a deteriorating world out a spacecraft window, she turned to environmental research for NASA.

name: Luiz Barroso
headline: Luiz Barroso, Who Supercharged Google’s Reach, Dies at 59
abstract: In designing warehouse-size data centers that behaved like a single computer, he changed the fabric of the internet.

name: Ted Morgan
headline: Ted Morgan, 91, Dies; Pulitzer-Winning Writer Straddled Two Cultures
abstract: An esteemed journalist and author, he was born to a French count but later shed his aristocratic roots (and name) to became a U.S. citizen.

name: George McGinnis
profession: Powered His Way to Basketball Stardom
headline: George McGinnis Dies at 73; Powered His Way to Basketball Stardom
abstract: He won two titles with the Pacers of the A.B.A. before joining Julius Erving on the N.B.A.’s 76ers, but it was 35 years before the Hall of Fame inducted him.

name: William G. Connolly
headline: William G. Connolly, Editor Who Updated The Times, Dies at 86
abstract: He sought more diversity among its newsroom employees and co-wrote a full-scale, and modernized, edition of the paper’s internal style guide.

name: Vera Molnar
headline: Vera Molnar, Pioneer of Computer Art, Dies at 99
abstract: Experimenting with algorithms, she began to employ the principles of computation in her work even before she gained access to an actual computer.

name: Neil Drossman
headline: Neil Drossman, Adman Who Sold With a Smile, Is Dead at 83
abstract: His sense of humor was evident in widely seen pitches he wrote for Meow Mix (“Tastes so good, cats ask for it by name”) and many other products.

name: Michel Ciment
headline: Michel Ciment, Eminent French Film Critic, Is Dead at 85
abstract: He helped define cinema as high art for generations of moviegoers and filmmakers in France and beyond, even if he irked some of them with his passion for Hollywood.

name: Mike Grgich
profession: His Wine Stunned the French by Besting Theirs
headline: Mike Grgich Dies at 100; His Wine Stunned the French by Besting Theirs
abstract: A Croatian immigrant’s California chardonnay was judged the top one in a famous Paris tasting. He later established his own acclaimed winery in Napa Valley.

name: Merle Goldman
headline: Merle Goldman, a Leading Expert on Communist China, Dies at 92
abstract: A lifelong academic, she stood apart in her ability to communicate her insights about the country to nonacademic readers.

name: Nawaf
headline: Sheikh Nawaf, Emir of Kuwait, Dies at 86
abstract: He was defense minister when Iraq invaded his tiny but oil-rich country, and he became ruler in his 80s.

name: Michael Stone
headline: Michael Stone, Psychiatrist and Scholar Who Studied Evil, Dies at 90
abstract: He attempted to define evil by plumbing the biographies and motivations of hundreds of violent felons who had committed heinous crimes.

name: Paul Chevigny
headline: Paul Chevigny, Early Voice on Police Brutality, Dies at 88
abstract: An eminent civil rights lawyer, he was one of the nation’s foremost experts on abusive policing. He also successfully challenged New York’s Cabaret Law.

name: Richard Hunt
headline: Richard Hunt, Sculptor Who Transformed Public Spaces, Dies at 88
abstract: He produced soaring installations of public art over a career that he said was shaped by attending the funeral of Emmett Till.

name: Guy Stern
profession: Fled Germany and Then Interrogated Nazis
headline: Guy Stern, Who Fled Germany and Then Interrogated Nazis, Dies at 101
abstract: He escaped as a teenager and later became one of the Ritchie Boys, a secret Army program that recruited refugees to gather battlefield intelligence.

name: Jeanne Hoff
headline: Jeanne Hoff, Pioneering Transgender Psychiatrist, Dies at 85
abstract: She shared the experience of her transition in a documentary to encourage her patients, many of whom were also transgender, to live openly and confidently.

name: Ken MacKenzie
headline: Ken MacKenzie, a Rare Winner on the 1962 Mets, Dies at 89
abstract: A left-handed reliever, he was the only pitcher with a winning record on a team that set a modern record for losses.

name: J.G.A. Pocock
headline: J.G.A. Pocock, Historian Who Argued for Historical Context, Dies at 99
abstract: He helped forge a movement asserting that scholars must put aside their modern-day assumptions and prejudices to fully understand how people acted and thought in the past.

name: Mars Williams
headline: Mars Williams, 68, Saxophonist Who Straddled New Wave and Jazz, Dies
abstract: He made his name in the 1980s with the Waitresses and the Psychedelic Furs, but his roots were in the exploratory jazz of Eric Dolphy and Ornette Coleman.

name: Dan Greenburg
headline: Dan Greenburg, Who Poked Fun With His Pen, Dies at 87
abstract: Women, sex and Jewish mothers were just some of the targets of his popular satirical writing in books, essays, screenplays and more.

name: Cari Beauchamp
profession: Chronicled the Women of Early Hollywood
headline: Cari Beauchamp, Who Chronicled the Women of Early Hollywood, Dies at 74
abstract: In books and magazine articles, she uncovered the forgotten story of the actresses and screenwriters who helped create the film industry.

name: Raymond Dirks
headline: Raymond Dirks, Whose Tipster Case Redefined Insider Trading, Dies at 89
abstract: In a far-reaching decision, the Supreme Court restored him from censured analyst to whistle-blower in a major corporate fraud.

name: Bob Pardo
profession: Pilot in Daring Vietnam War Rescue
headline: Bob Pardo, Pilot in Daring Vietnam War Rescue, Dies at 89
abstract: In an extraordinary act of aerial ballet, he helped a fellow pilot whose plane had become compromised until they could be safely rescued.

name: Robert M. Solow
headline: Robert M. Solow, Groundbreaking Economist and Nobelist, Dies at 99
abstract: His elegant work established that the main determinant of economic growth was technology, not growing capital and labor.

name: Antonio Negri
headline: Antonio Negri, 90, Philosopher Who Wrote a Surprise Best Seller, Dies
abstract: He became famous twice: first in 1979, for his imprisonment related to the murder of a former Italian premier, and then 20 years later, for his influential book “Empire.”

name: Irwin Cohen
profession: Turned a Factory Into Chelsea Market
headline: Irwin Cohen, Who Turned a Factory Into Chelsea Market, Dies at 90
abstract: He and his daughter transformed an abandoned Nabisco plant into a Manhattan destination for people who liked to cook, to eat and to gape.

name: Ethel Lindgren
headline: Overlooked No More: Ethel Lindgren, Anthropologist of Reindeer Herding Cultures
abstract: She is best remembered for importing reindeer to the Scottish Highlands centuries after they were hunted to extinction. About 150 roam there today.

name: Yacouba Sawadogo
headline: Yacouba Sawadogo, African Farmer Who Held Back the Desert, Dies at 77
abstract: Against the odds, facing the encroaching Sahara, he built a forest in Burkina Faso, becoming “a national hero” and winning acclaim abroad for his innovations.

name: Essra Mohawk
headline: Essra Mohawk, Self-Described Flower Child Singer-Songwriter, Dies at 75
abstract: She missed a shot at Woodstock glory. But she recorded well-received albums under her own name and worked with Frank Zappa, Jerry Garcia and others.

name: Giovanni Anselmo
profession: Leader of the Arte Povera Movement
headline: Giovanni Anselmo, a Leader of the Arte Povera Movement, Dies at 89
abstract: An artist of many mediums, he used a vast array of materials, including stone, paint, piles of earth and even lettuce, to provoke thought and wonder.

name: Carlos Lyra
headline: Carlos Lyra, Composer Who Brought Finesse to Bossa Nova, Dies at 90
abstract: When Brazilian musicians fused samba with jazz and classical influences in the 1950s and ’60s, he was among the first, and the best.

name: Laura Lynch
headline: Laura Lynch, a Founder of the Dixie Chicks, Dies at 65
abstract: She was on the band’s first two albums, but she was dismissed in 1995. She died in a car crash in Texas on Friday.

name: Mildred Miller
headline: Mildred Miller, Stalwart of the Metropolitan Opera, Dies at 98
abstract: In her 23 years at the Met, she sang with the greatest stars of her day. She had a second career as a leading figure in the artistic life of Pittsburgh.

name: Kamar de los Reyes
headline: Kamar de los Reyes, ‘One Life to Live’ Actor, Dies at 56
abstract: He was perhaps best known for playing a gangster-turned-police officer on daytime TV. He was also a voice on the video game “Call of Duty.”

name: Amp Fiddler
headline: Amp Fiddler, Versatile Keyboardist, Singer and Mentor, Dies at 65
abstract: A mainstay of Detroit’s soul, funk and electronic music scenes, he also offered guidance to young hip-hop and electronic music aspirants, notably J Dilla.

name: Paula Murphy
profession: Once the Fastest Woman on Wheels
headline: Paula Murphy, Once ‘the Fastest Woman on Wheels,’ Dies at 95
abstract: She proved that women could gain fame as speed demons on land by setting records on the Bonneville Salt Flats and on the nation’s racetracks.

name: Zita Carno
headline: Zita Carno, Concert Pianist, Coltrane Scholar and More, Dies at 88
abstract: A veteran of 25 years with the Los Angeles Philharmonic, she was known as much for her eccentricities as for her exceptional musicianship.

name: Tom Smothers
profession: Comic Half of the Smothers Brothers
headline: Tom Smothers, Comic Half of the Smothers Brothers, Dies at 86
abstract: Though he played a naïve buffoon onstage, he was the driving force behind the folk-singing duo’s groundbreaking TV show.

name: Wolfgang Schäuble
headline: Wolfgang Schäuble, German Politician Who Helped Forge European Unity, Dies at 81
abstract: An important figure in the reunification of East and West Germany, he played a key role in shaping German politics for decades and was once seen as a likely chancellor.

name: Gaston Glock
headline: Gaston Glock, Inventor of the Gun That Bears His Name, Dies at 94
abstract: A reclusive Austrian billionaire, he created the handgun worn by two-thirds of America’s police officers and the security forces of at least 48 countries.

name: Jiang Ping
headline: Jiang Ping, the ‘Conscience of China’s Legal World,’ Dies at 92
abstract: He was removed from his university presidency after supporting pro-democracy protesters at Tiananmen Square. He remained a relentless advocate for rule of law.

name: Herbert Kohl
profession: Former Wisconsin Senator and Milwaukee Bucks Owner
headline: Herbert Kohl, Former Wisconsin Senator and Milwaukee Bucks Owner, Dies at 88
abstract: A member of the family that founded Kohl’s department stores, he guarded federal budgets as a U.S. senator while spending lavishly to revive the N.B.A. team he owned.

name: Jacques Delors
headline: Jacques Delors, Passionate Architect of European Unity, Dies at 98
abstract: As the executive of the European Union for a decade, he oversaw its increasing economic integration and led the drive for a single currency, the euro.

name: Pope.L
headline: Pope.L, Provocative Performance Artist, Dies at 68
abstract: He is best known for crawling along the entirety of Broadway in Manhattan wearing a Superman costume, a work that blended satire and resistance.

name: Hanna Eshel
headline: Her Sculptures Were Ignored for 33 Years. Then She Got a New Roommate.
abstract: Hanna Eshel did not succeed in the New York art world. Her only reliable exhibit space was her own loft. But a musician in search of a home changed that.

name: Jim Ladd
headline: Jim Ladd, Free-Form Radio Trailblazer, Is Dead at 75
abstract: An institution of the airwaves in Los Angeles and beyond, he capitalized on the freedom the FM band offered in the 1970s to blaze his own path.

name: Bobby Rivers
headline: Bobby Rivers, 70, Amiable and Multifaceted Television Host, Dies
abstract: After getting his start as an entertainment reporter and film critic, he went on to host a show on the Food Network and establish a presence in the blogosphere.

name: Mike Nussbaum
headline: Mike Nussbaum, Celebrated Chicago Theater Actor, Dies at 99
abstract: He appeared memorably in “American Buffalo” and in the Pulitzer Prize-winning play “Glengarry Glen Ross.” But he gave up a career on Broadway for one in Chicago.

name: Gerry Holzman
profession: Master Carver of a New York Merry-Go-Round
headline: Gerry Holzman, Master Carver of a New York Merry-Go-Round, Dies at 90
abstract: He conceived and worked for 20 years — with about 1,000 volunteers — on the Empire State Carousel, featuring more than 20 handmade wooden riding animals native to New York.

name: Willie Ruff
headline: Willie Ruff, Jazz Missionary and Professor, Dies at 92
abstract: A master of the French horn, a rarity in jazz, he toured the world with the pianist Dwike Mitchell and taught music at Yale.

name: Mbongeni Ngema
headline: Mbongeni Ngema, Playwright Best Known for ‘Sarafina!,’ Dies at 68
abstract: Before the fall of apartheid, his plays, which also included “Woza Albert!” and “Asinamali,” challenged the South African government’s racial policies.

name: Les McCann
headline: Les McCann, Pianist, Singer and Soul Jazz Pioneer, Dies at 88
abstract: He released more than 50 albums but had his greatest commercial success with “Compared to What,” a recording that came together at the last minute in 1969.

name: Peter Magubane
headline: Peter Magubane, 91, Who Fought Apartheid With His Camera, Is Dead
abstract: He documented the cruelties of white South African rule, and he was made to pay for it, enduring beatings and 586 consecutive days in solitary confinement.

name: Ana Ofelia Murguía
profession: Mexican Actress and Voice in Coco
headline: Ana Ofelia Murguía, Mexican Actress and Voice in ‘Coco,’ Dies at 90
abstract: Her 60-year career in film, television and theater “marked an entire era” and made her one of Mexico’s most acclaimed actresses.

name: Frank Ryan
profession: Cerebral Quarterback Led Browns to 64 Title
headline: Frank Ryan Dies at 87; Cerebral Quarterback Led Browns to ’64 Title
abstract: Off the field, he earned a Ph.D. in mathematics and taught the subject at Rice and Yale. And he brought computers to the House of Representatives.

name: Maureen Flavin Sweeney
headline: Maureen Flavin Sweeney Dies at 100; Her Weather Report Delayed D-Day
abstract: She helped save General Eisenhower’s invasion from potential disaster, enabling the Allies to gain a foothold in France that was essential to victory in World War II.

name: Maurice Hines
headline: Maurice Hines, Tap-Dancing Star With His Brother, Dies at 80
abstract: He rose to stardom in an act with Gregory Hines and also performed on and off Broadway.

name: Eddie Bernice Johnson
headline: Eddie Bernice Johnson, Trailblazer in Congress and Beyond, Dies at 89
abstract: A Texas Democrat, she broke barriers in nursing and her state’s legislature before serving 15 terms in Congress.

name: Sidney M. Wolfe
headline: Sidney M. Wolfe, Scourge of the Pharmaceutical Industry, Dies at 86
abstract: For over 40 years, he and his organization, the Health Research Group, held government and manufacturers to account for unsafe medication.

name: Donald Wildmon
profession: Early Crusader in Conservative Culture Wars
headline: Donald Wildmon, Early Crusader in Conservative Culture Wars, Dies at 85
abstract: The American Family Association, which he founded, became a juggernaut in the Christian right’s campaign against sex and gay themes in art, television and pop culture.

name: Mike Sadler
profession: Intrepid Desert Navigator in World War II
headline: Mike Sadler, Intrepid Desert Navigator in World War II, Dies at 103
abstract: Like a human GPS, he guided Britain’s first special forces across the vast Sahara for hit-and-run raids on enemy bases in the battle against Rommel’s forces.

name: Martha Diamond
headline: Martha Diamond, Painter Who Captured New York Vistas, Dies at 79
abstract: Her work, at the border of representation and abstraction, influenced younger painters. But she did not gain broad public recognition until late in life.

name: June Jackson Christmas
headline: June Jackson Christmas, Pioneering Psychiatrist, Dies at 99
abstract: Dr. Christmas overcame race and gender barriers to run New York’s mental health agency under three mayors in the 1970s.

name: Glynis Johns
profession: Tony Winner for A Little Night Music
headline: Glynis Johns, Tony Winner for ‘A Little Night Music,’ Dies at 100
abstract: In a trans-Atlantic career that endured for more than 60 years, she was also known for her role in the hit Disney movie “Mary Poppins.”

name: Anthony Dias Blue
headline: Anthony Dias Blue, Whose Writing Elevated California Wines, Dies at 82
abstract: A longtime editor at Bon Appétit and a radio personality, he helped millions gain a new appreciation for the American wineries he loved.

name: Vinie Burrows
headline: Vinie Burrows, Acclaimed Actress Who Became an Activist, Dies at 99
abstract: Her Broadway career blossomed in the 1950s. But after finding a dearth of roles for Black women, she turned to one-woman shows that addressed racism and sexism.

name: Richard Gaddes
headline: Richard Gaddes, Opera Impresario Who Spotted Young Talent, Dies at 81
abstract: As leader of opera companies in Santa Fe and St. Louis, he welcomed new works as well as new artists.

name: David Soul
profession: Star of the Hit Cop Show Starsky & Hutch
headline: David Soul, a Star of the Hit Cop Show ‘Starsky & Hutch,’ Dies at 80
abstract: An actor and singer, he rose to fame in the 1970s as one half of the popular television crime-fighting duo. He also notched a No. 1 hit single in the U.S.

name: Anthony J. Alvarado
profession: Former New York City Schools Chancellor
headline: Anthony J. Alvarado, Former New York City Schools Chancellor, Dies at 81
abstract: He also turned two Manhattan districts into national models. But his tangled personal finances forced him to resign as the city’s first Hispanic schools chief.

name: Joseph Lelyveld
profession: Former Top Editor of The New York Times
headline: Joseph Lelyveld, Former Top Editor of The New York Times, Dies at 86
abstract: As executive editor from 1994 to 2001, he oversaw a period of growth, expanding national and international readerships, creating new sections and ushering in the digital age with a Times website.

name: Cordell Jackson
profession: Elder Stateswoman of Rock n Roll
headline: Overlooked No More: Cordell Jackson, Elder Stateswoman of Rock ’n’ Roll
abstract: A pioneering record-label owner and engineer, she played guitar in a raw and unapologetically abrasive way. “Whatever song it was,” she said, “I always creamed it.”

name: Joseph Hendrie
profession: Key Figure in the Three Mile Island Crisis
headline: Joseph Hendrie, 98, Dies; Key Figure in the Three Mile Island Crisis
abstract: He was chairman of the Nuclear Regulatory Commission in 1979, when America faced its worst nuclear power mishap in history.

name: Arno J. Mayer
headline: Arno J. Mayer, Unorthodox Historian of Europe’s Crises, Dies at 97
abstract: A Jewish refugee from the Nazis, he argued that World War I, World War II and the Holocaust were all part of a “second Thirty Years’ War.”

name: Mário Zagallo
headline: Mário Zagallo, Longtime Fixture of Brazilian Soccer, Dies at 92
abstract: The first person to win the World Cup as a player and a coach, he was a link to decades of Brazil’s success and failure on the sport’s biggest stage.

name: Klee Benally
headline: Klee Benally, Navajo Activist and Artist, Dies at 48
abstract: He helped found a punk-rock band when he was 14. That led to a long career as an advocate for Native American and environmental causes.

name: Norby Walters
headline: Norby Walters, 91, Dies; Music and Sports Agent Who Ran Afoul of the Law
abstract: He ran a highly successful booking agency, but his secret contacts with college athletes led to convictions (later reversed) for racketeering and fraud.

name: Joan Acocella
profession: Dance Critic for The New Yorker
headline: Joan Acocella, Dance Critic for The New Yorker, Dies at 78
abstract: She wrote about the leading figures in ballet and modern dance for more than 40 years. One of her books was about the brash choreographer Mark Morris.

name: Franz Beckenbauer
headline: Franz Beckenbauer, ‘Der Kaiser’ of World Soccer, Dies at 78
abstract: In West Germany, he revolutionized his central defense position and was one of only three people to win the World Cup as a player and a coach.

name: Alexis Smith
profession: Artist With Eclectic Eye on American Culture
headline: Alexis Smith, Artist With Eclectic Eye on American Culture, Dies at 74
abstract: She used installations, assemblage and three-dimensional murals in her commentary on Hollywood, fame and more. “I’ve made stuff out of everything,” she said.

name: Tony Fortuna
headline: Tony Fortuna, Restaurateur With a Congenial Flair, Dies at 76
abstract: He turned running a dining room into a fine art at each of his restaurants over a 40-year career, most notably TBar on the Upper East Side.

name: Herman Raucher
profession: Screenwriter Best Known for Summer of 42
headline: Herman Raucher, Screenwriter Best Known for ‘Summer of ’42,’ Dies at 95
abstract: His screenplay, based on his own youthful experience, was nominated for an Oscar. His other films included “Sweet November,” based on his own unproduced play.

name: Amalija Knavs
profession: Mother of Former First Lady Melania Trump
headline: Amalija Knavs, Mother of Former First Lady Melania Trump, Dies at 78
abstract: A patternmaker from Slovenia, she and her husband became naturalized U.S. citizens with the help of their daughter and then a focal point in the debate around Donald Trump’s immigration policies.

name: E. Leo Milonas
profession: Lion and a Defender of New York Courts
headline: E. Leo Milonas, 87, a Lion and a Defender of New York Courts, Dies
abstract: As an administrator of courts in New York State and New York City, he championed judicial independence and defendants’ rights and was unafraid to speak out.

name: Alice Parker
headline: Alice Parker, Composer Who Heard Music in Poetry, Dies at 98
abstract: A master of American choral music, she wrote arrangements of hymns, folk songs and spirituals used in concert halls and churches countrywide.

name: Norma Barzman
headline: Norma Barzman, Blacklisted Screenwriter, Dies at 103
abstract: After she and her husband, a fellow writer, saw work in Hollywood dry up during the Red Scare, they continued their careers in self-exile overseas.

name: Marisa Pavan
profession: Oscar Nominee for The Rose Tattoo
headline: Marisa Pavan, Oscar Nominee for ‘The Rose Tattoo,’ Dies at 91
abstract: The twin sister of the Italian ingénue Pier Angeli, she attempted to avoid the pitfalls of fame that befell her sister’s career.

name: Bud Harrelson
headline: Bud Harrelson, Shortstop for ‘Miracle Mets’ of 1969, Dies at 79
abstract: An outstanding fielder, he helped the team win the World Series that year and reach another in 1973. He stayed with the Mets as a coach and, briefly, manager.

name: Elmore Nickleberry
headline: Elmore Nickleberry, 92, Sanitation Worker in ’68 Memphis Strike, Dies
abstract: He was one of the last survivors of a historic walkout that demanded respect and a living wage and that drew Martin Luther King to their cause.

name: Edward Jay Epstein
headline: Edward Jay Epstein, Author and Stubborn Skeptic, Dies at 88
abstract: He questioned the findings of the Warren Commission, called Edward Snowden a prized Russian asset and exposed the diamond industry’s economic impact.

name: Alice Mason
profession: Real Estate Fixer and Hostess to the Elite
headline: Alice Mason, Real Estate Fixer and Hostess to the Elite, Dies at 100
abstract: She was the queen of Manhattan real estate when power brokers jockeyed for places in stately co-op buildings. Her dinners for them made the gossip columns.

name: Lynn Yamada Davis
headline: Lynn Yamada Davis, Whose Cooking TikToks Delighted Millions, Dies at 67
abstract: Older than most social media stars, she attracted a large following with her Cooking With Lynja videos, which were both wholesome and zany.

name: Russell Hamler
profession: Last of World War IIs Merrills Marauders
headline: Russell Hamler, Last of World War II’s Merrill’s Marauders, Dies at 99
abstract: The foot soldiers marched and fought through harsh mountainous jungle on a mission to seize a Japanese-held airfield. Dozens did not survive.

name: Red Paden
headline: Red Paden, Juke Joint ‘King’ Who Kept the Blues Alive, Dies at 67
abstract: His unassuming Mississippi Delta nightspot is one of the last of its kind, giving blues musicians a welcoming venue and lately drawing visitors from around the world.

name: Reggie Wells
profession: Makeup Artist for Oprah Winfrey and Other Black Stars
headline: Reggie Wells, 76, Dies; Makeup Artist for Oprah Winfrey and Other Black Stars
abstract: At a time when cosmetic brands did not cater to Black women, Mr. Wells found a niche working with Black stars and models who had struggled to find makeup options for their skin tones.

name: Robert Andrew Parker
headline: Robert Andrew Parker, 96, Dies; Prolific Magazine and Book Illustrator
abstract: His loose style of watercolor painting brought him work for nearly 70 years. He also created about 100 fake van Goghs for the biographical film “Lust for Life.”

name: Howard Weaver
profession: Helped an Alaska Newspaper Win 3 Pulitzers
headline: Howard Weaver, Who Helped an Alaska Newspaper Win 3 Pulitzers, Dies at 73
abstract: The Anchorage Daily News was the smallest newspaper and the first in the state to earn the medal for public service in 1976. It then won two more.

name: Phill Niblock
profession: Dedicated Avant-Gardist of Music and Film
headline: Phill Niblock, Dedicated Avant-Gardist of Music and Film, Dies at 90
abstract: Making music with no melody or rhythm and films with no plot, he became a darling of New York’s experimental underground.

name: Jay Clayton
profession: Vocal Innovator in Jazz and Beyond
headline: Jay Clayton, Vocal Innovator in Jazz and Beyond, Is Dead at 82
abstract: She sparred with avant-garde instrumentalists and used electronics to alter and extend her vocal palette. She was also at home in more conventional settings.

name: Leon Wildes
headline: Leon Wildes, 90, Immigration Lawyer Who Defended John Lennon, Dies
abstract: Battling the government for more than three years, he was able to prove that the Nixon White House was trying to deport the former Beatle for political reasons.

name: Peter Crombie
headline: Peter Crombie, a Menacing Presence on ‘Seinfeld,’ Dies at 71
abstract: He had an impressive list of acting credits. But he was probably best known for playing “Crazy” Joe Davola on five episodes of the hit sitcom.

name: Joyce Randolph
headline: Joyce Randolph, Last of the ‘Honeymooners,’ Is Dead at 99
abstract: She played Trixie Norton in the classic sitcom and was the last survivor of a cast of four that dominated Saturday night TV in the 1950s.

name: Roy Calne
headline: Roy Calne, Pioneering British Organ-Transplant Surgeon, Dies at 93
abstract: His innovations in the use of drugs to prevent organ rejection helped bring a remarkable increase in the one-year survival rate.

name: Norm Snead
profession: Skillful Loser as an N.F.L. Quarterback
headline: Norm Snead, Skillful Loser as an N.F.L. Quarterback, Is Dead at 84
abstract: A four-time Pro Bowl selection, he spent seven years with the Philadelphia Eagles, where his record was better than the team’s.

name: Zvi Zamir
profession: Israeli Spy Chief in a Critical Period
headline: Zvi Zamir, Israeli Spy Chief in a Critical Period, Dies at 98
abstract: He led the Mossad’s response to the massacre of 11 Israelis at the 1972 Olympics. A year later, he learned that Egypt and Syria were about to attack Israel.

name: Brian Barczyk
profession: Reptile Evangelist on YouTube and TV
headline: Brian Barczyk, a Reptile Evangelist on YouTube and TV, Dies at 54
abstract: A snake breeder, Mr. Barczyk amassed an online following in the millions with cheerful videos that captured his passion for snakes, lizards and other types of reptiles.

name: Tom Shales
profession: TV Critic Both Respected and Feared
headline: Tom Shales, TV Critic Both Respected and Feared, Dies at 79
abstract: An incisively funny Washington Post columnist, he earned nicknames like Terrible Tom and had the clout to make or break shows.

name: Claire M. Fagin
profession: Powerful Advocate for Nurses and Nursing
headline: Claire M. Fagin, Powerful Advocate for Nurses and Nursing, Dies at 97
abstract: “It is really hard,” a colleague said, “to identify anyone who has had a larger impact on nursing than Claire.”

name: Sarah Stackhouse
headline: Sarah Stackhouse, Star Interpreter of José Limón, Dies at 87
abstract: Her virtuosic dance technique, natural charisma and compelling acting perfectly suited Mr. Limón’s flowing movement style and abstract narrative works.

name: Joseph Zadroga
headline: Joseph Zadroga, Who Championed 9/11 Emergency Workers, Dies at 76
abstract: After the death of his son, a police detective, was linked to toxins at the World Trade Center site, he helped win federal benefits for other emergency responders.

name: Peter Schickele
profession: Composer and Gleeful Sire of P.D.Q. Bach
headline: Peter Schickele, Composer and Gleeful Sire of P.D.Q. Bach, Dies at 88
abstract: He wrote more than 100 symphonic, choral, solo instrumental and chamber works. But he was better known, and celebrated, as a musical parodist. Who can forget the “Concerto for Horn and Hardart”?

name: Nancy E. Adler
headline: Nancy E. Adler, Who Linked Wealth to Health, Dies at 77
abstract: She documented the powerful role that education, income and self-perceived social status play in a person’s health and longevity.

name: Joseph Esposito
headline: Joseph Esposito, Longtime N.Y.P.D. Chief, Is Dead at 73
abstract: For more than 12 years, he oversaw the city’s response to some of its most challenging disasters. He later led New York’s emergency management agency.

name: Annie Nightingale
headline: Annie Nightingale, Pathbreaking British D.J., Is Dead at 83
abstract: She was initially told there was no room for her on BBC Radio 1 because a woman’s voice lacked the authority of a man’s. Once she was on the air, she stayed there for 53 years.

name: Jack Burke Jr.
profession: Won 2 Major Golf Titles in a Season
headline: Jack Burke Jr., Who Won 2 Major Golf Titles in a Season, Dies at 100
abstract: A top professional in the postwar years, he won the Masters and the P.G.A. championships in 1956. At his death he was the oldest living champion of both.

name: Menachem Daum
headline: Menachem Daum, 77, Filmmaker Who Explored the World of Hasidim, Dies
abstract: His acclaimed documentary “A Life Apart” presented a complex portrait of a religious group usually depicted as somber and impenetrable.

name: Beatrix Potter
profession: Author of The Tale of Peter Rabbit
headline: Overlooked No More: Beatrix Potter, Author of ‘The Tale of Peter Rabbit’
abstract: She created one of the world’s best-known characters for children, and fought to have the book published, but she never sought celebrity status.

name: Tanya Berezin
headline: Tanya Berezin, Behind-the-Scenes Off Broadway Force, Is Dead at 82
abstract: At the Circle Repertory Company, where she said her goal was to “confuse people,” she nurtured a new generation of writers and actors in the 1980s and ’90s.

name: Lev Rubinstein
profession: Russian Poet and a Critic of Putin
headline: Lev Rubinstein, Russian Poet and a Critic of Putin, Is Dead at 76
abstract: He helped found an avant-garde movement fusing art and prose and was outspoken against the invasion of Ukraine. He died after he was hit by a car in Moscow.

name: Bill Iffrig
profession: Runner in Iconic Boston Marathon Bombing Photo
headline: Bill Iffrig, Runner in Iconic Boston Marathon Bombing Photo, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Iffrig had run in more than 50 marathons but gained national attention in 2013 for being photographed after the blast knocked him to the ground.

name: Robert Whitman
headline: Robert Whitman, Cutting-Edge Performance Artist, Dies at 88
abstract: “I wanted something physical, almost painful, passionate,” he said of his first major work, “American Moon,” presented in 1960. That was just the beginning.

name: Brent Sikkema
headline: Brent Sikkema, Influential New York Gallerist, Dies at 75
abstract: As the founder of the Sikkema Jenkins gallery, he discovered, guided, exhibited and sold a diverse and international rotation of distinguished artists.

name: Berish Strauch
headline: Berish Strauch, Path Breaker in Reconstructive Surgery, Dies at 90
abstract: He developed a wide variety of procedures and devices to reattach or replace vital body parts, including the first inflatable prosthetic penis.

name: Marie Irvine
headline: Marie Irvine, Makeup Artist to Marilyn Monroe, Dies at 99
abstract: Late in Ms. Monroe’s life, Ms. Irvine was her go-to makeup artist in New York City. Earlier this month, she became a TikTok sensation.

name: David Gail
headline: David Gail of ‘Beverly Hills, 90210’ Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Gail was known for his role as Stuart Carson on Season 4 of “Beverly Hills, 90210” and had dozens of other television show credits in the 1990s.

name: Mary Weiss
headline: Mary Weiss, Who Sang ‘Leader of the Pack,’ Is Dead at 75
abstract: As the lead singer of the Shangri-Las, she conveyed passion, pathos and toughness — and reached the Top 40 six times while still in her teens.

name: Ewa Podles
headline: Ewa Podles, a Rare Contralto With Sweeping Range, Dies at 71
abstract: With her molten chest voice and commanding presence, Ms. Podles, a galvanizing Polish opera singer, developed a cult following.

name: Norman Jewison
profession: Directed In the Heat of the Night and Moonstruck
headline: Norman Jewison, 97, Dies; Directed ‘In the Heat of the Night’ and ‘Moonstruck’
abstract: His genre-spanning movies — dramas, comedies and musicals, like “Fiddler on the Roof” — were magnets for Oscar nods, but he was best known for socially conscious films.

name: Joseph Hayden
headline: Joseph Hayden, Who Fought for Ex-Felons’ Voting Rights, Dies at 82
abstract: A former lieutenant in a Harlem drug gang, he earned two academic degrees in prison and became an advocate for parolees and convicts.

name: Ruth Ashton Taylor
headline: Ruth Ashton Taylor, Early Radio and TV Newswoman, Dies at 101
abstract: In the late 1940s, she was the only woman working on radio documentaries for CBS’s Edward R. Murrow. In Los Angeles, she was a pioneering newscaster and anchor.

name: Dexter Scott King
profession: Younger Son of Martin Luther King Jr
headline: Dexter Scott King, Younger Son of Martin Luther King Jr., Dies at 62
abstract: As the longtime chairman of the King Center, he worked closely — and clashed at times — with his siblings over control of their father’s legacy.

name: Arno A. Penzias
profession: Nobel Physicist Confirmed Big Bang Theory
headline: Arno A. Penzias, 90, Dies; Nobel Physicist Confirmed Big Bang Theory
abstract: His 1964 discovery with Robert W. Wilson settled a debate over the origin and evolution of the universe.

name: Shih Ming-teh
profession: Defiant Activist for a Democratic Taiwan
headline: Shih Ming-teh, Defiant Activist for a Democratic Taiwan, Dies at 83
abstract: He spent 25 years in prison for campaigning for Taiwan’s independence and democratization. After his release, he led protests to oust one its presidents.

name: Frank Farian
headline: Frank Farian, the Man Behind Milli Vanilli, Is Dead at 82
abstract: He had worldwide success with the disco group Boney M. He was better known for a duo that had hit records but, it turned out, only pretended to sing.

name: Charles Osgood
profession: Lyrical Newscaster on Radio and TV
headline: Charles Osgood, Lyrical Newscaster on Radio and TV, Dies at 91
abstract: A familiar face on television as the host of “CBS Sunday Morning” from 1994 to 2016, he was also known for his “Osgood File” segments on CBS Radio, often delivered with humor and a rhyme.

name: Howard Golden
headline: Howard Golden, Who Led, and Defended, Brooklyn, Dies at 98
abstract: Before it staged a revival, he was the borough’s president and Democratic leader for a quarter-century, sometimes clashing with mayors.

name: Dan Wagoner
headline: Dan Wagoner, Acclaimed Modern Dancer, Is Dead at 91
abstract: He worked with the Martha Graham and Paul Taylor troupes and then created his own group, Dan Wagoner and Dancers.

name: Naomi Feil
profession: Promoted Empathy as a Response to Dementia
headline: Naomi Feil, Who Promoted Empathy as a Response to Dementia, Dies at 91
abstract: She trained caregivers to “validate” the delusions of older people with dementia, rather than try to wrest them into the real world.

name: Carl Andre
headline: Carl Andre, 88, Austerely Minimalist Sculptor, Is Dead
abstract: He worked with elemental metals, granite, wood and brick in sculpture “free of human association.” His career was marred by accusations that he had a role in his wife’s fatal plunge.

name: Melanie
headline: Melanie, Singer Who Made a Solo Splash at Woodstock, Dies at 76
abstract: Just 22 when she charmed the festival crowd, she went on to enjoy success with songs like “Lay Down (Candles in the Rain)” and “Brand New Key.”

name: He
headline: He Died in a Tragic Accident. Why Did the Internet Say He Was Murdered?
abstract: Within a day of the death of Matthew Sachman, 19, on New York City subway tracks, so-called obituary pirates had flooded search results with false information.

name: John Pilger
profession: Journalist and Filmmaker on Human Rights Abuses
headline: John Pilger, 84, Dies; Journalist and Filmmaker on Human Rights Abuses
abstract: A prolific documentarian and writer who took sides, he was best known for a film about the Khmer Rouge’s genocide in Cambodia in the 1970s.

name: Bill Hayes
profession: Enduring Soap Star With a Davy Crockett Hit
headline: Bill Hayes, Enduring Soap Star With a ‘Davy Crockett’ Hit, Is Dead at 98
abstract: He logged more than 2,000 episodes on “Days of Our Lives” and rode the Crockett craze to a hit single in 1955.

name: Fred Chappell
profession: Admired but Unsung Writer of the South
headline: Fred Chappell, Admired but Unsung Writer of the South, Dies at 87
abstract: He wrote lyrical poetry and novels about life in North Carolina’s Appalachian Piedmont and was considered the South’s “premier contemporary person of letters.”

name: Edward E. Crutchfield
headline: Edward E. Crutchfield, 82, Dies; Banker’s Deals Reshaped the Industry
abstract: He built a small Southern bank into a regional powerhouse, helping to turn Charlotte, N.C., into a national financial hub.

name: Herbert Coward
headline: Herbert Coward, Actor Who Played Toothless Man in ‘Deliverance,’ Dies at 85
abstract: The actor was killed in a motor vehicle accident in North Carolina, the authorities said.

name: Jesse Jane
headline: Jesse Jane, Pornographic Film Star, Dies at 43
abstract: She starred in the highest-budget series in pornographic film history. She was also seen in some mainstream productions.

name: Jo-El Sonnier
profession: Sparked a Revival of Cajun Music
headline: Jo-El Sonnier, Who Sparked a Revival of Cajun Music, Dies at 77
abstract: An accordion virtuoso and a gifted vocalist, he scored country hits in the 1980s by putting a Cajun spin on songs like Richard Thompson’s “Tear-Stained Letter.”

name: Marc Jaffe
headline: Marc Jaffe, Publisher of Paperback Hits, Is Dead at 102
abstract: He oversaw a boom in the format beginning in the 1960s, turning out best sellers like “Jaws,” “The Exorcist” and “The Catcher in the Rye.”

name: Jon Franklin
headline: Jon Franklin, Pioneering Apostle of Literary Journalism, Dies at 82
abstract: He won two Pulitzer Prizes by transforming accounts of doctors at work into in-depth, narrative articles that read like dramatic short stories.

name: David J. Skal
headline: David J. Skal, Scholar Who Took Horror Seriously, Dies at 71
abstract: In books like “The Monster Show” and “Screams of Reason,” he examined the cultural significance of movies meant to scare the bejesus out of people.

name: Harry Connick Sr.
profession: New Orleans D.A. Criticized for Overreach
headline: Harry Connick Sr., New Orleans D.A. Criticized for Overreach, Dies at 97
abstract: The city’s top prosecutor from 1973 to 2003, he led an office that sent hundreds of Black men to prison and became known for its record of wrongful convictions.

name: Charles Fried
headline: Charles Fried, Legal Scholar Who Broke With Conservatives, Dies at 88
abstract: As solicitor general under Reagan, he argued against abortion rights and affirmative action. But he came to see the current Supreme Court as “reactionary, not conservative.”

name: Marlena Shaw
headline: Marlena Shaw, Venerable Nightclub Chanteuse, Dies at 84
abstract: She sang jazz (with Count Basie, among others) and later funk and disco, frequently in intimate venues, where she regaled audiences with tales of old love affairs.

name: N. Scott Momaday
headline: N. Scott Momaday, Pulitzer-Winning Native American Novelist, Dies at 89
abstract: The success of his novel “House Made of Dawn,” the first work by a Native American to win a Pulitzer, inspired a wave of Native literature.

name: Vera Klement
headline: Vera Klement, Painter Who Saw Both Beauty and Evil, Dies at 93
abstract: A Holocaust survivor, she once said that she sought in her art to “recognize the nightmare but confirm rather than deny human life.”

name: Jimy Williams
profession: A.L. Manager of the Year in Boston in 99
headline: Jimy Williams, A.L. Manager of the Year in Boston in ’99, Dies at 80
abstract: He led the Red Sox into the playoffs twice, had managing stints in Toronto and Houston, and won more than 900 games as a dugout skipper.

name: Khaled Nezzar
profession: General at Center of Algerias Bloodshed
headline: Khaled Nezzar, General at Center of Algeria’s Bloodshed, Dies at 86
abstract: In the 1990s, he oversaw troops that committed a host of atrocities against equally brutal Islamist rebels in what became known as the Black Decade.

name: Chita Rivera
profession: Electrifying Star of Broadway and Beyond
headline: Chita Rivera, Electrifying Star of Broadway and Beyond, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Appearing in scores of stage productions, she dazzled audiences for nearly six decades, most memorably starring as Anita in “West Side Story” and Velma Kelly in “Chicago.”

name: Letha Dawson Scanzoni
headline: Letha Dawson Scanzoni, Pioneer of Evangelical Feminism, Dies at 88
abstract: In books like “All We’re Meant to Be” and “Is the Homosexual My Neighbor?” she used the Bible to challenge beliefs that women were inferior to men and that homosexuality was a sin.

name: Jean Carnahan
profession: First Woman to Represent Missouri in U.S. Senate
headline: Jean Carnahan, 90, First Woman to Represent Missouri in U.S. Senate, Dies
abstract: Ms. Carnahan was appointed to the seat after her husband was posthumously elected to it just weeks after he was killed in a plane crash in 2000.

name: Melinda Wilson
profession: Helped Brian Wilson Through Mental Illness
headline: Melinda Wilson, 77,Who Helped Brian Wilson Through Mental Illness, Dies
abstract: Ms. Wilson’s relationship with her husband, a co-founder of the Beach Boys, was portrayed in the 2014 film “Love & Mercy.”

name: Jack Jennings
headline: Jack Jennings, P.O.W. Who Helped Build Burma Railway, Dies at 104
abstract: He was captured by the Japanese in Singapore and was one of thousands of prisoners whose hardships were the basis for the film “The Bridge on the River Kwai.”

name: Lawrence Langer
headline: Lawrence Langer, Unblinking Scholar of Holocaust Literature, Dies at 94
abstract: He insisted that there were no morals to be found in the murder of six million Jews, nor was language itself capable of fully describing it.

name: Toni Stern
headline: Toni Stern, Who Wrote Songs With Carole King, Dies at 79
abstract: A sunny California poet, she provided the words to songs on “Tapestry” and other albums, including the enduring hit “It’s Too Late.”

name: Jennell Jaquays
headline: Jennell Jaquays, 67, Dies; Unlocked Fantasy Dungeons for Gamers
abstract: She created scenarios with myriad paths for Dungeons & Dragons, levels for video games like Quake II, and art that invited novices to try role-playing games.

name: Adele Springsteen
headline: Adele Springsteen, Rock Star’s Mother, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Bruce Springsteen has long said that his mother was among his greatest influences and credited her with encouraging his musical ambitions.

name: Sandra Milo
profession: Had Star Turns in Fellini Films
headline: Sandra Milo, 90, Who Had Star Turns in Fellini Films, Dies
abstract: She was called Fellini’s muse. She claimed she was his lover. In a long career, she was best known for her performances in his movies “8 ½” and “Juliet of the Spirits.”

name: Albert K. Butzel
profession: Lawyer and Protector of the Hudson
headline: Albert K. Butzel, Lawyer and Protector of the Hudson, Dies at 85
abstract: He led grass-roots lawsuits that defeated plans for Westway on Manhattan’s waterfront and a Storm King power plant. His legacy also includes the city’s Hudson River Park.

name: Henry Heard
profession: Tap Dancer and Advocate for People with Disabilities
headline: Overlooked No More: Henry Heard, Tap Dancer and Advocate for People with Disabilities
abstract: With one arm and one leg, he upended assumptions that disabled people could not lead fulfilling lives, and his artistry had audiences clamoring for more.

name: Don Murray
headline: Don Murray, a Star in Films That Took on Social Issues, Dies at 94
abstract: An Oscar-nominated role opposite Marilyn Monroe in “Bus Stop” led to a long career in film and TV and onstage, in productions that grappled with race, drugs, homosexuality and more.

name: Carl Weathers
profession: Played Apollo Creed in Rocky Movies
headline: Carl Weathers, Who Played Apollo Creed in ‘Rocky’ Movies, Dies at 76
abstract: A former pro linebacker, he had a long acting career that reached beyond the boxing ring, appearing in action films, comedies and TV dramas and earning an Emmy nomination.

name: Alice Mackler
headline: Alice Mackler, Sculptor Discovered in Her 80s, Dies at 92
abstract: Originally a painter, she worked low-level office jobs for most of her life. Later, she started making strange clay figures, and found fame at 81.

name: Roger Donlon
profession: Vietnam Wars First Medal of Honor Recipient
headline: Roger Donlon, Vietnam War’s First Medal of Honor Recipient, Dies at 89
abstract: Despite being wounded multiple times, he led the defense of a jungle outpost against a Vietcong assault, inspiring his smaller force to “superhuman effort.”

name: Joe Madison
profession: Radio Host and Civil Rights Activist
headline: Joe Madison, Radio Host and Civil Rights Activist, Dies at 74
abstract: On the air, he urged politically powerful guests to take action on human rights issues. Outside the studio, he joined protests, including a hunger strike in 2021.

name: Wayne Kramer
headline: Wayne Kramer, Guitarist With the Incendiary MC5, Is Dead at 75
abstract: He was half of the twin-guitar attack that drove the influential Detroit band’s  live performances and  helped set the stage for punk rock.

name: Matisyahu Salomon
headline: Matisyahu Salomon, 86, Dies; Rabbi Warned of Internet’s Dangers
abstract: As a supervisor at America’s largest yeshiva, he wielded influence across the world of ultra-Orthodox Jews. He feared that the internet jeopardized the observance of Jewish customs.

name: Hage Geingob
headline: Hage Geingob, Namibia’s President, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Geingob had also been Namibia’s first prime minister after the country gained independence from South Africa in 1990.

name: Michael Watford
headline: Michael Watford, a Minister of Gospel House Music, Dies at 64
abstract: His signature hit, “So Into You,” was omnipresent in 1994 — the rare record “you heard at every club,” one D.J. said. But his time at the top was brief.

name: Robie Harris
headline: Robie Harris, Often-Banned Children’s Author, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Her children’s books on matters of sex and sexuality — notably “It’s Perfectly Normal” — became fodder for the culture wars.

name: Hinton Battle
headline: Hinton Battle, Three-Time Tony Winner in Musicals, Dies at 67
abstract: He won awards for his roles in “Sophisticated Ladies,” “The Tap Dance Kid” and “Miss Saigon” — the most ever in the category of best featured actor in a musical.

name: Inger McCabe Elliott
headline: Inger McCabe Elliott, Who Famously Became Con Man’s Victim, Dies at 90
abstract: She was a successful designer. But she was probably best known for being duped in a scheme that inspired the play “Six Degrees of Separation.”

name: Bob Beckwith
headline: Bob Beckwith, Firefighter Who Stood With Bush After 9/11, Dies at 91
abstract: Photographs showing him with the president atop a rubble-strewn  fire truck came to represent America’s fortitude in the aftermath of the attack.

name: Toby Keith
headline: Toby Keith, Larger-Than-Life Country Music Star, Dies at 62
abstract: He cultivated an in-your-face persona with hits like “Who’s Your Daddy?” and “Courtesy of the Red, White and Blue.” He announced in 2022 that he had cancer.

name: Clyde Taylor
headline: Clyde Taylor, Literary Scholar Who Elevated Black Cinema, Dies at 92
abstract: A leading figure in the field of Black studies in the 1970s, he identified work by Black filmmakers as worthy of serious intellectual attention.

name: Aston Barrett
profession: Bass-Playing Force With Bob Marley and Wailers
headline: Aston Barrett, 77, Bass-Playing Force With Bob Marley and Wailers, Dies
abstract: Known by his nickname, Family Man, he was the group’s musical director, crafting the hypnotic rhythms and melodies that elevated reggae to global acclaim.

name: Mojo Nixon
headline: Mojo Nixon, Who Mixed Roots and Punk Rock, Dies at 66
abstract: A self-described voice of “the doomed, the damned, the weird,” he was known for satirical songs like “Elvis Is Everywhere” and “Destroy All Lawyers.”

name: Dick Waterman
profession: Promoter and Photographer of the Blues
headline: Dick Waterman, Promoter and Photographer of the Blues, Dies at 88
abstract: A “crackpot eccentric Yankee” from Massachusetts, he revived the careers of long-forgotten Southern artists during the blues boom of the 1960s.

name: Si Spiegel
headline: Si Spiegel, War Hero Who Modernized Christmas Trees, Dies at 99
abstract: The son of Jewish immigrants, he was a pilot in World War II who later created patents to mass-produce artificial conifers.

name: David Soukup
profession: Advocate for Abused and Neglected Children
headline: David Soukup, Advocate for Abused and Neglected Children, Dies at 90
abstract: While serving as a judge in Seattle, he was inspired to start an organization to help children who did not have unbiased advocates in court proceedings.

name: Walter Shawlee
headline: Walter Shawlee, the Sovereign of Slide Rules, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Used by engineers for centuries, they were displaced by pocket calculators and all but forgotten until Mr. Shawlee created a subculture of obsessives and cornered the market.

name: Riad al-Turk
headline: Riad al-Turk, the ‘Mandela of Syria,’ Dies in Exile at 93
abstract: Imprisoned four times, he spent almost 20 years in Syria’s prisons, nearly 18 in solitary confinement, for speaking out against the Assad regimes. He died in France.

name: Seiji Ozawa
headline: Seiji Ozawa, a Captivating, Transformative Conductor, Dies at 88
abstract: He led the Boston Symphony Orchestra for 29 years, toured widely and helped dispel prejudices about East Asian classical musicians.

name: Robert Badinter
profession: Won Fight to End Death Penalty in France
headline: Robert Badinter Dies at 95; Won Fight to End Death Penalty in France
abstract: He spent decades as an esteemed defense lawyer but was best known as the justice minister who enacted a 1981 law abolishing capital punishment.

name: David Kahn
profession: Leading Historian of Codes and Code Breaking
headline: David Kahn, Leading Historian of Codes and Code Breaking, Dies at 93
abstract: His 1967 book, “The Codebreakers,” introduced the world to cryptology and inspired the emergence of private-sector encrypted communication.

name: Richard Gambino
headline: Richard Gambino, 84, Dies; Fought Discrimination Against Italian Americans
abstract: He directed the Italian American studies program at Queens College — the first of its type in American academia — and wrote about his ethnic group in “Blood of My Blood.”

name: Lance Larson
profession: Lost a Disputed Olympic Swim Race
headline: Lance Larson, Who Lost a Disputed Olympic Swim Race, Dies at 83
abstract: He had the fastest time in the 100-meter freestyle final. But after a corps of judges couldn’t choose a winner, the chief judge declared one. It wasn’t Larson.

name: Brooke Ellison
headline: Brooke Ellison, Prominent Disability Rights Advocate, Is Dead at 45
abstract: One of the first quadriplegic Harvard graduates, she became an author, professor and powerful voice for disabled people.

name: John Bruton
profession: Negotiated for Peace as Irish Prime Minister
headline: John Bruton Dies at 76; Negotiated for Peace as Irish Prime Minister
abstract: He made strides to end the sectarian violence that plagued Northern Ireland through the 1990s by collaborating with both Britain and the Irish Republican Army.

name: Brian McConnachie
headline: Brian McConnachie, Humor Writer ‘From Another Planet,’ Dies at 81
abstract: A contributor to National Lampoon, “Saturday Night Live” and “SCTV,” he had a patrician presence that belied a whimsical and sometimes anarchic wit.

name: Steve Ostrow
headline: Steve Ostrow, Manhattan Bathhouse Impresario, Dies at 91
abstract: The Continental Baths, which he opened in 1968, became a pivot point in Manhattan’s gay history and a launchpad for a young Bette Midler.

name: Ellen Gilchrist
profession: Writer With an Eye on the Souths Foibles
headline: Ellen Gilchrist, Writer With an Eye on the South’s Foibles, Dies at 88
abstract: In her novels and story collections, she took a sharp, lightly ironic look at the class from which she came, the Southern upper bourgeoisie.

name: Cecilia Gentili
headline: Cecilia Gentili, Transgender Activist, Performer and Author, Dies at 52
abstract: Once an undocumented sex worker and addict, she was a powerful advocate for marginalized people, and an irresistible story teller.

name: Bob Edwards
profession: Longtime Host of NPRs Morning Edition
headline: Bob Edwards, Longtime Host of NPR’s ‘Morning Edition,’ Dies at 76
abstract: He was “the voice we woke up to” for a quarter century, delivering news and interviews in a rich baritone that reached millions of listeners.

name: Kelvin Kiptum
headline: Kelvin Kiptum, Marathon World Record-Holder, Is Dead at 24
abstract: Kiptum, who came tantalizingly close last year to breaching the mythical two-hour barrier in the marathon, was killed in a car accident in Kenya.

name: David Bouley
headline: David Bouley, Influential New York Chef, Dies at 70
abstract: At restaurants like Montrachet and Bouley, he channeled French nouvelle cuisine to create the New American style.

name: Larry Taylor
profession: Vietnam War Pilot Lauded for Daring Rescue
headline: Larry Taylor, Vietnam War Pilot Lauded for Daring Rescue, Dies at 81
abstract: His evacuation of four besieged U.S. Army Rangers was belatedly recognized last September with the Medal of Honor.

name: Dries van Agt
headline: Dries van Agt, Former Dutch Prime Minister, Dies at 93
abstract: As justice minister he weathered a hijacking crisis and later pushed to resolve the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. He and his wife died in a joint act of euthanasia.

name: William Post
headline: William Post, Who Helped Create Pop-Tarts, Dies at 96
abstract: A bakery manager in Michigan, he worked with Kellogg’s to create the snack in 1964. It became a timeless American classic.

name: Joel Belz
headline: Joel Belz, Trailblazer in Christian Journalism, Is Dead at 82
abstract: Inspired by Time, he founded World magazine, covering politics, the arts and other subjects from a “God’s-eye” view.

name: Angela Chao
headline: Angela Chao, C.E.O. of Family’s Shipping Company, Is Dead at 50
abstract: Ms. Chao, whose sister Elaine Chao was President Trump’s secretary of transportation, led Foremost Group, operator of a global fleet of freighters. She died in a car crash.

name: Wilhelmenia Wiggins Fernandez
headline: Wilhelmenia Wiggins Fernandez, the Diva of ‘Diva,’ Dies at 75
abstract: A soprano who rose from South Philadelphia to the opera houses of Europe, she was memorably seen and heard in a 1981 film considered a paragon of cinematic style.

name: Don Catlin
headline: Don Catlin, Who Ran an Elite Antidoping Laboratory, Dies at 85
abstract: A medical doctor and an expert in pharmacology, he ran drug testing for sports leagues and the Olympics, unlocking the chemical codes for previously undetectable designer steroids.

name: Frank Kitson
profession: Helped Shape the Conflict in Northern Ireland
headline: Frank Kitson, 97, Dies; Helped Shape the Conflict in Northern Ireland
abstract: A British general whose specialty was counterinsurgency, he was accused of using unduly hard-edge tactics against Irish Republican forces during the era known as the Troubles.

name: Aleksei Navalny
headline: Aleksei Navalny, Russian Opposition Leader, Dies in Prison at 47
abstract: The Kremlin’s fiercest critic, whose work brought arrests, attacks and a near-fatal poisoning in 2020, had spent months in isolation.

name: Don Gullett
profession: Ace for the Big Red Machine
headline: Don Gullett, Ace for the Big Red Machine, Dies at 73
abstract: With a fastball that recalled his idol, Sandy Koufax, he helped lead the Cincinnati Reds and then the New York Yankees to World Series titles in the 1970s.

name: Ross Gelbspan
profession: Exposed Roots of Climate Change Deniers
headline: Ross Gelbspan, Who Exposed Roots of Climate Change Deniers, Dies at 84
abstract: A longtime investigative journalist, he wrote books and articles that documented a campaign of disinformation intended to sow doubt about global warming.

name: Charles Sallis
profession: Upended the Teaching of Mississippi History
headline: Charles Sallis, 89, Dies; Upended the Teaching of Mississippi History
abstract: He collaborated on a textbook so unsparing in its review of the state’s grim past that it was barred from schools almost as soon as it appeared.

name: Joe Louis Dudley
headline: Joe Louis Dudley, Pioneering Hair Care Entrepreneur, Dies at 86
abstract: Starting in their kitchen, he and his wife at the time built a thriving company making beauty products for Black consumers. They also founded a string of cosmetology schools.

name: Randy Sparks
profession: Founder of the New Christy Minstrels
headline: Randy Sparks, Founder of the New Christy Minstrels, Dies at 90
abstract: With a keen eye for young talent, he helped boost the careers of Steve Martin, John Denver, Kenny Rogers and many other performers.

name: Alvin Moscow
headline: Alvin Moscow, Shipwreck Chronicler and Prolific Collaborator, Dies at 98
abstract: After writing a best seller about the sinking of the Andrea Doria, he was a co-author with Richard M. Nixon, Patty Hearst, William S. Paley and others.

name: Pierre Toussaint
headline: Overlooked No More: Pierre Toussaint, Philanthropist and Candidate for Sainthood
abstract: He became wealthy working as a hairdresser in New York, then used his funds to free enslaved people, build churches and house orphans of color.

name: Charles V. Hamilton
headline: Charles V. Hamilton, an Apostle of ‘Black Power,’ Dies at 94
abstract: He popularized the term “institutional racism" and, with Stokely Carmichael, wrote a book in 1967 that was seen as a radical manifesto.

name: William Beecher
headline: William Beecher, Who Revealed Secret Cambodia Bombing, Dies at 90
abstract: His New York Times scoop enraged the Nixon White House, which ordered a tap on his phone. He later won a Pulitzer Prize for The Boston Globe.

name: Jules Harlow
headline: Rabbi Jules Harlow, 92, Dies; Helped Redefine Conservative Jewish Prayer
abstract: Rabbi Harlow’s prayer books, including “Siddur Sim Shalom,” became the standards of worship in Conservative synagogues across North America.

name: Damo Suzuki
headline: Damo Suzuki, Singer Who Ignited the Experimental Band Can, Dies at 74
abstract: His free-spirited music ignored genre boundaries. “If you’re a creative person,” he once said, “it’s important to break rules.”

name: Lefty Driesell
profession: Hall of Fame College Basketball Coach
headline: Lefty Driesell, Hall of Fame College Basketball Coach, Dies at 92
abstract: He built Maryland into a national powerhouse and became the first coach to win more than 100 games at each of four major college programs.

name: Monica Hickey
headline: Monica Hickey, Doyenne of Bridal Gowns, Dies at 100
abstract: As the director of salons at Henri Bendel, Bergdorf Goodman and Saks Fifth Avenue, she spent decades outfitting brides-to-be for their grand ceremonies.

name: Ewen MacIntosh
profession: Star of the British Sitcom The Office
headline: Ewen MacIntosh, a Star of the British Sitcom ‘The Office,’ Dies at 50
abstract: He was best known for his portrayal of the lackluster accountant Keith Bishop on Ricky Gervais’s celebrated series.

name: Jimmy Van Eaton
profession: Purveyor of the Sun Records Beat
headline: Jimmy Van Eaton, Purveyor of the Sun Records Beat, Dies at 86
abstract: His drumming lent spontaneity and imagination to the unfettered sound of seminal rock ’n’ roll records by Jerry Lee Lewis and others.

name: Charles Stendig
headline: Charles Stendig Dies at 99; Introduced Fanciful Furniture From Abroad
abstract: For nearly two decades he traveled to factories throughout Europe, sometimes behind the Iron Curtain, to bring modern furniture to Americans.

name: Hydeia Broadbent
headline: Hydeia Broadbent, H.I.V. and AIDS Activist, Dies at 39
abstract: Born with H.I.V. in 1984, she began raising awareness on television when she was 6 years old.

name: Steven Wise
headline: Steven Wise, Champion of Animal Rights, Is Dead at 73
abstract: He filed lawsuits to define chimpanzees as persons and to establish their right to what he called “bodily liberty” over confinement.

name: Niklaus Wirth
headline: Niklaus Wirth, Visionary Software Architect, Dies at 89
abstract: Pascal, the programming language he created in the early days of personal computing, offered a simpler alternative to other languages in use at the time.

name: Robert Macbeth
profession: Founder of Harlems New Lafayette Theater
headline: Robert Macbeth, Founder of Harlem’s New Lafayette Theater, Dies at 89
abstract: He created a vibrant space for actors and playwrights that became a seedbed for the emerging Black Arts Movement of the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Roger Guillemin
headline: Roger Guillemin, 100, Nobel-Winning Scientist Stirred by Rivalries, Dies
abstract: In the race to identify the hormones used to control bodily functions, he battled with his former partner. They later shared the glory.

name: Alfred Grosser
headline: Alfred Grosser, Champion of French-German Reconciliation, Dies at 99
abstract: A German-born Jew who became a French writer and activist, he devoted his life to healing the divide between two historic enemies after the trauma of World War II.

name: Claude Montana
headline: Claude Montana, Fashion Designer Whose Look Defined the ’80s, Dies at 76
abstract: With meticulous tailoring and a taste for leather, he was the architect of the decade’s highly structured and eroticized tough-chic style.

name: Marc Pachter
headline: Marc Pachter, Who Revived National Portrait Gallery, Dies at 80
abstract: He helped raise more than $20 million to keep Gilbert Stuart’s famous painting of George Washington on display in the capital rather than allow it to be auctioned off.

name: Chuck Mawhinney
profession: Deadliest Sniper in Marine Corps History
headline: Chuck Mawhinney, 74, Dies; Deadliest Sniper in Marine Corps History
abstract: He put the experience behind him after he returned from the Vietnam War. But fame finally caught up to him in the 1990s.

name: Steve Paxton
profession: Found Avant-Garde Dance in the Everyday
headline: Steve Paxton, Who Found Avant-Garde Dance in the Everyday, Dies at 85
abstract: With Judson Dance Theater and as the founder of contact improvisation, he expanded the possibilities of what dance could be, developing works around basic tasks like walking.

name: Henry Rono
headline: Henry Rono, Record-Breaking Distance Runner From Kenya, Dies at 72
abstract: Twice denied Olympic glory by his nation’s boycotts of the Games, he wrote himself into track history in 1978 by breaking four records in just 81 days.

name: Zong Qinghou
headline: Zong Qinghou, Beverage Tycoon in China, Dies at 79
abstract: A bitter but successful battle with Danone of France for control of a joint venture made him the richest person in China for a time.

name: Jacob Rothschild
headline: Jacob Rothschild, Banker Who Broke From His Fabled Family, Dies at 87
abstract: The fourth Baron Rothschild, he left the family banking dynasty to start his own company, becoming a powerful financier, patron of the arts and philanthropist.

name: Joan Holden
headline: Joan Holden, 85, Playwright Who Skewered Rich and Powerful, Dies
abstract: As the principal writer for the Obie-winning San Francisco Mime Troupe, she created iconoclastic left-wing satire that courted both chuckles and outrage.

name: Chris Gauthier
profession: Once Upon a Time and Eureka Actor
headline: Chris Gauthier, ‘Once Upon a Time’ and ‘Eureka’ Actor, Dies at 48
abstract: Mr. Gauthier appeared in dozens of television shows and films, including “Freddy vs. Jason” and “Watchmen.”

name: Paul L. Gioia
profession: Oversaw Nuclear Power in New York
headline: Paul L. Gioia, Who Oversaw Nuclear Power in New York, Dies at 81
abstract: As head of the state’s Public Service Commission, he clashed with Gov. Mario Cuomo over the management of two troubled power plants and was ousted by him.

name: Roni Stoneman
profession: Country Musics First Lady of the Banjo
headline: Roni Stoneman, Country Music’s ‘First Lady of the Banjo,’ Dies at 85
abstract: A featured player on “Hee Haw” and a member of the famed Stoneman Family, she was the first woman to play modern bluegrass banjo on a phonograph record.

name: Bruce Newman
headline: Bruce Newman, Leading Man of Antiques, Dies at 94
abstract: He oversaw Newel Galleries and its over-the-top treasures that embellished Broadway and Hollywood sets and the living rooms of movie stars and a first lady.

name: Melvin Way
headline: Melvin Way, Outsider Artist Who Depicted Inner Mysteries, Dies at 70
abstract: He struggled with schizophrenia, but he drew praise for the intricate diagrams he drew on scraps of paper while living in New York City homeless shelters.

name: Nikolai I. Ryzhkov
headline: Nikolai I. Ryzhkov, Soviet Premier Who Presided Over Economic Chaos, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Ryzhkov, who ascended to the Soviet Union’s second most powerful post in 1985, took much of the blame for the economic collapse that led to the country’s dissolution in 1991.

name: Richard Lewis
headline: Richard Lewis, Acerbic Comedian and Character Actor, Dies at 76
abstract: After rising to prominence for his stand-up act, he became a regular in movies and TV, most recently on “Curb Your Enthusiasm.”

name: Micheline Presle
profession: Actress Known for Devil in the Flesh
headline: Micheline Presle, Actress Known for ‘Devil in the Flesh,’ Dies at 101
abstract: A link to France’s first golden age of cinema, she drew international attention for a 1947 film that created a scandal in France and was banned in Britain for years.

name: René Pollesch
