headline: René Pollesch, Provocative Force in German Theater, Dies at 61
abstract: His avant-garde work, short on character and plot but long on verbal high jinks, could be irreverent, even goofy, but it was always intellectually serious.

name: Guy Alexandre
headline: Guy Alexandre, Transplant Surgeon Who Redefined Death, Dies at 89
abstract: His willingness to remove kidneys from brain-dead patients increased the organs’ viability while challenging the line between living and dead.

name: Nancy Wallace
profession: Fervent Savior of the Bronx River
headline: Nancy Wallace, Fervent Savior of the Bronx River, Dies at 93
abstract: She helped transform a watery graveyard for automobiles, tires and appliances into an urban greenbelt for New York City and Westchester County.

name: Günter Brus
headline: Günter Brus, Artist Who Shocked Postwar Austria, Dies at 85
abstract: A founder of a transgressive 1960s movement known as Viennese Actionism, he used his body as a canvas and blood and excrement as his materials.

name: Betty Fiechter
profession: Pioneer in the World of Watches
headline: Overlooked No More: Betty Fiechter, Pioneer in the World of Watches
abstract: She started out at Blancpain as an apprentice and eventually took over as an owner, a move that one industry insider noted was “totally unprecedented” for a woman.

name: Robert M. Young
headline: Robert M. Young, Filmmaker Who Indulged His Wanderlust, Dies at 99
abstract: The subjects of his documentaries included Indigenous peoples, civil rights sit-ins and the war in Angola. His narrative films included “Extremities” and “The Ballad of Gregorio Cortez.”

name: Iris Apfel
headline: Iris Apfel, Eye-Catcher With a Kaleidoscopic Wardrobe, Dies at 102
abstract: She came to fame in the fashion world in her 80s and 90s, and her wildly eclectic closet of clothes formed a hit exhibition at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

name: John C. Bahnsen Jr.
profession: Fierce Commander During the Vietnam War
headline: John C. Bahnsen Jr., 89, Dies; Fierce Commander During the Vietnam War
abstract: One of the most honored combat veterans in U.S. history, he was awarded 19 decorations for valor. He was blunt about what his job was: killing.

name: Chris Mortensen
headline: Chris Mortensen, ESPN’s Longtime N.F.L. Insider, Dies at 72
abstract: For over 30 years he covered the league for programs like “SportsCenter” and “Sunday N.F.L. Countdown.” As a sportswriter, he won a prestigious George Polk Award.

name: Mary Bartlett Bunge
headline: Mary Bartlett Bunge, 92, Dies; Pioneer in Spinal Injury Treatment
abstract: She discovered new ways to promote regeneration in the nervous system, offering hope to countless paralyzed patients worldwide.

name: Juli Lynne Charlot
headline: Juli Lynne Charlot, Creator of the Poodle Skirt, Dies at 101
abstract: Ms. Charlot’s creation merged seamlessly with the carefree youth culture of the 1950s, becoming visual shorthand for the entire decade.

name: Edward Bond
headline: Edward Bond, 89, Playwright Who Clashed With Royal Censors, Dies
abstract: His brazen first play, “Saved,” though it drew outrage, led to the end of more than 200 years of state control over the theater.

name: Antoine Predock
headline: Antoine Predock, Architect Who Channeled the Southwest, Dies at 87
abstract: His striking, acclaimed structures evoked the desert. But for major projects elsewhere in the world, he adopted the same principle: connecting buildings to their settings.

name: Ellen Bernstein
headline: Rabbi Ellen Bernstein, Who Saw Ecology as God’s Work, Dies at 70
abstract: She linked her passion for the natural environment to the precepts of the Hebrew Bible, beginning with the Garden of Eden.

name: Janice Burgess
headline: Janice Burgess, 72, Dies; Nickelodeon Executive and ‘Backyardigans’ Creator
abstract: She oversaw production of “Blue’s Clues” and drew on her childhood for the popular show in which five cartoon animals imagine their yard as a place of otherworldly adventure.

name: Shafiqah Hudson
headline: Shafiqah Hudson, Who Fought Trolls on Social Media, Dies at 46
abstract: When the hashtag #EndFathersDay began trending on Twitter, she realized it was more than a joke: It was a coordinated disinformation effort.

name: Estella Bergere Leopold
profession: Found Climate Clues in Ancient Pollen
headline: Estella Bergere Leopold Dies at 97; Found Climate Clues in Ancient Pollen
abstract: The last child of the pioneering ecologist Aldo Leopold, she also helped preserve her father’s legacy as a founder of the modern environmental movement.

name: Frank Popoff
profession: Sought to Lead a Friendlier Dow Chemical
headline: Frank Popoff, Who Sought to Lead a Friendlier Dow Chemical, Dies at 88
abstract: As chief executive, he pushed a company known for Agent Orange, napalm and chlorine to undo its confrontational reputation and promote environmental sustainability.

name: Josette Molland
profession: Told of Life in Nazi Camps Through Art
headline: Josette Molland, Who Told of Life in Nazi Camps Through Art, Dies at 100
abstract: She endured horrors as a captured member of the French Resistance, and to ensure that her story, too, would survive, she depicted them years later in a series of stark paintings.

name: Lucien Pellat-Finet
headline: Lucien Pellat-Finet, Fashion’s ‘King of Cashmere,’ Dies at 78
abstract: The aesthetic of the sweaters he designed, which included provocative symbols like marijuana leaves and skulls, was casual. Their price tags were not.

name: Anthony Epstein
headline: Dr. Anthony Epstein, Pathologist Who Discovered Epstein-Barr Virus, Dies at 102
abstract: His groundbreaking research, which he performed with Yvonne Barr, his doctoral student, uncovered the first virus capable of causing cancer in humans.

name: Buddy Duress
profession: Came Off the Streets to Find Stardom
headline: Buddy Duress, Who Came Off the Streets to Find Stardom, Dies at 38
abstract: He was a homeless heroin dealer when the Safdie brothers put him in their movies, and the critics raved. But the recklessness that gave his acting authenticity thwarted his career.

name: Lucas Samaras
headline: Lucas Samaras, Artist Who Was His Own Canvas, Dies at 87
abstract: A wild card even by the rabble-rousing standards of the 1960s, he once said that he used himself in his art “because it is still unorthodox to use one’s self.”

name: Richard Truly
headline: Richard Truly, 86, Dies; Shuttle Astronaut Who Went On to Lead NASA
abstract: In 1983, he commanded a Challenger shuttle flight. After the 1986 disaster, he was charged with leading NASA’s return to space.

name: Steve Lawrence
profession: Sang His Listeners Down Memory Lane
headline: Steve Lawrence, 88, Who Sang His Listeners Down Memory Lane, Dies
abstract: With his wife, Eydie Gorme, and sometimes on his own, he kept pop standards in vogue long past their prime. He also acted on television and on Broadway.

name: Akira Toriyama
headline: Akira Toriyama, Creator of ‘Dragon Ball,’ Dies at 68
abstract: His popular manga inspired numerous television, film and video game adaptations, reaching fans far beyond Japan’s borders.

name: David Bordwell
headline: David Bordwell, Scholar Who Demystified the Art of Film, Dies at 76
abstract: His scholarship focused on how movies work. Roger Ebert called him “our best writer on the cinema.”

name: Max Hardy
profession: Helped Bring Chef-Driven Cuisine to Detroit
headline: Max Hardy, 40, Dies; Helped Bring Chef-Driven Cuisine to Detroit
abstract: With his unique blend of Lowcountry and Caribbean influences, he ranked among the best of a new generation of Black culinary wizards.

name: Howard Hiatt
profession: Steered Public Health Toward Greater Accountability
headline: Howard Hiatt, 98, Dies; Steered Public Health Toward Greater Accountability
abstract: A physician, scientist and academic, he brought together experts across disciplines to focus on the economic, political and social causes of poor health, not just the biological factors.

name: Petra Mathers
headline: Petra Mathers, Author Whose Children’s Stories Soared, Dies at 78
abstract: Her winsome animal characters and their comic adventures expressed universal truths and feelings, rendered in a naïve and often surrealistic style.

name: William Whitworth
headline: William Whitworth, Revered Writer and Editor, Is Dead at 87
abstract: After writing memorable character sketches and fine-tuning others’ copy at The New Yorker, he spent two decades as editor in chief of The Atlantic Monthly.

name: Kathy Goldman
profession: Fought Hunger in New York City
headline: Kathy Goldman, Who Fought Hunger in New York City, Dies at 92
abstract: She helped introduce free breakfasts and lunches for schoolchildren and open pantries and soup kitchens for the poor.

name: Malachy McCourt
headline: Malachy McCourt, Actor, Memoirist and Gadabout, Dies at 92
abstract: Playing the professional Irishman, he returned from Limerick to New York where he tended bar and appeared in soap operas and, with his family, scattered “Angela’s Ashes.”

name: Ira von Fürstenberg
headline: Ira von Fürstenberg, Jet-Setting Princess and Actress, Dies at 83
abstract: With her aristocratic lineage, high-profile husbands and famous friends, she embodied a chic life of luxury as an international social figure.

name: Eric Carmen
profession: Raspberries Frontman and All by Myself Singer
headline: Eric Carmen, Raspberries Frontman and ‘All by Myself’ Singer, Dies at 74
abstract: He sang on the power-pop pioneers’ 1972 breakout hit, “Go All the Way,” before launching a successful solo career as a soft-rock crooner.

name: David Mixner
headline: David Mixner, Fierce Fighter for Gay Rights, Is Dead at 77
abstract: He persuaded Ronald Reagan to help defeat a proposed ban on L.G.B.T.Q. schoolteachers in California in 1978, and he sparred with his friend Bill Clinton over “don’t ask, don’t tell.”

name: Karl Wallinger
profession: Sang With World Party and the Waterboys
headline: Karl Wallinger, Who Sang With World Party and the Waterboys, Dies at 66
abstract: As a songwriter and instrumentalist as well, he blended pop and folk influences into music that helped define college radio in the 1980s and ’90s.

name: Marnia Lazreg
headline: Marnia Lazreg, Muslim Scholar Who Critiqued the Veil, Is Dead at 83
abstract: A sociologist in New York, she examined the power dynamics and difficult history of her native land from a feminist and anticolonial perspective.

name: Olga Murray
profession: Changed the Lives of Children in Nepal
headline: Olga Murray, Who Changed the Lives of Children in Nepal, Dies at 98
abstract: Her foundation rescued thousands of girls and young women from bonded slavery and secured meals and schooling for impoverished children.

name: Philippe de Gaulle
profession: Admiral and Son of Charles de Gaulle
headline: Philippe de Gaulle, Admiral and Son of Charles de Gaulle, Dies at 102
abstract: His exploits in World War II and later in Algeria and Indochina were not enough for him to emerge from the shadow of his father, for whom a thousand streets in France are named.

name: Len Sirowitz
headline: Len Sirowitz, Whose Bold, Offbeat Ads Captured an Era, Dies at 91
abstract: An award-winning agency art director, he brought a striking visual touch to campaigns for the Volkswagen Beetle, Sara Lee and Sony in the 1960s as well as to the antiwar and antinuclear movements.

name: Gerald M. Levin
profession: Time Warner Chief in a Merger Debacle
headline: Gerald M. Levin, Time Warner Chief in a Merger Debacle, Dies at 84
abstract: He was called a visionary in cable television, but his foray into the world of the internet, in a marriage with AOL, proved disastrous.

name: Ira M. Millstein
headline: Ira M. Millstein, Corporate Lawyer With Public Impact, Dies at 97
abstract: He crusaded for stronger corporate governance by company boards, advised New York City on avoiding bankruptcy and helped put Ruth Bader Ginsburg on the federal bench.

name: Giandomenico Picco
headline: Giandomenico Picco, Diplomat Who Freed Hostages in Lebanon, Dies at 75
abstract: As the “chief troubleshooter” for the United Nations, he spent months shuttling around the Middle East to secure the release of 11 captives.

name: Dan Wakefield
profession: Multifaceted Writer on a Spiritual Journey
headline: Dan Wakefield, Multifaceted Writer on a Spiritual Journey, Dies at 91
abstract: He was prolific and acclaimed, producing novels, journalism, essays, criticism, screenplays and, in a memoir, an account of his path from faith to atheism and back again.

name: Sydell L. Miller
profession: Self-Made Eyelash and Hair Care Mogul
headline: Sydell L. Miller, Self-Made Eyelash and Hair Care Mogul, Dies at 86
abstract: She and her husband, Arnold, made it big in the beauty industry by giving new skills, products and dignity to the workaday salon hairdresser.

name: Miriam Solovieff
headline: Overlooked No More: Miriam Solovieff, Lauded Violinist Who Suffered Tragedy
abstract: She led a successful career despite coping with a horrific event that she witnessed at 18: the killing of her mother and sister at the hands of her father.

name: Kent Campbell
profession: Pivotal Figure in the Fight Against Malaria
headline: Kent Campbell, Pivotal Figure in the Fight Against Malaria, Dies at 80
abstract: Among his accomplishments in a four-decade career in public health, he helped pioneer programs providing bed nets in Africa.

name: Doug Blevins
profession: Kicking Guru for College and N.F.L. Players
headline: Doug Blevins, Kicking Guru for College and N.F.L. Players, Dies at 60
abstract: He fine-tuned the mechanics of punters and kickers, including Adam Vinatieri, the N.F.L.’s career scoring leader, even as he lived with cerebral palsy.

name: Serge Raoul
headline: Serge Raoul, Whose SoHo Bistro Glittered With Stars, Dies at 86
abstract: Raoul’s, which he founded, was a celebrity magnet and a neighborhood institution in the 1970s and ’80s. But he had never planned on a life in the restaurant business.

name: Joe Camp
headline: Joe Camp, Filmmaker Behind ‘Benji’ Franchise, Dies at 84
abstract: He defied the odds to turn “Benji,” a live-action film series from a dog’s perspective, into a smash hit, and turned the film industry on its head in the process.

name: Dorie Ladner
headline: Dorie Ladner, Unheralded Civil Rights Heroine, Dies at 81
abstract: She risked arrest and worse in pursuit of her goals of integration and voting rights from the time she was a teenager.

name: Margaret Grade
profession: California Inn Was Beloved by Stars
headline: Margaret Grade, Whose California Inn Was Beloved by Stars, Dies at 72
abstract: Her Manka’s Inverness Lodge drew actors and writers who dined at Ms. Grade’s farm-to-table restaurant and reveled in her eccentric flair.

name: Byron Janis
headline: Byron Janis, Pianist of Romantic Passion, Dies at 95
abstract: He had a brilliant career before arthritis in his hands forced him from the stage, but he overcame the condition and returned to performing.

name: Steve Harley
headline: Steve Harley, ‘Make Me Smile’ Singer, Dies at 73
abstract: He was the frontman of the rock band Cockney Rebel, which landed several hits on the British charts in the 1970s.

name: Bernard Schwartz
headline: Bernard Schwartz, Antiwar Executive Who Built an Arms Maker, Dies at 98
abstract: Despite his opposition to the Vietnam War, as an investor he took over an ailing defense contractor, Loral, and turned it into a multibillion-dollar company.

name: Ed Mintz
profession: Gave Audiences the Chance to Grade Films
headline: Ed Mintz, Who Gave Audiences the Chance to Grade Films, Dies at 83
abstract: With CinemaScore, he broke new ground by building a business based on the opinions of moviegoers rather than critics.

name: Gylan Kain
profession: Founder of the Last Poets and a Progenitor of Rap
headline: Gylan Kain, 81, a Founder of the Last Poets and a Progenitor of Rap, Dies
abstract: He spun gripping portraits of the Black experience starting in the 1960s with the seminal Harlem spoken-word collective, laying a foundation for what was to come.

name: Thomas Stafford
profession: Commander of First U.S.-Soviet Space Mission
headline: Thomas Stafford, 93, Commander of First U.S.-Soviet Space Mission, Dies
abstract: The Apollo-Soyuz mission, amid the Cold War, broke new ground in space cooperation when an American capsule docked with a Soviet craft 140 miles above the earth.

name: David Seidler
profession: Oscar-Winning Writer of The Kings Speech
headline: David Seidler, Oscar-Winning Writer of ‘The King’s Speech,’ Dies at 86
abstract: He drew on his own painful experiences with a stutter in depicting King George VI’s struggles to overcome his impediment and rally Britain in World War II.

name: Andrew Crispo
headline: Andrew Crispo, Disgraced Manhattan Gallery Owner, Dies at 78
abstract: His fall from the pinnacle of the New York art world involved murder, torture, tax evasion, extortion and two terms in prison.

name: Paulin Hountondji
headline: Paulin Hountondji, Revolutionary African Philosopher, Dies at 81
abstract: He rebelled against efforts to force African ways of thinking into the European worldview. His thoughts had the effect of a bomb in African intellectual life.

name: Aribert Reimann
headline: Aribert Reimann, Masterful German Opera Composer, Is Dead at 88
abstract: His works, which were radically individual, were among the most celebrated of the late 20th and early 21st century.

name: Jean Maria Arrigo
headline: Jean Maria Arrigo, Who Exposed Psychologists’ Ties to Torture, Dies at 79
abstract: Risking ostracism by her colleagues, she fought against the use of psychologists in coercive interrogations by the military and the C.I.A.

name: David Breashears
profession: Braved Everest to Capture It on Film
headline: David Breashears, 68, Who Braved Everest to Capture It on Film, Dies
abstract: He risked death on the slopes of the world’s highest mountain to produce the highest-grossing IMAX documentary of all time.

name: Cola Boyy
headline: Cola Boyy, Indie Singer and Disability Activist, Dies at 34
abstract: Cola Boyy, whose real name was Matthew Urango, sang and produced his own brand of disco music. Born with spina bifida, he had been a vocal advocate for people with disabilities.

name: Martin Greenfield
headline: Martin Greenfield, Tailor to Sinatra, Obama, Trump and Shaq, Dies at 95
abstract: He dressed six presidents, coached designers and made thousands of suits for TV shows and movies. But his beginnings were dismal: He learned to sew at Auschwitz.

name: Bill Jorgensen
headline: Bill Jorgensen, Authoritative New York TV Newsman, Dies at 96
abstract: Getting his start in the Midwest, he was best known for leading the New York broadcast “The 10 O’Clock News.”

name: Frans de Waal
profession: Found the Origins of Morality in Apes
headline: Frans de Waal, Who Found the Origins of Morality in Apes, Dies at 75
abstract: An unusually popular primatologist, he drew the attention of Newt Gingrich, Isabella Rossellini, the philosopher Peter Singer and the reading public.

name: M. Emmet Walsh
headline: M. Emmet Walsh, Character Actor Who Always Stood Out, Dies at 88
abstract: His roles in films like “Knives Out” and “Blade Runner” were sometimes big, sometimes small. But he invariably made a strong impression.

name: Julie Robinson Belafonte
headline: Julie Robinson Belafonte, Dancer, Actress and Activist, Is Dead at 95
abstract: With the singer Harry Belafonte, she was half of a celebrated, and sometimes denounced, interracial power couple who pressed the cause of civil rights in the 1960s.

name: Yvonne Barr
headline: Overlooked No More: Yvonne Barr, Who Helped Discover a Cancer-Causing Virus
abstract: A virologist, she worked with the pathologist Anthony Epstein, who died last month, in finding for the first time that a virus that could cause cancer. It’s known as the Epstein-Barr virus.

name: Robert L. Barry
headline: Robert L. Barry, 89, Diplomat Who Negotiated Pact With Soviets, Dies
abstract: He was the chief negotiator on a troop-inspections accord that American officials saw as crucial in easing East-West tensions near the end of the Cold War.

name: Amnon Weinstein
headline: Amnon Weinstein, Who Restored Violins From the Holocaust, Dies at 84
abstract: Many were left behind by victims of the gas chambers. He let the instruments be heard again in musical tributes through his organization, Violins of Hope.

name: Norman Miller
headline: Norman Miller, German Refugee Who Helped Arrest a Top Nazi, Dies at 99
abstract: At 15, he escaped to England. At 20, he enlisted in the British Army and identified a German minister — whose roles included deporting Dutch Jews to labor camps — as he tried to flee.

name: Rose Dugdale
headline: Rose Dugdale, Heiress Turned Irish Independence Fighter, Dies at 82
abstract: Born into English wealth and Oxford-educated, she left it all behind for a life of radical and often violent activism.

name: Lyn Hejinian
profession: Leading Light of the Language Poetry Movement
headline: Lyn Hejinian, 82, Dies; Leading Light of the Language Poetry Movement
abstract: A poet, publisher and professor, she channeled the revolutionary spirit and deconstructionist currents of the 1960s to challenge the conventions of poetry.

name: Laurent de Brunhoff
headline: Laurent de Brunhoff, Artist Who Made Babar Famous, Dies at 98
abstract: After his father, who created the character, died, he continued the series of books about a modest elephant and his escapades in Paris for seven decades.

name: Maurizio Pollini
headline: Maurizio Pollini, Celebrated Pianist Who Defined Modernism, Dies at 82
abstract: His recordings of Beethoven and Chopin were hailed as classics, but his technical ability sometimes invited controversy.

name: Peter G. Angelos
headline: Peter G. Angelos, Owner of the Baltimore Orioles, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Angelos oversaw 14 consecutive losing seasons, the worst run in franchise history, but the team is now a winning ball club about to be sold to new owners.

name: Ben Stern
profession: Opposed a Nazi Rally in Illinois
headline: Ben Stern, Who Opposed a Nazi Rally in Illinois, Dies at 102
abstract: He was held prisoner in nine concentration camps. Decades later, he fought a battle against American Nazis that became a major free-speech case.

name: Shani Mott
headline: Shani Mott, Black Studies Scholar Who Examined Power All Around Her, Dies at 47
abstract: Her work looked at how race and power are experienced in America. In 2022, she filed a lawsuit saying that the appraisal of her home was undervalued because of bias.

name: Lisa Lane
headline: Lisa Lane, Chess Champion Whose Reign Was Meteoric, Dies at 90
abstract: She was the first chess player to appear on the cover of Sports Illustrated. But people focused more on her looks than on her ability.

name: Lee Berry
profession: Black Panther in a Radical Chic Time
headline: Lee Berry, Black Panther in a ‘Radical Chic’ Time, Dies at 78
abstract: He was one of the prosecuted Panther 21 in New York, and his account of abuse in jail was a catalyst for Leonard Bernstein’s famous Park Avenue fund-raising party.

name: Marjorie Perloff
headline: Marjorie Perloff, Leading Scholar of Avant-Garde Poetry, Dies at 92
abstract: A forceful advocate for experimental poetry, she argued that a critic’s task was not to search for meaning, but to explicate the form and texture of a poem.

name: Richard Serra
profession: Recast Sculpture on a Massive Scale
headline: Richard Serra, Who Recast Sculpture on a Massive Scale, Dies at 85
abstract: His tilted walls of rusting steel, monumental blocks and other immense and inscrutable forms created environments that had to be walked through, or around, to be fully experienced.

name: Daniel Kahneman
headline: Daniel Kahneman, Who Plumbed the Psychology of Economics, Dies at 90
abstract: He helped pioneer a branch of the field that exposed hard-wired mental biases in people’s economic behavior. The work led to a Nobel.

name: Stephen Adams
headline: Stephen Adams, Who Made Yale Music School Tuition-Free, Dies at 86
abstract: A billionaire businessman and a late-blooming piano aficionado, he set a record with the anonymous $100 million gift that he and his wife gave the school.

name: Kate Banks
headline: Kate Banks, Children’s Author Who Wrote About Grief, Dies at 64
abstract: She became an award-winning author of children’s books and young-adult novels despite debilitating health issues and the murder of her father.

name: Henrietta Leavitt
headline: Overlooked No More: Henrietta Leavitt, Who Unraveled Mysteries of the Stars
abstract: The portrait that emerged from her discovery, called Leavitt’s Law, showed that the universe was hundreds of times bigger than astronomers had imagined.

name: Joseph I. Lieberman
headline: Joseph I. Lieberman, Senator and Vice-Presidential Nominee, Dies at 82
abstract: He served four terms in the Senate from Connecticut and was chosen by Al Gore as his running mate in the 2000 election. He was the first Jewish candidate on a major-party ticket.

name: Peter Eotvos
headline: Peter Eotvos, Evocative Modernist Composer and Conductor, Dies at 80
abstract: A tireless Hungarian advocate of contemporary music, he adapted literary sources both modern and classic, instilling his work with “inimitable character and pathos.”

name: Linda Bean
profession: L.L. Bean Heir and a Conservative Donor
headline: Linda Bean, an L.L. Bean Heir and a Conservative Donor, Dies at 82
abstract: A granddaughter of the celebrated Maine brand’s founder, she set out as an entrepreneur in her mid-60s and used her wealth to fund right-wing causes.

name: Vernor Vinge
headline: Vernor Vinge, Innovative Science Fiction Novelist, Dies at 79
abstract: He conceived an early version of cyberspace and predicted the “technological singularity,” a tipping point at which machines would become smarter than humans.

name: Robert Moskowitz
profession: Abstract Painter of New Yorks Skyscrapers
headline: Robert Moskowitz, Abstract Painter of New York’s Skyscrapers, Dies at 88
abstract: He depicted the Empire State Building, the Flatiron Building and, most indelibly, the World Trade Center. Those paintings took on new meaning after 9/11.

name: Louis Gossett Jr.
profession: Officer and a Gentleman and Roots Actor
headline: Louis Gossett Jr., 87, Dies; ‘An Officer and a Gentleman’ and ‘Roots’ Actor
abstract: His portrayal of a drill instructor earned him the Oscar for best supporting actor. He was the first Black performer to win in that category.

name: Eleanor Collins
headline: Eleanor Collins, Canada’s ‘First Lady of Jazz,’ Dies at 104
abstract: A singer known for her mastery of standards, she found stardom in Canada on TV and in nightclubs. But she was virtually unknown in the United States.

name: Daniel A. Moore
profession: Founder of an African American Museum
headline: Daniel A. Moore, Founder of an African American Museum, Dies at 88
abstract: To tell the full story of the American Black experience, he created an Atlanta institution in 1978 and later moved it to a building “erected brick by brick” by Black masons.

name: Neeli Cherkovski
headline: Neeli Cherkovski, Poet Who Chronicled the Beat Generation, Dies at 78
abstract: His biographies of Charles Bukowski and Lawrence Ferlinghetti came to overshadow his own work. “I would love an interview,” he once said, “where Bukowski is not mentioned.”

name: Peter Shapiro
headline: Peter Shapiro, Political Groundbreaker in New Jersey, Dies at 71
abstract: He bucked the Democratic machine to become the youngest member of the state’s General Assembly and reformed government as the first Essex County executive.

name: Paula Weinstein
headline: Paula Weinstein, Hollywood Veteran and Political Activist, Dies at 78
abstract: Raised by a McCarthy-era rebel, the producer and journalist Hannah Weinstein, she followed her mother’s path into movies and television, advocacy and action.

name: Esther Coopersmith
headline: Esther Coopersmith, Washington Hostess and Diplomat, Dies at 94
abstract: A place at her dinner tables, which sat 75, provided access to networks of money, influence and power across cultural and political divides.

name: Lorraine Graves
headline: Lorraine Graves, Pioneering Harlem Ballerina, Dies at 66
abstract: Tall and commanding, she dazzled audiences as a principal dancer for the groundbreaking Dance Theater of Harlem for nearly two decades.

name: Betty Cole Dukert
headline: Betty Cole Dukert, Top ‘Meet the Press’ Producer, Dies at 96
abstract: She worked as a secretary before being hired as an associate producer at the NBC News public affairs show in 1956. She went on to spend 41 years there.

name: Barbara Rush
headline: Barbara Rush, Award-Winning TV and Film Actress, Dies at 97
abstract: She received a Golden Globe in 1954 as that year’s rising star and appeared in movies alongside Dean Martin, Frank Sinatra and Paul Newman.

name: Lou Conter
profession: Last Survivor of the Battleship Arizona
headline: Lou Conter, Last Survivor of the Battleship Arizona, Dies at 102
abstract: Escaping injury in the Japanese attack on the ship in Pearl Harbor on Dec. 7, 1941, he went on to help in recovering bodies and putting out fires.

name: Joe Flaherty
profession: SCTV and Freaks and Geeks Actor
headline: Joe Flaherty, ‘SCTV’ and ‘Freaks and Geeks’ Actor, Dies at 82
abstract: He first became known for playing a series of oddball characters on one of TV’s most influential sketch shows. He was later a familiar face in film and on TV.

name: Larry Lucchino
profession: Top Executive at Three M.L.B. Teams
headline: Larry Lucchino, Top Executive at Three M.L.B. Teams, Dies at 78
abstract: He oversaw design of new ballparks for the Baltimore Orioles and San Diego Padres, as well as renovations for Fenway Park with the Boston Red Sox.

name: John Barth
headline: John Barth, Writer Who Pushed Storytelling’s Limits, Dies at 93
abstract: His sprawling and boisterous novel “The Sot-Weed Factor,” published in 1960, projected him into the ranks of the country’s most innovative writers.

name: Maryse Condé
headline: Maryse Condé, ‘Grande Dame’ of Francophone Literature, Dies at 90
abstract: She explored the history and culture of Africa, the West Indies and Europe in work that made her a perennial favorite for the Nobel Prize.

name: Christopher Durang
headline: Christopher Durang, Playwright Who Mixed High Art and Low Humor, Dies at 75
abstract: In a career spanning more than 40 years, he established himself as a hyperliterate jester and an anarchic clown.

name: Eli Noyes
headline: Eli Noyes, Animator Who Turned Clay and Sand Into Art, Dies at 81
abstract: His innovative stop-motion animation influenced a generation of filmmakers, including the creators of Wallace and Gromit.

name: Gaetano Pesce
headline: Gaetano Pesce, Designer Who Broke the Rules, Is Dead at 84
abstract: He brought surrealism, and politics, into the design world, disdaining conformity and right angles. “He was an enemy of the grid.”

name: John Sinclair
headline: John Sinclair, 82, Dies; Counterculture Activist Who Led a ‘Guitar Army’
abstract: His imprisonment for a minor marijuana offense became a cause célèbre. He was released after John Lennon and Yoko Ono sang about him at a protest rally.

name: Michael Singer
headline: Michael Singer, Sculptor Who Used Nature as His Medium, Dies at 78
abstract: His work, on an increasingly large scale, attempted to highlight, and repair, the impact of human intervention on the landscape.

name: Richard Benedick
headline: Richard Benedick, Negotiator of Landmark Ozone Treaty, Dies at 88
abstract: He played a key role in securing the Montreal Protocol, an international environmental pact to protect the ozone layer by reducing the use of certain chemicals.

name: Lou Whittaker
headline: Lou Whittaker, Mountain Adventurer and Entrepreneur, Dies at 95
abstract: While his identical twin was the first American to summit Everest, he was best known  for his devotion to Mount Rainier, the peak of their youth.

name: Sami Michael
headline: Sami Michael, Israeli Novelist With Arabic Roots, Dies at 97
abstract: A refugee from Iraq, he explored in popular books the worlds of Jews living in Arabic countries or who fled persecution, and of Arabs living in Israel.

name: Howard Atlee
headline: Howard Atlee, Showman Who Promoted Dramas and Dogs, Dies at 97
abstract: As a press agent, he had his first big hit with “Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf?” In dog competitions, his first big hit was a dachshund named Virginia.

name: Lynne Reid Banks
profession: Author of The Indian in the Cupboard
headline: Lynne Reid Banks, Author of ‘The Indian in the Cupboard,’ Dies at 94
abstract: She explored the struggles of young women in the novel “The L-Shaped Room” but found her biggest success with a children’s book about a magical cupboard.

name: Margaret Tynes
headline: Margaret Tynes, Soprano Who Soared in Verdi and Strauss, Dies at 104
abstract: Because there were few opportunities for Black singers in the U.S., she began performing in Europe, where she was praised for her work in “Tosca,” “Carmen” and other operas.

name: Daniel P. Jordan
headline: Daniel P. Jordan, Monticello Leader in Changing Times, Dies at 85
abstract: He expanded the educational mission of Thomas Jefferson’s plantation. He also embraced research that showed Jefferson had fathered the children of one of his slaves.

name: Kate Coleman
headline: Kate Coleman, Who Documented the Bay Area Counterculture, Dies at 81
abstract: She wrote about politics and the patriarchy as a left-wing writer, then alienated her compatriots with exposés critical of the Black Panthers and the environmental movement.

name: Mary Ann Zielonko
headline: Mary Ann Zielonko, Partner of Kitty Genovese, Dies at 85
abstract: The murder of Ms. Genovese, and her neighbors’ reaction to it, generated headlines. The nature of her relationship with Ms. Zielonko was a different story.

name: Albert Heath
headline: Albert Heath, Jazz Drum Virtuoso, Is Dead at 88
abstract: He accompanied stars like John Coltrane and worked frequently with his brothers. “I’ve always thought I was a master,” he once said. Few disagreed.

name: Casey Benjamin
headline: Casey Benjamin, Free-Spirited Saxophonist, Dies at 45
abstract: A musical voyager who wouldn’t be limited by genre, style or even instrument, he brought exuberance to the Robert Glasper Experiment and other groups.

name: Jerry Grote
profession: Stalwart Mets Catcher on 69 Championship Team
headline: Jerry Grote, Stalwart Mets Catcher on ’69 Championship Team, Dies at 81
abstract: Known for his field savvy and his powerful arm, he helped propel the New York Mets through their storied 1969 World Series run.

name: Ralph Puckett Jr.
headline: Col. Ralph Puckett Jr., Belated Medal of Honor Recipient, Dies at 97
abstract: One of the Army’s most highly decorated servicemen, he received the military’s supreme tribute for valor, for his actions in the Korean War — 71 years after the fact.

name: Anthony Insolia
headline: Anthony Insolia, Who Led the Expansion of Newsday, Dies at 98
abstract: The Long Island paper won seven Pulitzer Prizes during his tenure, and he was a top editor for the Arizona Project, which investigated a reporter’s murder.

name: Herbert Kroemer
headline: Herbert Kroemer, 95, Dies; Laid Groundwork for Modern Technologies
abstract: He shared a Nobel Prize in Physics for discoveries that paved the way for high-speed internet communication, mobile phones and bar-code readers.

name: Peter Higgs
headline: Peter Higgs, Nobelist Who Predicted the ‘God Particle,’ Dies at 94
abstract: The Higgs boson was named for him. It was a key element of the Standard Model, which encapsulated all human knowledge so far about elementary particles.

name: Clarence Henry
profession: New Orleans R&B Star Known as the Frogman
headline: Clarence Henry, New Orleans R&B Star Known as the Frogman, Dies at 87
abstract: A local hero in his hometown, he was best known for his hit “Ain’t Got No Home,” which showcased the vocal versatility that earned him his nickname.

name: Trevor Griffiths
profession: Marxist Writer for Stage and Screen
headline: Trevor Griffiths, Marxist Writer for Stage and Screen, Dies at 88
abstract: For him, “art played a particular role in social change,” the director Mehmet Ergen said. “Everything was political.”

name: Cecil Murray
headline: Rev. Cecil Murray, Leader Amid Los Angeles Riots, Dies at 94
abstract: He used his church, First African Methodist Episcopal, as a base to address the social ills that confronted the city’s Black population.

name: Nijole Sadunaite
headline: Nijole Sadunaite, Lithuanian Nun Who Opposed Soviet Rule, Dies at 85
abstract: A dissident who promoted democracy and religious freedom, she was arrested by the K.G.B. After independence from Moscow, she was honored by Lithuania’s Parliament.

name: Thomas Gumbleton
profession: Catholic Bishop and a Progressive Voice
headline: Thomas Gumbleton, Catholic Bishop and a Progressive Voice, Dies at 94
abstract: He was arrested protesting war and clashed with fellow bishops in supporting gay marriage and the ordination of women and championing victims of sex abuse by priests.

name: Mister Cee
headline: Mister Cee, Pioneering Brooklyn D.J., Dies at 57
abstract: Born Calvin Lebrun, Mister Cee was a pioneer in New York City’s hip-hop scene and helped boost the career of the Notorious B.I.G.

name: Trina Robbins
profession: Creator and Historian of Comic Books
headline: Trina Robbins, Creator and Historian of Comic Books, Dies at 85
abstract: Obsessed with comics from a young age, she was a pioneer in a male-dominated field and later documented the contributions of other women.

name: Akebono Taro
headline: Akebono, First Foreign-Born Sumo Grand Champion, Dies at 54
abstract: Born in Hawaii, he moved to Japan in 1988 and won 11 grand championships. His success drove a resurgence in the sport’s popularity.

name: O.J. Simpson
headline: O.J. Simpson, Football Star Whose Trial Riveted the Nation, Dies at 76
abstract: He ran to football fame and made fortunes in movies. His trial for the murder of his former wife and her friend became an inflection point on race in America.

name: Evan Stark
headline: Evan Stark, 82, Dies; Broadened Understanding of Domestic Violence
abstract: He and his wife wrote pioneering studies; he used the term “coercive control” to describe psychological and physical dominance by abusers.

name: Lizzie Magie
headline: Overlooked No More: Lizzie Magie, the Unknown Inventor Behind Monopoly
abstract: Magie’s creation, The Landlord’s Game, inspired the spinoff we know today. But credit for the idea long went to someone else.

name: Robert MacNeil
headline: Robert MacNeil, Earnest News Anchor for PBS, Dies at 93
abstract: With his longtime co-host Jim Lehrer, he delivered thoughtful reports that stood in stark contrast to the commercial networks’ ever more sensational newscasts.

name: Roberto Cavalli
headline: Roberto Cavalli, Designer Who Celebrated Excess, Dies at 83
abstract: From the mid-1990s onward he was one of the biggest names in fashion, with stores around the world and celebrity admirers like Lenny Kravitz and Cindy Crawford.

name: Richard Leibner
profession: Savvy Agent for Top Broadcast Journalists
headline: Richard Leibner, Savvy Agent for Top Broadcast Journalists, Dies at 85
abstract: His negotiations led to Dan Rather’s elevation from “60 Minutes” to anchor of the “CBS Evening News” and sent Diane Sawyer from “60 Minutes” to ABC.

name: Rumi Missabu
headline: Rumi Missabu, Avant-Garde Drag Performer Who Glittered, Dies at 76
abstract: He was one of the stars of the Cockettes, a psychedelic collective formed at the turn of the 1970s in San Francisco, that was short-lived but inspired generations.

name: Bennett Braun
headline: Bennett Braun, Psychiatrist Who Fueled ‘Satanic Panic,’ Dies at 83
abstract: He diagnosed dozens of patients with what he said were suppressed memories of being tortured by cults. He later lost his license.

name: Eleanor Coppola
headline: Eleanor Coppola, Who Chronicled Her Family’s Filmmaking, Dies at 87
abstract: She made documentaries of her husband Francis Ford Coppola’s “Apocalypse Now” and her daughter Sofia Coppola’s “The Virgin Suicides” and recalled their lives in books.

name: Frank Olson
headline: Frank Olson, Executive Who Linked O.J. Simpson With Hertz, Dies at 91
abstract: He negotiated Mr. Simpson’s star turn in commercials, tapping into his football fame, and formed a social bond with him — until there were murder charges. They died on the same day.

name: Fritz Peterson
profession: Yankee Pitcher in an Unusual Trade
headline: Fritz Peterson, Yankee Pitcher in an Unusual ‘Trade,’ Dies at 81
abstract: He was a leading light on an undistinguished team. But he became known less for his achievement on the field than for exchanging wives with a teammate.

name: Don Wright
profession: Editorial Cartoonist With a Skewer for a Pen
headline: Don Wright, Editorial Cartoonist With a Skewer for a Pen, Dies at 90
abstract: He won two Pulitzers for Florida newspapers, commenting wryly on war, segregation, church scandals and more while reaching readers nationwide through syndication.

name: Faith Ringgold
profession: Wove Black Life Into Quilts and Childrens Books
headline: Faith Ringgold Dies at 93; Wove Black Life Into Quilts and Children’s Books
abstract: A champion of Black artists, she explored themes of race, gender, class, family and community through a vast array of media and later the written word.

name: Rico Wade
headline: Rico Wade, an Architect of Atlanta Hip-Hop, Dies at 52
abstract: As one-third of the production team Organized Noize, he nurtured the careers of Outkast, Goodie Mob and Future from the confines of his mother’s basement, known as the Dungeon.

name: Ushio Amagatsu
headline: Ushio Amagatsu, Japanese Dancer Who Popularized Butoh, Dies at 74
abstract: He brought worldwide attention to a radical yet elemental form of contemporary dance that emerged in the wake of wartime destruction.

name: Roberta Karmel
profession: First Woman Named to the S.E.C
headline: Roberta Karmel, First Woman Named to the S.E.C., Dies at 86
abstract: She got her training as a young lawyer for the Securities and Exchange Commission, but once she became a commissioner, she accused colleagues of arrogance and insularity.

name: David Egilman
headline: David Egilman, Doctor Who Took On Drug Companies, Dies at 71
abstract: His testimony as an expert witness in some 600 trials helped plaintiffs win billions of dollars in cases involving malfeasance by pharmaceutical makers.

name: Robert Beerbohm
profession: Pioneering Comic Book Retailer and Historian
headline: Robert Beerbohm, 71, Dies; Pioneering Comic Book Retailer and Historian
abstract: A professed archaeologist of the industry, he opened his own stores and partnered with other experts and vendors in the nascent comics business.

name: James Dean
profession: Founding Director of NASA Art Program
headline: James Dean, Founding Director of NASA Art Program, Dies at 92
abstract: He arranged for artists to have access to astronauts, launchpads and more. “Their imaginations enable them to venture beyond a scientific explanation,” he once said.

name: Patti Astor
profession: Doyenne of New Yorks Avant-Garde Scene
headline: Patti Astor, Doyenne of New York’s Avant-Garde Scene, Dies at 74
abstract: She was a founder of the Fun Gallery, which staged early shows by Keith Haring and other artists who defined the city’s downtown scene in the 1980s.

name: Maurice El Medioni
headline: Maurice El Medioni, Pianist Who Fused Jewish and Arab Music, Dies at 95
abstract: An Algerian, he combined the music of his Sephardic roots with Arab traditions, incorporating boogie-woogie and other influences to create a singular style.

name: Whitey Herzog
headline: Whitey Herzog, Hall of Fame Cardinals Manager, Dies at 92
abstract: He won three pennants and a World Series as the St. Louis skipper, promoting what was called “Whiteyball,” combining speed, defense and pitching.

name: Carl Erskine
profession: Star Pitcher of the Dodgers Glory Years
headline: Carl Erskine, a Star Pitcher of the Dodgers’ Glory Years, Is Dead at 97
abstract: The record-setting pitcher known as Oisk in Brooklyn was the last surviving member of “The Boys of Summer.”

name: Ken Holtzman
profession: Pitched Two No-Hitters for the Cubs
headline: Ken Holtzman, Who Pitched Two No-Hitters for the Cubs, Is Dead at 78
abstract: He was part of the Oakland A’s dynasty in the ’70s. He was also the winningest Jewish pitcher in Major League Baseball, surpassing Sandy Koufax.

name: Bob Graham
headline: Bob Graham, Former Florida Governor and Senator, Dies at 87
abstract: After the 9/11 attacks, Mr. Graham became an outspoken critic of President George W. Bush’s response and voted against invading Iraq.

name: Marian Zazeela
headline: Marian Zazeela, an Artist of Light and Design, Dies at 83
abstract: She pivoted from painting to lighting exhibitions, performance art, graphic design and minimalist music, performed with her husband, the composer La Monte Young.

name: Anne Innis Dagg
headline: Anne Innis Dagg, Who Studied Giraffes in the Wild, Dies at 91
abstract: She was believed to be the first Western scientist to study the animals in their natural habitat, but she struggled to overcome sexism in academia.

name: Barbara Joans
profession: Studied Biker Culture on the Open Road
headline: Barbara Joans, Who Studied Biker Culture on the Open Road, Dies at 89
abstract: In her 60s, she set off on a hulking Harley-Davidson and found a new area of anthropological research: bikers, and in particular, female bikers.

name: Dickey Betts
profession: Fiery Guitarist With Allman Brothers Band
headline: Dickey Betts, Fiery Guitarist With Allman Brothers Band, Dies at 80
abstract: He traded licks with Duane Allman and proved to be a worthy sparring partner. He also wrote, and sang, the band’s biggest hit, “Ramblin’ Man.”

name: Dinh Q. Le
headline: Dinh Q. Le, Artist Who Weighed War and Memory, Dies at 56
abstract: His most famous work — collages of Vietnam War photographs, popular film stills and Western imagery — focused on a history of his homeland that he feared was being lost.

name: Beverly LaHaye
headline: Beverly LaHaye, Soldier of the Christian Right, Dies at 94
abstract: A pastor’s wife, she formed Concerned Women for America to oppose the Equal Rights Amendment. Ronald Reagan called her “one of the powerhouses on the political scene.”

name: Mandisa Hundley
profession: Gospel Singer Seen on American Idol
headline: Mandisa Hundley, Gospel Singer Seen on ‘American Idol,’ Dies at 47
abstract: Her Christian-themed music made her a fan favorite on ‘Idol’ and won her a Grammy Award in 2013.

name: Frederick Celani
profession: Made a Career as a Con Man
headline: Frederick Celani, Who Made a Career as a Con Man, Dies at 75
abstract: His serial frauds included a waterfront development in Buffalo, a civil rights law firm in California and a package delivery company in Springfield, Ill.

name: Daniel C. Dennett
profession: Widely Read and Fiercely Debated Philosopher
headline: Daniel C. Dennett, Widely Read and Fiercely Debated Philosopher, 82, Dies
abstract: Espousing his ideas in best sellers, he insisted that religion was an illusion, free will was a fantasy and evolution could only be explained by natural selection.

name: Denny Walsh
headline: Denny Walsh, Reporter Who Tussled With Mayors and Editors, Dies at 88
abstract: He won a Pulitzer Prize for investigative reporting in 1969 and later joined The New York Times, which eventually fired him.

name: William F. Pepper
profession: Claimed the Government Killed Dr. King
headline: William F. Pepper, 86, Dies; Claimed the Government Killed Dr. King
abstract: He represented James Earl Ray and the King family in efforts to prove that Dr. King was the victim of a conspiracy, becoming a celebrity among the conspiracy-minded.

name: Ellen Ash Peters
headline: Ellen Ash Peters, Pioneer on the Connecticut Bench, Dies at 94
abstract: The first woman on the faculty of Yale Law School, she was named to the State Supreme Court in 1978 and became its first female chief justice six years later.

name: David H. Pryor
headline: David H. Pryor, Arkansas Senator and Clinton Ally, Dies at 89
abstract: During his 34 years as an elected official, Mr. Pryor was sometimes said to be more liberal, especially on racial issues, than the people who elected him.

name: Martin Wygod
profession: Winner on Wall Street and the Racetrack
headline: Martin Wygod, a Winner on Wall Street and the Racetrack, Dies at 84
abstract: After he made a fortune selling prescription drugs and providing medical information online, he and his wife became leading breeders of thoroughbred horses.

name: Roman Gabriel
headline: Roman Gabriel, Star Quarterback of the 1960s and ’70s, Dies at 83
abstract: In 16 seasons with the Los Angeles Rams and the Philadelphia Eagles, he played in four Pro Bowl games and was voted Most Valuable Player in 1969.

name: Terry Anderson
profession: Reporter Held Hostage for Six Years
headline: Terry Anderson, Reporter Held Hostage for Six Years, Dies at 76
abstract: The Beirut bureau chief for The Associated Press, he was kidnapped in 1985 by Islamic militants.

name: Lourdes Portillo
headline: Lourdes Portillo, Oscar-Nominated Documentary Filmmaker, Dies at 80
abstract: Her films centered on Latin American experiences and received wide acclaim.

name: Bob Heil
profession: Innovations Enhanced the Sound of Rock
headline: Bob Heil, Whose Innovations Enhanced the Sound of Rock, Dies at 83
abstract: A groundbreaking audio engineer, he provided the large-scale systems that brought tours by the Who and the Grateful Dead to life.

name: Lori and George Schappell
headline: Lori and George Schappell, Long-Surviving Conjoined Twins, Die at 62
abstract: They were distinct people who pursued different lives. “Get past this already, everybody,” Lori said, “get past it and learn to know the individual person.”

name: Joel Breman
profession: Helped Stop an Ebola Outbreak in Africa
headline: Joel Breman, Who Helped Stop an Ebola Outbreak in Africa, Dies at 87
abstract: Part of a team flown in to fight the deadly virus in 1976, Dr. Breman also worked to stamp out tropical diseases like smallpox, malaria and Guinea worm.

name: Phyllis Pressman
headline: Phyllis Pressman, Luxury Superstore Matriarch, Is Dead at 95
abstract: She started working at Barneys to be closer to her husband. Then, she became the architect of the Chelsea Passage, the home goods bazaar that helped make it an enticing destination.

name: Terry Carter
headline: Terry Carter, Barrier-Breaking Actor and Documentarian, Dies at 95
abstract: He was a rare Black presence on “Combat!” and “The Phil Silvers Show,” then made well-regarded documentaries on luminaries like Duke Ellington and Katherine Dunham.

name: Howie Schwab
headline: Howie Schwab, ESPN Researcher and Trivia Star, Dies at 63
abstract: He stepped out of his behind-the-scenes role in 2004 when he was cast as the ultimate sports know-it-all on the game show “Stump the Schwab.”

name: Helen Vendler
headline: Helen Vendler, ‘Colossus’ of Poetry Criticism, Dies at 90
abstract: In the poetry marketplace, her praise had reputation-making power, while her disapproval could be withering.

name: Carrie Robbins
profession: Costume Designer for Dozens of Broadway Shows
headline: Carrie Robbins, Costume Designer for Dozens of Broadway Shows, Dies at 81
abstract: She made a classic wig and poodle skirt for “Grease” (using a bath mat and a toilet cover) and turned actors into Spanish inquisitors, British highwaymen and more.

name: Alfonso Chardy
headline: Alfonso Chardy, Who Helped Expose Iran-Contra Scandal, Dies at 72
abstract: A Miami Herald correspondent, he powered a team that won a Pulitzer Prize for investigative reporting and helped snare three other Pulitzers for the paper.

name: Sheppie Abramowitz
headline: Sheppie Abramowitz, Who Advocated Relief for Refugees, Dies at 88
abstract: She helped people fleeing conflicts in Vietnam, China, Kosovo and elsewhere around the world, and established the Washington office of the International Rescue Committee.

name: Michael Cuscuna
headline: Michael Cuscuna, Who Unearthed Hidden Jazz Gems, Dies at 75
abstract: Possibly the most prolific archival record producer in history, he was a founder of the Mosaic label, which became the gold standard of jazz reissues.

name: Penny Simkin
headline: Penny Simkin, ‘Mother of the Doula Movement,’ Dies at 85
abstract: As a childbirth educator and maternal advocate, she promoted a profession that provides comfort to women giving birth and offers postpartum care as well.

name: Peter Schey
headline: Peter Schey, Tenacious Lawyer Who Defended Migrant Rights, Dies at 77
abstract: He won the right to services like school and health care for people illegally crossing the border into the U.S. He also fought the Trump administration’s family separation policy.

name: Mike Pinder
profession: Founding Keyboardist of the Moody Blues
headline: Mike Pinder, Founding Keyboardist of the Moody Blues, Dies at 82
abstract: His expertise on the electromechanical Mellotron helped define the band’s progressive sound in the 1960s and ’70s on albums like “Days of Future Passed.”

name: Michael C. Jensen
headline: Michael C. Jensen, 84, Who Helped Reshape Modern Capitalism, Dies
abstract: He heralded stock options and golden parachutes as a professor at Harvard Business School, influencing a generation of Wall Street executives.

name: Cecil Williams
profession: San Francisco Church Became a Haven
headline: Cecil Williams, Whose San Francisco Church Became a Haven, Dies at 94
abstract: As the well-connected pastor of the Glide Memorial Church in the blighted Tenderloin district, he preached a “radically inclusive” gospel in serving people in need.

name: Andrew Davis
headline: Andrew Davis, 80, Dies; Renowned Conductor Who Championed Britain’s Music
abstract: Celebrated for his long tenure with Lyric Opera of Chicago, he led this and other orchestras with force and a notably energetic podium presence.

name: Archie Cooley
profession: Football Coach Known as the Gunslinger
headline: Archie Cooley, Football Coach Known as ‘the Gunslinger,’ Dies at 85
abstract: At Mississippi Valley State University, he unleashed a high-powered, pass-heavy offense that featured the future Pro Football Hall of Famer Jerry Rice.

name: Robbi Mecus
headline: Robbi Mecus, Who Fostered L.G.B.T.Q. Climbing Community, Dies at 52
abstract: A New York State forest ranger who worked in the Adirondacks, she died after falling about 1,000 feet from a peak at Denali National Park and Preserve in Alaska.

name: Paul Auster
headline: Paul Auster, the Patron Saint of Literary Brooklyn, Dies at 77
abstract: With critically lauded works like “The New York Trilogy,” the charismatic author drew inspiration from his adopted borough and won worldwide acclaim.

name: Duane Eddy
headline: Duane Eddy, Whose Twang Changed Rock ’n’ Roll, Dies at 86
abstract: A self-taught electric guitar virtuoso, he influenced a generation of musicians. One of them, John Fogerty, called him rock’s first guitar god.

name: Olga Fikotova Connolly
profession: Olympian in a Cold War Romance
headline: Olga Fikotova Connolly, Olympian in a Cold War Romance, Dies at 91
abstract: She was from Czechoslovakia. He was from the U.S. And after meeting at the 1956 Games and winning gold medals, they married. Love had breached the iron curtain.

name: Richard Tandy
headline: Richard Tandy, Keyboardist for Electric Light Orchestra, Dies at 76
abstract: He helped shape the band’s futuristic sound, which blended Beatles-esque pop with orchestral arrangements.

name: Peggy Mellon Hitchcock
headline: Peggy Mellon Hitchcock, Who Helped Timothy Leary Turn On, Dies at 90
abstract: She was an enthusiastic supporter of the counterculture. And when she suggested that her brothers rent Mr. Leary a mansion, she made psychedelic history.

name: Frank Wakefield
headline: Frank Wakefield, Who Expanded the Mandolin’s Range, Dies at 89
abstract: A bluegrass innovator, he recorded numerous albums as a leader, and his list of collaborators included both Leonard Bernstein and Jerry Garcia.

name: Robert Oxnam
profession: China Scholar Beset by Multiple Personalities
headline: Robert Oxnam, China Scholar Beset by Multiple Personalities, Dies at 81
abstract: Through psychotherapy, recounted in a memoir, he learned that he had 11 personalities, or fractured parts of his identity. One of them told of childhood abuse.

name: Larry Young
headline: Larry Young, Who Studied the Chemistry of Love, Dies at 56
abstract: Professor Young’s experiments with prairie voles revealed what poets never could: how the brain processes that fluttering feeling in the heart.

name: Nancy Schuster
headline: Nancy Schuster, Crossword Champion, Creator and Editor, Dies at 90
abstract: A dedicated cruciverbalist, she won the first American Crossword Puzzle Tournament in 1978. She went on to test and proofread puzzles for The New York Times.

name: Joel Conarroe
profession: Hub of the New York Literary Wheel
headline: Joel Conarroe, ‘Hub of the New York Literary Wheel,’ Dies at 89
abstract: An influential arts administrator and educator, he was a trusted confidant to countless writers, notably Philip Roth.

name: Min Matheson
headline: Overlooked No More: Min Matheson, Labor Leader Who Faced Down Mobsters
abstract: As director of the International Ladies’ Garment Workers’ Union, she fought for better working wages and conditions while wresting control from the mob.

name: C.J. Sansom
profession: Mystery Novelist Drawn to Tudor England
headline: C.J. Sansom, Mystery Novelist Drawn to Tudor England, Dies at 71
abstract: He wrote a popular series of books revolving around a hunchbacked detective, Shardlake, whose troubles echo the author’s experiences of childhood bullying.

name: Frank Stella
profession: Towering Artist and Master of Reinvention
headline: Frank Stella, Towering Artist and Master of Reinvention, Dies at 87
abstract: He moved American art away from Abstract Expressionism toward cool minimalism. His explorations of color and form were endlessly discussed and constantly on exhibit.

name: Barbara O. Jones
headline: Barbara O. Jones, Actress Who Brought Black Cinema to Life, Dies at 82
abstract: Her arresting roles in movies like “Bush Mama” and “Daughters of the Dust” helped shape a generation of independent filmmakers.

name: Peter Oosterhuis
headline: Peter Oosterhuis, British Golfer Turned Broadcaster, Dies at 75
abstract: For a time he was one of Europe’s best golfers, winning 20 tournaments, before moving into TV, offering commentary for the Golf Channel and CBS Sports.

name: Jerome Rothenberg
headline: Jerome Rothenberg, Who Heard Poetry Beyond the West, Dies at 92
abstract: His anthology “Technicians of the Sacred” included a range of non-Western work and was beloved by, among others, rock stars like Jim Morrison and Nick Cave.

name: Laurent Cantet
headline: Laurent Cantet Is Dead at 63: His Films Explored France’s Undersides
abstract: His acclaimed “The Class” walked a provocative line between documentary and fiction. In that film and others, he explored the inescapable traps of late-stage capitalism.

name: Bernard Hill
profession: Actor in Titanic and Lord of the Rings
headline: Bernard Hill, Actor in ‘Titanic’ and ‘Lord of the Rings,’ Dies at 79
abstract: With a stout frame, bushy whiskers and a weathered visage, he embodied men of authority facing down danger with weary stoicism.

name: Kris Hallenga
headline: Kris Hallenga, Who Urged Early Breast Cancer Screenings, Dies at 38
abstract: After being diagnosed when she was 23, she became determined to educate other young people about early detection.

name: Gayle McKinney-Griffith
headline: Gayle McKinney-Griffith, Dance Theater of Harlem Star, Dies at 74
abstract: A founding dancer with the groundbreaking company, she served not only as a principal dancer but also as its first ballet mistress.

name: Lesley Hazleton
headline: Lesley Hazleton, Writer Who Tackled Religion and Fast Cars, Dies at 78
abstract: Born in England and raised Jewish, she became agnostic, writing books about her own lack of faith, the prophet Muhammad and her time as a car columnist.

name: Kim Ki-Nam
profession: Chief Propagandist in North Korea for Decades
headline: Kim Ki-Nam, Chief Propagandist in North Korea for Decades, Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Kim, who served under all three generations of the country’s ruling family, was likened to Joseph Goebbels, Nazi Germany’s propaganda minister.

name: Judy Devlin Hashman
headline: Judy Devlin Hashman, Record-Holding Badminton Champion, Dies at 88
abstract: She won 10 singles titles at the prestigious all-England championships.

name: Steve Albini
profession: Studio Master of 90s Rock and Beyond
headline: Steve Albini, Studio Master of ’90s Rock and Beyond, Dies at 61
abstract: A musician and audio engineer, he helped define the sound of alternative rock while becoming an outspoken critic of the music industry.

name: Milton Diamond
profession: Sexologist and Advocate for Intersex Babies
headline: Milton Diamond, Sexologist and Advocate for Intersex Babies, Dies at 90
abstract: He pushed back against doctors who recommended surgery on infants born with ambiguous genitalia, arguing for acceptance of diversity.

name: Dick Rutan
profession: Flew Around the World Without Refueling
headline: Dick Rutan, Who Flew Around the World Without Refueling, Dies at 85
abstract: His nine-day voyage, in a plane designed by his brother that resembled a child’s glider but had wings longer than a Boeing 727’s, made aviation history.

name: Pete McCloskey
headline: Pete McCloskey, Republican Who Tried to Unseat Nixon, Is Dead at 96
abstract: An antiwar California congressman, he defeated Shirley Temple Black in a special election before launching a long-shot bid for the 1972 G.O.P. nomination.

name: Barbara Stauffacher Solomon
headline: Barbara Stauffacher Solomon, Pioneer of Supergraphics, Dies at 95
abstract: Trained as a ballet dancer, painter and graphic designer, she was at the forefront of a movement that upended design and architecture with bold graphics.

name: Herbert Pardes
profession: Steered the Growth of a Giant Hospital
headline: Herbert Pardes, Who Steered the Growth of a Giant Hospital, Dies at 89
abstract: A psychiatrist, he ran New York-Presbyterian after a landmark merger, improving its patient care and finances and raising money to expand its footprint across the region.

name: Bernard Pivot
profession: Host of Influential French TV Show on Books
headline: Bernard Pivot, Host of Influential French TV Show on Books, Dies at 89
abstract: For 15 years, French viewers watched Mr. Pivot on his weekly show, “Apostrophes,” to decide what to read next.

name: Dennis Thompson
profession: Drummer and Last Remaining Member of the MC5
headline: Dennis Thompson, Drummer and Last Remaining Member of the MC5, Dies at 75
abstract: He brought his hard-hitting style to the band, which helped lay the foundation of American punk rock and is set to be inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame.

name: Bill Holman
headline: Bill Holman, Whose Arrangements Shaped West Coast Jazz, Dies at 96
abstract: His economical, linear writing helped define the sound of Stan Kenton’s band. He also led his own 16-piece ensemble for many decades.

name: Jim Simons
headline: Jim Simons, Math Genius Who Conquered Wall Street, Dies at 86
abstract: Using advanced computers, he went from M.I.T. professor to multibillionaire. His Medallion fund had 66 percent average annual returns for decades.

name: David Shapiro
profession: Gained Fame in Poetry and Protest
headline: David Shapiro, Who Gained Fame in Poetry and Protest, Dies at 77
abstract: A renowned member of the New York School of poets, he also found accidental notoriety when he was photographed during the 1968 uprising at Columbia University.

name: Ilon Specht
profession: Empowered Women With Im Worth It Ad
headline: Ilon Specht, Who Empowered Women With ‘I’m Worth It’ Ad, Dies at 81
abstract: She came up with the feminist campaign, for a hair color product, when challenging the notions of men at her ad agency.

name: Nancy Neveloff Dubler
headline: Nancy Neveloff Dubler, Mediator for Life’s Final Moments, Dies at 82
abstract: A bioethicist, she pioneered bedside methods for helping patients, their families and doctors deal with anguishing life-and-death decisions in a high-tech age.

name: Mary Wells Lawrence
headline: Mary Wells Lawrence, High-Profile Advertising Pioneer, Dies at 95
abstract: She was the first woman to own and run a major national advertising agency. Her company, Wells Rich Greene, was best known for the “I ♥ NY” campaign.

name: Eberhard Kornfeld
headline: Eberhard Kornfeld, Art Dealer, Collector and Historian, Is Dead at 99
abstract: Ensconced in a 15th-century Swiss manor house, he became an expert on the old masters and later tangled with heirs of a collector killed by the Nazis.

name: Jeannie Epper
headline: Jeannie Epper, Stunt Double to the Stars, Is Dead at 83
abstract: Her first stunt was riding a horse bareback down a cliff when she was 9. She went on to soar on the hit TV series “Wonder Woman” and in many other places.

name: Sam Rubin
profession: TV Anchor Known for His Hollywood Reporting
headline: Sam Rubin, TV Anchor Known for His Hollywood Reporting, Dies at 64
abstract: He began at the Los Angeles television news station KTLA in 1991 and went on to become a staple of morning viewing through his interviews with celebrities.

name: Roger Corman
headline: Roger Corman, 98, Dies; Prolific Master of Low-Budget Cinema
abstract: He had hundreds of horror, science fiction and crime films to his credit. He also helped start the careers of Martin Scorsese, Francis Ford Coppola and many others.

name: Alex Hassilev
headline: Alex Hassilev, the Last of the Original Limeliters, Dies at 91
abstract: The trio’s witty, urbane arrangements made it one of the top acts of the early-1960s folk music revival. His gift for languages helped.

name: Susan Backlinie
headline: Susan Backlinie, Swimmer Who Was the First Victim in ‘Jaws,’ Dies at 77
abstract: Ms. Backlinie, a stuntwoman, appeared in the terrifying opening scene of the 1975 blockbuster in which a great white shark attacks.

name: Christopher Edley Jr.
profession: Civil Rights Expert Heard by Presidents
headline: Christopher Edley Jr., Civil Rights Expert Heard by Presidents, Dies at 71
abstract: He pivoted between serving as an adviser to the Carter, Clinton and Obama White Houses and teaching at Harvard and Berkeley, where he was the law school dean.

name: David Sanborn
headline: David Sanborn, Saxophonist Who Defied Pigeonholing, Dies at 78
abstract: He was best known as a jazz musician, but his shimmering sound was also heard on classic albums by David Bowie, Stevie Wonder and Bruce Springsteen.

name: Alice Munro
profession: Nobel Laureate and Master of the Short Story
headline: Alice Munro, Nobel Laureate and Master of the Short Story, Dies at 92
abstract: Her stories were widely considered to be without equal, a mixture of ordinary people and extraordinary themes.

name: Daniel Kramer
headline: Daniel Kramer, Who Photographed Bob Dylan’s Rise, Dies at 91
abstract: For 366 days, he captured intimate images of the singer-songwriter as he changed the look and sound of the 1960s.

name: John Barbata
headline: John Barbata, Drummer With Marquee Bands, Is Dead at 79
abstract: He played with Jefferson Airplane and Crosby, Stills, Nash & Young. The first song he recorded with the Turtles was “Happy Together.”

name: Katherine Porter
headline: Katherine Porter, Painter of Intuitive Expressionism, Dies at 82
abstract: Her palette was entirely personal, making contact with the natural world just long enough to spirit viewers back into her own psychology.

name: A.T. Ariyaratne
profession: Hero in Sri Lanka for Helping the Poor
headline: A.T. Ariyaratne, a Hero in Sri Lanka for Helping the Poor, Dies at 92
abstract: He built Sarvodaya, an organization that battled dismal living conditions in his country’s villages and championed peace and mediation during a vicious civil war.

name: Barry Romo
headline: Barry Romo, Decorated Vet Who Turned Against the VietnamWar, Dies at 76
abstract: After serving as an officer, he became a leading antiwar activist. In 1971, he tossed away his medals during a Washington protest demonstration.

name: Jack Quinn
profession: Lobbyist and White House Counsel for Clinton
headline: Jack Quinn, Lobbyist and White House Counsel for Clinton, Dies at 74
abstract: A prototypical Washington insider, he once said, “The hot air index is actually down when people like me go on vacation.”

name: J. Gary Cooper
headline: J. Gary Cooper, Pathbreaking Marine Leader, Is Dead at 87
abstract: He was the first Black officer to lead a Marine Corps infantry company into combat. He later became an Alabama state lawmaker and an assistant secretary of the Air Force.

name: Bill Hosokawa
headline: Overlooked No More: Bill Hosokawa, Journalist Who Chronicled Japanese American History
abstract: He fought prejudice and incarceration during World War II to lead a successful career, becoming one of the first editors of color at a metropolitan newspaper.

name: Jasper White
headline: Jasper White, Chef Who Lifted New England Cuisine, Dies at 69
abstract: At Restaurant Jasper in the North End of Boston, and later with a small chain of family-friendly seafood establishments, he focused relentlessly on regional ingredients.

name: Samm-Art Williams
headline: Samm-Art Williams, Playwright, Producer and Actor, Dies at 78
abstract: He challenged racial barriers in Hollywood, was a producer of “The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air” and earned a Tony nomination for “Home,” a paean to his Southern roots.

name: Robert Dennard
headline: Robert Dennard, IBM Inventor Whose Chip Changed Computing, Dies at 91
abstract: He invented DRAM, the technology that allowed for the faster and higher-capacity memory storage that is the basis for modern computing.

name: Alta
profession: Irreverent Feminist Poet and Small-Press Pioneer
headline: Alta, Irreverent Feminist Poet and Small-Press Pioneer, Dies at 81
abstract: She wrote lusty work about her life. She also started what may have been America’s first feminist press, Shameless Hussy, in her garage.

name: Elba Cabrera
profession: Patron of Puerto Rican Culture in New York
headline: Elba Cabrera, Patron of Puerto Rican Culture in New York, Dies at 90
abstract: Nurturing artists and performers, she was the last of Las Tres Hermanas, three sisters revered for galvanizing arts, education and social programs in the Latino community.

name: Jon Urbanchek
headline: Jon Urbanchek, Who Led Swimmers to Olympic Glory, Dies at 87
abstract: He coached the University of Michigan to 13 Big Ten Conference titles and a national championship. Overall, his swimmers won 21 medals at the Summer Olympics.

name: Cyril H. Wecht
profession: Coroner Cast Doubt on Kennedy Assassination
headline: Cyril H. Wecht, 93, Dies; Coroner Cast Doubt on Kennedy Assassination
abstract: A widely respected forensic expert and frequent TV presence, he was also a powerful figure in Pennsylvania Democratic politics.

name: Tony Pigg
profession: Celebrated D.J. of FMs Golden Age
headline: Tony Pigg, Celebrated D.J. of FM’s Golden Age, Dies at 85
abstract: Arising from the free-form San Francisco radio scene of the 1960s, he became an influential voice on the powerhouse WPLJ in New York.

name: Dabney Coleman
headline: Dabney Coleman, Actor Audiences Loved to Hate, Is Dead at 92
abstract: In movies like “9 to 5” and “Tootsie” and on TV shows like “Buffalo Bill,” he turned the portrayal of egomaniacal louts into a fine art.

name: Phil Wiggins
headline: Phil Wiggins, Virtuoso of the Blues Harmonica, Is Dead at 69
abstract: First as half of the duo Cephas and Wiggins and later on his own, he was one of the best-known musicians playing the style known as the Piedmont blues.

name: Rex Murphy
profession: Dominant Pundit on the Right in Canada
headline: Rex Murphy, a Dominant Pundit on the Right in Canada, Dies at 77
abstract: In newspaper columns and on radio and TV, he was his country’s “premier provocateur,” gaining a wide audience for his conservative attacks on liberals and environmentalists.

name: Moorhead C. Kennedy Jr.
headline: Moorhead C. Kennedy Jr., 93, Dies; Hostage Who Chided Foreign Policy
abstract: A Foreign Service officer, he was one of 52 hostages seized in Iran and held for 444 days. He later challenged the U.S. government to reshape its diplomacy with the Islamic world.

name: Bud Anderson
profession: Last of World War IIs Triple Ace Pilots
headline: Bud Anderson, Last of World War II’s ‘Triple Ace’ Pilots, Dies at 102
abstract: He single-handedly shot down 16 enemy planes in dogfights over Europe. After the war, he became one of America’s top test pilots during the “Right Stuff” era.

name: Alice Stewart
headline: Alice Stewart, a CNN Political Commentator, Is Dead at 58
abstract: She had appeared onscreen as a conservative voice since the 2016 presidential race. A political strategist, she had worked for Republican presidential candidates.

name: Dolores Rosedale
profession: Found Fame as a Game-Show Sidekick
headline: Dolores Rosedale, Who Found Fame as a Game-Show Sidekick, Dies at 95
abstract: A model and actress known as Roxanne, she parlayed her modest role on “Beat the Clock” into magazine covers and the creation of a doll in her image.

name: Bruce Nordstrom
profession: Helped Lead His Familys Retail Empire
headline: Bruce Nordstrom, Who Helped Lead His Family’s Retail Empire, Dies at 90
abstract: Though he was the company’s president, he opted for joint leadership with family members as they made Nordstrom, starting as a string of shoe stores, into an international fashion retail brand.

name: Ebrahim Raisi
headline: Ebrahim Raisi, Iran’s President, Dies in Helicopter Crash at 63
abstract: The hard-line Shiite cleric was seen as a possible successor to Iran’s supreme leader. Mr. Raisi’s death comes at a moment of turbulence for a country facing a deepening conflict with Israel.

name: James Greenfield
headline: James Greenfield, Globe-Trotting Reporter and Times Editor, Dies at 99
abstract: He wrote about world affairs for Time magazine and worked at the State Department before becoming a senior editor at The New York Times in 1967.

name: Ivan F. Boesky
profession: Rogue Trader in 1980s Wall Street Scandal
headline: Ivan F. Boesky, Rogue Trader in 1980s Wall Street Scandal, Dies at 87
abstract: An inspiration for the Gordon Gekko character in the movie “Wall Street,” he made a fortune from insider trading before his downfall brought a crashing end to a decade of greed.

name: Jim Otto
headline: Jim Otto, Hall of Fame Raiders Center, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Despite his accomplishments on the field, he was remembered mostly for the many beatings his body absorbed, which left him in constant pain.

name: David Redden
profession: Brought Ingenuity to the Auction Block
headline: David Redden, Who Brought Ingenuity to the Auction Block, Dies at 75
abstract: He brought a P.T. Barnum-like showmanship to Sotheby’s, where he sold items like Babe Ruth’s bat and a research rover that had been left behind on the moon.

name: Paul Parkman
headline: Dr. Paul Parkman, Who Helped to Eliminate Rubella, Dies at 91
abstract: He also identified the virus, which can cause infants to be born with severe physical and mental impairments as well as causing miscarriages and stillbirths.

name: C. Gordon Bell
profession: Creator of a Personal Computer Prototype
headline: C. Gordon Bell, Creator of a Personal Computer Prototype, Dies at 89
abstract: It cost $18,000 when it was introduced in 1965, but it bridged the world between room-size mainframes and the modern desktop.

name: Frank Shrontz
profession: Led Boeing in the Last of Its Golden Years
headline: Frank Shrontz, 92, Dies; Led Boeing in the Last of Its Golden Years
abstract: Known for his leadership and his commitment to company culture, he left as chief executive in 1996, opening the door to a corporate makeover.

name: Shirley Conran
profession: Author Best Known for the Steamy Lace
headline: Shirley Conran, Author Best Known for the Steamy ‘Lace,’ Dies at 91
abstract: A divorced single mother, she started out to write a sex guide for schoolgirls and ended up with a tale of female autonomy that became a best-selling novel.

name: Joe Zucker
headline: Joe Zucker, Prolific Painter of Innumerable Styles, Dies at 82
abstract: His art, which he described as “conceptual and literal,” used a variety of materials, including cotton, wood and even squeegee handles.

name: Bob McCreadie
headline: Bob McCreadie, ‘the Master of Going Faster,’ Dies at 73
abstract: One of the winningest drivers in dirt racing history, he was a folk hero who cursed wildly, drove aggressively and crashed a lot.

name: Morgan Spurlock
profession: Documentarian Known for Super Size Me
headline: Morgan Spurlock, Documentarian Known for ‘Super Size Me,’ Dies at 53
abstract: His 2004 film followed Mr. Spurlock as he ate nothing but McDonald’s for a month. It was nominated for an Oscar, but it later came in for criticism.

name: Caleb Carr
headline: Caleb Carr, Author of Dark Histories, Dies at 68
abstract: His own dark history prompted him to write about and investigate the roots of violence, notably in his best-selling novel “The Alienist.”

name: Fred Roos
headline: Fred Roos, Casting Director and Coppola Collaborator, Dies at 89
abstract: Widely considered to have the best eye for talent in Hollywood, he shared the best-picture Oscar with Francis Ford Coppola for “The Godfather Part II.”

name: John Koerner
headline: John Koerner, Bluesman Who Inspired a Young Bob Dylan, Dies at 85
abstract: A spindly guitarist nicknamed Spider, Mr. Koerner was Mr. Dylan’s first friend in the scruffy world of Minneapolis bohemia where he learned about folk music.

name: Adele Faber
profession: Helped Change How Parents Talk to Children
headline: Adele Faber, 96, Who Helped Change How Parents Talk to Children, Dies
abstract: With her collaborator, Elaine Mazlish, she wrote “How to Talk So Kids Will Listen & Listen So Kids Will Talk” and other books that have endured as parenting bibles.

name: Michael Sugrue
profession: His Talks on Philosophy Were a YouTube Hit
headline: Michael Sugrue, 66, Dies; His Talks on Philosophy Were a YouTube Hit
abstract: After an academic career spent in near obscurity, he became an internet phenomenon during the pandemic by uploading talks he had given three decades earlier.

name: Grayson Murray
profession: Winner of Two PGA Tour Titles
headline: Grayson Murray, Winner of Two PGA Tour Titles, Dies at 30
abstract: Murray, who was outspoken about his depression and alcohol abuse, had begun a comeback after several volatile years, winning this year’s Sony Open in Hawaii.

name: Zack Norman
headline: Zack Norman, Actor Who Juggled Multiple Professions, Dies at 83
abstract: Best known for movies like “Romancing the Stone,” he also made a mark as a producer, a real estate developer and the butt of a Generation X-friendly television gag.

name: Richard Sherman
profession: Songwriter of Many Spoonfuls of Sugar
headline: Richard Sherman, Songwriter of Many Spoonfuls of Sugar, Dies at 95
