abstract: He and his brother, Robert, teamed up to write the songs for “Mary Poppins” and other Disney classics. They also gave the world “It’s a Small World (After All).”

name: Don Perlin
headline: Don Perlin, Comic Book Artist Who Found Success Late, Dies at 94
abstract: His Moon Knight was a hit in the 1970s, 30 years after he began his career. Bloodshot, another popular superhero, followed two decades later.

name: Sanford L. Smith
headline: Sanford L. Smith, Creator of Prestigious Art Fairs, Dies at 84
abstract: Over four decades, he produced more than 150 events. Some dealers reported selling more in a weekend at a Smith fair than in a year in their galleries.

name: Bill Walton
profession: N.B.A. Hall of Famer and Broadcasting Star
headline: Bill Walton, N.B.A. Hall of Famer and Broadcasting Star, Dies at 71
abstract: He won championships in high school, college (U.C.L.A.) and the pros (Trail Blazers and Celtics) before turning to TV as a talkative game analyst in the college ranks.

name: Stanley Goldstein
profession: Helped Make CVS a Pharmacy Giant
headline: Stanley Goldstein, Who Helped Make CVS a Pharmacy Giant, Dies at 89
abstract: The small chain that he, a brother and a third partner opened in 1963 had become the nation’s largest by the time he retired as its chief executive three decades later.

name: Sue Johnson
headline: Sue Johnson, Psychologist Who Took a Scientific View of Love, Dies at 76
abstract: She believed the bond between adults was as sustaining as that between parent and child, and developed a therapy to strengthen and repair broken relationships.

name: Richard Ellis
headline: Richard Ellis, 86, Dies; Artist Whose Works Included a Museum’s Whale
abstract: Once called the “poet laureate” of deep-sea creatures, he melded science with art in paintings, books and a notable life-size installation in New York.

name: Susanne Page
profession: Took Rare Photos of the Hopi and Navajo
headline: Susanne Page, Who Took Rare Photos of the Hopi and Navajo, Dies at 86
abstract: She was the first photographer allowed to document life among the Hopi, in the Southwest, since the early 20th century. Her work appeared in books and magazines.

name: Barry Kemp
headline: Barry Kemp, Who Unearthed Insights About Ancient Egypt, Dies at 84
abstract: An archaeologist, he wrote widely on everyday life under the pharaohs and did much of his fieldwork at Amarna, considered the Egyptian version of Pompeii.

name: Bette Nash
headline: Bette Nash, World’s Longest-Serving Flight Attendant, Is Dead at 88
abstract: A Guinness record-holder, she started flying in 1957, and never stopped. Her regular route from Washington to Boston was nicknamed the Nash Dash.

name: Albert S. Ruddy
headline: Albert S. Ruddy, Producer Who Won Oscar for ‘The Godfather,’ Dies at 94
abstract: A creator of the sitcom “Hogan’s Heroes,” he went on to win a second Academy Award for “Million Dollar Baby,” the boxing film starring Hilary Swank and Clint Eastwood.

name: Hansa Mehta
profession: Fought for Womens Equality in India and Beyond
headline: Overlooked No More: Hansa Mehta, Who Fought for Women’s Equality in India and Beyond
abstract: For Mehta, women’s rights were human rights, and in all her endeavors she took women’s participation in public and political realms to new heights.

name: Sam Butcher
headline: Sam Butcher, Who Gave the World Precious Moments, Dies at 85
abstract: His childlike porcelain characters thrilled and inspired generations of collectors. They also made him a millionaire.

name: Yael Dayan
headline: Yael Dayan, Israeli Writer, Politician and Daughter of War Hero, Dies at 85
abstract: She was hailed for her books and admired for promoting women’s rights. But her support for a two-state solution to the Palestinian conflict angered many.

name: Robert Pickton
headline: Robert Pickton, Notorious Canadian Serial Killer, Dies at 74
abstract: Convicted in the murder of six women (though he boasted of killing many more), he died of unspecified injuries after being assaulted in prison.

name: U Tin Oo
headline: U Tin Oo, Embattled Pro-Democracy Leader in Myanmar, Dies at 97
abstract: A powerful figure in his country, he helped found its main opposition party. “I had to face up to the harm I did to people when I served in the army,” he said.

name: Larry Bensky
headline: Larry Bensky, a Fixture of Left-Wing Radio, Is Dead at 87
abstract: A self-described activist-journalist, he was for many years the national affairs correspondent for the community-focused Pacifica network.

name: Terry Robards
profession: Lifted Fine Wines in America as a Times Critic
headline: Terry Robards, 84, Dies; Lifted Fine Wines in America as a Times Critic
abstract: In columns and notably “The New York Times Book of Wine,” he introduced Americans to European and premium domestic varieties in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Margot Benacerraf
headline: Margot Benacerraf, Award-Winning Venezuelan Documentarian, Dies at 97
abstract: She made only two films, but her “Araya,” a rumination on the daily rituals of salt-mine laborers, became an enduring work of Latin American cinema.

name: Janis Paige
profession: Star of Broadways The Pajama Game
headline: Janis Paige, Star of Broadway’s ‘The Pajama Game,’ Is Dead at 101
abstract: She first made her mark in the all-star 1944 movie “Hollywood Canteen” before finding acclaim on the musical stage. Movie and TV roles followed.

name: Marquis
profession: Member of Rap Group 2 Live Crew
headline: Brother Marquis, Member of Rap Group 2 Live Crew, Dies
abstract: Born Mark Ross, he was a well-known member of the group, which fueled a debate about artistic freedom.

name: Nonny Hogrogian
headline: Nonny Hogrogian, 92, Honored Illustrator of Children’s Books, Dies
abstract: A two-time Caldecott Medal winner, she brought multiculturalism to children’s literature by evoking her Armenian heritage.

name: Rob Burrow
headline: Rob Burrow, Rugby Star and A.L.S. Campaigner, Dies at 41
abstract: The “Mighty Atom” enjoyed a glittering professional career in Britain before gaining more acclaim for his charity efforts after a diagnosis of motor neuron disease.

name: Ron Edmonds
profession: Camera Captured the Shooting of Reagan
headline: Ron Edmonds, 77, Whose Camera Captured the Shooting of Reagan, Dies
abstract: Working for The Associated Press, he won a Pulitzer Prize for his sequence of photos showing the president being struck by a bullet while three others fell wounded.

name: Parnelli Jones
profession: Champion Auto Racer and Record Setter
headline: Parnelli Jones, Champion Auto Racer and Record Setter, Is Dead at 90
abstract: He was one of the greatest drivers of the 1960s and ’70s, winning six Indy races and four major NASCAR events while setting speed marks.

name: Erich Anderson
profession: Actor in Friday the 13th and Felicity
headline: Erich Anderson, Actor in ‘Friday the 13th’ and ‘Felicity,’ Dies at 67
abstract: Mr. Anderson had a breakout role in “Friday the 13th” and went on to appear in more than 300 TV episodes, including a recurring role as the father on “Felicity.”

name: Bob Kelley
profession: Made the Kelley Blue Book an Authority on Cars
headline: Bob Kelley, Who Made the Kelley Blue Book an Authority on Cars, Dies at 96
abstract: He knew all the data that went into determining a vehicle’s price, but he insisted that it was as much an art as it was a science.

name: Bertien van Manen
headline: Bertien van Manen, a Roving Photographer of Daily Life, Dies at 89
abstract: Inspired by Robert Frank’s book “The Americans,” she traveled to China, Russia and the coal mines of Kentucky to capture intimate glimpses of everyday routines.

name: Larry Allen
headline: Larry Allen, Dominant N.F.L. Lineman, Dies at 52
abstract: Even on the star-studded Dallas Cowboys roster of the 1990s, he stood out with his head-turning strength and bone-rattling pancake blocks.

name: T.D. Allman
profession: Globe-Trotting Journalist With a Pointed View
headline: T.D. Allman, Globe-Trotting Journalist With a Pointed View, Dies at 79
abstract: Reporting from more than 80 countries, he combined close observation with sharp conclusions about misdeeds or abuse of power. He was an author as well.

name: Harry Roland
headline: Harry Roland, ‘The World Trade Center Man,’ Dies at 70
abstract: Within months of the terrorist attacks of Sept. 11, 2001, and continuing almost until his death, he was a street orator hollering about that day’s loss and destruction.

name: H. Bruce Franklin
profession: Scholar Fired for His Antiwar Views
headline: H. Bruce Franklin, Scholar Fired for His Antiwar Views, Is Dead at 90
abstract: A cultural historian, he was dismissed by Stanford over his opposition to the Vietnam War, a stance that became a cause célèbre of academic freedom.

name: Jeannette Charles
headline: Jeannette Charles, Who Doubled for the Queen, Is Dead at 96
abstract: She bore a startling resemblance to Elizabeth II. In “The Naked Gun” and other movies, and in comedy sketches on TV, she wore the crown lightly.

name: William A. Anders
profession: Flew on First Manned Orbit of the Moon
headline: William A. Anders, 90, Dies; Flew on First Manned Orbit of the Moon
abstract: During the 1968 Apollo 8 mission, his color photograph of an emerging Earth, known as “Earthrise,” became an icon and driving force for the environmental movement.

name: Jürgen Moltmann
headline: Jürgen Moltmann, Theologian Who Confronted Auschwitz, Is Dead at 98
abstract: He drew on his experiences as a German soldier during World War II to construct transformative ideas about God, Jesus and salvation.

name: Sigmund Rolat
profession: Used His Wealth to Memorialize Polish Jews
headline: Sigmund Rolat, Who Used His Wealth to Memorialize Polish Jews, Dies at 93
abstract: A Holocaust survivor and a shipping financier, he returned to his home country, where his parents and brother perished, to help build a museum and other memorials.

name: Chet Walker
headline: Chet Walker, N.B.A. Champion and Movie Producer, Dies at 84
abstract: A vital member of the 1966-67 champion Philadelphia 76ers, he later produced a TV series based on the life on the point guard Isiah Thomas’s mother.

name: Jean-Philippe Allard
headline: Jean-Philippe Allard, Jazz Producer and Musicians’ Advocate, Dies at 67
abstract: He called himself a “professional listener,” and he tended to develop lifelong relationships with the artists he worked with.

name: Debby Lee Cohen
headline: Debby Lee Cohen, Who Helped Prune Plastic From Schools, Dies at 64
abstract: Her successful campaign against foam lunch trays in New York City led to similar city and statewide bans — and taught a group of fifth graders how to take on City Hall.

name: David Boaz
headline: David Boaz, a Leading Voice of Libertarianism, Dies at 70
abstract: At the Cato Institute, he argued against government interference in Americans’ lives, including policing their drug use, and supported legal equality for gay people.

name: Morrie Markoff
profession: Listed as Oldest Man in the U.S
headline: Morrie Markoff, Listed as Oldest Man in the U.S., Dies at 110
abstract: A rare supercentenarian, he remained remarkably lucid after 11 decades, even maintaining a blog. His brain has been donated for research on what’s known as super-aging.

name: Norman Carol
profession: Violinist in Historic Concert in China
headline: Norman Carol, Violinist in Historic Concert in China, Is Dead at 95
abstract: The concertmaster and first-chair violinist with the Philadelphia Orchestra for decades, he took part in a diplomatic breakthrough in 1973 with concerts in Mao Zedong’s Beijing.

name: Jerry West
headline: Jerry West, One of Basketball’s Greatest Players, Dies at 86
abstract: He was a sharpshooting, high-scoring Hall of Fame guard for the Lakers and later an executive with the team. His image became the N.B.A.’s logo.

name: Françoise Hardy
headline: Françoise Hardy, Moody French Pop Star, Dies at 80
abstract: With hit songs and an understated personality, she incarnated a 1960s cool still treasured by the French.

name: Fumihiko Maki
headline: Fumihiko Maki, Honored Architect of Understated Buildings, Dies at 95
abstract: A Pritzker Prize winner, he designed notable projects in his native Japan and in the U.S., including 4 World Trade Center and the M.I.T. Media Lab’s new home.

name: Howard Fineman
profession: Veteran Political Journalist and TV Pundit
headline: Howard Fineman, Veteran Political Journalist and TV Pundit, Dies at 75
abstract: From his beginnings with a daily newspaper, he moved easily through Newsweek magazine to cable news and, later, to the frontiers of online journalism.

name: Harrison White
headline: Harrison White, Groundbreaking (and Inscrutable) Sociologist, Dies at 94
abstract: A theoretical physicist-turned-sociologist, he upended his field by focusing on social networks to explain how society works. His writing was compared to James Joyce’s.

name: Tony Lo Bianco
headline: Tony Lo Bianco, ‘French Connection’ Actor, Dies at 87
abstract: Once labeled a “natural-born heavy,” he shined onscreen and especially onstage, securing a Tony nomination and winning an Obie Award.

name: Akira Endo
headline: Akira Endo, Scholar of Statins That Reduce Heart Disease, Dies at 90
abstract: The Japanese biochemist found in the 1970s that cholesterol-lowering drugs lowered the level of LDL, or “bad” cholesterol, in the blood.

name: Christophe Deloire
headline: Christophe Deloire, Who Fought for Threatened Journalists, Dies at 53
abstract: As the leader and spokesman for Reporters Without Borders, he rescued some, sought refuge for others and lobbied for pluralism in the press.

name: Warren Winiarski
headline: Warren Winiarski, Whose Fledgling Cabernet Bested the French, Dies at 95
abstract: His $6 bottle of Napa Valley cabernet won a historic tasting in Paris in 1976, astonishing connoisseurs and putting his Stag’s Leap winery on the map.

name: Frank Carroll
profession: Coached Michelle Kwan and Other Skating Stars
headline: Frank Carroll, 85, Dies; Coached Michelle Kwan and Other Skating Stars
abstract: His roster of students also included Linda Fratianne, but he did not coach an Olympic gold medalist until Evan Lysacek won in 2010.

name: Moshe Kotlarsky
headline: Rabbi Moshe Kotlarsky, 75, Dies; Expanded Chabad’s Global Reach
abstract: Chabad, one observer said, is “in more places in the world than any other Hasidic group and most visible to the world because of their outreach — largely thanks to Kotlarsky.”

name: Patrick Gottsch
profession: Found Rural America Fertile Ground for TV
headline: Patrick Gottsch, 70, Who Found Rural America Fertile Ground for TV, Dies
abstract: After a career as a satellite dish installer, he found success with RFD-TV, a 24-hour cable channel aimed at farmers and ranchers.

name: Mark James
profession: Writer of Suspicious Minds and Other Songs
headline: Mark James, Writer of ‘Suspicious Minds’ and Other Songs, Is Dead at 83
abstract: His songs became hits for Elvis Presley, Willie Nelson, Brenda Lee and many other artists. They were also heard on movie soundtracks.

name: Geneviève de Galard
profession: French Angel of Dien Bien Phu
headline: Geneviève de Galard, French ‘Angel’ of Dien Bien Phu, Dies at 99
abstract: A nurse, she tended to the wounded as the French were under fateful attack by Viet Minh forces in 1954. Hailed in France and the U.S., she was given a ticker-tape parade down Broadway.

name: Remo Saraceni
profession: Inventor of the Walking Piano Seen in Big
headline: Remo Saraceni, 89, Dies; Inventor of the Walking Piano Seen in ‘Big’
abstract: His keyboard, which became famous after Tom Hanks melodiously hopped on it, displayed Mr. Saraceni’s vision of technology powered by “people energy.”

name: Johnny Canales
headline: Johnny Canales, Influential Mexican TV Host, Dies at 81
abstract: He was known for introducing new musical acts to a wide audience, including Selena Quintanilla, whose appearance on his show in 1985 was one of her first live TV performances.

name: Martin Starger
profession: Influential Shaper of TV and Movies
headline: Martin Starger, Influential Shaper of TV and Movies, Dies at 92
abstract: In his decade at ABC, long the doormat network in prime time, he helped guide it toward the No. 1 spot. He later produced “Nashville” and won an Emmy for “Friendly Fire.”

name: John Wilmerding
profession: Helped Give American Art an Identity
headline: John Wilmerding, Who Helped Give American Art an Identity, Dies at 86
abstract: American paintings were largely overlooked and undervalued until he came along. A scholar, curator and collector, he oversaw important exhibitions over the last 50 years.

name: Edward Stone
headline: Edward Stone, 88, Physicist Who Oversaw Voyager Missions, Is Dead
abstract: He helped send the twin spacecraft on their way in 1977. Decades and billions of miles later, they are still probing — “Earth’s ambassadors to the stars,” as he put it.

name: Nick Mavar
headline: Nick Mavar, Fisherman and ‘Deadliest Catch’ Star, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Mavar, who ran a fishing operation in Alaska, starred in the reality television show for 16 years and captained his own boat.

name: Lorenza Böttner
headline: Overlooked No More: Lorenza Böttner, Transgender Artist Who Found Beauty in Disability
abstract: Böttner, whose specialty was self-portraiture, celebrated her armless body in paintings she created with her mouth and feet while dancing in public.

name: Ben Vautier
headline: Ben Vautier, Artist Whose Specialty Was Provocation, Dies at 88
abstract: A core member of the anti-art movement Fluxus, he died by suicide hours after the death of his wife of 60 years.

name: Lynn Conway
headline: Lynn Conway, Computing Pioneer and Transgender Advocate, Dies at 86
abstract: She made significant contributions at IBM, but she lost her job because of her conviction that she inhabited the wrong body. She later fought for transgender rights.

name: John Everett Benson
headline: John Everett Benson, Who Chiseled John F. Kennedy’s Grave, Dies at 84
abstract: A master of the ancient and exacting art of carving into rock, he was 25 when he began his first major commission, at Arlington National Cemetery.

name: Paul Pressler
headline: Paul Pressler, Disgraced Christian Conservative Leader, Dies at 94
abstract: A former judge, he helped steer the Southern Baptist Convention to the right. But at least seven men accused him of sexual abuse.

name: James Kent
headline: James Kent, Chef Who Was Building a Restaurant Empire, Dies at 45
abstract: He had opened two restaurants and a cocktail bar in downtown Manhattan, and he was preparing for a big expansion backed by LeBron James.

name: William H. Donaldson
headline: William H. Donaldson, Wall St. Lion Who Led the S.E.C., Dies at 93
abstract: He co-founded D.L.J., the first securities firm to offer shares to the public. As S.E.C. chairman, he pressed for a stronger watchdog role after a series of accounting scandals.

name: George R. Nethercutt Jr.
headline: George R. Nethercutt Jr., Who Ousted a House Speaker, Dies at 79
abstract: He defeated Thomas S. Foley of Washington State in the 1994 Republican midterm sweep. It was the first time since the Civil War-era that voters rejected a House speaker.

name: Angela Bofill
profession: R&B Hitmaker With a Silky Voice
headline: Angela Bofill, R&B Hitmaker With a Silky Voice, Dies at 70
abstract: Starting in the late 1970s, she scored multiple hit singles, including “This Time I’ll Be Sweeter” and “I Try,” but a pair of strokes in the 2000s ended her career.

name: Anouk Aimée
profession: Enigmatic Star of A Man and a Woman
headline: Anouk Aimée, Enigmatic Star of ‘A Man and a Woman,’ Dies at 92
abstract: The French actress had already made an impression in international film when she appeared in Claude Lelouch’s 1966 romance, a role that earned her an Oscar nomination.

name: Neil Goldschmidt
headline: Neil Goldschmidt, Portland Mayor Who Abused Teenager, Dies at 83
abstract: While he was reviving Portland, Ore., as a vibrant, pedestrian-friendly city, he was also sexually abusing a teenage girl over three years, he later admitted.

name: Bob Schul
headline: Bob Schul, a Singular U.S. Olympian in the 5,000-Meter Race, Dies at 86
abstract: His remarkable sprint in the final yards on a muddy track in the 1964 Games in Tokyo made him the only American ever to win the gold medal in that event.

name: Sarah Mandel
headline: Sarah Mandel, Therapist Who Told Her ‘Trauma Narrative,’ Dies at 42
abstract: She received a diagnosis of Stage 4 breast cancer late in her second pregnancy and described her experience in a book, “Little Earthquakes: A Memoir.”

name: Elinor Fuchs
profession: Leading Scholar of the American Stage
headline: Elinor Fuchs, a Leading Scholar of the American Stage, Is Dead at 91
abstract: As a journalist and later as a Yale professor, she provided the intellectual tools to help actors, directors and audiences understand challenging theatrical work.

name: Willie Mays
profession: Baseballs Electrifying Player of Power and Grace
headline: Willie Mays, Baseball’s Electrifying Player of Power and Grace, Is Dead at 93
abstract: Mays, the Say Hey Kid, was the game’s exuberant embodiment of the complete player. Some say he was the greatest of them all.

name: Ricardo M. Urbina
headline: Ricardo M. Urbina, Trailblazing Latino Judge in Capital, Dies at 78
abstract: Before being appointed to the bench in Washington, he was a track star who became a symbol of discrimination against Black athletes.

name: George Woodwell
headline: George Woodwell, 95, Influential Ecologist on Climate Change, Dies
abstract: The founder of the renowned Woods Hole Research Center in Massachusetts, he also helped shape U.S. policies on controlling toxic substances like DDT.

name: Barbara Gladstone
profession: Art Dealer With Global Reach and a Personal Touch
headline: Barbara Gladstone, 89, Dies; Art Dealer With Global Reach and a Personal Touch
abstract: An art world power, she represented more than 70 artists and estates and ran two large exhibition spaces in Manhattan as well as offshoots abroad.

name: Donald Sutherland
headline: Donald Sutherland, a Chameleon of a Movie Star, Dies at 88
abstract: In a wide-ranging career (from “M*A*S*H” to “Ordinary People” to “The Hunger Games”), he could be endearing in one role, menacing in another and just plain odd in a third.

name: Thomas J. McCormack
headline: Thomas J. McCormack Dies at 92; Transformed St. Martin’s Press
abstract: He turned “an insignificant trade house” into a powerhouse, publishing best sellers like “The Silence of the Lambs” and “All Creatures Great and Small.”

name: William Goines
headline: William Goines, First Black Navy SEAL, Dies at 87
abstract: He overcame segregation at home and in the military to serve three tours in Vietnam as a member of the storied special operations unit.

name: James Chance
headline: James Chance, No Wave and Punk-Funk Pioneer, Dies at 71
abstract: With the Contortions and James White and the Blacks, the songwriter and saxophonist set out to challenge musicians and stir up audiences.

name: Ángeles Flórez Peón
headline: Ángeles Flórez Peón, Spanish Civil War’s Last Militiawoman, Dies at 105
abstract: She was revered as an essential guardian of the country’s memory of war and repression long after the Franco dictatorship.

name: Nathan Hare
profession: Forceful Founder of First Black Studies Program
headline: Nathan Hare, 91, Forceful Founder of First Black Studies Program, Dies
abstract: Seeking to bring the ideas of Black power into the classroom — and coining the term “ethnic studies” — he clashed with a university as well as allies on the left.

name: Anthony O’Reilly
headline: Anthony O’Reilly, Flashy Irish Tycoon Who Led Unflashy Heinz, Dies at 88
abstract: He had success on the rugby pitch and in boardrooms, building a media empire and boosting Heinz’s profits, but his fortunes buckled in the global financial crisis.

name: Taylor Wily
profession: Hawaii Five-0 and Forgetting Sarah Marshall Actor
headline: Taylor Wily, ‘Hawaii Five-0’ and ‘Forgetting Sarah Marshall’ Actor, Dies at 55
abstract: He spent his early career as a professional sumo wrestler.

name: Ron Simons
headline: Ron Simons, Who Brought Black Stories to Broadway, Dies at 63
abstract: He left a career in tech and found success as a producer, winning four Tonys. His mission: staging productions about underrepresented communities.

name: Jeremy Tepper
headline: Jeremy Tepper, SiriusXM’s Longtime Alt-Country Impresario, Dies at 60
abstract: As a journalist, singer, label owner and radio producer, he fostered a community of musicians on the outskirts of Americana.

name: Silvano Marchetto
profession: Owner of Glitzy Greenwich Village Trattoria
headline: Silvano Marchetto, Owner of Glitzy Greenwich Village Trattoria, Dies at 77
abstract: Da Silvano was a celebrity hangout, drawing boldface names like Madonna, Barry Diller and Yoko Ono. It was often referred to as the downtown Elaine’s.

name: Frederick Crews
headline: Frederick Crews, Withering Critic of Freud’s Legacy, Dies at 91
abstract: A literary critic, essayist and author, he was a leading voice among revisionist skeptics who saw Freud as a charlatan and psychoanalysis as a pseudoscience.

name: Seth Binzer
headline: Seth Binzer, Crazy Town’s Lead Singer, ‘Shifty Shellshock,’ Dies at 49
abstract: He was the frontman for the rap-rock band Crazy Town, which was most known for the hit song “Butterfly.”

name: Eric Hazan
profession: Publisher and Historian on Frances Left
headline: Eric Hazan, Publisher and Historian on France’s Left, Dies at 87
abstract: He elevated many of France’s most provocative writers through his publishing house, La Fabrique, but he made his greatest mark as a politically engaged, and strolling, historian of Paris.

name: Sika Anoa’i
profession: W.W.E. Hall of Famer and Father of Roman Reigns
headline: Sika Anoa’i, W.W.E. Hall of Famer and Father of Roman Reigns, Dies at 79
abstract: He was part of the superstar tag team the Wild Samoans and a member of the dynasty of Samoan wrestlers that includes today’s biggest star, his son.

name: Tom Prasada-Rao
headline: Tom Prasada-Rao, Whose Song Elegized George Floyd, Dies at 66
abstract: His 2020 lament “$20 Bill” was covered by scores of artists and, a fellow musician said, might well be destined for the folk music canon.

name: Russell Morash
profession: This Old House and The French Chef Producer
headline: Russell Morash, ‘This Old House’ and ‘The French Chef’ Producer, Dies at 88
abstract: Hailed as a pioneer of D.I.Y. programming, he oversaw groundbreaking how-to shows on public television in the days before HGTV and YouTube.

name: Kaz Hosaka
profession: Led Two Poodles to Westminster Glory
headline: Kaz Hosaka, 65, Dies; Led Two Poodles to Westminster Glory
abstract: He began handling dogs in his native Japan and then became a poodle specialist, leading Spice and Sage to Best in Show victories.

name: Bill Cobbs
profession: Bodyguard and Night at the Museum Actor
headline: Bill Cobbs, ‘Bodyguard’ and ‘Night at the Museum’ Actor, Dies at 90
abstract: He was not a Hollywood household name. But his face was one anyone who watched TV or movies over the past several decades could recognize.

name: Shahjahan Bhuiya
headline: Shahjahan Bhuiya, Bangladeshi Executioner Turned TikTok Star, Is Dead
abstract: He hanged high-profile inmates in exchange for a reduction in his own robbery and murder sentences, and became a social media sensation after his release.

name: Kinky Friedman
profession: Musician and Humorist Slew Sacred Cows
headline: Kinky Friedman, 79, Dies; Musician and Humorist Slew Sacred Cows
abstract: He and his band, the Texas Jewboys, won acclaim for their satirical takes on American culture. He later wrote detective novels and ran for governor of Texas.

name: Buzz Cason
profession: Songwriter Best Known for Everlasting Love
headline: Buzz Cason, Songwriter Best Known for ‘Everlasting Love,’ Dies at 84
abstract: As a performer, he was a leading figure in the early days of Nashville rock ’n’ roll. He later found success as a writer, producer and publisher.

name: Elaine Schwartz
profession: Longtime Principal of an Innovative School
headline: Elaine Schwartz, Longtime Principal of an Innovative School, Dies at 92
abstract: A co-founder of the Center School in Manhattan, she implemented once-radical ideas that put the students first. She retired four decades later, at 91.

name: Jamie Kellner
headline: Jamie Kellner, TV Executive Who Started Fox and WB, Dies at 77
abstract: With an emphasis on younger viewers, he established the networks as serious rivals to ABC, CBS and NBC, which had ruled television for nearly 40 years.

name: Otto Lucas
headline: Overlooked No More: Otto Lucas, ‘God in the Hat World’
abstract: His designs made it onto the covers of fashion magazines and onto the heads of celebrities like Greta Garbo. His business closed after he died in a plane crash.

name: Paul Sperry
headline: Paul Sperry, Tenor Who Specialized in American Song, Dies at 90
abstract: He carved out a niche by singing the music of living composers from his own country. He was praised by critics at home and abroad.

name: Doris Allen
headline: Doris Allen, Analyst Who Saw the Tet Offensive Coming, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Her warning of a big buildup of enemy troops poised to attack South Vietnam in 1968 was ignored, a major U.S. Army intelligence failure during the war.

name: Martin Mull
headline: Martin Mull, Comic Actor Who Rose to Fame on ‘Mary Hartman,’ Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Mull, who was also an artist and a musician, had a long list of credits that included the sitcoms “Roseanne” and “Veep.”

name: Orlando Cepeda
profession: Baseball Star Known as the Baby Bull
headline: Orlando Cepeda, Baseball Star Known as the Baby Bull, Dies at 86
abstract: Only the second Puerto Rican native elected to the Hall of Fame, he hit 379 home runs but later served time in prison on a drug-smuggling charge.

name: Ann Lurie
headline: Ann Lurie, Nurse Who Became a Prominent Philanthropist, Is Dead at 79
abstract: A former hippie who chafed at wealth, she married a Chicago real estate titan and, after his death, donated hundreds of millions in her adopted city and beyond.

name: Soma Golden Behr
profession: Inspired Enterprising Journalism at The Times
headline: Soma Golden Behr, 84, Dies; Inspired Enterprising Journalism at The Times
abstract: The first woman to serve as the paper’s national editor, she focused on issues of race, class and poverty, drawing prizes, and rose to the newsroom’s top echelon.

name: Ismail Kadare
profession: His Novels Brought Albanias Plight to the World
headline: Ismail Kadare, 88, Dies; His Novels Brought Albania’s Plight to the World
abstract: Often compared to Orwell and Kafka, he walked a political tightrope with works that offered veiled criticism of his totalitarian state.

name: Shay Youngblood
headline: Shay Youngblood, Influential Author and Playwright, Dies at 64
abstract: She wrote memorably about her upbringing by a circle of maternal elders and the life lessons they imparted, and of her yearning for the mother she lost.

name: June Leaf
headline: June Leaf, Artist Who Explored the Female Form, Dies at 94
abstract: Womanly power was a recurring theme of her work, expressed in idiosyncratic sculpture and paintings that did not align with prevailing trends.

name: Bruce Bastian
headline: Bruce Bastian, a Founder of WordPerfect, Is Dead at 76
abstract: A favorite of early personal computer users, his company was eventually overtaken by Microsoft Word. He later came out as gay and became an L.G.B.T.Q. activist.

name: Robert Towne
headline: Robert Towne, Screenwriter of ‘Chinatown’ and More, Dies at 89
abstract: Celebrated for his mastery of dialogue, he also contributed (though without credit) to the scripts of “Bonnie and Clyde” and “The Godfather.”

name: V. Craig Jordan
profession: Discovered a Key Breast Cancer Drug
headline: V. Craig Jordan, Who Discovered a Key Breast Cancer Drug, Dies at 76
abstract: He found that a failed contraceptive, tamoxifen, could block the growth of cancer cells, opening up a whole new class of treatment.

name: Audrey Flack
headline: Audrey Flack, Creator of Vibrant Photorealist Art, Dies at 93
abstract: She painted and sculpted, but she was best known for her oversized still lifes, painted from photographs and crowded with color and detail.

name: Rob Stone
headline: Rob Stone, Master Marketer of Hip-Hop, Is Dead at 55
abstract: A founder of the influential music magazine The Fader, he also bridged the worlds of hip-hop and the Fortune 500 with his innovative marketing agency.

name: Nancy Azara
headline: Nancy Azara, Sculptor Who Created a Haven for Feminist Artists, Dies at 84
abstract: She helped establish the New York Feminist Art Institute. In her own work — monumental pieces carved from found lumber — she evoked ancient feminine imagery.

name: Keke Jabbar
profession: Starred on Love and Marriage: Huntsville
headline: Keke Jabbar, Who Starred on ‘Love and Marriage: Huntsville,’ Dies at 42
abstract: She was a frequent sight on the series, which began in 2019, and impressed fans with her straightforward attitude.

name: Paal Enger
headline: Paal Enger, Who Stole Munch’s ‘The Scream,’ Is Dead at 57
abstract: A promising player for a storied Norwegian soccer club, he instead found infamy for stealing one of the world’s most famous artworks.

name: Wayne S. Smith
profession: Leading Critic of the Embargo on Cuba
headline: Wayne S. Smith, a Leading Critic of the Embargo on Cuba, Dies at 91
abstract: A former State Department official, he resigned in protest in 1982 over Cuba policy, then spent decades trying to rebuild relations with the island nation.

name: Vic Seixas
profession: Winner of 15 Grand Slam Tennis Titles
headline: Vic Seixas, Winner of 15 Grand Slam Tennis Titles, Dies at 100
abstract: Once declared “the face of American tennis,” he was ranked among the leading players in the United States from the 1940s to the ’60s.

name: Stanley Moss
headline: Stanley Moss, Poet Who Evoked a Troubled World, Dies at 99
abstract: His moving and often painful free-verse observations on friends’ deaths, the Holocaust and other topics won him many devoted fans.

name: Yoshihiro Uchida
headline: Yoshihiro Uchida, Peerless Judo Coach, Is Dead at 104
abstract: A coach at San Jose State for seven decades, he helped establish the sport in America and trained generations of athletes, many of whom went to the Olympics.

name: Jon Landau
headline: Jon Landau, Producer of ‘Titanic’ and ‘Avatar,’ Dies at 63
abstract: In a decades-long collaboration with the director James Cameron, he produced three of the highest-grossing films of all time.

name: Martin Stolar
headline: Martin Stolar, Lawyer Who Fought for Social Justice, Dies at 81
abstract: His clients included antiwar protesters and terror suspects. His practice “not only defended needy people, it propelled social movements,” a colleague said.

name: Jane F. McAlevey
headline: Jane F. McAlevey, Who Empowered Workers Across the Globe, Dies at 59
abstract: An organizer and author, she believed that a union was only as strong as its members and trained thousands “to take over their unions and change them.”

name: James M. Inhofe
headline: James M. Inhofe, Senator Who Denied Climate Change, Dies at 89
abstract: An Oklahoma Republican who led the Environment Committee, he took hard-right stands on many issues but was especially vocal in challenging evidence of global warming.

name: Richard M. Goldstein
headline: Richard M. Goldstein, Who Helped Map the Cosmos, Dies at 97
abstract: Using ground-based radars, he pioneered measurement techniques that scientists now use to chart geographical changes on Earth.

name: Hope Alswang
headline: Hope Alswang, 77, Who Transformed Florida’s Largest Art Museum, Dies
abstract: As the executive director of the Norton Museum of Art, she oversaw an expansion by the British architect Norman Foster. “Great art,” she said, “deserves great architecture.”

name: Ursula Parrott
profession: Best-Selling Author and Voice for the Modern Woman
headline: Overlooked No More: Ursula Parrott, Best-Selling Author and Voice for the Modern Woman
abstract: Her writing, from the late 1920s to the late ’40s, about sex, marriage, divorce, child rearing and work-life balance still resonates.

name: Maxine Singer
profession: Guiding Force at the Dawn of Biotechnology
headline: Maxine Singer, Guiding Force at the Dawn of Biotechnology, Dies at 93
abstract: A leading biochemist, she helped shape guidelines in the 1970s for genetic-engineering while calming public fears of a spread of deadly lab-made microbes.

name: William E. Burrows
headline: William E. Burrows, Historian of the Space Age, Is Dead at 87
abstract: In books and articles he wrote about the militarization of space and believed that investing in exploration would ultimately “protect Earth and guarantee the survival of humanity.”

name: Carol Bongiovi
headline: Carol Bongiovi, Jon Bon Jovi’s Supportive Mother, Dies at 83
abstract: Nicknamed Mom Jovi, she founded the Jon Bon Jovi fan club, and earlier was a Marine and a Playboy bunny.

name: Joe Bonsall
profession: Tenor Voice of the Oak Ridge Boys
headline: Joe Bonsall, Tenor Voice of the Oak Ridge Boys, Dies at 76
abstract: His vocals on songs like “Elvira” were a key to the evolution of the group, originally a Southern gospel quartet, into perennial country hitmakers.

name: Mary Martin
headline: Mary Martin, Who Gave Music Stars Their Start, Dies at 85
abstract: Her eye for talent (Leonard Cohen, Emmylou Harris, Bonnie Raitt) made her a force in a mostly male business. It was she who introduced Bob Dylan to the Band.

name: David Liederman
profession: Found Sweet Success With Davids Cookies
headline: David Liederman, 75, Dies; Found Sweet Success With David’s Cookies
abstract: His innovative version of the chocolate chip cookie, studded with irregular pieces of dark Swiss chocolate, led to a chain of more than 100 stores worldwide.

name: Benji Gregory
profession: Child Star Best Known for ALF
headline: Benji Gregory, Child Star Best Known for ‘ALF,’ Dies at 46
abstract: The hit sitcom, whose main character was an alien, was seen from 1986 to 1990 but would endure in memory as a characteristic artifact of 1980s pop culture.

name: Shelley Duvall
profession: Star of The Shining and Nashville
headline: Shelley Duvall, Star of ‘The Shining’ and ‘Nashville,’ Dies at 75
abstract: Her lithesome features and quirky screen presence made her a popular figure in 1970s movies, particularly Robert Altman’s.

name: Hattie Wiener
headline: Hattie Wiener, Sex-Positive ‘Oldest Cougar,’ Dies at 88
abstract: She was an evangelist for older women having sex with younger men, and the health benefits that she said came with it.

name: Dylcia Pagan
headline: Dylcia Pagan, Imprisoned Puerto Rican Nationalist, Is Dead at 77
abstract: She was among 10 members of the terrorist group F.A.L.N. who were convicted on arms and conspiracy charges in 1981. President Bill Clinton granted her clemency.

name: Dan Collins
headline: Dan Collins, 80, Author Who Rejected View of Giuliani as a 9/11 Hero, Dies
abstract: A muckraking journalist, he helped write a revisionist account of Rudolph Giuliani’s role as mayor before and after the terrorist attacks.

name: Dorothy Lichtenstein
profession: Philanthropist and a Rare Artists Widow
headline: Dorothy Lichtenstein, Philanthropist and a Rare ‘Artist’s Widow,’ Dies at 84
abstract: A gregarious yet humble co-founder of the Roy Lichtenstein Foundation, she donated more than 1,000 of her husband’s works, notably to the Whitney Museum.

name: Judy Belushi Pisano
headline: Judy Belushi Pisano, Who Defended Her Husband’s Legacy, Dies at 73
abstract: She was married to John Belushi until his fatal drug overdose in 1982. She went on to celebrate his comic talent in books and a documentary.

name: Anthea Sylbert
headline: Anthea Sylbert, Costume Designer Who Became a Producer, Dies at 84
abstract: Her career unfolded in three phases: as the creator of costumes for movies like “Chinatown,” as a studio executive and as a producer, largely with her friend Goldie Hawn.

name: Bill Viola
headline: Bill Viola, Celebrated Video Artist Who Played With Time, Dies at 73
abstract: Inspired by Renaissance painters, he explored life’s passages — birth, death, romantic love, redemption and rebirth — in often moving, often thrilling exhibitions.

name: Ruth Westheimer
profession: Sex Guru Known as Dr. Ruth
headline: Ruth Westheimer, the Sex Guru Known as Dr. Ruth, Dies at 96
abstract: Frank and funny, the taboo-breaking therapist said things on television and radio that would have been shocking coming from almost anyone else.

name: Abe Krash
profession: Fought for a Constitutional Right to Counsel
headline: Abe Krash, Who Fought for a Constitutional Right to Counsel, Dies at 97
abstract: He provided the research and drafts that helped bring about the Supreme Court’s landmark Gideon v. Wainwright decision in 1963.

name: Thomas Hoepker
headline: Thomas Hoepker, Who Captured an Indelible 9/11 Image, Dies at 88
abstract: His photograph of five young people lounging on the Brooklyn waterfront as smoke engulfed Manhattan mesmerized viewers and stirred controversy.

name: Richard Simmons
headline: Richard Simmons, ‘the Clown Prince of Fitness,’ Dies at 76
abstract: He turned exercise from an arena of musclebound pride into a variety act of cross-dressing gags, teeny-weeny shorts and saucy repartee.

name: Shannen Doherty
headline: Shannen Doherty, ‘Beverly Hills, 90210’ Star, Dies at 53
abstract: Ms. Doherty, who also had roles in the TV series “Charmed” and the comedy-thriller “Heathers,” had continued to work after a breast cancer diagnosis.

name: Jacqueline de Jong
headline: Jacqueline de Jong, Rediscovered Avant-Garde Artist, Dies at 85
abstract: A Dutch painter, sculptor and engraver, she worked in experimental mediums, founded an influential multidisciplinary journal and enjoyed a late-career resurgence.

name: Bengt Samuelsson
profession: Nobelists Research Led to Medical Advances
headline: Bengt Samuelsson, 90, Dies; Nobelist’s Research Led to Medical Advances
abstract: A Swedish biochemist, he shared the 1982 prize for breakthrough discoveries that led to drugs that treat inflammation, glaucoma and allergies.

name: Evan Wright
profession: Award-Winning Reporter and Author of Generation Kill
headline: Evan Wright, Award-Winning Reporter and Author of ‘Generation Kill,’ Dies at 59
abstract: His best seller about Marines in Iraq, members of a “disposable generation,” was made into an HBO mini-series. He focused on subjects outside mainstream media coverage.

name: James R. Tallon Jr.
headline: James R. Tallon Jr., Who Steered Health Care Reforms, Dies at 82
abstract: As an influential committee leader and the majority leader in the New York Assembly, he led efforts, later embraced in Washington, to expand coverage.

name: Joe Bryant
profession: Former N.B.A. Player and Kobes Father
headline: Joe Bryant, Former N.B.A. Player and Kobe’s Father, Is Dead at 69
abstract: A 6-foot-9 forward known as Jellybean, he was drafted out of La Salle and had pro stints in Philadelphia, San Diego and Houston before playing in Italy.

name: Larry Light
headline: Larry Light, Marketer Behind Revival of McDonald’s, Dies at 83
abstract: A branding expert, he deployed the “I’m lovin’ it” campaign globally in 2003 to bring customers and sales back to the fast-food giant when it was in a slump.

name: James B. Sikking
profession: Actor Best Known for Hill Street Blues
headline: James B. Sikking, Actor Best Known for ‘Hill Street Blues,’ Dies at 90
abstract: His natural rectitude landed him roles on hundreds of TV dramas and comedies, including the beloved “Car Pool Lane” episode of “Curb Your Enthusiasm.”

name: Herbert Hoelter
profession: Prison Consultant to the Rich and Infamous
headline: Herbert Hoelter, Prison Consultant to the Rich and Infamous, Dies at 73
abstract: He helped Martha Stewart, Leona Helmsley, Michael Milken and other white-collar criminals win lighter sentences, and prepared them for life in prison.

name: Naomi Pomeroy
headline: Naomi Pomeroy, 49, Chef Who Made Portland a Dining Destination, Dies
abstract: Her refined palate and pursuit of excellence made her the city’s culinary matriarch, attracting diners and talent alike to Oregon. She died in a tubing accident.

name: Robert Pearson
profession: Hair Stylist Turned Acclaimed Barbecue Chef
headline: Robert Pearson, Hair Stylist Turned Acclaimed Barbecue Chef, Dies at 87
abstract: His Texas-style brisket, made with exacting precision, inspired a generation of New York City pit masters, who opened a wave of smoky joints in the 2000s.

name: Renauld White
headline: Renauld White, Debonair Model Who Broke Barriers, Dies at 80
abstract: The first Black American model to appear on the cover of GQ magazine, he was an avatar of male beauty for nearly half a century.

name: Dave Loggins
profession: Wrote Hits for Himself and Others
headline: Dave Loggins, Who Wrote Hits for Himself and Others, Dies at 76
abstract: After tasting fame with “Please Come to Boston” in 1974, he became a major Nashville songwriter. He also wrote the theme to the Masters golf tournament.

name: Monte Kiffin
headline: Monte Kiffin, N.F.L. Defensive Coaching Mastermind, Dies at 84
abstract: He distinguished himself as the defensive coordinator of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who rode his game calling to an easy victory in Super Bowl XXXVII in 2003.

name: Peter Buxtun
headline: Peter Buxtun, Who Exposed Tuskegee Syphilis Study, Dies at 86
abstract: A Public Health Service employee, he turned whistle-blower after learning of decades-long research involving hundreds of poor, infected Black men who were left untreated.

name: Pat Williams
headline: Pat Williams, Charismatic N.B.A. Executive, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Known for his unorthodox marketing practices, Mr. Williams, a founder of the Orlando Magic, was sometimes called the P.T. Barnum of professional basketball.

name: Pat Williams
profession: Last Montana Democrat to Serve in the House
headline: Pat Williams, 87, Last Montana Democrat to Serve in the House, Dies
abstract: His liberal politics, inspired by the safety nets of the New Deal, were shaped in working-class mining country.

name: Bob Newhart
profession: Soft-Spoken Everyman Became a Comedy Star
headline: Bob Newhart, 94, Dies; Soft-Spoken Everyman Became a Comedy Star
abstract: He was a show-business neophyte when he stammered his way to fame in 1960. He went on to star in two of TV’s most memorable sitcoms.

name: Lou Dobbs
profession: Former Fox Business Host and Trump Booster
headline: Lou Dobbs, Former Fox Business Host and Trump Booster, Dies at 78
abstract: He used his platforms on CNN and Fox Business to share baseless conspiracy theories. His tenure at Fox ended after the network was sued for defamation over claims of voting machine fraud.

name: Cheng Pei Pei
headline: Cheng Pei Pei, ‘Queen’ of Kung Fu Cinema, Dies at 78
abstract: She starred in kung fu movies from the modern origins of the form in midcentury Hong Kong to the worldwide breakout “Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon.”

name: Nguyen Phu Trong
headline: Nguyen Phu Trong, Powerful Vietnamese Leader, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Known for his “blazing furnace” anticorruption campaign, Mr. Trong consolidated power in one of the world’s few remaining Communist dictatorships.

name: Tommy Robinson
headline: Tommy Robinson, Colorful Arkansas Sheriff and Congressman, Dies at 82
abstract: He gained national attention for his unorthodox approaches to policing in Little Rock and then went on to win three terms in the House of Representatives.

name: Bobby Grier
profession: Overcame Resistance in Integrating Sugar Bowl
headline: Bobby Grier Dies at 91; Overcame Resistance in Integrating Sugar Bowl
abstract: Early in the civil rights movement, a Georgia governor tried to ban Black players from the game, but after a protest by Georgia Tech students, Grier was allowed to play.

name: Happy Traum
profession: Folk Scene Mainstay and Dylan Collaborator
headline: Happy Traum, Folk Scene Mainstay and Dylan Collaborator, Dies at 86
abstract: A noted guitarist and banjo player, he emerged from the same Greenwich Village folk-revival scene as his friend and sometime collaborator Bob Dylan.

name: Bernice Johnson Reagon
headline: Bernice Johnson Reagon, a Musical Voice for Civil Rights, Is Dead at 81
abstract: A singer, composer, curator and founder of the vocal group Sweet Honey in the Rock, she provided a gospel soundtrack for the civil rights movement.

name: Sheila Jackson Lee
headline: Rep. Sheila Jackson Lee, Champion for Progressive Causes, Dies at 74
abstract: A Democrat from the Houston area, she led the effort to make Juneteenth a federal holiday.

name: Thomas Neff
headline: Thomas Neff, Who Turned Soviet Warheads Into Electricity, Dies at 80
abstract: An M.I.T. physicist, he engineered an East-West deal that reduced nuclear threats and produced one of the greatest peace dividends of all time.

name: Fakir
profession: Last Surviving Member of the Four Tops
headline: Duke Fakir, Last Surviving Member of the Four Tops, Dies at 88
abstract: He sang tenor on hits like “Standing in the Shadows of Love,” “Reach Out, I’ll Be There” and “I Can’t Help Myself (Sugar Pie Honey Bunch).”

name: Noriko Ohara
profession: Gave Voice to a Beloved Anime Character
headline: Noriko Ohara, Who Gave Voice to a Beloved Anime Character, Dies at 88
abstract: She starred in “Doraemon” and other animated shows watched by nearly every child in Japan, and her voice became widely recognized.

name: Walter Shapiro
profession: Political Columnist With a Contrarian Streak
headline: Walter Shapiro, Political Columnist With a Contrarian Streak, Dies at 77
abstract: He brought to his writing a sharp sense of humor, honed in stand-up comedy clubs, and never pulled punches even though he was an unabashed Democrat.

name: John Mayall
headline: John Mayall, Pioneer of British Blues, Is Dead at 90
abstract: He was best known not for his own playing or singing but for recruiting and polishing the talents of one gifted lead guitarist after another, starting with Eric Clapton.

name: Rosa Ross
headline: Rosa Ross, Late-Blooming Author of Asian Cookbooks, Dies at 86
abstract: She was, she said, unable to cook a basic meal into her mid-20s. But she went on to a successful career as a restaurateur and an authority on Asian cuisine.

name: Lewis H. Lapham
headline: Lewis H. Lapham, Harper’s Editor and Piercing Columnist, Dies at 89
abstract: Born into a patrician family, he used Harper’s and later his own Lapham’s Quarterly to denounce what he saw as the hypocrisies and injustices of a spoiled United States.

name: Abner Haynes
profession: Star of the A.F.L.s Early Years
headline: Abner Haynes, a Star of the A.F.L.’s Early Years, Dies at 86
abstract: He was a threat as a halfback, receiver and returner for the Dallas Texans, the team that became the Kansas City Chiefs. But he still had to deal with racism.

name: Kathy Willens
headline: Kathy Willens, Photojournalist Seemingly Everywhere, Is Dead at 74
abstract: Guided by a keen sense of timing, she covered wars, sports, riots, politics and more for The A.P. in the ’70s, when few women worked as news photographers.

name: Toumani Diabaté
headline: Toumani Diabaté, Malian Master of the Kora, Is Dead at 58
abstract: He believed that music could transcend national borders set by colonialism and restore ancient ties, even as it embraced the changes of a globalizing society.

name: Bob Booker
profession: J.F.K. Parody Was a Runaway Hit
headline: Bob Booker, Whose J.F.K. Parody Was a Runaway Hit, Dies at 92
abstract: Most record companies didn’t think “The First Family,” which he and his writing partner created, was a good idea. It became the fastest-selling album of the pre-Beatles era.

name: Michael Hardy
headline: Michael Hardy, Sharpton’s Longtime Lawyer and Confidant, Dies at 69
abstract: He was general counsel of Mr. Sharpton’s civil rights group, the National Action Network, and defended him in a defamation suit arising from the Tawana Brawley case.

name: Willy de Bruyn
headline: Overlooked No More: Willy de Bruyn, Cycling Champion Who Broke Gender Boundaries
abstract: A premiere cyclist in women’s competitions, he helped pave the way for future athletes when he announced that he wanted to live the rest of his life as a man.

name: Darryl Daniel
profession: Illustrator of Snoop Doggs First Album Cover
headline: Darryl Daniel, Illustrator of Snoop Dogg’s First Album Cover, Dies at 56
abstract: The 1993 album “Doggystyle” went on to sell millions of copies around the world and solidified the career of Mr. Daniel, known as Joe Cool, as a hip-hop illustrator.

name: Martin S. Indyk
headline: Martin S. Indyk, Diplomat Who Sought Middle East Peace, Dies at 73
abstract: As ambassador to Israel in the Clinton administration and as a special envoy under Barack Obama, he was skeptical of Israeli settlements.

name: Sylvain Saudan
headline: Sylvain Saudan, ‘Skier of the Impossible,’ Is Dead at 87
abstract: His audacious descents around the world inspired a generation of extreme skiers. “One mistake,” he once said, “you die.”

name: Roland Dumas
profession: French Foreign Minister Tainted by Scandal
headline: Roland Dumas Dies at 101; French Foreign Minister Tainted by Scandal
abstract: A lawyer and confidant of François Mitterrand, he was in the forefront of French politics for decades, only to be undone by his taste for the high life.

name: Jerry Miller
profession: Lauded Guitarist With the 60s Band Moby Grape
headline: Jerry Miller, 81, Lauded Guitarist With the ’60s Band Moby Grape, Dies
abstract: He drew praise for his blues-inflected fretwork as his critically acclaimed band rode high, if briefly, during San Francisco’s Summer of Love.

name: Gail Lumet Buckley
headline: Gail Lumet Buckley, Chronicler of Black Family History, Dies at 86
abstract: She wrote two books about multiple generations of her forebears, including her mother, Lena Horne.

name: Edna O’Brien
headline: Edna O’Brien, Writer Who Gave Voice to Women’s Passions, Dies at 93
abstract: Her novels and short stories often explored the lives of willful women who loved men who were crass, unfaithful or already married.

name: Jill Schary Robinson
headline: Jill Schary Robinson, Who Wrote of Her Hollywood Upbringing, Dies at 88
abstract: A screenwriter’s daughter, she grew up in the glittering world of privilege and its contradictions, which became rich material for her memoirs and novels.

name: James C. Scott
headline: James C. Scott, Iconoclastic Social Scientist, Dies at 87
abstract: In influential books, he questioned top-down government programs and extolled the power of the powerless, embracing a form of anarchism.

name: Wolfgang Rihm
headline: Wolfgang Rihm, Prolific Contemporary Classical Music Composer, Dies at 72
abstract: Likened to a “court composer” for Germany, he wrote more than 500 pieces and was considered one of the most original and independent musical voices in Europe.

name: Francine Pascal
profession: Creator of Sweet Valley High Book Series
headline: Francine Pascal, Creator of ‘Sweet Valley High’ Book Series, Dies at 92
abstract: The series and its many spinoffs have sold more than 200 million copies and revolutionized the world of young adult publishing.

name: William L. Calley Jr.
headline: William L. Calley Jr., Convicted in My Lai Massacre, Is Dead at 80
abstract: Hundreds of Vietnamese civilians died at the hands of American soldiers, but Lieutenant Calley was the only one found guilty.

name: Tom Porton
profession: Hall of Fame Teacher on a Humanitarian Mission
headline: Tom Porton, Hall of Fame Teacher on a Humanitarian Mission, Dies at 74
abstract: At James Monroe High School in the Bronx, he inspired students to embrace the arts and to be engaged with the world, through AIDS programs and other community service projects.

name: Richard Crawford
headline: Richard Crawford, Leading Scholar of American Music, Dies at 89
abstract: American Music was a marginal subfield in the 1960s when he began his research as a student, and then as a faculty member, at the University of Michigan.

name: Don Buchwald
headline: Don Buchwald, Howard Stern’s Loyal ‘Superagent,’ Dies at 88
abstract: He had clients like Tony Curtis and Kim Novak, but his biggest score came when he negotiated the “King of All Media’s” landmark contract with Sirius Satellite Radio.

name: Randy Kehler
profession: Peace Activist Inspired Release of Pentagon Papers
headline: Randy Kehler, 80, Dies; Peace Activist Inspired Release of Pentagon Papers
abstract: Daniel Ellsberg was so moved by Mr. Kehler’s opposition to the Vietnam War that he decided to leak documents that changed the course of the conflict.

name: Joe Engle
profession: Trailblazer as Test Pilot and an Astronaut
headline: Joe Engle, Trailblazer as Test Pilot and an Astronaut, Dies at 91
abstract: He was the first to touch the edge of space and later to go beyond it in two different aircraft, an X-15 and a shuttle. But the moon, to his disappointment, proved out of reach.

name: Benjamin Luxon
profession: Rich Baritone Thwarted by Hearing Loss
headline: Benjamin Luxon, Rich Baritone Thwarted by Hearing Loss, Dies at 87
abstract: A favorite of Benjamin Britten, he won acclaim in roles like Don Giovanni, Eugene Onegin and Falstaff until his affliction forced him to largely give up singing.

name: Manfred Kirchheimer
headline: Manfred Kirchheimer, ‘Indispensable’ New York Filmmaker, Dies at 93
abstract: For decades, he meticulously crafted short films and documentaries in relative obscurity. Then, in his 80s, he enjoyed a burst of productivity and acclaim.

name: Peter C. Theisinger
profession: Led Mars Rover Missions for NASA
headline: Peter C. Theisinger, 78, Dies; Led Mars Rover Missions for NASA
abstract: He directed a team of engineers that built Spirit, Opportunity and Curiosity, mobile robots that offered astonishing glimpses into the planet’s ancient past.

name: Yvonne Furneaux
profession: Cosmopolitan Actress in La Dolce Vita
headline: Yvonne Furneaux, Cosmopolitan Actress in ‘La Dolce Vita,’ Dies at 98
abstract: An Oxford graduate who spoke five languages, she had an early career as a siren before finding critical acclaim in masterworks by Federico Fellini and Roman Polanski.

name: Alexander Waugh
profession: Literary Scion of a Literary Dynasty
headline: Alexander Waugh, Literary Scion of a Literary Dynasty, Dies at 60
abstract: The brother, son and grandson of famous English writers, he carved out his own space as a composer, critic, columnist and historian.

name: Anton van Dalen
headline: Anton van Dalen, Whose Art Examined an Evolving Neighborhood, Dies at 85
abstract: He traced the dramatic transformation of the Lower East Side from his building, where he lived for 50 years. He also assisted the cartoonist Saul Steinberg.

name: Ina Jaffe
headline: Ina Jaffe, Dogged and Award-Winning NPR Reporter, Dies at 75
abstract: She spent decades covering politics and aging in America, and she was the first editor of the NPR program “Weekend Edition Saturday.”

name: Tsung-Dao Lee
headline: Tsung-Dao Lee, 97, Physicist Who Challenged a Law of Nature, Dies
abstract: At 31, he and a colleague won the 1957 Nobel Prize in Physics for discovering that subatomic particles, contrary to what scientists thought, are not always symmetrical.

name: Barbara Howar
headline: Barbara Howar, Irreverent Memoirist of Washington Society, Dies at 89
abstract: She was already a prominent hostess in the nation’s capital when her uninhibited, best-selling 1973 memoir, “Laughing All the Way,” made her a star.

name: Walter Arlen
headline: Walter Arlen, Holocaust Refugee and Belated Composer, Is Dead at 103
abstract: After fleeing Vienna, he was a music critic and teacher before returning to composing in the 1980s. His memories of Nazi barbarism inspired his music.

name: Lorenza de’ Medici
headline: Lorenza de’ Medici, Who Elevated Italian Cooking, Is Dead at 97
abstract: A descendant of a storied family, she was an author, TV host and cooking school director who showed that Italian cuisine was about more than tomatoes, pizza and pasta.

name: Charles Cyphers
headline: Charles Cyphers, Who Played Sheriff Brackett in ‘Halloween,’ Dies at 85
abstract: He was known for his roles as the hard-nosed sheriff in the “Halloween” horror film series.

name: Joss Naylor
profession: English King of Racing Up Mountains
headline: Joss Naylor, the English King of Racing Up Mountains, Dies at 88
abstract: A sheep farmer, he set records in so-called fell running — rugged off-trail competitions that can last days and present painful hazards, including an irate cow.

name: Connie Chiume
profession: Black Panther Actor Bridged S. Africa Eras
headline: Connie Chiume, 72, Dies; ‘Black Panther’ Actor Bridged S. Africa Eras
abstract: Her career began during apartheid and outlived it, reaching a personal milestone in a blockbuster movie and its sequel.

name: Ann Abadie
headline: Ann Abadie, Champion of Southern Studies, Is Dead at 84
abstract: The longtime associate director of the Center for the Study of Southern Culture at the University of Mississippi, she also edited more than 50 books about the South.

name: Billy Bean
profession: Led Baseball on Diversity After Coming Out as Gay
headline: Billy Bean Dies at 60; Led Baseball on Diversity After Coming Out as Gay
abstract: As an outfielder, he hid his sexual identity from his teammates for nearly a decade before retiring and becoming a force for inclusion in the organization.

name: Tom Korologos
headline: Tom Korologos, Shepherd of Republican Nominees, Dies at 91
abstract: As a White House official and later as a lobbyist, he guided about 300 nominees through their confirmation hearings, including Supreme Court justices.

name: Mary Wings
headline: Mary Wings, Pioneering Creator of Queer Comics, Dies at 75
abstract: She was the first openly gay woman to write a comic book about lesbians. She went on to write detective novels with a queer woman in the lead.

name: Jacques Lewis
profession: French Veteran of U.S. Landing on D-Day
headline: Jacques Lewis, French Veteran of U.S. Landing on D-Day, Dies at 105
abstract: Believed to be the last surviving Frenchman to wade ashore with Americans, he was attached to an Army unit that stormed Utah Beach and helped drive Germans out of France.

name: Duane Thomas
profession: Enigmatic Running Back for the Cowboys
headline: Duane Thomas, Enigmatic Running Back for the Cowboys, Dies at 77
abstract: He led Dallas to its first Super Bowl victory after engaging in a well-publicized contract dispute in which he called Coach Tom Landry “plastic” and refused to talk to reporters.

name: Chi Chi Rodriguez
headline: Chi Chi Rodriguez, the Golf World’s Swashbuckling Champion, Dies at 88
abstract: He won eight PGA Tour tournaments and two senior majors — but it was his flair on the greens that made him one of the sport’s most popular players.

name: Kevin Sullivan
headline: Kevin Sullivan, Pro Wrestling’s ‘Prince of Darkness,’ Dies at 75
abstract: Modeling himself after the heavy metal bands of the 1970s and ’80s, he played the role of an occult-inspired villain and tangled with the likes of Hulk Hogan.

name: Ross Terrill
headline: Ross Terrill, Insightful Expert on Communist China, Is Dead at 85
abstract: In the 1960s, he was among the first Westerners allowed into the country, and for decades he helped the rest of the world understand it.

name: Mísia
profession: Brought a Modern Flair to Fado Music
headline: Mísia, Who Brought a Modern Flair to Fado Music, Dies at 69
abstract: With her smoky voice and her high-fashion look, the self-proclaimed “punk of fado” found stardom by shaking up a venerable Portuguese genre.

name: Renee Carroll
headline: Overlooked No More: Renee Carroll, ‘World’s Most Famous Hatcheck Girl’
abstract: From the cloakroom at Sardi’s, she made her own mark on Broadway, hobnobbing with celebrity clients while safekeeping fedoras, bowlers, derbies and more.

name: J. Robin Warren
headline: J. Robin Warren, Who Proved That Bacteria Cause Ulcers, Dies at 87
abstract: He endured skepticism but won a Nobel Prize for his work upending the conventional wisdom that stress, diet or alcohol caused the painful condition.

name: Howie Cohen
headline: Howie Cohen, Whose Alka-Seltzer Ads Agreed With Viewers, Dies at 81
abstract: A copywriter, he and a partner in 1972 came up with “Try it, you’ll like it” and “I can’t believe I ate that whole thing.” Soon, sales were, well, fizzing.

name: Susan Wojcicki
headline: Susan Wojcicki, a Pivotal Chief of YouTube, Dies at 56
abstract: She helped turn Google into an internet juggernaut and became one of the most prominent women in Silicon Valley.

name: Eddie Canales
headline: Eddie Canales, 76, Dies; Gave Migrants Water, and Dignity
abstract: After a long career as a union organizer, he came out of retirement in 2013 to form the South Texas Human Rights Center and provide lifesaving aid.

name: Bob Tischler
headline: Bob Tischler, Who Helped Revive ‘Saturday Night Live,’ Dies at 78
abstract: A producer of “The National Lampoon Radio Hour” and albums by the Blues Brothers, he became S.N.L.’s head writer after a dismal season early in its history.

name: Ángel Salazar
headline: Ángel Salazar, Comedian and ‘Scarface’ Actor, Dies at 68
abstract: He first made his mark doing stand-up in New York, but he was best known for his role as Chi Chi opposite Al Pacino in the hit 1983 movie.

name: Paul Bucha
profession: Medal of Honor Recipient With a Political Voice
headline: Paul Bucha, Medal of Honor Recipient With a Political Voice, Dies at 80
abstract: His quick thinking saved fellow soldiers in Vietnam. Later, he had a role in the presidential runs of Ross Perot, George H.W. Bush and Barack Obama.

name: Peggy Moffitt
profession: Defined 60s Fashion With a Bathing Suit and a Bob
headline: Peggy Moffitt, 86, Dies; Defined ’60s Fashion With a Bathing Suit and a Bob
abstract: She became famous for posing in the fashion designer Rudi Gernreich’s topless swimsuit. But she saw herself more as a performer than as a model.

name: Frank Selvy
profession: Scored 100 Points in a College Basketball Game
headline: Frank Selvy, 91, Dies; Scored 100 Points in a College Basketball Game
abstract: The feat, a collegiate record, came in 1954 in South Carolina. As a pro, he missed a shot that would have given the Los Angeles Lakers a championship.

name: Wally Amos
profession: Enterprising Creator of Famous Amos Cookies
headline: Wally Amos, Enterprising Creator of Famous Amos Cookies, Dies at 88
abstract: With a background as a talent agent, his aunt’s recipe and a winning personality, he built one of the world’s best-known brands of baked goods.

name: Jay Kanter
profession: Agent for Marlon Brando and Marilyn Monroe
headline: Jay Kanter, Agent for Marlon Brando and Marilyn Monroe, Dies at 97
abstract: Later a studio executive, he was among the last of the power brokers who dominated Hollywood in the latter half of the 20th century.

name: Shmuel Butman
headline: Rabbi Shmuel Butman, 81, a Brooklyn Voice of Ultra-Orthodox Jews, Is Dead
abstract: He was the public face of the Chabad-Lubavitch sect during the Crown Heights riots in 1991 and for decades lit its giant menorah in Manhattan every Hanukkah.

name: Betty A. Prashker
headline: Betty A. Prashker, 99, Who Pushed Boundaries in Book Publishing, Dies
abstract: A top editor and executive at two publishing houses, she was an advocate for women in publishing, and for equal pay in an industry that had long been male-dominated.

name: Gena Rowlands
headline: Gena Rowlands, Actress Who Brought Raw Drama to Her Roles, Dies at 94
abstract: Known for playing on-the-verge characters, she twice earned Oscar nominations for her work in films directed by John Cassavetes, her husband.

name: Seth Bloom
headline: Seth Bloom, 49, Clown Who Brought Laughter to the Rubble of War, Dies
abstract: A virtuoso of physical comedy, he performed around the world with his wife. Most notably, he helped stage clown shows in Afghanistan.

name: Peter Marshall
profession: Longtime Host of The Hollywood Squares
headline: Peter Marshall, Longtime Host of ‘The Hollywood Squares,’ Dies at 98
abstract: He played straight man to all manner of celebrities, asking questions on what was for many years the most popular game show on television.

name: Issa Hayatou
headline: Issa Hayatou, ‘the Emperor of African Soccer,’ Dies at 77
abstract: In his posts atop the governing bodies for African and global soccer, he fought to establish the continent as an equal to Europe and South America.

name: Greg Kihn
profession: Scored Hits With Jeopardy and The Breakup Song
headline: Greg Kihn, 75, Dies; Scored Hits With ‘Jeopardy’ and ‘The Breakup Song’
abstract: He carved out a place for no-nonsense power pop at the height of the MTV 1980s.

name: Jack Russell
profession: Singer for Great White and Survivor of Nightclub Fire
headline: Jack Russell, 63, Dies; Singer for Great White and Survivor of Nightclub Fire
abstract: At a show in 2003 with his band, a pyrotechnics display ignited a fire that killed 100 people, including the band’s guitarist.

name: Jerry Fuller
profession: Songwriter of Young Girl and Travelin Man
headline: Jerry Fuller, Songwriter of ‘Young Girl’ and ‘Travelin’ Man,’ Is Dead at 85
abstract: He found a musical sweet spot between romance and “out of line” desire for recordings by Ricky Nelson, Johnny Mathis and Gary Puckett and the Union Gap.

name: Charlie Moss
profession: Ads Spread Love for a Battered New York
headline: Charlie Moss, Whose Ads Spread Love for a Battered New York, Dies at 85
abstract: As a pioneer of Madison Avenue’s creative revolution, his “I ♥ NY” tourism pitches helped pump new life into a city deflated by the turmoil of the 1970s.

name: Leonard Hayflick
profession: Discovered Why No One Lives Forever
headline: Leonard Hayflick, Who Discovered Why No One Lives Forever, Dies at 96
abstract: A biomedical researcher, he found that normal cells can divide only a certain number of times before they age — which, he said, explained aging on a cellular level.

name: Alain Delon
headline: Alain Delon, Smoldering French Film Star, Dies at 88
abstract: The César-winning actor was an international favorite in the 1960s and ’70s, often sought after by the era’s great auteurs.

name: John Aprea
profession: Godfather Part II and Full House Actor
headline: John Aprea, ‘Godfather Part II’ and ‘Full House’ Actor, Dies at 83
abstract: He played Salvatore “Sal” Tessio in “The Godfather Part II” in 1974, and the father of a popular character on “Full House,” a sitcom.

name: Phil Donahue
headline: Phil Donahue, Talk Host Who Made Audiences Part of the Show, Dies at 88
abstract: Stalking the aisles, microphone in hand, he turned “The Phil Donahue Show” into a participation event, soliciting questions and comments on topics from human rights to orgies.

name: Ruth Johnson Colvin
headline: Ruth Johnson Colvin, Champion of Literacy, Is Dead at 107
abstract: Working out of her basement, and with no teaching experience, she created a nonprofit that helped people around the world learn to read.

name: Michel Guérard
profession: Lowered the Calories in Haute Cuisine
headline: Michel Guérard, Who Lowered the Calories in Haute Cuisine, Dies at 91
abstract: Appalled by the food options available to those seeking to lose weight, he developed a form of nouvelle cuisine for dieters at a spa in southwestern France.

name: Harold Meltzer
headline: Harold Meltzer Dies at 58; Composer of Impossible-to-Pigeonhole Works
abstract: His music, which was performed by many prominent ensembles, mixed melodic themes and rich textures with the sharp-edged angularity of modernism.

name: Maria Branyas Morera
headline: Maria Branyas Morera, World’s Oldest Person, Dies at 117
abstract: Born before the emergence of the telephone, she came to embrace the digital revolution and cultivated a following on social media as “Super Catalan Grandma.”

name: Charles R. Cross
headline: Charles R. Cross, Biographer of Cobain and Hendrix, Dies at 67
abstract: He tracked the rise of grunge as the editor of the Seattle music magazine The Rocket. He also wrote acclaimed books about two of the city’s most celebrated rock luminaries.

name: Myron E. Ullman III
headline: Myron E. Ullman III, Executive Who Remade Macy’s and J.C. Penney, Dies at 77
abstract: As a leader behind many of the world’s best-known brands, he exuded operational know-how. He also displayed a rare humility, which helped drive his success.

name: Bill Pascrell Jr.
headline: Bill Pascrell Jr., 14-Term House Democrat From N.J., Dies at 87
abstract: An outspoken progressive, he vigorously opposed President Donald J. Trump and focused on legislation to help “regular Americans pay their bills.”

name: Al Attles
profession: Golden State Warrior in Name and in Spirit
headline: Al Attles, a Golden State Warrior in Name and in Spirit, Dies at 87
abstract: He was known as the Destroyer for his gritty intensity as a player. He later coached Golden State to an N.B.A. championship and served as its general manager.

name: Charlene Marshall
profession: Central Figure in a Celebrity Scandal
headline: Charlene Marshall, Central Figure in a Celebrity Scandal, Dies at 79
abstract: Her husband, Anthony, was convicted of defrauding his wealthy mother, Brooke Astor. But in the tabloids, Mrs. Marshall often seemed to be the one on trial.

name: Geri Taylor
headline: Geri Taylor, a Voice for Alzheimer’s, Is Dead at 81
abstract: She turned her diagnosis into a command to live life passionately, leading to a 12-page New York Times profile and a new career as a public speaker.

name: Mike Lynch
headline: Mike Lynch, Tech Mogul Acquitted of Fraud, Dies at 59
abstract: The British entrepreneur was found not guilty of fraud charges in the sale of his company to Hewlett-Packard. He was celebrating his acquittal when his yacht sank off the coast of Sicily.

name: Silvio Santos
headline: Silvio Santos, Provocative Brazilian Television Host, Dies at 93
abstract: He was best known for the long-running variety show “Programa Silvio Santos,” on which he charmed his audiences with gimmicks and showcased a range of performers.

name: Peter Dykstra
headline: Peter Dykstra, Pioneering CNN Climate Journalist, Dies at 67
abstract: A former Greenpeace official, he drew on his command of environmental subjects to persuade his bosses at the cable channel to cover climate issues.

name: John Lansing
headline: John Lansing, Who Guided NPR Through Tumultuous Times, Dies at 67
abstract: He led the broadcasting organization during the coronavirus pandemic, a decline in revenue and a period of extreme political polarization.

name: Helen Fisher
headline: Helen Fisher, Who Researched the Brain’s Love Circuitry, Dies at 79
abstract: A biological anthropologist, she worked with colleagues to confirm for the first time that love is hard-wired in the brain.

name: Scott Bloomquist
headline: Scott Bloomquist, Champion Dirt-Track Driver, Dies at 60
abstract: Styling himself as a rebel, he won more than 600 races and nine championships in a 40-year career.

name: Mabel Addis
headline: Overlooked No More: Mabel Addis, Who Pioneered Storytelling in Video Gaming
abstract: She was a teacher when she participated in an educational experiment with IBM. As a result, she became the first female video game designer.

name: Hettie Jones
headline: Hettie Jones, Poet and Author Who Nurtured the Beats, Dies at 90
abstract: She and her husband, LeRoi Jones, published works by their literary friends. After he left her and became Amiri Baraka, she found her own voice.

name: Tom Brown Jr.
headline: Tom Brown Jr., World-Renowned Survivalist, Is Dead at 74
abstract: For decades, he ran a school in the New Jersey wilderness that taught thousands of students how to survive and even thrive in the great outdoors.

name: Mitzi McCall
headline: Mitzi McCall, 93, Dies; Comedian Confronted Beatlemania and Lost
abstract: She and her husband had the bad luck to make their “Ed Sullivan Show” debut the same night as the Beatles. They bombed. But their careers would recover.

name: Russell Malone
headline: Russell Malone, Acclaimed Jazz Guitarist, Dies at 60
abstract: He first gained attention with Jimmy Smith and went on to work with Harry Connick Jr., Diana Krall and Ron Carter. He also had a distinguished solo career.

name: Eric Butler
profession: Promoted Restorative Justice for Young People
headline: Eric Butler, 49, Dies; Promoted ‘Restorative Justice’ for Young People
abstract: As a counselor, he embraced an alternative to “zero tolerance” disciplinary policies that are disproportionately meted out to Black students.

name: Rudy Franchi
profession: Put Movies at the Center of a Technicolor Life
headline: Rudy Franchi, Who Put Movies at the Center of a Technicolor Life, Dies at 85
abstract: He brought French classics to New York, published a film magazine, worked as a Hollywood publicist and, as seen on “Antiques Roadshow,” thrived selling vintage film posters and other ephemera.

name: Sid Eudy
profession: Wrestler Known as Sid Vicious (Among Other Names)
headline: Sid Eudy, 63, Dies; Wrestler Known as ‘Sid Vicious’ (Among Other Names)
abstract: Listed at 6-foot-9 and 317 pounds, he faced off against some of the industry’s biggest names, including Shawn Michaels and Hulk Hogan.

name: Betty Halbreich
headline: Betty Halbreich, World’s ‘Most Famous Personal Shopper,’ Dies at 96
abstract: She was a local New York secret before gaining wider renown as the dressing-room companion of rich, powerful women. A dark past lay beneath her savoir faire.

name: Alastair Carruthers
profession: Pioneered the Cosmetic Use of Botox
headline: Alastair Carruthers, 79, Dies; Pioneered the Cosmetic Use of Botox
abstract: With his wife, Dr. Jean Carruthers, he conducted hundreds of studies on the wrinkle-erasing properties of the neurotoxin that causes botulism. The work revolutionized beauty care.

name: Theresa Kane
headline: Sister Theresa Kane, 87, Dies; Challenged Pope on Ordaining Women
abstract: A progressive nun, she used a welcome address before Pope John Paul II in 1979 to call for equality in the ranks of the Roman Catholic Church.

name: Ofra Bikel
profession: Filmmaker With a Focus on Criminal Justice
headline: Ofra Bikel, Filmmaker With a Focus on Criminal Justice, Dies at 94
abstract: Her award-winning documentaries for PBS’s “Frontline” series shed light on serious flaws in several convictions and helped lead to the release of 13 prisoners.

name: Betty Jean Hall
profession: Fought for Coal-Mining Jobs for Women
headline: Betty Jean Hall, Who Fought for Coal-Mining Jobs for Women, Dies at 78
abstract: She was a fiery lawyer from eastern Kentucky who charged coal companies with discrimination for their refusal to hire women. Her campaign was a success.

name: Kiingi Tuheitia
profession: King of the Maori in New Zealand
headline: Kiingi Tuheitia, King of the Maori in New Zealand, Dies at 69
abstract: The king, who had held the title for 18 years, was praised by New Zealand’s prime minister for his “unwavering commitment to his people.”

name: Landon Y. Jones
profession: Made People a Star Among Magazines
headline: Landon Y. Jones, Who Made People a Star Among Magazines, Dies at 80
