abstract: An unapologetic champion of the newsworthiness of celebrities, he also drew attention to teenage pregnancy and helped popularize the term “baby boomer.”

name: James Bjorken
headline: James Bjorken, 90, Dies; Physicist Who Helped Prove That Quarks Exist
abstract: His research enabled the discovery that protons and neutrons are made of smaller particles, contributing to a fuller picture of the subatomic universe.

name: Leonard Riggio
profession: Founded Barnes & Noble and Upended Publishing
headline: Leonard Riggio, 83, Dies; Founded Barnes & Noble and Upended Publishing
abstract: He pioneered the bookstore-as-superstore, a retail behemoth that dominated the industry before Amazon overtook it with its online reach.

name: Eliyahu Rips
profession: Claimed to Find Secret Codes in the Torah
headline: Eliyahu Rips, Who Claimed to Find Secret Codes in the Torah, Dies at 75
abstract: His work provided the basis for the worldwide best seller “The Bible Code,” but he later rejected the book as unscientific.

name: Arthur J. Gregg
headline: Arthur J. Gregg, Trailblazing Army Officer, Is Dead at 96
abstract: The first Black officer to achieve the rank of lieutenant general, he lived to see an Army post in Virginia renamed in his honor.

name: Pete Wade
headline: Pete Wade, Guitarist on Countless Nashville Hits, Dies at 89
abstract: His clean tone and less-is-more approach made him a studio stalwart and a pioneer of what came to be known as the Nashville Sound.

name: Antônio Meneses
headline: Antônio Meneses, Renowned Brazilian Cellist, Is Dead at 66
abstract: Winning major competitions early on, he became one of his generation’s premier musicians, sought after by top conductors and recruited to the Beaux Arts Trio.

name: Simon Verity
profession: Master Stone Carver on Both Sides of the Atlantic
headline: Simon Verity, Master Stone Carver on Both Sides of the Atlantic, Dies at 79
abstract: His Old World craftsmanship extended from Canterbury Cathedral in England to the Cathedral of St. John the Divine in Manhattan.

name: Virginia Ogilvy
headline: Virginia Ogilvy, Confidante to Queen Elizabeth II, Dies at 91
abstract: Born into New York wealth and married to a Scottish earl, she was the only American lady-in-waiting to the queen, serving for nearly 50 years.

name: James Darren
headline: James Darren, Actor, Singer and ‘Gidget’ Heartthrob, Dies at 88
abstract: His role as a surfer in that trendsetting hit movie led to success on television shows like “The Time Tunnel” and “T.J. Hooker,” and on the pop charts.

name: Noel Parmentel Jr.
headline: Noel Parmentel Jr., Essayist, Polemicist and Apostate, Dies at 98
abstract: A self-described “reactionary individualist,” he mentored Joan Didion and was credited with famously comparing Nixon to a used-car salesman.

name: Jim Riswold
profession: Creator of Bo Knows and Air Jordan Ads
headline: Jim Riswold, Creator of ‘Bo Knows’ and Air Jordan Ads, Dies at 66
abstract: His work for Nike — particularly commercials starring Michael Jordan and Spike Lee — blurred the line between advertising and entertainment.

name: J. Richard Munro
profession: Oversaw the Creation of Time Warner
headline: J. Richard Munro, Who Oversaw the Creation of Time Warner, Dies at 93
abstract: As chief executive, he expanded Time Inc.’s offerings, fended off a hostile takeover and built the world’s largest media company.

name: Linda Deutsch
headline: Linda Deutsch, The A.P.’s Dean of Courtroom Reporting, Dies at 80
abstract: Covering notorious trials, she offered readers an unvarnished view of the sordid side of celebrity, told through many of the country’s most riveting legal dramas.

name: Steve Silberman
headline: Steve Silberman, 66, Dies; Writer Deepened Understanding of Autism
abstract: Prodded by Oliver Sacks, he wrote a humane, award-winning book about the condition. A music maven, he also wrote liner notes for the Grateful Dead and his friend David Crosby.

name: Rich Homie Quan
headline: Rich Homie Quan, Melodic Atlanta Rapper, Dies at 34
abstract: At one time affiliated with Young Thug, he had a hit in 2015 with “Flex (Ooh, Ooh, Ooh),” which spawned a dance craze.

name: Brian Ketcham
profession: Effective Foe of Traffic and Smog
headline: Brian Ketcham, Effective Foe of Traffic and Smog, Dies at 85
abstract: An engineer and influential environmentalist in New York, he fought for bus lanes, bridge tolls and limits on parking and against more highways, as in the aborted Westway plan.

name: Sergio Mendes
profession: Brought Brazilian Rhythms to the Pop Charts
headline: Sergio Mendes, 83, Dies; Brought Brazilian Rhythms to the Pop Charts
abstract: A pianist, composer and arranger, he rose to fame with the group Brasil ’66 and remained a force in popular music for more than six decades.

name: Ted Drewes Jr.
profession: Frozen Custard King of St. Louis
headline: Ted Drewes Jr., the Frozen Custard King of St. Louis, Dies at 96
abstract: Celebrity chefs and politicians paid tribute to the man behind the extra-thick shake known as the concrete, an intrinsic part of St. Louis summers.

name: Jackie Winsor
headline: Jackie Winsor, 82, Dies; Sculptor Who Hammered, Drilled and Chopped
abstract: She gave complexity to simple shapes, drawing inspiration from her rugged Canadian upbringing. In her downtime, she swung on a trapeze.

name: Gwendolyn B. Bennett
profession: Harlem Renaissance Star Plagued by Misfortune
headline: Overlooked No More: Gwendolyn B. Bennett, Harlem Renaissance Star Plagued by Misfortune
abstract: She was a talented young poet and artist who was central to a fledgling cultural movement, but her life was shrouded by one tragedy after another.

name: Nell McCafferty
headline: Nell McCafferty, Larger-Than-Life Irish Journalist, Dies at 80
abstract: Her pugnacious writing on women’s rights, gay rights and other issues helped turn her country into one of the most progressive in Europe.

name: Clark Halstead
headline: Clark Halstead, Real Estate Broker Who Broke the Mold, Dies at 83
abstract: He employed audacious marketing campaigns to lift his agency into the top tier of New York firms representing luxury properties.

name: Lloyd Ziff
headline: Lloyd Ziff, Visionary Photographer and Art Director, Dies at 81
abstract: He designed some of the most visually exciting magazines of the 1970s and ’80s. But his real love, and eventually his focus, was photography.

name: Greedy
profession: Father to Many African Penguins at Maryland Zoo
headline: Mr. Greedy, Father to Many African Penguins at Maryland Zoo, Dies at 33
abstract: An African penguin who left many offspring in his long life, he belonged to the largest colony of the aquatic bird species in North America, according to the zoo.

name: Dan Morgenstern
headline: Dan Morgenstern, Chronicler and Friend of Jazz, Dies at 94
abstract: He wrote prolifically about the music and played an important role in documenting its history, especially in his many years with the Institute of Jazz Studies.

name: María Benítez
headline: María Benítez, Dancer Who Championed Flamenco, Is Dead at 82
abstract: “People came from everywhere to see her shows,” an admirer said — including, on at least one occasion, the ballet superstar Mikhail Baryshnikov.

name: James Earl Jones
profession: Powerful Acting Resonated Onstage and Onscreen
headline: James Earl Jones, Whose Powerful Acting Resonated Onstage and Onscreen, Dies at 93
abstract: He gave life to characters like Darth Vader in “Star Wars” and Mufasa in “The Lion King,” and went on to collect Tonys, Golden Globes, Emmys and an honorary Oscar.

name: Maria E. Redo
headline: Maria E. Redo, Who Won Discounts for Older Adults, Dies at 99
abstract: She started a nonprofit in New York City in 1971 by asking stores if they would offer reduced prices for people 65 and over. Thousands of retailers said yes.

name: Ed Kranepool
headline: Ed Kranepool, a Teenage Met Who Lasted 18 Seasons, Dies at 79
abstract: “Steady Eddie” joined the team at 17, played in more games than any Met and in 1969 helped a once-woeful franchise pull off a “miracle” — a World Series title.

name: Will Jennings
profession: Oscar Winner for My Heart Will Go On
headline: Will Jennings, Oscar Winner for ‘My Heart Will Go On,’ Dies at 80
abstract: As an in-demand lyricist, he won a shelf of awards for hits with Steve Winwood, Eric Clapton and Dionne Warwick, as well as for the theme song for “Titanic.”

name: Francisco Lopera
headline: Francisco Lopera, Pioneer in Alzheimer’s Research, Dies at 73
abstract: A neurologist in Colombia, he worked with the world’s largest extended family with Alzheimer’s and helped fuel research to prevent or delay dementia symptoms.

name: Frankie Beverly
profession: Frontman of the Soul Group Maze
headline: Frankie Beverly, Frontman of the Soul Group Maze, Is Dead at 77
abstract: A consistent hitmaker on the R&B charts for almost 50 years, he had announced just this year that he would be retiring.

name: Donald Sheppard
headline: Donald Sheppard, British D-Day Veteran, Dies at 104
abstract: He helped liberate Bergen-Belsen, the Nazi concentration camp where Anne Frank had died.

name: Lloyd Kaufman
profession: Saw Answers Behind the Moon Illusion
headline: Lloyd Kaufman, Who Saw Answers Behind the ‘Moon Illusion,’ Dies at 97
abstract: He advanced the study of a millenniums-old mystery: why the moon appears larger on the horizon than it does high in the night sky.

name: James Sasser
profession: Senator and Clintons Envoy to China
headline: James Sasser, Senator and Clinton’s Envoy to China, Dies at 87
abstract: He became ambassador after three terms as a senator from Tennessee. In 1999, he was made a virtual prisoner in the embassy in Beijing during a siege by protesters.

name: Alberto Fujimori
profession: Leader of Peru Imprisoned for Rights Abuses
headline: Alberto Fujimori, 86, Leader of Peru Imprisoned for Rights Abuses, Dies
abstract: During his decade in power, he revived the economy and crushed two violent leftist insurgencies. But he was forced out in a corruption scandal and later imprisoned for human rights abuses.

name: Charles Biasiny-Rivera
headline: Charles Biasiny-Rivera, Champion of Latino Photography, Dies at 93
abstract: A New Yorker of Puerto Rican descent, he helped start a collective that brought recognition to Hispanic photographers and illuminated life in the city’s barrios.

name: Mark Jury
profession: Stark Photography Captured the Vietnam War
headline: Mark Jury, Whose Stark Photography Captured the Vietnam War, Dies at 80
abstract: He produced an early photo book about what he called the first “rock ’n’ roll war,” documented his grandfather’s dementia and became a filmmaker.

name: Bob Weatherwax
profession: Trainer of Lassie and Other Celebrity Dogs
headline: Bob Weatherwax, Trainer of Lassie and Other Celebrity Dogs, Dies at 83
abstract: Like his father, who taught him, he bred and coached the collies that played the heroic star of television and movies.

name: Sybil Haydel Morial
headline: Sybil Haydel Morial, New Orleans Civil Rights Matriarch, Dies at 91
abstract: The wife of Ernest N. Morial, the city’s first Black mayor, she fought for equal rights for Black women.

name: Joe Schmidt
profession: Made Middle Linebacker a Defensive Quarterback
headline: Joe Schmidt, 92, Dies; Made Middle Linebacker a ‘Defensive Quarterback’
abstract: A Hall of Famer who played for powerful Detroit Lions teams and later coached them, he embodied a tidal shift in N.F. L. strategy with the rise of the passing game.

name: Screamin’ Scott Simon
headline: Screamin’ Scott Simon, Dynamic Sha Na Na Keyboardist, Dies at 75
abstract: A mainstay and manager of a rock ’n’ roll nostalgia band, he wrote the lyrics to “Sandy,” a song heard in the hit film “Grease.”

name: Chad McQueen
headline: Chad McQueen, ‘Karate Kid’ Actor, Dies at 63
abstract: The son of Steve McQueen, he was most widely recognized for his role as Dutch in the hit 1984 teenage martial arts film and its sequel.

name: Rebecca Horn
headline: Rebecca Horn, Enigmatic Artist With Theatrical Flair, Dies at 80
abstract: Her widely exhibited work in sculpture, performance, film and more didn’t represent anything in particular so much as it evoked an experience.

name: Herbie Flowers
profession: Walk on the Wild Side Bassist
headline: Herbie Flowers, ‘Walk on the Wild Side’ Bassist, Dies at 86
abstract: A celebrated session musician who appeared on a host of classic rock albums, he made his most lasting mark with his contribution to Lou Reed’s most famous song.

name: Mary McFadden
headline: Mary McFadden, Celebrated Designer of Shimmering Dresses, Dies at 85
abstract: She took symbols from ancient cultures and translated them into intricate embroideries, beadings and paintings on clothes worn by the likes of Jacqueline Onassis.

name: R. Peter Munves
headline: R. Peter Munves, Master Marketer of Classical Music, Dies at 97
abstract: As an executive at Columbia and RCA Records, he popularized the classics for mass audiences by applying the same techniques used to sell pop music.

name: George Berci
headline: Dr. George Berci, Whose Innovations Changed Surgery, Dies at 103
abstract: He conceived many of the techniques and tools that have revolutionized minimally invasive operations and procedures.

name: Michaela DePrince
headline: Michaela DePrince, War Orphan Turned Leading Ballerina, Dies at 29
abstract: In an impoverished orphanage in Sierra Leone, she longed to dance ballet. After being adopted by American parents, her improbable dream came true.

name: Tito Jackson
headline: Tito Jackson, Jackson 5 Singer and Guitarist, Is Dead at 70
abstract: Alongside Michael and his other brothers, he provided a soundtrack for a generation of young listeners in the 1970s.

name: Derek Boshier
profession: British Pop Artist and Bowie Collaborator
headline: Derek Boshier, British Pop Artist and Bowie Collaborator, Dies at 87
abstract: Starting in the early 1960s, he set himself apart from his contemporaries with paintings that critiqued the cultural dominance of the United States.

name: Cathy Merrick
profession: Advocate for Indigenous People in Canada
headline: Cathy Merrick, 63, Advocate for Indigenous People in Canada, Dies
abstract: She was on the front lines of dogged fights against injustices, including a recent series of murders of Indigenous women by a white man.

name: Elias Khoury
profession: Master of the Modern Arabic Novel
headline: Elias Khoury, Master of the Modern Arabic Novel, Dies at 76
abstract: In his fiction and journalism, he sought to illustrate the story of the contemporary Middle East and his native Lebanon.

name: Harrison J. Goldin
profession: New York City Comptroller in Fiscal Crisis
headline: Harrison J. Goldin Dies at 88; New York City Comptroller in Fiscal Crisis
abstract: He weathered the storm as the city’s chief financial officer for 16 years and jousted with Mayor Koch in a public feud and a losing primary bid to replace him.

name: Frederick Schauer
headline: Frederick Schauer, Scholar Who Scrutinized Free Speech, Dies at 78
abstract: In more than a dozen books and several hundred articles, he devoted himself, as he once said, to “questioning the unquestionable or thinking the unthinkable.”

name: John Cassaday
headline: John Cassaday, Award-Winning Comic Book Artist, Dies at 52
abstract: In series like Planetary, of which he was a creator, and Astonishing X-Men, his drawings conveyed a sense of realism in situations that were often fantastical.

name: Dusko Doder
profession: Cold War Journalist Falsely Accused of K.G.B. Ties
headline: Dusko Doder, 87, Cold War Journalist Falsely Accused of K.G.B. Ties, Dies
abstract: His career was ruined when Time magazine reported that the Soviets had recruited him while he led The Washington Post’s Moscow bureau. Sued for libel, Time apologized.

name: Valarie D’Elia
profession: Travel Reporter on TV and Radio
headline: Valarie D’Elia, Travel Reporter on TV and Radio, Dies at 64
abstract: She steered vacationers and business travelers to choice destinations, talked about the best deals, and offered up savvy tips on how to avoid vexation.

name: JD Souther
profession: Wrote Hits for the Eagles and More
headline: JD Souther, Who Wrote Hits for the Eagles and More, Dies at 78
abstract: A central figure in the Southern California rock scene of the 1970s, he later had a regular role on the TV show “Nashville.”

name: Lucine Amara
profession: Familiar Soprano at the Met Saw Bias There
headline: Lucine Amara, 99, Dies; Familiar Soprano at the Met Saw Bias There
abstract: She sang with the Metropolitan Opera for decades, often on short notice, including after lodging a successful age discrimination complaint against the company.

name: Mark Podwal
headline: Mark Podwal, Prolific Artist of Jewish Themes, Dies at 79
abstract: His art included cartoons for The New York Times, collaborations with Elie Wiesel and images that traced the history of antisemitism. He was also a dermatologist.

name: John A. Clements
profession: His Research Saved Thousands of Babies
headline: John A. Clements Dies at 101; His Research Saved Thousands of Babies
abstract: He identified the cause of a respiratory condition that was killing 10,000 infants a year in the United States. Then he helped design a drug that slashed those mortality rates.

name: Otis Davis
profession: Overcame Racism to Win Olympic Gold
headline: Otis Davis, Who Overcame Racism to Win Olympic Gold, Dies at 92
abstract: At the 1960 Summer Games in Rome, he set a world record in the 400-meter race and another in the 4 x 400 relay, where he anchored the United States team’s victory.

name: Ellen Armstrong
headline: Overlooked No More: Ellen Armstrong, ‘Marvelous, Mystifying’ Magician of Mirth
abstract: Carrying on a family tradition, she brought her singular act, full of illusion and humor, to Black audiences in the segregated South and on up to Philadelphia.

name: Nelson DeMille
headline: Nelson DeMille, Blockbuster Author Who Thrilled Millions, Dies at 81
abstract: In best seller after best seller, world-weary investigators tackled military malfeasance and Russian spies, cracking jokes and beers to the delight of legions of devoted fans.

name: Michel Siffre
profession: Descended Into Caves to Study the Human Mind
headline: Michel Siffre, 85, Dies; Descended Into Caves to Study the Human Mind
abstract: He was a pioneer in chronobiology, the study of how our bodies understand the passage of time.

name: Billy Edd Wheeler
headline: Billy Edd Wheeler, Songwriter Who Celebrated Rural Life, Dies at 91
abstract: His plain-spoken songs were recorded by Elvis Presley, Kenny Rogers and many others. The duo of Johnny Cash and June Carter made his “Jackson” a huge country hit.

name: Robert Lansdorp
headline: Robert Lansdorp, Coach of Tennis Champions, Is Dead at 85
abstract: His students, including Tracy Austin, Maria Sharapova, Pete Sampras and Lindsay Davenport, developed their ground strokes through his regimen of intense repetition.

name: Daniel J. Evans
headline: Daniel J. Evans, 98, Washington State Governor Who Went to Senate, Dies
abstract: A moderate Republican, he championed education, civil rights and environmental causes as a three-term governor and on Capitol Hill. He was eyed as a potential vice president.

name: Mercury Morris
profession: Elusive Rusher on a Perfect Dolphins Team
headline: Mercury Morris, Elusive Rusher on a Perfect Dolphins Team, Dies at 77
abstract: Part of a talented backfield triumvirate that also included Larry Csonka and Jim Kiick, he helped lead Miami to two Super Bowls and an undefeated season.

name: Tongsun Park
headline: Tongsun Park, Lobbyist Scarred by Koreagate Scandal, Dies at 89
abstract: An amiable Korean-born graduate of Georgetown University, he was imprisoned after a second scandal involving the U.N.

name: Kathryn Crosby
headline: Kathryn Crosby, Actress and Bing Crosby’s Widow, Dies at 90
abstract: She was a Texas-born starlet when she married the beloved crooner, but put aside her career at his urging.

name: Benny Golson
profession: Saxophonist and Composer of Jazz Standards
headline: Benny Golson, Saxophonist and Composer of Jazz Standards, Dies at 95
abstract: After forming a lauded band and writing tunes like “I Remember Clifford,” “Whisper Not” and “Killer Joe,” he had a second career composing and arranging music for television.

name: Caterina Valente
headline: Caterina Valente, Singer Who Was a Star on Two Continents, Dies at 93
abstract: Born in Paris to Italian parents and raised in Germany, she had her own show on television in the 1950s and was later a small-screen mainstay in the U.S.

name: Fredric Jameson
headline: Fredric Jameson, Critic Who Linked Literature to Capitalism, Dies at 90
abstract: Among the world’s leading academic critics, he brought his analytical rigor to topics as diverse as German opera and sci-fi movies.

name: Dick Moss
profession: Helped Usher In Baseball Free Agency
headline: Dick Moss, Who Helped Usher In Baseball Free Agency, Dies at 93
abstract: A labor lawyer, he was crucial to toppling a decades-old system that bound players to teams year after year, setting the stage for their rich contracts of today.

name: Cat Glover
headline: Cat Glover, Who Danced With Prince, Dies at 62
abstract: She worked with Prince on many of his signature works, including the “Sign o’ the Times” tour and the “U Got the Look” music video.

name: Naftali Herstik
headline: Naftali Herstik, Soulful and Influential Cantor, Dies at 77
abstract: Part of a long line of cantors, he led services at the Great Synagogue in Jerusalem for 30 years and helped train the next generation.

name: Frank Coppa
headline: Frank Coppa, Who Turned Against a Mobster Family, Dies at 82
abstract: His decision to describe murders to the F.B.I. led at least 10 other members of the Bonanno family to do the same and ultimately immobilized a mafia family.

name: Lloyd Macklowe
headline: Lloyd Macklowe, Leading Purveyor of Art Nouveau, Is Dead at 90
abstract: He and his wife began buying pieces to furnish their apartment. They wound up with a museum-quality collection and a pre-eminent retail business.

name: Nick Gravenites
profession: Mainstay of the San Francisco Rock Scene
headline: Nick Gravenites, Mainstay of the San Francisco Rock Scene, Dies at 85
abstract: A blues devotee from Chicago, he tasted fame in the late 1960s with the Electric Flag, a band that made its debut at Monterey but proved short-lived.

name: Maggie Smith
profession: Grande Dame of Stage and Screen
headline: Maggie Smith, Grande Dame of Stage and Screen, Dies at 89
abstract: She earned an extraordinary array of awards, from Oscars to Emmys to a Tony, but she could still go almost everywhere unrecognized. Then came “Downton Abbey.”

name: Neil King Jr.
profession: Wrote of a Long Walk of Renewal
headline: Neil King Jr., Who Wrote of a Long Walk of ‘Renewal,’ Dies at 65
abstract: His book, “American Ramble,” lyrically recounted a 330-mile trek from Washington, D.C., to New York City while he was in remission from cancer.

name: Richard Pettibone
headline: Richard Pettibone, Master of the Artistic Miniature, Dies at 86
abstract: He painted tiny reproductions of works by Warhol, Lichtenstein, Duchamp and many others, raising questions about originality and creativity.

name: Clarice Rivers
headline: Clarice Rivers, Earthy Muse of Two Artists, Dies at 88
abstract: She inspired Niki de Saint Phalle to create the fantastical female avatars she called the Nanas. She also inspired her husband, Larry Rivers.

name: Amadou Mahtar M’Bow
profession: His Tenure Leading UNESCO Was Stormy
headline: Amadou Mahtar M’Bow, 103, Dies; His Tenure Leading UNESCO Was Stormy
abstract: He was the first Black African to head a major international organization, but complaints about his administration led the U.S. and Britain to pull out of it.

name: Bill Lucy
profession: Pioneering Labor and Civil Rights Leader
headline: Bill Lucy, Pioneering Labor and Civil Rights Leader, Dies at 90
abstract: He helped popularize “I Am a Man” as a demand for respect during the 1968 strike by Black sanitation workers in Memphis.

name: Antônio Delfim Netto
headline: Antônio Delfim Netto, Brazilian Economic Czar, Dies at 96
abstract: He was credited for the high-growth economy during the early years of Brazil’s long military dictatorship. But critics said his policies brought only short-lived gains.

name: Kris Kristofferson
headline: Kris Kristofferson, Country Singer, Songwriter and Actor, Dies at 88
abstract: He wrote songs for hundreds of other artists, including “Me and Bobby McGee” for Janis Joplin and “Sunday Morning Coming Down” for Johnny Cash, before a second act in film.

name: Dikembe Mutombo
headline: Dikembe Mutombo, a Towering N.B.A. Presence, Dies at 58
abstract: Mr. Mutombo, who did not begin playing basketball until adolescence, retired with the second-most blocked shots in league history.

name: Donna Henes
headline: Donna Henes,‘Urban Shaman’ Who Heralded the Seasons, Dies at 79
abstract: Her solstice and equinox celebrations might involve an egg-balancing ritual and bonfires, all to remind modern New Yorkers of their humble place in the cosmos.

name: Ella Leffland
headline: Ella Leffland, Novelist Drawn to Portraying Outsiders, Dies at 92
abstract: Her work often drew from her upbringing in California amid World War II, such as her intricate novel about the Nazi leader Hermann Goering.

name: John Amos
profession: Star of Good Times and Roots
headline: John Amos, a Star of ‘Good Times’ and ‘Roots,’ Is Dead at 84
abstract: He was the patriarch in one of the first sitcoms with an all-Black cast and an enslaved African in the American South in a blockbuster TV mini-series.

name: Frank Fritz
profession: Host of the Antiques Show American Pickers
headline: Frank Fritz, a Host of the Antiques Show ‘American Pickers,’ Dies at 60
abstract: He and his friend Mike Wolfe launched the treasure-hunting show in 2010, part of a wave of reality TV aimed at finding fortune in everyday items.

name: Song Binbin
profession: Poster Woman for Maos Bloody Upheaval
headline: Song Binbin, Poster Woman for Mao’s Bloody Upheaval, Dies at 77
abstract: She was said to have been involved in the first killing of an educator during the Cultural Revolution, drawing official praise. She later apologized for her actions.

name: Ken Page
profession: Starred in Cats and Voiced Oogie Boogie
headline: Ken Page, Who Starred in ‘Cats’ and Voiced Oogie Boogie, Dies at 70
abstract: His career on Broadway spanned decades. But he has probably best known for providing the voice of the boogeyman in “The Nightmare Before Christmas.”

name: Ozzie Virgil Sr.
headline: Ozzie Virgil Sr., First Dominican-Born Major Leaguer, Dies at 92
abstract: An outstanding fielder though never an All-Star, he broke that barrier with the Giants in 1956 and later became the Tigers’ first Black player.

name: Eugene Gold
headline: Eugene Gold, Brooklyn D.A. Who Led the ‘Son of Sam’ Case, Dies at 100
abstract: He prosecuted high-profile cases in the 1970s and championed Soviet Jews, but, after retiring, he ran afoul of the law himself, charged with a sex offense.

name: Masamitsu Yoshioka
headline: Masamitsu Yoshioka, Last Pearl Harbor Bombardier, Dies at 106
abstract: He was 23 years old when he took part in the attack that triggered America’s declaration of war against Japan. He rarely spoke publicly about it.

name: Jay J. Armes
profession: Private Eye With a Superhero Story
headline: Jay J. Armes, Private Eye With a Superhero Story, Dies at 92
abstract: With steel hooks for hands and a flamboyant personality, Mr. Armes captured the attention, and scrutiny, of reporters across the nation.

name: Joel Fleishman
headline: Joel Fleishman, Influential Expert on Philanthropy, Dies at 90
abstract: Officially, he was an authority on nonprofit foundations. Unofficially, he was an unparalleled networker among the nation’s rich and powerful.

name: Joe D. Bryan
profession: His Murder Conviction Raised Troubling Questions
headline: Joe D. Bryan, 84, Dies; His Murder Conviction Raised Troubling Questions
abstract: After serving 33 years in prison, he was released in the wake of a cascade of questions about the soundness of the forensic testimony against him.

name: Richard Mayhew
headline: Richard Mayhew, Painter of Abstract Landscapes, Dies at 100
abstract: He drew from his Black and Native American heritage, as well as his own memory, to find an emotional resonance behind the beauty of nature.

name: David Burnham
headline: David Burnham, Times Reporter Who Exposed Police Graft, Dies at 91
abstract: Tipped off by the detective Frank Serpico, he wrote an explosive series on police corruption in New York City, sparking an investigation by the Knapp commission.

name: Marvin Schlachter
headline: Marvin Schlachter, Record Executive Who Championed Disco, Dies at 90
abstract: In the 1960s, he helped get wide exposure for Black artists like Dionne Warwick. A decade later, he brought dance music from the clubs to radio success.

name: James Magee
profession: Creator of a Mysterious Desert Monument
headline: James Magee, Creator of a Mysterious Desert Monument, Dies at 79
abstract: For 40 years, he built a group of stone and steel buildings in the West Texas desert to house his own monumental work. Only a few have been lucky enough to see it.

name: Peter Jay
profession: Headline-Making British Ambassador to the U.S
headline: Peter Jay, Headline-Making British Ambassador to the U.S., Dies at 87
abstract: His appointment sparked criticism and charges of nepotism. He later achieved unwanted attention as a character in the novel “Heartburn.”

name: Susie Maxwell Berning
headline: Susie Maxwell Berning, Hall of Fame Golfer, Is Dead at 83
abstract: She often took time away from the tour for her family. But she tallied 11 championships, including three in the U.S. Women’s Open.

name: Christopher Ciccone
headline: Christopher Ciccone, Who Dished About His Sister Madonna, Dies at 63
abstract: An artist, designer, choreographer and dancer, he was best known for writing a grudge-settling memoir about his formerly close bond with the pop star.

name: Robert Coover
headline: Robert Coover, Inventive Novelist in Iconoclastic Era, Dies at 92
abstract: Once called “probably the funniest and most malicious” of the postmodernists, his books reflected a career-long interest in reimagining folk stories, fairy tales and political myths.

name: Lore Segal
headline: Lore Segal, Mordant Novelist of Émigré Life, Dies at 96
abstract: Transported to safe haven in England as a Jewish child in 1938, she explored themes of displacement with penetrating wit in autobiographical fiction like “Other People’s Houses.”

name: Cissy Houston
profession: Gospel Star Guided Daughter Whitneys Rise
headline: Cissy Houston Dies at 91; Gospel Star Guided Daughter Whitney’s Rise
abstract: Hailing from a musical family, she won Grammys, sang backup to Elvis Presley and Aretha Franklin and helped shepherd Whitney Houston to superstardom.

name: Luis Tiant
headline: Luis Tiant, Crowd-Pleasing Pitcher Who Baffled Hitters, Dies at 83
abstract: Cuban-born and charismatic, with a personal tale caught up in politics, he was a dominant hurler with a quirky windup who helped lead the Red Sox to a pennant in 1975.

name: Greg Landry
headline: Greg Landry, Scrambling All-Pro Quarterback, Is Dead at 77
abstract: Known for his legs as well as for his arm, he was the last Detroit Lions quarterback to make the Pro Bowl for more than 40 years.

name: Lily Ebert
headline: Lily Ebert, Holocaust Survivor, Author and TikTok Star, Dies at 100
abstract: She survived Auschwitz, wrote a best-selling memoir, “Lily’s Promise,” and spoke to a following of 2 million fans on TikTok.

name: Thomas Rockwell
profession: Taught Children How to Eat Fried Worms
headline: Thomas Rockwell, 91, Dies; Taught Children ‘How to Eat Fried Worms’
abstract: His father, Norman Rockwell, depicted his childhood on covers of The Saturday Evening Post. The worms came later.

name: David Anfam
headline: David Anfam, Leading Scholar of Abstract Expressionism, Dies at 69
abstract: He wrote seminal texts on the artists Clyfford Still and Mark Rothko, in a jargon-free style that won him readers far outside the art world.

name: Ratan Tata
headline: Ratan Tata, Whose Indian Business Empire Went Global, Dies at 86
abstract: The patriarch of a powerful family, his Tata Group put an indelible stamp on Indian life while acquiring British brand names like Tetley Tea and Jaguar.

name: Donald L. Barlett
headline: Donald L. Barlett, 88, Dies; Prizewinning Reporter Bared Corruption
abstract: Over four decades, he and his colleague James B. Steele gained renown for resourceful, often explosive investigative journalism at The Philadelphia Inquirer.

name: Ethel Kennedy
profession: Passionate Supporter of the Family Legacy
headline: Ethel Kennedy, Passionate Supporter of the Family Legacy, Dies at 96
abstract: She never remarried after the assassination of her husband, Senator Robert F. Kennedy, and she devoted herself to working on behalf of the causes he had championed.

name: Billy Shaw
headline: Billy Shaw, a Singular Hall of Fame Lineman, Dies at 85
abstract: He was the only inductee to play his entire career in the American Football League, where he helped the Buffalo Bills win two championships in the 1960s.

name: Tim Johnson
headline: Tim Johnson, Senator Who Came Back From an Aneurysm, Dies at 77
abstract: One of the last Democrats from the Great Plains to be elected to national office, he built his career on delivering benefits to his home state, South Dakota.

name: Frances Conley
headline: Frances Conley, Neurosurgeon Who Protested Sexism, Dies at 83
abstract: She was the rare woman in her field, and a tenured professor. But when a sexist colleague was promoted, she quit, forcing a reckoning in her profession.

name: Warren Wilson
headline: Warren Wilson, Pioneering Los Angeles TV Reporter, Dies at 90
abstract: In addition to covering the 1992 riots and other historically significant events, he helped facilitate the surrenders of 22 fugitives.

name: Nobuyo Oyama
headline: Nobuyo Oyama, the Japanese Voice of Doraemon, Dies at 90
abstract: Her alto timbre, for which she was teased as a child, and radiant laughter shaped how millions experienced the blue robot in the quintessential anime of the same name.

name: Joseph H. Reich
headline: Joseph H. Reich, Charter School Pioneer, Dies at 89
abstract: When he and his wife opened the Beginning With Children school in Brooklyn to offer more educational opportunities to children, they set off a national trend.

name: Mariama Bâ
headline: Overlooked No More: Mariama Bâ, Voice of African Feminism
abstract: She became a literary star in Senegal with novels that addressed women’s issues as the country, newly free from French colonial rule, was discovering its identity.

name: Allan Blye
profession: Smothers Brothers Writer and Super Dave Creator
headline: Allan Blye, 87, Dies; ‘Smothers Brothers’ Writer and ‘Super Dave’ Creator
abstract: In his wide-ranging career, he also helped write Elvis Presley’s comeback special and appeared on an early version of “Mister Rogers’ Neighborhood.”

name: David Garrard Lowe
headline: David Garrard Lowe, Defender of Historic Architecture, Dies at 91
abstract: For over 50 years, as a historian, lecturer and author, he fought to protect Beaux-Arts buildings in New York and Chicago from falling to the developer’s wrecking ball.

name: Alex Salmond
headline: Alex Salmond, Scotland’s Former First Minister, Dies at 69
abstract: He led the Scottish National Party twice, guiding it from a fringe political group into a powerful electoral force in Britain.

name: Abdul Salaam
profession: Quiet Member of the Jets Sack Exchange
headline: Abdul Salaam, Quiet Member of the Jets’ ‘Sack Exchange,’ Dies at 71
abstract: A defensive tackle, he teamed with Joe Klecko, Mark Gastineau and Marty Lyons in the 1980s on a line that terrorized quarterbacks.

name: Lilly Ledbetter
profession: Fight for Equal Pay Changed U.S. Law
headline: Lilly Ledbetter, Whose Fight for Equal Pay Changed U.S. Law, Dies at 86
abstract: Her lawsuit against Goodyear helped pave the way for the 2009 Fair Pay Act, which was signed into law by former President Barack Obama.

name: Lillian Schwartz
headline: Lillian Schwartz, Pioneer in Computer-Generated Art, Dies at 97
abstract: Early in the digital era, she worked at Bell Labs on the intersection of art and technology, making films and at one point arriving at a novel theory about the “Mona Lisa.”

name: Ka
profession: Lone Soldier of New Yorks Underground Rap Scene
headline: Ka, Lone Soldier of New York’s Underground Rap Scene, Dies at 52
abstract: The rapper, whose birth name was Kaseem Ryan, self-produced 11 albums while also maintaining a career with the New York Fire Department.

name: Megan Marshack
profession: Was With Nelson Rockefeller at His Death
headline: Megan Marshack Dies at 70; Was With Nelson Rockefeller at His Death
abstract: She was at the center of rumors about the former vice president’s last moments, but she remained silent about their association until she wrote her own obituary.

name: Paul Lowe
headline: Paul Lowe, Award-Winning British Photojournalist, Dies at 60
abstract: He was fatally stabbed outside Los Angeles, and his 19-year-old son was arrested. Mr. Lowe had earned acclaim for documenting the siege of Sarajevo and other conflicts.

name: Thomas J. Donohue
headline: Thomas J. Donohue Dies at 86; Transformed Chamber of Commerce
abstract: Under his 24-year leadership, the lobbying group developed enormous clout in Washington, but he broke with the Trump administration over immigration, tariffs and the 2020 election.

name: Richard V. Secord
headline: Richard V. Secord, Middleman in Iran-Contra Scandal, Is Dead at 92
abstract: A war hero and a former Air Force general, he denied wrongdoing for his role in the Reagan-era shipment of arms to Iran to support Nicaraguan rebels.

name: Leif Segerstam
headline: Leif Segerstam, Who Wrote 371 Symphonies, Is Dead at 80
abstract: He mystified his Finnish countrymen with an unstoppable flow of compositions. He was also, one journalist said, “an alarming person to interview.”

name: Liam Payne
headline: Liam Payne, 31, Former One Direction Singer, Dies in Fall in Argentina
abstract: Payne, who was one of the group’s standout singers, fell from the third floor of a hotel in Buenos Aires, emergency services officials said.

name: Yahya Sinwar
headline: Yahya Sinwar, Leader of Hamas, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Sinwar climbed the ranks of the Palestinian militant group to plot the deadliest attack on Israel in its history.

name: Mitzi Gaynor
headline: Mitzi Gaynor, Leading Lady of Movie Musicals, Is Dead at 93
abstract: She was best known for starring in the 1958 screen version of “South Pacific.” But her Hollywood career was brief, and she soon shifted her focus to Las Vegas and TV.

name: Arie Kopelman
headline: Arie Kopelman, a Driving Force in Expanding Chanel, Dies at 86
abstract: Arriving at the luxury house two years after Karl Lagerfeld, he helped guide a boom in both products and revenues as president of the company’s American arm, Chanel Inc.

name: Bob Yerkes
headline: Bob Yerkes, Bruised but Durable Hollywood Stuntman, Dies at 92
abstract: A body double to the stars, he performed sometimes bone-breaking feats in movies like “Return of the Jedi” and “Back to the Future.” And he was still at it in his 80s.

name: Adam Abeshouse
headline: Adam Abeshouse, Prolific Producer of Classical Music, Dies at 63
abstract: A trained violinist, he found his calling in the studio control room. He also started a foundation to help fund recordings that lack major-label support.

name: Marvin Preston IV
profession: Saved the Martha Graham Dance Company
headline: Marvin Preston IV, 80, Dies; Saved the Martha Graham Dance Company
abstract: An expert at rescuing distressed companies, he took over the struggling organization in 2000, leading it through a painful restructuring and a lengthy legal battle.

name: Nicholas Daniloff
profession: Reporters Arrest in Moscow Ignited a Firestorm
headline: Nicholas Daniloff, 89, Dies; Reporter’s Arrest in Moscow Ignited a Firestorm
abstract: A veteran foreign correspondent during the Cold War, he was held on trumped-up espionage charges. He credited President Ronald Reagan with fighting for his release.

name: Libby Titus
headline: Libby Titus, Introspective Singer and Songwriter, Dies at 77
abstract: Her “Love Has No Pride” was widely recorded, and she had high-profile relationships with Levon Helm and Donald Fagen. But she was uneasy with life in the spotlight.

name: Sammy Basso
headline: Sammy Basso, Advocate for Progeria Research, Is Dead at 28
abstract: One of about 150 people known to have a rare condition that causes rapid aging, he sought to raise awareness and participated in the search for a cure.

name: Toni Vaz
profession: Stuntwoman and Founder of N.A.A.C.P. Image Awards
headline: Toni Vaz, Stuntwoman and Founder of N.A.A.C.P. Image Awards, Dies at 101
abstract: She created a program to honor Black artistic success in the 1960s. But she spent decades trying to get its organizers to recognize her role.

name: Michael Valentine
profession: Helped Drivers Stay Under the Radar
headline: Michael Valentine, 74, Who Helped Drivers Stay Under the Radar, Dies
abstract: An engineer who loved to drive fast, he helped build an industry-altering device that made its debut after the national speed limit of 55 m.p.h. became law.

name: Sally Butler
headline: Sally Butler, Nun Who Blew the Whistle on Sex Abuse, Dies at 93
abstract: In the 1960s, she worked with priests to serve residents of housing projects in Brooklyn. Decades later, she learned that those priests had been abusing young boys.

name: Fethullah Gulen
headline: Fethullah Gulen, Turkish Cleric and Erdogan Rival, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Gulen, who lived in the United States, was accused of plotting a coup against President Recep Tayyip Erdogan of Turkey in 2016.

name: Ralph Jennings
profession: Built Up Fordhams Public Radio Station
headline: Ralph Jennings, 86, Dies; Built Up Fordham’s Public Radio Station
abstract: He transformed WFUV from “a sandbox” into a professional operation, increasing its listenership nearly tenfold.

name: Andrew V. Schally
profession: Scientist Shared Nobel Glory With Rival
headline: Andrew V. Schally, 97, Dies; Scientist Shared Nobel Glory With Rival
abstract: His two-decade quest to find elusive brain hormones became a race against Roger Guillemin, a onetime colleague and an eventual fellow prizewinner.

name: Paul Di’Anno
headline: Paul Di’Anno, Early Iron Maiden Frontman, Dies at 66
abstract: He sang with the band in its early years before being replaced by Bruce Dickinson. He later worked with other bands and pursued a solo career.

name: Bruce Ames
profession: Biochemist Discovered Test for Toxic Chemicals
headline: Bruce Ames, 95, Dies; Biochemist Discovered Test for Toxic Chemicals
abstract: The Ames Test offered a fast and inexpensive way to identify carcinogens, leading to the banning of chemicals linked to cancer and birth defects.

name: Ward Christensen
headline: Ward Christensen, Early Visionary of Social Media, Dies at 78
abstract: Housebound during a 1978 blizzard, he and a friend began devising the first computer bulletin board, a forerunner of online services like Reddit, TikTok and Facebook.

name: Thelma Mothershed Wair
headline: Thelma Mothershed Wair, 83, Dies; One of 9 Who Integrated a School
abstract: In 1957, she and eight other Black students — the Little Rock Nine — enrolled in a high school in the face of racist mobs and a resistant Jim Crow governor.

name: Stan Asofsky
profession: Vociferous Courtside Superfan of the Knicks
headline: Stan Asofsky, Vociferous Courtside Superfan of the Knicks, Dies at 87
abstract: For decades, beginning in 1959, he was a regular presence at Madison Square Garden (in two locations), befriending players and heckling opposing players and refs.

name: Yehuda Bauer
headline: Yehuda Bauer, 98, Scholar Who Saw Jewish Resistance in Holocaust, Dies
abstract: A leading historian of antisemitism, he countered the prevailing narrative of Jewish victimhood and later pushed back against efforts to diminish the Holocaust’s significance.

name: Fernando Valenzuela
headline: Fernando Valenzuela, Pitcher Whose Screwballs Eluded Batters, Dies at 63
abstract: The Los Angeles Dodgers star won the Rookie of the Year and Cy Young Awards in 1981, when “Fernandomania” made him a household name and filled ballparks.

name: Julia Hawkins
headline: Julia Hawkins, Centenarian Sprinter, Dies at 108
abstract: She took up running after her 100th birthday at the encouragement of her children, and went on to set two world records in the 100-meter dash.

name: Gustavo Gutiérrez
headline: Gustavo Gutiérrez, Father of Liberation Theology, Dies at 96
abstract: Once considered revolutionary, his notion of empathy and advocacy for the poor has become a central tenet of Catholic social teaching.

name: Ron Ely
profession: Played an Updated Tarzan in the 1960s
headline: Ron Ely, Who Played an Updated Tarzan in the 1960s, Dies at 86
abstract: He later built a career as a reliable TV guest star. His life turned tragic in 2019 when his son killed Mr. Ely’s wife and was then shot to death by the police.

name: Monique Knowlton
headline: Monique Knowlton, ’60s-Era Model and Provocative Gallerist, Dies at 87
abstract: A Vogue cover girl in the early 1960s, she later pivoted to contemporary art, opening a gallery where being “outrageous counts as a plus,” one critic wrote.

name: Antonio Skármeta
profession: Wrote of Chiles Tears and Turmoil
headline: Antonio Skármeta, Who Wrote of Chile’s Tears and Turmoil, Dies at 83
abstract: His literary career traced the arc of his country’s modern political journey in stories about ordinary citizens facing repression and arbitrary government.

name: Tina S. Kaidanow
profession: Diplomatic Force in Kosovo and Guantánamo
headline: Tina S. Kaidanow, 59, Diplomatic Force in Kosovo and Guantánamo, Dies
abstract: She was the first U.S. ambassador to a newly independent Balkans nation and recently oversaw the transfer of cooperating Guantánamo prisoners to third countries.

name: Lynda Obst
headline: Lynda Obst, Producer, Dies at 74; Championed Women in Hollywood
abstract: She helped make films like “Sleepless in Seattle” and “Contact.” She also wrote widely about the industry, for The Times and other publications.

name: Patti McGee
headline: Patti McGee, Skateboarding’s First Female Champion, Dies at 79
abstract: She was on the cover of Life magazine and performed for Johnny Carson. She was, her daughter said, “a badass and a goody two-shoes at the same time.”

name: Jack Jones
headline: Jack Jones, a Suave, Hit-Making and Enduring Crooner, Dies at 86
abstract: With his smooth voice, he drew crowds to cabarets and music halls for six decades. He also sang the themes for films and TV shows, including “The Love Boat.”

name: Philip Zimbardo
headline: Philip Zimbardo, 91, Whose Stanford Prison Experiment Studied Evil, Dies
abstract: His provocative research made him a popular figure on campus. But his exploration of how good people can turn evil raised ethical questions.

name: Safeya Binzagr
profession: Saudi Artist Celebrated but Long Unseen
headline: Safeya Binzagr, 84, a Saudi Artist Celebrated but Long Unseen, Dies
abstract: Despite the gender restrictions of Saudi society, she claimed a place for herself, and other women, in the country’s art scene.

name: Margaret E. Knight
profession: Innovator of the Flat-Bottomed Paper Bag
headline: Overlooked No More: Margaret E. Knight, Innovator of the Flat-Bottomed Paper Bag
abstract: She came up with a method of automation so that workers would not have to make the bags by hand. Then she fought for credit for her work.

name: Barbara Dane
headline: Barbara Dane, Who Fought Injustice Through Song, Dies at 97
abstract: She was highly regarded as a folk, blues and jazz singer. She was also ardently left-wing and prioritized social change over commercial success.

name: Phil Lesh
headline: Phil Lesh, Bassist Who Anchored the Grateful Dead, Dies at 84
abstract: One of the first rock bassists whose instrument regularly took a lead role, he also had a hand in writing some of the band’s best-known songs.

name: Gary Indiana
headline: Gary Indiana, Acerbic Cultural Critic and Novelist, Dies at 74
abstract: He made films, video art and photographs, but was best known as a pioneering art critic and mordant novelist.

name: Tom Jarriel
headline: Tom Jarriel, Globetrotting ABC News Reporter, Is Dead at 89
abstract: In his 37 years at the network, he was a White House correspondent, weekend anchor and correspondent for “20/20.” He won 19 Emmy Awards.

name: Claire Daly
headline: Claire Daly, Master of the Baritone Saxophone, Dies at 66
abstract: She was celebrated for both her playing and her love of the jazz community. “My life in music,” she said recently, “is the smartest thing I’ve done.”

name: Mimi Hines
headline: Mimi Hines, a Replacement Star in ‘Funny Girl,’ Dies at 91
abstract: She was best known as half of a comedy team with her husband, Phil Ford, until her hall-filling voice earned her raves in a role made famous by Barbra Streisand.

name: DJ Clark Kent
headline: DJ Clark Kent, Who Introduced Jay-Z to Notorious B.I.G., Dies at 58
abstract: He was a producer and club D.J. who helped rappers find their voices and fortunes, and who later became known as a raconteur of hip-hop history.

name: Paul Morrissey
headline: Paul Morrissey, Andy Warhol’s Cinematic Collaborator, Dies at 86
abstract: In films like “Trash” and “Women in Revolt,” he brought movement, character and something resembling a story line to the Warhol film aesthetic.

name: Steve Mariotti
profession: Trauma Led Him to Help Youths at Risk
headline: Steve Mariotti, Whose Trauma Led Him to Help Youths at Risk, Dies at 71
abstract: After he was mugged, he took a therapist’s advice to work with “difficult students at a difficult school.” They ignored him until the lessons turned to business.

name: Teri Garr
headline: Teri Garr, Comic Actress in Offbeat Roles, Is Dead at 79
abstract: An Oscar nominee for her role in “Tootsie,” she was also a favorite guest of David Letterman and Johnny Carson and a three-time host of “Saturday Night Live.”

name: John Gierach
profession: Fly Fishing Author With Wit and Wisdom
headline: John Gierach, Fly Fishing Author With Wit and Wisdom, Dies at 77
abstract: Writing for anglers and amateurs alike, he found that the sport can reveal as much about people as it does about fish.

name: Rudy May
headline: Rudy May, a Stingy Master of the Curveball, Dies at 80
abstract: He overcame a dip in velocity to find pitching success with four teams, including the Yankees and Orioles, and had a dominant season in 1980.

name: Lewis Sorley
profession: Said the U.S. Won (but Then Lost) in Vietnam
headline: Lewis Sorley, 90, Who Said the U.S. Won (but Then Lost) in Vietnam, Dies
abstract: His Pulitzer Prize-nominated history of the war was warmly received by the Pentagon, but rejected elsewhere for ignoring what many said made the war “unwinnable.”

name: Charles Brandt
headline: Charles Brandt, Whose Book Inspired ‘The Irishman,’ Dies at 82
abstract: “I Heard You Paint Houses,” his true-crime best seller about the death of Jimmy Hoffa, was brought to the screen by Martin Scorsese and Robert De Niro.

name: Tsunehisa Katsumata
profession: Top Executive in Power Plant Meltdown
headline: Tsunehisa Katsumata, Top Executive in Power Plant Meltdown, Dies at 84
abstract: He was sued and prosecuted for his actions as chairman of the Japanese power company that ran the Fukushima nuclear facility when it failed in a 2011 earthquake and tsunami.

name: Richard A. Fineberg
headline: Richard A. Fineberg, Relentless Skeptic of Alaska Pipeline, Dies at 83
abstract: A journalist and an analyst, he was driven to hold oil companies accountable. Earlier, he was on the storied boat Greenpeace when he and others tried to halt a nuclear test.

name: Richard A. Cash
headline: Richard A. Cash, Who Saved Millions From Dehydration, Dies at 83
abstract: He worked alongside another doctor to show that a simple rehydration therapy could check the ravages of cholera and other diarrhea-inducing diseases.

name: Patricia Johanson
profession: Turned Grim Outdoor Spaces Into Art
headline: Patricia Johanson, Who Turned Grim Outdoor Spaces Into Art, Dies at 84
abstract: A groundbreaking environmental artist, she transformed water treatment plants and fetid ponds into enticing natural artworks.

name: Janey Godley
profession: Comedian Brought Humor to Harrowing Topics
headline: Janey Godley, 63, Dies; Comedian Brought Humor to Harrowing Topics
abstract: A Scottish performer, she said she believed there were “funny sides” to terrible experiences, including some that she drew from her own times of loss and hardship.

name: Dub Jones
profession: Scored 6 Touchdowns for Browns in One Game
headline: Dub Jones, Who Scored 6 Touchdowns for Browns in One Game, Dies at 99
abstract: A 6-foot-4 halfback and flanker, he was a tall, reliable target for Browns quarterback Otto Graham as Cleveland rolled to titles in the late 1940s and ’50s.

name: James Ledbetter
headline: James Ledbetter, Media Critic and Business Journalist, Dies at 60
abstract: He wrote the Press Clips column for The Village Voice, held top jobs at Inc. magazine and Slate, and wrote a book about how the startup magazine The Industry Standard fizzled.

name: Joey Jay
profession: First Little Leaguer to Get to the Majors
headline: Joey Jay, First Little Leaguer to Get to the Majors, Dies at 89
abstract: A pitcher who won 99 games in 13 seasons, he played for the Braves and the Reds. But when he retired, he never looked back.

name: Alan Rachins
profession: L.A. Law and Dharma & Greg Actor
headline: Alan Rachins, ‘L.A. Law’ and ‘Dharma & Greg’ Actor, Dies at 82
abstract: He became recognizable as a performer whose specialty was difficult men, in both absurd comedies and tense dramas.

name: Quincy Jones
headline: Quincy Jones, Giant of American Music, Dies at 91
abstract: As a producer, he made the best-selling album of all time, Michael Jackson’s “Thriller.” He was also a prolific arranger and composer of film music.

name: Murray McCory
profession: JanSport Founder Created the School Backpack
headline: Murray McCory, 80, Dies; JanSport Founder Created the School Backpack
abstract: He brought lightweight packs to millions of students and transformed the way they carried their textbooks to school.

name: Bernie Marcus
headline: Bernie Marcus, Home Depot Co-Founder, Is Dead at 95
abstract: In 1978, he came up with the idea of a warehouse-style store that would appeal to the do-it-yourself homeowner. With a partner’s help, it became the world’s largest home-improvement retailer.

name: Tyka Nelson
headline: Tyka Nelson, Sister of Prince Who Carved Her Own Path, Dies at 64
abstract: Out from under an imposing shadow, she recorded four albums as a singer and had two R&B hits before turning her focus to her brother’s legacy.

name: Warren Washington
headline: Warren Washington, Groundbreaking Climate Scientist, Dies at 88
abstract: He invented a computer model that made it possible to measure human-induced climate change. He also helped break a color barrier in science.

name: Geoff Capes
headline: Geoff Capes, World’s Strongest Man, Is Dead at 75
abstract: He pulled dump trucks, flipped cars and tossed five-pound bricks as if they were Kleenex boxes. Tending to parakeets brought out his gentler side.

name: Eikoh Hosoe
headline: Eikoh Hosoe, Photographer Who Elevated the Avant-Garde, Dies at 91
abstract: He pioneered a surrealistic narrative style in collaborations with dancers, artists and the author Yukio Mishima, with whom he created startling erotic tableaus.

name: Virginia Carter
headline: Virginia Carter, a Feminist Adviser to Norman Lear, Dies at 87
abstract: A physicist who headed a chapter of the National Organization for Women, she took a career detour to be a feminist voice in Mr. Lear’s empire of socially aware sitcoms.

name: Richard Winfield
headline: Richard Winfield, Protector of Press Freedom, Dies at 91
abstract: As a lawyer for The Associated Press and other news outlets, he challenged efforts to muzzle reporters and organized lawyers to promote free expression around the world.

name: Grant Ujifusa
profession: Lobbied for Redress for Japanese Americans
headline: Grant Ujifusa, 82, Dies; Lobbied for Redress for Japanese Americans
abstract: He helped sway Ronald Reagan to sign a bill offering cash and an apology to Japanese Americans who had been imprisoned during World War II.

name: Joseph Rykwert
headline: Joseph Rykwert, 98, Dies; Historian of Architecture Challenged Modernism
abstract: A “gloriously erudite” critic, he denounced the embrace of blandly functional architecture in efforts to rebuild after World War II.

name: Jim Hoagland
headline: Jim Hoagland, Distinguished Journalist on World Affairs, Dies at 84
abstract: A two-time Pulitzer Prize winner, he was a reporter, editor and columnist for The Washington Post, renowned for his deeply sourced dispatches.

name: Elwood Edwards
profession: Voice of AOLs Youve Got Mail! Alert
headline: Elwood Edwards, Voice of AOL’s ‘You’ve Got Mail!’ Alert, Dies at 74
abstract: Early in the internet era, he was also behind other AOL messages, including “Welcome!” “They said my voice was heard more than 35 million times a day,” he once said.

name: Jonathan Haze
profession: Star of The Little Shop of Horrors
headline: Jonathan Haze, Star of ‘The Little Shop of Horrors,’ Dies at 95
abstract: Best known for his star turn in the cult film about a flesh-eating plant, he was a go-to member of the low-budget auteur Roger Corman’s repertory company.

name: Linda LaFlamme
profession: Her White Bird Reflected a Hippie Fantasy
headline: Linda LaFlamme Dies at 85; Her ‘White Bird’ Reflected a Hippie Fantasy
abstract: With her husband, David LaFlamme, she founded the rock band It’s a Beautiful Day and wrote a soaring paean to a generation’s dreams of escape.

name: Ben Baldanza
profession: Brought No-Frills Flying to Spirit Airlines
headline: Ben Baldanza, 62, Dies; Brought No-Frills Flying to Spirit Airlines
abstract: He introduced ticket prices that couldn’t be beat, but asked fliers to pay extra for nearly everything, including water, carry-ons and printed tickets.

name: Dorothy Allison
profession: Author of Bastard Out of Carolina
headline: Dorothy Allison, Author of ‘Bastard Out of Carolina,’ Dies at 75
abstract: She wrote lovingly and often hilariously about her harrowing childhood in a working-class Southern family, as well as about the violence and incest she suffered.

name: Go-won-go Mohawk
headline: Overlooked No More: Go-won-go Mohawk, Trailblazing Indigenous Actress
abstract: In the 1880s, the only roles for Indigenous performers were laden with negative stereotypes. So Mohawk decided to write her own narratives.

name: Kenneth Bronstein
headline: Kenneth Bronstein, Who Put His Faith in Atheism, Dies at 85
abstract: The organization that he led advocated the separation of church and state, with no exceptions for holidays, currency, symbolism or blessings.

name: Trevor Sorbie
profession: Known for the Dorothy Hamill Wedge Cut
headline: Trevor Sorbie, Known for the Dorothy Hamill ‘Wedge’ Cut, Dies at 75
abstract: He also styled hair for Helen Mirren, the Beach Boys and others, and he was honored by Queen Elizabeth II for services to British hairdressing.

name: Tony Todd
profession: Prolific Actor Best Known for Candyman
headline: Tony Todd, Prolific Actor Best Known for ‘Candyman,’ Dies at 69
abstract: Mr. Todd’s decades-long career spanned across mediums and genres, but he was largely associated with a scary figure summoned in front of a mirror.

name: Baltazar Ushca
headline: Baltazar Ushca, Who Kept Andean Ice Harvesting Alive, Dies at 80
abstract: He trekked up Ecuador’s tallest mountain twice a week for six decades to hack ice off a glacier with a pickax. He is believed to have been the last of his breed.

name: Judith Jamison
profession: Alvin Ailey Dancer of Power and Radiance
headline: Judith Jamison, Alvin Ailey Dancer of ‘Power and Radiance,’ Dies at 81
abstract: She became an international star as a member of the company and later directed it, guiding it out of debt and boosting its popularity.

name: Bobby Allison
headline: Bobby Allison, Hall of Fame NASCAR Driver, Is Dead at 86
abstract: A three-time winner of the Daytona 500, he was ranked as one of NASCAR’s greatest drivers, with 85 victories. But his career was darkened by tragedy and injuries.

name: Paul Stephenson
headline: Paul Stephenson, 87, Dies; Advanced Britain’s Civil Rights Movement
abstract: The bus boycott and one-man pub sit-in that he led in the mid-1960s helped pave the way for a law outlawing discrimination in public places.

name: Ella Jenkins
headline: Ella Jenkins, Musician Who Found an Audience in Children, Dies at 100
abstract: Performing and recording, she transformed what was seen as a marginal genre in the music industry into a celebration of shared humanity.

name: Bruce Degen
headline: Bruce Degen, Who Drew ‘The Magic School Bus,’ Dies at 79
abstract: He memorably portrayed a frizzy-haired science teacher roping her elementary school class into adventures aboard a shape-shifting yellow bus.

name: Hama Amadou
headline: Hama Amadou, West African Political ‘Phoenix,’ Dies at 74
abstract: An embattled leader for decades in Niger’s rough-and-tumble politics, he alternated stints in high office with prison and exile.

name: Lou Donaldson
profession: Soulful Master of the Alto Saxophone
headline: Lou Donaldson, Soulful Master of the Alto Saxophone, Dies at 98
abstract: A player of impeccable technique and a mainstay of the Blue Note label, he recorded constantly as both a leader and a sideman beginning in 1952.

name: Sharath Jois
profession: Yoga Master and Heir to Ashtangas Founder
headline: Sharath Jois, Yoga Master and Heir to Ashtanga’s Founder, Dies at 53
abstract: He became one of the world’s most sought-after teachers of a style of yoga that his grandfather helped turn into a popular form of exercise worldwide.

name: Frank Auerbach
headline: Frank Auerbach, a Celebrated and Tireless Painter, Dies at 93
abstract: Known for his unyielding seven-day-a-week work schedule, he returned again and again to the same models and London street scenes.

name: Roy Haynes
headline: Roy Haynes, a Giant of Jazz Drumming, Is Dead at 99
abstract: An irrepressible force who remained relevant over the course of a seven-decade career, he had a hand in every major development in modern jazz.

name: Natasha Alexenko
headline: Natasha Alexenko, Who Exposed Backlog of Rape Cases, Dies at 51
abstract: Ten years after her sexual assault, she discovered that the evidence in her rape kit hadn’t been tested — and neither had thousands of others nationwide.

name: Gerry Faust
headline: Gerry Faust, Coach Who Lived a Dream at Notre Dame, Dies at 89
abstract: Jumping from the high school ranks to lead one of the most storied programs in college football, he lost games but rarely lost hope.

name: Timothy West
headline: Timothy West, Who Portrayed Kings and Prime Ministers, Dies at 90
abstract: A staple of British television, he played Churchill three times over a long career. Onstage, he was King Lear, Macbeth and Willy Loman.

name: John Robinson
profession: Inspiring Coach of U.S.C. and L.A. Rams
headline: John Robinson, Inspiring Coach of U.S.C. and L.A. Rams, Dies at 89
abstract: His Trojans won four Rose Bowls during his two stints at Southern California and shared one national championship. He took the Rams to two conference championships.

name: Theodore B. Olson
headline: Theodore B. Olson, Conservative Lawyer Who Took Up Liberal Causes, Dies at 84
abstract: A renowned Supreme Court litigator, he argued the Republican side in Bush v. Gore, but later championed gay rights and undocumented children.

name: Vardis Vardinoyannis
profession: Greek Tycoon With Ties to the Kennedys
headline: Vardis Vardinoyannis, Greek Tycoon With Ties to the Kennedys, Dies at 90
abstract: He built his family’s oil-refining operation into one of the largest companies in the country, and then used his wealth to benefit charitable causes.

name: Yiannis Boutaris
headline: Yiannis Boutaris, Vintner, Animal Defender and Greek Mayor, Dies at 82
abstract: A colorful figure in Thessaloniki, he tried to reconcile the city’s painful history with its Turkish and Jewish communities, and he extended a hand to his country’s foes.

name: Elizabeth Nunez
headline: Elizabeth Nunez, Who Chronicled the Immigrant’s Challenges, Dies at 80
abstract: In “Prospero’s Daughter” and other novels, she explored the legacy of colonialism in her native Trinidad and the struggle for belonging in an adopted country.

name: Murray Sinclair
headline: Murray Sinclair, 73, Who Reframed Indigenous Relations in Canada, Dies
abstract: He headed a commission that documented widespread abuse in Canada’s boarding schools for Indigenous children and sought to correct the history of Indigenous people.

name: Claire Gaudiani
headline: Claire Gaudiani, 79, Embattled Connecticut College President, Dies
abstract: Her unusual approach to building bridges between her wealthy campus and its beleaguered hometown led to a Supreme Court case and a faculty revolt.

name: Sim Van der Ryn
headline: Sim Van der Ryn, Early Practitioner of Green Architecture, Dies at 89
abstract: Credited with designing the first eco-friendly office building, he never forgot the lessons he learned observing communes in the 1960s.

name: Thomas E. Kurtz
headline: Thomas E. Kurtz, a Creator of BASIC Computer Language, Dies at 96
abstract: At Dartmouth, long before the days of laptops and smartphones, he worked to give more students access to computers. That work helped propel generations into a new world.

name: Shel Talmy
headline: Shel Talmy, Who Produced the Who and the Kinks, Dies at 87
abstract: Though he was American, he helped define the sound of the British Invasion after settling in London in the early 1960s.

name: Clifton R. Wharton Jr.
headline: Clifton R. Wharton Jr., Who Broke Racial Barriers, Is Dead at 98
abstract: He was the first African American to become president of a large white university, C.E.O. of a major corporation and deputy secretary of state.

name: Bela Karolyi
profession: Gymnastics Coach Was Revered, Then Repudiated
headline: Bela Karolyi, 82, Dies; Gymnastics Coach Was Revered, Then Repudiated
abstract: He rose to fame leading the Romanian and U.S. Olympic teams. He was later caught up in scandals involving the abuse of young female gymnasts.

name: Lawrence Robbins
headline: Lawrence Robbins, D.C. Lawyer in Newsmaking Cases, Is Dead at 72
abstract: He argued 20 times before the Supreme Court and prepared witnesses like Marie Yovanovitch and Christine Blasey Ford for their congressional testimony.

name: Celeste Caeiro
profession: Flowers Gave a Name to a Revolt
headline: Celeste Caeiro, Whose Flowers Gave a Name to a Revolt, Dies at 91
abstract: In Portugal in 1974, she spontaneously gave red carnations to soldiers on their way to ending a dictatorship in what became known as the Carnation Revolution.

name: Morgan Jenness
profession: Her Artistic Vision Influenced American Theater
headline: Morgan Jenness, 72, Dies; Her Artistic Vision Influenced American Theater
abstract: A beloved figure in the theatrical community, she redefined the role of dramaturg, influencing playwrights like David Adjmi and David Henry Hwang.

name: Sandra M. Gilbert
profession: Co-Author of The Madwoman in the Attic
headline: Sandra M. Gilbert, Co-Author of ‘The Madwoman in the Attic,’ Dies at 87
abstract: A poet, scholar and literary critic, she turned a feminist lens on 19th-century writers like Jane Austen and Charlotte Brontë, creating a feminist classic.

name: Arthur Frommer
profession: His Guidebooks Opened Travel to the Masses
headline: Arthur Frommer, 95, Dies; His Guidebooks Opened Travel to the Masses
abstract: After publishing “Europe on 5 Dollars a Day” in 1957, he went on to build an empire of guidebooks, package tours, hotels and other services.

name: Bob Love
headline: Bob Love, Rugged, High-Scoring All-Star for Chicago Bulls, Dies at 81
abstract: Love was a cornerstone of the franchise’s success in the early 1970s. He struggled with a stutter that he overcame only after his playing days were over.

name: Richard V. Allen
headline: Richard V. Allen, Reagan’s First National Security Adviser, Dies at 88
abstract: His tenure was short: He was forced to resign after $1,000 in cash was found in a safe in his former office, even though the Justice Department cleared him of wrongdoing.

name: Diane Coleman
profession: Fierce Foe of the Right-to-Die Movement
headline: Diane Coleman, Fierce Foe of the Right-to-Die Movement, Dies at 71
abstract: Her fight for disability rights included founding a group called Not Dead Yet, which protested the work of Dr. Jack Kevorkian and others.

name: Bill Moyes
headline: Bill Moyes, Australian ‘Birdman’ Who Popularized Hang Gliding, Dies at 92
abstract: A modern-day Icarus, he set a world record for the longest unassisted flight, was arrested after soaring into the Grand Canyon and nearly killed himself several times.

name: Vic Flick
headline: Vic Flick, Guitarist Who Plucked the James Bond Theme, Dies at 87
abstract: A busy session musician, he also recorded music for the Beatles’ film “A Hard Day’s Night” and contributed to several hit songs.

name: Reg Murphy
headline: Reg Murphy, Newspaper Editor Whose Kidnapping Made Headlines, Dies at 90
abstract: He made his mark on newspapers in Atlanta, San Francisco and Baltimore, but may be best known for having been abducted in Atlanta in 1974.

name: John Prescott
headline: John Prescott, Ex-Deputy Prime Minister of Britain, Dies at 86
abstract: He was a cruise ship waiter before rising in the trade union movement and becoming one of the country’s best-known Labour politicians under Tony Blair.

name: Dallas Long
headline: Dallas Long, Record-Setting Shot-Putter, Is Dead at 84
abstract: In an era when America dominated the event, he was one of the best. He retired after winning gold at the 1964 Tokyo Summer Olympics and became a doctor.

name: Steven J. Rosen
headline: Steven J. Rosen, Fiercely Influential Advocate for Israel, Dies at 82
abstract: He was a prominent behind-the-scenes figure in Washington whose career was derailed when he was charged with leaking government secrets. The case was later dropped.

name: Spencer Lawton Jr.
profession: D.A. in Midnight in the Garden Case
headline: Spencer Lawton Jr., D.A. in ‘Midnight in the Garden’ Case, Dies at 81
abstract: He devoted much of his 28 years in office in Savannah to victims’ rights, but he was best known for his role in a 1981 murder at the center of a best seller and its movie version.

name: Peter Sinfield
profession: Poetic Lyricist for Prog Rocks King Crimson
headline: Peter Sinfield, Poetic Lyricist for Prog Rock’s King Crimson, Dies at 80
abstract: His swirls of imagery helped define progressive rock in the 1970s. He later turned his focus to pop acts like Celine Dion.

name: M. Jodi Rell
headline: M. Jodi Rell, Former Republican Governor of Connecticut, Dies at 78
abstract: She was lieutenant governor when her boss, Gov. John G. Rowland, resigned in a corruption scandal. The second woman to lead the state, she was later elected in her own right.

name: Harold W. Sims Jr.
headline: Harold W. Sims Jr., Whose Museum Honored the House Cat, Dies at 89
abstract: He displayed some 10,000 cat-themed artifacts at the American Museum of the House Cat in North Carolina, which welcomed several thousand people a year.

name: Mike Shatzkin
headline: Mike Shatzkin, Colorful Publishing Industry Guru, Dies at 77
abstract: His blog, The Shatzkin Files, was an essential read for industry insiders. His observations about the changes digital publishing would bring were prophetic.

name: Alice Brock
profession: Restaurant Owner Made Famous by a Song
headline: Alice Brock, Restaurant Owner Made Famous by a Song, Dies at 83
abstract: Arlo Guthrie’s antiwar staple “Alice’s Restaurant” was inspired by a Thanksgiving Day visit to her diner in western Massachusetts.

name: Madeleine Riffaud
headline: Madeleine Riffaud, ‘the Girl Who Saved Paris,’ Dies at 100
abstract: Humiliated by a Nazi officer as a teenager, she joined the French Resistance. By the time she was 20, she had killed a German soldier, survived torture and captured a supply train.

name: Fred R. Harris
headline: Fred R. Harris, Oklahoma Senator Who Ran for President, Dies at 94
abstract: After eight years in the Senate as a moderate Democrat, he took a leftward turn toward “new populism” in a failed shot at the presidency in 1976.

name: Chuck Woolery
headline: Chuck Woolery, Host of ‘Love Connection,’ Dies at 83
abstract: After a career that included stints on “Wheel of Fortune” and other popular game shows, he took a combative turn as a right-wing podcast host.

name: Rico Carty
headline: Rico Carty, Exceptional Hitter Who Was Stymied by Injuries, Dies at 85
abstract: A Dominican baseball star, he had a dazzling rookie year and became a pioneering designated hitter, but injuries and tuberculosis held him back.

name: Charles Dumont
profession: Wrote Enduring Melodies for Édith Piaf
headline: Charles Dumont, Who Wrote Enduring Melodies for Édith Piaf, Dies at 95
abstract: His dozens of songs included “Non, Je Ne Regrette Rien,” a powerful anthem of redemptive love that became one of Piaf’s signature songs.

name: Tony Campolo
headline: Tony Campolo, Preacher Who Challenged Religious Right, Dies at 89
abstract: A mesmerizing speaker, he urged his fellow evangelicals to turn away from politics in favor of the values of charity and love espoused by Jesus.

name: Barbara Taylor Bradford
headline: Barbara Taylor Bradford, Whose Sagas Were Best Sellers, Dies at 91
abstract: Her own rags-to-riches story mirrored those of many of her resilient heroines, and her dozens of novels helped her amass a fortune of $300 million.

name: Paul Caponigro
headline: Paul Caponigro, Photographer in Love with Nature, Dies at 91
abstract: He photographed landscapes, deer, sunflowers and still lifes. “I knew that the forces of nature were a language,” he said. “Nature was really my teacher.”

name: Breyten Breytenbach
headline: Breyten Breytenbach, Anti-Apartheid Writer in Exile, Dies at 85
abstract: He wrote poetry in Afrikaans and prose in English in his fight against South African racial oppression, an effort that landed him in jail for seven years.

name: Margaret Getchell
headline: Overlooked No More: Margaret Getchell, Visionary Force at Macy’s
abstract: As the store’s first female executive, she helped turn it into what it is today, paving the way for other women to hold senior positions in retail.

name: Andy Paley
profession: Imprint Was All Over Pop Music
headline: Andy Paley, Whose Imprint Was All Over Pop Music, Dies at 73
abstract: Musician, singer, songwriter, producer and more, he collaborated with Madonna and a raft of other artists and helped resuscitate the career of the Beach Boys’ Brian Wilson.

name: Evelyne de Pontbriand
headline: Evelyne de Pontbriand, Champion of Biodynamic Winemaking, Dies at 73
abstract: The latest in a long line of women to run her family winery, she helped bring worldwide attention to sustainable viniculture.

name: Manfred Ohrenstein
headline: Manfred Ohrenstein, Liberal Lion of N.Y. Legislature, Dies at 99
abstract: He entered the State Senate as a reformer but during 34 years became part of the system he sought to reform.

name: Helen Gallagher
profession: Winner of Two Tonys and Three Emmys
headline: Helen Gallagher, Winner of Two Tonys and Three Emmys, Dies at 98
abstract: She was honored on Broadway for roles in “Pal Joey” and “No, No, Nanette” and then turned to TV, where she won three Daytime Emmys for her work on “Ryan’s Hope.”

name: Robert Dixon
headline: Robert Dixon, Last Surviving Buffalo Soldier, Dies at 103
abstract: A member of one of the U.S. Army’s all-Black regiments, formed after the Civil War, he trained West Point cadets in horsemanship during World War II.

name: Jim Abrahams
profession: Mastermind of Airplane! and Naked Gun
headline: Jim Abrahams, 80, Dies; a Mastermind of ‘Airplane!’ and ‘Naked Gun’
abstract: Along with his fellow filmmakers David and Jerry Zucker, he revolutionized film comedy with a straight-faced, fast-paced style of parody.

name: Peggy Caserta
profession: Wrote a Tell-All About Janis Joplin
headline: Peggy Caserta, Who Wrote a Tell-All About Janis Joplin, Dies at 84
abstract: Her Haight-Ashbury clothing store was ground zero for the counterculture. But she was best known for a tawdry book — which she later disavowed — published after Ms. Joplin’s death.

name: Alice Hudson
headline: Alice Hudson, Librarian Who Built a Trove of Historic Maps, Dies at 77
abstract: She transformed the New York Public Library’s collection of charts and atlases into one of the world’s largest and most accessible resources.

name: Earl Holliman
headline: Earl Holliman, Rugged, and Familiar, Screen Presence, Dies at 96
abstract: While never a big star, he was a recognizable one, with roles in “The Twilight Zone,” “Giant,” “Forbidden Planet” and the 1970s series “Police Woman.”

name: J. Stanley Pottinger
profession: Official Figured Out Identity of Deep Throat
headline: J. Stanley Pottinger, 84, Dies; Official Figured Out Identity of ‘Deep Throat’
abstract: A former Nixon official (and later a novelist), he led an investigation in which a shadowy Watergate figure squirmed when asked if he had been an anonymous whistle blower.

name: Lou Carnesecca
profession: St. Johns Basketball Coach With 526 Wins
headline: Lou Carnesecca, St. John’s Basketball Coach With 526 Wins, Is Dead at 99
abstract: Known for his quick wit and garish sweaters, he took the New York City university to national basketball prominence over 24 seasons.

name: Marshall Brickman
profession: Woody Allens Co-Writer on Hit Films
headline: Marshall Brickman, Woody Allen’s Co-Writer on Hit Films, Dies at 85
abstract: The duo won an Oscar for “Annie Hall.” Mr. Brickman went on to write Broadway shows, including “Jersey Boys,” and make movies of his own.

name: Peter Westbrook
headline: Peter Westbrook, Pathbreaking Olympic Fencer, Dies at 72
abstract: As the first African American to win a medal in a sport long dominated by white Europeans, he was compared to Jackie Robinson and Arthur Ashe.

name: Wayne Northrop
headline: Wayne Northrop, ‘Days of Our Lives’ Actor, Dies at 77
abstract: He was best known for playing two characters, Roman Brady and Dr. Alex North, in more than 1,000 episodes on the daytime soap opera.

name: Bob Bryar
profession: Former Drummer for My Chemical Romance
headline: Bob Bryar, Former Drummer for My Chemical Romance, Dies at 44
abstract: He joined that pop-punk band in 2004 and played on its most successful album, “The Black Parade.”

name: Debbie Nelson
headline: Debbie Nelson, Eminem’s Mother, Dies at 69
abstract: The two had a fraught relationship that was immortalized in many of Eminem’s earliest hits.

name: Thirman Milner
headline: Thirman Milner, Hartford Mayor Who Broke Race Barrier, Dies at 91
