abstract: He grudgingly transitioned from civil rights to politics and became the first popularly elected Black mayor in New England.

name: Morton I. Abramowitz
headline: Morton I. Abramowitz, Diplomat Who Made Refugees a Priority, Dies at 91
abstract: As ambassador to Thailand and Turkey, and later as president of the Carnegie Endowment, he pushed for making human rights central to foreign policy.

name: Mary McGee
headline: Mary McGee, Motorcycle Racing Pioneer, Is Dead at 87
abstract: Her most remarkable achievement came in 1975, when she became the first person, man or woman, to complete the Baja 500 race solo.

name: Brian Thompson
headline: Brian Thompson, Chief Executive of UnitedHealthcare, Dies at 50
abstract: Mr. Thompson, who was fatally shot in Midtown Manhattan, rose to the top of one of the world’s biggest insurance companies.

name: Kelly Powers
profession: Fox Health Commentator Told of Her Cancer
headline: Kelly Powers, 45, Dies; Fox Health Commentator Told of Her Cancer
abstract: A podiatric surgeon and a regular presence on Fox News, she used her television platform to talk about her brain cancer and treatment as well as cancer research.

name: Rohit Bal
headline: Rohit Bal, Exuberant Star of Indian Fashion, Dies at 63
abstract: Known as “the bad boy of fashion,” he was among a wave of designers who created modern Indian couture by updating traditional garments.

name: Peter B. Teeley
headline: Peter B. Teeley, Who Coined the Term ‘Voodoo Economics,’ Dies at 84
abstract: As press secretary for George H.W. Bush, he came up with the expression to attack Ronald Reagan’s economic plan. The term took on a life of its own.

name: Lance Morrow
headline: Lance Morrow, 85, Award-Winning Essayist for Time Magazine, Is Dead
abstract: His voice carried weight on the influential back page and as the writer of many “Man of the Year” cover articles. As a memoirist he chronicled his heart attacks.

name: Shalom Nagar
headline: Shalom Nagar Dies; Reluctant Executioner of Adolf Eichmann
abstract: He was the hangman chosen to carry out the sentence on the fugitive Nazi war criminal, in Israel’s only case of capital punishment.

name: Ron O’Brien
headline: Ron O’Brien, Who Coached Divers to Olympic Medals, Dies at 86
abstract: He may have been the most successful diving coach in American history, gathering more than 300 medals in competitions and nurturing stars like Greg Louganis.

name: Barbara Bowman
headline: Barbara Bowman Dies at 96; Visionary Educator for Preschoolers
abstract: She devoted her career to teaching teachers how to prepare the youngest and most vulnerable children to fulfill their potential.

name: Shuntaro Tanikawa
profession: Popular Poet and Translator of Peanuts
headline: Shuntaro Tanikawa, Popular Poet and Translator of ‘Peanuts,’ Dies at 92
abstract: A perennial front-runner for the Nobel Prize in Literature, he was a revered figure in Japan, not just in literary circles but also among casual readers.

name: Silvia Pinal
profession: Golden Age Star of Mexican Cinema
headline: Silvia Pinal, Golden Age Star of Mexican Cinema, Is Dead
abstract: She found outsize success in her native land and gained international recognition for her work with the acclaimed Spanish surrealist director Luis Buñuel.

name: Miho Nakayama
headline: Miho Nakayama, Japanese Music and Movie Star, Dies at 54
abstract: A top-selling pop singer as a teenager in the 1980s, she also had an award-winning career as a dramatic actress.

name: Chiung Yao
profession: Top Romance Novelist in Chinese-Speaking World
headline: Chiung Yao, Top Romance Novelist in Chinese-Speaking World, Dies at 86
abstract: Writing from Taiwan, she shaped her readers’ idea of romantic love with a raft of best sellers, many adapted for the screen. Newborns were named after her characters.

name: Angela Alvarez
headline: Angela Alvarez, Great-Grandmother Who Won a Latin Grammy, Dies at 97
abstract: Her only album made her a media star after she had raised four children and worked as a house cleaner — proving, she said, that “it’s never too late.”

name: Marvin Laird
profession: Musical Presence on and Off Broadway
headline: Marvin Laird, Musical Presence on and Off Broadway, Dies at 85
abstract: He conducted Broadway shows and worked with Bernadette Peters. But he was probably best known for writing the music for the darkly comic “Ruthless!”

name: Nikki Giovanni
headline: Nikki Giovanni, Poet Who Wrote of Black Joy, Dies at 81
abstract: As a writer, she tackled race, gender, sex, politics and love. She was also a public intellectual who appeared on television and toured the country.

name: Rocky Colavito
headline: Rocky Colavito, All-Star Slugger for Cleveland, Dies at 91
abstract: After he was traded in one of the most infamous deals in Cleveland’s history, the team floundered and “the curse of Rocky Colavito” was born.

name: Michael Cole
headline: Michael Cole, a Star of ‘The Mod Squad,’ Is Dead at 84
abstract: The show, about three hippies who become undercover crime fighters, ran from 1968 to 1973. Mr. Cole had been the last of its three stars still living.

name: The Amazing Kreskin
headline: The Amazing Kreskin, Mentalist and 1970s Television Star, Dies at 89
abstract: His display of mysterious mind-reading powers on TV made him a pop culture phenomenon in the 1970s.

name: Martin Benson
headline: Martin Benson, Regional Theater Impresario With Impact, Dies at 87
abstract: South Coast Repertory, a California company he founded with a partner, grew to stage world premieres of major works that made their way to Broadway.

name: Victor Brombert
profession: Princeton Scholar With a Secret Army Past
headline: Victor Brombert, Princeton Scholar With a Secret Army Past, Dies at 101
abstract: As a Jewish teen, he fled the Nazis for America — then landed at D-Day and swept across Europe in a unit that gathered intelligence. Its work was hidden for decades.

name: Fidelia Bridges
headline: Overlooked No More: Fidelia Bridges, Artist Who Captured the Natural World
abstract: A prolific artist, she was known for her graceful watercolors of birds, plants and butterflies, and was considered as the equal of Winslow Homer in her day.

name: Clarke Reed
profession: Helped the G.O.P. Conquer the South
headline: Clarke Reed, Who Helped the G.O.P. Conquer the South, Dies at 96
abstract: He built Mississippi’s Republican Party into a conservative powerhouse, making himself a regional power broker in the process.

name: Dolores Madrigal
headline: Dolores Madrigal, Plaintiff in Landmark Sterilization Case, Dies at 90
abstract: She was among hundreds of women who said they were coerced into sterilization at a California hospital in the 1970s. The lawsuit led to state and national reforms.

name: Louis Nelson
headline: Louis Nelson, Designer of Korean War Mural, Dies at 88
abstract: A designer of signage and product packaging, he was best known for his work on the 164-foot mural wall at the Korean War Veterans Memorial in Washington.

name: Martial Solal
headline: Martial Solal, French Jazz Piano Virtuoso, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Mr. Solal, who also wrote music for films and symphony orchestras, was revered in Europe and hailed in the United States on his rare visits there.

name: Jerome Kohn
headline: Jerome Kohn, Keeper of Hannah Arendt’s Flame, Dies at 93
abstract: He devoted his career to guarding the legacy of the philosopher known for her writings on totalitarianism and “the banality of evil.”

name: Charles Handy
headline: Charles Handy Dies at 92; Philosopher Envisioned Today’s Corporate World
abstract: Joining a pantheon of management thinkers, he embraced a humanistic path for business and foresaw outsourcing, remote work and a gig economy.

name: Rodney Jenkins
headline: Rodney Jenkins, Star of the Show-Jumping Circuit, Dies at 80
abstract: He had a feel for how horses behaved and thought, and won more than 70 Grand Prix events.

name: Gerd Heidemann
profession: Journalist Duped by Fake Hitler Diaries
headline: Gerd Heidemann, Journalist Duped by Fake Hitler Diaries, Dies at 93
abstract: What was supposed to be the crowning scoop of his career became his downfall when a trove of notebooks he acquired in Germany turned out to be forgeries.

name: Robert Fernandez
profession: Survived Pearl Harbor as a Teen
headline: Robert Fernandez, Who Survived Pearl Harbor as a Teen, Dies at 100
abstract: He was a 17-year-old sailor aboard the U.S.S. Curtiss when Japanese forces attacked. He said he had joined the Navy to see the world.

name: Isak Andic
headline: Isak Andic, Founder of Mango Fashion Chain, Dies at 71
abstract: Mr. Andic got his start by selling T-shirts in Barcelona in the mid-1980s. He died in a fall during a hike.

name: Polly Mellen
headline: Polly Mellen, Fashion’s Storied Cheerleader, Dies at 100
abstract: With photographers like Richard Avedon, Irving Penn, Bert Stern and others, the veteran editor created some of the most indelible images of modern fashion.

name: Lorraine O’Grady
headline: Lorraine O’Grady, Artist Who Defied Category, Is Dead at 90
abstract: She worked in collage, photography, performance, video and installation, and she dealt forthrightly with the complexities of race and gender.

name: Zakir Hussain
headline: Zakir Hussain, Tabla Virtuoso Who Fused Musical Traditions, Dies at 73
abstract: His collaborators included John McLaughlin, Béla Fleck, Ravi Shankar, Herbie Hancock, Yo-Yo Ma and members of the Grateful Dead.

name: E.B. Furgurson III
headline: E.B. Furgurson III, Who Covered Massacre at His Newspaper, Dies at 70
abstract: After five people were killed in the newsroom, he set up a work space in the back of his pickup truck and made sure the next day’s issue was published.

name: Orrin H. Pilkey
profession: Warrior in a Fight to Save Imperiled Beaches
headline: Orrin H. Pilkey, Warrior in a Fight to Save Imperiled Beaches, Dies at 90
abstract: An eminent geologist, he argued against putting condos and hotels on vulnerable coastal landscapes. Environmentalists applauded; many others didn’t.

name: Dick Van Arsdale
profession: One of First Identical Twins in the N.B.A
headline: Dick Van Arsdale, 81, One of First Identical Twins in the N.B.A., Dies
abstract: A three-time All-Star, he played for the Knicks and the Phoenix Suns. For one season, he and Tom Van Arsdale were hard-to-tell-apart teammates.

name: Arlene Croce
profession: Dance Critic With a Biting Wit
headline: Arlene Croce, Dance Critic With a Biting Wit, Dies at 90
abstract: Writing for The New Yorker, she was both admired and feared, wielding a sometimes merciless pen. Her study of Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers drew accolades.

name: Jim Leach
headline: Jim Leach, Iowa Republican Who Extolled Moderation, Dies at 82
abstract: During his 30 years in Congress, he resisted his party’s rightward tilt. He endorsed Barack Obama in 2008 and became a Democrat in 2022.

name: Rayful Edmond
headline: Rayful Edmond, Drug Lord Who Stoked D.C.’s Crack Cocaine Epidemic, Dies at 60
abstract: He rose to prominence in the 1980s, spending lavishly and befriending athletes, as the city was wracked by murders tied to the drug trade. He later became an informant.

name: David Bonderman
headline: David Bonderman, Private Equity Pioneer, Is Dead at 82
abstract: A globe-trotting lawyer turned investor, he helped transform a cottage industry into a colossus with influence on Wall Street and beyond.

name: Java
headline: Sir Lady Java, ’60s Drag Star Who Challenged the Law, Dies
abstract: Long before the term “drag queen” was widely used, her act was popular in the Black entertainment world but barred under a Los Angeles municipal code.

name: James Callan
headline: The Rev. James Callan, Renegade Catholic Priest, Dies at 77
abstract: He was excommunicated in 1999 after allowing women to celebrate Mass, blessing same-sex unions and offering communion to non-Catholics.

name: William J. Hennessy Jr.
headline: William J. Hennessy Jr., Sketch Artist of Courtroom Drama, Dies at 67
abstract: His lively drawings of historic Supreme Court arguments, impeachment trials and murder cases gave the public a peek into venues where cameras were banned.

name: Joanne Pierce Misko
headline: Joanne Pierce Misko, Ex-Nun Who Made F.B.I. History, Dies at 83
abstract: She and Susan Malone were sworn in together in 1972 as the first female agents, only months after the bureau opened the door to women.

name: Rick Kaufmann
headline: Rick Kaufmann, Impresario of Art Furniture, Dies at 77
abstract: Was it art or was it furniture? No one was quite sure what to make of the New York movement that an idiosyncratic gallerist led in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Marisa Paredes
headline: Marisa Paredes, Acclaimed in Almodóvar Films, Is Dead at 78
abstract: An esteemed Spanish actress, she was best known for her work in Pedro Almodóvar’s movies like “All About My Mother.” But their relationship was stormy.

name: Michael Brewer
profession: One Toke Was a Big Hit
headline: Michael Brewer, Whose ‘One Toke’ Was a Big Hit, Is Dead at 80
abstract: The duo Brewer & Shipley reached the Top 10 in 1971 with “One Toke Over the Line,” a ditty about marijuana that ran afoul of Nixon-era censors.

name: Cathy Cade
headline: Cathy Cade, Groundbreaking Lesbian Photographer, Dies at 82
abstract: She became a photographer the same year she came out, chronicling the lives of women in same-sex relationships — something most people had never seen.

name: Troy Masters
headline: Troy Masters, Pioneering L.G.B.T.Q. Journalist, Dies at 63
abstract: He was at the helm of several influential publications, notably Gay City News in New York City and, since 2017, The Los Angeles Blade.

name: Ann Rockefeller Roberts
headline: Ann Rockefeller Roberts, Champion of Native Americans, Dies at 90
abstract: The eldest daughter of Nelson Rockefeller, she founded a nonprofit to support Indigenous culture and helped fill two institutions with artifacts.

name: Rickey Henderson
headline: Rickey Henderson, Baseball’s Flamboyant ‘Man of Steal,’ Dies at 65
abstract: Widely regarded as the greatest leadoff hitter in baseball history, he was not just one of the game’s most exciting players but also one of its most eccentric.

name: Lee Edwards
headline: Lee Edwards, Historian of the Conservative Movement, Dies at 92
abstract: In his books about Ronald Reagan, Barry Goldwater and other figures on the right, he was, one observer said, “a keeper of the flame and spreader of the gospel.”

name: Alfa Anderson
headline: Alfa Anderson, Singer With Chic, Dies at 78
abstract: She sang the famous refrain “Le freak, c’est chic” on one of the biggest hits of the disco era and was a sought-after vocalist for many prominent artists.

name: Yoshio Taniguchi
headline: Yoshio Taniguchi, Architect for MoMA’s Expansion, Dies at 87
abstract: He was a surprise choice for the ambitious project, but his design won praise as “drop-dead elegant.”

name: Steven Englander
profession: Leader of an Outsider Art Outpost
headline: Steven Englander, Leader of an Outsider Art Outpost, Dies at 63
abstract: As director of the fiercely independent cultural center ABC No Rio, he led the battle to halt its eviction and later raised money to build a new home for the organization.

name: Perry Dahl
profession: Downed Nine Planes During World War II
headline: Perry Dahl, Who Downed Nine Planes During World War II, Dies at 101
abstract: His courage in battle brought him the Congressional Gold Medal, the Silver Star, the Distinguished Flying Cross and the Legion of Merit.

name: William Labov
headline: William Labov, Who Studied How Society Shapes Language, Dies at 97
abstract: He laid the foundation for sociolinguistics, and he showed that structures like class and race shaped speech as much as where someone lives.

name: Richard Perry
profession: Record Producer With a Golden Touch
headline: Richard Perry, Record Producer With a Golden Touch, Dies at 82
abstract: Known for his work with Barbra Streisand, Carly Simon, the Pointer Sisters and many others, he was one of the most reliable hitmakers in the business.

name: Desi Bouterse
headline: Desi Bouterse, Fugitive Former Dictator of Suriname, Dies at 79
abstract: He took power in a military coup in 1980 and later served as the country’s president. He was also convicted of ordering the murder of 15 political opponents.

name: Jacques Roubaud
profession: Poetic Master of Form and Whimsy
headline: Jacques Roubaud, Poetic Master of Form and Whimsy, Dies at 92
abstract: He was trained as a mathematician, but he gained fame in France, and won major prizes, for his modern verse.

name: Donald Bitzer
headline: Donald Bitzer, Unsung Pioneer of Interactive Computing, Dies at 90
abstract: In the 1960s and ’70s, he developed the PLATO computer system, which combined instant messaging, email, chat rooms and gaming on flat-screen plasma displays.

name: Manmohan Singh
headline: Manmohan Singh, 92, Indian Premier Who Spurred Economic Boom, Dies
abstract: The country’s first Sikh prime minister, he introduced free-market reforms that turned India into an economic powerhouse and sought reconciliation with Pakistan.

name: Richard Parsons
profession: Serial Fixer of Media and Finance Giants
headline: Richard Parsons, Serial Fixer of Media and Finance Giants, Dies at 76
abstract: His résumé is a catalog of corporate emergencies at Time Warner, Citigroup and the Los Angeles Clippers.

name: Dorthy Moxley
profession: Pursued Justice in Her Daughters Murder
headline: Dorthy Moxley, Who Pursued Justice in Her Daughter’s Murder, Dies at 92
abstract: For decades after Martha Moxley’s gruesome death, Mrs. Moxley remained a compelling figure in a roller-coaster case that captured the world’s attention.

name: Shyam Benegal
headline: Shyam Benegal, Indian Filmmaker Who Explored Social Issues, Dies at 90
abstract: He won acclaim from critics and audiences even as the gritty stories he put on the big screen grappled with some of India’s thorniest problems.

name: Sugar Pie DeSanto
headline: Sugar Pie DeSanto, Gritty Soul Singer, Is Dead at 89
abstract: A powerful performer who paved the way for later soul and hip-hop artists, she recorded with Etta James and toured with Johnny Otis and James Brown.

name: Osamu Suzuki
headline: Osamu Suzuki, 94, Who Turned Automaker Into a Powerhouse, Dies
abstract: He built Suzuki Motor into a Japanese global brand making small vehicles and motorcycles. Entering India’s market in the 1980s was one of his early successes.

name: Berrien Moore III
headline: Berrien Moore III, Pioneering Scholar of Earth Science, Dies at 83
abstract: As a researcher at several universities and an adviser at NASA, he used data analysis to show how the planet’s different systems are interrelated.

name: Ruth Butler
headline: Ruth Butler, Who Brought Artists’ Muses to Life, Dies at 93
abstract: After publishing a definitive biography of Rodin, she went on to write about the underappreciated women who modeled for the giants of 19th-century French art.

name: Greg Gumbel
headline: Greg Gumbel Dies at 78; High-Profile Sportscaster for Over 5 Decades
abstract: A dignified presence on camera, most prominently for CBS, he became the first Black announcer to call a major U.S. sports championship, the 2001 Super Bowl.

name: Shigeko Sasamori
headline: Shigeko Sasamori, Hiroshima Survivor Who Preached Peace, Dies at 92
abstract: Severely disfigured when the United States dropped an atomic bomb on Japan, she spent her life warning others about the dangers of nuclear war.

name: Kirsten Simone
headline: Kirsten Simone, International Ballet Star, Is Dead at 90
abstract: One of Denmark’s greatest ballerinas, she toured widely — in London, Moscow and New York — and played a version of herself in a Disney TV production.

name: Michel del Castillo
headline: Michel del Castillo, 91, Dies; Child’s-Eye Chronicler of Concentration Camps
abstract: His first novel, “Tanguy,” published when he was 24, was a fact-based Holocaust story that one reviewer said “begins where Anne Frank’s diary ended.”

name: Dayle Haddon
headline: Dayle Haddon, Model Who Bucked Age Discrimination, Dies at 76
abstract: Ms. Haddon, who carved a path all her own in the modeling world, was found dead on Friday morning from what authorities believed was a carbon monoxide leak.

name: Charles Dolan
headline: Charles Dolan, Cablevision Founder Who Sat Atop a Media Empire, Dies at 98
abstract: His business choices were diverse and prolific: He founded HBO, bought Madison Square Garden and the New York Knicks, and took over a Long Island newspaper.

name: Warren Upton
profession: Escaped Sinking Battleship in Pearl Harbor
headline: Warren Upton, Who Escaped Sinking Battleship in Pearl Harbor, Dies at 105
abstract: The last survivor of the U.S.S. Utah, he was a 22-year-old Navy radioman when Japanese forces attacked.

name: Charlie Maxwell
headline: Charlie Maxwell, Who Hit Homers in 4 Consecutive At-Bats, Dies at 97
abstract: An All-Star outfielder for the Tigers, he tied a major league record with that feat on a Sunday (what else?) in 1959 playing against the Yankees in Detroit.

name: Stanley Booth
headline: Stanley Booth, Music Journalist Who Loved the Blues, Dies at 82
abstract: He is best known for his book about the Rolling Stones. But he mostly wrote about blues artists, some of them famous (B.B. King) and some less renowned (Furry Lewis).

name: Jimmy Carter
headline: Jimmy Carter, Peacemaking President Amid Crises, Is Dead at 100
abstract: Rising from Georgia farmland to the White House, he oversaw the historic Camp David peace accords, but his one-term presidency was waylaid by troubles at home and abroad.

name: Rodessa Barrett Porter
profession: Member of a Storied Gospel Trio
headline: Rodessa Barrett Porter, Member of a Storied Gospel Trio, Dies at 94
abstract: The Barrett Sisters were a Chicago institution, known for their tight harmonies and joyful performances. She was the last one standing.

name: Olivia Hussey
profession: Teen Star of a Romeo and Juliet on Film
headline: Olivia Hussey, Teen Star of a ‘Romeo and Juliet’ on Film, Dies at 73
abstract: Her passionate portrayal of Juliet in Franco Zeffirelli’s 1968 adaptation won enduring acclaim. In 2023, she sued over the circumstances of a nude scene.

name: Linda Lavin
profession: Broadway Actress and Star of TV Sitcom Alice
headline: Linda Lavin, Broadway Actress and Star of TV Sitcom ‘Alice,’ Dies at 87
abstract: She won two Golden Globe Awards and an Emmy nomination for her role on the show. She also earned a Tony Award for best actress in the play “Broadway Bound.”

name: Dick Capri
headline: Dick Capri, Catskills Comic Who Took His Shtick to Broadway, Dies at 93
abstract: He was a regular at the mountain resorts where many comedians honed their acts, then had a star turn in the long-running revue “Catskills on Broadway.”

name: Lenny Randle
headline: Lenny Randle, ‘Most Interesting’ Major Leaguer, Is Dead at 75
abstract: His career was defined by bizarre episodes — blowing a rolling ball foul, knocking down a pitcher and standing at the plate when the lights went out in New York City.

name: Agnes Keleti
headline: Agnes Keleti, World’s Oldest Olympic Champion, Dies at 103
abstract: She turned to gymnastics after surviving World War II as a persecuted Jew and won 10 Olympic medals competing against far younger athletes.

name: Rosita Missoni
profession: Turned Zigzag Sweaters Into High Fashion
headline: Rosita Missoni, Who Turned Zigzag Sweaters Into High Fashion, Dies at 93
abstract: With colorful knitwear, she and her husband, Ottavio, built one of the world’s most recognizable brands, helping to make Milan a capital of “alta moda.”

name: Richard A. Easterlin
headline: Richard A. Easterlin, ‘Father of Happiness Economics,’ Dies at 98
abstract: He put forth the so-called Easterlin paradox, finding that the richer you are doesn’t mean the more satisfied you’ll be with your life.

name: Mary Anne Krupsak
profession: First as a New York Politician
headline: Mary Anne Krupsak, a First as a New York Politician, Dies at 92
abstract: She was the first woman elected lieutenant governor in the state after defying party leaders and her eventual running mate, Hugh Carey, to win the nomination.

name: Wayne Osmond
profession: Singer and Guitarist With the Osmonds
headline: Wayne Osmond, Singer and Guitarist With the Osmonds, Dies at 73
abstract: He was a founding member of the family pop group, whose slew of hits in the 1970s included the No. 1 record “One Bad Apple.”

name: David Lodge
headline: David Lodge, British Novelist Who Satirized Academic Life, Dies at 89
abstract: His 15 well-plotted novels teemed with romance and strange coincidence. An erudite literary critic with an ear for language, he also wrote a raft of nonfiction books.

name: Jocelyne Wildenstein
headline: Jocelyne Wildenstein, Socialite and Tabloid ‘Catwoman,’ Dies at 79
abstract: Her lurid divorce from the wealthy scion of an art-world dynasty earned headlines. Her elaborate plastic surgeries brought even more attention.

name: Britt Allcroft
profession: Brought Thomas the Tank Engine to TV
headline: Britt Allcroft, Who Brought Thomas the Tank Engine to TV, Dies at 81
abstract: She adapted the children’s book series to TV, creating a lasting cultural behemoth that spawned movies, merchandise and theme parks.

name: Charles Shyer
headline: Charles Shyer, Filmmaker Who Focused on Women, Dies at 83
abstract: His long collaboration with Nancy Meyers produced a string of hit movies, including “Baby Boom” and “Father of the Bride,” that spoke to the moment.

name: Marie Winn
profession: Wrote of a Famous Central Park Hawk
headline: Marie Winn, Who Wrote of a Famous Central Park Hawk, Dies at 88
abstract: She chronicled the melodrama of Pale Male, a red-tailed hawk who became an avian sensation as it took up residence atop a Manhattan apartment building.

name: Jeff Baena
headline: Jeff Baena, Film Director and Screenwriter, Dies at 47
abstract: Mr. Baena, who was married to the actress Aubrey Plaza, co-wrote the existential comedy “I Heart Huckabees,” and wrote and directed films including “Life After Beth” and “The Little Hours.”

name: Tom Johnson
profession: Minimalist Composer and Village Voice Critic
headline: Tom Johnson, Minimalist Composer and Village Voice Critic, Dies at 85
abstract: He charted the rise of musical minimalism on New York’s downtown scene in the 1970s. He later gained notice for abstract works of his own.

name: Richard Foreman
headline: Richard Foreman, Iconoclastic Playwright and Impresario, Dies at 87
abstract: The Ontological-Hysteric Theater, which he founded in 1968, presented more than 50 of his plays, among them “My Head Was a Sledgehammer” and “Permanent Brain Damage.”

name: Costas Simitis
headline: Costas Simitis, 2-Time Prime Minister of Greece, Dies at 88
abstract: Mr. Simitis imposed financial measures to prepare for Greece’s entry into the eurozone and laid the groundwork for the Olympic Games’ return to Athens.

name: Friedrich St. Florian
profession: Architect of World War II Memorial
headline: Friedrich St. Florian, Architect of World War II Memorial, Dies at 91
abstract: His design was criticized as banal and beneath its subject. It was also praised for fitting seamlessly into hallowed space on the National Mall.

name: Mel Shapiro
profession: Honored Stage Director of Two Gentlemen
headline: Mel Shapiro, Honored Stage Director of ‘Two Gentlemen,’ Dies at 89
abstract: He worked with the playwright John Guare in mounting his “House of Blue Leaves,” and they helped turn “The Two Gentlemen of Verona” into a hit musical.

name: Mike Rinder
headline: Mike Rinder, Scientology Spokesman Turned Critic, Dies at 69
abstract: In a memoir and as a host of the documentary series “Leah Remini: Scientology and the Aftermath,” he accused the church of fostering a culture of abuse.

name: Jean-Marie Le Pen
profession: Rabble-Rousing Leader of French Far Right
headline: Jean-Marie Le Pen, Rabble-Rousing Leader of French Far Right, Dies at 96
abstract: He ran unsuccessfully for the French presidency five times, riding waves of discontent and xenophobia as the leader of the National Front party.

name: Peter Yarrow
headline: Peter Yarrow, of the Folk Group Peter, Paul and Mary, Dies at 86
abstract: The trio he formed with Noel Paul Stookey and Mary Travers became a pop phenomenon, scoring hits like “If I Had a Hammer” and “Puff the Magic Dragon.”

name: Pippa Garner
profession: Conceptual Artist With a Satirical Streak
headline: Pippa Garner, Conceptual Artist With a Satirical Streak, Dies at 82
abstract: Her witty drawings, arresting sculptures and outlandish gadgets commented on consumerism, gender relations (she had transitioned), American car culture and more.

name: Josh White Jr.
profession: Built on His Fathers Folk Legacy
headline: Josh White Jr., Who Built on His Father’s Folk Legacy, Dies at 84
abstract: He began performing at 4 alongside his father, the celebrated singer and guitarist Josh White, and later carved out his own career.

name: Ed Van Put
profession: Hooked Jimmy Carter on the Catskills
headline: Ed Van Put, Who Hooked Jimmy Carter on the Catskills, Dies at 88
abstract: A master fly-fisherman, author and conservationist, he guided the famous, including a former president, and the not-so-famous in the hunt for rainbow trout.

name: Carole Wilbourn
headline: Carole Wilbourn, Who Put Cats on the Couch, Dies at 84
abstract: When cats bite or scratch, they’re trying to tell you something. Ms. Wilbourn, a cat therapist, was a pioneer in the art of listening to them.

name: Peter Fenwick
headline: Peter Fenwick, Leading Expert on Near-Death Experiences, Dies at 89
abstract: He was a neuropsychiatrist who was studying consciousness when a patient explained what had happened to him. He came to believe the phenomenon was real.

name: Otto Schenk
profession: Opera Director and Bulwark of Tradition
headline: Otto Schenk, Opera Director and Bulwark of Tradition, Dies at 94
abstract: A prominent practitioner of the historically grand productions that were once fashionable at the Met, he was especially well known for his stagings of Wagner.

name: Paul Oreffice
headline: Paul Oreffice, a Combative Chief of Dow Chemical, Dies at 97
abstract: He led the company as it flourished in the ’70s and ’80s while confronting veterans and environmentalists over its toxic products like Agent Orange and dioxin.

name: Bob Veale
headline: Bob Veale, Towering Fireballer for the ’60s Pirates, Dies at 89
abstract: A 6-foot-6 strikeout king, he was a star of the Pittsburgh rotation who left batters wary of both his fastball and his wildness.

name: Anita Bryant
profession: Anti-Gay Politics Undid a Singing Career
headline: Anita Bryant, Whose Anti-Gay Politics Undid a Singing Career, Is Dead at 84
abstract: The former beauty queen and spokeswoman for Florida orange juice was an all-American entertainer before she began crusading against L.G.B.T.Q. rights.

name: Mauro Morandi
headline: Mauro Morandi, Italy’s Robinson Crusoe, Dies at 85
abstract: He was the sole resident of Budelli, an undeveloped sliver of paradise off the northern coast of Sardinia. He embraced the solitude, until he was evicted.

name: James Arthur Ray
headline: James Arthur Ray, 67, Self-Help Guide Whose Retreat Became Deadly, Dies
abstract: A rising star among New Age motivational speakers, he was brought down by a disaster during one of his retreats in Arizona, where three people died in a sweat lodge.

name: Sam Moore
headline: Sam Moore of the Dynamic Soul Duo Sam & Dave Is Dead at 89
abstract: Mr. Moore and Dave Prater stormed the R&B and pop charts with indelible hits like “Soul Man” and “Hold On, I’m Comin’.”

name: Seymour P. Lachman
headline: Seymour P. Lachman, Who Exposed Political Cabals in Albany, Dies at 91
abstract: In “Three Men in a Room,” Mr. Lachman, an educator and former state senator, charted how power was secretly and corruptly wielded in New York State government.

name: J. Fraser Stoddart
headline: J. Fraser Stoddart, Who Developed Microscopic Machines, Dies at 82
abstract: He grew up playing with model construction sets. As an adult, he tinkered with molecules instead, creating nanomachines and winning a Nobel Prize.

name: Charles Person
profession: Youngest of the Original Freedom Riders
headline: Charles Person, Youngest of the Original Freedom Riders, Dies at 82
abstract: In 1961, he and 12 other civil rights activists were nearly killed for trying to integrate interstate bus terminals across the South.

name: Abigail McGrath
headline: Abigail McGrath, Founder of an Experimental Theater, Dies at 84
abstract: She was an aspiring actor when she was cast in an Andy Warhol film called “Tub Girls.” But she was best known for the beloved Off Center Theater.

name: Richard Hays
headline: Richard Hays, 76, Dies; Theologian Who Had Stunning Change of Heart
abstract: He released a thunderclap into the evangelical world by asserting that a deeper reading of the Bible revealed that same-sex relationships are not sinful.

name: Oliviero Toscani
profession: Driving Force Behind Provocative Benetton Ads
headline: Oliviero Toscani, Driving Force Behind Provocative Benetton Ads, Dies at 82
abstract: A photographer and art director, he broke the boundaries of advertising in the 1980s and ’90s, embracing activism with images evoking AIDS and racial and sexual diversity.

name: Leslie Charleson
headline: Leslie Charleson, ‘General Hospital’ Actress, Dies at 79
abstract: Ms. Charleson played Dr. Monica Quartermaine, a cardiologist and family matriarch, on the daytime series for 46 years.

name: Stuart Spencer
headline: Stuart Spencer, Political Pioneer Who Helped Propel Reagan’s Rise, Dies at 97
abstract: One of the nation’s first campaign consultants for hire, he advised leading Republicans, including President Gerald Ford, but Reagan was his prized candidate.

name: Martin Karplus
headline: Martin Karplus, Chemist Who Made Early Computers a Tool, Dies at 94
abstract: Proving skeptics wrong, he shared a Nobel Prize in 2013 for using computers to better understand chemical reactions and biological processes.

name: Karen Wynn Fonstad
headline: Overlooked No More: Karen Wynn Fonstad, Who Mapped Tolkien’s Middle-earth
abstract: She was a novice cartographer who landed a dream assignment: to create an atlas of the setting of “The Hobbit” and “The Lord of the Rings.”

name: Rick Kuhn
profession: Convicted in a College Gambling Scandal
headline: Rick Kuhn, 69, Dies; Convicted in a College Gambling Scandal
abstract: While playing basketball at Boston College, he participated in a point-shaving scheme with Henry Hill, the mobster later portrayed in the movie “Goodfellas.”

name: Bill McCartney
headline: Bill McCartney, Coach Who Led a Movement for ‘Godly’ Men, Dies at 84
abstract: After transforming the University of Colorado’s football team, he founded the Promise Keepers, a masculine revivalist group that drew millions of supporters.

name: Howard Buten
headline: Howard Buten, Autism Therapist, Novelist and Clown, Is Dead at 74
abstract: By day, he helped run an autism center he opened in a suburb of Paris. In the evening, he delighted audiences as a clown named Buffo. In between, he wrote novels.

name: Shirah Neiman
headline: Shirah Neiman, Pathbreaking New York City Prosecutor, Dies at 81
abstract: In 1970 she broke an unwritten rule against women lawyers in the Southern District’s criminal division. She went on to mentor a long list of prominent lawyers.

name: Bob Uecker
headline: Bob Uecker, Clubhouse Wit-Turned-Popular Sportscaster, Dies at 90
abstract: Uecker turned his meager baseball career into humorous fodder covering games on TV and as a commercial pitchman.

name: David Lynch
profession: Maker of Florid and Unnerving Films
headline: David Lynch, Maker of Florid and Unnerving Films, Dies at 78
abstract: A visionary, his films included “Eraserhead,” “Blue Velvet” and “Mulholland Drive.” He also brought his skewed view to the small screen with “Twin Peaks.”

name: Tommy Brown
profession: Teenage Talent for the Brooklyn Dodgers
headline: Tommy Brown, a Teenage Talent for the Brooklyn Dodgers, Dies at 97
abstract: He was 16 when he made his debut as a shortstop in an Ebbets Field doubleheader, becoming the youngest position player in modern major-league history.

name: Nathalie Dupree
headline: Nathalie Dupree, ‘Queen of Southern Cooking,’ Dies at 85
abstract: As a cookbook author, TV personality and mentor, she sought to burst the chicken-fried stereotype of the South. Sometimes her life was as messy as her kitchen.

name: Joan Plowright
headline: Joan Plowright, Award-Winning Actress and Olivier’s Widow, Dies at 95
abstract: She won many accolades — and was honored with a damehood — during a seven-decade career on the London stage, in film and on Broadway.

name: Jeanne Wakatsuki Houston
headline: Jeanne Wakatsuki Houston, 90, Dies; Her Internment Inspired a Memoir
abstract: In “Farewell to Manzanar,” she wrote about the years she and her family were imprisoned in a camp for Japanese Americans. It became the basis for a TV movie.

name: Zilia Sánchez
headline: Zilia Sánchez, Painter Who Found Fame Late in Life, Dies at 98
abstract: A Cuban-born minimalist painter who spent much of her life in Puerto Rico, she was in her 90s when her erotically charged work first appeared at the Venice Biennale.

name: Jean Jennings
headline: Jean Jennings, Who Wrote With Verve About Cars, Dies at 70
abstract: A cabdriver and mechanic before becoming a journalist, she brought personality and adventure to a once-staid genre. She once won a demolition derby and motorcycled across China.

name: Gus Williams
headline: Gus Williams, Guard Who Led Seattle to an N.B.A. Title, Dies at 71
abstract: Undersized but speedy and known as the Wizard for his acrobatics, he was a high scorer who in 1979 starred in a series that brought the SuperSonics their only crown.

name: George Kalinsky
profession: Madison Square Gardens First Official Lensman
headline: George Kalinsky, 88, Madison Square Garden’s First Official Lensman, Dies
abstract: With camera in hand, he parlayed a chance encounter with Muhammad Ali into a photography career documenting the Knicks, the Rangers and Garden headliners like Elvis Presley.

name: André Soltner
profession: Famed Chef at New Yorks Lutèce
headline: André Soltner, Famed Chef at New York’s Lutèce, Dies at 92
abstract: Customers returned again and again for his impeccable French dishes at a restaurant that one food critic said “set the gold standard.”

name: Melba Montgomery
profession: Country Singer Known for Her Duets
headline: Melba Montgomery, Country Singer Known for Her Duets, Dies at 86
abstract: Her high harmonies put an emotional charge into her work with George Jones and others. She also had solo hits, including “No Charge,” a country No. 1.

name: Heinz Kluetmeier
headline: Heinz Kluetmeier, Inventive Sports Photographer, Dies at 82
abstract: His work for Sports Illustrated included the renowned cover photo of the United States men’s hockey team celebrating their upset win at the 1980 Winter Olympics.

name: David Schneiderman
headline: David Schneiderman, Village Voice Editor and Publisher, Dies at 77
abstract: Named editor in chief of the venerable alternative weekly in 1978, he was not welcomed with open arms. But his commitment to strong journalism won people over.

name: Lynne Taylor-Corbett
headline: Lynne Taylor-Corbett, ‘Footloose’ Choreographer, Dies at 78
abstract: Striving to widen the audience of dance, she brought vitality to Broadway musicals like “Swing!” as well as ballets and Hollywood films.

name: Claire van Kampen
profession: Playwright and Arranger of Period Music
headline: Claire van Kampen, 71, Playwright and Arranger of Period Music, Dies
abstract: After she married Mark Rylance, the two often collaborated; her specialty was arranging music for Tudor-era plays.

name: Cecile Richards
headline: Cecile Richards, a Dynamic Leader of Planned Parenthood, Dies at 67
abstract: She oversaw the United States’ largest provider of reproductive health care and sex education from 2006 to 2018.

name: Jules Feiffer
headline: Jules Feiffer, Acerbic Cartoonist, Writer and Much Else, Dies at 95
abstract: In his long-running Village Voice comic strip and in his many plays and screenplays, he took delight in skewering politics, relationships and human nature.

name: Garth Hudson
headline: Garth Hudson, One-Man Band Within the Band, Dies at 87
abstract: A multifaceted musician, he was the last surviving original member of an influential group that mixed rock, r&b and an Americana sound.

name: Joel Paley
headline: Joel Paley, Writer of ‘Ruthless,’ an Off Broadway Hit, Dies at 69
abstract: The show, with music by Marvin Laird, portrayed a schoolgirl’s murderous theatrical ambition. Paley also performed in the parody dance group Les Ballets Trockadero.

name: Bimla Bissell
profession: Ambassadors Aide and a Social Hub in India
headline: Bimla Bissell, Ambassadors’ Aide and a Social Hub in India, Dies at 92
abstract: Her home drew generations of heads of state, U.S. diplomats, journalists and artists, who relied on her for her political acumen and were buoyed by her friendship.

name: Jeff Torborg
profession: Catcher of Three No-Hitters and a Manager
headline: Jeff Torborg, Catcher of Three No-Hitters and a Manager, Dies at 83
abstract: He called every pitch of Sandy Koufax’s perfect game in 1965. After 10 seasons playing in the majors, he skippered the White Sox and the Mets.

name: Carolyn Brown
headline: Carolyn Brown, a Shaper of Revolutionary Dance, Dies at 97
abstract: With Merce Cunningham, she forged one of the great partnerships in dance history. She later recounted those years in an incisive, unsparing memoir.

name: Clinton Bailey
headline: Clinton Bailey, Who Documented a Vanishing Bedouin Culture, Dies at 88
abstract: Armed with a camera and tape recorder, he spent decades preserving the ancient traditions of nomadic Middle Eastern tribes.

name: Lynn Ban
profession: Jewelry Designer and Bling Empire Star
headline: Lynn Ban, Jewelry Designer and ‘Bling Empire’ Star, Dies at 52
abstract: Her jewelry creations were worn by celebrities like Rihanna and Beyoncé. She died weeks after emergency surgery following a skiing accident.

name: José Jiménez
profession: Turned a Gang Into a Voice for Puerto Ricans
headline: José Jiménez Dies at 76; Turned a Gang Into a Voice for Puerto Ricans
abstract: He retooled the Young Lords into a militant advocacy and service organization, modeled after the Black Panthers. Based in Chicago, it had chapters nationwide.

name: Charles Phan
headline: Charles Phan, Whose Slanted Door Elevated Vietnamese Food, Dies at 62
abstract: A culinary star familiar on TV, he married local ingredients with the food he grew up on in running an acclaimed San Francisco restaurant and its offshoots.

name: Bertrand Blier
profession: Acclaimed Director of Sexually Blunt Films
headline: Bertrand Blier, Acclaimed Director of Sexually Blunt Films, Dies at 85
abstract: An award-winning French filmmaker, he won an Oscar for “Get Out Your Handkerchiefs.” But he divided audiences with explorations of misogyny and the male sexual imagination.

name: Aaron De Groft
profession: Museum Director Accused in Fake Basquiat Scheme
headline: Aaron De Groft, Museum Director Accused in Fake Basquiat Scheme, Dies at 59
abstract: In Orlando, he staged a blockbuster exhibition of works said to be newly discovered paintings by Jean-Michel Basquiat. He was fired when the paintings turned out to be forgeries.

name: Arthur Blessitt
profession: Carried a Cross Around the World
headline: Arthur Blessitt, Who Carried a Cross Around the World, Dies at 84
abstract: A street preacher from Hollywood, he set out on a walk to New York City in 1969 with a 110-pound cross on his back. Then he kept going.

name: Derek Humphry
headline: Derek Humphry, Pivotal Figure in Right-to-Die Movement, Dies at 94
abstract: His own experience assisting his terminally ill wife in ending her life set him on a path to founding the Hemlock Society and writing a best-selling guide.

name: Thomas Gaither
profession: Chose Jail After Civil Rights Sit-ins
headline: Thomas Gaither, Who Chose Jail After Civil Rights Sit-ins, Dies at 86
abstract: When he and other Black protesters were arrested at a whites-only lunch counter in 1961, they tried a new strategy — ‘Jail No Bail’ — and energized a movement.

name: Jo Baer
headline: Jo Baer, Minimalist Painter Who Rejected Abstraction, Dies at 95
abstract: After establishing herself as a leading proponent of nonrepresentational art, she left it behind — along with her position in the art world.

name: Nancy Leftenant-Colon
profession: Army Nurse Broke a Color Barrier
headline: Nancy Leftenant-Colon, 104, Dies; Army Nurse Broke a Color Barrier
abstract: After years of being barred from a segregated military, she became the first Black nurse in the regular U.S. armed forces. She was later an Air Force officer.

name: Mike Hynson
profession: Surfing Star of The Endless Summer
headline: Mike Hynson, Surfing Star of ‘The Endless Summer,’ Dies at 82
abstract: The hit 1966 surfing documentary immortalized the maverick California wave rider as an archetype of the footloose rebel surfer.

name: Carol Downer
headline: Carol Downer, Feminist Leader in Women’s Health, Dies at 91
abstract: She opened clinics, worked to educate women about their reproductive health, and promoted an abortion technique she felt was safe enough for laypeople.

name: François Ponchaud
headline: François Ponchaud, Who Alerted World to Cambodian Atrocities, Dies at 85
abstract: A French Catholic priest, he wrote a book recounting horrors committed by the Khmer Rouge that were responsible for the deaths of almost two million people.

name: Mauricio Funes
headline: Mauricio Funes, Salvadoran President Who Fled to Nicaragua, Dies at 65
abstract: He was a popular TV journalist when elected as El Salvador’s first modern-day leftist leader in 2009, but he went into exile hounded by corruption charges.

name: Jay Mazur
headline: Jay Mazur, Zealous Advocate for Garment Workers, Dies at 92
abstract: A blunt-speaking, Bronx-born labor leader, he successfully pushed to legalize undocumented union members but fought a losing battle against globalization.

name: Pableaux Johnson
headline: Pableaux Johnson, the Heart of New Orleans Hospitality, Dies at 59
abstract: As a photographer, cook and writer, he united communities through shared meals, vivid storytelling and a deep love of the city’s traditions.

name: Barry Michael Cooper
headline: Barry Michael Cooper, ‘New Jack City’ Screenwriter, Dies at 66
abstract: After chronicling the crack boom of the 1980s as an investigative reporter, he had a high-profile but brief second career in Hollywood.

name: William E. Leuchtenburg
profession: Scholar of F.D.R. and the Presidency
headline: William E. Leuchtenburg, Scholar of F.D.R. and the Presidency, Dies at 102
abstract: His writings, which stretched across eight decades, helped Americans understand a president who transformed the office and shaped the postwar years.

name: Stephan Thernstrom
headline: Stephan Thernstrom, Leading Critic of Affirmative Action, Dies at 90
abstract: A prizewinning historian, he, along and his wife, Abigail, was a conservative opponent of racial preferences, favoring school choice and voucher programs instead.

name: Iris Cummings Critchell
headline: Iris Cummings Critchell, 104, Dies; ’36 Olympic Swimmer Turned Aviator
abstract: The last survivor of the American team that competed in Hitler’s 1936 Games in Berlin, she went on to become a wartime pilot and an aeronautics instructor.

name: George Tice
profession: Bard of New Jersey With a Camera
headline: George Tice, ‘Bard of New Jersey’ With a Camera, Dies at 86
abstract: He found beauty in the prosaic: bars, phone booths, hamburger joints, barber shops — first in a downtrodden Paterson, then throughout the state and beyond.

name: Marianne Faithfull
headline: Marianne Faithfull, a Pop Star Turned Survivor, Is Dead at 78
abstract: A fresh-faced singer in the 1960s, she went on to experience more than her share of hard times before emerging triumphant in the ’70s.

name: Wolfgang Zwiener
headline: Wolfgang Zwiener, Waiter Who Built a Steakhouse Empire, Dies at 85
abstract: After years of waiting tables at Peter Luger in Brooklyn, he opened Wolfgang’s Steakhouse in Manhattan, the first of 35 restaurants around the world.

name: Loretta Ford
profession: Mother of the Nurse Practitioner Field
headline: Loretta Ford, ‘Mother’ of the Nurse Practitioner Field, Dies at 104
abstract: She transformed nursing by making it an area of clinical practice and research and recasting nurses as colleagues of doctors, not assistants.

name: Muhammad Deif
headline: Muhammad Deif, Hamas Military Commander in Gaza, Is Dead
abstract: Mr. Deif was assassinated in an Israeli strike on southern Gaza on July 13, Israel said. He was one of the most senior Hamas leaders inside the territory and one of Israel’s most-wanted militants.

name: Dick Button
profession: Figure Skating Champion and TV Commentator
headline: Dick Button, 95, Figure Skating Champion and TV Commentator, Dies
abstract: He won an Emmy for his enthusiastic and sometimes acerbic analysis on sportscasts, but before that he made history as a two-time Olympic gold medalist.

name: James Carlos Blake
headline: James Carlos Blake, Novelist of Outlaw Life, Is Dead at 81
abstract: His savage fiction, set in the U.S.-Mexico borderlands, demonstrated his belief that “violence is the most elemental truth of life.”

name: Barry Goldberg
profession: Backed Dylan When He Went Electric
headline: Barry Goldberg, Who Backed Dylan When He Went Electric, Dies at 83
abstract: He played keyboards with a host of rock luminaries, but perhaps his most memorable performance was as part of the band that shocked the 1965 Newport Folk Festival.

name: Phyllis Dalton
profession: Oscar-Winning Costume Designer for Historical Epics
headline: Phyllis Dalton, Oscar-Winning Costume Designer for Historical Epics, Dies at 99
abstract: A look back at some of her most celebrated works, including “Doctor Zhivago,” “The Princess Bride” and “Lawrence of Arabia.”

name: Jaune Quick-to-See Smith
headline: Jaune Quick-to-See Smith, Artist With an Indigenous Focus, Dies at 85
abstract: She began with modestly scaled abstract drawings and paintings but became best known for large works featuring collage and items evoking Native stereotypes.

name: Annie Easley
profession: Helped Take Spaceflight to New Heights
headline: Overlooked No More: Annie Easley, Who Helped Take Spaceflight to New Heights
abstract: She broke barriers at NASA and contributed to its earliest space missions as a rocket scientist, mathematician and computer programmer.

name: Suzanne Massie
profession: Reagans Window on the Soviet Union
headline: Suzanne Massie, ‘Reagan’s Window on the Soviet Union,’ Dies at 94
abstract: An author of books on Russia who spoke the language, she had no diplomatic experience but formed an unlikely bond with the president.

name: Horst Köhler
profession: Former German President and I.M.F. Leader
headline: Horst Köhler, 81, Former German President and I.M.F. Leader, Dies
abstract: He held the ceremonial post of German president after a finance-focused career. Shortly into his second term, he became the first German president in four decades to resign.

name: Millicent Dillon
profession: Chronicler of Jane and Paul Bowles
headline: Millicent Dillon, Chronicler of Jane and Paul Bowles, Dies at 99
abstract: A novelist and short-story writer, she devoted years to a nonfiction project examining of the lives of two eccentric authors who spent decades in Morocco.

name: Fay Vincent
profession: Baseball Commissioner in a Stormy Era
headline: Fay Vincent, Baseball Commissioner in a Stormy Era, Dies at 86
abstract: He presided in a period of union strife, the emergence of steroid use, the banning of Pete Rose and an earthquake that rattled a World Series.

name: Karen Pryor
headline: Karen Pryor, Guru of Positive Reinforcement, Is Dead at 92
abstract: She was so successful at training dolphins that she began applying the same techniques to other creatures, including dogs — and humans.

name: Marion Wiesel
headline: Marion Wiesel, Translator, Strategist and Wife of Elie Wiesel, Dies at 94
abstract: A fellow survivor, she was a literary and political adviser who helped her husband gain recognition as a singular moral authority on the Holocaust.

name: Merle Louise Simon
headline: Merle Louise Simon, a Sondheim Mainstay, Is Dead at 90
abstract: She originated roles in four of his Broadway musicals between 1959 and 1987, and won a Drama Desk Award for her performance in “Sweeney Todd.”

name: Alonzo Davis
profession: L.A. Gallery Became a Hub for Black Art
headline: Alonzo Davis, 82, Whose L.A. Gallery Became a Hub for Black Art, Dies
abstract: An accomplished artist himself, he and his brother created one of the few showcases in the U.S. for an emerging generation of Black artists in the late 1960s.

name: Kultida Woods
headline: Kultida Woods, Mother of Tiger Woods, Dies at 78
abstract: A frequent presence in her son’s public life, she stood by his side during a period of scandal that took him away from golf.

name: Richard Williamson
headline: Richard Williamson, Renegade Priest and Holocaust Denier, Dies at 84
abstract: Ordained as a bishop by a traditionalist sect, he was excommunicated and then reinstated by the Vatican, but he was undone by his antisemitic views.

name: The Aga Khan IV
profession: Wealthy Leader of the Ismaili Muslims
headline: The Aga Khan IV, Wealthy Leader of the Ismaili Muslims, Dies at 88
abstract: At the age of 20, Prince Karim Al-Hussaini inherited the reins of a Shia Muslim lineage and used his entrepreneurship to become one of the world’s richest hereditary rulers.

name: Samuel Butler
headline: Samuel Butler, Lawyer Who Helped Create Corporate Giants, Dies at 94
abstract: Leading the elite Wall Street firm Cravath, he became a go-to adviser on mergers and acquisitions — “all the big deals that were going on in the ’80s and ’90s.”

name: Gene Barge
headline: Gene Barge, R&B Saxophonist Who Played on Landmark Hits, Dies at 98
abstract: Known as Daddy G, he recorded with Jackie Wilson, Chuck Willis and others, but he was best known for the Gary U.S. Bonds smash “Quarter to Three.”

name: Harry Stewart Jr.
profession: One of Last Tuskegee Airmen to See Combat
headline: Harry Stewart Jr. Dies at 100; One of Last Tuskegee Airmen to See Combat
abstract: His boyhood dream to be an adventurous pilot was fulfilled thanks to World War II. But, as a civilian, racial prejudice kept him out of the cockpit.

name: Ernest Drucker
headline: Ernest Drucker, Public-Health Advocate for the Scorned, Dies at 84
abstract: He marshaled epidemiological research to press for changes in drug policy, alternatives to prison and needle-exchange programs to slow the spread of AIDS.

name: Paul Plishka
headline: Paul Plishka, Prolific Soloist at the Met, Dies at 83
abstract: Known for his liquid bass tones and flawless diction, he appeared in 88 roles, many of them comic, over 1,672 performances at the Metropolitan Opera.

name: Valérie André
headline: Valérie André, Daring French Army Copter Pilot, Dies at 102
abstract: She was the first woman to fly rescue missions in a combat zone, in Indochina and Algeria. She was also the first Frenchwoman to become an army general.

name: Anson Rabinbach
headline: Anson Rabinbach, Leading Historian of Nazi Culture, Dies at 79
abstract: He demonstrated that fascism had its own intellectual roots and showed how ideas, theories and an antisemitic “ethos” influenced German culture and policymaking.

name: Irv Gotti
headline: Irv Gotti, Streetwise Hip-Hop Music Mogul, Dies at 54
abstract: A founder of Murder Inc. Records, he helped launch the careers of Ja Rule and Ashanti and was credited as a producer on 28 records that made the Billboard Hot 100.

name: Susan Alcorn
headline: Susan Alcorn, Voyager on Pedal Steel Guitar, Dies at 71
abstract: With a daring avant-garde approach, she pushed the frontiers of an instrument best known for speaking with a down-home accent.

name: Susan F. Wood
profession: Quit F.D.A. Over Contraception Pill Delay
headline: Susan F. Wood, Who Quit F.D.A. Over Contraception Pill Delay, Dies at 66
abstract: She left the agency saying politics had slowed the approval of the morning-after pill for over-the-counter use. Her resignation drew national attention.

name: Virginia McCaskey
profession: Owner and Stalwart of the Chicago Bears
headline: Virginia McCaskey, 102, Owner and Stalwart of the Chicago Bears, Dies
abstract: The daughter of the Bears founder and football pioneer, George Halas, she witnessed much of N.F.L. history from a young age, then took the team’s reins in 1983.

name: Cleveland Harris
headline: Cleveland Harris, N.F.L. Coach Who Pushed for Diversity, Dies at 79
abstract: An assistant coach for 33 years, he never fulfilled his dream of becoming a head coach, a rarity for a Black man. But he pressed the league to open the door for future minority coaches.

name: C. Richard Kramlich
headline: C. Richard Kramlich, Early Investor in Silicon Valley, Dies at 89
abstract: He was among the first backers of Apple Computer and 3Com, earning windfalls, but it was his humaneness that distinguished him from other venture capitalists.

name: Mort Künstler
profession: Renowned Painter of Epic Historical Scenes
headline: Mort Künstler, Renowned Painter of Epic Historical Scenes, Dies at 97
abstract: His years illustrating pulp novels honed his sense of pictorial drama, and his meticulous research ensured historical accuracy, notably in his Civil War paintings.

name: Monica Getz
headline: Monica Getz, Advocate for Divorce Court Reform, Dies at 90
abstract: Her troubled marriage to the jazz star Stan Getz led to a headline-making divorce case. The result of the trial gave her a cause to fight for.

name: Howard Twilley
profession: Super Bowl Scorer for Undefeated Miami
headline: Howard Twilley, Super Bowl Scorer for Undefeated Miami, Dies at 81
abstract: After a stellar college football career, he spent 11 years with the Dolphins. He caught a touchdown pass in 1973 that concluded the team’s 17-0 season.

name: Tony Roberts
profession: Nonchalant Pal in Woody Allens Films
headline: Tony Roberts, a Nonchalant Pal in Woody Allen’s Films, Dies at 85
abstract: He had an acclaimed Broadway career in musicals and comedies, but moviegoers knew him mostly as the self-assured, easygoing friend of Mr. Allen’s insecure heroes.

name: Amy Lau
profession: Interior Designer and a Founder of Design Miami
headline: Amy Lau, Interior Designer and a Founder of Design Miami, Dies at 56
abstract: Known for her expertise on midcentury modernism and love of Southwestern colors, she also helped create an annual event showcasing the work of other designers.

name: Sam Nujoma
headline: Sam Nujoma, Founding President of Namibia, Dies at 95
abstract: As the self-exiled leader of the South-West Africa People’s Organization, he directed a guerrilla army in a 24-year war for independence from South African rule.

name: Gyalo Thondup
profession: Political Operator and Brother of the Dalai Lama
headline: Gyalo Thondup, Political Operator and Brother of the Dalai Lama, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Thondup’s influence in Tibet has been seen as second only to his younger brother, Tenzin Gyatso, the exiled head of Tibetan Buddhism, whom he spent decades trying to help return to their homeland.

name: Rutherford Chang
headline: Rutherford Chang, Who Turned Collections Into Art, Dies at 45
abstract: He was best known for amassing more than 3,400 copies of the Beatles’ “White Album” and using them to demonstrate the aging of a cultural artifact.

name: Tom Robbins
profession: Comic Novels Drew a Cult Following
headline: Tom Robbins, Whose Comic Novels Drew a Cult Following, Dies at 92
abstract: He blended pop philosophy and absurdist comedy in best-selling books like “Even Cowgirls Get the Blues” and “Skinny Legs and All.”

name: Tom Robbins
profession: Versatile Muckraker for The Village Voice
headline: Tom Robbins, Versatile Muckraker for The Village Voice, Dies at 76
abstract: He exposed corrupt officials and greedy landlords, and his reporting on prison violence was a finalist for the Pulitzer Prize.

name: Maria Teresa Horta
headline: Maria Teresa Horta, the Last of Portugal’s ‘Three Marias,’ Dies at 87
abstract: The book on which she collaborated with two fellow feminists drew global attention to the repression of women under their country’s dictatorship.

name: Helen Hays
profession: Helped Bring Terns Back to Long Island Sound
headline: Helen Hays, Who Helped Bring Terns Back to Long Island Sound, Dies at 94
abstract: Beginning in 1969, she spent five months a year on Great Gull Island, leading teams of young volunteers devoted to preserving the seabirds.

name: Christopher Jencks
profession: Shaper of Views on Economic Inequality
headline: Christopher Jencks, a Shaper of Views on Economic Inequality, Dies at 88
abstract: His clear prose, illuminating data and novel arguments, transformed debates around issues like public education and welfare reform.

name: David Edward Byrd
headline: David Edward Byrd, Whose Posters Captured Rock’s Energy, Dies at 83
abstract: His designs for Jimi Hendrix, the Who and others embodied the spirit of the psychedelic era. He also created images for stage shows like “Godspell.”

name: Michael Longley
profession: Northern Irish Poet of Nature and the Troubles
headline: Michael Longley, 85, Northern Irish Poet of Nature and ‘the Troubles,’ Dies
abstract: “Ceasefire,” his most famous poem, invoked the “Iliad” in exploring his country’s sectarian strife. But his work wasn’t Homeric in length: “Michael was a miniaturist.”

name: Jim Guy Tucker
profession: Ex-Arkansas Governor Caught Up in Whitewater
headline: Jim Guy Tucker, Ex-Arkansas Governor Caught Up in Whitewater, Dies at 81
abstract: He was among those targeted by the investigation that consumed much of Bill Clinton’s presidency. But his conviction was later questioned.

name: Lena Richard
profession: Brought Creole Cooking to the Masses
headline: Overlooked No More: Lena Richard, Who Brought Creole Cooking to the Masses
abstract: She hosted a cooking show years before Julia Child was on the air, tantalizing viewers with okra gumbo, shrimp bisque and other Southern specialties.

name: Barbie Hsu
profession: Taiwanese Actress and Star of Meteor Garden
headline: Barbie Hsu, Taiwanese Actress and Star of ‘Meteor Garden,’ Dies at 48
abstract: Her role in the teen drama catapulted her to fame as a pop idol. She was also a TV host and appeared in films.

name: Walter Robinson
headline: Walter Robinson, Exuberant Art-World Participant and Observer, Dies at 74
abstract: A painter who took his subjects from pop culture, he was also the founding editor of Artnet.com and chronicled the rise of the SoHo art scene in the 1970s.

name: Eleanor Maguire
headline: Eleanor Maguire, Memory Expert Who Studied London Cabbies, Dies at 54
abstract: By watching the brain process information, she discovered that a specific region plays a key role in spatial navigation — and that it can be strengthened like a muscle.

name: Ken Wydro
profession: Helped Create an Off Broadway Phenomenon
headline: Ken Wydro, Who Helped Create an Off Broadway Phenomenon, Dies at 81
abstract: He and his wife, Vy Higginsen, poured all they had into “Mama, I Want to Sing,” a long-shot musical that became an enduring staple of Black theater.

name: Graham Nickson
profession: Passionate Steward of the New York Studio School
headline: Graham Nickson, 78, Dies; Passionate Steward of the New York Studio School
abstract: An artist known for his lush, large-scale oil paintings, he also created the Drawing Marathon, a two-week boot camp that transformed the lives of participants.

name: Edith Mathis
headline: Edith Mathis, Radiant Swiss Soprano, Is Dead at 86
abstract: Known for her interpretations of Bach, Mozart and Weber, she was praised for her clear, bright voice and her perfect intonation even on the highest notes.

name: Nelson Johnson
profession: Labor Leader Wounded in Greensboro Massacre
headline: Nelson Johnson, Labor Leader Wounded in Greensboro Massacre, Dies at 81
abstract: White supremacists killed five people in a 1979 shootout in North Carolina. Mr. Johnson later led a commission that investigated the attack.

name: Yrjo Kukkapuro
profession: Made the Easiest of Easy Chairs
headline: Yrjo Kukkapuro, Who Made the Easiest of Easy Chairs, Dies at 91
abstract: A celebrated Finnish modernist, he designed a variety of furnishings but was best known for his seating, which, his company said, “almost every Finn has sat on.”

name: Ron Travisano
profession: Adman Behind Singing Cats and Joe Isuzu
headline: Ron Travisano, Adman Behind Singing Cats and Joe Isuzu, Dies at 86
abstract: The art director for Meow Mix and other memorable commercials, he began his career at the dawn of a creative revolution on Madison Avenue.

name: Zakia Jafri
profession: Sought Justice for Victims of Indian Riots
headline: Zakia Jafri, Who Sought Justice for Victims of Indian Riots, Dies at 86
abstract: For two decades, she waged a legal battle against government officials in India after her husband was brutally killed in Gujarat in 2002.

name: Paquita la del Barrio
headline: Paquita la del Barrio, Whose Songs Empowered Women, Dies at 77
abstract: In unflinching ballads that spoke of the pain men can cause women, the Mexican singer often relied on what she learned in her own relationships.

name: Gil Won-ok
profession: Crusading Victim of Wartime Sex Slavery
headline: Gil Won-ok, Crusading Victim of Wartime Sex Slavery, Dies at 96
abstract: She campaigned for a formal apology and reparations from Japan for what it did to thousands of women like her, mostly Korean, during World War II.

name: Anne Marie Hochhalter
headline: Anne Marie Hochhalter, Paralyzed in Columbine Shooting, Dies at 43
abstract: Fiercely independent, she publicly discussed the long-term effects of gun violence and spoke of forgiveness.

name: Dickson Despommier
headline: Dickson Despommier Dies at 84; Championed Farming in Skyscrapers
abstract: A Columbia microbiologist, he popularized “vertical farming” — raising crops in tall buildings — to remediate climate change and feed more people.

name: Dorothy Chin Brandt
headline: Dorothy Chin Brandt, Trailblazing Asian American Judge, Dies at 78
abstract: She was the first descendant of a Chinese immigrant to win elective office in New York State. She was also the state’s first female jurist of Asian heritage.

name: Gerd Stern
profession: Beat Era Poet and Multimedia Artist
headline: Gerd Stern, Beat Era Poet and Multimedia Artist, Dies at 96
abstract: An Aquarian Age savant, he was a founder of the artists’ collective USCO, which helped define the 1960s with psychedelic, sensory-overloading installations and performances.

name: Donald Shoup
profession: Scholar Saw the Social Costs of Free Parking
headline: Donald Shoup, 86, Dies; Scholar Saw the Social Costs of Free Parking
abstract: He took a dry topic and made it entertaining, capturing the attention of policymakers and influencing the way cities are built.

name: Souleymane Cissé
headline: Souleymane Cissé, Celebrated Malian Filmmaker, Dies at 84
abstract: He won multiple awards during his 50-year career, including the jury prize at the Cannes Film Festival, and spent his life championing African cinema.

name: David Boren
profession: Oklahoma Eminence as Governor and Senator
headline: David Boren, an Oklahoma Eminence as Governor and Senator, Dies at 83
abstract: A Democrat, he became a powerful voice on national intelligence in the Senate before leaving to become president of the University of Oklahoma.

name: Tom Fitzmorris
headline: Tom Fitzmorris, Colorful New Orleans Food Critic, Dies at 74
abstract: In print, online and on the radio, he parlayed a savant’s mastery of his city’s restaurant menus and a love of the spotlight into a career that spanned five decades.

name: Marshall Rose
profession: Helped Revive Two New York Institutions
headline: Marshall Rose, Who Helped Revive Two New York Institutions, Dies at 88
abstract: A real estate developer, he was instrumental in revitalizing the New York Public Library and transforming Bryant Park from a dangerous dead zone into a glorious sanctuary.

name: Jerry Butler
profession: Hitmaking Singer Known as the Iceman
headline: Jerry Butler, Hitmaking Singer Known as the Iceman, Dies at 85
abstract: With his resounding baritone and courtly manner, he led the Impressions before beginning a solo career, recording songs like “Only the Strong Survive.”

name: Olga James
profession: Star of Carmen Jones and Mr. Wonderful
headline: Olga James, a Star of ‘Carmen Jones’ and ‘Mr. Wonderful,’ Dies at 95
abstract: An operatic soprano, she had high-profile roles on film and stage in the 1950s. But after that, she mostly spent her career away from the limelight.

name: William R. Lucas
headline: William R. Lucas, Official Blamed in Challenger Tragedy, Dies at 102
abstract: The strong-willed director of NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center, he failed to pass on warnings from engineers that the space shuttle launch was at risk.

name: Voletta Wallace
headline: Voletta Wallace, Mother Who Shaped the Notorious B.I.G.’s Legacy, Dies at 78
abstract: She played the rapper music as a child, stood by him during his career and navigated the legal and artistic questions that arose after his killing.

name: Mel Bochner
headline: Mel Bochner, Conceptual Artist Who Played With Language, Dies at 84
abstract: His early work made use of unexpected materials like pennies and masking tape. Later, he created trenchant word paintings that provoked and delighted.

name: Patsy Grimaldi
headline: Patsy Grimaldi, Whose Name Became Synonymous With Pizza, Dies at 93
abstract: His coal-oven pizzeria in the shadow of the Brooklyn Bridge has drawn patrons from New York City and beyond.

name: Carlos Diegues
headline: Carlos Diegues, Filmmaker Who Celebrated Brazil’s Diversity, Dies at 84
abstract: Seeking to shed the gauzy influence of Hollywood and focus on Brazil’s ethnic richness and troubled history, he helped forge a new path for his country’s cinema.

name: Ken Rosenthal
headline: Ken Rosenthal, Founder of Panera Bread’s Forerunner, Dies at 81
abstract: He built a small chain of bakery cafes, with sourdough bread as its star. A few years after it was sold, it became nationally famous under a new name.

name: Lynne Marie Stewart
headline: Lynne Marie Stewart, Miss Yvonne on ‘Pee-wee’s Playhouse,’ Dies at 78
abstract: She was the “most beautiful woman in Puppetland” in the 1980s children’s show starring Paul Reubens, and more recently had a recurring role in “It’s Always Sunny in Philadelphia.”

name: Frank G. Wisner
profession: Diplomat With Impact on Foreign Policy
headline: Frank G. Wisner, Diplomat With Impact on Foreign Policy, Dies at 86
abstract: He headed U.S. embassies around the world and relished the role, bringing a gregarious style to promoting American interests. But he clashed with the Obama White House.

name: Roberta Flack
headline: Roberta Flack, Virtuoso Singer-Pianist Who Ruled the Charts, Dies at 88
abstract: With majestic anthems like “Killing Me Softly” and “The First Time Ever I Saw Your Face,” Ms. Flack, a former schoolteacher, became one of the most widely heard artists of the 1970s.

name: Clint Hill
profession: Sprang to Kennedys Side as Shots Were Fired
headline: Clint Hill, Who Sprang to Kennedys’ Side as Shots Were Fired, Dies at 93
abstract: A Secret Service agent, he leaped onto the president’s limousine in Dallas in 1963 and was credited with saving the first lady’s life. But he was haunted by his inability to save her husband.

name: Alvin F. Poussaint
profession: Saw Racism Affecting Black Mental Health
headline: Alvin F. Poussaint, 90, Dies; Saw Racism Affecting Black Mental Health
abstract: A psychiatrist at Harvard and an adviser to Jesse Jackson and Bill Cosby, he challenged Black Americans to stand up to systemic bigotry.

name: Al Trautwig
profession: Mainstay in the TV Booth at Madison Square Garden
headline: Al Trautwig, 68, Mainstay in the TV Booth at Madison Square Garden, Dies
abstract: He was a familiar face covering the Knicks and the Rangers and also appeared in broadcasts of 16 Olympics.

name: Marian Turski
headline: Marian Turski, Who Refused to Forget the Holocaust, Dies at 98
abstract: From influential platforms, Mr. Turski, an Auschwitz survivor from Poland, warned the world of rising antisemitism and the perils of indifference to it.

name: Michelle Trachtenberg
headline: Michelle Trachtenberg, ‘Gossip Girl’ and ‘Buffy’ Actress, Dies at 39
abstract: Police officers, responding to a 911 call, found her unresponsive in a Manhattan apartment on Wednesday morning, the authorities said.

name: Frankétienne
headline: Frankétienne, Father of Haitian Letters, Is Dead at 88
abstract: A prolific novelist, poet, painter and soothsayer, he was inspired by the chaos of his country and published the first novel written entirely in Haitian Creole.

name: Gene Hackman
headline: Gene Hackman, Hollywood’s Consummate Everyman, Dies at 95
abstract: The winner of two Oscars, he was hailed for his nuanced performances in films like “The French Connection,” “Unforgiven” and “The Royal Tenenbaums.”

name: Peter Elbow
headline: Peter Elbow, Professor Who Transformed Freshman Comp, Dies at 89
abstract: His struggles with writer’s block led him to create a process that favored an expressive, personal approach over rigid academic conventions that often stifled students.

name: Rose Girone
headline: Rose Girone, Oldest Holocaust Survivor, Dies at 113
abstract: She fled Nazi Germany in 1939 with her husband and baby only to be forced into a Jewish ghetto in Shanghai. Still, she would often say, “Aren’t we lucky?”

name: Betsy Arakawa
profession: Classical Musician and the Wife of Gene Hackman
headline: Betsy Arakawa, a Classical Musician and the Wife of Gene Hackman, Dies at 65
abstract: As the spouse of a two-time Oscar winner, she avoided interviews and stayed off social media. But in private, she typed up Mr. Hackman’s novels and helped edit them.

name: Boris Spassky
headline: Boris Spassky, Chess Champion Who Lost ‘Match of the Century,’ Dies at 88
abstract: When Mr. Spassky, a Russian, played Bobby Fischer, an American, in Iceland at the height of the Cold War, the media attention reduced them to pawns in a wider drama.

name: Joseph Wambaugh
headline: Joseph Wambaugh, Author With a Cop’s-Eye View, Is Dead at 88
abstract: In novels like “The Glitter Dome” and nonfiction works like “The Onion Field,” he took a harsh, unglamorous look at the realities of law enforcement.

name: Antonine Maillet
headline: Antonine Maillet, Writer Who Celebrated Her Native Acadia, Dies at 95
abstract: She gave voice to an overlooked French-speaking population in Canada, adapting an archaic language that had survived through oral tradition.

name: Maria Tipo
headline: Maria Tipo, Italian Pianist Who Beguiled Critics, Dies at 93
abstract: Admired by fellow musicians like Arthur Rubinstein as well as by the critics, she created what came to be known as an Italian school of piano playing.

name: Joseph Gitnig
profession: Central Park Minstrel Known as Pegasus
headline: Joseph Gitnig, Central Park Minstrel Known as Pegasus, Dies at 95
abstract: For nearly two decades, he delighted children and adults in New York City with songs and silly antics. He also scored a victory for free speech.

name: Maria W. Stewart
headline: Overlooked No More: Maria W. Stewart, Trailblazing Voice for Black Women
abstract: She was the first Black woman to publicly address other women, using essays and lectures in the 1830s to champion their rights and challenge oppression.

name: David Johansen
profession: Fronted the New York Dolls and More
headline: David Johansen, Who Fronted the New York Dolls and More, Dies at 75
abstract: In the 1970s, he and the transgressive Dolls were proto-punk pioneers. He later refashioned himself as the pompadoured lounge lizard Buster Poindexter.

name: Christian Holder
profession: Longtime Star of the Joffrey Ballet
headline: Christian Holder, Longtime Star of the Joffrey Ballet, Dies at 75
abstract: He brought his elegance and power to boundary-pushing ballets in the 1960s and ’70s, and he was a presence at the storied company for 13 years.

name: Hazel N. Dukes
headline: Hazel N. Dukes, Longtime Civil Rights Stalwart, Dies at 92
abstract: She was president of the national N.A.A.C.P. in the early 1990s and headed the organization’s New York State Conference from 1977 until her death.

name: Angie Stone
headline: Angie Stone, Hip-Hop Pioneer Turned Neo-Soul Singer, Dies at 63
abstract: After having success as a member of the Sequence, an early female rap group, she re-emerged in the 1990s as a practitioner of sultry, laid-back R&B.

name: Martin E. Marty
headline: Martin E. Marty, Influential Religious Historian, Dies at 97
abstract: A staunch champion of pluralism, he was described in Time magazine as “the most influential living interpreter of religion in the U.S.”

name: Khalil Fong
headline: Khalil Fong, Hong Kong Singer-Songwriter, Dies at 41
abstract: Singing in both Mandarin and English, he brought a soul and R&B sensibility to Chinese pop.

name: John Casey
headline: John Casey, Novelist of Salty, Rough-Hewn Characters, Dies at 86
abstract: He won a National Book Award for “Spartina,” beating out novels by Amy Tan and E.L. Doctorow. A longtime professor, he lived for a time without electricity on an island.

name: M. Paul Friedberg
headline: M. Paul Friedberg, Landscape Architect Who Celebrated the City, Dies at 93
abstract: He made his mark as a designer of experimental playgrounds in New York City and then used the same ideas to reinvent urban parks across the country.

name: Laura Sessions Stepp
headline: Laura Sessions Stepp, Who Reported on Teenage Sex, Dies at 73
abstract: A Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist, she went on to write about “hookup culture” and young women’s sexual experiences for The Washington Post and in a best-selling book.

name: Hal Hirshorn
profession: Artist of Otherworldly Photos and Paintings
headline: Hal Hirshorn, Artist of Otherworldly Photos and Paintings, Dies at 60
abstract: A ubiquitous presence in New York’s art world, he also existed outside it, using 19th-century techniques to create ethereal, haunting images.

name: Jack Vettriano
headline: Jack Vettriano, ‘Singing Butler’ Painter, Dies at 73
abstract: Critics largely rejected his work, but when it was last sold in 2004, “The Singing Butler” was the most valuable piece of art to ever emerge from Scotland.

name: Carl Dean
profession: Dolly Partons Husband of Nearly 60 Years
headline: Carl Dean, Dolly Parton’s Husband of Nearly 60 Years, Dies at 82
abstract: Mr. Dean, who inspired songs including “Jolene” and “From Here to the Moon and Back,” was known to shy away from the spotlight as his wife rose to fame.

name: Peter Sichel
profession: Wine Merchant With a Cloak-and-Dagger Past
headline: Peter Sichel, Wine Merchant With a Cloak-and-Dagger Past, Dies at 102
abstract: He played a crucial role in the early days of the C.I.A., as a station chief in Cold War Berlin and Hong Kong, before shifting gears to popularize Blue Nun wine.

name: Selwyn Raab
