headline: Selwyn Raab, Tenacious Reporter Who Covered the Mob, Dies at 90
abstract: At The Times and elsewhere, he wrote about wrongful convictions, fake methadone clinics and the five powerful Mafia families in New York.

name: Chris Jasper
headline: Chris Jasper, Who Helped Revitalize the Isley Brothers, Dies at 73
abstract: A classically trained pianist turned songwriter, he was a cornerstone of the soul group’s sound during its fertile second act in the 1970s.

name: Lincoln Díaz-Balart
headline: Lincoln Díaz-Balart, a ‘Free Cuba’ Republican in Congress, Dies at 70
abstract: The Florida scion of an anti-communist political family, he served in the House for 18 years at a time when Cuban Americans exerted peak influence on U.S. policies.

name: Sylvester Turner
profession: Sworn In as U.S. Representative in January
headline: Sylvester Turner, Sworn In as U.S. Representative in January, Dies at 70
abstract: A former mayor of Houston, he was in attendance at the president’s speech on Tuesday night and was later taken to a hospital.

name: Pierre Joris
profession: Translator of the Impossible Paul Celan
headline: Pierre Joris, Translator of the ‘Impossible’ Paul Celan, Dies at 78
abstract: A notable poet in his own right, he was best known for rendering into English the words of a poet who reacted to the Holocaust by inventing a new version of German.

name: Juan Hamilton
profession: Georgia OKeeffes Companion and Contested Heir
headline: Juan Hamilton, Georgia O’Keeffe’s Companion and Contested Heir, Dies at 79
abstract: As a young potter, he turned up on the doorstep of an octogenarian master of modern painting. They grew so close it became a scandal.

name: Roy Ayers
headline: Roy Ayers, Vibraphonist Who Injected Soul Into Jazz, Dies at 84
abstract: He helped introduce a funkier strain of the music in the 1970s. He also had an impact on hip-hop: His “Everybody Loves the Sunshine” has been sampled nearly 200 times.

name: L. Clifford Davis
headline: L. Clifford Davis, Who Fought to Desegregate Texas Schools, Dies at 100
abstract: As a civil rights lawyer who faced resistance and threats, he challenged school districts that tried to defy the Supreme Court’s 1954 ban on school segregation.

name: Ricardo Scofidio
headline: Ricardo Scofidio, Boldly Imaginative Architect, Is Dead at 89
abstract: With Diller Scofidio + Renfro, he brought a conceptual-art sensibility to cultural landmarks like Lincoln Center and to innovative public spaces like Manhattan’s High Line.

name: Betty Bonney
profession: Her Paean to Joe DiMaggio Was a Big-Band Hit
headline: Betty Bonney, 100, Dies; Her Paean to Joe DiMaggio Was a Big-Band Hit
abstract: Singing with the Les Brown band, she celebrated the Yankee star’s 56-game hitting streak in 1941. She also performed on Sid Caesar’s “Your Show of Shows.”

name: George Lowe
profession: Five Clips Capture His Kvetchy Space Ghost Alter Ego
headline: George Lowe, 67, Dies; Five Clips Capture His Kvetchy Space Ghost Alter Ego
abstract: He was the secret weapon behind the cult-classic Cartoon Network series that reimagined the 1960s intergalactic superhero as temperamental talk show host.

name: Helen Schreider
headline: Helen Schreider, Intrepid World Traveler, Is Dead at 98
abstract: She and her husband were the first people to travel the length of the Americas in an amphibious vehicle. But he was recognized for their accomplishments long before she was.

name: Uri Shulevitz
profession: Acclaimed Childrens Book Author and Illustrator
headline: Uri Shulevitz, 89, Acclaimed Children’s Book Author and Illustrator, Dies
abstract: A Caldecott Medal winner, he turned childhood memories of fleeing the Nazis in Poland into magical stories.

name: Melody Beattie
profession: Author of a Self-Help Best Seller
headline: Melody Beattie, Author of a Self-Help Best Seller, Dies at 76
abstract: Her “Codependent No More: How to Stop Controlling Others and Start Caring for Yourself,” a guide to shedding toxic relationships, has sold more than seven million copies.

name: D'Wayne Wiggins
profession: One Third of R&B Group Tony! Toni! Toné!
headline: D’Wayne Wiggins, 64, Dies; One Third of R&B Group Tony! Toni! Toné!
abstract: As a paragon of the New Jack Swing sound, the band recorded three platinum albums and a slew of hits, including “Feels Good.”

name: Gwen McCrae
profession: Singer Helped Open the Dance Floor to Disco
headline: Gwen McCrae, 81, Dies; Singer Helped Open the Dance Floor to Disco
abstract: Originally a gospel singer, she went on to meld soulful melodies with dance-floor-friendly grooves on songs like the 1975 Top 10 hit “Rockin’ Chair.”

name: Frank Saucier
profession: Slugger Sidelined by a Publicity Stunt
headline: Frank Saucier, Slugger Sidelined by a Publicity Stunt, Dies at 98
abstract: He had just recently joined the St. Louis Browns when he was replaced in the lineup by Eddie Gaedel, a 3-foot-7 circus performer, in a game in 1951.

name: Robert G. Clark
profession: Broke Race Barrier in Mississippi Statehouse
headline: Robert G. Clark, 96, Dies; Broke Race Barrier in Mississippi Statehouse
abstract: In 1968, he became the first Black person to serve in the Legislature since Reconstruction. Shunned by colleagues at first, he became a political force in the state.

name: Joan Dye Gussow
headline: Joan Dye Gussow, Pioneer of Eating Locally, Is Dead at 96
abstract: An indefatigable gardener, she was one of the first nutritionists to emphasize the connections between farming practices and consumers’ health.

name: Joey Molland
headline: Joey Molland, of the Power-Pop Band Badfinger, Is Dead at 77
abstract: He was the last remaining core member of a group that was both propelled and pigeonholed in the 1970s by its close association with the Beatles.

name: Flo Fox
profession: Street Photographer Overcame Blindness and Paralysis
headline: Flo Fox, 79, Dies; Street Photographer Overcame Blindness and Paralysis
abstract: She was legally blind and used a motorized wheelchair, but she managed to capture what she called the “ironic reality” of New York City on film.

name: David Sellers
headline: David Sellers, Architect Who Built What He Designed, Dies at 86
abstract: He believed that architects could design better buildings if they did the construction themselves. His do-it-yourself approach caught on.

name: Athol Fugard
headline: Athol Fugard, 92, Playwright Who Exposed Torments of Apartheid, Dies
abstract: In works like “Blood Knot,” “Master Harold” and “The Island,” he laid bare the realities of racial separatism in his homeland, South Africa.

name: Fred Stolle
headline: Fred Stolle, 86, Golden-Age Australian Tennis Star, Dies
abstract: In addition to winning 19 Grand Slam titles, including two singles championships, he was a coach, a club pro and a television commentator.

name: Art Schallock
headline: Art Schallock, Oldest Surviving Major Leaguer, Dies at 100
abstract: A pitcher, he played for the Yankees and the Orioles. When Mickey Mantle was sent to the minors in 1951, Schallock was called up.

name: Geoff Nicholson
headline: Geoff Nicholson, Author of Darkly Comic Novels, Dies at 71
abstract: In more than a dozen books, he created characters who were obsessed with maps, urban walking, sexual fetishes and Volkswagen Beetles.

name: Jessie Mahaffey
headline: Jessie Mahaffey, Survivor of Pearl Harbor Attack, Dies at 102
abstract: He was cleaning the deck of the U.S.S. Oklahoma when it capsized under Japanese torpedo fire. Less than a year later, he survived the sinking of another Navy ship in the Pacific.

name: Simon Fisher-Becker
profession: Actor in Harry Potter and Doctor
headline: Simon Fisher-Becker, Actor in ‘Harry Potter’ and ‘Doctor Who,’ Dies at 63
abstract: A versatile character actor whose career spanned film, theater and television, Mr. Fisher-Becker was known for small, memorable roles.

name: Wheesung
headline: Wheesung, a South Korean R&B Singer, Is Found Dead at 43
abstract: The artist was known for popularizing the musical genre in the country, but convictions for drug abuse damaged his image.

name: Larry Appelbaum
profession: Found Jazz Treasure in the Archives
headline: Larry Appelbaum, Who Found Jazz Treasure in the Archives, Dies at 67
abstract: He helped turn the Library of Congress into a leading center for research on the history of jazz, and made some surprising discoveries of his own.

name: Stanley R. Jaffe
headline: Stanley R. Jaffe, 84, Oscar-Winning Producer and Hollywood Power, Dies
abstract: His “Kramer vs. Kramer” won for best picture in 1980, one of many high points in a career that saw him in top jobs, twice, at Paramount.

name: Chris Moore
headline: Chris Moore, Illustrator for Classic Sci-Fi Books, Dies at 77
abstract: He conjured fantastical worlds with covers for novels by Philip K. Dick and Arthur C. Clarke. He also left his mark on albums by Fleetwood Mac and Rod Stewart.

name: Selma Miriam
profession: Founder of the Feminist Restaurant Bloodroot
headline: Selma Miriam, Founder of the Feminist Restaurant Bloodroot, Dies at 89
abstract: She and Noel Furie had just come out as lesbians when they opened an unusual gathering place for women in Connecticut. Nearly half a century later, it is still thriving.

name: James Reason
profession: Used Swiss Cheese to Explain Human Error
headline: James Reason, Who Used Swiss Cheese to Explain Human Error, Dies at 86
abstract: Mistakes happen, he theorized, because multiple vulnerabilities in a system align — like the holes in cheese — to create a recipe for disaster.

name: Jennifer Johnston
headline: Jennifer Johnston, 95, Novelist Who Probed Ireland’s Fault Lines, Dies
abstract: She explored tensions among the social classes and within families in fiction that prompted Roddy Doyle to call her “Ireland’s greatest writer.”

name: David Raven
profession: British Drag Performer Known as Maisie Trollette
headline: David Raven, British Drag Performer Known as Maisie Trollette, Dies at 91
abstract: A mainstay of England’s drag circuit, he performed for over five decades and encouraged other drag queens to flourish.

name: Sofia Gubaidulina
headline: Sofia Gubaidulina, Composer Who Provoked Soviet Censors, Dies at 93
abstract: Blacklisted at home but finding acclaim abroad, she sought to bridge East and West, the sacred and the secular, in vivid, colorful compositions.

name: John Feinstein
profession: Wrote A Season on the Brink
headline: John Feinstein, Who Wrote ‘A Season on the Brink,’ Dies at 69
abstract: A longtime columnist for The Washington Post, he also wrote dozens of books about basketball, baseball, tennis, football and the Olympics.

name: Ron Nessen
headline: Ron Nessen, Ford’s White House Press Secretary, Dies at 90
abstract: He pledged a new era of openness in the wake of the Watergate scandal, but his relationship with the press corps proved rocky.

name: Larry Buendorf
headline: Larry Buendorf, U.S. Agent Who Saved President Ford, Dies at 87
abstract: By grabbing a loaded handgun from Squeaky Fromme in 1975, Mr. Buendorf, as part of a Secret Service detail, thwarted a would-be assassin in California’s capital.

name: Felice Picano
headline: Felice Picano, Champion of Gay Literature, Is Dead at 81
abstract: At a time when, in his words, “nobody was writing about gay life,” he produced groundbreaking novels and memoirs and published books by Harvey Fierstein and others.

name: Anne Kaufman Schneider
profession: Ardent Keeper of Her Fathers Plays
headline: Anne Kaufman Schneider, 99, Ardent Keeper of Her Father’s Plays, Dies
abstract: She shepherded the works of George S. Kaufman from the 20th century into the next, encouraging regional theater productions and helping to steer two of them to Broadway.

name: Alan K. Simpson
profession: Folksy Republican Force in the Senate
headline: Alan K. Simpson, a Folksy Republican Force in the Senate, Dies at 93
abstract: A plain-spoken lawmaker from Wyoming, he balanced his conservative views with moderate stands on abortion rights, gay marriage and immigration reform.

name: Herman Graf
headline: Herman Graf, Who Helped Sell ‘Tropic of Cancer,’ Dies at 91
abstract: A major figure in independent publishing, he promoted Henry Miller’s once-banned book and helped make “A Confederacy of Dunces” a best seller after the author’s death.

name: Sheldon Greenfield
headline: Dr. Sheldon Greenfield, Who Exposed Gaps in Health Care, Dies at 86
abstract: The author of numerous studies, he urged patients to question their physicians and expressed concern about cancer treatment for older adults.

name: Beulah Henry
headline: Overlooked No More: Beulah Henry, Inventor With an Endless Imagination
abstract: She was so prolific — reimagining things as varied as toys, typewriters, umbrellas and ice-cream makers — that she earned the nickname Lady Edison.

name: Carl Lundstrom
profession: Backed the File-Sharing Site Pirate Bay
headline: Carl Lundstrom, Who Backed the File-Sharing Site Pirate Bay, Dies in Plane Crash
abstract: Mr. Lundstrom was a supporter of far-right causes and, at one point, an unsuccessful candidate for office. He was convicted of aiding copyright infringement in 2009.

name: Kevin Drum
headline: Kevin Drum, Influential Early Political Blogger, Dies at 66
abstract: Writing on his own and for Washington Monthly and Mother Jones, he earned a reputation as a serious policy thinker. He also invented Friday cat blogging.

name: Raul M. Grijalva
headline: Raul M. Grijalva, a Democratic Progressive in the House, Dies at 77
abstract: The son of an immigrant, he represented a majority Hispanic district in Arizona for 12 terms but had lately been absent from Capitol Hill while being treated for cancer.

name: Junior Bridgeman
headline: Junior Bridgeman, N.B.A. Player Turned Mogul, Dies at 71
abstract: He became an entrepreneur during a solid career with the Milwaukee Bucks. He later bought hundreds of fast-food outlets, a Coca-Cola bottling business and Ebony and Jet magazines.

name: Roy L. Prosterman
profession: Worked to Secure Land for the Rural Poor
headline: Roy L. Prosterman, 89, Dies; Worked to Secure Land for the Rural Poor
abstract: Seeing land rights as the key to lifting up the impoverished, he pushed authoritarian governments as well as emerging democratic ones to distribute farmland.

name: Nita M. Lowey
headline: Nita M. Lowey, Tenacious New York Representative, Dies at 87
abstract: A Democrat, she represented Westchester County for three decades and became the first woman to lead the powerful House Appropriations Committee.

name: Gene Winfield
profession: Cars Starred in Film and on TV
headline: Gene Winfield, Whose Cars Starred in Film and on TV, Dies at 97
abstract: He was know for modifying cars with innovative metal work and paint jobs, and for building vehicles like the Galileo shuttle for the original “Star Trek” series.

name: Slick Watts
profession: N.B.A. Fan Favorite and Headband Pioneer
headline: Slick Watts, N.B.A. Fan Favorite and Headband Pioneer, Dies at 73
abstract: An undrafted, 6-foot-1 point guard with patchy hair, he made an enduring fashion statement and became seen as the ultimate Seattle SuperSonic.

name: Lee Shau-Kee
headline: Lee Shau-Kee, Hong Kong Real Estate Tycoon, Dies at 97
abstract: Sometimes called the Warren Buffett of Hong Kong, he made his billions by initially building apartments for middle-class descendants of mainland refugees.

name: Émilie Dequenne
headline: Émilie Dequenne, Belgian Actress Who Starred in ‘Rosetta,’ Dies at 43
abstract: She won the Cannes Film Festival’s best actress award for her debut performance in 1999. She was later diagnosed with a rare adrenal gland cancer.

name: Jesse Colin Young
headline: Jesse Colin Young, Singer Who Urged Us to ‘Get Together,’ Dies at 83
abstract: As the leader of the Youngbloods, he sang an enduring anthem of the peace-and-love era, with the chorus, “Come on people now, smile on your brother.”

name: Mark Grossich
headline: Mark Grossich, Who Opened Landmark Luxe Bars, Dies at 74
abstract: His lounges in Manhattan settings like Grand Central Terminal and the Empire State Building conjured the elegance of a bygone era.

name: Thomas Moser
headline: Thomas Moser, Woodworker Whose Chairs Were Works of Art, Dies at 90
abstract: Self-taught, he practiced “the lost art of making furniture well,” producing pieces for collectors, presidents and even the pope.

name: Ming Fay
profession: Made Magical Sculptures of the Natural World
headline: Ming Fay, 82, Who Made Magical Sculptures of the Natural World, Dies
abstract: His artwork paid tribute to its surroundings, in New York City and elsewhere, rendering nature at an oversized scale that made it unmissable.

name: John A. Hemingway
profession: Last Survivor of the Battle of Britain
headline: John A. Hemingway, Last Survivor of the Battle of Britain, Dies at 105
abstract: A fighter pilot in a vastly outnumbered Royal Air Force — one of the “few” hailed by Churchill — he took to the skies to help stave off a Nazi land invasion of Britain.

name: D.G. Hessayon
headline: D.G. Hessayon, Author of Blockbuster Garden Guides, Dies at 96
abstract: His “Be Your Own House Plant Expert” and other best-selling manuals were a fixture of British life for half a century. Among his many fans was Margaret Thatcher.

name: Anthony Dolan
headline: Anthony Dolan, Speechwriter Who Gave Reagan ‘Evil Empire,’ Dies at 76
abstract: As a conservative presidential speechwriter, he also relegated communism to “the ash heap of history.” Earlier, he won a Pulitzer Prize as a young reporter.

name: Robert E. Ginna Jr.
headline: Robert E. Ginna Jr., Whose Article Bolstered U.F.O. Claims, Dies at 99
abstract: A founding editor of People, he also served as editor in chief of Little, Brown and produced films. But his public image was defined by a 1952 story for Life.

name: Hugues Oyarzabal
headline: Hugues Oyarzabal, Surfing Star Who Rode With a Camera, Dies at 39
abstract: With a video recorder affixed to his board or clamped to his teeth, he took viewers along for the ride, often inside the curling “barrel” of a wave.

name: J.B. Moore
headline: J.B. Moore, Producer of Seminal Hip-Hop Records, Dies at 81
abstract: He was a magazine ad salesman when he and a colleague, Robert Ford, teamed with Kurtis Blow and helped break rap music into the mainstream.

name: Jeffrey Bruce Klein
profession: Founder and Editor of Mother Jones
headline: Jeffrey Bruce Klein, a Founder and Editor of Mother Jones, Dies at 77
abstract: He was one of four journalists who started the muckraking progressive magazine in 1976. He returned as its editor in chief in the 1990s.

name: Lenny Schultz
headline: Lenny Schultz, Comedian Who Made a Lot of Noise, Dies at 91
abstract: A highly physical performer, he said he couldn’t tell jokes. But he became well known for a wild act that fellow comedians didn’t want to follow.

name: Kilmer McCully
profession: Pathologist Vindicated on Heart Disease Theory
headline: Kilmer McCully, 91, Dies; Pathologist Vindicated on Heart Disease Theory
abstract: His studies showed that a B vitamin deficiency could cause hardened arteries. It took the medical profession more than a decade to catch up.

name: Robert Denham
headline: Robert Denham, Lawyer Who Steered Companies Through Crises, Dies at 79
abstract: Among his rescues was teaming up with Warren Buffett to keep the investment bank Salomon Brothers afloat amid a bid-rigging scandal in the 1990s.

name: Bruce M. Selya
profession: Federal Judge Known for Polysyllabic Prose
headline: Bruce M. Selya, Federal Judge Known for Polysyllabic Prose, Dies at 90
abstract: Judge Selya enlivened his writing with original vocabulary and colorful figures of speech. “Selyaisms” included asseverate, crapulous and sockdolager.

name: George Foreman
headline: George Foreman, Boxing Champion and Grilling Magnate, Dies at 76
abstract: He claimed a world title in his 20s and, improbably, again in his 40s. He then made millions selling the George Foreman Grill.

name: Kitty Dukakis
headline: Kitty Dukakis, Activist Wife of 1988 Presidential Nominee, Dies at 88
abstract: Married to Gov. Michael Dukakis of Massachusetts, she became a proponent of electroshock therapy after unsuccessful treatments for alcoholism and depression.

name: Thomas Hoobler
profession: Half of a Prolific Writing Couple
headline: Thomas Hoobler, Half of a Prolific Writing Couple, Dies at 82
abstract: He and his wife, Dorothy Hoobler, wrote 103 books, most recently one about presidential love letters, “Are You Prepared for the Storm of Love Making?”

name: Max Frankel
headline: Max Frankel, Top Times Editor Who Led a Newspaper in Transition, Dies at 94
abstract: As executive editor from 1986 to 1994, he oversaw a period of financial, technological and journalistic change while lifting newsroom morale and diversifying the staff.

name: Marty Callner
profession: Director of Comedy Specials and Music Videos
headline: Marty Callner, Director of Comedy Specials and Music Videos, Dies at 78
abstract: At HBO in the late 1970s, he established the template for presenting stand-up on the small screen. He then became a mainstay of MTV in its early days.

name: Brian James
headline: Brian James, Pioneer of Punk Rock, Is Dead at 70
abstract: As the guitarist and main songwriter for the Damned, he helped spark an explosion on the British music scene in the 1970s.

name: Mia Love
profession: First Black Republican Woman Elected to Congress
headline: Mia Love, First Black Republican Woman Elected to Congress, Dies at 49
abstract: Ms. Love, from Utah, held a seat in the House for two terms until she aroused the enmity of President Trump. She was diagnosed with brain cancer in 2022.

name: Fred Eversley
headline: Fred Eversley, Sculptor of Otherworldly Discs, Is Dead at 83
abstract: With his engineering background, he thought about his work differently from how other artists did. His abiding interest was in energy, in the scientific sense.

name: Dag Solstad
profession: His Novels of Alienation Delighted Norwegians
headline: Dag Solstad, 83, Dies; His Novels of Alienation Delighted Norwegians
abstract: A winner of top awards in his country, he drew the attention of European and American critics. The prime minister said he “made us see Norway and the world in new ways.”

name: Horace Hale Harvey III
headline: Horace Hale Harvey III, a Pioneer in Providing Abortions, Dies at 93
abstract: A religious organization recruited him to help open New York City’s first independent abortion clinic, though it was unaware that Louisiana had taken away his license.

name: Michael Boudin
profession: Independent Judge From a Family on the Left
headline: Michael Boudin, Independent Judge From a Family on the Left, Dies at 85
abstract: His rulings on the U.S. bench might have rankled his father, a civil liberties lawyer; his uncle, a muckraking journalist; and his sister, an imprisoned radical.

name: Lou Nasti
profession: Brought Christmas Displays to Extravagant Life
headline: Lou Nasti, Who Brought Christmas Displays to Extravagant Life, Dies at 79
abstract: A robotics specialist, he animated puppets and dolls for displays worldwide. His “Toyland,” with a two-story-high Santa, drew sightseers to a Brooklyn home for years.

name: J. Bennett Johnston
profession: Senator Helped Shape U.S. Energy Policy
headline: J. Bennett Johnston, 92, Dies; Senator Helped Shape U.S. Energy Policy
abstract: A Democrat from Louisiana, he pushed for nuclear power and ending the nation’s reliance on foreign oil in his four terms on Capitol Hill.

name: Eddie Adcock
headline: Eddie Adcock, Virtuoso Who Pushed Bluegrass Forward, Dies at 86
abstract: A master improviser on banjo, he understood the genre’s roots but was also in the forefront of the later “newgrass” movement.

name: Dennis McDougal
headline: Dennis McDougal, True-Crime Writer and Hollywood Muckraker, Dies at 77
abstract: The author of more than a dozen books and an award-winning documentary, he died in a car crash in Southern California.

name: Oleg Gordievsky
headline: Oleg Gordievsky, K.G.B. Officer Turned Double Agent, Dies at 86
abstract: While climbing the ranks of the Soviet spy agency, he spent more than a decade working for British intelligence as one of its most highly placed moles.

name: Herb Greene
profession: His Photographs Captured the San Francisco Sound
headline: Herb Greene, 82, Dies; His Photographs Captured the San Francisco Sound
abstract: One of the first to shoot the Grateful Dead, he also memorably chronicled many of the other bands that were on the scene in the late 1960s.

name: David M. Childs
headline: David M. Childs, Skyline-Shaping Architect, Dies at 83
abstract: He was the chief architect of 1 World Trade Center, which soared in the wake of 9/11. As chairman of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill, he left a mark on New York.

name: Leonard Polonsky
headline: Leonard Polonsky, Philanthropist Who Supported the Arts, Dies at 97
abstract: After making a fortune in financial services, he funded the arts and made historical artifacts and documents widely available to the public.

name: Pilar Viladas
headline: Pilar Viladas Dies at 70; Journalist Chronicled Trends in Design
abstract: Schooled in art history, she brought authority and a human perspective to her writing and editing for Architectural Digest, HG, The Times and other publications.

name: Armand LaMontagne
headline: Armand LaMontagne, Meticulous Sculptor of Sports Greats, Dies at 87
abstract: Working in wood, he captured the zeal of New England sports with his exacting, lifelike renderings of Hall of Famers like Ted Williams and Larry Bird.

name: Clive Revill
profession: Original Voice of Emperor Palpatine in Star Wars
headline: Clive Revill, Original Voice of Emperor Palpatine in ‘Star Wars,’ Dies at 94
abstract: His voice can be heard for only a minute in “The Empire Strikes Back,” but it provided the first draft of a character that would be a mainstay of the franchise for decades.

name: Victor Emanuel
profession: Revered Birder and Pioneer of Ecotourism
headline: Victor Emanuel, Revered Birder and Pioneer of Ecotourism, Dies at 84
abstract: He had a reverential regard for birds from an early age, and he turned it into a thriving business. “I call him the Zen master of birds,” Peter Matthiessen said.

name: Jean Rice
profession: Advocate for the Homeless With Firsthand Experience
headline: Jean Rice, Advocate for the Homeless With Firsthand Experience, Dies at 85
abstract: Homeless on and off for years himself, he was a longtime pivotal member of Picture the Homeless, a group devoted to changing negative perceptions of the unhoused.

name: Gai Gherardi
headline: Gai Gherardi, Who Made Eyeglass Frames Fashion Statements, Dies at 78
abstract: Her L.A. Eyeworks boutique, which she opened with a friend and fellow optician, was a pioneer in turning ordinary frames into bold, artistic accessories.

name: Richard Chamberlain
headline: Richard Chamberlain, TV Heartthrob Turned Serious Actor, Dies at 90
abstract: An overnight star as Dr. Kildare in the 1960s, he achieved new acclaim two decades later as the omnipresent leading man of mini-series.

name: Gananath Obeyesekere
headline: Gananath Obeyesekere, 95, Dies; Anthropologist Bridged East and West
abstract: His wide-ranging work drew on field research in his native Sri Lanka as well as his extensive study of English literature and Christian mysticism.

name: Linda Williams
profession: Took a Scholarly Approach to Pornography
headline: Linda Williams, 78, Dies; Took a Scholarly Approach to Pornography
abstract: One of the first to write seriously about a fraught subject, she also played a major role in developing the field of film studies and feminist film theory.

name: Richard Carlson
headline: Richard Carlson, Journalist Who Led Voice of America, Dies at 84
abstract: The father of the conservative commentator Tucker Carlson, he won a Peabody Award for television reporting that uncovered a car company’s fraud.

name: Reinaldo Herrera
profession: Arbiter of Style for Vanity Fair
headline: Reinaldo Herrera, Arbiter of Style for Vanity Fair, Dies at 91
abstract: Both old school and Old World and married to a celebrated fashion designer, he helped define Manhattan’s high life for many years.

name: Hank Steinbrecher
profession: Helped Elevate Soccer in the U.S
headline: Hank Steinbrecher, Who Helped Elevate Soccer in the U.S., Dies at 77
abstract: He was also a key figure in raising American soccer’s profile on the world stage. Earlier, as a marketer, he saw opportunities in the football ritual of dousing coaches with Gatorade.

name: Betty Webb
headline: Betty Webb, Who Helped Bletchley Park Code Breakers, Dies at 101
abstract: Sworn to secrecy about the goings-on at Britain’s storied World War II decryption operation, she only later recounted the efforts to crack German signals.

name: Kathan Brown
headline: Kathan Brown, Acclaimed Fine Art Printmaker, Dies at 89
abstract: She helped revive the centuries-old tradition of intaglio printing in the U.S., producing fine-art etchings with artists like Chuck Close and Sol LeWitt.

name: Val Kilmer
headline: Val Kilmer, Film Star Who Played Batman and Jim Morrison, Dies at 65
abstract: A wide-ranging leading man who earned critical praise, he was known to be charismatic but unpredictable. At one point he dropped out of Hollywood for a decade.

name: Ralph Holloway
headline: Ralph Holloway, Anthropologist Who Studied Brain’s Evolution, Dies at 90
abstract: It wasn’t the size of human brains that distinguished people from apes, he theorized, but the way they were organized. He found a creative way to prove it.

name: Joe DePugh
profession: Speedball Pitcher in Springsteens Glory Days
headline: Joe DePugh, Speedball Pitcher in Springsteen’s ‘Glory Days,’ Dies at 75
abstract: A gifted athlete, he gave a clumsy teenage Bruce Springsteen his first nickname, Saddie. Years later, the Boss returned the favor, memorializing him in a song.

name: Richard Bernstein
headline: Richard Bernstein Dies at 80; Times Correspondent, Critic and Author
abstract: He wrote from Europe and Asia, served as a book critic and produced a raft of books, on subjects ranging from the French condition to multiculturalism.

name: Katharine McCormick
profession: Force Behind the Birth Control Pill
headline: Overlooked No More: Katharine McCormick, Force Behind the Birth Control Pill
abstract: She used her wealth strategically to expand opportunities for women, underwriting the development of the pill and supporting the suffrage movement.

name: Paul McDonough
headline: Paul McDonough, Whose Photographs Evoked Street Life, Dies at 84
abstract: His candid black-and-white images, prosaic yet provocative, captured the faces of a wide range of New Yorkers. He also took occasional side trips to the West.

name: Leonardo Patterson
headline: Leonardo Patterson, 82, High-Flying Antiquities Dealer Brought Low, Dies
abstract: Born into rural poverty, he climbed to the top of the art market. But he fell after being convicted of selling fake and stolen items.

name: Sam Keen
headline: Sam Keen, Philosopher of the Men’s Movement, Is Dead at 93
abstract: “Only men understand the secret fears that go with the territory of masculinity,” he wrote. His message resonated: His book “Fire in the Belly” was a best seller.

name: Robert S. Rifkind
profession: Defended a Libel Suit by Ariel Sharon
headline: Robert S. Rifkind, Who Defended a Libel Suit by Ariel Sharon, Dies at 88
abstract: In one of the biggest cases he worked on, he represented Time magazine when Mr. Sharon, Israel’s defense minister, sued it over its reporting on a 1983 massacre in Lebanon.

name: Theodore McCarrick
headline: Theodore McCarrick, Cardinal Defrocked Over Sex Abuse, Dies at 94
abstract: He rose in the Roman Catholic Church before allegations of abusing minors and seminarians and an investigation led Pope Francis to strip him of his priesthood.

name: Jean Van Leeuwen
profession: Wrote Oliver Pig Series of Childrens Books
headline: Jean Van Leeuwen, 87, Dies; Wrote ‘Oliver Pig’ Series of Children’s Books
abstract: She wrote for many ages, from picture books to young adult fiction. Her children led her to create a series of books about two pigs named Oliver and Amanda.

name: Dave Pelz
profession: Scientist Turned Golf Guru of the Short Game
headline: Dave Pelz, Scientist Turned Golf Guru of the Short Game, Dies at 85
abstract: After working at NASA, he became an expert on putting and shots close to the green through his coaching, books, television appearances and training aids.

name: Jesse Kornbluth
headline: Jesse Kornbluth, Magazine Writer Who Covered Everything, Dies at 79
abstract: He reported on the highs and lows of culture in the pages of Vanity Fair and elsewhere. He also wrote seven books of nonfiction and two novels.

name: John Peck
profession: Underground Cartoonist Known as The Mad Peck
headline: John Peck, Underground Cartoonist Known as The Mad Peck, Dies at 82
abstract: Among many other accomplishments, he illustrated a scholarly work on the history of comic books and wrote record reviews in four-panel comic-strip form.

name: Marcia Marcus
profession: Painter Rediscovered in Her Last Decade
headline: Marcia Marcus, Painter Rediscovered in Her Last Decade, Dies at 97
abstract: A popular downtown artist in the 1960s, she worked in obscurity after art world trends left her behind. Now her startlingly fresh work is on view again.

name: Edward Countryman
headline: Edward Countryman, Student of the American Revolution, Dies at 80
abstract: He wrote influential books exploring the dramatic changes wrought by independence, bringing in overlooked perspectives — what he called “a collision of histories.”

name: Denis Arndt
profession: Was a First-Time Tony Nominee at 77
headline: Denis Arndt, Who Was a First-Time Tony Nominee at 77, Dies at 86
abstract: After more than 40 years as a stage and television actor, he broke through in “Heisenberg” as a butcher who has a romance with a much younger woman.

name: Amadou Bagayoko
headline: Amadou Bagayoko, Half of Malian Duo Who Went Global, Dies at 70
abstract: As Amadou & Mariam, he and his wife were improbable pop stars on two counts. Their style was venturesome and eclectic, and they were blind virtuosos.

name: Jay North
profession: Child Star of Dennis the Menace
headline: Jay North, Child Star of ‘Dennis the Menace,’ Dies at 73
abstract: He was best known for playing the towheaded Dennis Mitchell on a sitcom that ran on CBS from 1959 to 1963.

name: Jeremiah Ostriker
headline: Jeremiah Ostriker, Who Plumbed Dark Forces That Shape Universe, Dies at 87
abstract: There’s more to the universe than meets the eye, he found. His studies led astronomy to the dark side, changing our view of what’s out there.

name: Clem Burke
headline: Clem Burke, Versatile, Hard-Driving Drummer for Blondie, Dies at 70
abstract: He provided both the explosive percussion on “Call Me” and the laid-back rhythm on the reggae-influenced “The Tide Is High.”

name: K. Holmes
headline: King K. Holmes, 87, Dies; Researcher Destigmatized Study of S.T.I.s
abstract: He took a down-to-earth approach to sexually transmitted infections, a subject no one wanted to discuss, arriving at novel methods of treatment and prevention.

name: Robert W. McChesney
headline: Robert W. McChesney, Who Warned of Corporate Media Control, Dies at 72
abstract: In over a dozen books, he explored the failures of journalism and the internet, blaming capitalism and calling for the nationalization of Facebook and Google.

name: William Finn
headline: William Finn, Tony Winner for ‘Falsettos,’ Is Dead at 73
abstract: An acclaimed musical theater writer, he won for both his score and his book and later had a huge hit with “The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee.”

name: Bob McManus
profession: Blunt Editorial Voice of The New York Post
headline: Bob McManus, Blunt Editorial Voice of The New York Post, Dies at 81
abstract: As the editor of the tabloid’s editorial page and as a columnist, he skewered those he considered phonies and symbols of failed progressivism.

name: Xavier Le Pichon
headline: Xavier Le Pichon, Who Modeled Movement of Earth’s Crust, Dies at 87
abstract: With a computer rendering, he helped scientists understand that the earth, with its shifting tectonic plates, is “an extraordinary living being” that is “continuously changing.”

name: John Nelson
headline: John Nelson, Conductor Who Got France to Cherish Berlioz, Dies at 83
abstract: He revived interest in a “problem child” in the pantheon of high romantic composers, bringing Berlioz overdue recognition as one of France’s greatest composers.

name: Tracy Schwarz
profession: Mainstay of the New Lost City Ramblers
headline: Tracy Schwarz, Mainstay of the New Lost City Ramblers, Dies at 86
abstract: He was the last surviving member of a retro-minded string trio whose celebration of prewar songs of the rural South put them at the heart of the folk revival.

name: Kim Shin-jo
headline: Kim Shin-jo, 82, Failed North Korean Assassin, Dies as Pastor in the South
abstract: He famously said the mission of a hit squad sent by Pyongyang in 1968 was to “slit the throat” of the South Korean dictator Park Chung-hee.

name: Fridrik Olafsson
headline: Fridrik Olafsson, Grandmaster Who Led Iceland’s Rise in Chess, Dies at 90
abstract: At a time before his country became a chess powerhouse, he defeated four world champions, including Bobby Fischer and another in an unlikely turn of events.

name: Gerald Luss
headline: Gerald Luss, Master of Midcentury-Modern Design, Dies at 98
abstract: His work on the interiors of the Time-Life Building helped set the tone for postwar office style and provided a model for the set of “Mad Men.”

name: Joan Brown Campbell
profession: Led Largest Ecumenical Body in U.S
headline: Joan Brown Campbell Dies at 93; Led Largest Ecumenical Body in U.S.
abstract: A minister who headed the National Council of Churches, she was active in liberal causes in the 1990s and sought to counter the conservative Christian Coalition.

name: Michael Hurley
headline: Michael Hurley, a Singer Both Eccentric and Inspirational, Dies at 83
abstract: A folk troubadour with an eclectic style, he built a devoted following for his songs about love, death, drinking and a particularly sad werewolf.

name: George Bell
profession: Considered the Tallest Man in America
headline: George Bell, Considered the Tallest Man in America, Dies at 67
abstract: Being 7-foot-8 posed “a lot of challenges,” he once said. “Like how do I fit in cars, or where do I find clothes?”

name: Alice Tan Ridley
profession: Subway Singer on Americas Got Talent
headline: Alice Tan Ridley, Subway Singer on ‘America’s Got Talent,’ Dies at 72
abstract: The mother of the actress Gabourey Sidibe, she spent decades singing full time as an underground busker in New York City.

name: Suzanne Rand
profession: Half of a Once-Popular Comedy Team
headline: Suzanne Rand, Half of a Once-Popular Comedy Team, Dies at 75
abstract: Like Nichols and May before them, Monteith and Rand had their own Broadway show. Unlike Nichols and May, they faded from view after they broke up.

name: Rick Levine
headline: Rick Levine, Who Gave Commercials Cinematic Flair, Dies at 94
abstract: An award-winning director, he created ads for brands like Diet Pepsi (starring Michael J. Fox) by bringing a Hollywood sensibility to the small screen.

name: Joseph Boskin
profession: Scholar of Humor and April Fools Prankster
headline: Joseph Boskin, Scholar of Humor and April Fools’ Prankster, Dies at 95
abstract: To oblige an eager reporter, he invented a story about the holiday’s origin. He didn’t realize it would turn out to be his “Andy Warhol moment.”

name: Max Kozloff
headline: Max Kozloff, Art Critic Who Became an Artist Himself, Dies at 91
abstract: He wrote extensively about the New York art scene in the 1960s and ’70s, then shifted to become a prominent street photographer.

name: Brad Holland
headline: Brad Holland, 81, Dies; His Subversive Art Reinvented Illustration
abstract: His stark and stunning work for Playboy, The New York Times and Manhattan’s underground papers heralded a new era of conceptual illustration.

name: Jean Marsh
headline: Jean Marsh, Actress Who Co-Created ‘Upstairs, Downstairs,’ Dies at 90
abstract: She not only helped develop the hit 1970s show, but also acted in it, and had a decades-long career in film, TV and theater.

name: Irmgard Furchner
profession: Secretary at a Hub of Nazi Atrocities
headline: Irmgard Furchner, Secretary at a Hub of Nazi Atrocities, Dies at 99
abstract: Her work for the commandant of a concentration camp in German-occupied Poland led to her conviction as an accessory to more than 10,000 murders.

name: Nicky Katt
profession: Character Actor on TV and in Film
headline: Nicky Katt, Character Actor on TV and in Film, Dies at 54
abstract: He began his career as a child actor and later played tough guys and henchmen. He was best known for “Boston Public” and “Dazed and Confused.”

name: Mario Vargas Llosa
headline: Mario Vargas Llosa, Nobel-Winning Peruvian Novelist, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Vargas Llosa, who ran for Peru’s presidency in 1990 and won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2010, transformed episodes from his personal life into books that reverberated far beyond the borders of his native country.

name: Elsa Honig Fine
profession: Historian Promoted Black and Female Artists
headline: Elsa Honig Fine, 94, Dies; Historian Promoted Black and Female Artists
abstract: As the founder of Woman’s Art Journal and the author of influential textbooks, she documented the work of many accomplished artists who had been ignored.

name: Marvin Levy
headline: Marvin Levy, Oscar-Winning Publicist to Spielberg, Dies at 96
abstract: For 42 years, Mr. Levy strategized behind the scenes to promote Steven Spielberg’s movies and ensure that the director was seen as Hollywood’s de facto head of state.

name: Richard L. Armitage
profession: State Department Official in a Turbulent Era
headline: Richard L. Armitage, 79, Dies; State Department Official in a Turbulent Era
abstract: While serving as Colin Powell’s deputy during the Iraq war, he found himself at the center of a scandal when he leaked a C.I.A. operative’s name.

name: Wink Martindale
profession: Popular and Durable Game Show Host
headline: Wink Martindale, Popular and Durable Game Show Host, Dies at 91
abstract: He was involved in more than 20 game shows, most memorably as the host of “Gambit” and “Tic-Tac-Dough” in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Leo Beenhakker
headline: Leo Beenhakker, a Soccer Coach Without Borders, Dies at 82
abstract: Among many other accomplishments, he led tiny Trinidad and Tobago to the World Cup and Poland to its first appearance in the European championships.

name: Andrew A. Beveridge
profession: Found the Unexpected in Census Data
headline: Andrew A. Beveridge, Who Found the Unexpected in Census Data, Dies at 79
abstract: With his own research group and as a professor at Queens College, he plumbed raw data for often-surprising insights about the way the country was changing.

name: Tim Mohr
headline: Tim Mohr, Berlin D.J. Turned Award-Winning Translator, Dies at 55
abstract: An American who had lived abroad, he sought out books by up-and-coming German writers, while ghostwriting memoirs for rock stars like Paul Stanley.

name: Ethel Lina White
headline: Overlooked No More: Ethel Lina White, Master of Suspense Who Inspired Hitchcock
abstract: A powerhouse of the genre, she published around 100 short stories and 17 novels, one of which was adapted into the acclaimed film “The Lady Vanishes.”

name: Nino Tempo
profession: Topped the Charts With Deep Purple
headline: Nino Tempo, Who Topped the Charts With ‘Deep Purple,’ Dies at 90
abstract: He was a busy session saxophonist, but he is probably best known for the Grammy-winning pop hit that he sang in 1963 as half of a duo act with his sister, April Stevens.

name: Elaine Wynn
headline: Elaine Wynn, Billionaire Arts Patron Who Helped Modernize Las Vegas, Dies at 82
abstract: She and Steve Wynn were known as the king and queen of Las Vegas. After their divorce, Ms. Wynn became a force in her own right.

name: Francis Davis
headline: Francis Davis, Sharp-Eared Jazz Critic, Is Dead at 78
abstract: He wrote prolifically about various aspects of the arts and popular culture. But he kept his focus on jazz, celebrating its past while worrying about its future.

name: John J. LaFalce
headline: John J. LaFalce, 85, Congressman Who Pushed for Love Canal Cleanup, Dies
abstract: A 14-term Democrat from Western New York, he sponsored financial reforms to aid consumers and pressed Washington to protect Americans from environmental hazards.

name: Abdullah Ahmad Badawi
headline: Abdullah Ahmad Badawi, a Calming Prime Minister of Malaysia, Dies at 85
abstract: From 2003 to 2009, he brought a quiet style of leadership to his Southeast Asian nation after the strongman rule of Mahathir Mohamad.

name: Don Mischer
headline: Don Mischer, Master of Live Television, Is Dead at 85
abstract: He produced and directed major events like the Oscars, Emmys and Tonys, as well as Super Bowl halftime shows and Olympic opening ceremonies.

name: Mac Gayden
headline: Mac Gayden, Stellar Nashville Guitarist and Songwriter, Dies at 83
abstract: Heard on Bob Dylan’s “Blonde on Blonde” among other albums, he also sang and was a writer of the perennial “Everlasting Love.”

name: Joe Nickell
headline: Joe Nickell, Paranormal Investigator and ‘Real-Life Scully,’ Dies at 80
abstract: A professional skeptic, he took on hundreds of mysteries, offering rational explanations for the Loch Ness monster, the Shroud of Turin and countless hauntings.

name: Mike Wood
headline: Mike Wood, Whose LeapFrog Toys Taught a Generation, Dies at 72
abstract: His LeapPad tablets, which helped children read, found their way into tens of millions of homes beginning in 1999.

name: Max Romeo
profession: Leading Voice in the Heyday of Roots Reggae
headline: Max Romeo, Leading Voice in the Heyday of Roots Reggae, Dies at 80
abstract: His early hits were filled with sexual innuendo. But he later switched to a soulful political message that resonated in 1970s Jamaica and beyond.

name: Francis
headline: Francis, the First Latin American Pope, Dies at 88
abstract: After decades of conservative leadership, Francis tried to reset the course of the Roman Catholic Church, emphasizing inclusion and care for the marginalized over doctrinal purity.

name: Chuck Connelly
headline: Chuck Connelly, Combative Neo-Expressionist Artist, Dies at 70
abstract: His heavily textured paintings brought him renown in the 1980s. In the ’90s, Nick Nolte played a character inspired by him in a Martin Scorsese film.

name: Herbert J. Gans
profession: Upended Myths of Urban and Suburban Life
headline: Herbert J. Gans, 97, Dies; Upended Myths of Urban and Suburban Life
abstract: A leading sociologist, he explored American society up close — living in a Levittown at one point — to gain insight into issues of race, class, the media and even the Yankees.

name: Aliza Magen
headline: Aliza Magen, Highest-Ranking Woman in the Mossad, Dies at 87
abstract: Her career at Israel’s national intelligence agency included working undercover before serving as deputy under three directors.

name: Eunice Golden
headline: Eunice Golden, Artist Who Mapped the Male Nude, Dies at 98
abstract: Like many feminist artists, she took the body as her subject. But while others were exploring their own bodies, she painted the male anatomy.

name: Roy Thomas Baker
profession: Producer of Bohemian Rhapsody and More
headline: Roy Thomas Baker, 78, Producer of ‘Bohemian Rhapsody’ and More, Dies
abstract: Among the most successful music producers in the 1970s and ’80s, he helped churn out hits for acts like Queen, the Cars, Journey and Foreigner.

name: Barry Benepe
headline: Barry Benepe, Who Gave New York Its Greenmarkets, Dies at 96
abstract: He brought farm-grown produce to the city’s streets, creating the largest network of farmers’ markets in the country and helping to revive neighborhoods.

name: Karen Durbin
headline: Karen Durbin, 80, Dies; ‘Fearless’ Feminist Who Edited The Village Voice
abstract: A fierce advocate of sexual liberation, she pushed the alternative weekly to cover women’s issues, as well as gay rights and avant-garde culture.

name: Arthur Fleischer Jr.
headline: Arthur Fleischer Jr., Prominent Lawyer in Corporate Takeovers, Dies at 92
abstract: He was a top deal maker in the world of mergers and acquisitions, during the 1980s takeover boom and beyond. He also had a keen interest in art.

name: Marco Grassi
profession: Brought Old Paintings Back to Life
headline: Marco Grassi, Who Brought Old Paintings Back to Life, Dies at 90
abstract: As a restorer who specialized in late medieval and early Renaissance paintings from Italy, he was in intimate touch with the paintings of long-dead masters.

name: Mike Patrick
profession: Voice of Sunday Night N.F.L. Games on ESPN
headline: Mike Patrick, Voice of Sunday Night N.F.L. Games on ESPN, Dies at 80
abstract: He did the cable network’s play-by-play for college basketball, football and baseball games, but his most important assignment was “Sunday Night Football.”

name: Masahiro Shinoda
profession: Leading Light of Japans New Wave Cinema
headline: Masahiro Shinoda, Leading Light of Japan’s New Wave Cinema, Dies at 94
abstract: His films tapped into the fantasies of disgruntled youth by embracing brazen sexuality and countercultural politics. But unlike his peers, he did not shun tradition.

name: Leonard Zeskind
profession: Foresaw the Rise of White Nationalism
headline: Leonard Zeskind, Who Foresaw the Rise of White Nationalism, Dies at 75
abstract: With “Blood and Politics,” he predicted that anti-immigrant ideologies would become part of mainstream American politics, and warned about downplaying the threat.

name: Andrea Nevins
profession: Turned Offbeat Subjects Into Moving Films
headline: Andrea Nevins, Who Turned Offbeat Subjects Into Moving Films, Dies at 63
abstract: Her documentaries, one of which received an Oscar nomination, explored subjects like punk-rock dads and Barbie dolls.

name: Steve McMichael
profession: Hall of Fame Tackle for Champion Bears
headline: Steve McMichael, Hall of Fame Tackle for Champion Bears, Dies at 67
abstract: He was a ferocious part of a dominant defense that swept the 1985 Chicago team to victory in the Super Bowl. After 15 N.F.L. seasons, he became a pro wrestler.

name: Gretchen Dow Simpson
headline: Gretchen Dow Simpson, Creator of New Yorker Covers, Dies at 85
abstract: A Massachusetts native, she painted geometrically precise images of rural and seaside New England dwellings that found fans among the storied magazine’s ardent readers.

name: Patrick Adiarte
profession: Actor Seen in Musicals and on M*A*S*H
headline: Patrick Adiarte, Actor Seen in Musicals and on ‘M*A*S*H,’ Dies at 82
abstract: As a young immigrant from the Philippines, he had roles on Broadway in “The King and I” and “Flower Drum Song.” He was later a familiar face on TV.

name: Jay Sigel
headline: Jay Sigel, Amateur Golfer Who Played Like a Pro, Dies at 81
abstract: Many considered him to be the greatest American amateur since Bobby Jones. So why didn’t he try for the PGA Tour? An old hand injury had something to do with it.

name: David Briggs
profession: Music Force in Alabama and Nashville
headline: David Briggs, a Music Force in Alabama and Nashville, Dies at 82
abstract: A first-call keyboardist, he worked with Elvis Presley and Dolly Parton, helped make Muscle Shoals a recording hub, and had a key role in redefining the sound of country.

name: David Paton
profession: Creator of the Flying Eye Hospital
headline: David Paton, Creator of the Flying Eye Hospital, Dies at 94
abstract: An idealistic ophthalmologist, he came up with an ingenious way to treat blindness in far-flung places: by outfitting an airplane with an operating room.

name: Virginia Giuffre
headline: Virginia Giuffre, Voice in Epstein Sex-Trafficking Scandal, Dies at 41
abstract: She accused Jeffrey Epstein and his co-conspirator, Ghislaine Maxwell, of recruiting her to join their predatory ring. She also sued Prince Andrew for sexual assault.

name: Jed
profession: Quirky Pioneer of Los Angeles Radio
headline: Jed the Fish, Quirky Pioneer of Los Angeles Radio, Dies at 69
abstract: With his off-kilter sensibility and deep musical grounding, he brought attention to New Wave and alternative artists at the groundbreaking station KROQ.

name: David Thomas
profession: Led the Avant-Garage Band Pere Ubu
headline: David Thomas, Who Led the ‘Avant-Garage’ Band Pere Ubu, Dies at 71
abstract: As a singer and songwriter, he pushed the boundaries of punk and art-rock, producing a half century of music, writings and performances and always upending expectations.

name: Alexis Herman
headline: Alexis Herman, First Black Secretary of Labor, Is Dead at 77
abstract: A social worker, she became a Democratic Party insider and joined President Bill Clinton’s cabinet during his second term.

name: Bianca Castro-Arabejo
profession: RuPauls Drag Race Star Known as Jiggly Caliente
headline: Bianca Castro-Arabejo, ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race’ Star Known as Jiggly Caliente, Dies at 44
abstract: Fans knew her for her sense of humor, vigorous dance skills and interactions with fellow cast members on the popular drag television show.

name: Zurab Tsereteli
profession: Polarizing Russian Sculptor of Colossal Works
headline: Zurab Tsereteli, Polarizing Russian Sculptor of Colossal Works, Dies at 91
abstract: In bronze, he glorified figures like Peter the Great and Vladimir Putin, often to the public’s distaste. Some works, like a giant Columbus and a 9/11 memorial, were reviled.

name: Valentin-Yves Mudimbe
headline: Valentin-Yves Mudimbe, 83, Dies; African Scholar Challenged the West
abstract: He deconstructed what he called “the colonial library”: the accounts of Africa by Europeans whose aim, he said, was to further colonialism.

name: Dick Barnett
profession: Champion Knick With a Singular Jump Shot
headline: Dick Barnett, Champion Knick With a Singular Jump Shot, Dies at 88
abstract: A high-scoring guard, he played on New York’s two title-winning teams in the 1970s. He was remembered for his “fall back, baby” shooting style.

name: Jean-Pierre Bonnefoux
headline: Jean-Pierre Bonnefoux, Sinuous Ballet Dancer and Choreographer, Dies at 82
abstract: He brought grace and power to his roles before a serious injury encouraged him to try choreography — “maybe the richest part of my life.”

name: Peter Lovesey
headline: Peter Lovesey, a Master of British Whodunits, Is Dead at 88
abstract: He wrote a series of witty police procedurals set in Victorian England and then turned to the present, introducing a cantankerous and technology-averse detective.

name: Jane Gardam
profession: Witty Novelist of a Waning British Empire
headline: Jane Gardam, Witty Novelist of a Waning British Empire, Dies at 96
abstract: “The Queen of the Tambourine,” “Old Filth” and other fiction vividly captured both working-class and aristocratic Britain in the last years of the colonial era.

name: Andy Bey
profession: Jazz Singer Renowned for His Vocal Range
headline: Andy Bey, Jazz Singer Renowned for His Vocal Range, Dies at 85
abstract: An admirer of Nat King Cole, he began as a child performer and as part of a family trio before emerging as a master of the American songbook.

name: Andrew Gross
headline: Andrew Gross, Best-Selling Writer of Thrillers, Is Dead at 72
abstract: A successful New York apparel executive, he switched gears in midlife and became a novelist, writing numerous best sellers, including five with James Patterson.

name: Julia Parsons
profession: U.S. Navy Code Breaker During World War II
headline: Julia Parsons, U.S. Navy Code Breaker During World War II, Dies at 104
abstract: Soon after her officer training in Washington, she was recruited to a classified code-breaking team. She kept her work secret for decades, even from her family.

name: Ted Kotcheff
headline: Ted Kotcheff, Director Who Brought Rambo to the Screen, Dies at 94
abstract: His films, including “First Blood” and “Weekend at Bernie’s,” covered a range of genres. He was later an executive producer of “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit.”

name: Stan Love
profession: Athlete With a Beach Boys Connection
headline: Stan Love, Athlete With a Beach Boys Connection, Dies at 76
abstract: A former N.B.A. player and the father of the All-Star Kevin Love, he was also the brother of the pop group’s Mike Love and a caretaker for its troubled leader, Brian Wilson.

name: Odile de Vasselot
profession: Teenage Aristocrat in the French Resistance
headline: Odile de Vasselot, Teenage Aristocrat in the French Resistance, Dies at 103
abstract: During World War II, she deceived her watchful mother so she could take part in dangerous missions. Later, she founded a girls’ school in Ivory Coast.

name: Bobby Torre
headline: Bobby Torre, the Soul of a Saloon, J.G. Melon, Dies at 81
abstract: His ribald one-liners, oddball knowledge and generosity helped define Melon’s, an Upper East Side fixture, where he manned the door for decades.

name: Joyce Brown
profession: Struggle Redefined the Rights of the Homeless
headline: Overlooked No More: Joyce Brown, Whose Struggle Redefined the Rights of the Homeless
abstract: She successfully challenged her involuntary commitment to Bellevue Hospital in 1987, setting a precedent for homeless people that remains relevant today.

name: Jill Sobule
profession: Sang the Original I Kissed a Girl
headline: Jill Sobule, Who Sang the Original ‘I Kissed a Girl,’ Dies at 66
abstract: Ms. Sobule, known for her advocacy as well as her music, died in a house fire. She had been scheduled to perform songs from an autobiographical musical she wrote.

name: Inah Canabarro Lucas
headline: Brazilian Nun Who Was World’s Oldest Person Dies at 116
abstract: Sister Inah Canabarro Lucas received a blessing from Pope Francis when she turned 110. She would have turned 117 in a few weeks.

name: Ruth Buzzi
headline: Ruth Buzzi, Purse-Wielding Gladys of ‘Laugh-In,’ Is Dead at 88
abstract: She had other roles onstage and on TV, but none more memorable than the wary spinster fending off male advances on that raucous sketch show.

name: Joel Krosnick
headline: Joel Krosnick, Longtime Juilliard String Quartet Cellist, Dies at 84
abstract: Widely admired for his intense and precise playing, Mr. Krosnick stayed with the quartet for over 40 years, longer than either of his cellist predecessors.

name: George Ryan
headline: George Ryan, Illinois Governor Who Halted Prison Executions, Dies at 91
abstract: A Republican, he imposed a moratorium on capital punishment, saying he could not support a death-row system “so fraught with error” that it might end an innocent life.

name: Stephen Mo Hanan
headline: Stephen Mo Hanan, Who Played Three Roles in ‘Cats,’ Dies at 78
abstract: He sang arias on the streets of San Francisco, performed on Broadway and collaborated on a musical about Al Jolson, which he also starred in.

name: Mike Peters
headline: Mike Peters, Frontman of the Alarm, Is Dead at 66
abstract: Leading the Welsh band known for 1980s anthems like “Sixty Eight Guns,” he later became a strong voice in the fight against cancer, which he battled for decades.

name: Pierre Audi
profession: Eminent Force in the Performing Arts
headline: Pierre Audi, Eminent Force in the Performing Arts, Dies at 67
abstract: After turning a derelict lecture hall into the daring Almeida Theater, he had a long career as a director and impresario in Europe and New York.

name: Bob Filner
headline: Bob Filner, Mayor of San Diego Who Left Amid Scandal, Dies at 82
abstract: A progressive member of Congress for two decades, he resigned as mayor after 18 women accused him of sexual harassment.

name: Cora Sue Collins
headline: Cora Sue Collins, a Busy Child Actress in the 1930s, Dies at 98
abstract: She was in films with Greta Garbo, who became a friend, and Myrna Loy, Bette Davis and others. She ended her career after being sexually harassed.

name: Sybil Shainwald
headline: Sybil Shainwald, Lawyer Who Fought for Women’s Health, Dies at 96
abstract: After taking part in a landmark case against the manufacturers of the synthetic hormone DES, she represented many other victims of harmful drugs and devices.

name: Will Hutchins
profession: Gentle TV Cowboy Lawman in Sugarfoot
headline: Will Hutchins, Gentle TV Cowboy Lawman in ‘Sugarfoot,’ Dies at 94
abstract: He starred in one of the westerns that dominated TV in the late 1950s. After losing traction in Hollywood, he became a traveling clown.

name: Philip Sunshine
profession: Pioneer in Treatment of Premature Babies
headline: Philip Sunshine, 94, Dies; Pioneer in Treatment of Premature Babies
abstract: A founder of neonatology, he helped revolutionize the care of preterm and critically ill newborns. “We were able to keep babies alive that would not have survived,” he said.

name: Lulu Roman
profession: Brought Big-Hearted Sass to Hee Haw
headline: Lulu Roman, Who Brought Big-Hearted Sass to ‘Hee Haw,’ Dies at 78
abstract: Obesity was a source of trauma for her, but also of her comedy, which she showcased, along with gospel singing, on the long-running down-home variety show.

name: Jim Dent
profession: Long-Driving Golfer on PGA and Senior Tours
headline: Jim Dent, Long-Driving Golfer on PGA and Senior Tours, Dies at 85
abstract: Honing his skills on segregated courses, he became one of the few Black golfers in the pro ranks, following the lead of Charlie Sifford, Pete Brown and Lee Elder.

name: Clarence O. Smith
headline: Clarence O. Smith, a Founder of Essence Magazine, Is Dead at 92
abstract: As president, he helped persuade companies like Estée Lauder and Ford to advertise in the pages of the first mass-circulation magazine directed at Black women.

name: Kenneth Walker
headline: Kenneth Walker Dies at 73; His Journalism Bared Apartheid’s Brutality
abstract: He shared an Emmy for his reporting on “Nightline” about South Africa’s policy of racial segregation. The National Association of Black Journalists named him journalist of the year.

name: Joseph Nye
headline: Joseph Nye, Political Scientist Who Extolled ‘Soft Power,’ Dies at 88
abstract: He coined the term, arguing that a country’s global influence can’t be built on military might alone. Diplomats around the world paid heed.

name: James Foley
profession: Directed Glengarry Glen Ross and House of Cards
headline: James Foley, 71, Dies; Directed ‘Glengarry Glen Ross’ and ‘House of Cards’
abstract: A veteran New York City-born filmmaker, he also directed the sequels to “Fifty Shades of Grey.”

name: David H. Souter
headline: David H. Souter, Republican Justice Who Allied With Court’s Liberal Wing, Dies at 85
abstract: He left conservatives bitterly disappointed with his migration from right to left, leading to the cry of “no more Souters.”

name: Robert A.G. Monks
headline: Robert A.G. Monks, Crusader Against ‘Imperial’ C.E.O.s, Dies at 91
abstract: A descendant of American wealth, he used his success in business to push for social responsibility in corporate leadership and encouraged shareholders to push back.

name: George Lee
headline: George Lee, Trailblazing Chinese Ballet Dancer, Dies at 90
abstract: He is believed to have been the first Asian to dance with New York City Ballet when he was cast in George Balanchine’s production of “The Nutcracker.”

name: Jack Katz
headline: Jack Katz, Pioneer of the Graphic Novel, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Hailed as a visionary (if a difficult one), he drew inspiration for his multivolume work “The First Kingdom” from no less a model than Homer.

name: J.C. Snead
profession: Golfing Nephew of His Uncle Sam
headline: J.C. Snead, Golfing Nephew of His Uncle Sam, Dies at 84
abstract: He knew he could never match the success of the great Sam Snead, but he won eight tournaments on the PGA Tour and four more on the senior circuit.

name: William L. Porter
headline: William L. Porter, Designer of Classic American Cars, Dies at 93
abstract: As a senior designer at G.M., he helped create the exuberant, elongated shape of 1960s and ’70s cars like the Pontiac GTO, the Bonneville and the Trans Am.

name: Margot Friedländer
headline: Margot Friedländer, Holocaust Survivor Who Found Her Voice, Dies at 103
abstract: She never spoke of her experience until after her husband’s death, when she returned to Berlin with a mission to tell her story, and to teach tolerance.

name: Koyo Kouoh
headline: Koyo Kouoh, Prominent Art World Figure, Is Dead at 57
abstract: Ms. Kouoh had recently been named to oversee next year’s Venice Biennale. She died just days before she was scheduled to announce its theme and title.

name: William H. Luers
headline: William H. Luers, Diplomat Who Backed Czech Dissident Leader, Dies at 95
abstract: His longtime career in the Foreign Service included protecting Vaclav Havel, the writer and dissident who became the first president of the Czech Republic.

name: Johnny Rodriguez
headline: Johnny Rodriguez, Country Music Star, Dies at 73
abstract: The first popular Mexican American country artist, he was best known for the 1970s hits “I Just Can’t Get Her Out of My Mind” and “Ridin’ My Thumb to Mexico.”

name: Terry Brunk
profession: Professional Wrestler and Hardcore Pioneer Known as Sabu
headline: Terry Brunk, Professional Wrestler and ‘Hardcore’ Pioneer Known as Sabu, Dies
abstract: Mr. Brunk rose to fame with the Extreme Championship Wrestling Circuit, pioneering a wrestling style that made use of props like tables and chairs.

name: Robert Shapiro
headline: Robert Shapiro, Who Made NutraSweet a Household Name, Dies at 86
abstract: His promotion of the sugar substitute was a success. But later, as head of Monsanto, he faced blowback after the company rushed into genetically altered products.

name: Sharpe James
profession: Revitalizing Newark Mayor Convicted of Corruption
headline: Sharpe James, Revitalizing Newark Mayor Convicted of Corruption, Dies at 89
abstract: He presided over a rebirth of Newark’s downtown but was found guilty after leaving office of conspiring to sell city-owned properties to a former companion for a fraction of their value.

name: Elizabeth Pochoda
headline: Elizabeth Pochoda, Journalist Who Traversed the Media World, Dies at 83
abstract: She was a writer and a top editor at publications as diverse as The Nation, Vogue and Entertainment Weekly. She also helped found Grand Street and reboot Vanity Fair.

name: Robert Benton
headline: Robert Benton, Influential Director and Screenwriter, Dies at 92
abstract: After collaborating on the script for “Bonnie and Clyde,” he went on to write and direct “Kramer vs. Kramer” and “Places in the Heart.”

name: Nate Holden
profession: Democrat With a Cameo in Trump 24 Campaign
headline: Nate Holden, Democrat With a Cameo in Trump ’24 Campaign, Dies at 95
abstract: Prominent in California politics, yes, that was him in the helicopter with Donald Trump, not the former San Francisco mayor Willie Brown.

name: José Mujica
profession: Leftist President of Uruguay Known for Humility
headline: José Mujica, Leftist President of Uruguay Known for Humility, Dies at 89
abstract: Serving from 2010 to 2015, he refused to accept a presidential salary or live on a presidential estate as he sought to improve the lives of ordinary citizens.

name: Christopher Bond
profession: Former Missouri Governor and U.S. Senator
headline: Christopher Bond, Former Missouri Governor and U.S. Senator, Dies at 86
abstract: A Republican known as Kit, he was the state’s youngest governor. When he retired from Congress after four terms, he said he didn’t want to be the state’s oldest senator.

name: Richard L. Garwin
headline: Richard L. Garwin, a Creator of the Hydrogen Bomb, Dies at 97
abstract: Many scientists contributed to the final result, but he was the one who, as a young physicist, designed the world’s most powerful weapon. He went on to advise a dozen presidents.

name: Nahid Rachlin
headline: Nahid Rachlin, Novelist Who Explored the Iranian Psyche, Dies at 85
abstract: One of the first Iranian novelists to write in English, she examined the clash between East and West. Her debut novel, “Foreigner,” provided insight into pre-revolutionary Iran.

name: Joe Louis Walker
headline: Joe Louis Walker, Free-Ranging Blues Explorer, Is Dead at 75
abstract: A product of the San Francisco rock crucible of the 1960s, he fashioned his own brand of the blues, blending gospel, soul, rock and other genres.

name: Nora Aunor
profession: Singer-Actress Called the Superstar in Philippines
headline: Nora Aunor, Singer-Actress Called ‘the Superstar’ in Philippines, Dies at 71
abstract: Her fans were called Noranians for their devotion to a performer who had enthralled her country — onscreen and on the concert stage — since she was a teenager.

name: Luigi Alva
profession: Elegant Tenor With a Lighthearted Touch
headline: Luigi Alva, Elegant Tenor With a Lighthearted Touch, Dies at 98
abstract: A Peruvian-born international star, he made a specialty of roles in operas by Donizetti, Rossini and Mozart, becoming one of their pre-eminent interpreters.

name: Andrew Cassell
headline: Andrew Cassell, Daring Sailor Who Won Paralympic Gold, Dies at 82
abstract: He survived the deadliest race in modern yachting history, won the first Paralympic sailing contest and founded a nonprofit for sailors with disabilities.

name: Joe Don Baker
headline: Joe Don Baker, Actor Who Found Fame With ‘Walking Tall,’ Dies at 89
abstract: His performance as a crusading Southern sheriff made him a star after a decade under the radar in character parts. He went on to play a wide range of roles.

name: Malcolm Potts
headline: Malcolm Potts, Irreverent Evangelist for Contraception, Dies at 90
abstract: He helped develop the device most often used for surgical abortions. He also spent more than half a century promoting women’s reproductive health in developing countries.

name: Charles Strouse
profession: Composer of Annie and Bye Bye Birdie
headline: Charles Strouse, Composer of ‘Annie’ and ‘Bye Bye Birdie,’ Dies at 96
abstract: He wrote some of the most enduring musical theater numbers of his era and earned three Tony Awards, a Grammy and an Emmy.

name: Ed Smylie
profession: Saved the Apollo 13 Crew With Duct Tape
headline: Ed Smylie, Who Saved the Apollo 13 Crew With Duct Tape, Dies at 95
abstract: He and his team of NASA engineers jumped into action to help three astronauts bound for the moon. His quick thinking earned him a shout-out from Richard Nixon.

name: David Tracy
headline: David Tracy, 86, Theologian Who Rejected Rome’s Supremacy, Dies
abstract: The author of influential books and essays, he was known for a contemporary theory of religion and Catholicism that advocated dialogue, not decrees.

name: Walter Frankenstein
profession: Hid From the Nazis All Over Berlin
headline: Walter Frankenstein, 100, Dies; Hid From the Nazis All Over Berlin
abstract: With his wife and infant sons, he took refuge in unlikely places, including an opera house, an abandoned car and a subway station converted to a bunker.

name: Walasse Ting
profession: Bridged Cultures With Paint and Prose
headline: Overlooked No More: Walasse Ting, Who Bridged Cultures With Paint and Prose
abstract: His style as a poet and artist was informed by his upbringing in Shanghai and his years in Paris. He then joined the Pop-fueled studios of New York.

name: Peter Lax
headline: Peter Lax, Pre-eminent Cold War Mathematician, Dies at 99
abstract: As the computer age dawned, he saw how the new technology could be harnessed to mathematics to solve problems in everything from designing weapons to predicting the weather.

name: Jonnie Boer
headline: Jonnie Boer, Dutch Chef With 3 Michelin Stars, Is Dead at 60
abstract: Long before the New Nordic movement, he saw the value in humble ingredients. So did anyone who ate at De Librije, his acclaimed restaurant in the Netherlands.

name: Steve Kiner
headline: Steve Kiner, Linebacker Who Was Open About Drug Use, Dies at 77
abstract: He was a star at the University of Tennessee when he began using LSD, mescaline and other drugs. He said he got clean while playing in the N.F.L.

name: Greg Cannom
profession: Made Brad Pitt Old and Marlon Wayans White
headline: Greg Cannom, Who Made Brad Pitt Old and Marlon Wayans White, Dies at 73
abstract: He won five Oscars as a makeup artist on movies in which characters transformed, like “Mrs. Doubtfire,” “White Chicks” and many more.

name: Shane Doyle
profession: Founder of a Storied East Village Venue
headline: Shane Doyle, Founder of a Storied East Village Venue, Dies at 73
abstract: An Irish expatriate, he created Sin-é, a bare-bones cafe that became an unlikely magnet for stars like Sinead O’Connor, Bono of U2 and Iggy Pop.

name: Vlastimil Hort
headline: Vlastimil Hort, a Memorably Selfless Chess Grandmaster, Dies at 81
abstract: He could have advanced toward a title when his opponent, Boris Spassky, took ill. Instead, he displayed one of the game’s greatest acts of sportsmanship.

name: Michael A. Ledeen
headline: Michael A. Ledeen, Reagan Adviser Involved in Iran-Contra, Dies at 83
abstract: A neoconservative who fervidly opposed Communism and the fundamentalist regime in Iran, he wrote many books and articles, some of whose theories were later discredited.

name: George Wendt
headline: George Wendt, a.k.a. Norm From ‘Cheers,’ Is Dead at 76
abstract: A burly, easygoing Chicago native, he became a staple of living rooms across the country for more than a decade as one of America’s favorite barflies.

name: Gerald Connolly
profession: Top Democrat on House Oversight Committee
headline: Gerald Connolly, 75, Top Democrat on House Oversight Committee, Is Dead
abstract: He had announced late last year that he was being treated for cancer of the esophagus. He told his constituents in April that he would not seek re-election.

name: Hans Noë
headline: Hans Noë, Architect, Sculptor and Proprietor of a Famed Bar, Dies at 96
abstract: He designed innovative houses and sculptures, but his most visible role in New York City’s cultural life was as an accidental restaurateur, running the venerable Fanelli Cafe.

name: Monroe Milstein
headline: Monroe Milstein, Burlington Coat Factory Founder, Dies at 98
abstract: His was not exactly a rags-to-riches story, but his family made $1.3 billion from an original down payment of $75,000 in savings.

name: David Lazer
headline: David Lazer, Executive Who Joined the World of Muppets, Dies at 89
abstract: At IBM, he hired a young Jim Henson to make humorous corporate films using his puppet creations. Mr. Henson later hired Mr. Lazer to help run his company.

name: Jim Irsay
profession: Longtime Owner of the Indianapolis Colts
headline: Jim Irsay, Longtime Owner of the Indianapolis Colts, Dies at 65
abstract: He took over the business from his father in 1997 and turned the team into one of the best in the league, with a Super Bowl win during the 2006 season.

name: Simon Mann
headline: Simon Mann, Mercenary Who Sought to Overthrow African Leader, Dies at 72
abstract: After Eton and a successful career in the British Army, he became, in his words, “the go-to guy for military coups.” The rewards (and risks) were enormous.

name: Judith Hope Blau
headline: Judith Hope Blau, Who Turned Bagels Into Art, Dies at 87
abstract: She began selling necklaces strung with mini-bagels on a dare from her husband. Bagelmania (and a career as a toy designer) ensued.

name: Yuri Grigorovich
headline: Yuri Grigorovich, Giant of Soviet Ballet, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Among the 20th century’s most significant choreographers, he led the Bolshoi Ballet for more than 30 years, creating epic ballets like “Spartacus.”

name: Sebastião Salgado
headline: Sebastião Salgado, Acclaimed Brazilian Photographer, Is Dead at 81
abstract: Known for his powerfully impactful images of nature and the human condition, he was widely regarded as one of the most important documentary photographers of his time.

name: Leslie Epstein
headline: Leslie Epstein, Writer Who Mastered Both Doing and Teaching, Dies at 87
abstract: His Holocaust novel “King of the Jews” was widely praised. He also wrote about his show-business family and taught writing at Boston University.

name: Michael Roemer
profession: Maker of Acclaimed but Little-Seen Films
headline: Michael Roemer, Maker of Acclaimed but Little-Seen Films, Dies at 97
abstract: His “Nothing but a Man” and “The Plot Against Harry” drew critical praise but never found an audience. He said he took “a certain pride in not having been a success.”

name: Susan Brownmiller
headline: Susan Brownmiller, Who Reshaped Views About Rape, Dies at 90
abstract: Her book “Against Our Will” argued that rape was a crime of power and violence, not passion; it led to laws that made it easier to prosecute rapists.

name: Nino Benvenuti
headline: Nino Benvenuti, Olympic Boxer Who Ruled the Ring in Italy, Dies at 87
abstract: Celebrated as much for his charisma as his boxing skill, he was a 1960 gold medalist in Rome, where he overshadowed a young Muhammad Ali.

name: Tony Bechara
headline: Tony Bechara, Painter Who Championed Latino Artists, Dies at 83
abstract: He turned away from a potential career in the law or international relations to produce abstract paintings, and he headed El Museo del Barrio.

name: Phil Robertson
headline: Phil Robertson, ‘Duck Dynasty’ Patriarch, Dies at 79
abstract: He founded the duck-call business that became the foundation of his family’s reality television empire.

name: Marcel Ophuls
headline: Marcel Ophuls, Myth-Shattering War Documentarian, Is Dead at 97
abstract: He was best known for “The Sorrow and the Pity,” a landmark film that debunked ideas of vast French resistance to the Nazi occupation.

name: Charles B. Rangel
headline: Charles B. Rangel, Powerful Harlem Congressman, Dies at 94
abstract: The first Black chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee, he was a political force for decades, only to be tarnished by an ethics violation.

name: Ronnie Dugger
headline: Ronnie Dugger, Crusading Texas Journalist, Dies at 95
abstract: As founding editor of The Texas Observer, he fought bigotry and exposed corporate greed, political chicanery and government corruption.

name: Rick Derringer
profession: Rocker Known for Hang On Sloopy and Other Hits
headline: Rick Derringer, Rocker Known for ‘Hang On Sloopy’ and Other Hits, Dies at 77
abstract: A Zelig-like guitarist, singer and songwriter, he collaborated with the likes of Barbra Streisand and Peter Frampton and composed Hulk Hogan’s theme “Real American.”

name: Sholom Lipskar
profession: Transformed Miami and Helped Jews in Prison
headline: Rabbi Sholom Lipskar, 78, Dies; Transformed Miami and Helped Jews in Prison
abstract: A charismatic figure in the Chabad-Lubavitch movement, he opened a synagogue in South Florida, unifying the Jewish community there, and founded the Aleph Institute.

name: Bruce Logan
profession: Blew Up the Death Star in Star Wars
headline: Bruce Logan, Who Blew Up the Death Star in ‘Star Wars,’ Dies at 78
abstract: A special effects artist and cinematographer, he also worked on “2001: A Space Odyssey” and “Tron,” and took a detour to comedy with “Airplane!”

name: Jerome Ringo
headline: Jerome Ringo, Outspoken Advocate for Environmental Justice, Dies at 70
abstract: After working in the petrochemical industry, he devoted himself to environmental activism — and to creating an inclusive movement that looked “more like America.”
