name: Ngugi wa Thiong’o
headline: Ngugi wa Thiong’o, Writer Who Condemned Colonists and Elites, Dies at 87
abstract: Mr. Ngugi composed the first modern novel in the Gikuyu language on prison toilet paper while being held by Kenyan authorities. He spent many prolific years in exile.

name: Robert Jarvik
profession: Designer of the First Permanent Artificial Heart
headline: Robert Jarvik, 79, Dies; a Designer of the First Permanent Artificial Heart
abstract: He worked with a team at the University of Utah to create a mechanical heart. It was later used in patients awaiting an organ transplant.

name: Harrison Ruffin Tyler
headline: Harrison Ruffin Tyler, Grandson of the 10th President, Is Dead at 96
abstract: He was the last of three generations spanning nearly the entire history of the United States: When his grandfather was born, George Washington had just become president.

name: Bernard Kerik
headline: Bernard Kerik, New York’s Police Commissioner on 9/11, Dies at 69
abstract: His meteoric rise to become New York City’s chief law enforcement officer was later tarnished after he pleaded guilty to federal corruption and tax crimes.

name: Charles Wadsworth
profession: Pianist and Champion of Chamber Music
headline: Charles Wadsworth, Pianist and Champion of Chamber Music, Dies at 96
abstract: As the founder, director and genial host of the Chamber Music Society of Lincoln Center, he helped drive the chamber music boom of the 1970s.

name: Loretta Swit
headline: Loretta Swit a.k.a. Hot Lips of TV’s ‘M*A*S*H,’ Dies at 87
abstract: She won two Emmy Awards for her sympathetic portrayal of an Army major on the hit TV show and had a long career in TV and theater.

name: Yasunao Tone
headline: Yasunao Tone, Composer Whose Métier Was ‘Anti-Music,’ Dies at 90
abstract: A Japanese-born multimedia artist whose associates included John Cage and Yoko Ono, he pushed digital music past its breaking point.

name: Étienne-Émile Baulieu
headline: Étienne-Émile Baulieu, Who Developed the Abortion Pill, Dies at 98
abstract: He became an advocate of a woman’s right to choose and once said, “It is always tragic when politics takes the most vulnerable hostage — in this case, women.”

name: Peter David
headline: Peter David, Comic Book Writer Who Repopularized the Hulk, Dies at 68
abstract: His long run with that venerable character was the highlight of a career that also encompassed Spider-Man, Aquaman and best-selling “Star Trek” novels.

name: Lynn Freed
profession: South African Writer With a Wry Style
headline: Lynn Freed, South African Writer With a Wry Style, Dies at 79
abstract: In seven novels, dozens of essays and a collection of short stories, she explored her Jewish upbringing during apartheid and the ways women negotiate sexual desire.

name: Valerie Mahaffey
headline: Valerie Mahaffey, Actress Who Played Quirky Villains, Dies at 71
abstract: She had memorable roles on TV shows like “Desperate Housewives” and “Northern Exposure,” and in the dark comedy film “French Exit.”

name: Al Foster
headline: Al Foster, Master of the Jazz Drums, Is Dead at 82
abstract: He was probably best known for his long tenure with Miles Davis, who praised his ability to “keep the groove going forever.”

name: Stanley Fischer
headline: Stanley Fischer, Who Helped Defuse Financial Crises, Dies at 81
abstract: He was the No. 2 at the Federal Reserve and the I.M.F. during periods of economic turmoil, and he mentored future economic leaders, like Ben Bernanke.

name: Guy Klucevsek
headline: Guy Klucevsek, Multi-Genre Accordion Virtuoso, Is Dead at 78
abstract: He elevated his instrument’s often-maligned reputation with deft musicianship, and by writing and commissioning a wide range of music.

name: Renée Victor
headline: Renée Victor, Actress Who Voiced Abuelita in ‘Coco,’ Dies at 86
abstract: She had many memorable roles in her decades-long career, including Lupita in the television series “Weeds.”

name: Alasdair MacIntyre
headline: Alasdair MacIntyre, Philosopher Who Saw a ‘New Dark Ages,’ Dies at 96
abstract: A Marxist-turned-Catholic who denounced individualism, he provoked and inspired fellow thinkers and gained a degree of popularity unusual for a moral philosopher.

name: Holmes Rolston III
headline: Holmes Rolston III, Pioneer of Environmental Ethics, Dies at 92
abstract: He began his career as a pastor. But he was forced out of his congregation in 1965, which led to a new life pondering the value of nature.

name: Alice Notley
headline: Alice Notley, Poet Celebrated for ‘Restless Reinvention,’ Dies at 79
abstract: Once called “our present-day Homer” for her sprawling, experimental epics, she was honored with prizes and was a finalist for the Pulitzer in 1999.

name: David Cope
headline: David Cope, Godfather of A.I. Music, Is Dead at 83
abstract: His EMI algorithm, an early form of artificial intelligence that he developed in the 1980s, prompted searching questions about the limits of human creativity.

name: Herbert Migdoll
headline: Herbert Migdoll, 90, Dies; Joffrey Ballet Photographer for Half-Century
abstract: His photos and graphic design for the Chicago-based company cemented its artistic reputation. He also painted and served as Dance Magazine’s art director.

name: Shigeo Nagashima
headline: Shigeo Nagashima, ‘Mr. Baseball’ of Postwar Japan, Dies at 89
abstract: A key member of the Tokyo Yomiuri Giants of the 1960s and ’70s, Japan’s most enduring sports dynasty, Nagashima was a star from his first season.

name: Per Norgard
headline: Per Norgard, Daring Symphonic Composer, Dies at 92
abstract: Considered the father of Danish contemporary music, he aspired to works in which “everything came out of a single note,” he said, “like the big bang.”

name: Pierre Nora
profession: Probed Role of Memory in the Writing of History
headline: Pierre Nora, 93, Who Probed Role of Memory in the Writing of History, Dies
abstract: A renowned French scholar and publishing figure, he looked at what societies choose to honor — and forget — in telling their stories.

name: Edmund White
headline: Edmund White, Pioneer of Gay Literature, Is Dead at 85
abstract: He mined his own varied catalog of sexual experiences in more than 30 books of fiction and explicitly candid memoirs.

name: Frank Graham Jr.
headline: Frank Graham Jr., Nature Writer Who Updated ‘Silent Spring,’ Dies at 100
abstract: He worked for the Brooklyn Dodgers and wrote about sports but mostly focused on conservation, publishing a sequel to Rachel Carson’s exposé on the dangers of pesticides.

name: Alf Clausen
profession: Gave The Simpsons Its Musical Identity
headline: Alf Clausen, Who Gave ‘The Simpsons’ Its Musical Identity, Dies at 84
abstract: He created the music for hundreds of episodes over 27 seasons, spanning jazz, rock, blues and musicals. He won two Emmys and was nominated for 28 more.

name: Sacha Jenkins
headline: Sacha Jenkins, Filmmaker Who Mined the Black Experience, Dies at 53
abstract: Shaped by early hip-hop culture, his documentaries put race in the foreground, whether the topic was hip-hop fashion, the Capitol riots or Louis Armstrong.

name: Orien McNeill
headline: Orien McNeill, Artist Who Made Mischief on the Water, Dies at 45
abstract: He was the pied piper of a loose community of DIY artists homesteading on New York City’s waterways, which he used as his canvas and stage.

name: Marina von Neumann Whitman
profession: Carved Path for Women in Economics
headline: Marina von Neumann Whitman, Who Carved Path for Women in Economics, Dies at 90
abstract: She was the first woman to serve on the White House Council of Economic Advisers. At General Motors, she became one of the highest-ranking women in corporate America.

name: Mara Corday
profession: Starlet of Monster Movies and Magazines
headline: Mara Corday, Starlet of Monster Movies and Magazines, Dies at 95
abstract: She appeared in Playboy and sci-fi films in the 1950s. Later, in Clint Eastwood’s “Sudden Impact,” she was a hostage until he uttered five famous words.

name: Philippe Labro
profession: Restless Chronicler of the French Condition
headline: Philippe Labro Dies at 88; Restless Chronicler of the French Condition
abstract: As an author (often blurring the boundaries between fiction and nonfiction), a film director, a lyricist and a host of TV and radio shows, he sought to capture his epoch.

name: Marc Garneau
profession: First Canadian in Space and Foreign Minister
headline: Marc Garneau, First Canadian in Space and Foreign Minister, Dies at 76
abstract: His career took flight with a newspaper ad in Ottawa, where he would later help steer the country under Justin Trudeau.

name: Paul Durcan
profession: Irish Poet of Tortured and Tender Souls
headline: Paul Durcan, Irish Poet of Tortured and Tender Souls, Is Dead at 80
abstract: He survived electroshock treatments and the threat of lobotomy to become one of Ireland’s most popular poets. The Irish Times called him a “literary phenomenon.”

name: Hong Yen Chang
headline: Overlooked No More: Hong Yen Chang, Lawyer Who Challenged a Racist System
abstract: He struggled to become the first Chinese American person to practice law in the U.S., then used his training to fight for other Chinese Americans.

name: Sunny Jacobs
profession: Celebrity After Freed From Death Row
headline: Sunny Jacobs, a Celebrity After Freed From Death Row, Dies at 77
abstract: Her story, fashioned into an Off Broadway play and television movies, was later questioned by an investigator in a 2021 book.

name: Jillian Sackler
headline: Jillian Sackler, Philanthropist Who Defended Husband’s Legacy, Dies at 84
abstract: Though the Sackler name was tarnished over Purdue Pharma’s role in the opioid crisis, Arthur Sackler’s should not be, she insisted; a company leader, he died well before the trouble began.

name: Scott Panetti
profession: at the Center of a Landmark Death Penalty Case
headline: Scott Panetti, 67, at the Center of a Landmark Death Penalty Case, Dies
abstract: Diagnosed with a psychotic disorder, he spent 30 years on death row. In 2007, the Supreme Court raised the bar for executing the mentally ill, though Texas still tried to put him to death.

name: Bill Atkinson
headline: Bill Atkinson, Who Made Computers Easier to Use, Is Dead at 74
abstract: A designer for Apple, he created software that made it possible to display shapes, images and text on the screen and present a simulated “desktop.”

name: Jane Larkworthy
profession: Top Magazine Writer and Editor on Beauty
headline: Jane Larkworthy, 62, a Top Magazine Writer and Editor on Beauty, Dies
abstract: She made her mark in publications like Glamour, W, Jane and Mademoiselle. In 2007, she was on the receiving end of media attention, testifying in a sensational trial.

name: Conrad Shinn
profession: First Pilot to Land at the South Pole
headline: Conrad Shinn, First Pilot to Land at the South Pole, Dies at 102
abstract: His Navy plane spent only 49 minutes on the ground and needed a boost from small rockets to break free from the ice and take off.

name: Frederick Forsyth
headline: Frederick Forsyth, Master of the Geopolitical Thriller, Dies at 86
abstract: He wrote best-sellers like “The Day of the Jackal” and “The Dogs of War,” often using material from his earlier life as a reporter and spy.

name: Valmik Thapar
headline: Valmik Thapar, Tenacious Tiger Conservationist in India, Is Dead
abstract: He started studying tigers at a reserve in 1976 and became a leading activist in efforts to save the tiger from poaching and shrinking habitats.

name: Sly Stone
profession: Maestro of a Multifaceted Hitmaking Band
headline: Sly Stone, Maestro of a Multifaceted Hitmaking Band, Dies at 82
abstract: Leading Sly and the Family Stone, he helped redefine the landscape of pop, funk and rock in the late 1960s and early ’70s.

name: Barbara Holdridge
headline: Barbara Holdridge, Whose Record Label Foretold Audiobooks, Dies at 95
abstract: Beginning with a reading by Dylan Thomas, she and a friend found unlikely commercial success in the 1950s with recordings of famous writers reciting their work.

name: Niede Guidon
headline: Niede Guidon, 92, Archaeologist Who Preserved Prehistoric Rock Art, Dies
abstract: Her work in Brazil challenged the prevailing theory of when humans first arrived in the Americas and led to the development of a forgotten corner of the country.

name: Richard Beattie
profession: Early Engineer of Private Equity Takeovers
headline: Richard Beattie, Early Engineer of Private Equity Takeovers, Dies at 86
abstract: A top Wall Street lawyer, he worked on some of the biggest corporate mergers in history, including KKR’s takeover of Nabisco in 1989. He also served in the Carter administration and in city government.

name: Brian Wilson
profession: Pop Auteur and Leader of the Beach Boys
headline: Brian Wilson, Pop Auteur and Leader of the Beach Boys, Dies at 82
abstract: A hitmaker elevated and burdened by the label of genius, he transcended the breezy surf genre to create complex harmonies and intricate soundscapes in the studio.

name: Paul Marantz
profession: Lighting Designer of 9/11 Memorial and Studio 54
headline: Paul Marantz, Lighting Designer of 9/11 Memorial and Studio 54, Dies at 87
abstract: Using neon, searchlights — or even shadows — he dramatically shaped the look of prominent spaces in almost every corner of the world.

name: Betsy Jochum
profession: Last Original Member of Womens Baseball League
headline: Betsy Jochum, 104, Dies; Last Original Member of Women’s Baseball League
abstract: Playing in the All-American Girls Professional Baseball League, which inspired the film “A League of Their Own,” she won a batting title and stole 127 bases in 1944.

name: John Wells
profession: Fled New York for the Solitude of the Desert
headline: John Wells, 64, Who Fled New York for the Solitude of the Desert, Dies
abstract: A fashion photographer, he built a do-it-yourself life on 40 lonely acres in West Texas, living like a modern-day Thoreau and telling millions of his experience on a blog.

name: Ananda Lewis
headline: Ananda Lewis, an MTV Star in the 1990s, Dies at 52
abstract: She rose to fame on “Hot Zone” and other shows before being diagnosed with breast cancer in 2019. She said last year that her cancer had progressed to Stage 4.

name: Enzo Staiola
profession: Starred in Bicycle Thieves as a Child
headline: Enzo Staiola, Who Starred in ‘Bicycle Thieves’ as a Child, Dies at 85
abstract: Discovered on the street in Rome, he had a brush with stardom when he was cast in what many consider one of the greatest films of all time.

name: Amanda Feilding
headline: Amanda Feilding, Eccentric Countess Who Backed Psychedelic Meds, Dies at 82
abstract: She was ridiculed for drilling a hole in her skull to increase blood flow. But her foundation’s research into the therapeutic use of counterculture drugs proved visionary.

name: James Lowe
profession: Rock Outsider With the Electric Prunes
headline: James Lowe, Rock Outsider With the Electric Prunes, Dies at 82
abstract: His band’s output ranged from the 1966 psychedelic hit “I Had Too Much to Dream (Last Night)” to what he called a “Catholic Mass done in rock veneer.”

name: David H. Murdock
headline: David H. Murdock, a Rags-to-Riches Corporate Raider, Dies at 102
abstract: He was a school dropout at 14 and homeless for a spell, but as a driven investor and chief of Dole he became a billionaire. Later came another quest: to extend life through better nutrition.

name: Rigmor Newman
profession: Behind-the-Scenes Fixture of the Jazz World
headline: Rigmor Newman, Behind-the-Scenes Fixture of the Jazz World, Dies at 86
abstract: She was a concert promoter, a nightclub impresario and the producer of an award-winning 1992 film about the Nicholas Brothers dance duo.

name: Wayne Lewis
profession: Singer With the R&B Mainstay Atlantic Starr
headline: Wayne Lewis, Singer With the R&B Mainstay Atlantic Starr, Dies at 68
abstract: The group reached No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1987 with the ballad “Always” and went on to leave a lasting impression on modern-day artists.

name: Graham Gund
headline: Graham Gund, Playful Architect Who Mixed Past and Present, Dies at 84
abstract: A noted art collector as well as a designer, he brought a personal, history-minded approach to his work around Boston and on college campuses.

name: Sunjay Kapur
profession: Businessman and Ex-Husband of Bollywood Star
headline: Sunjay Kapur, Businessman and Ex-Husband of Bollywood Star, Dies at 53
abstract: Mr. Kapur, who died of a heart attack after playing in a polo match in England, was formerly married to the Bollywood star Karisma Kapoor.

name: Arthur Hamilton
profession: Wrote the Enduring Cry Me a River
headline: Arthur Hamilton, Who Wrote the Enduring ‘Cry Me a River,’ Dies at 98
abstract: A hit for Julie London in 1955, it was later recorded by — among many others — Ella Fitzgerald, Barbra Streisand and Michael Bublé, who praised it for its “darkness.”

name: Harris Yulin
headline: Harris Yulin, Actor Who Perpetually Played the Bad Guy, Dies at 87
abstract: An award-winning actor and director, he appeared in scores of stage plays, movies and TV shows over six decades, most often as unsavory characters.

name: Foday Musa Suso
profession: Ambitious Ambassador for West African Music
headline: Foday Musa Suso, 75, Dies; Ambitious Ambassador for West African Music
abstract: A master of the kora who worked with Herbie Hancock and Philip Glass, his career was powered as much by experimentation as by reverence for tradition.

name: Dara Birnbaum
profession: Video Was Her Medium and Her Message
headline: Dara Birnbaum, 78, Dies; Video Was Her Medium and Her Message
abstract: As early as the 1970s, she demonstrated that mass media was fair game as artistic material, and that its power could be turned against itself.

name: Marthe Cohn
headline: Marthe Cohn, a Wartime Jewish Nurse Who Spied for the French, Dies at 105
abstract: Fluent in German and passing as an Aryan, she once crossed into Germany, uncovered Nazi military secrets and nursed a wounded, and deceived, SS officer.

name: Violeta Barrios de Chamorro
headline: Violeta Barrios de Chamorro, 95, Dies; Led Nicaragua After Civil War
abstract: The first woman to lead a Central American country, she served in the 1990s after the nation had been shaken by political strife.

name: Joel Shapiro
headline: Joel Shapiro, Celebrated Stick-Figure Sculptor, Dies at 83
abstract: His work conveyed a surprising depth of emotion, hinting at the threat of imbalance. He also produced more than 30 large-scale commissions.

name: Alex Polikoff
profession: Won a Marathon Housing Segregation Case
headline: Alex Polikoff, Who Won a Marathon Housing Segregation Case, Dies at 98
abstract: He notched a victory in a Supreme Court decision against the City of Chicago in 1976. He then spent over 40 years making sure the ruling was enforced.

name: Norma Swenson
headline: Norma Swenson, an Author of ‘Our Bodies, Ourselves,’ Dies at 93
abstract: She was a proponent of natural childbirth when she joined the group that produced a candid guide to women’s health. It became a cultural touchstone and a global best seller.

name: Leonard A. Lauder
headline: Leonard A. Lauder, Philanthropist and Cosmetics Heir, Dies at 92
abstract: He was best known for his success in business, notably the international beauty company he built with his mother, Estée Lauder. He was also an influential art patron.

name: William Langewiesche
headline: William Langewiesche, the ‘Steve McQueen of Journalism,’ Dies at 70
abstract: He was a master of long form narratives, often involving high-stakes topics. He reported for Vanity Fair, The Atlantic and The New York Times Magazine.

name: Beuford Smith
headline: Beuford Smith, Photographer Who Chronicled Black Life, Dies at 89
abstract: He was a prominent member of the Kamoinge Workshop, a collective that nurtured Black photographers at a time when they were marginalized by the mainstream.

name: Ralph J. Lamberti
profession: Sought Clout for New York Borough Leaders
headline: Ralph J. Lamberti, 90, Dies; Sought Clout for New York Borough Leaders
abstract: Staten Island’s president in the 1980s, he vainly pressed to maintain checks and balances in city government to prevent against what he called “an imperial mayor.”

name: Nina Kuscsik
headline: Nina Kuscsik, Marathoner Who Broke Gender Barriers, Dies at 86
abstract: Overcoming male resistance as a voice for equality, she was the first woman to enter the New York City Marathon and the first official female winner of the Boston race.

name: Walter Brueggemann
headline: Walter Brueggemann, Theologian Who Argued for the Poor, Dies at 92
abstract: He used biblical exegesis to argue that faith demands justice, calling on churches to challenge oppression and uplift society’s marginalized.

name: Alfred Brendel
headline: Alfred Brendel, Bravura Pianist Who Forged a Singular Path, Dies at 94
abstract: With little formal training but full of ideas, he focused on the core classical composers, winning over audiences (though not every critic) around the world.

name: Anne Burrell
headline: Anne Burrell, Chef and Food Network Star, Dies at 55
abstract: Her distinctive hairstyle and swagger in the kitchen made her one of America’s most recognizable Italian chefs.

name: David Hekili Kenui Bell
headline: David Hekili Kenui Bell, an Actor in ‘Lilo & Stitch,’ Dies at 46
abstract: Mr. Bell’s first role in a feature film was providing comic relief in the Disney hit.

name: Stanley Nelson
headline: Stanley Nelson, Journalist Who Investigated Klan Murders, Dies at 69
abstract: Born and raised in Louisiana, he investigated unresolved civil-rights-era killings in the Deep South. His reporting on one of those cases made him a Pulitzer Prize finalist.

name: Vicki Goldberg
profession: Saw Photography Through a Literary Lens
headline: Vicki Goldberg Dies at 88; Saw Photography Through a Literary Lens
abstract: An influential photography critic, she wrote essays, newspaper columns and books, including a notable biography of the photojournalist Margaret Bourke-White.

name: Gary England
headline: Gary England, Star Meteorologist in Tornado Alley, Dies at 85
abstract: Working for a TV station in Oklahoma City, he was known for using high-tech tools to give early warnings of tornadoes in the central U.S.

name: William Cran
headline: William Cran, ‘Frontline’ Documentarian, Is Dead at 79
abstract: Producing or directing, he made more than 50 films over 50 years, including a series on the English language and an exploration of J. Edgar Hoover’s secret life.

name: Edward Anders
profession: Duped Nazis and Illuminated the Cosmos
headline: Edward Anders, Who Duped Nazis and Illuminated the Cosmos, Dies at 98
abstract: His research unraveled mysteries about the solar system and the demise of the dinosaurs. In retirement, he turned his attention to the Holocaust.

name: Suchinda Kraprayoon
headline: Suchinda Kraprayoon, Thai Leader Who Set Off Bloody Protests, Dies at 91
abstract: A top general, he was appointed prime minister in 1992, a short-lived tenure that immediately incited the Black May uprising — and a violent backlash by his military.

name: Kim Woodburn
profession: British TVs No-Nonsense Queen of Clean
headline: Kim Woodburn, British TV’s No-Nonsense ‘Queen of Clean,’ Dies at 83
abstract: She was a blunt and bossy domestic dominatrix on the series “How Clean Is Your House?” honing a persona as the rudest woman on reality television.

name: Terry Louise Fisher
headline: Terry Louise Fisher, a Creator of ‘L.A. Law,’ Dies at 79
abstract: She channeled her experiences — and frustrations — as a Los Angeles prosecutor into an award-winning career as a television writer and producer.

name: Louis Diaz
headline: Louis Diaz, Undercover Agent Who Busted a Drug Kingpin, Dies at 79
abstract: He posed as a mobster dealing drugs and laundering cash to help topple Nicky Barnes, who as “Mr. Untouchable” ran a formidable Harlem heroin ring.

name: Lou Christie
headline: Lou Christie, ‘Lightnin’ Strikes’ Pop Crooner, Is Dead at 82
abstract: A late-1960s throwback to the days of clean-cut teen idols — he called himself “the missing link” — he rode his gymnastic vocal range to a string of hits.

name: Gunilla Knutson
profession: Star of Take It Off Shaving Cream Ads
headline: Gunilla Knutson, Star of ‘Take It Off’ Shaving Cream Ads, Dies at 84
abstract: A model who was crowned Miss Sweden in 1961, she became best known for commercials that one observer said “replaced the ‘hard sell’ with the ‘sex sell.’”

name: Nathan Silver
headline: Nathan Silver, Who Chronicled a Vanished New York, Dies at 89
abstract: An architect, he wrote in his book “Lost New York” about the many buildings that were destroyed before passage of the city’s landmarks preservation law.

name: Rod Nordland
headline: Rod Nordland, 75, Dies; War Reporter Who Also Wrote of His Own Struggle
abstract: Motivated by the helplessness of his boyhood, he described the lives of vulnerable people in conflicts around the world and later his own terminal illness.

name: Fred Smith
headline: Fred Smith, Billionaire Founder of FedEx, Is Dead at 80
abstract: His vision for how to ship packages overnight led to not just a new company, but also a new sector of the world economy and a now-familiar English verb.

name: Fred Smith
profession: Left Blondie for the Band Television
headline: Fred Smith, Who Left Blondie for the Band Television, Dies at 77
abstract: In the ’70s, New York’s bohemia was devoted to hostile yet arty rock. Mr. Smith had two qualities rare in the scene: personal and musical understatement.

name: James Lloydovich Patterson
profession: Soviet Poet and Symbol of Racial Unity
headline: James Lloydovich Patterson, 91, Dies; Soviet Poet and Symbol of Racial Unity
abstract: Years after being catapulted to national fame in the U.S.S.R. as a child actor, he wrote about ideals of racial harmony and international solidarity.

name: Arnaldo Pomodoro
headline: Arnaldo Pomodoro, 98, Sculptor of Monumental Fractured Spheres, Dies
abstract: His bronze works — smooth-skinned orbs slashed to reveal complex cores — are in public places around the world, including outside the U.N. headquarters and in Vatican City.

name: Bobby Sherman
profession: Easygoing Teen Idol of the 1960s and 70s
headline: Bobby Sherman, Easygoing Teen Idol of the 1960s and ’70s, Dies at 81
abstract: First on TV and then on the pop charts, he became so popular so young, he once said, that he “didn’t really have time to have an ego.”

name: Blake Farenthold
headline: Blake Farenthold, 63, Congressman Who Quit in Harassment Case, Dies
abstract: A Texas Republican, he gave up his seat after news broke that public funds had been used to settle the case, made by his former communications director.

name: Lynn Hamilton
profession: Steady Presence on Sanford and Son
headline: Lynn Hamilton, a Steady Presence on ‘Sanford and Son,’ Dies at 95
abstract: A former Broadway actress, she was a no-nonsense foil for the unruly Fred Sanford. She also warmed hearts with a recurring role on the “The Waltons.”

name: Marcia Resnick
profession: Camera Captured New Yorks Bad Boys
headline: Marcia Resnick, Whose Camera Captured New York’s ‘Bad Boys’, Dies at 74
abstract: A conceptual artist, she used photography to make surrealistic images and then went on to document Manhattan’s downtown scene and its mostly male provocateurs.

name: Mick Ralphs
profession: Mott the Hoople and Bad Company
headline: Mick Ralphs, of Mott the Hoople and Bad Company, Dies at 81
abstract: A guitarist and songwriter, he ditched glam rock at its peak and scored with meatier stadium-rock anthems like “Can’t Get Enough” and “Feel Like Making Love.”

name: Gailard Sartain
profession: Character Actor and Hee Haw Regular
headline: Gailard Sartain, Character Actor and ‘Hee Haw’ Regular, Dies at 81
abstract: Though best known for comedy, he also played serious roles, including a sinister sheriff in “Mississippi Burning.” The director Alan Rudolph cast him in nine films.

name: P. Adams Sitney
headline: P. Adams Sitney, Leading Scholar of Avant-Garde Film, Dies at 80
abstract: He championed works of cinema that were destined never to have a commercial breakthrough — which, to him, was the whole point.

name: Fred Espenak
headline: Fred Espenak, Astrophysicist Known as Mr. Eclipse, Dies at 73
abstract: He chased eclipses for five decades, wrote several books about them and worked with NASA to make data accessible to nonscientist sky gazers.

name: Valery Panov
headline: Valery Panov, Ballet Star Who Fought to Leave the U.S.S.R., Dies at 87
abstract: Trying to move to Israel with his ballerina wife, he was harassed and jailed while becoming an international cause célèbre and a Cold War symbol of the plight of Soviet Jews.

name: Léon Krier
headline: Léon Krier, Architect Whose Classical Work Won a Royal Ally, Dies at 79
abstract: Although many of his designs remain unbuilt — with a few exceptions, including King Charles’s Poundbury — he was a driving force in the New Urbanism movement.

name: Susan Beth Pfeffer
profession: Wrote Complex Stories for Young Adults
headline: Susan Beth Pfeffer, 77, Dies; Wrote Complex Stories for Young Adults
abstract: Her 76 books included “Life as We Knew It,” a late-career best seller that told the story of a family in postapocalyptic Pennsylvania.

name: Mortimer Matz
headline: Mortimer Matz, a Virtuoso New York P.R. Man, Is Dead at 100
abstract: He represented the lofty as well as the low. His credits included the Nathan’s hot dog eating contest and the obligatory raincoat to keep a defendant’s cuffed hands covered in a “perp walk.”

name: Bill Moyers
profession: Face of Public TV and Once a White House Voice
headline: Bill Moyers, a Face of Public TV and Once a White House Voice, Dies at 91
abstract: He was a renowned television correspondent and commentator who also had long ties with Lyndon B. Johnson, including as his press secretary.

name: Carolyn McCarthy
profession: Turned a Gunmans Massacre Into a Crusade
headline: Carolyn McCarthy, Who Turned a Gunman’s Massacre Into a Crusade, Dies at 81
abstract: After her husband was killed and her son wounded on a Long Island commuter train in 1993, she went to Congress on a mission against gun violence.

name: Rick Hurst
profession: Cletus Hogg on The Dukes of Hazzard
headline: Rick Hurst, Cletus Hogg on ‘The Dukes of Hazzard,’ Dies at 79
abstract: As the affable deputy sheriff on the popular CBS show, Mr. Hurst became a beloved figure for many fans of the show.

name: Jonathan Mayers
profession: Founder of the Bonnaroo Music Festival
headline: Jonathan Mayers, a Founder of the Bonnaroo Music Festival, Dies at 51
abstract: He helped bring crowds of music fans to a remote Tennessee cow farm with Bonnaroo, and to San Francisco with the Outside Lands festival.

name: Rosalind Fox Solomon
headline: Rosalind Fox Solomon, Whose Photos Captured Emotional Nuance, Dies at 95
abstract: Critics compared her unnerving images to those of Diane Arbus, but praised her ability to infuse her subjects with warmth and humanity.

name: Rotimi Fani-Kayode
profession: Camera Sought a Truer Image of Black Men
headline: Overlooked No More: Rotimi Fani-Kayode, Whose Camera Sought a Truer Image of Black Men
abstract: He was a pioneering figure in Black British art whose rebellious, symbol-rich images explored race, queerness, desire and spirituality.

name: Jack Kleinsinger
profession: Impresario Behind a Marathon Jazz Series
headline: Jack Kleinsinger, Impresario Behind a Marathon Jazz Series, Dies at 88
abstract: A lawyer by day, he created Highlights in Jazz, bringing together artists both famous and unknown in more than 300 concerts over 50 years.

name: Max Fink
headline: Max Fink, Champion of Electroconvulsive Therapy, Dies at 102
abstract: As a psychiatry resident, he became convinced of the benefits of ECT. But he spent years battling detractors and a misleading pop-culture depiction of the procedure.

name: Diana Oh
profession: Passionate Voice for Queer Liberation in Theater
headline: Diana Oh, Passionate Voice for Queer Liberation in Theater, Dies at 38
abstract: Oh’s politically provocative and often playful works, including the Off Broadway production “{my lingerie play},” asserted the right to be oneself while having fun.

name: Lalo Schifrin
profession: Composer of Mission: Impossible and Much More
headline: Lalo Schifrin, 93, Dies; Composer of ‘Mission: Impossible’ and Much More
abstract: He was best known for one enduring TV theme, but he had a startlingly diverse career as a composer, arranger and conductor in a wide range of genres.

name: Gerry Philbin
profession: Star Defensive End for the Jets
headline: Gerry Philbin, Star Defensive End for the Jets, Dies at 83
abstract: A sack specialist, he led the American Football League in taking down quarterbacks in the 1968 regular season, which was capped by the Jets’ upset win in Super Bowl III.

name: Mikayla Raines
headline: Mikayla Raines, Who Rescued Foxes and Other Animals, Is Dead at 30
abstract: She founded Save a Fox Rescue to care for foxes that had been abandoned or bred for their pelts on fur farms. She gained millions of social media followers along the way.

name: Dave Parker
profession: Power Hitter for the Pittsburgh Pirates
headline: Dave Parker, Power Hitter for the Pittsburgh Pirates, Dies at 74
abstract: Parker, a towering outfielder who helped propel the Pirates to the World Series in 1979, was elected to the Baseball Hall of Fame last year.

name: D. Wayne Lukas
headline: D. Wayne Lukas, Horse Trainer Who Saddled Winners From Coast to Coast, Dies at 89
abstract: He earned purses of more than $300 million in a Hall of Fame career that revolutionized thoroughbred racing with a modern-day corporate approach.

name: Jane Stanton Hitchcock
headline: Jane Stanton Hitchcock, 78, Dies; Crime Novelist Who Mocked High Society
abstract: A daughter of privilege, she mixed social satire with murder in a series of addictive mysteries.

name: Jimmy Swaggart
profession: Passionate Televangelist Was Ousted by Scandal
headline: Jimmy Swaggart Dies at 90; Passionate Televangelist Was Ousted by Scandal
abstract: A fire-and-brimstone preacher, he reached millions and made millions in a global enterprise before tumbling from grace over his encounters with a prostitute.

name: Lucian Leape
profession: Work Spurred Patient Safety in Medicine
headline: Lucian Leape, Whose Work Spurred Patient Safety in Medicine, Dies at 94
abstract: Despite resistance from the medical establishment, he found systemic ways to reduce errors, paving the way for a global standard. Thousands of lives have been saved.

name: Günther Uecker
headline: Günther Uecker, Who Punctuated His Art With Nails, Dies at 95
abstract: A member of the German collective Zero Group, he hammered thousands of nails — into columns, chairs, canvases — expressing the power of repetition to bring about complexity.

name: David R. Slavitt
profession: Poet and Critic With a Side Gig in Pulp Fiction
headline: David R. Slavitt, Poet and Critic With a Side Gig in Pulp Fiction, Dies at 90
abstract: He wrote more than 130 books, mostly collections of poetry and translations of classics, as well as lowbrow novels under a pen name.

name: Anne Merriman
profession: Mother of Palliative Care in Uganda
headline: Anne Merriman, ‘Mother of Palliative Care’ in Uganda, Dies at 90
abstract: A medical doctor and former nun, she found an affordable way to expand palliative care in the developing world, bringing pain relief to poor, terminally ill patients.

name: Richard A. Boucher
headline: Richard A. Boucher, Veteran State Department Spokesman, Dies at 73
abstract: Working for six secretaries of state, he was known for explaining and defending U.S. foreign policy in a noncombative tone, without interjecting his own opinion.

name: Alex Delvecchio
profession: Hockey Hall of Famer With Red Wings
headline: Alex Delvecchio, Hockey Hall of Famer With Red Wings, Dies at 93
abstract: A center who skated alongside Gordie Howe on the team’s famed “Production Line,” he helped win three Stanley Cups and stood out for his clean play over 24 years in Detroit.

name: Robert Holton
profession: His Potent Chemo Drug Saved Lives — and Trees
headline: Robert Holton Dies at 81; His Potent Chemo Drug Saved Lives — and Trees
abstract: His method of producing the drug Taxol, now used widely to treat various cancers, eliminated the need to source its active compound from endangered trees.

name: Dave Scott
headline: Dave Scott, Hip-Hop Choreographer, Is Dead at 52
abstract: A former basketball standout with no formal dance training, he came to provide moves for rappers like Bow Wow and dance-battle films like “You Got Served.”

name: Patricia Peterson
profession: Innovative Fashion Editor at The Times
headline: Patricia Peterson, Innovative Fashion Editor at The Times, Dies at 99
abstract: She oversaw fashion coverage beginning in 1957, when hemlines made headlines. She later made groundbreaking ads for Henri Bendel with her photographer husband, Gösta Peterson.

name: Sandy Gall
headline: Sandy Gall, Reporter Who Covered a Half-Century of Wars, Dies at 97
abstract: He was an intrepid journalist in Vietnam, Africa and the Middle East before becoming a mainstay news presenter on British TV.

name: Michael Madsen
headline: Michael Madsen, a Familiar Hollywood Heavy, Is Dead at 67
abstract: He had the air of a timeless movie bad guy in movies like “Reservoir Dogs” and “Kill Bill.” “I’m a bit of a throwback to the days of black-and-white movies,” he said.

name: Mark Brokaw
headline: Mark Brokaw, Theater Director Who Gave Rising Talent a Stage, Dies at 66
abstract: On and off Broadway, he worked with playwrights like Kenneth Lonergan and Paula Vogel, combining complex storytelling with the simplest possible productions.

name: Jim Shooter
headline: Jim Shooter, Editor Who ‘Saved the Comics Industry,’ Dies at 73
abstract: He brought order and profits to Marvel in the 1980s and helped establish the genre as a popular-culture tent pole for decades to come.

name: Ronald Ribman
profession: His Plays Mined the Absurdity of Existence
headline: Ronald Ribman, 92, Dies; His Plays Mined the Absurdity of Existence
abstract: He set his frequently neurotic characters in bleak, morally ambiguous situations where laughter, as he put it, “is a measure of the sickness of society.”

name: S. Daniel Abraham
headline: S. Daniel Abraham, Who Reaped Riches With Slim-Fast, Dies at 100
abstract: He turned a small family business into a billion-dollar weight-loss empire by replacing calorie counting and forbidden foods with “just add milk.”

name: Anna Ornstein
headline: Anna Ornstein, Psychoanalyst Who Survived the Holocaust, Dies at 98
abstract: Despite the unspeakable horror of her youth, she embraced a school of psychotherapy that stresses empathy and the belief that everyone can change for the better.

name: Sandra Neels
profession: Eminent in Modern Dance for 60 Years
headline: Sandra Neels, Eminent in Modern Dance for 60 Years, Dies at 85
abstract: She was a leading dancer for Merce Cunningham, a prolific choreographer and an admired teacher.

name: Paul Libin
profession: Enduring Force on and Off Broadway
headline: Paul Libin, an Enduring Force on and Off Broadway, Dies at 94
abstract: He staged a noted revival of “The Crucible” in a Manhattan hotel ballroom in 1958, ran Circle in the Square and oversaw the operations of Jujamcyn Theaters.

name: Joseph Giordano
headline: Joseph Giordano, Surgeon Who Helped Save Reagan’s Life, Dies at 84
abstract: He had built one of the country’s leading trauma centers in Washington, which made it possible for his team to respond quickly after the president was shot.

name: Stuart Burrows
headline: Stuart Burrows, Welsh Lyric Tenor Who Straddled the Atlantic, Dies at 92
abstract: He was a mainstay at both the Metropolitan Opera and the Royal Opera House, winning acclaim for his full tenor range and a rich, unforced tone, notably singing Mozart.

name: Julian McMahon
headline: Julian McMahon, ‘Nip/Tuck’ and ‘Fantastic Four’ Star, Dies at 56
abstract: He played a half-human, half-demon in the WB supernatural series “Charmed” and a playboy plastic surgeon in the FX series “Nip/Tuck.”

name: Jim Parkinson
profession: Logo Artist in Prints Glory Days
headline: Jim Parkinson, Logo Artist in Print’s Glory Days, Dies at 83
abstract: His work blended classic design with a loose ’60s-style energy, giving publications like Rolling Stone an identity that radiated with gravitas and personality.

name: Carla Maxwell
profession: Keeper of the José Limón Flame
headline: Carla Maxwell, Keeper of the José Limón Flame, Dies at 79
abstract: Her stewardship of the troupe that bears his name became a model for other dance companies, like Martha Graham’s, after their founders died.

name: Franklin W. Stahl
profession: Helped Create a Beautiful DNA Experiment
headline: Franklin W. Stahl, 95, Dies; Helped Create a ‘Beautiful’ DNA Experiment
abstract: He and a colleague proved a theory advanced by the Nobel Prize winners James Watson and Francis Crick, who discovered DNA’s helical structure.

name: Norman Tebbit
profession: Conservative Force in Britain and Thatcher Ally
headline: Norman Tebbit, Conservative Force in Britain and Thatcher Ally, Dies at 94
abstract: He was a potential prime minister until he left high office to care for his wife, who was seriously hurt in a bombing by the Irish Republican Army.

name: Ivar Giaever
headline: Ivar Giaever, Nobel Winner in Quantum Physics, Dies at 96
abstract: A former “D” student from Norway, he made his mark at G.E.’s Research Lab in the U.S., in part by confirming a pivotal theory about superconductivity.

name: Richard Greenberg
headline: Richard Greenberg, Playwright Whose ‘Take Me Out’ Won a Tony, Dies at 67
abstract: More than 30 of his plays were produced on Broadway and off. Many of them dealt with the manners and mores of New York’s upper middle class.

name: Paul Bugas
profession: Director of a Secret Doomsday Bunker
headline: Paul Bugas, Director of a Secret Doomsday Bunker, Is Dead at 96
abstract: The Cold War-era shelter, hidden below the Greenbrier Resort in West Virginia, was designed to house members of Congress in the event of a nuclear attack.

name: Henry Mount Charles
profession: Castle Was a Mecca for Rock
headline: Henry Mount Charles, Whose Castle Was a Mecca for Rock, Dies at 74
abstract: To preserve his Irish manor, he staged concerts on its grounds, drawing the likes of U2, Bruce Springsteen, Bob Dylan, Madonna, 50 Cent and the Rolling Stones as well as tens of thousands of fans.

name: James B. Maas
profession: Guru of Slumber and the Power Nap
headline: James B. Maas, Guru of Slumber and the ‘Power Nap,’ Dies at 86
abstract: An author, public speaker and professor, he taught a hugely popular and entertaining psychology course at Cornell that focused on the essential importance of sleep.

name: Jane Lazarre
profession: Wrote About Raising Black Sons as a White Mother
headline: Jane Lazarre, 81, Dies; Wrote About Raising Black Sons as a White Mother
abstract: With books like “The Mother Knot” and “Beyond the Whiteness of Whiteness,” she challenged liberal orthodoxies about feminism and the Black experience in America.

name: Dave ‘Baby’ Cortez
headline: Dave ‘Baby’ Cortez, Hitmaker Who Seemed to Vanish, Is Dead at 83
abstract: His “The Happy Organ” reached No. 1 in 1959, but his pop stardom was short-lived, and his death in 2022, with an anonymous burial, remains a source of mystery.

name: Thornton Willis
headline: Thornton Willis, 89, Who Brought Emotion to Geometric Painting, Dies
abstract: He spent a lifetime patiently excavating the problems and possibilities of the painted surface — in terms of color, texture, process and space.

name: Rebekah Del Rio
profession: Mournful Singer of Mulholland Drive Fame
headline: Rebekah Del Rio, Mournful Singer of ‘Mulholland Drive’ Fame, Dies at 57
abstract: Her pivotal role performing a Spanish-language cover of Roy Orbison’s “Crying” in the 2001 David Lynch movie raised her profile, but her career was marked by misfortune.

name: David Gergen
profession: Adviser to Presidents and Political Commentator
headline: David Gergen, Adviser to Presidents and Political Commentator, Dies at 83
abstract: He served under Nixon, Ford, Reagan and Clinton before becoming a top editor and a familiar TV pundit. “Centrism doesn’t mean splitting the difference,” he said.

name: Brian Clarke
headline: Brian Clarke, Stained-Glass Innovator, Is Dead at 71
abstract: Believing that the art form had to move from religious to secular settings, he designed installations in airports, corporate buildings, a country club and a marketplace.

name: Mark Snow
headline: Mark Snow, Who Conjured the ‘X-Files’ Theme, Is Dead at 78
abstract: It took a misplaced elbow, a quirk of Los Angeles geography and some whistling from his wife to produce one of television’s most memorable melodies.

name: Bill Dilworth
profession: Caretaker of The New York Earth Room
headline: Bill Dilworth, Caretaker of ‘The New York Earth Room,’ Is Dead at 70
abstract: For decades, he tended a SoHo loft filled with dirt, made by the conceptual artist Walter De Maria. People made pilgrimages to see it — and Mr. Dilworth, its magnetic steward.

name: Daniel Kleppner
headline: Daniel Kleppner, Physicist Who Brought Precision to GPS, Dies at 92
abstract: He worked to develop an atomic clock that is essential to global positioning systems and helped confirm a rare state of matter predicted based on work by Albert Einstein.

name: Andrew Kassoy
profession: Saw Capitalism as a Force for Social Good
headline: Andrew Kassoy, 55, Dies; Saw Capitalism as a Force for Social Good
abstract: He was a founder of B Lab, a nonprofit network whose lofty mission is “transforming the global economy to benefit all people, communities and the planet.”

name: Charles Reinhart
profession: Steered Modern Dance Into the Mainstream
headline: Charles Reinhart, 94, Dies; Steered Modern Dance Into the Mainstream
abstract: As the director of the American Dance Festival, he oversaw the growth of diverse dance traditions, both in the United States and abroad.

name: Samuel Abt
headline: Samuel Abt, Reporter Who Covered Tour de France for Decades, Dies at 91
abstract: An authority on cycling, he wrote about the elite race for The New York Times and The International Herald Tribune, bringing wider attention to it.

name: Muhammadu Buhari
headline: Muhammadu Buhari, Strongman President of Nigeria, Dies at 82
abstract: A former feared military leader, he won one democratic election in 2015 and another in 2019, but struggled to make good on promises to tackle corruption and terrorism.

name: Fanny Howe
headline: Fanny Howe, Poet of Unsettled Dreams, Is Dead at 84
abstract: Her heritage, as a scion of Boston Brahmins and the mother of biracial children, shaped a discursive verse style that veiled sharp edges and melancholy resolutions.

name: Fauja Singh
profession: Marathon Runner at an Advanced Age
headline: Fauja Singh, Marathon Runner at an Advanced Age, Is Dead
abstract: Competing in London in 2011, he claimed to be 100, though his exact age remained a mystery. “I run while talking to God,” he said in explaining his endurance.

name: John MacArthur
headline: John MacArthur, Fiery Preacher and Culture Warrior, Dies at 86
abstract: He was a theologically uncompromising pastor in Southern California who influenced generations of evangelical preachers.

name: Billy Jones
profession: Impresario of New Yorks Indie Music Scene
headline: Billy Jones, Impresario of New York’s Indie Music Scene, Dies at 45
abstract: He opened Baby’s All Right and three other nightclubs, a restaurant and a record store in a dozen years, helping the city maintain its cultural verve.

name: Andrea Gibson
headline: Andrea Gibson, a Poet of Love, Hope and Gender Identity, Dies at 49
abstract: A master of spoken-word performance, Gibson insisted that poetry, especially when read aloud to an audience, was a political act.

name: Steve Benson
headline: Steve Benson, a Skewering, Pulitzer-Winning Cartoonist, Dies at 71
abstract: With national reach, he won the prize in 1993 and was a finalist for it four times while at The Arizona Republic. Some of his work rankled his own Mormon community.

name: Martin Cruz Smith
headline: Martin Cruz Smith, Best-Selling Author of ‘Gorky Park,’ Dies at 82
abstract: He startled critics, readers and the book industry in 1981 with a novel set in the Soviet Union that had a flawed detective as its antihero.

name: Henry Raymont
profession: First to Report Bay of Pigs Invasion
headline: Henry Raymont, First to Report Bay of Pigs Invasion, Dies at 98
abstract: On assignment for U.P.I. in Cuba, he learned of the U.S.- backed effort to overthrow Fidel Castro and was imprisoned. He later worked for The New York Times.

name: Paulette Jiles
profession: Novelist Evoked the West in News of the World
headline: Paulette Jiles, 82, Dies; Novelist Evoked the West in ‘News of the World’
abstract: A poet and memoirist as well, she drew a wide readership with her historical fiction, notably with a post-Civil War tale that was adapted for a movie starring Tom Hanks.

name: Connie Francis
headline: Connie Francis, Whose Ballads Dominated ’60s Pop Music, Dies at 87
abstract: From 1958 to 1964, she was the most popular female singer in the United States, selling 40 million records with tunes like “Who’s Sorry Now” and “Where the Boys Are.”

name: Sol Stern
headline: Sol Stern, Lapsed Liberal and Conservative Heretic, Dies at 89
abstract: A writer, editor and political adviser, he broke with the left over its criticism of Israel and what he saw as its anti-Americanism. But he also became a critic of Donald Trump.

name: John Conklin
headline: John Conklin, Who Created Fantastical Opera Sets, Dies at 88
abstract: Realizing a childhood dream, he created scenery that was highly conceptual yet playful for the Glimmerglass Festival, New York City Opera and other companies.

name: Alan Bergman
profession: Half of a Prolific Lyric-Writing Team
headline: Alan Bergman, Half of a Prolific Lyric-Writing Team, Dies at 99
abstract: With his wife, Marilyn, he wrote the words to memorable TV theme songs and the Oscar-winning “The Way We Were” and “The Windmills of Your Mind.”

name: Felix Baumgartner
headline: Felix Baumgartner, 56, Professional Daredevil, Dies While Paragliding
abstract: Nicknamed “Fearless Felix,” he jumped from the edge of space in 2012.

name: Martin Izquierdo
headline: Martin Izquierdo, 83, Dies; Costume Designer Who Specialized in Wings
abstract: His work was seen in “Angels in America” and Victoria’s Secret runway shows. He also made outlandish ensembles for Heidi Klum and Marc Jacobs.

name: Jewel Thais-Williams
headline: Jewel Thais-Williams, Whose Nightclub Celebrated ‘Queer Black Joy,’ Dies at 86
abstract: Catch One, which she opened in Los Angeles in 1973 in the face of local animosity, became a glittering sanctuary for a largely shunned community.

name: Robert Alvarez
headline: Robert Alvarez, 76, Dies; Called Attention to Nuclear-Waste Safety
abstract: A self-taught expert, he spent decades working in both nonprofits and the government to expose problems in the production of atomic weapons.

name: Bill Dellinger
headline: Bill Dellinger, Runner and Track Coach Who Mentored Stars, Dies at 91
abstract: After running the 5,000 meters in three Olympics, he coached the likes of Steve Prefontaine and Joaquim Cruz at his alma mater, the University of Oregon.

name: Peter Phillips
profession: Was at the British Pop Art Frontier
headline: Peter Phillips, Who Was at the British Pop Art Frontier, Dies at 86
abstract: Known as the tough guy in a scene that produced David Hockney and others, he filled his paintings with gleaming car parts and sex symbols. Some of them landed on album covers.

name: Roger Norrington
headline: Roger Norrington, Iconoclastic British Conductor, Dies at 91
abstract: His work, largely unknown outside Britain until late in his career, was often based on historical treatises. It was seen by many as refreshingly innovative.

name: Polina Gelman
headline: Overlooked No More: Polina Gelman: Fearless ‘Night Witch’ Who Haunted Nazi Troops
abstract: She was a navigator with an all-female unit of Soviet aviators who attacked German troops at night, whooshing in wooden planes like witches on broomsticks.

name: Kenneth Colley
profession: Star Wars Actor With a Commanding Presence
headline: Kenneth Colley, 87, ‘Star Wars’ Actor With a Commanding Presence, Dies
abstract: A fixture onscreen and onstage, he became a fan favorite as Darth Vader’s ally, Admiral Piett, in “The Empire Strikes Back” and “Return of the Jedi.”

name: Jake Larson
headline: Jake Larson, D-Day Veteran and TikTok Star, Dies at 102
abstract: Mr. Larson, the last survivor of a unit that stormed Omaha Beach in 1944, shared his memories on social media where he amassed a wide following.

name: Jean-Pierre Azéma
headline: Jean-Pierre Azéma, 87, Dies; Chronicled French Collaboration With Nazis
abstract: He was among the historians who challenged national myths about the compromises his country made after being occupied by Germany in World War II.

name: Edwin Feulner
headline: Edwin Feulner, Heritage Foundation’s ‘George Washington,’ Dies at 83
abstract: As co-founder and longtime head of the conservative Washington think tank, he picked policies and staffers for G.O.P. presidents from Reagan to Trump.

name: William L. Clay
headline: William L. Clay, Missouri’s First Black Congressman, Dies at 94
abstract: A co-founder of the Congressional Black Caucus, he represented St. Louis in the House as an uncompromising liberal Democrat and advocate for the poor.

name: Malcolm-Jamal Warner
profession: Theo Huxtable on The Cosby Show
headline: Malcolm-Jamal Warner, Theo Huxtable on ‘The Cosby Show,’ Dies at 54
abstract: Mr. Warner, who played the only son of Bill Cosby’s character on the beloved 1980s sitcom, drowned in Costa Rica.

name: Ozzy Osbourne
profession: Prince of Darkness Turned Reality TV Star
headline: Ozzy Osbourne, ‘Prince of Darkness’ Turned Reality TV Star, Dies at 76
abstract: As the lead singer of Black Sabbath, he helped invent heavy metal. On “The Osbournes,” he presented a comedic counterpoint to his rock ’n’ roll infamy.

name: Sarah Morlok Cotton
headline: Sarah Morlok Cotton, Quadruplet Who Knew Fame and Suffering, Dies at 95
abstract: She was the last of four sisters who became a Depression-era sensation, performing onstage. Offstage, they endured abuse and were studied for their schizophrenia.

name: William H. Neukom
headline: William H. Neukom, Microsoft Lawyer Who Led Antitrust Fight, Dies at 83
abstract: In the 1990s, the U.S. called Microsoft a bullying monopoly and sought to rein it in. The company lost in a landmark decision, but emerged intact.

name: Jack McAuliffe
headline: Jack McAuliffe, Who Brewed a Craft Beer Revolution, Dies at 80
abstract: His New Albion Brewing Company, founded in 1976, was considered the first microbrewery. It set the model for thousands more to come.

name: Zelig Eshhar
profession: Engineered Immune Cells to Fight Cancer
headline: Zelig Eshhar, Who Engineered Immune Cells to Fight Cancer, Dies at 84
abstract: He made a conceptual leap in immunotherapy by creating a hybrid T-cell, known as CAR-T, that was genetically modified to destroy cancer cells.

name: Gilda Cruz-Romo
headline: Gilda Cruz-Romo, Soprano Celebrated for Her Power, Dies at 85
abstract: Critics praised the natural way she used her voice to inject character into her roles. She had, one wrote, a sound “perfect for Verdi and Puccini.”

name: Eileen Fulton
profession: Glamorous Villainess of As the World Turns
headline: Eileen Fulton, Glamorous Villainess of ‘As the World Turns,’ Dies at 91
abstract: She was a mainstay of the long-running soap opera for 50 years — so long that she liked to say she led a double life.

name: Joanna Macy
profession: Found a Way to Transcend Eco-Anxiety
headline: Joanna Macy, Who Found a Way to Transcend ‘Eco-Anxiety,’ Dies at 96
abstract: With books and workshops, she helped others deal with the stress caused by climate change, inspiring them to take action and not be paralyzed by despair.

name: Thomas A. Durkin
profession: Civil Liberties Lawyer for the Reviled
headline: Thomas A. Durkin, Civil Liberties Lawyer for the Reviled, Dies at 78
abstract: He relished skewering the U.S. government as he represented unpopular defendants in public corruption and national security cases, like those at Guantánamo.

name: Hulk Hogan
headline: Hulk Hogan, Shirt-Shredding Superstar of Pro Wrestling, Dies at 71
abstract: The charismatic wrestler helped build an entertainment on the margins into a cultural behemoth.

name: Chuck Mangione
profession: Smooth Jazz Hitmaker With a Fluegelhorn
headline: Chuck Mangione, a ‘Smooth Jazz’ Hitmaker With a Fluegelhorn, Dies at 84
abstract: In his signature fedora, he gained wide popularity and 14 Grammy nominations, winning the award twice, while scaling Billboard’s charts in the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Roy Black
profession: Defense Lawyer for William Kennedy Smith and Epstein
headline: Roy Black, Defense Lawyer for William Kennedy Smith and Epstein, Dies at 80
abstract: With a national profile, he represented the notorious and the celebrated, helping to secure an acquittal in the Smith rape case and a lenient plea deal for Jeffrey Epstein.

name: Shunsaku Tamiya
headline: Shunsaku Tamiya, Who Brought Perfection to Plastic Models, Dies at 90
abstract: He turned his family’s lumber business into a manufacturer of model kits that won global popularity for their quality and historical accuracy.

name: Joe Vigil
headline: Joe Vigil, Running Coach Who Shaped Champions, Dies at 95
abstract: He turned Adams State University in Colorado into a distance-running powerhouse and helped mentor two marathon medalists at the 2004 Athens Olympics.

name: Cleo Laine
profession: Grammy-Winning Jazz Singer With a Broadway Turn
headline: Cleo Laine, Grammy-Winning Jazz Singer With a Broadway Turn, Dies at 97
abstract: A Briton with a smoky voice, she recorded albums across six decades, toured the world and acted in “Edwin Drood.”

name: Gary Smith
headline: Gary Smith, TV Producer Who Put a Spotlight on Stars, Dies at 90
abstract: A multiple Emmy winner, he helped create sophisticated shows for the likes of Barbra Streisand, Elvis Presley, Mikhail Baryshnikov, Ben Vereen, Burt Bacharach and Bette Midler.

name: Patrick Ryan
headline: Patrick Ryan, ‘Terror Priest’ Who Aided the I.R.A., Is Dead at 94
abstract: He funneled cash and weapons to the Irish Republican Army from Libya, and was involved in bombings that targeted Margaret Thatcher and others, killing scores of people.

name: Rex White
profession: Hailed as One of NASCARs Greatest Drivers
headline: Rex White, Hailed as One of NASCAR’s Greatest Drivers, Dies at 95
abstract: He dealt with the aftereffects of polio to become a prolific winner in the Grand National Series (now the NASCAR Cup) in the 1950s and ’60s.

name: James Leprino
headline: James Leprino, ‘Willy Wonka of Cheese’ Who Revolutionized Pizza, Dies at 87
abstract: He turned a small family grocery store into a mozzarella empire, producing most of the cheese for American pizza chains like Domino’s, Papa Johns and Pizza Hut.

name: William J. Rutter
headline: William J. Rutter, Biotech Pioneer of Gene-Based Medicine, Dies at 97
abstract: His company, the Chiron Corporation, contributed important scientific discoveries toward treatments for H.I.V., hepatitis B, diabetes and more.

name: Raymond Saunders
headline: Raymond Saunders, Painter Who Rejected Racial Pigeonholes, Dies at 90
abstract: Widely admired if long underrecognized for his collage-based art, he died only days after the closing of his first retrospective at a major museum, in his native Pittsburgh.

name: Tom Lehrer
profession: Musical Satirist With a Dark Streak
headline: Tom Lehrer, Musical Satirist With a Dark Streak, Dies at 97
abstract: A mathematician by training, he acquired a devoted following with songs that set sardonic lyrics to music that was often maddeningly cheerful.

name: Joan Anderson
profession: Unsung Heroine of Hula Hoop History
headline: Joan Anderson, Unsung Heroine of Hula Hoop History, Dies at 101
abstract: Because of a deal made on a handshake in a parking lot, she was long left out of a famous toy’s story. When she was 94, a documentary changed that.

name: Ziad Rahbani
headline: Ziad Rahbani, Composer Who Defined a Tragic Era in Lebanon, Dies at 69
abstract: A son of Lebanese musical icons, he became one himself, with satirical critiques of his country’s dysfunction that melded Arab and Western music.

name: Michael Ochs
profession: Top Collector of Rock n Roll Photos
headline: Michael Ochs, Top Collector of Rock ’n’ Roll Photos, Dies at 82
abstract: He surveyed the trash of record companies, haggled with aging photographers and scoured estate sales, building an archive widely seen as unmatched.

name: Wallis Annenberg
headline: Wallis Annenberg, Arts and Wildlife Philanthropist, Dies at 86
abstract: She put millions from her foundation into projects in California, like a performing arts center in Beverly Hills and a wildlife crossing over the busy 101 freeway.

name: Thomas Sayers Ellis
headline: Thomas Sayers Ellis, Poet of ‘Percussive Prosody,’ Dies at 61
abstract: A verbal gymnast on and off the page (as well as a musician and photographer), he was a founder of the Dark Room Collective, a community of writers, and fostered a boom in Black poetry.

name: John Saladino
profession: Sensualist Designer With a Love of Ruins
headline: John Saladino, ‘Sensualist’ Designer With a Love of Ruins, Dies at 86
abstract: A renowned interior designer, he created instantly recognizable rooms using lush fabrics, oversize antiques and imperfectly plastered walls that convey a sense of age.

name: Ryne Sandberg
profession: Hall of Fame Second Baseman for the Cubs
headline: Ryne Sandberg, Hall of Fame Second Baseman for the Cubs, Dies at 65
abstract: Both a skilled fielder and a fearsome power hitter, he entered the national sports spotlight with two memorable home runs in a nationally televised 1984 game.

name: Gary Karr
headline: Gary Karr, Virtuoso Who Elevated the Double-Bass, Dies at 83
abstract: He made the cumbersome bass soar, sing and leap, and became one of few bassists in history to successfully pursue a career outside an orchestra.

name: Morton Mintz
headline: Morton Mintz, Muckraking Crusader for Consumers, Dies at 103
abstract: As a longtime Washington Post reporter and an author of 10 books, he held corporate America accountable for safe pharmaceuticals and cars.

name: Dwight Muhammad Qawi
profession: Boxing Champ Got His Start in Prison
headline: Dwight Muhammad Qawi, 72, Dies; Boxing Champ Got His Start in Prison
abstract: After joining a boxing program while incarcerated, he emerged a contender in the pro ranks, winning titles in two weight classes in the 1980s.

name: Horst Mahler
profession: Voice of the German Far Left, Then the Far Right
headline: Horst Mahler, 89, Dies; Voice of the German Far Left, Then the Far Right
abstract: As a young lawyer and a Communist revolutionary, he helped start the violent Red Army Faction. Later, he went to prison as a Nazi apologist and Holocaust denier.

name: Rose Leiman Goldemberg
profession: Her Burning Bed Was a TV Benchmark
headline: Rose Leiman Goldemberg, 97, Dies; Her ‘Burning Bed’ Was a TV Benchmark
abstract: A playwright and screenwriter, she adapted a book about domestic abuse for NBC, bringing a taboo subject into the national conversation.

name: David Nabarro
profession: Grappled Globally With Ebola and Covid
headline: David Nabarro Dies at 75; Grappled Globally With Ebola and Covid
abstract: At the U.N., he took on some of the world’s most challenging health crises in troubled areas, skillfully coordinating international efforts to reduce the spread of disease

name: Mary Gaillard
profession: Broke a Ceiling in Subatomic Research
headline: Mary Gaillard, Who Broke a Ceiling in Subatomic Research, Dies at 86
abstract: Overcoming discrimination in a mostly male preserve, she did groundbreaking work that showed experimentalist physicists where and how to look for new particles.

name: Cécile Dionne
profession: Found Fame and Despair as a Quintuplet
headline: Cécile Dionne, Who Found Fame and Despair as a Quintuplet, Dies at 91
abstract: The Dionnes, the first quints known to have survived infancy, became a global sensation and prey for the greedy. And Cécile came to resent it all. Only one of the five now survives.

name: Derk Sauer
profession: Champion of Free Press in a New Russia
headline: Derk Sauer, Champion of Free Press in a New Russia, Dies at 72
abstract: He earned a media fortune in the freewheeling but chaotic Russia of the 1990s and defended press freedoms after the industry became beleaguered and unprofitable.

name: Ross Rowland
profession: Railroad Preservationist by Way of Wall St
headline: Ross Rowland, 85, Dies; a Railroad Preservationist by Way of Wall St.
abstract: He made a fortune as a commodities broker, then used his wealth to back the American Freedom Train and other high-profile vintage excursions.

name: Michael Cardozo
profession: New York Citys Longest-Serving Chief Lawyer
headline: Michael Cardozo, 84, New York City’s Longest-Serving Chief Lawyer, Dies
abstract: As the city’s corporation counsel under Mayor Michael Bloomberg, he defended stop-and-frisk policing and a ban on smoking in bars and restaurants.

name: Flaco Jiménez
profession: Grammy-Winning Master of the Tex-Mex Accordion
headline: Flaco Jiménez, 86, Grammy-Winning Master of the Tex-Mex Accordion, Dies
abstract: Fusing traditional Tejano sounds with blues, rock and country, he recorded with Bob Dylan, the Rolling Stones and Ry Cooder.

name: Jeannie Seely
profession: Pushed Boundaries at the Grand Ole Opry
headline: Jeannie Seely, Who Pushed Boundaries at the Grand Ole Opry, Dies at 85
abstract: She blazed a trail for women in country music with the candor of her songs and her bold fashion sense. She was the first woman to host a segment on the Opry.

name: David Rendall
headline: David Rendall, Tenor Who Suffered Operatic Mishaps, Dies at 76
abstract: He appeared regularly at the Metropolitan Opera and sang in major European opera houses, but a stage accident in 2005 nearly ended his career.

name: Sandra Grimes
headline: Sandra Grimes, Who Helped Unmask a C.I.A. Traitor, Dies at 79
abstract: She became suspicious when she discovered large deposits in the bank account of Aldrich Ames, whose betrayal cost the lives of at least eight double agents.

name: Ann Harris
profession: Edited a Stack of Best Sellers
headline: Ann Harris, Who Edited a Stack of Best Sellers, Dies at 99
abstract: Her hits included “The Exorcist” and “The Thorn Birds,” as well as the autobiography of Betty Ford and an authorized biography of Warren Buffett.

name: Rahaman Ali
headline: Rahaman Ali, Boxer Whose Brother Was ‘the Greatest,’ Dies at 82
abstract: Some said he had shown nearly as much promise in the ring as Muhammad Ali. But he gave up his own career to join the champ’s entourage.

name: Loni Anderson
headline: Loni Anderson, Star of ‘WKRP in Cincinnati,’ Dies at 79
abstract: She won Emmy nominations for her sitcom role as a deceptively smart radio station receptionist. Her divorce from Burt Reynolds landed her in the tabloids.

name: Razia Jan
profession: Built an Enduring Girls School in Afghanistan
headline: Razia Jan, 81, Who Built an Enduring Girls’ School in Afghanistan, Dies
abstract: Before 9/11, she ran a dry cleaning business in Massachusetts; in the aftermath, she returned home after decades away to educate young girls.

name: Stella Rimington
profession: First Woman to Lead U.K.s MI5
headline: Stella Rimington, First Woman to Lead U.K.’s MI5, Dies at 90
abstract: Widely regarded as the inspiration for the recast of the James Bond character “M,” she was the first British spy chief to be publicly named and photographed.

name: Ion Iliescu
headline: Ion Iliescu, Who Steered Romania After Revolution, Dies at 95
abstract: As a three-term president, he guided the country toward democracy, but he was called an authoritarian at heart and accused of brutality during the revolt that put him in power.

name: Allan Ahlberg
profession: Teamed With Wife on Acclaimed Childrens Books
headline: Allan Ahlberg, 87, Dies; Teamed With Wife on Acclaimed Children’s Books
abstract: Over five decades, he produced some 150 books, many of them illustrated by Janet Ahlberg, including classics like “Each Peach Pear Plum.”

name: Leonard Lopate
headline: Leonard Lopate, Longtime New York Radio Host, Dies at 84
abstract: He mastered the art of the interview over 32 years on public radio, at WNYC. He was fired in 2017 amid allegations of sexual harassment, which he vehemently denied.

name: Joseph Lovett
headline: Joseph Lovett, TV Producer Who Shed an Early Light on AIDS, Dies at 80
abstract: At CBS and ABC, he pursued news segments aimed at destigmatizing gay life and drawing attention to an epidemic that at the time was largely overlooked.

name: Lawrence A. Bossidy
headline: Lawrence A. Bossidy, Who Led a Major Corporate Turnaround, Dies at 90
abstract: He took over the reins of the troubled Allied Signal in 1991 and within a few years made it one of America’s best-run and most profitable companies.

name: Eddie Palmieri
headline: Eddie Palmieri, Latin Music’s Dynamic Innovator, Dies at 88
abstract: He roped salsa into conversation with jazz, rock, funk and even modern classical music. “A new world music,” one critic said, “is being born.”

name: U Myint Swe
profession: Acting President of Myanmar Installed by Military
headline: U Myint Swe, 74, Acting President of Myanmar Installed by Military, Dies
abstract: A figurehead leader, he had little real power but did endorse measures that allowed the country’s generals to extend their rule after a 2021 coup.

name: Sallie Bingham
profession: Author at the Center of a Newspaper Drama
headline: Sallie Bingham, Author at the Center of a Newspaper Drama, Dies at 88
abstract: A novelist and memoirist, she famously clashed with her brother, leading to the fall of a Kentucky publishing dynasty that her paternal grandfather established in 1918.

name: Linda Hodes
headline: Linda Hodes, Dancer Who Championed Martha Graham’s Vision, Dies at 94
abstract: Her connection to the great modern dancer lasted a lifetime, from studying with her as a child to leading the Martha Graham Dance Company as an artistic director.

name: Michael Lydon
headline: Michael Lydon, Writer Who Rocked With the 1960s, Dies at 82
abstract: A founding editor of Rolling Stone and a seasoned music journalist, he spent time with the Beatles and toured with the Grateful Dead and the Rolling Stones.

name: Nicholas Clapp
profession: Real-Life Indiana Jones Pursued a Lost City
headline: Nicholas Clapp, 89, Dies; ‘Real-Life Indiana Jones’ Pursued a Lost City
abstract: A documentary filmmaker and amateur archaeologist, he was consumed by the desire to find an ancient city in the Arabian desert known as Atlantis of the Sands.

name: Robert Pursley
profession: Pentagon Aide Became Critic of Vietnam War
headline: Robert Pursley, 97, Dies; Pentagon Aide Became Critic of Vietnam War
abstract: He advised three defense secretaries, beginning with Robert McNamara, until the Nixon White House started tapping his phones. He retired as a three-star Air Force general.

name: Ángel Macías
headline: Ángel Macías, 1957 Little League World Series Star, Dies at 80
abstract: Playing for a team from Monterrey, Mexico, he pitched a perfect game in the event’s championship game, the first and only time that has happened.

name: Jane Morgan
headline: Jane Morgan, Singer Who Charmed Both Sides of the Atlantic, Dies at 101
abstract: Born in Massachusetts, she built a following in Parisian nightclubs before returning to the U.S., where she had a successful career as a torch singer.

name: James A. Lovell Jr.
headline: James A. Lovell Jr., Commander of Apollo 13, Is Dead at 97
abstract: He led the three-man crew that survived a near catastrophic explosion in space in 1970, and was later immortalized by Tom Hanks in the movie “Apollo 13.”

name: William H. Webster
profession: Ran Both the F.B.I. and the C.I.A
headline: William H. Webster, Who Ran Both the F.B.I. and the C.I.A., Dies at 101
abstract: A former federal judge, he first came to the F.B.I. just as two of the worst spies in American history were running rampant.

name: Don Elbaum
profession: Audacious Boxing Promoter and Heavyweight Raconteur
headline: Don Elbaum, Audacious Boxing Promoter and Heavyweight Raconteur, Dies at 94
abstract: He briefly mentored Don King and promoted fighters both well-known (like Muhammad Ali and Sugar Ray Robinson) and obscure.

name: Morton Meyerson
headline: Morton Meyerson, Texas Businessman and Perot Lieutenant, Dies at 87
abstract: He helped build H. Ross Perot’s company Electronic Data Systems into a leading data processing firm. He later played a crucial role in Mr. Perot’s 1992 presidential campaign.

name: Terry Reid
headline: Terry Reid, Rock Singer Known as ‘Superlungs,’ Dies at 75
abstract: He missed his chance to be Led Zeppelin’s lead vocalist, but his solo work — and his otherworldly voice — drew raves from Aretha Franklin and others.

name: Lloyd Williams
headline: Lloyd Williams, Who Helped Spur Harlem’s Revival, Dies at 80
abstract: As head of the area’s Chamber of Commerce, he capitalized on the community’s heritage to promote economic development.

name: Christophe de Menil
headline: Christophe de Menil, Art Patron and Designer, Is Dead at 92
abstract: A Parisian-born oil heiress, she collected art and supported major artists, designed costumes and moved in rarefied social and cultural circles.

name: Sheila Jordan
headline: Sheila Jordan, Fearless Vocal Improviser, Is Dead at 96
abstract: She was revered in the jazz world as a chance taker who communicated an effervescent joy in the pure act of singing.

name: T.S. Ellis III
headline: Judge T.S. Ellis III, 85, Dies; Stirred Outcry Over Manafort Sentence
abstract: He imposed a 47-month prison term on Mr. Trump’s former campaign chairman, who was convicted of fraud. Sentencing guidelines recommended up to 24 years.

name: David Mazzarella
headline: David Mazzarella, Editor Who Helped Reshape USA Today, Dies at 87
abstract: For five years, he honed the paper’s focus on hard news and enterprising journalism, distancing it from its reputation for fluffy, bite-sized stories.

name: Danielle Spencer
headline: Danielle Spencer, Child Star of ‘What’s Happening!!,’ Is Dead at 60
abstract: She played a witty teenager on one of the first American television shows that centered on young Black people.

name: Mario Paglino
headline: Mario Paglino, 52, and Gianni Grossi, 54, Die; Designers Made Barbies Into Art
abstract: They transformed dolls into one-of-a-kind pieces that sold for thousands of dollars. A married couple, they died in a car crash in Italy.

name: Leonard Tow
profession: Cable TV Magnate and a Major Philanthropist
headline: Leonard Tow, Cable TV Magnate and a Major Philanthropist, Dies at 97
abstract: Once on the Forbes 400 list of richest Americans, he donated substantially to the arts, higher education, hospitals and criminal justice reform.

name: Billy Howton
profession: Top Green Bay Packers Receiver in the 50s
headline: Billy Howton, Top Green Bay Packers Receiver in the ’50s, Dies at 95
abstract: He retired as the N.F.L.’s leading career receiver but was soon surpassed. In retirement, he went to prison for bilking investors in an $8 million fraud.

name: Molly Drake
profession: Maternal Musical Force Behind Nick Drakes Sound
headline: Overlooked No More: Molly Drake, a Maternal Musical Force Behind Nick Drake’s Sound
abstract: She was a poet, singer, composer and pianist whose melancholic home recordings from the 1950s hit on universal themes of despair, heartbreak, longing and loss.

name: Bobby Whitlock
profession: Keyboardist for Derek and the Dominos
headline: Bobby Whitlock, Keyboardist for Derek and the Dominos, Dies at 77
abstract: With Eric Clapton, he wrote “Bell Bottom Blues” and built one of the greatest — if most short-lived — supergroups of the 1970s.

name: Margaret Boden
headline: Margaret Boden, Philosopher of Artificial Intelligence, Dies at 88
abstract: A cognitive scientist, she used the language of computers to explore the nature of human thought and creativity, offering prescient insights about A.I.

name: Gregory C. O’Connell
headline: Gregory C. O’Connell, Developer Who Revived Red Hook, Dies at 83
abstract: A former N.Y.P.D. detective, he rejuvenated properties on the Brooklyn waterfront and restored a historic village in upstate New York.

name: Gerry Spence
headline: Gerry Spence, a Canny Courtroom Showman in Buckskin, Dies at 96
abstract: Calling himself America’s best trial lawyer, he won justice for Karen Silkwood and successfully defended Imelda Marcos. He also wrote best sellers.

name: Jackie Bezos
profession: Jeff Bezos Mother and an Early Amazon Investor
headline: Jackie Bezos, Jeff Bezos’ Mother and an Early Amazon Investor, Dies at 78
abstract: Ms. Bezos and her husband invested about $245,000 in Amazon when the online bookstore was in its first year.

name: Masaoki Sen
profession: Ex-Kamikaze Pilot and Tea Ceremony Diplomat
headline: Masaoki Sen, Ex-Kamikaze Pilot and ‘Tea Ceremony Diplomat,’ Dies at 102
abstract: Spared from flying a suicide mission in World War II, he became a grandmaster of Japan’s venerable tea ceremony and used his stature to speak out against all wars.

name: Robin Lakoff
headline: Robin Lakoff, Expert on Language and Gender, Is Dead at 82
abstract: In arguing that language enforces the power imbalance between the sexes, she inspired an entire academic field.

name: Frank Savage
profession: Business Leader Entangled in Enron Scandal
headline: Frank Savage, 87, Business Leader Entangled in Enron Scandal, Is Dead
abstract: He was one of the relatively few Black Americans to reach the upper echelons of global finance. He was also a competitive sailor.

name: Tommy McLain
headline: Tommy McLain, the King of Swamp Pop, Dies at 85
abstract: Playing a blend of rock, R&B and zydeco, he had a hit in 1966 with “Sweet Dreams” and inspired Elvis Costello, Nick Lowe and many others.

name: Doris Lockhart Saatchi
profession: Critic and Collector of Cutting-Edge Art
headline: Doris Lockhart Saatchi, 88, Critic and Collector of Cutting-Edge Art, Dies
abstract: With her husband, Charles Saatchi, she assembled one of the world’s top collections of contemporary art, featuring works by Andy Warhol, Julian Schnabel, Cy Twombly and many others.

name: Tristan Rogers
headline: Tristan Rogers, ‘General Hospital’ Actor, Dies at 79
abstract: He became a fixture on the popular daytime television show as Robert Scorpio, a spy who became a police commissioner.

name: Joel DeMott
profession: Lauded Documentary Was Rejected by PBS
headline: Joel DeMott, Whose Lauded Documentary Was Rejected by PBS, Dies at 78
abstract: Her “Seventeen,” a study of teenagers later recognized as a major work of cinéma vérité, was pulled from a public TV series in 1982 under pressure from its sponsor.

name: Terence Stamp
profession: British Cinema Luminary and Superman Villain
headline: Terence Stamp, 87, Dies; British Cinema Luminary and ‘Superman’ Villain
