abstract: Known for his “heartbreak blue eyes,” he also starred in “Billy Budd” and “The Collector” and had a memorable role in “The Adventures of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert.”

name: Joe Caroff
profession: Gave James Bond His Signature 007 Logo
headline: Joe Caroff, Who Gave James Bond His Signature 007 Logo, Dies at 103
abstract: A quiet giant in graphic design, he created posters for hundreds of movies, including “West Side Story” and “A Hard Day’s Night.” But his work was often unsigned.

name: Ronnie Rondell
profession: Stuntman Set on Fire for Pink Floyd Cover
headline: Ronnie Rondell, Stuntman Set on Fire for Pink Floyd Cover, Dies at 88
abstract: He was also known for his performances in “Twister” and “The Matrix Reloaded,” and came from a family of stunt performers.

name: Dan Tana
headline: Dan Tana, Whose Clubby Red-Sauce Restaurant Drew Stars, Dies at 90
abstract: Dan Tana’s was said to be as central to Hollywood as palm trees and Botox. On a scale of 1 to 10, the people watching was a 10. Even the steak came with pasta.

name: Jules Witcover
headline: Jules Witcover, Political Reporter and Columnist, Dies at 98
abstract: A journalist of the old school, he covered presidential races and political affairs for several newspapers and in many books, as well as in a long-running column, “Politics Today.”

name: Mike Castle
headline: Mike Castle, Bipartisan Delaware Congressman, Dies at 86
abstract: A fiscal conservative who supported gun control and other liberal causes, he was the last Republican elected to serve his state as governor and to represent it in the House.

name: Rodrigo Moya
profession: Photographed Che and a Changing Latin America
headline: Rodrigo Moya, 91, Dies; Photographed Che and a Changing Latin America
abstract: He documented poverty and protest in the 1950s and ’60s, and he created indelible images of Che Guevara and Gabriel García Márquez.

name: Warren Brodey
profession: Visionary at the Dawn of the Information Age
headline: Warren Brodey, 101, Dies; a Visionary at the Dawn of the Information Age
abstract: His work on complex systems and responsive technologies helped lay the groundwork for later work on artificial intelligence.

name: John Cruickshank
profession: Last World War II Victoria Cross Recipient
headline: John Cruickshank, 105, Dies; Last World War II Victoria Cross Recipient
abstract: He made a daring raid on a U-boat, suffered 72 wounds and helped land his damaged seaplane.

name: Stephanie Shirley
profession: Created a Tech World for Women
headline: Stephanie Shirley, Who Created a Tech World for Women, Dies at 91
abstract: In 1962, she started a software company at her dining room table with a revolutionary idea: to create a place where women could find a work-life balance.

name: Bruce Slovin
profession: Unified Jewish Archives in New York
headline: Bruce Slovin, Who Unified Jewish Archives in New York, Dies at 89
abstract: A corporate executive who specialized in mergers, he brought together five Jewish institutions and their collections at the Center for Jewish History in Manhattan.

name: James Dobson
profession: Influential Leader of the Religious Right
headline: James Dobson, Influential Leader of the Religious Right, Dies at 89
abstract: The founder of the evangelical group Focus on the Family, he spent decades denouncing what he saw as the unraveling of the social order.

name: Sonallah Ibrahim
profession: Egyptian Novelist of Irony and Dissent
headline: Sonallah Ibrahim, Egyptian Novelist of Irony and Dissent, Dies at 88
abstract: Starting with “That Smell” in 1966, he wrote with stark power about themes of repression in the Egyptian police state.

name: Frank Caprio
profession: Kind Judge on Rhode Island TV
headline: Frank Caprio, Kind Judge on Rhode Island TV, Dies at 88
abstract: A longtime municipal judge, he became a social media star for “Caught in Providence,” which viewers said showed his compassion in the courtroom.

name: Shelly Zegart
profession: Stitched Quilting to History and Art
headline: Shelly Zegart, Who Stitched Quilting to History and Art, Dies at 84
abstract: She was a pivotal figure in linking quilts to the American experience — although she herself never stitched so much as a sweater in her life.

name: Greg Iles
headline: Greg Iles, Novelist Who Wrote About Race in Mississippi, Dies at 65
abstract: In his best-selling books, notably the “Natchez Burning” trilogy, he addressed what one reviewer called “the pervasive impact of past events.”

name: Tiébilé Dramé
headline: Tiébilé Dramé, Voice for Rights in Mali, Is Dead at 70
abstract: A former foreign minister, he founded an opposition political party and then served in the government as an unflagging negotiator with northern rebels.

name: Ron Turcotte
profession: Rode Secretariat to the Triple Crown
headline: Ron Turcotte, Who Rode Secretariat to the Triple Crown, Dies at 84
abstract: With Turcotte in the saddle, Secretariat powered to victory in the Kentucky Derby and the Preakness in 1973 and then demolished the competition in the Belmont Stakes.

name: Chris Doyle
headline: Chris Doyle, Artist Who Brought the Inanimate to Life, Dies at 66
abstract: He used animation and other media to create worlds inhabited by anthropomorphic machines and industrious creatures. One curator described his work as “Narnia on acid.”

name: Theodore Friedman
headline: Theodore Friedman, Lawyer Who Triumphed Over Disbarment, Dies at 94
abstract: A zealous New York personal injury lawyer, he won many news-making cases before his professional fall. He was reinstated after 16 years.

name: David Ketchum
profession: Played a Cooped-Up Agent on Get Smart
headline: David Ketchum, Who Played a Cooped-Up Agent on ‘Get Smart,’ Dies at 97
abstract: He was frequently crammed into airport lockers, popcorn machines and grandfather clocks as Agent 13, the long-suffering spy.

name: Humpy Wheeler
headline: Humpy Wheeler, NASCAR’s Greatest Showman, Dies at 86
abstract: With fire-breathing robots and death-defying school-bus stunts, he brought spectacle to stock-car racing as the sport boomed in the 1970s and beyond.

name: Ozzie Rodriguez
profession: Off Off Broadway Mainstay and Archivist
headline: Ozzie Rodriguez, Off Off Broadway Mainstay and Archivist, Dies at 81
abstract: An actor, director and playwright for La MaMa Experimental Theater Club, he later found an even more distinct role: curating its vast archive.

name: Starling Lawrence
headline: Starling Lawrence, Editor Who Uncovered Best Sellers, Dies at 82
abstract: He discovered and nurtured Michael Lewis, Sebastian Junger and many other authors. He had, Mr. Lewis said, “the storytelling equivalent of perfect pitch.”

name: Annie Stainer
headline: Annie Stainer, 79, Dies; Enigmatic Mime Who Performed With David Bowie
abstract: She later became a powerful solo artist in her own right, creating a dance trilogy steeped in myth and feminine archetypes.

name: Lionel Taylor
profession: Elite Receiver in A.F.L.s Early Days
headline: Lionel Taylor, Elite Receiver in A.F.L.’s Early Days, Dies at 89
abstract: He caught 100 passes for the Denver Broncos in 1961, setting a record. As a wide receivers coach, he helped the Pittsburgh Steelers win two Super Bowls.

name: Maurice Tempelsman
profession: Diamond Magnate and Jackie Onassiss Companion
headline: Maurice Tempelsman, Diamond Magnate and Jackie Onassis’s Companion, Dies at 95
abstract: A private and politically connected gem merchant, he was thrust into the public spotlight when his personal relationship with the former first lady became known in the late 1980s.

name: Sheila R. Canby
headline: Sheila R. Canby, Curator at the Met Who Humanized Islam, Dies at 76
abstract: In overseeing the expansion of the Islamic art galleries at the Metropolitan Museum, she countered hostile narratives about the Muslim world that arose after 9/11.

name: Joe Hickerson
profession: Helped Preserve Americas Folk Song Tradition
headline: Joe Hickerson, 89, Dies; Helped Preserve America’s Folk Song Tradition
abstract: He was both the longtime archivist of folk music at the Library of Congress and a widely respected singer and songwriter.

name: Rainer Weiss
profession: Gave a Nod to Einstein and the Big Bang
headline: Rainer Weiss, Who Gave a Nod to Einstein and the Big Bang, Dies at 92
abstract: He shared the Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on gravitational waves, which helped confirm Einstein’s general theory of relativity and how the universe began.

name: Donald McPherson
profession: Naval Fighter Ace in World War II
headline: Donald McPherson, Naval Fighter Ace in World War II, Dies at 103
abstract: One of the last surviving combat aces from the war, he took down five Japanese aircraft and helped save a destroyer during the Battle of Okinawa.

name: Angela Mortimer
headline: Angela Mortimer, Tennis Champion Who Overcame Adversity, Dies at 93
abstract: Despite a loss of hearing, she won three Grand Slam championships, including one at Wimbledon, in ascending to the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

name: Gérard Chaliand
headline: Gérard Chaliand, Intrepid Authority on Geopolitics, Dies at 91
abstract: His considerable influence in the French-speaking world was based on an unusual attribute: He had actually been to the revolutions he wrote about.

name: Pat Moore
profession: Model Turned Institution at P.J. Clarkes
headline: Pat Moore, a Model Turned Institution at P.J. Clarke’s, Dies at 89
abstract: She went from fashion shoots to becoming a familiar server at that venerable Manhattan saloon for some 45 years. She dated two of her more famous customers, Tony Bennett and Frank Sinatra.

name: A.K. Best
profession: Master of the Art of Fly Tying
headline: A.K. Best, Master of the Art of Fly Tying, Is Dead at 92
abstract: His meticulously crafted, lifelike designs were said to have “shaped the soul of modern fly fishing.”

name: James E. Ferguson II
headline: James E. Ferguson II, Rights Lawyer Who Defended Busing, Dies at 82
abstract: He helped litigate a landmark school desegregation case before the U.S. Supreme Court and overturn wrongful convictions of Black defendants in North Carolina.

name: Joan Mellen
headline: Joan Mellen, Whose Bobby Knight Biography Sparked Debate, Dies at 83
abstract: Some sportswriters accused her of “deifying” Indiana’s irascible basketball coach. A professor of English, she also wrote about Marilyn Monroe and the assassination of John F. Kennedy.

name: Jim Murray
profession: Football Executive and a McDonalds House Founder
headline: Jim Murray, 87, Football Executive and a McDonald’s House Founder, Dies
abstract: Before helping to lead the Philadelphia Eagles to the 1981 Super Bowl, he co-founded the first Ronald McDonald charity to help the families of seriously ill children.

name: Rodion Shchedrin
headline: Rodion Shchedrin, Composer Who Captured Russia’s Soul, Dies at 92
abstract: He drew on Russian literature for his stage works and was an eager experimenter, inspired by folk tales, religious mysticism and melodrama.

name: Tran Trong Duyet
profession: John McCains Captor at the Hanoi Hilton
headline: Tran Trong Duyet, John McCain’s Captor at the ‘Hanoi Hilton,’ Dies at 92
abstract: He endorsed Mr. McCain’s presidential bid in 2008 after insisting, despite accounts to the contrary, that no Americans were tortured under his watch in the Vietnam War.

name: Frank Price
profession: Hollywood Studio Chief Several Times Over
headline: Frank Price, Hollywood Studio Chief Several Times Over, Dies at 95
abstract: He ran Universal’s television and movie businesses and had two stints at Columbia. Running a studio, he said, was “sort of like being the head of a small country.”

name: Margaret W. Rossiter
headline: Margaret W. Rossiter, 81, Dies; Wrote Women Scientists Into History
abstract: In her groundbreaking trilogy, “Women Scientists in America,” she told the stories of numerous accomplished but largely invisible women.

name: Cunningham
headline: Duke Cunningham, 83, Congressman Convicted in Corruption Scandal, Dies
abstract: A war hero turned politician, he was first elected to the House in 1990 but stepped down in 2005 after pleading guilty to tax evasion and conspiracy to commit bribery.

name: Tina Modotti
profession: Life Was as Striking as Her Photographs
headline: Overlooked No More: Tina Modotti, Whose Life Was as Striking as Her Photographs
abstract: Her work is now in museums, but in the early 20th century, it was obscured by her romantic relationships with prominent men, among them her mentor, Edward Weston.

name: Carol Saline
profession: Journalist With a Story to Tell, About Her Dying
headline: Carol Saline, 86, Dies; Journalist With a Story to Tell, About Her Dying
abstract: Terminally ill, she contacted obituary reporters looking to be interviewed about her life and imminent death — to be “at her own wake,” a colleague said.

name: Zdena Salivarova
headline: Zdena Salivarova, Who Kept Banned Czech Literature Alive, Dies at 91
abstract: In exile in Canada, she and her husband, the novelist Josef Skvorecky, published books that had been outlawed by the Soviet-backed Communist regime.

name: Lee Roy Jordan
profession: Ferocious Linebacker for the Dallas Cowboys
headline: Lee Roy Jordan, Ferocious Linebacker for the Dallas Cowboys, Dies at 84
abstract: He was a favorite of Coach Bear Bryant at Alabama, then helped make the Cowboys “America’s Team.”

name: Gene Espy
profession: Pioneering Hiker of the Appalachian Trail
headline: Gene Espy, Pioneering Hiker of the Appalachian Trail, Dies at 98
abstract: In 1951, always an adventurer, he was the second person to walk the trail in a “thru-hike,” from Georgia to Maine, in an arduous 123 days. He later met the first to do so.

name: Joe Bugner
headline: Joe Bugner, 75, British Boxing Champ Who Slugged It Out With Ali, Dies
abstract: A European titleholder as well, he twice went the distance with Ali and once with Joe Frazier, losing those bouts but gaining respect.

name: Vivian Ayers Allen
headline: Vivian Ayers Allen, Poet and Cultural Activist, Dies at 102
abstract: She forged an arts career in Houston while raising children who became accomplished entertainers: Phylicia Rashad, Debbie Allen and Tex Allen.

name: Graham Greene
profession: Oscar-Nominated Actor for Dances With Wolves
headline: Graham Greene, Oscar-Nominated Actor for ‘Dances With Wolves,’ Dies at 73
abstract: An Indigenous Canadian, he appeared in several other Hollywood blockbusters and remained active in film, theater and television.

name: Stephen Muss
headline: Stephen Muss, Developer Who Helped Revive Miami Beach, Dies at 97
abstract: The scion of a New York family of builders, he rescued the Fontainebleau hotel from bankruptcy, spurring a real estate boom.

name: Mark Knoller
profession: White House Reporter and Font of Presidential Facts
headline: Mark Knoller, White House Reporter and Font of Presidential Facts, Dies at 73
abstract: As a longtime correspondent for CBS News Radio, he kept meticulous records of presidential activities, from vacation days to teleprompter use.

name: George Raveling
headline: George Raveling, Coach Who Brought Michael Jordan to Nike, Dies at 88
abstract: He also worked security for the 1963 March on Washington, and ended up with Martin Luther King Jr.’s copy of the “I Have a Dream” speech.

name: Patrick Hemingway
headline: Patrick Hemingway, Ernest’s Devoted Second Son, Is Dead at 97
abstract: Inspired by his parents’ travels, he spent much of his life in Africa and helped complete his father’s safari memoir. He also published a volume of father-son letters. He was Ernest Hemingway’s last surviving child.

name: Rosalyn Drexler
headline: Rosalyn Drexler, Artistic Whirlwind Who Defied Categories, Dies at 98
abstract: She wrote plays, novels and an Emmy-winning Lily Tomlin special. She was a painter, a sculptor and a nightclub singer. Oh, and she also wrestled professionally.

name: Giorgio Armani
profession: Fashions Master of the Power Suit
headline: Giorgio Armani, Fashion’s Master of the Power Suit, Dies at 91
abstract: He created a male uniform whose feminized form won favor with women. An alliance with movie stars made his name all but synonymous with red-carpet dressing.

name: Robert Jay Lifton
headline: Robert Jay Lifton, Psychiatrist Drawn to Humanity’s Horrors, Dies at 99
abstract: His work led him into some of history’s darkest corners, including the role of doctors in the Nazi era and the torture of Iraqi prisoners at Abu Ghraib.

name: Edgar Feuchtwanger
headline: Edgar Feuchtwanger, Who Wrote About Being Hitler’s Neighbor, Dies at 100
abstract: He and his Jewish family lived across the street from the German leader in the 1930s. He became a professor and historian in Britain.

name: Steve Hayden
headline: Steve Hayden, Writer Behind Apple’s Pivotal ‘1984’ Commercial, Dies at 78
abstract: The ad for the Macintosh computer — which was seen nationally just once, during the Super Bowl — is considered one of the most memorable commercials ever made.

name: Joshua Abram
headline: Joshua Abram Dies at 62; Gave Workspace-Sharing an Upscale Spin
abstract: He and a partner made their co-working locations feel like private clubs. Among his other ventures, he sought to slash the cost of in vitro fertilization by using robotics and A.I.

name: Barbara Jakobson
profession: Art World Power Broker in New York
headline: Barbara Jakobson, Art World Power Broker in New York, Dies at 92
abstract: A longtime trustee of the Museum of Modern Art, she was a savvy collector who befriended young artists like Robert Mapplethorpe and made her townhouse a showcase.

name: Duchess Kent
headline: Duchess of Kent Dies at 92; a Royal Who Comforted a Wimbledon Loser
abstract: A member of an aristocratic family, she married the Duke of Kent, a cousin of Queen Elizabeth II.

name: Art Seitz
profession: Camera Caught Tennis Greats On and Off the Court
headline: Art Seitz, Whose Camera Caught Tennis Greats On and Off the Court, Dies at 82
abstract: Over a 50-year career as a photographer he built friendships with rising stars and captured many of them in their personal environments.

name: A. James Hudspeth
headline: A. James Hudspeth, Who Unlocked Mysteries Behind Hearing, Dies at 79
abstract: He was pivotal in discovering how sound waves are converted into signals that the brain can perceive as a whisper, a symphony or a thunderclap.

name: Flip Pallot
profession: Banker Turned TV Fly Fishing Star
headline: Flip Pallot, Banker Turned TV Fly Fishing Star, Dies at 83
abstract: His long-running outdoor show on ESPN helped popularize an adventurous saltwater sport bent on hooking some of the biggest fish in the sea.

name: Joseph McNeil
profession: Young Spark in a Civil Rights Battle
headline: Joseph McNeil, Young Spark in a Civil Rights Battle, Dies at 83
abstract: He and his classmates from a historically Black college in Greensboro, N.C., desegregated a Woolworth’s lunch counter in 1960, inspiring similar protests across the nation.

name: Hassan Ouakrim
profession: Brought Moroccan Dance to the U.S
headline: Hassan Ouakrim, Who Brought Moroccan Dance to the U.S., Dies
abstract: A director and choreographer, he introduced Berber dances and music to New York’s downtown theater scene. He also staged elaborate soirees for the wealthy, one attended by Donald Trump.

name: Davey Johnson
profession: Managed the Mets to a Memorable Title
headline: Davey Johnson, Who Managed the Mets to a Memorable Title, Dies at 82
abstract: Before his triumph in the 1986 World Series, he had a long playing career and established himself as one of baseball’s brainier and more self-assured characters.

name: Tom Shipley
profession: Ode to Weed Reached the Top 10
headline: Tom Shipley, Whose Ode to Weed Reached the Top 10, Dies at 84
abstract: With their “One Toke Over the Line,” he and Michael Brewer saw a musical in-joke turn into a timeless cultural phenomenon.

name: Mark Volman
profession: Turtles Singer of Happy Together and Other Hits
headline: Mark Volman, 78, Turtles Singer of ‘Happy Together’ and Other Hits, Dies
abstract: In the 1960s, he and his fellow singer Howard Kaylan embodied the feel-good sound of a popular pop-rock band. The two later found new fame as Flo & Eddie.

name: Ruth Paine
headline: Ruth Paine, Who Gave Lodging to Marina Oswald, Dies at 92
abstract: Her knowledge of Lee Harvey Oswald and his wife made her a noteworthy witness during the Warren Commission’s investigation into the assassination of President John F. Kennedy.

name: David Baltimore
headline: David Baltimore, Nobel-Winning Molecular Biologist, Dies at 87
abstract: He was only 37 when he made a discovery that challenged the existing tenets of biology and led to an understanding of retroviruses and viruses, including H.I.V.

name: Barnett Shepherd
headline: Barnett Shepherd, Champion of Staten Island’s Heritage, Dies at 87
abstract: A longtime resident, he devoted his career to Historic Richmond Town and Sailors’ Snug Harbor, two of the borough’s most important cultural institutions.

name: Rick Davies
headline: Rick Davies, Singer and Founder of Supertramp, Dies at 81
abstract: He wrote hits including “Goodbye Stranger” and “Bloody Well Right,” and his use of the Wurlitzer piano became one of Supertramp’s signature sounds.

name: Jacques Charrier
headline: Jacques Charrier, Movie Star Who Wed Brigitte Bardot, Dies at 88
abstract: Their marriage made news in France, but they were an unhappy couple, and it didn’t last. Years later, they attacked each other in dueling memoirs.

name: Christoph von Dohnanyi
profession: Conductor With a World of Admirers
headline: Christoph von Dohnanyi, Conductor With a World of Admirers, Dies at 95
abstract: Known for his long tenure at the podium of the acclaimed Cleveland Orchestra, he was sought after as a guest with major symphonies and opera companies.

name: Michael Seltzer
headline: Michael Seltzer, Who Raised Millions to Fight AIDS, Dies at 78
abstract: In the 1980s, when government lagged in its response to the disease, he solicited private support for prevention and treatment.

name: Andrew Huse
profession: Cultural Historian of the Cuban Sandwich
headline: Andrew Huse, Cultural Historian of the Cuban Sandwich, Dies at 52
abstract: He investigated which city of Cuban immigrants might have created the celebrated sandwich, Tampa or Miami. His finding was not altogether surprising.

name: Ken Dryden
profession: Hall of Fame Goalie in a Multifaceted Life
headline: Ken Dryden, Hall of Fame Goalie in a Multifaceted Life, Dies at 78
abstract: He led Montreal to six Stanley Cups before becoming an acclaimed author, a team executive, a sportscaster and a member of Canada’s Parliament.

name: Stuart Craig
profession: Designed the Movie World of Harry Potter
headline: Stuart Craig, Who Designed the Movie World of Harry Potter, Dies at 83
abstract: A three-time Oscar winner for production design, he was one of the few people to work on all eight Potter films and their three “Fantastic Beasts” spinoffs.

name: Polly Holliday
profession: Sassy Waitress on the Sitcom Alice
headline: Polly Holliday, a Sassy Waitress on the Sitcom ‘Alice,’ Dies at 88
abstract: “Kiss my grits,” her character, Flo, was known to say. But that high-profile role was just one facet of a long, busy stage and screen career.

name: Charlie Kirk
profession: Right-Wing Force and a Close Trump Ally
headline: Charlie Kirk, Right-Wing Force and a Close Trump Ally, Dies at 31
abstract: The founder of Turning Point USA played a central role in organizing young voters and giving shape to the pro-Trump agenda. He was fatally shot during a speaking event in Utah.

name: Rosa Roisinblit
headline: Rosa Roisinblit, Who Championed the Missing in Argentina, Dies at 106
abstract: She helped create the activist group Grandmothers of Plaza de Mayo, which sought to find relatives who had been killed or “disappeared” by the 1976-83 military dictatorship.

name: Erich Sailer
headline: Erich Sailer, Ski Coach Who Helped Shape Champions, Dies at 99
abstract: Using a modest slope in Minnesota as a springboard, he tutored a host of rising stars, including Lindsey Vonn. He was inducted into the U.S. Ski and Snowboard Hall of Fame.

name: June Wilkinson
headline: June Wilkinson, Pinup Star and Screen Siren, Is Dead at 85
abstract: Christened “the Bosom” by Playboy magazine, she rode her voluptuous figure to fame and became known as “the most photographed nude in America.”

name: John Mew
headline: John Mew, Unorthodox Orthodontist Who Went Viral, Dies at 96
abstract: He gained a following for techniques, notably one known as mewing, that he said could help fix crooked teeth without surgery. The medical establishment disagreed.

name: Robert Grosvenor
headline: Robert Grosvenor, Sculptor Who Challenged Gravity, Dies at 88
abstract: “The lone wolf of sculpture,” one critic called him. His enigmatic art turned familiar objects like boats and vintage cars into mysterious contraptions.

name: Michel Odent
headline: Michel Odent, Pioneer of Natural Childbirth Techniques, Dies at 95
abstract: His innovations, including homelike delivery rooms and birthing pools, were based on his belief that “human birth cannot work as long as a woman is thinking.”

name: Marilyn Diamond
headline: Marilyn Diamond, Who Wrote a Blockbuster Diet Book, Dies at 81
abstract: “Fit for Life,” which she wrote with her husband, was a best seller in the 1980s promoting good health ahead of weight loss. But doctors were critical.

name: Eglantyne Jebb
profession: Started a Movement With Save the Children
headline: Overlooked No More: Eglantyne Jebb, Who Started a Movement With Save the Children
abstract: She co-founded the organization after she was outraged to learn that children were starving after World War I, when the British blocked aid to several countries.

name: Bonnie Addario
profession: Survivor of Lung Cancer Made Fighting It a Cause
headline: Bonnie Addario, 77, Dies; Survivor of Lung Cancer Made Fighting It a Cause
abstract: After climbing in the business world, she received a dire diagnosis, spurring her to found leading nonprofit groups to promote early detection and research.

name: Nancy King
headline: Nancy King, Jazz Singer Who Flew Under the Radar, Dies at 85
abstract: Aficionados, and her fellow musicians, considered her one of the best living vocalists. But she chose not to seek a bigger spotlight.

name: Mark Norell
profession: Discoverer of Links Between Dinosaurs and Birds
headline: Mark Norell, 68, Discoverer of Links Between Dinosaurs and Birds, Dies
abstract: His expeditions, including many to the Gobi Desert in Mongolia, yielded rare findings and led to exhibitions at the American Museum of Natural History.

name: Hermeto Pascoal
headline: Hermeto Pascoal, Eccentric and Prolific Brazilian Composer, Dies at 89
abstract: A self-taught multi-instrumentalist, he rose from a childhood of rural privation to become a favorite of jazz musicians and audiences around the world.

name: Ricky Hatton
profession: British Boxer and Former World Champion
headline: Ricky Hatton, British Boxer and Former World Champion, Dies at 46
abstract: He retired in 2012, after a career in which he compiled a record of 45-3, including 32 knockouts. He had recently announced plans for a comeback.

name: Kim Seongmin
headline: ​Kim Seongmin, Defector Who Pierced North Korea by Radio, Dies at 63
abstract: As a military propagandist, he fled the North by jumping off a train. In the South, he broadcast forbidden outside news to isolated North Koreans.

name: Bobby Hart
profession: Helped Give the Monkees Their Music
headline: Bobby Hart, Who Helped Give the Monkees Their Music, Dies at 86
abstract: The hit songwriting duo he and Tommy Boyce formed in the 1960s was best known for the unexpectedly popular tunes of a made-for-TV band.

name: Eddie Giacomin
headline: Eddie Giacomin, Rangers’ Goalie and Fan Favorite, Dies at 86
abstract: A Hall of Famer, he led the N.H.L. in shutouts and single-season victories three times and was stunned when the Rangers let him go in his 10th season.

name: John Penton
headline: John Penton, ‘Godfather’ of Off-Road Racing, Dies at 100
abstract: He set a transcontinental motorcycling speed record, and then helped to revolutionize off-road riding with his own brand of nimble bikes.

name: Robert Redford
profession: Screen Idol Turned Director and Activist
headline: Robert Redford, Screen Idol Turned Director and Activist, Dies at 89
abstract: He made serious topics like grief and political corruption resonate with the masses, in no small part because of his own star power.

name: Mary Rose Oakar
profession: First Arab American Woman in Congress
headline: Mary Rose Oakar, 85, First Arab American Woman in Congress, Dies
abstract: In her 16 years on Capitol Hill, she emerged as a champion of women’s rights, especially equal pay for comparable work.

name: Pat Crowley
profession: Veteran Actress of Film and TV
headline: Pat Crowley, Veteran Actress of Film and TV, Dies at 91
abstract: Named the year’s “new star” at the 1954 Golden Globes, she appeared alongside the biggest names of her time. She later embarked on a long career in television.

name: Ronny Whyte
headline: Ronny Whyte, Cabaret Singer Who Personified Elegance, Dies at 88
abstract: Like his friend and mentor Bobby Short, he exuded haute style while imbuing American standards with grace and wit.

name: John McQueen
headline: John McQueen, Who Made Art Out of Burrs, Bark and Vines, Is Dead at 82
abstract: A pioneer of contemporary basketry, he used plant material from his backyard to create ingenious forms that blurred the line between art and craft.

name: John H. Luckadoo
profession: Last Pilot From a Storied Bomber Group
headline: John H. Luckadoo, Last Pilot From a Storied Bomber Group, Dies at 103
abstract: As part of a unit known as the Bloody 100th, he flew 25 harrowing missions in his B-17 bomber over German-held territory during World War II.

name: Bob Goodenow
profession: Gave Hockey Players Union Some Muscle
headline: Bob Goodenow, 72, Dies; Gave Hockey Players’ Union Some Muscle
abstract: He took over a weak N.H.L. Players Association in 1992 and led it through three work stoppages, including a lockout that forced the cancellation of the 2004-5 season.

name: José María Tojeira
profession: Pursued Killers of His Fellow Priests
headline: José María Tojeira, 78, Dies; Pursued Killers of His Fellow Priests
abstract: As the Jesuit leader in Central America, he pushed for justice when six priests were shot to death in the midst of El Salvador’s civil war.

name: Marilyn Hagerty
headline: Marilyn Hagerty, Whose Olive Garden Review Went Viral, Dies at 99
abstract: “The chicken Alfredo ($10.95) was warm and comforting on a cold day,” she wrote from North Dakota. And suddenly the national media made her a celebrity.

name: Agnes Gund
profession: Oversaw a Major Expansion of MoMA
headline: Agnes Gund, Who Oversaw a Major Expansion of MoMA, Dies at 87
abstract: A champion of contemporary art, she was the museum’s president for 11 years. She also founded the Art for Justice Fund, donating $100 million.

name: Susan Xenarios
headline: Susan Xenarios, Who Transformed Rape Crisis Response, Dies at 79
abstract: She helped found New York City’s first rape crisis center after encountering indifference when she herself was assaulted. Then she took on New York State laws.

name: Charley Rosen
profession: Basketball Lifer With a Prolific Pen
headline: Charley Rosen, Basketball Lifer With a Prolific Pen, Dies at 84
abstract: A college player and coach who became a best-selling author of books about the game, he was also a kindred spirit to the Hall of Fame coach Phil Jackson.

name: Jack Daniels
profession: Olympian and Worlds Best Running Coach
headline: Jack Daniels, Olympian and ‘World’s Best’ Running Coach, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Tutoring Olympians, he created a simple workout formula that was said to produce the best results with the least effort, earning accolades across the running world.

name: Nicholas Grimshaw
profession: British Architect Known for High-Tech Designs
headline: Nicholas Grimshaw, 85, Dies; British Architect Known for High-Tech Designs
abstract: He melded his country’s history of engineering and industrial design with a modern sensibility to help shape the face of 21st-century Britain.

name: Jim Edgar
profession: Popular Moderate Republican Governor of Illinois
headline: Jim Edgar, 79, Popular Moderate Republican Governor of Illinois, Dies
abstract: In the 1990s, he compromised with Democrats, backed abortion rights, increased spending for schools and used an income-tax hike to help tame a huge budget deficit.

name: Marian Burros
profession: Food Writer Famed for Her Plum Torte and More
headline: Marian Burros, 92, Dies; Food Writer Famed for Her Plum Torte and More
abstract: At The Times and elsewhere, she combined recipe writing with reporting on topics like consumer protection and food safety. Her torte was a longtime fan favorite.

name: Diane Martel
headline: Diane Martel, Inventive Director of Music Videos, Dies at 63
abstract: Over three decades, she worked with superstars like Beyoncé and Mariah Carey, and faced claims of misogyny with her video for Robin Thicke’s “Blurred Lines.”

name: Sonny Curtis
profession: Wrote the Mary Tyler Moore Theme
headline: Sonny Curtis, Who Wrote the ‘Mary Tyler Moore’ Theme, Dies at 88
abstract: A prolific singer and songwriter who got his start with Buddy Holly, he also wrote “I Fought the Law,” “Walk Right Back” and hundreds of other songs.

name: Zubeen Garg
headline: Zubeen Garg, Singer Who Charmed India With a Bollywood Hit, Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. Garg sang in dozens of languages and his music blended folk, pop and rock. His hit song “Ya Ali” was featured in the 2006 film “Gangster.”

name: Louise Vincent
headline: Louise Vincent, 49, Drug User Who Led Harm-Reduction Movement, Dies
abstract: She was instrumental in helping to promote wider use of needle exchanges, naloxone and tests to assist drug users in identifying dangerous ingredients.

name: Ron DiMenna
profession: Founder of the Ron Jon Surf Shop Chain
headline: Ron DiMenna, Founder of the Ron Jon Surf Shop Chain, Dies at 88
abstract: As the founder of a national chain, he was a key figure in surfing’s expansion into mainstream culture, with a life said to be “the stuff of folklore.”

name: Bernie Parent
profession: Hall of Fame Goalie for the Brawling Flyers
headline: Bernie Parent, Hall of Fame Goalie for the Brawling Flyers, Dies at 80
abstract: “Only the Lord saves more than Bernie Parent,” a bumper sticker said of his netminding for Philadelphia, which he led to the Stanley Cup in 1974 and ’75.

name: Joe Stevens
headline: Joe Stevens, Photographer of Rock’s Intimate Moments, Dies at 87
abstract: After a career shift, he became a fixture in the music world, capturing enduring images of David Bowie, John Lennon, the Sex Pistols and many others.

name: Claudia Cardinale
headline: Claudia Cardinale, Actress Who Was ‘Italy’s Girlfriend,’ Is Dead at 87
abstract: A sex symbol with girl-next-door appeal, she rose to fame in the 1960s and starred in more than 150 films, including the Oscar-winning ‘8½’ and ‘The Leopard.’

name: Tess Johnston
headline: Tess Johnston, Diplomat Who Helped Preserve ‘Old Shanghai,’ Dies at 93
abstract: She worked in American consulates around the world but found a home in China’s “Paris of the East,” where she documented a vanishing colonial architecture.

name: Abdul Gani Bhat
headline: Abdul Gani Bhat Dies at 93; Kashmiri Separatist Championed Dialogue
abstract: Mr. Bhat, a scholar of Persian literature, was a rare and eloquent voice of moderation in Kashmir’s often militant separatist movement.

name: Mel Taub
headline: Mel Taub, Creator of a Pun-Loving Puzzle, Is Dead at 97
abstract: He was the main whiz behind a crossword variation for The Times, whose readers delighted in his anagrams and sometimes groan-inducing wordplay. (Try one yourself.)

name: Akiko Tsuruga
headline: Akiko Tsuruga, Inventive Jazz Organist, Dies at 58
abstract: Known for her vast sonic palette, she made her mark playing with the saxophone master Lou Donaldson and also had a prolific solo career.

name: Richard Moe
headline: Richard Moe, 88, Dies; Mondale Aide Became Historic Preservationist
abstract: After working for the vice president, he was at the forefront of the fight to save endangered landmarks as longtime head of the National Trust for Historic Preservation.

name: Henry Jaglom
headline: Henry Jaglom, Indie Director Who Mined the Personal, Dies at 87
abstract: His discursive films, often centered on women and their emotions and relationships, confounded and delighted critics in equal measure.

name: Sara Jane Moore
headline: Sara Jane Moore, Would-Be Assassin of President Ford, Dies at 95
abstract: A mother of four on the fringes of radical leftist movements, she fired at the president outside a San Francisco hotel in 1975. She had hoped to spark a revolution, she said.

name: Maxine Clair
headline: Maxine Clair, Writer Who Came to Her Craft in Middle Age, Dies at 86
abstract: She published her first book of poems at 49 and her first work of prose, the acclaimed novel “Rattlebone,” six years later.

name: Assata Shakur
profession: Convicted Revolutionary Found Refuge in Cuba
headline: Assata Shakur Dies at 78; Convicted Revolutionary Found Refuge in Cuba
abstract: A member of a Black militant group, she was found guilty in the 1973 murder of a New Jersey state trooper, escaped from prison and fled to Cuba, where she taught and wrote.

name: Aron Bell
profession: Last Brother of a World War II Resistance Group
headline: Aron Bell, Last Brother of a World War II Resistance Group, Dies at 98
abstract: His three older brothers led the Bielski partisans, which attacked Nazi soldiers and saved 1,200 fellow Jews. Aron was a scout who ferried warnings to a ghetto.

name: Robert B. Barnett
profession: Washington Master of the Book World Megadeal
headline: Robert B. Barnett, Washington Master of the Book World Megadeal, Dies at 79
abstract: An influential lawyer, he negotiated blockbuster contracts for A-list clients, including the Clintons, the Obamas and the Bushes, while often acting as a political adviser.

name: Neil Kraft
headline: Neil Kraft, Visionary Adman Who Sold ‘a Mood and a Lifestyle,’ Dies at 67
abstract: His ads for Calvin Klein and others captured a fizzy moment in the 1980s and ’90s, featuring celebrities like the young rapper Marky Mark wearing nothing but underwear and a grin.

name: Jerome Cohen
headline: Jerome Cohen, Lawyer Who Plumbed Chinese Legal System, Dies at 95
abstract: He pioneered the study of Chinese law, was among the first foreigners to practice commercial law in China and spoke out about human rights there.

name: Leo Gerard
headline: Leo Gerard, Who Led a Growing Steelworkers Union, Dies at 78
abstract: He helped make it the largest industrial union in North America as he fought an influx of cheap metal from China and lobbied for anti-dumping tariffs.

name: Russell Nelson
profession: Led Major Changes to the Mormon Church
headline: Russell Nelson, Who Led Major Changes to the Mormon Church, Dies at 101
abstract: He left a career as a pioneering surgeon to become a church leader, diversifying its policies and its senior ranks. He became its president at 93.

name: Fred Queller
profession: Lawyer in a Notable Domestic Violence Case
headline: Fred Queller, Lawyer in a Notable Domestic Violence Case, Dies at 93
abstract: His client was 6 years old when her father savagely beat her during a visitation. Her mother had warned police that he was dangerous, but they ignored her.

name: Viv Prince
headline: Viv Prince, Rock’s Original Madman Drummer, Is Dead at 84
abstract: A drummer for the 1960s British band the Pretty Things, “the high priest of lunacy” set a high bar for fiery performances and offstage misbehavior.

name: George Hardy
headline: George Hardy, Tuskegee Airman Who Fought in Three Wars, Dies at 100
abstract: At 19, he was one of the youngest pilots in the all-Black unit to see combat in World War II. “I used to say the Army’s No. 1 job was segregation,” he said. “Winning the war was No. 2.”

name: Mika Immonen
profession: Champion Pool Player Known as the Iceman
headline: Mika Immonen, Champion Pool Player Known as the Iceman, Dies at 52
abstract: He won the world nine-ball title in 2001 and the 10-ball title in 2009, as well as back-to-back U.S. Opens, earning his nickname for his steely demeanor.

name: Otto Obermaier
headline: Otto Obermaier, Who Succeeded Giuliani as U.S. Attorney, Dies at 89
abstract: His temperate approach was in sharp contrast to his more combative predecessor, but he continued to pursue corrupt unions and financiers.

name: Lally Weymouth
profession: Globe-Trotting Reporter and Scion of Graham Family
headline: Lally Weymouth, Globe-Trotting Reporter and Scion of Graham Family, Dies at 82
abstract: She secured hard-to-land interviews with foreign leaders but found few opportunities for a leadership role at her family’s newspaper, The Washington Post.

name: Bobby Cain
headline: Bobby Cain, Barrier Breaker in School Desegregation, Dies at 85
abstract: In 1957, facing down white mobs, he became the first Black student to graduate from a public high school in the South under a court mandate.

name: Marilyn Knowlden
headline: Marilyn Knowlden, Child Actress of 1930s Hollywood, Dies at 99
abstract: A spontaneous screen test led to a career that lasted into her teens. She appeared alongside stars like Bette Davis and Katharine Hepburn, played piano with Chico Marx and danced with Charles Laughton.

name: Thomas Perry
headline: Thomas Perry Dies at 78; Writer of Popular, Unconventional Thrillers
abstract: His many novels, including the prizewinning “The Butcher’s Boy” and the Jane Whitefield series, could have sympathetic villains and intriguing heroes.

name: Jane Goodall
profession: Chronicled the Social Lives of Chimps
headline: Jane Goodall, Who Chronicled the Social Lives of Chimps, Dies at 91
abstract: Her discoveries as a primatologist in the 1960s about how chimpanzees behave in the wild were hailed as “one of the Western world’s great scientific achievements.”

name: Edward T. Blake
headline: Edward T. Blake, 80, Dies; Forensic Expert Sparked Innocence Movement
abstract: He was the first to use PCR testing on crime-scene DNA, inspiring a practice that has freed thousands of wrongfully convicted people.

name: Ann Fagan Ginger
headline: Ann Fagan Ginger, Tireless Defender of Civil Liberties, Dies at 100
abstract: She was among the last of a generation of activists and lawyers who weathered the Red Scare, and then helped train a new cohort in the decades that followed.

name: Leo Hindery Jr.
profession: Dealmaking Power in the Cable TV Industry
headline: Leo Hindery Jr., Dealmaking Power in the Cable TV Industry, Dies at 77
abstract: As an executive, he helped negotiate AT&T’s $50 billion acquisition of TCI and later led the Yankees’ YES Network. He also drove his sports car to victory in the 24 Hours of Le Mans.

name: Bessie Margolin
headline: Overlooked No More: Bessie Margolin, Lawyer Who Turned Workers’ Hopes Into Law
abstract: Her streak of Supreme Court victories, which began during the New Deal era, benefited millions of workers and continue to shape labor rights today.

name: Patricia Routledge
profession: Hoity-Toity Housewife of Keeping Up Appearances
headline: Patricia Routledge, Hoity-Toity Housewife of ‘Keeping Up Appearances,’ Dies at 96
abstract: Before she became known as the snooty suburbanite Hyacinth Bucket, Ms. Routledge was an acclaimed stage performer, appearing with the Royal Shakespeare Company and on the West End and Broadway.

name: James Grashow
headline: James Grashow, Who Turned Cardboard Into Art, Dies at 83
abstract: He was best known for huge, fantastical installations that were not always built to last, including a version of the Trevi Fountain in Rome.

name: Margaret Markey
headline: Margaret Markey, Who Championed Victims of Sexual Abuse, Dies at 83
abstract: As a New York State assemblywoman, she began a campaign that finally bore fruit in 2019, when the Legislature extended the deadlines for victims to file claims.

name: Ashleigh Brilliant
headline: Ashleigh Brilliant, Prolific ‘Pot-Shots’ Phrasemaker, Dies at 91
abstract: Over nearly a half-century, he wrote 10,000 epigrams, none longer than 17 words, and printed them on postcards, T-shirts, mugs and other products.

name: Phyllis Gardner
headline: Phyllis Gardner, Early Skeptic of Theranos, Dies at 75
abstract: A pharmacologist, she was certain Elizabeth Holmes’s blood-testing idea would fail, and spoke up about it. At first, few listened.

name: Ivan Klima
headline: Ivan Klima, Czech Novelist Who Chafed Under Totalitarian Regimes, Dies at 94
abstract: A writer, dissident, teacher and critic, he was deeply affected by an early experience of his life: incarceration as a boy in a concentration camp near Prague.

name: Belva Davis
profession: West Coast Trailblazer in TV News
headline: Belva Davis, West Coast Trailblazer in TV News, Dies at 92
abstract: Overcoming poverty and prejudice, she was the first Black woman to be hired as a television reporter in the region and later became a popular anchor.

name: Darleane Hoffman
headline: Darleane Hoffman, Innovator in Nuclear Chemistry, Dies at 98
abstract: Hailed as one of the 50 most important women in science, she found ways to study rare radioactive isotopes and advanced the understanding of nuclear fission.

name: Jilly Cooper
headline: Jilly Cooper, Widely Popular Romance Novelist, Is Dead at 88
abstract: A prolific British writer and keen observer, she sold millions of copies of her juicy, sometimes racy “Rutshire Chronicles” series.

name: Chris Dreja
headline: Chris Dreja, a Founding Member of the Yardbirds, Dies at 78
abstract: A rhythm guitarist and bassist, he was a “rock” for a band whose fiery lead players, Eric Clapton, Jeff Beck and Jimmy Page, had no shortage of ego.

name: Kimberly Hébert Gregory
headline: Kimberly Hébert Gregory, Actress on HBO’s ‘Vice Principals,’ Dies at 52
abstract: She was known as the brash principal on the show, a dark comedy set at a high school that debuted in 2016.

name: Ken Jacobs
headline: Ken Jacobs, Visionary Experimental Filmmaker, Is Dead at 92
abstract: Using found footage and toying with dimensions (2-D could seem like dazzling 3-D), he sought to explode cinema’s traditional boundaries.

name: Saul Zabar
profession: Smoked Fish Czar of Upper West Side
headline: Saul Zabar, Smoked Fish Czar of Upper West Side, Dies at 97
abstract: He led his parents’ appetizing store, Zabar’s, for more than 70 years, turning it into an institution synonymous with New York.

name: John B. Gurdon
profession: Nobelist Paved Way for Cloning of Animals
headline: John B. Gurdon, 92, Dies; Nobelist Paved Way for Cloning of Animals
abstract: His work in the manipulation of cells laid the foundation for stem cell biology and regenerative medicine and led to the first cloned large mammal, a sheep named Dolly.

name: Joan Kennedy
headline: Joan Kennedy, Who Married Into a Dynasty, Is Dead at 89
abstract: The wife of Senator Edward Kennedy for a quarter of a century, she both basked and struggled in the reflected glare of a political family always in the spotlight.

name: Jonathan Lear
headline: Jonathan Lear, Philosopher Who Embraced Freud, Dies at 76
abstract: Defying scholarly norms, he took a hands-on approach to research. To study resilience, he visited the Crow Nation; to explore Freudian theory, he became a psychoanalyst.

name: Bruce Cutler
profession: Pugnacious Lawyer for the Mob Boss John Gotti
headline: Bruce Cutler, Pugnacious Lawyer for the Mob Boss John Gotti, Dies at 77
abstract: He became one of the country’s best-known criminal defense lawyers after winning acquittals in three cases that spawned a new nickname for Mr. Gotti: “the Teflon Don.”

name: Joseph Herbert
headline: Joseph Herbert, Who Helped Catch Copycat Zodiac Killer, Dies at 68
abstract: A New York police detective, he used his knowledge of the killer’s handwriting — and a lucky twist — to solve a confounding case.

name: Oscar S. Wyatt Jr.
headline: Oscar S. Wyatt Jr., Wily Texas Oilman, Is Dead at 101
abstract: He made billions selling energy with his Coastal Corporation, courted presidents and dictators, and eventually went to prison for paying kickbacks to the Iraqi government.

name: Ruth Weiss
profession: Chronicled Apartheid After Fleeing the Nazis
headline: Ruth Weiss, Who Chronicled Apartheid After Fleeing the Nazis, Dies at 101
abstract: Her life and work were shaped by confronting injustice in South Africa and Germany. “Blacks under apartheid — Jews under the swastika. Was it all that different?” she asked.

name: Jim McNeely
profession: Innovative Composer for Jazz Big Bands
headline: Jim McNeely, Innovative Composer for Jazz Big Bands, Dies at 76
abstract: A Grammy-winning pianist, he was renowned for works that created “new ideas about line, harmony, rhythm, sound and musical architecture,” one admirer wrote.

name: Jean Dolores Schmidt
profession: Loyola Basketball Superfan and Team Chaplain
headline: Sister Jean Dolores Schmidt, Loyola Basketball Superfan and Team Chaplain, Dies at 106
abstract: She led the Ramblers’ players in pregame prayers, pointed out opponents’ strengths and weaknesses and supported the team in N.C.A.A. tournaments.

name: John Lodge
profession: Singer and Bassist With the Moody Blues
headline: John Lodge, Singer and Bassist With the Moody Blues, Dies at 82
abstract: He wrote some of the band’s signature songs, including “Ride My See-Saw” and “I’m Just a Singer (in a Rock and Roll Band).”

name: Renato Casaro
headline: Renato Casaro, ‘Michelangelo of Movie Posters,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Few moviegoers knew his name, but directors like Sergio Leone, Sylvester Stallone and Quentin Tarantino considered his vivid work invaluable.

name: Peter M. Fishbein
headline: Peter M. Fishbein, Lawyer Named in Savings-and-Loan Lawsuit, Dies at 91
abstract: His firm’s $41 million settlement in representing Charles H. Keating Jr. raised questions about government overreach.

name: Violeta Parra
headline: Overlooked No More: Violeta Parra, Folk ‘Genius’ Who Redefined Latin American Music
abstract: A self-taught composer and interpreter, she led an unconventional and itinerant life devoted to spreading Chilean folkloric music.

name: Nikola Pilic
profession: Wimbledon Boycott Helped Shape Modern Tennis
headline: Nikola Pilic, Whose Wimbledon Boycott Helped Shape Modern Tennis, Dies at 86
abstract: After he was suspended in 1973, 81 players boycotted the tournament in solidarity, highlighting a power struggle for control of the sport.

name: Carolyn Cheeks Kilpatrick
profession: In Congress, a Lifeline for Detroit
headline: Carolyn Cheeks Kilpatrick, 80, Dies; In Congress, a Lifeline for Detroit
abstract: Over seven terms, she garnered millions in funds in helping to revitalize the city. But the political scandals of her son, an ex-mayor, came to shadow her career.

name: Clark Olofsson
profession: Bank Robber Helped Inspire Stockholm Syndrome
headline: Clark Olofsson, 78, Dies; Bank Robber Helped Inspire ‘Stockholm Syndrome’
abstract: In a 1973 heist, he and another man held hostages who surprisingly came to defend them, drawing attention to a puzzling psychological phenomenon.

name: Diane Keaton
profession: Star of Annie Hall and First Wives Club
headline: Diane Keaton, a Star of ‘Annie Hall’ and ‘First Wives Club,’ Dies at 79
abstract: She brought an unconventional personality to scores of roles on television and in movies ranging from zany comedies like “Sleeper” to piercing dramas like “The Godfather.”

name: Jesse L. Douglas
profession: Aide to King in Marches From Selma
headline: Jesse L. Douglas, Aide to King in Marches From Selma, Is Dead at 90
abstract: A lieutenant to Martin Luther King Jr. and a fellow preacher, he played a vital role in organizing voting-rights protests in 1965 that began with “Bloody Sunday.”

name: Danny Thompson
headline: Danny Thompson, Bassist Who Defied Folk Conventions, Dies at 86
abstract: A bedrock of the idiosyncratic British group Pentangle, he went on to play with a host of luminaries, including Roy Orbison, Eric Clapton and Kate Bush.

name: Susan Griffin
headline: Susan Griffin, a Leading Voice of Ecofeminism, Is Dead at 82
abstract: With books like “Woman and Nature,” she pioneered a unique form of creative nonfiction, linking violence against women to the ravaging of the environment.

name: John Searle
headline: John Searle, Philosopher Who Wrestled With A.I., Dies at 93
abstract: His blunt debating and imaginative theorizing about artificial intelligence and the human mind made him a leading scholar. But sexual-harassment allegations ended his career.

name: Toby Talbot
headline: Toby Talbot, Impassioned Promoter of Art Films, Dies at 96
abstract: With her husband, Dan, she ran four theaters in Manhattan and a company that distributed foreign and independent classics.

name: Milton Esterow
profession: Reported on Art Stolen in World War II
headline: Milton Esterow, Who Reported on Art Stolen in World War II, Dies at 97
abstract: At The New York Times and then ARTnews, which he bought, he brought an investigative edge to stories about artwork looted by the Germans during World War II and the Soviets afterward.

name: Alfa-Betty Olsen
headline: Alfa-Betty Olsen, Behind-the-Scenes ‘Comic Conspirator,’ Dies at 88
abstract: After quietly helping Mel Brooks set the irreverent tone on “Get Smart” and “The Producers,” she had a long collaboration as a writer with the actor and humorist Marshall Efron.

name: Mike Greenwell
profession: All-Star Outfielder for the Red Sox
headline: Mike Greenwell, All-Star Outfielder for the Red Sox, Dies at 62
abstract: Roaming the same grass as Ted Williams, he played for Boston for his entire 12-year major league career and came in second in the 1988 M.V.P. voting.

name: D’Angelo
headline: D’Angelo, Acclaimed and Reclusive R&B Innovator, Dies at 51
abstract: After hitting No. 1 with “Voodoo,” the genre-melding 2000 album that he promoted with a risqué music video, he vanished for more than a decade.

name: Raila Odinga
profession: Champion of Kenyan Democracy and Former Prime Minister
headline: Raila Odinga, Champion of Kenyan Democracy and Former Prime Minister, Dies at 80
abstract: A pivotal political leader who helped usher in multiparty democracy in the East African country, he ran unsuccessfully for the presidency five times.

name: Derek Rose
headline: Derek Rose, Impeccable Purveyor of Luxury Pajamas, Dies at 93
abstract: His colorful men’s nightwear was like something made on Savile Row in London — perfect, pricey — except that it was rarely seen outside the bedroom.

name: Gilles Larrain
headline: Gilles Larrain, Photographer of 1970s Drag Culture, Dies at 86
abstract: He shot portraits of stars like John Lennon and Miles Davis. But he is best remembered for “Idols,” an intimate look at a vital New York underground.

name: Kanchha Sherpa
profession: Last Member of First Team to Conquer Everest
headline: Kanchha Sherpa, Last Member of First Team to Conquer Everest, Dies at 92
abstract: A trip to India to find work led to a career climbing the world’s highest mountain.

name: Jeffrey Meldrum
headline: Jeffrey Meldrum, Scholar Who Stalked Bigfoot, Dies at 67
abstract: His willingness to bring scientific rigor to Sasquatch studies earned him the gratitude of enthusiasts and the withering scorn of debunkers.

name: Susan Stamberg
headline: Susan Stamberg, a Longtime Voice of NPR, Is Dead at 87
abstract: In 1972 she became the first woman to anchor a national evening news broadcast. She retired this summer after 50 years on the air.

name: Ace Frehley
headline: Ace Frehley, a Founding Member of Kiss, Is Dead at 74
abstract: A consummate showman, he was known for playing guitars rigged with pyrotechnic effects and for his distinctive stage persona.

name: Tomiichi Murayama
headline: Tomiichi Murayama, Japanese Leader Who Gave War Apology, Dies at 101
abstract: His televised address as prime minister, delivered 50 years to the day after Japan announced its surrender, set a marker for his country’s “deep remorse” over wartime atrocities.

name: Baek Sehee
headline: Baek Sehee, Korean Writer Who Bared Her Struggles With Depression, Dies at 35
abstract: She turned recorded sessions with her therapist into a best-selling memoir, helping to normalize conversations around mental health in South Korea.

name: Teresa Ulloa Ziáurriz
headline: Teresa Ulloa Ziáurriz, Rights Advocate Who Fought Sex Traffickers, Dies at 75
abstract: In Mexico, where the cult of machismo has long held sway, she waged a lonely, sometimes dangerous and often single-handed fight against prostitution and organized sex rings.

name: Chen Ning Yang
headline: Chen Ning Yang, Nobel-Winning Physicist, Is Dead at 103
abstract: He and a colleague created a sensation in 1956 by proposing that one of the four forces of nature might violate a law of physics.

name: Alison Rose
headline: Alison Rose, The New Yorker’s Femme Fatale, Dies at 81
abstract: She started as the magazine’s glamorous receptionist and became one of its more singular writers. In one of her last articles, she memorialized her time (and lovers) there.

name: Manuel Trujillo
headline: Manuel Trujillo, Who Helped New Yorkers Heal After 9/11, Dies at 80
abstract: As Bellevue Hospital’s director of psychiatry, he guided rescue workers and grieving families through trauma when terrorists attacked in 2001.

name: Griffin-Gracy
headline: Miss Major Griffin-Gracy, Trans Activist Who Saw It All, Dies
abstract: She spat in a policeman’s face at the Stonewall Riot, ran a nursing service during the AIDS crisis and boycotted Pride parades when they welcomed corporations.

name: Daniel Naroditsky
headline: Daniel Naroditsky, Chess Grandmaster, Dies at 29
abstract: He earned the highest title in the chess world at 17 and built a career as an accomplished chess teacher, commentator and author.

name: George F. Smoot
headline: George F. Smoot, Who Showed How the Cosmos Began, Is Dead at 80
abstract: He led a team of scientists who helped confirm that a Big Bang was the source of the universe. The discovery earned him a Nobel Prize.

name: Roberta Alexander
headline: Roberta Alexander, Widely Acclaimed Soprano, Dies at 76
abstract: An African American who spent much of her career based in the Netherlands, she said her race was less of a factor in Europe when being considered for a wide variety of opera roles.

name: Stephanie Johnson
headline: Stephanie Johnson, Burlesque Dancer Known as Tanqueray, Dies at 81
abstract: Her stories of her days in the gritty New York of the 1960s and ’70s found a new audience in recent years and made her a social media star.

name: Terry Farrell
headline: Terry Farrell, Whose Buildings Embodied Late 20th-Century Extremes, Dies at 87
abstract: His architecture swung from austere to whimsical, with conspicuous projects like the sprawling headquarters of the British intelligence service MI6.

name: Soo Catwoman
headline: Soo Catwoman, ‘the Female Face of Punk,’ Is Dead at 70
abstract: With a tuft of hair on either side of her shaved head and long tendrils of eyeliner swiped across her lids, she helped define a scene.

name: Jackie Ferrara
headline: Jackie Ferrara, Artist Who Brought Mystery to Minimalism, Dies at 95
abstract: While others made sleek metallic sculptures, she favored humble materials like lumber and glue. The Times called her “one of our most gifted and inventive sculptors.”

name: Samantha Eggar
headline: Samantha Eggar, Oscar-Nominated Star of ‘The Collector,’ Dies at 86
abstract: She also had leading roles in “Doctor Dolittle” with Rex Harrison, “Walk, Don’t Run” with Cary Grant and “The Molly Maguires” with Sean Connery.

name: Dave Ball
headline: Dave Ball of Soft Cell, Band Known for ‘Tainted Love,’ Dies at 66
abstract: He was a producer and one half of the pioneering English synth-pop duo.

name: Shelly Fireman
headline: Shelly Fireman, a Showman Restaurateur for Showgoers, Dies at 93
abstract: With considerable pizazz, he ran a string of popular restaurants in Manhattan, many aimed at hooking the crowds from Carnegie Hall, Lincoln Center and Broadway.

name: Ruth A. Lawrence
headline: Ruth A. Lawrence, Doctor Who Championed Breastfeeding, Is Dead at 101
abstract: As a pediatrician, she helped elevate breastfeeding from a medical afterthought to a specialty of its own. As a mother of nine, she practiced what she preached.

name: Phyllis Trible
profession: Studied the Bible Through a Feminist Lens
headline: Phyllis Trible, 92, Dies; Studied the Bible Through a Feminist Lens
abstract: An influential scholar, she challenged centuries of biblical interpretation that presumed that women were unequal to men in the eyes of God.

name: J. William Middendorf II
headline: J. William Middendorf II, 101, Dies; Navy Secretary and Musical Diplomat
abstract: A G.O.P. fund-raiser, he was the Navy chief under Gerald R. Ford and held ambassadorships in the 1970s and ’80s. He gained notice for his classical music compositions.

name: Nebojsa Pavkovic
profession: Yugoslav General Convicted of War Crimes
headline: Nebojsa Pavkovic, Yugoslav General Convicted of War Crimes, Dies at 79
abstract: Found guilty in 2009, he had been serving a 22-year sentence but was released for health reasons at the request of the Serbian government.

name: Barbara Gips
headline: Barbara Gips, Creator of Memorable Movie Catchphrases, Dies at 89
abstract: Her best-known tagline was also her first to be published, written for “Alien”: “In space no one can hear you scream.”

name: Sirikit
headline: Sirikit, Glamorous Queen of Thailand Who Wielded Power, Dies at 93
abstract: As the wife of King Bhumibol Adulyadej, she traveled the world charming government leaders and the public.

name: Arthur Waskow
profession: Influential Rabbi and Activist for Social Justice
headline: Arthur Waskow, 92, Influential Rabbi and Activist for Social Justice, Dies
abstract: Through more than two dozen books and two organizations he helped start, he had a profound impact on the intellectual and political life of Jewish congregations in the United States.

name: June Lockhart
headline: June Lockhart, Beloved Television Mother, Dies at 100
abstract: She exuded earnest maternal wisdom and wistful contentment as a farm wife on “Lassie” and, later, as an interplanetary castaway on “Lost in Space.”

name: Benita Valente
headline: Benita Valente, Acclaimed Bel Canto Soprano, Is Dead at 91
abstract: Her career spanned decades, included performances at the Metropolitan Opera and brought her effusive praise from critics and operaphiles.

name: Francisco Pinto Balsemão
profession: Portuguese Prime Minister and Press Champion
headline: Francisco Pinto Balsemão, 88, Dies; Portuguese Prime Minister and Press Champion
abstract: In the wake of a revolution, he helped found a leading political party and tried to conciliate warring left and right factions, although his success was limited.

name: Drew Struzan
headline: Drew Struzan, Masterly Painter of Movie Posters, Dies at 78
abstract: He created realistic imagery for the “Star Wars” franchise, the Indiana Jones films and the “Back to the Future” trilogy. He also put Alice Cooper in a tuxedo and tails for an album cover.

name: Anthony Jackson
headline: Anthony Jackson, Master of the Electric Bass, Is Dead at 73
abstract: Besides his work with pop stars and jazz greats, he is credited with helping to invent the six-string contrabass guitar.

name: Jack DeJohnette
headline: Jack DeJohnette, Revered Jazz Drummer, Dies at 83
abstract: Endowed with spectacular range, he played with Miles Davis, led New Directions and Special Edition, and spent decades with Keith Jarrett’s Standards Trio.

name: Cody ‘Beef’ Franke
headline: Cody ‘Beef’ Franke, Barstool Golf Influencer, Dies at 31
abstract: “Know when to attack and when to put on the brakes,” Mr. Franke said in one of his last online posts. Dave Portnoy, the Barstool Sports founder, said he died suddenly over the weekend.

name: Prunella Scales
headline: Prunella Scales, Sybil on ‘Fawlty Towers,’ Dies at 93
abstract: Best known “for playing unfortunate wives,” she had a decades-long career in the theater and on television.

name: Michael McKee
headline: Michael McKee, Fervent Advocate for Tenants’ Rights, Dies at 85
abstract: A broken window transformed him into a professional organizer and lobbyist to regulate rents and restrain landlords in New York.

name: Annabel Goldsmith
headline: Annabel Goldsmith, a Queen of British High Society, Dies at 91
abstract: Annabel’s, the club that Ms. Goldsmith’s first husband named after her, opened in the 1960s and is still one of London’s most exclusive nightspots.

name: Edward J. Blakely
profession: Hired to Oversee Katrina Recovery in New Orleans
headline: Edward J. Blakely, 87, Dies; Hired to Oversee Katrina Recovery in New Orleans
abstract: An urban planner who specialized in disaster recovery, he was brought in to revive the city after the 2005 storm. The task proved larger than one man could handle.

name: Bjorn Andresen
headline: Bjorn Andresen, Reluctant ‘Most Beautiful Boy,’ Dies at 70
abstract: At 15, he played the muse to an ailing composer in Luchino Visconti’s film “Death in Venice.” He later said he’d felt sexualized by the director.

name: Pierre Robert
headline: Pierre Robert, Philadelphia’s ‘Citizen’ D.J., Dies at 70
abstract: He became a stalwart of Philadelphia’s rock airwaves after moving from California, broadcasting a live show for more than 40 years.

name: Patricia Crowther
profession: Brought Witchcraft Out of the Shadows
headline: Patricia Crowther, Who Brought Witchcraft Out of the Shadows, Dies at 97
abstract: As a high priestess of Wicca, a branch of modern paganism founded in England, she promoted an image of witches as early feminists who were benevolent and spiritual.

name: Marthe Gautier
profession: Had Key Role in Down Syndrome Breakthrough
headline: Marthe Gautier, 96, Dies; Had Key Role in Down Syndrome Breakthrough
abstract: She had to fight for recognition after a male colleague took credit for her work in identifying an extra chromosome as the cause of that genetic condition.

name: Selma van de Perre
headline: Selma van de Perre, Dutch Jew Who Resisted Nazis, Dies at 103
abstract: “It is impossible not to marvel at her steadiness and courage,” one reviewer wrote after reading her memoir.

name: Kelvin LaVerne
headline: Kelvin LaVerne, Creator of Enigmatic Furnishings, Dies at 88
abstract: With his father, Philip, he made idiosyncratic, often monumental bronze work influenced by ancient themes. But was it art or was it furniture?

name: Alison Knowles
headline: Alison Knowles, Artist Who Took Lunch to New Levels, Dies at 92
abstract: An early participant in the eccentric collection of artists known as Fluxus, she was perhaps best known for pieces centered on a humble tuna sandwich and a giant salad.

name: Hannah Senesh
headline: Overlooked No More: Hannah Senesh, Poet and Paratrooper Who Defied the Nazis
abstract: Senesh fled Hungary just before World War II. But unlike most Jews who escaped the Nazis, she went back to fight. Today, she is regarded as a hero in Israel.

name: Zoë Wicomb
headline: Zoë Wicomb, Acclaimed South African Author, Dies at 76
abstract: In novels and short stories, she delivered sharp observations of the constraints and contradictions of apartheid and its aftermath.

name: Juan Ramón Matta Ballesteros
headline: Juan Ramón Matta Ballesteros, 80, Dies; Cartel Kingpin Fed Cocaine Boom
abstract: Before being imprisoned in the late 1980s, he made a fortune as a Honduran power broker connecting Colombian and Mexican cartels.

name: Alvin Kass
profession: N.Y.P.D. Chaplain for Nearly Six Decades
headline: Rabbi Alvin Kass, N.Y.P.D. Chaplain for Nearly Six Decades, Dies at 89
abstract: The youngest and longest-serving chaplain in New York City history, he was also the first Jewish chief chaplain in the modern era.

name: Marcyliena Morgan
headline: Marcyliena Morgan, Founder of Harvard’s Hip-Hop Archive, Dies at 75
abstract: Her university’s vast collection of albums, scholarly essays and other ephemera helped establish rap as a course of serious study on a par with classical music.

name: Maria Riva
headline: Maria Riva, Dietrich Daughter Who Demystified the Legend, Dies at 100
abstract: She was her mother’s handmaiden and aide-de-camp. In 1993, her blockbuster biography told of the awful price she paid.

name: Martha Layne Collins
headline: Martha Layne Collins, 88, Dies; Kentucky’s First Female Governor
abstract: She rose from a junior high school teacher to the state’s top official, and helped persuade Toyota to build its first American factory in Georgetown, Ky.

name: Donna Jean Godchaux-MacKay
headline: Donna Jean Godchaux-MacKay, Grateful Dead Singer, Dies at 78
abstract: She helped shape the band’s sound in the 1970s, a decade that took the band to new heights.

name: Diane Ladd
headline: Diane Ladd, Versatile and Lauded Film Actress, Dies at 89
abstract: She was a three-time Oscar contender playing strikingly different characters, in one case starring alongside her daughter and fellow nominee, Laura Dern.

name: George Banks
headline: George Banks, Convicted Mass Murderer, Dies at 83
abstract: He fatally shot 13 people in Pennsylvania in September 1982 in what was then one of the nation’s worst mass shootings. Five of the victims were his own children.

name: Kim Yong-nam
profession: Longtime Ceremonial Leader of North Korea
headline: Kim Yong-nam, Longtime Ceremonial Leader of North Korea, Dies at 97
abstract: In a country where political purges are frequent, Mr. Kim was a notable exception and served three generations of its dynastic rulers.

name: Dick Cheney
profession: Powerful Vice President and Washington Insider
headline: Dick Cheney, Powerful Vice President and Washington Insider, Dies at 84
abstract: A former defense secretary and congressman, he held the nation’s No. 2 job under President George W. Bush and was an architect of policies in an era of war and economic change.

name: Sara Terry
headline: Sara Terry, Photographer Who Captured War’s Aftermath, Dies at 70
abstract: Her haunting work focused on the lingering traces of conflict in places like Bosnia and Sierra Leone, after the firing had stopped.

name: Bob Trumpy
profession: Star Receiver Turned NBC Football Analyst
headline: Bob Trumpy, Star Receiver Turned NBC Football Analyst, Dies at 80
abstract: He made his mark with the Cincinnati Bengals as a fast pass-catching tight end. He later joined announcers like Bob Costas and Dick Enberg in the broadcast booth.

name: John Russell Taylor
headline: John Russell Taylor, 90, Dies; Cultural Critic and Hitchcock Biographer
abstract: A prolific journalist and author, he wrote the only authorized biography of Alfred Hitchcock and heaped early praise on the future Nobel laureate Harold Pinter.

name: Paul Ignatius
profession: Navy Secretary and Vietnam-Era Defense Official
headline: Paul Ignatius, 104, Dies; Navy Secretary and Vietnam-Era Defense Official
abstract: He oversaw supplies for the war effort under Lyndon B. Johnson and later had a brief, rocky tenure as president of The Washington Post during the Pentagon Papers case.

name: Ed Moloney
profession: Chronicler of the Troubles in Northern Ireland
headline: Ed Moloney, Chronicler of the Troubles in Northern Ireland, Dies at 77
abstract: He wrote a history of the Irish Republican Army and directed a project that secretly collected oral histories of paramilitary fighters.

name: Tony Harrison
headline: Tony Harrison, Poet of the Working Class, Is Dead at 88
abstract: In Britain, he sought to be “free not to have to puff some prince’s wedding / free to say up yours to Tony Blair.”

name: Edward Arrigoni
headline: Edward Arrigoni, 91, Dies; His ‘Cop-Shot’ Charity Rewards Tipsters
abstract: A bus company executive, he founded an organization that offers $10,000 for information on gunmen who assault police. Its posters are ubiquitous in the New York area.

name: Stanley Chesley
profession: Class-Action Lawyer Called Master of Disaster
headline: Stanley Chesley, Class-Action Lawyer Called ‘Master of Disaster,’ Dies at 89
abstract: He won billions of dollars for plaintiffs in major suits against corporations but was disbarred for siphoning money from clients.

name: Owen
headline: Sri Owen, Who Popularized Indonesian Cuisine, Dies at 90
abstract: Settling in England as a young woman, she turned her nostalgia for the food of her youth in Sumatra into a career as an influential cookbook author.

name: Fatos Nano
profession: Albanian Leader in Era of Chaos and Transition
headline: Fatos Nano, Albanian Leader in Era of Chaos and Transition, Dies at 73
abstract: A political survivor during his country’s shift from brutal communist regime to flawed democracy, he served three stints as prime minister.

name: John Cleary
headline: John Cleary, Wounded in Kent State Shooting, Dies at 74
abstract: He was shot in 1970 by the National Guard during a student protest over the Vietnam War that left four dead in Ohio. A photo of him lying on the ground and bleeding made the cover of Life magazine.

name: Gillian Tindall
headline: Gillian Tindall, 87, Dies; Author Who Probed the Layers of Places
abstract: A novelist and biographer, she was also a preservationist, and her meticulous investigations of houses, villages and cities revealed intricate histories.

name: James D. Watson
profession: Co-Discoverer of the Structure of DNA
headline: James D. Watson, Co-Discoverer of the Structure of DNA, Is Dead at 97
abstract: His decoding of the blueprint for life with Francis H.C. Crick made him one of the most important scientists of the 20th century. He wrote a celebrated memoir and later ignited an uproar with racist views.

name: Pauline Collins
profession: Stage and Screen Star of Shirley Valentine
headline: Pauline Collins, 85, Dies; Stage and Screen Star of ‘Shirley Valentine’
abstract: She often played a particularly British character: a bubbly yet resilient woman facing down the corrosive effects of everyday modern life.

name: Robert H. Bartlett
headline: Robert H. Bartlett, Father of Innovative Life-Support System, Dies at 86
abstract: He developed extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, or ECMO, a treatment that can sustain patients whose hearts and lungs are failing — for days or weeks or longer.

name: Nabil Shaban
profession: Acclaimed Actor and Advocate for the Disabled
headline: Nabil Shaban, Acclaimed Actor and Advocate for the Disabled, Dies at 72
abstract: Born without the use of his legs, he appeared memorably on television on “Doctor Who” and onstage as, among many other roles, Hamlet.

name: Anthony Grey
profession: Journalist Held Hostage by China for Two Years
headline: Anthony Grey, Journalist Held Hostage by China for Two Years, Dies at 87
abstract: A correspondent for Reuters, he became a global symbol of China’s isolation and of the anti-foreigner hysteria spawned by its Cultural Revolution.

name: Peter Watkins
headline: Peter Watkins, Provocateur With a Movie Camera, Dies at 90
abstract: His Oscar-winning 1965 film “The War Game” depicted a post-nuclear-attack England, one of his many fictionalized docudramas against war and repression.

name: Paul Tagliabue
profession: Led the N.F.L. for 17 Prosperous Years
headline: Paul Tagliabue, Who Led the N.F.L. for 17 Prosperous Years, Dies at 84
abstract: He helped achieve labor peace, pushed for minority hiring and oversaw the league’s expansion. But he minimized the risks of concussions.

name: Ken Parker
headline: Ken Parker, Who Reinvented the Guitar, Is Dead at 73
abstract: He built groundbreaking guitars that were displayed in art galleries and played by Joni Mitchell, Trent Reznor and many others.

name: Richie Adubato
profession: Coach of Mens and Womens Pro Basketball
headline: Richie Adubato, Coach of Men’s and Women’s Pro Basketball, Dies at 87
abstract: He had a losing record in the N.B.A., but gained acclaim coaching a Liberty team that featured stars like Teresa Weatherspoon and Becky Hammon.

name: Lenny Wilkens
profession: N.B.A. Hall of Famer as Both Player and Coach
headline: Lenny Wilkens, N.B.A. Hall of Famer as Both Player and Coach, Dies at 88
abstract: A perennial All Star, he was cited as one of the league’s 50 greatest players and one of its top 10 coaches, winning 1,332 games and leading Seattle to a championship.

name: Tatsuya Nakadai
profession: Japanese Star Known for Ran and Other Classics
headline: Tatsuya Nakadai, Japanese Star Known for ‘Ran’ and Other Classics, Dies at 92
abstract: He was a fixture of postwar Japanese cinema, appearing in films by Akira Kurosawa and other leading directors of that era.

name: Nolan Williams
profession: Stimulated the Brain to Treat Depression
headline: Nolan Williams, Who Stimulated the Brain to Treat Depression, Dies at 43
abstract: A neuroscientist, he employed a battery of high-tech tools in devising a fast-acting therapy that targets the area of the brain where depression originates.

name: Cleto Escobedo III
headline: Cleto Escobedo III, Jimmy Kimmel’s Bandleader, Dies at 59
abstract: Mr. Kimmel said that he and Mr. Escobedo, who led Cleto and the Cletones on “Jimmy Kimmel Live!,” had been “inseparable since I was 9 years old.”

name: Hal Sirowitz
headline: Hal Sirowitz, Poet Who Mined His Mother’s Worry With Wit, Dies at 76
abstract: He wrote of his suffocating relationship with his mother to create mordant reminiscences and became a standout at poetry slams in New York.

name: Arline Bronzaft
headline: Arline Bronzaft, Who Campaigned for a Quieter City, Dies at 89
abstract: She studied the impact of noise on health and classroom learning and helped impose stricter regulations in New York City.

name: Lorinda de Roulet
profession: Briefly Led the New York Mets
headline: Lorinda de Roulet, Who Briefly Led the New York Mets, Dies at 95
abstract: A daughter of Joan Whitney Payson, the team’s exuberant first owner, she took over as chairwoman in 1978 during a lackluster time for the franchise.

name: Sally Kirkland
headline: Sally Kirkland, Scene-Stealing Actress, Dies at 84
abstract: She received an Oscar nomination for the 1987 film “Anna” but spent much of her prolific career as a go-to supporting actress in movies like “The Sting” and “JFK.”

name: William Rataczak
profession: Co-Pilot of Flight Hijacked by D.B. Cooper
headline: William Rataczak, Co-Pilot of Flight Hijacked by D.B. Cooper, Dies at 86
abstract: He was a witness to one of the most riveting unsolved crimes in American history, which inspired scores of conspiracy theories and obsessed amateur sleuths.

name: Michael Ray Richardson
headline: Michael Ray Richardson, N.B.A. Star Derailed by Cocaine, Dies at 70
abstract: A four-time All-Star, he dazzled fans, and fellow players, with his intense play for the New York Knicks, only to become the league’s first player to be barred for drug use.

name: Juan Ponce Enrile
headline: Juan Ponce Enrile, a Political Power in the Philippines, Dies at 101
abstract: A protégé of Ferdinand Marcos, he helped administer martial law for eight years before turning on his patron in the “People Power” uprising of 1986.

name: Jim Avila
headline: Jim Avila, Former ABC News Correspondent, Dies at 70
