abstract: He spent almost two decades at the network, covering a wide range of court cases and the White House. He was also at the center of a defamation lawsuit over “pink slime.”

name: Sharon Camp
profession: Mother of the Plan B Contraceptive Pill
headline: Sharon Camp, Mother of the ‘Plan B’ Contraceptive Pill, Dies at 81
abstract: An advocate for women’s reproductive health, she started one of the world’s smallest pharmaceutical companies to bring an emergency birth-control method to market.

name: Sabina Spielrein
profession: Visionary Lost Between Freud and Jung
headline: Overlooked No More: Sabina Spielrein, Visionary Lost Between Freud and Jung
abstract: She maintained a triangular correspondence with the two men, who overshadowed the significant contributions she made to the field of psychoanalysis.

name: Frank Chuman
profession: Pioneering Lawyer for Japanese American Rights
headline: Frank Chuman, Pioneering Lawyer for Japanese American Rights, Dies at 105
abstract: He was sent to the Manzanar internment camp during World War II, an experience that inspired a long career in civil rights activism.

name: Elizabeth Franz
headline: Elizabeth Franz, Versatile Tony-Winning Actress, Is Dead at 84
abstract: She won the award for her performance as Linda Loman in a 1999 Broadway revival of “Death of a Salesman” and played the matriarch Kate Jerome in two Neil Simon comedies.

name: Yvonne Brewster
headline: Yvonne Brewster, Godmother of Black British Theater, Dies at 87
abstract: When she studied acting in London in the 1950s, she was told she was unlikely to find work. She ended up starting one of the country’s foremost Black theaters.

name: Alice Wong
profession: Writer and Relentless Advocate for Disability Rights
headline: Alice Wong, Writer and Relentless Advocate for Disability Rights, Dies at 51
abstract: Born with muscular dystrophy, she received a MacArthur “Genius” grant in 2024 for her decades of calling attention to the need for equal rights for disabled people.

name: Chris Ponnet
headline: Chris Ponnet, Priest Who Preached Social Justice Far Beyond Pulpit, Dies at 68
abstract: Courting arrest, he protested against war and the death penalty. He also performed an annual burial ceremony for hundreds of unclaimed bodies.

name: Todd Snider
profession: Folk Singer With a Wry Wit
headline: Todd Snider, Folk Singer With a Wry Wit, Dies at 59
abstract: Mentored by the likes of Jimmy Buffett and John Prine, his big-hearted ballads told of heartache even as his humor revealed a steadfast optimism.

name: Homayoun Ershadi
profession: Kite Runner and Taste of Cherry Star
headline: Homayoun Ershadi, 78, Dies; ‘Kite Runner’ and ‘Taste of Cherry’ Star
abstract: He was an architect with no training as an actor whose life was changed by a chance encounter. He inspired rave reviews and a New Yorker short story.

name: Bill Ivey
profession: Quelled Conservative Ire Over U.S. Arts Agency
headline: Bill Ivey, 81, Dies; Quelled Conservative Ire Over U.S. Arts Agency
abstract: As the head of the National Endowment for the Arts, Mr. Ivey, a leader in country music, shifted the agency’s focus away from avant-garde work and won more funding.

name: Sid Davidoff
headline: Sid Davidoff, Powerful Aide to Mayor Lindsay, Dies at 86
abstract: In the 1960s and ’70s, he was a brash lieutenant to a young, ambitious, reform-minded mayor and ended up on President Nixon’s “enemies list.”

name: Alice and Ellen Kessler
headline: Alice and Ellen Kessler, ’60s Singing Sensations, Die at 89
abstract: The twin sisters from Germany, who were nightclub stars and regular guests on international variety shows, chose to end their lives together.

name: Bonnie Munshin
profession: Velvet Hammer of a Hamptons Hot Spot
headline: Bonnie Munshin, ‘Velvet Hammer’ of a Hamptons Hot Spot, Dies at 84
abstract: At Nick & Toni’s, a restaurant beloved by celebrities and locals alike, she managed its coveted prime real estate, keeping everyone happy and the looky-loos at bay.

name: Henry Todd
headline: Henry Todd, LSD Kingpin Turned Everest Guide, Dies at 80
abstract: He helped make and distribute millions of LSD tablets in the 1970s. After seven years in prison, he ran mountain climbing expeditions in the Himalayas.

name: Robert L. Stirm
headline: Robert L. Stirm, Returning P.O.W. in Pulitzer-Winning Photo, Dies at 92
abstract: The image immortalized a Vietnam veteran’s joyous homecoming to his beaming family, but it hid the truth about his unraveling marriage.

name: Richard Lamparski
headline: Richard Lamparski, 93, Dies; Wrote ‘Whatever Became Of …?’ Books
abstract: He turned an obsession with forgotten stars into a popular series, long before “Where Are They Now?” features became ubiquitous.

name: Stephen Anderson
headline: Stephen Anderson, Linguist Who Refuted Doctor Dolittle, Dies at 82
abstract: In “Doctor Dolittle’s Delusion,” he argued that language is a biological system unique to humans, despite the widespread belief that it extended to other animals.

name: David Bellos
headline: David Bellos, 80, Dies; Wrestled French Wordplay Into English
abstract: He translated nearly 30 books, including novels by Georges Perec, a master of linguistic games, and Ismail Kadare.

name: Ward Landrigan
headline: Ward Landrigan, Jeweler to the Stars, Dies at 84
abstract: At Sotheby’s, he provided famous diamonds to Elizabeth Taylor and Richard Burton before reviving Verdura, a venerable jewelry company founded by a Sicilian duke.

name: Burt Meyer
profession: Made Lite-Brite and Rock Em Sock Em Robots
headline: Burt Meyer, 99, Dies; Made Lite-Brite and Rock ’Em Sock ’Em Robots
abstract: Starting in the 1960s, he collaborated on the designs of classic toys like Mouse Trap, Toss Across and Mr. Machine.

name: Mark Mellman
headline: Mark Mellman, 70, Dies; Helped Democrats Understand Their Voters
abstract: A pollster and political strategist, he was a key figure in John Kerry’s 2004 presidential campaign and used his prominence to speak out in defense of Israel.

name: Terry Martin Hekker
headline: Terry Martin Hekker, a Happy Housewife Scorned, Dies at 92
abstract: She wrote two popular memoirs: the first about the joys of married life, the second about her husband serving her divorce papers on their 40th anniversary.

name: Dorothy Vogel
profession: Librarian With a Vast Art Collection
headline: Dorothy Vogel, Librarian With a Vast Art Collection, Dies at 90
abstract: On modest civil servants’ salaries, she and her husband amassed a trove of some 4,000 works by art-world luminaries, storing them in their one-bedroom Manhattan apartment.

name: Lee Tamahori
profession: Director of Film Voted New Zealands Best
headline: Lee Tamahori, Director of Film Voted New Zealand’s Best, Dies at 75
abstract: He reimagined “Once Were Warriors,” a novel about a Maori family, as a film that became a worldwide phenomenon. He went on to direct Hollywood movies.

name: Jamil Abdullah Al-Amin
profession: Black Power Activist Known as H. Rap Brown
headline: Jamil Abdullah Al-Amin, Black Power Activist Known as H. Rap Brown, Dies at 82
abstract: A charismatic orator in the 1960s, he called for armed resistance to white oppression. As a Muslim cleric, he was convicted of murder in 2000 and died in detention.

name: Jimmy Cliff
headline: Jimmy Cliff, Singer Who Helped Bring Reggae to Global Audience, Dies at 81
abstract: His Grammy-winning records as well as his starring role in the cult movie “The Harder They Come” in 1972 boosted a career spanning seven decades.

name: Dharmendra
profession: One of Bollywoods Top Leading Men
headline: Dharmendra, One of Bollywood’s Top Leading Men, Dies at 89
abstract: In a career spanning nearly seven decades and more than 300 productions, he became widely popular, and wealthy, playing heroes and thieves.

name: Skye Gyngell
headline: Skye Gyngell, Chef Who Championed ‘Slow Food,’ Dies at 62
abstract: The Australian pioneer of sustainable cooking practices that preserved local traditions died in London. She had been diagnosed with aggressive skin cancer last year.

name: Gramma
profession: Galápagos Tortoise Older Than the San Diego Zoo
headline: Gramma, a Galápagos Tortoise Older Than the San Diego Zoo, Dies at About 141
abstract: Gramma, who died at the zoo on Thursday, was believed to have been born in 1884, when Chester A. Arthur was in the White House.

name: Viola Fletcher
profession: Oldest Survivor of the Tulsa Race Massacre
headline: Viola Fletcher, Oldest Survivor of the Tulsa Race Massacre, Dies at 111
abstract: At 7, she bore witness to one of American history’s most violent spasms of racial violence. She was 106 when the nation reckoned with the crime.

name: Udo Kier
profession: Familiar Movie Villain and Fixture of the Offbeat
headline: Udo Kier, Familiar Movie Villain and Fixture of the Offbeat, Dies at 81
abstract: A German-born actor, he appeared in more than 280 films, from Hollywood action fare to a Warhol horror tale. Madonna liked him for her videos.

name: Joan Branson
headline: Joan Branson, Richard Branson’s Wife of 35 Years, Dies at 80
abstract: Mr. Branson, the Virgin Group founder and one of Britain’s best known business figures, announced her death in an Instagram post.

name: Eli Zeira
profession: Israeli Official Dismissed Warnings of Yom Kippur War
headline: Eli Zeira, 97, Dies; Israeli Official Dismissed Warnings of Yom Kippur War
abstract: As Israel’s head of military intelligence, he disregarded signs Egypt and Syria were about to attack in 1973. A commission blamed him for the lack of preparation.

name: Miroslaw Chojecki
headline: Miroslaw Chojecki, Solidarity’s ‘Minister of Smuggling,’ Dies at 76
abstract: First in Warsaw and later from Paris, he supplied anti-Communist activists in Poland with steady stream of leaflets, newsletters and banned books.

name: David Lerner
headline: David Lerner, a Mr. Fix-it of Apple Computers, Dies at 72
abstract: He and a partner founded Tekserve, a Manhattan emergency room for frozen hard drives, keyboards, screens and their confounded owners.

name: Paul Ekman
profession: Linked Facial Expressions to Universal Emotions
headline: Paul Ekman, Who Linked Facial Expressions to Universal Emotions, Dies at 91
abstract: Often called the world’s most famous face reader, he inspired the TV show ‘Lie to Me.’ But some questioned his assumption that human expressions were ‘pan-cultural.’

name: Robert A.M. Stern
headline: Robert A.M. Stern, Architect Who Reinvented Prewar Splendor, Dies at 86
abstract: He designed museums, schools and libraries before winning international acclaim late in life for 15 Central Park West in Manhattan, hailed as a rebirth of the luxury apartment building.

name: Ruth Thorne-Thomsen
headline: Ruth Thorne-Thomsen, Photographer of Dreamlike Tableaux, Dies at 82
abstract: Using a pinhole camera, she captured miniature landscapes that she had fashioned to resemble surreal versions of 19th-century travel photos.

name: Ellen Bryant Voigt
headline: Ellen Bryant Voigt, Poet With a Musical Ear, Dies at 82
abstract: Her nine volumes included “Kyrie,” a suite of sonnets about the 1918 influenza epidemic. She was also Pulitzer Prize finalist and a poet laureate of Vermont.

name: Walter Dowdle
profession: Public Health Leader in Times of Crises
headline: Walter Dowdle, Public Health Leader in Times of Crises, Dies at 94
abstract: Dr. Dowdle, a microbiologist who became the No. 2 official at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, helped lead the nation’s response to AIDS.

name: Tom Stoppard
headline: Tom Stoppard, Award-Winning Playwright of Witty Drama, Dies at 88
abstract: Drawing comparisons to the greatest of dramatists, he entwined erudition with imagination in stage works that won accolades on both sides of the Atlantic.

name: Colleen Jones
headline: Colleen Jones, Curling Champion and Broadcaster, Dies at 65
abstract: She won two world titles and six Canadian national championships, and was also a television anchor, reporter and commentator.

name: Fuzzy Zoeller
profession: Won Two Majors on the PGA Tour
headline: Fuzzy Zoeller, Who Won Two Majors on the PGA Tour, Dies at 74
abstract: He was a witty and popular figure, but his racially insensitive remarks about Tiger Woods at the 1997 Masters led to death threats and many apologies.

name: James Riches
headline: James Riches, Fire Chief Who Lost Firefighter Son on 9/11, Dies at 74
abstract: He spent months searching the wreckage of the World Trade Center for his son’s remains, then suffered lung illnesses attributed to toxic dust.

name: Biyouna
profession: Algerian Star With Tart Tongue Onscreen and Off
headline: Biyouna, Algerian Star With Tart Tongue Onscreen and Off, Dies at 73
abstract: For generations of Algerians, the fierce independence of her persona reflected their struggles in a country torn by civil war and repression.

name: Daniel Woodrell
profession: Country Noir Novelist of Winters Bone
headline: Daniel Woodrell, ‘Country Noir’ Novelist of ‘Winter’s Bone,’ Dies at 72
abstract: His tales of violence and squalor in his native Ozarks had the timeless quality of fables and inspired several movies.

name: Kai Erikson
headline: Kai Erikson, Sociologist Who Probed Invisible Scars of Disasters, Dies at 94
abstract: A professor at Yale, he immersed himself in communities after catastrophic events like Three Mile Island, the Exxon Valdez oil spill and Hurricane Katrina.

name: Reginald T. Jackson
headline: Reginald T. Jackson, A.M.E. Bishop Who Helped Sway Votes, Dies at 71
abstract: Influential from New Jersey to Georgia, he was part of a long tradition among Black clergy of fighting bias and getting out the vote. “No vote, no clout,” he’d say.

name: Eugene Hasenfus
headline: Eugene Hasenfus, Gunrunner Who Exposed Iran-Contra Plot, Dies at 84
abstract: He emerged out of obscurity when his cargo plane was shot down while illegally ferrying arms to Nicaraguan rebels, setting off a scandal that tarnished the Reagan and Bush White Houses.

name: David Pryce-Jones
headline: David Pryce-Jones, Conservative Writer With Clout, Dies at 89
abstract: The author of novels, histories, biographies and influential political essays, he approached them all with a droll British wit and a steadfast commitment to Western values.

name: Yegor Ligachev
headline: Yegor Ligachev, Gorbachev’s No. 2 Who Turned Foe, Is Dead at 100
abstract: As the Kremlin’s hard-line Communist ideologist, he initially embraced his boss’s modernizing reforms before turning against them as threats to the Soviet order.

name: Ludwig Minelli
headline: Ludwig Minelli, Founder of Swiss Assisted-Suicide Group, Dies at 92
abstract: Dignitas has helped more than 3,000 people take their own lives, an act that Mr. Minelli maintained was a fundamental exercise of free will.

name: Mel Leipzig
profession: Painter Called the Chekhov of Trenton
headline: Mel Leipzig, Painter Called the ‘Chekhov of Trenton,’ Dies at 90
abstract: He put fellow New Jerseyans at the center of his work, and a critic praised the “mysterious emotional tensions” in his pictures of ordinary people.

name: Steve Cropper
headline: Steve Cropper, Guitarist, Songwriter and Shaper of Memphis Soul Music, Dies at 84
abstract: As a member of Booker T. & the MG’s and as a producer, he played a pivotal role in the rise of Stax Records, a storied force in R&B in the 1960s and ’70s.

name: Charles Norman Shay
profession: Tribal Elder and World War II Hero
headline: Charles Norman Shay, Tribal Elder and World War II Hero, Dies at 101
abstract: As a medic, he saved soldiers from drowning off Omaha Beach on D-Day before becoming a prisoner of war. Back home, a decorated veteran, he was forbidden to vote as a Native American.

name: Dorothy Wise
headline: Overlooked No More: Dorothy Wise, the ‘Grandmother of Pool’ Who Defied the Odds
abstract: She elbowed her way into what had long been a man’s game and won the first women’s national championship in 1967 — and then repeated the feat four more years in a row.

name: Dominik Duka
headline: Dominik Duka, Czech Cardinal Jailed Under Communism, Dies at 82
abstract: While in prison in 1981, he befriended the dissident and future Czech president Vaclav Havel. Later, he became a conservative voice in Rome.

name: Rebecca Heineman
headline: Rebecca Heineman, Transgender Video Game Pioneer, Dies at 62
abstract: Fleeing an abusive home life, she went on to win a national Space Invaders tournament, taught herself to program and left a trail of popular games in her wake.

name: Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa
profession: Last Emperor and Mortal Kombat Actor
headline: Cary-Hiroyuki Tagawa, ‘The Last Emperor’ and ‘Mortal Kombat’ Actor, Dies at 75
abstract: The actor, born in Japan, starred in dozens of film and television shows, including Amazon’s “The Man in the High Castle.” His career spanned more than three decades.

name: Frank Gehry
headline: Frank Gehry, Titan of Architecture, Is Dead at 96
abstract: He designed some of the world’s most recognizable buildings, notably the spectacular Guggenheim Museum Bilbao, his masterpiece.

name: Erik Bulatov
headline: Erik Bulatov, Russian Painter Who Undermined Soviet Propaganda, Dies at 92
abstract: For years he lived a double life, secretly making anti-Communist paintings. He found fame in the late 1980s, once his work was shown outside the Soviet Union.

name: Hamilton O. Smith
headline: Hamilton O. Smith, Who Made a Biotech Breakthrough, Is Dead at 94
abstract: A Nobel laureate, he identified an enzyme that cuts DNA, laying the groundwork for milestones in scientific research and medicine, like insulin.

name: Chuck Kesey
headline: Chuck Kesey, Probiotic Yogurt Pioneer, Dies at 87
abstract: The younger brother of Ken Kesey, the novelist and counterculture luminary, he turned a defunct creamery into what is now Nancy’s Probiotic Foods.

name: Robert B. Fiske Jr.
headline: Robert B. Fiske Jr., First to Lead Whitewater Investigation, Dies at 94
abstract: He had overseen high-profile cases as a private lawyer and a U.S. attorney in New York when he was named to examine the role of Bill and Hillary Clinton in a failed development venture.

name: Pam Hogg
headline: Pam Hogg, Clothes Designer Who Went to Extremes, Dies at 74
abstract: She was a star of London’s post-punk D.I.Y. fashion, art and performance scene, and dressed a generation of rock stars in her otherworldly handmade clothes.

name: Guy Cogeval
headline: Guy Cogeval, Boundary-Pushing Museum Director, Dies at 70
abstract: His innovative approach drew crowds to the Musée d’Orsay, one of France’s flagship cultural institutions, which he led from 2008 to 2017.

name: Martin Parr
headline: Martin Parr Dies at 73; Photographed Britain’s Unvarnished Quirks
abstract: Calling his work “subjective documentary,” he seemed to take an almost anthropological delight in chronicling the absurdities of human behavior.

name: Fern Michaels
headline: Fern Michaels, Prolific Author of Romance Novels, Dies at 92
abstract: In her 40s, the self-described New Jersey housewife started building a women’s fiction empire, churning out dozens of popular books.

name: Cora Weiss
headline: Cora Weiss, Lifelong Champion of Social Justice, Dies at 91
abstract: With a group called Women Strike for Peace, she helped organize demonstrations against the Vietnam War and nuclear weapons. “We managed to get things done,” she said.

name: Donald E. Petersen
headline: Donald E. Petersen, 97, Who Rescued Ford Motor Co., Is Dead
abstract: An ex-Marine and a 40-year company veteran, he turned a nearly bankrupt money loser into the world’s most profitable automaker.

name: John Noble Wilford
headline: John Noble Wilford, Times Reporter Who Covered the Moon Landing, Dies at 92
abstract: He gave readers a comprehensive and lyrical account of the historic mission in 1969. His science coverage as a Pulitzer-winning journalist and an author took him around the world.

name: Iain Douglas-Hamilton
headline: Iain Douglas-Hamilton, Who Studied, and Protected, Elephants, Dies at 83
abstract: Born into an aristocratic British family, he turned his empathy and knowledge of the world’s largest land mammals to the cause of saving them from poachers.

name: Raul Malo
profession: Frontman of Latin-Tinged Country Band Mavericks
headline: Raul Malo, Frontman of Latin-Tinged Country Band Mavericks, Dies at 60
abstract: As the group’s singer and principal songwriter, he brought a new sound that broadened the boundaries of country music in the 1990s.

name: DéLana R.A. Dameron
headline: DéLana R.A. Dameron, Writer of the Black South, Dies at 40
abstract: An award-winning poet and writer of fiction, she moonlighted as a competitive horsewoman and owned a horse farm outside Columbia, S.C.

name: Rod Paige
headline: Rod Paige, Education Secretary Who Defended ‘No Child Left Behind,’ Dies at 92
abstract: The first Black person to hold that cabinet position, he resigned amid discord over George W. Bush’s major legislative effort to improve public education nationwide.

name: Sophie Kinsella
headline: Sophie Kinsella, ‘Confessions of a Shopaholic’ Author, Dies at 55
abstract: Writing under a pseudonym, Madeleine Wickham cultivated an international following for her series centered on a young woman addicted to shopping.

name: Stephen Downing
headline: Stephen Downing, Police Officer Who Wrote for TV, Dies at 87
abstract: While serving in the L.A.P.D., he began delivering scripts for series like “Dragnet” and “Adam-12.” After retiring, he was a showrunner for “MacGyver.”

name: Donald McIntyre
profession: Starred in New Vision of Wagners Operas
headline: Donald McIntyre, 91, Dies; Starred in New Vision of Wagner’s Operas
abstract: As Wotan in Patrice Chéreau’s neo-Marxist staging of the “Ring” cycle, he was part of a celebrated, polarizing moment in opera history.

name: George Altman
headline: George Altman, Slugger in Negro Leagues, M.L.B. and Japan, Dies at 92
abstract: The rare player to compete in all three, he had an impressive career, becoming a three-time All-Star in the major leagues and later a fan favorite in Japan.

name: R. Bruce Dold
profession: Chicago Tribune Publisher and Pulitzer Winner
headline: R. Bruce Dold, Chicago Tribune Publisher and Pulitzer Winner, Dies at 70
abstract: As head of the editorial page, he encouraged The Tribune’s support of Barack Obama, resulting in the paper’s first endorsement of a Democrat running for the White House.

name: Thomas O. Hicks
headline: Thomas O. Hicks, Texas Money Man Who Owned 3 Teams, Dies at 79
abstract: A master of leveraged buyouts, he bought baseball and hockey teams in Texas and an English soccer club, only to lose them in an avalanche of debt.

name: D.L. Coburn
headline: D.L. Coburn, Playwright With a Sole Hit, ‘The Gin Game,’ Dies at 87
abstract: His two-character work won a Pulitzer Prize and had a long Broadway run, but he never replicated its success and struggled to get his later work staged.

name: Joanna Trollope
headline: Joanna Trollope, Popular British Author, Dies at 82
abstract: Her books, many of which were best sellers, often described empty marriages, love affairs (with tasteful sex) and heroic clergymen.

name: Joseph Byrd
headline: Joseph Byrd, Who Shook Up Psychedelic Rock, Dies at 87
abstract: A veteran of the Fluxus art movement, he brought an anarchic spirit to the California acid-rock scene with his band, the United States of America.

name: Arthur L. Carter
profession: Investment Banker Founded a Cheeky Newspaper
headline: Arthur L. Carter, 93, Dies; Investment Banker Founded a Cheeky Newspaper
abstract: After making a fortune on Wall Street, he bought The Nation magazine and founded The New York Observer, which one writer called a “maypole of Manhattan gossip and intrigue.”

name: Phil Upchurch
profession: Jazz Guitarist and Sideman to Stars
headline: Phil Upchurch, Jazz Guitarist and Sideman to Stars, Dies at 84
abstract: A self-taught session man extraordinaire, he played with a constellation of stars, including Michael Jackson, Curtis Mayfield, Chaka Khan and Dizzy Gillespie.

name: Marina Yee
headline: Marina Yee, Elusive Avant-Garde Designer, Dies at 67
abstract: She was one of the Antwerp Six, young Belgians who upended the fashion industry with their innovative designs and turned their country into an unlikely style hub.

name: Jo Ann Allen Boyce
profession: Braved Mobs in Integrating a School
headline: Jo Ann Allen Boyce Dies at 84; Braved Mobs in Integrating a School
abstract: She was one of the Clinton 12, Black students who broke a race barrier by entering a Tennessee high school in 1956 in the face of harassment by white segregationists.

name: Roy Kramer
headline: Roy Kramer, Transformational Executive in College Sports, Dies at 96
abstract: Leading the Southeastern Conference for 12 years, he masterminded its rise as a national power, lifted by a flood of money from TV rights, bowl games and other sources.

name: Peter Greene
profession: Pulp Fiction and The Mask Actor
headline: Peter Greene, ‘Pulp Fiction’ and ‘The Mask’ Actor, Dies at 60
abstract: Mr. Greene, who built a four-decade career uncannily portraying villains, was found dead in his apartment in Manhattan on Friday, his manager said.

name: Abraham Quintanilla Jr.
profession: Music Producer Steered Daughter Selenas Career
headline: Abraham Quintanilla Jr., 86, Dies; Music Producer Steered Daughter Selena’s Career
abstract: As a teenager, he hoped to make it big in the Tejano music world. He realized that dream through his daughter.

name: Jeanette Winter
headline: Jeanette Winter, Who Told Children About Artists’ Lives, Dies at 86
abstract: Her picture books found models of perseverance and imagination in figures like Emily Dickinson, Georgia O’Keeffe and Benny Goodman.

name: Rob Reiner
headline: Rob Reiner, Actor Who Went on to Direct Classic Films, Dies at 78
abstract: After finding fame in “All in the Family,” he directed winning films like “This Is Spinal Tap,” “When Harry Met Sally … ” and “The Princess Bride” and got involved in liberal politics.

name: Anthony Geary
headline: Anthony Geary, Luke on ‘General Hospital,’ Dies at 78
abstract: Portraying Luke Spencer, he was one of the best-known soap opera stars in American television. His onscreen romance with Laura Webber, played by Genie Francis, changed the landscape of daytime television.

name: Robert J. Samuelson
headline: Robert J. Samuelson, Award-Winning Economics Columnist, Dies at 79
abstract: He was a familiar byline in Newsweek and The Washington Post for decades, explaining the intricacies of economic policy in reader-friendly vernacular.

name: Joe Ely
profession: Texas-Born Troubadour of the Open Road
headline: Joe Ely, Texas-Born Troubadour of the Open Road, Dies at 78
abstract: Thanks to his eclectic style and tireless touring, he was among the most influential artists in the early days of Americana and alt-country music.

name: Ruth Kiew
profession: Botanist Made Discoveries in Remote Forests
headline: Ruth Kiew Dies at 79; Botanist Made Discoveries in Remote Forests
abstract: Trekking across Malaysia, her adopted country, she found more than 150 unrecorded plant species. “She’s one of the greatest botanists who ever lived,” a colleague said.

name: Norman Podhoretz
headline: Norman Podhoretz, Literary Lion of Neoconservatism, Dies at 95
abstract: A New York intellectual and onetime liberal stalwart, his Commentary magazine became his platform as his political and social views turned sharply rightward.

name: Gil Gerard
profession: Star of TV Series Buck Rogers
headline: Gil Gerard, Star of TV Series ‘Buck Rogers,’ Dies at 82
abstract: He was best known for playing the title character in “Buck Rogers in the 25th Century,” which ran on NBC from 1979 to 1981.

name: Ceal Floyer
headline: Ceal Floyer, Incisive Conceptual Artist, Dies at 57
abstract: Her work had a clean, minimal aesthetic at odds with the ambiguities it suggested. It was also unusually accessible.

name: Christine Choy
headline: Christine Choy, Documentarian of Asian American Life, Dies at 76
abstract: Her film “Who Killed Vincent Chin?” earned an Oscar nomination in 1988 and was inducted into the National Film Registry for its cultural significance.

name: Hans van Manen
headline: Hans van Manen, Celebrated Dutch Choreographer, Is Dead at 93
abstract: He rose from poverty to become one of the Netherlands’ most revered dance makers, creating more than 150 works in a career spanning eight decades.

name: Peter Arnett
headline: Peter Arnett, Pulitzer-Winning War Correspondent, Dies at 91
abstract: He won the award for his daring coverage of the Vietnam War for The Associated Press. He went on to cover conflicts for CNN for nearly two decades.

name: John E. Olson
headline: John E. Olson, Analyst Fired for Enron Skepticism, Dies at 83
abstract: Working for Merrill Lynch, he refused to recommend the energy trading company. His employer pushed him out, but his stand made him a hero.

name: Sue Bender
profession: Wrote About Living With the Amish
headline: Sue Bender, Who Wrote About Living With the Amish, Dies at 91
abstract: “Plain and Simple,” her best-selling 1989 book, was a go-to text of the anti-materialist movement known as voluntary simplicity.

name: James B. Hunt Jr.
headline: James B. Hunt Jr., Governor Who Kept North Carolina Blue, Dies at 88
abstract: During his 16 years in office, he earned national acclaim for his focus on education. But losing his bid for the Senate in 1984 cost him a shot at the presidency.

name: Theodor Pistek
headline: Theodor Pistek, 93, Oscar-Winning ‘Amadeus’ Costume Designer, Dies
abstract: He worked on more than 100 films, but that wasn’t all: He was also a racecar driver and a painter of photorealistic works, many depicting cars.

name: Rafael Ithier
headline: Rafael Ithier, Ambassador of Puerto Rican Music, Dies at 99
abstract: Leading the acclaimed salsa group El Gran Combo de Puerto Rico, he brought the music of his native island to a worldwide audience for more than 60 years.

name: Emily Korzenik
headline: Emily Korzenik, Rabbi Who Took a Bar Mitzvah to Poland, Dies at 96
abstract: Among the first women to be ordained in America, she went to Krakow, still scarred by the Holocaust, to preside over the rite, the first there in decades. It didn’t go smoothly.

name: Allan Ludwig
headline: Allan Ludwig, ‘Founding Father’ of Gravestone Studies, Dies at 92
abstract: His Pulitzer-nominated book “Graven Images” inspired a reassessment of Puritan art, challenging the belief that imagery carved on headstones was meaningless.

name: Lou Cannon
profession: Journalist Chronicled Reagan as an Author
headline: Lou Cannon Dies at 92; Journalist Chronicled Reagan as an Author
abstract: He was a foremost authority on the president, tracing his career in unvarnished accounts from his time as California governor through his years in the White House.

name: Robert Mnuchin
headline: Robert Mnuchin, Stock Trader Turned Art Dealer, Dies at 92
abstract: A major player in the block-trading boom, he left Wall Street for the art world, winning a Jeff Koons sculpture at auction for $91 million in 2019.

name: Inge Lehmann
headline: Overlooked No More: Inge Lehmann, Who Discovered the Earth’s Inner Core
abstract: She pointed to evidence that the Earth’s inner core was solid — not liquid, as scientists had believed — a discovery that was ahead of its time.

name: Kevin Arkadie
headline: Kevin Arkadie, ‘New York Undercover’ Co-Creator, Dies at 68
abstract: The screenwriter and producer created several television hits about law enforcement. He made one of the first police dramas to star two main characters of color.

name: James Ransone
headline: James Ransone, Actor Known for ‘The Wire,’ Dies at 46
abstract: The character actor had grown up in Maryland, where “The Wire” was set, and went on to star in horror films like “It Chapter Two.”

name: Betty Reid Soskin
headline: Betty Reid Soskin, Nation’s Oldest Park Ranger, Dies at 104
abstract: She began working as a park ranger at age 85, educating visitors about the women and people of color who served on the home front in World War II, herself among them.

name: Jerry Kasenetz
headline: Jerry Kasenetz, a King of Bubblegum Pop Music, Dies at 82
abstract: With his producing partner, Jeffry Katz, he made lightweight ditties like “Yummy Yummy Yummy” that soared up the charts in the late 1960s.

name: Chris Rea
headline: Chris Rea, British Singer-Songwriter and Hitmaker, Dies at 74
abstract: A blues-influenced guitarist, he built a lasting career, particularly in Europe, with soft-rock ballads like “Driving Home for Christmas” and “Fool (If You Think It’s Over).”

name: Vince Zampella
profession: Formative Designer of Call of Duty Games
headline: Vince Zampella, Formative Designer of Call of Duty Games, Dies at 55
abstract: Mr. Zampella co-founded two game studios and also worked on the Medal of Honor, Titanfall and Battlefield franchises.

name: May Britt
profession: Her Marriage to Sammy Davis Jr. Sparked Outrage
headline: May Britt, 91, Dies; Her Marriage to Sammy Davis Jr. Sparked Outrage
abstract: She was a white actress, he was a popular Black entertainer, and their relationship elicited racist reactions in 1960, worrying John F. Kennedy’s presidential campaign.

name: Robert Nakamura
headline: Robert Nakamura, ‘Godfather’ of Asian American Film, Dies at 88
abstract: In his work, he often returned to Manzanar, the camp in which he and his family, along with thousands of other people of Japanese descent, were interned during World War II.

name: Phyllis Lee Levin
headline: Phyllis Lee Levin, Times Fashion Reporter and Biographer, Dies at 104
abstract: Her 1960 essay about the frustrations of educated women prefigured Betty Friedan’s “The Feminine Mystique.” She later wrote books on John Quincy Adams and others.

name: Lewis Berman
headline: Lewis Berman, Veterinarian to the Stars, Is Dead at 90
abstract: He served a New York clientele with names like Kennedy, Kissinger, Fonda, Bacall and Trump by making sure Chappy, Buzzy, Spike and other cherished pets stayed healthy.

name: Peng Peiyun
headline: Peng Peiyun, 95, Dies; Official Renounced China’s One-Child Policy
abstract: She was given the “hardest job under heaven”: upholding birth limits enforced by often brutal local officials. She came to support softening the policy, then abolishing it.

name: Robert Lindsey
headline: Robert Lindsey, Times Reporter and Reagan Ghostwriter, Dies at 90
abstract: The nonfiction spy thriller “The Falcon and the Snowman,” which became a film, grew out of his work as a journalist covering the West Coast for The Times.

name: John Carey
headline: John Carey, Literary Eminence Who Excoriated Snobbery, Dies at 91
abstract: An Oxford professor and renowned critic, he was pugnacious, fearless and disdainful of the received wisdom of his intellectual milieu.

name: Michal Urbaniak
headline: Michal Urbaniak, Pioneering Jazz Fusion Violinist, Dies at 82
abstract: One of the first jazz musicians from Poland to gain an international following, he recorded more than 60 albums and played with stars like Miles Davis.

name: Perry Bamonte
profession: Guitarist and Keyboardist for the Cure
headline: Perry Bamonte, Guitarist and Keyboardist for the Cure, Dies at 65
abstract: A former roadie, he joined the band in 1990, played on five albums and in hundreds of shows, and was “a vital part of the Cure story.”

name: Annette Dionne
headline: Annette Dionne, Last of the Celebrated Quintuplets, Dies at 91
abstract: She was the first to crawl, the first to cut a tooth, the first to recognize her name, and the last to die. And, like her sisters, she resented being exploited as part of a global sensation.

name: Gary Graffman
headline: Gary Graffman, Piano Virtuoso and Renowned Teacher, Dies at 97
abstract: Mr. Graffman was a child prodigy whose career was curtailed by a neurological condition that restricted him to his left hand.

name: Joseph Hartzler
profession: Led Prosecution of Oklahoma City Bomber
headline: Joseph Hartzler Dies at 75; Led Prosecution of Oklahoma City Bomber
abstract: He and his team secured the conviction of Timothy McVeigh, who in 1995 committed the deadliest domestic terror attack in American history.

name: Brigitte Bardot
headline: Brigitte Bardot, Movie Idol Who Renounced Stardom, Dies at 91
abstract: “And God Created Woman” made her a world-famous sex symbol in the 1950s. She later gave up acting to devote her life to animal welfare.

name: Don Bryant
profession: Co-Wrote I Cant Stand the Rain for His Wife
headline: Don Bryant, 83, Dies; Co-Wrote ‘I Can’t Stand the Rain’ for His Wife
abstract: He and Ann Peebles made up one of Southern soul’s most accomplished partnerships. He finally broke through as a solo act at 75.

name: Melanie Watson Bernhardt
headline: Melanie Watson Bernhardt, ‘Diff’rent Strokes’ Actress, Dies at 57
abstract: Her four episodes on the sitcom marked a rarity: a disabled actress onscreen.

name: Louis V. Gerstner
profession: Revived a Faltering IBM in the 90s
headline: Louis V. Gerstner, Who Revived a Faltering IBM in the ’90s, Dies at 83
abstract: Installed as an outsider, he engineered a comeback, shifting the company’s focus from a waning mainframe computer business toward consulting and services.

name: Khaleda Zia
headline: Khaleda Zia, Bangladesh’s First Female Prime Minister, Dies
abstract: In office for three terms, she traded the country’s leadership with Sheikh Hasina, the head of another political dynasty, over decades. She was believed to be 80.

name: Carmen de Lavallade
headline: Carmen de Lavallade, Dancer Whose Career Spanned the Arts, Dies at 94
abstract: Over six decades she worked in theater, opera, film and television alongside luminaries like Alvin Ailey, Lena Horne, Agnes de Mille and Harry Belafonte.

name: Tatiana Schlossberg
headline: Tatiana Schlossberg, Kennedy Daughter Who Wrote of Her Cancer, Dies at 35
abstract: An environmental journalist and child of Caroline Kennedy, she wrote of her struggle with leukemia in The New Yorker in November, drawing worldwide sympathy.

name: Masashi Ozaki
profession: Japans Dominant Golfer Known as Jumbo
headline: Masashi Ozaki, Japan’s Dominant Golfer Known as ‘Jumbo,’ Dies at 78
abstract: A World Golf Hall of Famer who could drive a ball more than 300 yards in his prime, he recorded 113 victories.

name: Ben Nighthorse Campbell
headline: Ben Nighthorse Campbell, Native American Senator, Dies at 92
abstract: A Colorado Democrat turned Republican, he was the only Native American during three terms in the House and 12 years in the Senate. He was also a judo expert and an Olympian.

name: Isiah Whitlock Jr.
profession: Scene-Stealing Character Actor in The Wire
headline: Isiah Whitlock Jr., 71, Scene-Stealing Character Actor in ‘The Wire,’ Dies
abstract: He was reliably versatile across TV and screen roles and a regular presence in Spike Lee movies like “25th Hour,” “BlacKkKlansman” and “Da 5 Bloods.”

name: Richard Smallwood
profession: Choral Leader and Composer of Gospel Hits
headline: Richard Smallwood, 77, Choral Leader and Composer of Gospel Hits, Dies
abstract: He sold millions of albums with the Richard Smallwood Singers, and his songs, many influenced by classical music, were recorded by stars like Whitney Houston.

name: Mohammad Bakri
headline: Mohammad Bakri, Palestinian Whose Film Was Banned in Israel, Dies at 72
abstract: His 2002 documentary “Jenin, Jenin” exposed the often harsh realities of life experienced by his fellow Arabs in Israel.

name: Jacqueline de Ribes
headline: Jacqueline de Ribes, Tastemaker and Fashion Avatar, Dies at 96
abstract: One of few people in the world of style who could legitimately claim the status of icon, she dressed to impress even before she became a designer.

name: Janet Fish
headline: Janet Fish, Painter of Luminous Still Lifes, Dies at 87
abstract: From her student days, she stubbornly refused to follow popular artistic trends. Instead, she spent decades exploring the effects of light on glass.

name: Richard Pollak
headline: Richard Pollak, 91, Dies; Edited Magazine That Criticized the Media
abstract: He was a founder of More, which skewered the foibles of the press in the 1970s, and later wrote a critical biography of the psychoanalyst Bruno Bettelheim.

name: Pamela Colman Smith
profession: Artist Behind a Famous Tarot Deck
headline: Overlooked No More: Pamela Colman Smith, Artist Behind a Famous Tarot Deck
abstract: She hand-painted around 80 illustrations for the Rider-Waite deck, which is still used around the world to predict destinies.

name: Dick Zimmer
headline: Dick Zimmer, N.J. Congressman Who Sponsored Megan’s Law, Dies at 81
abstract: The landmark legislation, a response to the rape and murder of a New Jersey child, required states to disclose where convicted sex-offenders live.

name: Diane Crump
profession: First Woman to Ride in Kentucky Derby
headline: Diane Crump, First Woman to Ride in Kentucky Derby, Dies at 77
abstract: She was the first professional female jockey to compete at a track in the United States where betting was legal, and notched up 228 career victories.

name: Asad Haider
headline: Asad Haider, Leftist Critic of Identity Politics, Dies at 38
abstract: In “Mistaken Identity: Race and Class in the Age of Trump,” he argued that focusing on identity obscured a more fundamental injustice: economic inequality.

name: Francis Patrelle
headline: Francis Patrelle, Champion of the Story Ballet, Dies at 78
abstract: Founding his own company, he built a tightly knit community in New York around his classes. His “Nutcracker,” set in the city in 1895, was his most popular production.

name: Robert Heide
headline: Robert Heide, Daring Playwright and Warhol Collaborator, Dies at 91
abstract: He helped create the Off Off Broadway theater scene, wrote and acted in Andy Warhol’s films, and turned his fascination with collectible Americana into books.

name: Ahn Sung Ki
profession: Towering Figure in South Korean Film
headline: Ahn Sung Ki, Towering Figure in South Korean Film, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Ahn, who made his onscreen debut as a 5-year-old, appeared in more than 180 films. President Lee Jae-myung said he “left a great footprint in Korean film history.”

name: Eva Schloss
profession: Anne Franks Stepsister and Holocaust Survivor
headline: Eva Schloss, Anne Frank’s Stepsister and Holocaust Survivor, Dies at 96
abstract: Freed from Auschwitz, she was silent about her ordeal for four decades. Then she decided to dedicate her life to educating people about the dangers of prejudice.

name: Steve Sheetz
profession: Popularized Convenience Stores as a C.E.O
headline: Steve Sheetz, Who Popularized Convenience Stores as a C.E.O., Dies at 77
abstract: Sheetz, a family-owned company that started with a single convenience store in Altoona, Pa., has more than 800 locations in seven states.

name: Bela Tarr
headline: Bela Tarr, Titan of Slow-Moving Cinema, Dies at 70
abstract: The master Hungarian filmmaker’s movies included “Satantango” and “Werckmeister Harmonies.”

name: Doug LaMalfa
headline: Doug LaMalfa, Who Championed Rural California in Congress, Dies at 65
abstract: A Republican in the House since 2013, he portrayed himself as a voice for his constituents in his northeast district. His death narrowed his party’s slim majority in the chamber.

name: Rosa von Praunheim
profession: Captured Gay Life in Germany on Film
headline: Rosa von Praunheim, 83, Dies; Captured Gay Life in Germany on Film
abstract: His first feature-length movie, in 1971, was called his country’s “Stonewall moment,” for jump-starting a gay-rights movement. He became a leading voice of it.

name: Aldrich Ames
headline: Aldrich Ames, C.I.A. Turncoat Who Helped the Soviets, Dies at 84
abstract: As chief of the counterintelligence branch of the C.I.A.’s Soviet division, he had access to some of the nation’s deepest secrets. He had been serving a life sentence since 1994.

name: Michael Reagan
profession: Presidents Son Fought for Right-Wing Causes
headline: Michael Reagan, 80 Dies; President’s Son Fought for Right-Wing Causes
abstract: The son of Ronald Reagan and his first wife, the actress Jane Wyman, he built on his father’s conservative legacy with a radio talk show and columns on right-wing sites like Newsmax.

name: Bruce Crawford
headline: Bruce Crawford, Arts-Loving Adman Who Led the Met Opera, Dies at 96
abstract: He helped build the ad agency BBDO International into a powerhouse before channeling his passion for opera into managing the Met and revitalizing Lincoln Center.

name: Arthur Cohn
profession: Film Producer With an Oscar-Winning Touch
headline: Arthur Cohn, Film Producer With an Oscar-Winning Touch, Dies at 98
abstract: Six of his movies received Academy Awards, including the Italian drama “The Garden of the Finzi-Continis” and the trade-union strike documentary “American Dream.”

name: Glenn Hall
headline: Glenn Hall, Pathbreaking All-Star Hockey Goalie, Dies at 94
abstract: Known as “Mr. Goalie,” he created the so-called butterfly style and played in a record 502 consecutive games, without wearing a mask. He received 300 stitches.

name: Lynda Blackmon Lowery
profession: One of the Youngest Selma Marchers
headline: Lynda Blackmon Lowery, One of the Youngest Selma Marchers, Dies at 75
abstract: Her activism began as a teenager in 1963, when she heard the Rev. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. speak. It set her on a path to nonviolent protest.

name: Ron Protas
profession: Polarizing Keeper of Martha Grahams Legacy
headline: Ron Protas, Polarizing Keeper of Martha Graham’s Legacy, Dies at 84
abstract: Graham, the great modern dance choreographer, named him her heir, setting off a bitter legal battle between him and the troupe she founded.

name: Amos Poe
profession: New Yorks No Wave Film Pioneer
headline: Amos Poe, New York’s No Wave Film Pioneer, Dies at 76
abstract: He documented the punk and post-punk music scene in the East Village, leading an independent film movement that was proudly unprofessional.

name: Jerome Lowenstein
profession: Teaching Doctor With a Literary Sideline
headline: Jerome Lowenstein, 92, Dies; Teaching Doctor With a Literary Sideline
abstract: When not guiding students in a compassionate approach to patient care, he led a tiny publishing imprint that put out a much-rejected debut novel that won a surprise Pulitzer Prize.

name: Thomas V. Cash
headline: Thomas V. Cash, Cartel-Busting D.E.A. Chief in Miami, Dies at 85
abstract: He helped take down the Panamanian strongman Manuel Noriega and the Colombian drug kingpin Pablo Escobar.

name: Joel Habener
headline: Joel Habener, Whose Research Led to Weight-Loss Drugs, Dies at 88
abstract: His discovery of the protein fragment GLP-1 was crucial in the development of Ozempic, Wegovy and other blockbuster obesity and diabetes treatments.

name: Bahram Beyzaie
headline: Bahram Beyzaie, Filmmaker Who Led Iran’s New Wave, Dies at 87
abstract: Despite a ceaseless battle against government censors, he was celebrated as one of his country’s greatest auteurs, winning praise from luminaries like Martin Scorsese.

name: Hessy Levinsons Taft
profession: Jewish Baby on Cover of Nazi Magazine
headline: Hessy Levinsons Taft, Jewish Baby on Cover of Nazi Magazine, Dies at 91
abstract: Without her parents’ knowledge, her portrait was entered as a prank in a contest in 1935 to represent the ideal Aryan infant — and she won.

name: Mohammed Harbi
headline: Mohammed Harbi, Who Rewrote Algeria’s History, Dies at 92
abstract: He was an official in the revolutionary government, then, after the country won independence from France, was imprisoned and eventually wrote from exile.

name: Stewart Cheifet
headline: Stewart Cheifet, Host of TV’s ‘Computer Chronicles,’ Dies at 87
abstract: He spent two decades hosting the PBS series, during the formative years of personal computing. It was seen in more than 300 cities at its peak.

name: Bob Weir
profession: Guitarist and Founding Member of the Grateful
headline: Bob Weir, Guitarist and Founding Member of the Grateful Dead, Dies at 78
abstract: His songwriting and rhythm guitar playing helped shape the San Francisco band’s sound as it became an American institution.

name: Erich von Däniken
headline: Erich von Däniken, Who Claimed Aliens Visited Earth, Dies at 90
abstract: His 1968 book, “Chariots of the Gods,” sold hundreds of thousands of copies, but one critic called it a “warped parody of reasoning.”

name: Richard Codey
profession: New Jersey Acting Governor Many Times Over
headline: Richard Codey, a New Jersey Acting Governor Many Times Over, Dies at 79
abstract: He was the state’s longest-serving legislator, and as president of its Senate he was frequently called on to serve as a fill-in governor, being next in line of succession.

name: Jirdes Winther Baxter
profession: Last Survivor of Epidemic in Alaska
headline: Jirdes Winther Baxter, 101, Dies; Last Survivor of Epidemic in Alaska
abstract: An outbreak of diphtheria inspired a celebrated sled dog relay of nearly 700 miles to deliver lifesaving serum to the remote town of Nome.

name: Daniel Walker Howe
headline: Daniel Walker Howe, 88, Revisionist Historian of Jackson’s America, Dies
abstract: In a Pulitzer-winning book, he saw modern America’s origins not so much in one president’s policies as in the sweeping social and technological changes wrought in the years 1815-48.

name: Elle Simone Scott
headline: Elle Simone Scott, Chef and Cooking Show Stalwart, Dies at 49
abstract: She was the first Black cast member on the PBS show “America’s Test Kitchen,” and used her influence to help other female chefs of color.

name: Scott Adams
profession: Creator of the Satirical Dilbert Comic Strip
headline: Scott Adams, Creator of the Satirical ‘Dilbert’ Comic Strip, Dies at 68
abstract: His chronicles of a corporate cubicle dweller was widely distributed until racist comments on his podcast led newspapers to cut their ties with him.

name: Claudette Colvin
profession: Refused to Give Her Bus Seat to a White Woman
headline: Claudette Colvin, Who Refused to Give Her Bus Seat to a White Woman, Dies at 86
abstract: Her defiance of Jim Crow laws in 1955 made her a star witness in a landmark segregation suit, but her act was overshadowed months later when Rosa Parks made history with a similar stand.

name: David Webb
headline: David Webb, Investor Who Took On Hong Kong Tycoons, Dies at 60
abstract: From his internet platform, he became a tenacious watchdog fighting financial regulators for minority shareholders and exposing shady business dealings.

name: Jim McBride
profession: Brought Honky-Tonk Back to Country Music
headline: Jim McBride Dies at 78; Brought Honky-Tonk Back to Country Music
abstract: He was best known for his long-running collaboration with Alan Jackson and their signature hit, “Chattahoochee.”

name: Rebecca Kilgore
headline: Rebecca Kilgore, 76, Dies; Acclaimed Interpreter of American Songbook
abstract: An elegant jazz singer with adventurous taste, she counted among her fans the performer Michael Feinstein and the songwriter Dave Frishberg, who called her technique “flawless.”

name: Renfrew Christie
headline: Renfrew Christie Dies at 76; Sabotaged Racist Regime’s Nuclear Program
abstract: He played a key role in ending apartheid South Africa’s secret weapons program in the 1980s by helping the African National Congress bomb critical facilities.

name: Frank Dunlop
headline: Frank Dunlop, 98, Dies; Director Who Gave Theater a Free-Spirited Spin
abstract: In 1970, he founded London’s Young Vic, an adventurous “people’s theater” (the Who took the stage at one point) before shaking up the Brooklyn Academy of Music.

name: John Cunningham
headline: John Cunningham, Character Actor and Broadway Stalwart, Dies at 93
abstract: He was a familiar face from Broadway productions of “Company,” “Titanic” and “Six Degrees of Separation” and from many movie and TV appearances.

name: Harvey Pratt
profession: Designed the Native American Veterans Memorial
headline: Harvey Pratt, Who Designed the Native American Veterans Memorial, Dies at 84
abstract: A self-taught artist, he also spent more than half a century creating forensic sketches and reconstructions for law-enforcement agencies.

name: Jim Hartung
headline: Jim Hartung, Gymnast Who Helped Deliver U.S. Gold, Dies at 65
abstract: In an upset victory over China at the 1984 Olympics, he and five others became the only American men ever to win the gold medal in the gymnastics team competition.

name: Leonard D. Jacoby
profession: Brought Legal Services to the Masses
headline: Leonard D. Jacoby, 83, Dies; Brought Legal Services to the Masses
abstract: He and Steven Z. Meyers opened their first low-cost legal clinic in 1972. Within a decade, they had revolutionized the legal industry, and Jacoby & Meyers had become a widely known brand.

name: Walter Steding
headline: Walter Steding, Otherworldly One-Man Band and Portraitist, Is Dead at 75
abstract: A self-taught musician, he wore flashing goggles while playing the violin. But his real skill was as a painter, and his portraits offered an eerie commentary on the times.

name: Gabriel Barkay
headline: Gabriel Barkay, 81, Dies; His Discoveries Revised Biblical History
abstract: One of Israel’s leading archaeologists, he found evidence that the writing of the Old Testament likely began much earlier than historians had thought.

name: Rhoda Levine
headline: Rhoda Levine, Pathbreaking Opera Director, Dies at 93
abstract: Starting out in the 1970s as a rare woman in a field dominated by men, she directed the premieres of a pair of politically charged modern classics.

name: Joel Primack
headline: Joel Primack, Physicist Who Helped Explain the Cosmos, Dies at 80
abstract: A professor at the University of California, Santa Cruz, he was a key contributor to a landmark paper that laid out how the universe came to look like it does today.

name: Kristina Gjerde
headline: Kristina Gjerde, Advocate for Ocean Biodiversity, Dies at 68
abstract: She played a key role in negotiating a landmark United Nations treaty to protect the high seas, an agreement that went into effect this weekend.

name: Tina Packer
headline: Tina Packer, Powerhouse of Shakespeare Performance, Dies at 87
abstract: She was a founder and the longtime artistic director of Shakespeare & Company, a repertory theater in western Massachusetts, and directed all his plays.

name: Joe Montgomery
headline: Joe Montgomery, Who Made Bicycles Lighter, Dies at 86
abstract: A founder of Cannondale, he was among the first in the U.S. to mass-produce bikes frames out of large-diameter aluminum tubes, replacing heavier steel.

name: Wilbur Wood
profession: Ironman Knuckleballer for the White Sox
headline: Wilbur Wood, Ironman Knuckleballer for the White Sox, Is Dead at 84
abstract: He threw more innings in a season than any player since 1917. A three-time All-Star, he also had four 20-win seasons.

name: Ralph Towner
profession: Eclectic Guitarist With the Ensemble Oregon
headline: Ralph Towner, Eclectic Guitarist With the Ensemble Oregon, Dies at 85
abstract: A composer and pianist as well, he was a prolific recording artist who integrated jazz, classical and world music traditions in a career that spanned seven decades.

name: Valentino Garavani
profession: Regal Designer and Fashions Last Emperor
headline: Valentino Garavani, Regal Designer and Fashion’s ‘Last Emperor,’ Dies at 93
abstract: Valentino, as he was called, created one of the most durable and fashionable labels and became an equal of his high society customers.

name: David Rosen
profession: Video Game Visionary and Co-Founder of Sega
headline: David Rosen, 95, Dies; Video Game Visionary and Co-Founder of Sega
abstract: He transformed his Japanese photo booth business into a gaming industry giant that created Mortal Kombat, Sonic the Hedgehog and more.

name: Georges Borchardt
headline: Georges Borchardt, 97, Dies; Literary Agent Championed Wiesel’s ‘Night’
abstract: Renowned in his field, he counted among his clients five Nobel laureates, including Elie Wiesel, and eight Pulitzer winners as well as the estates of Tennessee Williams and Aldous Huxley.

name: Manolo Villaverde
profession: Tender Father on Bilingual TV Show
headline: Manolo Villaverde, Tender Father on Bilingual TV Show, Dies at 89
abstract: He played Pepe Peña on “¿Qué Pasa, U.S.A.?,” a series about a Cuban American family that is believed to be the United States’ first bilingual sitcom.

name: Stephen Hess
headline: Stephen Hess, 92, an Eminent, and Quotable, Political Scientist, Dies
abstract: A Brookings Institution scholar, he advised presidents and wrote books on the media (assessing reporters in one) and government (including a study of beleaguered press officers).

name: Barbara Aronstein Black
profession: First as a Law School Dean
headline: Barbara Aronstein Black, a First as a Law School Dean, Dies at 92
abstract: A legal historian, she broke a gender barrier as the first woman to lead an Ivy League law school, serving as dean of Columbia Law from 1986 to 1991.

name: Rifaat al-Assad
profession: Paramilitary Leader and Butcher of Hama
headline: Rifaat al-Assad, Paramilitary Leader and ‘Butcher of Hama,’ Dies at 88
abstract: The brother and uncle of Syrian tyrants, he commanded a unit that killed up to 40,000 civilians in a 1982 uprising against his family’s rule.

name: Barbara G. Walker
headline: Barbara G. Walker, Guru to the Kniterati, Is Dead at 95
abstract: After teaching herself to knit, she invented and cataloged stitch patterns, publishing seven foundational books that sold hundreds of thousands of copies.

name: Alfred McLaren
profession: Submariner Led Secret Cold War Missions
headline: Alfred McLaren, 93, Dies; Submariner Led Secret Cold War Missions
abstract: He participated in the first baseball game at the North Pole. Later, he became an expert in the impact of climate change on Arctic ice sheets.

name: James Bernard
profession: Founding Editor of a Hip-Hop Bible
headline: James Bernard, a Founding Editor of a Hip-Hop ‘Bible,’ Dies at 58
abstract: One of the most influential voices of the seminal magazine The Source, he chronicled rap’s rise and its explosion into the cultural mainstream.

name: Louis E. Brus
headline: Louis E. Brus, Nobel Laureate Who Illuminated the Nanoworld, Dies at 82
abstract: He accidentally created some of the first quantum dots, tiny semiconductors that now power many electronics.

name: Pedro Sanchez
headline: Pedro Sanchez, Who Helped Feed the Developing World, Dies at 85
abstract: A soil scientist, he partnered with the United Nations and other organizations to bring productive agricultural practices to uncooperative terrain.

name: John H. Beyer
headline: John H. Beyer, 92, Dies; Architect Championed Historic Preservation
abstract: The last surviving founder of Beyer Blinder Belle, he helped safeguard New York City’s past even as developers raced to push the city into the future.

name: John Brodie
headline: John Brodie, a Star Quarterback for the 49ers, Dies at 90
abstract: He endured years of frustration before emerging as the N.F.L.’s most valuable player.

name: Edith Flanigen
headline: Edith Flanigen, Award-Winning Research Chemist, Dies at 96
abstract: She and her staff at Union Carbide created synthetic materials that improved various industrial processes, including purifying water. She also developed a way to make emeralds.

name: Beatriz González
headline: Beatriz González, Who Chronicled Colombia’s Turmoil in Paint, Dies at 93
abstract: Often drawing from reproduced images or newspaper photos, she made work that quietly yet memorably critiqued her country’s social and political order.

name: Pat Montandon
headline: Pat Montandon, Socialite Who Sought Publicity, and Then World Peace, Dies at 96
abstract: She was known for her lavish parties and her marriage to one of the richest men in San Francisco. After he left her, she found a new purpose: visiting world leaders to plead for peace.

name: William H. Foege
profession: Key Figure in the Eradication of Smallpox
headline: William H. Foege, Key Figure in the Eradication of Smallpox, Dies at 89
abstract: His containment strategy helped wipe out the disease in the 1970s, one of the world’s greatest public health triumphs. He also led the C.D.C. and promoted childhood vaccination worldwide.

name: Marian Goodman
headline: Marian Goodman, Eminent New York Art Dealer, Dies at 97
abstract: Although known for promoting German painters, she also sought out artists who shunned painting in favor of newer mediums, like photography and film.

name: Floyd Vivino
profession: Throwback Comedian Known as Uncle Floyd
headline: Floyd Vivino, Throwback Comedian Known as Uncle Floyd, Dies at 74
abstract: His silly, vaudeville-style variety show was filled with his piano playing, skits, puppets and guest stars like Cyndi Lauper and Jon Bon Jovi.

name: George Cabot Lodge
profession: Last of His Family to Battle a Kennedy
headline: George Cabot Lodge, Last of His Family to Battle a Kennedy, Dies at 98
abstract: The two Massachusetts clans faced off in elections for decades, until a final 1962 Senate race. Despite his loss, Mr. Lodge praised his opponent, Ted Kennedy.

name: Thomas Fogarty
headline: Thomas Fogarty, 91, Who Helped Revolutionize Vascular Surgery, Dies
abstract: Drawing on his love of fly-fishing, he developed a balloon catheter that removes blood clots from patients’ limbs in a minimally invasive way. It has saved millions of lives.

name: Peter H. Duesberg
headline: Peter H. Duesberg, 89, Renowned Biologist Turned H.I.V. Denialist, Dies
abstract: His pioneering work on the origins of cancer was later overshadowed by his contrarian views, notably his rejection of the established theory that H.I.V. causes AIDS.

name: Gladys West
profession: Unsung Figure in Development of GPS
headline: Gladys West, Unsung Figure in Development of GPS, Dies at 95
abstract: As a Navy mathematician in the 1950s and beyond, she played an unheralded but foundational role in making possible the global satellite-based mapping system.

name: Johnny Legend
headline: Johnny Legend, a King of Trash Culture, Dies at 77
abstract: His forays into rockabilly music, wrestling and erotic films made him a cult hero in a career as confounding as that of his friend Andy Kaufman.

name: Sly Dunbar
profession: Drumming Brought Complex Beats to Reggae
headline: Sly Dunbar, Whose Drumming Brought Complex Beats to Reggae, Dies at 73
abstract: As one half of the famed rhythm duo Sly and Robbie, he played with some of the biggest names in music, including Bob Dylan and Mick Jagger.

name: Geoff Mason
profession: Sports Producer Thrust Into Covering Terrorism
headline: Geoff Mason, Sports Producer Thrust Into Covering Terrorism, Dies at 85
abstract: He played a critical role in ABC Sports’s reporting on the attack by a Palestinian group at the 1972 Summer Games in Munich that left 11 Israeli team members dead.

name: Angella Ferguson
profession: Leader in Sickle Cell Anemia Research
headline: Angella Ferguson, a Leader in Sickle Cell Anemia Research, Dies at 100
abstract: A Black female doctor when that was rare, she developed a diagnostic test for the disease that is still a standard tool, as well as treatment guidelines.

name: Shirley Raines
profession: Gave L.A.s Homeless Food and Makeovers
headline: Shirley Raines, 58, Who Gave L.A.’s Homeless Food and Makeovers, Dies
abstract: Her work feeding people and dyeing their hair through her nonprofit, Beauty 2 the Streetz, was known to millions online.

name: John L. Allen Jr.
profession: Journalist With Inside Access to the Vatican
headline: John L. Allen Jr., Journalist With Inside Access to the Vatican, Dies at 61
abstract: He seemed to know everyone at the Holy See, and it showed in his reporting for the National Catholic Reporter and his website, Crux, though some said he grew too close to his sources.

name: Michael Beck
profession: First to Report Symptoms of Havana Syndrome
headline: Michael Beck, 65, Dies; First to Report Symptoms of ‘Havana Syndrome’
abstract: As an employee with the N.S.A., he claimed he was exposed to a direct-energy device that led to a diagnosis of Parkinson’s disease at the age of 45.

name: Catherine O’Hara
profession: Home Alone and Schitts Creek Actress
headline: Catherine O’Hara, ‘Home Alone’ and ‘Schitt’s Creek’ Actress, Dies at 71
abstract: An Emmy-winning comedian with oddball charm, she got her start with the influential Canadian sketch comedy series “SCTV.”

name: Björn Roth
profession: Steward of an Expansive Family Art Practice
headline: Björn Roth, Steward of an Expansive Family Art Practice, Dies at 64
abstract: With his father, the artist Dieter Roth, and later his own sons, he created unconventional installations that he described as a “search for beauty in nothing.”

name: Roger Allers
profession: Helped Put Lion King on Screens and Onstage
headline: Roger Allers Dies at 76; Helped Put ‘Lion King’ on Screens and Onstage
abstract: A Disney fan who once “flew” off his couch as a 4-year-old Peter Pan, he was a co-director of the animated film and a co-writer of the Broadway musical, both of them megahits.

name: ‘Produce Pete’ Napolitano
headline: ‘Produce Pete’ Napolitano, a Fruit and Vegetable Celebrity, Dies at 80
abstract: For more than 30 years, he drew fans for dispensing weekly produce punditry on a New York television station, building on a sales career that began when he was 5.

name: Dan McQuade
headline: Dan McQuade, a Catalyst in Cosby’s Downfall, Dies at 43
abstract: His viral video of the comedian Hannibal Buress calling Bill Cosby a rapist helped spur broader coverage of sexual-assault accusations against a once-beloved entertainer.

name: Morris Waxler
headline: Morris Waxler, F.D.A. Official Who Switched Stance on Lasik, Dies at 88
abstract: While at the federal agency, he approved the laser device for eye surgery but later warned of its potential to cause harm.

name: Jimmy Reed
headline: Overlooked No More: Jimmy Reed, the Bluesman Everyone Covered, Then Forgot
abstract: His most enduring hits were recorded by Elvis Presley, Aretha Franklin, the Rolling Stones and the Grateful Dead. But his own career faded from view.

name: Demond Wilson
profession: Long-Suffering Son on Sanford and Son
headline: Demond Wilson, Long-Suffering Son on ‘Sanford and Son,’ Dies at 79
abstract: As Lamont, he was a young man in constant battle with his father and business partner, played by Redd Foxx, on the popular 1970s series.

name: Laura Maioglio
profession: Restaurant Is a Theater District Mainstay
headline: Laura Maioglio, Whose Restaurant Is a Theater District Mainstay, Dies at 93
abstract: Since 1962, she oversaw her father’s stately Italian restaurant, Barbetta, and became one of the city’s most enduring female restaurateurs.

name: T. Kumar
headline: T. Kumar, Rights Activist Who Was Shaped by Time in Prison, Dies at 76
abstract: After being jailed as a resistance organizer for the Tamil minority in his native Sri Lanka, he spoke out against governmental repression worldwide.

name: X.J. Kennedy
headline: X.J. Kennedy, a Poet of Wit Who Clung to Rhyme and Meter, Dies at 96
abstract: Spurning the free verse of many of his contemporaries, he held to an older tradition. He also wrote spirited poems for children.

name: Robert Pratt
headline: Robert Pratt, Federal Judge Who Derided Trump Pardons, Dies at 78
abstract: He was chastised for remarks ridiculing the pardons of two congressional campaign aides who had been convicted in a bribery plot.

name: James Sallis
headline: James Sallis, 81, Dies; Novelist Whose ‘Drive’ Became a Hit Movie
abstract: A storyteller of modern America’s underbelly with a literary, ruminative style, he inspired a Ryan Gosling movie and earned critical acclaim.

name: Billy Bass Nelson
headline: Billy Bass Nelson, Original Bassist for Funkadelic, Dies at 75
abstract: George Clinton, while working as a barber, recruited him. Mr. Nelson went on to name the group and, with his bandmates, to be inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame.

name: John Forté
headline: John Forté, Who Forged a Hip-Hop Redemption Tale, Dies at 50
abstract: He seemed destined for a glittering career, working with the Fugees and solo, and then landed in prison. After his sentence was commuted, he clawed his way back.

name: Woodie King Jr.
headline: Woodie King Jr., a Driving Force in Black Theater, Dies at 88
abstract: His New Federal Theater in New York provided a rare stage for Black playwrights and emerging actors, among them Denzel Washington, Phylicia Rashad and Chadwick Boseman.

name: Chuck Negron
profession: Hitmaking Singer With Three Dog Night
headline: Chuck Negron, Hitmaking Singer With Three Dog Night, Dies at 83
abstract: His tenor anchored generational hits like “Joy to the World” and “One” by one of pop music’s commercial powerhouses of the early 1970s.

name: Michael Parenti
headline: Michael Parenti, Unapologetic Marxist Theorist and Author, Dies at 92
abstract: A prolific writer and lecturer, he viewed U.S. history through the lens of class struggle. But some accused him of defending brutal regimes in the Soviet Union and Serbia.

name: Tom Britt
headline: Tom Britt, Designer of Larger-Than-Life Interiors, Dies at 89
abstract: A master of the grand gesture, he was as theatrical as his rooms, which were inspired by French chateaus and Italian palazzos. As he put it, “Why be ordinary?”

name: Virginia Oliver
profession: Maines Lobster Lady and Folk Hero
headline: Virginia Oliver, Maine’s ‘Lobster Lady’ and Folk Hero, Dies at 105
abstract: She fished off the New England coast for more than 80 years, and intended to continue until she died. “It’s not hard work for me,” she said at 101.

name: Lee H. Hamilton
headline: Lee H. Hamilton, Congressman Who Helped Lead a 9/11 Inquiry, Dies at 94
abstract: A moderate Democrat from Indiana for 34 years, he chaired the House Foreign Affairs and Intelligence committees and helped investigate the Iran-contra scandal and the Sept. 11 attacks.

name: Mickey Lolich
profession: Detroits Hero of the 1968 World Series
headline: Mickey Lolich, Detroit’s Hero of the 1968 World Series, Dies at 85
abstract: Pitching for the Tigers, he notched three complete-game victories in defeating the St. Louis Cardinals for the championship, earning the Series’ M.V.P. honors.

name: Blanche Marvin
headline: Blanche Marvin, 100, Dies; Critic Was, Maybe, ‘Streetcar’ Inspiration
abstract: She was a ubiquitous presence at London theaters and claimed to have inspired the name — and final words — of Tennessee Williams’s Blanche DuBois.

name: Ted Berger
profession: Indefatigable Patron of Artists and Schools
headline: Ted Berger, Indefatigable Patron of Artists and Schools, Dies at 85
abstract: As head of the New York Foundation for the Arts, he oversaw almost $23 million in grants and helped bring arts education to struggling schools.

name: Myra MacPherson
headline: Myra MacPherson, Who Wrote Wrenchingly About Vietnam Vets, Dies at 91
abstract: A political reporter at The Washington Post, she wrote the book “Long Time Passing,” about the Vietnam War’s social, political and psychological aftereffects.

name: Sonny Jurgensen
headline: Sonny Jurgensen, One of N.F.L.’s Greatest Passers, Dies at 91
abstract: The Hall of Fame quarterback threw 255 touchdown passes with the Philadelphia Eagles and Washington Redskins.

name: Saalumarada Thimmakka
profession: Planted and Nurtured Thousands of Trees
headline: Saalumarada Thimmakka Dies; Planted and Nurtured Thousands of Trees
abstract: Believed to be 113, she spent decades building an environmental legacy in India, inspired by her grief at being unable to conceive children.

name: Philippe Morillon
profession: General Made a Fateful Promise in Bosnia
headline: Philippe Morillon, 90, Dies; General Made a Fateful Promise in Bosnia
abstract: “I will never abandon you,” he told residents of Srebrenica amid sectarian armed conflict. The town later suffered the worst massacre in Europe since World War II.

name: Roland Huntford
headline: Roland Huntford, Lore-Debunking Historian of Polar Exploration, Dies at 98
abstract: He caused an uproar by challenging the heroic status of Robert Falcon Scott, the Briton who led a doomed quest to the South Pole in 1912.

name: Suzannah Lessard
headline: Suzannah Lessard Dies at 81; Stanford White Descendant Who Wrote a Haunting Family Memoir
abstract: Growing up in a family of secrets, on a compound designed by her great-grandfather, made her a writer who investigated the built world with a wary eye.

name: Brad Arnold
headline: Brad Arnold, Rocker Who Fronted 3 Doors Down, Dies at 47
abstract: He wrote the band’s breakout hit, “Kryptonite,” in a high school math class, and would go on to be nominated for three Grammy Awards.

name: Mark Marquess
headline: Mark Marquess, Who Made Stanford a Baseball Powerhouse, Dies at 78
abstract: Over 41 seasons as head coach, he won two national titles, and more than 200 of his players were chosen in the major league draft.

name: Ray Handley
headline: Ray Handley, Ill-Fated Giants Coach, Is Dead at 81
abstract: He took over a champion N.F.L. team, succeeding the popular Bill Parcells, then led it to two disappointing seasons, drawing the ire of players and fans.

name: Philippe Gaulier
profession: Revered Clown and Tormentor of Aspiring Comedians
headline: Philippe Gaulier, Revered Clown and ‘Tormentor’ of Aspiring Comedians, Dies at 82
abstract: He often insulted his pupils, but many became stars, including Sacha Baron Cohen, Emma Thompson and Rachel Weisz.

name: Gabor Boritt
headline: Gabor Boritt, Refugee Who Became Expert on Lincoln, Dies at 86
abstract: He survived the Holocaust and Communist rule in Hungary, arrived penniless in New York and made himself into a pre-eminent Civil War scholar.

name: Hudson Talbott
profession: Wrote and Illustrated Wide-Ranging Childrens Books
headline: Hudson Talbott Dies at 76; Wrote and Illustrated Wide-Ranging Children’s Books
abstract: His book about time-traveling dinosaurs became a Steven Spielberg-produced movie, and he adapted the Stephen Sondheim musical “Into the Woods” for young readers.

name: Ray Mouton
profession: Lawyer Warned of Pedophilia in the Catholic Church
headline: Ray Mouton Dies at 78; Lawyer Warned of Pedophilia in the Catholic Church
abstract: After defending one of the first priests charged with child sex abuse, he coauthored a 1985 report warning that the problem was endemic and ignoring it could be catastrophic.

name: James Van Der Beek
headline: James Van Der Beek, Teenage Heartthrob of ‘Dawson’s Creek,’ Dies at 48
abstract: He first appeared in a hit TV drama as a wide-eyed 15-year-old who then grew up over six seasons. He announced he had cancer in 2024.

name: Andrew Ranken
headline: Andrew Ranken, Whose Drumming Powered the Pogues, Dies at 72
abstract: Known as “The Clobberer,” he pounded out driving rhythms that fueled the band’s boisterous blend of traditional Irish music, rock and punk.

name: LaMonte McLemore
headline: LaMonte McLemore, Founding Singer With the 5th Dimension, Dies at 90
abstract: His group notched smooth hippie-era hits like “Up, Up and Away” and “The Age of Aquarius” in embracing a genre-blurring sound they called “champagne soul.”

name: Ken Peplowski
headline: Ken Peplowski, Who Helped Revive the Jazz Clarinet, Dies at 66
abstract: Also a saxophone standout, he served as stylistic bridge between the Benny Goodman swing era and the genre-blurring present.

name: Tamas Vasary
headline: Tamas Vasary, Pianist of Power and Sensitivity, Dies at 92
abstract: He bought technical brilliance and stylistic authority to Romantic-era music, particularly the works of Chopin and Liszt.

name: Bud Cort
headline: Bud Cort, Who Starred in 1971’s ‘Harold and Maude,’ Dies at 77
abstract: The role, one of his first, made him a household name and a film idol of the anti-establishment 1970s. But it also limited his growth as an actor.

name: Helmuth Rilling
headline: Helmuth Rilling, Who Recorded Huge Swaths of Bach, Dies at 92
abstract: He was the first to record all of J.S. Bach’s nearly 200 sacred cantatas, a project that stood out not only for its range but also for its steadfast style.

name: Daniel Cathiard
profession: Turned Bordeaux Estate Into Champion Winery
headline: Daniel Cathiard Dies at 81; Turned Bordeaux Estate Into Champion Winery
abstract: He came to winemaking late, after a career in retail, and turned the 18th-century Chateau Smith Haut Lafitte into one of France’s most esteemed vineyards.

name: Clifford Brown
headline: Overlooked No More: Clifford Brown, Trumpeter Whose Brief Life Left a Lasting Mark
abstract: He was one of the most talked-about jazz musicians in the 1950s. After he died in a car accident at 25, his influence grew.

name: Greg Brown
headline: Greg Brown, Guitarist Who Wrote Cake’s Biggest Hit, Dies at 56
abstract: His song “The Distance,” released in 1996, became an anthem for the disaffected members of Generation X.

name: Vicki Abt
profession: Said TV Talk Shows Coarsened Society
headline: Vicki Abt, Who Said TV Talk Shows Coarsened Society, Dies at 83
abstract: A Penn State sociology professor, she warned that hosts like Oprah Winfrey exploited vulnerable guests on television and sensationalized deviancy.

name: Bob Croft
profession: Dived Deep Into the Ocean on a Single Breath
headline: Bob Croft, Who Dived Deep Into the Ocean on a Single Breath, Dies at 91
abstract: His derring-do and unusual lung capacity led him to make record-breaking dives of more than 200 feet into the Atlantic without wearing a scuba tank or fins.

name: Ebo Taylor
profession: Musical Innovator of Highlife and Afrobeat
headline: Ebo Taylor, Musical Innovator of Highlife and Afrobeat, Dies at 90
abstract: Borrowing from jazz and African rhythms, he forged a singular style that helped define music in his native Ghana — and West Africa — for a generation.

name: David J. Farber
headline: David J. Farber, ‘Grandfather of the Internet,’ Dies at 91
abstract: A researcher, professor and federal policy adviser, he guided students who went on to do groundbreaking work in connecting the world online.

name: Roy Medvedev
headline: Roy Medvedev, Soviet Era Historian and Dissident, Is Dead at 100
abstract: His score of books and hundreds of essays documented Stalinist executions, Communist repressions and censorship, and the transition to post-Soviet Russia.

name: ElRoy Face
profession: Ace Forkballer and Effective Closer for Pirates
headline: ElRoy Face, Ace Forkballer and Effective Closer for Pirates, Dies at 97
abstract: Face was one of the first major-league hurlers to make the closer job a specialty. Not an overpowering pitcher, he finagled outs with a tricky forkball.

name: Leatherbury
headline: King Leatherbury, Trainer and Trader of Horses, Dies at 92
abstract: He trained mostly lesser-known, cheaper thoroughbreds in Maryland and was the fifth-winningest trainer in North American history.

name: Alfred Blumstein
headline: Alfred Blumstein, Who Transformed the Study of Crime, Dies at 95
abstract: An engineer by training, he used systems theory and quantitative analysis to examine criminal behavior, revealing the systemic patterns of crime.

name: Jerry Kennedy
headline: Jerry Kennedy, Who Helped Define Music in Nashville, Dies at 85
abstract: A guitarist and record producer, he played a role in creating hits by popular singers like Roger Miller, Roy Orbison, Tom T. Hall and Tammy Wynette.

name: Henrike Naumann
profession: Artist Set to Represent Germany at Venice Biennale
headline: Henrike Naumann, Artist Set to Represent Germany at Venice Biennale, Dies at 41
