abstract: Her death from cancer was the second sudden loss for this year’s edition. Naumann’s exhibition will still go ahead in May, according to a statement.

name: Richard Ottinger
profession: Fought for the Environment in Congress
headline: Richard Ottinger, 97, Dies; Fought for the Environment in Congress
abstract: A New York Democrat, he spent 16 years in the House over two stretches, beginning in 1965, championing the health of the Hudson River and opposing the Vietnam War.

name: Robert Duvall
profession: Chameleon of an Actor Onscreen and Onstage
headline: Robert Duvall, a Chameleon of an Actor Onscreen and Onstage, Dies at 95
abstract: An Oscar winner, he was known for disappearing into wide-ranging roles in movies like “Apocalypse Now” and “The Godfather” and in the television series “Lonesome Dove.”

name: Frederick Wiseman
headline: Frederick Wiseman, 96, Penetrating Documentarian of Institutions, Dies
abstract: He exposed abuses in films like “Titicut Follies,” a once-banned portrait of a mental hospital, but ranged widely in subject matter, from a Queens neighborhood to a French restaurant.

name: Jesse Jackson
headline: Jesse Jackson, Charismatic Champion of Civil Rights, Dies at 84
abstract: An impassioned orator, he was a moral and political force, forming a “rainbow coalition” of poor and working-class people and seeking the presidency. His mission, he said, was “to transform the mind of America.”

name: Ed Crane
headline: Ed Crane, Who Built Cato Into Libertarian Stronghold, Dies at 81
abstract: Starting with $500,000 in seed money from Charles Koch, Mr. Crane made the institute the nation’s pre-eminent libertarian think tank.

name: Frederick Vreeland
headline: Frederick Vreeland, Diplomat and Spy Who Served With Style, Dies at 98
abstract: A son of the influential fashion editor Diana Vreeland, he had an upbringing well suited to his overt and covert duties during the Cold War.

name: Anna Akhmatova
headline: From 1966: Anna Akhmatova, Leading Soviet Poet, Is Dead
abstract: A towering figure in Soviet literature, she was once silenced in a Stalinist literary purge.

name: Fania Fénelon
headline: From 1983: Fania Fénelon, 74; Memoirs Described Auschwitz Singing
abstract: In “Playing for Time,” she recounted how singing in an all-female orchestra while she was in a concentration camp saved her life.

name: David Hays
profession: Top Broadway Designer and Theater of Deaf Founder
headline: David Hays, 95, Dies; Top Broadway Designer and Theater of Deaf Founder
abstract: He created sets and lighting for dozens of productions, including “Long Day’s Journey Into Night,” and established a new art form with his theater of the deaf, combining sign and spoken language.

name: Jo Ann Bass
profession: Matriarch of Joes Stone Crab in Miami Beach
headline: Jo Ann Bass, Matriarch of Joe’s Stone Crab in Miami Beach, Dies at 94
abstract: For decades, she oversaw a money-gushing South Florida restaurant that has drawn celebrities like Frank Sinatra, Muhammad Ali and Madonna.

name: José van Dam
headline: José van Dam, Suave and Riveting Opera Star, Dies at 85
abstract: One of the most esteemed singers of his era, he had a wide repertoire that included Mozart, Wagner and the title role in Messiaen’s epic “St. François d’Assise.”

name: Billy Steinberg
profession: Hitmaking Lyricist of Madonnas Like a Virgin
headline: Billy Steinberg, Hitmaking Lyricist of Madonna’s ‘Like a Virgin,’ Dies at 75
abstract: He co-wrote five pop-rock songs that soared to No. 1 in the 1980s and shared in a Grammy for producing Celine Dion’s 1996 album “Falling Into You.”

name: Cees Nooteboom
headline: Cees Nooteboom, Voyaging Author of Enigmatic Novels, Dies at 92
abstract: A prolific Dutch writer of fiction, poetry and travel books, he was often mentioned as a potential recipient of the Nobel Prize in Literature.

name: Doug Moe
profession: N.B.A. Coach as Freewheeling as His Style of Play
headline: Doug Moe, 87, N.B.A. Coach as Freewheeling as His Style of Play, Dies
abstract: A former college All-American touched by scandal, he was irreverent and unpredictable as he piloted his fast-paced Nuggets and Spurs.

name: Eric Dane
headline: Eric Dane, McSteamy on ‘Grey’s Anatomy,’ Dies at 53
abstract: His breakout role came in 2006 as the handsome Dr. Mark Sloan, nicknamed McSteamy, the head of plastic surgery at a Seattle hospital. He died 10 months after announcing his A.L.S. diagnosis.

name: Christopher S. Wren
profession: Times Bureau Chief in Hostile Lands
headline: Christopher S. Wren, Times Bureau Chief in Hostile Lands, Dies at 89
abstract: Over three decades, he reported from Moscow, Beijing, Tehran and elsewhere and wrote well-received books based on his reporting, including one about his globe-trotting cat.

name: Michael Silverblatt
headline: Michael Silverblatt, NPR’s ‘Bookworm’ Who Interviewed Authors, Dies at 73
abstract: His public radio show, “Bookworm,” was a literary salon of the air for 33 years, drawing guests like Joan Didion, Susan Sontag and David Foster Wallace.

name: John Shirreffs
profession: Trainer of a Nearly Perfect Horse
headline: John Shirreffs, 80, Dies; Trainer of a Nearly Perfect Horse
abstract: He guided Zenyatta, a spectacular mare, to 19 consecutive wins. Earlier, he won the Kentucky Derby with Giacomo, a 50-1 long shot.

name: Bill Mazeroski
headline: Bill Mazeroski, 89, Whose 9th-Inning Blast Made Pirates Champs, Is Dead
abstract: It was Game 7 of the 1960 World Series, when an infielder known for his glove, not his bat, crushed the powerful Yankees with one swing, bringing joy to Pittsburgh.

name: Theodore Conklin
profession: His Rescue of an Inn Helped Save Sag Harbor
headline: Theodore Conklin, 77, Dies; His Rescue of an Inn Helped Save Sag Harbor
abstract: By rehabilitating the American Hotel, he turned a hard-luck village on the East End of Long Island into a mecca for pop stars and plumbers alike.

name: Willie Colón
headline: Willie Colón, a Luminary of Salsa Music, Dies at 75
abstract: A trombonist, singer, bandleader, composer and arranger, he collaborated with Rubén Blades on “Siembra,” a 1978 release that became one of the top-selling salsa albums of all time.

name: Tom Noonan
headline: Tom Noonan, Actor Renowned for Onscreen Menace, Dies at 74
abstract: He played memorable screen villains, notably a psychopath in “Manhunter,” but also wrote, directed and starred in well-received plays at a theater he founded in Manhattan.

name: Norman Francis
profession: Led Xavier U. in New Orleans Into New Era
headline: Norman Francis, 94, Who Led Xavier U. in New Orleans Into New Era, Dies
abstract: He was among America’s longest-serving college presidents, with a 47-year tenure, and played an important civil-rights role in New Orleans.

name: Susan Sheehan
profession: Chronicler of Lives on the Margins
headline: Susan Sheehan, Chronicler of Lives on the Margins, Dies at 88
abstract: As a journalist and author, she wrote meticulous portraits of people for The New Yorker. Her book “Is There No Place on Earth for Me?” won the Pulitzer Prize.

name: Leah Stavenhagen
profession: Advocate for Young Women With A.L.S
headline: Leah Stavenhagen, Advocate for Young Women With A.L.S., Dies at 33
abstract: She started a group intended to counter the notion that A.L.S. was an “older white man’s disease.”

name: Edward Hoagland
profession: Literary Explorer of Nature and Himself
headline: Edward Hoagland, Literary Explorer of Nature and Himself, Dies at 93
abstract: In his lyrical writings, he examined physical landscapes as well as the interior terrain of his own life — up to the blindness that overtook him in his later years.

name: Robert Carradine
headline: Robert Carradine, Actor Who Played the Father in ‘Lizzie McGuire,’ Dies at 71
abstract: A member of a renowned acting dynasty, he also earned fame for his role in “Revenge of the Nerds.” His family said he struggled with bipolar disorder.

name: Éliane Radigue
headline: Éliane Radigue, Composer of Time, Silence and Space, Dies at 94
abstract: Her Tibetan Buddhist spiritual practice and her experiments with synthesizers came together in vast, slow-moving works that drew wide acclaim.

name: Susan Leeman
profession: Explored How the Brain Influences the Body
headline: Susan Leeman, 95, Dies; Explored How the Brain Influences the Body
abstract: In an era of overt sexism in the sciences, she made two major discoveries, including identifying a chemical signal in the brain linked to chronic pain and migraines.

name: Lauren Chapin
profession: Youngest Child on Father Knows Best
headline: Lauren Chapin, Youngest Child on ‘Father Knows Best,’ Dies at 80
abstract: For six seasons, she was Kathy, a giggly tomboy whose father, played by Robert Young, called her Kitten. Her offscreen life, however, was harrowing.

name: Ann Godoff
profession: Top Editor and Publisher of Best Sellers
headline: Ann Godoff, a Top Editor and Publisher of Best Sellers, Dies at 76
abstract: Considered an “author’s publisher” at Random House and then Penguin, she cultivated the careers of dozens of celebrated novelists and nonfiction writers.

name: Antonio Tejero Molina
headline: Antonio Tejero Molina, 93, Dies; Spanish Colonel Led Failed Coup
abstract: He held Spain’s Parliament hostage for 18 hours on Feb. 23, 1981, before surrendering after it became clear that he had little support from the country’s armed forces.

name: Jeff Galloway
headline: Jeff Galloway, Olympian Who Transformed American Distance Running, Dies at 80
abstract: A runner, coach and best-selling author, he created the widely embraced run-walk-run method, which helped make running more accessible to the public.

name: Rose Lesniak
headline: Rose Lesniak, Poet Who Rescued Children and Trained Dogs, Dies at 70
abstract: A magnetic personality, she reinvented herself twice, bringing the same spirit to investigating child abuse and communing with dogs that she did to writing poetry.

name: Oliver Grant
headline: Oliver Grant, a Business Architect of Wu-Tang Clan, Dies
abstract: He was behind the scenes with Wu-Tang Clan, the New York rap group, since its founding and helped expand its reach with a fashion line.

name: Teresa de Lauretis
headline: Teresa de Lauretis, Coiner (and Critic) of Queer Theory, Dies at 87
abstract: She came up with the term as the title of a 1990 conference but saw its later popularity as a little superficial.

name: Dan Duckhorn
profession: Made Merlot a Napa Valley Star
headline: Dan Duckhorn, Who Made Merlot a Napa Valley Star, Dies at 87
abstract: A founder of Duckhorn Vineyards, a California winemaker, Mr. Duckhorn transformed merlot from a blending grape into a premier American variety.

name: Jean Widmer
headline: Jean Widmer, Designer of Celebrated French Graphics, Dies at 96
abstract: His minimalist road signs became a visual hallmark of France’s highways. He also created logos for cultural institutions like the Pompidou Center.

name: Jo Ann Bland
profession: Child Activist in Civil Rights Struggle
headline: Jo Ann Bland, Child Activist in Civil Rights Struggle, Dies at 72
abstract: At 11, she was one of the youngest at the 1965 “Bloody Sunday” voting rights march in Selma, Ala., and was injured while crossing the Edmund Pettus Bridge.

name: Edward L. Deci
profession: Found Self-Determination as a Key to Happiness
headline: Edward L. Deci, 83, Dies; Found Self-Determination as a Key to Happiness
abstract: His work with his colleague Richard Ryan changed how psychologists understand human motivation and what people require to flourish.

name: Bobby Garnett
headline: Overlooked No More: Bobby Garnett, ‘Godfather’ of Vintage Dealers
abstract: His store, Bobby From Boston, transformed the way vintage men’s wear is sold, serving as a model for a generation of retailers.

name: Sondra Lee
profession: Originated Roles in Peter Pan and Hello, Dolly!
headline: Sondra Lee Dies at 97; Originated Roles in ‘Peter Pan’ and ‘Hello, Dolly!’
abstract: With her frenetic energy and 4-foot-10 frame, Ms. Lee seemed destined to play a certain kind of stage character: excitable, endearing and charmingly scheming.

name: Iris Cantor
headline: Iris Cantor, Philanthropist and Art Collector, Dies at 95
abstract: She and her husband, the financier B. Gerald Cantor, amassed one of the largest private collections of Rodin artworks, donating much of it to museums around the world.

name: Neil Sedaka
profession: Singing Craftsman of Memorable Pop Songs
headline: Neil Sedaka, Singing Craftsman of Memorable Pop Songs, Dies at 86
abstract: He sang and co-wrote some of the definitive teenage anthems of the 1950s and early ’60s, including “Breaking Up Is Hard to Do,” and then reinvented his career in the ’70s.

name: Ed Iskenderian
profession: Hot Rod Pioneer Known as the Camfather
headline: Ed Iskenderian, Hot Rod Pioneer Known as the ‘Camfather,’ Dies at 104
abstract: “His influence can be felt in every form of motorsport today,” Car and Driver magazine wrote of the man who powered some of the fastest cars of his era with his innovative engine camshafts.

name: Joe Randall
headline: Joe Randall, Chef Who Celebrated Black Cooking Traditions, Dies at 79
abstract: He helped bring the African American cooking of the Carolina Lowcountry to the world and became known as the “dean of Southern Cuisine.”

name: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei
headline: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Autocratic Cleric Who Made Iran a Regional Power, Is Dead at 86
abstract: As Iran’s second supreme leader, he brutally crushed dissent at home and expanded Iran’s footprint abroad, challenging Saudi Arabia for dominance in the Middle East.

name: Isaiah Zagar
headline: Isaiah Zagar, Creator of Tile-Swirling, Mind-Bending Murals, Dies at 86
abstract: He covered Philadelphia with more than 50,000 square feet of madcap mosaics, showcasing his work at the Magic Gardens Museum.

name: Bruce Froemming
headline: Bruce Froemming, a Durable, No-Nonsense Umpire, Dies at 86
abstract: He called 5,163 regular season major league games over a record 37 consecutive seasons. And he wouldn’t hesitate to give a player or a manager the boot.

name: John P. Hammond
headline: John P. Hammond, Pioneer in 1960s Blues Renaissance, Dies at 83
abstract: With his acclaimed interpretations of Delta Blues standards, he was a fixture on the Greenwich Village music scene for decades.

name: Christian Astuguevieille
profession: Created Strange Scents and Enigmatic Objects
headline: Christian Astuguevieille, 79, Dies; Created Strange Scents and Enigmatic Objects
abstract: For Commes des Garçons, he designed improbable perfumes that conjured burning rubber and cars leaking oil. His uncanny art pieces were equally contrarian.

name: Juan Jose Valdez
headline: Juan Jose Valdez, Last Marine Out of Saigon, Dies at 88
abstract: During the fall of the South Vietnamese capital in 1975, he helped evacuate thousands, and was nearly left behind.

name: Bob Power
profession: Hip-Hop Engineer and Tribe Called Quest Collaborator
headline: Bob Power, 73, Hip-Hop Engineer and Tribe Called Quest Collaborator, Dies
abstract: He helped pioneer a newly complex approach to sampling in rap music, including on A Tribe Called Quest’s influential 1991 album “The Low End Theory.”

name: Lou Holtz
profession: Coached Unbeaten Notre Dame to a Title
headline: Lou Holtz, Who Coached Unbeaten Notre Dame to a Title, Dies at 89
abstract: Known for reviving football programs, he led six major colleges to bowl games, winning a national championship in 1989 after restoring the Irish to greatness.

name: António Lobo Antunes
profession: One of Europes Most Revered Writers
headline: António Lobo Antunes, One of Europe’s Most Revered Writers, Dies at 83
abstract: In a career studded with literary awards, he was the author of dozens of books that grappled with his nation’s legacy of dictatorship and colonialism.

name: Ronnie Eldridge
headline: Ronnie Eldridge, a Fixture in N.Y. Politics, Dies at 95
abstract: She was an adviser to Senator Robert F. Kennedy, Mayor John V. Lindsay and Representative Bella S. Abzug before serving on the New York City Council from 1989 to 2001.

name: Hannah Arendt
headline: From 1975: Hannah Arendt, Political Scientist, Is Dead at 69
abstract: She caused controversy with books like “Eichmann in Jerusalem,” published in 1963, which grew out of her coverage of Adolf Eichmann’s trial for The New Yorker.

name: Jiang Qing
headline: From 1991: Suicide of Jiang Qing, Mao’s Widow, Is Reported
abstract: A former actress who grew up in poverty, she was one of the most hated women in modern Chinese history for her role in the Cultural Revolution.

name: Gabriela Mistral
headline: From 1957: Gabriela Mistral, Poet, Is Dead; Won Nobel Prize for Literature
abstract: She was recognized in 1945 for three “Soñetos de la Muerte” (“Sonnets of Death”), which were first published in Chile in 1922.

name: Anna May Wong
headline: From 1961: Anna May Wong Is Dead at 54; Actress Won Movie Fame in ’24
abstract: With a film career spanning three decades, Miss Wong, who rose to stardom with “The Thief of Baghdad,” was acclaimed as a versatile and talented performer.

name: Josephine Baker
headline: From 1975: Josephine Baker Is Dead in Paris at 68
abstract: She performed with a string of bananas tied around her waist, an electrifying act that led her to become first a local sensation in Paris, and then an international star.

name: Zora Hurston
headline: From 1960: Zora Hurston, 57, Writer, Is Dead
abstract: Although her books, written in the dialect of the Deep South, established her as one of the foremost writers of Black folklore, she died in obscurity.

name: Billie Holiday
headline: From 1959: Billie Holiday Dies Here at 44; Jazz Singer Had Wide Influence
abstract: Miss Holiday, who became a singer more out of desperation than desire, was one of the most influential jazz musicians of her time.

name: Audre Lorde
headline: From 1992: Audre Lorde, 58, a Poet, Memoirist and Lecturer, Dies
abstract: Her large body of work, which included poetry, essays and autobiography, reflected her hatred of racial and sexual prejudice.

name: Dorothy Parker
headline: From 1967: Dorothy Parker, Literary Wit, Dies at Age 73
abstract: She enjoyed a lifelong reputation as a glittering, annihilating humorist. For her epitaph, she suggested, “Excuse My Dust.”

name: Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis
headline: From 1994: Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis Dies of Cancer at 64
abstract: She became an object of fascination to generations of Americans after her husband, President John F. Kennedy, was assassinated in 1963.

name: Nellie Bly
headline: From 1922: Nellie Bly, Journalist, Dies of Pneumonia
abstract: She was best known for her trip around the world in 1889, which she completed in 72 days 6 hours 11 minutes.

name: Maria Callas
headline: From 1977: Maria Callas, 53, Is Dead of Heart Attack in Paris
abstract: Considered the most exciting opera singer of her time, she thrilled audiences with her penchant for spectacle onstage and in her personal life.

name: Martha Gellhorn
headline: From 1998: Martha Gellhorn, Daring Writer, Dies at 89
abstract: One of the first female war correspondents, she covered a dozen major conflicts during a career that spanned more than six decades.

name: Jane Addams
headline: From 1935: Jane Addams Dies in Her 76th Year
abstract: A world-famous social welfare worker, she won a Nobel Prize for her efforts on behalf of world peace.

name: Marjorie Merriweather Post
headline: From 1973: Mrs. Marjorie Merriweather Post Is Dead at 86
abstract: The owner of General Foods Corporation, she was a generous philanthropist whose great wealth also allowed her to entertain lavishly and live regally.

name: Marlene Dietrich
headline: From 1992: Marlene Dietrich, 90, Symbol of Glamour, Dies
abstract: “Dietrich is something that never existed before and may never exist again,” the actor Maurice Chevalier said of her. “That’s a woman.”

name: Christine Jorgensen
profession: Was First to Have a Sex Change
headline: From 1989: Christine Jorgensen, 62, Is Dead; Was First to Have a Sex Change
abstract: Her gender conversion began with hormone injections in 1950. On her return to the U.S. in 1955, she was sensationalized in the tabloids.

name: Teresa
headline: From 1997: Mother Teresa, Hope of the Despairing, Dies at 87
abstract: She won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979 for providing care and comfort to the impoverished.

name: Indira Gandhi
headline: From 1984: Indira Gandhi, Born to Politics, Left Her Own Imprint on India
abstract: The dominant figure in Indian politics for nearly two decades, she was elected prime minister four times before being assassinated by her bodyguards.

name: Natalie Wood
headline: From 1981: Death Ends a 39-Year Career, Starting With Child Roles at 4
abstract: Natalie Wood evolved from a child star into a teenage ingénue and then a mature actress, until her trajectory was tragically cut short.

name: Marilyn Monroe
headline: From 1962: Brilliant Stardom and Personal Tragedy Punctuated the Life of Marilyn Monroe
abstract: One of the most famous stars in Hollywood, she suffered severe setbacks in the last years of her life.

name: Selena Quintanilla Pérez
headline: From 1995: Grammy-Winning Singer Selena Killed in Shooting at Texas Motel
abstract: Known as the queen of Tejano music, she was beloved as an idol and a heartthrob on both sides of the Mexican border.

name: Karen Carpenter
headline: From 1983: Karen Carpenter, 32, Is Dead; Singer Teamed With Brother
abstract: The Carpenters sold more than 30 million records with the irresistible combination of her soft-rock contralto and her brother’s lush arrangements.

name: Wilma Rudolph
headline: From 1994: Wilma Rudolph, Star of the 1960 Olympics, Dies at 54
abstract: She won three gold medals as a sprinter in the Games, an achievement that seemed unlikely given her poor health as a child.

name: Babe Zaharias
headline: From 1956: Babe Zaharias Dies; Athlete Had Cancer
abstract: From the time she made the headlines during the 1932 Olympic Games at Los Angeles, she reigned as the world’s top all-around female athlete.

name: Toni Stone
profession: First Woman to Play Big-League Baseball
headline: From 1996: Toni Stone, 75, First Woman to Play Big-League Baseball
abstract: She was hired as a novelty by the Negro League’s Indianapolis Clowns, but went on to win recognition for her historic career.

name: Florence Griffith Joyner
headline: From 1998: Florence Griffith Joyner, 38, Champion Sprinter, Is Dead
abstract: She revolutionized women’s sprinting with her speed and flamboyant fashion sense, and was a three-time gold medalist at the 1988 Summer Olympics.

name: Lise Meitner
profession: Paved Way for Splitting of Atom
headline: From 1968: Lise Meitner, Physicist, Is Dead at 89; Paved Way for Splitting of Atom
abstract: She laid much of the theoretical groundwork for the atomic bomb, although she did not participate directly in its production.

name: Golda Meir
headline: From 1978: Golda Meir, 80, Dies in Jerusalem; Israelis Acclaim ‘Stalwart Lioness’
abstract: Once a teacher in Milwaukee, she climbed the ranks of the Labor Party to become Israel’s first female prime minister.

name: Charlotte Perriand
headline: From 1999: Charlotte Perriand, Designer, Is Dead at 96
abstract: Le Corbusier famously told her, “We don’t embroider cushions here,” when she sought a job at his studio. Then he recognized her talent for design.

name: Jeremy Larner
profession: Wrote The Candidate, a Political Film Classic
headline: Jeremy Larner, 88, Dies; Wrote ‘The Candidate,’ a Political Film Classic
abstract: His Oscar-winning 1972 screenplay starred Robert Redford as an idealistic public interest lawyer making a run for the Senate.

name: Alan Trustman
headline: Alan Trustman, Lawyer Who Wrote ‘Thomas Crown Affair,’ Dies at 95
abstract: In a wide-ranging career, he was a member of a Boston white-shoe firm, a Swiss currency trader and a Hollywood screenwriter (“Bullitt” was another of his scripts).

name: Thaddeus Mosley
headline: Thaddeus Mosley, Sculptor Who Found Fame in His Last Decade, Dies at 99
abstract: A self-taught artist, he turned reclaimed wood into striking abstract works influenced by Brancusi, Noguchi and African art.

name: Tatjana Wood
headline: Tatjana Wood, Award-Winning Comic Book Colorist, Dies at 99
abstract: She was part of the acclaimed creative teams on comic book series for DC Comics, including Swamp Thing, which she called “Shvampy” in her German accent.

name: Country Joe McDonald
headline: Country Joe McDonald, Whose Antiwar Song Became an Anthem, Dies at 84
abstract: One of the starring acts at Woodstock, he and his band, the Fish, came out of the Bay Area’s psychedelic rock scene. He went on to a long career as a solo artist.

name: Colman McCarthy
headline: Colman McCarthy, 87, Journalist Who Waged Peace in the Classroom, Dies
abstract: For decades, he wrote a syndicated column in The Washington Post promoting nonviolence. That became the subject of a course he taught for nearly 40 years.

name: Bernard Lafayette Jr.
profession: Civil Rights Leader Helped Plan Selma March
headline: Bernard Lafayette Jr., 85, Dies; Civil Rights Leader Helped Plan Selma March
abstract: A close associate of Martin Luther King Jr. and John Lewis, he was involved in many of the key moments of the Black freedom struggle in the 1960s.

name: Bo Gritz
profession: Vietnam Veteran Called a Real-Life Rambo
headline: Bo Gritz, Vietnam Veteran Called a Real-Life Rambo, Dies at 87
abstract: He served in the Special Forces, led a postwar raid to find P.O.W.s and became a voice of the right-wing anti-government fringe.

name: John Caldwell
profession: Father of Cross-Country Skiing in U.S
headline: John Caldwell, Father of Cross-Country Skiing in U.S., Dies at 97
abstract: A former Olympian himself, he wrote the sport’s bible, coached the American team at five Winter Games and helped make Vermont a hub of Nordic sports.

name: Alexander Butterfield
profession: Revealed Nixon Tapes in Watergate Scandal
headline: Alexander Butterfield, Who Revealed Nixon Tapes in Watergate Scandal, Dies at 99
abstract: “There is tape in the Oval Office,” said Mr. Butterfield, a former White House aide, in testimony that rocked the Watergate hearings and led to the president’s resignation.

name: Karen Petrou
profession: Influential Fiscal Policy Analyst and Critic
headline: Karen Petrou, Influential Fiscal Policy Analyst and Critic, Dies at 72
abstract: Her insights on financial regulations and monetary policy guided big banks and Washington policymakers.

name: Monti Rock III
headline: Monti Rock III, Gleefully Untalented ‘Tonight Show’ Favorite, Dies at 86
abstract: He couldn’t sing, dance or tell funny stories. But Johnny Carson loved him and his persona: a D-list star clinging to celebrity.

name: Matt Snell
profession: Carried Jets to Stunning Upset in Super Bowl III
headline: Matt Snell Dies at 84; Carried Jets to Stunning Upset in Super Bowl III
abstract: His pounding runs for the underdog New York team against the Baltimore Colts secured a pivotal win for the American Football League.

name: Dan Simmons
headline: Dan Simmons, Genre-Leaping Author of ‘The Terror,’ Dies at 77
abstract: He moved easily and prolifically through science fiction, fantasy, horror, thrillers, crime and historical fiction. His book “The Terror” was made into a cable TV series.

name: Anthony J. Leggett
profession: Won Nobel for Theories on Superfluids
headline: Anthony J. Leggett Dies at 87; Won Nobel for Theories on Superfluids
abstract: When scientists unwittingly turned helium into a superfluid — a feat many thought was impossible — Dr. Leggett not only recognized what had happened but also explained how.

name: Angelika Saleh
headline: Angelika Saleh, the Angelika of Angelika Film Center, Dies at 90
abstract: After making the journey from prewar Germany to Madison Avenue opulence, she gave her name to one of New York’s most influential indie cinemas.

name: Jan Timman
profession: Fearless Chess Grandmaster and Bon Vivant
headline: Jan Timman Dies at 74; Fearless Chess Grandmaster and ‘Bon Vivant’
abstract: A Dutchman, he was considered the best player outside the Soviet Union for two decades, although he described himself as “lazy” and was open about using alcohol and drugs early on.

name: Peter Schneider
profession: His Novels Explored a Divided Germany
headline: Peter Schneider Dies at 85; His Novels Explored a Divided Germany
abstract: His best-known work, “The Wall Jumper,” proved prescient in its contention that the country would remain split even after reunification.

name: Stephen Koch
profession: Champion of a Belatedly Hailed Photographer
headline: Stephen Koch, 84, Dies; Champion of a Belatedly Hailed Photographer
abstract: A writer and critic, Mr. Koch struggled for years to shepherd his friend Peter Hujar’s underappreciated, Bohemian-world artwork to posthumous glory.

name: Bob Harlan
profession: Steered the Green Bay Packers to a Revival
headline: Bob Harlan, Who Steered the Green Bay Packers to a Revival, Dies at 89
abstract: Under his watch as president, the team brought on key players like Brett Favre, modernized Lambeau Field and once again became a Super Bowl threat.

name: Yanar Mohammed
profession: Iraqi Womens Rights Advocate, Is Killed by Gunmen
headline: Yanar Mohammed, 65, Iraqi Women’s Rights Advocate, Is Killed by Gunmen
abstract: She established a network of safe houses for abused women and was an outspoken critic of her country’s repressive institutions, despite the constant threat of violence.

name: Ron Delany
headline: Ron Delany, Runner Who Won Olympic Glory for Ireland, Dies at 91
abstract: As a Villanova student, he captured the 1,500-meter event in the 1956 Games in Melbourne. No Irish athlete since then has won another Olympic gold medal in track and field.

name: Roscoe Robinson
headline: Roscoe Robinson, Gospel Star Who Minted 1960s R&B Hits, Dies at 97
abstract: Although he wasn’t blind, he sang in three different gospel groups known as the Blind Boys before making a splash on the R&B and pop charts.

name: Walid Khalidi
profession: Scholar Called Father of Palestinian Studies
headline: Walid Khalidi, Scholar Called Father of Palestinian Studies, Dies at 100
abstract: As a historian and diplomat, he gave intellectual shape to his people and made sure that they played a role in negotiating their future.

name: Ernie Anastos
headline: Ernie Anastos, New York’s Everyman Newscaster, Dies at 82
abstract: A television journalist for four decades with 30 Emmy Awards, Mr. Anastos especially enjoyed delivering good news.

name: Lewis Lehrman
profession: Store Chain Executive Ran for N.Y. Governor
headline: Lewis Lehrman, 87, Dies; Store Chain Executive Ran for N.Y. Governor
abstract: After helping his family’s Rite-Aid drugstore empire flourish, he waged a surprisingly close but losing race as a Reagan Republican against Mario Cuomo in 1982.

name: Eleanor Abbott
headline: Overlooked No More: Eleanor Abbott, the Creator of Candy Land
abstract: She invented the game nearly 80 years ago to distract children who were suffering in the hospital during a polio outbreak.

name: Margareta Magnusson
profession: Wrote of Cleaning Up Before Dying
headline: Margareta Magnusson, 91, Dies; Wrote of Cleaning Up Before Dying
abstract: Her best-selling book encouraged people to tidy up homes and lives as death approached — as a gift for loved ones and to revisit memories.

name: Bobby Douglas
headline: Bobby Douglas, Pathbreaking Olympic Wrestler, Dies at 83
abstract: In 1964, he was one of the first three African Americans to compete in wrestling at the Games. He went on to have a distinguished coaching career.

name: Jürgen Habermas
profession: One of Postwar Germanys Most Influential Thinkers
headline: Jürgen Habermas Dies at 96; One of Postwar Germany’s Most Influential Thinkers
abstract: In dozens of books, he rejected postmodern cynicism about truth and reason, arguing that rational communication was the best way to redeem democratic society.

name: John M. Perkins
headline: John M. Perkins Dies at 95; Evangelical Minister Espoused Social Justice
abstract: Inspired by the Gospel, he helped create a national network of community-development ministries “styled on the life of Jesus, who had the greatest concern for the weakest of people.”

name: Paula Doress-Worters
headline: Paula Doress-Worters, an Author of ‘Our Bodies, Ourselves,’ Dies at 87
abstract: She wrote about postpartum depression when it was an unmentionable like abortion or birth control, and her research on her own suffering helped countless women.

name: John Bengtson
headline: John Bengtson, Modern-Day Silent-Film Sleuth, Dies at 68
abstract: Enamored of stars like Charlie Chaplin, he matched outdoor scenes from their movies to contemporary locales, creating a visual record of vanished cityscapes.

name: David A. Keene
headline: David A. Keene, Leader of Two Right-Wing Groups, Dies at 80
abstract: He led the N.R.A. and, for 29 years, the American Conservative Union, which organizes the influential annual Conservative Political Action Conference, or CPAC. He was also a columnist.

name: Judy Pace
profession: Actress Brought Layers to Black Characters
headline: Judy Pace, 83, Dies; Actress Brought Layers to Black Characters
abstract: On the prime-time soap opera “Peyton Place,” she played one of TV’s first Black female antagonists. She was also a fixture in blaxploitation films.

name: Len Deighton
headline: Len Deighton, Author of Espionage Best-Sellers, Dies at 97
abstract: His Cold War thrillers “The Ipcress File” and “Funeral in Berlin” brought a documentary-style realism to the spy genre.

name: Albert Zuckerman
profession: Literary Agent and Hero of the Blockbuster
headline: Albert Zuckerman, Literary Agent and ‘Hero of the Blockbuster,’ Dies at 94
abstract: During his 50-year career, he represented dozens of best-selling authors, including Ken Follett, Stephen Hawking and Michael Lewis.

name: Christopher A. Sims
profession: Won Nobel on Ways to Steer the Economy
headline: Christopher A. Sims, 83, Dies; Won Nobel on Ways to Steer the Economy
abstract: He shared the 2011 prize for devising statistical tools to help guide central bankers and other policymakers on matters like tax cuts and rises in labor costs.

name: Richard Mauer
headline: Richard Mauer, Reporter Who Probed Corruption in Alaska, Dies at 76
abstract: He routinely took on the powerful and was part of a Pulitzer-winning team at The Anchorage Daily News that investigated alcoholism and suicide among Alaska Natives.

name: Alfredo Bryce Echenique
headline: Alfredo Bryce Echenique, 87, Dies; Novelist Bared Peru’s Privileged Class
abstract: “The other Peruvian” (alongside Mario Vargas Llosa), he exposed the heedlessness of the upper crust, which he knew well, and the suffering of the underclasses.

name: Ali Larijani
headline: Ali Larijani, a Top Iranian Politician and Emissary, Is Dead at 67
abstract: Killed in an Israeli attack, he was Iran’s leading national security official and a confidant of the former supreme leader. He led a brutal crackdown on protests this year.

name: Alvin Greene
headline: Alvin Greene, a No-Show Senate Nominee Who Won Primary, Dies at 48
abstract: He made no effort to campaign but won the South Carolina Democratic primary in 2010, becoming the state’s first Black major-party nominee for the Senate.

name: Carol Kitman
headline: Carol Kitman, 96, Dies; Photographer Documented the Vindman Twins
abstract: A chance encounter in Brooklyn led to a decades-long project following the boys’ lives, from childhood to national prominence as critics of President Trump.

name: James Barnard
headline: James Barnard, a Global Force in Wastewater Treatment, Dies at 90
abstract: An environmental engineer, he invented a biological method to remove nitrogen and phosphorous from wastewater, an advance that transformed the industry worldwide.

name: Jane Lapotaire
profession: Actress Hailed Across the Atlantic for Piaf
headline: Jane Lapotaire, 81, Actress Hailed Across the Atlantic for ‘Piaf,’ Dies
abstract: A distinguished British stage veteran, she won an Olivier award in London and a Tony in New York for her dramatic portrayal of the French singer Édith Piaf.

name: Thomas Gentille
headline: Thomas Gentille, Artist Who Made Wearable Sculpture, Dies at 89
abstract: He was a master jeweler, but his pieces looked more like miniature contemporary artworks than anything you’d find at Cartier.

name: Patriarch Ilia II
profession: Spiritual Symbol of Stability in Georgia
headline: Patriarch Ilia II, a Spiritual Symbol of Stability in Georgia, Dies at 93
abstract: The longest-serving leader in the history of the Georgian Orthodox Church, he helped guide his country in its transition from Soviet repression to modern statehood.

name: Calvin Tomkins
headline: Calvin Tomkins, Who Profiled Giants of Modern Art, Dies at 100
abstract: On the staff of The New Yorker for more than 60 years, he wrote about Duchamp, Rauschenberg and many others. His books include “Living Well Is the Best Revenge.”

name: Chuck Norris
profession: Black-Belt Action Star of Movies and Television
headline: Chuck Norris, Black-Belt Action Star of Movies and Television, Dies at 86
abstract: He channeled his martial arts skills into heroic roles in films like “The Delta Force” and “Missing in Action” and in the long-running TV series “Walker, Texas Ranger.”

name: Bernard Rands
headline: Bernard Rands, Pulitzer-Winning Composer, Dies at 92
abstract: His early successes in the 1960s, writing in the complex vein of high modernism, yielded later in his career to a more accessibly lyrical style.

name: Shigeaki Mori
profession: Dogged Hiroshima Survivor Embraced by Obama
headline: Shigeaki Mori, 88, Dogged Hiroshima Survivor Embraced by Obama, Dies
abstract: He lived through the first atomic bombing in Japan and then spent decades researching the identities of 12 American P.O.W.s killed in the attack.

name: David Botstein
headline: David Botstein, Gene-Mapping Pioneer, Dies at 83
abstract: His method of locating genes in human DNA allowed researchers to find disease-causing genes, and later to map the entire, sprawling human genome.

name: Nicholas Brendon
profession: Beloved Sidekick on Buffy the Vampire Slayer
headline: Nicholas Brendon, Beloved Sidekick on ‘Buffy the Vampire Slayer,’ Dies at 54
abstract: He played the part of Xander Harris, one of Buffy’s closest friends, on the hit television show about a teenage girl who protects the world from monsters.

name: Umberto Bossi
profession: Fiery Founder of Italian Separatist Party
headline: Umberto Bossi, Fiery Founder of Italian Separatist Party, Dies at 84
abstract: A charismatic populist, he channeled the anger of a disaffected North, arguing — in inflammatory oratory — for secession and railing against a tide of migrants.

name: Paul Brainerd
headline: Paul Brainerd Dies at 78; Pioneered Desktop Publishing With PageMaker
abstract: His software brought printing into the digital age, allowing users to stop manually splicing columns of text and graphics and instead create layouts on a virtual pasteboard.

name: Robert S. Mueller III
profession: Rebuilt F.B.I. and Led Trump Inquiry
headline: Robert S. Mueller III, 81, Dies; Rebuilt F.B.I. and Led Trump Inquiry
abstract: He imposed the most significant overhaul of the F.B.I. in its history. Later, after concluding that Russia had interfered in the 2016 election, he became a target of the president’s anger.

name: Jeff Webb
headline: Jeff Webb, Who Built a Competitive Cheerleading Empire, Dies at 76
abstract: Through Varsity Spirit, the company he established in 1974, he turned cheerleading into a multibillion-dollar juggernaut and exerted control over almost every aspect of it.

name: Lionel Jospin
profession: Helped Set France on Socialist Path
headline: Lionel Jospin, Who Helped Set France on Socialist Path, Dies at 88
abstract: As prime minister beginning in 1997, he introduced a national 35-hour workweek and oversaw the replacement of the franc with the euro.

name: Lilias Folan
headline: Lilias Folan, Who Brought Yoga to Middle America, Dies at 90
abstract: With her bright leotards and soothing, welcoming tone, she helped to demystify a discipline that many Americans in the 1970s viewed as a counterculture practice.

name: Augie Meyers
headline: Augie Meyers, Pioneer of Tex-Mex Music, Dies at 85
abstract: His carnival-like swirls on the Vox organ helped define the sound of the border with groups like the Sir Douglas Quintet and the Texas Tornados.

name: Brian Doherty
headline: Brian Doherty, 57, Dies; Chronicled Libertarians and Other Outsiders
abstract: Fascinated by the fringes, he wrote a definitive history of libertarianism and books about underground comics and the Burning Man festival.

name: Catherine T. Nolan
headline: Catherine T. Nolan, a State Assembly Power From Queens, Is Dead at 67
abstract: In nearly four decades in Albany, leading key committees as a Democrat, she was an early supporter of liberal causes like labor rights and abortion protections.

name: Valerie Perrine
headline: Valerie Perrine, Screen Siren Who Won Critical Acclaim, Dies at 82
abstract: Known early on for skin-baring temptress roles, she later earned rave reviews, a Cannes award and an Oscar nomination for her performance in the Lenny Bruce biopic “Lenny.”

name: Mel Schilling
profession: Dating Expert on Married at First Sight
headline: Mel Schilling, Dating Expert on ‘Married at First Sight,’ Dies at 54
abstract: Ms. Schilling, an Australian psychologist, was diagnosed with colon cancer in 2023. Two weeks ago she said the disease had spread to her brain.

name: Mike Vernon
profession: Helped Spark the British Blues Boom
headline: Mike Vernon, Who Helped Spark the British Blues Boom, Dies at 81
abstract: He produced albums — by John Mayall & the Bluesbreakers, with Eric Clapton, and the early Fleetwood Mac — that defined 1960s blues rock. He also shepherded David Bowie’s debut album.

name: Michel Rolland
profession: Renowned but Polarizing Global Wine Maven
headline: Michel Rolland, 78, Renowned but Polarizing Global Wine Maven, Dies
abstract: A consultant with more than 150 clients on five continents, he was hugely influential. Supporters said he was a genius. Critics called him formulaic.

name: Kermit Gosnell
profession: Imprisoned Abortion Doctor Convicted of Murders
headline: Kermit Gosnell, 85, Dies; Imprisoned Abortion Doctor Convicted of Murders
abstract: Philadelphia prosecutors in 2013 said he killed babies who had emerged alive during late-term abortions. The case became a rallying cry for anti-abortion activists.

name: Larry Reed
headline: Larry Reed, Master of Shadow Puppetry, Dies at 81
abstract: Entranced by traditional Balinese puppet theater, he developed a modern, multicultural version that he performed around the world.

name: Tracy Kidder
profession: Author of The Soul of a New Machine
headline: Tracy Kidder, Author of ‘The Soul of a New Machine,’ Dies at 80
abstract: A Pulitzer Prize-winning narrative journalist, he wrote deeply reported books that often focused on heroic goodness in people.

name: Daphne Selfe
headline: Daphne Selfe, World’s Oldest Professional Model, Dies at 97
abstract: Starting in 1949, she had an on-and-off career that lasted for 75 years. But her biggest success came late in life, modeling for labels like Dolce & Gabbana.

name: Pat Steir
headline: Pat Steir, Painter of Luminous ‘Waterfalls,’ Dies at 87
abstract: Spilling paint onto canvas and letting it streak down as it pleased, she often said that her celebrated works painted themselves.

name: Boubacar Ould Messaoud
headline: Boubacar Ould Messaoud, Leader in an Antislavery Fight, Dies at 80
abstract: Despite being imprisoned and harassed, he helped found an organization to combat slavery in his West African nation of Mauritania.

name: Heisuke Hironaka
headline: Heisuke Hironaka, Groundbreaking Mathematician, Is Dead at 94
abstract: A recipient of his profession’s prestigious Fields Medal, he devised an algorithm that helps solve mathematical “singularities.” It now permeates the field.

name: Leonid Radvinsky
headline: Leonid Radvinsky, 43, Dies; Built the Adult-Entertainment Giant OnlyFans
abstract: By leveraging social media and the influencer economy, he turned his website into a byword for online pornography in the 21st century.

name: Chip Taylor
profession: Writer of Wild Thing and Other Rock Hits
headline: Chip Taylor, Writer of ‘Wild Thing’ and Other Rock Hits, Dies at 86
abstract: The brother of the actor Jon Voight, he wrote songs for Frank Sinatra, Janis Joplin, Anne Murray and, with “Angel of the Morning,” Juice Newton.

name: Dash Crofts
headline: Dash Crofts, of the Soft-Rock Duo That Sang ‘Summer Breeze,’ Dies at 87
abstract: Seals & Crofts had a number of Billboard Top 20 songs in the 1970s before their chart topper brought them global fame.

name: Robert Fox
profession: Acclaimed Producer in Britain and on Broadway
headline: Robert Fox, Acclaimed Producer in Britain and on Broadway, Dies at 73
abstract: A favorite of actors like Maggie Smith, he produced dozens of plays, including “The Audience,” about Queen Elizabeth II, which was made into the Netflix show “The Crown.”

name: Sam Kieth
profession: Creator of Surreal Comic Book Series The Maxx
headline: Sam Kieth, Creator of Surreal Comic Book Series The Maxx, Dies at 63
abstract: A cocreator of Neil Gaiman’s Sandman series, he dreamed up The Maxx as a homeless character in the real world and a superhero in a subconscious realm. It was adapted for an MTV series.

name: Lee Geun-an
profession: Infamous Torture Master Under South Korean Dictator
headline: Lee Geun-an, Infamous ‘Torture Master’ Under South Korean Dictator, Dies at 88
abstract: The name of Mr. Lee, a former police inspector, had long incited fear and hatred in the country.

name: Jesse Roth
headline: Jesse Roth, Who Advanced the Understanding of Diabetes, Dies at 91
abstract: His research showed that Type 2 diabetes was caused by insulin resistance at the cellular level, a controversial idea that initially met with disbelief.

name: Coleman Barks
profession: Popularized the Islamic Poet Rumi in the West
headline: Coleman Barks, Who Popularized the Islamic Poet Rumi in the West, Dies at 88
abstract: Although he did not speak a word of Persian, his interpretations of the 13th-century mystic’s work made Rumi a New Age icon for millions.

name: Letizia Mowinckel
profession: Procured Jacqueline Kennedys Pink Chanel Suit
headline: Letizia Mowinckel, Who Procured Jacqueline Kennedy’s Pink Chanel Suit, Dies at 105
abstract: Mrs. Kennedy was wearing the suit when her husband was assassinated in Dallas in November 1963, and it became soaked in his blood.

name: Alexander Kluge
headline: Alexander Kluge, 94, Revolutionary Filmmaker in Postwar Germany, Dies
abstract: As a director, theorist and prolific author, he was one of his country’s towering artists and public intellectuals.

name: Gertrude Chandler Warner
headline: Overlooked No More: Gertrude Chandler Warner, Author of ‘The Boxcar Children’
abstract: Her best-selling series, about four children who live in a train car and solve mysteries, inspired sequels, spinoffs and animated films.

name: Robert Trivers
headline: Robert Trivers, Eccentric Scientist Who Probed Human Nature, Dies at 83
abstract: A visionary evolutionary biologist, he drew comparisons to Charles Darwin with his theories on the genetic roots of seemingly detrimental behaviors like self-deception.

name: James Tolkan
profession: Tough-Talking Actor in Back to the Future and Top Gun
headline: James Tolkan, a Tough-Talking Actor in ‘Back to the Future’ and ‘Top Gun,’ Dies at 94
abstract: Mr. Tolkan’s career spanned decades but his breakout roles came as an authority figure in two popular films of the mid-1980s.

name: Judith L. Rapoport
headline: Judith L. Rapoport, Pioneer in Understanding O.C.D., Dies at 92
abstract: Her best-selling 1989 book, “The Boy Who Couldn’t Stop Washing,” based on her groundbreaking research, brought public awareness to obsessive-compulsive disorder.

name: Henry C. Lee
profession: Forensic Scientist Testified in Defense of O.J. Simpson
headline: Henry C. Lee Dies at 87; Forensic Scientist Testified in Defense of O.J. Simpson
abstract: The Times called him “the world’s most highly regarded forensic criminologist,” but later in his career he faced accusations that he had hidden and fabricated evidence.

name: Eric Overmyer
headline: Eric Overmyer, Who Wrote for Modern Television Classics, Dies at 74
abstract: Trained as a playwright, he got his first TV writing job on “St. Elsewhere,” then worked on “Homicide: Life on the Street,” “The Wire,” “Treme” and “Bosch.”

name: Nicholas Haysom
headline: Nicholas Haysom, Apartheid Foe Who Became a U.N. Peacemaker, Dies at 73
abstract: As an anti-apartheid lawyer, he was jailed several times. Later, he was a top adviser to Nelson Mandela and held key posts at the United Nations.

name: Agosto Machado
headline: Agosto Machado Is Dead; Artist Memorialized New York’s Avant-Garde
abstract: An experimental theater veteran, he collected the ephemera of his friends and colleagues. As they began to die, he made shrines honoring them.
age_note: Believed to be in his late 80s

name: Mary Beth Hurt
profession: Actress Acclaimed in Interiors and Garp
headline: Mary Beth Hurt, Actress Acclaimed in ‘Interiors’ and ‘Garp,’ Dies at 79
abstract: She elevated supporting film roles with insight and improvisational skill, a talent she took to Broadway, earning Tony nominations.

name: Ben Stevenson
headline: Ben Stevenson, Choreographer With Global Reach, Dies at 89
abstract: He created dances performed worldwide, and, under his leadership, the Houston Ballet grew into one of America’s largest and most prominent troupes.

name: Melvin Edwards
headline: Melvin Edwards, Sculptor Who Wove Black History Into Art, Dies at 88
abstract: Lynch Fragments, a series of abstract steel sculptures he created starting in 1963, evoked the long, devastating history of violence against Black Americans.

name: Slava Tsukerman
profession: Directed the Cult Classic Liquid Sky
headline: Slava Tsukerman, Who Directed the Cult Classic ‘Liquid Sky,’ Dies at 86
abstract: A Russian-born director, he created a film about New Wave models and killer aliens in 1980s New York, helping to reshape independent filmmaking in America.

name: Josefina Aguilar
headline: Josefina Aguilar, Who Depicted Mexican Life in Clay, Dies at 80
abstract: Her sculpted figurines were hailed as exemplars of folk art, drawing a Rockefeller’s admiration. She continued her artistry even after losing her eyesight.

name: Stephen Lewis
profession: Leftist Canadian Politician and AIDS Activist
headline: Stephen Lewis, Leftist Canadian Politician and AIDS Activist, Dies at 88
abstract: Part of a political dynasty, he led Ontario’s main progressive party, became Canada’s U.N. ambassador and campaigned against the spread of AIDS in Africa.

name: Bettina Köster
headline: Bettina Köster, a Leading Voice in Berlin’s 1980s Avant-Garde, Dies at 66
abstract: She sang lead for influential all-female bands, including Malaria!, and toured in the U.S. and elsewhere with groups like the Birthday Party and New Order.

name: Liamine Zeroual
headline: Liamine Zeroual, Algerian President During Civil War, Dies at 84
abstract: Cutting short his five-year term amid a scarring conflict, he was perhaps a first: an Algerian leader who left office without being forced out or dying.

name: Biruté Galdikas
headline: Biruté Galdikas, Champion of Endangered Orangutans, Dies at 79
abstract: With Jane Goodall and Dian Fossey, she was one of three prominent researchers of great apes who were sometimes called the “trimates.”

name: Pedro Friedeberg
headline: Pedro Friedeberg, Whose Hand Chair Drew Outsize Attention, Dies at 90
abstract: Known for his hallucinatory canvases, he cemented his fame with a chair, shaped like a hand, that was both a work of art and a pop culture curio.

name: Dolores Keane
profession: Singer Known as the Soul of Ireland
headline: Dolores Keane, Singer Known as the ‘Soul of Ireland,’ Dies at 72
abstract: She sang of homesickness and longing, and often collaborated with American musicians like John Prine and Emmylou Harris.

name: Carol Mullins
headline: Carol Mullins, Who Illuminated Dance for Decades, Dies at 86
abstract: She knew nothing about lighting when the director Robert Wilson asked her to work on his shows. She then spent over 40 years as a designer for Danspace Project.

name: Orion Samuelson
headline: Orion Samuelson, the Elvis Presley of Agricultural Radio, Dies at 91
abstract: As a host at WGN in Chicago for 60 years, he shared news that was essential to farmers in a homespun style that appealed to listeners from the city.

name: Tom Valenti
headline: Tom Valenti, Who Made Lamb Shanks a Showstopper, Dies at 67
abstract: At Ouest, on the Upper West Side, and other Manhattan restaurants, he served robust dishes in a style he called “haute cuisine with the grandma gene.”

name: Mary Rand
profession: Star British Olympian in the Swinging 60s
headline: Mary Rand, Star British Olympian in the Swinging ’60s, Dies at 86
abstract: In 1964, she became the first from her country to win a gold medal in track and field, in the long jump, becoming a celebrity in the Beatles era.

name: Elisabeth Waldo
headline: Elisabeth Waldo, 107, Who Fused Indigenous and Western Music, Dies
abstract: A classically-trained violinist, she incorporated traditional instruments native to Latin America in Western-style scores to create an atmospheric hybrid.

name: Ronald H. Spector
profession: Traced Social History in Books on War
headline: Ronald H. Spector, Who Traced Social History in Books on War, Dies at 83
abstract: A Vietnam veteran-turned-academic historian, he drew acclaim for portraying conflicts from the perspectives of generals as well as grunts on all sides, both in Vietnam and in World War II.

name: Joe Conzo Sr.
headline: Joe Conzo Sr., Guardian of Tito Puente’s Legacy, Dies at 83
abstract: He went from being a fan of the “Mambo King” to becoming his manager and personal historian. Later, he kept alive memories of a bygone era of New York Latino culture.

name: Peter Schrag
profession: Wrote of Dangers of Californias Populist Streak
headline: Peter Schrag Dies at 94; Wrote of Dangers of California’s Populist Streak
abstract: His best-received book explored the state’s infatuation with voter initiatives, which were sometimes pushed with anti-immigrant fervor.

name: Linda Dresner
headline: Linda Dresner, Old-School Guru of Avant-Garde Fashion, Dies at 88
abstract: Her minimalist gallery-like store on Park Avenue was a destination for generations of moneyed New Yorkers and helped change the way clothing is sold.

name: Norman Bussel
headline: Norman Bussel, Who Chronicled Veterans’ Unseen Traumas, Dies at 102
abstract: After a grueling year in a German prison camp during World War II, he endured crushing nightmares and survivor guilt back home, leading him to spread the word about veterans’ suffering.

name: Nathan Farb
headline: Nathan Farb, 85, Dies; Photographed Hippies, Siberians and Mountains
abstract: His camera captured subjects as diverse as New York City during the Summer of Love in 1967, Siberia under Soviet rule and the Adirondacks in upstate New York.

name: Craig Reedie
headline: Craig Reedie, Who Fought Doping in Global Sport, Dies at 84
abstract: He led the World Anti-Doping Agency when Russia’s state-sponsored doping system was exposed a decade ago. He received blowback for the agency’s response.

name: Wayne Perkins
headline: Wayne Perkins, Guitarist to the Stars, Dies at 74
abstract: Mr. Perkins worked with Bob Marley, Joni Mitchell and many others, almost joined the Rolling Stones and turned down an offer from Lynyrd Skynyrd.

name: Jim Whittaker
profession: First American to Reach Everests Summit
headline: Jim Whittaker, First American to Reach Everest’s Summit, Dies at 97
abstract: As an executive with the outdoor-supply retailer REI and an experienced climber, he conquered Mount Everest in 1963, when fewer than 10 people were known to have done so.

name: Martin Gugino
profession: Activist Shoved by Buffalo Police at 2020 Protest
headline: Martin Gugino, Activist Shoved by Buffalo Police at 2020 Protest, Dies
abstract: Mr. Gugino, 81, had filed a lawsuit in 2021 against the city of Buffalo and members of its police force after officers fractured his skull at a Black Lives Matter protest.

name: David B. Cornstein
profession: Envoy Helped Build Trumps Ties to Orban
headline: David B. Cornstein, 87, Dies; Envoy Helped Build Trump’s Ties to Orban
abstract: A former jewelry-counter magnate, he served in Hungary under his friend President Trump, strengthening relations between the two countries as Orban tilted rightward.

name: Rodolfo Acuña
profession: Forthright Scholar at Forefront of Chicano Studies
headline: Rodolfo Acuña, 93, Forthright Scholar at Forefront of Chicano Studies, Dies
abstract: An activist in the academy, he wrote a foundational text in the field, “Occupied America: A History of Chicanos.” It is still in print and still assigned to students.

name: Afrika Bambaataa
profession: Often Called the Godfather of Hip-Hop
headline: Afrika Bambaataa, Often Called the ‘Godfather of Hip-Hop,’ Dies at 68
abstract: A pioneering rapper and D.J. from the Bronx, he was a key force in propelling hip-hop into the mainstream. He was accused of child sexual abuse later in his career.

name: Bob Law
headline: Bob Law, Trailblazing Talk-Radio Host, Dies at 86
abstract: His wee-hours show “Night Talk” was a nationally syndicated stalwart, examining tough issues and spotlighting Black cultural and political stars.

name: Hilde Limondjian
headline: Hilde Limondjian, Met Museum’s Longtime Concert Impresario, Dies at 89
abstract: She gave New York debuts to artists like Cecilia Bartoli and Peter Serkin, and introduced new music by Philip Glass and others.

name: Fred Drasner
profession: Feisty Leader of The Daily News
headline: Fred Drasner, a Feisty Leader of The Daily News, Is Dead at 83
abstract: A former New York cabdriver who never lost his edge, he was co-publisher alongside Mort Zuckerman as he took on rival papers in the so-called tabloid wars.

name: Eliot Engel
headline: Eliot Engel, a 16-Term Bronx Liberal in Congress, Dies at 79
abstract: After defeating a Democratic fixture in a 1988 primary, he rose to lead the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and then was toppled himself in 2020, undone by an overheard comment.

name: Thomas S. Langner
profession: Linked Social Ills to Mental Illness
headline: Thomas S. Langner, Who Linked Social Ills to Mental Illness, Dies at 102
abstract: He helped lead what became known as the Midtown Manhattan Study, which showed that mental impairment is highly correlated with low socioeconomic status.

name: Davey Lopes
headline: Davey Lopes, Base-Stealing Maestro, Is Dead at 80
abstract: He was one of baseball’s most efficient thieves, and part of a storied infield quartet with the Los Angeles Dodgers, playing in four World Series.

name: Margaret Gipsy Moth
headline: Overlooked No More: Margaret Gipsy Moth, Fearless CNN Camera Operator
abstract: She covered conflicts across the globe, joking after she was injured in Sarajevo that she would be returning to find her missing teeth.

name: Pearl Fryar
headline: Pearl Fryar, a Picasso of Plants, Dies at 86
abstract: A self-taught topiary artist, he discovered a talent for carving trees and shrubs into extraordinary shapes, creating a world-famous garden in a tiny South Carolina town.

name: David Sklansky
headline: David Sklansky, the ‘First Nerd to Enter Poker,’ Dies at 78
abstract: An influential author and professional player, he helped transform a game long ruled by intuition into one based on game theory, probability and logic.

name: Edna Foa
profession: Pioneered Exposure Therapy to Treat PTSD
headline: Edna Foa, Who Pioneered Exposure Therapy to Treat PTSD, Dies at 88
abstract: A psychologist, she urged patients to confront the things that frightened them, revolutionizing her field’s approach to post-traumatic stress disorder.

name: Asha Bhosle
headline: Asha Bhosle, Longtime Voice of Indian Cinema, Dies at 92
abstract: Her distinctive and adventurous voice was the soundtrack for generations of Bollywood films.

name: Sid Krofft
profession: Created Zany TV Shows for Children of All Ages
headline: Sid Krofft, 96, Dies; Created Zany TV Shows for Children of All Ages
abstract: With his brother Marty, he released a string of wildly inventive programs, including “H.R. Pufnstuf” and “Land of the Lost.” Some became cult favorites, even among adults.

name: Adriano Goldschmied
headline: Adriano Goldschmied, ‘Godfather’ of Modern Denim, Dies at 82
abstract: An energetic entrepreneur, he developed more than 50 brands of jeans, including Gap 1969 and other cult classics.

name: Ishmael Jaffree
headline: Ishmael Jaffree, Who Won Case Rejecting School Prayer, Is Dead at 80
abstract: An Alabama parent, he objected to prayer in his children’s classrooms. The Supreme Court ruled for him, a high-water mark in the push for the strict separation of church and state.

name: Mario Ríos Montt
profession: Bishop and Brother of Genocidal General
headline: Mario Ríos Montt, Bishop and Brother of Genocidal General, Dies at 94
abstract: In Guatemala, he led the Catholic Church’s human rights office. His brother, a dictator who took power in a coup, was convicted of crimes against humanity.

name: Barbara Gordon
profession: Wrote a Best Seller About Her Pill Addiction
headline: Barbara Gordon, 90, Dies; Wrote a Best Seller About Her Pill Addiction
abstract: Her 1979 memoir, “I’m Dancing as Fast as I Can,” which also became a movie, detailed years of prescription drug abuse and offered an indictment of American psychiatry.

name: Carol Greitzer
headline: Carol Greitzer, Tireless Defender of Greenwich Village, Dies at 101
abstract: A lifelong New Yorker and longtime City Council member, she opposed Robert Moses’s wrecking ball, championed historic preservation and fought for women’s and gay rights.

name: Roger Adams
profession: Invented the Rolling Sneakers Known as Heelys
headline: Roger Adams Dies at 71; Invented the Rolling Sneakers Known as Heelys
abstract: You could walk in them like gym shoes, but if you rocked back on your heels the wheels emerged, turning them into roller skates. In the early 2000s, the company sold millions.

name: Mark Mobius
headline: Mark Mobius, Pioneering Investor in Emerging Markets, Dies at 89
abstract: Gaining a reputation as the brilliant, risk-taking “Indiana Jones” of his field, he encouraged investors to take chances on Asia, Africa, Latin America and Eastern Europe.

name: Celeste Dupuy-Spencer
headline: Celeste Dupuy-Spencer, Painter of Hotly Topical Images, Dies at 46
abstract: Her vibrant yet brooding work explored the crises of the Trump era, with paintings depicting the Jan. 6 riots and a mangled Confederate monument.

name: Iris Long
headline: Iris Long, Scientific Mentor to AIDS Activists, Dies at 92
abstract: A chemist, she lent her expertise in drug research to ACT UP, an organization known for its street protests, and helped accelerate the approval of H.I.V. and AIDS treatments.

name: Kevin Klose
headline: Kevin Klose, Who Made NPR a Reporting Powerhouse, Dies at 85
abstract: A longtime journalist at The Washington Post, he used his unexpected fund-raising talents to greatly expand the radio organization’s coverage.

name: Paul Waldman
profession: Creator and Curator of Art Museum for Birds
headline: Paul Waldman, Creator and Curator of Art Museum for Birds, Dies at 89
abstract: A dyslexic teenager, he reinvented himself as a bodybuilder. Then he turned to art, producing transgressive paintings and elaborate birdhouses.

name: Don Schlitz
profession: Prolific Writer of Country Music Hits
headline: Don Schlitz, Prolific Writer of Country Music Hits, Dies at 73
abstract: He won a Grammy for the Kenny Rogers song “The Gambler,” and also wrote for Randy Travis, the Judds and Mary Chapin Carpenter.

name: Harry Keyishian
profession: Lead Plaintiff in Academic Freedom Case
headline: Harry Keyishian, Lead Plaintiff in Academic Freedom Case, Dies at 93
abstract: He was one of five University of Buffalo faculty members fired for not signing loyalty oaths. In a landmark decision, the Supreme Court ruled in their favor.

name: Elaine Ingham
headline: Elaine Ingham, Who Taught That Soil Is Alive, Dies at 73
abstract: A scientist and leader in the organic farming movement, she popularized the “soil food web,” an understanding that soil is a complex realm of microorganisms.

name: Gwendolyn Chisolm
profession: Rhymed on Raps First Female Hit
headline: Gwendolyn Chisolm, Who Rhymed on Rap’s First Female Hit, Dies at 66
abstract: A chance encounter led to overnight success for the Sequence, a seminal trio whose “Funk You Up” broke barriers.

name: Moya Brennan
profession: Voice of the Gaelic Pop Band Clannad
headline: Moya Brennan, Voice of the Gaelic Pop Band Clannad, Dies at 73
abstract: The group could be heard on the soundtracks of the movies “Patriot Games” and “The Last of the Mohicans.” Its “Theme From Harry’s Game,” from a TV series, was a hit.

name: Desmond Morris
profession: Zoologist Saw Links Between Humans and Apes
headline: Desmond Morris, 98, Dies; Zoologist Saw Links Between Humans and Apes
abstract: His immensely popular, and controversial, 1967 book, “The Naked Ape,” argued that ancient genes, shared with apes, shape our lives.

name: Patrick Muldoon
profession: Days of Our Lives and Melrose Place Actor
headline: Patrick Muldoon, ‘Days of Our Lives’ and ‘Melrose Place’ Actor, Dies at 57
abstract: He played the handsome Austin Reed on the NBC daytime soap opera “Days of Our Lives” in more than 400 episodes.

name: Barbara Hatch Rosenberg
headline: Barbara Hatch Rosenberg, Who Joined Hunt for Anthrax Culprit, Dies at 97
abstract: An expert on biological weapons, she emerged as an influential voice during the F.B.I.’s rocky search for a suspect after the deadly anthrax attacks of 2001.

name: George Ariyoshi
profession: Americas First Governor of Asian Descent
headline: George Ariyoshi, 100, America’s First Governor of Asian Descent, Dies
abstract: A Democrat, he served three terms as Hawaii’s governor (1974-86), rising out of a tough district of Honolulu. He tried to diversify an economy heavily dependent on tourism.

name: Andrew Hacker
headline: Andrew Hacker, Author Who Challenged Conventional Thinking, Dies at 96
abstract: In a host of books and articles as a political scientist, he attacked received ideas on the battle of the sexes, the usefulness of high school math and other subjects.

name: Dave Mason
profession: Songwriter and a Co-Founder of Traffic
headline: Dave Mason, Songwriter and a Co-Founder of Traffic, Dies at 79
abstract: An English singer and guitarist, he wrote classic-rock mainstays like “Feelin’ Alright?” and “Only You Know and I Know.” He also had a successful solo career, singing “We Just Disagree.”

name: Oscar Schmidt
headline: Oscar Schmidt, Brazilian Superstar Who Spurned the N.B.A., Dies at 68
abstract: A Hall of Fame forward, he was a basketball scoring machine and an early master of the three-pointer. “There was not a shot I didn’t like,” he said.

name: Nathalie Baye
headline: Nathalie Baye, Versatile and Admired French Actress, Dies at 77
abstract: In films like “Day for Night,” “La Balance” and “The Return of Martin Guerre,” she was adept at portraying sensual, reflective or excitable characters.

name: Alan Osmond
headline: Alan Osmond, Who Led His Brothers in Song, Dies at 76
abstract: He was the eldest original member of the Osmonds, a family singing group that hit it big in the 1970s with songs like “One Bad Apple.”

name: Joy Harmon
profession: Car-Washing Temptress in Cool Hand Luke
headline: Joy Harmon, Car-Washing Temptress in ‘Cool Hand Luke,’ Dies at 87
abstract: All it took was a bucket of soapy water and a slinky housedress for her to achieve movie immortality in the 1967 Paul Newman classic.

name: Michael Tilson Thomas
headline: Michael Tilson Thomas, Celebrated American Conductor, Dies at 81
abstract: A galvanizing force in classical music as a conductor, composer, pianist and evangelist, he spent 25 years as music director of the San Francisco Symphony.

name: Ruth Slenczynska
headline: Ruth Slenczynska, 101, Dies; Piano Prodigy Overcame Father’s Abuse
abstract: Treated brutally, she went from celebrated child star to 15-year-old “burned-out candle.” Against the odds, she later resumed performing.

name: Darrell Sheets
headline: Darrell Sheets, Auction Bidder Who Starred on ‘Storage Wars,’ Dies at 67
abstract: He appeared in 13 seasons of the long-running reality television show about storage-unit auctions. He later opened an antique shop in Arizona.

name: Doug Allan
profession: Polar Cameraman for David Attenboroughs Films
headline: Doug Allan, Polar Cameraman for David Attenborough’s Films, Dies at 74
abstract: He was renowned for his skill at capturing candid scenes of penguins, polar bears and other cold-weather creatures — and for his ability to tolerate extreme discomfort.

name: Michael Harrison
headline: Michael Harrison, 67, Dies; Inventive Composer Who Played With Tuning
abstract: Influenced by Indian raga and nontraditional tuning systems, he created hypnotic works with a spiritual bent and created an unconventional piano.

name: Aldwyth
headline: Aldwyth, Ascetic Whose Artwork Reordered the World, Dies at 90
abstract: Holding to an austere lifestyle on a South Carolina island, she made collages and Joseph Cornell-like contraptions that told stories about art history and her place in it, and outside of it.

name: Wayne Moss
headline: Wayne Moss, Guitarist Who Helped Broaden Country Sound, Dies at 88
abstract: A top Nashville musician, he played on Bob Dylan’s “I Want You,” Roy Orbison’s “Oh, Pretty Woman” and Dolly Parton’s “Jolene.”

name: Lionel Rosenblatt
profession: Led Daring Rescue of Vietnamese Refugees
headline: Lionel Rosenblatt Dies at 82; Led Daring Rescue of Vietnamese Refugees
abstract: In an unsanctioned mission, the Foreign Service officer helped evacuate about 200 South Vietnamese citizens from Saigon days before the city fell in 1975.

name: Sonia Pressman Fuentes
headline: Sonia Pressman Fuentes, Early Women’s Rights Lawyer, Dies at 97
abstract: In a conversation with the feminist writer Betty Friedan, she planted the seed that became the National Organization for Women.

name: Semyon Gluzman
profession: Doctor Dared to Criticize Soviet Psychiatry
headline: Semyon Gluzman, 79, Dies; Doctor Dared to Criticize Soviet Psychiatry
abstract: He was imprisoned for calling attention to the practice of declaring dissidents mentally ill. He later led efforts to confront his field’s dark past.

name: Eugene Braunwald
headline: Eugene Braunwald, Whose Research Reshaped Cardiology, Dies at 96
abstract: His work changed how doctors understood heart attacks, heart failure and coronary artery disease, and helped lead to therapies that saved millions of lives.

name: Raghu Rai
headline: Raghu Rai, Photographer Who Captured Modern India, Dies at 83
abstract: Mr. Rai documented major figures like the Dalai Lama and Indira Gandhi, as well as the victims of a poison gas leak in the city of Bhopal.

name: David Malouf
headline: David Malouf, Novelist of Australia’s Divided Heritage, Dies at 92
abstract: Declared a national living treasure in 1997, he wrote poetry and short stories but was best known for his nine novels, including “The Great World.”

name: Luis Puenzo
headline: Luis Puenzo, Director of Oscar-Winning Argentine Film, Dies at 80
abstract: “The Official Story,” set during Argentina’s brutal military dictatorship, won the country its first Academy Award for best foreign language film, in 1986.

name: Nedra Talley Ross
profession: Last Surviving Member of the Ronettes
headline: Nedra Talley Ross, Last Surviving Member of the Ronettes, Dies at 80
abstract: With towering hairdos and perfect harmonies, she and her cousins Ronnie and Estelle brought a fresh edge to the girl-group sound in hits like “Be My Baby.”

name: Nick Pope
headline: Nick Pope, U.F.O. Sleuth Who Chased the Truth, Dies at 60
abstract: Often likened to Agent Mulder from “The X-Files,” he worked for Britain’s defense ministry and became a leading commentator on extraterrestrial matters.

name: Donald W. Riegle
headline: Donald W. Riegle, Representative Who Switched Parties, Dies at 88
abstract: Elected to Congress in 1966 as a Republican from Michigan, he grew disenchanted with his party during the Nixon presidency and became a progressive Democratic senator.

name: Dirk Kempthorne
profession: Former Idaho Governor and Interior Secretary
headline: Dirk Kempthorne, Former Idaho Governor and Interior Secretary, Dies at 74
abstract: A Republican, Mr. Kempthorne rose to prominence as the mayor of Boise in the late 1980s and early ’90s, as the city became a haven for outdoor enthusiasts.

name: Peter Raven
profession: Botanist Warned of Perils of Climate Change
headline: Peter Raven Dies at 89; Botanist Warned of Perils of Climate Change
abstract: He transformed the Missouri Botanical Garden into an international research hub and laid out the existential threats posed by deforestation and unchecked development.

name: Lester Wright
headline: Lester Wright, the Fastest Known Centenarian, Dies at 103
abstract: In 2022, at 100, he set what was believed to be a world record in the 100-meter dash at the Penn Relays in Philadelphia, beating 86- and 92-year-old competitors.

name: Roger Sweet
profession: Creator of the He-Man Action Figure
headline: Roger Sweet, Creator of the He-Man Action Figure, Dies at 91
abstract: The musclebound character he developed as a toy designer for Mattel gave rise to the Masters of the Universe franchise and helped define the machismo of the 1980s.

name: J. Craig Venter
headline: J. Craig Venter, Scientist Who Decoded the Human Genome, Dies at 79
abstract: A risk-taking outsider, he brought speed, competition and controversy to one of science’s biggest races.

name: David Allan Coe
headline: David Allan Coe, Singer Who Personified Outlaw Country, Dies at 86
abstract: Mr. Coe, who wrote “Take This Job and Shove It” and other hits, was a transgressive exponent of the outlaw country movement of the 1970s and ’80s.

name: Dean Tavoularis
headline: Dean Tavoularis, 93, Oscar-Winning Production Designer for Coppola, Dies
abstract: He worked on 13 Francis Ford Coppola films, including “The Godfather” trilogy and “Apocalypse Now,” and recreated the Las Vegas Strip for “One From the Heart.”

name: Georg Baselitz
headline: Georg Baselitz, German Neo-Expressionist Painter, Dies at 88
abstract: Along with contemporaries like Anselm Kiefer, he mounted a frontal attack on Minimalism and Conceptualism, the dominant “cool” styles of the 1970s.

name: Gerry Conway
profession: Creator of the Punisher in Spider-Man Comics
headline: Gerry Conway, a Creator of the Punisher in Spider-Man Comics, Dies at 73
abstract: The brutal assassin’s skull logo later took on new life as a political symbol. Mr. Conway was also responsible for the death of Gwen Stacy, Peter Parker’s love interest.

name: Stephanie Chernikowski
profession: Photographed the Rough Magic of Punk
headline: Stephanie Chernikowski, 84, Dies; Photographed the ‘Rough Magic’ of Punk
abstract: She captured the radiant chaos at New York City clubs like CBGB in the 1970s, when bands like the Ramones, Blondie and the Patti Smith Group were emerging.

name: Andy Kershaw
headline: Andy Kershaw, Radio D.J. Who Tuned Britons Into World Music, Dies at 66
abstract: A longtime BBC host, he traveled the world in search of artists his audience “didn’t know they wanted.” Then he took an unexpected turn into war reporting.

name: Seymour Bernstein
profession: Stage Fright Cut Short His Piano Career
headline: Seymour Bernstein Dies at 99; Stage Fright Cut Short His Piano Career
abstract: After giving his last public concert in 1977, he moved into teaching. A 2014 documentary directed by Ethan Hawke put him in the spotlight once more.

name: Steve Clark
headline: Steve Clark, Olympic Swimmer Who Confronted Depression, Dies at 82
abstract: A three-time gold medalist in the 1960s, he was a champion when athletes were expected to be stoic and vulnerability was viewed as a sign of mental weakness.

name: Nicole Hollander
headline: Nicole Hollander, Acerbic Feminist Cartoonist, Dies at 86
abstract: For more than 30 years, she wrote and illustrated “Sylvia,” a comic strip about a tart-tongued, witty woman unafraid of expressing her many opinions.

name: Ronald Smothers
headline: Ronald Smothers, Times Reporter Who Covered Protest and Politics, Dies at 79
abstract: In a career that included 35 years at The New York Times, he chronicled the Rev. Jesse Jackson’s 1984 presidential run and the bombing at the 1996 Olympics in Atlanta.

name: Jack Thornell
headline: Jack Thornell, Pulitzer-Winning A.P. Photographer, Dies at 86
abstract: He captured one of the most wrenching moments of the civil rights struggle: the agony of James Meredith after he was shot on a Mississippi highway.

name: John Sterling
headline: John Sterling, the Yankees’ Most Enduring Announcer, Dies at 87
abstract: He called over 5,600 games, more than any other announcer for the team, and was known for his personalized, slightly wacky home run calls.

name: María Nieves Rego
headline: María Nieves Rego, Who Helped Spark a Tango Renaissance, Dies at 91
abstract: With her dance partner and onetime husband, Juan Carlos Copes, she reinvented tango for a global stage, including in the hit stage show “Tango Argentino.”

name: Donlyn Lyndon
profession: Last Surviving Creator of the Sea Ranch
headline: Donlyn Lyndon, Last Surviving Creator of the Sea Ranch, Dies at 90
abstract: With his classmates Charles Moore, William Turnbull Jr. and Richard Whitaker, he designed an icon of modern architecture on a windswept bluff in Northern California.

name: Ted Turner
profession: Creator of CNN and the 24-Hour News Cycle
headline: Ted Turner, Creator of CNN and the 24-Hour News Cycle, Dies at 87
abstract: As one of the most important figures in media history, he oversaw a vast cable empire of news, sports and entertainment channels.

name: James Loehr
profession: Showed Athletes the Power of the Mind
headline: James Loehr, Who Showed Athletes the Power of the Mind, Dies at 83
abstract: He began practicing sports psychology before it was a profession, teaching athletes the importance of mental resilience and how to cultivate it.

name: Kendall Myers
headline: Kendall Myers, American Spy for Cuba, Dies at 88
abstract: While working for the State Department, he delivered top secret information to his Cuban handlers for 30 years. He was convicted and sentenced to life imprisonment.

name: Jack Bass
profession: Dean of South Carolina Political Journalism
headline: Jack Bass, Dean of South Carolina Political Journalism, Dies at 91
abstract: In articles and books, he wrote about the rapid racial, political and economic changes that transformed his state — and the South as a whole.

name: George Herms
headline: George Herms Dies at 90; Turned Castoff Objects Into Art
abstract: One of the last Beat Generation artists, he embraced the messiness of everyday life, making collages and assemblages from rusty junk and decaying objects.

name: Manuela Hoelterhoff
