headline: Manuela Hoelterhoff, Pulitzer-Winning Arts Critic, Dies at 77
abstract: She won the top journalism honor for criticism while with The Wall Street Journal. She later wrote a wry, perceptive book about the backstage world of opera.

name: Philip Caputo
headline: Philip Caputo, Who Wrote Blistering Vietnam War Memoir, Dies at 84
abstract: “A Rumor of War,” about his service as a Marine Corps infantry officer and published in 1977, relentlessly detailed “the things men do in war and the things war does to them.”

name: Festus Mogae
headline: Festus Mogae, Botswana President Who Tackled H.I.V., Dies at 86
abstract: He led the southern African nation for a decade and embraced a flagship American aid program credited with helping to eradicate the country’s AIDS epidemic.

name: Xia De-hong
profession: Persecuted in China, She Starred in Daughters Memoir
headline: Xia De-hong, 94, Dies; Persecuted in China, She Starred in Daughter’s Memoir
abstract: “Wild Swans,” a best-selling 1991 memoir, told the story of a stoic mother holding her family together amid torture and imprisonment under Mao’s regime.

name: J.H. Prynne
headline: J.H. Prynne, Erudite and Elusive British Poet, Dies at 89
abstract: Even admirers admitted his densely intellectual work could be “punishing.” Still, some considered him one of England’s most important poets.

name: Alex Zanardi
headline: Alex Zanardi, Racer Who Made Daring Comeback After Crash, Dies at 59
abstract: After losing both legs, the Italian champion persevered in auto racing. He also became a hand-cycling marathoner and Paralympian.

name: Edith Eva Eger
headline: Edith Eva Eger, Psychologist Who Barely Survived Auschwitz, Dies at 98
abstract: Her time in concentration camps brought her an understanding of humanity that helped her treat her patients.

name: Bobby Cox
headline: Bobby Cox, One of Baseball’s Top Managers, Dies at 84
abstract: He led the Atlanta Braves to victory in the 1990s and was later inducted into the Baseball Hall of Fame for his leadership.

name: Abraham Foxman
headline: Abraham Foxman, Warrior Against Antisemitism, Dies at 86
abstract: For almost three decades, he led the Anti-Defamation League, winning access to presidents and prime ministers and meeting with Pope John Paul II.

name: Dean Buntrock
headline: Dean Buntrock, Maestro of Waste Management, Dies at 94
abstract: Anticipating how the environmental movement would affect trash disposal in the United States, he built a 12-truck garbage company into a coast-to-coast behemoth.

name: Rex Reed
profession: Film Critic Known for Acerbic Reviews
headline: Rex Reed, Film Critic Known for Acerbic Reviews, Dies at 87
abstract: He fawned over Old Hollywood stars and sparred with Frank Sinatra. Nora Ephron marveled at his ability to get his subjects to say the things they did.

name: Leigh Magar
headline: Leigh Magar, High-End Milliner Turned Indigo Artist, Dies at 57
abstract: She was known for bespoke hats that attracted a celebrity following. Then she left Charleston for an island off South Carolina, where she began cultivating indigo.

name: Joni Lamb
headline: Joni Lamb, Whose Christian TV Station Went Global, Dies at 65
abstract: She and her husband, Marcus Lamb, founded Daystar Television Network, which reached more than 200 countries and made the couple into televangelism stars.

name: Betty Broderick
profession: Murder Trial Was Grist for TV Movies
headline: Betty Broderick, Whose Murder Trial Was Grist for TV Movies, Dies at 78
abstract: She killed her ex-husband and his new wife after what she described as years of psychological abuse. The crime inspired TV adaptations, a podcast and at least five books.

name: Claire Maurier
headline: Claire Maurier, the Narcissistic Mother in ‘400 Blows,’ Dies at 97
abstract: A landmark of New Wave cinema, “The 400 Blows” brought her enduring global attention. She later appeared in “La Cage Aux Folles” and “Amélie.”

name: Jason Collins
profession: First Active N.B.A. Player to Come Out as Gay
headline: Jason Collins, First Active N.B.A. Player to Come Out as Gay, Dies at 47
abstract: His achievements on the court were eclipsed by an essay he wrote in Sports Illustrated in 2013 in which he declared: “I’m a 34-year-old N.B.A. center. I’m Black and I’m gay.”

name: Nancy Cox
profession: Worked to Conquer the Wily Flu
headline: Nancy Cox, Who Worked to Conquer the Wily Flu, Dies at 77
abstract: As the leader of the C.D.C.’s influenza division, she battled to keep up with an ever-changing viral opponent, building a global network of researchers and forecasters.

name: Jackie Pung
headline: Overlooked No More: Jackie Pung, Pioneering Golfer Whose Setback Became Her Story
abstract: She was the first golfer from Hawaii to win a national championship. But she is best remembered for a mishap that cost her the biggest title of her career.

name: Koji Suzuki
headline: Koji Suzuki, Whose Horror Novels Inspired ‘Ring’ Movies, Dies at 68
abstract: Sometimes called the Stephen King of Japan, he helped create a genre known as J-horror and spawned one of the highest-grossing horror films ever made.

name: Cynthia Shange
profession: Defied Apartheid at a Beauty Pageant
headline: Cynthia Shange, Who Defied Apartheid at a Beauty Pageant, Dies at 76
abstract: She was the first Black South African to enter the Miss World contest, becoming an enduring symbol of glamour and resistance.

name: Judith Barnard
headline: Judith Barnard, of Best-Selling ‘Judith Michael’ Fame, Dies at 94
abstract: At 50, on a lark, she published a romance novel with her husband, Michael Fain. Like their characters, they found their lives transformed by unexpected success.

name: Clarence Carter
headline: Clarence Carter, Singer of Lust-Filled Soul Hits, Dies at 90
abstract: In songs like “Slip Away” and “Back Door Santa,” he performed with the fervor of a backwoods preacher and the bawdy humor of a juke joint.

name: Frank Stack
headline: Frank Stack, Painter Who Secretly Drew ‘The Adventures of Jesus,’ Dies at 88
abstract: For 20 years, he hid his identity behind the nom de plume Foolbert Sturgeon as he chronicled Christ’s encounters with modern-day hypocrites in comic-book form.

name: G. Robert Blakey
headline: G. Robert Blakey Dies at 90; Drafted the RICO Anti-Racketeering Statute
abstract: He was also the chief counsel to the House Select Committee on Assassinations in the late 1970s and spent years as a Notre Dame law professor.

name: Joe Sedelmaier
profession: Auteur Behind Wheres the Beef? Ad
headline: Joe Sedelmaier, Auteur Behind ‘Where’s the Beef?’ Ad, Dies at 92
abstract: He directed nearly 1,000 comedic commercials, including a much-quoted spot for Wendy’s and one for FedEx featuring a manic speed talker.

name: André Cerdini
profession: Judge in Trial of Nazi Klaus Barbie
headline: André Cerdini, Judge in Trial of Nazi Klaus Barbie, Dies at 96
abstract: He calmly presided over the historic 1987 trial in which a French court, for the first time, convicted a Nazi official of crimes against humanity.

name: Claudine Longet
headline: Claudine Longet, Entertainer Who Shot Olympian Boyfriend, Dies at 84
abstract: A singer and actress, she drew wide attention for the fatal 1976 shooting of Spider Sabich. She was convicted of negligent homicide.

name: Jack Douglas
headline: Jack Douglas, Producer for Aerosmith and Lennon, Dies at 80
abstract: A onetime Beatlemaniac, he helped shape the sound of hits like “Walk This Way” and “(Just Like) Starting Over.”

name: Félicien Kabuga
headline: Félicien Kabuga Dies; Accused of Masterminding Rwanda’s Genocide
abstract: One of his country’s richest businessmen, he fled arrest and escaped prosecution for allegedly financing and directing the bloodletting that cost 800,000 lives in 1994.

name: Peter G. Neumann
headline: Peter G. Neumann, Who Warned of Computer Security Risks, Dies at 93
abstract: For decades, he criticized the industry’s lax attitudes toward computer security and individual digital privacy. He also developed solutions.

name: Beverley Martyn
headline: Beverley Martyn, Whose Folk Music Breakthrough Took 50 Years, Dies at 79
abstract: As a rising star of the 1960s, she dated Paul Simon, brooded with Nick Drake and drew Barbra Streisand’s envy. Then she sank into an abusive marriage.

name: Edmund Phelps
profession: Upended the Way We View Inflation
headline: Edmund Phelps, Who Upended the Way We View Inflation, Dies at 92
abstract: He won a Nobel in 2006 for challenging the conventional wisdom among economists that higher inflation was a necessary price to pay for low unemployment.

name: Mark Fuhrman
profession: Flawed Witness in O.J. Simpson Trial
headline: Mark Fuhrman, Flawed Witness in O.J. Simpson Trial, Dies at 74
abstract: A Los Angeles police detective, he was discredited during Mr. Simpson’s 1995 murder trial by defense lawyers who pointed to his past use of racist language.

name: Felicity Lott
profession: Elegant Soprano in Opera and Song
headline: Felicity Lott, Elegant Soprano in Opera and Song, Dies at 79
abstract: Tall and self-possessed, with an air of wit and sophistication, she was superb in works by Mozart and Strauss, and was also a wide-ranging recitalist.

name: Greg Hyman
headline: Greg Hyman, Co-Creator of Tickle Me Elmo, Dies at 78
abstract: An electronics wizard, he was already a veteran inventor when he collaborated with Ron Dubren on an idea for a toy that giggled. The rest is retail history.

name: Barry Blaustein
headline: Barry Blaustein Dies at 71; Eddie Murphy Was His Muse
abstract: He helped create Buckwheat, Mister Robinson and other characters Mr. Murphy played on “Saturday Night Live,” and was a writer of films like “Coming to America.”

name: Barney Frank
profession: Gay Pioneer and Liberal Stalwart in Congress
headline: Barney Frank, Gay Pioneer and Liberal Stalwart in Congress, Dies at 86
abstract: Often voted the “brainiest,” “funniest” and “most eloquent” member of the House, he was also the first to come out voluntarily and helped normalize being openly gay in public office.

name: Sam Sianis
profession: Cheezborger-Flipping Owner of Chicagos Billy Goat Tavern
headline: Sam Sianis, ‘Cheezborger’-Flipping Owner of Chicago’s Billy Goat Tavern, Dies at 91
abstract: His dive bar became famous thanks to Mike Royko’s columns, a baseball curse and a “Saturday Night Live” skit.

name: Robert Woodson
profession: Leader of the Black Conservative Movement
headline: Robert Woodson, Leader of the Black Conservative Movement, Dies at 89
abstract: A veteran community activist, he believed self-reliance — rather than affirmative action or government help — was the way to fight racism, poverty and crime.

name: Mary Lovelace O’Neal
headline: Mary Lovelace O’Neal, Whose Paintings Were Saturated in Black, Dies at 84
abstract: An artist and activist, she gained prominence with monumental canvases that she soaked in the darkest substance she could find.

name: Michael Pennington
headline: Michael Pennington, Commanding Shakespeare Actor, Dies at 82
abstract: A mainstay of the Royal Shakespeare Company, he later started a rival theater group. He also appeared in “Return of the Jedi.”

name: Mert Lawwill
headline: Mert Lawwill, Champion Motorcyclist Who Starred With McQueen, Dies at 85
abstract: Featured in the 1971 documentary “On Any Sunday” with Steve McQueen, he was also a star in his own right, a national champion who designed innovative bikes and off-road gear.

name: Valie Export
profession: Made Art With Her Naked Body
headline: Valie Export, Who Made Art With Her Naked Body, Dies at 85
abstract: In provocative performance pieces and films, she forced viewers to confront misogyny in the media and society at large.

name: Kitty Bruce
headline: Kitty Bruce, Caretaker of Lenny Bruce’s Legacy, Dies at 70
abstract: As Mr. Bruce’s daughter, she maintained boxes of video and audio of his groundbreaking and often scandalous work.

name: Kyle Busch
headline: Kyle Busch, ‘Rowdy’ NASCAR Star, Dies at 41
abstract: The versatile (and at times intemperate) Busch was unsurpassed with 234 cumulative victories in the organization’s three national racing series.

name: Carlo Petrini
profession: Slow Food Movement Transformed How We Eat
headline: Carlo Petrini, Whose Slow Food Movement Transformed How We Eat, Dies at 76
abstract: Through his Slow Food organization, he spurred a worldwide shift toward sustainability and thoughtful cuisine.

name: Rob Base
profession: Rapper Known for It Takes Two
headline: Rob Base, Rapper Known for ‘It Takes Two,’ Dies at 59
abstract: The singer died on Friday after a “private battle with cancer,” according to his official Instagram account.

name: John Marion
headline: John Marion, the ‘God of Auctioneers in America,’ Dies at 92
abstract: For three decades, he was the face of the auction house Sotheby’s, presiding over an era in which art evolved from an object of passion into a commodity.

name: Grizz Chapman
headline: Grizz Chapman, Actor on ‘30 Rock,’ Dies at 52
abstract: Mr. Chapman, who played a member of Tracy Morgan’s entourage on the show, died on Friday, according to his cousin.

name: Rafe Pomerance
headline: Rafe Pomerance, the Paul Revere of Climate Change, Dies at 79
abstract: An environmental lobbyist and activist, he was a pivotal figure in drawing public attention and political support to the existential issue.

name: Manny Nosowsky
headline: Manny Nosowsky, Whose Wordplay Enlivened Times Crosswords, Dies at 94
abstract: For nearly two decades, the prolific puzzle maker, a retired urologist, charmed solvers with his penchant for witty, waggish puns.

name: Clarence B. Jones
profession: Helped Shape I Have a Dream Speech
headline: Clarence B. Jones, Who Helped Shape ‘I Have a Dream’ Speech, Dies at 95
abstract: A confidant and lawyer for Martin Luther King, he was an unseen hand behind major civil rights events, including the 1963 March on Washington.

name: Sonny Rollins
headline: Sonny Rollins, Giant of the Jazz Saxophone, Is Dead at 95
abstract: Even by the standards of a music that prizes individuality, he stood out, as both a musician and a personality.

name: Ben Morea
headline: Ben Morea, Principal Provocateur of 1960s Anarchist Group, Dies at 84
abstract: An abstract painter who wanted to creatively destroy the gap between art and revolution, he loosely led a band of radicals with a profane name.

name: John Barbour
profession: Played Key Role in the Rise of Reality TV
headline: John Barbour, Who Played Key Role in the Rise of Reality TV, Dies at 93
abstract: He was a creator and producer of “Real People,” a hit NBC series about eccentrics and unusual lifestyles, which spawned imitators like “That’s Incredible!”

name: Robert Daley
profession: Multifaceted Author of Prince of the City
headline: Robert Daley, Multifaceted Author of ‘Prince of the City,’ Dies at 96
abstract: He wrote 31 books, often drawing on his experiences as a pro football publicist, a foreign correspondent and a gun-toting spokesman for the N.Y.P.D.

name: Manny Fernandez
headline: Manny Fernandez, Bulwark of Dolphins’ Defense, Dies at 79
abstract: He played a critical part in Miami’s 17-0 season in 1972, which ended with his spectacular defense in Super Bowl VII against Washington.

name: Donald E. Newhouse
profession: Low-Profile Heir to a Media Empire
headline: Donald E. Newhouse, Low-Profile Heir to a Media Empire, Dies at 96
abstract: He ran the newspaper division of Advance Publications, while his older brother, Si, ran the Condé Nast magazine operation.

name: Russ Hodge
headline: Russ Hodge Dies at 86; an Olympian, Like His Mother
abstract: Nicknamed Russell the Muscle, he finished ninth in the decathlon at the 1964 Games. His mother, Alice Arden, placed the same as a high jumper in 1936.

name: Margot Wellington
headline: Margot Wellington, Who Helped Save Grand Central Terminal, Dies at 91
abstract: As the director of the Municipal Art Society, she led the fight to rescue countless New York City landmarks from the wrecking ball.

name: David Henderson
headline: David Henderson, Innovative Poet and Hendrix Biographer, Dies at 83
abstract: Part of the Black Arts Movement of the 1960s, he went on to reclaim a leading musician of the psychedelic era as a distinctly African American artist.

name: Totó la Momposina
headline: Totó la Momposina, Colombian Folk Music Star, Dies at 85
abstract: Timbaland, Jay-Z and Major Lazer sampled her work, and she received a lifetime achievement award from the Latin Grammys in 2013.

name: Bob Horner
profession: Powerful Slugger in Atlanta and Japan
headline: Bob Horner, Powerful Slugger in Atlanta and Japan, Dies at 68
abstract: With the Braves, he hit a home run in his major league debut, won the Rookie of the Year Award, and later hit four home runs in a game.

name: Frank Hayden
profession: Led Global Growth of the Special Olympics
headline: Frank Hayden, Who Led Global Growth of the Special Olympics, Dies at 96
abstract: His research showing the positive effects of athletics on intellectually disabled children led Eunice Kennedy Shriver to ask him to help stage the Games.

name: Randall Bourscheidt
headline: Randall Bourscheidt, Wide-Ranging Arts Advocate, Dies at 81
abstract: He helped triple New York City’s arts budget, led research to promote cultural funding and supported artists with H.I.V. and AIDS.

name: Nancy Sheung
profession: Camera Captured Women on Their Own Terms
headline: Overlooked No More: Nancy Sheung, Whose Camera Captured Women on Their Own Terms
abstract: In 1960s Hong Kong, she used photography to portray women as bold, self-possessed and unconstrained by traditional expectations.

name: Marc Johnson
headline: Marc Johnson, Street Skateboarder Who Shaped a Sport’s Culture, Dies at 49
abstract: His appearance in the 2007 film “Fully Flared” helped earn him one of the sport’s most prestigious honors: Thrasher Magazine’s skater of the year.

name: Abdu Rabbu Mansour Hadi
headline: Abdu Rabbu Mansour Hadi, Exiled Ex-President of Yemen, Dies at 80
abstract: In a country fractured by civil war and other crises, he held the title of president from 2012 to 2022 and was widely seen as an ineffective ruler.

name: Claude Bessy
headline: Claude Bessy, Who Ruled Paris Opera Ballet School, Dies at 93
abstract: A tall, commanding ballerina, she led one of the world’s top dance institutions for decades, though her rigorous methods eventually drew criticism.

name: Dang Van Phuoc
headline: Dang Van Phuoc Dies at 90; Intrepid Photojournalist in Vietnam War
abstract: A photographer for The Associated Press, he spent a decade on the front lines of combat in his native Vietnam and lost his right eye in a grenade explosion.

name: Edgar Morin
headline: Edgar Morin, ‘Grandfather’ of French Intellectuals, Dies at 104
abstract: A former member of the Resistance, he went on to a career spanning eras and disciplines. His books and pronouncements carried moral authority.

name: Raymond Berry
profession: Hall of Fame Receiver for Champion Colts
headline: Raymond Berry, Hall of Fame Receiver for Champion Colts, Dies at 93
abstract: He was the quarterback Johnny Unitas’s secret weapon with flypaper hands, who rose — leaped, actually — to big occasions.

name: Andy Halliday
profession: Star of Vampire Lesbians of Sodom
headline: Andy Halliday, a Star of ‘Vampire Lesbians of Sodom,’ Dies at 73
abstract: A beloved member of Charles Busch’s Theater in Limbo repertory, he had an irrepressibly comic stage presence that masked a shy, tender disposition.

name: Rick Adelman
headline: Rick Adelman, Hall of Fame N.B.A. Coach, Dies at 79
abstract: His teams made the playoffs 16 times in 23 seasons, and he twice steered the Portland Trail Blazers to the league finals.

name: Marcia Lucas
headline: Marcia Lucas, Oscar-Winning ‘Star Wars’ Editor, Dies at 80
abstract: A close collaborator with George Lucas, her second husband, she was “the warmth and the heart” of his early films, the actor Mark Hamill said.

name: Bruce Crandall
profession: Part of a Heroic Rescue Mission in Vietnam
headline: Bruce Crandall, Part of a Heroic Rescue Mission in Vietnam, Dies at 93
abstract: “Fourteen times he flew into what they called the valley of death,” President George W. Bush said in awarding him the Medal of Honor in 2007.

name: Peabo Bryson
profession: Soul Singer Known as the Voice of Love
headline: Peabo Bryson, Soul Singer Known as the Voice of Love, Dies at 75
abstract: He was admired for impassioned duets with singers like Roberta Flack and Celine Dion and for the Disney hits “Beauty and the Beast” and “A Whole New World.”

name: Ruth Shack
profession: Early Champion of Gay Rights in Miami
headline: Ruth Shack, Early Champion of Gay Rights in Miami, Dies at 94
abstract: She sponsored one of the nation’s first anti-discrimination ordinances for gays and lesbians and later helped make Miami a global arts center.

name: John McClain
profession: Helped Keep Michael Jacksons Profits Flowing
headline: John McClain, Who Helped Keep Michael Jackson’s Profits Flowing, Dies at 72
abstract: A music executive with longstanding ties to the Jackson family, he worked to make Janet a star and Michael a posthumous commercial powerhouse.

name: Alex Younger
headline: Alex Younger, Former Head of Britain’s MI6, Dies at 62
abstract: As director of the espionage agency from 2014 to 2020, he confronted a range of threats, including international terrorism and an emboldened Russia.

name: Marjane Satrapi
headline: Marjane Satrapi, Artist and Author of ‘Persepolis,’ Dies at 56
abstract: Her popular graphic novel series, published in the early 2000s, followed an Iranian girl through the Islamic Revolution and the Iran-Iraq War.

name: Alan Gribben
headline: Alan Gribben, Twain Scholar Who Excised Slur From ‘Huck Finn,’ Dies at 84
abstract: He made it his mission to track down every book Mark Twain owned — and to fix what he saw as flaws that kept schools from teaching the author’s most famous works.

name: Limmie Pulliam
headline: Limmie Pulliam, Tenor Who Overcame the Stigma of His Size, Dies at 50
abstract: He quit singing in his early 20s when opera companies objected to his appearance, but after a 12-year absence he revived his career to acclaim.

name: Bernard Roizman
headline: Bernard Roizman, Virologist Who Demystified Herpes, Dies at 96
abstract: He mapped the herpes simplex virus genome, revealing how it invades cells. His work also helped lay the groundwork for potential vaccines and gene therapies.

name: Diane Carlson Evans
profession: Led Campaign for Vietnam Womens Memorial
headline: Diane Carlson Evans Dies at 79; Led Campaign for Vietnam Women’s Memorial
abstract: A former Army nurse who served in combat, she coordinated a 10-year effort to create a monument recognizing the contributions of the war’s thousands of nurses.

name: Speight Jenkins
headline: Speight Jenkins, Who Brought Adventure to Seattle Opera, Dies at 89
abstract: He had never produced a performance when he was hired as the company’s general director in 1983. But over 31 years (and lots of Wagner) he became beloved.

name: Alan Saret
headline: Alan Saret, Sculptor Who Made Clouds of Wire, Dies at 81
abstract: His best-known works were large, airy tangles that suggested tumbleweeds, nests or tulle. If a window was open, they might sway in the breeze.

name: Ned Jarrett
profession: Champion Stock Car Racer in the 1960s
headline: Ned Jarrett, Champion Stock Car Racer in the 1960s, Dies at 93
abstract: He won the sport’s most important series, NASCAR’s Grand National, and his son followed in his footsteps. Both were inducted into the Hall of Fame.

name: Anthony Head
profession: Buffys Watcher and a Ted Lasso Heel
headline: Anthony Head, Buffy’s Watcher and a ‘Ted Lasso’ Heel, Dies at 72
abstract: The British actor was a mainstay of influential television shows who first found fame as a Nescafe pitchman.

name: Pamela Hicks
profession: Lady-in-Waiting to Elizabeth II of Britain
headline: Pamela Hicks, Lady-in-Waiting to Elizabeth II of Britain, Dies at 97
abstract: The queen’s third cousin, she was a bridesmaid at the royal wedding in 1947, and witnessed firsthand pivotal moments in British history.

name: Alan Riding
profession: Times Correspondent in Latin America and Paris
headline: Alan Riding, Times Correspondent in Latin America and Paris, Dies at 82
abstract: He was a cosmopolitan observer and interpreter of societies he knew firsthand, whether writing about war in Nicaragua or the history and cultural salons of France.

name: Bob Packwood
profession: Senator Forced to Quit in Sex Scandal
headline: Bob Packwood, Senator Forced to Quit in Sex Scandal, Dies at 93
abstract: An unorthodox Republican, he helped shape tax policy and women’s rights legislation before resigning in 1995 amid accusations by more than 20 women of sexual misconduct.

name: Bernadette Chirac
headline: Bernadette Chirac, Formidable Ex-First Lady of France, Dies at 93
abstract: Long seen as the cool, coifed wife of the president, she emerged as a political player in her own right, as well as a relentless champion of charities.

name: Robert Coles
headline: Robert Coles, Pulitzer-Winning Child Psychiatrist, Is Dead at 97
abstract: His five-volume “Children of Crisis” series, published between 1967 and 1977, drew on his conversations with American children whose voices were not often heard.

name: Billie Tisch
headline: Billie Tisch, Influential New York Philanthropist, Dies at 98
abstract: The billionaire widow of Laurence Tisch, she raised money for WNYC radio and other cultural organizations, along with Jewish, medical and educational institutions.

name: Gordon S. Wood
headline: Gordon S. Wood, Pioneering Historian of Early America, Dies at 92
abstract: In a Pulitzer-winning book, “The Radicalism of the American Revolution,” he wrote that the colonists rose up against an entire worldview, not just against taxation.

name: Hoyle Schweitzer
headline: Hoyle Schweitzer, Who Brought Windsurfing to the Masses, Dies at 93
abstract: With his friend Jim Drake, he built the Windsurfer, a sailboard that was cheaper and more portable than most sailboats. It became a global phenomenon.

name: Albert Wolsky
headline: Albert Wolsky, Costume Designer for ‘All That Jazz’ and ‘Grease,’ Dies at 95
abstract: A go-to designer for directors like Bob Fosse and Paul Mazursky, he won two Oscars and created Olivia Newton-John’s indelibly sultry ensemble in “Grease.”

name: Julio Le Parc
headline: Julio Le Parc, Op Art Master Whose Sculptures Moved, Dies at 97
abstract: His socially engaged works, created over a 70-year career, sought to engage viewers through shifting lights, motors and even Ping-Pong balls.

name: John Basinger
profession: Memorized All 12 Books of Paradise Lost
headline: John Basinger, Who Memorized All 12 Books of ‘Paradise Lost,’ Dies at 92
abstract: After nearly nine years of practice, he made John Milton’s epic poem vividly dramatic for audiences and inspired a study of his “memory virtuosity.”

name: Souleymane Diallo
headline: Souleymane Diallo Dies at 80; Daring, Mocking Journalist in Guinea
abstract: He was harassed and briefly jailed for his work on Le Lynx, his satirical weekly newspaper, which investigated and caricatured a series of repressive leaders.

name: Duane Michals
headline: Duane Michals, Photographer With Stories to Tell, Dies at 94
abstract: A self-taught artist, he brought narrative to modern photography with sequences of staged black-and-white images, often accompanied by wry or lyrical captions.

name: Ernest Chambers
headline: Ernest Chambers, ‘Smothers Brothers’ TV Show Producer, Dies at 97
abstract: In the late 1960s, he and Saul Ilson oversaw a variety show known for its social and political satire, and together they helped fight network censors over its content.

name: Lee Raymond
headline: Lee Raymond, Who Created Exxon Mobil, Dies at 87
abstract: He oversaw Exxon’s acquisition of a rival, cut costs relentlessly and denied the scientific consensus on climate change.

name: William Coupon
profession: Wanted to Photograph Everyone in the World
headline: William Coupon, Who Wanted to ‘Photograph Everyone in the World,’ Dies at 73
abstract: Self-taught, he became a go-to portraitist for politicians, rock stars and other celebrities. He also documented Indigenous people and inmates on death row.

name: Cleve Moler
profession: Unlocked the Power of Computing for Millions
headline: Cleve Moler, Who Unlocked the Power of Computing for Millions, Dies at 86
abstract: He built interfaces that allowed engineers, scientists and everyday people to solve difficult problems without having to write the underlying code.

name: Alan Hale
headline: Alan Hale, Sky Watcher Who Created a Comet Sensation, Dies at 68
abstract: In 1995, he and Thomas Bopp spotted, from different states, the same mysterious object in the sky. What turned out to be a comet was named after them: Hale-Bopp.

name: Bha
profession: Seen by Some as Heir to Thai Throne
headline: Princess Bha, Seen by Some as Heir to Thai Throne, Dies at 47
abstract: Ever since she collapsed in a park three and a half years ago, speculation has swirled in Thailand about who could become the next monarch.

name: David Hockney
profession: Restored the Human Form to Art
headline: David Hockney, Who Restored the Human Form to Art, Dies at 88
abstract: His colorful figurative paintings were both conservative and iconoclastic, defying the dominant abstract schools of the mid-20th century.

name: Joe Negri
profession: Handyman and Music Maestro on Mister Rogers
headline: Joe Negri, Handyman and Music Maestro on ‘Mister Rogers,’ Dies at 99
abstract: An accomplished jazz guitarist, he appeared on more than 300 episodes of the public television show, playing alongside musicians like Wynton Marsalis and Yo-Yo Ma.

name: Charlie Dalin
profession: Set a Sailing Record While Battling Cancer
headline: Charlie Dalin, Who Set a Sailing Record While Battling Cancer, Dies at 42
abstract: Last year, while suffering from an advanced stomach tumor, he won the grueling Vendée Globe race, sailing 24,000 miles in just 64 days.

name: James Blood Ulmer
headline: James Blood Ulmer, Guitarist Who Smashed Through Genres, Dies at 86
abstract: A protégé of the saxophonist Ornette Coleman, he borrowed from and greatly influenced styles like funk, punk, jazz and the blues.

name: Charles Dennis
profession: Founder of the Avant-Garde Space P.S. 122
headline: Charles Dennis, a Founder of the Avant-Garde Space P.S. 122, Dies at 77
abstract: A performance artist, dancer, choreographer, videographer, filmmaker and curator, he was a central figure in the downtown Manhattan experimental arts scene.

name: Gene Shalit
profession: Film Critic Bristling With Hair and Puns
headline: Gene Shalit, Film Critic Bristling With Hair and Puns, Dies at 100
abstract: One of the nation’s most recognizable characters, he delivered his wacky commentary for more than 40 years on the “Today” show.

name: David Plowden
headline: David Plowden, Who Photographed a Disappearing America, Dies at 93
abstract: With his haunting images of steam locomotives, steel mills and Midwestern farms, the celebrated lensman revealed the poetry in the artifacts of manual labor.

name: Dito van Reigersberg
headline: Dito van Reigersberg, Avant-Garde and Drag Virtuoso, Dies at 53
abstract: A co-founder of Pig Iron Theater Company, known for its surreal productions, he also gave energetic performances as his alter ego, Martha Graham Cracker.

name: Jane Yolen
profession: Books for Children Drew on Everyday Life
headline: Jane Yolen, Whose Books for Children Drew on Everyday Life, Dies at 87
abstract: She wrote some 450 books, including novels, poetry and nonfiction in many genres. One critic called her “a modern equivalent to Aesop.”

name: Jean Ziegler
headline: Jean Ziegler, Swiss Gadfly Who Provoked His Countrymen, Dies at 92
abstract: In a nation that sees itself as a tranquil oasis of prosperity and business virtue, he drew death threats for pointing out a dark underside.

name: Ronald LaPread
headline: Ronald LaPread, Funky Bassist for the Commodores, Dies at 76
abstract: A talented musician, he lied when asked by Lionel Richie, the lead singer, if he played bass. Then he taught himself how, and was essential to the band’s success.

name: Abdullah Ibrahim
headline: Abdullah Ibrahim, Eminent South African Jazz Pianist, Dies at 91
abstract: His song “Mannenberg” became the unofficial anthem of the country’s fight against apartheid, with Nelson Mandela calling him “our Mozart.”

name: Roy Hattersley
headline: Roy Hattersley, Frontline Warrior of British Politics, Dies at 93
abstract: A Labour Party deputy who spent years in opposition, he criticized Conservatives and members of his own party, and was at the heart of major political moments.

name: Gregory Williams
profession: Academic With an Uncommon Perspective on Race
headline: Gregory Williams, Academic With an Uncommon Perspective on Race, Dies at 81
abstract: As a child, he discovered that his father — and therefore he and his siblings — had been passing for white. For the rest of his life, he identified as Black.

name: Carlo Ginzburg
profession: Told the History of the Obscure
headline: Carlo Ginzburg, Who Told the History of the Obscure, Dies at 87
abstract: In books like “The Cheese and the Worms,” he helped push beyond the story of great events and leaders, entering the minds and hearts of peasants.

name: Richard Tapia
headline: Richard Tapia, Mathematician Who Pushed to Diversify His Field, Dies at 88
abstract: A math whiz as a young man, he later blazed trails, both with his theoretical advances and his advocacy for minority students.

name: Robert Thurman
headline: Robert Thurman, Leading Interpreter of Tibetan Buddhism, Dies at 84
abstract: A former monk who was also Uma Thurman’s father, he made sure Buddhism retained its intellectual and spiritual rigor as it spread through the West.

name: Daveigh Chase
profession: Lilo & Stitch Voice Actor and The Ring Villain
headline: Daveigh Chase, ‘Lilo & Stitch’ Voice Actor and ‘The Ring’ Villain, Dies at 35
abstract: She brought the plucky Lilo to life in the popular animated film series, and unnerved viewers as the child villain Samara in the horror film “The Ring.”

name: Tariq El Sawah
headline: Tariq El Sawah, Guantánamo Prisoner Sent to Bosnia, Dies at 68
abstract: He spent nearly 14 years in U.S. custody and never had a day in court even as his deteriorating health drew scrutiny.

name: Danny Simmons
profession: Painter and Activist From a Creative Family
headline: Danny Simmons, Painter and Activist From a Creative Family, Dies at 72
abstract: The older brother of the music mogul Russell Simmons and the rapper Joseph Simmons, he made his own way as an artistic and entrepreneurial force in Brooklyn.

name: Renato Rosaldo
headline: Renato Rosaldo, Anthropologist Who Disrupted His Discipline, Dies at 85
abstract: After his wife’s death while doing fieldwork, he rejected writing as a detached observer, setting off a profound shift in cultural anthropology.

name: Jean Houston
headline: Jean Houston, ‘Midwife of Souls’ Who Advised Hillary Clinton, Dies at 89
abstract: The author of books like “The Possible Human,” she held workshops that drew on mythology, psychology and the experiential ethos of Esalen. But she refused to be called a guru.

name: Brian Large
profession: Brought Opera Vividly to Life on Film
headline: Brian Large, Who Brought Opera Vividly to Life on Film, Dies at 89
abstract: In a directing career that included over 70 Met Opera broadcasts, he said his work was “dictated by the music, by key change, by orchestration, by phrasing.”

name: James Burrows
headline: James Burrows, Master of the TV Sitcom, Dies at 85
abstract: Beloved by actors, he helped create “Cheers” and directed more than 1,000 episodes of hit shows like “Taxi,” “Friends” and “The Big Bang Theory.”

name: Robbie Basho
headline: Overlooked No More: Robbie Basho, Guitar Mystic Who Sought Enlightenment in Sound
abstract: He lived with chronic pain and deep loneliness, which he poured into boundary-pushing music that incorporated multicultural sounds.

name: François Englert
headline: François Englert, Nobelist Who Helped Predict the ‘God Particle,’ Dies at 93
abstract: His work paved the way for the discovery of the Higgs boson, which explained how particles acquire mass, solving one of the deepest mysteries in physics.

name: Tom Dreesen
headline: Tom Dreesen, Comic Who Kept Sinatra’s Crowds Laughing, Dies at 86
abstract: He rose from a hardscrabble childhood to form a pioneering interracial comedy duo. He later spent years opening for Frank Sinatra.

name: Mark Singer
profession: Longtime Writer for The New Yorker
headline: Mark Singer, Longtime Writer for The New Yorker, Dies at 75
abstract: He joined the magazine’s staff at 23. Among the subjects of his profiles were the magician Ricky Jay and a pre-politics Donald Trump.

name: Margaret Kerry
profession: Body and Soul of Disneys Tinker Bell
headline: Margaret Kerry, Body and Soul of Disney’s Tinker Bell, Dies at 97
abstract: A film crew and illustrator meticulously documented her pirouettes and pouts, giving substance to a character depicted previously as a spotlight onstage.

name: Alan Greenspan
profession: Fed Chairman Through Prosperity and Crisis
headline: Alan Greenspan, Fed Chairman Through Prosperity and Crisis, Dies at 100
abstract: The pre-eminent economic policymaker of his time and a skilled political operator, he favored market-friendly stances that would later come to be associated with destructive financial forces.

name: Clive Davis
profession: Hitmaking Titan of the Music Industry
headline: Clive Davis, Hitmaking Titan of the Music Industry, Dies at 94
abstract: He rose from a midlevel position at Columbia Records to become one of music’s most powerful executives, shepherding stars like Barry Manilow and Whitney Houston.

name: Ramiro Valdés Menéndez
headline: Ramiro Valdés Menéndez, Architect of Cuba’s Surveillance State, Dies at 94
abstract: Considered the country’s most powerful leader after the Castro brothers, he was the first director of the Interior Ministry, keeping a close eye on dissent.

name: Charles Hinman
headline: Charles Hinman, Who Brought New Dimensions to Painting, Dies at 93
abstract: Starting in the early 1960s, the New York artist blurred the line between painting and sculpture with his shaped, protruding canvases.

name: Lorcan O’Herlihy
headline: Lorcan O’Herlihy, Architect of Innovative Urban Housing, Dies at 66
abstract: Arguing that architecture is a “social act,” he built affordable homes on small lots in Los Angeles and elsewhere, with an eye toward smarter, more equitable design.

name: Jill Smokler
headline: Jill Smokler, Who Blogged as Scary Mommy, Dies at 48
abstract: A mother of three, she turned a whim into an online powerhouse, sharing a warts-and-all look at parenting that attracted millions of readers.

name: Shirley Lord
headline: Shirley Lord, Beauty Editor, Novelist and Society Fixture, Dies at 93
abstract: An early champion of the mind-body connection, she held influential positions at Vogue, wrote steamy novels and regularly appeared in the tabloids.

name: Norma Yaeger
headline: Norma Yaeger, Barrier-Breaking Stockbroker, Dies at 96
abstract: Over her husband’s objections, she became a Wall Street broker in the 1960s. She later started two securities firms in the overwhelmingly male financial world.

name: David Clayton-Thomas
headline: David Clayton-Thomas, Lead Singer of Blood, Sweat & Tears, Dies at 84
abstract: He was also the key lyricist of the Grammy-winning, genre-blending band, whose hits included “Spinning Wheel,” “And When I Die” and “You’ve Made Me So Very Happy.”

name: Frank Guarini
headline: Frank Guarini, Seven-Term New Jersey Representative, Dies at 101
abstract: A reform-minded Democrat, he served on the tax-writing House Ways and Means Committee and offered a pragmatic mix of progressive legislation and conservative fiscal philosophy.

name: Jerry Moriarty
headline: Jerry Moriarty, Painter Whose Brushstrokes Elevated Comics, Is Dead at 88
abstract: A self-described “paintoonist,” Mr. Moriarty created cartoons with spare dialogue that reminded his admirers of poetry or Samuel Beckett’s plays.

name: Nigel Cabourn
profession: Mens Wear Designer Revered for Vintage Aesthetic
headline: Nigel Cabourn, Men’s Wear Designer Revered for Vintage Aesthetic, Dies at 76
abstract: The antithesis of fast fashion, his clothes were modeled on heritage garments and mostly made in his native Britain.

name: John Stockwell
profession: Wrote a Tell-All Book About the C.I.A
headline: John Stockwell, Who Wrote a Tell-All Book About the C.I.A., Dies at 88
abstract: A former covert operative, he published his resignation letter in The Washington Post and went on to write “In Search of Enemies,” a book the agency sought to suppress.

name: Ann Blyth
headline: Ann Blyth, Oscar-Nominated ‘Mildred Pierce’ Actress, Dies at 98
abstract: She was just 17 when she played Joan Crawford’s ungrateful daughter in the classic 1945 melodrama. It was the high point of a robust but short film career.

name: Yves Lacoste
profession: Exposed U.S. Bombing of Vietnams Waterways
headline: Yves Lacoste, Who Exposed U.S. Bombing of Vietnam’s Waterways, Dies at 96
abstract: He used a geographer’s tools to demonstrate that North Vietnamese civilian infrastructure had been deliberately attacked, threatening millions of lives.

name: Richard Scolyer
headline: Richard Scolyer, Cancer Expert Who ‘Became His Own Subject,’ Dies at 59
abstract: His lifesaving melanoma research in Australia illuminated the treatment he underwent for his own brain tumor, an ordeal he courageously shared with the public.

name: Om Malik
profession: Blog Shaped How Silicon Valley Saw Itself
headline: Om Malik, Whose Blog Shaped How Silicon Valley Saw Itself, Dies at 59
abstract: Gigaom, which he started in 2001, established him as a leading voice in the tech world and signaled a shift in how the media covered the industry.

name: Bruno Bischofberger
headline: Bruno Bischofberger Dies at 86; Gallerist Championed Warhol and Basquiat
abstract: He was a quintessential art dealer of the go-go 1980s, when the booming market turned painters into celebrities.

name: Colette Shulman
headline: Colette Shulman, Soviet Analyst With On-the-Ground Insights, Dies at 94
abstract: She arrived in Moscow in 1955, two years after Stalin’s death, and spent several years as a journalist covering major events and ordinary Soviet lives.

name: Tony Brown
profession: Host of Public Affairs Show Aimed at Black Audiences
headline: Tony Brown, Host of Public Affairs Show Aimed at Black Audiences, Dies at 93
abstract: On “Tony Brown’s Journal,” he interviewed guests like Jesse Jackson and Lena Horne, and made programming decisions by asking himself, “Will it help Black people?”

name: Mignon Dunn
headline: Mignon Dunn, Mezzo-Soprano Known for ‘Carmen,’ Dies at 98
abstract: Growing up in Arkansas, she dreamed of singing at the Metropolitan Opera. She did so more than 650 times over 35 years.

name: Philippe Stern
profession: Heir to the Patek Philippe Watch Brand
headline: Philippe Stern, Heir to the Patek Philippe Watch Brand, Dies at 88
abstract: In an era of electronic timepieces, he marketed $40,000 handmade watches as status symbols, breathing new life into a struggling industry.

name: Les Mills
headline: Les Mills, Whose Gyms Helped Popularize Aerobics, Dies at 91
abstract: A New Zealand Olympian, he started a small gym in Auckland that grew into a worldwide chain.

name: George Gresham
headline: George Gresham, Health Care Union Powerhouse, Dies at 71
abstract: Until he lost an election last year amid accusations of self-enrichment, he was a longtime influential force in Democratic politics in New York.

name: Abdul Ahad Momand
profession: Only Afghan to Fly in Space
headline: Abdul Ahad Momand, Only Afghan to Fly in Space, Is Dead
abstract: A pilot in the Afghan Air Force, he was recruited for the Soviet space program. His 1988 flight took place as the Soviets were fighting a war in his country.

name: Courtney Sale Ross
profession: Founder and Funder of a Quirky School
headline: Courtney Sale Ross, Founder and Funder of a Quirky School, Dies at 78
abstract: Instead of home-schooling her daughter, she spent hundreds of millions of dollars building an idiosyncratic educational institution in the Hamptons.

name: Judah Gribetz
profession: Key Negotiator in New York Citys Fiscal Crisis
headline: Judah Gribetz, Key Negotiator in New York City’s Fiscal Crisis, Dies at 97
abstract: A top aide to Gov. Hugh L. Carey in the 1970s, he was an influential figure in talks between the governor and Abraham D. Beame, the mayor, as the city faced financial collapse.

name: John Loring
profession: Longtime Design Director at Tiffany & Company
headline: John Loring, Longtime Design Director at Tiffany & Company, Dies at 86
abstract: One of the country’s influential tastemakers, he oversaw the rapid expansion of Tiffany in the midst of seismic shifts in luxury retail.

name: Victor Willis
profession: Lead Singer of the Village People
headline: Victor Willis, Lead Singer of the Village People, Dies at 74
abstract: Often performing dressed as a helmeted police officer, he also co-wrote the group’s biggest hits, including “Y.M.C.A.” and “Macho Man.”

name: Michael Byrne
headline: Michael Byrne, British Stage Actor, Dies at 86
abstract: He had a long career in theater, and several small roles in big movies, including “Force 10 From Navarone” and “Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade.”

name: Charles H. Townsend
profession: Led Condé Nast During Digital Transition
headline: Charles H. Townsend Dies at 82; Led Condé Nast During Digital Transition
abstract: By 2016, when he retired from the parent company of glossy magazines like Vogue, Vanity Fair and The New Yorker, print was seriously struggling.

name: Rosemary M. Collyer
profession: Judge in F.B.I. and Guantánamo Bay Cases
headline: Rosemary M. Collyer, Judge in F.B.I. and Guantánamo Bay Cases, Dies at 80
abstract: From her seat on the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court, she criticized the way the F.B.I. had sought to wiretap an aide to President Donald Trump.

name: Herbert Lust
headline: Herbert Lust, Collector Who Befriended Giacometti, Dies at 99
abstract: He gravitated toward the work of artists he knew personally, like Alexander Calder and Robert Indiana, in amassing an unusual, important collection.

name: Robert Kimball
profession: Helped Uncover a Trove of Broadway History
headline: Robert Kimball, Who Helped Uncover a Trove of Broadway History, Dies at 86
abstract: He excavated a treasure hoard of manuscripts by George Gershwin, Cole Porter, Richard Rodgers and others that were found in a warehouse in Secaucus, N.J.

name: Artur Dmitriev
headline: Artur Dmitriev, Two-Time Olympic Pairs Skating Champion, Dies at 58
abstract: He won gold medals in 1992 and 1998, and was known for his dynamic power, elegance and charisma.

name: David S. Doty
headline: David S. Doty, Judge Who Helped Shape the Modern N.F.L., Dies at 96
abstract: He presided over the 1993 agreement that led to free agency and the salary cap, and for years oversaw the league’s disputes with its players.

name: Victoria Cruz
profession: Veteran of the Trans Rights Movement
headline: Victoria Cruz, Veteran of the Trans Rights Movement, Dies at 79
abstract: She was at the Stonewall Inn on the night of its 1969 police raid, and she later became a forceful advocate for survivors of anti-trans violence.

name: Stanley M. Gartler
headline: Stanley M. Gartler, Pioneer in Cancer Research, Dies at 102
abstract: He provided the first convincing evidence that cancerous tumors develop from a single mutated cell and later helped expose contamination by cells taken from Henrietta Lacks.

name: Bill Archer
headline: Bill Archer, Influential Texas Congressman, Is Dead at 98
abstract: Serving for 30 years, he eventually wrote virtually all tax laws considered by the House and was a major influence on budget bills as Ways and Means chairman.

name: Bertrand Grébaut
headline: Bertrand Grébaut, Influential French Chef, Is Dead at 44
abstract: He ventured to the Right Bank to create Septime, a restaurant focused on vegetable-oriented cuisine “that changed the trajectory of French cooking.”

name: Richard H. Glanton
headline: Richard H. Glanton, Combative Head of Barnes Foundation, Dies at 79
abstract: In the 1990s, he took 80 of the art institution’s paintings on tour — going against the founder’s wishes — to raise money for a renovation.

name: George E. Johnson
headline: George E. Johnson, Who Built a Black Hair-Care Empire, Dies at 99
abstract: Mr. Johnson’s hair product company, a longtime sponsor of “Soul Train,” was the first Black-owned company listed on a major American stock exchange.

name: Indio Solari
headline: Indio Solari, Argentine Rocker Who Packed Stadiums, Dies at 77
abstract: A counterculture icon with broad appeal, he compared himself to Bob Dylan and developed an especially fervent following among working-class youth.

name: Louise Lasser
headline: Louise Lasser, Star of TV’s ‘Mary Hartman,’ Is Dead at 87
abstract: She began her screen career in Woody Allen movies (he was also her husband), but she was best known for her portrayal of the Ohio housewife in the pigtails and puffed sleeves.

name: Penelope Keith
profession: Effortlessly Posh Star of British Sitcoms
headline: Penelope Keith, Effortlessly Posh Star of British Sitcoms, Dies at 86
abstract: A veteran stage actress, she starred in two of Britain’s most beloved TV comedies of the 1970s, “The Good Life” and “To the Manor Born.”

name: William D. Zabel
profession: High-Flying Lawyer and Civil Rights Champion
headline: William D. Zabel, High-Flying Lawyer and Civil Rights Champion, Dies at 89
abstract: He brokered celebrity divorces and recovered billions for victims of Bernie Madoff’s Ponzi scheme. But he was proudest of helping to legalize interracial marriage.

name: Bonnie Tyler
profession: Sang Total Eclipse of the Heart
headline: Bonnie Tyler, Who Sang ‘Total Eclipse of the Heart,’ Dies at 75
abstract: With a voice both weathered and operatic, she minted 1980s pop anthems like “Total Eclipse” and “Holding Out for a Hero.”

name: Wally Funk
profession: Set an Age Record for Space Travel
headline: Wally Funk, Who Set an Age Record for Space Travel, Dies at 87
abstract: As a young woman in the 1960s, she wasn’t allowed to become a NASA astronaut. She finally realized her long-held dream of flying in space as an octogenarian.

name: Joseph Fraumeni
profession: Helped Discover Genetic Link to Cancer
headline: Joseph Fraumeni, 93, Dies; Helped Discover Genetic Link to Cancer
abstract: Considered the founder of molecular epidemiology, he worked with Frederick P. Li to identify a hereditary disorder that increased the risk of developing cancer at a young age.

name: Garrincha
profession: Brazils Brilliant and Broken World Cup Hero
headline: Overlooked No More: Garrincha, Brazil’s Brilliant and Broken World Cup Hero
abstract: He helped lead Brazil to two championships alongside Pelé, but his on-field brilliance was eclipsed by a tragic personal life.

name: Hershel Parker
headline: Hershel Parker, Melville Scholar of Ahab-Like Obsessiveness, Dies at 90
abstract: The author of an exhaustive two-volume biography, he was “fanatical about his approach to scholarship and infatuated with Melville,” a colleague said.

name: Charlie Cunningham
headline: Charlie Cunningham, Mountain Bike Innovator, Dies at 77
abstract: In the late 1970s, he built what is considered the first off-road bicycle with a frame that was aluminum rather than steel, one of his many inventions.

name: Randolph Mantooth
headline: Randolph Mantooth, Who Played John Gage on ‘Emergency!,’ Dies at 80
abstract: His portrayal of the firefighter and paramedic on the 1970s television hit helped expand the American public’s familiarity with emergency medicine.

name: Yaacov Agam
headline: Yaacov Agam, Who Made Kinetic, Kaleidoscopic Art, Dies at 98
abstract: An Israeli artist, he became a global sensation, creating sculptures, paintings, toys and public works that delighted the eye and confounded perception.

name: Jayson Conner
profession: Gave Thousands of Backpacks to Those in Need
headline: Jayson Conner, 48, and Jeffrey Newman, 58, Die; Gave Thousands of Backpacks to Those in Need
abstract: The couple, who died within a few days of each other, provided needed supplies, like socks and wet wipes, to people living on New York City’s streets.

name: Lindsey Graham
profession: Republican Senator and Staunch Trump Ally
headline: Lindsey Graham, Republican Senator and Staunch Trump Ally, Dies at 71
abstract: He consistently pushed for the use of U.S. military power overseas. The Washington, D.C., medical examiner said he died of an aortic dissection, a tear in the body’s main artery.

name: Hamad bin Khalifa
headline: Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa, Ruler Who Transformed Qatar, Dies at 74
abstract: Under Sheikh Hamad, the tiny nation of Qatar developed immense natural gas wealth and cultivated influence far beyond its borders.

name: Sam Neill
headline: Sam Neill, Leading Man in ‘Jurassic Park,’ Dies at 78
abstract: He appeared in more than 150 films and TV shows over a five-decade career, but was perhaps best known for his star turn in the dinosaur blockbuster.

name: Shahrnush Parsipur
profession: Iranian Writer Imprisoned for Her Novels
headline: Shahrnush Parsipur, Iranian Writer Imprisoned for Her Novels, Dies at 80
abstract: Her best-known work, “Women Without Men,” was longlisted for the International Booker Prize this year.

name: Tony Rayns
profession: Helped Bring Asian Film to the World
headline: Tony Rayns, Who Helped Bring Asian Film to the World, Dies at 77
abstract: In reviews and at festivals, he played a key role in introducing English-speaking audiences to directors like Wong Kar-wai, Jia Zhangke and Bong Joon Ho.

name: Ed King
profession: Scarred Veteran of Mississippis Civil Rights Struggle
headline: Ed King, 89, Scarred Veteran of Mississippi’s Civil Rights Struggle, Dies
abstract: A minister disfigured in an attack on his life, he became what one historian called “the most visible white activist in the Mississippi movement.”

name: Pat Oliphant
headline: Pat Oliphant, Cartoonist Who Skewered the Powerful, Dies at 90
abstract: The winner of countless awards, including a Pulitzer Prize, he was described in 1990 as “the most influential political cartoonist now working.”

name: Antonio Rattín
profession: World Cup Expulsion Led to Penalty-Card System
headline: Antonio Rattín, Whose World Cup Expulsion Led to Penalty-Card System, Dies at 89
abstract: The ejection of the Argentine soccer star during a 1966 match against England led to the introduction of yellow and red cards.

name: Leonard Abramson
headline: Leonard Abramson, Health Care Innovator and Philanthropist, Dies at 93
abstract: He created U.S. Healthcare, one of the first H.M.O.s, and used his great wealth from the sale of the company for causes like advancing cancer research.

name: Phil Regan
profession: Dodgers Closer Known as the Vulture
headline: Phil Regan, Dodgers’ Closer Known as the Vulture, Dies at 89
abstract: He won 14 games in 1966 in relief, some of them following brilliant performances by the team’s starters, including Sandy Koufax, who bestowed the nickname.

name: Scott Bryce
headline: Scott Bryce, ‘As the World Turns’ Actor, Dies at 68
abstract: He originated the role of the scheming Craig Montgomery and appeared in 280 episodes of the CBS soap opera over more than two decades.

name: Guy Scott
profession: Caused a Stir as White Leader of Zambia
headline: Guy Scott, Who Caused a Stir as White Leader of Zambia, Dies at 82
abstract: Two decades after the fall of apartheid in South Africa, he served briefly as Africa’s only white president.

name: Akihiro Miwa
profession: Actor and Singer With Gender-Fluid Glamour
headline: Akihiro Miwa, Actor and Singer With Gender-Fluid Glamour, Dies at 91
abstract: In Japan, he was one of the first androgynous pop-culture stars and an inspirational figure. Abroad, he was known for his work in animated films by Hayao Miyazaki.

name: Mary-Dell Chilton
profession: Helped Create First Genetically Modified Plant
headline: Mary-Dell Chilton Dies at 87; Helped Create First Genetically Modified Plant
abstract: In 1982, she led the research team that figured out how to genetically alter plants, a discovery that would eventually transform global agriculture.

name: Dave Kendall
profession: Creator and Host of MTVs 120 Minutes
headline: Dave Kendall, Creator and Host of MTV’s ‘120 Minutes,’ Dies at 63
abstract: With his English accent and ubiquitous leather jacket, Mr. Kendall was the face of alternative music on MTV from 1989 to 1992.

name: Roger Summit
profession: Invented an Early Online Search Service
headline: Roger Summit, Who Invented an Early Online Search Service, Dies at 95
abstract: A research scientist at Lockheed, he came up with the idea for a computer system that would search scientific and technical literature almost instantaneously.

name: Brenda Fricker
profession: First Irish Actress to Win an Oscar
headline: Brenda Fricker, First Irish Actress to Win an Oscar, Dies at 81
abstract: She won for playing a stoic mother in “My Left Foot” and achieved cult status as a pigeon whisperer in Central Park in “Home Alone 2.”

name: Rudolph Marcus
headline: Rudolph Marcus, Who Illuminated Electrochemical Processes, Dies at 102
abstract: He received a 1992 Nobel Prize for developing a theory that explained fundamental processes behind photosynthesis, respiration, oxidation and even how fireflies produce light.

name: Lam Wing-Kee
headline: Lam Wing-Kee, Hong Kong Bookseller Who Defied Authorities, Dies at 70
abstract: One of five booksellers kidnapped by Chinese officials in 2015, Mr. Lam spoke out after his release and became an international cause célèbre.

name: Garfield Sobers
headline: Garfield Sobers, Renowned ‘All-Rounder’ Cricket Star, Dies at 89
abstract: A longtime West Indian captain, he could do it all on the pitch.

name: Ron Hunt
profession: Record-Holder for Being Hit by Pitches
headline: Ron Hunt, a Record-Holder for Being Hit by Pitches, Dies at 85
abstract: Though he was notable as a Met, his record for being hit by pitches the most times in a modern-era season — 50 — came while playing for the Expos.

name: Walt Odets
profession: Delved Into the Minds of Gay Men
headline: Walt Odets, Who Delved Into the Minds of Gay Men, Dies at 79
abstract: A psychologist, he wrote during the AIDS crisis about survivor’s guilt and depression in his H.I.V.-negative patients.

name: Joe Melson
profession: Wrote Only the Lonely and Other Hits With Roy Orbison
headline: Joe Melson, 91, Dies; Wrote ‘Only the Lonely’ and Other Hits With Roy Orbison
abstract: Working together closely, the pair turned out more than 200 songs, including “Crying,” “Running Scared” and “Blue Bayou.”

name: Lillian Roberts
headline: Lillian Roberts, Crusading New York Labor Leader, Dies at 98
abstract: She unionized state hospitals and battled with Mayor Michael R. Bloomberg during her feisty leadership of the nation’s largest municipal workers union.

name: Hal Williams
profession: Actor in First Wave of Black Sitcoms
headline: Hal Williams, Actor in First Wave of Black Sitcoms, Dies at 91
abstract: As a divorced father of three in Ohio, he moved to Hollywood to pursue his boyhood dream to act. He became a recognizable face on “Sanford and Son.”

name: Dave Dawson
profession: Co-Founder of Bespoke Lighting Company Urban Electric
headline: Dave Dawson, Co-Founder of Bespoke Lighting Company Urban Electric, Dies at 53
abstract: He and his wife knew nothing about the business when they decided to produce lighting in Charleston, S.C. Their company became a beacon of American manufacturing.

name: Denise Oliver-Velez
headline: Denise Oliver-Velez, a Powerful Voice of the Left, Dies at 78
abstract: She became the highest-ranking female member of the Young Lords in New York, where she pressed for women’s rights, and later joined the Black Panthers.

name: Susumu Tonegawa
profession: Nobel Laureate Showed How Antibodies Fight Infection
headline: Susumu Tonegawa Dies at 86; Nobel Laureate Showed How Antibodies Fight Infection
abstract: The first Japanese scientist to win the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine, he went on to discover how memories are stored, advancing understanding of how the brain works.

name: Plas Johnson
headline: Plas Johnson, Saxophonist Behind ‘The Pink Panther,’ Dies at 94
abstract: His recording for the theme song, written by Henry Mancini, included a solo improvised in the studio. He also backed Frank Sinatra and Barbra Streisand.

name: James Woolsey
headline: James Woolsey, Embattled C.I.A. Director Under Clinton, Dies at 84
abstract: He arrived in Washington a conservative Democrat and drifted rightward, supporting the 2003 invasion of Iraq and Donald J. Trump’s 2016 presidential bid.

name: Bobbi Queen
headline: Bobbi Queen, Fashion Arbiter Who Nurtured Stars, Dies at 84
abstract: As an influential editor at Women’s Wear Daily, she championed generations of designers, including Donna Karan and Vera Wang.

name: Doreen Broadnax
profession: Famous (as Sparky D) for 80s Rap Battle
headline: Doreen Broadnax, Famous (as Sparky D) for ’80s Rap Battle, Dies at 61
abstract: Tossing verbal grenades back and forth with Roxanne Shanté, she helped establish a lasting hip-hop truism: Bad blood is good business.

name: Peter Lassally
headline: Peter Lassally, Longtime Late-Night TV Producer, Dies at 93
abstract: He was known as the “host whisperer” for his success at producing shows starring Johnny Carson, David Letterman and Craig Ferguson.

name: Clint Reilly
headline: Clint Reilly, Political Consultant Known for Feuding, Dies at 79
abstract: As savvy as he could be volatile, he advised Nancy Pelosi and Dianne Feinstein, ran for mayor of San Francisco and bought The San Francisco Examiner.

name: Freddy Cannon
headline: Freddy Cannon, Rocker Who Sang ‘Palisades Park,’ Dies at 89
abstract: Known as Boom Boom, he recorded a string of hits in the 1950s and ’60s, including “Tallahassee Lassie,” which began as a poem by his mother.

name: Barbara Rubin
profession: Teenage Filmmaker at the Heart of New Yorks Underground
headline: Overlooked No More: Barbara Rubin, Teenage Filmmaker at the Heart of New York’s Underground
abstract: She made the landmark underground film “Christmas on Earth,” and helped bring together artists like Andy Warhol, Allen Ginsberg and Bob Dylan.

name: Chuck Russell
profession: Director of The Mask and Third Nightmare on Elm Street Movie
headline: Chuck Russell, Director of ‘The Mask’ and Third ‘Nightmare on Elm Street’ Movie, Dies at 74
abstract: His work, including “The Blob,” a remake of the cult 1958 horror movie, was known for its use of brash visual effects.

name: Guy Tudor
profession: Art Brought Obscure Birds to Life
headline: Guy Tudor, Whose Art Brought Obscure Birds to Life, Dies at 91
abstract: A self-taught ornithologist, he won a MacArthur fellowship for his precise, resplendent illustrations that appeared in definitive field guides to tropical songbirds.

name: Ida Schmertz
headline: Ida Schmertz, Who Studied Women in Politics, Dies at 91
abstract: An immigrant who aspired to government service, she helped found the pathbreaking Center for American Women and Politics at Rutgers.

name: Charles Gaines
headline: Charles Gaines, Whose ‘Pumping Iron’ Sparked Schwarzenegger’s Career, Dies at 84
abstract: An author and sportsman, he helped create the game of paintball and wrote the book and movie that made Arnold Schwarzenegger a household name.

name: Paul Andrews
profession: Founder of the Woodstock of U.F.O.s
headline: Paul Andrews, Founder of the Woodstock of U.F.O.s, Dies at 77
abstract: An annual convention in the California desert offered a safe space for believers to discuss extraterrestrial encounters, crop circles and other paranormal phenomena.

name: Betye Saar
headline: Betye Saar, Artist Who Upended Black Stereotypes, Dies at 99
abstract: Working with dolls, family photographs, fabric scraps and other found objects, she became a leading figure in assemblage art.

name: Bill McGlaughlin
headline: Bill McGlaughlin, Who Unlocked Classical Music for Many, Dies at 82
abstract: His public-radio programs “Saint Paul Sunday” and “Exploring Music” were, at their height, listened to by hundreds of thousands of people a week.

name: Keigo Higashino
headline: Keigo Higashino, Best-Selling Japanese Mystery Writer, Dies at 68
abstract: His works, which included “The Devotion of Suspect X,” were widely translated and adapted for the screen.

name: Lilly Yokoi
headline: Lilly Yokoi, Acrobat Who Dazzled on a Golden Bicycle, Dies at 96
abstract: With her family troupe — and later as a solo star — she performed balletic, gymnastic tricks in circuses and theaters, at fairs and on television.

name: Gunther von Hagens
profession: Creator of Polarizing Body Worlds Exhibits
headline: Gunther von Hagens, Creator of Polarizing ‘Body Worlds’ Exhibits, Dies at 81
abstract: A German scientist, he developed a process for turning corpses into posable figures. His shows drew millions of visitors, and many detractors.

name: Glen Hansard
profession: Frontman of Irish Band the Frames
headline: Glen Hansard, Frontman of Irish Band the Frames, Dies at 56
abstract: The popular singer-songwriter won, with Markéta Irglová, an Oscar for the song “Falling Slowly” from the film “Once.”

name: David Hirsch
profession: Turned Sonoma Coast Into World-Class Wine Region
headline: David Hirsch, Who Turned Sonoma Coast Into World-Class Wine Region, Dies at 81
abstract: He helped establish a windswept part of California as a source for great American pinot noir and chardonnay grapes, and later built his own winery.

name: Clara Ester
profession: Was With Martin Luther King Jr. in His Last Moments
headline: Clara Ester, Who Was With Martin Luther King Jr. in His Last Moments, Dies at 78
abstract: A Memphis college student and activist, she witnessed Dr. King’s assassination in 1968 when he was shot at his motel and ran to him to check his pulse.

name: Simone Forti
profession: Movement Artist Inspired by the Everyday
headline: Simone Forti, Movement Artist Inspired by the Everyday, Dies at 91
abstract: The creator of Dance Constructions that borrowed from sculpture and performance, she was a deep influence in the early 1960s on ideas about what dance could be.

name: Jennifer Finch
profession: Scalding Bassist for Alt-Rock Band L7
headline: Jennifer Finch, Scalding Bassist for Alt-Rock Band L7, Dies at 59
abstract: Often performing barefoot, she provided the thunder for a breakout feminist band of the 1990s, which had an alternative hit with “Pretend We’re Dead.”

name: Jeannette Etheredge
profession: Hosted San Francisco at Tosca Cafe
headline: Jeannette Etheredge, Who Hosted San Francisco at Tosca Cafe, Dies at 85
abstract: As the North Beach bar’s proprietor for 33 years, she turned it into a hub for actors, directors, writers, dancers and politicians.

name: John Esposito
headline: John Esposito, Who Challenged Negative Views of Muslims, Dies at 86
abstract: Starting out in the 1970s as a rare American expert on political Islam, he became a prolific scholar and a prominent public intellectual.

name: John Ali
headline: John Ali, Nation of Islam Official Who Clashed With Malcolm X, Dies at 98
abstract: He was widely suspected of being an F.B.I. informant and of playing a role in the 1965 assassination of Malcolm, the charismatic Black activist.

name: Mildred Pitts Walter
profession: Author of Books for Black Children
headline: Mildred Pitts Walter, Author of Books for Black Children, Dies at 103
abstract: Teaching kindergarten in South Central Los Angeles in the 1950s and ’60s, she realized that her students were not represented in the books they read. So she wrote her own.

name: Paul Sanasardo
profession: Creator of Intense (and Even Brutal) Dances
headline: Paul Sanasardo, Creator of Intense (and Even Brutal) Dances, Dies at 97
abstract: His dreamlike, expressionistic style influenced the vividly theatrical works of the German choreographer Pina Bausch, an early collaborator.

name: Olga Soffer
headline: Olga Soffer, Fashion Maven Who Studied Caveman Couture, Dies at 83
abstract: After working for a department store, she switched to archaeology and made important discoveries about prehistoric clothes and gender roles.

name: Vincent Pastore
headline: Vincent Pastore, Whose ‘Sopranos’ Character Ratted Out Tony, Dies at 80
abstract: He played Salvatore Bonpensiero, a mobster’s foot soldier turned F.B.I. informant known to his friends as Big Pussy, on the celebrated HBO series.

name: Vicki Wickham
headline: Vicki Wickham, Behind-the-Scenes Force in Pop Music, Dies at 87
abstract: She managed artists like Labelle and Dusty Springfield, and helped run the influential 1960s British TV showcase “Ready Steady Go!”

name: Monty Roberts
headline: Monty Roberts, Horse Trainer Who Preached Kindness, Dies at 91
abstract: His approach ran counter to centuries of conventional wisdom, and it won the enthusiastic approval of Queen Elizabeth II, with whom he became friends.

name: Kay Granger
headline: Kay Granger, Pathbreaking Texas Congresswoman, Dies at 83
abstract: She was the first Republican woman from the state to be elected to the House. It caused a stir in 2024 when she was discovered to be residing in a senior living facility while still in office.

name: Mary de Rachewiltz
headline: Mary de Rachewiltz, Ezra Pound’s Daughter and Defender, Dies at 101
abstract: Sent away as a baby, she remained loyal to her famous father, translating his poetry while fighting to distinguish his literary legacy from his fascist politics.

name: Dudley Laufman
headline: Dudley Laufman, Eminent Folk Dance Caller, Dies at 95
abstract: A farmer, poet and musician, he revitalized contra dancing in the 1960s and ’70s, bringing the tradition to a new generation.

name: Emidio Pepe
headline: Emidio Pepe, Maker of Prized Abruzzo Wines, Dies at 94
abstract: He was one of the first to make a case for the local grapes and traditional methods, even as others abandoned them, inspiring a younger generation.

name: Ursula Hegi
profession: Wrote Searing Novels About Nazi-Era Germany
headline: Ursula Hegi, Who Wrote Searing Novels About Nazi-Era Germany, Dies at 80
abstract: “Stones From the River,” her best-known work and an early Oprah’s Book Club selection, was set in a fictional German town in the early 20th century.

name: Lou Koller
headline: Lou Koller, Ambassador of New York Hardcore, Dies at 61
abstract: He screamed as much as sang, as his heavy-metal-inflected punk band, Sick of It All, spread the sound of the New York underground to the world.

name: Sydney Towle
headline: Sydney Towle, Who Chronicled Her Cancer on TikTok, Dies at 26
abstract: For an audience that grew to more than a million followers, she challenged assumptions about how people with serious illnesses should look and live.

name: James R. Urbaniak
headline: James R. Urbaniak, Master of Stitching Back Fingers, Dies at 90
abstract: He was among the first to perform microscopic surgery in the 1970s and revolutionized techniques to treat traumatic injuries.

name: Thomas S. Hines
profession: Helped Put L.A. Architecture on the Map
headline: Thomas S. Hines, Who Helped Put L.A. Architecture on the Map, Dies at 89
abstract: A historian at U.C.L.A., he showed how Los Angeles’s architects and planners made the city a global center for modernist design in the 20th century.

name: Elizabeth Smith
headline: Elizabeth Smith, Voice Coach to Acting Royalty, Dies at 91
abstract: A founding faculty member of Juilliard Drama, she helped the actors Kevin Kline, Patti LuPone, Wendell Pierce and others find their voices, quite literally.

name: Charles S. Faddis
headline: Charles S. Faddis, Ex-C.I.A. Officer Who Pushed Conspiracy Theories, Dies at 68
abstract: After 20 years in the C.I.A., he emerged as an outspoken critic of the agency and as a leader of the election-denial movement in Pennsylvania.

name: Bill Goichberg
profession: Reshaped Competitive Chess in the U.S
headline: Bill Goichberg, Who Reshaped Competitive Chess in the U.S., Dies at 83
abstract: Over a six-decade career, he drastically expanded chess through the tournaments he started, especially the competitions for young players.

name: William Orbit
profession: Producer for Madonnas Ray of Light
headline: William Orbit, Producer for Madonna’s ‘Ray of Light,’ Dies at 69
abstract: A three-time Grammy winner who was renowned for his mastery of electronic music styles, he also worked with Blur, Pink, Britney Spears and All Saints.

name: Abbe Lane
profession: Sultry Singer With a Latin Flair
headline: Abbe Lane, Sultry Singer With a Latin Flair, Dies at 94
abstract: She was a Broadway dancer before becoming Xavier Cugat’s star vocalist and later building a solo career.

name: Geraldine de Haas
headline: Geraldine de Haas, the ‘First Lady’ of Chicago Jazz, Dies at 91
abstract: After a successful singing career, she led the revival of jazz in the Windy City in the 1970s and ’80s, organizing festivals and concert series.

name: Don Nelson
profession: Hall of Fame N.B.A. Coach and Celtics Star
headline: Don Nelson, Hall of Fame N.B.A. Coach and Celtics Star, Dies at 86
abstract: One of the winningest coaches in league history, he led the Bucks, the Warriors and the Mavericks. He also had a brief stint with the Knicks.

name: Maura L. Gillison
headline: Maura L. Gillison, Who Linked Throat Cancers to HPV, Dies at 61
abstract: She challenged the conventional view that most head and neck cancers resulted from cigarette smoking and excessive alcohol consumption.

name: Ben Jones
profession: Dukes of Hazzard Actor and Congressman
headline: Ben Jones, ‘Dukes of Hazzard’ Actor and Congressman, Dies at 84
abstract: He played the mechanic Cooter Davenport on the hit television series before serving two terms as a Democratic congressman from Georgia.

name: Arlene Smith
headline: Arlene Smith, Whose Song ‘Maybe’ Helped Define Doo-Wop, Dies at 84
abstract: With the Chantels, a groundbreaking female vocal group, she tugged heartstrings with the indelible hit and paved the way for a wave of “girl groups.”

name: Richard Lingeman
headline: Richard Lingeman, Cultural Historian and Biographer, Dies at 95
abstract: He spent decades as a magazine editor and wrote an acclaimed history of small-town America, as well as biographies of the novelists Theodore Dreiser and Sinclair Lewis.

name: Zhu Rongji
headline: Zhu Rongji, Former Premier Who Pushed China to a Market Economy, Dies at 97
abstract: As a vice premier and then premier, he helped transform China into the world’s leading manufacturing power and led his country into the World Trade Organization.

name: Ward Churchill
headline: Ward Churchill, Professor Who Challenged His Dismissal Over 9/11 Essay, Dies at 78
abstract: His inflammatory essay about the attacks prompted his dismissal by the University of Colorado for unrelated research misconduct. A jury later found that he had been wrongfully terminated.

name: Johanna Fernández
headline: Johanna Fernández, Historian of the Young Lords, Dies at 55
abstract: She wrote an award-winning book about the leftist collective, a Latino counterpart to the Black Panthers.

name: Alfonso Fanjul Jr.
headline: Alfonso Fanjul Jr., Cuban American Sugar Baron, Dies at 89
abstract: With his brother, he presided over a family empire that includes the world’s largest cane sugar refiner and the Domino and C&H brands.

name: Raoul Vaneigem
headline: Raoul Vaneigem, Whose Manifesto Inspired 1968 Revolt in France, Dies at 92
abstract: “The Revolution of Everyday Life,” published in 1967, was his cri de coeur against mindless work, materialism and authority.

name: Carlos Garcia
headline: Carlos Garcia, Activist Who Helped Revive the Lower East Side, Dies at 80
abstract: He led a Puerto Rican group known as Charas in turning a crumbling public school into a community center, rehabilitating a desolate slice of New York.

name: Christy Knowings
headline: Christy Knowings, Who Starred on ’90s TV Show ‘All That,’ Dies at 46
abstract: The actress rose to prominence playing absurdist characters on the Nickelodeon series known for its diverse cast and joyful silliness.

name: Youman Wilder
headline: Youman Wilder, Baseball Coach Who Said He Faced Down ICE Agents, Dies at 63
abstract: He told reporters that he intervened when federal agents approached his young Black and Latino players after a practice last summer.

name: Mary Morello
headline: Mary Morello, Free Speech Activist Who Defended Explicit Lyrics, Dies at 102
abstract: An Illinois teacher — and the mother of the rock star Tom Morello — she took on Tipper Gore during culture war skirmishes over warning labels on records.

name: Hiroshi Okuda
headline: Hiroshi Okuda, Disrupter Who Revived Toyota in the 1990s, Dies at 93
abstract: As the car company’s president, he made decisions quickly and shook things up, expanding overseas manufacturing and introducing the Prius, a milestone in automotive history.

name: John Carro
headline: John Carro, Jurist Who Had Early Brush With Lee Harvey Oswald, Dies at 98
abstract: Decades before his rise to the New York State appellate court, he was a probation officer who tried to help Mr. Oswald, then a teenager living in the Bronx.

name: Mark Rydell
profession: Actors Director Known for On Golden Pond
headline: Mark Rydell, ‘Actor’s Director’ Known for ‘On Golden Pond,’ Dies at 97
abstract: Having started out as an actor, he was able to coax sensitive work out of performers like Bette Midler, Katharine Hepburn, Henry Fonda and John Wayne.

name: Mary Heilmann
headline: Mary Heilmann, Painter of Vividly Wobbly Abstractions, Dies at 86
abstract: An emblem of the obstacles faced by women artists of her generation, she was 67 when her first museum retrospective opened to rave reviews in 2007.

name: Violet Hensley
profession: Ozarks Fiddler Made Opry Debut at 99
headline: Violet Hensley Dies at 109; Ozarks Fiddler Made Opry Debut at 99
abstract: She performed old-time mountain music at the Silver Dollar City theme park in Branson, Mo., for more than 50 years and appeared on “The Beverly Hillbillies.”

name: Bou Meng
profession: Rare Survivor of Khmer Rouge Torture House
headline: Bou Meng, Rare Survivor of Khmer Rouge Torture House, Dies at 85
abstract: Saved by his ability to paint, he was one of only a handful of prisoners to make it out of the brutal prison Tuol Sleng.

name: Zale Parry
profession: Aquatic Hollywood Star and Early Acid Tripper
headline: Zale Parry, Aquatic Hollywood Star and Early Acid Tripper, Dies at 93
abstract: A diving feat landed her on the cover of Sports Illustrated and led to a film and TV career. She also took part in one of the first LSD studies.

name: Tommy John
headline: Tommy John, Pitcher Who Gave His Name to Career-Saving Surgery, Dies at 83
abstract: After tearing an elbow ligament, he underwent a risky procedure and returned at his best, changing baseball and giving new hope to injured players.

name: Hayden Panettiere
headline: Hayden Panettiere, Star of ‘Nashville’ and ‘Heroes,’ Dies at 36
abstract: In May, she published a memoir after a tumultuous decade that involved depression, substance abuse, losing custody of her daughter and stints in rehab.

name: Pauline Clayden
