profession: Dancer in a Seminal 1949 Sleeping Beauty
headline: Pauline Clayden, Dancer in a Seminal 1949 ‘Sleeping Beauty,’ Dies at 103
abstract: She was the last known surviving soloist from an event that changed American dance: the opening night of Sadler’s Wells Ballet’s first U.S. tour.

name: Frank Beard
headline: Frank Beard, Beardless Drummer for ZZ Top, Dies at 77
abstract: The only member of the Texas power trio without a beard, he propelled the band’s blend of boogie, Southern rock and blues for more than a half-century.

name: Skip Bertman
headline: Skip Bertman, L.S.U. Baseball Coach Who Packed Stadiums, Dies at 88
abstract: Over 18 seasons at Louisiana State University, he won five national titles and was voted the second-best college baseball coach of the 20th century.

name: Derrick Parker
profession: Known as New Yorks Hip-Hop Cop
headline: Derrick Parker, Known as New York’s ‘Hip-Hop Cop,’ Dies at 65
abstract: A veteran detective with deep connections in the city’s rap scene, he served as a one-man intelligence unit and liaison to the music world.

name: Ileana Cotrubas
headline: Ileana Cotrubas, Sensitive Soprano Known for ‘Traviata,’ Dies at 87
abstract: Able to convey the pathos of operatic heroines with her pure, expressive tone, she was also involved in prickly disputes with some directors and conductors.

name: Ted Striggles
profession: Helped His Fellow Dancers as a Lawyer
headline: Ted Striggles, Who Helped His Fellow Dancers as a Lawyer, Dies at 84
abstract: He was best known for the influential 1976 guide “Poor Dancer’s Almanac,” which aimed to help starving artists survive in New York.

name: Lloyd Robertson
headline: Lloyd Robertson, Unflappable Canadian Broadcaster, Dies at 92
abstract: His 41 years as a national television news anchor surpassed the tenures of Walter Cronkite and Tom Brokaw.

name: Nancy Kissinger
profession: Wife of Former Secretary of State
headline: Nancy Kissinger, Wife of Former Secretary of State, Dies at 92
abstract: A foreign policy specialist, she was politically savvy and well versed in global issues, and traveled widely with her husband, Henry A. Kissinger, on his diplomatic missions.

name: John Rousmaniere
headline: John Rousmaniere, Who Documented a Sailing Disaster, Dies at 82
abstract: Known as the dean of American sailing historians, he wrote a chilling firsthand account of a deadly 1979 race and influenced safety standards.

name: Carlo Borlenghi
profession: Turned Sailing Photography Into an Art
headline: Carlo Borlenghi, Who Turned Sailing Photography Into an Art, Dies at 70
abstract: For four decades, he documented yachting’s top competitions. But the sailboats weren’t always the focus of his images.

name: Victor Niederhoffer
headline: Victor Niederhoffer, Trader Who Went Boom and Bust (Twice), Dies at 82
abstract: He pioneered a technique for using computers to predict short-term movements in stock prices, something that proved to be hugely lucrative — when it worked.

name: Dave Marsh
headline: Dave Marsh, Rock Critic Who Loved Springsteen and Hated the Dead, Dies at 76
abstract: A passionately opinionated veteran of Creem and Rolling Stone, he was part of a generation of writers who influenced how the world saw the golden age of rock.

name: Margo Howard
profession: Reluctant Columnist and Daughter of Ann Landers
headline: Margo Howard, Reluctant Columnist and Daughter of Ann Landers, Dies at 86
abstract: She published two books about her famous mother but didn’t fully embrace the family business until her late 50s, when she began writing “Dear Prudence” for Slate.

name: Patricia Douglas
headline: Overlooked No More: Patricia Douglas, Who Challenged Hollywood’s Culture of Abuse
abstract: Eight decades before the #MeToo groundswell, she took MGM to court after alleging she was attacked at a studio party in 1937.

name: Yvette Roudy
profession: Frances First Minister for Womens Rights
headline: Yvette Roudy, France’s First Minister for Women’s Rights, Dies at 97
abstract: Maintaining that access to abortion was as much a matter of economic equality as women’s rights, she successfully championed state reimbursement for abortions.

name: Nancy Kassebaum
profession: First Woman to Chair a Major Senate Panel
headline: Nancy Kassebaum, First Woman to Chair a Major Senate Panel, Dies at 94
abstract: A moderate Republican from Kansas, she served three terms before tiring of political strife. “I couldn’t get elected today,” she said in 2013.

name: Jeff Conolly
headline: Jeff Conolly, Manic Garage-Rock Frontman, Dies at 70
abstract: Known as Monoman for his love of vintage LPs, he kept the punkish torch burning by leading Lyres, a Boston group that became an institution.

name: Shelley Fabares
headline: Shelley Fabares, ‘Donna Reed Show’ Actress, Dies at 82
abstract: She also starred in Elvis Presley movies and the sitcom “Coach.” Somewhat reluctantly, she had a No. 1 hit in 1962 with “Johnny Angel.”

name: Man
headline: Man Who Told of a Childhood With Wolves Dies at 80
abstract: Marcos Rodríguez Pantoja’s improbable story of a wild youth became the subject of a study, and inspired a novel and film.

name: Robert Skidelsky
headline: Robert Skidelsky, Definitive Biographer of Keynes, Dies at 86
abstract: An economic historian and political maverick, he was a sometimes polarizing public intellectual and a member of the House of Lords.

name: Dolly Parton
headline: Dolly Parton, Superstar Whose Songs Spoke to Millions, Dies at 80
abstract: Known for her outsize persona, appearance and talent, she rose from rural poverty to become a top-selling singer, songwriter and entrepreneur.

name: Len Brown
headline: Len Brown, the Kidlike Creator of ‘Mars Attacks,’ Dies at 84
abstract: He brought a juvenile creative sensibility to the Topps Chewing Gum company, where he was able to unerringly predict what would appeal to adolescents.

name: Peter Nadas
profession: Author of the Greatest Novel Written in Our Time
headline: Peter Nadas, Author of ‘the Greatest Novel Written in Our Time,’ Dies at 83
abstract: Susan Sontag gave that high praise to “A Book of Memories,” a labyrinthine chronicle of life under Communism.

name: Tim Curry
profession: Star of Rocky Horror and Much More
headline: Tim Curry, Star of ‘Rocky Horror’ and Much More, Dies at 80
abstract: The actor’s gift for garish eccentricity was indelibly appropriate for the outlandish, cross-dressing mad scientist Frank-N-Furter.

name: Janie Bradford
headline: Janie Bradford, Co-Writer of Motown’s First Hit, Dies at 87
abstract: One of the label’s first hires, she worked on “Money (That’s What I Want)” and went on to have a hand in many other songs.

name: Yayoi Kusama
headline: Yayoi Kusama, Pop Artist Who Expanded and Endured, Dies at 97
abstract: The Japanese artist’s polka-dot-covered paintings, phallic sculptures and public performances caused a stir in New York City and Europe in the 1960s.

name: Ratko Mladic
headline: Ratko Mladic, Murderous ‘Butcher of Bosnia,’ Dies at 83
abstract: A general during the Balkan wars of the 1990s, he was convicted in the killing of some 8,000 Muslims at Srebrenica, Europe’s deadliest massacre since World War II.

name: Laura Spector
profession: Turned a Loathsome Vine Into Art
headline: Laura Spector, Who Turned a Loathsome Vine Into Art, Dies at 71
abstract: Using Asian bittersweet, the much-hated invasive species, she created whimsical rustic objects and enchanting furniture.

name: Jaye P. Morgan
profession: Hit-Making Singer and Bawdy TV Personality
headline: Jaye P. Morgan, Hit-Making Singer and Bawdy TV Personality, Dies at 94
abstract: With a humorous stage name adapted from that of the New York financier, she made a 1950s Hit Parade splash and later was a flamboyant talk-show regular.

name: Benjamin Rosen
headline: Benjamin Rosen, Who Brought Venture Capital to Tech, Dies at 93
abstract: An advocate for Apple on Wall Street, he was also a founding investor in early personal computing firms like Lotus and Compaq, where he served as chairman.

name: Peter Cullen
headline: Peter Cullen, Voice Actor Who Gave Optimus Prime a Soul, Dies at 85
abstract: He voiced the main protagonist of the “Transformers” franchise on television and in blockbuster films for more than four decades. He also had success as Eeyore in “Winnie the Pooh” cartoons.

name: Harald V
profession: Norways King as Tradition and Modernity Collided
headline: Harald V, Norway’s King as Tradition and Modernity Collided, Dies at 89
abstract: His 35-year reign opened an ancient monarchy to marriages with so-called commoners and to an incendiary association with Jeffrey Epstein.

name: Benjamin Alire Sáenz
profession: First Latino Writer to Win PEN/Faulkner
headline: Benjamin Alire Sáenz, First Latino Writer to Win PEN/Faulkner, Dies at 71
abstract: A former Catholic priest, he later became an acclaimed author, writing more than two dozen works about life in the U.S.-Mexican borderlands.

name: Roy Slaper
headline: Roy Slaper, Unlikely ‘Legend’ of Denim, Dies at 54
abstract: After filling his apartment with industrial sewing machines, he began producing high-end jeans that made him famous with denim-heads in the days of lumberjack chic.

name: George Cave
profession: C.I.A. Officer With a Role in Iran-Contra
headline: George Cave, C.I.A. Officer With a Role in Iran-Contra, Dies at 97
abstract: He worked throughout the Middle East before joining a secret team that tried to obtain the release of Western hostages in Lebanon in exchange for arms sent to Iran.

name: Azriel Blackman
headline: Azriel Blackman, Airline Mechanic for 80 Years, Dies at 100
abstract: With a career commemorated by Guinness World Records, he started as an apprentice in 1942 and worked on a panoply of propeller-driven and jet aircraft until he retired in 2022.

name: Édouard Balladur
headline: Édouard Balladur, Embattled French Prime Minister, Dies at 97
abstract: His time in office coincided with France’s fraught role in the 1994 Rwandan genocide and the corruption scandal known as the Karachi affair.

name: Wendell Berry
headline: Wendell Berry, Writer Who Extolled America’s Agrarian Past, Dies at 92
abstract: A Kentucky farmer, he railed against agribusiness and championed small family farms and the environment, winning widespread acclaim.

name: Juan Tamariz
profession: Master Magician of Misdirection and Joy
headline: Juan Tamariz, Master Magician of Misdirection and Joy, Dies at 83
abstract: A magician’s magician, he was a philosopher of the craft. He didn’t just want to fool people; he wanted to share in their awe of the inexplicable.

name: Sliman Mansour
headline: Sliman Mansour, Artist Who Depicted Palestinian Struggle, Dies at 79
abstract: His idealized images of heroic Palestinian women, men and children made their way into hundreds of homes as inspirational posters.

name: Ada Yonath
profession: Chemist and First Israeli Woman to Receive a Nobel
headline: Ada Yonath, Chemist and First Israeli Woman to Receive a Nobel, Dies at 87
abstract: Her mapping of the ribosome, which led to new designs for antibiotics, faced years of derision, as many scientists saw it as a dead-end effort.

name: Patrick Gleeson
headline: Patrick Gleeson, Who Made Synthesizers Part of Jazz, Dies at 91
abstract: He abandoned a job teaching college English in the 1960s to become a pioneer of the instrument, playing onstage with Herbie Hancock’s jazz band.

name: Paul S. Russell
headline: Paul S. Russell, an Innovator in Transplant Medicine, Dies at 101
abstract: In his over 70 years at Massachusetts General Hospital, he led the way in turning new findings in medical science into successes in clinical practice.

name: Cassandra Wilson
headline: Cassandra Wilson, Star Jazz Singer, Dies at 70
abstract: With a low and smoky voice, she conjured the blues tradition of her native Mississippi in both her own songs and in covers.

headline: Barbara Furrer Goodman Educator, 74, Dies
abstract: Mrs. Goodman was a teacher and former chairwoman of the board of trustees at Teachers College at Columbia University.

headline: Comedian Red Buttons Dies at 87
abstract: Comedian Red Buttons rebounded from obscurity to win an Academy Award for his dramatic performance in the 1957 film “Sayonara.”

headline: Wife of Rev. Billy Graham Dies at 87
abstract: For more than 60 years, Ruth Bell Graham devoted herself to her husband’s career as the 20th century’s most enduring evangelist.

headline: British Journalist, Ludovic Kennedy, Dies at 89
abstract: Mr. Kennedy campaigned against miscarriages of justice and religious dogmatism and in support of euthanasia and independence for his native Scotland.

headline: African-American Golf Pioneer Bill Powell Dies at 93
abstract: Mr. Powell was the first African-American to build, own and operate a golf course.
